_childDocuments_.review: One of the most unique games out there today. The album/soundtrack is fabulous, and the story, even though - or probably because - it is so tragic, is addictive.It's absurd - even though I have only 3.2 hours of gameplay so far, I've spent so much time watching walkthrough videos and the game store's pre-recorded stream of act I over and over again, listening to the music and learning how to complete the objectives.So in fact I have spent dozens of hours watching those videos and listening to the music, and obviously the music and the story kept filling my mind throughout the ~12 days since the game release.I do agree the gameplay mechanics (fighting and QTEs) need to be improved, but in my opinion it doesn't affect the overall experience, which is a blast.I would give this game 9.9/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Of Bird and Cage

_childDocuments_.review: This game is interesting. The music is great, the story is twisted and good. The gameplay is a bit rough, and some of the animation are not that good. I did like the choices and the possibilities. Sometimes the gameplay was just too hard, but the experience was interesting. Im interested to see the other endings.
_childDocuments_.name: Of Bird and Cage

_childDocuments_.review: Accidentaly wrote it as a comment, but...Wow.......What a great soundtrack for a game. There were moments were I could just sit back and vibe with the music. I wish sometimes there were a bit more time, or maybe a bit more guidance on where to find things, since everything is time based in the game, it was hard to explore when your'e busy chasing the clock all the time. On top of everything - this was such a great experience. I hope they make it into a genre and make more albums this way.
_childDocuments_.name: Of Bird and Cage

_childDocuments_.review: For me, this is the first experience of playing in such an unusual genre. The game is cool!Their pluses:- graphics- musical accompaniment bomb- plot (there is something to think about, for this many thanks to the authors and developers)As such, I didnt see the minuses, but for beginners, especially those with mediocre knowledge of the languages ​​in which the game is now available, it can be difficult. Since many "tasks" in the game go on for a while and you need to make decisions right away, and not think about what to do and how this or that action is translated. But again, this can wake up interest in the game and in what is happening, which will provoke people to additional training! This is great!Rating 8/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Of Bird and Cage

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished a run with the game! The music is top-notch and level design really conveys the atmosphere of each song. I especially liked levels that were more abstract, that shows Gitta's subconscious and past memories. It was a very unique way to experience a music album, and I believe I'll return to it for a replay to try and catch things I've missed in my first run, now that I know the context behind it.
_childDocuments_.name: Of Bird and Cage

_childDocuments_.review: There's no denying that the music is great and in my honest opinion actually makes the game shine for that specifically.I've played through the first two acts and it's been a bit of an emotional roller coaster while trying to guess everything that's gonna happen and think about how everything I do will be affected.That being said, it felt like I didn't have a lot of control as I would've preferred... QTE within a timed environment is interesting, but I guess maybe it works better with the music?I found it pretty difficult to control things properly at times and adjusting wasn't that easy, but that might be just me.I also personally found it a bit more difficult to track what's happening at times through the story because as soon as I learned something, something else happens and changes my perspective but I believe I need to play more to understand it even better.Also, it might be worth to making the seizure warning stand out a bit more early when you load the game.For the music specifically, I do recommend it or if you're a completionist and really want to go through the game multiple times ^_^
_childDocuments_.name: Of Bird and Cage

_childDocuments_.review: After 30-40 minutes of playing this game I thought it would be sufficient enough time to leave a review. The concept of the story is interesting especially with the main character being a drug addict because the hallucinations add another layer of detail. Of Bird and Cage utilizes the old school concept of suspense and suggestion for the danger/scare aspect. This is similar to how old school horror movies or the horror short stories of Edgar Allen Poe, think Pit & The Pendulum, work to draw audiences in. Overall I find this to be a solid concept and look forward to playing more in the future. Considering this is far outside my genre of normal games (JRPGs, Mario, Zelda, etc.) I think a follow up review would be appropriate after additional play time but didn't want to let my initial impression of the game slip through my fingers
_childDocuments_.name: Of Bird and Cage

_childDocuments_.review: So yeah, I've played through this game once as of now, missed about every possible quick time events available, but still had a blast with this game. Incredibly engaging, squeezes the soul and never quite let go. I'll try to do better next time, because there WILL be another time through this game. Yes, I bought the soundtrack as well, but it's not the same experience (still a great OST, I highly recommend getting the whole package).
_childDocuments_.name: Of Bird and Cage

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, This game is so rocking, from the start all the way to the end...The music sucks you in and then the story sucks you in even more. I can't praise Capricia Productions enough for your 6 years of work. This game is for sure a game that will be replayed until all possibilities are found. I have never seen a game like this before. I don't think there will ever be a game like it again....unless they make another one. Seriously if you haven't done so already go buy this game. You will love it.
_childDocuments_.name: Of Bird and Cage

_childDocuments_.review: Good story progression, For you crazy gamers that like to 100% everything there are collectables and puzzles and things to keep you busy :)For sure the music is good in this game and integrates with the story very well.I went through the first run of this game and reached one ending and would love to play it more soon and change choices and see what other mischief and results I can get from doing things differently.I caught myself staring at the monitor to see what happens in silence, I caught myself headbanging to the music while listening to the lyrics to understand who is who and what's going on!Overall I would recommend this game and I have enjoyed my first run and I'm sure I will enjoy the following ones as well to see what other endings I can get :D
_childDocuments_.name: Of Bird and Cage

_childDocuments_.review: Of Bird and Cage is a unique metal album presented through a two-hour-long story-driven game. Play music in a brand-new way. Featuring famous artists like Ron "Bumblefoot" Thal (ex-Guns N' Roses), Rob van der Loo (Epica), Ruud Jolie (Within Temptation), and many others!

name: Satisfactory
detailed_description: Satisfactory is a first-person open-world factory building game with a dash of exploration and combat. Play alone or with friends, explore an alien planet, create multi-story factories, and enter conveyor belt heaven! Construct Conquer nature by building massive factories across the land. Expand wherever and however you want. The planet is filled with valuable natural resources just waiting to be utilized. As an employee of FICSIT it’s your duty to make sure they come to good use. Automate Construct your factories with gracious perfection or build intricate webs of conveyor belts to supply all your needs. Automate trucks and trains to reach your faraway outposts and be sure to handle liquids properly by transporting them in pipes. It’s all about minimizing manual labour! Explore & Exploit Venture on expeditions to search for new materials and be sure to put everything to good use. Nature is yours to harvest! You have vehicles, jetpacks, jump pads and more at your disposal to make the exploration easier. Equip the proper safety gear as well, just in case you run into the local wildlife. FEATURES • Open World: Explore the huge (30km2) alien planet that is Massage-2(AB)b with its unique fauna and creatures. • Co-Op: Build a factory yourself or share the joy with your friends. Up to you! • Factory Building: Experience building a huge factory from a first-person perspective. Automate and optimize it to perfection for your personal satisfaction. • Customization: Customize your factory to your own liking. Build at high altitudes or over wide plains, there is almost no limits in the making of your tailor-made factory. • Vehicles: Travel the world with class. Use jump pads, factory carts, jetpacks, hypertubes, trucks or trains. The choice is yours!

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best factory games out there.It is definitely more of a chill experience. You don't need to optimise or be resourceful, but you absolutely can. You don't need to make it look cool, but you absolutely can. It often gets compared to Factorio, and rightfully so, but they differ in some pretty major ways. Satisfactory is more about building things to your own goals and specifications, then sitting back and admiring. Factorio has real win and loss conditions, as well as antagonists. Factorio can stress people out because you have a constant nagging feeling that you are either running out of something, or about to be swarmed. Satisfactory is much more casual in that regard, and therefore leans more into the relaxation or idler type games. Long story short, leaving your PC running is a strategy for success in Satisfactory. In Factorio, bugs will bite your face off.If you are remotely interested in this game you should get it.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: Satisfactory hit me hard. I had no idea it even existed until 1.0 release. The game is basically a first person sandbox factory building game with soft survival elements. The developers have masterfully implemented what they call mission command in military or mission oriented leadership in business. The player is given a set of goals to achieve, limits and resources. The player is free to choose how the goals are achieved within those limits and with resources in hand. The goals and therefor factory automation challenges become harder over time.Although the core game play goal is to automate the factory, player can still choose not to do that. You can build a massive factory or put down just one machine that produces the goal part and manually feed it with parts crafted by the player in workbench. The scope is really left for the player to decide. Everything built can be dismantled and all resources used for the construction are given back when dismantling.The game world has passive and aggressive creatures in it. The aggressive ones will kill you but you can kill them also and better tools to do that will become available as the game progresses. For me, the aggressive creatures are a sort of developer after thought and in my opinion should not have been implemented. But, they can be dealt with so no big issue.Visually the game is beautiful. There is a day night cycle of about 30 minutes of real time. The world is huge with many distinct environments. Being a sandbox game, some built structures sometimes clip trough the environment and sometimes there is little of texture fighting between two or more structures. The factory can be visually modified almost any way you like and you unlock more visual stuff as the game progresses. The game has short back story and more lore and story are revealed during game play and exploration. But the story is not why you should play this. It's just there to give something for the player to justify the game. Exploration is somewhat optional in the game, however, you do need to find resources and exploration can help greatly in the game.The game requires a little bit of grade school math and problem solving skills but there are online resources to help calculate and plan factories. Plus an extensive community that gives you ideas or blueprints for factories.I have not come across any game breaking bugs. There are few very minor ones though. For example, when the player inventory is full and you dismantle something, the resources are put in a specific dismantle grate. Sometimes these grates can spawn underground and there is no way to remove them in the game. There is a online web site where you can do that though.All in all, very good game and worth your money provided that this type of game fits you. Definitely recommend.

If you want a less hateful sandbox than factorio, this game is for you. I have the tendency to remove the download so I can continue on with life, you may experience the same issue. I always come back, you should too
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: It starts out fun then dives down. The reason it stops getting fun is the game begins to artificially force you to waste time. It starts by simply making required items take longer and longer times to craft. And then it requires you to make hundreds of those items that each take a long time to make. After that the game makes resources hard to get. It does that by placing required late game ores not only far away but on terrain that you cannot traverse without wasting over an hour. It all just boils down to the game puts the breaks on you very hard and that makes it no longer fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: Where to begin?! I was a bit skeptical at first since I'm not really into the whole "survival" genre but seeing some of the gameplay online I decided to buy the game. I've got the game a few days now and already I played around 29 hours haha!! Time flies when you're having fun! Highly addictive gameplay and I really love the overall design of the machines and the way things work. The most incredible feat for me is that the game is in Early Access and already there are ton's of features, machine's and ways to get stuff. I'm about to unlock Tier 5 & 6 and I hope the fun and new stuff never ends because that's what keeps things interesting I think. Yes, sometimes you see a bit of weird stuff going on, animals not obeying the boundry boxes of objects and I've found stuff that can't be used right now but probably in the next update I hope ;-) Stuff is getting bigger and bigger! Keep it up Coffee Stain Studio!
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: Satisfactory is very much early access done right.The game runs well and has a reasonable degree of polish.The devs have opted for less frequent but larger updates which while not quite my preference, they are handling it all well.Overall would absolutely recommend for anyone who likes automation and organization in their games.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: I LOVED this game! I played with three other friends, and it was a great experience. Very seamless - there was no time (Except for the very end!) that I felt bored or unoccupied. There was always something to automate, explore, and exploit. Funny Dialogue, satisfying numbers, and really meaningful progression. There was no time during this game that I wasn't going "Oh wow, this is so nice to have!"All the variety created by the alternates is awesome, too. Using vehicles, belts, drones, and even TRAINS (Which were probably my favorite!!! Shoutout to my fave locomotive ShupoShupo!!!) made using the map fun and enjoyable, and downright scenic on our rail line. Part way through we dabbled with mods and found a great variety of nice QOL ones that didn't break progression and instead just made the game more fun.I think this is genuinely my favorite game of 2024, and I played TOTK this year! I heavily endorse it to anyone who wants a truly unique problem solving game.

_childDocuments_.review: I normally would get easily frustrated playing games like Factorio, despite the idea of loving the overall mechanics of the game-- but this game finds a healthy balance of allowing me to clean up messes and use buildings to make things more manageable, and I don't ever feel frustrated with getting the layout wrong.  In fact, I usually get excited about retrying, whereas with other games I usually would just quit.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: As a big fan of Factorio and the automation genre, Satisfactory comes across as just... disappointing. The automation buildings themselves are massively over-sized and their restricted options for I/O orientation, combined with the lack of space requirements and massive amounts of clipping allows, and even encourages lazy belt spaghetti. Automating an intermediary was never fun, and felt like it took way too long as it was difficult to size out and place all these massive building from the very limited first-person perspective.The resource nodes may be my biggest complaint with the game. Having unlimited resources on each node means that even from the beginning the game is practically in 'creative mode' already. It doesn't matter if you've built good  or bad infrastructure when the resources will flow either way. And the same map and nodes with absolutely no variation means very limited replayability.While not every factory game needs to have hostile enemies, if you are going to have hostile enemies they should at least do . There's no buildings or turrets that interact with the enemies and they don't even attack your infrastructure meaning they are a minor annoyance at the beginning, and then you never have to interact with them again, save for walking to a new resource node.There's so many more of of these gripes I have with this game, but those are just the major ones. The lack of basic QoL features could be attributed to the 'EARLY ACCESS' state of the game so I will save those complaints. The vehicles seem neat, but again there's not much of a reason you can't just belt everything. Satisfactory at its core is underwhelming and fails to scratch the same itch as other factory games.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: I just need to finish this last thing before I get off...Wait.  I should really hook up one more ore node.  Ok, I need more power.  Let me just clean up this area a little...6 hours later...the hunger sets in.  I remember I am mortal.  I must leave the factory to sustain myself.Yeah, I'd say it's a pretty fun game.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, just wow...Most of my highest played games I eventually get sick of, in fact the games I have the most fond memories of I have some of the lowest hours in.Satisfactory isn't like that, 300hrs and I still adore the game, its endlessly satisfying, sounds amazing, and looks even better! I've just started a new playthrough with the full release and am absolutely loving the early game setup, not to mention the little story hints popping up here and there. I'm looking forward to sinking many more hours into this game!THE FACTORY MUST GROW
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: I do not play base building style of games. They have nailed it here though, for me at least. I love the game and play it a lot now. I have almost 80 hours into it now...and it's still the right amount of engaging, challenging, and stimulating that there was at hour 1. Everything is spaced out extremely well, no waiting hours to hit a milestone or waiting for something to be crafted. They nailed it here. If it looks the slightest bit attractive to you, buy it and you'll have a lot of fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: I wish there was a neutral or meh option instead of yes or no, but for me this game is a resounding not for me.I'm a builder and I was initially chased away from the Early Access because of the addition of the creatures. I understand that people wanted to have this in the game, but I was not one of them. With the release of 1.0, I was excited to try things again with my friends and at the time of writing this, the server is still up and going.The more I interacted with the game, in particular the building tools, I became disillusioned with what was available. The decal paints don't work on half blocks and they take up the whole block even if the decal is only half of it meaning you cannot combine decals. I didn't know this and had made an entire road, hoping I could use the decals on the half blocks to make working roads with a center for trucks/tractors and side half block roads for people and carts. This is currently not possible. We need to have more texture options and more texture control. I get annoyed when a concrete block decides to change its texture from the two variants and I cannot change it back to the other. I wish there was also wooden walls, flooring and columns as well as stone and/or brick. This addition alone would improve build variety.There are also a lot of small pieces that if added to the game would assist in the designs currently capable. _childDocuments_.review: I have been Hyper-focusing on this game for the last 10 hours (played for a total of 50 hours) and it is honestly the most satisfying grindy game. Automating any process is easy, but doing it well is very difficult. I've torn down my entire factory and rebuilt it for a better layout once and now I'm building hundreds of feet in the air so I can do it again with a completely flat surface. The sense of achievement you feel from perfectly balancing a production line is unlike anything I have felt in any other game. On paper you would think that a game about such things would be boring but I am only left with the need to keep expanding and consuming resources for my grand machine. The sky beast requires more and more complex products requiring more and more resources and you wish to provide so you can improve your machine further. As I continue to bend the world to satisfy the whims of the sky giant, destroying flora and fauna with equal prejudice knowing that I am dooming many of its number to similar fate or perhaps worse. I feel mad glee at sending these arbitrary bits to the stars for the enjoyment of my unknowable god. The game world is beautiful with its colorful natural environment and picturesque vistas. As I cover it in concrete the creatures who only seek to protect their territories bear witness to my great works and despair. For on some level they know, the sky beast’s hunger is ceaseless and I will not stop until the entire world is part of my machine.    Also you can pet the lizard doggo so 10/10 game of the year.

_childDocuments_.review: I originally wrote a review for this title back around Update 5 in Early Access. It was a great singleplayer and co-op experience (Minus a few minor multiplayer hiccups). Now here we are at the 1.0 release for the game. I've spun up a dedicated server and now have six friends all together on a world at once, and with the amazing amount of QOL changes that have been made over the past few years, this game is absolutely amazing and I could not recommend it enough to anyone on the fence. It's a true story of Early Access done right and I cannot commend Coffee Stain enough for their work on this title. I gave this game an 8/10 during Early Access, it is easily a 9-10 / 10 now for me.The basic premise is that you are dropped on a world to exploit its resources to complete what is known as Project Assembly. To do this, you need to construct highly intricate parts that become more complex over time, and that's where the "factory" in the title come from. Automation of parts helps to cut down workloads significantly, but these too can become quite complex in the late game, and that adds more fun to the mix. Exploration of the large world will help you scout out locations to acquire more or new resources to help you, and also discover some secrets to power your factory in interesting ways, but beware, because the world can throw some little nasties back at you, but a few intuitive creations will solve those problems quite quickly. :)All in all, a wonderful game that you can run solo or with some friends. Having some friends will cut down on workloads for larger setups, but it also introduces the chance to see different build styles in your world. The community is great and the dev. team has been with us the entire way through. Here's to many more years of automation and optimization! Now where did I put those damned power shards?

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE AFTER 1.0Oh man, this thing was WORTH THE WAIT. I just checked, 636 hours now and almost 200 of those are from after 1.0. Addicting isn't even capable of describing this game and how it is. Also, for those of you who care, I know, there are dozens of us, this game works perfectly on Linux. I now game exclusively of an Arch VM running on a Slackware host and it runs beautifully. All i am gonna say is, what they did with the Mercer Spheres and Sommersloops from when I firsdt started playing and they were WIP to now is just flipping genius!!! PLAY THIS GAME!!!So, Just put in a little over 100 hours over the last few weeks while recovering from COVID and also a little after while working from home now. SO I have had a chance to accomplish EVERYTHING this game has to offer, 100% of it. Yes, I do realize it is still early access right now and there will eventually be more to do but for now it's done. SO what do I think? Yeah, I like, it, kinda right up my alley so to speak with the crazy automation, rat's nests of conveyor belts, automatic trucks that drive around moving supplies and such back and forth, and a flipping automated train... a TRAIN... Yeah...There are a lot of things I would like to see, a LOT of bugs, water that acts like it's not there, phantom water you can swim in that isn't there graphically, whole missing chunks of geometry, odd behavior for placing belts, pipes, and especially terrible funkiness with train tracks. It is early access I get it but some of them make some of the gameplay rather hard to manage. All this having been said, I enjoyed my time with it and I do intend to in the future buy a second copy of this so my son and I can play multiplayer, and I don't buy multiple copies for local multiplayer of games very often. By not often I mean a small handful of times in my whole life and I am a 36-year-old husband and father so if anyone needed to do so, it would be me. Yes, yes I know the developers of this game did the terrible thing of announcing a Steam game yet signing a deal with EPIC for money to be exclusive for 6 months, and yet KEPT getting free advertising from Valve, Free Forums, it's an ethical nightmare. No, No one can ever do this again because the new Steam Contracts disallow that sort of thing. After all, the developers of both this and also mainstream games like Borderlands 3 ALSO did and unashamedly took advantage of Steam to sell their game on another platform for FREE. If you are like me, you can and will never trust a developer again who does this sort of nonsense and you could be very right in not buying this game at all because of it, I probably should have done that to make a statement. HOWEVER!!! If I didn't buy the game on STEAM then I wouldn't be a sale to them at all, what says I would have bought it in the first place? As a paying customer on the better platform and avoiding the moral issues of what EPIC is/was doing, I have a voice. I bought the game on Steam, and only on Steam, not because I am a fanboy or whatever, but because I just plain prefer it and I have moral issues with how EPIC does their thing. These are my thoughts, that's it. I will NOT allow this to affect my enjoyment of this game and it will not affect my review because I am reviewing a game, not a developer's lack of morals. In conclusion, I LOVED my time with this game and I do look forward to more time as it updates and gets closer to the final product. I would say, buy it, for the number of hours I got out of it right now without ever playing it again in my whole life, it was worth it.EDIT: Typos galore, YIKES. I fixed a boatload of them.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is like a combination of Factorio and Subnautica, which sounds like a winning combination, where I look forward to the exploration as a way to boost my factory and vice-versa. In reality both are watered down versions of those games and I'm not excited about either part.The exploration is disappointing, although it's a lesser part of the game. The creatures are jankily animated and boring to fight. The world is sparse and feels like procedurally generated Unreal Engine terrain. It all seems kind of moot anyway because it to keep things organized everything should be built on foundations.I wouldn't mind all of the above but factory building is such a slog. Placing buildings in 3D and lining up your belts and wires is so finicky and frustrating. It's absolutely brutal to calculate exactly what buildings you need to place for your factory in 30 seconds, and yet you still have 10 minutes ahead of you placing and hooking up everything. The satisfaction I get from my working factory and progressing along the tech tree doesn't make up for the tedious micro gameplay. The last straw for me was realizing I miscalculated the ratios of inputs and outputs after turning on my factory, and now I have to scrap 30 minutes of work and try again. If Factorio is like coding embedded C++, and DSP is like coding Java microservices, this game feels like coding with punchcards (not that I've done that but my point is it's painful)It wasn't a surprise to me to learn that this studio made Valheim as well. I was genuinely enjoying that game but the tedious stamina and death mechanics just outweighed whatever I would look forward to in the future. They either don't test their own games or they're all such elite gamers that they never face these frustrations.

_childDocuments_.review: This game satisfies (heh) my ocd with the ability to make any factory as aesthetic as you want or as efficient as you want, and the experience still being entertaining either way. While the lack of blueprints may turn some off, I feel the requirement of doing everything in vanilla by hand adds to the impressiveness and satisfactory feeling when you finish a large project or get something finished the first time. Also, i've played 200 hrs without mods and i've read online that the mod community is amazing and easy to get into, and for a game this early in its updates (recently the fluid and QoL update has dropped introducing packagers and finally ladders!) its pretty cool to see a thriving mod community.Edit 11/23/22: After another 230 hours, (430 total) lets get an update! I did take a long break between some of the updates, so I haven't fully explored each. The previous updates have continued to bring wonderful improvements! Newer vehicles like drones have brought different transportation method to factories. New and improved equipment like the electrical hoverpack have brought easier ways to continue building factories as well! Other great additions bring new recipes and alternatives to existing items, and QoL updates like the map system and additional equipment slots have been wonderful to play with as well. Other additions such as beams and signs bring a huge amount of decoration possibilities and interesting placement options, I honestly think they may have been one of the greatest additions to the game. Hilariously, the end of my old review mentions blueprints and they have recently implemented a blueprint type system in the experimental version of update 7! It's a fairly new system currently, but has been fun to try out so far.

_childDocuments_.review: From the moment I planted my virtual boots on the alien soil of Satisfactory, I knew I was in for an experience unlike any other. This game is not just 'satisfactory' - it's phenomenal. It's a masterpiece of game design, a brilliant blend of strategy, creativity, and exploration that consistently impresses at every turn.Starting with the basics, Satisfactory is a first-person open-world factory building game. But that simple description doesn't do justice to the extraordinary adventure that awaits within. The graphics are stunning, showcasing an alien world filled with vibrant flora and fauna, towering mountains, sprawling plains, and deep oceans. It's a visual spectacle that never ceases to amaze, no matter how many hours you pour into it.The core of Satisfactory is its factory building and automation mechanics. And let me tell you, it's a treat to watch your industrial empire grow from a modest iron mining operation to a sprawling, complex network of interconnected factories and supply chains. The game's open-ended nature means there's no 'right' way to build, allowing your creativity to run wild. The level of detail and complexity possible is truly awe-inspiring, with intricate conveyor belts, pipes, and factories all working together in perfect harmony. It's a sight to behold when your meticulously designed factory buzzes with activity.One of the standout features of Satisfactory is the sense of progression. You start with simple hand tools, and over time, unlock more advanced technology, allowing you to automate and optimize your operations on a grand scale. Each milestone feels significant, rewarding your strategic planning and hard work with new tools and capabilities. It's a continuous cycle of setting goals, achieving them, and then setting your sights on even loftier objectives.The game's exploration aspect is equally impressive. Uncharted territories beckon with the promise of new resources and discoveries. The world of Satisfactory is not just a backdrop for your factories - it's a living, breathing ecosystem that invites exploration and adventure. The sense of wonder you get from discovering a new species or stumbling upon a breathtaking vista is simply unforgettable.However, what sets Satisfactory apart from other games in its genre is its multiplayer mode. Collaborating with friends to construct colossal factories is an experience filled with joy and camaraderie. The game brilliantly balances cooperation and competition, making for an exciting and dynamic multiplayer experience that's hard to beat.The developers, Coffee Stain Studios, deserve high praise for their commitment to the game. Regular updates bring new content, improvements, and bug fixes, ensuring the game continues to evolve and keep players engaged.To wrap up, Satisfactory is a triumph of game design. It's a game that celebrates creativity, rewards strategic thinking, and provides a captivating world to explore. Whether you're a veteran gamer looking for your next challenge or a casual player seeking a relaxing and rewarding experience, Satisfactory is a must-play. I cannot recommend it highly enough. It's more than just satisfactory – it's a gaming nirvana that will keep you coming back for more.

_childDocuments_.review: For a factory game where infinite resource nodes line up quite precisely with maximum quantity per minute on belts or in pipes, mechanics surprisingly makes for an INFURIATING and UNBEARABLE task to even try achieved such satisfactory efficiency.To flip this thumb, they really need to apply some tolerance so you can achieve 100% throughputs reliably.After 100s of hours, any rewards from getting things up and running are already completely spoiled beforehand due to the hopeless frustration endured.Not a game for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: ♥♥♥♥♥♥ RADICAL! Allows for creatives to find efficient/stylish methods of manufacturing materials while still having the option to embrace its numerical nature by min/maxing machines to function on the perfect percentiles of power. Even better with a friend or two although, after extended periods of time, anyone who isn't the host might experience some minor bugs and/or lag. Highly recommend if you need something to sink time into.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: I've had this game for a while. I love Satisfactory. I place this neck and neck with Factorio and other games that involve crafting. Satisfactory is my favorite survival crafting exploration game. There is this massive handcrafted world. Unlimited resources. Awesome graphics. The immersion is great and this is maybe the most chill game I've ever owned. It's a game you can play with an addiction and there is little to no violence and the pace is what you make it.  There is no pressure. You just play it and build something neat that looks pretty. Progressing to the next tier. Exploring. It's been ages and now the game is finally 1.0. A complete game.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: Easy to play, hard to master. Turns hours into moments. Not as frantic as for example Factorio because enemies won't actively come for the player but not a pushover either. Unless you prefer peaceful mode which is available.Looks really nice on modern hardware while still playable on my 15 year old 3 series I5 and GTX1660 TI.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: best factory game i have ever played. I have seen games like Factorio and Mindisty and this game is like a perfect blend of the two. Things to fight and kill along with a big world to build giant factorys with. It blows my mind every time i remind myself this game is still in beta (at the time of writing this).
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: This game really has come a long way since I first picked it up to play with my buddy (great multiplayer game even in its early state).To get the elephant out of the room yes it dose feel a bit like a 3d version of factoria but that's doing both game a disservice.Sat feels more chill and zen/puzzle like then Fac ever did. It feels like Factoria and Subnatica had a baby but it was chiller then either parent. I think I get the subnatica vibes from its rich alien world that full of strange flora and fauna. Coupled with a compelling build system.It also boasts a robust modding community, despite the fact that game updates can and do break bigger mods for a time. This is not to say that the devs don't care in-fact it seems they go out of there way to help foster mods for there game. But they also want to improve their game and sometimes that means big changes. They do put out exerimental updates and such so savy modders usually know what to expect.Lastly, about the dev team. If you don't already know coffee stain studio you should stop whatever your doing right now and look them up. It's ok I can wait...Are you back yet? Yeah they make/produce all those games. That cool indy title you saw someone stream the other day? They probably are working on that too. It might just be me but it seems that every game I have been playing and loving they have some sort of hand in it. This is all to say if I see a Coffee stain Studio game on early access I know that I will probably rack far too many hours on it and I never worry about it being some cash grab or abandon ware. These guys are the real deal.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy supply chain management and exploration, with or without friends in multiplayer, you will like this game. It's very similar to "Factorio" but obviously more polished graphically. It's still Early Access so there are some bugs, especially in multiplayer, but the game is definitely worth the money in its current state. I look forward to seeing what future updates will bring, and thank you for bringing this to Steam!
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: This is an amazing game, grindy AF and a progression system that keeps you working towards something for so many hours its ridiculous. Smooth running with hardly any issues. Obviously being early access its expected to have hiccups which are very minimal. Can't wait to see the product when its finished! This should be the benchmark of all EA games. Keep up the great work Devs! thank you for the GG :)
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: Although this is still an early access game, it is working quite nicely. There are some crashes every now and then but these only happen once i stream and i blame my GTX 1070 for running out of VRAM for it. The game is fun, you can do whatever you want and you can even Co-OP. Follow "let's game it out" and create a mess or follow your next youtuber and create a perfectly organized factory - or several at that, no one tells you what to do or how to do it. Despite all the good, there is something bad: One minor flaw with the fauna is, that sometimes it renders quite late and it spawns right on top of you, which makes the default settings for aggression a bit annoying. I would recommend to set it to retaliate, if you have the same problem.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: Graphics = BeautifulGameplay= Smooth and polishedInterface easy to understandMechanics of the game (the building and crafting) = IntriguingCombat what i've seen so far = kidna mehh, similar to minecraftStoryline: none that i know of yet.Content seems to be plentyFrom the perspective of the game as a builder/farmer game i'd rate it as an A-Game. if they add more creatures, more technology, improve on the combat system and perhaps add a storyline. this game will be complete and i'd give it a tripple AAA status. i would like the game to go through the history of using sticks and stones to highly advanced space tech. that'd be epic.Conclusion/TLDR: Still the best smoothest/polished farming/building simulation i've ever played,  yeah i recommend it!.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: Started playing the game the second time after a few years.  I am sure this time Everything will be logical.Cut to 30 hours later and There are thing everywhere and I only really know where things end up and not how they got there.It's just so satisfying.Updated for 2022, I feel like still calling this early access is a stretch, it's been out for too long for that.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: The first hour I played I was like "Oh this is kinda neat". I had tried Factorio before and bounced off, my head struggled to focus on learning how to build and managing the RTS aspects at the same time, so I thought maybe the same would happen here. I was wrong, and I've now been sucked in completely.It's pretty to look at, it's satisfying to build in, and in my opinion, way easier to get into than Factorio.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: Very good game for creative people.  Lot's of lee way for building things your own way, whether precisely or in a complete "Gameitout" free for all!   Great for teamwork with friends, or alone.  Enough of a challenge to keep you interested, but  not too bad to keep moving up to bigger and better factories.  And don't forget the people cannons!  Lot's of travel options, but being shot across the map is fun!  So gather up some friends and come play!   Ruue
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: The Games Amazing Scenery. Huge World, And you get enemies to kill and harvest there skins to unlock new stuff. The Technology is very well thought out. You literally have nearly infinite combination or Factories. The factory buildings are very awesome. Satisfactory is Very Worth the cost I would give it a 10 out of 10 for graphics building designs and vehicles and the sheer size of the map Way to go Coffe Stain I love it
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: I might like Satisfactory more than Factorio...Would definitely recommend Satisfactory to folks who have played Factorio, and would suggest Satisfactory as the better entry point into automation games. They have their similarities, but both games do their own thing and scratch different itches for within the overall factory game itch.I suspect most folks don't expect much sentimentality or emotional/funny experiences to happen in factory games, but I have two memories I will forever hold dear from my first Satisfactory co-op game:1. Early in the game, maybe 10 hours in, beholding the belt spaghetti disaster containing unaligned platforms and factories of nonsensical ratios:Me: It's horrible, I love it. What do we call it?Friend: The Misery Engine.2. The end of the game, 100% achievements, 120 hours in, us standing atop a tower to the tip of the skybox, beholding the mess we created upon this world.Sounds silly probably, I could go on and on of memories of just that world. I know there will be many more. A top 10 all time for me.I have much I could say about various elements like building vertically or the combat, or compare the game to Factorio, or ponder design choices, but I think I'll just leave it at I love this game and hope folks give it a shot. Solo or co-op, can't go wrong.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: i rarely write actual reviews, and when i do it is only for games i TRULY enjoy, above average. this is the perfect mix of minecraft, subnautica, and fallout. the sandbox genre of minecraft, the wonder of subnautica and the look of fallout. this game starts off with you constantly struggling for fuel and resources. hours later, you will find yourself optimizing already running factories. why make iron ingots when you could craft it into iron plates and rods? why just have rods when you could also turn half of them into screws? and then why not combine those screws with half the plates, and make reinforced iron plates for the mk II conveyors? its an amazing game that goes from struggle to keep it running, to struggle to keep it efficient, to struggle from restraining yourself from optimizing. oh, and watch the trailer if you're still on the fence.jk this game is just fine
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: I am a 55 year old biker and trucker father, and probably one of the oldest people playing this game. I am a single father to my Son, who is 15 now. My son got this game for from his uncle, so we installed it on his computer and he started playing. By the end of the week he had 12 hours on this game. This was horrible for me, as it was already hard for me to find ways to spend time with my son, as he is always out with his friends or just watching YouTube. So i decided to make a Steam account and get this game to see if I could maybe play alongside him. I loaded into the game and started playing but I was stuck on what you where supposed to do. I asked my Son for help and he let me borrow his controller. Me and my son then played in turns and I loved it as it was the best time I had spent with my Son since my wife had died. This game has ever since brought me and my son closer again and now we actually spend time together outside the house together as well. This game reminded me that there's fun to be had in everything, and it has brought both me and my son many happy memories.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: Satisfactory has been an amazing Sandbox experience where you can really immerse yourself into engineering tasks and manufacturing logistics.With friends, this game is even better.  A 3 player experience is fantastic, but I would recommend 4 if you don't mind getting into arguments over efficiency and workflow.Fantastic game, especially with the free updates and continued support.  Another hit by Coffee Stain studios!

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately I can't recommend this game due to the lack of a blueprint / copy+paste ability.  Without this, later stages of factory building are very tedious since every building and every connection has to be placed manually.  I pushed through it to complete the final milestone, but it was a real slog and I don't have much desire to play again.  The endless mouse clicking saps the fun from factory design. _childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: This is an amazing game, and with the latest update, Update 5, there is no reason to put it off anymore. There's a lot of new buildables, and being able to use the "global grid" you're ensured that you're not setting yourself up for failure later.One tip that has helped me cope with the enormity of this game is building several smaller factories which just produce a certain item on their own. Then with Update 5's new truck system you can now easily route all those produced items anywhere you like.Keep your projects small, and you won't be depressed like me for my first 200 hours...Definitely would highly recommend this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: Oh do I ever recommend this game!!! After watching a few friends employ OCD levels of precision and care to make sure everything is 'just right'... I was curious... but never really tempted to play this game. But... then I discovered Josh from Let's Game it Out... (Thank you, Josh!!! You are a god amongst gamers!!!) I learned that you can have actual fun playing this game. Oh Sooooo muuuuuch funnnnnn!!!! and at the expense of all that exists in the game! Exploitation of nature without all of the annoying protesters getting crushed under the wheels of the truck... whoops, I didn't say that out loud did I? -giggles- Plants, animals, resources to be used as you like. Be efficient or embrace the chaos and mayhem and throw some lunacy into the mix and make a truly horrifying world where you can't figure out where it begins or ends. And you guys at Coffee Stain... please keep up the amazing work!! gawwwwwdz I love this game!!! What can I mess with next????(Oh yes, my world makes a few of my friends weep at the mere sight of the madness that I have wroght)

_childDocuments_.review: Best game I've played in years, if you like puzzle games or sandboxes or industrial manufacturing games this is the creme of the crop. Just unlocked the current update maximum, and am still playing my save file so that I can get ready for the next update, but also so I can make my world more efficient. 10/10 play however you want. Make a spaghetti monster or try to get 100% efficiency. Love it and please keep more coming coffee stain.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: Recent engine update made the game more hardware intensive all around, while actually making the game look WORSE. UE has been trash for the fact that it is a resource hog at all times (lowering settings does very little to increase performance) for most devs that don't recode it in-depth (which is damn near all of them), but this new lighting 'feature' has the worst looking blending. It's like a continually-flushing toilet of chunky lighted pixels on reflecting surfaces, making the game look 'fuzzy' everywhere.So, thanks for making the game not only look worse but also run worse.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: I don't even know where to begin, this game is amazing, no need to wait for the full release, there is a ton of content to play through as is. Don't expect any story or even an in depth campaign, it's more of a sandbox with some overarching goals but chasing those goals is incredibly fun and addictive. While the world is quite large and pretty to look at, the combat and exploration is a bit shallow, however the real meat of this game is in planning and constructing the most efficient mega factories that you can dream up. The building systems seem simple at first but as you unlock more elements to build with the possibilities open up quite a bit, throw in vehicles and all sorts of character equipment like parachutes and jetpacks for some added fun and it's a nearly perfect mix. I've been playing for over 300 hours across both steam and the original release on the epic store and I still find myself daydreaming about it all the time.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: Like Factorio but in first person. Love the graphics, the grind is hard yet rewarding.The map is HUGE! The game has potentially hundreds of hours of entertainment.Love the tech tree(s)Well worth £20.00 big thumbs up.Its one of those games where you advance on the tech tree, then go back and re-do all your hard work so it looks aesthetically pleasing :D
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: I would highly recommend this game if you are into automation and a little bit of exploring. Also, the humour in this game, even if it's only there when you get certain upgrades, is actually pretty good. But no, I definitely give this a 10 out of 10 and would recommend to a friend. _childDocuments_.review: Automation and Factory building games has become my favourite genre. This is by FAR my favourite of them.It has:# Static but beautiful world with many different biomes.# Solid progression systems that allow multiple ways of unlocking new tech, cosmetics and automation recipes. # Friendly community managers that inform players of patches and updates on Youtube.# Large modding/addon community.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy shooting zombies, driving fast cars, leveling up your character, and a deep rich story... this is not the game for you.If you enjoy tedious logistics, math, exploration, and resource gathering... this IS the game for you!Tedious makes it sound un-enjoyable, but the tedium is part of the fun. Constantly adjusting conveyor lines to improve productivity. Calculating efficiency rates to manage faster factory lines. Implementing transportation routes including trains and aerial drones. TONS of unlockable research and new buildings. At 285 hours, my crew and I have finally completed the final phase of the space elevator. Can't wait for update 6!!!Excellent chill game with great multiplayer. Dedicated servers made the online experience so much better!
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: Really good game for people with slightly higher IQ and/or 3d planning skills.I don't have either so its not for me but I wish I could progres past some basic modular frames.It have everything you would wish for - infinite resource nodes, mining, automation, crafting, exploring...It hurts really bad that I'm too dumb to be able to progress and enjoy later stages of the game :(
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: Oh man, this game is heavy. Starting out with trying to understand the mechanics and how things work with each other was a grueling task. Only 50ish hours in at the time of typing this review, however those 50 hours have made me feel like I've aged 20 years. The game itself is fantastic, visual masterpiece which requires lots of troubleshooting and can really wear you down mentally if you care more about the effeceincy side of the game. However, after all the headache and frustration, this game truly does hold up to its name. Its just so... Satisfactory.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: Satisfactory has been an exhilarating journey, with over 300 hours spent meticulously building and automating in anticipation of its upcoming full release on September 10th, 2024. Developed by Coffee Stain Studios, this first-person factory building game immerses players in an alien world ripe for industrialization. Its gameplay, rated at 9/10, seamlessly blends automation and resource management as you crash-land and set up efficient production lines amidst diverse biomes—from lush forests to expansive cave systems. The thrill of exploring and optimizing factories in a dynamic environment is unmatched, with each decision impacting productivity and efficiency. With its stunning world design and engaging gameplay, Satisfactory promises to deliver even more excitement and depth upon its full release, making it a must-play for fans of intricate strategy and creative engineering.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: Short version: This game is more addictive than heroin.Long version: This game is huge in every way. The map is unfathomably large, and even after 700 hours in my current world I have only unlocked about 2/5 of the map. The size of the factorys you can build is absolutely insane, and all of them can be different. This game perfectly meshes together the FPS, Open world, and factory management genre. Your factory always has a way to improve, look better, or be more efficient. It also does what middle school me thought was impossible, make math fun. I legitimately enjoy doing math to make sure my factory is running at full capacity. And even if you manage to complete most of the fun things in the base game, which is basically impossible due to how much there is, the modding community is huge and adds so much to the game. Along with this, the game is still in early access, so it is always getting new fun ways to expand what to automate. Oh, and one last thing, it has a multiplayer. Even though it is a little buggy, it is one of the most amazing games I have ever played. Would recommend, but once more a warning that this game should be regulated like a drug due to how addictive it is.Story: 5/10Gameplay: 10/10Multiplayer: 9/10Community: 8.5/10Personal Impact: 7/10Open World: 9.5/10Level Design: N/AAesthetic/Art Style: 9/10Consistent Bug Fixes: 10/10Major Gameplay Updates: 10/10Overall: 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: This is an incredible, beautiful, addictive game that will have you enjoying it for countless hours!  It is like Minecraft meets Subnautica and I absolutely LOVE it!  There is a massive world to explore and build in.  Satisfactory shows what a passionate developer studio can really do.  This is the perfect game to chill to as you listen to music or a podcast.  I HIGHLY recommend it!!!  It's worth every penny!  Now excuse me as I get back to building my gigantic aluminum plant :)

I would recommend anyone who has the money and the determination to GET THIS GAME.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game in alpha version and I no one regret it. I think this game one of the best games, in which I played for all time. So interesting and unique gameplay, incredible graphic, excited soundtracs and a lot of other. Gameplay in this game on 150+ hours. It's something special for singleplayer game. "Feeling of progress". Games about base bilding and autimation must ensure "feeling of progress". And satisfactory copes with this so good, progress felt on early-game to end-game. Actually I think Satisfactory is the best game with "feeling of progress".Open world. Satisfactory this game with one of the largest open world in game industry. This world truly excited explore. A lot of locations, so many bioms, and a big quantity mobs. Incredible graphic. Game was made in Unreal Engine 5, in consequence of which graphic is so amazing. It's something Incredible for not AAA project.Soundtracs. Ofc it's not Death stranding or Omori, but also amazing musical accompaniment, that complement the gameplay nicely. _childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: To sum it up: Efficiency is the name of the game. Honestly, I absolutely love the amount of detail this game has. It does take a bit of getting used to, but as you progress through the game, from simple machines to using coal and nuclear power, there's so much depth to the game. Research, finding the best "spot" to build your base(only to realize there's another area which has significantly better resource nodes nearby/close to a good body of water), seeing what kind of nodes spawn and looking for resources to make bigger and better complex items is honestly a blast. There's really no wrong way to play the game, and while at times it can be a bit tedious and difficult(figuring out exactly which biomass burner ran out of biomass), I'd strongly recommend giving it a try.

The game does have math to it like seeing how much a Mk . 3 miner puts out in a smelter , also the game is mainly based around building factories and power plants which are some of things I like

The animals that attack you have a very basic AI which is far too easy to predict and counter and you only need to obtain the next weapon up to become practically invincible, you don't even need the rifle.Sorry, but at this stage in time, it needs a LOT of work to make it worth playing in my view.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not any better than any other factory game... actually its a lot worse. I highly recommend you save your money to get another game. And i really wish i didn't have to say this. its just that satisfactory suffers from little to no quality of life features. And the progression in game is slow... very slow, simply because its super finicky and nearly impossible to build anything that feels worthwhile in the game. It also has 0 incentive to progress because there is no real danger/driving force, no quota no enemy to attack my base, no feeling of accomplishment, no nothing. There's barley any reward complex. It just feels like a constant grind to play this game, and it could easily be solved if they just made it easier to build and expand as well as adding more quality of life features. Specifically, I feel the blueprint system does nothing to ease mass production which is the whole point of a factory game, but it's also unlocked super late in the game. There are no bots to help you build things out of reach or that are simply too large, and the games closest compensation is simply allowing you to make less machines by overclocking them, just trash. Belts are also very glitchy and feel impossible to line up even with grid snap, so forget about modular systems. Additionally they don't connect sometimes and have a very very strict cap on the angle. In conclusion, its amazing to me that i was able to put more than 20 hours into this game without throwing up. 0/10
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: This game strives to be like a 3D Factorio, but falls short because there is no opposition.Some people enjoy these factory games without any sort of enemy to fight against, but I don't as much. I enjoy games like Factorio, Creeper World, etc. because you are building with a purpose. In Satisfactory, you build... just so you can build more. It sadly reminds me of Starfield's disappointing outpost system, in the sense that you certainly CAN make a nice base, but WHY?In games like these I enjoy the incremental feeling of pushing against some boundary, some enemy, who can surprise you and test you. The only enemies in Satisfactory are just some animals that stay in one spot and you can completely ignore them.Despite this, I still enjoy the game a lot. I'm hoping to "complete" it by finishing up the achievements, but I think I'm done after that. Some games continue to challenge you by ramping up the opposition against you. _childDocuments_.review: "Satisfactory" is a masterclass in engineering fantasy, a game that is nothing short of a digital wonderland for the creatively inclined. It's the quintessential lose-yourself kind of experience—relaxing yet addicting, with layers of depth that make it as intricate as it is engaging. The game's core premise is simple: build and automate. Yet, within this simplicity lies a complex ballet of production lines, efficiency optimization, and exploration that can consume countless hours without ever feeling like a grind.The world of "Satisfactory" is a breathtaking alien landscape, ripe for exploitation and exploration. It's a canvas where your industrial dreams take shape amidst the verdant flora and fauna of an uncharted planet. The sense of scale is immense, and the satisfaction derived from constructing a well-oiled machine of industry across this vast terrain is unparalleled. As you progress, the initial tranquility of manually mining and crafting gives way to the hypnotic hum of conveyor belts and the rhythmic dance of robotic arms—all harmonizing in a symphony of progress.The game's visual and auditory feedback is a cut above, with every machine and structure offering a satisfying sense of physicality and purpose. The attention to detail is meticulous, from the way resources flow down production lines to the realistic day-night cycle that bathes your factory in the golden hues of dawn or the cool shadows of dusk.Mod support is nothing short of amazing, breathing new life into the game with each community-created addition. Mods range from quality-of-life improvements to complete gameplay overhauls, ensuring that "Satisfactory" remains endlessly replayable. The developers have fostered a symbiotic relationship with the modding community, resulting in a game that evolves in exciting and unexpected ways.But it's not just the game itself that's impressive—it's the dev team's commitment to their community. Their transparent communication, regular updates, and genuine passion for their creation shine through in every aspect. They listen, they respond, and they deliver, making "Satisfactory" not just a product but a growing experience shaped by its players.In conclusion, "Satisfactory" is a game that offers a unique blend of relaxation and complexity, a sandbox of industrial possibilities that can capture the imagination for hours on end. Whether you're a solo player orchestrating a private empire of machines or teaming up with friends to tackle logistical challenges, this game stands as a remarkable achievement in the world of sandbox simulators. It's a testament to the genre and a beacon for future titles to aspire to. "Satisfactory" is, in every sense, a truly satisfying endeavor.

_childDocuments_.review: 7/10PROS:Whoever said work's not supposed to be fun clearly never played Satisfactory.  There's just something about how everything flows together that makes the game absolutely addicting!  The pacing of the milestones, the way the game constantly has more work for you to do, and even the freedom of exploration that comes with having such a massive area to work with.  So long as you’re willing to put in a bit of effort to find something to work on, Satisfactory will never leave you without things to do. The game is visually gorgeous, everything from the simplest stone to the tallest of buildings is breathtaking, and I will never get tired of watching buildings get constructed.  The fact that you can follow your resources along conveyor belts, watching them go from ore, to ingots, to products is also a simple yet incredibly satisfying process.  Everything you find while exploring will look wonderfully alien, yet not so out of the ordinary that you can’t figure out at a glance what it’s use is.  Wood, plants, ore, and everything in between are visually clear, so there wont be any times when you pick something up and are left totally clueless as to what it’s for.While the music isn’t always present, and feels more like the occasional jingle than a full blown soundtrack, I have to admit it’s spot on.  Coffee Stain has always had a real knack for immersive music, and I’m happy to say that Satisfactory continues that trend!  Aside from the songs the sounds are also great.  Hitting rocks, slugging it out with monsters, and even the simple process of picking up leaves off the ground, and of course pretty much every building in the game makes noise to some extent, and they all sound wonderfully accurate and believable!CONS:This game is still in early access, you will find bugs, some funny, some harmful. Nothing has ruined my experience as of yet, but that doesn’t change the fact that they do exist.Not much goes on within the game outside of your primary objectives.  If you have downtime while waiting on a resource to be constructed, you’re encouraged to take the time to explore the planet, yet outside of the occasional monster encounter, or (positively gorgeous) vista find not much else goes on.  Exploration for the sake of exploration is enough to keep me occupied in a game like this, but for some there’s a possibility you’ll be left with some ‘No Man’s Sky’ vibes.  From a gameplay balance perspective, I find myself genuinely surprised about how little concrete I need.  I almost always flood the resource in abundance even when only mining Limestone from a single source.  I know it’s an odd complaint, but I would like to see either more builds that require it, or perhaps up the quantity required for already established builds.  Lastly the game drills the concept of automation into your head to an almost ludicrous degree.  I understand that is more or less the core concept of the game, but I’m a man who likes to tinker and work with my hands.  I enjoy creating things myself, yet the sluggish workbench crafting speeds, as well as the game’s own jargon, really make me feel scummy when I do something myself rather than leaving it to my machines.  At the risk of sounding like I don’t understand the game at all, I would like to see some more options for the “hands-on” fic-sit employee.  Perhaps some M.A.M research options that would allow you to speed up personal crafting or something along those lines…CONCLUSION:This is a building man’s sandbox.  There’s plenty to do, lot’s to see, and no shortage of content for those willing to hunt for it.  In short: If you’re the kind of person who plays games like Minecraft and Terraria because you like to build, then this is a game I know you will enjoy!

_childDocuments_.review: This game probably just became my favorite game that I'll keep playing for as long as I can. However, there are a few things you should know about before getting into it.This game requires a massive time investment. You will constantly be building, managing and rebuilding your factories. Mostly, due to the fact that a lot of cosmetic options are not available from the start and you have to unlock them through an in game mechanic of sending items you produce into a machine called AWESOME Sink. The more items you send in, the more points you will earn. Once you reach a certain amount of points, you get a ticket that you can print and spend in the shop. Doesnt sound too bad considering you will most likely be busy doing something else while your factories are sinking items, but each ticket requires more and more points to be earned. As such, only now, after almost 200h, I finally unlocked everything in the shop and thats considering I got a bunch of tickets for free from the advent calendar, which is a time limited event for christmas. And on top of that, even if you did have everything unlocked from the get go, you wouldnt be able to build it anyway, as a lot of it requires new materials that you might not know how to craft yet. Another reason you will be spending a ton of time building is the fact that there are alternative recipes in the game, some of which allow you to significantly reduce the amount of machines necessary to produce the same/more amount of items that you could before. But these recipes have to be unlocked via items called hard drives, that you have to find on the map, and on top of that you are limited to recipes appropriate for your current progress tier. That means that if you are unlucky and dont get useful recipes early on, then you will have to spend a lot of time just exploring the map looking for more drives. Of course, all of that can simply be ignored and you will be just fine playing through the game without any of the shop items or alternate recipes, but your factories wont look nearly as nice as they could and definitely not as compact/efficient. So if you are someone who doesnt have a ton of free time, then I dont think this game is for you.Other than that the game is amazing, it looks great and runs alright. Although, on weaker pcs you should definitely spread out your factories and try to make them as compact as possible, otherwise you will be lagging a lot. The game is easy enough to get into, but manages to keep you entertained all the way through as you build more and more complex factories that require some careful planning. LPT: start building on the world grid right away (hold ctrl when building), will save you a lot of trouble.As a side note, the devs seem to be a bunch of really fun people who put a lot of love and care into their game.10/10 I wish there were more games like this one.

_childDocuments_.review: If you’ve ever dreamed of being a mad scientist with a penchant for conveyor belts and industrial chaos, then Satisfactory is your dream come true. This game is like Minecraft and Factorio had a baby, and that baby grew up to be an overachieving factory manager with a caffeine addiction.From the moment you land on the alien planet, you’re greeted by a world that’s both beautiful and terrifying. The local wildlife might try to eat you, but who has time to worry about that when there are iron nodes to mine and factories to build? Your mission, should you choose to accept it, is to turn this pristine wilderness into a sprawling industrial nightmare. And let me tell you, it’s the most fun you’ll ever have ruining an ecosystem.The game’s name is a bit of an understatement. “Satisfactory”? More like “Industrial Insanity: Build, Break, Repeat!”.You’ll start with a simple goal: build a small factory. Fast forward 50 hours, and you’re knee-deep in a spaghetti mess of conveyor belts, pipelines, and hyper tubes that would make any OSHA inspector faint. But hey, who needs safety regulations when you’ve got efficiency?The real magic of Satisfactory is in its ability to make you feel like a genius. You’ll spend hours optimizing your production lines, only to realize you’ve created a monster that even Frankenstein would envy. And just when you think you’ve mastered the game, it throws a curveball at you—like nuclear power. Because nothing says “fun” like handling radioactive materials in your backyard.Multiplayer mode is where the chaos truly shines. Team up with friends and watch as your carefully planned factory descends into hilarious pandemonium. There’s nothing quite like the joy of accidentally launching your buddy into space with a poorly placed jump pad.In conclusion, Satisfactory is a game that’s anything but. It’s a delightful blend of creativity, strategy, and sheer madness. Whether you’re a seasoned factory builder or a newbie looking for a new obsession, this game will keep you entertained for hours on end. Just remember to take breaks, or you might find yourself dreaming in conveyor belts

_childDocuments_.review: Satisfactory is an open-world factory building sandbox in Early access which, practically, the current end goal is to accomplish full automation, at least that’s my goal. From the get-go, you’re basically free to play the game however you want, of course following physics and things like that. Within my first 3 days, I’ve exceeded over 30 hours and play it constantly and I haven’t even accomplished half way through what I can unlock, build and craft making the game continuously packed with fun and enjoyable content. Coming from someone who has never enjoyed factory builders and has no sense of automation, the game offers amazing and  building, exploration and combat as well as amazing visuals. Therefore I highly recommend this game to open-world enthusiasts and builders alike. You start with creating the world. At the time of this review, the game currently offers 4 maps for different preferences of difficulty and your own experience. The map I recommend for you to first start on is a large, open map with large flat fields, many choices for base locations and multiple mining spots for different ores. This is the only map I have played, as I’m on my first playthrough, but I  recommend this if you’ve never played satisfactory, seen gameplay or even touched a factory game. After setting that all up, you can decide between the tutorial and starting straight off the bat. I highly recommend the tutorial,  the tutorial can take up to at least over an hour (though it is useful), therefore you can either play through the guide or watch a beginner’s guide youtube video. There are plenty out there to choose from.Now to the actual gameplay. Satisfactory, as in the name, is a factory building game. It is set in a large open-world environment with hours of exploration available and the game offers smooth and well-executed mechanics. In my 30 hours experience, I’m a really big fan of the building aspect. The building, construction and the satisfaction of crafting your first ever automation line (even just for iron ingots) is just… unexplainable. Anytime I’ve built a new machine and it worked, I just punched the air. Just the accomplishment of creating a new automation line gets me craving to build another… then another… until I look at the time and see I’ve been playing for hours (thank you lockdown). Satisfactory provides a nice and smooth learning curve to gradually introduce you to new and advanced ways of playing the game. For example, it introduces you to biomass burners for powering the factory (basically just burning wood and leaves), and eventually later on, introduces you to a new and complex energy source (coal and water). In the end, this game is very noob friendly and it doesn’t take a course in engineering to figure stuff out. Most of it comes down to common sense. Overall, the gameplay is amazing and immersive and keeps me entertained for hours at a time. The game is very polished and smooth and I’m in love with it. I have a prediction it’ll be 100+ hours until I’m tired and done of this game. This game offers the most smoothest performance I have ever encountered from an Early Access game. I’ve only had framerate issues in my friend’s factory which had over 1000+ buildings and platforms so obviously it’s a very CPU intensive games like most building games are. I’ve barely ran into any bugs and the visuals are very stunning even on low-medium so I highly recommend this as long as you have a strong CPU.

Certain things seem to have been deliberatly made more casual (like e.g. the almost non existing clipping for belts) in favor of gameplay.Any "story"-related dialogue, the few lines that are there, are well delivered and quite funny.The world is maybe my absolute favorite among this type of games.
