_childDocuments_.review: Update: So, as a final version, the game is great and very addictive. The possibilities are endless. The only problem i have with the game, is the complete lack of resource management/panel that describes how much resource you are using and how much you are producing for any particular task. Apart from manual inspecting each production unit to see how much of that resource is using and compute how much you need overall for the end product, there is no other way of knowing what and how much you need for a certain end product. In the beginning, this is doable, but later on, if you want to optimize your production, this is very time consuming. Something like the power graph but for resources would be very nice. Hopefully we will get something like that in the future. Until the, The Sink is your best option to resolve overproduction or overmining.After 5 years in early access, taking into account the game was good from the start, ATM the game feels like live service than anything else. There are basic stuff that are not implemented nor considered, like management panel for multiple factories and such, the artifacts are still to this day WIP and i'm tired of waiting. By the time this game is out 1.0, most of the ppl will be done with it and have moved on. The game is good and all, but you will hit a wall in the late game where you do more micromanagement by running back and forth than actual building, because there is no management option, like to be able to see if your factory is working well other that inspect every machine to see if it's supplied well etc. PS Will change my review if it's worth it in the future when the game is finished. _childDocuments_.review: This game is a mixed bag of good and badAs of right now do I think its good. NoLets start with the good- Incredibly fun to get stuff balanced on belts and watch things craft. - Some of the best animations to go with it for each thing early game to get through-humor and love poured into various systems like the ficsit game in the hub. And various jokes aroundThe bad (Sorry im not a professional reviewer)- Late game is very very poorly balancedLets expand on thisI am not saying with a big enough factory and with enough time things wont craft. Because they will. But if you want to truly optimize / get things crafting at a fun and steady rate its borderline impossible.You have to create so many foundrys / constructors / manufacturers / things. Blueprints would make this easier but they have them so limited that you cant even really fit in the end game buildings (Im looking at you quantum encoder.And sure you can clip and glitch the game to get it to fit. But is that intended???Also like people seem to hate comparing this to factorio but like its the same genre and this game is heavily inspired by it so if this offends you :PFactorios blueprint / copy and paste your factory system works much much much better for expanding factorys to the sizes they are asking for late game.Also like no bots or anything to build ur inventory sucks but ITs fine when you consider sloops / mercer spheres  Its not great but its much much better.Let alone the Fluid systems. No priority switches. No good way to pump it. Only mk2 for late game. So all of the problems with fluid stays late game. And then they expand it by expecting you to use it more and more and more. It just really shows all the flaws with the fluid late game to the point it just doesnt feel fun to work with . Now the other issueLAGI have a 4070 / Ryzen 9 I am not low end pc. And with the mass building thats late game it lags soooo bad.We even switched it to a deticated server and the lag got better for awhile. But eventually the mass of buildings required to do some stuff late game just creates a laggier and laggier game. Its not fun to deal with. We were gonna try to 100% automate everything but the lag got so bad we rushed the ending. This is not fun or satisfying in this matter. And it just ruins all the build up and fun of automatingAnd the reward for all of this is a small cutscene that the story has basically explained to you if you have been collecting sloops etc long before you even see it. Which whatever the story doesnt matter automaton game. But like when the automation doesnt feel good that is just a cherry on top of a bad game. Will totally change my review if they fix lag / endgame balancing / add better blueprint systems. first person factory automation game comparable comment). power management is very tedious at times but its still quite rewarding mass automating is nearly ever-ending in this game with over 90+ fully automate-able items and growing(each requiring up to 4 items/raw ores) it gets very complicated quick also with over 80+ alternate recipes to unlock via scattered and hidden hard-drives there is many ways to 'skin this cat'. the games build area is about 46 km2 so don't worry that's enough room to just build it out if you want. the game is simply beautiful the entire world is hand made the quality _childDocuments_.review: I played Satisfactory on Epic for 40 hours.Games like this rarely keep me entertained for too long, but Satisfactory manages to keep everything fun by being complex, while at the same time making everything easy to do.The game's goal is to just keep building and upgrading.You start off with a measly structure, and throughout the game, build and design your very own Factory. You really feel accomplished as you see your plans come to life.You start by scanning for materials. Once you've done that, you mine them, smelt, all the typical stuff that you'd expect in games of this genre.However, the fun part comes from automating everything. You can easily connect machines to each other via conveyor belts, and you can really be quite creative by making them cross each other, stack them, loop them around or attach to walls.Eventually you start doing more complex things, like building machines that assemble different parts in order to make something else, or even program trucks to automatically transfer goods from far away. There's something so cool about seeing it all just work after all your tinkering. While doing all this you need to manage your power. Making sure not to overwork your system, while supplying enough fuel to your generators. Don't worry there's nothing that tries to screw with your buildings like in Factorio. No monsters or pollution to worry about, just building.Throughout my playthrough, I had a few cool stories to tell of how I planned ahead and finished a big project. Games like Factorio also do this well, but the 3D perspective Satisfactory brings obviously allows you to play around a lot more. There are multiple biomes to choose from.The worlds you can explore are really beautiful, and interesting. Which is helped by being populated by many interesting looking creatures.Overall I'm in love with the game, and was anxiously waiting for its release on Steam, since the Epic version I played last year had limited content. I've heard its grown a lot since then, and will update my review when I get around to playing it here! Still, even what I played back then was amazing, and I highly recommend the game!

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely *satisfying* factory builder in the same genre as Factorio / Dyson Sphere Program, but with more of a focus on combat, exploration, and detailed management. Also in 3D, with rewarding and fun movement mechanics and combat options. Provides a unique cycle of exploration (finding very valuable resources on the map, fighting, and discovering new types of resources) and exploitation (utilizing resources efficiently, building infrastructure, managing power, and researching new technologies) not common in the factory builder genre. It is a slow burn, and requires significant effort to design efficient factories, but it is very rewarding when you get to the other side and everything runs perfectly. You will not get to the same level of automation and copy/pasting designs as Factorio / DSP, but I think that these constraints improve the experience. You ALWAYS have to be in the weeds of production lines, manually connecting belts and calculating ratios. Your life is also ALWAYS threatened by combat, with zero combat automation - Satisfactory is also an enjoyable and sometimes difficult FPS. However, combat happens on your own terms in Satisfactory, so you do not need to worry about being ambushed - you should know by exploring what you are getting yourself into. Also, the lack of infrastructure / factory damage by alien threats further reinforces the fact that only your life, your exploration progress, and what you have in your pockets is at stake, which is not as punishing as other factory builders. There are also many viable power sources, so there's also some flexibility in how you want to customize your experience. You can easily get lost designing gorgeous factories, or you can give into the belt spaghetti. With the official release, they addressed the final major rough patches and added significant content, demonstrating one of THE MOST successful early-access releases to-date. I think Satisfactory can finally take its place next to Factorio and Dyson Sphere Program as one of my new top factory builders, and with fully online multiplayer, low stakes, fun automation, a strong feeling of progression, an expansive map (that I have only half explored with nearly 150 hours in the game), and so, so much more, I think Satisfactory is the easiest 10/10 I have ever given.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: stunning graphics and light representations with new game engine with your good hardware. - a lot of time to sink in this game - you are not forced at all to to something . if you want to speed-run game through all content - you are welcome ! if you want to spend 50 hours staring at a machine working  - you are welcome ! - it encourages you to be creative. - repeatability & VERSATILITY! cons: - resource-intensive , what this game can show you with good hardware , you will spend $$$ to be able to see those graphics.- on experimental / early acces and all instability and small bugs that it comes with.- sometimes being solo you can get easily bored if not knowing how to entertain yourself using what game has to offer. conclusion: this game saved my in some way. story time : 2 very close friends and a game .Imagine a young engineer going through hard times in both life and work. The engineer's first friend introduced them to a game that captivated them immensely. The engineer became so engrossed in the game that they began creating elaborate schemes and plans for factories, meticulously automating every intricate detail.One day, while showcasing their magnificent and flawless factories to the engineer's second friend, the engineer couldn't help but vent about their dissatisfaction with life and work. The second friend posed a thought-provoking question: "Why don't you apply the same level of research, planning, and perfection to the way you think and act, and strive for satisfaction in your own life?"Prompted by this question, the engineer embarked on a journey to find satisfaction in their life. As a result, they eventually gained the opportunity to lead a real factory. This game, in a way, saved the engineer and secured a better future for both them and their family.I want to express my gratitude to the team behind the game for their tremendous effort! If any member of the team happens to read this, please know that you are an inspiration to someone. Keep up the fantastic work!

I don't want to start over on a new map to continue enjoying the game, I guess, I want to leverage my base-building investment and go adventure.I also wish there was more of a combat/aggression element (as-is, the guns are pretty useless, you will ultimately just hover around using power poles until you get bored, avoiding combat most of the time.) Here’s a positive review of Satisfactory:Satisfactory is an absolute gem for fans of resource management, factory building, and open-world exploration. From the moment you set foot on the vast, beautifully crafted alien planet, you’re met with endless possibilities. The game blends the satisfaction of automation with the thrill of exploration, creating a perfect balance between strategy and creativity.The visuals are stunning, with a vibrant, detailed world that feels both lush and industrial. Whether you’re building sprawling conveyor belt systems or climbing mountains to scout for new resources, the world feels alive and inviting. The game’s environment design is top-notch, offering biomes that each feel unique and challenging in their own ways.What really sets Satisfactory apart is its depth. The progression system is incredibly rewarding, as each upgrade or new technology unlocks fresh opportunities to optimize your factory. For those who love problem-solving, the intricacies of managing power, logistics, and production chains are deeply satisfying.Multiplayer adds a whole new dimension, allowing you to collaborate with friends to create even more ambitious projects. _childDocuments_.review: Satisfactory, developed by Coffee Stain Studios, is a captivating first-person factory building game set on an alien world. It offers players a unique blend of resource management, automation, and exploration in a vast, visually striking environment.The game's core strength lies in its immersive 3D presentation, which brings the factory building experience to life in a way that 2D counterparts can't match. Players start with manual resource gathering and simple crafting, gradually progressing to complex, sprawling production lines that span the landscape. This sense of progression is deeply satisfying, as your initially humble outpost evolves into a massive industrial complex.Satisfactory's alien world is a character in itself, featuring diverse biomes ranging from lush forests to barren deserts. Exploring this beautiful, sometimes hostile environment adds an element of adventure to the industrial focus. The ability to play cooperatively with friends further enhances the experience, allowing players to tackle ambitious projects together.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like building games with a lot of freedom and no Hunger/Thirst then you will probably enjoy this. You can go at your own pace. I often found myself logging in during EA to "Just do a bit" and then a couple of hours would pass of happy building.If you like games where you can build enormous factories with almost limitless resources then you will almost certainly enjoy this. The only in-game resource needed is your time, If you are happy to bounce around exploring with the various transport methods available (and there are quite a few) over some beautiful and completely destructible flora and fauna, all while your small factory churns out your components to get you to the next tier, then go for it! If you want to spend your time building a 10 floor Megafactory that sucks in a world full of resources by Drone/Conveyor/Train and Truck, then you go for that as well! Its one of those rare games where you get out what you put in, but with a little extra. I've never regretted time spent in this game, including when I've logged in to just mess around on my Jelly Bounce pads for 30 minutes.If you like games with the above but with the added freedom to build a massive people cannon that will shoot you across the map in seconds then you will definitely enjoy this.If, like me, you are one of those people that yearn for optimisation and efficiency in your factory games and absolutely love when a game developer heavily leans into that, then... say good bye to your friends or even better, see if they want to join, take time off work if possible, get yourself a fresh notepad and get Satisfactory.  Worthy of mention, Coffee Stain Studios has listened and engaged with the community with an openness that is becoming quite rare in modern game development.Summary : I've more than had my moneys worth, If any of the above things seem up your street, then I hope you will as well.

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly wasn't expecting to like this game this much. If you like the creation part of Subnautica, you'll like this. It has a very good tutorial. _childDocuments_.review: This game has that sort of gear progression similar to minecraft, where your character doesn't actually get any better at anything(aside from inventory upgrades & hotbar expansions), but you get better at building and managing things.Definitely a game worth playing, since I can't get an experience like this anywhere else, except maybe factorio but that game is 2D and I've never played it(a sin, I know).Absolutely love that there is always something to do, even when progressing to the next phase, you can research things and unlock maybe not as big, but extremely useful things like the smart splitter or the GUN.Seeing some of the community works is also very inspirational, and super cool to look at some of the stuff people have made, similar, again, to minecraft. Not something the devs forced or actually made, but allowed and gave enough players the tools to make something really interesting and cool, reminds me of Valve.I also adore the amount of thinking that needs to be done, and the fact that sometimes you just do not have the space for a conveyor or a certain machine. Makes you rethink and remake entire factories for efficiency and easy movement.Overall this game is super fun and addicting, with a special kind of combination of originality, good development, and inspiration, really makes this game pop and stand out, reminds me of when games used to be like this more often then not.

It will certainly subject human beings to greater indignities and inflict greater damage on the natural world, it will probably lead to greater social disruption and psychological suffering, and it may lead to increased physical suffering even in “advanced” countries.2. The industrial-technological system may survive or it may break down. If it survives, it MAY eventually achieve a low level of physical and psychological suffering, but only after passing through a long and very painful period of adjustment and only at the cost of permanently reducing human beings and many other living organisms to engineered products and mere cogs in the social machine. Furthermore, if the system survives, the consequences will be inevitable: There is no way of reforming or modifying the system so as to prevent it from depriving people of dignity and autonomy.3. If the system breaks down the consequences will still be very painful. But the bigger the system grows the more disastrous the results of its breakdown will be, so if it is to break down it had best break down sooner rather than later.4. We therefore advocate a revolution against the industrial system. This revolution may or may not make use of violence; it may be sudden or it may be a relatively gradual process spanning a few decades. We can’t predict any of that. But we do outline in a very general way the measures that those who hate the industrial system should take in order to prepare the way for a revolution against that form of society. This is not to be a POLITICAL revolution. Its object will be to overthrow not governments but the economic and technological basis of the present society.5. In this article we give attention to only some of the negative developments that have grown out of the industrial-technological system. Other such developments we mention only briefly or ignore altogether. This does not mean that we regard these other developments as unimportant. For practical reasons we have to confine our discussion to areas that have received insufficient public attention or in which we have something new to say. For example, since there are well-developed environmental and wilderness movements, we have written very little about environmental degradation or the destruction of wild nature, even though we consider these to be highly important.So 10/10 bombs by mail
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: When I first reviewed this game I recommended that people didn't get it - but I am revising this recommendation with smallish caveats. I think everyone needs to remember that this game is not Factorio and we shouldn't expect the devs to make it in the likeness of Factorio. (I am a player of that game with, currently, more than 2000 hours...). I apologise for my previous snotty review.First though - I am running this Windows game on an Ubuntu 18.04 (Linux) system (AMD FX6300 + 16GB RAM + 4GB nVidia 1050ti) using Steam Play.It is beautiful - it looks and sounds good [even without the music that sounds a bit like Astroneer].  The beauty is the first thing that strikes you when you walk out of your lander at the beginning. The devs have quite clearly put a lot of effort into making things realistic but other worldly at the same time. The creatures and plants  they have populated this world with are wonderful - but some of them are just too vicious - more about that later too.  The buildings you put in place to make your factory are likewise gorgeous. It would be nice if there was a better way of lining them up when building for the perfectionists amongst us - but I am only at the start of the game so perhaps I will unlock something... or work out how to do it - but so far no luck in that... The recipes you construct have seemed,  up till now, very sensibly worked out. Now for the bits I am not so happy about.At first I was having trouble getting an online session  which created issues with my saved sessions when I kept coming back as a different character after reloading or respawning. I created an Epic account and plugged away at getting on line - it turned  out my default browser was blocking access to Epic and hiding behind my full screen game window - once this was sorted I got online with a player name and now even offline sessions seem to work as they should. Some of the critters are totally vicious, worse than biters in Factorio because they begin immediately you start and come thick and fast. If you don't regain your health you will die. If you haven't got the initial building built you're stuffed because your respawned character shows up on the map somewhere random and you don't know where the zombie is and so you lose the material for the first building - it's just best to start a new game.Other players (and me) are begging the devs for a way to tone this down or turn it off. Obviously some people do like it, that's fine - but I don't like killing even on a computer and  I just want to explore the wonderful world the devs have created and build factories using their amaziing machines.  So buy this game - and if you get a base started (which I didn't for a number of starts because I am just not very good at fighting - but I having to get better) you stand a chance of getting further - but be prepared to fight. I think the game's absolutely worth it - I am now over 70 hours in and haven't played a session of Factorio since I bought Satisfactory... Ooops
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: Reading comments about people disassembling their factories, bah, amateurs. I just reroute the power and ore belts to a new factory and "start over". Ain't nobody got time for the undo button. Currently on my third factory on the same save and the spaghetti belts remain.Abandonfactory is easily my favorite game right now. I can't remember the last time I've spent over 50 hours a week on a single game.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: First Person, HD, Factorio.  No base defense or tons of enemies that constantly attack but there is some combat and exploration.  Robust building system allows you to pretty much whatever you want wherever you want.  Also there is a modding community.  If you enjoyed Factorio or similar games you'll like this too.  (A note for Factorio players: one big difference between this and Factorio is that this game the "fields" of minerals do not run out, but you'll still find yourself expanding a ton.  All the modes of transport can and will be needed/used: belts, vehicles (can automate vehicles with an autopilot, really cool imo), trains.  This is a game I can recommend, even if it's not on sale.  $40 bucks is more than reasonable for what you get.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: Nothing quite compares to the joy of strapping 107 nukes to my friend and sending him straight into orbit. Truly an amazing experience.Besides that "little incident", we built an underground railway system because why not, right? Most the conveyors? Hidden. Underground. Out of sight, out of mind (and danger of more accidental nuclear incidents).We used most of our last resource to print coupons, and now it’s the only currency allowed in our base. No coupons? No access. We went full couponocracy all for the golden nut statue.Honestly, this game is peak chaos engineering. Highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: I did not expect to be so hooked by this game.I'm an engineer. I like to build stuff and make it efficient.You start the game for the first time with the mindset of "ok, lets play the tutorial".I could not stop. This short reinforcing feedback loop is so damn addictive.If you are currently confined to your flat required to fast-forward your time... (2020) this game is for you.It is also for you if you care less about character progression and multiplayer than just building stuff without pressure.This is all about creativity.I came from deep rock galactic and i have the impression coffee stain stands for high quality gameplay oriented games.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great.   You probably already know if you would like this game or not, and I don't expect to change anyone's mind.  I will say some of the little things are what made this game work for me.  Resource nodes never run out.  It is easy to unmake something and doing so gives you back everything you used to make it.  There is no real punishment in this game, no fail state, and for me that worked.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: It's fun.  It's still early access and I think it has a lot of potential. So far, so good. I like world builders so this right up my alley. Also exploration and invention. It's not perfect but what early access title is? They have a feedback channel and I have one or two suggestions...we'll see. So far, I dig it. My main computer is undergoing an upgrade right now and the machine I'm playing on kinda sucks(slow, meh graphics, etc.). Fine for the Internet or whatever but when I get the main machine screwed back together, this game is gonna be a lot more fun!So if you like to world-build, explore, progressive advancement and especially conveyor belts, check this out. Good stuff.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: I'm so happy to see this game grow so fast and see how the devs work so closely with the community, listening to feedback and keeping the entire community up to date on all WIP updates and new ideas. The game has come a really long way since I first picked it up, it was lacking content and had a reasonable few bugs especially in multiplayer.I'm glad to say this game now has hundreds of hours of content and ever evolving challenges with each new unlocked technology tier. Bugs are few and far between and only seem to be present in very high intensity co-op worlds.All in all, I thoroughly recommend the game to anyone interested in min-maxing and high efficiency game play, or even just as a casual game to play in spare time almost completely stress free.Great job coffee stain :)
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: Addictive, and Satisfactory. Watching your tiny shack grow into a blossoming hub of industry producing all kinds of odds and ends is a task that takes many hours and is something of a commitment, it takes a little bit of math, a whole lot of strategy, and a little bit of deforestation to really get your factory on its feet.You must manage power, machines, rail lines, drones, truck transport routes, build a factory floor, manage equipment, and build a space elevator to progress, it is a task that can only be undertook with a heart for math, organizing, and planning.Satisfactory is game I love deeply and cannot stop coming back to, it keeps pulling me in with all its conveyors and building, and its massive map, the SCALE is unbelievable there is so much to do, if you like the idea of simple strategy, with a little math and combat, and a big commitment to production quotas this game is 100% for. also don't just take it from me this game is overwhelmingly positive on steam right now, its clearly a great game, with a great price, and you will probably love it.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: This game is quite the experience. A masterpiece of a game that has been an obvious product of love to it's players. It is and has been worth every hour you will spend in the game whether that is by yourself or with your friends. I have played games for 35+ years and there is a handful of games that have been good enough that long after it's days I will remember and have fond memories of playing and this is one of them.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: Finally 1.0 and... ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.. I was never this happy to see stairs (matching other foundations)! Every major update added so much stuff and they did it again for 1.0..If you love working endless hours without sleep for a ...wonderful, cosy .. company in your own build factories to exploit a planet's resources, FICSIT Inc. is what you need and this is your game!One of the absolute best factory games out there. Building in this game is like meditation and the automation... the game lives up to it's name. Absolutely love the game and it is one of my all time favorites.Early access of this game was a wonderful journey. This game made such great progress over the years and the result is just amazing. Never saw better communication between developer and community and I think it is one of the best examples for early access as it is supposed to be.Played around 2000 hours in early access from day one on Epic and I'm looking forward to the next 2000 here on Steam!Thank you and keep up the good work Coffee Stain!
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: I've played Factorio and Dyson Sphere Program, and this game is just like it - optimizing factories, creating massive contraptions and chains and modding the crap out of it - I LOVE IT!! 3d view in first person also gives the game a huge "immersion" feel the other 2 didn't do, and would be amazing if I ever get VR.Early access still has some unpolished elements, but DEVs are bringing a ton of stuff with each update that corrects most of this - it's awesome to see it evolve!!
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: Im blown away, Coffee Stain created a game that has an incredibly rewarding progression and also ends at just the right point.  I thought a Tier 9 ending would feel too soon, instead it was just right.  Leaving the game open to letting players go as big as they want, post objectives, is icing on the cake.  There are some hiccups in rendering, a few bugs here and there, nothing of which got in the way of good game-play.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: As a kid I was always obsessed with marble contraptions and things that were automated like battery powered trains that move by themselves... I saw the name for this game and I could not believe they made a game FOR ME basically. Bought the game on epic for Update 3, 300hrs thereLegit would not change a thing 9.5/10 cant wait to see how 1.0 looks
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: Well, its a pretty good game. But somehow I'm missing factorio or elements from factorio, I feel like the factory aspect is done better in factorio, there are other things in this game that this does better. Working in first person makes placing buildings etc a bit annoying when you have to rebuild just because you placed it wrong. The graphics are obviously better in this game than in factorio.Need to play this game more to give a better review in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: FICSIT Inc. Reviews SatisfactoryWelcome, Pioneers! Ever wanted to be dropped on an alien planet with nothing but a zapper and a mandate to "make it work"? Satisfactory is the game for you! From conveyor spaghetti to colossal factories that would make OSHA faint, this game lets you live out your wildest FICSIT dreams. You'll automate, optimize, and maybe get trampled by the local wildlife, all in a day's work.The game’s all about turning chaos into profit—FICSIT style! Warning: You might lose track of time (and possibly your sanity) figuring out how to automate a single screw. But hey, that’s progress!
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: Love the game, BUT!!!...   They made it necessary to have one power plant per functional building. This makes your base a MUCH, MUCH bigger and very cumbersome to try to lay out in a way that is reasonably functional and navigable... I would LOVE to see that particular requirement altered to allow a MINIMUM of 2 functional buildings ran from each power plant (preferably 4 or more), especially when it comes to the "In-line" pumps. They are small enough we should be able to hook 5 or 10 of those to a single power source. Multiple electrical connections are the norm EVERYWHERE else! Why not here? With the size of the buildings in this game, any one you can avoid having to build 20 or 30 (or more) of is very helpful.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: Got this years ago, finally sat down to give it a proper go, and MAN is it awesome. The environments are lush and well designed, the creatures on the beginner stage are believable as alien creatures, the general construction and building aesthetic is VERY well thought out and designed... And I've barely scratched the surface of the game. This is one of those games you can play for years and still enjoy. The game plays, in my eyes, like Subnautica on land (much less terrifying) - a survival crafting game where you harvest resources, build a base and lots of machines to help out, fight alien creatures, unlock tons of... unlockables that keep changing the game, and just play in a giant, open world. If you like games like Minecraft or Subnautica, you'll love this. I am very excited to play some more a little later.
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: What an incredibly well done game. I have been playing this game for years, and I always keep coming back to it, especially now that it has reached 1.0. If you are interested in Factory games, or haven't tried one yet, then I highly suggest you give Satisfactory a go. The world is beautiful, the game mechanics are incredibly satisfying, and the sheer scale is magnificent. I love this game, and will be playing it for many hundreds of hours more.

_childDocuments_.review: Satisfactory is an open world factory building game. In broad terms, you work for FICSIT Corp. and you are sent to a planet to extract resources and complete milestones for the benefit of the corporation. In practice, it's a game about automation, where you start off exploring the world, mining ore, and crafting it into stuff yourself. And end up with automated systems mining resources across the map, run trains to deliver it processing hubs where you have all sorts of machinery processing it all, stockpile the basics, and deliver the completed products to fill the milestones which unlock further tech, equipment, and fun. If you're familiar with Factorio, it's a broadly speaking a game in the style of that, but in first person, made by a far better development studio, and with so much color and personality to boot. It's one of those games that is difficult to describe in a way that is fun, but it's genuinely an incredible experience that is ridiculous amounts of fun to play and that only works so much better in co-op. It's easily one of my top favorite games and is also a great game to just sit back, zone out, and watch all of the stuff flying everywhere, being smelted, processed, assembled, and so forth.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has the best example of what a great team of devs can accomplish.  The devs give weekly streams about updates, roadmaps, Q & A and player entries. They genuinely listen to players recommendations and have added a number of QoL features based purely off players suggestions. I love this game because of its content, its professional release and there is a full time dedicated team of developers working on continual improvements and bug fixes. I would love all games to have this much dedication and support as a lot of games are 'early release' and then the devs just seem to vanish off the face of the earth! This is not one of those games, this game is worth every single cent and you can be sure the devs put your experience and enjoyment at the top of their list.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty darn fine game. Subnautica meets Factorio in Satisfactory. It's hard to find a game with movement as good as this - it's a joy to get from A to B. The gameplay is good, but unlike Factorio, I didn't feel that I was as compelled to go to the next goal. Upon finishing Phase 1 of the space elevator, you look at the requirements for the next phase and just think "Well that's gonna be a lot of grinding" The game need to drip-feed the space elevator goals to you a bit more, I feel. The game isn't like Factorio in that you don't suddenly find yourself having sunk 4-5 hours at a time on it.FYI, this was written in Update 5, so some stuff may have changed. 8 / 10

_childDocuments_.review: I got it at about 2 pm, felt bored. I landed on an alien world, and then placed down the hub. Got a few miners set up on some limestone, copper, and iron nodes. I also took a second to upgrade the hub a bit.Next, I placed down a few smelters to make iron and copper ingots so I can focus on other things. Speaking of which, I finished the hub. I got down some miners going to smelters, which bring ingots to storage containers. I think I'm starting to have a bit of fun.I then automate production of iron rods and plates, and screws too. Now, I can start to build stuff wherever I feel like, without having to go back to the hub to craft the necessary materials. Next, I automate concrete, copper wire, and cables, just for the hell of it. My factory's starting to look cool!Then, I notice something. "Huh, my room looks a bit dark," I say to myself. I look nervously at the clock. It's three in the morning. This game's a drug y'all.

_childDocuments_.review: So. If you're looking for a Minecraft or Space Engineers experience, this isn't your jam. This is many orders of magnitude better. This game is labeled as "Early Access" but the content available at this time is polished and for all intents and purposes, bug-free. I have spent the better part of the last 60 hours purposefully attempting to either A) Crash my frame rate or B) Crash the game. So far my efforts have been in vain.Some high points: - Full refund system on buildings in the game. If you're anything like me, you try to throw stuff down entirely faster than your brain is capable of doing anything with even a minimal degree of accuracy. The game understands we're knuckle-dragging neanderthals and allows us to regain all of our materials to go back and fix the inevitable eye and sanity destroying disaster our lack of patience has wrought. - No wonky physics. If you stack things, they will not, all of a sudden decide to start flossing or moonwalking for no obvious reason (Or... completely mind-boggling reason either). As a programmer myself, kudos Coffee Stain for actually play-testing your code and getting the gremlins out. It shows, and in my opinion SHINES here. - As I mentioned above, frame rates rarely tank, even with a huge amount of resources in your renderable range. The performance of this game is jaw-dropping, truly. I will again state... I purposely tried to crash/flood or otherwise tank the performance. The Engine, The Code and the Graphical Layers work well in concert with each other and seamlessly balance the experience. Well Played... Well played indeed.Some (I know... I know... I didn't want to do it either) Low Points:- You don't start with a map. Even though Ficsyt sends you to a planet they supposedly surveyed. My complaint with this, is the map should be lower in the tier progression. When you unlock the Object Scanner and Beacons, the map should come along with it. (I understand the WHY of this. It's just something I personally would like to see.) That will give players an easier time progressing through the MAM.- There are some weird clipping issues in the game I have found (Which is my only real game-mechanics complaint) you can essentially overlap conveyor belts, objects can collide and things still just work. There does not seem to be hit boxes that are referenced by items, so keeping things neat is more of an arbitrary task rather than a runtime requirement. - For large object placement, you're only option to get a better view of what you're dropping is to build a lookout tower, you cannot adjust your camera to get a better angle of what you're doing on-the-ground. While I'm not opposed to building the lookout tower and using that, it's a bit annoying when you're in a tight space trying to align objects to each other without a method to control the camera even minimally. I would suggest an option to "Glance" around instead of being locked to a set perspective.All-in-all, I think this game is amazing despite what I've said in the negative. Well worth your 30 bones, I promise you.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm sure this review is going to be controversial being that I have less than an hour and a half of play time and I’m sure a lot of other people aren’t going to understand why it’s a big deal, but here goes…I love this style of game (the factory building survival crafting RPG) and honestly wish there were more of them.  I love the beauty of the world in Satisfactory and how the machines feel like each one has a purpose.  I especially love that the game keeps growing with more and more things being added on a fairly regular basis.What I don’t love is one specific thing that the game is not.  It is not accessible.  It’s a first-person game with a locked perspective that for people like me make it almost entirely unplayable.  What it’s not is exactly why I only have 81 minutes of play time.  That was literally the limit of trying to fuss with the FOV and other visual setting that I was able to stand before I became so nauseous that I couldn’t go on.I’m sure a lot of people are going to think I’m whining or that I’m being unfair by making this a negative review, but honestly, all I’m saying is that I don’t feel like it’s too much to ask for game developers to take a moment to think about who they’re excluding when making their games especially when other developers seem to manage a third-person option (or high contrast, or descriptive text, or other inclusive features) just fine.

_childDocuments_.review: Honest Review:In the 28 hours I have devoted to this game, I can honestly say I am not even a little over half way done with the 'story' element to the game. This game has SO MUCH potential. Who doesn't enjoy running over large aliens with a vehicle? But seriously, this game has hours and hours of content and for sure replay-ability. You can get lost enjoying the vast world not even playing the game how it was meant (mindless-exploring), or you can spend HOURS on designing your factory and making it more efficient. There is so much to do, and the game for sure makes ways to make you put in the work to advance. And I mean it gets really advanced the further you get. This IS NOT just a factory building game. It's a fantastic survival game with its' own twist on the genre.PROS:-Running over aliens-Survival with an extensive amount of replay-ability-Survival with A-LOT of content, in terms of items, resources, areas to explore, etc-Beautiful graphics-Optimized-Very limited bugs (from what I have experienced)-FREEDOM, to do whatever you want (Obviously completing tasks gives you more advanced fun things to do, so i guess not 'full' freedom per-say)-Alien dogeCONS:-Multiplayer Co-op is fair but it for sure has its fair share of communicable bugs-Updates (To expand, the game has not got too many updates since launch..but is that really a con for how well it is?)-Minor bugs (i.e. your transport vehicle goes off the given path you dictated and ends up 1000km down a cavern randomly)-No player customizationOverall:9/10Why? It is fun, it has content, it has SO MUCH potential as a Survival in its' own nature. And most certainly, it is a rather chill game that you can pick up and get lost in playing for hours trying to make an even more insane factory, or just..get lost lol.I am excited to see what is in store for this game (i.e. more planets, more structures, more resources, player customization).Please, buy the game and support the developers! I promise if you are into survival games, you will enjoy this game. There is so much depth to this game.

_childDocuments_.review: For a game with complex mechanics, Satisfactory has the best quality-of-life implementation that I have ever seen. In most games, when done well, quality-of-life features go unnoticed, and draw attention only when they fail. Satisfactory is different. Every time I expect a glitch or a failure, every time I expect Satisfactory to fail to handle an unexpected situation, this game defies any expectation short of pure excellence. Every step of the way, Satisfactory's interface makes the experience as convenient as possible. Every step of the way, if I want to do something specific, Satisfactory gives you every interface shortcut you can possibly want.For example, when you build early-game power lines, the interface will intelligently infer that you also intend to build power poles, and will allow you to build both in one step.The biomes are some combination of beautiful and exotic (my only complaint is the apparent absence of colder biomes) and are a pleasure to explore.Options for custom intelligent automation appear to be limited compared to other well known factory games, but that is understandable because at the time of writing (March 28, 2024) this game is still in early access. If this game is completed with all custom-logic-automation-related features, and the modding community gets going, I would not surprised to see Satisfactory crowned the new gold standard of factory games.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of Factorio, you will feel right at home in Satisfactory. In fact, I would say Satisfactory is what you would play when you want a break from the stress of factory defence in Factorio. Both games have their advantages and disadvantages. For Factorio, I love defending my factory and the aesthetics of factory design in 2D, top-down environment. However, apart combat that comes in the form of fighting creatures one meets as they explore the world, Satisfactory leaves the player alone to focus on one thing: build your factory!The game does not force you into factory defence game play or limit you with finite resource nodes. The player is free to explore and build (and rebuild and rebuild and rebuild) their factory. This does not mean that the world is easily tamable. While no creatures will attack your factory, they will attack you if you get too close. And, while not especially difficult (so far in my experience), they can be lethal if caught off-guard. The world itself is hand made and it shows. All I will say is that the world is gorgeous and is really fun to explore! I even lost my way once and had to suicide because the world is so intricate in how each biome connects to each other. It is quite easy to get lost!This game is well named because it is incredibly satisfying to see your factory grow and to see all of those conveyor belts moving materials. One feels quite kingly looking over the vast terrain to see how it was conquered by your machines and power lines. Advances along the technology tree present the player with new ways to design their factory. I am on my first play-through, currently at tier 5 (of 7 at this time) and have rebuilt my factory at least 3 times. And I'm sure once I have access to trains, it'll be time to rebuild again!Although still in EA, it is already a very full game. The game DOES NOT feel like EA. At this stages, you are getting a game that will provide 1000s of hours of entertainment and there is still more to come.Having said that, while this game puts emphasis on building, I hope that the developers do more with the world and environment. By all means, keep the current quasi-peace mode of building with (from what I've experienced so far) infinite resources and co-existing with creatures that do not attack my factory. But, I would sure like that as an option, both finite resources and creatures that can cause some havoc to the factory. The world is incredibly beautiful and I would like to have, as a player, to deal with environment hazards such as weather, earthquakes, pollution, mutation of flora and fauna, and degradation of the land. There should be options for environmentally conscious players who may want to construct their factories inline with their own code of ethics and morality. If you enjoy factory building and automation games, you should definitely give this game a try. It will certainly scratch that OCD itch of proper 90 degree angles and efficient use of (3D) space! Or, if that's not your style, feel free to get lost in your own spaghetti factory!

_childDocuments_.review: Satisfactory has truly set the bar for early access games. The amount of enjoyment packed into this title is staggering, guaranteeing you hundreds of hours of immersive gameplay. What makes it even better is the seamless cooperative mode, turning every session into a laugh-out-loud experience with friends.While the game generally runs generally smooth, it's important to note that performance can be a bit finicky, especially on the experimental branch. This occasional hiccup aside, Satisfactory still manages to provide an uninterrupted and enjoyable gaming experience overall. The developers are not only responsive but also proactive, consistently rolling out updates that introduce new tiers, machines, resources, and various fixes. It's refreshing to see a team so committed to refining and expanding the game based on player feedback.One delightful aspect that adds a quirky charm to the game is the concept of "spaghetti factories." Navigating the chaos of interconnected conveyor belts and machinery to create a functioning system is both a challenge and a source of endless entertainment.In conclusion, Satisfactory is more than a game; it's an evolving experience filled with fun, camaraderie, and continuous improvement. If you're seeking an early access title that delivers on its promises and keeps you hooked, look no further than Satisfactory.

It is just so much fun. The dev team has updated this game a lot and it runs well but you might need a fairly good pc system to run it. Once you start getting a lot of machinery working. I'm running a strong up to date system with a Amd 7900 xtx and the game crashed once. Granted it was only once so far and I had the game running for over 6 hours. While still unfinished and in early access, the level of polish on what is completed is an achievement of the developers.  I have yet to have a single crash in singleplayer, and only a few instances where I became stuck in the map, normally clipping with a built factory, which the respawn feature made only a minor annoyance, not a game breaker. _childDocuments_.review: I would just like to leave a review for those individuals who disable comments on their negative review complaining of crashing when they admittedly in some cases and probably implicitly in other cases have a 1000 series or similar age graphics card:PLEASE turn your DirectX version in the settings from 12 to 11.If the game will not physically start, you can do this in the files, google it.It will make your game run better for those individuals and probably stop crashing so much, I just had to change my review to this because it's mind boggling that people are putting the fact that DX12 and unreal engine 5 rarely run without crashing on hardware that is starting to get older on the devs, it is outside their control, you should complain to epic who developed the unreal engine if you have problems with it, but in the meantime you should just switch your DX version to 11, which will stop the crashing. I had the same problem on my old laptop with an older gpu, and I changed it to DX11 after they updated the engine in a past update and it stopped crashing. If your game still crashes, then it probably is another issue that needs to be revolved and the negative review is warranted, but please try this first. Thank you!

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, it wasn't just that I "wanted" to like this.  I EXPECTED to like this.  You don't hear much of anything negative about SatisFactory.  So...It's tedious.I tried.  I really did.  I've been working on this for six hours and some.  And.  It's tedious.  I normally LOVE games with figuring out how to make conveyor belts and assemblers and stuff all fit together.  And add in some exploration and dangerous wild life?  That should be my jam and a half and a bag of chips.  I thought this was going top be my game to replace Disgaia and MineCraft.  But I've spent over half of the past six hours (and some) on gathering leaves to fuel the factory that I'm still trying to get running. Maybe with research you can unlock something really futuristic like, I don't know, solar power, later in the game.  But in the first... quarter?  You spend  more time gathering leaves and flowers to fuel the generator than you do building anything.  And THAT is not something I've found a way to avoid.  THAT is a major design error.  Because it's boring.  I could quibble and say that I'm annoyed that even though they do have a supposedly dedicated single player mode the game is SO bloody dedicated to the "multiplayer experience" that it does not pause for anything.  So, if you are an actual adult there's another reason to avoid this.  I could say it's a bit rediculous to send a single person (or a small party of... what 4?) to an unexplored alien world with known dangerous wild life armed with melee weapons.  I could forgive all that if it weren't for the fact that the game is tedious.  If it weren't for the fact that after six hours (and a bit) I'm sick of the thing and it does not seem to be getting any better.So, do yourself a favor.  Wait till it's out of "early access."  Maybe they will figure out a few of the bad ideas they have going in this by then.

_childDocuments_.review: Boy, oh boy, where do I even begin.This game is anything but what the name implies. Now, i understand that i'm being biased here and having played Factorio prior to Satisfactory definitely did something to set the bar way too high. Satisfactory has a few tremendous dealbreakers for me, that basically prevented me from enjoying it. At all. Number one would be the first-person perspective. It ABSOLUTELY destroys the factory readability, the thing that is crucial for a game revolving around building a factory. Doing that from the fist-person perspective simply does not work. It's like having an RTS game with a fixed first-person view, or a racing game, that would utilize point-and-click controls. You get the idea. Probably. My second personal problem with this game would be the hard requirement to integrate Epic Games services with Steam, or at least as far as i recall, it was a thing few years ago, when i got this game. But probably the absolute worst of them is the fact that you can not use a rather nice-looking chainsaw to let the local wildlife know it's place. This feels like a huge pile of just squandered potential. I'm not asking for DOOM (2016) level of gore whenever the player character applies the chainsaw to the squishy bits of alien wildlife. Just some damage. But no. You are limited to your stunstick tazer thing. That's about it. Meanwhile Factorio has a whole arsenal of thins you can eradicate agresssive eco-activ... err, bugs with. Including nukes. Unlimited resource nodes. This completely eliminates the incentive for factory growth. And what is worse - this makes the game painstakingly casual. You don't need to adjust your factory design or improve it anymore. This completely removes a huge chunk of the challenge.As if it wasn't bad enough, there is this arbitrary limit of four people per session, even if the host alters the config files it still won't guarantee the success. So if you have more than four people in a group that (for some reason) wants to play Satisfactory - you are out of luck. Wait for your turn. There is a bunch of other things. Game-breaking updates. Desync problems that are even worse than the ones with Escape From Tarkov (and that speaks freaking VOLUMES). And what is worse - it does not feel like there is even a bigger purpose for all this. Unlike - AGAIN - Factorio.At the end of the day i feel like a bit of an asshat slandering the game i got for free. But the sheer feeling of spite and resentement towards this product is stronger than the feeling of gratitude. Thus, Satisfactory is one of those games i find it almost painful to play. I can't recommend it. At all.

Very very good game.

You start with basic recipes with some initial hand-crafting but will rapidly start creating intricate automated production lines that get steadily more complex.This is achieved by a tiered progression system which ensures you always have another goal but builds you up without being overwhelmed at the start.The map is large and has an interesting assortment of biomes to explore which you will need to traverse to take advantage of new resource nodes. _childDocuments_.review: I am amazed at how good this game is. It is quite chill, in that it doesn't punish you for doing things in a stupid way; however, if you like, you can also spend quite a bit of time in figuring out how to do things in an optimal fashion. There is a lot to play, although there is some grinding to do in several stages. I played the game for 100+ hours both alone and in multiplayer a few years ago. Now, with the newest updates, I started playing it again because the game was so much fun. I see that there have been some very good improvements: for instance, in the earlier versions, health did not regenerate to full and you had to instead forage for food to get back to full health, while now one does regenerate to full even though somewhat slowly so that one may still want to have the food as an option.I also immensely enjoy the accuracy of the game with respect to the real world. At the start, you power your equipment with biofuels. In practice, this means stripping out the lush nature of its shrubs and trees, leaving barren landscapes - which you will slowly pave over by concrete to build more factories. Crashing your power grid is also a bad thing. Like in the real world, many power plants require electricity to start. If you have a large grid that crashes, restoring it will take a long long time...

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the finest games I've ever played, for a number of reasons. The main ones are:1. Well-scaled factory sim. The game lulls you in with the perfect amount of simplicity at the start to make every added bit of complexity make sense in the larger scale of the game. Often factory sims drop you in, teach you a couple of things, then let you get overwhelmed with the scale of the project in front of you. I felt this particularly with Dyson Sphere Project - the game tells you what the endgame is, then gets you started on a scale that seems so impossibly small you don't feel like you're making progress. It's not a bad game at all, but I think the drip-feeding of ever-increasing complexity, depth, and scale make Satisfactory a real winner in this regard.2. The first person perspective is a terrific choice. Often the top-down/isometric view factory sims seem too remote, too abstract. Being on the ground and walking around your factory makes it really rewarding to indulge in...3. your architectural dreams. The game is all about systems planning, throughput efficiency, and logistics, and you can indulge in all of that without ever dressing up your factories or making them look nice. But if you like designing a brutalist monolith as an homage to Arne Jacobsen then this is possible. The game has plenty of scope for aesthetic sculpting.Drawbacks: not many, but I do hope they will be implementing some story elements, and the game can feel a bit lonely and empty of purpose as a result of this I think. Purpose is provided by your own ambitions and by finessing your production lines to achieve the next level of complexity - this is fine, but it would be nice to have some flavour or unexpected reasons to adapt production from time to time. Special projects or the like.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just delightful. The big release videos for new milestone updates are hysterical.The mechanics of the game are fun and intuitive, and the replay value is pretty substantial for anyone who likes optimizing production and aesthetics and functionality. The world is big with diverse biomes and fun challenges to overcome to meet production/organization/efficiency demands.Just a little bit of combat, but not enough to get stuck on.

_childDocuments_.review: This game can be addictive if you're into crafting type games. Starting out there really wasn't a tutorial or maybe there is and I didn't see it because and Friend and I just jumped into a game. However, once you learn the commands this game is easy to do and can sometimes hurt your brain on trying to construct the right chain of buildings to get the desired product efficiently. We're now 14hrs into our first game and still feel like we've barely scratched the surface on what we can do. You're constantly trying to figure out what to build next, what you're short on resource wise, and how to produce needed items. Starting out our base of operations was very confusingly placed around. Once you get an idea of the kind of products you need to make with which resources, it's a lot easier to plan out your buildings. Definitely recommend building close to the first 3 main resources at start (Iron, Limestone, Copper). Once you get the hang of things, it's limitless on what you can do to organize your base and make everything nicely organized. TL;DR - If you like crafting/management games, this game can be addictive and fun. For being early access, definitely an amazing game and I can't wait to see what they add or change to make the game even more fluid then it already is. Highly Recommend
_childDocuments_.name: Satisfactory

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: Welcome to 1.0+ further game play updates, and some recipes changed. The map was tweaked and I am mixed about that.I still recommend the game. As I have played an additional 1300+ hours I definitely got my money's worth. The only question I have come up without a resolution in 1.0, is do I finish this run, or do I start a separate one to build a more concise set of factories? Decisions, decisions, decisions. Please enjoy the gameGreat game overall. The factory builder genre have some variations. Satisfactory lets you make a lot of the items yourself, but you have to actively make them. So, it really benefits one to automate, automate, and - oh yeah - automate.For newbies, unlike many resource -> acquire -> create -> use loops Satisfactory does not run out of resources. If you have a copper node to mine (by hand, by little mining bot, or big mining machine) it will never run out. They also use coupons to acquire new items for your factory construction. The method for acquire those is a Sink.Yep, they . Very funny. However, it is difficult for newbies, as it was for myself, to just dump good material down the Sink. Well, get used to it. Any and all extra can be sunk. Since resources never run out (95% sure of that) you can always redirect if you were sinking something then needed it elsewhere. The more goods, and the higher level those goods are, that get sunk, the more points you get which gives you coupons to get more stuff to build better factories. See the loop?If you like building things, and automation, this is a great game to play.Good Luck

_childDocuments_.review: Satisfactory tricked me into playing an open world game and the wild part is I actually enjoyed it. The map is huge and also still full of life with lots of explorable items and secrets to find. I found myself extremely far from home after going out for one or two specific things because there was constantly something tempting me into just going a little farther. The factory building progression and the exploration progression feed into each other so you're rewarded for doing both together, and it unlocks more of the map as you unlock the gas mask, explosives and the jetpack, so then not only can you explore farther but revisiting old areas is rewarding as a result. The game is still in EA so there's a couple bugs (getting stuck in trees is the biggest one) and not everything is done but already there's so much content that's gotten me addicted in a way I haven't in a while.

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun, I can never stick to one game for more than a week, but I've found myself coming back to this game so many times because of how addictive it is. _childDocuments_.review: This is a brilliant game so far, I'm glad to have discovered it, with a lot to explore and a lot to do I really enjoy getting on this game after work and just losing myself in it. Below I'm going to put a pros and cons list. Please keep in mind that this is my opinion.Pros:-Plenty of things to build and mine-Exploration takes you through some very pretty places-Building things takes actual resources and you will feel the hit of building something if you're under-prepared-Creating a fully functioning and efficient system of machines is a great feeling that holds some accomplishment-Still being updated and having things added so you'll have plenty to work towardsCons:-Some things feel extremely resource heavy even if you've been mining a material for a long time and think you have enough, sometimes you'll find your products are too resource hungry-There should be a better way to fight hostile mobs in the game, currently feels like they are either too spongy or you're too weak-Sometimes things aren't as intuitive as they should be, I was almost 100 hours in before I realized you can create new hotbars and figuring out how to put items on the hotbar took me a little longer (this is just one example)Overall, I think this game has a lot to give and creates an experience wholly unique within a resource management/survival game, I highly recommend you get it and try it out.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an excellent and addicting game.Let's travel through time:1) What was I looking for - I was looking for a game similar to Subnautica and Below Zero. A building and survival game. What I found was Satisfactory. I did not read the description properly and assumed it was the same or similar. So I started playing the Demo. It's similar but not the same.What do I mean - Well, first off, while there is some aspects of it, this is not a Survival game. It's a construction / building / production game.2) The Demo - The demo itself was addictive. The exchange rate does not make it easy for me to purchase a lot of games, so I usually wait for Discounts or Freebies. I purchased this game at full price (I think) and I am Satisfactory ;)3) Noob - The beginning was a little tough to get into, but was fun and challenging which I expect from ALL games. It's a different play style to what I've played before, so was a nice change.4) Getting into it - Slowly grasping the concept of game play and what was required of me to succeed, I needed some assistance for game play and strategy, You WILL NOT be disappointed. There is SO much help, videos, guides, blueprints, etc that you will, 99.9% of the time, get the help you need.5) Grasping it - Everyone is different and everyone has different play styles or ways that they interpret or handle things. A lot of people are Mathing their setups which is what you're supposed to do to get the best out of your productions and as good as I am with maths, that is too much for me although I am now getting into that too.6) Help and Resources - The community is massive, you will find what you need.7) Dev Support - The Devs have a clear direction where they want 'THEIR' game to go, and despite what some silly 1-100hrs only game players may say, the devs do listen. Just check out their support page and their YouTube videos. A lot has changed because of Community feedback.8) Finishing off - DON'T criticise a game that you have barely played or experienced. Get into it, look for support or guides, or watch some YouTube videos and play-through's. I i'm not just referring to Satisfactory, but all games and applications and all experiences in life. Not that many people read books these days, but some people will open the first page and read the first paragraph and say how cr@p the book is without even completing the first chapter. STOP Comparing games unless it is a sequel.Just because it is similar to another game DOES NOT mean it has to be the same, that would be copying. If the other game is so great, then play that game.

_childDocuments_.review: after playing my first save for 39 hours, i can say it is safe to say the game is very much worth it. but there are some things i feel you should know before you start up your own world and get into it, don't worry it is nothing bad about the game. if anything, it makes the game better,1. plan your power grid, i cannot stress this enough. each power pole has 4 connection, but 2 of them are always going to be needed for connecting to other poles, one to hook it up with power and one to hook the next one up.2. plan your conveyor belts! if you don't, you will end up with a very messy base as they can clip through one another and you end up with spaghetti conveyor belts and they are hard to clean up.3. overclocking is helpful, once you get coal and move away from biomass, overclocking is so worth it. 4. underclocking is amazing early game, biomass is a pain to get so underclocking is very helpful.5. get coal power as soon as possible! it makes your life so much easier and produces so much more power.6. have fun!

_childDocuments_.review: At the current state I'd give Satisfactory 8.5/10, only because of one bug, otherwise it's 9.5-10. I'll start with more of general points and then dwell into specifics.The game part:: Awesome, wonderful, fantastic. I could do with less drastic changes of filters in some locations(namely desert and red forest) and the swamps are way too dark at night man.: Feels very nice, I was usually exploring after completing stages, gathering HDDs, then unlocking milestones and gambling alt recipes(I got the steel beam screws way too late and I could live without coal recipes though).The caves were fun and I'm surprised how unique they felt, everything is hand placed and is full of attention to details. World design in general is one of the best I've seen past decade. : I like all the biomes except red forest. No resources (except coal and bauxite), bad terrain, a lot of annoying vegetation and enemies, feels like a placeholder. My favorite biome is probably the swamp, I hate spiders with all my soul(once had a prolonged fight with like 14 big ones there) but something about it just feels nice. Swamp does destroy my fps though.: It's there.:I've spent so much time on phase 5 I don't even have a lot of memories about previous ones. My least favorite one (apart from 5) is probably 3. 1, 2 and 4 are equally good.Phase 5 starts pretty fun, but there's not a lot to do on actual phase 5. If need be one can finish phase 5 in ~8-10 hours (assuming 2 pasta/min) and some spare tickets to manually create everything else.Phase 5 for me was: 1) Solve Fuel: I opted for 1200 rocket fuel and 200 Ionized Fuel(optional);2) Solve Power: I did 36 Uranium: 9 Plutonium: 45 Ficsonium Fuel Rods(only to recycle plutonium waste); 3) Solve Resources: Tens of Specialized Factories (or just SAM/Time Crystal Nodes) each with Drones coming in/out (by the end I had like 250 Drones);4) Solve Traversal: I did 120 Singularity Cells (90 for Ficsonium, 25 for phase 5 part), somersloop one for bonus 25 - 30 left for 15 portals. However much I despise somerslooping I despise nuclear pasta more;5) Finish Phase 5.All of this except traversal, phase 5 (duh) and ficsonium I could've done phase 4. And you don't really need traversal if you aren't making specialized factories. By itself phase 5 is extremely weak. I mean I guess power shards are nice. I also hate the quantum encoder building. Now for some more detailed thoughts.: All of them are fixed by reload, unless you get the frozen drone bug and it lost all fuel, it's still fixed then but if it lands on a non fueled port it's gone. My least favorite ones:Hoverpack bug: Remembers last altitude change input on entering building menu(or portal);Radiation bug: If you sort inventory with a radioactive item the radiation will persist even after removal of said item.Frozen drone: The worst offender and the one that almost made me quit game. Occasionally (once in 4-6 hours) random drone can just stop moving and stand in place. Can happen both in open field or near port. This breaks production chain, and if it is your waste recycling facility, it will result in surplus of waste, which is very annoying. Another bad case, drone that is used in singularity cell production, which will just cut you off all portals. Even worse case, if it came to that, total halt of nuclear power plants and not having enough power to make the fuel rods.Drone port choice: Occasionally the port that you choose and the port that the drone will actually fly to are different, same as the swatch loadout bug, you have to choose the port above the desired one. Can break production chain horribly. Relevant ports shows the correct one, This port information is unreliable.Drone alititude recognition: If you build drone port near (~30m) high altitude for some reason the drone will try to gain the alititude before landing, which takes forever, I had 600m trips on 10m altitude delta take 4 minutes on ionized fuel (near the highest plateau with uranium).The lesser ones are rifle reload radial popup, teleporting rad hogs, enemies stuck in terrain, swatch loadout choice, arms on top of your head, unable to use hotkeys to build.Also standing near power bank or geothermal thingey will destroy your fps overtime, same as every time you dare to look in the waterfall up close. I don't even get how waterfalls can be this taxing, the VFX looks like the most compressed GIF ever made.Now for the even more specific thoughts:: Late game energy is badly designed imho. With the recipes I used I had 450 GW coming from 72 250% NPP using 36 Uranium Fuel Rods, waste recycled into 9 Plutonium Fuel Rods using base recipes.Now I either fuel another 36 250% NPP for extra 225 GW (don't really need it) and have the pleasure of having to get rid of 90 plutonium waste somehow (90 singularity cells), or just sink the rods.And I definitely don't need the ficsonium power. Obviously I don't need any of that but the recipe cost of ficsonium is too high for what it will realistically give you(assuming base recipes for non-fissile uranium and plutonium rods it is 8:4:2 Uranium:Plutonium:Ficsonium NPP ratio), it's basically holding plutonium energy as a hostage.Even if it was buring at like 0.5 Rods at 250% I am not building another 90 NPP (finding place in open sea, positioning NPPs, making water extractors, making pipes, pumps, splitters, wiring). All for adding more power(laughable amount at that) which is already a non-factor. There's literally zero motivation to make/use ficsonium, at least make the smoke green when using it or smth.If you do want enough power to meet all your needs(unless something crazy with 10s of somerslooped 250% quantum encoders) I'd suggest going for lower number of uranium, say 18 rods, giving >=450 GW with plutonium+ficsonium implementation while cutting singularity cells production in half-ish. Also, let me get this straight, you can't sink ficsonium, the power it gives is ass, requires a lot of SAM to process plutonium waste, and it's still radioactive, and it's stack is still 50 so you can't even reasonably store it (at 45/m it would give you 5 1/3 hours of storage with 6 Industrial units. It's just plain terrible. : MK6 conveyor belts are not supplying the advertised 1200/m rate. When traveling over any decent distance >40-50m and having multiple (5+) split or merge points the MK6 is incapable of operating at 100%.  Your best bet is to assume output of like 1000 through the belt.Buffer: This will apply if you split at an entry point. Low amount transferred over drones requires some good buffer built up, and having low amounts(20-30) arrive rarely split over like 10 buildings (I'm looking at you PCC -> nuclear pasta) can take forever to build up to 100% uptime, without supplying system with buffer. The 36 Uranium Rods for 76 NPP took about 35 hours to fill and even then the last 2-4 buildings were starving, had to feed it from outside the system for it to stabilize (I checked the I/O 5 times).:Caterium and Quartz are kind of one trick ponies, one goes to quickwire, another goes to quartz crystal. Also why is Crystal Oscillator so popular(and so so good) but the max you can make is 4.6875 on one 250% manuf, please make itt like 10.I feel like batteries are extremely useless. Require a lot of resources (I honestly just kind of hate sulfur) and are only used as fuel source (much worse to make compared to rocket or even oxidized) or in 1(one)alt rec.In general, unless its only me, late game is horrible with the freezing drone bug making you amass nuclear waste, which you can dump somewhere obviously, but why should you. I can live with it breaking some Phase 5 production (although it's annoying to fix sometimes) but the waste is so annoying to handle. With my final breath I will ask for alt Fluid Tank recipe, pleaseeee.
