_childDocuments_.review: As a gamer whose education is in anthropology, I was really looking forward to this game. Unfortunately it seems like it was designed by an inexperienced team. The graphics, sound, programming, and concepts are great. The main problems are in design and can be summed up with three things: bad controls, bad interfacing, more frustrating than fun.①　Whether using mouse & keyboard or a controller, the controls are non-intuitive for either a newbie or experienced gamer. Too many conflicting actions are assigned to the same key/button. For example, moving quickly, dodging, jumping, and grabbing onto foliage (but not branches) are all the same button. This means your apes fall to death more way more frequently than non-human hominins would—but more importantly, it kills the fun. The content was as accurate as current understanding of the period permits, but the design makes brachiation harder than believable for 10 MYA, ruining any immersion. I didn't mind starting with a small tribe that had no previous knowledge of what foods had helped them survive before I entered the story (even though that too makes no sense), but missing the foliage I was aiming for happened so often that I started over 3 times. In the end I just stayed low to the ground (again, killing the immersion for this time period).②　It's fine, and I expected that they wouldn't give hints on skill tree / evolutionary progression, what foods do, how to make tools, what threats might exist. This was the experience I was seeking. But, again, it's bad design to make the player guess how they have to interact with the game to do obvious behaviours like putting down a child or mating. Such things should be instinctual for any animal.If you do buy the game, here's some hints:   ・Tap a button to sense perceive things in the environment, but HOLD the button to sense perceive what your holding onto.    ・The blackish swirls around things mean they are unidentified, not poisonous.   ・Picking bugs off of another ape does not satisfy your hunger need. It's a rhythm minigame which leads to making that ape your mate.   ・To mate, tap the button to first lie in your bedding. If you hold it, it will just put you to sleep.    ・If you can't figure out how to do something seemingly obvious, try laying down in bedding first. There's several things there.   ・Don't collect the apes from outside your clan until the game gives you that mission. I had them join up as soon as I saw them, so when the mission came it was impossible to finish and get the next mission.③　Most importantly, the design team seems to have not heard the industry mantra, "follow the fun." They had a very specific vision and they hammered the game until it fit that shape instead of playing the game as it way being programmed and following the fun that the game  revealed on its own. Countless games became unexpected hits because the developers let the game show them "what it wanted to be."The graphics, level design, audio, and general grandeur of the game are of high quality, so it really sucks that the design prevented Ancestors from living up to it's potential. I got the feeling that the lead designer has a big ego and didn't take suggestions from his team. I'm honestly surprised he has headed up multiple games before this. But, I heard he did Assassin's Creed which I also recently played and oof, it doesn't hit its potential either. Cool climbing, but it triggers when you don't want it to (another example of underusing buttons/keys) and so very repetitive.Some of the problems in ancestors are too deeply embedded to fix, but maybe they'll open it up to modding some day and we can make it better as a community. Ancestors could be 10/10—and I rarely rate anything above a 9. As it is, I can't rate it above a 4 because games should make you want to keep playing. But each time I boot it up I just quit in frustration—not even rage quitting. Just disappointment and frustration.I really want to like this game. Please fix it!(Edited for clarity, proper grammar, & spelling.)

_childDocuments_.review: There's about 5 hours of content here. You can construct about four structures, craft maybe six items, and get mauled by three kinds of animals (I don't say "fight" because your choice is between running away or trying to scare them away by screaming). Play time is padded by revoking some of the skills you've already unlocked and making you unlock them again (and again, and again, ...).The apes are supposed to be evolving toward being human, but there's nothing more human-like for them to do as they progress. No fire, no stone spearheads, no atlatls, no straw rafts, no bows or arrows, no pottery, no hunting or trapping, no mud huts, no clay figurines (and  no metalworking). You're stuck as a chimp-like hominid that slowly gets better at sharpening sticks and making leaf beds. (Allegedly there's spearfishing, but the fear mechanic is blocking me from exploring widely enough to find a fishing spot to try it out.)It feels like this game's development was cut when it was 20% done, and they're trying to recoup losses by selling what they had anyway.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly the complaints surrounding this game are mostly people who haven't learned to play the game yet. The mechanics of the game are simple when you understand them. When you understand that the game is a blast! This game is intense, but it's not anywhere near dark souls level like some people make it out to be. Simply put this is how you 'beat' the game: When I first wrote this review I was still discovering all sorts of new items, activities, animals, and places, whether it be gemstones, fishing, beaches, breaststroke, etc. I've since 100%-ed the game. Every thing, activity, neuron, location, prey, predator, craftable item, structure, kill animation, location and more I've completed.This game is by no means flawless. Glitches and bugs are very very rare. On occasion animal and ancestor AI can bug out, but never to the point it's game breaking or even immersion breaking. Every location is capable of being explored. Every nook and cranny is reachable.  There's tons of content to enjoy so learn that's what the game is about.This is just another GET GUD KID review. _childDocuments_.review: Hard to say I would recommend it.The game is fascinating. It is beautiful. It is all about learning how to play. It is also very exciting.Controls are hard to handle at the beginning but then it is fine. They are some explanations in the menu and pressing the down shift of the cross of the pad will make info stay on the screen. I play with a pad. I had to use the mouse in the neural menu because it is buggy. It is probably done to only play with a pad like said some comments. I am not sure. I have no issue playing with it.In this game you play more a prey than a predator. It is about exploration, discovery and most of all the evolution of your tribe. Till you have tribe members, you can still evolve. You completely lose when you finish alone (I suppose, I never faced that yet). You can make reproduce young fertile females with males. With a limit of 2 babies per female and per generation.It is a mandatory to ensure the continuity of the game.The reason why it is very hard to recommend it: there is no save except when devs decided it. So it seems if you lose, you will have to start everything from scratch. The game is long, slow paced most of the time. If I have to restart again from scratch... Not sure I will do it.I have a thumb up for all the pleasure I have discovering the universe and all its possibilities. Also for the excitement in some situation, especially with some predators and the couple of situations you can face them. If you stay in the trees, you are quite safe and you can continue to explore and grind. Reading the doc in the menu is a mandatory.Saving in a game is a proven efficient concept since probably close to 20 years now. On a platform game, I can understand the checkpoints and it can be enough since the challenge is to achieve one piece of a map in between 2 checkpoints. Other cases, it is just a fail from the devs. Why could I not leave at any time and restart where I left my game? Why should I be forbid to test something and redo if I want by just loading my own save done just before my action.Here I used to have 6 babies. just by trying to have a new settlement for the first time, I loss one, I loss one adult as well...Because of this, all the nice progresses I did till then are crippled. The disappointment of losing them once is enough, no need to make me lose the pleasure of my progress as well... If devs like to please some players who like to suffer by restarting from scratch, make it optional. But why while making a game which is by nature supposed to please, devs frustrate people and make their game unpleasant... I cannot believe since there is high skills in dev this one, there was a lack of skills enough to not know how to dev a save option. So, it is definitely another skill which is missing...--This edit here is just to get some trophy thingy during 2020 awards--

_childDocuments_.review: Ancestors is a game where you play as a monkey trying to evolve into a human person but like not really. It's about trying to learn about stuff like plants animals and places while trying to expand your brain (skill points). It's definitely a struggle as the game does not explain things to you such as how to construct certain things like a bed or a fence wall thingy, but I get the point it's trying to make here. It's trying to make you feel like you're a monkey with no idea how to ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ do anything trying to figure out what building even is or what plants are or what animals are. The game reminds me a lot of spore in the creature stage where you go around as a primitive thing trying to level up to become less primitive. I can understand why some people really hated this game because it's really unforgiving at some times but I also don't understand why anybody would love this game. The whole thing of this game was it's like marmite you either love it or you hate it but I have no idea how you would love this game. in the end it just turns into a massive collection game where you have to really slowly go through the giant map looking for things that you missed because you really wanted to get out the jungle. It's kinda fun to be a monkey climbing trees and ♥♥♥♥ but all together it just gets really annoying really quickly and you notice that the game does ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ things like every now and then a tiger jumps out of nowhere and attacks you but to dodge the attack you need to hold down A/X and then let go, but if you let go too early it hits you. I always ♥♥♥♥ this up because the fastest way to get about in this game is to halo jump (constantly press A/X) this means every now and then when you're exploring you have to go back to your base because this ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ cat came out of nowhere. You can't kill it as well it's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ just keeps coming back.Overall I'd give this game a 6/10 not really worth playing but kinda cool. i would've really liked it if I could've progressed as a human and made a small tribe or something but the game cuts off when you reach the first actual human, before that you're just a kinda humanish ape that walks a tiny bit. I never bothered to actually finish the game because it would've taken forever to finish. So yeah 6/10 a just good enough for me.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game but it is not for everyone. Getting used to the UI/ somewhat janky and unintuitive controls (keys have multiple functions which can lead to some very annoying situations) will take some time and it is definitely a steep learning curve. Combat doesn't really change throughout the game and it isn't hard to master. Personally I found the most enjoyment in the game exploring the map and interacting with Pleistocene fauna which is (most of the time) beautifully animated, especially in the fight cutscenes. Being able to hunt large animals such as hippopotamuses, rhinos and elephants is incredibly satisfying. The stalker cat will also keep you on your toes thtought the game and really make sure you don't ever feel completely safe while playing just as our ancestors did 2million years ago. Overall a great game for lovers of natural history but not without its flaws.
_childDocuments_.name: Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey

_childDocuments_.review: Pro- Anyone who enjoys exploring a large map and learning things as you go with the least possible hand-holding will enjoy this game. There's a sense of accomplishment as you gradually reach the top of the food chain and find yourself leaving dense forests in favor of having more room to run. The flow is natural with the closest thing to a "story" being following the meteorites to discover new types of scenery.Con- It's more of an RPG than a survival game and while I like the RPG aspect it seems Survival is just too easy. There are certain abilities and items you'll just never use, one of which (slow motion) doesn't seem to serve a purpose at all. Lastly, while you have the option to sneak around you cannot use this offensively as you are only capable of counter-attacking rather than initiating the attack.All in all Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey is a fantastic game of exploration that I do recommend despite the Cons listed above as these Cons make up so little of the overall game that you might not even notice them.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:+ Good graphics+ Rewarding mechanics; you feel like you've achieved something when you make a new discovery or craft something new+ Apes... Cons:- Game is quite repetitive: you mature neurons and then pass onto the next generation, but you can only lock in a certain number of neurons per generation, meaning you have to go back and re-mature certain neurons before progressing- There is no real objective or end goal; whilst it's kind of the point, there is no real sense of wanting to go back to the game after a whileOverall: Recommend because it's a unique game that is more of a simulator or scientific endeavour. _childDocuments_.review: Concept is great, but execution is terrible.  The tutorials/help popups don't tell you a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ thing, so you end up feeling like a stupid monkey, which maybe is the point but it's frustrating.  There's ways to get rid of things like bleeding, broken bones, poisoning, etc. but you don't know how to do any of this unless you magically find the right combination of things or go looking for info online.  The 'minimap' tells you absolutely nothing, it doesn't give any direction or aid whatsoever and the little dots on it are never explained.I could deal with all that, but the worst thing about this game is the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ tigers.  Every time you leave your home/nest/den/whatever, you get stalked by a tiger.  The only way to avoid them is to stay in the canopy, which you can't really do if you want to progress in the game, so you're forced into these encounters.  Even if you dodge perfectly, every tiger encounter ends up with you bleeding to death and limping back home to try and bandage yourself up (if you've even figured out how to do that, or have the resources to do so).The only recommendations I've found for dealing with that issue are "kill the tiger".  So, I figure out how to sharpen some sticks - the only real weapon you can use in the game - and arm my entire 8+ monkey warband with sharpened sticks, then go off hunting for the tiger.  As soon as it makes the first pounce at me, my stupid ass monkey loses the stick, can't pick it back up because the tiger pounces every 3 seconds leaving you completely on the defensive while you take injuries and bleed out.  My idiot monkey warband scattered or just got mauled to death because none of them knew how to use the sticks (mine didn't either, apparently, there is no "stab" button).  The entire thing is a frustrating mess where you basically have no option but to die, either then and there or after running away and bleeding to death.

_childDocuments_.review: Panache Digital Games came up with a game we always desired. Start your journey from scratch and evolve accordingly. There are not many restrictions imposed on the players. If you want to tarry with your group and don’t leave the settlement, you are free to do so, or gather your clan and evolve throughout a journey of exploring new kinds of stuff. Feel the adventure of surviving the world that ages up to 10 million years ago. Monitor the growth of your hominids as you traverse, explore, survive, and evolve through time. Carry on your knowledge and discoveries to the new evolved generation. The game is slow-paced because of its “help yourself” idea and might feel frustrating sometimes. With the numerous possibilities, you can surely grind a good chunk of hours.Ancestors has a slow-paced complex gameplay that might feel frustrating over time. The gameplay might vary according to your playstyle. If you want to stay close to the settlement and increase your domestic skills, then your gameplay might omit danger from wild animals and fear of the unknown. Migrating your settlement to search the unfamiliar lands might inflate tremendous danger and can wipe your entire lineage. The controls feel too complex and are not fun. Climbing and swinging through the trees is frustrating. Most of the time, you will experience difficulty locating the next branch to jump on, as the tree positioning is weird and poorly made. One button can perform multiple operations, which can result badly in certain situations. You are supposed to educate the species about every possible useful kind of stuff, from sticks to rocks to edibles. Establishing communication between the clan is very important, as you will need to switch characters to keep the evolution going. The idea presented is pretty good, but it lacks proper execution.  The graphics are not bad, neither wondrous, but they are quite enjoyable and don’t affect the gameplay. It lacks details in the interaction of characters with the environment. It looks more of an old game instead of a new-gen game. Keeping in mind that this is a new concept game and the development team had limited funds at that time, this is quite promising. The map is enormous with numerous focal points , and also very diverse flora and fauna. Some of the effects like fear of the unknown and infection are pretty good. But somehow, these above-average graphics require good GPU power, which is quite unusual. The cinematics are top-notch with great story portraits and realistic quality graphics. Little things like dream showcases and animal fight cinematics bring an extra level of detail to the game.Don’t rush things, learning is a slow process. Most of the time, you will have to figure out the solution yourself. Turning down the music will help a lot, as most of the actions in-game are executed on a beat. Without spoiling too much, we can say that both hands are useful and can craft wonders. Most of the players neglect to carry a child, but actually, they provide you extra experience, and you can carry up to 2 of them. This is an interesting detail of the game that you will undergo during the exploration of new regions. When you are away from your familiarized territory, your character will feel scared and might enter the state of hysteria. This will result in losing your current clan member, and you will return to your main settlement. To conquer this, focus on your senses and identify the elements nearby. If your hominids recognize them, he will feel confident and will calm itself.The game’s objective is to finish the evolution before the actual time that was taken according to history. So your first objective is to enhance your species and not a sole character. Tarrying on one character will influence your progress and might back-fire. Keeping the clan guarded and prosperous is your foremost goal. This concept certainly raises our expectations and makes us biased towards the game. The story should have been stretched to the start of human civilization, but it ends at a generation switch that feels incomplete. It provides a mesmerizing experience to the gamers. Recommended buying during a sale.Rating: 7/10Reviewer:  Walking on two feet.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: 9/10. Buy it if you can make the commitment to playing it the way it was meant to be played.Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey is a very unique game on the market. It follows the idea of human evolution. As the player, you are responsible for taking your clan of hominids from something very similar to a chimpanzee to ♥♥♥♥ ergaster, which was supposedly a precursor to ♥♥♥♥ sapiens, and everything in between.I highly encourage you to play this game without looking up any hints online. The idea of this game is that you can use your own human learning to discover new things about this game, which is represented by your evolutionary progress. The process is very immersive, and a great many things can simply be figured out by using your innate ability as a modern human to learn new things.The game very much rewards you for playing in the way that you want to play. If you often try to intimidate predators, you will get better at intimidating predators. If you do so in a group, you will get better at communication. If you often hunt with tools, it will become easier for you to make tools. If you prefer to dodge out of the way of predators rather than attack, you'll become more proficient in that too.The process for evolving is very easy to understand. Doing activities matures neurons and gives you neuronal energy to develop them into new abilities. When passing a generation, you can reinforce a certain number of those abilities so that the neurons don't need to be developed again (this is usually equal to the number of kids in your clan). Finally, an evolutionary leap will allow you to leap many thousands of years and allow you to develop genetic mutations that have come up throughout the generations.There are only a few minor complaints I have with this game. First, the AI of your fellow clan members is abysmal. They don't eat unless you eat around them or give them food directly. Even while you're away from your settlement, your fellow clan members just stand there and don't take care of themselves at all. They don't even sleep at night. In addition, the combat is entirely reactive. There's no ranged combat, either. I would have loved to be able to throw a rock at the crocodile waiting at the bottom of the tree for me, or throw my sharpened stick at the gazelle that was yet unaware of me, but no such ability exists. Perhaps that's intentional. Lastly, I would have loved to be able to play as ♥♥♥♥ ergaster! We do get to see what they look like in the ending cinematic but it's not possible to play as them. I do partially understand this though, because the ability to control fire would radically change the dynamic of the game. My hope is that the developers could make either an expansion or a sequel so we can continue to evolve.Many people have complained about the controls of this game, but I played this game for 72 hours with a keyboard and never found them to be a problem. Some might prefer to use a controller, however.Pros:- Great visuals- A great many opportunities to exercise the innate abilities of your own human brain- You're rewarded for nearly everything you can do- Intuitive evolution system that gives the game a cycle and makes it fun to learn new abilitiesCons:- Horrible AI for clan members, they're basically useless- Combat is totally reactive- Inability to play as the final evolutionOverall, this game easily receives a 9/10 from me. Progression is slow, but it is steady. Making discoveries feels just as rewarding for the player as it does for the character. If you're willing to make the commitment to learning, absolutely buy this game.

_childDocuments_.review: In an industry saturated in sequels, re-releases and bald-faced ripoffs, this game gets my thumb-up just for representing a new IP with a novel premise.And yet, sadly,  isn't something I can recommend to everyone... because it isn't for everyone. Going into this with expectations that you're about to play a typical open-world survival game is a sure road to disappointment.  is willfully, stubbornly esoteric; even the HUD doesn't provide any comforting familiarity and will take some time to understand, playing into the game's overarching theme. That theme is discovery, and as a reflection of it, the gameplay is alien and somewhat impenetrable. The game won't hold your hand much, and you must largely figure things out on your own.What do you get if you manage to overcome 's initial curve? You get about 50-60 hours of pleasant ambient exploration, some lessons in anthropology, surprisingly cathartic kill animations, and the simple joy of hearing baby chimpanzee squeaks wherever you go.Full disclosure: I took a few courses in anthropology during college. The foreknowledge it gave me might count as cheating at this game. It also means I knew what a sahelanthropus was before playing , and if that doesn't earn me nerd cred, I don't know what will. But I swear to all the gods, the next one of you that calls the player characters "monkeys" is getting a lecture!

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly ,I should be paid for this amount of effort. Its actually taking a mental load on me to describe how/why this game is so bad. I wish I could just say "It's boring!" Or "its too hard!" but that wouldnt do this game the justice it deserves. This game is one of the most insulting wastes of my time/money I have ever experienced.The game is trying to do too much. Each button controls wayyyy too many things, and each of things are context dependent. The game cannot stop tripping over itself when trying to determine what object you want to interact with and how you want to interact with it in a sea of objects. All it takes is two thing to be too close and the entire game sh*ts the bed. The movement/travel is really where it lost me because the game becomes unplayable. So you cant walk on the ground for too long because you have to watch out for predators and its too slow, so you take to the trees right? Hahaha WRONG IDIOT. You see, if you fall from too far you get injured or die. Makes sense, however, all the branches you can grab are past the danger height, and they all point up making you go HIGHER. So you're constantly moving up and being at more risk, not to mention going to the top is asking for an eagle to get you. There is no way to traverse the trees practically because you cant move forward, you can only go go UPPPPPP only to then come all the way back DOWNNNNNNN having spent like 2 minutes to move a few feet forward on the map and you find yourself asking what the hell am I doing with my time?Imagine a game like Spiderman where you swing around in a sort of arc pattern. Going up an down, but playing with your momentum to ultimately go forward. Same with Assassins Creed. Sure there are reasons to climb up to the top of something, whether to get a better vantage point or just so see how high up you can reach, but there is a means to travel distances. Structures that were built with the intention of allowing the character to move forward smoothly. Not in this game. No, you climb up and half the branches are just dead ends. You cant jump to anything else or climb higher so you have to climb all the way back down and find another possible route.Swinging from the foliage puts your camera INSIDE the foliage so you cant SEE anything from that point, leaving you to just guess where the best spot might be. God forbid you end up where three branches meet or your character will have a confusion induced seizure and fall out of the tree in an attempt to escape this god awful game he's stuck in. I know its a survival game but good lord the amount of maintenance you have to do makes the game such a chore. The time between needing to eat/sleep/drink needs to be drastically extended. YOu already cant move around well, so take the amount of time you waste trying to navigate the trees and add onto that needing to eat and sleep/ plus the injuries you sustain from inevitable falling from the trees or getting attacked by something, plus the rain and night time cold depleting your stamina AND fear of the unknown stopping you from getting places, the game essentially gets in its own way over and over AND OVER againI love the concept, but would I recommend? No. HELL NO. NEVER could I recommend this game to a friend, and I'll tell you why. Because only a nerd like me who is fascinated by the concept of this game will deal with the mind numbingly frustrating issue with gameplay. I dont even know if I'll be able to finish it.Good luck! I'm insainly pissed off atm so take that into consideration)

_childDocuments_.review: Ancestors: The Human Odyssey is an interesting game that follows a possible history of the evolution of early hominids of the human lineage. You can tell that the game is very much made by former Assassin’s Creed developers based on how you traverse the trees early on, so it has decent developer lineage.  Has very minor spoilersPros:Unique gameplay:  While it has an obvious AC lineage, it s a very unique implementation and gameplay compared to your bog standard AC or Arkham or clone. Beautiful graphics and scenery:  It is a gorgeous game with tons of foliage and well-designed animal and hominid models.The sensory detection:  The game has the “sensory” mode where you can mark things via sight, sound or smell.  Some things are easier to detect one way than the other and provides extra game choice in how to keep appraised of your surroundings.The neuronal/generation/evolution system is very interesting and rather unique way to employ for lineage improvements (a type of level up system) that affects your current abilities for current generations, next generations, and for the evolution (long term) ways.Once you get use to the traversal, it is for the most part well done.  Swing from branches and jumping from tree to tree is fairly seamless once you understand the mechanics.The protection (medicine) and crafting (weapon/tool) system is fairly simple once you understand it but makes things more involved. The feat system to compete/increase your development/evolution speed when compared to what science reports for development/evolution speed is an interesting way to do the “be better than history” that historical fiction games often have.Cons:Fairly player unfriendly when you first start, even with the tutorial.  There are many mechanics it basically does not explain at all nor what prompts and signals mean or how to react to them.   You will likely die a couple of times before you figure out the combat/dodge/jump system cues. Alterations and tool/construction is very unintuitive and will likely cause frustration until you understand how it works.Meteorite system is not explained well or how/when to best use them.The objective system was added post launch and not well integrated and will give you objectives you have already done if you ignored them.The game mechanics are rather simple and repetitive once you get them down.  The later parts of the game (particularly the canyon/desert/beach) feel VERY empty and unfinished compared to the earlier parts.  It seems the dev team spent most of their time on the jungle and savanna areas.Ground level rocks suck.  The climbing mechanics really needed to be better optimized to not climb ground level rocks.The Astute Dominator Feats are horribly implemented.  They are not needed to complete the game or even the achievements but if you want to 100% they will take the majority of your time.   Otherwise the game is fairly quick to run through with even getting all achievements likely only to take 20 or 30 hours to get once you know what you are doing.  At least double that if you want the dominator feats though.TL;DR – A niche game that if you like anthropology, evolution and Assassins Creed, might interest you.   Sadly it is a bit user unfriendly in a not Souls/Rogue-a-like good way and has some major slog issues if you want to 100% complete it.  Get it on sale (like right now when it is 10 dollars), but probably not worth the full price.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a tentative recommendation, honestly. The concept is really cool and if you're into fairly chill games with casual mechanics and/or survival you'll probably enjoy it.That said - the implementation needs work. Getting around in trees is made much harder because of the poor limb-to-limb navigation controls. You'll constantly be jumping down to receive your broken legs. Sometimes if you get into combat too close to a tree or wall you'll get stun-locked and unable to see what's happening. The controls are often just annoying (constantly swapping what is in which hand), some of the crafting you'll miss (basalt and granite are different and make different objects, but look almost exactly the same), the monke AI is really stupid, and some mechanics are poorly explained.Once you figure out the core gameplay loop about 2 hours or so in, that's really it. There's nothing else to experience and it's mostly a grindy exploration simulator.I enjoyed my time, but after about 60% through and on the third to last species, I think I'm already finished. It's just too much grind. Neither the gameplay nor progression are enough. A game this simple should not take 40 hours to beat.

_childDocuments_.review: Once you get past how obtuse the game is you start to understand it, and I have to admit the devs did a good job of making you feel like a dumb monkey whose brain is evolving. It's really hard at first, you're trying to get comfortable with the controls (KB+M purists stay away, you NEED a controller for this) and your monkey clan barely has any capabilities. But train yourself to get those neurons firing and you can eventually make spears with ease, scaring off predators with your monkey gang. But I can't stress enough that the game really doesn't spell most things out for you. If you're not willing to put in the hours learning its systems (and maybe a little research into how to play) you're going to have a bad time. Don't worry about managing your tribe's resources, their meters freeze as long as they're not being controlled and aren't following the monkey you're controlling.  So I'd recommend if you're a survival game fan who wants to jump from trees and run from or fight predators predators as you explore a pre-historic map.

_childDocuments_.review: Whoever commissioned, greenlit, and designed a company splash animation of a jump scare of a moose being run over should never be allowed to touch video games again.Just trying to get into the game requires sitting through so much pretentious nonsense, including credits for all the people involved in the game, probably because they know if they don't assault you with it from the beginning, no one would see them due to lack of caring enough to check them out from the settings.The game tries so hard to sell itself as some sort of 'experience' with an epic monologue intro to set the scene that only accomplishes getting a cringe response at how hard its trying to sell itself as more than a modern ripoff of Tokyo Jungle,After seeing the icon used to depict Left and Right click I almost puked, it is by FAR, the WORST way to depict left and right mouse buttons in any video game ever made, combined with the arts and farts intro monologue, and the opening credits to the 'developers' its obvious no one working on this game has ever  a game before, and that they're not even trying to make a game. This is an art student 'experience', not a game, and not one I want to bother spending more time on than I already have. The controls and gameplay are so clunky and counter-intuitive, it feels less like being a monkey fighting for survival, and more like trying to wrestle a monkey for your own survival. You have to fight almost every instinct learned from any other game, and try not to develop RSI trying to learn how the controls and mechanics are intended to work. I truly cannot stress enough how much this does not play like any other video game, and that is an insult, not a compliment. Prompts will for example tell you to press a button to 'remember' something, however this does not change if you already remember that thing, meaning you instead forget it. The only time the prompt changes is immediately after you 'remember', so if you leave an area and try to follow the 'remember' prompt, you will just forget the things you previously added to your memory, It's gameplay aspects like that that really indicate lack of awareness as to what a game does versus what a game needs to do. If you're trying to innovate and create a new experience, do so with the options in actions in the game NOT through trying to reinvent the wheel by giving them bumps in the form of completely warping controls and core gameplay mechanics anyone who  played a single video game before is familiar with. A completely backwards approach to innovative game design.This will definitely be enjoyable for the kind of steam user who loves games like The Witness, where the game is more about taking in the beautiful graphics and being left alone to explore and enjoy the game without popups and menus, but do not be deceived by the 'hehe monke' reviews thinking you'll play a monkey roleplay survival experience, or an upgrade to the gameplay you would find in Tokyo Jungle. If you want a  that focuses on generational survival where you can play as a monkey, just go emulate Tokyo Jungle, and stay away from this up-its-ass interactive ''retelling of the story of evolution''

_childDocuments_.review: It's a bit hit 'n' miss. (there should be a 'mediocre' option rather than just positive/negative. This one's in the middle) On one hand it's quite and interesting in that you can see your little moneys progress slowly through evolution and all that, but on the other hand, you don't have any means of saving the game and there are mechanics and other aspects to the game that can ruin your experience, like trees. Sounds silly, but you'll be climbing trees a lot being a monkey and all, but it's such an awkward mechanic, that being in the trees will be a reccuring cause of death. You can hardly see whare you want to go, and you don't always jump in the exact direction or distance you want in order to not fall to your death.Another pain point, is in regards to predators.and dodging/fighting them. The whole mechanic is too basic. You don't really have any control and there will be times where, you'll find yourself with your friend monkeys, being pounced by not 1, 2, 3, or 4, predators, at once, but 5 predators all at the same time, at various locations on the food chain, yet because you're at the very bottom, and despite your friends, everything all wants to eat you at the exact same time. It's good, until it's not. Then it's an 'alt-f4' experience, and you'd better not hesitate else you'll reload and find hal;f your monkeys and baby monkeys are dead, because you didn't alt-f4 in time to prevent the game from retarding out.Honestly, if you're considering picking this title up, think about how you'll go about extracting/backing up save files, so if the game decides to go 'full r3tard' you can load it back.Thus far I've not done it myself, but it's now a priority for me to find out how, because I'd very much like to be able to 'enjoy' the game. Another suggestion would be to use CheatEngine to manipulate gameplay speed. Honestly, I couldn't imagine playing this game a x1 speed (*except during quicktime, which is practically every mechanic in-game besides walking). Walking, swinging, eating, drinking. All of these tasks take far too long to complete where you're spending a minute at a time waiting for ape-man to fill his belly, with the same slow cinematic/sequence. I usually stroll/walk at 1.5, 1.8 or 2x speed, and then bump up to 3x speed to eat and drink.Without CheatEngine I wouldn't waste my time, literally.

_childDocuments_.review: DISCLAIMER: THE ENDING OF THE GAME IS VERY UNSATISFYING: You only get a short animation of neanderthals walking. And then it ends. Very boring ending. Not worth all the effort to get to it.The game is fun and enjoyable for a while, you discover new things and slowly progress, dodging predators, then scaring them off, then killing them. The game at first plays like an adventure/discovery game. The game is all about discovering new things and "progressing". Once you get to the final area of the map though, the beach, the game stagnates. You realise there is no more new content left, and you now have to go back to all the previous areas to unlock every "evolution point" to evolve. These include things like, killing all animal types, dodging all animal types, using all healing plants, intimidating all animal types, etc... This is not fun at all, and even annoying like it was in my case, trying to get a white rhino to spawn for hours so I could kill it to evolve. And after all that work, you're rewarded with a short animation of neanderthals taking a few steps. No gameplay, no big cutscene, no in-game scripted event to end the game with, no playing as a neanderthal, no making fire. Also you never get to make proper tools. The furthest extent tools go is "sharpened stick" and rocks. You don't get to make a spear with a flint head. No fire-making. So the ending of the game is truly unsatisfying. However you will have good fun for 20 hours as you discover the game. So I'd say it's worth it on a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Playing this game is like watching a Discovery Channel documentary. You start out as a helpless monkey trying to figure out how to use a stick with nothing but your wits and a strong will to survive. But within minutes you've discovered the magic of the pointed stick and suddenly you're the jungle's alpha predator, killing everything in your path. It's like a real "Survivor" series. It's like real life, but with less paperwork and more animal blood.But the real highlight of this game is the sense of power and accomplishment you feel as you progress through the evolutionary stages. I stopped for months, then started again and wondered why I was doing this to myself again. But every time there's that "aha" moment and I break through on my own, it adds to that sense of personal accomplishment. You will feel like a god among beasts.This game is criticized by people who are used to having a glowing arrow with a path to every important location, piece of gear, mission, etc. This isn't that kind of game. This is a survival game designed to make you think. You have to put yourself in the monkey's shoes and think as if you were a real early hominid trying to discover everything around you. It's fun to do something as simple as take the cubs to a meteor location to get that extra boost for the next generation. However, every time your clan is decimated because you didn't do something right, you have to start over or face the consequences of failure later. This definitely adds to the replay factor, especially when you're trying to figure out almost everything on your own.Overall, this is a good game, but it's not for the faint of heart. If you are looking for a game where you can unleash your inner wild and take over the animal kingdom, then this is the game for you.Ancestors is not only an exciting gaming experience, but also educational. The game is based on real scientific research, and the developers have done an excellent job of incorporating this knowledge into the gameplay. As you progress through the game, you will learn more about human evolution and the various challenges our ancestors faced during their development. It's like taking a crash course in anthropology and archeology without having to sit through boring lectures.In addition, the game also provides players with a lot of information about the different species and ecosystems, so it's a great way to learn more about the different animals and plants of the prehistoric era, as well as the dynamics of the environment in which they lived.All in all, Ancestors: A Human Kind Odyssey is not only a fun, challenging, and enjoyable game, but also an excellent way to learn about the history of our species in an interactive and engaging way.One silly thing is, if you don't do it first, your tribe won't eat or drink even if it's important.

_childDocuments_.review: Well this is something you won't find anywhere else, 'monkey simulator 2020'. In saying that, this is a niche game and will appeal to only a select few, so ignore the majority of the negative reviews as they are nit picky. We get to play as monkey people millions of years ago as they start making their way toward human evolution. This is done through exploration of the environment and your monkey's skills with the addition of raising your monkey families. So what does this mean for the game overall? Grindy grindy grindy! It's a constant battle of trial and error, of which the consequences from mistakes can be dire to say the least. That exploration is what makes this game fun. I highly recommend going into this one blind and without walkthroughs, because the discovery aspect is what creates the enjoyment. The satisfaction is real as you discover new ways to survive and move along the evolutionary chain.Most peoples biggest gripe with this game is the controls. I'll say this, if a game opens with “best experienced with a controller”, then don't use a mouse and key board! Playing the actual game does come with a steep learning curve, but the in-game tutorial holds your hand enough to keep the pace moving while not revealing too much. At first it's extremely tense as you are constantly being hunted down by predators, always playing on the back foot, constantly in survival mode. However, after you get into a groove in regards to the overall formula, you can really start to dominate each region you take over. Once you hit that aforementioned groove, the tension dies right down and overall game-play becomes very placid. At this point you really need to be the 'sim enthusiast' type to enjoy the game as there is a lot of rinse and repeat. Even if you're not that type of player, what saves the game is the very nice visuals and expansive environment that is always open to explore.Like I said above, this game does not cater for everyone as it is very particular with what it's trying to achieve. But it hit's the mark with what it tries to achieve, even if it's not for everyone. I did find the novelty wearing off at the end of my run, but that was after 20 odd hours of game-play. Well worth the price if it interests you as you won't find anything else like it.

_childDocuments_.review: imagine hideo kojima wanted to make a game solely about being an ape and this is what you'd get. for better or worse, there truly is no other game like it. i really liked this game but it has one glaring issue - how it ends. i remember wishlisting this before release but didn't actually get it until it was featured in a humble monthly, and i just got around to playing it. you get thrown in with basically zero direction so you have to fend for yourself, which i really liked. though you really don't need any direction, you just play, survive, and evolve. it's been out for over two years and there are plenty of other reviews that can go into better detail than i can, so after repeating that i thoroughly enjoyed every minute i spent playing, i'll tell you what i really hated.. you can't complete it.. or at least i couldn't. maybe with prior knowledge and proper planning someone could, but i didn't have that luxury on my first playthrough. i didn't know the game has a hard stop after you get to a certain point in your evolution, and you need to evolve in order to lock in genetic mutations (basically perks/traits). there aren't any achievements related to this, or any missable achievements for that matter, but i would've kept playing to unlock all the genetic mutations and evolution feats. yet i literally can't. evolving leads to the credits with the only viable option to reload. so, that sucks. i'd love to see a patch or mod to fix this.

_childDocuments_.review: It's an interesting idea but ends up pretty shallow and repetitive. _childDocuments_.review: The concept of the game is great, but the gameplay completely falls apart. Simply said, Ancestors is an open world survival game. You eat, drink, procreate, sleep, fight, craft and go out exploring (not essentially in this order). Sounds fun? Maybe in the first 5 hours or so, before you realize those are all the actions the game has to offer. You repeat this set of actions on different parts of the map until you make enough discoveries that make you and your clan evolve through million of years. Most of these actions can be done by simply holding down a button, while some like fighting only include one boring QTE. Sprinting and jumping is tied to the same button and often lead me to some risky moments when I didn't want to jump off the tree but I did and got injured. Overall commands feel really clunky and not intuitive.The tutorial is mostly lacking and doesn't really explain things well, which can result in some confusing moments when the game asks you to do something, but you have no idea where you should start. Even the UI is so minimal that during the first hours you will have an hard time understanding your stats and the useless radar on the corner.The progression system is disappointing and completely defeats the game purpose. After million of years you are supposed to evolve and retain what you learned, instead you are forced to restart with mostly your basic skills and grind all over again. Every time you evolve you respawn on a random location that you previously explored, meaning you can be brought back to any of your first explored areas and will need to move to your latest ones if you want to continue discovering new lands. Having to restart from distant locations not only is time consuming, but it's also quite frustrating. Unfortunately, the world around you stays exactly the same with no variation after million of years and the same goes for animals.Clan growing options are disappointing too. You can make them follow you but they are completely brainless and most of the time they will just stare at a predator coming for them instead of getting on a tree like I do. This means that bringing your clan with you while exploring can be completely annoying as you have to do lot of baby sitting and if they die you will lose "points" when evolving or possibly risk a game over due to extinction. Even after evolving they never really help you in any crafting or fighting activity; you need to put items on their hands so they can replicate what you do. So while you evolve they basically stay the same, unable to do anything on their own without your commands.The open world looks good and has different biomes, but it's maybe too big and there is not enough variety of content. There are only a few animals and hostile predators, some food and a few materials to craft. For some reason they didn't add snakes on trees, which makes them the safest way to move around the map (although not always will be possible).In conclusion, Ancestors is the classic game that looks great from the trailers and probably for the first ten hours too, but just like you learn how to survive and discover new lands, you will also unveil the hidden repetitiveness of the gameplay and the pointless progression system. Fair warning: while I didn't play the game 'til the end and probably never will, I have to admit that the ending I saw online could have gotten me mad, particularly after 40+ hours of gameplay. I don't recommend the game, but if you are still going to play it I strongly suggest to avoid wasting much time on it.

_childDocuments_.review: Totally unique, a vast land to discover, hunt, gather, build, communicate, have children, befriend outsiders, evolve.I have never played anything quite like this before. You start as an early ape like species with no knowledge of your surroundings or your own abilities. This is really a game of learning how to play the game. There are no tutorials. You have to figure things out for yourself but that is also part of what makes it a really interesting experience. Its also what makes it hard at first.Trying to survive in a hostile environment is no easy task. You are always having to balance risks with potential rewards. Stray too far from clean water or food and you could starve to death. Eat the wrong food and you could end up disorientated and lost. Fall too far or get attacked by a hostile creature and your injuries could be fatal or leave you bleeding to death or with broken bones. Slowing you down. Making you an easier target. You could lose everything you have worked for. That is unless you managed to find a mate and had children with who can pass on your genes and your skills.There are planned sequels to this game as the evolution of the species doesn't take you all the way to modern humans. Hopefully they will be made.This is another highly recommended game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the most disappointing gaming experience I have ever had. I majored in anthropology, it is my absolute favorite subject and I have always lamented the fact that there are very few games set in prehistoric times. I was excited to try this out and gave it a fair chance, but it is filled with so many irritating bugs and amateur design choices that the game winds up being a total mess.From the outset the game blatantly lies to you: it recommends you play with a controller. Don't. The controls are absolute garbage. Then the game further insults you by presenting the most obnoxious tutorial I've ever experienced. Text boxes will pop up on the screen to explain mechanics the first time you do something. The game doesn't pause so you can read it, the text boxes move randomly across the screen for no reason, and the text is written in such poor English that google could have done a better job of translating it. The devs should be embarrassed to make this the first impression of their game. Moving text boxes? WHY?I almost uninstalled after that but decided to give it a second chance. This time using the keyboard and skipping the tutorial and going straight to survival mode. The game is unbearably easy. It's boring to the point of tears. There's nothing to do but eat food and wander around looking for landmarks to activate the meteorites. This is where the game completely falls apart. The only real objective you have in this game: search out meteorites to facilitate your evolution is frustrated by the fact that your only indication where these meteorites are, a black plume of smoke, is temporary. This obligates you to go get them as soon as they spawn because if you don't it's a tedious chore to search them out. Did you want to explore this cave? Did you want to build up stockpiles of supplies? Did you want to play an open world game at your own pace? Too ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ bad because you are obligated to play the game at the pace the devs intended. But what was their intention? Who the ♥♥♥♥ knows because it's a sandbox open world game and guessing the devs intentions is not interesting or dynamic gameplay.The final straw for this mess was having an ability downgraded mid-game. This is a design decision I simply cannot fathom. Up until I evolved to Orrorin I was able to intimidate animals simply by right-clicking when anything was near me. In fact, if something was off-screen about to attack a following ape, I would be alerted to it and be able to intimidate immediately. For some reason, the ability changes from a 1-button mechanic into a 3-button mechanic and no longer automatically activates when near an animal, thus giving predators an advantage over you that they didn't have in the early game. Apparently this mechanic is supposed to allow you to "sneak" by enemies, however this is completely irrelevant due to the ease of the game thus making the change mid-game objectively a downgrade. Stupidest ♥♥♥♥ I have ever seen in a video game.

_childDocuments_.review: What can be said about this game.  From a technical stand point the game is beautiful,  The Control scheme follows what can best be described as what you would see in the Assassin's creed type game.  But this game also borrows a lot of other aspects as well from those games.  The understanding of history, understanding evolution and forging your own path forward.  Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey isn't a game about what is, it's a game about what if.  Use your mind, and a lot of things will become evident, use your senses to understand your surroundings, and with understanding your surroundings you better understand yourself and which direction you want to take.  The game doesn't hold your hand.  Sure there are systems in place, but those systems basically define life, who lives, who dies.  in this game it really is about the survival of the fittest.  So ask yourself.  How will you evolve, and how will you rule the jungle.

_childDocuments_.review: Bought Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey wanting to scratch my Stone Age survival itch not realizing the game ends once you become ♥♥♥♥-Ergaster meaning you spend the whole game as an Ape/Ape-man and this certainly made me sad but I ended playing the game all the way through and beat it. While it's not a perfect game at all I found myself enjoying swinging from the branches and exploring the MASSIVE game world.The Good stuff: - Fun Ape antics such as swinging on branches and climbing EVERYTHING- Exploration is quite fun and each location is unique or at the very least distinct- Each biome is unique and introduces new creatures and challengesThe Bad stuff:- Survival in the beginning/mid-game is ridiculously easy, animals will hit you once and run off meaning combat is easily survivable.- Combat becomes trivial once you master the timing (and it only gets easier as you evolve). My ape from 10 MYA to 1 MYA was a one man extinction machine with only a rock and a wooden spear. It's the ultimate combo.- Who in God's name thought making your company's visual credit (which plays at full blast when you start the game) a jump scare was a good idea. Yeah I'm docking Good Game Points over this because it's obnoxious.In conclusion I'd recommend this if you love Human Anthropology or expansive exploration games.As a note to the Devs I think this game, despite it's low points, is quite entertaining and I'd love to see either a sequel or DLC which let's you play as ♥♥♥♥-Habilis up to ♥♥♥♥ Sapien; this would be something I think many would be interested in, especially if you're given the choice to play as some of Humanity's cousins such as the Neanderthals or Denisovans.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun game but after a point it becomes tedious. Explore, Find Food, Add new traits. Evolve. Spend 15 minutes finding mates for your apes, have them mate... Rinse, repeat. Rinse, repeat, rinse, repeat. Kept playing because I thought hey...they'll evolve to do this... but it quickly got bogged down into niggly bits like "attack just a tad faster" "Oh hey you run just a tad faster" Bleah. Granted this was fun for quite awhile and the game is merciless at making you figure out everything on your own (or you cheat and look online) but after a few evolutions it became. "Huh. All the fruit looks the same. Oh look a different colored saber tooth. Oh look a different colored snake..."The scenery though is amazing.Either way this is an "old product" where people have already played the heck out of it last year--so this review might not be worth the read.Wait for this in the bargain bin before picking it up.[Edited as follows]Note on play time: Brush Fire near house, left game on. I'm gonna say I got about ~20-30 hours total play time. I stand by the arguement that play time does not equate to a great product. I still posit that if you read a book, find it really great at first then by the middle it downright turns into trash then it does not deserve a good review. Same applies to a game. Game concept is great. Scenery was awesome. Worked well for a screen saver on my compuer for a week while I was away. So well worth the price as a screen saver.
_childDocuments_.name: Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey

_childDocuments_.review: Fascinating game if you're into thinking about evolution at all. The idea that you and your apes learn together is neat to consider. Immersive, beautiful world and music that you can disappear into for hours. The tension of keeping yourself alive and monitoring those you bring with you keeps humming. How you regard the world around you determines your fate. Says it's best played with a controller but I've had zero issues with a keyboard and mouse, other than my own mistakes (watch your dopamine when trying to trigger fights, hysteria will get you killed). Early game is tough, every loss is tragic, 10/10 would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey

Very fun to swing around and leap through the trees while picking fruits to take to my monkey wife. Also, getting yeeted by an eagle the size of a truck is always a pleasant surprise. RIP Yu, he only wanted his meteorite shard back.
_childDocuments_.name: Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey

I like how the game doesn't hold your hand and things can be challenging to figure out in the beginning stages. I hope they make a sequel and do something interesting with a variety of things to do.

_childDocuments_.review: Compelling in many ways, especially the progression system, this game has frustrating controls which unfortunately make the act of controlling your character a bit of a chore and overall unpleasant. _childDocuments_.review: To the developers, the game is good and it has a lot of potential. I hope you guys don't give up on it. This game has heart. Here's a list of my opinions:- Graphics are alright, but if you have a pretty lit GPU, you'd probably want a little bit more out of it, Not a deal-breaker tho.- The controls are challenging, but it adds to the immersion. And by immersion, you might wanna see a few guides on YouTube. Just remember, you're a human being! You'll probably get the hang of it a lot faster than any ape. - If you are a fan of the Planet of the Apes movies, you would enjoy this game. But there are elements that I wish the game would have like a clash/union of 2 clans, a coordinated attack on an animal as a group. Or maybe see a few remnants of an old civilization lying around.. I'd love to see an ape scratch their head over an old and rusty AK-47, but yeah, that would be a stretch. - The developers don't need to make the game suuuuper realistic, so why not add a few bits of fun like drawing/scratching on the rock walls with a stone?? It might not be 'historic' but what the hecc do we know?! - More building please and a way to order other apes to build at a specific location. Why can't we use a rock to chip wood off of trees...

_childDocuments_.review: Very cool concept, and very challenging at first. You will waste a lot of time. I eventually found myself peeking at hints online, and it lead to a lot of HA! moments. If I had figured some of those things out on my own I would have felt quite satisfied with myself lol. Im not one to go looking for all the hints, hacks and tips in a game, I like to figure itout on my own and experience games as they were meant to be played. But I admittedly had to go look for some help with this one.A couple of things I dont really like about it:The game is not designed for keyboard and mouse. The PC controls are fairly cumbersome. The game itself still needs to "evolve" away from a controller. Controllers are for a lack of a better term, prehistoric...and this game is designed for a controller.Also, there is a lot of micro managing that needs done to keep your lineage rolling. You have to switch around to various members of your group quite a bit and do tedious things to keep it all going, without giving away too much. The game isnt going to help you much at all in terms of how to do anything, which is cool in a way. Its up to you to figure it out.Saying too much about specifics of the game will give things away, but I can say there are some aspects that are really cool and new that you will not find in any other game. They didnt copy much from other games, making this one feel like a whole new experience from other games I have played over the last 20+ years. All in all I would recommend it, but be warned it is quite challenging and you will likely find yourself looking for help online on how to do this or that. If thats not you and you like to figure things out on your own, you will enjoy a considerable challenge.
_childDocuments_.name: Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey

_childDocuments_.review: The camera's sensitivity will fly 360's around your character multiple times upon the smallest flex of your wrist on the 0 setting. Besides that, the controls are so asinine I can't imagine how even the developers themselves were able to play this. And the whole "no answers will be provided, figure it out yourself" thing would be a cool challenge so long as everything was intuitive... and it's NOT. The way you interact with things makes it insanely difficult for your character to learn anything or obtain mutations let alone craft literally anything. The hyper specific things you have to do with the objects you pick up in order to do anything with them takes an eternity no matter if you're on a keyboard or controller. To the point that I believe this game was originally meant to be in VR, and if it wasn't... I think it would be more playable if it was in VR! Just so it has a more intuitive and ethical control scheme that actually allows you to do the things you're meant to do. Otherwise having to use two of your real life hands to shift/click joysticks, shift/click the mouse, tap/hold several buttons, basically manipulating an entire NASA rocket console of command prompts for the littlest simplest things like looking around and identifying objects as well picking up and crafting with those objects is unplayable on top of the seizure inducing camera sensitivity. Terrible game, I get the immersion of being realistic but this is beyond realistic and needs to be severely simplified along with slowing the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ camera the hell down and turning off the brain dead motion blur so I can actually SEE things.

Theres no guide to the controls for mouse and keyboard and it seems like half the character actions are not even mapped (at least from what I could tell from trial and error).Beyond that, its got pretty clunky controls and gameplay regardless. _childDocuments_.review: This game is punishing, and doesn't hold your hand, but it is also one of the most unique and rewarding experiences I have ever had as a gamer.I hope to see DLC in the future that continues the gameplay into more modern progression, but I have over 80 hours in so far and still am working on finishing evolution and taking on the last the game has to offer.The world is huge, and there is a lot to figure out. _childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing... to me. But be warned, it's not for everyone. It will teach you important mechanics and the basics like staying healthy and alive, but read every tip box like it's the words of a God, they don't come often. Other than the most basic mechanics, the game will teach you nothing, but the world really is open. Trust your intuition. Check the Help section of the esc menu frequently. Once you unlock crafting, bang some rocks together and see what happens. Every recipe is for you to find, and if you think it'll work, it just might (with a little elbow grease).It's a hard game, with little ♥♥♥♥ to give if you sink or swim, but I think it might just be my favorite thing.From here, it's an Edit: I've finally put this game down, 136 hours and several weeks later. This game has a place in my heart and it will never leave. I hope to someday come back to this game, maybe in 10 years when Panache finally makes a second Ancestors game, and I've long forgotten how to play. Perhaps I'll rediscover my love for this strange game, in it's unique oddity. If there were rating stars, this would be an easy 5. Screw the game journalist idiots who gave this game 4/10 y'all didn't even try to learn.Another edit: I played the game all the way through 4 times on a keyboard&mouse, getting every achievement but the astute dominator ones. While it is surely different on a controller, I found the keyboard to be perfectly fine for making fine movements in tense situations.

_childDocuments_.review: 9.3/10Without a doubt the greatest experience I've ever gotten out of a game so far. A hidden, underappreciated, and underrated gem. I'm of course going to be biased here since paleoanthropology and primatology have always been personal interests of mine.Even the concept by itself is shamelessly unique, but Panache really pulled out all the stops with executing it as well. I honestly wish I could forget the experience to play it again entirely blind. The aesthetics, the unorthodox and challenging gameplay mechanics, the expansive and exceedingly detailed setting in Miocene Africa, the lack of guidance provided to the player, all of it has clearly been thoroughly thought out and near-flawlessly executed. Everything works in tandem and forces the player to think like their ancestors in order to survive. The player needs to explore, expand, adapt, and evolve, if they want their lineage to continue.My biggest piece of advice into anyone looking to play this masterpiece of a game is to look up as little as possible. Learn as much as you can through personal experimentation, observation, active thinking to solve the situation you find yourself in - and to some extent, trial and error. Potential downsides for some: Somewhat grindy (I don't mind this personally but many do); almost no direction given to the player, they are left to do their own exploring and learning of the sometimes unintuitive mechanics (this is a feature I actually adore, given how well it simulates the confusion and survival mentality of ancient Miocene apes, but I can certainly see why it might put off a lot of people); and very little replay value (this is the one that really stops it from being a 10/10 for me, playing the game a second time will never truly feel close to the first time I explored the map and learned new mechanics). All in all, a fantastic game. Look up as little as possible, and give this one a try, especially if you're into anthropology, human evolutionary history, and more science/history oriented games.Some suggestions for improvement:1. Randomly generated environments. While the map in this game is absolutely huge and by itself presents a challenge and visual spectacle for the player, it can become repetitive once you're already familiar with it. This is especially problematic for players who have explored the entire map and haven't yet finished the game - or players revisiting the game after having finished it before (this links back to what I said before about replay value). This game would 100% benefit from at least having an option for a randomly generated or semi-randomly generated environment. Even just adding this for the Survivor difficulty would be an amazing addition to the game without many downsides.2. Dynamic environments. Another minor issue I see with the game - although this is something that honestly didn't bother me while playing it, since the player is always moving through biomes which present new gameplay mechanics, challenges, and force the player to adapt in order to survive - is that while the player's clan evolves, the biomes do not. If at the end of the game, you choose to return to an older biome, nothing has changed, none of the animals have undergone any kind of evolutionary shift or counter-adaptation to the player, which might come off as unrealistic or a jarring waste of potential to some players. This is less of a problem and more of a missed opportunity, I suppose.3. Actual difficulty variation. The difficulty options when starting a game are rather shallow and deceiving, in that the only changes they actually offer are reduced UI (or no UI at all). There's no way to increase how deadly your adversaries are, or to increase the difficulty of accessing new skills/species. Ultimately this game would benefit from a more challenging mode wherein even experienced players will have a hard time surviving.
_childDocuments_.name: Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing but loses its honeymoon phase rather quickly. I would still recommend this game, however, because it is incredibly fun to play, the world is big and beautiful, and learning how to play it was a fun experience all on its own, but beware that it can become daunting and you may end up forcing yourself to finish it instead of doing so because it comes naturally.Learning, exploring, and running for your life made the first few hours of the game an amazing experience. I went in blind with almost no expectations and found the game to be incredibly satisfying. The movement systems were great once I learned them, the world was big and beautiful, and every time I learned something new I found myself feeling very rewarded.That all comes to a halt pretty fast. The list of items to interact with is incredibly small. As in: 6 tools that are of any use small, and you'll quickly find yourself wanting more diversity. I made the mistake of reading into the title too much, I had hoped the game would be about starting from an ape lost in the jungle and finding my way to becoming ever more human-like, with learning to make bigger and better tools and eventually building homes and more things of the sort along the way. Ancestors is not a game about going from ape to human, it's about going from ape to a more human-like ape. The basic gameplay loop stays the same and about 30 hours in I started to wonder if there was any point in continuing, I was just running around from waypoint to waypoint trying to unlock everything and starved for new things to discover.
_childDocuments_.name: Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey

_childDocuments_.review: This is an excellently fascinating game, though I recommend spending a few generations in the starting place, first, the jungle oasis settlement. Do not "discover" the jungle oasis for a few generations, and make sure you do not generation-forward before you find and recruit a few additional apes and manage the bonding for their unity with others.It bears mention that same-sex couples do appear to be able to be formed in this game, which I think is both accurate and awesome. However, it may not be wise to do so unless poly relationships can also be formed, given the importance of the ability to generate offspring.

Vibration is a huge part of the gameplay as a physical cue from dodging to attacking to crafting. You need it.

_childDocuments_.review: Great concept, great potential, but overall lacking.It's fun to play at first but it gets incredibly repetitive and boring after a while, almost looks like they stopped developing the game in the middle of the process. Going into this game I was expecting more things to unlock the more you evolve but that's not really the case. You evolve new traits and that's pretty much it.It's really challenging, which takes a major role on the fun in this game, trying to learn as if you were actually there trying to survive when you start since you aren't given really a tutorial, but the game tells you that.Never actually fully finished the game because, as I mentioned, it starts to get monotonous and isn't really enjoyable to play anymore.Overall, I like the game but I wouldn't say it's worth it paying full price for it.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay so here is my review after 25 hrs. This is normally the time frame that i feel i have seen and done enough to say something about the game. Although the game length says 50 hrs plus i am already on 25 hours and only gone up 3 times in generation and 1 evolutionTo the review.  7/10The graphics in the game really are lovely. They are not  amazing like major AAA publishers but the game has so many wonderful aspects that it all completes it. Dont get me wrong the scenary is beautiful and its all done so well but after all it is only jungle, rocks and so on but a beautiful landscape to explore.  8/10This is where it gets interesting. The devs have taken a survival game which has been very popular in the past few years and flipped it. Its nice to not have a narrative or  text to readthe HUD display is unique rather than bars and all sortsPlaying this period of time is beautiful so think we once was from this backgroundEverything about the way the game works is amazing and new.    7/10With pc the elite always push and prefer mouse and keyboard but we also want to use pc for the raw power and improved  graphics. Game pad is a must for this game and works well in my eyes. Sure like many 3rd person games sometimes you get in to a tight spot  and the mechanics shuffle and you need a couple moves like turning around on a branch of a tree or to pick something up, but its not game changing at all so dont read the comments, its mostly those who want to use a mouse and its a no go. Button config is perfect in my eyes with everything at reach and easy to follow with on screen help if you have hud on.     8/10There is no story as such and no really missions like many open world games. There are tasks and stuff to unlock and activate to proceed up the evolution but the game is set out beautifully along with the skill tree and evolution time line. When i played  this game it was a struggle but thats what its about.... evolution, the beginning so cleverly we tech monsters cant seem to work things out or impatient. It so lovely to pick something up and bash it, or combine it to work out what it does or makes it really feels like your leaning and become part of the game. Its a lovely genre to be part of and you get very connected with your characters. As babies with unique names they grow in to adults and then how sad to see them as elders only to eventually die and new family comes in. Its a special moment and along with the fundamental elements of evolution, it really makes you think. II spent so long and not gone really far at all just by enjoying the game what it offers only scratched the surface. I put the game off for months and while on sale i thought why not. Would u buy at full price, i think i would looking at how little i have done and time spend on it. Its a game that will be around for a while when i feel like the mood for it. It is emotional and nice to get away from all the shooters and other style of games out thereOverall solid 8/10
