_childDocuments_.review: Great setting, atmosphere and graphics, intriguing concept of how to explore and learn, fail and get better with every attempt. Developers did bring this approach to the very game itself, giving the player a hard time of not only mastering mechanichs and controls, yet also a hard time of even finding out the basics. Over time, this works out, and there are plenty of hints what to do and how, e.g. in the achievements you need to grow into a higher-evolved species.The two core items the game lacks is imho:- identification with individuals, as those are not playing too much of a role over time; as well as any achievements done by your tribe. Naturally, no great buildings, medals, equipment - what remains is in the player's memory, or sunken into the tribe's genes. Does fit to the game's concept, yet you need to be willing to only see your progress in form of the improved skills of your individuals.b) A development in the core game principles, the game concept along with your tribe. You can do basically anything from the start (though a decent percentage of it will not work out too well at the start, whereas the majority of the remaining tasks might kill you). Though once you master the "sharp stick" and worj as a "hunting group", the only ris ein challenge comes by ever greater opponents, yet relies on the very same principle for quite a big part of the game. A little bit of grind for food and neuronal energy (eqauls experience) included..Overall, some fresh and really striking ideas - with a small downturn in the mid- to late game motiviation. Still, definitely worth to be looked at for those captivated by new approaches - and games covering unusual ideas.
_childDocuments_.name: Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey

_childDocuments_.review: Great for 20 or so hours. The interesting content ran out after most of the ingame tips were applied. After that the game is repetitive and tedious. The programming for the AI monkeys to collect healing meds is hit-or-miss. It's frustrating because there are a ton of attacks that will then require healing and this collection is mostly done manually for the entire tribe. Exploring with the tribe was a pain until unlocking the counter-attack and group crafting perks and even after I had to do almost everything  while in combat because the AI is hit-or-miss.Before these traits were unlocked the monkeys would basically just get mauled over and over even if I climbed a tree and tried to regroup them into the tree. The AI was too stupid to climb the tree if my character was not past the programmed maximum distance threshhold, so if there aren't the tallest trees nearby to climb then the monkeys won't get to safety. This mechanic is worse the bigger the tribe gets and there was little point in climbing trees for safety when I had a maxed clan because there are usually a few monkey AI standing idle at the base of the tree seasoning themselves up for the tigers. Those monkeys then promptly get mauled and I have to scare away the predators or agro them to my character, bringing the monkeys back out of the tree and repeating the cycle. AI has the ability to switch hands when they're holding an object but they won't be able to eat or drink when they have something in their "active" hand. It requires telling them to switch hands or drop the item they're holding so they can grab and eat food. This overall feels lame, as I expected starving monkeys to decide to drop whatever they're holding to grab food on their own when the rest of the tribe is eating. That's what the whole game is supposed to be about, monkey see monkey do.There are a ton of unintuitive features in this game, but it was well worth what I paid for it on sale and the experience of discovering new things in this game was great. I could continue to evolve the tribe but I don't have plans to because it's a slog from here, and I'm convinced the best of the content has already been experienced at 26 hours in.

_childDocuments_.review: Possibly the greatest survival sandbox i have ever played and an amazing 3D platformer. The controls feel tight and fluid and do not do you the disservice of making navigation too easy. Sure you can traverse virtually any surface, but if the rock face has a fissure in it such that the rock above juts out above your head you will have to navigate a different way. The gameplay isnt like assasins creed where the points the character jumps to are always super precise and flawless in execution and require no more than the holding of a couple buttons; if you want to soar through the tree tops and leap from branch to branch in this game, you will need skill, timing, and the ability to make split second decisions that will either leave you swinging from the next limb or falling down through the canopy several dozen feet. And all that is just the core movement and navigation. This game is all about the joy of discovery and conquering the unknown, so i wont say much more about it other than it appears very well polished, highly functional and realistic, and suprisingly quite the thrill ride through and through. Honestly i was prepared for a more casual experience, but i was delightfully suprised by the amount of depth and inensity to be found. 10/10 would reccomend. Last note, there is a distinct lack of multiplayer support, and while this would be a great boon to the game i wouldnt want multiplayer support to sacrifice any of the  other amazing aspects of this game. Who knows what may happen when you wish upon a metiorite...
_childDocuments_.name: Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey

_childDocuments_.review: Don't listen to all the bad reviews, they are just people who don't understand what this game is really about. This game in my short time playing is cool and unique.many people are complaining about the controls being weird, well guess what, it tells you it is best played with a controller, so people complaining about weird controls with keyboard are morons. People complaining about unskippable cutscenes are either blind or lying, since you can skip all cutscenes except for the opening one.This game is meant to be difficult, it tells you it won't hold your hand through out it. You are meant to explore and try out new things in this unknown world, test different things, bang different types of rocks together, munch on the strange new fruit. This is a game of exploration and survival.The reason some things you can't do in the beginning is because you haven't unlocked it yet, you need to learn and reinforce the skills into your tribe of early Human ancestors. your meant to fail and then learn from those failures. I kept getting food poisoning from these berries in the first base area until I learned to look for the brighter pinkish red ones which were better to eat. I learnt bashing obsidian and Granite rocks can create a grinder which makes making a healing plant easier and more effective. A really cool thing I found out is you can throw things in your hand by holding down the button for altering (or dropping, Can't remember since it has been almost a day since I last played at the time of writing this) if you have nothing in the other hand.I give this game a solid 9/10.It looks great.It sounds great.The mechanics are solid.It is a very interesting concept and premise.This game is meant to be unforgiving, we are meant to fail and learn and try again. We are meant to explore and conquer our environment through trail and error. This is a true hardcore survival game, you will die, you will get hurt, you will get poisoned. But that is the point, you are meant to learn from it.Listening to the reviews with less then an hour in the game is pointless, as they have essentially only been in the gameplay section itself for like 10 minutes before giving up and whining about the game being hard and thus the game is garbage, rather then actually exploring and learning.

_childDocuments_.review: Very immersive, very unique! This game is all about exploration and discovery. There are no points, but it is so much more rewarding to parading your tribe of chimps on expeditions through the jungle, cliffs, lakes, etc. There is no main character, and you learn to use all of your chimps to their strengths and breed the most powerful breed with the mutations features! _childDocuments_.review: I do not recommend this game at full retail price, only when it is on sale for $20 or less. Please read my full review to understand why.A visually stunning adventure game that captures the essence of early human evolution. With a strong emphasis on graphics, gameplay, and atmospheric elements, the game aims to immerse players in a primal world of survival and adaptation. While it boasts several positive aspects, it also falls short in various key areas, leading to a mixed experience for players.Positive Aspects:- Visually stunning graphics that were groundbreaking for its time.- Engaging early gameplay that effectively captures the essence of evolution and adventure.- Diverse evolutionary paths that allow players to choose their playstyle and shape their tribe's destiny.- Impeccable attention to detail in animations and an immersive atmosphere amplified by ambient sounds and weather effects.Negative Aspects:-Dependency on player ignorance can lead to a lack of content for experienced gamers, resulting in a less satisfying experience.-Limited variety in gameplay mechanics, particularly in the number of structures and uses for collected items, diminishing the overall depth of the gameplay.-Inability to utilize critical evolutionary milestones such as fire, leading to missed opportunities and a less immersive experience.-Repetitive animations and environmental elements that detract from the overall immersion, despite attempts at realism.- Imbalanced traits system that incentivizes grinding over exploration, undermining the game's intended adventurous spirit.- Lack of depth in relationships and the absence of engaging quests, resulting in a less compelling narrative and gameplay experience.Conclusion:While Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey provides an engaging initial experience with its vivid world and immersive gameplay, it ultimately falls short in several key areas, hampering the overall enjoyment for seasoned players. Available at a discounted price, it serves as a worthwhile introductory experience, but the lack of content depth and repetitive gameplay elements may deter players from fully completing the game. Therefore, unless purchased on sale, the game may not be worth the full retail price, especially for those seeking a more immersive and dynamic gaming experience.Overall Score: 6/10 (based on its groundbreaking graphics and initial gameplay experience, but deductions for the lack of content depth and repetitive elements)

_childDocuments_.review: This is my first negative review in years. I had hoped this game was worth what I paid (full price), but even if it had been free I'd had put this down after 10 minutes too.After downloading and running the game there was a two or three minute wait sitting through credits and cut scenes, no music just the sound of a waterfall. Before any menu appears, the game says it's best played using a controller. Fair enough, I use keyboard and mouse and it's never been a problem, until now. For some reason the game decided I had a controller, which explains why "Press A" did nothing when I pressed the A key on the keyboard. Using ESC to get to settings helped, where I changed the input to keyboard and mouse. Why it defaulted to controller I have no idea - I don't use one.I get the impression there's supposed to be music, but even with all three volume sliders up to 100% there's no music. There's sound from moving etc. but no music.I was eager to get to grips with a game that won't hold my hand, but some basic pointers about how to control your character was definitely expected yet absent. The mouse moved the view around okay, but interacting with your surroundings was hit and miss with nothing to guide except "Q", "A", or "E" - which sometimes did nothing.I have hundreds of games from Steam, and I've never encountered issues like these. It's a real shame and I am very disappointed things fall apart right at the start of the game.YMMV, it's likely some settings.

_childDocuments_.review: I gave a negative review of this game at first. It is boring and repetitive to play after the 20 hour mark.So why did I change my mind?Well, it's an unusual game in that it's about us, we humans. As I played it I began to consider what our ancestors had to go through to get where we are today. It made me think about the skills we obtained over time and what skills or evolution we might take in the future.I changed my mind about this game because I didn't want to discourage other developers to make these types of games in the future.I finished the game to the end at 90 hours. It was a chore towards the end but for some reason I still kept going back and plugging at it to see where it would end up. What form of human it would be at the end.The environments were fantastic to be honest. So was the music. _childDocuments_.review: Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey is a survival game where you will lead your clan to the top of the food chain. In this game you will start playing as the Missing Links and slowly evolve through different hominid species. The game is overwhelming at first, but it becomes very enjoyable once you learn how to cover your basic needs and how to fight predators. I thought that the game would become repetitive after a few generation leaps, but the evolution system is designed in such a way that your tribe will make basic activities faster, so you may focus on developing your new skills and exploring new areas. For instance, as you develop your motricity skill you will walk faster and consume less energy while doing so.In summary, Ancestors has become one of my favourite games and I strongly recommed you to play this game. I hope that some day it receives a sequel where we play as the ♥♥♥♥ genus, master the stone crafting and the control of fire.

_childDocuments_.review: A cool game. But more for people that are into natural history and want to experience an approximation of what our ancestors went through. _childDocuments_.review: I'm going to set this as a yes because it is good fun activating some monkey neurons.But the more I play, the more the cons out-weigh the pros.But one of the biggest turn-offs in video games for me is when the devs try to boost the difficulty by spawning enemies behind you on a regular basis. You can put your back to a clear dead end, start crafting something, and within a minute you'll have a tiger spawned behind you and already locked on.There are just so many annoyances. _childDocuments_.review: There's been an influx these last few years, of games that look really interesting but have a steep learning curve before you can play and are not in any way user friendly. They're always highly rated, and it's a mystery as to why. This is 2021. If you can design an entire game, you can design a tutorial that makes sense. If you can't design a good tutorial, it's not a good sign for the rest of the game. The tutorial is the introduction, the hand-holding part of the game. It's meant to teach the player how to play. Unless your game is a standard shooter, your players need to be shown how to play.When games teach you about real life concepts, that's great. When a game assigns you homework in order to play, that's boring.For me, maybe my tutorial was broken. But it didn't provide the kind of guidance needed from a tutorial and I had no intention of wasting more time than I'd already spent looking up guides and watching Youtube videos.

_childDocuments_.review: This game doesn't lie when it says it won't hold your hand, but no one held our ancestors' hands either. This game doesn't give you a clear objective, but our ancestors didn't have a clear objective either, they evolved and innovated because the would go extinct if they didn't. This game captures those ideas perfectly.If you're curious, like survival games, like open world games, like simulation games, or are interested in human evolution you should definitely pick it up... even if you have to wait for a sale.In the first hour of this game I couldn't decide whether or not I hated it, but after this long I can definitely say that this game is awesome and I highly recommend it.The only cons for me personally are unintuitive controls and the lack of an in-game encyclopedia/bestiary, that would really help me remember what I've discovered and crafted.Overall 8/10 - if you think it looks interesting, no need to wait for a sale, it's worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: Very interesting game. The "mixed" tag is largely about two things: the lack of directions, and the poor controls. In the latter case, yes, this game was designed for consoles and, due to the number of available actions possible in this game, has a lot of context-sensitive actions that can sometimes be a struggle to wield with the "realistic" movement this game models. The port to KB/M unfortunately did little to remedy this, as the number of available buttons was not expanded, just remapped. It's not unplayably bad, and you can fiddle with the controls in the settings if you like.Regarding the first point, though: the game literally tells you that it's not going to help much. The game is a roguelike survival sandbox of sorts, and to better model what life was like for a primitive ape, you're going to have to figure out a lot of stuff yourself. As far as I'm aware, there's no such thing as a "game over" state, or at least it's quite difficult to achieve one, so don't worry about that. But if you aren't the kind of person that's willing to go into this game blind, I don't think I can recommend it for you, because that's where a lot of the fun seems to be. Sure, you can look up some info on how the UI works, since some parts of it are a little confusing, but for the actual game world: I think you should figure it out yourself. That's how I've been enjoying it so far.

_childDocuments_.review: 🌍 Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey – Embrace Your Inner Ape! 🐒Ever wanted to experience evolution first-hand? It’s not just a jungle gym—it’s a world filled with danger, mystery, and the occasional leap of faith. One wrong move, and you're lunch for a giant snake. But hey, that's evolution for you! 🐍😬The evolution system is brilliant, and the satisfaction of seeing your clan go from timid tree-dwellers to brave tool-makers is next level. Watching your descendants evolve based on your actions is incredibly rewarding. _childDocuments_.review: I waited a long time before I finally caved and purchased this game. This game explores an interesting side of evolution, the evolution of the Human Brain. THe first few hours were a complete slog, but once I understood the mechanics of the game it really opened up for me and sucked me in. The main Mechanic is exploring, you run around as a hominid exploring a prehistoric Earth, specifically the continent of Africa the birth play of Human Life. The world is filled with prehistoric dangers such as giant eagles, large cats, giant snakes, all of which pose a huge threat to you and your tribe. There is plenty to explore and learn, I think I'm 12 hours in (at the time of writing this) and I still haven't discovered 20% of the content in this game. My  biggest gripe with the game is how useless the other tribe members are. I was hoping for some more interesting mechanics similar to State of Decay's however as you start to unlock more neurons (this game's version of their perk tree) they are at least more tolerable. They're mostly there for you to take over if you die out in the unforgiving jungles.

_childDocuments_.review: Good game with an interesting concept and execution. I honestly had a blast and would love a sequel.the enemies are diverse and interesting and the biomes are extremely well down with a lot of detail. As you unlock more skills and master your environment the game becomes easier and easier and it feels so deserved. The way you interact with items in the game is well done and sometimes you are forced to improvise on the fly. The exploration always feels good and the unlockable skills are all fairly useful other than concentrate which seems bugged for its intended purpose. A few caveats though the skill tree  or neurons becomes so grindy late in the game, and at times you are as clueless as your apes on how to upgrade certain branches as it is not entirely made clear. Also you sometimes randomly just lose a hominid that has been following you and it is not clear why it stops following you. You have no way to track it down and if it is carrying infants you are handicapped for the rest of the game. I would like to see recruitable hominids play a bigger role. An ideal play though is literally just recruiting an additional female at the start then just having six offspring at all time so there is no need to recruit.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall I enjoyed this exploration and discovery game. The sound track was charming, the way the hominids move about and interact with the environment, each other, and predators was fun. Graphics were very polished. And there was a majestic contrast when moving from the densely laden steamy jungle areas, out into the open drier plains and desert.Once you have mastered the mechanics of dodging, attacking wildlife, and tool-making, the formula gets too repetitive though. I was invested enough to want to finish though.Not much replay value because of this, but overall, an enjoyable experience!

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy open world survival games, i mean REALLY enjoy the genre, then you should give this game a try. be aware that you wont receive much help or instruction but the things the game does teach you early on about manipulating and altering items by hand to make tools basically carries through the entirety of the game. you also really need to play with a controller, i always prefer mouse and keyboard for everything but i just cant see how it would be better in this game at all. i love the survival mechanics, eating, drinking, sleeping; just remember you need to take care of all your apes; and i recommend looking up specific instructions on how to dodge attacks and how to counter attack, as not knowing what i was doing wrong early on made for some frustrating gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an interesting game. Take your usual Ubisoft fare like Far Cry with its exploration mechanics and revealing points of interest on a map, add a survival system with hunger and injury management, throw in a bit of colony management with leading your clan to nests closer to resources, then link it all together with tech trees that advance as you unlock skills by experimenting with your environment.Don't get too attached to your first ape colony, however. To reach your full potential, you will need to selectively breed beneficial mutations into your bloodline and advance time to allow them to become permanent traits. As time is such a relevant mechanic in this game, your apes will age and die, passing on their knowledge to the next generation.It's definitely not a fast-paced game. You can fight tigers and snakes, swing through the trees at breakneck speed, and reach nearly every corner of the map, but these aren't the core of the game. If you're looking for a game with a unique take on survival, this could scratch that itch. Return to monke.

_childDocuments_.review: I am torn on how to rate this game. On the one hand, I have sunk 90 hours into a game that I received in a Humble Bundle, so on that note, I would definitely say I have gotten my money's worth and then some. On the other hand, the game has some stability issues and its crafting system, while very exciting at first, becomes stale after a short amount of time. I'll do my best to lay out some more detailed pros and cons, but since the main beauty of this game is in the act of discovery, I'm going to try and be careful with marking spoilers.In short, I'm going to recommend this game. I can't say it's the best game ever, but that wouldn't be a fair criteria for whether you should buy the game. I'm recommending the game because for 90+ hours I have enjoyed running around playing fictional proto-human and exploring a beautifully crafted world.The most positive aspect of Ancestors is its ability to inspire. , I could truly imagine being a world where I was the first creature to have done that.  And throughout my first playthrough (not to completion, more on that later) I was attempting to use every object I found with every other object. The game world is also massive, and beautifully designed. It clearly shows in the game that the artists involved are very talented. The soundtrack, too, while consisting of half a dozen tracks or so, sets the mood nicely and I found myself bobbing my head along with the music when my favorite of the tracks started playing.I didn't find the "survival" aspect of the game too difficult, but that's okay for this type of game. The survival boils down to meeting three basic needs (sleeping, eating, drinking) and avoiding/confronting other inhabitants in the wild. When I first attempted to go exploring, I found out very quickly what can happen to a poor simian with no food, water, or defensive mechanisms. After an unfortunate incident or two, I became quite paranoid in my preparations to go exploring. I didn't find myself spending the majority of my time in game just running around trying to find food and water, which I appreciated.Lastly, though confusing at first, the three-tiered evolution system is an interesting take on an upgrade system. Certain upgrades () had me saying "Oh, that's wonderful, this will change the game significantly." As much as I have enjoyed the game, and do still recommend it, I felt there were so many things in this game that came so close to being great, but unfortunately fell just short. Mainly, the crafting and upgrading system (the two areas closest to my core desires as a gamer). I would also say there are some quality of life issues and UI pains. Unfortunately, most actions in the game consist of press and hold a button for a long duration of time (which is a major no no). Want to get back to your monkey family this year? Hold down "A" to shuffle through the jungle rather than your usual meandering pace. Thirsty? Hold down "A" by a watering hole until your meter is filled. Hungry? Sleepy? Same thing. Ready to unlock that new upgrade? You guessed it, mash that "A" button. For anyone easily fatigued by repetitive game play mechanics, this might not be the game for you. Lastly, before the spoilers part, there are some major stability issues that I have experienced, just full on crash-to-desktop (CTD) right in the middle of climbing a massive cliff without it having autosaved in a while.Okay, so there really is no way to discuss some specific pain points without spoiling the discovery aspect, so I will mark the rest of the review as a spoiler.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm enjoying the heck out of this game. I love sandbox games where I can make my own story... Like the time I brought the kids to the swamp so we could get used to the area and not be afraid, but on the way home we got ambushed by a warthog. My dude was bleeding to death, carrying the only 2 children of the clan. We escaped into the trees and right as my guy was about to bleed out, he discovered medicine in the trees can stop bleeding. We also found some fruit to eat. After a brief rest we climbed down, got drunk on fermented berries and crawled back home. It was a fun adventure!!It's the kind of game that some people might not enjoy. There is no objective! It's pure sandbox. Like driving a car or flying a plane, except you're controlling a clan of primates. Pay attention to the available prompts and try stuff. it's fun and not dangerous to you, the player. I mean it sucks when you clan wipe your clan, but life's hard man. I'm also new to the game so it's still very mysterious which adds to the excitement. I can't say how you will feel after a few hours of play time.I think the most off putting thing might be misunderstanding the level up system. The game is not a grind at as I've read in other reviews. To get smarter you have to bring a kid out exploring. It's like teaching them. Doing actions in the world will create new 'skills' based on how you play. Carrying children with you while interacting with the world will gain 'xp' towards those 'skills'. There are 2 ways to 'level up', by generation to lock in skills or by species to carry over genetic mutations. Yes you can lose skills, but xp seems so easy to get that it's no big deal to lose a few skills after advancing a generation. Just go look at stuff, enjoy the scenery. smell it, listen to the sounds. Move to a new location, build a fence, whatever. Just don't get too attached to your first lineage (sigh...save file name...) because they will probably suffer horribly while you learn the controls and game mechanics. You should try and enjoy that part too. Don't go asking the internet for help on your first play. I've just started my third lineage and this is the one man , we gonna make it this time.You will never become a human and drive around in fast cars with guns or even light a fire. You're a primate, you eat food and drink water for a living. Go figure out how to poke something with a stick in your free time.How is that not the most epic fantasy setting ever? I think it's beautiful and I hope the game can get more updates. maybe even a sequal at some point in the future after enough updates and interest.

_childDocuments_.review: The recent reviews had me scared, so I thought Id let everyone thats considering buying it on sale know before the sale is over.The game is built for YOU TO FIGURE IT OUT. Well please, go play a preset storyline that holds your hand through it. That way you can have your predefined 50 hours of fun.Ive only just started with under 10 hours, but since the "i cheated the game to get to the end, and now I dont have any content" kids flooded with reviews, I thought Id let everyone that actually enjoy these type of games know that is actually quite nice. Play it as its supposed to be played and I'm very confident its 100+ hours of playtime - probably more.Think logically through playing and choose a difficulty your comfortable with (1 to 4) and you'll have a hell of a lot of fun. If pure originality (which is hardly ever seen in new games nowadays) and a bit of brain twisting is something you enjoy, you'll love this.Edit after 30 hours : The game is even more than I thought. One of my all time favorites already.

_childDocuments_.review: When only 80% of players have achieved the basic milestone of playing the game, it raises concerns about the overall experience. This title was gifted to me, prompting reflections on the appropriateness of maintaining a wishlist for games I am skeptical about, given the disappointment that followed.Initial impressions within the first 30 minutes of gameplay were marked by several issues:    The startup features full-blast music, a common but significant pet peeve among players. Prioritizing sound options as the first menu upon startup could alleviate this concern.    The inability to skip the intro, coupled with the controller becoming unresponsive after alt-tabbing, presented an unnecessary hindrance to the overall experience.    Despite being touted as best experienced with a controller, inconsistent functionality raised questions about the game's programming in comparison to other controller-supported titles.    Attempting to explore the supposedly "free world" resulted in random deaths due to unclear starting locations and insufficient guidance on initial objectives.    Completing the full tutorial proved to be an exercise in frustration, as the tutorials were both unhelpful and persistent, obstructing a significant portion of the screen and hindering visibility of objectives.In summary, the game has left me confused and dissatisfied. While a refund may be warranted, the absence of this option for gifted games raises questions about the overall customer experience. With improvements and input from competent game designers, the potential for a great game is evident, but the current execution falls short of expectations.

_childDocuments_.review: Right off the bat, I'll say that this game is not for everyone.I will say, after you've figured out how to evolve, pass generations, and gain genes, the game gets pretty repetitive, even if there are plenty of genes for you to unlock and places to explore. Once I'd reached Ardipithecus ramidus, which is the middle stage of the game, I'd already explored basically all of the map. And the fact that this game tells you almost nothing about how to play it is both a positive and a negative for me. Positive because it's pretty realistic, as prehistoric hominids didn't have a guide either and had to figure out everything themselves. But it's a negative because you're often left utterly confused and/or frustrated. This may or may not be a problem for you however. You will have to determine for yourself if you like this play style. All that being said, I had a fantastic time with this game. I have a good 190.7 hours. If you are at all a fan of survival or prehistory, especially the history of human evolution, you might get a good kick out of this game. Just don't come to this game expecting a history lesson. There are giant centipedes and eagles for Christ's sake.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so deeply weird that I don't know where to begin.I'm not sure what I was expecting, but it wasn't quite... this. I was expecting an action-adventure ape game, maybe a good itch-scractcher after watching Planet of the Apes, and I wasn't exactly wrong, but that's not the whole story. Let me just summarize this before I get to the rating part.You're an ape some 10 billion years ago. Your goal is to make the ape human - or at least human adjacent, since it doesn't quite get to the ♥♥♥♥ sapiens stage. You do that by being ape in action-adventure openworldesque setting, by running, climbing, learning to make and use simple tools, so forth, but the real progress happens in the Evolution menu.Which is a little complex.You've got nodes, not unlike skills in a skill tree. They're initially invisible to you, you can only see the ones that you're ready to unlock. How do you unlock them? By being ape. Better running speed is unlocked by running. Walking on two legs better is unlocked by trying to walk on two legs. Senses are reinforced by using them - and so on. But that only unlocks the node.You actually buy the node using "neural energy" which is generated by - apparently - teaching kids. So performing actions with kids present. Conveniently, you can piggyback two and have others nearby, either piggybacked by other apes following you, or following you themselves. Perform enough actions, get the energy, buy the neural node. Which isn't the end.Then you need to reinforce that neuron by passing the generation - which normally allows you to reinforce only 1 node per kid in the clan, so you want to do that often. Kids also get to have random mutations which get revealed when they mature, but only activate upon evolution leap. Which in turn is passing millions, even billions of years (depending on evolution feats) and potentially making your clan into new species.That was a mouthful.It boils down to the gameplay loop of filling in your clan with kids, performing actions to get some evolution feats, unlock new neural nodes and get some neural energy, maybe migrate your clan to a new area, passing the generation, doing that again - and once your elders and adults have mutations available, performing an evolution leap. And that for about 8 billion years.Thing is, it initially does a really good job at showing what it could be like to be ape. You're rather clumsy, and the controls show that. Even if you do things mostly right you'll break your tools, you won't be able to communicate, you'll move slow, it's... a struggle. It gives an impression of bad controls and bad design - which they're not. They're a bit awkward, but not bad.But as you evolve, you realize that this gameplay loop is actually quite engaging. You slowly make the environment yield do you, as you both learn it and as your clan becomes more adept at being ape. The controls slowly become more reasonable, and the game kinda starts to flow. Reaching the end then becomes a fairly relaxing and satisfying experience.So in summary, can I recommend the game? I can. Not to everyone though. It's a deeply weird game that will appeal to players who like unusual games. I find it difficult to put it in the sentence "If you liked X you'll like Ancestors". But I have to admit that once it clicked with me - which required effort - I enjoyed my 30-something hours run very, very much.Try it if you like games that present you with unusual mechanics and provoke some unusual thoughts.

_childDocuments_.review: Panache Digital Games came up with a game we always desired. Start your journey from scratch and evolve accordingly. There are not many restrictions imposed on the players. If you want to tarry with your group and don’t leave the settlement, you are free to do so, or gather your clan and evolve throughout a journey of exploring new kinds of stuff. Feel the adventure of surviving the world that ages up to 10 million years ago. Monitor the growth of your hominids as you traverse, explore, survive, and evolve through time. Carry on your knowledge and discoveries to the new evolved generation. The game is slow-paced because of its “help yourself” idea and might feel frustrating sometimes. With the numerous possibilities, you can surely grind a good chunk of hours.Ancestors has a slow-paced complex gameplay that might feel frustrating over time. The gameplay might vary according to your playstyle. If you want to stay close to the settlement and increase your domestic skills, then your gameplay might omit danger from wild animals and fear of the unknown. Migrating your settlement to search the unfamiliar lands might inflate tremendous danger and can wipe your entire lineage. The controls feel too complex and are not fun. Climbing and swinging through the trees is frustrating. Most of the time, you will experience difficulty locating the next branch to jump on, as the tree positioning is weird and poorly made. One button can perform multiple operations, which can result badly in certain situations. You are supposed to educate the species about every possible useful kind of stuff, from sticks to rocks to edibles. Establishing communication between the clan is very important, as you will need to switch characters to keep the evolution going. The idea presented is pretty good, but it lacks proper execution.  The graphics are not bad, neither wondrous, but they are quite enjoyable and don’t affect the gameplay. It lacks details in the interaction of characters with the environment. It looks more of an old game instead of a new-gen game. Keeping in mind that this is a new concept game and the development team had limited funds at that time, this is quite promising. The map is enormous with numerous focal points , and also very diverse flora and fauna. Some of the effects like fear of the unknown and infection are pretty good. But somehow, these above-average graphics require good GPU power, which is quite unusual. The cinematics are top-notch with great story portraits and realistic quality graphics. Little things like dream showcases and animal fight cinematics bring an extra level of detail to the game.Don’t rush things, learning is a slow process. Most of the time, you will have to figure out the solution yourself. Turning down the music will help a lot, as most of the actions in-game are executed on a beat. Without spoiling too much, we can say that both hands are useful and can craft wonders. Most of the players neglect to carry a child, but actually, they provide you extra experience, and you can carry up to 2 of them. This is an interesting detail of the game that you will undergo during the exploration of new regions. When you are away from your familiarized territory, your character will feel scared and might enter the state of hysteria. This will result in losing your current clan member, and you will return to your main settlement. To conquer this, focus on your senses and identify the elements nearby. If your hominids recognize them, he will feel confident and will calm itself.The game’s objective is to finish the evolution before the actual time that was taken according to history. So your first objective is to enhance your species and not a sole character. Tarrying on one character will influence your progress and might back-fire. Keeping the clan guarded and prosperous is your foremost goal. This concept certainly raises our expectations and makes us biased towards the game. The story should have been stretched to the start of human civilization, but it ends at a generation switch that feels incomplete. It provides a mesmerizing experience to the gamers. Recommended buying during a sale.Rate: 7/10This game has been played on  platform before tested on .

_childDocuments_.review: Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey ReviewA prehistoric adventure like no other! Some key points that this game offers:1.	Unite your species to form a clan2.	Explore Savage Africa3.	Nature is more than unforgiving, behind every gorgeous scenery lies a predator waiting to pounce on you4.	Learn, adapt and overcome every obstacle 5.	Incredibly detailed skill systemSpecial Note:The game has been released on Steam as well now. Even though the game received mixed reviews when it was released initially, the developers have since updated and improved the game immensely. They added new features and altered others. I left my original Review intact so that you can see how the developers took what the gamers said, and improved the game. For a full list of changed and improvements, view the patch notes here.Gameplay & Controls:The controls for the game are rather discomforting, and unfortunately, that has nothing to do with the layout. It is the way the controls are implemented. For example, running and jumping is the same button. You run by holding it down, and when you leave it, you jump. This does not work well with the gameplay itself. There are some movement bugs present in the game, but those will be patched out in the days to come. The game can be played on the keyboard and mouse; however, it is suggested that you use a controller. The game takes place 10 million years ago in the Neogene period in Africa. You take control of hominids, a pre-cursor Ape species. You will have to build a clan, by recruiting outsiders and mating. Your clan needs to eat, live, and survive. It is up to you to teach them. There is a massive world just waiting for you to explore. Everything can be examined to determine its purposes, be it a tool, medicine, or food. As you learn and adapt to your surroundings your species start learning new skills and abilities, such as refining plants for alternative uses. In one instance it’s a food, but ground up, it becomes a paste used to stop bleeding.The same with tools, a branch for example can be stripped clean of the smaller branches increasing its attack power, and later on, a second tool can be used to sharpen the stick. This world is filled to the brim with things to figure out and explore. As you explore and discover things, you trigger neurons which improves the survivability of your species. In the beginning, you are prey to almost every other creature out there, but slow and steady you evolve and adapt becoming better at defending yourself and later on become the predator yourself. This world is truly big and divided up into different biomes, each very realistically tailored to offer an immersive experience. In each of these biomes, there are numerous places for you to discover and even a few that you can move your clan to establish a new home.As it stands, the game is more than fun and sure to offer you a fantastic time. It has some issues and minor bugs. The game lacks some important features too. For example, the lack of a tutorial system makes the game unnecessarily difficult. Figuring stuff out is part of the learning curve for sure, but the lack of basic information makes a game less fun. Then predators seem to constantly attack you when you are out in the open, you barely have any room to breathe or actually just enjoy the game, not sure if this is a bug or deliberate implementation. Graphics:Absolutely beautiful doesn’t begin to cover it. Each biome has been gorgeously created to represent a very realistic environment. There are Jungles, the Savanna and so much more. The day and night cycle along with the weather system doesn’t just add more beauty and depth to the game; every sunrise is a new gorgeous day for you to enjoy.Character models were done just as beautifully. I can’t say for certain what any of these animals looked like back then, but the representation here is done quite remarkably and beautifully as well.All in all, the game is pretty much gorgeous no matter where you are, but there are some spots that you discover that truly offer you beauty like no other.Under the settings menu, we have several options to customize our game.Sounds:Another brilliant add on. The music for the game is astounding! It adds to the realism of the game immensely. The game is best experienced with the volume turned up or with a headset. There are so many background sounds that play vital roles in bringing the game to life. Whether it is you wading through water or the sounds of a massive python hissing at you. The sound brings life to this game in a remarkable way.The animal sounds were marvellously incorporated into the game.Under the settings menu, we have full volume control.Replayability:The game doesn’t really have a new game plus feature. However, the original playthrough will take you a long time to complete, especially if you go for total completion. There is a lot to discover and experience. That alone will keep you busy for quite a while.MGR Gaming’s Conclusions:Spoilers Ahead:More than a brilliant game for sure. There is tons of fun to be had and a very memorable journey to experience. A lot of unique elements went into the game. The Neuron system was incredibly well thought out and implemented. It offered an RPG experience unlike anything else I’ve come across, especially on how you unlock these Neurons. Very well thought out.The Generation and Evolution systems further adds to the unique gameplay mechanics of the game. I must admit that they really went all out here in terms of out of the box thinking and it really paid off well. There are so many discoveries to make and so many memorable experiences to witness.To put it frankly, you are in for the time of your life. This game will offer you an experience unlike anything else you’ve experienced thus far.I do hope they update the lack of a tutorial system for the game, it will make the game a lot friendlier and more fun to get into. The game is an open-world simulation, but the lack of any quest or general direction further adds to the unnecessary difficulty. All things considered, this is still a great game that can be improved.The Official trailer for Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey:Score 7By: MGRzaDate: 4 September 2019Additional Info:Platforms: PC: PlayStation 4: Xbox OneGenre: Action-Adventure: Atmospheric: Choices Matter: Crafting: Exploration: Historical: Hunting: Immersive Sim: Nature: Open World: Open World Survival Craft: PvE: Science: Singleplayer: Survival: Third PersonCensor Rating: Violence: Blood: Partial NudityAge Rating: TeenDeveloper: Panache Digital GamesPublisher: Private DivisionRelease Date: 27 August 2019MGR Gaming Steam Curator:MGR Gaming:

_childDocuments_.review: Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey is a rough game. The controls are awkward, the goals aren't clear, the story is minimal. Despite this, I found it fascinating and put almost 100 hours into it. The world is beautiful and surprising, and exploring it reminded me of Zelda: Breath of the Wild, though of course without the Nintendo polish. Without spoiling anything, you begin as a tree-dwelling ape and end up an upright, tool-using hominid, though the mechanics aren't always consistent. Swinging in the treetops was exhilarating and probably one of the better mechanics of the game, but one it explicitly pushed the player away from with the level design and the implication of becoming more human-like.If the premise of this game is appealing to you, you should give it some time, but if you're not having fun by the time you're walking upright and fighting instead of running, you probably shouldn't play further

Idk...just didn't do it for me. Kind of tired of these console games coming to steam store just for more money when its not really meant for hardcore PC players that use keyboard and mouse.
_childDocuments_.name: Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey

_childDocuments_.review: The idea of the game itself is pretty cool. You get to be a human ancestor, survive with your monkey abilities and craft tools to use in your primitive world as you slowly  implementation it is very grindy and repetitive. You make babies, you go and activate neurons for very marginal new bonuses, rinse and repeat. Is that realistic? Maybe. Is it fun? Not at all. The whole game is going to new areas to discover new things to activate your neurons; but I can't stress how repetitive it all is.It's the same slow crafting of pointy sticks, the same making of beds to establish a base, the same looking bugs in a monkey's back so they can couple and have a baby, the same examine, examine, examine until your neuron activates; then lock 2-4 of those each generation and start all over.The idea itself is pretty cool; that you have to hand to them.
_childDocuments_.name: Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey

_childDocuments_.review: It's simple, you are a monkey 10 million years ago. You have your ears (B), eyes (Y), nose (X), your mind (R1), your hands (A). And using those with the environment you'll gradually evolve. Amazing game, story. It CAN be challenging if you're not a seasoned gamer, jumping between trees is a little tricky in the beginning. But this game worth every penny.
_childDocuments_.name: Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey

_childDocuments_.review: Love this game so far! The concept is great and like nothing else I've played. You get to play as Apes that lived about 10 millions years ago, band together as a clan, and learn how to survive in the jungle and evolve. Controls are kind of hard to figure out at first, so I'd highly recommend a controller to play. Once you figure out how to swing from the trees (which you absolutely should learn to) then traveling and exploring is much easier. Overall, the best way to play this is to just figure it out yourself and try not to get too frustrated in the beginning.
_childDocuments_.name: Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey

_childDocuments_.review: The game has one of the more unique approaches to crafting i've ever seen.You start out bearly able to cope with boars but by discovering how to use various tools, developing your senses, evolving various beneficial mutations you end up being able to hunt some of the biggest and most dangerous animals on the continent. The core gameplay loop and sense of progression is pretty cool.
_childDocuments_.name: Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey

_childDocuments_.review: 30 hours into the game and still waiting for the fun to begin.The game could be a lot, but it has, as others extensively stated three main problems; complexity, controls and progression.It is somewhat complex, which is hard to get into without any sort of tutorial. The bad controls don't help, there are just too much actions to have a sensible control scheme, no matter if you play on keyboard or controller. The progression is... slow and the apes can't really do anything. The only reason to travel in a group is the effectiveness of group intimidation, otherwise traveling alone is much more convenient.When you grasp how the game works (most of it is not explained), the game loop becomes very mundane; breed, move to a few new locations while doging/killing new enemies and eating new stuff, settle down, skip to next generation. Do that two times while also looking for meteorites and then you do an evolution, this maximizes the genetic mutation while minimizing time. Nothing of that is explained, you have to figure it out by yourself. If you realize this is how it works, the game becomes vey repetitive.There also isn't really much of a progression, it's basically always "you get better at x" and nothing more. I Expected to evolve, but that isn't really the case. The stuff you can do/make in the beginning is the same stuff you can do/make at the end.I'm mainly giving up because the apes are useless. I'm at a point where the enemy attacks in groups. After each attack you need to gather healing resources and heal your apes because they can't do that on their own. Weapons have to be made and given to them, making them drink/eat is a pain in the a** because if their main hand is occupied, they can't do anything so you have to make them switch hands (which is problematic if some have a weapon in the left, others in the right hand - imho a design flaw, instead of "switch hands" the command should be "ready weapon" because it has no other use). In older versions, apes also got stuck often, luckily they now teleport. Which is good for predators, because if you're next to a cliff they sometimes teleport onto the cliff, getting attacked by a predator and there is nothing you can do because you can't reach them, can't intimidate from this distance and running away won't teleport them because they're in combat. In general, managing your apes is a true nightmare. The game would be a LOT better if predators would avoid a large, armed group of apes.Graphically its nice. The music is ok if you ignore the random wanna-be-african-atmosphere mixed with some scifi-music stuff that pops up seemingly at random.The cutscenes have a big problem. If you inspect or discover something, a cutscene will play, which is nice if the time would stop. So while in the cutscene, your apes get murdered. You can skip the cutscene, but that really shouldn't be necesarry. This creates a sense of urge and insecurity to rush everything and ignore the scenery. I'm pretty sure this is not what the devs wanted to achieve because the terrain is really nice.While i'm at the negative aspects, there is also the very cool concept of unknown territory. If you're in a new area, you will get...lets call it a massive senses debuff, which you have to negate by simply using your senses and doing stuff in the new territory. If cone correctly, you need to "go into the center" to claim the territory. The center of an unknown territory... yeah, that's a nice joke, there is an "indicator" but most of the times that indicator points back to a known territory. So, conquering a new territory is mostly running around in hope the prompt appears. Very good idea but bad execution, which could be the motto of the whole game.The more i write, the more i'm reminded of how bad the game is. You play as a monkey who is able to jump from tree to tree and yet i can't remember the last time i did that. Because it mostly ends in death. Often the apes don't grab to a branch that is clearly in their jump path. Jumping from the end of a branch into their death without you pressing any button is also a random occurance. Oh and if you're not already in climbing animation, there is no way to climb down. So despite being a monkey, the ground is your friend.I'm struggling to say anything positive, so my tldr;- Extremely good ideas but executed rather poorly- Needs better controls, better ape management and more significant progression*EDIT: whwo this became more of a rant than a review. I'm sorry, but i'm not exaggerating, the game really is frustrating
_childDocuments_.name: Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey

_childDocuments_.review: It feels like there could be a lot here. I love games that have growth mechanics.But there's so much that feels.. clunky. The idea of not being handholded is good, but there's a difference between that and throwing a child into the deep end of a pool. Dodging wildlife is difficult, there's no clear sign that you are training nodes, the objectives are unclear and the imposing nature of the world makes it difficult to even want to go after the objectives, especially when you enter the "Fear of the Unknown" area.If there was just more to do, if the other members of the settlement DID MORE, this would feel a lot better. But for now, don't waste your money.
_childDocuments_.name: Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey

_childDocuments_.review: Played this from my friends library. Controls are absolutely abysmal and anti user friendly. The 'tutorial' doesn't help at All and left me confused and unable to do simple things like using a held item. Needs option to yeet babies into space because i was stuck with one on my back. Monkey apparently did not know how to use its own clans nest. I have no idea why the pc version has console controls on by default.This said. I want to be monkey :pensive:
_childDocuments_.name: Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey

_childDocuments_.review: It's a very good game, but I tried playing on pc with a ps4 controller and it said R1 to drop something and it didn't let me with any buttons, then I looked at what all the buttons do and it turns out theres no button to actually drops something with the controller. (I would like to retract this, a while ago I figured out that the controller was broken and it was fine since! This was previous me's mistake and it is an incredibly good game!)
_childDocuments_.name: Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey

_childDocuments_.review: Intimidated a python only to get mowed down by a boar. Escaped up a tree and moved on with life. About 30 minutes later I evade a boar straight into the jaws of a hyena (maybe a leopard. Not sure. That neuron hasn't evolved that far yet.) Again managed to escape but upon returning to the scene of my near death a short while later I had developed a sort of PTSD I had to conquer. I did so and was swiftly mauled by a hyena (yes. the same one.). Oh yeah, at some point through all that I watched a giant python constrict and kill one of my clan. It was pretty brutal to watch and be absolutely clueless on even attempting to save him :(.Death animation is dramatic as hell. I lost 3 clan members so far and well... It hurt lol. I kinda miss them. Great game but requires patience. Looks amazing and is honestly just a really interesting and cool premise.
_childDocuments_.name: Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey

_childDocuments_.review: 9/10 would beat things to death with a rock again.Solid adventure game. Map is HUGE. Fresh interesting concept executed surprisingly well. Encountered maybe 2 or 3 bugs in 47 hours, none of which were game breaking.If you enjoy a drastically unique game, figuring stuff out yourself and discovery as the story..this game is for you. After the initial learning curve, the game really shines.If you have no patience to learn controls and mechanics while this game tries to murder you..you won't have a good time.Very leisurely taking my time exploring and evolving, it took about 30 hours to complete the main objectives. Now I'm just finding hidden/achievement stuff.Also I bought this game on sale, definitely worth the 15$ at the time, I'd say even 25$ it'd be worth it.Late game can become a grind, after the novelty of discovering things wears off.
_childDocuments_.name: Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey

_childDocuments_.review: This feels more like an overly-ambitious science project than a video game. What's interesting is the premise of simulation human evolution in a virtual system. What it ends up being, in practice, is an unapproachable mess of hidden interactions and completely impossible to navigate terrain. Could have been fun if either the realism were expanded upon or if there was more control in the hands of the player.
_childDocuments_.name: Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey

_childDocuments_.review: Be prepared to put in some time figuring this one out. I haven't yet but I'm looking forward to it. Like nothing else I've played before. Sure there are things you could complain about but what game doesn't have issues. If you're concerned about spending the money just don't. But if the $24 on sale is going to break the bank for you I say go for it. Even if you never figure it out and fully get into it I think it is worth experiencing.
_childDocuments_.name: Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey

_childDocuments_.name: Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so fun to play! I bought this game ... two days ago? Three? I don't know because I've been practically living in this game for the past thirty hours.  Matter of fact, I may play it once I'm done.  This game is extremely exploration and discovery heavy, but that actually kind of suits me. This doesn't hold your hand and if you are not careful - like me - you will die. A lot. Pros: This game is something that can almost soothe you into a false sense of security and then BAM, hits you with something out of nowhere. Don't know why I like this but I do. It allows for extreme creativity with minimal goals allowing you to make your own story. The world is so varied and gorgeous and dangerous that you WANT to linger... and not be eaten of course. This runs into my next pro, to make this game have a real difficulty curve, they take away any sense of strength or smarts. You have to figure out how to switch Items you are holding in your hands for example. You don't get anything. I like that freedom. Cons: Alright alright, everyone says this - having to breed MORE ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ monkeys after every generation. I wish there was more ways to interact or get attached to your little ape family.  The most I feel when a family member dies is "♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ how'd I ♥♥♥♥ up" and not "OH MY GOD NOOOOOOO".  Sometimes the big cats or enemies LITERALLY spawns out of nowhere. Hard to see in jungle areas but easy to see in the desert and ocean areas. Other than that - not too much. Love it! Would love to play a sequel too!
_childDocuments_.name: Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey

_childDocuments_.review: Sick game especially if you are an anthropology nut. It requires thinking and logic to survive in this game. It gets kinda easier as you go but even during endgame when i was too cocky i almost lost an ape and two kids.Totally recommend. I hope they will make a sequel where we can advance into Neanderthals
_childDocuments_.name: Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey

_childDocuments_.review: Return to monke. A fascinating and some might say also educational game. It's pretty damn brutal quite often and early game is hell until you establish yourself. Think of it more like an rpg game, where you occasionally need to bank skills to advance, leading to some new skills and new options.Music is nice and atmospheric for your actions, visuals are decent, though often you will find that anything and everything tries to kill you, especially the saber cats who seem to exist to hunt you down no matter where you are. Still, you can go from a helpless primate outdone by everything to the new apex predator.
_childDocuments_.name: Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to play this game before it existed, really cool concept of walking through human evolution. The gameplay is fun and relaxing simultaneously. I found climbing trees and jumping from branch to branch quite fun. The game doesn't really explain anything which is good and bad at the same time, because you can miss things and get I found myself playing the game "incorrectly" for a long time until I read the wiki. I find the AI a bit annoying and sometimes you have to micromanage your tribe too much. But all in all I enjoyed the game would recommend it for people who enjoy single player games, exploration and figuring things out.

_childDocuments_.name: Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey

_childDocuments_.review: I am a 45 yo father, probably one of the oldest people playing this game. I am a single father to my Son, who is 14 now. My son got this game for Christmas in 2021 from his uncle, so we installed it on his computer and he started playing. By the end of the week he had 24 hours on this game. This was horrible for me, as it was already hard for me to find ways to spend time with my son, as he is always out with his friends or just watching YouTube. So i decided to make a Steam account and get this game to see if I could maybe play alongside him. I loaded into the game, picked my character and world and started playing but I was stuck on what you where supposed to do. I asked my Son for help and he hosted a game for me to join. I loved it as it was the best time I had spent with my Son since my wife had died. This game has ever since brought me and my son closer again and now we actually spend time together outside the house together as well. This game reminded me that there's fun to be had in everything, and it has brought both me and my Son many happy memories.

_childDocuments_.name: Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey

_childDocuments_.review: The premise of the game looks interesting, but, so far, playing it has been incredibly frustrating. Let's start with the first interaction of the game: Press A to Continue. Naturally, I have no "A" to press, as that's a controller A not a keyboard A. The game defaults to controller. The game says using a controller is the preferred way to play it. I hate controllers and I won't use them -- if that's not your case, ignore my comments about controls.The mouse/keyboard controls seemed to have been made by someone intent on making them as difficult to use as possible. Trivial things like looking around _with a mouse_ are made incredibly difficult. Let's give an example: I'm close to another member of my tribe and I want to know who that is. If I use E to identify that member, the information will be off my viewscreen because they are close. If I move the mouse to look up, it exits the information mode. I have to move further away to see the information, or next to them to analyse.Shift, control, alt, the standard modifiers we use to change modes like sprinting, aiming, looking around without changing direction, etc, they are not put to use. Left click and right click are used in unnatural ways and in an irregular which results in a constant fight to get what you want done. And some of the key combinations are just mind-boggling, like pressing control and up-arrow (up arrow? that means taking your hand out of the mouse!), then pressing space, then pressing W... In summary you'll get very frustrated if you play with mouse and keyboard.Next, the UI. The UI is full of symbols which are meaningless to me. The tutorial shows some of this stuff from time to time -- usually when it's least convenient and you are concentrating on something else. And you better memorize them right then and there, because I can't find any information about what I'm seeing in the HUD afterwards. And speaking of user interface, there's no apparent way of skipping the introduction, and sound levels do not seem to be respected in it, which leaves the game blaring in my ears, and keeping anyone from hearing what I'm saying on stream.But what finally pushed me over to write this review is that if you inspect one particular spot in your starting area then an event happens that moves you elsewhere, and good luck finding your way back or continuing the tasks you were doing.Oh, and there's no save game. There's no way of getting back from _looking_ at something and having that change the game irrevocably. Or just experimenting with different ways of doing stuff without having to restart.
_childDocuments_.name: Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey

_childDocuments_.review: Rigid and slow. Many game mechanics wipe out 30 minutes or an hour of effort with nothing you can do to avoid it (evolution leap sent my clan back to the first settlment repeatedly). Repeatedly had a tiger pin a clan member, every time I got close enough to distract the tiger, my clan member just stood up and didn't move, just to get pounced on by the tiger again. I've had saves delete clan members, kept getting knocked back to 2 adults. Sooo many annoying features, everything about the reliance on and utilizing senses is just a boring grind. You have to be visiting the wiki to figure out the mostly nonsensical crafting (the dev apparently takes pride in not guiding you, leaving you to evolve and grow by yourself).It is pretty immersive. There's some pretty neat unorthodox story-telling going on here. If you're in the mood to sip tea and wander around an ancient, dangerous jungle, then this has some merit. Otherwise, don't be enticed by the pretty screenshots.
_childDocuments_.name: Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey

_childDocuments_.review: UI is absolutely horrendous, tutorials don't explain ♥♥♥♥, the mechanics turn out to be rhythm games with 0 indication that it is what they are, on one hand you have very vague UI without much information, and then there is a massive genetics menu that is also not explainedThis game requires a massive commitment to play it, and it doesn't seem even remotely worth it even if you decide to play this for several hoursBought it on -60% but still refunding, definitely do not recommend for the full price. Interesting concept that didn't translate into fun gameplay at all
_childDocuments_.name: Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really disappointed by this game's mechanics, not only is it tedious but the controls are also clunky and jumping from branch to branch is beyond frustrating for something that should be as easy as breathing for an ape. The controls themselves wouldn't be as much of a deal-breaker if only the tutorial system was at least somewhat decent. I can understand not making it way too easy for the player, but to not even explain all the HUD elements is inexcusable in my book, as of writing this review I still don't understand how the map works beyond showing white, yellow and red dots on it. As a result, I decided to get a refund at least until the game gets polished into a decent experience. Such a pity because the concept of making an evolution-based action game is without a doubt a very intriguing idea that deserves much more depth than the developers of this game were willing to give.
_childDocuments_.name: Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey

_childDocuments_.review: I've had this game on my wish list for seven months counting down every day and to say its a let down is an understatement. The game has the weirdest controls that even 1.6 hours in I can't understand them. The HUD disappears randomly and the sleep/food checker is a mess. The controls are a garbled mess of random buttons and every second is being confused. The attack system makes no sense and the evolution part is just downright confusing. There's no way of under standing what is food and whats poison, whats water and whats poison. If you want a game where you are confused every second and have no clue what to do with your monkey then be my guest but save your money please.
_childDocuments_.name: Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey

_childDocuments_.review: Thank goodness I got this as part of a humble bundle and the other games were still worth it, because I cannot figure out what I'm supposed to be doing. The "full tutorial" barely explains anything beyond what button does what as you stumble into different situations.The third-person camera seems to be locked with my monkey filling two-thirds of my screen, it's way too zoomed in and I can't find any options to adjust this, so most of the time I cannot see what I'm doing, it would have made more sense to be in a first-person view.I had to draw the line at the dodging "tutorial" though, which had me randomly attacked and locked my camera angle to be looking directly at my enormous monkey butt with an on screen prompt to "hold space to ready the dodge, and release it at the right time to finish the dodge", except I couldn't see what was attacking me, how it was attacking, where it was attacking from, or how close it was. When is the "right time"??? No on screen indication, nothing, just repeated deaths every time the tutorial pops up because I can't see a thing.If I had purchased this game independent of a bundle I would 100% refund it.
_childDocuments_.name: Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey

_childDocuments_.review: The game is quite confusing when you play it for the first time, but once you get the hang of it, it becomes a very interesting experience. It is something that you've never experienced before in any video game. For some reason it reminded me of Spore, so if you've played Spore in the past there is a high chance that you will enjoy this game as well. I wasn't sure what to expect but I DID like this game very much so I recommend this game to you as well especially if you're looking for something new, something refreshing then this game is for you..
_childDocuments_.name: Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey

_childDocuments_.review: I was originally going to just write "monke" for the review, but this game is actually so good that I'd feel like an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ for making a joke out of it.It's definitely not for everyone, but what it sets out to do, it excels in. It's the kind of game that Spore should have wanted to be, but couldn't even have thought of becoming.Of course its scope is much, much more focused - but it still offers the same kind of feeling of progression, while making sure that every step is enjoyable.The main gameplay is very similar to the dozens of crafting survival indies - so don't expect a whole lot on that front - but it feels a helluva lot better.Especially because of its unique UI design and language, and its weird control scheme. It just works wonderfully well.It is hands down the most immersive experience I've ever had. It's so far beyond anything, I legitimately can't compare it to others. No heavily modded Skyrim or Half Life Alyx can stand up to this.One word of caution. If this is your first time playing, DO NOT start in immersive controls mode. The controls are so unique that you will have no idea what you're doing.
_childDocuments_.name: Ancestors: The Humankind Odyssey

_childDocuments_.review: Its an enjoyable game that puts you in the position of our ancestors, Foraging, hunting, and being hunted. Its an educational game. it took me 96 hrs on normal mode to finish it through my first time but you honestly can spend ages collecting food for your clan and hunting, exploring and making the local fauna kill each other. though not 100% to real history, i accept it for how it is, No major bugs, Beautiful graphics, amazing music and for me endless fun.Controller highly encouraged while playing this game, it will make game play much easier.
