_childDocuments_.review: I played this on the free weekend as I didn’t believe the game worth paying. I wasn’t wrong.The game tries to create a new concept by commanding a hovercraft (called gravcycle) with various guns while also commanding several other walking soldiers with various abilities.Now, for a shooter game I didn’t believe this whole concept is needed:1-	Why am I not allowed to choose my weapon and team before getting into a mission? That is a SHOOTER game. What kind of a shooter game that doesn’t allow the player to choose his weapon?!!2-	What the use of the other team units? Their abilities? That could just have been added to my arsenal and I could change the weapon on the fly to whatever suits the situation. Remember I’m using a hovercraft? That must mean I can equip it with various weapons.3-	Why am I not allowed to command my units to attack the bid monsters/bosses weakness points?! They are my team. They should be supporting me but instead I must fight all the bosses/big monsters on my own as in the end there are ineffective when it comes to hitting the monsters point of weakness. That beats the purpose of the whole team concept.4-	What about the story? I have gone through the game twice trying to achieve all the goals and even after playing the whole campaign twice I didn’t even remember what it’s all about! The story seems totally irrelevant and I wasn’t even interested enough to know who is talking about what!5-	Some of the story events are pretty silly. Like for example how an actual cripple manages to escape or why do any android actually care about life?! They are basically immortals for god’s sake!6-	Game is unbalanced when it comes to difficulty. One the easy one I managed to finish the level in an average of 10-15 minutes as it seems enemies are dying from one or two shots. on the hard level though I expect a challenge but not to the fact I would literally hit a drone more than 3 minutes with my whole team to shot it down while one or two shot from it and I’m dead! Totally unbalanced specially without the ability to customize your weapon according to the situation. Basically the developers tried to do something new and they failed miserably

_childDocuments_.review: I was somewhat excited about the game before getting to play it, as on paper it looked like Battlezone (1998) - a game I thoroughly enjoyed in my teens.Sadly, this game disappointed the very first minutes. Let's see how exactly.The developers didn't even care to integrate the training mission into the story - instead, it's just a soulless faceless set of rooms. And that is going to be, unless you'll choose to skip the training, the very first experience of the game.Training mission aside, the game has the most boring and uninvolving start. Instead of following the nicely laid out by many, many other developers path of involving the player right off the bat - like it's done in the Last of Us and Arkham Asylum - V1 Interactive instead shows an extremely long intro movie. While you could have actually started experiencing the story through gameplay right away, you have to watch a dreadful introduction sequence. Now, I don't have anything against stunning introduction movies of Blizzard quality or the ones from the Final Fantasy games. Disintegration one, although being pre-rendered, is using the game engine level of graphics and is not nice-looking at all. Furthermore, it's rendered at - I would say - 1080p resolution and looks abysmal on the 1440p screen. It's also full of noticeable compression artifacts. Despite being very long, the intro movie still fails to color the universe of the game and instead tells a rather boring, unoriginal, 2-dimensional story.When the game finally began, it turned boring for me midway through the very first mission. You literally have to follow almost a corridor of the level and have copy-paste battles every 2-minute intervals.AI is extremely stupid, battles are anything but spectacular, the shooting experience does not have any pop to it and the strategic element is so simple, I wouldn't even care to call it strategy.I don't know how true this is, but the Wikipedia article on the game tells that the designers were inspired by Myth video games. I've only played Myth: The Fallen Lords and I still recall it being one of the most exceptional games of the time. It appeared very original and captivating to me. Now, Disintegration has zero originality. The blend of FPS and strategy was done before and every game (that I personally played) that did it before did it better. Nothing I have seen so far in this game is interesting or original. For instance, before each mission you can run around the hanger and talk to some random people there to get additional objectives for the upcoming mission. The guys that give you these objectives are not even voiced-over. It's literally an additional chore you have to do in order to get some additional goals. What prompted this design choice? Why not just automatically include these? Or why not then add some story behind these?In addition to all the existing problems, although there are plenty of checkpoints in each level, if you quit the game, not only you have to start the level all over again, you also have to talk to three random robots at the HQ to get those challenges I've mentioned before. And levels are 30+ minutes long, unless rushed. Basically, you are forced to spend around 30 minutes or lose your progress. This is the year 2020. Dark Souls - made in 2011 - allowed to save the complete state at any given moment outside the battle.This is not a AAA game, but graphics are pretty boring even when compared to your modern indie game.At this point, I have very little interest in continuing with this game. Even though the introduction movie was long, it still failed to hook me up on the story. As the gameplay was mediocre for my taste, I don't see myself coming back for that either.After initially writing this review, I've played the game a bit more. It literally kept delivering exactly the same sort of experience further down the road. The levels look the same and play the same. Every fight I've experienced so far felt the same way as the very first fight in the very first level.This game is not worth it even with a sale price tag.

_childDocuments_.review: It's engaging enough I guess, sort of like Halo if you were trapped in your vehicle, your regenerating shields stood 50 feet away from you, you couldn't run people over, and every time you missed a grenade throw it felt like the game was poorly programmed. Having a squad that you control while you also move around and shoot can work if there's a hefty incentive to do flanking maneuvers... but you fly so the cover mechanics don't work very well and the aggro mechanics are quite ambiguous so you can't use your pals (who regenerate, while you don't, remember) to pull aggro.This game says it's an RTS, but I think, if I were to rank all the shooters in the world by how well they scratch the RTS itch, this one probably might not get into the top half. It's not really very strategic as shooters go, and it doesn't really have the veneer of an RTS either... there's two resources you collect for upgrades, but the upgrades don't affect how you play, your loadout is predetermined by mission (actually this bit works alright, makes the missions feel a bit more diverse) and you certainly don't train units or build buildings.The intro in the campaign is also quite oddly designed. It wasn't until like two hours in that it reveals: there are actually plenty of other weapons for your gravcycle, you won't be stuck with the dinky SMGs forever; and, your enemies are the bad guys. The intro just establishes that your character has a slur for the antagonists, and that people are robots now? Really odd narrative choice there.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to love this game. I love games that explore unconventional concepts and ideas and I followed the development of this game closely. I honestly expected it to be quite fun. When I saw the reviews come in and then saw the price-tag I was immediately turned away, now having played only an hour of gameplay during its free weekend I am left with a knot in my stomach.My conniptions with the game:-Your units are brain dead, often times they'll just run around shooting whomever, sometimes your command button works, other times it doesn't. I've seen units run off into landmines and instantly die for no reason.-Commanding your units to target a specific enemy will send them out from their cover and into the open, putting them at high risk and often killing them, this also sometimes happens when you trigger one of their abilities.-Commanding your units is incredibly frustrating, you're basically telling them "stand in this general area" and praying they pick the big rock as cover and not the easily breakable wood fence.-The Grav-cycle is a cool concept, poorly executed. Your guns are weak and swapping to the healing nanites is a bit slow, making micro-management stressful.-You can often get stuck in trees when you try and boost away from enemy fire, often leading to your death.-Your units follow you, even though you commanded them to move to an area behind you.-I only played on normal but I felt so squishy, like I was constantly at 10% health.Only one hour and every single one of these thoughts ran through my head in the first mission. I wanted to love this game so badly and I still do. I love the aesthetic, have a super bias towards robots so I thought that there's no way I'll hate this game but I just, cant love it. Don't get me wrong, this game has SO MUCH POTENTIAL!!! that it honestly saddens me it isn't living up to it. It's my honest hope that the devs are able to sift through the negativity, read the honest criticisms and use those to make their game what people see that it can be and wish that it was. I'll forever keep an eye for when this becomes what it should've been because I want to love it. One day I will. Best of luck to V1 Interactive! <3

_childDocuments_.review: Such an awful experience. You see the trailer, expect a Destiny/Halo campaign, you get one of the worst story intro ever created. They don't explain you anything about characters, factions or lore, you're just there with an old black guy forcing robots to work for him until you hear the next mediocre joke and watch a loading screen. Graphics look old and characters voices are out of sync, making cutscenes look bad and unemotional. Fine, who cares about cutscenes, right? Let's get into gameplay. Well gameplay is slow, clunky, repetitive, boring (both gunplay and driving the cycle). There's no real strategy, you have some troops and only two buttons to command them, one for moving/attacking the enemy and the other one for special attacks. The rest of the job is being done by a poorly designed AI which no matter what will bring your troops in the middle of an open field just to get "disintegrated" (got it?), then you have to revive them every single time otherwise the mission will fail in 25 seconds. Levels are too linear with repeated arena locations where enemies spawn. After accidentally leaving the "mission area" I got 5 seconds to go back in, but I failed so the game reloaded my 10 minutes old checkpoint (instead of putting me back in the mission area). That's when I finally decided to uninstall the game and never touch it again, even if free.Conclusion: It's a indie game with an awful story/narrative, broken gameplay and sold almost like an AAA title. After only one month they gave it for free on Alienware Arena and it's currently free for the weekend, so don't waste your money or your wallet will be the only one getting disintegrated.

Character/NPC gameplayThe RTS experience is bare bones, its like they gave up half way and went 'this will do'. That's not even the worst part - your units will be getting blasted and won't take cover. Even if you move them to cover, the chances of them taking cover properly is slim. The animations are really lacking too. I know they're in a robot suit, but it doesn't look all that smooth. I would give them a command, they would do it, but after that I would just forget they're there, there's no connection - nothing to make me feel worried they will die. In Gears of War or Ghost Recon I didn't want my guys to go down, I would feel bad. But these little robot dudes? No worries. I would only remember I have them because the voice comes over saying "team mate down" or whatever.FPS is really fun - I enjoyed flying around and bring death from above, but after the first 10 or 20 minutes it was more like riding a turtle while it's on sand walking up hill. Beside that it was enjoyable in an annoying kind of way.Levels designLevels also feel like HQ - they're empty and boring. You start in a forest surrounded by cliffs & rocks, walk down a hill and find something that I think is supposed to be a building? It's like the framework for a building is there, but nothing was finished. There was nothing in the environment that made going from a valley forest, to strange not-quite buildings to open barren fields make sense.Audio/GraphicsSound design was amazing - being able to hear everything super clearly with no jarring sounds was great. The visuals are really smooth and I just had a great time staring at everything, especially how the textures blended together. PvPI'm not sure about this - I didn't find a match after sitting in the queue for almost 10 minutes.Overall, disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: RTS + FPS mix in sci-fi world7.5/10   RecommendedThe game is good. Well deserves a try. Here are the pros:1. Gameplay is really enjoyable and quite simple once you get the hang of it.Each mission throws a new mechanic at you and if you want to get all the quests/achievements, you need to figure out how to handle them.Disintegration has a few RPG elements, basically in the form of upgrading your squad with chips you scavenge for in missions.The short tutorial helps a lot. Then throughout the game using the scan mode in the world (press E) gives gameplay hints as well as story clues. The first mission tests your abilities. 2. I like how the difficulty levels you choose from vary from Story mode to harder. I chose Maverick (i.e. Hard) and it put me on my toes and made for great gaming sessions.3. Actual gameplay graphics look good + Cinematics are great.4. The game runs smoothly, even on a 4-year-old system (A big plus for me).5. Characters are light-hearted but not cringey. I hang around my squaddies between missions and quite like the banter between them. (Hey, anyone notice how the older dude is a carbon copy of Morgan Freeman's character from Oblivion? :)6. -I'm very interested in the story but I feel it isn't fleshed out enough. Maybe the devs will add an explanatory video/cinematic at the beginning to at least explain who are these Royun and why are they such ducks (not with a u).Kudos to the devs/publishers for the free weekend.I'm seriously considering buying this game. I don't think the price tag is very encouraging though. Let me be frank: $50 for a single-player game in a new IP, no less, isn't really a bargain.I'd love to see an end-of-mission report accessible and archived: first to see how I've done and second to go back and replay a mission if I want to 100% any side quest. Update: It's already there! (You see it from the console when selecting the mission). Update: Nov.2020 They removed multiplayer. Sad.I love this game :)

_childDocuments_.review: It was a decent game, worth the $20 I spent but I'm glad I didn't spend more. It was pretty short. Good to waste a little time and get a small story out of it. I put about 12 hours into the game, and much of that was trying to get through some of the more difficult missions. The gameplay was a little unbalanced in one or two missions, but nothing too terrible.The gameplay wasn't great. Nothing really new is introduced you haven't seen in any other game, and other things you have are missing. You're a gravcycle pilot, but instead of racing around in the gravcycle tearing it up in a sort of motorcycle meets hover-gunship death machine, you're stuck mainly floating around the battlefield, dodging some gunfire and trying to return fire and not die because you're too slow to really fly around, and not as powerful as you'd like to be. No real cover system to speak of, since you typically are floating above most of your enemies. You don't even have the ability to use your boost to damage enemies or break any of the destructible stuff on the battlefield really. The attempt to integrate more strategy into an FPS could've been awesome. An RTS where you can still blast the heck out of enemies directly. But it instead lacked in both areas. You cannot direct your units individually just tell all of them to choose one enemy, or move to a different location. You can only directly select specific units when telling them to use their abilities. So some of the more tactical applications where you could've separated out your force, dealt with different threats at once, and generally done what you do in a strategy game, while still pitching in and blowing the hell out of some of the smarter or stronger enemies weren't available to you. It made it very bland and not something that would've added a whole new spin on 'shoot em ups'.No upgrades to speak of either, or ability to kit your own gravcycle out the way you want to for each mission. Not that there were huge differences between the frames of each gravycle, from what I could tell. The story was kind of fun, but too short. I don't know if it was just because the game was so short, but the story was missing a lot of what would've made it good. Backstory, more interactions, etc anything that really went beyond a very basic storyline wasn't there. I do think there should be a Disintegration 2, but it needs to have something new, something exciting that makes gameplay a thrill (c'mon you're in a hovering motorcycle with guns. add speed and courses rather than small mission areas, zipping around in the air... the whole concept should be self-explanatory and intuitive!) , and definitely more storyline. I really want to know more about the world of Disintegration.

_childDocuments_.review: So I read about this game only a few days before it's release and immediately decided that I want to buy it. Why? The RTS/FPS (two of the genres I play the most) sounded awesome. Therefore I was on board on day 1 and finished the campaign within around 12 hours. Afterwards I wanted to give the multiplayer a shot. This first impression revealed several pros/contras:Contra:- Missing base building. Could've known about that but imho this just belongs to an classical RTS game.- You can't control your team mates individually. This should've given more tactical freedom, but on the other side, it's also a pro (see below).- Small player base so it is hard to find mates for MP.- Few skins for your troops in multiplayer.Pro:- Very fluid gameplay! Disintegration made me dive deeper into the hybrid genre so I tried several other games like Eximius and Executive Assault 2. Even though both are great games as well, both are much more stressful as you switch from commander/RTS to FPS sight a lot if you want to really enjoy both. And every time you feel like you miss something. Disintegration reduces the hybrid idea to first person with the control of your squad via right click, so as easy as it can get. From this point of view it also makes sense that you can only control your squad as a whole and no single units.- Very committed player base and active devs. Check out the respective discord and you will see that there're multiplayergames almost every evening...you just have to know, when.- Most important: The game is just fun. You can always complain about individual aspects of a game but all this matters less, when the whole picture is entertaining! And Disintegration fully delivers on this part.- 9 teams in multiplayer with different attacks/specials so you can always chose a different play style. This aspect even reminds of a hero shooter, just with gravcycles and a team you can command. So you got tanks, healers, snipers a.s.o.- Lots of unlockables in multiplayer (except for the skins as mentioned above)So, is it a perfect game worth 50 bucks? No and this has already been addressed to the devs, but imho it is not by far too overpriced. Do I regret the buy? Absolutely not! It's just fun to jump on your gravcycle, shoot robots and learn some tactics.This game is one of it's kind that uses elements from other games and combines them to something unique. If you got the money buy it now and support the devs. Otherwise wait gor a price drop to 30-40 bucks. One way or the other: It's definitely worth it!

_childDocuments_.review: It's hard to really hate the game, you can see that the devs have put a lot of care in the thing.It looks good, it sounds good, the cinematics and overall photography is remarkably good.But where the game fail, and HARD at that, is the game play.You get an hybrid shooter/rts where both are very, very flawed.First before going into detail here's one baffling point : You CANNOT choose your load out or team before a mission. You are just served a random assortement of weapons and teamate which is incredibly frustrating and feels extremely arbitrary.You gather 2 ressources in the missions, one is scrap and the other is chips.Chips are basically level up that you can spend on you or your team to increase flat stats, its boring and it's heavily limited by the level of the characters, so you often have more points than slot to use them.And the scraps... I have no idea. It looks like something you'd spend in some kind of crafting system, right? So... what's the point exactly?It's a very weird choice on the devs part since letting the player manage that kind of stuff would not only have been easy, but felt way better than having good weapons given and taken at the whims of the game.Then comes the actual gameplay.The FPS side is extremely weak. You are flying so you are constantly exposed, you got a dash, but is has an incredibly long cooldown, your weapon range from interesting to frankly boring, and since you can't CHOOSE them it just frustrating. You'll soon learn that the only skill required here is to abuse the vertical movement since unlike the vertical one, it makes the ai almost unable to hit you.The shooting itself gets very repetitive since you don't really have to aim for weak points (outside of the pretty borring bigger enemy) and everything, even the standard troops, feel very bulletspongy.The comes the rts side, managing the team of ground troopers you have with you.Welp, that side is basically a lie. You'll learly quickly that it's impossible to mange them.You can't give them orders individually, you can't them any standard orders you'd expect of a tactical rts like getting behind that cover or stuff like that, and since they move very, VERY fast their positioning overall doesn't matter. You'll just end up using on CD their "skill" that feel mostly like if you were the one doing them... except with a delay, and some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ tied to pathfinding and line of sight. Having them die don't matter at all beside forcing you to grab their corps (which should always be very close to you anyway) and they'll respawn in a handful of seconds.So in the end you'll just start to ignore them entierly, even not bottering to tell them to focus fire on something because if you are looking at it to tell them to shoot, it means that you too can just do that and will kill the thing faster than they'll do anyway.Probably the most anoying part is the mine/grenade the enemy some times drop on the ground. The only way to remove them is to shoot at them, but your soldiers by default move toward were you aim, thus making them jump right in the mines that will one shot them. It's probably the most frustrating thing in that game and shows how little understanding the gamedesigners had of their own game.Overall it feels like an incredible wast of opportunity, both on the shooting and the rts side.That dull gameplay coupled with the very limited, and frankly unintersting, pool of enemy makes the 12 missions (and around 10 hours) of gameplay a chore to finish.

_childDocuments_.review: After seeing the reviews here beforehand I went into this with low hopes for the game, but thanks to that I ended up not hyping up my expectations for this so I like to think I came into this with reasonable expectations. Saying that I've clocked in 1.4 hours of play time of the campaign for the first two missions and have some points to make about the gameplay first:Pros:+ controls are simple to fly around with and to command your units.+ the RTS (but more like an RTS-lite) element comes into play by choosing where your units move to and each have an individual ability that they can use with the hotkeys. simple and effective (but ends up having little variety but that's in the cons)+ is fairly easy to control and move your units and then moving on as yourself to lay down support fire on weaker groups of enemies + the FPS and RTSlite elements blend together nicely and is intuitive to play+ mission environments have a good variety in the missions that ive played. mainly a forest/farm area moving through open fields to narrow forest paths leading up to a wreckage of a crashed ship.cons:- There seems to be little variety with the abilities of the units being mortar, grenade, and slow time AOE ability(edit: there is also a fourth ability that i've noticed but never got to use). this is between the 4 story unit characters. hopefully in the future there can be a system that allow you to choose what abilities your units can have in the upgrade menu- The units only have one ability leaving no variety again. this could be forgiven if there was a second ability they could use similar to how mass effect handled it with a menu wheel popping up.- no way to individually move units to separate areas or to even make them take cover behind objects or walls. that would have been a good edition to the game.- there was an ability that was shown in the tutorial that i could preform in the game. it was to deploy a healing AOE. it worked in the tutorial but i was unable to do it in the campaign missions. i believe it was to hold Q while aiming at the ground.- sometimes it would seem like if i was too far away and shooting at the enemy then the first few seconds of connecting shots wouldn't do any damage at first before seeing the health drop down at the usual rate you expect. not sure if anyone else is experiencing this but that could just be my fault.for the story i only have a few things to say about it:1: the main story seems OK so far following the story of these 5 misfit characters that*spoiler**spoiler**spoiler*begrudgingly join together to band a resistance with some old the online aspect yet, i would say this game is fun and enjoyable for what it is, but i wouldn't recommend that this game stays at the current price it is, at £40. i would say wait for this game to go on sale or reduce in price to at most £25 and at least £20. that seems like a fair price for what the game is at this current time and hopefully the devs wont be too afraid to add major changes to the gameplay mechanics and other adjustments to further improve the feel and enjoyment of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Disintegration is a game for people who never got over the five Michael Bay Transformers movies.  Whether this is good or bad depends on your view of Bayformers.It has a fun ragtag group of robot* characters, some nice voice acting and character design, scenic and cinematic views, and mid-to-late 2000s humor.  It also has cliches abound, an assumption that players understand the backstory and lore and doesn't wait for them to catch up, a tough female love interest who is essentially there to be tough and female and a love interest, and mid-to-late 2000s humor.  Pulling away from the story for a bit (because in the spirit of Bayformers, this isn't really about the story and characters (although its a nice bonus); its about a blazing guns and the big explosions), there's an interesting combination of first-person shooting and real-time strategy; you're assigned guns and a squad at the beginning of each mission and have to adapt to what you have.  The gravcycle can feel very floaty (and not in the way it should, considering it does literally float), the guns need to reload way too much, and the squad AI can get confused sometimes...but in general the gameplay loop is very smooth.  The game scaffolds its difficulty, easing players in to the truly chaotic battles later on.  There's a lot of unseen potential, too; I would have loved to be able to pick and choose how to build my gravcycle or have more options for squad members (which might have been in multiplayer; I don't know, because by the time I got this game that mode had been removed completely).  But what we have is what we get.I, personally, love me some cool robot dudes.  I love me some cool robot dudes shooting other cool robot dudes.  I kinda wish this game had done better so that we could get a sequel that fixes up a lot of the janky bits (I personally choose to blame Epic and their exclusivity for the failure), but what is there is good.  It has that 2007 soulfulness.  It has unique ideas that could have used a bit more refining.  The overall product is fun and I would say the game is worth it if you like weird shooters. *yes I know they're human brains in robot bodies and that drives the lore and conflict, we could sit here all day and debate whether a human brain being the only organ in a mechanical body makes it robot or human, but for the sake of simplicity i'm going with "robot"(also i call dibs on doyle.)

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR Tactical gameplay is the main draw of the game, with lovable characters coming in second place, and an interesting but ancillary scifi story in the background.I'll elaborate on a couple of issues I see other people raising and then list my own pros and cons.Issue #1 - limited variety in (a) character customization, (b) enemy type, and (c) gameplay. (a) Character customization is limited to using chips that you find in missions to upgrade your squad in health, damage, ability recharge, health regen, and seemingly one unique upgrade per class.(b) Almost every mission introduces new enemy types. There are support enemies, melee and ranged enemies, flying enemies. This is more than enough to make the levels feel varied.(c) There are a variety of combat arenas which, in combination with aerial movement and the ground squad, make for lots of tactical flexibility: for example, you can send your squad into a building and fly around the outside shooting through the windows, you can set up flanks, play high/low ground, etc. There is a great deal of room for creativity. Combine that with the different abilities and mission objectives and I don't think the accusation of repetitive gameplay sticks to this any more than it does to halo, destiny or any similar game.Issue #2 - dumb AI/bad controls for squad.I have only noticed one instance where the AI feels dumb and that is when an enemy throws a proximity grenade. Your squad will stand right on top of it and not move. You can command them to move away and they will (and their response is very fast). Otherwise the AI is good. It does require attention, but I think that is by design (at least on the higher difficulties); you are supposed to play the grav-cycle AND your squad. This isn't an FPS with an AI squad following you—and I think the RTS comparison is not apt, either. This is more like an FPS where you control two characters in unison (the gravcycle commander and your squad). I also haven't had any problems getting my squad to do what I want them to; no pathfinding issues or "I didn't tell you to go there!!" or "I told you to stay there!!" moments.This won't help you decide if the price is worth it, but keep in mind that the dev team is around 30 people. Okay, now my pros and cons.Pros+++ The tactical landscape. It is very fun to set up ability combos and execute combat plans—flying around the battlefield and directing the flow of combat. It's great fun to flush out a group of enemies with your squad straight into the double auto-shotguns on your gravcycle, or to set your squad up on high ground and then fly around the side and flush enemies out into the open. Controls are also polished and intuitive.+++ The difficulty. Outlaw (the highest difficulty) is awesome; rarely do I play a game and feel like I need to utilize everything available to me in order to win. I think to beat missions on outlaw, you really need to use your squad optimally: combo abilities, use good tactical placement of both your squad and your grav-cycle (must be able to multi-task!!), and have a high level of situational awareness. You get a scanner (which is basically like a toggleable Widowmaker's sight from Overwatch (it highlights enemies through walls), except that it highlights explosives, too) and it is key to mapping out the battlefield: more often than not on Outlaw, I scout with my scanner and then set up my squad in an ideal position to take advantage of the enemy's position.++ Voice acting and character design are top notch. Each member feels unique even though they are robots without facial expressions. + The world is not incredibly inventive, but it is full of cool scifi ideas and the general presentation is engaging.+ The backgrounds are beautiful and the models, textures and animations look AAA tier even though the dev team is small.Cons-- Invisible walls everywhere. Part of the game is exploring for caches (which can contain the chips to upgrade your units), but it is usually not clear what paths are actually available to go down. This is exacerbated by the lack of a minimap or map (but I actually enjoy not having a minimap that I'm constantly referencing). - Getting your grav-cycle stuck. This is related to the first con but, despite the controls feeling very fluid, it's pretty easy to get your grav-cycle stuck in a hallway or on a piece of the environment if you try to fly anywhere confined (e.g. around the pillars in mission 3).- There are some problems with narrative flow (there aren't always great transitions between story points). I think this is largely due to the hubs; it feels disjointed to have the cutscenes play on interaction with the console instead of in a fluid motion from point A to B. There is also a bit of "disorientation" in understanding where you are. It might help to have transition cutscenes showing how you get to the hub or leave the hub, or a "map" that shows the various mission positions compared to the hub (though I kind of like not having a world map and experiencing the world in a more natural way). Overall, if hours of challenging tactical combat with a unique FPS system sounds appealing to you, I highly recommend Disintegration. If you want to play primarily for the story, I think you will probably be disappointed with what the game has to offer, but—as an accompaniment to the great gameplay—the story, and especially the characters, are more than serviceable.

Controlling may feel overwhelming at the beginning.Combat is restricted, which gets boring sometimes.Cinematic, visuals, voice and music are decent.Story is not that gripping.Facial expressions and voice synchronisation are quite bad.Encountered few bugs, due to which I had to play couple of stages multiple times.Multiplayer is not alive much. Played one MP stage after so many tries of matchmaking and unlocked two achievements related to that. I can't say much about multiplayer by playing it for just 5-10 minutes.I've got 100% achievements at around 22 hour mark. Played through the campaign again on easy to focus more on the story.Only recommended if it's available on a heavy discount.I won't buy this right now. It's overpriced even on 40% off.On top of that, it's not regional priced. (Why publisher?)Overall, this is an average game. There were some frustrating moments here and there (playing on second hardest difficulty) but overall the singleplayer was a pretty enjoyable experience. The chracters are decently written, the story is interesting enough to keep you playing, the gameplay is the right mix between FPS, RTS and comining it into innovative gameplay. But the cutscenes are at a level of 2010 AAA games, both graphically and also considering voice acting.I tried playing multiplayer too, managed to find 2 matches, both very fun, but other than that the multiplayer is so dead currently, that i simply couldnt find any games after waiting for 15 minutes. The multiplayer does show some promise to keep the game alive after singleplayer, with some nice customization (emblems and banners like old CODs) and a lot of different classes to try out.EDIT July 29th: The multiplayer is completely dead and since they aren't adding bot matches either I#m changing my review to not recommended, there is literally nothing to do in this game.

_childDocuments_.review: To be clear, I don't think this was a "bad" game but I don't think they managed to make the RTS/FPS hybrid work. I played through 4 or 5 levels (around 3 hours on the 2nd hardest difficulty) so I don't know if this changes or not later in the game but for those first few levels you have no control over your loadout. The  last level I played gave me a pair of shotguns on my gravcycle instead of the assault rifles but took away my preferred secondary that allowed me to heal myself I also couldn't pick which of the 3 soldier classes I got to bring on missions. While I don't mind weapon gradually being made available as the game progresses, I don't like not being able to choose the set up I engage a mission with.As far as the RTS portion goes, the controls felt decent and the units responded quickly which was nice, but the progression of units, unit variety, and not being able to pick your squad wasn't great. I understand certain characters not being available for story reasons but it didn't seem like there was any reason some characters weren't able to come on a mission, in fact one of the characters even laments that you don't bring him on one of the missions.If someone would like to correct me about loadouts being locked (perhaps they become customizable later in the game), I would be happy to adjust my review accordingly but as it stands I would only recommend buying this game on a steep sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Went in on a free weekend not expecting much. Robot racer dude and his gang of misfits really didn't appeal. But despite my reservations I found an enjoyable enough campaign with some absolutely lovely cinematics. The minimal command controls are functional and a little lacking feedback, the gun-play is frustratingly broken up by limited ammo, weapon cool down, and no ability to select the weapons you use for a mission. Which combined with the floaty sluggish movement of your vehicle can be very frustrating, especially when rough terrain will make you constantly fall out of the air or bump into things while strafing. However, despite those problems with the core gameplay, I still found myself compelled to finish and do think it was time well spent. Once I got past the initial impressions I found the world of the game, and even the character writing fairly compelling. It's definately a world I would love to see more of, though in future I would prefer more front loaded exposition, working alongside a faction for 4+ missions before a mission challenge told me who they were was ridiculous). Over all I would give it a 6/10. A decent enough experience, a little above average, despite its flaws. Wait for a sale, but it is worth your time. Oh and an honourable 10/10 for not experiencing a single bug, or major glitch in an entire campaign playthrough. Not many games I can say that for, especially when its such a polished game from a small studio.

_childDocuments_.review: Picked up and played a little of this game during the free to play weekend, so I do not own this, nor did I pay for itFor clarity, I have only played the campaign, and I have not beaten the campaign (didn't really have enough time in my schedule to justify playing all the way through, nor did I want to confirm my suspicions on what the multiplayer would be like after playing some of the campaign), but I do believe I can give some information. Not as much as others, such as SecretAgent:KiiN, who appears to have a much more detailed review of this game for potential players out there, so I recommend reading their review if your looking to decide whether pick this up or not.This game is an interesting style. I enjoy the concept of having to play a FPS while also having to control more than that. You are given a small squad, one where you have to control their movement, and can direct firing. This is difficult on occasion, as your troops like to constantly move ahead of you, unless you specifically tell them where to wait. In addition, this leads to further difficulties in playing. For example, when you are getting shot at yourself, and trying also to coordinate your squad to most effectively take down the vast numbers you are faced with, while also healing them and yourself. This makes for a very interesting split in your mind, where you need to be both good at FPS games, and also still have the mental ability to coordinate your troops and use all of their abilities.Personally, I am a fan of the grav cycle, even keeping in mind the complaints that I  with a majority of reviewers. The grav cycle doesn't get too high off the ground and it isn't as fast as I would like. Abilities take longer to come back than I want. Boosting your speed takes a hair too long to reset cooldown so you can dip in and out (maybe a fix is 2+ boosts, or faster cooldown, unless grav cycle speed is bumped up, to maintain some balance). The grav cycle adds some verticality to the game in a different way from standard genres, and I do appreciate that, but it needs to be fine tuned still. In addition, I was not able to choose what weapons I wanted on the grav cycle. Every campaign mission I played just gave me whatever grav cycle the developers designed for that mission, and it was a little annoying for me. For example, you were able to heal troops from your grav cycle, but in one mission the way to do this is a direct fire on your allies (which does seem to follow them a little, so no real need to worry about being super precise), and another mission it was a press and hold to activate ability that set down a healing zone for me and teammates. Was the change-up more effective, as I can now heal everyone, including me at once? Yes. Was it nice to have my entire previous way of playing uprooted, without being given the choice, nor really knowing about it until I was in a bad situation, trying to heal and couldn't figure it out, because it was a push and hold, instead of a point and click? Not at all.I personally like the mix of FPS, real time strategy (in a weird way) and especially the verticality of the game! It is very different from the standard mix of genres currently available, so a little time will be needed to truly learn and enjoy the game, but it can be done easily and quickly. However, I believe that this game still needs more polishing. I currently love the idea of this game, more than I love the actual game. IF this game was to get some serious polishing up, I do believe it could become very popular and successful, but as it lies currently,

_childDocuments_.review: Disintegration gives you pretty much exactly what it said it's going to give you in the description of the game. A first person shooter with real-time strategy mixed in and being extremely important at times.Instead of focusing on how much ammo you have you have to focus on how long it takes for your abilities to cool downHow long it takes for you weapons to rechargeAnd how much ammo you have in that specific shotWe're able to play this in three dimensions fighting things above below and in quite literally every direction of you. Well simultaneously controlling three to four troops who themselves have special abilities and health barsOn all hearing that at one point in time would sound.... Oppressive. IntimidatingBut once you get into the actual fray It almost becomes natural if you have a good idea of what you need to doOver the last 7 days I have spent about 8 to 12 hours straight playing this campaign. And in that time I have come up with good and bad about the game.Let's start with the bad parts.In the scenes in between missions the graphics are a little wonky. It looks almost as if each frame during movement was hand-painted. This results in an effect that if focused on even unintentionally. Can cause nausea and for me cause temporary motion sickness. during the same scenes if you focus on how the character moves between going left to right to left to right it's almost as if you are two steps ahead of the controller or the joystick or the keypad and going in a circle while being spun around. like you're stepping forward while on a disc that is spinning to the right left. For those who pay close attention to detail this can be rather distracting.Now let's talk about the good. In my opinion the storytelling was good. I went into this campaign knowing the bare bones having only seen one or two trailers and played the beta test for the multiplayer.I had absolutely no idea what I was getting myself into. Those some things I had to piece together myself for the most part seemed like the story would give you the information you needed when you needed it and let you figure the other stuff out. It was telling a story but still giving you the information you needed to understand the story. You weren't giving all the information up front that wouldn't have made it fun. You're given the information when it's relevant And I for one agree with that. It keeps you on your toes It keeps you paying attention to what people are saying. Banter between the characters during the gameplay and cutscenes and pre-mission gameplay gives small insights into what the story truly is and the backstories behind each character. In my opinion the gameplay was challenging and frustrating but at the same time on point. I couldn't afford to look away from the screen. I had to focus. I had to pay attention and keep an eye on every part of the screen at all points in time just to make sure that I had who I needed when I needed them.This created a minor panic but at the same time great exhilaration as I was rushing against the clock to heal my allies while at the same time telling them where to shoot and how to shoot.I would met at a first glance the final part of the campaign was lackluster however upon a second look I realized that it told the story just as it had to be told. There are of course things that I would change if I was in charge but those are things that I will leave feedback on in a later post. On all in my opinion this game is definitely worth playing. The campaign pulled me in and kept me guessing about some things while telling me upfront about others. there were parts of the story that I had to go searching for in order to understand what was going onI was able to get an idea of how the story should have gone without any guides I only played the game I never went to any other media about itAnd to be honest I'm glad I didn't look at any other media. It would have ruined the campaign for me. Even now the plot twists that take place still surprise me just looking back on themHowever due to the cons that I have already mentioned as well as a feeling of lacklusterness to the end of the campaign. I only feel comfortable getting the game currently a seven and a half out of 10 with room for improvement and a hope for improvement. This is a beautiful game and very clearly a work that came from the heart not necessarily the mind. I hope it stays that way

_childDocuments_.review: *BUY ON SALE* in my opnion, this game is probably worth $10-15, not $30. I tried this game out for the free weekend, so i didn't play the whole game. Pros:1. Interesting gameplay - It's a sci-fi FPS with RTS elements. you fly around in this thing called a Gravcycle and command your allies to do stuff (attack enemies, open stuff, use their special abilities, etc.) as well as shoot at things. 2. Decent story - you play as this guy named Romer, an integrated (brain in robot body) guy who escapes from a sky prison and joins a group of other integrated people to form a resistance against the bad guys, whose names I forget. It isn't something spectacular, but its alright. Cons: 1. Dead multiplayer - In my experience, i couldn't get into a single match of the multiplayer. I waited 7 minutes at most, but i couldn't get into a match. I was very let down by the multiplayer because there was no one online, 2. Gameplay can sometimes feel repetitive - sometimes the levels can drag on and feel repetitive gameplay wise because you do a lot of the same stuff. I also wish that you could take control of your ground troops and play as them in first-person, but also be able to switch back to Romer. 3. If you quit during a campaign mission, you loose all of your progress in that mission. 4. You don't get to pick your loadouts each mission - in each mission, you the game chooses who you go with and what equipment you use. Some of them have awesome abilities, and others have less-awesome abilities.  Final Verdict: I don't recommend buying this at full price, wait for it to be $10-15. Don't expect an amazing story on par with the first Halo, or The Last of us. Expect good gameplay that might feel repetitive. Don't expect a good multiplayer experience, or any multiplayer experience for that matter.

_childDocuments_.review: Where to even begin.This train wreck of a game is fundamentally Halo released for the first time but 20 years too late.The combat is not only clunky but an order to engage one specific target allows your entire squad to run out into the open and get slaughtered.  They just ignore cover.  That does not even take basic testing or programming to figure out that this is bad game design.  Dawn of War II does squad 100x times better than this and that has been out for many years.As for the character personalities... yikes.  They are random and poorly executed.  Most of the time they are in your face and you do not even know who these people are.  It is real cringe at times.  I bought cringe and frustrating combat with beautiful scenery. I'm sure eventually this could change and it's simply a blank slate, but it feels a bit bland. 3. I qued "quickplay" multiplayer for over 10 minutes with no games. There just aren't enough people playing this game right now.Pros:1. Unique and exciting gameplay mechanics. 2. Challenging.3. Very cool cinematics and story progression in the single player.Overall I would absolutely recommend the game, although I think they needed to do a couple things on release to make this game more accessible. I mean... it only has 31 reviews in the first 24 hours. That's CRAZY low for the kind of game this is. Anyway I believe the multiplayer and campaign should have been sold separately with maybe even a free to play multiplayer option. I strongly believe if there was a free-to-play option for multiplayer there would be tens of thousands of game downloads already and a lower price point of $19.99 for the campaign mode would have sold thousands of copies already after people got a chance to play around with the game in multiplayer. This is just a way smarter business model. I have friends I play other games with who like the looks of this game but they just can't justify spending $49.99 on it when so many other free to play games are currently available to play. Obviously I know developers need to grow their businesses and make a profit, but a $49.99 price point to even dip your toes into a game seems like such an antiquated business model at this point.

_childDocuments_.review: [My recommendation at this point is WAIT TO BUY, not NO as recommendation]I played DISINTEGRATION for +18 hours and completed the campaign story mode at maverick difficulty. This review will be updated when I complete 25 of gameplay as PVP sessions weren't open till game release date.Gameplay OverviewDisintegration is a shooting game with some RTS gameplay mechanics. It has 12 campaign missions and 3 PVP game modes (5v5) with various cosmetics options. Most of the gameplay you will be shooting enemies, targeting crews' special attacks, and collecting loot boxes.You play as a GRAVCYCLE (flying hover motorcycle) PILOT that fights and commands a ground crew. The "FLYING" DEFINES a lot of the gameplay experience.It is required a good view distance to manage the crew, which reminds the viewing perspective of an RTS game. Being far away from combat, naturally makes it LESS INTENSE than an FPS game. And... as there is an FPS character and vehicle to control, crew mechanics can't be as complex as RTS games.Here are the review toplines:1. Disintegration is an FPS game with RTS elements. It is less intense than an FPS and not as complex as an RTS game. 		2. The gameplay consists of shooting, controlling the vehicle, commanding a crew, and collecting loot boxes.		3. The game is full of cutscenes, every mission has one scene at the beginning and end. 		4. After the first half of the campaign mode, the game lacks novelty and new challenges. 	5. The campaign mode (PVE) is short when compared to the price tag, so to get an honest value out of the game, playing PVP is almost a requirement. _childDocuments_.review: I really wish I could recommend this. I stuck with it longer than most people, and there was some fun to be had in small doses. By the time you've played 2-3 missions, you've basically seen everything the game has to offer. Or even just making the levels more complex, with more opportunities for tactical positioning and choices in approach. But it just didn't happen.(Is it possible these get added even later in the game? Sure, but if so, they waited far too long.)So it turned into a situation where every mission felt fundamentally the same: Flying through linear corridors, fighting the same enemies in nearly-identical battlefields over and over, with the same aggravating spawn patterns... just with every mission adding more enemies, making battles go on for obnoxiously long, and with fewer and fewer opportunities to heal. So once it got to the point the missions were genuinely difficult, it felt like a pure grind, and there just wasn't enough good about the game to keep me going.

_childDocuments_.review: I was hesitant at first about this game due to its hybrid nature. Thankfully I got a free key to try it out.Initially the game was surprisingly refreshing in the way the controls and mechanics work. The tutorial was very helpful in setting you up for success and all controls are easy use. While you can deal damage yourself, your squad is your core. The graphics an great and the sound is solid. Even the writing is pretty good. However, what could have been a new take on Destiny or Mass Effect ultimately is ruined by the fact that game play is repetitive and your choices are forced. Essentially the game devolves into a go find this or destroy that. It is a linear path and the game guides you. Difficulty settings determine how much of a fight this is and in the long run again a plus for the game is the game will either give you the mission or make it damn near impossible to get past the first wave unless you got some Pro StarCraft 2 reflexes. Upgrades are based on the amount of scrap caches both in view and hidden. In a lot of cases there were caches hidden that forced replay of the level. In most cases this would be fine but when you have to literally replay the mission cut scenes and all this is a huge problem.With missions you are forced to take certain operatives leaving a huge desire in building a team that fits with your play style. While there were missions that specific operatives are necessary there were others where the forced choice didn't make much sense.Multiplayer is not apparently online at this point or if it is I wasn't willing to wait longer than 5 minutes to find a match.I hope that these things will be addressed as there is potential here for a very unique and good game, but this overall feels like a trial of capabilities to see if this studio can do bigger things. I hope to see a patch soon and give it another go.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy the core of this game; riding on the bike feels smooth and has a nice feel to it, ordering your units is definitely simplified but still gives you enough control that, especially in the higher difficulties, makes them a crucial aspect of the combat to learn and master while you're busy shooting as well, and as someone attempting to play on the highest difficulty, while I wish there were more checkpoints and in mission saves so that I could come back to a mission later if I leave, it is absolutely brutal sometimes but victory does end up being very satisfying for it, understanding your squad and the environment is key and it is just fantastic when everything is going well. I will say though that I'm still early in the campaign and especially the opening story elements feel pretty rushed so at least so far it's the gameplay that I think is going to be the selling point.Now the multiplayer....I love it, but there's already a population problem and while V1 and PD have said in the discord that they are looking into ways to fix this issue I do think that the buy in price along with the niche aspects of it are turning people away which means, as of this review, 4 days in, I'm struggling to find games; I won't downvote it for that though, because I know I love the multiplayer, and telling everyone "don't buy because dead" isn't exactly going to solve the issue, just know that I am enjoying the campaign so far and when I can play multiplayer I do genuinely adore it....It's the when that worries me, I truly wish perhaps more people felt like I currently do in regards to it or at least that there was some form of bot match with private match support because that would be amazing, until then though I have to make this positive review incredibly bittersweet; I genuinely hold this game is really fun, but I will say that if you're buying this just for its multiplayer that might be an awkward proposition right now, and I find that thoroughly heartbreaking.

First off, the game claims to be a FPS/RTS hybrid but thats not entirely accurate, it feels more like Mass Effect from the permanent seat of a vehicle - you can tell your team (npcs only sadly) to move to various spots , form up on you and use their abilities when they are off cooldown, sound familiar? The main difference is there isnt waist high cover in every combat region, and much of the cover that is around is destructible. There is a lot of areas that could use polish of course, so I can't recommend this game for full price but for its sale price sure (around $40CAD at the moment of this review) seems fair, I think if the developers stick to their guns and make a sequel thats better and more polished, emphasising a more RPG aspect and allow for more customizations they would have something special on their hands.

_childDocuments_.review: Note: I did get this game for free. Getting the game for free doesn’t affect my review at all.---In today's day and age with titles only being online-only and featuring no campaign, it's nice to see a company making a game with both online capability and a decent campaign for their game even though the campaign is kinda corny.The Disintegration campaign consists of 12 missions, if played on Regular difficulty it will take you about 9 hours to complete. Give or take if you die at specific missions as I did. Disintegration has many cut-scenes some are very detailed and some even detailed to real-life locations. It's a cliche hero story, though it was fun to play going through its humor moments to its sad moments.I do though have to say, $50 seems like a steep price for this type of game with out-of-game currency. Out-of-game currency? Sadly, you can buy skins with currency that you can buy with real-world money ranging from $4.99, $9.99, $19.99 and $49.99.I do agree that the developers need some sort of income to help develop this game further with free DLC and content, though I feel like they could have done it a better way. Maybe a Battle Pass similar to Call of Duty: Modern Warfare with new weapons where you can earn new Gravcycles through this Pass. For those without the Pass or if the Pass has ended, the user can unlock this Gravcycle through in-game challenges.Multiplayer is fun just like the campaign where you can control a crew but instead of doing it all alone, you have teammates on your side this time. Hopefully, cross-play with console players gets hammered out soon so the player-base for multiplayer can stay active. On a disappointing note, if you beat the campaign, you don't get any exclusive banners, badges or emotes for multiplayer use. At the moment, Disintegration doesn't feature any private servers so you can't host your own games / tournaments.Based on that, the game is not worth $49.99, I would personally price it at $29.99 or $19.99 like the Surge titles.Like my reviews? Follow my  and get updated about my latest reviews.

_childDocuments_.review: I believe that there's nothing inherently wrong with the game. It looks good, sounds decent (apart from missing OST), controls are responsive, weapons and abilities are distinctive, units mostly go where i want them to, level design is decent, and story doesn't drag on and I like how it starts in media res without explaining too much.Most importantly, it's a fresh take on shooters being a hybrid between FPS and RTS, and that is interesting by itself.That being said, game feels plain, like it suffered too much adjustments from publisher or conservative business persons.To fix this, campaign could use some overhaul. First, I would give the player freedom to pick soldiers and weapons for missions (perhaps with some restrictions so not to break balance in existing missions). I also feel that allowing user to upgrade flight capabilities (speed, maneuverability) of their vehicle would help, especially in later missions, where's a lot of air combat which sometimes feel slow and plain.I really hope this game gets some kind of sequel or somebody else makes similar game to explore the ideas further.

_childDocuments_.review: i play this game during the free weekend, so that might clouded my judgement. That's my disclaimer.Gameplay is actually pretty interesting, the genre-mixing is actually working but not in the way it should be.If you boot this game up and expecting a good RTS gameplay and nice fps icing on top, you'll be disappointed.This game feels like FPS with RTS part as a crowd control abilites and side mini gameThe game feels like they compromise too many unique RTS gameplay mechanics such as micromanaging, positioning for the sake of good FPS gameplay flowMaybe the V1 think micromanaging might kill the fps pacing, who knows?On top of that, the game don't allow you to choose your setup for different mission. You just need to run with either 1 of 3 gravicycles the game had with 2-4 from 6 of the available crews, depend on where you are in the campaign.and by this way they can manage to introduce you different units and abilities without overwhelming the playerDespite very small numbers of enemy type, the game manage to challenge you with making you with different lineup or sometimes take out some mechanics to challenge you in either the RTS part or the FPS partDoes it make the game challenging? Definitely yes. Does it make the game interesting? I can hardly agreeFrom the devs interview, this game was actually developed to be a RTS game but due they mixed the fps part later on to make the game stand out. Which i might commend that they actually succeed.The production is actually decent, but not great. The visuals, musics, character designs, and abilities are decent with some gut weird quality drop, here and there.Sometimes they forgot to put in the music despite having really nice soundtrackSometimes they cut the cinematic very weird ways, the pacing feels off with so many good lines interspersed with long silence, or they change the mood too fast you don't know what to feel.This game has so many late 90s and 2000s influences all over it and it seems like they really not notice how out of touch they are with the gaming community todayI feels like this game might be working better if it was published in late 2000s, when player expectations were low and anything that is playable with console command is eaten up by the mass audienceThe game was developed by 30 developers without crunch, published for 3 platforms and tried to present itself as a AAA titles. I don't know how to feel about thatV1 actually tried so many things, many studio did't triedBut at the same time they really struggle to make this game stands on it own without getting it judged by the market's expectation, and i find the lack of polish and different encounter to be the game's weak pointThis game is actually worth playing just to experience it as a case study of genre blending.In the age where every developers seems to go for the safe bait, i find this game to be a great endeavor, despite not meeting the market expectation.Should you buy?at any price you want, set your expectation low and wait for a deep salesBig claps for Marcus Lehto and V1 interactive for this beautifully foolish endeavor, i take this game with more heart pour into it more than whatever bungie is doing now

The game though is fun, old school fun! The control of the troops on the ground is very easy to use, so they dont get in the way. The grav-cycling about is fun although it can get chaotic when lots of troops are around you.
