_childDocuments_.review: Got this product for free but i wont give you a biased opinion (i'm an italian reviewer for multiple sites).Darwin Project is a game that deserve to be played cause he's different from the average battle royale.The game is tense and full of tactics and, despite only two weapons (bow + axe), with the crafting wheel you can fully customize your game experience and strategies. I'd say that this game is a great example of "Easy to learn, hard to master" title. You can play aggressive and track the others, or you can lurk in the snow waiting for the right time to strike. The choice is yours.The gameplay is also arcad-ish and offers lots of fun. Fast 7-10 min games where, even if you are behind, you can do epics comebacks (with good aim and good strategies).Can't wait for the incoming 2v2v2v2v2 mode (at the moment you can only play Free For All or you can be the Show Director).You can create private matches already (2+ players) if you just want to have fun with your friend!The Show Director is fantastic and you can shape the game like a dynamic TV version of Hunger Games. If you are a streamer (Twitch or Mixer) you can let the crowd interact with this title to make every game unique and fun.Technically the game is pretty solid for being an EA title. I Crashed only 1 time in 8 hours of play. With an old Rig i'm playing 1080/60fps medium/low (5 presets available) with rare drops to 45-47.I will buy the game on the Xbox One as well (to support the developers, crossplay not supported atm) cuz it really deserves a lot.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually review games but this really does deserve it. For multiple reasons but I feel like I should set the record straight.Darwin used to be 15$ but just became F2P and many of the negative reviews are complaining about this. About how they want a refund or how they got scammed. In no way did you get scammed. This game was most definitely worth the 15 dollars however the playerbase just wasn't big enough to let players meet anyone new. Plus you get compensation for peviously owning the game. You will receive the Founder’s Pack containing 2 Legendary sets, 3 Legendary Axes, 3 Legendary Bows, a full jumpsuit collection, and 5 Fan Gifts on the 24th. So how exactly did you get scammed because that's a lot of items. Not to mention this is an Early Access game and even though it is one of the best Early Access games out there, you knew what you were signing up for.So on to the actual review.The game is honestly amazing. One of the best Early Access games you will ever play. It is a battle royale game similar to Fortnite and PUBG however there are many twists. Such as1: the fact that there are no guns or grenades or anything of the sorts, you have a bow and an axe. 2: you can craft the majority of the things you will need3: there is a survival aspect which is the coldness. you have to stay warm4: there is only 10 players instead of 100 and the map is much smaller5: zones close one by one instead of a storm or gas closing in6: there is a director that can somewhat influence the outcome of the game. and i say somewhat for a reason7: people watching streams of the game can vote for certain director actions8: you can track down other playersAnd those are just the major differences between this and other BRs. So this game immediately stands out from the pack but another reason it greatly stands out from the pack is the dev crew. They are one of the best development teams out PERIOD. They have a discord in which they listen to the community HEAVILY. Your voice will be heard there. They help out people with game issues, support the members and listen for feedback. Even adding new features that are frequently requested or that they like. Not to mention the amazing community in this game. Hospitality is all over the place. There is minimum toxicity which can easily be reported so getting tilted by others isn't something that happens much.All in all I fully recommend this game giving it a 8/10 and thata's only because I think a game can always be improved. In this case the power of the director should be toned down from "somewhat influencing the outcome" to "barely influencing the outcome".

_childDocuments_.review: Brilliant. Absolutely brilliant. I'll do two quick reviews, one for each role in the game.TL;DR: If Fortnite and Hunger Games had a baby, added a simple and tactical survival mechanic, and added in a really, REALLY great community, this would be it.As an Inmate: A game with a very simple premise, just enough depth to allow you to sort out your own playstyle, and an emphasis on tactics and skill over luck... with just enough of a luck factor thrown in to make it very interesting. I don't even know how many battles I've had that were close and intense and came right down to the wire. It's a very well balanced game. The clashes are great - when two people hit each other with their axes at the same time, they'll deflect and bounce off each other instead of just each hitting the other. Axe swings deflect projectiles, too - it makes for seriously good combat. There's only a couple "tricks" and you can do just fine without axe-teleporting anyway...As a Director: THIS IS SO MUCH FUN. I'm a shoutcaster, so this plays to my strengths already, but oooh man. Being Show Director is even more fun than playing as an Inmate, for me. This is where you really get to see the awesome community Darwin Project has - when you're watching two people battling and their zone begins to close, and they stop and help each other escape safely only to continue their battle once they're both safe and ready, it's awesome. Or seeing three players duking it out in a small room, only for a fourth to literally dive in the window and wipe them all out, out of nowhere.And it's FREE. Oh man. Install this right now.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great. It fixes everything that's bad about other battle royale games, namely:- RNG. The outcome of the game is not determined by whether or not you got a good gun 5 seconds earlier than the opponent who spawned right next to you. Because people don't spawn next to each other. Nor can you get an insane advantage over your opponents by getting more lucky with loot, seeing as your main tools are still an axe and a bow, which are available from the beginning of the game, and the loot you are getting will always be very similar to the loot everybody else is getting, because it consists mostly of 2 basic resources which you can use to craft whatever you need at the moment;- Looting. Some people might not see that as a bad thing, but for me, constantly getting new weapons, which might just be slightly better or worse versions of the weapon you already have, bullets of all sorts, other stuff like that, and managing your inventory just isn't fun. It's not a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ rpg. Although in my opinion it's not a fun mechanic even in rpgs, for that matter. In Darwin Project, the process of looting is very simple, because, as I said before, most of the loot is just wood or leather. You get it and craft what you need. Apart from that, it can be one of the three boosting items, an upgrade to your gear, and that's about it. No need to mess with inventory at all. Love it;- Killing from huge distances. There aren't any open spaces on the map. It's all covered in hills, cliffs and big ass trees. And you also can't really snipe from afar with a bow. And one, or even two shots from a bow are not enough to kill you in this game. So you'll always get a fair fight;- Camping. In Darwin Project the problem of sitting in the bushes is solved rather elegantly. The tracking system allows you to learn the player's current position by lookiing at the things they left after crafting or looting something. There are actual tracks in the snow in this game too. And if you get lucky and the area where you did most of crafting and looting gets closed, you still can't hide for long thanks to the heat system. Eventually you gonna have to build a fire to not freeze to death. And that fire will let everyone in a big radius know where you are. And the director can also make you are target of a hunt, which, I believe, lets everyone know where you are.On top of all that, this game also has a very unique setting, cool traps and powers, and the show director system, which I'm yet to learn about. All in all, I'm really impressed with this game. Can't stand other battle royale games, but this one is so much better. Highly recommend it.The only things that bother me are the main menu screen and the loading screen. They look ugly as hell, please change them.

_childDocuments_.review: Besides a few small issues, the Darwin Project is the most unique and best take on the Battle Royale genre since the original ARMA 3 Mod. In This rendition there are only 10 players in a quadrant styled arena. This, by itself, makes the rounds much more "personal" in a way. The game is 'controlled" by a director who goes around talking to players and causing events to happen. Closing "zones" so they can't be re-entered (this game's version of the circle in Fornite and PUBG) and causing little game events like Nukes, Anti-Gravity, and a Manhunt. It makes the games more unpredictable, but in a way that feels fair as opposed to the RNG nature of Fornite and PUBG. Most of the directors are, for the most part, entertaining although occasionally you'll get those directors that attempt to take you down personally if you are racking up many kills by healing people mid battle etc. Although this never felt completely unfair as he could have easily done the same to myself. Its a social game and rewards communication between you and others in the game either banter or asking the director for stuff. The combat is a perfect example of "easy to play hard to master" where you are only given two weapons, the bow and the axe. There are no direct upgrades, and all of the "damage buffs" can be easily obtained by changing which arrows you craft/ which axe buff you have in your Crafting Wheel. I never felt like I was at a major disadvantage in any fight, even if I was outclassed many times by others who had great aim. The combat feels floating and smooth which works (technically) wondrously for the most part. Hits pack a punch and the game informs you when anyone does damage to anyone on the map which makes it fun to strategize where you want to go and who you want to interact with. There, of course, are a few issues with the game's current state. One of the biggest issues is the hitboxes can be downright deceptive at times. Falling from above onto someone, you are much more likely to get a hit then someone looking up swinging at you. There have been also some weirdness with the rage of mele hits that feel random. Sometimes an enemy two feet from me doesn't hit me, but I can hit him. Little issues like that, that do not kill the experience, but are annoying nonetheless. Also it is really easy to "force chain" hits when you corner someone into a house, where unless you stop attacking you will be able to "combo" the enemy to death. This feels unfair as it leaves the defender at a unswayable disadvantage. There are also some oddities, like how wildlife falls from the sky occasionally, it makes it all look a bit cheap. There is also a slight lack of content. Besides playing over and over (Which I don't have an issue with 6.6 hours in) there aren't many things to do past your first few games. There is one map and that is it. I can't call this a total "issue" yet as its still in Early Access (released a week or so ago) and I am sure that they will be beefing up the content. Don't let the low player numbers fool you (555 late at night to 1.8k during midday) it is never an issue getting into a game (partly due to the small game size, only 10 required players makes up to 55.5 active games at the most dead of night) check it out! It is well worth the cheap 15$ price tag!

_childDocuments_.review: So, in this game, you can play as an Inmate or a Director.  As an inmate your goal is to be the last one standing, however many obstacles are in your way. For example, you have to build a fire every once in a while-  because you can freeze to death. The Fire produces smoke which reveals your position to any players that look in the sky. You have 2 weapons, a bow and arrow, and an axe. The Bow and Arrow does 150 damages by default (you have 600 health) and the axe does 150 as well. You can upgrade the damage it gives by sacrificing two woods and two leathers. There are trees and chairs scattered around the map that you can harvest to gain those materials. There are also zones, if you are inside a closed zone (The Forbidden) You will start freezing to death.  As a Director, you are in the game to spice it up. You gain one action point per minute, with those action points you can purchase certain ability's that will spice the game up, those abilities include -Turning off Gravity 5 Action Points, set off a gravity storm in the entire arena, the jump height is increased by 20% for 2 minutes and 21 seconds. -Nukes Costs 5 action points, gain the ability to set off a nuclear bomb in a zone. Once you place the nuke down, inmates have to vacate that zone in 41 seconds or they are instantly knocked out of the game. -The Ability to close a zone There are Seven zones. You have the ability to close 2 of those zones for 3 action points, you can choose what zone you want to close. If an inmate is inside a zone, their cold meter starts going down, so they start freezing to death. Goes handy with nuclear bombs. -Manhunting an inmate You can purchase a manhunt with 5 action points, the manhunt will trigger immediately on the player you choose. What it does is it places a bounty on the man hunted inmates head, and the position of that inmate is shown to all remaining inmates. Manhunt cannot be used if there are only 2 inmates left. -Placing an Electron You gain the ability to place an electron on 1 position out of 8 in the 7 zones, an electron is a rare crafting material which grants the ability to either Teleport, Go Transparent or Go Invisible. You can also craft a turret, which I have not figured out how to yet. -Heal, Speed Buff, Warm Up or invincibility. You can also help the inmates as a director too. If you choose to do this, you can either Heal them (2 AP) Speed Buff them (3 AP) grant them invincibility for 20 seconds (4 AP) or Refill their cold meter (1 AP)  The Directors appearance is a huge freaking drone. The Director can also talk to the inmates, if he is within a 50m range of them. I personally have roleplayed as jigsaw while the director.  because you know, do you want to play a game.  So, do I like this game so far? Absolutely! The Beta ran Extremely smooth for one, I didn't freeze once, and it all around is just a good game! However, the queues for being a director were HORENDUS. I had to wait about 15 minutes to get a game, but as an inmate you instantly got into a game. Also, if you want to play with friends, you have to be in voice coms, but they are planning on adding a custom game system soon, and me and my friends are looking forward to that. Well, one of the only things I found wrong with this game was that in order to really have fun, you have to have a microphone. People who didn't talk ended up dying first, just like in SOS or Friday the 13th, you have to have a microphone.  Nice job Scavenger studios!

_childDocuments_.review: I am 32 years old.My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and we adopted our son together. Both are now 4 years old.When we were going through our separation, I felt lost and unhappy. I was self-destructive. One day, I was so angry with everything spiraling out of control that I punched a concrete wall in a moment of overwhelming emotion. This resulted in breaking my fifth metacarpal in my right hand—the hand I worked with, played games with, and used to carry my children to bed—the hand I desperately needed to ensure I could continue providing.Upon learning the severity of the self-inflicted damage, I became almost suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man, with no history of depression or anxiety. I had never experienced anger outbursts, nor was I the type to break down and cry, but I was in a tough situation that truly prevented me from seeing the light on the other side.With nothing better to do, I looked for a game I could play WITH ONE HAND while recovering. Somehow, I stumbled upon this game and read some of the comments. I decided it was worth a try... I must admit I didn't beat the game, nor did I play as much as some of you. In fact, I may have played this game for only a day or two. That being said, after doing so, I had a new joy and hope for life. I managed to leave behind the pain and suffering that had been thrust upon me. I could experience the joy and happiness of other people. I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥ minutes listening to this music, long enough to realize that I would be okay.After realizing this, I turned off the game and went back to work. My hand hurt a lot, but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so sorry for myself and became the father I needed to be at that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving like.Today, I am close friends with the mother of my children. We don't fight, argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents and friends.Now I have 3 children. My third child is, wait, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my separation, and we just unexpectedly stumbled into each other's lives. We have been dating for a year and are very happy together.Moral of the story: you never know what life has in store for you, and if I had given up when all odds were against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.Thank you.

Preferring players over others, making it unbalanced. Etc. All in all, it's a really fun game, which has its own learning curve. Definitely pick it up while it's this cheap, and you better start practicing with the bow and arrow. :)Cheers.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: typosComing to this game after playing other battle royales such as PUBG or Fortnite, the game feels as smooth as a baby's butt. The graphics are cute, nifty and at higher graphics settings, beautiful. I've been hyped for this game since I found out about the open beta.Playing as a prisoner in this hexagonal post apocalyptic winter arena gives me that Hunger Games vibe, except it's more focused on gameplay than story, of course. Speaking of gameplay, the game runs smooth and the replayability feels endless because every match is different than the previous one. Unlike PUBG, looting, while helpful, isn't crucial to win, you already start with your weapons and those don't change, everything you loot is just variables. The map is well built and always feels fair and random.As a show director, as long as you have a good rating, you get to affect the map, players, and electronic drops (which are basically airdrops that give you a special power). Your job is to be entertaining and fair. I like to help out the players who seem like they would fail without my help, have a nice small talk with the players and overall make sure everyone has a fighting chance.The game has an entertaining announcer that reminds me of GLADoS with its wits and snarky comments such as "You can die tomorrow" when you win.I do have one complaint however, and it's that in the main menu it tells me I'm getting a solid 70 ping, but when I'm in a match, I magically have 200+ ping which is kind of annoying, but still very much playable, I guess.I received this game for free so not many complaints from me, overall, I enjoy 90% of my matches which is more than I can say for other games in my library on which I have pegged over a thousand hours (coughcoughcsgocoughcough).Thank you for the free game, I hope you do well in your sales, this game is definitely worth the price in my opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: beta was fun, really enjoyed it. The game is good, and I do recommend it, but NOT right now. I'll explain. Wait for the game to go free-to-play before you get it. I personally don't see the game lasting long unless it goes FTP, but that's my opinion.The game is smooth, runs well, and the overall concept is brilliant and unique.I really like directing, and the overall concept of directing. Directing was the main attraction to me, not to mention I enjoy the BR genre.but as it stands the only people who actually play this game are twitch streamers, and the people who no life it. If you get this game, prepare to get rekt in your face for a few games, as the skill difference will be apparent. If you're going to try to just have a casual experience right off the bat, this game isn't for you. My biggest quarrel is with the knockback system. When you get hit, you go flying, and people can lead another free shot on you if they have any common sense. This is even worse in the low gravity zone (think Flying Scoutsman from CS:GO, because that's EXACTLY what this director-enabled zone effect is. You fly around trying to axe each other or shoot one another. I feel sorry for the poor soul who gets melee'd off the ground and shot with an arrow, because you will be sent flying across the map). You're basically a sitting duck in the air, and it sucks to be in low-gravity. You're better off staying grounded unless you absolutely have to jump.I feel like this game could use a "ground slam" mechanic to counteract the knockback and bouncing in low gravity. I like the fast paced fights, I just hate how there isn't much counterplay to getting knocked back, especially if the director cucks you and buffs your attacker.The female character is very "meh" at the moment as well.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a big fan of the BR style games ever since I got into the Hunger Games series because that whole idea is very intriguing. But Darwin Project is as close an adaption of that model than I have seen so far, the director role when done correctly is super fun and coupled with a director that has a decent viewership it adds that extra Hunger Games dimension of trying to win favor. The gameplay is solid if not just a little lacking in equipment in its current state and I hope the devs add a lot more options for the director to utilize during a match. _childDocuments_.review: This game has an incredible potential thanks to a very clever design that get rid of everything I hated about other battleroyale. A lot of good ideas that still need to be fine-tuned for balance though, but overall the game is very well produced. It's very fluid, not a single technical issue in 6 hours (+ as much time watching streams), no freeze, no lag, no frame drop. What's more, I trully love the graphics and the models (lacking diversity right now but the EA is only 6 days old). The private match and spectator mode are truly efficient, better working that most multiplayer games, same for the matchmaking : 10 sec in average to find a game. It might seems silly in 2018 but yet it feels good to have a game that is actually robust, everything is smooth, quick and without that feeling that everything might or might not crash at anytime (even though I have a great PC it happens on lots of game, to stay on BR : PUBG for instance, even on low because it's not just graphic related).The streamer friendly system is really doing some good to the game but it also might make non-streamer players feel like they are "inferior" for not streaming and having a community behind them to use the twitch integration. However it is an absolute pleasure to watch private matches streams among streamers/friends.I really hope this game will have the player base it deserves and that it will keep it until the release and long after, unlike so many before that had their hype moment in EA before disapearing in the abyss of Steam 2 weeks after.Good job Scavengers Studio, keep it that way !

_childDocuments_.review: Updating this review to add some extra contextI've played this game ever since the alpha stages. It was an extremely impressive Battle Royale/Hunger Games/Game Show style game that immediately peaked my interest, especially when the Show Director mechanic was shown, I was instantly hooked. A major issue with the game though was a massive lack of marketing and promotion. One trailer at E3 and that was pretty much it unless you followed the social media accounts. The playerbase was dying fast because there was nobody new coming in, and the game had a lot of issues at the time that weren't being worked on (Example: There was no tile system before, so the map was completely identical before that was fixed, so almost every game felt the same unless there was a good show director, which even that had it's issues). After MONTHS of players asking for it as well, the devs made the game Free2Play, but at the same time removed a lot of features it had before when the game fully launched (No duos at launch when they've had it for the longest time in early access and a very piss-poor Battle Pass system)A MAJOR issue with this game though is the dev team. This team is being led by the same people who worked on ACE: Arena Cyber Evolution, a 3v3 multiplayer game that, much like this game now, was abandoned due to nearly identical issues with a major lack of marketing and overall the dev team not giving a damn about the game, so they've abandoned Darwin Project to most likely work on another game that will most likely be abandoned after a couple months or a year much like all of their games beforehandDo not play this game or any other games made by this studio. So many amazing games with great potential that gets abandoned before it could ever even get a chance.

_childDocuments_.review: The combat system is simple but flawed.You get an axe, and you get a bow.You can bounce arrows if they hit mid-axe-swingbut the .5 second startup does not allow you to bounce arrows. Those very small moments are what matter, so your best bet you have is to hope you swung at the right time while hoping to make contact with an arrow of which only benefits you by negating damage and giving you another arrow. All while the attacker is far enough away to fire several more without problem.There is very high reward and very little risk for using bows, you slow down slighty and that's about it...  not like slowing down is going to hurt you much when both melee and ranged attacks send opponents flying the same distance.They recently introduced a combat roll, allowing you to quickly roll in any direction. But this takes up 33% of your stamina, something incredibly important if you want to close the distance on that guy chucking pointing sticks in your direction.  Plus, a well-timed combat roll doesn't negate damage, it just makes you change directions. So you can both waste your energy AND get shot.Your health is also incredibly low, with melee only doing *slightly* more damage that can be matched anyway with a headshot from an arrow.You'll deal 200 base melee dmg and 150 base ranged damage. With a health supply of around 600. That means it'll take 3 melee swings or 4 ranged body shots to eliminate someone. A very small difference during any fight, assuming you aren't even wounded from a previous battle or damaged from traps.Even with craftables, the only things that are going to help in a fight is primarily CC (stuns and slows), nothing very interesting and you get to land a free hit each time. Though deploying these have a cast time, but the timer is short enough for anyone to run around a corner and slap down a massive tripwire that'll make you fall flat on your face for a short period. During my gameplay, I have yet to see any traps that are actually visible, so it just leaves you to guesswork to hope you hit something that could've gotten you killed. Again, being able to spot these isnt even beneficial, it's just "ok you don't die this time I guess."The game is fun... Most of the players I've met have good sportsmanship... And I believe that there's potential for the combat. But having the whole thing down to pure luck with axes and basic aim with bows is just incredibly unfun.

_childDocuments_.review: First off I want to iterate that Darwin Project is an Amazing game, well done for an early access project and should be kept in mind if you are looking to purchase. While the Darwin Project still has and needs lots of growth, it is truly a great start into the Battle Royal arena. You need to understand that while the Darwin Project has similarities to Fornite, PUBG and H1Z1 that does not mean it is aimed at being like those Games. This game shares the Battle Royal fun that has hit the gaming seen over the last few years, however it has it own Twist and Turns to figure! The game takes place in the Ice Lands as I call them and the the player count at the moment is way lower. But the concept to be the last man standing and using your surrounding to do so is the same. The maps play out in similar fashion with a collapsing areas and time count downs.  At the moment, I have seen but one map and customization is minimal. However the cost is cheap and the game play is fast. So that is a bonus, but I find its major flaw being that there is no controller support at the moment. On the other hand you gain loads of control through hot keys and a easy to use crafting wheel.   All in all this game is still in development like most others, however I would say do not give it a COLD should, infact try it I am sure it will warn your game loving heart!

_childDocuments_.review: I have leveled up to level 13 by now I think and so far it's very good. There's a lot of people with microphones and I recommend not to play it if you don't have a microphone because most of the fun from this game is through interacting with the other people while fighting them or talking to the game director.  The game is very different from other battle royales right now, and i'll explain now.When you join a lobby before a match begins you can hold "Q" to see your equipment, which you can change with ease. You can change the type of arrows you use, the type of cloak you use, the type of boots you use and choose three abilities from about 9 different ones. When you start in a match you already have your weapons, an axe and a bow. You can farm material by cutting trees for woodand cutting worn down chairs for leather. You can craft arrows, cloaks, boots, and upgrade your axe with those materials. Game directors (which i'll talk about more later) can place down electronics, that you can gather so you can use an ability. As a game director, instead of playing within the match as a survivor you can instead, place down electronis, talk to the survivors, close xones, and much more. I mainly play as director and do quizzes with people so if they get it right i lt them choose what they want me to do.I highly recommend this game for battle royale players and for people who just like conversations with others.

_childDocuments_.review: This review is in this game's early stages still. Darwin Project kinda did like Fornite BR did in regard to PUBG...it offered such a cool take on BR games that was a breath of fresh air to PUBG.So we have crafting, which is great because you can customize what you'd prefer for your matches, but you can always change that up inbetween matches.You're in the cold, so your warmth meter adds a survival element to the game, which is interesting. Don't worry, you can craft stuff to slow your warmth meter from decreasing at a rapid rate or just build a fire to regenerate it!There are only 10 inmates per match so the games almost never go over 15 minutes, at least in my personal experience. The map is still a decent enough size that you can always find materials and chests lying about!Did you ever get annoyed with weapon variety in other BR games due to the overwhelming assortment of armaments to choose from? In Darwin Project, you needn't worry any longer! You have 1 melee and 1 ranged weapon. You can craft a type of arrow that suits your play style, as well as an axe upgrade that could maybe give you a damage boost or even heal yourself when you loot other players!Now, that does sound amazing, doesn't it? Let's add in a Show Director that can change the course of the game by closing zones off, lowering gravity so you can jump super high, or even give you the ability to loot a crafting material that isn't easy to come by...an Electronic! The Show Director probably has a microphone and will likely swing by to say hi to you. Now more often than not, the Show Director is a pretty chill guy/gal that probably won't take sides and won't pick on you for just no reason. However, people can be jerkoffs sometimes, so they might be helping their friend or maybe a streamer. It can happen but that's why after you WIN (or die), you can rate them based on performance! That's the best way to make it so their rating gets low enough that they lose abilities in their future matches. This game is EASILY worth $15! I only play as Show Director (could you tell?) and I'm going to pay $15 for it. If the developers keep working on this game and improving my favorite role, the Show Director, to be a balanced and ever-evolving role then I'll be around for a long time to come!
_childDocuments_.name: Darwin Project

_childDocuments_.review: Truly the king of battle royale games:It doesn't have most of the flaws that made fortnite just straight up unfun and frustrating for me, while also introducing some interesting new mechanics such as the show director.And for the Twitch Streamers of you it has Twitch Integration for the full murder-gameshow feeling.I could see this game being as famous on twitch as fortnite, if only it got more popular; so try it out if haven't already and recommend it to your friends if you like it.Also, it's free, so what are you waiting for? Go get it and bring a friend or even a whole crowd of twitch viewers for maximum fun.Edit:Now that it got out of Early Access, I must say that it is even more fun. The slow early game, annoying ressource gathering and ressource management have been reduced to a minimum while also introducing three classes that each have their own unique and fun to use trait.Hopefully now that the devs are actually advertising this game, it maybe could take off, but considering that the BR-hype has kinda worn off, it probably won't happen, even though this game really is one of the most unique games of it's genre.Only issue I have with it now is that it no longer has the duo mode, which will hopefully be brought back with the next patch.Also, the game is still free, so just give it a try if you haven't already, it really is fun.

_childDocuments_.review: I just picked up this game and it is AWESOME. After watching a few gameplay videos I was still unsure whether I will actually like the game, but it is simply brilliant. The community is mature and super nice, the game directors are usually doing their best to make games fun and interact with players, and what's most important, this is an actually good stealth game.Should you play ?If you like stealth games - DEFINITELYIf you are neutral to them - YES / You will probably fairy enjoy this games as it has more than enough action.If you HATE stealth game - Probably not, but there is still a small change you will enjoy it.The gameplay: top notch. Everything is incredibly smooth. No server or machine lag. Tons of fun tracking other players (it is not as boring as it sounds), and even more fun running from other players.Let me give you an example: I am being chased by some player. I hide in a cabin and place traps next to every window. In the middle of the lodging area, I place a huge turret. When they finally catch up with me, they enter the house through a window (yes you can do that), fall right into the trap, get hailstormed by my turret and I finish the guy with a single axe blow.It is even needless to say that you can craft barriers, invisibility cloaks and a lot of other stuff.All in all, this is a way better game than all of these battle royale games out there. In fact, if you are looking for a hunger games esc game, this is the one for you.Needless to say that it is way cheaper than other games  pub *cough* g, and is way more fun to play.p.s. This game keeps being fun even if you lose, as you get to watch the match, and trust me when I say that it can be even more fun to watch a game of Darwin Project than any other game out there,

_childDocuments_.review: Darwin Project is a unique game and take on the current battle royale genre. However, there are glaring issues that cause me to not recommend this, at least until the game is further down the road.Optimization is solid, and controls are smooth. Where is falls frusteratingly short is some gameplay decisions made by the devs. Spending a lot of time crafting up armor, cloaks, boots, and sharpening. Getting electronics for strong equipments. All of it is negated by the large amount of fall hazards in the map, accompanied by the arrow and axe knockback distance that is almost impossible to take into consideration when positioning.I cannot say how irritating it is to be one of the last two alive, and the other guy is hiding in a corner near lava who will have a clear shot on knocking you into the lava is. The idea, the core concept of the game, is unique and fun. But the director role is bothersome. Out of the 5 games I played, 3 of them I never saw the director, or the director was placing buffs on one solo person. Making it so directors cannot use powers if their stars are below 2.3 is a smart move, but I don't think it's enough.I'm not even touching how annoying it is to have a director screaming play by plays in your ear. But that's a personal gripe.Personally, I hope this game evolves and works on some of the glaring issues. Maybe players like the knockback. Maybe people like the director yelling play by plays. If that's the case, maybe the game just isn't for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Simply put, Darwin project is an incredible battle royale game with huge potential to become a phenomenal game, but there is one huge factor that will always hold it from reaching that level. The biggest problem in this game is also its most unique selling point, the "Director". Basically, the director is a god that controls when zones close, where powerups spawn etc, he can also directly affect the players and give them health, shields and other buffs.Sounds like a great idea right? Well currently it is a terrible ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ idea. Since literally anyone can become the director, you have all these dumbasses teaming with players, giving them shields mid fight, informing them about other players locations and spawning electronics right next to them. All this while they can also bully people they don't like, closing zones or trapping people into nukes or putting a manhunt on you so everyone in the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ game can see you.Ofcourse there are the good directors that help the underdogs and make the game interesting for everyone, but since over 50% of all the directors are russian kids under the age of 10 that just want to go on a huge power trip and team with any fellow russian player they can see. This removes all competetive aspect from the game, It wont matter how well you play when 9 yr old Dimitri makes the last guy in the 1v1 INVINCIBLE.I really hate to give this game a negative review, I mean the first 6 hours were amazing, I was in a complete trance by the skill based movement/combat, the indepth resource gathering/crafting and absolutely gorgeous environment. But as long as there is no way to play without a director I simply cannot recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly a really good game, I'm having a lot more fun on this than I did with Fortnite. Never got into PUBG because I refuse to pay $30 for it. You don't need to sort through loot at all, and you don't have bag space or a limited inventory. There's two resources in the game that you can use to craft literally anything else you need, and a special drop-only resource for abilities.You set up your loadout in the main-menu or in the ingame lobby and that's what you can use/craft/loot in the next game. The best thing about said equipment is that you don't need to play or pay to unlock ANY of it. Every different gadget, ammo type, and special ability is unlocked from the moment you install the game.Your only weapons are an axe, and a bow. The only other things you can get are based on your loadout, which can vary greatly, but are mostly for utility and escape purposes.
_childDocuments_.name: Darwin Project

_childDocuments_.review: While technically fitting into the battle royale genre, this game is unlike anything else out right now. I don't normally do reviews on games I've played so little of, but those few rounds I played already were really compelling. The "story" behind the game is a bit convoluted, but it still works, and the basic mechanics are quite simple, but still require both strategy and skill. So how does it differ from other BR games? 1) instead of 50-100 players there are 10, either 10 solo or 5 teams of 22) you aren't air dropped and have no choice over where you spawn3) instead of starting with nothing, you get an axe and a bow, and the only "drops" are small trees, chairs, and electronic boxes that can be harvested for crafting materials.4) you get to customize your crafting menu a bit before entering the game to differentiate a bit from the other players. For instance, you can choose basic arrows and start each game with 5 in your inventory, or choose flaming arrows at the expense of having to craft them all from scratch. Craft boots that make you run faster when you're tracking an enemy or being tracked by one. Switch out the bear trap for a hang glider, etc. I've only played solo so far, but I could see this being especially strong in teams. 5) instead of a procedurally generated circle shrinking every few minutes, there is an 11th player who takes on the roll of director/game master. This person can take pity on you or make your life hell. They can give players invincibility shields, lower gravity, nuke entire zones, etc. My first game I just kind of jumped in without knowing half of what I told you above, including the whole director bit. Out of nowhere a giant robotic eye came floating down to me and spoke to me in a god-like voice (The director was using lots of reverb and pitch shifting on his voice lol) saying "The Woodsman, eh? Interesting name... do you like to chop wood?" I hadn't bothered to look up the push to talk key before jumping in, so I just ran to the nearest tree and started chopping. "No answer... hmmph... typical... I'll take pity on you anyway. Head towards the electronics I just spawned on the map and grab it before the others get there, they're already on their way." he says.I had little to no idea what he was talking about, but I saw the icon on the map and ran as quick as I could. Somebody was already there, so I drew my arrow and missed. I shot a few more times but only hit once and next I know I'm out of arrows. I charge in with my axe and before I reach the enemy he deals the killing blow with his arrow. My next game I actually had my mic working, and a better idea of what I was doing. I even customized my loadout a bit. I started gathering everything I could find until I ran across the first item that had already been harvested and searched it, making the enemy who had gathered it pop up on my screen and I began the chase. I wasn't gonna let anybody get the jump on me this time. Well I got a few shots in before he knew what was even going on. The director mistook me for a good gamer or something and decided to help out the other guy. He gave him an invincibility shield, but he just kept running and shouting over the mic "OMG I'M GONNA DIE I'M GONNA DIE" and as soon as the shield disappeared, he did. Mr Director wasn't happy about that, apparently, because I happened to be right near where 3 different zones meet, center, southern, and eastern. The south was already off limits, and he sets off a nuke in the east where I am, so I run west for the center and he marks that off limits, too, so I turn north and run as fast as I can. With about 30 seconds left to get out of there I giant white light emerges from the east. I knew it was about to get nuked but that was F'ing beautiful. I forgot to mention I was freezing for the entire duration of the run. I was trying to build a campfire when he did all this. I finally make it to safety and set up my fire, with only a few seconds left before I would have froze. As soon as I'm nice and toasty, I'm flanked by another player who noticed my fire. TL;DRdespite fitting into a genre that is the current flavor of the week and rife with cheap, sad knockoffs, this game is utterly original. Easy to learn, difficult to master. Runs smooth and gorgeous for an EA title that just barely came out. F2P and no microtransactions at all at this point, with only cosmetic stuff in the future. definitely worth giving a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: Darwin's Project shows us that you can make a game inspired by someone's else idea, without completely copying it. Yes, it is a battle royale game, but it does so many things differently.Plot of the game is that you are one of the ten prisoners who can win their freedom by winning a battle royale which is watched by huge audience. It goes so far beyond to emulate the real audience feel by having unique twitch integrations and giving people ability to be "show directors", which have complete freedom of watching (show directors control small camera drones). Show directors can also pick which zones will be closed, drop items for players, make player "hunted" so all other players see him and even more stuff! Their job is to make the game as exciting as possible. And greatest thing about it is that anyone can be a director! Its selected as a game mode.Now onto the player's part, game is set in a unique snowy map for a specific reason. Since there are only 10 players in each match, so the game is focused on tracking other people down, and if you pay enough attention, you can even notice the footsteps as a good trail. Each time you gather materials or craft something, red glowing items will appear on your spot, which other players can inspect, and if they do, they will see your location and other stats through wall for few seconds. But even if you arent a good tracker, there are houses around the map which have screen that shows location of all the other players on map.When it comes to fighting, Darwin's Project has a bit of a learning curve. There are only two weapons - axe and bow, which alter the gameplay a lot compared to classic battle royale games with guns. Axe can be upgraded with materials and bow uses limited amount of arrows which you can craft and pick up after you fire them. Since materials are quite scarce you'll usually have 3-4 arrows or less, so if you miss with those, you can either run to gather them first, or resort to axe fighting. Aiming with bow is not that easy and requires good practice to get a hang of especially since player movement is very fast and there is a lot of jumping around in fights. Both axe and bow deal 150 damage (although axe can be upgraded, and bow deal +50 on headshot), which compared the player's hp - 600, leave space for interesting fights where you dont have to worry about getting one shotted from behind.The materials are used for improving your gear (boots, axe, cloak) and crafting gadgets (smoke grenades, traps, etc), arrows and armor (protects you from one hit). There are only two different materials - wood and leather, wood is usually gathered from trees and leather from sofa chairs hanging around the map. Besides them, there is a resource called "electric" which show directors spawn on certain locations shown on minimap. Electrics are used for unlocking special, very powerful abilities. There are multiple different gadgets, upgrade buffs and electric skills, however you can only pick certain number of them to use in match, and they are selected before it starts, in the menu. One more thing to mention is that there is a small survival aspect "cold", which forces you to build fire to warm up and leaves additional trails in process.Not much more to say about it, the Darwin's Project does its own thing, and it does it decently. Pros:- Different from other battle royale games- Play as a player or the show director- Skill based- Duos (5 teams of 2 players)- Crafting and tracking aspects- Character customization- Decent selection of gadgets and different upgrade buffs- Twitch integrations- LeaderboardsNeutral:- Matches can be sometimes too much show director dependant, if someone doesnt like you, you will have harder time playingCons:- Needs more content and game modes, feels too shallow for now- Somewhat high learning curve, noob traps- Female character looks weird - Gets boring quick- A lot of gadgets feel gimmicky and arent used that much- No guns

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know whether or not to recommend it.  It is free, so, worth the price for sure.  It isn't finished, but it is early access, so no surprise, and it may end up being a great game a year from now.  It just isn't yet.The game's main hook, what makes it something other than an already decent mash-up of Fortnite and Hurtworld is the Director: a Game Master who spectates, can talk to all the players, and can hand out bonuses or change game rules while the match is in progress.  Also, people who are watching the match be streamed can vote on many of the same things, meaning popularity can tip the game.  It feels sort of Hunger Games inspired to me.  I think it's a cool feature for sure, but there seems to be some indecision about what the Director's or audience's role should be, how much power they should have, etc.  It has been kind of a mess so far in my experience.  The Directors keep losing power, but the game is really only something special with a good Director.  Not that they are all good.  That is the good reason *why* they keep being controversial and getting power taken away.Which bring me to the next point.  The game is more social than most.  When it is working as designed and not being derailed, the players often doing a lot of talking to each other and the Director as the match goes on.  So the game lives or dies by its community.  Its ftp online shooter community.  Which can be problematic.  Consider yourself warned.It gets old pretty fast and feels a light on content and unfinished, but it is early access.  There is only one map and it has bugs in it.  It only has two weapons, axe and bow, and all players always have both.  You can craft snowballs or a turret, but they very situational, and not part of your standard kit.  The controls and physics for the axe and bow are intenionally cartoony, which I am not a big fan of, but more than that feel really janky.  Timing your axe swings is a required skill, but the axe is an unresponsive beast at best.  Arrows have a fairly slow flight speed, and do drop over distance, but they drop only slightly, and not in anything so logical as a graceful arc.  For TF2 fans out there, they move more like soldier's rocket than sniper's arrows.  Right down to smoke trail, which I assume they added in just to make it easier to tell where you are being shot from.  When hurt, a character doesn't bleed, but does go flying, smash bros style.  A big hit can knock you right across the map.  Or out of the map.  And not in a 'ring-out lose' way, but a 'I'm not sure that was supposed to happen' way.  It seems like they wanted this to look like a cartoon, or a trippy violent grown-up cartoon, but they could have committed a lot more to the aesthetic if that was the idea.  I wonder how many of these decisions are made for game play vs aesthetic reasons vs trying to keep a teen rating in a game about axe murder.Anyway.  The game isn't bad, but it isn't finished.  It will probably be great after a couple more major updates, assuming it gets polished up without accumulating too much toxic community or bad design decisions.  But isn't isn't there yet.  I would suggest checking back on this one in a few months to see where it is.

_childDocuments_.review: A unique Battle Royal game that is more Hunger Games than PUBG. A 10 player free for all where the only weapons at your disposal is an Axe and Bow & Arrow. As like most BR games, you start with nothing, and have to loot to gain power to get an advantage over you opponents. While in other BR games, you usually loot weapons, in the Darwin Project, you need to harvest supplies to craft your ammo, armor, gear, gadgets, and traps. There is also a lite survival mechanic where you have to keep warm by crafting warming cloths, and building fires. All of these items are made with two crafting materials (wood and leather), so it becomes a balancing act of what to craft first and when.The combat is very high flying and arcady. This game is not a realistic shooter. Every hit a person takes, with an arrow or axe hit, knocks the player back and sends them flying. This seems to "reset" the combat almost every hit and makes it more about timing than spamming.The arena is split into 7 zones that will close off over time, similiar to other BR games.  Staying in the zone will drain your warmth making you freeze to death.  So instead of a cricle that gradually gets smaller, different areas of the map become locked out randomly.And lastely, another feature that sets the game apart from others is the role of the "Director". It's essentially an Observer mode were the Observer/Caster can affect the flow of the match. They gain engery over time that is used for "powers" of various types. They can manually close of zones themselves, launch nukes that can temporarly close out a zone, heal or warm up players, etc. The purpose of the Director is to try and make the match more fun and interesting, and keep it competative, but sometimes, they can just make the game a bad time for a few. At the end of the match, you can Rate the Directors performance if you feel they did a great job, or were just trolling. Directors that have bad ratings lose access to powers they can use during a match to discourage bad behavior.I'm personally having a great time with this game, and was lucky enough to get it for free by downloading the Open Beta. The Early Access price is only $15 currently, and I would have defintely paid that price if I didn't get it for free. It's a fresh take on the BR genre and it's great to finally see some games coming out that are really changing up the formula.

_childDocuments_.review: Bare bones atm but well worth 15. If ur tired of pubg and/or fortnite (even some other multiplayer games) give this game a try. Mostly positive community and in the 5.4 hours I've played, as of writing this review, I have only had 1 lobby where there was a salty player in the lobby. Games are quick to get into as an inmate, but I was told there is a longer que for the Director. It's connected to Twitch and Myxer so if u stream your stream can place votes to who they think will win(if you're the Director), or vote for you(if you're the inmate) so they feel more involved.There is a significant skill gap but as the youngins may say you just have to, "gitgud" (play it more). There are no cosmetics atm but I believe that is a good thing as the people playing are just playing to enjoy the game. I have NOT felt as if when I got killed it was due to the other player hacking or cheating in any way nor have I had a truly unfair Director in my game. If you see someone complaining about a Director and they are still playing, chances are they are trolling for some unknown reason. You can rate the director and if/when their rating goes low enough they cannot directly affect a player which is a perk gained through progression.There are craftable and pickup items to make your character faster and armored, but there is no weapon that is weaker than the next (only bow and arrow with dif types of arrows, axe, snowballs, and traps); in saying that, even if another person is armored or a speed boosted, if your aim is better, all that doesn't matter. No lucky shots,  No "where did he shoot me from" if u get killed chances are you got out played. That's coming from someone who hasn't won a SINGLE FREAKIN GAME YET, but yet and still I had fun in EVERY GAME even when I was the first to die.Everyone spawns in to crafting materials but what you do with them is your choice, make arrows or clothing to help you better survive what's to come. You can be the hunter or the hunted and if you are the latter you will know, unless they are just following your foot prints but if they can see you, you know they can see you. If you are the hunter you just may be going into a trap so you always have to be prepared.TL;DR: Game is fun, me likie game, u should try.

_childDocuments_.review: Just won my first game, I have to say, Snowballs are op. For the most part I enjoy the game a lot, the RNG aspect of finding weapons in most BR games isn't here, you start with an axe and a bow; you can change your loadout to reflect how you want to play, whether it means changing what arrow types or craftables you have. The combat is pretty fast paced, you hit someone they go flying mach 10 into another dimension so there's a chance a fight can turn either way. As I mentioned earlier snowballs are op, why? Well there's the cold mechanic which is while you're playing a match your character will start to get colder until the bar reaches zero and you take DOT's (damage over time). Snowballs apply 14 frost damage on hit, and require nothing to craft, so my tactic is at the start of each match craft 10 for a fight, and after each fight recraft the ones you used. Overall this is a very fast paced BR game, with matches lasting about 5-10 minutes, I would reccomend playing this because well... It's free, and fun.

This is a good thing if you want to relax and enjoy a game and not get angry, but sometimes 100 player battle royales get you more drawn in and attatched to the game because if you lose, all of the work and possibly kills and time you've spend goes down the drain. So I will call this game the 'healthy' battle royale, for it lacks in rage and overall addiction. So if you want to settle down and enjoy a nice game, play Darwin project, but if you want a game that can connect you with the game and something you would consider playing for many hours, though I know some people who have done so with this game, in my opinion it lacks that 'game to human' connection that I have gotten from other battle royales.Nevertheless, this is without a doubt still a well made and enjoyable game, and I would reccomend it at the end of the day, as the majority of people will enjoy this battle royale game!

_childDocuments_.review: I have recently started playing this game but I can definitely say it's a great one. The graphics are very good, but that's not that important in this case. This is one of the few unique Battle Royale games. Others are the exact same thing over and over again, Darwin Project is extremely different.The only thing that connects Darwin Project to other BR games is the fact that the last man standing wins. Otherwise, the gameplay is unique, there are elements of surviving and crafting added to it. The amounts of different builds and tactics you can use is great. You always have a new style of playing to try. Add to that, the zone system is a lot more interesting, the map is also not that big, which makes things a lot more stressing, faster-paced and funnier.The combat itself might seem pretty simple at first, it's mostly using an axe and a bow, but there's a lot more to it. All of the different techniques you can use during combat is what makes a good player a good player. I've played other famous BR titles before and I usually had no problem getting used to the combat, but the case here is different. I've had my ass kicked by good players numerous times, and I'm still getting used to the system here.The game is still in early access but I think in its current state it is a really good game, I can't imagine how much better it would be after some time. I have great faith in the developers and I can see this game becoming a top title in the BR genre. Surely recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: I really did enjoy this game quite a bit and loved all of the unique feautures it brings into the scene. I feel that of course it needs more work, it is an early access after all and that is a given. The biggest problem people have is that the whole "director" mechanic is unbalanced and ruins the game, however, as someone who loved playing as the director, I can easily point out 2 reasons why people say the directors are biased. First off I just need to say that directors are there to improve the overall feeling of the game and atmosphere, they are there to spice things up and make what is otherwise a standard battle royale, into an interactive and fun environment. A director isnt going to favor someone who either A. Doesn't have a mic or B. Doesnt do anything interesting (e.g. hides until they can no longer hide, doesn't speak to the Director or other players). Think of a sports announcer having to talk about what a player is doing while they are sitting on the bench. There is nothing there for the announcer to make interesting. The Director isnt going to help you out in a situation unless you make yourself interesting and known to the Director. Bottom line, the Director can just be bad, or are learning, but if you want to be noticed and interacted with, dont hide, speak up when the Director talks, be bold and trust me the director wont seem so negligent of you.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR - Amazing game with alot of fun possibilities, tons of fun.Everybody not wanna read gone? okay.When I first got the game was the day it went free, and boy let me tell you I was hooked from the start. There are alot of different aspects of the game that I enjoy, and I'm gonna go through most of the things in detail here.Customizing your loadout:The fact that you can create the loadout that fits your playstyle is something I wish every game like this one has, since it gets more people to enjoy the game their way. I personally go with a loadout thats more of a "Get in their face and hit it until it dies" tactic, that has focus on defencive and movement abilities and some sustain, which works pretty well for me.The outfits:I'm a big fan of the fact that the only way to get clothing is to level up (so far atleast), since it shows that you play this game alot and have some way to show it to others. I wont jugde if they add some way to buy clothing since they went F2P and they could probably need some of the cash.The gameplay:Love it, just absolutely love it. You start off in the lobby which normally is just a mess of people shooting each other and talking to each other on the mic, then when you start you spawn some distance away from the other's which gives you time to loot and craft whatever you need. And the fighting is simple, yet addicting. The electronics ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ is also something i really like the consept of. It's pretty much a must have for late game and it's often contested by other players. However, the game director function is mixed in my opinion. Some games you get an amazing director that makes things happend all around the map and brings action to the table, while some directors just choose a favorite and does everything for their advantage, but then again that just makes it a bit more of an challenge.The verdict:It's F2P, dont take alot of space and is pretty much one of the better battle royales that has come up recently. I beg you to try it out for yourself and have as much fun as i do with it.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: Updating review to reflect my recommendation. Pretty much nothing has changed from alpha/beta to early access and most of what I say remains the same, but due to the EA price, I don't recommend the game. I did update that I received the product for free moving from alpha/beta to EA for whatever reason, though can't say that it changed my mind as I don't give points for developer kindness, sorry.I actually don't like the base game at all, but I like the director thing. The base game is really kinda bland and too simple for my taste. There's one type of combat and it's the bow, though you do have an axe. If you can't aim, then don't bother playing. There is no axe playstyle, it's just that thing you use to deflect incoming axe attacks made by other players. Let me say that once again. THERE IS NO AXE COMBAT PLAYSTYLE. If you use the axe vs anyone with skill, you will eventually lose because every attack you make will be deflected and then they will use the space to shoot you. I don't give a ♥♥♥♥ about 'the bow requires skill'. Going by that logic they could also make 'deflecting arrows requires skill'. Instead it's literally just swing your axe and hope the poor sod is bad at timing shots and you'll make breathing room or run around like an idiot and hope he misses. A good bow player will win EVERY TIME. The axe is LITERALLY just there to deflect other axe attacks and that makes the game inflexible and BORING. If you're gonna do melee, you need to have the possiblity of a melee playstyle. You can't just let them counter each other out and make space. YOU CAN'T DO THAT. Why even HAVE melee? You could also make deflecting arrows a possible thing since arrows are pretty limited. BOTH OF THESE ARE NOT A REAL OPTION. Because you CAN'T predict when someone will loose their arrow and you CAN'T hit a guy with an axe if he knows you're coming because he will just deflect it. In other words the only playstyle is the bow. Hope you like bow and arrow :3.Also the tracking system in this game is trash. It doesn't matter how long ago someone looted something, you always get a 100% view of the player for x amount of time. The lack of depth destroys the trackinig system making it literally just a glorified wallhack. The worst part is that you can use smoke bomb, but hey they just track you using another thing you looted. It's a horrible system with zero depth.I also feel middled by the number of players as there are so few (10). Then again, when I do director mode I struggle to give attention (and annoyance) to everyone equally. I like being able to chat with random people as that's not something I would ever do in a pvp situation. I just don't like conversing with my opponents. But when I get to sit over their shoulder like the annoying brother, that feels fun for me. Though I do still have to get down the part where you don't talk to someone when they're near someone else and ruin the game for them. I do understand that people don't like you chatting at the last part of the game where they're fighitng for the win.I think my biggest complaint is that the director system is totally lame with the 'review' system. Whenever a player dies, they get the option to rate the director (I think it has some limitations?) and it's a 1/5 star system. The biggest thing I realized is that people don't like silent directors. No matter how hard I tried to just make the game fun, no one liked it. Not just that but directors lack the TOOLS to make the game fun directly. But when I started being a nuisance, my rating started to go up. Flashing my lights, telling people to jump in lava there's a secret in there, asking people if they'd like me to close their zone and when they say no I close it anyway. Seems like my rating managed to climb up.And when I say climb, what I mean is that is hung around 3.10. This wouldn't be a problem except that you get some powers taken away if you drop below 2.3 which definitely could happen to someone as mediocre as me who is trying his best to entertain. Realistically that's what you do as the director. And you really have limited interactivity. So if you wanna be a non talking director, there's no options. And because it's so social heavy that means I'd only play this game when feeling social because I don't care for the base game. If I could do more to entertain that didn't require me to put invincibility on one guy, heal the other while shouting 'oh no I ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up! hold on I can fix this!' and then nuking the sector and waste all 10 points, things would be better. I also noticed no one likes some abilities. If I heal someone, people ♥♥♥♥♥ and say 'Oh you're playing favoritism on that guy'. If I throw invulnerability during a fight? People ♥♥♥♥♥. Anti-grav? No one ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ likes it. NO ONE. I asked everyone and the only guy who wanted it didn't know what it did and immediately afterward he said 'wow this is lame'. The worst part is that there are SO MANY BAD DIRECTORS. I didn't realize it the first time I played the game, but now when I had to play 5 matches again and then a few more after that, I realized that there are a ton of bad directors. Not only do they play favoritism for the 'twitch' streamer, but sometimes they'll literally call you out. 'He's undergeared, go fight him over there' or, or, OR you could shut the ♥♥♥♥ up and let me use the 12 wood and 7 leather to put on armor, make a couple traps and upgrade my ♥♥♥♥ you ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. And don't even try to apologize by healing me, the other guy is better with the bow and I'm ♥♥♥♥. Just let me die you ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.Back to the director. The problem is that the abilities being used for what they're supposed to be used for no one likes. If I use them jokingly or throw them away at the start of the game cause some guy said 'just use invincibility on someone as soon as possible' BAM, more points. The system encourages you to be an entertainer cause if you drop below a certain rating, you lose your abilities and then YOU don't have fun. But you can't DO what you're supposed to with the abilities so no matter what you either play as an entertaining director by flying overhead while making car sounds, pulling people over making police sounds and wasting your abilities on NOTHING, or you use your abilities as you see fit and you lose them cause you're trying to actually use the abilities.I mean I'm not complaining that it's that way, but if it's gonna be that way the abilities shouldn't be so geared towards actually helping. Give me the ability to just start vomiting watermelons or spawn random balloons and other cooky ♥♥♥♥. This isn't even mentioning how some of the abilities are actually useless. The nuke can be dodged by walking out of the zone, into even a zone that's closed, and then just walking back in. It's one of the worst abilities and I'd gladly give it up to bombard a zone with exploding rubber duckies.As the director you are an ENTERTAINER. That's your job whether you like it or not. Also there isn't really much incentive to play director beyond the raw enjoyment. You don't gain any levels or unlocks and that's a real downer for me. Let me unlock rubber ducky abilities dammit.Monetization turned out to be a flat 15 bucks which means I can't recommend. The game just isn't worth that amount and I'm prettttty sure it'll go F2P after exiting EA.Oh and one last thing, I'd much rather kill the players than help them and I think they'd enjoy that more. I REALLY think they'd like it more. Not. Even. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Kidding.

You find what you need and its up to you to choose what you want to craft based on your playstyle.Pros:-Quick paced, easy to learn.-Smooth graphics and gameplay.-Fresh take on Battle Royale.-Directors can be pretty cool.-Optimized for streaming on Mixer.Cons:-Somewhat small game world (could be a Pro to be honest).-Current lack of of variety of weapons (early access)-Sometimes unfair depending on the actions of the Director.Overall this game is very very fun which really should be our main factor when considering games, right?

_childDocuments_.review: This game, is the perfect battle royale.Scavenger Studios first game and they hit the formula right on the head. In this review I'll tell you a bit about the pros and cons. Furthurmore I'll tell you how the pro's outweigh the cons.PROS:-10 PlayersThe whole 100 players in other battle royale proves to be unsatisfying, and makes it demoralizing when you get to top 2 just to die.-No RNG (For the most part)Ever played a game of PUB just to rush into a house, not find a gun, die immediatly, and have about 5 minutes of time wasted out of waiting for that game and getting into it just to die. Well in Darwin there is no rng besides where the zones close. The closing of the zones for better players in easy to ignore aswell.-Fun CombatWhile this is gonna partly be in the cons aswell, but for the most part the combat is really fun. The Axe combat is my favorite personally, but the bow combat people love aswell, The speed and force of the combat makes you feel strong and it is super satisfying to hit someone with an arrow or axe hit. The sound and graphical elements makes the combat feel awesome aswell as preform great.-Custom PlaystylesWanna scavenge and get super OP before fighting anyone, theres a build for that. Wanna be a ninja and sneak around players to get the advantage on them, theres a build for that. Wanna be a speedy boy with an axe that does half their health bar, thers a build for that. No matter how you wanna play, Darwin has fully customizable builds for you to suit your playstyle so you never feel awkward with the game forcing you to play a certain way.-Show DirectorWhile on paper the Director sounds like a terrible idea, in practice it helps the game a lot. Where a game can get stagnant ther is an omnipotent being that can spice up the game and make it more interesting and fast. The Director has a rating which can be used to determine what abilities they can use. So no fear if you see a director teaming with one player, vote him one star and he will no longer have the ability to influence players directly in future games. This also turns the game casual in most games, making the community much less toxic because nobody really gets mad when they lose. Which takes me into my last pro before I keep naming off everything I love about this game-CommunityThis game has, hands down, the best community of a game I have ever played. Everyone is friendly to eveyone else, except for the few asshats you meet but thats to be seen in every community. No one gets overly mad when they die, most of the time when I kill or am killed I say GG and am met with a GG back. Scavenger should be proud of the community they have and work to do everything they can to keep it.Now for the ConsCONS:-OptimizationThe game is pretty poorly optimized, but it being in its early stages that is most likely gonna change. Not really much else to say here. But on lower setting there are graphical glitches ive noticed, mainly in areas where snow should deform but on lower settings it does not so you end up clipping.-Sometimes jank combat.The hitboxes with axes are thicc asf, and when arrow fighting your body hitbox is also a thicc boy with your head being the hardest to hit thing in the game.-Director ratingWhile I said the game is casual and people don't get mad, some people do. And when I play as director I can do great the whole game and be fair but the guy who dies cause I closed a zone trying to push him twords other players is of course gonna vote me as a one. This makes it so I can't use heal, nuke, etc. I can still use other stuff but the values on some of the items need to be scaled down cause it makes them damn near impossible to use them somestimes.The Darwin Project, a Diamond in the rough. Install today and never go back to Fortnite or PUB :D

_childDocuments_.review: A unique, faster-paced take on the battle royale genre. The emphasis on survival through the cold meter mechanic and tracking is interesting, forcing players to focus more on the risk-reward of scavenging to craft better gear versus the flat hunt for better weapons in Fortnite. However, bow and arrow are way too strong, and the massive knockback you get hit with when an arrow shot hits you is just annoying, not fun. When combined with the anti-gravity effect that nearly every MC is going to use once it's down to the final two players, most of your 1v1s for the win come down to whoever getting hit with an arrow first getting knocked clear out of the zone, and dying due to being in a restricted area. This trickles down into the Electronics resource, which the MC spawns on the map and is always visible on everyone's map, forcing players to fight over it. Because of the way matches end, certain power-ups are just far better; invincibility for a few seconds is the difference between winning and losing when knocked out of the zone, meaning that it, along with Radar to find other players and hunt effectively, are almost always going to take up 2 of your 3 slots for tech. Because of the floaty knockback and the strength of ranged over melee, almost every player is going to have more or less the same loadout, with 1-2 slots of the trap category taken up by snowball and tripwire, with the remaining slot filling some kind of rarely-used niche. That said, this could be fixed by reducing or removing the knockback from arrows, because it's excessive at this point. Anti-gravity should also be removed; as a mechanic, it can be fun to see from a spectator's view, but it works against the other mechanics in the game, making arrows far too strong because of their knockback, making melee useless, and ultimately turning every fight where it's turned on (read: probably every single 1v1) into a test to see who can land one arrow first. Replacing it with something else that forces players together would be much better; instead of giant jumps, let the MC permanently reveal and track all players to each other when there's less than 5 competitors left. Spawn animals that attack the remaining survivors. Spawn a blizzard that drastically reduces players' cold meters, forcing more campfires, thus, more confrontations. You want more fights to break out, not have one fight end anticlimactically - especially when that fight is the final duel for the win.Overall, though, the game has a solid base. The survival mechanics in place are great, hunting and tracking is more nuanced and leads to more viable strategy and choice than in Fortnite, the announcer / MC is, barring some of the more questionable events they can spawn, an original and plain fun design choice, and overall, each match plays out in different, interesting ways.
