_childDocuments_.review: Darwin Project : By Triple F"Darwin Project", the exhilarating and innovative entry in the battle royale genre, takes survival of the fittest to electrifying new heights. Set in a post-apocalyptic Canadian Rockies arena, this game brilliantly blends the primal instincts of hunting and survival with the strategic complexity of a real-time showstopper. With its unique twist on the genre, "Darwin Project" doesn't just stand out in the crowded battle royale landscape; it ascends to a new tier of gaming excitement.Visually, "Darwin Project" delivers an awe-inspiring spectacle. The frozen wilderness setting is nothing short of breathtaking, with its dynamic weather system and intricately designed landscapes adding depth and challenge to each match. The changing environments are not just eye candy, but strategic elements that players must master to survive. From crafting tools and weapons to tracking opponents, the game artfully integrates its visuals with game-play, creating a seamless and immersive experience.But it's the innovation at the core that truly sets "Darwin Project" apart. A Show Director, an omnipotent being with god-like abilities, can manipulate the battlefield, influencing the flow of the game and shaping the fate of participants. This adds a thrilling layer of unpredictability, as well as a strategic dimension that transforms each match into a dynamic chessboard of survival. The interplay between the Show Director and the contestants is a masterstroke, turning the typical battle royale formula on its head and fostering an ever-evolving ecosystem of tactics.The combat mechanics are a symphony of skill and strategy. The focus on close-quarters melee combat, combined with ranged combat elements, demands players to adapt swiftly to rapidly changing situations. Hunting down opponents requires more than just precision; it requires a keen understanding of the environment, the ability to read tracks, and the dexterity to execute split-second decisions. The result is a pulse-pounding experience where the rush of a successful kill is only matched by the adrenaline of narrowly escaping death.Crafting is the heart of survival, and "Darwin Project" nails it. The resource management system, where players scavenge for materials and craft essential gear, enhances the immersive nature of the game. The race against time to gather resources while evading opponents maintains a constant tension that's hard to shake off, ensuring that complacency is never an option."Darwin Project's" interactive spectator experience is a genius addition. As a spectator, you're not just a passive observer; you can influence the game by voting, casting your opinion, and participating in the overarching narrative of survival. This bridges the gap between players and viewers, making each match a communal experience where everyone is vested in the outcome. The symbiotic relationship between those in the arena and those watching adds layers of entertainment that other battle royales lack.In conclusion, "Darwin Project" isn't just any game; it's a revolution in the battle royale genre. With its stunning visuals, strategic innovations, and immersive mechanics, it creates an experience that's equal parts heart-pounding competition and edge-of-your-seat entertainment. The fusion of survival instincts, resource management, and real-time manipulation creates an intricate tapestry of game-play that's as thrilling to participate in as it is to watch.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing. Over my weekend off of work, I had plans to complete the Warhammer: Vermintide 2 story, but picked this game up instead. And did not regret it. This game is extremely fast paced when in a fight, and requires you to think within a fraction of a second. You can craft your way to a full loudout, or hunt other players for theirs. You can gain the favor of the show director by doing as he says or playing valiantly. Yes, this game does has its bugs, some players can shoot through trees, some players knock others back so far they're in a nother zone, 3 away from their starting one. And some show directors, do favor streamers. However, this game is Early Access, so it's expected.Overall, I give this game a 9/10, polished, nice, fun, with a few annoyances.

_childDocuments_.review: After a rough start with black-screening and lock ups I finally got the game to work and I feel I can give an honest asessment of the game. And I can do this rather fast. It seems like theyve crammed a bit much into this title for the type of game this is. In additon, the controls are clunky, ranged combat is mediocre while playing and while spectating. I appreciate what the devs are trying to do, and I think its a good idea branching out from the BR formula...but it feels a little like the 60 yr old guy who is 5'1" and buys a yellow corvette.*Combat*Heres my biggest gripe. It feels like its made for players with controllers but has way too many options fora controller. 1,2,3,4,5,6 + R, F, G are all weapons, traps, special abilities...things you will likely need in battle. In addition, you have Mouse 1 for melee and HOLD Mouse 2 + Mouse 1 for ranged (bow). Thats 11 options to decide between while in an encounter. Ive used less keybinds in ARMA. Im not being facetious here. ARMA has multiple stances, a hot key for a watch, compass, weapons, etc and it still uses less keys. Its known as one of the most complicated keybinds of all time. This is just took the cake*Class system*I like the class system. But theyve made it obsolete or unneeded by having 11 combat options no matter your class.*Actual Gameplay combat*This is beyond clunky. I turned my mouse down to 400 dpi and accuracy is still a challenge. Landing shots with the arrow is unpredictable. Try it in a lobby to a moving target. You'll see what I mean. If my arrow is going to connect on a moving target without leading it, make it that way. If its going to connect with leading the target, make it that way. For some reason we have what sems to be a mixed bag. Almost as if the shots are slighlty randomized...like BF1. And again, that was done to grab the controller kiddiesAxe swings have a weird and hard to time delay which is absent in the lobby. So if youre trying to time swings in a lobby, just realize it will be totally different in-game. That made sense to someone. But the overall comabt is just pure garbage. I havent seen an encounter that was memorable. its mostly just people missing each other wwith arrows and axes for too long of a time. Srsly, I spectated two players trying to kill each other and I was able to go outside, grab my mail, answer a text, and come back in front of the screen and the battle was still going on. Time to kill in a BR game needs to be shorter. The longer your 1v1 engagement takes the higher the chances of it turing into 2v1. Matter of fact, the best thing is to try and wait for two poeple to fight, observe, and then just attack them both. They'll drain each other and youre good.*Scoring system*Just stay alive and away from everyone. You'll score more points and place higher and you dont have to engage anyone. So stay near a map and away from players. Our last match the #2 high score was a person who encountered no one, did no damage...essentially just sat in one quadrant. Everyone knows that in BR style games your score is (or should be) based on your rank + the damage/kills you rack up for the round. I understand its EA, but still. This is pretty basic. It had to be made this way*How does it Run?*Fine. Its Unreal. It should run fine so long as you dont get too close to realism or overly complicate it. Case in point: Fortnite and Realm Royale both run pretty good (Fortnite better obviously, its their engine)*Is it a god idea?*I think so. It will tell us if players running lobbies can bring this into a broadcasting environment and engage and audience beyond the players themselves. I hope it works and I hope they make necessary changes*So wtf is your problem mate?*My medication hasnt been tweaked in some time and and sick of clunky combat made for controller kiddies realeased into the wild like a badger being let out of a trap. Devs lately say "Holy cow I think we got something...back up, we're going to release this!" Ever had to fight a badger while youre on mushrooms? I do this every Saturday. But it doesnt mean Im going to recommend it to others. I'll give them the same advice...just wait. One day it will morph into a beautiful butterfly. And then you can eat it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game, whew, where do I start. I guess it's best if I tell a story about my first win. We started the game and I was immediately hearing another player gathering rescources. The show director comes up to both of us and makes us do a gladiator battle for his favor, I won. Once he had given me a speed boost, and then placed a nuke in my area, I ran as fast as I could, until I met three playes fighting over an electronic. I waited it out while they all fought, once they killed the third player, I landed killing shots on both of the of the other players while they were fighting, I then managed to grab the electronic and get the cloak power up. The show director then put a manhunt on me and the other three players remaining tried to hunt me down.  As I was running up a tall canyon with looming cliffs on either side, I saw a small flash behind a large grove of trees, someone was hiding in them, I wanted to make the player think I didn't know they were there, so I kept walking. I then saw where the player was going to teleport, putting all my trust in timing, I ran and jumped at the mark and swung my shovel just as the player phased right in front of me. BOOM, kill. I also escaped the manhunt and continued on. I soon heard two players fighting, so I activiated my cloak and headed over, once one player killed the other, I spang out and had an adrenaline pumping fight to the death, for 4 minutes we traded arrows, fighting in the shade, if you know what I mean. I then said screw it and ran at him, one hit with my fully upgraded shovel and it was over. All in all it was a boring match, compared to what fun you can normally have in Darwin Project.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, after investing a fair amount of time into this beauty of a game i feel like i need to defend it and shed some light into it's Pros and Cons, since most of the positive reviews of this site are very vague and coming from people with low playtime and the negatives are critisicing small issues that ain't really that bad or just plain wrong, i'm yet to see any negative review which adresses the actual core issues that this game has (that there really are).WARNING: Long ass review incoming.Part 1: "The Game, is fun, if it's not fun, then why bother?" - Reggie <3So, the game is a Battle Royale, you've heard it millions of times, you loot, explore and kill upstanding members of society in order to become the last man standing. More or less the same, right? Well, you would be kinda right, but this game has some core changes to what i will call the "Royale Formaluae". Namely these are:-Lower playercount: The game's matches are meant for 10 players, 11 if you count the Show Director (we'll get into that later).-No weapon/equipment looting per se, in replacement, the game features a simple and intuitive crafting system which requires you to scavenge resources such as wood, leather and electronic devices in order to craft all the goodies, which include (at the time of writing this review) Four diferent types of arrows (some track, some hurt a bit more, some come in with ammo at the start and some give you stamina boost), three types of axes (More damage, faster looting and crafting times and heals when looting corpses), four cloaks (to resist cold more effectively aswell as to track enemy attackers, have more stamina and lessen enemy track timers), a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ of tools (Bear traps, tripwires, gliders for easy movement, fake chests, tripcages, hooks to get close and personal) and electronic powers (Shrink, teleport, energy shield, ice bolt, power leap, arena and a turret).-Tracking System: One of the best and most unique features of this game is the tracking system. The devs felt like the most boring moment on battle royales such as PUBG and others is the time spent between the exhilarating encounters and shootouts with other players, and felt like just looting wasn't fun enough, so they decided to make it so that every action you perform (crafting, looting, shooting, even your tracks on the snow by walking) can and WILL be tracked in order to find you and probably kill you. This helps increase or decrease the rate of fights depending on the will of the players or their ability to be sneaky.-And last but not least the Show Director: This truly is the most special feature this game has to offer. Each match is issued a Show Director, a player who queues up for that role and is intended to be the director of the match, think Dungeons and Dragons Dungeon Keeper, alright? These Directors have a Power Deck filled with different abilities to use in order to spice up the match, such as closing zones, activating events (Zero gravity, a period where everyone is tracked by everyone, double loot, etc) and many more to come.Besides from all of that, the game also features a Tile-based map which randomly chooses between the available tiles to create an unpredictable and amazing map. The quality of these vary, but i dare say that the last ones are great and very different from any other BR map, really.Part 2: The community.Now, this is a social game, and if you dont mention the community then you can't really talk about it. I've been playing since the very launch of the game and the community has obviosuly had it's ups and downs, but today i am glad to say that it is one of the most welcoming, caring, and competitive communities out there. Everyone strives to be the best, but without being toxic with others or disrespectful in any way, there are some very creative directors out there that really spice up and improve the game for everyone, and the competitive scene is actually quite stable and H A R D (which i love) and since getting gud requires a good amount of time, basically everyone knows each other on the so-called "high ranks".Part 3: But is it really that good?Sadly, the game suffers from quite a bit of issues, some major and some are just some nitpicks of mine, but issues nonetheless. The Devs really try their hardest to deliver good content in schedule, but big content droughts and badly optimized/balanced patches do happen more times than i would want to. There are some core issues related with the way the axe works and its hitbox, some patches it is really inconsistent, some patches it hits really far away or some other ones make it straight up impossible to axe fight without a lot of parries and deflects that make it really hard to make any damage, making it so that people restrain from using it too much and go to the security and consistency of the bow and arrow. The low playercount takes it toll on the matchmaking system, it's not an uncommon ocurrance to see complete newbs go in a lobby against top tier players, making the experience really frustrating and hard for new players, and moreso due to the lack of a proper tutorial which explains it all to them. Some Directors have it quite easy for teaming, and if it weren't for the general strictness of the devs and players towards this attitude it could be easily exploitable, the list could really go on if you count the technical issues and glitches (although that is to expect from a Early Acess game).Part 4: ConclusionI really ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ love this game despite it's evident faults and problems, because it just ticks off some of my most wanted boxes in games, it really scratches an itch that none other game in the market does, and the amount of cool people and friends i've made thanks to this game realy makes it worth the experience, ESPECIALLY since it is free during it's EA period. If you are just remotedly interested on the game, give it a try, join the official discord community for tips, or you can also look for local communities and make some friends (if you're spanish go check out our amazing community :D), and if you think that i got something wrong, please state it on the comments so that i can make this the  U L T I M A T E review.Thank you very much! TL:DRIt's got its ups and downs, but since it is so unique and fun, and free i really dont see it NOT worth playing.

_childDocuments_.review: Darwin Project, a unique entry in the battle royale genre, sets out to revolutionize the formula with its focus on player interaction, environmental manipulation, and a captivating setting. However, while it succeeds in some aspects, it ultimately falls short of its lofty ambitions.One of Darwin Project's standout features is its emphasis on player interaction and strategy. The ability to track opponents, set traps, and engage in intense one-on-one combat adds depth to the gameplay, creating tense and exhilarating moments that set it apart from its competitors.The game's setting, a post-apocalyptic Canadian wilderness, is visually striking and brimming with potential. The inclusion of a Show Director, who oversees the match and can influence its outcome, adds an extra layer of intrigue and unpredictability, making each match feel like a unique and dynamic experience.However, Darwin Project is let down by several key issues that prevent it from reaching its full potential. One of the most glaring issues is its lack of player base, which leads to lengthy matchmaking times and empty lobbies. This not only hampers the overall experience but also makes it difficult to fully appreciate the game's innovative mechanics.Furthermore, Darwin Project suffers from balance issues and a steep learning curve, which can be off-putting to newcomers. The disparity in skill levels between players can make matches feel unfair and frustrating, detracting from the game's potential for strategic depth and meaningful player interaction.Additionally, while the inclusion of a Show Director is a novel concept, it often feels underutilized and poorly implemented. The role lacks meaningful impact on the outcome of matches and can sometimes result in arbitrary interference that disrupts the flow of gameplay.Despite its shortcomings, Darwin Project remains a promising concept with a solid foundation. With continued support and refinement, it has the potential to carve out a niche for itself in the competitive gaming landscape. However, until these issues are addressed, it's difficult to wholeheartedly recommend Darwin Project to all but the most dedicated of players.

Releasing in 2018 the game has gone through many changes such as becoming free to play after their first year, becoming available to Xbox and Playstation, and game changes such as introducing a class system to your character. Darwin project is set in the cold North of Canada where 10 players are dropped into an arena with an axe and bow with one goal, be the last one standing. Apart from gathering resources and battling the cold, Darwin turns this into entertainment by adding the Director who commentates and communicates with the players to make each battle unique.Full Review Here:

_childDocuments_.review: I've tried Fortnite, I've tried PUBG, and I like a lot of things about them, but my brain falls asleep and I never felt the "addictiveness" people talk about. Just feels like "same sh** with different people" and it's boring to me. Well, Darwin Project is the first Battle Royale-inspired game that I actually "get". I see why people like this stuff now.I thought only having 10 players instead of 100 would make it feel stupid and unfair and make matches end too fast, but each player feels like a League of Legends champion. They're powerful, resilient, and have unique ability choices that give each person their own unique signature. Players last beyond the first gunfight, the second, the third, the tenth. Players feel more like heroes instead of defenseless naked children, and that helps it be amazing instead of garbage.Oh and also, the game actually does a lot to remind you that this is a show people are watching! That helps a lot too, including the real-life Twitch and Mixer integration.[]It's a Battle Royale game that doesn't feel cheap and half-baked. It's a "FPS/TPS with one person commanding from above" game that's truly fun.A couple ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ for the developers though, which didn't impact my fun in the end but I think you should address anyway:♥♥♥♥♥♥ 1: I strongly, strongly feel that $14.99 is too high. I think $9.99 would be a better impulse buy, which is what you want. People who say "Oh well, eff it, I'm bored so let's try this" are going to be your long-term target audience. Make it cheaper (fill it with evil cosmetic loot boxes to make up for the lost profit even, I don't care) and I'd be happier about the chances of your game still being packed with people a year from now. I dunno about most people, but for me, $14.99 is teetering on the line where I ask "Hmm, wait, do I really think I'll *love* this?" and $9.99 is more impulse buy territory.♥♥♥♥♥♥ 2: I don't know if it's a bug or a feature, but whenever I listen to voice chat in-game, it sounds scratchy and high-pitched and just plain broken. I don't know if it's my computer or this game, but there's a lot of clipping (the kind of clipping where audio reaches max volume and sounds like your speakers are crackling), please fix it. I play Overwatch, I play Battlefield, I play awful 3D group chat programs - and none of the voice chats sound like they took a trip through the 1950s before reaching my ears.♥♥♥♥♥♥ 3 (this is a big one I think): I tried the Xbox trial just to see how things are over there, and on the Xbox One X at 4K, the framerate is *deplorable*. It's just freaking downright pathetic and unplayable. Please put in some dynamic resolution thing, force 1080p, I don't care, 10fps is not enough to have a chance at winning.Anyway that's all! This game really caught my attention and stood out to me as more than just a cash-in on the BR craze. It's thought-out, lovely, and all-around fun.

It also feels great to learn all the details of the map, as there is only one so far. The show director system is very nice, too. You'd think a system like this would be prone to abuse, but instead the community is sane enough to make the show director's interaction feel exciting, and not at all annoying.Only the matchmaking could be better. I feel like I've reached a point where I'm regularly put together with noobs instead of experienced players - this could be a Duo mode problem though, as I'm only playing Duo with my mate.And it's not completely optimized:  When I first launched the game, it made my screen flicker, and I had to go into the settings and switch to fullscreen, which was a pain in the ass.All in all, very good game, especially considering it's F2P and offers only cosmetic microtransactions. Clearly recommended.Edit: Played some rounds as a show director now, and the rating system is pretty bad. Seems like only those who're unhappy rate at all. I even tried only helping people, without annoying anybody (no closing zones etc.) and after the round my rating was even worse. Have a 2.22 rating now, can't use any powers. It's no surprise then that most rounds don't even have a show director.EDIT:Not working anymore since the last update. Constant blackscreen and fiddling with the settings does not help at all.

_childDocuments_.review: First off, I would like to clarify something. If you are a very competitive person, or a very casual person, you may love this game. I myself got addicted to this game back in early 2018. I then committed myself to playing the game as it was the only fun game in my library. I got better and better over time, eventually becoming an above average player. I started participating in tournaments and scrims (basically practice tournaments). However, once I got to a certain level of skill, it felt like I was no longer getting any better. So I did what most people would do. Either really try to get better, or look for a new game. Quick side note: If you get competitive in this game and you're generally competitive anyways, you might find yourself getting pretty mad at times. Whether it be that an arrow shot "shouldn't" have hit you, or that axe that you just got hit by was "bs". And sure, these things do happen, but just remember that every game has bugs. Anyways, with that out of the way, I really want to go OVER the game itself. I like the idea of classes in darwin project, however with any huge update like changing the entire combat system, bugs / glitches are bound to happen. I'm not gonna sit here and say that they should revert, but I think they should put a LOT of time into discussing the future of classes if they want to keep the ball rolling with this game. Personally, my favorite part of this game is that you can talk / meet with existing friends, or make new ones. I have probably made 30 or so people on my friends list just from people on Darwin that I just met in game or something like that. But of course the main focus of the game is combat, etc. I like the combat system a lot. (besides all of the dash attacks, etc). The gameplay with just the axe and the bow is so incredibly simple, that it's just so refreshing to see. I haven't seen ONE other battle royale that has used an axe as the main way of combat (besides the bow). Now, the only problem I see with this system however is the fact that since professional players have been using these weapons for over 2 years, they have practically mastered the bow and axe. So when new players come along, sure they'll know "how" to use them, but they won't know things like bow jukes, and how to properly dodge arrows. The main reason this game isn't as popular as it is if you ask me is because when new players come along, they get obliterated by all of the OG / good players, then they stop playing because their rate of improvement is so incredibly slow. As for some suggestions, I recommend adding crossplay. I'm sure you've heard it from a ton of people, but it really would help this game out. For one, the servers on PC as you may know are running pretty low right now. 10 PLAYER LOBBIES are BARELY being filled up. However, with the addition of crossplay, this would no longer be an issue due to their being more players on Xbox. Next up, fix your servers. And once again I'm sure you've been hearing this as well Scavengers Studios. But honestly, FIX  THE  SERVERS. I don't mean to be rude, seriously. But I really do think that people are leaving this game for that reason. Consistent game crashes. Lobby crashes, launch issues, the list goes on. I'm not saying you need to fix everything I say now, but in the future I think this is what the game needs to survive and flourish. As for 2 little personal things that I would like to see added into the game, I think instead of just being able to turn DOWN the Field of view, I think you should be able to turn it UP as well. 2nd thing, and I believe I sent this as a suggestion as well, but make the default crosshair when you boot up the game for the first time the original crosshair from before you could change it. Now I'm not saying to make it to where you can't change it. But I'm saying to just make it the default, and you can change it if you would like. I think that after using that crosshair for so long, and just for it to be taken away and not being able to use it again really threw (SOME) people off like myself. As for small other things, try to optimize your game a lot because I tend to see that I get abnormally high ping / latency only while playing Darwin project. Make the feel of the game better / make the gameplay a lot more smooth. Those last couple of things aren't as big as some of the other suggestions, but they were just things that I personally think would make the game better. I have one last thing to say, and It's the most important thing you must do. This isn't a suggestion, but rather a MUST. And for the third time, you've heard it so many times, but I'm here to remind you and tell you again, They know what they want. Overall I think the game is in an overall limbo. It's not dying like everyone is claiming, but it's not gaining in popularity either. This game has so much potential, and I want to see it come alive. But unfortunately that won't happen if the game company won't listen to their players. Thank you for reading.

_childDocuments_.review: [Edit: Game received for free after playing the open beta. Will update impressions after I play it more]Never played a Battle Royale game before. Played this during Open Beta #1.For a Beta (which should mean "bug/balance testing version of an already complete game, I think), this game had less content than a lot of Early Access games out there. Few customization options, few weapons, few variations on gameplay elements like maps, perks and crafting materials.But the game was actually very fun. The survival, tracking and crafting dynamics are actually very clever, although very simplistic. The loadout system adds a layer of strategy and planning, and having to decide between almost freezing to death or warming yourself with a fire that can be seen for miles is quite a nice touch. This game actually feels like something Blizzard would make nowadays: take a popular genre and make it as simple and casual as possible, but still entertaining to play (at least for some time). As I said, I have no experience with other battle royale games, but this one surely felt very arcadey. Even compared to other survival games like Rust or Minecraft or Don't Starve, there is only so much you can do in this game...I played some rounds, and then left the game with a curiosity on what it will turn out to be when it gets released. I have a fear that it might get repetitive, and lost among many other games that are fine but don't catch on.[Edit: now the game is on Early Access and it is not free. Not sure yet if I would recommend it as a paid product.]I don't know how much this game will cost after release. At the current state, I would only play it as a F2P game, and I recommend it for other people to try it if they can do that for free as well.

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10, VERY addictive and fun game.A lot of people are going to be sceptical "oh, another battle royale game, there's only hundreds out there already", but let me tell you: This is different. And really, really, really good. It is fast paced, intuitive, competitive and a hell lot of fun.I played a couple of rounds, and even won some, and I will certainly play this game a lot more in the future.You join a game, and have to fight against 10 other people, last one to live, wins. Sounds easy, but there are some differences from your standart BR game.There is a show director, which is a moderator who can use specials and buffs for players, nuke certain areas, apply moon-gravity to places, and a lot of other cool stuff. The directors will help you if you are nice to them, and sometimes ask questions to find out if you are worthy of their skills. It makes the battlefield feel a lot more dynamic than in all other BR games I have played. If you stream on twitch, your viewers can actually vote for events in the game!Also there is crafting, which is necessary to get things like arrows, pitfires, traps and some boosts to speed, warmth etc.You can either play solo against 9 oher players, or as a duo against 5 other duos(which I haven't tested out yet)One of the biggest positives for this game is the community. Aside from a few hot-micing russians or infants the people I played with were extremely nice. There is local voice chat, so even though I haven't experienced it once yet, there are certainly going to be a few salty people as well (which you can mute easily), but so far I am amazed by the nice community. At the end of a round you can rate the director 1 to 5 stars, if you feel like he significantly preferred other players, or even teamed up against others, making the game unfair, you can vote him 1 star and he will be restricted in his actions in future matches where he plays as a director.TL:DR:+Beautiful, fitting comic-like graphics+Very good performance+Completely free (no pay2win whatsoever!!!!)+Very generous community+Very easy to learn, hard to master+Combat is very rewarding+Frequent updates+Developers communicate with playerbase, and do a good job at it+Good crafting system-Rarely unfair games because of ♥♥♥♥ directors

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATED: January 2020.OLD: This game is fun and unique. The push from the devs to encourage fighting from happening more often than in games like PUBG and Fortnite is brilliant, and executed wonderfully. And even with only 10 players, the game still feels tense like the other major BRs. With no weapon RNG, it can easily be more balanced for all the players, and the only way players can get the edge is not being lucky and finding a super powerful weapon, but getting enough crafting materials to upgrade their gear, tools, and powers. Getting the materials, wood and leather, is pretty easy. Getting electronics is a bit more luck based, but still decently fair in the terms of a BR.When I first posted this review, I stated that the director needed work. Originally, the problem was that the director could team and be abused; however, things have changed since then. There is now a rating system which, if the director is a bad director, will eventually get low ratings until he cannot use abilities that cannot affect one person at a time. You can also report people not following the rules, so that will be useful.I recommend it, but you may not like the differences in this game compared to other BRs. I think the game is already good in many aspects, and I hope it continues to grow in a positive direction.P.S: Scavenger Studio gave all alpha and beta testers (yes, even the ones during the beta) a free key for the game. That was amazing, and I am greatly thankful for them doing that. And as of 4/20/18, now the game was made free to play for everyone, so go try it out!UPDATE 1/17/20:Ok, so down below, the general idea is still the same, but they made some big changes for 1.0. First, the customization is constricted (less freedom but more balanced and easier to understand) with classes. Three classes currently exist, the jetpack (mobile, airborne, aggressive), grapple gauntlet (mobile close range brawler), and the headhunter (longer range stealth and tracking)). They all have their own set of powers you can choose from. Down below I mention leather. Well, guess what, it is gone. Darwinium now exists, and it is used to upgrade your character or earn such powers (Electronic spawns now are just huge deposits of Darwinium). Also, I mention the director. Well, it has been expanded on and changed much more over the period of Early Access, so it is much better (but is a bit grindy when it comes to unlocking all the stuff). Anyways, read on below.

_childDocuments_.review: Darwin Project™, is honestly in a very werid spot, in a year thats honestly very over saturated by battle royale style games, such as PUBG, Fornite, Radical Heights and more to come, this game manages to subvert all of my expectations and be a very unique experience and one of my favorite games of the year.Pros:- The tracking system in this game is one of its greatest draws, when you have to think about all of your resources you use, where you place fires, from where you even walk, makes this game alot more tense than it should be, words don't bring justice to how intense it can be when your getting tracked down by someone, not knowing how far they can be away from you, knowing that they can see PERFECTLY clear where you are.- Combat in this game may be simple, but it keeps you on your toes and makes you constantly think. Having a stamina par, and being equip with a bow and a axe at the instant the game starts, puts everyone at a fair playing field, timing with your axe is key, as well as having a keen eye and a good shot with a bow. What helps as well is that armor in this game can only block one hit, keeping it a high risk high reward of resources.- Unlike other royales, this game likes to keep it small, having a 10 man lobby, this keeps large enough so you don't have to worry about seeing others as you spawn, yet it manages to keep the flow of the game short enough not to feel like your hiding in a building or "in the zone" for 5-10 minutes checking your phone while waiting for some tosser to walk past your door/windowCons:- ♥♥♥♥ off  or however the ♥♥♥♥ you spell your name, you are to good at this game- Some of the items that you can craft need some nerfs, tripwire and turret mostly-Having a bad comentator can ruin a game for you, you could be in the middle of a fight and they could start healing the enemy constantly, having experiences like this constantly can ruin a game for you-Since the game is currently in Alpha, it suffers from a lot of werid issues, I myself have experienced currently, Slow loading, black screens, and the game taking up 80% of my CPU usage for 2 secondsFinal Thoughts:This game is easily one of the best games I have played this year and easily the best battle royale style game I have played, alot more enjoyable than my whole experience on PUBG, Fortnite and Radical Heights. I highly recomend picking it up, even more so if you have some friends willing to try it with you, as you can setup private lobbies.Gameplay: 9/10Graphics: 7/10Singleplayer: 8/10Duos/private matchs: 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: "It looks like Fortnite and will play like any other Battle Royale game probably."That were my thoughts upon seeing this game on Steam today. Oh boy, I was so wrong! 'Darwin Project' definitly is one unique Battle Royale game. It's easy to learn and hard to master. Ten players fight on a map consisting of multiple territories that get's smaller and smaller the longer the game goes on. Last one standing is the winner. Along the way you have to watch your "Coldness Meter" in order to stay warm and not freeze to death. You'll have to hack down trees, take apart leather chairs (to get leather, for some reason you just loot chairs made out of leather lmao), hunt deer and loot chests to craft and upgrade your gear. You can customize your "crafting wheel" in order to suit your playstyle. Wanna go in there and f*ck sh*t up? Take the axe damage buffs, berserker arrows and stamina cloaks. Wanna go sneaky beaky assassin style. The ninja boots and ghost cloak got you covered! Wanna be fast af boi? Yeah there's loads of items that give you a speed boost depending on the situation. You can experiment around a lot! There are also abilities like a teleport, a damage shield, camouflage, a super jump etc. which you can unlock by gathering rare electronic parts in game.The director, a spectator and sort of a gamemaster, views the entire thing and can manipulate it by closing down territories, nuking a territory, speeding/healing/warming up players and so on. You can also talk to other players and the director, which makes for funny situations. Seriously! Right now, upon winning you don't get anything but some EXP. No fancy unlocks, no shiny gear, nothing. And know what? It's completly fine since the actual gameplay is so much more satisfying than pulling a win. You'll laugh or even completly lose it in every match you play. A funny interaction with the director, a hilarious kill, a sudden save by the director or getting completly f*cked over by him/her is always a fun experience if you're light hearted.There are no guns in 'Darwin Project' so far. And I hope they keep it like that. You can of course use your bow, but aiming isn't that easy and you'll run out of arrows if you don't land your shots. Then it's time for the AXE TIME, BABY! You'll not get anywhere with button smashing in this game, so time your attacks properly and you might get out alive. Utilize traps, abilities and your trusty axe properly, while also landing your arrows and you'll definitly come out on top!'Darwin Project' is a nice game. It's got a solid concept and gameplay but what really is the factor that kept me playing the entire day was the amount of social interaction. I can't say this enough, every match is like a huge fun party and you want to be part of it. You almost feel like you're missing out on something when you see people fighting in the combat chat log and you're not part of it.Starting in the pre-game lobby and ending at the defeat or victory screen you'll be talking/screaming/yelling at other people while fighting or talking to the director. It all depends on the director and the other players but generally speaking if you're a fun, light hearted person the others will join in on the fun.Yes! Yes you should absolutely get this game! People who participated in the alpha/beta got the game for free and it is only 15 bucks. _childDocuments_.review: SummaryGame feels very boring and uninspired. Controls are loose and slippery, Music is nice, but sfx is loud and annoying. Environment is . Characters... I havent seen characters this ugly since jimmy neutron.GameplayIf you've played any other Battle Royale game then you know what to expect for the most part. Main differences are you only have one weapon, and matches are currently restricted to 11 players. The 11th being the "Show Director"; a disembodied voice actively rigging the match, who can reveal players location, give powerups directly, spawn powerup drops on the map, and restrict area on the map. If this isn't your sort of thing then this game really isn't for you.Also, maps are too large for the small number of players you'll be up against, for most of the game you'll be on your own unless you purposefully spend 6-or-so minutes running accross the map to where you last saw an enemy.ArtEnvironments are nice. If you've played any arcade/anime-inspired MOBA within the last quinquennium then you'll feel right at home.The in-game character designs and animations are awful.  I don't know what planet they came from if they thought it would be appealing in any way... (probably Planet Sheen if i had to guess) but whoever gave the greenlight to these character designs really shouldn't be making those kinds of decisions. Thankfully though you'll be staring at their backs for the most part. SoundMusic is nice though not quite appropriate aesthetically imho. Like "Get Even" some of the music contains breathing percussions, which can be a hit or miss for some.Announcements and Kill sfx are overly loud and alarming when theres really no need, as most of the time the game is quiet and you're just running around the map. _childDocuments_.review: BR games are getting stale as ♥♥♥♥ but this one stands out above the crowd.Higher TTK than PUBG or Fortnite resulting in battles being determined by "who can aim better" and not "who shot first".Show Director and viewer relationship actually feels like the Hunger Games take on the Game Master and Sponsors. Make fans with the crowd or the director and you have a huge advantage on the other 9 players. Match-making makes it hard to queue as a show director in order to boost friends. Hard but not impossible unfortunately.Tracking system is a very, "you can run but you can't hide" sort of deal. Sure you can run for the entire game just zipping across the map but there are so many ways for other players to get your exact location resulting in a very hunter/tracking driven system. Works very nice, camping is utterly useless. Either you run or you fight. There is no hiding in houses.The take on zones closing never once made me feel cheated like in PUBG or Fortnite. There's teleports on the edge of each zone to take you into the opposite zone and the zones close randomly for the most part which allows you to take the route that you imagine is best and not the route that the game just forces upon you. It was your decision to go to the west zone rather than the east so if you get screwed later you know you could have played it differently. The show director has the ability force you into a bad spot but there are always ways to survive as long as you have enough wood for fires or if you have an electronic that allows you access to teleport or superjump abilities.Bows take skill to aim with and shoot. The net-play feels very smooth. Never was I shot with an arrow after I got behind cover. Never have I felt that an arrow should have hit someone when it did not. Axe takes some getting used to since the range is very short but being able to time your swings to deflect other player's arrows or snowballs and then going in for the kill has never felt better.Overall I don't think the BR formula has been perfected because there is always room for improvement but these reasons alone make me feel like it's a massive jump in the right direction. This is the game BR developers need to copy, not PUBG or Fortnite with 100 people and RNG circles and bullets that kill you behind cover.

_childDocuments_.review: This is honestly one of my favourite games ever, and comfortably my favourite multiplayer title (though I also love L4D2) - it's unique take on the Battle Royale gimmick in having a show director to influence games is a fantastic addition and the depth of content stellar - the ability to use things like traps, gliders and turrets for example open up many new strategies of play, which is then further augmented by the ability to customise your characters loadout both in terms of items and stat buffs. This wideness is playstyle also means there is a very high skill ceiling for this kind of game.Of course however this game is not without it's flaws - most of which relate to it's playercount: it's too low. It's not uncommon to start a game with an incomplete lobby (which also means skill based matchmaking doesn't happen) which really slows down the games pace. Furthermore, the few people who have clung on are very often big fans very near the aforementioned high skill ceiling (myself included) which means a VERY high skill floor. Players new to DP (and especially competitive FPS games in general) WILL be killed quickly and ruthlessly by more experienced players. When/if the playerbase expands (hopefully at full launch) this will not be as much of an issue - but right now it's hard to really get involved.I've written a lot about that one issue, but don't let that overshadow it. Put the time in and this game is actually stellar - my over 500 hours played is testament to how sincere I am in that statement. Highly recommended to play and stick at for a while (the bot practice helps with the skill floor) and tell your friends too.

_childDocuments_.review: Note: If you're interested in a shorter review, read the conclusion at the end of this review.It was a really cool game at it's release state. Now since it was abandoned, you could guess why I give it this negative review. There are pretty much no players and you could only play it against bots with no Show-Master which is one of the main features this game can offer.Overall Darwin Project changed since it was released. It received alot of tweaks and balance changes and was treated with care by the developers. It was fun too play aswell since an aggressive was rewarding and experience + skill could make a huge difference. Oh and if the Show-Master didn't like you, you would probably lose anyway because of their really big influence. As Show-Master you can heal players, give them a temporary shield, speed boost them (or drug them), activate Low-Gravity or close specific parts of the map to force encounters between players and much more! While the Show-Master spectates, you are able to use Voicechat to talk to players and give them information, ask them dumb questions or make them hallucinated.  Players could talk to each other too. You were able to trashtalk your opponent mid battle or have a serious argument about your arrows phasing trough the opponent. It really was a fun little mechanic.Players need to collect Wood, Darwinium to craft different abilities, consumables and stat-boosters. There are different abilities, consumables and stat-booster available with other effects supporting all kinds of playstyles. But there is still a best Loadout/Meta in these. Looting from a Tree to get wood, crafting or looting will leave trails behind, which other players can use to track the player down who left them. In Combat you can utilize your axe or bow and arrows + the abilities or use a dodgeroll (it sucks). Landing headshots is difficult but rewarded by dealing extra damage. If you're out of arrows you can still pick up arrows from the ground that missed it's target or deflect an arrow with your axe (really cool stuff).The Game died when they decided to add a battlepass and cosmetics to the game, which was at the same time as the game was made Free-to-play, and when the grapplinghook was introduced. Yes that's right, the game costed 15 euro but as it went free, players who already bought the game, were given 2 Lootboxes which I didn't care about (I'm still mad btw). Moving on to the Grapplinghook, which was a cheap consumable that guarantee's a free hit on your opponent and was not really thought through by the devs and since the game died it never will be balanced.Conclusion: Darwin Project died, because of a too low playerbase and does not receive Developersupport anymore. If you plan on playing this game without friends, you can try to find a lobby (Only if you're not using American servers) but you're likely to not find one. Prepare to play with the ingame Bots that are not really eventful and fun to play against. Or grab about 4-8 friends to play in a private lobby and actually have some fun, as the core mechanics of Darwin Project are fun and enjoyable.

_childDocuments_.review: In today's cluttered last-man-standing genre, a lot of BR's look and play the same. Parachute down on a large map, procure weapons (usually firearms), and pick off opponents while pressured into a progressively smaller area. Darwin decided to do something others have not: Fuse a survival game into a king of the hill combat mold. And to a degree, it actually works.Up to 10 players are teleported into a randomly generated map. The map itself is a shuffle of preset "biomes," all mid-winter, but with notable differences: A central frozen lake, scattered treehouses, a futuristic city, a rustic town with a central chapel, a shipping yard, and a molten canyon complete with expansive piping, to name a few. As combatants navigate these, they hunt down chests, chop down trees, harvest darwinium (energy resource), and the occasional robo-deer for special items and healing. Using gathered resources, you can craft arrows, a couple traps, and class-specific upgrades to boost your offensive, defensive, or tactical abilities.It's a lot to take in at first, but with practice, becomes second nature. Darwin is a high skill ceiling game for those who dare to master it, giving you all the tools to pull of incredible trickshots with a bow, intense melee axe fights, or satisfying 4D chess plays of out-maneuvering opponents into hidden, preset traps. There are many montages on youtube that showcase Darwin at its peak, and indeed, it's mesmerizing. Here's just one example: During its early days, Darwin was not built on classes, but rather, customization. You could directly upgrade and build any combination of powers you pleased, limited only by resources and the time to craft them. On launch, they removed this freedom and narrowed your abilities into three classes: Jetpack, Grapple Hook, Seeker Drone. Jetpack focuses on verticality / aerial bow use / speed, Grapple on melee / shields / 1v1, Seeker on tracking / trapping / invisibility. Within your class selection your access to abilities is limited, so you need to make the most of your strengths. Ultimately, though, every class comes down to quick reflexes and good aim.Darwin's survival element has you juggle a constant pressure against cold, which, if ignored, will steadily deplete your HP akin to a poison effect. To combat this, you craft fires that warm you up, but give away your position to the enemy by a stage-wide visible smoke signal. You can put these out early by crafting snowballs, or use them strategically to throw off opponents. Speaking of snowballs, you can lob these at opponents to lower their cold resistance and possibly seal a battle of attrition if they can't warm up.Last but not least, the game had a novel idea of tasking one spectator player as a show director, granting the power to spice things up to their whims. These had access to "cards" (randomly selected events) including things like resource gifts, buffs, zone closure, and even a nuke, forcing players to evacuate or risk KO by countdown. It featured a twitch integration to let the audience vote and grant bonus XP to the most entertaining participants.So why is the game in maintenance mode, then? As per usual, my thoughts: - Before it went F2P, Darwin was a pay to play title, which likely kept potential players at bay (the early access dilemma). Eventually, the game extended to other platforms, but had limitations: It was never available on Switch, and for Xbox players, Live was required. Though it utilized Twitch and picked up some streamers, where else was it advertised? If the intended market was competitive, where were the tournaments and the big prizes? There were some, but I can't recall hearing about them. - Unlike its cartoonish appearance, Darwin is no casual game. If you didn't already, watch the linked video above to get a sense for how fast combat can be... significant precision and foresight are needed to land your shots, deflect attacks, or lure opponents into traps. I'm not sure that Darwin pulled enough of the esports type, which the game seems made for. When streamers picked up the game, some rose to the challenge and improved their skill. But others, soured by continuous losses, became detractors, and their complaints shaped content changes. It's a catch-22 of wanting a competitive audience but catering your game to players who weren't as dedicated, and the end result was alienating both experienced alpha testers (who didn't like the class system) and the newcomers getting stomped by pros in the full release, who may not have stuck around long enough. Speaking of which, some casuals didn't even make it past the survival mechanics to manage their cold meters. They wanted faster games. - Touched on above, not a lot of early adopters appreciated losing the full crafting wheel and being pigeonholed into classes. Battlepass came late in the life cycle, finally giving players something to strive for with tasks to perform. And not to be forgotten, duos - party with a friend - was a defining draw to the game, and it was taken out on release (in favor of ranked free for all). Some people only want to play with pals, and that forced these out altogether.Today, you can still experience vanilla Darwin under custom matches - I suggest you do so - to see what could have been. If you enjoy it, search the forums for discord links to find premades and get a real game going. You can gamble on midweek and weekend randoms but true challengers all go customs.: Typical grind achievements. Very time consuming... there is no consistent way to get XP outside of 1 daily win + top 3 finish. You can farm with a friend or use an idle account. Must be done in public matchmaking, customs don't count. Level 50 is easily a 3 month or so commitment.And caution about the legendary weapon skin. It costs 1500 ramen which you will earn as you grind levels and perform daily tasks. You could get lucky and find one in a level up crate, but if not, be sure NOT TO BUY LEGEND CLOTHING. My mistake cost me another month of grind.~50-100 hrs to 100% ?

name: Half-Life: Alyx
detailed_description: Half-Life: Alyx is Valve’s VR return to the Half-Life series. It’s the story of an impossible fight against a vicious alien race known as the Combine, set between the events of Half-Life and Half-Life 2. Playing as Alyx Vance, you are humanity’s only chance for survival. The Combine’s control of the planet since the Black Mesa incident has only strengthened as they corral the remaining population in cities. Among them are some of Earth’s greatest scientists: you and your father, Dr. Eli Vance. As founders of a fledgling resistance, you’ve continued your clandestine scientific activity—performing critical research, and building invaluable tools for the few humans brave enough to defy the Combine. Every day, you learn more about your enemy, and every day you work toward finding a weakness. ABOUT GAMEPLAY IN VR: Valve’s return to the Half-Life universe that started it all was built from the ground up for virtual reality. VR was built to enable the gameplay that sits at the heart of Half-Life. Immerse yourself in deep environmental interactions, puzzle solving, world exploration, and visceral combat. Lean to aim around a broken wall and under a Barnacle to make an impossible shot. Rummage through shelves to find a healing syringe and some shotgun shells. Manipulate tools to hack alien interfaces. Toss a bottle through a window to distract an enemy. Rip a Headcrab off your face and throw it out the window. COMMUNITY-BUILT ENVIRONMENTS A set of Source 2 tools for building new levels is included with the game, enabling any player to build and contribute new environments for the community to enjoy through Half-Life: Alyx's Steam Workshop. Hammer, Valve’s level authoring tool, has been updated with all of the game's virtual reality gameplay tools and components.

_childDocuments_.review: Half-Life Alyx continues to be the most developed and ambitious VR game made to this day, in 2023. Across all VR platforms and the PC that exist as of right now, Valve managed to not only release a new installment 13 years after the last Half-Life title with a twist that re-wrote the end of Half-Life 2 Episode 2, but also combine everything I constantly miss about VR games - fluid gameplay in all actions with polished technical elements, all into one package.I'm particularly fond of the Gravity Gloves, which are super quick to learn and super easy to use. It's not on a level like Half-Life 2's sandbox gameplay with it's Gravitron, but still allows for cool moves in the world. Sometimes foregrounded physical objects that you accidentally pull towards you can be the reason you get frustrated when using them, but those moments are pretty rare.And speaking of physical objects: Every object in the world can be interacted with as you would expect in real life: Understandable, with weight, sometimes requiring two-handed actions. I found myself very often just playing around with rattling a box of matches near my ear to hear them moving in the box or just throwing and jiggling cardboard boxes around. It's a lot of fun.The weapons serve their purpose in the world, although I would have liked to see a rudimentary melee weapon to knock down wooden slats or headcrabs, even though i can sort of understand why it is missing in the world because it can make inventory management a whole lot easier, taking away the situation Alyx is in. But a pipe you can smack something like 3 times with would've been cool nonetheless. What i dislike about the weapon selection is the pistol, which like in many VR games, takes the design of the 1911. We've had enough games that use this as a standard. Other than that, the game shifts the focus from the pistol being the main weapon to the SMG in the second half of the game with the shotgun being the weapon which is the most coolest out of them, but also the one barely used because of how few shotgun shells you find for it.The multi-tool is cool and is also well incorporated into the game world.The story is well-written and i liked to experience it while playing, although the connection to Half-Life 2 Episode 2 in this game makes me want to see another game in the franchise again. Normally, when people beg Valve for another Half-Life game, i often roll the eyes, but now Valve brought it up to themselves with the ending. Characters in the world are also very well designed, have amazing voice actors and body motion within the world, with the exception of Alyx' voice. Russell is normally a character i'd despise of in real life, but through the conversations i had with him, i started to like him more and more. The conversations with Eli are often only "I miss you baby" and "I can't believe it". A little bit uncanny is the Vortigaunt's mouth when speaking, since i was so used to the design in Half-Life 2.The game world is very well designed and fun to move around in, with the only thing in it that i can't understand being the existence and placement of resin balls which are used for weapon upgrades, or the fact that there is always ammunition scattered around and on some people and ONLY the ones YOU need, which makes the feel of the world a little bit out of place. SMG rounds being found somewhere is fine, since it's a weapon actually used by someone else than you, but finding shotgun shells and pistol magazines when seemingly no one else has a weapon like it doesn't make a lot of sense to me.But even with little logical mistakes or irritating design choices - at least in my eyes - the game is a must-have for everyone who owns a capable PC and a VR headset. The community-made campaigns, especially Levitation, are also incredibly well-made, making them the big cherry on top of your dessert. And especially in a sale for about 24 euros, which is a bit more than Blade & Sorcery or Pavlov VR outside a sale, it's totally worth it. You can also use the NoVR mod if you don't own a VR headset, in that case tho except a lot less of the impressions that VR players normally have with Half-Life Alyx.

_childDocuments_.review: Experience with mid settings on a gaming laptop and a PSVR2 headset/controllers.Honestly this is one of the best VR experiences to get and for Half Life fans a treat. I was extremely bummed when this was announced/released that this was a VR 'exclusive' experience. Yes, we all know there is a NOVR mod by now but honestly you shouldnt play it with NOVR you are depriving yourself of a superb experience.The good: visually absolutely gorgeous and thats not even everything maxed out. Gameplay is fun, engaging and very immersive/interactive. The gravity gloves make sense. You do not feel overpowered in any way.Honestly I really felt like playing HL2 for the first time again. Its the same kind of leap in technology/immersion and most of the time it makes me think: 'how will VR games be in a couple of years after this one?'. Same as Half Life 2 did with me back in the day.Nothing but praise for Valve. Ballsy move to finally release a Half Life title after all that time and have it be VR exclusive but I fully understand why. However though I do not see myself ever playing VR games only as a replacement for the classic games. VR is a great and cool addition to games and should be treated as addition to the classic games, not a replacement.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, just wow. Visually stunning, a breath of fresh air for the Half-Life franchise. The puzzles are surprisingly fun - simple, yet innovative, they do get old though after a while. Combat is sharp, although it is the most simplistic in the franchise. What really sells this game for me is the level design and attention to detail. Half-Life Alyx is insanely atmospheric, filled to the brim with different locations and props for you to interact with, often reminding me of the best parts of HL1 & HL2. I just wish they expanded on the interactive aspect of the game a bit more. Valve, however were the first to make a full-fledged VR game, so overall, it is a marvelous experience that is a MUST PLAY for everyone owning a VR headset.

_childDocuments_.review: Simple things that you don't really think about in normal games become absolutely incredible in Alyx. You actually feel like you're doing something at all times. Looting a filing cabinet isn't just pressing a button - it's walking up to the cabinet, opening the drawer, and peering inside. If supplies are inside, you're physically reaching out and grabbing them and putting them in your backpack. No longer are you pressing a single button to loot something and seeing text of what was inside. As a side note, the flick wrist motion to grab objects far away works great. It's silly how cool it feels to flick pretty much anything towards yourself and catch it.The combat feels real. Just like looting, no longer are you pressing a single button to perform actions. You're not dumping a magazine and then pressing a single button to reload while you backpedal using a stick. If your gun runs dry while enemies are coming at you, you're dropping that mag from the chamber, reaching into your backpack to grab another, inserting it, and getting one in the chamber before you're back in the fight. Hopefully you remembered to create some distance during that time, because that probably took you a lot longer than pressing a single button to reload.I waited for this game to go on sale after finally jumping on the VR train, but it's definitely worth full price. If there were more games like this in VR, regular gaming would no longer be a thing. This is an absolute game changer.

_childDocuments_.review: Eh it's alright. People are calling this the most revolutionary VR game yet- its not. It's the best most complete VR game to date, sure, but don't let anyone tell you it reinvents everything. Almost every single mechanic is something that's been done before and the narrative is standard and boring especially if you're not the average redditor who gives a free pass to anything with a crowbar in it.No- about the only thing special about this game is just the refinement that comes from such a large studio putting enough money behind it. Please don't get me wrong and think I'm ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ on the game, merely pointing out that there is nothing special about this game other than how expensive it was to make. Pavlov has better shooting mechanics and Boneworks better character interactions which makes up the majority of the padded run time.I got this game for free with my 300 dollar Index controllers and I've got to say this game doesn't feel like it was made with them in mind which is a little funny cuz I'm assuming they were being developed at the same times. Guns are glued to your hands so you don't even have to hold on which is a lot bigger immersion breaker than you would think, the fingers seem to curl in only 3 splits so when you close your fingers it looks like they just jump from open to closed until every other game that supports them. The puzzles are poorly designed and pad the run time- speaking of run time Alyx walks like she's just taking a neat little stroll even in combat, ridoinkulously slow and without immersion breaking teleportation I'd turn that shotgun on myself.Look it's a great game and despite not having comments on for this review I know that a lot of you are going to go angrily wank to a picture of le gordan freimam pretending like HL3 is just around the corner and will be a real 2D game. I'm sorry, I just can't stand all of the reviews that claim this is literally the best VR experience of all time because honestly it's just a standard 2D shooter conversion and I feel bad for all the Half Life fans who won't get to play this because Valve wanted to sell Index wands.

_childDocuments_.review: Super good game. If I was going to criticize it a bit my only complaint would be Half-Life 1 & 2 were unapologetically full fledged first person shooters. Half Life: Alyx while it was definitely superb in the quality department and had great gameplay, I felt it was holding back.I know from playing Serious Sam and Boneworks that jumping and high speeds are totally doable and even if you don't want to jump that high or move that fast you can still deliver the same experience. One of my favorite games of all time is Jet Island and it's the speed and freedom of movement that makes that game so wonderful.Half Life: Alyx uses the mechanics it has as perfectly as is humanly possible, but I want more exhilaration. The kind you get from crazy first person acrobatics and interacting with a versatile open ended map.So Half Life: Alyx is the best overall and deserves high praise, but in some way I would say Boneworks is the future. I felt more immersed in Half Life: Alyx and I was genuinely proud to be a girl for awhile, but in Boneworks I had more fun moving the guy around and interacting with things.Also when the monsters attack and kill you, I say go for the gusto. Seeing my heart get yanked out or my limbs torn off would give me a huge mortalgasm, but I do respect the strangulation and chemical attacks as well.Last thing is: No hand to hand combat? You guys have got guts!
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: The wait... The wait was over, and after all the time that passed there was a small glimpse of what's to come, a small blip in a dark void that all of us where looking for.  It was a shocker that after all that a new technology was necessary to play it. Most of us took the leap and OH BOY... was it worth it. The game puts you in the center of it all like never before. Valve staying true to their nature made a big leap in technology but this time it was way beyond mere graphics. A whole new world to interact with, in a way that few of us ever dreamed. The graphics, the tone of the world, the sheer sense of dread and scale like never before. Free to roam, touch, interact with the environment in an organic and natural way. The game while slow paced, makes you feel like you are there a part of it, and It a part of you. The story is polished with a few throwbacks here and there to present day endings of the half life universe, but you are in the past well before any of it happened. Stunning art stile and comic value in the Valve way made the game ever more enjoyable, and the puzzles with the new mechanic where a pleasure to solve. This and many more encounters like Jeff, antlions, Vortigaunts, and Gman where jaw dropping seeing them close to you, almost like you could touch them. Valve in their usual way came and Raise the "Crowbar" again with stunning animations and visuals that will have people talking about them for years to come, Just like the demo the Source engine had, blowing people away with it's features. Was it a long wait? YES... oh god, yes... Was it Worth it? Honestly if I where to have to wait another good chunk of "valve time" for Half life 3 or any other Half life related games, with this kind of quality and polish, I would gladly accept. Thank you Valve for keeping us entertained and ensnared in this universe that you created, let no corner be unchecked, no rock be unlifted, no Gnome be left unlaunched and no Crowbar left behind. Looking forward to Doctor Freeman's return.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: To get it out of the way: this IS a full HL game. The atmosphere is true to the Half-Life games. The art team really nailed in the intimidating appearance of the Combine and the props that you see in the environment depict the alien invasion flawlessly. The environments are convincing and will make you slowly go through each one to appreciate them. As usual for Half-life games, you get to know a little more about the characters based on the way they interact and talk with you rather than reading a bunch of text, which is great. (Played on hard difficulty)The game has a nice balance between rewarding and challenging. You will be required to evolve your muscle memory and improve your reactions throughout the game.Combat feels very satisfying to play. I see the low variety of weapons as a good thing because it keeps the game simple, and you can also improve them as you like, adding new functionalities that replace the need of extra guns. The AI could improve a bit in how they react to your actions in some cases, but other than that, it feels very organic and rewarding to shoot enemies and plan your encounters.The puzzles are also interesting and rewarding mechanics, that are much better than the usual "pressing a single button to continue". Some of them are built on top of the environment which is awesome for realism and interaction. The puzzles do scale as in difficulty as the game progresses, but this could be more pronounced in my opinion.To wrap it up, Valve has set the bar for VR games with this one. I hope other game companies can learn a lot with this release.

_childDocuments_.review: It is not VR's killer app to justify buying a VR headset for, but it is a game that anyone with VR should buy. There are also a lot of little touches that I've liked so much. Pretty much the only thing I disliked was that the game will let you make jumps that will kill you. I mean, seriously, you already know if the jump will kill me before I jump. can you just put a virtual guard rail to prevent me from jumping. Thanks…I am unsure if Valve (and/or the world) is ready for a Half Life 3 just yet. But Alyx has given me hope that Valve can tell more stories in the Half Life universe without needing to evoke the number 3. Consequently, I remain optimistic as to the future of the Half-Life universe and how Valve will explore it.

_childDocuments_.review: It is hard or impossible to give this game a review without giving the state of VR as a whole a review. So let me begin by saying that I am reviewing both at the same time. The most impressive thing about this game as a developer is that they achieve a VR compatible frame rate despite the level of detail. The level of detail isn't perfect but I've messed around with UE4 and VR enough to know that this is really much harder to do than just create the same type of gfx on a flat screen.The second thing that immediately appeared to me is that despite the good realization I didn't like the setting at all. I get that the game has a history and all, but I live in an eastern european ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, and playing inside another eastern european ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ with even more debris felt kind of sad. Fortunately after Alyx enters the starship I see some much more enjoyable scenery. The old apartments with wonky gravity are very atmospheric. I wish the whole game had been like that! The sci-fi ending was also much better than the initial city 17 environments which constitute more than half of the game.Now because this is a solid game it shows everything about what's great with modern day VR and what is not so great. 3D perception is spot-on for objects about 1-2 meters away. Objects more far away suffer greatly from the low resolution of the headset display (regardless of which one you're using). The big starship in the sky appears to be pasted on. There i no depth perception for far away objects. You can slightly improve this by increasing lens distance mechanically on the headset, but not by very much. It is still possible that the issue is not with depth perception at all but just resolution. One thing that I would have done different is lighting. A lot of scenes are brightly lit. Even dark scenes try to have a dramatic dynamic range, so parts of the screen are black and some are very bright. An even, darkish illumination works wonders to reduce the pixelated effect. The most realistic environments were at the end in the dimly lit apartment building. There are some glitches which are the scariest part of the game (grenade doesn't grab from your pocket because you didn't open the hand fully beforehand, cartridge falls to the floor instead of going into the gun) but the controllers work so well that it would be unfair to ♥♥♥♥♥ about this, it rarely happens. It makes you very mad when it does though.This is the best we can do in VR today. A more narrative game set in a prettier world would have been much better but that's my own personal taste. As things get more real, the huge issue of locomotion is impossible to ignore. Had I been able to actually walk through these environments, it would have been completely different. But using a joystick or teleporting completely break the immersion.VR has a long way to go. There are no significant breakthroughs on the horizon in either high resolution haptics (especially full body) or programmable walkable terrains. And you wouldn't have space in the house anyway.Let's look forward to brain implants even though the risks to freedom are enormous. Congrats to Valve for putting this together, and for taking this huge business risk.I really wish we could move away from "shoot everything" kind of games and use the medium to create more artistic experiences. I wish we could use the medium to make worlds that are more beautiful than our own, not worse (that goes for movies as well). Now what I want to know. Does the Source 2 engine use forward or deferred rendering? Is it possible to get this frame rate on UE4 or did they do some optimizations that would not be possible on another engine?A final note, the human characters (Russel, Alyx's dad, Mr X at the end) are much less realistic than the environments.
