_childDocuments_.review: Review done after beating game once on the highest difficulty.Half-Life Alyx sets a new bar of quality for all VR games. With it's great controls and well-designed levels and scenarios it delivers an experience unlike any other. On top of that it's another game in the beloved series.I feel confident in recommending this to everyone who has VR.More about pros and cons below.The biggest pet peeve of mine in almost every VR shooter/action game is the lack of collisions for player's hands and weapons. In Alyx if any box or barrel stands in your way you don't have to grab it with a button press, you can just use your hands to shove it right out of your way. It sounds like "duh, of course you should be able to do that", but most VR games don't even have weapons collisions, not to mention hands. I'm looking at you Skyrim and Fallout 4 VR, you overpiced pieces of f...The only thing I'm sad isn't included is some kind of a melee weapon. Would be cool to whack a headcrab and beat zombies to a pulp with a stick or something.You end up having 3 primary, upgradable weapons. While it may seem like it isn't much, the quality of what's here overshadows the lack of quantity. The pistol is your go to weapon for conserving ammo with careful headshots, the shotgun is for those "oh, sh..." situations where you need to kill something real quick and the combine pulse rifle is pretty much your general workhorse in prolonged engagements. On top of that you can throw grenades and use healing syringes dropped by enemies. Throwing works very well, better than any other VR game I ever played. Like in Fallout 4 or GORN I can kinda throw things in general direction of the enemy, but in HL Alyx it works very well. Dunno if the game compensates with some kind of a gentle auto-adjustment to throwing arc, but it feel so good to throw a good grenade that takes out multiple enemies. The only thing I'd change is the inability to store more grenades than the 2 item slots shared with every other item you find (excluding ammo - that gets stored in your backpack and has no limit, although you cannot store partially empty magazines, only full ones)Reloading your weapons is manual. You press a button on the controller to eject a magazine from pistol or open up the shotgun. The pulse gun ejects automatically. Then you reach to your backpack over your shoulder and press trigger to grab a magazine/shells. Then you manually put in the ammunition into your gun and if the gun was fully empty - you also have to chamber the first round with a manual motion using the trigger and moving your hand towards the grip. It feels like loading a real gun, similar to how it is in Gun-Club VR. Every shooter from now on should have similar mechanics.You point your hand at an item press the trigger and flick in some direction and the item will fly towards you in an arc corresponding to the direction you flicked. It's really simple, responsive and very fun to work with.Every nook and cranny can be explored. All drawers can be opened, and there's usually items hidden in some of them. The biggest find is the material used for upgrades at special stations. Each weapon upgrade is useful, from holographic and laser-sights to attached grenade launcher on the shotgun.This game drops some serious reveals at the end of the game. I'm happy that we got some more story, but at the same time disappointed that only people with VR get to experience it.Bodies get stuck in the terrain and are often unable to even be turned around to look for supplies attached to their uniforms, let alone moving them.On few rare occations items or my character would fall through the ground. Sometimes a grenade blast would kill me from behind a wall. Range on some enemies melee attack is much longer than what it seems to be from their animation.Can't talk much about it, but there's a thing you get at some point near the end of the game that just doesn't feel right to use. While it's flashy and has cool effects, the mechanics just weren't there.At some points during my playthrough when I entered another kitchen filled with shelves and drawers I thought to myself "oh, this is going to be a chore to go through". And indeed sometimes the exploration is taking a bit too much time, especially when a lot of things are hidden inside container, but then a lot of them are empty as well.After playing Alyx I can't go back to other VR shooter without noticing how basic and barely VR-worthy they are. Arizona Sunshine, A-Tech, Sairento - they are all basic compared to HL Alyx, with very few things that couldn't have been achieved without VR. Alyx is designed to work with VR and with VR only and it's incredible what can be achieved when a competent, AAA-level studion builds a game that's meant for VR from the ground up.It's easly the best non-arcade VR game I ever played, easly taking a second spot on my favourite VR games right next to Beat Saber.I'd give Half-Life Alyx a very solidOne of the best VR games of all time and a worthy addition to Half-Life franchise. Unfortunately it's design makes it so that if it's ever ported to a pancake version it will lose almost everything that's good about it.Time will tell if we'll get a proper HL3, but after Alyx I can safely say that if we do - it's gonna be great.

_childDocuments_.review: Half-Life Alyx is Valve's full fledged vr game, coming out in March 2020, about 4 years after the HTC Vive and Oculus Rift and almost 12.5 years since Half-Life 2: Episode 2. Was it worth the wait? You play as Alyx Vance (go figure), as your father (Eli Vance) is taken away by The Combine for stealing a combine reactor.Your mission is to free him from the combine and take down their vault, which your father has been researching about.Alyx is a physics centric first person shooter, just like its predecessor. Unlike HL2, you only have access to 3 weapons (Pistol, Shotgun, Rifle) and a tool, and you use them throughout the game to gain access to new areas, get items, and defeat all enemies which stand in your way. Each gun has its uses and ammo, and you physically reload ammo when it comes out, which gives some tension when reloading during a firefight.a Unique mechanic to Alyx are the gravity gloves (The Russels™) which allow you to grab far away items with ease, this makes grabbing items off the ground, high up, and out of reach much easier and doesn't disrupt the flow of the game. honestly they're so good it makes alyx so fun to play just grabbing stuff.Overall encounters were managable, probably because I was playing on Normal. Not to say fights weren't fun, they were. Trying to move around enemies, using the weapons I have. It was exhilarating taking them out with the shotgun and grenades.There's a new collectible called Resin found throughout the game, they're used to upgrade your weapons 4 different upgrades. They serve as a reward for exploring any nook and cranny, alongside ammo and health itemsEven when playing on the lowest settings, the game looks incredible and makes you feel really immersed in the world. Sound was also incredible with a lot of sound effects, ambiance, and music which conveys the tone of scenes really well.If you're interesting in VR or already own a headset, then get Alyx. It's an incredible title which shows the amazing power of VR and hopefully is a nice intro to future VR games which build on it.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm very new to VR, and I've possibly spoiled myself by this being one of my first VR games played to completion. Alyx sets a new standard for gaming, as it introduces us to what VR can actually bring to the table for a fully fledged game. The level of interactivity and immersion is insane compared to anything released before. To accomodate for the differences between VR and a normal FPS, the gameplay, -speed, and -mechanics are very different compared to the rest of the series. The gun play is exciting and memorable, but the game has a strong focus on (well executed) horror and puzzle elements as well. For this reason, it's hard to compare it to non-VR FPS games. This gives the game an increased variation and balance to gameplay that I feel is very welcome to the tired genres, and makes it a better game overall than anything before in this series (however excellent these were).The game's only drawback, is that its interactivity does not extend to using physical objects as a weapon (although you can certainly throw objects at your enemies, with some effect), as apparently Boneworks does (haven't played it). I feel that would have made the game a near-perfect experience. Nonetheless, what's there is a very complete package that already comes close to the potential I imagined.As far as I'm concerned, this is THE killer app for VR, and I'm glad they've developed it specifically for VR, as they would otherwise be limited to showcase its potential. I expect Alyx will inspire an entire generation of new games, and I look forward to it.Played with a Valve Index (full kit) in a room setup of 2.5x3m on a GTX 1070 Ti with not a single issue, very stable all throughout. I think that playing the game with the Index controllers will quickly make other VR controllers feel inferior (in this game specifically), but I'm told it still plays well on any setup.

_childDocuments_.review: I was anticipating Alyx, but I had worries too. What if I overhyped it? What if it's not as good with the Vive wands since they built it for index? My CPU is below min-spec, will it even run on my machine?Well let me tell you, my worries were unfounded. It is amazing. I literally squealed with delight at both the jaw-dropping scenery and the tiny little details. The massive citadel that opens the game is impressive as all hell, but so is the way your hand smudges the dry erase markers on the windows. The sprawling cityscape is alive with sounds and people and combine tech, but also the paint can makes a sloshing noise when you shake it.As for the controls, top notch. The only issue I had was the need to click to move in the joysitck-style movement (Vive trackpads suck for that, as anyone who owns them will attest), but it was easy enough to re-bind it to moving on touch so my one complaint soon vanished. Otherwise everything strikes a perfect balance between videogamey convenience and immersive realism. The guns aren't as functionally detailed as something like , but they're detailed enough be interesting to interact with. Your grabbity-gloves are a delight. It's a long-distance grabbing tool that makes for convenient VR play, but the "flick and catch" that you have to do gives it a great sense of physicality.Also IT. IS. GORGEOUS. It's so, so pretty. I figured my 1070 would handle it fine, but I was worried my creaking AMD FX8320 would have a hard time with the physics stuff. But it runs great, and I didn't even have to lower the settings. Everything defaulted to HIGH, and it works. And whoever did the lighting, my hat off to you. The lighting is so perfect everywhere always. It nails the mood and, again, is SO PRETTY.TL;DRA new standard for VR and videogames in general in every way. Simply amazing. Also you can put a bucket on your head, if you want.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game! Half-Life Alyx paves the way for all future VR games. This game has everything. Puzzles, Shooting, a spooky factor, amazing story, garden gnomes...You just cannot go wrong. I played it through twice, the second time to get achievements I had missed. I had just as much fun the second time as the first! It is a must play for VR! I played on Oculus Rift S.

_childDocuments_.review: An inflection point in VR gaming. A sensory feast.  Can you spend 20 minutes just messing around with stuff and staring at the city in the opening scene? yes you can! Want to play a piano?  That works too!  Great ebb and flow pacing.  Wonderful puzzle aspects.  Only nitpicks are that occasionally some of the scaling of objects in the world were way off and occasionally getting glitched inside an object.  Can't wait to play a KOTOR/Mass Effect/Red Dead/Fallout type of game at this level of execution!  Feet tracking needs to be next, as I counted about 100 times when I wanted to kick a door open or use my foot to close a sliding drawer.

_childDocuments_.review: I got the HTC Vive on Thursday to help pass the time during quarantine and immediately hopped into Obduction, Talos Principle VR, etc...while all great and immersive in their own right, none of them lent themselves to switching to VR rather than just keep playing them flat-screen (besides Beat Saber, which is totally different class of game for VR only).Then I fired up Half-Life: Alyx - real quick background, I'm not a heavy modern gamer by any means.  I shunned any new PC or console after 2004.  Lo and behold, I played HL:2 for the first time ever last year on a whim after playing Portal/2 (also for the first time as well) and loving every second of that series.  I still do not really like FPS (I am a heavy puzzle gamer) and I first got back into free-roam in 2018,  but the combination of roaming, small puzzles, and relatively light battle compared to some other games in HL:2 was so well-balanced that I finished it - the first FPS since Halo 2 for me. The controls take about 5 mins to get used to (I use teleport mode, I prefer it since it eliminates motion sickness and I'm used to it due to games like Myst & Riven)  Within those 5 minutes though, I realized this was something radically different than I've ever experienced from playing a video game.  This game induces true physiological responses to facial expressions, heights, and fear.  Besides the teleportation - everything else is as real as it possibly can get to your brain with VR: physically aiming flashlights and guns, manually reloading ammo, picking things up (the gravity hands.........enough said), throwing things around, lifting, pushing, pulling, ducking, and the sounds...any time you throw this game on, you actually lose track of reality.   Possibly for the first time in your life, you are truly *INSIDE* a video game.Wherever this game falls in the scope of the "uncanny valley" chart or whatever development process this went through  is where we need to be right now.    This is not pushing the envelope per se, but if there ever was a live master class for VR gaming done 100% correctly and naturally for 2020, "this" is it.  I am hooked.  I am impressed.  I am entertained more than I ever thought I could be.  Half-Life: Alyx makes the VR investment worth it and we need more of "this" really, really, really soon.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Oh. My. God! Finally. Finally finally finally, the first true AAA VR title. If the devs are seeing this review, I want to thank you for taking the risk of pumping out such a mind blowing experience.  This game will frighten, embarrass, intimidate, and hopefully — inspire every other VR dev out there. This is my feedback:***THE GOOD***Game mechanics: It takes the physically immersive mechanics from Boneworks, but without all the confusion. Story:It’s a story that you’d get with any full blown game. It’s not like every other VR — puzzle based, repetitive, wave shooter, or ‘pretend to fly cuz you can’t in real life’ BS. No. The game itself is largely driven by immersive stories, but is so well balanced. It doesn’t force hours of dialogue (like MGS) and never forces you to sit and listen without progressing.UX/UI:It takes the totally immersive, diegetic UX from DeadSpace, mixes it with the beauty of LoneEcho’s and Stormland’s beautiful UI, but delivers a completely unique UX experience that I’ve never seen before. The UI is so good that you never even notice it’s there. Quality — holy sh**:Finally, the 3D design and high-res UV/texture outputs are absolutely phenomenal. You really notice this stuff in VR because you’re so close. And my god, you really notice the immense amount of perfection in every inch (literally every inch) of this game. There isn’t a single molecule that has been forgotten or lazily designed. This comes with a bit of perf struggle but nothing that ever affects in-game framerate***THE BAD***(Scratching head). Okay three fairly big things:1) claustrophobic environments: the dark cave/basement feeling environments are a bit overwhelming in VR. I was hoping for more of the city itself. The map seems massive, yet it’s completely Linear to the linear story itself. Seemed like a waste of a huge map. 2) price: while the quality of the game is AAA, the length of it did not meet the expectations of a fully priced $60 game. There is no replay value and the game is massively repetitive. From the very beginning, you fight enemies that repeatedly show up to the very end. The idea of progression at that point is minimal and discouraging.3) no replay value: once you’re done, you’re done. Again, not worthy of most $60 games that make this an absolute must. $40-50 seems like the most fair price for this.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; I recommend this game to anyone who has a VR Headset. Even if the price is a sticking point right now and you wait for a sale or for the price to eventually drop, I recommend buying it when you can afford to. I believe that everyone that has a VR Headset should try this game.My experience was with an Oculus Rift S/Touch Controllers, with Sennheiser CX 100 In-Ear Earphones and Room Scale Movement. Graphics Settings were set to the highest option available within the game (No external graphics enhancements applied). I was Playing with Smooth Turning Enabled and Smooth Walking (Coupled to head orientation) as my method of movement and turning with the Right hand as my Weapon Hand.As of version 1.2 which released on 29th March 2020, there was a patch to fix left-hand/right-hand movement control configurations which were a sticking point for some players. A good portion of the negative reviews I was seeing before buying was for the game was about this, I feel it would be good to mention it has been addressed. As I understand it, players can now adjust which hand is used for movement and which is to be used for turning however they wish. Visually it is amazing as VR Games go. The visuals are so smooth and crisp. The headset you are wearing feels like it has a higher resolution when playing this game. It amazes me how just the game that is being played on the headset can swing the visuals so heavily. I imagine it looks stunningly lifelike with the Valve Index.The Audio is excellent. Spacially you get a strong sense of where sounds are coming from, and the weapon audio all feels powerful and authentic. Music throughout the game really helps to set the tone for scenes, including the lack of it in certain instances. The Voice Acting so far has been very well done, with some comical dialogue to ease the tension a little bit as the game progresses.With regards to mechanics and gameplay, I really enjoy the Gravity Gloves. They effectively give you a sort of Telekinesis and can summon objects to your hands. It takes a bit to get used to the motion, but once it's down pat, it comes as second nature. It's enjoyable to just do this to the various pieces of debris that are around as you move through the game, and it is implemented well for progressing the game. Sometimes there is Ammo across the room or through a broken window, and you can't approach it. Or there are Barnacles (Enemies which tether anything passing by and pull them up to eat them) blocking the way, and you pull an object from passed them to distract them.The Hacking tool, or "Alyx Tool" as Alyx calls it, is a neat implementation on puzzles/hacking. I believe I haven't seen all of the possible puzzles that are possible with it yet. Still, it is an elegant and refreshing implementation of puzzles that involve 3D space and positional hand tracking, which some games don't do well.Some scenes offer a decent level of tension. The game introduces you to new challenges and enemies in a way that you can understand how they work before you are then expected to deal with them on the fly. So far, these initial encounters haven't felt forced or felt like tutorials which pull you out of the rest of the game, which I believe has been well executed.The gunplay is nice, but not amazing like in some other games. Given that this game isn't aiming to focus heavily on gunplay, I think the gunplay is decent for the game. The guns feel, look and sound powerful with upgrades that are available to them as the game progresses to make them more practical or more effective. It is also clear that care was taken with their design to make it seem realistic and possible to be using them in just one hand, which I really liked. I've only found the first two guns, and I don't know how many there will be by the end, so this may change as I find more.One criticism I have is that once weapons are equipped, that hand has a gun in it until it is unequipped, it can't be "dropped" or put away without using a button/toggle. I find this a bit annoying because as I am not actively "holding" the gun in my hand at all times when it is equipped, my hand feels free to use. I find that I try to use my right gravity glove instinctively but can't as my hand is occupied with a gun. Unequipping weapons is easy enough, but it takes a moment of thought to do it, which doesn't feel natural at the moment.In terms of the levels, I personally feel they are a bit short, but I am still earlier in the game, and this could change later through it. I imagine this is intentional to offer frequent enough step off points for those players where VR can quickly start getting uncomfortable. I feel like each level so far has taken about 10-15 minutes to complete, maybe 20 if I am spending more time than necessary messing with the environment or investigating. I haven't timed this, and my guess on times could be way off. All I can really say is that when I hit a new loading section, I find myself thinking "already?".I like to consider myself to have strong VR legs, and prefer experiences that have fewer comfort options. This game has a lot that can be changed or disabled which is good. Some are built-in and can't be changed.Falling is artificially slowed down to make it more comfortable for players and less nauseating. For me, this feels unnatural and almost has the opposite effect of making me feel nauseous.Even with smooth walking enabled, there is a teleporting/jumping mechanic which allows you to teleport short distances, which is useful for getting over walls or obstacles in the game. Personally, I would prefer a genuine jumping mechanic, but I can live happily with the teleport implementation.All in all, from my experience, I feel like this game is an example of what a single-player narrative-based game for VR should aim to achieve. What it does, it does well enough in all areas to be a one size fits all experience that almost anybody can pick up and play. The parts that make this uniquely a VR game stand out strongly enough to appreciate that it is a game made for VR. This isn't a game that was designed initially and the ported with some quick VR implementation. I would recommend that everyone who owns a VR Headset or has access to one should at least try this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me get this out of the way: I HATE puzzles! That being said, I did refer to YouTube walk-through videos more than once to get past particularly frustrating parts of this game. Note to developers: MAKE PUZZLES OPTIONAL! Some of us think for a living and don't need or want to in our leisure!Beyond that, this is the very best VR title I've encountered, and I've played a lot. Worth the price of admission, even if you have to buy a mid-range headset to start. I wouldn't go so far as to buy an Index, but a Rift-S or other equivalent-in-price headset would be an easy buy just to play this (and hopefully future other titles of this quality).

_childDocuments_.review: It was nice to be able to play a new Half-Life game from Valve, and being in VR is very easily more nightmare fuel than any of the other HL games, with one chapter playing out like straight up survival horror with FPS elements as an afterthought. Nothing like manhacks slicing you up, headcrabs jumping on you, or barnacles eating you in VR. I also liked the electrical wiring puzzles and the hacking mini-games, tho the "drag the blue lock over to the other blue lock" hacking mini-game started to seem a little repetitive after a while. Even on low fidelity it still manages to be plenty immersive. The new "VALVE" intro somehow looks so much grander in VR. The "collecting resin to upgrade your weapons" mechanic kinda reminded me of Singularity, and introducing new varieties (not seen in any other HL game) of familiar creatures was also a nice touch and kept the gameplay fresh. Just like with other HL titles the level design eases you into more and more difficult set-ups, which is what TvTropes refers to as an antepiece.Some minor issues were that the loads and loads of loading got particularly annoying in areas where it's easy to die a lot, and I also kinda missed having some kind of weaker weapon to fall back on since AFAIK you're pretty much a sitting duck if you run out of ammo.Kinda like how the original HL was my gateway into FPS games, this is like a gateway into VR titles.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: My purchase finally went through.(And no, I did not refund, it is just a bug, I own this game.)From scary experiences like seeing a zombie or a headcrab, to engaging in hard action combat with the combines, this game is a must-play for any Virtual Reality Headset owner out there. The story progresses very well, and characters are introduced very well. The combat is extremely fun and can be challenging depending on your difficulty setting. You also have the ability to change your movement settings to better match your comfort. 10/10 Virtual Reality Game. A very thrilling experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Half-Life has been my favorite game since 1999... ANY chance to play / continue the story is always worth it (especially after so many years with no movement)!  The only issue?  I'm not into VR, but thankfully this game dropped on sale and I noticed the NoVR mod update awhile back allowed me to finally play the entire game, so I gave it a shot (why not for 60% off right?).  I can 100% feel for how awesome this is in VR and appreciate all of the work Valve put into this game for VR, but thankfully the mod allowed me to continue the Half-Life journey on my terms. :)  Luckily, the game played extremely smooth and looked great at 4K with max settings.  I enjoyed the story of Half-Life: Alyx... and maybe, just MAYBE, someday, I will finally get to play Half-Life 3 and see this awesome story come to a close.  Or maybe not, either way, awesome game!
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Oh my gosh. Where do I even start! This was the best game I've ever played! I've never been this amazed by a video game before. Let's start with the graphics. Everything looks so real! The graphics are amazing! Combined with the fact that everything you see can be interacted with in some form makes you feel like you really are in the game. At one point I almost set my controllers down on an in-game table thinking it was a real table. And the ending... I won't spoil anything, but it is a MUST SEE! This game made up for most of the awful stuff that has happened in 2020. This was so much fun. 10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Do you want to ruin VR gaming for the  rest of your existence? If so, start with this game! Absolutely amazing in both graphics and game play. I wish that the main game had a bit more combat sections, but that is easily covered by all the mods you can quickly download from the Workshop. If you need a reason to get into VR gaming, this is it right here.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: So far the best VR experience around. A pioneer of using all the advantages that VR offers, as opposed to just porting traditional games. Great use of index controllers. The gravity glove gesture is so intuitive and immersive. The game feels so thoughtfully executed and polished, especially compared to many current VR games which are just ports or tech demos.I still haven't decided if playing on hard is a mistake or not. The ammo scarcity is a good addition while you are worrying about each shot, but becomes incredibly frustrating when you do run out of ammo. Your only chance at that point is to outrun the enemies, which (mainly with VR teleportation) is very unsatisfying and even feels like cheating.Zombies (and headcrabs) in VR are terrifying, and especially when they are coming to you and your magazine runs out. 2 hours in (chapter 3) I still often make a mistake when reloading, which just enhances that experience. I don't like horror movies or games, in HL:A I'd say it's bearable, but only because the games is a masterpiece. On the other hand scary moments like that are a powerful and immersive experience, so I don't know if I'd say it's a positive or a negative.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely nuts. Got stuck a couple times trying to figure out what to do but everything else is awesome.  Obviously not done playing but i will probably replay just to not miss anything.  Try to save ammo by not shooting everything that breaks apart if possible, if not.. well there is more ammo scattered about.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: For years I have been playing little "indie" VR games that I thought were game-changing and were the next big thing.And then I loaded up Half-Life Alyx. This game does what you're typical Valve game does, it raises the bar on video games for the next 10 years. Trying to explain this game to my friends isn't possible, this is something you have to experience for yourself.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: This would not be the same if it wasn't in VR, I absolutely loved this and deserves the overwhelmingly positive review rating. If you have or want to get a VR, this game is an absolute must buy. Bought it full price and it is one of the few triple A games I would say is actually worth that value.Edit: I will say, if you play this with a ceiling fan above you, barnacles will take on an all new fear when you get caught by them.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: For the first Half-Life game i've played through to completion, this game is by far one of the best games I have ever played.Story - 9/10 - The story in this game is captivating, full of laughs, but isn't afraid to make you feel for the characters at times. It's funny, sad, and full of those awesome explosions.Combat - 10/10 - The combat in Alyx is probably some of the best i've seen in the gaming industry, and where i'd say the game truly shines. The gravity gloves (Russells) feel so smooth to grab things from afar, and mixing it with some familiar weapons from past games, you've got yourself a deal.Gameplay - 8/10 - The gameplay in Alyx is great, mixing familiar elements with brand new ones. For instance, the Gravity Gloves. You can grab ammo from a far away shelf, steal a stimpack from a zombie, or snag a grenade midair and throw it back! Replayability - 7/10 - Although the game is a wild ride and an absolute MUST for Valve fans, once you beat the game after a long playthrough, it's kind of hard to go back and do it again. It will take a bit, but i'm sure soon enough i'll be hungry for more.Half-Life Alyx is a must play for not only valve fans, but for horror and shooter players as well. It mixes horror with fun so well, making it one of the best games as of now on Steam. Alyx paves the way for more Half-Life content, and hopefully we see some light on it soon.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished the game and I am speechless. Valve have done it again. This game is absolutely stunning, from the already impressive first chapters to the mind bending finale. With this game, Valve have shown what VR games can be capable of. Not just that, they completely knocked it out of the park. The visuals are superb, the environments and objects are so incredibly detailed, animations are incredibly well done and because everything is based on physics, the world becomes so much more believable and immersive. And ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, it's HALF LIFE! After such a long wait, we finally get to return to this world and this time we're *IN* it! It's been 30 minutes since I witnessed the end and I'm still pumped with adrenaline and endorphin. I can't believe what I've just played, the things I've seen. And I'm so damn happy to finally have played another Half Life game in the absolute best way imaginable. Please Valve, we need more of this! Don't let us wait another 13 years!
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely stunning game, valve for sure have produced one of the greatest games of 2020 and seeing the future works with Source 2 like Gmod 2 and SFM 2 it will only get better and better as time goes on, i give this game a solid 100 from the playthrough i have done, with a gen 1 vive and index controllers this game has just been outstanding!
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Shattered my expectations. This game is full of awe-inspiring and terrifying moments alike. Smooth performance, great graphics, it really puts you into the dystopian world ruled by the combine. 10/10 Reccomend!Another plus, Epileptics and other photosensitive folk, they have a setting to reduce strobes for us! I've been alright so far!
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Outstanding.  Simply outstanding.  I thought VR was going to be gimmicky, but I'm so impressed.  Easily one of the best video game experiences I've had.  One caveat that make a difference is having a room with some space to play.  It really does improve the experience to be able to have a few feet of walking around to utilize, especially because some of the moments can get intense, but oh man, what fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: This game and Boneworks are the definitive VR experiences and something any VR owner needs to have and play. As is typical with Half Life games at this point, this game has great combat, a great story, amazing voice acting (seriously, this is really good), and is one of the best looking VR games ever made. I can only hope that if we ever get a Half Life 3 that Valve make it as good as they have made this experience
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Wow WEE!Not only has this title set the bar for all upcoming VR titles, as a Half-Life fan from way back, the ending made my jaw drop.The last 5 minutes of gameplay is the best 5 minutes of gameplay almost anywhere in gaming history. This is why video games were invented.If you have VR, please just get Alyx.You've got work to do.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: I just recently completed the game, and I gotta say. I was overwhelmed with the amount of detail this game has.I had just recieved my Valve Index along with this game, and I was in awe from the very start when I played the first chapter.The game has an insane amount of detail and great graphics, especially the posters and circuit boards that had fingerprints where you touched them, and the perfect metallic appearance that made it look real.The only real limitation of the graphics were the vr goggles themselves. It was like playing a game where you're slightly nearsighted, I couldn't find a solution to this, but it wasn't too bothersome either.The game's story was pretty ok, not absolutely amazing but not lackluster either. As for combat, it was above average, although just slightly. I really liked the idea that I had to physically go in cover by crouching behind a wallblock or a window in order to not take damage, and then peek out with a pistol to snipe the combine's heads, it was pretty fun. The combine's AI, however, could use some tweeking, since it was sometimes full on aimbot from like 30 meters away that were on point, even with a shotgun. I played on medium difficulty, but the combine sometimes could just sniper me for 80% of my hp in just a few shots, which made me hide behind cover most of the time.The level design was also pretty good, although was a bit too much for me to find the solution to a puzzle, since I'm not the smartest person on the block. But I reckon that most players (80%) could probably get through all levels without getting stuck for more than 20 minutes. The sound and SFX was on point, nothing much to say there.Overall I would give the game 8.9 / 10. Since it wasn't the game of the year for me really, but it was definitely close.A good thing to note however, was how annoying it was to wear the Valve Index at times. After 40 minutes of playing, I would get a headache and blurry vision that somehow would become unbearable. This is because the Index weigh a bit more than most VR goggles, forcing me to take a lot of breaks in order to finish the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Important info from first playing on Windows 10 I7 16 GB Ram gtx 1060 on Oculus Rift. I attempted to run this game even with drastically reduced SteamVR settings, the stuttering choppy video is unbearable even at lowest graphics and texture. It was almost tolerable using snap turn and shift movement. Several rounds with steam support and the forums, no luck.After upgrading to RTX video card and switching VR to desktop, it is actually pretty amazing, as in a ground-breaking game, just beware if you are at or close to minimum specs.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: I had heard a lot of praise for this game, but it doesn't do it justice. This game is hands down the best VR game yet. I was surprised at how much fun I had looking around for ammo and resin. There are some intense moments that made me pee my pants a little, so be warned of that. I wouldn't call it a horror game, but at the same time i would? I'm not really into scary stuff, but I would recommend this to anybody.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of praise needs to be given to Valve, it was a bold step to make their much anticipated return to the Half Life world VR only, this massively narrows their marketplace, but also progresses the field massively, I for example have always been intrigued by modern VR despite being easily affected by motion sickness, but nothing really seemed to push me over the edge. I was still skeptical of Alyx despite great looking previews, but the reviews made it clear this was one of those defining moments in gaming that comes maybe a few of times in a decade if we're lucky. The cost of entry is high, though fortunately it appears Valve has made a game that will still look great on lower end hardware, as you can make a cheap gaming PC but VR headsets especially their own Index are still very expensive items. The game looks great even on lowest settings because the art design and animation is beyond exceptional. This was my first real VR experience, and I have to say I was blown completely away. If I had any negative comments it's that the game doesn't overload you with enemies and combat and for good reason, this is still a mainstream game, and many people such as myself have a learning curve to adjust to the new way of interacting and playing. But as I started to get towards the final chapters, and seriously enjoying the combat and the physics, I just wanted more, but unfortunately much like great Titanfall 2 which also spends the majority of the game teaching you the mechanics, the game ends just as you feel things are getting into 5th gear. But just like Titanfall 2, it's a highly satisfying experience. Beg Borrow Steal a compatible headset and or PC and just allow yourself to experience one of the most important moments in modern gaming.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: I thought it was a little weird that this game was labeled as masterpiece before it was even released.Now that I've finished it, I agree 100%. This game is incredible, and it feels like Half-Life mixed with the horror and atmosphere of Resident Evil 7. It has a much slower pace, which encourages you to take your time and look around the environments - which is incredibly easy, considering that this is quite possibly the best looking game ever made.TL;DR - One of the best gaming experiences I've ever had - thank you Valve! That last chapter is the stuff of legends. Also, I <3 Jeff.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: probably the best VR game. if you are looking for a great story and amazing Gameplay then this is for you.The ending was a bit disappointing but the rest of the game sure makes up for that.The genre is a bit of everything you will feel scared have a bit of a laugh and even feel sad at certain points of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Half-Life: Alyx is the gold standard from which all VR titles now must draw inspiration from.  The graphics are amazing.  The locomotion options are phenomenal.  I'm so happy with this title that I really can't think of a negative thing to write about it at this moment.  I sincerely love it!!! 10/10 would play every single day.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Really amazing game, even though it's not a fitting sequel it still connects the dots a bit more and they even changed the ending of the 2nd episode which is very interesting. Really good graphics and breathtaking sights.  They introduced new enemies which I like, love the new mechanics with it. I do like that they made it a slight horror game also. I really do love the final part of the game, best part of the game in my opinion, everything about it is perfect. Like it that they made the combine a bit harder to fight also instead of just running towards them and then just shooting them once with a shotgun and they die. This is honestly the best game I have ever played, really hoping that half life 3 will come out even though it will most likely not.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Best VR Game so far. Once again, Valve is making a big step forward in the gaming industry. A good mix between a scary game packed with action, amazing gun control, physics and fun little 3d puzzles. Sadly I have two downsides: Firstly, in my opinion the objects are interactive, but are still missing something more unique, like crumbling a cardboard box (like the soda cans) or tearing it apart to unveil even more items inside.Second con is the teleportation movement: I am on the lucky group of player that hasn't felt dizziness playing most games in VR. So having a full body movement, walking around/jumping/crouching and even prone makes the whole gameplay more realistic and enjoyable for me. And sometimes, the annoying teleportation loading arrow had to take over the movements to continue to the next room instead of jumping or crouch walking.Otherwise, such a perfect game and can't wait for mods or other games like this one to come out afterwards.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: I had been sitting on a roof admiring the sunset for about an hour. This game is so beautiful and well made, I don't have enough words. And only VR can do this, no VR mods just won't be able to capture the whole beauty of it. Everything, including the plot, humor, gameplay, visual style, level design, audio is great, and it's all in VR! It also fits very well into the franchise.Thank you Valve.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: If this game didn't have VR support it would still be one of the best games of all time. The pacing and level design are superb. The physics and gunplay are magnificent.The fact that you can play it in VR just elevates it above all others. You will remember it as something you lived instead of something you played.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely jaw dropping.  As others have said it captures you and keeps you in.These are the kind of games and experiences that will bring VR to another level.  Had to make myself stop playing so I can be an adult.  Playing on the Rift S, sometimes the hands are a bit touchy but the game is so good who cares.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: A revolutionary gaming experience that takes advantage of the VR medium to its fullest. You haven't played a more polished and refined experience on VR than this title and I hope that this marks a new wave of top tier studios also betting on the platform, because this is leagues beyond what we're playing on other traditional FPS games. Just sheer brilliance throughout the whole game. If you have a VR headset, you NEED to play this.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Half-Life: Alyx is an important landmark in not only the future of VR as commonplace in many peoples PC setups, but also for Valve as a company. After the long wait since Half-Life 2: Episode 2 you'd think that they had lost their magic for making games but assuredly it is still present in Alyx. It feels like you're playing another classic chapter in 2 but in VR. It blends so well with what they had already done while feeling completely new.There's no doubt that this is the new benchmark for VR games and hopefully a wake-up call for other AAA developers to begin investing in VR-only projects to help the medium flourish.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Now that I have beat the game, I can make a full review. First off, this is one of the first VR experiences that actually felt like a full-length game rather than a tech demo for me. The story is your typical great valve storytelling and you're never pulled out from the perspective of Alyx Vance.The atmosphere is done perfectly and really immerses you into the world and the combat can be pretty fun as well as the puzzles.There is plenty of replayability here as well as the workshop increasingly gets filled with more and more quality mods such as C17: Breakout.This is a spectacular game and I couldn't recommended enough.That being said, and with most of my VR reviews, take this review with a grain of salt as I streamed this game via virtual desktop on the quest as I do not have other standard headsets and link doesn't work for me. Therefore I did not have the "traditional" experience, and many problems I had with the game I attribute to that fact.I was also underneath minimum specs, but this game for the most part still ran smoothly on a 1060 3GB. The optimization is really well done, and if you have an even decent graphics card from the past 4 years then I guarantee you can run this game even smoother than some indie VR games even.Still, take this review with a grain of salt as I did not experience it in the "traditional" way. There are many other reviews that explain why you should buy this game better than I could.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: If you have VR and if you love Half-Life, then this game is for you. It is incredibly immersive, and it feels great to be back in City 17! The only downside for me is the lack of melee combat. It would have been nice to be able to pistol whip, beat headcrabs to death against a wall, or swing a chair at the enemies. But this doesn't take too much away, and the game is still incredible!
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: I'll be honest. This IS the best VR game of all time and the best Half-Life game as well. Graphics and audio are gorgeous, gameplay outstanding, storytelling the best that Half-Life ever had and the game even runs well below the min specs.I know there is a lot of hate for the game being VR only. Believe me, the game wouldn't be the same without VR. There is no chance this game would ever come out as a non-VR version, because the experience would degrade significantly.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the best VR game and among the best games over all that I have played. I get very seasick in some VR games and was worried about this one but I could play as long as I wanted per session without any discomfort due to the way they let you choose the movement type.The way they pushed my Rift S to its limits has me thinking why other titles do not do everything the same way.The level of detail blew my mind. This game has pretty much ruined other VR games in terms of detail and comfort.I am very excited to see what other games bring to the table in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: I'm still just amazed there's another Half Life game out, really didn't think that was going to happen.It's great fun ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ around with props and poking through all the nooks and crannies, seeing all these creatures and characters in VR is just breathtaking, the game looks and sounds beautiful, controls work very well, guns are fun to handle. The story's pretty good too, all around a wonderful game.Worth the wait.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: omfg. Half-Life is back and it's amazing. It's not Half-Life 3, but it lives up to the hype of basically being Half-Life 3. This is THE vr game to have. Valve has solved all the complicated problems of vr by using simplicity to their advantage. To switch guns all you  do is hold a button and wave your hand in the direction your preferred gun is indicated, and you won't drop it. To reload you press a button to empty your mag, reach behind your back for a new one and load it in. Everything is a bit dumbed down compared to other vr games, but somehow it adds to the immersion. And immersion this game has. Creativity and irl movement is surprisingly effective during combat. At one point, I was overstressed by a combine battle so I got by a car and not just crouching, I actually instinctively fully sat down, methodically reloading all my guns, with the occasional grenade throw to fend them off. I know that sounds like a small interaction, but those type of things happen all the time and absolutely immerse you in the world. And now for some small things. I wish headcrabs would stick to your visor, similar to crablets in boneworks. I wish the earlier parts of the game tried more ambitious stuff like the last act. I REALLY WISH YOU COULD MELEE. Imagine how scary things could get if they robbed you of all your weapons, gave you a melee like a 2x4 or a knife or something, then just threw headcrabs your way. But hands down, this game solidifies itself as one of my favorite games ever for the last half of the game. Early on it's some pretty basic sewer gunning with a few scares. This is super fun and terrifying to play through, but then you get to the distillery, and the zoo, and the nest, then the vault. These last sections are phenominal, and show why Valve is still one of the best game designers out there. I want this to be spoiler free, but the very last part of the game, The Vault, is one of if not my favorite expierience in any videogame ever. Absolute 10/10 please Valve keep making games.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot stress this enough. If you have a VR headset. You MUST play this game. Amazing visuals. Fantastic game play. Solid Half-Life story. Bonus points for WMR support. Worked great in most parts but there are some annoying moments that required using a tool and a certain part towards the end of game with hand movements but I think that's more to my headsets limited tracking.Cannot wait for the next game. Just don't leave it so long Valve!
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: I'm still playing this game (18hrs on play time), it's probably the easiest review ever. If you have a PC/VR powerful enough to run this game then it's the title that proves VR is worth the money. Fantastic graphics, fantastic physics, fantastic story line, fantastic combat, fantastic mechanics, fantastic fantastic.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: This game is what we have been waiting for in VR. Its not a simulation game, or a 'Youre in a room throw stuff everywhere and have fun' game. This game is an actual Triple A title with an amazing story and great gameplay. To anyone who has a VR headset, this is a must have! The only down side i had with this game was the long loading times, and the occasional freezing (Which might be explained by my ♥♥♥♥ laptop i used) Get it, its very good
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: This is hands-down the best VR game so far.  I am just playing on an original CV1 Rift, and it's outstanding.  I bet it is insane on a newer headset.  It does beat the hell out of your video card, though.  I have a RTX2080 Super, and I am able to run it on ultra, but just barely.  One scene was dropping frames, but other than that, it's been barely able to hold it.    If you have the gear to run this, it's a must-play.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: As a long-time VR player who started with the original Vive, this is the most immersive VR game that I have played. The environment is detailed. The scripting is top notch and immersive, and at times whimsical and fun. Definitely a worthwhile VR game to play. I am also enjoying watching others play it on my account as they are drawn into the experience. I am playing it on the Valve Index with the Index Controllers. My one negative comment is that Family Share is currently not enabled so I can't share it with my children and have to let them login to my Steam account.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: I give a thumbs up because it's FINALLY a new Half-Life game but as far as the vr goes.... Boneworks feels WAY better, looks WAY better, and plays WAY better. In Half-Life: Alyx you can tell that the free-locomotion was something they added later on, you can't see your ****ing arms or body which is a real bummer. There are moments where this game lags out the ass, but I'm sure that will get patched.Cons:No armsNo bodyNo weapon holsters (just a horribly done weapon wheel)Extreme lag at timesFree-Locomotion kinda sucks(again about the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ arms) Floating hands are a real immersion breakerJankie grab systemPros:IT'S A NEW HALF-LIFE GAMEThe story is alright(To Valve: Please, for the love of quality, add arms, a body, and some kind of weapon holster. I also wouldn't mind a co-op mode of some sort, but that's beside the point.)
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: This game is quite literally a masterpiece, it is one of the if not best gaming experiences I've ever had and that from an amazing single player campaign no outside multiplayer interaction. I had to stop chapter to chapter to preserve the experience for long as possible, that's how good this game is. I wanted to make it last for long as possible and I did and do not regret it one bit. This game without a doubt is a masterpiece.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so insanely good. The world building and level design were superb. The story was witty and engaging and on the same level as the rest of hl2+episodes. The sound design was so good. Make sure you have good headphones. I am not a fan of teleport or slow paced locomotion, but I still overall enjoyed the way Valve designed things. Doing the kind of warp teleport instead of fading in and out didn't break my immersion. There were two bugs I experienced that were pretty bad. With one of them, my left hand disappeared. If this happens to you, go into the options and swap weapon hands and, then, swap them back. I experienced two things that were effectively crashes.The orb puzzles were the worst.Overall, one of the best games I've ever played and easily the best AAA story driven game in VR right now.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible game!! Makes me very angry that we probably won't get anything quite like it any time soon. Has the perfect straight shot journey through the world that makes the Half-Life games feel like such special journeys, Experiencing everything in VR is incredible! I was especially dazzled by how well they didwhich was probably the coolest thing I've experienced in VR thus far. Also keeping with the Half-Life tradition, you can do lots of fun stuff in the middle of dialogue sequences if you aren't too concerned with the immersion. I personally enjoyed throwing things at Russell and caressing Vortigaunt's faces.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Like with previous Half Life games, Valve once more did an absolutely outstanding job with this game. I can't think of other developers, that are as passionate about making games like Valve is. There are many things, that make this game good, a nice balance between puzzles and shooting sequences, with the classic top-tier story, make it super exciting from the very start. The different elements alone wouldn't make this a great game, but how everything is presented, how polished and well-made it is, makes it a mind-blowing experience, that couldn't work better in any other environment than in virtual reality. It's because of this, I'm sure many elements seen in Alyx will be groundbreaking for the gaming industry in the future.See you all in 2045, when Half Life 3 finally releases!
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: This game introduced me to my absolute favorite gaming franchise ever. Was I VERY late to the franchise? YES, but was I even born when HL2 came out? No. This is also the definitive VR game you need to play; everyone with a VR headset and a PC has to experience this. It has set a bar for VR that honestly will take years to be even touched by anyone else.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: 3 Hours in, the games pretty good. Definitely the best looking and most polished VR game, but thats what you'd expect from a game made by valve, especially when their competition is mainly small indie teams. As far as VR mechanics, the game doesn't really do anything that we haven't seen before, and in some cases feels like a step backwards, for example, not having the ability to quickly switch which hand your gun is in and the lack of smooth turn (not sure if this is a bug or not) or  not being able to crouch with a button and the fact that you are often forced to teleport (Which I expected since smooth locomotion was an after thought when it really shouldn't have been). Not being able to store more than 2 additional items is also quite annoying. Otherwise, the games good though.

_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: The Valve Index and Half-Life: Alyx were my first VR experience. I can't tell you how blown away I was at the level of immersion. The story so far is great, it is truly a next-gen Half-Life game. It's been so refreshing to get more Half-Life since Half-Life 2 came out. You can tell it's the same core team who worked on this game who delivered the other Half-Lifes. The locomotive mechanics are spot-on. There is so much to this game that makes use of VR, especially with the hands. There are some puzzles in this game and you use your hands a lot to solve them. You can open drawers, doors, windows, pull of chunks of wood, grab things, move things, etc... It is so immersive!Next I want to tell you about the graphics: I have subsequently purchased many other VR games after this one, and I can tell you, there is NO OTHER GAME that can even come close to competing with Half-Life: Alyx. The graphics are second to none. Literally everything in the environment has been carefully thought out. Nothing appears to be arbitrarily placed. You really feel like you are in City 17 fighting as a resistance member. There is so much detail in all of the models and props. The lighting creates a very realistic atmosphere for the player to experience.I definitely recommend this game and hope more and more players can experience this wonderful treasure for themselves!
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Probably one of the best, IF not THE best VR game to ever grace the fields of VR itself. The game itself looks beautiful, the gameplay is as you expected with a Valve game. Action set pieces mixed it with tons of puzzles. This game sets the bar so high for VR that any other VR game that I have play since has stale in comparison. The thing that got me about this game is the visuals but on top of that the amount of interaction that can be done with the environment. Being able to draw with a marker, being able to pick up glass bottles and toss them, gun play is terrific and so forth.There are tons of things that I can rave about this game but everything I'm going to say has already been covered numerous times. So, realistically... if you've just bought a VR set and are looking for a VR game to play, buy this game and never look back. This is quite honestly one of the BEST VR games out there on the market.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: The game we've been anticipating since 2007. Honestly, it lives up to all of my expectations. Shockingly good, a masterpiece in gameplay, visual design, level layout, graphics quality. You name it, this game ticks the box. Runs fantastic on my PC even though I'm below minimum spec (i7 4790k and RX480 with a mild overclock). Looks absolutely stunning on my Samsung Odyssey+. Honestly can't stop playing this game and I highly recommend you look into playing it if you are a half life fanAlso: This game is insanely immersive both in terms of visuals and audio. The gloves as your UI and simple inventory make everything super intuitive and natural. You can very easily get lost in this world. Not even considering the fact that IT'S A NEW HALF LIFE, it's also one of the most well-polished VR experiences I've seen and it worth a purchase on that merit alone. Such a perfect game, so happy VALVe is back
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: I'm pretty much lost for words, having just finished this game I can only say: go and buy it and if you don't have a VR Headset, buy one of those too or borrow one from a friend. My mind is literally blown. Not only was this a fantastic game in general, it was also the best VR experience I ever had and it being in the Half Life universe is just the lovely icing on the cake with a delicious cherry on top, absolute 10/10, one of the better games I ever played in general.If you're a fan of Half Life, this is a no-brainer, I know that the entry fee to play this game is pretty high, but it is worth every damn penny.Story was so well structured, when I heard that this was going to be a prequel I rolled my eyes at first, but it is sooo worth it, trust me. The levels were extremely well designed, it reminded me of Dark Souls in a way that everything seems connected, so many moments where you go: oh so that's where I just was. It is not for the faint of heart this game, not only because it is so awesome I was standing with my mouth open just gushing at it half the time, but also because of how immersive this game is. Gave me a proper scare and the creeps quite a few times.The fighting is done amazingly too. You never feel overpowered but if you learn weakpoints and how to deal with certain enemies you can get quite good at combat in general. It is always stressful to get into a firefight because sometimes it really feels like you're being shot at by alien soldiers that took over earth in just seven hours.Now stop reading this review and go play Half-Life: Alyx
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Alyx and Russell screamed 'ah!' two seconds before a jumpscare, giving me plenty of warning, but I still jumpedThe real reason I don't recommend this anymore is because of so many new modern VR games coming out that overshadow both the functionality of the VR mechanics and the gameplay/fun aspect of things in comparison.Also they talk a lot in this for a Half-Life game I feelMinus points for how buggy the gnome achievement is. Granted I can hold a weapon and the gnome each in one hand, the gnome often glitches out of existence on loads or reacts weirdly to physics.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Boneworks is more ambitious and impressive than this game, but Boneworks was also very glitchy and finnicky. This game was very polished and has very few issues that break immersion. Half-Life Alyx pushes the story forward despite being a prequel. Its sort of a retcon which sucks but it also implies more games in the series. Honestly the story carried this game more than anything else. The chapter "Jeff" is really well done and the ending of this game is absolutely insane. Its so good, in fact, that its worth playing this game just for the ending.

_childDocuments_.review: This is by far the best VR game and experience to date across the board.  This is what you call a masterpiece and sets the bar for gaming companies to reach for the next decade.  The passion they put into this game is thrown at you in full force.  It's from people who care what content you experience every moment you are playing.  I was Excited, happy, sad, scared, frustrated, and even laughed out loud while playing the game.  Some parts I got stuck at for like 20 minutes because my dumbass didn't see the clue right in front of me, but would I want to forget that experience?  Not at all!  It was worth the suffering of realizing how dumb you are after you figure it out lol.Alot of games like Talos Principle and Boneworks got me taking breaks from motion fatigue and nausea, but this game...Alyx does it so well that it seems second nature for me to play with no issues or feelings of nausea.   The game has a mix of puzzle solving, horror, action, adventure, and nostalgia that needed to be filled since HL2.   So if you are holding back because of the 59.99 price tag, don't.  You are not going to be dissapointed.  You're paying for one of the true AAA titles out there in line with Mario, Final Fantasy, Call of Duty and what made them famous.  This was a life changing game that should set the bar of all VR games and even regular games I want to experience from now on.If there was any negative concern about this game, it would simply be I can't play other VR games now the same way knowing they could've create an experience like this.  Its like eating the most amazing piece of steak(or vegetable if you're vegan) in a faraway land that you can never go back to and you're stuck with subpar steak at home.  It's like being with that 10/10 partner that you could never find in your life again after that one night stand.   Its like loving Game of Thrones till the last season and now you're like wtf Directors why did you ruin that ending and the last 6 years of my life.Anyways.  Is it worth buying a whole VR set?  Yeah if you have expendable income.  If not, go to a friends and use their VR...but remember COrOnaVIRUS its gonna get ya.  Stay at home plz and wash your hands!

This is exactly what I hoped for - if more VR games come out in that quality it might finally become as popular as it should be. Thanks Valve!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is prob one of the most immersive VR experiences out there. In fact, I am quite p!ssed that this was the first game I played on VR because it set the bar so high! One thing I found myself excited about was the fact that you actually reload the gun. Eject clip, insert new clip, ♥♥♥♥ weapon. YOU, the player does this, with your hands. _childDocuments_.review: This game is what childhood me envisioned when I watched spy kids 3 for the first time.Really the first big blockbuster  VR game so I'm giving them alot of leeway on the errors I have found. Because there really isn't another game to compare this game to at the moment. Pros:-graphics and environment. This game blew my mind. -really easy to get into the game, this game gives baby steps and the learning curve is very natural-Mix between horror and action video game.This game isn't quite Dead Space where you're on the edge of your seat, but it isn't Halo either where you're an unstoppable juggernaut. You are vulnerable to dying and you will feel like you're in the middle of the fights.Cons:-Somewhat easy for an enemy to get stuck. Leads to their body being stuck on something while I take easy shots at them.-I was stuck here for longer than I care to admit. Didn't feel like a puzzle, I just felt like og Duke Nukem "Where is it?" as I went around clicking on things trying to get something to activate.Places that could have been improved but don't break the game/where I give leeway:-My name is Alyx Vance and I'm the fastest woman alive: So the default movement system is simple enough, you point to where you want to go, and click. you instantly teleport there. This is the best movement system in the game and you're not going to want to try the others, heavy motion sickness followed me in the other modes. The problem with this is that in combat, you basically become the Flash with a shotgun. I have fought mutliple enemies by just activating my inner goku, Instant Transmission behind them, and suddenly I'm flanking these enemies who can hardly react before I blow their head off with my shotgun. It's also not uncommon for me to run like the coward I am when facing overwhelming enemies, teleport away, reload in safety, turn around and fight. Out of combat this movement system is great. however in combat, maybe movement should be restricted a little? definetly takes away from the horror aspect of the game when I'm basically a super hero.Well Supplied:Horror action Games like Dead Space, The Last of Us and Resident Evil typically aren't just visually and audibly scary, there's also the scarcity of items which messes with the mind of the player. "When will I next get ammo?" "Have to hold onto my heal item, even though i'm less than half hp, don't know when I'll next get health." HL:Alyx will constantly throw you new items. first time I discovered grenades, I found 6 of them. First time I got the SMG: I got 8 clips of ammo. The game will always give you an item you need, right before you need to use it. The most recent example that comes to mind is that I was on a ledge, and I had a grenade I had been saving for tricky situations, I opened a window and right in front of me were 4 enemies in one small room and a grenade sitting on the window sill. I chucked the grenade on the window sill in, closed the window and went in after the boom 3 seconds later. After the first 2 hours of the game, the need to reserve ammo, health packs, grenades really doesn't apply. End:Buy this game, it's friggen great, you wont regret it. First game I've played on my VR headset that feels like an attempt to utilize everything the occulus and VR gaming has to offer. Even the cons and things I complained about dont detract from the game, you'll still have a blast and you'll love everything this game has to offer.

_childDocuments_.review: NON-SPOILER REVIEWAmazing game. Haven’t even finished it yet, so I don’t even have that much to spoil. Regardless, great gunplay, great physics, and OH MY COMBINE THOSE GRAPHICS. AAA graphics were truly what VR needed. Boneworks showed the necessity of a fully developed physics engine for VR games, and I have a feeling that HL: A will display the necessity of AAA graphics and a cohesive story for VR games.Good on Valve for finally making another Half Life game (albeit the long wait), and I look forward to further installments in the series (which have been promised) and the continuity of a renewed interest in VR as a result of this game.Consider this a must-buy for a VR owner. For some serious die-hard Half Life fans, it may make VR a must-buy (even though the price may be an issue).Is it worth the price of $60? Absolutely. AAA game, so it deserves a AAA price.P.S. this game continues to push the top-notch story of the previous games. I suspect this is why many have purchased the game at all (but to be honest, who can blame them?).

_childDocuments_.review: The gold standard of what VR games should be.Incredible sound, stunning visuals, immersive world.The story is great, but it's no Half-Life 3 unfortunately.Half-Life Alyx is an amazing game that far exceeds other VR games.I spent the majority of time just picking up objects, shaking them and throwing them around.Every glass bottle I found I picked up and smashed against a wall or table.I can't recommend this game enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Even without hype in the equation, this game still manages to blow every single VR game/experience to date out of the water. Its as though Valve took a giant 5-year leap forward and showed us what VR can really be in terms of polish and immersion with our current tech.Is it perfect? Is it the virtual reality sci-fi has always dreamed of? No. We're not there yet, but this game does push the absolute limit of what's currently possible and it really solidifies VR as a technology that is here to stay.I predict the biggest downside to this game will be that there won't be a ton of replayability since its very much linear (staying true to Half-Life's roots) but it doesn't matter. The first experience of this game will likely be a very memorable one that marks the first full-fledged real VR game.Valve is back!

_childDocuments_.review: Paired with the Valve Index, this is the ONLY AAA VR game I've played. I've had the HTC Vive since 2016, and there are some great games out there. One that comes to mind is Arizona Sunshine. Just got the Index and Half Life recently, and it blows everything else out of the water. I haven't tried HL with the Vive, and I don't plan on it... the finger tracking is pretty slick. Story is cool, visuals are cool, I love the movement, (I get motion sickness with movement, so I like that you can teleport to move) One thumbstick to teleport, one thumbstick to rotate so you don't get your cord all twisted. There's only a few guns, but I like them a lot. There is a decent amount of upgrades you can make to them also. I'm looking forward to other VR games catching up to this one.... _childDocuments_.review: Without a slightest doubt - the most technologically advanced product on the market. If this is not future of gaming, what else can it be? And this game proved that miracle is till possible. Thus, from now on I'm waiting for HL3 more than ever. It's so great, that I can finally walk down the streets of City 17 myself, shoot headcrabs and throw trash cans into combines. And Alyx is cool as always. For those who are still demanding non-VR version of Alyx - this just has no sense. The game is so great only because it is in VR. Don't be deluded by that fact that non VR mod for Alyx exists. _childDocuments_.review: You can view my full review here: + looks absolutely gorgeous, several epic mini-moments+ runs extremely well, even on my 1060 GTX+ animations & VOs+ attention to detail (e.g. being able to draw on the window or feed pet alien bug through jar)+ lots of settings (teleport, full locomotion, crouch, & comfort options)+ guns are accurate & combat & puzzles are generally fun+ you can interact with lots of objects, physics are really good for the most part+ sound-design is top-notch, environmental details as well+ explosive grenade shotgun upgrade+ tagging walls with a marker or breaking windows with just about anything+ generous auto-saves (you can also manual save)+ satisfying ending+ Steam workshop (great community, adding amazing content post-release)- - jumping / mantling is done in an awful way (forced to teleport at times)- holster weapon or tool by pressing down on joystick / it materializes with press on joystick- stowing ammo by putting it over shoulder- easy to grab wrong item with gravity gloves or accidentally teleport- several items you can't interact with (including some drawers you can't open)- seeing your avatar hands move away from door handles of sliding door- melee combat physics is almost non-existant- loading screens- too linear ... several areas blocked off- mini-puzzles got very repetitive & tedious by the second half of the game- no sprinting (so you have to teleport, at least during this one segment of the game)Those are my initial impressions. I know I wrote a lot of negatives, but this game is definitely awesome and worthy of high-praise. However, it's not perfect and some of those negatives are rather disappointing and unexpected. Still, this is one of the best games in VR and a must-buy if you own a VR headset.Anyways, I will update my review if needed.EDIT 11/25/2020 - nominated for GOTY 2020. Steam Workshop is excellent.

_childDocuments_.review: Half-Life: Alyx is, without a doubt, the pinnacle that virtual reality has to offer us. It is unfortunate that this is still the case 2 years after its release, but that is more a reflection on the state of Virtual Reality, than this chapter in the Half-Life series. This game manages to create a world that is so detailed you could spend hours just marvelling at the unique small creatures, the fluid dynamics of liquid inside of bottles or just simply the vibrant backdrops that surround the player. Though, there is still room for improvement. For one, the locomotion of walking through the environment can be quite jarring. The character will often walk over obstacles that give the player an unnerving height increase that feels unnatural and ruins the immersion. Ultimately, the game is fantastic and should be experienced be all who have found themselves in possession of a Virtual Reality device.
