_childDocuments_.review: April 14th update:Since I can't play Onward atm (left stick drift, still waiting for controller RMA), I've decidedto pick up Alyx again to try the XenThug wavemod, seems to be fun.Not a proper review, a simple and random collection of thoughts from a quarantined sleep deprived man,so please forgive any absence of formatting, grammar or even sense 💀I first tried FPSs in VR back in 1995 on the Forte VFX-1 by renting it, by 1998 when Half-Life came out,I wished I could afford to buy it (or the upgraded VFX-3D version). I even had a lucid dream once, playingon it and being able to give simple voice commands to the scientists and Black Mesa guards.Fast forward to 2014 when I succeeded getting a Rift DK2 on day 1 as a developer, I managed to playthe entirety of Half Life 2 standing in front of my trackball and keyboard (no Razer Hydras unfortunately),that made me completely motion sickness proof and made me wish for motion controllers.Starting in 2016 on the VIVE I had zero issues playing h3vr and Onward with smooth loco at full speed.As an Index owner I received  Alyx in my library for free back in November so I couldn't complain,however the rumors at the time about teleportation were really making me dubious about it.Finally it came out last month and I did 2 complete playthroughs by March 25, then yesterday after 2 weeks of inactivity, I was prompted by a reddit post to try it for a third time with a twist, this line:+hlvr_continuous_normal_speed 350 +hlvr_continuous_combat_speed 350 that is more or less thenormal running speed in H3VR and similar to the one I remember in Half Life 2 back in the dk2 daysAll 3 times I played on a 4790k 16GB with a 2080ti, 136% resolution, no motion smooth, ultra detail 90Hz,hard difficulty and smooth locomotion hand based direction, 4x4m roomscale and snapturn 45°The game looks very good and I rarely get reprojection, but if I try 120Hz it is juddering even on mediumdetails, so probably cpu bound by my 6 years old machine held up only by the gpu. The audio is, in a word,flabbergasting! I rarely set the index above 19% volume, Alyx made me go up to 34%Only strange issue is the apparent jitter on the hands when close to the face , only game that has this,but it is a very minor annoyance during normal play. First time I basically played as a dev observer, basically examining every inch and angle of every 3D asset,this took me 12 hours to finish, second time more as a normal person and it took me 9 hours, third and lasttime with the aforementioned speed set to a normal (at least to me) 350 value it took 8 hours, absolutelynot playing like a speed run but normal campaign, opening every single furniture drawer, not jumpingdialogues, waiting for events, picking up every single resin and ammo, etc.What I can say is that it seems to be designed specifically for walking at snail pace and teleporting, byincreasing the speed it feels way better in some areas but finicky and buggy in others. Also it is way tooeasy for anyone that has even a very basic firearms proficiency in RL, there is way too much health andeven ammo in the levels to be found (E.G. I ended up with a total of 270 Combine smg before being disarmed), again this was playing at hard difficulty settings, however a few times they manage to one shotthe player at full health if it teleports in the wrong spot (or in my case the left stick drifting, waiting on my4th controller replacement) out of cover. All in all the mechanics are good but not H3VR good, butcertainly better than the janky physics interactions in Boneworks.That said I can recommend this game to everyone than owns a VR HMD, what it lacks in firearms realismit makes up with a compelling storytelling campaign. so suspension of disbelief is mandatory to enjoy it!

_childDocuments_.review: I thoroughly enjoy this game, but I find myself grappling with a sense of monotony, especially when comparing it to my experiences with Medal of Honor. The primary culprit is the relentless presence of Headcrab Zombies as the main adversaries. Unfortunately, their ubiquity has become a source of weariness for me. It feels like every few minutes, I'm confronted with the predictable scenario of a door opening, only to reveal another Headcrab Zombie emerging.In the expansive Half-Life universe, renowned for its diverse range of formidable foes, it's disheartening to see the gameplay overly focused on dispatching variations of Headcrabs. The repetitiveness of encountering these creatures has dulled the excitement that initially drew me to the game.Nonetheless, despite this critique, I acknowledge the game's overall brilliance and my enduring love for the Half-Life series. The narrative depth, engaging mechanics, and captivating world-building remain commendable. My only wish is for the franchise to swiftly unveil a new instalment, perhaps delving into unexplored aspects of the narrative. I still eagerly await the release of Episode 3, hoping for a refreshing shift in the enemy dynamics and a return to the diverse challenges that have defined the Half-Life experience for so many fans.

_childDocuments_.review: This game changed my opinion of VR gaming.  I purchased the Valve Index originally for use with racing simulators. It works absolutely great for that but any other style of game I tried seemed clumsy and annoying to play.  I started to think VR gaming is a novelty that would never work fluidly and I was not willing to purchase any new VR games.  Valve really did themselves a favor by giving Half-Life: Alyx to existing Index owners.   I don't remember when the game was released but it was several weeks (if not months) before I bothered to try it out because my expectations were so low.  I'm so happy i finally tried it because it brought be back to being a VR fan.   This game is the answer to all of the complaints I have about VR.- All of the font in clear and easy to read and the image/graphics quality is very good.   For some reason other games I've played (racing sims included) seems to have very low resolution. This seems to be a function of the game rather than the headset. The "home base" of valve's VR (i forgot what it's actually called) looks very good but as soon as you start most games it seems like the resolution is dropped to 25%.  That's not the case with Half-Life: Alyx. Every part of this game looks just as good as the VR home base. -The controls are natural and work everytime.  The only other game I've played that had real Index controller integration is No Man Sky.  That game has fairly natural controls also but I find myself repeating actions constantly because they did not work.  In Half-Life: Alyx, everytime i drop an item over my shoulder, it goes in the backpack without fail.  Every time I pull an ammo magazine out of the backpack, it's in my hand without fail.    The only thing i struggle with is that i slam the controllers together when i put a new magazine in the pistol. I literally just forget the controller is in my hand (they are very comfortable) and try to hit my left palm against the bottom of my right hand, which results in me cursing and hoping i haven't done any permanent damage to a controller.- Your body (though invisible) follows your head.  In other games i've played your headset location only controls the cameras point of view and has no effect on your in game body.  This allows you to move the camera through walls, outside of a vehicle, etc. and if you play room scale, you may think you body is in a safe place when actually it's a few feet away from your camera point of view and still in danger.   In Half-Life: Alyx you body stays with your head, it's not just a point of view for the camera and the game restrict you from putting your head places it shouldn't be, such as through a wall or fence.There is still certainly room for improvement in the physics of the game. It seems like there are only 3 object masses in the game... paper, things too heavy to throw, and everything else... a metal gas can, empty plastic bin and cardboard box all throw the same distance and without any wind resistance.  Also, when an object is in your hand, such as a pipe or broom, you cannot swing the object with any force.  Your arms act like they are made of rubber and the object just sort of slowly flaps around.    I'm very curious what will happen when/if i run out of ammo and need to fend off some zombies.    As far as i can tell, using in world objects is not going to help at all.Overall it's a fantastic game that brought my enthusiasm for VR back.  Had Valve not given this game to existing Index owners for free, I would have purchased it, now knowing how great of a game it is and the quality experience that it brought to VR.

_childDocuments_.review: There comes a time when a game just advances everything you know and believe about the medium of gaming entertainment. I remember the first super mario brothers, I remember the first doom, I remember the first MMO I played (Everquest) and each of those changed fundamentally how gaming was played and worked.  Half-Life: Alyx was visually stunning, so immersive that there are times when you forget you are not standing over the edge of a drop, terrifyingly crazy good when being attacked by aliens from all around you, audio wise a treat for the ears. Just holy cow this is one of the most amazing things I've experienced and it goes beyond just a game and turns into an experience for body and soul and mind.  Just ... WOW. I know people are complaining that it's only for VR but honestly any other way to experience this would just cheapen it. _childDocuments_.review: Playing it on an Index so can't really comment on how it plays and runs on other VR-headsets. Thus, everything being said here is mostly for the Index.The controls in game feel intuitive and quickly become second nature. In typical Half-Life or Valve fashion you are introduced to new elements or mechanics organically and get some time to practice them before having to use them in puzzles or combat. The worldbuilding and expansion on the Half-Life universe is excellent. This game sets a new bar for VR-games and is a must have in your VR-collection like so many before me have commented.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the platinum standard for VR games. The world feels excellent, interacting with objects and UI is fluid and spot on. The weapons feel great in your hands and are easy to use. Never did I feel like the UI got in the way of me having a good time, and it never got in the way of combat. Valve once again demonstrates themselves to be masters of level design, with enough of the familiar to keep gameplay smooth while introducing just the right amount of strange to keep things exciting and fresh, ending with the truly bizarre and magnificent. They've also done a fantastic job with the characters and story. There are not a lot of characters, but the ones that are there are very well realized and excellently written and performed, giving a much needed dose of humanity in the midst of a world run by aliens.Now to be a little nitpicky and highlight the less than amazing bits. The game feels a bit hand-holdy a lot of the time. No doubt Valve was very set on wanting to introduce as many new players to VR as possible, which is a very smart business decision. But people with more experience with VR may find themselves at times wanting more. For example the combat feels good and is very fun, but even on hardest difficulty I rarely felt myself actually challenged. I also ran into some technical issues. Inventory space is limited to 2 objects, so it's very tempting to try to grab one of the many crates and start shoving stuff you want to take in there. It sort of works, but objects have a bad habit of clipping through and falling out. Also I discovered that there is a hard limit to the number of objects you can have in the environment at once. There is one section that has infinitely spawning grenades until you solve the puzzle that requires them. So naturally I took a crate and started filling it with grenades. But carrying around a crate with only about a dozen grenades caused the game to randomly hard crash. No warning, just gone.But those small things aside, this is an amazing VR title and one every Half Life fan should experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: There have been a lot of mixed emotions over the years for the Half-Life universe. As time passed by, the hope for another official installment of the ground-breaking series (I won't dare say its name) had just about died. I can confidently say that I never believed it would grace our screens again, but then I saw a trailer for Alyx. Like any relationship, I was hesitant at first. It seemed too good to be true, and I couldn’t bare another broken heart. As more information about this game continued to surface, I began to lower my expectations to protect myself. I remembered the moments of awe I had with HL1/2. I remembered how I became enamored with a story that left me begging for more without a hint of hope on the horizon. When I found out that the story of Alyx was based in-between HL1 and HL2 I was confused. The mechanics looked fun, the graphics amazing, and we would be seeing a new side of the Half-Life story that no one had really given much attention to over the years, but...why. To me it felt like a missed opportunity to throw the series into the forefront of the gaming world yet again by continuing the epic story I remembered. I was still excited for the game, but I had settled into the belief that this wasn’t the Half-Life we knew and loved, instead, it would be a fun side quest as Valve figured out their take on VR.   I could not have been more wrong.   Without giving away any spoilers, this is genuine Half-Life, just like we knew it from the beginning. A game that re-revolutionizes a genre and brings things to the table that have not been seen before. It follows the sequencing of prior Half-Life games in such a beautiful way, as does the gameplay. I cannot recommend this game enough. Not just to die hard Half-Life fans, but to everyone. I will say though, if you are part of that former group, then you MUST watch through the credits. Valve really pulled of an Ingenius way of handling the hiatus of this series. They found a way to make this story feel alive again. If they had really started the next installment of the series with this VR game, I’m sure it would have been a lot of fun, and a great ride, but by pulling off what they do with this game they have all but assured themselves that when they do drop the HL3 bomb (whatever it may look like) that we will absolutely lose our minds. Something else is coming and I for one cannot wait to see what it looks like.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Easily the best VR game on the market currently.  It's immersion is incredible, occasionally I would scream when a headcrab jumped out at me from the dark, something not achieved in any past Half-Life games or Valve games in general.  I found almost zero bugs in my playthrough other than the occasional model clipping through the wall.  The only major complaint I have for this game is the way they handle Melee combat, it's nonexistent.  You could hit a headcrab with an entire chair and it wouldn't flinch.  Other than that issue, I say this game is really good, and definitely worth the VR headset.

_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: It’s absolutely the best VR game I've ever played and it's a real Half-Life game. It doesn't feel like a queue TV spin off for a tech demo or a waste of time. Devs go all in on this and Valve is really here doing great things. If you're extra sensitive the game does have surprises around basically every corner, so be warned! I would say if you can't play it on the VR, You should try to watch a good play through online, maybe like preferably someone not screaming over it. Because it is really good and really immersive even still if you watch it.I think you can play Half-Life: Alyx on most PC based VR headsets and my friend played it via an oculus quest plugged into his PC via the oculus link. It works pretty flawlessly with some dropped frames, but it was fun. He finished the game in less than 5 hours and he was satisfied ;D So, about Half-Life: Alyx: 11/10  I highly recommend it if you have the means. The one thing I didn't expect is like maybe I had way too high of expectations, but Half-Life: Alyx  doesn't really reinvent the wheel, well.. you know.. at least not in some ways. The movement options are all there and each one works pretty great. I chose to move around freely with the joy stick on my touch controller and snap left and right if I need to change directions. That's pretty advanced for the average user, of course!! And I feel great.Once you get used to moving around and you get the magic gravity gloves which allow you to grab stuff from a distance, which is definitely the ace here!!! This is where Valve got really clever because it solves the problem of.. well.. you know, tediously picking stuff up, and it's so much fun. It makes things so much less tedious and thankfully the tracking is really great for everything else.The AI isn't over the top to be honest I think many sequences of the game are a bit on the easy side, but not terribly so and thankfully the game does get harder as it goes. On the second half really picks up.

_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: I received this game for free alongside my Valve Index kit.And I will say with complete sincerity that I would have still paid the $60 to get this game even if there was no deal included with the Index.This game is, in my opinion, the best single-player VR title that currently exists. Not only does it blow the door wide open to continue the Half-Life series, but it also represents a huge milestone in VR gaming. Everything from the visuals and characters, and the callbacks to the original Half-Life in subtle, but extremely recognizable ways, to simple the way the game controls, and how natural it feels to interact with the environments. It's all a true work of art. If you are lucky enough to own a VR kit, and don't already have this game, DO NOT SLEEP ON THIS. Especially if you own an Index. There is quite a bit of replay value, too, so it won't just be a game cluttering your library years down the line. Unlike a lot of recent VR titles, this game is NOT based around gimmicks or the simple "wow" factor. It REALLY wants you to feel like you are Alyx Vance, and it's you vs. The Combine.10/10; 5/5; ★★★★★; etc. Whatever rating you want to give it, I give it the highest no matter what. Valve really outdid themselves with this, and I can't wait to see what's next for Half-Life and VR!
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

Needless to say when i heard about this game i was excited but also had high expectations given the long long 13 year wait for any form of Episode 3/Half Life 3/A half life title. _childDocuments_.review: The game is a technical masterpiece, one of the most polished VR experiences in terms of interactivity and combat with phenomenal graphics. If this is all you care about, buy this game. I have no idea who wrote the dialogue in this game but unfortunately, it is an unrelenting stream of cringy attempts at jokes that constantly fall flat. If laughter was sexual arousal, then this game does to my sense of humor what jumping into a frozen lake would do to my junk. And did I mention that it's relentless? The dialogue just doesn't stop in this game, unlike any other Half Life. Unless you can deal with constant and pathetic attempts at humor that will literally make you cringe with embarrassment for the writers, give this a miss until it's on sale. Then buy it for the incredible graphics and gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: Alyx is a once-in-a-generation experience; a true showcase of what's possible in VR with the same amount of resources dedicated to it as traditional games have. That's perhaps the most impressive bit of Alyx; that Valve managed to pick up their franchise after 13 years and not only continue the story, but add to it. In a world of awful reboots, it's excellent to see a story team paying respect to what made their story popular in the first place.

_childDocuments_.review: Current golden standard of VR game.Visuals, audio, story and everything else is 9/10 for me.It's not perfect though (I'm sure someone already nitpicked on those):1) No crowbar combat - this one is big minus *sad panda*2) Almost no soft body physics - only ones I know of are pillows. Far too few to even notice;3) No water or swimming;4) Light being cast is inconsistent - some items don't cast shadows from some light sources or don't receive lights. There are 2-3 light bulbs like that in chapter 1;5) Some monitors cast no light or shadows, though some do;6) Inconsistency with market writing: in very beginning you can write with markers on monitors and most other glass, but not door glass window, but literally next room with markers you cant write on any glass surface or even note book. There could'v been some puzzles where you might need to mark some items or write something, otherwise it's underused gimmick;7) So many food bars, but you can use only syringes... I know there is mod for that, but c'mon Valve;8) Pinned bodies - you can kind of interact with them, but can't move them - again there is mod for that;9) Smaller items lose shadow when picked up and regain em only 1-2 after being put down;10) Items don't get reflected in glass or that 1 puddle in chapter 111) Graphical settings are non-existent.Most of above I think is due to performance issues, but still those should be configurable... aand we can't do that (point 11.).Even with all that it's 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: ...Time, Valve Software?Is it really that time again?It seems as if you only just arrived.Half Life: Alyx is the best looking and most fun VR Game I have ever played. It quickly took over BONEWORKS place and really shows the true potential of Virtual Reality. I am sure that this game was one of the few titles to really revolutionize Virtual Reality and set a basic foundation for future VR games to come.Unlike Boneworks, the controls for Half Life: Alyx are quite simple and less complex. Busting a bit of realism for more freedom. My ONLY real big complaint about this game is the lack of melee combat and a climb mechanic that BONEWORKS had. For the most part you're pretty grounded.Now, I don't get motion sickness from VR. But I can see why things were tweaked to make the camera smooth. (Ex: You fall very slow. But fall damage is busted as I died climbing down a ladder manually lol. Also, the lack of a jump mechanic means the teleport feature does have to be used from time to time.)On a final note, this game is worth the price in full. The ending was not at all what I was expecting and I really hope we don't have to wait another 4 billion years for the next game.

The guns reload is easy to use and you can do parts with a button or with an action yourself, the movement is amazing and some of the best I have seen though little things here and there bring it down slightly, and some are actual bugs.I address a few points later so I'll skip those but my main issue is the menu, and inventory. I love hording things so not being able to have all the items is a little annoying for me but not that big a downside. Again more an annoyance than anything but forces you to pick and chose what to take and what to throw at some pore dead zombie. The menu though and the fact that i can't have my multi-tool and gun out in my hands at the same time is more annoying. Its not really needed at the same time ever but it would have been nice. I'll probably get use to it as I play more but still a bit annoying.There are a few main issues i have been seeing around and they boil down to 4 game points and then one/two not so game points. _childDocuments_.review: I was of a mixed mind as I went into this game. I knew I had to play it, and I knew it came with a lot of baggage. I loved the heck out of every HL title so far, and I appreciate the role they played in gaming history. I had read about HL: Alyx being 'short' and had played other VR 'experiences' that definitely left you wanting.I am glad to say my fears were quickly put to bed. As soon as I heard the opening ambient sound effects, I was transported back. I had not read anything in depth, didn't know how many chapters there were, and as the game progressed, I was always afraid I was near the end. However, it just kept going. They introduced new concepts, enemies and weapons at a leisurely, digestible pace. They tested you with combat, then some puzzles. The same formula that made the original games so engaging was here again.It was wonderful seeing and hearing all the familiar set pieces in glorious VR. They did an amazing job. I played seated with snap turning and smooth locomotion (with some use of teleport when things got crazy) on the original Oculus Rift. The controls were great and I felt like all my movements translated well. I didn't feel hobbled or even aware of the controllers most of time. In the end, I played 19 hours at a very leisurely pace. I died a little over a dozen times, but saves were frequent and manual saves were quick. While I would love to see more, I do feel this is a complete AAA game. The overall quality and story easily make the price worthwhile. There has not been a game like this in VR. Lone Echo was the only game I played that gave me the same sense of awe and immersion, and this is definitely ahead of that.There was a bug I ran into where if I died while pressing one of the sticks in a direction, there was a chance that controller stick was ignored after I loaded a saved game. It happened a few times during my play through. I don't know if it is Oculus exclusive or just me, but reloading the game fixed it.Overall, I couldn't be more pleased with this game. Everyone involved should be proud as hell that they carried the Half Life torch forward into a new era. I hope it does for VR what the original did for FPS. I am not too proud to say I was getting misty after the credits. Fogging up my headset.... 10/10 would cry again.

_childDocuments_.review: Valve does it again,Best game in VR hands down not even a contest.There's a reason Gaben is considered a god, I dont know how he does it but running both steam and all games released so well is just amazing, please don't change valve.Some about the game Graphics- are great they run on my 1080 pretty well but it lags if on best graphics which is to expected honestly, vr is demanding and this game looks amazing.GamePlay - they didn't honestly come up with game changing mechanics for the game but everything is so polished and the things you see in other games are just done polished and right here. nothing like the rush of  panic reloading when an alien wants to eat your head.Story - i still didn't finish it but so far  I feel like the main way you feel the 'story' is in a new way not experienced much in normal games, you really feel like you're in the world and part of it. i think VR changes the way you tell a story in a way, honestly the game could go without one word or conversation  and i'd still consider it a good story just for the feel of the world and the environment , i think that's the story in the game.Good job valve please keep doing what you've been doing for years now.

_childDocuments_.review: THE standard for whatever wants to call itself a AAA VR game. It has everything in spades: beautiful graphics, rich spatial audio, lovely soundtrack, fantastic atmospherics, a good story, solid mechanics, fairly intuitive, and one  could keep going down a list to check any other boxes. This game delivers if you got the kind of machine and HMD that can handle it.One thing that irks me about VR videogames, is that they tend to lean towards polygonal type characters and environments, because most developers are making games for the lowest common denominator of devices. This is understandable, because this way they can make the most money for the least amount of work, especially if they port. Then there are some VR games that deliver AAA 2D game quality: in gorgeous, stereoscopic, richly detailed environments and characters, beautifully lit, well staged, fun performances, with great VFX, physics, and AAA visuals that would rival any AAA 2D game, only in VR. Right now, I think I could count all such VR games on one hand, in mid-2021, and this game is #1. "Half-Live: Alyx" is unquestionably THE AAA VR STANDARD by which any and all such games will be compared for many years to come.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful addition to the Half-Life series. A company such as Valve creating a mainstream VR game is likely to help push more AAA studios to make games for VR, and get more innovation and optimization into the gaming scene.On a lower note, even with Valve pushing Steam Play, Proton, and SteamOS, the game has come out natively to Windows only. It's the easiest game I've gotten to work with Proton, but with Valve pioneering the Linux gaming scene it would have been nice to have native support for Linux. On Linux the game has a high chance of crashing whenever it loads new portions of the map, or in level transitions that would otherwise be very smooth. Currently I am unable to enter the  as the game crashes upon loading.

_childDocuments_.review: Played on the original Oculus RIft.The immersion is unbelievable!I've been experimenting with playing the game standing up ( cable is hanging from the ceiling ),  without teleporting too much, but after a while ( ~ 30 mins ) I start to loose balance from time to time, so I've been sitting on a chair and from time to time get up and look around. Teleporting is good at traveling fast between spots ( the stalker scene was done with 0 damage via teleportation ), and helps a lot during combat, as you can sneak behind the combine soldiers.Speaking of combat, the music played during the combat scenes gets you pumped up and ready to fight, and you certainly need that, as they are very intense.The graphics are surreal, it's like the reality has been drawn in front of your eyes ( the chosen colors are clearly not real, but fit great within the game ).The amount of stuff available to do in the world is really at 'Half-Life level", I've tried playing the piano,  but kind of hard with only 1 finger XDThe puzzles are great, sometimes too obvious, but sometimes I got stuck due to bugs making me think that there's more to do.I've encountered several bugs during the gameplay: 1) doors that were stuck and wouldn't let me pass. After reloading the previous save, the issue was fixed.2) I've also been able to fall to the floor on the last level, without dying and being unable to return to the correct path.The bad stuff?There are no melee attacks... like that was one of the biggest things that bothered me. It happened to me to be out of ammo in my gun while a drone kept attacking me, and my first instinct was to wack it at it, doing nothing and taking more damage... I get that we couldn't use any object we can grab to deal melee damage, but not even the weapons ? or are they too fragile ?What happened to the 'grab item with gravity gun and throw it at the enemy' approach ? I think it would have been a great thing to do, throw stuff at the enemy, if not to kill them, at least stagger while you reload or run for cover.Speaking of running for cover ( I've read that you can increase the 'walking' speed via console or start arguments, haven't tried it yet ), there is no running, just teleporting.Still, I ,ist recommend people buy a headset and play this awesome game! After that finish, you will not be disappointed with your choice. The end scenes have given me goosebumps.

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful return to the Half Life series. Very few spots where framerates weren't a crisp 90 on an i7 8700k GTX 1080 Ti rig, one of the best optimized VR games I've ever played. LOD changes when approaching certain areas were sometimes more visible near the end of the game, but you'd have to specifically *try* to notice them and backtrack for them to become an annoyance. Sadly there's no melee combat, but physics do exist--you can deflect headcrabs with objects. The level of detail they put into everything in the game is astounding, and most things you think you can do, you can. I had several moments where I couldn't help but smile or chuckle because, "I'll be damned, that worked." It hits many of the tonal marks the original half-life games did, and does so very well.9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Right now there are many VR developers out there that don't know what exactly works, and this game shows solutions to that problem that work really well, such as refining controls and physical interactions. I started playing this game with high expectations and even that was heavy underestimating of how advanced and fun it is.This may just be the game that refines how things work in VR games, setting the bar high. _childDocuments_.review: This is my revised review on HL:A and I have a lot to say for this title.Before I begin, I would like to note out that Valve's main Half-Life titles pushes the limits and raise standards for video games; much like Half-life and Half-Life 2.Half-Life: Alyx doesn't stray from this formula.The game is optimized to run consistently well on most, if not all, VR headsets and STILL maintains high fidelity with its Graphics, Modeling, Physics, and the Environment around you.Some might even call it sorcery, I'd say it's brilliance.If you want to get into the Half-Life lore I suggest playing from chronological order, starting from Half-Life, HL:A, HL:2.However if you are only interested in an immersive VR campaign experience, I believe one's expectations might be met, if not far succeeded.So, yes, I ABSOLUTELY recommend this game. _childDocuments_.review: This is a must play if you are VR fan, curious about VR, Half-Life fan, or even just someone who wants to experience a game unlike anything else. The workshop content adds a lot of additional fun too giving you a good reason to boot the game up even if you have already beaten the main story.The gameplay tends to switch between segments of wandering through environments contaminated by Xen flora and fauna which are more survival horror than previous Half-Life titles, and faster paced action segments where you'll be fighting Combine soldiers and later antlions. Every area in the game feels like it was based on a core gameplay concept or story element and then meticulously designed and iterated upon to perfection. The gun play takes a bit of getting used to due to the level of interaction required to accomplish actions like aiming and reloading but once you are comfortable it feels exceptional and you'll be popping off pistol head shots in no time.Various types of puzzles are also found throughout the game, as is Half-Life tradition, and range from recurring mechanics such as unlocking Combine ammo caches and routing power, to unique physics based puzzles which feel like evolved versions of the puzzles found in Half-Life 2. I personally enjoyed all of the puzzles but I can see how some of them might become repetitive after a while for some players not keen on needing to unlock a Combine replicator every time they come across a new one in order to upgrade their weapons. While not new to the series, exploration definitely takes a much larger role in this entry and the player will spend a good deal of time searching rooms and peeking under debris looking for ammo and resin, which is used to fuel weapon upgrades via the Combine replicator mentioned earlier. This might be a daunting task in a traditional game but in VR and with the new gravity gloves, aka 'Russels', to help this is extremely enjoyable and can lead to finding all kinds of neat easter eggs or details that would otherwise be skipped over.The graphics are phenomenal by VR standards and better than most traditional titles even. Everything has incredible attention to detail and feels real when you are in game. Playing this on ultra settings with a 2080ti, AMD 3900X, and Valve Index the game ran at 144fps most of the time but there definitely were some dips to 90 when it got intense. Lighting is very realistic feeling although i did notice that Alyx's hands do not cast a shadow which was somewhat disappointing. Environmental audio is incredible and every area is crammed full of ambiance by way of interesting sounds that comes at your ears from all around. Gameplay sound effects such as gun reloads, physics interactions, and enemy vocal clips all pack a punch, with some nostalgic queues thrown in for series staples like health stations and elevator dings. The music was fitting when played although a bit sparse, mainly saved for combat or other action sequences. However, the music was not as iconic or impactful as some of the notable tracks from previous Half-Life games.The plot of the game plays out at a decent pace and is conveyed to the player mostly via radio conversations with important characters and Valve's signature environmental story telling. Occasional interactions with NPCs are very rich and the voice acting and intense facial animations bring life to the scenes. The overall story is fantastic and will thoroughly excite any Half-Life fan, while players new to the series will still be able to follow along through most of the story beats.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: What can I say. The frist time I played this at a friend's place with the friend's VR set - the same evening I ordered my own VR gear just so I could continue playing Alyx at home. Simply amazing experience - both the VR, as well as the good old authentic Half-Life 2 feeling all over again. Best way to bridge the time until Half-Life 3 is finally released... soon(tm)
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Valve do it again - I never thought Alyx could live up to the hype after such a long wait for a new HL, but it totally delivers in every way. The implementation of the VR is truly innovative and a huge step forward for the medium. The storyline progresses the HL lore in a meaningful way (despite its prequel status) and the mixture of puzzles, action and horror is every bit as polished as you'd expect from a game from the HL tag.You know you've played a masterpiece when you can't stop thinking about it days after finishing. A MUST have for any PC gamer.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Must have VR game. If you ever had doubts about VR well this game will put them to rest. 10/10P.S. for smooth locomotion turn fan on, use dramamine, hydrate, and take breaks often. I know some people have issues with that. If you cant stand it, teleport is fine. Game was designed to work with teleport first and they added loco later. Cheers
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: It is unbelievable how great a VR game can be. Playing with Valve Index. This is, by far, the best VR game available right now. It is immersive and I can interact with virtually everything. It took me 20+ minutes to leave the opening room because I was so busy playing with the environment. When I got out, I spent another 10 minutes going down the first set of stairs lining up all the pictures. It's that level of detail, if a painting on a wall looks crooked, adjust it. It's not the point of the story, but this is the point of the game as a demonstration of what a good VR title can do.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: The writing is snappy and witty; the visuals are efficient and lucid; the controls are the best VR has to offer, with the wrist-flicking grabbity glove item retrieval mechanic being the stand out creative masterpiece I hope every VR title would use; and the combat is precise and challenging. Finally, a VR game with high production values which follows HL-2 closely in terms of design, art, and quality, and surpassing it in writing, atmosphere and visuals. A+
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: One of my favorite vr games. This was truly a breathtaking experience, some parts have stuck in my mind since the day I started. There are a few flaws such as the stupid orb puzzle thing (you know what I'm talking about) and there was no melee combat, which is a staple of the series. But if you look past those small missteps, you've got an amazing game that only costs about $1060. 9/10, this is the way to follow up Half Life 2.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: As a person who typically avoids horror games (half life alyx being one of the few that I actually played), I would still highly recommend this game. The best game I have ever played - the main reason being how immersive it is.Almost everything in VR was extremely satisfying to do - Reloading weapons, having super-like powers like grabbing items from the air, shooting off an antlion's leg, etc. If i had anything to complain about it would be the puzzles for opening certain boxes/doors/upgrading stations. These puzzles were fun at first but later became old and felt like a hassle towards the end of the game.If you do not have a vr head-set, get one to play this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: This is what VR should be!  It has everything, good gun play, good puzzles, great graphics and most importantly and a real feeling world with a good story.  Only other game I had played like this VR up to now was lone echo but this is so much better.  Played on CV1 rift.  I would highly recommend anyone with a VR headset gets this game.Also i think the ending suggests....
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty cool, but missing a key aspect that would really make it feel more half lifey. The physics puzzles. half life always had its combat sections punctuated by some quiet, scenic physics puzzle. In Alyx the puzzles are just those little multi tool puzzles. which are alright at first, but they get old quick. It's a shame too cause physics puzzles are great in VR. moving stuff around with your actual, virtual hands in order to solve puzzles is great. A missed opportunity IMO.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: In my opinion the best VR game to come out yet. I've played it through twice now and it never fails to impress me. The combat is great, good story, super immersive environments. Everything you could want and more from a VR game is here. If you have a VR headset you owe it to yourself to play this game (and the rest of the Half-Life series in general). Seriously, a 10/10. Playing it through again with the developer commentary turned on was very interesting since you get to hear some of the dev's thought processes that went into making a lot of the different areas and effects. Pretty interesting to hear some of their ideas compared to the final product. If you don't have a VR headset, I'd honestly say it is worth buying one just to play it. It's that good.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game and story. Needs a little tweaking in the preferences to make it just right. Everything about it is incredible. Not too short either. And brings a satisfying connection to the rest of the series. If this doesn't usher in HL3 then there's no hope, but with this game at least I can die happy.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: This is it. This game is to VR as Half Life 1 was to FPS games. Taking everything to the next level. Incredibly polished, well thought out and beautiful. The controls never give you any issues, it's like the game reads your mind at all times and "just works". This is the Valve quality everyone knew and loved. Now give us VR's Half Life 2 :)
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: love game mechanics and visuals but the story feels what ever and the constant puzzles and constant trash searching for getting weapons better to survive and nothing for killing enemys perfectly ruined game . this is mine opinion :) also you cant progress in the game if you dont follow one and only path in game cant go further if u want to skip something :)
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Clearly so far, without a doubt the best VR experience I have ever had and one of the best gaming experiences I have ever had. If you ever watched a movie and wondered, what would it feel like to be in that scene, running and hiding from the bad guys, being close to those bursts of bullets and explosions, big things moving and collapsing. Its ineffable, just being in presence there is something else. This is the game If you want to experience something close to that feeling. I would love to see more type of content like this game, specifically in VR. Valve just set the bar high for VR gaming.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Heads up may need to optimize settings for your VR through Steam VR's settings along with the settings on the Oculus app if you are using the Oculus Rift S like me, I'm a new VR user and when first playing this game I experienced weird choppy visuals but after looking around online I found the perfect configuration for my PC setup and now the game runs perfectly smooth, has something to do with Steam VR and the Oculus app running at the same time not the actual game that's causing these issues, The game though is beyond amazing and would recommend to anyone looking for an extremely interactive VR game, the fact you can practically touch and move every item, or something as simple as seeing inside an empty water bottle is amazing, the graphics legitimately make it feel like your actually there, and playing with a fan blowing in the background while standing on the balcony overlooking the city in the beginning of the game made it almost feel too real lol, all in all get the game! This is definitely worth the asking price.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game with the purchase of my Valve Index and i've played through it and everything about this game is great! The Graphics, The Story line, controls (As of playing on Valve Index). The immersion as well is phenomenal. Also as a first time player of Half Life This Sparked A Change in me in which i want to play the whole franchise of Half Life Now.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: I was a VR skeptic before I played Half Life: Alyx. I picked up a few VR games here and there and they were fun, but they always felt gimmicky to me. Even when I was in the process of putting in my credit card info and buying the game, I was unsure. That is until I put on my VR headset and started playing! I was blown away that a VR game could be something like this! I didn't know it until I started playing Half Life: Alyx, that this was the entire reason I purchased a VR headset in the first place!I'm playing on an Oculus Rift S and it works like a dream. At the time of writing this I am currently 11 hours in and haven't finished my first play through yet. I don't want it to end! When I finish my first run, I plan on turning up the difficulty and going again! I am hoping that there are more enemies in the encounters at the higher difficulties. That is my only gripe so far, in that they don't throw more enemies at you. Some encounters feel a little short. Right when you're really getting into it, and ready for more, the encounter is over. I don't see this as a bad thing. That's what you want in a video game in my opinion. You want to leave wanting more.If you are having any doubts like I did, do yourself a favor and buy this! Especially if your a Half Life fan! When this game was announced I was disappointed, like a lot of people, that this wasn't Half Life 3. After playing, my disappointment is gone. Of course I'll always hope for HL3, but Half Life: Alyx definitely relieves a lot of that HL3 heartache we've all had since 2007. So stop reading this and go and play this game!EDIT: I just finished the game at almost 14 hours, and....there aren't words! That ending! I had chills!! Amazing game!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Half life Alyx offers you over 20 hours of gameplay. It has great mods, impressive graphics and a good physicality. Overall i thoroughly enjoyed this game, which caused me to play the main campaign twice. However, this game is very linear, with levels that dont really allow exploration. Its story is told in an extremely effective way, and keeps you enticed all the way through.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: My first VR game and oh boy. The ending is absolutely mindblowing. Surprising. Flabbergasting. And they confirmed Half Life 3 with it! Looking forward to it.The gameplay is interesting and entertaining.Only the levels with exploding barrels and electro "dogs" were frustrating a bit. Some enemies and mechanics reminded me of old school games like Dead Space - the Combine weapon upgrade stations for example. And the electro "dogs" were a lot like Necromorphs from DS. That's good. Nostalgic emotions++.I am writing this review within 30 minutes of finishing the game. The ending is easily the strongest emotional consequence (pun intended) of the game for me.UNFORESEEN CONSEQUENCES. These two words have ENTIRELY new meaning now. Just HOLY SH*T!!!!!I don't see how I will sleep today.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Half-Life: Alyx is absolutely brilliant, the developers have played to VR's strengths, and utilised them incredibly well. Unfortunately, as it turns out, many of VRs strengths revolve around terrifying you. Bleak, muted colours to avoid eye strain; small confined spaces to maximise performance; high fidelity, spatially accurate, creepy sound effects to heighten immersion; massive, hairy, spidery, head crabs to facilitate the wetting of your under garments. Yes, HL: Alyx has all of that, and more!  It essentially lays the ground work for how VR FPS games should work.  Also, I've been playing for 25 hours and I still haven't completed the story. I strongly suspect that the game can be won in 3 or 4 hours, but if you're like me and have to crawl at a snails pace, peaking around every corner, bracing yourself before entering every room, then you'll probably get really good value out of the game.  I've just met Jeff and its possible I will never be able to complete the game... That guy... just, no. That's my verdict, awesome game, I recommend it up until Jeff.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: [NO SPOILERS - or substance at all, really, just how I felt. I played this on the Oculus Rift S and I really enjoyed it, though I'm sure all VRs on the store page will work wonderfully.]I wasn't sure whether or not to buy a VR early - on one hand, I wanted to make sure I was able to play it on release, so I minimized the risk of being spoiled (and didn't have to continue testing my patience!). On the other hand, there was always the risk that the game might not be very good - and that VR still had time to go before it comes up to the bigger market.I decided, perhaps foolishly, to buy VR prior to release, betting on the fact that it'd probably be at least good. I went into the game extremely critically, and frankly, every problem I had was simply a limitation of VR technology (or in some cases, just a limitation of MY setup). As much as I tried to be in that critical, 'grrr, this is not as good as the old games' muh nostalgia mindset, I simply couldn't help enjoying and loving this game. It's one of the best new releases I've played in the last DECADE, and I was not let down at all. The ending alone makes this game worth every penny, and I look forward to what Valve will do in the future. Let's just hope that optimism ages well, and I don't return to this review in 5 years with no new news about their upcoming projects.If you are in a position in life where you reckon you want VR - or you REALLY want to play more Half-Life - I cannot recommend Half-Life: Alyx enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: This is by far the best experience you can have with VR yet. Valve has definitely made a strong comeback with this. Half-Life: Alyx is extremely immersive and incredibly fun. I would 100% recommend this game if you have a VR headset. However, the game is definitely targeted towards those who have played Half-Life 2 Epsiode 2, so I'd recommend playing the Half-Life 2 series before playing this.Obviously this game isn't without its flaws. It has taken very great steps in the right direction for VR, but it's still clear to see that VR has limitations that held this game back a bit. It has bugs here and there, though I experienced them very infrequently. Some of the hacking puzzles got rather annoying and some ended up being a nuisance more than being fun. The combat was very enjoyable overall, although it definitely was simplistic so that it wouldn't be unfair, for example they only ever send at most 5 ranged enemies at you at once, which after the first few battles feels a little underwhelming, although it's counteracted by the intensity of having to aim and reload manually which can lead to some very tense situations.All in all I'd give this game a strong 9/10 and am super hyped to see what amazing things Valve will do in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: This is the best and most immersive VR experience there is. You don't have to be a fan of the franchise to enjoy this game. You don't even need to care about the story or anything. The combat and puzzles are very enjoyable, and so is this game in it's entirety. This was definitely worth to wait 13 years for a new Half-Life game.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Jesus Christ on a Stick this game is amazing.And yes of course I'm biased, I played Half-Life one back when it came out in '98 and I'm now 31.I didn't buy my VR Headset (Oculus Quest 2) exclusively for Alyx, but this was one of my first experiences with VR as an FPS game, seeing how it had teleporting, thus reducing motion sickness.And what can I say? I've played SuperHotVR before this, I've played Lone Echo (not finished) and the myriad of VR demos, but NONE of them reach the level of "photorealism" that Alyx reached. I'm quoting that word because everything looks..... organic, yet when you get close enough, the textures start to show their ugly head. Sure, it's understandable; they needed to cater for as many specs as possible, and performance is amazing, except for some setup I had to do on my end to circumvent some game-breaking stuttering I encountered.Sound is also amazing, with positional audio being exploited to its ultimate potential, with some soundtracks being placed at just the right moments to enhance the experience.However what really, truly stands out from Alyx is the gameplay. Boneworks may have its verticality and fully physics based, full body experience. Lone Echo may have its awe-inspiring vistas, but Alyx does that all in such a gradual and welcoming way that it allows even a VR noob like myself (I barely reached 120hours of SteamVR just now, after 2 weeks) to fully discover the uses of the technology, while also allowing for exploration and clever use of cover, weapons and physics. I do wish the game had more jumpscares -as crazy as it may seem-, as the medium really lends itself to it, and headcrabs are amazing as they are.Another thing I wished the game had more of is more scenes that are not as.... obvious in terms of layout in combat. I mean sure, it's an amazing introductory game, but I think they could've exploited the system to push the player to do more daring things. Maybe a higher difficulty allows for that? IDK, I'll most likely replay it later.Story wise.... I won't spoil anything other than what we already know; you play as Alyx Vance and find yourself in A city. As for the rest, you'll find out soon enough, hopefully.All in all, what's most intriguing about Alyx is not its superb production quality, its incredible graphics or outright top-notch setting and story-telling, but perhaps how it is tied to a technology that (at least now) is still not widely available for everyone, and requires quite a bit of setup, extra money and a beefy PC. In any case, I can't really wait until Valve surprises us again in the next..... 10 to 12 years, and in what conditions.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: one of the best VR games out there, worth buying and is the perfect game for trying out VR especially on the valve index, very accessible for everyone if your sitting or left handed or any minor problems, you wont experience any motion sickness if you use the right movement settings, it comes with any valve index and the roughly 15 hours of gameplay is just amazing with many scenes just blowing you mind, the graphics and environments were so detailed i usually couldnt even see any polygons, only problems are with such action gameplay i hit my ceiling multiple times while throwing grenades or doing some puzzles, (6.1 feet tall) also can be confusing without playing half life 1 or 2, and jeff is the nicest character and totally does not give me ptsd. a rare instance where i rate a game 9.5/10 since im usually harsh on my ratings but honestly i think everyone should play this at some point
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Halife Life Alyx is one of my first VR experiences after recently taking the plunge into the world of VR. It's an amazing game to experience for sure. I get sucked in and don't stop for hours at times, though I have been going through it on hard and gotten stuck a couple of times and quit in frustration. That's on me for playing on hard, but I would recommend it as when you overcome a few tough spots it's rewarding. The game has a creepy atmosphere, and is fun to just explore around and not know what you will find around each corner. My one and only complaint really is the lack of weapons, but other than that I plan to replay it again, and with the recent release of mod tools this game will give you many enjoyable hours. Valve likes to take things to the next level, and they tend to do a good job at it!
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: It's quite rails. It's totally more simple and more grounded than other games like boneworks. And yet, like other valve classics. It's very polished and full of character. Handcrafted with beautiful skylines and horrid, grotesque flora/fauna. This game does have some creepy moments in case you aren't into that. It was clearly not developed for crazed experimental vr players with sea legs. It was evidently made with first timers in mind, while I prefer the more open ended "natural" gameplays of other stories, this isn't that and that's okay.  Fun to shoot in. Plenty of ammo management, tons of collectible currency and ammo to dig around for with worthwhile and tactile upgrades. The puzzles weren't so memorable to me or quite fun. But the rest of the game was plenty to make up for it. Immersive looting and shooting.F the "water temple" of this game. Iykyk.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the biggest step for VR, showing how this tech can really deliver an experience. The gameplay is fun and anxiety inducing at times, the progression of this game is constant and does not feel rushed. The more you play the more natural body movement in game becomes to the point things are second nature. The horror aspect in the Half Life series really shines in this game and made me freak out like Ravenholm did when I played years ago.The combat shines in this game well, and never makes you feel that the Game is at fault, for when you die in game or take damage. The combat is well made and very immersive and you lose yourself as you hide behind barrels from combine cover fire.The soundtrack is very immersive and I wish they made this a vinyl pressing.10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely one of the best games and next gen feeling. I play on a Quest2 and its the best VR mind blowing so far as well.  I know there are a few others possibly as good, but, i haven't played them yet. game play has been smooth and I don't get motion sickness from bad Lag or jitters etc.. although I do feel slightly strange for a bit after playing at least 30 min.  this is a must have if your computer can support it.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good. Definitely more well-done than any other VR game I've tried, and really shows me that Valve hasn't lost their fine-toothed comb touch in all these years.Absolutely worth the purchase, and while I don't know if its worth spending all the money on a valve index for, you could certainly purchase a cheaper set for a few hundred after looking at your options. A lot of people look at the price-tags on VR and get scared, but its an easier choice to make if you just think of VR as a PC upgrade, one that's granting you access to a wider range of games to play.I do hope this polished AAA entry into the sphere of VR will encourage more companies to try the same.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: To me this is a natural progression. Half Life (software rendering), Half Life 2 (GPU mainstream rendering with physics) and Half Life Alyx (Immersive Rendering with GPU and physics)The team at valve have always seemed to ones to deliver what I expect next from my gaming technology, not sure why but they always deliver what I perceive as the next step in gaming. To me Half Life has always been a VR experience of sorts, no cut scenes, seamless loading interactive NPC's. Maybe i took for granted the other aspects of the Half Life games that people enjoyed but for me, its always been about immersion, like being in a movie, being one of the characters and fully committing to the experience.Half Life Alyx delivers this notion in every way, it is quite simply the best gaming experience I have ever had.Next stop, the holodeck.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing. Best VR game ever. I came into this thinking I would be a bit dissapointed since it does not have melee fighting. and I LOVE melee fighting. However, this game is still the best VR game ever. So good, that it's ruined other games for me like Boneworks, Walking Dead S&S, and even Blade and Sorcery. Man this game is amazing. Amazing gameplay, sound, physics, intractable environment, atmosphere, story, movement, enemies, ai, and weapons. And as a bonus, it has the perfect amount of horror for me. Not too much that I stop playing, but enough to keep me very scared. This can get you an easy 15+ hours. I've played 17 hours so far, and I'm gonna do a second replay before I most likely stop. AHH, I wish it had more replayability (multiplayer and other modes). However, every part of the story felt unique and not repetitive. !!!!This is the BEST VR game ever, and I loved every minute of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing. As an advocate of VR development since the beginning, this game was a huge morale booster. The only other game that rivals this in VR is Resident Evil: Biohazard, and I think its fair to say that this game is a huge step up. The jump scares are not too much, even for me, who cannot watch movies without looking up a list of jump scares. The atmosphere is beautiful, regardless of settings, in my opinion. This game ran well, surprisingly, on my Oculus Quest 2, even though I was playing through Virtual Desktop on a laptop that only has a 1060 Max-Q (on low!).
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: This game has exceeded some pretty high expectations. Makes my slightly reluctant VR headset purchase very satisfying. Easily the best game I have played on VR so far.I have spent a solid amount of time just looking around and admiring the scenery. Picking up pieces of paper or reading labels on bottles or anything.Plays like an actual game. Does not feel like the usual VR arcade sandbox. I don't feel sick when I play, which has happened with a few games. Haven't made it too far into the game yet, but it has been a fun journey so far. Easy choice if you own a VR.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: I would rate this 3/3 but Valve does not know how to count to 3, so neither do I. This game is revolutionary, unbelievable, amazing, beautiful. Gunplay and handling, throwing, interactions, you name it,  Alyx masters it!. This game defines VR but it has no melee which is a slight dissapointment! Anyhow, this is a game you must have in your VR library.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: I never got around to playing any of the Half Life franchise but heard all good things about it. Since day 1 I have thoroughly enjoyed the experience. I'm on a 2016 Asus ROG20 (GTX 1080) with Oculus Rift with Touch controllers. Graphics are great, sound is fantastic, interface I love. Game play is totally satisfying. I need to take a break ever-so-often, to 'calm down' from creep-factor. Love it.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: WOW... what an achievement. There are games that are "converted" to VR, there are games that have "VR SUPPORT" and then there are games that were made just for VR.  It's a heck of a commitment to make a game that a small number of people would buy based on the VR only, but boy did that gamble pay off.From the opening scene you know that this is probably the most robust and advanced VR experience out there. I honestly don't think you'll get a better VR video game with this much work and production value. It may be a long time before we see something for VR on this level again.If you just got your VR headset and are looking for content, do yourself a favour and buy Half Life Alyx. It was designed for the format from the ground up and is just an amazing interactive experience. Both VR thumbs way up!
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Virtual Reality was crying out for a proper triple-A title to kick it into the mainstream and of course Valve were the ones to do it with a new Half-Life game that is more than worthy of the name.From the moment you first look out over City 17 towards the iconic citadel, Half-Life: Alyx is incredibly detailed and one of the most immersive VR titles I've played. Even the simplest tasks such as emptying a bucket or writing on a whiteboard are immensely satisfying. It feels like Valve have taken the relatively novel VR mechanics we've seen before and polished them to perfection. In 1998, they gave us immersive textless storytelling; 2004, real world physics integrated into gameplay. Now in 2020, Half-Life shows us virtual reality gaming the way it should be.The novelty of VR aside, this is also undoubtedly a Half-Life game. It's wonderfully paced, set in a beautifully realised dystopia and cuts the tension with humour at just the right moment. Then there's the story. We were all disappointed when Half-Life 2: Episode 3 never materialised but the way Alyx connects with the events we've played to date and adds more mind-bending sci-fi wrinkles is nothing short of genius and makes me wonder whether this was the plan all along. There is definitely more story to be told, but in what format? After ditching the mouse and keyboard with this much success, it's going to be very hard to un-ring that bell.Pros:It's Half-LifeCons:On my second playthrough I'm not so excited about collecting resin.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing VR experience! The production value is through the roof, at times it feels like you're playing a Pixar animated movie. It's that good.I've been a gamer all my adult life and one of my first FPS-games ever was indeed the original Half Life. I am now in my 30's and still going strong, but I'm not going to lie. Games have been going in a direction I don't appreciate lately, and my enjoyment of newer "AAA"-games have been on a steady decline for a few years now. Cue Half Life: Alyx... it completely revitalized gaming as a hobby for me. Not only was it my first VR-game, it was the first time in YEARS that I truly lost myself in an amazing digital world just like I used to so many years ago.Thank you Valve! For keep my passion alive for me!
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: I've been waiting for a continuation of the Half-Life saga for several years and it was well worth the wait. Regardless of it being a VR game and its specific interactions truly improve the already amazing experience, the story is what you would expect out of a Half-Life game.Once I started playing it, I couldn't stop thinking about anything else but the game and having to know what happens next kind of consumed me. It's a rare occurrence for me in recent times to want to finish a game in such a short time span.The controls are highly intuitive and the fluidity with which you can play the game contribute to a more seamless experience. The ~15 hours you'll spend playing this game are fleeting but they are worth not only the game price but the acquisition of a VR Kit as well.The only con I have is that I nearly had a heart attack when my wife touched me while a headcrab was flying in my direction.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't play much due to when I did play I was playing with a gpu below the minimum required, but even then, the game was fantastic, I'm going to be buying it again to finish it now that I have a better gpu.
