_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Has it flaws, I hope the add more options but as is, probably if not the BEST V R experience overall. The amount of graphical fidelity is absolutely amazing absolutely terrifying at times but also lots of "HOLY COW" moments where the story and environment just blew my mind. Will be looking for mods to ad replay ability and hopefully upcoming additional chapters to keep the fun moving.Cons;-no way (with oculus) to hot swap between free movement and blink/ teleport movement. -free movement is a walk speed, hopefully the can add a sprint with a stamina bar. - limited inventory space (preferential to player/game play mechanic ) -no melee weapons (wheres the famous crobar?)Pros ;-Almost all items have interaction-Graphics are Amazing for VR-Gun mechanics feel realistic-Sound effects and ambiance are incredible (adds to immersion)-Lots of content for 60$ price (only 5 hours in and I am hooked)-Feels like a legit "Half Life" titleP.s. Valve please give us more. <3 <3 <3
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: SPOILER FREE!Absolutely worth the decade+ wait.In true Valve form this entry ticks off the two main things Half Life is known for: Gripping, first person story and industry changing innovation. The gameplay is fine. Never bad, sometimes spectacular. Pacing is slow but that's a positive as it really helps with the atmosphere and makes the small enemy encounters very intense. The final two combat sequences... absolute masterpieces. Puzzles are almost all annoying, easy and worst of all boring. There are a few gems though.The guns are disappointing. There aren't many of them and the upgrades are pretty plain. There are basically three must have upgrades which you can probably get all of them by the half way point. Definitely takes away from the reward of searching every room as most things you can find are resin for upgrades. Graphics... I haven't experienced anything like this in VR. The atmosphere is just so thick. Staring down a long dark hazy hallway with a bit of light at the end and... is that a headcrab? Just part of the wall? The only game that's ever made me more afraid of a hallway is P.T. And the sense of SCALE!! So... the VR aspects of the game are mostly good. Movement is responsive... guns are responsive... gravity gloves are a cool excuse for teleporting items to you and they work well. But this game suffers from what many VR games suffer from: Everything just feels way too big. Like the dimensions of everything got multiplied by 1.25. They also went overboard with non adjustable comfort things like making Alyx REALLY slow and instead of falling when you jump off an edge you float to the ground like you drank the green potion in Prince of Persia. The story... is... perfect. Literally perfect.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game to ANYBODY with a VR headset. This game is worth the price. Everything in this game can be interacted with. Period.The bottles of beer and wine if you look inside have liquid, and bubbles in them. You can draw on glass, and whiteboards, and light will fade through your drawings.I suggest you look around the environment anytime you can and just look around. It's absolutely beautiful.The voice actors absolutely knocked it out of the park, and the modelers even more so.After beating the campaign, there are hundreds of amazing mods, both lore accurate and original and I just cannot recommend this game enough.100/100, would play again.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: After playing this game, all VR games before appear to just be demos or beta versions.This game combines a really well developed VR game with Half Life - this feels like Half Life 2, this sounds like Half Life 2, so I would say this is at least Half Life 2.5.Positive:+++ liquid shader!!!+ physics - which is in VR much more fun then in a conventional shooter+ it's Half Life+ reloading your weapon is tricky when you are attacked, each weapon has to be reloaded in a different way+ the loading screen+ there are only 3 weapons and 2 types of grenades, this limitation is very good for the gameplay and due to the upgrade possibilities, weapons do not get "boring"+ there are only a limited amount of enemies, but all of them are so different that there is a good variety during the campaingn+ quite long, it took me 16h to complete the main game (i'm not the fastest player, have enjoyed it and search a lot for resign and ammo)Neutral:~ Zombies and headcrabs in the dark~ sometimes you can somehow feel the weight of objects, sometimes they are like balloonsNegative:- using the gravity gloves pulls the object towards you and not towards the hand you used to drag- long loading screens (but acceptable)
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: A worthy return to Half-Life, and an incredible next step for games. Alyx is a showcase of how VR can immerse you into a story and world like no other medium. When you play it, you're there, and I couldn't have enjoyed my stay more. A thrilling, one of its kind ride.As a Half-Life game, it gracefully transitions the universe and its characters into the current generation with beautiful visuals and updated designs. It explores interesting new areas of the Half-Life timeline and even manages to satisfyingly push the story ever so slightly forward after being left on a cliffhanger over a decade ago. Beyond what it is, what it represents and promises is worth a lot.As a VR game, it demonstrates how virtual reality can allow unique interactions with a game world, seamlessly woven into every moment of gameplay. Normal conventions are flipped on their head and even something as simple as aiming a gun or opening a door requires all-new thinking and input from the player in a way that only feeds further into immersion. The novel gameplay is then wrapped in unbelievable levels of polish felt everywhere from the lovingly handcrafted environments, slick animation, and soundtrack. It's incredibly refreshing, presented incredibly, and so confident and successful that it easily sets the standard of what a story-based VR adventure should be.Alyx is the best of both worlds. The game's existence should make anyone excited about the future of the once dormant Half-Life, one of the most innovative and notable shooter series in history, and the way we can experience video games going forward.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Just wow. Absolutely amazing and engrossing from the moment you enter the game through the end. Right before any game mechanic or visual may get stale, things are switched up and something new is there to pull you in or blow your mind. This is not only the best VR games I've played, but one of the best games I've ever played.I have to go figure out what to do with my life having finished.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: This is the best VR game to date - Granted I haven't played every VR game out there, but I am confident in saying that this is the best. And the ones I have played don't come near this one in terms if visual fidelity and polish.That said, there could still be improvements made. I found using the Index controllers a bit frustrating at times - the grip registry can be very finicky, as well as tracking, hands getting stuck on objects, or objects getting stuck to your hands. Fortunately, you can get past this by just using the trigger to grab things instead of the hand grips, and teleporting away from stuck objects.But those are more or less minor issues, that don't really detract from an overall great game.This installment leans heavily into the horror elements of previous HL games, which as a person who doesn't play horror games, it was super effective. There are some truly terrifying parts in this game, and I hate/loved every second of them.While not perfect, this is a huge step forward for VR and gaming in general. I can't wait to see what this inspires other developers to do, and what other offerings Valve comes up with.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: My review is from the perspective of an inexperienced VR user. This game was my main reason for buying the Oculus Rift S. Thus, I had very high hopes going into Half-Life Alyx.Going into this game I've played HL, HL2, as well as ep 1 and ep 2. And if you want to keep up with the story I would strongly recommend playing the three latter.As with most Half Life games (in my opinion) story comes secondary to gameplay. I find that to be the case in this game as well, although I enjoyed both of which immensely.From the very beginning of the game it feels real, and after less than half an hour you are IN the game. This is a result of the amazing interactivity of the world by being able to pick up every small object you can find. Because of the amazing gameplay elements, I found this to be the perfect introductory game to VR. It is much more satisfying to kill a zombie by first aiming down the sight of your gun, than simply by moving your mouse. And every gun fight gets your adrenaline pumping, making them feel like they last far longer than they actually do.The pacing of the first couple of hours is perfect for inexperienced VR players, as there are no sudden changes in difficulty nor any out-of-nowhere jumpscares. The moves you do are intuitive, i.e. using gravity gloves and reloading. And every puzzle makes sense after some thinking.The story is not especially convoluted, nor very long (any more focus on story would reduce the time to enjoy HL Alyx's gameplay). Without spoiling the end, I may say that it does - however - open many doors as to where the Half-Life story may continue.In summary, the game had me hooked from beginning to end. Temporarily for the gameplay. Subsequently for the story.This game is a masterpiece, and I would even go so far as to recommend renting/buying a VR headset just to experience it if you can afford.Best (out of the two) VR game I've played. However, being better than Beat Saber is impressive in its own right.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a Half Life fan, have a VR rig, what else are you waiting for? Still remember the awe of Half Life in '98 and jaw dropping in '04 for Half Life 2. Now to be able to experience Half Life 2 environments in VR is mind blowing. Even if you're not a Half Life fan, this is definitely the best VR title I've played to date. It has a little bit of everything and is extremely well executed. Plus I am sensitive to motion sickness and felt absolutely none using smooth locomotion. Not to say it didn't have its quirks. Had to deal with major fps drops and game crashes until I figured out settings that worked for me.Win 10 64bitRyzen 7 2700xRTX 207016 GB RAMQuest 2 Headset /w VD for wireless (I usually use Airlink but wouldn't work with Alyx)**** EDIT - Airlink works now for me as of Nov 4 2022.SSDSo how I finally got it running smooth with no crashes? May not work for everyone but here are my settings.Launch options:-novid -console -vconsole +vr_fidelity_level_auto 0 +vr_fidelity_level 3 +vr_render_scale 1.0In game graphic settings all set to minimum. Honestly on a Quest 2 it wasn't that much of a difference and really helped FPS rates and latency studders. Switched over to a stand alone router set to exclusive 5ghz which helped a lot as well.The big change that really stopped all crashes was adjusting my virtual memory to 8gb. I've never had to do this for any game, usually have it set at 4gb. For whatever reason, it completely fixed all crashes especially for the later chapters where it seems a lot of people suffer from crashes and fps drops. Probably would've run smoother hooked in with a link cable but I'm spoiled now and never going back to wired VR. The freedom with wireless is worth every setback imo.If you have a VR rig, this is a must buy, especially on a sale. 11/10

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a true masterpiece. Never have I ever enjoyed a vr game this much. The physics remind me of when the physics for half life 2 were considered unheard of. I spent like at least 10 mins. just messing around with the objects even before I got the gravity gloves. The story is way better than I expected. _childDocuments_.review: Holy crapNever played a half-life game before and I still love this game. I'm sure I'm missing a lot of details (of which I'll research here soon now that I've finished it) but the basic story wasn't hard to follow even without prior knowledge of the series.I only have the basic Vive, but even then, the experience is phenomenal. Partway through I measured the actual distance between my eyes so I could better adjust the lenses and HOLY CRAP, the difference was astonishing. I spent so much time just gawking at the scenery.The gameplay is easy, fun, interesting, unique... if I absolutely HAD to complain, I would only say that it gets a bit tedious partway through (lots of exploring corridors and trying to figure out how to progress) but it picks up fairly quickly. If you get stuck, just retrace your steps and make sure to keep an eye on where the wires lead (that's what stumped me the most). The cutscenes are fascinating, the dialogue is fantastic, and this is the closest I've ever been to genuinely being scared in a video game. (granted, it got less scary as it went on; you get used to it)This is the first $60 game I've paid for in who-knows how long, and I don't regret it one bit. Now all that's left is to explore what the steam workshop has to offer. Here's hoping Valve keeps this stuff coming

_childDocuments_.review: Absolute masterpiece.As much as it's not Half Life 3, it still is a very nice chapter in the saga.Gameplay is engrossing and immersive. I had to see the Chaperone's limit barrier at a certain point to realize I was not actually in the game world.The combine soldiers are excellent. I didn't think they could have remade them better than in HL2, but I've been contradicted hard by their quality in this title.Weapons are all made to be used with one hand and even though I don't much get why that'd be their decision, I've never had any reason to whine about it during the whole campaign.The powerups you can obtain for said weapons through the use of resin, scattered around the levels and sometimes really well hidden, making you use your exploring skills and taking full advantage of VR world manipulation capabilities to full extent.Some heart pounding scenes are to be expected and do their job egregiously, especially the first time you go through them.And of course the storytelling is in line with Valve's narrative skills.If you have an Index headset, you're a proud owner of this gem. _childDocuments_.review: Half-Life: Alyx is among the very best VR experiences I have played. It is a half-life game through and through. Valve really did it.I do have some gripes about various design decisions that I believe could be addressed without changing the game too much:- Segmented movement even in continuous mode. What I mean by this is that there are some parts of the game where you have to use some form of teleporting movement to progress. The biggest of this is jumping; while there are areas where you would normally jump, you here have to use teleportation since there is no jump mechanic. Other things that requires teleporting include moving down ladders, through small spaces, through broken windows, etc.- This is a minor one: Pushing open doors is not fully physics based. Basically no matter how slow you touch a door with you hand, they will be bashed open at a set velocity. This has killed me at least once.- Being unable to simply drop you weapon.- Putting the inventory point behind your shoulders. In pretty much every single firefight, right up until the end, I would always go for the waist for a new mag before remembering where valve put it. Not only is waist inventory for ammo faster and more intuitive, but pretty much every other VR FPS does it there.- Feather falling- Not sure if this is by design or bug: Not being able to move bodies. You can pick them up, but it is like there is always some limb that seems to basically be glued to the floor. This is annoying when I want to search bodies for supplies.I will rate this a solid 9/10. One point lost for the above mentioned design choices.

_childDocuments_.review: Half-Life Alyx NO-VR review: In 1998 when HL was released, I was already a nearly-40-year-old fanboy. That means here in 2024, I’m an even much older fanboy—who, unfortunately, also has intermittent vertigo problems and suffers from severe motion sickness if I’m not careful. So, if I were ever going to be able to play Half-Life: Alyx, it would never be in its native VR form. Ah, getting old ain’t for sissies, as they say.That’s why I was out-of-my-mind excited to hear about the Alyx NO-VR mod. I would finally be able to jump back into the dystopia that is City 17 and get gunned down by the Combine--before I croak in real life, that is. Now that I’ve made my way through the entire game using the NO-VR mod, I thought I’d write a little…update?I won't extensively review the game. Plenty of other reviews here. But if you are reading this because you are also a longtime HL fan who can’t (or won’t) strap a contraption to your head but want to play the game, here’s my short advice: DO IT! The mod works. You can play the game from beginning to end sitting 12 feet away from a flat screen (or on your couch in front of ye ole’ TV box) and not vomit. Some of the VR-heavy functions in the game have been simplified (or removed) for flat-screen use, but the big, overall narrative experience, high-tension firefights, and creepy locations are still lovingly in place. Sure, it’s not the same innovative experience as it is in VR I guess, but also…you know…no vomit, no having to lay down for an hour to make the room stop spinning. Anyway, the game looks amazing (even now, 4 years after release), and the story and actors are as good as ever. The NO-VR mod has added in workable character models (hands, arms) and reload animations so it plays like a classic HL FPS. Maybe it’s my nostalgia talking, but wow.However since the NO-VR mod is…well…a MOD, my recommendation has caveats. So as of February 2024, here are the hurdles I (quite happily) had to jump as I played through the HL: Alyx NO-VR mod. Since the mod is in active development, I expect many (or all) of these issues will get resolved (if they haven’t been fixed already).GENERAL ADVICE: 1) SPAM THAT QUICKSAVE BUTTON. There are some technical issues with the current build of the NO-VR mod (again, we’re talking Feb. 2024 here…read below) that could be frustrating. Saving often helps soften those problems. There is a decent Steam community controller mod (if you play with controller) which works well, but I personally made one major configuration change to that community controller setup: I assigned the quicksave function to a single button on my controller so I could always have fast access to it. 2) BACK UP YOUR SAVES FOLDER. The way the NO-VR mod works, you only have a limited number of saves (something like 3 autosaves and 3 quicksaves that are continually overwritten, and the NO-VR mod does NOT support saves that were made in the regular VR version of the game—you must use your own NO-VR saves with the mod). The game’s save folder is located within the main install HL: Alyx folder and is clearly labeled SAVES. Take the time to create a copy of that folder and keep multiple copies of it somewhere. Why? It is possible for you to get yourself into a non-reversible situation (again, see specific issues below) and all your saves have been overwritten and you have no way out, other than starting the game from scratch. You do you, but I choose the low-frustration route.SPECIFIC ISSUES I FACED>CONTROLLER PROBLEMS: I play my PC games with a controller (Xbox Series X/S via Bluetooth connected to Windows 11). You might not, and if you use KB+M, then you don’t need to read this. The NO-VR mod supports both KB+M players and players who use controllers, but two issues with my controller happened. First, MOST of the time, after the NO-VR mod booted, it would NOT recognize my controller as being connected even though I had the Steam community controller configuration loaded, applied to the game, and Steam input activated (which you have to do ahead of time). It was super frustrating. BUT I finally figured out what I had to do to fix the issue. I had to boot the game AND Steam in a specific order: 1) With NOTHING running (not Steam, not the mod) and making sure my controller was connected via bluetooth to Windows, I simply had to> 2) Double-click the NO-VR mod launcher.exe itself. 3) This starts the NO-VR mod launcher. (Steam is still NOT running.) 4) In the NO-VR launcher, click play. 5) This auto-starts Steam. 6) Then Steam auto-starts HL: Alyx. If I had anything running ahead of time (like Steam already running, or the NO-VR launcher already running), my controller would not be recognized. This is how I fixed it.CRASHES: When I would die 3 or 4 times in a row (it happens as the Combine firefights get tougher towards the end) and the game would restart from a checkpoint, after the third or fourth checkpoint load, the NO-VR mod would crash to desktop. This is one of the reasons you should spam the quicksave so you don’t lose progress. But outside of this specific situation, I NEVER experienced a crash. It only happened after several quick restarts in a row.STUCK: Due to the nature of the mod, it can happen that you end up stuck on a piece of geometry (usually because you are somewhere you shouldn’t be). Thankfully, the NO-VR mod has auto-enabled the “no clip” cheat to a specific key (V) so it is super-easy to unstick yourself if this happens.FORWARD MOVEMENT STOPS: This one I had to grin and bear it. But Alyx would often simply stop walking forward when she encountered even the smallest object on the ground in some places. A small rock, a tiny cardboard box, a little cable on the ground—these are things she would normally glide right over, but instead she would come to a dead stop. There were some maps where I would have to hop my way through it if there was a lot of debris around. The problem seemed to come and go, but it was especially frustrating in a firefight when I was trying to beat a hasty retreat to reach some cover…and Alyx comes to a complete stop because there was a piece of paper on the ground--and then she’s full of Combine bullets.GUN MODS: The game has Combine machines you can insert your gun into for upgrades. After the upgrade animation ends, the gun is supposed to pop back into your hand. In some chapters though, I found that my gun was still sitting in the upgrade machine after the animation stopped, and I could not retrieve it--all I could do was look at it. I certainly couldn’t go forward without a gun. So this is why I say: Spam that quicksave! Get in the habit of saving BEFORE you do anything major. Most of the time, I would just ignore that non-working upgrade machine and wait until I reached the next one.SCRIPTED EVENTS DON’T TRIGGER: There were two cases where major scripted events would not trigger for me, and the game would not move forward. Again, this is a reason to back up your saves folder so you can revert. One was in the “Jeff” chapter where the monster you are stealthily avoiding is supposed to follow you into an elevator. No matter what I did, Jeff would NOT get into the elevator—he was stuck in an earlier part of the map banging on an invisible door. The second instance was where I deactivated a Combine force field, but it still wouldn't let me go through. In both cases, I used the built-in “no clip” cheat that the NO-VR mod has enabled, and the game moved forward, ignoring the glitched script. Yay.Though the above list might sound like they are all reasons to NOT play the NO-VR mod, that is not the case at all. As with so many mods (and especially one of this magnitude), you have to be prepared for workarounds, restarts, backups…all that good stuff. I was so happy to be able to play this high-quality HL game. I got those old tickly HL vibes all over again after so many years. YAY!! Oh, and that ending! Oh yeah, that ending!

_childDocuments_.review: Half life Alyx has the most detail of any VR game I've played yet.The gun play is rather simple compared to other VR titles like H3VR or Boneworks, however there is less jank and ultimately that translates to a smoother experience, the most bombastic VR experience, that is awesome in every way of its gameplay and story telling. But it's not without its faults, and certainly not the most advanced VR game in regards to gameplay.Some examples of this:- You can't drop your gun, it's stuck to your hand.While this in itself is not very realistic, the immersion of the game negates this, I could not imagine the horror of having headcrabs and zombies attacking you, while your gun drops to the floor due to having sweaty hands, not holding the gun correctly or just being clumsy. Having the gun permanently stuck to your hand doesn't really take anything away from the experience, it just contributes to a smooth experience - it's just not as realistic as other VR games.- You can´t physically interact with enemies in combat (no melee combat), and this is not necessarily a problem or a negative. It's just pretty jarring coming from last year's Boneworks where EVERYTHING you picked up could be used as a weapon, to Half Life Alyx's few weapons.- The puzzles doesn't utilize all there is to VR. What I mean by this is that it's true that puzzles in Alyx requires six degrees of freedom, they could not be translated 1:1 to a flat screen, but they can all be done standing in place, it doesn't fully utilize all capabilities of roomscale VR. I believe this was done to ensure the game could be played both sitting, standing, and in room scale - however it makes most puzzles rather samey.Overall it is still the most polished, beautiful, immersive VR game to date.Also it's spooky as ♥♥♥♥, I thought headcrabs were scary in Ravenholm, however those smaller ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ are on another level in VR, living jump-scares.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll be real- if you want a good demo for what VR could be, play first few chapters of Alyx and be amazed how interactive the world is. Heck, I can't even use environment apart from exploding barrels-it's the same puzzles over and over again. They are fun at first but I rolled my eyes after tenth of the same "connect the power lines"-The further the game goes, the performance dips to the point of being unplayable. Do you like tearing? Now imagine it in full VR goggles. If I had epilepsy I would've been found dead.Overall, good tech-demo but not a game I would buy for full price.

_childDocuments_.review: It's been 13 long years and Valve really delivered. In the same way Half Life 1 felt revolutionary for it's story telling and connected worlds and Half Life 2 felt revolutionary for the physics Half Life Alyx felt revolutionary to me. Just seeing City 17 rendered in so much detail in VR was amazing. The production values are amazing, Valve obviously spent as much time and money as they needed on this game and other VR games I've played so far just feel so much more limited in scope.  The visuals are truly amazing aside from a few bad looking assets here and there.Combat feels more intense in VR. Combat is very much designed around VR and some of the limitations you face (like slower reloading). You typically face fewer enemies and have overall fewer combat encounters than a flatscreen Half Life. There are enemies like the armored headcrab that can only be shot in the soft underbelly who would be much easier to kill in a standard game but in much harder in VR. The only surprise to me was the lack of melee weapons in the game. The game switches between horror sections and more standard combat against the Combine section/levels. Every level feels really well designed for it's section, for example you're often running very low on ammo in the horror areas but have plenty in the Combine sections. Despite being a prequel the story really ramps up and I was constantly looking forward to the next story section. The new character Russel is pretty fun and I enjoyed his interactions with Alyx. Despite being a prequel it doesn't lean as heavily into character cameos as you would expect and there's several characters missing that you would expect to show up. The two new gameplay elements are upgrading your weapons and scavenging through the environments for upgrade materials and ammo. Both of these are really designed for VR and work really well, the upgrades because you have a limited number of weapons and I feel like the scavenging is much more fun in VR than it is in normal games.Puzzles return, but not the physics puzzles you would expect. You use Alyx's device to link broken power lines behind walls and solve 3D puzzles. Both are fun enough but the lack of physics puzzles made the game feel a little more static than Half Life 2 in a way, which was too bad. Overall I had a ton of fun with this game. If you have a VR headset it's a must play. I'm hoping the next Half Life game is also in VR since it does feel like a few things were missing from this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Play it.No, really, if you have a VR headset, this is a must IMO.I'd strongly recommend you play the rest of the Half-Life series first, but if you really, really don't want to you don't even have to do that.I wish this could have been my intro to the platform, it's that good and that immersive. I've been doing this for almost 3 years, yet I spent about a good hour just shaking around bottles and reading random newspapers. I felt like I was THERE, and I've already been desensitized to VR.Now, time for breakdown:The Good:-Half-Life in VR, heck, an official Half-Life game released in 2020 is a pro by itself. The only reason I didn't play it sooner wsa I didn't have a good PC.-The guns feel good to use! Not quite like H3VR, but they're satisfying and have cool upgrades. I didn't even mind that there were only 3, because those 3 were done well.-The graphics are great, like, I was on medium and could still clearly read the aforementioned random newspapers. Bonus points for the characters- the humans look "real enough," and the zombies made me feel genuinely disgusted from a game for the first time in years. But despite this...-It's optimized too. I only had significant slowdown a couple times. I did have an issue with the game crashing while it was on a loading screen, but it turns out that was from streaming to friends on Discord.-It controls well, but I think equally important in VR is that your interactions with objects feel good too. Carrying heavy things like explosive barrels has some noticeable weight to it, for one. You can also grab a headcrab mid-jump, do what you will with that information.-Gravity Gloves should be in more VR games, they're just so... good. I don't know what makes them so good exactly, you'll have to find out yourself. They were still fun even at the end of the game.-I liked the character interactions, some are genuinely pretty funny.-And, it's meant to be beginner friendly, so yes, it can be your first step into the virtual world like I wish it was for me.-But most importantly, of course, you can eat a headcrab heart. 10/10.The bad:-It's meant to be beginner friendly. That's both a blessing and a curse, because really, I just wish jumping was an option.-There are no melee weapons. Granted, they are hard to pull off correctly in VR, and you *can* slam a headcrab with random objects if you really want to. Besides, realistically, I don't know what a teenage girl with a blunt object could do to armored soldiers.Seriously, play it.THE VERDICT: 9.6/10.

_childDocuments_.review: This is quite possibly the best game ever created.Pros:The mechanics are so well designed that once you get the hang of one you are on to a new one. The game iterates on itself making the progression amazing and smooth. Never a dull or repetitive moment with just enough time with each new game element. The environments are crafted so beautifully and detailed making it an absolute blast to check ever corner of the game. I played switching between medium and low graphics and still found the game to be breathtakingly beautiful.The story is so gripping and if you're a Half Life fan you will be satisfied beyond a doubt. The characters are amazing, the dialog is done so professionally I truly became immersed the characters of this world. Cons:Parts of the game feel more like I am on a roller coaster as in I am just being railroad-ed from scene to see to look around as if I'm on a ride instead of immersed in a game world. Though these moments are sparing and are in stark comparison to the rest of the game in which I feel like I have more autonomy and freedom.Much of the game takes place in claustrophobic narrow halls and rooms. This I'm sure is to lend to an easier VR experience with everything being close enough for you to see and grab with little movement needed. However I would've liked some more open and less suffocating areas. Summary:My minor nit picks don't even come close to taking away the overall experience of the game. The emotions I felt playing this game are beyond what gaming or any other media has done to me before. This is the future of gaming and I feel like we've barely scratched the surface of what can be done on this medium. Half Life: Alyx is a revolutionary game and I will not soon forget it. I will likely play it a over again a few more times before the end of 2020
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredible, the bar has been set exceedingly high for other future VR games which I can totally stand by. So, where do I even begin? The visuals are absolutely astonishing, to be standing inside a video game that has such high quality in detail, the effects, the sound, it feels too good to be true - but it is! The length of the game is long enough for you to really enjoy and get yourself immersed; I just couldn't find myself ever getting bored because I had a mission to complete. The scenes we are given from beginning to end, interactions with characters, and the thrilling moments set out for you, it is hard to get over. And for this game to make me scared but want to continue, it has made me laugh too. I cannot even begin to describe the emotion near the end which I will not leak. I strongly hope Valve makes more games in this type of style. For this type of VR game to come into existence is what I live for, but as for someone who never even played the other two games is why I say, I would like to see something else. Still, I very much love the game, the story, challenges, characters. All of it. Thank you Valve!

_childDocuments_.review: 1. No melee, so if you run out of ammo in a room of headcrabs, good ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ luck. You get to spend the next five minutes dodging headcrabs while scavenging for ammo. _childDocuments_.review: Its tough to put into words just how fantastic Half Life Alyx truly is. I'll try to explain it in two parts:Part 1: As a Half-Life gameHalf life alyx is a spectacular return to the world of half life and city 17. There is the return of plenty of familiar faces (or lack thereof), headcrabs, overwatch soldiers, the combine architecture, but also so many new and fresh things we've not seen before. The new types of soldiers, the new weapons, the environments. The quarantine zone is something we have not seen at all until now and it is both terrifying and amazing at the same time.Its hard to say too much without spoilers, but its absolutely safe to say that whilst this is technically a "prequel" to half life 2, you will be given so much new information and many new experiences in the half life world that should keep anyone satisfied. This is a prequel....but you should ABSOLUTELY play half life 2 and the episodes 1-2 before playing Alyx. The reasons will become clear laterHalf life is back, and it is brilliant.Part 2: Why VRThere are plenty of games that use VR, or were even designed for VR, but could reasonably be done on a standard mouse and keyboard. Gunslinging in VR is great fun, but we've been doing it on traditional PC controls for decades too.Half life alyx however was clearly built for VR, with nothing keeping it to the typical design restraints of "Normal" PC controls.utilising cover is critical, the way you interact with the environment, grabbing, holding, throwing things, looting and just about everything you do feels so natural and simply could not be done with normal controls.VR is an expensive thing for many, and so its understandable why people are angry they may not be able to play.But the experience of half life Alyx simply cannot be replicated in any other way.Creeping through dark hallways, physically covering your mouth to avoid coughing from the spores, throwing a bottle to distract an enemy and quickly scrambling to grab that power cell you so desperately need is genuinely terrifying, thrilling, and fantastic in VR.People asked for a killer game for VR, this is not just a killer game for VR, this is a masterpiece, period and absolutely one of if not the most thrilling and engaging gameplay experiences I have ever had on any platform.

_childDocuments_.review: Very vague almost-spoilers below!--------------------This is hands down (lol) one of the best games I have played in a long time. If the game was flat with the same story, it just be good, not great. If the game was just the VR mechanics with a different story, same thing. Good, not great.The combination of the two make this damn near a masterpiece. Without giving details, I teared up when certain life or death things happened. My hands shook a few times when surprise headcrabs... well, surprised me. I effortless learned to duck behind cover, reload, pop around a corner, and headshot enemies across the room like a badass. I humorously failed to hug characters I saved out of joy. A certain unforgettable scene found me physically backing away and bumping into my desk in video game fear.This game has emotionally moved me in a way not many have. Oddly enough, a certain infected friend was just fun, not scary to me. Go figure.I have very few and very small complaints. Effectively, this is a 10 star game to me. It's a brilliant showcase and introduction to VR gaming.

_childDocuments_.review: HL: Alyx - some of the best graphics in a VR game ever. I can't believe what I'm seeing with my super old low resolution Rift CV1. I thought I'd never be satisfied with VR graphics but Alyx proves that VR can have good graphics.The VR mechanics have been polished to near perfection and this will likely dictate the way future VR games will be made.Dropping ammo into your backpack / shoulder is the best ammo management system in VR ever. The sound cues of when your hand is at the right spot is the perfect solution. The ammo stomach pouch done by other games is not perfect because my stomach gets in the way. So every game should do shoulder / backpack ammo from now on.The issue of holstering and switching guns have been solved quite significantly. In other VR games you try to pick up a virtual object stuck to your hips and sometimes you just don't manage to pick it up. No longer a problem with Alyx. Same with grenades. Because weapon selection is a button hold + gesture.Storing small items on your wrist is an excellent way to see what item it is and easily find it when you need it. Instead of storing stuff stuck to a virtual torso.Gunplay of course there's no problems there. VR gun aiming has been pretty much perfect for a while now. Alyx's style of reload is simpler but not arcadey. Its visceral and you need two hands so in a gunfight you need to get good at reloads. This makes gunfights more visceral and pulse pounding. YOU CAN MESS UP YOUR RELOAD AND DROP YOUR AMMO LOL.Alyx chooses to go with single-hand weapons which makes sense. Two hand weapons in VR creates a weird effect because your hands aren't connected in real life and thus won't have realistic feeling 2-hand guns.Picking up objects is solved by magnetic gloves and feels very polished. With a bit of a snap lasso gesture and then snatching the object in the air, it makes for a better object "magnet" effect than Oculus Home where you point at something and press a button to pull it to yourself.The guns have indicators that show ammo count so you can keep track of half-spent guns. Very nice.Your gloves also has a spare ammo count and health meter. Good way to communicate that.You can wear masks, hats, etc.Now, let's talk about the physics engine and why its important for VR. And Half-Life is perfect for this because the gameplay of the flat HL games already use a lot of physics.Your gloves interact with every object in this game. Even walls. You can feel walls. Even though your physical hand goes through them, the in-game hand stays on the wall and you feel vibration feedback. This gives you presence in the world you didn't have before. You can feel doors. You can feel cabinets. You can feel beds. You can feel guardrails. You can feel anything.Having your hands feel things allows you to feel the wall when you're taking cover. Giving you the exact data to process where your hand should be when you need to shoot behind cover.You feel the cabinet when you open it. You feel the door when you open it. You feel the box when you move it. Believe it or not, most VR games don't do this.Physics is amazing too, because you can even use your gun to push objects. I use the muzzle of my gun to pull cabinets open, push doors, etc.The best way to explain physics is you can use ANY object to block a headcrab from jumping onto you. That's physics.Alyx doesn't have melee combat though, because honestly in VR you can't feel what you're hitting except for the small vibrations. So you can technically waggle like the Nintendo Wii and that's just not fun. Guns feel much better in VR.Traversal is quite well thought out, and you get many options of movement and turning. The important ones are here like teleport and smooth movement. And they added smooth turning a day after release - something super important for me. You can even grab ladders to pull yourself up. So yeah basically, well thought out. Jumping is also solved and is sort of like teleporting so its good for when you get stuck in some weird spot between boxes or weird geometry.Other than those, that's mostly it for the VR mechanics done right by Alyx. There's also spatial puzzles you need to solve, sometimes you need to throw a grenade to a vent that needs a bit of basketball skills.Personally I feel like there's a bit too many multitool puzzles especially the orb ones. Its a pain especially once you get to the trip mines. Looking around boxes and every nook and cranny for upgrade ingredients can also get kinda repetitive.I wish there were more physics based puzzles like carry a box here to weigh something down, you know? Instead there's multitool puzzles and switches. 9 out of 10 makes you feel like a tool.Story is pretty simple. HL is never known for its amazing story and Alyx is the same. The plot is basically an excuse for Alyx to go around shooting stuff solving puzzles and whatnot. Of course, this is still Alyx and she's a main HL character so she ties into the entire canon story of HL and HL2 and Gordon Freeman, so its cool to see parts of the story of this world. The ending makes an interesting statement too.Essentially, Half-Life: Alyx is VR mechanics perfected. It takes the best of all VR games' method of presence and picks the best ones, while having the polish of triple A game. Being in VR, the world is much more memorable and tactile. I wish it had more gunfighting, less multitool puzzles, and I wish you could run, but other than that this is the perfect VR game.

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't nominate Half-Life: Alyx to be my "VR Game of the Year." I couldn't because I already nominated Half-Life: Alyx to be my actual "Game of the Year" and I couldn't nominate it twice. This VR game is the reason why I purchased an HTC Vive in early 2018, back when the VR Community was awaiting an announcement from Valve about one of their "3 VR Games." Of course, it took nearly 2 years later for Valve to eventually reveal Half-Life: Alyx. I already loved my VR Headset and put it to good use in Arizona Sunshine, BeatSaber, SUPERHOT, and Tilt Brush, but the announcement for HL:A finally made my purchase feel justifiable.I can give praise to almost ever aspect of this game. The graphics were beautiful and sucked me right into the ruined architecture and quarantine zone of City 17. The Grabbity Gloves were a stroke of genius. The characters were well written and enjoyable (Russell has become my new favorite Half-Life Universe character and I want more from him), and the headcrabs, zombies, and combine soldiers were even more terrifying when standing at life size right in front of you.I have to give extra praise to Chapter 7: Jeff. This level solidified to me that this game can ONLY be played in VR with motion tracking controllers. Having to juggle covering your mouth from toxic gas, solving electricity puzzles with your multi-tool, and throwing vodka bottles to distract the hideous, blind creature that is stalking you at every turn, is an experience I will never forget. If you played a non-VR mod of Half-Life: Alyx, that would be like playing Super Mario 64 as a 2D sidescroller. Yes, you could get the gist of the experience, but it is in no way comparable to the actual game.Not only was Half-Life: Alyx the experience that defines this generation of virtual reality, containing story writing more fantastic than I could have ever wanted, and the level of polish that you expect from a developer of this caliber; this game also proved that Valve still has it, that magic touch that no other developer can even attempt to emulate. I can't wait to see what they come up with next.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Edit - The boneworks comparison is just a pure mechanics comparison. Obviously Half-life is gonna have a better narrative between the two. Boneworks is just better in fights despite having less varied enemies. You can pretty much do whatever you want and get away with it. VRcrab on your face? Pop it off with a cleaver, pick it up, and bash it against the floor or wall. Or just catch it mid air and chop it up in your hand. You can't really get that kind of experience in Alyx. After I beat this game i doubt i'll come back to it anytime soon unless i wanna do some achievement hunting. End edit.-If you've played Boneworks, this game is gonna come as a disappointment to you on some level. The level of interactivity and creativity available to you there are leaps and bounds ahead of this. I was actually surprised to see the reviews overwhelmingly positive here. That being said, this game is not bad. It is Half-life after all.It definitely feels like a Half-Life game, but it fails to bring the intuitive and creative nature of VR properly. You can pick things up but trying to interactive with them in any other way just feels clunky. Two handing a broom? Good luck. Not that there's a reason for you to do so anyways since you can't use anything but what they specifically give you as weapons.The movement system is okay, but as of right now, smooth turning is bugged so you'll have to deal with snap turning until they fix it. It's kind of amazing in it's own right. You'd think something like that would be one of the essentials to have right on release.Edit- They were quick on the fix for this one. Turning is much better now.Along with the nifty new Gravity Gloves, apparently Alyx picked up some anti grav boots cuz any fall just gently floats you down gently. There's need to at least be a option similar to the Barnacle lift where you can choose whether or not falling is normal. There's also no jump option. Instead, it's replaced with a pseudo-teleport "jumps" for gaps(only one so far in 2 hours) and mounting if you want to get on top of something.Speaking of those Gravity Gloves, those things are surprising nice to use. At first I felt like it was kinda cheap since technically stuff like the gravity gun didn't exist yet (to my limited knowledge), but instead of it feels like a prototype of the technology used for the gravity gun. You can't grab and hover things. Instead, you only use it to yank things towards you for you to catch, which is fun on its own. It perfectly fits thematically and gives us a reason to have a force pull.Now, on to the weapons. The first thing you think of for Half-life weapons would probably be the iconic crowbar. It's the go to we all fall back on when we wanna conserve ammo and bust a couple head(crabs) open. I have not seen this weapon yet. I expected it to be my first pick-up followed by some epic valve music letting me know that i'm back in the mother****ing saddle that is Half-Life. Nope. Got a pistol (hilariously at least). Someone mentioned in a comment that the crowbar was "Gordan's weapon". Screw that. We got to use it in Blue Shift as Barney as well. If you ask someone if they wanted a crowbar in this game, i'm sure most would say heck yeah.The pistol feels oddly large and is pretty accurate. Not after too long you get options to upgrade it with with  some upgrades. My biggest gripe is that reloading is a bit weird with you pulling clips out your backback and being unable to store half empty clips, which is sucky. Unless i'm missing something, if you want to use all your bullets you pretty much have to accept you're gonna have to go into every fight with a low clip. Ending a fight with 2 bullets left feels terrible. I'd like to be able to at least refresh my clip without having to waste precious ammo in the process. The old games did this, why not Alyx? Once you get the reservoir upgrade this pretty much isn't an issue ever, but it's still meh and would be better if you could just store bullets freely.The Shotgun is the only other weapons i've encountered so far, and it's kind of a small weird pistol hybrid shotgun that you use with one hand, probably to make it more user friendly. It's effective like a shotgun, but doesn't feel like one. Also has some upgrade options, which assume comes with all weapons. Not much else I can say here.I should also mentions grenades, which is probably the funnest way to kill something in this game. Feels great to get that perfect throw on a distance enemy. A nice change of pace since you're normally just shooting slow enemies all day.I've never run out of ammo yet, but if I do i'm curious on what i'm supposed to do to defend myself. Maybe the weapons can actually be used for melee once it runs out? Who knows.All the weapons are accessed via a menu by holding down the trackpad(index). I prefer the holster system other games have used, but I can completely understand why they'd do this for Half-Life. Usually in these games you have access to a small armory so i'm hoping that ends up being the case here as well.Overall, i really don't hate this game. At the end of the day it's still Half-Life. It's just missing some much needed VR functions like improv weaponry and some navigation adjustments. Wouldn't mind picking stuff up to be less clunky either.TL;DR+Looks great+Weapons are accurate+Gravity Gloves are amazing-Navigation is a bit clunky. (no jump, no sprinting)-No crowbar, melee weapons, or functioning improv environmental weapons.-Weapon sizes are a bit strange (Large pistol, tiny shotgun. Hardly an issue)-Interacting with things feel off, especially 2 handing anything like brooms or smaller things like clipboards. Once again, not really an issue, just tragic.-Reloading via pulling clips from over the shoulder instead of waist is a bit awkward. (You get used to it. Hardly a negative but I figured it's worth mentioning.)I probably would have given the game a positive review if it weren't for all the people blindly giving the game thumbs up followed by lots of praise. I just want to point out some of the flaws people are glossing over. If you don't understand or have never played Boneworks, please go give that game a run. Story isn't much but it's mechanically sound and very engaging.If you love Half-Life, pick it up. Just don't expect anything groundbreaking. So far it's probably the weakest game in the series, but it's far from bad.P.S. Stop being so salty. A bit of criticism never killed anyone.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the best game currently available in VR, and possibly the best entry in the Half-Life series as well. The narrative is cohesive, and the writing is serious without taking itself too seriously. _childDocuments_.review: Still not quite finished the game but I think the actual content, well you can look to other reviewers for that. It's great, obviously, because otherwise Valve wouldn't have put it out- or at least wouldn't have called it Half Life. The game is really very scary and I can only play it for about an hour or two at a time once every few days which is why I still didn't finish it. I find the firefights etc really immersive and the horror elements make me feel a bit sick. Every play session gets my palms sweating!No this is a review for the game as it runs on Oculus Rift CV1. I had to get a decent upgrade- more RAM and  an SSD- and even then it seems I should have got a better CPU as well. This game is VERY intensive, so I need to close every computer program except Steam, Oculus and HLA to run it without this weird jerking effect in which the screen freezes and my head moves without VR moving for half a second, which is obviously terrible.The actual controls don't work so well either. For example one action you'll be doing a lot is priming then throwing a grenade towards big enemies. Maybe, again this works better with Valve's own hardware but on CV1 half the time it treats the throw as a drop and you end up killing yourself by dropping the primed grenade at your feet. In general the game itself does not have the high amount of interactivity I expected from all the hype- you can pick up a bike for example but it has no chain and does not roll, just falls. Many cabinets have fake drawers you cannnot open. Of course with CV1 touch controllers you do not have full finger control so cannot do the crazy piano playing seen in the hype videos. Despite the performance and control problems, I'm still happy to have invested in an oculus a few years back and the mandatory pc upgrade to be able to play this game at all even if I'm obviously not getting the top notch experience that is advertised for index users.

_childDocuments_.review: By far, the best game I have ever played. Every time I booted up the game it got more and more fun. The later chapters are definitely the best, which does have the downside that the first three chapters, in my opinion, are fairly lackluster. _childDocuments_.review: The level of detail is absolutely insane for a big VR game. The pacing is perfect, because it adapts to you. The Gravity gloves are amazing and fun to use. The story is, well it's Half-Life. The atmosphere is creepy and perfectly dystopian. Some models are splendidly sick and disgusting. It takes me forever to play through areas because I just walk around in awe, looking at things, existing in the HL universe. My only gripes are the spatial audio that seems somewhat lackluster and at times way off, and that all of the details in the world makes me sort of expect that I can interact more with some objects. All in all a jaw-dropping experience. Half-Life is back, and VR is finally here for real.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, I mean just wow.  I mean seriously, do I even need to state how good the game is?  I understand some peoples predisposition against the game since it is VR only, but, you have to experience the game to understand why it fits best in VR and it is worth it.  With a flat-screen version, you would not only loose the deep immersion HLA's atmosphere puts you in, but also a lot of features that would be more tedious and annoying on a flat-screen version are instead fun and exciting in VR.  Valve knew they wouldn't get good feedback if they ♥♥♥♥ out some crap, non-physics based VR cash grab, but this is far, FAR from anything even remotely close to that.  You start off in an incredibly detailed area with an astonishing view, interactable objects everywhere and even in the first moments of the game you get to understand why this is belongs in VR.  On a flat screen version, you can't really feel how heavy an item is, but in here, when you pick up something like a watering can, you can tell the weight difference immediately from a can of soda or a box.  The game so far has had a great story line and a great pace of story development.  Almost all dialogue so far has been enjoyable and not at all immersion breaking and really shows off a lot of Alyx and company's characters.  Moving on to level design, where should I even begin?  Every single room looks as if it has been meticulously designed and had hours upon hours that could rack up into multiple days poured into it.  I can't even put into words how good of a job the level designers did on this game, let alone the entire dev team that worked on this.  If you watched any interview with Robin Walker(or any VNN video related to the topic), specifically the interview conducted by Geoff Keighley, then you would know that they analyzed all of the play testers actions, and learned from what they did.  They changed the game according to how they played and reacted, so every level, every room, every single item that was placed and positioned had the player in mind and how are you going to react to it.  This Resulted in the best level design in a VR game I have ever played, and will be so for years to come.  Please, If you have VR, you NEED to get this title, and please, once you realize how great of a game this is leave a good review too because this will help show the dev team that they need to keep creating outstanding, tremendous games like this [no pressure though dev team :) ]  The only thing I would say that is "negative" is that there are a couple of the bugs at the moment.  For a fully physic based game that just released(and compared to the amount of bugs in the V1 version of HL2 and other VR titles), the amount of bugs that I have experienced so far is low, but there are still some.  There have been a couple of janky things that happen, like dropping something in a certain position or the hands messing up when grabbing certain objects, but these are to be expected in a AAA game that just released, mind you it's also in VR, where the player has a lot of more ways to mess with the game and make a situation where things will be wonky.

_childDocuments_.review: You know how they say "the longer you wait for something, the less chance it will meet your long dreamed expectations."? Well this doesn't apply to Half-Life: Alyx. I have been waiting for a new Half Life for years, like many out there. It might not be Half Life 3, but this game is the next best thing. Despite how long it has been, this game still captures the essence of the Half Life universe exactly, but in VR. The enemies, the weapons, the locations, the sound design, and the soundtrack did not stray from the series roots. And it truly feels 100% designed for VR (meaning there is 0 chance this will ever receive a non-VR port). The gameplay is amazing too. While I only used my Index controllers (have the vive wands too), I highly recommend purchasing the Index controllers for this game. Although this is one of the few games that actually utilizes the Index controllers to their full potential, it is a game changer (literally). The immersion factor changes so much by being able to catch and release objects with the gravity gloves by simply grabbing and releasing the controller. For me, this experience alone was worth the price investment into the controllers (especially since you get the game for free for getting the controllers). You also lose health fairly quickly in this game (especially when shot), so it encourages you to use cover when shooting. The experience of aiming down sights and reloading is very satisfying as well.Now for the best part...the story. I'm not gonna give anything away, but this was the biggest surprise to me. Most VR games so far haven't had remarkable story lines (not saying they are usually bad, but a little dull I guess). This is not the case for Half-Life: Alyx. All I'm going to say is PLAY THE OTHER HALF-LIFE GAMES FIRST BEFORE YOU PLAY THIS ONE (if you haven't already). You will thank me later and will bearhug Valve with all your might. Finally, if you are debating on getting a VR headset because you're a huge Half-Life fan and want to play this game, this game is worth it alone. I Mean It. I'll admit that I love VR and have dozens and dozens of games that I love (even though many can be short and feel more like pricey demos), but this is such a great experience and to me is worth the cost of a headset alone.

_childDocuments_.review: I am currently going through my second run of this game and I can already tell it's going to be 100% worth it.It took me awhile to figure out just what made this game so great aside from the graphics, sound design, weapons, ect.But I have realized what it is and it can be summarized into 3 words, "The Gravity Gloves" or "The Russels"Plenty of other VR games that I've played just have an item or weapon magically bend the laws of physics and zip into your hand for VR sake, and while it makes sense to have a feature like this, for comfort and accessibility for those who cannot physically bend over, its always felt so "game-y" to me and too much disbelief had to be suspended in order for something like this to fit.However in Half Life: Alyx, the Gravity Gloves solves this issue and blends perfectly into the half life universe, you have gloves that DOES the magical yanking, but of course looks and context are only half the story for these fun pieces of handwear, because picking up stuff, or "yanking" it from afar is LEAGUES more interactive and engaging compared to the magical, superhuman abilities of just mindlessly pressing a button while pointing at an item and boom, it's there in your hand. HLA requires a sense of timing when it comes to catching an object weather its just a spare magazine you found on the floor or catching a grenade at the apex of it's trajectory and hurling it back at the combine, which is just so flipping cool.It takes skill, attention, and brainpower, And I absolutely love it.Please play this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: This is a masterpiece!!!! OMG!Firstly, I am running this game on my 980Ti with no lag, no problems. I have 16GB RAM and i7-4790K. I have an Oculus Quest headset and using USB 3.0 Anker cable to do the Link to my PC and so far my experience has been flawless.Second of all, from the first moment, it is impossible not to be wowed by this game. The sense of scale (first time I ever felt any VR game really got this 100% right), the layers, the details, the interactivity! OMG! This is like the first time I ran H-L2 back in 2004 and being blown away with the world and the physics. This is the same times 10!! This is undoubtedly the best VR experience currently out there and one of the best gaming experiences I have ever had! I am sooo glad they went ahead and expanded upon everything, adding layers and layers of details, fleshing out the world even more! I didn't think the Source Engine was capable of doing this and I didn't think my set up could handle it either. I am so glad for both working out.Alyx's hands do the thing I want almost 100% of the time and that's amazing. The presence is incredible! Wow!I am tearing up man. Thank you Walker and the team. Thank you Valve!!! I just...I just need more. I need Portal, I need more in H-L universe! You guys nailed it, c'mon Gabe, no reason no to continue now!Edit: How am I expected to enjoy any other game now?! Thanks Valve for ruining everything else!
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the best VR game ever made. The only downside for me is that it makes too many concessions to comfort and accessibility at the expense of immersion. Such as:- Free locomotion is a bit of an afterthought. You really need to use teleportation a lot of the time.- A lot of stuff that could be really scary/unnerving is neutered (e.g. headcrabs don't attack your head, but your torso).- Instead of drawing your weapons from holsters you have to use a menu system, which is bizarre in a VR game.- Human enemies are way too passive.I'm sure all of this was done to make it easier for VR newcomers to get into, and get through, the experience. But I think some potential was lost as a result.Still... it's astoundingly good. I've replayed the base game from start to finish maybe ten times. And when you consider that it also comes with a level-editor and a very convenient system for accessing community-made content, you've got a game that's excellent value despite it's AAA price.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: This is not what half life fans were expecting from valve when it was announced. For many it isn't what they wanted from valve. But I can guarentee that regardless of what you wanted for a new half life game, this is a spectacular experience. The gameplay is fun and intuative, just like all half life games have been. The combat feels exhilerating and fast. For people who have not played in VR before, don't play this game first, it will make all other VR games (except maybe boneworks and saints and sinners) feel sub-par. The game is so well made and every moment is enjoyable. Right from the opening scene looking out on city 17 all the way to opening the vault is full of breathtaking views and stunning sound design. The gritty feel of city 17  has not been lost in the 15 years since we were last there, it in fact has become grittier due to the new Source 2 engine and Valve's ability to design set pieces. This game is well worth the money. I have not played any community workshop maps yet but the fact they exist means the game has infinite re-playability as new stuff is being added for people to play around with.10/10 would reccomend
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: It goes without saying that this is one of the best VR RPG adventure experiences out there, and for good reason, this game was the reason for me buying a valve indexThe Story and detail in this game is absolutely phenomenal, the second you step into the actual game you could spend an hour in the first room just ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ around and enjoying the atmosphere, there's so much unnecessary attention to detail and small interactive things in the world that bring it to life and help to immerse you. The story is fantastic too, getting to see some of my fav Half Life characters in VR in this level of quality is really cool, it really does feel like the next step up from half life 2, and fits very cleverly into the story The game play is so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ cool, the gunplay, the way you can use the gravity gloves in and out of combat, minitool minigames, the upgrade system, it's all so well done. Even the enemies in the game feel organic and smooth, like they're really there and not just fixed animations. The weapons are satisfying and have their own little qwerks and interesting designs. Everything about the gameplay is exactly what you would expect from a VR half life game.I could totally understand why people would give this game a perfect score, but because of a slight few things i personally think are a bit eh in the game that aren't really worth noting in this review, i'll give it a 9.9/10. But you don't need this to read this review to know it's a good game. FIND A WAY TO PLAY THIS, IT'S GUD
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: A preview of the future of AAA VR titles, and a good preview at that. Controls like it should and is simply a blast to play. Gunplay feels right and not always something you can yell at the game over, only blaming yourself. Graphically, the game is a treat. Depending on your card, of course. There are options for graphics, and the recommended 2080 is not a joke. You'll enjoy the game much more with high graphics. It's still perfectly playable on lower-end cards, but go in with an open mind, and expect lots of slowdowns during loading and explosions.On the topic of options, HL:A is filled with lots of comfort and control options, and a fair amount of replayability, albeit not that much outside of achievement and Resin hunting. I have yet to try community maps, but I'm sure I'll spend a good amount of time in them in the future.I don't want to say much else about the game so as not to spoil it, but don't let yourself get spoiled.And if you haven't played any other Half-Life games, make this the last one. It'll be worth your while. Roughly 10 hours.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a game. It's fun. It's in VRPros: -Its a game. A full blown, fun to play, fleshed out with campaign game. Think of a pro that involves a full length game and it probably has it if it's from the story, enjoyment, or gamplay of the game.--I would have liked more firefights. They were frantic and FUN.Cons: -Some VR mechanics are great. Others are questionable. Every gun is a pistol grip? I get it, it's an easy solution to avoid the clunky two handed guns of VR. I don't care that two handed weapons are hard to make feel good, do better. I want to be racking that shotgun!!! Another, teleport jumping? Good for motion sick people but I choose free motion for a reason. -Not really any replay value. You can play through it to try to find all the Resin in the game but at that point it becomes more of an Easter egg hunt in the game rather than the actual game so I wouldn't really count it.-Headcrab zombies enemies just felt like cannon fodder and would be beyond boring if not for being THE head crabs. VR should be moving away from the "well these enemies walk at you" type of things as they're low hanging fruit.It's awesome, its fun, and I hope it's only the tip of the iceberg for VR

_childDocuments_.review: Half Life: Alyx is an amazing game and a true showcase for the VR platform.The combat is exciting, the puzzles are interesting and engaging, exploration is a blast, and the whole experience feels very polished.I played through on an Oculus Quest 2 using a wireless link. Performance was mostly stable, but I did experience a number of crashes and stuttering issues, especially when there was some kind of collision.Overall, the technical issues didn't diminish the experience and I was able to complete the game with few interruptions.I'm a consummate late adopter, and I would not have picked up a VR headset on my own, but I received the Oculus as a gift and read that Half-Life: Alyx was the killer app for VR. It's made a believer of me. I'm very much looking forward to getting my crowbar around the next Half Life VR title and I'm looking forward to seeing the VR platform take off more.

_childDocuments_.review: Holy crap what an amazing experience it was to play this game! If you take your time and soak in the environment and explore the beautifully crafted levels in this game you'll probably spend around 13 hours or so.The pros of this game is its fantastic sound design, some fairly realistic physics to anything that moves, fantastic level design, great performances from all of the characters and some pretty immersive gunplay and some fun puzzles that can sometimes prove to be a bit challenging but none are so difficult that most people couldn't figure out at a glance, be creative. There's a decent variety of enemies from headcrab zombies, Combine soldiers and Ant-lions, but DAMN you'll never want any of those headcrabs to get anywhere near you ESPECIALLY if you have a fear of spiders or anything else that crawls and jumps at you. After thinking about it for a while the only downside I could see to this game is the lack in weapon variety knowing all the cool guns that exist in the Half-Life Franchise. Maybe because the game is on VR that means there could be a few moments where you feel some motion sickness or have to adjust the headset every so often so that you can see further away without it being too blurry but its not too detrimental since most enemy encounters are either close to mid range.

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game worth $1,000? Absolutely YES! Keep in mind that this game also has workshop support and mods are already flooding in. On top of all this, HALF LIFE 3 IS INDEED CONFIRMED!VR is the way of the future. It may not become mainstream in the next 10 years, but neither was PC gaming itself 20 years ago. But there is no feeling that comes close to this. No traditional game could match this experience. It's like describing 4th dimensional geometry.By investing $1000, you're not just getting HLA, you're not just getting a Source 2 modding community, you're not just getting HL3, you're investing in the future of gaming. Industry doesn't grow without financial risks, so if you want cheap and affordable VR, you'll need to invest now. Save your pennies because this game is worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: Best VR game out now.  Admittedly, I am relatively early on in the game, but its all the little things that just click.  In other VR games throwing a grenade is weird.  Either throwing it super far, or dropping it at your feet.  In Alyx the grenade goes exactly how far I'd expect for how fast I'm moving my arm.The simple fact that the world actually interacts with you, ie, if there is a door your hand doesn't float through it, Alyx's hand will stop  and go flat against it.  This little change I found myself stopping my hands on objects naturally even though I physically could push through them.  That weird divide of reality and VR actually shrinks because of this little touch.Loading guns is soooo satisfying.Graphics are insane (I have an Index and a 2080ti so playing on the max settings)So far best moment for me was when I first started getting into shootouts and realized I was ducking behind barricades, and hiding behind a wall leaning out to shoot that I was like, Whoa....this is it.Great game.

_childDocuments_.review: For environment and graphics this game is astounding, the detail, polish and story feels great. There is nothing wrong with how it looks or how the environment feels. But the gameplay is another thing, since I am a greedy bastard I expected a equal roster weapons but there were none, yes you can customize/upgrade them but that does not change how bored i felt after I got the SMG, the same goes with the fact that there are no two handed weapons in the game. Lastly that there is a lack of melee in the game, since Half-Life 2's literal icon for the game is its crowbar it honsestly suprised me that we got no melee, also this game w̶a̶s is suppose to be a physics based game.Talking about combat too, I get that the inventory system is limited, that dosn't really bother me but MY GOD is it annoying that I can't switch out a half used mag for a new one and being able too keep the half used one. Movement is kinda weird, the game was built for teleportation only, whoever thought that was a good idea is an idiot. But luckly enough they added the ability for walking, thank lord they did that cause the teleportation feature is garbage, imagine if you are going through the Jeff area an especially when that headcrab knocks down some bottles, like most people you are gonna freak out, since a giant ugly punking monster is running at your general directiom, this is often gonna mess up your aim with the teleport so you will probably die in most cases. Also I get that they didn't have time to impliment a jump feature but jesus it does really ruin my immersion when I have to teleport from one place to another to "jump".Overall a great game, I rate it 7/10, not to much replayability since the gameplay designs, feel free to bash me in the comments.

_childDocuments_.review: Just mind blowing. It's the first VR game I've played that doesn't feel like a demo, or a tech experiment, or a proof of concept. It's just a great game that happens to use VR. They nailed the movement speed and controls so you move slowly enough that you don't get motion sickness. It has a great balance between combat, puzzles, and some stealth horror, and everything feels fresh because VR is a major part of each game element. The only thing that I think won't age well is opening cabinets and drawers to look for supplies, but for the first few hours it's still fun and interesting to poke around the environments, because it feels so real. This game is the reason to believe VR will succeed, and is not just a passing fad.
