_childDocuments_.review: Overall I'd recommend the game BUT:To start off I'm not a Half-Life fan. My experience with the series was playing like 5 minutes of HL2 to test my family computer when it came out, and a TON of HL1 deathmatch. So none of my opinion has anything to do with the previous games. Ultimately I don't think this game is worth picking up a VR setup for, nor do I think it was worth Valve making this a VR game in the first place (see my negatives section for why). A lot of what I'm finding engaging is the characters and story. It's not much of a breakthrough VR game from a gameplay standpoint (not nearly as much as I'd consider Boneworks to be). It makes use VR nicely in some areas, but I wouldn't say it was necessary considering that it's not pushing it from a gameplay standpoint with physics, or gunplay, or really any features. It IS a solid VR game, but if it wasn't half-life I don't think it would really be that outstanding. Boneworks has certainly spoiled me overall and I was expecting much more from Valve honestly. I'm only disappointed that this game doesn't push their own hardware in ways that other games haven't or done more with.Positives:The highlight of the game I'd say so far is the characters and story. It's pretty immersive and engaging, and has had enjoyable dialogue between Alyx and Russell.The visuals are also very good and the game runs very well too. I didn't notice many performance dips at all while playing (with a gtx 1080 gpu at max settings). The gunplay is very satisfying, and I'd say it matches up to Boneworks on this purely from the point of aiming and shooting, recoil, etc.Negatives:Doesn't push the hardware from a gameplay standpoint. It just doesn't match up to what Boneworks has done with physics and making you really feel present in a space. Movement is very basic. I use full smooth motion and was really disappointed to see that jumping is just teleporting, as is going through smaller crawlspaces or windows, etc. Even falling from a height is either very slow, or simply teleports you to the bottom. I understand people get motion sick (as do I after a while) but I don't see this as a reason to kneecap a game like this. Either add the option somehow or people play in shorter settings, or have a sit-down mode. There isn't nearly enough to movement in this game imo that warrants it to not be a sit-down type game (maybe I missed this option?).Physics and Freedom. There really isn't much especially compared to Boneworks. Things have physics but you're pretty set in stone as to what you can really do with it. As of right now the only thing I've been able to do is use something as a shield, but it hasn't been useful in any scenario against zombies obviously. You can't switch what hand you have your gun in without using a menu, and there's no real reason to pick up things from the environment to use other than the general ammo and health pickups. I wasn't able to hit a zombie with a bottle or brick and have it do anything to it.Controls and how you interact with the world. It's not that great honestly. I don't like how set in stone you are with your gunhand being either right or left from a menu, and I certainly don't like that changing the dominant shooting hand just flips your controls entirely. I'm left handed but why in gods name would I want to move with the right thumbstick then? This could be fixed by more options or manual remapping (I think?) but in general I just don't like how locked in everything seems.Overall negative is what I stated above really. All of this compounds to making the game less like the "tech demo, yet has a compelling story" that I wanted it to be. I was expecting more use out of the index controllers, more physics and more freedom to tackle obstacles. But really you're left with a game that while it *does* use vr, none of the ways are very original or necessary. I understand *why* they made this game a VR exclusive, but I don't think it was worth it with how the game turned out. If this game had really pushed physics, and interacting with the environment with puzzles and whatnot, I would get it. But as it stands it's a VERY enjoyable story and game, but it would probably be just as enjoyable if it *wasn't* in VR.

_childDocuments_.review: Its been so long that I played Half-life, I pretty much forgot the story. In my playthrough however, I quickly remembered all of the lore, play style, and the feel of the game. This was spot on.With Valve, you can really see the way they design their stories, the increasing difficulty, and the eventual outcome. This really reminds me of Portal 2 (I don't think its possible in VR? Might cause me to be super sick?) and the glados interactions throughout. Character Design, Audio, Level Design, interactivity (you cant open every door, but definitely alot!) searching for ammo and resin, this game is amazing. I was using a Valve Index and the Knuckles controllers (waited yearrrrssss for these to finally come out!) and they are amazing. Following were the highlights for me of this setup;1. I can actually read text.2. comfortable!3. the fingers work quite well and don't infuriate me trying to get the controller to recognize what I want (but in some games?!)4. Haptics!5. Gripping!6. Selecting gear and interacting with the environment.One particular note, there were parts of the game I wish I could just escape; they were very intense!!! Chapter 7 for sure. Don't read any spoilers or any reviews, the game needs to be experienced raw.I did find that I just wanted to get through some sections, leaving my feet and legs quite sore having to stand and move around during the play session. As far as the effects of VR, Im not the best at motion sickness in VR, however I chose to have the walking and moving experience with no teleporting (except for jumping) and had zero issues. I was reading that this game may continue on in VR, but seeing the amount of money, time, and people spent on this project, I don't think they would continue. _childDocuments_.review: Not only is this the best VR experience I've ever had, it is quite possibly the best gaming experience I've ever had. I waited until the game was on sale but honestly it is worth the full price. You truly have not experienced the potential of VR until you have played this game. The fact that it is story based gives it replay value and has had me glued to my VR headset. So much so that I find myself forcing myself through discomfort and physical strain just to find out what happens next in the story. Not only is the story amazing but it challenges you to be a critical thinker and find ways to advance further (I found myself using Youtube to find out how to get past one part...damn you Jeff). My most notable wow factors are the looting (which I find myself looking in every nook and cranny for secrets and alternate paths), the weapon upgrading, the various 3D puzzle solving, using the multi tool to follow electricity currents through walls, and the ability to select far away items and flick them up to you can grab them (very satisfying). Also note that I am 9 hours in after only 2 days, and it feels as though I am maybe halfway through the story. A must buy if you have a VR headset.

_childDocuments_.review: There is no argument from me, this is the most polished and immersive VR experience going on any platform. Incredible physics, sound, interface, and story telling combined with AAA graphics means this is not only a worthwhile addition to the franchise, but a groundbreaking work in its own right. I liked the slow pace and humor elements as well, because you need time to just stuff about, enjoy a view, or see how hi you can stack the toilet paper sometimes.The characters are OK but a little straight forward. Alyx herself is chatty and confident, although its amazing how she can happily rip through a few squads of elite soldiers despite having no hazard suit, then be uptight about a little darkness? The other characters are rad. Head crab who is attached to a mannequin is my favourite, but the comedy provided by Russel isn't terrible or too invasive.Fighting the soldiers feels strange. You are a slow mover in this game, and soldiers can sponge those valuable bullets really easy. There are strangely few opportunities to improvise complex but efficient deaths of soldiers for a Half-Life game. I was expecting traps, explosives, improvised melee with the gloves, maybe even throwing or catching things, but mostly it was head-shotting from cover and throwing grenades behind the big guys. At least in VR you actually have to crouch to fit behind cover, so I actually got some squats in for a week.It is quite an accomplishment, and miles ahead of anything else on VR. I actually thought I was going to choke on the alien pollens at one point, however I never felt motion sickness once using the locomotion.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm 8 hours in at Normal difficulty and just started Chapter 6. This game is insanely good. The physics are top notch, I'd say what people expected Boneworks to be but much better. You can always do exactly what you want to do when grabbing an object you'd like to move or lift. Never had it fail on me. The voice acting is superb, good humor, the ambience always fits perfectly the place you're in and really leaves you wary of everything around you. Pretty good scares that make sense, so no cheap jumpscares most horror games resort to. The game looks beautiful, the graphics are stunning and everything just feels so right to do and flows so well. The Gravity Gloves work absolute wonders. Puzzles are really fun to go through and inventory is managed super well. There's very few things that had me go "ehh" and one of them is the headcrabs behavior. They're super scary the first 2 or 3 encounters but after that their pattern becomes so very predictable that you don't feel in danger anymore when you're around them. I wish they would've randomized their attack pattern a little bit, with different timings between snarling and jumping at you or maybe sometimes not even snarl at all and just jump straight away. The other thing is not being able to run with smooth locomotion. It kind of breaks the immersion when you want to run away or run into cover and you have to walk super slow if you don't want to teleport (which if you do, takes the fun and danger out of it). Finally, the falling speed is way too slow, feels weird. Those are just small things that really don't take much from the game and I'd still rate this 10/10 anyday. Looking forward to the remainder of it!

_childDocuments_.review: If there is one game a user with VR headset has to play. It's certainly this. At the time I am writing, Alyx is very much way above the VR competition. While some sacrifices had to be made, to make it a VR title, it's the first game I have played, where the number of advantages of using VR and room-scale movement manages to outweigh these sacrifices.It's also great to see Valve's signature environment storytelling together with the environment leading the player be back with full force. I have really missed that... and yeah, sure  - the latter has its flaws, cause you are always risking the player getting stuck, by not telling him precisely what to do in the area, but nevertheless - when done right (like Alyx does it), I am going to prefer getting stuck than being told what to do especially that - with me now being a game developer - it makes me appreciate how much thought was put to make these levels look so well, tell such great small stories and at the same time not be swarmed with detail to the point, where environment hints become invisible as such putting graphics over gameplay. It is really some fantastic level design work and the number of level design iterations had to be crazy to pull it off.But it's not just story, graphics (as for VR standard), and performance where Alyx shines. The gameplay is a Half-Life's signature mix of action setpieces, first-person cutscenes (where Valve once again, outdone themselves with how naturally these facial animations look, while simultaneously having characters react to the player's actual existence in the world - like come on, it's 2021 now and somehow this is still a problem!) and light environment puzzles, and it's the player to world interaction where everything just *clicks*. Half-Life 2 was already going crazy on having a highly interactive physics system and while pretty much nobody in the industry managed to match Valve's physics precision in over 15 years since Half-Life 2 release, Alyx takes it much farther, somehow managing not to be an outright broken mess. Sure, occasional physics glitches happen (as they pretty much have to with such absurd dependence of physics), but the result achieved by the world objects reacting so naturally to the player's actions is well worth the price. If anything, maybe few more things could be even more interactive (as you often find objects that could work as melee weapons), but at this point - it really is scraping the barrel for issues.If I were to have any major complaint - I guess it's the stability issues I've experienced with SteamVR, where my Index would often freeze (especially during loading) forcing a full game restart. Other than that - this is also one of the smoothest, least vomit-inducing VR experiences I have had so far (to a point, where - if the game manages not to crash - I could be playing it for 2+ hours and not for a moment feel sick).So yeah. If you have VR headset capable of running Alyx - get Alyx!

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely well-crafted game, lives up to the name of the Half-Life franchise. Not only is just playing the game engaging, I just had some of the most fun playing with props and ragdolls and interacting with the phenomenal physics engine. The game runs good at higher settings on a mediocre PC, and would have ran even better had I set them lower. The game also works just fine with the Oculus Quest 2, so worrying about spending $1000 dollars on the Index isn't something you should have to worry about. (unless you hate Facebook) The SDK is a great way to create mods, and is a great hobby to get in to. Although it takes some getting used to coming from Source 1 hammer, it is a direct improvement for one reason. No leaks. Over all, worth the 60 bucks. Thanks, and have fun.Edit: I haven't waited 13 years for a new half-life game, so that might change the perspective.

_childDocuments_.review: I played this with a PSVR, Switch controllers and a fing Kinect on a gtx 1050 and still had fun. Believe me, it isn't that bad.Playing this made me feel the same thing I felt when I played a videogame 20 years ago, pure magic.This is an amazing game, it has some minor problems due to its medium, there are some game design decisions that I do not agree with (specially near the end), but I can understand why those decisions were made. After all, this supposed to be a first time vr experience to a lot of people. Compared to other traditional FPS, HL:A is a slow experience, naturally, you shoot and move a lot less than in the past Half-Lifes, this game is closer to the survival horror genre IMO. During combat situations I had the fun of my life. Personally the scavenging can get a bit tiresome after a while, both physically and mentaly, at least for me, maybe I'm just lazy.This is also the most detailed game I've ever played; visuals (even playing on low), physics and sound truly are next level. Source 2, after 13 years in development, really was worth the wait, this is a high quality game.A thing to notice, this game can be a very strong experience to some players, specially in a specific chapter focused on pure horror. _childDocuments_.review: No Spoilers Review. I have many words for this game and one of them is Phenomenal. The gameplay is top notch and I have come across only two glitches throughout my entire playthrough, but more on that later. In terms of the gameplay, extremely immersive, intuitive, and user friendly. While I enjoy the complexities of the VR game Boneworks, Half Life: Alyx’s less complex mechanics are extremely enjoyable. However, one very infuriating bug I came across was that my left hand disappeared for a period of time, making reloading impossible. Luckily, this bug disappeared after a level switch and will most likely be fixed soon. Otherwise, the mechanics are well suited for experienced VR players and newer ones. I also love the different options this game has for controls. Its nice knowing people with one arm or left-handed people can just as easily play this game. As for the story, it’s very fitting, immersive, and takes a lot of unexpected turns. I’m glad to see valve return to the Half-Life universe and create something truly amazing. Not once throughout the game was a moment dull or dragged out. I loved the ending of the game and was impressed with the creative direction they took. Characters were great too and interesting in their own ways. As for the level design, I never felt lost and the puzzles always felt fair and put up a challenge. The level of detail throughout the game was consistently impressive. Overall, I highly recommend this game to anyone looking for a proper, action-packed VR experience. It is one of the best VR games, and overall games I’ve ever played.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Don't wait. Just buy it. You won't be disappointed. For Valve:Amazing work, don't stop doing what you're doing!Is there a new game+ or a VERY hard difficulty on the way? This was my first VR title (and first Half Life title) and I played hard with 2 vodka bottles up my sleeves from distillery to finish on my first play through. It didn't quite scratch the difficulty itch I was hoping to.. (Removing save anywhere function, random enemy spawn locations, mini game failure consequences [less ammo/items in ammo boxes after failing an unlock mini-game], etc.) Just a couple ideas for a harder difficulty.When is the level editor coming out? We're waiting... and we're stoked!!!Hands down, best VR experience available to date!

_childDocuments_.review: I have waited patiently for VR equipment to mature since the first consumer-level VR headsets were released in 2016.  I did not want to be an early adopter.  The moment I saw this title's upcoming release on Steam was the second I was done waiting.  I got a Samsung Oddessy Plus (LOVE IT! and still use it as of 2023) and bought this game and everyone knows what happens next.  Your video card is not good enough MAOR MONEE PLZ.  Jokes aside, it was an incredible experience and an introduction to VR gaming.  I really hope Valve will give us more HL VR content and, if we're lucky, some Portal VR content as well.  To all the whiners about wanting desktop port, just go buy a refurbished headset off eBay and enjoy the dang game already. 9.7 / 10
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Half-Life: Alyx is truly a worthy successor of what felt like the long forgotten Half-Life series. With the addition of VR gameplay, especially well crafted gameplay by Valve, it exceeds at being a new and fresh Half-Life experience. The story as well is entertaining, enthralling, and justified despite being a prequel to Half-Life 2 that at first glance would have no implications for the overall story of the franchise. The audio and visuals are such a treat as well, with the best graphics I have ever experienced in a VR game, and a fitting and fun soundtrack that is also worth a purchase! If you have VR or are considering purchasing a headset, I can not recommend Alyx enough!
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: A no-brainer for everyone connected to the Half-Life story - that's why I purchased it the day it was released. I feared, however, my typical main issue would be motion sickness - something I usually suffer from when 'walking' or driving on uneven terrain in VR. In Alyx the player may choose among 4 different types of movement control of which one suited me perfectly - and by that my concerns were rendered obsolete.The story, the visuals, the sounds and the overall immersion are awesome and unmet by anything I've personally encountered in VR yet. Do I recommend it? Absolutely!

_childDocuments_.review: After 13 years, this game changes everything. _childDocuments_.review: All I have to say is wow. I don't normally leave reviews for games, but this just impressed me so much that I had to say something. This is a must buy. _childDocuments_.review: Without any doubt or hesitation, the best VR game that exists, full stop.Arguably one of the best games I've ever played.Easily meets and exceeds the extremely high bar set by the Half Life franchise.If you have a VR headset, you must play this game. If you do not own a VR headset, get  of them (200 USD buys a WMR headset right now) and play. Please do not mod the game to play pancake mode (on a monitor). You will lose a massive amount of why this game is so good and so important.Valve set out to solve a lot of design and implementation challenges in VR when they made HL:A. That is how the Half Life franchise exists-- they release a Half Life game when a challenge exists in the video game landscape. HL:A laser-sights these challenges, and knocks them out of the park. There is simply not a better VR experience or game on the market, full stop, period.If you're not a Half Life fan, the game will blow you out of the water. If you ARE a Half Life fan, the game will blow you out of the water and the story will completely catch you off guard. Even if you think you know what's coming, you do not.This is beginning to ramble a bit, but I'm still coming off the high from finishing the game. Buy this game. It is likely the most impressive and well-designed games I have ever played. 10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: Quick take - Have VR? Must buyLong take - There is nothing I can say that has not already been said. Half-Life:Alyx is one of, if not the, best VR games available. At the time of the review, I played with a WMR head set (HP) and even at that entry level, it was wholly captivating to an extent rarely achieved. More importantly, that level of enjoyment is sustained throughout the whole experience. Head crabs are terrifying... and in the dark much more so. This is no walk in the park, you are challenged mentally both with puzzles as well as being put through conditions that make you fear walking around corners or opening doors. Leave no stone un-turned and no locker, box, crate cranny or corner unexplored. You will want to take it all in, just as I have been.Enjoy the new bar of VR gaming.

_childDocuments_.review: My god, I was thrilled to continue the game even though it was something else completely. I have to say, the mechanics, experience and that final sequence are not something you can recreate outside of VR, and anybody watching the game on stream really is missing out. The game would simply not be fun in a flat version, and even though some of the physics and gunplay doesn't feel as cool as Boneworks(no jump button, no running, snap only), the story will absolutely make up for it. As far as artstyle goes, idk what kind of drugs they are doing at Valve, but it is the most incredible looking VR game, nice blend between photorealism and nice character art. The audio design for gun sounds leaves a bit to be desired, but the ambient noise is right up there, more than a few occasions I had a small panic attack from ambient sounds I thought were enemies.The story, starts off okay, really doesn't seem like a gigantic deal until you reach one specific point in the story and I guarantee you will rush to the end from that point on. I highly, highly recommend the game to anyone who cares about the franchise. It's starts off as some sort of spinoff quest and at about the last two hours becomes something you need to experience as a Half-Life fan. The repercussion of these events leave a lasting change on the franchise.

_childDocuments_.review: It's been 12 long years. 12 full years and a few extra months and Valve decided to release a VR only Half-Life prequel with demanding specs with a voiced protagonist. And somehow, not only is it a fantastic game but it's a worthy addition to the Half-Life series.Pros- The visuals are phenomenal, everything is beautifully crafted. Props from HL2 are recreated with high attention to detail, and new assets fit right in with the series as previous games established.- The best VR gameplay I've experienced. It's a full, real video game with highly polished mechanics and it's clear that lots of thought went into transitioning the Half-Life experience. For example, there are 3 weapons, but they all have a good use and upgrades to keep them important throughout the entire game. Magazines and other important items glow to let you see them easily, health packs are replaced with small items you can keep with you while you play, and they've added real interactivity to things that used to be a single button press, without getting too complicated. It's intuitive and easy to understand.- The writing, especially dialogue, is some of the tightest I've seen in a game in years. I didn't like Portal 2's focus on story and cutscenes and jokes but unlike there, you aren't forced to stop and listen outside of a few very short scenes. The jokes are better, the characters feel natural. For the overarching story, everything fits together and gives the player clear motive and a reason for what they're doing at all times. It straddles the line between being big and feeling like a real accomplishment without making past events in the series seem smaller than it in comparison.- Music is great, it fits the series very well and that's made clear when the game starts playing music from past Half-Life games alongside it. The music fits the encounters and scenarios it's played in, and it's just really well made in general.- Plenty of fangasm moments that reference older games and made me freak out while playing. Cons- I dunno, there aren't many. New voice actors for existing characters are a bit jarring, but not much can really be done about that.If your PC can handle it and you have access to VR, buy this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

_childDocuments_.review: This is hands down the best game I have ever played and is now my favorite game of all time. The VR experience on its own is leagues ahead of anything I've experienced before and the gameplay is phenomenal. As a huge Half-Life fan, the story aspect is even better. I felt right at home back in City 17 and am hoping another installment (Half-Life 3?) to be on its way soon. Another one for the books for Valve.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright. First Review here. I do Architectural Visualization for a living, and am usually using VR for those purposes. But, i'm also an old gamer, and had to give this a shot (you know, because Half-Life). To be clear, I'm used to seeing photo realistic architectural scenes in VR, and I know the work that goes into games like these.This game completely blew my nipples off. They are on the floor. The attention to detail here is incredible. The animations are perfect, the interaction is insane. Nothing looks like an afterthought. To be honest the ONLY thing I dislike is that the game is actually scary, and I sometimes panic and twist around in awkward positions, probably just how I would in real life in a situation like that. and I'd be zombie for sure.If you've got a VR headset, this is THE game that takes it to the next level. Highly recommend. Will show all my friends.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR, Yes. Buy it. Best VR Game I've honestly ever played, nothing has quite topped it for me.This game is by far one of the best games I've ever played in Virtual Reality, if not *the* best. The story is great, at least coming from someone who had not played any other half life game prior to owning this. The environments, the lighting, the sound design, the music, just about everything was wonderful and you could tell this game was made for VR. The world just feel so real to be in, even from just the first section where you're able to draw on the windows with the markers. I feel like I can't even really express how it feels to be in the world of this game. The darkness actually makes you feel tense and even a bit scared while you're trying to find your way out while being chased by headcrabs. Getting jumped on by a headcrab is a terrifying experience, gravity gloves are such an amazing tool to have and I love using them even if it's just to pick up the insane amount of props that you're able to interact with. Without spoiling anything, Jeff is SUCH a cool dude and really added a lot for me personally. I thought it was such a great design choice and honestly I really can't recommend the game enough. If you happen to buy VR this is one hundred percent a must have, even if you have never played anything Half Life related before.Edited -I recently replayed this again after so many months to pick up the last of the few achievements I needed to get 100%, the gnome run included and I'm still surprised just how good it feels.It's had some updates since I had played to include minor things like liquid in bottles and honestly it just all adds to the experience. I didn't think it would really change much but after picking up the first bottle and seeing the liquid inside move exactly like how it would was a really weird feeling. It almost felt to me like it had real weight to it even though I was just holding the controller in reality. They also added in a developer commentary mode to explain some game related stuff that you're able to pick up and listen in on, I found a lot of it really interesting and it might be worth revisiting if that sort of thing could interest you. In my original review I had said that the only downside I had was due to the index controllers randomly grabbing and dropping items by itself. This is not really the case, I think I just wasn't used to them at the time since I had gotten my index a few weeks before playing... Everything felt really smooth now since I've had a ridiculous amount of time in VR since playing so I've gotten used to it by now.

_childDocuments_.review: Two words to describe this game, "BLOWN AWAY".  Right off the bat first thing I noticed was the amazing graphics and how polished everything looks.  The attention to details is crazy for a VR game, from cars, furnitures, and everything that you can interact with.  The gun feels great to fire and has a great feedback.  Upgrade system for the gun is cool too, feel like something out of a dead space game but in VR and interactive.  Voice acting is good and audio is amazing.  Physics is so fun in this game.  There was a zombie hanging from a window and I literally grab both his ankle and pushed him over.  A lot of things in the world you can interact with and the text are really clear and easy to read.  I am not a huge Half life fan but I am a valve fan and love VR.  This title is the title that will change VR and make people want to go out and buy a headset.  The game optimization is really good.  I can run it stable on High settings @ 120fps solid on my INDEX with a 2080ti.  I get zero motion sickness and I feel i can play this game for hours without stopping.  Great job Valve!!!

_childDocuments_.review: Currently the best VR game out. If you play it, just be ready for other VR games that are currently out to not be as good. This will be hard to top. Fantastic addition to the Half Life series but you don't need to have played any of them to enjoy this honestly. Gave me fear of heights, chills, goosebumps, at certain points I needed to catch my breath, and some of the best stress and panic a game can induce. I felt like a child enjoying video games again for the first time. Please make Half Life 3 with or without VR.

_childDocuments_.review: If you took away the VR aspect then Half Life hasn't advanced in 20 years to be honest. A lot of the game is indoors, down narrow corridors. Limited confrontations with Combine, no AI on enemies by the look of it.However, it is VR and that changes everything. The gun play is superb and this is the finest implementation of VR to be found anywhere. An essential game.

_childDocuments_.review: * * * WARNING * * * This review contains information about the ending of Half Life 2: Episode 2.The most wonderful gaming experience of my life. I've just finished it, and bawled my eyes out at the ending. I think you'd need a heart of stone not to, and I believe that anyone else who, like me, had pretty much given up hope of the story ever continuing will understand and feel the same. Damn, I'm getting sentimental in my old age!I'm pushing 60, and have been playing Half Life games for over 20 years. Shortly before this one was released I replayed HL2: Episode 2 for the first time in several years; I find the sense of triumph and achievement after the final, frantic Strider battle in that game, and the subsequent launch of the rocket that closes the portal, so powerful that I can no longer bring myself to watch Eli's death and Alyx's heartbreak, and have to quit before the end.Thank you for this game, Valve, from the bottom of my heart. It's a masterpiece of game design _and_ story-telling. In technical and gameplay terms you've hit the ball clean out of the ground, just as you did with Half Life and HL2. I spent hundreds of pounds on an Oculus Rift S headset and some major hardware upgrades just to play this game, and it was worth every penny. You've made an old man very, very happy.Side note: the text box into which I've typed this review flags up mis-spelt words, but right-clicking on them doesn't invoke options to correct them, in the way other sites' spellcheckers do. Somehow, that strikes me as _so_ 'Valve'; it's as if they're saying, "We'll point out what you've done wrong, but we won't tell you how to fix it"!

_childDocuments_.review: Half Life Alyx is not a perfect VR game, but it is one of the first VR games I've felt really shows what VR can do as a medium. The pacing of the game reminded me less of Half Life, and more of Bioshock. I spent a lot of time digging through the environment for any spare bullets, thinking if I couldn't reload my pistol that my next encounter with the Combine would be my last. The writing is phenomenal and keeps you engaged, and every nook and cranny in the game has secrets hiding in it. Half Life Alyx makes a very strong case that it is the best VR game made to date, and anyone who has the means to play this game would almost certainly not regret it. Valve has once again, raised the bar.

_childDocuments_.review:
Half-Life: Alyx is Valve's VR return to the Half-Life series. It's the story of an impossible fight against a vicious alien race known as the Combine, set between the events of Half-Life and Half-Life 2. Playing as Alyx Vance, you are humanity's only chance for survival. The Combine's control of the planet since the Black Mesa incident has only strengthened as they corral the remaining population in cities. Among them are some of Earth's greatest scientists: you and your father, Dr. Eli Vance. As founders of a fledgling resistance, you've continued your clandestine scientific activityperforming critical research, and building invaluable tools for the few humans brave enough to defy the Combine. Every day, you learn more about your enemy, and every day you work toward finding a weakness.

ABOUT GAMEPLAY IN VR:

Valve's return to the Half-Life universe that started it all was built from the ground up for virtual reality. VR was built to enable the gameplay that sits at the heart of Half-Life.

Immerse yourself in deep environmental interactions, puzzle solving, world exploration, and visceral combat.

Lean to aim around a broken wall and under a Barnacle to make an impossible shot. Rummage through shelves to find a healing syringe and some shotgun shells. Manipulate tools to hack alien interfaces. Toss a bottle through a window to distract an enemy. Rip a Headcrab off your face and throw it at a Combine soldier.

Extra content for Index owners
Customers who have purchased Valve Index hardware by the end of 2019 will have access to unique bonuses starting early next year:

* Explore environments from Half-Life: Alyx in your SteamVR Home space
* Alternate gun skins to embellish Alyx's arsenal
* Special Half-Life: Alyx-themed content for Counter-Strike: Global Offensive and Dota 2

Community-built environments

* A set of Source 2 tools for building new environments will ship with the game, enabling any player to build and contribute new environments for the community to enjoy. Hammer, Valve's level authoring tool, has been updated with all of the game's virtual reality gameplay tools and components.
_childDocuments_.name: Half-Life: Alyx

name: Deep Rock Galactic
detailed_description: Roadmap, Publishing, Game Editions and Discord Game Editions STANDARD EDITION The standard edition is simply the base version of Deep Rock Galactic, nothing more, nothing less. DELUXE EDITION Get the DELUXE EDITION to unlock the base game as well as three packs of Cosmetic DLC: The awesome MEGACORP, DARK FUTURE, and DAWN OF THE DREAD Packs! MASTER EDITION Includes ROUGHNECK, RIVAL TECH, and ROBOT REBELLION packs, on top of everything in the DELUXE EDITION. DWARVEN LEGACY The full package - includes the base game, all Cosmetic Packs, the Supporter Pack, and the full game soundtrack split over two volumes. About the Game Deep Rock Galactic is a 1-4 player co-op FPS featuring badass space Dwarves, 100% destructible environments, procedurally-generated caves, and endless hordes of alien monsters. 1-4 PLAYER CO-OP Work together as a team to dig, explore, and fight your way through a massive cave system filled with hordes of deadly enemies and valuable resources. You will need to rely on your teammates if you want to survive the most hostile cave systems in the galaxy! 4 UNIQUE CLASSES Pick the right class for the job. Mow through enemies as the Gunner, scout ahead and light up the caves as the Scout, chew through solid rock as the Driller, or support the team with defensive structures and turrets as the Engineer. FULLY DESTRUCTIBLE ENVIRONMENTS Destroy everything around you to reach your goal. There is no set path so you can complete your mission your way. Drill straight down to your objective or build an intricate network of paths to explore your surroundings -- the choice is yours. But proceed with caution, you don’t want to stumble into an alien swarm unprepared! PROCEDURALLY GENERATED CAVE NETWORK Explore a network of procedurally generated cave systems filled with enemies to fight and riches to collect. There’s always something new to discover and no two playthroughs are alike. HIGH-TECH GADGETS AND WEAPONS Dwarves know what they need to bring to get the job done. This means the most powerful weapons and the most advanced gadgets around - flamethrowers, gatling guns, portable platform launchers, and much, much more. LIGHT YOUR PATH The underground caves are dark and full of terrors. You will need to bring your own lights if you want to illuminate these pitch-black caverns.

Do you enjoy intense music along with a beautiful but simplistic art style that really sets the mood? Then this game is for you! _childDocuments_.review: The game that keeps on giving.I've played this game for the first time back when it first launched, and oh boy has this game come a long way.The developers are constantly pushing free updates, adding more content into the game, keeping it alive and fresh.Deep Rock Galactic offers you EASILY one of the best co-op experience today, and I promise you, you won't be disappointed.After a mission or two of slamming dreadnoughts, detonators and smaller alien bugs alike, whilst collecting minerals. You'll then find yourself in the main hub with your friends. You go to the bar, order a beer that'll buff you up for the next mission, walk right next to the jukebox to set the mood and see which one of your friends dances the best. You gulp down your beer whilst dancing, decide to go to the bar again, and order some beers and down them all. You'll find yourself seeing in double or even triple. You start playing catch with an empty beer mug, or a barrel with your friend. Or even attempting to play the barrel hoop game, and failing horribly, then rage quitting and jumping into the hoop yourself, then finding yourself in the med-bay not 5 seconds later. You then get out the med-bay, go the upgrade station, use the minerals and credits you've earned from the previous missions you've completed, give your guns or equipment some nifty upgrade. Then going to the shop, customizing your dwarf with some new armor and a fluffy beard that smells purely of testosterone. You select the next mission, board the rocket, you complete the mission successfully. Rinse and repeat.Do yourself a favor and grab a friend or two on this amazing journey. I bet that you and your friends will end up going "Just one more!" till you both realize it's 3 AM. We need more indie developers like Ghost Ship Games that pour their love and passion into their games.

Even in a team of just 2, this game has an immense amount of charm and fun in store. From the intense thrill of running away from a bulk detonator that just dug up behind you, to the quiet reflection time that mining morkite gives you, this game manages to be my Zen zone and a whole ton of fun all at the same time. Every co-op lover on earth should own this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Deep Rock is a fantastically realized game. In my 1100 hours at time of review, I have played it consistently since picking it up, and it has been both a comfortable game to return to, a place to challenge myself to do better, and somewhere I let my creativity go in the form of mods and certain gamemodes.  The core loop is dropping into a randomly-generated cave, with varied biome themes or mission types, then searching for minerals to collect from the walls while fighting off the local wildlife. Eventually you collect the minerals you need, or repair the machines you came back to recover, or destroyed a boss-like enemy containing a cache of data you're there to recover, resulting in a dash to the escape pod and a (hopefully) triumphant return.What keeps me coming back to DRG is the sheer sense of exploration, the never-seen-it-twice wonder of "wow, what on earth is this" that some caves elicit, and the excellent combination of team-oriented equipment each of the four classes carries with it. When my friends play for twenty hours and say "Well I've seen it all, haven't I?", the answer is a resounding !NO!, you have not. The game has barely begun to open up to you, and the true depth of customization doesn't reveal itself until you promote your first character at level 25. Once that happens, a slew of new options opens up, and the rabbit hole that is weapon overclocks (additional mods which change the basic functionality of a weapon), Deep Dives / Elite Deep Dives (multi-mission campaigns which reward overclocks & cosmetics), and extra difficulty options which push your skills to the limit (and beyond, if you want to use difficulty mods).Each class has three primary weapons, three secondary weapons, and three grenade options as of the April 28th, 2022 patch, and now the game has DLSS / FSR compatibility as well, meaning higher framerates and sharper images than the previous TAA implementation allowed for. Did I mention you can customize your pickaxe? or your little robot friend that follows you around in 'solo' missions? No? Because there's even more out there to mess around with, and I haven't even gotten to talking about all the depth of buildcrafting possible with the various weapon mods and how they interact with one another.Deep Rock is, to me, the perfect game to play when I just want something to do, with whatever kind of stakes I feel I need at the time, and it asks only as much as I want to give it of me. I can sweat in an EDD with pubbies or solo and chill at hazard 2, where death is such a far-flung possibility that falling off a ledge is more lethal. The game world is positively dripping with character, and every time my dorf waltzes up to the bar and rings the bell for the robotic bartender, I snicker a little inside at the absurdity of it, while loving the simple joy of this alternate space. The environment is so consistent within itself, between the post-industrial horror of a space station mining sentient life from a dangerous planetoid, to the bored-yet-frustrated handler who speaks to you throughout your missions, and back to the station where your dwarves relax in the interminable time between drops, everything works together and just feels like it could be real, despite the ridiculous nature of it.Coffee Stain has a reputation for good coop games, and if you haven't played Deep Rock yet, you owe it to yourself to hop on with a few friends (or alone, and join some public games!) and let the caves of hoxxes guide you to a memorable experience. Rock and Stone!

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not huge into shooter style games, but Deep Rock Galactic has really impressed me and swayed me to rethink my stance on the genre.The game is first and foremost a really enjoyable co-op game and although you can play it solo, the real meat of the fun comes from getting down into the hell pits cave systems of Hoxxes with friends (or randoms) and having a jolly.There are four distinct classes to take on, the Gunner, Engineer, Scout and Driller. They can all shoot bugs, they can all mine minerals but it is the unique support structures they bring to the team that make them shine. This game is about sticking together and leaving no dwarf behind.You all descend into a procedurally generated cave system of varying length and difficulty with an objective to complete. It may be mining minerals, collecting eggs, destroying big bugs (or something else) and this is what you need to focus on as a team. However there are unique mini objectives you can find in certain missions and these are randomly created to boot. The aim is to get in, get the job done and get out alive.The game marries two distinct modes together, a calmer mining game where you must work together to traverse the biomes of Hoxxes to get the most minerals out to get a bigger pay check and a fast paced combat game where swarms (akin to Left for Dead) of bugs descend upon you to rip your beer soaked beards off. Its the switch and flow between the two modes that really makes this game enjoyable, and keeps a pace going.There are tons of customisations for your miners, weapons and armor so you can make the most insane looking miner ever seen.Some may find the missions repetitive, but since they are procedurally generated and look downright beautiful in their aesthetics, it is easy to chalk that potential complaint off. I must add that the developers are really on the ball with patching and adding content and aim to add more content post release. I have faith in them from what I have seen to date.If you are looking for a fun, co-op game where you can drink beer with your dwarf (or leaf lover) buddies and then get down and dirty in a mine filled with flesh eating bugs then I highly recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Quite possibly my favourite co-op shooter of all time. It's a really solid teamwork-based game, where co-ordinated teams will quickly find themselves excelling in missions. There is a lot of different mission types and weapons that behave differently, so it's hard for the game to become stale, especially with the game still being actively updated.What I love most about it, is that each class has its place. While you can stack classes, I often prefer to have every class because they have a tool that is often needed, and it makes missions so much more fluid. They appear simple on the surface, but each has its own nuance and advanced techniques that make you fall in love with certain classes harder than others. I genuinely believe there is a class for everyone.If you like Dwarves, silly voice lines, lots of cosmetic options, and solid co-op first person shooter experiences, you will love this game.(also there is a boardgame version of it, if you wish to get your fix in a different form).14/09/2023 - Having played the boardgame a lot, I recommend both heavily!

_childDocuments_.review: Rock and stone! I played this pretty much all night. I went from not knowing what was going on and being quite confused and frustrated to semi sorta figuring some stuff out. Reading the map is something I definitely need to get better at, but from what I've played of just the Scout class so far, it's a lot of fun. A lot more fun than Darktide was and maybe still is. I went to go check it's updates and saw a bunch of people saying to come play this instead, so I did. Mainly after seeing there was 20k active players at that time and assuming if I got lost, the other players could help me find my way. I was right.My first 3 or 4 missions, I didn't really know what I was supposed to be doing and I was just going around mining the shiny looking stuff and trying to follow the other players. After that, I was starting to figure out how to unlock upgrades for my gear and unlock passive and active perks to make the game easier and more fun overall. Perks like being able to instantly revive a downed player during a match or hover in the air for a few seconds or make enemies take damage when they melee strike you. The different weapon upgrades can increase your damage and boost your ammo capacity and the gear upgrades can do the same as well as boost your max health. All things that help make the harder runs more manageable just like in other games of this genre, but unlike those games, it has a pretty good and rewarding feeling progression and cosmetic system.I feel like even when I fail a mission, I'm still being rewarded somewhat for the effort I put in-and during missions, there is plenty of side content to do like gathering the nitra and gold deposits or whatever special resource spawns in that biome/map type. That's another thing I think this game does really well is how many different map types/biomes there are and how different they look and feel from each other. From the icy region that has random blizzards that roll thru and obscure your vision, to the desert looking region with a lot of easily dug thru sand to the swampy region with a lot of mushrooms and hanging green growth.That doesn't even touch on the 7 or so different mission types I think I did. My favorite surprisingly being the escort mission which notoriously sucks in almost any game. I liked riding the drill and repairing it and getting fuel for it and protecting it at the end while it did it's thing. Every part of that mission was a blast. There are also other missions like grabbing alien eggs, mining a specific resource, repairing an abandoned drop pod, building some pipelines to process liquid materials you need to extract-so many different mission types in so many different map types with at least so far a few different enemy types and I haven't even promoted one of my classes yet or unlocked all the different types of assignments.It may sound daunting to hear you have to complete 10 missions to even unlock the assignments and all the map regions, but it only takes a couple of hours to get thru that and by the time you're done, you'll have basically gone thru the game's version of a tutorial and gotten a feel for how to unlock all the different things you'll be using in the game's many modes as well as what to do during each of them. There's also what looks like a seasonal battle pass, but I don't even hate that cause it looks like a lot of cool cosmetic items and earning some sort of tokens that you can use to pick various cosmetics you'll unlock in addition to the stuff you get just for leveling your way thru the pass-and none of it seems locked behind a "buy the battle pass" paywall.The only cosmetics that look locked behind a paywall are the ones you see there on the store page and given how much is already in the game and how often they seem to put those cosmetics on sale for insanely cheap-cheap enough to actually feel like a microtransaction to a cheap miser like myself-I don't mind having or adding more of those paid cosmetics. They clearly keep also adding cool free cosmetics you can earn in game alongside it. I already have one for my scout class. A weird, living purple crystal looking thing that looks like it's taking over my shotgun.Speaking of, the Scout class getting a grappling hook, flare gun, assault rifle, and shotgun feels like a perfect class. You've got the visibility in the dark caves, the mobility to zip around them, and 2 different guns to handle threats. I know the other classes are useful and have their uses/special traits, but I love this Scout. In summation, i gotta say, I regret sleeping on this game and not giving it the proper time and attention cause it's probably gonna be my new favorite game in this genre.

_childDocuments_.review: DRG is a game that has eluded me for a while. Let me explain;I've known its existence for pretty much since it launched in early access on Steam and a friend of mine was an early adopter. He told me to check out the game, but for some reason I wasn't convinced. The concept of the game was surely unique, but the YouTube videos I initially saw didn't really make me all that enthousiastic for it for some reason. So I decided to hold off.Fast forward to October 2020, the game has been officially released since May and recently my mate started to mention it again and as I am stuck at home due to COVID I thought it was a great moment to finally try out the game.Man, have I been so wrong and foolish! In only five days I have clocked over 40 hrs of gameplay! It's become my game of the year instantly and I have been a fool for not having started playing sooner!I still think YT footage often does not do a good job of selling the game, though. Like, VR its something you just have to experience before you truely see its a gem of a game.Several reasons make it such a great game:1) Community; first and foremost the community is excellent! Apart from a few non-communicative players, I've mostly ran into friendly, co-operative and fun teammates.The community has developed their etiquette which is fun; touch the dice for good fortune, always greet a newly arrived team member, killed a big bug-> rock and stone, finished a goal -> rock and stone! Host buys everyone a round at the virtual bar. Things like this really add to the experience and fun.2) Randomized maps: even though you play a finite set of mission types, the map is always randomized and can be made from several different biome types. It makes for interesting gameplay on each and every mission. On top of that there are random secret rooms and events on most maps (perhaps all?).3) Scalability: the game lets you play what your mood dictaces; play a low hazard mission to just relax and farm resources, or a high hazard one or deep dive to get the blood pumping. Your choice.4) Progression: the game offers several tiers worth of character levelling, however this does not mean you can endlessly upgrade weapons. In fact, even low level players can add something to a group, regardless wether the rest is much higher in level.Most weapon and skills will be unlocked rather early in your character's career, but as you gain levels you can promote into other tiers (Bronze, Silver, Gold, Platinum, Diamond, Legendary, 3x 25 levels in each tier).I haven't got enough experience yet to know what the different tiers unlock, but the first tier unlocked specific events for me that I can now activate when I find them on the map in a mission.I assume the system will evolve as you level up.5) Developers: these guys are a small team (20, last I checked) and are super dedicated to their game and its community. Constructive feedback is often replied to by one of the devs on Discord and Reddit (these two I frequent, perhaps there are more) and good community suggestions have been known to be implemented into the game.So in short; very fun objective based cooperative gameplay on randomized maps with 4 classes to choose from who all play very differently and in a non-toxic overall friendly community.Oh and dwarves... no leaf lovers, Dwarves! And beer! For Rock and Stone! ... and Karl! Try it! You will not be dissapointed if this sounds at all even mildly entertaining!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is awesome on so many levels!I m not going to go deep into how it looks, but more about how playing the game feels like.And it feels great. _childDocuments_.review: This game saved my life.I am 25.My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and adopted our son together. They are now both 4 years old.When we were going through our separation, I found myself lost and miserable. I was self destructive. I got so mad one day from everything spiraling out of my control that I punched some concrete in a moment of overwhelming emotion. That caused me to break my 5th metacarpal in my right hand... my working hand... my games hand.. the hand that I held and carried my children to bed with.. The hand I desperately needed to make sure I could continue to provide.After learning of the severity of my self-inflicted damage, I was borderline broken. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man with no history of depression or anxiety. I have never had fits of rage, or been one to break down and cry, but I was in a low spot that just really buried me from being able to see the light on the other side.Having nothing better to do, I searched for a game I could play, ONE HANDED while I recovered. I somehow stumbled upon this game and read some of the reviews. I decided that it had to be worth a shot... I must admit, I didn't beat the game, or play nearly as long as some of you. In fact, I may have only played this game a day or two.. With that being said, after doing so, I had a new found joy and hope for life. I was able to put behind me the pain and suffering that had been cast over me. I was able to experience other peoples joy and happiness. I was able to see the fruits of my "labor". I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥ing minutes to this music long enough to realize that I was going to be okay.After coming to that realization, I turned the game off, and I went back to work. It hurt my hand like hell but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so damn sorry for myself, and I became the father I needed to be in that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving as.Today, I am close friend with my kids mother. We don't fight, or argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents, and friends.I now have 3 kids. My third child is, wait for it, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my own separation, and we just stumbled in to each others life unexpectedly. We have been in a relationship for a year now, and are very happy together.Moral of the story, you never know what life holds in store for you, and if I would have given up when all the odds were stacked against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.Thank you

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun co-op game. Endlessly replayable. Each mission is randomly generated and the mechanics make for good pacing every mission with intense moments of combat and calm downtime spent mining. Like other good multiplayer games, each player serves an essential role, so teamwork happens naturally even without communication. This game is also constantly being updated with new content for free. This is both a good and a bad thing, since some of the content is great like new biomes, new missions, new weapons. A lot of the content is unnecessary bloat though. Pointless unlocks that you have to grind for. XP bars on top of XP bars. Incremental stat upgrades and perks and items that just muddy the waters and distract from the core gameplay. You can argue that all of this can be ignored, and I do try to ignore it, but it's still there and I think the game would be better served without it. Keep it simple. The Left 4 Dead games have none of that stuff and tons of people still play them to this day.I definitely recommend the game since it's a great game, but I suggest picking it up sooner rather than later, before the feature creep gets out of control.

_childDocuments_.review: I am dwarve. An engineer. With my three fellow miners I drilled down deep into the rock to get the precious gems my people desire. We got out of our drop pod and swarmed the cave. It was all gloomy, wet and it smelled like mushrooms. We digged trough a number of chambers until we found our first gold deposit. We cheered, got the loot and that was the time when the rattling noises started. Dozens of bugs crawled our way and I just barely had the time to set up my sentry guns in order defend us. Both guns bled their lead into the bodys of those monsters. Minutes into the fight I looked at the sentries. Gun 1  was on 20 ammo, Gun 2 on 50. BLAM! BLAM! Gun 1 on 5, second on 20. BLAM! BLAM! first one is dry, second on 10... but it was just enough, the stream of bugs ended shorty before our ammo ran out. Maybe they gave up. We didnt though... We dug deeper...Deep Rock Galactic is the miners dream! From the trailers I expected greatness and the game delivered. The content the game already has is shiny and polished already and there seems to be more to come.The game features matches with up to 4 coop dwarves in suprisingly nice looking generated caves where you explore, fight and mine. The more time you spend in the caves the more likely a failure becomes, but the more stuff you bring home.I havent encountered bugs, just some connection issues. If you remotely like the idea of this game: Buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: I have played DRG since soon after it was available as Early Access. It's greatest strength is the procedurally generated levels in its different biomes. Every level is a new adventure in some deep and interesting cave. You definitely get the odd level that sticks in your memory, when you're struggling for ammo the whole time and just trying to get the job done.The creators are great at taking onboard player feedback and have always communicated a strong content roadmap, giving players lots of assurance about great stuff that is coming. This is a game that you can always come back to, because content updates happen regularly enough that even if you go a month or so without playing, you'll find something new when you pick it up again!

_childDocuments_.review: Not often do I play a multiplayer game and love it as much as the singleplayer games in my library; there's a lot of stuff this game does, and it does it all well.I describe this game as a mixture of  and  Although it isn't the child of these games, it does take the best bits from both of them - the nice looking aesthetics that ASTRONEER has are present in this game, alongside the encouragement of teamwork (from L4D2) by, not limited to, having a great synergy between the different classes and their functions.Surrounded by AAA games and corporate developers, it's rare to find such a great indie game, with such great developers. _childDocuments_.review: Dwarves.  Dwarves in space.  Space Dwarves...Space Doorves!You work for the Deep Rock Galactic Mineral Trading Company, utilizing the latest and greatest in space excavation mining equipment, with one simple goal in mind:  mine the minerals of the planetoid, Hoxxes IV.  No one else has rights to the planetoid but you and your dwarven brethren and the company you work for.Dive deep into subterranean caverns of various flora and fauna, and combat the natural insectoid inhabitants of Hoxxes IV who want nothing more than to chew on your doorvan keester.  Find the myriad of minerals around these deep, dark caverns, collect them, and extract them...or die trying for the glory of Deep Rock Galactic!Play by yourself with a little robot companion named BOSCO, or bring along up to three other dwarven friends to face off against the worst of your nightmares:  corporate greed.  Equip yourself as up to four classes:*Heavy Gunner, using big guns, ziplines, and explosives.*Engineer, assisting your teammates using a platform-scaling foam gun, shotguns and advanced technology weapons, and maneuverable turrets.*Driller, with drilling arm-cannons to quickly dig tunnels through the depths, and a host of explosives, fire and cryo weaponry.*Scout, with speed and maneuverability as your skill set and survival, using a grappling hook to reach high-or-far spots in a zip, precision-based weaponry, and support-based throwables.As you play, level up your chosen classes, buy perks for various playstyles.  When you reach Level 25, take on a quest to Prestige your chosen Doorve (reset to Level 1, but keep all bought perks and item/weapon upgrades).  Choose from a variety of mission types:  from general mining, drilling station defense, to extractions of specific resources, and even hunting the biggest, baddest baddies on Hoxxes IV.So jump on in, dive deep down...and GET YOUR ROCK ON, DOORVES! \o/

_childDocuments_.review: I picked up DRG a couple of months after it debuted in early access. Early access titles have been hit and miss the past couple of years. Thankfully, I am able to say that DRG has fulfilled the persona of a game that justifies the early access.The gameplay loop is relatively simple. Dig, mine and shoot. There is only so much variety between 4 classes, but DRG managed to present an enjoyable progression and incentive to do so over the years. And it continues to do so. This is among the best aspects of DRG.DRG is great with friends. Solo play is satisfactory... that's about it. The meat of the content is the cooperation, for without that, this game would struggle to stay afloat. This game is worth getting if that is of interest to you.DRG followed it's road map pretty well, and the game has improved so much over the years. The game is almost not even recognizable compared to when it came out.If Deep Rock only had a year earlier for its release, I would even endorse as a game of the decade. Wait, it's a new decade... Right. Yeah, let's go with that. On may 13th, I call this a game of the decade 2020-2029. I don't care if this sounds stupid. DRG is worth it. 10/10; and ROCK AND STONE.

_childDocuments_.review: Dwarven Delight: A Gem in Co-op Mining Madness!Deep Rock Galactic is an absolute gem of a game that combines the thrill of cooperative gameplay with the satisfying chaos of dwarven mining expeditions. Despite my relatively short 4-hour playtime, I find myself compelled to share my initial impressions, as Deep Rock Galactic has already left a lasting impact on me.Gameplay (5/5):From the moment I stepped into the shoes of my trusty dwarven miner, I was hooked. The gameplay is a seamless blend of action, exploration, and strategic decision-making. The randomly generated caves ensure that each mission feels fresh and unpredictable, keeping the excitement levels high. The diversity of mission types, from point extraction to egg collection, adds a layer of variety that prevents the experience from ever feeling repetitive.The heart of the game lies in its cooperative play. The synergy between the different dwarven classes—Gunner, Engineer, Driller, and Scout—is crucial for success. My limited playtime has already shown me that effective communication and teamwork are not just encouraged but absolutely essential for overcoming the challenges thrown at you. The sense of camaraderie and shared objectives elevates the experience to new heights.Graphics and Atmosphere (4.5/5):Deep Rock Galactic boasts a visually stunning underground world that captures the essence of a dwarven mining operation perfectly. The attention to detail in the caves, the lighting effects, and the distinctive character designs contribute to an immersive atmosphere. The game's aesthetic manages to be both charming and gritty, striking a balance that suits the theme of dwarven mining.The dynamic lighting system deserves a special mention. As you traverse the dark, cavernous depths, the use of flares and the glow of precious minerals create an atmospheric tension that is both thrilling and beautiful. The game achieves a perfect blend of tension and excitement, especially when swarms of hostile creatures descend upon your team.Progression and Customization (4/5):Deep Rock Galactic offers a satisfying progression system that keeps you coming back for more. The ability to upgrade and customize your dwarf, both in terms of equipment and appearance, provides a sense of personalization. The variety of weapons, tools, and perks allows for different playstyles and strategies, adding a layer of depth to the overall experience.However, I must admit that after only 4 hours, I have just scratched the surface of the progression system. It seems promising, but I look forward to exploring it further as I delve deeper into the game.Community and Support (5/5):One of the standout features of Deep Rock Galactic is the active and friendly community. Whether playing with friends or joining a random group, the community's cooperative spirit is infectious. The developers, Ghost Ship Games, have shown a commitment to the game with regular updates and engagement with the player base. It's evident that they genuinely care about the success and enjoyment of their creation.Conclusion:In my brief 4 hours with Deep Rock Galactic, I've found an engaging and thoroughly enjoyable cooperative experience. The game's blend of intense action, strategic teamwork, and dwarven charm has left a strong impression on me. With its promising progression system, stunning visuals, and an active community, Deep Rock Galactic is a must-play for anyone who enjoys cooperative games or just wants to embark on a thrilling mining adventure with a group of friends. I can't wait to see what the depths of Hoxxes have in store for me as I continue my journey with this delightful gem.

_childDocuments_.review: I am honestly SUPER surprised by it! If you like anything along the lines in the wide region of Warframe, Borderlands, Diablo or Destiny, you'd probably love it!So let's do Pro's, Con's, Note and TLDR? Scroll down for TLDR xDPro:+ World interaction in terms of environmental destruction is extremely similar to Minecraft, but the graphics and the rendering style is adjusted in obvious ways to assist in this.+ Guns and stuff have layers to how you can upgrade and customize them, to which you get introduced gradually by way of levelling, which is awesome.+ Teamwork and coordination helps A BUT LOAD, which I love to see in games.+ Procedurally generated stuff means it is fresh and new (to a fair extent) every time!+ Achievements, Milestones, Perks and Statistics tracking! All the stuff a completionist and perfectionist like me should avoid, but never do!+ Allows for public lobbies as you would find in Diablo III, Warframe, etc+ Joining a friend, and inviting a friend, is STUPID simple, easy and fast! Like Fall Guys level easy, except that it is just as easy to join a friend who allows friends to do so - so even better than Fall Guys in this aspect!Con:- Can't find any public lobbies. Not sure if it is because I am in South Africa, due to ping, or perhaps my level, but still kinda sucks to want but not find.- Quite a few of the stuff is not very clear. IE: You can only have one upgrade per row for a gun (found out by buying two in the same row), How to promote a character (still don't know), etcNote: Despite a lot of reviews and people saying they recommend it for Minecraft players, I really wouldn't! It is nothing like it, for two main reasons:1. Since after every mission, the cave you were in is gone, it makes zero sense to build stuff meticulously. It does help when you need to go back though, but it is still approached very differently to Minecraft, for the second reason below.2. You do not pick up the stuff you destroy, only the resources you want to haul back to base, which is an incredibly small portion of the tilesets you'll find! So if you dug yourself a hole, you can't "build back out", you will have to dig out!Thanks for coming to my TED talk!In the spirit of Millennialism or whatever:9/10Would RecommendOne of the best early experiences I've had in almost any game!

_childDocuments_.review: Simply the most fun you can have in a coop PvE shooter. Really, I mean it ! The game takes blatant inspiration from TF2, like its wacky weapon design, highly customizable characters, and different classes with different roles in the team. Being a big TF2 fan, it warms my heart that some more modern games adopt similar design strategies. It offers diverse mission types, and multiple sidegrades and weapon overclocks (that can modify from stats, to core mechanics of a weapon), so there's always something new to try in this game. Of course, I highly recommend that you play it with friends, because, while the game can be fun in solo, it's at its most awesome when "crisis managing" with your buddies, and making it out alive. So, chug your beer, we're heading straight down. Rock and Stone, miner !

_childDocuments_.review: A game to simulate the kind of brotherly camaraderie that can only come from potentially lethal expeditions into the grim and unforgiving caverns of alien planets.  Obviously, this is the kind of experience every modern man is looking for.  Experience it in all its hyper-masculine glory, before the inevitable 5th-wheel female dwarf class is added.Mechanically, this game is brilliant.  One example - cave leeches.  In another review I read, the reviewer asked for cave leeches and 'grabbers' to be removed, but that would be a terrible mistake.  You see, in this game, if you decide to strike off on your own, you might make it a mile or two.  But good luck to you if a cave leech comes down from the ceiling and decides to feast on your skull.  You'll be as good as dead without some comrade-in-arms to fire two or three bullets into the thing and save you.Contrary to what some others seemed to have implied, this is *good* mechanic (dare I say an essential one), because while they aren't so prevalent as to ever become an annoyance, the threat of the random cave leech grab promotes group coordination and sticking together with at least one other brother.  There is a ton of manly atmosphere here:  Get drunk before a mission?  Great!  Get ready to experience twice the danger, because you're going to be seeing double.  Got drunk before a mission but don't really want to be?  Order up a leaf-lover's special, and rinse it out of your system on your way to the drop-pod.  Right now all of the classes feel unique and useful.  Levels and upgrades feel rewarding without feeling mandatory - a level 1 dwarf and a level 25 dwarf can comfortably exist in the same mission without one feeling useless and the other looking ridiculously overpowered.I could go on, but how many more positive things do I really have to say about this game?  Like I said at the beginning, this is the experience you're looking for.

_childDocuments_.review: (DRG) is a class based Co-op and Solo first-person shooter with procedurally generated levels and an heavy emphasis on customization, set in a universe where Dwarves have colonized space far and wide. Orbiting the planet Hoxxes, you and your eventual companions will engage in a variety of missions deep under the earth, infested with countless numbers of hostile aliens. Shoot, blast and dig your way to success for glory, promotions and rich rewards..🟩 🟥 🎮 Gameplay is divided into Preparation, Exploration, Objectives and Combat. Is done at your space station, using a variety of terminals to equip yourself, accept assignments and modify your appearance. There also is a bar where you can drink beer for various hilarious effects, while some grant passive bonuses for the next mission. The station also includes a variety of minigames and silly things to do such as kicking barrels around. Each of your classes can be assigned three different sets for diverse occasions, and as you rise through Global and Class ranks you will unlock new weapons and upgrades.Is performed on foot and by using a variety of tools unique to each class. Drillers will employ a powerful excavator to make tunnels, Scouts will use their hook to fly around, Gunners build ziplines to traverse gaps, and Engineers can shoot platforms to build bridges and walkways. Exploring each environment thoroughly is important to find all the required materials such as minerals or parts, to complete the mission objectives and call supplies.  A handy terrain scanner allows to see a 3D map of the caves, while markers and waypoints can also be placed. Illumination is always a concern and flares are for that. Hordes of enemies will keep spawning so being also fast is key. Finding events and hidden loot is time consuming but rewarding.Vary for each mission, and include a Primary target needed to call the Pod and evacuate, while also a secondary one for extra XP and credits. In an Extermination mission you will have to take down multiple Glyphid bosses, while in a Repair mission you need to fix some MULEs and an entire Pod to use to escape, while attacked on all sides. Assignments are global quests that usually require you to complete a series of regular missions, and award cosmetics, weapons or licenses depending on the type. Deep Dives are basically 3-in-1 missions with two Primary targets each and higher difficulty - but also special rewards.Plays out in FPS fashion and focuses on a variety of status effects, weakspots and positioning. Each enemy has certain weak points that if hit inflict massive damage, while also resistance or weakness to certain elements. Many weapons and enemies inflict status effects such as Stun, Burning, Frozen and so on - using such at your advantage while positioning well in the map is fundamental. Taking on a horde of 100 enemies in the open is not a good idea, kiting them in a narrow passage is. There is a good amount of strategizing, synergy between weapon effects to discover and employ. You can never truly die but get incapacitated, a companion can revive you in this case, with 10% HP unless specific perks are used. Deforming terrain to your advantage proves really useful to combat if the conditions are right. Stay together or die alone.
