_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: A satisfying and fun co-op shooter where you can expect a lot of content baked into it. If you've played games like Payday 2 or Left 4 Dead 2, this might be up your alley. You'll be amazed at exploring and learning the many things that this game has to offer. Graphics are very simple, but still beautiful with the lighting effects. Really fun for people who play solo as well!I'm roughly 50 hours in and I've only finished scratching the surface of what this game has to offer, that's how deep this game is. Oh and did I mention that this is only 3 GIGABYTES?? And that this game is REALLY OPTIMIZED?? I first played Deep Rock Galatic during a free weekend, and damn it made me realize that I really should've played sooner. This is a co-op game, but still very playable when going solo. The gameplay loop is very satisfying and addictive. Start the mission in a cave of sorts, collect minerals, collect mission objectives, and then get out, simple as that. There's numerous mission types to keep your busy, with varying biomes and modifiers to change up the the experience quite a bit. While for some this might get repetitive and boring, I don't find it that way. I can just enjoy the game and shut my brain off, at least on the lower Hazards (difficulties). To add to this, the different caves look beautiful. While yes the VERY simplistic look of the textures may throw you off, the colors and the lights make up for that. The visuals are beautiful all things considered, especially since this game is very optimized and is really small in size at only less than 3 gigabytes.I have really yet to explore all the aspects of this game. I've only really focused on one class so far, and currently trying to level up another. There's enough weapons to make each class feel different in terms of their play-style, and the devs are adding even more later down the line. On top of that, each class has its strengths and weaknesses, but none of them stand out to be "the best" class. In fact, I feel like all the classes are fairly balanced when compared against each other, taking into consideration their weapons and gadgets. If you're still deciding whether you should buy this game or not, I urge you to really try it. Words alone can't describe how fun this game is! If you're still on the fence, then wait for a sale, at that point this game is even more worth your money.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually write reviews but if you're on the fence about this one, I recommend purchasing it, even at full price. Why would I say that? You may be thinking, "It's still in Early Access and incomplete..." First I will go into the genre, and from there the features in greater detail, without giving away any spoilers. I hope this is an enjoyable read for all of you that informs you with what you need to make your purchasing decision. Drop Pod Initiating...-GENRE-Deep Rock Galactic (DRG) is a sci-fi cooperative (or single player) first-person shooter mining game. If you've ever seen the film Starship Troopers, basically combine the combat from that film with dwarves, mining underneath an alien planet named Hoxxes IV (where all of the missions take place). The environments are procedurally-generated and completely destructible. The gameplay includes light RPG, level-up elements and unlocks that make progression more fun, interesting, and ultimately necessary to play at the higher difficulty levels. There is A LOT of replayability here already.-GAMEPLAY-You first pick one of, for now, four classes, each with their varying strengths, weaknesses and personal weapons and gear. Don't worry if you love a certain class and someone on your team has already picked it. Your entire team can be made up of Drillers if you really want. You also pick one of a variety of missions, from collecting eggs or minerals deep within cave systems, to repairing lost mining vehicles and bringing them home, to battling huge 'boss' bugs that have special abilities, impenetrable exo-skeletal armor, and more... All the while you are being attacked by a variety of waves of hostile alien insects. -DIFFICULTY-On easier difficulties, they are less so, on higher difficulties they get more intense to nearly impossible to be not overwhelmed by. Based on your personal experience, skill-level and the upgrades you have purchased, you can take on whatever difficulty of mission you like, whether alone, with friends or with random players, to suit your tastes. The higher the difficulty and the longer the mission however, the more rewards. Missions can take anywhere from 20 minutes on the low end to 1.5 hours on the high end. Literally anyone who's decent with a mouse and keyboard, or a controller can play and find both a mission duration and difficulty level that will suit their time limits and skill.-DIALOGUE-I don't want to make this much longer, but I will say that the voice lines are very creative, sometimes witty, and usually very funny. They just added a few more in the last patch, so I'm looking forward to more jokes and dialogue options as the game continues to be developed. -ENVIRONMENTS (BIOMES)-The biomes are one of the first things I noticed while playing that, for some reason, the screenshots do not convey. They are quite literally beautiful. Being procedurally-generated means that you will never enter the same cave twice, so each mission's setting is unique and uniquely beautiful. The more complex the cave system in my opinion, the more beautiful to look at they tend to be.Some biomes are foggy, swampy and humid. Others are psychedelically-colored alien forests, teeming with strange, docile creatures and beautiful, glowing flora. While other biomes are crystalline caverns whose formations reflect like mirrors a sparkling light as you toss flares down their narrow tunnels. Blowing up hundreds of giant, dwarf-eating insects never looked so pretty... But then again there's no other game out there that's doing this.-CLASSES-The Class progression, abilities and vanity items are all very cool. You can tell that, even though the gear isn't interchangeable between classes, and there's no switching weapons of any kind for now, all of the upgrades are meaningful, and truly improve your dwarf's capabilities without ever feeling like they're too powerful to ruin the experience. This is the most apparent with the Engineer, who dishes out the most firepower against waves of enemies. Despite his killing power, he never feels overpowered, especially on Challenge Level 3 and (4 being the highest) where your personal skill is increasingly important and tested, as well as teamwork being ever more essential to success and ultimately, that fat paycheck at the end of the day. -REWARDS & PROGRESSION-At the end of each mission, you earn experience, credits, and rare minerals that you've mined in the cave system. Experience goes towards the class you just played, credits are spent on upgrades and vanity items, and rare minerals are used to help unlock gear upgrades and vanity items as well. For now the level cap for each class is 20, which still takes maybe 20-30 hours per class. I personally believe they will add to that level cap, as they've already added a whole new ability system, new armors, beards, hats, mustaches, skin colors and more.-THE DEVELOPER-I can tell Ghost Ship Games loves the game they are creating. They have already made something that is almost completely devoid of bugs or crashes, and all it's really lacking now is more content and features. Regardless of still being in Early Access, this game is 100% worth the current price and your support. I would not have written such a lengthy review if I didn't feel so strongly about it. -CONCLUSION-If you can see yourself enjoying casually mining minerals either alone or with friends, this is for you. If you can see yourself enjoying taking on fun, and sometimes massive challenges that will test your hand-eye coordination, threat assessment and FPS skills while working with a team and screaming "ROCK AND STONE!" at each other when victorious, then this game is also, definitely for you! Commando Kal over and out. See you in the Drop Pod!ROCK AND STONE, BROTHERS!

_childDocuments_.review: After playing this game for 700+ hours, I think I can finally say that Deep Rock Galactic is an amazing, fun and exciting co-op shooter game.The game has a large amount of great content, ranging from it's procedurally generated maps for different missions and the enemies you encounter, to the cosmetics items you can unlock in-game and the music. The community in Deep Rock Galactic is also very welcoming, and veteran players are willing to assist newbies (or Green Beards as they're know) if they ask for any help. The co-op aspect is also and very fun and interesting treat. Usually playing with friends is more fun than playing with randoms, but in this case, I feel like playing with randoms is equally as fun as playing with friends. Most of the time, your team mates will know what to do, especially the more experienced players.Overall I highly recommend this game to anyone who is looking for a fun FPS co-op shooter that has a lot of charm, content and memories to make!

_childDocuments_.review: In a time of games that are unfinished upon release, buggy, uncivil playerbases, microtransactions, paid battlepasses, and so much more, Deep Rock Galactic shines through as the light of what a game should be. I have played this game on and off for years and never have one bad thing to say about it. The updates are amazing, and free, no microtransactions other than cosmetic based packs you can purchase (which this game is so well done, it might make you consider buying one because of how well the Devs treat their playerbase.The gameplay is absolutely perfect. You wanna chill with your friends and just mine rocks while you fight the occasional bug while you listen to Lo-Fi Hip Hop Beats, you can. Do you want to sweat so much that your mouse slips out of your hand and you have to shower afterwards? You can do that too. The gameplay is rewarding, addicting, as intense as you want it to be and most importantly, it's fun. (Wild concept I know).The progression is great and you'll always have something to work towards. It's very reminiscent of old games where all of the cool helmets, crazy powerful guns, and sick paintjobs are behind pure progression and not paywalls. If you see someone with a cool armor, you can get it just by playing. Want that gun that sends out TOW missiles that explode in a radioactive burst? You get it by progressing. It's always rewarding and keeps you going the whole experience.The graphics are also great. I'm personally a fan of artistic style games and not hyper realism and this one takes the cake. The caves are all generated randomly and have a beautiful and awe-inspiring size to them. The lighting is vibrant and honestly one of my favorite parts of the game. Shooting a flare into a massive room only to see the flare continue flying and disappear down another cavern shaft is always a fun experience. There are so many other great things about this game. From the beer drinking with your friends, mini games on the Space Rig, finding hidden secrets in every mission that make you hunt for long lost armor or take on a dormant evil robot, finding new armor upgrades or a weapon improvement. It is truly one of the greatest games made in modern day.Rock and Stone Forever <3

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game! It's simple and to the point. Select a mission, prep if you can, mine and massacre, repeat. You can do things as fast or as slow as you want, granted you have ammo and health to last. I love that simplicity, and just the sort of screw-it-all attitude you could have with the game. I like all of different dwarves- each has a mobility and support tool, and their effectiveness can change depending on what they are built for or if you are playing with others. If a scout accidentally grapples up to the roof of a cave and will die if they drop? If you have an engineer, they could place a platform for you to land on and be able to get down. Though, I favor the driller for the flames and scout for the mobility.My only complaint is that the difference in a single difficulty was so much. On Challenging hazard difficulty (2/5), anyone with a basic knowledge of the game can easily solo a quest, but on Dangerous hazard difficulty (3/5), I have never been able to leave the drop pod without immediately being on half health. Granted, I was doing solo, but if a single difference in difficulty can make that much of a difference, I think it's a little too much and I can't even imagine what lethal difficulty is like other than essentially Hyrule Warriors: Age of Calamity except you can't kill enemies that quickly.I'd say miscellaneous collection could be worked on a little. The beer and upgrades require plants and special ores, but if you go on a mission, there is a chance you don't find a single plant or any special ore unless you have a side mission based on that plant (which I don't know if you do get in the end) or you're just really lucky.Good, simple game about mining and killing bugs with funny and crazy moments in between. Difficulty differences could be a little lowered, a little. Maybe make materials a little less RNG based, but I understand why it is how it is.

_childDocuments_.review: The most unique co-op game on the market right now.Imagine the mining aspects from minecraft crossed with a traditional horde shooter focused on hitting weakspots and resource management.Goodstuffs:Gives you a lot of freedom in how you approach any mission, caves are procedurally generated and the real challenge is navigating them safely while watching out for bugs and hazards.Insanely good customisation, both on a cosmetic and gameplay level.SFX and visuals are simple, but very effective. Always feels satisfying to hold down the trigger on your minigun and kill a zillion glyphids like you're mowing the garden, except that the grass screams in pain and gets green blood everywhere.Music is really good and atmospheric, there's a different playlist of tunes depending on what phase you're in, similar to PAYDAY.Classes are easy to pick up and each have unique techniques and mechanics to master.The thing that separates DRG from other co-op games is that it's more focused on exploration than combat.After a certain point you'll realise the actual challenge and fun is navigating the procedurally generated terrain of the caves, avoiding getting cornered by the glyphids, reaching minerals in difficult spots without falling and finding all of the bonus loot, like cargo crates and machine events.Compared to something like L4D or vermintide I would say DRG is 50% combat and 50% exploration, it's a lot less intense than both of those games, although if you like things to be tough the devs recently added a custom difficulty mode where most enemies can 2-3 shot you.Badstuffs:Not much really, my only real complaint is that the game can get a little grindy, many cosmetics and weapon modifications are found randomly, so if you're looking for a specific one you can expect to spend a lot of time looking for them.Hitting the extraction button after completing your main objective should require multiple dwarfs to press it, there are a lot of times where a crew of dwarves have tried to clear out the cave completely for all the loot after meeting their quota, only for a careless greenbeard to hit the button without asking. Not a game-breaking issue, but an optional vote-to-extract would be a great boon to most lobbies.Another minor nitpick is the game not being as intense in terms of difficulty, at least compared to other co-op games, but this is my least complaint overall, considering the DRG team is doing a really good job of increasing the difficulty without mindlessly pumping up damage or health numbers like other games do. Instead they're adding new enemy types every season that force you to learn how to adapt and overcome to new threats, stingtails and stalkers were a great addition and make you play much more carefully when they're skulking about.

_childDocuments_.review: Rock? Stone? It matters not.This game is a gem, both literally and figuratively. You like games where you mess around underground like Minecraft and Metro 2033? You like games that require teamwork in utter chaos like Left 4 Dead and Killing Floor? You enjoy the nutty sometimes dry humor of Team Fortress?Well here's Deep Rock Galactic. A game that delivers all this in one finely tuned, polished package. Four different dwarves, each incredibly well balanced and necessary for smooth gameplay. Each dwarf has different ways to play, unlockable weapons, mods for said weapons, and it all just works. Theres a weapon type for every playstyle amongst the four dwarf classes. If you like precision, its there, if you like colossal explosions, its there, you like bullet hoses, it there.Easy to use waypoint and mark system with the laser pointer also means its quite easy to communicate with your team without needing to type in the chat or use voice chat, although both are available. The biomes are all unique and beautiful in their own way.Each dwarf has their own way of getting around the randomly generated environments, each very different, but when working together you can turn even the biggest clustered mess of topographical nightmares into your own weird jungle gym.And best of all? Low-spec. The game has a very early-playstation-2 look. Everything is designed to be low-poly with simple textures. Its clean. Its consise. You always know what you're looking at from a distance. And this allows the devs to go nuts on the particle effects, of which there are many. Lots of smoke, fire, steam, sparks, fireballs, etc. Enemies are generally color-coded as well so even from far away you can identify critters in the caves based on their hue or the parts of their bodies that glow.Theres a lot of interesting features in the caves as well besides the enemies. Old weird dwarf machinery, strange geological formations that can be interacted with, hazardous plants and fluids.And it just WORKS. Very very few bugs. Almost no crashes.  Even when theres hundreds of bugs onscreen and explosions everywhere. And that WILL happen. Sometimes, often, ♥♥♥♥ just hits the fan in this game and you'll find yourself going toe to toe with craploads of creatures of various types. Theres no healer in this game. Theres no regenerating health. It's all on you to mitigate damage and know when to shoot and when to run.I wish games like this came out more often. No predatory practices. No fomo. No bad balance decisions. The developers actually play their own game and understand how it works and you can feel the difference between this and a lot of other modern games where you wonder if the devs have even played their own software.I'm glad this game is as big of a success as it is. It deserves all the praise and accolades. Its intense, its hard, its silly, and it pokes you right in that wanderlust gland as well. Its the full package. And one nice feature is if you fail a mission (and this will happen sometimes cause the game is random and sometimes chaos is unleashed), you dont lose all progress for death. You don't get nearly as much XP or loot but you never walk away from a mission feeling like you wasted your time.The tagline on the OST says it best:"The richest mine ever discovered just happens to be on the deadliest planet in the galaxy. It's also where you work."- Z

_childDocuments_.review: This game is everything a gamer can ask for. Fun missions, fun enemies to fight against, great weapons to use, great content to earn. And by earn, I mean really earn. - This game does not have microtransactions (unlike certain games) unless you want certain cosmetics. And even then most cosmetics have to be bought with in-game currency or earned post promotion. Something that has been seriously lacking for years- Going up the ranks is consistent to play time and effort, especially if on higher hazard levels- Seasons. The Performance Pass is also consistent when it comes to progression. Even better, unlike season or battle passes in other games which cost something, the performance pass is free. and even if you fail to complete it, all content remains in the game with nothing going away.DO NOT SLEEP ON THIS GAME! Admittedly I had doubts about this game when it was gifted to me by a friend a few years ago but now I'm a greybeard and still going strong. This one is the GOAT! THE GOAT!

_childDocuments_.review: Fun solo or multiplayer. The graphics are fun and well supported by the thoughtful animations and sound design. The immersion is complete. Classes are well-balanced and engaging when choosing what to play. There is continuous opportunity for unlockables and mixing and matching their implementation.In short - it's expansive and immersive and the community is wholesome and welcoming. _childDocuments_.review: An absolutely fantastic co-op experience. It manages to merge the best qualities of Left 4 Dead, Earth Defense Force, and *ahem* Minecraft all into one very cohesive and fun experience. The gameplay is simple and smooth, the game as a whole is relatively bug-free at the moment, and each of the four characters feels unique and interesting as far as their play-styles go.The only gripes I currently have with the game are: The lack of a "Vote to Kick Player" option in the menu.The lack of items to spend your currency on (this is early-access, so it's completely understandable)And the lack of enemy variation. (Spiders, Big Spiders, Flame Spiders, and... that's pretty much it)But again, most of these problems are due to the game being in early-access. They could honestly fully release the game right now and it'd feel finished, but with a bit more content, the game could be something truly amazing. I definitely feel like this game was worth my money, and even more importantly, my time.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been looking at Deep Rock Galactic for sometime but never seemed to get around to it, lucky for me it was part of the HC this month and I played my first 2ish hours worth of solo play and really enjoyed it.   It is kind of relaxing, that is of course until a swarm appears and then it is hellish for a few moments then back to the joy of just mining. _childDocuments_.review: "ROCK AND STONE!"...The words that you cheer when getting launched into the depths of Hoxxes IV. Your job is to mine resources, recover lost technology and collect alien eggs, all while killing many dangerous creatures along the way. Completing these missions will allow you to change your appearance and upgrade your firepower. Work hard enough, and management may put you up for promotion. This will grant you access to the more challenging assignments for greater reward.A variety of distinct biomes and mission types along with procedurally generated cave systems add a lot of depth, replayability and unique challenges to each mission which keeps you coming back for more. You don't know what assignment you'll be dealing with next.I have followed and played Deep Rock Galactic from its early access stage and I can confidently say that the developers at Ghost Ship Games care about their game and their community. They are constantly bringing out new feature updates and bug fixes.This is only a brief overview of what this game could offer you. There is a lot more for you to discover on your own or with your friends.I highly recommend this game."Congratulations on signing on for Deep Rock Galactic, miner, and welcome on board." - Mission Control.
_childDocuments_.name: Deep Rock Galactic

_childDocuments_.review: This game is getting better all the time.From day one it ran like a top. No lag, No stutter, great connections. They really focused on having a game that worked well, and does it ever!Since then updates have been slow and steady with bugs left in the dirt behind you. New areas, new enemies, great new cosmetics and upgrades along with the new Perk system (kind of like a skill tree)it's better yet. Its great fun and has a nice hazard system for difficulty and along with that "length" + "Complexity" (how complex the caves are.....Very complex, to put it lightly. There's something for everyone in this brainchild of L4D meets minecraft meets.....something new, something nice. I find myself putting in 2-3 games a night and I couldnt be happier with my purchase.

_childDocuments_.review: Played during a free weekend with friends and now I treat it as my go-to game. It's a 4 player co-op game where the gameplay switches between exploration, traversal, mining and hoard shooting at various phases. To this effect, the four classes are really well balanced and synergise really well together. You can play solo with a commandable drone but every extra player makes the game more fun as your combat, traversal and support abilities complement each other.

_childDocuments_.review: Deep Rock Galactic is interesting in that on paper it sounds kind of boring despite being really fun to play. Fact is that it’s a smartly designed co-op shooter with great class design, pacing, and difficulty scaling featuring just enough variety to keep players engaged. You’ll have an enjoyable time digging holes, gather resources, and shooting alien bugs regardless of your group size and, to my mind, that makes the game one of the best cooperative experiences of recent memory. Deep Rock Galactic is well worth a look, doubly so if you have a group of friends you regularly play games with.Rock and Stone!Full review if you enjoy reading:

_childDocuments_.review: I don't play a lot of games and probably have an unrealistic standard to which I hold games.  One of my favorite franchises was Left 4 Dead when it comes to coop and it's been hard to find a game that fills that void.  DRG is a game that captures the right balance of tension in the macro flow of the game and the intricate synergies between the playable characters.  A typical game involves aspects of managing and finding resources, strategy, and a bit of chaos making each game played unique.  Each of the characters has unique abilities which are designed to play off each other.  The engineer can build turrets and platforms, handling access and adds to the overall DPS of the team.  The scout can grapple to any part of a cave and use special flares that illuminate areas to make resource gathering and defense easier.  The driller can quickly excavate certain resources quickly and navigate new pathways in and out of cave systems.  The gunner blows ♥♥♥♥ up and has the ability to make zip lines other players can use to move between hard to reach areas.  Together, they are very complimentary to each game so it makes the multiplayer experience dynamic in terms of problems to solve and relying on each characters respective abilities.One area that I feel is undersold is the Discord integration.  The in-game mission HUD is pretty good for finding and starting multiplayer games but doesn't attract players that are vested beyond a single mission or two.  The players you will meet on the official DRG Discord server are genuinely friendly and are more likely to be vested for a few games and have a mic.Outside of the basics of the characters, gameplay, and community, DRG offers the right amount of detail in the form of equipment upgrading, item collection / forging, and a ton of personality.  The developers really put a lot of thought into the minute details crafting a highly re-playable experience that is unique and exciting every time you login.  I highly recommend DRG as a great coop game that strikes the right balance between explosions, coop-action-strategy, and chaos.

_childDocuments_.review: You know the companies that ship an early access as a full release? Yes, Fallout 76, I'm looking at you. Well, Ghost Ship Games ships a full release as an early access. It is beyond me how a little indie dev can deliver such a fantastic experience. Deep rock Galactic is the best game I have played this year. But what is it about?DRG is a cooperative shooter. Together, as a team of 4 dwarven miners, you shoot, burn and explode your way to the rich deposits in the depths of a hostile Hoxxes IV. Sounds simple, but the caves are not a welcoming place. Happy, worriless shooting is complimented by more logical tasks like traversing the caves. Dwarves need to cooperate to get from point A to point B, as every one of them has different tools at their disposal. Audio-visuals are stunning. The soundtrack of the game is composed of the electronic tracks that deliver the feeling of an alien distant planet in the futuristic world dominated by omnipotent companies. You can think of artists like Scandroid or Perturbator - synthwave mostly. And the looks... ah, the looks. I'm still surprised how the engine can handle the glow on every single element in the game. The caves are illuminated by radioactive crystals, bioluminescent flora, explosions, flames and mining lights. Even the particle effects reflect light. During your voyages to the caves of Hoxess IV you will see the pictures reserved only to late autumn trip to mountains, when you wake up in a tent at 6 a.m. and see the rising sun casts its rays on a morning mists, light sparkling on a droplets of dew. And then someone lights the neons from the central Tokyo hidden behind the trees. Only then you will be close to what DRG looks like. The devs work hard on the game, with every update causing me to discover their work anew. Truly a company to behold. If you didn't yet bought the game, it is now the best time to do so, with a recent gun update and the assignment system slowly gaining its purpose.

_childDocuments_.review: Rock and Stone! One of my favorite co-op games to date, had a real blast playing this with friends. Each class feels very unique, and does good at certain things while not so good in others. They complement each other very well. Procedural generated caves means not one mission feels the same.Every single small detail of this game has been given utmost care by the developers to create the incredibly amazing community that exists today. From the beer bar to the jukebox, the music, the small details like kicking barrels around or playing with the hanging dice in the drop-pod. The unique dialogue you can get from pointing at compressed gold "WE ARE RICH" or even the wormy maggots on the wall. Strangely enough the simple addition of pressing V to raise your pickaxe and shout ROCK AND STONE creates such a greeting and feeling of camaraderie that hardly exists in many Co-op shooters. Even playing online and meeting a fellow dwarf, pressing V to cheer and getting a reply creates that very unique feeling that everyone is together. Ghost Ship Games have given so much care to this game with even more to come even after early access. I hope to all my friends that eventually do get this game that we get to play together eventually. This is truly one of my favorite co-op experiences of all time.

_childDocuments_.review: Very good game to play with friends but it's very good to play solo too. So go buy this game already if you have the money to!

_childDocuments_.review: Deep Rock Galactic is an interesting game to tackle. It's fresh take on rogue-like dungeon crawling, complete with different classes with their own specific abilities and weapons, with different methods to handle any mission thrown your way. There's even a bot to make things easier when you're playing solo, and believe me, especially at higher levels, you'll want to play with other people to make the difficulty feel like it can even be accomplished. I haven't beaten the game yet, and might not just due to not being able to put in the time. Another thing to consider is the movement speed, which at first feels unbearably slow when compared to most games. Think Minecraft crouch walking as the default move speed, but with the sprinting feeling more like normal walk speed. It's a little painful, but not impossible to get used to after awhile. That being said, there's plenty of game to learn, explore, and unlock as you progress; enough to overlook the small things. Worth giving a try, if you're considering it, and an even better buy if you're planning on playing with friends.

They release new content every month which actually adds more elements to the gameplay, rather than the redundant updates other developers pump out. Overall the feel of the game is refreshing and the future of this game is bright due to the amazing developers.

_childDocuments_.review: Let's start off with saying the game is incredibly underrated and deserves much more. Like L4D2 and other gameplay loop orientated games, it's very addicting. Excellent co-op gameplay with randomized cave systems, objective based missions and waves of angry bugs to shoot. It has four very distinct classes with customization and perks. It's just a very well designed game overall. The game does have proper a solo option for those that want to venture alone. While I found it relaxing and engaging, it is not as fun as playing with a group of friends. The community blew me away! From my experience everyone is super friendly and welcoming to newer players. Barely any toxicity because there is no competitive pressure.Unfortunately, The endgame may be underwhelming like most of the other gameplay loop orientated games. Once you've done everything, there isn't much of an incentive to play other than just having a short session with friends. However, it will take a while reaching end game. There's just so much to do objectively, that it doesn't get old fast. Overall, It's just so fun, there's no pressure to rush anything. It's the type of game you can hop in for an hour or two.

_childDocuments_.review: EDF! EDF! EDF!!I mean....Rock and Stone! Rock and Stone! Rock and Stone!!I've had this game in my library for a few years now. When I initially bought it, it had some refined gameplay mechanics, solid combat, and clean interface. I played it for a bit, but it didn't hook me - it felt lacking in something that would make me invest my time.I came back to it a couple of months ago, and got hooked. the progression mechanisms, the various weapon choices and loadouts, cosmetic customization, and general social tomfoolery are brought together in a synergy that I will look back at with fondness for the rest of my life. What's more, is that the dev team is very active in the community, constantly pushes out updates and hotfixes, and has never strayed from treating their playerbase with respect. Absolute kudos to these rockstars - I wish them long, fulfilling, and happy lives.If you do pick up this game, make use of the DRG discord server. While there is in-game voip, the dev team has also made some amazing integrations with discord on the side, to the point where you can send/accept invites from discord directly into the game. It also fosters a certain sense of community that's rarely seen, and you'll find some really good people of all skill levels on there. Stop by and say hi.

_childDocuments_.review: DRG is a well-designed but very niche game; only certain types of players will be able to enjoy it.  It takes some time and effort to get established in a way that lets you appreciate the different dwarves' roles, and this game is much more fun when played in its intended co-op mode than it is when played solo. The synergy between the different dwarves' roles is a significant factor towards the flow and enjoyment of the PvE missions in this game.There are guns, but I don't really consider DRG a shooter.  I'm personally awful at hardcore shooters - they require too much in the manner of physical reflexes, and my body cannot keep up with my brain, so I end up predicting what's going to happen but not being able to do anything in spite of that.  DRG is different, though.  There are lots of cues that can give you forewarning: sound cues from dangerous flora/fauna way before you can see them, predictable spawn patterns, suspicious low-visibility ceilings and ledges that encourage you to exercise caution, etc.  Sure, some of the swarms can be rough (and the procedural generation can put you in a nasty situation), but your shooter skills are far less important than teamwork, efficiency, timing, and good decisions for accomplishing the mission.I love how the four dwarf roles interact.  Each role contributes something that's really useful for team traversal and survival.  The game is balanced to encourage cooperation between the 4 roles, and when you have a coordinated team, cave diving feels smooth and incredibly rewarding.Aesthetically, some of the caves are very beautiful.  But even the plain-looking or downright ugly ones with harsher environments achieve a good atmosphere.  DRG had a style that it was going for, and I think it accomplishes it well with the foul-mouthed dwarves, acceptance of mortality, and complex cave systems that really make you work to traverse them.  It gives a sense of "Yeah, we're pioneers in a harsh alien world. And we're dwarves, so to some extent, we kind of don't give a ♥♥♥♥.  When's the next paycheck?" I'm not sure that I've properly articulated exactly why I enjoy this game or why I feel that it fits together as a well-designed whole, but I'm definitely willing to give it a dwarven cheer.  "Rock and Stone!"

_childDocuments_.review: Deep Rock Galactic is a great hybrid class-based FPS, Mining game, and waved based survival game. What makes this game stand out is the mining system uses a polygon system instead of a cube voxel based system. These same polygons are used to create a unique and hard-edged art-style that feels properly dwarfy. Teamwork is an important aspect as any dwarf on his own will die a terrible bug ridden death. Sound design is crisp and sounds just like digging a hole in real life with a drill or pickaxe. The game could use a bit more content, but the developers are responsive and are actively developing the game for the better.There are four unique classes in the game to choose from and they are all really enjoyable to play. These classes work best when used in conjunction with one another. While it can be fun to have four gunners, one of each class is the best way to find success in the missions. The Scout has a stereotypical FPS assault rifle, a double barrel shotgun, a really fun grappling hook to traverse the huge caverns, and a flare to light up aforementioned large caverns. The scout pairs really well who has a semi-automatic shotgun, a grenade launcher, sentries, and the platform gun. The platform gun can place yellow, octagonal platforms against any wall. This mean that he can put platforms at high, hard to reach mineral deposits and the scout can grapple to them. The Gunner has a Gatling gun, revolver, zip line gun, and satchel charges. The driller is the most unique class as it directly and greatly effects the digging component of the game. He has a flamethrower, a pistol that is weaker than the gunners, satchel charges, and giant dual wielded power drills. These allow the player to easily shape the world around them to their liking.The mining in the game includes the digging of dirt and the digging of minerals which are found in the dirt. There are few different mineral types such as: gold which gives the player credits, nitra which allows players to call in supply drops to refill ammo, morkite which is the objective of some missions, some specialized ores which work the progression system, and some large gems which require quite a bit of digging. The world is comprised of triangle polygon system of digging. While a dwarf mining will remove a square amount of dirt, explosive enemies can leave oddly shaped craters in the ground which look great. Each cave system is also randomly generated so that each mission never feels the same. The special mineral fuel Deep Rock Galactic’s progression system.Each class has permanent upgrades which can be bought for every part of the class’ equipment. For example, armor can be upgraded so that the player has more shielding or a weapon can have more max ammo. Flares can also be upgraded so that the dwarves have more of them and they last longer. This equipment lights up the darkness that the dwarves find themselves in. These upgrades can be bought with credits, but the more powerful upgrades require the special minerals. This makes sure that the player does not play only the easy biomes. Different biomes have unique obstacles but they also vary in the amount of hits they require to break the dirt blocks. The driller is great because his drill doesn’t care about hardness and will cut through any rock like butter. These upgrades help fend off the monsters in more difficult mission and biomes.Enemies spawn in both small pockets and giant waves. These occur randomly and make the game quite challenging. There are a few different enemy types to challenge the unlucky dwarfs mining a faraway asteroid. One type explodes and does quite a bit of damage and can set off a chain reaction with other explosive bugs. Another type has an armored front but an exposed abdomen and diffuse poison gas into the air upon death. The varied nature of waves and their random compositions help to keep this game mechanic fresh and challenging. A player can predict what kind of enemies will be on a particular mission which makes the darkness all the more frightening.As with any multiplayer game, I must talk about the quality of the community around the game. While this game is great with friends, sometimes they aren’t around and randoms are one’s only option. From my experience, the community is really nice and every player actively revives their teammates and tries to win. The powerful abilities and friendly fire could make grieving prevalent, but it isn’t. I think that this is because a game of Deep Rock Galactic takes on average thirty minutes to complete. No one wants to lose twenty minutes of work so everyone plays nice to get the materials they need.Overall, this is a really fun game with friends and randoms that combines wave based FPS gameplay and mining. Progression feels rewarding and makes the player get out of their mission comfort zone. The developers are also actively adding more content, which is the major gripe that people have with this game. The game’s sound design is excellent. The music is used only for ambiance and never distracts from mining or gunning. The dwarves all have really enjoyable lines that are immediately funny and memorable (ROCK AND STONE BROTHER!!!). Mining sounds are realistic and it really felt like I was a dwarf mining in a cave. Guns have great audio feedback and are satisfying to use on the future squelching bug bits. The graphics have a really unique style. The polygonal mining system’s art style is used on the dwarves and enemies to give the world a harsh, hard edged look. It helps to create the theme of four dwarves stranded on an asteroid while being yelled at by a corporate manager who doesn’t care about their safety. The colors are quite muted and all of the materials are matte to once again create a desolate effect. The graphics are quite crisp and I never became confused when looking at different enemy types as they are all uniquely models. With such a complex mining system I was pleased to find that the game ran excellently on my computer on max settings. The game looks beautiful with these settings and I don’t even have the highest PC specs possible. Great CommunityFun GameplayMemorable Sound DesignResponsive ControlsUnique SettingCould Use Some More Content

_childDocuments_.review: I read Deep Rock Galactic can be somewhat compared to Left 4 dead, especially in terms of replayability and co-op fun. With that note I decided to buy it. Trailers and gameplay looked fun and me and some friends needed a new solid co-op game.Now there's not a lot of content, levels are randomly generated but in the end they all fall back on 1 of 3 basics layouts. Either kill bosses, gather resources, or dig in the ground to find big minerals. The core mechanics are really solid and well worked out. This combined with co-op and regular free updates gives the game endless replayability.Despite the things mentioned above being really solid/well done we did get bored with it after a while. I just missed some depth in the missions themselves.Let's dive a bit deeper into the actual gameplay. In Deep Rock Galactic you run around randomly generated maps doing objectives such as collecting resources/killing bosses.Levels are well-made, and always exciting to play. There is no clear path forward so you'll have to dig/create your own path and fighting of hordes of aliens is always a thrilling experience.  You have the option to choose between 4 different classes. Each class has its own weapons/gadgets that can also be upgraded with the resources you gather during the missions. Next to this each class also has new unlockable weapons. These can be unlocked by reaching certain levels with a class which will then unlock a mission you need to complete before you can buy it. The weird thing about this system is that through this way only the host can unlock weapons for his/her class. If another party member has reached the needed level, the host cannot start that mission. The same thing happens with all the missions you can unlock by reaching milestones with a class.Thanks to this, after a while of playing we ran into the problem of the host not having any new missions anymore, while other party members did, requiring us to switch host.Something Deep Rock Galactic does really well is creating a good and unique atmosphere. Funny voicelines, humor, levels with dynamic lighting, and a solid main hub to play around in. The game has everything needed to create a unique universe for itself.Talking about the main hub, it's something I really liked. When for example the host is not ready to start yet, others can mess around a bit, play a minigame, do some drinking or check out the trophy room to see what has been achieved so far.Overall, I do recommend Deep Rock Galactic. Especially to people who like to play co-op. Keep in mind this is still an early access game.Currently It's well worth the money but you can expect the game to get a bit boring after a while. Luckily they are providing us with regular free updates. Let's hope they keep it this way.

_childDocuments_.review: Its like a combination of alien swarm (objective based hoard shooter) and minecraft (digging and mining). Couple things to keep in mind: -Its really dim and easy to get lost. Use your flares (F) and map/scanner (Tab)!-Pressing 'X' pings other of your location, and laser pointer (think Ctrl by default) allows you to point/tag stuff for others to see-Cosmetics/upgrades purchased do not carry over between classes (my biggest gripe tbh)-Pressing '5' lets you call in a resupply pod in exchange for Nitra (not having ammo is roughhhh)-You need to equip perks to use them (oops) Gripes: -cosmetics/upgrades don't carry over between classes-weapon/class upgrades take a while to get, and are locked behind certain resources which can be tricky to acquire-finding liquid morkite veins for refinery can be stupidly tricky/impossible feeling at timesRock and stone everyone! Hope you enjoy the game as much as I do~

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. It's L4D meets Minecraft. While it's slightly rough around the edges (as you'd expect with an Early Access title), the kernel of a great game is in there.As it stands there's 4 different classes that synergize well with one another. Maps are procedurally generated and the current missions consist of killing targets or going for certain minerals as an objective. Extra minerals you mine along the way can be sold or used to upgrade weapons, armor, or purchase cosmetics. Right now, there's no cash shop for cosmetics. Not sure if there ever will be, but I think it's worth mentioning as everything can be bought with IN-GAME currency you earn by playing (just like the good old days). Some of the cosmetics are a bit of a grind, but it's easy to amass resources and doesn't feel like a chore as the game's fun. If this team continues to iterate and polish DRG, we're in for a phenomenal title. They seem to have slowed to monthly updates, but from their write-ups, it seems that they're moving forward with bigger chunks of content with each update. They also recently opened a development branch where you can test out the latest build. If you do so, just know that you're characters don't transfer between the development build and the actual game.If all that I've mentioned sounds up your alley, check it out. I've been having a blast and can't wait to see what these guys do next.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most unique, polished, and fun games that I've played, Deep Rock Galactic is a shining example of indie done well.  It's brimming with charm and is immediately lovable. Each of the four playable classes bring fun gameplay mechanics and playstyles to the table, and they compliment each other in ways that make playing cooperatively a pleasure. Ghost Ship Games does not disappoint with free content updates and continuous improvements.One thing worth noting is that this game's player base is predominantly very casual for an objective-based FPS game with a surprising amount of nuance for efficiency, so finding good players can be a trying process. I strongly recommend going in with at least one friend. That being said, the game shines its brightest when played cooperatively, and at this point in the game's lifespan most players know what they're doing at higher difficulties.All things considered, Deep Rock Galactic is a real gem of a game that keeps getting better and I fully encourage everyone with cooperative FPS competency to try it. It's clear to see that this IP has become well established, now spawning several titles under its belt.

_childDocuments_.review: There's a lot to like here.There's always a new problem to solve.  The classes are diverse and complement each other extraordinarily well.  Weapon options are also meaningfully diverse, and the upgrade paths render everything in your kit more useful and flexible than you think.  There are wrong options, but there aren't 'right' ones, if that makes sense.  There's plenty of room for build diversity and player preference.  The skill cap is high enough to keep you constantly growing as a player, but not so high that you can't enjoy the game in co-op right off the bat.  Bosco supports solo play well.The community is great.  Problem player ratio is below 1/100.  The unlock system doesn't keep players from getting in over their heads on Haz 4/5 or the Deep Dives, but it does guarantee at least a basic level of competence to access the game's actual challenges.There are two main criticisms.  First, the upgrade system is shallow and the best unlocks are both random and time-gated.  It takes months to kit out your players the way you want, though at least it's not grindy.  You can play sparingly and progress on that front just as fast as someone that plays obsessively.  It makes a great change-of-pace game as a result.  You can play for five hours a week and get just as many overclocks as someone playing forty.Second, the two newest mission types can be buggy and frustratingly time consuming.  They are also not noob-friendly - the Drilldozer is fragile and you need to have a good handle on map movement and terrain alteration to get pumpjack sites identified and pipelines built in a timely manner.That gets to the last positive - the developers support the game extremely well, both with fixes and new content.  The new mission types were not really ready for prime time when they were added to the mission pool, but the bugs get squashed with regularity.  There are still frustrations (for the love of God, please bind 'Grind' to something other than the same key as 'Build Pipeline', or at least let me change it in the options), but it's night and day when comparing the day they left the beta build to now.

_childDocuments_.review: Very replayable coop action game, thanks to the number of biomes (with unique gameplay features), class gadgets, game 'mutators' that change up things, and more. Oh yeah, having a destructable procedural terrain system also helps a lot in that regard! :PIt has a solid progression system, where basically every hour of game is going to be able to give you something, like a new perk, a new weapon or weapon upgrade, a new overlock, etc. The feeling of progression in excellent.It's also a game that easily accomadates to any player skill and mood, thanks to 5 difficulty settings. And the difficulty will scale up or down depending of the number of players, other coop games should learn how it's done. In the lower difficulty settings the dependency with the other players isn't actually that high, that leps with the public play experience (and you always can play on Haz5 if you want that!).Beyond the technical, coop or rpg aspects, it feels like a good action game. It knows that shooting the same 4 enemies would get tiring eventually, and offers a wide array of them, beyond what trailers show, with more than 20 variations. Some are fliers, others spit webs or poison, some are big like mini-bosses, some are armoed and their armor has to be avoided or broken first, and others can catch you and wisk you away.Finally, the game has an interesting mix of chillout (exploring, mining) and intense action gameplay that makes it unique in comparison with others games from the competition (L4D, Vermintide, Payday...) it's an interesting experience. Oh, and they have made their homework, with good tools to allow player communicaiton without mics.

_childDocuments_.review: DRG is arguably the best co-op shooter you can be playing right now, up there with the greats such as Left 4 Dead. It's one of the few cases these days where a game is just a joy to play and you don't have to worry about keeping up with a meta to contribute to your team, as you can quite literally customize your experience to your heart's content.Deep Rock Galactic comes, out of the box, with the following:- Deep Progression- A massive amount of customization. (Mining suits, helmets, hats, color schemes, beards, moustaches, side burns, weapons, passive perks, active perks, weapon mods, weapon overclocks, and even pickaxe customization down to the individual components!)- Varied Enemy design to keep you on your toes during expeditions.- 4 Distinct classes that bring something to the team and never fall flat, each with their own means of traversal.- Rewards for promoting your miners once they reach max level, unlocking even more content.- A Monster Hunter-esque bar where you and your fellow miners can drink to get buffs for the next mission, or simply get wasted.- Various difficulty levels that are NEVER forced on you in an attempt to gate your progression. Play how you like.- Steeve. :)Keep it up, Ghost Ship. You've struck gold.Rock and Stone.

_childDocuments_.review: Every one of the games belonging in this genre feels slighty different from the other and it can get stale quickly. I think that Deep Rock Galactic (which I will just call DRG from now on) is an hell of a much waited exception.Why not starting from the repetitiveness and what poisons the genre. DRG lacks the scary deja vus, compared to the other games of its genre (Warhammer: Vermintide 1/2, Payday 2, World War Z, Killing Floor 1/2), where, after a while, the environment and the maps gets numbly repeating and you just become a mindless robot running towards the end as fast as possible. The helping hand comes from the procedurally generated levels that features in DRG, they feel always fresh and are simply fun to explore, giving you a sense of new found will to go and hunt for the minerals that every frantic dwarf craves! The characters are all quirky and silly, I also believe that they're all dubbed by the same guy...well, I'll throw my hat to you man, they can be stupidly funny at times. Oh, the soundtrack is pretty amazing too, and if you DIG (ugh...) 80's synth it will feel like home!The combat/exploration/minerals collection alternation loop is successful, the mission variety is fairly good and  level difficulties that go from low risk, challenging, to dangerous (respectively easy/medium/hard) never leave you exhausted after you're over with and it is just fun to pickaxe colorful minerals and dive deeper into the caves between every enemy encounter. If you like the challenge, missions can get even harder (extreme/lethal) and are equally fun to engage as they get pretty much intense, without being impossible.The co-op formula just works, and it has to be the best feature in the game so far. It is fun to play solo too, I mean, Bosco, the relentless minibot that they provide you if you decide to go solo, is a beast, and can easily overcome every task you give to it.Where was I? Oh, so, while it is also fun to play alone, the enormous waves of unique, cool looking enemies are insanely chaotic and fun if you go for a full team, and working together becomes a necessity, all thanks to the DRG team that managed to create an impressive alchemy between every class, wisely suggesting you to pick a different character for each player, because every member of the team is essential and feels part of it!The progression system is well thought and there's a general passive skill tree that doesn't interfer with your class, you can unlock one more primary and secondary weapon for each character (so far), various utility gadgets and a solid endgame that features more of the same content, but better, every character is costumizable and you can finally spend your sweated minerals to upgrade your looks!Lastly, I think that the only thing that DRG is missing to be just the perfect game in its genre, is the crazy amount of content that most of the other aformentioned titles got, like, weapons variety, bosses and missions, other than that, it gives you a full package of much more than worthy content for the right price! In hope to see you join us, ROCK AND STONE to you, fellas!

_childDocuments_.review: DRG mixes exploration of procedurally-generated caves with mining minerals, while also fending off alien bug creatures and completing various objectives.You can both start your own mission and have randoms join you, group up with friends, join others' lobbies, and even play Solo, with a lovely robotic companion to assist you.There are 5 difficulties you can play the game on (ranging from very easy to pretty hard, the harshest of which needs to be unlocked via an assignment) and, as you play, you'll be able to improve your performance via upgrading weapons and tools, and by unlocking perks for some extra benefits.The gameplay loop at its core doesn't change much, as you progress: you go in, explore, do the objectives and kill bugs with a bunch of fine dwarven pals. The several biomes and mission types, along with the procedurally generated maps and all the random players you can meet, though, make it so every mission can be an unique, and fun, experience (this has been the case with me, a least!).I personally find the game to be very charming, with all the sights it can provide and the various, lovely aspects one can enjoy (even just the dwarves talking is music to mah ears :D), on top of being easy to pick up to simply play one or two missions, or play for hours on end.Definitely recommend givin' it a shot. Hope tah see ye all in tha mines!

_childDocuments_.review: Developed by Ghost Ship Games, Deep Rock Galactic is a co-op first person shooter set on Hoxxes IV, a planet rich in minerals but filled with dangerous wildlife and hazardous environments. You play as one of four classes of dwarves working for the Deep Rock Galactic mining corporation.Deep Rock Galactic is one of the best co-op games out there. It's fun, challenging and has great combat. The best part is that new content is free, including the cosmetics and it doesn't shove microtransactions down your throat (because there are none), unlike most games these days.
_childDocuments_.name: Deep Rock Galactic

_childDocuments_.review: I thought this game looked fun from the trailer, but when you actually get your hands on it, it’s a whole new world. This game is instantly so fun/satisfying, filled with beautiful art, creepy lighting effects and a fantastic soundtrack. The gameplay is extremely addicting and it was very gratifying every time I completed a mission. For a game that came out a couple months ago, it feels way better than most early access games, and they actually update it frequently too! (Unlike most early access rip offs) I strongly strongly recommend this game. <3
_childDocuments_.name: Deep Rock Galactic

_childDocuments_.review: There's a lot of customization to find a playstyle you like with many weapon builds, overclocks (gun mods), perks. With the weapon builds and overclocks you can have bullets that ricochet from enemies, specializing your weapon for primary shooting or charged shots, elemental effects and even shotgun jumping. You can only choose up to 3 passive and 2 active perks that allow you do things like return melee damage, insta revives, shield boosting and the best of all, taming an enemy bug that you can pet!The best combo in the game is the engineer's platform with the scout's grapple to get to any place out of reach. The driller can create a makeshift bunker by drilling the wall or use his drills to directly reach the drop pod. And the gunner has zip lines to help carry teammates and big ores.The main lobby features a Barrel Hoop mini game where you kick barrels into a moving hoop, lots of beer that have plenty of fun effects and some that give buffs during a mission and a jukebox with a dance floor. After you experience the main content of the game, you can level up to get prestige, get dwarf and pickaxe customization, complete the weekly deep dives and get overclocks. Overclocks are sadly dropped randomly, with some choice on machine events, so it might take a while to get an overclock you like.Compared to similar co-op games, DRG provides content updates for free, while paid DLCs are only for soundtracks and cosmetics.For achievement hunters:There are some challenging ones that are easier in co-op and some that require 4 players in the same lobby. You have to complete 100 solo mission and the biggest grind is getting all 4 dwarfs to Gold promotion.
_childDocuments_.name: Deep Rock Galactic

_childDocuments_.review: An utterly fantastic co-op experience with an oddly striking visual style that lends itself to toe-curling chasms and pitfalls and tight, claustrophobic Alien-esq corridors and tunnels. The biomes are steadily being made more and more unique, and you'll be bound to have your favorite places to shoot some bugs and least-favorite places to die in toxic fungus. The soundtrack has no right to be as good as it is, either. The only negative I can think of is that theres no way to replay the in-game soundtrack via the jukebox at home base. Heavy Mass Effect vibes from the tunes here. If you're a fan of Left 4 Dead, Vermintide, or even just Minecraft, drag your friends into this nasty bug world and get filthy rich.

Each biome is hellish in its own way on high difficulty levels. The four classes are very balanced and I really appreciate the thought the devs put in the game.

_childDocuments_.review: It is pretty great. Defenitely one of the best contestants for CooP focussed gameplay, but also very good alone. Bosco, your drone companion in solo gameplay, is effective, simple, and gives another layer of deptht to the gameplay, while playing as a group is just fun. I have only played with friends so far though, but I can only recomment to learn together.The game is well paced, I am 150 hours in now and have accomplished alot, but still got things to uncover and build up. It's a blast, for both casual fun and stressfull, yet rewarding, high difficulty gameplay. Noone forces you to go into higher threat levels, but you get your rewards faster if you do. Rewards you choose yourself. A word to the studio:I am amazed by the detail and love you put into your game. Little things most players will probably gloss over, like hidden voicelines and sparking cables in the Rig... stuff like that makes the game feel alive, without adding any convoluted story or complexity. Thank you. Thank you for your subtlety.

_childDocuments_.review: Remarkably supportive development team.The generated maps don't get stale or repetitive like so many procedurally generated games do, and there are a myriad of side-jobs, mini-bosses, easter eggs, special events and mission types beyond just Rock and Stone. Plenty to do. Come for the mines, stay because you're indebted to Mission Control from kicking the barrels into the launch bay too many times. 10/10Also, I'm playing on Linux Mint, works flawlessly.
_childDocuments_.name: Deep Rock Galactic

_childDocuments_.review: Deep Rock has not only charming low poly graphics and intense swarms of hordes to decimate but also an epic soundtrack that makes gameplay feel epic at the peak of swarming attacks. Absolute chef's kiss!The game gives you 4 class options engineer, gunner scout, and driller. Loads of cosmetics that can be unlocked or bought and even customize your beard, who could've dreamt that? Customizations to your weapons and the hard to find pickaxe upgrades. The game has a lot of varying biome types that you can choose from a varied selection of mission types and even status effects to an entire map, like double XP or exploding swarms. The game is procedurally generated and sometimes this can make completing a mission hard occasionally if something is out of reach. Nitra, a resource you mine to call for ammo refills, can sometimes be lacking adding to the intensity or frustration to the mission. I've played 20 or 30 hours solo, so while it is a coop game the developers have balanced it by including Bosco which is a drone that will help shoot and mine resources for you to pick up. The variety of game modes has certainly kept the game from feeling stale and extend from resource collection to drone rescue missions. Playing online coop with strangers is a gamble and you can get teamed with people who aren't really trying to play the game or hide when the swarms show up. I have 100 hours of making this review and I feel like I'm still discovering new things.

_childDocuments_.review: Doretta's head is the ultimate litmus test for whether a person is capable of self-governing.To return Doretta's head is an easy, convenient task and one which we all recognize as the correct, appropriate thing to do. To return the head is objectively right. There are no situations other than dire emergencies in which a person is not able to return the head. Simultaneously, it is not illegal to abandon Doretta's head. Therefore Doretta's head presents itself as the apex example of whether a person will do what is right without being forced to do it. No one will arrest you for not returning the head, no one will fine you or otherwise punish you for not returning the head. You will gain nothing by returning the head. You must return Doretta's head out of the goodness of your own heart. You must return it because it is the right thing to do - because it is correct.A person who is unable to do this is no better than an animal, an absolute savage who can only be made to do what is right by threatening them with a law and the force that stands behind it.Doretta's head is what determines whether a person is a good or bad member of society.ROCK AND STONE!

_childDocuments_.review: This class based game is about completing objectives, mine minerals and fighting off swarm while managing ammo. The same minerals are used for upgrading your weapons and equipment.The combat is satisfying. Every class has its unique guns/equipment and different role assigned. Mining and missions are fun on procedurally generated levels with 9 different biomes (11 biomes now). Updates are regular without any micro-transactions or season pass. If you are into customizing your character with skins and paint-jobs then you can earn all of them in-game as a tertiary mission or buy them with your in-game money.Oh, and don't forget to spam the "V" button whenever you join someone. ;)Update 2022: They've actually started releasing themed Season Pass every six months for various cosmetics, which is and will remain absolutely free. What could be better than that?

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so fantastic I often use it as an example of how to make a good first person shooter that is fun to play on your own but improved with other people due to the game's natural inclination towards promoting teamwork, and how well each of the four classes play off of each other. _childDocuments_.review: Deep Rock Galactic is one of those rare games that continues to receive loving updates from its developers. To this day, new content is regularly released, including new weapon overclocks, mission types, enemy types, cosmetics, and more. Most cosmetics can be earned through SEASONS, which are completely FREE. It’s a solid co-op shooter that offers four different playable classes: Scout, Driller, Gunner, and Engineer.For the best gameplay experience, it's recommended to form a team with all four classes (the game is best balanced for four players but is still fun with fewer). Each class complements the others with its unique utilities. Here’s a brief overview of each class:Gunner: The least mobile class, but provides the highest sustain damage. The Gunner’s strong suit is the shield, which can be deployed at a chosen location to protect anyone inside from enemy damage.Driller: Offers high mobility for the entire team by drilling through the cave walls to access hard-to-reach areas. Most of Driller’s weapons deal steady damage with fire, acid, or frost, making him effective against smaller enemies and conserving ammo.Scout: The most mobile class, able to quickly grapple to cave walls, making it easy to reach difficult spots. The Scout is typically the main miner of valuable resources that are hard for other classes to access. Provides utility with a flare gun that lights up the cave. The Scout’s weapons focus on single-target damage to weak spots.Engineer: Has weaker primary weapons but incredibly strong secondary ones designed for high burst damage. The Engineer provides utility with deployable platforms, great for helping Scouts reach high places and reducing fall damage. Additionally, the Engineer can set up sentry turrets.A major advantage of the game is the extremely friendly player base, with the lowest number of toxic players compared to other multiplayer games. This low toxicity is partly because it’s a PvE game, where players are more focused on fun than competition.Replayability is high, with endless goals like collecting all the cosmetic items (none of which are pay-to-win). The only purchasable content is available on the Steam store as DLCs, offering visual upgrades for weapons and armor sets. However, the game provides plenty of these upgrades through regular gameplay without needing to buy DLCs. As a regular supporter, I own all available DLCs, but I still use many in-game-earned armor sets and weapon upgrades.Managing ammo effectively is crucial, as you don’t have unlimited supplies. Another key aspect is maintaining good situational awareness, avoiding being surrounded, and always having an escape route.I highly recommend the game. If you don’t have friends to play with, don’t worry. You can join other players, and most communication happens through pings, so there’s no need to worry about social anxiety. The developers respect your time and money, avoiding predatory practices common in many modern games.Rock and Stone!

_childDocuments_.review: I am a 45 yo father, probably one of the oldest people playing this game. I am a single farther to my Son, who is 14 now. My son got this game for Christmas in 2021 from his uncle, so we installed it on his computer and he started playing. By the end of the week he had 24 hours on this game. _childDocuments_.review: Deep Rock Galactic is a fun, player-first experience that combines elements of horde shooters, resource management and the "Space-Dwarf" Genre. While matchmaking can certainly be fun, and playing alone can be rewarding in it's own right, a group of friends feels necessary to approach such a refreshingly cooperative yet casual experience. That said, DRG can be deceptively challenging at times. Difficulty can spike, but never in ways that feel unfair. After all, death is never very punishing, and you're always in control of adjusting the difficulty. The more complex elements of the game feel like the right kind of slow-burn, and will keep casual fans entertained for as long as this game is supported.Simply, DRG is the perfect hang-out game where everyone can contribute without having to hyper focus on bosses or objectives. Seize the chance to enjoy some consequence free fun while you can because it doesn't come around very often.
_childDocuments_.name: Deep Rock Galactic

_childDocuments_.review: *For my full thoughts and everything you need to know about Deep Rock Galactic check out my 15 minute video preview Welcome to a co-op cavern crawl powered almost entirely by hearty Dwarven beards.Ghost Ship Games has delivered a solid piece of sci-fi, class based, bug stomping and spelunking goodness here and they've done so by ensuring that even this early build of the game contains a substantial gameplay loop to give early adopters something to sink their teeth into. Replayability is relatively high thanks to the games use of procedural generation to build out the caverns of its diverse biomes, each comprised of their own hazards, fauna, flora, and environmental wonders. Multiple difficulty options allow you to go from enemy free strolls and relaxing cave dives to Starship Trooper levels of OH SH*T that will have you shouting and possibly losing some friends along way all in the name of increaing your mission rewards as well as your chance of ending up as bug food deep down in a dark cavern somewhere.The progression and reward system is a bit a light at the moment but there's plenty of satisfaction to be found in the gameplay of Deep Rock especially when rolling out of your drop pod with a group of friends. Teamwork is essential and the game's four classes all come locked and loaded with their own unique weapons, gear and gadgets ensuring each class will have their time to shine as your team searches for mining glory. I should also mention that while co-op is at the forefront of the teams efforts, you can play solo with the assistance of a drone that can mine resources and even assist you in combat.It's been great seeing the team make leaps and bounds over the past year as they've went from closed pre-alpha testing to early access here today. With plenty of room to grow, a promising roadmap and a strong focus on community feedback Deep Rock has the potential to become one of the best co-op experiences of 2018. If you spent countless nights loosing sleep and calling into work with games like Left 4 Dead and Payday, Deep Rock Galactic will likely strike your fancy, just remember to bring some friends, it can get lonely in the dark even when you're a Dwarf.

_childDocuments_.review: The Good: While the gameplay can grow repetitive at times, the overall experience is sublime. Four classes which are distinct enough to be enjoyable variations but similar enough that switching between them isn't punishing. Different mission modes are entertaining, usually requiring scrounging up a specific material and delivering it back to the station or eliminating a specific threat. While that might sound like Minecraft or No Man's Sky, the actual flow of gameplay feels closer to Vermintide or Left4Dead, usually resulting in a run-and-gun experience with collection coming second to survival. The graphics are stylish, and the music is a joy for anyone who enjoys 80's synth. The Bad: Progression can feel slow at times, but that's usually because the game's in-game world is a little too jumbled with different options to select (via a hoard of different computer screens accessed in the hub world or hotkey) which would be combined into a smaller grouping. Slightly more obnoxious is the UI design decision to make perks extremely easy to miss on the equipment screen. While the procedural generation makes it feel like certain caves are completely impossible to navigate, learning how your abilities work makes this a moot point.TLDR: Recommend if you like cooperative run-and-gun style games and completing objectives under pressure. Avoid if you think it's Minecraft or No Man's Sky.
_childDocuments_.name: Deep Rock Galactic

_childDocuments_.review: Probably one of the best co-ops in the past 5 years that I've played. Each class is completely different, and their guns handle completely differently and don't so much as have weaknesses, but just places they excel. The tools to get around the caves each class have all offer their own advantages but can, with enough effort, replace each other in many situations.The missions work well, and so does cave generation. There's just this sense of wonder and exploration that's different to an open world game. You wonder what treasure and danger you're going to find around every corner.Every now and then, something extremely rare appears, that gives you thousands of gold, or experience, or just something to remember for the fun situation it causes.I cannot rate this game highly enough.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: Played it again, still boring.Not feeling this game after playing it with friends a few times.There's quite a lot to do, but it feels like a job. The sense of progression is pretty slow, I've put 4 hours into the game already and I've barely accomplished anything while sticking to one character most of the time. That might excite some players, but for me, I can't justify dumping hours into a game which rewards my time with minor character upgrades and cosmetics.My ultimate criticism is this game lacks substance. You run around, find a thing, retrieve it, then leave. All while occasionally killing enemies. That's the loop. You're basically an online grocery shopper, except replace all other customers with hostile monsters. And instead of real money, you get fake money that you can use to buy a mustache.The best thing this game gave me is the realization that people with thousands of hours in this game are not to be ♥♥♥♥♥♥ with. They're borderline insane, and God help you if they figure out you've got a jewelry box that's only a few pickaxe hits away.
