_childDocuments_.review: Alright. It's time I finally get around to writing a review for this masterpiece of a game. Where do I even start... Well first off. The concept for the game is absolutely amazing. Nothing screams, "masterpiece" to me other than a group of four dwarves who are more of a threat to each other than the bugs you are in a constant bullet hell with 24/7, spewing profanities and insults at each other. Secondly, we got the sacred procedural generation and caves. Every cave you play in feels so fluid but unique at the same time and sometimes the scenery can be quite captivating. Except for Magma Core. We don't talk about that biome. Then we also got the peak weapons design and cosmetics design. I can give nothing but praise to the devs for the amount of effort they distilled into the firearms and cosmetics for your dwarves just to give to that slightly cooler looking helmet. Come on, we all know the real endgame is fashion. And lastly, just the cooperation aspect. It's really the only game I find myself joining random lobbies to play with random people I've never met. I've made a number of friends on this game and the community for the most part is really kind and helps out new players (greenbeards). If I have to give one pro tip from my near 700 hours on this game collective between console and PC it would be: Don't trust a Driller under any circumstances.10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Deep Rock Galactic

_childDocuments_.review: Don your biggest and snazziest beard, down a Red Rock Blaster and get ready to dig deep.Tunnel your way into randomly generated voxel caverns filled with precious minerals, lethal hazards, vicious aliens and harmless critters (that you can blow up because reasons), and much more. Fight the swarming monsters and bag all the shiny loot on your own or in co-op, either of which will provide hours of fun and genuine challenge for even hardcore Minecrafters and Quake FPS gods.Deep Rock Galactic mixes genres in a wonderful way that is both aesthetically unique and gorgeous while also having engaging and fun gameplay, whether alone or with friends.Controls are top-par and both movement and shooting feels smooth and responsive. The ever-changing environments ensure that you never know what to expect or where to go, as  is entirely randomly generated; effectively adding a rogue-like element.Pick between four different dorf miner classes, from the agile scout who can zip around like Spoodermon with his cable gun to the grizzled driller who can quickly carve makeshift tunnels through the destructible environment with his trusty dual-wielded boreheads. Or go oldschool and play the veteran gunner who just blows sh** up with his arsenal of 800-pound gatling guns and equally heavy magnum space revolver.Rank up your dwarves to unlock more weaponry and perks that can be best suited to your playstyle and make things a  easier as you venture into higher tiers of difficulty. And die anyway. Cus, y'know, this game gets friggin' challenging. And that's good.DRG is a breath of fresh air in the modern gaming scene. A game that blends popular elements and genres from games like Doom, Minecraft and Vermintide into a title that works exceptionally well at what it does. A proper gem that should not be passed up by anyone who enjoys either of the above.I rate this game 10.5 Dorfs out of Short Women With Beards.

_childDocuments_.review: Deep Rock Galactic basically feels like what Helldivers would sorta be if it were an FPS, notable differences being:a) We're dwarves.b) Good news is we work for a seemingly galactic mining company.c) Bad news is we work for a seemingly galactic mining company.d) Beers and ales are common and fun to gulp down.e) No stratagems but then again, we're dwarves, we don't need strats.So if yer a fan of Helldivers and specifically the mining part of Minecraft, then this game is for you cause it's both rolled into one! I'd say I'm pleasantly surprised by the amount of things to aim for in the base game alone.You do need to get a feel for the game at first but then again, so does Helldivers. All in all, a 5 beards/5 rating from me.P.S: Do not kick barrels. Have been informed that Management will dock your pay for that.

_childDocuments_.review: Not many games can hold me for more than an hour due to my disorders, but DRG is one of the special cases.Whether it's solo or co-op (With randoms or friends), the randomly generated caves with little to no generation bugs/issues (I've so only encountered one, so far) will provide tons of fun, especially with a variety of missions in their environments.Mix in the mutations, random loot chests and the events, and you've got this very solid and fun game.If you can't be bothered to read it, I like this game a lot.Rock and Stone, brothers.

_childDocuments_.review: Played with a friend, we were casually mining stuff, but he accidentally fell in to a pit with no way back up to me, so I had to come and help him out. Right as I came to him - the swarm started, and after a short while mission control announced, that dreadnought is coming. . We tried our best to defend but we were cornered and quickly overwhelmed with a lot of bugs - decided to flee. Luckily we were cornered into a dirt, which usually leads to another cave. We started to dig as fast as we could, turrets were almost out of ammo, dreadnought was already next to us. But then, we finally dug enough to see a hole to the next area, everything started to explode, we were low on, basically everything and we instantly started to run for our lives from this swarm, my friend shot a platform to seal the hole we ran from. After that we found ourselves at the edge of a cliff, we stopped for a second and then - screw it. We jumped, rolling down the steep ground and found ourselves in a big, radioactive cave, filled with some amount of red sugar . We were stranded, alone, in the silent darkness. The mission control was not responding, like they lost connection to us, pressuring silence, until we managed to recover and complete our main task, and found the way we came from. Felt like it was days ago, like long lost miners. The thing is, this  is still in early access, and can already give you adrenaline rush, similar to the one you used to get when you was rushing solo on final chapter from Left4dead 2.Buy it already, you are a dwarf with a pickaxe, in space. What else do you want?Rock And Stone btw.

_childDocuments_.review: Dwarfs? Big insect swarms? Endless booze? Sign me up! Good game single player, but this game definitely shines in random pubs or with a group of friends fighting the endless swarms of bugs that want to eat your face. Great replayability, randomly procedural generation on every mission, no cave system is the same. Game is actually difficult at the higher levels. Plenty of unlocks for each character, weapons, cosmetics and mods.

_childDocuments_.review: Deep Rock Galactic is one of those games you can keep installed for months, just hopping in for a few missions  to pass some time without worry about being left behind in the long run. There's also something to be said about the generation of terrain in this game. I've never felt like I've seen the same layout twice. Not even remotely. You can compare the procedural generation to other games, but nothing comes close to how unique every mission feels. Knowing nobody else will experience a map in the same way you have is both sad, and very exciting at the same time. By the time you're ready to leave a dive into the mines, you feel a sense of attachment to what you've just accomplished. It's truly something to appreciate.

_childDocuments_.review: - from a technical point of view, the game functions perfectly without lagging or bugged maps- like with any game you buy, check the settings to see which button does what and if you need to lower the graphics- gameplay wise, all the classes feel amazing and all their weapons and tools function as they should- I love the attention to detail on the ships and the character models... next level creativity. I'm not sure how long does it take them to make the updates and seasonal events, but the wait will be more than worth it- 10/10,if you have the money, can't recommend it enough

_childDocuments_.review: Dwarves, procedural generation, digging, and guns. This game was a big surprise to me when I first got it. It is a ton of fun so far that I have played. One of the few early access games I don't regret picking up. The updates come frequently, and it seems the devs are looking to keep updating the game even after release. The main premise of the game, is to dig with pickaxes to mine certain minerals, or grab certain items all while having alien bugs try to attack and kill you. There are multiple classes in the game each with their own upgrade trees. I have mostly only played solo so far, and even solo the game is a lot of fun. Definitely a big recommendation from me.

_childDocuments_.review: I have over 200 hours in this game on steam, probably another 50 from when I initially tried it on gamepass, and could play it 300 hours more and not get bored for a single moment. Whether it be the accessibility of in game cosmetics, the continuous updates the game still receives to this day, or just the appreciation of the fan base and the sneaking in of community memes. Get this game and you will never have a dull moment with it, and remember, when you rock and stone, you're never alone!

_childDocuments_.review: Truly one of the best games I've ever played in my 30+ years of gaming -- just look at how many hours I have in it.  This is a cooperative based game with no PVP.  But don't think it's easy, the PVE gets very challenging!  There are four extremely well balanced classes -- if you don't like one, try another, they all play quite differently.  When I first started playing, I had a favorite class, but now I love them all.  They require different skill sets, so there's always something more for me to learn or get better at.
_childDocuments_.name: Deep Rock Galactic

_childDocuments_.review: This game came a long way since the first version of early access, every aspect they improved upon heavily overtime until it was finished, to expanding environments to explore,adding more weapons,adding more enemies,improving visuals and making the perk system more unique and not just tiny % modifiers.It's really an excellent unique co-op game , offering randomly generated and varied cave system to explore each time you drill down into the planet which make sure runs don't get dull any time soon. Gun play feels fantastic and satisfying thanks to excellent animations on them, satisfying impact, great sound design and the fact enemies lose parts of them as you damage them over time which all contributes to making the shooting feel great. Environments are fully destructible, it's awesome seeing a cave area after a large fire fight, just holes and craters everywhere from explosions,gunfire and what not.Visually the game has a very clean art design that's supported by fantastic lighting and shading, the game often looks gorgeous thanks to the dynamic lighting and lovely shading and colors on offer while at the same time running pretty well, only some of the really big cave areas can chug a bit but mostly it runs great.I easily recommend this if you're looking for a fun and unique co-op experience with some buds, devs did a great job with early access period and created a good finished product that's still getting supported.

_childDocuments_.review: is a great co-op experience with friends or randoms. You can play  with or without friends as the game has a server browser so players can join strangers' lobbies to form a team and embark on mining or hunting adventures that take you to underground caves of unusual biomes that will put on a challenge for players.In , you play as a dwarf that you pick from four classes which are the , the , the , and the . Each team/lobby consists of four players, and there is no limit on how many players can play each class. However, having all the classes present in the game will provide the best experience due to the need of teamwork while mining and navigating in the caves. I'll explain why teamwork is important with one simple scenario, which is when there is a certain mineral located on the ceiling or high up on a wall, the  can shoot platforms while the  uses his grapple hook to conquer hard-to-reach areas. Teamwork is necessary to smoothly operate in expeditions so the players you meet are often very communicative.With all the players helping each other to achieve the same targets, it makes for a very fun experience. The maps are also procedurally generated so they look similar but have different routes. More complex maps will require players to have a better sense of direction and stick with their teammates so they don't get lost or get left behind by their teammates. Solo players have a higher risk of getting killed by waves of enemies so this promotes grouping up to face off against countless enemies that become hungry for dwarf flesh every once in a while.The developers are also very active at updating the game while being very communicative with the playerbase. Bugs are taken seriously and the developers squash bugs rather quickly after they acknowledge the bugs' existence. The game is shaping up to become one of the best co-op games to ever exist with every update that adds fun and exciting new features. Go ahead and try it out.I give this game a

_childDocuments_.review: I was part of the closed testing phase so i have gotten the pleasure of seeing this game grow from a barebones cave digging simulator to a truly remarkable 100% dwarven bug smashing experience. I havent played it constantly over the years but the more updates the game got the longer i got hooked and now i play almost every day. The maps and biomes are lovely made, the missions are entertaining, the fighting is great, the visuals are pretty nice, the tools for cooperation (the laser pointer) are pretty good,  the sheer amount of stuff you can unlock adds a ton of longevity, and the game is full of dwarven personality (like the whole beer system or the voice lines) that just brings everything together. I can only quote the game itself:" ...you've grown into your role and have more than proven yourself. It's my personal pleasure to announce that management has granted your promotion. Rock and Stone, Ghost ship games! Well done."

_childDocuments_.review: Deep Rock Galactic is a unique game that is without a doubt a grind, but still remains replayable for hours. The use of a interactive hub instead of a main menu gives a better sense of dwarf immersion, and its minimal use of 'standard' loading screens is very good.Playing DRG it is clear it's intended to be done co-op. Either with friends or in open-lobby games. The community is welcoming and in the 50+ missions I've done with randoms, 90% have been fun and enjoyable. The use of the laser pointer to mark ores, items and enemies is an amazing addition, instead of having to rely on voice or text communications.Without a doubt DRG should be in everyone's library, especially when it's 50% off. Even so, I would pay full price again for this game. Also, DLC's are cosmetic only, but are worth it to support the developers :)Rock and Stone!This game has had great continuous support for years, absolutely worth a labour of love award :)

_childDocuments_.review: My name is Walter Hartwell White. I live at 308 Negra Arroyo Lane, Albuquerque, New Mexico, 87104. This is my confession. If you're watching this tape, I'm probably dead, murdered by my brother-in-law Hank Schrader. Hank has been building a meth empire for over a year now and using me as his chemist. Shortly after my 50th birthday, Hank came to me with a rather, shocking proposition. He asked that I use my chemistry knowledge to cook methamphetamine, which he would then sell using his connections in the drug world. Connections that he made through his career with the DEA. I was... astounded, I... I always thought that Hank was a very moral man and I was... thrown, confused, but I was also particularly vulnerable at the time, something he knew and took advantage of. I was reeling from a cancer diagnosis that was poised to bankrupt my family. Hank took me on a ride along, and showed me just how much money even a small meth operation could make. And I was weak. I didn't want my family to go into financial ruin so I agreed. Every day, I think back at that moment with regret. I quickly realized that I was in way over my head, and Hank had a partner, a man named Gustavo Fring, a businessman. Hank essentially sold me into servitude to this man, and when I tried to quit, Fring threatened my family. I didn't know where to turn. Eventually, Hank and Fring had a falling out. From what I can gather, Hank was always pushing for a greater share of the business, to which Fring flatly refused to give him, and things escalated. Fring was able to arrange, uh I guess I guess you call it a "hit" on my brother-in-law, and failed, but Hank was seriously injured, and I wound up paying his medical bills which amounted to a little over $177,000. Upon recovery, Hank was bent on revenge, working with a man named Hector Salamanca, he plotted to kill Fring, and did so. In fact, the bomb that he used was built by me, and he gave me no option in it. I have often contemplated suicide, but I'm a coward. I wanted to go to the police, but I was frightened. Hank had risen in the ranks to become the head of the Albuquerque DEA, and about that time, to keep me in line, he took my children from me. For 3 months he kept them. My wife, who up until that point, had no idea of my criminal activities, was horrified to learn what I had done, why Hank had taken our children. We were scared. I was in Hell, I hated myself for what I had brought upon my family. Recently, I tried once again to quit, to end this nightmare, and in response, he gave me this. I can't take this anymore. I live in fear every day that Hank will kill me, or worse, hurt my family. I... All I could think to do was to make this video in hope that the world will finally see this man, for what he really is.

_childDocuments_.review: Maybe my GOTY. It's a great premise, but the execution is incredible. Most fun multiplayer experience in ages, and YMMV but I love even exploring some caves single player with good ol' Bosco. The incredible attention to detail in the social area, dwarf voice, and above all game feel (awesome sound design, animation, VFX, and art all make the tools, weapons, and heavy equipment feel heavy and powerful) all work to make the world immersive and satisfying. Brilliant little design details ranging from beard customization to grinding along your own rollercoaster like pipelines add unexpected moments of joy over and over. I also appreciate the reasonable price point and tiny download size. Have bought this as a gift several times now. This game has helped me connect with some far away friends for gaming. The range of ways to play, the deep cooperative missions with so much variety and replay, all make it a perfect fit for almost any type of player who can see themselves as a space dwarf.

_childDocuments_.review: November of last year, I wrote: "Rocks, Dwarfs, Mining, and Giant Bugs. There isn't much more to ask for. Active devs, neat mechanics."  A year later, I am pleased to say that my statement remains true. DRG has a wonderful development team, which actively works on new content. Unlike most Developers of this era, no Micro-transactions are present in DRG.  This updated review is coming off the heels of Update 35, which has been very well received. New weapons, a new mission type, and their version of a season pass. Which, inherently, the term "season pass" is usually a negative thing nowadays, however, the folks at DRG did it right. It's free, each season lasts several months, and the rewards can be received *after* the season ends. If you play around 10 hours a week, you gain a level an hour. The new pass system seems fairly well designed, and a much better standard I hope the gaming industry takes note of for the future. As always, Gameplay can be a bit grindy and repetitive, but fun nonetheless. With numerous mission types, each randomly generated each time you enter them, with varying modifiers and teammates, it doesn't typically feel too repetitive. Four classes, each with 3 main weapons and two side weapons to pick between, hundreds of different weapon builds, as well as weapon overclocks to really make them *pop*; this allows for immense diversity of character loadouts, and creates immeasurable numbers of play styles. I recommend it to anyone who likes to slay bugs, drink beer, and show your worth, as a dwarven convict. Content is a tad bit on the smol side, but the game is mainly focused around progression and playing with friends/other dwarves, so it is of little concern, especially when you factor in the replayability. Solo play is fun, but to have consistent fun as a solo, you need to be promoted and have a few good overclocks for that class; otherwise, solo play, for a greenbeard, can get old after a few hours. Great Devs, Great Design, Great Game8.8/10, would play again.Rock and Stone

_childDocuments_.review: This is incredible.  Ghost Ship Games is amazingly in tune with what is fun about a game.  There are many minor details in Deep Rock Galactic that make your playing experience very enjoyable.  This game is fun solo, with randoms, or with friends.  The game is built in a voxel environment, so terrain destruction is quite satisfying, grenades and explosions leave massive craters and you can reshape the terrain. It would be difficult NOT to have the time of your life playing this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy this game, I'm nominating it as my "labor of love" for the steam awards because it's well-polished, funny, and actually pretty challenging. They managed to do the "fully destructible environment" without making it kill your PC or look ugly. The art direction and style works perfectly for having a fun level of detail without being distracting, or once again choking out your PC. One of the big points in this game's favor is that all of the gameplay is FREE. The DLC they offer are additional cosmetics which while snazzy, aren't actually required. I really love seeing a game with having DLC content only being cosmetics, and supporting the game itself with new patches and seasons. While this method doesn't work for every kind of game, I feel like it really works well for a multiplayer-focused game. Deep Rock can be played solo or played with friends, personally I recommend you play with friends/other folks as the party banter is hilarious. Did I mention you get to play as a SPACE DWARF? All dwarves from Tolkien to Dwarf Fortress to Minecraft will absolutely love this gem of a game. Full recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: My favorite game !So, after almost a 2000 hours of gameplay, I am ready to state what is this game about, and what is special about it.in shortsolo or up to 4 players CO-OP, choose between 4 unique classes of dwarfs, go on a missions underground in a randomly generated caves in a 10 different biomes, more than 50+ different type of enemies (aliens, plants, robots, flying and ground insects, and even bosses) all with their own mechanics, abilities, and weakspots, mine minerals, kill enemies, finish your main objective, and extract to complete the mission.what makes Deep Rock Galactic special:1- No mission is the same ! :  every cave is generated with a lot of different combination, so every mission will be special in terms of atmosphere and exploration, and even spawned enemies and items. you could find gold and many more materials, or some rare items, lost treasures, optional trials that grants rewards, and much more.2- you are free to choose between a scale of difficulty from 1 to 5 before starting any mission, so if you are trying to chill and go on a relaxing mission, you can select hazard 1 or 2, while if you are here for a challenge, select hazard 4 or 5.3-solo player? no worries you have the option to bring with you an AI drone that can be commanded to help you through out the mission.4-not a solo player and no friends? no worries again, host your mission as a public, or join other players that has the same mission you are on. 90% of the time you will find a group5-no micro transactions, no locked missions behind real life money! : everything is obtainable for free, the only paid things are the DLC's which are simply just cosmetics, and does not gain any sort of advantages, besides there are tons of free cosmetics in game already, armors, weapon skins, pickaxe appearance and much more.6- another special thing about this game which shows you how amazing the developers of this game are is that we are now in season 5 and guess what?, every battle pass is free !!, for example if you liked something in season 2 battle pass, a weapon skin, framework, pickaxe part, armor or whatever item you could just activate the season and grind for that item, so you have every battle pass from season 1 to 5 in your POCKET !a little extra details: -unlock many perks that enhance your class, in total if all slots unlocked, you can equip 3 passive perks and 2 active ones. -every class has a total of 6 unique weapons, a total of 24 weapons !-every weapon has a different upgrades which you can combine with overclock to change how the weapon works and damage entirely, but it is not just the weapons, even class equipment can be enhanced.-there is a total of 16 unique throwables.-some missions has modifiers that affects the mission in a positive or a negative way, "anomalies" are on your side, such as extra gold, low gravity, double XP, and much more. while "warnings" on the other side increase the difficulty of the mission, such as an infestation of a creature, a plague, higher spawn rate of projectile or explosion based enemies , low oxygen that limits your movement distance and much more.

_childDocuments_.review: The best early access game I've ever played (not joking about that).Game isn't complex, not by a long shot. It's a simple game about simple things but the execution of the simplicity that is this game is amazing. the combat is like a horde shooter, so you get the small "trash" units and then the heavy boys who slap each with their own unique look and design so you can easily tell who is the bigger threat. The classes or Dwarfs all have their pros and cons E.G Gunner is slow but really good at controlling a crowd of bugs, Scout is used more for support rather than in the thick of combat, he snipes and uses flares to light up the surrounding area to help the team out with visibility and is used to take out the big boys. so the game is simple but more important fun.If you have the cash I would highly recommend giving this game a fair chance as it's one the best examples of a good early access game.

_childDocuments_.review: About time I put in my two cents on this absolute masterpiece of a game.This is a first person shooter with spelunking elements, you dive into randomly generated caves with preset mission objectives as one of four different classes, complete your primary and secondary objectives and then evac out via a drop-pod. Deep Rock Galactic gets so many elements right that its difficult to talk about it all without seeming like a total fan-boy. So i'll try to get to the point quickly:Classes are excellently crafted and balanced finely, plenty of combat play-styles, each has their own ways of navigating the caves and crunching through enemy hordes. Scout is the pathfinder of the team, he does good damage but has somewhat limited ammo capacity, meaning he doesn't deal with hordes too well but he can get anywhere and provide lighting and supporting fire. A clutch class that can finish tight objectives and missions in dire situations.Engineer has excellent base firepower but limited range, as you upgrade his kit you get access to tools that allow for powerful tactics via planning, for example, he has a platform gun that allows the building of bridges or plugging on gaps, but an upgrade on this causes enemies to avoid stepping on the platforms (To an extent) which means that you can funnel enemies and create kill zones, combine that with a proximity mine and a sentry gun and you can completely change the flow of a cave/fight.Driller has the highest skill ceiling via his ability to straight up drill tunnels through any part of the cave, makes him excellent on extractions as you can just drill straight back to the drop-pod providing you've got the fuel remaining. His weapon upgrades also scale the hardest, meaning a low level driller feels quite weak but get him to end game and you can single handedly decimate entire hordes. Before playing driller, you may think "Who would ever play him? I get by just fine."  but after playing him you'll go "How does anyone ever play without driller, this is incredible!"Gunner brings high sustained damage output and is the front-line of the team, a high damage bruiser who will reinforce the team and push you through any hordes. Pretty much the least mobile class but has a shield generator that provides a safety bubble for the team to breathe for a few seconds. You can build is weapons is so many different ways that he can specialised in any way required and plug any gaps in a teams strengths.Combat is extremely fun, enemies are satisifying to kill as you can blow chunks off any foe, armour gets shot to pieces, toothy jaws splattering on the cave walls from shotgun blasts, the size of the hordes is enough to get the blood going and there enemies are plenty varied. Exploring the games is essentially a puzzle in itself as you figure out how to navigate it and secure the resources held within.Mission types are hugely varied now as well, with the new additions being extremely fun, everyone has their own favourites and you can choose whatever you fancy.  Beyond the game itself, the Dev's are a truly great bunch, they've taken on many suggestions from the community, including a suggestion or two from myself which just feels great, a fantastic example was when weapon skins were first introduced, colours and weapon meshes (Meshes change the model of the gun) were exclusive to one another (So you could either pick a new colour OR a new mesh) but a bug allowed you to apply the colours to the meshes and within a couple of months, the dev's straight up added this, allowing you to pick a mesh and a colour scheme together. They're talkative, helpful and great people. The community is also very lovely with one small exception, the ideas board for Deep Rock is really saturated with a lot of repeated suggestions and the communities patience grows a little thin with people suggesting the same thing over and over again (Mostly about new classes) but honestly, i'm nit-picking - In game, the community is lovely and you have full control over your lobbies, so if someone is being as ass, you can kick them.The Montisation has been on point as well, with only a couple of cosmetic DLC's and the cosmetics earnable in game are absolutely stellar, so don't think you need to spend any extra money to look like a badass. Give it a go, its a absolute blast to play alone, with randoms and friends. Cannot recommend enough, a rare gem in today's over-saturated, mass-produced, money milking treadmill games.Rock and stone brothers.

_childDocuments_.review: This game kicks butt.  The four available classes all compliment each other in nice ways.  Not having one of them available immediately becomes apparent, which things like massive open gaps making you go "I wish we had a gunner for his ziplines."  Or seeing materials high up on a wall you can't reach and lamenting "I wish we had a scout to get those."The game can be played singleplayer, if for whatever reason you want to do that.  Bosco, the little robot that will accompany you, is suitably powerful.  He floats, never needs to reload, lights up areas, can revive you (but only a set number of times as compared to the unlimited times you can be rezzed in multiplayer) and will even haul large mineable objects around if you order him to.  While it's still better to play with a full team, if you want to go it alone for whatever reason, Bosco has your back.  And if you're playing multiplayer and everyone but you leaves, he'll show up anyways so you can at least stand a chance of finishing.  Good robot, best friend.The random generated caves are always fun to go through, with the comment of "I hate this place" being fairly common, but in a good way.  There's tons of ways to navigate and with full destructable terrain, you can always make your own path.  Don't want to take a long winding trail back to the drop pod?  If you got a driller and he has the fuel to spare, just dig in a straight line to extraction.  Nothing besides a ticking countdown timer says you can't and 99% of the time, you'll make it with minutes to spare.I will say it is MUCH better to play with people you know vs randoms.  Don't get me wrong, I've had random players who never spoke a word but stuck near teammates and did everything they needed to do and then some all without communication, but this is a game where four people in a voice chat coordinating what they're doing will ALWAYS be better than some drop in people who might just leave the moment things go wrong.  Karl wouldn't approve of them.If you're looking for a good team based game where you mine 50% of the time, fight bugs 40%, and spend about 10% traversing through random generated caverns just delving deeper and deeper into this hellhole of a planet, then you'll love this game.  And it's not even out of Early Access yet and it's basically a full fledged game!  How awesome is that?  Heck, they're putting together (at time of this review) the finishing touches on the End Game stuff right now!   And there's STILL stuff they want to add.  THIS is the kind of game people want from developers. Rock and Stone brother.

The in-game hazard levels provide an excellent progression challenge and the new addition of modded hazard levels showing up in the server browser makes the difficulty and fun exponential. I took a long hiatus from the game at a certain stage and came back when the addition of overclocks was introduced. this reinvigorated some excitement in the game for me in that the weapons and tools had a massive new potential. overclocks and my desire for some OP ones, has kept me engaged. I know which ones I really want and still haven't gotten them all after months of casual grinding. I kind of love that..The developers engage a lot online and are constantly fulfilling and entertaining the communities requests and fantasies. This is one hell of a game with a near cult-like community if you are into this kind of thing. Space dwarves killing alien bugs, craft beer mission buffs, a mutual and well understood disdain for elves.. just give it a shot if this perks your ears... hopefully they are'nt pointy..

_childDocuments_.review: 3 questions. Do you like Darkness? Danger? Dwarves? If so, then look no further as you find all three in this glorious hole digging adventure.This game is probably one of the best early access games I have seen. I myself really enjoy the way they had made this game. (All the maps are procedurally generated too) (Also runs great, always 100+ FPS max settings with a 1060)There are four different classes in this game. You have the Engineer, who happens to have a glorious beard, has a automatic shotgun, grenade launcher, platform gun (Which will shoot a projectile that creates a platform for your team to stand on for various reasons), and 2 sentry turrets. The turrets themselves once are placed down will need to be constructed, which doesn't take long (I think it's like 4 or so seconds, and can go quicker with multiple people building it). They will automatically target hostiles and shoot at them, which when they run out of ammo, you'll have to resupply them with. (You can recall your turrets to your inventory with R).The Gunner is the brawn, with free tickets to all of his gun shows. He has a gatling gun (Which overheats if you continuously fire it for too long), a revolver for some longer range engagements, a zipline gun to allow his team to easily get from point A to B (wether it's a large gap or elevated), an satchel charges (Which are great for dealing with swarms of large enemies)The Driller is a bit like a naked mole rat. He brings a flamethrower to deal with the pesky hordes of small creatures, he also brings a pistol just in case he needs it, his power drills are useful for digging through the compact dirt between caverns/tunnels, burrowing tunnels back the pod or just a simple staircase. The detonation packs he brings leave a huge boom-boom that are like a nuclear F-Bomb (They're basically just satchel charges.)The Scout is a dwarf that is faster than the gnome Keemstar. He has an assault rifle which gets less accurate as it fires (surprising right?) which is good for some long range tapping or some good ol' spray n' pray. The double barrel shotgun he brings packs a huge punch but it's range isn't the best. The grappling hook is amazing for getting around large packs of enemies when needed, reaching high up places, scouting ahead for any mission objective ores/items. He also has a flare gun which shoots a very bright "flare dart" that sticks to surfaces and lights up a cavern for a bit.There are 2 main forms of light in the game. Your headlamp (Which kind of sucks but is good for it's purpose) and flares. Flares you just throw to light the way, they change colour based on your class. Without any upgrades on the flares, you can hold 3 (4 with the upgrade) and they start recharging as soon as one is thrown. It doesn't take long for them to regenerate. There is also the Scout's Flare Gun, which is the best source of light.While you are mining, enemies may just randomly come in small hordes at you, which can overwhelm you if not careful. But the waves, you will be alerted for them, and alerted again when it is almost over. They can be easy or really hard depending on the difficulty you play on.For storing minerals, you have your M.U.L.E. which follows you around and allows you to deposit minerals for the mission.For missions. There are 4 kinds of missions, Mining Expeditions, Collection, Elimination and Point Extraction.Mining Expedition is just your classic go in and mine x amount of Morkite, and some optional items and get out. It generally is just more tight tunnels than large chasms.Collection is where you are searching for eggs, but they are not in the open. They are normally behind panels of dirt with red bubbles coming off of them. The caves are small chambers connected by compacted dirt normally. Along with optional items too.Elimination is when you are hunting for these large Glyphid Cocoons. The map generally is tight, but multiple chambers with some open areas for fighting the cocoons. You also have the optional items to gather too.Point Extraction is where looking for Aquarq, a blue glowing mineral, along with another optional objective. You don't have a M.U.L.E. for this mission so you have to carry back all the Aquarq you find to the mine head. These are not out in the open like Morkite, they are embedded in walls and can be found by small blue crystals embedded in said wall. You must dig said wall. These Aquarq also take both hands to carry and you cannot equip anything while carrying them without dropping it. Which is okay to kill stuff. The cave is generally one large cavern with pillars and items high up or lower down.There are a decent bit of enemy kinds in the game, I won't go over in detail, but there are essentially the-Tanks -Soldiers -Swarmers -Spitters (Web and Acid) -KamikazeBriefly, but important, progression. There isn't a whole lot, but it's neat. Every class has their own upgrades on their universal stuff that suits them personally, along with upgrades for their guns and tools, along with new guns to unlock for each classNow for my own thoughts on the game. This game is great to play online and with friends. Especially with friends.The dev's from what I have heard/seen are active and proud of their work they have done, and I can say I am proud that they are properly using the early access system and their progress. I have heard of hack that just gives you a bunch of credits and ores ruining your progression in the game. I myself would hate to have this happen to me. I highly recommend this game, and I am hoping to see this game leave early access with significant progress. I also really like the low polygon count art style.To the devs (If they read this): If you don't already have this on a to-do list, I would suggest adding perks for the individual classes and unlocking new weaponry for the classes. :)

_childDocuments_.review: 'bout time I left an employee review, Deep Rock Galactic got me working a few hours.TL;DR: Best job ever.A game that scratches all the right itches. Even though graphics are far from realistic, I immediately feel immersed when I enter the space rig; I'm a dwarf with a job to do, so hurry up and finish your beer ya leaf lovers. On one hand, I spend a lot of times laughing at the shenanigans these dwarves get in to. Whether it's greenbeards getting hit by a supply pod or the driller blowing himself up with c4 (this happens a lot). Even though you can be mixed with inexperienced dwarves, I rarely find myself frustrated about it, the community is generally top notch and wants to learn. The game really drives you to work together too, it's incredibly satisfactory to combine some of those nifty gadgets to traverse the terrain that looks like the seventh layer of hell. It's easy to find each other and point at things with your laser tool, there's no gain in claiming kills/minerals for yourself. Polite dwarves salute their fellow miners when they are granted access to those precious minerals. I think the mechanics are great.On the other hand, when the moment comes you hear Mission Control broadcast "SWARM!" and the ominous soundtrack starts playing, it becomes a serious hardcore FPS, with waves of bugs starting to hit you from all sides. Once again teamwork is key here, true dwarves stand side by side mashing aliens into green paste. No matter how many waves I've made my way through, this still gets my blood pumping. Oh and have I mentioned massive exploding bulk detonators?The four classes are well balanced with each their own pros and cons, two sets of unique primary/secondary weapons, 3 unique grenades, a unique bug control tool (like sentries or the c4) and a unique traversal tool. The devs have been adding awesome "overclocks" to the game as well, which can really change things up, turning the engineer's grenade launcher into a nuke launcher for example. A lot of tweaks and stuff have been added since I start playing, each one better than the previous, keeping things interesting for a veteran like me. And even though this game is great already, I can still see room for great expansions with current mechanics, keep it up devs.All and all, a true work of art, heavily focused on co-op and crazy beards.So what are you waiting for ya whale piper? We've got a job to do.Edit: Nominated for "better with friends" because I have not yet completed a single solo mission in all these hours

With the updates the game has received over the last two years, Ghost Ship Games is dedicated to meeting the roadmap updates that they have promised to the playerbase, meeting expectations thus far.Update: Ghost ship games has recently delivered 2 new game modes which deviate from the norm of resource gathering that is prevalent in the older missions.  These have proven to be a step in the right direction, with additional mission types, biomes and enemies being planned early next year.  Hopefully the dev team continues to deliver what they promise to the community.

_childDocuments_.review: HISTORY OF THE DWARFSThe Dwarves are one of races that inhabit Middle-earth in Tolkien’s universe. They play a central role in both The Hobbit and The Lord of the Rings. In the Poetic Edda, in Völuspá (Voluspa), the dwarves are created from the blood of Brimir and the limbs of Blain. Both names are other names for the giant Ymir, who was killed by the Aesir (a clan of Norse gods).Snorri Sturluson tells the story in his Gylfaginning from the early 13th century of how, with Odin at the helm, the Aesir created ​​the earth out of of the dead body of Ymir. Brimir’s blood became the sea and Blain’s limbs, the mountains (created by his bones).All of the dwarves’ names are mentioned in the Poetic Edda. There are many similarities between the dwarf names mentioned in the Poetic Edda and in Tolkien’s works, including Durin, Bombur, Nori, Thorin and Egeskjold. Tolkien makes a big point of mentioning the dwarves by name when they are introduced in The Hobbit. And the myth of their origin and family relationships is also more complex in Tolkien’s universe than in medieval literature.In the Sagas, dwarves often have great insight and are described as very clever. In the Edda poem Alvíssmál, Thor takes on the dwarf Alvis, which means “all-wise”, in a battle of wits. The dwarves are often associated with extensive knowledge and skills in the art of forging. Several of the Norse gods’ most famous weapons and pieces of jewellery were created by the dwarves. Skáldskaparmál describes how Loki contacts the dwarves called Ivalde’s sons. They produce golden hair for Sif (Thor’s wife), Skidbladner (Frey’s magic ship, which is no larger than a handkerchief when not in use), and Odin’s spear, Gungnir. Two other dwarves, Brok and Sindri, forge Mjolnir (Thor’s hammer), Draupnir (Odin’s magic ring) and the magic boar, Gullinbursti, for Frey.The dwarves also belong to the underground world and cannot tolerate sunlight. When Thor takes on Alvis, it is Thor who asks the questions. The aim is simply to drag it out until the sun rises, ensuring that Thor “wins” the contest, even though the dwarf could solve the riddles. Gandalf makes use of the same trick in The Hobbit, when the travelling party is taken prisoner by three trolls. Gandalf keeps on asking questions, playing for time until the sun rises and the trolls are petrified. And the riddle contest is also used deep inside the mountain, in the legendary riddle contest between Gollum and Bilbo. A number of other stories recount that the dwarves live in boulders or in the mountains. In Norse mythology, the dwarves live in mines and underground halls known as Nidavellir. This draws references to the city in the Lonely Mountain and the ancient capital in the Mines of Moria, described in both The Hobbit and The Lord of the Rings.

_childDocuments_.review: Treat this game as something similar to Left 4 Dead. You have hordes attacking you, and need to complete objectives to get out before they overwhelm you. If you go down, you can be picked back up, but will have next to no health once you do get back up. You have unlimited downs, but trust me when I say all 4 dwarves being downed is common in this game (it is the lose condition after all). Certain dwarves struggle against specific enemy types, and building to counter that weakness will make you weak to something else. Unless you're a *really* good player overall, SOMETHING will be a nuisance to you in this game. These weaknesses can be negated by sticking close to your teammates, and working together as a team to get through the horrors of Hoxxes.The game excels as a team-based game, and I consider it to be my current favorite coop title. It's a good time running from a horde of a hundred Glyphids as your whole downed team is getting pounded into the floor by 3 Oppressors.Do be warned though, that you will have seen all of the content the game has to offer at only a few hundred hours. I have as many as I do from wanting to get Gunner to Legendary. The game is incredibly grindy with not really enough gameplay content to warrant replaying as much as I have. Expect a few hundred hours, and unless you're really committed, you will start getting bored like I did.Updates are slow, non-cosmetic content even slower. Mods definitely help this, though.I'd add more here, but at that point, I should be making a Deep Rock Galactic Ultimate Guide. It's a good title, like with Left 4 Dead 2. Pick it up, even at full price. It's 100% worth the purchase.

_childDocuments_.review: Banana Bread recipe :Difficulty: Easy PREP TIME  10 mins  COOK TIME 55 mins  TOTAL TIME 65 minsIngredients : -2 to 3 medium (7" to 7-7/8" long) very ripe bananas, peeled (about 1 1/4 to 1 1/2 cups mashed)-1/3 cup butter, unsalted or salted, melted-1/2 teaspoon baking soda-1 pinch salt-3/4 cup sugar (1/2 cup if you would like it less sweet, 1 cup if more sweet)-1 large egg, beaten-1 teaspoon vanilla extract-1 1/2 cups all purpose flour1.Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C), and butter a 4x8-inch loaf pan. a mixing bowl, mash the ripe bananas with a fork until completely smooth. Stir the melted butter into the mashed bananas.3.Mix in the baking soda and salt. Stir in the sugar, beaten egg, and vanilla extract. Mix in the flour.4.Pour the batter into your prepared loaf pan. Bake for 50 minutes to 1 hour at 350°F (175°C), or until a toothpick or wooden skewer inserted into the center comes out clean. A few dry crumbs are okay; streaks of wet batter are not. If the outside of the loaf is browned but the center is still wet, loosely tent the loaf with foil and continue baking until the loaf is fully baked.5.Remove from oven and let cool in the pan for a few minutes. Then remove the banana bread from the pan and let cool completely before serving. Slice and serve. (A bread knife helps to make slices that aren't crumbly.)Wrapped well, the banana bread will keep at room temperature for 4 days. For longer storage, refrigerate the loaf up to 5 days, or freeze it.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, DRG runs pretty well. I have encountered no crashes during my current ~56 hours of playtime, nor any gamebreaking bugs or glitches. I have encountered very occasional and brief stutters during hectic gunfights, but those are extremely minuscule and rare enough to hardly be worth mentioning. There is some weirdness to the games’ physics, which seems to be intended by the developer but can lead to some strange interactions with the game environment. For example, any movement seems to carry momentum, meaning that the player may stand still on a rising platform, but jumping off will carry the momentum of the platform regardless of which direction they may be jumping.Being a game that features fully destructible terrain, DRG is not a particularly "good" looking game, but it carries its art style confidently. There is great variety in how to customize any of your four playable dwarves, and where the game lacks in visual fidelity, it makes up for it with charm. For example, the Space Rig, a smallish hub area the player returns to between missions, feels like more than "just" a bit of empty space with a bunch of upgrade terminals. Instead, there are pseudo-minigames, little knickknacks that are scattered around waiting to be found and played with, and copious amounts of things to coax out interactions between players in a multiplayer lobby.Dwarves may not be identifiable at a single glance, but enemies are. Despite there only largely being two categories of foes you may encounter: bugs and robots, sub-types are quite easily recognizable, which enhances the gameplay experience of the faster swarm fights. The same holds true for biomes; while there may not be an immense variety, the simpler but still distinct look and geometry subtly teach the player how to navigate each of the different areas.The music at large is good and features a solid selection of tracks. Guns feel weighty, and the voice acting, even when comedic, never feels grating or otherwise out-of-place, which is something that a lot of more humorous games tend to struggle with. There is some noticeable repetition of voice-lines, and the mission "narrator" can be overly chatty during certain moments, such as constantly and obnoxiously screaming at players during the M.U.L.E. salvage objective if they leave the contested zone.Fundamentally, Deep Rock Galactic is a L4D-esque co-op FPS. The L4D comparison here is incredibly light and is more so to reference the very core principle of the game being co-op-centric and each map featuring occasional enemy swarm mechanics. DRG also sets itself apart by having a class system: gunner, engineer, driller, and scout. Each of which comes with a main- and subweapon; a traversal tool, for example, a zipline; and a grenade weapon. Important to note here is that this means that while every dwarf has a distinct niche that they excel in, they all have tools to engage with the environment and the map objectives.In total, there are eight different map objectives that cycle on a global thirty-minute timer across the eleven different biomes. Additionally, they spawn with three modifiers: cave complexity, cave length, and affixes. This means that a player's favorite objective may not always be available on the map of their choosing and may be further altered by the aforementioned modifiers. Thus, it’s also hard to gauge how long a game of DRG may actually take, as I’ve seen any of those objectives last between ten and fifty minutes, making it hard to view DRG as a game to just hop into on the fly.The only other game mode is Deep Dives, which is merely a kind of hard mode that ties three regular missions together with shared resources across all of them. These also cycle on a regular basis and provide the last tier of progression for the player characters in the form of 'Overclocks'. These are items that can be crafted after randomly obtaining their recipe through those aforementioned Deep Dives, and they strongly tweak the gameplay of any of the weapons they are attached to. Like with the seasonal affixes, these provide a decent incentive to keep playing the game, but fundamentally do not offer a different experience from the basic missions. Deep Rock Galactic does not feature any sort of campaign or story missions. It does, however, hint at its sci-fi setting and has some surface-level worldbuilding. In general, players are part of the titular mining company, Deep Rock Galactic, with the dwarves themselves being somewhat of an elite force that is only sent to the most dangerous digsites, one of which is Hoxxes IV, where the game takes place. The rest is delivered through voicelines during the missions themselves; these, however, never get more detailed than hinting at the ideals of the company or the deadliness of Hoxxes, but more so through the subtext of the assignments given to the player. Assignments are little more than milestones that are unlocked by playing a selection of missions in order to unlock an upgrade, be it a new weapon, cosmetic items, etc. Deep Rock Galactic is a fantastic experience in a quite narrow genre. If you’re willing to adhere to the game’s progression systems, are looking for an almost strictly multiplayer experience, and are willing to overlook the lack of immersive elements in favor of charm and humouristic presentation, then DRG is a pretty safe recommendation, whereas players who are looking for a more flexible gameplay loop, are completionists, or may not have enjoyed games from this genre earlier will probably not find anything groundbreaking here.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't recommend this game enough.  This is an actual coop game where the strengths of all can lead to some truly sublime gameplay.  When every player is using the strengths of their character you actually feel like a team, not a gang of random yahoos competing for individual glory.In essence this is a mining game crossed with Left for Dead.  You and (up to) 3 others get dropped into a dark cave to complete various types of mission, mine resources, defeat a boss, collect eggs, repair stuff.  Each player has a unique role, the gunner has a big gun and a zipline, the engineer can place platforms to help with resource collection and has 2 turrets to help with crowd control, the driller is able to drill through the environment and the scout has a reusable zipline and can light up the environment.  Along the way you collect minerals and gold to fund upgrades to weapons and buy cosmetics.  There are always resources to find and collect.  It's an important point to note that just collecting the minerals feels satisfying and rewarding, they nailed this aspect of the game.But the game really comes alive when it shifts to its other "phase", that is when a swarm of enemies attack, and then you have to defend against a seemingly endless stream of enemies.  In this regard its very like L4D, but there are more enemy types, each with their own weaknesses and you need to learn how to deal with all of them.  The environments are procedurally generated, no two caves are the same but they follow general patterns, the same applies to swarms.  There are special enemy types, the first time you encounter a bulk detonator your first instinct is to run and it's well founded but after a while you learn how to deal with them yourself.A significant difference with L4D however is that you get to pick your own difficulty, every mission has a "hazard level", ranging from 1-5.  If you aren't wanting to change your underpants then maybe go for a level 2-3 mission, or if you wore your official DRG stone panties that morning maybe go for a level 5.  The hazard level changes the amount and difficulty of enemies (your own personal character level also has an impact on this, as does the number of players in a team), so you get to choose what you feel comfortable with but with higher levels comes higher rewards.There is character progression in the game, you can level up each character, their weapons and kit.  Each weapon is well designed and fits with the theme of the character, for example the scout is not designed to take on swarms so his weapons are weak, as a scout your movement is your biggest advantage.  The gunner is designed to take on swarms so his weapons are powerful but his mobility is limited.  There is also a bewildering array of cosmetics that you can buy (with resources you get while playing, no microtransactions here!) so you can customize your character however your like.With update 25 coming up, the replayability of the game will go up although I enjoy the game playing just for its core mechanics of collection and combat.

_childDocuments_.review: (Insert YogsCast Diggy Diggy Hole)So this game is Dwarves in space. There are 4 classes to play as. Shooty boy, Runny boy, Helpy boy, and Diggy boy. You mine through a procedurally (eNGLIsh) generated level, and these levels change depending on the area, as well as the mission. You get to drink bear, either to harm your self horrendously through creative means, or give your self an edge on certain things, such as gaining more resources more quickly for one of the missions. The beneficial ones are random and only last for one mission. No Ubermensch status for you.The variety of enemies is great. The main hostile force you will counter is the Glyphid Swarms, the main inhabitants of Hoxxes, the planet.The 2nd enemy would be the Mactera Blight. The rest are your random affair of creatures that have grown here, such as rolly pollys and those stupid brain numbing cave leeches.The weapons at your disposal is a rather substantial arsenal, with your primary and secondary having 2 options, and the upgrades adjustable and many. Speaking of upgrades, should your stones and jewels be of sterner stuff, you will achieve a promotion giving you some neat little prizes.I personal recommend just buying the game before you see more, but your choice.So when you reach promotion, you will have some neat options available to you, all of witch revolving around the usage of the Forge, also granted upon promotion. The forge allows the crafting of cosmetics, special victory poses for your alpha male pheromones to be satisfied, and OVERCLOCKS. Cosmetics, if you for some reason are unfamiliar with this term, are basically special paint jobs for your weapons, as well as special beards hair and other such jazz. Victory poses you'll know if you play. Overclocks are the upgrades beyond what you can already purchase, with a mix of Clean overclocks, giving a small boost to some stats, balanced, giving a buff and a debuff, and an unstable overclock, granting a strong power or great buff along with some kind of substantial debuff. The other prize for promotion is availability to a mission assignment to get more matrix cores (*What items are referred to that is in the forge) With sometimes giving you a blank, which you can use when you encounter these random events known as Machine events, which are only activatable by your self after promoting a dwarf, but others can activate it if they have and you have not. There's not much in it for you though besides a fun challenge and an XP boost. Upon completion, you can use a blank core one the activation mechanism to choose one of 3 matrix cores. And thus, the final reward for those Dwarves that have climbed the ladder of the many, you have also become eligible for the DEEP DIVES!!!!!!!!!!!! There are Regular ones and Elite ones. These are essentially 3 missions tied together, and your gold and another resource are carried onwards as you play. The Elite Dices are the ones that requires the most teamwork as well as the most vigilance. And that's pretty much it. There will most likely be more since this game is still in beta. I can give it a good pass. Anything I didn't mention you're just gonna have to get yer arse up n get diggin!                                 For Karl, Rock and Stone.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is like a combination of Minecraft and Left 4 Dead, except better. Sprinting through caves at the end of the mission, intense music playing, alien creatures hot on your heels and flamethrower in hand, it's the first game in a long time to get my heart racing in fear and excitement at once. The character customization is fun and fresh, beard styles to choose from, different clothing items to buy as you level, santa hats too! And with that, the progression system is good, constantly rewarding you with new mission types and areas to play, along with cosmetic items for purchase. One of the best things about the game is definitely the HUB area. You can interact with plenty of different objects, kick stuff, get yelled at by Mission Control for it, visit a few different areas and get blind drunk at the bar with you Dwarven friends!Having 4 different classes and a completely destructable environment gives you many different ways to take on a fight. Use the Engineer's turrets to cement a defensive position, go guns blazing with the Gunner's minigun and offensive firepower, Bunker into a wall with the Driller's HUGE drills and set traps with his Satchel Charge, or keep on the move with the Scout's ability to quickly traverse the environment with his grappling hook... or combine all of your abilities together with 3 friends and create the ultimate defence against those pesky aliens.If you're on the fence about this game, just do yourself a favour, get the damn game and then get your friends to get it too.EDIT: Look, I just have to come back and say that the Developers are doing a great job. They have overwhelming support for this game, and are very active about letting the community know about future updates, in the form of a roadmap and their Twitter Account @JoinDeepRock . My opinion stands. This game is so fun. With the new added difficulty (Haz 5) and completely overhauled weapon modding system, the game always seems to dish out fresh content, so there is always something fun to play around with. Update 25 looms around the corner as I am currently typing, projected for late September. It is to add late game mission such as Deep Dives, hard, endgame mission that reward you heavily with not only credits and resources, but the potential for Functional Weapon Mods and Cosmetic Weapon Mods. The Devs put in some time to properly explain this system in a video that you can easily find on youtube, just search 'Deep Rock Galactic Update 25' and you should find a video released by Ghost Ship Games. The voice of the Mission Control is so perfectly done. The voices in general feel like they are just done right. Whether they're screaming 'Molly!' at the top of their lungs, proclaiming the hideousness of the foul creatures before you, or Mission Control frantically sputtering "Five!.. Ten!.. ah? ALOT of aliens coming at you!" Combine this with a perfect soundtrack. Combat Music that can only be rivalled by you playing 'Thunderstruck' as you cut down hordes, and ambient music that fulfills the adventurous exploring of caves.Alot of the new underground biomes they added are IMMENSE! I specfically remember a mining mission, with random Dwarves. We entered a cavern that put other mining games to shame. You couldn't see the other side. We navigated it on branching rock formations, utilising the Gunners Ziplines and the Scouts Flaregun. Everyone was baffelled by the sheer size of it, we felt miniscule. Other biomes share amazing lighting that makes you feel starstruck, filled with wonder. It is unreal.I cannot exclaim how good the developers are at communicating with the community. I find myself taking some time off this game, waiting for the next update, stalking twitter accounts for scraps of information to fuel my desire to play when the next update drops, I share this information with friends in an attempt to coax them into playing a magnificent game. The game just makes me truly happy inside, an early access game which isn't a crap heap, but rather, a blossoming flower that I'm sure one day, is going to get a tonne of exposure and take off astronomically. Spelunking. Cave Diving. Alien Slaughtering.Dig. Shoot. Kill.Guns. Gold. Glory.Beards. Beer. Party.Rock. Stone. Bone. Danger. Darkness. Dwarves.It doesn't get any better than this, friends. Strap up, strap in, we got a fight ahead of us.Edit: Oh wow! They added more mission which are *amazing* and they keep striving for more. Lovez

Like both of those?  You'll love this to death as my friends and I have.  Already bought it for my wife as well...Although I had a couple of crashes, technically this is already better optimised and more beautifully rendered than many PC games are today, after shipping and late patching.  Gorgeous stuff and refreshing to see the core game already so gleaming.  They take advantage of the processing headroom they gain with low-poly graphics by cranking the texture shaders and reflections to 11.  Play this on all-Epic settings and you see real-time reflections that embarass AAA games - all without slowdown.I have full confidence that they'll add more cruft and late-game material to cement this one as a defining example of the co-op wave-fighter genre done stunningly right.Update: since the review they've lost most of that processing headroom by cranking up environmental effects and room sizes to levels that were absolutely impossible to see years ago, and that's honestly not a bad thing, lol

_childDocuments_.review: Sometimes I wonder if mining is all there is to life, then I punch myself in the nose. YOU!Shut up. Take this gun. Keep your head down. Stay on my ass. Don't touch anything but your trigger. Grow a beard. Drink. Tip the bartender. Bring friends. Be excellent to each other.It's Left 4 Dead crossed with Starship Troopers, with Dwarves in space. An OSHA nightmare simulator.My wife says it’s like the movie Aliens meets Snow White plus beer.My wife’s boyfriend says it’s like spelunking in Minecraft, but with guns, more aggressive mobs, everything is polygonal and looks like a PS2 game, and you’re dwarves playing pretend Pest Control. For me it’s just like Left 4 Dead but instead you get to take revenge on the entire spider population of Australia.Just a heads up: The second you download Deep Rock Galactic you become a big manly 37 year old dwarf with a big bushy beard.It’s the saga of 4 space Dwarves that constantly scream "Rock and Stone!", and how they drain a planet of its resources. It's a FPS, but you are a badass Dwarf from space and you fight big ass-spiders and you drink beer and mine for ore that you can trade for money and so you can get cooler guns. Did I mention there is beer? Yup, there’s also an ingame bar you can get sh*t faced in.So… you got an irrational fear and hate of bugs? Well down here at Deep Rock Galactic we give you a chance to exterminate those fu*kers!You're a space dwarf employed by a mining Corporation that sends you on suicidal missions to bug infested planets, missions include: retrieving rare minerals, mining precious metals, exterminating space bugs, building infrastructure, search and rescue of mining equipment, etc. You are put into the caves by management with a job to do, so you always have an objective, the progression is great. Boxes will randomly spawn sometimes with some stuff from old events so you will never lose out on some fashion You go alone or with friends into the surface, and complete various missions as enemies try to kill you. The mix of fighting and mission offers a nice balance.The point of the game is to have fun, kill bugs, die horribly on occasion, and mine minerals.  Not necessarily in that order.  There is no narrative to it, it's a free-form sandbox where each map is randomly generated at the start.  It's a lot like Left 4 Dead crossed with Minecraft - the fun comes from playing, fighting, creating, and those close shave escapes where your team barely survives when things go horribly horribly wrong.  Or, on occasion, those desperate last stands where everyone dies and no one escapes.It's a PVE class shooter where each class plays differently (and is very important to the team). You have 4 main classes, each with various weapons, tools, and traversal options. You can upgrade, collect resources, and improve characters. Every class has 3 primary weapons, 3 secondary weapons, 1 support tool, and 1 traversal tool. You only start with 1 of each and have to unlock the 2nd and 3rd primary and secondary weapons by levelling up and doing missions. Also, the soundtrack, although being the genre synthwave and not my style, is incredible. The neutral music can range from mysterious to very ambient to beautiful (listen to Fathomless Tomb), and the chase music is perfect adrenaline fuel. In addition, every class comes equipped with a pickaxe and some throwable, rechargable flares. Every dwarf can shape the environment how they want, but the driller is exceptional at it.You can play Solo, or with up to 4 Players. It doesn’t matter which class you choose, you can have a team of any combination of the different classes, though having all four classes will get you the most whole experience in the mission, as everyone has an important part in the group. You can invite your friends or join a random lobby or host your own public lobby. You can also invite a friend and then have randoms join during the mission, via drop pod.If you like co-op horde-mode style games such as Left 4 Dead, Vermintide, Killing Floor, etc, then you'll like DRG.  If you don't, well, you won't. Overclocks and new weapons provide different and often quirky or terrifying new options for mining and killing, changing up how each mission plays and allowing for great clutches, tragic mistakes, or the ever-present omnicidal Driller's brutal slaughter of the team.Deep Rock is the epitome of the phrase, "It's not about the destination, it's about the journey." You don't play the game for the material rewards. Unlocking cosmetics and overclocks is fun, but it isn't the point of the game. The point is surviving a detonator encounter or wiping a swarm with a well-placed explosion. It's bringing Doretta's head back and seeing it waiting for you in the space rig. It's getting drunk in the abyss bar during an impromptu game of space kickball. A lot of other games have something you're trying to achieve by playing. In Deep Rock, playing IS the achievement.DRG is honestly my biggest positive surprise in the past several years of gaming. This studio puts many AAA devs to shame and playing made me realize just how distorted and dystopian modern online gaming has become. DRG has no predatory monetization, no exploiting FOMO, no toxic enforcement of competitiveness. The game is designed in a way so that you help your team by most of what you do even if you don't aim to do so, and the benefits of cooperation are massive. This results in the absolute most positive experience with randoms I have had in any online game ever to the point where I had to sit down and think what's wrong with me to be nervous about playing with randoms, because so many online games have conditioned us to loathe the experience. DRG is full of players genuinely just wanting to have a good time goofing off and working together to complete a mission and maybe buy each other beer afterwards (in game and IRL). It is a game anyone would seriously lose a lot on to miss.Amazing game from an incredible developer. The best example I can think of for “hey maybe we can make games without ridiculous amounts of monetization and treat our customers well”. DRG is definitely worth the price.  It is arguably the most beloved co-op game ever, and for good reason. It’s an absolute blast to play with friends.  I wish I had friends that play it, but even with randoms it is a lot of fun. It even surprised me with how good it also plays solo. There is a reason why every gaming suggestion forum is filled with people shouting ROCK AND STONE!! In summary, the game is endless and the content never repeats as long as you enjoy the gameplay cycle. I highly recommend it; it's fun with strangers, friends, or alone. Seriously bro, if you don’t rock and stone you’re not going home. It’s that simple.Finally,For those new brothers about to Rock and Stone, we salute you!10/10

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not one to usually write detailed reviews but for this game...I MUST!Before buying this game (I bought it in early access), I was slightly thrown off by the screenshots and videos of the gameplay and I thought to myself, this is just gonna be one of those brainless run around shoot and repeat kinda game with graphics that looks mediocre by some indie developers. Oh Boi was I wrong...The 4 different classes [Scout-Driller-Gunner-Engineer] each has their own set of weapons, grenades, traversal tool and more. For example, the scout is able to use a grappling hook to navigate hard to reach places, as well as provide flare support to light up the very dark cave while Gunner has a zipline that allows his team to cross high or low areas where you could fall and die and the gunner has a shield that provides a small aoe of (almost) impenetrable defense for a short time.Your role is key and what is your role exactly? Even tho each class has certain playstyles, let's talk about how you have SO MANY WEAPON UPGRADES TO CHOOSE FROM. You would have to pick strategically (or as you personally prefer) the upgrades you would like for your guns, armor, type of grenade, traversal tool and others. You are free to change your upgrades at anytime after you use your resources to unlock it. Maybe the stage involves you killing a huge boss and you need armor breaking, that's the perk to go for! Or maybe you need to clear large amounts of waves, you could get piercing bullets to cut through multiple enemies.The upgrades I mentioned may sound basic but trust me, there is ALOT more to it. Especially once you reach level 25 and unlock the "endgame", you have countless amounts of mods that could turn your gun to something completely different. (I have a mod for my shotgun that makes my scout fly upwards everytime I shoot downwards LOL) I also have a mod for my engineer which makes the laser like gun's projectiles come back to the gun after shooting it out, essentially damaging the enemies twice.There is so much more than just running and shooting and reaching checkpoints. You have many different objectives and secondary objectives that do not feel repetitive. There are many different biomes that each has their unique set of creatures and elemental damages. Every round you play will not feel the same as the system's randomizer changes the way the caves looks and how often the enemy spawns, what type of enemies spawns etc....every time you enter a new round.This game's soundtracks are also great! The synth style really gets you in the moment when a wave spawns or when a certain big bug spawns. This game got me into this genre and that says alot.In terms of the graphics, it has improved alot since i played in early access. The lighting, models, art style, is so beautiful and guess what? Would you believe me if I told you that this entire game uses less than 3GB of your storage size? For mine, it is only 1.88GB specifically. At first I thought there was some error or I am only downloading an update patch or something but nope. That's the total game size.The beginning of the game is probably confusing for many people but do not give up so fast! The game is much simpler than you think and if you put in some time into it, you will see why this game has such a positive rating on steam :DAside from the amazing gameplay and humor in the game, I truly enjoy two things that I find to be rare in other multiplayer communities.1. The community, Deep Rock has one of the most nicest and helpful community I've ever been in. The gamers here wants a good time and that's exactly what they will get! I've learnt alot playing with others and through their official discord, played with one of the discord mods. He was so friendly and taught us many things about the game, talked about few things the devs kept or took out in the past and how the game is going overall.2. THE DEVS! You can just see that there is so much love poured into this game. All the way from the beginning, the devs have not stopped bringing additional content and listens to the interests of the community. This game is not pay to win and all the dlcs you see in this game is a way to support the devs. I bought the supporter upgrade because I feel like the devs deserves it. They deserve the support and I will happily recommend this game to anyone who games.ROCK AND STONE FOR KARL!!!!!(Side note for those who has motion sickness)There is a setting to turn down camera shake and head bobbing. Couple friends of mine including myself has motion sickness. The settings in the game made the game playable for us once we adjusted the settings.
