_childDocuments_.review: Deeply fun and engaging co-op experience, between the dwarves themselves, the buggos and a lot of little details all spun together. This little game has a lot of charm and character. It's hard to not recommend if you are a fan of cooperative shooters.My only gripes would be a bit of a struggle for mission variety, but it's kept me going near 400 hours so the level generation and chaotic moments unique to each level can keep that down. Along with the game getting frequent enough updates that every couple of months there tends to be something new on the table.
_childDocuments_.name: Deep Rock Galactic

_childDocuments_.review: I love Co-op games. Don't get me wrong, I play and enjoy single-player games and PvP games, but Co-op is where I'm happiest. Getting to meet new people and NOT having to sour relations immediately by shooting them in the face or sending an army of minions to fight them is, quite honestly, a relief. So, it should come as no surprise that I enjoy Co-op games like Left 4 Dead and Vermintide, which really emphasise teamwork and fun, visceral combat. I'm also a sucker for sandbox stuff, as long as I can work together with my teammates. Whether it's overcoming challenge with friends in a game like 7 days to die, or (I'll admit it;) working together with friends on a Minecraft project, Co-op is my favourite way to play.And you're reading a review for one of the best Co-op games I've had the pleasure of playing. Ever.Deep Rock Galactic is a gem, and you need only look at it's reviews (Currently Overwhelmingly Positive) to understand that. Quite honestly, if you don't own the game already, I'm gonna give you a speedy review-in-a-review; Do you like Co-op, Beers, digging stuff, shooting things, compelling progression and a warm community? If you answered yes to like, at least 3 of those, go buy the game now. You won't regret it. Better yet, find some friends and get them to come tag along too. The more the merrier!May've review-splurged a little too early there, so let's get back on track!Deep Rock Galactic pits you, a brave dwarf (and up to three dwarf friends), against caves full of ravenous, flesh eating spider thingies. Oh, and exploder spider things. And fat flying spitty things. And giant Venus Flytrap looking plant-monsters that shoot massive globs of acid. And massive behemoths wreathed in fire. And even worse things await you in dark, cold depths... Why then would any sane person choose to brave the horrors of Hoxxes IV? Riches, my friends. Riches. Each Dwarf has a pickaxe and you'll be spending your downtime in the caves stripping the destructible walls, floors and ceilings bare of valuables. You'll then (hopefully) return home. Well, your home away from home anyway.Welcome back to the Spacerig, Miner! Spend your hard earned gold and minerals on upgrading or customising one of four classes. Each class has four weapons. Each weapon has between 10-15 different modular upgrades, of which you'll pick 5. You can (later) also gain special upgrades called overclocks that can change these guns further. You can also choose from different grenades, upgrade your armour and upgrade your support equipment. You can also customise your characters extensively, utilising all sorts of loot in the game from animations to armours to gun models, as well as purchasing nifty haircuts, armours and hats from the Spacerigs store. And when the stress is too much, relax at the Abyss Bar. It's a good job you've been collecting all those brewing ingredients, because your Robo-Bartender can make some stunning brews. Drink with friends. Dance at the Jukebox. Party all night. Kick some barrels into the- wait, message from management, they keep telling us to leave the barrels alone. We shan't.Back to the Droppod. Back to the Mines. Back to Work. An Engineer uses his ingenious platform gun to create walkways near the ceiling, next to a vein of gold. A Scout, having lit the cave with his flare gun just a few second prior, sees this and uses his trusty grappling hook to reach those dizzying heights and gets to work digging. The Driller opens up a blocked tunnel using his massive pneumatic drills, and a horde of Glphyid Grunts come rushing out of the newly exposed cavern. Not to worry though, for the Gunner is at hand with his Minigun, tearing through alien grunts like paste (and good lord, the gunplay is satisfying). This is something you can expect to see happen within the first 20 seconds of a mission. A mission that could be 15 minutes long or an hour long, depending on your team, your hazard level, cave complexity, mission length and your general pace. Another minute or two could see the shriek of an approaching horde, the discovery of a rare gem, a fearsome monster to fight, or one of your teammates just goofing around on the job. I've seen it all.I'd love to go on, but I've just had more orders from Management. Apparently there's some "Haunted Cave" that fellow dwarves have been too scared to traverse. Greenbeards and Leaf-Lovers, the lot of them. Not to worry, I'm not the superstitious sort. Neither was Karl. I'll grab my stuff, hit up the drop pod, and be back for a few beers before you can say "To the bone!" I'd ask you to wish me luck, but we're dwarves - we don't need luck.Rock and Stone, Brothers!
_childDocuments_.name: Deep Rock Galactic

_childDocuments_.review: A masterclass game; only 2-3 GB of storage needed, easy to run graphics (that still look very pleasing), cheap pricetag and an active passionate devteam! DLC is not needed as it's only cosmetic and everything else is only obtainable via playing -> NO IN-APP PURCHASES!!! It is playable alone or with 3 others, I suggest having friends with you to heighten the fun but playing public games with randos is also very fun (the community is very kind and helpful).  The game difficulty can range from very easy to super hard depending on the hazard level you choose for missions. Anyone can play this game imo from kids to adults (although there is violence, alcohol and some 'foul' language). The music is fine but ramps up insanely during 'swarms' or events, this music is insanely good and I always find myself bopping to it. There is no story however there is lore sprinkled throughout the game. The game is constantly swapping from full action to serene mining periods. You play as a DWARF! Need I say more?
_childDocuments_.name: Deep Rock Galactic

_childDocuments_.review: Has one of the friendliest communities I have ever seen. Very good gameplay, many mission types, mission areas and difficulties. It has good and flexible modding support. You can either play with other people or play solo with companion drone bot that will help you with tasks, fight and gather. It has many lategame weapon upgrades/cometics to keep you entertained. Developers actually play their own game and enjoy it, they don't make bad and unpolished updates like other bigger companies do. The updates here are awesome and season pass content is free! The only paid content are optional cosmetic dlcs (there is much more free cosmetic stuff available ingame). Even stuff from previous seasons and events can still be obtained later, nothing goes away forever. You can dance, drink beer and get drunk with friends and can even go drunk on missions.
_childDocuments_.name: Deep Rock Galactic

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like to mine?Do you like to drink?Do you like game progression, where your character levels up unlocking better equipment and upgrades?Do you like beards?!?Do you like smashing bugs, and eating bacon? (sorry, bacon has nothing to do with the game, I do like it though)Do you like playing with your friends or making new friends?Do you like playing solo?Do you like a challenge?Do you like an easy/relaxing run?Well, if you said yes to more than one of the above, then you should get this game!! I've put in just shy of 150hrs (when posting this) so far, and can honestly say it's been a lot of fun. I can easily see myself putting in triple that amount or more in the future (which says a lot considering at the time of posting this game, I own hundreds of games, but have only put over a hundred hours into a handful of them). It gives a lot of options for the new player, so you can play alone to get the feel of the game or jump into a match with others to get help while playing (plenty of matches out there welcoming new players).This game gives a lot towards customization while you level up, both with the account, and the individual characters classes. I personally find it adds a nice depth to the game, while giving you goals to reach as you play.  So if you're one of those players who likes to level up and unlock options/upgrades/cosmetics, then you'll find this game a lot of fun, with all the added customization that is available as you level up. If you're someone who needs goals to reach while playing, then this game should satisfy that itch for you as well. Plus for added depth, each mission you run is done on a random gen map, that you can have bonuses/hazards on as well. Things like extra damage to the bugs, while having to deal with no oxygen which forces you to not stray too far from "molly" the minecart on legs, or getting gold to drop from the bugs, while dealing with a creature that is invincible that chases you the across the entire map (moves slowly so easy to avoid if you pay attention). That just names a few of the combinations that is available while running the different missions. Of course, most of the time, you're allowed to choose which mission you want to run and if you want to deal with a hazard, or just have a bonus or nothing at all. There is an exception to this, and that is Deep Dives, were you won't know what you're getting into until after it launches.I honestly could go on and on about the perks of the game, but to avoid the dreaded wall of text growing any further, I'll just leave it with this.Get the game, it's worth way more than they are charging, and is a lot of fun!!
_childDocuments_.name: Deep Rock Galactic

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very good game. Its very easy to play and get the hang of and it probably has hours upon hours of fun.Its fun is cemented by its multiplayer feature where you work together with your buds to do missions. Working together is essential to complete the mission and I really like this.To summarise, its a game set in space where you are a dwarf and you are tasked with doing various missions such as mining for a certain mineral in a certain region or protecting a drill to get it to a hard to crack mineral. This is all done while fighting the many many aliens. There are 4 different classes each for whatever play-style you fancy. This is a good game.- Rock and Stone.
_childDocuments_.name: Deep Rock Galactic

_childDocuments_.review: Remember folks: If you don't Rock and Stone, you ain't coming home.But seriously, play this game if you're a co-op fiend like myself. Gift your friends this game and play with them several times. If they're hooked, it could become the default game for Game Night!It's a "mission based" first-person multiplayer co-op (or solo! Bosco's a helpful buddy.) FPS, where every mission layout never really feels the same. It's got Dwarves. Mining...or doing other things. In space. Pesky bugs. Robotic rivals. The latest infection-riddled meteors...and it's got silly hats, beards and mustaches....and you can drink as much beer as you want. Interested in the game now? Great! Have fun!(A clone of the familiar bird flapping mobile game you may remember from days past is now in the game in arcade form. Dare you to try and reach the 4th level.)
_childDocuments_.name: Deep Rock Galactic

_childDocuments_.review: What you have here is a video game quite unlike any other: An online co-op shooter with 4 distinct dwarf classes that all bring something to the table and a gameplay premise that ensures the emergence of unforgettable memories. A unique art style that looks great on any setting. A development team that consider suggestions and regularly update and improve an early access game with unprecedented polish. What you have here, is my recommendeeshrie. "Rock and Stone"
_childDocuments_.name: Deep Rock Galactic

_childDocuments_.review: A masterwork of a game. It combines all the best parts of action, shooting, exploration, problem solving, progression (without the grind!), and theme. Action packed shooter for the thrill seekers. Shooting for people who like awesome guns. Exploration in dark unknown caves for the adventurous. Problem solving for clever people in a terrain you can dig and carve out any way you want. Progression in a timely manner without the grind by upgrading your guns to advance in difficulty and challenge. And the theme, my goodness the theme. The music, alien bugs, awesome guns that are plain fun to shoot, well written humor and characters just full of personality. And you can scale the difficulty for nearly any gamer! Also, the community is amazing and always willing to work together as a true team.Rock and stone!
_childDocuments_.name: Deep Rock Galactic

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not sure I really enjoy DRG. The actual gameplay, I mean. I can tell that the Devs very much enjoyed making it and I like playing with friends, but the gameplay isn't super interesting to me. I like other aspects of the game, like the silliness of the Space Rig and all the little details that the devs have put in, but the core aspect of the game seems like a time sink with little to no significant reward. The other thing is that the build structure seems completely played out.There are optimized ways to perform each task or mission that have long since been discovered and laid out, but even with future updates, nothing new is being added to the game outside of additional threats in the form of New enemies or regions.I see the appeal, but the game is too similar to the 'same-y-ness' of games like Left for Dead or Gears of War. You're essentially just running over the same ground (or under, as the case may be), indefinitely to pass time. Level ups feel less impactful knowing there's nothing significant waiting for me at the endgame outside of (again) long discovered and laid out modifiers for the existing abilities.If you like the kinds of games that I listed above and enjoy a simplistic 'horde mode' with gradually increasing difficulty and lots of grind, then by all means, pick it up. The community is extensive and there's lots to enjoy. Ultimately though, its not engaging enough for me without more significant progression or story. As a cooperative experience its interesting, but if you're looking for personalization or uniqueness in your build or the way you play, you won't find it here.
_childDocuments_.name: Deep Rock Galactic

_childDocuments_.review: It's hard to call a game perfect. You have to be willing to endure the inevitable counterpoints citing legitimate flaws, whether small or large, nitpicks or critical, and even the smallest legit complaint removes the accurate description of "perfect." But I'm going to go to bat today and say Deep Rock Galactic is a perfect co-op FPS. It is undoubtedly a top quality game, an easy 9/10, a fighting 10/10 and one of the best multiplayer experiences I've ever had.DRG offers you four multi-faceted classes to play. Scout provides critical additional lighting and can do support fire, crowd control or targeted heavy assassination and pairs well with others for exploration or can master amazing personal mobility. Gunner has overwhelming firepower, an astounding defensive cooldown that doubles as area denial and a wholly unique zipline tool. Engineer has astounding crowd control, sentries for area and support fire and can generate small platforms for molding terrain or climbing it, even reducing fall damage for forced drops. My favorite class, Driller, can move through a majority of maps at will and create openings and tunnels anywhere he pleases so long as fuel holds out and possesses astounding AoE damage and options for different support fire, including some single target muscle. Easy to learn, satisfying to master, multitudes of options. From the start DRG is a joy to play.Select a mission from a wide variety of types and go at it. Accomplish objectives and successfully escape. DRG is pure gameplay. There isn't an overarching story, there's just the satisfaction of a job well done. Do missions, have good times with friends, get new gear, push what you're capable of by raising the difficulty, learn new classes, realize you've put 50+ hours in and only made significant headway with half the classes. Hit level cap with one of them, promote, unlock additional ways to get new gear. Try deep dives, get good incentive but not overwhelming pressure to hop in once a week and have some fun. The gunplay feels fantastic, everything works reliably almost all of the time, there are virtually no design decisions that emphasize anything but great game feel and entertaining gameplay.Where DRG excels is the variety of tasks to undertake, the creativity of several of them and the multitude of enemies you face crossed with your complex classes. What could be simple and repetitive generic quest generation instead organically produces a new story almost every round. Each cave is mostly randomly generated(after dozens of hours you'll begin to recognize set pieces), bug waves are director AI randomly generated, there are dozens of enemies and hazards, each biome is a touch different and some are more dangerous than others, you get the idea. The sheer creative sand box nature of some missions and the player freedom is unequaled. Setting up pipelines is my favorite mission type because of the open-ended nature of the task. It's hard to describe without urging you to play the game awhile and feel it yourself but DRG really lets you make great use of creative and smart solutions. Want to dig a shortcut? You can. Want to build cover for an expected fight? Sure. Want to demolish it and see the enemy coming? OK. The synergy the Dwarves show is astounding and delightful and amplified pleasingly by the variety of challenges that can come up.What truly amazes about DRG is the fine touches, the softer details. There isn't a big story, there's barely a story at all, yet the setting is deeply loreful. The dialogue the Dwarves share and the back and forth with management creates an atmosphere of the company that is easy to soak in, there aren't dedicated cutscenes or expository audio logs but you'll be drafting a story in your head as you play. Perhaps the greatest rarity in DRG is the sense of camaraderie in players, even public games. An ingenious hotkey for a morale boosting pickax salute and rallying cry is a universal greeting, affirmative, thanks and cheer. It is spammed often but not obnoxiously, allowing even the voice-shy to communicate and encouraging everyone to stick together and preserve the team. There is in-game voice chat and text but I've also seen an unequaled level of general chill in the playerbase. Perhaps everyone is always having a good time. I can't guarantee this of course but so long as a player respects the hazard level they're capable of even greenbeards get on well with old vets.What else is there to say? I could gush about this game for hours. The soundtrack is full of atmospheric wonder ranging from ominous dread to upbeat meandering, accelerating smoothly to catchy tunes and wicked bangers when the swarm comes. Enemy variety is on point, everything has a place in the swarm from distraction to building danger to specialized danger to serious doom and there's dozens of them mixed with the environmental dangers and then on top of all that even the most basic enemies are engaging to mop up. The graphics are a good mix of stylized art design and impressively smooth, looking both a touch retro and helping the game run well on more systems while also looking good overall.It's just a fantastic game where everything is done right. The only flaws I've seen or felt are some very rare bugged spawns(one Korlok in the air in 88 hours), the occasional oddity in Mule/Drilldozer pathing, and some caves are very cruel to solo Scout/Gunner exploration, although the solo drone Bosco does a lot to cover for this. Try this game. Play it with your friends, look for an online community and hop in, join up when the nightly call to action sounds. Solo enjoyably, play with pick up groups. It's an easy game to start and worth full price all of the way.

_childDocuments_.review: I really really enjoy this game, I've had this game since day 1, then it was pretty ok, little bare bones, and repetitive. I got my moneys worth then stopped, I kept up with the updates and play a little whenever a patch comes out, to see what changed, and for the most part, enjoyed my time, THEN the update that added the new guns and assignments came out, and now whew boy. This game is all new, 2 new guns for each class, giving a side arm and a primary option for every class, all of them seem viable if not straight upgrades to the base game weapons, along with a tweak to cosmetic options and map generation, and weapon upgrades, the game had new found life in it for me, when i stopped playing originally i had around 20-30 hours clocked and would play a One and Done™ level to see what they added every few months. After this combat/weapon/cosmetic update. I have clocked in an additional 100 hours. What saves this game is its combat. its combat is probably some of the most fun I've had in a game styled like this, think left 4 dead, but you need to actually place your shots, because some aliens have hard carapace armor, that will blunt your attacks. All of this franticness is taking place in a huge chasm behind you a 400 meter drop into darkness, in front 40+ little monsters covered in the aforementioned carapace armor some shrugging off grenades and rockets, as your team of Dwarves, chews through the Xeno threat, a quiet descends on the cavern, weapons reloaded, and now there is minerals to mine, flares go up and the light gives purchase to what lies below.Along with the combat, the lighting engine in this is working overtime, whoever implemented this, should be given a raise, the light as your flare bounces down a chasm, or the flareguns huge illuminating glow, or the engineers sentry guns spotlight, even the miners headlamps. Make this game really striking visually, some people say the most expensive and best graphics look best, but they would be wrong, its all about art style and lighting, this game doesn't look like anything special when you're in the hub waiting to leave for mining operations, but once the drop pod leaves and you enter the cave, I would dispute this game has some of the coolest visuals I've seen in a long time. This lighting works in tandem with the map generation, which is partially randomly generated, which sometimes can give some truly funky and weird caves to run through, providing unique challenges to the players making them have to use their tools given to them differently. For example one of my personal favorite things to do, is one class the Gunner, has a zipline gun, used to cross vast gaps and chasms, I however use it for topside cover and string it across an objective and become a Dwarven AC130. Update for November 24th 2021. This game keeps getting better, more guns assignments, cosmetics, etc new modes still probably the best coop shooter ive ever played. Update for November 22nd 2022,Another year another season and a new progression of the DRG story line, new weapon changes and new batch of grenades added to each class, totaling 4 options for each class the new grenades are all interesting and some are powerful, shout-out to the buzz saw for the driller dealing EXTRA Friendly fire damage. I was worried when they first unveiled the season systems, but the fact there's 0 monetization aside from cosmetic skin packs that aren't even part of the "battle pass" and if you miss some of the seasonal rewards they get added to the regular cosmetic pools in game. This is how you do battlepasses, I wish and i COPE that this will become the standard of the games industry henceforth. (It wont.) DRG has and will continue to be one of the best games ive ever played, and should be a STANDARD for Co-op FPS games . TL:DR, Great game, semi random generated maps, player progression, weapon upgrades, great lighting and artstyle, combat is great. 9/10 ROCK AND STONE, TO THE BONE.

_childDocuments_.review: A game about the natural conclusion of Dwarves and industry; That is they go to space and mine everything there is to mine to create incrementally more awesome weapons, tools & armour but most importantly... BEER! Yes you heard me, half the Morkite you mine and Red Sugar you find go straight into amazing drinks! That's what a Dwarfs most important possession is isn't it!?An insanely fun game that gives me Starship Troopers vibes when waves upon waves of enemies crash into you and you have flamethrowers or icethrowers or anti-matter bombs or heavy gatling cannons or rifles going off in all directions, turrets and shields and sheer ravines, volcanoes and erupting fire! While it's a tad grindy on the levels, if you play with four other peeps you can crank the difficulty up and make the grind a lot faster, plus you get better weapons, more cosmetics, stronger armour, etc. To help you gauge when you're ready for that skull-crushing difficulty of 100%! It's funny, it's hectic, and it is well supported. ROCK AND STONE TO THE BONE!

_childDocuments_.review: Join Deep Rock Galactic for exploration, gold, treasure, and job recognition! Can't find a route to suit your preference through the dark tunnels of Hoxxes IV?  Use that pickaxe of yours to dig your own route because that's the Deep Rock way! Your ability to solve the problems in front of you is only limited by the creativity inside you – and your explosives, don't forget about those.That sounding a little monotonous to you? You say you joined up for adventure? Well let me tell you, Hoxxes IV is filled to the brim with all matter of dangerous wildlife! These caves aren't just creepy for what could be around any dark corner, they're creepy for what unimaginable horrors we know are around them!You'll always have to defend yourself and keep your eye out for all sorts of danger when mining for Deep Rock Galactic. So just remember, any time that mineral hunt gets a bit dull, focus on the endless swarms of bugs hoping to turn you into their next meal. Oh and don't worry, we have plenty of upgrades for you to earn and purchase, making the task of squashing those bugs easier or just a little more satisfying. Maybe you buy those upgrades to keep the bugs off you while you mine, or maybe better dominance over those six legged creeps is its own reward. That's the beauty of working with Deep Rock Galactic, your goals are permitted to shift to whatever you're most excited about, keeping the collection of valuable minerals fresh forever. Why, even after a hundred hours of diving into that planet's surface, you'll still be considered a greenbeard next to your peers. But the fun doesn't end there! We've decked out your Space Rig hub with a dance floor, a fully stocked bar, and plenty of barrels to kick in case you need to blow off steam after one of those tougher missions. Our friendly drone, Lloyd, will be happy to serve up any of our pre-approved beverages. Perhaps you'll pass out, perhaps you'll grow three times your size. There's always something new to discover with Deep Rock Refreshments!Our workplace culture is also one of the best in the business. Don't worry about gathering up a dedicated group of friends to sign up with, there's always plenty of miners just as ready to have a great time mining with you as anyone you've known longer than the 20 seconds it'll take to match you up. And if that doesn't suit you, Bosco, our patented All-Purpose drone, will take the place of three dwarves and won't give you no lip neither. Whatever your approach, it's all a great time waiting to happen with Deep Rock Galactic, so what are you doing still reading this when you could be 'Rock and Stone'ing with your new brothers today?!

_childDocuments_.review: For me personally the best quality of this game has to be its core gameplay. There are many other great little things about this game but when you strip it down to its bare bones, it's still vastly enjoyable to swing a pick at a shiny gem or to launch a grenade into a horde of bugs and watch them all go pop. The crunch when you kill a grunt with critical hit is a thing of beauty. That and other little things of its ilk is what has given me many hundreds of hours of enjoyment with this title. Of course, there are many other things that serve to make this game memorable, two of them being Mission Control and the soundtrack. Mission Control manages to convey the information you need, add a splash of humour, and seriously contribute to the tone of the game, despite only being a single static images and a wide array of voicelines. Such a seemingly small thing adds so much charm to the game, and manages to create an emotionally investing character with few components. They're memorable, likeable, and quotable.The soundtrack boosts both the ambience of the calm sections and the frantic action of the big fights. I find it a shame I can't nominate this game for multiple categories in the Steam awards, since it excels in many categories.Plus, the random generation of the caves genuinely gives a different experience each time. It's much different having to fight bugs in cramped corridors or having to traverse huge open caverns, so you end up having to solve logistical problems by using the full extent of you and your teams kit. I think this game serves as an excellent example of random generation being used to its fullest extent. It also means that the whole game size is less than 2Gb, which is pretty impressive in this day and age. I highly recommend this game if you enjoy first person shooters, frantic action games, 4 player coop, or any combination of them. Even if you're not a fan of the genres I would still say to try it out, as I can't really name anything else out there that's quite like it.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a dang good game. If you have enjoyed four player coop shooters (such as Left 4 Dead 2 or Payday 2), or are looking to get into one, I highly recommend Deep Rock Galactic.The difficulty options have something for everyone, whether you are still learning, just casual, or here for something hardcore. The lowest difficulties are so easy I could perform them drunk (irl), while the highest require real skill and strategization.The gunplay is excellent. If you have good aim and experience with shooting games, there are guns that will very reward those skills. But in the case you do not, there are plenty of weapons and customizations that do not require precise aim.But its not just the gunplay, the traversal is just as good, and particularly unique for a coop shooter. The game has randomly generated caves, with a great deal of interaction and verticality. You can dig tunnels as any class, and each has a unique tool to help yourself (and your team) navigate the terrain, such as a creating platforms or a grappling gun.Oh, and above all, this game has a superbly friendly community. Any coop shooter is fun with friends, but even playing with randoms is a wonderful time.This game is worth it all the full 30 dollar price. However, it regularly goes on sale to about 10 dollars, and at that price it is an absolute steal. I hope to see you in game, Rock and Stone! oT

_childDocuments_.review: Almost 850 hrs in and it's still a blast. I kinda understand the negative reviews saying it gets stale but let's be honest, they probably either play alone or tryhard on top difficulty which is noticeably less fun than playiing as a party of 3-4 in VC and just goofing around while still doing stuff. You should give it a try. If you look for a game for 2-4 players to have a blast of an experience and lots of fun you've hit the spot. If you don't play with friends it's about 100 hrs before it can get stale which still is a lot of time even for a full price.Basically a certified Australian experience as you find yourself removing eight-leeged buggers and oversized flies from the face of the planet with pretty much any possible way you can think of. Shoot then? Yes. Burn them? Yes. Freeze them to death? Sure! Melt them in acid? Why not! Tactical nukes?! Coming right up! With 4 classes each having 3 primary weapons and 3 secondaries you are bound to find something you like. At first it seemed to me that lack of the ADS mechanic ruins the gunplay experience but you will grow to appreciate it when you fing youself in the middle of the swarm. There are a few mission types and honestly they get progressively more and more cringe with seasons and there are some really questionable decisions made about their usage in assignmemt chains but you still get a luxury of not playing them if you don't enjoy them (unless you are trying to prestige).The game is heavily focused on team cooperation and the best way of playing is in a full lobby of 4 different classes. The laser pointer tool paired up with dwarf voicelines is just a perfect method of communication. There are almost no situations in which you would need to use in-game chat or VC and it's definitely a plus. As for the players DRG is literally the most wholesome community I've ever seen. Of course there are exceptions but most players here are friendly and understanding. Some lobbies do expeсt you to have at least some skill (usually they request some amount of prestige in description) but there are a lot of high-level players that will gladly accept a relatively new player and help them along the way. And on top of that YT has years of video content with gameplay tips, loadouts, obscure trics etc.All gameplay content comes in the base game. All DLCs so far are purely cosmetic. The weapons are not evenly balanced but all weapons are totally viable even in their base state. As you play more with a single class you unlock other weapons and weapon mod tiers that let you fit the gun to your playstyle. Once you get the maximum EXP with one class you can promote it (prestige) and this unlocks the rest of the content, mainly overclocks (an extra weapon mod) and deep dives (gauntlet). Up until player rank 100 (which is like 12 promotions and about 150-200 hrs) you will get progression assignments that boost your unlock speed. It took me about 250 hrs to get all the gameplay unlocks and in 850 hrs I still do not have all of the base game cosmetics. The battle pass is totally free and awesome and all the content you missed from it is added to base game unlocks when it rotates to the next one.As you get stuff and get good at the game you have two ways of playing. You can tryhard and sweat at top difficulty which ins't fun consistently imo but still is an option. On the other hand as you get better you can make your builds progressively dumber and still complete objectives. Suddenly all of the "lackluster" overclocs and weapons are not just ridiculous but ridiculously fun. I've been clearing pre-top difficulty with all kinds of builds and having your friends witness you use up half of you ammo in a second to oneshot some big bugger is a ton of fun. As a bonus you virtually become a millionaire (but the prices of everything except the beer skyrocket as well).As I already mentioned they are purely cosmetic. Don't listen to the reviews saying devs are milking players with them, just read the DLC reviews. Most players buy them out of respect just to support the devs. The skins are really cool yet the base game also has a bunch of fire skins.There are already tons of mods. You can adjust literally anyting from sounds to balance. Cherry on top is that with a little research you can make some basic mods too and it is surprisingly easy even if you don't know any programming languages.Try it. It's amazing. Rock and Stone future miners!

_childDocuments_.review: A preposterously fun, comical, and immersive team-based game that excels at rewarding positive behavior in-game and giving the player plenty of enemies to shoot and loot to collect. Blast pesky bugs with grenade launchers, assault rifles, laser bombs, or just swing at 'em with your trusty indestructible pickaxe. Mine for rare minerals that let you soup up your weapons and gear for extra firepower. You are  rewarded by playing nice with others and are usually adversely punished in the opposite case, as trolling is not taken lightly and you'll probably understand this after a couple play-throughs.In terms of gameplay, there are four classes you can play as: Scout, Engineer, Gunner, and Driller. All of these classes hold very important value and utility and it's generally impossible to win a mission without having some class diversity in your squad (you can play w/ up to four players). The tutorial does an absolutely  job of teaching you controls and how to use your gear based on what class you choose to learn when you first start up the game. Even if you skip the tutorial, it probably won't take you more than 5 minutes max to learn every class as the learning curve can be easily classified as "easy to learn, hard to master."TL;DR dwarf kill bugs and make money

_childDocuments_.review: What makes DRG a good game ? . If DRG were a bad game. I wouldn't be sitting here discussing it with you now would i.Taking simple concept and refining it over the years . As taking inspiration from other things but also changing them up  to fit the game framework . what resulted in unique game .1- Game loop and mission pacing : you start the mission . exploring and collect resources . Then the ambiance music get replaced by tension escalating music as mission control warns about the incoming threat . A moment of brief peace  get broken by incoming onslaught of enemies . Then after the dust settle . the loop repeat itself . 2- 4 classes with multiple items that means your progression can take over 30-45h just to unlock most of them .3- A cooperative driven game that still fun in solo : Every one of the 4 classes can do one thing or another thing better than other classes but no one is under-powered or overpowered . And every class got a unique utility items that really come handy. From a zip-line helpful to get the whole team to the bottom of the cave . To a flare gun that light up the whole area etc.... Not mentioning the crazy amount of builds you can run and still have fun time testing them . Some may be worse or better but i do say they all can work . As solo player . you get a useful bot that can mine and attack . Even revives you . (i am a solo player of +400h and I still enjoy the game)  4- Mod support . 5- Pretty good soundtrack and art style .6- Cosmetics and progression are not locked behind paywall . *yes . we have cosmetics DLC but you pay for it and you get a whole set of them for the 4 classes and the in game cosmetics are as good looking as the DLC one . Majority of cosmetics in the game are earned by playing the game and acquired by spending the in game currency (I will say that like 90% of cosmetic in this game are  bought by in game currency).7- The game still getting major updates every 4-5 months (they are funded by the cosmetics DLC. but this game doing DLC the right way)8- The game is not trying to nickel and dime you like other games . 9- I like the community/fandom surrounding the game . 10- pretty chill game that also can be tense. (hazard 5 is not a joke).Rock & Stone . For Karl!Edit: 2023. it's never late for the party. the game still worth it.Edit: 2024. Still peak!

_childDocuments_.review: Oh man, this game, i was meaning to make a review for it.First of all, don't let the name fool you, you're not just mining. Many missions will have you doing things like hunting down giant bugs, transporting a drill machine to it's destination, collecting bug eggs and much more; to say the least, there's many ways to play and you have the freedom of choice for what you feel like doing.Second, we've got those Dwarves, as they have their different roles. those were explained pretty well in the trailer but it goes to mention that you can have a lot of customization done, up to 3 upgrades per branch in a tree of upgrades for your tools and weapons, an alternate set of weapons that you can unlock that have their own unique functions and your own set of perks.Third we've got gameplay, the game has many different areas to travel to with their own unique ecosystems and monsters to deal with, anything from an oversized fly that spits acid to a massive ant-like beings that can cause massive explosions just by stomping, let alone unleashing a titanic suicide bomb attack when killed. You're got Beers, which you have to gather various hops for in missions that once made, have various funny effects like making you outright combust or burst into a dancing mania. some also hold actual benefits like increasing health for a round but these positive buffs are rotated so you don't get an easy way of winning the same way every time.Lastly the soundtrack, man this is one of the ONLY games on steam i've bothered actually buying the soundtrack for, i think that speaks enough.TL;DR Fun loot shooter that goes above and beyond to make each round special and extremely enjoyable with decent depth, Definitely something i would recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Easily one of the most fun co-op games out at the moment. The well-crafted randomly generated level design, fun weekly challenges, and a progression system filled with countless unlockables make the game quite replayable for hundreds of hours. Each dwarf class has their own strengths and weaknesses that become apparent in group play. Even with different load outs, each class falls into a soft role that fulfills a useful asset to the team.On top of this, the developers are still consistently releasing free updates for the game every few months which add a significant amount of extra content in the form of new mission types, biomes, or other neat features. I will say that playing solo, while decently fun, pales in comparison to the experience when playing with others and team play is where the game truly shines. Luckily, the Deep Rock community is one of the best and nicest I've seen in the gaming sphere so do not count out playing with strangers if you do not have enough friends yourself.The gameplay, graphics, atmosphere, and the unique character the game has come together to make it one of my favorite co-op games ever. The price is definitely worth the experience. Rock and Stone!

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game back in March, and they could have stopped making content then and it still would have been better than most other multiplayer games out there. I'm very impressed just how often and how much content they tend to release though since I've been playing. You can expect a new update once a month at least and sometimes twice a month. The game already looks much different than it did when I started playing.I decided to write this review now at 86 hours because that's how long it took me to retire every (currently four) character. So even with the limited amount of content the game has right now there is still atleast enough content to drive you through to 80 hours of gametime. They have already said they are planning on releasing a fifth class and adding in female dwarves along with more game modes. Daily missions and new weapons, along with an in-depth weapon upgrade system, is on it's way this month and will add much more content. One thing I would like to see if some sort of campaign mode, but this is one of those games where the story will be told through the missions and in-game lore.The caves themselves are dark and brooding with fantastic lighting that creates some awesome screenshots good enough that I actually put some of them as my background. There is multiple types of enemies to worry about as well along with periodically generated swarms of enemies that sparks some really engaging combat music. Music in general in this game is very well done and some of the best music out there, which has caused me to boost my music sound far higher than any other sounds. So far as I know there is only one type of "boss" creature that has a small chance to spawn instead of a swarm, but they have promised to add in more.Each of the four classes feel unique to each other without any of them really overshadowing the others in usefulness. No class in the game just feels like it doesn't belong in the game and they all work together in amazing ways. They intentionally designed the game where you can play four of the same class and it still be able to work as well. You can also solo the entire game yourself (though you do have a robot companion named Bosco with 3 free revives) with any character without it becoming too much of a hassle. Every character does have it's own up's and down's though but they all have their own unique devices to transverse the landscape with. They're all so useful and unique that I often have a hard time deciding which one is my favorite or which one is my least favorite.For a game as good as it is and how often they stay on their development of the game I don't think I could recommend a game more than DRG. I'm usually annoyed by early access games and I'm also an achievement hunter but I actually enjoy this game so much that none of that even matters to me. Sometimes I have a hard time choosing a game to play after a hard day and I just want to relax but I also want some excitement (if that makes any sense) and this game has come to the rescue for me. I am constantly suggesting this game to friends and even acquaintances as one of the best games out there right now, especially for the low price. Just buy it, I guarantee you'll enjoy it no matter what type of player you are.5/5 Rock and Stone, brother!

_childDocuments_.review: There is something really special about this game. It's incredibly fun, even after maxing out all of the character levels. It presents a very simple and easy-to-grasp form of gameplay: mine the ores, kill the aliens, get home safe, and each of the classes in the game feels unique and fun to play. One of my favorite selling points of the multiplayer in this game is that each class offers something unique and helpful, but if your team is missing one of them you can still do just fine. Everybody can go the same class and it all works out. The meta is very flexible and you can play however you like and still be successful (most of the time). It's charming, fun, and offers endless replayability with its procedurally generated levels. I love this game.

_childDocuments_.review: In this game, you and your crew of dwarf miners explore alien caves, tackle dangerous creatures, and complete missions together.Every mission feels like a new adventure, with procedurally generated caves offering fresh challenges each time you play. You'll encounter all sorts of environments, from vast underground networks to eerie fungal forests. Most of what you do is mine but it's not just about mining – you'll also face off against swarms of hostile creatures called Glyphids. Combat is fast-paced and requires teamwork to survive.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the pinnacle of co-op shooting fun. One to four players take the role of four dwarfs in a sci-fi setting where a Dwarven mining company is attempting to strip mine a hostile alien planet that takes a page right out of starship troopers.The dwarfs have four playable classes. The Scout-a fast and mobile explorer who excels at getting up to those hard to reach places and not breaking every bone in his body on the way down.The Driller-An expert of breaking through the rough untamed underground wilderness of Hoxxes as well as destroying large swarms of hostile aliens with a variety of area of effect heavy weapons like the flame thrower and cryo cannon.  If you need something blown up he is also the one you call.The Gunner-With a series of heavy weapons the gunner is adept at dishing out direct damage in just about any situation. Destructive grenades and a lot of bullets define his role. He also brings a defensive shield to buy his team time  when the swarm is surrounding them and can create zip line routes allowing teammates the ability to traverse the massive caves of Hoxxes with relative ease.And finally the Engineer-bringing with him a variety of homemade gadgets the Engineer can offer a number of useful utilitarian options for his team. Along with an automatic shotgun he excels at shocking enemies with a number of weapon mods. Create electric fences with your turrets, strip the armor off your foes  with his vicious breach cutter, or launch a grenade (or a tactical nuke) from his hand grenade launcher. He is also equiped with a turret for crucial point defense and create foam platforms to help his team overcome any number of obstacles or even control the flow of the enemy swarm.Hoxxes is filled with an ever growing number of enemies and challenges as well. New biomes and enemies keep getting added and while glyphids remain the most common enemy type they are by no means the only thing you will find. Each biome itself offers a variety of challenges to overcome. From a hostile tree filled with sentient thorns and roots to a volcanic hellscape filled with flaming geysers and terrain that will split itself open to reveal a scorching chasm.And the mission types will change a great deal as well. From simple mining expeditions to complex oil drilling operations with a number of side challenges such as rogue robotic war machines or enviromental hazards. Overcome all of that and more and you can gather an entire armory of weapons, perk points, cosmetics, pick axes, and weapon mods that can change how you look or how you play.  Hours and hours of content. And while it is focused on co-op keep there is also Bosco your robotic teammate replacement unit capable of reviving you several times, fighting, carrying, and mining enabling a decent solo experience as well.If you like horde shooters, co-op, or anything with destructable terrain this game is must try. Outstanding game with great developers who have kept building on what they launched with.

_childDocuments_.review: Deep Rock Galactic is a very complex game that takes you to a space station, from which you go on missions to different biomes, caves, where you have to mine minerals, fight hordes of aliens, or perform various other tasks. Each cave and mission is different and therefore unique thanks to a different generator. In this game you have 4 dwarves who complement each other perfectly with their abilities. Over time, you can unlock cosmetic modifications from the entire gear to different beards and colors, as well as weapon modifications, more difficult missions and also the Deep Dive challenge, which is a mission that resets once a week and is characterized by the fact that it is three missions behind where players have to save with minerals and ammunition. The developers take very good care of the game and optimize it + add new content. I have no complaints about the graphics of the game and the overall optimization, because I like the graphics precisely because they are different from games. Overall, I have to say that I really enjoy this game, because there is always something to do in it, and I definitely don't get tired of shooting alien spiders.

_childDocuments_.review: This game saved my life.I am 50.My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and adopted our son together. They are now both 4 years old.When we were going through our separation, I found myself lost and miserable. I was self destructive. I got so mad one day from everything spiraling out of my control that I punched some concrete in a moment of overwhelming emotion. That caused me to break my 5th metacarpal in my right hand... my working hand... my games hand.. the hand that I held and carried my children to bed with.. The hand I desperately needed to make sure I could continue to provide.After learning of the severity of my self-inflicted damage, I was borderline suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man with no history of depression or anxiety. I have never had fits of rage, or been one to break down and cry, but I was in a low spot that just really buried me from being able to see the light on the other side.Having nothing better to do, I searched for a game I could play, ONE HANDED while I recovered. I somehow stumbled upon this game and read some of the reviews. I decided that it had to be worth a shot... I must admit, I didn't beat the game, or play nearly as long as some of you. In fact, I may have only played this game a day or two.. With that being said, after doing so, I had a new found joy and hope for life. I was able to put behind me the pain and suffering that had been cast over me. I was able to experience other peoples joy and happiness. I was able to see the fruits of my "labor". I relaxed for 5 :hillary: :hillary: :hillary: :hillary: :hillary: :hillary: :hillary: minutes to this music long enough to realize that I was going to be okay.After coming to that realization, I turned the game off, and I went back to work. It hurt my hand like hell but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so damn sorry for myself, and I became the father I needed to be in that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving as.Today, I am close friend with my kids mother. We don't fight, or argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents, and friends.I now have 3 kids. My third child is, wait for it, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my own separation, and we just stumbled in to each others life unexpectedly. We have been in a relationship for a year now, and are very happy together.Moral of the story, you never know what life holds in store for you, and if I would have given up when all the odds were stacked against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.

_childDocuments_.review: Early on, this game will seem unfocused, weird and gimmicky. They drop you into missions and you finish it then wonder "is that it?"If you embrace the premise, and view it through the lens of a co-operative game, you will quickly learn why the missions can become so fun. Each dwarf has advantages and weaknesses, and each dwarf can cover eachothers weaknesses. Missions require very active participation from everyone in the cave. The scout needs the engineer to make platforms, the gunner needs the driller to create pathways, etc. The more thorough a team is about collecting resources, the more everyone benefits in terms of currency, materials, xp and so on. These resources serve as the players progression, weapon unlocks, cosmetics, everything that matters is 100% accessible through gameplay- no real money needed. You can unlock everything yourself, in a timely manner, and you can always have something to do, and the game doesnt gouge or entice you into doing it like a second job. there is no FOMO, no predatory daylies or battle passes, there is just gameplay and then rewards for gameplay. But most importantly? it's a FUN game. the dwarves can interact verbally, they can reach insane topspeeds and they can do insane damage to the enemies, environments or their own teammates. It is a game that approves of any playstyle, the objectives are diverse and challenging but not frustrating (mostly- save for korloks and corruptors). Just play it

_childDocuments_.review: The reviews are overwhelmingly positive for a reason. An up-to-four-person mining/shooter set in a space-age capitalist setting. _childDocuments_.review: It's difficult to describe Deep Rock Galactic; in many ways, it's an experience better played than described.  If you take Left 4 Dead, pour in a hefty helping of Dwarf Fortress, and then add a dash of Minecraft, you'll be somewhere close; it's a really unique take on the Horde Shooter genre that combines elements of exploration, resource gathering and class-based shooters to provide a fresh and unique experience that really has nothing quite like it around.All the more impressive is the level of polish and clarity with which this is accomplished, given that this is the development team's debut game.  Of course, all of that is less important than one simple fact - you revive your teammates by pouring beer on them, and if that doesn't at least make you want to look into this game, there might be something wrong with you.The real charm of this game doesn't come from the gameplay; while it's very fun and well-executed, the game's real sparkle comes from the setting and the aggressively-dwarven aesthetics of virtually every aspect of the game's systems.  Your melee attack is a pickaxe, the same pickaxe used to bash minerals and precious metals out of the cavern walls; you can go to the pub in between missions and knock back pints of ale until you pass out, or buy a specially-potent drink to buff yourself on your next mission.You can spam salutes to your teammates as you mow down waves of homicidal bugs, and your response to a nightmare death world full of dangerous environments and creatures is a bigger gun and a pint of alcohol.This game has a huge amount of potential, and I really hope the devs are able to capitalize on it - but as it stands this game is well worth your time and money.  The only downside I can think of at present is that you'll get the best experience from playing it with friends, since it is at heart a co-op game.

_childDocuments_.review: Deep Rock Galactic is what I would consider a perfect video game. It has everything that I like: Shooting satisfying guns. Grinding for loot. Advanced movement mechanics. Appropriate use of procedural generation to create unique experiences and infinite replayability. Genuinely funny characters with rich personalities. Intense gameplay that requires your full attention, with perfectly paced downtime to get your bearings. Teamwork that is heavily suggested but not required in order to succeed. An uncharacteristically friendly community (I play in open lobbies 99% of the time, and I can count every toxic encounter I've had in six years on one hand.) Loadout variety. Theory-crafting and metagames. Incredible atmosphere. A distinct and unique visual style. And a banger soundtrack that I will never turn down in the audio settings. Always blasting that ♥♥♥♥.I love dropping into a cave on Hazard 5, the doors opening to what I can only describe as "Bug Normandy" and diving headfirst into the chaos. I love single-handedly cutting through an entire swarm with Gemini sentries and a tricked out Breach Cutter. I love sitting on top of Dorretta and chucking grenades behind her into the tunnel filled to the brim with bugs and watching them all explode. I love setting up a Driller bunker and filling the chokepoint with green sludge. I love using the RJ-250 to not only nuke an entire group of Grunts, but to fly away to the other side of the cave and placing a fall-damage-reducing platform under my feet just before I hit the ground. I love when I'm just about to get into the drop pod with 60 seconds left, but the Greenbeard Gunner goes down 150 meters away... and suddenly the objective switches from escaping with my life to a full fledged rescue mission because NO DWARF LEFT BEHIND. There are countless things in DRG that are so incredibly memorable, so exhilarating, and so satisfying... I'm constantly blown away by how much content can be extracted from this game.DRG is the one game that I can always come back to when every other one of my favorite games has some kind of botched update, or fails spectacularly in some way. Over the last 6 years, I've been able to know that if there's nothing good to play tonight, I can always hop on Deep Rock. It's consistently been an S+ tier game for as long as I can remember, and that's an incredible feat in today's gaming landscape. If Team Fortress 2 hadn't already taken my heart and locked it away long ago, Deep Rock Galactic would sit at #1 on my list, no contest. It's just so incredibly good, and the experience never gets old. And they're STILL updating it and adding QoL features that somehow make it even better. Seriously, GSG is quite possibly the most underrated game development team in the history of video games. Deep Rock just stays winning, forever. Rock and Stone!
_childDocuments_.name: Deep Rock Galactic

_childDocuments_.review: Deep Rock Galactic is an outstanding achievement in cooperative format gaming. They give players roles, the ability to communicate without speaking to great effectiveness and in game tools that give the metaknowledge necessary to convey to others what the goal of the game is.The game is also highly rewarding of your time, boasting hundreds of cosmetics and weapon mods that upgrade/alter features of your weaponry. None of these are gated behind paywalls of any kind, save for three cosmetic DLCs and the Supporter Pack which make up a mere fraction of the total. DRG boasts a wealth of biomes and strategies to deal with them and isn't just a run of the mill Left 4 Dead clone like Vermintide. Fully destructible terrain and randomly generated levels give this game a whole lot of life that you'll never get from another co-op hoard shooter. Give a shot, you won't regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: Deep Rock Galactic

_childDocuments_.review: DRG very quickly became one of my favourite games after only a few hours of playing, and I've since happily wasted many many more.It is best experienced with friends, up to 3 others, or many more if you choose to dabble in mods, although it is not hard to find games with randoms, and everyone, in my experience, is super chill and friendly.If you can't, or don't want to play with randoms, single player, while not as rewarding, is still very fun.Even the lobby (known as the Space Rig) is fun to spend time in, with many things scattered around, such as the arcade games, the dance floor and bar, the no-gravity switch, and let's not forget all the barrels. You know you love to kick the barrels. The Prop Hunt mini-game they've recently added is super fun as well, especially since you need to drink a beer to become a prop : )DRG features 4 main classes, each with a unique play style. They are extremely well balanced with respects to one another, and although it may not be as "fun" as a team of all Scouts, generally speaking most missions will work best with all classes represented in your team. The mechanics of the game are easy to master, and the ability to ramp up or down the difficulty of each mission ensures you'll never get bored. Weapon customisation, as well as many extra 'overclocks' to boost certain stats of each weapon, mean there is a million different ways to play each class.This game has  had a lot of love and care put into it by the devs to. It's obvious when looking at the Space Rig, as there are so many tiny details, easter eggs, and hidden interact-ables everywhere. Missions are no different, with tons of different types of enemies, biomes, events, mission types, available weapons and weapon mods, and the fact that every cave is unique, meaning you will never play the same mission twice.Really the only reason I'd recommend against getting this game, is if you have a fear of spiders, or bugs, as most enemies resemble these, albeit very stylised.So pull up a seat at the Abyss Bar, grab a Blackout Stout, and don't forget to Rock and Stone!

_childDocuments_.review: This is another long-winded review, but bear with me - it's worth it.Pros:+ Concept and excuse plot alone is unique in itself. Dwarves? Mining? For the titular futuristic megacorporation Deep Rock Galactic? With guns? IN SPAAAAAACE??? Yeah. You won't find a game like DRG anywhere else.+ 4 distinct classes with distinct advantages/disadvantages and varied equipment compared to the others. Duo synergies exist and are pretty amazing (scout/engineer, gunner/driller). Each class plays much differently from the rest despite the cosmetic similarities, and there is something there for everyone.+ Multiplayer integration is 100% seamless. You can start a friends only game as the only one going down to the surface and then people can join you through Steam (or Discord) and instantly get thrown next to you in a drop pod. You get the same rewards and can help out the host who plays through the entire mission. You can even bail your buddies out if they're up sh*t creek without a paddle.+ Several (~10 or so) unique and visually distinct biomes, all procedurally generated, which add a unique variety of architecture, hazards, and enemies to the standard experience.+ Lots of options for difficulty. You can progress the game on any difficulty (hazard level 1-5), but higher difficulties give a fixed % bonus to your final earnings; you are rewarded for higher difficulties instead of being punished for lower difficulties. Some missions will feature red modifiers that make the game a lot more challenging (low oxygen, lethal bugs, no shields, haunted cave, etc.) but also give an additive fixed % bonus to your final earnings. There are also yellow modifiers which make the game less challenging but more fun/lucrative (exploding bugs, low gravity, gold rush, mineral mania, etc.). Any given mission can have a red modifier, yellow modifier, none, or 1 of each.+ Guns and gear are varied enough. Some loadouts are objectively better than others, but if you like a particular gun or playstyle enough, you can still have fun making it work. The options for guns was recently expanded upon as well since in the latest update each class gets a new alternative primary weapon.+ Enemies and mission types have a decent amount of variety. There is a lot more to do since all the content added even in the past year or so (and continually being added!), and I haven't even played the latest update yet that has once again doubled the game's content.+ Game's sense of humor and one-liners are absolutely spot on. You will basically be reminded every 30 seconds or so that you are a dwarf, and that you are the poor, bloody infantry working for a privatized capitalist space mining company (not that you need to be reminded of it). There are about 20-30 different lines for any given unique interaction, and the real gutbusters are the retorts for friendly fire. Also there is a dedicated button (V) for a "salute" which is your dwarf raising his pickaxe into the air and shouting some variation of "ROCK AND STONE!" which tends to be very contagious in multiplayer. If you are holding a beer, you will give a toast.+ Devs legitimately care about their game. They listen to feedback and consistently optimize the game and add content. The latest update is "their most ambitious update yet" and it is just the first in an episodic series of free updates. Also, DRG has been around since 2018. It is still getting massive content updates. Need I say more?Cons:- Core gameplay loop gets a bit stale after you've done everything there is to do and killed everything there is to kill 10/20/100/500/10,000 times over. This goes for just about anything - mission types, modifiers, enemies, bosses, mini-bosses, objectives, bonus objectives, KPI's, etc. The one exception to this is spamming your salute key - because it's contagious, and "ROCK AND STONE!" never gets old. Honorable mentions for "never gets old" is any of the multiplayer shenanigans on the Space Rig or at The Abyss Bar, or finding a giant gold nugget or bittergem and tagging it repeatedly to keep your dwarf belting off "WE'RE RICH!", or finding and tagging a xenofungus to make your dwarf say "MUSHROOM!" over and over again.- There is a bit of a grind for collecting crafting materials that you need to upgrade or unlock equipment, purchase cosmetics, or build overclocks/special cosmetics at the forge. This tends to be a lot more noticeable after you are burnt out on the game (see previous point above).- Learning curve is a bit steep at first, mainly due to feature creep/information overload. Your saving grace here is the mediocre tutorial and muscle memory from other first-person shooter games. However, depending how fast of a learner you are, you can get over this relatively quickly especially if you have a buddy playing with you to tell or remind you how to do stuff.Other:> This game was designed from the ground up as a multiplayer game; therefore, it is infinitely better with friends than without friends. If you play with friends you will have a blast. If you play solo, you will probably lose interest a lot sooner. Randoms are generally good fun to play with though.> More of a nitpick than anything, but still probably worth mentioning. You will eventually run out of ammo during a mission, especially on higher hazard (difficulty) levels where there are a lot more enemies. To replenish ammo you have to find and mine a specific but generally common red ore called Nitra until you have 80 units of it banked, then you can call a supply drop with 4 half-restocks on it (i.e. if you have 1 dwarf, you can fully restock all munitions twice, 2 dwarves can fully restock munitions once, and 4 dwarves can stock up to half munitions on one resupply pod). While this is a fun and unique mechanic, and usually not a problem, there are rare occasions where you will get shafted by the cave generation and simply not have enough Nitra to keep stocked on ammo. This reduces you to nothing but your pickaxe which is an utterly pathetic melee weapon. If this happens in the middle of a wave of enemies (which appear at regular intervals), your only option is to try and kite the horde away while you finish your objectives and get out. This is pretty much impossible to manage 90% of the time. The only reliable way to avoid this entirely is to rush the objective and conserve ammo if you cannot find any Nitra, but still, running out of ammo has cost me many (otherwise very successful) runs. IMO to make this less of an issue, the game should detect when all players are out of ammo and then stop spawning more big waves of enemies until at least 80 Nitra gets banked by the team.Final verdict:Deep Rock Galactic is an all-around fantastic game, both in theory and in reality - the concept is unique and they nailed the execution and presentation. Even though the repetition can get stale, there is not really any way to avoid that from happening and it's not really the game's fault. Even so, new content is constantly being added and the game is being improved at regular intervals. There is a lot to do and there is a lot of fun to be had here. The game is focused solely around multiplayer and teamwork and gives players lots of opportunities to mess around with each other, meaning that naturally, it breeds camaraderie.Overall, I would recommend DRG to just about anyone. It's a great game for the group of dudebros who want to get together on a Friday night and drink some virtual beer and go smash some bugs instead of going out to drink real beer and smashing barstools. It's a great game for breaking the ice or building trust with people you don't know all that well (which lends itself well to playing online with randoms). It's a great game for couples who are past the honeymoon phase and are perfectly fine taking the piss out of each other. And most importantly, DRG is FUN.10/10 - If you don't "ROCK AND STONE", you ain't goin' home! ROCK AND STONE, TO THE BONE! FOR KARL!

_childDocuments_.review: If I had to make a list of my top 10 favorite games, DRG would make that list without a second thought. This game is one of the best shooters on the market. There's a ton of build variety, the cave generation is excellent, and the co-op is second to none. If you want a game that you can play with your friends or random people for hundreds of hours, this is it. The developers and the community are some of the best I've seen. The game is constantly getting updates and patches to fix bugs and to add free content. I would generally recommend that when you start out, test out all the classes. Then, pick one and get it to level 25 and promote it. This will allow you to access the rest of the content in the game on all the other classes. Matrix cores baby.If you get into the game, google what matrix cores and overclocks are. Read about them. Then, if you're a hardcore gamer that plays a lot more than a healthy person should, you'll find out that you are limited to ~9 cores per week. At this point, download a save editor and give yourself a bunch of blank cores so you can still make that sweet, sweet overclock progress instead of waiting around.

_childDocuments_.review: The co-op game to try if your friend group is burned out on competitive multiplayer shooters. It offers a great balance of silly fun and serious challenges. Tons of mission variety paired with endless swarms of bugs. You unlock upgrades and  cosmetics at a perfect rate, with procedurally generated caves so it rarely gets old. There's seriously hundreds of hours worth of content to unlock, and it's an addicting process acquiring it all. Even the hub world between missions is full of places to explore, mini-games, and a bar with weird beers. Nothing like getting hammered and kicking barrels around after barely making it back from the last mission alive. Can't recommend enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Deep Rock Galactic

_childDocuments_.review: Great game.Not one that I would say I absolutely love like San Andreas, but one of those I am so happy of having and playing.The devs are having a lot of fun with this one, would seem. The game has a lot of little niche features that suggests it like the lobby, what do we have for a lobby? A space station were you can go arround, find easter eggs, have silly games and have a in-game beer with the rest of the guests. HA, so fun, great idea.Game is very fun and can be played either casually or hardcore, it has a lot of progress that will have you coming back for more, all the dwarves are fun, all the weapons too, all the gadgets, there are many game modes, etc. Can't think of anythink that I find annoying.The most fun part of the game is the completelly random level you get each time (even though you know what can you can expect depending on the mission biome). You have to find your way through it and you might have to dig your way through it, some levels are very vertical and difficult to move if you have a high cave complexity.Already too long. Get this if it seems you would enjoy it, you probably would.Can be played and enjoyed single player, but I guess it will be much better in MP.
_childDocuments_.name: Deep Rock Galactic

_childDocuments_.review: A very fun co-op shooter game. It actually requires some teamwork to get going, and the mining gimick is suprisingly fun. The atmosphere of being dwarfs is a good one, and before you realize you'll be hurling empty beer mugs at your mates.I do feel there is somewhat of a lack in gameplay variety though. There are a decent amount of monsters, locals and objectives, but not enough to keep it fresh for that long. Furthermore, the progression of new content / dwarf upgrades is a tad bit on the slow end for my taste.I would currently rate this a solid 7,5/10 - but there are definitely improvements to be made to buy this at full price.Edit: Having since originally writing this review played a good 100+ hours; this game has kept on trucking. Especially now with the seasonal update, variety is finally getting added into the game more and more. Although the time between big patches is on the slower side, the content itself has been worth the wait. The core gameplay-loop is fun, and taking away the biggest flaw (lack of variety) may make this one of the better co-op games for years to come.
_childDocuments_.name: Deep Rock Galactic

_childDocuments_.review: I like it, although I could complain about the lack of competition in game. I often don't know how I can improve myself since the metrics are meaningless and once you can perform your class "good enough", you should be able to play the hardest difficult. I can't really compare my performance with the other classes since they are so different and the game itself is presented randomly to each player.Each class has a max lvl of 25, then you can unlock more upgrades and game systems which can make you even stronger, however most of my classes are below 20 and I am already able to play Hazard 5, the top difficult.I would love something harder, but the way the game works... well, it will require a lot of thinking in order to make it harder while not making the enemies simply bullet sponges.I would like to compare this game to Vermintide 1 and 2. I actually find it more satisfying because there you can recognize when you are getting better at the game, you can do things others can't do (the better you play and acumulate experience)..

_childDocuments_.review: Get this game, you will not regret it. Best co-op experience I've had since L4D1/Halo/Borderlands/. Teamwork is essential, and working your way through the caves while finding loot and killing baddies is incredibly fulfilling. One of the most polished early-access games I've seen. Even with what small part of the game is out now, it's worth the money. Can't wait to see what this Developer has to offer going forward. Rock and stone to the bone!
_childDocuments_.name: Deep Rock Galactic

_childDocuments_.review: An Early Access game well worth the price of admission and genuinely one of the best co-op shooters on the market today ⁠— more so than many mainstream counterparts. Rock and stone brother. Each class is well balanced and unique, capable of independently tackling the sprawling seed-generated caverns in your hunt for minerals, which makes it all the more fun when you put together a team of your friends (or online strangers in an easy to navigate menu that lets you jump into numerous online games). Light problem solving and brilliant moments of intensity as you and your fellow dwarves fight an onslaught of alien bugs, this game can be both hilarious and thrilling. In addition, upgrade your gear, gain skills, and customize your dwarves with a surprisingly large amount of customization options that only cost you the same minerals you mined so hard in the game. Absolute banger of a game.

_childDocuments_.review: Deep Rock Galactic is a 1-4 player co-op FPS featuring badass space Dwarves, 100% destructible environments, procedurally-generated caves, and endless hordes of alien monsters.
