name: art of rally
detailed_description: 'To do something dangerous with style is art...' art of rally is a stylized experience inspired by the golden era of rally from the creator of Absolute Drift Race across the world through colorful and stylized environments in top-down view. Compete for first place in the leaderboards with daily and weekly challenges. Will you master the art of rally? Experience the golden era of rally in Career mode, travelling across 78 stages from Finland to Sardinia, Norway, Japan, Germany, Kenya and Indonesia. Get behind the wheel of your favorite vintage cars, ranging from the 60’s to the 80’s, Group B, Group S and Group A. From beginner-friendly options to driving modes that’ll challenge the most expert drivers, all players can tackle the races using their favorite rally driving tricks: Scandinavian flick, counter steering, left foot braking, handbrake turns. Get your name out at the top of the Leaderboard in our daily and weekly challenges. Show off your driving skills, or simply your favourite landscapes, with the integrated Photo and Replay mode.

_childDocuments_.review: F1 is not a more interesting sport than rally. It relies on the politics and personalities of the drivers moreso than everything unique about driving. It takes an extremely amount of skill to be even close to that level, but you are still watching a no-contact, all-traction, precision engineering sport where every car is the same and the cup is determined by the drivers.♥♥♥♥ that. In Rally, the car is the one with character. From the rich history to modern day, the sport is about flinging yourself on roads not designed for the sport, in heavily modified cars that are sold to the public, over multiple surfaces, random weather, and constant loss of control at speeds that reach over 100 mph. Instead of witnessing the bleeding edge of technology, you are witnessing two guys in a car on the bleeding edge of wrapping themselves around the next birch tree, midair and sideways. It's tenfold more brutal, tenfold more focused on the actual culture of civilian accessible cars, and tenfold more interesting.art of rally is a celebration of rally. If you care about the sport (or would like to), this game is good. If you don't, it's a surprisingly difficult time trial racing game. Still good, but knowing the stories behind these years and these cars is the real core of the experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Easy to play, very difficult to master! Art of rally is a very fun game, but make no mistake, the arcade style doesn't mean you can just "pedal to the metal" and steer right or left, controls are difficult to master, especially on slow tracks. Everythin is attractive, the graphics, the old cars, the lovely tracks and the lighting, but there's also a con, which are the penalties. Sometimes you get penalties even when you're just on the side of the road, and the mechanism that rules them feels whimsical, to say the least. If the devs can fix that, this title would almost be perfect.

_childDocuments_.review: Art of Rally or: How I Learned To Stop Worrying And Love The GamepadThis game is arcadey for a sim racer and simulatory for an arcade racer.i bought this game, tried to play it with a wheel, then tried with a keyboard. then i refunded it.when i bought my steam deck i have it another chance, and it's has not disappointed!it's my favorite game on the steam deck.it does most of the things you expect in a sim racer, but they are all a bit smoothed-over. i don't think that's a bad thing. more on this later.art:beautiful! you can see the pictures for yourself.the music is also great. interesting tracks and a good tempo for this sort of driving.levels:pretty good. there are definitely enough (though more is always better).different locations all have their own feel and style. differing amounts of elevation etc. different tracks in the same location are pretty varied too.the terrain is made with a pretty low resolution heightmap. it shows in a few places. driving over it can ♥♥♥♥ you up.sound:i have mixed feelings.the good: it's detailed. you can hear all the parts of your car; tyres, engine, brakes, su-tu-tu, (you can even hear clunks from the dog box as you shift!)the bad: the engine sound is disappointing: seems like it's one sound sound for go, and another sound for engine braking.to my ears, it seems like the go sound is modulated in volume based on engine load. then rpm changes pitch and a filter (or maybe it's just a second high pitched sound)I've been spoilt by the sound in dirt rally 2. maybe that's an unfair comparison, but that game gets it right. just a the engine in a naturally aspirated car from that game has tons of detail. graphics:the game mostly runs smooth 60fps on the steam deck.very occasionally it will stutter. when that happens, it's goes away after a couple corners and generally doesn't happen again for the rest of the play session.damage:generally very forgiving (although this depends on the car)some cars you can throw into walls all day, others one nick will set your engine on fire.there are no catastrophic failures as far as i can tell. tires don't blow, engine doesn't blow up from a money shift. you can finish a rally with your engine on fire the entire time.generally it's pretty detailed:radiator damage will damage your engine slowly, suspension damage effects steering, gearbox damage makes shifting sloweri think over revving does damage the engine.my only wish is for the clutch to get damaged.nits:these are all really minor tbhheightmap terrainyou can't click through the end of rally results quickly.playable boundary is inconsistent.i wish there was a mod to add the real car names.sometimes the camera doesn't let you see very well. (generally this is not a problem but it does happen sometimes)some obstacles are concrete that shouldn't be: eg kenya has orange plastic fences that don't break. animals don't run out of the way, instead you hit them and they are made of concrete. (i don't think they should snap like twigs either, since hitting a large animal will ♥♥♥♥ you up)only the driven wheels make skidmarkssimulatory:there is no co-driver. i wish there was for sometimes but your view us pretty high up so it's not bad. a co-driver would also ruin the music so i understand.going up/down is stimulated pretty well. if your wheels are pressed against the ground you get super grip, if you are almost flying you have very little grip.wheel lock-up from breaks does not happen much. i have the anti-lock breaks setting at 0%. it does happen sometimes but it's uncommon. this may be intended.all cars have one setup. you can't change that.

_childDocuments_.review: Hello there! I first and foremost want to get this outta the way really quick.... I DID NOT OBTAIN THIS GAME FOR FREE IT WAS PURCHASED UNDER MY OWN FREE WILL WITH MY OWN MONEY.Secondly, i am a die hard Rally fan and i have been since i was a little child.I have a lot to say about "ART OF RALLY". Graphics : I chose to start with graphics because it is literally the worst thing about Art of Rally, and concidering the fact that the old school blocky art style of this game in my opinion is "COOL", "REFRESHING" and completely modernizes this game in some strange semi-arousing kind of way, only heading up in quality from here is a VERY good start.The colors are FANTASTIC!!!! The scenery is FANTASTIC, the stages are all randomly generated with an endless possibility of tracks plus the game uses models of "REAL CARS" (with different names) that are super important and only add to the overall immersion. Car models from old Cosworths, Porsche, Lancia, Audi AND SO SO SO much more. I was very VERY pleased with the overall car selection :) And to cap it all off a very simple and easy on the eyes menu system makes for a pleasant experience outside of the car.Music: The music is actually one of this games strongest points! Growing up in the 80s and early 90s i was exposed heavily to retro music. AND THIS GAME HAS NOTHING BUT RETRO !!!!!!!! Turn the volume up and prepare to get AN EAR FULL OF KEYTAR BABY LETS GOOOOOO!!!!!Gameplay: Initially i was worried about the game play..... I usually find myself playing games like "Dirt Rally" and "Assetto Corsa" and didn't think this game had a chance in HELL of being anywhere close to as enjoyable as those games to play... BOY WAS I WRONG. This game has VERY good physics to go along with a relatively controlable steering system that makes for an overall very good game play experience. You don't need to be f**king Mario Andretti to play this game is what i'm getting at. To be honest i'm fairly confident that someone who has never played this game could pick Art of Rally up and within one night be drifting corners up a mountain in Japan somewhere.... DON'T BE SCARED HOMIE, THIS GAME IS ULTRA PLAYABLE FOR ANY SKILL LEVEL!!!!!!Game play Options: Hmmmmm...... where to start??? Free roam mode? yes. Campaign mode?? YES! Time attack mode?? YESSSS!! Custom Rally mode?????? YESSSSSSSSS! ONLINE EVENTS?!?!?! YASSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSSS!!!!!Price: .... This was a little touchy for me.... The game is rather expensive for a plain and simple indie game, however with that being said....... QUALITY OVER QUANTITY ANY DAY! I paid 30$ for this game and have not had a single regret about a single penny! Money well spent if u ask me! And if my 30$ is gunna go towards helping this kick ass DEV. make future badass games like this then i'm all for it!CONS!!!!!!! YES CONS! This game does have some things that in my opinion are lacking, nothing major.... But perhaps in the future they can be worked on.... Things like car camera views, the game only has about 7 views and they are ALL CHASE CAMS which kinda sucks but i understand the chase cam just fits the feel of the game. However maybe a bumper cam, or a roof cam would be a solid edition. Also i would love the chance to modify vehicles. Not large scale just things like rims, body kits, and suspension. OVERALL i am going to give this game a 8.5/10 !!!!! DON'T JUST SIT THERE MAN, YOU NEED TO LEARN THE "ART OF RALLY"! -Thanks Pat.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't often post reviews but I was compelled to because this is an absolutely gorgeous game. If you like their previous release, Absolute Drift, then you'll like this too.There is a nice variety of tracks and locations which can be played at various times of day and in different weather. On top of the career mode there is a free roam mode where you can drive around the various environments and search for collectables. For me, as a fan of Synthpop and Synthwave, the soundtrack is great.Art of Rally is certainly the right title for the game, as it is a brilliant work of art and has bucket loads of charm.A couple of things I'd like to see improved or added:The replays are cool as they are now but I'd like to see a replay editor for saving replays and placing custom track side cameras, think of something a bit like what Driver had back in the day. It's not something I would usually be that bothered about in a racing game but here the environments are so beautiful that I actually want to spend more time flying a camera around and chopping together custom cameras in replays.More camera angles would be nice. Even the lowest camera option can get a little frustrating at times as changes in elevation can be hard to see. Or you can see a hill coming but then it turns out to be much bigger than you expected and you send your car rolling. I also find my eyes flicking between my car and the top of the screen a lot as I attempt to see what the track ahead is doing meaning is sometimes lose control of the car because I wasn't looking at it. I think a lower more traditional chase cam would help with these issues and would just be a nice additional option to have.But the camera doesn't detract from the game that much for me, although it can be a little frustrating it doesn't stop me wanting to do the next race and the next and so on.It's a beautiful, charming, addictive, game. I highly recommend picking it up, well worth the price in my opinion. 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR - Fun casual racer with high skill ceiling.art of rally is an excellent minimalist rally racing game, even in its' current state where there are definitely things that could be added to improve it. I've never played Funselektor's other games, but Absolute Drift always looked like an interesting idea for a game, but I wondered how the game would handle. art of rally seemed like a home run to me when I saw it, as I've been obsessed with group b and rally history for a while recently. The game both has almost every historic rally car the average person could name, and has 0 licensed cars at the same time. Right now there are no car customization or modification options, but the cars all FEEL different enough that I didn't miss that feature (plz add tho). I usually play with keyboard, and the cars feel fantastic and unique. It's a perfect balance of something like gran turismo, where the cars feel heavy and realistic, and something like RC Pro AM 2 where the cars drive effortlessly and predictably. Its' basically a rally racing game equivalent of an ink blot test: if you want a casual racer to just have fun with, you will have a blast with art of rally. If you want to full send every rally and set world record track times, it has too. The art style is pretty to say the least, and the free roam mode is an unstoppable timewaster. I also really love how the game motivates the player to learn passively, and that the older cars featured are excellent to learn the basic handling on. Some cars from every era are available from the start, but others require you to complete the career mode (Mitsubishi Evo, Lancia Stratos, Audi Quattro for example are locked at the beginning) which spans the decades of rally from the 1960s through group b to modern day and beyond. Right now I'd call it a 9/10.  The gameplay is addictive and fun, and the visuals are gorgeous. The soundtrack is worth buying, which is the highest praise I think I've given an indie game's soundtrack. A few features that could make it 10/10 for me:-More ghost features: developer ghosts ala mario kart etc would be super fun to race against, and if in single player mode you race against the ghosts of the computer racers that would be awesome and add reference for other drivers in the rally you are up against.-Damage balance: car damage should be more severe IMHO. We should also be able to turn off car reset after going too far off the track as well for added challenge. Parts of career mode feel too easy even on high damage severity.-First Person View / VR. First game I've ever played and genuinely wished I had a VR option just to look around. Not at all a requirement to make game better, but would be insanely pretty in cherry blossom trees, winter areas etc.-More everything. There are tons of fun tracks already in the game, but more dev or community created tracks would be killer. More cars would be cool as well, but there are already a crazy number that all feel unique and interesting to play with.Bought on sale for $18, worth every penny. Worth full price if you're into rally or racing games, once you start playing it I doubt you'll give it up without putting some hours into it.

_childDocuments_.review: It's an arcade game about rally.The controls aren't realistic, the car handling doesn't feel realistic. But, when you get the hang of it, it's not that bad. It is fun to go full blast through stages without crashing once.Don't even try to do a clean stage with a Group B car, they are actually uncontrollable and I don't think the devs really know how these type of cars behave under full capacities. They we're called monsters, but not because they would spin out of control every time you touch the steering. Also, screw the fact that you get reset and +5 seconds on your time for cutting a corner a bit too much, cutting happens all the time in rally, same goes for drifting through someone's crop field. Let us eat the penalties and get back on track ourselves, make the limits further away.Another thing, Japan never really seen any big rallies, nor did it see all groups of rally. I feel like the developers were trying to put their Initial D fantasies in the game instead of great mechanics, feels like I'm playing a Absolute Drift 2, I don't know about you but mountain rallying? Also, If you really think a rally Subaru pushes 820hp through an EJ22 you are dreaming big time, engine will go kablamo before you even think about it.I recommend this game for anyone who is a fan of rally, if you have no interest in rally. Don't get it as it will only frustrate you on how much the handling sucks, doesn't compare to any real simulation racing game. The cars are too bouncy and they lose control over nothing.The art, the visuals in this game are amazing, it goes hand in hand with the music. Though it feels they put all their efforts into that, and not the actual driving.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is easily my favourite single player racing game and has been for about 3 years or so. I love physics based racing games with good drift mechanics and satisfying manual gear mechanics. I played in automatic initially but after playing for so long I wanted to add some difficulty. I am gonna break down my points in a bit of a section style starting with visuals:Visually really beautiful, especially if you like games that have retro inspired graphics but without any limitations to lighting and with lots of added variation. It has great weather and time of day represented through the sun position, really pretty sunsets and sun rises, rain effects and snow. Also night racing which is pretty sketchy too and adds a bit of difficulty. With lots of nice detail and clutter around the tracks to make it feel lived in and interesting to explore even though you are usually passing through too quick to notice.Mechanically really enjoy the feel of the driving, especially in manual which gives a lot more control in drifts in this game, every car has super unique handling, different styles of driving suited better for different tracks or weather conditions.Really tough to anticipate though as it is pretty random what the weather is like (which adds to realism for me), and the set pieces that make up the track each time is randomised which I really appreciate. Others might want to be able to prepare but having that random unpredictability is what has kept me coming back to this game for multiple years. Feels a lot less repetitive this way. Extra challenge in the difficulty levels of the AI in career and in the damage sustained from your mistakes and accidents are really nice ways to increase difficulty without just making weather and track conditions just being arbitrarily harsher.I really appreciate the attention to detail with concern to the damage the car sustains. from the gearbox to cleaning the mud off, when your repair comes in a long season on career mode, you feel the relief. Very well designed and very carefully balanced. There  are other game modes that I haven't really explored yet as I am still in the process of completing all career seasons and getting 1st with highest difficulty and most realistic damage with manual gears. So there is plenty of gameplay to get out of this game for the price I think definitely worth it.They have clearly put an insane amount of effort into the control and feel of each car as well, I cant stress that enough.It has the right atmosphere for me. And I enjoy the super hard core racing mechanics and punishment for mistakes whilst having a more arcade like camera view and graphical style. Definitely captures a bit of a minimalist feel, similar to Lonely Mountain Downhill which is also an awesome game.I would say it takes quite a great deal to damage a wheel and affect your turning from doing so, this is probably unrealistic but also increases quality of life in game play. In a game like wreckfest where realistic damage is on and one wheel is damaged, it does mean you will almost 100 percent of the time have to restart instantly so I actually kind of prefer this way although initially I found it to be too weak.Im pretty sure these devs have been consistently updating this for the entire time I have owned the game. They have been working on the set pieces and increasing the amount of variety in the generation of courses.Really love this game. Get it.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty neat challenging indie game with surprisingly good physics. Feels like a love letter to the history of the WRC, the campaign takes you through the eras of rally and the engineering over the years is fascinating. For sim racing fans like myself this isn't nearly as sweaty as Dirt Rally 2.0 on a wheel but I can kick back with a podcast and play this with an Xbox controller. For casual types that play a couple hours of need for speed every time that game comes out, this game is more challenging and maybe it can serve as a soft introduction to the sim racing world (where you have to fight the car instead of it driving for you).

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun, somewhat steep learning curve if you don't do racing games.  My suggestion for a good play-through...Settings:FOV maxedAutomatic (although the shift logic is weird, even more-so with the 4 speed cars)Camera view closest to the carABS set to 60%Stability set to 0% (This is important, the stability in this game is intrusive and wants to correct over-steer pretty aggressively, made everything twitchy for me.  Turning it off might be difficult at first but plays huge later when all the stuff is 4WD). As for difficulty.  I think your first time should be Novice.  Only because you need to learn the tracks.  The German stages get super difficult and you will damage the car like crazy.  This just makes you get frustrated.  Do it on Novice, unlock some cars and livery's.  Enjoy the stage art and get accustomed to the physics of the game (it's not a sim racer by any means).  Had a blast playing this game.  It really feels like a passion project.

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful, and surprisingly fun. What worried me most was the camera angle, yet I believe it has succeeded in execution. A lovely little game, great with a controller, however there are some visual bugs that sometimes irk me, such as vegetation pop-in and light-flickering on some terrain, even on highest settings. I happily look past these minor errors as the game is content-rich, feels fantastic, and is just overall great. Happy to support the devs with this!
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: A love letter to rallying. Immaculate vibes, great audio, and really unique visuals make for such a nice package. The physics are the icing on the cake, with realistic physics that make for a game that is easy to pick up but really really hard to master. Some minor gripes:- Some of the jumps in the game are really hard to judge based on the camera position which makes for either breaking heavily before hand or simply launching your car into the trees- Although there are a lot of cars to choose from here, and almost all major cars from each respective era are present, there are some notable exceptions that some other reviewers have pointed out. Not a huge thing but something that I did notice.Overall, this game is great. Amazing that it was made by a team of basically one person, and the amount of content and replayability, coupled with the fact that it's only $25 (or even cheaper on sale) makes for one hell of a steal. This is a great racing game, although its appearances may look a little cartoon-y, and one that is quickly becoming one of my favorites.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best games I have ever came across in a long time!Simplistic graphics with some semi-realistic physics that matches up with games like Forza, and the fact it supports custom liveries is worth every penny I've spent for this! :)The rivals however, need a little tweaking though, especially in master difficulty, there will be times I set great time records reaching top 50's to top 10's in online leader boards but still get gapped by the rivals by 5-10 seconds even if my stage run was flawless with fluid maneuvering and no mistakes, also I notice that the rivals are handicapped by adverse weather conditions.Did a little experiment, I tried playing the same stage with different weather, I noticed that I will easily have a 15 to 20 second lead in rainy or snowy weather even with a couple crashes and mistakes. But when in dry conditions, night and fog, I usually get a 2-4 second lead and when I'm unlucky, I fall behind the pack by 5-10 seconds no matter how well I handle the stage.Mentioning this as I'm trying to have 100% victories and no restarts used but kept on getting unlucky with the end results of some stages no matter how fast I went. The impossible podium finish problem became an issue for me when I reached the 1986 season of Group B, I only get lucky when the stages are either raining or snowing.That aside, the game is still a lot of fun, I also enjoy the photo mode a whole lot, I can happily make some desktop wallpapers for my other fellow car enthusiast friends with the photo mode lolHoping to see more cars and locations to be added, this game has lots of great potential! :)

_childDocuments_.review: Update- September 2021:This game continues to improve. Recent updates have improved the way vehicles drive, reducing the high-RPM twitchiness. The recent Kenya update introduces much faster tracks (vehicle speed) and new cars are introduced with every major update. I've recently completed the 'Race in 1,000 events' achievement and here are my quick-take thoughts after this milestone:--Group 2 vehicles are so slow and a terrible way for new players to be introduced to the game as the handling of the vehicles are not really indicative of how the rest of the faster classes handle. Combine this with the strange perspective and more 'arcadey' art style and its easy to see why people would get turned off right away. --Group 3 and Group 4 are fantastic and I love everything about them. Most of my time is spent racing in Group 4. --Freeroam is weird and takes like 1hr to complete every one of them and then there is no reason to return. --Music is awesome. Totally jamming out to these tracks.--The difficulty change to make 'Master' difficulty harder is great. It makes mistakes costly against the AI. However- there are some stages where it still seems unfair. An example is a world top 10 time and still being classified as 3rd or 4th against the AI. Ultimately it's just a number, so who cares. Because the real longevity is....--Leaderboards! People are so dang good at this game. The Leaderboards have some extremely fast and consistent drivers. --Still some jumping issues where the car lands weird and shoots off out of bounds or into a tree. Makes higher-speed jumps veeery risky. Original review:A nuanced and complex simcade racer with an unusual view. Persevere and get comfortable with the handling model to find a supremely good rally racer.The top-down view is jarring. It's the first thing people see and it is easy to think that this game is simply just an arcade game. The view is height-customizable, so you can adjust to your preferences. The thought is that without a co-driver, the top-down view helps determine upcoming corners better than a standard third-person or in-car view. The handling model is complex. There is some weirdness in slow-speed corners, but it opens up nicely. This is a brutally challenging game. The skill cap here is high and the handling model is the reason for it. Nailing your first good slide through a corner is addictive and you will soon be racing for that perfect run. This is where the addictive nature of the game comes in. There's very little downtime between racing and it's very easy to get right into a race for your next run. Unfortunately, I recon that some people will be unable to get used to the handling and give up on the game early before unlocking the second group of cars. That's a shame, but the low speed handling can be off-putting. There are a number of environmental conditions and tarmac types. Dirt, clay, gravel, tarmac are all represented. You can race in the night or in the rain (or both). Getting past that, the cars are beautifully modeled and all of them act differently. A Group B car really does feel like a rocketship with no brakes. Overall, I really enjoy 'art of rally' and can't wait to see what Funselektor Labs can do next.

_childDocuments_.review: In the long history of racing, rally is an acquired taste.  It's history spans shorter than other goliaths of the track, but the respect given to the drivers, or survivors in the same breath, is much earned & well placed in the racing community.  To push vehicles to a level expected on private pavement and asphalt, but unleashing it on dirt, snow, gravel, or whatever is wide enough to drive on: it's a level of finesse, adrenaline, & pure chaos and that only be dialed in by a chosen few.  art of rally embraces these connoisseurs of speed with a love letter devoted to the history of the sport.art of rally's aesthetics will take you into a dream-like world that looks like it belongs in a Micro Machines or a PLAYMOBIL catalog.  Each country is lush with vibrant colors and small details that show an attention to detail while maintaining its overall minimalist feel.  Cherry blossoms surrounding the roads on Japan, the snow capped forests & sheets of ice in Norway, to the teeming tone of sepia & Autumn in Germany: each stage is beautifully crafted & are an absolute sight to behold, especially when fiddling around in art of rally's Photo Mode.  Take your pick of over 50 cars to choose from, spanning different eras of the rally world across 5 decades.  Each car comes with a little history lesson for interested drivers, & a litany of decade-reminiscent colors to choose from.But the sport of rally has always gotten its popularity & love for the way its drivers handle these combinations of steel & power, so does art of rally extend its love letter in its gameplay?  Well, yes & no.  I'll be the first to point out that I have not played many rally games in my days, but what art of rally achieves is making you feel like a genius in one turn but an absolute idiot on the next.  These roads require, near demand a feathering of both the accelerator and brake & a knowledge of when to floor it to shave any time off your run.  But knowing when to hit these requires more than just a knowledge of the road.  It requires a knowledge of your vehicle, terrain, & knowledge of your past mistakes, & art of rally expects perfection of these aspects to qualify a successful run.  Just don't do what I did: start on career mode.Career mode takes you through six groups, each spanning a different decade of rally, showing off art of rally's 30 pre-made tracks, becoming 60 with reversed starting points.  Here you will pick your car & difficulty (I played the normal AI difficulty with the standard car damage setup) & participate in five seasons per group, which hold 1-4 rallies with around 2-5 stages in each rally.  It's a strange enigma how career mode unfolds, because in my experience it felt like an elongated tutorial, but with how one-dimensional the gameplay is, I couldn't imagine working on my problems outside this mode.In broad terms, art of rally masters the feeling of controlled chaos, but the case against this is that there are plenty of times where art of rally's commitment to this cause sacrifices a lot of fun in playing its game.  No matter your terrain driven or car seat sat in, your rally experience will feel like it's on ice at all times, & art of rally's lack of a specific tutorial mode makes the learning experience a tough one.  You will spend the first few hours of art of rally careening off of the road & into whatever is around: walls, trees, rocks, cliffs.  The learning of the mechanics is not particularly the problem I had, since hitting those beautiful hairpin turns in one fell swoop is a joy that is to be experienced.  The problem is by the time you've learned how art of rally works, chances are you've seen everything the game has to offer.Career mode's rallies are randomly generated, so there's a good chance that by the 2nd or 3rd group, you would have played every stage in the game.  While you have been learning on slower vehicles how art of rally actually works, each group takes you forward to a faster vehicle, removing all the muscle memory from the previous group & throwing you back in the learning bin all over again.  As career mode gets farther in, the seasons become even longer: where in the first two groups you may do 2-4 stages per season, the later groups will have you run 15-20 stages in one season, bloating the career mode to something over 15-17 hours.  I personally enjoy the gameplay for what it's worth, but I was struggling to even bother finishing career mode, and the fact that only 7% of all players on Steam have finished it gives me a clue that I may not be the only one who feels this way.Another issue is how art of rally's career mode rewards are given out.  Completion of seasons will unlock different vehicles to choose from, while colors are given by keeping a certain number of restarts throughout the season.  While unlocking cars isn't a problem, though having slower cars be unlocked in later groups is a little odd, unlocking colors almost feels brash in execution.  art of rally demands perfection to achieve a truly fun experience; so messing up would instinctively require a driver to restart & try again.  With limited restarts, messing up forces the player to forgo progress & restart entire seasons, which are already long, or stumble through new stages & vehicles with the promise of unlocks after you crawl past the finish line.  To hide unlocks behind a system that would help your drivers understand the game better is confusing & downright rude.And you will need these restarts, because getting a clean rally is aggravating under certain weather situations.  Players will have their gripes on different terrains, but the addition of snow & rain slows art of rally to a crawl, with rain soaked roads making turns a nightmare & snow capped area requiring a pedestrian touch to even think about placing; it becomes an absolute bore to play & groan-inducing when your randomly made season is a majority of these two.By this point you've spent countless hours in career mode, with each stage only holding a 2-5min run time: you at this point have played the living Hell out of every stage imaginable.  So its other modes feel almost unnecessary.  Time Attack is a single stage run with a shot at the leaderboard.  Custom Rally is a make-your-own-season category.  Online Events are half-winded, as Funselektor pick a specific mode & stage, daily events are 1 stage & weekly events are a full rally, & lets players duke out for the best time.  Free Roam is the best of the bunch here, allowing full reign over the territories in which the stages are made from, with some collectibles to find: but mostly it's to just launch your car off cliffs at 120mph.But it's not the inclusion of its modes that feel underwhelming, but the exclusion of modes that would have helped so much.  Where are the challenge modes?  Specifically made stages, like a hairpin turn course or a S-curve track, could not only be used as practice modes but add another chip on a racer's shoulder.  Playing specific terrain w/ the ability to replay spots would help with the lack of a specific tutorial.  This genre of racing requires practice & practice can be made fun & accessible, but replaying levels ad nausea is a rough ask when you have that massive career mode looming in the distance.So art of rally puts me in quite a bind.  When you put forth the effort & time expected, it's a gratifying run through history & an immensely rewarding experience under specific circumstances.  But the lack of a tutorial for a game that absolutely needs it, tedious playing conditions that bog a tough as nails driving experience, & a 15 hour career mode on 3 hours of content make this a hard recommendation for anyone who isn't balls-to-the-wall for rallying and its style of racing, even if the art, aesthetically and physically, is as beautiful as they hoped.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to love this game.  It's clearly made with a passion for rally, and so much of shows through.Alas, I ended up bailing after playing career mode though to group s -- by then I just felt beat down.  I'd love for the game, especially the career mode, to deliver that consistent great feeling from nailing the drifts around the turns.  But, sadly, so many just end up being missed to the point that it's just a slog to get through the stage.I think there are a couple design choices that exacerbate this.  You have very limited restarts.  The game punishes you for using restarts as there skin unlocks for not using them.  With no rewind, there's no easy way to learn from your mistake and retry a turn with a different line.  Different surfaces and weather and a changing selection of cars means that it can be difficult to get used to the nuances of whatever combination you are currently driving.  Taken all together, it means that you just eat all these crashes, and at the end of a stage you don't feel like you've risen to the challenge of a difficult race, but rather you've just stumbled your way through it.  I had hoped that that feeling would go away as I played though the years in career and got more used to the handling, but because of all those factors that just never happened.I wish I could recommend this title.  It looks so beautiful.  An I acknowledge this could be a me problem -- if you are on the fence then try the game out -- just keep your eye on the playtime for potential refund.

_childDocuments_.review: Unpopular opinion, I guess.The game's aesthetic, music, and car selection are the only things to choose it for, if that's what you care about.If you're not a huge fan of cars or driving (or rallying, for that matter), then this game is for you, and you'll have fun.Otherwise... well, everything else is a pain.The controls are clunky at best, cars feel heavy and lazy to turn with traction being practically nonexistent regardless the surface you're on.This game's driving feels like what a person, that has never driven a race car in their life, would imagine rally driving to be, based on a few videos from internet: basically like a normal non-sporty car driving, but faster and ooh-slide-y.Each race here feels like a 5-or-so-minute chore that you have to power through. Just a series of single-car A-to-B drives, over and over.And no information is given about the track. Why, of course. Rally is just racing, but on dirt, right? 😅In classic rallying, much of the thrill and fun comes from only having a slight idea of the track's course beforehand, with your co-pilot giving you directions which draw the track in your mind and help you position your car adequately in order to take the next turn correctly. Therefore, with each turn, the track cements itself in your mind, as you fly through turns positioning your car just at the right moment, with all of it culminating at the finish line...So... none of that here.You don't know anything about the track, not even having a possibility to take a shakedown run.You don't have  directions from the co-pilot. Well, I assume you don't even have one.You don't even have a proper way to tell what's in front of you, since the camera's view is basically top-down even in the most flat setting. It's like driving in complete darkness with headlights off.Therefore, it's  to plan your route at all, not even the next turn - you just don't see it!Yes, reacting at-the-moment and quickly repositioning the car is a huge part of rallying. But your car is a heavy and lazy understeer-machine, which makes driving feel unrewarding even when you time your reactions right. And to top it all off - you just don't feel the car, not a single wheel! It just behaves like a chunk of metal, that doesn't like you.So at least co-pilots hints would've helped! But nope.Therefore, mistakes don't feel like  mistakes. Each mistake feels like it has an objective reason: "oh, I didn't see that turn coming!", or "oh, the car lost traction here? Ah, I didn't see this shadowless polygon sticking out", or "why, this car understeered on me again", or "ouch, the game's cut off my throttle here again", etc.And if mistakes don't feel like mistakes... then why would you have any motivation to fix them?Game sees it's main challenge for the player in completing races with the least amount of retries possible, just like "the big boys", like Dirt Rally, do.So, a perfect race here would be the one completed at first try, with the first place taken.But the game gives you no motivation nor instruments to do that - just some cool visuals and music.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is quite rough around the edges performance wise (i5 3600K paired with a RTX 2070 Super for reference), however, given that this is by one person and is a much larger project than their previous game (Absolute Drift) I think they've done a fantastic job.It is a love letter to rally from the 60's - 90's and it captures a lot of it really well. _childDocuments_.review: It's a simplified rally experience with a different perspective (literally). It's like micro machines for big boys.For me this is mostly a kind of zen game where I can zone out and do a bit of racing to kill time. There's some progression with unlocking cars and eras of rally, as well as a free roam mode that I haven't really played much of (I'll say why later).You can tell with this game that Funselektor used their experience developing Absolute Drift when making this game. The cars in this game like to drift more than anything, which is good on the one hand, but not so much on another (again, more on this in a bit).The game also has some nice details like a description of each rally era that gives the player more of an idea of how the sport evolved. Something that higher profile games ignore in my experience. They're too busy showing off the graphics and the simulation to be bothered giving you more of an experience with the sport itself.You also notice that the fans and spectators are literally on the track. A bit of a callback to how in your face the sport was. Crowds of people would part like the Red Sea before Moses, and this game actually shows this in any capacity at all.With the crowds however begins the drawbacks of the game, and I'm going to emphasise these more because I'm more of a critical person and I want to see this game get even better.The crowds of spectators will often not move until your car brushes them aside. And while this is more an expected consequence of them being present, the spectators do sometimes block obstacles from view, such as the tombstones in Germany and the hay bales. There's also a place in one of the towns in Sardinia where they will float up to the rooftops of 2-story buildings when they move out of the way. It's funny at first, but seems like the devs got lazy there. Normally the spectators know what a wall is.Next, and probably more importantly, is the driving physics. They're not perfect. Drifting is fine and cool and good and nice and all. But it's a bit too easy and you find the cars will oversteer all the time. Understeer doesn't exist in this game at all.Steering is especially pronounced as the course changes inclination. Driving over a crest works about as expected, but driving through a dip increases the grip and steering sensitivity to rediculous amounts. Several times what you would expect. Couple this with the already oversteer-heavy controls, and going through dips becomes almost uncontrollable.Now after you go through a dip, you'll probably go off the course and crash. But instead of crashing harder consistently causing more damage, and light bumps causing light damage, the damage system seems to be all over the place. I have it set on the hardest setting and I have many times hit a rock or railing at high speed and done no damage. Conversely I've lightly bumped into obstacles overcooking a turn and had my car start smoking. There's also never damage applied to more than one subsystem at a time. It always seems to pile up on one part per crash.Also, I think you can pop tires. I believe it happened to me a couple times before release when I was playing the demo. I don't remember that happening at all to me post-release. Nothing seems to affect the car's performance other than suspension damage either. You can be spewing black smoke and still feel just as fast. Or even fire in one case.The vehicle customisation in the game is alright. But there are  too many camo skins. Rally cars don't get painted with camo. They just feel lazy and I don't like using any of them. There needs to be skins of actual liveries used in the actual sport. Not full detail of course, but I need to actually want to use these skins that I'm trying to unlock. Either that or they need to be cool like some neon livery that actually glows or something, not just a random pattern that was copy-pasted on.Now. Something that the game really needs that would make me want to play Freeroam mode is multiplayer. And this is something that higher-profile games don't do well, so it's something that I was hoping to see. Leaderboards are for hardcore players and unless you're speedrunning they're not going to see any use. This is a chill game where a leaderboard doesn't make a lot of sense. I would much rather cruise around the free-roam maps with a few buddies or go head-to-head in rally races with or without collisions.Also workshop support or DLC eras with cars. I need my Fiesta R2 and R3.Overall it's a really good rally game that does something different. It's not as focus-intense as some other rally games while giving you enough realism to make it less bland. There are of course areas where it could be improved and I want to see it improved. I really enjoy it, and it would be great if didn't simply remain as just a simple rally game/sandbox just because it isn't made by Codemasters.

_childDocuments_.review: A better rally game than Dirt Rally or any other rally game that has come out in 8 or 9 years.  Sound track is awesome.  Physics are great.  Cars feel good.  As with any rally game, it takes a few races to get a hang of how the cars handle.  Don't let the aesthetics fool you, this is not much of an arcade racer.  It takes some finesse to get the cars around the track.  Highly recommend playing with some sort of controller.  Only cons I can think of are: I've experienced some framerate drops from time to time and no force feedback on a racing wheel.

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished my first play through. The game is absolutely amazing, highly recommended!The graphics look really amazing. They fit the game nicely and don't leave much to be desired. Don't be fooled by the "simple" looks though, if you want to run this at 144fps on high resolutions/ultrawide, you better bring a beefy PC.Best gamepad driving experience I have ever had. Once you get the hang of it the driving becomes second nature and you can easily fall into a real flow state, similar to driving a car to work the same route every day. After a few minutes you "wake up" and realize you are still gliding through the amazing scenery. They absolutely nailed it. A single play through took about 17 hours. I did not spend any time on the free roam maps or daily/weekly events, so these will add a few more hours easily. The game features tons of cars and stages, with a nice sense of progression throughout the career. It takes you through the different years of rally racing, with the corresponding cars.Speaking of cars: The cars are really nicely made, with lots of love for the small details. Lovers of rally cars will have lots of fun identifying the cars based on the descriptions and looks (there are no licensed names in the entire game). Same goes for the stages and driver name, many of which resemble real rally drivers and stages.The music takes you back to the nineties and has a really relaxing vibe to it. Fits the game nicely. The car sounds are very well made and you can clearly hear the different engine characters/turbos/etc. The only thing I found a little overdone was the anti-lag in group A. I know it sounds brutal in real life as well, but I found it a little too loud and overpowering of the rest. The other groups where nicely balanced.10/10 would rally again. This is the perfect game if you need a break from your hardcore sim games or just work. Sit back, relax and have a smooth drive through the beautiful scenery. Highly recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: In the realm of pixels and polygons, "Art of Rally" emerges as a paradoxical tapestry of racing. It's a digital odyssey that transcends time, inviting players to navigate the serpentine tendrils of history with a fleet of vehicular phantoms. The game's minimalist veneer belies a profound simulation, a dance of drifts and turns that demands a maestro's touch. Yet, amidst the symphony of engines and the ballet of tires on virtual tarmac, one finds a meditative solace, a quiet in the storm of competition. It's a rally cry in whispers, a race not just against time, but against the very nature of reality itself.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to love this game but unfortunately it is too hard for me to enjoy, although I've been playing racing games with controllers since Colin McRae Rally 2 and Gran Turismo 2 times :( The problems are:- there is absolutely no change in the sense of speed so you never feel if you're too quick or too slow for a corner- the unique camera angle and movement makes it hard to judge steering inputs (I tried adjusting things in the settings but that didn't help)- steering inputs AND physics both feel inconsistent. grip levels and steering sensitivity seem to not change in a linear way that you could anticipate but instead they change rapidly and unexpectedly. - you can't judge the terrain in terms of grip and elevation, which leads to going into corners way too fast, jumping over seemingly minor crests and then flying into oblivion, etc...I don't get it, especially because their other game, Absolute Drift, handles brilliantly and is very intuitive to learn. Very sad for this beautiful game to lack enjoyable, straightforward controllability =(

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not a huge fan of top-down racers (specifically), but this has had my interest for a while and I finally got it from a recent Humble Bundle. If you're into top-down racers, you'll probably like this too. If you're not, it won't change your mind. + Graphics/AudioThe game is pretty, just look at the screenshots. The simplified car models look good. Cars sound distinct as well, which is great for an indie racer like this.+ Driving PhysicsCars feel nice and all feel unique to drive. Definitely on the arcady side of things, but you'll still need to take care to not put your car into a tree.+ Runs great on both desktop Linux and Steam Deck.- PenaltiesA penalty system should punish players who try to cut corners, and in some cases it can double as recovery time for major crashes. I think DiRT R/4/R2 nail this, here's how these games would handle off-track situations so you can understand why this is a negative for Art of Rally.1. Flying off a cliff, with no chance of driving back on track.DiRT: Immediately recover, time penalty added.Art of Rally: Immediately recover, time penalty added.2. Sliding off track, stuck in a ditch, etc.DiRT: May prompt to recover, but will not do so automatically. You can manually drive back on track if possible. You've suffered a time loss from the mistake, but that's it.Art of Rally: Immediately recover, time penalty added. You've suffered a time loss from the mistake AND you get a penalty for making the mistake, adding insult to injury.3. Sliding slightly off track, overshooting a corner or cutting a little too much with no need for a recovery.DiRT: No recovery, no penalty.Art of Rally: Immediately recover, time penalty added because screw you.I understand DiRT's track design is significantly more dense and makes corner cutting and track extending less appealing, but Art of Rally's automatic car recovery is so frustrating in comparison. More than 75% of recoveries in my play time I could've manually recovered from in less time than the penalty gave me. I don't think DiRT has ever recovered me when I didn't want it to across dozens of hours in those games.* CameraI'm not a huge fan of top-down racers like this, so this might just be me. I found the default camera configuration to be awful. You can't look ahead while retaining the ability to see your car or feel what it's doing. Luckily, you can max out the camera rotation setting to have the camera follow the movement of the car. If the car slides, your entire view follows it. This doesn't solve the problem, but was a huge improvement. I would've preferred a first person or chase camera instead, but that's not an option.Aside from those two complaints, I am still enjoying the game. 7/10 so far.

_childDocuments_.review: REVIEW UPDATE:I'm leaving my original review below for reference because it was my true expereince playing M+K. HOWEVER, I decided to switch to a controller and the game drastically improved for me. So I'd recommend playing this on controller vs keyboard. MK: 6.8/10Controller: 9/10DISCLAIMER: In reality I'd give this game a 6.8 (with potential to be much higher)First off, this game is beautiful. The music is beautiful. The colors. The chill. All things considered I'm happy with my purchase. Having said that, I'm not sure I fully grasp the mechanics of the game. Like I can't tell if I'm just not getting it, or if there is something genuinely wrong with how the game is designed. I'm no stranger to racing games. Played most of the need for speeds, Crew, and for more advanced side of things I played a ton of Forza and GT. But this game's mechanics/physics are borderline meticulous at times. Ex. When someone taps/pulls the e-brake,  the speed of the car should arguably decrease as it slides, even if out of control. Yet sometimes it feels like the ca hangs at the same speed for much too long after traction is broke. Again, physics...Speaking of brakes, the braking in this game is awful in general. How come when I handbrake my car slides 100 feet at 80 mph, but when a normal brake the car dead stops in like 10 feet regardless of speed. This makes it difficult to find a happy medium when preparing to corner. Honestly, I switched my settings to manual transmission because for whatever reason, gear changes brake traction in a somewhat manageable way. In reality, or advanced racing games, you would never want to shift gears inside of a turn, but the under steer is so bad at times (even with assist turned to max) that I time my gear changes to counter the understeer (because I promise you the brakes will not cut it). In simpler terms, for me at least, I've nearly abandoned using the braking system at all in favor of using gear changes to brake traction and properly slide through a turn. Now I'm sure with enough focus and consistency I can master these odd gaming mechanics but just know going into this that it's not easy and there is a massive learning curve. I'll still recommend the game because the overall vibe is super charming and it's a world that's just fun to be in. If you accept off the bat you're gonna be hot garbage, and maybe never finish a race without going off track, you'll be fine. If anything, this game has been incredibly humbling and taught me that I don't have to win to enjoy a game.

_childDocuments_.review: Please note, I played art of rally on a controller with default assists and with vibration off.This game is pretty simple graphics-wise compared to other games, but it fits the style of the game really well. It's different from other racing games, which is a good thing when almost every other racing game looks the same. I find the graphics of the game very nice to look at.One thing to note is that this game has massive pop-in.This game has some difficulty settings, and I found this game relaxing and often played on a easy difficulty compared to what I could manage. The game doesn't give rewards for higher difficulties as far as I know, and that's fine with me, because that allows me to play on a more relaxing difficulty. I often played on the "novice" difficulty, when I still was able to win a rally on "master" difficulty.If you didn't know yet, art of rally DOESN'T have any force feedback. When I tested the game on my G923, I didn't feel comfortable with it. I do play a lot of "realistic" driving/racing games, often in interior view. With no force feedback and the camera being far away from the car, I didn't feel a good connection with the car.Art of rally DOESN'T have an interior or hood camera. The camera is far away from the car, and works well at what it's supposed to achieve: seeing the road and upcoming turns. Art of rally doesn't seem like a very heavy game to run, but for me, the game had some bad performance at the start. If you start to have performance issues after playing for some time (for example 1-2 hours), set the vegetation renderer to instanced. For me it fixed the issue, and the game runs pretty well.The photomode of art of rally is very good in my opinion. It really has everything I would want from a photomode. I enjoyed taking pictures of different moments when driving. You can enter it by pausing the game at any time while driving and choosing "Photomode".Art of rally is the best arcade racing game I have tried, and I don't have really have anything to complain about it.I would give art of rally a . The game is pretty short, at the time of writing this I have completed the career mode and gotten all the collectibles in freeroam, other than australia, which is dlc, and I am 1 achievement away from perfecting this game. I do recommend checking some other reviews, since most of this review is just my opinion. Thank you.Edit: After 24.6 hours of playing, I have now gotten every achievement.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr - At this time, I am not sure I can recommend this game for two reasons only that are important to me:* the handling model* the car soundsI love simple arcade racers. I also play a lot of simulation racing. However, these two detractors keep me from being able to recommend this game.If those factors are not affecting you, I believe the remainder of the game is outstanding!The Handling==========There are two options within the menu system that you can modify to manage the yaw / turn-in of the car and subsequent drifting response / counter-steering.These options are:* Stability : 0 --> 100%* Counter-Steering: 0 --> 100%The problem comes in addressing the two places in a turn:1. Turn-in response of the car (speed, entry angle, initiating yaw)2. Exit response ending sliding and going back to gripThe resulting inconsistent result I have is over-slowing or pushing into the turn and then uncontrollable oversteer and tank slapping on the way out (the latter being the real detractor). The fact this is inconsistent is the real deal-breaker as I cannot pin down the exact reason. This is compounded with different behavior based on elevation, grip level / surface, and car type.While, yes, this can be a user problem of not having enough seat time, I don't think this is the case. I can / will attempt to continue to learn the system, but it is a system that seems very unnatural and very strange. It is counter to all other types of driving I have done (loose gravel, dirt, track, autoX, etc) and simulation driving.Since this is a KEY part of the experience I cannot seem to grasp what it is asking for, I believe this is a deal breaker, if at least for me.Car Sounds=========When we are talking about problems with sounds, let it be clear that I am talking about car sounds.For any legacy racing experience, the great point about these times-long-gone was the audio experience of these cars.While I am not asking for a 1:1 representation of sound recreation of these cars in an arcade experience, I am asking for vehicle sounds that don't make my ears bleed or at least remind me of actual Group A cars. These sounds spectacularly fail to deliver this *really* important detail and ultimately sour the experience for me.Summary=======Aside from these two points, everything else in the game is outstanding. I love the cinematics, the stages, the free roam, the car selection, the service stages within the rally, the course design....However, if the cars control like wet noodles and sound even worse... it just isn't an experience that I can recommend.If both of these options were resolved, this would be a 9.5/10 for me.With these problems, this just isn't a game I am going to struggle or attempt to play anymore, at all.Thanks for the great effort. Sorry these two items just make this a `no go` for me. :(

_childDocuments_.review: Perfectly done.Everything about this game is incredibly polished,Don't be deceived by the graphics, which at first glance may look like this is a casual game.There is depth here in every single aspect.The handling is sublime, and more reminiscent of the sort of power/control needed in WRC 9/Dirt Rally 2 than you might think.  The cars have real heft, momentum, inertia etc, and as they work up through the gears you feel the increasingly fragile stability.The cornering is a really fine art (and the game works brilliantly with a controller)  Suffice to say, without the perfect physics the rest of the game wouldn't matter--but the physics are perfect so...Brilliant selection of locations and tracks-very fleshed out for the price.Astonishing graphics-the lighting and other effects make this game a feast for the eyes hour after hour.  There are a wide variety of camera angles, but camera '5' for me is lovely. It's reminiscent of the old Amiga racers like super skidmarks and affords a huge view of the world.  I say again, the stylised graphics are not retro-they aren't even like lonely mountains really as the lighting takes them to the next level.The career structure is simple but lengthy weithout getting dull.  You basically play a set of races for each year, with new generations of cars unlocking every 5 years.  Simple but gives good sense of progress.The reward comes from not only unlocking new years, but learning where in the global rankingsa you are.  Each race tells you in very simple terms that you are in the top x% of times for that race.The overall presentation is also beautifully stylish.Screenshots can't do justice to how much love and attention has gone into every aspect of this game.What I really love is the purity of the whole thing.  It's a game, playing it is fun, it's uncomplicated by fussy controls or upgrades but with a great depth of control.  You can always do better.  The risk/reward of pushing the cars is just so.Ok, I like it!  I originally thought the price was a bit high, but having played it I can see that it was worth every penny.

_childDocuments_.review: This games exterior hides a very fun and challenging game with very competent physics. Each car in the same class handles completely differently and has its own nuances to be dealt with. One of the few games where i am glad they started me off in the lower power category and ramped it up due to the amount of skill required and make no mistake you will need skill and it will be acquired through blood sweat and tears.Worked well with my RC transmitter plugged into a USB port and you will really want a controller at least to play this game. _childDocuments_.review: I love rally racing, I've been sim-rallying for a majority of this quarantine. I don't know what attracts me to rally so much, the drivers, the cars, or the culture, it's amazing nonetheless. Rallying can be quite taxing on the mind, sitting there for hours chasing the fastest time on the leaderboard makes me want to jump of a bridge at times; one little mistake can ruin an amazing run. On the contrary, Art of Rally takes a more laid back approach to rally racing games, but it doesn't hold your hand either. It captures the culture of rallying so well it's beyond impressive, there are so many little easter eggs and nods to rally's history it's bound to make you smile. _childDocuments_.review: Art Of Rally is the antithesis of modern rally games. Instead of being a white knuckle experience where your co-driver screams instructions at you over the deafening roar of the engine in an attempt to keep you both from eating a tree and dying, it's surprisingly chill. Zen, even. I haven't played a chilled out, casual rally game since DiRT 3. In today's world of sim-focused racing, it's nice to have something like this again.If you've played Funselektor's previous game, Absolute Drift, you'll be at major advantage here. The cars in this game are just a hair more grippy, but the underlying physics are really similar. I'd actually say that this game is much more forgiving, and outside of drivetrain and vehicle class there's not a whole lot of difference between the cars. Hell, this is the only rally game I've played where I can take a Lancia Stratos (I'm sorry; ) and confidently chuck it into a slide without having to wonder if my will is up to date. What I'm trying to say is, this game is built for just turning your brain off and relaxing as you chain slides and jumps together, weaving your way through colorful vistas all the while. It's not as engaging as DiRT Rally or Richard Burns, but  If you go into this game expecting something realistic you can play with your $1000 Fanatec setup, you're not going to like it. But if you just let Art Of Rally do its thing, it's pretty rewarding in short bursts. Pick it up if you like casually sliding around corners for the fun of it.

_childDocuments_.review: An essential game for anyone into racing games. It boggles my mind that a game of such quality and depth came out of just one guy (helped by a small team, afaik). And this is not a case of "Oh, it's pretty good for a game made by one guy! It deserves to be played!". No, this game stands head and shoulders above most of the arcade racing games out today, especially the AAA ones.Getting into some specifics. This is the first rally game I played, and I haven't played any sim racing games yet. The art is gorgeous, the music is top notch and fits the game perfectly. The handling of the vehicles as well as the camera angle is just right - it is difficult to pull off your first drift and do a clean turn, but you're gonna love it when you get it. The driving is not exactly realistic, but definitely much, much more challenging than your average arcade racer. For anyone else coming from other arcade racers into this, I recommend learning to drive with manual transmission - it helps with the drifts a lot. It will take a few hours (you are dropped in a free roam map when you first start-up the game), but the sense of progression from not being able to keep the car on the road to anticipating and pulling off drifts to navigate turns is immensely gratifying. Speaking of progression, the game has a fantastic career mode - with races in different eras in the history of rally. I really appreciate the small blurbs and quips about the history of the cars and events. It  makes the game more complete. Made me appreciate and want to go learn more about rally. The career can also be played through multiple times - since each time the tracks for a season are randomized.In conclusion, if you have even a passing interest in rally racing, and you love racing games, this game is an absolute must play. Chef's kiss. Bellissimo 🤌

_childDocuments_.review: I am dissatisfied with the following aspects of this game. It is not good at rendering the terrain ups and downs, but the vehicle grip in the game is greatly affected by the slope. The grip on the bottom is very great, and the top of the slope is easy to take off or oversteer.  player needs to constantly change the focal point. the dashboard is at the bottom. the car is in the 1/4 bottom of the screen and the coming corner is on the top 3/4 of the screen, Compared to the traditional racing game camera, in which peripheral vision is useful to handle vehicle dynamics.Unfortunately, the game requires a relatively high vehicle dynamic perception ability and vehicle distance judgment ability around you. There are many obstacles set at the edge of corners around many tracks. It is easy to hit them with just peripheral vision in aerial view. and in terms of colour palette or landscape design, obstacles are hidden in the grass or blocked by the crowd and hard to be seen. only after playing many times. PS, one can increase the control of vehicle dynamics by increasing the Camera rotation. is generally fine but when the car is in R gear and using a handbrake to do 180 turn, it feels like the rear tire fraction is off.

_childDocuments_.review: The beautiful minimalist graphics, menus and music of AoR sum up to a presentation that can occasionally induce mild euphoria.More importantly, the drive model is nuanced and reasonably authentic. At 0% assist and 20% ABS with manual-sequential gearing, a RWD car handles sensibly and fairly predictably; for example, the back kicks loose eagerly at high RPM but finds its grip again when slammed to the next gear up, or when the throttle is dropped. I hesitate to call it a simulation, but it handles a lot like one, is gratifying to get a grip upon, and feels earned when you enter a flow state and begin to execute naturally.It's nice to have such a compelling driving game available to play without lugging the wheel/pedal/shifter rig out of the closet.However, there's a significant frustration I run into occasionally (and for Finland stages, escalates to a devourer of restarts): the chase camera is great help for predicting turn geometry, hence no co-driver, but combined with the minimal art style, visible changes to elevation range between "subtle" and "ambush". ...as a result of under-telegraphed elevation changes, sometimes you'll hit a minor crest that would be challenging to see under any conditions (let alone at 90mph), your car pops an ollie, and you hovercraft into the woods to get sasquatch's autograph. Other times, a major hill, further announced by a large archway prop, will roll away from you imperceptibly and deny you the 30% of brake path you thought remained, making you an unannounced guest at the local vineyard's wine tasting. It takes me by surprise in AoR more often than a semi-claustrophobic helmet cam in a simulator.A much lesser concern is that the crowds on the road behave with squirrel logic, and it's more distracting than immersive. Instead of clearing the track in an effort to be blameless if struck, they'll read your angle of approach in a straight line from your bumper, and juke *onto* the road in droves, whereupon your car harmlessly parts them to the sides like an inline-6 Moses. It's a spectacle of G-rated vehicular terrorism that unfortunately complicates the "less is more" style of AoR... but, I guess if I had to stretch, I could say the contemptuous immortality of this altverse's citizens might help to explain why Group B still exists here. Let's go with that.In summary, I know there's way more wordcount about my issues than the things AoR gets right, but honestly, that's just a testament to how pure of an experience it manages to deliver when it's on point. It's hard to expand on what AoR promises because it generally does so at or well above expectations. Overall, I firmly recommend this to anyone who wants a healthy dose of rally driving, but doesn't want to fill the room with the clacking and whirring of large plastic peripherals. Or, y'know, can't even be arsed to set all that up.It's good, try it.

_childDocuments_.review: Being first across the Finnish line (pun totally intended) as the game starts you off in Finland and presents you with an isometric "Supersprintesque" type view and you are free to zoom around the first course before heading into the serious business of rallying.I am blown away by the simplistic heads-up display with a number representing the gear you are in and dots indicating your current speed.  Inertia and real world physics play a major part here and go to fast around a sharp bend and it's curtains!  The camera tracks your car to perfection and the beautiful landscapes roll on by with buttery smoothness and all of this is aided by retro 80's glory music.  I am an old fart so this is heaven to me!  And the cars are straight outta Group B rallying with subtle name changes/ode to artistic licence.I love everything about this game and knew from the demo that I played for many hours which seriously indicated that this game would be something very special indeed.Worth the money?  Yes, without question and the focus here is not on graphical realism with oodles of ray tracing but no, rather the contrary, put the game back into game equalling F U N and you are in for a real treat.  Enjoy this game as this and Horizon Chase Turbo prove that fun can be derived from old fashioned retro goodness imbued with that 80's nostalgia.The soundtrack is worth buying if you want to splash out a little extra and support the wonderful devs.

_childDocuments_.review: This game absolutely achieves what it sets out to do. It is a fun, deceptively hard (realistic) take, on the most famous years of WRC. _childDocuments_.review: While this is far from a true rally sim like the Dirt Rally Series and WRC; it is an enjoyable, minimalist but colorful, rally-arcade game. This game has been out a while and has been getting consistent updates from the developer, who loves their game with all the post-release updates. Runs great on the Steam Deck and yet will use a large amount of graphics power (wattage) on a PC with maxed graphics settings at a high refresh rate.

_childDocuments_.review: I came into this game not expecting much.With a background of many racing games, from arcade to hardcore sims, art of rally was a refreshing experience, something that needs a chance.The best thing about this game is the art style, unsurprisingly. The closest relation I can draw in my mind is the first MicroMachines games or ReVolt, that I both loved as a kid.The second best thing about this game is the physics, surprisingly! It is not realistic by any means, but all rear and 4-wheel-drive cars behave the way you expect. All cars feel extremely light on jumps, but this is something that fits with the whole theme of exaggeration in the game.The soundtrack is something that gives a nice 90s vibe, covering masterfully the mediocre car sounds and lack of sound effects in general.Finally, performance is the weakest point of the game, with fps dipping as low as 35 with a Radeon RX580. The card is no monster but runs modern shooters and racing sims at high settings @ 70+ fps. Also I experienced a couple of crashes, but only in the free roam, so I feel it's not a big deal.TL,DR: Cheap entertainment, beautiful style, nice humor in most aspects of the game. Certainly worth a try to support the small development team.

_childDocuments_.review: Been invited into Alpha in march 2018 shortly after cancer took my dad from us (not a great start for a review i know), and despite the unusual frustrations i experienced during that time, i went in bright eyed and played. Somehow it helped me un-focusing my RL issues for a while. Which brings us to the best thing about art of rally! It´s simple nature. You just go in and do some stages, no strings attached. The game will never be mad at you for ragequitting or coming back 3-6 months later. No relearning of combos, no forgotten storyline or plans on doing things right, all you really need is that short little attention span you feel needs filling after a hard days work. Absolute Drift, the 1st game released by funselektor, & art of rally both are very ZEN like experiences. The former being more like washing the dishes, the latter being the same but with your schlong on fire.In case i´ve not made it clear enough, yes, i do recommend art of rally to you!

_childDocuments_.review: ✅ RecommendedFun driving mechanics, but sadly mostly in the late career where the cars are more reliable in terms of stability and more fun in terms of speed. Environments are great but too few. The music is awesome!So this was a close call to be honest, but in terms of recommend/don't recommend I'll still recommend it. Here are some more specific things I want to mention that may or may not turn you off. I'm going to sound more negative about the game than I actually am, but I feel like others may not overlook these things in the same way that I did.* Career overstays its welcomeOne of my main gripes with games in general is when devs don't understand the value of their product or how to keep things fun. This game is fundamentally a good game, for sure, but the fact that the career mode is so so long is just barely worth it. The same environments are just looped over and over again with the same tracks but with slightly better cars. It could have been cut by 75% and I would still buy the game, I would even give it a better score. Which similarly brings me to the next point.* Early cars are boringQuite frankly, the first few cars of the game are simply boring to drive. They are slow, front-wheel driven cars that almost made me quit the game right away. While they're at it, take out the next category of cars as well.Now combine these two points for a great career experience!One final point I want to make is that I really like the way you can set up your own difficulty in the game's options menu, very appreciated.I know there are more environments coming, which is great and I look forward to playing them!
