_childDocuments_.review: Art of rally is a great game, with cars ranging from low powered historic cars such as group 2's the Meanie (mini cooper s) to high powered super rally cars of group S, a set of rules that was slated for rallying but was unfortunately canceled due to safety concerns. in art of rally? its a parallel universe where group s lives on! This game has some realy great visuals and music, as a person who LOVES the genre of Eurobeat and overall 80s techno music, this games music sounds amazing, it takes you right back to the 80s with it wonderful music.It is also a pretty as hell game, just drive around the japan map during a sunset and maybe take a pretty photo of your dirtied rally car, i know i cant get enough of going through my replays and looking fora pretty slick drift or a nice jump.when i first heard of this game i was having a pretty bad day and just thinking of it and playing the demo made me feel a lot better, later on in the night i had a pretty bad breakdown and my friend bought me this game, it only took me learning of it having group S and just playing it some made me forget all about my troubles.would i recommend this game? HELL YES, it is a great rally game, if not a little too arcady, don't buy this game if your going for complete realism, but if you just want too see just how fast a AWD mid engine Audi that was never actually made slide around a hairpin like its not even there in the beautiful landscapes and snakes of japan this is the game for you.
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: Basically the opposite of what you would expect out of an arcade rally experience, rather than being inside the car, you're far above it. Rather than eurodance and intense duels it's meditative solo racing. You get better at about the same pace as the cars get faster so by the end you can drive cars that felt uncontrollable at the start. If you liked their previous game, Absolute Drift, you will very likely like this one, it has a very similar vibe.
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: Art of rally is a really fun game that anyone can enjoy. It's definitely not a simulator, but it doesn't feel like a super ''arcadey'' game like some other racing games. It took me a few hours to get the hang of the driving mechanics on a controller and I could also see this being really enjoyable on a wheel.Some of the things I like about it were:- Art style that is simplistic and fun to look at with some cool environmental effects.- The car choices, car names and all the extra vehicles are a really awesome touch.- Courses; Unique, fun, and challenging at times, but overall a good time. It's refreshing to not play the same 10 courses that every other rally game has.- Settings that allowed you to fine tune all of the various in-game driving assists. I wish you could turn everything down to 0%, but that wasn't a big deal.Some of the things that I did not like:- Camera settings were odd at first. I wanted to a closer 3rd person view and after playing it awhile I totally understand why they want you zoomed out so far(no co-driver so you kinda need to see the turns ahead of you). After awhile I got used to them.- Some of the Norway locations, when you drove on the ice sections, during sunset were practically blinding. It turned your screen almost a pure white and could hardly see the course. One of my biggest complaints that hopefully will be adjusted in the near future.- Some parts on various courses the road was really jagged and bumpy that didn't seem to get built properly.It took me around 15-16 hours to complete the campaign and another 4-5 was just messing around and playing in free roam. The daily/weekly challenges are a nice touch to the online game play.Overall I would totally recommend this game, I got it on sale for $17 USD and I feel that price is perfect for what I got out of it. At $25 USD the price is a little steep with the little features and vehicles there are in the game. I don't think that takes anything away from the game itself, because it was a fun and relaxing game to play in the end. Great job to the small team of people who work on this game! :)
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, enjoyed it more than Absolute Drift (same devs). There are tons of cars and roads to select, with different times of day and weather.  So much replayibility.  You can tryhard on the leaderboards or go on a photography shoot in the replay mode. _childDocuments_.review: This game is just extremely good. And I really didn't expect it to be. I usually don't play single player games anymore. I am not an enthusiast for minimalistic/stylized graphics or indie productions. I don't think I really would've ever bought the game if I hadn't been so annoyed by long loading times of other games (Forza) or would my friends have been online to play some multiplayer game. But damn am I happy I did.This game... it reminds you of better times. For me it feels like a throwback to being younger, playing old video games, but at the same time it is such a unique game and concept. This game is innovation while being traditional to what is already really good in racing games. Its relaxing and thrilling at the same time.It's beautiful, innocent and quick. It hooks me just the way Need for Speed (2:SE, 3:Hot Pursuit; Most Wanted 05; Underground 1/2...) did when I was younger, but I can't describe the feeling really well. And in all of that it tells the real history of rally. It truly is art.Its. just. r(e)ally. Good.It also has leaderboards, which is surprisingly enough to keep my multiplayer addiction satisfied.After playing I almost feel obligated to also buy Absolute Drift as well, just because it's the same developer.And not to forget one of the best parts: From starting the game to being on a rally track it takes around 20 seconds. No BS.

_childDocuments_.review: The art is really beautiful, the ambiance is perfect. The camera placement really lets you experience the game's beauty, but it's also functional as you'll need to look far ahead if you're going to be fast.There's a huge variety of cars and they're unique and incredibly rewarding to drive. When you learn a car and a track you can really get into a flow where you can constantly find improvements to your racing line. The better you get, the more confidently you can throw the car around.
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: Great idea! But...It has it's own way of handling controls and don't expect any realistic feeling as it does not seem to be the goal of the game. It feels like a drifting game made into a rally game and it creates a highly challenging experience that I personally find mostly frustrating. The game is not ready and is filled with basic bugs.Not worth the price, should be much lower to meet expectations but streamers playing the game made it possible to set the price higher, so you know what you pay for.
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: The physics and driving are tough to master but very satisfying when you start to string multiple near perfect corners together. There's a good selection of cars to choose from with most of them based on real rally icons throughout history.The maps are static but there is a large selection of them and the rally events themselves are randomized so each playthrough still feels fresh.Some of the music are absolute bangers and unlocking new tracks from the free roam mode is a good break from the pace of real rally events.The 'off track' respawn is way too aggressive in some cases. Sliding out and recovering the mistake yourself would be way more satisfying than the game teleporting you back to the track with a punishing 5s penalty on top of what you already lost from screwing up in the first place. I often felt like I could have got back on track in much less time if the game didn't teleport me. Though I understand this is mostly in place to prevent corner-cutting.Some sections of track are just way too low poly. This is extremely rare but in some cases you can swing in to touch the apex on a corner and suddenly just get thrown off of your wheels into the trees because the track's geometry is too jagged to actually support the shape of the curve. Rare, but it happened more than once. This also extends to the terrain around the track. Sometimes a slight slide off of the road catches the edge of the terrain's jagged geometry and you are just flung into space.I really wish there was a proper split/segment time for the rally courses, it would make time trials way more fun to chase down if you could see how you were actually doing in the moment.Very fun game, highly recommended if you're a fan of no-BS racing games and Rally especially. It's tough to master but very satisfying to learn. Really hope to see a return to this series or a similar concept from the dev some day.Also buy the Australia DLC, those tracks are fun as hell.
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: The best single player game I've played in years (and that's coming from a guy that hates racing games)! If you love rallying then you will love this game. It's somewhere between sim and arcade, but its simplicity is its greatest strength. It's super satisfying when you get that corner juuuust right (even if you crashed 15 times before that corner). 9/10 (would like more locations to race at)
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: The controls/physics are downright unforgiving: The cars skid when starting from a standstill, drift in most curves, are prone to oscillate back and forth if you turn a bit too far, and don't get me started on how engaging the handbrake simply sends you down the cliff sideways; but therein lies the challenge and the "art of rally". Once you finally get the hang of it, it's very satisfying to drift past the cheering crowd in a perfectly balanced line.P. S. The cars have secret messages written under them. Be sure to check them out while you roll out of control after hitting yet another rock on the side of the road. #tofu

_childDocuments_.review: This fantastic game is a hidden gem. I've been craving a racing sim for a while but didn't want to invest in a wheel for something that might just be a fad. Art of Rally scratches that itch without the large outlay for a wheel. The vehicle physics are on point, music is top notch and it's so so satisfying to play. Easy to pick up and play but hard to master, it just feels great when you nail a corner. Love this game and is easily my game of the year.
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: Art of rally is a game with an incredibly high skill ceiling even after 160 hours I still get better with every session and once you master the game you can destroy other people's times just by using the skills you built up. _childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: It's clear the people who made this game love cars and love Rally as a sport because while the game is very arcadey and fairly easy to pick up and play, they absolutely nailed the feeling. From the little descriptions to the handling behavior, to the way little people behave on the track, it feels like what you imagine being at a rally to feel like.If I pick a car, like say, their lookalike of the 911, it may not handle exactly like a 911 but it feels like what a 911 would feel like in this world. _childDocuments_.review: To start off I'm gonna to admit, I am terrible at this game. If there truly is an art of rally, I dont have it. I can see where I'm making a mistake and everytime I play I get a little better. Not enough so that I can stay on track for more than 5 seconds, but Im getting there.2. I heard theres other cars too, not sure why but kudos to the developers for considering people who have *WRONG* opinions.2 flaws with this game that I'd like to see addressed:1. The horn: Every time theres a crowd of people I get far too smug and forget that Im in a race and end up more concerned about trying to honk that chant(?) that goes dun, dun, dundundun, dun dun dun dun, dun dun. _childDocuments_.review: I came to this game expecting a purely arcade experience. I knew I misunderstood the assignment the moment I reached my first turn and flew off straight into a tree. _childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: God, where do I begin.... Stunning art-style, gorgeous music, fun-to-drive cars, well made photo mode. It's a feast for the eyes and the ears, and definitely not something I'll be putting down anytime soon. The career is fun, and although I haven't played it for TOO long, I can happily say that with the amount of tracks, cars, and weather conditions, this will not get stale anytime soon. Custom rally is basically career mode but limited to one country (though you still get plenty of track options) and you get to pick weather conditions, car group, etc. Free roam allows you to explore the full maps that the tracks come from, and find little secrets along the way. I've heard some complaints about how there isn't a co-driver giving notes or a minimap to guide the player, but honestly the game feels perfect the way it is. The large top-down FOV given is the map your need, and all you need to do to use it as best to it's ability is to keep your eyes on the road. This game does that so well. There are times where I almost just zone out and let my hands do the driving, and when I snap back to reality I somehow haven't crashed yet! I still can't believe that this was all created by one man. ONE. MAN. Big triple A games like the Forza, NFS, Dirt, and Gran Turismo Series have tried so much to pull audiences in with next-gen graphics are a quirky gimmick or a trip down nostalgia lane. But this guy, funselektor, does it all with the power of simplicity. This is one the best games I have played in a long time, and if I could choose what game should be deemed Game of the Year.... without a doubt, art of rally (not capitalized btw) is the clear winner.
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: The target group for this game are rally enthusiasts from the very beginning. There are historic cars, there are lovely details and the game design in the style of graphic art - almost Art Deco - is very appealing, indeed. The gametitle is therefore almost appropriate. Almost? Because the Art of Rally should also be about the art of driving. As an adult, I expect a game that is everything but not arcade. It can't be that I drive against a house and actually gain an advantage. It can't be that I drive through a cornfield with almost no drag. It can't be that I can only drive with a bird's eye view. This is arcade! I don't want that! I can't get a feel for the speed, the different surfaces, bumps and damage to the car. It can't be that a game from the year 2000 (Colin McRae Rally 2.0) was much more immersive and beats this game from 2020 in this respect.I hope that this game will be developed further. It has potential and the fact that it runs on my Mac is great! I really hope for a reply. It might change my mind.
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: This game should be called ART OF CUTTING CORNERS. XDAnyway, silly fun. When you get the hang of it, you feel like a drifting god. Ntw, it has AE86 and multiple touge courses, of course it would be silly fun. It also let you understand why Group S would be too dangerous (I would crash on every corner on those cars).Most fun I've had in a racing game in years, wayyyy more fun than NFS or dirt. _childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: Put your Helmets on! Fasten your seatbelts! Tighten your racing gloves! ... 3, 2, 1, and off we go!Right upon starting the game for the first time you're thrown into free roam of one of it's 7 countries the game takes part in. In order to unlock the next country for free roam you'll have to find all the necessary collectibles. The great thing about this is that you'll not only get a feel for the game and a certain map before actually racing on it but collectibles are picked up in this game mode so you won't have to restart a bunch of career races because you missed a cassette tape.The game doesn't seem to have official licensing for the cars but it found a fantastic workaround in giving each car a nick name like the esky for the Ford Escort. Also they look like a perfect miniature drawing of its original and come in a variety of liveries that have to be unlocked by progressing through the career mode.The career mode takes you through the years 1967 all the way to 1996 in rallying featuring all the important classes of it's decades from Group 2 to the unforgettable Group B and it's successors. You're racing against the clock on various stages randomly chosen by the game. The cars all handle and sound slightly different and therefore give you a real feel of depth. Different weather conditions and surface varieties will make your live misserable at times but it also adds to the games ralism that you wouldn't expect from it's initial presentation.A birds eye view accompanied by the cute graphics style suggest the game is aimed at young audiences and while they definately should give this a go the game can be very challenging especially if you up the difficulty settings. Handling can feel a tad unrealistic but also has some sliders in the options menu to adjust for example counter steering.The soundtrack is fantastic. If you fancy synthesizer music this will be right up your ally. Also car sounds are superb featuring sqeeky breaks, popping exhausts and rattleing gearboxes. Additional game modes like time attack and Online MP round things up.This then is a great Indi Racing Title with a lot of depth and love for the History of Rally Sport. I recommend taking the game for a spin and enjoy its soothing soundtrack.

_childDocuments_.review: Another easy to learn hard to master game by this team and its just as good if not better because of visuals and control.  This is a game that asks for you to try each stage multiple times while not only slowly memorizing the course but also memorizing the speed, angle, gear, and even how much brake to apply for each curve.  Sounds obvious for a racing game but this one does so in a very simple and straight forward manner that i didn't realize that i missed from older games.  Extremely simple menus and every button you would want for a game like this is there for you (While also being able to change inputs for any button you want).  I always love it when people making games understand what they can do for quality of life for their players way before people ask for it in the first place. _childDocuments_.review: TL:DR: Great aesthetics, decent soundtrack, good amount of content, terrible controlsI've been a lifelong fan of racing games (especially sims) and I have to say, this game feels worse than any other I've played. My biggest issue is the way the game handles vehicle weight and weight distribution. When going over a bump or crest, your vehicle feels weightless with how easily it becomes airborne. When steering side to side though, the vehicle's weight gets violently thrown around, which results in you being tugged from side to side way more than any car would in real life (you can even see this in action in their trailers). Speaking of steering, there's an awkward delay in the steering with every car (on controller anyway). On top of this, cars turn more sharply when going faster speeds which at least I never could get used to. Another thing that is just way too sensitive is the brakes. Even with ABS turned completely off, i'm able to slam on the brakes and instead of them locking like you would expect, I slow down from 60mph to 0mph in about 1 second. My point with all of this? ANy experience you have is not going to help you in this game because this game does not handle like any sim you're used to, like any arcade racer, or even any real life car. It handles like... well... it.If you're looking for a racing game somewhere between sim and arcade, I'd recommend the Forza Horizon series, Dirt 3 or 4, or Initial Unity. Skip on this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Art of Rally is an interesting game; it’s a clear evolution from the dev’s previous game Absolute Drift and has been created with a clear love of rally racing and its history. The game looks great and the overall experience in the game is top notch.But…the driving model. It’s…not bad at all but very unique. There is a ton of momentum to all the cars and weight transfer forwards and back is very exaggerated. This is a double-edged sword: on one hand, finding that groove and being able to pull of a series of drifts around corners feels great! It’s not easy to do and there is a real level of mastery of the driving model to accomplish it. On the other hand, if you fall out of that rhythm or can’t quite give the game the level of attention and investment it wants, it can turn into a frustrating mess where you can barely even keep the car on the road.If you have a love for rally racing or really enjoyed their previous game, definitely check this one out. That said, it’s a cautions recommendation from me because I think some will simply find the driving model too unforgiving and give up on it before they can get a sense of how it all clicks together once you have a good feel for things.

_childDocuments_.review: To keep it short; If you enjoy/have enjoyed absolute drift you'll like this. It's in the same vein but much more robust. The graphics are better as are the physics while still being very much funselektor from top to bottom. It's still stylized in all the best ways. Sound design is good even though it's not fancy pants simulation sounds. The whole package is tight and well done. It's a blast.
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a must have for anybody interested in rallying or motorsport history. It doesn't have a huge amount of content, but what is there is so delightfully well detailed that I don't care. In terms of difficulty, this is not a full simulator, but it's more realistic than something like Burnout. The cars are unforgiving, but the AI drivers and damage model are forgiving. The AI on the hardest difficulty are still hard, but they can be turned down, and damage can be turned off altogether. A few things that I don't mind but might be dealbreakers for some people:No cockpit cam or proper chase camNo pacenotesNo modern rally cars (nothing newer than 90s group A)It's clear that this game was made with passion. It's a great arcade racer that includes countless parts of classic rally history.
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game with great driving and great visuals, good car selection but the best thing about this game is definitely the music. The best soundtrack I've ever heard, I listen to it for weeks at a time and it really gets you into the mood for driving fast! The whole game is just amazing and i come back to it after finishing it just to feel a good 'simcade' rally game.
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: I went into this game expecting a chill arcade rally experience, fooled by the graphics it offered.It doesn't feel really accessible to casual players, the learning curve is kinda steep and there's not much tutorial going on.If you're willing to stick with it, doing pretty badly in your first few races, you're in for a treat.It leans on the simulation side of driving - hitting turns too fast will send you out of the road, where you'll get a penalty.This means you've got to pay attention and can't simply keep the acceleration trigger pressed. This also means that hitting a turn at near full speed, with the right trajectory and managing to stay on track feels very rewarding. For what I played, I liked the art direction and the variety of tracks / countries. There's a good selection of cars, resembling the old rally glories.Performance on steam deck feels a bit weird - I had a few hiccups here and there and lots of object pop-in / way too Visuals are cool, on steam deck too much popup and way too flashy level of detail. I didn't spend any time dealing with settings so I'm sure that could be fixed.There's a free ride mode but I didn't care about it.There are weekly and daily events, consisting of tracks where people can compete for a high score.Career is nice but feels a bit barebone, I went through half of it and it's getting a bit repetitive.Pretty fun game, I got it for cheap in a bundle, I wouldn't pay full price for it but definetely worth trying it out if you're a fan of the genre or if you can get it for cheap.7.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: Art of Rally is a beautiful and soulful celebration of rallying in an accessible package.  Even though I don't get most of the references, you can tell a lot of love and care went into every aspect of this game.Because rallying is just you and the road, the handling has to be great.  Art of Rally's biggest accomplishment is nailing the feel, characteristics, and "soul" of rallying in a controller-friendly and accessible way.  Even though you're so high above the car, you get a great feel for how to take turns, how to get your car straightened out, and when you're going WAY too fast.This is a perfect "zen" game if you're into rally or racing games.  Just throw on your own tunes and handle the turns as they come.  Probably one of the best rally games of all time, up there with Dirt Rally, Rallisport Challenge 2, and Richard Burns.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Great, simple arcade-style game.I honestly find myself coming back to this game incredibly often. While the physics and driving are absurdly floaty and a far stretch from realism, the whole game oozes of something I am hard pressed to find in most video games today: passion. And where you see passion, you can also admire the fact that no corners were cut in these aspects. Funselektor clearly has a true appreciation for the sport of rally and it shows, from the car designs, incredibly iconic and instantly recognizable, yet simplistic enough where they look almost cute, to the description text accompanying each and every one, lauding their accomplishments in the world of rally or simply adding a touch of humor to the cars. The soundtrack is also loaded with bangers that make you feel like a badass even as you crash into every tree on the stage from start to finish.Gameplay-wise, the game is dead-simple. The WASD controls definitely make steering harder and far less precise than, say, a racing wheel, but if you own a racing wheel and are looking for a game to use it on, this definitely isn't it. Initially, the cars feel far too slidey, as if you're constantly on ice, but you do come to get used to it, and once you get the hang of it, you'll be able to rotate the car seamlessly and hit the most satisfying Scandi flicks around hairpins.For lovers of rally, this game is an extremely entertaining arcade-style game with a splendid art direction, but if you're looking for a realistic or immersive experience, try Richard Burns Rally instead.

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely game. Enough of a challenge without being massively rage inducing as rally games often are. Simplistic graphics work really well. It's a really pleasant place to spend some time.The steep camera angle shows enough of the road ahead to do away with the need for pace notes, which is nice. It took me a while to figure out why the camera angle needs getting used to.Typically in driving games, your eyeline is aligned with the direction of the car. It's therefore sufficient to look at the road ahead and let your peripheral vision take care of keeping track of the car's attitude.With the top down view, if you look at your car, you lose track of the road ahead. If you look at the road ahead, you lose track of the car's attitude.The solution seems to be to focus at a point halfway between the car and the edge of the screen. Your peripheral vision then takes care of both, with occasional glances back and forth to check on one or the other. Hope that helps someone :-)

_childDocuments_.review: My feelings on this game are mixed and come with a great caveat. Don't play this if you feel like you have to come in first place every race. Thankfully Art of Rally isn't balanced to require constant victory, but its still annoyingly hard.I'll start positive because there is some good here.Firstly the amount of content is unbelievable, 53 cars across 10 classes, and nearly as many tracks. All of which can be raced forwards or backwards, at three times of day, with fog, rain and snow as weather options depending on the track. There's also four surface types (dirt, gravel, snow, tar) with their own handling characteristics AND many tracks will mix paved and unpaved sections together.All of the tracks are well designed and offer varying levels of challenge. Some are just flat out sprints while others are much more technically challenging with lots of hair pin turns and narrow road ways every track tries to have at least something unique going on.Another feature I like is that you can create your own liveries but it does require that you have photoshop or something similar that can read and edit PSD files. Still its a lot more creativity than a lot of racing games are willing to give.Game play wise the game is tough, some of it is fair but a lot of it isn't. Thankfully the AI doesn't have a consistent running order meaning its actually possible to win a season without having to finish in first place every single race.The cars don't exactly feel the most realistic, but they do drive well enough to be fun and interesting. I wish the stat cards would have included more detail like engine size and placement and that we could have cars with more than five gears (looking at you Celica.) The worst part though is the camera. It's birds eye view and by default gives you NO idea where your going at all. If you tilt it so you can see forward then expect a performance dip because it will cause more of the game to be loaded than is really necessary and you will see loads of object pop in.Honestly that's one of the worst problems, graphically the game looks alright. It's cell shaded with minimal details but the camera makes it look so much worse because it hampers game play and draws attention to the stupid amount of pop in. Another issue is the AI. By the time I was consistently finishing in the top 40-50% of players I was still consistently loosing to the AI. It took me almost 20 hours to achieve that kind of skill and not only was I still doing "above average" I was getting my ass kicked on NORMAL difficulty. I can't imagine that being fun for any body. Thankfully you never need to win a race to unlock anything or progress but it's still stupid to expect someone to start achieving consistent top 10% of players type speed before he can start getting some consistent wins.Another area where the game lacks polish is car damage, there is no visual representation which part of your car gets damaged seems utterly random. Since every race is on an empty track (excluding time trial ghosts) you never have to dodge other drivers wrecks or get an opportunity to pass them.There's no pace notes or mini map, so you just have to drive every course until you know it. If you angle the camera it helps a lot with being able to see the upcoming track but it just makes the game feel lonely with no co-pilot or other races inside.Lastly my biggest problem is there's not time comparison or checkpoints. So you never know if your ahead or behind until you finish a race and you have no idea where you've gained/lost time which is a huge deal for time trials and trying to be top of a leader board. Honestly, I'd almost recommend Art of Rally. Sure the AI races aren't fun but the leader-boards are active and the game has a lot of content. And with the promised release of mod support maybe we'll get to see some fan tracks or new cars?If you like racing games then by all means, its a bit meatier than your average kart racer but its not so much of a sim it should scare anyone off.

_childDocuments_.review: Art of Rally is perhaps the one rally game that fans of the genre since ye olde Colin McRae days have been hoping to see come to fruition for quite a long time now. The last good rally game in the arcade-leaning sense was DiRT 3, a title which not only was released over 9 years ago (has it really been that long already?), but isn't even available for easy purchase anymore due to the plague that is expiring licenses. D4 was crippled by its reliance on an under-developed track generator, D5 is still yet to be released as of this review, and V-Rally 4... was terrible.So amidst all this and the much more serious sims that are DR2 and WRC8/9, we now have AoR. And after playing through the game to 100% completion, I can say it's been the kind of rally game I've been waiting forever to play.THE GOOD+ Straight away: the soundtrack. Good lord, this has got to be the OST of 2020. The synthwave music meshes with the game absolutely perfectly, and with just over 50 songs and over 4 hours of playtime across them, you have something truly special that can last across an entire long playsession without feeling even slightly repetitive.+ The entire aesthetic of the game is completely fitting for something with 'Art' in its title. The simple, clean style of AoR looks absolutely beautiful and makes a very welcome change from the ultra-realism that continues to get pushed in the modern era of gaming.+ The gameplay and handling is also almost completely on point. Every vehicle feels subtly different enough from the next to where you don't feel like you're just driving clones of each other while exploring the various wheels of a given Group. The way the cars drive feels incredibly satisfying, especially when you manage to make that one especially long turn while completely sideways, without immediately smacking the car into an errant tree.+ The stages themselves are also mostly excellent and are a massive breath of fresh air from the claustrophobic narrow roads of DR2 and WRC8. The tracks are nicely wide, meaning that you don't have to be especially precise and can enjoy doing those wide slides across every corner. If the stages were as narrow as those two rally sims, AoR wouldn't be anywhere near as good as it is.+ The car variety in AoR is absolutely staggering, with over 40 classic rally cars going from the mid-60s all the way to the mid-90s, and it might even be the only game in existence that allows you to drive the maniacal Group S prototypes that were never given an opportunity to race in real life. And despite there being so many cars, all of them feel different to the next. + The leaderboards are also done incredibly well. Not only are they able to be filled in runs done in Career and Custom Rally (which I feel like it's not a thing in other rally games), but each and every stage has TWENTY separate leaderboards: 10 for each vehicle class and another 10 for when it's raining/snowing.THE BAD- The weakest part of the game's presentation is the engine sounds. Most of them sound quite... synthetic, for lack of a better term, and some of them don't sound anything even remotely close to the cars that they're based on. Normally something like this would be a minor issue at worst but, in a game like this, it's a stand-out problem.- The way the ground of the various maps seems to be put together is via heightmaps. While easy enough to create some proper landscapes with, it also presents problems if said heightmap is not of a sufficient resolution, and this is sadly present in some of AoR's stages. Most notably in Japan, the sides of some steep hillsides is sawtoothed to quite a glaring degree. Not only does this look quite poor, they will also make them feel unrealistic should you end up driving into them, crashing to a complete halt as opposed to tilting the car on the hillside and potentially rolling over. This isn't the only problem with the heightmap either: it's too high in places and causes the ground and grass rendered atop it to clip through the road in several places throughout the game, the most glaring examples being Japan's Free Roam map and Mount Haruna.- Physics-wise, gravity in AoR is almost non-existent. Although a stylistic choice, I feel like it gets in the way of driving the game fast much too hard. For any reasonable jump, you pretty much are forced to back off or even hit the brakes so you don't go off the jump too fast. If you don't, you either hit the ground and immediately lose control, or just sail off the road entirely and either smash into the scenery or fly out of bounds. Either way, it's not a good thing.- Stagewise, although the vast majority of the game is fantastic, the Germany rally drags everything down a notch. Not only is it by far the longest rally in the game on average, it's also the most punishing of mistakes thanks to all the stones lining the edges of the road like bollards in places. And unlike the similarly-long Japan, it's an all-Tarmac rally which makes the stages feel the most samey amongst the five countries. Even the snow represent in Norway has snow, gravel and asphalt to drive on.THE IFFY= Graphically, the puddles that appear on the track when it's raining look very bizarre and pixelated in shape. It's unclear if it's a design choice or not, but it does look especially jarring in contrast to the rest of the game.= The pacing of the Career Mode is a bit inconsistent. Every final event in a given Group is considerably longer than sometimes even the last few events combined, and by the time you reach Group B, the length of the events starts to drag on well beyond their welcome. In more weirdness, the finale of Group S is the same length as the very last event in the game in Group A, and is longer than the entirety of all five events in Group 2.= As of the first patch, the game is not without some glitchiness, the majority of which affects the bonus vehicles. They inexplicably suffer from issues such as specific sections of track in a few stages causing the car to behave like it's driving through grass and not accelerating or, much more glaring, taking specific jumps causing the wheels to clip through the ground, getting the car stuck and forcing a respawn.= Also regarding the bonus cars, none of them are available for use in Custom Rally and are only driveable in Free Roam and Time Trial. It is minor, but it does much to make the Leaderboards for the Bonus categories feel a bit barren since there's less reason for people to drive them.= The performance of the AI drivers was, at least at launch, a bit too easy for those who got used to the handling. Many consider this a problem, although personally it's a much more welcome change to the brutal and wildly inconsident AI of DR2. However the very first patch has changed their performance, so it's not yet clear as to if this is still the case.Overall though, I'd say that Art of Rally has easily been one of my highlight games of 2020, and undoubtedly has the best soundtrack of recent memory. At 20 quid the price is arguably a bit steep though, so do take that into consideration. However the developer did say that there is going to be more content in the pipeline, and if this comes in the form of free updates the value proposition becomes a lot better.In short: if you like rally games, there's no reason to not pick this up.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolute Drift provided a surprisingly robust simulation of the interaction between tires and terrain, considering it was the work of a single creator. Now, that creator has taken that simulation and applied it to a rally format. Rather than the abstract dreamscape of its predecessor, Art of Rally sees you carving your way through more realistic outdoor settings, and more carefully recreated real-life tracks. Overall, the level of visual fidelity is a mark above Absolute Drift, even if it's not quite as .In order to earn first place - even on normal difficulty - you'll need to develop a keen awareness of how road types and elevation change effect your traction. This is not an "arcadey" racer; in fact it's quite punishing compared to many titles in the genre. That's where some of its more irritating aspects become more visible.Glancing a guardrail will frequently bring you to a dead halt, rather than merely slowing you down while you slide against it. The curved terrain outside the track is many polygons short of smoothness, creating jagged edges that kick you into the air if you contact them. Worst of all, the off-road area to either side of the track has invisible boundaries that - if crossed - will fade out the screen, put you back in the center of the road Lakitu-style, and penalize you five seconds.  They are not a set distance from the track - they seem wider on the outside of turns and more restrictive inside of corners - and even in the late-game I found myself accidentally crossing them, without having lost control of my vehicle. Penalizing me for cutting corners is fine, but at least give me a visual indication of how much cutting is too much for each turn!There are also, it must be noted, a couple of really grindy achievements - one which requires you to drive 555 km in one of the cars, and another which requires you to complete 1000 races (for context, it takes <250 to complete career mode).If you want the mechanics of a proper rally game with a low-poly aesthetic, Art of Rally is the game for you. Just be prepared for frustration with the track boundaries.Recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Artistic, arcadey, but pretty good physics simulation. If you liked Absolute Drift, you'll most likely like the Art of Rally.It's not very challenging, the AI times and your position is rather arbitrary, more so that you can adjust the difficulty of AI and how fast your car breaks down. As the Buddha in the beginning said - "To finish first - first you must finish" - you only need to finish each and every race in career mode, to my knowledge you can finish at last place and you'll still unlock most stuff, and the only two limitations are the difficulty of tracks/car handling, amount of restarts you get and damaging your car makes progress harder since you can repair the car only at certain races and you have limited amount of time to do it.I would say that the game is at it's best when you find that car in the season that you really like and driving it is just pure Zen, and the challenge and progression is getting better at handling it and driving around tracks as perfect as possible.The visuals are simple but stunning. Cars handle incredible even on keyboard (except for the group b rotary, holy heck is it hard to control). Sound design is also nice. Tracks are varied and challenging in different ways, rain weather makes a drastic impact on handling.Linux-native, too!For me the only downsides are:- Some glitches on linux with AMD when using bloom at night (something similar happens in other games too tho), easily fixed.- Physics can get wonky sometimes - hitting a hay bale sometimes can pinball you away, slightly scratching your car with guardrail at 200km/h can result in terminal damage (have to restart)- AI times are not challenging but also not very consistent, you can potentially still get 1st place even though you finished 4-8 places in the season, purely because you still got more points than AI.- AI is arbitrary, you never see them, they just appear at race results in table as names, times, flags and car. Each race is essentially a time trial - there's no car behind you and no car ahead of you. It feels a bit tacked on because rally has to have some competition in some form.

_childDocuments_.review: Let’s start with something which came as a shock to me. I rarely talk about the soundtrack of a game, but art of rally is a stand out case. The beautiful blend of synthwave and eighties beats gave me goosebumps. It fits perfectly with the retro aesthetic of this wonderful rally game. I will happily admit the soundtrack alone caused me to lose focus numerous times.No matter which location you drive at, the view is undeniably gorgeous. The low poly style combined with the vibrant colours, makes for a beautiful game. And this leads perfectly into art of rally’s photo mode. Which really lets you take in these sights, I'm a sucker for a good photo mode and there is no doubt in my mind that most players will end up giving this a try. It’s so easy to use.There is also a great commitment to historic rallying which is presented like a sort of encyclopedic. Each vehicle comes with a short history lesson, about the origins of its appearance and performance in the rallying world. When you enter career mode (which is split into decades and then years) you're provided with a short summary of the direction the sport was taking during those periods as you progress. Of course this is all completely optional reading, but as someone who is interested in the sport i appreciated the detail it provided.However, my one negative was the in-game camera as it does struggle from time-to-time, especially in the corners. You might find yourself unable to see around a corner properly, or in the event of having a handshake with a tree, positioning you so you can’t actually see which way your vehicle is facing. This honestly didn’t happen enough to be a major issue, but it did occur enough to be a slight nuisance.This year has seen some excellent quality within the racing genre. And this is one of the best of this year’s offerings, and one that I see myself returning to again and again. So do yourself a favour and jump into the driver’s seat. Can you master the art of rally?

_childDocuments_.review: Motorsport games have always been a mix of power, precision, and noise. There have certainly been plenty of titles that have managed to combine these 3 qualities into intriguing packages, but none have managed to pull this off with such stylish bravado. Developer Funselektor has put together an incredibly minimalist, yet stylish, package that deserves the attention of any keen Motorsport enthusiast.From the very first time you take to the tarmac, the game’s strict adherence to minimalism is at the forefront of every decision. Not only are the graphics absolutely gorgeous, but this minimalist approach stretches to every nook and cranny of the game. The menus here are simple and clean, with little fuss or hassle. Real brands have been replaced by sleek and simple slogans. Combine this with the lo-fi soundtrack and you have the recipe for what is a very calming and zen-like experience. Driving takes precedence in this game, and I’ll be damned if it doesn’t look good doing it. Fans of Funselektor’s previous game, Absolute Drift, will certainly feel right at home immediately.The game isn’t just pure eye candy either. Art of Rally contains a diverse roster of over 50 different cars. All your favorite vehicles from rally games old and new have made it, along with some fun vehicles I won’t spoil. None of the official likenesses have made it in the game, but this doesn’t really affect things in the long run as its very easy to spot your favorite rally car. I had particular fun sliding around corners in Funselektor’s version of the Ford Escort MK2. Whether you’re driving a 1960 classic or one of the modern competitors, each vehicle handles differently. Some of the antiques can be small and nimble, requiring good use of momentum to keep speed around corners. On the other hand, some of the more modern cars require more force as they surge to speeds that will leave you desperately fighting for control. I certainly didn’t expect this level of nuance in the gameplay. Don’t let the graphics fool you, the controls have more in common with a sim like Dirt Rally than Sega Rally.Art of Rally also comes packed with a handful of different modes to keep you entertained. There’s a free roam mode that initially chucks you into the lush forests of Finland, where, after a brief introduction with the “God of Motorsport”, you’re left to explore on your own whim. This exploration also includes some collectibles that have you search for letters around the map like a Tony Hawk game. This was a fun way to get to grips with the controls of the game.Once you’re feeling a bit more confident, you can tackle the more traditional career mode, which places you into the beautifully created stages around the world. This includes the gorgeous cherry-blossom trees of Japan or the sunny beaches of Sardinia. Every stage felt handcrafted with a beautiful backdrop that sometimes distracted me due to the sheer gorgeousness in the landscape. I now understand why the developers included a photo mode. It was hard not to stop and gawk at the visuals. Once you’re done being mesmerized by the visuals, you can get to the actual racing again. The career mode allows you to slowly unlock new vehicles and liveries depending on how well you do. This serves as a great place to try out all the different vehicle classes as you race through the decades, unlocking new vehicle groups.More traditional fans will no doubt spend most of their time in the time trial modes. The game features a robust set of challenges, from custom rallies to ever-rotating daily and weekly online time trials. I’ve already been addicted trying to set a high score in today’s daily time trial. None of these modes would matter if the driving wasn’t up to scratch. Thankfully, the robust handling and inertia meant every stage was a constant test of reflexes. The aforementioned car handling was smooth and there wasn’t a location or weather condition I did not enjoy driving in. One small mistake in a chicane or hairpin turn often spelled the end of a good run. This kept me on my toes for the entire run.The only issue I did have with this game is that the camera often became my own worst enemy. The dolly-tracking style used was sometimes a little bit too slow for a corner, however, this issue was rare and did not detract from my overall experience with this game.Overall, the minimalist approach has definitely paid off for Funselektor. What they’ve managed to pull off here is nothing short of marvelous. Motorsport enthusiasts will no doubt enjoy the smooth handling and abundance of modes to keep them occupied. From the soundtrack to the menu, every part of Art of Rally has been meticulously tailored to provide a zen-like experience that is unparalleled in top-down racers. Art of Rally is a stylized experience that is not to be missed.

_childDocuments_.review: Even if you don’t win a stage, it never feels like a failure. Controls are intuitive but challenging, giving you constant satisfaction of nailing a corner, even if you only do it once a race.At its core, Art of Rally occupies a perfect middle ground. _childDocuments_.review: Probably my favorite driving game that I play with controller (I tend to use my wheel/pedals on sims). I'll just list what I love about it:PROS-Graphics are phenomenally good, I mean aesthetically for me they are simply gorgeous and have a unique look. Quite scalable too, can make it run barely good enough on my surface laptop.-Much more sophisticated handling than first appears. You can use some real rally techniques, Scandinavian flick, left foot braking (weighting the front wheels), over/under steer, weight transition, throttle control in powering out of corners, it's all there. No tuning, but there are different cars and characteristics to get used to.-Handling through different weather conditions/surfaces is done quite well.-A real homage to a golden era of rallying, namely the 80s-90s, where the Group B shone and real prototypes were getting limelight for brave tuning and engineering out of the box. ALL car models look great.-Fantastic soundtrack that plays seamlessly and unobtrusively the whole time, I love it, you will too if you appreciate decent synthwave. Couple of extra nice songs to unlock via the free roam mode.-Steep but fair difficulty curve, the master difficulty can be conquered too if you are patient enough. You would have to be at the top of your game though, but even the AI still makes mistakes here and there.-All locations are so unique and capture what made each of them special-plenty of content when it comes to cars and locations to unlock and master, the game is intensely satisfying when you really 'become one' with it, and start to be more precise with placing the car where and how you want it.It's unbelievable value for what it is, give it a try if you like driving sims or rally racing, you won't regret it. Not too mention, no scummy practices when it comes to DLC or microtransactions, just a damn solid game (the Kenya update was extremely nice welcome, and I hear there's even more coming with a location in Indonesia where I live. Can't wait!!!!)CONSNot a lot to say here, just:-if the game says it can't Sync upon launch, just close it and open again, DON'T play or you will lose all your progress. Yes I had a 100% game lost due to this, heartbreaking stuff, but to be honest I didn't mind the excuse to go through it all again, this time master 1st trophy on all career mode-I can understand why they reset your car and give +5sec penalty for cutting corners, but sometimes it happens just from going a few meters outside of the track. Not sure why, just wished it was a bit more lenient on that, if I went that far off it's already costing me time, not benefiting, but maybe it's for preventing being able to roam too far from the track I'm not sure, mildly irritating is all.-Be careful with the graphics options, there are very few things which will kill your framerate out of the blue if your rig is not up to it. On the whole, it is extremely well optimized though.

_childDocuments_.review: Funselektor Labs Inc.'s "art of rally" is a veritable feast for the eyes, made by one dev and released on 23.09.2020, featuring some stunning environments and a really competent photo mode. As many other reviews have pointed out, however, this incredibly admirable single dev effort has some glaring design issues, which are unfortunate and need to be listed for potential players to know. has been getting updates, content and even a DLC ever since. The game even has historical facts about the niche sport of rally, which it seems to idolize (for better or for worse), which makes for an extremely interesting quasi-historical experience, with some possibly questionable beatification (such as crowds being faceless rectangles, who just magically teleport out of the way at the speed of light when accidentally ran into), that all makes for a one-of-a-kind experience.The minimalist graphical style is beautiful, and fits the game well, and along with some post-processing on the game's highest settings makes for some stunning images, views and landscapes. The vehicle skins which you unlock through competition and placement in the titular rallies, are also really lovely and exhaustive, as is the game's options menu.Unfortunately, the fun rally game suffers from a marked lack of drifting. Your cars can, at times, behave erratically, and attempting a drift, which is half of what this exhilirating sport – that the game ostensibly pays great homage to otherwise – is known for, is a surefire way to skid into the nearest tree or lose complete control  of your vehicle and tumble into the next lake. This is not very fun, and many of the game's world records, found on Youtube (), while stunning displays of skill and control in their own right, are actually pretty bland to watch, because they feature the safest, most boring ways to take turns imaginable, because that is the only valid way to play the game, unless you're a sadist who wants to scar your nameless and faceless rally racer forever or cut their life tragically short, for some reason.The second, somewhat smaller, issue are the inconsitencies in the invisible walls, which make the screen go black, and the player's car to be respawned on the road, while simultaneously accruing a 5 second time penalty. Sometimes you can take a turn wide, sometimes you can skip a bit through the grass, other times you'll just be hit with a penalty while driving slightly off-road.Lastly, sometimes you'll just not see an elevation change, or a turn coming in time, due to the game's strange camera angles and occasionally large and opaque foliage or fog.A final observation is the liminality of the experience, which is not inherently critical, but something that I certainly find strange. You cannot see your driver, houses on the sides of the road are seemingly empty, no amount of squinting will make your eyes pierce the non-translucent windows, the crowd are, as stated elsewhere, set dressing, placed at random intervals, and invulnerable to any of your roadside blunders, the sound effects are only of the car, and an occasional, sterile cheering from the crowds, as you pass them by. Animals that may appear in the environments look placed down and don't move a muscle, an inch a single iota of their models. You race by yourself, and other racers only appear as names on a leaderboard, similarly faceless to everyone and everything else. It feels like you're driving through a peculiar, yet undeniably enticing dreamscape at times. is a somewhat fun, odd and flawed experience, all at the same time, and I still do recommend it for hardcore fans of the sport or video games based on it, due to the historical elements and the incredible passion and work displayed by its sole developer. Just maybe pick it up on a sale, or in a bundle and/or strongly temper your expectations, as it is not a perfect game, by any means.

_childDocuments_.review: Update: After playing the first two stages (offline).  This game is a perfect blend of "Drift" mechanics and arcade racing. What are "Drift" mechanics? 1. You don't lose momentum moving laterally (sliding). Instead of your car flipping over you slide real fast. 2. To counter this, the game gives you super-counter-steer, the front wheels work real good when sliding. What this leads to is a different way of cornering. But here's the thing, you can still corner the traditional way, albeit at a slower speed, but once you get used to the "Drift" way, it's so much fun. So why did I hate "absolute Drift and love this game? A.Drift was a 2D open world parking lot with one car that you couldn't change. This is a proper racing game with many different cars, beautiful tracks, and you can adjust the "Drift" effects to match your style.---------------------------------1. There is a demo, try it.2. This is not Drift. I love drifting in 3D driving games but hated Drift. This has some similar mechanical aspects but you can adjust them and don't have to do 20 figure 8's in a row.3. You can adjust Stability and Counter Steer and and ABS. I've had luck putting Counter Steer at it's lowest and then adjusting Stability based in the speed of my car.  Fee Roam mode is a great way to mess around with settings, try different cars, and get collectibles.4. Finally, this game is like Trials in that there are no Skills, Abilities, or cheats. Once you have a car your time depends on you and not your level.5. There's a lot of content as far as maps and cars, and so far the cars seem to drive differently based on drive wheels and class, so whether you want to relax and drive around or try and 'git gud', there's a lot to occupy you.

In art of rally you get something that you don't see in the screenshots and trailers: A great handling model, beautiful tracks while it's much more challenging and deep than you might think. This game has been made with passion and by people who clearly seem to know a thing or two about rally racing.It's not 100% my cup of tea as i prefer to enjoy pure arcade racers (Dirt 5 at the moment) so i might not play much of it, but if you like a good challenge, look no further. Even if i end up refunding it as it's not 100% for me, i want to recommend it to pure rally fans and everyone who has a weak spot for leaderboard challenges and artsy visuals.

_childDocuments_.review: is a minimalistic, bird’s eye view racing game. Your goal is to win championships spanning from the 60s and through to the mid-90s.One of the most striking things about  is the presentation: a wonderful, vibrant low-poly visual style, which also includes atmospheric volumetric lighting. Driving towards the setting sun on evening stages is a sight to behold. On top of this, a photo mode is available for your pleasure. It lets you enjoy the lawyer-friendly rally cars blasting through the track, leaving trails of thick smoke in their wake and with their brake discs glowing and sparking. The trackside spectators being cubes may seem odd at first, but they actually complement the game’s aesthetics very nicely.Despite its simple and unassuming looks, this game is quite intensive. I managed to get a consistent 60fps at 1440p on my  system after lowering the “quality” option one step from the maximum. It only seems to affect vegetation density, and the game still looks fantastic with the remaining options at maximum. Otherwise, I’ve not encountered stability issues with this title.For your listening pleasure, please enjoy the  of sensational retrowave soundtrack created by Ukrainian-based composer . It successfully captures the high stakes nature and intense atmosphere of the motorsport and will make you want to drive . Beyond the music, this title nails the sound effects with the same elegance that it wins me over visually. The clusters of spectators whistle and cheer, the Finns shout “oy oy oy!” as they should, the cars sound properly beefy, and later on the backfires sound closer to . Now that’s how you burn fuel in style!This is a racing game entirely devoted to the eponymous motorsport: you must complete point-to-point stages without wrapping yourself around trees or guardrails and try to beat the other opponents vying to do the same. Consistency is king - overdriving can waste valuable time, if not outright ruin your race. Defying tradition, you don’t get a co-driver or pace notes throughout events. The absence of these hallmarks of rallying can appear jarring, but  makes up for it with the camera; it is placed high and far behind your car, letting you see well into the distance and anticipate the changing road conditions. You can even alter its rotation speed, height and field of view, so you’re pretty much guaranteed to find something comfortable. A big challenge that the camera system faces is how to convey elevation and banking changes, and that is also resolved through clever darkening of the track and marking possible jumps with the classic rally gates. From your starting roster of 60s passenger cars all the way to the monstrous prototypes, each vehicle feels satisfying to handle. They have the right balance of accessibility and depth to their handling, and you’re certain to find your favourite rides quickly. You’re going to have great fun tossing these things around hairpins, regardless of using the keyboard, a gamepad or something more exotic. There’s the odd steering re-centre speed when coming out of a slide which may catch you off-guard or indeed send you into a guardrail, but it can be thankfully minimized through the plentiful assist and controller options. There are just so many options! What next, blood type? In the career mode, you will participate in championships spanning over 30 years of rally history. Each race group has five championships that are randomly generated with a sequence of stages; later championships grow longer and more complex. Every region has unique characteristics, both visually and mechanically. As an example, Finland is the classic high-speed dirt roller-coaster with plenty of chances to catch air time, while Germany is top speed asphalt racing on tight roads. Spectators litter each rally stage in large clusters, frequently near opportunities to catch big air time or power-slide through a hairpin. These blocky fellas are absolutely nuts, they try to get close to your car even as it barrels towards them – much like in real life rallying! I’m hesitant to claim these people's ability to occasionally leap onto building rooftops as “realistic”, but it sure is funny. On the other hand, the damage system feels rather undercooked. Moderately fast impacts into trees and rocks have only a chance of degrading your components, while merely scraping against a rail at top speed wrecks your car and can force a restart. The consequences of low part health also seem imbalanced. Suspension understandably makes you pull to one side and worsens your stability, while critical engine condition has you drive an impressive fireball through the stage. That being said, the remaining components could do with better feedback as they sustain wear and tear. Very rarely, you may get a tyre puncture, but in all my time playing I only suffered this twice. At the end of the day, the damage modelling serves as a basic yet functional incentive to not make like Samir and break the car.The stages are open, and the roads are fairly wide, but you must curb your instinct to cut corners too deeply. It’s not just because of dangers like ditches, rocks and trees; instead, there’s an aggressive corner-cutting prevention that resets your car onto the road with a minor time penalty if you try to gain too big of an advantage. It’s understandable why it exists, I just wonder if it could have been done more smoothly, or have that measure removed in its entirety. Your goal through each championship is to finish on the podium without retiring. Complete the five championships in a group to advance to the next one; complete all groups to win the game. Simple and straight to the point. You unlock new vehicles as you progress, and finishing championships without exhausting your restarts also unlocks a bonus skin for each of your cars. It keeps to the spirit of rallying, where just finishing in one piece is commendable, yet at the same time it doesn’t explicitly demand perfection. Do note that the  AI difficulty is rather unbalanced, as they can score seemingly impossible times on early or mid-game stages, then suddenly forget how to drive in rainy weather. At least their mechanical faults are amusing; “bird in cabin” should say enough.You can expect the career mode to last around 20 hours. This may be on the lengthy side for some, given that you only ever race in a single discipline. Players who crave for more, though, can cruise around separate free-roam maps and collect their goodies; these include extra music tracks, beauty spots and the developer’s real-life van, hidden somewhere in each level. The long-term longevity comes from this game being a collection of time-attack courses, and with six tracks per region, reverse layouts plus leaderboards for dry vs. wet for each car class, becoming the best in the world will take a long time.

Easy to get into, hard to master. 10/10 :)---EDIT: Game came out and it was good. 38 hours of play later, running the game in Master difficulty and keep finding the AI doing some strangely fast times. I'm consistently into the top 1% of overall times (by humans) and yet the AI is smashing my best times by sometimes full 5 seconds.Went digging and apparently times are derived from the human leader boards which are riddled with impossible times or probably times from a time attack run from a human with a cherry picked car for that specific stage, making the running of the regular "career" mode in Master difficulty basically impossible.Initially I thought it was me and then I kept seeing my own time within the global top 15 and still not get first place on the stage because someone has put in a time 20 seconds short of anything possible as they'd need to go full speed with the car around all corners. _childDocuments_.review: Not really arcade, not really sim, art of rally is a compelling top down racing game with multiple layers to be discovered and a high skill ceiling. Chill but also competitive, it's demanding enough to stay interesting but the whole atmosphere, beautiful aesthetics and a banging soundtrack also make it a relaxing and memorable experience. The different cars have a weight to them and feel amazing after a bit of a learning curve, you feel completly in control. The difference in handling is really noticeable between the vehicules, the best example being RWD vs AWD. If you're familiar with racing/rally you'll find techniques like weight transfer, handbrake turns and drifts can and should be applied here. You can even clutch kick. The game offers manual or automatic transmissions and controllers and wheels are supported. ( And highly recommended, please don't play this game on keyboard.) There is A LOT of cars to try and mastering them will take time, some will fit a specific driving style, some will control you more than you control them. Most engines sound great, some better than others, but they are pretty decent overall. The lack of pacenotes is justified by the top down camera which can get some getting used to, although it is entirely customisable and you can get it closer to your car while still having vision of the turns ahead ( in some rare cases visibility can be a problem, but honestly nothing dramatic ) My camera settings : 1/35/70/30.The replay and photo modes are well implemented and a welcome feature.There's five locations with six unique forward/reverse stages, playable at any time of day plus the addition of rain. Five free roam locations with collectibles/unlockables. All this with an interesting career mode will keep you busy for a while.But for me the game really starts once you start getting into leaderboard attack. There's nothing quite as satisfying as finally getting that top 100/50/10 you've been setting your eyes on. This is where you can really feel your improvements and skill refining in the game. This is where most of my time playing the game is, because it is honestly addicting. I don't have a lot of negative things to say about the game.  Stages all have the same width. I wish there was a night mode, that UI background is bright. More stages and locations, replay viewing/import from other players ( just to see what other planets some drivers live on... ), more custom cameras. Less bouncy jump landings. Optimized vegetation/less popping. Favorites cars : group 2 : das 119igroup 3 : the rotary 3, il nonno 313, the zettogroup 4 : das whip, turbo brick, the cozzie sr5group b : the cozzie sr2, das hammer v1/v3, il monster ( the rotary b7 in this category is probably the car I dislike the most)group s : the rotary s7, the umibozu, il gorilla e1group A : They're all good. But it's the fujin. My personal favorite car in the game. 1500+ km driven, top 100 in all stages with a few top 20/10 here in there. If in doubt... just flex :DSpecial mention to the 4 hour long exeptionnal soundtrack.Now should you get it? Don't care about racing or time attack : hmm??You like racing : yes. You like rally : what are you waiting for?! stop reading this book of a review and buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: There are some game design decisions I don't like, e.g. the 5 sec penalty mechanism, no co-driver / pace notes but goofy restart system etc. But none of that really matters, the game is focused like no other I've seen in years. It's no-nonsense driving from the very beginning without extra crap, beautifully balanced and polished progression. It's not difficult, but it's definitely not easy to master. This is how I like my games. Extra point for the glowing brake disks.

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute gem! This comes across almost deceptively, but the stylize artwork is just gorgeous, the soundtrack is relaxing and not tiresome, and the overall game is a true work of love. It is evident in the descriptions, the gameplay, the sounds, the cars and more. It deliberately ignores the trend of other rivals all striving to be more real than real, and instead stays true to its mission of providing a seriously addictive experience. You will start confused and crashing left and right, but this passes as you learn to handle the cars, speed and more, and I have only played with training wheels on. One can manage full clutch and gear changes. Highly recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just so good. I was not sure if I would like the camera beeing top down all the time as I usually prefer cockpit cameras in any kind of racing games and hugely dislike third person views, but in this game it fits just so good.Driving the cars feels really good as well, not as realistic as games Dirt Rally or such but also not as arcardy as Need for Speed. Really surprised by the handling of the cars as they seem to really differ from car to car.Beeing able to adjust or disable the driving aids is also a big plus for me, as this gives the player a better choice to adjust the driving to the own preferance.The option to change gears manually was unexpected, as I did not think it would be possible. But it is, so that's a big plus for me.Even though I did play the Demo, I did not know that there would be free roam in this as well, which is really nice. Beeing able to just drive around and enjoy the car and open world is definitely nice.Then there is the graphics and performance, which is also really nice. Playing on 1440p with max settings and having ~80 - 120 fps with a Gtx 1080 or so is really nice. The artstyle really looks gorgeous.The sound fits the graphics perfectly and also gives it a touch of retro games, which is nice. Really enjoyed just driving around, listening to the car and the sound track and enjoying the beautiful sunsets :DEven though I do not know how much playtime I can get out of this game yet, I definitely recommend  this game to anyone who likes racing games (rally in particular, as i do not think you can race on the same track against other cars).
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: A great rally racing game at a good price.The low-poly art style is great, and somehow manages to look good even in the photo-mode where you can get right down to the road to take pictures with some fairly extensive settings to get that shot "just right".Soundtrack is basic but good.Game is mostly single player but includes daily and weekly events to compete against others and leader-boards just like Absolute Drift.Car selection is quite large and the different cars do handle differently, so you're not just picking a body style and going.The game doesn't take itself too seriously either, with several car names and descriptions being fairly humorous (such as the Volvo "turbo brick").Overall highly recommend as a pick-up and play rally experience.
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: This simple, yet unmistakably beautiful and intriguing sleeper of a game completely took me by surprise.  I used to watch the WRC back when it was in it's hay day.  I loved the Evo's and the Subies always having head to head times.  Anyway, this game will keep you guessing and learning every single time you change track, time of day, weather, the car you choose/unlock or just simply the direction of the track. You don't get to choose which races you do first, but it does offer something else that is equally fun and entertaining.  There is a free roam option where you drive around different locations/tracks and collect the "Artifacts" that are placed around the area.  You can also stop at the camera locations and take some quite nice photos using the photo mode.  Next, you have time attack options and even though I have already beaten the campaign section, it doesn't take too long if you're a good gamer/driver.    I just hope they continue adding conent because finding this game is one of the better things that's happened recently!!! Anyway, you can compare your speed/times to the records and try to move up in standings.  The further you progress, the faster, easier and more fun you end up having!  Out of 10 stars, this game, and #Funselektor get 9. Not much can reach a ten, much less an idnie developed game.  The vehicles are each completely different to drive and control.  Anyway, I will give this game, out of 10 Lancer Evo's, I give the game a 9 and the only thing I'm taking points away for is the amount/number of tracks.....   I know the game is very gorgeous and fun either way, but I just wanted to point out that for a smaller game and not very CPU or GPU straining, I'm still going through trying to 100% each map on each track in each class.  Anyway, the Game has it's very own unique and nice soundtrack.  It is well worth the money!  Enjoy!MiAtCh
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: A love letter to the golden era of rallying, with a hint of alternative history, featuring a huge selection of iconic cars from group 2 through a suped up Group A (including Group B and Group S). This is not a sim racer, but it's no push over and is demanding enough to reward replay and mastery. The cars feel distinct and behave intuitively (RWD cars feel like RWD cars).The soundtrack is 50 tracks of great retro synthwave and the art style is clean, pleasing low poly.This is rally and chill. A zen rally game that you can play with having to intensely focus on pace notes. All I would add is more content (because I love what's here and want more) and more long term structure and incentives. The daily and weekly online events are nice, but pretty bare bones. You don't really get anything from playing them and the leaderboards disappear once they next event starts (unless I missed something).
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: art of rally is a game where the base driving physics are solid enough to carry the game on it's own despite its quirks. The way the game handles can be extremely satisfying, especially if you're a time attack nut like myself.It doesn't have everything, and there's still problems. Here's the shortlist.1. S class has one dominant car (Rotary S7), and the rest are just on the whole frustrating to drive with very little reward for mastering a lower tier car.2. Gear management and rev management using the clutch is counterproductive, and will deter some players from getting serious about top level driving.3. Some cars just hate jumps to a point where it feels less like the chaos of rally conditions, but moreso that the suspension geometry is actually just a problem on cars that should otherwise be capable.4. In their effort to create a minimalist driving experience, some staples of the rally genre are missing, i.e split times for sectors. It really sticks out, but its arguable that the clean look of the game is to it's merit.If you can appreciate a solid, unique driving engine, and can handle some jank, art of rally is a must play. If you're looking for a fully rounded out experience, perhaps look elsewhere.
_childDocuments_.name: art of rally

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game! As someone who has gotten bored of most big name rally games from the past 5 or so years, this game is so refreshing to play. Unlike the most recent DIRT or WRC -where once you build up enough skill- moving to the next game in  the series just kinda feels like more of the same game, this game feels far more unique even compared to it's developer's previous title Absolute Drift. The variety in how each of the cars handles through bumps and corners as well as the variety of courses, challenges, and locations will definitely still feel fresh in a year or two.
