_childDocuments_.review: The core premise is of seeing the opponents actions before they happen is cool, but you aren't allowed to track when missiles will land and kind of just have to hope you dashed at precisely the right moment, since that's the only way to avoid them, otherwise they are pretty much guaranteed to hit. Once there's whole swarms of missiles in the air good luck keeping track of them. Sure there's a lot of customisation but unless all your mechs have light builds good at dodging missiles they'll just get torn apart. Also you can't save during missions which is silly, it's a single player game who cares? Stability issues have cost me hours of progress. There's a good game underneath those glaring flaws but until they fix missiles at the very least I can't recommend Phantom Brigade.

_childDocuments_.review: Good, but flawed. With a specific neutral realistic approach to mecha, that may seem boring to some people. but to me this is one of the "dream games", the ones you fantasize about as a kid, all the complicated mechanics and systems. It solves most of the problems of such design with adult methods, and makes it work (kinda, however there are problems with balance). Turn based combat that makes sense in context of the world? Check. Valid reason why player only has several mechs and not an army of them? Check. Have a pilot system with pilot hp that makes sense in the context of the world? Check. Pilot emergency ejection system mechanism that makes sense? Check. I could go on, but you get the idea. Some systems are complicated but they are elegant and make sense with how they work together, not everything is fleshed out yet, some features need some balancing or more development, but there are no major bugs. It really feels like an indie game with a clear vision, but one that is pretty solid on release, which is not always the case for some popular releases. Best bought with a discount.

_childDocuments_.review: A creative and fun mech game. It's technically turn based but it's more of a 'plan and go' style where you plan your moves at the beginning of the turn and then everything gets acted out in real time.The overworld gameplay is actually closer to Mount & Blade than an XCom derivative. You have a single mobile base that goes around areas to capture areas. The loop is you 'farm' an area for upgrades, then when you feel ready you initiate a war to gain control, which gives you timed objectives to capture towns in the area. It works, but I wouldn't call it particularly strategic.Negatives:The pilots are blank ciphers with no stats, they only function as a limiting resources and you can move them between different mechs and they won't influence how they behave. Even the random events don't mention any pilots by name. This part is particularly frustrating because very early concepts of the game had fleshed out pilot personalities and a 'nemesis' system with rivalries. Absolutely nothing like that made it into the final product.The interface is stylized to the point of being useless, it took me a bit to figure out how to swap out parts on my mechs because the icon isn't easily recognizeable and it was a click and hold button that didn't immediately switch to the loadout, worse yet the equip screen defaulted to the color customizer instead of the more useful equip screen.

_childDocuments_.review: I am 16 hours in, and so far, am thoroughly enjoying the game. It takes awhile to learn the ropes since it's quite different from a typical X-Com like turn-based strategy game, but once you do, it's so rewarding. The design is genius and probably the most innovation I have seen on a TBS game in the last 5 years. The UI does take some getting used to it, but it's well designed and allows you full control over your squad once you learn the full extent of it, which admittedly isn't conveyed well in the tutorial missions. There is a solid game here which I hope the developers will build on if they decide to make a sequel. As others have mentioned, it would be nice if the pilots have some uniqueness of them, in terms of traits, skills, and perhaps some voice acting. It would add a lot of the immersion if they were given more character. That said, this is not a AAA title and is not priced as such, so it's understandable that the developers may not have had the time and budget to put in all the features they want. It seems that most of the focus is on combat, which they have delivered beautifully. Setting up your moves can at times feel a bit arduous, especially when you have a lot of units to control, but the payout when you click "Execute" makes it all your meticulous planning worthwhile. The replays are a joy to behold, and as some have mentioned, if they can make a playback function for the complete mission, that would be icing on the cake. Overall, a solid effort and worth the price tag (I paid about US$14). Hope to see more from these developers, perhaps in the form of expansions, or new features.

_childDocuments_.review: This yes comes with some buts. If you like timeline style tactics games like Frozen Synapse or Frozen Cortex or other games in that vein, I think this is an auto buy, you'll get your moneys worth out of it. If you like strategy games in general or need more convincing, read on. It's worth a look on sale, at the very least.They've just released an update so I may update some of these negatives once I see how the changes to combat shake out when I find the time. Things I want to see improve:- There's something that I find a bit unfun about the mobile base element of the game. I understand that it's fairly core to the whole game, but I feel disenchanted moving around the wider world. Unfortunately I can't think of ways I'd suggest to improve it, earlier updates addressed my original issue which was that all the combat was samey which is definitely not the case these days.- Equipping and management of mechs. There's some elements of navigating the mech customization menu that feel a bit cumbersome. I'm not sure if this is a console game at all, if so, I can understand some of the choices to make the game controller agnostic but I don't enjoy the experience too much on PC. Further to this, I find it difficult to compare multiple parts as options in a slot, if there was a way to create a 'sublist' of items to compare so you can measure which options you're thinking of putting onto the mech, that would be super helpful. I like having north of 16 options to pick from for my reactor, that is cool, however it's a pain in the ass to see and make the choice to what I'm going to put onto my mech. This leads to my next point which actually may be a positive for some people.- At time of writing I've played launch, update 2, and will be coming back for a bit of update 3 after my V rising bender is done. So most of my experience relates to update 2 specifically. The volume of choice available to your mechs is staggering. I find that I'm often having change chassis configurations for the specific encounter. That's part of the fun but for some it can feel like a fairly burdensome system. If there's a way to save mech templates or premade configurations I haven't found it in as many hours as I have at the time of review.Anyway if you've gotten this far hope that helped.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't make many reviews, so let's give this a shot.Phantom Brigade is a great top down tactical turn based strategy game.  You basically get to see 5 seconds into the future and plan your moves around what the AI is going to do.  It's a unique take at the genre and for basically a team I've never heard of, it's an amazing product.  The core gameplay loop is enough to keep you wanting to fight battles and there is a decent enough variety in map layouts and enemy composition/difficulty that I didn't feel overwhelmed for most of the game.  It felt relatively balanced and it was definitely fun to try out new weapons and mech configurations. I will give fair criticism here though... and I have some negatives.  Namely, a lack of secondary objectives to spice up combat, a true progression system that makes your pilots feel unique and special, and lack of variety on the overworld map.First, the secondary objectives.  This feels like a nobrainer, but "Destroy x building to stop reinforcements" and "stay still on this objective to capture this thing" are not fun.  Something like "take out a VIP or your team will be hunted by elite enemies" or "The enemy has decided to carpet bomb your location, stay on the move to avoid damage."  I don't know... anything to make it feel like you are in a war and the enemy is really trying to stop you.  As it is right now... they just kinda lay over and let you take back provinces.  There's no tug of war, no push or shove.  I understand why it's designed this way (so you aren't constantly driving back to rescue areas liberated), but you can add spice to the boring gameplay after the core is exhausted.Secondly, there's no pilot customization!  I would have loved to see my ragtag group get progressively stronger with their mechs.  Maybe three trees for you to work down to make combat feel more varied.  An aggressive tree where you get speed and heat management, but pilots are forced to use more close range weapons, or a tank tree where they get more concussion resistance and are able to make better use of heavy mechs.  Anything would've been better than what we got, which was nothing.  Sure the pilots have "personality" but that doesn't really factor into the core gameplay and support it in any way.  It was a missed opportunity here, but I can definitely see improvements on a second installment if this one does well.Lastly, the overworld map was just... bland.  You had the same 5-6 objectives, taking on different battles just didn't feel impactful and I never once lost a contested province.  Not once.  Never even came close.  This is probably the weakest part of the game and I think the most rushed from the devs.  Places have rich lore, there are varied environments to fight over, and the lore directly ties into the resources in the area... except none of it matters.  Just keep capturing provinces, capture a 2 camps, 1 convoy, and a city and the base in the area just collapses... Like there isn't anything interesting happening.  Maybe make the base the final objective and every province is a mini boss fight with a more powerful mech, or maybe have artillery support drop from the sky to wreck havoc on the battlefield?  God there are so many options to play with and I feel the dev team didn't do anything with it.  Make an airport and artillery objective and have them directly support the main base and secondary objectives.  Just... so many options and none was taken.  The core was there, but this was left wanting.  Overall this is a great game and is definitely worth a buy.  I will warn people that the gameplay can drag on and feel "samey" at times, but the core gameplay is just so addicting.  Devs, if you make a second game please fleshout the rest of the game.  Core gameplay does make this game a 100% buy in my eyes, just needs a bit of polish.  Good job devs.  I complain because I care and I hope this review finds you guys :)
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: The best demo I've ever played. There's just not enough 'game'. I put 70 hours into learning the mechanics, lots of work in an excel to understand and optimize my build, weapon, and module choices, and I went about conquering every province. Very very grindy. And if it all resulted in a "The end, and they lived happily ever after." then I would have been disappointed, but at least it would have had an end. After you conquer every province, the game just... continues.Your nation has been invaded... and the invaders are never given a name, or any kind of identity (or even a logo) and no reason is given. Your nation is never identified either and no reason given why either you were attacked or why your armies failed to hold back the tide. There are no outsiders either conspiring against you or offering aid (if you could just liberate this province or this port).The game starts and you just have this magic device that lets you see 5 seconds into the future, and that is the gimmick for this turn-based strategy game. And as a game mechanic, it's fine and fun, but really this feels like a mobile game without the MTX brought to the PC. What this game needs to earn my endorsement:* more than zero story. Give the enemy a name and a rallying cry. Why do they fight? Why were we attacked, and how did they sweep over 95% of the country before being pushed back?* what does victory look like? How could there not be a game-over screen, or any kind of escalation as the number of liberated provinces increases? I see "patrols" and "elite patrols" if I dilly-dally too long in freeing the province, but where is the "Enemy Advance" that pro-actively battles to hold their ground or retake territory? THE ENEMY HAS NO AGENCY, they sit and wait to be defeated.* a change to the flow of time. I had a sprint where I did something like 15 combat actions in a single day, destroying something like 50 enemy mechs. I used the same pilots and the same mechs the entire time, just blowing through 3 provinces in short order. These sort of maneuvers make a mockery of the flow of time and distort the narrative of the game. Looting needs to take time, damage to mechs needs to take more time, body parts and weapons or just the modules need to need to be replaced, to force the player to collect and store spare/replacement parts, or at times use sub-optimal builds. * I feel like a big narrative component is the "scrappy underdog", which is completely lost when my four mechs have all-rare equipment/modules and are winning combat in 2 rounds and they can leap from battle-to-battle-to-battle, nearly infinitely, because they're taking little to no damage each time.* The infinite momentum that comes from rejuvenating pilots via random events and refilling liquid fix by defeating a repair convoy is devastating to the narrative. The player experiences zero scarcity, only a dearth of rare parts from which to build new items. When I can even build new mech frames behind enemy lines, after the early provinces, why would I ever return to a friendly city? After learning the game, I never did.* Bugs. Events that don't fire and can't be completed, tooltips giving wrong information, modules not working as described. Meh.TLDR, to change my mind, give me a story, give me an enemy that fights back, and remove the infinite momentum loop a player gains just by playing the game. Lean into the premise of an underdog fighting "the Empire."

_childDocuments_.review: First couple of hours are fun, then the reality sets in. This game is so micro management intensive that it feels like a second job. You'll have to scroll/comb over each mechs timeline so minutely, because for some reason the devs couldn't be bothered to add a small marker on the timeline for when your mech will be attacked.The whole concept of this game is that you have a magical device that can look 5 seconds into the future, allowing you to plan your movement/actions to avoid damage. However quite often you'll be hit by attacks that aren't listed in the upcoming timeline making it impossible to actually make use of what is the entire concept. This is especially noticeable when fighting enemies using missiles. And you can't save during missions so one of these mistakes can easily result in a GG.The balancing also seems completely off. I can focus fire with several mechs vs 1 target, planning my shots for 90+% hits. Yet I still have to spend several rounds to kill 1 mech, however the enemy mechs have godlike precision quite often straight up murdering you. We are talking light mech in full sprint with shields raised and the enemy mech still manages do 300+ damage with an assault rifle............................This is patch 1.0 I shudder to think what earlier stages of the game was like.

_childDocuments_.review: There's a good mech frame, but it's missing the parts.For the first 10 or so hours everything seems amazing. The core game design is slick. Pulling out a perfectly coordinated strike is enthralling. Finding new weapon makes you go back and put together a new mech (too bad there is no simulator to try out a build). But then the grind of the game kicks in.Essentially, there are no stakes. You cannot lose, unless you really try. The game patiently waits for you, only giving you idea that the titular brigade is outgunned, that there is a war going and you're the only hope. At first the world map seems daunting, until you learn that the enemy is passive. The combat doesn't evolve past what you learn during the prolouge. Furthermore, combat maps begin to repeat pretty fast, thus accelerating how quick you reach the depths of the game.The base upgrades, except for one that allows you to field 4 mechs, are mostly pointless. Your pilots do not gain veterancy, and the game just teases the fact they have personalities. In truth no fatigue and no personal stories come into play (except for some mute world events), thus you grow no attachment to your crew. Mech combat becomes trival once you get that perfect build for the mechs and just mow down patrol after patrol, only sometimes hitting a Missile Launcher wall which ignores the whole Prediction mechanic. Further more, mech parts seem extensive at first but lack of actions except for moving, attacking, shielding, dashing and ejecting pilot shows how shallow combat is. There aren't any interesting choices such as deploying IR flares to lose missile lock. Using smoke to stun enemies (smoke is Base upgrade instead, allowing you to disengage from a fight) or scrambling enemy sensors so they become "allied" for a turn.Again, there is a frame of a good game. But the parts aren't there yet. XCOM, and its numerous spawns handle the "outgunned" motif way better. The world map reminds me very much of Mount and Blade, but not as developed, as its good guys and the bad guys. Truthfully, a map torn up with numerous factions and only player controlled Phantom Brigade able to use the experimental Prediction tech, bouncing between conflicts or by swearing loyalty to one faction, would make for an interesting concept.The nail to the coffin: for a game with simultaneous turns played out in 5 second segments there isn't a way to replay the whole fight. From what I understood from the developer - this is due to physics simulations occuring. It works to simulate what happened 5 seconds prior though, so maybe it will be introduced with future patches? Games with similar gameplay like Frozen Synapse and Battlestar Galactica Deadlock had it nailed down.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: I am generally a big fan of tactical games like XCom 1/2, Wartales, and of other games with both a tactical and strategic layer like Total War, and I wanted to like this game. I think this game looks really good and you get some really visually satisfying results when things go well (although I seemed to have some graphics problems). In terms of gameplay, the whole "we're massively outnumbered but can see the future" thing is interesting but ultimately I think makes encounters too predictable. A huge part of the challenge in similar games is the risk management, ie. thinking of all the moves the baddies might do and balancing how exposed you are to those potential moves vs going on the offensive. And the pain of not anticipating a move they make. This makes Phantom Brigade like playing chess against someone with twice as many pieces as you, but who always tells you what their next move is. A bit strange, maybe it works for some people.The AI is also not very clever. It often seems to choose to target one of my guys halfway across the map behind a load of buildings rather than one right next to them in the open, and I've even had it do this against stationary targets, i.e. I didn't even have to move, the AI just decides to target someone its impossible to hit at any point during it's attack. Bad AI is one thing and not that uncommon in games, but knowing in advance the AI will do something nonsensical next turn makes for a fairly unsatisfying experience in my view, once the novelty of the cool mech animations wears off a bit.As for the strategic layer, again it looks great, I personally would like to see a little more gameplay depth and progression in this layer though. All in all, the game is ok. And at the price, maybe I'm setting my expectations a bit high. Personally though I won't be picking this up again.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: The conceit of this game is that in some far future (implied to be a colony planet deep in space), an evil red country has invaded your peaceful blue country. Both sides fight with piloted mechs (along with tanks and crawlers), but you're part of a special squadron that has super tech that allows you to predict an enemy's move 5 seconds into the future. The evil red country conquers all of yours, but you and some of your soldiers and mechs manage to escape, and some time later launch a guerilla campaign to liberate your land.The process of doing so involves fighting turn-based battles with your mechs, but the way turns work in this game is REALLY interesting. It's not quite like Front Mission or XCOM. Rather, you and your enemies take each turn, which is exactly 5 seconds, simultaneously. However, you can see what your enemies plan to do and where they plan to attack, so you set up movement, your own attacks, etc. on a bar at the bottom of the screen, almost like video editing. You have to match up where you move with your enemies' movement so you're in the right place at the right time for your attacks to land. You also have to worry about weapon overheating, how each of your parts has its own HP and can be crippled (a la Front Mission), and so on. It is amazingly cool, a brief description can't do it justice, but no other strategy game makes me feel like I'm actually piloting a mech, you'd have to get into actual action games like ZoE or Mechwarrior for that feeling.The customization part is pretty cool too. Out of battles, you can assign pilots to different mechs and customize each mech too, just like Front Mission--body, legs, left arm, and right arm, along with 2 weapons (no shoulder weapons unfortunately :< ), as well as some other stuff like thrusters, reactors, etc. There is a HUGE variety of weapons: Front Mission's rifles, shotguns, missiles, and melee maces, but also two-handed vulcan gatlers, railguns, beam weapons, slug cannons, and so on.The grand strategy is also enjoyable. Sort of like XCOM 2, you operate a mobile base that can travel around the map, from which you need to both take important enemy positions and avoid patrols (if a patrol catches you, you need to win the battle or else its game over). Much like XCOM 2, you can spend resources gained from winning battles on improving your base, increasing its speed, the number of mechs you can deploy, etc. And since this is a guerilla war, your objective is to liberate your whole country, which you do province by province by 'contesting' provinces, which gives you a set of tough battles you need to get to and win within a time limit in order to assist other guerilla forces who are also fighting alongside you (the Home Guard) so that the province is totally cleaned of evil red country forces. You also have to be careful about losing allied units in battle, as they reduces your reputation with the Home Guard (making battles tougher if you can't rely on them) and protecting civilian buildings in some maps, as destroying those reduces Hope, which gives you less time to do the liberation missions. It works pretty well.I have two big caveats, though. First, though you can customize your pilots' looks, the only stat any of them have is HP (as sometimes the pilot takes "concussive" damage from enemy attacks and can be knocked unconscious rather than killed, you can also do this to enemies, which gives you more salvage). They don't have any ranged, melee, etc. stats, and no skills like in Front Mission. Secondly, there is no plot whatsoever. Though there is some voiced dialogue, you're given no explanation for why the red country invaded, no heads of state for either side, and hell your own country doesn't even have a name. In fact, as I mentioned above, the only hint I had the game takes place off-Earth was a mention in one random event that a meteor shower was caused by the planet's ring, aside from that I couldn't tell you if it took place in an alternate isekai world! Most games of this type like Front Mission sell themselves on the quality of the narrative, and even the Battletech strategy game and XCOM 1 and 2 sort of had narratives where you learn more about the alien forces as you progressed. There's absolutely none of that in this game, which is a big shame and a sizable ding against it.Still, the battle system is SO good that I absolutely must recommend it. I hope this game does well enough they make a Phantom Brigade 2 with more plot!
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: While the time based turn system is very innovative and fun to use, I wish it's implemented on a better game.I don't like the Diablo-esque loot system. Lots of symbols and crap shown in the UI that remain unexplained even after the tutorial. The first boss is just so stupidly difficult because no matter what, it'll keep on targeting two of your team of four mechs. Since you can't use the buildings as shield for very long so they'll always have to dodge and run in the entire battle making it a slow and boring process. I've taken it down with one mech lost but it's really stupidly designed.From now on, if the reviews are Mixed, it's nixed.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: THIS IS A YES-BUT RECOMMENDATION: Let me start out by saying that this game initially packs the mother of all punches. It's visually fantastic, incredible even, the controls and mechanics are amazing and - as far as I know - first of it's kind. Phantom Brigades brings so much potential to the table. The combat gameplay is incredibly stylistic, the movie-editor-like system makes you feel like an absolute tactical genius while not being overpowering. The game forces you to make decisions, some good, some bad in order to preserve/protect your force while smashing through enemy mechs. The graphics, designs and effects are simple but wonderfully executed, long range combat makes for spectacular light shows while melee combat sounds and feels weighty, especially with a proper heavy mech. Customization gets an instant 10/10 with how stylish and distinct parts look and the functions as well as pros/cons they provide. All of the pros listed above brings all the more pain to me as I say that the game, for as wonderful as it is, feels like an unfinished project. The story takes no time to play through, once you've liberated a couple of region a-la Far Cry you've practically seen it all. Except for the few set piece scenarios towards the very end, combat (as fun as it is) feels repetitive. Once you've assembled your best all-star team it becomes slightly monotonous with no additional challenge. The "boss" fight features enemies with beefed up mechs and harder hitting weapons but ultimately serves no real challenges. Yes you can totally play past the ending as there are many MANY regions to liberate but why would you? At the end game you no longer feel like a "Phantom Brigade", you are no longer a guerrilla fighting force, you're a force of nature. In my playthrough I actively seek out the biggest baddest randomly generated fights and still blew right through them. With mechanics this innovative and fun, with graphics this good, with THIS much potential, I wanted to see so much more from this game that I've grown to love and then grown tired of.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: The game looks cool and the core combat mechanics are fun but if you were expecting a story line or pilots with any character or individuality you'll be sorely disappointed. The pilots in this game are interchangeable and little more than batteries for your mechs that need to be swapped out and recharged occasionally. The campaign map is large but the missions repeat all too quickly and becomes stale fast.I'll give it a thumbs up because it was fun for the first few hours and they're adding more content but if you wanted a mech game with a story then look elsewhere.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: Great tactical mech combat, loads of juicy destruction and a replay system that means you never have to miss a second of it. Plenty of customisation to get into once you start dragging the salvage home. Only thing missing is making the pilots matter more. Right now the pilots are just a health bar and it's a missed opportunity to add another layer to your squad makeup. The story is light and the bad guys are bad for the sake of being bad, but does the trick and I predict a lot of hours will go into the campaign. It took me 2 hours to get past tutorial land but the hand holding was done after mission 1 which I really appreciated.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: If you want a solid turn based tactical Mech battler look no further, but be advised that's all you're getting.  No plot, no music, no real frills other than very pretty graphics.  That said the combat is very fun, but once you find the four loadouts you like you won't deviate much from them.  For me it's sniper, missile, Vulcan and shield tank (usually I run some type of medium range weapon).  Short range loadouts are not really advised b/c melee doesn't always seem to work and the amount of damage you take before and after getting in range isn't worth it.  The base upgrading is not very involved and most of it isn't needed, though it does help a bit.  The only real downside for the combat is how dumb the enemy AI is and the lack of challenge once you get your lineup sorted.Pros:Solid turn based combatLots of customization optionsLooks prettyNo real plot to speak of, just fightingCons:No real plot to speak ofAlthough there are lots of customization options there are really only a few viable options.Absolute lack of mission variety
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: Semi-randomized grind that does level-scaling in such a way that it's impossible to either avoid grinding or gain any long-term advantage by doing extra grinding. There's very little variety, very few random events, no particular story outside of the opening and (presumably) the ending . . . just not enough to keep me coming back. I put far too much time into this as it is before doing some testing and realizing the futility of almost all of my play time.ETA: After another 13 hours of modding game and save files just to see what the ending was like, I find that I had more fun digging through YAML files trying to learn the game's code than actually playing it. Still don't recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: I wish there was a public roadmap / dlc roadmap for the game. The core gameplay loop is awesome it prompts creative battle choreography and produces highly cinematic fights. But the systems on top of it feel like placeholders: - pilots are just images and backstories you don’t care about (and I sent to get extremely attached to xcom soliders, rimworld colonists or dumb faces of battle brothers). I’d literally buy a dlc that makes pilots have a personality and act on emotions occasionally, resulting in an unchangeble turn for them. Or a bit of pilots abilities and some enemy mechs having meaningful pilots that could use those abilities or have a trait like “unpredictable” or “berserk” actually meaning they might get kinetic or overheat their mech to the brim.- Random events seemingly affect nothing. The shed with parts was the only memorable one, except the parts were trash in fact :/- Parts are feel like an ngu after 10 hours.- Every encounter has almost identical set of enemies and map pool is small. So you end up doing almost identical actions without changing your load out for the event at all. Oh and enemies usually have 2-3 mechs on the field making you a majority 90% of the time.So all in all I really hope devs find a way to make the game engaging long therm, and for now I’ll put it on a shelf and wait for it.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: I love how fresh its take on mech combat is, but also have some significant reservations.A few mechanics combine to make a few hours of play-time enough before putting this down.Tactically, you'll face a downward spiral in which you have to pick fights, but that raises combat difficulty, which leads to losing a mech, which puts you in a whole you can't climb out of. So you'll save scum.Strategically, the 'campaign' is liberating many provinces, which is very fun the first 3 times, and then between save-scumming and having to repeat that process many more times, makes you realize you've seen enough.Beyond that, there's definitely fun.The 'projection' combat system is very fresh and fun, and makes combat predictable enough that you can make informed decisions, while remaining unpredictable enough that you never know the outcome, and can be surprised.Building and equipping mechs, looting equipment, and deciding what and how to keep things, and balance resources between mechs and upgrades, is a lot of fun.   The strategic portion of moving across and around provinces, deciding which fights to take, how to defeat the enemy and so on, is also really fun. You very much feel like your decisions are impactful.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: I want to say first of all that I actually enjoy this game, so the negative review may seem odd. But here's the thing; we all know you're not trawling through the positive reviews full of "Loving it so far!" and "Awesome game - hope they do more!" just to feel good. You're looking for the negative reviews to see if any of the faults of the game are deal breakers. It's like a relationship - sometimes one big thing, or a collection of smaller things just let you know that it just won't work out. Maybe she smokes. Maybe he runs his fingers down your face like John Travolta's character does in the hit 1997 action movie "Face Off". Maybe they *are* John Travolta. There's always going to be something that you just don't want to deal with, and that's okay. Negatives are far more likely to give you that than not.So here's the salient parts.The good:- A initially very enjoyable gameplay loop - you join battles, zip around in a HIGHLY cinematic battle for a number of turns in 12 foot tall eastern style mecha and save the nation! Battles look awesome, slow motion gives the zipping of bullets and echoing of gun retorts an awesome feel, and it's very satisfying. The simultaneous planning of actions in 5 second slots then enacted out at once, but with a prescient knowledge of the enemies moves take a bit of getting used to, has some kinks, but is otherwise fresh and fun.- The mechs generally look pretty cool, with sleek aesthetics.- The sound of the battles, the crunching of buildings getting chewed up, and things exploding is pretty damn enjoyable.- There's a ton of variety in choosing load outs for mechs, from limbs, accessories, armour, and weapons.Aaaaaand now we're onto the longer section.The bad:- That gameplay loop? Yeah, that's it, again and again and again and again. Every battle feels pretty much the same after the initial excitement wears off, which is a shame, because it *is* initially very fun. At the 18 hour mark I'm not really dying to jump into another battle anymore.- Zero story other than "Someone took over your country, you hid, now you're saving it from them". Who are they? Dunno. Who are you? Why the Phantom Brigade silly, of course. Yeah, but who are you? What do you stand for? Winning the country back! Duh! Riiigggght. Electrolytes are what plants crave and all. - Battles are kinda bizarrely brief with some odd design choices. Each turn is five seconds, which you can rewatch after it completes it run. Except the last turn. Y'know, the really cool one where you snatch victory from the jaws of defeat with an almost Napoleonic level of master tactics and plugged the last enemy in the back of the head with a burst of riffle fire (think Mechcommander)? Yeah, no, you can't watch that turn. Or a replay of the whole battle. WHICH, by  the way, is probably six turns long. 30 seconds and you're done.For reference here, in table top battletech, and HBS's game, a "turn" represents 10 seconds, which means a lot of Battletech battles are, to quote Tex of the BlackPantsLegion conducted in a "Blaze of glory", lasting 2 - 7 minutes tops. Still a bit longer than 30 seconds, which also makes you realize how insanely fast everything is zipping around...- The aesthetics, while good, are incredibly.... generic. Everything looks the same. Every map, every town, every mech. Swapping out different body parts just looked like thinner or thicker versions of the same arm. Weapons all look kinda the same.Compare this with the remade XCOM (another frequent comparison for it's resistance focused, resource grabbing, turn based qualities) - in that, and especially XCOM 2, you can make your agents look utterly uninque, from tacticool combat gear in bright pink, to post-apocalypse raider punk (complete with mohawk) to wearing the skins of your fallen opponents. PB completely misses that. - The pacing. There doesn't seem to be any. In XCOM if you ♥♥♥♥ about, you will, sooner rather than later, find out. There is always a sense of pressure to weigh choices; do you save the civilians in the terror mission knowing it will keep Inidia on the Council, but there's a high chance of sustaining injuries to agents you *need* for the next big mission, or not?  XCOM doesn't let you relax strategically until quite late in the game. PB has none of that.When you take a province you kind just sit on it. Take your time a bit. The enemy in all other provinces seem to level up to just above you regardless, so take your time! There's no rush to, y'know, overthrowing the benevolent dictators who took over! There's often timed events that essentially pin your team for several hours. The most obvious is "refuelling" which takes 7 hours in which you put the strategic map on full speed and wait for the time to run out. You're not worrying that spending those 7 hours getting precious resources (they're not precious) is a gamble (it isn't) that could stop you getting the edge on your opponenet (it wont). You just wait those seven hours. - The writing, when it's there, isn't.... great. I started skipping a lot of it. It's very... erm, well? Saccharine comes to mind. Saving kids and families and telling people that they're strong enough when they're at breaking point. For a game that's missing a lot of features, it almost feels like this one should have been left off. There's a lot of little events and they all kind of run along this very trite "do the right thing for your people" vibe which feels very forced, given we know sweet FA about these people to begin with. Which leads me onto....- So much isn't explained. In the above case you have a scenario where you find a box, which gives you the choice to pick it up. If you do, it's a bomb.  Then you have a choice of giving some resources (70 out of the 1000 + I had at this point), waiting 5 hours or so, or doing nothing. I always paid the scenario off. Then I could choose to keep the bomb! Obviously I did this. What does this do? ♥♥♥♥♥♥ if I know. Never found out with five bombs in my possession.And that's a lot of the game, it feels like a good manual or more expansion tooltip system should be in place, because there's so much that seems like you have to bumble around until you work it out. Reinforcements (which are a pain in the behind - more on that in a second) can be completely negated by the use of a comms jammer! I found that out on the forums after getting frustrated and rage quitting. Turns out you can research an upgrade for your mobile base and then build comms jammer deployables and then use them before a mission. If this was explained in the game I must have missed it several times. And there's a lot more like that.- Speaking of frustation, the game has lots of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ with the combat - reinforcements, if they do show up, are mere turns apart & getting four more units on turn 5, then three more on turn seven on the other side of the map. It's a bit more. Missiles were an absolutel joke of an unbalanced mess until the devs (bless them) hotfixed them within a week to not spawn constantly with every unit and track you with near perfect precision. - The UI. It's... bad. To having to double click or hold-click menus to select hem is just a bizarre for a start. Comparing the many items you use is borderline impossible, and makes swapping out items a chore.So look, the game is fun, but it's lacking sooo much. It's a great core game that has so many features haphazardly bolted on, poorly implemented, or missing altogether than it really detracts from long term playability and enjoyment. The devs seem responsive, so I really hope they bring the features and polish the game needs to really shine. But it would need a lot. If you've somehow made it this far, you deserve a cookie, a glass of warm milk, and a nap. Go, treat yourself. You've earned it.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: There are quite a few things to improve on this title, however I think the game is enjoyable enough to justify purchase.  I would also like to see a lot more levels, bring the unit cap from four to ten, or dare I say twenty (go big or go home, as they say).  The mecha customisation needs more... customisation.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: - UPDATE -Appears this game isn't going to be getting the post-launch support that was needed, and suggested. A shame really, but if the game isn't going to be improved then there's no way I can recommend this considering the pre-existing issues.- ORIGINAL REVIEW -Once you manage to get into the mindset of how the game wants you to approach combat, this can become an incredibly fun strategy game similar to the more prevalent titles available. The customisation between mechs is superb (though more colour palettes wouldn't go amiss!) and some of the weapons are massively satisfying to have land.I've only liberated one sector of the map, and it seems like the kind of game you need to be in the long-haul for as there is A LOT of work to be done on the players part. Some further variance in environments would bring some much needed freshness as the game progresses, as whilst it's nice to approach the limited spaces from different angles of attack (different starting positions, turrets placed randomly at bases) some true variance in scenery would help make the game feel more developed.Some spaces like ravines/large bodies of water could add not only some visual and tactical differences, but gameplay too since traversal with the mechs can be so varied - perhaps we could see the addition of some airbourne mechs too?
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: Have had fun with this game, trying out different mech builds and watching the fights play out, but have recently run into lag, stuttering and crash issues. Have played with both high and low graphics settings but it still occurs. Unfortunately, won't recommend for others until it is optimised more.Also feels as though they had greater plans with this game and then cut back during development leaving odd things that seem half-finished.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: So much fun, feels quicker and more lethal than most of pre-gauss battletech. World map could do with more love as at the moment it just exists to keep the fighting going but I don't really ever feel specialized or unique in this playthrough in any way. Mods will make this game spectacular in the long run, even today it is good fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: The game is either way too slow in offering you actual tactical options or just doesn't have them.  4 hours in and I can only now just start building a new mech, I still can't jump, and I've got 4 weapon types, with a shield.  There's seemingly no actions besides run, wait, shoot, raise shield, and dash.  No grenades, no AOE shields for temporary cover.  The last mission I lost because I couldn't jump beneath the bridge to avoid gunfire.  I shouldn't need special leg parts to fall down 10 feet.The entire combat system is restrictive rather than creative.   You can't dash and shoot at the same time.  You can't use your shield and shoot at the same time.  You can't dash and shield at the same time.  Not only is this just not fun but it doesn't even make sense because if you were in a mech you'd want to do these things together.  XCOM 2 has buffs that allow you to throw a grenade and shoot in a single turn.  Phantom Brigade cuts off your knees.This is done likely to preserve a balanced difficulty but why not just overtune the enemies to compensate?  I already know exactly what they're going to do.  You can largely do the same predictions in XCOM 2 which overloads it's enemies with insanely overpowered moves that you outsmart using priority targeting and skills which manipulate the battlefield.  Here the enemy has nothing surprising and you can't even outsmart gunfire.It's hard to imagine how they could strip down tactics as much as they have and still use the word.  4 Hours into XCOM 2 and you'd have 8x as many tactical options on offer.  The real time aspect seems primarily used to make combat cumbersome rather than tactical.  In exchange for movie editor gameplay we lost the plot, the strategy, and QOL features.  As far as I know you can't even save mech designs.I'm going to play and probably enjoy XCOM Chimera Squad more than this.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: A game where you can view 5 seconds ahead of time and see what your enemy suits will do, from there you'll plan out the actions of your own suits in response to that prediction. You lead a rebel group of mobile suits, liberating your country province by province. There's quite a large number of provinces to go through. At launch the variety of mission types was limited, but since then additional modes and improvements have been added.The animations & details present when you scrub thru the timeline to see each individual missile shot, explosion and impact adds a lot to the replayability of the game, if you're into that thing. Zooming in and witnessing the stimulated carnage up close makes for a lot of fun.Would recommend if you like a more involved turn based game and/or mecha in general.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: this is one of those games that it either clicks with you or it doesnt. i feel as though this is a really unique game, that can be as rewarding as it punishing. the learning curve this game has isnt the most steep, nor is it the most shallow. as i said, it will either be a great game for you or the worst. give it a shot!
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: What a great surprise, Phantom Brigade is a fantastic strategy game with an interesting gimmick and very rewarding gameplay.Queuing up a barrage on the last remaining enemy mech and watching it get torn to shreds... *chefs kiss*edit: after a couple dozen more hours of play I feel like the later parts of the game advancement and growth and it turns into a bit of a grind loop of bigger damage numbers verse bigger armour numbers making it feel like you're kind of just playing the same loop over and over. Would be nice if some more overworld elements were introduced later on as you help the allies gain more forces to speed up the end game.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: By far the best mech game in recent years. I think Daemon X Machina also is a contender for this, but it's a fascinating game. It's rather fun to watch the battles take place and executing all your maneuvers. I do wish there was an option to play back the entire battle after you complete the mission in real time though.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: This is genuinely a bit of a hidden gem. Great little tactics game with really solid core gameplay, having a lot of fun with it. I can see that it has potential to get a little grindy later on - the world is very big and there's a lot of territories to take back - so more variety later on will be important, but early to mid game is absolutely great so far~
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: Combat UI and the timeline mechanic falls short in too many ways. The rest of the game may be great but it's frustrating that gameplay elements so central to the game aren't more polished, especially since its been done before.The UI should work with the player, not against them. If they can fix that, this may be worth checking out down the line.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: In this instance, less would be a lot more. There's just way too much stuff packed into the game. If you want to dump a bunch of time into a game doing repetitive stuff, then the game would be fine for you. If you want to enjoy a cool combat system without a bunch of extra make-work, this isn't it.Has promise though. If they made a game that just focused on the tactics then that could be fun, or if they focused on the overworld part with faster simplified combat.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: it's pretty cool.  not a ton going on but it's less than half a normal game price, so that's fine. prediction-based turns like frozen synapse, but unlike frozen synapse you don't have to predict your enemies, they always do exactly what the preview says they'll do. this makes it less like frozen synapse and more like being the aliens from that tom cruise movie, where you know what they'll do ahead of time and any problems you have are 100% you being dumb.  the only exception is missiles, their flight paths aren't previewed except at launch so sometimes you can get in trouble.  the prediction system can take some getting used to. melee especially is a little hard to predict at first but you get the hang of it eventually and it's really strong. likewise you'll kill your teammates a few times, or put yourself in impossible predictions, but you get the hang of it.  there's a decent bit of mech customization but don't expect battletech.  once you've gotten over the initial hump it starts to get pretty easy, aside from missiles enemies are easy to avoid and exploit since you know what they're gonna do ahead of time. eventually you start methodically taking them apart without letting them get more than a couple hits in.it's fine.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: The combat system is in a class of its own. If you're a turn-based strategy game fan, this is definitely a good game to get just to see that simultaneous movement of all your units in slow-mo, gun blazing. The detail on the particle effect and destruction of buildings were awesome! Zooming in to watch the bullets fly as they collide with the mechs and the environment were well worth what I paid for!But the story can definitely need some serious upgrade. The characters are VERY generic, and with the 'pronouns' and uni-sex look mixed in, they're as boring as a blank piece of paper. Players often want to, at some level, immerse themselves into the roles of the characters in the game. Making them all the same helped nobody with the immersion; and as a result, it's hard for people to care about the story that's being told.The unit count on each battlefield is pretty low by strategy game average, but the planning and slow-mo execution of your plan does make up for it in terms of content.The world map is pretty big, with plenty of provinces to take over. Game flow is pretty straight forward: take over one province at a time, with several battlefields sprinkled throughout in each province, until you get to the capital. With some random encounters here and there.At a discount, definitely a good grab just for the combat system, but don't expect any emotional or in-depth story-telling.I've been a Front Mission fanatic since the first one on SNES (Evolution is trash), this combat system is without a doubt, a great fit for that franchise. For the devs, maybe consider collaborating or getting a deal with SquareEnix to combine your combat system with their story-telling, that will make a hell of a game.9/10 - Combat System2-3/10 - Story / Characters

_childDocuments_.review: So let me start by saying, all these idiots saying this is like xcom, are idiots. This is nothing like xcom, it is literally jagged alliance: back in action with mechs. Xcom is grid based, it has cover points and overwatch. This game has none of the above. If you want to take cover get behind a building. No overwatch.My main gripe with this game is, you get through the tutorial and your given your first region to invade, except i now have 2 convoys that move towards me then run away, which alerts the patrol to my position. I beat the patrol, immediately another patrol spawns. I have probably had 25 fights, just against patrols, and haven't even traversed half the FIRST sector.Second gripe is the upgrade window. You cant zoom out, i didn't even realise for awhile that there were trees basically straight up from the base tree, because you can't even see the lines connecting them. The tree to unlock the fourth slot for mechs is straight down, not down and and across like it had some sort of progression, it is literally just straight down. Without zooming it makes upgrading painful.Next gripe, I'm getting over this game real quick. Its the same biome......every fight. Its against the same enemies....every fight. Supposedly there are these beam weapons, but i haven't ever fought a team with beam weapons meaning i can't loot beam weapons.I recommend this title because it has potential. _childDocuments_.review: Barely a recommend and only for people looking for exactly this kind of game. If you aren't super keen for a short term planning game about mechs, you're not going to like this at all.Good:Mechs! Customise your mechs with limited partsExecute perfect missions, enemy doesn't know what hit themMixed:Out of combat encounters are text driven. They are very simple, and it's never really clear what you're picking. They could telegraph the outcomes a lot better. Also there's room for a lot more of these, as this would be the only interesting thing throughout a long campaign.Gear levels. Taken on its own, this could be really bad. But it has the function of you being strongly encouraged to try out different gear.Bad:Writing. The tutorial mission has voice over, then when it's done hard handbrake turns into a different story with different characters. It feels like vestigial parts from an earlier version of the game that the designers couldn't bear to part with.Spread too thin. The campaign has a burst of interesting stuff at the start, then get settled in because there's 40 regions of cut and paste. There needs to be at least one of these text encounters per region, plus one almost every time you rest. Also just far fewer regions for a normal play through.Mech builder UI. Figuring out what parts combine how is obtuse. After 20 hours I couldn't tell you the differences between different similar gear. The descriptions and tooltips with stats just don't provide good information.

_childDocuments_.review: Man, this game is so bitter-sweet. Many people have already stated the big pros and cons, and for the most part they are right. Great gameplay loop and overall combat mechanics and awesome presentation from the music and the visuals, followed by gripes with the UI and general Qol issues like missile prediction being absent and no replay for the full mission, etc.Some things that aren't being discussed however, are the things like the lackluster home guard allies and the absolutely zero difference between pilots. Firstly, from the advertisement and promo material, I thought the home guard were going to be a bigger factor in this game. Going from the dev logs, they made it sound like the home guard were going to take a more active role, where they would be constantly fighting the larger scale confrontation whilst you would be free to help them by taking part in missions that would cripple the enemy from behind the frontlines, or maybe you'd take a more upfront role and join them when they were on the offensive. That sounded awesome, because not only would it be incredibly fitting for the setting they are trying to portray, it would be a breath of fresh air! Where in games in this genre, it is so often the case that you, the single commander, are the one and only reason your entire military remembers to tie their own shoelaces before entering combat, having to control every engagement and battle. Instead, it seemed, like you were going to be a small part of the overall conflict, where your decisions would have incredible weight just because of how elite and unique your small phantom brigade was.Sadly, that is just not the case here. Just like XCOM or Xenonauts, you are basically the only capable commander in the entire defense force. You get to decide when to contest a region, and when you do, battle missions will spawn where the home guard will simply never win. So, common to many strategy games, you and your squad are the only factor responsible for victory. The entire liberation lies squarely on your shoulders, so much for not being alone in the fight.Secondly, besides being cosmetically customizable and some really well written text adventure type random popups, your pilots are essentially clones. There is no real mechanics when it comes to your pilots other than if they are a little banged up or 100% healthy. This is a shame, because part of the reason XCOM was so successful was because you got to build a cool roster that you could get attached to and that each of your squad could be a unique specialist that gave them purpose and character. Arguably, you could say that the mechs are more of the main characters than the pilots, sure, but I just think that the potential is there to help flesh out your band of freedom fighters while also giving them fun gameplay mechanics like individual skills and quirks. Overall, however, I think the game is worth it on sale. It's a unique title with obvious heart put into it. It just is so painfully close to being something so extraordinary that with more time, I honestly think it could be a cornerstone evolution for the genre. There are many great suggestions put forward by the community and some general bugs that need fixing, but the game stands firmly where it is right now. I just only hope they continue to work on this project because if they do, it would easily be one of the top dogs in the turn based strategy genre, hands down.

_childDocuments_.review: Fairly priced, and well made. Its been in development for a long time, including going through Epic Games Exclusivity (wooooow so evil). I played it on Epic when it was new, and at that time it was quite rudimentary. I can definitely recommend it now. There's boss battles, a decent tutorial, and scaled progression based on your own unit's equipment. I would call this game round-based. Combat takes place in 5-second increments, with the player having a prototype prediction device, allowing you to see what the enemies are going to do in the next 5 seconds and plan your own moves in response. There is modular damage and a concussion system, rewarding you for flanking or using weapons that focus on concussion (non-lethal?) instead of other damage types. As simple as the damage model may seem, there is reason to do more than just deal the highest DPS possible while standing still. For example, a marksman rifle or sniper rifle can do decent damage. But, if you can get behind an enemy and make a well-placed shot in the back, they may very well go down in a single attack, keeping the mech/vehicle intact for cheaper/better salvage opportunities.There is a story, but personally I don't play for that. It is passable, but the combat and unit building are by far the best elements of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: The mech combat can be fast,and tastefully brutal.But. That's all there is. The Tutorial is the story. Beyond that? There isn't much else. It isn't like Barotrauma(another very good Rogue like game) because Barotrauma has MANY more feathres to round out it's weaker aspects.Phantom Brigade is odd. On one hand,the in game visuals are surpisingly good. But when you see the people models,and notice how every.single.one. of them is an androgynus Hapsburg clone it really takes you out of it. The quality difference is astounding. The mechs look fairly good. The characters that pilot the mechs could all fall out of the ugly tree,hit every branch on the way down,and still come out looking like they got improved.There's so few mission types,one is literally the same,just cruise missiles instead of drones,and it's just as annoying.The boss battles are the most fun,but they're the same. It's a variation of the largest walker.Parts are..well. They're there. But it's a lot of number go up issues. And it needs to die in a fire because that's padding. And devs who pad an already padded game should be shamed.Did I mention the padding? There's enough padding here that you could make a house out of it. The overworld? Fully padded. It's so large and the crawler so ungodly slow that you'll spend ages trundling along looking for the next mission,and then having to do one of the same 2-3 mission types. Demolition is the worst. You'd think blow up buildings could be fun,cause it's mechs' right? Get a bad map roll and it's awful.The padding wouldnt' be so bad if it were to round out the world,but there's no real story here. I don't know who I'm fighting,or why. They're just the Red Team. There's lots of little bugs here and there that often require the use of the dev console to fix.Like Battletech 2018,it's one Lance vs a legion of enemies.  It wears out it's welcome here,like it did in BT,but at least with BT with mods you get way more customization.Basically,what I'm saying is,buy Battletech 2018,learn how to mod it,and install BTA or one of the other huge compendiums.I *want* to enjoy the game. The loop is great. It's got good bones. But there's zero meat on them. But the padding that's there,just tastes like foam. It sure ain't ready for prime time and needs another 2-4 years in the cooker. A proper story and ditch the terrible numbers go up system.

_childDocuments_.review: Solid 7/10, recommend at 25% off, or full price if a strategy fan. Reasons belowAt its core its very good game. The timeline mechanic is absolutely unique enough to carry it for its worth. The depth of gear, parts and modifications allows for highly specialised mechs in the late game and lovely ramshackle monstrosities in the early game when chasing stats. the game however suffers in a number of ways with the first being that its overworld, whilst interesting enough in enemy territory it feels very empty when within friendly territory. this is compounded when you realise Homeguard is beyond useless when contesting territories, and defense of owned territories does not seem to be a thing.The next major problem is that melee is not clear in the slightest. 9/10 missing a target entirely or crashing into them before the swing executes. There is a finesse that is made worse by it being unclear if you have hit or not.The last major downside is that pilot progression is non-existant at least i could not find anything to attach me to them. Why are these pilots fighting? it feels empty when Pilot A dies, oh just recruit another for 200. None of the events that do happen really effect pilots in truly impactful ways which compounds the first problem.if in the future the three points are fixed the game would be 10/10.  As of 1.0.3 it feels like its missing something that shifts is from good to excellent

_childDocuments_.review: This game has interesting mechanics, namely a battle prediction system where you can see moves 5 seconds ahead of time, then plan accordingly and play. It also has cool stompy mechs which I love.The prediction system makes enemies very easy to manipulate. The AI is really dumb to begin with, they waste their shots by trying to shoot through hills and buildings, and also take shots that are out of range. AI movement is pretty bad too. Often times reinforcements collide and crash into each other, and it's kinda sad. You combine bad AI with the ability to see their predetermined actions, the outcome is an unchallenging experience. When I play this game I feel like I'm bullying a kid. The AI also lacks tactics, they'll just banzai charge you and you can just stand there and pick them off from afar. Basically, if they do not outgun or outnumber you, they cannot challenge you. Even if they do outnumber you, they play so suboptimally that you can lead them into a kill box, or let them chase one of your mechs and they'll turn their backs to 3 shootersOverall, the tuning of this game feels "off". It feels kind of like a demo more than a full fledged game. Levels have little variety between them, and the crunchy bits like equipment, mechs, enemy stats, etc.. seems very unbalanced. Even the boss fights get stale after a while. What playing this feels like is I'm playing with a DM who is very good at making cool mechanics, world building for his TRPG but is bad at making the levels and items and challenges. There's a lot of potential for sure, but the game needs more fine tuning and variety. This is especially apparent when higher challenge maps just throw one wave of units at you at a time. There's no challenge in there, it's just wasting time by padding out the level. It's like if the DM ran out of ideas and just goes, "oh you killed everything already? Let me throw yet another wave of goblins that can't harm you to make this encounter 10 minutes longer"I hope the dev's next project is tighter, and better put together. There's a lot of good potential here.7/10

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very fun turn based strategy with a unique and well executed core mechanic. Planning out the moves of each mech beforehand is quite fun and intuitive after the first several missions, and the movie-maker like time slider makes for some really cool simultaneous movements among your troops. However, the game does not have enough depth to make it to the end game, and struggles to provide new challenges other than tougher or more enemies the farther in you go. Great concept muddled by a tiresome grind to the finish. 7/10, would recommend with caveats.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really not sure which way to go on this one. Lots to recommend the game, but there are some distinct problems that detract from the experience, from the game's primary conceit, and from the fun in general.I'm going to go with "Thumb's up but complains about the game all review."So the idea is probably pretty clear to you if you're considering buying the game. It's big stompy mechs, chock full of customization options, and asymmetric warfare. You get fewer dudes than there are enemy dudes, but you, and this is very important, can *see the future.*Except for missiles. Missiles are outside the timestream, nobody knows how they work, and that's why they're an invaluable part of the armaments of both sides.Missiles sometimes take a while to reach their target. They also sometimes just miss their targets because of oblique angles. Different launchers have different speeds and accuracy, different firing arcs which determine what cover they can get around (yours and your enemy's), a wide variety of ranges.But you can't see what they'll do. Can't see the progression of the missile into next turn. Can't even see if you've already targeted one of the largely fungible little red targeting markers last turn, which is important for salvaging purposes. Your missiles will miss constantly, while attempts to slip enemy missile fire with anime-style rapid dashes through city streets and multiple 90 degree angle turns will shake approximately zero to one missiles out of twenty.You can easily see if an enemy firing at you will be able to hit you with your future sight. If the line they draw to you is dotted, some or all of their shots will be intercepted by your cover. Sometimes you will forget than an enemy shot an especially high arc of missiles at you one or two turns ago, and your guy behind cover will be very upset at their timely delivery onto his or her noggin.Fascinatingly (to me, anyway) I discovered that the max range of my missile launchers... wasn't. It's not the max range. The actual max range was about 15% less than it said on the tin. I replayed the same turn over and over with the replay button, watching a vast host of missile shaped death approach my enemy sniper, and they all exploded midair at the same time. It was in range according to the range finder, but not according to the missile fuel budget. This, too, would have been a nice inclusion in my future sight.Also, as a small aside, never trust the dotted line when the enemy firing at you is a sniper. If the shot can possibly get over the lip of that ridge and hit your dome, it will.So the future sight is wonky, a category of weapons that is wildly useful to everyone seems to be made out of Time Free materials, and this is, frequently, more frustrating than fun.But I really, really like customizing robots, so here we are.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: X-COM + Front Mission + Battletech = This game. I have been looking for a game like this for a long time, this is an awesome mix of Turn-based/ Real time strategy. Great customization, sending out orders with a timeline system is the most ingenious way of doing a game like this, Being able to send out an order to not only attack an enemy, but to defend from fire, move closer, use my shotgun and keep moving so you collide with a different enemy target all because I custom built my turn, and that is just for one mech. If you have any interest in mech TBS gameplay with a twist, I implore you to get this game. For $30 it is well worth the asking price, a way better game than most. if not all AAA games coming out today that are asking more than double what this is asking for.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: I don't want to call this a bad game because all elements that need to function do in fact function very well. Combat system is fun and innovative, mech building is interesting, mobile base expanding does function and has meaning, item construction gives items which have oompf and there are so many parts, weapons etc. that I'm absolutely positive I haven't tested even half of all weapons and items available in game when i'm all done with it. In all these regards Phantom Brigade isn't a bad game, its quite excellent in fact.. but.Game is built with so vague way words cant ironically even described it. Its like majority of the material which would make the core of the story is just shining with its absence. Story begins with you, assumed soldier or officer, testing a new system given to your, assumed special, unit for testing. A force of generic evil army attacks, you protect civilians while enemy facerolls over, assumedly your, countrys army. Someone called Cadet does a heroic schpiel about protecting civilians and paying back or returning.. aaaand game skips to a point where your now guerilla unit returns with remnants of the homelands army and starts reclaiming areas with your help.The vagueness of everything is just highlighted by everything that follows. There are several counties with their own filler information, plenty of small events in habitation hubs you can fight in and reclaim.. It feels like there is a lot of content but what would glue all of that together, the core of the story.. backstory... what is your country and who is the enemy.. "the WHO ARE YOU?" is missing. That all doesn't mean the say the game isn't fun to play.. it just comes in a form which doesn't make you feel invested or interested for a long period of time. I'm gonna finish this game some day.. but its gonna be a long long process of barely bite sized chunks of me just enjoying gameplay rather than diving in and being invested into the story which stretches playing sessions to unhealthy lengths.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: It's not Battletech. What do I mean by that? In BT there is a dichotomy between the metal, ie the big stompy robot and the meat, the fragile monkey who pilots it. That's what makes the mecha genre interesting, from Voltron to well, Battletech. It shouldbe a tragedy when either your mech gets shot up or you need to hose out the cockpit and now install someone with flippers for hands instead of the skillgodwho unfortuneatly now is being sent home in a matchbox.In Phantom Brigade all pilots are the same. Losing one isn't a blow because theres a new pilot who is, just the same. stepping up. The Mecha are also generic and felt like they were from IKEA. A mecha should have it's own personality and not feel like it has been assembled from legos.The strategy phase was interesting, even if it was designed by an autistic nutcase for whom intuitive is an alien concept.But even if, and it's a big if you work that out you still quickly realise your driving IKEA mechas who are piloted by interchangeable nobodies.Which is why I reloaded Battletech and installed some mods.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished the game. It is a huge disappointment. I suffered through it - save yourself and do not play it. Certainly don't buy it.First gameplay, then aesthetics.Gameplay:You "win" by taking the Capital Province. That took me about 35 hours. There are a ton more provinces to capture, but I'm not playing past this point. If the game has anything more to offer, then developers are foolish to gate it behind 30+ hours of gametime.This game was in development for Lord knows how long, but the developers failed to include basic quality of life features that you encounter within an hour of playing. You have to fight with menus to see what equipment modules do. Most of the items' descriptions don't say what they even do. This is a big problem in the crafting menu, where you can craft items... but aren't allowed to see what their stats are! You have to go back to your inventory and hope you have one in stock to look at.There's more. Your attack information sometimes doesn't show up when you mouse over your icons. You have to constantly place & remove & replace your orders to get something that works right.There are major problems that directly affect gameplay. Weapon balance is all over the place. Plasma Launchers are ridiculously overpowered. Cannons are worthless. Some subsets of weapons are worthless too. If you play this you'll find some weapons are good and others are not worth even considering. That said, despite the bad options, there is enough variety that it feels interesting.Some people complain about missiles being too good. The major problems are:- Dash lies to you. It says Dashing breaks missile lock, but this is not true.- You can't track projectiles after they've launched. You're telling me our time travel device can tell what enemies' exact actions will be in the next 5 seconds, but it can't track projectiles?You don't get to choose where your mechs deploy. Every battle starts you off in close range to the enemies, often from terrible tactical positions. Like, ambushing a convoy by running straight down a wide open road with no cover. Why would we do that? It looks as if they had a deployment mechanic and then scrapped it for some reason.The Concussion damage type is overpowered as well. It is both the best tactical way to destroy enemies, and the best strategic damage type to use, because you get more rewards for enemies killed via Concussion. The general rule for design is that something good tactically is bad strategically. Think of the explosives from modern XCOM 1. It helps you win the battle, but in exchange you lose out on strategic resources. That's the correct way to implement this sort of mechanic. The numbers involved with Concussion damage vs regular damage needs to be seriously modified to make it worthwhile to not focus on Concussion.Barrier is a bad mechanic, yet it takes up half of the game design space on armor. It's supposed to let you regenerate HP mid-battle. But there's a major flaw in this design: Time-to-kill on mechs is 1-2 turns. Neither you nor enemies have meaningful time to regenerate HP.Speaking of damage, every time you land a hit, damage numbers fly up all over the damn place. There are so many numbers flying around you can barely tell who's doing what. After a while I just gave up trying to figure it out.There are rumors on the discussion forum that there are hidden mechanics that further obscure numbers from you. If true, any developer involved in that ought to be fired. Hidden mechanics affecting your stats in a game that's entirely about making decisions based on those stats is directly counter to the core gameplay. But, I don't know if that's true, so I won't go off too much about it.Aesthetically, the game is soulless. Utterly soulless. There's no love put into it. There is no story - everything is written so generically that you don't care about your guys or the enemy in the least. This game does nothing to advance mecha games. It's a worse game than mecha tactics games from literally 20 years ago.Here's another aesthetic failure of the game: Every turn you can replay the last 5 seconds. But:- You can't see the last 5 seconds of the fight, since you go straight to a victory screen after winning or losing- You cannot save the entire battle and play it back!- You can't see damage numbers in the replays. Remember how there are numbers flying all over the place? Maybe you thought "it's okay, I'll watch the replay to sift through that noise and make sense of it." Well, too bad. The devs didn't deign to let you see the damage results from thatWhat's the point of a replay mechanic if you can't understand what happened to improve yourself, or watch the entire battle for fun? Toribash got this right 15+ years ago. Why can't you?Don't play this game. Do not give them money for this. Do not reward releasing unfinished games.
