_childDocuments_.review: I hate to give this a thumbs down, but as you progress you start to see all the flaws that this game has. The biggest issue is the UI. It doesn't tell you enough. The intractability makes everything feel clumsy and irritating. Cover isn't  cover. Will this building  block these shots? Line of sight  is not obstructed. This bad guy  isn't dying. I don't know how much damage this will  do. It's a game that tries to emulate Xcom-style combat without the RNG, but creates its own RNG by mechanics just not working how they're supposed to most of the time. Whether you survive or perish depends entirely on whether or not the game decides it will play by the rules that it created, and you are shackled to. These things culminate into something very frustrating and unfun. Not because you're losing, but because things are happening that don't make sense. Things just don't work right. Or at least, they don't work how they game implies they're supposed to.If they improved the UI and added to it, informing you of what exactly is happening and not forcing you to guess at the survivability of every moving part in the game... it would be fantastic. As is, I can not continue playing this. It's too irritating. It's like playing Chess with someone that makes up their own moves for each piece.

_childDocuments_.review: Damn dude, my dream finally came true for a Front Mission sequel (not Evolved!)Innovative (or at least I haven't played anything like it) turn-based and real time strategy hybrid.  Every turn starts paused (like any turn-based strategy game).  What's different is that when you 'execute' your attack or turn, they are essentially in 5 second chunks.  Your movement and attacks are carried out in real time but you get to see what every enemy plans to do within that same 5 second window.  Turn completes/carried out for the 5 seconds.  Game pauses again and you plan your next 5 seconds.  5 seconds of real time execution of your plan, then back to pause/plan phase.  Repeat.I'm only 3 hours in, and there are more mechanics to be explained, but so far, I'm love it.  And for this price?  It's a must try for any Front Mission fans IMO.

_childDocuments_.review: The premise is simple: you're a rag-tag bunch of rebels with some scraps and a dream and an almighty computer program that accurately predicts five seconds of combat. You give your pilots orders via a nifty "video-editor" system that is mostly intuitive and have them execute the most flawless plan ever.The result is that every single time Phantom Brigade goes into real-time you are given an action-movie set piece trailer that is often as great as the premade cutscenes that they produced to promote the game in the first place. If they can ever get the full replay system working I can practically guarantee that even a random battle would end up looking like promotional material.This has the added benefit of making you feel awesome. You're not just going "shoot guy, shoot guy more" - you're juking behind cover, hopping between (or on top of) buildings, you're hacking enemy mechs so hard with a giant sword that their bodies are sent sailing through the air until they collapse into a building somewhere. You're shooting gaping holes through buildings to take out the enemy. You're diving in front of allied mechs with a shield, tanking the hit and then charging into the enemy mech to knock them over. You're dodging rockets and firing so many bullets that the sheer number of impacts stop a sprinting mech dead in its tracks. In short: You are the action movie hero. You are the director. You are making the most badass underdog story you can.And then you're getting cocky, running into an encounter that you can't physically win, getting wiped out and reminded that no, you cannot in fact kill 12 enemy mechs and vehicles with just three pilots. The enemy in this game is more numerous, better equipped and often has weapons you don't have yet - until you pry it from their cold, dead hands, that is. You limp home, get a couple rustbuckets and outfit them with whatever you have left, and then try again.I give this game a strong recommendation. Best mech game to come out in years and I'm not just saying that because there's basically no competition. It's cinematic, satisfying, the weapons vary between reasonable and efficient and a giant machine gun bigger than your mech that sets you on fire when you use it but I'm never going to stop using it you can't stop me this is my life now. Couple of side notes: They are working on the battle replay system but apparently it's quite memory intensive due to the physics engine making thousands of calculations a second and, well, having to record the results of all of those while continuing the fight means consuming  of the memory. Pilot progression is still being worked on, AFAIK, but was stalled due to them wanting to polish up 1.0. We'll see where they go from here, but honestly I can confidently say that this game could easily receive a metric buttload of DLC and I'd buy 'em all.

_childDocuments_.review: Update: Changed my review to recommend.  A year later a large update addressed many of the issues, and mods filled in much of the rest.  Still not a perfect game, but I say it is fairly worth the money.--original--It isn't a terrible game.  And if you're into the genre (XCOM + Battletech) it can be pretty good.But, it is clearly unfinished.  I waited for the first update to give them a chance to correct some issues before reviewing, but the update was pretty minimal and does not address many of the issues.A ton of UI elements are clearly placeholders.  Either with copy+paste text of similar items, or text that doesn't match what the item does at all.  Events can trigger over each other leaving you with no choice but to alt+f4 the game to get out.  There are probably less than 10 maps, and you see them all the time.  Even back to back.  There's very little context help or information on what does what, and the tutorial is not only incomplete, but seems to cover features that were either removed or never fully made it into the game.  This is especially egregious as major mechanics are either barely explained, or not explained at all.  Why is your mech taking damage when it fires?  What does a reactor do?  What do the symbols on the map mean?  What does the difference in enemy labels mean?  Figure it out on your own.Depth and nice QOL of additions are also glaringly absent.  Pilots are just clones with no meaningful stats.  After battle reports tell you nothing.  I found out I lost a pilot by the achievement unlocking, it wasn't mentioned anywhere else.  You can salvage parts, but you don't know what you're getting for any of it.  You don't know if anyone was hurt, if you lost a mech, or everyone is now crippled.  I could go on, but suffice it to say, maybe wait for some updates.  With some polish this game could be great, otherwise only worth it if you're particularly into this type of game.

_childDocuments_.review: It's Front Mission with Frozen Synapse's simultaneous turns, and it's pretty good, gameplay-wise. There's a lot of granularity to the customization, meaning you can make a lot different builds on a relatively small set of parts, and you can end up with wildly different mechs in your team, highly specialized for their roles. Which is hella cool.Outside of the gameplay, however, the UX is pretty bad and the story is basically non-existent, so there is a noticeable lack of polish. To me, the gameplay is more than enough to compensate for these issues, especially at this game's price point. Bottomline, if you like mech tactics and you're looking for a purely gameplay experience (and are willing to overlook some indie-style lack of polish), this should be a solid pick.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: Pro: A Strategy System that deserves the name. Contra: Story falls flat, heavy difficultyThe round based System with a 5 Second forcast of potential enemy actions is awesome. It lets you take cover and storm out to attack. And it is really necessary to keep strategy and tactics in mind, and not just storm out and shoot everything that is red.The sad part is the heavy difficulty despite the round based (no time limit) planning phase. And the story is also a bit flat. An ambiguous enemy attacks your nameless nation and you have to reconquer it. You are told about civilians, but you never see any of them. There is no emotional connection to your mission.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty neat concept, but the game loop gets really tedious after a while. After you loot and see the initial types of mech parts, finding and comparing new pieces stops being fun after a point, and feels like just comparing numbers. The overall campaign map is HUGE. This would be great, if not for the tedium I mentioned earlier. There is procedural generation for each level, enemy spawns and movements start to feel really formulaic after a while, like there's a "perfect" set of moves you should be doing each level. It's cool that the enemy spawns and loadouts change when you save scum, but again, the tedium. After all the novelty wears off, this game is just tedious.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: Solid core gameplay loop but you will encounter all the possible body piece and weapon types within the first ten hours or so. The only rarities are as shown, white, green, blue. Blue is quite scarce and you will drown in greens. This makes the game get old quick. Each combat plays out pretty similarly with the same old rewards that collect dust in your endless pile. For an underdog your Phantom Brigade wipes the enemy armies with ease. Even impossible missions are stress free. It's also mad easy to take a province, simply win four objective battles. A few positives are that the game looks and sounds great, combat feels good but disconnected. Melee for example can miss easily and can only be swung from the right arm's side. The movement is nice, you are able to dash on top of roofs and most wherever you please, positioning is quite easy for such big mechs.TLDR: Reverse skill issue, game is real easy and grindy without reward variety plus lack of content and meaning behind what you are doing.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: WWWAAAAAAAGGGGGGGGHHHHHHHHH!!!!!!!!!!!CRAP ON A STICK THIS AIN'T!!! It's exactly what I was hoping when I first saw it announced way back. This, this is the only way to do "Turn Based" combat. Even if it didn't have the other half of this particular games core mechanic, it would still be epic.Looks good, plays good. And the combat command method? For us turn based junkies this insane. Crafting the flow of choices on an evolving timeline that responds, be it for good or for worse, based on how and where you tell your units to move. Then getting to watch it unfold in real time. MORE! MORE! MORE!!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: THIS GAME DESERVES A GOOD STORY WITH YOUR AMAZING INTRO. What is here is 15-20 hours worth of battle content that you could stretch out to 100 hours if you complete the campaign map. Despite this being a negative review, I do genuinely recommend this game. BYG, I hope you read this and I hope you feel the love coming from me. Don't let the negative reviews deter you from working on this more. You have something that could be amazing here, it just needs a little more.     Phantom Brigade is pure fun, at least in its battles. Despite having fun and engaging battle mechanics, everything else feels bland. They have an amazing core product here, allowing for a multitude of mech builds using different equipment and tactics. The problem is that it's all it has going for it right now. Having to liberate 20ish provinces that all look exactly the same while fighting enemies that behave the same with objectives that are the same and completing the same 10 overworld "missions" turns a fun idea about guerrilla mech battles into a massive slog.     A few more overworld mechanics, at least one new enemy type, more dynamic events, a campaign story, and more information about the war and our invaders are some key things Phantom Brigade needs. The invaders are evil, but why? Why did they invade? Why can't we see why they're evil? According to the campaign map, bar a select few overworld events, everything seems fine. It seems the devs wanted an emergent "tell-your-own-story" campaign with dynamic events. But after seeing the same event enough times it gets boring. Give us a compelling story about retaking my homeland. I want it, I REALLY REALLY want it.     Here is the absolute one thing that would get me more involved. Have several regions. Have each region be a part of a story, with a story mission pertaining to each province in the region. Give us big bonuses and unique unlocks for each story mission completed and each REGION liberated. Have the regions look unique. Everything is forests. Even smaller countries in our modern day have vastly different ecosystems depending on where you are. Give each region a part of a story that combines into an overarching narrative that makes me weep tears of joy once I finally liberate the capital.      I already feel somewhat connected to the starting 4 pilots. Cut out pilot deaths altogether, make your pilots a core team that grows and learns together. I get what you were going for with this emergent style of campaign, but a game like this, with the amount of love you put into its mechanics, deserves an equal amount of love for its story. There are a lot of things I would love to see added, but this is the one thing Phantom Brigade NEEDS. Contesting a province should be an EVENT, not an eye-rolling slog of patrolling back and forth between a province. Give us more scripted battles. Give us more story events. I want more dialogue aside from the tutorial. I wanna learn about the world and my pilots.Despite how negative I sound, I still love your game, and will continue to play it, at least until I finish this first campaign. After that, I'm not sure.Much Love, BYG.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: Too basic in all the aspects of the game (and the plot is so shallow...).It lacks a lot of features that you can already find in Battletech.Add a new battle system, but is a bit confused and lacks a lot of feedbacks and information about your actions.A 5.5 on 10, could be fun, but it's not worthy the full price. Maybe try it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game, and very much worth it's price.Only main issue, is that for whatever reason, this game likes to freeze my entire computer every couple of missions, which is the only thing keeping me from playing it more. This is not unique to my computer; some of my friends who have this game also have experienced this game freezing their entire computer, and it really hurts to freeze during the rewards/scrapping section of a mission, and even more when you explicitly plan to concuss all the pilots to get their stuff, only for the game to freeze. Digging into some of the other reviews on this game, it seems we are not the only ones.I want to play this more often, but I hate having to force restart my entire PC every time I play this game, and it's discouraging knowing that if I want to sit down and play this game, I'll have to deal with that. Please fix this.Otherwise, great game.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: Wish I could recommend, but this games need a small overhaul first.  The tutorial isn't great, and there are many times I was just confused on how to accomplish simple tasks.  Want to fight an enemy convoy?  Well, clicking on it so your troops approach it will do just that...you walk towards it and then stop once your reach it.  How do you actually engage it?  Oh, you have to move your group to actually run into the enemy on the map. So intuitive...it's little things like that, along with an incomplete tutorial, that really frustrated me to the point of returning it.  If you love RTS and mechs, it's a no questions buy.  But if don't regularly play the genre this is not the best start for you.  Will say the combat system and customization are really great, but its the rest of the game that lacks.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: A fascinating game with a brilliant combat concept.I'll replay battles just to try out different tactics.The ability to modify and equip your 'mechs' is outstanding with room to improve.All in all a fantastic game with a lot of room to grow, if you like intense tactical battles with destructible buildings and almost no RNG to drive you nuts, then this is a good one for you!
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: This game is genuinely fantastic. What I've seen mostly out of the negative reviews is a focus on the rough edges, but I really think that fails to emphasize just how much this game can capture you. There's nothing else like it, and while the UI has some issues and it's rough with the balance here and the mechanical clarity there, the experience is overall so fantastic that I can't help but be captivated by the potential this thing has. They capitalize on a lot of that potential, but if they support it well then this game could become a genre/sub-genre in and of itself. As someone who's played the closest analogues -- all of the Frozen Synapse games, and I guess Achron -- this game is a genuine accomplishment.Making a game this genuinely unique and bold comes with caveats, and this game's issues are fixable as hell. You gotta try this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Front Mission was one of my all time favorites. As a long time fan of Robotech, Heavy Gear, Front mission, and my all time favorite Battletech. This game is a great addition to the genre. I would love an option to replay the whole battle after its over. its a shame its not there, as the replay we do have can be epic. Ive used it a couple times to remind myself of what happened the turn before. But otherwise it is a very cool feature that is under used. Watching a replay of the battle is a much more interesting application than the last turn. I would really like to see more attachments and mech designs added. EWS being something that would be a fantastic addition to melee builds. All in all, good game. I'm hoping for more in the future. Including a multiplayer skirmish mode. P.S. Assuming there is a sequel, can we stop with the Epic games release ♥♥♥♥.

_childDocuments_.review: Good, yes, perfect no. There's some issues, so grab it on a saleGundam style mechs that can see 5 seconds into the future. Plan your movement, attacks, guarding, and dashing based on knowledge of where the enemy is going, who they're shooting, and when. Bring your mechs from a patchwork of whatever you can find to an optimised kit packing interesting weapons. Mech building and core gameplay is good. Combat runs on accuracy cones and effective ranges, with a heat system. Be outside effective range, dashing to throw off tracking, or behind coverThe flaws are in the strategic layer. No progression for pilots and no time pressure forcing decisions. You can loose parts and pilots, or just get your repair resource drained by soaking damage. If you fail, you can just go resupply and try again or harass patrols to farm up some parts. World map events are rather barebones too. The game pushes you to keep experimenting and trying new things as enemy parts (and thus, your loot) go up in HP/damage by levelSo, enjoy some beautifully choreographed combat, but take a break before it wears out its welcome

_childDocuments_.review: Great game , i see some people are complaining about missles and what not , ill give you a tip (dash) is your friend .You have to understand the concept of mech to mech battles , watch like a gundum or something , missiles are OP if they hit ya , thats in every circumstance even in IRLAlso note you are a guerrilla force disrupting a occupying force , you want to be fast, deadly , and precise and get the hell out of town , speed is your friend and using the terrain to your advantage is your friend All in all im enjoying the game and for the price i think its well worth the buy if you like to be a Commander and like mechs !

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Just go play HBS's BATTLETECH game instead.I'm enjoying the game a lot but there is still a few things holding this game back from it being a full recommend. Sometimes it feels like it needed to be in Early Access a bit longer.All it really has is it's core gameplay, which is incredibly fun and great to look at, but unless you really really enjoy it, there isn't much besides that. Your pilots aren't really unique and you can't level them up or anything like that, they're just bodies you throw in the mechs that can sometimes randomly get lost to random overworld events. And its hard to get into situations where you're forced to deployed mechs that are damaged from previous battles so there really isn't much in the way of emergent stories either.The writing is pretty horrendous, there are points where it genuinely feels like the dev team didn't have a writer on board, like the enemies you fight aren't given a name or a motive on why they invade the player's country, so much of the world-building just isn't there, it's all very disappointing. I think this is my biggest issue with the game.I'm running on minimum specs and the overworld map lags horribly for me, though in the actual missions and combat it runs just fine and actually looks quite good. A lot of it feels like the dev's wanted to copy some aspects from BATTLETECH but they never really match the same impact that stuff had; and I'd honestly recommend more people to play that over this game in it's current state.

This game was a little anemic at launch, but the devs have managed to not only meet launch promises, but exceed them, continuing to add wild content like Boss Fights.And best of all, it doesn't look like they're slowing down.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: This is what happens when the 'Ideas Guy' actually learns how to code.Nothing is new under the sun, and a game is judged by how many other games it takes to describe it: Phantom Brigade is Battletech meets Into The Breach meets XCOM meets Katana: Zero with a splash of Mount & Blade Warband and Total War. You don't know joy until you witness your units wombo combo the everloving ♥♥♥♥ out an enemy shield mech.Updates for this game come slow but whenever they drop one it substantially changes the game. While the base game got repetitive by hour 10, all the updates since launch have doubled the amount of content in this game and then some. I hope this trend continues. I haven't run into a single feature that has negatively affected my gameplay experience.This should be an instant buy for you if you like turn based strategy and mechs. In fact, I think you should serve jail time if you haven't already put this in your cart.This was GOTY 2023 for me and it's not even close.
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: [+] Extremely original simulatenous turn system,along with mechanics such as collisions that allow for a lot of clever plays (and makes the battle look more exciting than your average turn based game)[+] Fully destructible environment,which acts as dynamic cover[+] Graphics,although simplistic are saved by the fancy particle effects[-] Lacks much depth and difficulty,once you figure out a decent line-up,you're good to go to steamroll the entire game[-] Not much progression aside from "numbers go up" (see above),base upgrades are expensive gimmicks that don't help much anyway[-] AI is dumb as a shoe,constantly attempts to shoot things through walls,moves to nonsensical positions without firing[-] The mechs themselves look fairly bland and the animations are bare-bones,taking a lot from the "cool factor" you'd expect from a mech game[-] As far as I've played,there's no major time pressure (aside from the escalation system),meaning you're free to roam the world and grind better parts as you please,compared to games like XCOM where you're fighting a constant arms race(maybe then base upgrades would start to make sense?)Overall I give it a weak 7/10,you won't find a similar turn system anywhere else,which is the main thing keeping this game afloat,hopefully the future updates will expand more on the mechanics,as it starts getting repetitive after 10 hours

_childDocuments_.review: [Edit 2024-09-25] When I wrote this review I was pretty sure they were just going to abandon this game after launch. They didn't. The bosses they added are quite fun and there have been numerous tweaks and additions to the game that are quite good, with a big one coming out soon. Therefore I'm changing the review to positive, even though I still think it falls short of what I wanted it to be.Good system, unfulfilling game. Quickly, what is good: mech customization, combat and I like that you can salvage anything from your enemies. Surprisingly fitting music.This is like if the team that made  wanted to make . Both of those games are more satisfying. Unless they finish the game then I need to give this a Not Recommended. I've enjoyed most of the gameplay but overall the game left me with a bad feeling and I don't even care to retry the final mission (I didn't even bother to prep for it). It's hard to review games like this because I got it for like $22 on sale on release so I'm not sure what I'm supposed to expect but for the reasons below I cannot recommend:The first and major issue is that there is no match deployment. There is a (weirdly huge) worldmap and there's a tactical map when you assault a location but they are mostly just for show. You can go to different regions on the worldmap and get the exact same tactical map. Furthermore I've gotten the same map 4 times in a row despite traveling farther, only with my starting position rotated! They NEED to implement a deployment aspect to this game. One of my favorite things to do in video games is scout out optimal locations and this game completely ignores that strategic layer. The whole premise of "knowing the next 5 sec of every enemy" is completely shot when you start a match and an enemy mech and 2 tanks are 4-seconds away from hitting you with shotguns with no cover to run to and your sniper mech is at the front of deployment.Everyone already mentioned the "final replay" being a necessity to the game that's ALL ABOUT having a tight ~25 second match coming together perfectly. What kind of team leadership at Brace Yourself Games would let the game ship without this? I have to imagine this is a limitation of their engine or their expertise. You can't even replay the final 5 seconds of a match. And even more importantly, you don't see damage numbers in the turn "replays." These are mind boggling decisions. There is simply no excuses for these things missing.It's nearly impossible to look at a mech and know what it does. The guns all look bizarrely the same. They don't understand visual language in game design. I spent way too much time in every match trying to click on enemy units to see what weapons they have--and that's pretty much all that matters. Halfway thru the game I realized you can hold down Alt to see unit info but it was just cluttered and confusing, and it shows the icons of weapons which, again, all look the same.There are tons of ways to configure the mechs. But there are so many mechanics that only really become clear once you've put tens of hours into the game (and at that point you've seen everything the game offers). They never, once, mention that Heavy equipment holds more heat (heat is the most important and most obscured stat)--just that it dissipates heat less quickly, and I couldn't figure out for 20 hours why anyone would run a Heavy mech. There are also inconsistencies with the tooltips display--sometimes gun details do not show during gameplay, and sometimes workshop projects visually disappear until you reload a save. And there were typos as the patch notes indicate that some equipment does the opposite of what it says. After playing quite a bit of this I've accepted that English as a second language might be hindering the clarity of this game. I also see weirdness in the game's writing. Every has mentioned this game has no "story." There are paragraphs of flavor text but there is something discordant about it that I won't elaborate on.I rarely write reviews but I had to after the confounding nature of this game. The mechs and the mech combat are satisfying but everything else is maddening. I read an early review saying this game is soulless. I would say that it's passionless.

_childDocuments_.review: I’ve waited several years for Phantom Brigade and after being on Epic Store early access for quite some time now. The game has finally launched on steam on version 1.0. So I had to play it. This means retaking the capital city or clearing every province. I only completed the former since the latter takes up way too much time. And is it worth the wait? Well…Maybe. It has some things to be concerned about.First, the game is set in a sandbox fictional world where you control a group of mechs who can use a prototype device to see a bit into the future and “predict” what the enemy will do for the next five seconds. In those five seconds, you may position your mech squad to run, dash, shield, or attack the enemy within that time frame. Once you’re sure of your commands, you can lock in your planning phase and let the real-time kick in and watch as your mechs go toe to toe against hostile enemies. If your enemies are still alive, you’ll have to plan for the next five seconds on the timeline and continue inputting your planning phase before executing. This will repeat until all enemy hostiles are eliminated.This is the main hook of the combat of Phantom Brigade and honestly, it is satisfying going into combat and watching those moves play out. Especially, when I had to face off multiple enemies against a small squad. Making my chances for victory slim, but with careful planning, positioning, and knowledge of what my weapons could do and how far my mechs could move. Anything is possible to achieve victory.I’d say it took me between one to three hours before I got the hang of things and once I had unlocked 4 mechs in my squad. You don’t unlock a full squad off the bat. You need to unlock it from the upgrade menu in the overworld. Once I had a full squad, I became more confident in conquering new territories.Or as the game likes to call it, provinces. At the start, you and your crew hold no provinces at the start. And as you look at the world map. You can see quite a lot of enemy territory. Each with their levels marking how dangerous they are and the capital.It may look easy at first glance to retake a province, but you’ll need to contest the area first. Where you'll need the Homeguard to help. Think of them as allies. From there a meter of your forces and the enemies is displayed. Winning battles in the contested area or taking a key objective like cities, outposts, patrols and more will reduce the enemy meter. Do enough battles, and soon enough you can take back the province from enemy hands.This is the rinse and repeat of Phantom Brigade and one of the key points of my following critique of the game.First, taking provinces, I enjoyed in the beginning to mid-game until I got bored of doing the same thing again. And again. And again. I became fatigued as my pilots do since nearly every battle became samey after retaking a province. Sure, there are other features the game has, like enemy patrols and different units defending caches and key locations, which do a bit to randomize the back-and-forth battles.But there just isn’t enough of a main hook to appeal to me more. And granted I admit I'm more of a story player, instead of gameplay first. However, I still enjoy games on the opposite side. And this game hits some of those notes well. Except it could be better.Second, it would’ve been nice to replay the whole battle. Yes, there is a replay feature, but that only works after 1 turn. So if a battle took an ‘x’ amount of turns the player has the option to see the whole mission play out in real-time without any interruptions. Kinda like how Super Meat Boy does it.Third, inject some story narrative in me to care more about ‘player-driven stories.’ This is ripped straight from the steam description. And I find it a bit misleading. Since, the game shows random events happening on the world map which can make the player choose various decisions from helping the townspeople, investigating, and even espionage outcomes like holding a captive. But, outside of the overlying objective of retaking the capital or retaking all provinces. There just isn’t enough within the contents of the game to make the player relate more to those objectives.Fourth, there is no pilot progression at all. So taking your pilots into continuous battles will not yield them any bonus skills or hidden passive they’ll unlock later on. They’ll lose health if they sustain enough damage in combat and you can recruit more pilots. But that’s it. The only thing they’re good for is being substituted if my pilot has low health after repeated engagements with the enemy. Make pilots matter.Fifth, the battles in provinces use the same dialog for beginning intro into battles and good lord does it get tiresome to see again and again? I didn’t skip any of the intro battles for each of them to see some variation and to be frank very few changes. Some more flavorful text injected would’ve helped liven up battles a bit. Like: “Hey rebels are holding out here. Take them out,” “There was a drunk party and a lot of enemy pilots are in mechs doing crazy stunts. Take advantage of that and eliminate them," This mission will be a bit difficult, and honestly I recommend you don't enter this battle and retreat. But if you are insane, by all means, go ahead and fight this near unwinnable battle.” You can go further and extend this by adding witty, sarcastic, grumpy, cheerful, and more voices here. Just about anything will do to liven up text in intro battles.Sixth. Please diversify main objectives in battles. Instead of fighting, have my squad sneak around the map to obtain the cache supplies. Hold out against waves of enemies and escort missions. Additional random elements like helicopters, bigger tanks, very huge mechs or super tiny mechs, implemented to prevent it from being copy paste. Heck, you can even add optional objectives like going into battles with only melee and shields. Win using only missile weapons or sniper etc.And that’s it. I could say more, but I'll withhold the laundry list. But, I hope you all get the picture with my six points.Excusing my critique, I would like to say there is a great deal of customization here I enjoyed a great deal. You can set up your mechs with a variety of weapons and body parts. It’s not quite as extensive as Armored Core, but for folks coming from Battletech and Into the Breach, you’ll notice a bit of similarity between the two. Xcom too. And salvaging is worth it after a battle to see what parts you can gain from your enemies that will benefit your squad. To my absolute delight, destructible environments like buildings and mech parts. They add a strategic layer to combat. Since you can see enemies' projectiles and where they’ll hit in the timeline. You can manipulate their a.i. For them to hit buildings or a small cliff in the environment. Thereby saving your unit if they don’t have shields and allowing your squad to mop up the ai’s grave mistake. Once I realized the enemies couldn’t do anything more advanced than following through with their actions, the game became easier.Speaking of difficulties. I have to give the developers credit for making a good list of options available to tweak how hard or easy the game can be. And it is worth editing for any players having trouble with enemies dealing too much damage or your squad overheating.Overall, I’d say Phantom Brigade is something I’d recommend for those interested in mech games, without a story narrative and purely for gameplay first and a sandbox experience. And even then I hesitate because of the price. So you may be better off waiting to buy the game on a sale. However, it does feature a lot of hours to sink into if you enjoy the gameplay loop of battles, salvage, customizing your mech squad, and retaking provinces. Then this game might be for you.6/10

_childDocuments_.review: Phantom Brigade is an exciting new take on turn base strategy. Moving through battles 5 seconds at a time combines the thrill of real time combat with the cerebral engagement of strategy play. The strategy element expands even further with the tactical analysis of how to approach liberating provinces and constructing your squad of mechs. It is visually interesting and fun to watch as the battles unfold, although it can be a bit difficult to keep track of all the different engagements going on in one fight. The game's cinematics stalled out hard for me, but it wasn't a distracting element. There are several elements that are opaque, like understanding how your units might collide or how to target melee attacks, but ultimately the game is a lot of fun to play and I recommend it highly to any fan of strategy games.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, feels amazing when you pull off a good plan. Still some things lacking but 110% worth it currently. It's a bit of a slow start and has a learning curve that in order to not take 20min to plan out what your gonna do so I'd recommend just a few things. Combat-Try out different weapon types and use ones you enjoy with the heavy/med/light mech type, I personally run a light sniper, heavy laser chonk, frontline with shotgun and shield, and then a mobile flanker with a railgun. It took losing a few mechs and pilots to learn the comp I like so dont feel flustered if you lose some. -For combat the general recommendation I'd give is go through your mechs one at a time, see who is being shot at and try to get them behind cover (also take note at what exactly is shooting at you). During this time try to take advantage of the wait/move to peak out of cover when you're not being shot and then return to cover if needed. I noticed early on the AI was very fond of missiles so be mindful of them as they can do alot of damage to med/light mechs BUT you can use your booster to dash out of the way. When you finish the planning it may be a good idea to quickly skim through the timeline to make sure you dont friendly fire your mechs from behind. Flanking from behind is always an easy thing to do to quickly kill but it poses risks if you move without any cover, keep at your optimum range with the flankers and just be mindful of whats around you. -In short for combat; shoot when not being shot, use cover, lasers go bur and can remove enemies cover, hit em from the back for ez slap. Workshop: Upgrades and crafting-Getting the initial increased capacity is a great thing to do, so far the max amount of mechs I've been able to bring in is 4 but it isnt a bad idea to have extra just in case you keep getting picked by patrols and cant repair. -Get the "usable" items, the ones to call in support, lower the difficulty of the fight, and then cutting of reinforcements. These are all great items and can turn a fight your would lose into an easy stomp. Open world map and overall difficulty-Dont be afraid to pull back from a zone if it starts to get too difficult, just throw on a youtube vid as you hit the double speed and in a few the difficulty will be more manageable. You can also just go hit another region while one cools off. -Hit the supply/equipment/convoys: they give blueprints and supplies and for the most part are easy kills. -You will NOT repair while using the 'boosted speed' or the stealth-9 times out of 10 that crate you find after a fight probably is a bomb BUT it can also be loot, if you have extra supplies ya might as well try your luck. -I believe you can lower the difficulty during the campaign (i went in with nothing adjusted and never felt like anything was too difficult or far too easy) so if you're struggling try it out.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played this game pretty consistently, and am about halfway through my first campaign. I recommend a purchase, even at full price. I am left with some wants, but overall I'm very happy with the current state of the game. First, the time mechanic is the point of the game. If you want turns, play XCOM 2. It's great. I have plenty of hours over there and the time mechanic is a refreshing departure from the I-move-you-move board game. My recommendation to players: Play with the No Resource Caps mod. You can find it on the Nexus Mods page for the game. Currently there is a cap on the number of components and supplies you can have at any one time, which can really bottleneck your experimentation with all of the weapons the game has to offer. I've had much more fun with wild builds since I installed this mod. It also makes losses hurt less late game so you can play with riskier and (in my opinion) more fun builds. Others in these reviews have said that the time mechanic feels cheesy, and that they can just move their mechs into cover when they get targeted and that makes the game easy! It's not quite that simple because of missiles and railguns. Also, if the game becomes too easy when you cheese it, don't do that. Play your way, but if it's not fun don't do it. There are other ways! Things I want:- A Skirmish mode! The campaign is great and has kept me on my toes on the default difficulty, but I was to be able to have fast action with all of the game's tools at my disposal at the same power level. - Better inventory screen descriptions and information. Examples being the Ajax and Svalinn shields both have the same description, Workshop screen not giving any item information before you build an item, and mech part descriptions not explaining the strengths and weaknesses of each part. All of this would be helped with a detailed wiki, which there is not. Thanks for reading my overwritten review! I hope the features I'm wishing for get into the game. If not, I'm sure the mods will come!

_childDocuments_.review: Oof.  So, I was really looking forward to this one.  And after playing the demo, I was convinced it was gonna be great.  The problem is that the demo had literally the entire game.  Oh, sure, there were more sectors to take over, but they were all identical to the first - only worse because after the first one, the progression slows to nothing - you get ~5 tech levels in the first zone, and then <1 in the following zones.That wouldn't be bad, exactly, but the result is that every fight is exactly the same.  In similar games like X-COM, there's some variation - squad comp changes as soldiers got wounded, or new abilities as troops level up, or just different map types with UFO crashes or supply collection or whatever in addition to kill quests.  PB doesn't have any of that - you basically only have a single squad, damage isn't really an issue 95% of the time since you repair by the time you reach the next fight, and the maps are very, very samey quiet little towns, or slightly larger quiet little towns with walls/towers.  And without any new abilities or, most of the time after the first zone, any new parts worth your time, you end up doing a huge number of fights with exactly the same team on an exact same map or one that's indistinguishable.  Technically there are supply gathering quests, but the one time I tried to gather supplies instead of just clearing all enemies, I lost a mech after getting surrounded, but I've never had a problem when I go in with intent to win via clear (and you get more salvage too), so you basically end up with 100% kill all enemies in quiet little town with exactly the same team over and over and over and over again.   I'll probably push through a bit more just to see if there are any more interesting aspects in later zones, but I already don't give the tiniest hockey puck about actually completing the campaign, and the research is pointless wastes of resources for base "upgrades" that are usually just tradeoffs.  Not a single future upgrade in the upgrade tree excites me.Which is really unfortunate - the basic gameplay loop is actually really good.  It's a fantastic combination of Into the Breach with a more modern X-COM or BATTLETECH style feel and campaign.  Instead of having enemy intents for 1 turn, you have 5 seconds of realtime enemy prediction to play against, and it's honestly really fun making sure whoever is getting targeted is safe, and the rest are pumping out good damage.  Still, after clearing a half dozen sectors, I don't feel like there's a lot more that the game has to offer.  That said, getting 10-15 hours before the tedium really takes over at sub 30 bucks is worth a recommendation.  Just because I was hoping that this would be my next 100+ hour game doesn't change the fact that I got my money's worth.

_childDocuments_.review: "Phantom Brigade: An I Plan; I Go, Marvel of Mech-tactical Brilliance"Phantom Brigade mech-stomped onto the scene recently, and I must say, the experience is captivating and entertaining. Developed with a keen eye for detail and a love for strategic gameplay, Phantom Brigade stands out as a shining gem in the realm of "I plan; then I go" tactics."I plan, I go" (or "we plan/we go" is a game mechanism where your moves are planned out in short bursts of time.  Once your movement, defense, and attack plans are complete; they are executed in real-time in an armor-shredding display of destruction.  This mechanism was pioneered by strategic games like Combat Mission and developed with a more tactical focus by games like Shadow Tactics and Frozen Synapse. This mechanic injects a thrilling dose of unpredictability into every encounter, keeping players on the edge of their seats as they meticulously plan their moves and witness them unfold in real time. The result is a harmonious blend of strategy and action that feels refreshingly dynamic.Although not taken to the nth degree, the game's commitment to realism extends to its destructible terrain, a feature that adds a layer of depth to battles. Watching buildings crumble and landscapes transform in the wake of intense firefights between lumbering tanks and towering mechs, adds a visceral and immersive quality to the gameplay, making each skirmish feel like a true battleground.The arsenal of weapons available in Phantom Brigade is nothing short of impressive. From beam lasers to energy swords and railguns, the game provides a satisfying variety of tools for players to customize their mechs and adapt to different challenges. Crafting and a technology tree further enhance the strategic depth, allowing for meaningful decisions and specialization as you progress.  Do you want stealth at the sacrifice of speed? The decisions are yours.The heart of Phantom Brigade lies in its ability to let players assemble and control large mechs. Managing pilots and fine-tuning these colossal war machines adds a layer of personalization and attachment that makes victories all the more satisfying. The liberation of territories, rendered with great graphics, becomes a visual feast as your mechs stomp through landscapes, toppling trees, and leaving destruction in their wake.In conclusion, Phantom Brigade is a triumph in the world of tactical gaming. It's a great blend of established gameplay mechanics, destructible terrain, diverse weapon selection, lite crafting, meaningful technologies, and solid graphics.  Phantom Brigade is a great choice for fans of strategic depth and immersive mech combat. The joy of planning and executing maneuvers, managing your mechs and pilots, and liberating territories is an experience that will keep you hooked for hours.  Dollar per hour; it's well worth the time!  And if multiplayer were added - wow! It would be even more amazing!

Looks good, feels good to play especially when you execute some great moves.It has a lot of issues however.  0: It crashes for me, a lot.  I don't know why but it is extremely irritating.  I've redone this level for 4 hours now, it has been a total waste of my time.  1: Performance is subpar and extremely demanding. This game doesn't look bad but that just means it's way too demanding for its fidelity.Worse yet, you have limited graphics options.  You can't disable antialiasing (♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ why?), you can't disable the HORRIBLE depth of field (again, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ why?) and the options in the settings are atrocious and unacceptable for any modern PC game. At first it seems alright, but trying to compare items, scrap them, organize them, and keep track of them requries bouncing between tabs and trying to mouse over things that shouldn't be hidden to begin wtih. _childDocuments_.review: My biggest complaint with the game is the number of times I have said out loud "this is stupid" and then had to reload and try a fight again. I am fond of tactical gameplay, and this offers a unique version of that, but entering missions without a full understanding of the objectives, or even where the enemies will be despite having a "holomap" that shows nothing useful, is very frustrating.Further negatives include a total lack of character development for your pilots: these guys are literally just the meat, and the metal is all that matters. They don't need names, or back stories, or faces for that matter. There is no memorial wall for the fallen, they just get deleted. I have no idea what my country is called, nor who the enemy is that invaded. I don't know what happened to my nameless lieutenant and two cadets from the first mission, I don't understand why we went underground for years, In other words the story is basically "everything was fine until the fire nation attacked...now take it all back."The camera is frustrating in that in order to see the map and your units you often cannot tell if you are properly in cover or not, and when looking to see if you are in cover you can't see what you are shooting at. You also don't get to pick your deployment positions, meaning often times you will spend a round or two just trying to shuffle your mechs into position, all while taking fire.Back to the pilots: they don't level up or improve either, so the meat really is just a squishy thing in the middle of your metal that if you could get away with not having it you would want to not have it.The game runs smooth, the combat system is unique and fun, and I spent two nights in a row staying up way too late trying to enjoy this thing. I clearly had fun, and if the devs add a few patches adding in things to flesh out this game, it could be a true masterpiece. As it stands now, I am not sure I am even going to be bothered trying to finish it, given that there is no story to drag me in, no character development to get the feels going, and the missions are clunkily executed aside from the neat-o predictive combat system.I really do wish on games like this there was a closed fist option on the review. I don't hate this, so I can't bring myself to not recommend it, but it is in an unsatisfying state which makes it hard to want to recommend it.Giving it the thumbs up because I got two nights of amusement out of it, but the burn out will set in fast. Highly recommend picking this one up when its on sale, not full price, and I pray for some good content updates.

_childDocuments_.review: Phantom Brigade is a game with great mechanics in combat but needs more detail, depth and world building where it matters to give context. I have many praises to provide the game in some areas, but I also have many complaints. It is one of the few games that does so well in one area that it mostly makes up for its issues in the others, but with some work, it could be so much better.Firstly, the formula will be somewhat familiar if you have played Battletech. Build your mechs, fight in a turn-based format, manage your heat and win through tactics and guile. Where Phantom Brigade shines is its unique prediction mechanic that is unique enough to make combat vibrant and exciting without sacrificing the challenge. Liberating every province took me 50+ hours, so you get your money's worth. I must also praise the animation quality of the mechs, which are truly impressive.  I lament the lack of a proper tutorial; I did not fully understand the ins and outs until about 10 hours in. There is no explanation for why my melee attacks were not hitting, how to manufacture items, or the levelling mechanic, for example. The tutorial was just a couple of combat missions. A proper tutorial would significantly improve the game, so you could start using everything at your disposal right away. Your pilots are forgettable and have no personality. A necessary addition would be something to make you care about them. What are their backstories? How does their backstory tie into the game? What are their perks when piloting a mech etc? As for the story, there is no story other than another country has invaded yours, and you have to fight back. A more thorough explanation would be appreciated. The enemies are equally generic as well. This lack of context, which I previously mentioned, takes away from the whole package. More world crafting needs to be done to truly make this game stand out. Unique enemies when you get to higher levels would also be welcome, as the game gets monotonous. Facing local commanders of notoriety is one idea I have. You could tie the elimination of them to Home Guard support and the hope mechanic.The levelling system leaves much to be desired. There is no research or special weapons you can get as you level up. Your level just goes up for the sake of levelling up with no cap, as far as I can tell. There needs to be meaning to levelling up, with new access to weapons, tech and research as you salvage items. That would add more depth to the game, rather than just farming rare parts as it is. My last gripe is that there is no way to use heavy mechs effectively, except on defence. Since you are always attacking, that is very rare, if ever. The mech reactors only give so much power so your heavy will always be pitifully slow. The items are not balanced either, so you will always be min-maxing using the items with the most modifications, rather than variety. Some perks like pilots being better with some mechs/parts or major bonuses for completing a set of mech parts would be nice to incentivize you to use a variety of parts. A way to see parts values without having to take off mods in the mech lab would be nice too. Having to remove mods over and over just to find that a higher level part weighs slightly too much is not fun. I suggest a toggle button. Lastly, some of the mods, like the hybrid/range sensor do not seem to affect the weapons stats at all. This is either an error with it not showing on the UI or those mods are not working at all. Bug-wise, there are still several. You cannot manufacture boosters or the DC1 Cannon. I do not know if that is intentional. The PLS Curve projectiles do not hit often, especially on vehicle targets, rendering that weapon unusable. The defector event never goes away, and you cannot complete it. This bug happened in both of my games. I also had an issue with attacking a mine cache that never went away, and I could not complete it. No crashes in my 50 hours, and the game ran very well otherwise. There may be an issue with how melee weapons hit targets, particularly non-mech vehicles. Overall, I would give this game a lukewarm 7/10. With some added depth in the areas mentioned, it would help the game be much better than it is currently, where monotony sets in eventually. I would be willing to pay for DLC if the developer offers it. The combat is excellent and redeems the deficiencies in other areas. A good buy for the price, if you do not mind that it gets a bit boring as you play.

_childDocuments_.review: I tried to take an enemy base for a quest, this resulted in me getting hit by a patrol. I did not realize that nearby forces also send squads to come in as backup, so this patrol was backed up by the base I was after, a nearby outpost, and a nearby equipment convoy.Enemy reinforcements arrived on turns 2, 4, and 10. I ended up fighting around 14 enemies with my squad of 4. By the time we hit turn 24 or so, I had two concussed pilots, and two pilots driving one-armed mechs. One heavy mech with a shield and no gun remaining, and one medium mech with a pistol remaining. The enemy had an autocannon tank and a missile launcher mech.I used my heavy shield mech's thruster to position it along the enemy mech's path, and stopped it from shooting by then having the mech run into it, which crushed the enemy mech. Then a long game of hide and seek with the tank went on for a bit until I realized we really couldn't beat this tank with a pistol before it caused real damage with its autocannon, so my heavy mech then trampled the tank as well. Victory!

_childDocuments_.review: Unique take on turn based combat, it has 5 second rounds that you manage with a timeline, it predicts enemy movement/actions.It has mech style loadouts, a little more simplistic than mech warrior but still gives customisation.The main game takes place over zones on a map you drive around in capture/assault different objectives to gain control of the zones.Tech tree plays a role in your overall ability to do certain things, such as store more mechs, more salvage power, scanner range, movement speed (on map), utility such as stealth, speed burst, crafting speed etc.So far I have not found anything I dislike about the game other than sometimes feeling it is a little too simplistic in certain aspects (especially early game loadouts/choices) and the amount of Missile Launcher enemies you have to deal with sometimes.

_childDocuments_.review: Frozen Synapse with mech-building-via-salvaging and a xcom-ish campaign. On the tactical side, each "turn" is a 5 second slice of time. You get to see what the enemies will do in that 5 second slice. Work around what they are doing, what lines of sight they are using, etc. You don't have ammo or action charges, you manage a heat gauge. Anything besides walking is going to spike your heat. Exceed heat cap and you start taking damage that rapidly will cause problems. Cooling is rapid enough though you never feel limited, but you always have the option to go past what is safe.On the economy side, you can slag every mech you come across in combat, but if you can rattle the mech enough to concuss the pilot you can salvage the parts for cheap, instead of having to rebuild the stuff you broke before it can be used. I laughed when I realized I could just hit the boosters out of cover, slam my mech into an enemy to take them both off the board for a turn, and then let another one of my guys come up and clock the other mech for easier loot. There's definitely shortcomings, it's an indie game. One thing that is blowing my mind is that I don't seem to be able to look at my armory when I'm choosing what to salvage after a battle. Turn replays don't show how damage progresses, it's locked to their HP from the end of the turn. But I think the fundamentals are enough to carry the rough edges.

_childDocuments_.review: Good gameplay at first with a taste of salt after a few hours.The games Concept is unique, awesome and the reason I kept playing but after almost 50 hours many issues result to a lacking game experience. This game still feels like a BETA!- UI bugs:   * Melee not hitting where it shows it does   * If you overcool your Mech the Heat prediction is wrong in the Mech lab   * Gun overlays sometimes not showing on all Friendlies and Enemies for the remainder of the battle   * Shots sometimes penetrate solid ground, although it indicates it would be blocked   * Sometimes ground blocks shots, where there is no ground - Balancing:    * Missiles are OP!   * Shotguns and incendiary repeaters miss too much- Modules:   * Some do not work at all   * Some do not do enough, of what it says it does (Wrong % calc)- Other:   * Sometimes unable to get into a fight or finish a mission objective on the overworld until saving and reloading the save file   * Underwhelming Overworld   * Uninspired separation of mech visuals (compared to BattleTech)   * GPU at 100% for no apparent reason (unoptimized)   * Sometimes crashes during game starts   * Sound issues galore   * No tutorial on how liquid fix for barriers works in battles and that all guns have infinite ammunitionApparently, many promised features are still missing!Let's hope they use the funding from the games "release" to fix as many of these issues before the game gets inevitable abandoned, since it was in development for 5 years now.I still got more fun and playtime out of this game, then I got out of many AAA titles I played, which is why I would still recommend this game to anyone, who seems interested in its unique concept.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game with a really fun mechanic. The graphics are awesome and the way the mechs moves is natural. I have only two wishes for this game. The first is a way to replay the whole match is one go so you are able to see all of your perfectly timed work happen all together in real time. I know this may be difficult but it would be nice to see in a future update. The second if for the enemies to stop using missile launchers in cities when I have been tasked with keeping damage to a minimum. I started a turn with no damage to structures. Enemies fire missiles during their turn. End the turn with 38 damage to structures. Like what am I going to do when the guy on the other side of the map decides firing a slug missile at point blank into house is a good idea. I can't use snipers (he's behind a building), I can't use missiles (more property damage would be caused) I can't try knocking him out with any of my close range, non building destroying weapons (because he is still behind a building). So, yeah. No more missiles in cities please. Or at least less of them. 7 enemies and 3 of them with missiles is not fun.

_childDocuments_.review: There is a very, very solid core here. And lots of potential for replayability. Game's still missing a few bits though. Pros:- Mech customization's pretty goshdarned deep. You can make a sniper mech. You can make a mech that totes a vulcan gatling cannon that farts out thousands of rounds a minute. You can make a tank mech. You can build light skirmishers. You can paint your mechs. - The timeline mechanic is unique. Really, truly, sublime. Props to whoever came up with that as a gimmick, it's really just kinda great. Cons: - The UI's kinda weird. It feels like it wasn't designed for PC in a lot of places. Timeline customization in particular's kinda wonky. - Lot of QOL things missing, like warnings if your mechs are about to collide with each other when you move them or indicators that tell you if missiles're going to be hitting one of your mechs that turn. - Story's really bare-bones. Could use some more fleshing out.- Pilots don't actually matter in this game. You can hose them out of the cockpit for all that they matter, they're just bodies you throw in mechs. About the only stat that matters on pilots is the amount of damage they can take before they have to go night-night. Speaking of...- Concussion damage's just... Awful. It feels ridiculously easy right now for your pilots to get concussed, and then that's one mech taken out of the fight without taking any damage at all. That feels like it needs to be addressed.- Research system could use some explaining. Didn't know you had to get uncommon/rare components from dismantling until I did. Whoops. - No full replay system. Which makes me kinda sad, a full replay system would be amazing.

_childDocuments_.review: Version 1.3: Patches keep coming and I'll keep recommending this game.It's a simultaneous turns tactics game. You have perfect information on what the CPU will do each round, and each round is a plan of actions for a five second real-time phase where everything happens. It's a fun and puzzly system, which is extremely rewarding when you pull of a flawless round, jumping all over the place and dodging enemy fire while dashing from cover to cover.That said... I can't say it doesn't get repetitive after a while. It's good in short sessions where you don't get burned out but can enjoy the puzzle.

_childDocuments_.review: feb 2024 edit: the most recent 1.2 patch is a series of good gameplay tweaks and incremental content for the combat layer like new missions and maps. if you are craving generic mech action it's a good buy. but despite adding more of that same content there's still no narrative or campaign, just a bunch of mostly-procedurally generated provinces to conquer and nowhere near enough characterization, background, or plot to bother caring about any of it. you need very little narrative and writing to make a game feel alive (think INTO THE BREACH, COBALT CORE, BATTLETECH, XCOM-2) but without it the game feels very dead indeed. original: the RPS got it right (for once) - "Phantom Brigade review: entertaining mech battles carry a toothless campaign" a great battle engine is made to feel sterile and lifeless because of the lack of world-building and narrative.  if you're a battletech / front mission die hard it's just servicable enough to keep you going, but even so it started feeling like a chore almost immediately after the tutorial region.  that contrasts sharply with battletech, which despite flaws, dripped with personality and story.  the team is great and i hope they succeed in bringing the game where it needs to be - hoping some DLC that adds narrative and some interactivity will bring the game to where it needs to be.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoy the game, but ahh there are many little things that should so obviously be in the game that are missing.The things that would push this from a good to a great game: - add post match replay of the whole combat - fix the workshop level: either make it so it matches its current description or update its description to accurately represent how it actually works, which is average equipment level of equipped gear on your first four mechs + 1. Yes, if you have just 1 mech with just one gear equipped, you can craft a +1 equipment, equip it and repeat to level up for as long as you can afford it. - in workshop, for ALL blueprints: add to the description more information and ideally even base stats for items. Having to craft a bunch of items just to be able to compare the differences between them is a serious design flaw in this workshop part of the game. - alter how reputation and hope works: my reputation and hope are permamently maxed out and it doesn't seem to really matter either. High reputation is supposed to provide more Homeguard units to assist, but their number only went up from 1 to 3 and their equipped gear stays irrelavantly weak in my games. What is Hope even supposed to do? It's so irrelevant I forget. I keep it up because it's no effective cost and trade-off on my part and I'm roleplaying a Brigade who are out to help out its people. Mechanically it doesn't really matter though. - I may be mistaken on this point as I've yet to find a good light-mech setup, but the issue is: Heavy mechs with huge, no cost thrust distances are VASTLY superior to high speed light mechs. I can have a UHMG heavy mech dash to the other side of the map in a single turn, while a light mech can maybe cross a quarter or half of the map with very optimized, lightweight gear. But the heavy mech also doesn't care for weapon weight restrictions, it can kill enemy light and even medium mechs by ramming them with their superior bulk, they can tank more shots, they output insane damage... I believe this needs some attention and I suppose some balance changes.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a *pretty good* mech strategy game with a unique twist to turn-based gameplay that, despite having a rather steep learning curve, missing quite a few quality-of-life features, lacks an engaging story, and features menus that display far too much information at once, earns a solid recommendation from me. It's not perfect, it could absolutely be improved (and it definitely will), but it's a fun game that tests your ability to micromanage an army and take risks; definitely worth the $30 asking price.

_childDocuments_.review: A solid base combat system dragged down by the brittle skeleton of a game built around it. The campaign is basically an empty sandbox with some skirmishes for you to fight, pilot progression is nonexistent, the actual mech building is limited to swapping out a handful of parts for higher level objectively stronger ones, and the story is limited to "Some other country took over your country, fight back against the invaders". Just an absolute lack of atmosphere or tone of any sortI might STILL have been able to recommend the game on the strength of the combat system alone if not for the obtuse UI and frequent bugs. The combat relies entirely around a system in which you are shown your enemies' actions each turn and plan your moves during the next 5 seconds, and so it's very easy for seemingly minor bugs or UI issues to ruin the experience, I've seen multiple instances of the following:-Units colliding with buildings/eachother despite no indication during planning (there is a yellow circle that is SUPPOSED to indicate unit collision but it frequently doesn't show up)-Enemies attacking units on a turn where there is no indication of them targeting said unit, thus killing mechs that you had every reason to believe were safe for the turn-Melee attacks randomly miss or collide with terrain-Missiles are pure RNG, you have no indication of where they're going when planning and the dash mechanic meant to dodge their lock on is unreliable at best-Enemy reinforcements come in at random locations without any indication, often appearing right next to or behind your mechs mid-battle-Buildings that can be destroyed for certain effects, like cancelling reinforcements or deactivating turrets, are not marked in any way. Unless you memorized their relatively generic appearance during the one tutorial mission that points them out you're out of luckAs a huge mech fan I was really expecting more from Phantom Brigade. It's possible that many of these issues could be patched and improved over time, but after looking at how little progress was made from Early Access to 1.0 I do not have great faith in that happening
_childDocuments_.name: Phantom Brigade

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR this game needs some more time in the oven.Don't get me wrong, this game's core is phenomenally fun. The satisfaction of setting up an effective crossfire as an enemy mech stumbles and crashes into a building. The then horror as you realize the enemy stopping there leaves a friendly mech right in the way of said crossfire. It's great! However, after a few hours, the game really shows it's cracks.ISSUES: AI: I get that AI can be a difficult thing, but enemy units are pretty braindead at times. Bring a heat weapon, and they'll be reluctant to even fire, and will often just beeline for friendlies. Sometimes, they won't even act at allMAPS: They're tiny, with terrible spawns. In larger engagements you and the enemy will spawn mere spaces away from eachother. On top of this, there arent even that many. I shouldn't be seeing repeats of maps only after a few hours. They're usually not even that complex, and I feel like either the game needs a load of new maps or even just a simple map generation system.REPLAYABLITY: After starting a few new games, this one becomes pretty apparent. Patrols are preset. Starting the game, there will always be a broken down convoy right across the border.BALANCE: Lord, this game needs a balance pass. Some weaons will do piss for damage, while others are able to reach out from the other side of the map with impunity (looking at you missiles). Tanks are incredibly weak to any sort of mech, as all it takes is you bumping into them at speed and they lose all of their actions for the turn, while also taking massive damage. A fix for this would be at least adding in more medium/heavy tanks so not every one is just ram fodder. EQUIPMENT: It's... nonsensical. Same parts of the same rarity and level can have wildly different stats. Things like heavy parts can end up being lighter than so called "light" parts. It feels like borderlands's gun generation is all the worst ways. Combine this with how the UI doesn't always accurately reflect what a part will actually change on the mech, it leads to a more frustrating than fun experience. Also, parts having the paintjob of the mech it came from is neat, but gets obnoxious after a while if you want a consistent paintjobUI: While it works decently, it has a few flaws. For example, you due to the drag and place way waiting works, you cant wait less that .5 seconds, since you end up just clicking on the mech. Certain things that should be shown in the UI like weapon ranges aren't always visible, or how fast enemy missiles will travel.Overall, this game has great potential, but needs some time to get there. If you plan on playing for more than a dozen hours, I wouldn't recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, the first 5 or so hours I had with the game was pretty awesome! The combat felt meaty and impactfull, and it was such a blast planning and directing my mechs. But, this faded extremely fast for me.The positives:- Good graphics and effects- Loved the driving around with my base in overworld, hitting that boost to quickly charge at a base :D- The combat system is very fun and pretty easy to graspThe negatives:- The combat gets veeery repetitive very fast. You do many combats and even though they are over pretty quickly, it's still way too many. In Xcom, for example, even though that also gets repetitive, you get at least some new different aliens and/or new cool tech and gadgets.- The enemy is just me. Since there are no aliens or they don't have some outlandish tech, other than some new weapons, it just feels like I am fighting the same enemies over and over.- The pilots are just a checkbox. A mech needs a pilot, BUT the pilots never seem to get any skills, xp or anything. They are just a boring photo that doesn't bring anything to the table.- You can manufacture mech parts and weapons, but you seem to always get better gear after a fight.- Th AI is just dumb. I can't tell, how many times a sniper mech, with intact weapon, just runs straight past me and then just stand there, or a shotgun mech constantly going backward. Or they run into each other and/or over their own tanks.- I have played for 12h, have taken 3 areas, and not ONCE has the AI attacked my land? Is that not even a thing? I though I was going to have to help my own areas, but so far, no attack has happened.This is all I can think of now. I really wanted to like this game and I did have a blast in the beginning, but with so many games, the interest quickly faded since it feels very very bare bones and not much going on. And is also quickly very repetitive. Hopefully they will make some patches and/or dlc that would add something fun.So if you, unlike me, can stand games that gets repetitive fast then I still think you might have fun with this, but sadly, as it is now, it's not for me :(

_childDocuments_.review: You can play the game play loop in less than 2 hours. Try it before you buy it. SKIP the tutorial. That is the only story this game has and it isn't particularly fun. The combat mission tutorials introduce gameplay mechanics that only exist in that tutorial mission. It teaches you to focus on targeting a building to disable turrets, but that mechanic only works in that 1 mission even though there are many maps with the same building and turrets. Even if it worked it's a terrible tactic. You can destroy a mech or a couple tanks with the firepower needed to destroy the building and you can just stay outside the range of the turrets or in cover. The world map tutorial teaches you how to play the hard way. Taking each province by triggering a conflict, taking key points, and fighting in the battlegrounds to win is just poor instruction. Instead you should just raid the province for it's unique supplies or caches then move to the next province to do the same. Then when your low on supplies or gas just queue up your workshop after scrapping everything then fast travel back to base. This time skips so all your workshop stuff gets done and the provinces escalation drops. Then you trigger the conflict. That is the closest thing to strategy this game has.You will get a false sense of depth and story if you don't SKIP THE TUTORIAL. Simply start a new game. Save. Go back to main menu. Then you should have an option to start past the tutorial. I liked the game, but had to put a lot of my own work into it to make it enjoyable. I had to learn to use the quantum console and mod the game files. There are options that can only change by this method. For example you can increase the amount of units the enemy deploys or the maximum amount of supplies you can hold. The only reason I have double digit play time is because all the testing and troubleshooting. Although the mods made the game enjoyable and rewarding, I just can't recommend it right now at this price. Buy it at half off since it feels like half the game is missing for you to finish.Friendly AI is so bad. Make them eject the first round to save yourself the trouble and turn time. Enemy AI is incapable of handling common tactics like moving to cover and staying out of range. Naturally countering missiles and railguns doesn't happen, trivializing encounters. There are meta builds that are so cheesy like flying light mechs with gattling guns that can move across the map with no weapon cooldown or simply giving everyone railguns. Waiting for a AI mod or game update before I recommend the game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an insanely cool gimmick, in a shiny wrapper, with absolutely no meat to it. The tutorial is the only part that feels like a real game, afterwards all the slick rendered animation and voice acted cutscenes disappear and you get a world map that looks like something out of a free mobile game. The Battles feel great until you've done enough to realize that they all play out exactly the same way, and the strategy never changes. It really feels like they got about 40% of the way to a finished game, really polished up the first hour of gameplay, and then pushed it out into 1.0.tldr; Very cool, totally unfinished, and given the month of silence post 1.0, probably not going to get a lot better. I'll amend my review to a 'yes' if post-launch support turns the game around, but I won't hold my breath.
