name: Robonauts
detailed_description: The beloved game that was originally released only for the Nintendo Switch console is coming to PC gamers now! Learn the story of Robo and help him save the galaxy, alone or together with family and friends. Welcome interplanetary traveler! In a nutshell, Robonauts is that arcade game which includes 12 levels. Each level will challenge you. You will explore a universe which consists nearly 50 planets, facing Bosses and creatures and meeting powerful opponents bent on universal destruction. Who will you be (literally)? Robo is a little robot whose curiosity got the better of him and led to his sudden exit from the confines of his safe environment. Now little Robo is far from home, fighting for his life against a constant barrage of enemies. When developing Robonauts, we chose to give Robo human traits based on our own emotional experience. Robo acts like you and I, and we sense his emotions when has to choose between sides in a battle, trying to figure out who the good guys are. Once you get to know him, it’s hard not to love Robo. Universe! While the game is very dynamic, you get to choose your tempo of gameplay. A lot of troubles await you on every planet. We have tried to fill Robo’s universe with enough graphically various worlds that everyone who plays can find a unique favorite to which they can return. The graphics in this game are truly spellbinding. And the color scheme makes the game enjoyable for both kids and the kid inside every adult who remembers what it was like to spend a day in the arcade. We really wanted to recreate the experience of the best arcade games from our childhood, so to pass a level, you have to jump between mesmerizing planets and destroy every opponent that stands in your way. Really, there are no words to adequately describe the Robonaut universe. Music - the best for last Game soundtrack composer, Simon Viklund. Yes the same Simon Viklund who worked on PAYDAY series and Bionic Commando Rearmed!!! His music exemplifies the very essence of Robonauts – dynamic, retro, arcade-style, energizing. What Simon has created is not only music for our game, but also the perfect soundtrack to your life - if you're just like us, that is. FEATURES: - great for the whole family, - solo and local co-op - local versus mode - 12 unique planetary systems, - large variety of weapons and enemies, - explosive art style and graphics, - epic music composed by Simon Viklund, - easy-to-learn yet challenging gameplay, - 2 difficulty settings: casual and hard.

name: Necromunda: Underhive Wars
detailed_description: Deep below the nightmarish, polluted hive cities of Necromunda, in the twisted, vertiginous, dark tunnels of the Underhive, rival gangs fight to the bitter end for personal power, wealth, survival and the honour of their Houses. Only the strongest survive. Lead, customize, and grow your gangs of Escher, Goliath, and Orlock. Specialize each member and send them to battle in hazardous dystopian environments. Exploit the terrain in tactical gunfights: climb raised walkways to take advantage, set traps, and ambush foes to force them into bloody melee engagements. Learn new skills, loot equipment and bring your evolved gang to 4-player online gang fights. Lead and evolve your gangs in this compelling tactical-RPG Follow a rich narrative campaign in the Underhive Engage in immersive and persistent game modes First video game adaptation from mythical tabletop game Necromunda, the most famous Hive World of Warhammer 40,000 Play solo or join thrilling 4-way online gang fights

_childDocuments_.review: Look, let's be honest.  This is not X-Com or Phoenix Point, it's not what you call a traditional tactical game. It's a digital adaptation of a tabletop miniature game that has been played by hobbyists for 3 decades. Critic reviews are already not liking the game but that's because you can tell they never played the tabletop game. It's a niche game for a niche group.  One review writes:"The gang customization and sandbox mode/operations will be a treat if you’re into that content. However, since it doesn’t tie into the story and knowing that the campaign itself is forgettable, you’re looking at two disconnected modes that could’ve been combined to make the progression and narrative more entertaining. "That's everything that makes Necromunda the game it is! The single player story is fine enough, it serves as a small introduction to a vast wealth of underhive lore and game mechanics.  THE game is the sandbox mode with operations, missions with 2-4 AI/Humans, seeing your team level up, getting new gear from the missions, losing people, getting injuries that give your team members personality, having those crazy stories where your juvie takes out a heavy and steals his gun against all odds.  This game is the mordheim engine with some benefits but it oozes Necromunda.  Do I recommend it to non tabletop Necromunda players?  Probably not, it's not an X-Com game, it's a digital Necromunda for good or bad and I'm loving it.

_childDocuments_.review: Currently after not quite 4 hours I cannot recommend this game. If you want something more engaging in story and mechanics I´d suggest the predecessor Mordheim: City of the Damned.At this point the only praise I have for this game is that the AI seems to be better than inMordheim, but that´s it.I´ll revisit this review and build upon it if something more comes to mind and I remember.Not worth the money,.UPDATE:Not quite six hours in and I´d really would like to refund this game.It´s pretty to look at but then I could just take out my minis instead.Main souces of salt:You have to see all the actions the characters take. It´s like looking at someones vacation video of a walk in some unpictoresque town. And everytime someone does a buff there is an animation. I´d wager that more than half of the game time is taken up by animations that are mindnumbingly annoying after the second time they do them.As in Mordheim, against AI, Never split the group and high ground is key. There is no kind of defensive stance, which is odd for a game that´s built to have both melee and ranged. For ranged you can crouch and try and hide.In the story mode the arena fight against the champion can just go and ♥♥♥♥ off.Stay tuned for my next rage induced outpouring of distain.

_childDocuments_.review: Mordheim with less rats, more guns, and better voice acting.This is an improvement over Mordheim in every way, and there is a lot more polish than I thought there would be at launch. I played and loved classic Necromunda on the tabletop, and I enjoyed Mordheim by this same studio (warts and all), but to be honest I was skeptical that this would be any good. My expectations have been exceeded.I haven't experienced any of the crashes that others have reported. Other than that, there are the usual basic launch day problems/bugs, and there are the usual balance and AI issues you see with games like this. The developer has been super responsive to complaints and feedback on Discord, so it seems like it's getting the support it needs.I truly do not think this game deserves the level of vitriol it's getting here. "Not even beta" and "early access at best"? Get real, get the heck out of here with that. Some people are absolutely raging mad because they have to watch AI turns and plasma doesn't melt a dude's face clean off his skull and House Cawdor isn't flooding the map with cheap units and etc and blah.  I don't want to invalidate anyone's frustration, but maybe put down the friggin' gasoline can for a minute. Yeah, there are some balancing issues and some UI problems, but this is already more than any reasonable Necromunda/40k fan would expect at this price, and it's just going to get better with updates.Cut scenes are incredible, the synthcore bgm is fantastic, movement and combat make so much more sense than in Mordheim, the scenarios are great. It has that same punishing flavor as Mordheim. Necromunda steps up acting like it's gonna hold your hand through a nice long tutorial, but instead it just shoves you into a burning building and runs away laughing. It's got no bugs or balance problems that can't be patched, and the issues that do exist are fully livable until then. If you kinda liked Mordheim but you thought it was a little clunky and wish it had more flamers and boltguns, pick this up and give it a spin.

_childDocuments_.review: Long ramble below, the TL;DR is: If you enjoy the setting and liked Mordheim, you should enjoy this and it will only improve with some patches and future DLC.Long ramble in 3...2...1...So, elephant in the room: The AI. It is derpy and makes mistakes often at the starting operation and then after if you are playing low difficulties. The highest 2 difficulties are MUCH closer to Mordheim level of aggression and play.Something odd about the early difficulties AI isn't even how they derp about the map, ignore what seem prime targets or accidentally gas themselves and co-workers. It is outside of the battles - if you get a strong start, wipe the whole team and ensure you pillage EVERY weapon they are holding then most likely, they will not buy replacements and you will be fighting what equates to a fist-toting scavenger party for the rest of that operation - they will just go to grab the items and Extract! I felt bad enough when the objective was to kill each other and/or extraction was banned (even more so when I raided their HQ) and they could only thump their puny fists and feet against my armour-clad murder-machines as I wiped them by the end of round 2.Other complaints I have seen have been about the long time-to-kill and seemingly wet-noodle attacks. This is ONLY in the beginning when you are using the beginner (Tier1) items and armours. Time To Kill will be much closer to table-top by the time you are using/facing Tier3 across the board and every play/mistake will result in someone dying (unless a tanky Brawler) when Tier5 is the majority.The maps are cool and have plenty of opportunity for playing different styles - especially if you play to the House strengths.The gang development, levelling and ranking up is superior to Mordheim, it has evolved and improved. The visuals are a massive step-up too.♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ that could benefit from patching:No dodging animation - you can avoid the damage but the visual will still have you taking a heavy/bladed/cutty thing to the face and a blood-splatter.Glitches for collecting items for objectives - it is infrequent and tends to only affect 1 of your gang at a time. Annoying but not enough to make me spew bile and shoot fire from my fingers.Disconnects - I have had one disconnect, but have spoken with a lot of people playing that have not been so fortunate. I logged back in and it had autosaved the turn before, no great loss.Ambush/Overwatch tuning - Ambush is terribly unreliable in current iteration - overwatch triggers when they move more than a few steps within your engagement bubble, works better.Final thoughts - once your gang is established (Tier4 with some Tier5s and at least rank 8 on everyone) then this game really starts to shine and require planning, forethought and a little luck. I personally enjoy the early stages when building a gang, but can see why some enjoy it less whilst they are impatient for the 'true' sense of the game. I just hope we don't have to wait too long for the next gangs - I imagine I will do 2-3 iterations of each House gang we have now before I start feeling desperate for new stuff :)

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay is nice, a little balancing here and there might be required, but else good.There's quite a lot of bugs, but lets just hope they get fixed asap.HOWEVER, the story is boring, you get fixed characters to play with, meaning there's no way to specialise, and there's no difficulty option, in case you're having a hard time, and you swap between the gangs too much (I've only reached story mission 5, but have already swapped gang once and get's fustrated with the lack of abilities, after having played operations).OPERATIONS and MULTIPLAYER is where the games strengths are, you customise your own gang, train them up, give them the abilities YOU want, and see them grow and get hurt, and maybe even see your hard work disapear, because they can also die, making it feel much MUCH more personal.I would've personally prefered if the story was instead done with YOUR OWN gangs, so you could train and prepare between missions (to balance it, you could simply not get any rewards, but in return, you should not lose anything if failing).While operations are the better part, it still needs working, more diffrent types of missions, more options here and there, and more different gear would be more than welcome.So in short, story missions sucks (can't speak for the story STORY, yet)Oerations and multiplayer is the best partSome gameplay needs to be balanced a bitBugs needs to be fixedAnd more content is not just welcome, but needed.At the moment, it's not worth full price.

_childDocuments_.review: I was really enjoying this game. It suffers from a lot of the jankiness that Mordheim (dev's previous title) had and it is obvious they didn't learn enough lessons from that game's shortcomings this time around. But I was having fun nether-the-less. It is addictive to theory-craft the different possible gang builds and having fond memories of the tabletop version from ages past doesn't hurt either.However, there are a lot of bugs. Some make the SP campaign pretty much unplayable. But it's levelling up your own gang and building something formidable to troll your friends with that appeals, so i could look past them mostly. But then I was hit with the reset infamy bug. You acquire infamy points for making certain in-game (not steam) achievements that give you points to spend on operations even when switching to a new gang. It's the main draw for levelling up lots of gangs and gives you something for all the hours you've put in when starting again which adds a lot to the replay-ability.So, having lost all the infamy points I'd accrued over my 125+ hours of playing has pretty much been the last straw for me.

_childDocuments_.review: So lets start with the good.This is not a bad stab at bringing the new table top version of Necromunda to the PC - however that is part of the origin of some of its short comings.Graphically it looks ok, with some well thought through arenas and solid character work and some good environmental, lighting and effects work.The mehIts slow, this is very much not a fast play!Progression mechanics don't 'feel' that meaningful especially in terms of equipment.The world feels empty - if the various cut scene's didn't point out that a hive world is meant to be teaming with humanity you'd be forgiven for thinking that the gangs are few and sparse. There are some level design touches that try to give the impression of some level of inhabitedness (and some concept art in loading screens) but it dosn't really got that far and dosn't sell that the place is anything but abandoned.Weapons are  mostly flavour with little to pick between them.Gang size being limited to 5 is probably due to the way the new tabletop game works, in the original one of the choices that you had was to go tall or wide in terms of gang composition. In this iteration you take 5 gangers, due to the action economy if you -do not- have 5 gangers you will get squished easily as there isn't reeeeallly the ability to go Tall with abilities or kit. Every gang is basically a box. The gang hide out / operations mechanic is meh - its a real shame. The bad:As others have commented the AI is as thick as a plank making really dumb choices - but not in a dumb person way, in an inexplicable broken way. For example you will see Brawlers ignore opponents -right next to them- in favour of running around the map and spamming various other abilities (other than strike). It is cripplingly dumb. TBH its probably trying to do something complicated but this is not working in terms of gameplay. It would be signficantly better to acctually have a much simpler set of AI routines that at least would not be so painfully thick. Or if the developer wanted to do something interesting open it up to the community?Its buggy, mostly with crashes back to desktop, There are some weird graphical glitches (vibrating camera due to environment intersections) and wacky physics. Its a real shame as the IP is interesting and the developers obviously are talented, as it is -ok- . But it could have been something special.If you liked their previous titles and/or the new table top game you'll probably get on with this, if not maybe avoid for the moment or pickup in a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Underhive Wars

_childDocuments_.review: Having played 2 hours again last night after the initial disappointment  upon release of the game, which was initially bug-ridden, unstable, and painfully slow, I enjoyed playing last night.  Perhaps this is premature, but it seems to me that many of the problems have now been fixed, and given the continued investment in the game by the developer, I'm hopeful for the future.  I do think, however, that this game should not have been released in the initial form, and can only think that the developers were in desperate need of cash.  That's not an excuse, but might provide an explanation.  I hope that they are being sufficiently compensated, but do feel that they should give something back to the original community in the way of a free dlc or something.  More free levels, a gang, more story plot etc.

_childDocuments_.review: How to review a game without being a fanboy? well let's try to consider the facts, this game wants to be a turn based strategy game with HQ and Teams progression system based on loot, skills, stats and scavenging.As a strategy game turn based it uses a fluid movement system ,that means you move freely by X meters depending on how proficient the character you're moving is, and you have a pool of 2 different meters to perform actions and tactical skills.So far so good yes? Well the problem is that, despite the depth in every single aspect of the system on paper, the gameplay is atrociously bad.Why is that? Well because they made a dumbed version of a TT game, that doesn't even feel like a PC strategy game because everything has to be dumbed down to a point it makes every system absolutely irrelevant.You see in Mordheim you had a way to perform zone control and crowd control, and this thanks to the fact that characters moving in an influence area of an enemy would get stuck in melee combat, if they were to disengage their offensive and movement capabilities would have been debuffed if not totally removed in favour of a retreat (same thing as in TT BT♥♥♥♥INGWAY) and so on. Here? Here not so much, you can retreat, do whatever you want, creating a mess on the battlefield that AI makes a great job in highlighting. There's no unit coesion as everyone runs freely with no sense of positioning, that is caused also by the IDIOTIC decision to field 5 characters at a time in a game that, being insipired from the TT, requires at least a minimum of 10 per team to have a decent strategy, tactic, and overall experience. This decision also insanely increases the health of every character making it more like a deathmatch style of game were cahracters run here and there and take 3000 shots or nades or whatever to die. The game features a campaign that has the sole purpose to be a tutorial for the totally unexperienced, you might dig it Idk, but all these features of management and customization of your crew are obviously absent, it's just a chain of standard mission and overpriced cinematics that could have been scrapped entirely with a good basic tutorial, saving time and avoiding paying somebody to write you a lame story. But HEY! _childDocuments_.review: I will give this a precarious thumbs up.With not much experience in the War Hammer franchise I cannot really comment on the lore or be an authority of judgement on that matter.What i can say is its fairly neat.One of the slowest turn based games I've played but the fidelity of the graphics and scenery holds it together and sometimes can feel cinematic.With that being said, its ruined by a rough handled AI that enjoys colliding with what ever is in its way for a bit leading to very long play sessions. This happens often enough to be an issue.Atop this the camera will jut around scenery, instead of through it, making it a rather jarring experience.The minute to minute game play is dragged on by a lot of this.But you can customize your crew, which is also a very slow process. I would not call it deep, however, there are tons of character builds to play with. There is noticeable progression in perks and weapons and it flows rather well from a design a game play point of view. There is also limited character customization. You can paint your gear and change your outfits and what the crew looks like. There's just not a whole lot of it.I do not have the DLC and cannot comment on it. Other than its already in the game, you are paying to unlock it...There are interesting dynamics to the combat system itself. I personally love the grappling hook abilities that add nice mobility to the game. Though its big dumb you cant drag people off ledges. _childDocuments_.review: Thanks for the game, I'm sorry it didnt do better. Recommend.Back to my first 5 hours review:Infinite Vertical Movement: I get it. I still disagree with it. However, the movement system creates new tactical dilemmas: force your opponent to expose themselves to get a clean shot etc. If youre higher than your opponent, advantage is huge. And there are options to control  movement, sabotage the lifts or zip wires and you can have very firm control of the high ground.Indistinct Abilities:The abilities are small bonuses who's benefits arent immediately apparent, but persevere: they are better than they appear. Unfortunately there are also simply trash skills.Which brings me to consumables...oh my what a sh*t show. 1: Sort option? Please? After a few hours your stash is packed with crap with no way to sort them.2: Levelled items, you can have each item in 5 different levels, that dont stack, and do nearly the exact same thing. And I get it 5HP can make the difference...but there are better ways to handle it. Have them scale to gang rating, have the med facility upgrade them?  3: Random. Theres a gang focused on consumables (Escher)and acquiring consumables  is random? Orlocks arent randomly out of ammo, Goliaths dont have random moments of weakness. So..?Awful Campaign:No change. Its a travesty that the game was released with this terrible excuse of an introduction to the game.Bugs:99% squashed!Good:See 5 hour review, all unchanged: I cant wait for the first expansion. (slated for December..? :fingers crossed:)- The game's mechanics have some lovely synergies, Anoint Armaments and Plasma weapons, Iron Will and the Gravely wounded skill that gives even more hit resistance, etc The depth is really confusing at first but really worth thinking over and is a true highlight...spoiled only slightly by the fact that the good skills completely eclypse the bad ones, limiting your choices, although there are still excellent choices!Finally I have to mention the AI. Its not great. BUT.With the level design and scope of abilities and options I am not surpri the AI is lacking, its choices are vast, and making a system able to comprehend them and evaluate them property is a momentous task. Other games have managed but I have some sympathy here: in creating an environment in which two players can play against each other with the maximum of options they have stuffed up their AI. A choice I would have made also. I  hope this gets fixed and more solo and coop options are added. Id love to see Operations with/against other players.Probably my last update here, the game is excellent, buy it, even full price is a bargain. The scope means you'll need patience, or enjoy it with friends where the AI plays no role. Because the core of the game is astoundingly good. Recommend.I started playing hesitantly, on a family library, because of the mixed reviews.I followed the game's guidance: campaign first "to learn the game".What a horrible mistake! Its supposed to teach you the game, what it does instead is cut out every fun element of Necromunda: gang development, controlling the growth of your gang, learning how best to use abilities, acquiring gear, and being able to be proud of your heavy plasma gun that you stole from some scum-sucking Orlock.Instead the tutorial is a random series of spiritless encounters with gangs that change so often that you cant possibly give a monkeys about because you could well be trying to kill them next match. You have no control of their development or the abilities they have, and you cant get used to using any abilities as next game you wont have them any longer.Once you get into the campaign mode its a delight, everything you would expect from a modern AAA and from Necromunda, developing your gangs and kitting them out with armour pieces and weapons to be proud of, the right Stims to make them monsters of combat, and learning how best to use their abilities you chose.At this point the true drawbacks to the game are pretty much exclusive to the AI. Which can have moments of genius: laying mines in choke-points, and then setting overwatch over that point. But it can also have moment of chronic stupidity: walking into boxes, throwing grenades at walls or just failure to path. Most heinously it has no idea how to deal with destructible walls. I hesitantly recommend. - Infinite vertical movement. This makes it movement wildly unintuitive and the AI has a natural advantage in using it due to superior 3D comprehension. It means the AI can move seemingly infinitely far, eliminating most strategy in placing your people, because the AI can just get above your cover anyway and knows exactly how to do it. Cover :is: strategy in TT Necromunda, not only should it have a greater effect it should be harder to bypass, which isn't achievable with infinite vertical movement. It also makes the AP cost for using zip lines redundant in some maps as walking around to get up there is free, it just takes longer. Which is dull, and unrewarding when you could be zipping about, which is cool!- Abilities are numerous and not individual enough. eg I don't want 8 healing variations with slightly varied other spam on them. 1 is fine, maybe 2 if you can make them distinctive enough. - The campaign is awful. Not because of the story or because of game-play but because it fails heinously as a tutorial. See Above.- Zero control over progression in campaign. Because you cant shape your gang(s) you have zero pride in your them, and even less understanding of abilities that change often. See Above.- No rewards. Collect some gear in a mission? Its gone when you end the mission. Turn based without rewards is not a winning formula. At least have loot carry over!- The map is a work of art! Understanding your position is simply pressing M. Mouse wheel to scroll through layers. Excellently done.- Bugs & Devs. Largely cleared up, (tho some obscure conflicts remain) so prompt work by the devs gives huge kudos in my mind. The AI needs work, but isn't nearly as bad as some claim.- Combat is good. It feels gritty, damage is certain, teamwork is core. You feel the need to plan and the excellent map enables it nicely, there are clear objectives. And rewards for completing them (whilst on the map) such as no more reinforcements or valuable healing items.- Great level design. The maps are intricate but easy to navigate, the multiple levels add a great deal of interest, combined with destructible bridges, and zip-lines, placeable terrain and traps, simply outstanding!- Beautiful. Graphics are great, awesome atmosphere, really does the maps justice. Gangs and weapons are distinctive detailed.- I found difficulty well balanced, always peril without feeling overwhelmed all of the time. You can loose at times. I am still in the campaign, so I hope it continues into building my gang. - The potential. DLC gangs would be amazing, new tiles sets? Possibilities are huge.

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game, as I am a huge fan of all things 40k, however there are some issues in dire need of fixing. I am honestly not sure how these kinds of issues get through testing, because quite frankly, they're annoying and no one likes to be annoyed by something thats suppose to be fun. My biggest gripe with this is the rather bad ai pathfinding. I played a single mission for nearly an hour due to the ai fighters walking into junk piles or walls and just ending their turn there after trying to walk through the object for a minute straight. That or they'll walk their full move range and then backtrack to go somewhere else and you get to watch this all for each enemy character. Another thing I felt needed work and maybe this is just me, but I feel like the ai gangs prioritize the player even when there is a third gang on the field. I often get to watch as an enemy gang walks right through another enemy gang just to repeatedly attack my characters. During one operation, which is a series of missions, I managed to strip one enemy gang of weapons so they'd show up with just fists as weapons. Kinda funny to watch at first until you realize they get 3-5 attacks that deal 4-15 damage, which can end up being about the same damage as one swing from a 2 handed weapon. Personally I don't feel like that its logical to be able to beat a character who has a big ol axe with bare fists but that's just me. One final problem I've noticed, slightly less annoying than the others, is the seeming lack of penalties for disengaging. I have managed to get an enemy to low health only for them to disengage, turn their back on my fighter, and proceed to use the med station to heal most of their health back, with no real penalty for having done so.While it does have its issues, overall I am enjoying Necromunda. There is a fair bit of variety in weaponry and colors to customize your gang. While some additional clothing and hairstyles would be nice I feel there is a decent amount of visual customization for a game of this type. Map design is great, with multiple floors and an atmosphere that really goes well with what I'd expect from a gang heavy environment. After nearly 12 hours playtime I haven't noticed any real repetitiveness in map design. I have a fair bit of playtime in Mordheim and one thing that always bugged me was how easy it was to have characters die or be injured to near uselessness. I felt it was difficult to easily replace a veteran in the later game, (Although i was never very good at mordheim) however with Necromunda it seems more forgiving with the injuries and I haven't had a character die at all. Although not sure if they can actually die, but I try to keep my characters alive as much as possible because I'm sentimental or something.TLDR: Good game for 40k fans, with some issues needing fixed but nothing overly game breaking, that I have seen, with nearly 12 hours play time.

_childDocuments_.review: Before you even consider buying this game, you need to realize that it is NOT based on Necromunda: The Game, it is based on Necromunda: The Books. This game does not play anything like the cult classic miniatures game, and instead plays like their previous game Mordhiem with sci fi skins. Besides the name for weapons and gangs, there's pretty much nothing actually from Necromunda in here, not even the gangs themselves; every gang behaves exactly the same, but has six unique traits only they can equip. This of course is a far cry from how Necromunda actually works, where every gang is supposed to have strengths and weaknesses. In this game, you have have an active team of four not-leaders and a leader; each of which has an arbitrary class that locks specific weapons to them. Brawlers can use the good melee weapons, heavies get big guns, etc and it's just screams of laziness. While brawlers kind of automatically win melee combat, there is a problem in that division to: This game runs off of percentile, and only borrows mechanics from Necromunda rather than actually implement the Necromunda rules. So if you try to play this game as a Necromunda fan, you are going to just be pulling your hair out screaming "How could they screw this up!?" So gangs don't have agency, gangers have arbitrary classes, and the only game mode is stealing carried objects. There are several creatures and factions depicted in the games art, none of which actually shows up in this game. The Palantine Enforcers are in several artworks, and don't seem to actually appear in game. And this kind of moves onto my big, final point about this game: It's clearly meant to invite Necromunda players, but is a total bait and switch. Entertain me on this thought experiment, okay? Every now and then one or two people go into the forums and defend this game, saying that this is not meant to be sold to Necromunda players, but is actually intended to get new people into Necromunda. We, as fans of the series, are the ones to blame for expecting a licensed game to be true to it's license. Here's the big problem with that, this game outright disobeys how the actual game works. If I tried to show people this game, and then get them to play the real Necromunda, they would be thrown for a total loop. It's kind of like how somebody tried to tell me once that Warhammer games are not marketed towards Warhammer players (they are)I bought this game when it was 60% off in order to really figure out how bad this trashfire is, and it's bad.... if you approach it while judging it as a Warhammer game. If this was just some generic Sci Fi punk game, it honestly would not be that half bad. BUT, sorry, the geniuses that made this game used a Warhammer license so if it's nothing like the licensed game, it's just not worth playing. For some reason, developers keep buying Warhammer licenses and making generic strategy games in the hopes that another total Warhammer will happen.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't normally review games but I thought Necromunda deserved a thumbs up from me after the hours of fun I've had with it. I've been a Necromunda fan since the first TT edition came out back in 1995, and I picked it back up again when it was re-made in 2017. This game is a fine representation of three of the six great houses engaging in turn-based objective-centric skirmishes. Please note that I haven't tried the multiplayer yet, so this is from the perspective of single player content only.This is not a 1:1 digitisation of the TT game, but rather has it's own ruleset. I see the wisdom in this, because the digital format allows for more complex abilities and background calculations to occur. There are many more skills and abilities and lots of factors weighed in to every shot. However, until you understand these systems the game can feel a little arbitrary or off balance at times, and I think there is still work to be done to perfect these new systems.Plus points:- Graphics are great- Lots of customisation- Sound is good (although the Lascannon could do with a little more oomph)- Level design and traversal is great- Turn based battles- Good stability, I've only had one CTD (ymmv - some forum users and reviewers claim the game is broken beyond repair)Negative points:- AI behaviour can be very odd/broken at times, making many scenarios easier than intended- Weapons feel too homogeneous. A plasma gun should be a substantial upgrade from a lasgun, but there is little apparent difference in damage output- Poor voice acting in the single player campaign. The guilder does a good job but the gang leaders leave something to be desiredOverall, if you're a fan of Necromunda or turn based games, I would recommend this, particularly since it is at a budget price point. It is far from perfect and needs work to balance the different classes and weapons. I'd also like to see some DLC support for the missing three great houses.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm so sad not to be able to recommend this, as were it not for the ridiculously silly AI the game could be *fantastic*.  The graphics are great, gang customisation extensive enough that they really feel like *your* gang, maps and missions are interesting (they do run out after a while, but that's true of almost every base game of this type), and the gameplay is satisfying, with even that touch of silliness that brings memorable moments I recall from playing tabletop Necromunda (e.g. skilling characters so they can do crazy movement around the map and take out a 'safe' opponent from behind).  But the AI is so awful that there is no challenge to the game, and it really hurts the immersive, role-playing experience.  I get that no AI will be truly like a human opponent, and tend to be predictable, but many games still manage to make them act broadly sensibly.  In Underhive Wars, they regularly use their movement to jump off a platform then action points to zip-line back to their starting point, for no apparent reason.  They move close to a target and then throw a grenade so they hit themselves/their allies rather than simply doing it from further back.  It's neither a fun contest nor a thematic, role-playing experience, which the game could otherwise offer so well.  Yes, you can ramp up the difficulty to give them skewed advantages to try and present a challenge, but it then becomes about gaming the system and exploiting the stupidity.  Like fighting an idiotic giant who swings around randomly and occasionally clubs themself in the face, rather than a balanced battle between rival gangs.  Or like playing tabletop with my 6yo who wants to randomly run around then make things go "boom".  In other games you can make it an interesting contest by giving the AI some minor advantages to make up for the limitations of programming, but in this game the AI is just too silly for this to work.Sadly, I reached a stage fairly quickly where the AI's craziness outweighed the fun immersion of playing and developing my gang.  If the AI gets improved I'd jump at playing this again, and I'd happily buy whatever DLC was required if it truly fixed it, as I love tabletop Necromunda and the rest of the experience is so well done.  But every time I get drawn in by this to give it another go, I quickly realise why I stopped playing.

_childDocuments_.review: Before buying and playing this title, I have to admit that I was really put off by the negative reviews - here on Steam. Then I got it dirt cheap on a sale and still had a bit of anxiety trying it.While I've waited for the download to complete, I dug deeper in the reviews and I have to say this: many people complain about the bad UI and difficulty/stability (yes, it has a bad UI, something that feels to be ported directly from consoles - but still pretty functional). The difficulty doesn't feel neither too hard, nor too easy. At least in the Story mode. Ofc, this may come and bite me in the ass along the way - but so far (having played 4 missions) - it seems pretty reasonable. Yes - there is no way of choosing the difficulty mode, but that is not an issue.I've seen reports of having bad AI. Well, what can I say: I wasn't expecting much - but so far, I haven't seen enemies running in front of a wall and hanging there. You shoot them, they shoot back or run and shoot back. Pretty standard AI for this type of game. The ranged classes seem that always try too keep their distance. At least in the Story mode.Stability wise, I had no real issues. Sure, there is the occasional camera glitch here and there - and sometimes the reflections/textures glitch while moving the camera fast (in the tactical mode), but nothing to really bother you. I've played Gothic 1 back in the day and this is nothing to that glitchiness. No crashes so far as well. I'll update this review if that happens. And c'mon - this is not a AAA game. Remember Cyberpunk at release? This is nowhere near that.Lore wise, you ask? I have no idea. I'm a fan of the 40k universe, but my interest was more along the lines of the Black Library books and DoW games. Probably the 5 factions available (3 default and 2 DLC gangs - all playable in the Operations/Skirmish mode) are not exactly 100% accurate, but honestly? It doesn't bother me that much. The mechanics are fun and there seems to be a decent learning curve - as long as you play the Story first. Even the game tells you that: "play the story first".Mechanics are plenty. And even though the UI is not the most uncluttered out there - it's still serviceable. With a bit of practice, you'll learn what you need by playing it, mostly. The rest is flavor.Sadly, the MP is dead. I guess the bad press took care of that. I would have loved playing vs. some human opponents.From what I've seen around the web - the launch was a mess. Might have been. But this was years ago. While not really updated since 2021 - One more thing: I've seen people comparing it to Mordheim. This is not that either. It's an entirely different game, made by the same company - using a bit of a similar gameplay. But don't get this if you are expecting a game like their first title.PS: It also has cool cinematics that really give flavor to the action. This is definitely an uncut gem for the 40k fans out there ;) .

_childDocuments_.review: I'll get this out of the way right now. Necromunda: Underhive Wars is the type of game which will be great in two years. Does this mean that I think the game isn't worth playing now? No, it is worth playing! Just be aware that Necromunda: Underhive Wars captures the Your Dudes aspect of GW's Specialist Games about as well as one can expect of a video game. If you're going into this game and not taking the time to come up with a little story for your guys, then you're missing the point of Necromunda.Yes, Necromunda: Underhive Wars is full of jank, moreso than one would expect on a game at launch. Yes, there are only three gangs out of the eight in the newest edition of Necromunda.No, that isn't the point. The point is watching Queen, my Orlock Lay-Tech showing the Esher gang leader who I've fought shift after shift exactly what happens when someone steps onto my turf. It's watching my merry bomb throwing Juvie Tiffany Trio hock three of her homemade grenades at two Goliath thugs, teaching them the meaning of spacing. It's watching Ace pick off enemies after crossing the entirety of the map by jumping down and leaping up from building to building like it's Assassin's Creed.If you want to suspend your disbelief and enjoy watching Your Dudes grow through success and failure, then enjoy. If not, then check this again in a year or two.

_childDocuments_.review: Solid 4/10The worst AI I've ever seen in a published game.  Makes the AI from Mordheim look like Einstein.  Eg. one of the five classes, the Saboteur, only ever runs around like a headless chicken throwing grenades at itself.  WTF.  It makes you watch ridiculous "YOUR TURN" "ENEMY TURN" animations every time you switch characters.  Every single action, including crouching, has lengthy animations, effects, and cinematic pauses baked in.  95% of my playtime is spent tabbed out while the AI circles the map, gets stuck on every corner and object, while randomly spamming all its abilities, only to go right back to where it started.The mechanics, skills, unit variety have all been dumbed down.  It's a leap backwards from Mordheim in every aspect.  Especially the movement system.  How do you go from a sensible, logical pathing method, to this trainwreck that gives unlimited vertical movement, that lets units run unlimited circles around terrain, that lets you run into your opponent's spawn in the first or second turn?  Why have all the classes transformed into Usain Bolts, with no movement differences between them?Building gangs is fun.  The art department is on point. But this has no business being a full release.  It's an early-access pre-alpha demo at best.

_childDocuments_.review: Overview: A fun but flawed game. Quite a few rough edges that need to be fixed, and a lot of content I'd like to see added, but Necromunda is a solid gang-builder with enough customization, skills, and satisfying gameplay to keep me playing. I'll absolutely pick it up again when there are some improvements and DLC.Reasons why you should play this game:- You enjoy building a team, upgrading them, finding fun skill and weapon combos, and then unleashing them on your enemies.- You really like the 40k universe and enjoy seeing the weapons, environments, and characters brought to life.- You don't mind repetitive gameplay.Reasons why you should not play this game:- Bugs, glitches, and exploits are dealbreakers.- You require competent AI to feel challenged.- You really, really, really liked XCOM and this looks similar.- You hate repetitive gameplay.The good:- Graphics are solid.- Level design is pretty good, with a lot of vertical movement and fun ways to get around the map.- A variety of weapons, with enough differences that you might build a character and a team specifically around different types. - Advancement actually feels really solid, with stat upgrades giving you an excellent overview of *precisely* how they will help, and many skills being a lot of fun to use.- The interface is pretty quick and intuitive, with your movement and action points feeling pretty sensible in terms of how they're used to interact with the world around you.- In Operations, it's an absurd amount of fun to loot all the weapons off your dead enemies, and watch as the gang becomes more and more impoverished over the course of an "arc." Eventually, they'll be coming at you with little more than fists and whatever they could buy off a trader, while you brandish all their old gear. And laugh maniacally.- Autosave is magnificent, allowing me to get right back into the action even with CTDs.The bad:- There are some serious bugs at the moment. I've had more than a few CTDs, and part of the advancement system for your custom gangs is broken.- For some reason, you need to complete the story mode before you can unlock all the customization options for your custom gangs.- The aforementioned story mode isn't great. It's not bad, but it's not great, with widely-varying difficulty and a pretty uninspired plot. It also goes on for way too long.- Weapons are not all created equal. Deadeye, for example, gets access to a perk that grants Action Points for scoring a critical hit. Critical hits are on a per-round basis, so weapons that fire more rounds (the autogun) are much, much easier to score crits with than a single-fire weapon (the lasgun, plasma rifle, etc). The amount of bonus action points is enough that you can fire again. Firing twice, even with a slightly inferior weapon, is the significantly better option. Hence, even with many fun options, I have never used anything but the autogun on my Deadeye.- Some skills are very underwhelming. Charge, which ostensibly allows you to melee attack an enemy without triggering Overwatch, has an oddly specific range of 8-20 meters. This means that if someone goes into overwatch too close to you, you can't use it. Too far away, and you can't use it. If they have a ranged weapon, they shoot you as soon as they can see you move, but charge requires a VERY clear path to hit them. I tried to love charge. It does not love me. The ugly:- The AI is broken. Period. It works okay when you're just fighting each other, but throw in objectives and it has no idea what to do. I've watched six gangers from two different gangs share a tiny platform, caught in a loop of buffing their teammate and raising a flag, without ever actually attacking. I've watched melee fighters run up, take overwatch, then change their mind and run away. They put a huge priority on buffs and item use, and actually fighting is secondary.- Movement Points make zero sense with the vertical layout, as movement is calculated by drawing a big circle around your character, as opposed to how many STEPS you've taken. This may seem like a small thing, but it's very frustrating to watch the AI run up 10 flights of stairs, zipline over to an objective, grab it, jump down, and then run halfway across the map to an extraction point. - There isn't much mission variety. The custom gang Operations are all centered around simple objective grabbers, which typically turns into whether you can set yourself up in such a way as to pulp the enemy before they use said terrible movement system to steal the objectives out from under your noise and run to the extraction point, laughing and pushing each other into the bushes.- Once all the enemy gangers are dead, you immediately enter the "looting round." This is your only opportunity to grab both loot from the enemy, and any objectives left on the map. So what if you killed all 15 opponents in 2 out of 6 rounds and control the field of battle? You gotta be HOLDING those batteries, missy, otherwise it's no points for you.That's all I got. For me, the positives outweighed the negatives - building up my own gang, turning them into broken killing machines, and slowly stripping all my competitors of their weapons while moving up in the world kept me going for a good long time. It's not a great game, but it's a fun one.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR I expected Mordheim in future - I got DisappointmentWot I liked- Well made GUI: you can get most information which you need. It has its own quite unique stylisation and control scheme, but once you get used to it, it's quite friendly;- You can use space in character names! For some reason most games don't allow you to do it;- Operation seems to be the main game mode (skirmish is a random combat arena): you're set out at a part of Necromunda and has to carry out several missions to vie for resources with 2 competitor houses - all missions are eliminate or extract with the cargo;- Infamy points system provides your current operation with 2 facilities (chosen from 4) and 12 buffs (chosen from about 30). In order to increase your Infamy you need to complete various tasks in-game;- There are 6 classes with slightly different roles. The leader variant of the class provides access to leader skills;- There are 8(9) items slots: 3 implants, body armour, arms, legs, weapons. Each class has its own version of equipment;- You can choose 5 passive skills (chosen from about 24) and 5 active skills (chosen from about 24). Each House has some unique(ish) skills;- Enjoy crawling in the biggest city in the universe's underbelly;- Third person tactical turn based game;- Very impressive and useful 3d map;- An interesting Mordheim redux;- Pretty loading screens.Wot I disliked- Very few of everything;- Maps are dead. The textures look fine (just fine, definitely no eye-candies for 2020), however there are but none interactive elements: ziplines, lifts, trap spots, barricades, gangplanks, healing stations and chests. Of course there are no destructible environments;- Environmental hazards, pick-ups, traps or barricades are ineffective and are never used by AI (or you) and are largely unimportant and affect nothing;- The game’s visuals are very PG-13: no gore, no wounds, no gory finishers, hardly any blood (hardly any animations to be honest);- Houses are basically the same with very minor difference in visuals, weapons and skills. Two houses are given as paid DLCs — you’re paying for dozen skills and skins;- Campaign (I think 90% of players will start and end Necromunda experience with it) is hot garbage:  you cannot change the composition of your team, you cannot change the loadout of your team, you cannot back one house and have to play for all of them, the list goes on and on;- Operations are quite grindy: it would take you quite some time to get your team to max level. Party members can get injured, which can make them basically useless, meaning that you have to start over;- Crashes, bugs, glitches i.e. some skills and mechanics not working (melee cannot destroy barricades, ambushes failing), dumb AI, etc...To sum it all up, I expected Mordheim in future but got a severely limited and handicap copycat. The campaign is so awful I could not finish it and dropped after mission 6. Operations is a much better and fun mode yet still a limited game.

_childDocuments_.review: The only thing this game has got going for it is its visuals which perfectly captured the aesthetic of 40k and Necromunda. As a game itself, it is a buggy, feature starved, poorly written/voice acted mess of a game that should have remained in development for at least another year. It was a barely functional alpha when officially "released" and had horrendous AI. The game was in such a bad state that the multiplayer was dead on arrival after just one week. The singleplayer "story" revolves around the three core gangs rushing to be the first to uncover a powerful relic - which is never revealed or explained why it is so important. It's just a macguffin to tie the three gangs to the same location. The story jumps every couple of missions between gangs and serves more as a tutorial than an actual narrative campaign. Worst of all is that you cannot level up, customize, or even edit the loadout of your gangers. Combined with the point of view switching every few missions to a different gang leaves the player completely detached and unable to identify or care about their warband.All in all there is not much here. The singleplayer is a glorified tutorial, the multiplayer is dead. The only thing worth playing is Operations mode - a kind of repeatable string of missions where you can play against the AI. It was supposed to be like an endless campaign you could play but it was poorly done and is boring and repetitive. Combined with the terrible AI Operations mode sounds great on paper but is dull and very shallow much like the rest of this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I played the Table-top game when it came out briefly, but was put off due to the intensity of sweaty nerds. I did  however very much enjoy it, and understood why people had such passion for the game then. A lot of people gave this game bad reviews, and to be fair, there are a few things that concern me. Like, for example, certain skills not working (Hydraulic Slam, why won't you work?), is the main culprit for me not giving this a greater review than it should get.That being said, the game is really good fun, but perhaps not for those who are in the min-max mindset. I enjoy it thoroughly however, and will continue to support the developers through the bad times until it gets to the level at which Mordheim has reached. Patience is key, and its not like the game was overpriced anyways. It needs more time to cook in the oven, but it's still deliciously tasty and addictive. Most people who hate the game have also clocked hundreds of hours playing it, and are simply frustrated at the current state of the game. Give it time and it could be a masterpiece, but it's still quite a gem even at this stage.

_childDocuments_.review: I was put off from picking this game up even though the concept intrigued me by the negative reviews, but I haven't seen anything during my playing to make my opinion negative. I'm guessing this got some updates ever since its infamous early days because this game ran fine!It looks nifty. There's a lot of personality in the storymode and you can play individual gangs you can customize after you're done with the story so there's a lot of gameplay here. This is a game that takes patience. Each turn is a series of strategic decisions, and the enemy will try to out maneuver you. There's quite a bit of interaction in the world based on different classes like some that set traps and some that sabotage the environment. I've experienced a couple glitches (very minor visual hitches) but nothing game breaking. I get the feeling people were expecting something other than a faithful adaptation of a slower paced board game with lots of options. If you don't mind micromanaging and love the lore of this little seen aspect of Warhammer this is an excellent game.

_childDocuments_.review: Rogue Factor returns with an ambitious Necromunda: Under hive Wars. I finally got a first look at this follow up to the cult classic Mordheim. Some things I was impressed with and boy some work needs to be done. I will keep it short and sweet.What I liked:Cinema-tics: The Real Engine was a nice choice for the animated sequences and story mode. This table top translation has some passion to its scope and presentation that bring it to life.  So far so good.Tactical Warfare: Whether console, keyboard or controller. There is a lot of little nuances you like. Its clear and precise to the attributes and skill choices.Third Person: Still the best presentation of table tops and turn base mechanics instead of the old isometric that forces you up close and into the action. Still love it.Improving Modeling: An improvement in the customization and models from the Unity Mordheim that made the looks of the character more aesthetically pleasing.Music: Not a bad sound track that fits Necromunda's universe.What needs to get better:AI issues: The same stuck characters, coding and bug issues that plagued Mordheim, are even more profound in Necro, which was disappointing. Incomplete: Despite the great setting. Barely any of its needed as you play within a very confine space. Do not ask me to go up and down an elevator again. Tedious: Unlike Mordheim where you had large warbands to control that made tactical play more enticing. Here it is slow and redundant.  Small parties just don't have the same power as watching one character surrounded by 4 in Mordheim. PVP: Tables tops are pvp, but in game its disregarded because of the solo game play. If this was 1 v 1 clan leader pvp. I still would not do it. That tells you something. Choices: This plays like battle chess table top with guns and knives. Then an under hive massive war band war. Each character has limited animation sequences that become mundane. ShameMode: This franchise may have been better served in a different format than turn base even if it is a table top game. DLC clans: A practice of models w skins to me. Then true story mode additions. A mistakeFirst impressions. They matter and I applaud their ambition. It has some wondrous scenes in Necromunda. However, I felt even with 20 clans. The game felt limited in its scope of game play with small parties that hurt tactical game play. Mordheim, to me is a better table top game translation despite its flaws where Necro feels incomplete and small in comparison. I never played Necromunda's Table top, but I found this to be less about story and more about moving and shooting. The Necromunda world was reduced here. Please see the game play in Video above discussion before deciding. Is it worth the price of admission? I would wait for a sale. I wish Rogue Factor the best because I did enjoy Mordheim so much. They get a marginal thumbs up simply for the passion and effort. However, despite its beauty, it has some issues it needs to fix that take away from it. Execution of ideas is everything. I do reserve judgment when development is fully completed, but for now. My Score 2.2 out of 5.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me first say that I was a big fan of Mordheim: City of the Damned. It was a flawed game, but it had a lot of those little things that made it special in my eyes. I thought that Rogue Factor could only learn from their mistakes with Mordheim and improve upon the formula. I was very wrong. Rogue Factor does not seem to know who their audience is, and they don't seem to care to listen. They sacrificed the depth of the game for a multiplayer mode, instead of shaping a multiplayer mode around the depth. Your fans like a single-player experience first and foremost.I just couldn't see how these guys could take everything they learned from Mordheim, and come out with this. Must have been budget restrictions, or pressure from their publisher, or just pure incompetency, or all of the above. If they add 7-9 character squads/point buy-ins, more gangs for free, more class variety between gangs, and an integrated campaign system I might consider buying this again in the future. These were the most irksome things for me.I started the disappointment of a campaign, where it's just a continued series of missions that feature each gang, which I found annoying. No discernible progression or customization to be seen. I could be wrong, but from the first couple missions, and from what I've gleaned from reviews and other discussions, that's how it is throughout. An extended 10-15 hour training session.That leaves us with what is essentially the framework for a potentially fun multiplayer-focused game with a tacked on main campaign. Sure, you can take random missions in the "sandbox" mode alongside your multiplayer experience - which is kind of similar to the whole non-campaign mission structure of Mordheim - but what made Mordheim special for me was how integrated all of these things were. Having those challenging and driving main campaign missions to work towards with the random missions in between was a nice structure, and never left me feeling like I was spinning my wheels. Being able to jump in and out of multiplayer with my warband at whatever stage they were at was an awesome touch too, especially when I'd get messed up in a skirmish and have to return to the single-player dealing with the consequences of a missing limb, or generally disabled units. Now that they separated those aspects, I feel like I'd just be playing generic random missions, in order to hop in a multiplayer game and play against real people in another generic random mission.The whole thing just feels completely pushed out the door, mismanaged, slipshod, and sloppy. I was having a little bit of fun on the battlefield the few times I was on it, but I ultimately felt the shallowness of the experience already creeping in through the cracks, and I didn't want to trick myself into possibly wasting $30 and feeling even more disappointed after 10 hours of playing it. Throw in the lack of great things like missing limbs, fog of war, and sense of deadliness in general that made Mordheim so tense, and I ended up thinking it wise to just step away. The game runs kinda clunky on my mid-range system too, which is pretty unacceptable for how it looks. That's a minor issue, but kind of a slap in the face after everything else.I would love to see them address these many issues that I have with the game, but I highly doubt that's going to happen. It feels like the game is half-cooked and never going back in the oven.

_childDocuments_.review: So here's another bad review of Necromunder Underhive Wars.When I first heard that there was going to be a game based on Necromunder had me exited because it's another 40K game and I've been a fan of 40K since I was a kid.But playing the game left me feeling a bit let down.Let me explain, Necromunder is basically UFO Enemy Unknown but set in the 40K universe.The whole game IMO feels like UFO and that's where the similarities end.It's not as slick or as polished as UFO.The AI is dumb, I mean so dumb that if the AI fell out of a boat it couldn't hit water!The enemy will (for me at least) run what sometimes looks like half the map, shoot you in the face and then run off again or they'll find a corner and hide in it, in either ambush or overwatch and because you have literally no idea how far the range of them are you inevitably run into the area of overwatch or ambush and trigger them, just the addition of range rings would help here.Then there's the map.It's (at least for me) genuinely annoying as its so difficult to orientate yourself as the game keeps changing the angle.It's also a pain in the arse trying to figure out N,S,E,W the addition of a CONSTANTLY VISIBLE COMPASS!Before you say, but Cheese you noob there IS a compass, yes you're right there is, but you have to hunt for the bloody thing!The addition of adding waypoints to your map making navigation easier would be welcome.The 3 gangs ( I hope there's plans to add more down the line, maybe Arbities, Morlok and the other various houses and maybe JUST MAYBE they'll add CHAOS) are so similar, there's nothing that really sets them apart.They all feel, move and act the same.The weapons have no flavour text added to them giving them a brief description ass to what a Bolter or a Servo arm is would be a welcome addition.Then there's the "skills"  and the same thing applies here the same as I mentioned in regards to the weapons.There's no actual description as to what they each do other than what numbers change or how many AP or MP points they cost or give you back.For example there's a skill called double tap which is self explanatory but if you don't know what double tap means you're stuck with a small number 2x and a few words.Why couldn't there be a small amount of text describing what the skill does, along the lines of "Double tap fires x2 rounds into the face of your enemy"?In short i feel that the game could have spent a little longer in the oven and many quality of life improvements made, also the enemy AI needs a lot of work, because as it stands the AI couldn't put M&M's in alphabetical order!On the plus side the game does look good, the customisation is pretty good too and the overall atmosphere of the game is pretty spot on.The voice acting could be better and they could have used actual English people to the voices because as usual it sounds a bit meh.Overall I'd honestly say leave the game alone for a few months as maybe there'll be improvements made, but the way it is now, give it a miss.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a review based off my initial impressions - I have not put much time in yet!1. If you like Mordheim, this game already feels like a marked improvement. The level design, moving around, interacting with the environment, the addition of a campaign with a story...2. As a Necromunda fan, they absolutely nailed the atmosphere. The cut scenes and set pieces have been a joy so far. Even the music and voice acting is above and beyond what I was expecting. I can't wait to play through the campaign.3. The AI is...wonky. I've seen it do some very smart things and some incredibly dumb things. I suspect this game will thrive in PVP. 4. This is not a fast paced game. As others have said, the ability to speed up AI turns, or even to control the camera during their turns, would be amazing. That said, I didn't find it painfully slow. Nor do I suspect it is a game you can just jump in and play without spending sometime climbing that learning curve. There is a LOT going on with the UI, tactical view, inventories, etc.Look. I'm a fanboy. It's not going to take much to get me excited about something that says Necromunda on it. This game clearly has some issues, but it also has some amazing potential. Here's to hoping the devs keep updating this game, adding new gangs, and most importantly: listening to their players. See you in the underhive.

I don't want a tutorial that takes me hours to go through and just jumps me around from gang to gang and gives me random upgrades.Online, not bothered trying it, if I want to play some pvp I'll go play Planetside 2. At least that game is solely a pvp game with multiple roles to play and map changes and all kinds of other ♥♥♥♥♥ you just won't find in most other 'pvp' games. Plus it's free if you're happy to just tag along and womble.But this, Necromunda Underhive Wars, It's works best when you build a custom gang and level it up from the start. Raid other HQ's, run missions, kill lots of ♥♥♥♥ and get down and dirty among the muties and sludge that is Necromunda's Underhive. _childDocuments_.review: If you like fast passed games with rewards at the end of battle this is not the game for you. If you enjoy planning things out, coming up with squad based tactics  and winning with minimal  to Zero rewards, then look no further. Necromunda  is an unforgiving game. Loosing a battle will leave you bruised, battered and empty of hope. While winning a battle  will leave you with a hollow victory unless you take the time to loot the map.  when you defeat all the enemies the game gives you 1 turn to loot,  so you really have to take your time and plan your moves between looting, the main objective and the rival gangs.  when your characters fall in battle they can get injuries and this is where the game can make you loose all hope. injuries can be temporary or permanent and it could take some time for your gang members to recover  and if you bring them to battle before they recover you risk their injuries becoming greater. the injuries can be harsh to the point where you might have to let that character go, and if you have no money from looting to hire new crew, your basically boned your next match.  i think this game is great and it brings me back to my days playing Morheim.   the only thing i could think of that would make this game better right now is if they added some kind of law enforcement  such as The Adeptus Arbites ( the Judge Dredd for the Warhammer universe) or even some Tech Priests looking for old tech. i hope some one finds my ramblings useful.  over all its a  good game, with a few bugs that can be expected at launch. but its not a game for everyone.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm sad to have to say, this game is hot trash. I really enjoyed mordheim and its faithful adaptation of a classic table-top game into a video game. I will say this, I never really played Mordheim in its table-top form, as I always liked 40K more and mordheim didn't have any representation of the harlequins who were my favorite army in fantasy. That said, I felt they did a great job with it and encouraged me to get a bit more into a setting I hadn't fully explored. They added features like an over arching story that made it enjoyable to run these gang skirmishes against an AI so you could progress your gangs gear and starts to meed the growing challenge level. It recreated the sense of attachment to your gang members as that one favored hero, or elite unit came limping home missing an arm or a leg. That said I want to get it out there I don't want to be overly critical for a developer trying new things. I like this and want to see more of it, my big issue is that Necromunda fails in its attempt to innovate. So this go around obviously they put some focus on multiplayer adding an "up to 4 person" option. I seriously question this choice, looking back at Mordheim, it was NOT a success for its vibrant multiplayer scene. In fact the multiplayer was a virtual ghost town that seemed to mostly be used to skirmish friends you knew IRL. So will adding 2 more players as an option change it from total flop of a multi player game, into a success. I HIGHLY doubt that will be sufficient. The issue here is what was chopped to make time for this effort. The "campaign" is just plain ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. I think they should have done a tiny bit of research on Black Library before they got themselves an author, as every fan of GW can tell you, there's some good authors in GW, and there's like 30-50% of them that are just GARBAGE formula writers. The author for this story is obviously from the latter category. A compelling narrative this is NOT, it hardly even makes sense in the setting. Three gangs from three different houses go after a treasure and team up to fight.... their own houses for it? wtf kind of mess is this. genestealer cult, chaos cults, the freaking spire dwellers and their super tech all exist in the setting and COULD have been used as a "big bad" to compel these factions to work together, but I assume they want those factions for DLC. The campaign itself is a failure in storytelling as well. Where morheim brought that sense of growth and attachment to your gang, Necromunda just has you run scripted mission after mission. Did one of those red shirts in your gang die the last battle? No worries he's magically back next level. Don't worry about your gangers stats or gear either all that will be done FOR you as the story switches haphazardly between the prospectives of 3 different gangs it's trying to follow. Why this could not have been done in the same way as mordheim, with each mission being a "story mission" as you progress your gang I have no clue. However this change utterly destroys any feeling of progress or attachment. In short, it makes the game feel utterly pointless. Other features they decided not to go with seem to be the ammo system, I've yet to see any indication that ammo is even a thing, they've replaced it with "weapon durability" which everyone can just burn some movement points to repair weapons like an extra type of reload, very compelling stuff. The injury system seems to be just gone, at least it's not a factor in the "story" portion of the game, maybe it serves some role in the multiplayer that no one will ever use. Another big design choice was to make gangs consist of 5 people and have 5 classes. Typically, I would say when adding something to an established game that's got a following already you want to ask yourself two questions. What is the content I'm putting in going to add to the overall experience, and what am I going to have to remove to do this. So what was added was a VERY generic set of "classes" basically range, melee, tech support, leader, assault. and some AOE type bubble abilities, with some stat buffs and rebuffs, all pretty old tired gimmicks in the genera. What was removed? The ability to have a customized army in more senses than just the paint job. This additional content in essence prohibited them from making larger group sizes likely to deal with the "now with up to 4 players" think no one ever asked for.  The ability to make a truly custom army was sacrificed on the alter of making new class types for the game and the size limitation. The story was sacrificed to get hype for a "known author" big HUGE air quotes there, I will point out that I say this because it would have been possible to write this story without a cool faction like a genestealer cult for the "big bad" but instead the author just made a cluster ♥♥♥♥ that made no sense at all and furthermore didn't even really introduce anyone to ANY of the uniqueness of the gangs it focused on. The most I heard were some throw away lines about how "those crazy ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ love drugs" This is getting ranty, I do not intend to address all the other complaints I see being posted commonly like bad AI and how viewing every turn ruins the game. _childDocuments_.review: 4/10Well, your feelings on this will depend a lot on how you felt about mordheim. The game is just...very dated. It was already dated when they used this same system in 2015, but there was less competition for TBS skirmish games, so it kiiinda got a pass (though even then it wasn't very popular).The recent xcom games frankly just have raised the bar too high for this. Turns in necromunda are slow and clunky. The ui is clunky. I frequently found myself screwing up an entire turn because something didn't work the way it seemed like it should have. There are many skills I just don't use because they either are bugged or don't seem to do what their descriptions suggest they should. I don't really know which it is, because the descriptions aren't very clear. The visuals are not great, and textures are very slow to render. I don't care that much about that...but it just doesn't hold up to the other options out there. Also the fact that there are only 3 factions and the 4th is a DLC you have to pay for is...pretty irritating (would have been fine if the rest of the game was polished...but it just isn't). There is almost a really cool game in here. The levels seem like they should be a lot of fun...but they aren't. I mean...they are very vertical which is pretty cool. Too bad movement is a total slog.Get any of the xcom games instead. Xcom 2 is amazing, especially with the DLC, and the long war mod is like a whole new game. Hell, with mods you can practically made xcom into the game you wanted necromunda to be. Phoenix Point has it's issues but is also a great alternative. It's not terrible but don't spend more than $10, it's decent for a $10 game...but then again you can usually get something better for (like xcom) for $10. It's just below average in pretty much every respect.All that said, I'll probably play a couple more hours, because I really wish this was good and I really want it to change my mind.Edit:I ended up playing this a lot more because I was bored and I really wanted this to save itself somehow. I completely regret it, it feels like a total waste of time. Other notes:The story is...whatever. Pretty much on par with any other 40K game.I love the character models for the Cawdor coming up. Too bad it's not really possible for that to change the gameplay, and I would have to spend more money on this. Maybe somebody has modded the skins into xcom...

_childDocuments_.review: The short version : This game is hot garbage with many problems that spoils an otherwise promising game that could have been great.The long version :Keen Necromunda table top player here. I bought this game when it first released, then ignored it for three years, figuring that if it was anything like Mordheim - Rogue Factors game they did prior to this - then it would need time to mature and iron out all the crap.It appears that the crap has never been ironed out and Rogue Factor have walked away from it at this point - not before releasing a couple of crappy DLC packs for missing gangs as a blatant cash grab.So what's up with it exactly ?Many things !1) Dumpster fire AI. It barely knows how to play the game. It can run in circles, make the most stupid mistakes. and best of all, can't even traverse terrain at times without hilariously getting stuck and running on the spot. And this is  a patch was released to at least stop the Stuck On Terrain AI from completely halting the game. Rather than actually fix that problem, the AI "times out" after a while and tries a different - random - path.2) UI bugs, inconsistencies, lack of testing and polishing. Problems lie everywhere. From inconsistent buggy actions in places, to misleading overlays, and frustrating minor bugs that can lead you to completely whiffing a turn due to the game just being a mess.3) Pacing. Lazy mission design. Bonkers level design. A lot of this you can look the other way with. Grind your teeth at times. But combined with everything else it reeks of a game that has never been properly tested, never been properly finished and in many aspects has beta or even alpha code and design.All in all it's a great shame. Necromunda is a fantastic IP, and the core of the game is here. It  have been something really amazing, but instead is a disaster of unfinished, uncoordinated garbage.You *can* play this game and extract some enjoyment from it. But oh boy, it's not great. And once you start to see the AI running around in circles like a headless chicken only to run on the spot stuck against step. Yikes.The development on this was so bad I did a bit of digging about Rogue Factor. It's a management problem as far as I can tell. Egotistical. Uncoordinated. Undisciplined. Blue sky nonsense. Whoever is at the top there needs to be kicked out or demoted to tea boy.Such a waste of a good IP and a lot of clearly good effort to get the game so far.In future I will be treating any development by this company with prejudice - horrible developer.
