_childDocuments_.review: There's really three major problems with this game that prevent me from recommending it for purchase; the first deal breaker issue is the AI is dumb as bricks. It will spend whole turns casting one turn buffs on itself and I've seen it literally run it's turn in a loop without doing anything (walk, jump down, walk, grapple up, return to starting point, end turn).  It's really dissatisfying to see it walk past guys it could engage and kill, particularly since the four gang model means it's often not your guys it isn't killing. Second deal breaker issue is that they didn't speed up the enemy's turn at all. Since the AI will walk super far you spend a maddeningly long time watching them walk around. The third deal breaker issue. Is that they chose to make the movement points super wonky. No matter how much you walk in a circle it uses the same movement points. The problem is if you start in the middle of a building for example, you can walk out an entrance on one side double back, and walk all the way around the building. easily completing a move that would take 3-4 turns if distance was measured linearly. I get that the probably implemented this to prevent having to backtrack but they could have done it much more elegantly with a reverse path finding model (imagine stretching a string behind you from the starting point and measuring the mp used like that. I only mention this because I hope they will patch it.) The other crazy thing is it doesn't seem to count vertical distance at all, I think you could climb up 14 floors in a single move if you could find stairs. There's also a number of nice to have UI features that are missing. Necromunda (the place) is large, dark and vertical, and sometimes I feel like I'm playing a find the object game when I'm trying to shoot guys. The crazy thing is that in Mordhiem they showed you when you had enemies that were eligible to hit and give you a hit chance as you moved around. Not so in Necromunda (the game) and I have no idea why they cut this. The other thing that the game could use is a mini map and compass. I probably hoof it in the wrong direction about one in three times because orienting yourself in the underhive is not a simple task. would be great to have a bit of help. I honestly think the core game could be pretty fun but they have to iron out a number of issues before I could recommend getting yourself a copy.  Even in the current state it's not so bad as to be unplayable, but I wouldn't buy it at the current price ($32 USD) in it's current state. IMO right now Mordheim is the superior Rouge Factor game.Edit: I forgot one thing, I honestly think the virtue vice system trolls you based on your stat allocation because I've got so many ruinous virtue/vice combinations on my shooters. It's freaking maddening!

_childDocuments_.review: Necromunda: Underhive Wars is another excellent turn-based strategy from Rogue Factor. Expanding and improving upon Mordheim: City of the Damned, Necromunda: Underhive Wars moves the squad-based RPG tactics to the 40th millenium, taking place in the dark corridors and forgotten causeways of Hive Primus' underbelly. If you liked Mordheim, or you're a fan of other turn-based tactical RPGs, like Final Fantasy Tactics, you'll most likely enjoy this.Necromunda plays out much as one would expect from a turn-based tactics game, in turns where each player moves their fighters individually to combat the enemy and accomplish mission objectives. Turn-taking is shaken up a bit from the standard formula, where instead of a pure initiative-based turn order, each player selects a unit per "round", with the unit with the highest initiative moving first. Once all units have been activated, the turn is over. This gives the player a bit more agency in using their units - selecting a heavy first means you might not move before your opponents, but you might also get some critical shots off onto your opponent's lighter units.Units are divided into five distinct classes - Deadeyes, who fill a sniper/marksman role, Brawlers, who are melee specialists, Heavies, who specialize in heavy ranged weapons, Saboteurs, who control the battlefield by trapping choke points and enabling or disabling environmental items and effects, and Lay-Mechanics, who can fix the damage caused by Saboteurs and interact with the environment to create healing points and other utilities. While these classes suggest a certain style of play, they are by no means restrictive - this is not XCOM-2. Special weapons like chainswords and autocannons are restricted to certain classes, but the player is given a lot of leeway in developing their troops, and you may find yourself making a melee-focused Saboteur or a Heavy who can switch from their gun to a pair of axes if they're cornered in melee.The meat of the game is in its Operations Mode, which you may access by creating your own gang, with a plethora of cosmetic customization options. Here, you compete in a mini-grand strategy map with multiple AI enemy gangs. You play out each "Cycle", or day, on the map by selecting missions to compete for scarce resources, fighting up to three other enemy gangs at once. Objectives here are varied, but you can generally expect to gather specific items from the field. You use the resources and salvage you gather to develop your gang.The campaign mode is a bit of a trap - it seems like the obvious main mode, but in truth acts as more of a tutorial for the game's systems. It contains none of the persistency or progression of the Operations mode, and suffers from difficult design in some areas. Mission 5 is already becoming a dreaded encounter for many players, and hopefully this will be fixed.Necromunda, as the title implies, is set in the same world as its tabletop predecessor, which itself is a spin-off game in the Warhammer: 40,000 universe. If you're familiar with the universe, you'll recognize many elements within the game, while the game is also not too arcane to understand for a newcomer. The premise is very simple - you play as one of the many gangs fighting and dying in the ruined and lawless underbelly of a Hive City, a man-made megastructure housing trillions upon trillions of humans. The environment design and graphics all communicate this very well - the game runs well on a mid-range machine from 2016 without any hiccups or crashes (so far). The atmosphere appropriately conveys the grunge and grime of the industrial wastes of the Underhive, without seeming too same-y like many environments from Mordheim.The soundtrack is a definite highlight - the electronic industrial music provides excellent ambiance, and dynamically changes with the gameplay, rising in intensity in combat and when a unit is put out of action. It is reminiscent of the late-80s and early 90s that the original game took inspiration from in its aesthetic, and you might be reminded of RoboCop or Metal Gear Solid while listening to it.Necromunda: Underhive Wars is a very well-made turn-based tactics game. Despite some early balancing problems and the presence of some bugs, I have confidence that Rogue Factor will continue to polish this gem as time wears on. This is a definite must for anyone who is a fan of turn-based tactical RPGs - there are very few games which allow for this level of customization and character creation. Hope to see you in the Underhive!

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a huge fan of Necromunda, 40k and turn based strategies, so this game should have been a home run.After initial load into the tutorial it was obvious that this was designed for consoles, with the interface poorly designed for a PC platform turn based strategy. Trying to orient myself was an exercise in frustration, tabbing in and out of the map to work out which way I was facing and wanted to head.Although not ideal, I wasn't going to write off the game because of this.  Not what I was expecting or used to, but would give it a shot.  On the second level one character got stuck halfway up an elevator when moving the gang to a different floor and was essentially out of action for a turn, but it wasn't game breaking as I completed the level without issue after that.Move to the third level where the game CTD halfway through the first turn.  A little more frustrating, but the game auto saved one move prior so didn't really lose any progress.  On the third turn however, I experienced a movement bug that sucked motivation out of wanting to continue.  Twice, the AI did two circuits of the map with one character on a single turn, dropping down to stun 3 out of 5 of my gang.  It appears the game gives you unlimited movement within an area centred on where you start, rather than using movement points the further you travel.  The other bugs I could deal with, but this one was game-breaking for me as it completely ruins the intended game mechanics.Unfortunately I'm not eligible for a refund as I didn't purchase on Steam and it occurred after 2 hours of playtime anyway, but I would have refunded if I had the chance. _childDocuments_.review: The game looks like Necromunda, the character models are great and the environments look awesome. But beyond that, it hasn't lived up to the expectations of me and so many others.Many elements that were enjoyable for me in Mordhiem are gone, like the sense of urgency. There is at this time, no way to lose - you can lose gangers, but even if you do terribly, you won't be punished and can not end up not being unable to play the operations anymore... The story is separated from the custom gangs, meaning that you play the Story with a gang that isn't yours, you have no progression within it and switch between one gang and another.Gangs are limited to 5 members being active at one time. I think this has been done to lower the time spent in maps, as you can have 4 gangs facing each other - if everyone had 10 gangers, the games would end up being very long, and the maps are not designed for so many gangers either (they would have to be twice the size).The map sizes is an issue, as most gangers can travers the entire map, especially vertically, as there are no 'break' points in the movement like there were in Mordheim. Ziplines makes the maps feel even smaller, as you spend action points to move very far across the map with them. If movement range was reduced by 50%, it might not feel like such an issue.The AI is confused most of the time, making it a walkover outside of the Story - it is clear now, that the work has to be put into the AI for this game to become just somewhat enjoyable to people.The only way, right now, that I'm still playing, is because of my D.I.E in the Underhive rules - which I've designed to make the game harder for myself, and adds consequences to it. Now that doesn't change the AI, but for now at least it is keeping my interest in the game.I will admit that my review until now hasn't been totally clear - if there was a middle ground to recommending the game, I would take it - but there isn't. Recommendation; Watch some gameplay, and if you like it get it and can live with the above apparent issues, then go ahead and get it - otherwise, hold off for now until they get some more updates in.

_childDocuments_.review: So full disclosure: I got given this copy for coverage. Now I have a few more hours under my belt, mostly because I  wanted a good Necromunda game I feel secure in giving a verdict: It's bad.Firstly there's the state of the game, then there's the content and design. We'll start of with the first one since that's the easiest to critique and the one most widely lampooned.Fair warning, I haven't played the multiplayer and don't intend to. From what I understand getting a connection is rough since even in offline game the game helpful tells me once every few hours that I have been disconnected from the server and that I should check my internet cable was plugged in. Once while I was streaming the game...The bugs are omnipresent, the obvious one is the AI.- It'll throw a buff AoE on just one character... twice in the same turn. Even though it doesn't stack. In another characters turn it'll do it again... and again... Last match it buffed the same two characters SIX times despite the buffs not stacking.- It'll walk into walls and objects until it reaches timeout before trying another action... often walking into a different wall or object...- It'll disengage from melee. Walk away. Walk back. Then go back into melee.- It'll place traps... and then walk over their own traps. In the same turn. With the same character.- It'll sometimes send a full game hiding one unit in a corner. Doing nothing but repeat buffs.- The AI does not understand destructible scenery .Other bugs, such as being unable to interact with objects on certain maps or in certain places (like stairs), are an ever present situation. In terms of polish, this feels more like a janky public alpha or an internal late alpha. Putting this out as a finished product is highly disrespectful to customers.Sadly the game mechanics and design choices don't feel much better. The elephant in the room is that it features . This means that'll you'll be facing the same clans over and over and no match will stand out. This despite having several load screens that tell you cool tactics and units that other clans have... who aren't featured in the game in any way. Speaking of units, the variety of classes (only 5) combined means everything is a rather homogenous. Most squads run the same 5 different classes in their 5 person squad - or they run 4 different and 1 dupe. Which, when combine with the AI which always seems to use the same tactics (it's hard to tell if there are any other AI profiles such as offensive/defensive/mobile/objective focused or whether it's just  bug ridden that they all look the same), means that every match feels like every other match. This is by far the biggest complaint to be level in terms of the content - there's hardly any actual meat. Little variety and load scenes that actually look more inviting than the game you're playing.The one slightly redeeming factor is the maps are pretty numerous, however they all follow a similar 3D layout which means that although the maps might be different the general playstyle is the same. This, however, is also defeated by the mobility system. Necromunda uses a system that gauges how far you move by measuring your distance from your starting point or last action - great! This is better than Mordheim (the studios previous game) where you felt you had to optimise each move. But sadly they made a huge and obvious mistake. Every map is hugely 3D with typically 5 distinct floors and multiple ways of traversing them... while shooting ranges etc. are measure in 3D space your movement, and the refund system, is measured only in 2D space. . In more practical terms it means that you can, and the AI  jump off a ledge 5 floor, take a zipline, walk down some stairs, take a lift up 3 floors, walk across a bridge... and end where you started without having spent many movement points at all. While you might not do this the AI  since it calculates it. It'll often do this just to attack the same character it started the turn in melee with. Or you can just use the system to move ludicrous distances across the map in one turn.This contributes massively to how long a turn takes. Because each AI will take its turn (and sometimes you’ll play in a 4-gang fight) with long walks and pauses between each action the only way I have managed to get this far was by watching Netflix with Necromunda on in the background for when it was my turn.The campaign is awful, forces you to play a certain gang, the voice acting is bad, the writing is something for a cereal packet, and it's littered with bugs. I stopped playing so I could just (wishfully) enjoy freeplay Operations mode. But of course unlocks for Operations are gated behind the Campaign? Sigh. When you first start operations it won't even let you have access to the shop for 2 missions, which in the release candidate means that you would have to fight with only 4 people against gangs of 5  the game telling you to get a 5th - you didn't have the money. As a day 1 patch they reduced the number of gangers in easy enemy gangs to 4, but it is galling that this is the sort of balancing and thought that went into this. Which leads me to the shop and items...The Shop has limited goods, and when it restocks it seemingly only has a single type of items in a class. For instance left leg armour. In my campaign I didn't get a single piece of chest armour until I used unlocks from Infamy. All the items are classed into tiers , fans of 40k will recognise a Lasrifle, Autogun, and Plasmagun... but they maybe wouldn't put them all on the same power tier. Common Tier 1 Autoguns being just as powerful and expensive as tech marvel Tier 1 Plasmaguns makes little sense, and further compounds the homogenous feeling of the game when all that matters is the tier rating of the weapon and less so the type.A far better solution would be limiting rarities like plasmaguns to higher tiers and introducing variants of weapons. A Mars and a Triplex pattern lasgun are hugely different for instance. The game doesn't even touch sniper rifles, longlas, or bolters (despite having boltpistols).There's more. Oh so much more. Like the game modes all being  similar. Or the rare game mode that forces melee only invalidating a third of the clans and half the classes. Or the special archaeotech mission that sounds really cool... but is just another ‘collect the item’ mission. Or the boltpistol soundeffect.  Or the fact that your own abilities can cancel each other out as invalid after your turn. Or that basic UI elements are missing such as the ability to switch character in the gang menu, or that the customisation menu is bizarrely laid out.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll start by saying that I played and enjoyed their previous game, Mordheim: City of the Damned.Both games share a lot of similarities, one thing that I disliked in Mordheim was that enemy composition was exactly the same as yours. In this one, you don't know what the enemy will have before you start the mission and you can be outmatched, or you can also have two enemy teams instead of one.One the plus side, the campaign is well done and fun to play, the underhive is a beautiful place to melt people in, team customization is nice.Now the bad side. It has been said, I say it again, the AI is dumb. Some decisions it makes are quite good, like focusing on the mission objective or not, but it has a lot of problems with situational awareness, it places ambushes in an empty corner, it runs half the map instead of finishing an opponent ... there is certainly room for improvement. This makes the game easier than it really is.Also, contrary to Mordheim, once you finish the campaign and start creating your own gang, you realize after a couple of custom missions that there is not really much to do. No story events, no ultimate goal, just custom missions over and over while leveling your gang. This isn't good at all, and it's clearly something the devs will have to expand further. Just so you know, the main campaign has 15 missions, each one taking less than a hour to do. There's the multiplayer, but there isn't that many players online, and I tend to prefer playing alone for these types of games.Some words about sound. It is rather quiet all game, but when you kill someone you have some synthwave going on and it's really cool. I want more of it! I'd also want more gory blood and shouted curses, it's too ... calm, when there's supposed to be chaos.So, the most important things to improve are the AI and what we could call the endgame, other than that I believe that Necromunda can become a game as fun as Mordheim is now.

_childDocuments_.review: So they did continue support, and some/most of the bugs appear to have been removed, but several of the most egregious remain a year later.Being unable to shoot despite having the AP and a working weapon, because the game can't seem to always count your AP properly (particularly if your AP changed during your turn). Characters who have been downed being replaced by upright character dolls T-posing, or often stuck mid animation. Also, a new one for me, AI characters skin remaining the white semi-transparent texture it is before the character has activated for their first turn. Clothing and equipment is textured properly, but the skin is not. AI is still terrible to the point of being almost worthless. Despite several blog posts to the contrary, I didn't notice an appreciable change in AI behaviour between launch and now. The AI will still hide in the corner of the map on overwatch all game. It will still spend all it's movement points running around in a circle, ending up essentially back where it started. It will still use redundant buffs. It will still ignore enemies (mostly AI enemies, there is a clear priority for the AI to target human players. But even so, it still struggles to do this). It is simplicity itself to start a new game on the highest difficulty with a starter gang and wipe multiple AI gangs in the first battle, steal all their stuff and essentially dominate the entire operation from there, entirely because the AI behaviour is so stunted, confused and frankly useless.This AI issue was a predictable problem, because Necromunda environments are very complicated for an AI to navigate, as they have a lot of verticality, and moving through them is essentially a 3D puzzle for AI pathfinding. Sadly Rogue Factor are not up to the task of creating a competent AI to solve this problem, which is also predictable, because they aren't a huge studio and the problem is such that many larger studios would fail just as hard. However, this is a problem they set themselves when they decided to make this game, and the resulting game suffers for it hugely.We have an additional two gangs now, but they are essentially graphical reskins with no difference in AI behaviour.I haven't edited the second half of this review because frankly, nothing has changed here.On the plus side, the graphics are good. the environments are good, they do evoke a Necromunda vibe. Animations could do with being smoother and being blended into each other, eg. a charge attack will show the character run at an enemy, stop adjust, and then make the attack. Look real awkward. But on the whole graphics are decent.The story is ok, pretty generic, but I think Andy Chambers just pulled it out of an old White Dwarf article, or some other piece of Necromunda lore he wrote tbh.Given that most people who consider this game as fans of the old tts game will want to recreate a Necromunda campaign with friends in digital, it is predictable that you can't do this. Even if the MP actually worked, it only allows the full gang campaign to work in single player, with single custom matches of pvp.I bought this game based on hope and nostalgia, knowing I would likely be disappointed, and I was. I have played through the single player story mode, and a couple of different gangs, almost entirely on nostalgia and hoping to recreate the old Necromunda experience. Sorry to say, it isn't here.

_childDocuments_.review: A little about me: I have logged about 84 hours with Necromunda Underhive Wars as of this writing and I must say I have been really enjoying my time with it.  I also have not attempted any PvP matches, I tend to prefer single player games. The brief description of this game is: This is a turn based strategy game with a 3rd person perspective rather than the traditional isometric birds-eye view, character improvement is from a point-buy system for statistics and abilities, and from acquiring progressively better equipment looted from your foes or purchased with in game credits.  The game includes a thematic story mode following three different gangs written by Black Libraries author Andy Chambers, and a Campaign system where your custom gang can engage in an A.I. driven turf war with random objectives/mission types, player selected A.I. skirmishes to practice or boost gang experience & credits, or PvP multiplayer skirmishes.  The big take away should be: it is a turn based game and has the pacing as such.  Positioning, activation order, squad synergies, and thoughtful counter-play are what makes your gang victorious.  This is not a fast paced action game, but rather a 3rd person perspective adaptation of the Necromunda table top game by Games Workshop.  As a long time player of the table top version, they did an excellent job of capturing the thematic feel of the IP and a decent job capturing how the game plays on table top.  This definitely feels like Necromunda in an immersive way.On to address some of the not so great aspects of the game: · The biggest disappointment for me is the illogical A.I.; It's not uncommon for the A.I. to run in a big circle to end up back where it started after having taken overwatch fire or wasted action points jumping and climbing.  Sometimes it will be far to cautious, hiding in a back corner not contributing to the engagement, or sometimes recklessly charging into the middle of an opposing gang to make a big attack, but then leave itself open for severe counter attacks.  It has it's moments when it outmaneuvers you in unexpected ways, but also moments when it gets stuck running against some crates and eventually times out with its turn wasted.· I also experienced some crashes to desktop.  I recall 3 during the story mode; they were immersion breaking, but I quickly reloaded the game to get back in the action. 2 occurred during A.I skirmishes; one a simple re-load, the other corrupted my custom gang briefly after about 8 hours of play time.  I had to use the Steam tool "verify integrity of files" which recovered my gang, then I updated all my drivers per the developers recommendations. I have now played another 50 hours or so and have not had a single crash since.  If you get this game update all of your drivers including BIOS!· The story mode doubles as the tutorial and has allot of necessary information to understand the games mechanics.  The problem is the tips are off to the side in an unobtrusive part of the screen, and easily missed when you are deep in concentration for your next action.  This wouldn't be an issue if you could open a panel to read all of your past tips, but if it exists I couldn't find it.  I re-played a couple missions just so I could go back and read some of the missed tips.To complete my review: I am a happy customer and have had great fun with the game, I have absolutely gotten my moneys worth and them some out of it.  It has some quirks that will hopefully be resolved with patching, but honestly as is, I would still recommend it for anyone that enjoys the GW table top version of Necromunda, or for those that like turn-based strategy games.  As is, it is fun; with successful patching it could become great.

_childDocuments_.review: If Steam had an award for worst AI of the year, Necromunda Underhive Wars is in with a great shot at winning it.  I cannot recommend buying this in its current state.I really wanted to enjoy this - I loved the tabletop game years ago, and think they've done a good job creating that world and atmosphere in a video game.  I like the design of the environments you fight in, that you can build your own gang, customise it and progress.  You find new weapons and equipment, level up your fighters and give them the skills you choose.  But then you start playing and get hit by bugs and the most stupid AI that saps the fun out it.I've come to expect bugs at launch, and I do try to look beyond them to see the game it could be.  I've had the game crash 10+ times in my initial 30 hours, but pushed through it (70h+ at the time of review).  I've used skills in battle that fail to work when they should, then trigger when they shouldn't.  A lot of balancing needs to be done with skills, but that can be sorted out.One game breaker is the save system - a single file that overwrites with each action - until it corrupts and you lose your gang completely.  I hit that twice, and only kept playing because I had manually copied my saves as a backup seeing others falling foul of this.We should be able to put our gangs up against other players, but the multiplayer is so unstable that matches are almost impossible to complete.  Not sure if it has been fixed reading this?  look at the achievements and global % for multiplayer wins achievements.Which leaves us with single player and the biggest problem - the AI.  Watching an enemy leader run around in a circle, throw the same (non-stacking) buff 3 times, then crouch in a corner would be funny, if it didn't take all the challenge and fun out of the game.  You will be in range of an AI with a rifle, but they don't shoot.  A melee brawler runs right past your fighter, has enough points to attack, but doesn't.  You can up the difficulty of the mission to give them more hit points, do more damage, but if the AI is too poorly coded to rather pick up a box rather than fight, there simply isn't a challenge.I also can't figure out what endgame there is meant to be.  While you can have 15 fighters in your gang, you can only deploy 5 in a fight, and it doesn't take long to get them to max level with all the skills you want.  You can already destroy the AI, and multiplayer is too unstable to use.  There isn't much distinction between the three houses, and even the five classes are only distinct by making certain weapons only usable by one class.But on top of that, despite lots of players posting on their forum and discord, there seems to be a complete lack of urgency on the part of the devs or publisher to address these problems and get it patched.  Bugs can get patched and fixed, but overhauling the AI or more fundamental design decisions?  Those are not things that get fixed quickly.

_childDocuments_.review: The game has a lot of issues but over time the developers have steadily worked to improve.The Pros:- Necromunda in splendid 3D glory. One thing I love about it is that for the first time we get to actually see the insides of these places in gorgeous detail. The graphics are amazing and a step above Mordhiem although I will say after a while the maps do get a little repetitive. But it's nice to see your own hideout and actually play missions in it as well is fully customize your individual warband members a lot further than their previous title.- Play at -your- own pace. No longer are the missions' difficulty randomly generated. Want to work up a brand new gang while training new recruits? Set your next operation to Easy or Normal and allow your team to build up a bit before tackling harder operations. Want a greater chance at rewards and increased experience? Set it to harder difficulties. This seriously has won me over as I prefer to tackle turn based games at my own pace and learn them fully before I'm thrown against impossible odds.- Very good ganger skill development system with built in "skill resets" in the form of memory wipes. Finally you're not stuck with bad builds you made a mistake in early on as the ganger developed. Now you can easily swap out skills. Additionally you can outright buy gangers that are higher levels and customize their skills yourself (there are some potential negatives however).- 3 Ganger Crew slots (5 members each), allowing you to swap out ganger builds as you see fit.- Unlimited Sandbox campaign mode not connected to the main story. Play your favorite warband forever if you so desire.The Cons- The Maps are vertical in design in conjunction with a move system that mainly counts movement horizontally. This causes an issue where on vertical maps (most are), both you and your opponent could in theory go across the entire map in one turn. This can be off putting to some, and when combine with the lackluster AI, can be easily abused to the point of cheesing the game.- The A.I. although improved is still lackluster at best. I don't mean they hit soft or are a pushover; rather their decision and prioritizing can leave a lot to be desired. The A.I. currently focuses too much on map objectives. Since these objectives have to be carried (losing a weapon hand), they can easily end up weakening themselves significantly. The A.I. also tends to spend most of its action points on ally support and self support abilities to the detriment of its own survival. I just had a game where the A.I. never attacked any of my gangers.At first it may seem like things are fun for you and you're just wrecking the A.I. Over time however, it begins to feel cheap and as if you're just steam rolling the AI no matter the difficulty. Difficulty levels really translate to hitpoint padding and damage multiplying in a vain attempt at making the A.I. more 'difficult'. When you finally start playing harder games, the A.I.'s shortcomings become very evident as they pretty much do the same actions just now as damage sponges.- Main tutorial campaign required for a few direly needed customization options. The customization options for gang leaders is very limited. The main campaign once you complete it unlocks an additional one to each of the gangs.- All the gangs are practically the same yet cosmetically different. The differences between the gangs are very minimal. Each gang gets a few bumps in statistics points here and there. Given the padding involved with the various ability scores, these differences are minimal at best. As such, the differences between the gangs are really the graphics. Escher you're limited to all women models, the others lets you pick between genders, the armors and weapons are unique to each gang but otherwise exactly the same in statistics and numbers. Picking up weapons and armor from a different gang automatically changes its graphics to that used by your gang.ConclusionI'd definitely get it. For me at least the pros outweigh the cons. Anything that can help keep the balance more or less the same is good in my book. I suspect the design decisions were made so as to make it easier for the developers to maintain online multiplayer balance while being able to also work on the A.I. to provide some sort of challenge to the player (as little as it can muster).

_childDocuments_.review: So first of all let me address the elephant in the room, the crashes, obviously people are having the game crash allot.All I can say is I have 67 hours playtime at the time of writing this review, i have finished the story mode and i have almost maxed out a custom gang with max stats and level VI equipment, and I have NEVER had the game crash, not once.I don't know if it has something to do with system specs, running it off SSD as apposed to SATA etc, just sharing my personal experience.Now as for weather or not its a good game, well first of all i have to admit its lacking content. there are only three gangs out ofd the 11 now available in tabletop Necro, there are no pets and the weapons and equipment are very limited when compared to what's available in the tabletop game, i'm hoping this all comes in DLC sooner rather than later.That aside its a good game, story mode is decent, basically a long tutorial before you get into what Necrounda has always and should always be about, creating your own gang.Classes and play differs from the tabletop game but not in a way that turned me off as a fan of the tabletop game, especially if they add additional classes in DLC later, the visual customisation is quite good and the aesthetic and feel of Necromunda is definitely there.Gameplay is fun, a little slow paced, waiting for your turn can be a little annoying, especially because the AI needs some work, they can make some silly decisions and occasionally get stuck walking into walls but the progression of your gang and tactics are very satisfying.Where the game truly shines is where the root of Necromunda has always and should always be PVP, get your mates together and blow the limbs off each others gangers! _childDocuments_.review: So this is a turn-based 40k-game (shocker) where you get to play as 3 of the original 6 House-gangs. The campaign has 15 Chapters where you both try out all 3 gangs and different scenarios while being fluffed out as a hunt for archeotech as a story. The plot is incredibly thin, and the campaign feels like regular skirmish mode fleshed out with some voice acting. It will guide you through a tutorial of how to play the game.When you've finished the 15 Chapters and know how to play, you should try out the Operations part of the game, which is skirmish mode, only that you get yo style your own gang with weapons, armour and other equipment. This is the fun part, as anything that happens in a match carries over to the next. I've put 51 hours into this game at the time I've writing this, and I would say this is the short version of what I think of it:+  very cinematic videos in between the Chapters.+ Decent graphics for a 40k game.+ Fun to build out and style your own gang.+ great representation of all type of people (skin-colour, body-types ect).- awful A.I. that can't do two things at the same time.+ awful A.I. that doesn't give you too much of a challenge.- not a very deep storyline in campaign.- voice-acting ranging from good to awful.- It gets repetative very quickly with missions being gather materials quicker than the opponents, pit brawls where you fight each other with only melee weapons and some shooting in between. It would have been fun if they included more elements from the setting: mutants, Enforcers, hazardous enviroment ect.So I'm an achievement hunter, so that's why I am playing this game still, but I can't for the love of it, recommend this game to anybody. You could (if you're still curious about it), get this when it's on sale (as I did). Wait for the range of 60-75%. Then you'll get a few hours of turning off your brain while shooting enemy gangers.

_childDocuments_.review: There's a lot to like about this game - the environments are impressive, the gang customization and progression system is extensive, and the tactical gameplay is (I think) pretty good... But unless you're planning on playing strictly multiplayer, I can't really recommend it for one simple reason: the AI is so dumb it might as well be deciding its moves entirely at random.Seriously, I played through a dozen or so encounters (against what were theoretically evenly-matched AI gangs) and not only did I never lose, none of my gang members ever even got knocked out.  The AI was just COMPLETELY incapable of mounting any kind of effective offense. Occasionally it was because it didn't seem to understand how to navigate the complex levels, but more often it was just that the AI just... didn't really attack me.  I mean, it would get a hit in here and there, but it never focused its fire on a weakened gang member and half the time would just run around trying to pick up mission objectives rather than fighting... which just lead to me killing them and picking up the objective items they were trying to run away with.So... yeah.  Basically, playing against the AI is pointless, unless you enjoy slow-motion curbstomps of brain-dead robots.  And since I'm not really into multiplayer, this made the game in general pretty pointless to me.  If you're here for PvP though, its probably fine.

_childDocuments_.review: This should have been a fun multiplayer game but it's actually a bit bland overall and the bugs are a bit bad.I love multiplayer pvp and that was why I tried this product out and I did manage to play a few pvp games against players around the release time with minimal waiting time.  Since then, the population has dropped right off from 2,000 people active in the game at the beginning to an average of 300 ish online at any one time.  Consequently, the chances of finding people to pvp with are much reduced.  No one is in queue now and I'm not prepared to wait infinitely to find someone.Release date is the time when your product is displayed to the world in all it's glory, and it's the best time to grab player attention (and also make some money).  So I dived in on release to find a horrible AI (yes enemies sometimes stand in corners facing the wrong way the whole game or just don't support each other whatsoever) and game breaking multiplayer crashes to desktop.  If you get a multiplayer game and the enemy is losing, they can just quit without further penalty to their side also... so you will likely miss out on loot and experience you could have earned.    You will still get a loot box for staying for the whole match, if the multiplayer bug doesn't crash you. I'd like to say I'll play this game again.  At the moment, it doesn't feel that I will and the player numbers are horribly low.  The developer needs to quickly address the issues and I'll keep checking back every now and again to see if things have been improved.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very broken.PVE -   AI would legit be better if it just attacked the first thing it saw.  in the current state it will instead run by everything it sees and stand in a corner use buff skills and protect that corner or barrel its hiding behind with its life.   I have seen it run past 2 of my units, use a zip line to the top floor of a building just to jump off, run past my units again and use the same zipline ... AGAIN.The 15 story missions are alright i guess.   The objectives and such are fine, but again the AI is awful and sometimes you have AI on your team but they wont do anything to help you for the most part but they will throw grenades at you or set traps at your feet so i guess thats better than hiding in a corner?  PVP-  Also broken.   if you do manage to find a game its very likely it wont connect and if you DO connect because its the second Tuesday on a full moon and all planets are aligned you better not kill anything because if anyone tries to pick up a downed player the game crashes.   "oh no i'm down to 2 units and i don't want to lose i guess i'll just run past everyone and try to pick someone up!"   easy disconnect.If you are looking for a game like this just play Mordheim but buy it on sale.   I was looking forward to this game because I figured they would learn from the mistakes in Mordheim and build on that with the 40k version of the game but somehow they managed to make it flat worse with a fresh coat of paint.I do think the game could be great if the AI didn't have the tactical prowess of a cat walking across the keyboard and if the PVP worked, but currently neither of those things are true.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm enjoying it. I'm enjoying running one of each gang through operations. I'm enjoying working my way through a fun SP campaign. I'm enjoying avoiding PvP, because no game has ever had a player-base in MP worth interacting with ever anyway (except MechWarrior 4).Yep, the AI is terrible. Yep, damage output is pathetic, and yep, the game pacing would be much better if combat was more lethal, even with just 5 active fighters per match max. Turn-over in a Necromunda gang is supposed to be high, and you shouldn't be getting attached to your first hires like you do in XCom anyway.Yup, the game is somewhat over-priced, probably due to the fact publisher pressure means an early access release that isn't categorised as such. However, other publishers have forced releases of games in a similar state at far higher prices, so keep that in mind when deciding to go for it at this price. You aren't promoting such business methods being the norm and acceptable. You are showing your support for the developer.Commit now, and help support improvements to game stability and AI. Or watch as attempts at funding through DLC content fails because the actual game itself doesn't get the fixes it needs. You'll be missing out, and the game will be abandonware after about six months, I'd guess. S'up to you.Like I said I'm enjoying it, and am happy to buy-in at this price.

_childDocuments_.review: Meh, 3 hours into this one and already bored to death.... Why you ask?For one, the battles take F-O-R-E-V-E-R!! The constant selecting of your fighter, then waiting for the screen to tell you it's your turn, and watching the other team makes their moves first...etc. etc. So far I have played 3 missions in the story-line....... and it took 3 hours of tedious running around fighting. The game previews are very misleading as they give the impression that the pace of this game is much faster than it really is.Also, the game does not do well with letting you know what things do.. Icons and classes and this and that. In fact, you are kind of thrown to the wolves to figure things out yourself. This isn't horribly bad...but still a little annoying trying to understand the environment.  The worst part of this game so far is the STUPID AI....and I mean AI as in artificial ignorance. Watching the enemy run by 3-4 of my fighters aimlessly to attack someone far away...or watching the enemy run around without doing anything just to double back and then buff themselves was just terrible.  It would be nice if there was a way to speed up the context menus by clicking through them.. like, how many times do I need to see each fighter and wait for the dialog to tell me it's my turn?  The game could be much better if it allowed more use of your mouse for clicking items etc. like most tactical turned based games. This is by far the slowest moving and overly boring tactical turned based I have owned... It looks great and I like the concept...but there needs to be less clutter and more user control. I spent $40 for this game and now beyond my refund limit. This game is not worth $40.

_childDocuments_.review: I was expecting a far better game experience than what was delivered. I love Mordheim but there is something lacking with Necromunda. The AI is not intelligent at all and the enemy will often get stuck on terrain or run in circles. The AI doesn't seek out any tactical advantages, as I went to raid a enemy base and watched all the enemy AI units bunch up on a single roof top where my sniper and heavy just bombarded them into submission. Also some of the enemy seemed to have twice the amount of movement and action points than I had, for a new gang this was a pain as you would get a enemy run across the map, shoot three times at me and then run all the way back from where they came from. The visuals are nice, but the camera gets wonky when it gets trapped between the terrain and characters. The cut scenes in between the story missions are nice but suffer from a bit of lag on my machine which is fairly beefy. The story missions see you flitting between various Houses in the Underhive, I would of liked to see each gang with its own story. As a Warhammer fan it pains me to see such a promising tactical turn based game with problems like I have experienced, and after playing Xcom game along with Mordheim it falls short on being just a good game. As of right now best not buy it, wait till it is on sale or till the developer has fixed some of the problems.

_childDocuments_.review: The Game looks fantastic and the customisations are pretty good. Weapon skin options could be expanded but I spend about a quarter of my time fiddling with setups and load-outs between missions.Why do I spend 1/4th of my time with equipment? Bad Gear management tools and inventory systems. With no way to sort gear into tiers/value/similar types if you try keeping things you might need you end up with too much gear. Would you like to have all these boosters for your gang so you get more crits/hits? Yes.Will you end up with lower tier chaff you have to dig through the inventory system to sell? Double yes; the fix to this is a sell from inventory option, along with more sorting options.Model/Crew Customisataion: On point! Without a full palette you still get a great selection to customise your gang, The highlight of the game really.Maps: There are some and after a little while you will get to know them very well. Watching the AI navigate efficiently will teach you tricks, but after 40 hours they are already repetitive.AI/NPC: They move efficiently, and then move like idiots. They get caught on geometry and get stuck instead of efficient use of AP/MP (action/movement economy). I've had missions become boring because instead of a challenge I was just eliminating enemy gangers who were doing daft things; I had a 1v1v1v1 Pit Fight where they all went into the lowest "pit" and I camped the 2 exits, this is bad AI.Gameplay Design: The Early game has a vibe of lethality. The wrong move, low tier gear, lower skills all give you the Necromunda vibe of a harsh life in the Underhive. You get some wins, collect more gear, get more skills and progress through missions. Things get harder, the enemy gears up, gets higher skills, and after a mid game of pwning you end up with later gameplay feeling akin to early gameplay; the enemies just have more HP and better gear so you have skills but things are back to the same feel of early gameplay. It just feels unchanging.Bugs: AI can PATH the hell out of getting to their spot and sometimes they play smart. But this becomes more and more surprising as you watch them run in circles and get stuck more commonly. So you plan on it, and use it to your advantage to win missions. Infinite AP/MP Glitch: I have not replicated it but I got an infinite AP/MP glitch from kneeling and standing in one mission (On a Lay Mechanic). Damn right I exploited it! Dropped turrets everywhere, wiped out all the other gangers. Hoarded all the loot into a Loot Chest. • I am testing replication methods, keeping the 3 influencing gangers for it. Will post a howto/bug report if I do it again.• Loot Chests have infinite capacity. So they are excellent dumping spots for salvage so you can cherry pick what you want to keep. Combine this with an infinite AP/MP glitch and you save yourself a lot of trouble finding what to take back to your hideout. Loot crates should not have limits, but with the glitch it's an obvious benefit.CAMERA FREAKOUT SHIMMY: Every now and then the follow camera will glitch into geometry and freak out, press space, move camera. Not a huge bug but a pain. Summary: I enjoy turn based tactical shooters, so I will keep playing this, but for as much as I enjoy it, I can't recommend the game.+ Gang Customisation+ Captures the Necromunda Skirmish Vibe- Repetitive- AI/NPC likes to run around in circles like a bored Zoo animal- (AFAIK) no Map Tools or modding support to make this game into a player driven cult classic. I am rather aware that GW Licensing is just a perineum swamp and they wont allow this, but it would transform the game monumentally.- Enemy Gangers can Spawn and throw a seemingly impossible grenade across the map. - Gameplay just becomes repetitive. Higher difficulties don't bring much to the table but more HP/DMG and the crippled AI doesn't scale to offer a challenge tactically.

_childDocuments_.review: Put it simply? If you like Necromunda in the tabletop, get it. It'll tie you over till you get back to your gaming group with this pandemic is over or whatever.If you've never heard of Necromunda, but want a turn based strategy game? This may not be for you.This is the sort of game that really feels like it can be good, but isn't out of the gate. Just a few more tweaks, adding in some extra FREE features from the tabletop (An actual morale system, kidnapping rival gangers, certain weapons are cheaper depending on your gang, etc), and making the gangs feel different from one another (outside of customization).Story: It exists, I guess. From what I understand, the story missions are just one big tutorial to get you used to how the gameplay works. You cannot customize any of the gangs within the story, it is set in stone.Gang War: This is the real game, and let me tell you, it is... Let's just go through some things.---A.I: The A.I in this game has what I like to call Fire Emblem Syndrome. FES, to shorten it, describes the NPCs in almost every FE game:They will, with no regard to their own life, rush the weakest character they can find to try and murder it. This usually means the NPC dies horrifically in every instance. Now, imagine that where, in a game where making a mistake can cost you the match, the NPCs do this to any living creature that is holding a box. NPCs will walk through multiple traps, multiple overwatches, some random ambusher, only to finally limp to their target and whiff entirely. I would say that is a random occurrence, but it happens every single match. Not to mention that the A.I will get stuck on random little cliffs for who knows how long, run in circles for no reason, grenade themselves, stack unstackable buffs on top of one another, and usually not make smart decisions.---Map and PoV: While I understand having a map helps in this game, there are times where I think the map can be a big crutch. I don't mean this in a bad way. Again, this game has multiple levels on each map that you have to keep track of. But, I truly wish the map wouldn't show you where the enemy is, only where the enemy will spawn. You're fighting what amounts to a maze that happens to look like a city, it should feel like that. That goes for PoVs and actions as well. I shouldn't know where the enemy is until I see them. I shouldn't know what he has up his sleeve until he tries something. Knowing someone is peaking a corner for a sick overwatch makes games very predictable. I understand that in the tabletop, you know where everyone is and you know what everyone is doing, but that's so everyone doesn't get confused about what's doing what and who's who. Trust me, play the tabletop with a buddy and you'll understand what that means a whole lot more.---Actual Matches: Each match goes on for a set number of rounds, which is fine until you remember that you are usually fighting against two or even three different gangs. In the TT, in order to make each loss feel bad, they made a morale system. Losing gangers too fast? Take a break check. Pass the check? Keep on fighting. Fail the check? The gang grabs whoever they can and bolts before they lose more of their gang. This made players more aware of their decisions and made them play with a more tactical mindset. In the video game, the matches drag on so hard that it honestly made me leave a mission to just get it over with. Adding in a few more factors that will help end matches sooner would help so much.(Small little things)Adding a biography section to each character would be amazing for those that want to have a connection to each ganger. It would add so much to everyone's gang and make each victory and defeat feel more impactful.Let us have our 10v10 matches. Even if it means losing out on free for all gameplay, I want my gang to feel like a gang. Right now, it feels like you're just a few friends that wanted to go and punch people for fun one night.Conclusion: In all honesty, there is so much they could have just borrowed from the TT. From the battlefield advantages of holding territory for your gang, to twists that randomly occur on the field.Do NOT get me wrong, this has massive potential that is hidden within. This has the possibility of being the golden child of the Warhammer fandom, but not right now. If you bought the game and have issues with it, take to the forums and talk about what they need to add into the game. If you haven't bought the game, take to the forums and talk about what WILL make you buy the game. You literally have the power to make sure this game doesn't turn into DoWIII, a game that no longer has official support from the devs. Fight long, fight hard, make sure this game gets the recognition it deserves.

_childDocuments_.review: I played a lot of Mordheim so I was excited to basically play single player and build my gang. The experience is ok. I wouldn't say they improved anything from Mordheim. It feels like they tried to make the same game with a different skin/flavor.I would have liked to see them improve on their loot and armor systems a bit, and add some more features to customize the gang so that it really feels like mine is unique.Instead it seems like they have struggled hard with the AI, which routinely nades itself when no enemies are around, has pathing issues, and just generally doesn't seem to have a cohesive strategy.My other big issue is that combat is painstakingly slow. You have to watch each character to everything, including your enemies and it's just a time sink. The AI takes a while to figure out what it wants to do sometimes so that makes it worse. The repetitive "your turn" and "select your character" is annoying and you can't skip past it. Even when there's only one character left to pick it still makes you select them. This just makes the game feel clunky and unpolished. These design decisions must have eaten up a lot of QA time as it takes a lot of wasted time to go through a round of combat.There's the potential for them to salvage this with patches and turn it around with some cool DLC later, but they really need to fix the AI and flow of combat.I would also strongly recommend they don't release additional unit types as with Mordheim, as these didn't really add much to the game. I'd prefer they release something that changes the feel of the game or a faction that feels different. The chaos faction for Mordheim were a lot of fun because they mutated as they gained experience. It made me want to play a separate run just with them. The skaven also felt unique. I haven't played all three factions yet, but they don't seem to be utterly distinct in a deep and meaningful way at a glance.

_childDocuments_.review: Underhive Wars is, at it's core, a team-based turn-based tactical game (somewhat similar to XCOM). That said, it's effectively split into two main elements.The first element is the single-player campaign/tutorial. It's fun overall. The story is serviceable and the AI is brainless, but it's still entertaining. Depending on how familiar you are with these kind of games and how much of a speedrunner you are, this will likely take you 20-35 hours to complete. The second element is the multi-player aspect. This is where you play against other players, attack their hideouts, and so on. I don't have a lot of experience with this so I won't comment too extensively, but it's about as close to you can get to a digital version of tabletop Necromunda right now. I get the feeling that this is where the developer focused their efforts and it's the game element they're really selling.Why did I point out the two elements? Because it kind of seems like they should be separate games. I would have happily paid for just a fully fleshed-out single-player campaign game, but I will never extensively play multiplayer. On the flip-side though, I guess they never could have sold the mutliplayer aspect as it's own standalone game. Dunno. Overall it's worth the money I paid for it. Your mileage may vary.Thanks for reading!

_childDocuments_.review: A Disappointing Return to Necromunda – 2/5 StarsHaving embarked on my Necromunda journey 25 years ago, I was eagerly awaiting the release of this game, hoping it would capture the essence of the classic tabletop experience. Unfortunately, the reality of Version 1.0 has left me deeply disappointed.On paper, this game had immense potential. The gritty, tactical combat and the richly detailed world of Necromunda should have been a recipe for success. Instead, what we received is a buggy mess with painfully flawed AI and gameplay that feels more like a chore than an enjoyable experience. Each match drags on endlessly, leaving me frustrated and unfulfilled.One of the most glaring issues is the movement mechanics. Characters zip across the map with unrealistic speed, with AI units often covering vast distances in just two turns. This not only breaks immersion but also makes strategic planning nearly impossible. The lack of a proper tutorial only adds to the confusion, forcing players to turn to online resources just to figure out the basics. The weapons, which should be a highlight in a game like this, are underwhelming and fail to inspire any excitement.It’s clear that a significant amount of effort went into the models and terrain, which are undeniably beautiful. However, it seems that the developers realized early on that the gameplay was severely lacking, leading to delays after the alpha stage. One can only imagine how much worse it must have been at that time, considering the current state is still so deeply flawed.A prime example of the AI’s incompetence: I watched in disbelief as an AI character, standing right next to a doorway, chose to run up two flights of stairs, jump off the level above, and land on the other side of the very doorway it could have simply walked through. This 40-second spectacle left me baffled and impatient, waiting for the turn to finally end.Before any DLCs are released, this game desperately needs a major overhaul. The foundation is there, but the execution falls woefully short. For now, I’d recommend trying Mordheim instead. While it has its flaws, it’s far superior in delivering a tactical experience.Consider this a warning—proceed with caution.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're old enough to remember the tabletop game, then this is for you. If you're not, it's for you (because you like domination). You only need to play a few hours to realise it's paid itself back on the purchase price (pretty low these days, from what I can see, especially if you get it in a sale). After a few hours you will find time for this game. It's frustrating at first but then you see how it's intended to be played. We'll get into that a bit later, but first a discussion of what the game is like.Graphically, it is quite adequate, especially considering it is a few years old now. The graphics are minimal in glitches and run quite smoothly, better if you have a high end PC but also works with integrated graphics, say intel 600 as a half-decent minimum, and 8-16gb of DDR4 and a decent processor like an i7-8000+ as there's lots of computational aspects to crunch.Visually the game is polished, the characters are detaied and the worlds elaborate enough, without being extreme and exclusive to high-end. There isn't really much ugliness to detract (partly due to the immersive gameplay) and you won't have time to stop and stare as you need to get on and develop your skills, and (ahem) kills. Cut scenes are pretty fun too, and the ladies aren't to be messed with - just see what's left of those who have.Tactically the game involves the understanding of strategy basics and you are expected to be shot at in order to learn them. You are put in the line of fire and on the back foot, and that's what you have to do to the enemy ultimately, in order to outlast them. There are hazards abound and choices you make affect outcomes down the line, so it's quite a brain-teaser and something you need to be capable of on automatic, but it takes a few rounds of dying with your whole squad to learn this. The developer has really mastered the gameplay flow, the level design (okay, there are a couple of snags but it's near perfection), the character load-out and skills they have. Fortunately the AI falls into traps tactically if you don't just throw yourself at their mercy - do that and they will dominate you!Faithfully this game plays true to the general lore of the Necrumunda world - anyone who remembers what this is is either avid or has an unusual sense for these sorts of things. About the only weapon I recollect is the Lascannon and Autocannon, and their single-handed compliments. There are grenade loudouts, and players can not only go on overwatch at the end of a round and get entrenched, they can also create an aura of protection that heals nearby team members. It all seems fairly faithful to the tabletop game and anyone who remembers better than this is probably an employee or kept the figurines well after giving up playing them. This game is not for all, no game is, but it is incredibly accessible for a turn-based 3D shooter tactic game, something that is fairly new - especially since there aren't cut scenes in between actions like  there are in XCOM 2.So in summary, it's a 3D virtualised world you could never fit in your bedroom when you were a child but is twice as mean as your parents were when they needed to collect you from your friend's house and you'd got part way through a game of the tabletop version. There an immersiveness that sticks with you, even when you've mastered it, and there are fond memories of when you entered the level for the first time and were buffeted by the acridity and post-apocalyptic industrial griminess. There's the laughter at seeing your team decimated over and over - until you 'get' it and the sense of humiliation at letting them face their peril. There's also the new things the game brings, like the level of atmosphere you no longer have to imagine which instantly teleports you back to your childhood memories of the tabletop version. This isn't just replication or imitation, it's thought-provoking additions that add a sense of haste to your recollection, and a 'safe' place again for a bunch of cherished memories.

_childDocuments_.review: Quick bits:+ The tactical nature of the game works nicely.+ The grimdark setting (Warhammer 40k universe) feels spot on, particularly with all of the items and references to the TT game (even minor ones like Second Best).+ Mechanically varied with enough complexity to keep a player engrossed.+ Most importantly (for me at least) the game is fun so far!- Some of the AI decisions and pathfinding appears to be a bit buggy, needs some polish in this area.- The gameplay feels slower than I normally like, even for a tactical game- The level design/movement areas could use some additional work, particularly with multi-level spots.- I do wish we had more gangs (Van Saar, Delaque, Cawdor). If the game does well, I'd expect to see more down the road.* Some players may find the environments and perspective to be difficult to get your bearings.* Navigation is trickier than other tactical games and needs some getting used to.* Focus on picking up the basics in the campaign mode as it generally does a good job explaining things. I think the gameplay tutorials are *only* found there so jumping into another mode before you do some campaign missions may prove difficult.I've long been a fan of the WH40k universe and have been waiting to see when a Necromunda tactics PC game would arrive. It really is nice to see all the little details that Rogue Factor has put into the game itself and I'm looking forward to playing through more of this.There's a lot going on in the game, particularly with how you can set up your gangers' skills, or just the gang itself. As your gangers go through warfare with other gangs, they'll gain XP which you can use to upgrade stats or purchase abilities. Of course, if they get shot down, they may come out of the battles with significant injuries as well. The gang management aspect seems pretty nifty, though 100% make sure your gangers are going into battle equipped. It may have been a bug, but suddenly joining a match with repercussions without your weapons was an unwelcome surprise.As a fan of tactical games, I have enjoyed this iteration of the concept so far. Criticisms as seen above, mainly have to deal with some of the AI and pacing challenges. The AI in particular could use a little extra poking as there were more than a few times we see an enemy making more questionable decisions than expected. While one could say these gangers were on more than a healthy amount of drugs which affected their behavior (fitting for the setting) it happened with a higher regularity than it should. The pacing overall was slower than expected. Not too out of the ordinary for tactical games, but definitely on the slow side even for that genre. A lot of that time is soaked up in watching your opponents make their moves which can take time since the AI thinks really hard about what it wants to do, followed by running around for a marginally better angle to just overwatch behind a wall. Finding where everything is sitting can be difficult and I'd highly recommend using the tactical view point and strat map regularly.Overall, I do recommend the game. I found it to be enjoyable with a lot of potential, particularly with how much is going on just in the Necromunda setting. The flaws listed above may be dealbreakers for certain people and if you're looking for a faster-paced game, this may not be your bag. If you enjoy tactical games or like the setting, give it a try!

_childDocuments_.review: It's basically Valkyria Chronicles but instead of being weird jank weeb speedrun nonsense, it's a fun and engaging small-squad tactics game. I was expecting something more like XCOM, but honestly? This is fine, and possibly even better because the new format means I'm not measuring it against XCOM, but against Valkyria Chronicles. _childDocuments_.review: I'd recommend this game with some reservations. Things I like:-Streamlined some elements of Mordheim, such as movement, troop deployment, and so on.-The aesthetic is fun. They function as mini-campaigns and it's pretty engaging overall.-Wield a fire arm and a melee weapon at the same time. I like the aesthetic of itThings I don't really like:-The skill system does not feel robust - there is not much synergy, and the synergy that does exist seems to make anything that doesn't involve dealing damage a waste of time and effort.-Class options, likewise, seem pretty meh.-Environmental hazards are virtually non-existent-I'd like there to be some big bad monsters, and it's just more gangers.-the kinds of missions available in operations are very samey-The AI is, um, not great.-Cosmetics are locked behind a campaign that I have zero interest in continuing.If you liked Mordheim: COTD and you like the gutterpunk aesthetic of Necromunda, then you -might- like this title. _childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love this game, but there is no way I can recommend it to anyone as it currently is. TLDR version is that it feels they were trying to make the fights LONGER, not BETTER. Its entirely possible that you fight 1 engagement per hour, meaning you won't be able to refund after your second mission due to Steam's 2 hour of gameplay refund policy. Let me review the game, based on the description on its store page.DIVE INTO THE NECROMUNDA WORLD LIKE NEVER BEFORE:This is absolutely a great game when it comes to exploring an Underhive. Its not just a flat or 2-3 level surface like Mordheim or XCom. You're climbing, jumping, ziplining, and using elevators and grappling hooks in every direction. The 3-D movement adds another dynamic to the game that was non-existent in other games like this. Aesthetically, it does give the sense of chaos and desperation that exists in the Necromunda world. LEAD YOUR OWN GANG IN BLOODY TACTICAL COMBATNow begins the problem. While you CAN customize your gang, some slots are locked until you finish the story mode. The Story mode itself is 15 missions (about 10 hours of gameplay) so you can't just breeze through it. The tactical combat isn't that satisfying either; movement is based on distance from starting point (not distance travelled) and it will only measure that distance horizontally, meaning a soldier could run up 10 flights of stairs and not spend any Movement Points. There's very little advantage that can come from going into cover, since its so easy to flank people. Close range combat is off to, because its sooo easy to disengage from your opponent. You also need to worry about your weapon jamming after 3-4 shots, in addition to reloading when you run out of ammo. There's no way to skip or fast-forward AI turns, and the game forces you to watch every single enemy move (keep in mind, in some levels, there's 2 AI combatants to every one of yours). All this means that you'll spend nearly half your time waiting for your turn. PLAY SOLO OR UP TO 4 PLAYERS ONLINEThis is where they promote their 'rich narrative campaign', or the story mode. Simply put, the story mode is bland, boring and predictable. You switch between three factions in the same campaign, and there's no customization of your troops in between, so there's no connection between missions. Since you don't spend time with one faction, you end up not caring about any of the characters. Also, the story has so many immersion-breakers and plot holes. Each faction leader is led by someone with a specific name, such as Captain Flynt (Orlocks) and Blutvor (Goliaths). These two were enemies you have to kill in the 2nd and 3rd missions, yet you play as them later as if they never met you. A glaring plothole happens before the final mission, when Tesserra jumps through vault doors as they were closing, seemingly abandoning her allies. Yet when the mission starts, all her allies start next to her.Overall, I'm only still playing because I slogged through the story mode to unlock all options in the sandbox mode, and I don't want to feel I wasted my time. I wouldn't recommend this to anyone as it is, and I really hope they fix the pacing and combat issues.

_childDocuments_.review: At first, I thought this game was a decent 5 or 6 out of 10: fun enough if you like this kind of game, especially if you also like the setting, although not something to recommend to a general audience. After another few hours, I don't think so. The game falls apart with more than one AI team on the map. 5/10 1v1s turn into 2/10 when you introduce 1v1v1v1: it's a game, it runs, but it's never fun. The AI falls apart, turns take f o r e v e r, and mission success or failure is determined by what random direction the AI's braindead flailing goes in. 1v1v1v1 are more common than not at later tiers of the singleplayer Operations, and the campaign is boring, so unless you're going to play the game exclusively on "Custom 1v1"... game is bad.Ordinarily, 20 hours of gameplay before running into design choices that break the fun would still be plenty for a $33 game, but not when about 13 of those hours have been spent w a i t i n g.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game for $7 NZD on sale and it is definitely worth the money IMO. Here is why:The Good:Graphics are great and the aesthetics are bang on. The gangs feel pretty unique and the customisation makes them feel like *my* gangThe UI is good and clean and I have only had a few minor quibbles which mostly arise from me not reading the tutorial stuff carefully. I played a lot of Mordheim (and liked it) but that UI was ****ing janky as. They have ironed out the issues in this one and pretty much all of my issues with that one have been resolved!The story is good (solid 7/10) for the solo campaign and I enjoyed playing it all.The actual game play is fantastic. They have nailed Necromunda and they managed to escape so many of the limitations of the actual table top game. I love the near unlimited range of options and ways you can approach things. You can sabotage ziplines (THE ZIPLINES ARE AWESOME!!!!), set up traps, destroy features in the environment, create features (pheromone traps, barricades, health stations, etc.) repair ziplines, etc, on top of all the combat and support stuff! There is also a huge range of mission types to boot.The Bad:There are two significant issues with the game.There are very few people in the servers, so having a MP match with a random player is very very unlikely, which is a massive pity.The second issue is the AI. As you will see in almost ever bit of feedback, the AI for the computer is super dumb. Like ridiculously dumb. It will consistently make terrible moves which means that there is almost no challenge if you are going to play single player, which is really really unfortunate since everything else is so good!The good news is there is a way around both of these problems - buy it cheap for you and your friends and play with them!!!! Unfortunately it does look like the devs are finished with the game but it is certainly worth the price I paid and I would have been happy to pay probably twice that for the game as it is now, even with it's foibles.

The animations can sometimes chop a little, or lag in the middle of an animation, but we'll chalk that up to being part my machine and part the game.Sound: Good, solid sound. The guns give the feeling of heft and power, and none of the sounds (especially death sounds) makes me want to put my hard drive in a chipper.Gameplay: A few issues with game balance, to be honest, with opponent squads starting in obviously advantageous positions in the story campaign, making some missions a slog to get the objectives complete without losing half your gang to traps and initial starting positions that look like your gang lost their way and got caught in the open.All in all, the game is very worthwhile to me as a single player fan. I won't go into MP, as I don't give  two whits about it. I'll leave that to others.
