_childDocuments_.review: Seems like quite the Marmite game. Casual puzzler wrapped up in some immersive environments and shiny graphics.Turn based tactics on unreal engine, with some persistent downtime admin to be done between games in the form of gang management. Scratches the same itch as games like Xcom although the IP and mechanics are very different.If you're coming from Mordheim then expect it to be different not just more of the same but with guns, that said it does share a lot of similarities and ones experience with the game will translate pretty quickly and provide some comfort to the learning curve.The campaign is more of a series of set piece scenarios linked by an audio narrative and cut-scenes. There is no persistent gang or much player agency one simply has to beat the scenario with the assets available and can re-try or replay as many times as they desire before moving onto the next mission once unlocked successfully. The campaign does serve as an extended tutorial and interactive story, with a few non essential cosmetic unlocks as reward on completion. However, it is entire skippable for those that don't like that form of puzzle play scenarios.The alternative is the persistent gang where one is much more hands on and immersed in the development and well being of their own gang and takes on "operations" a series of turns where one can select from the available missions each turn and compete against rival gangs in these mini campaigns. The operations have definable parameters that remain in affect until there completion or the player opt out. In this manner a gang can be developed as the player repeatedly takes on new operations with challenge tweaked as the player desires.Multiplayer can be taken at anytime and can count towards or be done separately with regards to persistent consequences. The MP formats are fairly restrictive but do allow for both pvp and pvE match set-ups.The biggest complaints i've seen on feedback are game instability and poor ai.The game runs on unreal engine, as with most games i find this reliable on my system with the same being true of Necromunda. I have yet to experience any real instability or game breaking bugs commonly reported although i have had to restart a turn when a series of actions consistently caused the animation to clip the character out the map. In instances where the path is blocked the movement animation now seems to skip and the character is teleported to the end point. While a  little ugly, it does seem to prevent crashing.The ai, does do a lot of dumb actions and doesn't necessarily punish the player in a way a live opponent would. However, it does seem to use a lot of the abilities (not always optimally) and it has a decent grasp for moving the characters around the quite complex 3d landscape but again not all ways in the most tactical manner. It is less predicable and more nuanced than Mordheim AI, but that in turn makes it less aggressive and in the most case far less of a challenge.I think the biggest issue is less the AI but the lack of fog of war. With the player having full access to info on all actions taken by all parties on the map it hinders the inherent advantage of the AI while allowing the player to circumvent the AI actions that could have under surprise conditions have had much more impact. Given that there are skills that "scan the battlefield" and precedent for blind fights was established through Mordheim mechanics it does feel like a backwards step in design choice.The other mechanic that i miss from Mordheim is ambush and or map creeps, either that or i have been incredibly lucky thus far or not played with enough rep to test the harder operation settings. Every mission is what it says it is, the objective doesn't ever get flipped with a "surpirse!" and the maps don't have any un-expected "3rd party additions" adding variety only the gangs that were announced pre-mission will attend the level.For those that like the IP, the environment and casual turn based puzzle games this game still has a lot to offer and good replay/grind value to pass away the hours while watching ones efforts mature in the form of a persistent gang(s), especially on a discount.However, if you're looking to flex and need something to brutally punish the player with hardcore 'cause and consequence' game play, then Necromunda will probably disappoint.win10 x64, 8gb ram, gtx970 (4gb), 1920x1080@60hz native - 60fps (v-sync'd)

_childDocuments_.review: You are probably reading reviews to decide if you should buy this game or not. I will stop you right there. Don't bother: instead go to the steam discussion page and enjoy the complete sh!& sh0w that is happening there. You will wonder no longer. Instead of this game, check Mordheim (you can read my review about it - which was on the #1 on the top page for a long while). Put your hype/fanboyism/whatever aside and bear with me for a while ;)When Necromunda has been announced the hype was there. Mordheim, after experiencing a very harsh launch and a wave of negative reviews (deja vu?) still has a large-ish fanbase up till this day. Just see the reviews for the game, especially made by people with  No wonder then, that when hype train departed and we stopped hearing anything new about the game right after, people started to worry. Suddenly, when people thought this project was abandoned news came in! Game will launch soon, real soon! Head to steam and preorder asap! Wait... what? And where is the gameplay? Where are details about the game? What about preview/early access (at least for streamers). Amount of info they gave us was very limited with scripted youtube videos showing almost nothing.People were worried that they are going to recieve half-baked product that has reached its deadline and was pushed to release in whatever the state it was . It did not take a clairvoyant to predict exactly what had just happened with Necromunda. And there it was. The release date. We still had hope - it cannot be this bad, right? Game has holes like a swiss cheese. Its basically an empty shell with basic features riddled with bugs and undeveloped AI.There is a fair amount of players who bought this game purely for PvP. Probably as a way to play digitalized version of a tabletop game. PvP. Is. Not. Working. Since. The. Release. Yup, not kidding. People have major issues with finishing a  PvP match. Now let us think, when do the games like this offer their biggest multiplayer potential? During the release, when in-game player numbers are peaking. Necromunda is already in a serious decline at this point, will there be anyone to play PvP after the issues are fixed? Sure, but will it be enough to keep that mode going? Doubt it. For me, campaign is not so bad as people say it is. Cinematics are a nice touch - they don't give any of the Warhammer Grimdark vibe though, teenage cartoon more like. Although they could implement story in so many better ways - in a current state that is only one kinda OK thing in the whole game.So, what about the main treat - gang wars? Bland. Just so you know, in Mordheim I have a warband I've invested roughly 150 hours into (which in Mordheim standards is not even that much) and I still have tons of things to do with it untill I will be completly done. Here? People with 40-60 in game hours claim that they have maxed out all they could and have nothing else to do. After spending about 15-20 hours on the campaign (had to repeat 2 missions DUE TO A BUG) I'm left with 25 hours in gang operations and it is already starting to feel repetitive. Nothing new happens and sadly, from what others say it never will. Your first couple games will look mostly the same as your end-game. You'll get items with bigger numbers on them, maybe a cybernetic limb if you are super lucky and a set of skills where you will be using mostly 1-2 of them.I've been rather negative the whole time so let's talk about positives for a bit:+ game looks really nice, love the artwork+ on the visual side maps look very different, which is nice. + games are shorter (or at least would be shorter if not for the AI and poorly implemented notifications) - I personally prefer it that way. In Mordheim I could easly lose 1-2 hours to a single match, and having to leave in a middle of the game would mean basically starting over. Here you automatically save after quitting, so some lessons have been learned I guess.+/- easier to learn than Mordheim: with all of the gangers available from the start, and a bit more simplistic character development you can really quickly get a hang of things. Downside is, the game really lacks depth due to this :(There are so many unfinished, rushed, ill-considered implementations that I could write a book about it, so lets stick only to the best ones:- Picking a different house/gang doesnt really matter. All of the gangs have the same classes, same weapons, they mostly play the same. Only difference is one faction gets + X to a certain stat and other gets + Y to the different one and additionaly a set of house skills.- customization and item design is no different between levels. Your characters look the same, only thing you get are additional skills, chipsets that are basically stat boosts and higher numbers on items. There are no new items and modifications that unlock along with your progress.- some items are just plain useless. Using them costs almost the same amount or Action Points as basic shot or skill, with most of the nades/mines doing next to no dmg or having shi77y effects. Debuffs/buffs are pointless for most of times as well imho. I found it way better to just blindly rush on and nuke your enemies than to ACTUALLY TRY USING TACTICS. And I'm talking about hard + difficulties. - Small maps combined with high movement: 90% of the encounters are extraction: so most of the maps, objective wise you will be able to rush and finish your objective in couple of turns OR see as AI moves, picks up q item and runs to extracts in one single turn without any way to stop it. That is just poor game design. - ... With so many defective parts of the game bugs are not even suprising at this point.-  is hilarious at first, sad later and straight up annoying in the end. Couple years ago me and my friends had to write a basic unity game for a project. We were not interested in gaming industry so we scrapped a quick crappy rpgish game with hard coded set of rules for enemy AI. I swear we did it better than this game. Issues with this game are numerous and most of people end their reviews or topics with "Hopefully they will fix this or that". But just think about it for a sec. Will they really? Today most of published games are result of market research: what we can publish using the minimum effort and getting the maximum profit and then move on to the next project. Some issues with this game will be easy to fix but other? Like AI or simply no content, especially for the late game? I don't think that devs will put xxx more hours in repairing what is basically a very basic and early game design in the first place. With already bad rep and mixed steam reviews there is no point of saving already lost project.Thanks to all who managed till the end!You are beautiful and deserve better games!

_childDocuments_.review: After Rogue Factor's attempt at Mordheim, I went into this game not expecting much. However this attempt at Necromunda has so far been absolutely fantastic. Leaps and bounds better than Mordheim as much as I hate to say it, as I have a lot of nostalgia for The tabletop Mordheim.Don't be swayed by all the negative reviews on here. I've read most negative reviews and they are from people who complain the AI is iffy, we'll I must be lucky because the AI has been perfectly fine for me except on one occasion where the enemy ran at a wall for a few seconds before stopping and going into overwatch. So what? I'm sure the AI will improve with updates anyway.People also complain the game is too slow or you have to wait too long for your turn.. This bewilders me. A lot of the people saying this have stated they have played Mordheim, well Mordheim feels slower than this game so I don't understand where they are coming from. This game is based on a tabletop game, so yes you will only be playing your turn, then waiting for other players to play their turn. That's the problem with society these days, no-one has any patience. If the AI took their turns at super speed, it would ruin the game and confuse the player/s. The speed of this game is just about right I'd say.Other's complain the Story is boring, well they obviously don't understand that the Story mode is there to teach you the game. I don't think the dev's were going for a best selling novel.Visually the game is very nice and an atmospheric soundtrack add's to the well designed rendition of the underhives.This game won't be for everyone, but it has exceeded my expectations.

_childDocuments_.review: In Necromunda, you play a small warband against the AI or other players. There are 5 classes (2 ranged DPS, 1 melee DPS, 1 offensive and 1 defensive support) and you can develop your characters in a sandbox.  You select scenarios and play against up to 3 AI, receive loot and exp. There is also a linear campaign but without character development which serves as a lengthy tutorial. There is also a multiplayer mode but I havent played it yet. While there is great potential, the game is very buggy including bugs with complete loss of progress and seems overall poorly polished.Good-graphics are great with great warhammer 40k vibe-nice variety of characters and skills, even though it's simplified compared to its predecessor Mordheim-matches against several parties at once (unfortunately, this also greatly rewards passive and defense tactics as it's best to hold back and only attacked weakened enemies at the edges)Neutral-enforced ironman- some like it, some notBad-tons of bugs- abusing you customers as beta-testers is not ok; game should not have been releases in its current state--crashes take you back to the desktop and you might lose progress due to corrupted save files (which should just not happen with enforced ironman)--loss of gang achievements ("infamy") due to bugs-horrible AI which makes the game even on deadly (highest difficulty) was too easy: as you have to watch every enemy move seeing them grenade themselves or running in circles is only fun for the first few times-very slow gameplay-weapons are simplified and quite similar/ generic, e.g. plasma guns are just quirkier versions of autoguns etc.

_childDocuments_.review: A good tactics game thats a 90% improvement from their last game Mordheim. Whats the ten percent? The AI's been handicapped to let people win which may have been a overreaction from their last game where people jumped in lost their first game and uninstalled right away. That and the camera shakes when between a model and a object behind the model a problem with games since 3d games were made. The story mode exists and its basically a tutorial mode. Its not bad but serviceable the voice acting though leaves much to be desired. Its awkwardly delivered and too clean to be about juvenile criminals. Former is on voice director's part the latter I blame Black Library and modernity for being too afraid of being called out to make something memorable.Moving on to positives, The customization is the best in any Warhammer game released better than Space Marine. There is a great amount of models and colors to choose and you can change the colors on every piece of the model to be different so you can make a vomitous mess which fits in this setting and is 100% on point for THE Kitbashing tabletop game. A massive leap forward from mordheim where the faces were just a texture and there were only 2 choices. The character leveling and skills are also massive in how characters can be made into and what they can specialize in that also applies to what fighters you take on your team for that specific mission. It all culminates in game where the tactics are the deciding factor in winning or losing.How you use your tactics to bring victory is on you and there are punishments for making a wrong decision. If your fighters lose all hp they aren't dead but roll on a table that has injuries and includes the possibilities of death. You are not promised a win and if its going badly you should get your gang out to avoid accumulating injuries on them. Eventually you may have to make a new gang when your current can no longer be up to even par, Such is Hive life.All in all its an improvement from their last game in almost every way, has deep customization and is on the players decisions making skills to win victory or to decide if a pyrrhic victory is even worth it. Its about the story in your head about your creation and to see if its a victory or a tragedy.

_childDocuments_.review: Necromunda is a turn based tactical rpg where you pit 5 of your cyber gangsters against 1-3 other same sized gangs. The game is essential a ranged and smaller squad focused version of its predecessors Mordheim, which is also an excellent game worth checking out. The significant draw back of the series is the lack of customization with different houses, the small number of classes, and the current stats and abilities leave a lot to be desired in leveling.  These are all areas that Mordheim shined in, and is sad to see Rogue Factor play them down so much. Despite that, Rogue Factor has made the game look and run amazing, especially in comparison to Mordheim. The AI is a bit wonky and sometimes make long winded moves for no reason, but the speed at which they do it and actually process the game is probably the best I've seen in any tactical rpg in this genre. The combat looks and feels amazing, and it leaves me hoping that with time, Rogue Factor will fix their wonky AI and add more customization. If they do fix those issues, this game will be the best in the genre (IMO). If not, its a simple, quick, and fun game you can drop some time into.

_childDocuments_.review: So I'm one of those people who played Necromunda in high school back in the 90s, and has picked up the reworked version of the tabletop game more recently as well. This game is not those games. But it does, I think, manage to capture something of the spirit of them, and it's definitely nailed the atmosphere. The game isn't perfect though. A lot of people have griped that some options are locked behind the campaign. That's a legitimate complaint, especially given the options in question (gas masks are pretty much iconic in Necromunda), but I kinda get it at the same time - they wanted you to be rewarded for completing it. At least they didn't paywall them, right? My bigger concern going forward is that the gangs really feel the same right now. I need to play more to be sure, but the gangs all appear to have more or less similar access to the same weapons and items, which tamps down on some of their unique appeal. I also strongly dislike the decision to make all the gangs co-ed because it strips the Escher of their uniqueness as the lone female gang. At least the devs allow you to opt out of "progress" during gang recruitment. Anyway, I suspect that the decision to introduce the saboteur/engineer classes also contributes to the feeling of same-ness. What the heck do Goliaths need a saboteur for? Why are the Escher tinkering with mechanical stuff instead of hurling chemicals every which way? Don't know, and no explanation appears to be forthcoming. Evidently the level design required it, so here we are. Looking a bit deeper, it's true that each gang has a small set of gang-specific skills, but those don't look sufficient--to me--to really set the existing gangs apart from each other. There are ways to get around this, of course. Offer individual gangs access to special armaments, limit/ban use of classes in certain gangs (will Van Saar really need a melee specialist?), etc. Guess we'll see what happens. The game isn't perfect, but I think it has a lot of potential and I have enjoyed playing it so far (though I did use the workaround to avoid the campaign). As a guy whose play-style is not particularly given over to objective-based play, I particularly enjoy that annihilating the enemy and then snagging a few objectives during a "looting round" is still an option. Nice touch, that. Stomping hipster Orlocks in the face is what Goliaths do best anyway, right? In light of how well the devs did with Mordheim, and given the wealth of material for them to explore in Necromunda (gangs, outlanders, guilds, Arbites, various underhive flora and fauna, etc.), I'm optimistic it'll keep getting better. (I haven't touched the PvP, so I cannot speak to that.)

_childDocuments_.review: I've already had a half-dozen people reach out to ask my opinion of the Necromunda: Underhive Wars video game. I guess my reputation for loving that IP really does proceed me. Well, I'm going to write it here instead of repeatedly pasting across Slack, Facebook Messenger, Steam Messages, and so on.TLDNR: Mediocre game that could improve with ongoing development (as is no doubt the plan). If you love Necromunda you're in for a bittersweet and skin-deep application of the IP to a mediocre turn-based strategy that's presently glitchy. You're probably better off waiting a couple years for the Legendary Edition, like with most Focus Home Interactive adaptations of Games Workshop Titles. If you're not a Necromunda fan, pass. Play any of the other XCOM-likes and you won't miss out on much. I will say though, the vertical traversal and map-altering gameplay may have appeal to niche competitive players that accept the phony ways the game deals with things like the nature of the universe.Caveat: I've only played the first half-dozen Story missions, but done so carefully. Regardless, your mileage may vary.It's set in the Necromunda world and leverages some of the tabletop game's great lore and art, but shares none of the tabletop rules. Once again, a game studio decided that well-balanced tabletop rules can't translate to video games, and as a video game developer I disagree. The story and cutscenes are neat, but not high quality for 2020 while the writing and voice acting play out like a 2001 Japanese PlayStation game.Gameplay is a lot buggy, and that can be frustrating when a silly bug or UX issue costs you a one hour game on the last infuriating click you should be able to perform. I can't seem to find instructions, but that'd help. The deeper I get into Necromunda, the more I'm baffled by some decisions.For instance, there are few mechanics that take verticality into mind. Most weapon ranges are horizontal only... so a 10M range appears to be an infinitely tall 20M cylinder, meaning you can shoot someone 9M away and 6 stories up, but not someone 11M away directly in front of you. However, template weapons like flamers actually calculate real distance and project cones - so the game must have the 8th grade math to calculate a hypotenuse.... they just decided it's better not to use it. Also, running 50M on a flat plane and then shooting is the same cost as running around and down five stories inside a complex building, 25M out the front door, shooting, then 25M back inside, and all the way back upstairs... even if the stairwells are placed in alternating corners of the building. That definitely left one of my gangers feeling unreasonably safe when he was probably a 400M journey around many corners and down many stairs, when he was really only 30M away straight as the crow flies on an XY plane.The arena mission is a total pain because AI Ambush skill always works, whereas your Ambush skill only triggers half the time, even with clear and unimpeded LOS. I've tested this repeatedly, and I have yet to two of my characters ambush an AI that walks between them, and so on.At times the AI seems to either have more AP than they should, or a bug is charging 2H attacks for the AP cost of 1H attacks. It could be some sort of buff or stat advantage they have, but the buffs are very poorly described and difficult to consume even if you really want to.So far I'm avoiding the good things about the game, and I'll keep doing that for a minute. I'm also avoiding the bad things most people would complain about, because I'm a game dev and understand why the AI is friggin' terrible. The many systems they've put in for traversal, exchanging MP for AP, and trading off buffs for cost, and radically altering the playing field... well they're not very interesting for humans but super tricky for AI. Frankly, the AI is bafflingly random and bad but I don't think I could do a better job with it. Where this rears its head though, is in balance. The Story Mode is balanced heavily in favour of the AI to compensate for how randomly stupid it is. This makes matches a crap shoot that's more about 'Did the AI inexplicably run into a corner over landmines it just laid, therefore giving me a fighting chance?' or 'Is the AI only stupid this time, and therefore wrecks me with its huge advantage?' Again, super tough problem for AI engineers to solve because of the upstream decisions of the design team, so that gets a pass from me.What doesn't get a pass are the friggin' bonehead UX decisions that would be so very easy to fix - and knowing games like this there's very little chance they'll be improved post-launch. Here's a very simple example: What does '↑' mean? If you guessed the arrow up key, you're wrong. The control map has that symbol for shift, and not because they're avoiding Latin script in their UX because the Control key is called 'CTRL'. Here's another one: three quarters of your early matches are played with a character that has a flamethrower and a virtually identical character that has an icethrower. The weapons and their icons look identical unless you compare them side-by-side, and the only way to see which is which is to hit 3 or I on that ganger's turn, then click their weapon and read the name on it. Not great. However, you have to choose which  ganger to select first every single turn and there's no way I've found to determine what their weapons are before you choose who to play. The biggest difference between them? It's only visible if you rotate the camera to the front, but the flamethrower has a rat skull on the barrel. There are many more examples of the UX failing players, so I'll stop here.Worst, in a game that's supposed to be all about consequences, progression and growth, the story mode doesn't let you keep looted weapons, doesn't care if you let characters die, and yet doesn't explain that. This led to me working really hard to keep all my gangers alive and loot all the good weapons, at a strategic sacrifice, for no reason.As a long-time Necromunda fan and game dev, I have to say I'm disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: Update Update: There has been another patch and a hot fix to the patch after a weekend because the patch broke everyone's ability to play.  Where are we at?  The AI may occasionally hit you with a grenade now, but in general it's still incompetent to an insulting degree, and I will still crash occasionally.  Also consider that when you crash it reverts to giving you next to no XP for your gangers when you come back in to the game, and despite it being crash heavy from day 1, they never thought to fix it by just looking at difficulty settings when calculating XP.At less than 100 players on average even after the last patch I will just leave 2 bits of advice.Rogue Factor:  Next time you release a game, slap an Early Access title on it.To anyone else considering the Necromunda license, this game in no way shape or form failed because of the license.  This game failed because of it's alpha version state at release, and it staying in this state for so long you have to wonder if more than 2 people are working on fixing it.  A lot of the original purchasers, many of them were wise enough to get a refund, are dying for a Necromunda experience on PC.Update: There has been a patch, I've played a fair amount, good news and bad news, but still don't buy yet.I haven't had it crash yet so they have definitely fixed at least some of the crash issues, I am seeing reporting crashes still so I may just be fortunate.There is still a fair amount of bugs that are evident and a real problem, such as max stat upgrades disappearing if you don't spend them immediately, but the reason you shouldn't buy right now is because right now, this is by far the worst AI I have ever seen.  Never before have I ever seen an AI that is so incapable of playing the game it is made for.  It is incredibly detrimental to the experience, why are you spending time on a game about the progression of your gang when you can go max difficulty with a starting gang and win?Original Review:Trust me I don't want to say this, but don't buy yet, keep an eye on it.There are so many good things about this game, tons of different maps, a great aesthetic and score, a character and gang development that will keep you engaged for many hours, and 3 different gangs that will each encourage you to use them differently.There are some minuses that could be mentioned like only 3 gangs and the slowness involved in the amount of down time in a battle.  Writing about how bad the AI is in this game I wouldn't know where to end if I started, but this isn't why I'm telling you not to buy.Don't buy because this game is broken as hell.  Frequent crashes, don't use a Lay-Mechanic because just trying to find a place to build something will cause a crash.  Don't move around looking for a good hit chance, that causes a crash.  Not hopping 2 times and doing a twirl before touching the mouse will cause a crash.I have had bugs that have completely screwed 10s of hours of development of my gang.  The AI will get stuck permanently with no way to continue, loading the save the AI will make the same move and get stuck, so the only way to continue is to forfeit and 4 of my 5 guys pick up career ending injuries.  If you were enjoying the good elements of the game stuff like this will destroy any fun you can have.We are 17 days after release now and there has been no patch.  No patch to get rid of the career ending clear all your infamy bug.  No patch for the AI getting stuck meaning your gangers get perma injuries.  No patch for any of the many crashes.  The amount of issues with this game if they are hoping to fix it all with one patch they would need several months.As a big player of Mordheim, their previous work, I have high hopes this will become a game I come back to for many years if they put in the work to iron out the issues, but right now I have to let people know that this is not a working game, and is in a criminally bad state as of the time of writing.

_childDocuments_.review: Personally, I'm really pleased with how this game turned out. It feels like Mordheim with some nice improvements and a setting I find more engaging. Despite it being set in the dark, dank, rusty underhive its also a fairly good looking game. There are only 3 factions available but luckily there are plenty of strategic options available, I will be interested to see if they add the other factions though. So far, the campaign is interesting enough as well, even though its very linear, and it does a good job of teaching you how to play.Now this game isn't without its issues. The game is slow-paced to a fault, and whilst personally it doesn't really bother me, I can understand why it's such a deal breaker for others. The enemy turns do take ages, you probably spend double the time waiting you do in something like bloodbowl 2 for example, which isn't exactly fast-paced in the first place. Hopefully they can patch the game to allow you to speed up enemy turns down the line.The two other issues that you'll see mentioned time and time again in these reviews is the AI and the bugs. I'll be honest, I've not had too bad a time with either of these. There has been the odd time for me and enemy has gotten stuck but I've not seen anything too bad yet. In terms of bugs, I encountered one where the game froze after throwing a grenade but luckily all I had to do was restart the game and unlike others, I didn't lose any save data or progress.Overall, I really like this game and I feel it has the opportunity to be something special, as the core of the game is brilliant. I would recommend giving it a go if you fancy it but if you are more on the fence or don't like slow-paced gameplay, I'd probably give it a few months until they've hopefully patched out some of the more egregious issues

_childDocuments_.review: Don't get me wrong, this is a decent game, but I was expecting them to do way better than this, after the experience with Mordheim. Characters can basically cover the entirety of the map in 2 turns; setting up a defensive position to carefully plan out your strategy is not an option, you will always find yourself in combat turn 1 and the fact that most of the missions consist of "pick up and get the heck out" with a 6 turn time limit does not help things at all. AI is abysmal, but the saddest part is that it HAS to be, otherwise you would get utterly annihilated every single time, since you constantly find yourself fighting 5 vs 15. Also warbands are all pretty similar, they use mostly the same skills and the same archetypes, the only thing changing is the overall bonus they get. Summarizing it gets very repetitive very fast.At the moment Mordheim is a far superior game, but I'm not saying things may not change in the future if the devs fix the issues. As of now though I'm kind of disappointed

_childDocuments_.review: Do not buy this game.This game does right what Mordheim did wrong and does awfully wrong what Mordheim did quite right:In Mordheim you had several warbands to chose, allowing you to have a very interesting warband composition up to 10 or so members, with interesting builds that  made it work the way you wanted to as long as you knew the game mechanics and skills etc.There were only 4 or so  maps available in Mordhein (plus the campaign related scenarios, those were different), with lots of random variables but at the end of the day were rather repetitive.Each warband had its own campaign INTEGRATED into the endless gameplay mode: this means that you could play the daily random missions for as long as you wanted and play the campaign whenever you wanted, not when the game told you to do it.In Necromunda Hive Wars we got so far 5 different gangs (3 on release, 2 dlc) whose main difference is some stats/special skills/visual cosmetics.While the stats make it for more suitable oriented builds depending on the gang (melee, ranged, buffs/debuffs) these differences are marginal.Oh and forget about the gang specific stuff like van saar energy shields, special weapons bla: all gangs have access to basically the same basic weapons.When you start a mission, you can only have a group of 5 gang members max, as opposed to Mordheim 10 active members. A terribad decission supposedly aimed to invigorate the inexistant (and uninteresting) multiplayer scene so that up to 4 players can play a match against each other without the waiting times a larger gang would imply.Too bad many of us played this game for the endless missions mode and not for multiplayer.This time the campaign is a standalone campaign, and the endless mode (operations) is thing apart... terribad decission.Finally, in Necromunda there is a huge variety of maps where the missions take place, different themes, lots of verticality and scenery that feel mostly empty with the max of 4 gangs per match that feel like what was a normal 2v2 in Mordheim.

_childDocuments_.review: GAMES WORKSHOP STRIKES AGAIN! FRANCHISE LOVERS, SUSPEND YOUR DISBELIEFNo, I mean it. Like hardcore, because otherwise you gonna have a bad time:The GW universe and its products have contributed to shaping my childhood and still to this day, I find awesome. The feel, the lore, the implicit horror behind every single little arc, it's been fatastic. True to form, Necromunda: Underhive Wars captures the essence of what the game is like: merciless squabbling for dwindling resources. Fight, kill, steal, yoink, yeet and flee-the-scene-if-you-wanna-keep-your-stuff your way through some pretty sweet decor or the titanic Hive Primus of Necromunda, doing the bidding of the Houses.You can customise your gang, swap out weapons, loot your opponents (oh the joy of facing up a gang you've stripped bare in a previous fight), fine-tune skills and stats and to an extent, appearances. The feel is very much there.You know what else is there? A learning curve: ladies and gentlemen, Games Workshop proudly presents yet another half-baked game. While I'm a fan, I'm a little frustrated that yet again, GW couldn't figure out a way to produce what could have been a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ masterpiece. EVERY GAME could be just properly incredible, but EVERY GAME is like an old-timey car: pretty, but will let you down in the details.The Story: You do not get to do the story with your own gang. This in itself was a big frustration because by the time you do get to build your own team of lowlifes, the story is over. All your left with is what it's like to play tabletop Necromunda, which is to say just battles strung together by a "looting campaign". The story was written by Andy Chambers, and if you know your who's-who in GW, you know you're dealing with one of the OGs. Still, the characters' flavor is let down by poorly written dialog - I'll recognize that the characters aren't exactly thespians, but still, coherence is appreciable. Adding to this, you only get the same bloody loading screen about one of the Hive's critters during the story. If you want any others, play the "operations" after the story. The AI - Questionable decisions made on demand, a non-exhaustive list:- Not pulling the trigger when it could put a bullet in you.- Camping away from the action- Attacking allies (yes, even if you're the ally)- Walking into own traps- Not evacuating with lootPresumably having only played in Easy & Normal, I could expect better decision making in higher difficulty tiers, but I feel that you tune the AI's ability, not decision-making in order to get a difficulty setting? Anyway, weird calls by the opponent. Add to that pathing issues, and you get a few opponents trying to walk through obstacles.Mechanics: Movement is based on distance from your starting point, in a straight line. So you could technically walk out of a 100-meter spiral if it was contained in a 40-meter circle in a single turn. You can't end your turn in an "unsafe area", which are zones in which there are interactable objects, first aid machines, zip lines, collapsing bridges. The latter is especially disappointing, because that peans you can't shoot the bridge from under someone's feet. Interface: A little buggy, the inventory icons would get shifted down the list when you add something to a ganger's pack. So you think you're popping a cold one, when in fact you reached for a grenade. "Field repair" will automatically target another ganger, so you need to actively select the active ganger to use it on him. Can waste your time. Not the most fluid of UIs, but it gets the job done.Crashes: none to speak of.All in all, I still recommend it, I kept playing for 40 hours. Somethign about the feel of the game and the ease of success was relaxing enough for me to feel like it was a fun experience. But if you're easily frustrated by sub-par performance here and there (XCom kinda laid the foundations, there's not much of an excuse to not get somethings right) don't get this game.

_childDocuments_.review: IN SHORT:-	game looks and sounds really great (except for the voice acting, which is at times very OUF)-	the AI is the worst AI I have ever witnessed in a video game-	the game tends to crash a lot. Thankfully, the game autosaves with every character that starts to move, so you don’t lose progress. If you’re lucky…-	You have to finish the campaign to unlock hair and gasmask cosmetic options in the other mode. (W H Y ???)So all in all, definitely don’t buy it yet, unless you really just care for the story or some Necromunda Vibes. Wait until they fix the AI and save yourself a lot of anger.IN DETAIL:***SPOILERS***Let me start from the beginning…So when I decided to buy this game I was way more intrigued by the “Make your own Gang and do randomized missions”-Mode. So naturally, that is what I instantly clicked when I first saw the menu screen. The game, of course, warned me, that I should first play through the campaign to get a grasp of the gameplay. “Sure thing, that makes sense I guess” I thought and started the campaign. And thus I got my first Introduction to Necromunda: Underhive Wars.So the game starts off with a huge load of tutorials. I wish these were a little bit more in your face and not just some textbox on the top right corner of your screen. It happened multiple times during the whole campaign, that the textbox showed new stuff and it instantly vanished, just to get replaced by a tooltip that I’ve read a thousand times already. But besides that, I was into the vibe the game was setting up. Mission 1 was a pure movement and shooting tutorial. Mission 2 felt like the first actual Mission but was also still a tutorial. But after that it started to get rough. I had a couple of hiccups during Mission 3, because of vanishing tooltips explaining the classes. Other than that, the Mission was fairly doable. Mission 4 suddenly gives you an entirely different Gang and it was in this mission where I first started to notice the… “special” behavior of the AI. Your goal was to storm a multi story building, defeat all the Banecatz and rescue a dude, that they’ve captured. The place was rigged to hell and back with traps, literally everywhere you stepped there was a trap. Now like I said, I am a big fan of Valkyria Chronicles in which you have a soldier class, the pioneer, which can spot mines. So if he’s near one, you’ll get a visual and audio cue, so you don’t run into them like a moron. In Necromunda its quite a bit different. You get NO visual or audio cue and you’re just expected to see the traps (which look like a small canister of gas) in between all the dimly lit rubble and the other scum that’s on the floors of the hive. When I was onto the final missions I still ran into every damn trap because they are so hard to see. So I thought to myself: “Maybe I should lay traps too.” And so I did.Now, the weird thing is: The AI kept running up and down the stairs inside the building, jumping from roofs and all. So obviously I wanted to limit their movement by laying traps on the stairs. And suddenly from that point onward the AI avoided the stairs like the plague and just jumped out of the window. This happened quite a lot during the whole campaign. The AI just instantly knows where your traps are and they avoid it. So what’s the point? I guess it works against other players but there are several missions where you have “Lay X Traps” as an optional goal.Onward to Mission 5. This mission can just buzz right off. It’s an arena match against a melee focused enemy gang. For some reason the developers thought it would be a good Idea to let them all start with melee weapons, while your gang has to get them from the battlefield or the corpses of your slain foes. The enemy leader is for some reason even on a second enemy team entirely, which means once he joins the battle there will be two enemies moving at the beginning of each turn. I failed the mission two times, they just overran me. Only when I started to camp with all of my guys and gals on the middle of the map (an around 1 meter high platform) I managed to cheese the AI into defeat. But it did not feel like an earned victory at all.Mission 6 switches you back to the Banecatz and you have to raid a base. The mission was kind of ok, though AI hilarity made the run into their own traps.Then, all of a sudden, you get to play as yet ANOTHER different gang, with new abilities and new weapons. Tutorials for that? Gone before you can read them. Though I have to say, Mission 7 was quite fun. It was a nice and simple take and hold mission, of course easier than expected because of the AI.Mission 14, were almost at the end and boy did I rage at this. Not because it was hard, but because of the sheer incompetence of the AI. So what’s different this time? Easy: You have to storm a fortified gate that is filled to the brim with enemy gangers. Way more than you would normally control. So to “”””””””help””””””” you, the mission gives you some buddies. But here’s the catch: They’re controlled by the AI. At the beginning it was funny. When I had to restart the mission because they would just sit in their spawn, LITERALLY watch the paint dry on the wall and sometimes throw grenades in their own face my mood was as grim dark as the 41st Millennia. I yelled at my screen while the Melee AI-Teammate ran into a group of four enemies, ran past them, ran up to the second floor, jumped down into the group again and then cowered into a corner and ended his turn. And all of that without stopping ONCE to attack or do ANYTHING useful AT ALL. I don’t know how I got through this mission but somehow I did. And there it was. Mission 15, the final one.At first, I was happy, because it was almost over. Then I noticed that the AI teammate was part of the mission again. I cried a little bit, then started to pay attention. The mission itself isn’t too hard. Lock enemy reinforcement routes, defeat bosses, press buttons. The usual. And it even went quite good, except for the usual AI behavior. Almost at the end, I really wanted to kill one of the two last guys. But I already clicked on “Fire” when I noticed that my dude, who was about to unload his entire mag, only had one shot left. So I went back to the menu, knowing that the game saved when I started to move my guy. And it did. However, THE ENTIRE MISSION PROGRESS WAS RESET. And I don’t just mean reset. It was reset AND IT DIDN’T TELL ME. It took quite a while to lock all the 11 doors and to kill off the last enemy gangers. And then after the reload SUDDENLY EVERY DOOR WAS OPEN AGAIN. Did they show up as unlocked on the map? NOPE. So I had to go to every door and check whether the lock reset itself. With three people left standing. With the AI not being able to kill the swarms of reinforcements that were swooping right the frick in. When I was done with the mission I was about five percent off of having a damn stroke. It was just a mess. And then after all that we get to see what its all about. We get to see why the hair and gasmask customization was locked. Because you unlocked the hairstyles of the three gangleaders. Sooooooo…WHY. DID. YOU. HAVE. TO. LOCK. EVERY. OTHER. HAIRSTYLE. THEN??????It’s not even that these were super secret. You see them in Mission effin ONE!Honestly, I don’t know when I will try out the other mode, because that AI hassle has just blown all the fun out of my life in an instant. As I said above, don’t buy it yet. If you’re interested then wait until they fixed the worst of the bugs and glitches. There’s also a lot of stuff that I didn’t get into, like every corpse T-Posing and asserting dominance when you reload a mission. But this is pretty much the experience you will have when suffering through the campaign.I hope you guys have a better time than I had.

_childDocuments_.review: One of my favourite settings, I've loved Necromunda for years, and was really excited to hear a game was finally being made. I played Mordheim previously and it seemed like the right engine for it, they just needed to polish a lot of the weird animations and make the gameplay loop more engaging. Sadly it wasn't a good sign when their PR and marketing before release was absolute ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, next to no information about the game, no hype, nothing.I tried it on release and was impressed by the environments. The environment art team has done incredibly well with the locations, it really evokes the feel of Necromunda and pulls you into the setting. Sadly, most other areas of the game pull you out of it. The animations are janky and unnatural. If you dual fire with pistols, the character flicks their arm out to shoot before teleporting back to the idle location whilst the other flicks out, then repeats. It looks like a first pass of animation, then no one went back to make sure they were ready for release. It's amazing that they seem to be fine with anims that look like they're from 2005.The character models don't match up to the quality levels of the environment. When trying to customise a character, I couldn't get them to look right. The colours are so washed out and drab that they don't feel like they belong in the environment at all. And surely you'd want your characters to stand out, right? To be more visible on the battlefield, so you can recognise them more easily? Really lackluster art design for the models, made worse by how good the environments look.Overcomplicated skill trees. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, there are so many sources of tiny bonuses that it feels like a chore to level your character. You have stats to improve, you have skills and skill points to assign, but there's so much of it that I lose interest. Do I want a 1% increase to ranged critical strike damage or a slight increase in accuracy or extra dodge chance vs melee? Don't spread out your bonuses too thin, no one cares or will notice a 1% increase. Make the points more powerful so it's actually fun and simple to upgrade them. Too complicated for no reward.So there are other issues, namely AI, but I haven't played recently and they have apparently fixed some of these issues, so I won't mention them. My main problem at the moment, and the reason I would avoid buying this game is that the developers seem to have abandoned it. No updates in 6 months, plenty of complaints going around, and the score of the game doesn't seem to have improved after the updates that have been released. As I mentioned before, their PR/Marketing efforts are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ terrible, so they could be working on something but not telling anyone, but it feels like they've checked out and the publisher won't fund any more updates.A real shame, one of the few games I was generally looking forward to(the other was Beyond Earth, which was also ♥♥♥♥). Too bad it was handled incredibly badly. I don't recommend this game, in case that wasn't clear. Just a waste of money.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok where do I start:Synopses: Its a game about the world of Necromunda Underhive which is itself a certain part of the societies withing Warhammer 40k that are more like SLUMS where only the strongest gangs can survive and take resources from the others to do this. Its a war for control in a place somewhat reminiscent of a babel tower with different factions.Story mode: Very interesting. Introduces you to the different gangs (3 of them) along with their motivations and purpose wich at the end is to reach a prize and I dont want to spoil more for you cause its good.Technical: Its the closest thing you'll get to a true (table top) experience in a 40K game yet. Mechanics are there. Map:  Is very reminiscent to what you see in tabletop but rather more complex cause its a video game and can expand more on that side. Map view is superb to lay out strats for aproaching enemies, highly customizable in terms of how you can view the map and your models (Characters you play look like table top in map view). Everything is very well laid out for you to know where you can move. All sites and maps are different and beautifully detailed. If you play on a good PC you'll have 40k eye candy.Mechanics: As you can expect there is classes (Customizable) with a range of buffs,debuffs, weapons, 5 classes to choose from, stats, etc. There is a wide arrange of things that can affect gameplay and reasource management is very important to this effect. As I said, is very tabletop.Movement and turns: Did I mention this game is close to a tabletop experience? I guess I did. Well, as you expect you can move through the lay out of the map within the range of your model, do the actions permitted by you AP, the characters turn is laid by its INI stat (what turn it will take within the other models within your party and those against your party) in every single turn. You do have to make a choice there to know if your model will move before those you are against for strategic overwatch, retreive of a resource, whatever your strat is. You have to see in full what the opponent is doing in a turn and so does your opponent have to do the same for you even in story mode. There is people with 40 mins played in the game ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ about turns taking too long because of it. This game is centered in PVP. Its supposed to be a tabletop game. Not an action game. In tabletop you have to wait for your opponent to make their moves. Why not here? Yes, maybe in story mode they could have a fast forward feature but in reality, this stresses your PC or Console to calculate to fast and take more resources that could make your computer or console to crash the game. This game was also released on console. I assume they thought about it but is better not provide you with a feature that you will not have when playing the real game.Customization: You have 3 houses and 5 classes to choose from. Different initial stats to start your models with to choose from and everything else is up to you. You can hire more gangers, make leader whomever you want after certain points. Great customization for cosmetics including individual parts of the body and color palettes. Some people ♥♥♥♥♥ about not enough houses but again, this is just ♥♥♥♥♥ mode. Game is new. Hardly there is marginal differences between houses from stats or certain gimmics that are not as important and in all reality the real important houses are players. So, there is no point on ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ about it. I saw first day people with 0.4 hours rushing to do reviews and I laughed so hard at this bad reviews because these people have no Idea or are so hardcore necromunda fans that have their heads very up into their asses that cant see anything good about any 40k game ever. No game is good for them exept tabletop. I understand fanboyism or coming up with the highest expectations possible but rarely any of 40k games are good because its easy to license. This is one of the few games that is actually GOOD for what it is and what it offers. DONT PAY ATTENTION TO PEOPLE WHO HAD PLAYED THE GAME LESS THAN 10 HOURS. These people dont have any sort of grasp or objectiveness for what the game offers or what the objective of the game is. I love the game, feels closer to the genuine experience of 40k than any other.

_childDocuments_.review: So I thought to meself that day, this one looks great, there's clearly lots of love put into the game by true fans and I wonder why it was reviewed so badly.An hour later, I thought to myself: Ah, no wonder it was reviewed so badly.See, the core gameplay is so wrong. It's a mixture between turn-base traditional tabletop mechanics and real time third person shooter angle. In short, it doesn't work. You got no satisfaction from playing a typical third person shooter as you don't actually aim and shoot. It's a turn based chance based traditional game; dice do the job and you just stand there and pray for a six. But you don't get the advantage of managing your team in a turn based strategy game either, because the camera is limited to a third person angle, so you have worse situational awareness than Scharnhorst at the North Cape.The result is an experience that combines the worst of the two genres and it's frustrating. Not because it's bad, most games are bad nowadays. It's genuinely sad that it didn't work out because someone clearly put lots of care inside and for better or worse, that's some mighty innovation there. I guess 'trying something new' isn't always a good thing. Innovation is the first step to Heretek, am I right, Archmagos?

_childDocuments_.review: First, I'm a big fan of Mordheim. I also don't care about multiplayer or story. So read this review with that in mind. I'm here for the endless mode and maybe some co-op comp stomping later.1. Graphics: Good 'nuff. 8/102. Map Design: Amazing. 10/103. Art Style: Great. Perfectly captures Warhammer 40k. 10/104. Gameplay: It's what I came here for. See below for notes. 8/105. Sound: Pretty okay. 8/106. Music: Does its job. 7/107. Gang Customization: Great, except for stuff being locked out until I complete the story--which I will probably never do. Boo. 8/108. Enemy AI: Absolutely brain-dead. Dumber than a box of rocks. Some of the worst I've ever seen. I'm actually almost getting second-hand embarrassment. It's really, really, really, bad ya'll. My first game the enemy did nothing but hide in a corner on their first turn. On their second they ran to the extraction zone with 2/5 of their gang, leaving the other 3 to be viciously murdered by mine. 0/109. Design Choices: Utterly baffling. Not hiding enemy turns, not allowing any speed-up options, programming the AI to make moves in an order that invalidate their previous moves (I'll kneel after I Overwatch so when I end my turn my Overwatch stance removes my kneeling stance!). _childDocuments_.review: Revised review - still don't recommend this game.This is what happens when you blow your budget on scripted video and sh*tty voice acting instead of focusing on core gameplay mechanics. When will developers big and small learn that no amount of shine can polish the turd of poor or buggy gameplay?I love Necromunda, but I can't recommend buying this. That we never even got the full gangs roster is telling. The devs appear to have abandoned a game they released broken and couldn't fix - so if they don't believe in it why should you? Don't buy this unless it's heavily discounted on sale and you have a friend or two you can play PvP with for a while.The multiplayer game is good. Excellent actually. Though it's a huge shame you can't do operations and campaigns just with your friends' gangs. Single player unfortunately has terrible AI. A problem that makes the stale, solo campaign all the more frustrating and boring. The AI decision making is incomprehensibly bad at times. They don't seem to exploit opportunities at all. They often go straight into overwatch at their spawn on the first turn. This leaves them outgunned in the middle of the map where they feed themselves to you one at a time. Or they'll get confused and run around in a loop then eventually just end their turn having achieved nothing. The outright game breaking bugs seem to mostly have been fixed, but be warned: the save corrupting bugs are still a real threat. I haven't had another instance of having to forfeit games just to get past repeated crash-to-desktop during AI turns since the Cawdor update at least. That shouldn't be something that needs celebrated though..  Ultimately, as with before (even giving the frequently cringeworthy voice work a free pass), I still have to conclude that this isn't a finished product. All the pieces are there; it looks excellent, gang customisation is mechanically decent (though visually limited) and the sound and atmospherics are on point. Most importantly though, the stability, AI and mechanics are a let down. Necromunda remains unfinished and a poor successor to Mordheim. It wasn't ready for release and still isn't. This had so much unrealised potential. Such a genuine shame.I'll be cautious about buying in to the next release from this developer. I do hope they can bounce back from this, but I won't be gambling my time and money without at least a demo in future.

_childDocuments_.review: Whelp here we go again. Do I recommend this game? Short answer yes with an if, long answer no with a but. I was really excited for this one because I loved Mordheim,  the tabletop version of this game, and tabletop kill team. Got pretty worried when this got stuck in development, not sure what happened, whatever. The setting of this game is perfect, dark, rusty underground facilities that are all stacked catwalks, tis great. It adds dimension to the arena and looks fantastic. Fun to set up ambushes, block exits, and crowd around the occasional healing station. The options for gang customization are nice looking, fun to play around with. Graphically Necromunda looks amazing. Turn based gameplay is one of my very favorites, and I love all the little tactical options, all of this is fine. 3 houses is all GW gave us to start with. Goliath (hulking brutes), Escher (All ladies), and Orlock (team generic). I wound up going with Orlock because I like a mix of Guys and Gals, however, and I know this is subjective, but if i have the option I'd rather not play human in my fantasy games... I get to do that in real life every day. I was really hoping for some Genestealer Cults or some Chaos, I'm into the really unique and grotesque that goes along with the high gothic fantasy that is the Warhammer universe. The lack of diversity is compounded as well, in that the gangs are just really not that different or unique. All weapons can be used by any different house, stats are flexible enough that your skinny Esher girls can be just as brutal and hearty in melee as a Goliath gorilla. Its too easy to compare Necromunda to mordheim (which i put about 600 hours into over many years). That game each warband had its own strong and unique flavor. Tanky caster sisters of battle, Flintlock firearms and stealth with the skaven, magic and mutations with chaos. The uniqueness of the factions, the tactics you had to employ with each, and the weapons which were unique to each added a ton of depth to the game, strategy, learning curves, beautiful asymmetry, and replay ability. They really need to do something to give each gang their own unique flavor because as it stands its purely an aesthetic choice, which makes the actual replay kind of boring. I'm assuming multiple of the other gang houses will be released as DLC, which seems to be GW's MO at this point, I've accepted it as an unfortunate fact of life, and at this point I'd welcome it, I really want to play my Genestealer Cultists. This has many of its own problems as well though, will the new gangs have anything new or different? Will there be a power creep to encourage people to shell out money for the new warbands? Probably... Mordheim's 2 DLC factions were laughably more powerful than the originals, Witch hunters being pretty strong, and Vampires being completely OP. Theres always the possibility also of them just not being made because of lack of interest due to the oddity of Necromunda's release or the mixed reviews. I worry about these things. Basically I recommend Necromunda if you're a die hard 40k fan, or if you know for sure you like this type of turned based tactics, because there's tons of room for improvement. Hopefully the game wont be abandoned and we'll get to see the Necromunda the fans deserve. GW has a quantity over quality policy that's always really rubbed me the wrong way, with this game all the elements of a great turn based tactical arena are there, a few tweaks and this could be a really standout game. I just hope that GW and Rogue Factor have the grit to address the issues rather than shelving Necromunda and moving to the next project.(Edit) *  So, I changed from recommended to not recommended for a few reasons here. First off, having to play through the single player campaign to unlock cosmetics is incredibly stupid. People like me, who've played a lot of games like this and just want to build their own gang and play are bored to tears by a 15 mission tutorial, no thank you. Second are the "Vices" targeted to your class? Played through with 3 gangs so far. My leader, first time out was a sniper. Got the vice that gives you -10% Ranged damage and immediately scrapped the gang. Its easier to just start over that level a lowbie leader with high level followers. Second time went with a melee boss.... -10% melee damage. Third gang, made a heavy weapons leader... -10% ranged damage. If this is just epic bad luck then thats great, but when perks are things like (gets extra healing from healing stations) amazing thats useful for like 1 out of 50 battles, but taking a 10% hit to all your damage is unacceptably punishing when the perks are generally trash. Third the AI is terrible. The camera zooms in on them, then you wait about 90 seconds to watch them take an elevator to the top level, then jump down to the lowest level, to walk past 2 enemy gangers and call the elevator back and take it to the top floor and end the turn. They dont know how to destroy barriers, so you can just wall off the exit. Then position your guys around the barricade, picking off all the enemies that collect the loot and bring it directly into your trap one at a time to die horribly. Also, don't start releasing paid DLC before the basics are working.-TLDR-Ultimately the incredibly vanilla feeling of all the gangs, the broken AI, and the tedious nature of the snatch and run missions make this a forgettable and often boring game.

_childDocuments_.review: It's every bit as bad as the last minute game play trailers looked.Nearly everything wrong with Mordheim is still in there:-Tons of stats and abilities to sift through, while only a handful actually matter.-The character models are very nice, and they force you stare at them, thanks to the senseless over the shoulder camera perspective.-It is based off of a table top game, and plays much like one but is nothing like the game it is based off of.-Everything in the game is a dice roll or arbitrary and the huge open environments mean that the game is ever more dependent on the dice than Mordheim, since there is relatively little strategy to be had outside of your character builds.-The mixing of single player and multi player is still a poor idea in my opinion.-Being forced to watch a dumb AI move it's pieces around while you watch is incredibly annoying.-Three gangs with the same five character classes don't really make me feel like I have a ton of options in builds or play styles, just 3 slight variations on the same set of tools.-The sandbox/campaign system is incredibly shallow and uninteresting and the tactical battles are just repeat skirmish fights against the AI that feel repetitive after like 3 matches.The only real improvements are in the way they changed the campaign/sandbox mode and post battle looting. You don't lose just because you can't collect enough resources, you can concentrate on playing the missions and the campaign doesn't just put you up against a gang of exactly the same power level each time you go into a battle, the other gangs seem to level up and evolve as yours does. Also, the game now allows you one extra turn to move around and loot the map rather than just giving you a random amount of what's on the map after you win. But those two improvements while needed, aren't enough to fix the real problem which is boring, repetitive game play that just seems like grinding for the sake of grinding.

_childDocuments_.review: *EDIT* putting in a ticket for refund. This game might have been worth picking up in a year when they have it fixed up and the price is 75% off. Then again, for their first community update, they are announcing that they will be "working" on fixing major game issues which they simply can't have missed in testing, while also announcing DLCs. Basically they released a game they knew weren't done and didn't have sufficient content. Do the gaming community a favor and stay away from titles that use these tactics. Put out a working game with plenty of content, this trend with releasing non-working games with a long line of DLCs prepared is just pure ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.Currently the positives review are just fan-boys who are getting defensive, because the game is rightfully being called out on being a mess that got pushed through release.Go see the forum before buying, the people who "like" this game are literally defending it by saying "It's only 30 euro", "I expect a new games to need patches", and similar.----------------------tl;dr: Not worth buying at this point, get Mordheim and play that for a year, then come back and check on Necromunda.If we pretend that these guys didn't make Mordheim and this was the first game they put out AND it was the first game to ever be put out in this genre. Then this game might not be half bad, but that's not the case, which makes this game really bad.Why do we need to spend so much time going from one round to the other? Why do we need to spend so much time picking characters? The only real defense for the lacking rosters for the clans and the size of your party, would be speeding up multiplayer. But then we got all this other stuff just taking up time for no reason. Seems like half of the gameplay time is going to be spent watching "End of round X" etc. Why leave the movement system from Mordheim behind and not improve it? I guess there has been some attempt to smooth out the movement from Mordheim. However it doesn't work as intended, the movement is cluncky and it's unclear what the limits are and this just leads to even more backtracking than Mordheim had.So we basically got a lot of effort/budget put into cut scenes, voice acting and visuals, I'm not sure who decided these were the important parts for a decent turn based strategy game, but they probably shouldn't be invited onto new projects. Unfortunately they only spend 5 minutes considering what worked and didn't work in Mordheim, and then decided to remove the things that worked and left the things that didn't work. Like the AI will still run into walls for a couple of seconds, before just skipping their turn.Even the graphics options are lackluster, why are we forced to have motion blur on?At least now we know why they didn't put out any actual gameplay until 6 days before release. This just feels like an instant refund, guess it still has around an hour to convince me. At this point Mordheim is just a more complete game, which tries to do the same things, but actually succeeds at it. It's hard to believe that the same people made both games.Someone who hasn't played Mordheim or similar games and gets Necromunda without any expectations for the gameplay and wants a generic WH40K strategy game might enjoy this.

Pros: -Good atmosphere (music and design)-Great customization options for your own gang (weapons, skills, colours, etc)-Good and interesting leveling system-Long (potentially never-ending) campaign mode-Up to 4 player multiplayer matches (2v2, 1v3, free-for-all)-Good gameplayCons:-Bad AI! Needs some tweaking to make them not complete morons-Really annoying tutorial/Story mode-Various bugs (getting stuck, crashes, freezes, unstable camera on corners, etc) that need fixing!Overall, the game needs work, but I would still recommend it for fans of the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: Editing just ahead of the first DLC's release. The game is now in a much less buggy state, although some gamebreaking bugs persist which isn't ideal when save files can't be loaded in an indefinite campaign relying on ironman saves. The AI also is a little more challenging, although it is still prone to bizarre behaviours at times. Even under the latest patch I've seen an AI gang member try to 'nade himself to death, and heading into a corner to overwatch nothing still happens.Turn times are much faster however. Although the fixed camera angle is still fixed in place.Would I recommend this game? No. Not really. Or at least not without caveats as there is no doubt a niche market for it. There are good things to this game but they are still buried under design decisions which really don't work for me. Whether further work on the game will escape the strait jacket the developers made for themselves, seemingly intended to balance an MP scene which never came to exist, remains to be seen. But as it is this is a game relying on its very well done 40k aesthetic to carry it in SP while it has died on its backside for MP.-----I know I'm only an hour in. But I'm already considering a refund. If you check my reviews, I do try to be really fair when I review before that option.Good things first. It looks fantastic. There's so much care gone into detail of environments and gang members themselves. The actual gameplay, the skills and the mechanics of combat, are very similar to this developers' Mordheim with some refinements and they play really nicely once you've gone through to figure out what's what.But there's some pretty major problems right now. The first should be a relatively minor one in the grand scheme of things but is exacerbated by the second. The game's got a problem in SP when the first melee fighter I come across runs up to my character, runs around my character, and then heads off to a corner and kneels facing away from all of my gang members. One off? Not really, in just 1 hour I've had an enemy 'nade himself almost to death against an object. I've watched enemy gang members go on weird detours to sightsee I don't know what. Now it's not always that bad at all. In fact, it can also be very impressive with using the environment to get around to make a shot. But all these AI glitches are really thrust into your face because of the second issue. Which is...You're forced to watch each and every AI gang member take its turn. And from a fixed camera. If you can move it so you can look about, I've not found it yet and apologies for being wrong. But fundamentally, there's no tension to this at all - you know where everyone is all of the time. Even if you don't want to. Even if you'd just like the AI to crack on so you can finish a full turn. It's a really, really bad design decision for SP. I can't honestly recommend this game. Hopefully the AI issues will be further patched and this review will be laughably out of date very quickly on that score. If you can live with the slow turns and the fixed camera to watch it then there's a lot here to enjoy. It's just a deal breaker for me on such a fundamental level of playing TTB.

_childDocuments_.review: It's in a bad space right now. It's no wonder we didn't see any gameplay footage of it until about a day before its release. I've had characters fall through the floor (rendering my team composition effectively meaningless), the AI is a buggy mess of absurd decisions (such as throwing grenades at literally nothing, walking into terrain until they decide to give up, or even walking into their own traps), and the UI, in my opinion, is a mess of bad decisions (unclear or too-similar symbols, no designation of sight-lines for overwatched enemies). All of this I can personally play through because I want to enjoy the game, and I do still find some enjoyment in it, but then it is compounded by even more fundamental issues, the most egregious of which is definitely the fact that the hit chance calculation lies to you and will frequently bug out, rapidly changing percentages when standing completely still. It doesn't help that the game also feels generally underdeveloped in the options it affords the player to customize their squad. Every House gets the exact same skills and abilities, except for the six specific to that House. This will likely pigeonhole players into a specific playstyle that their House prefers, which isn't necessarily bad, but I can't see much reason to play each House more than once to a relatively decent power level and then just giving up.I think this game has the potential to be really fun, and I would love to play it more once these issues are fixed, but as it stands right now, I can't recommend it to anyone who isn't super into tactical, squad-based games like this.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to like this game, I really do.Downtime between turns you play is staggeringly long. Especially in 1v1v1 maps. Being able to see what the opponent/AI does is powerful sure but Mordheim's way where you could only see them if you had line of sight was better.  Ambush is a pretty terrible ability with the lack of stealth lol.Speaking of the AI, too much potato in its current form. I had to watch an AI run cross 3 paths to take the wire down to where they started just to attack my character... It doesnt seem to really care about overwatch, my heavy weapon guy with barrage (Overwatch but can fire off multiple times if they move a certain amount within the sphere of influence) is making an absolute murder.I realised quickly theres no incentive to go for the objectives, just kill and loot the opponent and then try and grab objectives on the "loot round" after defeating the enemy factions. The AI likes to prioritize objectives over you so you can get some free encounters/first attack. In Mordheim looting as much warpstone you could get your hands on felt super important where balancing between skirmishes and running around and looting felt like an attractive style of play.There are good things about the game. Most of it you can experience in Mordheim. Removal of the upkeep is nice. Giving them gear and watching them getting some strap of metal attached to that part is nice.But the core game experience is not refined enough for me to recommend this game. Mordheim is great, there was a lot of fun in that game with the varied factions (here we got 3 different types of human factions) and the varied units inside the factions (no "champion" or "monster" units in this).I think the different classes are good too. Some do feel more basic than others. Saboteur and Engineer (whatever its called, the one with the servo arm) feel like the most fun classes to build. I keep the devs in good faith however. If they can improve the AI and give this game some QoL changes I can see myself changing this to a thumbs up review. But right now, Mordheim's base game is the better experience of these two.I hope there will be future DLC if the games sells good enough. I know there are other gang houses for the game, but I'm more so interested in seeing genestealers and ork warbands.

_childDocuments_.review: PRO+/-CON Review:PRO+For its current price (£5) it is worth every penny. Its fun, the voice acting is cheesy in the good sense, and the graphics look nice. The setting is exactly what you'd expect from Necromunda. The sets really feel like a high-budget tabletop setup.The AI is a bit dumb, yes, but you don't get the XCOM AI treatment where they all hone in on 1 unit for the sake of p*ssing you off, which is nice.The game's pace feels like an actual game of Necromunda. If you've not played the tabletop game you might find it a bit alien the way the chess-like turns work and how action points are used.Honestly I don't get why there are so many negative reviews.-CONUnless you have friends, don't expect to play multiplayer. It is almost completely dead.It is a little repetitive, but just do a mission or 2 when you want an inject. Unless there are timed objectives to secure, you've no reason to plan your strategy for the mission. The enemies don't usually pose that much of an intellectual threat. There is no perma-death in the main story. This is a CON purely from my own opinion because I love the likes of Darkest Dungeon and XCOM where this feature heavily weighs in on the risk/reward, much like playing Necromunda SHOULD feel.Finally, The characters aren't that cool. You'll find your favourites but personality wise they're forgettable and if one falls, meh. They'll be back next mission. The custom gang feature should be in the main story as it is in the skirmish mode.
