_childDocuments_.review: I want to thumbs up this game so badly, it's so damn close but so far from completely playable...I'll start with the positives: The graphics and Necromunda immersion, maps, weapons etc etc are all on point.  I spend so much time just messing around with my gangs in crew management.  The skill system, general gang creation, customisation and personal touches are honestly amazing.  When the game-play does not bug out the combat and non-combat in match mechanics are excellent and in-line with the tabletop game.  It's so damn close to being a top tier gameworkshop inspired game....Finally the reasons why I cannot thumbs up....Ok here goes... The AI is only describable using foul language and expletives.  I personally have not experienced excessive game crashes however they do occur.  The crashes also have a tendency to bug other things within the game.  Case in point a previous match a deadeye of mine was injured and I had no stims left to get him up.  Unbelievably I actually had a good injury roll and he lost an eye only to get my second ever bionic upgrade giving him increased ranged states (oh hell yeah..) the next match my game crashed and what do ya know... it somehow healed his permanent bionic and his real eye is back.  Explain that one.  The only other bionic I got was also on a deadeye who lost an arm and now has increased melee stats with his bionic arm (yipee...) and he has retained that amazing improvement.  So on bionics... honestly - once a body area has a permanent injury like stupid stomach bugs that somehow you can't get some damn anti-biotics for permanently ruining the AP cost of everything on that character you've heavily invested in and became attached too.... rant over.. you should be able to opt for bionic replacements.  The only way you can get them is permanent loss of said area which only happens in death/downed end of matches risking everything.  Tier 6 chest pieces are like hens teeth.   The AI is stupid almost selectively.  The AI makes me angry.  The AI sucks.  Ok so there are times the AI even in a 4 way winner takes all... just B lines it for you.   They ignore the other gangs and focus kill your dudes.  Interestingly enough when they actually do fire at other AI opponents they almost always graze/evade or do minor damage.  But wait a second... when they shoot or hit my dudes with maxed out stats and gear they always do max damage or critical's then loot my stuff and run away with seemingly infinite action and movement points.  The amount of times I've been watching an enemy turn and just put my hands up in the air and said a lot of expletive remarks for an excessive amount of time is silly.  Personally I don't mind DLC pay barriers for new teams but when its released so close to launch while the game is in a barely playable bugged out state then you know too many people involved in the games creation couldn't have cared less amount the longevity of the game.  They rely on diehard fans of gamesworkshop IP like myself to just play anyway.  Judging player activity in this game on the "players currently in the hive" stats would say to me - you failed - you failed miserably and should hang your heads in shame.  There were clearly some people involved in this game that cared, honestly I believe they cared a lot and it is a shame others ruined their game.  To the people who did their best with this game - you were so close - the game is so close to being amazing...  but once a bad taste is left in a persons mouth the odds of them trying the improved version is little to none.  If you ever give a .... and want to put a little more effort in - a campaign based version of this game in a deathwatch format would have soooooooo much potential.  Just don't Necromunda it...

_childDocuments_.review: Would I recommend Necromunda? Not in it's current state.There's nothing wrong with the game, but really there's nothing outstanding about it either. Lets ignore the clunky UI and AI, lets get over the sometimes glitchy graphics... lets actually look at the gameplay.When you look at the concept Necromunda should be good, the foundations of the game are solid and the replayability is there. But the devs missed a key aspect of game design, the gangs are essentially all the same. The only really difference is how they look, besides that they play pretty much exactly the same... and that really detracts from the experience.My other gripe is the lack of strategic depth, tactical gameplay exists, but the overarching strategy level is missing. Basically you load up your highest level toons with your highest level gear and set them loose upon the map. Give us a point limit for our squad and actually make us think about how to best use those points, do we run 3 high level well equipped mercs, or do we run 10 low level expendable guys with basic gear? The other thing they need to do is make the gangs different, Van Saar are meant to be technological advanced... they're not. As I said earlier there is no real difference between the three gangs and there should be.If the dev does that then this game will be great.At the moment it's rather meh, good for a blat... but not worth full price.

_childDocuments_.review: So... stay with me here, I like this game. I really do. Also when you 'finally' do get a match it's not gonna be balanced gang levels wise, expect it to crash as well at some point.Classes are the same approximately for whichever gang you choose. Heavies are pretty much broken due to a consumable and 2 talents = shots for 0, your heavy can pretty much shoot down 4-5 people in a turn if you are good.Crashes, so many crashes. CTD happens too often for a game like this.Devs are 'hinting' at a new gang coming in the next patch, sadly I am guessing this will be just a few more different cosmetics for the already tired same same bunch of classes (there are loading screens with mention of Cyberhounds being used by 1 gang for instance!).

_childDocuments_.review: This a borderline positive review.  I am not objective.  I am a Games Workshop fanboy.  I enjoyed Mordheim, for all its faults.  I expected nothing more than a reskinned Mordheim.  I am writing primarily to address those people who have compared Necromunda unfavorably to Mordheim.Necromunda is directly comparable to the way Mordheim was at launch.  Indeed, some of the most obnoxious AI issues were never fixed in Mordheim.  Knowing nothing about AI programming, it's certainly easy for me to say that Rogue Factor should have figured out by now how to avoid AI characters getting stuck on procedurally generated terrain.  But they haven't, and at this point I guess they're not going to.One significant change is that the single player experience (after the bespoke Story mode) lacks the special campaign missions that marked progress in Mordheim.  Personally, I found those missions to be hit or miss in Mordheim, so I'm not bothered by their absence. _childDocuments_.review: Better movement system than Mordheim, though similar play. If you liked it, you'll probably like this. _childDocuments_.review: As someone who loves Mordheim I enjoy the game quite a lot, but there is considerable caveat caused by some flaws the release version has. The most annoying and primary issues to me are mostly technical problems and design choices. I will exclusively focus on these most pressing issues, but know that I like the game none the less.=Current issues=-The AI is mediocre at its best, and crazy/suicidal/illogical at its worst.-I've witnessed AI units countless times running unecessary loops using the maps verticality, just to end the turn very close to the location it started its turn. I've witnessed the AI several times throwing grenades straight into friendlies or a wall, even though no enemy unit is located anywhere near the area or direction. The AI pathfinding gets frequently stuck on flavor objects that hamper movement or edges/ledges that the AI can not interpret. Luckily I never experienced a softlock or something as sincere as that, but once the pathfinding is completely glitched you are forced to watch that unit trying to get out of the mess, which usually takes roughly a minute before it gives up or manages to do so. While not gamebreaking, it can ruin the challenge, the immersion and waste your time considerably. Improving the AI needs to be a priority.-Technical crashes and glitches.-In my 16 hour playing the game I had it crash 2 times on me. The frequent autosaves prevented that being more than an annoyance. Additionally there are some infrequent visual glitches, which don't affect gameplay.-The unit variety feels lackluster (especially compared to Mordheim).-Of course this comparison is unfair since Mordheim, including its dlc and free updates, features especially good unit variety. But imo the three factions are not differentiated enough gameplay wise. I can't comment on the Tabletop since I never played it.-The campaign is suffering from the missing warband management.-To me this is a weird design flaw. It is relatable why this descision was probably a lot easier to implement, but customizing, "build"ing and equipping your warband is probably one of the most valued feature of this genre. So far I enjoy the campaign, but for me this devalues it and I have no clue if I will ever finish it. The story is interesting, the cutscenes are nice, but I still prefer the "real" gamemode with warband management and actual progress and consequences.-Turning the camera while you are forced to watch the AI take its turn.To me this is just a missing quality of life feature. I don't mind watching all turns and I don't mind knowing where every unit is located. But I would appreciate it if there was a moderate speedup option AND the camera perspective could be controlled, since this would actually help you plan your moves while waiting.=Conclusion=Especially for the modest price this is was an easy purchase for me, but you should be ok with putting up with the things I pointed out. The developers improved the game a lot compared to the predecessor Mordheim. We have actual coop skirmishes, the presentation is great, the visuals almost stunning for this genre. They did a great job with most of it, but some of the existing issues can subjectively be severe. They are for me.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy this game so far, but it does have a lot of issues and there are a lot of things that I think could be better. That's basically the tl;dr of the this review, so while I recommend the game, its probably best to wait until a few patches come out.Also, I've yet to play the story mode outside of the first mission, so I can't really review that. Which also means that there may be stuff about the game I don't know about yet. I also haven't done the multiplayer and can't give any insight into how good it is. The Bad:I figure its best to just start here really. There's a lot that needs to be said.1. The AI. Its pretty bad right now. Enemies will just walk against walls or other obstacles for about 5 seconds before turning around and just going a completely different way. I've seen the AI throw a grenade on itself. And I've seen it completely ignore my units even when it could have probably killed them easily and still gotten away. The AI just seems to be a big issue for right now.2. The Stats. I kinda hate how the stats work in this game. They don't really contribute anything to increasing your damage, outside of increasing penetration. I can understand guns not getting more damage for being better at shooting, but melee weapons should deal more damage the more strength you have. Melee prowess is fine, no reason to really change it, but add a melee damage modifier to strength. Also, add a health increase to toughness would be nice too. So far, I don't really know how to increase my unit's health at all, outside of the passive skill Vanguard which increases max HP by 25 but decreases action points by 10. I think adding a health increase to toughness would be nice, but maybe also just increase health by like 2 points when you upgrade any of your stats and then increase it by like 6 for each point in toughness. That's just a thought on how to do it.3. The Factions. All of the factions' house perks just seem pretty underwhelming. If the house perks were a little better or if the factions had like 2 special career paths for your units, the factions would feel a lot better. Also, only having 3 factions feels really low. Even just one more faction could help a little bit. Another idea is that each faction could specialize in a certain career so that their units in the career have a slightly better bonus. Its just another idea on how to help improve it.4. Unsafe Zones. The little metal bridges or the areas right in front of the zip lines are unsafe zones that your units automatically get moved out of if you end their turn in them. I think it would be far better to let people stop in those zones. If someone comes across the zip line and someone is in the way of the destination, make it so that the person in the way gets knocked back and lands on their back and have to spend action points to get up. If someone ends their turn on a bridge and the bridge gets destroyed, let them fall down and take damage. If it makes them fall off the map, you could either make it so they get put back onto the platform that they had been on, or just make it and instant KO. Either one would be fine by me.5. Bugs. Overall, I actually haven't encountered too many bugs. Except for one where my game has crashed about 3 or 4 times. Its a little annoying, but the game saves after each turn so it doesn't cause too much of an issue. Its just an annoyance.I think that about wraps it up for my big issues with the game.The Middle Ground:This is just stuff that isn't necessarily bad, its just not great.1. Unit Customization. It is nice to have some customization, but the customization is far from the best customization I've ever seen. There's enough there to work with, but you won't really get any impressive looking units out of it. I do like that the units' body changes based on which physical trait you choose. That's pretty cool.2. The Careers. Overall, they hit the basic types of careers you could want. Most of them don't feel particularly special, aside from maybe the lay-mechanic who have a servo arm that can have a drill or power saw and can build barricades and health dispensers. I don't know much about the lore around Necromunda(or Warhammer in general), but I'm sure there's more that can be done with this lore than what has been done so far.The Good:1. Personality Traits. These consist of a virtue, vice, and talent that can be discovered upon leveling up once your unit has reached level 5. While discovering a vice for your character could be a bit of an issue in how you use that character, I like how it helps give each character just a little bit more of their own identity.2. The Combat. Now, I'm mostly comparing the combat in this game to the combat in Mordheim. Overall, I feel like this is a decent improvement from Mordheim's combat and I'm happy with it. Movement points have changed in this game from how they were in Mordheim. You generally have 60 points of movement that you can use to move around. Similar to how Mordheim worked, the area you can move in is still a circle, but its a giant circle now rather than a collection of small circles. I also like the change to action points. My two-handed axe wielders can actually attack twice already, as long as I have some action points saved up or I entrench them. Also, this game does a better job of taking line of sight into account compared to Mordheim. The new action points system just feels like it really allows your units to do more on their turn than just swing once and be done.3. Unit Experience. I just really enjoy how it works now. Your unit gains XP and you use that XP to buy stats and skills for your unit. After having purchased so many stats and skills, your unit ranks up. I just think its a cool way of doing it. Very happy with this system.4. Operations. I like this mechanic as well. Basically, you choose a sector and you have a certain amount of missions you can do before your time in that sector ends. You want to try and collect as many resources as you can in that sector before you have to move on to the next one. There are 3 tiers of rewards you can get based on how many resources you collect. The third tier gives 4 chests with random items and money. Just to be clear, the chests aren't able to be bought with real money, just the in game currency.5. Infamy/Facilities. The facilities give you a passive buff for the duration of the operation. Something like giving your units extra XP after fighting or giving you pieces of armor after each mission. The infamy system gives you points over the duration of the operation that you can then use to give yourself a bonus on the next operation, like decreased cost of items or a new unit or pieces of armor. There's a lot of stuff it can give you.6. Injuries. I just really love this mechanic. I love it in Mordheim, I love it in Battle Brothers, and I love it here too. I like the idea that you units aren't dead just because they fall in battle. They can end up having received an injury that gives them a debuff. You still have the character, they are just a little worse off now than they were. I haven't had too many different injuries yet, but I'm hoping that the types of injuries have increased and that the injuries can open up new possibilities for characters.Overall, I do recommend the game. It can be a little rough around the edges, and there are some things that need to be fixed, but those don't ruin the game. I still really enjoy the game and believe its a good game, but I also know it can be better with some changes, which is the entire reason I'm even writing a review. I like the game and I want to see it get better.

Different gangs that really are different both with how they play and how they look isnt a thing here right now. As of now they all have that samey cant tell the difference feel to them. Once you have customised and created your gang with their skills and stats. You will find that the Gameplay is a little slow sometimes but still interesting. It keeps you engaged but again that has some issues too. The AI is as dumb as a bag of bricks. I am constantly sitting here cringing at the choices made by the AI. They are not at all threatening or pose a challenge to you no matter the difficulty. They will get stuck on objects and run for a while until they realise they are stuck and give up and go into over watch mode. They grenade themselves to death...They make you feel like you are playing against a 4 year old quite commonly. Id like to say this isnt often but it is..Though the devs have said they are working on this. The other issue is watching every AI take their move. again this wouldnt be an issue for me if they actually could make good choices but again i am forced into internal yelling at the ai as to what they hell they are doing.  The ability to speed this up would be great. The levels are always interesting and well layed out. I have had plenty of fun moments setting up traps and watching as a plan goes really well. Again if i could give this a neutral score i would but id say it just passes as a thumbs up for me. If the issues are fixed then this would be a for sure thumbs up. Maybe buy it if you want to support it or just wait if you are unsure. Atleast until the issues are fixed as some of these issues can really ruin the fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Underhive Wars

_childDocuments_.review: Compared to Mordheim that plays a bit similarly in terms of movements, usage of skill, mechanics and interactions between characters, Necromunda does a few things differently, one thing is apparent and fairly obvious, verticality and range, the maps are a lot bigger and not just in size, making use of height advantage is a big factor that comes into play and given the nature of the game itself, with this game shifting from a melee oriented to a range oriented formula, having the bigger guns with the longest range will generally be a smart idea. What also changed is now the story elements are sparated from the main course of the game, now we have a campaign, with cutscenes, which are absolutely great. Game modes are for the most part the same and plays a lot the same as Mordheim, other than the campaign, you make your own gang, chosen from 3 different houses, customize it, lead it into either single player operations or multiplayer skirmishes and based how you do in those, your gangers will net experience that'll make them stronger, raise stats, buy perks and skill, insert implants for more aimed quirks, suffer injuries both permanent and non-permanent if they fall in combat, loot treasure in the field and extract with it so you can sell it in the market in exchange for credits, useful for new and better gear, it's a very customizable experience that leaves you the freedom to play this game however you want. My only complaints are that the AI, at times, may take stupid decisions such as sit in a corner safe from harm and just spam overwatch while their respective team is getting slaugthered, or, abandon what they were doing so they could pile-on a vulnerable and dying adversary, moving from one corner of the map to the other and potentially suffering from multiple overwatch shots because of it, its very inconsistent.Another complaint is the number of houses present at the moment, only 3, but this can easily change if the game does well in terms of sales, which i hope because i like it a lot. All in all, for the price it's well worth it and it can only get better with time.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: The devs have now released a series of tip trailers for a game that exists only in their minds. There has been no patch. There has been no act of good faith in even addressing the issues beyond a compilation of them. No one should support this kind of business practice. It's simply not worth it. Perhaps, one day, the game will be playable -- but there are core gameplay decisions that will likely never be addressed if they are this willfully ignorant to the truly abysmal state of the game. It is, at best, a time waster in singer player and at its worst unplayable in multiplayer. As my original review shows -- I was in high spirits and had hope but this is the worst kind of management on display and should come with some kind of consequence for those responsible for it.In good conscience -- I can't call this unsalvageable. Perhaps I've simply been in the UnderBustle for too long already. Still, it is, indeed, a representation of the Warhammer tabletop experience. You gather your crew. I like to make mine unique by making them all women. Since that's what makes them interesting, it's the ways in which they're all ubiquitous with one another that highlights their ability to carry a gatling gun in sensible wedges. It's very hip, you just likely wouldn't understand the references -- given your upbringing. Look, you'll get it just watch out for traps, okay?Then you make sure that they are looking just -- gorge. You let the paint dry and possibly realize it's long since time to open a window or two. Then you go to your local game/hobby/tiny space-cult battledome campaign simulator longhouse and sit in an empty room while you move the figurines around a elaborate 3D map your mom crafted from things she had left over from scrapbook class. Don't worry, your Elite Halfway House 4 Wayward Industrial Ne'er-Do-Wells get chased by the manager's Gang that he set up on hotwheels and programmed to stunt on ya for an hour and a half until closing time.You laugh now, but once Kryla-T600 Death from Above's you into another dimension twice, you realize that it's not magic -- but where else? Where else could you get this experience? Even X-Commie: Alien Hater 2 only let you dress them up funny, but never really took it to outerspace. You could crawl inside the Snake Queen's body, buy you couldn't play the campaign AS the Snake Queen! It's not Mordheim, but it is a small unit tactics experience from the Warhammer lich masters. Because that was also a deeply flawed, poorly tended & ultimately still somehow the best option contender in its magical wonderbox of the small-unit tactical murder-o-rama and Polly Pocket genre at the time. This lacks much of the charm, story and ultimately diversity (class differences don't make up for fielding an iconic House/Faction/Archetypical Thingamadoodle to scramble up nearby walls while your dim-witted, but hot bodied, Leader gets pummeled to death by rat goblins. I think that's a shame, others may not.) It does make up for it with promoting a heavier use, or at least opportunity for, skills and that's fun.You win some, you lose some. I don't regret giving them the money. Even if they just ran Mordheim: Mord Simulator through this graphics engine and called it a day, I'm glad that they're still trying to make whatever this is into something that is playable. Since this is, when compared to the starter kit and my empty padded cell anyway. There are definitely circumstances by which I think it could be something that the same people who regularly turn dice and plastic into hellscapes of enjoyment for the whole family will manage to arrange for themselves eventually.The only real advice for what to do with -- whatever this currently is would be ... maybe stop trying to appeal to the Mass Market with Slaanesh & Papa Nurgle. I don't think it's going to be everyone's thing and when you try to reskin a cat that's been anointed as sacrifice to the personification of humanity's collective resentment -- like, it just kind of going to come off as inauthentic, ya know? Silly shooting games don't make up for it, sorry Dad-Mom Hellbeast, it's not a phase and I'm not just going to get over it. Mordheim was a trundling mess, but it was full of life. This is a slightly more polished mess, but is a little soulless in the bad way. As a tech demo, it's cool.Like goat simulator, but you sacrifice it into the void at the end and I can't say I regretted my time. Then, I waste that on all sorts of poorly thought out dumpster fires. No one called me a newb or a dweeb and none of my figurines got Mountain Dew spilled on them. The future is now! Your experience of the Necromunda: SpanxHive Hardcore Space-Ganger Team Dressup Sim-Opticon may, of course, differ. Just don't throw the baby out with the bathwater. Just the baby please, the water's fine -- jump on in!

_childDocuments_.review: The Issues as I see them...Munda has a lot of potential but most of it is potential that is wasted in its current state. Let me start with the positive. I like the look of the game and the Gangs. I like the ability to do do Co-op and PvP. I like some of the attention to detail. I like the 40k universe as so this tickles my fancy quite a lot. All of those things turn a lack luster pain in the butt of a game into something that I still like playing even though it is nearly as frustrating as it is fun while hoping sincerely that the game gets some heavy overhauls.Now to the bad stuff. I have a reasonably nice gaming laptop; not top of the line but better than average and its struggles to  keep up with the visuals as soon as auras and environmental graphics like sparks and ash become persistant on the screen. This feel like its most likely due to some poor coding than an hardware issue but that is admittedly not my wheelhouse and I am just guessing based on personal experience. That said what is there I like a lot.... Id just like it a lot more if I didn't have to play the game at its lowest graphics setting to stop it from lagging out even during single player.The game difficulty feels like it was designed for a preteen/teen demographic. It is far too easy with rudimentary at best strategy involved. All the tools are there in one form or another to make the game either challenging, like the table top game, or both but they all feel dumbed down to attracts children with a 15 second attention span.The story mode is a long drawn out and nearly useless tutorial since many aspects of the game are not even explained, and you never really get used to any build because they are changed from chapter to chapter. A better idea would have been to build your own gang and run through each of the three versions of the story arc dependent on which gang you built. That said the cut scenes are great (minus some truly horrific voice acting choices).There is FAR FAR FAR too much capacity for movement and action in the game. Tactics become almost pointless because most fighters can almost endlessly traverse vertical distances and can cross most of the map in a single turn. In the correct circumstances I have traversed bottom to top the entire map and gone 180 degrees around the outside of the map using only my normal move, my hook, and some jumps. To make things worse you can intersperse all that movement with far more actions that is reasonable. There really should be a single bar of "actions pool" that counts toward movement and actions both which forces players to decide between more movement or more actions. This is truly one of the most disappointing aspects of the game and its correction would lend toward a pretty simple and vast improvement. My buddies and I found that putting a 60 second turn timer on our PvP and Co-Op games forced a bit of speed and was a bandaid correction for this problem.The Camera positioning during animated scenes like attacks and actions often leaves you either staring at a wall close up and missing the action OR doing its best to give you a seizure by flickering at a rapid rate.Object location is an issue particularly with the Gangers. Try to activate an elevator going down with a toe still on the level and you will see the elevator descend with you hanging in the air while you little toe presumably supports your body weight. Or allows you to walk off of a platform into mid air because there is a crouched bad guy below you but then forces you to be stuck there. On a similar note if you kneel (which is often what I do when Im at the end of my movement) and attempt to end your turn but are in a Danger Zone (basically on or in the path of terrain that can be altered) you are forced to move off of it in a computer defined manner after a warning and often into a senseless location (like under a bridge rather that to one end or another). However the warning comes too late for you to not get screwed out of the points you just spent to kneel. No I understand that at a certain level big boy rules should apply but seriously either allow us to cause harm to players who end up on dangerous terrain OR give us a better warning indication so we aren't wasting actions. Preferably let us harm characters that are silly enough to put themselves at risk.The game makes you go though a senseless amount of turn burning when there is no enemy left on the field. On a similar note the game play is aggravatingly slow due to silly messages that essentially tell you the obvious but spend forever tell it to you and making you watch the enemy do their actions in what seems like slow motion. There is just a lot of time wasted.The game has repeatedly crashed on it's own during multiplayer and in single player. The AI is hopelessly stupid. I was going to list the ways in which the AI is just abjectly useless but it would be easier to point out the positive things about the AI and that is really just to say...... They on a rare occasion take an action that almost seems like a sane and rational human being would have considered making it. I'm currently writing this as I sit here for going on 30 minutes while an AI character stares at a wall and am hoping (foolishly) that it snaps out of it and I can complete this important mission without having to forfeit or crash the game intentionallyMany of the abilities and smaller screen icons are never really explained in any way leaving us to guess at what they meant though trial and error.It would be nice if captured weapons retained their original appearance if they came from an opposing House. It would add variety and make for a fluffy and fun trophy appearance.

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game as a table top game when I was younger.  It was great then.  This is an interesting take on the same game.  The worst part about the game is the AI doing some strange things as well as the story missions being a plain pass because it takes away what makes the game great, the gang members and making them into individuals.  Over all I like this game.  It is strategic, I play single player, and have found it to be a tad easy but fun.  They are updating it and have improved it already, so that is a bonus.  You can outsmart the AI in a battle of attrition and have them do a lot of dirty work for you, but that is part of the joy of it all.  The Operations are what make it fun for me and seeing how I can come out of one with more resources than the other gangs is fun.  The sense of height in the maps really is meaningful as well, if you have the high ground you tend to win more than not.  I have to say if you are a tactical fan and loved Mordheim you should pick this up and give it a go.  Great Game and helps bring back that feeling of leading my game in Necromunda back in the day.

_childDocuments_.review: So I've seen a few other people speaking to most of the problems I see with this game. It feels like a huge step backwards from Mordheim. Every improvement they have made comes with serious drawbacks around this.-Loading times have been cut down, in return the game "revamps" the initiative system, and intersperses each turn with (and I have counted) 4 completely unneeded 3 second pauses, as well as a higher than 50% chance of between 30-120 seconds of following the AI walking into walls and throwing grenades at themselves before you get to take a turn.-the much better map comes with no fog of war, cutting down on the amount of tension in the gameplay as you always know exactly where every enemy character is.-The story is completely separated from your custom gang, instead of building up your team, learning how to use each type of character in your gang and developing their abilities you get handed a squad with not real indications of what each of them actually do unless you navigate something like 6 different menus during the mission for each character, then after a few missions they hand you a completely new group of people so you have to figure it out all over again. -Nothing really differentiates your characters besides what weapons you choose to give them, at least when you are starting out. all the "big" variety in builds comes down to small mechanical things that the colour of your clothes gives you, and they seem pretty low impact.At the end of all this though this game has so much potential to be great that it makes it all the more frustrating. I really really hope that I can come back to this after 6 months and see a game worth playing.
_childDocuments_.name: Necromunda: Underhive Wars

_childDocuments_.review: Five hours played and starting to appreciate the tactical aspects of this game. The turn system is unique, both/all sides select their character, Then you get to see the opposition choice...and what order of activation based on Initiative number.  Do I activate a high initiative character early, or save that for later in the turn ?..With up to four players in a battle, getting this stage of selection right  can give a critical tactical advantage.Maps are another aspect of the battle that need to be factored in, there is a very nice Map view that lays everything out simple and clear, and holding the CTRL key highlights gang members and other important features clearly. Presentation and personalisation has been created by a team who understand what Warhammer gamers love, personalising their figures. There is a comprehensive Gang creation system that allows almost limitless customising of each gang member. I have played for five hours and barely scratched the surface, personally I have not encountered game bugs..though I am aware of them through the feedback section. Overall I am more than happy with my game, of course there are those who disagree.....but that is what Necromunda Underhive was created for, settling Disagreements.

_childDocuments_.review: This may sound like a negative review but, all in all, it is what you expect from a first release these days. It is buggy. It crashes unexpectedly. Some things don't work correctly and some descriptions contain the programming code rather than the description. All in all not a bad successor to Mordheim. These days most releases are buggy with a zillion patches to come. Also I would expect many DLC's, with the usual Games Workshop price tag, as the board game had 8 clans and this version has 3. Having said that, if you enjoy turn based strategy with good list design depth this would be a game for you. If you missed the sale then I would not buy it straight away. Play Mordheim some more, unless you don't mind debugging this game for them for free. It should be a good game in about 6 months and I will try to update this review then.

_childDocuments_.review: Just writing down this review to explain why people freaked out over things, and make some negative reviews more "clear"TL;DRAI is really bad, game is fundamentally really cool. Long:- I have no idea why but people just go in story mode and didn't even bothered try the real gem " Gang " mode. As far as i understood , story mod is more like a tutorial to make people understand whats going on , and explain the lore behind Necromunda. In my opinion little pop up s work well and you understand the basic UI in 1 or 2 missions. If you played X-Com or similar games before, you already kind of know what to do.- After understanding the basics, i just get in the gang mode and it's pretty much what you expect really. You can create a gang, you got plenty of customizations, you recruit guys, select and go for missions and get rewards. Also have a multiplayer thingy but i'm not sure if its working at this moment. -  There are some cool mission features like HQ attacks, special quests etc. Also its basicly simulating other gangs at the same time while you are doing missions, so they get resources on their own and/or attack things without you joining in. So it's nice.Negative things i agree on;- AI is really bad, like really bad. Most of the time they are just going around and hiding in weird places, attacking you mindlessly without an actual reason, they are just basicly playing deathmatch on their own regardless the objectives. Also they are trying to run inside walls, just stuck and stand there for multiple rounds. Sometimes tho, AI works as intended and basicly planning traps, doing sneaky stuff and actually working fine. So for this problem i kind of thinking like playing the game on Easy-Normal mode, sometimes they just act like Einstein, sometimes more like midless zombies ( well, most of the time ) - Maybe adding some extra tooltips to mission objectives can help a lot. I kind of didn't understand what to do on one mission, thought i'm gonna lose it in the bery end and actually won a decisive victory. Still have no idea why i get it. - Just add a "Tutorial" term on the first 1-2 missions on Story mode, or maybe something to indicate that it will explain you the basics, instead of letting player know with a" i think you should play story first bro " kind of message. People cant understand that and just passing by, so yeah that's why whining about. Overall, i think the game is good at the moment but the price is a bit high for a broken AI. If you like warhammer in general, you'll probably like it as it is. But if you are just an X-Com fan and trying to find something like that in this game, let me just tell you before you actually buy it. It's not X-com, you'll not find that feel in here. Only similarity is basicly 3rd person turn based combat thingy, other than that , it's not the same.

_childDocuments_.review: Campaign is garbo, Singleplayer a mess, Multiplayer lacks the polish to make it playableCampaign:-No customization progression for characters one of the main draws of this genre.-Tutorial content is spread out beyond reason, on the flip side the start of each mission is like an information dump of tooltips without demonstrating utility effectively.-Is to short to be a "campaign" but far to lengthy to be a tutorial-Does a no/minimal explaining of what his happening on enemy turns but forces you to watch them for 1+minutes each unitSingle Player:-Gamebreaking bugs + AI Unit pathing can break causing an unending AI turn that will force you to concede-Animations are ok the first few times but with no AI acceleration forced to watch nonsense moves from AI really highlighting poor AI and pathfindingMultiplayer:-Disconnects count as wins for the person unplugging their internet but no rewards for anyone even if someone leaves with 1 unit left can also be used to dodge injury in "real" mode but can also be used to rack up wins in exhibition mode. _childDocuments_.review: I'm really enjoying this game so far. If you are a fan of Turn Based Tactics games, you might find something you like here. It looks great and is very atmospheric. At first I had a few teething problems. For example, found the camera quite janky, but changing graphics settings (to medium/60fps) sorted it out. I also found switching to controller made for a better experience overall. I've played 11 of the tutorial story  missions so far, as well as about 10 missions with own gang. I couldn't complete story mission 11 due to a bug (Vex couldnt put down the toxin container , so couldn't enter the vent) which was annoying, and I'll have to replay.  So far, I much prefer the missions with my own gang, and enjoy the progression. Some of the skills are very very satisfying to use. As other have stated, the cons are the AI, which can be hit and miss, and the long turn times due to the camera following the AI throughout their turn. However, I found I got used to this after a while, and it's only annoying when the AI wastes it's turn (which it does from time to time). Finally, there are some issues with pvp - in my second match we found a bug that caused both players games to crash to desktop. So far 6 out of 7 pvp games have crashed. So if you are interested in pvp, wait to see if it is fixed. If you are on the fence about this game, check out some of the gameplay videos on Youtube (AirsickHydra or GamekNight). However, if you have a low tolerance for buggy games, it might be best to wait for some patches.

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR (quite long) - Wait until on sale, wait until patched, Wait.I understand I am in the minority of positive reviews, but hear me out.I'm gonna break this down through the different modes of play, and end with thoughts. If you actually read this, thank you.General Issues:Expect the occasional Crash To Desktop. Expect the AI to be poor. Expect items and abilities to have {Damage_Value%} placeholder tags. Even when just playing a match, expect things to be Laboriously Slow as every ganger has a "Turn Start" and "Turn End" screen that you can't tab past. Expect a whole lot of Bugginess. Expect, above all else, to be Confused All The Time.Now, on to how this game works.Campaign:The campaign is a mission-by-mission storyline that follows three different gangs as they race for archeotech. The voice-acting is middle-ground, the music is average grungy sci-fi and the the storyline is  blase, but we're here to watch gangers kill each other over perceived sleights and need for resources. This aspect gets a pass.Gameplay wise, though, it's a tutorial. The whole 15 something missions, just one big tutorial, teaching you about different game modes and class abilities, items and weapons, interactables and the like. But... It doesn't actually teach you how any of those matter, outside of the campaign. You don't keep the items you pick up from one level of the campaign to the next. You don't get to decide what skills your gangers get, or what your crew is made up of. It's a mechanical tutorial, and after about 6-7 missions you're pretty much able to just drop it and go play Gang Mode, unless you're truly invested in the storyline. (you won't be.)Gang Mode:The game will suggest you finish campaign mode, but trust me, it will not brief you on the things you need to know; like what character statistics are, how you choose different abilities and passives for a gang member, how to SHOP, and how you manage everything. You're thrown to the wolves out the gate with Gang Mode.Mechanically, Gang Mode is the meat of what Necromunda is. You make a gang, and through dozens of matches try to make them rich and infamous. You're given complete control over how your gangers are leveled up, spending earned experience on upgrading statistics that effect the ability of a fighter or on actions or passive buffs that WIDELY change how your ganger is going to work inside the game; You also spend currency an time managing what equipment your gang hoards and wields. None of these are taught to you, and understanding them differentiate a gang that'll durdle in a match or a min-max'd crit build on a heavy with an stubgun that drops two gangers turn one.There are currently two ways to play Gang Mode: Skirmish, and Operations.Skirmishes, right now, will be pretty much against AI only. The queues are empty, but you can always set up a custom match against AI, or if you have one online, a friend. Custom Matches with friends would be, imo, the sole way you will want to play this game.Operations, as far as I can tell, are vs AI exclusively. You're given some extra loot, the ability to use your gang's infamy to acquire more, specific loot, or cheapen the prices of leveling up your characters, and as long as you preform well and complete some side-quest style missions you can walk away wealthy. The fact the AI will spend a lot of your games running into crates and path-finding poorly means this is the place to Grind.Now, for why I'm giving this game a recommendation.I grew up playing first edition necromunda with friends. We still fall back on stories and characters that we built together as our gangs clashed on the tabletop (or countertop, or floorspace). The fun of Necromunda is in the emergent narrative- in making something living and the shared experience of characters rise, fall, and recuperation. I think, honestly, that Underhive Wars could be that. I've had a BLAST playing gang mode and building a gang. Watching characters grow, seeing how they take on traits that change how they'll fight, and even feeling outright outraged when one of my gang members died. I actually tunnel-visioned an AI character for the purpose of enacting a revenge for a passed on ganger. In this game is a glimpse of what Necromunda is.You will need friends, people who will slog through the Much Less Than Acceptable bugs of this game, to find it. You'll need dedication to finding a story together and a whole lot of patience. But I love what this game reminds me of, and I love that right now (written in a US State that is still enforcing shelter-in-place measures) I can play a game of necromunda, with my friends, if I want to.So what do I suggest?I think with a lot (and I mean a LOT) of love from the devs, with patches and quality of life updates and serious focus, this game could become something really memorable. Personally, I think the game -looks- good. It's atmospheric, the environments are grungy and fit 40k, and character models can actually end up looking pretty damn impressive once they have some gear on 'em.But if you a. don't have a group of friends willing to slug it out in a game with bugs, b. don't want to spend more than an hour to play a match where you take 3 turns, or c. Just aren't willing to play games that aren't up to polish, do NOT get this game right away.Get this game when it's been fixed, or is on sale.I want people to get this game; I cannot tell you to get this game NOW.

_childDocuments_.review: This game didn't get the support from fans that it deserved. Now that Chaos Gate: Daemonhunters has been released you can go back and see how this one succeeded and failed.I think the Story not being tied into the Gang Campaign either split work or otherwise hurt the initial launch. Perhaps instead of a linear narrative story mode the writer could have written "scenarios" where you have occurrences and events interwoven into the gang management campaign, something like Wildermyth has, which subjects your gang members to vignettes and events that could randomly change things up. The pathfinding at launch was pretty bad, and while it has improved drastically, there are still some issues with NPCs trying to navigate sharp turns and makeshift (destructible) terrain and bridges. Sometimes you glitch out if you hump on objects too much. It's much improved and functional given the amount of verticality in this game (zip lines, grappling hooks, fast rope, etc.) I know people would like squads to be bigger, but the 4 Gangers per deployment have a lot of progression and customization and can pull off crazy turns. It's not like Mordheim where you have a lot of cannon fodder that get one attack and pass. I would have loved more support for this, like the oddball gangs of Scavvies and Ratskins, or Hired Guns to change things up like Mordheim, but I'll be coming back to this after the "newness" of CG:D wears off   :)

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking to scratch a 40k/ gritty sci-fi itch, Underhive Wars does this reasonably well. The game looks nice and the aesthetics of your gang make it much more enjoyable. Though, only 3 factions being available leads to some disappointment if you dont like Roidy Beef Boys, Coomerbait, or Biker-Looking-Dudes. I haven't gotten too far in the story, but the ball really feels dropped in the voiceover department; despite everyone wearing masks and rebreathers, they sound way too crisp and bland; the voices should have been put through a filter.If you're looking for a challenging and deep squad based tactical skirmish game, you probably won't be too enthralled. The AI still has the same problems that come with the free movement system and probably wouldnt be as bad if it was just made gridbased. It's very easy to create broken characters once you start getting experience. In the beginning it will seem like a slog where everything takes 3 characters turns to take down, but with a couple skills you can easily burst 1 or more enemies with a single character's turn. There's even a melee passive for leaders that makes it impossible for enemies to engage you with melee unless they are prebuffed to reduce AP costs. Once you get a hang of the mechanics, You can easily beat gangs of 1k score higher than you.So far loot is the same weapons with stat bumps per level progression; I would have hoped for an actual modding system, but this still works just fine because there is no health creep on character leveling. Some weapons and abilities do seem flat out better than others. For instance, grenade abilities for saboteur do the spread weapons job better and don't restrict what's in your hands. While unpolished, I do find the game pretty fun. I feel like with enough care and content addition in the form of gangs, modes, and maps it could be much better. If this was priced at 60, I wouldn't recommend it, but I definitely enjoyed my time so far for the current price.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, so, let me first say that I almost quit and uninstalled the game within the first hour.  I'm very glad that I didn't.The setting is amazing, the character design is amazing, the story is great, except...  The quest design is so unclear it becomes very frustrating.  You'll have a 5 turn limit to do a task, only for that task's completion to give you another task.  (Example:  You have 5 turns to get supplies to a door, but once you do that, you learn that a specific character now needs to complete another task with no additional time.  That character may be no where near the objective as you haven't been planning for them to need to do that task.)  Its also unclear of what you have to do, lacking very good quest indicators.  So in short, the tutorial is terrible at teaching you the game.The pacing is slow with certain unnecessary slowdowns that just add up, (Like when there is only one character to select in a turn, why does it ask you what character you want to select?) There is also a pause before each enemy moves which is a few seconds, and the pathfinding is pretty bad with enemies trying to walk through fences and obstacles.All that said, they did such a fantastic job with the world, characters, and most impressively; the customization.  Compared to Mordheim, Necromunda has a lot more running and gunning which is a lot more fun.  (Played both)  I also have always loved the setting of Necromunda more as you can really get a taste of gangs struggling to survive vs just a bunch of adventurers trying to get rich.If you can struggle past the unclear story missions, and bad pathfinding, I think this game starts to shine.I can't wait for additional gangs, especially if my Cawdor fanatics ever show up!

_childDocuments_.review: It breaks my heart to say this because I love Mordheim but this game isn't ready for a full release. It's clunky, buggy, poorly balanced, uninviting and very disappointing. It could well develop into something as good as Mordheim, but it's going to need some work - and, even still, some of the core design choices I find strange. The lack of movement pips, like Mordheim had, removes all nuance from a well executed turn - instead, you basically have a big circle that you can move anywhere within. This, coupled with the fact that everyone seems to have vast amounts of MP, means that a unit can literally assault a building through a window then make an attack before leaving again through the same window and returning to the original cover outside. This is utterly ridiculous. Turn-based squad combat games are all about the cunning use of combined arms, moving and covering, flanking and out-flanking. In it's current form, Necromunda is about dog-piling the weakest enemy unit in the hope your foe goes a unit down before you do. It's like the designers wanted all this gimmicky verticality and wouldn't budge on it and the actual game-play has been the price.I dunno. Maybe I'm being harsh. I've not given up on Necromunda. But the fact is even in it's rawest beta state when there were no skills, no legacy, no campaign and a gazillion bugs I genuinely loved Mordheim - it just had this certain magical something. And I don't see that here.

_childDocuments_.review: For me, this game is sort of a mixed bag.  While I love the Necromunda setting (I used to play the miniature game long ago), I struggle mightily with the '3D-ness' of the level maps.  Likes:- General setting:  The developer did a great job with the level design aesthetics.  Lots of variety and tons of places to hide.- Character building:  I really like the way you can develop your individual characters to make them your own.Dislikes:- The same level design that I like it the main reason why this game frustrates me.  I just seem to get lost in the maps and really struggle with positioning my team so they don't get hammered during the next combat.  I know that playing longer may overcome my struggle, but until then I guess I will continue to get my butt handed to me over and over again.Conclusion:If you love turn-based strategy games (VERY heavy on the strategy) and can put up with the quirkiness of the maps, then by all means get the game.  I have not given up on it (despite my continual losses) because the developer did a great job of capturing the world of Necromunda and one day, when I am ready to put much more time into learning how to play, I will return to the game and become the strongest game in the Underhive!

_childDocuments_.review: After about 25 hours I finished the story. I didn't run into any game breaking bugs, and only had the game crash a couple of times. My biggest complaint is, with Mordheim, I got to play a story mode with each group. In this, you only have one story line to play down. I get I am probably the minority in this, but I really enjoy story mode. I enjoy getting bits and pieces of the whole story and having a goal to work towards. I don't feel like there is too much of a goal to work towards in the game once the story is over... and PVP was never my thing.I know several people have had issues with the game, the biggest being corrupted save files. That would absolutely be devastating, but I personally haven't ran into those issues yet. Lets also be honest that Mordheim and Necromunda will have bugs that will never be fixed. I lost count of how many times I had to restart a Mordheim mission because it bugged out... and Mordheim took WAY LONGER to complete a game of.The long and short of it is, if you enjoyed Mordheim and enjoy this kind of game, grab it while it's on sale. Just don't expect it to be perfect.  At the very least, it's good enough for me to get a thumbs up versus a thumbs down. Take that as you will.

_childDocuments_.review: While at first glance Necromunda looks like a more awesome version of Mordhiem, there are some major differences, besides of course the setting. While the maps are awesome and huge, multilevel arenas with beautiful imagery, there isn't much the maps offer that Mordheim didn't. The level system for your party and units isn't missing anything per se, but compared to that of Mordheim there are seemingly far fewer ways to customize your team. While the color scheme and costume customization are far more detailed, the skill lists and unit types are more limited. All in all if you loved Mordheim as much as I did or are a fan of Warhammer games, then I recommend this game, but I would caution that you might wait until the game's numerous bugs are polished out and there is a sale and/or for more gangs to be released through DLC (assuming and hoping this is the case) as there are only three factions to choose from, in order to really get your money's worth. Or go buy Mordheim!

_childDocuments_.review: For context, I'm a Warhammer 40k fan. As a kid, I played 40k tabletop. I remember reading about Necromunda in issues of White Dwarf and dreaming about playing it. As an adult, I still dabble in a bit of tabletop - I purchased the recent Necromunda Underhive boxed set and have enjoyed playing it - and I love the fiction of the 41st millennium. I also played a lot of, and enjoyed, the Mordheim adaptation by the same developers of this game.The TL;DR is that this is an enjoyable but deeply flawed 40k tactics game. As someone who is grateful as a video game adaptation of Necromunda, I've enjoyed playing it but I can't help but feel disappointed at this missed opportunity.The process of creating and growing a gang is a load of fun. Abilities and perks are interesting. Ganger customisation is really good cosmetically - it's clear that a lot of effort has gone in here.The environments are expansive, with impressive verticality. The ability to traverse ziplines and grappel down from great heights and destroy traversible terrain, adds to the tactical gameplay and forces you to think in three dimensions.As a new player, you must learn assimilate a lot of information to play effectively, and the UI just doesn't do a good enough job. I'm genuinely not one of these PC master race folk, but it's clear compromises have been made here. I understand that design decisions are made to give the best experience across multiple platforms with reasonable effort, but I can't remember the last time I was so desperate to mouseover an icon and read a tool tip.It's soul-crushingly slow. Other reviews have gone into this in detail, so I won't. Suffice it to say that the cycle of watching the AI take its turn, selecting one of you fighters and then operating them is a chore and feels unnecessarily drawn out.The singleplayer campaign - particularly the writing - is absolutely dire. As a tutorial, it's drawn-out and ineffective. What a waste of time. It's not necessary unless you want to unlock a handful of haircuts for ganger customisation, but what a missed opportunity to showcase the awesome fiction of a hive city. As a fan of the fluff, it's so disappointing.I could be wrong here with my limited playtime, but there doesn't feel like a big enough difference between gangs. Each has basically the same archetypes and I don't understand properly what makes each gang unique - not in the same way as looking at the tabletop rules, for example. Again, this may be inexperience on my part.The presentation and player experience are generally and constistenly unpolished. It's also buggy (as of a couple of days from launch).On completing a mission, the ending dialogue will play and the save icon will spin in the lower right corner of the screen. The game will stall here, with a force quit and replaying the final turns of the game the only optionSometimes the AI will just walk into a corner or platform edge perpetually. This can also happen on your turn, when moving one of your fighters triggers an ambush from an AI player. Sometimes the AI sorts itself out. At other times, it's force quit after a couple of minutes.Dead enemy fighters will stay on the map so that you can loot their corpses. However they'll often T-pose, which makes them look like they're still active. This can draw you into making bad decisions.When fighters are closely packed, the game can get confused. This has led to me not being able to target an enemy when an ally is immediately adjacent.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a huge fan of Necromunda from back in the day, but unfortunately I can't find anyone local to play with. I was hoping that Underhive War would scratch that itch, but sadly the game isn't really that much fun at all. Not only is the A.I. terrible, even compared to Rogue Factor's other game, but the Story Mode is a joke. I have to spend it as a rotation of gangs with varying members within it so its basically a paint by numbers game instead of allowing me to build up my own strategies based on my Ganger selection. And on that note, limiting the number of the gangs to start and selling us the rest of them later is JUST lame! All the core gangs should have been available from day one. If you MUST have DLC it should have been things like Pyskter powers a/o Brutes. Come on if Games Workshop wont give is Phyrr Cat models, can't a video game at least do it. I will admit the models and stages look great and being able to save and come back later is great for someone like me who doesn't always have to the time to sit down for a full match. But those things that would be cherries on top of a good game, not the reasons to buy a game. I am really sad this wasn't a better game, since as I said I'm a huge fan of Necromunda and think this COULD have been an amazing game.

_childDocuments_.review: The good: Graphic, Level Design, and soundtrack is top notch, really captures the feel of the gritty world of Necromunda. Character customization options are very robust.The bad: The interface can be counterintuitive, eg, character's unable to move past others due to enormous collision boxes (if you've played the tabletop game, picture every ganger on a 32mm base and unable to move past one another) Story mode lacks any sense of progress or continuity because items/gear/skills don't progress between sessions and you switch sides often.The Ugly: game is very unstable and has had significant crashes (bad enough to require a full system reboot) every 6 hours or so of playtime. cut scene audio often desyncs entirely.Conclusion: I'm a necromunda fan and I'm enjoying this game quite a bit despite some pretty significant technical issues.

_childDocuments_.review: Giving this a positive review since the game feels amazing. I've played this for 25 hours after launch, I've enjoyed it so much. So easily worth the promotional $32 I spent. Art and style are fantastic, game is fairly stable (despite some of the other reviews I've seen, I've only had one CTD which was likely my own fault for alt-tabbing during a loading screen), and overall the effects look very clean.BUTI skipped the story after the first four missions since I had little to no investment in the plot and went straight to building my own Gang. So far, I'm glad I did.AI direction at higher levels seems to have improved massively. I see fewer enemies chucking grenades at their own feet. However, it still needs work. When the AI is working, the enemies feel clever and adept at staging runs for objectives in order to leave with the loot. But if you get a few good rounds where you dumpster your opponents and take their weapons, the remaining operations in the set become way too easy as the AI doesn't seem to know how to handle unarmed fighters effectively. Great since it makes taking out your opponents feel meaningful, but bad since it still feels the AI is lacking. Content feels like a good start, but ultimately a little shallow. I've gotten my gang up to around rank 8 on every character, and I've maxed out my available active/passive abilities on my core crew. But I can only get so many Lascannons version III - V before the equipment starts to feel a touch stale. There is functionally no difference between a Chain Sword, a Power Sword, and a regular Sword. A regular sword overall does more damage, a powersword has 20% more armor penetration (but roughly 10% less damage) and a chainsword has a very small bleed effect (but also, 10% less damage) but the latter two have a reload requirement. Effectively making a regular sword vastly more AP efficient while sacrificing practically nothing. I could see more equipment specific abilities allowing you to specialize your people more deeply, or greater requirements for using specific equipment of higher potency. Like, put an intelligence requirement on using power weapons to sap EXP away from Brawlers, and make power weapons deal higher melee penetration or greater damage. Make them correspondingly rare and more expensive to fit the lore. Might also consider weapon modifications to keep things a bit more fresh. Perhaps this changes somewhere after the fourth operational level, but I haven't gotten there yet.Match flow is just... outright bad. Once you get used to the individual hotkeys it moves at a steady pace, but the amount of time that is wasted while selecting a new fighter is just way too damned high. There are three transition screens between every "Round", with up to five "Rounds" in a turn. And watching the AI soft-lock the game repeatedly while running into obstacles gets very tiresome.I also feel the game is a touch too easy since you can see the entire map, and melee is ridiculously OP. You can run farther on a turn than most weapons can shoot, so getting up next to your opponent and twin-striking them to death is pretty simple. I don't mind being able to see the entire map, but maybe add in some camo options to make ranged combat a touch more meaningful. I could also see reducing visibility but increasing the range of weapons to make sniper ambushes possible, or just slow everyone down so they can't sprint all the way across the map in a single round. Melee doesn't need to be nerfed so much as Ranged combat needs to be buffed to make things feel more deadly. There is no good ranged equivalent to Stun.Overall, this feels like a great start. It's a good platform to build on, and if the Dev improves the AI and match flow, you'll have a solid re-playable strategy game which is more than worth the money and could host numerous DLCs. But it needs some TLC before DLC.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually do this but rather than launching into a lengthy and convoluted description I'm going to start with a list of pros and cons starting with the bad:Cons - The story campaign is linear and initially confusing and despite being directed there as a means to learn the game the tutorial elements within it are not that helpful.- The expanded height of maps compared to Mordheim can be more confusing than interesting and the map display does not make this any easier.- Character types and abilities are not as well defined as they are in Mordheim and even the different factions don't differ much other than in their starting stats.- No prestige units as far as I can tell.Pros- Despite being linear the story campaign is fairly entertaining.- "Operations" that take the place of the "Warband" campaign and represent the core of the single player experience are great fun. You can build and improve your units here but, strangely, injuries have very little bearing in comparison with their dynamic use in the previous game. Character traits, active skills, and passive skills are quite diverse allowing for varied build approaches.- Multiplayer is fun (but will likely be ruined by 'let's play' and min/max players pretending to be new to the game by using low level teams).- Players who complained about "rng" in Mordheim will be happier with this as you rarely miss.Overall I much prefer Mordheim and in a few ways Necromunda is a step backward. It seems to have been deliberately simplified at the tactical level for those who complained about the previous game being too difficult or complex. But this comes at the cost of strategic depth. This said, it remains another excellent offering from Rogue Factor that will provide hundreds of hours of enjoyment for comparatively little outlay. Since Mordheim is my favourite tactical turn based game EVER my response could be somewhat biased both positively and negatively.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't normally write reviews, but it seems a bunch of players are complaining about the AI without understanding how the game mechanics work, so I wanted to explain it.  That being said the AI isn't perfect, like the AI in almost every video game known to man, they are stupid compared to human players.Firstly the AI takes awhile to find a path sometimes do to the detailed battlefields with lots of debris.  This does not affect their movement points in a negative way though.  The game calculates spent movement points based on where you end up when you perform an action.  So if you walk around in a a circle for 10 min and only end up a few feet away from where you started, then you only spend a few movement points.  So the long pathing doesn't gimp the AI.Second the AI likes to kneel often, even if it doesn't make much sense at times.  This is because kneeling makes you harder to hit versus ranged weapons. It seems silly seeing the AI always kneeling even if they have no one who can shoot them, but from the AI perspective its the right thing to do, even when an enemy is around the corner who will run up and stab you.  They don't think 10 moves ahead, they just kneel at the end of their move if they have the action points left for it.  The AI loves to use its buffs and auras, sometimes a bit too much.  Occasionally the AI with spend too much time buffing themselves and not dealing enough damage early on.  Again, AI can't yet plan ahead or actually think, we don't have Skynet yet.  Buffing is better output in the long term, the AI can't predict that you are going to send your whole gang after one or two of their members and kill them before they get to benefit from the buffs.  The AI can be summed up as all Strategy and no Tactics.  It does take advantage of your mistakes though, so be careful.There are some glitches from time to time, but I haven't found anything game breaking yet.PLAY THE CAMPAIGN, at least the first few missions, so you know how the game works before you try to make your own gang.The only major flaw right now is that there is too much movement.  You can have certain gangers with the right skills that can run across the map in a single turn.  The game is balanced around it and melee isn't OP.   You can disengage from combat after they maniac runs across the map at you (for a cost) and blast them to bits, but its just a bit silly how far they move at times.The game is good, solid bones and decent muscle, just needs to be fleshed out a bit.  More customization would be great, but that is easy enough to add in patches down the line.  The game is fun, and the price is fair, especially with sales on many sites at launch putting it in the $25-33 range.  If this was $60 I would expect more polish, but at this price point it is perfectly playable, replayable, and the atmosphere is spot on.
