_childDocuments_.review: Here is my Review for the Game, after roughly 6 Hours, in both, Story and free play mode.To get a few things out of the way first:1. my system is quite a bit BELOW the MIN. specs given.At points where this is important, i mention it seperately.The in my oppinion good:The game runs rather smooth, on an below min spec system.Sometimes gun shots wont show, but thats most likely a problem with my system.Sometimes Loading textures takes a bit long, again, thats most likely a problem with my system.It captures the flair of the underhive quite good, if you like necromunda, you will recognize  lot of the terrainfeatures.The graphics are okay, quality wise. The Tutorial / Campaign, written as an "Interactive Novel / Movie" is a nice idea, with a rather medicore application.My biggest gripe, rules and mechanics wise, it has nearly nothing to do with Necromunda.Its the basic rules system, the devs designed.Short version:i can not Recomend the game in its current State because:1. The AI is Bad, as in, really really Bad, and there is no dificulty slider.2. Crashes, "only" 2 in 6 Hours, but they are bothersome, especialy if the game freezes entirely3. You can Save the game, but you can NOT pick an save and reload, you basicaly have ONE savefor the campaign, and one per gang in Free mode. (which brings up a few more annoying problems,see the long review)4. It is designed for consoles, which makes the controls wierd in times, you have, for example,use the Nummber Keys on your Keyboard, to manouver some menues, you can not click the desired option.Long Version:1. campaignLets start with what is good about the campaign:It is meant to tell a story, and give you a Tutorial while it is at it.The idea is nice, and i like how it is done.What is Bad about the campaign:Content is locked behind a mandatory campaign playtrought, it is "only" visual Options for your gangs,alltought i think, content should never be locked behind a Tutorial, especialy not if it is basic content.I would like the Idea, if yoou could unlock special skins for your Gang by, for example, doing all missionswith all optional objectives.The Campaign as a Tutorial is not that good, basicaly, a lot of the Tutorial, is just a Text window, in the upper right ofthe Screen, so you have to read trought it, to even know what they want from you.This is not a problem in itself, but the tutorials change, without notification.Personally i missed some tutorial texts, because i went about the mission, and did something the tutorial wanted me to doby accident. That way you easily miss important information, hidden in that Wall of text.Could have been done way better.The Campaign has one, and ONLY one Save, which brings in the Following problem(s):You can save at any time, but if you, for example, save just before something happens, which makes you loosethe mission, you can only reset the entire Mission.If you stop playing mid mission, and you save the game, to continue later, or if it crashes on you,and you load into the Mission again, you are FORCED to sit trought the whole Intro Video for the mission again.So, if you lose a mission, the game crashes, or you have to take a break, tough luck, here is the Video, again.!System spec related Note:On my underwhelming System, the videos tend to stutter, which makes watching the videos over and over againeven more annoying, but that is clearly hardware related.Crashes:Missions tend to crash, or freeze, if you (seemingly) progress to fast. One Example:In Mission 2, if you kill the last enemy, and escape right after, the game gets stuck in an infinite loading screen.I had to kill the game, and re load the mission (3 turns earlier, watching the video again).You have to wait one turn, after you take the last enemy out, then reinforcements for the enemys arrive,you have to wait till the reinforcements are there. Which is a bit annoying, especially because the gamedoes not tell you "Hey, not so fast please, i want to explain reinforcements to you"General and Free play mode:The problems here tend to play a bit into campaign mode, but they are worse outside of the Tutorial, so i mention themhere.1. The AI, it is really really bad. As in absolutely bad.Yes, sometimes the AI does have its bright momments, like, taking a control point, sabotaging the acess to the point.so you have to take a long tour to get there, very smart.But then, the AI is really unfocused, sometimes it does start right next to your fighter.Runs away, across the whole map, doing an circle, back to your fighter, to attack the very guy, it did start next to.I had a Game, where the AI had the mission objectves, went for the map exit, stoped ONE step in front of the exit.Jumped of the plattform, instead of just winning, cowered down in a corner, so i could take the fighter out, grab the items,and win 3 turns later.On other ocassions, the AI takes out grenades, and bombs its own fighters into oblivion.No enemy arround, it just throws the grenade into a group of its own fighters, then runs off, and spams some buffs.The AI and fighter gear.For some reason, the AI is not able to work with weapons inside the Backpack of Fighters.you can just block off enemy ranged Gangers with one or two of your fighters, and the AI ganger will just step forward andback all the time, untill the AI lets him duck and ends its turn.If you loot an enemy ganger clear, and fight against the same gang again later, chances are good, the looted fighters,will not have any Gear, because the AI doesnt really re stock its guys (it does buy new Gear, puts it into the backpack,then never uses it).Mechanical Problems:Ok, lets get to the Mechanical problems, those should NOT be here (a Bad AI, ok, its not like the preceding game Mordheim, was known for its Solid AI)First:Sometimes Dead Gangers (especially after re loading a game in progress) are Stuck in the T Pose, standing there,no way to interact with them.But to be fair, that problem happens to a lot of Devs, Total war Warhammer had some Agents Stuck on their horsesin T Pose recently, so it happens, it just needs to be fixed asap.The Movement Point system.This one is really Bad.So, each Fighter has a certain ammount of Movement points, to run arround.The Map is 3D, so it goes over multiple levels.If you use Stairs, which go back and forth (like first stair goes north, second one south)you use x points to move up stair 1 towards the maps North, then you get your Movement points REFUNDEDfor moving up the stair towards the maps South, because the system seems to think, you just move back to where you came from. Meaning, Moving up between levels is basicaly free.Translation:The German version of the game is cringworthy as far as the translation goes.Skill names make no sense, in the german version, if you lose a Mission, the game tells you"Besieger" which is a nonsense word.The Sub titles do not Fit the language used on the videos in most cases.But given that you can not turn sub titles off, it gets annoying, if you try to listen to the originaltext, and get those wierd and often entirely off, translations on the screen.The UI and the Controls in general:As allready stated, the UI and the Controls are clearly designed for console.This leads to some wierd (most likely) oversights.All options are locked to specific nummerical keys, fo you press 1 to attack, then 1 to attack, 2 for overwatch,3 for grenades, and so one.In some Menues, you can use the mouse to naigate.In others you cant.This can get annoying in some situations, like:Move to an downed enemy.Press F to interact.Press 1 for loot.Select the stuff in his backpack with your mouse.Press F to transfer it over to you fighter.Use the mouse to decide how many items to take (if it is a stack of items)Klick the next item to take, or press 3 to leave the loot menue.Could have been solved better.

_childDocuments_.review: great fun tactics style game; if you're a fan of XCOM series you will enjoy the individual unity customization and lasting effects from falling in battle such as lasting wounds negatively effecting certain stats or actions up to and including suffering from shell shock. plenty of different objectives and a lot of 1v1v1 style fights that add an interesting and fun mechanic of deciding whether to initiate combat or hang back and try and pick off survivors; either way you like to play, there are plenty of different melee and ranged weapons from cryo guns and chainswords up to massive hammers and giant heavy plasma guns or regular old fasioned assault rifles. lastly the different "class options" for individual unit arctypes are useful to keep balancew in a squad as there are fun mechanics and abilities unique to each of the 5 aside from what weapons each have access to, you will surely find use of a deadeye's grapple hook ability to quickly ascend floors to gain height and distance advantages over melee tanks or close range specialists who will be left having to retreat or find alternate ways to close the gap; other class unique abilities include the heavy weapons' specialist utilizing wide constant auras that buff party members toughness or accuracy or perhaps the ley-mechanics servo arm options and ability to build cover, health tanks and more. all of this and that's not even touching on multiplayer which is a riot with teams or free for all style matches.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR Recommended, barely, if a fan of Necromunda or 40k universe Game looks damn good, at least the environment, animations are ok a little wooden but decent enough. Level design is pretty solid, plenty of options. The AI is very hit or miss, often miss and can make the missions really drag out, an operation will take 30-60min depending on how many players there are. The choices it will make, while often beneficial to the player are hilariously bad sometimes, especially if there are loot crates around. Game did ok blending the tabletop with a video game, some weird choices but overall I think they work. Mordheim was also sorta terrible when it launched and was really a damn solid game once they got to fix it; hoping that is the case with this one as Necromunda is a really fun, interesting setting within 40k.  It's rough, by far a perfect game and feels like it really could have used some more polish but who knows what happened behind the scenes. _childDocuments_.review: When I was a kid, I remember seeing Necromunda the miniature based game on shelves... and boy did I want to play it.  But like most games workshop games, the tabletop has a steep investment before joining and by the time I was able to afford to get started the game was all but almost forgotten by GW (what else is new?).  While there were some minor resurgences, nothing would ever generate that buzz.I instead played Mordheim, and Bloodbowl with some locals - and it was fun.Fast forward, I own the PC games of each intellectual property and while I have frustrations with each one, I enjoy them. While I wish I could see more expansion of this game that will likely never happen, it's still a fun romp despite taking some time to get used to the mechanics translated into a 3rd person tactical game.  The storyline is weird as you keep bouncing between three factions that all want eachother dead, but makes for a decent narrative from the perspective of a shady dealer trying to get his hands on something ancient and powerful.

I'd played 40K with friends, but Necromunda was . One long summer 4 of us played a long campaign...I don't collect the miniatures any more. But I do play the video games (they're better at painting than I ever was...)I've enjoyed Total War Warhammer, and Battlefleet Gothic Armada, and Sanctus Reach, because they  like the tabletop games I remember playing. I liked the first Dawn of War, but I'm not so keen on the more recent ones. As games, they're fine. But they just don't feel right.So when I saw this game announced, I was excited.When I saw it delayed, I was nervous.And...It's good!I tried out the first two story missions, which are a sort of tutorial on the basics of gameplay. It looks good. It sounds good. And best of all, it  like Necromunda. Dark, gloomy, industrial environments. Cover, doors, walkways, structures. It's all good so far.A few ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ with the controls - mouse inversion doesn't seem to stick properly. But a nice surprise: full native support for the Xbox controller too!I'll check back once I've played some more, but so far I'm very happy.----------------UPDATEI've now finished the single player campaign. The story over 15 missions serves to teach you about all the different game types: ambushes, objective take/hold/grabs, firefights, etc.I really like this game. I've found myself becoming attached to some of the characters.Now I've created my own gang and I've started playing the main game. Let's see what happens!I've had a couple of crashes, and some glitches, but nothing serious. I'm sure the devs will get those sorted out.I understand the complaints people have about the AI - but I don't agree with them. People ask "Why did the enemy just walk past my ganger and ignore him?"To answer this, let's talk about chess. Chess is a game of "perfect information" - i.e. both players can see the whole board, and know every move their opponent can make. Necromunda on the tabletop is also a game of perfect information, and with Underhive Wars they have gone the same way. So when the AI decides to run past your guy, it's because it's figured out a better move than just taking the first pawn it sees.Or at least, it should be. Maybe the AI is dumb sometimes... but when it doesn't just blindly attack the first enemy it can see, that's not necessarily a bug.Not every video game has to faithfully replicate the tabletop game it is based on. But check out the reviews for the various Space Hulk games to see how that can turn out...Another common criticism is the time spent watching the enemy when it's not your turn.In a large game with lots of fighters, it is a bit stop/start waiting for your turn. I'm not really sure what they can do about that. Maybe a skip button that simply simulates the other fighter's move and then updates the environment with the results? I don't know.I'm kinda OK with playing a bit, then watching the enemy. But I understand it might not be for everyone. SPOILER ALERT: if you play Necromunda on the table top, sometimes it is the other person's turn!! ;)On the whole, I am enjoying playing this game and I'm glad I bought it.

_childDocuments_.review: OK... so I don't genuinely review games because opinion is often so divided on what one individual will enjoy and another will despise. Yet I felt compelled to say a few things about this game, so will jot them down here to be read or discarded at leisure.Firstly I would like to say that in terms of whether I am giving the game a thumbs up, the answer is yes. As you will probably have seen through other reviews the game currently has some flaws. Many minor, some major - I will get to those shortly. Outside of the bugs, however, if you're a fan of the whole Games Workshop 40k vibe and enjoy strategy games... then I would say that it's a must have. Yes it has issues, but I believe these will be addressed, in time. Unfortunately it suffers from what has become something of an "epidemic" amongst modern computer games... where the people holding the purse strings determine release schedules and not the developers. I have worked in the industry for 20 years, so I do know a little of what I'm talking about. When the devs say they need three years and the company tells them they have 18 months... you know you're in for trouble from the outset. Games will release buggy and the additional development time will emerge as patches and DLC. It's shortsightedness. Financial losses through poor reviews could easily be avoided by a few more months of careful bug fixing. But I'm wandering off point. I shall start with a few negatives, as I would prefer to finish this mini review on a positive note.1. As mentioned elsewhere the AI is... <sigh> ...at times it beggars belief. As one example I saw an enemy gang member run to an edge, drop 7 levels on their wire, move to an elevator and use it to go back to the ledge they just jumped off. And what did they do when they got to the top? They jumped off again. <insert face palm> I can only assume that whatever logic governs their movement is affected by a limited, local situational awareness. So when this unit reached the bottom it's plan changed. Yet it immediately began it again once it reached the top. This is odd because there is no fog of war... everything is visible. So planning a move before you make it (player or AI) shouldn't require second thought part way through. Some reviewers suggested that there should be a concept of fog of war, but I for one disagree. It's designed to be fast paced and you'd end up creeping about for fear of being ambushed/shot.2. The tutorial is... not great. I could use choicer words. I abandoned it after the first mission and dived straight in to learn it on the fly. Initially there's a lot to get your head round and it can seem overwhelming, especially the separate Action Point/Movement Point system. But I recommend this over the actual tutorial. If you are unsure about something, check YouTube would be my advice and avoid the in game story mode.3. AI character path-finding is woeful at times. I had to abandon a mission after collecting every item I was after and killing all enemy gang members but one. The last one, during its turn, ran straight into a barrel and just carried running on the spot. Unable to spend its movement points, yet determined to reach a place on the map that required it to run through that spot. It had no concept of the barrel being there and that was that. I left it running, made some food and came back fifteen minutes later to find it still there, running on the spot. I quit the game, restarted and it picks up where you left off... the AI character did exactly the same thing. No way out. So the only choice I had was to Forfeit mission and accept defeat... after killing 9 form 10 of the enemy and securing all the objectives, without losing a single one of my own. "Defeat." Bullsh#t. Why is there not some code in place that after 30 seconds or so kicks in... Something's wrong here, end the AI character's turn. Solved, boom. So simple, but to omit it is just sloppy. Sorry devs, if any are reading... I am a dev and this is an easy solution to a game-breaking bug.4. Woah-WTF! OK... so not a bug, but a mind-bender. Once you learn how to manipulate your movement and action points, you can achieve so much in a single turn that it is borderline nonsense. And before YOU ever understand how to do it, the AI will give you a short, sharp lesson on it. Forget using cover. The AI don't fight from distance as a rule. If you kneel behind a barricade, you can guarantee that an AI character will run half the length of the map to expose you, just to take the shot. It's why I'm not a huge fan of the movement and action points being separate. Movement SHOULD inhibit action and vice versa. It doesn't. 5. Camera quake. Some games cut through the terrain if the camera moves into an odd position, showing the inside of the environment models. While that is never desirable, I prefer if to the whole... screen vibrating so intensely that I may vomit if I don't tear my eyes away right this instant approach that Necromunda seems to embrace.6. Player bases! Yes I know that in the board game the figures have bases... without them they would have trouble standing. But in the computer version? Each character has a green "base" beneath them that is perhaps a metre across. And these define the width of the gang members. So if you finish a character's movement in a narrow corridor and haven't left space for the green base of the next gang member to fit through... you've created a blockade. Even if the actual character model fits easily... if the green disc doesn't, then you're screwed. This has ruined several turns for me when I realise that I have effectively walled my other guys/gals in because the first one stood too central in a corridor. This is very poor. I have also seen an AI character spawn inside a team mate's base. The first member spawned, carried out some actions and then knelt down where the next member was due to spawn. Once it did... the two became conjoined and neither were able to move again, but simply ran on the spot. Instead of trying to reach some place they couldn't, however, they just chose to expend their entire turns with buffs and overwatch. I simply ignored them as they were no longer a threat. Devs... come on. If the spawn area isn't clear... spawn within the bounds of the environment somewhere close. 7. Biggest bug to date and I still have no understanding of how/why it happened. It's a mission where your gang members come in one per turn. I spawn my heavy weapon guy in and place him on overwatch. As soon as I end his turn... he groans and falls over dead. No environment hazard and no enemy units even on the map at this point. What happened? No idea. So I click Forfeit on the battle. When I get back to my HQ screen... EVERY one of my gang members has lost all their weapons. Tier 5 weapons that I had slowly accumulated over time. How/why/where? Does forfeiting a match surrender your equipment? It doesn't declare it. And these gang members had never even reached the battlefield - why should they lose their weapons? I do hope that this is a bug. I can understand it MAYBE if your gang members are already deployed... as it's kind of a surrender. But for them never to have even reached the field... nah. Bullsh#t.So if anyone is still with me... why am I playing when there are so many bugs and flaws so evident in the game? Because despite everything I have mentioned above, I am actually really enjoying it. I can't even put my finger on quite what it is that I like the most about it. Character progression, team set-up, finding new weapons and equipment. And I've not seen the same battlefield twice!!! In thirty hours of gameplay I have not yet fought on the same map. So kudos to the devs for that. And I think DLC will bring other gangs to the mix. I have run out of space, so can't fit anything else in... good job for you guys still reading. But yes, despite the flaws... I give it a thumbs up. And it's only going to get better!

_childDocuments_.review: First of I play games to avoid people, so I haven't tried the multiplayer part, and probably never will, so this is only focused on Story and campaign/gang mode.What I like:1. Great game to pick up and leave if you wanna do the single missing or more2. Campaign mode is the most fun where you customize your gang and skills as you progress, and upgrade their gear (mostly by raiding the corpses of your rivals)That's kinda it.What I hate:1. The story mode is messy and boring. They made it into one long tutorial, and I actually stopped playing it to try out the gang side of the game. I came back to it only to unlock features in customization for my gang that's locked behind the story mode.So, playing the story mode I remembered why I hate it. They use a turn-based system where you have x numbers of turns before you fail a mission. That's fine when it comes to building tension, but they don't tell you WHEN and how long that timer actually is. Just failed a mission where all of my team was in the endzone, but I lost because the timer ran out before the scripted event opened the [curse word] door!Since I don't do multiplayer story is really important, but gameplay can save a bad story which brings me to.2. The gameplay is boring and super buggy.All games have repetition, but with this game, you really feel it. _childDocuments_.review: I run the local Necromunda Dark Uprising campaign at my LGS and the tabletop has been my central go-to for board gaming a few years on now. _childDocuments_.review: Updated review:A few more hours in and... yeah, sorry, but I can't recommend this game as it currently stands. The more time I've put into it, the more bugs have risen to the fore, the more game play issues have tarnished the enjoyment (AI is really, REALLY poor) and the more I came to realise that if this game wasn't in a setting I have a lot of nostalgia for, I would have probably refunded it. As seems to be the case FAR too often these days, they've released the game before it's finished. It doesn't just lack polish, it lacks the feeling of being complete in some of the core mechanics.If you're not a Warhammer fan, don't bother. Yet. Original Review:So it's... ok.It's pretty much the same game as their previous warhammer venture, mordheim, only so far without as much flavour or personality...That said, I'm yet to run into a bug, whereas Mordheim had some pretty gamebreaking ones right out of the gate.There are definitely some areas that need to be addressed though, including, most worryingly, one of the core game mechanics in movement only being measured laterally, not vertically- these multi-tier environments are great... but not when a character can essentially run infinite distance as long as they stay within their 'pillar' of movement range.Seriously, how this mechanic survived the transition over from mordheim, where it was far less of an issue due to the less vertical terrain layout, I have no idea.Pros: - runs smooth- good cut scenes so far in story mode- yet to find a true bug- new mechanics like tactical view, etc, definitely make the game more accessible... but at the same time I kinda miss not knowing what's waiting around the corner!Cons:- so far at least, gangers all seem pretty homogenous - when everyone has 60AP no one feels special like they did in mordheim- movement needs a rethink- being 'teleported for ending your turn in an unsafe area' is immersion breaking- controls feel unintuitive at times - disappointing to only see 3 gangs... I hope they don't rinse us too badly for the inevitable DLCs.I'd be disappointed if I was paying AAA prices, but I'm hopeful the rest of the game keeps my interest- hopefully it doesn't fizzle out entirely once the story mode is done?6/10 - playable, enjoyable, but not loveable... hoping for more from it as I delve deeper into the underhive.

_childDocuments_.review: So you know where I'm coming from, I enjoyed Mordheim and hoped for more of the same or improvements in some areas.  I didn't expect or want a tabletop recreation of the game.  I wasn't expecting to be blown away or for it to be more than a reskin or slight evolution of Mordheim.  With these fairly moderate expectations even I was surprised by just how disappointing the game is in its current state.The good:- Atmospheric graphics and setting- Customisation options are an improvement though not quite as extensive as the developer videos suggested- Nice to have multiple gangs in play (but see turn time comment below)The bad:- AI is awful- No seriously the AI is a joke - think of the worst AI you've seen in a game and double it- The turns are tediously slow  - the more gangs there are the longer and more drawn out the game is.  Sounds exciting 4 gangs fighting each other - it should be, but you'll spend more time on the internet or watching youtube then playing the game due to the turn speeds.- The AI animations constantly show them doing dull chain buffs one after the other (why do I need to see an animation for this!!)- Loads of cover, levels etc yet we can all see where each other is at all times so there's no fog of war, and therefore no ability to pull off or be surprised by AI in overwatch or ambush mode like in Mordheim.  - Don't buy this if you want any form of challenging single player play.  It's a cakewalk from the first mission and it doesn't get harder.- Can't I have an option to reserve points for crouching so this automatically happens at the end of the characters turn unless I turn it off- The skill options just confused the hell out of me I accept it's personal preference but I never got confused or overwhelmed with the mordheim skill selection but I do here- Perhaps this game is good in multiplayer but it crashes to desktop during most of the multiplayer games I've attempted so I've simply stopped trying.Without significant patching this is a lost cause, which is a real pity as I've been a fan of Necromunda for years.  It feels like an early access game, it plays like an early access game except it's not they're charging full price and this is allegedly a fully finished game.  The latest update from the Company alluded to there being feedback from the community regarding the AI.  Anyone who played a single game or even round would have known the AI was in an appalling state, so it's laughable this is the sum of their reaction to justified reviews and comments raising this as an issue.  Genuinely reviewers aren't overemphasising how bad the AI is.  And whilst I don't expect an AI to be amazing the AI here doesn't even put up any form of convincing challenge or enjoyable game.  This is Necromunda, these are hardened gangers and fights should be brutal and desperate.  Except they're not.  Most games the enemy might shoot or attack me in melee 3 to 5 times in an entire 90-120 minute game, the rest of which they run round like lemmings picking up objective crates whilst I calmly and easily pick them off.  Every game plays like this.  There have been a few times when they've surrounded one or two of my gangers and I thought oh no this is tense to immediately see their 5  guys in turn run away from my 2 cut off, wounded and cornered gangers to pick up crates.Mordheim was a flawed gem in my opinion and it's quite telling after a largely unenjoyable almost 10 hours of playing Necromunda that I reinstalled Mordheim and had a significantly more enjoyable, quick and challenging experience.  Mordheim is a significantly better game than this (except graphically).   If you didn't like Mordheim I can't see you liking this.  If you liked Mordheim you'll likely be disappointed with the challenge and speed of this game.  If you're a die hard Necromunda fan, maybe, but only if you enjoy zero challenge with AI or are prepared to put up with unstable multiplayer.

_childDocuments_.review: So I'll try to make this quick as can be. The game is Xcom-like, and it is fun, but is is held back by several quality of life issues that the devs should take the inititive to take care of. These things are not the worst things imaginable, but when put together, they grate and make the game not fun. No skipping! Only the cutscenes are skippable, and for some reason, you can't skip them straight off. I watch all the cutscenes in games, but I hate watching most more than once, and this is just annoying. BUT not half as annoying as having to watch the AI player take each individual turn with no skipping. Come on guys, its not hard to know you should put that in, play your own game for a few hours and you will see how annoying this is. In addition, the logos when you start the game are not skippable either. This just leads to a lot of small waiting. Wait here, wait there. Thats not fun, make the game more fun, make more of this stuff skippable. Its small, but it grates after hours. AI. The AI is a little silly, this will probably get better, but it runs around funny and makes its easy to kill randomly. Not such a big deal for me, but its a thing. The Story. Look, I came into this game to make my own gang. To customize them, and field them, and give them names and what not. I did not PURCHASE this game to play premade gangs that I cannot customize. I do not care about Tessra. I do not care about Blutvor. I. Want. To. Play. The. Game. I am 6 hours in and I am still playing this limp story mode, and I JUST DO NOT EFFING CARE! PLEASE do not gate the ability to customize my gang and play the main game behind this time consuming trudge of a story. I cannot stress how much I DO NOT want to play these levels, they are not fun for me because they are not the reason I purchased the game. I understand wanting the players to know how to play before releasing them into the game, but, again, I am 6 hours in. I am about to drop this game that I really want to play because I cannot fully customize my gang until after I have finished a story mode that is completely seperate from, to me, what the core features of the game are. There is nothing more frustrating than wishing heart and soul that the story will just end so that I can ACTUALLY HAVE FUN. Look, locking special customization items behind levels and achievements and such, I understand. Locking the ability to customize your characters head behind the ENTIRE campaign is madness. If this is not fixed very very soon, the game devs WILL see playtime for the game drop like a rock. I have been far more patient with this game because I LOVE warhammer. But this should not depend on my fan love of the series to lube their gameplay. This story thing is a big effing problem, its making me not want to play a game I purchased. Thats not Good, please think better of game design. There is no point in forcing the entire story down the throats of the players when it is SO lack luster and basic. I would be more than willing to change my review if these things were addressed, but until then, the game is a trudge, and it does not have to be. All the pieces are there, but I guess the polish isn't finished.

_childDocuments_.review: Necromunda: Underhive Wars is a turn-based strategy game in third person. Unlike in TBS games like XCOM, your point of view is mostly from a third-person perspective, which makes it feel like a hybrid between TBS and third-person shooter. People who played Mordheim will exactly know what it feels like. In fact, this game is made by the same devs as Mordheim but is it actually as good as Mordheim?As a person who played a few Warhammer games and never really got into these (story-wise), I don't understand most of the story. Maybe it's also the fact I just don't care much about it. Several gangs are fighting over the supremacy in the underhives.. or over scrap metal. I can't tell. Well, in the beginning, your searching for the rest of your gang. As you find them and your leader, another gang attacks and you'll need to defend yourself and escape from them. People who are into this Universe will know it better anyways, everyone else will get as much as I probably. As an upside, the story is told through actual cut-scenes which is a big plus because they are high quality and nice to watch. The visuals are beautiful, the voice-over is good and this makes the overall experience nice enough to enjoy the story throughout the 15 campaign missions, even if you don't get much out of it.You can select one of three gangs (or two more if you buy the DLC's) to build up your gang, go for scrap and get supremacy over the underhives. There is a shop, operations, online skirmish, you can recruit new members, level them up, customize them, and all these things you want to see in a game like this. Most people will want to play this, though the game tells you to first complete the story to fully get everything the game has to offer.The first story mission is basically the tutorial. It will teach you the basics. After that, new text boxes will pop up every time something new is available, you discover a new menu or anything like that. It's a good and easy tutorial especially compared to Mordheim IMO. I was a bit overwhelmed in Mordheim because I felt like I'm reading a book. In Necromunda, they made it way smoother. This is the heart of the game. This is what matters. The rest can be as good as ever, but if the fights suck, the game sucks. Let's cut to the chase. The turn-based battles are a joke. This is absolutely a joke of a game. Not because there aren't enough weapons, classes, tactics, or anything like that - but because the AI is a joke. The very first enemy I met ran into a wall and ended his turn. I thought this might be a bug and "Well, it's just the first mission" but no. This sums up the whole game. Even if the AI has a good day and will TRY to battle you, it's not hard. They will run 10 meters, shoot one time, run back. There is no strategy involved. It's like playing against your 3-year-old brother - most of the time he doesn't know what he does but sometimes he gets a lucky shot. This is especially sad because the game offers a lot in battles. Thanks to the third-person view, it feels different than most TBS games. There is also a tactical map to view all levels of the map, objectives, enemies, etc.. this lets you plan the whole mission or even just your next move or turn on a high tactical level but you don't ever need it when you're not playing online. Speaking of which, the online mode is basically dead. Peak players within 24 hours are around 70 and the game was on a steep sale like a week ago. Necromunda: Underhive Wars has a lot of potentials. Many things are very well done and could lead to a fun and tactical experience most strategy fans would pay a lot of money for but it doesn't. The AI is so bad, it's not fun in the slightest. I paid 11,99€ on sale for this and I regret it. If you're like me and don't enjoy playing TBS games online against others, don't buy it, delete it from your wishlist or wait for an even higher sale. If you like to play online - make sure to get a friend to join you because the multiplayer is as good as dead.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm only recommending this game in hopes that the devs will solve the issues I mention down below.This list is mostly glaring issues and cons/bad stuff i have noticed so far in the game.Quick Comparisons with Mordheim: City Of The Damned---FRIENDLY MOVEMENT/ACROBATIC LOCATIONS--- Your troops cannot move through/pass eachother within a certain range (about 1 meter). Everyone has a green "Engagement" bubble, similar to the previous title, but allies cannot move through it, even if your ally isn't engaged or in danger. This will basically prevent you from passing eachother in tight corridors and (somewhat) narrow bridges or walkways. If you have not played the game yet, you won't know the feeling of frustration.Also, Ziplines are used for travel, and you can also jump from most perches. In mordheim, there were designated locations where you can do this. In Necromunda, there isn't, unless its a fixed zipline location. The reason why i mention this is because you can't "tactically" block the locations with your body like you could in Mordheim for those of you that remember. If you attempt to end your turn in said locations, it is deemed as a safe/unsafe zone and the game will forcibly move/teleport your character a short distance away from that spot. This can ♥♥♥♥ you if you aren't careful.---TURN ORDER--- Turn order isnt entirely based on Initiative anymore like Mordheim. There are multiple "TURNS" within 1 "ROUND" of combat. Every player uses their first "TURN" to select 1 character in their gang that hasnt moved yet. The characters selected have their Initiative compared to eachother, and can move based on who has the highest initiative going down to the lowest initiative.In other words, you can select your first dude (on turn 1) with a low-ass Initiative of "38" , and match them to everyone else's characters for that "TURN", but still act first before all of your opponents "high initiative" characters if he/she has yet to select them. That low initiative character you picked will move last in the current "TURN" compared to everyone else's quick fighters, but is still technically acting before every other High Initiative character. This system is stupid to meOnce all of those selected characters have finished their actions, that "TURN" ends, and every player selects another one of their inactive/unused characters and compares the Initiative again. You repeat the process until all characters have moved (unless a turn is skipped). After all characters have been used, a new "ROUND" begins.---SPAWN SELECTION/IMMUNITY--- So, unlike Mordheim, you can see where the opponent is spawning at, including looking up what their character's class is and other various stats and information. They are not hidden from you based on Line Of Sight. Essentially, the there is no Fog of War when selecting spawn locations, and no fog of war throughout the entire battle. By pressing "CTRL", you can activate your scanner and see everyone and just about everything through objects. This kinda sucks in my opinion, since not knowing where your enemies are is the best part and makes the game THAT much harder. In a skirmish (pvp), id assume that this makes overwatch and ambushing alot less effective.When all players select their spawn locations for each of their characters, they are given the option to select one character as i have mentioned before. What i didnt know (and correct me on this if im wrong) is that every other character that hasnt been used yet is shaded in a light gray/grey color. Everyone with that color cannot be targeted by any attacks, but you can still place traps in front of them, go into an ambush stance right before them, or set up overwatch with ranged weapons if need be.---STRESS--- I still don't know what stress does, and im not sure if the campaign teaches that to people since I've yet to start it. But as far as i can tell, stress doesn't affect you as hard as "Morale" did back in Mordheim. You won't be seeing anyone running from fear any time soon, or breaking as far as i can tell. Although, the AI is usually smart enough to retreat and exit the battleground you are in so they can preserve their troops.---INVENTORY---Everyone (as far as i can tell), including every class, starts off carrying up to 7 items in their bags. I personally wish this wasn't so, and that they reduced the amount and/or made it similar to Mordheim's inventory system, where your Strength determined your carry capacity. I have killed a few enemies with carry capacities up to 11, but im not sure if that was level related or a special perk they got.---AI & THE ♥♥♥♥ THEY DO---Im sure you saw it in other reviews while you were browsing through, but the AI in this game are literally retarded. I've been in 3 way battles where one opponent (AI) runs over to a near death character belonging to another opponent (AI), and simply kneeling a few meters away from them instead of finishing them off. They even had a full magazine and Action Points to do it. Ugh...They walk into edges or corners every now and then. They seem confused af on where they actually want to go. Ive seen bots run in one direction, stop, then turn back around just to use an item. Im not trying to delve into the science behind how they act, but lemme make this easy for you... The AI in Mordheim, on an easy mission, could completely and utterly wreck a decently equipped gang controlled by the AI in Necromunda!---THE STORE--- ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ is this store barren as ♥♥♥♥. Its dryer than an african's ashy feet in the desert while he's wearing sandpaper sandals. As mentioned by others, the Store can only be opened after completing your first two missions. Once opened, i was loving how i can finally access and purchase various pieces of weaponry and equipment. So they first time used the shop was great!2-3 missions later, im stocked full of money i made from selling looted gear from my dead foes, and the store has finally replenished and rerolled its contents... And man was i pissed. Hardly anything changed, besides a few weapons here and there and the same bunch of Left Leg Shin Guard armor. But then i was like...ok ok. Thats cool! I got a bad roll for items. Ill wait for the next one....Then the next one....Then another next one...Then the other another next one.I dunno man. Mordheim's store inventory is freaking loaded with crap. Weapons, armor, gear, consumables, enchantments OH MY!!! Then you got Necromunda...oof.---WEAPONS---Who was responsible for balancing the weapons in this game? Im actually frustrated a bit, and lemme tell you why...... so come closer dammit!There is a class called Deadeye. Your friendly neighborhood Sniper/Ranger. Your Gang Leader can pick the Deadeye as its class...ok cool. No problem so far. Then i noticed that new deadeye gangers typically start off with a weapon called the Autogun, which im sure most of you know or at least heard of. Why does this typical weapon have such a high amount of Dps compared to other guns? Why is this damn basic-♥♥♥♥♥ weapon so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ effective at murkin people left and right?So my Deadeye Gang Leader got a special ability (that only leaders can obtain) i selected called "Heroic Barrage". And holy hell, lemme tell you about this broken ass ability...With an Autogun, I can activate this ability once per turn, and fire 3  bursts at a single target. Add some crit buffs, and you can guarantee 1 kill per round in the early-mid game!---UNFINISHED CONCLUSION---I wanna tell you more, but Steam is limiting my ability to inform (although im not even efficiently doing it) y'all. Anyway, I can't rail on it too hard. Its still a brand new game, though the price we are paying for it certainly doesnt make me feel like im playing a decently complete game here. More like an Early Access Indie if anything. Its a shame too! i was looking forward to all the new game announcements like Total War Warhammer 3, Blood Bowl 3, and this.

_childDocuments_.review: It has the exact same problem Xcom 2 had at launch where the game just hangs on enemy turns for anywhere from 5-30 seconds. This is frustrating. Other than that it's a pretty well made 40k game. It has in-engine cutscenes for each mission. The voice acting is ok, not great, not the worst. Enemies do not take that long to kill, you won't ever kill them on your first round of attacks, that's true, but most get killed on the second. Really my biggest gripe with the gameplay is that I have yet to see any AI enemy swap to melee. They carry melee weapons, you can see them in their backpack after they're dead, but they will always either dig in or run away and shoot at you if you engage them in melee. But really if you liked Mordheim you'll like this.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDr; It's currently buggy but fun.Let's get the elephant out of the room right off the bat, the launch was beyond rough. I, like most, do not condone games being rushed out for a quick buck. There have been reports of debilitating bugs, corrupted saves, and borked AI. But the issues have been reported and Focus has posted that they're working on a fix. I have been lucky enough to barely experience the worst of the bugs; a few crashes, and infamy rewards not activating. So now that's out of the way, is it fun? Oh, hell yeah.Is the campaign worth it on its own? I enjoyed it, but it is honestly just a prolonged tutorial. Which isn't necessarily a bad thing, imo. Minor cosmetics are locked behind completing the 15 mission campaign, and if that worries you, you aren't missing much. Just a few gang specific customisations and a couple gas masks, nothing special honestly.How is PvP? Infinitely more enjoyable than PvE, but with the litany of bugs some have found it unplayable. Though, a portion of players have had no issues with it.Overall its a great game that has also disappointed a large number of people. Once the kinks get hammered out the salt should wash away.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to start this with saying I've played the table top version of Necromunda since it's original release back in '95. I made custom scenery, scenarios, fan fiction and even bought the huge hardcover rule book because my copy that came with the game was starting to look worse for wear. Take that to mean whatever you will but I have some experience with it to say the least. Now that we've put that out there, is this the perfect adaptation of that game? Nope. So why am I recommending it? Because it's Necromunda with what feels like a set of house rules designed to make it playable on pc. I put off buying this due to all the negativity and finally gave in during the sale and bought it. I'm glad I did. It takes me back to the countless hours sitting huddled over the Underhive planning line of site setups, plotting which direction to hit and run from, hoping that die roll wont bring a grenade exploding in my juve's face. Zip lines, jumping down, ascension, health dispensers, sabotaging the battlefield with taking out walkways are all new to pc. They are almost needed for a more fluid experience or you would be unable to get to levels from lower or higher levels. I've read review complaints about how far one can run in the play area which, again, is due to this being a pc game. Movement on the table top version was very limited (four to five inches most often). Imagine trying to play a game on these large levels and only being able to move 8 or so steps. It would take forever for your units to get any where close to the enemy. Another complaint I noticed was grouping up on single units and taking them out. That has always been a viable and popular tactic and for good reason. If you're willing to take a unit off by itself you make it a target. This isn't exclusive to the game's AI, it happen's on the table top as well. The idea is to use your cover and make sure you have someone covering your unit from someplace else. The Underhive is full of gangs for a reason, going it alone won't keep you alive long. Ai is...interesting. It does some things that make me scratch my head BUT thinking about this I've come to the conclusion that anyone I've ever played against at the table has done something strange that made no sense to anyone but them no matter how good they were at the game. It's human nature so watching a ganger use a flamer to try to take out an enemy and fry his own unit instead just brings back those "just why did you do that" moments. It's not perfect but it IS a good pc version of a game I've loved for many many years. It's nice being able to start it up and bash out a game when there's no one around to play over the table with. It scratches the itch nicely.

The AI is absolutely dogfood insane; the story mode does absolutely nothing to explain the mechanics, skills, stats (despite insisting you should play story mode to learn these things); and the game modes all boil down to variations on "just kill everything in sight and complete the objectives when they're dead".Things I like? You move her into cover and out of eyeline. Enemy above you moves heavy weapon to edge of platform negating your cover, shoots down on you, then backs away from the edge of the platform so cannot be shot.  On top of this basic failing the AI sees enemies running around in circles, running into walls and activating talents almost at random.Definitely skip this game unless you're desperate to own all the 40K stuff, then wait until it drops to under a tenner at least.

_childDocuments_.review: Necromunda has great potential and is certainly a challenge. Sadly for all the wrong reasons. If your interested here's my pros's and cons.Pros--Artwork and characters look visually great.-combat system has good potential as does the leveling skill trees.-Characters injuries and traits etc is very close to the original. Accountability and consequences always satisfying in these sorts of endeavours.-with work could be amazing.Cons.-The enemy computer players are clueless. For a strategy game its useful to have an opponent who makes decent and dangerous moves. The enemy gangs are not peers they are prey. Haplessly running off to grab boxes or into walls. no unit cohesion nor strategy._The buffs silly activation sequence. seeing someone roar for 6 seconds on overwatch or whatever time after time gets wearing. All it requires is the word to come up and if its an aura then a non flashing circle. too many unecessary drags between action.-The turn order jumps and pauses.Its seemingly your fighters turn,then it jumps to whoever has the higher initiative. And at the end (you get a turn looting at end of every engagement) it still jumps, even when all enemies are dead or fled. Stop.Blur.wait.blur.stop.Start. Really jagged,clunky delivery. Feels like original Knights of the Old Republic, not a game from 2020. This, plus the time it takes for enemies to make decisions leads to this ragged,non rhythmical, janky experience. As I said before this game is a challenge but its the bad elements of it all coming together to create an experience where one feels they must prevail against them, rather than playing a virtual version of Necromunda.-the same missions in operation. over and over.-As mentioned before the two things that kill this experience is no strategy and no rhythm. Only as a 40k fan could I put up with all these flaws for as long as I did. very unlikely newcomers will enjoy this, which is a shame as it has a lot of potential.

_childDocuments_.review: Im still not through the campaign. Its so soulless and I feel like its going on forever.Whoever green-lit the idea to remove character management from the campaign mode in a Necromunda title is, frankly, completely out of touch with why anyone plays this genre of game. Was the plan to 'streamline' things and appeal to a more casual audience? If so, horrible call. Fail-city. This is a turn-based strategy game... if you remove the gang management, you're only left with turn-based fighting. With no stakes attached to that, its probably the most bland gameplay possible, given the subject matter at hand. The whole thing that drives these games is trying to balance the completion of objectives and combat with your enemies with trying to keep your squad safe so their progress isn't ruined by injury or death. Risk/reward/mitigation.  <<<that's why people play these games, not because they like waiting for three different AI teams to finish climbing 5 flights of stairs just to jump off and then duck behind a corner to pop three auras and kneel.I'm still going to keep playing it and see if the other modes redeem it at all, but damn this campaign is so bad. I went to make my own gang and it said I couldnt customize some things without finishing the campaign first, so Im making myself do it.Im tempering my expectations already though. The mechanics seem to do what they were meant to do, which is good. The weapons look good, the environments are great, the verticality is awesome and the animations are well done. Gunplay is pretty intuitive and when I shoot at someting or charge into melee everything seems to go down as expected.But damn if doing 8 actions to ultimately not kill a guy with a salvo of lascannon blasts, only to then spectate the AI taking way too much time to do practically nothing isn't a ridiculous buzzkill. I somehow doubt if waiting for two other players to do their own thing will be that much better an experience.Mordheim was phenomenal. Bigger groups, tempered with more lethality.  <<< I want less actions required for more results, multiplied by more fighters which when taking place within the framework already established here should be phenomenal.Is it too late for that? Maybe. But its not too late for you guys to patch out the recommendation that people play that godawful campaign before anything else.Hell no. Do it. Its a really bad first-impression for your product.

_childDocuments_.review: Greetings!  Today we’ll be reviewing “Necromunda: Underhive Wars” a frankly disappointing take on the miniature game.  The game is a tactical squad based game with a heavy amount of verticality.  I’ve always loved this genre and even more so the source material so why am I so disappointed?  Let’s discuss.Green Juuve:  The game starts out amazing, the campaign story is exactly what you’d expect from Necromunda and I’m even able to forgive that.  Though I continue to be annoyed at writers being forced to shift their stories to fit the game which makes the stories predictable at best, boring at worst but the game does make it clear the campaign is more of a tutorial than stand alone, so that’s done well…right?  Nope, the tutorials are just little text boxes in the corner that pop up and disappear randomly, in the ‘current year’ this really should be audio, with visuals or at least pop-ups you have to dismiss.  As best I can tell you don’t even have access to an encyclopedia of any kind of tutorials, this would have been at least okay.  Double Tap: So beyond the tutorial the campaign is great right?  Well, kind of.  The campaign has you taking control of 3 random gangs throughout the campaign and you never really get to know the gangers abilities and they feel like they are constantly changing (which they are) but most importantly you are left with a feeling of meaningless as there is no management of any kind during the campaign.  You heard me, the biggest side-attraction of any tactical game, managing your gang, is completely absent during the campaign.  I love taking a brand new fighter and turning them into a hive champion but nope, you got to wait for the ‘real game’.  But without that you have little to no attachment and you are left with a disappointing campaign that couldn’t even properly teach the mechanics.Recycled Air:  So, positives…okay, positives.  The game feels 40k through and through, from the way they talk to the graphics, everything.  It’s amazing, the guns feel right (sans the melta gun) the world looks great everything!  So yes! The bones are amazing, could be great if some of the above (and below) issues were resolved.  The verticality is amazing too, jumping down and climbing up is something only a few games have tried in this genre.  Once you are done with the campaign and start the ‘real’ game of building and leading your gang the game does improve significantly.  Most of this is faithful to the setting and miniature game but that’s the rub though, the moment you start a gang of your own a ray of light comes from the upper spires and you see what the game was meant to be.  It feels like this was created first and the campaigns ‘tutorial’ was created not to compliment it but because one was needed.  The games doesn’t explain so much that becomes easily obvious the moment you start your own gang.Cover your mouth:  I kept hearing how unbelievably awful the AI is on this game, I ignored it thinking ‘sure many games have bad AI and I enjoy them’ but I was not prepared.  The single greatest breaking point of this game is the beyond awful and completely unplayable AI.  Most matches the AI would run around jumping up and down the terrain MAYBE debuffing me or overwatching but most of their turns would hold zero effect.  The AI doesn’t even seem to be able to go after objectives.  I had one mission where one of the AI picked up an objected, so I spent a few turns watching it and it didn’t even try to extract.  The unplayable nature of the AI is what breaks this game, so much of the game's issues can be forgiven once you get into the real game (after the campaign) if only the AI functioned at a modicum of intelligence.  Oh, and a fast forward option would be amazing while the AI acts.No Servitors Allowed:  I want to take a moment to say that if you are going to be playing this with other people (or lizard men) then an overwhelming amount of issues I have with this game is null and void as the game at its core is great.  The AI is beyond terrible and I could see a lot of fun starting an operation with your friends, though I would have liked to see a bit more of a ‘campaign mode’ option that is more faithful to the table-top.  The game is in dire need of smoothing out beyond the AI but at least getting them to behave enough to down one of my gangers would be appreciated.Ultimately, I want to love this game, it has everything someone like me could want: heavy management aspects, the tactical gameplay and 40k aesthetic but the game is just drowned in a mediocre front loaded campaign that couldn’t even base itself as a decent tutorial and an incompetent AI that doesn’t even have the decency to attack every once in a while.  This game could have been vastly improved by just one person going through the campaign and smoothing out some of the tutorial non-sense.  Although, I hope for an update to fix this I just don’t see those Spire-Born fixing this anytime soon.  Enjoy!

_childDocuments_.review: Great visuals, very nice custom gang maker. The combat is fun when you get the hang of it. It plays like XCOM but with a interesting 3rd person control twist. Unlike the Mordheim game by the same dev, Necromunda is actually really easy to navigate the levels with inbuilt map viewing and objective viewing functions. The campaign is a slog and a half though with very poor voice acting and I think literally every character has a mask on in the cutscenes so that the mouths don't have to be animated. That aside, the actual voice actors often sound ill suited to represent the crazy looking 40k characters, apart from some of the Escher ladies. I wouldn't complain but some cosmetic stuff is locked behind completing the campaign so if you want to really make your gang look as awesome as it can be then you have to complete it. A ton of little bugs too, which seem to be fairly common and noticed by the community already so hopefully they get fixed. All in all, I would say it's a 5/10 right now but with some updates it could for sure be a 8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Been playing this game for about a week now. I'm through a lot of the story mode, and I've played a few missions with each of the different factions. I'll take a moment and share what is good about the game, and what needs some improvement. Pros: Maps- Love the fully 3D environment. You really have to consider elevation and how to navigate terrain. Really changes how you play. Factions- Each faction shares units of similar types, but each faction also has characters that feel different. Theme- I used to play the tabletop game with a friend of mine. This feels very thematic to what we played. Visuals- not a huge seller for me, but this game does look good. It's dark and gritty, and the characters look awesome. Terrain- somewhat covered under maps, but there are good areas to lay traps and navigate. I even like how you can sabotage pathways so others can't follow you. Story- Seen some mixed reviews on this, but I like the story so far. It's not in depth, and it's designed to get you to play each faction a bit to see what you prefer. I like that. Each faction also has their own rules and methods, so I like that too from a story perspective. Cons: AI- Lot of people are talking about this, and I get it. The AI is either really good or really bad. Many times I made a bad play, but the AI just went around me and did nothing. Doesn't always happen, but it happens every mission so far. Bugs- Only had the game crash once, but I have seen some screen bugs when enemies kneel in certain places. Abilities- This game has a pretty good learning curve to play. It took me a while to really understand what classes can do what, and to figure out what skills are useful and when. Still learning this, but it takes time. Pace- This game is a bit slow, even for a tactics game. AI plays like another player, so you have to wait each turn to see what they do. Sometimes their decisions make no sense at all. Overall, this game isn't without it's problems. Right now I'd probably rate it a 6.5 or 7 out of 10. I needs a few tweaks to really get it going, but there's enough here to keep me interested until it does. It's fun, but it needs a little work still. I hope they drop some DLC with new factions, maps or challenges.

_childDocuments_.review: After logging over 300 recorded hours (and more not logged) into Mordheim, I was really looking forward to Necromunda.  Sadly, I cannot recommend this game.  The gangs are too small and too homogeneous, the AI is either incomplete or total trash, and the usual release bugs abound.First - the gangs are boring.  We went from having 3-10 active fighters in Mordheim to 5 in Necromunda.  FIVE.  It's not a gang - it's a group of folks going to lunch.  Worse, there are five "careers," so your gang composition is pre-determined (one of each career), unless you want to roll the dice on not being able to complete a mission or objective because you don't have a Lay Mechanic or what-have-you.  Compounding this, and perhaps most damning, available equipment is limited by your career.  You're telling me I can't give an autogun (a basic rifle) to my Saboteur because only Dead Eyes can use them?  A BASIC RIFLE?  Trash.  So now every game is composed of the same careers, with the same pre-determined equipment limitations.  Aside from minor stat and skill differences, every gang is the same.  This is the opposite of "customizable."  I can't even build my tiny little fire team the way I want.  This is completely setting aside the fact that Orlocks are, for no good or logical reason, built to be Van Saar.  Not that it would make a difference, as they're all essentially the same anyway...Then there's the AI.  Let's be clear - I've literally watched allied AI stand facing each other in a corridor and refuse to move, like the north going zax and the south going zax.  I've watched allied AI *on the same team* grenade and trap each other.  I've watched allied and opposing AI literally do everything in their power to avoid harming each other, including walking right past each other unleashing warcries and using abilities but refusing to actually attack.  It's as if they literally decided to engage in a shouting match rather than fight.  Consider that there can be 20 fighters on the field, and you only have 5.  This means you spend 75% of your time watching brainless AI avoid each other, only getting to actually play 25% of the time you spend in that particular match.  Who in God's name thought this was a good idea?Finally, there are the usual release bugs.  The strategic map (which is nice when it works) will grey out, preventing you from seeing anything or planning your run.  The camera will go berserk when AI is near a corner, giving you an epileptic fit.  The game will crash to desktop from time to time, and the UI frequently either does not work or is unintuitive at absolute best.Ultimately - this feels like a game that changed direction mid-development and then was published incomplete, midway between two different visions.  It has tremendous potential, and if Mordheim is any indication it will receive continued support and will be a decent game... eventually.  Hopefully the developers will at least remove the equipment restrictions so players can meaningfully outift a gang as they wish.  It seems unlikely we will be able to field more than five gangers at this point, so it would be nice to at least be able to equip them the way we want.  As it was released, however, this game is hot garbage.  I think I will return to the City of the Damned for now; Necromunda is still under construction.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like Necromunda, you'll hate this game: - No multiplayer campaign which is the entire point of Necromunda.  I can not overstate how important this is.  GW constantly drops the ball on their games.  There are sets of GW games based around persistence and playing with friends.  Failing to put this in the game is stupid.  Across all of the GW video games that have been released, lack of campaign and multiplayer support is a pretty consistent theme and it shows that GW only wants you gathering around a table.  The video games are usually just cash grabs.  - Only THREE gangs come with the game and you can get 2 more with DLC  - Each gang can only field 5 gang members  - Within the game, very little of what you do matters.  No permadeath and rarely even any lasting injuries.  It never really feels like anything is changing or developing over time.  - I picked this up for about $8 with all of the DLC and don't think it's worth it.  Would have rather gotten tacos and a beer

AI Hilarity:  Characters still get hung up on walls and items on the ground just like Mordheim.  The AI occasionally runs all the way one way and then when you think it's out of move points it circles back to where it began.  Sometimes it runs by my characters without attacking and other times it will run by me and kneel in a corner amongst my gang.  This is basically the same game as Mordheim, you'd think these issues would be long gone.  Embarrassing that they're not.Catastrophic Design Flaws:  You're forced to watch each individual AI move up close and personal.  Like you're literally running up stairs with them and turning around corners before kneeling behind a crate.  Every.Single.Move.Every.Single.AI Turn. Not only is it punishing in terms of wait times but you know where everyone is at all times which quite literally ruins the game.  There's no suspense or wonderment around positioning, overwatch or ambushes.  On top of that, the 3D map also shows you where everybody is at all times.  Watching every AI move is obviously unacceptable and ultimately a deal breaker but knowing where every enemy is any given minute is game breaking and not in a good way.  I can't stress enough how bad these two issues are.  They need to be addressed immediately and totally.Another mind numbing flaw is that at the beginning of each of your characters turns they further slow down the already incredibly slow turn times with a graphic that comes up telling you, "It's Your Turn" or "End of Turn" for every single turn.  It's a self inflicted wound, those two time wasting pop ups don't need to be there.  Just pick your team member, play your turn and immediately end your turn and on to the next.  It's like they're trying to annoy the player.  This nonsense needs to be removed immediately, it serves zero purpose.  Other notably annoying facts: Characters still can't move through or get by their own gang members just like in Mordheim.  Members of your warband blocking hallways, doorways or jump/climb points would be impenetrable walls, unwilling to let a team member get by even though their lives depended on it.  Again, why do it?  Have that just apply to the enemy in order to create blockades and choke points.   I've had the game crash to desktop a couple times so far.  Not the end of the world but it just adds to the gong show.My last gripe is that they've removed the ability to automatically see when you're in range of an enemy and what % chance to hit you have.  You end up really missing this feature especially with a greater focus on range.  You now have no idea when you're in range as your attack is buried under two layers of menu. Removing this feature has made the game much worse.Anywho, they must realize they have months and months worth of rewriting and redesigning to do which is unfortunate because it's a pretty bare bones game with just 3 gangs that are pretty much all the same minus a few behind the scenes skill scores and their general appearance to a point.  It's sadly nothing like Mordheim where every faction was truly unique.  I'd wait until Q2 next year before checking back on this title.  They need to dump a ton of resources into this before making DLC.

Sometimes they do things which seem silly to me but I just consider those little blessings from the Emperor.I have enjoyed the story, not only the writing and voice acting, but also the cut-scenes. There are tons of skills for your gangers which can mesh in very complex ways allowing tons of different builds and strategies. The gang customization is great and varied. It is clear the Devs embraced the lore because the game really has that 40k look and feel. I bought the table-top boxed game back in the 90s and played with a group. I feel this game is a fantastic adaptation. Finally, I have an I7-3930k, 16 GB ram, a SSD, and a GTX 1080 (non-Ti) and so far I haven't experienced any bugs or crashes. _childDocuments_.review: It is exactly as expected - Necromunda brought to the screen with similar mechanics as Mordheim, but of course adapted to the newer Necromunda rules and setting.There are some minor glitches and bugs, but nothing which is not expected on a launch date.I highly recommend playing the storyline / tutorial, because it teaches you about all the skills, setups, objectives, tactical map, etc. Yes, it does not cover clan management, something tabletop players look forward to, but it has a nice fitting Necromunda storyline and teaches you at the same time. And even there are even some tricky situation where not so tactical players might want to start again ;) is there room for improvement? Yes, some part of the handling feels slow, some AI glitches, etc. But nothing which is game breaking. I look forward to play more and wish for more gangs and maybe even some more campaigns as DLC (with full clan management).Update: I have played now over 60 hourse and still can recommend the game and do so if you like these kind of games. I did not suffer from the safe game bug and had no problems with MP and I understand that they are annoying. But the game is worth the money. The above mentioned flaws and bugs like the AI or some glitches can and will be fixed, especially the pathing issues (which do not come as a suprise with such an enviroment). But even with the AI doing strange things sometimes, it often also suprises with very nice actions putting me or some other AI gang in trouble. So the potential is there. Also regarding the campaign/tutorial - I hightly recommend playing it. Yes, it can be annoying sometimes (especially mission 5), but it also teaches you a lot about tactics and strategy in this game and forces you to think a bit different than in other comparable games.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is full of flaws and bugs. The AI is horrendous. The Story Campaign is so bad it reaches the point where progression in it is harder than driving your own head through a brick wall.Endless Mode though, is fun. This is the mode where you manage a gang, and take them through multiple fights, levelling up, gaining injuries and equipment as you go. This is where the game is at it's best. Unfortunately, the AI really lets it down. Turns are incredibly slow as you have to watch the AI move each individual turn in full -- and it often runs in circles or spends 2 minutes trying to run through a wall -- you can't do anything while the AI does this, you just have to sit there and watch. Each and every time it does this, and it will do this multiple times in a mission.So, a very flawed and often frustrating game with game breaking bugs and terrible AI. This may be fixed with significant patches, and I hope it is -- because I always loved Necromunda. The environments are pretty nice and the soundtrack is dope. The actual models and customisation (at least the stuff not locked behind the frustrating Story Campaign) are sweet. There is great potential in this IP, it's just been squandered here. TLDR: If you do buy it, skip the story campaign. Don't even bother, it will just make you angry. Play endless mode and maybe read a book or something while the AI turn plays out.Edit: Came back to play again in Dec 2020, after the Van Saar DLC released. The game runs slightly better. The AI decision making is a little better, but mostly really daft. The AI still gets stuck on obstacles and sometimes tries to run through walls. The campaign feels slightly more fun to play. It's still buggy, and you'll still crash to desktop. If you're interested in the universe/lore, and you can pick it up on sale, then maybe take a look. Otherwise don't bother.

detailed_description: Special Offer Owners of Blazblue Centralfiction on Steam automatically unlock exclusive Jin and Ragna cosplay items in the Pixel Lobby for all characters. Owners of Skullgirls 2nd Encore on Steam automatically unlock exclusive cosplay items in the Pixel Lobby for all characters: Cerebella's Hat Vice Versa, Peacock's Hat, and Bomb minion George. About the Game Them’s Fightin’ Herds is a 2D fighting game featuring a cast of adorable animals designed by acclaimed cartoon producer Lauren Faust. Beneath the cute and cuddly surface, a serious fighter awaits! Key Features Streamlined Combat - 4-button fighting mechanics, magic system, enhanced super attack, and juggle decay to prevent infinite combos. Story Mode - An episodic adventure filled with exploration, combat challenges, minigames, and boss fights! Chapter 1 (starring Arizona) is available now. Additional chapters are in development and will be released as free updates. Local Versus and Online Crossplay Matchmaking - Fight opponents offline or battle across the globe with GGPO’s powerful rollback netcode. Tutorial and Training Modes – Learn the ropes with combo trials and guided tutorials, practice combos in the data-rich training room, and view replays from your matches! Pixel Lobby - Unlock accessories, customize your avatar, and explore a top-down visual lobby with other players online. Dynamic Music System - Rockin' battle music adapts to the characters to make every match feel like a clash of champions.

Characters are well designed and decently varied in playstyle so many can find someone they click with in a short amount of time. Online experience is great as well with the game having good implementation of rollback netcode, along with a lobby system with fun explorable environments and simple player challenge systems. Community is small but dedicated but unfortunately will most of the time require you to be in a dedicated discord to get consistent games. It also has a fun story mode that functions as a more live tutorial, and feels like a well made adventure game with fighting game combat. All made by a small indie team.In short this game is a good package made by a dedicated indie team that has a clear respect and passion for the genre and what its players want.While I can easily recommend this game on its own merits and the small teams efforts I would think it is better to get this game on a sale given the recent news of content coming to a halt for the future, especially the story mode which wont be completed due to having to end future support.All in all, I think with what content is currently here the game deserves a chance and doubly so if you can snag this on a decent sale and can enjoy with friends and/or a small local community.
