_childDocuments_.review: I've been following this game's progress since the Fighting is Magic days, though I've hesitated for quite a long time to buy it, simply for the fact that I do not particularly enjoy fighting games. I finally decided to pick it up a week ago and I am happy for the most part! Let me state what I did and did not enjoy:Pros: - This game has so much personality and each character has their own unique fighting style that fits them perfectly. It's not everyday that you see a fighting game with cute animals!- The tutorial is great at teaching you how to play the game, even if you're a beginner like me. - Pixel lobbies are not only fun to hang out in, but contain particular activities to do together (ex: salt mines run, fighting for chests)- Story mode is a diamond in the rough, expands the lore and story of each character.- Music dynamic! According to whoever is winning a round, the game will play a variant of the track that includes that particular character's main instrument (ex: Pom is winning, you will hear a flute variant). Cons:- Due to its fairly small playerbase, you'll have a hard time finding players around your same skill level. Not entirely a bad thing, but it can be tiring to get repeatedly beaten up by players that have spent hundreds of hours into the game.- The roster is small, it only has 7 characters at the moment. New characters will eventually arrive, but via a season pass which you'll have to pay for.- Lack of content in general. This game has been released in 2020, yet 2 years later there has been hardly any new content. I understand that the team does not have many members, yet you'd think they'd focus more on completing the game first before releasing it on consoles (for a higher price might I add). Story mode is unfortunately still at chapter 1, as well as other things that have been listed as coming soon for a while now.Final thoughts:Even though I have put a thumbs up for this review, I would much rather say that it depends. This game has an equal list of pros and cons. Most cons will be fixed with time, but it is up to you if you wish to play a game for some hours and then keep it on a shelf to collect dust until new content is released. This game has a lot of potential and is crazy fun, I hope to see it grow in the future so I can 100% recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Them's Fightin' Herds is wonderful fighting game for beginners and experienced players alike. Since the characters all have differing playstyles, I have found that it is much easier to find a main to stick to and master. Having a training option on hand is very helpful, and the addition of rollback netcode is as well. The cartoon visuals are stunning, especially true considering that a few legends in the animation community played a role in bringing this game to life. The soundtrack is absolutely fantastic and  it's uniqueness comes from the fact that each character has their own variations of the stage music. TFH is truly an underrated gem that most of the fighting game community is yet to discover.

This is not a fault of the game itself, but rather a mistake on my part by assuming that "this time it will be different"Regardless, after the crushing PvP experience, all I had left was waiting for the story mode, and now, it's never coming.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a quick review after playing for a couple of hours.Short version: Even after such a short amount of time I highly recommend Them's Fightin' Herds. Go buy it now.  Long Version:  I love fighting games and have done for many years, but not just *any* fighting game will do. I'm happy to say this isn't just a low effort game and I would recommend it to any fan of the genre. Them's Fightin' Herds' (TFH) fighting system isn't breaking new ground, but it has enough features to have it's own feel. It feels kind of like a dialed back anime fighter. There are no air dashes, super jumps or double jumps outside of unique, per character passives. The combo system is the usual Light > Medium > Hard fair, but there are variations based on each characters individual moves. The magic button handles auxiliary special moves and features of each character, somewhat similar to Blazblue's 'Drive' system.Pros:-Solid fighting game mechanics.-Beautiful hand drawn graphics.-Great net code (GGPO).-Unique characters.-Fully, I mean FULLY featured training mode.Cons:-Only 6 characters (I think they are adding more later).-No story mode (as of this review. It is being added later).Honestly, if you don't mind the small roster and like fighting games, it is well worth the asking price. Bear in mind, the small roster still represents a lot of variety; there are no shoto clones here and you are sure to find a character you enjoy playing. The net code is solid and I've been able to find matches easily and play with minimal lag.Buy.This.Game.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a long-time fighting game fan, and this is one of the best fighting games I've ever played. On a technical level, on a design level, and with a focus on welcoming newcomers to 2d fighting games into the core concepts without holding their hands. The animation, character design, tutorial mode, and overall fighting mechanics are wonderful. The first chapter of the story mode is challenging and charming in equal measure. The fighting is fast but responsive, fluid, and with a smartly designed combo system and a clever character-unique "magic" system.I love every single character in this game, they all pop with personality and their fighting styles match them perfectly. As mentioned, their designs and their animations are top notch.That's all why this is such a tragedy. This is a lovingly-crafted fighting game made by genre enthusiasts and fans of animation... that has been taken away from its creators and shuttered, unfinished, by an uncaring publisher after they acquired the rights.I love this game, and it's immensely well-made. But recommend? I can't. It's quite literally unfinished and never will be finished. And this publisher does not deserve to have this stolen and hollowed-out project make money for them. A sad, sad story.

_childDocuments_.review: I may not be a brony, but when I first touched base with this game, I somehow grew an interest in it. I was even more intrigued after seeing famous people in the FGC like SonicFox and Maximilian Dood play the game, and seeing what can be done as a pro player, it just draws me in (I actually fought SonicFox a few days after I bought it, and of course, they destroyed me because of my unfamiliarity to the game. Now that I think about it, I might want a rematch in the future with them as of 1.0). Since I'm an experienced fighting game player, it's pretty much any fighting game these days that get my attention. Anyways, this GGPO powered game is the second to use Lab Zero's Z-Engine (which was first used for Skullgirls), and that is where the mechanically deep gameplay comes in, just as the description said.Them's Fightin' Herds is a perfect example of combining Marvel vs Capcom's and Skullgirls' gameplay, with a hint of Killer Instinct's combo limit mechanic and Injustice's gravity scaling mechanic, only instead of causing a blowout like in KI, it allows you to continue the combo, but after you have filled up a bar underneath your health bar, your opponent will fall faster and faster with each hit, making it harder to keep up your combo.Since there are also pixel lobbies in the game, which is the more popular form of lobbies in TFH, the game offers up a really good way to interact with fellow players. You can customize your character in it, like in other games with those types of lobbies (i.e. Blazblue Centralfiction and Cross Tag Battle, Guilty Gear Xrd, etc.) and request matches in it as well, like in any other game with this type of lobby. What's different with this particular lobby system is that it has voice chat, and more recently, channels you can switch from in order to talk to anyone in that channel you'd like without being disrupted by other players. Also, you could do memes, roleplay and stuff if you really wanted to.It might be in early access right now, but I still feel that getting this game was totally the right call for me! Hopefully you consider it too! It's a pretty neat fighting game! And as a friendly tip from my experience, the game appears to be more active in the evening (Eastern Standard Time Zone), so I think you could find some matches in the pixel lobbies then. Alright, I'm done here. Have fun with TFH, or don't. Doesn't matter to me. That's right, I'm talking about the Story Mode! It's real good for people who want to experience the lore of the game, and unless you either don't care for spoilers or have already played through the story mode, don't head into the spoiler zone. Go play the story yourself and find out just how good it is! Find some secrets, get some jokes, and just have a good time. It's all the way down there under the 2.0 edit so nobody accidentally goes over it.All I have to say here is that Shanty is a fun character, and now I main her.Anyways, you can get to the story now if you either went through it already or just don't care about spoilers. Have a good one!

_childDocuments_.review: I am a competitive fighting game player with multiple Top 8s across different games. This was the best fighting game I had ever played, despite the gameplay and balance issues. I played this game, competed, and did pretty well in events for the majority of the pandemic. This really was the best fighting game I had ever played during that time, despite the gameplay and balance issues in older versions (which, while annoying, weren't any more overblown than any other fighting game). I don't regret my time with this game at all. However, it's gotten extremely hard for me to recommend as more time has passed. For every strong point in this game, there's something else about it that is frustrating for a competitive player. This has some of the best QoL features of any fighting game, yet major bugs go unfixed for long periods of time. There are some really dedicated, awesome, passionate players & staff members who will give up everything to teach you and make your time with the game loads of fun. Yet, there are also insufferable members of the staff & community who may make discussing and grinding the game as a competitive player more frustrating. This scene has always been very tight knit and close, which means it becomes harder and harder to avoid those people- thus souring the experience. Every community has its issues, so whether or not this affects your experience may vary. Personally, in spite of it all, am very grateful for the friendships that I made during through this game.If you're looking for a fighting game that feels good to play with friends, or you have a small scene with your friends- I would still recommend it. Especially if you're in EU or Asia (look up Fauna / EU discord for this game, they have great scenes full of passionate players). It's also a fantastic casual game, with a groundbreaking story mode for fighting games and breathtaking aesthetics. As a competitive player, though? This game has turned into a hard pass. I finally sat down with the newest versions on console after not playing at all since 2.X, and while the direction of the game seems more sound- it's still not going to be a great fit for everyone competitively. Knowing the team, this will get better with time- but updates and fixes have slowed down over the years.Still worth checking out depending on your goals and interests in the genre. But if your interest lies in competing- look elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: I really,  hate to give this game a negative review. I truly do. I wanted so badly to love it. So before I get to the negatives, I'll give a few positives. Do keep in mind I'm a solo gamer and don't have any interest in playing multiplayer games with randos online, so my review will reflect that and mainly focus on solo play/story mode.The style is great. The character designs are fun and creative, as are the stage designs. All the animations are excellent. All of the art is fantastic. The music is nice as well. Overall the aesthetics are worthy of lots and lots of praise. The team clearly put a lot of love into these aspects.There are even certain gameplay elements I appreciated. It's not just a "pick two characters and start brawling" fighter. There's an actual, decent story mode, that even includes some platforming elements and some minigame-type fights. (Which I realize isn't everyone's cup of tea, but I for one like the fact that it mixes things up.)The game even has an extensive training mode AND a tutorial mode, both of which give you different ways of sharpening your skills and memorizing combos.Unfortunately they're useless. And this is where the negative comes in. The ai cheats, pure and simple. And no, this is not a "git gud" situation. Listen, I've played plenty of fighter games in the past, and while I was never a "champ" at them (except maybe Soulcaliber, to a small extent), I was never bad at them either. I'd like to consider myself reasonably average at them. I started on the default "intermediate" difficulty, assuming (quite reasonably) that it'd be a good balance of challenge and fun. And for a number of the quick mini-fights with the "predator" shadow-creatures along the way, they were. But then you'd come across the actual character fights and that all went out the window. They almost always somehow miraculously seem to perfectly counter any move you make, and seem to be able to somehow start new attacks before their current one even finishes, making for a miserable slog. You have to rely on luck way more than you should. All that combo-memorizing is useless since 95% of the time, you'll be relying on basic weak strikes to try and whittle your enemy down, and with some characters, such as Oleander, you'd be lucky if even those hit half the time. There is simply no open timeframe for anything more complex. It'd be one thing if you could learn how a character operates and come up with good counter-strategies, etc. You know, like any fair game difficulty should be. But this is just pure misery. I may try the "easy" difficulty to see if it's at least tolerable, but judging from other comments on the discussion board, it's basically the same thing. And I shouldn't have to go to "easy" just to get something that's not equivalent to the harder modes on most other fighters.It's a crying shame for an otherwise great game to be so ruined by one fundamental issue like this. I actually really wanted to see the story through. Again, the characters and aesthetics are all great. If the solo mode ai wasn't so unbalanced, I'd happily recommend this game to people. Some people may not even care about that and just want a multiplayer fighter game, so maybe you'd be fine with it if that's your thing. But it's a shame considering how much they clearly put into the story mode, only to have it ruined by endless, unfair frustration. If the ai is rebalanced so that the difficulty settings actually mean something in the future, I'll be happy to change my review to reflect that. But as of now, it pains me to say I absolutely cannot recommend this game.

The very day it came out I bought it.Truthfully I've never been a strong '2D/3D fighter' player. It's a genre that's never been my forte. So I went into this game expecting to lose a lot - and make no mistake that I  lose a lot. My competition in this game has reaction time that feels like a computer on the highest settings. Long story short if you ever fought me in this game you'd think I was a 7 year old that found the game on their parents computer or someone's mom looking to play what looks like something relaxing and cute -  is what I'm saying. I expected to lose and accepted it.The TFH community is very unfriendly though. Both in forum and in game. I only found it worth mentioning as the community TFH birthed from (as well as the cute atmosphere of the game) would lead you to expect differently.After the novelty of this game being something I was looking forward to for years wore off... all that was left was a genre I was barely interested in and a community that was  unwelcoming.But that's just my experience. When you get rid of personal preferences and community-related aspects the game is sincerely solid. Especially the dynamic music.In short: Only get this game if you're interested in 2D fighters in and of themselves - or simply to support the developers. get this game if the reason you want it is related to being part of the MLP fandom. You won't enjoy any people you meet.

_childDocuments_.review: Currently quite divided on this one. On one side, the game looks great, runs great on just about any rig and has some pretty great characters.The actual combat however.. it's not bad, but it needs some *serious* polishing. Some attacks, most notably heavy attacks have hitboxes larger than their animations, Tianhuo's slide attack hits the target the moment the animation of it begins *even if you're out of range* and then there's the special move system, which works by pressing a combination of keys in a certain sequence, this however often either does not work, or performs a special move when you wanted to do a normal attack, something that happened a lot to me when I wanted to perform a dash and immedeatly attack afterwards.Another issue are the combo's, in many an occasion once you get knocked up, or knock your opponent up and start hitting them with combo's, the target can just as well leave the computer, quietly make themselves some tea and come back without their character's control actually returning.Sure, the game's not pricey, at 15 bucks, but if I pay for it I'd very much like to actually be able to play the game, and I did not pay to see my character being flung through the air and I'm sure neither did my opponents.Besides all that there really isn't anything that makes this game stand out amongst other fighting games of its kind, other than that the characters are all 4 legged animals.In its current state I rate it a 6/10, I hope the developers will polish up their gameplay before the full release so I can improve this rating.EDIT:It's been a long time now. Still no campaign mode, which was promised to come "soon" and the game itself still has tons of issues.You know those sweet fighting games with that hitbox porn? This isn't one of them. Half of the time you're hitting opponents by hitting the air around them.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing fighters for basically my entire life, stemming from the Street Fighter Alpha series, Tekken 2 and 3, Ultimate Mortal Kombat 3, and pretty much everything that came out after. I also have a natural knack for these kinds of games. A few minutes in training mode to fiddle around with the characters and mechanics, and I'm basically ready to compete with high skill level players.Fast forward to somewhere in 2012 and Skullgirls is released, and I have to say, it's been my favorite fighting game the day I downloaded it on my Xbox 360 even until now. I can go on about why it's the perfect fighting game, at least from my perspective, but this isn't a Skullgirls review.While Skullgirls is arguably the best indie fighting game ever made, Them's Fightin' Herds has potential to be the next indie fighter powerhouse. It may be it's close resemblance to Skullgirls in which that it uses the same engine as it, or the hand drawn characters, or the GGPO netcode, but those are all things that made these games spectacular. I've only been playing for a few hours, but it's held my attention more than any fighter that came out since Skullgirls, and that's why I'm certain that this game will proseper. That is, if the devs keep up with it, which they seem like they are.This is in early access, so obviously there are going to be bugs, there are going to be modes missing, there aren't going to be many characters, so critiquing the game being unfinished would be just plain foolish. The game is playable, the online is smooth, and it's just plain fun. If you like 2D 4-button juggle heavy fighters, Then this game is for you.Also I'm not a brony by any means.This game isn't specifically for bronies. You don't have to be a brony to buy this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been looking into this game ever since I heard about it in a few YouTube videos. I love fighting games (have since I was a little girl, since back in the 90's the genre was the only one that had decent, strong, female playable characters on the regular), I love games with a colorful aesthetic (Why are games that are supposed to be "realistic" looking cursed with muted color palettes 85% of the time?), and I love animation, so this game was one I was really excited to get."Them's Fightin' Herds" has a very good tutorial section that covers most of the game's mechanics fairly well, and a roster of colorful characters who are full of charm and personality. You can tell this evolved from a concept of a "My Little Pony" fighting game not just because of the visual style but, if you've watched at least the first season of the show, you can tell which characters are based off of which member of the Mane Six (and I'm sure someone is already writing a cross-over fan fic). My favorite of the bunch so far is Velvet the reindeer, who reminds me of a certain purple-maned, white unicorn (come on, replace her ice with gems, and she's totally a snootier version of Rarity). The combos and specials are fun to use and challenging but rewarding to master, and I'm having a blast trying all of the characters out.I also enjoy this game's approach to a story mode. Most fighting games I've payed have a story mode that's just arcade mode with dialogue and cut scenes, but TFH has taken the approach of blending RPG dungeon crawling and puzzle solving with platforming and the game's base combat mechanics into a very interesting and fresh take on the classic story mode. The dialogue is pretty well written and there are hidden goodies and side-quests to uncover all over the place. My only two gripes about this mode are the decision to use the game's combat movement mechanics in the platforming sections and the fact that boss battles with playable characters have them pulling ultra-moves that you don't have any access to as a player.In terms of the platforming, let me be clear that I've been playing platformers for almost 30 years. I know how to negotiate traps, moving platforms, bottomless pits, and those annoying "Surprise Sucka!!" enemies that come out of nowhere just to mess with you. I know my stuff. So, believe me when I say that because of how precise the inputs for the super jump are, it makes platforming very annoying at some points in the story.  You have to hit down and up or up-diagonal in such a rapid succession that if you have a slippery thumb stick and a D-pad that puts those darn divots in the diagonal spots, you will not have a fun time executing this maneuver at all. You will think you did it right, swear you did it fast enough and accurately enough this time...and then you fall though some troll gap between the platform you're on and the platform you need to get to and you end up 5 levels down! It's very, very frustrating. I understand the input timing for when you're fighting, but when platforming, they should tweak the input timing to be a little more generous. You know, like 0.5 seconds instead of 0.2 seconds. With the timing as it is, it makes platforming more of a chore than an enjoyable addition to the game.My other gripe, the one about the ultra moves for player character bosses, is not only because it's slightly cheap. I'm used to fighting game bosses being cheap. It's a staple of the genre at this point. However, when a boss is also a playable character and they're being cheap with over-powered moves and mechanics that you have no access to when you play the character yourself...that's a little annoying. It took me about 5 or 6 tries to beat Velvet's boss fight in story mode because of her tantrum tornado at the end, and Oleander...well, all I have to say to the devs on that is: You know how wrong that was.Other than those two minor complaints about some frustrating design decisions for story mode, however, this is overall a great game. I, for the most part, recommend this game for players of all ages and skill levels, from experts to your 5-year-old niece who you're trying to introduce to the genre. The characters are fun and full of personality, the art style is colorful and cartoony, and the music is pretty good too.My Final Score: 8.5/10Overall great game, but there are some cheap and trollish moments in the story mode.

_childDocuments_.review: While it is sad that active development of this game will be ending soon (though it has been an impressive 7-year dedication, which we all must acknowledge), that shouldn't stop anyone from picking up this title's deluxe edition.First off, the story mode is very nuanced and inspired. There's a full story, some adventure elements, and, I must admit, it is cool to have a boss give you grief from the background. Though, as mentioned above, we'll likely never see the conclusion to the story, so a bit sad on that point.Never-the-less, the overall gameplay is solid. Special moves and supers are kept to simple haduken inputs, and the mechanics for just about every character are diverse, yet not super complicated once you see how they work in examples. You can pull off stellar combos, the palettes are fun to customize, and as a rushdown player myself, I had a blast with Shanty, truth be told.And, can we talk about the stages?! The fact that there are so many, with day, night, and twilight variants, AND amazing themes. That's a pretty deep layer of icing on an already meaty cake!If you couldn't tell by now, I love this game, and can't recommend it enough to other fighting game enthusiasts, as well as those who want to get into fighting games, but want something a little more cute-n'-cuddly for their first outing.The only downside I see is the lobbies. Either their at capacity, or they're ghost towns. My advice is to make sure you have some online or IRL friends who want to play and are already set up.Solid 9.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: What you're paying for isn't some huge budget fighter such as Dragon Ball FighterZ, but what you ARE paying for is a passion project built from what used to be an already amazing My Little Pony: Friendship is Magic fighting game (before Hasbro shut it down for obvious legal reasons).The game was built from the ground up with help from the creator of MLP:FiM Lauren Faust to make a completely original, yet simple, fighting game based around the 6 character simplistic fighting game that the old MLP game was.Like I said before, this wasn't just a game, it was a passion project from Kickstarter that took a few years to make, and I can personally say that I like the outcome so far, even without the story (which is coming soon as of this review). The fighting isn't hard to learn but maintains the heart of a fighting game without becoming a jugglefest (due to a juggle cap, which is an incredible feature).The pixel lobby is a great idea. Like in Dragon Ball FighterZ, there's a lobby of 20 players where you can choose your favorite character, put a hat or neckless on them for fun, and chat in the lobby. You start multiplayer fights there, make friends, or be silly with random people! It's my favorite addition to the game.From a DMCA take-down to a Steam release, I'm glad to finally be a part of the process of a kickstarted game, watching it grow over the years into what it is, and look forward to seeing where it goes now.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the game you want if you're a new player to fightning games!   is your normal 2D fightning game. Except it's filled with animals to fight with as opposed to humans or mutants. The game's controls are  to pick up and play. That means if you're fairly new to playing games like Skull girls this is a breeze. Otherwise, You the new player, does not need to sweat it, just learn the moves first and make sure you have a controller to play with. There isn't too much to hightlight in general since it's still .Each character has their own unique voice and playstyle. Although, they are adorable to to play around with they all have pretty simple combos to use against players. Others having their unique playstyle to combo and their pretty nice defensive moves. This allows you to easily counter players who have you stun locked and give them a nice surprise!The game has split screen support and online multiplayer lobbies called "Pixel Lobby". It has a similar layout to "Pony Town" the online flash game, but it allows you to dress your characters and fight with them. The lobby has enemies to fight NPCs as well and an easy to use chat the system.Don't be tempted by previous fightning games that have confusing combos. Them's Fightn' Herd allows you to practice your relatively simple moves in any matter you would like and there are people in game that are willing to help you train as well. Generally, You have to pay attention to your opponents range and what attack is apporpriate for their distance. I picked up the range and moves to use so fast, I was generally surprised with myself.While this is still a new game, You can generally point out which characters still need work. Genearally speaking, their characters design still seems to be in progress. However, the characters are pretty well designed, in terms of their "art design attack", which is the animation whenever they attack. The scenery is also very pretty and has matching music to really get the player ready for their opponent.Overall..If you're new to fightning games try it out! It's really easy to pick up and learn.If you already have  You get a  for the game. Like horses, deers, sheep, llamas, lizards, or COWS! Then look no further.

_childDocuments_.review: So I have always sucked at fighting games, and probably always will. Button-masher, full-stop and always. Only ever been marginally competent at Smash Bros and the original DBZ: Budokai, a little bit of Soul Caliber II, tried my hand at Skull Girls to some success on easy mode.That didn't stop me from backing the Indiegogo campaign for this one some years back. Dynamic Music is pretty cool, changing depending on the characters fighting and who's winning. The visuals are fun and appealing. Character designs are distinct and full of personality - but of course, that's Lauren Faust's doing. The RPG-style Pixel lobby is a fun way to interact with other players. But my reaction times are terrible! Some of the timing based things are super frustrating! I don't know what these terms all mean! The first level boss is wiping the floor with me! But I guess I'm getting better? Seems like I'm struggling a bit less now. I'd like to blame my tired old XB360 controller and its worn analog stick, but let's be real; I'm not good enough to notice a difference yet. The tutorials are helping work past button mashing to actually understanding the controls. The tools are there, it's up to me to make use of them. Seems rather ideal for a beginner like me so far!

_childDocuments_.review: While this game is fun I do have some issues with it. I play it on a laptop which support games like this just fine but I prefer to play with an Xbox 1 controller. The main problems on the controller is the sensitivity issues. I can input a simple command such as "walk forward" only to see the character standing still because it either didn't take the prompt or will be delayed up to two full seconds which is utter ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ in a fast paced fighting game. combos are difficult to pull off or even start when the controls randomly refuse to work because you can't personally adjust the sensitivity to your needs making the game unnecessarily difficult to play.The training NPC's difficulty is also horribly misbalanced. I went from the lowest difficulty to where the bot would barely move and fight back to the next one up for a bit of a fight only to receive an asswhoopin so through that I had to physically close the game to get it to stop long enough to get it changed back. I felt like I deserved an apology afterwards, the beating ways just that bad! I want to play and fight more online as the lobbies look like a lot of fun to play in but once again, the finicky controls have me scared to even jump into a fight as I can't use the keyboard (which is far more reliable and reactive) to save my life.As for why I would actually recommend this game, the story, characters and the over all game play it's self had me in stitches. I haven't laughed so hard in a story mode as I have in this game in over a year. If the problems listed above were fixed then I would find this game so much more playable and enjoyable.

_childDocuments_.review: These days, if a fighter doesn't have over twenty fighters, people complain that it's pretty limited in terms of content. I'm generally one of those people - I threw a lot of shade at Blazblue CTB when it first came out, and it was primarily for that reason. A fighter generally needs a decently sized roster to allow people to mix up their options a bit so the game can keep feeling fresh.That's not the case here.How does a fighting game with only six characters (so far) lend itself to so much replayability? Because the devs put their heart and soul into making sure every move, every option that you could possibly take at any given time, was dead solid perfect. I've had this game for a decent amount of time, since I got the early access version off of Humble. Let me tell you - it was tight back then. But now? It's AMAZING. The framerate is extra smooth no matter what I run it on (I've played the game on both a 1080 Ti monster desktop and a Vista-era laptop!), and the responsiveness of the characters goes beyond framerate - it was CODED tight, and it remains tight at all times. Even the few times it did lag for me in early development, it always seemed like ONLY the graphics hanged, but the gameplay itself went on unimpeded. That shows you their priorities, and I'm beginning to think that every fighting game should be coded with that kind of mentality.Another reason it keeps so fresh is that it really mastered the "four-legged battle" concept that other games didn't dare to tread for so long. Remember the uproar that came when MvC3 launched and people raved about how unique Amaterasu felt? It's like that, but times six (again, so far). Movements that you wouldn't think would feel natural, even COULD feel natural, DO feel natural. I'm almost beginning to suspect that the dev team members all have four legs themselves.And, of course, the style of the game is superb. Looks great, sounds great, the character designs and dialogues are great, the whole shebang. I REALLY appreciate the option to choose between 2D and 3D backgrounds, that helps a TON with keeping the game hardware-accessible (something that many "AAA" teams should take some cues from).Overall, the game is great! It packs a heap of content in despite what seems initially to be a very small roster, and I know you'll have a blast with it!

_childDocuments_.review: Full disclosure: I backed this game and received a closed beta key.Them's Fightin' Herds is a fast, fluid four-button four-legged fighter featuring a cast of fantasy quadrupeds. The gameplay is butter-smooth, with easy-to-grasp controls and a satisfying whump to every hit. The characters, designed by cartoon producer/director Lauren Faust, are colorful and full of personality. It was kind of amazing to see these characters come to life as their "cardboard" placeholder animations were gradually phased out. The music is crazy good, and hearing the character instruments dynamically take over the song over the course of a match is just fantastic. The voice acting, which was just recently implemented, surprised everyone with its highly experienced cast. This ain't no fan project!Netplay is generally pretty good, but it obviously depends on your connection. I've had a few bum matches in the past.It's also kind of easy to get comboed to death if you go up against someone who's real good, or fight the CPU on above the default difficulty. That's just how fighting games go, though.Overall,  I'm running out of ways to say this game is real good. If you like the hand-drawn cartoon style and/or quick, responsive fighting action, give this game a shot.Touch the COW. Do it NOW. (9/10)Full release update: The game's still excellent, but now even more so. Pick it up.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm normally a big fan of fighting games, especially Skullgirls and Smash. That said, I'm going to be requesting a refund on this one. I'll do my best to explain, because I do believe this game has a lot of heart and potential.1. I don't like to use the "standard" 4 button control scheme, with "special" assigned to the A(Xbox)/X(PS4) button, then light, med, heavy going clockwise from there. I prefer to have A/X be the light attack, X/Square med, Y/Triangle heavy, and B special. Upon changing my scheme, however, that caused the B button to start acting as the A button would in the menus, and the Y button becoming the cancel. Some games have an option to change this, but I didn't see one here. This is almost a deal breaker for me, as it's a very simple functionality that should be in place already.2. While the art and overall style of the game, and especially the characters and their movesets is fantastic, the game is simply too barebones for me in its current state. If you are only interested in the game for the fighting mechanics, well then I think you will be satisfied. I gave this game a chance because I thought I'd be happy with it even during the early access period, but it just doesn't have the features I expect in a fighting game.  And, as quoted from the devs below: "It is mostly feature complete to our intended amount and type of content for a Full release." There's not even a way to have simple matches with AI partners outside of the Arcade mode yet. There's no challenge mode in place to familiarize yourself with the characters movesets. I knew there was no story mode yet, but what I didn't notice until now is that the story mode will be released piecemeal, and I'm not thrilled about that idea and generally don't like the paradigm of releasing in chapters - even if it's going to be free. 3. I generally don't play these sorts of games online,  but rather with friends in person, so I can't comment on the functionality there. EDIT: I did not realize that owners of Skullgirls (myself included) got a 4 dollar discount when purchasing the game. Still leaving the next part for posterity. This short paragraph is the only edit I have made to the original review, and any others that may be made in future shall be noted.4. Lastly, I just went and checked out this game's Indiegogo page. The lowest price all of those 4500+ people payed for this game was $15 bucks. I had no idea this game existed until today, and yet I paid 4 bucks less than they did. I'd be a bit annoyed about that if I was them, as the discount should be given to those who believed in the project from an earlier point in time, in my opinion. However, it's possible those people who backed it wouldn't mind at all, because they liked the project that much. Still, it seems unfair.I'm sorry I had to give a negative review, and I don't feel good about it. It's clear that a lot of time has been put into creating the characters and theirs abilities, and I hope that none of you who read this think less of the game because of my review. I would encourage anyone to give it a try, especially those who are fans of games like Skullgirls and perhaps even fans of a certain tv show. (I've never seen the show, personally!) I'm clearly the odd one out here, as there are nothing but glowing reviews. I can only give my honest opinion in the end, and this is it. I may come back at a later point in time to see what the game has become, but for now, it's just not what I was looking for.

_childDocuments_.review: This review will be going against the grain a bit, but I wouldn't recommend this game based on its own merits. For me, the story mode is always the most important thing of nearly any game, and that's where this one disappoints the most (even without being apparently unfinished).The actual fighting game core mechanic is fairly well made, though I'm personally a fan of controls that don't require using your movement keys to block (my preference is more Smash Bros, less Mortal Kombat). That difference of opinion aside, however, the fighting controls are serviceable and the action fluid, so no real complaints.The problem comes with the story-mode integration. Injustice is a great example of how you can tell a great story through a fighting game, and integrate non-fighting game elements (mostly quick-time events in that game). This game, however, takes the wrong approach in trying to integrate both RPG and platforming elements into the game, some aspects of this work well, while others are atrocious and ruin the game.The RPG elements are mostly moving a character around on an RPG-maker style map. This is very basic, but adds an interesting exploration element. Something like this is an easy way to add story, with the fighting gameplay being the result of "random encounters" on the map. It's even designed so that losing a fight doesn't immediately cause you to lose. Instead, you lose an amount of your overworld hp each time you lose (or a smaller amount if you win, based on in-fight damage taken). The problem comes mainly in the form of bosses being instant game over - the hardest foes are the ones you aren't allowed to lose against. This is made worse by these enemies having very unique moves, like involving multiple opponents, or dodging attacks the boss spits from the background. While fun and interesting mechanics, these new strategies to adapt to are exactly why bosses should  be an instant game over if you lose, especially given the length of time needed to get back through the RPG elements.And then you have the platforming. Do not make a platformer without a jump button. Just don't. Not only does this game not have a jump button, but it has three different jump heights depending on how fast you move the controls. Frustratingly, this is  sensitive, and counter-intuitively both short and long jumps require faster presses. Protip: if a handful of ledges are your entire puzzle, your control scheme is f***ed.So in conclusion, if you just want a fighting game with cute characters, this isn't a bad choice. If you want to play the story mode, you should probably choose a different game that doesn't try to dabble too broadly.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, let me preface this by saying: Them’s Fightin’ Herds is, or at least was prior to Modus / Maximum Entertainement, a great game, which I’ve praised publicly many times as one of the best packages you could get in terms of fighting games: Good and compelling story mode (even if it was just Chapter 1) which actually taught you how to play the game, solid netplay feauring rollback netcode and crossplay, as well as functional lobbies, a fun PvE side mode, feature-complete training and tutorial mode, a fun (if small) cast of diverse characters with lots of depth and unique mechanics… This was, for all intents and purposes, one of my go-to recommendations alongside Guilty Gear XX Accent Core +R’s PC port, which was also ahead of its time.And then Modus happened.While the buyout of Mane6 by Modus did come with the added perk of console ports, localization and the promise of extended support through a Season Pass, it has been clear for a while that this buyout was not a good thing. Already, Stronghoof’s release felt a tad unpolished, and a lot of cost-cutting measures could be seen. (Stronghoof’s VA acting as his own announcer, low res trap textures on even the Series X port, the lack of a dynamic musical theme…) We get it, crafting a fighting game character, let alone a fully hand-sprited one with huge, HD sprites, takes a lot of time.But what really broke the camel’s back was the fact that between Stronghoof’s release and the Nidra / Baihe patch, the entirety of Mane6 was laid off by Modus save for 3 employees, two of which have since left of their own volition, cancelling the continuation of story mode, and leaving ONE PERSON to have to craft two entire characters on a strict time constraint. And it shows. The official TFH Discord server was left abandoned and prey to p*** bots, and the final patch breaks the game like never before. Both Nidra and Baihe come with a load of infinite combos and bugs which break the game in a significant way, the combo trials are broken, and all of that was discovered in less than an hour after the release of said patch. Who knows what else we could find on legacy characters.As such, it kinda breaks my heart to tell you: DO NOT BUY THEM’S FIGHTIN’ HERDS. Maximum deserves no money for what they’ve done to this game, and that’s without mentioning whatever is happening with their other fighting games, God of Rock and Diesel Legacy. It also serves as a good overview as to what to expect with their upcoming Avatar The Last Airbender fighting game. If you already got scammed by Maximum Entertainement, revert to the previous patch by going to the "stable" beta branch in the Steam settings. If you got it on console… Well RIPMaximum Entertainment is not worth your time. Steer away at all costs.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: The devs have announced the end of active development for this game. Do NOT buy this game as it is quite literally a scam with fine lettering to make it look like it's all fine.-------------------------------------------Fantastic fighting game with a great story, but ruined by changes to development direction.I really, really want to recommend this game as it is one of the most well designed games I've ever played, but ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ I'd be lying if I said I trust these devs in any shape or form. They've been changing their development direction ever since the game's inception, though it never *actually* hurt the game until what they had done to it a year ago.It's frustrating, and maybe even depressing to look at this game's announcements. They've completely shifted aside the story mode and they just focus on new DLC which people (mostly the big fighting game fans that cycle between the games as they go up in popularity) swear is required to be in the game because "other fighting games do it too". Then the comments section is just as frustrating, mainly because they have one dude trying to shut down any criticism ever made in the forums, to the point it feels toxic. If I kept my comments open here I'd probably get a reply from that one dude, if my review doesn't just get flagged and taken down.We were given the (over ambitious) promise of getting the entirety of story mode complete by the end of 2022. Obviously, that was too good to be true and it was clearly a big promise made to be reduced to much less than that, so it'd be foolish to blame them for not delivering on that. However, they didn't deliver even a bit. We got absolutely *nothing* for the story mode. Not one chapter or even any previews for the next one, literally nothing. They just brought up a season pass DLC that they claim you "don't have to buy" and that if you don't like it then you don't have to get it, etc etc, you get the idea.The most we got was them claiming that the story mode is indeed "in the works", and that's it. But now we got yet another DLC reveal and there wasn't even anything for the story in the announcement for it. Hopefully I'm just speaking too early and the next announcement has real details about the upcoming story chapter and not just "yeah it exists". But even then I'd expect the release of just one chapter to be delayed to the very end of this year, and that feels like too much to ask for at this point.It doesn't just stop there, though. This game is pretty much well on its way towards an early playercount death, even during their cherished DLC scheme. The playercounts are REALLY LOW. And to be honest, a lot of people are swayed away from the game solely for the fact that it's a "pony game". It is by all means a "pony" game, and I could try all I want to say otherwise (like the fact there's actually only one pony character), but it all comes down to the same thing: People know Them Fightin' Herds as the MLP fighting game. It's the hard truth and i've watched multiple fighting game fans completely avoid this game regardless of how good it might actually be, solely because it is what it is.So here's the thing, they don't even actually get to attract these players with their DLC season pass scheme, because those people are NOT going to play anyways. And all they do is scare away other potential players AND existing players due to the questionable pricing. The game has been price hiked AND it has multiple DLCs now, seriously.I really want to say what's actually good about this game, but it kinda falls flat because the best thing about it is the story, followed right up by the actual gameplay. Both are absolutely just great. I ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ love this game. But the story has been outdated for years, and all we're getting is DLC. I seriously cannot recommend this game to anyone, I'd have to lie to your face to do so, and hide all the little details about what's wrong with this game.EDIT (DLC2 Update): It gets worse and worse. New update has absolutely zero mention of story mode (effectively shelved), and moving forward new stages aren't going to have fully dynamic music like what TFH always had. It's become a pretty terrible DLC platform in my opinion. I advise you do not buy the DLC for this game.Honestly, I don't even want to actually give this game a rating. _childDocuments_.review: I got over 40 hours of fun out of this game based solely on the multiplayer during early access. I found Pixel Lobbies, a mode that lets you wander around as an avatar of one of the game's fighters while challenging other players to fights, to be one of the most enjoyable modes I've ever played in a fighting game.Now that the singleplayer is out, and I've given it a shot, I have to say I'm done. The main reason stems from the design: Them's Fightin’ Herds, while not as broken and ♥♥♥♥♥♥ on newcomers as Skullgirls, still retains some of the combo-strings and pushblocking that can leave you feeling hopeless. I was never a fan of Marvel vs Capcom 2 & 3; if you are, you know the kind of game I'm talking about and Them's Fightin' Herds is probably for you.As the online community has gotten better and better, I've found it harder to put up a fight and eventually lost all interest in playing online. So, I turned to singleplayer, and I've not been impressed. The Story mode is exceedingly long-winded, and packs forced tutorial segments and bosses in awkwardly. The AI does nothing to diminish the painful fighting mechanics, and instead re-enforces their inherently unfriendly nature.Them's Fightin' Herds is a prickly, hardcore fighting game experience disguised as a friendly, MLP-influenced fighter. I honestly wish I could avoid recommending it, but after 40 hours I don't think I can do anything less than recommend it before uninstalling it.

_childDocuments_.review: It's funny, it's cute, the music is phenomenal, the fighting is fun and easy to get into. The character roster may be a tad small, but the current six characters are each unique and have different playstyles, not to mention the pallette references, oh the pallette references. Also, I don't care what you've heard, you don't have to be a fan of any cartoon show to appreciate this game. The game also uses the Z-Engine, which you may have heard of from Lab Zero and their game, Skullgirls, who helped the devs of Them's Fightin Herds, Mane6, by letting them use the Z-Engine here. Currently it includes a single player arcade mode, training and target mode, with story mode currently being worked on to be released soon in episodic format for free. Multiplayer modes include a lobby play function, and the pixel lobby, which is essentially a lobby with avatars from which you can challenge other players to 1v1 fights, and get cosmetic hats in the pve salt mines. The Game's lore is also fairly interesting (the lore info is on Mane6's website) as well as the overall aesthetic of both the characters and world. The world and characters are somewhat adorable, but that doesn't detract from the fighting by no means. For those of you out there who are fans of a certain TV Show.....y'all might be interested to know that Lauren Faust helped to design the characters and world as well. As for gameplay. I normally suck at fighting games typically. This wasn't that hard for me to learn, it helps that theres only 4 attack buttons (Light, medium, heavy, and Special), whereas other games have things like kicks and such to add onto that. Also, specials and combos aren't that hard. Each character plays differently, you have Arizona, a brawler/grappler, Pom, a pet user / summoner, Tianhuo, an aerial attacker who can string combos very fast, Velvet, who excels at controlling the field and playing keep-away with attacks that block or push you back, and finally Oleander, who is basically Houdouken-Horse. As for community, there is a small following which will likely grow as the game reaches the end of Early Access. Also, while I hate to say it, fighting games on PC are by definition, a bit of a niche, even with big titles like FighterZ and arguably Blazblue, you don't have that many PC users as compared to the console versions. That being said, the game is still fun, both in singleplayer and when you get a MP match. The real thing that I'm looking foward to though is the singleplayer, as it's supposed to have an RPG mechanic and overworld to it, which is something no other fighting game has done, in addition to the fact the game already has a ton of lore. Now, to end this review on a high note, allow me to just ask you a simple questionWhat other game allows you to play as a headbanging cow or sorceress with a necronomicon on the same engine as Skullgirls for ONLY 15 dollars? None? I thought so. AlsoOleander is best Po-I mean Ungulate 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Now I know what you're probably thinking (unless you're not the kind of person who takes things at face-value). Yes, this is a pony-based fighting game. We get it. Y'all think it's trash just cuz the characters have very distinct similarities to that one very familiar pony show that everyone seems to love to hate on. We get it. But if you're gonna just disregard this whole thing based solely on its surface-level design decisions, then you're gonna miss out on a hell of a good game.If Skullgirls is an introduction to Street Fighter based games, this game is the Skullgirls of games like BlazBlue or Guilty Gear. Which is also kinda funny since this game is built with the Skullgirls engine, so you catfighting fenatics already know that the engine certainly works smoothly. And it's not just that part that works either! The controls are responsive, the gameplay is fun and easy to pick up, and the characters are very diverse and introduce players to different styles of fighting characters. (Except grapplers. Unless you count Arizona as a grappler, which...I don't, really.) I had never even considered picking up a zoner character until I played Oleander, and it's the most fun I've had with the archetype.The game also comes with a Pixel Lobby, which basically functions as a way to find players to fight without having to directly seek them out and make a lobby with them, while still having a bit more interactivity than the Skullgirls Quick Match system. The game itself has about 8 official lobbies, with a whole bunch of fan-created lobbies to spice things up if those ones are full. When entering, you are given a little avatar you can customize with hatsand accessories. Bored of the hats you're given? Go to the Salt Mines! There you can fight Predators and open chests to get salt which can be used to open more expensive chests to get the aforementioned Hats and Accessories.Cons? Well, it's hardly finished, for one, though I wouldn't let that bother you too much. All that's really "missing" per se are things that wouldn't really affect gameplay otherwise, like missing animations and stuff. That's not counting things like Story Mode and quick matches, but you can get a lot of the content missing there through other means, like Arcade mode and the aforementioned Pixel Lobby.In the end, I'd say the game has a lot of potential, and definitely is a lot of fun right now. I implore you to look past first impressions and give the game a try. You just might find a fighting game that you'll really enjoy. I hope this helps you in your purchasing decision.

_childDocuments_.review: Brony or not, you should play this game, because it's a little masterpiece and should be praised for what it is, considered the love, dedication and care the small team of developers behind it has put in it.-Online is GGPO powered rollback netcode, with a very good-looking Pixel Lobby system.-Only 6 characters (1 planned as a DLC, is currently under development) but you can play them in so many ways it's almost impossible to get bored.-Frenetic action (Guilty Gear like) with 4 buttons' attacks: Light, Medium, Strong and Magic.The "Magic" attack is a unique attack for each character that consumes its own dedicated bar when used).-Training mode is probably one of the best you ever seen.-An original and fun-to-play Story Mode that gets updated for free as the time goes by.Each character has it's own episodes and i don't know how many episodes for each are planned for the future (currently, it has only one chapter).-The characters are very charming, cute and very well animated, but also very entertaining.-Voice acting is really good, too bad Story Mode is not fully voiced... :(-A dynamic music system that allows to play each characters' variation on a stage theme, during a battle, when certain conditions arise.The community is still "young" and so, not as big as you would expect, but overall, it's worth a shot, believe me, you won't regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: First, this needs to be said: the reason this game is in early access is because of major complications with the story mode, which includes the "how to play a fighting game" tutorials, and there are still a (very) few unfinished animations. If you prefer learning from tutorials, your best bet for maximum enjoyment is to wait until full release.HOWEVER...If you want to play a fast-paced, 1 v 1 fighting game with oodles of training mode features, the best available netcode (granted, not perfect, but still better than the rest), and characters with personality, there's no reason not to pick it up now. Players coming from a Marvel \ anime background should feel at home quickly after adjusting to particular character quirks (for example, every character's movement options are a little bit different). Feeling a little lost? The friendly community has your back, regardless of whether you prefer Discord, Reddit, or forums. The pixel lobby system is great, especially if you're a fan of the 8 & 16-bit eras, though I do wish you could fit, say, 32 people in a single lobby instead of the current limit of 20.  My only real complaints are mostly personal taste: some of the stage music feels too low-energy for fight music (seems more like music for a story scene), especially compared to the main menu theme, and chip damage (damage taken from blocking certain attacks, usually specials and supers) seems a bit high for a game that allows chip-outs to win rounds (though this is probably just my bias, since I typically play games with no chip-outs, and of course will likely change as they continue to balance the game before full release).

_childDocuments_.review: Alright let's cut to the chase right away and worry 'bout the details later.The game is fun. It is the testimony that crowdfunded games can still be made and not be awful. It's the very opposite of awful. It is amazing.The inclusion of a pixel lobby transforms what would have otherwise been just another fighter game(but with quadrupeds), into an almost RPG like game... you could probably role play too if you were so inclined. I've spent hours playing the dungeon raids to get more interesting wearables and it is fun. The fighting feels good and exciting and the graphics are beautiful.There are a few graphics and artwork missing here and there and some still having the sketch placeholder but those are just in a couple of places. They delivered an almost complete game, it was stable with only one minor crash when I changed resolution but it didn't reproduce. The game works really well with a controler (tested with Xbox 1 controller), and has a voice chat and text chat, as well as a small board with quick responses such as Hello, GGWP, and a couple quick question buttons to ask others to fight you or train with you or maybe reconsider that rematch they declined.The game's roots from the original Fighting is Magic are still present. The characters are very familiar to anyone who has watched MLP:FiM, yet they are completely new and unique. They truly managed to strike the center of the target. Making something completely new and giving players exactly what they had wanted back in 2013. An amazing quadruped fighter game.Netcode worked quite well. When playing with nearby players or even slightly further away the experience was good.Though if you intended to match with your friend from Australia you may experience issues with performance and everything stuttering. Which isn't to say the game is bad, quite the opposite, the game deals well with the issues of high latency, as much as it can. It's just not a problem that can be fixed, unless someone makes a really fast internet connection from Europe to Australia. Players are given an option to tweak some settings and try to achieve better experience while playing with distant friends. I've not had the time to test or play with them but the game does well with default ones, even recommending different values so you don't have to do the guesswork.The game comes with plenty of options for new players to practice, such as practicing their moves and combos without time limit or health limit, and you can also do it with another person if you want to take your practice to the next level and simulate real battles with your friend.  You can play against an AI in arcade and practice your skills against someone who is very much not fair (though you can make the AI easy, normal and so on all the way up to unfair difficulty). The game also has a list of challenges you can complete in the Target mode where you have to destroy the target's in a specific way as quickly as you can.If the game is this good on release, who know's what it will be like when they polish it up with updates and the additional character the Goat, and the Linus/MacOS support. Unfortunately the Story Mode didn't make it into the release but I will definitely eagerly await for them to finish this piece of the game. Cause who doesn't like a story mode?Happy Fighting.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, I wanna preface this by saying that I WANTED and would've given this a thumbs up, but there's a lot of smaller add-up problems paired with fewer-but-huge, serious issues with this game that I can't and won't overlook. There's a lot to like about this game, but the major problems, some others have already written about, are so big that I can't give this game a pass in good faith. If you're absolutely set on getting this game I strongly reccommend waiting on if the community and story mode is actually completed -it's at barely 20% and that's being generous, and getting something else in the meantime. But honestly just get something else period.Like with my first review i'ma list things in pros+cons point format for the most part for sake of ease. And this review's gonna be in several parts because it got too big for the character limit. Click for full review. --- There's a lot to love about this game and where it might be going potentially.- Loveable characters who have a lot of potential for some meaningful arcs. (I'm lookin at you especially Pom, Velvet and Paprika) and cool, colourful and sketchy art style that I wish I saw more of (another example I love for anyone who also likes this style and similar, is Super Mario Strikers.)- Worldbuilding's interesting, humourous and draws me in. Though there are some questionable spots, there's lots of room for some amazing stuff if done well. - The story mode structure has you getting to see some of the world of Foena, top-down rpg style.- The lobby makes for a neat little hub, and if you play certain areas in Story Mode you might gain more appreciation for the connections and worldbuilding.I wish I could add more on pros compared to cons but that's all I can put.--- Conversly there's a lot to hate about this game and it's intended direction and current excecution, mechanically. And there's also other major issues.- So that worldbuilding? y'know where I said questionable spots? Yeah let's talk about that consitution in the Reine Museum cause uhhhh-- The Alpace Region. To be fair the storymode's extremely unfinished, but right now without spoiling too much, the current setup of the Alpace people is: being characterized as a native and traditional, but EXTREMELY long-suffering people whose hardship, suffering and dedication to tradition is deliberately played up to illogical degrees for laughs. I have extreme and seriously doubtful apprehension about this, because in terms of joke and plot setup this is a big gamble and can either be a well-done tearjerker+underdog plot (especially because it's clear from jump they have MASSIVE ties to the main plot and worldbuilding), or wind up a ♥♥♥♥♥♥-up punch down. It already is starting from a punchdown perspective with the whole played for laughs thing. We'll see. And the part about it being illogical is hard to explain without spoiling anything so i'll put it this way: There's every last piece of evidence thier region was more than liveable, it was thriveable. And so in thier current situation, it literally makes no sense for them to be living they way they are with such hardship. Wouldn't they have retained something? What happened?All that being said given the previous location, I have some theories about how that arc might wind up being handled, why they're in thier current state, and I hope i'm proven right. But i'll stop there -this is a review.--- You know how I just said the story mode's unfinished? I lied. It's WOEFULLY unfinished -This is gonna be another subsection so expect a long read. - Arizona is the only playable character, the current amount of content is very, very much padded out with more fights than needs to be necessary imo -even for a fighting game, and worst of all those fights wind up stressful by horrendously unbalanced AI. So much that I skipped entire sections of areas and sacrificed full completion JUST to avoid dealing with them.- Going into that, the story's tutorials don't teach you how to deal with said CPUs. They teach you competitive techniques which isn't in-itself bad, Problem is they try to cover it up as being needed for the story... namely to cross over needlessly hard terrain. This comes with later predators thrown in that your techniques don't help with dealing with AT ALL, because they weren't built around that or even with that in mind, and the commands I found were very analog-stick unfriendly as I had consistantly, only slightly, less trouble on the dpad.. Until I had to fight an opponent. which meant switching between the two and often. In other words Story mode tutorials don't feel like they match at all with the actual intent, if anything it felt like the Competitive Tutorials were shoehorned in with no real thought on weaving them into the story play properly as an option and viable solution to dealing with predators. Again, instructions don't feel built with those parts of Story Mode you're playing in mind. [1/12]

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who only started playing Fighting Games in 2018 with the release of Dragon Ball FighterZ, I would still consider myself fairly new to the genre - but it's been some of the most fun I've had playing video games in a long time. While I'm not great at them by any means, I absolutely love the competitive nature that fighting games bring, as I also like going deep into learning the systems and workings of each game I pick up. In these 2 years, I've also played Skullgirls, MK11, SFV, Smash Ultimate, MvC 2 and 3, and now TFH. And I can say without any doubts that this game is certainly my favorite.The art and animations alone are more than worth the extremely low cost of this game - and that's simply the foundation of this amazing fighter. Every character is extremely smooth to play, each with a distinct, unique playstyle that differs from the others. Never do I feel like my inputs don't go through or are misread as different moves, it's always what I want to do, I will do. Hits carry weight and are extremely satisfying to pull off, giving you an amazing sense of gratification when you see your enemy either go flying back or get slammed into the ground. And while yes, a roster of only 6 may seem small by today's standards, these characters are by no means shallow - just trying to learn even 1 character means you will have to dedicate some time if you want to get good with them. This doesn't even include how amazing the online play or story mode is. The former, I will say is hands down one of the best on the market right now. A netcode that genuinely works without double digit frame input lags is insanely refreshing in today's world. And the story mode - just play it. While there's only 4 chapters right now that can be completed in around 4 hours, it is hands down the best story mode for any fighting game, period. It doesn't just sit you through 5 minutes of cutscenes and then put you into a fight, and then show you ANOTHER 5 minutes of cutscenes - no, it actually allows you, the player, to fully explore and interact with the world around you, filled with plenty of fun secrets to unlock customizable items for your online character. And it isn't even just fighting enemies either - there's also platforming sections, and a combination of the two for a mix of platform fighting. I'm just simply astounded at how a game this amazing is so under the radar. This game is truly what the industry standard for fighting games SHOULD be. And those who turn away from it because of it's artstyle are truly doing themselves a disservice. Judging this book by it's cover doesn't even give you a taste at how fantastic a game TFH is.

_childDocuments_.review: So a little backstory. It was around 2013/2014 and I was a complete noob at fighting games(still kind of am). I was however very into MLP:FiM. Now I understand this game has it's own identity in no way related to MLP but back when it was still 'Friendship is Magic', I gave it a shot mainly playing Applejack and really enjoyed just messing around. It also showed that the team at the time had a lot of potential(which now a lot more people have come to realise). 'Them's Fightin' Herds' is a really solid fighter for veterans and first-timers alike. Don't judge it by it's aesthetics and solely by it's gameplay. The tutorial is solid, detailed, and will show any newcomer to the genre all they need to know even including topics like hitboxes and frame data. The music is amazing and it shows they really put in a lot of love into this game. There are only 6 characters which some might call a con but they're all very unique and spread out. There is a Goat character coming in the next major patch as of this review and hopefully more after. I can understand they wanted to polish everything in the game for their 1.0 release before working on the roster so imo shouldn't really fault them too much for that. The story mode beats imo most other fighting games period. Great dialogue and it goes over some basic character movements in the platforming sections. The lobby is arguably the best in the genre. Fun customisation, PvE in the salt mines which leads to more cosmetics, and a cutesy little hub to just vibe in. Netcode is just as great as people claim and it's only going to get better from my understanding as they plan to get the same update that Skullgirls got for their netcode. The developers are involved with the community and open to play matches or discuss issues or ways that the game can be improved. I love that in games in general. There aren't that many players at the moment but the numbers are steadily growing and I really wish the team great success because their dedication and passion definitely merits it. Sorry this review's on the messy side but just wanted to give my thoughts in no particular order. Great game, great community, and great team. What more does one need?Also TIANHUO REPRESENT!

_childDocuments_.review: I was enjoying this game a lot when I originally reviewed it, but the devs have failed to deliver on their ambitious promises for years and the issues that myself and many others had with the game were never addressed. As of today, they have announced that development will cease after the season pass is finished. The game was already on life support 2-3 years ago, but now it is officially dead. My thoughts from my earlier review below:1. Story mode. This is the #1 criticism you see in steam reviews because it's still only got 1 chapter out of 8 (finale + Shanty) after almost THREE YEARS of this game "releasing" out of Early Access. There's no excuse at this point. Give people what they paid for. The devs chose to prioritize Level 3 supers and, generally, the competitive scene over finishing story mode. I can sort of understand them making Shanty (who was originally a DLC character), because the other most common criticism is that the roster is small, but delivering what they sold people should take priority. At this point, I think people should be getting refunds because they were not given the game that they paid for.2. The game balance is utter trash. The devs must have an unhealthy attraction to Oleander because they refuse to nerf her in any meaningful way. She's been top tier for the game's entire lifespan and just gets privileges that other characters don't. In the most recent patch, they made it so that Pom's dogs (puppets) can't attack if Pom's in blockstun, but Oleander's puppet, Fred, does not have that same restriction. Why? ♥♥♥♥ you, that's why! Though I'd argue that's not even the worst part.I mained Velvet when I played this game and enjoyed her a lot, but it became evident, even in my amateur eyes, that she was just blatantly worse than every other character in the cast. She has no ways to really open people up and is supposed to rely on chip damage to do most of the work, but her zoning requires resources to be good and even with said resources, every other character has tools that just invalidate half her moveset and force her to rely on her garbage normals, all of which are mids. The devs did buff her chip damage in 2.0, which was at least a step in the right direction, but what did they do to her most recently?They nerfed her. They nerfed the worst character in the game. Her ♥♥♥♥♥♥ DP, which requires a resource to even use and can be easily jumped over, was nerfed yet again to be even more minus and will now trade way more often, because god forbid this character be allowed to play or do anything at all. This nerf is made even worse by many universal changes in 3.0 that made defensive options way weaker. You can't tech roll safely, ever, you can't backdash on wakeup for 8 frames of invincibility to mix up your reversal timing, you just die now. Cross canter (alpha counter) was also gutted, where it was one of Velvet's few strengths thanks to her meter gain in 2.0. A lot of people didn't like these changes because matches tend to snowball way more than before, but for a character like Velvet who desperately needs to keep the opponent out, but can't do so reliably, having basically no defensive options makes her painful to play.3. Selling DLC when the game isn't finished is not okay, especially not after 3 years of being out of early access and promising people the game would be finished. I could forgive Shanty if the very next thing the devs did was Chapter 2, but that's not how things played out. Apparently, with Texas, they're going to add him as a boss fight to Chapter 1 and do something similar with future characters in the season pass. This just strikes me as pure scope creep. I also don't know why it took another 15 months for them to finish the level 3 supers after they showed them on a stream being basically finished, but that wouldn't have been a problem had they just prioritized story mode like they should have in the first place.Do not buy this game.

_childDocuments_.review: So this game is legit one of my favorite fighting games released recently. The only games I like as much or more are UNICLR and BlazBlue at this point but both have terrible netcode. This game has some of the best netcode in fighting games with one of the best training modes I've used in a fighting game. The tutorial is also one of the best in all of fighting games. TBH I can't really comment on the story mode but I've heard nothing but good stuff about it.  I would say that the biggest con is that the amount of players online is not as much as Tekken or Street Fighter but there's still plenty of people that wants to play online. The community can also be pretty helpful (not always true but that's multiplayer online). The game even has the ability to get combos from the community for practicePros- Amazing Training Mode- Complex but easy to understand Gameplay- Great Charm-Future  Updates to add More Features- Functional Lobbies- Entering Matches if Quick- Saltmines and Extra Features - Amazing SoundtrackCons- Lack of Single Player Modes outside of Story Mode - Competitive game makes it harder for players new to fighting games to enjoy- Only 6 characters (soon to be 7) - Lack of Ranked / Replay features (to be added) I'd say that the game can be hard for newer players to hop into but that can be alleviated by using the official discord for help and matches as a new player. Probably the best $15 I've spent on a game in a while and I'm glad that people are starting to see just how amazing it is.Edit: If you are new to fighting games and are currently struggling to learn it, please feel free to reach out to me or anyone in the discord. (mileage may vary however) I'm always willing to help new players.
