_childDocuments_.review: TFH is a fighting game with excellent player expression, quality of life (for its time), great animation and wonderful community sense. Some of its defining features are its fast paced grounded anime neutral and a solid blend of responsive play and broad RPS, with the system encouraging you to mix it up with every step so that it always feels fresh and entertaining to play and watch. Unique mechanics play into this well such as Juggle Decay, which encourages well placed risk-reward management, fast tempo resets and gives you the tools to starve the opponent of their resources whenever it's necessary. It's a lab monster's dream out here, parallels can be made to high level concepts in other fighting games in ways that hold up really well. It's hard to overstate how valuable this is to have as someone's first FG.That said, the 3.0/3.1 update has done its share of damage to the game and what makes it stand out from other fighting games. An effort was made to address what were considered issues with the game's meta with system changes that solely exist to limit what the player can and can't do in many different situations. There wasn't much of a focus put on how they feel, how intuitive for new players they are even with prior FG experience, and they negatively affect a number of the game's core dynamics that have held up well over the years. What I mentioned about Juggle Decay earlier is now a lot less relevant for most of the game's characters ontop of being less valuable overall, and on some characters the game rewards you for disregarding it entirely in favor of doing a single approach every time. I can't even shill the game by telling them about this dope mechanic anymore, only tell them about how good it used to be.Sure they addressed their problems with the meta but it's extremely hard to not feel the weight of these changes every time you play even when you're not trying to exploit them, and it can cause frustration more often than not due to the juxtaposition between the game's flexible foundations and these new restrictions. The update's implementation was not great and after a year has passed you'll still hear high level players express their discontent with how it was handled as well as at the lack of direction it gives to its players. An example I can give is the guard cancel rework, which was hooked up so that it encourages RPS exchanges after being used while at the same time punishing you for taking well calculated risks with the meter lockout  mechanic. Best I can say is to expect this sort of friction and try make peace with it.More recent changes to the game dealt with a particular pesky reversal and handled it in a way that actually encourages both the user and opponent to think and get creative about dealing with it across different scenarios while keeping its identity as a move intact, which was fantastic. It may be a sign of things improving from here. I still find this game to be worth recommending, it's worth coming to know and the community is absolutely stellar. The developers do a wonderful job and the QA/community managers are at least welcoming to discussion & feedback while putting in the work to make things go smoothly and the atmosphere feel lively.

_childDocuments_.review: Short review of Them's Fightin' Herds after the first hour I did some training and arcade mode.This is an indie fighting game, powered by Skullgirl's engine. The original name of the project was My Little Pony: Fighting Is Magic. An fan made game based on . They sadly had to stop the project, renamed it and change the characters, that's why the game was delayed. So, what we can find after those changes? A good fighting game, powered by the most interesting and latest 2D fighting game engine created by Lab 0 for Skullgirls.The main system of the game is close to Blazblue. 3 attacks levels (light, medium, strong attacks) and a 4th button for chara spec abilities. I don't remember abilities since I don't play enough, but the cow can throw a losso, the unicorn can charge the super bar, ect...Wait, did I speak about cow and unicorn in  a fighting game? Yes, they change My Little Pony's characters for 4 feet animals. That sounds logical indeed, but there is the originality of the game. Your hitbox is very different of others games, and you have to keep it in mind for your spacing.The only bad things are the soft feels unfinished yet, but it's an early access so this can change in future patches. Some animations are missing, sound can be delayed sometimes, and small things like this. Stages are not bad, but motionless/lifeless. Not a lot of characters for now, 6 playables chars and a boss wich is 4 animals (a bear, a snake, etc...) to beat with only one life bar.But because all of this can be fix in the near future, and because this is a cheap game, I highly recommend to go for it.

_childDocuments_.review: "The cow goes yeee" - Nov 25, 2021---------------------------------Nov 25 2023 Edit:As a long time follower and player of this game, the recent negative reviews have given me a good reason to give my own in depth review.TFH is a fantastic 2D fighter, and could be considered one of the most well-made fighting games of all time. It is more than worth the purchase price of $20 by providing a fun, fluid, and balanced fighter with GGPO rollback netcode and is (mostly) crossplatform. (More on that later.)Within the last week, the developers Mane6 announced that after they release the next two characters of the season pass, they will cease development on the game, except in the case of "game-breaking bugs." As of today, saying that the game has ceased development or is dead is not true. However, this means that the majority of story mode, a goal promised in the Indiegogo campaign, will not be finished. The devs have not given any reasoning and have said they are not at liberty to say anything more. I have followed the devs' communication since day 1, and I know that this is not like them at all. I can only assume they are under NDA from their publisher Modus. It would be extremely inconsistent for Mane6 to want to stop developing TFH or feel no need to explain their actions.Regardless, this does affect the value of the game depending on what kind of player you are. If you want it for story mode, sorry; for the foreseeable future it won't be happening. If you want a good fighting game, it is and will continue to be a great value even after active development ceases. The devs always intended for the game to be playable even after they are dead and gone. Fights are peer-to-peer, and lobbies can be hosted by anyone. Unless they fix crossplay on independent servers, though; that will only be possible on the game's official servers—the future of which is unsure. The game's playablility will ultimately be determined by you, however. Buy the game, join a discord, get some friends to play with you, etc.; and you will add value to the game. In full disclosure, the game's active playerbase is currently shrinking slowly; but if for that reason you decide to quit or not buy the game, you are only cementing that further.Setting aside this recent drama, let's look at the fighting portion of this game. It's phenomenal!  Visuals and sounds are pleasing with good feedback. Characters are unique with a broad range of playstyles. Combos and attacking are beginner friendly while maintaining a lot of nuance. The soundtrack is amazing and the game has a dynamic music system. Online play is smooth as butter. Training mode has many useful features, and combos + replays can be saved and shared (on PC). The tutorial is also the best FG tutorial out there, teaching universal concepts along with specifics to the game. The community has also always been receptive to new players and there will always be people willing to help.Negatives: A few moves are not visually consistent with their hitboxes. It can be played around just fine but makes some interactions feel bad. That's all I can think of.tldr; Play TFH

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: Since I reviewed this game 2 years ago, there have been plenty of updates, including the long-awaited arrival of Story Mode (Chapter 1, at least), tutorials (including in-depth concepts such as frame data, advantage, and negative edging, which is very useful to newcomers), and quick matches. The cons from this review have pretty much been eliminated, and I am also happy to see this game get a resurgence, _especially_ given the current state of the game. The review below will be left for posterity, but know that it is now outdated. (Also, paprika is _still_ best. {•ᴗ•} )TL;DR: A cute exterior with well-polished mechanics complex enough to be engaging, but not so overwhelming as to be unwelcoming to new fighter players.Pros:+ Built on Lab Zero's engine (Same as Skullgirls)+ Very well done aesthetic and art direction+ Normals feel very snappy and satisfying+ Not too focused on infinite or super-long combos (see: skullgirls)+ Each character has a distinct playstyle and character feel+ Pixel Lobby has a PvE environment to grind out cosmetics for Pixel Lobby (TF2 fans, go nuts)+ Various QoL things, like context menus for pixel lobby on chat with controller, or keyboard chat+ The soundtrack is surprisingly good+ Each character has a well-established personality, and this combined with the aforementioned playstyles make each character stand out and feel uniqueCons:- AI (as of this review) is overtuned, and the gaps between difficulties are staggering- Art is currently unfinished with certain vfx (e.g. Oleander's Magic Teleport) being rendered in animatics- Online matchmaking is limited to lobbies (as of this review)- No story mode as of yet- Extra cosmetics (i.e. Skullgirls, Blazblue, et al.) only are obtained if you have the "full" game (second encore for skullgirls, rev 2 for xrd, etc) [this is in the fine print but just in case people get confused]- No tutorial (however, there is training mode, and there are combo lists within training that you can practice)Overall, the game is very well done for an Early Access title, and I feel like the state of the game can only improve over time. If you are just starting out at fighters, maybe wait until the AI gets fixed, or persuade a few friends to help you learn, but this is a very enjoyable experience for those who are even remotely interested in fighters, while also having enough detail and potential to be mastered by veterans.(p.s. Paprika is best ' ͜ > ' )

_childDocuments_.review: Game was announced and started development in 2013.This game was supposed to be released in 2015 after completing a successful crowd funding drive. They raised enough money even for their stretch goals to add a story mode.It's now 2023 and the game is being abandoned unfinished after a decade with only the beginning of the first chapter of the story mode added.---This isn't normally a genre I dabble in and it's not a storyline I would have invested in (and I didn't). Personally I ended up with a key from a random bundle that cost me less than $1. But since I ended up with it, I'm gonna review it.1. The story for me is nonsense. It obviously has a target audience, I'm just not it. I wouldn't hold this against it really since it's pretty obvious from the store page what they were aiming for.2. The gameplay has two types. Mediocre 2d fighting for the combat and super-basic RPG-Maker style for the story mode exploration. I don't know how a story mode this simple should be incomplete after all these years unless the developers simply flat out ignored the game for most of those years. I've seen amateurs put out RPG maker games like this that were longer and more complete after just a few months, let alone an entire decade.3. Without the story mode (which is what many of the core fans invested in specifically during crowd funding) what's here is a 2d arcade fighter with 4 legged animals. It's OK, but I find myself winning just by button mashing without really needing to put much thought into it other than occasionally blocking. It's functional, but not impressive.As I said, I had no expectations for this, I didn't seek it out and buy it and I wasn't an early investor like so many others. It was just a cheap random key for me. But when I play things I look into them and try to get a broader perspective. I could probably have found an excuse to give this an upvote if it was a complete game. But it's not and with it being abandoned it never will be.The animations, story (what little there is) and voice acting would probably all be OK for someone who enjoys this style and genre, there just isn't much of it. Or rather, it would be OK for a game from the early 2010 time period. It certainly doesn't feel like a game from 2020.I'll probably finish grinding out the achievements, uninstall and forget it exists.---Bottom line: A mediocre 2d Arcade fighter with an amateur tacked on RPG maker story mode that isn't even complete.---

_childDocuments_.review: This game was well worth the multi-year wait for it. The animations are solid, the voice acting beautiful and the fighting fluid and quick. This is definitely a combo fighter's game for sure.Pros:-Music is amazing and the dynamic music system runs almost flawlessly-Pixel lobby is a great way to experience and explore the realms, though I wish there was more to do in them. It's early access so can't expect a huge amount.-Fighting is crisp and fluid, though the characters feel a bit heavy at times. Makes your hits seem sharper and more damaging, but it makes it a bit harder to start and maintain decent combos.-Lauren Faust's designs are beautiful, the voice acting is spot on, and the multiple color pallate options give each character a sense of personalization that you don't get from other games where characters may only have 2-6 colors.Cons:-The game, especially the arcade mode AI, is insanely unforgiving for inexperienced players. Combos can be hard to get started and maintain, and when you are trapped in an AI's combo it ranges from hard to downright impossible to break free without taking around 20-30 hits.- Some content is missing, though the developers are upfront about it and what we have avaliable is well worth the price of admission. This isn't a critism as much as it is me wanting that missing content (Story Mode, Quick Match, etc.)- The roster is small. This doesn't bother me in the slightest because there is so much to learn in the game I could spend hundreds of hours learning and mastering the movesets of the 6 characters. Would I like to see more characters and lore in the future, of course. What we have however is amazing.- Just not enough to do in the pixel lobby right now.All in all TFH is an amazing game, well worth the journey from Fighting Is Magic, and I really hope to see more content and more tweaking in the future. If you don't mind a little bit of missing content and can handle the large number of times you might get your butt kicked, then this is the game for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Heard this game had some good stuff in it for beginners so I gave it a purchase. Didn't find that to be the case. Game's very stiff. Most characters can't dash, no air dashes, no dodge rolls. No "quality of life" mechanics in it at all really. First impression was that it was unusually combo heavy based on the fact the standard chain combo is A>B>C>Launch>A>B>C. Seemed like a strange choice if it's a beginner game. What I played of the Tutorial was pretty standard and the story mode forces game mechanics on you in a way that I found quite unpleasant. For example you fight some wolves that seem to only be vulnerable to anti-air attacks. Had to actively fight my instincts to Anti-Air instead of block and punish like I would if I were playing normally. If you buy I recommend going into arcade, online or story right away to see how you feel about it. I blew my refund chance trying the characters in practice and doing the tutorial. By the time I was actually playing the game it was already over 2 hours. So don't do that. (Never wanted to refund a fighter before so I didn't realize how long my standard process takes to actually get to the game)TL;DR: Stiff game play, not very beginner friendly, awkward story mode.EDIT: I found a friend to play it with and have improved my opinion of the game. Still think story mode stinks. It's like playing the annoying cheap boss at the end of arcade mode except it's every fight. But the gameplay is okay and relatively accessible compared to other games like this. (other games like this being Skullgirls and to a lesser extent the Versus games)I discovered there are combo trials out of Training Mode, and I can give those a glowing review. They're actually useful (not just for challenge like trials usually are) and you can download new ones from the community. Excellent feature.The game has recovery rolls and teching in it, which is something I struggled with. I'm used to not having wake up options and having more to worry about in that respect gave me trouble. To put it another way I'm used to the mix-up/Oki starting when I wake up, not when I'm in the air or just hitting the ground. Less time to think and I have no experience with that kind of mix-up.PS: voice clips are great, would giggle again.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games that I tentatively recommend. It's well put together with great visuals, music, and even character design, but it also lacks what a good fighting game should have: a decent roster. Now, I understand the direction to an extent, they wanted to make a smaller cast of more unique fighters instead of a bunch of interchangeble ones like how most fighting games end up having it, and in that regard, they succeeded. The six fighters present at launch do fill very different niches well, but the thing is, that's still only six fighters in the roster. Even Skullgirls, a game that went a similar route with its roster, still had eight characters from the start, and many more added later.So then, even with the one chracter planned to be added to Fightin' Herds, that still only gives us seven, and six or seven fighters does not create a very varied match expierence. With only six fighters, I expect the game to grow stale quickly, and thus I think it's only a good purchase on signifigant sale. I'd say at least 25% off.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: On November 22th it has been officially announced that there will be no more Development for the game once season 1 is done, and that Story mode is officially cancelled, after lying for years that it was coming. _childDocuments_.review: Edit: At the time of writing this review, it was in the early stage before Shanty came out. I'll not change the "recommendation" due to Mane6 deserving better... but I would suggest you hold off from purchasing this game until it is given back to the original development team.I did pick the game on Humble Bundle. Spoiler alert: awesome work from Mane6!After playing a couple matches online, taking a look at the Tutorial and practicing the different characters, I can honestly say that Them's Fightin' Herds is worthy of attention.Let's start with the odds: the characters all look comically absurd because they are animals fighting each other. You have a cow, a sheep, a reindeer, a flame horse, a unicorn and an alpaca. Much like Skullgirls, they are female (and yes, Skullgirls now has two male characters but that's not the point) and are fully-voiced with pre-fight taunts. Lauren Faust has also contributed to the design of these characters so if you're a My Little Pony: Friendship is Magic fan, you'll be at home.This game feels extremely fluid and responsive yet like every fighting game, Fightin' Herds will take a lot of time to understand if you're a newcomer. Thankfully, Mane6 has come up with an incredible tutorial that will allow you to go through the basics and, if you're wise and take your time to read and get past the comedy, you'll eventually learn the concepts of the fighting game genre allowing you to understand the basics and apply them in other games of the genre.The training mode is Skullgirls level of genius (it's the same engine) with frame data, attack data, hitboxes and input display which, in a modern fighting game, is required and most welcome. Each character has a Magic button for different mechanics with Supers to be spent over the match. You have three buttons like in Injustice with Light, Medium and Heavy Attacks and an universal launcher for Juggle Combos. Of course, you have defensive options like blockpush, perfect blocking (more daunting than it sounds) and different ways to get your character up post-knockdown. There's a level of depth that is explained and worth practicing.While this game does compete with Skullgirls for the value proposition, Fightin' Herds is a passion project worth supporting thanks to its odd and funny characters but the crowning achievement is the implementation of the excellent GGPO netcode in the same style as Skullgirls (now featuring GGPO) and the incredible rollback system featured in Killer Instinct. The online matches have been quick, fluid and soul-crushing because I've yet to figure out my own combos, parts of the system for me to fully grasp and the craziness that is happening on screen.If you are a fighting game fan and you wanna send a message to the editors, Fightin' Herds is that message! And it's an excellent product. Yes, you can criticize the amount of characters but even Killer Instinct and Skullgirls started with less characters. Fightin' Herds is on par with Skullgirls and Killer Instinct as the best fighting games you can play online with friends or simply for learning the basics of the genre without feeling intimidated by poor explanation.

_childDocuments_.review: + The tutorials are extensive, covering system and character specific mechanics as well those that can be applied across all fighting games.+ Soundtrack has some bangers+ Netcode is excellent+ PVE sidegame in the online lobby is a fun distraction and well implemented+ Story mode is charming and also teaches you how to play- Small cast (6 as of this review)- Combo routes feel restricted (overall), particularly if you've going for optimized routesI think TFH as a package has absolutely worth $15 (and more). That said, as a fighter I feel it's severely limited by it's roster. While each member of the cast has a distinct play-style, if you don't feel yourself meshing with any of them,  you'll quickly find yourself bored (like I did).Overall, I think 1.0 serves as a strong base for whatever the devs plan to do with it. Definitely a game I'll be keeping an eye going forward.
_childDocuments_.name: Them's Fightin' Herds

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not going to pretend to be good at this game(or fighting games in general). But having said that theres still fun in this game to be had, even for a casual player whom may have never been into fighting games before (such as myself). Between the charming charters and quirky dialogue the game just oozes with charm and personality that can make even losing occasionally bring a smile to my face just to hear different characters quips. Though that's not to say the game is shallow, far from it. Like any good fighter their is depth in how characters play and have to change play styles between different matchups(though i'm probably not the person to speak too on all those intraciese, but as someone whos just a passive observer I can tell you I can even see a few). All this is to say if your looking for something to sink your teeth into and practice to “get good”  without worrying about the frustration failure this is a great game for it, as the community is nothing but kind and will provide dozens of helpful pointers(while kicking your a** of course). Whether it be against bots, people, win or lose you're sure to find enjoyment. It truly does feel like a passion project of people whom have a clear love for their product. The only game I can think of that manages to do this same thing is Team fortress 2(in reference to how community and the charming nature of the setting can help stop frustration and make it fun to learn). P.s: while i'm in the subject, give this game “the best soundtrack”, it really is a banger, really listen to it yourself if you haven't heard it. I can think of few other game soundtracks I love as much as this, plus the deves deserve some kind of acknowledgement for the hard work they put into this wonderful game.

name: The Outer Worlds
detailed_description: The Outer Worlds is an award-winning single-player first-person sci-fi RPG from Obsidian Entertainment and Private Division. Lost in transit while on a colonist ship bound for the furthest edge of the galaxy, you awake decades later only to find yourself in the midst of a deep conspiracy threatening to destroy the Halcyon colony. As you explore the furthest reaches of space and encounter various factions, all vying for power, the character you decide to become will determine how this player-driven story unfolds. In the corporate equation for the colony, you are the unplanned variable. KEY FEATURES The player-driven story RPG In keeping with the Obsidian tradition, how you approach The Outer Worlds is up to you. Your choices affect not only the way the story develops; but your character build, companion stories, and end game scenarios. You can be flawed, in a good way New to The Outer Worlds is the idea of flaws. A compelling hero is made by the flaws they carry with them. While playing The Outer Worlds, the game tracks your experience to find what you aren't particularly good at. Keep getting attacked by Raptidons? Taking the Raptiphobia flaw gives you a debuff when confronting the vicious creatures, but rewards you with an additional character perk immediately. This optional approach to the game helps you build the character you want while exploring Halcyon. Lead your companions During your journey through the furthest colony, you will meet a host of characters who will want to join your crew. Armed with unique abilities, these companions all have their own missions, motivations, and ideals. It's up to you to help them achieve their goals, or turn them to your own ends. Explore the corporate colony Halcyon is a colony at the edge of the galaxy owned and operated by a corporate board. They control everything... except for the alien monsters left behind when the terraforming of the colony’s two planets didn’t exactly go according to plan. Find your ship, build your crew, and explore the settlements, space stations, and other intriguing locations throughout Halcyon.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like Fallout New Vegas or Borderlands, this is if they met and had the most beautiful baby that ever rampaged through a space colony. Outer Worlds has fantastic characters and dialogue, with I don't even know how many ways to play and beat the game. Great open spaces to explore, lore to find, stuff to steal, and lots of enemies to blast through. It's just a hell of a ride!
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this, but with some precautions. Is it fun? Yes. I found the gameplay very satisfying and fun. Does it deliver a decent RPG experience where I feel I am using my skills I invested in? Yes, and very much so in conversation for speech skills. Is the world building good? Here is where we come to the complicated spot. IT CAN BE GOOD, but it can also pull you out terribly. There are definitely spots where you can feel like the writers devoted way too much time to one thing, and way too little to a broad spectrum of things. The tongue in cheek humor can be a little much at times, so be prepared for that. The characters are exactly as surface level basic as they seem. The world kind of just sucks aside from the atmosphere created by color palette and change of fauna and flora. TL;DRIt's Fallout/Mass Effect/Bioshock in space with no actual space travel. You just go from one planet landing pad to another. Underwhelming story. Still fun.6.8/10 Will probably play again. Couldn't give it an even 76/10    Would describe to a friend and let them decide for themselves. Half-recommend
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not only funny, but your choices natter immensely! You can permanently kill people in the game, even the people that help you advance the story. If you do kill said person, the game with often provide you with sometimes simpler but most times a much more round about way of doing thing. The amount of freedom in the is game is amazing! And no, its not technically open world per se, but the planet maps you have to explore is pretty big, and there are so many places to go you just could just explore for hours. Also, the dialog options had me dying sometimes in laughter to the point of tears  just because your owned by corporations as property, not ppl so its like a dystopian future but highly satirical as well

_childDocuments_.review: My favorite game of 2021. From the minor things you find in logs and audio actually coming up in conversation, to the unique flow of how the characters you can ally with come together and grow into their own throughout the campaign, but then with the replay-ability of being able to take SO MANY different paths. from psychopathic barbarian to honorable sniper, there is just so much to do in more than one play-through.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, it's not that I dislike this game, it's just not all that. It's also actually really difficult to write this review since I have a LOT of mixed feelings about it. 1. The game is really well written. From the game world to the dialogs and all the different options and consequences and reactions you can get exploring it. HOWEVER, this does not translate to the main quest. While the idea is interesting, it's very short and it doesn't feel urgent and they mostly make a very bad job of making you care about it. 2. The characters have the exact same problem. While you get -some- backstory, it's just that. Mostly, their companion quests are not related to it (some kinda are) and, when they are, it's all very shallow. Shallow is the word I would use to describe the companions in general. You don't care about them, you're not involved in their lives, they only exist to be your meat shields. Their banter is uninteresting while on the party and, when on the ship, it lets you know they're arguing, but you can only be a spectator. After they finish talking/fighting they will only go their own ways, not even acknowledging your presence. Also, and that's a very personal opinion, having them wearing their cumbersome armor while on the ship is really absurd and kinda breaks me out of the story.3. The combat is ridiculous. I usually play every game on normal, so that's what I did. Other than the first two hours, where I was getting used to the controls, it's all very basic. I'm not usually good at shooters and I always play sneaky sniper. But this! THIS!  First off, the sneak doesn't work for combat, first shot and EVERYONE knows where you are, doesn't matter if you're behind a wall, or THEY are behind three walls, they know EXACTLY where you are. Not kinda know your area, they know it EXACTLY. And don't think that using a silencer helps, no no no. It's the same to the end of the game, what a silencer does is, maybe, call only half of the base to you, instead of the whole thing. But still, it is SO EASY that it doesn't really matter, just as it doesn't matter who you're taking with you. You don't have to strategize, just take who you like and it's gonna work flawlessly because everything melts when you shoot it. Seriously, just play it on hard. (BUT, and that MAKES ME SO MAD, the sneak works ABSURDLY well out of combat, you can breeze past people as long as they have their backs to you, no matter the noise you make. I rolled my eyes so hard I'd have sprained them if that was possible.)All in all, this is...ok. It has a lot of flaws which didn't allow me to enjoy it and I kept putting it off and making excuses not to play it, but it may suit some audiences. I just expected a much more in-depth story out of such a heavy dialog-based story. There's a LOT of reading to be done and I was hoping for at least some... feels? Maybe at least some sympathy for my people? Anyway, I couldn't connect, but it's not an absolutely lost cause. If you get it, do it on sale. 6/10.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: If you loved Fallout New Vegas, you will love this game! It has the same feeling even tho it's in space. The crafting system works great and gaining flaws is a fun mechanic! You cannot help compare it to Fallout, since it's so similar. Which is why the only thing i miss is Fallout 4's base building and 1 large map. This game has a bunch of smaller maps on, sometimes more on some planets, which works for the game, but there's less "going off the beaten path" when the maps are smaller.All in all, a wonderful game with great voice acting and amazing story!
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: Everything you do is just meaningless. Almost every character doesnt have any emotions so you just dont care at all about the quests. All people have almost the same player model, even some 60 year elder characters have just the standard player model with some modification of the skin surface in their face. In the dialogs nobody is doing anything, they just stand static in front of each other, focusing the camera straight to both faces. It doesnt matter if you tell a mother you rescued her son, or you killed em. Its so static that you simply dont care. You can feel the low budget almost at every single corner. The gameplay itself isnt good as well, you have a nice amount of weapons with different levels, therefore you always collect all items you find and just scroll threw everything looking for higher numbers in level.The first planet with Spacers Choice Fraction was fun and solid written, but after the first 10 hours the writings were worse and its boring as hell. Parvati is pretty good written and Max is okay, the rest of your companions are just meaningless. They all follow you for absolutely no reason and you simple dont care about the companion quests. Thats the problem with the game, you simply dont care after some hours. Its not that one big point is bad, its just that you dont want to play the game any longer because everything is so irrelevant
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the game, and what a ride. I defintely recommend the game.Reasons to play:- The main story (and side stories) are relatable and engaging. The story is quite grey and it is to you to make the decisions of how things are going to unfold. Choices feel like they have impact, narratively at least, not so much in actual gameplay per se- Many different viable playstyles. The devs really want it so you play like you wan to. You can play super sneaky and charismatic if you want and this way avoid many confrontations and the like. Melee-tank is super cool too and the deadly sniper or heavy weapon plus shotty. It is all viable and fun to play. For example, when you do not have a very good combat build, you can actually skip the (only) bossbattle in the game if you have maximium lockpicking. - Progression and combat feels very right. At start of the game you are pretty weak, but when you play it with some actual thought and start to upgrade yuo really start feeling like a baddass. Finding better weapons feels great and powerful, while still being vunerable when you start blazing without really regards. Enemies will kill you when you are not careful, and I like this danger which makes that feeling of being a badass feel worth.- All quests are handcrafted and felt good to do. There are many secrets alll around for the observant and patient players.- The environments are beautifull and detailed, although a little too vibrant in a way for me somehow, so I turned some of the details down... personal preference - The game is not open world and smaller than a fallout game. This is not really an issue but it does lower that sense of scale somewhat. Also the game ends somewhat short. But it does not diminish the quality since there is no filler content.

_childDocuments_.review: It's all a bit meh - 5/10. Is it fun to play? Yes, fairly. Would I recommend it to a friend? Only if it was discounted.The good bits: The graphics are great. You can customise your character and your companion's weapons, armour and abilities. The weapon/damage type does make a difference in combat. The game is pretty mindless to play (which definitely has a time and place - especially after a long day at work) - but that's about it.The bad bits: There isn't much to the game (feels unfinished/rushed)- very few types of enemies. Not many places to explore and those you can explore feel repetitive. The main quest line is short and it ended abruptly. There are lots of "go and fetch" side quests. It's riddled with NPCs you just don't care able/are boring. Not enough content to get you to level 30 (which has an achievement - so is unnecessarily annoying). After a few hours the whole thing feels a bit like a chore rather than a game. I will continue playing it until I get all the achievements, but once I've done this it'll immediately be uninstalled and never played again. Hope this helps. Happy gaming!

Yeah, I say it now - I even stopped playing Cyberpunk 2077 (which is by far not a bad game, imho) to continue my over the top space journey!

_childDocuments_.review: I would like to make a neutral review. (I've played it using microsoft game pass for many hours)- not as interesting as Fallout: NV (I don't feel like i want to explore bcs there is very few things to find outside of the main roads on maps)+ more impressive than Fallout 4 (many ideas are the same, but with better implementation)- on Supernova difficulty it's hard to keep your companions alive bcs of poor AI (they are just rushing enemies and die after few shots)+ really cool world design (I mean it's absolutely new world, not like a post-nuclear-war world)- poor level design (mostly the same structure of levels with nothing to explore, you always know where to go for cool stuff)+ very cool flaws idea (you can exchange some stats for new perk, e.g. you are afraid of falling)- very poor perks (they are mostly absolutely useless)+ cool weapons (guns design is pretty, and the game has science guns with special abilities)- poor weapons variety (at some point you just get SomeWeaponName mk2, and will mostly use 1-2  guns for the whole walk-through)+ jokes (I like jokes)- not that much of choices and ways to finish a mission (mostly it looks like a "choice" in particular mission is just for illusion that your choice matters)+ reps with fractions (so you decide which fraction-vision is most suitable for you)- reps are very easy to earn (and do nothing except for discounts\attack-on-sight)+ mode with starving\thirsting\sleep-need (it's pretty immersive imo)- you cant choose it for any difficulty, only for 'supernova' one (so you can't sleep outside of your bed and you can't fast travel also)----- released on Steam after 20194281094 years (I have like almost any Obsidian's game on the Steam account)I love the attempt but there is a lot of things to improve. AND RELEASE ON STEAM NEXT TIME, PLEASE!

_childDocuments_.review: Good game with a fun story with some real RPG choice and consequence. The over-the-top anti consumerism/rampant capitalism satire is pretty fun, through gets a bit oversaturated after a time. The worlds are pretty well made and interesting to explore but not quite to the caliber of the Fallout and Mass Effect games. Dialogue and characters are probably better for the most part. Weapons and armor are a bit disappointing in that they feel very un-unique. In general I think that loot in The Outer Worlds has the same issue that the newer Fallout games have in which randomized loot drops/finds are very humdrum and nothing ever seems like a big, game changing find. Where the first 2 Fallout games were able to work in completely unique items (albeit with the possibility of completely unbalancing the game), and Diablo managed to make complete randomness in drops compelling decades ago no one has really done it right since. Ultimately if you enjoyed KOTOR, Mass Effect, and Fallout, you'll probably like this too.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: In a nutshell: The game is a mixture of Fallout and Mass Effect, but it doesn't reach the class of either game. Gameplay is solid and includes classic RPG elements, such as leveling system, crafting, companions, but I personally found it too easy (played on hard). The world is interesting, but too small. The same goes for the story. Basically interesting, but too short, even if you do side missions. Overall, I think it's ok, but it doesn't reach the quality of the games from which it was inspired. It's definitely not worth the full price, buy it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of people have bad things to say about this game, having put around 50 hours in my first ever play-through I have found little that disappoints. This game has so much depth. I found the dialogue enticing, the gun-play is incredibly fun, quests are well put together (Some are short and pointless, and some, like The Electric Fling in Peril On Gorgon are eternally broken, one of the few bad things I have to say.) Overall, this is a great title and shows what obsidian is capable of. If you're looking into this game, I highly recommend it for the experience, though the DLC is necessary, it's worth every dollar.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a very pretty game, but tedious. The story is lackluster, and has little depth or plot twists. Combat is weird - i restarted after spending 2-3 hours in story mode, it was just excessively easy. Combat is either insanely fast and overwhelming, or super dull - pew pew pew you're dead, next.I completed the game on normal difficulty and then deleted it off the hdd.  The slow time trick is great for folks with slower reflexes, did enjoy that mechanic.Maybe get it on a 80-90% off sale, otherwise, dont bother.

_childDocuments_.review: [SHREDVIEW] – From someone who actually plays and finish the games before he reviews them. The Outer Worlds  – If Borderlands and Bioshock had a baby.- About the game:If you’re a Borderlands Fan than you should definitely try “The Outer Worlds”. The reason I’m mentioning another game in reference to this one is because its abundancy in humour and silliness along with its spatial setup roamed by humans, marauders and alien wildlife is something I’ve met before. Inspired from one of my favorite FPS saga or not, it stands out with it’s meticulously story driven gameplay experience and characters that are extremely well developed each. I found “The Outer Worlds” to be a joyful ride soaked in beautiful use of graphics, from merely killing an enemy to exploring every corner of the map. - Gameplay:Upon starting you get hit with a Skyrim take on character creation although not offering as much variety, then you pick a name for yourself which will also be used in all Dialogue segments along the story. THE GAME HAS A VERY GOOD AND WELL WRITTEN STORY: The story surrounds a character that was part of a colonial ship containing Earth’s Brightest minds which was sent on a mission to aid the newly terraformed solar system where all the action takes place. In the first hour of gameplay you’ll also be granted your own Space Ship which later on becomes your mobile base of operations and unlock / recruit 5 very unique companions as your crew. The point of the story is to rescue the rest of the geniuses aboard “The Hope”, your former colleagues and friends from the hands of greedy corporations that plunged the colony into a steep decline. As you’re slashing and shooting through the campaign, you get introduced to a lot of Borderlands similarities which will make the game very easy to get along it (Take note! They’re not exactly the same but you get my point). The gameplay circles around the following mechanics:1.	LOOT SYSTEM:•	Ingredients (Game uses an inhaler system with 4 slots max in which you mix up different ingredients with or without different effects, this is how you heal or get yourself drunk and high)•	Weapon/Armor Parts (These are used to repair your gear)•	Weapon attachments (Every weapon has 3 slots which can all be filled at one time) – Somewhat similar to BL Elemental damage.•	Armor modifiers (Every armor has 4 slots which can all be filled at one time) – Somewhat similar to BL Shield•	Junk (Sellable Items, stuff you loot only to sell for currency)•	Vending Machines – Somewhat similar to BL but there’s not as much variety, definitely not as much as you would expect. 2.	CHARACTER DEVELOPMENT:•	Skill Attributes (Intelligence, Lockpick, Hacking, Dialogue Skills such as Persuasion, Intimidation), Weapon Skills, Stealth Skills, etc. SOME OF THESE ARE CRUCIAL IN MAKING YOUR LIFE EASIER, study before you play)•	Perk Points (You also get a perk point tree which you can adapt to your playstyle)•	COMPANION System (You can take up to 2 max companions in every adventure which give you a lot of bonuses)•	Map with “Fast Travel from Anywhere” •	Faction Reputation System (You get attacked on sight or reduced prices depending on reputation with the faction, there’s a good variety of factions in the game)•	Decision taking and dialogue handling affects the storyline.This should provide enough insight to decide whether it floats your boat or not, I loved this game and done 2 playthroughs for the achievements including both DLC’s. I highly recommend this game to anyone looking for a casual single player adventure. As every game it has goods and bads but definitely nothing to stay in your way of playing the game. Pay attention! The game is as I said, extremely STORY DRIVEN, one if it’s cons for me is that 70% of the gameplay I spent talking to NPC’s but I still went through without issues, you can also spam Enter and don’t give a ****. With all this said: “It’s not the best choice, it’s Sacer’s Choice”[PROS and CONS]PROS:-	Amazing Graphics, well optimized. For my setup, had constant 60FPS with no drops. -	Choices influence the Story outcome. -	You can switch direction of an elevator mid-air (that saves so much time, love it)-	Companions intervene in discussions with actually great input and each of them is unique in their way.-	Excellent character development for all NPC’s related to questing. -	Easy to master, friendly interface, menu, inventory, map. -	Straight forward quest objectives. Can also toggle Inactive Quests in map in case you missed anything. -	Attribute Skills actually influence character’s reputation or presence and also influences other NPC’s behavior.-	Very few cutscenes and skip-able (Done a great job for a game like this to have such limited amount of cutscene)-	Great loading screen design, fairly fast, was not a problem. -	DLC’s were excellent, game actually tags all quests with different colors to know which are from dlc and which from main game, I found this feature amazing. -	Characters curse and it’s not censored! Good job, rare sight with all this Disney s**t. This gives a lot of color to a character.CONS:-	So much f***g dialogue. I get that it’s based on interactions and characters but holy s**t.-	Combat could’ve been way more challenging, it gets linear and predictable. -	You cannot really freely climb stuff you get an open world experience. -	Give me more weapon variety (2 snipers, 2 shotguns, 2 plasma guns, a grenade launcher, 2 rifles, 1 light machine gun, 1 heavy machine gun and some science weapons which kinda suck) -	Give me more stats variety on armors and upgrades.-	Why have 2 planets in the solar system just to be grayed out. There’s reddit threads about it, of course I want to travel there, it’s in my face all the time, duh. -	Could use more character diversity (looks wise, most women if not all are short haired, most men have the same faces)- All the politics and humor gets kinda old and boring as you go on. [SHORT STATS]☐ Has CO-OP / Multiplayer☐ ONLINE CO-OP☐ Online Multiplayer☐ SPLIT SCREEN☑ NO•	GRAPHICS:☐ Fire the designer.☐ Fairly old game, what you expect?☐ Decent☐ Great☑ Eye Candy•	REPLAYABILITY:☐ YES☑ EVERY NOW AND THEN☐ NOT SURE☑ RARELY / ON MAJOR UPDATE / DLC RELEASE☐ NO •	STEAM ACHIEVEMENTS:☑ YES☐ NO•	GAMEPLAY:☐ WTF IS THIS ♥♥♥♥☐ TERRIBLE☐ DECENT☐ ENGAGING ☑  HAD A BLAST•	DIFFICULTY☐ DARK SOULS☐ BAFFLING☑ CHALLENGING☐ MEDIUM☐ WALK IN THE PARK•	STORYLINE:☐ A WHAT? _childDocuments_.review: I planned to write this review a bit later, after I finish the game.But as the game is currently being included in the Humble Bundle this month - I decided to write the review early, to help people decide if this game is for them.This game was created by Obsidian entertainment, the creators of Fallout: New Vegas (and of course the original Fallout games).Which creates pretty high expectations of them from the get go.If we compare Fallout 3 (Bethesda) to New Vegas (Obsidian) - we see that Obsidian are much better in storytelling, side quests and humor.But on the other hand, F:NV had loading screens every time you switched locations - while F3 and F4 contained a huge open world.Looking at this game: it is also an open world RPG in a futuristic setting (which begs the comparison to F:NV), but this time it's also an original IP from Obsidian.And I must say, it fares pretty well.Not perfect - but still, pretty well...RPG elementsFirst of all weapons - there are 4 categories of weapons (melee, light, heavy, long), of each you have sub-divisions (for example: 1-handed & 2-handed melee weapons, light handguns, rifles and machineguns, etc.).In addition there are also 4 categories of damage (blast, plasma, corrosion, N-rays), which can be applies to any gun in the game.Each weapon starts with a basic version, and as the game progresses (and you level up) you can find additional (stronger) versions of the same weapon.In addition, there are "unique" versions of weapons, which you cannot mod, but have special mods already installed.And on top of that, there are completely unique (science) weapons which you find usually after doing special quests - which have unique death mechanics unlike any other weapons in the game.And on top of that - there are 3 mod categories for ranged weapons, 2 categories for melee weapons and 4 categories for armor.And speaking of armor - there too you have variety, with different bonuses and debuffs, and progression over the game.So weapon and armor-wise - you have an amazing variety of different and interesting weapons. And weapon-crafting in itself is a game-within-a-game.Skills-wise, you have several levels of skills distribution you can choose from, when creating your character.During the game, when you level up, you have both skill points and perks/bonuses you can choose from.And every 20 skill points, you can an additional perk/bonus to that skill.In addition, you are occasionally offered to take a debuff, in exchange for an extra perk/bonus point.And on top of that, you also have the ability to redistribute your points (for a small fee) during the game, if you discover you did not distribute well enough, or you decide to try a different build mid-game.So skills-wise, the game also offers a large and interesting variety.In addition, you have up to 2 followers you can take with you.And the followers have bonus points of their own for you to distribute, and weapons and armor they can use.And if you choose to go solo - there are perks that give bonuses to builds without followers.So overall, as you can see, the Role Playing element of this game is very well made, and is one of the strongest points of the game.Open WorldOne the one hand, in open world games you want a big map. And the game is pretty huge here.You have several planets you can visit - each with it's own biome. And each will building or even whole towns you can explore.And some planets you can land on different parts of the planet, and get different maps in each.Or sometimes land in different locations on the same (huge) planet map.On the other hand, many buildings and cities you visit, are not actually part of the same map (in-game) and require loading times when moving from/to them.Also on a less positive side: there is almost no diversity in creatures. Same creatures can be found on every planet.Over all the planets there are only 2 distinct species of creatures (ape-types and arachnid-types). (and 1 more in one of the DLCs) In addition to humans and robots, which can be found throughout the game, but besides being togher in late game (deadlier and harder to kill), they remain pretty much the same (same weapon types, same armor, same loot, etc.)Story / QuestsOn the positive side:This game epitomizes the cornerstone of any Open World RPG - (almost) every quest can be solved in few different ways.You can go in guns blazing.Or talk your way out of a fight.Or sneak in and do what is needed without being discovered.And as an added bonus: More often that not, you can negotiate your reward after finishing a quest (if you pass the required skill checks).And also, as was tradition in Fallout games - this game also has a sense of humor.There are plenty of easter eggs scattered about in the world.And in general - many of the quests have a funny side to them.Now to the less positive side, I've seen mentioned in other reviews as well.The plot/story here is simply weaker than Fallout. I'm not sure what's the reason. If the world is just less interesting because it's too much apart from ours.Or maybe the writing is not as engaging. Or the factions are not very thought out.But the bottom line is - as much as I enjoy the RPG-style gameplay of the game, the main story itself does not feel engaging to me.The factions all seem like ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ - and don't make me want to help any of them.And there is simply too much text terminals. Every large rooms contains at least 1-2 terminals, and some even 5-6 terminals. And each terminal has several messages (half a page long on average) - so in an average location that's dozens of pages of text to read.And 95% of them are just superfluous text, that adds nothing to the plot.At some point I just stopped reading them altogether. I'm pretty sure I missed some jokes, and probably some dialog options for talking with people - but that's just too much text to read.Some additional nitpicking:At least in the original release - the graphics seem very cartoony. Even too much so.A serious Open world RPG, needs to have a serious look.You can't look like a $10 indie game, and expect to be taken seriously.Also stealing mechanic is not very well implemented.Stealing / Lockpicking / Hacking has almost zero repercussions, and are very easy to perform even if you're playing a completely non-stealthy character.It's so easy - it takes all the fun out of stealing :(After I already had around 20 hours in the regular edition, I upgraded to Spacer's choice edition - and can attest to the differences between the two.The new edition has much better graphics. Not just better resolution, but many graphical changes.The people look much more realistic (to the point that some have completely different faces), planets have additional huge structures in the background, which make them look much better. And other minor changes as well.It does come with a cost though. It definitely takes up more GPU resources than the original, and some people have reported bugs & crashes (although I must admit, in my 40+ hours I have not encountered any)In addition, the new edition has more/better Steam achievements.And the game itself is slightly more difficult - when playing the same difficulty level as the original.Overall I felt the new version was the better version, and having the choise - the one I prefer to be playing.But that may not be the case if you have an older/weeker GPU...The game has 2 DLCs (for which I will post reviews separately):Peril On Gorgon - Has a whole new map filled with enemies to kill. And an engaging story (better than the main plot of the game IMO). In addition, this DLC has more skill levels, and more bonuses (for the higher levels).Murder on Eridanos - I have not finished it yet, but it's a kind of a detective mystery. With some new creatures and fun guns to try out.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't buy it. It's a watered-down AND sized-down Fallout 4. Start a new play-through in Fallout 3, NV or even 4 is strictly better than buying this rip-off. I gave this game too much patience to refund it, don't be like me.Alright, if you need more details to convince you, here are some grudges I hold against it:1. Crashes: I didn't really met any game-breaking bugs, instead the game just vanishes into thin air and let me stare at my desktop whenever it feels like it. I had to avoid a certain location and lock my FPS to 60 just to reduce the frequency, even though my machine can easily handle 130+ FPS.2. Shallow: Did I mention it's a watered-down fallout 4? It basically took a drop of Fallout 4 and mixed it with a swimming pool of pure nothingness. I don't know how devs manage to do it but EVERYTHING feels shallow--combat, item, quests, perks, world building, everything. There's nothing for you to figure out, at all. If I want some mindless action I will not play RPGs thank you very much. Not to mention the action part isn't good either.3. Small: Without DLC you are expected to finish the game within 20 hours (by finish I mean completing most quests if not all of them). The game world is basically a series of small maps connected by a menu. And those can be VERY small maps that only has 3 rooms.4. Empty: Yes, even with the small size the game still manages to feel empty. You can grab some quests from settlements and that's it. There is not much to explore and exploring is not rewarding either--no unique item no interesting locations, nothing. Just some generic monsters that you can kill and ammo and money you can loot. Yes I know there's science weapons but these does have a quest and there is not enough of them.5. Confusing world building: The world doesn't make sense. Everyone except you seems to be complete idiots that makes decisions dumb beyond comprehension. Yet the game refuse to make fun of itself and let go a lot of opportunities to introduce some ridiculously funny elements. I was devastated when I learned that there's no aliens in the game.5. No improvements: Why play this game when it keeps most aspects the same as a decade ago? It's 2020 at least you can add some pictures and icons in these bloody terminals. The game brings nothing new or at least nothing meaningful to the industry.6. DLC: The first DLC is less watered-down and at least has a meaningful plot. ofc it just goes to show that the main game is just a glorified concept demo. Too little, too late.

_childDocuments_.review: I got this for $17 on GMG. I would recommend it for $20 or less. This is absolutely not worth $60, so shop around or wait for a steep discount. At first it seems like Fallout in space, but eventually you see how much is missing compared to a FO title and it starts to feel like a knockoff FO you bought at KMART. Enemy respawn rate is weird as hell, in a lot of areas enemies flat out didn't respawn. Stealth system is pretty bunk, if you stealth shot one mob, the rest usually know exactly where you are and buzz straight to you. Reading the consumables descriptions is an eye sore (seriously what the ♥♥♥♥ were they thinking with UI there), so it's easier to just ignore them and spam sell them all since they're entirely unnecessary anyway unless you're playing on Supernova mode which requires eating. And the buffs are next to useless.It's not a true open world, changing planets is just a menu click away and each planet is rather small for a game like this. It basically is a hub system with tiny zones, reminiscent of a PS2 era game. For some reason there is a large woke culture overtone that is kinda weird the longer the game goes on, it feels very overly token.The loot system is pretty meh, usually in a game like this you'd be able to take pretty much every single item an enemy has when you kill them, but here it's a bit random where you may or may not get something they're using and when you loot the gear it's still on the corpse. Sometimes you get locked into dialogue and have to spam a few responses until you get to one to end dialogue. I've had keys to doors disappear after I picked them up, some disappeared after using them once despite still having doors that need the same key. Not sure if that's a glitch or a dumb decision to make keys one time use?The color gamma in this is weird and tough to find a spot that looks good without being washed out or too artificially rich looking.This is all odd because Obsidian has worked on the Fallout series so you'd expect this to be a lot better than it is and have added features not less. The gear mod system is pretty restrictive and trash. For some reason you can mod body armor, but not helmet armor; kinda weird decision. Some weapons that clearly should have multiple attachments only have 1.The skill/perk system is pretty bunk too. You level cap at 30, so that means you can only max 3 skills, 300 SP/100 SP. Then out of the 42 possible perks, you can only safe unlock 15, because you only get 1 perk every two levels. Although you can unlock additional perks through the Flaw system, that requires being subjected to certain enemies, items etc, repeatedly; to unlock the option to take permanent stat debuffs, in return for another perk point. Only 20 flaws, so even if you find each one you can still only unlock 35 perks in total. The ♥♥♥♥?It's basically knock off Fallout. I enjoyed it because I bought it cheap and it slightly scratches the space game itch, but it's a solid 3/5 game. Nothing particularly unique or great, but not entirely ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ either. It's alright, but I don't look forward to grinding achievements for 100%.

_childDocuments_.review: I lost interest around less than 1/4 of the way through and left the game for a good while. Picked it up year later and again, lost interest.Decided to play a chaotic route this time. Playing as a manipulative, assassin or straight up terrorist sort of character and still couldn't find much interest.I found the enemies would only ever rush you. The enemy variety is pretty limited. The combat strategy will pretty much remain the same due to the environmental layouts. The story script writing was average, companions barely acknowledge your actions in the world.Quests feel like the usual fetch quests or kill this thing and do my laundry while you're at it.The game isn't exactly bad. _childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: I first played this game on the Xbox One X, but have recently switched to a PC. To say that it's an upgrade compared to the console is a given. But what I love most about the game is that, despite it being a new IP for Obsidian,  and the fact that they didn't think this game will do well; is even more testament to how well they told the story and presented the characters. So much so that it compelled me to play hundreds of hours across three different systems and give rise to two expansions, with the last coming soon in the future. Yes their are flaws, as with the level cap originally being 30, but now 33 with the Peril on Gorgon DLC. Sometimes the characters can feel drawn out and repetative. Even the quests feel the same sometimes. But their are a lot of moments the game gives you where you are just awestruck at how well it is told. For example, Parvati's romance quest line is not only interesting, but it leaves you wanting to find out if she ever did find love among the stars. Or even Vicor Max's quest to understand "The Plan" and helping him find his path. But in my honest opinion it'll have to be the main story itself that I love the most. I would highly recommend this game to anyone who loves RPGs.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: As woke as Starfield, but still a better game. The GLA representation is of the lipstick variety. The girl bossing is over the top. The hatred of corporations comes thru, but someone with basic understanding of economics can choose options to help the corps thrive and help everyone. And at least the devs know that dimorphism in the human settlers means two distinct forms of the same species and the pronouns match this.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: Love this game.  Very fun mix of Fallout, Mass Effect and Firefly.  You assemble a crew of misfits and take to the space to either support or overthrow the local corporate overlords.  The game is very funny - humor in games is hard to pull off, but Obsidian managed to pull it off.  Having worked in the corporate world, their mocking tone is very on target.  You have a series of planet/settlement hubs you travel to for missions but you are free to solve them how/when you want, from combat to dialogue.  I very much hope for a sequel, just bigger and better.  I recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fun, when it works. My game crashed repeatedly right after character creation. It never saved so I had to make my character over and over again. I was finally able to fix it by putting the game into Fullscreen, Locked at 60 FPS, and Vsync On.It worked for about 4 hours and then it keeps crashing in the Geothermal Plant whenever I get melee attacked by a robot.You'd think after an entire year these issues would have been resolved.So far the game has been a lot of fun, and the dialogue choices have blown me away. Obsidian did a great job.But until these Crashes get fixed, I cannot recommend this game.Edit: I am running a i7 8700K and a 1080ti with 32GB of DDR4 RAM, it's NOT my hardware.HOWEVER. I found that disabling the Steam Overlay seems to help. I will continue testing it.Edit 2: Nothing works. I disabled every running process in my background. I disabled my AntiVirus, I ran it at a lower resolution, I turned off the Windows Game Bar, I ran the game as Admin. The crashes have increased as a matter of fact.I give up.EDIT 3: I built a new PC back in December and just recently managed to get back to this game. It seems the crashing issues have stopped, so there may have been issue with the underlying hardware and not the game itself. I apologize this review got so popular while 'negative'. I changed this review to positive and hope more people will give this great game a try.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: Finally I found a game that buying my new machine was worth for.Take the best of "Borderlands" (weapons and their atributes, the spaceship) and "Fallout" (companions, armor, killing and looting random enemies) and mix it together, Normal mode is not too hard, which is good, because fighting feels a bit stiff at times.The graphics are stunning (playing on Ultra), the humor is quite good. The story (if you need one) is O.K.. This is a nice FPS, if you need one that keeps you busy. I am 10 hours in and drown in quests already.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: I am not gonna waste your time with a very lengthy and in depth reviewThe game is fun, has an interesting storybut is short and has no post ending sandbox type freeplay justlike New vegas (that was a big dissapointment)And wait for sale, its a bit too pricey as of nowOverall the game is good, but it feels like a lot of things got cut out before launching it
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: I was so hyped for this game, but in the end it just turned out to be as average as a game can be and perhaps in some areas even worse. Didn't buy it first because of EGS exclusivity and now I regret that I did.My first gripe is the weapon levels. I thought we were over this BS. How can a gun have levels?It's one thing that in a fantasy game a sword can be made with better materials, imbued with magic, etc...This whole levelling system makes skill points pretty much useless and mods as well, just go and tinker the s**t out of the guns or buy a higher level one when you can. Problem solved.3 ammo types.4 weapons slots and 3 ammo types just shows how they try to peddle the melee combat.Yeah, because bringing a knife to a gunfight always ends well. I know it's the far future and everything, but how do you put the same ammo into a shotgun and a pistol? Shortcuts, that's how.You can't go and use a pistol and a shotgun as you will eat the same ammo with both and after the first hour you realise you are out of ammo.Armour.It consists of 1 suite and an head piece. That's it.No mix and match. No boost for putting on same faction stuff. No mistaking you to be an enemy when you waltz in to a city with a full marauder armour on with the helmet hiding your face.Consumables.They litter the whole world, but never felt the need to use them. Giving personality boost for 20 seconds? Useless...All of them.Small, but empty world.The places you can go on a planet (a whole planet) is very limited and they are small. Small settlements cluttered here and there, but nothing out of interest. And the worst part is, that it is empty. A lot of crap around you, but somehow it is still empty. Enemies are scarce and a lot of buildings are closed, so you can't even go in. And the ones you can go in, they are either mission related or just asset flips. Why not just make everything an asset flip then? Wouldn't make any difference at this point.Story is bland.The BIG BAD CORPORATIONS ARE CONTROLLING THE WORLD!!!!How original is that? Not much.There are a couple good parts where you can feel the negative side of your decisions, but in general it's bland. It's so bland that I don't even bother to read the terminal logs if there are any. Fallout games (not 76) were oozing with story on every corner. Every terminal, diary and letter had a lot of stuff to tell about the people writing it.Characters look and sound bland.Besides all of them looking the same, they have nothing interesting to say.Old characters look like a young actor who was made 30 years older by a makeup artist.None of them are interesting and most of the time they are annoying as hell and listening to them makes your ears bleed. At least you can kill them if you feel like it.This game was piggybacking on the success of Fallout New Vegas, but it doesn't come even close to it on any level. Which is bad as the world has so much potential.And besides this it's not even an enjoyable FPS.

_childDocuments_.review: Cant recommend this at asking price. _childDocuments_.review: Very fun game, classic Obsidian.  I loved what they did with Fallout: New Vegas, and this was a great return to form.  Funny dialogue options, satisfying RPG mechanics, and lots of factions to ally yourself with.  Not to mention the beautiful and inventive scenery. Equal parts Fallout and Borderlands, this is a fun game and well worth the money.  Highly recommend, especially if the infinite playthroughs of FO:NV and FO4 are wearing thin and you're looking for something different.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: If you come here for modern action gameplay, you'll find it a bit lackluster. Even from a storytelling perspective, it isn't perfect, sometimes running the narrative too slow and frequently running its themes rather too on the nose. That said, I'd still say this is easily the best roleplaying game to come out since Fallout: New Vegas. If that's what you're into, it's unquestionably worth a look.If you're coming here for Tim Cain and Leonard Boyarski, I'd say that while they aren't at their absolute best here, they still did a rock solid job. Plus, for once, they've come out with something not only fully-functional, but well-polished. I might still love Arcanum more than Outer Worlds, but at this point it's probably going to be Outer Worlds I replay when I need to scratch that old itch.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game, it has a great story line and awesome characters. I found the weapons/combat to be fun, albeit nothing groundbreaking. The game felt very similar to other RPGs I have played so again, nothing totally new or groundbreaking but still enjoyable.My only qualm with the game is how short it is. I played through it twice, once just the base game/story line and any side quests I found, and then again with the DLCs (+ side quests that I was able to find). I still was able to complete both DLC's in one day each, and the side quests didn't take much longer. I'd say I was able to play through it completely twice, which for only a bit over 80 hours doesn't feel like a lot/ a full game. It just feels like a short game for the price. I do understand that it is very re-playable and you can try new play styles and choose to work more with different companions (which affects your story line/decisions). That is awesome, I just wish the game had more content and side quests available to make it more fleshed out.Still recommend the game though, just because the story, characters and dialogue are enjoyable and playing the game was still so much fun. I'm just glad that I got it on a sale for I think $20. Def worth $20 but idk about paying the full $60 price for this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Sure, a lot of people felt underwhelmed by this one, but it's really and truly worth the money. It's also worth the time and mind you put into it. _childDocuments_.review: This game is the greatest open-world FPS RPG I have ever played. This statement is not to discredit any other similar game of this genre. I'm a fan of the Fallout franchise and New Vegas is probably my favorite. Makes sense, then, that I would be equally blown away by this solo project from Obsidian (the developer of NV). The Outer Worlds gives me KOTOR flashbacks, especially the pacing and growth of the story through planet hopping. Dialogue is dramatic, witty, violent, dark, mysterious, depressing, and sometimes a few of those at the same time. Combat is challenging, but not hard to master. Through the modification of weapons and armor, the game never once feels grinding. I highly recommend this game to anyone who is looking for an adventure with a lot of inter-personal character development. An adventure rife with conflict and people relying on you to be a hero (but you don't have to be). Five Stars *****

_childDocuments_.review: A game of mediocrity.The gun-play is passable, but lackluster with a small variety of weapons and only 3 ammo types.The writing is passable, if goofy 95% of the time.The levelling system is passable, but uninspired with boring "make the number go up" perks.There was nothing new and exciting during my 16 hour playthrough of this game, which included the main story, side quests, and exploring. When the credits started to roll, I wasn't disappointed, pleased, or anything in between.If you enjoy RPGs, namely Fallout, you will most likely get your money's worth out of this game. I would wait for a sale.If you are looking for a game that recaptures the feelings that New Vegas gave you, just play New Vegas. This ain't it, Captain.

_childDocuments_.review: Performance is horrible like really erratic frame rate bad horrible, whenever your inside its lovely and smooth however when outside the frame rate just bounces up and down up and down sometimes hitting picture frame rates and at times locking my character onto a spot on the floor.Ryzen 3900XT32GB RAM2x 1080tiEVO 860The game is not even at max graphics its set to high i cant run fullscreen as i think thats where most of my constant frame hiccups are coming from, if i want to run 3440x1440 i have to run in windowed fullscreen as fullscreen only works at 2560x1440 and that simply stretched the image.  I just landed on Monarch and was fighting the ♥♥♥♥ in the town there and my frame rate is boucing up and down so much its noticeable and feels horrible and like i mentioned earlier my character keeps getting stuck or trapped on certain parts on the ground.Such a shame cause when the game runs good it feels lovely and is a joy to play (down with Bethesda).UPDATE:  Changing this to a recommend as the game really is a joy to play, its the Fallout 4 that we should have got and honestly i'm kinda hoping that maybe Fallout 4 will get redone in this quality one day but i imagine that is highly unlikely as Bethesda wont even consider it unless it has layers of MACRO transactions.Graphics are lush and very colourful, the idle banter between squad mates is great it feels fluid like they are actually communicating and simply two people reading stiffly from lines, although sometimes conversations can start at the end instead of at the start so at times theres no context but they just continue like they have been chatting the whole time.SOLUTION: Unfortunately the game is not very well optimised it does not support ultrawide resolutions at all and the maximum it does is 2560x1440, you have to run Windowed Fullscreen to get 3440x1440 and when doing this the game is constantly stuttering and lagging sometimes down to single digit frame numbers which really detracts from this otherwise quality product.  Disabling SLI for me netted me at maximum an extra 3 frames which made no difference so i re enabled it and enabled G Sync for both Fullscreen and Windowed applications, i'm happy to say that while my frame rate did not shoot through the roof it made a noticeable difference in frame stability and overall a more enjoyable experience, its a shame because i ran it at 2560x1440 just to take a look as it stretches the image horribly but when Fullscreen is enabled and working properly its buttery smooth (95 FPS)  i really hope they sort this out and enable ultrawide but according to the community they have no interest in making this a reality.
