_childDocuments_.review: The Outer Worlds is a Satirical Joyride through a capitalist hellscape. It's charming and campy (like, the good kind of campy) with Easter Eggs and chubby snakes. You get Fallout and Bioshock vibes off of this game like crazy.You also feel like one of maybe 10 people that's actually free in the galaxy, and when you're sitting in your ship listening to the calm background music, looking at the stars and talking to Ada, you honestly feel a little more free in your own life as well.There are more role-play opportunities in this game than the vast majority of action RPGs, and it's honestly a breath of fresh air for the Genre.The Outer Worlds is an excellent game that's a bit on the short side as far as the base game is concerned, but if you do all the companion quests and a bunch of side missions, then go back for a second run, you definitely get your money out of it. I originally owned it on PS4, but I got it on here as well so I could keep playing it now that I don't play my PS4 at all anymore. The reasonably priced DLCs help a lot. Murder on Eridanos was excellent, and I only just started on Peril on Gorgon. I'm excited for what comes next. Both for this franchise and for Obsidian in general.

_childDocuments_.review: Firstly this isn't a bad game - just isn't a great game to me.ProsBeautiful visuals - I've visited 3 or 4 planets so far and each have been great to look at. The art guys really made the most of the brief. As with other parts of the game, however, the human side of the design seems to take most of its inspiration from the same vein as Fallout, with classic 50's sci-fi aesthetic in the armour everyone wears. The builds, on the other hand, are straight out of Star Wars, with curves and antennas and sliding doors. It's a small point but the settlements are all relatively small but there are massive neon signs everywhere announcing the name of every tiny district which is odd.Gameplay: pretty solid, if unoriginal. The time dilation mechanic is similar to Fallout 4 VATS, the floating damage numbers are Borderlands, as are the weapon qualities. It works fine, it's somewhat fun. I've only tried ranged, mostly sniping but it's enjoyable enough. Never really feel in any danger during combat unless I'm completely reckless, playing on normal difficulty.ConsPretty much everything else. I found myself dreading speaking to anyone in the game because dialogue is so long and tedious. Everyone wants to gleefully tell you their life story or dance around the information you need. If you want to have this extended dialogue you really need to match it with cut scene type visuals or at least vary the camera angles because staring at a talking head while they recite 50 lines is not engaging.The quests these people offer also quickly become tedious. Collect someones poster from the post office. Really? Sort out a pay dispute at a guys job. Is this what a space adventure is supposed to be? HR Intergalactic? Thankfully these are side quests that don't have to be done, but it is still content.At one point I'm walking around and a guy appears, exclaiming that there has been a murder. After explaining where, he says he is so upset and nauseated that he's going for a lay down. And that's it - it's then up to you to either investigate or ignore this murder. There's no police, the neighbours don't even react to it. I think if I killed someone in the town the AI guards would be all over me. But not in this case; don't involve the police, some passing stranger will do.Inventory and items in general seems off balance. You can find a huge number of buff items, but I haven't used (or needed) any yet. Enemies die fairly easily without causing too much damage, and I passively heal out of combat anyway. Companions seem invincible. There are these weird vending machines absolutely everywhere. I don't know if I'm supposed to be using more items that they sell or if its a commentary on the commercialisation of space exploration, which would fit in with the narrative but also seems unnecessarily functional for that purpose? I just end up selling all the junk that weighs my character down.In terms of the main quest it's fine so far, in so much as it involves going out, killing bad guys (marauders who are never really explained - just shallow default baddies) finding a thing, bringing it back. Not sure how many more times this quest pattern will be interesting.Conclusion: It looks good, it plays ok, I can't stand listening to the dialogue, overall it's pretty shallow, not sure I'll finish it (about half the play time was AFK).

_childDocuments_.review: A paradise for feminists..You seriously get sick of the holes in the logic of this game.So yeah it's like fallout in the play style, but less immersive and pushes political agendas left right, and center.The main Agenda of the game "We want to show you Women are Tough!, but we will do it, low-key repetitive"80% of the lead characters in the game I encountered were all female, and were playing the "I'm Tough look at me" or "I'm a witty smart ass" role.Personally it just made me instantly dislike the game, for the simple reason that.. it took away from the logic of the story.I first clued onto this when the "character creation" screen starts on a Female.. then you steal a ship with a female AI.. then your first crew mate is female.. then the leader of the first planets rebellion is female..In this game, 80% of males you encounter are stupid or jerks..you get your second crew mate on the Groundbreaker(spaceship outpost).. he's the classic "troubled kid/thief type".. The captain of the Groundbreaker is Female.Then you get two more female crew members, and a robot.Point is, most of the game is Male vs Female. Female is always doing the right thing, and male is always reckless or greedy..If you side with a male npc.. chances are someone is going to die or get hurt, which sucks if you want an unbiased roleplay experience.It frustrates me because the target audience for games like these are normally males.So as an experiencer of this game it feels like they are trying to shove socialism down my throat..I literally play games to escape this ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, and now it's found it's way to games..They ruined Star Wars with aggressive political correctness.. and now this.I just wanted to say this in case some dev thinks they were being sneaky and we wouldn't notice.. we notice these things.Game itself.Game play - 5/10Sound - 7.5/10Visual - 7.5/10Main comments:Tedious gameAverage learning curve Lots of dark stories Perk system seems like an after thoughtFeels very linearLacks the fallout experience, but delivers a rough feelA conspiracy theorists wet dreamSometimes CrashesGot a refund after 12 hours.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of being lectured about the proper pronouns for robots and computers or really like it when every woman in a game looks and behaves in stereotypically masculine ways this is just the game for you. If you always wondered why not every single female character in a video game wasn't either running a powerful criminal organization or a space station or multi-billion dollar company while all the idiot men weren't either evil or simply incompetent this might be the game for you. If you want a laughably over the top attempt at commentary on capitalism and the free market that strays far beyond parody into the realm of a socialist fever dream you might consider picking it up.  If you work for Kotaku, you will love it. If you can get past the patronizing political and social messaging that you are essentially beaten over the head with from start to finish you will find a mediocre FPS with light RPG elements in the vein of the Fallout reboots (unsurprisingly given it is made by Obsidian.) The gun-play is so-so, the story is derivative and trite. Your companions are boring at best, with at least one of them being tear-your-hair out irritating. "should i ask her out? what if she doesn't like me? I think I am in love with this person I spoke to for 2 minutes and now need you to take me across the galaxy for special things to give her! Also, what if she doesn't like me?" This is the first time I ever decided not to complete a quest line purely out of spite. It wants you to care for your companions but they're so bland and derivative I just couldn't. Technically it is a mixed bag. The performance is good aside from the biggest pop-in issues I have ever seen when transitioning between areas. It's a fairly ugly game. Character models are good, but everything is muddy. It all just kind of bleeds together into this green/brown mess when you are outside of the various settlements. They seem to have gone out of their way to place ample road signs and markers which suggests they knew that the environments were redundant with very little to distinguish one area from another. The overall gameplay is by no means bad. it is enjoyable for the first 10 hours or so, but it wears out it's welcome fast. Obsidian's return is "meh" at best.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately the game doesn't live up to its reputation. The worlds are repetitive and every world is basically the same village with a different look... with a world built around it. The worlds itself are "flat" you cannot go everywhere - they're full of barriers... It feels like an old half life or quake or unreal engine game. There no way this thing is "open world". While the worlds themselves look pretty even the enemy types repeat. This is a pattern that goes through the whole game... The characters etc... But I've to add that it feels like an Fallout ripoff where they weren't able to actually catch the humor Bethesda and Obsidian offered in the Fallout universe. Its for the most part simple and boring conversations with the same repetitive jokes. it feels like as if a 10th grader hasn't done his homework properly and copied it from various classmates while the atmosphere got somewhere lost.I wouldn't buy this game again. It's a waste of money, you're better off trying anything else. Even the gameplay is repetitive, the weapons are boring too. There was simply no effort put into this game. I play usually a wide range of games and never felt the urge to actually warn people to buy something in the last 10 years, but this game really needs the stamp "at least you tried". Not even one part of the game is worth exploring it further. Maybe in the future when I forgot how bad it really was I will try again. But its one of those games that force you to take a route in a open world game. But the only thing that is open about this game is the devs wallet. everything else is limited like the levels.... However, if it would still be possible I would ask for a refund, so better watch some gameplay videos and decide for yourself before spending money on this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed this game a lot. Unsurprisingly, this game reminds me a ton of Fallout New Vegas, and really scratches the itch for a solid 1st person shooter/RPG game. It was somewhat shorter than expected, taking about ~20 hours to finish the story and maybe half of the available side quests (not including any DLC). The re-playability is high, and I anticipate enjoying many playthroughs of this game to experience some of the many different styles of character development. Highly recommended for fans of RPG games in general, or fans of Fallout 3/NV.

_childDocuments_.review: The Outer Worlds... Now, where do I start?I'll start with the disclaimers: 1) what I write in here is my own opinion, and 2) possible spoilers ahead. There are many other things people could be doing with their time other than reading stuff they don't agree with and finding out about in-game stuff before they wanted to. With that said, let's continue...I have the impression that the team who developed TOW was aiming pretty high, but budget constraints and white collar executives got in the way as usual, and spoiled it for everybody else.Other than being (in my opinion) a mediocre console port with all it's console hardware impairments and limitations ported over, the game feels unfinished and it seems a lot of content was crudely severed at it's final stages of development.The companion AI is plain stupid. Where their behaviour settings read "Passive/Defensive/Aggressive", in reality it is "Dumb/Dumber/Suicidal", particularly true when playing on Supernova - which by the way is the only difficulty setting to go, if you want half a challenge.If you put them on Passive or Defensive and hell breaks loose, they just stay around as if nothing's happening, they won't take cover and worse, they place themselves between you and enemy NPCs, taking fire from both sides. Put them on Aggressive and first thing they do is charge a Sprat when you're trying to sneak past a Mantiqueen. You get the picture.The companions themselves, with the exception of Parvati and maybe Felix, are pretty annoying and totally forgettable. I only took them on their very own quests and only for the sake of getting that much needed XP out of that. There are lots of stuff copy-pasted from other games, the more charitable among you may call it "references", I just call it blatant stealing ideas already seen in other games because they couldn't damn well come up with something new.I could make a long list of stuff they put in there which I've seen on FONV, Deus X Human Revolution, Mass Effect and others, but I can't be bothered, really. Even Guild Wars 2 has been stolen from: the Mantiswarm is nothing but almost a carbon-copy of the Mordrem Troll Insect Swarm from GW2.Anyway, the only two locations I enjoyed was Monarch and Tartarus. Had the dev team pushed through to deliver the remaining part of the game they abandoned, it would probably be a good game in the end. It's kind of frustrating seeing so many locked out locations/planets and not being able to land on them and explore at least.Does it have any replay value? I don't think so. I might start another playthrough only to get a few achievements, but maybe I won't even bother, as the consequences to whatever choices are pretty easy to predict, and not very exciting to experiment with.So, to finish it off, I'd give this game a fair score of 6/10.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: Well. That was....disappointing. The game is fine, if a little lurid in it's colour scheme. I won't complain too much about the way survival is a difficulty, not a setting (wrong approach - makes survival a bad option). And the gameplay is good - lots of dialogue, very amusing in places. I even laughed out loud a few times! But there is just so little of it! The game is over within a few hours. For a full RPG game I expect more. Less than 50 hours to work through the main quest and most of the side quests is not a game, it is a DLC. I have seen mods developed by hobbyists that last longer than this so-called game. Very frustrating, and with little or no replay value as the quests are essentially linear, and the different role play options fairly limited. As I say....disappointing.

_childDocuments_.review: - It feels polished, as in animations and controls are mostly smooth, feels mostly optimized.- Yet still has glaring issues such as sounds will cut in and out, Save bugs, and performance issues carrying over from console.- Shameless low effort Console Port, developers didn't even bother putting in keyboard for control layout screen.- Only 6 companions total in game, you get to use 0-2 at a time. ( I liked Parvati best )- Rewards feel underwhelming.- No prompt that you can skip through dialog using  key.- Inventory seems to clog fast- No indicator/Feedback when you have same model weapons with better stats then currently equipped.- Beyond face customization, expect a very lackluster character customization system for the current generation of games. (very disappointing)- Story and characters often feel, shallow & hollow as expressed in other reviews.- Many dialog options will lead to same/similar results (big turn off, given it is so story focused.)- Though it is open, feels very linear, there is definitely a specific order they are pushing you towards visiting places to unlock the broader content. Places you visit before intended time in main story feel lacking in purpose to be there.- I appreciate that they didn't hypersexualize all the women. (You can give your lady a beard)Due to my love of Fallout 3, Vegas, Morrowind, Oblivion, Skyrim etc... each of the titles listed I have put in between 700 - 1200 hours of game play EACH before thinking about putting them down for another game. Players loyal to this genre should not expect the same mileage and replay-ability. After only 20 hours I found myself missing my other games and finding "The Outer Worlds" much less engaging, juicy, or as open world feeling as I would like.After 20 hours of playing the game I just don't care or feel any emotional attachment for 99% of the characters or the fate of this fictional universe, I feel apathetic towards the story/world.The series of map levels, lack of variety in mechanics, and equivalent fetch quests, betray the beautiful art style, audio work and concept this was built upon, and sadly I expected more from this studio especially vs. Bethesda.I just can't recommend this game a this time even for the 50% off price of $29.99, and would advise anyone to give it a hard pass for any higher price. I can see the passion put in, it isn't technically bad, it simply just isn't a fun or rewarding game to play if you have played many games from the same genre before.Could be a solid experience for first time players into games like this.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: I remember when the game was announced the hype was unreal people saying this game was the next Fallout New Vegas and at the time I was feeling the hype. It was delayed on the steam store by a year and was an epic games exclusive for that time, I felt pretty pissed about this and saw it as a ♥♥♥♥ move on obsidian's part.  So flash forward a year and it’s on steam on almost constant 50% of sale and here’s why, it’s a bad game.  The story is nothing you can care about and the game breaks down to fetch quests and done badly. A lot of games have many fetch quests but they make up for this by being fun to play. You have talent skills in the game but I felt they had 0 impact on the game play beside a few obvious talents anyone would pic. You have a crew who you pick up along the way but I couldn’t name 1 of them since they are just boring and generic.  The only reason I finished this game is because I had paid for it and felt it might get better as you move along and if anything it would be something to kill time, I was wrong.  The game doesn’t get better and just ends. I got far cry 3 on sale for like 3 Euro and I had way more fun playing that then this rubbish.

_childDocuments_.review: A surprisingly short game, especially for an RPG. Compared some other open world RPGs i've played like Fallout 3,4 or even Obsidian's own New Vegas took me atleast 60 to 80 hours to beat on a first playthrough without DLCs yet here it only took me 30. Mind you i did most of the side quests and allied with most if not all of the factions (except the Board). Nothing too special but not bad either.The companions once again face a similar issue as the world itself, there's a lot of potential within their backstories that could've been expanded even further.Overall. it's a good game, i enjoyed my time with it. _childDocuments_.review: Obsidian definitely took what they learned from making Fallout New Vegas, and applied it here.  There's room for improvement, yes.  For starters the planets need to feel bigger.  I know the open world areas were huge, but we're talking about planets.  Whole epic games can occur on a massive open world map that only translates to a spot on our globe.  Space games in general don't do a good job of making a planet feel like a planet so much as an individual city, and this game is no exception.  One thing that adds to this feeling is having the same ten or some monsters present in all locations no matter what planet you're on.  Different planets should have different flora and fauna, with the invasive species transported by humans being the rare exception, not the norm! For space locations like asteroids and space stations, the devs should definitely play around with the gravity and make low and micro gravity environments part of the gameplay.  This isn't something new to games, and I feel like it could be incorporated into space games with starship travel.Other than that, make sure your hardware meets the requirements and you should be fine.  Solid gameplay and story.  I feel like there needs to be a cookbook that explains how to make an imitation of the food in the game.  I want some Lemon Slapp for a hot summer's day, some Glacial Aged Whiskey for special occasions, a sampling of every color of Rizzo's spectrum vodka, I want to know what tripicale is even supposed to be so I can attempt tripicale pasta, and, OH YEAH, the cystypig food items now have me wondering if you can actually cook and eat a pig's cancerous tumors!  No kidding, I'm morbidly curious about that now.  Thanks C&P!  Also, EVERY purpleberry product in the game is making me wonder about whether you could engineer a berry to taste like the purple grape koolaid flavor and make all of those products with that.  GOD the capitalist advertising stuff in this game actually gets in your skull!  Now when I go to a bad hotel I'm telling people that the hotel "is not the best choice, it's Spacer's Choice!" As a way of telling them how bad it is!  Obsidian really nailed soul-eating, mentally cancerous late-stage capitalism in this game!

_childDocuments_.review: What can be said?Outer Worlds has all the FPS/RPG tropes we've come to expect. It's, familiar.And that's probably why I like it. It may not be earth-shattering or groundbreaking in any fundamental way, but it plays how you expect it to play.It does offer an interesting skill progression system that I have found to be far less over or under whelming than other systems can be. It isn't so complex and expansive that you feel like there's a lot of wasted skill sheet or that you're missing out, but it also isn't so simple that you feel like there's little point to really spending time considering and mapping out your progression.For me, the skill system is very well balanced and tuned and, if for no other reason, it does make this game stand out a bit from the pack.The gameplay is by the numbers for the genre. Stealth in, scope things out, pick your first couple targets, use the limited combat ability to slow things and give analysis data, then finish off whatever is trying to maul you with the accuracy through volume philosophy.Talk to everyone, use your dialog skills when you can, get the quests, do the quests.Pretty standard fare.The story(so far) is the usual corporations bad, common man blinded by drudgery imposed on them by "capitalistic" overlords. It tries hard to be funny, and there are certainly a few guffaw or wry smile moments, but, again, pretty standard fare.The world is a series of 'open' map areas you travel to, a la Borderlands or, maybe, and I'm stretching here, Mass Effect(mostly because you're traveling from one planet area to another on different planets).Enemies have very set tactics and AI and you once you know what to expect, you pretty much develop your methods and repeat them with each group's enemy type.None of this is to say it's bad. It's just, what you expect. It's familiar. It's using tried and true elements of the genre. And that's fine, it's good even. Not everything has to be evolutionary, not every game needs to try to reinvent the wheel. Familiar means it isn't bad, it isn't ruined, they didn't do something terrible in trying to up the ante, things we see quite often from well established studios and publishers. Just look at what's going on with the EA and Ubi franchises.The 'same old' in a new body can be just as good as something brand new that works. I would kill for Skyrim in a new body, say ESVI, I'm SOOOO tired of looking at ESV in my library and thinking "I really loved that game, but I'm tired of playing it." Same with the other hiatus franchises like GTA or DA. Give me the same game in a new world, a new story, I would be happy with that.And Obsidian did that here. Brand new world and story(in detail at least), same old genre. And it works.Grab it on sale, get the DLC to get a few more hours out of it, and enjoy the nostalgia repackaged.*And definitely head to Stellar Bay from Cascadia even if you got the key. Don't deny yourself that bit of fun.

_childDocuments_.review: I love RPGs. Having enjoyed other games by Obsidian in the past, having played this - and the two DLCs - through to completion - I regret to say I can't recommend this game at all. But let's start with the positives:1. It has high aspirations. The plot is epic in scope, and lives are on the line, and you're SUPPOSED to give a ♥♥♥♥ about all of this. I can respect that. 2. It does, at times, feel a little bit like the series Firefly was made into a video game? I mean, to the extent that you're a captain of a ship in space and you're exploring places that have kind of a wild west feel to them (with heavy corporate influence) - and maybe even the little touches like your ship is pretty dinky and your engineer sounds like the actress from that series.3. It's very stable. Never crashed, not once. 4. Very straightforward - missions objectives are always highlighted on your map if you've selected them.5. There are some genuinely funny moments, especially if you take the time to read everything. 6. The DLCs add a lot of value and I find better/more compelling, than the main game. 7. The game does give you a lot of choice - there are many ways to complete the same objective. ... and now the downsides:1. The game is mostly just a series of fetch quests. I know what you're thinking: EVERY modern RPG is basically a version of fetch quests in some form of another. Even The Witcher 3, or Mass Effect, or KOTOR, or KC:D, are basically at their heart, a series of fetch quests. True, but those other games had stories that were compelling in their own way through better stories, or writing. This game lacks any emotional hooks to tie you into the story. Sort of like if you took those games, but decided to hire B-class writers. 2. The combat system is (and admittedly I played this on Normal mode) way too easy. And I am by no means good at video games, but put zero points in any combat skills, everything in my speech, etc, and even going out of my way to get into fights near the end (in my struggle to feel something for this game), every fight was just bizarrely easy. Maybe if I went without companions or something? Or... I don't know. Now this isn't necessarily a dealbreaker for a game: a game needn't be challenging, you could think of some games as just interactive movies, and if you come in with that attitude then you will probably enjoy this more than I did. But then you would suffer from point 1 above and be watching a movie you have trouble giving a ♥♥♥♥ about. ... I really can't put any more effort into typing things out. I struggled through playing this (I had played too much to return it by the time it dawned on me that I feel nothing for this game). I hope someone proves me wrong. The DLCs did make the game a little more interesting, but seem bandaids applied to a dead patient. Save your money, buy something else.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is quite honestly the perfect mashup with the usual suspects. Fallout, Borderlands, Skyrim.First, I suggest you commit to a specific class type and keep on that. Ranged/Stealth has done me good but I can see how others are good. There are a few systems to the game and they are pretty simple. Such as the ability to upgrade gear to match levels even if the item doesnt 100% represent that level of an item. The biggest thing that sets itself apart to me is the companion system. Or Crew. You can change their combat behavior, weapons, gear. They offer quests and insight into certain choices. If you decide to do something evil they might even abandon you completely. They interact in the story dialogue and everything. I only wish i could take 5 people with me instead of just 2. The gear system is slightly scattered but once you learn a few things you start to understand how it all works and is setup. When you see a piece of kit thats really good it might have a downside and you actually feel those downsides. Such as the inability to hack a door because you have -5 to stealth on your armor. Its really good. Perks are also pretty decent. While i think some of the choices suck, the system itself is great though. Followers get perk points too! Overall, this is a solid game and worth the price!

_childDocuments_.review: This game takes everything wrong with the genre to the extreme. I'll just give a few examples because I don't feel like typing for an hour.Extreme junk overload. There are 1000 different consumables. You will never use or need them. They are pointless. They take up weight an you sell them. That is it. Constant junk gear falls out of every crevice. Repair system is annoying. You are just constantly repairing everything. It adds nothing to the game other than making me annoyed.Companions: They say a lot of nonsense occasionally, but for the most part they just kind of exist as poor AI.Stealth: Worst stealth mechanics I have ever seen in a game.Skills: Aren't fun and don't add to the game.Shooter: Guns feel bad. None of them feel real. Real old style janky point and shoot. Enemies: Hard enemies are just bullet sponges.Fall damage: You take fall damage and are slowed from falling 5feet. You die if you fall 10feet. Just really annoying.The game feels like it is a slightly polished beta. It seems like it needed another year or more in development with play testers explaining what players want to the devs as it is clear the devs themselves have only briefly heard of the genre and never played it.Anyway. Game is worth maybe $15. It isn't very good, but if you are bored it is mildly entertaining.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a journey. My expectations going into this game were very high, as the creators of this game have been very powerful devs in the past. I was let down by some aspects of this game, but impressed and entertained by most  others. Of all the games that are soaked with corporate satire this game does it the best. The satire isn't overwhelming or invasive to how you enjoy the game. Cons short main storysomewhat rigid combat limited combat options Pros ha ha funnyindustry standard writing (sets the bar for other games)enjoyable and interesting NPCs wonderful style and art directionengaging and well executed side quests strong character creation systemlegit freedom of choice ideologically compelling sheds light on the morally grey nature of realityThe game has some minor issues that in my opinion don't distract from an enjoyable game experience. The writing and characters had me hungry for more missions and quests to complete. I felt my characters choices mattered and were reflected in the world. Visually it's not comparable to more modern releases, but it owns it's visual direction with soft colors and vibrant lighting. The outer worlds truly feels like an outer space adventure. If you're looking for a game similar in foundation to 3D fallout games this is one of the closest things you can get. There are elements of Borderlands and Masseffect in the game mechanics so if you liked those games you'll probably like this game. This game also nods it's hat to the iconic show Firefly. You can see the shows influence in the world building and writing everywhere. The game is short relative to other titles in the genre but more than makes up for this with rock solid writing and enduring characters. Given the short nature of this game I recommend waiting for a sale to stock up on the DLCs and save money.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been a fan of Obsidian going back to their first games, and to Black Isle Studio before that. So it's a bit sad that I find myself spacing out while playing Outer Worlds. There's a competent enough FPS somewhere in there, though I'm not really playing an Obsidian RPG for its FPS. The world built starts out fascinating, though as you progress it's clear they ran out of imagination after the opening world. But it's the characters and writing that's the let-down, in a game from Obsidian of all places. Individual characters are 2D caricatures, the philosophy espoused is shallow and hamfisted, and the dialog drags longer than a bad year. It's sad, because I forgave them so many bugs in KOTOR2, or FO:NV, or NWN2, because the games ultimately had so much soul and love. With Outer Worlds you get almost none of the bugs. Too bad the soul was extracted alongside them.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most tedious, un-enthralling and genuinely uninteresting RPGs I have ever played. Amazing idea, absolutely awful execution. Combat is woeful, levelling system is completely unneeded (really adds nothing to the game other than you can sometimes say another line of dialogue, which changes practically nothing, wowzers!). People will rave about the amazing world building, I have just finished the game and honest to god couldn't tell you the main antagonists name, they're so undeveloped and irrelevant to the whole plot. The world is pretty enough but thats about it. The worlds dead, the NPCs are lifeless, you fight the same 5 enemies over and over. It's like a proof of concept that got released as a full game. Quests are tedious and uninspired (oh cool, a mysterious family has invited me in for dinner, I'm sure they wont be cannibals for the 5354th time), the quests for your companions especially so. By the time I got to Byzantium I was so over even pretending to be invested in the story that I just shot everyone I came across, which given how awful the combat is didn't really improve the experience. I played it back on release date on the game pass and found it boring then, I had hoped that with updates and time that would have changed, but no, it's still an overhyped pile of trash. Avoid, unless you feel like wasting a few hours and can get it really cheap.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is OK for what it is. But I would recommend to buy this during sale. 60€ (without DLCs) is maybe a bit to much compared to other similar games. Here is my Pro/Cons List after round about 20 hours of playing:PRO:- Graphic is OK even though not like a AAA Title- Runs very fluid and stable with my RTX2070 and Ryzen 2600 on highest settings in 1080p- Ability, Skill and Item System is nice  and understandable- Story has a nice depth, you can skip some unnecessary dialogs if you want to.- Game has a very cool humor- Some Weapons and abilites are cool to useCONS:- Fights are fun, but get repetitive over time- A Feature to store items (in the ship for example) would be nice. The capacity you can carry is reached very fast- The world does not feel very realistic in terms of People and monsters. Games like GTA or Witcher 3 feel way more like a busy and realistic world- Feature like TZD, stealth attacking are nice but not really mandatory to useConclusion:My list might not be complete now. I would definitely recommend to play on a harder difficulty than "normal". It is very easy to win fights without using a lot of items or abilities on this level. Maybe I did not play enough but I visited a few planets now and the designers could have made more of features like stealth attacking or consequences of decision making during dialogs. It tries to be like an unlinear open world but at some parts it does not feel like it. It is still fun to play but I would not pay the full price on it. But compared to other "RPG like open world FPS" it feels polished and stable. Couldn't find a lot of serious bugs.

_childDocuments_.review: About 16 hours in and I'm having the most fun with this game than I've had in a long time with an FPS RPG. Maybe the most fun since Fallout: New Vegas. The art direction is really amazing in my opinion, it's a very beautiful game and has a distinct feel. I like the world, and would love to see additional games in this universe. Good characters and voice acting. Of course it is very reminiscent of Fallout 3/4/NV, but more linear of course. Little quirks here or there but it's FUN and that is what matters. _childDocuments_.review: The planets aren't exactly enticing, they definitely do not keep me interested in the game for long play sessions like similar games in this genre. That said, the freedom you have in The Outer Worlds is pretty fun to experiment with. I actually enjoy having less to manage in my inventory. I never care about how my character looks, I rarely see them in 3rd person anyhow. I've enjoyed how characters are written, I quickly decide if they're a friend or someone I don't need in my game, IE just offing them entirely. The freedom is immense. Have a serious playthrough or just go into everything like you're Doom Guy and rip n tear. Combat could use some work but the game is likely not going to see a change that large anytime ever. I really enjoyed the game at the time of release, haven't had a ton of reason to pick it up lately other than wanting an easy chill game that has achievements, lots of them. Over 45 I think maybe? It is worth it to get on sale, arguably full price if you've got past experience with Obsidian or just like a good space mystery. I have yet to play any of the DLC content but I will get that when I 100% this game. Overall, buy this if it's just sat in your wishlist. Sale or not, worth it imo.

I don't understand why these issues haven't been fixed by now this game has been out for well over a year and these problems still persist. _childDocuments_.review: This started off well. Good graphics, great story, companions that don't get in the way too much. Ultimately though, it's a small world, and the game ends once the not very long main quest does. Not exactly my idea of a sandbox, open ended world.The DLC is funny, as is most of the main game, but Peril on Gorgon pretty quickly got boring and Murder of Eridanus was nothing but a run from one spot to another quest that very quickly got tedious. You also need to do them before you complete the main quest. If I'd known that before I bought the game, I wouldn't have bothered. Hated it with Fallout NV and Fallout 3. At least Bethsoft removed that from FO3 with their DLC.Game play wise the combat is a bit simple, the weapon mods all much the same, the perks are so-so and I didn't get the idea of crippling your character with a flaw just to get another mediocre perk. In a game that spans and entire solar system the wildlife amounts to about half a dozen creatures of various different levels and sub-types.I did like the companions, though they do get in the way in combat and I couldn't find a way of taking that horrible slow-mo camera off when they do their special attacks, so I didn't use them. I didn't use the time dilation thing either, I find stuff like that annoying (like VATS in Fallout), yet a lot of the perks were based around it.I found no use for any of the consumables either, only the adreno. That said, it was enjoyable while it lasted and I might play through it again, but for an open world game it did get very shoot-em-up in places.

_childDocuments_.review: Alot of the Open world feels very forced, different enemy groups that should hate each-other are within a step. Alot of the ship landing zones feel quite forced, like the terrain literally bends to the will of the platforms [Roseways Landing Platform] You could pass this off as just lore, since it was Terraformed, but it feels weird to do so.The majority of quests are either, fetch quests that need you do go from one planet to the other and so forth, to just killing a small / Medium group of enemies.Alot of the games assets(trees, buildings, Weapon models) blend together too easily; making it quite hard to isolate objects. - I noticed this from the tutorial.Suggestions:-> I wish when you boarded your ship it didn't immediately take off; i would go to my ship to drop off some weapons, or modify my gear, and boom im in space, then shortly after, im back-> Skip drives animation is just a png travelling across your screen, i do wish there was some sort of first person animation, where you actually drive the ship and get to use your captain's chair.

_childDocuments_.review: These guys made New Vegas and while I've not played it enough to say anything more about that, I just thought I would mention that, and how obvious it is that they did. Game's a slick mix of Fallout (duh) and oddly, Borderlands, but it leans more into Fallout. Stick to what you know, I suppose. Its also, not a power fantasy to a high degree like Borderlands tends to be towards endgame. Outer Worlds likes to remind you that you are, in fact, very vulnerable and can absolutely die if you're not careful. Yeah I can, have, and will always, chain 4 headshots on doofus' whilst under slowed-time, dropping all of them. But in the same stroke, I could always, be killed in less than 3 seconds because dudes behind me never stopped shooting me, and I, at the time, was not able to force them to stop shooting. If you just think of TTD as a way to make dudes dead (VATS; *wink wink* *nudge nudge*), it works ok.Not only do you take fall damage, but you can also die very easily from it. Kinda irritating.Story isn't groundbreaking, but I liked the ending I got. It can be best summarized as; "Yep I'm still here. Do something about it."Game has a nice, more subdued sense of humor that I really dig.Twists I had expected didn't occur, but it did have its tense moments, where I was sure I was seconds away from being correct. Props for subverting. AI Pathing isn't great. Companions, while interesting, just kinda get in the way. 3 cheers to those that go it alone. We're out here. Usually I just railroad the story, but I found myself actually doing side-quests. Still managed to beat it in under 20 hours. Expect similar, at least on Normal difficulty.I had fun at Halycon. 7/10. This game reminds me why sniping is so fun. Give me something with a good scope, and its all over. Pure Serotonin. Thanks for the fun, see ya in Avowed.

_childDocuments_.review: Worth a buy if it's on sale.What a roller coaster. The first 15-20 hours are addictive, exciting, and fresh. All of the elements immediately measure up. The gunplay is satisfactory, the dialogue and plot are interesting, and the player is quickly given the agency to change the world around them. For this reason, the last stretch of the game hurts so bad. At about the 15-20 hour mark (some say more like 25-30), everything becomes lackluster. RPG elements and perks are not interesting, gun upgrades get VERY stale or are non-existent, the plot comes to a crashing halt rather than an enthralling climax. Oof. To Obsidian's credit, they want to reduce bugs in the game and they did, so props for that. 10/10 beginning, 4/10 ending, 7/10 overall.

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the most disappointed i have been in a game recently.Really good characters and exceptionally good moral choices, although characters still don't compare to the ones in falloutSome pretty cool building designs and weaponsAnd that's where most of the good stuff ends, Boring and unoriginal areas both outside and inside towns(Mostly outside, half the time it feels like No Man's sky.) some weapons have cool effects and designs, but there is so little variation among them that you will be thinking "Wait, i've seen this one before" half the times you find/earn a weapon, Combat manages to be somehow worse than Fallout 4, As in you will be fighting giant bug enemies during most non-human encounters, which gets even worse when weapons don't have any "Impact" to them and there is no permanent crippling to enemies.Headshot someone with a shotgun? they will get a minor headache and lose accuracy for 8 seconds or so.Get this with a major discount and if you don't really care about fun gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: Fallout meets space. That's the best way to describe this game. You play as a colonist that was lost in space that has been revived by a mad scientist that wishes to wake everyone else from your ship up. There's just one problem. He's wanted by the space authorities and he needs your help to make his plan work. How you go about doing it is up to you. Do help this person or betray him? The choice is yours. Such is the baseline premise here. The story itself is very open ended much like that of the fallout games but mixed in with sci-fi elements.The gameplay here is solid but not without its downsides. First off the RPG elements here are all rock solid and the combat is as well. Nothing ground breaking yet nothing you haven't really experienced before if you've played other RPG games with choice and multiple ways to complete objectives. The game itself uses a series of smaller maps which makes each area and location feel unique while not feeling overwhelming which can be the case in large scale open world games. This approach works well for this game as it helps add character to each place you'll visit over the course of your adventure in the cosmos. You'll also get to recruit companions along the way to help aide you in your quest. These companions do help but at the same time they won't automatically engage enemies unless you tell them to. However you can upgrade their equipment and unlock perks for them that can help you in the long especially depending your play style. Despite all these positives the game can get boring at times. With all the talking and breaks in the action. Almost like the game itself leans a bit more towards exploration and dialogue and less on moment to moment gameplay. This can lead to times in which it just feels like the game itself isn't fully balanced to make the most of a unique take on the fallout formula. Some may disagree with this opinion but there is no denying that at times you'll feel like all your doing is talking and not really doing a whole lot which can lead to boredom. On the technical side of things this game looks really good and it runs well but it does have one issue. The game likes to crash randomly at times. Sometimes its once an hour while others it'll be the same place a couple of times in a row before it fixes itself. Thankfully though the game is generous with frequent auto saves so that does help relieve some of the frustration that comes with it. If you like RPG's with choice and consequences mixed with solid RPG elements then this game is defiantly worth taking a look at. If on the other hand your a little bit put off by this and the instability of the game at times then pass. This is one of those games that can be hard to recommend to some people while others it's the opposite. For me it falls somewhere in the middle. Not quite a full thumbs up but certainly not a thumbs down either.

_childDocuments_.review: I think 20 hours are enough time to form ones opinion of a title. This game is pretty much like all the bad things from Fallout New Vegas and I do not understand the hype that surrounded this game. Then again, I also do consider Fallout New Vegas way overhyped.There is no exploration in this game. Invisible Walls abound, making sure you have to stay in the areas and no location, which offers something to find, isn’t bound to a quest in some fashion, thus disincentivizing exploration entirely. Just like New Vegas.. This is a game where you are expected to turn your brain off and let the quest marker guide you.Usually I would read every Mailing log and entry I could find in these games. Here? Those are boring and usually super mundane. Reading someone gripe about inane things like having to keep some animal cages locked doesn’t really add anything, other than stealing my time.There is barely any environmental storytelling, as you might know from Fallout 3. Where you’d walk into a location and go “Huh? I wonder how that happened!”And worst of all, you are expected to make big choices, like the fate of a colony with barely 10 sentences being exchanged. Worse, if you then make the choice you think its best, after you read some mails about how the corporation send killer robots to punish workers, you can’t even use that knowledge as justification.This game is so full of needless jokes it undermines itself. The world is a caricature. Corporations that refuse to supply meds to workers, because apparently nobody told Obsidian how much cost is associated with training workers and they easily outweigh the cost of some meds to keep them healthy and productive. Its like Apple Iphone Production Plants with Suicide Prevention Nets dialed to 11 and used as a joke. “Haha, look how bad corporations are, get it? Get it? Haha!”Obsidian, how about you stop treating people as if they are children? Do you really want to tell me you made a hybrid of Borderlands and Fallout to be aimed at small children that needed to be beaten over the head like this?I am honestly just disappointed. I got the game because I thought it was a good Roleplaying game but the story sucks. The only interesting characters, where the Devs put some effort into are the companions, and everyone else is a bad stereotype.If at least the combat would be fun.. But i am more than half way through the game, at this point (and i am probably not finishing it) and been to 4ish planets and its the same enemies everywhere. Robots, Apes, Raiders, Dogs and Bugs. Only the bugs will be new, the first 4 you will meet on the first starting planet.. And that is as good as it gets.It is just not enough. This game is so worn out in its tropes, it even has the “cannibal family” storyline in it.This game is just unoriginal and trite. I expected so much more and I am done forcing myself through this.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: On the one hand, good on the company for painstakingly rebuilding what appears to be from the user experience end literally, exactly the engine and asset list from Fallout 3, I presume from scratch.That said... a really, really bare-bones RPG that plays more like a Fallout 3 reskin than a new game?  With a 100% linear story with no player agency and no actual meaningful impact of player choices, with juuuuuuust enough of the fake-choice stuff that stopped fooling anyone a decade ago in RPG design to make that linearity and lack of player agency an annoying deficiency instead of a forgivable design choice?You guys are better than this.  I give this produce one point out of five or so for at least having the cojones to write the story with a very clear political message instead of trying to bland it down to nothing, but 1/5 is a fail.  Especially from this studio.  Come on, guys.  We know you're better than this.  You game that was LITERALLY a Fallout 3 mod was better than this, by MILES.

_childDocuments_.review: My name is Hush. I used to be a game design person. I have too many games.So I've started a mission to clean out my entire Steam library! I'll do this by beating all of my games and reviewing them. TLDR at the Bottom of Each Section.6/10/2021The Outer WorldsOverview:I'm way late to this party. I probably will be for most of my games! The Outer Worlds is the worst type of game. A game that was on the brink of being something REALLY amazing, but just falls short. The Story:The story of The Outer Worlds is really engaging. You can really sink your teeth into it, and if you take the time, read a lot of the  journal entries about the company employees, you will find an interesting plot that will suck you in. The problem? They Never really get around to introducing big plot points. I spent most of this game wandering around planet to planet, not really knowing anybody on “The Board” ( The Outer Worlds big villain). I didn't know who Chairman Rockwell was, what he looked like, or really what he was doing for a good 90% of the game. I NEVER knew who Sophia Akande was, until I put a bullet in her because she was shooting at me. I spent most of the game walking around and wondering, “What is the point?” and having several existential crisis’s. I feel like the villain of this game should have been a big overarching crippling character in most of Halcyon's colonies. For as much damage as They had done, I sure didn't see much of a representation of them anywhere in the game at all. The game just keeps assuring you that they are bad, tells you some info about them, and moves on. Even when you eventually get to the main city of Byzantium the place is almost completely empty. Sure, it's filled with a couple pompous idiots, but where are the resources that are being drained from everyone? Why is the city so ran down? Why is everything broken? Then they hit you with a right hook: THE WHOLE COLONY IS ACTUALLY FAILING! The game becomes accelerated to a million miles an hour. Lots and lots of plot points are happening really quickly. Almost as if they forgot to put the rest of the story in the early part of the game where it was very slow. Before you know it, it's over. Somehow by killing two people I eliminated the whole Board. There never was a big boss battle. It just... Ends…Strange.5/10 - “What just happened?”TLDR: Story is pretty blah. It has the makings of being a good story, but they executed in the most wild and silly way ever. It ends pretty unremarkably.  A good message in bad packaging..Characters:I felt no emotional connection to anybody in this entire video game other than Parvati. No one else was believable. I really wish I had more to put in here, but I really don't remember anybody That I met along the way that I would say is a standout character. Maybe SAM the cleaning unit. He had some funny moments. 5/10- “Remarkably average.”TLDR: Parvati is the only good one. Gun Play:The Gunplay was pretty cool until you realized that the whole gun Market is controlled by certain companies in this game. Whether this was by Design or not, there was a very limited amount of weapons. Each company brought to the table a pistol, rifle, heavy weapon, and possibly a sniper. I opted for the heavy weapons because I think big guns are “sweet as ♥♥♥♥”.Now I may have had a weird experience in this game, but somewhere around halfway through the game I found this minigun made by Spacers Choice that was just WILDLY overpowered for some reason. Then I started to find more, and figured it was pretty normal so I started to give them to my companions. The game after this became boringly easy. I was already playing  the Hard difficulty setting and found myself just casually walking through places. In an effort to make it harder, I had to use different guns. But it seems like what I was mostly encountering was either now weapons that were woefully underpowered or capable of creating a crater the size of Texas. I'm really surprised that in a game that is controlled by a giant corporate Overlord there isn't some sort of underground Gunrunner movement or black-market weapons? You can have all sorts of very fun exciting things there but instead they often stick with the boring and call that reality.Let's talk about science weapons. I didn't use these for about 75% of the game because I didn't know they existed. Again, I have no idea how I was supposed to be introduced to these, but I found one by accident and then was prompted by a series of missions where I can go get more! “Ohhh, ok.  This is why the guns have been so boring this game! It’s because I didn't even know there was a whole other half!” I was wrong. There are about four of these.   Each one of them is pretty fun in their own right, but two of them are completely useless. The Gloop Gun is my far the best. The Shrink Ray and the Mind Control Ray are both very fun to play around with in concept, but don't make really any sense. Using them was kind of a hassle and didn't render many benefits. Modding feels pretty boring and doesn't really change much about the weapon unless you're changing the energy type or ammo type. Tinkering with weapons for some reason costs money and not components and you don't really grow attached to any weapons because they all look the same and act the same.5/10-  “I want my black market guns.”TLDR: Gets really oldGraphics:The graphics feel pretty crisp! I will say that they did do a pretty good job at making you feel like you're on a different planet. Unfortunately The Outer Worlds likes to reuse a lot of the same creatures which is really a bummer. I don't know why raptadons would be on multiple planets, but they find a way to explain that away in the game. To me it seemed like laziness in order to avoid making tons and tons of different creatures. Outside of the city it seemed harsh and dangerous and you can walk around and really enjoy the sights. I think my only complaint is that everything felt so damn empty.7/10 - “They do the job!”TLDR: Too many raptadons. IN CONCLUSION: The Outer Worlds promises a lot and unfortunately just doesn't deliver. Although I am happy to see this type of genre getting a little bit more attention lately, I'm sad to say that this one just didn't meet the standard in my book. Much like space, The Outer Worlds provides a few interesting bits, but the rest is lost in a vacuum. Overall Score: 5/10   “Finished it.”

_childDocuments_.review: This game is boring, which is unfortunate because I was hoping for more. I waited for this game to be available outside the Epic platform, intentionally ignoring news and articles about it with the intention of experiencing it without any preconceptions.The game starts in a humerus fashion with some quirkiness at the start. I am then introduced to "light sidearm weapon 1", a nondescript pistol. It turns out that nondescript weapons are throughout the entirety of the eight hours I played. It kind of reminds me of Borderlands in this sense - you pick up nondescript ammo for your nondescript weapon, which can be modified with nondescript modifications you pick up in nondescript ways from places that sort of make sense, but not really. If you want to make your weapon better, pay money and it's done. No real mechanics to it - you just increase the number of damages it does, and there you go. Boring.Anyway, you get a few melee weapons, find the first character you can speak with, and find a ship that you need to *ALARM* FETCH AN ITEM TO FIX *ALARM*, and are sent to a town full of boring people. A hint to writers: if it's your intention to create a city full of boring people who hate their lives, and that's the first place you're going to subject a player to, what do you expect to have a player experience? Elation? Excitement? Boredom?A compressed conversation with the first denizen I find from the city: "Hello, what's your story?"*ALARM FETCH NUMBER 2* "I'm a grave digger who needs to collect money from living people. Go bother these poor ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ for money plzkthx and come back to me with the money."Then I go inside the town, speak to the town leader, and am given a fetch quest where I get to screw over a bunch of people I don't care about. Fetch quest 3.After that, I go and get a fetch quest about robots (this is a three part fetch quest, fetch quest 4, which extends to 6). Then I get a fetch quest about a religious text (fetch quest 7). Then I get a fetch quest about some medicine (fetch quest 8)...You get experience discovering nondescript locations which are given names to somehow imply importance. The first place I ran into was something like "ship wreckage". I believe I also found "cargo wreckage" and "cave hideout". You're telling me that there's only one of these named instances? Is this the only wreckage in the game? What's the story behind it? Why are there dead bodies all around? What attracted gigantic monkey-beasts to this site to kill all the marauders? None of this is made apparent.There's a lot of garbage which can be collected. Junk can be sold to vendors at prices which imply they're not junk, but money doesn't seem to mean anything because I never really ran into a proper vendor. Maybe I wasn't paying attention, or maybe I didn't really care at this point. Unsure.Armor is found on the dead. Weapons are scattered everywhere, and ammunition is generic and plentiful. There's no real need for inventory management, you can disassemble everything to its basic components as you acquire it, and making tough choices for bartering isn't really something that you run into.The AI is not fun or smart, the enemy models aren't cool or interesting. Actually they're really generic. I think I ran in to about four or five different marauder models. They have different names, sort of different weapon configurations, and behave the exact same: run toward your character, and hide behind something to fire a weapon. No need to take cover. No need to hide from sniper fire, nothing like that. When you fire a weapon, everyone knows where you are, and make an immediate beeline toward your location. There's some sort of gorilla which comes in three different models - two of the same color, and one different color which is a little bigger and more dangerous.The concept of a company owning people as chattel for their entire life is interesting, but it's played out in the most ham-fisted way possible.An example:Old man: "I AM AN OLD MAN WHO IS DYING. THE COMPANY NO LONGER THINKS I AM WORTH KEEPING AROUND, AND I'M RESOLVED TO MY DEMISE. I NEED A MEDICINE TO LIVE. PLZ HELP OR NOT WHATEVER."Me: "Well golly, that's just awful. I'll be glad to help you out of the kindness of my heart and the money you may or may not give me later on. I just want to drive this story, old man. Whatevs..."*fetch old man medicine*Old man: "THX DUDE. HERE. I GUESS I GET TO KEEP LIVING OR WHATEVER."Me: "yw. have a life or something. I dunno. Bye."Nothing useful or interesting. There's no "good part" to any of this. I am left wondering if helping him live was better than gunning him down right there.The dialogue was skippable, the discussions were mundane, the concept of corporatism and morality is hit with glancing blows. I have no idea why people would pay for a grave site when religion seems to be only mildly adhered to. From a futuristic perspective, why would you care where your body ends up? Are you religious or not? No discussion of an afterlife or heaven, just an intention to deal with ones corporeal leftovers in a fashion which implies that they care where their body ends up. Yet there's LITERALLY DEAD BODIES EVERYWHERE.This game isn't fun. There's nothing good about it. I am really happy Steam offers refunds. Even if I'd pirated it, I would have uninstalled it by now.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game but dislike it just as much for the jarring end.  The Outer Worlds suffers from a problem that plagues Obsidian titles.  They've created such an interesting and compelling new IP then only gave us content to constitute half an RPG.  Just as the game is really starting to pick up steam and you the player are ready to tackle the multiple unused worlds on the galaxy map... it's over.  I would have preferred to wait another year or two than to have a game with such potential end as abruptly as Kotor 2.  Gameplay is stellar, rewarding and very challenging on 'Supernova' mode.  I only played once, on Supernova and finished in 18 hours.  If you're looking for the next Skyrim or Witcher 3 to carry your gaming experience for the next month or two this game is not it.  You'll be done in a week, maximum.  If you're looking for a quick, fun and challenging sci-fi experience with some compelling and quirky characters then you've come to the right game.  Some highlights for me were Parvati's companion quest chain, anything to do with Sam, and Byzantium.

_childDocuments_.review: Corporate lunacy. The Outer Worlds is a bite-sized RPG weaved through ridiculous satire. Some of the time it works, some of the time it doesn't, and that's the tale of The Outer Worlds. If the game manage to stick the landing more on mechanics and story beats, it would've been an incredible game, and while it doesn't stick the landing all the time, at least it takes those swings. That doesn't help some pieces of the game, such as combat, from feeling empty. The jump from Groundbreaker to Monarch is particularly jarring. On the former, the player is jumping from character to character going through dialogue. On the latter, the character spends most of their time fighting creatures and marauders. There's plenty of freedom given to how the player approaches the game, but at its most linear, the pacing leaves a lot to be desired.Nonetheless, The Outer Worlds is full of fun characters and engaging side quests. There are multiple ways to approach each section, sometimes resulting in multiple outcomes. It's an RPG you can jump into and have a blast without needing to give it too much investment. It's also very easy and very short. I was able to complete the main story on the hardest difficulty in under an hour (using some speedrun techniques). Go in expecting a *good* RPG and you'll get a good RPG. Not a great one, not a bad one, but a *good* one.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed the Outer Worlds, it really scratched an itch I didn't know I had for a fallout-style space western game. It has its limitations, a lack of mechanical depth in certain areas, but its clear that these largely arise from a limited budget during development. For what it is, The Outer Worlds is an excellent and enjoyable game. The writing and voice acting is really good, all things considered, and definitely beats out that seen in comparable Bethesda games. The factions and world are interesting and the companions and side-characters are well developed and extremely likeable. The gameplay is good, but not exceptional. I can't pick out anything specifically wrong with the gunplay and combat, other than it just seems a little off at times. I think the game could maybe benefit from a more developed combat HUD, since I often found myself losing track of enemies, but that could just be a skill issue on my part. As a fan of Firefly, I think the Outer Worlds captured the vibe and feel of that setting very well, and I really appreciated the homage paid to the series. One of my larger critiques would be the weapons. There are simultaneously a lot of them, yet few feel particularly distinct. This even goes for the unique weapons, which rarely have an effect that makes them stand out beyond just a stat boost, and as far as I'm aware (outside of the Science Weapons) none have unique models or textures to differentiate them from regular weapons of their type. The one unique weapon that stood out to me was Irion's Flintlock, which had a truly unique effect, firing in two-round bursts rather than single shots like the regular variant of the pistol. It would have been nice to see more things like this, unique effects that are more than just a specific stat modifier, or an effect that can be made obsolete through modifying a regular weapon at a workbench. The inability to modify unique gear also remains a huge drawback. Ultimately though, I'd highly recommend the game, and I can't wait to see what Obsidian can accomplish with more resources going forward. I'd give the game a solid 7 or 8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the epitome of wasted potential. Save your money... I bought and played through this game in a relatively short time. I basically powered through it - AND the DLC. I was VERY interested at first - it seemed to start off so well. By the end I was just wanting to get it over with, and the end comes VERY quickly and abruptly. The DLC added a decent amount - but it ultimately felt pointless.I did not go into this expecting it to be fallout, like so many other people. I was perfectly happy with it at most being like 'fallout lite' - but even that, it wasn't. The very streamlined natured of the mechanics - while still feeling 'deep' had me really hooked, but I thought they would start shallow and then get deeper as time went on. They didn't. Like, AT ALL.The way the mod system works (or is PRESENTED to work) suggests there will be a lot of depth and customization but there is not. I pretty much had my loadout decided by level 10, and higher level iterations of it were essentially the same. Each weapon has 3 tiers... none more interesting than the next, just higher numbers. There is only an armor and a helmet slot - but I thought the mods would compensate for that, they don't. The armor 'types' are borderline completely meaningless. Increase defense, boost skills, that's it. The mods BARELY matter at all. The game had SO MUCH WASTED POTENTIAL. It's really such a shame. And all the depth of the decisions you THINK matter wind up being a sentence of exposition in the end-game voiceover, nothing more. There's no sense that any of what I did mattered. I'm tempted to play through it again the opposite of how I played through it the first time in the HOPE that I'm missing some depth, but I doubt it's there, and then I remember how bland the gameplay was and there's just no chance. The characters, the setting, the concept - all great, but the GAMEPLAY was just trash, and I'm sad about it. Legitimately sad.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, I really wanted to like this game. Unfortunately, it missed the mark for me. Many have already written about the subpar gameplay, so I'll skip it here and just highlight some of the game breaking moments for me: 1. Many of the NPC characters that you meet are truly terrible human beings, and some of those folks end up on your own crew. I don't know about you, but I don't need to spend my valuable game time playing alongside people I would rather not be around. And it's not as though they offer a variety of difference between them anyway. Take the robot, take a human - it on't matter - they all fight and do damage on an equal level if you upgrade them and their gear enough.2. Additionally, the ship's AI is just not funny, which is what the designers had aimed for. In fact, she is so annoying and stupidly asinine that if the option to turn her off completely was there, I would have. How anyone could enjoy their interactions is beyond me.  3. Most of the other NPCs that you'll meet are dull and, quite frankly, kind of all the same. This also goes for the weapons, of which there are only a few varieties (you just get more powerful versions of the same weapons as the game progresses), as well as the armor. If you like things looking the same other than a slight color variation, then you're going to be happy.Conclusion:Comparing OTW to Fallout 4 is somewhat unavoidable, despite the fact that one is on earth and the other is in space. I know many hated the base building aspects of Fallout 4, but I'd take that over The Outer Worlds and day of the week. The reality is that TOW just isn't that interesting. It's boring, derivative and uninspired. And in a video game designed to entertain, that's simply inexcusable.

_childDocuments_.review: Playing the Outer Worlds was a lot like paying for a Ferrari and getting a Honda Civic. It still gets you from A to B, but at the end of the day you are left wondering why you paid top-tier price for mid-tier performance. The story had less depth than a bathtub, the side-arcs were about as exciting as cold oatmeal and Obsidian still stubbornly refuses to properly optimize its games so as to prevent infuriating micro-stutter while in open areas (looking at you Monarch). Also I'm not sure what your creative team has against in-game romances, but it makes your games ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and really shows the lack of talent present in your studio.TL;DR: Wait for at least a 75% off sale f you want to play this. It just isn't worth 80 bucks.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: It feels like this game was rushed in many aspects. The writing is quite good, there are many sub-stories that are interesting to dive into and companion's quests are a nice touch. The world design however, while graphically astounding at first, is way more linear that it pretends to be. Character creation and intro are decent.In a general sense, I think the game is way too easy on normal difficulty and I fear it will be on hardcore because of the profusion of resources. If you have quest-OCD like I do and complete every quest before taking new ones, you will end up steamrolling the rest of the game for hours (I'm talking like un-subtle progression, one-shoting every mob). Maybe, try playing on higher diffculty from the start if you want some challenge.The enemies aren't very diverse (marauders, raptidons, insect-like thingies and gorillas on scylla ... did I forget something ?).
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished first time completing the game and both DLCs, took over 85 hours to finish it all of it. Looking forward to playing again and experimenting with different skills and choices. Very stable on PC platform for me. I very much enjoyed the story, the artwork, the graphics, the characters. Not as "Open World" as I like, For me I would have liked the option to personalise/customise my captains quarters but I guess you can't have everything.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: The game is...fine. The graphics are passable, the weapons and crafting system are standard, some of the characters are moderately interesting, but this game is really just a sci-fi reskin of more modern Fallouts, but with downgraded graphics. Instead of raiders, you have "marauders" and even the ammo boxes look the same with just a few greebles added on and the color palate changed.I love Fallout, but this was just such a lackluster copy that I honestly can't be bothered to go further in the game, searching the same abandoned settlements, picking up the same items but with a slightly more dull setting, which is strange because on paper it sounds great! Getting to run around to various planets on missions with your companions (you can take up to two and they give various bonuses) but the gameplay is just so bog standard and there is just nothing that pops out about this game that makes it worth recommending over Fallout 3/4/NV. And if you've played *any* of those games, there's zero point in buying this one.Very thankful I picked this up on a steep sale because I still regret the $15 or so I paid for it. If you've never played a modern Fallout game and like absurdist sci-fi humor, this might be for you, but anyone else who has experience with similar games, it's a skip.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: If you like KOTOR, or Fallout, or Mass Effect, or Borderlands, this is a good game for you. It has a streamlined loot system so you're not wasting time on inventory management too much. The gunplay/combat is really satisfying. If you're considering whether to buy the DLC - get it before you beat the game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: Game seemed fun for the first hour, but after I entered the city for the first time and got a quest, it crashes to desktop every time I zone back out. It has happened on 2 different saves. I've tried a myriad of fixes that people suggested online (I guess this is a common problem when zoning) but none worked. I can't recommend this.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: I would call this a generic RPG, don't get me wrong it is done well. It has all the necessary mechanics and they are polished, mechanically this game is very good. However it lacks a certain spark, it lacks a soul if you will. While playing the game I was initially interested in the story, but I quickly became bored with it, I never felt attached to the characters, everything felt generic and not immersive. The side quests, armors and weapons feel bland and uninteresting,  not once have I found an armor that I would call cool and nice looking... Same goes for the weapons.I am really on the fence about this one, however I give this one a negative score, because I finished it half way and I am not planing to pick it up again.

_childDocuments_.review: New Fallout New VegasIts pretty much New Vegas except in a more Borderland-ish setting and with an engine capable of rendering normal human faces.Theres multiple zones instead of a single big world. Most of them arent that big but i didnt mind, kept them unique and detailed enough without 30% being filler consisting of samey buildings and funnily posed skeletons.Minor nitpicks :Unfortunately while theres the possibility to make a low intelligence character this doesnt result in dumb or radically different dialogue like in Fallout 1/2, its more an occasional choice like with any other dialogue check.Flimsy reasons for some companions to join up. Theyre ok otherwise but if they werent the obvious sidekicks of the game id prolly told some of em to go away (which you can do).Good stuff, recommended
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR Fallout in spaceIts immediately clear some heart went into this game. Dialogue and voice acting are great, choices feel meaningful, game world is populated with lots of things to see and feels lived in. It’s not perfect however as weapons and combat felt a little lacklustre to me. Overall story is good but not remarkable. If there is an overall narrative theme, its that Corporations are evil and the whole setting is built on this notion. It gets old very quickly. One thing that I am grateful for is no-microtransactions. This is one of the reasons I never bothered with Fallout 76 and its nice to return to an FPS RPG of that style without having to worry about monetisation. I really hope Obsidian go onto make more of this style of game. They are clearly great at it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: Being a hardcore Mass Effect fan I never thought I would see any game that could potentially get my attention to the same degree. Yet I now believe that this game being a unique mixture of Fallout and Mass Effect (with a flavour of Kotor here and there) has all the rights to set new RPG standards in the coming decade. Obsidian are surely full of surprises and can take on a leading role that used to be Bioware's in the past. I hope to see more games like it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: It's an actual space colony game. It is from the team that created Fallout so the setting is charming, the people are cool, and the factions are neat. The crew are all well realized, and the mechanics are better than a lot of games. Combat was the part I liked the least, but honestly it's fine, my only major issue was that a lot of the goons look the same, and there are some endgame areas that have multiple factions present, which made this section hard as they will react to friendly fire. There are some bugs here and there but honestly I didn't mind them.Game feels like it was made with some love. My only true complaint is that I wish it were longer and bigger, which won't be an issue as they're making another soon.

The worlds just feels empty. While the story lines are nice the game is overall a bit on the short side. The game is good but not great, but I do recommend it.
