_childDocuments_.review: As a longtime fan of Fallout New Vegas, I enjoyed this game. It was shorter than I expected (35 hours with all side quests and a lot of exploration), but I'm okay with that. Combat was definitely an improvement over Bethesda titles, which was nice. I might suggest playing this on a harder difficulty for experienced players. The array of weapons, armor and mods are initially are cool, but become repetitive. Loot similarly isn't very rewarding. By the end game you probably don't need to pick up anything. The perk system is pretty amusing and the idea of phobias to counter balance your character is fun if you're more into the RP side of things. I was not, so I never took any extra perks, which already by the end game seem superfluous. Overall, I found the game to be a nice romp through the creative minds at Obsidian and though the experience was short, it was fun while it lasted.

_childDocuments_.review: Nice, solid gameplay with Elder-Scrolls-style combat. Well furnished maps with options for all the gamer types, from sneaky scout to brute force bludgeoner. Well thought out, immersive world, with fun enough storyline, plenty of sidequests, and good humor. The Item + crafting system is a wee on the meek side, though. Missing skip option in dialogues makes you think twice about chatting up your more long-winded companions. The current price is a tad high for the amount of content in a solo game, IMHO, but definitely worth buying for an RPG fan when it's on sale.7.5/10 from me. Going up to 8.5 once the price is halved.Also, the game might grow if expanded properly, let's see if there's more DLC coming...

_childDocuments_.review: IntroCaptain of the unreliable I presume? Solid RPG with an interesting backstory, although a little shallow at times. In my mind this is a shorter version of what Fallout 76 should have been.Story – SPOILER ALERTThe outer worlds starts with you being resurrected by a ‘crazy scientist’ who says you need to help him free he others. Sounds familiar although I don’t know from where. You go on to become a leader of a ‘rebel-kind-of-group’ which decides what is best for them. You have multiple options when completing quests, and after having finished one run, I am certain I can reach 2 different endings than what I had at this point. Personally, I think the writing of the overall story has a solid base, but it lacks that final oomph, that little spark which could have really set this game apart. Don’t get me wrong, I loved going through missions and I almost never felt bored doing quests. But I feel like there could have been more. Certainly, at the end of the story, I felt as if there could have been an ‘act two’, as the final battle comes relatively quick. Overall, enjoyable and on certain points quite original. 7/10GameplayBefore addressing the gameplay, I must admit I left a big chunk out of my playthrough. I didn’t use consumables (other than the occasional attribute inducer), heavy weapons, melee weapons and slow-motion combat. This certainly limits my view of the entirety of it, but I still feel I can accurately say: It is good but needs a little bit of work. At the start, surviving was difficult, and I found myself dying more than I expected, not helped by the awful and garbage heal-system (Come on guys, fix this s***). Spamming ‘heal’ during combat and hoping you get a little room to breathe thanks to your companions isn’t constructive nor fun. After a while however, when putting skills into specific perks (long ranged, crit damage, …) the combat became a breeze towards the endgame. Looting, stealing, transporting and going about felt satisfying most of the time and fit right into the theme of the game. Although, I must clarify that this is not a ‘borderlands’ kind of loot. You find a good gun, upgrade it to whatever max it goes at your current level and then use it for the rest of the game. I used exactly 5 different weapons from 3 classes throughout the entirety of the game and was disappointed that I just started selling everything I looted. No loot had a specific value or advantage, everything was just replaceable.Overall, fine for a casual playthrough, although a little bit shallow. 6/10 (7/10 If combat was a bit better).MusicThe music in the outer worlds never really stood me by, but I think of this as a good thing. Never had I felt that it distracted me from the game or its gameplay. I enjoyed the encompassing soundtracks, Although I have a hard time remembering any specific thing about it now… 7/10Artstyle / graphicsThe graphics of this game are fine. Just, fine. Not bad, not the best I’ve ever seen (certainly in this day and age), but it didn’t take away from anything. I liked the artstyle from the start and loved the environments. Variation was not the most important value when developing this game, as every asset is the same on every planet, but this can be addressed to story-related reasons. Lootbox = yellow, door open = grey, door closed = red. Could it benefit from better graphics? Hell no. Could it benefit from more assets and more variation in these assets? Certainly. Overall 7/10Oh and I have to mention: The first 10 minutes I had to adapt to the first-person view of this game. It was really difficult to focus on my screen and not get sick. I have never experienced something like this and at first I thought it was a setting that got screwed up. After session 2 or so, I got pretty used to it. Still, people with glasses or depth-perception problems, beware.AftermathWhen finishing the game, I didn’t feel empty, I didn’t feel the urge to overthink everything or wanted to start the whole experience again. Instead, I thought ‘wait, what? Done already?’ It felt like whole sections where left out of the game, or as if the second half was left for a second game. Leaving the game felt a little incomplete, but returning and starting over again knowing where it will end again kind of deters me. I will probably not play this game again for the coming years, but that doesn’t mean I didn’t enjoy my time.To summarizeOverall, the outer worlds is a good game with a solid base. Although noting really stood out to me (personally), I enjoyed playing and was kind of invested in some of the characters. As for the total score, I value the whole game a lot more than just the sum of its parts. The latter would result in a 6.5/10, but this game deserves a lot more. Everything together puts me in a place where I can easily recommend this for the standard price, IF you are into the RPG-genre. If not specifically or if you are just curious, picking this up on a discount is an absolute win.  Final score 8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good game - dying genre. A wonderful and pleasant journey in open world, that is more than rich in several factions, places of interest and side quests to get full imersed into the world. Solid 30-40 hours of single-playthrough of gameplay with high re-playability.Absolutely wonderful leveling system, which allows you to pick 'the way you want to play' - without 'punishing you' for 'not taking' certain traits and skills. You can absolutely "ruin" your character and still finish game smoothly (yes, you will be lacking in several apsects, but you wont 'lock yourself away')Armors that are plesant visually. Weapon customization system which is simple, but not 'insulting' to the player. Colorful (both litreally and methaporically) world with interesting characters. Here and there you can see certain 'flaws' - some planets are "insultingly small", and content which is put on them could be easily fit into some 'more empty' places on 'bigger planets', as well as only 2 companions seemed to have actually 'bigger' quests line to their names - max and parvatti (if i dont butcher the name) - it took about 'hours and some' to finish their quests - other? Minutes - it "smelled a little bit" of devs being rushed.That aside - Weapons? Beautiful. Ammo system? simple and enjoyable. Game is often funny, sometimes dreadful. Game worth full price and 'cheff kiss' to whole staff. More of that please!!!Solid 9/10 title

_childDocuments_.review: When this game was first released 1 year ago it had its gameplay issues. I played it for a few hours and noticed it is just not worth my time, gave the devs my feedback and hoped for the best when the game comes to steam.Now it is here and I am still not impressed. What bothered me 1 year ago is still there, no fixes, no improvements, no optimization.The graphics are actualy not that "superb", and yet, I have a good pc, running various games at max settings in 3k without problems, but outer world freezes at lowest possible settings every 5 steps.THere are still functions with locked key bindingsThere are still functions without a keybinding.There is still no manual opening of picklocks/security, if you do not have the "scriptes" number of tools with you, you are out of luck. That is a realy cheap way to limit the players progress in an open world.Companion commands are clunky and very limited, the AI is very bad.When you are not a top notch player, you are out of luck. Open world especialy RPG games offer you some sort of grind, if something becomes too hard, you go get some extra levels. Not in outer worlds.And the worst, the interaction of other people was not optimized. You initiate a dialogue and when you are lucky, the NPC talks back, when not (like 75% of the time) you wait few second, up to 2 min so far, starring at the NPC and waiting till s/he starts talking. Best "scenario" so far... entered Hawthornes ship for the first time, so at the very beginning of the game, got the subtitles when Ada says there is nothing that can be stolen, but the voice did not say anything until I was already full in converation with her. Thats just... Extremely immersion breaking. Everytime you talk to someone you just do not know whether it progresses normaly or you have to wait an unknown amount of time.1 year ago I had not, but cant remember anymore. This time, I have enough after 78minutes. Going for a refund, doubt it this game will be fixed.

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished a playthrough on Normal difficulty that took about 50 hours.Pros:  Good graphics, beautiful imagery.   This is a really pretty game, even when it's being gritty and soulless.  It's got solid shooter characteristics, and a well built combat engine.  It's also bug free as far as I can tell, during play I did get a couple of CTD incidents but frankly those could easily have been problems with my rig.  The writing is great, it feels somewhere between Fallout and Borderlands in tone.  Voice acting is high quality, and there are no text only conversations.Cons:  the combat engine feels like it has things missing, with no grenades, no cover shooting, and limited customization.  Well, actually customization is pretty open, its just most of the mods have little obvious use.  Unique weapons are base models instead of the upgrades that start appearing as you level, so I never found one that was worth using.  "Science weapons" also were so statistically inferior that they didn't seem any better than just plain shooting people in the face.  The damage system is a little opaque, so other than "use electricity against robots" I'm not sure what plasma, acid, and n-rays are for.  Weapons "tier up" as you progress through the game, but this bump happens fairly early on, and there is only one, so equipment improvement virtually stops half to two thirds of the way through the game.All in all, I consider this a middling game with a top tier story.  I think I got it for 25% off, and I would recommend it to anyone at that price point.

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR I give it a 6/10 for effort by the team, save the writers.I really wanted to like this game, but the story line pretty much broke within the first ten levels of the game because I needed TWICE the amount of "bits" i had (currency) to progress without a giant level gap when there are literally no other quests in the entire universe around my level. The lady says let's make a deal, so I made the deal. But the deal wasn't for the super expensive thing, it was just a generic task and she didn't really reward me with anything. (I even loaded my game because I ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up, went back, and found this out. Very disappointing)The weapon choices are dull and the mods for them are generic and don't change much except for armor penetration and damage type, more ammo, more zooming, etc. The price of upgrading the damage became needlessly exponential without an equivalent damage bonus.I didn't think the followers were too cut and dry, but they would want to join you way too quickly. Though the dialogue was without brevity (though the writers know that word, surprisingly) and I found myself skipping it way faster than I care to admit. Another thing is that people talk in a lot of archaic dialects, e.g. saying afore instead of before. This does not make sense, seeing as how it's in the future. I don't know who started this trend, but please stop it.I do think the game is very pretty, and gives me a borderlands mixed with bioshock vibe, but that isn't something I care about much anymore, to be honest.Within ten minutes of playing I noticed gaps in the mapping, (I could see through a rock and the level into the void, for example) and noticed a few more within my short time playing the game. Just seems a bit rushed.Hope this helped you make a decision.

_childDocuments_.review: Aloha, this is my review of Outer Worlds. A FPS RPG set in a science fiction dystopian future, and plays like the love child of Fallout, Max Payne, Bioshock got drunk and watched Flash Gordon. You are the lone wanderer, awakened from a lost colony ship and can choose to help [or kill] the inhabitants of Halcyon. I played as a stupid "Starbarian" that punched, shot, and stabbed through the galaxy to a bowl of ice cream. The game is an space themed amusement park, you pass through, shoot the cans, talk to the fortune teller, leave with your stuffy space gorilla.The Good: the graphics were colourful, the setting was unique, combat was fun [you get to use Bullet time to do strategic attacks], character customization was decent with multiple builds being viable, and sliding difficulty and multiple factions and paths to take to encourage multiple plays. The story was decent, from what I could tell and there are multiple ending depending on who you help or kill. I really liked that I was able to play through the entire game by shooting mindlessly until the end and still got a half decent ending, even after eradicating an entire town [something that would usually plot break another game] the game was like "Okay, their company now hates you and charges you 50% more" instead of the usual "you can't kill him, plot armour reasons", I even killed one of the main companions accidentily because of this, so good on you.The Bad: The characters were unique... but spelt yuniqweh, everywhere you went there was "Hey, I'm quirky, notice how quirky we are." then they would say or do something to tell me how quirky they were. After the first hour I started skipping most of the dialogue, because Lord suffering was it bad. The characters were flatter the further you played, and the more cardboard cut outs I saw, the more I shot. Until eventually it was like an Undertale genocide run. The companions were meh, and I spent most of the game with the emotionless robot that was obsessed with cleaning, because we shared a similar goal, eradicating all life. Which despite my best efforts to play a stupid "Starbarian" I got a pretty decent and optimistic ending, with ice cream!The Ugly: "Don't worry boss, I'm good with numbers."

I felt like this is just a game that I just go to a destination, talked with some NPCs, shoot stuff and end quest. I tried to search every nook and crannies, I can't find anything that's worth seeing. Everything is just the same & repetitive. The only differences are different dialogues, NPCs & enemy models & difficulty. Where's the "Grandma Gangs", the "Holy Hand Grenades", the tiny details?Should I even invest more time in this game?

_childDocuments_.review: This game is like if Fallout: New Vegas had been removed from the Fallout universe and set in space instead.  The setting is more reminiscent of the Borderlands universe, with ridiculous corporate entities and space cowboy style.  The writing is great, running the gamut from hilarious to crushingly sad.  The characters are interesting and well-developed.  It would probably be easier to talk about what I haven't liked so far.  The combat is good, but the learning curve is a little rough.  I feel like I'm cheesing most difficult fights, and it's not really clear how the different damage types and mods will affect the various things you fight.  I am learning things by experimentation, but in the early game, the mods are expensive or hard to come by and cannot be retrieved once used.  I made a silenced pistol thinking that it might help to get some stealth kills, but since the pistols don't do a ton of damage per shot, the target will almost always alert anyone nearby before you can finish them.  Also, I've been having a weird interaction where the game keeps detecting my controller and making my mouse cursor disappear.Anyway, I highly recommend the game.  It's what Fallout: New Vegas should have been if Obsidian had been given the time and resources to finish developing the game.  I look forward to anything else they release in the future!

_childDocuments_.review: The Outer Worlds is an action role-playing video game developed by Obsidian Entertainment and published by Private Division. It was released in 2019 and became an Epic exclusive. I guess that is why I'm finally getting around to playing this after so long. Let's dive into it.1. Well-written storyline set in a futuristic world where corporations run all aspects of life.2. The game offers a lot of player choice, allowing you to make decisions that have an impact on the game's outcome. I like how the choices can lead to different endings and affect how other characters perceive you overall.3. The game in my opinion offers a variety of interesting and unique characters, each with their own backstory and personality. I think there is one for everyone here. 4. The game's dialogue system is one of its strongest features, with a wide range of dialogue options that allow you to interact with characters in different ways. You can choose to be persuasive, aggressive, or diplomatic, depending on your playstyle.5. The game's world is incredibly detailed, with a lot of lore and backstory to discover. The various planets you visit all have their own unique environments and cultures, and there are plenty of hidden secrets to uncover.6. The game features a lot of humor, with witty dialogue and satirical commentary on modern-day society. The game doesn't take itself too seriously and has a fun and lighthearted tone.The game has been well recieved by player and the critics. There are things I would have liked to see improved.1. Some players including myself criticize the game's main story for being relatively short, with some players completing it in around 20 hours. For me it leaves me feeling unsatisfied and kind of sad.2. I feel like the game's weapon selection is somewhat limited. I find the weapon upgrade system rather simple in design. Which isn't a bad thing. However, I feel like they could have done more here. I think that maybe this was one of the last things they worked on before getting it out the door.3. The game's side quests can be repetitive, with similar tasks and objectives appearing throughout the game. I really feel this is something that really needs to be improved on their follow up if there will ever be one. I feel for a space adventure there is all kind of situations you could have put me the player in that they didn't. 4. There really isn't enough replayability for me. with not enough different choices leading to drastically different outcomes.5. Where the hell is the romance options?6. Slapping players in the face with that lame ass SPACERS CHOICE upgrade. It's like they took a page out of the in game corporations playbook to just slap people in the face. Don't waste your time or money on that hot garbage.Lastly I want to close with this. Having a page up on steam and then only going EPIC exclusive. That I bet impacted the sales of this game. I didn't touch this game for a long time. An no way would I buy it at full price. I used game pass to play this when it dropped. I will never purchase a game at full price that is an exclusive on another platform. It's not worth it to me as a consumer.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: If you liked Fallout: New Vegas, you'll get a lot of fun out of this too. You can easily get 30-40 hours out of this, but it has issues. Get it on sale. I highly recommend getting the Peril on Gorgon expansion, it's some of the best storywork in this game.Setting:A rogue scientist gets onto a lost ship floating in space with hundreds of colonists frozen in suspension. He only has the time and resources to unfreeze one of them, and that's you. It's a dystopian (or utopian if you're a libertarian) hellscape where corporations own everyone's life, and their children's lives through employment contracts. Most people barely survive, to feed the elite living in luxury in Byzantium. A group of the biggest corporations form the ruling council for the solar system called The Board. Together with the scientists, you have to go out and save the rest of the colonists and break The Board's tyranny (or not, if you want), picking up side-quests, companions, and shooting stuff along the way.Graphics:The game generally looks very pretty, often. Really gives you the "spacer" experience. However, there are not a lot of different planets to go to, but they still look very similar (except the gorgeous one in the DLC). It's kind of the same trap that most space-themed games fall into. They say you can visit loads of different planets, but they still all look like a brown/green blob. Visually, it's like Fallout and Borderlands, with a good dose of Bioshock, especially in the cities. The characters also look really well in conversations, although the faces could have shown a bit more emotion.Gunplay:Being a Fallout-esque game, you're gonna be in fights a lot. This is probably the most lackluster part of the game, sadly. The weapon variation is pretty low, and the shooting is pretty boring. There is sort of like a bullet-time mechanic, but it's nowhere near as fun as Fallout-gunplay (as broken and dumb as it is). There is weapon-augmentation, but very basic. The enemy variation is also pretty low. You got your crazy bandits, bug-monsters, robots and monkey-monsters. That's pretty much it. There are some cool melee weapons and some crazy "science weapons" /which require you to spec into for them to do any damage), so to maximize your fun, I would advice one of those builds. Gameplay, dialogue and choice:Being a Fallout-esque game, dialogue is going to be a central aspect of this game. And this is where it has it's strength. The voice acting is pretty solid through and through and the dialogue is mostly very well written and often quite funny. But it's funny in a very dark way, since the setting is so dystopian. It also has the computer files you can read, that we all know and love from Fallout, and they're also very well written. The companions you pick up go from very interesting to completely forgettable. Each companion has their own questline. The two first, you pick up, Parvati and Vicar Max, are by far the best ones. Parvati is an asexual lesbian engineer, who falls in love with another engineer and has you set up the perfect date. Max is a vicar in the corporate propaganda religion, but struggles with his faith and the meaning of life. None of your companions can be romantic partners, which is honestly refreshing. Also, this game doesn't have a dialogue wheel, like in Mass Effect or Fallout 4, which is great.The game takes a dive into different ideologies and looks at life. However, I wish it went a bit more in-depth. For instance, on one planet, two factions are fighting: one is a company that was pushed out of the board. The company isn't completely horrible to it's employees and tries to do good for them, but they're under embargo from the board and can't afford providing very much for the employees. On the outskirts of town, the former partner of the CEO went his own way after an argument and has now formed a sort of anarchist militaristic cult. He thinks he's better suited to run the town. You have to decide what to do, and get to have conversations with them about their ideologies. My problem is that it doesn't really go deep enough. I have conversations about the fundamentals of these ideologies that I don't get to ask. This game has been held up as some sort of scathing criticism of capitalism, but it really isn't. It doesn't really ever dive into capitalism or alternatives to capitalism. You will never encounter a socialist in this game, and you don't really get to be one yourself. This game has loads of different endings (although they are mostly variations on about 4 basic endings), but none of them end in a fundamental change of the economic system.This game also handles the choices where there are no clear cut answers and where you can see benefits and detriments to the different solutions. This is seen in the first major choice of the game compared to the first major choice in Fallout 3. (LIGHT SPOILERS FOR THE FIRST MAJOR CHOICE IN BOTH GAMES). In Fallout 3, your first major choice is to either nuke a city, or help them. In The Outer Worlds, the first major choice is about where you want to supply the power. There is a small town, where people are literally being worked to death and there is a plague. The robots in the power plant went haywire, killed the workers, and now no one can get in there (although it is heavily implied that the robots went "haywire" on purpose so that the corporation owning the settlement could collect the insurance). There is also a very enviromentalist faction that has formed a settlement in the outskrits where their leader has managed to spread some plants and returned nature somewhat. The settlement is mostly made up of deserters from the town (quitting your job is punishable by death) and they grow their own food and seem much happier. The leader of the corporation in town wants you to divert the power to the town, destroying the enviromentalist settlement and the nature there, hopefully leading the deserters back to work, so they can raise productivity and make the lives better for the inhabitants, but you don't really know if that's going to work. The leader of the enviromentalists wants you to divert all the power there so she can continue her work, however, this would render the town out of power, making lives worse for a lot of people who can't make their way to the settlement. She also gives off a vibe of wanting the town to suffer. There was more detail in the game, but this choice was actually very difficult.Overall, an enjoyable experience, but clearly has some issues and could go much more in-depth. I'd give it a 7/10, buy it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Haven't yet played the expansions, so this is for the base game only. Started Outer Worlds about a week ago and have been coming back to it every day until I finished it, which is telling because I tend to jump around games quite a bit. Don't expect Fallout in space, it's not one large open world - but takes place across numerous fairly large hub areas which you're more or less free to explore at your leisure as and when you gain access to them.Plenty of side quests to keep you busy and from my initial playthrough, there seemed to be a good deal of choices to personalise your journey. There were numerous moments where I actually had to stop and think which option was the morally better one and the impact was usually noticeable - immediately and further down the line. Needless to say, I'll be making alternative choices in a subsequent game and I'm sure it'll be a different adventure.The shooting/combat is fun. There's a good amount of customisation for weapons (and weapon types) to keep things interesting. I liked my companions too - spent more time with some than others, but all were fun to adventure with and get to know as the story unfolded.Overall - well worth a play. Completed in 25 hrs but will be returning to do quests I've missed and try out other choices.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has significant similarities to the fallout series, once adopted by Bethasda.  It's different in some ways, where the entire visual scheme is a little more cartoonish (but not so bad like borderlands).  The game play itself leads to some rewarding firefights, but I have to say that they tend to either end quickly or drag on far too long (against primals, for example).  Companions either kill enemies too fast or die too fast.  So everything is quite fast paced.The perk system was made with fallout in mind (10 skill points per level, perk every 2 levels), but the perks themselves are kind of dissatisfying after a while.  The game play does seem quite repetitive, but it's ok; I'll do it.One thing that is nice is the ability to fly to other worlds/areas.  Having that additional degree of openness is somewhat unique and refreshing.  I'm on the "recommend" side of the fence, but I'd recommend getting it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: From the studio that gave us Fallout: New Vegas comes... basically that, but their own original IP.There's a lot to like here - the writing can be very, very good and runaway corporate power is a more 21st century setting than the freaking cold war.  It's pretty great to go from outlandish stuff like a colony getting fines for allowing 'company property' (people) to commit suicide or a vendor contractually obligated to speak in slogans while wearing a mascot hat to "oh, and now they're mishandling a pandemic for short term gain and only the corporate elite have healthcare."  Oh, and they do a pretty good job letting you use your stats and skills in conversation and your conversation skills in combat, which is pretty nice.There's also a lot to dislike, though - combat is pretty bland for a game with this kind of pedigree and for all it's scathing criticism the game doesn't have a lot to say beyond "corporations bad, science good" which feels like a missed opportunity.  Nor is the central storyline very interesting, a lot of time is spent hinting that your employer may not be on the level and... he 100% is.  Which is fine - I liked the guy - but why spend so much time hinting at it if you're not going anywhere with it?Cool game but not where I'd like it to be.  Maybe they'll do a sequel with the wrinkles ironed out.

_childDocuments_.review: Damn this game is good and very disappointing at the same time :\Coming from Obsidian it has a fun story with plenty choices, but it also keeps reminding me of how much I love and miss Fallout, New Vegas in particular.The good: +++ It's kinda what you may expect, nice scenarios where you can be who you want, do whatever you want, piss off whoever you want, and massacre them too if you feel like it, that's something I always appreciate.+ The general sci fi ambiance and scenery, nice exotic views+ The combat has some nice improvements like the location damage that you can use for status ailments, and the dash move which I have some fun using with my melee character+ Follower control is perfect this time, I like having hotkeys to send them places immediately anytime and trigger their special moves, feels inspired by Mass Effect which is not bad in this regard. This made me have my main character with a follower build.+ Parvati and Nyoka, kinda, Max I thinkThe bad: -- It's not really an open world, you have a handful of places, somewhat open, but somewhat annoyingly linear and often restricted to paths. The playable areas feel tiny and too few, and the travelling between them is annoying, this is something I also recall from Mass Effect but I didn't miss.- The decissions, ew, I often find myself thinking: Why do I have to choose between these 2 things? I'd suggest a bit of this and that. I'm not clever enough or I don't have an otherwise pointless skill high enough to suggest some common sense and I have to stick to taking a lame side in this conversation? Ugh, so be it, I'll pretend the bs didn't happen during the ending.- The combat again, yeah it has nice new touches but it still feels obsolete in a world where games like Dying Light exist and have plenty moves to keep things interesting- The balance is non existent, I find great difference between builds, a companion focus seemingly overpowered in all senses compared to other archetypes, damage wise and skill wise with the big boosts you get to things like lockpicking or dialog.- How useful everything is, is never clear from the very beginning when you have no idea what you're selecting for your character attributes, let me respec everything including the basics, any limitation to this is a massive waste of time.- Ellie and Sam.It's still money well spent, much more so during a nice sale.

_childDocuments_.review: A rushed console-port means an unoptimized mess.  Performance is terrible, even on high-end systems, even years after it was first published.  Stutters, dropped frames, crashes, you name it.Support for the game is no longer done by Obsidian, but Private Division.  Differing graphical settings (low, medium, high, ultra) are barely noticeable in-game.No low gore/dismemberment/gibbing setting.  Priced like a triple-A game when it simply isn't.  You should avoid until they improve the game.Will revisit my review if Obsidian/Microsoft/whomever stops making DLC for the game and instead of fixes the base game.

_childDocuments_.review: Think of this game as Fallout in space with a more scripted interactions and quests.  Moving between worlds keeps content a little interesting.  Monsters are reused,  Lots of different clans/people to meet.If you want to role play a female in a world ruled by women putting up with idiotic men, you've come to the right place.  If you'd rather not, then there is plenty of other options.Start sarcasm: One epic quest takes you on an epic adventure as you talk feelings with your companion encouraging her to start a lesbian relationship with an engineer she met on a space station.  You will spend countless fun filled hours on about 10 different quests baking fish casserole, picking out dresses and being her emotional crutch while she texts this other woman and spills all of the gossip.Sometimes I think they were trying to write a "Life is strange" sequel  and not a dystopian space shooter.

_childDocuments_.review: Good lord, am I disappointed in this game..I've tried several times to like this game. I have given it chance after chance until it's now officially unplayable due to the game crashing to desktop without any warning at the same part of the story every time. I really was looking forward to playing OuterWorlds as I am a huge fan of Obsidian's Fallout NV (which could honestly be my fault to compare the two), but this game was just a complete let down. Even if it wasn't for constant game-breaking crashes, the amount of times I've gotten stuck/glitched on an object and forced to reload is insane for a game that has won so many awards and currently has very positive reviews on steam. Aside from the bugs, the gameplay just felt like a lazy mix of Fallout and Borderlands to me. Cons:- The game has crashed to desktop without warning several times.- The difficulty Supernova is unplayable due to it the crashing or getting stuck on objects. You can't save manually in Supernova so If either happens then you've lost any forward progress that wasn't auto-saved. - The AI companions are dumb as rocks. Also, if you shoot a single enemy within a group then the entire enemy group becomes alerted exactly where you are regardless if they are in different rooms or buildings. - The gameplay is very linear. After playing about 5-6 hours, you've pretty much seen it all aside from some enemies with special abilities or more health. Pros:- The different dialogue options and voice acting is done very well. - The weapons are diverse enough to keep the game somewhat interesting. - The story line was okay. What keeps the game entertaining are the different choices you can make between factions.If I were to rate my overall experience with OutWorlds: 4/10Let me end with this: I bought OutWorlds 50% off and I'd refund if I could. Very disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: This gets a very lukewarm recommendation to me, which honestly means I wouldn't recommend it. I got it at the 50% off price which is the only reason I'm not more disappointed I think. The gunplay feels good, the slow time is fun, the art style is really nice. Those are the things that carried me for 7 hours.The story is poorly paced. It suffers from the device where every character says "I got what you need, but you'll have to do something for me first ;)" which slows down the story immensely. The writing is terrible, which is personal taste to be fair. That said, I can compare it to Borderlands what with the wacky random humor and all. If you liked that then you'll like this. That said, Borderlands wasn't trying to backdrop their game with a critique of political economy and capitalism; what I mean is, the message is conveyed very inelegantly when in the next breath there's some joke about "lol please kill all those unemployed pieces of human garbage! We hate them!" Speaking of that criticism of capitalism, under the view the game puts forth (in the future, corporations will own you and everything about you) this setting probably wouldn't work. Highly concentrated wealth accumulation would occur way before inter-stellar travel would ever be possible, essentially creating a situation where only the incredibly wealthy would be able to leave behind a ravaged earth, assuming said wealth disparity didn't collapse society beforehand. There wouldn't be any people to sell products to in this scenario. The story would have been better served just going the Fallout route and placing the setting in the near future rather than this contradictory space setting. Honestly, the space setting makes talking to NPC's worse. These people live in abject dystopian poverty and the majority act like it's completely normal. I know there are parallels to be made here to our own society, but come on, starvation, plagues, and literal contract assassins when you miss a debt repayment? There would be revolts.The characters are incredibly bland and childish as well, there is a quest where you counsel a companion about her in-progress budding love interest with an NPC that you met no more than ten minutes ago. That's fine if a little fast, but an adult would have a conversation with the object of their affection, not go to a bar and whinge about how relationships are just "so hard for them." This is high school level maturity. To be honest, that's what I felt about both the writing and the voice acting: written/performed by people with the mental maturity of high schoolers. Maybe that's not fair to the voice actors, they work with what they're given after all.Speaking more about the gameplay, it's pretty shallow. Perks simply increase health, carrying capacity, slow time gauge, etc without any real variance to gameplay. Weapons are not very dissimilar to one another meaning looting is unsatisfying. There's also a flaw system where you can take a flaw to take an extra perk, but the flaws are way worse than the benefits of a perk which makes the mechanic pointless. Quests devolve into "do this task for me if you want this mcguffin, and I'm very evil!" and when you get halfway through the quest you meet someone else who says "I'm not evil, don't do this to me! Take my side instead!" or you can pay someone money to make the problem go away. Or you can be a psychopath like me since I was getting fed up with everyone's crap and just murder them. This is the level of choice we achieved decades ago. People criticized this sort of thing when KotOR came out AT RELEASE in 2003, it's just not compelling anymore. tl;dr I would be much more upset if I bought this for 60.00 as I said earlier. So if you're thinking about playing and you didn't experience this when it was released a year ago like me, be sure to get it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: A great RPG experience, if over-hyped by professional games journalists/reviewers.  Don't expect anything new, or revolutionary here.  The combat, level design, and story are all serviceable, but none of it really stands out in any way.  It's basically the video game version of a summer "popcorn blockbuster" movie.  The main story itself gets pretty tired, and I recommend taking breaks from it to play through the DLC stories as soon as they become available, and as soon as you've got the character levels and gear to tackle them without getting murdered.  The story can effectively be boiled down to "corporations suck, anarchists suck, hippies suck, intelligent people suck, dumb people suck, just all people suck, and true progress can only be found by following the path of the Enlightened Moderate and balancing everyone's innate suckiness against one-another."  My one real complaint is in regards to level design.  They attempted to create this game with minimal invisible walls, but for some god-forsaken reason chose to still gate areas by making any textures (other than the ground itself... usually) too "slick" to jump/climb on.  This leads to tons of frustration for anyone trying to get any kind of height advantage over their opponents, or just trying to find a shortcut from one place to another, since you will constantly be getting stuck on/in boulders, rocks, other environmental objects, or just the terrain itself.  It gives all outdoor areas a very slippery, glassy feeling, and can make combat in many portions of the environment just a chore.  Treat the outdoor areas as linear experiences, stick to the roads and obvious paths whenever possible, and don't try to jump over/in to any "off-the-rails" areas unless you can actually see something there to go get (e.g. an item chest).Still, it's a good game to pick up during a dry spell (especially on sale) and just play 'till you're done with it, or something better comes along, whether or not you've actually finished anything.  Game gets a B- grade, just don't go in to it with any grandiose expectations and you'll be fine.

_childDocuments_.review: I am wowwed. Normally I play a game, fight until the end and then I am bored with the game. First I played this game on normal. Then I got frustrated not able to find all the quest objectives. Then I found out I can doubleclick a quest in the journal to help find the objective. Then I got tired of walking from point A tot B... Then I found out the "fast travel" option, which allows to jump from point A to B. I watched 3 or 4 youtube video's when I got stuck (finding the C3 camp). I am not a fan of shoot-um ups. I am a fan of RTS and RPG's. I REALLY like the options and consequences of the dialogue. The goodDialogue, choosing your own path, choosing between tinkering, or weapons skills, or dialogue or a combination. The game captivates. Good storyline. I fell in love with the characters.It makes me wonder: what if... The badIt is impossible to win this game without using violence I think... Maybe I should try it. Some dialogues are "locked". Which means it does not matter what you say or do, the outcome is the same. When replaying the game there are a lot of terminals which provide background story, but are not necessary to complete the mission or game. There is no way to disable those. I can't remember every spot which is useful of not useful.  The companions backgrounds are uneven. Parvati and Nyoka have great background stories and character. Vicar Max is acting like an angry toddler. Felix is some fun. The robot (SAM) has no real dialogue or background (he came form a crate). Elly is very entertaining to have around, but is not useful in conversations. There is no reason to dump a companion, except for Vicar Max using the toilet all the time. I'd like to choose 3 companions out of 5. Less choice means more thinking it through. Now I just use Vicar max to help me with the end game and his own quests, but no more. Come to think of it: Is it possible to complete the game with no companions?  The ugly.Tinkering weapons and the inventory menu. Ugh. When Parvati is with you, you gain an engineering bonus. When breaking down weapons this is useful. However breaking down weapons on the ship means losing this bonus. Why? Then the following problem arises. I have 2 identical weapons equipped on two different companions. I want to tinker the weapon of companion 1. How do I know which is which? And after tinkering my own weapon I want to switch it with my companion. This is not possible in the workbench menu. I think these menu's could be done better. Also: when selling all my weapons and armor makes it impossible to change weapons between me and my companions. Switching through inventory of companions makes the menu switch to weapons. When comparing armor of 4 companions this is a hassle. When in town I'd like to slip in normal (non-battle) wear with better dialog skill bonuses. No quick switch option available. Overall this game is great. I would recommend it to buy. I completed the game 3 times. 2 times on normal, 1 time on supernova.

_childDocuments_.review: I think before I make this review I need to point out a few things, so that people will understand why I have such an opinion.Outerworlds really is...decent. If you're looking for something like fallout 4 where you can spend thousands of hours upon hours exploring than it aint it fam. This game is dissapointingly short. Like...Really short. It also just generally lacks in content. There's not a lot of armors, not a lot of weapons, not a lot of quests, bare minimum of customizability and at this current state it REALLY needs a modding scene if it wants to be kept afloat for longer and not be forgotten in like 2 years.So WHY am I recommending it if it sounds so "bad" ?Because outerworlds at its core is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ God-tier.I think its important to understand who the main demographic of this game was ment to cater; the Fallout Fandom and RPG fans. Fallout has had some...conterverisal entries lately and has been on a downward spiral of mediocerty, however one of the main reasons why its still going somewhat strong is the fact that its very mod-friendly and things such the world to explore, the gear, the gameplay the side quests ETC.However its fundamental flaw was the lack of a proper core: The role playing elements. The writing in modern fallout games left much to be desired and the lack of roleplaying elements felt insulting to a lot of long time fans. There is also the fact that the series lore had been brutalized and bastardized to a point where it makes people weep.Outerworlds core is however the polar opposite; It lacks in content but makes up with a solid core.  The skills and build will impact your playstyle, your choices actually matter, the charcaters usually tend to feel like characters and not strawmen, factions tend to have decent reasoning and its not half assed to the point where they seem dumb, unreasonable or just lazy (Unless that what the intent), the writing is pretty ♥♥♥♥♥♥ good and the gameplay is pretty based.I'm not going to lie, during a spoiler heavy quest I manage to get two factions who hated each other to work together and the feeling of satisfaction was amazing I genuinly cried. Why?Because I had been waiting for something like this for a LONG time. I missed writing that made sense, I missed characters who were reasonable, I missed factions with motivations that made ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ sense. Sure not EVERYTHING in the quest area is 100% perfect, theres still a bit of IRL political bias here and there sprinkled in the bunch and the writing wasn't done by legends like chris avellone.However it gives me the same vibes I had when I played Fallout NV the first time 8 years ago. It feels like if they had put a tiny bit of effort into extra content and gotten a few more areas instead of having them behind a DLC wall because the game was probably rushed  due to publishers,  and added mod support, the game could have been considered a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ master piece.Honestly I want to personally thank the devs for this. It was good playing a proper RPG with FPS gameplay again. Just hope the next titel or that the next games get better support....though considering how MS bought Bethesda MAYBE we are gonna see some cross studion work? Perhaps leavse bethesda making the gameplay, sideqquests and side content and obsidian making the Core, roleplaying and story?But ALAS thats wishful thinking.Do I recommend the game ? Absolutly! If you love games with the story and dialouge like the old fallout games and NV you'll feel right at home. If you prefere however the more hectic and combat focused and exploretatry nature of Fallout 4, then this game might not be for you, but i'd still play it for the story.Anyway 7/10, not bad for the start of a game series, hopefully the next (if there ever is gonna be one ) is gonne be better and ♥♥♥♥ Epic Games.P.S don't make exculsives at Epic Games, its one of the main reasons why the hype for the game crashed harder than the COVID economy.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a Fallout 3 clone with a Fire fly skin on top that's trying to have Borderland's sense of humor. . . I guess?At it's core, it really is just Fallout 3. That should be your starting point. If you can't use that game as a frame of reference, go play it first. And if you have played it, you need to know that there aren't improvements. It feels like a well made clone that doesn't add to the genre. And this is where it gets weird, because it has flaws Fallout 3 doesn't have. The writing is atrocious and I still don't know the intention. It never reaches the point of farce, but details become farcical. You can't insist that I take the world building seriously while also ramping up the corporate evil to extremes that just don't make sense. While I initially felt that companions were underwritten, I will say that improves as things progress. But that doesn't make up for the fact that the story (up to the point I played) was completely non existent and almost frustratingly pointless. Graphically, things look plastique. It's not a pretty game and it really should be. To boot, it doesn't run great, even on low settings. I'm by no means top of the line here, but I don't really have problems playing much of anything on lower settings. Here? There were some noticeable drops in quality. The big demerit for me is the RPG aspects. Builds? Skills? Eh. Don't get me wrong, those aspects are here, but they feel incredibly inconsequential. in the early to mid game because the game pairs them together and you have to level them up in groups at first? It's beyond bizarre. And unlike Fallout, I never had that moment where i felt I was missing out on an experience by taking certain skills. A perk system further tries to add depth, but once again, not meaningful choices. I can't stress this enough, one of my favorite parts about Rpgs is the builds and the paths you can take, and this game conditioned me to not care. On the plus side is the Firefly aspect I talked about. I guess we could also call it Knights of the Old Republic. You have a hub ship where everyone gathers and lives. While Fallout feels expansive and meandering, this gave a good sense of grounding. Planets might be compartmentalized, but then you visit a space port and the game feels more cohesive like you and your party really are on this space adventure. Overall, it's worse Fallout 3. This game exists in that weird niche of recommendation where i say play it if you want more of that thing you like. 6/10.

_childDocuments_.review: The Outer Worlds is an enjoyable and funny RPG that has similarities with Fallout:  New Vegas (same devs) and feels like Mass Effect.  It still has its own unique playstyle however.The developers, Obsidian, have put together a fun adventure across a fictional new solar system called Halcyon that has been colonised by humans who set off from Earth many years ago.  Frozen in time, a mad scientist wakes you up and you set off to do his bidding (or not...)The main story is essentially a choice between working with or against the corporations that rule Halcyon.  Along the way, you create your crew and traverse across different worlds and meet various factions who you can choose to help or otherwise.The typical RPG elements are all there - character customisation, loot, levelling up, perks to name a few.  Combat works well; gunplay is tight and fast paced but you can stealth through also.You can play the game your way but I would recommend putting some skill points into the dialogue and lock picking options to fully explore everything.  The game doesn't force you into any direction and you can kill almost all NPCs if you are that way inclined!Graphics are colourful and smooth.  I didn't experience any issues.Highlights of the game for me are the voice-acting, humour and simply exploring the world.  The Outer Worlds isn't the biggest RPG you will ever play and there are some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, for example, the level cap (30) is too low and some of the world is 'repeated' with similar buildings and the same enemies cropping up but, overall, this is well worth picking up.

_childDocuments_.review: I went into this title expecting to get the "full" 50+ hour story RPG fans come to expect from mainstream developers. I didn't get that. Instead, I found a endearing world with interesting characters, classic RPG elements, and a, by comparison to most titles, brief story. This isn't a long game. With dedicated play time you can easily polish off a run in 2-3 days. I commend the devs for their choice in making this game short however. There is absolutely 0 filler in this game. No fetch quests for the sake of fetch quests, no trailing missions before getting to the real mission 20-ish minutes later. None of the pesky video game-isms that we've become numb to. That being said there are things this game did well and some things I didn't much care for. I won't cover all my thoughts about the game for the sake of brevity.The goodThis game does the trick older Fallout titles did so well in forcing to player to make a series of morally grey choices. You will never satisfy all parties involved and the game doesn't make it clear at any point that there is a "right" or "wrong" choice. Your companions will from time to time voice there concerns about the player-characters actions but it is ultimately left up to you.The characters in this game are interesting. Not in the way that their passive AI is impressive, or they live full day & night cycles, but chatting with a bartender or shop keep will reveal interesting facts about the world and themselves. It's a really nice touch the devs absolutely didn't have to go through with and it makes the game feel all that more special.The badThe perk system. It's one of the most uninspired I've ever seen in an RPG. Every other time you level up you are presented with a series of options that are nothing more than statistical improvements. There are no "cool" perks that would change the way you play the game. It amounts to a series of "handguns do N% more headshot damage" or "you can carry N kilos more weight". These aren't a problem in and of themselves, but playing into level 20, 30, and beyond I found myself thinking "I don't know, let's just pick one. Not that it really matters". It's really a shame and limits future playthough fun I might have.The weaponry. As you play you tend to catch on that there really aren't all that many options to choose from. Very few of the guns and mele weapons feel distinct and the ones that do tend to do gimmicky/ impractical things. As you level out of your beginner set of weapons the game introduces an "entirely new set". This boils down to using a revolver MK.2 instead of a normal revolver. Again, similar to the perk system this aspect of the game feels uninspired more so than a major flaw with the game. It's a shame that a world with such interesting lore, sub-plots, and morally grey decisions it falls flat on the aspects of the game you will be arguably interacting with the most. TLDR. This isn't a perfect game, like any RPG title it has its strengths and weaknesses. Strong RPG elements and captivating story/ characters absolutely outweigh the bad, however. 8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly can't remember much about this game or my time playing it.  Initially I was having fun for the first couple of hours but found the experience wearing off fast.  At first I saw the skills and the factions and looked forward to a second playthrough, but quickly dropped the idea:The way that skills work means that you will be over-levelled by the mid game.  All difficulty was lost as I could become good in multiple skills, meaning my character had no role play value in my role play game.  Any obstacle I could overcome with little to no thought.  There were no stakes, no challenge, no builds as I became the mono-build.There is no one large map, but instead multiple small maps, and they lock progress to the other areas based on story progression, and when you complete the quests in an area, there is rarely a reason to go back, this makes the game disappointingly linear.The factions are surface level, they exist only on their own little areas.  If you murder-hobo your way through the story there are no real consequences as you can just leave their localised area and not have to deal with them any more.  I did this to a faction because I couldn't be bothered to complete a fetch quest and there were no repercussions.  Contrast this to fallout new vegas (a previous game by the same developer), where the factions seemed a genuine force over the entire map and a threat if you cross them.The game sets up the corporations as the big antagonist but the way they portray them I think goes to the game's detriment: every opportunity the game shows them as an incompetent, evil, bureaucratic nightmare but at the same time is the butt of every joke and is a clown.  There is a massive tonal clash that I found jarring, and it raises the question of why would I ever help them.  I won't spoil too much, but at the end you can side with or against the corporations, the game aggressively does everything to convince to to go against them.  It did not feel much like a choice.  Compare again to new vegas where there were many grey areas with each major faction, each making there case to choose or go alone, and Caesar's legion as the main antagonist being compelling and my first choice because of it when I first played the game.  And when the game ended I immediately loaded the game again for a second playthrough to see the other factions.The enemies are faceless and generic, and seem to only exist as a roadblock for the player to shoot as a distraction rather than being a fleshed out part of the game.  The whole combat system felt empty.I stopped picking up loot mid way through the game because there was so much of it that it all became useless.  What use are healing items when I'm too powerful never need them?  Money where I can loot corpses for the best weapons and armour in the game from grunt-level enemies?  Or bullets when I have so many I will never use them all?The lack of challenge or choice makes the game for me so forgettable, the game felt too safe, in the sense that the developers didn't seem to want to risk anything or try anything new:  The game itself feels like everything was recycled from fallout games but even the fallout game they made felt superior.

_childDocuments_.review: I really tried to give this game a chance. At first I was really excited about it, I had it on my wishlist for a long time. Unfortunately, it's WAY too demanding of my PC, it needs to be optimized REALLY BAD. My PC can run ARK and ATLAS on ultra graphic settings and be perfectly fine, this game makes my PC sound like a damn lawnmower. The mechanics for fighting are horrendous. You have to hit dead-center mass or your shots don't count at all, not even head shots count. There is one, single spot on every enemy that counts and if you don't hit it exactly there, then it does nothing at all. The fighting mechanics are trying to mimic Fallout 4 but only have the worst aspects of it. It's trying to be like Bethesda games except everything is as dumbed down as Bioshock. Another problem (but this isn't unique to this game) when an enemy is supposed to be difficult to fight, don't just make it nearly invincible, that's just boring and uncreative. Have the enemy be quicker or heal themselves or dodge stuff, not just have endless HP. For the all the hype, this really didn't live up to it. 4 out of 10 for me. Glad I didn't have to pay for it.

_childDocuments_.review: With the Spacer's Choice Edition™ "coming soon"™, a new wave of players will no doubt be clicking on this Steam page and wondering if it's finally time to give Obsidian's satirical romp on corporatism a spin. The screenshots look good. The reviews are in, and they are , baby! (Almost aggressively so!) And it's an RPG?! What's left to say? Click that pretty little green "Add to Cart" button and get to doing whatever you do in an RPG. Looting corpses? You bet! Choosing funny dialogue options? Sure, yeah, you can do that too. Dull combat? Hell yes! Making "choices"? Technically!Here's the thing: , despite what you've heard, was never particularly good. The grand story arc was fine, but the minute-to-minute storytelling (the stuff that is supposed to stick) was bland. The characters? They're mostly bland too. The choices you make are slight and ultimately exceedingly limited. You say the right things, do a single quest, and boom, a critical, satirical, or emotional response has been triggered! "Don't you feel satisfied?" the game asks. "I don't even know this person," the player replies. "How about a punchline instead?" the game asks again.Do this about 50 times, and then the game ends. Everything works out just fine, perhaps even better than you imagined it might. Isn't that lovely? Well, yes, but as a game sold on its main developer's pedigree with this sort of thing, absolutely not. You never feel like you've made a difference. You never feel like you've built a character and approached the world in a unique or character-driven way. You shot the things. You looted their corpses. Long live the action RPG.But I suppose this isn't the end of the world. A bland action "RPG" with some funny bits might well be worth the admission price. The reviews (overall) are still gleaming. It's not like 20,000 people (or 20 critics) could be wrong. Maybe, yes, but then again it might be helpful to reflect back on what made it so popular in 2019 (when it initially came out), to consider what exactly made this milquetoast masterpiece such a hit.It wasn't Fallout 4.That's it.  was never a particularly great or memorable RPG in its own right. It inherited too many things from Bethesda's brand of RPG for that to happen -- the emphasis on looting, the dulled storyline with duller factions, the more detailed but less immediately engaging visual style -- and so it became the arbiter of milquetoast RPG design: acceptable across the board, totally playable, even fun (on rare occasion), but also fundamentally unsatisfying in the way that really matters in an RPG. You don't build your character; you play the role you've been assigned. Get dragged around by a mad scientist on a quest you may or may not have any interest in pursuing. But it wasn't Fallout 4! And maybe that's enough! But, after playing the whole game through (on Xbox and PC), as well as its DLCs, it's worth remembering that you can do so much better.Ask someone who played this game to name a single memorable character, to name their favorite companion, to recall any particularly wonderful part of the plot, and you'll probably get the same answers every single time. You'll probably hear about Ellie's companion quest, or about that one Spacer's Choice salesman on Groundbreaker, or the diet toothpaste escapade. You will experience the exact same things if you give it a try. Maybe that's enough for you. But if you enjoy the idea of an RPG, about the disparate branches pulling you in different directions, about secrets hidden behind obscure dialogue options, it will never be what you want it to be.

_childDocuments_.review: I generally really like these types of RPG with a mixture of story, combat and skill building. I was looking forward to play one that takes place in a SF setting, but the game was to me kind of a disappointment.First of all, the whole place feels small. You are roaming around a star system, with a large planet, moons, space stations and asteroids; but overall, it seems smaller than, say Witcher 3 or Skyrim. My second main issue is that everything looks and feels too much like Borderlands: frontier towns run by corporations, with half-abandoned settlements overrun by bandits, raptors and primate; ammo crates everywhere; lots of useless guns and vending machines that never have anything interesting for sale.On the plus side, the story is quite taking. As a stranger to this world, you can see that people are miserable and you slowly understand why.In terms of gameplay, everything is smooth and I like the skill/character building system, which lets you grow your character as you like. The game is very easy in normal difficulty; at least it was for me. I died a few times at the very beginning because I explored the wrong areas. But after that, it was pretty much a walk in the park, until the end level. And even then, I only died because I had learned not to be careful. The last boss was a joke: lift with gravity gun, shoot, use companion abilities, rince and repeat.Other minor points: there is an ammo system, but there is so much of it everywhere and no limit to what you can carry, so I never even came close to running out (and I basically only used handguns). Similarly, you need to maintain your weapons and armor, but there is so much raw material that this is never an issue. I don't even know what happens if you let your weapons degrade too much, as it never came close to happening. I would recommend buying only when at a discount.

_childDocuments_.review: Its not for me. I am a little surprised how positively reviewed this game is. Ill try and break it down by parts: - It feels very much like a persons first world building for a custom D&D game setting. In person, you can ask a question that the person probably never thought of, but seems obvious to you, and they give you answer. In a video game, that cant happen. There are a lot of eye brow raising logic in the way people behave that is hard to really take anything seriously. The corporations are comically evil, and everyone is just okay with it. like you would suspect there to be much more dissent in the populous the way they are treated and arbitrary penalties. Its a culture where Mass suicide would make sense because no sane person would look at the world and want to keep participating in it.It has the same kind of energy of a horror movie where there is clearly a knife welding killer in the house and the characters all just kind of wander around in their undies saying "Hellllllo?". Just destroys any verisimilitude of taking the world seriously because the people don't act or behave like people. its a big pet peeve of mine. - I found this to be pretty lack-luster too. There was never really a character I enjoyed. Similar to above with most of the characters - they seem unable to grasp that the corporation is clearly evil. Every one behaves like they need help using a microwave, or use only Velcro shoes. Even the 'smart' characters seem a bit too dumb. The dialog options are usually like:1) Progress quest2) Some boring world building in which the person will boot lick the corporations again3) some other question which will end in a 2 word reply4) leaveThere may be some branching dialog, but I never found any of it interesting to listen to or surprising. it was all very 'meh'.Every quest felt the same. It always person A tell you Person B is bad, but wont really tell you why or elaborate on it, usually some paper thin reasoning. you talk to Person B and they say the same but provide proof of person A. You confront Person A and they have this like scooby-doo monologue "I would have gotten away with it!" or something similar. All of the quests are like this. - I found the combat to be difficult until about level 4 or 5. at which point you get way better weapons and the combat becomes much easier. There is also this whole thing they are trying to sell you on when you play the game called something like "Taking flaws". basically when you are playing the game the way you like, pop ups will occur outside of combat when something happens, like you took 200 acid damage total, or something like that. It will ask you if you would like to take a flaw. The flaw will give you a negative to the way you currently play in circumstances related to the pop up - like when you take acid damage you have -1 perception and 10% more weapon sway etc - for 1 perk point. Normally you get 1 perk point every 2 levels, and the perks are very disappointing. There was never one I was excited for, or looking forward to getting. whenever I had to select a perk, it was always kind of a chore to find the least bad one / most helpful. Some example of perks are like "walk speed is 25% faster", "Carry weight is 30kg more", "you can move faster in slowmo mode". Nothing that gave me the feeling of "Wow! this will help me I cant wait to try it" It was really just for fixing inconveniences which, honestly, probably should have just been fixed without the need of perk points. The walking is slow, just make the default 25% faster.You get companions, you can take 2 with you out of a selection of 6. They are all very bland. No one really had an interesting story. There is a crisis of faith priest who is/was a criminal - it was not totally clear to me. A gay engineer who wants a girlfriend. Doctor with daddy issues. The guy who gets fired from minimum wage jobs wants to me find his friend he has not heard from in a while. And Lady who wants to bury her old friends.I don't think I am being too unfair with their characterisations because they felt very 1 dimensional. to be fair I used mainly doctor with daddy issues and Gay engieer who wants GF real bad. They seem to try and do something like give the companions an "arc" in that they will bring up the same issues and stuff when you go outside of the ship. They also interact with each other when you enter the ship, but there seems to be like only 10 interactions when you enter the ship, and you will enter the ship a lot. The ship will inform you they are interacting when you want to go anywhere it becomes quite annoying. Similarly annoying is that every companion has a special combat ability, and they shout 1 line every time you use it. some characters have a stun or do damage or something - its usually useful, so you will be using it a lot! I heard the same line like 25 times and I just muted the game. I had the companion for only their "companion missions" which was total like 1 hour it sucked. "AYYYYYAAAAGGHHHHYYYYY" please don't do this, i just need your damage. When you use their ability the camera pans on them and you have to watch them use their power for like 3-5 seconds which is also annoying when you are in a gun fight.I just really did not enjoy the game so much. I felt like I was being hit over the head with ideas that are not subtle but the game thinks is. I don't know if its a case of "But the players wont get it unless we spell it out for them 3-5 times" I get it, the corporation is evil, but can they have a better reason? There is a "Twist" at the end, but it changes nothing and is not interesting. Your perspective on the factions should not shift at the revelations. I will spoil it to give you the whole deal and save you 10-15 hours of play. . Overall its okay, but very disappointed its a 5 or 6/10 for me.

_childDocuments_.review: The game isn't 0/10 bad, but it was a huge disappointment for me.I was hoping for more of a specialised character feel, but it really just ends up being an fps. Unlike an RPG like New Vegas, Outer Worlds doesn't let you solve many missions in any way other than fight and kill -- sometimes break into a container. The decisions in your character build feel essentially meaningless. Will buff a few qualities, but nothing changes the way your character feels in the world. I certainly wouldn't be motivated to try a new playthrough as a 'different' character (something I often do in Skyrim fallout, ME, etc.)Your squadmates can't use cover, you can't order them to do much, in hardest difficulty I just tell them to wait back because they just die and then I feel bad.The world isn't open and is instead made of multiple, small areas you can travel between. At first I thought this would be rgeat because I expected them to be dense,d etailed and interesting. Instead they were small AND cookie cutter copy/paste buildings and objects. The world wasn't much fun for me to explore.5/10. First 30 mins seemed like the game would be awesome. Kinda just kept going downhill for me.

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of gamedesign elements fall into the uncanny valley and thus the game suffers from immersion hick-ups. The game feels like a demo addressed to investors of what could be. Half backed very much.This opinion contains spoilers.* Compability:** This game works great with proton on linux. It's the only reason i considered buying this game. Big plus.* Gameworld style:** The designers succeeded in implementing a style that is similar to the old 2D games. The retro-future style transforms the game into a fantasy game rather than a sci-fi game. But it has downsides. More later.* Visuals:** Very often i came across a wallpaper like scenery. Often very appealing.* Quest GUI:** I liked the summary bullet points in the quest log. They were very helpful.* Enemy design:** This game has all of the possible enemytypes. The enemies feel like static papertargets (obviously except the chargers). It's apparent that this game was made for consoles.* Companions:** In dialogs with NPCs the companions occasionally have some remarks. Interesting concept. Unfortunately it’s not possible to ask them anything about the current quest. ** The companions are boring with boring quests and forgettable. The only one interesting one was Felix with his uplifting remarks. I liked Felix.** I don’t understand why do they have to wear the armor that i assigned to them inside the unreliable. Don't the have their own wardrobe?** If ADA says that some of the companions would cause a disturbance, there is no gamemechanic for me to interact with them and knock it off.* Dialog options:** There is a lot of dialog in this game. Sometimes too much. My first meeting with Sanjar ate up 30 minutes. There was a lot of uninteresting stuff to discus with him.** Lots of options. Different decisions have different consequences with little reward. The consequences are shop prices, some mid level armor or gun and the diashow you get when the game ends.* Weapons:** Weapons have levels (what i think shouldn't exist in any game at all). Bad is that the higher leveled guns have just an postfix to their name (like mk2 or Ultra), but the model and texture remains the same. IMO it's much better to introduce a new 3D-model for a higher tier weapon.** The shotguns weren't that impressive and were rendered useless by melee weapons.* Leveling:** The leveling is so extreme that going back as a Lvl 30 to the first area kills an enemy with just one bullet while before it required some 100 bullets (for strong enemies).** Skilltrees aren't skilltrees but bufftrees. The only skills that can be learned are dodging and powerful melee attacks. Everything else are just buffs.* Character control:** Without hesitation i can say that it's the worst that i have ever experienced. Player will on specific terrain parts just randomly slide around and get stuck, because of the awful gameengine charactercontrol implementation. Now i understand why there is every 3 minutes an autosave. I had to use it often because of that.* World mechanics:** Besides of the NPC's the world is dead. The complete lack of physically interactive objects kills immersion.** No climbing, no tossing, no risky exploring, awful jumping rounded up by invisible walls (to prevent you from trying out swimming, because swimming doesn’t exist).** Also gravity is everywhere the same. On big planets and on asteroids. No zero gravity mission/area. There is no variety here.* Gameworld style:** The retro-future style didn't work for me. The colony is dying, there is resource shortage and (supposedly advanced) inter/stellar traveling but there are resourcehungry 1930s ornaments. The industrial dieselpunk appearance doesn’t fit, was immersion breaking and it didn't catch me.** Also the rounded and comical design of houses/ships/etc.. hindered every raise in tension. Round things don't catch humans attention, sharp and edgy stuff does. Very often i would overlook things because the environment is cluttered with the same roundy shape.* Atmosphere:** The colorful appearance and passive NPC's don't fit into the story. IMO the presentation of the story failed. It would have been better in a thick horror-thriller atmosphere.** No NPC/Storygiver had an extreme emotional expression. Best example of how bad it was, ** No demonstrations/panic/any other extreme expression because  There was simply nothing to react to except the enemies with guns and claws.* Exhausting quest structure:** Very often the quest at some point would boil down to the question 'either them or the others' and you decide. Those dilemmas are cheap and aren't entertaining.* Missing story theme:** I never had the feeling i would solve a mystery. The biggest mystery was raised literally just 1 minute before the game was over.* Quests:** The quests were just quests. Very often detached of the main story, or in other words, no side NPC had a rational problem because of what's going on. Rarely were they interesting. Mostly just fetch quests.If it's important, I played a max speech, gun wielding character and managed to talk the end bosses into just leave, not killing any corporate soldiers at all.
