_childDocuments_.review: In short: This game is OK. Not brilliant, not terribly bad. Mediocre. Buy it on sale with a 70% discount. I'm still voting for it because despite it's not a masterpiece by any means I can see developers were trying to make it a good game giving it their love, care and dedication. At very least there are no microtransactions which is already nice.Quests and story are well written but don't seem to be real exciting or thrilling or having unexpected twists or deep moral dilemmas. They're just OK. You have some choices but those are quite straight forward. There is a considerable amount of backtracking involved  especially if you try to complete all side quests. The game partially mitigates backtracking with plenty of fast-travel points.From time to time I was under impression game devs tried to include some references to iconic RPGs like Mass Effect or even borrow some ideas. But unfortunately the execution is poor and don't stand a chance in comparison. Shooting and gameplay mechanics are OK. Weapons made fine and look nice and have mods and options to be upgraded. However fights are just too simple made. No covers, no tactics, no throwables. Some very basic stealth mechanic is also there.Loot system is very excessive and overburdened. You're drowning in tons and tons of differently named but doing precisely the same consumables. It makes you try to never open up consumables tab of your inventory to avoid pain and suffering of sorting those things up. Also there are really plenty of weapons and armor and you gonna spend a lot of your play time sorting/breaking to parts/selling your loot if you tend to be greedy and can not stand any pickable object laying around.Graphics is fine but it's heavily styled and includes visual filters some people might find hard to look at. Partially the visual effects can be disabled in video settings which makes it somehow easier to look at the picture. I'd say it could use some more optimization to my liking. Even though I play in 4K resolution with all video settings set to ultra, I don't really see the picture that could possibly cost me frame rate reduced to 40FPS on i9 and 2080.

_childDocuments_.review: whilst it obviously worked for sales, i feel like the advertising for this game really worked against it. it was advertised as something akin to new vegas, which it just isn't. it was advertised as a comedy game and whilst the darkly comedic tone of people working themselves to the bone for corporations who don't care for them in the slightest is always present, the game is not particularly about comedy or trying to be funny apart from the opening few hours.the outer worlds is truly a relatively short (in this genre at least) character based cRPG-lite with some good writing, especially in the companions and the main quest. i feel like most of the side quests were rather forgettable except for . i beat it and both DLCs in 35.5 hours on the normal difficulty and the game became a cakewalk after the first area. by level 23 or so (the level cap is 36) i was melting enemies almost instantly. the final bosses of both DLCs and the base game were laughably killed in 10 seconds or less. areas are small maps with quests and npcs to talk to - ala baldur's gate or icewind dale.armour designs are pretty cool thogame gets a 7/10 from me. doesn't even come close to obsidian's magnum opus that is poe2

_childDocuments_.review: It's a great game with many similarities to Fallout New Vegas, Borderlands, and Bioshock. Like the former, you'll be presented with an A- story that suffers from C+ first/third person shooter elements. I think the developers knew this and provided a system similar to VATS from Fallout that helps the combat in many ways. The story is decent, and there is enough of an open-world factor to reward some exploration. I bought the game on sale and I feel I got my moneys worth. Just a quick sidenote - I'm a geologist and I was blown away with the level of world design these folks did. Volcanic areas have jagged features that hold jointed basalt and mafic lava flows (both geologic features that I'd expect in the real world). Sedimentary-dominated areas have visible stratigraphy and accurate erosional landforms as well as cave systems. These developers are incredibly detailed with something mundane for most people and it shows how much thought they put into the design and art. 6/10 game, 10/10 geology*Edit* After finishing the game completely I feel about the same. The story was a bit shorter than I expected but I felt it was satisfying. The Outer Worlds is absolutely worth the sale price. At full price I start to compare it to AAA games and studios, which it falls a bit short of.

Player choice feels real, and the individual character story lines with the people you pick up are wonderful. The writing is great - so much memorable dialog and story experiences. There's humor, drama, action, intrigue, couldn't ask for more. Best solo gaming experience that I've seen in a while.And ZERO BUGS!!! I can't tell you how many EA and Bethesda experiences I've had in recent years that were just riddled with bugs and issues that pull you out of the immersion. There were NONE in this game. Obsidian clearly did their job and created a beautiful (both graphics and sound, really), fully fleshed out game, and made sure it was perfect.

_childDocuments_.review: From Obsidian, I think I got most of what I expected. TL:DR - good dialogue/writing, combat gets stale very quickly.Disclaimer - this review is from a FO:NV fan and that's the baseline of comparison. I think that's fair as it probably is a big portion of the target audience.The writing and world building clearly got the most effort put into them. In a very similar tone to the Fallout series, everything is hilariously dystopian. The visual storytelling that NV was loved for is back, aftermaths of battles or other events are planted around for you to find in your exploration, some are plot/character relevant, some are just fun little self containted tidbits. Characters are fun and snarky for the most part, and you as the unvoiced player character have plenty of fun, mean and goofy dialogue choices. Lots of moral ambiguity, and the game intentionally avoids shoehorning you into a "good" or "evil" role, you have freedom in that regard. I will criticise the aesthetic a little bit though - the character design seems to explicitly go out of the way to avoid gender norms; I don't inherently consider that a bad thing, but the result was that a lot of the characters are a bit (visually) samey. I appreciate the representation of the queer community, but also feel they need to acknowledge that's not the entirety of it - not every queer person has to look butch or androgynous.Gameplay-wise though, we're quite lacking - there's the classic fallout ways to deal with obstacles: sneaking, combat or dialogue. Dialogue is probably the most interesting way on account of the aforementioned writing, but obviously you will need to employ one of the other two methods for non-sentient challengers. Combat is where the game really lets me down - at first, gunplay is fine, controls are fairly responsive, the feel of the guns are OK, but once you get into it there's very little variety - only a few different types of guns - pistols, automatic weapons, shotguns, sniper rifles, and a handful of heavy weapons that don't fit neatly into those. Along with those are elemental effects which basically just serve as a pokemon kinda type advantage system, almost no depth to speak of. There is very little within each category to differentiate guns - while weapons have special effects, there are only really a handful of those as well, and they pretty much just amount to stun, DoT, or extra damage. Some sacrifice a bit of fire rate for damage or vice versa, but in the end, you'll probably just pick the one with bigger numbers. As you level, you get access to new weapons, but again, it's just bigger numbers - literally. When you outgrow your starter pistol, you start finding the Starter Pistol Mk 2. Yay. Enemy variety so far is a bit lacking as well, unless there's more that opens up later on, so far we have humans, bugs, dogs, apes and lizards. Kind of dull for the length afforded by the freedom of an open world game.I feel as though the game is at least in part a response to FO4: addressing many of its criticisms regarding the player character and writing, but failing in a lot of areas that it did improve or otherwise continue to do well in. Overall, would I recommend the game? To someone looking to scratch the New Vegas experience of exploring, experiencing a lively world/characters and freely roleplaying a character of your choosing, yes. If your focus is on experiencing a good looter/shooter, this is not the game for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok , I wanted to play enough of the game to see if what everyone was complaining about on the forums was justified. Final verdict? It isn't lolFor this particular review, I am going to compare this game to KoTR-2, Fallout 3, Firefly and Red Dwarf. IF you know what all 4 of those things are - you are awesome. For tldr crowd. Combat is satisfying, story is decent, spent about 10hrs on starting zone. So enough content. I give the game a thumbs up. Would tell my friends to get it. Now to expand on what I just said. First with what few flaws I have found so far. Main one being the random items you pick up. Most don't seem to have a real good use. Lot of flavor text sure, but meh. If you want to comb the galaxy for junk to make cooler crap out of ...sorry, but no. You'll end up selling most of it. Other flaw being a weird AI trait. To elaborate - I killed a worker to steal something (am bad lol) - no one saw me. There were no alerts. Everything fine. I come back, two other works are red and trying to kill me. I kill them, no one cared. I leave, do some exploring - come back again, now two guards are trying to kill me but NO ONE else. It's just really odd. I think it's a bug, one the EGS gamers and gamepass gamers didn't notice or care about reporting. Lastly, the "kill cam" (i.e when you kill a mob and it flashes to them dying) is jarring. Not smooth at all. Definitely not how Fallout 4 approached it. I would say turn it off. OH and a little thing. Not ALL of the buildings can be entered. We've seen this in other games, but ...I still dislike it. They are there, I want to explore them lol. Now for the comparisons. The game is obviously meant to a Fallout style game. In this regard it feels closer to New Vegas and Fallout 3 than say Fallout 4 - which is a good thing. Fallout 4's story was....boring, borderline non-existent if you got caught up in Preston's BS lol. Storytelling wise - this is the company behind games with amazing stories, closest one I am comparing is KoTR 2 Sith Lords. Sadly, I don't see the same depth and nuance to the writing, or to the characters in this game. However, I believe that is because they wanted this game to be more comical. That is why Firefly comes in. Because, being real, I feel as if the devs watched Firefly and serenity and said "let's make a game" lol. It feels THAT much like the spirit of that show....with a TOUCH of Red Dwarf's dry comedy thrown in.I'm digging it. An I love using a plasma greataxe that sounds like a chainsaw to murder marauders haha. Very satisfying. I definitely think this game is worth buying at full price. Definitely think it was worth the wait. Am glad to have it on Steam, and hope to see more added to it.

_childDocuments_.review: So I've been a fan of Obsidian ever since KOTOR2. Before that, if we count the games some of the folks there worked on back in Black Isle. Despite the tight schedules those early sequels were on and some resulting clunkiness and bugs, I loved (and still do) most of their games. The Outer Worlds though? Well, it's complicated.Lets knock out the visuals first - graphics are about what you'd expect from 2020 game, still looking good. Visual design though? Not a fan. I feel like the whole retrofuturistic vibe doesn't fit the setting at all and is only there to emulate Fallout - where the 1950-60s vibe was much more fitting and plausible. Everything being oversaturated to the point of being painful to look at doesn't help in the slightest.Alright, but RPGs should shine through the story, not visuals. Does the story hold up to Obsidian standards? Yes and no. There is some really great writing and fun quests in there, but it's in the minority. Overall impression the game left me with is "Stupidity written smartly." Dialogs are witty and competently written, but they hardly compensate for 85% of characters you meet being complete idiots. Game actually touches on some serious issues - big corporations destroying environment and ruining people's lives for profit margins - but then goes out of its way to make a mockery of it all by turning stupidity to 11, from blabbering idiots of npcs and corpospeak emails present on every in-game computer to majority of sidequests being idiot plots (that is, stories which only happen because everyone involved has an IQ roughly equal to comfortable room temperature). "Corporations. Pretty stupid, hehe." is the one and only note writing has for the majority of the game. It's most prevalent in Emerald Vale, the first area of the game - which might be why almost 30% of players dropped the game at that point.The only time I actually noticed the brief respite from everpresent idiocy and some real, human emotions was during the Gorgon DLC. My companions' reactions to some horrifying experiments were written extremely well and it's probably the moment that stuck with me the most.Gameplay wise - not much to say, it's still the basic Bethesda RPG game loop. Exploration, looting, some mediocre shooting, more looting, pick some quests, sell loot, some more shooting, some lockpicking and more looting. Loot is not all that exciting, as you'll rarely find meaningful upgrades, aside from unique Science Weapons, which are probably the most fun to play with. Enemy variety is nonexistent, consisting of about 4 types of animals, 3 types of robots, melee humans and ranged weapon humans with AI that's as basic as it gets.There's now also a 'Spacer's Choice' edition, but it seems the only major changes are turning up color saturation even more and raising level cap from 36 to 99, so you don't have to make any build choices/sacrifices. At 9$ upgrade price, I'll pass.Overall, The Outer Worlds is not a bad game and there is some fun to be had. Still, it's mediocre at best and definitely the weakest Obsidian game I've played, which makes it hard to recommend. At this point, I'm much more interested in Avowed than Outer Worlds 2.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't get why this game gets so much hate from the Fallout community. While this game may not live up to New Vegas and this isn't the same Obsidian as back then, this is still a really great game, better than anything Bethesda has ever released and probably ever will I think.If you're tired of playing New Vegas and want something new to fill that void, this is it. While the story may not be amazing, it's passable and the characters may not be ♥♥♥♥♥♥' Garrus from Mass Effect (there are a couple of stand outs being Parvati and Ellie), and the progression for gear is admittedly not good, oh and there are some pretty noticeable performance issues but nothing too bad.. unlike Cyberpunk. But apart from that the dialogue is fun and well written, there's so much freedom in how you tackle quests and how you complete them and branching paths, the combat gets the job done, I personally really like the art style and I think this game is, for the most part, really stunning.The DLC; is ok overall. I think you can skip Perils on Gorgon as it's very short, yet feels very padded too, feels very rushed and the new area is AWFUL- but if you get it all cheap then ♥♥♥♥ it why not. Murder on Eridanos is great, the new world is interesting, the characters are fun, it has a lot of intrigue (even if it's admittedly quite predictable), and long enough to be satisfying while now overstaying its welcome.I finished my playthrough after almost 2 days of playtime, even though I am quite slow and like to see everything a game has to offer the game felt satisfying to play through and apart from a couple of small bits here and there, I didn't feel like it dragged or was too padded.Overall I highly recommend this game, although I'd recommend getting a cheaper code from "A2G"  or someplace like that, but I'd definitely play it again in the future and I'll 100% be getting the sequel whenever it comes out.

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay is just fine.  It's kinda like Fallout 3 in space.  Combat is fun.  Skill trees are fun.  RPG elements are there.The problem is that its bland and forgettable.  The NPC's and the story are not memorable in any way.  I put in 20 hours and then took a break for a few months and honestly I can't even tell you what the plot was about, the name of ANY of my team members, or what their motivation/backstory was.   Compare this to a game like Mass Effect.  Every single NPC in that game is memorable.  You will remember their names and backstories for years to come after you beat the game.So yes the gameplay, combat, RPG elements and UI is more enjoyable than Mass Effect/Fallout 3, but the story, NPCs, and atmosphere is much less engaging. Do you want to play a "better game" that is forgettable?  Go with Outer worlds.   Or do you want to play a "worse game" that is memorable?  Then go with Mass Effect 2.

_childDocuments_.review: Great! Colorful and funny satire of mega corporate capitalism. The dialogue and voice acting feel genuinely human. Elevator pitch: Firefly meets Fallout: New VegasI'm trans and that factors into my reviewWeak points: -Combat! Not enough like an FPS or RPG. I'm pretty critical of most first-person action RPGs' combat systems and this game is no exception. Companion combat AI feels like an afterthought. Maybe I just haven't got the hang of it, but games like Mass Effect have handled 2-companions in combat significantly better than here. I ended up enjoying melee combat more than firearm combat. It felt like a chore more than an opportunity lots of the time.-No 3rd person. There is an "idle camera," but no true over-the-shoulder 3rd person for walking around in towns. -No voice acting for the player character or even reaction shots/cuts back to the player character during dialogue. I was longing for at least reaction takes from my character. In a game with such a heavy emphasis on decision making and characterization, it feels weird to operate a rarely visible avatar whom never emotes.-NO ROMANCE. Okay there is one very cute romance between two characters, but your PC can't romance anyone. Strong points: Everything else! Notably, though:-Refreshingly short. I went through at a pretty average pace, completed every side quest that I picked up and the main quest at 38 hours total. I prefer this! Makes the game more replayable and encourages new playthroughs with different builds and decision making. -Character creation allows some gender-bending, and has more options that are authentic examples of real human diversity (though textured/tight curled hair options are lacking). There's also only face/hair/makeup/scar customization - no bodily changes other than "male" and "female"-Weapon and armor customization and design. There's just some great stuff here. Running around with a corrosive scythe and dismembering capitalists is pretty damn satisfying

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR (Its not Fallout New Vegas in space. Decent game but not worth full price)If you are expecting space age Fallout New Vegas, this isn't it. The story is much more linear, and sometimes repetitive. Go to planet, two factions are mad at each other, kill one faction or make the two get along then move on to the next planet. Thats the vibe I felt while playing the game. In the name of fairness, I would like to mention that I have only done 1 playthrough, where I took the rebellious route rather than the corporate route, perhaps the other is more engaging but I find that doubtful. While I was playing I did my best to engage in sidequests but found most of them to be disappointing as well. Out of the around 20 sidequests I completed, only one was actually in depth and spanned across the campaign. Not only was the story structure not what I expected it to be, but combat was also somewhat lacking. Throughout the game, I fought about 6 different enemies, Canids, Mantisours, raptidons, corporate soliders, marauders, and mechanicals. The first three on that list comprise ALL THE ALIEN LIFEFORMS you will have to fight. For an interstellar game I was really hoping to fight a wide range of cool and unique alien enemies and this was painfully disappointing. The character creator was good, so for those of you who are fans of that need not worry. I wont comment on the companion system as I never bothered to really figure it out. Supposedly there are special abilities your companions have but whenever I tried using them they didn't work? I wasn't sure if they were circumstance based or something so maybe it was something really cool I never tried. I was also very disappointed by the weapon system in the game. Fallout New Vegas had different weapons of all kinds, with preset damage outputs and could be found in certain areas generally based on how difficult it was to clear said area. Not in this game. No matter where you go and how difficult the area is to clear, weapons deal damage based on their 'level' which is dictated by your level. If you get really lucky you might find a 'unique' weapon with a special name but only differs from other weapons in that it might have some mods already installed, and maybe a special bonus to sneak attack damage or something. In most cases, unique weapons will look near identical to other basic weapons. Outside of unique weapons, there were science weapons and as far as i know, there were only 4 of these in the game. Science weapons (while hyped up to be really cool) to me seemed almost useless in gameplay. There are perks that you can take to increase their damage, but that only about doubles it, and you only get to do so in endgame where doubling their damage leaves them about half as effective compared to other weapons. In the end I only used one science weapon out of all of them where it worked on the final boss even though it really shouldn't have.---Spoiler Warning! Below I discuss my qualms with the ending I got---The ending felt rushed. You have to break into the most secure prison in the colony on a storm planet that is hyped up as in 'inescapable labyrnth' to free your mad scientist friend. Honestly, the way it was described I thought it would be really epic, but it was painfully not so. When you land on the planet a corporate solider tells you "hey, we are going to kill you for landing here unauthorized" despite not shooting down your ship, and if you succeed in a dialog check you get him to send you his ID which you can use to go through THE ENTIRE END DUNGEON without combat. At least even if you went this route you still fought the end boss. I would be fine with the stealth ID route if the end dungeon was actually a labrynth and not linear, but because its so linear you can easily make it through the whole thing without your disguise wearing off. The end boss fight was lacking. Severely. Big bad corporate bossman tells you that you have to fight the most powerful automechanical ever made to get to him. Apparently the most powerful automechanical ever made just means having a shield, ramming at you, and breaking down each time it does so. It was pretty much the propeller-head miniboss from resident evil village. No second stage or interesting battle dynamics here. To make things worse, if you had the mind control science weapon, the fight was a cakewalk since you could just brainwash the final boss for a while to recover health whenever you wanted. A brainwashing weapon should not work on machines, let alone a final boss! After you make your way through that fight you confront the head of the board, who for some reason didn't execute your science friend the whole time you were fighting the robo-excuse-for-a-boss, despite having the guy in an electric chair. The head of the board dies in one or two shots and then you free your friend. The screen abruptly cuts to him talking to you and at the end of the talk the final cutscene plays. I was very confused because I still had to escape this maximum security prison. I stealthed my way all the way through and kill the head of the board while freeing a death row prisoner but the escape wasn't important enough to have in the game? Whats the point of hyping up the end dungeon as inescapable if they aren't even going to add the escape to the game?! Anyways, I had to include this long description because I just found it so disappointing, especially the bossfight.--End Spoiler Zone--Conclusion: While I did mainly focus on what I found to be the negative aspects of the game, there is certainly a lot here that Obsidian did well. The landscapes looked genuinely alien, the characters had depth and were well designed, and actual combat (despite lacking in a wide range of enemies or weapons) was interesting. To those who are looking to play space style Fallout New Vegas though, this isn't it. Overall, its a decent game, but not $60 decent. Try to get this on sale if you plan on playing.

_childDocuments_.review: I've honestly never been so bored in my life. Kept thinking it was "about to get fun" and then it was one mini- "boss" and  credits rolled. There almost nothing to do in the base game, nothing but useless items you never need to use, very annoying characters, very lame quests. Most interesting thing was the graphic design of the posters, loading screens, etc. There was more character and charm in the graphic design of flat objects than in the entire game!
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: Love it! While not as great as Fallout:NV, that is still a high bar to set. But if you love the humor of fallout 1/2 and NV, then get this game, period. End of review.I stole this game originally from a certain Bay controlled by Pirates, waiting for its Steam release. Yes, I stole it as I do all Epic games, as a serious F YOU to EPIC. I despise Epic. As I usually do, when they are good games, I promptly bought the game once it had a Steam release, despite already beating the game at no cost to me. Once again, F you Epic. Die horribly, Epic marketers.So there is my endorsement on whether this game is good or not: I paid money I hardly have to support the devs even though I had already played this game and beat it. (Plus, to be honest, I want to play the DLC, which unlike a lot of other modern games, looks to be good, an actual expansion of the game.)The story is not completely original, but I still found parts of it to be fresh and quite funny. _childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: I don't like giving long winded reviews, so i'll just get to the point and say it's mediocre. Story options are okay, but some quests feel unfinished and leave you feeling unsatisfied, even with the "best endings". Character build options are about what you'd expect, with each level giving you points toward an attribute, but Perks are useless most times, and the "flaw" system is dumb (and since perks are useless, there is no actual reason to take them). The story is it's strongest attribute, and it is insanely good. I would love to see a sequel, but only if they take the time to flesh out the game more. Lastly, if there is one solid way to reliably measure an RPG's worth, it's the modding community. And let me tell you: it's dead and buried.I reluctantly tell you to play Starfield instead. At least you can mod the weird ♥♥♥♥ out.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: This game is like a swan song to a great age of gamingThe story is great, as expected from ObsidianThe amount of content is meager and there is sadly no real innovation to be found in the gameplayIt seems there are DLC's coming to fix the small amount of content, but the price of the base game is way too steep for the amount of game you get for it. (get it in a sale, the price is fairer)Still though, despite the low quantity of gameplay, the quality is highIn my opinion this is better then Fallout 4, but doesn't even come close to fallout: New VegasYou could  say it's the little brother of Fallout: New Vegas, in space, with way less content, more basic gameplay and less interesting characters. But Fallout: New Vegas was an absolute jewel so it's hard to live up to that.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, love it, and I've played through it several times. But I don't agree with the patch being something you have to pay for. Anyone who already owns the game, deserves it for free. I love Obsidian Entertainment but this is just too far. I hope it was because of Private Division instead because I'd hate to see Obsidian go down this route.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: This game kind of feels like someone's way of holding a middle finger to anyone who says games shouldn't be political.  Because, boy-howdy, it is.But, its also has the kind of solid, shooter-rpg based gameplay that you would expect from the company that made probably the best fallout game since it made the switch to 3d.  Along with a well-built, lore-filled world; with interesting characters and a unique almost steampunk / future punk aesthetic.Nothing that's revolutionary, or knock-your-socks-off, but solid, stable, pretty and entertaining.  Definitely worth a playthough or two.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: To start I've played most fallouts and elder scrolls games. Was hoping OW would be the same and was pleasantly surprised when it was not. OW is a unique experience that offers a range of ways to play. It also learned from the past mistakes. Example, in fallout you recall a terminal or a door at the endgame that you just didn't have the skills to break into. OW has a respec feature that allows you to pay for respec, break in where needed and respec again as needed. Plenty of opportunities to be a perfectionist and work around skill limitations.Only real downside is that there isn't really a ton of things to do like with ES or FO. The game has bugs and gameplay issues to work through but I think this was Obsidian charting a new course and for what I'm hoping is just the beginning of their new journey. All the game issues are easily worked around and there's nothing I found game breaking.Also increasing the skill check cap from 100 to 150 was not awesome. However respec system and companion buffs provide easy workaround. I understand not wanting the player to be super over powered but at the same time I think more dynamic and maybe "realistic" (ie less bullet sponge situations) combat would be a better way to challenge the player.I'm only leaving a review because I hope more positive reception for OW will inspire Obsidian to really throw themselves into the sequel. I had fun, will replay it some more and look forward to the next one.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: So far a very good Fallout-esque RPG shooter.The World and characters are fun and interesting.The combat is much better than any Fallout game.The character development brought skills back, could be a pro or a con depending if you prefer Fallout 4's character building or the old Fallout games system.  Has a lot of skill checks in conversations similar to Fallout NV.The loot and crafting/modification is not as in depth as Fallout 4's. Overall a great game that I am thoroughly enjoying.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: This is definitely one of my top 5 games of all time and definitely the best game to come out within the last year or so. It's like Fallout: New Vegas in space and the nostalgia is there. Never have I enjoyed a game so much that I immediately started another play through immediately after beating it. I played through this game 3 times on game pass for PC and loved it. So glad that it's now on steam so I can buy it on the platform I prefer and try out the DLC. F*ck epic games. The only problem I've encountered while playing this game was that it would occasionally crash in the loading screen whenever you go to exit the ship or fly elsewhere. The only work around was fast travelling somewhere from inside the ship or loading a previous save. Not necessarily game breaking or as inconvenient as the corrupted autosave bug in FNV but nonetheless annoying.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ this game ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ slaps, I honestly think it's better than Fallout: New Vegas (however they are both very good games that I will continue to play). I got the game for a discounted price for $25 dollars off of humble bundle, worth every cent (and if I knew it was this good I would have bought this for anything under $70). The way I played it was by going through the normal quest, taking on any side-quests that were given to me, but not actively seeking them out. After that, I bought both dlc and reloaded a save previous to the final event. I completed both dlc (both having about 5 hours of content using the same strategy that was used for the main quest, not actively seeking out side quests). This game feels very fluid and there were very few times that I felt as though something was boring or useless, every activity was done with a purpose, not "go complete these 17 fetch quests for basically no reward." The fetch quests that did exist were side quests and. in my opinion, the least fun part of the game, the reward is significant, but as some fetch quests rely of random chance event (ie: getting a specific item to drop from a specific enemy). Even though that was my least favorite part of the game, the game was still enjoyable as the stunning graphics and visuals make walking for long distances a more enjoyable experience than it would otherwise be, you will also never be walking too far, and enemy camps being scattered around gives you plenty opportunity to think about what you are doing, do you sneak past them, oh but they have loot. Now the story, the main story is one of them favorite parts of the game, I wont go into detail here in case you haven't played the game before and I don't want to spoil anything, but everything I learned about who you are and what the world around you consists of, is believable, there are many sides to every story and this is no exception, you have to choose how you go about completing the story, and I may not know all the ways, but rest assured I will be figuring them out. Now to my favorite part of the game, the companions. My two personal favorite companions to bring out on quests with me were Ellie and Parvati, but other companions were used whenever their skills would seem to be needed in the near future (and oh boy were they). I love the passive dialogue that happens between your two companions in the wilderness, I love they have in-depth personalities and opinions on what you're doing and what you're being offered, I love that they interject during conversations to add their opinions to the conversation. I also love the quests that they offer you, whether it is to make peace with dead partners, to find love, or to screw over your stuck-up family, I loved every second of learning more about my crew and helping them out. I never felt forced into doing anything (other than the main quest, obviously, but I could take my time as there were many side-quests to do). I didn't gain access to them until later (because I am a doofus and forgot to level up the required skill) but companions abilities are an extremely fun part of the game, what they do is while looking at an enemy, pressing a designated button (default keys are "c" and "v") to have one of your companions (depending on which key you pressed) do a special attack on that enemy with a special animation and has a decently long cooldown (about 30 seconds to a minute from what I remember). These abilities can also be improved as the companions level up. Now the skills, I really like the way the skills were done, putting each skill (which are affected by you base stats) into a category and allowing you to level up the category (usually with 3 skills) until each skill is level 50, at which point you level them up individually, getting bonuses for every 20 levels in that skill (and 150 if you have the dlc). I played the game on hard mode and that forced me to always be in the moment with the game as many of the high-level enemies could kill you before you can even say "oh ♥♥♥♥!" But, when all else fails drugs are always there for you. Now the non-game aspects, the load times are definitely longer than New Vegas, but, as a trade-off, the majority of buildings do not require a loading screed, they were already loaded in by the time you get there, meaning you are in way fewer (albeit slightly longer) loading times, I would take this trade-off any day of the week and love how the implemented it. I intend to play much more of this game with many more characters and choices to make.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: Nice game. Really has a Fallout4 feel to me, with many ideas coming from many other games, including Mass Effect. However, it sometimes feels the ambition isn't met.You have a spaceship but it doesn't give a sensation of freedom as the game is very linear.You can mod your weapons and armor but end up using the same builds all the time.You can do many sidequests, but then you'll level up too quickly and the game becomes too easy (including the fact that the enemies' difficulty isn't openly readable : nothing can tell you that an enemy can be one-shot or make you use all your ammo).Overall it's a very strong RPG-FPS game with lots of shooting, looting and dialogues. The lore and general atmosphere are refreshing. Graphics are good. Never had any bug.I didn't buy the DLCs, maybe they added nice things in them. I'll never know.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: Some of the most fun I've had with an RPG in a long ass time- Compelling story and side quests that beg ethical and social questions- Cast of unique and memorable characters, and Felix is an absolute Gem in my opinion- combat feels better than most RPG's, heavy weapons feel punchy and melee feels impactfull- Adaptive story with no restriction to your actions. kill who you want, befriend who you want, be who you want. True RPG freedom-- The relative low budget of the game shows through in some places such as with reused animations, models, and lack luster explosion effects. But doesn't detract from the overall experience and still looks fantastic in my opinion-- Shorter than I hoped it would be, but very replayable

_childDocuments_.review: The Great: It truly does play like Fallout New Vegas: Space Edition. The art style is heavily inspired by Fallout, while having it's own unique "space-y" touches.  It's very visually stimulating without going over the top. The different worlds and towns are unique to themselves, and don't feel repetitive (yet).  The satirical dialogue is done well, you'll get some laughs out of the goofiness or downright stupidity of the cast.  The companion system is well done, with lots of dialogue options as well as character and location specific commentary. Most importantly they almost never get in your way or slow you down.The Not-So Great:The entire combat system feels weak, especially in the beginning. The "dodge" skill feels useless against enemies that mostly have guns - The melee weapons all seem to have the same drab 3-hit combos - and the special weapon effects don't feel very powerful. The exploration and looting systems also don't bring anything new or unique to the open world RPG genre. Although it's definitely not "bad" per se, it just feels stale. Overall I would definitely buy this game again. Story-Driven Open World RPGS like these will forever hold a place in my Hard Drive.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: 6.5/10 I went into this game with high hopes and was left pretty disappointed. There was enjoyable moments but it ultimately felt more like a long demo than a full AAA game. Pros-The combat is laid-back, not overly complex and made for an overall enjoyable experience-I liked the crew/companion aspect of the game - Felix and Max were my favourites (also enjoyed Phineas' character)-There are some genuinely worthwhile side quests hiding amongst the fetch and grab tasks-Some of the dialogue is top notch (falls flat in certain areas though) voice acting is good also-I liked the use of Fallout:NV style faction reputations but felt it could've been expanded on-Some areas of the game are truly beautifully designedCons-The "open-world" areas are minuscule, repetitive and offer no real incentive for you to explore-There is little to no variety in weapon/armour and the tinkering/mod system is pretty bland-The RPG elements in the game are lacking-The game has been poorly optimised for PC -The overall 'anti-corporate' tone of the game falls kind of flat and the world feels under developed -The vast majority of NPCs are quite shallow and one dimensional (there are a few exceptions)-The main quest-line is painfully short and seemed to end very abruptlyVerdict: If you can pick this game up at a severely discounted price, have a weekend to kill and are looking for a *NEW* FPS (with vague RPG elements) then yeah, I would probably recommend it but don't go into it expecting a open-world, Bethesda/Bioware style RPG.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: Thought I'd add it to my steam library and give it another play-through (previously bought it on epic, but not a fan of that). Doesn't seem to be everyone's cup of tea, but I really loved it.Combat can be a bit easy, even on the harder difficulties, especially on a second play-through. The gun-play can get a bit same-ey, so not amazing build variety (especially since you can pretty much just max out all the passives by the end) but where it excels is the story, I really like the humour. Though that only really works on the first play-through, but there's still things to do on a second and third, like murder everyone, get different endings, try some skips... (I'm now coming back for the 2nd DLC)

_childDocuments_.review: Optimization is still dreadful. 2070s and Ryzen 7 3700x get around ~80fps on High settings at 1440p.The gameplay is just boring. Shooting is barebones. Leveling combat abilites only grants you some passive effects that are quite shallow. Exploration and loot are boring. All you find, wherever you go, is ammo, cash and random consumables sprinkled with n'th of the same gun model. Within the first two areas of the game you will have seen 80% of gun and weapon models the game has to offer. Weapon and armor modding are boring, uninspired. Just slap a +3 mag size or +x physical dmg reduction.I decided to go a lone wolf path, because i cba with these companions. So... uninteresting. Boring characters... Writing is somewhat interesting at times, if you can get past the Talking Heads From Oblivion. They even give you an option to turn in your biggest ally at the start of the game. Sadly it doesn't do anything and the story just goes on as it normally does.It's a watered down and minimized New Vegas. With little to no innovations to push the game into 2020. It feels old and boring.

_childDocuments_.review: There's some fantastic dialogue writing here, but the amount of time you spend looting junk in this game made my brain melt. I started having fever dreams about shaking down another shower cubicle for valuables. The quest design is also disappointing. While the set ups are intriguing, they almost universally end in three options: help group A, help group B, or do a bit more work to keep both happy. The ending missions were also disappointing for a number of reasons (both mechanical and narrative) that I won't spoil.All that aside, some of the conversations you can have with companions and others are so good that if you really like looter-shooter mechanics I can still recommend this.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: It's this simple.You launch and try to play FO4, and then you gotta' go and mod the living daylights out of it to improve it's performance, as well as the ability to load and not crash. Which is always a gamble. It's the same for many recent Bethesda games. New Vegas, imo, was the crowning jewel.Now you got Outer Worlds. Made by Obsidian. The one's that made New Vegas. No crashes. No bugs. No glitches. Smooth running, loading, it's just New Vegas in space.Forget the wastelands. Space is where it's at.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: Decent RPG kind of old school classic style. I didn't complete it got too bogged down with side quests and lost focus but it's a fun RPG nothing stands out as exceptional but no bugs or grind either. A solid buy on sale. I enjoyed switching up my team as I unlocked characters but generally stuck to the two that were most useful to my build. Never used the doctor for example. It's a story game not a combat game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really enjoying it lots of people will compare this game to Fallout New Vegas they will say that this game is fallout New Vegas but in space, this game to me feels like a Fallout game mixed with Borderlands. This game doesn't have the longest story or the biggest open world maps if you compare it to other RPG's, but overall game is great & it's not a Broken mess that New Vegas was.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: Despite the internet saying its not worth it, I genuinely say the internet is largely wrong here. The roleplaying element is extremely fun and fitting, since the world and quests gives you a lot of opportunity to roleplay often. Fallout NV had good roleplay too, but it didn't let you act it out in dialogue as often and almost as consistently as here. The major choices you make are interesting, they're quite in the gray area but most of them do stick the "did I really make the best choice here?". This is supported by the fact that the lore and backstory of practically everything is quite rich.I think this is due to Outer Worlds being smaller, and the dialogue opportunities and encounters are huddled together more so maybe that's whats making me feel that way. Talking bout the game world; I really recommend just a single playthrough to experience it, coz it really is extremely unique and fun to get into. You'd think the gimmick of a corporate owned civilization gets old, it doesn't and it ends at the right place and time.My only gripe with Outer Worlds was that its a little too short, and the gear doesn't vary enough to help with the roleplaying. BUT the gear thing kind of makes sense considering the lore and everything. The RPG elements aren't so bad, it was nice to theorycraft a build and the levels are designed to allow any sort of character. Its FNV lite RPG character building elements, which imo isn't such a bad thing here.The gameplay is smooth and fun, even the gunplay was decent for this kind of title. I specced my character into a squishy genius sweet talking gunslinger, and over time he became a drug addict that has a fear for specific wildlife and is extra vulnerable to electricity. The rest of it fell into the story's and world's hand quite naturally for roleplay purposes.The story is alright, nothing super amazing, but its nice enough to warrant a sequel. The side quests though is where most of the immersive meat comes in and its pretty fun to get into. All in all, it is worth a try. Steam says I've played it for 28 hours over the month I've had it lol, but I enjoyed every second of it even though I could only play a few hours a day (if I get the time to play it)My advice, play a roleplay style character, stick with it and you'll be able to enjoy this game like I did
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: Aggressively mediocre. If you are desperate to play a first person RPG, this will do. But I can't actively recommend it. Replaying New Vegas for the 10th time will likely be more fun.Loot and gear in particular are some of the most boring you'll find anywhere. It's similar to Fallout 3, but with even less variety, and a silly level-based gear system. Replacing a generic level 25 pistol with a generic level 30 pistol is so fun!
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: I am going to compare this to its closest competitor, Fallout 4. I really enjoy the game, and I think the comparison to the latest installment in singleplayer Fallout is fair.Pros:- As an RPG this game shines way more than Fallout 4 does. The dialogues between 2 people are alive and so are the characters. You see what you can say and there are different possible reverberations to how you act. The game gives you much freedom in dialogue which is one of the key points in my opinion. However the character customization and stuff are very superficial, which we will get to later on.- Overall gameplay is quite nicely designed. I like playing on the hardest difficulty when I play games, and it feels challenging and fair. The slow time feature is way WAY better than the one in Fallout and makes more intuitive sense. The game flows at a smooth pace.- Quest variety is wonderful and the world is affected by what you do greatly.- Optimization is way better than Fallout's despite being a newer and more demanding game. I did not experience any drops of any kind anywhere.Cons:- Level design of some locations is very bad. You land on a planet, thinking it is a planet, but then it just ends up being a 20 minute exploration to discover everything located there.- A laughably bad perk and skill system. It is shallow and not well thought.- Horrible variety of weapons, armours compared to Fallout 4. Who even made this? The same weapon just called "Mark 2" and it is better. That's it.- It isn't nearly as open world as Fallout in my opinion. It feels that way at times, but looking at the bigger picture, it definitely is not.- So this one is not necessarily a comparison, but a personal opinion. You can actively play matchmaker for 2 characters in the game, however you cannot romance anyone yourself. I really enjoy seeing the realationships between 2 characters develop, possibly into romance, so this irritated me.I did not want to get into every detail so I will conclude this here. If you enjoy the Fallout franchise, this is a must buy in my opinion. Wonderful game, just very narrow, compared to Fallout 4. Buy it, especially on sale, and you won't regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: Basically Fallout: New  SPACE!!!!Seriously though, considering who developed this, the parallels are hard to ignore: You start of as a nameless nobody who gets caught up in extraordinary circumstances and an epic plot with the lives of millions on the line, along the way meeting a whole bunch of quirky characters that will help you on your quest. Choices matter in that it will affect how people react to you, what resources become available to you, and how lives and who dies which may or may not have ripple effects throughout the larger story as a whole.And in the middle of all that is a whole lot of shooting (or melee if that's your style)That said it's not completely like Fallout though or it's cousins, the elder scroll games. You don't have a huge open world that you can hike across. Instead you have a space ship that can take you to a lot of smaller worlds that, while not as big, are still plenty enough to explore and provide a decent variety in environments to keep the game interesting though do expect to revisit locations several times if you go for all the side quests. In that sense what this game actually feels like a Fallout mixed with the travel systems of Knights of the Old RepublicAside from the shooter mechanics and somewhat compartmentalized exploration mechanic, another thing to praise about the game is the great writing and well-developed charters. All your companions (minus one mechanical exception) all have interesting personalities you'll want to get to know and interesting backstories you'll want to check out through their individual loyalty quests.All that said though, my main grips with this game is that compared to previous works by Obsidian it does feel a little short. A main story of the game can easily be cleared in under 10 hours and the combined side quests adds about just as much game time as that (The DLC helps to add a lot to the story and play time so consider getting the season pass if you can afford it). This left me feeling that there could've been a lot more to this game. But for what's here, it worth the price of admission.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: The Outer Worlds, or how I would call it: Fallout New Vegas in space! The skill system was clearly the main part of Obsidian's work in both FNV and TOW as they share similarities. Even Star Wars Knights of the Old Republic has the same style. If you enjoyed those games you will also not mind to take a look at this one.The only problem I got with the game is the performance. I am running barely 50fps with a 2080ti on a 21:9 3440x1440 4k monitor.Conclusion: AAA title worth picking up on sale, perhaps even full price if one is dedicated to the game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: First game I'm gonna really review, I first saw it on Xbox as a friend was playing it and waited for it on Steam. Visuals can be breathtaking on higher end systems and the story is really engaging, I search for any bit of story I can because they're really well written quest lines and such, especially the companions. This is the first RPG with companions involved that I've played and actually enjoy playing with them involved. I have all 6 quest members and have actively done all the quests that have come up. They don't get in your way. Gunplay is a solid 9\10 only because the obvious Spacer's Choice guns are pretty bad but that's kind of the point, seeing as they're the cheaper brand. Modification system is excellent and isn't overbearing but gives you a sense of control over what you want. If you want a RPG like Fallout: New Vegas, which is made by the same company, but better, then you have most certainly come to the right place.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: The very definition of generic.Is generic "bad" in the scope of things? Not at all. Generic cereal is fine. Generic pop is fine. Generic products, in general, are fine. That's kind of the point: you want a specific, generic thing and you don't care that it's not exactly perfect because the thing you wanted wasn't perfect or close to perfect to begin with. Have you played Fallout: New Vegas? Skyrim? Fallout 4? Well, this is the generic version of those games. The only thing this game has over them, in general, is graphics.Open world? No, not really. You have several places to choose from, but you'll have to unlock the content as you go. You're not "locked in" like most linear adventures, but you might as well pretend you are for the first several hours of the game.Interesting conversations with a useful dialog system? I mean, I guess, but it's nothing you haven't seen before. The NPCs are even more generic then usual. If I pretend to be someone I'm not, and you call me out on that, and it just so happens I'm impersonating one of your friends, you'd think there would be some character behind that interaction. You'd be wrong.Do you like Role Playing Games? Don't expect innovation here. It really is mostly "Hey, let me strangely explain to you an ENTIRE situation in which strangely you can solve by going from here to a map marker, killing some things, and then picking an item up."Ultimately this is a game Obsidian put a lot of time and love into, in an attempt to create the kind of game they think we're looking for. The problem? We found those games, we played those games for thousands of hours, and we really, really needed something new.
_childDocuments_.name: The Outer Worlds

_childDocuments_.review: This game is Obisidians first stand alone RPGFPS and overall it is worth the playthrough, getting the DLC on sale also add to the games interesting world built. However some of the locations and maps felt very linear and not as open world as one would have liked. The story was slightly interesting but didn't have me wanting more, and the characters were kind of dull and their companion quests weren't exactly super compelling. As far as leveling up once you max out at level 36 after the DLCs you can just breeze through any missions afterwards. The skills you can gain don't feel worth it unless you've piled them into dialogue or tangible skills like lockpicking and hacking. Unreal Engine is a beauty and the graphics are great to look at and the locations look fantastic, gunplay felt relaxed but engaging and the quirky and at times downright funny dialogue prompts display that classic Obisidian we come to know and love. Exciting to see where the studio goes from here!

_childDocuments_.review: The Outer Worlds is effectively the Fallout 3/New Vegas formula, scaled down exponentially in size, and sillier. While both The Outer Worlds and the Fallout games have dark comedy, The Outer Worlds is a bit more whimsical and over-the-top on a more frequent basis than the Fallout games. There were definitely a lot of dark events I read about and a couple of dark story beats throughout the game, but Fallout is the more serious setting. That said, by the time the credits rolled in The Outer Worlds, I had certainly gotten thoroughly invested in the fates of quite a few of the characters and the colonies. This game basically very similarly to a Fallout 3/New Vegas game, complete with mountains of items to steal and pickpocket from people. The setting/tone and size of the game are the big differences here.Although my play time shows as 67.5 hours, I don't know how many hours of that were me being AFK. However, this game is markedly shorter than a game like Fallout 3/New Vegas (I'm not bringing up Fallout 4 because I think The Outer Worlds' dialog systems were MUCH better than Fallout 4, in my opinion). If the selling point for you in Fallout games is that they take dozens and dozens of hours to finish, then you might not like The Outer Worlds. If you don't like space-faring settings or comical shenanigans, then you might not like The Outer Worlds.The only things I can really complain about with the game are that while the main storyline is present/active throughout the length of the game, it felt like it was absent in most of the middle of the game. On the one hand, it's cleverly subtle and doesn't feel like the main quest is a separate "thing" from the rest of what's going on in such a way that it's jarring. On the other hand, though, you may feel like the main storyline "stopped" a little ways into the game and doesn't really pick up again until you're in the final hours of the game. Other than the storyline, the companion characters were rather hit or miss. One annoyed me to no end, one has no personality, and one was a fellow who just didn't interest me. I adored the engineer girl, Parvati, however. I don't think I ever removed her from my party unless I had to. Oh! Last complaint: jumping feels weird in this game. There are no quests I can recall that require "platforming," thankfully, but there are a few boxes you leap to or shortcuts you might try to take which would have you jump on things. The jumping is clunky and did not satisfy me at all in this game, but these are minor gripes.Without spoiling what happens in the ending, I will say that it consists entirely of a slideshow and narration, much like Fallout 3/New Vegas. However, I LOVED it. I was shocked at how many different characters/factions were given ending narration, and the conclusions for them were generally really fulfilling. Now, if I had been a violent psycho-killer and ruined everything, the ending may have been a lot less satisfying (or more? =p), but I was left smiling and pleased with the ending of the game. It's nothing artsy or shocking, but I was not left disappointed. It's financially cheap to make an ending like this when compared to animated endings, but honestly, if they have as much screen time and decent writing as we see in The Outer Worlds' ending, then I would love to see other games adopt this sort of ending. Far too often, there isn't enough in the budget and a crappy 30-second movie plays that doesn't give you any closure. This ending is one that delighted me as a fan of closure. I'm not saying it's amazing, but it's the kind of thing I'd like to see more of in games, since endings tend to be some of the worst things in games, in my opinion.In closing, it's my opinion that if the gameplay loop of Fallout 3/New Vegas, space-faring sci-fi settings, and dark/silly comedy are things you would enjoy in a game, that there's a good possibility you may like The Outer Worlds. Unlike some who place a large amount of value on a game going out of its way to take a long time to complete, The Outer Worlds takes that Fallout 3/New Vegas gameplay and compacts it down into something that doesn't waste as much of players' time. There are a handful of locations that aren't related to quests, but not a lot, and I love that. The Outer Worlds respects your time compared to Fallout 3/New Vegas, and for that, it has *my* respect.

_childDocuments_.review: Games like this would not exist if the consumer culture was a little savvier. Well, they might exist, but in a better form. As it is, you market a game as a redefining of the genre from experts in the field and you'll get a million bored people with disposable income dropping cash on it before it even comes out. With the way gaming journalism works, you have 'reviewers' lining up to give it 9 or 10 outta 10 immediately, so they can farm those clicks and make their money off the surrounding hype. The game itself doesn't need to be good by that point - everybody who stands to make money has made it, and if you're left with a half-baked RPG, who cares? Certainly not the people who made it.This is not a revolutionary RPG. This is Bioshock-Borderlands-Fallout, and each of those games did a 'corporations are the enemy' storyline more compellingly, discussing issues of trust, responsibility and consequence. This game abandons nuanced ideological investigation in favour of patting you on the head for supporting the poor. Gunplay is adequate. Environments are ugly and shallow. Take a few things out of the Fallout character building system and add a few gimmicks from other FPS games and you're good, right? Who cares if the gameplay is a disjointed, hollow mess? Insulting.At some point, the consumer has to start exercising some discretion, or we're going to see every beloved developer milked for tripe like this based on pre-order cash alone. Also, what is it with games about evil corporations being made by evil corporations? This should never have been an Epic exclusive. Would not recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I found the game an entertaining carefree distraction. Hence, my thumbs up but not an enthusiastic thumbs up. It's a decent distraction if you can get it on sale, just don't set your expectations too high and try to enjoy the ride. Honestly, it is rare for me to feel so conflicted about a game. Typically I either obviously like it or I don't. Here, I don't regret playing it but I don't feel like I was invested in or inspired by it either. Bonus points for having silly marketing jingles that pop up in your mind even when you aren't playing though.The world: My initial feelings about TOW was "Fallout 4 in Space." However, as things progressed I found the gameplay mechanics are about at far as the similarities go. TOW does not have the sprawling and living world to explore like F4. You have what is supposedly a whole galaxy, but really the game still runs you on tracks. You are generally locked into a sequence of stops. Sure, you have the ability to go back to those other places, but there's nothing really there beyond some respawning wild enemies and some corpses/loot containers that get magically refilled. Otherwise, once your major quests are done the areas are pretty dead. Companions: There's also no feeling of depth to the companions but they do seem to fight well. You take them through their ho humm quest lines and *shrug*. There's no real point or change. They don't seem particularly invested in you nor you them. More of a "we're doing this until we're not." I think even the devs understood this, because the chat choice to boot each of your companions from the crew is ever present when speaking to them. More than any enemies in the game, I feared I would accidentally click the wrong chat choice and have one of my main party members disappear for good.Story: It's a decent story with some noticeable big decision points where you can change the end-game slide show. But it is short. Even while trying to explore every area I could find, loot every box, and do every side quest, the game felt short. I would rank the length of the main story track to be somewhat around the size of a F4 DLC. I did not try the new DLC for the game. Since it occurs sort of in the middle of the game instead of being the next step after finishing the main story and I had already played through all the way, I didn't feel any strong desire to backtrack.Overall, it was moderately entertaining and not particularly challenging. It also gets super super easy if you give your party nice weapons, get a certain *cough* science *cough* weapon for yourself, and enhance to the max. I was basically able to stroll around massacring entire groups of enemies without even pausing. Heck, the final opponent lived maybe 2 seconds and got a grand total of 1 shot off with their weapon. I suppose if I tried to sum the game up with just one word, it would be either "sufficient" or "adequate." Maybe 2 and 3/4 stars out of 5.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game, large open worlds that are tedious and feel empty. Lots of cool mechanics and item are ignored or  forgotten bc they are never necessary. The characters and interactions are the reason to play for me. Although the story was lacking and was very predictable, I enjoyed it. My main complaint, and everyone else's, is the extremely low difficulty making combat boring to all hell. it was only in the last battle that I used some cool tricks and actually had a challenge. There are no boss fights except for the end. Needs more boss fights and elites, personally would have liked them at the end of the companion quests. Side note, Pavarotti and Ellie are the best.  All this and the same flaws Fallout has with its mechanics like speech checks being over-powered and boring. With all these flaws and more, I am a fan of the universe and I would recommend a playthough when it goes on sale. A lot of love has gone into this game and it is dearly felt. I can't wait to see what game these devs come out with next. TLDR, flawed combat and story, but fun to play and some good talent went into this game. Voice acting and writing, especially the companions, make the feel of the game and make it worth it to me.

_childDocuments_.review: Well if there was a 'neutral' option I would select that, but all things considered, I'm leaning much more towards negative on this one after 26 hours. I'm right at the beginning of the final mission, so that can give you an idea about length. First of all it's too easy. I played it on normal, as I always do with games, but it's way too easy. Never really died instead of a few instances where I sprinted into the middle of some hostiles while mindlessly running to my objective. It is very difficult to die on normal difficulty. So if you are buying the game and have played some kind, any kind of RPG before, just play on hard from the start. There are no boss fights, you can talk your way out of most situations and even the "most difficult" missions involve killing 4-5 enemies with overpowered guns. But seriously, there are no difficult missions. Secondly, it's too shallow. I mean yes, there are choices and consequences and whatnot, but I really couldn't see any appeal. Nothing really makes much difference. Companion missions are meaningless, they add nothing to the game. At some points you think 'ah, maybe now the game is getting deeper' because someone starts talking about the universe and the cosmos etc. but no, it stays at that. The story looks promising at first but turns ♥♥♥♥ quite fast. You have all these reputations among factions but they are also meaningless. I am the end game now with more money than I could ever spend, extremely powerful weapons (which are also very repetitive and ♥♥♥♥), with persuasion and lying skills so high I can probably finish the game that way as well. Pros: Some dialogue options are funny. But in conclusion, I could teach either a 4 year old or a grandmother this game in half an hour and they would also beat it no problem in 30 hours without dying much.

_childDocuments_.review: 62.9 hours edit: Highly Recommended, Great Game, Unique Game, Good and Interesting Story, Good RPG systems, Good Weapons Systems which have grown on me over the hours of play, Good amount of Character Customization to suit desired play style, Very Few Bugs, and most importantly THE OUTER WORLDS is not, nor is it in any way intended to be, related in any way to the FALLOUT series. Take THE OUTER WORLDS for what it is: a great game in its own right. I've so far made it to level 23. I play pretty slowly though. I enjoy exploring.Negatives: I'm not deeply in love with the ranged weapons even though I set up my character to use them (am level 5 currently) [at level 23 ranged weapons are great!]. I would like to not HAVE to order my NPC party member to defend itself (trying to avoid potential spoilers). Perhaps there is a setting somewhere I have missed? Yep, I found the settings and now my NPC party members don't require constant micro-management!Positives: This game has attitude and a LOT of it! It's funny, it's sad, it's a bit nihilistic, and it's generally fun. I would like to play it on a machine that could handle maximum visuals but even with my i7-4770, 32GB RAM, and GTX 950 it's gorgeous and smooth [even better on new machine with everything on highest settings!]. Combat should be approached with some attention paid to tactics. The story has held my interest unlike most contemporary RPGs I've tried to play.I bought it as soon as it hit Steam and was not expecting 50% off at that time so that was nice. I think it was worth it. I don't think hardly any game is worth $60 though, so maybe I'm biased there.Overall, so far, I'm enjoying this FPS RPG in the limited time I have to play.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those "I wish I could give neutral review" games.   I say that not because the game is bad, but because it just doesn't quite do things well enough to be an easy recommendation.  I've played, enjoyed/loved, all the Fallout games especially Fallout 3 New Vegas and even Fallout 4 + DLC's.  This game tries to be similar to those games, and in a lot of ways it is, but doesn't quite capture the open world feel that I got in other titles.  Rather than finding random upgrade parts, scrap, ammo, perk magazines and such scattered around the world... everything is looted from loot chests (more or less) which brings the immersion down a bit for me.The skills, weapons, and upgrade systems aren't bad but it feels more like just dumping points into specific builds vs growing and evolving a character to fit your play style.The questions are well voiced and generally enjoyable but I don't recall doing anything that made a meaningful impact on the world as I progressed through the various stories and locations.  I'm fairly confident that most every person who plays this game will experience pretty much the same story and same outcomes with very little deviation.I still recommend this for anyone that enjoys mostly open world shooter RPG games with character progression and relatively decent story telling.

Every space-weirdo you meet feels unique but believable in their context and your companions all have their own questline which effectively develops their personality. The game uses its sublime writing to explore modern topics of corporate ideology and capitalism among many others in a superficial manner which adds a bit of weight to the otherwise goofy presentation. The gameplay is not exactly innovative and has it's quirks but It's solid and well-polished so It doesn't distract from the story.If you don't make the mistake of expecting this game to be New Vegas 2 you will find a great compelling RPG with It's own character and strenghts.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great so far. I've struggled with single-player games for a few years — they aren't as fun to me as they used to be. I don't enjoy games that are not a challenge to me, and single-player games tend to be very rich in story while being mechanically very easy. This game isn't particularly any different, but the player can choose how difficult they want their experience to be. Overall, I would recommend this game to anyone who enjoyed the Fallout franchise but I would not consider it one of my top 20 favorite games.Pros:- This game is not overwhelming for an open-world. You'll receive a steady amount of side quests that won't deter you too far from the main quest. This is good for me, because I don't really like to play games over again. There isn't so much to do that would require you to start a new character, but there is enough that I didn't feel bored or restricted.- This game is very familiar but is new enough that I didn't feel bored at any point. The game has character customization, perks, skill points, and a wide variety of weapons and modifications. Compared to the Fallout franchise, Outer Worlds allows players to travel to different worlds in their universe and explore different environments. You might hate what you encounter on one planet, but find quests, characters, enemies and weapons that are more your style on another. Outer Worlds doesn't invent anything new, but it does improve upon what many other open world games have to offer.- The enemies are very unique and diverse. I like that you'll find different enemies depending on what planet you're on, and what zone of each planet you're on. You can find a planet full of giant golems, or a planet full of agile beasts, or cities overrun by marauders. Some of the other reviews compared the game to Borderlands, and I think this is where there were similarities. Enemies have strengths and weaknesses, so its worthwhile to keep a variety of weapons.- The combat is simple but there were often times where I had to run for cover or even got overwhelmed by pressure from enemies. At the start of the game, I played it sort of like a run and gun and it wasn't particularly impressive. As enemy difficulty scales, you'll find yourself playing more strategically by taking advantage of your environment, enhancement drugs, weapons, etc. Cons- The weapons and weapon modifications weren't very impressive to me — at least where I'm at now. You can change your weapon type to incendiary, plasma, shock etc. and that can be good. But everything else is a little underwhelming. The modifications are more towards stabilization or noise suppression but that has never been an issue for me with base stats. There isn't a huge variety of weapons either. There are a lot of rarer weapons hiding around, and those can be good, but I've been using a sniper for a while and one-shotting most of my enemies. There are only 3 ammo types: light, heavy, and energy. Every gun fits under one of these categories. I was disappointed to see that an incredibly strong rocket launcher uses 4 heavy ammo rather than a limited rocket ammo, for example.- Your character play-style is limiting (or maybe not limiting enough?). At level 12, I don't feel that I really had to make any sacrifices to my character's perks or skills. I prefer to play without companions and with ranged weapons, which means that I haven't put points into companion or melee skills. Everything else is completely well-rounded — which I don't really like. You can upgrade ranged weapons, dialogue, sneak, etc. in groups. So upgrading the "ranged weapons" skill will upgrade short-range and long-range at once, for example. When sub-skills hit 50 points, you can only upgrade them individually. This means that although I have been building my character to be a sniper, I can use short-ranged weapons like shotguns or pistols, or even heavy weapons like machine guns, flame throwers, grenade launchers etc. at the same efficiency. I can swap out all of my light gear and weapons for heavy gear and weapons mid-fight without any consequences. - Looting is not particularly rewarding at a certain point. I'm at Level 12 and on my 3rd planet out of a dozen. I have so much ammo from looting the other 2 planets that I don't bother looting dead bodies anymore. I also have so many credits from side quests that I don't feel the need to pick up loot to sell to vendors. If I am fighting a group of 10 enemies, I will probably use about 15 - 20 heavy ammo from my sniper. After looting, I'll find around heavy ammo per enemy corpse. If I loot the crates around their camp, I will find around 20 - 40 heavy ammo. I'm shooting significantly less than I am finding ammo, and I am sticking primarily to one gun and ammo type. At level 12, I have around 800 heavy ammo, over 1500 light ammo, and over 500 energy ammo. Unless the enemies become drastically difficult, I don't think I will ever even think about how much ammo I have. It's also so incredibly easy to steal from cities or towns. The NPCs don't follow you around, so you can loot their locked rooms and find rare weapons or weapon parts without any effort whatsoever. I don't even bother being stealthy and haven't been caught doing it.- Fall damage really annoys me in this game. The planets have weaker gravity, so your character jumps higher and farther. However, your character takes fall damage as if the weaker gravity doesn't have an impact. When you do take damage, your legs are crippled and you walk slower for a duration of time. This can happen if you are sprinting and jump on a declining slope.
