_childDocuments_.review: Quick score: 5/5Notes: Don't buy it expecting gameplay similar to the original meat boy. However, if you are a fan of platformers in general, this game is actually great. It is an "autorunner" technically, however there is a LOT of depth to the mechanics and plenty of room for speedrunning and shortcuts. The overall game feels much closer to something like the chase sequences of rayman than a typical "autorunner".Lots of people crying about the auto runner aspect don't seem to recognize that once you start speedrunning and optimizing most platformers, they all devolve into auto runners to some extent. You hold the run button and time your button presses, the only difference now is that the game holds the run button for you. Look at almost any speedruns of platformers like Rayman, Donkey Kong Country, Super Mario Bros, etc. and they are almost all indistinguishable from "autorunners" 95% of the time.And for the record, I usually hate autorunners such as geometry dash or the bit trip series. But there is so much depth and nuance to the seemingly simple mechanics of this game that it honestly shouldnt even be considered an autorunner at all because it doesn't really play like any other game in the genre. You can use walls to completely stop, and you also frequently change direction, both things that pretty much break the rules of the genre.While there may be a bit more trial and error when it comes to learning the stages, you are given plenty of checkpoints and they are often spread less than 10 seconds apart so deaths are not at all painful. People also like to pretend that the original super meat boy didn't involve trial and error, but that is absolutely not the case. Not even to mention the homing missile and and homing black ball enemies, super meat boy was all about dying repeatedly until you "figured out" the timing of levels and mastering the inputs. So while in some ways it is different, in practice it is really not that different..

_childDocuments_.review: I tried, I really tried, but this game just isn't good. I don't care that its an autorunner, but I do care about the difficulty that isn't difficult in a way that Super Meat Boy was, but instead only frustrating. Some levelpieces are so incredibly tight to get through, that if it wasn't for all the checkpoints, I would have quit way earlier.I played through many hard games in my life, but this one is hard for all the wrong reasons.Yes it is hard, but it isn't fun.I had no problem, trying a hard level in Super Meat Boy for multiple hours, because it always felt like I missplayed and it was fun getting better.In this game however, it always feels like the game wants you to already know everything there is to know about the game, which only happens if you die to each obstacle to understand how it works. But with enough patience, you'd eventually have memorized everything. But I don't want to play a puzzle, I want to play a platformer if I'm playing Super Meat Boy.The worst part are the bosses. They just don't work. The first boss was easy, saw no problem in there and honestly every boss should have been somewhat like that, but they aren't.The second boss is way too tight. It wants you to press down to fall faster, to be able to dodge its attacks. Fair, its an autorunner, what else are you gonna do? But it feels like you get a few frames to do so. It is unnecessarily hard, just a tiny bit more time, would make it feel much better.The third boss was alright, fitting for a third boss imo.The fourth boss feels like you're trying to fight a swarm of flies, but if they ever touch you anywhere, you're dead. But you have to touch them in order to progress the fight. Sometimes you hit the enemy and die soon after, just because you didn't hit the entire mob and one tiny piece kept running at you, even though you're in your attack. It took me way too long to beat it and it didn't feel satisfying at all.The last boss i fought was the fifth (I don't know if there is more) and after half an hour, I still haven't figured out the puzzle on how it actually supposed to be done. I only ever get to the first time hitting him, but climbing up the wall to the second part seems to already be the hardest part of it. I don't know wether I'm supposed to be quick, save an extra item or I'm just running a wrong path. No idea. Sometimes it worked, sometimes it didn't. More times it didn't...Up there I didn't even understand how to proceed at all. The game has two controls, what is there that I could possibly be doing? Seems like its once again something very tight... and feels like that boss should have checkpoints there.So, I gave up. I didn't even get to see the Dark World. While I did do 100% in the original Super Meat Boy. What the hell man....

_childDocuments_.review: There's a lot of things to like about this game, but most of them are not the actual meat (not much pun intended) of the game.  The cutscenes are cool, the slightly-more stylized art is appealing, the in-your-face support for rando racing is fantastic for those in that niche....but.  The pure platforming charm of the original, which was so-finely tuned to work both to train the casual player and reward the master, is completely gone.  In its place is a runner game controlled with a slide button and a jump-punch button.  There are nuances here, but you can't ever walk up to them.  You're running running running and the game simply demands that you react, and do so perfectly.Even the so-called tutorial bits come at you at absurd speeds.  A little sub-window shows off what a button does, but only about a half-second before you need to use it, and use it with precise timing, or you get splatted back to the start/checkpoint.  This isn't just ignoring new players, it's outright hostile.The original Super Meat Boy was an all-time classic.  This disaster of a jumped-up phone game sequel is already being quickly forgotten.  I picked it up at 90% off via Summer Sale, and I'm thinking I regret it already.  Seriously, though.  Who thought that  degrees of freedom of control in a platformer which otherwise has the same game-world physics was a good idea?

_childDocuments_.review: Oh boy, this game. Super Meat Boy Forever is a hardcore precision platformer, and it's definately not for everybody.SMBF is an autorunner, and that intriguing modification of classic formula divided community straight in half. That said, this game is extremely well made and polished, do not compare it to your generic free to play mobile phone autorunners, quickly slapped together to make some bucks on ads.Clarification of some crucial points:1. Not an endless autorunner.2. Not randomly generated.Each world has 6 levels and a boss fight. Levels are made of hand-made chunks of varying difficulty, randomness only comes from order and selection of said chunks.Team Meat not only managed to perfectly recreate original fluid and highly responsive movement of Meat Boy, but to add so much more new mechanics and gimmicks to every single of 5 worlds, while not damaging core gameplay in any way.This is still a Super Meat Boy game, you still have your wall jumps, warp zones, traps, global timers, intricate, borderline convoluted level design and a lot, a lot of trial and error and frustration. Some chunks even feel more like a puzzle now, you actually have to understand what the heck is going on before making progress.Original Super Meat Boy is a hard game, and maybe my memories of it are a bit blurred, but man, SMBF actually feels so much harder. This game is . Insane timings, tight squeezes and nuclear mix of absurd mechanics are already melting grey matter, now try adding generally faster gameplay on top of that.They did such a fantastic job with visuals in this game. Every world is distinct, every color palette is balanced and pleasant. Light worlds are filled to the brim with vibrant colors, while Dark worlds are gloomy and bleak. More than that, every single level has its own style, lighting and background, depending on what gameplay mechanic it represents. Also I absolutely love angry Sun in Tetanusville.Storyline is served via cinematics after each chapter, totalling up to about 40 minutes long cartoon.Every sprite is crisp and readable, every animation is smooth and well telegraphed. Well done, Team Meat.I find it kinda hilarious that some people claim music being bad in this game. World 1 music is pretty bizarre, I get it, I also understand that most of people claiming said thing never actually did make it past World 1, but come on, haven't you heard main theme, its right there, on title screen, which comes before World 1, have you? Well, at least that's a good sign of a person whose opinion is not really relevant, I guess.Also, simple fact that music was done by Ridiculon and Scattle already ensures a lot of bangers in here, ye know. Overall musical arrangement is fitting and well made.Super Meat Boy Forever is a very fun, extremely challenging and so different, yet so familiar precision platformer.If you are able to leave "used to be better" mindset behind, you will get many, many hours of entertainment out of this game.If you enjoy difficult and diverse platformers - give it a shot, don't let negative reviews with 15 minutes of playtime scare you away.This game clearly is a labor of love, and I'm giving it my wholehearted recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll give my positives first, because I have to give this game SOME credit. the presentation is ultimately better than the first game; they clearly had a bigger budget and created a fully 2D animated game that adds more style and detail to the setting and character designs. And, while not as memorable as the original Danny Baranowsky score, the soundtrack is pretty good, with a wider range of instruments.Also, just like the first game, the controls are super precise and immediately respond to the player's input. Another cool addition is being able to attack enemies.Finally, getting the true ending doesn't require finishing the Dark World, and you'll appreciate that, trust me.Otherwise, this game was TERRIBLE! From what I heard, it was originally planned to be a spin-off game exclusive to mobile devices, but then they turned it into a direct sequel on consoles, and it certainly shows. They didn't put in any of the effort it takes to turn a mobile game into a console game, and it's even worse that THIS is considered the follow up to the original Super Meat Boy from 10 years ago. My problem with this game is its design. No matter how good the control is, no matter how hard you try, nothing will prepare you for the gameplay and the stage design. Unlike the first game, this is an AUTO-SCROLLING game, and each stage is comprised of several pre-made fractions of a stage; when you create a new file, all of the fractions of each stage are RANDOMLY GENERATED, so you can't even use a guide for this game, unless it's the first stage in a world. You're constantly running forward, and you cant stop, unless you stand in a corner or pause the game. And there's little breathing room for finishing a stage however you want. Even if you move faster or earlier than intended, there's a 90% chance that the obstacle in front of you will kill you in one hit, because it moves slower. Granted, you have checkpoints this time, but most of these stages go on WAY longer than they did in the first game, sometimes going on for 5-10 minutes at a time. Each world has a different stipulation, all of which should have been a part of your basic move set, i.e. turning back without wall jumping, and air-dashing up. And I bring this up, because this game also brings back the time trials. If you complete a stage with a Grade A+ rank, you unlock the Dark World version of that stage, a.k.a its hard mode. But NONE of these stages, or the pre-made fractions, were designed with time trials in mind, because you have to constantly dash to the goal-post, and you may end up losing by just ONE second. But, more importantly, HOW do they expect us to complete time trials in an AUTO-SCROLLER?? To make things worse are the boss fights. ALL of them go on way too long, and they, once again, have to be defeated in the most specific way possible. If you try jumping instead of ducking, you'll die. If you attack way too many times, a projectile will come up from behind you and kill you. Unlike the regular stages, these multi-phased boss fights have NO checkpoints, so you can be stuck on them for over half an hour!None of these issues are made easier with the unlockable characters. Most of them are just a change in cosmetics, with no unique abilities of their own to make the stages easier.In short, this is a poorly designed platformer, and a worse sequel to such an amazing indie game. Just stick with the original. It's much easier to pick up and play, and it's nowhere near as punishing for making mistakes. Best of all, you have complete control of your character, and you have the ability to come to a complete stop. MAYBE play the next game, because the ending implies that there will be another sequel. But do NOT waste your time or money on this game, it's not worth the frustration.

_childDocuments_.review: I knew this game was going to be an auto runner before it came out. But after having played the game up through to the boss of Tetanusville, I had to put it down, cause I was just not having fun.Super Meat Boy was a devastatingly hard game of precision platforming, and this has some of the same spirit. But the de facto inability to control your movement, and more importantly, many of the games puzzles and bosses being built around these limitations, will be a constant burr in your side. IF you've never played Super Meat Boy, and you enjoy auto runners, give this a try first. Maybe you'll like it for what it is, and you'll be able to look past the things it so clearly isnt.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, still. Let this genre be known as a chunky-environment-puzzle-platformer.4K on a GTX1070 is easy, 8x AA, no issues. Let's get this straight from the start: The game is auto-running for you, but that doesn't mean the control of movement is not there. There are specific golden triangles that enable you to stop, and/or change direction if required. There are more frequently enemies that are near the spinning blades but when sliding in crouch , you may easily attack, as if to be sweeping the yard.Playing with the controller is awesome. You will generally be double jumping, once to jump - Hold it for longer/bigger jumps, and then tap again for Kick or Punch, LT is a way to kill yourself, and restart the current chapter you're on.The auto-mechanic mechanism has cleverly caused each level to be broken up into chunks that you pass, and 'conquer' while trying to reach the end. Instead of best times now, it's more like, how many deaths per level. Could you do it with 0 ? practice of 2-3 per level -yes, you easily could. The constant challenge is now present, unlike Super Meat Boy which originally had many fast-paced levels , where even shortcuts could make up some time,  this game tries to punish you, and make you look ahead, even when you are surrounded, and trapped at the same time. You need to be looking for ceilings to slow yourself down/prevent your forward running, and go the other way, while the environment initiates traps as it enters the scene.All the traps, and interactions await your arrival to begin.Sweet Replays are still there just like the first one, and it's pretty awesome to see it happen as one smooth timeline after you have conquered any given levels. You actually appreciate these replays even more than the first, because you can spot your own mistakes here too. The level design, Spawn random seed at the start of each Save/Campaign is probably where this game will blow up. The value of this game is actually infinite, when you think of 6000 chunks, and 70+ levels, which use roughly 100 pieces per level, to bring your chapters that you pace through it in.I won't lie, there was incredible anger, and energy on not passing a specific spot, but the beauty is that you can just proceed to the next level - unlike last game-  and still play the same levels with different characters. The character roster looks HUGE - obviously, as a noob that just started, I have bandaid and super meat beater, I'm sure the originals and more will be there too, with some new spices to add along. What Super Meat Boy was famous for was level-design, and how quickly we got through them. This is exactly the same, whilst actually ramping up the times that you spend per level, because you are not fully in control. So, what this causes is each level to be a puzzle. It is up to you to scout ahead with the parts you see in your window currently.The biggest big is the menu not having a Quit button ?  -> Probably a Forever™ joke, It's fun, it raises the heart rates, and gives good sense of accomplishments. You may challenge friends with the same Campaign Seed-generation, but no co-op is here, maybe it will arrive in a DLC, Overall, the original formulae were amplified to cater to an even larger audience, while adding, and subtracting from what made it great, it's still a gem to behold, and all the negative reviews are either Epic-store haters, - [ungrateful game claimers] or people that are not able to mentally stimulate themselves to play a classic™ genre with a 2020's concept, even if it were to be put on rails for them.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a runner. Pretty good one, but still a runner (it looks and feels like a mobile game). If you ok with this, then go ahead and get it – it's good. There's a lot of additional hard levels though (dark version of every level and at least one additional world).- It's not the same as the Super Meat Boy game, though the feel of the game is pretty much the same.- Doesn't require too much brain juice. Playable with some TV show on the second screen.- It's pretty hard (mostly on bosses). Sometimes you need to spend 30-60 minutes on the same level. If you are not into hardcore games, it's not for you.- Level design in different then Super Meat Boy, seems more like The End is Nigh: there're checkpoints on the level, levels are longer then in Super Meat Boy, but there're ~10 checkpoints on every level.- Plot is pretty strange. A lot of animated scenes. Feels like a cartoon for small children. It's not bad, but not my cup of tea.- Graphics are... Well, they are ok, but feels too cartoony. Some stuff looks great, but if you see the game on the stream, you probably will not want to play it (too mobile visuals, I guess?)- Music is ok overall. Although World 1 music doesn't fit, it still sounds nice.- This was supposed to be a mobile game if I understand right. Somehow it's a PC game now, and there's no mobile version of it, which is pretty strange.- After some time of playing you want to play again Super Meat Boy.If you ok with controlling only jumps and punches, get the game. _childDocuments_.review: I was exciting to try this out, but I am incredibly disappointed.  I am not even giving it much time because I do not want to waste my life away with something that I know I do not like.  I loved Super Meat Boy which is made clear by my 30+ hours on record.  Even after beating the game I kept playing.  SMBF, hereafter referred to as F, is not fun -- the only requirement for a game.  You literally press one button.  It runs for you.  You have no control.  It is like watching a movie where you need to press a button to make the frames move forward.Games with simplistic controls can work, but those games still need polish.  Autogenerated, autorunner levels where you press one button lack quality control.  For example, One Finger Death Punch, is an inventive and fun game.  They took the time to make sure it was carefully balanced and the controls feel tight.  SMB had tight controls and was fun to play even if you died over and over again.  If you wanted more challenge, you can have it.  If you got frustrated with a level, you could simply come back later.  And it even had competitive aspects for speed runners without randomization.  F completely lacks the qualities that made SMB good.There is no way this game should be priced higher than SMB.  It is like a bad mobile app.  I do not recommend purchasing F unless it drops to $1 or below.  I hope that the next game learns from the mistakes of this one.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a great game, but not what you want from a sequence of Super Meat Boy...There are great visuals, the story it's there, like in the first game (although, in the near the end things get a little uninteresting to me), there is a gameplay that works (with its flaws), there are few songs with eletric guitar that are very good, some secrets that are fun to unveil and it is a Super Meat Boy themed game. It's a good game...While in the original game every stage is a little obstacle course where you have to keep improving your skills and trying new approachs in order to get the rankings (You die, you try again from beginning until you improve your skills or find a better route to win), in Super meat boy Forever, you are challenged with long stages divided in little segments where you have to find out what is the solution for each segment by trial and error and, if you want a better ranking, you have to memmorize every obstacle of a stage and hope that the gameplay doesn't screw you. It's not satisfying, feels like a chore honestlySMB1 - Fast-paced short trial and error stages with room for exploration.SMBF - On-rail long stages with patterns to memmorize in order to execute precision commandsSo, you see, you take a game with stages with a lot of room for exploration and different ways to win and switch it to one that takes away any agency from the player to show its skills and force it to do precision memmoriezed commands.... You just can't simply take away resources from your player and demand it to do it in a harder and more boring way.I guess, in the end of the day, it's a good game, the main issue lies in having it marketed as a super meat boy 2, not a spin-off. People waited for a Super Meat Boy but got a Geometry Dash kind of game...

_childDocuments_.review: The first SMB is easily one of my favorite games of all time. A+'d light and dark including cotton alley (minus some dark rapture levels and IWBTG because I just don't have the sanity) Was a little unsure how I'd feel going into Forever. I've never actually played an auto-runner before so I didn't really know how I'd like it, even with the familiar and beloved characters.After completing the first world, I was still on the fence but I think it was mostly due to me still familiarizing myself with the controls and gameplay. After beating the first boss and getting into world 2, it all just kind of clicked and the game managed to grab full hold of my concentration very much the same way SMB did when I first played it 10 years ago. I don't know exactly why or how but very few games have given me the drive to succeed as much as these 2 games.Forever is obviously a different game than the first but I've found this game to scratch the same itch for fast-paced gameplay and control inputs that SMB did, just in a different way. I wanted to wait to review until I did a basic completion of the game and even though I've died a few thousand times, it was never frustrating. I still kept coming back and striving to beat it. Both games are very good at that, at least for me personally. Now that Forever has kind of clicked for me, I'm excited to replay it for A/S rankings and collecting and trying out different seeds.As far as the other aspects of the game, the soundtrack and animations are great. The storyline cut scenes are fun to watch and still has a fun sense of humor about them. Definitely not quite as dark comedy as SMB unfortunately but still funny. Most likely dialed it back for the wide range of platform releases but that's just how it is.All in all, if you loved SMB and are open to the genre change, I think it's worth checking out. For me at least, it still hit all the notes of what I loved about SMB in a new and different way. I definitely see myself revisiting Forever the same as I do for SMB. If you're absolutely against auto-run games, not much you can do really so probably skip out.

_childDocuments_.review: I would just like to start with saying that this game is alright, the developers tried something different and it worked out in my opinion.  I believe a lot of people who really liked it expected Forever to be the exact same kind of game and got mad when they bought it and it wasn't, but literally reading the second sentence of the description tells you that the game is an autorunner, very different from the first game. While I do think that the first Meat Boy is better than this game, this game is solid and worth a shot.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Meat Boy Forever

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: It's not more of the same, but when SMB is as perfect as it is, why make more of the same? Autorunner was a great choice for SMBF to create perfection in another game style while still retaining the Meat Boy feel. Naysayers don't know anything other than clinging to the past.No, it's not a platformer like Super Meat Boy, yes, it is an autorunner, and yes it is still very much Super Meat Boy in feel, tightness, and creativity. The autorunner format is really taken advantage of well with new and sometimes crazy mechanics being added into the mix that can only work in an autorunner. All the chunks that allow for randomly generated levels felt good to me. Yes, I've read the complaints that some chunks are more difficult than others. They're not impossible. The hard ones are well designed and just require thinking outside of the box at times. Other complaints I've read are about the controls being difficult or unresponsive. First, no... not at all unresponsive. SMBF is as responsive and tight as SMB. Second, difficult controls?! There's two buttons! Down and a punch/jump button!There is still a challenge here but it's a good feeling challenge. Overall, it's really a good feeling game. Art style is great, cutscenes are darkly-cute and funny, difficult chunks are entertaining because they're so creative and well done, and the secret levels hit just right as love letters to classic gaming.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Meat Boy Forever

_childDocuments_.review: Ok so this game is..., weird. I will seperate this review into sections, each will focus on a part of the game.First of all - GraphicsSuper Meat Boy Forever unlike regular Super Meat Boy has very smooth finish, like glossy, glossy meat doesn't sound good, does it? Well it is great! ...and thats it, it is all that i can say about graphics here.Second Of all - Sound & Music Sounds are great, nothing else to say, but music is.... interesting. All the music is fine and all, but, it doesn't fit the area, bossfight, etc, it's just like you would listen to a paper mario music on a graveyard, or play megalovania in front of a Pope.... WAIT IT HAPPENED? But well it just doesn't fit.Third of.... Whatever - GameplayUnlike previous Meatboy game, this time, it is an autorunner. What does it mean? For me it means that i cannot explore for my myself, and am resctricted to planned paths, and for you, it mean that you can't stop running. Like literally, you run, forever. The same mechanic was used in Vector mobile phone games, but executed way better. Another change, that was implemented in this release is punching, kicking, attacking, however you name it. I really like it, combos chains are satysfying. And that's all about it. BossfightsOh man time to break down over a video game.... oh man it is time.I hate them in this game, they are tedious, they are difficult, they require a lot of practice and a great memory, WAIT NO, cross last one, there is RNG. Yes, there is, for example, there is a boss that spins and shoots lasers, first time it spins clockwise, second time counterclockwise, but third time is random, and it can REALLY screw you up. Or attacks that you cannot evade because they were paired up by the stupid RNG. But hey, it is meatboy, what did you expect.Performance It runs great.That's itIs it worth the price? For me and where i live? Hella no. I bought it, because i was hyped, when i saw an email in my mailbox, that SMBF is available, i ran to the pc, and bought it while the special offer lasted (like -30%). But now that i have played it, i wouldn't unbuy it. It is really good time killer, even if you rage, you WILL come back.Level DesignThey are repetitive, that 5300+ levels was a bit of a lie. (and every level set (5 worlds, each has 5 - 6 levels) needs to be on another save file and you have only 3 to choose from) But they are still designed great, haven't seen a softlock, ever. And you always know what to do in each level.Warp ZonesYes. they are here, and they are really difficult, not tediuos, not unfair, just difficult as ♥♥♥♥.Cutscenes & PlotActually great, not gonna lie, cutscenes are well made, and the plot is a joke, and i love it.Did i experience the whole game? _childDocuments_.review: This is just another case of gamers being too illiterate to read the the game is an AUTO-RUNNER. Digimon Survive was already enough.That aside, this game is great. It has all the personality of the Meat Boy series, with a banging soundtrack by Ridiculon (The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth, The End is Nigh) and an updated form of the original game's art style looking sharper than ever.If you don't like auto-runners, that's fine! They're not for everyone. But if you do, this is an amazing one that's definitely worth your time and money - especially on sale, because it's discounted often.-The movement is top notch, with slick and incredibly customizable controls yet based on simple mechanics that anyone can grasp: jump, slide, punch.-There's a ton of unlockables, ranging from playable characters to "oh yeah, I did this" achievements to show off on your Steam profile.-It has great replayability value thanks to a level generation algorhythm and a seeding system.-And it's a tough-as-nails challenge to get S rank on every level, of which there's lots and lots.And to anyone who left a negative review saying "oh my god it's an auto-runner my life is ruined", kindly reconsider going back to school. Literally: just read. It's not that hard.

_childDocuments_.review: This review was originally a bad review, but honestly, I kinda like the game. Just don't go into this game expecting super meat boy 2, it is anything BUT a precision platformer. I still do have some gripes with the game though: Every single death felt less like a lack of skill and more so the games fault.I will say, the art in the game is GODLIKE, it's 10 times better than the og meat boy art and cutscenes.I bought this game as soon as it came out on Steam because I loved the original Super Meat Boy. I bought it with the only prior knowledge being that it was a "Sequel" to the original Super Meat Boy.This is a sequel story wise, but not gameplay wise. It feels more like a spin-off game, but the fact that they announced this game almost 7 years ago and it turned out to be an auto-runner is really frustrating. The story mode was also not as long as I had hoped, there are only 6 levels per world and you can beat the whole story within 4 hours.If you want a game that's actually like Super Meat Boy, go play The End Is Nigh if you haven't already, it's very similar in the platforming aspect.

_childDocuments_.review: I just want to write a positive review to help push the game out of mixed reviews.Yes, the game is an autorunner. This info was available for 8 YEARS and is literally said on the store page, so I have no idea how there are people who buy the game and then realize it's an autorunner.Admittedly, it was a mistake on the devs' part to advertise this game as "Super Meat Boy 2". This may be a direct continuation of the story from the first game, but it really should have been advertised as a spin-off, because that's what it is.Also, many people judge the game from the first impressions that they get. They see this as a really basic game with 2-button controls and no gameplay variety, but that's just the start of the game. It gets a lot more interesting later on.Lastly, an explanation as to why I only have 32 minutes of playtime yet talk about how the game gets better later on and, according to my achievements, already beat the final boss - I just played the game outside of Steam at first. The achievements got unlocked when I launched the game through Steam for the first time.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Meat Boy Forever

_childDocuments_.review: I played the original Super Meatboy, and I thought this game was just as much fun. The platforming is done very well and the autorunning really keeps the game moving. I'd recommend this to anyone who enjoys fast-paced precision platforming.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Meat Boy Forever

_childDocuments_.review: I've played a full playthrough already on the switch and bought it on steam to play it again because I enjoy it so much :DIt is a platformer that feels really good to play and has a lot of replay value with its newgame+ option and how it generates a unique set of levels with each playthrough. Despite it being an autorunner, it has a very compelling time trial system that feels really good once you get the hang of it! (Tip: Punch in the air, even if you're just running on the ground!)
_childDocuments_.name: Super Meat Boy Forever

_childDocuments_.review: I know this game gets a lot of hate, in fact I used to dislike this game too, but honestly, even though it plays differently from the original, it's still a damn good game, I'd say it's just as good, I got this game during the spring sale, wanting to try it again, it took some getting used to, but it's still really fun, Ridiculon's soundtrack, while not as good as their 2015 Super Meat Boy songs, is still really good, the controls are what heavily divided the SMB fanbase, but I think they're fine, and the punches and kicks are fun additions, and the new movement mechanics are really fun to utilize (except the Clinic's fans, but then again the fans in the original Super Meat Boy sucked, and the fans in SMB are less prevalent so it kinda cancels out how unfun they are) and the fourth stage, The Lab, has some amazing mechanics introduced, while the bomb blocks are basically just more dangerous breakable blocks the punch modifiers added are amazing, the fireball has fun chunks utilizing it, the reverse punch and uppercut are absolutely amazing and so fun to use, and the warp punch is a unique idea that works so well, of course, I do have some criticisms, the bosses don't feel as fun, especially the 3rd-5th bosses, and the last warp zone character unlock requirement feels way too punishing, but overall, it's a solid game, I'd recommend

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't wanna buy into the negative reviews and figured I'd give it a shot. It's really not a BAD game but it's not even close to the tier of the original. The art is way different, the feel of the movement and the lack of control is off-putting. Auto-run takes away the finesse of mastering it. The addition of attacking is GREAT but it feels like it was just shoved in there to detract from the loss of free movement? I wanted to love this game and it was alright for a couple levels but man, having to fight the second boss over and over and realizing there really is only ONE way to get through the level and I have no creative freedom? No thanks. Glad it hit me before the 2 hr mark, I'm gonna refund this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite everyone else's gripe with it I feel like this game being an auto runner is a pretty nice idea. However, my biggest issue is that you cannot turn around, I could barely pass the second level because there were about a million obstacles I could have cleared in seconds if the player had the ability to turn Meat Boy or Bandage Girl the other way instead of always going forward. _childDocuments_.review: Quick Description:-Super Meat Boy Forever is the much anticipated and extremely divisive game that released last year to Epic Games and is now available on Steam.  Precision platformers are my favorite genre and Super Meat Boy is one of my very favorites, so I had been following this game for many years leading up to it's release.  SMBF is not for everybody, that's very clear.  However, if you go into this game w/ an open mind and embrace it for what it is, you might just find that it's an incredibly challenging and innovative runner-precision platformer hybrid that may change your perspective on the auto-runner genre.*Notes:-I bought this on Epic last year and played it for about 25 hrs.  I completed the game and unlocked the N+ Mode.  I died over 9800 times, collected 30 pacifiers, unlocked several characters, completed several warp zones, and completed 83% of the content w/ 100% on World 1, 105% on World 2, 94% on World 3, 101% on World 4, 83% on World 5, and 58% on World 6.  My very favorite levels were the Dark World Lab levels, those were incredibly fun.  I picked it up on Steam a few days ago and have played for a little over 3 hrs before writing this review.  All of my stats transferred over from Epic which was a nice touch by Team Meat.*4 Lines of Negative Rhetoric that I want to immediately address b/c I heard all 4 of these negatives even before the game released, and I've noticed that 99% of the negative reviews parrot these same narratives.  Everyone has their own opinion, and it's fine if you don't like this game, but I find it bizarre that I've heard the same 4 lines repeated for about two years now and that no one ever elaborates on why this is a supposed bad game:1.) Auto-runners are bad when it comes to Super Meat Boy (This seems like a silly thing to be unhappy about, but as I will explain in detail later, this game is not a typical auto-runner.  Ironically, games like Bit Trip Runner having glowing reviews, but ppl seem to think that auto-running is inherently bad when it comes to the SMB games.)2.) This is a phone game (Yes, this was a phone game 8 years ago, but now it's not.  This is not a cash grab, but instead, the entire game was rebuilt from the ground up once Team Meat decided that they wanted it to be a PC game.3.) Edmund left b/c he knew this game was garbage (No one knows why Edmund and Tommy went there separate ways, so this is just pure confirmation bias.  BTW, Super Meat Boy was made by both Edmund and Tommy.  Yes, Edmund is extremely talented, but so is Tommy, who was the coder for SMB and created SMBF.)4.) Random Generation = bad level design (The levels are not random at all.  Every single level has been hand crafted and broken down into chunks.  Every single possible combination has been tested, which may be one the reasons this game took a long time to create.  These chunks allow for so many subtle variations of the levels, which helps replayability a lot.  I've never heard ppl complaining about Enter the Gungeon or Binding of Isaac having terrible level design b/c of the random generation of levels.)What's Good:-I'm not a big fan of auto-runners, although I can't say that I've played a ton of them.  I enjoyed Geometry Dash and thought that Bit Trip Runner was fine.  SMBF has far more in common w/ Super Meat Boy or Celeste than it does w/ Geometry Dash or Bit Trip Runner imo.  SMBF feels far more like a hybrid of the two genres than any other game that I've ever played.  The Dark Levels are especially creative and challenging.  If every game in the auto-runner genre had this level of depth, I would play a lot more games like this.-There is a ton of content here.  It took me about 24 hrs to 85% the 6 worlds, collect a good amount of pacifiers, unlock N+ Mode, and mess around w/ a second file.  I've heard that you can play the N+ Mode 10 times before seeing identical levels.  Getting all of the pacifiers, completing every warp zone, and unlocking all of the characters will be especially challenging.-The bosses in SMBF are a huge improvement over the bosses of the original SMB.  To be fair, bosses are typically a weakness in this genre, but these bosses are excellent imo.  They are big, bad, menacing, but most importantly, they utilize the games main mechanics in fun and innovative ways.  Every world has a boss and each one felt better than the last.-I'm a big fan of this aesthetic even if it isn't for everyone.  It reminds me a lot of Rogue Legacy 2, which I thinks looks great.  For some reason, ppl compare this aesthetic to a Flash Game, which seems really silly to me.  I think the animated scenes look great visually, the levels are packed w/ bright colors and detail, the bosses look really cool, and this runs just as smoothly as any top tier Indie game.  SMBF went for a different tone and style than the original, and I think they pulled it off.  Another reviewer mentioned that he had frame rate issues, yet on my very basic rig, this game ran at 60 fps w/ very little load time and I experienced zero bugs.-SMBF is an extremely easy game to learn the basic mechanics, but offers a fairly high skill ceiling.  Since the game auto runs for you, the devs could really ramp up the creativity when making complex levels.  This is typically a challenge for precision platformer devs b/c if the player doesn't understand where they are supposed to go, they won't be able to complete the sequence.  In this game, you are always guided towards your solution but you have to use your wit to find the solution to the problemCould Use Some Changes:-There are checkpoints which make perfect sense b/c of how long the levels are, but they do take away from the exhilarating feeling that you normally get when finally finishing a platforming sequence perfectly for the first time.  I found the thrill of completing a level less rewarding than my favorite games in the genre.-The first World is very simplistic and imo the least interesting visually.  This is the way most games are though, so I understand why the devs designed the game this way. Unfortunately, far too many ppl played for 20 minutes, and refunded the game.  One of the complaints was that they didn't like the soundtrack or the platforming sequences in world 1.  To be fair, the original SMB World 1 is just as simplistic, but very few ppl have complained about it.-If you skip all the Dark Levels and only complete 4 levels per World, you can fight the boss, so it's actually possible to complete the first 5 worlds in 2-3 hrs.  This may give some players the impression that this isn't a very long game, when that is not the case.  Most players will need 20-35 hrs to fully 100% a save file on your first playthrough.Thoughts:-I was very skeptical going in last year when I decided to pick this up on Epic.  I almost never play games on Epic and I'm not the biggest fan of auto-runners.  To make matters worse, I didn't enjoy World 1 all that much.  However, as I pushed forward, I began to enjoy the game more and more w/ each passing level.  It felt like I was playing a new genre, and one that I could enjoy quite a bit.  I don't think that SMBF is as good as the very best precision platformers out there, but I don't think it's that far behind them.  I've played and reviewed 40-50 different precision plaformers, and I love so many of them.  I've noticed that most diehard precision platformer fans tend to like this game b/c they go into it w/ an open mind, and don't expect a clone of the 2010 SMB.Consensus:-Solid Game (Tier 3 and makes up 35% of my reviews).  I don't think that SMBF is as good as Celeste, Super Meat Boy, The End is Nigh, Remnants of Nazieth, N++, Sunblaze, or Octahedron.  However, I think it's just as good as games like Slime-San, Super Magbot, Q a Neon Platformer, Rifter, or Dustforce.  That's good company, and Team Meat should be proud of what they have created.  I'm looking forward to many more hrs of this runner-precision platformer hybrid!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is being judged way too harshly, especially when the developers put "auto-runner" in the store description. I always try to judge a game on what it is rather than what I want it to be, and this game is great. I'm a massive fan of the original SMB, and as much as I would've liked a traditional sequel, Super Meat Boy Forever is still fantastic in its own right. The platforming feels just as good as in the first game, and the levels are all very unique and challenging. The animated cutscenes are very polished and well done, even if they are missing some of the charm and humor of the original. My only wish would be that the levels were shorter. Part of the appeal of the first game was being able to play through single bite sized levels over and over until they were beaten. In this game, these previously small levels are grouped together into larger areas that must be completed all in one go, which makes getting through the game more of a slog and special challenges like pacifiers harder and more tedious to get than in the first game. I also wish playing through all the randomized levels wasn't tied to resetting your whole game, it makes completing challenges kind of a drag when you know you have to start all over and delete your progress to experience more content. If there was a way to just infinitely play through randomized level segments on each world that would be cool. Even though SMBF isn't perfect and not what most people wanted, I still think it's an amazing game that's worth your time. If you're able to accept the fact that it's an auto-runner, see what it has to offer and you'll have a great time. It's a game that proves auto-runners can actually be good.

_childDocuments_.review: This is quite a difficult one to review, but I'll try. If you're looking for a number, I'd personally give it a 7/10 - fun for a while, but I'm really not sure if I care enough to unlock/complete all optional content.It's quite a good one among its own genre, but I feel like it's limiting its potential by being designed for mobile screens. Long explanation and thoughts below.First, a couple of disclaimers: it's an autorunner, so I'm going to review it as one. If you buy this game expecting a platformer like the original SMB, you're going to have a bad time. Autorunners as a genre are almost rhythm games more than platformers, as there's a really clear set of inputs you need to press in order to progress. Basically: if you despise the whole idea of an autorunner, just don't buy this one. :DI've tried many autorunners (mostly on mobile), but rarely played any of them for more than an hour or two - most of the available autorunners are mobile games filled with p2w microtransactions. Even though some of the mobile design can be seen in SMBF (I'll come back to this), there's none of the microtransaction stuff here - just a plain old challenging game which you buy to play.When I opened this game I had open mind willing to give it a try, hoping for the best.The whole game works with 2 buttons:I really think the game would be better if jumping and punching were in separate keys. There was a couple of spots where I needed to jump and punch in quick succession, and I feel it would've been much easier and smoother to handle by using different inputs for different actions rather than tapping one key in odd rhythm.There's also one area where there's black holes that suck you in, and you can press the jump button to shoot yourself out. You can choose the shooting direction by pressing the slide key - every press of the slide key turns the aim direction 45 degrees clockwise. This felt really dumb, since it would be much smoother to just use dpad/stick/wasd to aim.I feel like the choice of sticking only to 2 buttons really comes from the game being designed with mobile in mind - when the mobile version launches, I'm expecting something like "left half of the screen = slide, right half = jump/punch". This is good *for mobile*, but feels limiting on PC. On one hand I understand that this way you have no balancing issues on separate versions of the game since everyone has access to same actions, but hey - .Levels are mostly good, but there's quite a bit of trial & error here and there - eg. there's occasionally some moving which you really can't predict until you see how they move, and you'll just die and try again from a different route. But since retrying from nearest checkpoint takes like 4 seconds, it's not as big of an issue as it might be in some other game. Still annoying though.The structure of the game is as follows:It took me roughly 4 hours to kill the boss in 5th world and see credits (and 1 hour of that was spent at the last boss), but unlocking dark world versions will take a while if I want the challenge.At this point I could also choose to start a "new game plus", which keeps my collectibles and unlocked characters, but  - all normal levels in this game are randomly generated by using premade "parts" in a randomly chosen order. You won't see the same levels as your friend, unless you manually choose the same seed when starting a new save.I was positively surprised by the boss design, most of them were quite fun - and something I've never seen in other autorunners. You're practically in a small room, running left and right, always turning around at the walls, punching boss in the middle as you run past (or something similar).But then there's the last boss, which seemed to be just trial & error from start to finish - there was really no way to predict most of the mechanics in that fight. I could list at least 10 different spots in that fight where I had no way to know what's going to happen next, until I actually just died to the mechanic. And even after that, there was a couple of spots where I literally just tried going in different directions to see which one is correct, because I had no way to know without testing and dying.Other bosses had a couple of similar spots, but they were more "free form" - the last boss has only one route to completion.

_childDocuments_.review: I have >400 hours on switch+epic version of this game.Not one to typically speedrun any game, but I liked this game enough that I decided to start speedrunning it (half that playtime is from speedrunning). The other half the playtime is just playing casually, getting max% took some time, and it's pretty fun to clear levels on the switch when lazing around.Common misconceptions that the game is:a) endless runner. it's not endless, there are levels, story, bosses and chapters just like in the first smb.b) randomly generated levels. The levels are not completely randomly generated, each level is made by piecing together handcrafted chunks.The gameplay does not fit the mold of an autorunner, and the only element it shares with them is that you move forward without pressing anything.Most runners, like geometry dash, bit-trip runner series, the gameplay loop revolves around reacting to the stage, reacting to what's thrown at the player, often like a series of quick-time events or playing to a rhythm. While that still happens in SMBF, it is to a much lesser extent, here, the player is given control and the stage/game reacts to you.While the autorunning makes the gave less forgiving, as it's hard to recover from mistakes. Once you get used to the autorunning, it kind of takes a backseat, and it plays more like a platformer than a runner - as you're able to use dives and dashes to make adjustments to your movement rather than just having the fixed trajectory of your initial jump. Getting S ranks is akin to going for SS in games like Dustforce, where you're trying to get a clean run throughout the entire level.The game does suffer a little bit from telling the player what to do, especially in the later stages, where chunks can be pretty convoluted, it takes a bunch of death to parse the level and figure out where to go.

_childDocuments_.review: tl:dr: I played hundreds of hours on Epic during the first year. Great game, 9/10. Autorunning is implemented very well with plenty of movement options and interesting platforming, but IS different from the original game. Legitimately amazing for speedrunning.Steam version appears to be mostly the same, with a DLC menu option indicating more content coming soon.---Ive put hundreds of hours into Super Meat Boy Forever (SMBF) during the first year it was exclusive to Epic. I highly recommend this game, and I'll break down why for two perspectives: casual and speedrunning.First though, I'll address the elephant in the room compared to the original Super Meat Boy (SMB): this game is an autorunner. Many people dismiss it right away because of that, but by doing so I think they're missing out on a great game. Its not as restrictive as it sounds. You're given many movement options: a jump, an air dash, a slide, a dive, the ability to turn around by jumping off walls, and even more options introduced in later levels. The levels are well designed puzzles that are much more complex than just running left to right. I quickly forgot my movement was "restricted" after the first chapter or so. However, at the end of the day this IS different than SMB and other traditional 2D platformers, which is important to acknowledge. Its a risk the devs took that I personally think was executed very well.------Casual------The game can be thoroughly enjoyed in under 10 hours or so for the main story. 20-30 hours more to complete everything else. Then the game is basically infinitely replayable thanks to its New Game+ feature and seed based level generation. Each play through will be different.The main story is great and a really enjoyable experience. The cutscenes are really well done and I found myself surprisingly invested.Typically after completing the main story, you'll enter the same gameplay loop that the original SMB uses, combined with the New Game+ feature. You'll replay levels to unlock extremely difficult dark levels. You'll find warpzones and collectibles hidden in various levels to unlock different characters, etc etc etc.The good:⁃ Level design: complex, difficult, and leverages the core autorunning mechanic very well. Levels are generated by using a very large pool of well designed "chunks" that are stitched together, rather than just random obstacles.⁃ Difficulty: the main story is challenging, but not excessively difficult for people who aren't experts at platformers. The extra content provides those sections of sadistic difficulty to provide a much greater challenge. Dark level collectibles will make you question your sanity.⁃ Variety: Light levels, dark levels, collectibles, EXCELLENT boss fights, and warp zones that will have you playing mini games in the style of famous retro games (f-zero, punch out, etc). Lots to do that all feels different from each other.⁃ Replayability: The large pool of "chunks", New Game+, and the seed based level generation means the game can be played many times and still provide a unique, solid experience each time. And theres a speedrun timer! (More on that later).The bad:⁃ Has a rough start in the first chapter in my opinion. Thats where the autorunning feels most jarring since you arent used to it, and since its a "tutorial" chapter the puzzles dont feel particularly interesting. After that the game gets very good, particularly in chapter 3 on.⁃ Unlockable characters are just skins for the most part, and dont introduce any interesting gameplay mechanics. This is a disappointing missed opportunity, especially if you liked the character variety that was present in the original SMB.------Speedrunning------This is where I've spent the majority of my time while playing this game, and I can't recommend the game enough for speedrunning.Any% is a very approachable length (you'll quickly be around 30 minutes, WR is under 20), with plenty of options for longer categories. Thanks to a spammable air dash, there is a ton of mechanical potential to push speed in ALL stages of the game. You can play fast.Theres two main ways to play: random seed and set seed.In random seed, each run will feel different and its extremely fun to build up your knowledge of all the chunks and their skips (some intended by the devs, some not). The routing is interesting and varies between runs. The randomness is low enough to not kill runs unless youre really pushing for top times, and instead mostly adds variety and excitement.Set seed is your traditional no-rng run, where everything is the same each time. This will force you to heavily optimize your movement through each level and implement the most difficult skips as you practice them.There is an active discord with a positive community, resources to learn from, and tooling thats been built (autosplitter, seed setter, etc). The game has a built in speedrun timer that ignores loads, so you dont have to worry about having a powerful PC to compete. The devs are supportive of the speedruns and pop in every so often to discuss the game or celebrate good runs.---8/10 casual experience, 10/10 speedrun.9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Super Meat Boy Forever is a procedurally-generated autorunner and probably not the game anybody wanted a sequel to Super Meat Boy to be. Though in fairness, I'd expect it would be hard to recapture the magic of the first one.While it  an autorunner, it is also a pretty damn good one that you can have a lot fun with if you fight the impulse to compare it against it's predecessor. Instead of being a ultra high-speed/precision platformer like the original this game converts the gameplay loop into a sequence of randomly pieced together puzzle sequences forcing the player to figure out where and how to change direction, boost, dash, and dive to get to your goal. Additional mechanics and are sprinkled into the game as you progress to keep things fresh as you go.The cutscenes include some fun references to gaming classics but for the most part don't add much of value; thankfully, they're all skippable. Other than that it's hard to find too much else to knock the game for.I would say this game is worth a try if you're looking for something to fill a quick 10-20 mins of gaming to kill a little time.

_childDocuments_.review: Super Meat Boy Forever is a better game than Super Meat Boy.Because it does more with less. Instead of having full control, now it is an autorunner. Jump button is still there, and dash down button is added. With this little twist it manages to create more ways to control the character and interact with the level than original could. Each of around thirty-ish levels introduces new mechanics, and they get combined in some rather clever ways. It has some improvement in all other aspects – visually it looks better and neater. I like music of SMB more, but this one is just okay. Backgrounds change between the levels – it still has nice touches like those, and some transitions are pure chef’s kiss. There is more story… if you were playing it for the plot. And the story is a natural continuation of previous game. I never liked bosses though, and they do not add much to the formula here either, they are more of a minigame to complete. Finally being able to punch regular enemies feels way more satisfying.Random generation makes sure things stay fresh on each new game mode. It is an interesting choice, as other games choose to dump all levels together for numbers. Here they are shuffled and you will see only a fraction of total. Still, it decided not to take a path of infinite runner and provide a more finite, better refined, experience. It chose quality over cheap mobile quantity, and deserves some respect for that.But is it a better Super Meat Boy game?SMB itself was a sequel to flash game, Meat Boy. Developers took their time, learned from mistakes and created an almost perfect platformer. At that time, game was a huge step up and showed that indie games could achieve things big ones could not. SMBF does not try to do that, it is not a revolutions by any means. But sure, it is a solid game and might be one of the best in the genre.It has all the meat boy DNA there – hard levels, quick restarts, references to other games, interesting game design decisions, shortcuts hidden inside levels, par times that unlock WAY harder versions of the level. But it is not platformer any more, and if that was the only thing that made SMB a solid game for you, then no, it is not a SMB. SMB achieved near perfection in its genre and there can be no sequel to it, just like there can be no sequel for chess.Speaking of chess… it is also a puzzle, sort of. Reacting fast is not enough, sometimes you will have to think how different game mechanics interact with each other. Given level editor, people would be able to make Super Mario ROM hack levels of difficulty easily. 20+ hours in the game I sill was discovering mechanics that the game had hidden from me, as some obstacles interacted in unexpected ways.The road to making the game was not easy – after being announced as SMB mobile port in 2014, game has been delayed numerous times. Finally it got released on PC, and became Epic Games exclusive for some time, and that caused a lot of backlash. But we have what we have now, and the wait is finally over. Making the game was not easy, and it was a time well spent – tons of creative levels with interesting mechanics. If you choose to ignore EGS exclusivity, consider the game being released just now. This one got too much hate for that, but now that wait’s over, I judge the product. And it is good. And will be.Forever.

_childDocuments_.review: Yet another prime example of what happens when the focus is on improving visuals at the expense of everything else. The ambition of making a procedurally generated auto-runner is not necessarily a bad thing, but this incarnation of it has issues. Levels feel like disjointed busywork, the auto scrolling nature leads to some VERY unnatural-feeling solutions to level segments, and it just feels pointless. But then take all of that in the context of it's predecessor -- which had tight, hand crafted levels with a natural flow -- and you have a recipe for a cautionary tale. Also, that first-stage music would have been irritating even if it hadn't been naturally contrasted with the original's soundtrack.

_childDocuments_.review: I had tons of fun with that game, it's a damn shame that it got poor reviews and ended up being hated by so many people. 3 main reasons why ppl hate this game is A) it was published on Epic games prior to Steam, B) it was primary made for mobiles, C) it is an auto-runner. It's easy to figure that A and B have nothing to do with the game itself. As for C - I was very confused at first but it took me an hour maybe to get used to the auto-running thing and few more hours later if felt absolutely natural.Some actual reasons why this game is very good:- TONS of content, every level is randomly constructed out of premade chunks and there are many-many chunks for EACH level in a game. And while some chunks are annoying for one or another reason most of them are wery well made. - level design is SO good. There is a huge amount of different mechanics and are used in many different and creative ways, levels never repeat themselves, you never get bored when playing.- game keeps the spirit of the original SMB. Characters are adorable, story is silly but enjoable. There are tons of references to old classics including some hidden mini-games.The only thing I did not like about this game is that in order to get 100% completion you must grind a lot to get 90 pacifiers (collectables). Reducing this amount to 60 or something would be much better. But other than that this game is fantastic.

_childDocuments_.review: As of writing this I've beaten 2/4 of the current worlds. As a huge fan of the original game, of which I learnt a lot of shortcuts, speedrun tactics, and tried to perfect my ability with re-running the first 6 worlds... I actually enjoy this game. It's not an official Super Meat Boy 2 or anything, and yes, it is a auto runner, but there is enough given to the player to feel agent in their ability. Jumping and sliding off walls still feels like the originals (smoother than the Newgrounds game), and it captures the essence of how Meat Boy feels to play. You're given a slide that acts as a kick and a way to control your momentum downwards in the air, and you're given a punch/kick that acts as a dash, and gives you the ability to control momentum sideways in the air. These two abilities, and your natural sliding-off-wall self, give the player more than enough control where the auto-running aspect takes a backseat mentally. After sometime I stopped thinking about it being an auto-runner, and was instead just enjoying myself. It helps that levels don't restart from the very beginning, and that checkpoints between levels are comparable to a usual Super Meat Boy stage. There are apparently 6000 custom designed levels, which is nuts compared to the 300+ of the original, but I agree with some other comments regarding most of these feeling less defined/unique. They still did a good job, and adding new mechanics like wood requiring a saw to break, or glass, purple guys that swallow you and you have to break out, timed needle sections, switches that change the level, and so on... It really adds to what would be otherwise a really generic platformer. Everything from the Xbox/Steam Super Meat Boy is still here. You have collectables, portals, dark world, multiple playable characters, animated reference cinematics, etc. The visuals are a lot cleaner than the original, embracing the more cartoon nature over the pixel art. The animations are cleaner as well. It feels more polished in general, but there is an odd problem I encountered. For some reason there is no "quit" button... I don't know if this was because it was made for the Nintendo Switch, which you usually rely on the main menu to quit out, but it's odd to have to rely on alt+f4 to quit a PC game. While it is not the sequel people have been waiting for, or a game developed by Edmund McMillen, it is still a good game, and with the free DLC coming out and a 50% sale right off the bat (I know it's because of the Epic deal, but it's still nice), I'd say it is worth it for anyone who enjoys Super Meat Boy or platformers - it definitely scratched my itch while I wait on a potential future where Super Meat Boy 2 exist.

_childDocuments_.review: Ignore the negative reviews. Rather than make the same game again, the developers went for something new and innovative. The result is much more memorable than yet-another-precision-platformer in a market that's now saturated with SMB's imitators. If you actually want more of the same, play The End is Nigh instead.The two-button controls don't stop them from designing difficult and clever levels with creative gimmicks, puzzles, and setpieces. The quality of levels are just as high as the previous game, and the quality of bosses is much higher.The main campaign is a bit shorter than the previous game, only 4-5 hours to reach and kill the final boss. But after that there's still A+/S ranks, dark world versions of each level, hidden collectibles, hidden levels, user levels, and the "meat grinder" mode (which has daily challenges and something I assume is endless mode). $20 is a bit much for the short campaign, but they frequently apply a huge sale discount to this game and it's definitely worth it at anything under $10.

_childDocuments_.review: No... Just no... This game wants to be a precision Platformer  a auto-runner which sucks because you can't be precise when you can't even control the characters movement.This game just fails at being enjoyable. It not bad because it's a auto runner or that it strayed from the original, It's bad because it needs the precision of the first meat boy without giving you any of the reaction time or controls to adjust. Half of the Chunks are not clear at all at what you need to do so you're left with trying to figure out what you need to do and all the while meat boy is repeatedly running into something that kills him, and sometimes after repeated attempts and finally passing it, it doesn't feel satisfying. In fact it just feels even worse because you won't know what you did to get pass and you don't get a moment to figure it out either cause you're already onto the next chunk trying to figure that one out. Getting A+ rank is even worse, if you can believe it, because you're not just trying to figure out which parts you can do better but also trying to speed up your running by punch spamming (in a P R E C I S I O N platformer) to try to help but even then it doesn't do much so you die because you spammed punch at the wrong time. over all this game is just bad... not in a fun way, not in a way that can be fixed with updates or with dlcs, it's just bad to the core.

_childDocuments_.review: RATING• Very bad: 0 / 10STEAM DECK• Runs perfectly POSITIVES• Graphics• Great cut scenes • Interesting mechanics• Has potentialNEGATIVES• Frustrating for the wrong reasons• Precision platformer with controllers failing often or game reactions not responding as they should (like dashes with different lenghts for no reason)• You do not control the character movement, it runs on its own which in turn makes it seem like a mobile game and creates unfair challenges without any learning curve• Stages are way too long with bad located respawn points. Be prepared to go through very challenging parts and then die to unexpected objects and have to do it all over again and again and again each time with a new surprise attack to kill you and make you respawn way back• Lots of bad designed sections with no learning curve. You have to do it again and again and again until it works. Not because you got better, but because things aligned. Since things are moving on their own, you will not have the time to learn. You die and repeat and respawn endlessly until stars align• Did you go through that difficult part and want to stop? Too bad, you either leave the game open or lose your progress. Terrible thing, especially on those long stages that never end...• Terrible soundtrack in stages. Repetitive and lame. I turn it off even before I start, that's how bad it is... which is very weird because the soundtrack in cut scenes is great...• There are many game breaking bugs on the Steam version of the game.POSSIBLE IMPROVEMENTS• Make auto run a game mode, not the main one• Better placed respawn spots• Save states from start menu that allow players to stop gaming mid-stage and return to the same place• Get a good team to re-work the whole in stages soundtrack, it's really badBUGS• Stage "A ONE C 99.99" from Dark World has a bug on Steam version that makes it almost impossible to finish, because you need 2 air punches, which should not be possible without an enemy or wall to punch. Eventually a glitch happens for no reason at all and you may be able to finish it after 1 hour or more trying... • Same bug happens on Steam stage "WINDOW TAPPING". • Other versions don't have these bugs, as you can check on walkthroughs online, because the sections are different than the Steam version where you have to keep playing until game glitches randomly and you manage to go through somehow. • There are probably many other stages with these bugs, but I'm uninstalling the game since it makes no sense to do the same thing for hours waiting for a random glitch to happen just to be able to 100% the game.CONCLUSIONThe original Super Meat Boy is one of my favorite games. This, however, is a mobile spin-off with lots to improve. The soundtrack in stages is really bad. And the game is frutrating for the wrong reasons with no learning curve... I am not going to recommend given all these flaws...this Steam version is a bug fest and a precision platformer with no precision controllers and full of glitches. DO NOT BUY!

_childDocuments_.review: Ignore the controversies and keep your mind open - Super Meat Boy Forever is a fantastic game, and improves upon the original Super Meat Boy in nearly every single aspect. The reaction to the release of SMBF is a perfect example of the fact that one of the worst parts of the gaming industry is, unfortunately, gamers.  Games are really, really hard and expensive to make. If you don’t have a multi-multi-million dollar marketing budget, and you don’t trim off every single sharp edge in your game and create a generic Ubisoft/EA game that appeals to the lowest common denominator, there’s a pretty good chance that the game you’ll make won’t make its development money back. Indie game devs are the ones that take the biggest risk, especially teams with more than a couple of mouths to feed. It’s no wonder that when a rare opportunity comes to secure money for development that many devs will go for it. I don’t intend to purchase a game on the Epic Games launcher in the near future (mostly out of the convenience that having all my games on Steam provides), but I have nothing necessarily against its existence, and I think that a new storefront (i.e. a new place to find customers) that gives a larger sales cut to devs (88% vs Steam’s 70%) AND gives a good chunk of change in return for 1 year platform exclusivity is a good thing. Clearly people didn’t react as negatively for Manifold Garden and Outer Wilds (both incredible games, would highly recommend btw), which were also mid-sized indie games that had an exclusive deal with Epic Games but are sitting at 95%+ positive reviews on Steam. Not sure where the double standard comes from. And I think the 50% launch discount (on an already fairly priced game) is a nice gesture. SMBF being an “autorunner” has been known since the game was announced nearly a decade ago. I think people using this label in a derogatory manner is similar to referring to a game like What Remains of Edith Finch as a “walking simulator”. SMBF is not Temple Run or Jetpack Joyride. It is very clearly on an entirely different level. The game is brimming with ideas and mechanics that are introduced essentially every level. As someone who’s spent 200+ hours on the original Super Meat Boy, I think I have a pretty good grasp on what made that game good. I also know that once you reach “mastery” in SMB, you’re holding the sprint button at almost all times, and are hardly changing directions anyhow unless you hit a wall and need to wall jump. Taking away the left and right buttons from you in SMBF, somewhat surprisingly to me at first, didn’t affect the feel of moment-to-moment gameplay that drastically. Add in the new dash/punch move, as well as all the new mechanics, and SMBF turns out to be far more dynamic and interesting than the original. The original SMB was great for its time, but in the year 2022 it’s a pretty basic platformer with somewhat wonky physics – easily outshone by the likes of Celeste. SMBF on the other hands feels fresh to me. I’m back to slamming my desk in frustration trying to get a tricky  pacifier, and feeling progress in my skill when I come back to a previous level and do it flawlessly. If a true Super Meat Boy 2 (and note that this game isn’t titled that – the devs aren’t tricking anyone) came out right now, I don’t see how it could hold up. If you’ve 106%ed the original, how could a new game with the same mechanics pose a challenge without alienating newcomers? If you really want something closer to Super Meat Boy 2 – just get The End is Nigh. It’s an excellent (one of my favorites) platformer that’s made by Edmund McMillen (one half of the original Team Meat). Now that I’ve gotten those out of the way, here are my brief feelings about the game.Other than music (admittedly I'm probably biased due to nostalgia), I think Super Meat Boy Forever improves in all areas that I can think of. The graphics are clean, and the cutscenes are incredible (the animation is fantastic, and the story and squirrel sub-plot were both funny and surprisingly emotional towards the ends). The bosses (which was probably the weakest part of the original SMB), are far more interesting and thought-out. The random generation, while prevents the memorability of levels, does make for smoother and more continuous gameplay, as well as makes it so that everyone plays a custom version of the game which I think is neat. As mentioned previously, the numerous gameplay mechanics keeps the experience fresh throughout. The effort behind warp zones is jaw-dropping – basically recreating classic NES titles but themed to Super Meat Boy and adding jokes/easter-eggs. The Punch Out!! mini-game referencing King Hippo from the original NES game I especially loved. Other than a couple key-bindings involving restarts not (currently) working, and the possibility of some occasional weird difficulty curves due to the random level generation (for some reason a chunk from one of the first levels in the second last area was far more difficult than any other part of the game for me), there really aren’t many issues that I have with the game. Definitely one of my favorite platformers of the last couple years. I hope when this initial wave of anger calms down, and people actually play the game, that Team Meat get the respect they deserve for the hard work they’ve been doing throughout the years. Making games is hard, especially one as well-designed and polished as Super Meat Boy Forever.
