_childDocuments_.name: Ooblets

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so goofy and fun.  The characters are so much fun, the sound design is incredible, and each little ooblet is adorable.  There's a lot to do in this game, and so many cute little critters to befriend.Unlike pokemon, you actually respect the ooblets, and instead of combat you have dance battles because ooblets love dancing.  I have so much fun with this, and it works great on the steam deck as well (which is super cozy).
_childDocuments_.name: Ooblets

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of my favorite games of all time!!! I love the art style and the dialogue and even catch myself dancing to the music. The game play is simple and easy to follow and does not feel like a get the quest, bring the item, now next quest, kind of game. You want to do the next task because it is always something fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Ooblets

_childDocuments_.review: Ooblets is a wonderful little experience where you get to collect cute friends. One of the best parts is they get to follow you around. It has a task system that makes sure you always have a goal to reach which makes it so the farming and gathering aspect doesn't get old. The goals are also actually attainable.
_childDocuments_.name: Ooblets

_childDocuments_.review: I already knew this game would grant me at least 10 - 20 hours of fun, but it really has become my cozy game of the year. The time management aspect becomes only as hectic as you allow it to be, making for a fast paced farming/townie sim or a relaxed "one thing at a time" animal crossing-esque game. There are loads of different categories of things to be collected (for progression and just for fun) and the challenges asked of you are never too daunting. I feel no rush to get to the end of this game ASAP and know I will be coming back to it to see different holidays and seasonal events for at least another year or two. It is extremely accessible for all levels of gamers, works great with controller, m+k and steam deck and watching a silly little ooblet dance never fails to brighten my day :) Highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Ooblets

_childDocuments_.review: I normally have a terrible time playing games that have a 'real time' management system where the in game passes based on the real world clock. It leaves me feeling stressed, which is counter to what the game usually wants to achieve. Ooblets has this time system, but the different tasks and milestones feel like things to look forward to rather than deadlines I have to meet! If you are like me and don't particularly like a clock counting down your in game day then I am happy to report this one is not at all overbearing or egregious like other examples.
_childDocuments_.name: Ooblets

_childDocuments_.review: Such a good balance of cute/cozy with your time and energy as a resource, but doesn't feel like as much of a time crunch as with many other games like it. This lets you explore more and takes some of the stress out that I often find myself feeling in games where the days pass faster. Also did I mention how CUTE it is?
_childDocuments_.name: Ooblets

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so much fun and I am so happy its finally on Steam!! I have been playing it on the Nintendo Switch for a while, but much prefer my Steam games, so I was over the moon when I heard it was coming to Steam and I just love playing it! The music is so fun, and has my SO playing along at times on his bass. The characters are so cute, and the gameplay is pretty easy as well. Its has a kind of Stardew Valley/Pokemon vibe and I am so here for it. Def recommend this game! Shout-Out to my bestie who introduced me to this addicting game LOL.
_childDocuments_.name: Ooblets

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the cutest games I've ever played. There's so much to do: upgrades, dance battles, cooking, monster cataloguing, socializing with the townspeople, unearthing a vast and mysterious conspiracy, etc. etc. etc. This game incorporates elements of Stardew, Animal Crossing, and Pokemon, but it has a unique flavor all its own. You can really see the heart that went into every little detail of this wonderfully silly world.
_childDocuments_.name: Ooblets

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game, it is very relaxing and fun to play. The soundtrack and sound effects are really entertaining and the characters and dialogue are really silly. There's dance battles as a deck builder creature catcher, as well as mini games, unlocking new areas, farming, and running your own store. Ooblets feels very finished for a game that came out not even 2 months ago but it still feels like there is plenty of room for expanding. The whole thing feels very adventure time esque.
_childDocuments_.name: Ooblets

_childDocuments_.review: I was in high school when the ooblets kick starter started. Instant hyped back then. After a few years I asked "what happened to ooblets?" so I went and googled it. Saw it was on Epic and bought it there. After the own your own shop update I put down ooblets for a while. Saw it finally release on steam and bought it again. There are only a few games I have bought on every console I own. But this is the first game I bought on 2 different launchers. I love the music. Amazing. Love the coziness. If I had to add a single gripe by force it would be the lack of difficult options. I like that the dance battles are easy, it adds to the cozy. But when I've built my team well it's embarrassing seeing the opposite ooblets at 0 points and I'm at 40 in a handful of turns. If you like farming sims, creature collecting, decorating, and like to 100% games this game is perfect and sprinkles a little perfect music and vibes to sew it all together. If your someone who is looking only into creature battles then I'd recommend watching some game play first.
_childDocuments_.name: Ooblets

_childDocuments_.review: Love my little oobies! It's so cute to see them dance battle and follow you around. I got a car for one of them and its just the best. Serotonin booster game for sure. The story was also pretty good, saving the little town from the big corporate baddies--love to see it. I am still playing even after completing the story though, because I need to collect all the oobs. I want more!!!!!!!!!!!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Ooblets

_childDocuments_.review: A fun game with lots to do.  IF you like gathering things, catching things and turn based "combat", you'll love this game.  The characters are fun and wacky, and the overall vibe is charming.  2 minor notes: time is wonky, I always either have too much or not enough energy per day;  and there are not enough late game achievements.  By the end of the story,  I had all of my badges, and it felt kind of draggy,  If you don't mind that, this is a fantastic way to spend your time.
_childDocuments_.name: Ooblets

_childDocuments_.review: This game is SO adorable and has a lot of unique qualities. I streamed this and other community members were loving the names and creativity that go on in this game. It's just different, but also super cute and cozy. I can't wait to progress in the game and hoping there's a Christmas event! The halloween event has been fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Ooblets

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game; it's fun, silly, cute, and overall just a vibe. I would play this game for 6 hrs at a time & not even realize how much time had passed. The achievements aren't too difficult to get either, aside from maybe a couple being a bit grindy, but I really didn't mind because I was just chilling playing the game post story line. If you're a cozy game fan or a farming sim fan, Ooblets is definitely worth looking into.
_childDocuments_.name: Ooblets

_childDocuments_.review: This was a gift from my boyfriend, and at the time I didn't know anything about it. How it's going: I play every day, and last Saturday I played for ten hours straight. Sometimes I forget to eat because of this game. The music goes so hard for no reason. I even made an Excel sheet of all the different Ooblets so I know what I need to get. I tell my real-life friends to play Ooblets. Ooblets has consumed my life. My boyfriend now kind of regrets getting it for me because it's all I want to do. Thank you so much creators of Ooblets.
_childDocuments_.name: Ooblets

_childDocuments_.review: I've been a devoted fan of Ooblets since its very first release on Xbox. This game has captivated me to the point that I intend to own it on every platform available. The stunning aesthetics, delightful dialogue, and wholesome gameplay make it an all-time favorite. I couldn't be happier with the chance to decorate my house, farm, and collect these adorable critters through dance battles.The overall experience is truly enjoyable, but there are a couple of minor setbacks. The regeneration time for certain materials, like Quibs, can be a bit frustrating. Additionally, obtaining some recipes after completing the storyline can be a tad difficult. It would be great to keep receiving recipe papers for all recipes instead of relying on the dance barn. Nevertheless, I highly recommend this game to any wholesome gaming enthusiast. It has helped me unwind and escape into a world filled with endless charm.It's a delightful experience that I wholeheartedly appreciate.
_childDocuments_.name: Ooblets

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game with plenty to keep you occupied for many, many hours.Everything about the game is first class, art style, dialogue and overall ambience, keeps me totally enthralled. A relaxing game with many laugh out loud moments, what could be better than that, highly recommended.I supported the team on Epic and watched the game evolve.Glad it is now on Steam. With such a great game, happy to pay twice.The minds of the developers must be a wonderful place, to envision such a game.
_childDocuments_.name: Ooblets

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game almost every evening and am now through the main quest. It is really cute and a good way to wind down. Would totally recommend to people, who like this kind of game and cutesy humor.I have two small complaints though. While PortVoran was a fun area with a lot of mini games, was the mountain rather tedious with the quests sending you up and down the mountain. It felt almost like a stupid joke after I won the mountain climbing badge in a dance off.And the second complaint (at the time of writing) is the lack of controler suport for the Reconstitooter. I could only access the menu with mouse and keyboard. I hope they fix that soon.Overall is the game fun though, with quirky characters and lovely weird ooblets.
_childDocuments_.name: Ooblets

_childDocuments_.review: Even if you aren't vaguely aware that there is a stupid Internet fight about this title with both sides accusing each other of being entitled, out of touch, snowflake monsters, you will immediately notice that whoever made this game is extremely pleased with themselves.It starts with the language. Just about every noun - proper or otherwise - has been been intentionally misspelled or changed to a diminutive or punny form of itself. Treats become "treabies." Fructose? "Froobtose." Watering can? "Dribbly Can." Hoe? "Dirt scraper." Coffee? "Beanjuice." I leave you to deduce what "fartichokes" are. It's like kawaii culture and Australian slang had a filthy, greasy pound session under a neon tarp in a vacant lot, and both were sober enough to know better. Your item list by the end of the game is such a confounding jumble of nerdy lunch table inside jokes that it's hard to keep pushing through.So, you may be inclined, if you are over the age of 20 and just a slight bit jaded, to view this joyful, goofy, carefree, psychedelic mess of a thing with the same wry, dissociative disposition as you would your sugared up grade school cousin. Fun to watch, but the check better cash soon.I think Ooblets largely delivered what it promised, if not how it promised. Publishing cat fight aside, the game is a unique mashup of the cozy farm and monster collection genre that is worth a look. The detailed animations, quirky characters, and small sprinkling of expectation subversion will occasionally inspire a half smirk.There are warts. Lots of polygon clipping between character costumes and the environment. The item management needs to be massively streamlined. Storage is far too expensive and takes up far too much room. The day/season cycle seems to be a strange mashup of sleep-to-save/end day cycle of Stardew and the real-time-is-real-time convention of Animal Crossing. You can't pass time without sleeping or napping, but you must be low on energy to nap or after a certain time of day to sleep. Seasons appear to follow the actual season of the year. I spent the entire game in Halloween.Pick it up on sale. Worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Ooblets

_childDocuments_.review: I love Ooblets. This game is peak coziness, it brings me comfort and joy.The designs, the story, the characters (Oobs and Ooblets alike).My only complaint- really I swear the only one- is that it's not multiplayer.But it's so many other things! Please consider, and give it 90 minutes at the very least, you need to grow into it.
_childDocuments_.name: Ooblets

_childDocuments_.review: The art style of this game on my recommended list is what initially drew me in, reminding me of similar minimalist/simplified style games I enjoyed this year. When I went through the recent reviews of this new release I kept seeing comments referring to some controversy with the devs. But I wanted to just play the game unbiased and here's my honest review of what my experience has been so far!- There is SO much to do, like all the time. I never feel like there's nothing I could be doing with my day in-game. - The Ooblets are so cute. I mean do I have to say it?? (yes, yes I do) They are adorable and there are  many to catch my GOD. The gleamy versions are actually kinda rare feeling too so that's cool. (I was afraid they wouldn't be)- Plenty of items to collect, hoarding items in games makes me happy and the game offers many a container for you to store them in. - The player shop is very fun to operate, there are many mini games in Ooblets which I appreciate. - Some sort of icon or something in our Almanac indicating which Ooblets you've already scanned/printed statues at the Lernery would be helpful. - a mini-map of any kind to toggle with 'm' would be super helpful. Especially for the later areas that are much larger. - More clothing/player customization! There aren't a lot of cute clothing options in the game. Some of the shoes clip through pants and some hats don't fit most of the hairstyles. Eyebrows I wish would match the hair color for example and a lighter skintone for us vampires? Maybe spend gummies to unlock special skin colors like lilac, green etc.?- Icon/something to indicate quantity of the furniture item you've clicked on to purchase. I've accidentally bought multiple of something I didn't need copies of a few times now.- Quick use function for the consumables on your hotbar? Unless there's a secret I don't know about I have to hit tab and click to use each consumable, making my hotbar useless unless I have a hankering item/tool there.Overall I love this game and I'm sure some things will be worked on in time, very happy with this so far though. It is pretty grindy but I'm the type of player that enjoys grinding. Happy gaming!
_childDocuments_.name: Ooblets

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely a cute game. certainly gives off vibes of Animal Crossing, Pokemon, and Stardew, all in one game.The music also reminds me of Here Comes Niko's OST. which is also a very cutesy game in nature. I have also heard this game is "Time consuming and Grind-y", but it really isn't. it's actually rather peaceful and slow. and it lets you grasp what's going on. the dialog also lets you take your time to read it as well.Another thing I'd like to add is that; the characters also tend to say some witty things, that feel a bit AI generated, but really aren't. and are surprisingly funny, I have gotten a chuckle out of some of the dialog while playing myself actually!Overall, I recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Ooblets

_childDocuments_.review: I adore Ooblets. I've had it on Switch since launch and I jumped at the chance to get it on Steam. It's so close to being a perfect game. If you like farming sims or monster-collecting game I would put Ooblets at the top of your list. It does start a tiny bit slow, give it a couple hours if you're unsure of whether to keep playing. Otherwise the pacing feels so good. This is one of those titles that I keep coming back to. I would love to see more complex card game mechanics and the choice to make the AI more challenging. I also LOVE the dialogue, it's so funny, but would like to see more of it, especially with the filler NPCs.
_childDocuments_.name: Ooblets

_childDocuments_.review: Saw this game on a Gab Smoulders play through, wasn't planning on purchasing it, but then finally did after the Halloween update  :) It's a super fun game. It's one of those games that you can play all day long or for short 1-2 in game day periods.Playing it on my laptop atm, but this game is seriously making me contemplate on getting a Steam Deck asap :) Would recommend this game to both young and old. The dance battles with cards aren't super difficult, so anyone can do it. Just get it <3
_childDocuments_.name: Ooblets

_childDocuments_.review: The ooblets are SO cute. You can pet them all, they follow you around and they can help you in your farm. The way this world acknowledges and treats these creatures is real cute too. It's chill and a very easy game, the stakes are never too high. Don't go in expecting anything profound.The dialogue could do better— I feel like every character in this game is all whimsical and ironic, but maybe too ironic? The way this game is chill and feel-good, the cast is awfully self-aware in a way that didn't land much to me. It may be funny at first, oh look how self aware this game is, but in the end it makes it harder for immersion.I personally do like that there isn't a romance mechanic! I like that there are shiny ooblets and they SHINE for real!I'm sad that the ooblets don't evolve :( That'd be so coolHaving completed the main quest I'd say: don't expect the perfect mix of all the games this one takes inspiration from. Those are big shoes to fill, and there's definitely room for improvement. But it's at least like 40 hours of gameplay that I'm very satisfied with, and will probably keep playing for a while (it's a good depression game)
_childDocuments_.name: Ooblets

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so cute! I waited for its release for years after I saw iHasCupquake play it on Youtube, and when I got the email that it was available and on sale I just couldn't resist. I love the art style of the game and the creative names for everything, it's one of the few games that has managed to put an actual smile on my face.
_childDocuments_.name: Ooblets

_childDocuments_.review: Steam's HOTTEST game right now is called OOBLETS! This game has everything! Collecting creatures, weird names for regular stuff, weird names for stuff that isn't anything at all, DANCE BATTLES? It even has Taffy, a weirdo character who I'm not sure if they are a mime or if that's the seasonal content. Can't wait to find out. I love you, Taffy!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Ooblets

_childDocuments_.review: Its just really really fun for all ages i first watched Claire Siobhan Play it three years ago and ive been waiting to Play it ever since I got my pc last year (i couldn't be bothered to make an epic games account my bad) Im only on day 16 so far but i really like the dynamics of the game and my little mushroom dude from mosssprouts is hella cute
_childDocuments_.name: Ooblets

_childDocuments_.review: This game is super cute and there is so much to do! But you can do it at your own pace and you don't need to stress. There is always something to collect, expand, upgrade, etc. The little ooblets are adorable. The music gets stuck in my head all day while I'm working and wishing I was playing this instead. I am in love!
_childDocuments_.name: Ooblets

_childDocuments_.review: I've been wanting this game for ages, and i bought it on Switch before deciding to wait for it to come out on Steam. I played on the Steam Deck and at 40 hours in, i just beat the main storyline but I'm still working on completing my almanac and finishing up some achievements. The farming is fun, and the game has a few irritating parts (tippy top mountain ergh) but I'm in love with this game and i look forward to continuing to play, even having completed the main story beats :)
_childDocuments_.name: Ooblets

_childDocuments_.review: No opinion on the whole feud. Just my opinion about the game only. You can tell devs worked hard on this game. There's a lot to do that, as a busybody, i love! You can also play at ur own pace to relax. At 10hrs in, there is still a lot to do and it seems the world ig is huge! SPOILERS AHEAD Lots of customization tho i wished there were more skin colors (lighter skin tones esp.) I really hope they come out with dlcs or expand the game so vets in the future don't run out of content. There's currently a halloween event for the next month and its super cool with all the disguises and store decorations around town. There's a whole lot of dancing with turn-based card play. You can dress up ur little oob pets and the rare ones are unique and sparkly. You get fun things from townspeople after friendship levels. It's simply adorable. I think this game can be enjoyable for those who like cozy gameplay, achievements, lots of customization/decor, adorable dancing, exploration, farming, and detailed friendship building, and perhaps a bit of strategy. I will see if i can update after more significant game completion. Thank you for your efforts, devs! A relaxing and destressful way to get my mind off what's going on in the real world. Keep it up :)
_childDocuments_.name: Ooblets

_childDocuments_.review: Despise the bad reviews regarding its release I think this is a fantastic game. Very addictive and entertaining. Perfect game if you like casual and relaxing farming sims, but not only limited to farming! To me the best part is the collecting side of it, the ooblets are adorable, and the overall feel of the game is exactly what I was looking for :)

_childDocuments_.review: Essentially a two-sentence summary: if you like the gameplay loop of , but sprinkle that in with turn-based dance battles to collect creechers, then yeah you'll like this game. Don't expect the same amount of content though.For anyone unfamiliar, ' main gameplay loop is essentially gathering & farming & doing your chores. Day in, day out, because your crops fuel all game systems. You need resources to get money, more seeds, get collectibles, get creatures, etc. You start out with nothing and slowly build up your Crop Empire. Each day you have a certain amount of energy to spend, which replenishes when you sleep. I ideally wouldn't have this bedtime thing at all, because that's the main feature that sends that anxiety spiking, but ah well.So, where do the ooblets come in? They make your farming life easier, and they also are essential in unlocking 'the rest of the world' and the quests for the light-hearted story. You seem to collect them at a pace similar to , so about a handful in a particular town- But you can unlock bonuses to add more creatures (besides other upgrades). You can also dress them up with accessories and pet them- And each ooblet has 3 colour variations with different rarities, if you're into that sort of thing.The story is very light-hearted and generic, which pushes you to go on errands to unlock feature x, buy thing y at the store, or go to place z. You might come across an accidental psyops note or whatever, but I personally don't give a ♥♥♥♥ as I'm just A Farmer Tending To My Animals & Crops. There's a particular approach to humour, so for example the 'yes' or 'okay' button is written as 'dunnit'. You know, like, 'done it', but written 'quirkily'? A lot of characters talk like that, with the pipsqueak noises akin to . Sometimes it's funny, other times unnecessary, mostly I just skip right past it to be honest. I do wish there was an accessibility option for particular wording to be written 'normally'. Why do.. Wires? Have to be called 'nurny'? Why are wooden planks 'planklets'? It'd be way easier if common language like that was written as such.Graphics and colours have a cozy feel to it, which I like in most cases. The only exception is anything to do with winter and mist, because in my experience, everything becomes one bright white blob of eyestrain. If there could be a setting to tweak brightness/contrast/turn off mist, that'd be appreciated. Currently, there's also weird flickering with the dance battle lights in Nullwhere, which makes doing anything there strenuous- Though I'm assuming that's a bug to be fixed in an upcoming patch, which is hopefully soon.At the end of the day  is a good game, I enjoy it!  wasn't my cup of tea, but I like creature collecting, even if it gets kinda overwhelming with all the crops, tasks, ♥♥♥♥ to buy, dance battles etc. hours in (that's on me though). I don't know if the devs plan on adding future content, but if they do then I'll sure be interested to see it!

_childDocuments_.review: 34.7 hours24/27 achievements(two of the remaining 3 achievements are less than 5 minutes progress from being completed. 100% on this game is just about as simple as beating it. then the last few cleanup should be almost done.)Rating: 8/10(advice section as spoiler at the bottom)Pros:Its an extremely cute and simplified mix of a life sim and a turn based pet battle game. Nothing ever feels like its going to be an uphill struggle just to get to the next step. Pet battles are pretty easy to understand, and the dance barn provides an amazing place to regularly train up your new oobs! (WITH REWARDS!) For a relaxing adventure with some surprisingly dark side plots. While they require reading WAY between the lines. Almost dark souls level. The game has a very creepy undertone, and i love it. Cons:The farm was.. okay? "Underutilized" if I had to pick a word. You can very easily beat this game without ever expanding your farm. (though late game does require a decent sum of nurnies and plankets, so if you dont plan on expanding, expect a decent slowdown. Lump sum supplies of wishes feel like they run out CRAZY fast. Really think about what you want to invest your wishies into before you go spending the fat stonks on the wishie well. MAIN story? immensely forgettable. I feel like this was not the main focus of the game whatsoever, but worth noting if that is something you are looking for. Because, I am too. hard to find life sims with genuinely good story lines. I never figured out how to make it snow in the game. If there is some sort of condition you have to meet before that weather event will happen. but It literally never snowed in my play through. And it did on my wife's twice. Advice for your run. I hope you enjoy this game half as much as I did. <3

_childDocuments_.review: I adore this game so much. This is the third time I've bought it actually! AND it's the best version I've played so far. The first release was great but the launcher gave me problems. The switch port was great but the loading times were soooo bad. But this one? This one is fast, loads quick, and I've yet to have a crash. Most stable version I've played so far tbh.As for the reason I bought it three separate times? Well. There's so much variety in how you can customize your team, your clothes, your farm, and your house. And you can accessorize your ooblets! There's so many little things I can do every in-game day, which is a good length and never feels punishing. Does it take a bit to get the ball rolling on progress? Of course! But that's actually a good thing, as it lets you really feel out your place in this world.The dance battles are the right level of challenging, and you can save by quitting to the main menu before one if you really want to retry. The mechanics developing over time and the various ooblets of the different regions having wildly different movesets really makes you have to strategize how best to face them, reworking what doesn't work and keeping what does. It's so easy to learn the more nuanced techniques, and once you get a good team going it's a real treat.Off to sink another 200+ hours into this game once again. Amazing job, Glumberland, and thanks for patching bugs so quickly!

_childDocuments_.review: Dance Battle monster collector with easy enough farming mechanics!TLDR; It's silly, fun, calming and easy. Slow to start and doesn't have deep mechanics you need to worry about mastering (from what I've experienced so far). OST is a banger. Managing Ooblets is pretty annoying, especially as a collector, you run out of space fast, and swapping them between your team, your farm and the Wildlands is cumbersome.Positives:I would consider farming games and card games an over saturated market in recent years for the indie scene. For me, a mixture of the great use of what feels like the entire color spectrum, silly and simplistic Ooblet designs, and NPCs that feel outright unnatural (which I am considering a good thing) while being sassy or quirky make this game stand out. I really enjoy that the NPCs are asshats along with their dry humor; everyone wears their personality on their sleeve, actively making fun of you or other NPCs or simply being the weirdest/quirkiest they can be. I would note that I usually hate quirkiness, as I don't find it very charming or cute, but the dry humor of the game offsets it that I still enjoy my time with that aspect. Possibly most importantly, the tracks in the game are absolute jams. I love getting into dance battles just to be able to hear all the songs often as I can, and I most certainly listen to the OST out and about. The dance battles themselves are fine! I don't really find myself having to think very hard about it; they're easy and simple, I usually just go into them using whatever ooblets are low level to get them leveled up. I've lost a couple dances, but nothing major.Negatives: What has frustrated me most so far is managing Ooblets.If I have a full 8 Ooblets following me you can always send one of your Ooblets home. What's obnoxious is that you can't simply call an Ooblet to your team from the menu. You have to physically find the one you want while it's wandering on your farm, among the rocks, branches, weeds, coops, stations and crops which can be very difficult based on their size, shapes or colors. It simply doesn't make sense to me that I can tell my Ooblet to head back to the farm from the menu, and they know exactly where to go, but I can't call the Ooblet back to me from the menu, ESPECIALLY if I am already on the farm.Transferring Ooblets between the Wildlands, farm and team is also pretty tedious and from what I've seen, you cannot get rid of an ooblet permanently in any way, so the list that gets sent to the Wildlands grows very long when you don't have space on the farm or simply don't want some, which makes organizing a horrible hastle.So in all, my only issue is with tedious design choices with managing Ooblets.

_childDocuments_.review: This game to me is essentially Pikmin trapped in Stardew Valley in the style of Adventure Time. At times the dialogue can feel a little 'hello fellow kids', but overall it's a really fun game. It checks all my boxes for addicting gameplay loop, the kind that makes me lose track of time because I hit the 'just one more day' mode and suddenly it's 4am. The graphics are cute, even if there aren't many character creation options (minimal hair/skin colors and no eye colors) and you forget how your character looks pretty quickly under all the clothes you buy or the customizations of the little critters you tame. The pacing is good and there's always something to do, so if you Liked Pikmin but thought it was way too stressful, this has the Pokemon grind but much more at your own pace. It even had Pokemon shinies, though they are supposed to appear at a higher rate. At almost 24 hours in I've only seen one, but that doesn't mean others hadn't spawned in areas I couldn't get to yet. Highly recommend because I'm having fun.

name: Papetura
detailed_description: CHECK OUT UPCOMING GAME About the Game Papetura is a handcrafted puzzle adventure game made entirely out of paper. Along with atmospheric music made by Floex, it creates a mysterious and unique paper world, shrouded in shadow and light. Features Unique point and click adventure experience, for about 2 hours. Everything is made out of paper, from tiny insects, strange creatures and monsters to truly magical locations, Atmospheric and beautiful music is made by Floex - Tomas Dvorak , Puzzles are a part of the story and the world, The story is told by animation and strange noises, there are no dialogues. The Story Papetura tells a story about lonely paper creature Pape , trapped in a flowery prison. One day Pape escapes and finds little Tura , a magical being that he’ll take care of. Together they will have to face dark and flaming monsters which will try to burn down their beloved paper world. The Team The team consists of the creator Tomasz Ostafin (Petums) , music artist Tomas Dvorak (Floex) , and sound designer Juraj Mravec . The game was being made for many years, inspired by old classic games like The Neverhood , Machinarium , movies of studio Ghibli , and fascination with architecture and paper sculptures.

_childDocuments_.review: Sadly, it's a beautiful and short experience, about 90 minutes with no replay value, but otherwise a very wholesome adventure game - on that note, I think the game missed a few opportunities to have optional achievements. The use of handcrafted scenery gives the games an unusual look that would be difficult to achieve with 3D graphics, I think it gives the experience more soul, same as it does with movies when people use the real thing. As good as it looks, the soundtrack is equally great, and not so much because I like the songs, it just has excellent timing when setting up the mood. I would say the puzzles were pretty good, creative but not difficult, with the exception of 2 puzzles that had some randomness to them. I really like the optional hint system, while it's a pretty common feature these days, I think the little mini-game made it very cute. I expected to have more issues with the hotspots due to the nature of the visuals, but it's not a very bloated game in that regard, there are only so many things that look interesting. The only nitpick I have is that sometimes your "gun" overlaps with hotspots, maybe it would help if you could toggle with an optional command.I will give the game credit for making me laugh so hard, the 'paddle' totally killed me, and there are a few other moments that were just as good. I assume those were real shadows with a light source behind the props, or are you using some engine effects as well? I mean in general, the game looks great, although I don't like the blur effect when you are too far away from the character, not sure if that was intentional. Also, I like that game tells a story with no dialogue, I think visual storytelling is very effective when done correctly. Personally, I wish you did a little bit more at the end to make the journey more wholesome, but overall, I enjoyed my playthrough.(+)  - using real props to make the levels, and presumably some light sources as well, just gives a really cool feel to the experience. Lovely soundtrack, the game has an immersive atmosphere because you timed the sounds and music so well. (+)  - I think the puzzles should be creative, not difficult, and I think this game does it very well (with the exception of maybe 2 puzzles). There are so many games that do it wrong and bash you over the head with sequencing, if you make another game, keep that mentality.(+)  - I always tell the devs to use more visuals and fewer words, you should never need a wall of text to explain what is going on on the screen. The game had many funny and heartwarming moments, I think you did a really good job keeping it simple.  - there were only 2 puzzles that I didn't like, the one with the fish because the targeting was off, and the one where you play pinball because you potentially forcing the player to do it several times. I consider it double-dipping when I have to interact with a sequence that I already solved, so I didn't even consider it to be a possibility until I used a hint. Whenever you make a linear game, it's beneficial to have some optional achievements that rely on doing something creative, maybe you could fish again and give it to another character, something like that. You could also mark some of the exits better, the one where you climb up and go down after a key comes to mind.I loved just about everything that this cute story had to offer, it was a beautiful experience, even though I probably will never come back to it. Yea it's very short and has no replay value, but you know, not every game needs to be complex - wait for a sale if 90 minutes is too short. I would recommend having some optional achievements in future projects, a few secrets can justify replaying the game.

_childDocuments_.review: is an abstract wordless point and click adventure told in a paper-sculpture world painstakingly made by the developer over many years. The quality of the finished game is incredible, even though it's short. I took my time with the game and spent under 2 hours finishing it, as the world is small and the puzzles fairly straight forward.But the most impressive thing about this game is the hard work that went into creating the world. You do not have to look at it for long before you start to appreciate just now much effort was spent making the smallest of details. See this video here from the developer's YouTube channel to showcase some of the processes and care that had to go into creating the sculptures:In classic point and click fashion, you will be guiding the main character through a series of puzzles in order to progress the story along. The puzzles found within this game are all fairly straight forward and progression is linear as well. Because of the relatively abstract nature of the characters found within and that the story is wordless, there's not a lot of plot development that tugs at the players' heartstrings, nevertheless, every moment spent while playing this game is very enjoyable, if nothing else, then just by looking at all of the fine details in the sets created for the game.One thing to note is that there are some tedious and slow-walking sections that if you are bothered by these, you might find the sections a bit lackluster. Another hugely important item to mention is that in the 2nd half of the game there are a couple of small timed sections. For people who have trouble clicking and maneuvering around on a timed restriction, this can be troublesome. This is just a caveat, as I have a friend who is struggling to complete the game due to this.You play with the mouse only.This game doesn't just have graphics, it has art, in full 3D solid form, as every aspect of the game was carefully designed and hand-built as paper sculptures to give it that very unique look and feel. The game is simply beautifully constructed, and I spent most of my time oggling at the stuff on the screen during my time spent so far.The music and sound effects are all done rather well. There are high points, low points, and everything in between. The sounds change depending on your interactions with the environment, and you will pretty much experience all of the music and sound effects because there is nothing optional here in this game.For people who want to ooh and aah at some really impressive artwork that took the developer years to build and for those who want to support a truly impressive feat in indie game design. The point and click game within is decent and short but is also not outstanding in anyway, with not very challenging puzzles and the timed element causing headaches to some. You will get all achievements playing the game just once, there's nothing hidden, so it's an easy 100% for those looking.The base price is $11.99/9,99€ and so the money:time ratio doesn't necessarily meet the requirements for a lot of people, but it is totally worth it. You are taking a bit of time to wander around the virtual museum of paper sculptures that were actually pieced together bit by bit, slowly, over years, by the developer to give this unique look and feel. It's truly a remarkable undertaking and the end result is something that we have never seen in a game before and may never see again. is dazzling in its artistic prowess, and is worthwhile to look at just for this alone. The little game that accompanies the artwork is a bonus, and serves to showcase every bit of this small paper-made museum. It is fairly easy and there are hints that you can use to give you some ideas if you feel stuck.I would recommend that anyone who is interested to at least wishlist and follow the game. I don't know if we will see a sequel or perhaps a parallel project because I cannot fathom the number of hours it must have taken just for the level designs. So enjoy this unique game design as it is truly refreshing.I do wish that the timed parts can be a bit more forgiving, as my friend is actually struggling to personally see to the end of this beautiful game, which is sad.Score: 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: A work of exceptional hand-made, which is quite capable of becoming for its author what Samorost once became for a well-known studio. It has exactly the advantages and disadvantages that you would expect from a game created by one person. The author's fully realized fantastic idea of creating a unique paper world inevitably coexists with the limited resources of one person, which leads to a short duration of the game (it took me about 2 clean hours). I have never regarded the length of the game as its decisive factor, I will not this time, much more important is the depth of immersion in the emotional layers of the world that the creators manage to achieve. The quirky inhabitants of these places amaze with their sophistication, and this applies not only to the two charming main characters, but also to the secondary creatures fleetingly encountered on the way. The world of the game pulsates softly on the player's temples, creating a light fabulous effect of the ephemerality of what is happening.The plot in the game is quite simple, although the villain turned out to be a rather standard "scary, almost shapeless black something, dreaming to destroy the world" character. He does not spoil the story, but he also does not say what causes any emotions (in contrast to the main characters, for whom you really worry throughout the entire time). The puzzles are good, even if one of them seemed somewhat illogical to me, most of them are tied to the physical properties of objects, which I really like. The only gameplay drawback can be called the rather slow walking of the protagonist, which greatly interferes with solving riddles in large locations. It is noticeable that the author very carefully approached the issue of connecting puzzles with the outside world, so that they do not look like something foreign, but are perceived naturally.These games are to be appreciated. The titanic work done on the material is visible from the very first seconds, forcing you to close your eyes to some imperfect things. This very cute and inspiring little game gives you the belief that the real enthusiasm for creating unique games is still alive. And that's great.

_childDocuments_.review: Sometimes you stumble upon projects that you can’t help but respect the dedication and effort put by their creators into it. Yet understand that the end result of all that dedication and effort is, while impressive, not very good. Papetura is one such example. Reminiscent of the impressive fluid clay animations of The Neverhood, except with paper. And except not exciting and not fun to play.Papetura is a point and click adventure game where most if not all visual elements of were handcrafted out of paper. And it does look impressive and very nicely put together visually. Especially when you consider that all of the game, but the sound and music, was done by one developer going by Petums. The sound design by Juraj Mravec is cute and the music by the legendary Tomáš Dvořák (Floex) is not his best, but very good nonetheless.But it’s a point and click adventure game first and foremost. And it’s not fun to play. Vast majority of the “puzzles” in the game are more or less tedious tasks, some involving repeating the same action over and over again, some just waiting a whole lot while nothing is happening. Some “puzzles” simply make no sense unless you check the hints system, because of really poor visual guide. And sometimes you stumble upon some random not obvious thing you can do, do it, because you think it’s some sort of cute bonus, and then realize that you’ve just solved a game critical “puzzle” that you had to do.Now, it’s not like the already mentioned The Neverhood was a great game – it had lots of poor gameplay sequences and puzzles. But what it also had was excitement, creativity, energy, fun. There’s none of that here. Papetura is “cute”. The story is simply present and is all style over substance, with no sense to this paper world. Scenes simply happen with no good pace or structure. And there’s nothing here that could define the game, even the cool idea with the main type of interaction of the game never feels like it’s used in any interesting way.It’s a shame, but I simply cannot recommend Papetura. I could understand if someone wishes buy the game just to support the impressive undertaking, but don’t expect to have fun with the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: Short and sweet can perfectly summarize my experience within Papetura. It proved to me once more, that we never truly grow up. There's a child at heart in most of us and they are yearning for the long lost innocence & simplicity regarding the joy of discovering new things daily. Unravel also made me feel like that and it's sharing the distinct features of cleverly using particular childhood themes and toy materials while conveying the storyline. Wool yarn is now replaced by titular paper mache. The lighting plays a crucial role as well. Being the developer / publisher's first Steam project, I am glad they focused on something original instead of trying to adapt the look or gameplay of similar point & click titles. Petums' debut is clearly a labour of love just when you realize how much time was spent on recreating those levels by hand before turning them into a digital format. Do not rush it, just stop and admire the inherent creativity of simple materials and ideas reaching the right hands and minds.Entirely abstract as it may be, Papetura's story is heart-warming and there could be some relatable themes in there, it's up to the players to interpret them. Definitely more than Good versus Evil, shining Light against the ever-consuming Darkness. Seeds and keys, are powerful symbols in their own right. You will not find it hard to connect with the abstract elements in Papetura since they do not contain any malignant undertones. Actions will speak lounder than words, since there's no dialogue whatsoever.With the puzzles being an integral part of the story, you can't judge them separately. They won't hold your hand, yet won't stress you either. The risk of failing has been taken out of the equation. All it takes is patience, really. It is strange not being able to label the game world but at least it allows players to make up their own mind in regards to character motivations. Adults overthink it too much, I'm sure the younger audience won't be bothered by the lack of context at any given point. Since there are no puns, innuendos or clearly depicted violence, I can safely assume that Papetura is a game for all ages.  Built with the help of the Unity Engine, no one will be able to complain about any usage of asset packs in Papetura since the entire project was likely first conceived on actual paper models before being adapted into the video game before us. Aforementioned paper mache mixed with origami-like elements that also employ shadows and light sources in a similar manner to LIMBO or INSIDE. Overall, the effects are perfectly animated, the motion is fluid and there wasn't a single instance of technical error I could notice. I do have a minor gripe with the game's permanent reliance on chromatic aberration, since I usually disable this option alongside motion blur as soon as booting up a title. It's still a small inconvenience and it didn't deter me from capturing as many screenshots as I wanted in Papetura.It dispenses with any HUD components and its set piece locations are quite elaborate. Beautiful even in that monochrome filter that's more akin to sepia. A flawless performance across the board.The sound department is suffering in silence, one might say. I didn't really mind the lack of voice acting or the discreet soundtrack in-sync with the various level sections you can explore at your own pace. Dialogue bubbles with images are a universal method of communication after all. Fits Papetura's themes just fine. Smooth instrumentals are pretty much the only subgenre that click here if you're looking for a custom soundtrack. The OST is being sold separately along with the game's artbook as a DLC pack.Linear level design with minimal backtracking. And just as advertised, it can probably be finished in under two hours, though I obviously took my time to examine every nook and cranny within Papetura. Be aware that there's no actual replay value in the form of collectible hunting or side quests. All the character interactions are crucial for moving the story forward. From certain fetch quests to puzzle sections or mini games involving the manipulation of the environment, they are playing out in a strict order which sadly, doesn't allow future revisiting unless you restart your entire playthrough. You can easily gain 100% of the game's Steam Achievements and that's precisely what I did.Even without any real risk of losing progress, there are plenty of checkpoints if for some reason you wish to take a break from this experience that's length-wise more cinematic that what poses for 2022 cinematography. Perhaps you will be compelled to replay the game at a later date, introduce it to someone else and so forth. It's never a finite story if it was memorable enough for you.All I can say next is how much I'd like to try out a sequel or something similar in terms of Papetura's visuals. Clearly there's a lot of hard work in manually designing such assets. I hope Petums will continue down this path of labour intensive originality. Steam and the independent gaming scene direly need more light-hearted adventures to counterbalance the daily downpour of one digital massacre after another. If the current pricing is out of your reach, wait for a Steam Sale. Be sure to pick Papetura at some point and allow it to share its tale. You won't regret it and might even encourage you to start your very own paper mache hobby.+ Beautiful art style.+ Relaxing gameplay.+ Steam Achievements.- No Steam Trading Cards.- No replay value.

_childDocuments_.review: Playing a game often means that you are trying to have fun, pushing your limit and most of time it needs a balance between difficulties, complexity of the system and, of course, be challenging enough for having a sense of accomplishment once you're done beating to pulp a monster hard to kill.This isn't what you'll find in that game. There is no challenges, only simple puzzles which can be solved with an infinite clues system you can use whenever you feel stuck. It remains fun to play as you dizcover the universe and think of how long it took to make this game happen.Sure, you can rush and glance around once every 10 minutes, probably feeling disappointed by your experience, but it would be your own fault for picking a game for the wrong reason.This game is a love song to the talent behind the scene, to the hours spent making this whole universe in paper. In each area, you can simply stay and enjoy what you're looking at, pondering how long it took to layer the background of this flower with so many inner petals. It is a piece of art gifted by a single man who worked tiredlessly on this beautiful game until delivering the result to us.So, here is my advice : Play this game as you would visit an art galery. Take the time to look around and to appreciate the work of the artist who made it. Maybe play a second time to see your favorite place or figure how were made those little cute fish. You wouldn't run in a museum, so don't rush it, enjoy the visit, that's how you'll manage to appreciate this game for what it is.For those who are curious and want to know more, don't forget to watch this little documentary called "Paper Magic", you'll see the game through the eyes of his creator as he carefully build it for 6 years :

_childDocuments_.review: Have you played Samorost, Machinaria, or any visuals-first point-and-clicker? This is that but missing a few things, and I don't mean just the color blue..Papetura is unremarkable in game design. Puzzles are intuitable, but there are plenty of irritating parts, like slow walking and backtracking, having puzzles in one room trigger something in other rooms without telling you, a couple puzzles require really superfluous clicks, there's a too-tight timing puzzle, and there are other niggling poor practices in click-adventure games. It is bad in story. There are few characters and none of them receive any characterization. There is a big monster that maybe threatens to blow up Paper Earth, but it isn't confronted. I won't spoil an 80 minute game much, but I will say it resolves limply and there is never tension, drive, or any character moments.It is remarkable in its cool paper design. It does often look awesome. The detail and texture are warm and fun. They should be why you buy the game. Using only these shades of amber and tan is an extraordinary choice and it is very cool to stick your face up against the screen and say "Whoa! That's so fuzzy and real!" The basic style is pretty thrilling and the lack of color and focus on shading make it seem very deep and architectural. It's an extremely unusual style and an incredible way to deliver a simple surreal aesthetic.The interesting narrative premise/twist (that the bad guy has fire in a world of paper!) isn't really explored in the art, story, or puzzles, which was surprising and disappointing. Sorry for that spoiler, but you should go into this expecting barely-linked puzzle rooms that are fun to look at, and not that kind of breadth or payoff.It wasn't exasperating to play but it wasn't engaging outside of the environmental art. For the 81 minutes it took me to beat, the most positive thing I have to say is that it looks neat. And it really does! I did buy it on big discount, and I would be furious if I bought this for $12. For $6, ehh.I look forward to seeing more stuff from this artist, though. Hopefully something with more depth to hook in to. This would be absolutely fantastic with any kind of complexity outside of the art. I love seeing this kind of art in video games and I think it's rad that people are making games that take these kinds of artistic chances. I also feel like it took me just as long to write this review as it did to complete Papetura, and I don't know which one I'll remember longer. I hope it's Papetura.

_childDocuments_.review: Papetura is a short game very reminiscent of Amanita's games. It manages to differentiate itself though by taking place in a gorgeous world made of paper based upon paper models. The game's soundtrack was composed by Floex who almost always works with Amanita and man, do his compositions utilizing strings, piano, and some soothing synth bring the atmosphere to life. Papetura is a story about a paper creature trying to stop a corrupt entity from burning down their little world of paper. The game's environments are wondrous, and despite the short run time they have a decent variety of interesting puzzles to occupy you with as you make your way through this brief adventure. Many puzzles make use of a projectile ball to move obstacles,  There's also a fun fishing minigame and a pacman-esque puzzle section. Another element of the game was the hint minigame where you had to reach all of the blue dots while avoiding the red enemies which got progressively harder over the course of the game. Finally the story had some heartwarming moments and managed to create relatively distinctive and unique characters without using voice acting and in a short period of time. All in all I would recommend this game on a sale if you are a fan of Amanita games for they have many similarities among their imaginative worlds, beautiful music, fun stories, and engaging puzzles.

_childDocuments_.review: A reluctant thumbs up. This is a  short,  derivative, and  tedious (for its length) point-and-click adventure. So, why thumbs up? Because of its superb soundtrack and soundwork by Tomáš Dvořák (Floex) and its pretty and wonderfully weird artwork (mostly hand-drawn). Basically, it's pretty. :) A superficial thumbs up.But first of all: play  only if you've played all the games from Amanita Design and don't have patience waiting for their next one. This is so obviously an "inspired by" game and copies almost every art and gameplay and even storytelling device they introduced. And of course Floex is on board. So it's easy to mistake this for one of their games. But ... it at best would be like a very early game from them, or even a mere demo of one their games.Sounds like harsh criticism? But so it goes: if you make a homage then you have to expect that you will be compared to your source, likely unfavorably.As pretty as it is, the gameplay is below mediocre. The puzzles are uninspiring (and there are very few; it's a super short game). They can also be quite obtuse. There is a pretty cool in-game hint system, but unfortunately once it actually made things worse for me and I had to look up a solution online. The character moves very, very slowly, which is annoying due to the large amount of backtracking (well, again, as a percentage of the game's short length).I hate to say this, but if you're a fan of Floex's music you might be better off just buying the soundtrack. (And if you do, please buy from him directly and not via Steam!)

_childDocuments_.review: A charming, short puzzle adventure made entirely out of paper. The monumental effort it took a single developer to make this game comes through the screen with lots of love and lots of style.You play as the tiny paper creature with a delightful frown waking up to find a menacing being stealing light from the paper world you inhabit. That’s not good – who wants to live in the dark? Paper is fragile as it is, so any unnecessary meddling with it could lead to catastrophic consequences, and you already caught a glimpse of… fire? This must be stopped. So off you go, on the journey through the strange leaves and branches, meeting all kinds of creatures on your way to save this paper universe. You won’t be alone in it, there is a mini companion strangely resembling tiny paper cat. Tiny paper cat. What other words could possibly make anyone play this game more than those three? Tiny paper cats have been known to draw players to games for centuries, but this practice has been long forgotten. Good thing it came back in full force here, so you can enjoy it in all its glory.There isn’t any verbal narration here, as the plot is moved by stylized visuals, and characters you meet along the way largely communicate with thought bubbles containing short animations. It does the job well, however, as aside the names of the heroes (which you can learn only from game’s description), the end goal of the level is almost always clear, and the overall story never gets confusing. It matches the style of the game – simple, smooth, and paper-magical.Puzzles are interesting enough to make you think for a bit (mostly due to having no descriptions of anything) and are built on environment manipulation along with physics-based layer. They are more of a relaxing category rather than challenging, which is the whole vibe of “Papetura”. Once you’ll get your companion (yes-yes, the tiny paper cat) – you’ll start using little guy pretty much as a multitool, which is quite amusing. He’ll serve as your inventory (by swallowing items), a mini-cannon by way of shooting what could be tiny paper hairballs, and generally will be used as anything from an oar to a plunger. It remains a mystery whether your buddy was ever thankful to have met you after all these shenanigans, but he kept on with the journey, and it’s probably better to be a temporary oar then to have the entire universe burned, so in the end he appeared to be determined (and masochistic) enough to keep being your friend. Didn’t you always wanted one of those friends you can use to unclog your pipe or hit another friend with if he got out of control? You get this dream to come true here.The strongest part of “Papetura” is, of course, the world and the graphic element. Just watching the video of making the game – gluing a bajillion little pieces of paper together, wiring tiny lights, filming them and coding everything into a game – can make anyone feel like the most unproductive human being on the planet. The sheer effort put into creating this universe is astounding and deserves accolades in itself, but the fact that the result turned out to be simply magical requires some kind of alien award. Gentle paper flowers with flickering lights, strange, delightfully animated paper creatures, paper houses and paper bars (you heard that right) and even paper underwater – the entire universe is covered in lights and shadows and textures and miniature details and is simply magnificent. Many a word can be said about the visual part of this game but playing it and seeing the brilliance of hard work and talent behind this creation is the absolute best way to give it its due; it is a truly unique concept realized to the best possible degree.With the absence of voice-over, characters communicate with a myriad of sounds ranging from something that sounds like gurgling on helium balloon to spooky “aargh” of a bad guy, and they support thought bubbles that serve as dialogues. Another myriad of well-made sound effects (mostly, of course, of paper variety) will be helping the immersion. And the soundscape matches the visual part adding that extra oomph “Papetura” never really needed, since it’s pure oomph in itself already. Ambient sounds reminiscent of soft techno/trance take the overall atmosphere up, up, up. They change with the story or location, staying within chosen style yet reflecting different moods, environments or even danger or happiness with a stylish subtle variation fitting paper universe to a T. Despite being only 2.5 hours long, “Papetura” manages to unfold a complete story taking place in a wholesome unique world. Tremendous energy that went into making it pays off with stunning paper world containing relaxing, charming puzzles that meant to calm and entertain. Lovely inhabitants fighting to save their universe will undoubtedly make you smile and say “awwww…” every few minutes. Playing through it is a very soothing, magical experience that wasn’t meant to blow minds but rather make you feel warm and fuzzy and bring about some lightheartedness. Also, remember how there was a tiny paper cat? You thought that was the most compelling thing about the game? Well. The best is always saved for last. There are tiny paper dolphins taking shots here. I’ll see myself out now.

_childDocuments_.review: - Quick confession: I have a terrible eye candy addiction. If a visually interesting game manages to earn even a room temperature critical reception, it will wind up on my Steam wishlist and eventually in my library once it gets bundled or put on a deep sale- Papetura was certainly one of those games for me. Just take a look at some screenshots. Hell, if you don't mind sparing 5 minutes, look up the "making of" video on YouTube. You'll see the amazing papercraft, origami, and papier mâché world that took its artist 6 years to put together. It's a truly impressive artpiece, and getting to explore all the hard work is truly a unique experience- If you appreciate attention to detail in visual design, it's hard to think of a game that checks that box as emphatically as this one. Every crease, fold, and wrinkle was carefully added by a single extremely talented artist. And even though things like lighting were touched up in Unity, much of the background and ambient lighting is actually real. It's just not something you get to see in most games- Being an artsy puzzle platformer, you already know that the soundtrack is a moody mix of piano, strings, and synth. It's a pleasant enough collection of tracks, but none of them stand out enough to serve as a highlight. Serviceable, but forgettable- Being a bite-sized experience, Papetura's narrative doesn't have much time or space to develop. You start off as Pape, a small scrap of paper that's been imprisoned for reasons that aren't ever explained. I'll choose to believe it's something benign like drug possession or tax evasion and not something sinister like murder or a series of DWIs- The plot kicks off not long after you manage to escape. A flaming monster suddenly appears, threatening to burn down the paper world. In the chaos surrounding its grand entrance, you wind up rescuing a small cat-shaped creature Tura. Together, you'll attempt to prevent your entire civilization from being turned into a pile of ashes- The vibes are moody, yet magical. Sure, the story is pretty dire and the visuals are quite moody and monotone owing the dimly lit paper setting, but it's hard to not just be constantly in awe of the fact that you're playing your way through an artpiece- In terms of moment-to-moment gameplay, Papetura isn't going to show you anything unique. It's a side-scrolling puzzle platformer without difficult puzzles or challenging platforming. You mostly just utilize Tura's ability to fire projectiles from his mouth to solve physics-based puzzles. Think of Limbo, but with much simpler puzzles and a much less depressing tone- There aren't any clever mechanics or gimmicks to play with here, so there's nothing at all to distinguish Papetura from any other puzzle platformer you may have tried in the past. It's a shame, too. As impressed as I am that the game (including the gorgeous handmade setting) was made by a single person, I feel like a collaborator or two could have helped develop and enhance the gameplay- You don't actually need a gamepad to play this game; Papetura permits point-and-click movement, allowing you to complete it using only a mouse. This proves to be a double-edged sword. On one hand, it allows you to beat the game on virtually any platform (even mobile). On the other, Pape shuffles around the screen at a glacial pace- Given that I 100%ed the game, I don't really feel the need to revisit it any time soon. I may look up screenshots from time to time, though. Despite not being much fun to play, it's quite memorable- This is sort of a hard game to score. In terms of presentation, it's one of the most unique games I've ever played. The only other title that I can think of that took place within a self-contained physical medium like this is The Neverhood, an old point-and-click that I wish was on Steam but is at least available if you know where to look and have an environment that can emulate Windows '95. In terms of gameplay, though, Papetura is overwhelmingly mediocre, if not kinda bad. Not awful, but merely bad- It ran well on the Steam Deck and played fine with the gamepad controls, but I highly encourage putting this on as large of a display as you can. Make it easier to appreciate all that visual splendor . Looks aren't everything, but they aren't nothing either. In this case, they're just enough to elicit a tepid recommendation if you want to spend 1-2 hours experiencing a beautiful and fairly novel setting

_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: Very sweet and short Point & Click adventure. The story is pretty okay, the riddles are quite simple but still entertaining and the soundtrack fits perfectly. _childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: Visually amazing and beatifully crafted game by polish architect and solo game developer Tomasz Ostafin, which took seven years to finish. Before this little research I was sure that the project was made by some of the guys from Amanita Design, who founded their own studio. In addition, the soundtrack was made by Floex. But now I think Papetura is a little bit more surreal, strange (in a good way) and a little bit darker maybe than Amanita`s games. It somehow reminds me of the film adaptation of Neil Gaiman`s Mirror mask (2005), which I really love, and also of these hand made decorations for old expressionist movies like The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari. In such projects you just don`t care about game design flaws if there are any. This is an animational piece of art which definitely deserves acknowledgement. This game is for aesthetic pleasure.
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: Probably best to think of Papetura as an interactive children's art book over a video game. It's beautiful in both art and music and for that alone is worth a playthrough, but the "game" portion lacks a bit. Puzzles can be kind of confusing and thankfully there's a clue mini-game to help move you along, but there are parts where that doesn't help much. This game is not for everyone, but for those that love point and click, artsy-fartsy style games with great music, this is definitely worth a purchase.
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, the game was made by one man from a little Polish studio and, as if that was not enough, just look at the craftsmanship emanating form each scene - to made something like that by hand and then bring it to life with animation, gorgeous music by Floex and play of lights... Hats off. I think a lot of inspiration was drawn from Czech studio Amanita and games like Botinicula (which I absolutely adore), although Papetura is lacking some of the Amanita's diversity in terms of enviroments or puzzles, it makes up for it with its unique atmosphere and palette where brown, orange and gray are  the dominant colors. I mean, after all it's all paper, right? Whole scenery is oniric, mesmerizing and makes you wonder what else there is to discover in this peculiar paper world. The puzzles are not too hard but in case you're stuck, just eat a suspicious looking ball - it will make you  a bubble with the prophecy (yeah, I'm serious) and after a quick mini game, you will get your answer. I only wish some animations were a bit more fluid, and that the game itself was longer (it takes around 2h to finish). The story could also be a little more complex, but there is a certain beauty in its simplicity. Beside that, just grab this game and spend a magical evening with it. <3 Btw, did you know that 'paper' in Polish language is 'papier'? Well, now you know. :)
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: Papetura is a lovely but simple game based on a sequence of simple puzzles, each in a slightly different atmospherically lit location. The game is short (it's not a flaw) and took me 75 minutes, while the producer claims it takes about 2 hours. In my opinion this is slightly exaggerated. At the very end the game tells a nice story, at some moments even touching, and is definitely worth getting familiar with.
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: A visually and aurally beautiful game, made out of paper! Aesthetically and tempo-wise, it reminded me of 90's games like The Neverhood and Down In The Dumps, which also leads me to the game's criticism.It's pacing was quite slow, to the extent of testing my patience sooner than I hoped. This resulted in feelings of annoyance while trying to solve puzzles, which often were also slow, vague and made no sense until I repetitively/incidentally figured them out. These two elements, of pacing and annoyance, repeat themselves throughout this short game (it has only 5 or 6 levels), which makes the game sluggishly last a little longer.I was relieved finishing the game, to feel it's done and I could move on, which I haven't often felt with (adventure) games. Papetura has all the elements wonderfully in place, but somehow doesn't quite hit the right frequency as a whole, along the way.
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: To begin with the positives: Stunning visuals. The effort put into it shows itself in every moment of the game. This game feels more like something that should be in an art exhibition rather than Steam. That statement can be both interpreted as a good and a bad thing,
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: Can prolly be completed in under 2 hours, but don't let that put you off. There's loads more than 2 or 3 hours of visuals to take in/wonder.I bought it during Summer 2022 sale for a discount and I'm completely thrilled with the game.  The art is stunning, the story is endearing, the puzzles are fun and funny: I laughed out loud with the solutions for a couple.  This is all mouse/point'n'click, and as in the game description, there are no human languages involved.Things I liked/loved:  1.) The artwork, a pure feast for the eyes.2.) Solutions that reliably follow rules of classical physics without dishing out pain for fails (I enjoy permadeath as much as anyone, but it's also nice to get unqualified do-overs)3.) Biological referents via an aesthetic...  for which I have no words.  I was not expecting physiology fun when I purchased this, and I was delighted.4.) Tea pot.  I love tea.Things I'd change:1.) The protagonist could be less grumpy over totie wee difficulties that arise.2.) I have mixed feelings about the ending, as technically, it violates scientific facts we were relying upon, earlier: Do I have an ideal alternative ending?  No.  Definitely, I do not.  And I was very happy with the final outcome despite "mixed feelings."  My brain tells me:  'tis but a fairy tale, afterall, as the smile spreads across my face. 10/10  Will play again, just to look at the art, but also to engage with the various characters. _childDocuments_.review: This game desperately wants to be something like what you expect from Amanita Design: unorthodox looks, non-verbal storytelling, slightly art house vibes. But Papetura is just incapable of reaching the level of Machinarium or Botanicula. The visual design is absolutely stunning (and I hate to give a negative review to the game that gave me such esthetic pleasure) but it remains more or less the same throughout all 1,5 of gameplay. And yes, it is the second big problem with it - it awfully, tragically short. Also, horribly, inexcusably  slow. The character and creatures design is Ok, but none of them truly stand out, they are just too bleak, I just couldn't get myself to like their story like it always happened with lil' robots and lil' plants/insects from Amanita.Papetura seemed exactly my type of game, but in the end I just loved the looks of some areas.
