_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: There is simple and then there is boring. Papetura is a beautiful, but unfortunately boring experience. It is an artpiece for sure, the time and effort put into the visuals clearly show throughout and this is without a doubt the highlight of this release. I wouldn't personally call this a game though, it's an interactive story book that reads slowly, tediously and confusingly.The StoryThe story is said to be told through the visuals and graphics with no dialogue, however I personally struggled to come away from the experience with any meaningful message. And for a game that focuses so heavily on the story and so little on the gameplay, it effectively reduced the entire experience to what felt like a wasted 100 minutes. I felt no connection to the characters, I was confused as to who the antagonist was and without reading the description of the game listed on Steam, I would have had no idea what my objective really was. This game tells you the story, there is no effort on the player's part to piece things together and interact with the world, which on its own wouldn't be so bad, but this game relies on story and it didn't do anything for me.The Graphics and AudioBy far the highlight of the entire game is the graphics. It is amazing to think that all the visuals done in this game are handmade paper sculptures and it is a treat for the eyes, however from a gameplay perspective, this style sort of shoots itself in the foot. The lack of colour makes the world feel really flat and boring after taking it in for the first half an hour or so; it's either warm oranges or grayscale. This self-imposed limitation also hurts gameplay by making it harder to give visual aids to the player, which in a point-and-click title is one of the most essential things to get right. It's a shame, because it is something I really want to love, the artwork in the book for the game looks great as well, but I'm reviewing this as a game and the artwork for me felt quite repetitive and dull after about an hour, I wish there were more intervals were it was spiced up a bit. On another note, I felt the lack of colour and the flatness made it really hard to discern what I was actually looking at, the weird creatures are good concepts on their own, but when placed into this environment everything blends together and as a player who has never seen these creatures and weird objects before, I have no clue what I'm looking at. On it's own as an artpiece, this is fine, - as a puzzle game, this causes problems. I need to know what I'm looking at so I can apply it to different puzzles and situations. I have finished the game and I still don't know what a lot of the things I was looking at were supposed to be or represent. I haven't got much to say on the soundtrack to be honest, it was quite forgettable. It wasn't bad it just did it's job as background music but there's nothing of interest worth mentioning.The GameplayThis is where everything falls apart for me. A game can have stunning visuals, an amazing soundtrack and an incredible story, but if the gameplay doesn't work, then the whole concept doesn't work. As a game, this plays horribly, it pains me to say. For the most part, you will be watching your character move at a snails pace across the screen to get to some object or door, at so many points I was ready to stop playing due to boredom because of how long the character took to move to one area. It almost feels like the character was made to be slow as to pad out the gameplay time, because of how little substance there is. The pacing of the game is incredibly bad all round, from cutscenes interrupting the flow of the gameplay, to the slow movement and clunky interaction with the surroundings, this game does not flow well and I found myself bored and frustrated at how long it was taking to do a simple task.The puzzles themselves are mediocre, but to be fair to Papetura, there are a select few interesting moments. A lot of the time though, your interaction with the environment feels clumsy and you feel like you have to rely on the hints system. In puzzle games, hints should be the back-up option when you can't figure out the puzzle, not the go-to. A typical puzzle will go like this: after exhausting all your options, you go to the hints system and it turns out the thing you already tried was the right answer, but due to the poor visual aids and the game not teaching you how you are able to interact with the world, you discover you can do something you didn't know you could. And not just that, at other points, there are areas you can actually access, but due to the flat colouring and poor visual aids, it doesn't look like you can, and again you have to rely on the hint system to tell you that. Some puzzles are just plain boring and tedious, it didn't feel like I solved anything when playing this game and I felt like I was no closer to any objective.To sum up, this isn't what I'd call a game, its an interactive artpiece. If you do buy this, don't expect a fun gameplay experience and at nearly £10, I'd say it's not worth your money or time. It hurts to be so harsh on this when it clearly took so much effort and time, but as a game, I don't think it is very good. I would say though if you aren't really into games, you might just like this title, but for the majority of people who already play games and expect a fun and exciting experience, I suggest you look elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like games like Machinarium or Lumino City, you'll probably also enjoy this one. With about 1 to 1.5 hours of playtime, it won't be the most extensive gaming experience out there - but to me, every minute was worth it. I think the price is absolutely fair, considering the amount of love and dedication that must have gone into creating this game.The visuals are pure art and absolutely stunning. The initially bland white of the paper material is atmospherically staged by masterful use of shadows and coloured lighting. Phenomenal to look at. There is no text and no speech, only icons/pictograms and noises, similar to Machinarium and other games of this sort.The gameplay is mostly relaxed, there are only a few short sequences with a little more time- or agility-critical action, but none of them are unfair or unmanageable. That said, I was thankful that guides for this game are available on Steam, because not every situation explained itself to me immediately. But with a little nudge here and there, the puzzles all felt quite logical. Best of all - NO SLIDE PUZZLES! :)There is no save function, only a load function, the game seems to auto-save at certain points. I got a very nasty shock when I thought "this must be near the end, let's save" and I pressed the icon next to the load icon, only to find myself back at the title screen, expected to start over from the very beginning. Luckily, the load function let me restart from a point just a few seconds before I tried to "save" the game, but still. I feel that a little text to make the menu items more comprehensible wouldn't have undermined the nature of the game. ;)

_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: The fascinating paper-based art direction in its monochromatic splendor and expressive lighting doesn't have any comparable peers. The amount of dedication and craftmanship is beyond evident. It's only too bad we don't spend enough time here to get a true feel for this place and its inhabitants.Reminiscent of Samorost 3 and Machinarium in terms of gameplay and how hand-drawn thought bubbles are presented, even the vague story or character expressions are an offshoot of these two classics. Its puzzles are about similar in style, though much shortened in scope. The main character will handle another creature to throw mosquitos or other objects, bringing an original puzzle solving mechanic to the genre.The always excellent Floex provides music, another nod to the obvious Amanita inspiration, supported by excellent sound design.Two distinct and perfectly adapted interfaces support KBM or controllers, unexpectedly plays best with a gamepad.Hints are available on every main screen. Simply gobble up items in the mini game to reveal a small animation, which helped in many cases get to a solution faster.Definitely worth discovering once, perhaps not engaging enough to kindle a second stroll.

_childDocuments_.review: Took me all of 10 minutes to hate this game. Hate is a strong word, but still. You get dropped into a world with zero instructions; no menus, no pause button, nothing. You have to randomly click on everything around (literally EVERYTHING) until you figure out the game dynamics and character movement; the movement is also very slow as far as speed goes. I felt like I was back in the 90s playing Mist. I wanted to play a nice relaxing game, not get stressed out because nothing makes sense. Additionally I do recognize my bias here, as I am a gamer that hates relying on walk-throughs or guides to play, and this game absolutely needs a guide.
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really beautiful game-for-art. I don't think I have ever seen a game rendered this way, and especially not to such impeccable craftsmanship and lighting quality. Each scene really does work well and is striking and immersive.My issues are 1. the runtime and 2. the gameplay. It took me 1hr 15mins to finish the game entirely, and that was with dallying sometimes. The issue I have with the gameplay is that the game can easily feel tedious as it tries to pad out it's runtime by making the game more tedious than it needs to be (you walk like animated molasses, etc). It's not unplayable, but if I were in the mood to , I would turn this off in less than 10 minutes.The story was sweet, though nothing even close to novel or worthwhile on it's own; the puzzles were fine. Just fine. For the price of $12, I can't say I'm satisfied. Its a shame since there is obviously a lot of love that went into this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: The good- Gorgeous aesthetics and artistic approach. The monochromatic world made of real paper models is unique and surreal. Warm lighting is atmospheric too.- Cute, well designed characters. You'll forget them soon though.- Some cool gameplay mechanics and well implemented physics when the balls that you throw interact with the surroundings.- Animations are a bit slow, but also smooth and pleasant.- Great, calm, atmospheric music.- Funny creatures' sounds.- Cool hint system that involves a mini game.The bad- Puzzles are a little bit childish and their structure doesn't follow a logical turn of events. You solve them almost by intuition. You don't have exactly a purpose based on a story. You do things without knowing what's gonna happen next, just because they're there. - Very abstract story. In fact I don't think that there is much though behind it. It's just a surreal situation full of biblical type of symbolisms that just tries to create an eerie, mysterious atmosphere without having anything to say.- Movement and actions are annoyingly slow.- Too small. It's like you just played the prologue of something bigger.- Pricey for what it offers.

The world reminds me of what I would think the inside of a paper wasp nest looks like. You play a little paper curl man, on a quest to stop this ominous dark creature from apparently trying to set your home on fire, with the help of this little cat-like creature. _childDocuments_.review: A beautifully crafted point-and-click game reminiscent of Amanita games, with music by Floex.Papetura's visuals are unique. Backgrounds and characters have all been handmade and cutout of paper and card and then brought into the game. The amount of time and effort that must have gone into designing this game is impressive and works to great effect. Backgrounds and scenes look fantastical and real at the same time, making the visuals for Papetura stand out amongst similar titles. The music by Floex is of course always amazing and lends a lighter tone throughout our character's journey.This game is short. On the home page there is a mention of a 2 hour play time, I myself finished the game in around and hour and a half. But don't let that put you off as the journey is well worth your time. _childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game in the Christmas sale, which made it a no brainer for 2 hours of entertainment for a few quid. I'm recommending this game based on that price. The concept of how it was made enticed me and I liked the idea of supporting an artist. Papetura is not so much of a game, rather than a chance to explore someone's hand crafted paper scenes. I would put it in the category of relaxing, stress free, indie games. I personally didn't find the graphics to be anything spectacular, given that it was handcrafted, I had expected that aspect to be brought out more and taken advantage of to differentiate it from other games, but to me the graphics didn't look that different to computer generated textures (for instance like in Little Big Planet). In other words, if I hadn't know from the trailer that it was handcrafted, it wouldn't have been able to tell from playing it. And it seems to be entirely beige!I wouldn't recommend this game at full price for a few hours of clicking (there are only a few puzzles which aren't taxing at all and are very linear). Better puzzles and further depth to the environment (scenery and items being revealed based on actions etc) could have made this quite captivating.
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

But if we consider all the hard work that the dev spent on literally hand-crafting every little thing in the entire world, this game's "value" would far exceed its "price".  I would consider Papetura as an interactive art piece instead of a game with interesting gameplay. If you also appreciate the beauty of its handcrafted world, you should definitely give it a shot, and not rush to finish the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: This is a yes and no recommendation.  If you are a fan of point and click games then definitely get this title.  The visuals and sounds are great and the hint system gives you subtle hints to help you along with no hand holding involved.If this is to be your first attempt at a point and click game then I would advise against this title.  It is slow and can be a bit tedious at times.  Some puzzles take a bit of trial and error to achieve even with the hints given.
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: Quick:3/5.  A sight to behold, Papetura is a visually appealing point-and-click game with a novel art style.  As its name suggests, the game is designed presumably by taking photos and videos of paper characters and backgrounds, that I believe were modeled by hand.  The art style is phenomenal.  It has a great soundtrack, and pretty decent game-play.  I recommend that you play this game if you are looking for a very short, and unique point-and-click game. More:Papetura is very pleasing to look at.  I have never played a game with this type of visual aesthetic.  If nothing else, the appearance of Papetura will keep you interested throughout your experience.  There is a slight orange / sepia hue to the game that is very relaxing and easy on the eyes.  Though great to behold, you probably won't be wowed by anything in this game.  I can't remember being excited or overwhelmed at any time, however I did feel good while playing it.The main character appears to be a sheet of paper.  You take control of them, and set out on an adventure through a strange, and flammable world.  There are many puzzles that you will have to solve, some a little more obscure than others.  You will eventually find your way if you persist.  I was stuck perhaps once during my play-through, but I did not have to look up a guide to progress.  I enjoyed the music a lot while playing this game.  There are no tracks that stick out in my mind, now, yet I remember thinking that the audio was great while playing it.  All of the music in this game was immediately copyright struck in any video that I tried to upload or stream... so if you plan on making a YouTube or Twitch video of this game... just be aware of that.  I do not fault the developers or composers for this, because the music is that good and unique, in my opinion.Character designs are very fun, and you may even learn to love some of these critters during your short romp through this paper world.  Yes, the game is short.  It took me 98 minutes to play through this game from start to finish.  I have the impression that it could be finished in an hour if you already know what you're doing, though.Overall, I do recommend this game.  I have never played anything quite like it, and I greatly appreciated how different it was.  In the future, I hope that these developers make another game just like it, only much longer.
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: That was a superb experience for two hours of my time. None of the puzzles were overly complicated, and the environment was a staggeringly impressive feat to explore. The details kept a fairly simple game so engaging. I love that the hints themselves were a mini-game! Highly recommend for people who want a chill experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: The game presents astonishing art and imagined world worked out to the detail. The fairy tail story charmed in the paper and motion. Saying game has amazing graphics is like saying nothing. You can be dumped into architected world where emotions and values plays a role. This is enjoyable playable game. You won't be challenged with extremely sophisticated puzzles therefore it is very suitable for kids. It can turn to family play if you would like, what I did with my daughter.
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: A delightful game that's worth a buy!Here's why. (unintentional rhyme)Pros:- FANTASTIC soundtrack. Audio in a game is just as important as everything else, and this game has an incredible score to really bring you to a new world.- Smooth controls. While it's a simple Point&Click style gameplay design, the path-finding is very nice, and usually very responsive. Even the hint feature has a gameplay mechanic that works very well for challenging players that want to be given the solutions to the puzzles.- INCREDIBLE environments, that are all REAL! The dedication, time, and creativity put into designing and crafting each level, lighting and all, gives this world so much more heart and life! It's what makes you fully respect and agree with the choice of pricing it at 12 dollars.Cons:- Short. I don't blame the people behind this game, as for the number of levels there were, each one got a crazy amount of work put into them. But it is something to keep in mind when going in.- Not a lot of replay value. It's short, so it's no hard work to go through. And you could challenge yourself to a speedrun, but there's no secrets or alternative endings/decisions you can do. You'll get all the achievements on your first playthrough, as they're all based on progress.- Weird pacing. Most of it is very well paced. But some points you'll feel like things jumped ahead a bit, whether it's escalation in tension, or exposition dumps. Makes it feel like the levels and puzzles were thought of first, then the story/plot that we follow with it second.Overall, I highly recommend this game, just to bring yourself into this fascinating, beautiful, atmospheric world!
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: Papetura is a puzzle adventure game, it is beautiful, short and sweet. You can tell the dedication the developer has towards the art in this game, it is made out of real paper and therefore, the art relies heavily on the paper texture and the lighting, which makes this game art unique and original. The simple color scheme suits this game a lot, if not it actually enhances the graphic even more. The environment design is great, and character design is adorable as well. I actually regret not taking any screenshots in the game, mainly because I got too immersed in it. I received this game from my friend as a gift, but I say this game absolutely worth the price, for it is a masterpiece.
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: I really recommend this cool little Indie puzzle game though be aware it is only 2 hours long. It's funny how I completed it in only 115 minutes and could have still been eligible for a refund. I am not going to refund though that would be an unfair thing to do because Papetura is a fun, charming game and has obviously been made by some talented people. The puzzles are simple but fun to solve and quirky. The main appeal is the world design, it's all real miniature sets made from paper and cardboard. You can tell it's "real" just as you could tell Wallace and Gromit animations were made from real modelling clay. The character and creatures are well animated with some real imaginative designs. There is a very basic story which is very cute and put a smile on my face. It's a short puzzle game but for the creative talent on show and the games charm it's worth every penny in my book.
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: Simply gorgeous game.  Original paper design that is beautifully executed.  The soundtrack by Floex is a wonderful complement to the flow of the game. Yes it is very short and I agree with the other reviewers that it is worth it.  A huge labor in background and detail of movement and puzzles.  I took my time to enjoy the play time.  Most will finish under 2 hours.  Kudos to the developer.
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: this game is relatively simple, but it is also rather challenging in some parts. its a cute little plot, but what really blows me away is the animation; everything in this game is made of paper, and i couldn't be more impressed. its games like these that really make me appreciate video games as an art form (which i know sounds weird but iykyk). totally recommend, especially for those who appreciate the time people put into making interactive works of art :)
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: Stunning game. Gameplay is fairly easy -- a couple puzzles might take a moment to suss out but mostly it's a feast for the eyes and ears. The care put into the game is evident, and I may have fallen absolutely in love with the little kitty (although I will fall in love with any cat). I may have actually cried at one point...I wish it were longer! Well, I wish it went on forever. That's the pain of these handmade pieces of art, they will rarely be very long, but gosh was it ever worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: This game was so beautiful to play through! I really appreciate the time and energy it took to make the sets and characters. There were parts of the game that made me laugh out loud from the effects/characters and I thoroughly enjoyed every minute of playing. I will say that there were some parts of the puzzle that were difficult to complete and took me a while to get because there are no written cues, but it could just be me! Overall, loved the aesthetic, soundtrack, and gameplay. The characters move really slow and that bothered me a bit at first, but then I realized that the game itself is not actually that long. I guess the speed of the characters moving helped compensate for what would have been an extremely short game had they not moved so slow.
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best games than I have played in my life. Respect for the team, I'm impressed for the handwork and all dedication on it. While I was playing the game, listening to the perfect soundtrack, I could feel all the love that you put on this project. Congrats, I wish to know more about you soon guys.
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: There are a few gameplay issues with puzzles (mainly the process of solving them because there is a help button with a cute minigame in case you get stuck) but other than that amazing and very unique game with an interesting worldview. The absence of words even in menus means anyone can understand it no matter how old they are and where they are from. Hats off to the developers for the colossal paperwork and sticking with it for such a long development time.
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: I love the mood and ambiance of the world. Really incredible work. The puzzles are tough sometimes and will stump a person for a bit. That being said, some effort is required and they can be overcome. I love how unexpected the results of certain encounters are- totally unexpected results sometimes. I also love the plot.About 2.4 hours for me to beat- I usually like to take my time on these sorts of games and really try to understand the ramifications of my actions.I'd love to see more of this game style.
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: A cute point and click adventure with beautiful visuals it's got a great soundtrack by Tomáš Dvořák (Machinarium)At it's core; it's a basic point n' click adventure, nothing groundbreaking mechanic-wise.It's got a neat hint system, when you click on it's icon it prompts a short mini game.When completing the minigame it gives a visual clue to where you're supposed to go.Nothing too challenging, but alot of charm.it's very short game though, i completed it in just shy of 2 hours, for some people that might be an issue.The value is in the experience, not the length.I'd give this a solid 7/10
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: A very short (1-2h) but atmospheric experience with great music.The gameplay isn't all that fancy, if you have played Amanitas games you know the drill.A few cool concepts though that stand out, just wish they'd done more.Hopefully they can expand on what they've learned and make a longer game later on.
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: Great little game!  The artwork is made entirely from paper and is amazing.  Music is great!  It reminds you of the games by Amanita-Design.  If you enjoyed playing Botanicula, Creaks and Churchel,  you will enjoy this game. The price for the game is fair considering the amount of effort that went into designing the paper art.  There is a video out there that shows how the art was made. Well worth a peek!
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: Was enjoyable, entertaining and good quality, as well as very original.The puzzle/logic aspect combined with the story adds to the fun and charm of the game, with just a touch of humour.I would recommend this if you are looking for something that is both an adventure and puzzle.Only change I would have liked is that there were more levels or stages (if you can call them that).
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: Echoing sentiments of others. Beautiful game with wonderful music. The gameplay is where it falls short. Character movement and interactions are so slow it discourages experimentation, and the puzzles almost exclusively exist to just be in the way, there's nothing particularly clever or interesting about any of them. it's also a very short game. Recommended for the art and music with the caveat that you probably have to be a fan of games-as-art and the point and click genre to enjoy yourself.
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: It's a delightful little game with some good vibes going on, I wasn't sure of it during my first couple of minutes but warmed up to the whole thing right after. It is rather on the short side, which is represented in the pricing, but I would have been happy if there were more puzzles and time spent in each location so you could take in the sights and sounds more. Make sure to stop occasionally or just do another playthrough if you want to take in the world a bit more. It is very much in the vein of Amanita design point and click adventure games, so if you enjoy the vibes those games have, you will enjoy this one without a doubt. I especially love the creature designs and their sounds and the way they move! I think my favorite were the tiny round fishes or the flying fishes! All of them are fun and delightful designs.The story however I was expecting to go to more places and was a bit disappointed to see it end where it did. Despite that, the ending still gave me some good vibes and was nice, but I just wanted a bit more (I mainly just wanted the bird to not die in the end as I felt they were a bit undeserving of such fate!) Good music, good sounds and good visuals, if you want to be delighted for 1.5-2 hours, this is it right here!
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: Truly an artistic triumph that looked and played great on my TV using Steam Link + Steam Controller (using a mouse configuration). From the astounding paper craft world and engrossing sound design to the charming hint system, I wholeheartedly recommend this short but sweet experience to anyone that's a fan of quirky/surreal point and clicks inspired by Amanita Design games.
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful little game, but it is shorter than I was expecting. The soundtrack by Floex is beautiful - you can buy it on bandcamp or on vinyl with download.The puzzles are not too challenging, the pacing is a bit more like a walking story than a game. It's a well crafted story - I hope the story evolves and that the puzzles are harder next time around.
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: This beautiful little game is an art, nothing less. Instabuy, instarecommend, instadelight. A cozy, soft, pretty experience that even non-gamers would enjoy.The developer said, "I want to make an  perfect game". Well Tomasz, sorry, but you've failed at that and made an  perfect game instead. Thank you, it was worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: I played the game mostly for its unique artstyle, and it delivered! The visuals and the lighting are really striking. The adventure is good, although nothing groundbreaking as far as point-and-click games go. As someone who doesn't play a lot of them and usually doesn't have the patience required to finish them, I was happy with the hints system implemented.Really worth trying if you're in for a short game with a lot of charm.
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game creator work and great effect. The game is very addictive and difficult at times, but solving the puzzles gives a lot of satisfaction. The characters are charming (the kitty - I love him), the sounds and music are well-chosen (again the kitty steals the whole show). Great job. I recommend it to all those who like to activate their gray cells a bit and explore the strange and amazing world of Papetura.
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun and gorgeous game, it's a point and click game thats very simple and easy to play. it's about 45 minutes of playtime if you go back and know what to do but if you don't and just enjoy the game it's probably around 60 - 90 minutes. Visually amazing game thats created by hand using paper. PAPER!!!have a 4K playthrough on my channel here :
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: This is a gorgeous little game! It was clearly inspired by Amanita games like the Samorosts and Machinarium, and I think that's a great thing - those are some of my favorite games, and I love to see another in a similar vein. I can't imagine how much work it must have been to create the entire thing out of paper, and it makes sense that this is a short game given how time-consuming that must have been. To me, the tradeoff of shorter play length for absolutely stunning graphics is definitely worth it. Gameplay is pretty simple, but there is an elegant hint system that, I admit, I did use a couple of times.
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing, you can see the inspiration from Amanita Design games and so much more built on top. Great respect for the creator and for Floex for delivering yet another beautiful album. The game is short, but worth every penny, it's one of, if not THE most beautiful game ever. Thank you for bringing Papetura to life and I'll be waiting for whatever comes next.
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: I have always wondered why there weren't more developers emulating the Amanita Design style. This game does just this and does little to separate itself from it, which is fine since it's something I can always use more of. It is however disappointingly short and feels a little expensive from less than 2 hours of gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: Very cute game. The visuals and music are the best part of it! The puzzles are not very challenging, although a couple of them were not very clear to me. Maybe it was just me though. Story was nice also. It's a liiiiittle bit shorter than I expected, but that's not a big problem for me. Overall it was a very nice experience. Totally recommend it!
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: I was alittle weary purchasing this for some reason and I'm not sure why. Once you watch the trailer and how everything is made, once you jump in game you appreciate it that much more. I obviously love the fact that everything is hand made but the interaction between the character and the environment is super easy and the hints are a plus! (love the mini game addition.) With only an hour in I have ran in to some difficulties with the puzzles, but once you figure them out it clicks. For sure recommend for the price. link for reference.
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: Really was looking forward to play this one from the first moment I found it. As a big fan of Amanita design and Floex, this became another must have game. And I wasn't dissapointed at all in my expectations. The feeling is really close to Samorost, both with graphics and sound. And the fact that the creator made the whole thing in real from a paper and used the paper structures to work with the light, that's unbeliavable and I am glad that I could play the game and know the fact that everything was made by a real hand. I can't imagine the amount of work you had to put in the making. Hope to see soon your future projects, hopefully you will find other talented artists to help you with creating so you can make bigger and even more beautiful games in a shorter time!I really wish the game would last longer. For the price I couldn't ask more, it's just that I would really like to enjoy this world more, well, surprise us with your next game! Papetura 2 or a DLC maybe? :)
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

_childDocuments_.review: Papetura is an atmospheric point & click adventure game, handcrafted entirely out of paper. Little creatures Pape and Tura will face monsters that will try to burn down their beloved paper world.
_childDocuments_.name: Papetura

name: Visage
detailed_description: WARNING: This video game may potentially trigger seizures for people with photosensitive epilepsy. Player discretion is advised. IMPORTANT NOTE: The game focuses on exploration and builds tension slowly to create a deeper and more meaningful experience. Its story is unveiled through surreal imaging and subtle environment details. Be mindful that it is a difficult game in unconventional ways. Visage is a first-person psychological horror game. Explore a mysterious ever-changing house in a slow-paced, atmospheric world that combines both uncannily comforting and horrifyingly realistic environments, and enjoy a genuinely terrifying experience. Environment The game is set inside a huge house in which terrible things have happened. You’ll wander through the gloomy corridors, explore every dead room, and get lost in endless mazes, your head filling with memories of the dead families that once lived in this very home. This twisted environment, void of any life other than yours, takes you to places you couldn't even bear imagining. Storyline This house is stained with a terrible past. Families were brutally murdered by their own family members, people went insane, many committed suicide, and other grisly events occurred. Each and every room has its story painted on an invisible canvas. As a player, you will relive parts of this dark past, and each of its fragments will leave you restless and terrified. You’ll soon wish you could join the dead's ranks in their abyss, but death won't help you leave this place. Will you run from it, or will you try to uncover the truth behind the shadows? Dark entities The families that died in the house will haunt you and leave you restless. They’ll follow your every move, watch you from every corner, play tricks with your mind, and try to attack you. Why do they haunt you? What have you done? This you have to find out on your own. Gameplay In Visage, you are defenseless; no weapons could save you from the dreadful entities stalking you from the next corner, the next door, or underneath your feet. You’ll be able to pick up key elements, interact with the environment, and search for things that may help you escape this nightmare or pull you deeper into it. Dying is part of the game. You need to avoid terror at all costs, as dark entities are attracted to it. Maintaining your mind as sane as possible will keep you from joining the ranks of the dead. Doing so will not be easy, and you'll have to figure out ways, like staying in the light, to avoid going insane.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game, I really enjoyed it. Probably one of the scariest games I've played in quite sometime. It is very immersive and really uses the environment to mess with you. Great for an early access game. I am concerned about it ever being released though. It has been in early access for a long time and there have been few updates and little communication by the developers until very recently. Still worth a play through even without the full release IMHO. Thanks for reading.
_childDocuments_.name: Visage

_childDocuments_.review: Visage is a surprisingly unusual type of a linear horror game that has freedom of choice when it comes to chapters and in - game actions, which makes it unique and pretty creepy unlike most linear horror games. This game doesn't rely a lot on jumpscares and has some really horrifying moments that are capable of frightening some of the more experienced horror fans out there. I have to admit that I got pleasantly surprised by this game and I didn't run into many game - breaking problems. The only issues that I got were a crash of the game after a specific scene () and some huge fps drops in certain areas for a few seconds (I think that they were around 8 areas). Overall I would say that this game is worth a try if you can get it on a 50% discount. It has a lot of things to offer, even to those of you who are used to horror games about paranormal activity. I can give Visage a rating of 7/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Visage

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely well made horror game, all the elements and realism... loved/hate every second of it... many jumpscares, Music/Ambience very well made, it's like putting Outlast 1+ Outlast 2 combined, then giving it steroids. Looking forward for the next realeases :Dsometimes u'll get lost, but the game does a good job trying to "lead" u with some things on the ground,etc ALSO USE UR RESOURCES WISELY!!
_childDocuments_.name: Visage

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the best Horror game i've ever played. I've played a lot of horror games including all the outlast games and some of the Resident evil games. And its up there with the best as its great graphically, story wise and immersion. The game is really creepy and eerie especially some of the characters that you end up facing off against as they chase you and you feel like you will ♥♥♥♥ yourself any time. Each chapter includes a different character story and levels and some of them are really sad and messed up which adds to the game. Plus you play all of these events within one house but this house expands and changes as you play which I really loved. The best game I can compare it to is if resident evil 7 and P.T combined
_childDocuments_.name: Visage

_childDocuments_.review: Visage is Scary. When you get the clues in a decent amount of time you will come across sections that hit you in the face with scary. When these sections happen they are great and the scares do what they are supposed to do. After a while though the fact that every single item needed to be found to progress in the story started to wear on my patience. I had a very good pace for the first chapter. Items were hard to find but only a little poking around and you were golden. The chapters after were much harder, it was like a slight curve for searching every nook and cranny for the first chapter and then the second and on chapters was like a mountain of hidden clues, horrendous amounts of backtracking and the death of a steady pace were prevalent in the game after the first chapter. I love looking around for items but for a casual horror fan be ready to search everywhere for every little item you can find. I want to reiterate when you get to the horror it is great sometimes even amazing, creepy figures in the dark, killer grandma ghost stalking you and trapping you in rooms, the little girl driving your sanity into the floor were all great. This part of the game I loved and is a shining game in light of the P.T Craze and Silent Hills cancellation. I just feel that in the early onset of the later chapters the steep cliff of searching and backtracking for items is fun for a little but wears out the fun after about an hour. This will get better if you start finding items in the chapters it becomes better in each chapter once the game focuses on horror and give you easy to find items to keep the momentum going. The One thing that will keep you wanting to play this game is the amazing sound design, stellar atmosphere and all around great horror moments and elements injected into this game. Just be ready to fight tooth and nail with the items to find them, find where they go, and how to utilize them. all in all a great game.8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Visage

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game. Only 1 of 5 chapters released and already I am completely blown away. The attention to detail in this game is very impressive. The horror mechanics that are in place are used very tactfully. Pros: Looks great, truly tense and terrifying moments, challenging environments that force you to explore and interact in significant detail, more than just jump scares the game makes you feel completely overwhelmed and engulfed by the atmosphere. Cons: The voice acting leaves a little to be desired for but I am being very nitpicky because its my only complaint.
_childDocuments_.name: Visage

_childDocuments_.review: My girlfriend and I love playing this game in the dark with a couple of candles lit. I saw someone say something about the whole keeping the lights on mechanic annoying or something to that nature. To me its what make even more butthole puckering. You're exploring parts of the house and the lights go out behind you. I just start screaming and run for my life. It really is an experience. Its not something you're just going to walk through and beat. Its the journey in between of exploring a creepy house with dark rooms and random paranormal activity. (i recommend not playing alone and watching a Disney  movie afterwards.)
_childDocuments_.name: Visage

_childDocuments_.review: The atmosphere & scares are among the best in the genre. One of the creepiest games ever made. I can confidently say this game has stuck with me the most in terms of atmosphere. That being said, the puzzles are almost impossible to do without a guide. I'm not joking, there is no way anyone who hasn't seen a walk through could figure some of these puzzles out. It's too bad SadSquare doesn't seem to be around anymore to make another game.
_childDocuments_.name: Visage

_childDocuments_.review: After 100% completion of this game, I shall review.It's great. If you like walking simulators and pooping your pants in terror, buy it. Rather short though so maybe wait for ~30% sale.The story was actually pretty deep, explained to you quite well throughout the game. I enjoyed it so much that I immediately went to YouTube (F censorship) to put a more complete understanding together and I loved it. The gameplay is typical for this type. I will say though, your character moves INCREDIBLY slow and it's just unnecessary. No real combat but some very tense, "move your arse" moments. The ever changing environment is awesome, but familiar. You WILL get lost, and depending on the severity of it you may run out of resources, and get stuck in a death loop with the monster killing you repeatedly. This may lead to a complete restart of the game like I did. (This is why I have 11 hours, about 3 of them were waste) Akin to this death loop, sometimes the monsters get unfair. I recall one spot in particular where I could not get through a dark hallway because I had to maneuver around some broken environment, and the monster was always lurking right there. Killed me 6 times without taking more than a few steps. Through trial and error I found that crouching THE INSTANT your game loads, lead to the monster behavior changing and thus moving along. The sound, wow. It's pretty basic stuff honestly, footsteps on a wood floor. Guttural, visceral moaning and chatter of the dead or undying, rain drops on the window... Basic stuff, but it's good. Real good. Put your headphones on for sure.A simple and short review, play the game. Experience it for yourself. _childDocuments_.review: It has potential, but it's not there yet.This game is absolutely fantastic at creating atmosphere. The lighting is sublime and the audio work is spot on, so it's really good at creating a sense of dread. However, the control scheme seems purposely designed to be obtuse. I know the idea of having to move the mouse to open doors was popularised by other horror games, but it's just garbage. It's not adding anything to the gameplay and it's made even worse in this game with its terrible implementation. Sometimes you have to move the mouse horizontally to open a door, whereas other times its vertical and it just makes you motion sick because your head ends up moving all the time when you don't guess at the correct direction. Then the core mechanic seems to be built around depriving the player of light. There's electricity in the house, but for whatever reason 90% of the light bulbs are burnt out so you have to find replacement bulbs which are somewhat rare, or find candles and a lighter with which to light them. Both the lighter and the candle eventually burn out which wouldn't be bad if I could keep more on me, but going back to the purposefully obtuse design, you can only carry an object in each hand and 5 that can be dynamically swapped out from your inventory. I quickly found myself in a situation where I knew there were lighters that I left behind in the basement somewhere, but I couldn't find them because my lighter ran out and the candles burn out if you move with them. That's when I decided to call it quits. After nearly 2 hours of gameplay, pretty much nothing happened. There were some creepy audio cues which definitely scared me, but it was all auditory. I did get one ghost like person who appeared conveniently right after I ran out of lighter fluid, and that was an awesome moment. Otherwise, I knew where I needed to go, but couldn't find the item necessary to give me access to that part of the house so I decided to give up. If the mechanics were changed to be less about frustrating the player, then I could see myself really liking this game, but as I said, they've designed it this way on purpose, so I don't see myself coming back. Can't recommend it right now.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm pretty sure this is supposed to be a horror game, but it's not scary. It's slow (par for the course for a walking sim, but even this is a little much), everything is tedious (why the actual ♥♥♥♥ do you think a player would want to faff about with the mouse to get a dresser drawer open? It wasn't fun when Wii games did it with motion controls, and it isn't fun now. Just open the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ drawer with interact and stop trying to repeat Rockstar's annoying and ♥♥♥♥♥♥ realism-obsessed game design), I ended up wandering around the house for 40 minutes trying to make any progress beyond the mirror key (which is useless and just opens two doors to a room that serves no purpose), and there's not even any tension or stakes. About 15 minutes in, I started turning off all the lights to stress my character out, because I wanted to see what the failure state looks like. Nothing. Ever. Came for me. It's just "spooky" noises and events, like lights turning off, doors closing, and a bell going off. I waited in the darkest place I could find for 5+ minutes and nothing happened. I went "insane", but all it did was make the paranormal events happen slightly more frequently. I wanted so bad for something to jump out at me, or for my character to just jump out the window or something, but it never happened.Let me tell you about a game that does sanity well and is actually stressful to play. It's called Dead End Road. In DER, you drive a car from town to town while trying to gather the supplies you need for a ritual. Driving by itself stresses you out, and the more stressed you are, the more the demon is able to mess with you. It messes with you by making you hallucinate, by spawning the "turn that light off" guy (can kill you), and by spawning objects to damage your car. The hallucinations aren't that bad, but they take you out of reality and make it very likely that you'll crash into something on resume. If you crash, you die. If your car breaks down, you lose. If you run out of fuel, you lose. So with your limited budget, you're supposed to manage your sanity, your car's repair state, your fuel and your items. You will die a lot.This game. Is nothing like that game. AFAICT you cannot actually die, even though the game says it's "dangerous" to lose your sanity.I suppose the house could be a tutorial where there are no stakes so that you can learn, but then that's on the devs for pacing the game poorly. The tutorial should have ended (if it didn't) 10 minutes in when you get the first key and enter your first "chapter". So how come I didn't die in over 30 minutes despite *trying* to get killed? Either the whole game is like this or the beginning is bad, which is a death sentence in itself. And I don't agree that you need to play a game for some arbitrary amount of time to form an impression. If I hate a game within 5 minutes of starting it, then I am valid in saying I think it's a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ game. There's a saying that in a web video or TV show, you have about the first 15 seconds to a minute to grab the viewer's attention and keep it. Why should it be any different for a game? If a game cannot hold your engagement/immersion for longer than 5 minutes, then it's not a very good game, is it? I was bored of this game by 10 minutes in. The only reason I didn't quit then and there is because I found a key and thought I had made some progress. After I was disappointed by the empty room of emptiness, I spent the rest of the game deliberately trying to kill myself, and failed. After 40 minutes of wandering without anything happening, I got fed up and quit the game.The only thing this game has going for it is its atmosphere, which is mediocre. It's not bad, but it's not great. Sure you could probably immerse yourself with a VR headset (assuming the game supports VR) and some headphones, but here's the thing: I am not easily scared. I don't generally play horror games to be scared anyway, because I know I'll just be disappointed. I play horror games because they tend to have other things going for them that make them an actually good game, and I have fun with it. Resident Evil, Silent Hill, Lost in Vivo, Bendy and the Ink Machine, Devil Daggers. All of these games are interesting, have cool mechanics, are fun to play and occasionally even have some stressful/WTF moments. So if you're gonna have a boring walking simulator with spooky lights and prankster ghosts, you're gonna need some actual stakes, because the game cannot ride on atmosphere alone.To really drive the point home, consider this: You know that game, A Hat in Time? It has a level where you're in a mansion trying to hide from some ghost woman thing. Hat in Time is not a horror game, but that level is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ terrifying. How does a cute, cartoony, light-hearted collect-a-thon adventure do horror better than an actual horror game? In comparison, Visage comes across more akin to Spooky's House of Jumpscares. Not the rooms after ~150, because that game actually gets very WTF very fast. I'm talking the cute cardboard cutouts that pop out at you and the occasional monster. Even that is a better "horror" experience than this, and SHoJS/SJSM is a !Quick update: After looking through some other reviews, I have no clue why I didn't run into any monsters or whatnot. I'm pretty sure the chapter when you pick up the mirror key is the "Dolores" chapter. The brain was fully visible. The house was completely dark. I wandered around trying to find any progress at all, only to be told about a laundry room via a random note and never find it (I checked the bathroom, too). No creepy lady ever came running up behind me. So it could just be that my copy is broken/bugged. Which is bad cause that would mean the game is bleeding players.

_childDocuments_.review: This review contains some gameplay mechanic spoilers so be careful of that.By the way, this game is extremely ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up and deals with subjects that some people simply cannot handle (Deaths of loved ones, dementia, other mental sicknesses etc) and uses them as catalysts to make the story into what it is. It isn't entirely reliant on the supernatural. There is some real ♥♥♥♥ in this game so if you can't handle that then the game is not for you.I have literally hundreds of hours in horror games across steam and ps4. No other horror game has gotten close to being as soul-crushingly oppressive and dread-inducing as this game. And the best part is it never, and I mean NEVER lets up. I have 4 hours in this game because I need a break after an hour or so. Just a few things the game does really differently that make it stand out.           -Pressing escape is not a pause button. To pause what is happening, you need to press escape and click "Pause Game". IT then counts down slowly from 3, and THEN it is paused. The game requires you to be able to keep your wits about you when you are being attacked. I died 4 times out of panic until I finally managed to get away by the skin of my teeth.           -  On the topic of being attacked, it is completely random when it happens. You will be walking along with nothing happening just long enough to let your guard down and then the ghost appears, which means you need to run for your life.           -  Random scares are peppered throughout the game, constantly surprising you with things like ghosts peaking their head around a corner at the end of a hall about 7 feet from you, or a random light switch turning off to drain your sanity, giving you the immediate panic of trying to restore it to lower your chances of being attacked.Play this ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ game. Do yourself the favor. One of, if not the best, horror games I have EVER played and I WILL finish it and update the review.

_childDocuments_.review: Visage is an amazing horror game that will remind you a lot about P.T. It's incredibly scary and unpredictable, difficult but not unfair. This game is meant to be challenging but the game will provide you with helpful items once you think you're in a tight spot and unable to move forward. The game does have some bug issues.. the one that stood out the most to me is the manequinn-chase scene in Rakan's chapter. When you hide in one of the control rooms, there will be a corner around a plant which you simply cannot move again once you have entered that space, it is really annoying as it forces you to restart the chase part of the humanoids, and that part is the hardest one in Rakan's chapter. Otherwise everything else was fantastic This is my 3rd playthrough of Visage, first one with my boyfriend, second one on my own through Steamunlocked and a third time on Steam for a speedrun. The hallways are very narrow and will make you feel claustrophobic. The ghosts that are haunting Dwayne can spawn in the middle of nowhere and kill you on the spot, they are unpredictable but the game will warn you a couple of seconds before the ghost even appears. This is usually through flickering lights, loud music followed by a strange noise, each ghost has their own authentic sound depending on how they died. Visage is also very open for interpretation and as the player you are thrown directly into the game without any clue or context and what is going on. You play through 4 chapters, the 4th one only being unlocked once you have finished the other 3 chapters. The environment is semi-open and you will find helpful items spawning randomly around the house but you must be very careful about traversing through the house as you are never safe and a ghost will ALWAYS be stalking you and hunting you regardless of whether you have started a chapter or not. You are never safe in Visage. Like most other hardcore super-fans, I do also need to criticize it a little, tinsy bit for the very limited inventory system. You'll often find yourself dropping random things, picking it up, going back to the storage room, leaving, picking up and repeat. The storyline is very deep and all equally disturbing but in their own way, I found Dwayne's the most emotional and I really felt for his family at the end of the game.I love Visage, it's one of my favorite games and despite the bugs and limited inventory system I would recommend it to everyone who loves psychological horror. The atmosphere is just great too, you need to have a lot of patience with the game. The ghosts that haunt you are made to be even scarier if you percieve them to be scary. For example it's very easy to forget how many mirrors you can escape into in the Dolores chapter to stop her from chasing you because of how terrifying she looks and if it is your first time playing you might end up standing still, panicking and not knowing what to do. That was definitely what happened the first time I played Visage, but so long as you stay patient with yourself, allow yourself to feel the fear but do it anyway, use your items sparingly and take advantage of the environment around you, you will be fine Again, Visage is difficult but it is not unfair. Sometimes the game will be helping you out, other times it will punish you. Learn to identify the patterns of the ghosts too that will be very helpful.

_childDocuments_.review: The only truly "scary" thing I've found in this game is the control scheme, which is part of the reason I didn't play this game for very long. For mobility reasons, I can't play on wasd like most other people. I need to be able to edit keybinds, which you can't in this game. And even then, the control scheme makes NO sense. If you're going to be mostly interacting and looking at objects, PUT THAT ON LEFT CLICK. Have use on e like almost every other game.The second "scary" thing is the tutorials, which randomly pop up in the worst way. With the way the game is made, where you have a sanity meter that can be effected by "paranormal activity" in the game, you NEED to pause the game while those tutorials are up so people can actually read them if you're going to shove them in their faces. More than once I was trying to understand what the block of text was and there would be a "scary something" that happened in the background, usually a lightbulb breaking or switch being flipped, which lead me to cancel out of the tutorial before I could read it and have to find a place with light so my dumb character wouldn't be afraid of the dark for half a second. Which brings me to another annoying part of the game, if you're in early access and want to have particular parts blocked off for the main game, for the love of god don't say something's 'not available in early access' in the game. Just say the door's locked or the lock is broken or something. It kills the immersion that should be in a horror game to make it scary as badly as the tutorials. Personally, I didn't find the game scary. Maybe that comes with how little of the game I could play, but having stock 'you should be scared now' sounds happening when I'm not looking at whatever should be scaring me is more annoying than anything else, especially when it tanks the character's sanity meter and I'm left spinning in circles asking wtf is supposed to be scaring me. At the very least the scares should happen when I'm looking at the light, or the radio should pop on when I'm far enough away that's it's not 'oh, the radio again'. Not only that but the scares should be spead out enough that I wasn't thinking 'oh, it's been 45 seconds, time for another spook.'If you're going to have a mechanic that lowers sanity in the dark, don't spam that you shouldn't stand in the dark for so long when someone's only been in the dark a couple seconds, especially when there's items that you have to get by going through dark areas to get! For a game that tries to brag that it's a hard game, which is suspect and laughable in most cases because the devs shouldn't have to try to convince you that a game is hard, it does a LOT of hand holding. If it's an exploritory game, let people explore without so many warnings and pop ups. If you're worried that people are going to quit the game because it's artifically hard, then drop it! Make it a more casual and enjoyable experience if you want to tell a story with your game. Otherwise, actually make the game hard and not just annoying because of bad qol changes. I honestly had high hopes for this game, but it's left me laughing and wanting a much better experience. Unless there are meaningful changes to the game, I'm not going to pick it up again and I certainly won't be recommending it to anyone.

_childDocuments_.review: If your a fan of psychological horrors with jump scares, then this game is for you. Overall, this game was extremely fun even though I am not one for these types of games. This is the first one of hopefully many games that I will play in regards to this type of horror. A couple of pros and cons about this game that I do have and will share with the community.Pros:- Awesome story within each chapter that will be revealed the more you proceed with each chapter. Even though there is only two chapters out so far, the story of each has left an everlasting impression on what more is to come.- The music and the ambient sounds from the game are memorizing. It always leaves you on the edge of your seat as your proceeding through the chapters of the game.- The random generated events requires you to have your head on a swivel and will always pull your attention that something may happen or not. Your attention is always stuck on what is going on and the game does not leave any room where you can take a break from the chaos that you will eventually run into.- Critical thinking in some part of the chapters makes you rethink everything that has happened thus far and try to figure out the next upcoming step.- The First Person Point-of-View gives this game a more intertwined and immersed feeling as you are viewing everything first hand. What the character sees and hears, you feel that your actually at that moment and time within the chapter.Cons:- There have been a couple of spots where I have randomly got stuck and unable to move. With that said, I would have to reload the save file from the latest auto save. Whatever the case may be with that, kinda glad that I was in a somewhat "safe" part of the chapter that I was proceeding through.- Items randomly floating in the middle of the room or staircase. Thank you for the extra items but it is a little weird in seeing them floating around randomly and in random locations. Always thought that they would be empty or not usable anymore but they were.- When sprinting through the game, there are a couple of lag spikes where you wont be able to move or interact with anything in the game. Not terribly bad, but that couple of seconds with something coming after you, you need to run like hell.- When exiting the game and proceeding back to the main menu, it will crash most times then not and I would have to restart the game.Overall, never thought that i would enjoy this game apart from the funky glitches and bugs I ran into throughout the game, however, it has become my "must come back to" game once the next chapters have been revealed. I cannot wait to see what is in store next with this game.

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10.Overall, really good if you like single player horror games.Pros:* Graphics are really nice.* Story is pretty intense.* Pretty long story overall, compared to many similar games.* Well done puzzles, and lots of neat easter eggs.* Absolutely terrifying. Like any game, some will say "it's not scary, what do you mean," but I play in the dark, by myself, volume cranked. I want to be as scared as possible, and this one definitely delivers.Cons:* Controls are.. Weird. They work once you get the flow of it, but I can't help imaging there must've been a much easier way of doing it.* The puzzles are challenging, but doable. But at some points it's very difficult to figure out where to go. Better than habd-holding, but still a but tough.* Movement speed is just a tad slow. Couple this with the longer gameplay (which is good) and the frustration of getting lost, not knowing where to go, and/or backtracking, you end up losing a few hours overall just wandering.* Overall, the story is great and really well done, but there are just a couple.. Meh moments. A but cringey, over-the-top, etc.* Definitely some bugs. Nothing game-breaking, but sometimes you'll crash on retry, things won't activate, and other small optimization issues. It seems like things that could be fixed in one pass, though I believe the developers are finished with the game. Again, nothing too bad, but it could be a source of frustration.

_childDocuments_.review: Probably one of the most scary games I've played and a fantastic homage to P.T. The atmosphere was masterfully created and well maintained throughout the game. Exploring the house and being caught in darkness/paranormal events was deeply unsettling and often left me sprinting for known sources of light. Using the fear of what lies in darkness as a tool was extremely well done, in particular with Lucy's chapter. No spoilers, but the camera mechanic was terrifying as it was unique and I held my breath for *probably* the entire chapter. Whoever worked on the sound design deserves all the praise in the world- the subtle sounds like glass crunching, light switches being turned off, the chandelier swinging, light bulbs breaking, and footsteps elsewhere in the house were a really nice touch, while moments of silence that were randomly shattered by the chiming of that damned clock and hall radio instantly made me tense up. Some minor criticisms were the lack of direction in some parts, the darkness of the game (I was torn between turning the gamma up and losing some of the atmosphere, or wandering aimlessly and hugging walls in some parts), and some minor controller issues that felt counterintuitive at times. All of these things weren't too glaring of an issue- as the game does warn you right from the beginning about the difficulty of the game- but I had moments where I literally had no idea where to go/what to interact with to progress which was slightly annoying. Overall I highly recommend it, especially if you were a fan of P.T, and I REALLY hope SadSquare Studio comes out with another game like Visage.

_childDocuments_.review: Great horror game, not focused on jumpscares but on building up the tension and making the player always feel uncomfortable.The house the game takes place in plays a major role in all of this, with paranormal events (flickering lights, turn on and off of electronic appliances, sudden closing of doors) and strange sounds constantly surrounding the player.The narrative is divided in chapters, that can be accessed by interacting with specific objects inside the house. When in a chapter the tension and the horror factor ramp up, as you are not simply pressed by the events inside the house, but also by other entities which threaten your life. The story of the single chapters is interesting and delivered in a crude but effective way, even if its difficult to relate to the opening cutscene.The game lacks a bit of polishing here and there (understandable considering the early access), but it's worth the price considering the overall length (6-9 hours up to now) and the fact the are still half of the chapter missing (2) which must be released to complete the story.In addition the improvements made in the design from the first to the second chapter, clearly shows how the team is improving while creating the game, which bodes well for the future.EDIT:After having completed the game, my final idea stays in line with what I’ve written above with a couple of additional considerations.Chapter 3 and Chapter 4 do not achieve the peak reach by the first two, with the third more similar to an outlast-like horror with a lot of chasing and scripted sequences and the fourth one which is not really a full chapter but a collection of micro sequence needed to tell the overarching story of the main character. Still both of them deliver good horror moments and are enjoyable to play. The change of setting in Chapter 3, in particular, is an interesting and refreshing twist.The overarching story is quite interesting when the pieces are all put together (not only from through the narrative told in the chapters but also through some collectibles, like the comic’s pages), but it’s too cryptic in the way is narrated. This is purposely done to keep an aura of mystery and leave space to interpretation, but, at the same time, it is highly likely that most of the player will finish the game without understand it.To summarize for all the people who played the game in early access, the final product provides solid additional hours of entertainment and a good conclusion to the story.For all the people new to the game who like horror, instead, this game is a must buy, capable of offering one of the most frightening experience the genre has to offer.

_childDocuments_.review: Some feedback after playing your game in early access. Please note: I REALLY want this game to succeed. I love horror and that never happens to me! A huge achievement. The way it plays with your fears and anxiety of the dark is just next level creepy! Graphics and sound design are fantastic!Where it falls over are the gameplay mechanics. You have a sanity meter that fills up if you stand in the dark too long. When that happens, lights start to switch off and there are more paranormal events. It worked at first, but then just become a major hindrance in the immersion of the game and quickly replaced all feelings of fear with frustration. This completely pulled me out of the game. Simple inventory management is fine but lighters running out of fuel and having to search for more sanity pills just gets boring real quick.Here’s hoping you go back and cull all these roadblocks out and just let us explore this incredible house! -Dane Fabri

_childDocuments_.review: After 3 years of waiting, I finally was able to play Visage. I have to say, this is one of the most terrifying experiences I have had with a survival horror game, in years. I couldn't even imagine playing this in VR. Which I do hope the devs put in later. This game feels like a love letter to "P.T." and it is wonderful! After the disappointing news of the cancelation of Silent Hills, I always wondered what the game would have been like. I think Visage is very close to what P.T. (Silent Hills) would have been.Right when you start playing, the tension and atmosphere start to build. Which turns to dread and fear later on in the game. This, I think, is mainly thanks to the photo realistic graphics and it makes you feel like you are investigating a real home. (if that makes any sense)Unlike most horror games out there today, which rely heavily on jump scares, this game has far and few of them. The only scares you will encounter, is the feeling of what could be around the corner. I felt like I held my breath most of the time just to prepare myself of a scare, when in turn, there is nothing and builds the tension even more.Even the music and sounds in the game put you on edge the entire time you are playing. During the game you encounter events that trigger certain sounds, which really don't help when you are already about to ♥♥♥♥ your pants. (in a good way? LOL)So, the combination of the graphics, sounds and atmosphere make this a true horror experience. The only problem I have with the game is the inventory system and confusion with certain items (which have been fixed). Also, I had issues with items that I had in my hand clipping into doors and walls.But with those things aside, if you love survival horror or psychological horror, pick this game up. As of right now you can get a good 2 hours into the game in early access. I honestly can't wait until full release of this game.9/10!

_childDocuments_.review: This is actually a negative review based on personal opinion, tastes and impressions. I can still recommend this game to the fans of the genre, because even with the enormous load of issues it has, it's still not a complete trash and there are definitely some enjoyable moments.Horror games of this type are one of my favorite genres - a mix of walking simulator, puzzles, survival, exploration and narrative-driven gameplay in various proportions. At least that's what Visage seemed like.I almost believed all the hype, because the game started strong. The beginning cutscene was so stupidly slow and long that it lost all tension and shocking value, but oh well, disturbing enough. You stumble around an almost perfect haunted labyrinth of a house, turning lights on, looking for clues, hearing scary sound effects, turning lights on again, exploring next room only to hear more scary sound effects, which indicate that something -  probably some environmentally conscious, angry and OCD poltergeist - turned the lights off yet again.Then it gets very spoopy very fast. And not in a good way.You have all the done-to-death horror clichés here. Ominous dolls, little girl ghosts, spooky empty hospitals, black ooze seeping everywhere, cheap random deaths and even cheaper loud jumpscares aplenty. What you   have is a cohesive horror experience. The plot goes like this (beware spoilers duh):There is this girl, she had a scary demon imaginary friend, went CRAZY and ripped her own jaw! Boo!There is this woman, she had a baby, went CRAZY and took her own life! Boo!There is this guy, he had paranoia and obviously went CRAZY! Boo!There is this other guy, he used to mix drugs with booze and then went CRAZY and killed his own family! Oh, and you are also playing as him. No, there are no connections or explanations. Boo?..Crazy ppl r crazy bc they r crazy SCARY. No questions are asked, no answers are given. Everything is random and disconnected - just a bunch of spooky tropes.That said, I still really liked Dolores chapter (which I played first). Gameplay-wise it reminded me more of Painscreek Killings than Layers of Fear - solving series of multiple interconnected puzzles which are meant to contribute to resolving a bigger puzzle near to the end. All while crawling around the house, pixel-hunting, inspecting every inch. Puzzle design isn't really as bad as it sounds - most of the times you can see what solution developers are hinting at. Also that music\audio puzzle bit is delicious.But overall gameplay design is just bad and overdone in almost every aspect. Excruciatingly slow and boring animations of many actions are just painful to watch. Why drag them for like three times too long? It does not feel suspenseful, it's just tedious and repetitive. Player character has no legs, no hands, no world model at all - which ruins the immersion. Items which you hold in your "hands" are just floating in the air, get stuck around every corner and glitch with every collision (and in your face). Inventory system is unnecessarily overcomplicated and adds nothing but frustration to the gameplay (both that and the "progress room" seem to be RE-inspired, but oh well).And the last nail on the coffin - technical issues. So. Many. Bugs. The game can easily glitch you out of progress, corrupt its own saves, fatal error you to desktop if you look at something at wrong angle. Postprocessing is broken and you can't even turn it off in the settings. DoF focus shifts all the time and blurs everything, FOV is locked, and FILM GRAIN, oh my.It could have been so much more. They have been making it for all these years and the result is this.No, just... No.
