_childDocuments_.review: This review contains mild spoilers, mostly relating to names of areas, characters and gameplay elements. It does not contain story spoilers.  However, anything that could be deemed as such, I will hide. $49.95 $16.28 22 hours (100%) N/A Epic/Very HighMotherboard: ASUS ROG STRIX Z490-ECPU: Intel i7 10700K @ 3.8GHzGPU: NVIDIA RTX 3080 10GBRAM: 32GB DDR4 1600MHzDrive: Silicone Power 500GB M.2 PCIe SSDOS: Windows 11 Quite a lot of hitches when loading an area, but for the most part, the performance was good enough. Some things were really bad, like clutter objects on some of the shelving being essentially blocky blobs in the vague shape of the item they were meant to be, while others were very good and detailed, like a box of laundry detergent that was fully readable and examinable. For the most part, this game is visually good. I wouldn’t say it’s anything groundbreaking, but horror games usually aren’t played for their visual fidelity, but rather their atmosphere, which this game does has in droves. Plenty of weird/awesome stuff to look at that doesn’t make any sense but is visually very interesting.  The overall story arcs of Dwayne (the player character), Delores, Rakan and Lucy were very well written, I thought. I wouldn’t fault anyone for wondering how you make any sense out of the admittedly bat-sh** crazy events that take place, but nevertheless there is a clear story in each scenario; each of them tied strongly to differently mental health conditions. I admit that I have a few questions after finishing the game. . Aside from those questions, I pretty much got the gist of things and enjoyed it.  Controls are pretty weird and unintuitive. I get wanting to try new things with control schemes, but I felt like I was fighting the controls, and you don’t want that when you’re in the middle of stressful situation. You eventually get used to it, but it really could have been a lot better. Hell, just let us rebind keys. Gameplay-wise I thought Delores’ chapter was the best of them, followed closely by Dwayne’s and Lucy’s. Somehow Rakan’s chapter didn’t have that same feel and was more like a running sim than an investigative horror experience. It’s not that Rakan’s story was bad, but the gameplay for it was too focused on escaping, in my opinion.Level design, while absolutely mind-bendingly frustrating at times, was actually really well done. Delores’ chapter being the highlight for me again. This game really trips you out in the best way.I’m 50/50 on whether I liked the core gameplay loop of “Search room, find thing, leave room, come back to room later and it’s slightly different”. On one hand, the subtlety is masterfully done, but that also meant that I spent half my play time scratching my head, visiting the same rooms 37 times because I couldn’t figure out what the heck I was meant to do/see. There is no hand holding in this game, and the hints for progress were very, very subtle, if at all even noticeable. I encountered a bug with the light bulbs that you find throughout the house. I put the spare ones in the storage room but when I came back, they were all gone, and after that, I never found more, nor did any lights break.The stairs leading to the lighthouse wouldn’t let me past about halfway up, like there was a barrier there. Somehow, pressing left instead of forward allowed me to pass.The game frequently had troubles auto saving and I had to do manual saves. At least the game tells you when it can’t auto save. I never pick horror games because I want to be scared. I pick horror games because they seem to be the one genre of games where you get to experience some truly crazy stuff. Stuff that makes your mind explode because it’s so strange, yet interesting. Visage has these experiences in droves, and of course, plenty of things that would make me scared if I wasn’t dead inside…but alas! Yes, on sale. If you enjoy the horror genre, or if you like weird/crazy experiences in games, or even if you like puzzles and figuring stuff out. This one’s worth a play.

_childDocuments_.review: Fair warning: this review is going to be a bit of a book and will contain spoilers.I intended to play this game on stream, but my curiosity ended up getting the better of me. I knew that going into it, that the puzzles were not going to be as straightforward as Resident Evil's, but I enjoy horror and puzzle games enough to decide that I'd give it a try. I wanted to go as far as I could without looking up a guide, and BOY, that did not last long at all. If you are like me and need a bit more handholding with the puzzles, the guide over at NeoSeeker was incredibly helpful to me!I'm not sure if the chapters are intended to be played in a specific order, but I will list them in the order that I played them.I feel that this chapter had the best, easiest to follow story from start to finish. The chase scenes are very creepy and panic-inducing, so big thumbs up for that. It could have been simply because I was still learning the layout of the house at the time, but this chapter blocks off certain rooms and the use of the mirrors just made it so much more confusing to me. I spent a lot of time in this chapter wandering aimlessly in the house because I couldn't remember which mirror was the one that would take me to the basement and after a while, it certainly did get frustrating, especially with the sanity drain mechanic.Overall, I think this was the best chapter in the game.This chapter had a very different feel from that of Dolores, and in my case, it's not a compliment. Instead of spending the majority of the puzzle in the house itself, the player is instead in a hospital of sorts, walking through visions - or perhaps illusions? - as we "learn" about this person. In a strange way, this setup felt disconnected from the rest of the game, and it was very immersion-breaking for me. Perhaps I didn't pay as much attention to this story as the others, but in my opinion, we really didn't learn that much about Rakan other than he's incredibly paranoid about being watched and spent time in the psych ward being medicated for it during his time there.There's a bit at the end where you have to run and find the exit door while evading patients that patrol the halls and walk out of rooms and the random spawn points for them made it very frustrating to try and get through, even with the use of a guide.In my opinion, this story was by far the weakest of the three.This chapter is marked as the first chapter, and perhaps if I'd started with this one, it would have better prepared me for the ones ahead, but ultimately, I ended up doing it last. Lucy's chapter was a refreshing return to a nice balance between being in the house and being in the strange places that these dark entities concoct for us, the player. While the main plot point is one that I've heard before, Visage did it well. This mysterious "friend" likes to pop up out of nowhere and kill me, which eventually proved to be fairly frustrating, knowing that I could die at any point to no fault of my own, but it is what it is. Nobody is supposed to make it through the game without dying at least a few times.I liked this chapter. It was delightfully creepy and was much better than Rakan's.Overall, this game was very good, and I would recommend it so long as you don't mind the seeming necessity of using a guide. There are things hidden in this game that I feel the player would have absolutely no way of knowing unless you were to use a guide. And while I don't really like that particular point, the experience overall was one that I would say is worth it. The devs use the atmosphere and audio to create a very eery and unsettling atmosphere, and it was done very well. TL;DR, If you are NOT the type to enjoy a game where using a guide will likely be necessary, then do not purchase it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one house that will stick with you. Much like the halls in P.T., SadSquare's vision of a haunted house in Visage is creepy enough to be unnervingly memorable long after you've finished playing the game. While it clearly borrows inspiration from the cancelled Silent Hills project, Visage manages to stand on its own remarkably well. It utilizes a sanity system that will see lights turning off on you, doors closing suddenly, radios activating themselves, and more, as you scramble to stay out of the dark and take your pills. Though the game leans heavily on the atmospheric, the chapters into which it's divided tell stories that are as brutal as they are frightening. Each chapter creatively seems to diverge from themes and ideas used in the others, so that what will aid you in one could almost get you lost in another, if you're not careful. Surely, one of the highlights of the game is Rakan's chapter, during which you make a little detour to one of the most unsettling abandoned hospitals ever created for a video game.Unlike many psychological horror games of its kind, Visage is not afraid to really keep you guessing at its puzzles. The creators seem to well understand the usefulness of leaving the player scrambling around in the dark, literally and figuratively, having to put real thought into what has to be done to progress. The game even warns you of its own difficulty in the beginning, but rather than being too frustrating an experience, this provides a level of immersion and scary problem-solving rarely seen in horror games.The voice acting is perhaps one of the few things I found wanting with Visage. The sound design is phenomenal, and will likely make your hair stand on end at times. Unfortunately, it's obvious in more than a few key moments that amateur voice actors were used for the game. Though the effort poured into Visage is admirable, this is one aspect of it that may detract players from the overwhelming atmosphere. Aside from this, the punishing learning curve and occasionally imprecise controls are other areas for improvement, although they honestly do not get in the way of the experience.When I first purchased and planned to play Visage, I had hoped to get it working in VR. I soon found out this feature has apparently been removed, but after actually playing some of the game, I'm admittedly a bit thankful for this. Visage is a genuinely terrifying game, one that I, even as a big-time horror buff, have doubts about experiencing in VR. In that situation, no amount of pills and no time in the light will help one's sanity all that much. If this in itself is not a shining recommendation of the quality and originality of Visage as a horror game, I'm not sure what is.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR It's overall one of the better horror games but it has a good handful of flaws that you'll have to be patient with.When it works, it works, (even if it does use a lot of horror tropes and ideas "inspired by" PT) but there's still a lot of things that hinder the experience. There's a sanity meter in the game which is a cheap way to build tension. Not only that, but the sanity meter will occasionally bug out and the medicine you take or the light you stand in won't properly fix your sanity, eventually resulting in an insta-death. Speaking of glitches and bugs, there's a lot of them. There's the aforementioned sanity bugs, Items will frequently spawn in, floating in mid-air, there's a few sections where the player character can get completely stuck in place and others have reported other, more game-breaking glitches. I'd also recommend having a walkthrough on hand because sometimes, the way forward can be pretty convoluted (many instances of "Oh, how was I supposed to know that you could go there?"). The puzzles are extremely easy though, with the game often just telling you the answer so don't worry about getting stuck with any of them. Again, it's not bad and worth a try, it's just not "amazing" either.

_childDocuments_.review: I generally don't agree when I see people complaining about technical problems or games being unfinished, but I think folks may be onto something with this one. I think the devs may have shoved it out the door a LITTLE too early, to capitalize on Halloween, because it probably wasn't going to be done for another 4-6 months (probably at most; so it's close).Anyway, incredibly slow, very, VERY little conveyance to help you figure out where to go in a house that is frankly PATRICIAN in its size, and no obvious delineation between interactable and non-interactable objects. By which I mean you can pick up every single mug, glass, or crumpled beer can, and there is no sort of effect that makes apparent what is, say, a discarded soup tin and a lighter, which is actually an item you can USE (and indeed, need to get around). That probably sounds ridiculous, but since part of the game's unfinished state is the poorly-constructed collision rules, a lot of times important items will be sunk slightly (or completely) into other textures, obscuring them from view. And when your cursor/reticle is ALWAYS enlarged to show clickables, and you are ALWAYS looking at the "Left click to interact" prompt, it doesn't trigger your attention the way it should when you mouse over something you might want/need. And that's to say nothing of key items actively HIDDEN inside environmental objects (like a key hidden in pants hidden inside the dryer hidden inside the laundry room, which is squirreled away somewhere in any of the 78 rooms in this apprently-44,000-sq-foot house). I had assumed it was like any of the other 600 cabinets I could open that have nothing in them; it was only because I found a note saying that Jenny had left the key in her pocket when she washed her pants that I figured out to open the bloody thing. And as weird a note as that is, it's an exception, not a rule; a lot of times the game feels like a pixel hunt in a MONSTROUSLY large environment. And sometimes pixels are burying other pixels.I don't know. It's really really slow, the atmosphere is okay, but I didn't find the item management all that difficult, my sanity was always fine, so nothing ever happened, other than some ambiance and the occasional sound of footsteps. The intro is nightmarish, but I found it pretty domestic after that, and I was not gonna wait four hours for the game to decide to do something to justify the FORTY DOLLARS I spent on the bloody thing.I'm disappointed; this has been on my wishlist for like two years, and I've played the EA release with my friends for some time in expectation. I was really quite giddy when I saw it was out of EA, but I don't feel like any of the issues I had that I chalked up to it BEING in EA were addressed with this full release.Maybe I'm thicker than an asphalt milkshake, but I really don't see this one as worth it. Save yourself some money, wait for a complete, competent LP to come out, and enjoy that.

_childDocuments_.review: As Jon Padgett so eloquently described in the opening to 'The secret of ventriloquism', horror runs along several vectors, it can be visceral and violent, the cosmic horror of the unknown, and the internal, cloying horror that lurks in the jungle of one's own mind. It is this third brand of horror that Visage does so well. It tracks this internal horror splendidly, and reminds us that the terror of being consumed by guilt, depression and nihilism lies not just in the truths it reveals, but in the sense of reality slowly slipping beneath a pearled darkness, as the sunlight appears through the ashen surface of the water to a drowning man.The game takes place in a purgatorial house, with superb attention to detail in both image and sound, as confusion and discomfort slowly rise to disgust, horror and despair. The atmosphere of this game is excellent,  and the opening scene sets the tone of a quite unsettling and adult exploration of regret. The pacing is a bit slow at the start, and it takes a bit of time to get the hang of what the game wants you to do, but it builds effectively and most of the game is neither too fast nor too slow. The puzzles are entertaining without being taxing, and there's not a lot of pixel-hunting. It is a story-driven game with little action or stealth.It reminded me somewhat of Danielewski's amazing postmodern horror novel 'The house of leaves'. As a fan of both very bad and very good horror, I recommend this as the latter. If you care to spend an evening wallowing in a self-loathing Hell as grief and madness suffocate what is left of the world, then, this may be for you. Or, if you just like creepy atmosphere.

_childDocuments_.review: Early Access review for chapter 1 of Visage:This game is a psychological and paranormal survival game with currently only 2 hours of gameplay. Here's what I thought about it so far.It's very rare for a P.T. clone to actually pull off a decent result, but so far Visage looks far from expendable. I have very mixed feelings about this game. Half the time I enjoyed it. The other half I felt annoyed and frustrated. I can't say much about the story as it is unfinished, but I can talk about everything else. The gameplay mostly surrounds the concept of an interdimensional house with sequential events leading to psychological environments and atmospheres. You progress to new events and occurances through investigation, puzzle solving, trying to unravel what the game is telling you to do, and this is one of my biggest complaints about the game so far.The puzzles and detective-like nature of this game are more frustrating and boring than they are scary or enjoyable. A major reason for this is the sanity system. Your sanity decreases so fast and so easily that you will find yourself a lot more focussed on keeping yourself from dying than solving puzzles. There were 5 instances in my experience where I had to look up what I was supposed to do because I got so annoyed and so bored of burning through my resources and dying because of sanity over and over again due to the ridiculousness that is the sanity system, which really ruined the immersion for me. I have nothing against puzzles in horror games no matter how hard they are as long as they're done correctly. It's when you put such an irritating and crucial obstacle in between me and the puzzle that I start to a have a problem.One thing I do like is how this game handles its scare factor. The atmosphere throughout this game both visually and auditory are captivating and kept me on the edge of my seat, dead silent, which I respect. This could have been THE scariest game I've played since Amnesia, but unfortunately the frustration over the complex puzzles and sanity system just ruined it for me. The enemies aren't too bad either. The only problem I have with them is that they're a bit too random. There isn't a single scripted encounter at all, which creates the possibility of not encountering them whatsoever. I don't expect only scripted encounters, but creating a nice balance between the two I think will make this game a lot more engaging and intense in certain areas.I could mention a few other criticisms I have, including the inventory system, lack of lighting, overuse of paranormal events and the tediousness of the first chapter. But many people have already mentioned these things and I just wanted to talk about what I liked and disliked most about Visage since my opinions on this game are very mixed.Since this IS an early access build, I think this game has potential to be a great atmospheric horror/puzzle game, the successor to P.T. everyone's been waiting for. I hope the developers will take what I and a lot of other people said into consideration to bring us an interesting second chapter. At the very least, make the game a lot less frustrating during the puzzle sequences, which essentially means the sanity system needs to be reworked IMO.At the moment this is a very "buy at your own risk" type of game. $25 for what is currently 2 hours (at most) of gameplay isn't very promising. I believe it has potential, though. I like the direction it is going and I respect the effort the devs are currently putting into it and how much they're paying attention to user feedback.Pros:Great atmosphere (both visual and sound wise)Concept handled wellGood use of subtlety and immersionUltimately, has the potential to be greatCons:Sanity System (everything to do with it)Puzzles too complex (which wouldn't be as big of a problem if it weren't for the first con)Mechanics are sloppy and all over the placeEnemies are way too infrequent and easy to avoid (can get underwhelming after a while)Not much content for chapter 1.For now I give it a 5.5/10. Though I wouldn't advise refraining from buying it due to my rating. A lot of people seem to really enjoy the game in its current state even with the majority of the game unreleased.

_childDocuments_.review: is a game a long time coming, it’s original announcement rising quickly off of the excitement surrounding ’s release, popularity, and Kojima’s subsequent falling out with Konami and the shuttering of the  title.  is a clear attempt at bringing that title’s meticulously crafted sights and scares to a wider market, while additionally building upon and expanding outside of the playable teaser’s short scope. Unfortunately, while  delivers in spooks and sights, it falls short in a department far more critical: gameplay design. At the time of release, I have experienced several issues pertaining to gameplay. The game often fails to provide sufficient audio and visual clues to indicate to the player where to progress or what to do, which can be fatal during chase sequences. Enemies that chase the player regularly spawn in areas you can’t effectively escape from, and occasionally insta-kill you through walls and other geometry. The “advanced” control option for doors that allow you to swing them open gradually with the mouse is far too underpowered, and will sometimes “slip” off the door as you attempt to drag it open. While the door controls can be changed in the options to a “simple” mode that will fully open the door by clicking on it, this removes a significant amount of interactivity that would otherwise contribute to the game’s atmosphere. The controls for manipulating examinable objects is additionally clumsy. Objects held in the character’s hands are actually physically modeled, meaning they can and do unintentionally get stuck on geometry and be pulled away from you. And I’m sure there are other minor issues that escape me at the time of writing. A shame, as this game genuinely does well in building atmosphere and setting scares. Sure, there are several occasions of simple jumpscares, but few ever feel cheap and are often bookended by crafted moments of drawn out dread and tension. Many of these scares owe their effectiveness to the excellent environmental, character, set piece, and audio design. The developers have come up with some effective and clever ways of putting players into situations they don’t want to be in. I just wish all of those were due to scary moments, rather than the rough gameplay. Ultimately, I would suggest those interested to wait a bit for more updates to be released before dropping full price on the title. The developers seem to be addressing major bugs and technical issues. With luck, they’ll tweak gameplay issues along with it. For those who can’t wait to see what the game has in store, perhaps consider watching a playthrough on YouTube. You’ll get many of the spooks without all of the frustration.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright I've finally beat the game. First of all, as an early access it is a great game, The game has many problems, bugs and things that could be improved and I'm pretty sure that they will be improved but overall it is a great experience. I was scared and tense most of the time, the atmosphere, the darkness, the noises, the breathing, everything contribute to make you feel uneasy and scared of everything and it makes your mind see things (I was scared of a freaking lamp Xd) There are I would say many jumpscares but they are well incorporated into the game and they are here for a reason, they are not randomly placed to be like Boo ! . The fact that you have the camera and that you have to use it to progress contribute to the jumpscares. You kinda expect the jumpscares to happen when you flash the camera but at the same time you don't. Btw the use of the camera to spawn these jumpscares is very clever honestly I loved it. Also the visuals in this game are really good.Alright now getting on the things that are bad and that could be improved I'll list what I didn't like. It's not meant to be like it's ♥♥♥♥ etcc cause I liked the game it's just to give my personal feedback on the game and maybe help the developers improve the game if they see this feedback - The fact that your character has no body and feels like you're controlling a floating head is horrible, especially since the game contains interactions that would be clearly better if you could see the body of your character (For example the interactions with the bath) You hear the sound of your character get in the bath but since you're a floating head it's kinda weird. Adding a body to the character that you could see could be nice (As in Outlast for example)- The fact that you have to click E and then drag the mouse in the direction you want could maybe be improved if the whole click and drag was done entirely with the mouse, like E could be the left button of the mouse or the right button. I had some trouble adapting to the use of the keyboard and then the mouse to interact with objects but it's fine- Light bulbs and candles felt like they were useless, at least for me I didn't need them to complete the game, maybe these two items could be improved so that they are more useful and nessecary to progress- The inventory system is just terrible and I think everyone would agree that it can be far more improved- Items that you carry around with you sometimes get stuck in doors, elements of the game as you walk- Items sometimes are just levitating in the air for no reason- Some choices that your character make during the game are just stupid, as an example I can take the bath interaction, when the bath was filled up why would you be like "oh great my bath is ready it sure is time for a good night bath despite the dark entities running around and all the paranormal events happening in my house" - Perhaps the pacing of the game could be improved, sometimes it's very obvious and I got lost just because I was an idiot but sometimes I feel like it could have be improved, for example the camera event, I had a hard time trying to make this event occur and it was just because I didn't look at a certain item of the house (The panda) That's all I can think of right now I'll edit the feedback if some things come back in my mind.Do I recommend this game though ? YES , totally ! If you're looking to be scared or even terrified you should definitely buy this game and enjoy playing this in complete darkness

_childDocuments_.review: Right off the bat, you can tell what sort of influences the developers had when Visage was made. A lot of people tend to think PT is the big inspiration here, but that's a bit of a stretch to me. Sure there's a few nods to it in map design and so forth. But I personally think Silent Hill 4 and Amnesia was the big source material here. The bulk of the game mostly consists of exploring the house and letting the enviroment tell the story. It's up to you, the player, to put two and two together to figure out what's going on in this unsettling house of yours. But tread lightly as something is in the house with you. Whatever it is, it sure as hell doesn't like you very much. This is where the sanity mechanic comes in. Witnessing strange events, standing in darkness for long periods of time, and just being in areas of frequent hauntings will drain your sanity. You will need to keep your nerves steady in order to proceed forward in the game. Getting too cracked will leave you vulnerable to danger and cause a game over. You can recover sanity by staying in well lit areas, moving away from hauntings, and taking your pills.  But keep in mind, paranormal events can and will happen anywhere you go.Ṉ̵̆̇̓o̷͎̿ẉ̴̖̈͜h̶̯̞͈͝e̵̮͋̔͆ŗ̵̠̰̍̒̒e̶̱͛̅ ̷̖̩̽́i̶̮̱̽̿͝ͅș̶͕͇̿͠͝ ̴͉͖̌͑̓s̶͉̈́̑a̵̼̫̜͂̕f̸̢͝e̸͈̦̝͒̏.̸͚̗̒.̵̢̯͂.̷̜̒̈́͗.̷̮̖̈́͊͝ͅ.̷̗̳͚̽̔.̴̧̤͖̍͒My only real gripes with the game is that the sound design could use tweaking.  It's unsettling and provides a creepy atmosphere, sure. But it can make the scares kinda predictable after a while. It also doesn't help that some scares are repeated a little too much. Too much repeatiton like with the clock scare can really just dull their effect. On top of this, it really can make scares confusing to know which are dangerous and which are not. And the music still plays regardless if you witness them or not. So if you walk into a room and a horror occurs in a certain spot that you're not looking. The music still plays even though you just missed out on the event entirely.  It's a bit of an atmosphere killer.  Also, some more signs of sanity status would be good. Like nervous breathing, twitchy movement, chattering teeth, irrational thoughts, etc. Anything to give a more clearer status of your mental health would add to the immersion and balence.  Some of the items could use some work. It really doesn't make sense to me that the player has to carry around several pill bottles at a time just to hold three pills. Why can't they just dump them into one pill bottle if they're the same medication? Also, candles could be better IMO. I never really saw much point in them as half the time a regular light source would do. They're not very bright and just jarring them even slighty puts them out. They're honestly more annoying to use than being useful. Also, the dynamic inventory system is the same in this regard. The controls could be better here. Accidentally throwing away items/storing them when trying to use them just gets annoying after a while. Also, there's no way to organize your items to make them easier to equip on your hotbar. This feature would be nice to have. But apart from some minor gripes. This is a pretty good concept we have here. A good little spooky romp perfect for Halloween.

_childDocuments_.review: NOTE: this game and review contains suicide.Let me say first of all this game is amazing and problems with the game are nit-picky at best besides one. I must warn you if you are thinking about purchasing this game, while it is a wild and terrifying experience, it does lack direction. If you have a difficult time putting things together, exploration, or finding your way through the complete lack of guidance then DO NOT BUY THE GAME. That aside, Visage is an easy 8.5-9/10. Before my PC got a huge upgrade I was rocking a 1060 with 8gbs RAM, The game looked amazing. After my upgrade the game had minor graphic changes and had reached the point where most shots from the game look damn near real. The games visuals were insane for that 1060 and with what I have now, It's still eye candy to look at. Everything looks absolutely beautiful besides two things. Chapter 2 or Dolores' chapter's main antagonist looks stiff and has odd details on the head. The other is a door in chapter 1. Again these are insanely nit-picky but I believe this goes to show the craftsman ship and pure artistry this game is. Those previously mentioned look fine but everything else in the environment looks extremely realistic.The gameplay for visage is fairly basic. You are given a problem or obstacle and you are tasked with finding something to overcome said obstacle. These obstacles typically have a simple way to solve them however, there are a couple circumstances that are poorly instructed as to how to solve them. I don't want to spoil the plot but I'm talking about a specific floor panel and a hammer. Also the "hints" they give in chapter 4 are either way too helpful or the exact opposite of helpful.Firstly I'll give a spoiler free plot and then go into details with spoilers as to why this game is remarkable story telling wise.Basically, in Visage you play as a man named Dwayne who, commits . Dwayne wakes up in his house and its his job to learn of 3 people who lost their lives in the house.For a critique on the game plot wise, everything below will be spoilers.Visage is simple with their spooks and its very effective. Visage does not go use too many jumpscares. jumpscares are a rarity in Visage. Visage uses subtle spooks, ones you can miss if you're not paying attention, most of them are spine chilling and Visage will abuse your memory in the coolest ways possible. Visage will introduce a sound to you as a signal that something cool is coming just to bring back that sound to indicate something totally sinister. I love this games horror, the game is an actual horror masterpiece. Overall. good game, buy now, get scared. :)

_childDocuments_.review: Let's start with the positive things: I really like the atmosphere, graphics and mystery. And I can honestly say: yes, the game is indeed scary. As a fan of horror games and movies, I thought that nothing would scare me and that this warning addresses only people not used to horror. It did not cause sleepless night, but it indeed contains some scenes that scared me.In the negative side, the developers made some design decisions that are annoying. I see that the game is on "exploring the environment", but more hints on what to do would be nice. Most of the time you just walk around, interact with everything and hope that something would happen. The story is hard to follow (paranormal events, etc), so one is basically left alone. This alone would be acceptable, but together with the fact that there are unnecessary hardships it gets annoying sometimes. These hardships can be summarized as follows: IT IS WAY TOO DARK (yes, horror games must be dark, but dark should not mean a completely black screen). You can use lighters and candles to get some light, but 1. candles are basically useless (cannot be used while walking), 2. lighters are very rare and they also have a very limited usage time. Also, you can carry only 5 items at a time, so sometimes you even have to leave helpful items behind. One very often runs out of light while trying to figure out what to do (and running out of light basically means death within seconds). Also light switches sometimes have to be pressed TWICE. I assumed that if the light is off then pressing the button turns it on, and if this does not work, then the light is broken. At some point I found out that pressing the button twice may help. If you don't know this, you might walk around in the darkness even more than necessary. And as if this was not hard enough, sometimes the very few light bulbs in the house get broken or the electricity fails (in which case you have to find the electric room in the dark basement to restart it). Even with a walkthrough guide, it is hard to master this game because ... you. don't. see. anything. This is not challenging, this is annoying. To summarize: devs should have added more lighters, increased their usage time, or make you able to walk with candles. So simple and would have been a great improvement.I was thinking for a while if I should suggest this game. Finally I did because the developers added clear warnings on exactly the points I did not like.

_childDocuments_.review: First and Foremost, what this game excels in is eerie atmosphere building. It's all Spook City here. The details of the scenery are well designed.Someone else had pointed out that the influences are too strong on the sleeve here. The beginning was an exact match to walking into the first door of P.T. . The monster's moans are very similar to that of P.T's as well.Being early access, faults are expected.- The handling controls between using the lighter and other objects felt a little clunky/difficult to navigate and use your items with fluidity in my opinion. - The paranormal events happen too frequently and fast. I wouldn't even notice it happened in my surrounding if it wasn't for the constant audio cue, which is overbearing from the event itself.- The sanity gauge is told to negatively affect you but the game doesn't punish you for it. I held myself in dark spaces after exploring to see the reaction yet was meet with nothing to show for. Past that, some phasing objects here and there but that's nothing I'd expect to see in the final cut. _childDocuments_.review: I love the heavy focus on investigation and exploration. Free-roaming in the house, outside of the main chapters, is surprisingly relaxing once you get a handle on the house's layout.  The resource management brings a few challenges but they can be avoided by staying near the light as often as possible. Progressing through the story felt very satisfying when I pieced together what I learned while exploring.Playing through the chapters, on the other hand, was very stressful. Each chapter brings different reasons to be terrified.  The overall art direction and audio mixing also helped Visage become a great achievement in horror.The story is pretty interesting, but I felt that it was a bit vague and open to interpretation on some details. I just wish that it was a bit more concrete, so I guess that's the one thing I found disappointing.  After finishing the game, I recommend reading some theories on Visage's story, and from there players can make their own conclusions.

_childDocuments_.review: Visage is not quite there yet. It carries the burden of succeding to games like Observer and Soma, both of which handle narrative design, quest structure and overall fear factor with much more subtlety. Very mild spoilers ahead, but you might continue reading if you're planning to play Visage from start to finish.Visage's narrative design is a mixed bag. It really wants to be this deep dive inside the daily sufferings of troubled minds but can sometimes feel heavy handed -in a "bruh, schizophrenia" kind of way. However I ended up really invested in the different chapters, and the game is clearly empathetic towards its characters, which is a nice touch. "Rakan" is my favorite.The quest structure is shoddy. The fact that the game heavily relies on clues (both comitting suicide in the basement and watching tapes on the TV will point you to the next task) is a confession that the developpers haven't really thought out how to build proper puzzles. The "Aha" moments are more "sh!t, seriously ?" moments, and it can get tiring to shuffle through the house looking for one particular item to progress. Kudos to the portrait room in Dolores's chapter where I had to turn up the gamma just to see the room at the end of the corridor.The fear factor is by far what Visage does best, with a sanity meter that threw me back to Eternal Darkness on the Game Cube. This, and the light and dark system kept me on my toes all along. However, apart from the "Lucy" chapter, you'll quickly (hopefully) devise strategies to avoid death. The best part of the game was getting familiar with the house's layout to have fall-back plans.As it is, I see Visage as a foundation for a more polished and refined game, but overall it's still a jarring experience if you're hardcore into horror walking sims. Oh, and it's pack full with Silent Hill easter eggs.

_childDocuments_.review: Visage is a very good horror game. I really enjoyed it! It was one of the scariest games I've played in a while. The story isn't something you can figure out from the start, you need to search and find things that relate to each chapter and Dwayne. I'm gonna start with Lucy's chapter: It was a good chapter for the first one. The chapter had a really nice atmosphere and many jumpscares but in my opinion was the worst between the 3. Dolores' chapter: This was a very very good one. The atmosphere was just insane, Dolores can kill you anywhere. The only thing I didn't really like was the puzzles wich were pretty hard. The story in this chapter was the best out of all. Rakan's chapter: This one was my favorite. It started strong with jumpscares, then you go into the hospital wich was a very scary place and then at the end it became a pretty repetitive chapter but it was still the scariest in my opinion. And then the final chapter is about Dwayne. What I understood is that Dwayne was working in the water plant from the affliction tape. His job was to poison the water and that is how Lucy and Dolores died. And then when Rakan came into the house he was an agent and he was the one that spied Rakan and locked him in the cell. And then Lewis was another resident of the Visage house but we do not have a chapter about him. He found out what Dwayne is doing and Dwayne killed Lewis. And then when Dwayne moved into the house the factory was closed. He had the guilt of killing the four and he started drinking alcohol and drugging himself. Then, because of the guilt he killed himself and his family. When you play through the 3 chapters ( Lucy, Dolores and Rakan ), he was a ghost, that's why he didn't have a reflection in mirrors and we didn't see his hands. So the family reunion ending is about Dwayne joining his family in heaven even after what he's done. The purpose of the 3 chapters was for Dwayne to feel the pain of his victims ( Lucy, Dolores and Rakan ) and then he could go in heaven along with his family.

_childDocuments_.review: Review as of Oct 27, 2018.One of the best horror games i've played. The only other horror game I can say I truly enjoyed is Amnesia The Dark Descent. However, Visage is early access at the moment so you'll run into some doors and other parts that will remind you that the content is not available yet. But for the review of it's current status: Visage is one of the best horror games of this year. There aren't many any jump-scares at all compared to a lot of other horror games. As of now, the only jump-scares are when the it/she catches you, but because of the trial-and-error nature of the game, dying is normal, and you'll get used it to it to advance in the story. But that's what makes the game good, it's not built on the premise of jump-scares like a lot of the current horror games are. It's built on a creepy, slow-built, psychological horror that leaves you saying "oh ♥♥♥♥."The story is actually pretty good, maybe typical (movie like story) but good nonetheless. Visage is dark and eerie, slow-built and random. _childDocuments_.review: It saddens me that this game comes so close to hitting the mark, yet it runs so poorly. This is one of the most bug ridden games I've played, worse than old bethesda (equal or better than new bethesda). My pc is equipped with a gtx 1070 and an i5-4590. I know that the cpu is pretty outdated, but this is enough to get about 60+ frames in GTA V and Witcher 3 on Ultra at 1080p. Visage is a good looking game, but it should be nowhere near as hard to run as GTA or Witcher. Just walking around the house my framerates are stuttery, occasionally being stable only for performance to drop back down to garbage. There are many audio errors. I often encounter a bug in which music will be playing, and when I'm walking instead of playing the footstep sound it will just cut off all audio. Every. Single. Step. Also some weird balancing at points, like the shotgun easter egg is disproportionately louder than the entire rest of the game. By far the worst issues I have with this game are the rendering problems. Falling out of the map is something I can forgive happen one or two times in a game. Not everything works out 100% of the time. But in this game, if you aren't aware of the signs that part of the map isn't loaded (the lighting in this game is very inconsistent, sometimes areas that are usually well lit end up pitch black even though the lights are on) you could be walking right of the edge of the loaded map and into the abyss below to die of insanity (in game and irl). A bug like this should NOT be in a game. I don't see any excuse as to why a fully released game that costs $35 can be such a mess. Horror games can't be like skyrim where the bugs are a charm and occasionally funny. Horror games need to be polished to all hell or you risk breaking your players immersion, ruining any scares they could experience, and thus failing as a horror game. There really are great elements here. The level design is very visually appealing, and unnerving (when it loads), the random ghost attacks are a great way to keep the player on their toes (although idk why you lose the ability to run in the ONLY situation where you want to run). tl;dr 3/10 until they fix the god awful bugs, once they do then it's a solid 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Visage is one of the scariest horror games ever on flat screen. To find similar sensations my mind has to go back to Alien: Isolation! I specified flat screen because, talking just of fear, it cannot compete with VR horror games like RE7 or Paranormal Activity. VR adds an extra dimension to horror! I hope developers are working on the VR version! The best feature of Visage is the lore, so tense and deep, like in the ghost story of the Lucy's chapter. You feel really immersed in the scary house thanks to AAA graphics, audio and state-of-the-art illumination. I loved the main mechanic of avoiding the dark by turning on lights and candles.  The sequences in the house are clearly inispired by P.T., but Visage is more than that, you explore several locations and play in the shoes of different characters. Luckily it's not an action horror, forget RE or Dead Space. And it's not based just on jump scares. It's a psychological horror, fear comes from insane sutations and extremely thrilling atmosphere. However Visage comes with some defects. The inventory management is a pain in the ass, I cannot understand why developers have not implemented smarter solutions. Puzzles are boring; you have to find too many items and they are too much hidden. You have to go up and down the house countless times; sometimes you don't know what to do and end up consulting youtube. Puzzles interrupt the lore, the immersion, they distract you from the story. The latter on paper is interesting and original, but storytelling is disappointing. Story is splitted in four chapters apparently disconnected. The excessive focus on puzzles leaves the story in the periphery, on the background. In the end you don't understand what you played! You can guess something, get a vague idea, but not the whole story! Again you have to google the web for finding explanations! And explanations are not satisfying! In conclusion I suggest the game to horror fans because of the incredible graphics, audio, illumination, lore, making it one of the scariest flat games ever. However it is far from perfect because of silly inventory management, too hard and boring puzzles destroying the lore, interesting story marred by disappointing storytelling.

_childDocuments_.review: Before starting the game you should know that it is advisable to play the game in the dark with the sound at a good audible volume. *wink wink*Visage is divided into 4 chapters, which together can take more than 20 hours.These are a nice number of dark evenings that you can fill with the jump scares that the game has to offer.Often you will do it with little or no clue's until you find a clue while searching or spontaneously, so that you can work in a more focused way and know where to go or what to do.The house where Visage is set is also very large and contains many rooms, it is therefore important to keep a map in your head so that you do not keep going in the wrong direction.Also always look out for candles, you often find them in numbers but often they are also scarce and it takes a while to find, also be careful that when you use a candle that this candle is lit in a useful location.While you shouldn't waste enlightenment, longer periods spent in the dark can trigger fear and the paranormal.To prevent this you need to find pills, these pills you can take when the tension gets too strong so that you always keep both feet on the ground when you wander through dark corridors or rooms.What is also very useful are the double controls, by this I mean that you can use both your left and right hand to hold two items, both items can then be used without having to go into your inventory to change items .This may cause confusion at first, but as you use these dual controls more often it will become automatic.I found it very helpful to walk around with a lighter and a jar of pills in both hands.Before starting the game myself I read quite a bit about 'Visage' and also heard about it from a friend who was very actively playing on it.My current experience has certainly shown me that these rumors are not exaggerated and that there is something to be expected further in the game.This makes me very curious to experience terrifying scenes through, for example, virtual reality.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to preface this right now: this game is getting a positive recommendation, but I'm going to have a lot of criticisms. Ultimately, this game is tantalizingly close to brilliance, and so its shortcomings become all the more sharp. It makes some big errors, but ultimately I would tell you: if you want a scary and good horror game, this is that. It's exactly what you want from a horror title and a genuine step above the common chaff. So then, with that being said...This game's ending sucks eggs. And that's not the only problem. (Some spoilers BELOW)Some more pros first: the atmosphere is absolutely stellar. The concept of a haunted house is well demonstrated here, and I love the way they take advantage of the space. I like the concept of the Sanity meter and I like how it serves to make any and all progression potentially threatening. I do think this creates an arbitrary element to the difficulty, sadly -- a trope of modern horror games that this one doesn't seem to shake. Sometimes enemy spawns just straight up kill me, other times I'm faced with an adventure-game like scenario of having to find the correct spot to go to or else die. This becomes more common towards the "end" of the game, though since you can play the chapters in any order, the "end" may be very different for you.Either way, in terms of being "a scary game" this is an A+. Absolutely terrifying, the way they build tension, the way they ensure that a "scare" in-game has negative consequences on a mechanical sense, this is all great. Graphics are really good as well. I do think the game suffers for being way too obtuse -- a little more guidance or a means of finding out where you need to go would be great. Why not have the Compass point me towards quest items that I haven't collected, or help locate collectibles? Why is the camera useless outside of Lucy's chapter?I see so much potential to build upon for a prospective sequel. The chapter tools could have been used to unlock whole sections of the house. The house should have had multiple house layouts as well -- I enjoy the use of the static space, but you can tell that the development was maybe struggling to find new ways to remix it. Delores' chapter has the best in that regard, with the mirrors transmuting the space and you needing a key item to unlock them. Having new mirrors spawn after that chapter that'd create new pathways in the house would have been cool.This could almost have been a sort of horror Metroidvania, but sadly its structure kneecaps its own tension-building. Each chapter can be done in any order and you're locked into the chapters you choose. Each chapter has its own enemy ghost, though two of them largely function the same way and one is largely part of scripted chases. The distinctions and similarities are kind of moot, these Chapters form the bulk of the game's actual gameplay and they are wholly self-contained. The items you gain from them have very, very little use outside of them.So "outside" the chapters is the secret "fourth chapter", where you uncover the protagonist's backstory that led to the traumatic incident the game's start. For how much effort is put into this, this is the part of the story that feels the least fleshed out. For one, most everything is communicated in vague metaphors. This allows some very interesting interpretations of the plot, but it means for most of the game, you're just gonna be confusedly wandering from one set piece to another, one creepy cutscene to the next.I had a hard time feeling sympathetic for the main character and it's hard to see him as a blank slate when he most clearly isn't, yet the game tries to treat him like one. The way the game handles the main character is very odd -- it reminds me strongly of the Seventh Guest, an old PC adventure game. The way the camera moves and the overall tone is actually pretty similar to that game as well. The story fails to resolve any of the supernatural mysteries. There's so much left unexplained you could write whole novels of subjective interpretation and probably be just as valid based on the evidence as anyone else. If you are playing hoping for some payoff at the end, don't. The payoff is lame. Play it for the experience the tension and the great creeping dread. There's some beautiful scenes of horror and misery, there's some great scares and some fantastic tension. I just wish, dearly, that this game could have delivered better on tying it all together. The plot is the weakest part and I feel like this will severely hurt my willingness to replay it.It's definitely a game where you'll get the most out of it in your first playthrough. The majority of your playtime and the danger you'll face comes from wandering around in search of the next puzzle to solve. My playtime reflects a single playthrough with only minimal outside help sought. There is a LOT of head scratching puzzles to solve here. The game also generally just declines in quality towards its end. The non-early-access chapter is the weakest of the three by far. It is basically Alone in the Dark without the combat; but it's quite good. Silent Hill has a worthy up-and-comer to challenge it, and the work and effort in this game is worth your time and money. Just, don't expect much replay value.I will say, as well -- I wish there was more you could do to interact with the enemies in this game. Unlike Alien : Isolation, there's really not a lot you can do but run and take advantage of the weaknesses of the AI in order to evade threats -- most of the time you just leave the area until an enemy despawns and then continue whatever it was you were doing. But there's very little you can do to impact the enemies, and that's a real shame. For the record, I never once had to use a light bulb to fix a light fixture. Not once. I don't know if it's random or what, but the a.i. never broke a single light bulb. Take of that what you will.

_childDocuments_.review: While not without serious caveats and some disappointing inconsistencies, the bottom line remains that in spite of some of its shortcomings, I will remember Visage as one of the scariest games I have played up to this point in my life.To open with a major criticism, one of the first things you'll notice and begin hating immediately, is that cursed inventory system, which somehow went through years of early access without being axed in its entirety. You have separate buttons for left hand, right hand, 5 "dynamic" inventory slots, a "key item" inventory, a magical cupboard where some key items respawn, some items that require the use of both hands, forcing you to drop something li,e a box of pills to use, and it's just chaos. I genuinely want to have a conversation with whoever designed this, because it's one of the worst aspects of the game, and it could have SO EASILY been avoided if they just implement something as basic as let's say Amnesia 1's inventory system. The game's greatest strength is, without a doubt, the utterly masterful tension building. Through dark subject matter, sound design, ominous music, pitch-perfect lighting, quick glimpses of something scurrying away under the bed, nerve-shredding extended periods of quiet followed by balls-to-the-wall jumpscares (the good kind), the game manages to generate a sense of paranoia and evil unlike anything else I've played. You could have lit a match on my arm from the goosebumps I had almost constantly, and I really, really missed this feeling in a game for a long time. That said, a few of the chapters do a better job at maintaining momentum, so some words about those:-Lucy's is probably my favourite. Perfect buildup, perfect balance of hand-holding and direction, panic-inducing monster encounters, and some very creative set-pieces. Having to use the camera's flash in pitch black to navigate, reveal certain things  led to some of the game's most visceral scares, and including it was a stroke of pure genius. 10/10-Dolores's chapter has the creepiest opening ever, furthermore this chapter has the most oppressive atmosphere, with the nastiest, subtlest scares that really get under your skin. Overall though, it's also a slightly frustrating chapter to finish, as after the opening sequence is over you lose all sense of direction and are forced to work your way through a series of obscure puzzles that have a preferred sequence that the game does not communicate whatsoever, so you end up backtracking 50 times trying to remember where you might have seen what you think you might need in that other place you've already forgotten the location of. It's also here that the game's obsession with pixel-hunting begins to take its toll, with some key objects taking literal hours to find  .- Rakan's chapter is perhaps the most "mainstream". By far the most linear, with very obvious puzzle solutions, it basically plays like Outlast. Not a bad thing at all, it was kind of a relief after the previous chapter's aimlessness, although perhaps the tension isn't as intense as in the other chapters , although some very creepy imagery in the latter half manages to stick out.- The game's closing hours are unfortunately the most underwhelming. While having some good moments sprinkled throughout, it's lacking in scares compared to what came before, and the level of pixel-hunting honestly puts 90's adventure games to shame, destroying any semblance of pacing, and turning the proceedings into a hidden-object game that has no place in here. It could have worked if you were at least a little bit guided, but that's not the case, and I have no guilt admitting that I used a walk-through to progress the plot. For one thing, some objects you need appear in places that you ALREADY LOOKED before in the game, like cupboards and certain drawers, and you have no reason to assume anything reappeared in these places, leading to just chunks of wasted time and loss of momentum. Really silly mistake.Despite going out with a whimper, what came before is still so memorable and powerfully scary - the fundamental goal of any horror - that you will forgive these considerable shortcomings. It's also good value for money, it took me 18 hours to beat, even if at least a handful of those were spent a bit annoyed.

_childDocuments_.review: I’m forever chasing the high that few games other than the Outlast series and Resident Evil 7 have given me when it comes to horror. I’m always optimistic and often disappointed by what’s out there, though every once in a while I come across something that’s at least not a complete waste of time. A title that offers some enjoyment and even an occasionally legitimate horror atmosphere that keeps me pushing through to see what’s next. Visage falls into this category, and although it doesn’t quite hit all of the marks that I was hoping for based on its price and Steam reviews, I will say that it satisfied me enough that I wasn’t dozing off an hour in.The house that you spend most of your time in during Visage is not a pleasant one. Even when everything is relatively low-key, lights will flicker and go off, radios will pop on, and doors will slam around you. When the house has started to take its toll on your sanity, you’ll experience much, much worse. Four chapters detail the stories of the unfortunate souls who have lived (and died) here in the past. Each of them has its own theme that stands out from the others with puzzles and game mechanics that are different enough from the others that they keep the experience from becoming stale. As a matter of fact, I would even say that most of them are grade-A horror if you were basing it solely on the narrative and terror-inducing atmosphere. On a less fortunate note, the quality among the chapters varies wildly.By chance, I ended up doing Rakan’s chapter before the others, though most seem to agree that it should be done last. The story was fairly bland as it involved a rugby player who was out on an injury that suffered from extreme scopophobia, a fear of being stared at. Although it’s nice to see that this character was worked into the game due to them being a backer who’s similar to the character involved, this chapter truly feels like it was forced in without the same level of passion and skill as the others. By the time I’d reached the end of his story, I was concerned about whether or not Visage was for me.I decided to press on and see if the rest of the game was as dull and I was pleased to discover that it wasn’t. That’s not to say it was a masterpiece, there were plenty of flaws that I’ll dive into in the next section, but I played Lucy’s chapter next and found it to be worth the wait. Lucy is a young girl who you quickly learn had an ‘imaginary friend’ that she had bonded with. This friend was important to her, but as time went on, it began to become increasingly dominant leading to plenty of terrible events to follow. As opposed to Rakan’s chapter, Lucy’s was marred only by the rough-around-the-edges gameplay that seemed to not really know which sub-genre it belonged to, the primary flaw of this title overall.Visage builds tension and atmosphere better than most horror titles that I have played and I can say that with full confidence that most fans of the genre would agree with me. The house is big and creepy, the locations that you visit outside of it keep you on your toes, and the stories of those who came before are well-written and keep you wanting more. What frequently gets in the way is the gameplay though. Well, that and the Rakan chapter…You’re informed that Visage is a difficult game from early on and this is accurate. You’re likely to die plenty of times from start to finish, though being chased by the entity of the chapter isn’t particularly exciting. There’s no way to hide, you simply run away until they disappear or they catch and murder you in an animation that loses its luster and takes up way too much of your time after you’ve seen it the first time. The scripted encounter sequences tend to do their job admirably, but the random appearances get old quickly. Puzzles are the name of the game here and I can’t even count how many times I was interrupted and chased around as I was trying to figure out what I was supposed to be doing next. You’ll likely find yourself forgetting about the excellent atmosphere often as your awe and suspense are replaced by frustration. At least the auto-saves are placed in convenient locations, for the most part.An equally irritating flaw comes in the form of the inventory system. While I’m certainly not expecting to have my mind blown by a walking simulator-ish horror adventure, this one really took the cake for being a pain. Just about any time you’re going to use an item, you need to navigate through an inventory window while the world around you continues. I consider myself lucky that this didn’t kill me far more often than it did, though I’m under the assumption that others won’t have such luck and will become increasingly frustrated with it. I’m unsure whether it was the intent to have the feeling of digging through your pack while danger is closing in on you, but it was more of an irritation than an atmosphere builder.Visage is one of the better horror titles that I’ve gotten my hands on lately, though it’s far from perfect due to several notable flaws. An excellent setting with a flawed chapter is forgivable enough, but a horror game that loses its thrill by consistently killing the player is inferior to one that forces them through near-death experiences due to the simple fact that the segment is no longer new or frightening, but exactly what you’ve already seen. Others manage to strike a strong balance here by offering additional action and stealth mechanics that allow for these close calls, though Visage does nothing of the sort, forcing the player through events that require them to escape but without giving them any of the more fun and creative methods of doing so.At the end of the day, Visage is a solid enough horror title that shows its PT inspiration, but it falls short of becoming an instant classic. I’d recommend it to horror fans who are looking for a new challenge and interesting setting to explore, though I can’t help but think that it would’ve been a significant improvement if it had leaned more into its excellent atmosphere and story more and its running sequences less.

_childDocuments_.review: Aight, just played through the game...and its extremely hard to say if i recommend it or not.It really depends on the player.The good things first.The horror is as good as people praise it to be, its very well done. Jumpscares are there but theyre not too excessive and the atmosphere is astoundingly creepy. Good visuals support the atmosphere and generally the feel of the game quite a bit. The story isnt bad either, its very interesting and involves mental illness, addiction etc. and is pleasant to puzzle together and experienceNow to the bad Part:If you love finding little secrets, that are partly extremely well hidden with little to no proper indication, this game will be a treasure trove for you.If not, everything will just start falling apartThe outstanding horror is overshadowed by the sheer "complexity" of the game, to call it nicely.Progress has to be made by obtaining different items, interacting with different objects or generally through triggering events which can vary from picking up a clearly visible key, to something as stupid as looking at a seemingly decorative stain at a ceiling and clicking on it. This wouldnt nearly be so annoying if the "house" wasnt an entire palace.There are so many different rooms filled with so many decorative and inspectable items, that  searching for important stuff becomes extremely frustrating and time consuming.I needed to look up guides at least 5 times throughout this entire playthrough and would probably have needed multiple more, if i wasnt just lucky at times and found what i needed by randomly clicking things.And lastly the inventory system.What the hell were they thinking?You get used to it but its very unintuitive and annoying to deal with at first.Which doesnt help is the fact that the character doesnt have arms or a body, which firstly takes a massive amount of the immersion out of the game, especially in cutscenes and secondly, items in your "hands" are just "free floating". Something like a lighter can just get stuck on an object that you passed and fly into your face again after some distance, which jumpscared me multiple times.Additionally to that, in this game you get chased quite a lot.These chases are random at some points of the game, which will lead to you dying because the chase started a centimeter next to you and you just couldnt get away in time.Also, i dont think the "stress system" was a good implementation.Its more of pain to deal with because in most circumstances, when you need to explore in the dark, your stress meter goes up and you have to return to a light source to regain sanity (not every *visual* light source counts btw) . This added nothing to the gameplay besides being another frustrating nuisance.Which lastly brings me to the "random paranormal events" around the house.I really liked those at first, they kept me on my toes and scared me from time to time. The problem being, after a while it was just the same thing over and over and over again, bringing your sanity down and slowing your progression because you had to sit in the light for half a minute until your sanity is recovered again.TLDRIn conclusion id say that the horror and the atmosphere, as well as the story and graphics are amazing and very captivating. The "game" part of it is just sadly all around terrible, with a clunky and unrefined inventory and stress system, very directionless tasks with little to no indication at some points, in a gigantic house, with repetetive  random events or unforgiving chases, which slow you down or even kill you because of bad implementation etc etc etc which overall just makes the "game" more of a chore than an engaging experience, especially for the pricetag. If you dont believe me that this game is frustrating, look at the games achievement statistic with only 10-15% of the players having completed the endgame.IMO this would make a better movie than an actual game but maybe im just stupid.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, this is definitely one of my favorite horror games. I took my time to finish it and streamed all the way. It was a fantastic experience. I liked that each chapter had a completely new dynamic to it and it required different skills, modus operandi and basically scared you in a different way (if you are afraid of the dark you're going to hate/love chapter 2). It has you on the edge all the time but doesn't really go overboard with jumpscares. It is very atmospheric and has some of the creepiest moments I've seen in a game that doesn't involve anything "sudden".It is a hard game. You will wander around not know what to do a few times for sure. In Dolores chapter there are so many things to do and since you can find them in a non-linear way you may be wondering what an object is for an hour before you actually get to the place you actually need it. It does feel very rewarding when you finally piece everything together.The game isn't one without issues and I could say the controls are kind clunky, you have to manage each hand separately so expect to misuse or drop items you didn't intend for the first couple ours. Hopefully it clicks like it did for me at some point and you can leave that nuisance behind. Also there are some parts that are better written and managed than others so I wouldn't call it stellar in that regard but good enough. I kind of didn't enjoy Chapter 3 as much since it has a lot of chases and to me that feels a bit cheap after hours of atmospheric horror. I never want to feel like I'm playing Outlast in a horror game (I just don't enjoy those kinds of games), but I'm sure that will be a pro, for some.Also, if you don't respect the game rules about sanity you WILL have a very bad time, because then it becomes a jumpscare/chase simulator. I think this is a good thing because it prevents you to just run mindlessly through the house without thought and makes you stop to think and feel the atmosphere but It can get frustrating, specially at the beginning.Overall I'm happy this finally released. I thought it wouldn't, but it did, and what a pleasant surprise.

_childDocuments_.review: I give it a thumbs up because it is a unique experience. However, there is a lot to be desired as far as quality of life improvements. First, the key mapping is bad. When you first start up the game, don't change the Zoom bind off of "V" or else you break it, and make sure you have your key binds exactly the way you want them because once you start the game, trying to rebind keys later mid game because something didn't feel right (like Run/Crouch) wont work. You will have to find the Visage File in the Appdata file location, delete it, then start up again and try once more. Also, deleting that file, the only work around I found, also resets all other options settings... So, redo Graphics, Audio, such and such each time.Making your way through the game is not very intuitive. You're not going to Sherlock Holmes your way through, you're going to Happy Accidents you're way. Just about everything can be interacted with and there is nothing to distinguish between whether those environmental items are important or not to completing a task. You will literally walk around for hours until you accidentally solve something. The Dolores chapter is THE WORST when it comes to this. . It kind of feels like tasks were designed by a team so thoroughly familiar with the house and every nook and cranny details that they forgot to think, "Oh wait, only we have this level of insight of where everything is and what to do to complete these tasks... the average player wont know what we know, we should probably tone it down." lolHaving said that, I know it sounds like a negative review, I still recommend playing... but it's going to be painful... but the experience, story, and just overall visuals throughout the game are really good. There's just so much they can do with QoL that would make it a superb game. It is legitimately scary and anxiety inducing. If you like Psychological horror, you wont be disappointed. You just have to grit through the painful mission mechanics.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, this is not a 60 hour game. The devs deleted saves moving out of early access so I played half the game twice and I've left the game running paused quite a lot. Depending how you play you might get 10-30 hours out oft his game on your first run.But is it worth it? Personally, I think yes. The graphics, audio and atmosphere are all superb. The chapters are varied and interesting, although the early access chapters were the best IMO, both for level design and scariness. This isn't a fast paced, run and gun horror game, instead being very psychological and slow (even the sprint button only gets you to a fast walk in most situations) but it does what it does amazingly well: Delores' chapter would send me into waves of goosebumps throughout, (even on my second playthrough), and there were plenty of occasions in Lucy's chapter where i almost woke the house up at 2am screaming. Rakan's chapter was more stressful than scary.Each chapter has its own self contained story, with the fourth chapter wrapping things up for the protagonist.  Once again it was Delores and Lucy's chapters that shine through and although there are multiple endings, .There also seem to be some optimisation issues too, as even running a Ryzen 7 3800x and RTX 2080ti, I had semi-frequent frame rate drops and there's 3 places that should be permanently lit where the lighting would pop or bleed in from the surrounding areas as you passed through them.All in all though, I'd give this game a solid 8/10. It could have done with some better planning for the endgame and a little more polish, but it's a great effort from a new developer and I honestly haven't had a game effect me like this since playing the original Silent Hill at 13 in the middle of the night almost 20 years ago, and that in itself is an achievement.
