_childDocuments_.review: Let me start by saying I really wanted to enjoy this game. I love horror games, walking sims, and games that make me feel feelings. I tend to really get invested in games like this and really relate to the protagonist, feeling those emotions the main character feels. I mean, I full on ugly cried playing Hellblade because of the voices, the scenery and the pure anguish Senua feels, so I felt the awe of the surroundings, the sadness and pain, and the fear of not being adequate enough. I struggled trying to decide whether to recommend the game or not. And while I can see the appeal for other people, I ultimately decided that after full completing the game  couldn't recommend it.I went into the game blind, only knowing that it was supposed to be very scary, so I was excited for my heart to race and to feel the overwhelming sense of dread that everyone else felt. Unfortunately, I didn't get that from this game at all. There were maybe one or two moments where a jump scare got to me or something unexpected happened , but for the most part I think the game left me feeling indifferent to what was happening. The game opens with a strong shock factor intro that definitely left me feeling unsettled. However, the intro left me no connection to our protagonist Dwayne. I struggled to be immersed in a story that seemed like it offered little more than the shocking opening. I think it pulled me out of the scenario and left me more confused as I progressed through the house. I liked how the random noises, the doors slamming, the breathing that felt like it was right behind you, and the music were well placed and definitely added to the ambiance and feelings of uneasiness, but I still struggled to be fully immersed and feel genuine fear or dread.There just seemed to be a lot of things that pulled me out of the game atmosphere. The death animations felt long. In a game that doesn't hold your hand, but swiftly punishes you if you make a wrong move, having to sit through those long death animations felt like a chore more than a scare. I don't mind trial and error! You do a lot of it in the game and I can see the merit in doing so. The game also provides so many hints as to what you're doing next. However, there were a few times where I just didn't hit the progress point fast enough and I was instakilled by one of the chapter enemies with what felt like little warning. It was especially frustrating when it felt like the rules were constantly changing. For example  Perhaps this was a tactic to keep me on my toes, but more than once I screamed "WHAT DO YOU WANT FROM ME!" at the screen. There were also many times where I turned a wrong corner or wedged myself in between objects in the environment and getting stuck where I just had to watch the enemy of the hour just approach me. I feel like I should have been screaming with fear as the enemy approached. Instead I was left with the feeling of "please just kill me so I can go back and figure out what you actually want me to do". There were also scene that felt like they took so long that it took me out of the game and just left me wishing for it to end. . I guess the pacing of those scenes, coupled with the pacing of the game really yanked me out of the immersion. The sanity meter was also a little vague and hard to understand. Coupled with confusion about what was and was not considered a light source, it was not an easy thing to manage. Unless the game told me my sanity was too low, I had trouble grasping what red splash but no brain, red splash with visible brain, no red but visible brain, and visible brain but suddenly no brain even meant. It seemed when taking pills, the brain wouldn't go away, but standing next to a lamp in the TV room the brain disappears? Standing next to a lit wall sconce the game would tell me to "stay out of darkness", but next a static-y TV the light is okay? It just further hindered my ability to immerse myself in the game. The episodic chapters, while interesting in and of themselves, felt disjointed and very separate parts instead of a complete piece. I was left confused as to why I should care about what Dwayne is going through or how it relates together. And yes, if you uncover the tidbits scattered in the house, you can somewhat piece together how everything is related, but it's also still vague. I think that leaving this up for interpretation can be a great storytelling tool if used right. However, with this game it just made the game feel like for every chunk I was given, another chunk was purposely left out, leaving me without anything whole or cohesive. Rakan's chapter felt especially out of place, taking place mostly in the hospital instead of the house. I had high hopes for his chapter with the way it started. It seemed like it would relate to other chapters, but my hopes were quickly dashed when the games moved primarily to the hospital setting. I did enjoy the final "chapter" or Dwayne's story with the tapes. It was an interesting way of uncovering more and making me feel anything about him. I also enjoyed that I could explore those things throughout the game, instead of just all at the end. However it felt like too little, too late for me to ever form that connect to him. I think the endings left me the most upset. The "good" ending felt out of place.  The "bad" ending made a little more sense, I suppose. The game was also kind of buggy for me. There was one part in Lucy's chapter where I somehow got warped into her bedroom closet when the closet wasn't there. I couldn't get out and had to wait for the sanity meter to completely deplete and then wait some more before Lucy came through a wall to present me with my demise. I also had items in my hand clipping through the walls and disappearing. This was especially annoying in Dolores' chapter because I had to constantly go back to the storage room for items that bugged out and disappeared. Overall, did I find parts of the game enjoyable? Yes. Do I think it lived up to the hype as a super scary first person horror game? No, not at all. And as a whole, it felt like the bad outweighed the good. While I understand that my opinion completely differs from the norm, I felt like I should offer a different perspective and I tried to express my feelings as to why the best I could.

_childDocuments_.review: This is easily one of, if not the best horror game I've ever played. The atmosphere is perfect, the scares are genuinely freaky, and for the first time in years I felt afraid to keep playing a game. Speaking of scares, something I absolutely love this game for is the fact that it doesn't rely on cheap jumpscares to get a reaction from you like so many other modern horror games and movies like to do. The horror is genuine, and it makes you dread turning that light switch back on or opening the ominous-looking door just ahead. The game's mechanics are simple enough to understand as well, and while the story is somewhat vague, that's actually a good thing because it leaves a lot of room for interpretation. It reminds me of a good ARG in that there's a great story present but not every question is answered, not every loose end is tied up, and enough mystery is still present at the end that it keeps you thinking about the game long after you've beaten it. My only complaint is that Visage can be rather vague about what it wants you to accomplish. You'll often find yourself wandering around an area trying to figure out what key goes in which door or where exactly you're supposed to go next, but that can be forgiven when the rest of the game is as perfect as it is.Visage is an excellent game and an amazing horror experience. If you're a fan of the genre, make sure to check this one out.

I also want it to be known while I say others should play this game does not mean it even comes close to a perfect game.So 8 hours to complete the full game.  Only twice did I give in and look at guides.  first time was to figure out the picture frame puzzle and the second was the last tape.  both in the final chapter. _childDocuments_.review: I've played literally every horror game I could get my hands on, and lemme just say, Visage is possibly one of the scariest ones I have ever played. Not enough horror games can build up dread the way this one does. The atmosphere itself feels very realistic and creepy, very immersive. Ghostly events like lights going off, doors opening or closing, footsteps, ghoulish sounds, ghosts following you around, etc offer a diverse unpredictable set of scares to keep you always on edge. The environmental storytelling is both its greatest strength and possibly its biggest weakness, and it can be difficult to figure out how to progress a storyline. You have to really look closely at your surroundings, as you start to see patterns that push you in the right direction. For any horror fan, this is a MUST play!

_childDocuments_.review: Update: Tried really hard to gather courage and actually played through the first chapter. Game IS scary, atmosphere is phenomenal. This game has a little bit of everything that may scare you. Are you afraid of the dark? Of the unknown? Of being stalked and followed both by things you can and can't see? Maybe you're scared of narrow spaces. Or scared of wide open areas. Scared of not knowing where or who you are. Maybe you're like me and loneliness is terrifying. This game has a little bit of all of those and more. Do be careful if you suffer from deep trauma, mental or cardiac illness, and stop playing if it's too much. The game will be waiting, and it won't punish you for it.I will preface this by stating that I haven't played more than a few minutes for reasons I'll explain below. My opinion on the game might change after I man up and play more, but so far first impressions are a resounding 500 out of 10. The atmosphere and mood set by the game are downright terrifying starting with the subtle and eerie sounds of both an empty, quiet house and things that go bump in the night, all the way through an intro cutscene so tense and chilling that you can't help gagging and wanting to run away to spare your eyes from the evil developing right in front of you. But Visage didn't let me look away. It gripped me and went "you're going to witness darkness and gaze deep into it with no way to escape".I'm not really into spooky stuff, since it's never done anything even close to making me feel uneasy. I played Visage because a friend said this one is actually scary and yeah it ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ is. This is the first game to ever give me a sinking and ever growing feeling of dread that just screams something is about to be very, very wrong and you can't stop it. I had to steel myself to even consider looking down a dimly lit hallway, nevermind the dark nooks and crannies you can peek into. The game does an amazing job of making you ♥♥♥♥ your pants with every small creak emitted when you open a door. How? By letting you go around a few places shown in the videos in the store page. You see that closet all the way in the back and your gut starts screaming no, but you press on, and slowly pull the creaking, whining door open, peering into the murky black inside, afraid you'll get snatched. But then there was nothing. But what about next time? What if you turn your back and then it gets you? The game nails the feeling of being small and helpless in the face of eldritch abominations and ghosts with unknowable motivations.Indeed the game isn't perfect, but it's still in early access. I've only played a few minutes before being spooked into waiting for someone braver or stupider to play with me, with lights on of course. At the very least, Visage deserves massive praise for sheer presence with its sound design. Best wishes for the team behind the game as a whole, I'm looking forward to getting a heart attack while playing one of your games

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: I watched a walkthrough of the full game. The next morning, I had the worst panic attack of my life. THE WRITING IN THIS GAME IS NOT JUST BAD, IT IS IRRESPONSIBLE. Meaning, if a game has flashing lights, and there is no epilepsy warning, that is irresponsible. Some of the reason this triggered my PTSD is personal. But there are lines in this game, directed straight at the player, that I genuinely think could push someone over the edge if they were contemplating suicide. I think the people who made this game wanted it to be more than scary, and so they dug into actual psychological triggers and just tossed them around haphazardly. Anything to get a reaction. And the result is a scattershot mess that is more uncomfortable because its pieces do not fit together. The ending is completely incompatible with the preceding 3/4ths of the game, and renders them meaningless. I am now not just repulsed at the unacceptable unfinishedness of the game, I am disgusted at the thoughtlessness of its creators.---How did this game make it out of early access in this condition!? Visage is not scary; Visage is not hard; Visage is ANNOYING.I'm done. I finished Lucy's chapter, but Dolores can go to hell. I'm sick of wasting pills when I try to open doors. Sick of getting the same hints over and over. Sick of having no idea what's considered "in the dark". Sick of being unable to put things in my inventory because the menu won't show up. Sick of lights not working depending on whether I've reloaded my save. Sick of the camera being caught on doorframes. Sick of events not triggering. Sick of LOUD, IRRITATING JUMPSCARE NOISES.Sick of the absolutely arbitrary reasons why everything does or doesn't, can or cannot happen. If the front door is jammed, and made of glass, why can't I open it with a sledgehammer? I'm carrying a hook for the attic. Why can't it open a window to get the compass? No; I have to backtrack and do everything on rails.I keep finding myself contrasting Visage with its obvious counterpart, Layers Of Fear, and it's miles apart. Everything WORKED in that game. And yes, it was linear as a tightrope. But it felt different, because it wasn't text boxes telling you where you couldn't go. Bloober team handles immersion and signposting much, much better. With Visage, too many times I'd get sick of wandering around not knowing what to do next, checking a walkthrough, and recoiling at, "Wait, THAT!?" There's a reason I don't play point-and-click adventure games, because I don't enjoy waving the mouse around, clicking everything, trying to find the utterly-unintuitive way through. Especially not while also dealing with a #!*@(% dead grandma wandering around trying to stab me. ALSO I HAVE A SLEDGEHAMMER AND I'M A GROWN MAN, BUT I JUST STAND THERE AND LET HER DO IT!?I'm so frustrated because, when things work, they work WELL. Lucy's chapter had parts that genuinely gripped me and had me feeling true horror. The lighting is INCREDIBLE. The textures and modeling are great. When the glitches aren't breaking the immersion, I am 100% in this house and feeling these events. And then some other dumb moment breaks the illusion.I don't care anymore. I am not going through two and a half more chapters of frustrating inconsistency. This is like being served a gorgeously decorated cake, that you cut open and it's all half-baked and leaking in the middle. No thanks.

_childDocuments_.review: Three major gripes with this game....1.) There is a "sprint" button.... which takes your walk speed from .25 mph to .3 mph. It is not fun holding shift down for an entire game for the speed boost equivalent of finding the good phone number for your dial-up connection. Make it a toggle or just increase walk speed and call it a day.2.) Dark areas are not dark, they are literally black. If you do not have a light source of some kind, you don't really get to feel your way through, you are immediately lost in the darkness and might as well reload a save...3.) All Cutscenes, including the ones where you die, are completely unskippable and are extremely padded in length for no reason. There are quite a few sections where you will die a LOT, and you have to sit through 15-20 seconds of the exact same death animation over and over and over. You see a wall you can break down, so you interact with it that starts a cutscene, and first the camera has to wobble for 20 seconds before you start breaking the wall down. There are a ton of these examplesWith that said, the general unscripted nature of this game made it a lot scarier, so if you're looking for a horror experience, this is very very good. There are other things that happen like the objects you're holding might clip into walls or have weird physics or just general bugs, but not enough to take away from the experience in my playthrough.As someone who plays a lot of puzzle games, this was at that perfect level of challenge, and nothing seemed too abstract. There were some moments where it did feel like you were just wandering aimlessly trying to find the next interactable object, but at least for me, I could tell when those moments were, and I would "sprint" my way around the house.Overall a good horror experience. Did exactly what I was hoping it would with the exception of my three initial gripes. 8/10 for me.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not the biggest horror game fan but I still buy them occasionally, I don't know why but I just do and Visage is one of them. It's easily one of the best in the genre but it's not without some minor flaws if I'm being honest. First I have to talk about the controls, the items handling is a learning curve with the inventory and the dual wielding, once you get used to it it's alright but still kind of unintuitive. After that part is the door opening, you have to drag your mouse while holding the button down, it's slow and clumsy especially frustrating when in a rush.Now for the horror, I think it's good as in it doesn't rely on jumpscares but atmosphere so you don't really know when to expect the game to get you. The game takes place in a house in which you are relatively free to roam around. The house gets distorted to fit the story which is divided in 4 chapters telling the story of 4 different characters mostly about one mental illness or the other which ended up bad as you might have expected it. They can be done in any order and the quality between them vary a bit so I'd advise to start with Lucy first (you start a chapter by picking an item so you will have to look it up if you are to chose your order). The overall story is not mind blowing and quite vague at times but it's probably intentional so I went with it. For those who are not used to playing detective, this is pretty much the entire game outside of some chase sequence and exploration so you might have to pull up a walkthrough / guide just in case you are hard stuck. I say that because the game is presented as hard and it is, you have a sanity meter to maintain so you don't get paranormal activities which sound more intimidating than they are really. The events are things like flickering lights and hearing someone breathe in your ear which are really annoying after a while so you don't really want to get stuck for too long. The atmosphere while roaming gets repetitive fast, as there isn't much to it outside of the paranormal events I mentioned but it does an alright job at setting the tone for the story that it doesn't feel empty or not too intrusive. The visuals really shows the PT inspiration and I think it's one of the better aspect of the game, sounds being rather okay.Overall it's still an excellent horror game it's just not quite perfect because of the aforementioned flaws with the controls, inconsistency with the chapters and the sort of underwhelming roaming aspect. The horror and visuals are what shines for me and the sound is a rather neutral point.

_childDocuments_.review: This game may be only Early Access but this is by and large one of if not THE scariest game I've played. I can't explain to you how many times I screamed like a little girl and had wanted to stop playing. At one point the game actually scared me so bad that my chest genuinely hurt. I had to take a moment to catch my breath before returning to the game. It's not just cheap jumpscares, and this game does a great job of playing up the scares and building the tension before giving you a release worth the wait. It does start a little slow, but the first real enemy encounter/scare left me terrified to explore. I would definitely not suggest this for someone who doesn't handle horror well. People who try to act macho and as if they are impossible to scare will definitely have their work cut out for them in this game. So let's get down to the specifics.The graphics are gorgeous and truely suck you into the terrifying atmosphere of the game. The ambiance from sounds alone is enough to rival Dead Space's sound design, except with far more subtlety and nuance. The game's controls can be a little unintuitive, the amount of times I accidentally dropped something by pressing F is somewhat annoying. I remember losing a lighter that way and being unable to find it later. The way the world interacts with the physics of the objects you're holding can provide some goofy weird moments, including getting objects stuck on the other side of doors only to have them teleport into your hand or having them knock against walls and behave awkwardly.The only other slight qualm I have with the game is that once your sanity is in the danger zone candles seem to offer no actual effect on refilling your sanity. I may have misunderstood, but I definitely had 2 candles directly next to me and stood there for a while suffering all the ill effects of dangerously low sanity.That is literally all I can think of as far as negatives, and honestly they're almost non-existent enough for me to not care. The items and resources can be a little scarce but I do not find that a negative, it just adds to the challenge of the game.Honestly I can't believe this game is in early access. Even as is for the asking price and the incomplete product I'd say you're getting far more than your money's worth. Not to mention the cute little easter eggs at the end of the game and the reference to another survival horror series that I was quite entertained to see. So devs, color me insanely impressed. I can't think of another horror game on steam that would even come close to being on par with this if I'm honest. Not even "Triple A" releases. Thank you for the clear hard work and love you've poured into this game and I cannot wait to see what you add to the final product. Even if I may curse your name when your game makes me scream like a big ol' baby.

_childDocuments_.review: Visage is a really good game that could have been a classic, but for one nagging problem.First, the good parts: The game is absolutely TERRIFYING! The house is a masterwork of atmospheric horror and feels like a real place straight out of the 80s. Top-notch lightning and sound design. Jump scares are rare, which makes them all the more effective. Graphics are screenshot-worthy; I love the mix of 80s modern and supernatural as you move about. Chapter stories are engaging as you reveal more about the ghosts that haunt the home. Puzzles are clever and satisfying to solve... when you can find them.That brings me to the problem. This is a game badly in need of a hint system. The puzzles range from reasonably challenging to "WTF??". If you don't keep notes and/or consult a walkthrough guide from time to time, you'll spend far too much time wandering around the house wondering what to do next. That's not fun. The developers could solve this by offering the player progressively more specific hints (a la The Room) to keep the action moving forward if they're not making any progress. In the meantime, my advice to players is have a walkthrough handy so you can experience this great game without the frustration.

_childDocuments_.review: Refreshing dive back into slow-burning survival horror. This game takes a lot of cues from Konami classics like the Silent Hill series games from the last 90s and early 2000s. I never owned a PS4 or played P.T., but judging from the videos I've watched, it draws a lot of elements from P.T. as well. The game is beautifully rendered in the Unreal 4 engine and is certified as being one of the scariest games I've played in a while. Resident Evil 7 drew some suspense from me, but I have not felt that since. The sound design is also amazing, from the ambient noise of the ghostly apparitions, light switches, and the creaking and groaning noises that the house makes. It actually makes you feel as if you are trapped in a living, breathing house where terrible things have happened. 9/10 Highly recommended, especially if you are a horror fanatic and like good challenge.

It needs to be a lot simpler.One more detail: the sanity icon looked a bit cheap. In Amnesia, you start to have these disturbing visual effects that make it seem very real. _childDocuments_.review: Is the game scary to play? Yes. 100 percent. It nails sound design, tension, visuals, art direction - all a home run. Like wow. I love horror games and this could've been one of the best horror games ever made, but it fails miserably in progression and puzzle solving. You would need hours and hours of aimlessly walking around and not knowing what to do without some type of guide. I got to chapter two where you need to smash mirrors throughout the house to solve puzzles and found around 5 mirrors and went into them, not completing the vast majority of the puzzles. Why? BECAUSE YOU MAYBE DIDN'T FIND THAT SINGLE MIRROR HIDDEN IN A CLOSET IN THE DARK THAT YOU NEED TO GET A SINGLE OBSCURE PIECE FROM TO SOLVE THE NEXT PUZZLE. Which next puzzle you may ask? Oh WHO THE F*** KNOWS? You just have to hope to go into the next mirror and have the right tools/equipment to solve that one from a previous mirror. This means that my intellect or any type of game knowledge or environmental knowledge I've gained from the house means absolute bunk. It's whatever the devs have in their own mind with ZERO CUES or hints to point you in the next direction. Do some people love this? Yea because they are masochistic. But wandering around for hours aimlessly trying to solve obtuse puzzles that require a guide isn't my idea of a fun time. Absolutely dropped the ball on this one. What could've been a 10/10 game has been destroyed by obtuse puzzles, aimless wandering, and a story that has no cohesiveness.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been hyped for this game since its announcement and as soon as I saw the developers announce the release of an early access version I immediately hopped on Steam and made the purchase. My expectations were high and the opening cutscene made me think my expectations would be met or exceeded. Seriously, that was ballsy opening cutscene and I loved it. I can't really say the same for the rest of the game. PROS-Graphics are great. The aesthetics of the house and its transformations are phenomenal.-A shocking and hooking opening cut scene.-Creepy ambience and environment. I especially liked the section of the game in the woods/tree house when the demon's voice came on the radio. I legit panicked when the wood boards started blocking me in.-Ghost/Demon appearance. They were genuinely creepy. The first time the demon with the talons appeared and started floating toward me scared the s**t out of me. And jawless Lucy was creepy as well especially when you find out what happened to her. Although her constant moaning following me around the house was sometimes annoying.-Physics! You can pick a ton of items up and I always find that entertaining. It's a bit glitchy right now, at least for me, but I still liked it.CONS-Only about 1 and a half - 2 and a half hours of gameplay depending on how fast you find yourself able to progress. Not currently worth the $19.99 I paid for it. This point is subject to change as long as the future content is an improvement over the current one.-I constantly asked myself if I was making any progress. Sure, the game's description mentions that it is slow paced and emphasizes exploring the environment--but there were times where it was frustratingly slow. Sometimes you just had to wait for a certain amount of time to pass to progress, other times a certain action needed to be performed, and other times I just found myself walking in circles until something happened. I can appreciate a level of mystery and uncertainty, but it felt like too much in certain parts of the game.-The glitches!! I don't know if anyone else experienced this or if it was just my sh**ty luck, but dropped items would sometimes get stuck in doorways and prevent a door from being opened or closed. This wasn't always a big deal--sometimes I could just go around but other times it trapped me in a room with only one way in or out. Other times I had to load a previous save because I was literally trapped. And I'm referring to used lighters and pills that get dropped. Tiny items that create an invisible barrier!  Another bug I faced was a fatal error and game crash after beating the game when you can finally open the safe with the Safe Key. Every time I walk into that room the game crashes. So I never got to see the Room 302 and dancing Lucy myself. Objects that can be lifted and examined would also phaze through walls and other objects or cause nearby items to start glitching out. And one time, the curtains on a window took my camera and lighter. I closed the curtains and my camera and lighter just floated away. There was also an entity of some kind that, when it appeared behind me, was glitched into a door (not very menacing when that happens). Lastly, the storage cabinet in the basement didn't work for me.  The game is early access though, so it was really just the first two problems that bothered me the most.-Teasing me with doors, hatches, and vents that, when interacted with, say something like "Content unavailable in current version of game." -The inventory system wasn't very user-friendly and intuitive. It wasn't exactly difficult to use, it just seemed like a hindrence at times. When I was first using it and I'd use the last pill in one of the bottles, I didn't realize I had to manually drop it before putting another item in that hand--it would literally block you from pulling out another item until you dropped that empty pill bottle. Also, there were instances where I could store literally almost anything in my inventory like a ketchup bottle. Why? -Benefits of using candles and lightbulbs seemed nonexistent. If they're going to be a usable item, make it more beneficial to use them. I pretty much only ever used a lighter and pills and rarely ever died/became overwhelmed with insanity despite the light from candles and lightbulbs being able to lower your insanity. The camera also didn't have much use except showing ONE hidden blood trail and becoming my only light source at the end of the game. Maybe I missed some secrets it could reveal or maybe they'll add more uses in the future.-Lack of gameplay variation. It's a first person horror game but doesn't really bring anything all that new to the table. I just walked around and waited for things to happen a lot of the time. Also, this could be its own point, but opening drawers was almost entirely a waste of time except for in the cages room and maybe one other instance. Huge waste of time to go through all of them and find nothing.-Sanity system was EXTREMELY sensitive at times. I think the sanity system is an okay feature, I mean come on, who wouldn't lose their mind in a situation like this? But there were times where a lightbulb flickered or went out early in the game and the character about had a breakdown. Then there were other times where a major paranormal event occurred and my sanity was barely affected. It just didn't seem consistent/proportionate to events that took place.Despite writing more in my cons section, I still think this game has potential and I will definitely play it when the full release is out. I enjoyed the game when I was actually progressing and entering new areas, but more often than not I was asking myself, "Is this the end? Is it over yet? What now?" and not in a good way. I'm surprised by the number of positive reviews and the praise the game is currently receiving. Everyone's take on it is of course subjective, but I just don't understand how some people are seeing it as one of the best horror games ever or one of the scariest games ever. With all that being said, I don't think its a "bad" game, I just can't currently recommend the game, although I look forward to seeing its progress and improvements.My playthrough:

_childDocuments_.review: Perhaps the most surprising thing about this game is how different it feels from PT. While its inspiration is obvious, Visage manages to have some very nice surprises up its sleeve and manages to create a rather phenomenal horror game that kept me thoroughly engaged in its 10-12 hours of gameplay.You play as Dwayne, a man who's stuck in a rather terrifying haunted house after witnessing one of the ballsiest opening scenes I've seen in a while. The goal is figuring out the history of the house, its previous inhabitants and what happened to them. It deals with topics like alcoholism, neglect, abuse and many other rather heavy topics in a fairly interesting manner.The game is split in 3 chapters, each dealing with a former inhabitant of the house. And this is where a lot of people will probably be disappointed because aside from some neat puzzles, it's a mostly linear experience with some moments where interactivity gets thrown out of the window and it starts feeling suspiciously like a walking simulator. There is variety, sure, but it can feel incredibly repetitive to walk around the same house and rooms over and over again until the game takes you out of your comfort zone and takes you to some rather unexpected places and mechanics. Brace yourselves for the moments involving the camera.Rather than a health system, you have a sanity system indicated by a red splotch and a brain on the lower left corner. If you don't take pills, there will be more paranormal activity and you could die. Which isn't harsh since it loads your last autosave. However, the items you'll be using the most are candles and lighters. These are crucial since being in darkness will decrease your sanity. Light bulbs can also break and be replaced but I only had to do it twice on my playthrough.I also have to mention that this game has one of the clunkiest inventory systems I've ever encountered. It's bad, it's really, really bad. Made even worse during moments where you have to react quickly. To call it aggravating would be an understatement.Visually the game looks stunning and runs fairly well... most of the time. Hitching was an issue in certain moments and the visual settings are rather confusing. I was wondering what was the difference between high and max resolution scaling but apparently max is just native resolution, which is baffling. I had never seen it being labeled like that. However, the art direction and lighting is superb. As I previously mentioned, the game isn't afraid of taking you out of the house at certain moments and let me tell you: It gets creative.The house is wonderfully detailed with lots of small details and things to examine. And just like PT, you might miss a small change that makes the house even scarier. It likes to play with your expectations.The music is good but I didn't feel it was fantastic. The audio design shines bright, though. Moans, lights flickering, footsteps, wood creaking and clock alarms are all mixed superbly and gives tI also have to mention the ending. It's underwhelming at best. It sort of stops if that makes sense. A shame since I was quite engaged in the storyline. There's two endings so the other one might be better?Overall, it can be a bit too janky at points but if you want something a bit similar to PT while also seeking a great horror adventure, this is a must play. My first playthrough took me around 10 hours and there are collectibles plus an additional ending so I can easily say it's worth a purchase.Just be wary, it does get legitimately disturbing at points.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start by saying this is the scariest thing I've played since P.T. It's fantastic, and I absolutely love the respectful nods it gives to Silent Hill 4 and other classic horror titles. It's the first-person horror I've been waiting for, and there's so much love poured into every scare. Fascinating visuals and a gradual descent into surreal horror makes it a vivid, uncomfortable experience from beginning to end.Now let's talk controls. My brother and I played the original scheme for our first playthrough on his account, and I picked up the controller on my account to try out the new scheme (which is why my playtime is so short, and yet I comment on the entire game). It's an improvement, but it's still very unintuitive, I feel. It won't let me store candles in the dynamic inventory, and I can't figure out whether or not this is intentional. I don't care for the "hold to use" as I feel it sprinkles frustration in when you're rushing to use things, and diffuses tension. I assume this change was made to avoid bugs or something, but I liked it the original way better.I like the fact the two inventories are now combined. I wish the dynamic inventory had more slots, but I'm an old school Silent Hill fan who wants bottomless pockets, so I think that's more of a subjective opinion than something to be taken as serious criticism. But it's a little annoying that the dynamic inventory is so small and the key inventory is so massive when you never have more than a few key items at a time. Maybe this changes in future chapters? I'm not sure, but for now, it comes across as not very well thought out.Picking up, storing, and retrieving items from the dynamic inventory is still a nightmare at first (there were no tutorials to teach the new scheme, either, so that was an experience of button experimentation), and even when you get used to it, there's a lot of fiddling that completely ruins the immersion for me. I would strongly recommend the devs pick a more classical inventory system that players are familiar with and stick with that rather than trying to reinvent the wheel. It's still very clumsy and frustrating. I've dropped way too many bottles of pills just trying to back out of the inventory screen because I'm so accustomed to "B" backing out of a menu.However, the candle placement has improved massively. I love the new red cloud to indicate sanity loss. The sanity system overall seems to be better balanced (but perhaps it's just a result of having a more clear UI that allows us to better manage it). I really appreciate the updates to drawings on the walls for hints to puzzles that are very unclear otherwise. They're done in a way that maintain the atmosphere and don't make the game feel "dumbed down".Overall, I would recommend the game, but with a disclaimer that the controls still feel very experimental and unbalanced. I love the fact the devs are listening to feedback, however, and I'm happy to support them. If you're not willing to purchase a game that's still experiencing growing pains, be sure to at least keep an eye on this one, because I think once it's been ironed out, it's going to become a horror icon. I can't wait for the next chapters.

_childDocuments_.review: Been playing this since Early Access but only managed to finish the first chapter that was available back then because it scared the dingleberries out of me. Now, almost 4 years later to the day, I finally got around to playing the content that was added later on, and after finishing the second chapter, I'm mildly disappointed.It's probably worth noting that my initial infatuation with the concept of this game sorta died out, and I suppose I must have grown some hair on my balls too because I'm not really affected by the kind of scares that it offers anymore. But if there's one thing that it can be commended for is that it successfully accomplishes it's goal to recapture the style of P.T., and also expands on its basic concept in a way that it ultimately feels like its natural, more elaborate successor. If you're looking for a game that can effectively unnerve you without relying on jump scares or other cheap tactics, and instead attempts to do something more cerebral and atmospheric, then this game will do the job. The realistically rendered house that has this sort of lived-in, cozy, and familiar feel to it really gets under your skin once the paranormal events start to happen all around you, because that very familiarity is what makes it so unnerving. It's so much easier to make your own imagination work against you when scary stuff is happening in a bedroom or a basement that looks uncannily similar to your own...Anyway, the game is really good at freaking you out and some of the set pieces are truly brilliant. But where I think it all falls apart is in the puzzles and how the chapters are scripted. Because using the word "puzzles" would be a very generous way to describe it. A puzzle is when you are presented with some sort of a riddle to decipher or piece together, while Visage's idea of a puzzle is to give you some sort of a task to perform in one part of a house without a context, and a literal solution scribbled down on a note that you have to find in another part of the house. For example, one of the puzzles involves a room with about a dozen paintings scattered about, and three empty spaces on a wall where you need to put specific paintings. Now, if this was a quality puzzle, then you'd be given some kind of a limerick or an enigmatic note that would provide you with clues as to which paintings you need to hang on the wall. But instead of having something fun like that, in Visage you just need to go over to another room in the house and look at the solution through a hole in the wall and just sorta remember it.It's incredibly lazy and it only scratches the surface of how disappointing the puzzles are in this game. Another part that makes this game a bit of a chore is how obtuse it can get in terms of what you need to do next at any given moment. The first chapter of the game was the best one so far (I still need to finish the final one), because the bread crumbs that you had to follow in order to progress were laid out before you in a very logical way and you could easily pick up the trail even if you got turned around and went into the wrong room. But once you get to the chapters with more expansive set pieces that require you to wander all over the place, you're just gonna get lost all the time and walk around in circles, hoping that you'll eventually stumble d!ck-first into a scripted event that will trigger the next portion of the story. It gets incredibly tedious after a while, and the problem is only exacerbated by the painfully slow walking speed of your character. I'm not ashamed to admit that I eventually looked up a walkthrough just out of sheer boredom-induced frustration because i was tired of wandering between the same five rooms and missing some tiny notes tucked in between couch cushions, or getting led astray by some optional collectable hunts without even realizing that it's not a part of the main storyline.TL;DR - if you're willing to put up with some of the tedium or don't mind playing with a spoiler-free walkthrough on the side, then it's worth recommending for the sheer dread and subtle scares that this game can provide. But if you're the kind of person who's pretty much immune to video game scares, then don't bother. You're just gonna be bored out of your pubes.

_childDocuments_.review: The good- Nice visuals with good graphics quality and mostly cool atmospheric lighting. Some regions that are very artistic and worth hitting that screenshot button.- It has some interesting gameplay mechanisms like the walkie talkie and the compass. They are pretty refreshing and fun, but also inconsistent and don't last long.- Dolores chapter has good structure and pace. The house gets transformed into a big puzzle full of mysteries. Unfortunately the rest of the game gets pretty linear with less creative mechanisms and questionable decisions.- If you like to explore every corner of a game for hidden secrets and collectables this is a game for you. It can get pretty tiring though when you don't know what you are looking for.- Initially it has a calm, sick, dark atmosphere that makes it really scary. Unfortunately after some hours tons of silly jump scares, and cheap tricks ruin it.- The fact that you play the game using daily life objects, like lighters and candles is a nice choice and makes it more scary. You don't always need to be the super human that runs and guns everything.- Cool enemies. They're nothing unique for sure, but they're creepy enough to give you some chills.- If you like splatter scenes, well, it has a lot of them. They tend to be pretty cliché though.The bad- Very bad puzzles' logic and structure. The player doesn't feel like having a purpose to fulfil and this is mainly related with the random outcome of each puzzle and the fact that they seem like not actually supporting a storyline based on a series of logical actions. You can anticipate most of the staff you have to do in order to solve the puzzles, but what comes after it seems random. For example you see only one slipper on the bed, so it's easy to understand that you have to pick the second one from the floor, but the result of doing this is to open a door. You end up doing things casually because they are there but without knowing why. The story moves forward when you solve a puzzle but has no real connection to it. There is no logical series of events. It's like they initially designed some cool puzzles and threw them inside a house without minding that all these are actions of an actual plot. You just explore solving puzzles while lights turn out and creepy things scare you. Also, in many occasions it doesn't give you enough clues for the next puzzle. It gets transformed into a "spot the difference" game that forces you to endlessly circle around the house trying to figure out what has changed.- It doesn't have a specific design language neither a consistent horror concept. It's like they just threw in there every cheap, worn trick that they came up with. Dolls, little girls in white dresses, hanged bodies, faceless people, optical distortions, rotten rooms, trails of blood, flickering lights, random screams, babies' cry, creaks coming from nowhere, doors shutting by themselves,  scary music turning up mostly for no reason and of course tons of silly jump scares. Even an Esser's painting is in there to indicate the protagonist's mental complexity. Too easy and cliché . A horror theme park just to impress.- Awkward controls and tons of glitches. Interactions are messy. Opening doors and wardrobes is slow and problematic. Examining and rotating objects is clunky. The tools that you carry and are floating in front of you (yes, there are no hands) get into other objects' geometry. In narrow passages they tent to get stuck and left behind you. When carrying big objects you cannot see where to go. There are many completely dark regions, that you're not allowed to use your lighter for some reason. You end up doing circles without knowing where to go. Some scripted events get triggered with much delay so you just stand for a while wandering what to do next. Running is annoyingly slow.- The sanity meter, that it is supposed to drop when being in dark for long periods is inconsistent. Sometimes it drops, others not. A core gameplay feature that doesn't give you accurate feedback is one of the most annoying things in gaming for me.- For some reason it allows you to carry only one "key" tool. You have to go to the storage room every time you wanna equip a different one with a result of adding a few more hours of pointless wandering around the house.- Except of the Dolores' chapter, that has some creative ideas, all the others are pretty linear and force you mainly to search for keys, exits and locked doors while scripted encounters happen around you.

_childDocuments_.review: Ever since playing this game, my wife and I quote the opening warning card that shows when you start it up, "Visage is hard," which feels like a defensive excuse fired off for the obtuse puzzles and relentless death mechanic you're about to embark through.That obtuseness is why I don't love this game, but there's too much it gets right to not recommend it; the atmosphere, the sound design, the writing, all knocked out of the park. But the journey to get through it is a trudge; not quite the lightbulb in a tin can nonsense you'd get from SH, but enough like that without any direction to become understandably frustrated. Pair that with haunts that can kill you and the lack of a quicksave option and you get moments that become unimmersive and just plain maddening.It's hard to work in a death/punishment mechanic in a horror game that doesn't result in these unimmersive moments (i.e. I've already been through this part, I'm not scared, I'm just trying to progress!), but it would've been appreciated to have difficulty options to lessen the death moments so I could enjoy all the work put into the game environments without the added pressure of punishment, like a New Game+ mode even.Oh well, again, not enough of a problem to not recommend because it's heart is most definitely in the right place, but you should be aware that "Visage is Hard," enough for them to disclaim it and enough for it to frustrate a decent chunk of the playerbase. If you are in that playbase, there is no shame in using a walkthrough, of which there are some great ones in the Community Tab that don't include spoilers.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone desensitized to horror media these days, I can say for a fact that the feeling of a ghost or spooky entity standing behind me and breathing down my back is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ horrifying, and that's exactly why this game is so scary.Right now this game is a bit bare-bones, with "4-6 hours of content" (though from what I've seen, it's more of 2 hours average-- must have used their 12 year old child to test length, or embellished the time), but the content that is there is downright ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ evil with how spooky it is. The comparison has been made 100 times, but if you've played P.T. you have a general idea of what's going on here:You start as man, presumably the antagonist and protagonist of the story locked in a house with a very dark past that you may or may not have had a hand in. I'm not quite sure of the player character's motive, whether he just has the world's biggest balls, or the house literally just wont let him out, but as with any video game  you're gonna keep going further in. As you proceed further, in that Silent Hill/ PT fashion things slowly ramp up, doors start slamming and opening themselves, light flickers, shatter, and even turn off moments after you just turned it on so you can proceed further into a room. Footsteps, knocks, items falling; it has it all and with a good pair of headphones you'll hate and love every moment of it.Gameplay-wise, what sets Visage apart from any other walking simulator horror game is not combat, but a sanity system reminiscent of Amnesia, and an inventory system.... also reminiscent of Amnesia. The inventory system is your usual puzzle item/ key Resident Evil style system, but you can store pretty much anything you can pick up. A variable amount of minutes into the game you're given a small zippo lighter that provides your means of lighting when the lights don't work/ don't shine far enough to light the whole room for you. This zippo will eventually run out of gas and you'll have to find a new one, or be stuck in the dark searching frantically for a new one or a light switch as your sanity goes down. Once your sanity hits the floor you begin to see more paranormal events which as far as I've noticed only consists of doors moving/closing/slamming, the sounds, and an enemy to locate you and stalk you. I wont spoil when, where, what, or how, but at some point in Chapter 1 a ghost or two will begin stalking you everytime your sanity reaches low levels, making it important to manage how much light you are around. If it gets too low I think it's an instant death/ the ghost just teleports to you and kills you. The ghost itself is not that disturbing when you're caught to be honest, so you might not really be jump scared when it does catch you, but the  is where it truely shines. That ♥♥♥♥♥♥ is just so creepy to see wandering around. This isn't the only entity in the house in Chapter 1 though, so keep an eye out...Graphically, the game is top notch. It's not quite the level of P.T. but it's slightly better than Resident Evil 7; it's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ gorgeous to look at, and downright photorealistic at times. Not to mention it runs beautifully. The recommended settings to run on Max at 1080p is an RX 480 with a Ryzen 5 CPU, and I have exactly both of those, and it does not disappoint. For all of Unreal Engine 4's opimiztion woes, these guys know how to make it work, while delivering a very eye-poppingly depressing experience.As EA notices say, if you're excited to play the game in the state it is/ with the content it currently has, absolutely ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ buy it. I've been waiting for a real full length game in this style for awhile, and since it's currently October I have been in urgent need of something to get me spooked.As for the EA model the game seems to have, they said they will add content on a "as it's done" basis, hopefully meaning we wont have to wait all 4 months to get more content, so that's a very good deal as well.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, as a person who has been exposed to TONS of psychological horror I can say without a doubt: This experience is not "stupid scary" as some would put it, more "scary stupid". In fact the scariest aspect of the game would be how unpolished and dumb its mechanics are. To start off is the whole mechanic which guarantees your survival, the light/sanity meter. It is a dumb concept, as survival horror is supposed to make the player feel as the victim, this does the exact opposite. The inventory system is a pile of steaming garbo designed by some deranged lunatic that has never heard the word "intuitive".  The items literally do not make sense (lighter light v. candle light) and for survival horror there are too many items lying around; so much that its both gamebreaking and laughable. The monsters are cheap rehashes of J-horror antagonists from at least a decade ago, stupid really. Also the opening cutscene is so try-hard edgy that I almost threw up, its edgier than the one kid in my highschool class that claimed he could swallow razors (complete with mascara, black fingernail polish, Hot Topic, and My Chemical Romance). I saw him for what he was, an attention grabbing loser, which also sums up (in parallel) my opinion of the game.Now an address to the developers. Wow, talk about leaving a polished turd, not finishing it, charging pretty highly for what it is, then somehow managing to deceive the rest of the horror "fans" (check the rest of the reviews on this game, my god, they wouldn't know scary if it shot it's family then itself.) into greedily scarfing down your doo-doo sandwich and calling it "good".  Bravo, on successfully pulling off the most blatant con-job of this decade.Tl;dr:This game is baby-go-waaah levels of scary, its unplayable and its mechanics gamebreaking. I am glad I was able to get it refunded. Also I know there is a lot I missed in this negative review, but its so much a chore to even think about that I cannot take the time to go into any more depth. Do yourself a favor and keep looking for better (albeit more realistically priced) horror experiences, I know I have played excellent and well made horror games which are a fraction of what this costed me.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played a plethora of horror games and it's been tough to find a good one recently. Visage shows an EXCELLENT amount of promise. It does horror perfectly, has a compelling story, and looks great doing it. Graphically the game looks very impressive with just the right amount of film grain to add a subtle cinematic feel. Visuals are photo realistic and is similar to an unfortunately cancelled horror game. The gameplay is like a walking sim, but with a bit more engaging gameplay. Managing your sanity through light sources is key. You'll go digging around to find lighters, candles, and a camera flash is a great and eerie way to explore dark areas and the game accents this wonderfully. The story starts with a bang (pun intended) and you'll spend the first chapter figuring out what's going on and I felt myself geniunely curious as to how everything fit together between the themes of the horror elements and the narrative. The drawback is that a lot of the areas are closed for Early Access, however the first chapter is completely available and the game won't let you stray off somewhere only to run into areas that are inaccessible. The game takes awhile to build up the horror elements, but once you met your first paranormal experience, man it's all a roller coaster ride from there. Horror. I hate shrilly cheap scares from games that resort to loud audio noises to be "scary." On the other hand, I hate games that strictly just have a creepy atmosphere, but never any sense of danger. This game was super creepy, great well timed jump scares, but maybe the only thing I didn't like is that if you linger in an area too long, it'll spawn one of the ghosts to kill you. Overall it's not horrible, but it's meh. All in all, great graphics, compelling story, engaging gameplay, great atmosphere, well placed jump scares. It's a great horror game and well worth your time and money!

_childDocuments_.review: I was all over very dissapointed and frustrated with this game due to it's huge missed potential.The main problems of this game come from it's missuse of difficulty that completely ruin the great tension it tries (and rarely succcedes in) building.It has a great setup that evolves and developes in interesting ways, but is ruined time after time by lackluster, clumsy puzzle design that is cyptic (but not in a fun way). It forces the player to navigate areas over and over, which wouldn't be a problem in its self if it were for other reasons than flat out bad game design. It comes to a point where it is immersion breaking due to boredom and frustration with little payoff. The biggest missdirection in my opinion is the use of each chapter's antagonists. They are always introduced and presented as mysterious, menacing entities thanks to some truly great sound design, and terrifying situations. But this is all counteracted by the game's desire to make them actually "dangerous" to the player in a missguided attempt to create stakes. It ends up leading to the complete opposite effect where they become more of a dull, unfair, unballanced, poorly designed nuisance. They will constantly insta kill even the most careful player, in a way that destroys all sense of tension and mystification that the previous buildup created. After seeing each enemy in closeup detail many many times throughout long death animations I no longer feared them and saw them more as an annoyance to avoid solely out of fear of seeing the cheap payoff of them catching me again. I should add that they often seem to appear out of litteraly nowhere right next to you in a way that feels cheap and almost comical (if it wasn't so dull, painfully long and frustrating). Whenever I thought I had worked out some form of pattern for each enemy's movements, player detection and aggro, I always ended up by being crushed by the realisation that there was simply not that amount of thought put into them (or if there was it was so poorly executed that it was as good as useless).All these aweful game design decisions leave me with an all over dreadful, frustrating, tensionless experience. Which is such a shame when paired with all the things the game does really well. it has a really interesting premisse and amazing location and sound, design. but those truly aren't enough to justify the rest of the experience in any way.Sadsquare give the impression of a team of skilled craftsmen who ultimatelly just don't understand horror, nor how to create the effective, tense, mysterious and dread filled game they were aiming for.This one really left me very empty and reminded me how good countless other horror games truly are.It definitely got a visceral reaction out of me, but not a good one.

_childDocuments_.review: It's hard to say why the game is great without spoiling what makes the horror so effective. In truth its the pacing which makes the atmosphere so interesting (and the later lack of any which ultimately ruins it).I was greeted by what I consider to be one of the most masterful psychological horror experience of the past decade, and ended with what I can only see as rushed content to meet a October 2020 deadline after years of early access promises. The opening storyline was absolutely dreadful (and I mean that in the most recommending way possible). The Mirror key sends one on a blind journey through what I have to say some of my favourite scenes in a recent video game. The 4th final chapter with the tape finding mechanics is at the least VERY interesting.But its ultimately the entire hospital section that led me to looking up a walkthrough so I could just get through the poorly designed, poorly paced, poorly created mess of a chapter. I absolutely abhor the thought of someone picking that as their second chapter after the masterful introduction chapter. I REALLY want to see the devs take what they have learned and completely remove that hospital chapter in favour of staying in the hauntingly designed house environment and telling a more focused story of the events there. Any storytelling that took place in the hospital chapter was completely overshadowed by the lack of pacing and direction. _childDocuments_.review: After a few years of waiting, Visage finally releases, and having finally beaten the game the other day with a group of friends, it doesn't disappoint. If you're a fan of psychological/supernatural horror, puzzle solving, and just being stressed from something, anything coming out to destroy your life, this is the game to play. But note that this game isn't for everyone for those same exact reasons.If you're playing Visage for the first time and haven't played a puzzle solving game like it before, it's incredibly easy to be daunted by the lack of clues the game provides. With guides, I beat the game in 8 hours. Without guides, it would've took me a much, much longer time. The game starts off with a short cutscene before bringing you into the world (the house). The house acts like a main hub. It initially gives you a tutorial whenever you discover something for the first time (the first time you pick up a lighter, a pop up appears telling you the mechanics of the lighter, same with light bulbs, paranormal events, etc.). While in the hub, paranormal activities, such as light bulbs flickering, lights turning off, etc., all happen from time to time, but note that . Once you finish a chapter, you return to the house in it's "normal" state, to which paranormal activities continue happening, but again, there's no ghost since haven't started another chapter yet, and therefore can't be killed by anything. However, this does change when you complete Chapter 1 (Lucy) and Chapter 2 (Dolores) as . There are no more tutorials past the basic mechanics of the game. It's a double edged sword that some players will love, and others will hate. The game can sometimes "hint" at where you need to go next (and by hint, I mean the player using some thought, but not much), and sometimes not give any hints in the slightest way, as you aimlessly examine every corner of the house looking for that one special item, and then spend even more time figuring out what to do with it.When players complain about the game being tedious and boring, this is what they mean. They're completely lost and the game offers no hints. My first time playing this game when only Chapter 1 and 2 were out, I spent a solid hour walking through the house doing nothing because I expected the game to be some linear, story focused horror game. Because there's no ghost to kill you while you're in limbo (since you haven't started a chapter), it's very easy to see why those who are lost get upset and think it's tedious and not scary. They're not sure what they're looking for, lights keep flickering for no reason, and nothing is coming out to ruin their day.Once you get a feel for the hub and how the game and it's "Start Chapter" system works, you can finally delve into it and begin the chapters. Each chapter has its own main antagonist/ghost, and that is the main thing that tries to haunt and kill you throughout the chapter. As mentioned earlier, you get few, if any hints on what to do, and this is what the game capitalizes on. The game wants you to wander aimlessly, figuring out what to do, in fear/stress of being surprised by the ghost randomly spawning and chasing to kill you. Because the ghost has a dynamic spawn system (with only a few scripted pop up chasing), you never know when, or where it'll appear until it's too late. This is why some playthroughs are easier then others. Some players will get lucky and not have the ghost dynamically spawn at all, and others will get the whole fist. My first playthrough of Chapter 1 and 2, I beat them both in about 2 hours each with guides and got slammed with the ghosts. On my 3rd playthrough, after the developers deleted everyone's saved data, I speed ran through both in 30 minutes each without a single dynamic ghost interaction.The 2 Hand/Inventory system is a bit clunky at first until you get use to it. If you pick the game up here and there, it's very easy to forget how the controls work because not many games work the same. However, if you're dedicated to it, you get use to it. Each hand can hold an item. One hand can hold a lighter, while the other a camera. Some items require you to hold it with both hands. This is useful information because there will be parts in the game (that the game doesn't tell you), that you'll need to use one free hand, or both hands, in order to interact with something, or to use a specific item on a specific part of something, and that item requires the use of both hands. You have to drop items specifically from the designated hand. If you want to drop a lighter, equip it in your left hand, and prop your left hand to drop what it's holding. Tedious for new players who have never played a game like it, but again, you get use to it. There's a small inventory strictly for perishable items, such as candles, lighters, light bulbs, etc., and a larger inventory strictly for key items. The story is really nice, albeit very convoluted. If you read the Steam description of the story, it specifically states that you're in a house that has a history of murders, and you're basically going through each murder (chapter), discovering the horrific event that occurred in the house. With the way the game works in terms of starting chapters (with the exception of Chapter 4, which isn't actually a chapter, it's just you finding 7 pieces to a mask), you'd think "okay, yeah, it's basically like American Horror Story". You might view yourself as the detective, or perhaps just an unfortunate individual that happened to find themselves in the house.Once you actually beat the game, you realize that none of that is true. There are 2 endings to the game. The bad ending keeps you trapped in a dark, endless abyss, and the good ending lets you meet your family again. That's right, that cutscene at the beginning of the game was you murdering your family. In truth, you're an alcoholic and a drug addict who murdered his family and then commit suicide. The chapters in the game are indeed from different time periods throughout the history of the house, but have no relevance to main story or your character, not even metaphorically. Lucy made friends with a Demon and killed herself and her bird, Dolores was Bi-Polar and Schizophrenic and killed herself and her husband, and Rakan had Ommetaphobia and was hospitalized. It's not until the fourth "chapter", do things actual become relevant to you, the main character. Each tape (7 total) has you learn more about yourself, the alcohol and drug addictions, and how it's destroying your family. As far as I'm aware, in order to get the good ending and meet your family in heaven, you need to find all pieces of the mask, making sure that the gun located in the basement (where you killed yourself and your family) doesn't run out of ammo. If you run out of ammo and shoot yourself again without obtaining and using the mask, you get stuck in limbo (literally) for eternity, not being able to meet your family in heaven. So yes, the story is essentially you're a spirit trapped in itself and in order to earn your way into heaven to meet your family, you need to come to terms with reality, accept who you are and move past all of your sins. Chapters 1, 2 and 3 literally play no part in this, so the developers must've changed their vision of the game at some point in development. I'm limited on text space now, so I'll finish up by saying Graphics and Environments were awesome, bugs were minimal (none game breaking from my experience), and go buy this game!

_childDocuments_.review: Visage is a decent enough game. It's hard to rate it as a whole because all of the chapters are quite different. I think overall probably a 6.5 maybe 7/10. That doesn't seem high, but it is above average and it loses points for some issues the game has. Some spoilers below: So first off, the highlight, Dolores chapter. I would say this is about an 8-9/10. Some of the creeps and scares by Dolores are very good. As the chapter progresses it gets even better right up until the end. I'm not an easy person to scare but Dolores found a way to get me a few times. Overall the best chapter. Next off, the worst chapter, Rakan's chapter or whatever his name was. This chapter, with the tapes, started off great. Then it sunk and sunk and sunk as it just got boring and repetitive. It felt more like a chore than anything to get through and I wasn't scared by anything. It was very tedious. Maybe if you have a specific type of fear, like, VERY specific, this might get you but, this was terrible for me. 2/10. Lastly, the mid chapter, Lucy's. Lucy's chapter starts off again, very strong. Utilising the camera to see the path of the shadow, to see in the darkest areas as the lighters stop working at times. Then in the next area, again, it starts quite well, switching between lighter and camera based off need. Then they just make you abuse the camera only. This is where it sinks. You have a good idea, and you over use it to death. It became annoying. It was sore on my eyes and I started to get frustrated with having to use the mechanic. The end of the chapter then is good but that whole middle point where they over use the camera, under use the ghost (its just non existent after the start) just sinks it a bit. I'd say a 5/10 and a warning that if you have epilepsy don't play this game. So thats my summary. I do recommend the game as long as you don't have epilepsy.

_childDocuments_.review: After all these years I finally found a good horror game, one that does not rely just on cheap scares but instead messes with you constantly inducing fear and panic slowly. 👍 +Excelent atmosphere.+Great sound design.+Psychologically scary.👎-Ending is garbage.-Rakan chapter doesn't feel as connected to the main story compared to the others.Let's be honest, it's a horror game so don't expect an emotional, detailed, and oscar worthy story, you won't find that here. Instead, you'll find a heavily inspired story from other renowned horror games such as Silent Hill. The first time you start the game it immediately and brutally puts you in the shoes of Dwayne who murders his own family and then kills himself. After that, you somehow reawaken in the house all alone with no task at hand. As you explore you find unique objects which start a chapter. There are 3 main chapters and each tells the story of previous tenants that live in your house and their tragic story. When I say tell, it's mostly through visual horror and you just have to deduce what happened to them as you reach the end of each chapter. There's no order in which you have to play these chapters so feel free to start with whichever item you find first. Lucy, Dolores, and Rakan are the 3 main chapters with the 4th being, what I'm assuming, the present where you are situated in time before starting a chapter. Lucy and Dolores's ones are really nice and extremely frightening to experience, and they somewhat feel attached to your character and the house more than Rakans who honestly feels very disconnected and kinda pointless as most of the action in that chapter takes place in an asylum. It's also the least scary of them all. I won't go into detail to avoid spoilers but as you complete all the chapters and find the final object to end the game, you are booted to a credits scene with no explanation whatsoever and that's it. It was sh*t. No nicer way to say it. One can guess what happened but honestly, it felt incredibly rushed and way too "happy"? If you can even call it that. Story rating: 7.5/10Visage is a first-person puzzle/exploration horror game, where you're tasked with, surviving, investigating, and solving several exploration puzzles, all of this while being mind ♥♥♥*ed by the game. What I mean by that is, as you explore the house and whatnot, whether you're in the chapters or outside of them, the game slowly builds panic into your soul by handling objects around the house, such as closing doors behind you, turning on the radio, etc. Those small cheap scares are just the beginning of the nightmare as you being a chapter the environment changes more or less and you slowly descend into horror and oh boy there are a lot of scary moments, especially in the Dolores and Lucy chapters. If you have some form of phobia against scary little girls and old ladies then be warned as you will get chased, haunted, and scared the living hell out of you. The Rakan chapter while it has its scary moments some crippled nut job did not have much effect on me. Avoiding the monsters in that chapter was pretty easy. Besides exploration and surviving you'll have to solve and figure out a pretty big number of environmental puzzles, more so in the Dolore chapter, a lot more so. Half the game is probably spent on that chapter alone and it's quite hard. Imagine being stressed by not knowing what to do while in the meantime being stalked, and messed around by the horrors around you. It's definitely not for the faint of hearts. I really loved the Dolores chapter and Lucy as well but sadly the quality suddenly dropped immensely in the Rakan one. The game was in early access for many years and it's a clear indication that whoever worked in the previous two chapters was no longer a part of the final one or they just didn't bother anymore. A shame really, as this could've been an incredible experience completely but instead it falters in the final hours.Gameplay rating: 8/10A horror game is nothing without a good sound design and luckily Visage does a good job at creating an eerie and scary atmosphere. It's not filled with aggressive and loud spammy sound effects like other weak horror games. Instead, it relies on a quieter environment with small sounds here and there slowly crawling into your ears. The same thing applies to the music, there's barely any songs in the game but when the tension rises you'll hear it and you'll dread it. It's simple but effective. As for voice acting, there are some well-voiced characters in the game, especially Dolores and your neighbor among others so overall I have no complaints regarding the audio. Well done.Audio rating: 8.5/10Yes, visually the game did take some inspiration from PT, Silent Hil, and some other horror games but it's far from being just a cheap copy. The game looks gorgeous as hell. The house is filled with so many details and the way the story is presented most of the time visually is also a nice factor. The models, the scary ones, also look scary as hell and quite gruesome. Sadly the animations are not as good and most of the actions you do are with invisible hands and legs and you just float around the objects you use. What the hell were they really doing all these years in early access? Anyway, the level design is fantastic as well and you will backtrack a lot so if that's an issue for you, this game might not be for you. The house is the main protagonist of the game and while you may reach other places they're all bound to the house. The house has many secrets so make sure to watch the tapes after each chapter. As for performance I had no problems running the game maxed at 1440p on a 2080. There were some small bugs here and there but nothing that hampered my experience. Graphics, performance and tech analysis score:  8/10It's good to have finally found a nice horror game. I haven't felt stressed and scared while playing in many years and while certainly, the final parts are not so good, overall the game is a great horror and I highly recommend it at any price.

_childDocuments_.review: Visage is a farily cool game. Developers did a good job, and under some aspects they did great, better than I tought from the earlier versions, but not that good in some other cases.Graphics are good, and some effects look cutting-edge sometimes. The story is very immersive, but some points are not completely connected between the each other. I would have expected a little bit more, but anyway I had a good experience.The experience is pretty unique, infact, and in most parts the game was able to keep me stressed under a certain tension. The game scenario is good, and reached very high points near the endgame. However, the game design in terms of "level design" was sometimes tricky, and some parts are nearly impossible to overcome if you don't have a guide, because the lights won't help you and the objects or rooms are way too hidden. A disclaimer to this last part is displayed at the beginning of the game, and here and there when you load your save, but I'm a player who went trought a lot of complicated games, since the '90s, and it felt like some things were just nearly unreacheable. The sound is calibrated and proper, as well as the music (good job there too). Some parts and some meachincs about the mobs are a little bit unclear or even impossible to get through at the first run, and you'll inevitably have to die a couple of times at some hard points. Also, a little bit less of dead moments would be good, but I appreciated the resemblance to the old horror and investigative game that Visage recalled in me. If you are going to try this game, my advice would be to wait until the developers make a few more adjustments, or the price goes a little bit lower, but if you like the genre don't hesitate to buy it.In a nutshell, I liked the game but I was expecting a little bit more.
