_childDocuments_.review: I have been on Steam for a long time, and I have only reviewed several games.  If you are a fan of the Horror Genre, then purchasing this game is a no-brainer.The graphics are great (I was able to get it running at 5120x1440p which was a treat), and the gameplay is exceptional.  The game doesn't hold your hand and tell you what to do next.  You have to pay close attention to everything.I believe that most people giving this game a bad review simply give up on it. I love horror games and movies and this is probably the best one i've ever played.  The atmosphere, and sound is top notch.  Definitely play this game in the dark - and if you are a masochist, play this alone in the dark with your headphones on.I probably had to look up a way to progress like 5 times during the entire campaign. _childDocuments_.review: I've been an owner of the game since the early access and have been waiting to leave a review until the full official release of the game.  Now that time has come, I'm very happy to be able to recommend this to others looking for a genuinely scary, atmospheric horror game!  Clearly inspired by PT (and thank god, we need more good psychological horror), Visage pulls no punches off the bat.  One of the most atmospheric games I've ever played, I feel uneasy just walking around the house in-game, let alone when things start getting really terrifying.  I generally don't get scared by most horror games anymore, but this games scares the hell out of me.  It excels in creating anxious moments full of tension, and capitalizing on them when you least expect it.  If you're looking for a slow-burn, melancholy horror experience, you'll find it here.No game is perfect though!  Sometimes the item-management controls can feel clunky ("I just want to drop this stupid beer can!") and there appear to be some bugs ("I just opened this door and now one of my pill bottles is gone?") but the pros strongly outweigh these issues.  Congrats to the devs in pressing through to get Visage officially released.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is definitely good it focuses in on atmosphere and the jump scares are for the most part really timed out well so at it's current state 20-25 bucks for the game is a really good deal in my opinion the graphics are amazing and the scares are pretty good and I would definitely recommend this game for anyone looking for a good horror game.Now for my gripes about the game. The mechanics are a little confusing some if not most of the time it terms of your psychological meter (your brain meter) is a little confusing to understand in terms of understanding when it's being affected ex ; when you're losing sanity or when you're gaining it back. There's no clear indicator on what counts as enough light and when you sanity is dropping besides a brain feeling in and the constant reminder tip at the bottom of the screen that lighters are not helping sanity or that sanity is decreasing fast even when sometimes you'll be standing directly under a light source. Not to say a tip bar for each indicator is the solution but I don't know make it apart of the game where if you're losing sanity you start hearing whispers louder and louder not too obnoxiously loud  but like they're getting closer and when you find a light source they start to back off not to say that is the solution but just an idea. Which follows into my next gripe is the tip bar. Now for the beginning of the game  would say the tip bar is kinda useful but after a hour or two of playing the tip bars get obnoxious and take the immersion out of the game. A possible solution to not needing the tip bars so often for the same tips over and over is to make items like the lighter when it starts to lose fuel instead of getting a tip for it every time to make it flicker on or die out so that it indicates that it's losing fuel. And lastly the predictability of the scares. This game does scares really really well up until the end I was still getting scared. BUT after a couple hours you kind of get a sense of what's a threat and when that threat is coming and easily get away from it enough to where you don't have to worry about it. A suggestion is to add them silently in and since a big focus with the game is to listen to the environment to them sliding their feet across the floor towards you or scratching or something.These are only suggestions so take what I say with a grain of salt. I really enjoyed this game and definitely recommend this game to anyone looking for a really well executed game even given it's flaws you can really see the heart put into this game and I hope to see more for these developers.If you would like to check out my game play of it  look up DanniPai Gaming.

_childDocuments_.review: I've found this to be a stunning horror experience, both solo and split headphones with a friend. The only way to be played is lights off, headphones on and volume up. Visually the game is very akin to PT, in fact the influence of PT is not hard to miss at all, which is no bad thing. The audio is also exceptionally well done, both work well together to provide a constant state of unease in the player before things kick off, and kick off they do. Controls and inventory system are a bit clunky, but once you get used to them they're perfectly serviceable. I experienced a few small glitches but nothing game breaking. With the full release coming soon, if you're looking for a intense horror experience that provides a sense of dread, dark stories that require your participation through investigation and interpretation with perfectly executed scares then give this game a look. Most effective horror game I've played since PT.Edit - Full game release version finished. Although the new chapters maybe don't quite hit the heights of Lucy or Delores, they are still well above the quality of other indie horror titles out there. So for everything this games offers, it is well worth buying and I hope for more in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not scary, believe me.It has good atmosphere but weird mechanics.Most importantly, it has good graphics but incredibly gameplay.It relies on a "sanity" mechanic which is a total pushover if you can manage to hold a candle and keep the lights on.It doesn't have jumpscares and it has very dark lighting even with all of the lights turned on (your lighter produces more light than lightbulbs the size of your head).All of this can be looked over individually, but all together it makes for an unpleasant game. Especially, when you factor in the very worst things of things:1) enemies with AI dumber than a wallnut that forget you exist when you turn a corner2) convenient enemy spawns that are literally IN-YOUR-FACE3) chase after chase after chase after chase after chase - and they're mostly pushovers4) deaths feel very cheap. And its insta-kill.Also autosave is busted because it can save while you're being chased (again). So next time, you respawn and they immediately get you. Surprise! You're stuck in a loop. Go back to your previous autosave, 15 minutes ago and repeat 5 more chase sequences.There's more, I'm sure. And unfortunately I can't recommend this game.It has very nice atmosphere, the graphics are on point and the ideas are there. Clearly a lot of work was put into this.But gameplay-wise, it's a big no.Horror games are about being scared, hurt and running, not getting repeately insta-killed.

_childDocuments_.review: Most of the way through this and it is a visually rich and very anxiety-inducing game. With a darkness-based 'sanity' game mechanic which took complete 'inspiration' from (read: lifted from entirely, call the lawyers) Amnesia: Dark Descent and an inventory management scheme that gets in the way at every turn, this game most assuredly brings the pressure in both good and bad ways.A lot of the tension comes from a total sense of helplessness against an ever-present, randomly lethal force as you struggle to find the square block to fit in the square hole. The puzzles you're meant to solve feel arbitrary and and the solutions are poorly-hinted at.This amounts to running around the house depleting resources, turning lights on, looking for a clue all the while the big bad evil force pranks you by closing doors, turning lights off on you, turning on/off appliances, and doing other things often well out of your sight - each with an accompanying musical sting. Most of the time this sting is the only way I know something has happened. Whether or not you see it - it still damages you.Occasionally and arbitrarily, this force will just outright murk you though, jumpscare style - regardless of the sanity mechanic.I still recommend it though, because despite all of this it makes me want to complete it. I can't really explain that.

What's good: Beautiful artwork and detailsGood musicGood ambienceControls seem to function as intendedWhat's bad:Everything other than those things. I know it's brutal and vague, but unfortunately, it's accurate.My experiance upon launching the game:The game starts, I set my gamma balance as requested, then I see the whole opener, and wake up in the hall with the Mary statue. I find a candle which says it needs a lighter, but no lighter to be found. I spend a significant amount of time scouring my surroundings for one, and not finding any. So I put that aside and begin to explore the house for approx. ten min, being introduced to a few of the game's features and mechanics, when suddenly 2 "paranormal events" occur simultaneously, locking me in a pitchblack bathroom. I can't see anything, my monitor is literally just a black screen, and it's not like real life where I can just feel my way around, so I have to go into the options and turn the gamma WAY up just so I can see a door. While all this is happening, the pills I found that are supposed to repair your sanity are all consumed, one by one. Then because I was in the dark for so long, my sanity has gone to ♥♥♥♥. I thought, but that would never happen, because of how this game is built.In this game, there is a mechanic where low sanity causes an increase in "paranormal events", so now LITERALLY EVERY 5 SECONDS, a light goes out plunging me into pitchblack darkness, where I am in now staring at my now, black monitor, trying to get my character to move towards something that triggers a visible interact prompt while being unable to see anything at all. _childDocuments_.review: I got this game when it was in early access and only had one chapter and it was a must have for any fan of the horror game genre back then. Now there are 4 chapters and the game is one of the best horror experience I've had with a video game. amazing atmosphere which always has you tense and on edge. About 10-20 hours of story gameplay when going in blind with a couple more hours on top of that when going for all the achievements.Each chapter is unique and offers a different play style along with the traditional horror game tropes.Inspiration can be seen from the original Resident Evil trilogy in terms of item based puzzles and backtracking through a claustrophobic environment, Silent Hills (P.T. more than anything) level of psychological horror and tension, and a chapter which pays tribute to Outlast's chase simulations and setting. 1 chapter is admittedly not as good as the other 3 in my opinion but the game is by no means a cash grab, walking simulator. Some jumpscares are present but the game has no need to rely on them. Puzzles are challenging but not too obscure. Exploration, perception and experimenting is encouraged.The story is fairly cliche and obscure, and i found myself slightly confused by the time the credits rolled, but the atmosphere, tension and length more than make up for it. A must have addition for any horror fan.

_childDocuments_.review: I was so freaking excited to finally try this game! As a horror streamer who'd not played it before, it was recommended to me over and over and over! So when I finally decided now is the time to play it i was very hyped. I started with Dolores chapter and quickly realizes that from my point of view the game does not at all live up to the hype. People sold this to me as the scariest game ever... and what can I say. The game is so convoluted, that I was so busy being lost and not knowing how to progress, that the scares got fully lost on me. The atmosphere is so wonderful, the visuals stunning, the stories kinda cool but the game design and interfaces are absolutely disappointing. Someone tried to tell me "They did this on purpose, you you would feel lost and confused as the characters. No sir, this is a really bad excuse for bad game design choices. I feel like this wanted to much maybe. Being a PT style walking sim horror, but also implement the sanity system that people loved since the first amnesia, have a good story and make the players feel a lot of things and maybe also a bit of an inventory management game...I did find some people who did not like the game and they said things like "The puzzles are to hard!" but I do not think this is the problem. The problem is finding the puzzles in the first place, or realizing something is supposed to be a puzzle...I gave this a good shot. I played almost 12 hours always hoping it would spark and I would get the love. I did not want to write a bad review. I wanted to love it like others to. Finished Doloes' chapter, and Rakans chapter (which was much better design wise I think) and after the first couple of minutes in Lucy I had to call it quits because I was just furious. I was killed over and over and there was no indication of what I was doing wrong or how I could avoid it or even when she was coming. I do not often put a game down before I finish it, but this time I just did not feel anything positives for the game that could drive me to finish it.Honorable mention to the stair room in Dolores' chapter and the "buying beer in the supermarket" scene. Those were really good! In general the idea of the stories and the visual design aspects where wonderful.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are looking for an actual scary game that doesn't hold your hand whatsoever, pick this up. I have played countless horror games, if you picked a random one that's worth its salt, I have probably either watched it in its entirety or played it myself. I cannot stress enough that this game's status in the horror genre surpasses any other I've played, and gives other well-known games like the Outlast series a run for their money. The game has four to five chapters, depending on how you look at it, to play through. With the first two being easily the scariest to complete. Although the following two are scary in their own right, they mainly serve as a progression in the story, having more (intense) environmental horror scenes than jump scares. The jump scares that do occur throughout the game can either be effective throughout the story's progression, or they are just initially scary and then end up becoming annoying, especially in the chase sequences or if you end up stuck. There are two ways I would suggest playing this game depending on the desired experience:1. Playing the game as it was made without external help is massively challenging in multiple aspects, and in my opinion, becomes immensely more scary to get through. I say this because you will definitely become confused, stuck, and without a sense of direction at some point or another. At which you will progressively lose your sanity, and start to visualize more hallucinations of the demons prowling in the dark. The demons can and will kill you, but the way to remedy this is by taking the pills lying around the house. It is important to note though that there is a finite amount of materials in the house that don't respawn after each chapter, I would have liked to have known that before I took all of the pills in the house prior to even beginning chapter 4. When playing without assistance, you are going to see some freaky stuff, but good luck getting through some of the chapters in doing so.2. The second way to play this game is to have a walk-through for it open while you are playing. There are still plenty of effective jump scares, especially if you are following the guides loosely and are at least attempting to get through it on your own. Perhaps only using the guide as an objective marker would serve best in balancing the game to avoid spoilers of potential scares to come.Overall, I highly recommend this game to anyone who is a fan of the horror genre, particularly if you enjoy intensely horrifying, immersive, mind-bending, story games. I suppose one of the things I liked the most about this game was that all the stories told, including the alleged protagonist, connect in an overarching way, that is if you pay attention to the finer details in every scene and piece of evidence you find.

_childDocuments_.review: ***Initial Review: Read the edit below it***I picked up this game after hearing that it was a very good horror experience with strong P.T. vibes. What you do get is pretty good. The house is unnerving, the sanity effects are ominous, and the current/only monster is creepy as hell, both in the way it looks, as well as the way it moves around and disappears. It's all quite tense.However, there is, and has continued to be a general lack of content. I was under the impression that the game was mostly complete as the page seemed to suggest they only planned on having the game in early access for four months while they finalized the rest of the content. Well, I completed all available content in ~1 1/2 hours ( note that what you see in the screenshots for the game is not representative of what is available, and I'm not sure how much of it will actually be in the final release ) and  many months later and there still hasn't been any content update to the game.This wouldn't be a problem if they perhaps communicated progress through the updates on their steam page. I went as far as going to the Kickstarter, though I am decidedly not one of the backers, to see if there were updates there. Nothing. The most recent update was an update updating the users on how sorry they were for not updating them more often and promising more updates and saying things were being finalized. I also learned that this game had some pretty lofty expectations initially, but didn't raise enough money to reach them ( i.e. multiple endings at 160K, some surprise at 250K , and the game taking place in a town at 1M. It only reached 120K).Now as of current the game feels like a very good demo, but nothing more. I understand why the community would be upset as the estimated delivery date on Kickstarter was 2017, the steam page suggested the full game would be ready sometime early 2019 and now as of mid 2019, there is still only one of three chapters available with no real estimate as to when the second or third will be complete and how much content it will add. It feels dead in the water.For these reasons I am giving it a negative review which is subject to change if and when more content is made available.***EDIT***About two weeks after posting this I was informed that new content was available. At this point I've played through the new content after having started a new game and running back through Lucy's story. If you're observant and don't miss to many items, then you'll get about an hour and a half of additional content  in Dolores chapter. If you're prone to missing stuff and or are a completionist, then there's around 2-3 hours of additional content. This puts the game at around ~3-4 of content currently.While I do like the new chapter, I don't think it's as good as the first. For one the monster/ghost for this chapter isn't nearly as horrific to look at. That's not to say it wasn't creepy, but it wasn't nearly as disturbing as the first. There are a few more jump scares than Lucys chapter and quite a few more Layers of Fear-esque visual gags and general gross out portions of the chapter that are kind of reminiscent of Agony ( you'll know when you get there ), but at no point was I quite as afraid of being caught by the monster. In fact, I felt pretty safe throughout the chapter as there are certain rooms that Dolores wont cross and always contains light so if my sanity started dipping lower than I'd like I could just run in and crouch in the light for a little bit. That and unlike Lucys chapter, the house lights are, for the most part, always available so I didn't get the same sense of urgency or foreboding as I did with the Lucy chapter.While I do appreciate that additional content was added, it's not as much as some people are claiming or as much as one might expect from almost an additional year of development, nor was it as polished as one might expect. There are quite a few visual and what appears to be physics bugs in this chapter. It is early access though so hopefully these will be fixed on the final release or sometime before the next chapter is released. While I'm a tad bit disappointed with the new chapter, I'm going to change my review to positive because I am glad that the developers did not abandon the project like it seemed they were going to and the game is getting closer to feeling like a full game rather than a demo.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could choose a neutral recommendation for this one. Firstly, fantastic ambiance, setting, visuals, sound design, all that jazz. Unfortunately all that is really held back by the gameplay. The hand system and two inventory system is funky to get used to but not a deal breaker, the sanity system I feel is unnecessary and really takes away from the moment, and I spent all my playtime wondering what it was the game wanted me to do even though i'm just one chapter done so far. For instance: in one chapter i'm supposed to avoid flickering lights and spooky sounds because it means i'm about to die from something invisible, but at the same time the game cues me into where to go in the big maze of a house by guiding me with, you guessed it, flickering lights and spooky sounds. Is it where I need to go or sudden death? Who knows? Half the time when I died I didn't know why, and upon reloading and doing the exact same things I would be fine. The sanity system is a steep slope that's hard to climb out of to boot. I loaded up some auto saves after dying only to be instantly killed by an invisible entity a second later I didn't know how to run from. When your sanity gets dangerously low you need pills, but they're super hard to find if you have no lights which you probably don't if your sanity is low in the first place. I feel like I can't take the time to feel spooked either because i'm only worried about my sanity level. I would really really like to enjoy this game and appreciate its magnificent ambiance and get spooked but the gameplay keeps interrupting the fun and replacing it with confusion and comedic untimely deaths instead. Maybe the other chapters are different and I just started out with a bad one, but so far the good in the game is really being held back by the bad. It's not a bad game at all, it just has a few design choices that really step on and cover up what's special about it.

_childDocuments_.review: If its still October when you read this, find another horror game to play this month.I got right up to the very final door in the game, and yet I have not beaten it. I will not be beating Visage, and for good reason.Visage is easily one of the most frustratingly bipolar experiences I have ever had in gaming, and by far one of the most deeply unplayable games out there. There are some stupidly high highs but the lows are so, so low.The reason I will not be beating this game is because after trudging through the entirety of Dolores' chapter as my final chapter I got to the end and the game would not autosave nor allow me to save. The final door bugged out and could not be opened (something that had happened many times during the 7 hours I streamed, we softlocked probably close to 6 or 7 times). I could not save, it was not an option. The game kept telling me it could not autosave either. The nearest autosave that I was forced to reset to was all the way back in the music maze of doors. Almost an entire hours worth of progress, completely wiped.In other, better games this would be frustrating, but because of how close to the end I was I would probably finish it out in those cases. I had *zero* desire to replay any sections of Delores' chapter, and most of my problems stem from some very core issues in this game. I called it quits right there.As always, credit where credit is due. This game (aside from some animations) looks very good. The sounds are great and the scares *can* be great. Lucy's chapter is a highlight, although the instakills on the demon in her chapter are frustrating thanks to stupidly long load times. There was even one point that I actually caught her with the camera flash, the thing that is supposed to deter her, and yet she still instakilled me. While it is frustrating to be reset and have to sit through a long loading screen, I think the way the demon works is more indicative of what is frustrating about this game than anything else. While you can play it without one, this is THE most deeply unplayable game I have ever played thanks to its mechanics being janky but more importantly, the absurdly cryptic, confusing and tedious puzzles. It is almost a requirement to have a guide handy for when you get stuck because you will get stuck."Puzzles" is a strong word, as some of the solutions didn't even make sense once I read the cheats to the puzzle. I was fine in Lucy's chapter, had to cheat a few times in Rakan's chapter and in Delores' chapter I basically had to cheat the whole time. The map of the house changes completely for that chapter and each of the puzzles usually needs something from another puzzle in the house to progress through these mirror rooms. They act as separate challenges but still connect thematically to one another. There was a lot of "Really, thats how that works?" and I do realize I sound as though I have all complaints right now. That is not the case, there are some very high highs like I said. The themes and story hidden behind all the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ are great, but basically every active decision the developers made about HOW you play the game hurt it. The inventory system is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ nightmare. I had to drop things constantly to pick up something and use it for half a second then go back or god forbid drop the sledgehammer in a puzzle then have to trek down to the basement to pick it up again. That journey to the basement takes about 2 full minutes, just to grab something to use once on a mirror. In cases like that, I am fully fine with you suspending realism and pretending the character has a sledgehammer sling. There was just so much ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ backtracking to get items and then the way that you use the items is annoying too. By the end I figured it out, but it didn't really matter by that point.As far as the actual scares in this horror game, they aren't all good. Lucy's chapter is relatively strong, and easily the highlight of the game. Finding the box of light switches was great.Rakan's chapter just didn't do it for me. The faceless creatures were a bit spooky but even though Rakan himself is like 10 feet tall, the slow crutching after me wasn't very scary. It suffers from Outlast syndrome where after the first time you get caught the enemy stops being scary and more annoying to run away from.Delores' chapter was the least scary. Her character model looks like, as someone in my chat called it, a Bethesda model. The face is ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up and it looks like one of the ghouls from Fallout 4. Any actual jumpscares are also lost in me being frustrated by the confusing and overly complex mechanics of this chapter, I don't think I got scared once here.I'll be honest. The scariest part of Visage is actually having to play it. From what I've been told watching me have a bad time was pretty funny on my stream, but the experience of actually having to go through this game is just plain unfun. It is abundantly clear that the developers are talented, and while I realize that budget is a part of this and there wasn't a huge crew working on it, budget had nothing to do with the inventory being wonky as hell and the structure of the last chapter. I can overlook a game not looking great, but Visage does look great, mostly. I can overlook a game not having a good story or atmosphere, but Visage does mostly. Its the moment to moment where you interact with the systems in place that this game suffers. I think that if they actually have a real budget and lay the ♥♥♥♥ off of the annoying puzzles and kill their habit of making things tedious for no reason, they might make a really great game someday. This game is not that.I review games on Youtube, and originally was going to make a full highlight of my stream of it and do an in depth review with direct examples, but watching back the VOD actually made me annoyed even a day later. The game just kept breaking and softlocking on me and some of the mechanics just don't make sense. I would very much not recommend purchasing this game, but more so playing it. Even if its something you get for free, do yourself the favor, save yourself the high blood pressure and pass on this one. While I understand why people rant and rave about this, the things that make a game a game are poorly made here. It is not fun to experience because getting to the good moments requires far too much effort and it ends up being more about doing chores than getting spooked. Honestly, seeing what "game" they developed, I wish they made this a walking sim instead. They very much chose to include game elements rather than just have it be something you walk and run around in, and its worse off as a game, a story and a horror experience for it.

_childDocuments_.review: For me, the etalon of horror is Silent Hill 2. Never ever played a game which gave me that kind of scare... until now. Visage is the game we horror fans were waiting for! The atmosphere is just amazingly terrifying, everything looks beautiful and detailed. You just feel so alone and helpless walking around. The sounds... Damn, the sounds are perfect! Especially the sound of the ghost, which has those big nails is so scary, that when I heard it first I got shocked, I was like oh my god, what now? What the hell is this? And then I got killed. If Death makes a sound, when he comes for you, that should be it.I loved the parts where you had to think, look around, or remember for older places where you've been. The game plays with your mind in a way like no other game does. You even get scared when browsing the settings menu, because everything happens in real time. The whole house is haunted, paranormal events happen everywhere, and can happen anytime. No event happens twice in the same place, they are not scripted, which I found damn amazing. You'll always feels paranoia wandering around... Oh, and it's pretty long for one chapter (it will have 4), tho I like searching every cm.Some small graphical glitches here and there, but the 1st chapter is 100% doable, you even get achievements.I recommend this game for all horror fans, it's an absolute 10/10 in the genre! The best horror game in many years, can't wait for Chapter 2, and for the whole game!

_childDocuments_.review: Terrifying with plenty of ambiguity that encourages you to come to your own conclusions about what took place in the game. Each chapter focuses on a different horror element from supernatural to psychological. Some clunky resource management but nothing too difficult to overcome.Your jaw will drop, or Lucy will tear it off for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Probably my favorite horror game. Very creative and very atmospheric, heavy inspiration from PT. If you're someone who gets scared from games or movies this will definitely get you. Game has some bugs and some lulls due to ambiguous objectives, created almost solely out of the sheer fact that there are too many unnecessary items to pick up and investigate, leaving you at a complete mental loss with where you have yet to pick up an item and spin it around looking for your next puzzle piece.Overall A+ game even with it's few cons.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is one of the best horror games 2018. The gameplay feels good, only the inventory is a little bit confusing. The sound design for this game is amazing. It's just a lot of fun and I am sad I finished the early acces version. I am really hyped for the full release. I can recommend itIt is also really good optimized 70-100+ fps with gtx 1050ti and i5 7500.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best horror games i have ever played, every chapter introduces new mechanics that keeps the gameplay fresh for the whole lenght of the game (about 10 hours to complete). It can realy scare the **** out of you, the game does not relly on cheap tricks, there is an omnipresent eerie atmosphere and sense of dread. All of the jump scares are well executeted and unpredictable. The audio is just amazing, and so is the graphics (besides a few low-res textures), i also haven't experienced any bugs or glitches. In terms of story i am not going to spoil anything, but once again the game does a tremendous job in telling a compelling and deep story about addiction, greef, and mental problems. The only downside are the controls that can be a bit clunky at times, also the system of losing you mental sanity in the dark is sometimes unreliable (you start to lose sanity in full light and the game tells you not to stay in the dark for too long XD).Overall after playing the early access i knew that the game will be great, nevertheless i was impressed by the final version and i can't but recomend it to every fan of horror games.For me it is a strong 9,5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Visage has to be the best horror game that I have played so far. This game puts you in terrifying situations without even a slingshot to defend yourself. _childDocuments_.review: Excellent game. Was able to keep up a tense atmosphere throughout. I wouldn't say it's terrifying, but it kept me in suspense and I struggle to find horror games that do even that, so I enjoyed it. I also enjoyed some of the more puzzle aspects of the game. As others have mentioned, finding a guide will be helpful. I had to look up what to do a couple times cause there wasn't enough direction, but it wasn't too bad and didn't feel super convoluted. The only thing I really had an issue with was the cutscenes. Some of them felt really slow and took me out of it a bit. Other than that though it was a very enjoyable game and I'd definitely recommend

Bugs, glitches, missing animations and camera queues and pretty unclear objectives hinder this game more than they should.All in all, good scares, good atmosphere, but still incredibly rough around the edges and not as creative as it could be.

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the most terrifying game I have played to date, and I don't think it will be topped anytime soon. As a fan of the horror genre (both games and movies), Visage delivers a positively conflicting experience in that it was exactly what I was hoping for in a paranormal-centric horror game, but at the same time it made me want to stop playing many times throughout because of that exact reason. In terms of critiques - some of the discoverables can be quite hard to find without looking it up online which could then lead to the player running out of lighter-fluid (rip), and some parts of the story was personally a bit cryptic hence there were points in time were I continued playing for the sole reason of perpetuating the nightmare without much regard for the story. P.S. Streaming the game for a group of friends makes for some hilarious, memorable moments of synchronised screaming.

_childDocuments_.review: Atmosphere is great, deeply enjoyed this game so far, though have some issues with it that I hope are addressed.Pros: Visuals look niceSanity/light mechanic is neatLights being turned off/destroyed is a cute way to mess with you.Cons:Puzzles/Objectives are difficult to follow at times (). It doesn't need to be EASY, but it should be straight forward enough that you stumble across it without much trouble ().The music gets a bit repetitive over time, and it can lead to LESS tension once you get used to it.Some physics glitches are present. Some doors wouldn't allow me to open them unless I was able to "bump" them from specific angels to open. One of these blocked a key item.Overall I think it's a good start. Got a few hours out of it and haven't finished. It does what it's supposed to do, which is spoop you like crazy. Want to see more as it progresses. My hope is that rather than get on to new content, that they spend time polishing up what is out there to make it really shine. This might be a good candidate for an episodic release schedule.
_childDocuments_.name: Visage

_childDocuments_.review: This is overall a very solid horror game and really excels best at offering an incredibly diverse variety of horror concepts. There's body horror, religious iconography horror, paranormal event horror, chase mechanics, psychological and surrealist horror, and even some grounded emotional sections that illustrate some troubling aspects of real life. Longevity seems exceptional as well given that I'm right at halfway through with 8 hours of play time. The main drawback of the game is that it suffers from clunky controls and quest/puzzle design. You'll fumble around with key objects and items and almost certainly have to look up a walkthrough at some point as you go, particularly if you take a break from this game and need to pick up where you left off. Additionally, the game frequently changes the rules about how you're supposed to react to things or treat certain situations which results in a bit of frustrating trial and error. I'm often frustrated by these aspects in the moment but time and again I find that the payoff is worth the trouble as the game continually sticks the landing in exploring so many different horror genres and providing novel and highly memorable horror experiences.
_childDocuments_.name: Visage

_childDocuments_.review: This game is super spooky and does a lot of really wonderful things that will get you uncomfortable. But if you're not a fan of directionless games, this might not be for you. It often expected you to learn through failure, which would be fine it it didn't happen so very often. There was a section where I died very often to learn what the game was expecting of me, and it really stopped being fun.But that's not to say it's a bad game! I just personally think it would have been far more enjoyable if it offered a bit more direction. The game play changes often, which is fantastic, but it doesn't explain what new things it wants from you when it does. I personally can't recommend, but I can see why people enjoy as well.

_childDocuments_.review: A Outlast-esque thriller that does well to keep the suspense and tension high throughout the entire game, not afraid to explore more controversial themes and subjects. First chapter was nearly flawless and hope that the 3rd chapter doesn't rely so much on jumpscares as the second one. If the studio keeps up with this game and continues taking their time in crafting the game it'll be a classic for sure. 9/10.

_childDocuments_.review: And to think, this is an early access...Flawless horror by any aspect! Not for the faint hearted! Jumpscares and shivers guaranteed. Definitely a must for every horror fan..The devs did some serious work over here, well organized, and you realize it from the very beginning 'til the last moments of the game.You are Dwayne and the story takes place inside a house which some tragedies occurred, a house that looks like some kind of maze and as you progress, you'll find some spots (which most of it are in Dolores chapter) that leads you to another places of the house..like entering a ghostly dimension! And thank goodness seems they work like a safe places....from Her, in those spots! In Lucy's chapter it works differently. You'll find out!Your only help against the dark, is a lighter, candles, some light bulbs and a camera. After some long uses the lighter will ran out and you'll need to find another. Or you can use the camera's flash to light areas of the house but soon will make you uneasy..Playing time i think is long enough and satisfying and varies from player to player (especially if you're looking for hidden collectibles also).Graphics of the game are in great detail in that perfect enviroment, haunting sound effects all over, creaking floors, flickering lights, sinister and creepy atmosphere with P.T. influence! Also there was a couple scenes they reminded me a Silent Hill "touch". It's 3 a.m. ..nightmare is already here..stay in the light by any means!

_childDocuments_.review: After a horror free year of decent titles imo, this little gem pops up. If you like horror, suspense, slow pace and hearing and feeling your own heart beat every step of discovery, this is screaming at you to be played.The artwork, graphics rendering and sound design are stunning for detail. The controls on a controller are  a bit clunky and fidgety for now, but that might be ironed out. The graphics are solid and detailed. It's a VR must, so i hope it is done for VR eventually. I don't scare easily at horrors, but VR would be a whole different ballgame, and rest assured, once again, i would pee ma kilt if it ever comes to VR ! Backing this game would be a no brainer and wholly worth it for the finished article, if this early access is anything to go by.

name: Freedom Planet 2
detailed_description: Join the heroes of Avalice as they face their greatest challenge yet! An ancient terror has emerged from the depths of the ocean. Merga, a water dragon from Avalice's oldest and deadliest war, has been freed from her crystal prison as a consequence of the Kingdom Stone's destruction. War is imminent once again, but this time, the heroes are split between sides. As friendships are tested, will the girls stand united when Bakunawa rises? Features Four playable characters available from the start, each with her own unique fighting style: Lilac the Dragon (Speed Type), Carol the Wildcat (Brawler Type), Milla the Hound (Explorer Type), and Neera the Frost Knight (Power Type). Explore the world of Avalice in Adventure mode. Travel through a sprawling world map filled with treasures, landmarks, and over 100 unique animal NPCs to interact with and catalog. Dive straight into the action with Classic Mode. Accessible after completing Adventure mode once, this streamlined navigation screen gives you quick access to stages and other important features without the need for travelling. Test your fighting skills in the Battlesphere arena. Once reached, the Battlesphere hosts a variety of challenges featuring enemies and bosses you've previously encountered, along with brand new surprises! Parry enemy attacks with the new Guard button. If timing's not your thing, an Auto Guard option in the Assist settings makes your character automatically guard against attacks if possible. A new Revival system gives you a chance to clinch victory during very close battles. Use it wisely - it costs a stock and two more hits will knock you out again! Power up your heroine with customizable potions. Collect and mix a rainbow of ingredients that boost her vitality in different ways, such as increasing her stock count, shield durability, attack power, speed, and more. Change the rules with a multitude of equippable items. Amulets and Charms provide helpful effects, while Brave Stones make combat harder in exchange for bonus crystals.

short_description: The fast paced platforming of Freedom Planet returns! Become a full-time cartoon heroine and use abilities and items suited to your play style to explore the world of Avalice and defend its animal citizens!

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not good at writing detailed reviews, so this is all I'm gonna say.In a world dominated by sprawling open world games with realistic graphics, this humble retro platformer managed to keep my anticipation for it higher than anything else for the 6 years I was waiting for its release. And you know what? It's already worth it. Highly recommend it whether you're already a fan of the first game or if you're new to the series because it delivers the same fast paced, incredibly fun gameplay of the first game with vast graphical improvements, *many* new features, quality of life improvements, and of course, the new story.Hats off to GalaxyTrail for setting a fine example for the gaming industry. It took a long time, far longer than even they anticipated, but they used that time to make sure they delivered a quality game to the fans.It's really nice to be back in Avalice.
_childDocuments_.name: Freedom Planet 2

_childDocuments_.review: Freedom Planet 2 is like Freedom Planet but with more Freedom. And more Planet. And more good.It's good.Go play it.EDIT: I have fully completed Freedom Planet 2, so here's some more in-depth opinions.The game is very fun, and the story is a wonderful improvement over the last game. It's also an improvement over the last one in basically every relevant fashion. But it's not perfect, and my criticisms mainly come in the form of two areas.1. The S rank system. The way the HUD presents it is confusing, as it makes it appear that collecting gems is actually important for getting them when it's exclusively about that multiplier. In addition, the entire challenge is completely ruined by three bravestones - Expensive Stocks, No Revives, and No Stocks, as getting the S ranks requires not dying with two brave stones equipped (or not taking damage with one brave stone/no items equipped, but that's far more difficult as-is), and these brave stones quite literally only punish you for dying rather than actually making the run more difficult. I would suggest a rebalancing of the multiplier bonus you get from the various bravestones to make the others more appealing to use.2. Neera. Lilac is fun to play and a surprising powerhouse, Carol is my favourite to play as and feels even better than FP1, and Milla remains an amazing character locked behind needing good skill to access, but Neera feels lacking in comparison. Her mobility options are poor as they require utilising enemies and the floor to make use of, making most of them completely unattractive to use, Focus conflicts with the intended purpose of Guard, forcing you to choose between avoiding damage or conserving your Energy for where you need it, and in actual combat her attacks are close range and precise but don't deal quite enough damage to make up for that finicky precision, despite being labelled as the brawler character.That being said, this game is still absolutely amazing, and the 8 years of development have most definitely been worth it!
_childDocuments_.name: Freedom Planet 2

_childDocuments_.review: Hard to find anything Freedom Planet 2 doesn't do that greatly improves over the first game.Everything about the sequel is DAMN good, from the gameplay and visuals to the music. Mix that all together, throwing in a fourth playable character while also enhancing upon the pre-existing trio from FP1, and you got yourself an extremely solid platformer that'll bring back those ol' Treasure vibes.I'll always be thankful to Sabrina and the team over at GalaxyTrail for not only gracing us with an absolute banger of an indie title, but also bringing this wonderful game to fruition at a particularly rough point in my life and indirectly helping me push my way into a better spot. Much love to you guys!
_childDocuments_.name: Freedom Planet 2

_childDocuments_.review: Look at this absolute unit of an action platforming game.Look at this enormous chunker-on-a-bone with over 25 fully-fledged levels. Each different than the last.Look at this thick behemoth of a production values, outclassing everything in its genre.Yep! That’s Freedom Planet: The Second: Electric Boogaloo baby. First game is still to this day an incredible benchmark of quality for 2D action platformers and straight out of the gate I can say that most of the good qualities you could attribute to that game, apply to the sequel 1:1. Sequel retained it's identity as a high-speed joyride: mixing gameplay mechanics from multiple sources (mostly Sonic, Mega Man X and Gunstar Heroes), that are delivered with excellent feeling controls, creative gimmicks and stages, jaw-dropping setpieces and multiple characters to choose from with vastly different playstyles.Freedom Planet 2 never ever drops down from a set baseline of quality at any given moment and despite few minor flaws or disappointments (in comparison to the first game), it maintains a package of speed and solid quality that could go through military grade blast doors.Improvements over the first game include a higher fidelity graphics which exchange Genesis charm of the first game for the gorgeous details and colors of Hi-Bit aesthetics, which is awe inducing in multiple places. All playable girls each got themselves major or minor changes to streamline their gameplay plus new 4th hero joins the fray with difficult but definitely unique playstyle.Game also addresses most of the common complaints from the first game. Bosses are still tough as nails, but this time not only I didn’t encounter any mishaps with missing telegraphs or unfair moves, but also a new item system was put in place that helps you modulate the amount of pain you can induce on yourself. This system is incredibly flexible and shall you look for either smooth sailing or ultra-nightmare experience, you can set up those pretty easily.Story is also a good improvement over the first game, especially when it comes to pacing. There are no longer 20 minute cutscenes between levels. Odd tone shifts are gone as well. Plot still isn’t noticeably unique and themes lack subtlety, but great character interactions never left and it is a joy to hear and see. Highlight goes to some minor villains that do often steal the show because how entertaining they are. It’s just a little shame that the main antagonist isn’t as memorable this time around. She is not Lord Brevon unfortunately and she doesn’t have the impact on narrative and gameplay his shenanigans brought.I also need to bring up, that while there are absolutely truckton amount of levels, those are a little less dense and evolving this time around. I do miss the two act structure of the first game quite a bit. I believe this was made to keep the game’s scope in check (which you can also see by some enemy recycling mid-game).However as I say that, the individual levels themselves are designed with no major flaws and they are still as fun, creative, fast, unique, colorful and expertly designed as in the first game. Again, nothing goes here below that baseline.The only thing that sadly could be considered below that aformentioned baseline is the OST. It's a big shame, since first game was all bangers all the time and it's a big part of first game's charm. FP2 delivers a lot of great stage themes and character motifs but boss themes mostly lack that excitement pill that elevated the first game. I wouldn’t be honest to myself if I didn’t mention this small disappointment.But that’s the end of downers. Most of other users mention the 7 year wait for the game and if it was worth it or not. I’m biased here – I’m a fan of a first game and of course I could weigh in on this question. However, I do consider this a bad metric to actually answer what does Steam ask you.  - to a random Joe that might stumble over this game an wonder if it’s worth their hard earned cash.To those people I will first say, Have a nice day! And secondly… It is a bit expensive, but Freedom Planet 2 seriously blows away all the competition out of the water with sheer amount of quality content that will occupy you for hours on end. First playthrough took me 9 hours which is double of the first game! With ONE character and NO side objectives! We are talking about Hollow Knight levels of measuring contest and everybody knows how that game was severely underpriced at launch.Freedom Planet 2 deliver top-of-the-line 2D action gameplay nowhere to be seen on the market, despite few flaws here and there. I’m still fresh of finishing the game. I might change my stance on few things later, but at the end of the day, like its predecessor, it’s a top tier gem waiting to be discovered and cherished by you and your friends. I highly recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Forget Sonic, there is a new here in town!In Freedom Planet 2 you and the heroes of Avalice fight against the greatest threat ever.An ancient danger has awakened in the depths of the ocean.Merga, a water dragon from the time of Avalice's oldest war has been freed from her crystal prison and war is about to break out, but our heroes are divided.Will the girls manage to stay together during these difficult times? _childDocuments_.review: Literal Masterpiece. 7 years in development well spent, and they DELIVERED! First off, this game's gameplay improves massively over the first game, which was already fairly good on its own. This? This is just the perfect 2D speed platformer. It's so good it basically puts every 2D Sonic game to SHAME.It's gonna take you a little while playing around with the controls to understand how to make the most out of the mechanics in this game, so please do not get discouraged early, there is a very rewarding learning curve as you progress through the game. Not to mention that many of the stages are meant to be replayed, either to lower the time, or find new secrets. Your first run of a stage might take you, idk 7~10 minutes for most. Then once you get acquainted with the mechanics, you'll see that time be cut in half if not even more. All 4 playable characters have their own strengths and weaknesses, but they all perform about the same once you've picked up some practice. Often you'll find yourself going to different parts of the stages with different characters. The story? TLDR: It's a story about colonialism with a tragic character. Not spoiling much else, but do go out of your way to collect the time capsules, they hold some VERY juicy information regarding the lore. Another thing of note is that each character has specific cutscenes throughout the story, so I highly recommend playing through it with all 4, or at the very least with Lilac and Carol, since those two hold the most specific cutscenes of all the 4 characters. The 2D sprites in this game are BEAUTIFUL. The main 4 characters are extremely expressive, the side characters have pretty good variety, the NPCs are honestly really cute, I love how bats look in this game. I know that the lead dev's favorite animal is a bat, so no wonder why they look awesome. The stages are wildly varied, with many details hidden in the background, as well as other attention to detail elements that you'd only noticed if you stopped to look. THE VOICE ACTING, OH BROTHER THE VOICE ACTING. General Serpentine's VA is awesome, love hearing him. Both Neera and Merga have crazy good emotional performances, love them both. Milla's voice fits her character way too well, and a massive improvement over the first game. Same for Carol. Glad to hear Lilac again. _childDocuments_.review: Ever wonder what games would look like if 3D didn't happen and major studios kept pouring the lion's share of their effort and resources into 2D games? Well you can stop wondering, cause Freedom Planet 2 is what that timeline looks like. Bigger, better, faster, stronger, everything about it screams "Extra."The most immediate and striking improvement you'll notice is the pixel art. It is  detailed. On everything, from playable characters and stages down to each individual NPC and bossfight. You jaw will drop the first time you fight one of the larger bosses. Then it will keep going through the floor when you realize there's 39(!) of them. You'll also notice that almost everything has a unique track on the OST - each level, hub area, and subsection of the map has a unique, certified-GalaxyTrail-quality musical piece attached to it.On the gameplay side of things, the addition of items and the guard button makes for combat that's easy to get into (just like the original) but satisfying to master for the game's later, more complex fights. And you'll have plenty of time to master it as well, on the whopping 24(!) levels that you'll be traversing. Their count does not diminish their quality - each one is tightly designed, with different tempo and memorable gimmicks to make them stand out. It also does not diminish the storytelling. Quite the opposite - the new episodic chapter approach makes it so the plot advances at a brisk pace, whilst also finding plenty of time to develop each character's personal stakes.Throw in high replayability in the form of 4 playable characters, the ability to talk to over 100 NPCs (who all have unique sprites!), tons of extra challenges, and an effin' museum for the spritework, and you get a dizzyingly rich package for the asking price. The only possible flaw that I can think of is how that sheer size makes for less cohesive narration: The episodic format means that the player characters get a lot of air time, but the main conflict and villain do not. This can often leave you feeling like the story is... unfocused, that certain levels are unrelated side-quests at best, even though they are still mandatory. Other than that, though? Practically flawless.

_childDocuments_.review: Sequels are never easy, even more so when the original is so beloved. Balancing the things that made the original great with innovations that make a sequel stand out is a difficult act, and not one every studio can succeed at. When done poorly, players just get more of the same, or in the worst cases, a whole that is lesser than the sum of its parts. When done well, players get a fresh experience that iterates on the original's successes while avoiding its flaws.Freedom Planet, a love-letter to the 16-bit era, was one such beloved title, and the developers had their work cut out for them. With such a fantastic first entry, the sequel would need to do so much more, while still keeping the spirit of the original intact. A seven-year development period followed, and at long last, the game was released. But how did it do? Was it a fantastic follow-up to the original, or does it fall short--Of course it's good. It's really good. It's so good. It's one of the best 2D platformers, period. We can cut the theatrics now.Almost everything the first game did, the second game does just as well, if not better. The artwork is more detailed and thematic, and the visual effects are fantastic. The gameplay is refined far beyond the first game, giving the characters a new array of well-balanced abilities that give them versatility without making them more powerful. Every character is fun to play. Nearly every stage flows immaculately, even on a first play. The mechanics are beautifully balanced, allowing for a surprising degree of player expression without any blatantly overpowered options. The sound effects are great, and the voice acting is as well. The music is thematic and fits the setting perfectly. The story, probably the most contentious part of both games, has a great degree of depth and thought put into it, and it avoids the tonal and pacing issues of the first game's.The game has been out for two years or so now, but I bought it a little bit later. I just got around to writing a review because I couldn't find the right words to accurately express how good this game is. Even this barely scratches the surface of how I feel. There's so much to it, I couldn't possibly cover it all.Are you on the fence if you should buy this game? Here's a quick guide:*  This game is everything you could ever want in a sequel and more. You should buy FP2.*  FP2 improves the weak aspects of FP1 while improving the strong ones. You should buy FP2.*  FP2 is a great game, even on its own. You should buy FP2.*  FP2 isn't the same, but it's similar, and it's very good. You should buy FP2.*  FP2 is a good 2D platformer. You should buy FP2.*  FP2 might change your mind. You should buy FP2.*  The console releases are coming up very soon! You should buy FP2.*  Now you are. Also, you should buy FP2.Also, there's a free sample version of the first stage, so try that out! The full game is even better.Okay, that's all. Buy the game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is honestly one of my favorite platformers of all time, and I loved FP1 heavily.It's got pretty sprites, lots of levels that don't overstay their welcome, and good replayability.And the parry mechanic in this game is really good and fun to use, major points for that mechanic alone.Also, it comes with decent item loadouts, which I liked.The only few things that I prefer in FP1 over FP2 are the following:The OST in this game is still great and lively, it's just that FP1 does that better imo, some of the soundtracks feel like they're messing something to make 'em pop.Overall, great music, Nalao Lake is probably my favorite.I personally think the story is structured better than in the first one, but at the same time FP1 has the better main villain, .Honestly, Lord Brevon is one of my favorite indie villains, smuggy and violent. You might call me an edgy for it, I don't mind, I feel like game stories should bring out the violence in villains, I mean he's a villain, of course he would be violent, it's makes the fiction a bit more real, but not too real imo.Merga in the other hand just didn't hit the mark for me, I don't really hate her or even dislike her, she's just not as exciting as Brevon, not even close.Good villain introduction, and a cool ass ship she got, but spoiler alert in the true ending, it made her lamer for me personally.Not bad, but it isn't Brevon.This game has 4 playable character, 3 of them are fun to play, but the character that I was interested in the most to try, Neera Li, came as a bit of a disappointment.She's the "hardest" to play yes, I usually love playing the challenging characters, but she's really not that fun to play, I could get into details why, but I'll just she's doesn't feel as rewarding as playing the other 3 characters.Overall, a fantastic game, shame it released at a very bad time, I wish it was more popular if it had a proper release date.

_childDocuments_.review: Probably one of my favourite platformers of all time. Great gameplay, story, and music. Definitely worth picking up if you're looking for something new to play.I can describe the gameplay best as a mix of Sonic, Rocket Knight/Sparkster, and Gunstar Heroes, but improves on all of them significantly. The movement and combat is fluid, and unlike Sonic where you take damage on enemy contact (which slows the pace to a crawl if you're trying to avoid damage) enemies have to land various telegraphed attacks, giving you an opportunity to dodge, parry, or attack, making it feel a lot faster paced/less stop-and-go.The game features multiple characters with their own mechanics, attack combos, and movement physics, which adds replayability to the game and depth to the combat and platforming. Some of the speed-running strategies people have come up with for this game using the different characters are honestly quite insane.

_childDocuments_.review: First thing I want to say before I get into this review, I thought this was a fine game. Yes I know its a negative review but that will be explained later.Freedom Planet 2 was a game I was waiting to play for several years after I played and enjoyed the hell out of Freedom Planet. While I enjoyed this game, I feel like it completely failed to live up to its predecessor's legacy. Pros:-The platforming is really good. The momentum, speed and physics are very fun and it feels/plays similar to the original game which is great. I was very glad it was like this for this game.-The updated sprites look really good, lots of characters got huge visual upgrades and the backgrounds within the game look great.-The hub worlds which I thought would be pretty bad addition to this game, were surprisingly nice to have. They felt like needed breaks in-between the story and game play.-Character interactions were great, there was a lot of comedy that got me laughing (especially mayor zao, phenomenal job on his part).Cons:This is going to be a long one, I really wish I had less complaints with these games-Combat. I didn't like how this game wanted to become more of an action platformer. In the original, bosses took damage when you hit their weakpoint. In this game you have to hit the weakpoint multiple times just to remove one bar of health (I beat the game with lilac so it might be easier with other characters). I think adding hp bars to the bosses was dumb as it felt more annoying to deal with bosses compared to its predecessor. It also makes me feel as if I'm playing a megaman zero or megaman x game instead of something like sonic. I understand why they did it as they wanted to move the series away from being a sonic clone, but I believe they perfected it in the original. -Backgrounds. While I do love the backgrounds, it really makes it hard to tell what I can and cannot jump on and this has lead me to die several times within the game.-Sprites. The only sprite change that I didn't like was Lilac's. I was always a fan of her original design, other than that everyone else's sprites are very good.-Story. While I don't think the story is too bad or too good, there definitely felt like various moments were shoehorned in to add more of a dramatic tone shift. That mixed with the limited sprites for the characters made some of those moments feel awkward or failed to get my attention.-Guarding. Guarding is super awkward to the point where I don't know if I'm actually guarding properly or it just doesn't work because I still end up taking damage.-Level design. While some of the levels in the design are really fun to play through, a lot of levels later on feel really poorly designed. The puzzle levels were obviously very annoying because they're puzzles. There were times where I would get hit by projectiles that were off screen or I was completely unable to dodge an enemies attack at all because I was simply unable to see them. The inclusion of guard is only because they couldn't properly design levels without you taking a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ of damage. I don't understand why the level design ended up this way because they did a great job with levels in the first game.-Music. There were a few songs in this game that were pretty good, but for the most part it is all super forgettable. The first game had some of the best tracks I've heard in a video game and when compared to this its just very sad to see.-Spoiler - Another spoiler -Glitches. I had gotten "softlocked" on 3 separate occasions during this game and they were all when I had gotten pretty far into a stage. It felt annoying that I had to keep restarting/reloading to a prior checkpoint because I was "too fast" for the game.Overall, I really wanted this game to be just as great as the original. When I played that first demo, I definitely knew something was up with this game and I tempered my expectations. While I've only done a run of one character, that being lilac, I do plan on playing as the rest of them and seeing how their respective playthroughs work. This is a good game and I don't hate it, but in good faith I cannot recommend this to someone who's played and loved freedom planet.

_childDocuments_.review: Y'ever wait six and a half years for a game to come out, and it's everything you ever wanted when it does? No disappointments, no missed potential, just a perfect grand slam of an experience from front to back that validated that years of desperate thirsting? Not everyone has, but Freedom Planet 2 was exactly that for me. I admit, I was not exactly the most patient person. Especially in the early years, I look back on some of my desperate pleading for the game to come out as kinda cringe, letting my hype get in the way of wanting Galaxy Trail to have all the time they needed to deliver in spades. But as I kept seeing previews, I not only realized that I needed to calm down and be patient, but that I was in for a delicious treat. And boy, was I right.Freedom Planet 2 exemplifies the idea of what exactly a follow-up can do to truly succeed. Not just copy and paste the original with some fresh paint, not unnecessarily changing everything for the sake of "being different", and certainly not the modern, cynical AAA experience of a minimum-viable skinnerbox with a fancy cosmetic storefront. This is a . It takes what made the first game great, compounded on those strengths, trimmed away the fattier issues, made logical improvements across the board, and did everything it could to validate its existence as a follow-up.Gameplay is pretty familiar to those who played the original, but improvements are immediately noticeable. Every character's moveset feels fantastic with very little jank or redundancy. The camera's auto-zoom feels fantastic during high-speed sections. The new guard mechanic feels like something that was always meant to be there. The level designs feel just that much more distinct and tightened up. The social spaces in Adventure Mode feel so much better for the game's story than just having Adventure Mode only be a bunch of cutscenes like the first game. Brave Stones and Potions are a brilliant alternative to a conventional difficulty system. It's polished to a mirror sheen, and it's so fantastic to just sit back and enjoy thoroughly.Another particular strength I have to point out is the art direction. The first game had an interesting art style, but sometimes felt just a little close to the Sonic fan game it started life as, particularly in regards to character design. Not only does Freedom Planet 2 heavily redesign most of its cast to great success, but proportions and details in the character designs truly make them feel as original as they could be. Additionally, with the work that went into the game's social spaces for Adventure Mode, as well as the genuinely fantastic-looking environments for the levels, Avalice feels fully realized as a setting. It's not just a vague mental map of where places could be, wondering how the level environments diegetically fit into the world. Everything fits together and looks organic. Shang Tu's beautiful ivory city among the water, Shang Mu's neon urban sprawl, Shuigang's humble snow-capped village look, Parusa's beautiful tropics... They all come together to make the levels you run through feel just that bit alive.The story of Freedom Planet 1 was something I struggled with early in. It obviously wasn't the primary thing you were there for, but it often struggled to hold my attention. And in two specific cases, felt like sudden, polarizing tonal shifts that came out of nowhere. While I eventually embraced it for what it was, Adventure Mode was something I never really felt compelled to touch again after doing my first run with each character. Freedom Planet 2, though? Significant improvement. Not only does a vast majority of the voice acting feel much better with less of a Saturday morning cartoon vibe to it, with many actors () being able to fully carry an emotional moment, but there's just significantly better flow to story scenes, better lines for the script across the board, better charm and charisma for a lot of the cast... Better everything! Rather than impatiently waiting for a cutscene to end, I was always thoroughly engaged in seeing what was happening next. Going to the social spaces in Adventure Mode and talking to all the characters I could find was a treat I always relished. And with each new playthrough, I was excited to see the few character-exclusive scenes and moments that I didn't get to see from Lilac's perspective on my initial run. Just such an improvement.I could keep going, especially on things like the music. Amazing soundtrack, by the way, grab a copy on Bandcamp! But I think my point is thoroughly made. I waited six and a half years to finally play this game. Not only did it come out in time to basically be a belated birthday present to myself, but it completely validated every year, every month, week, day I waited to find out just when I could finally play the sequel to my favourite indie game of all time. Having played it pretty extensively now, and getting VERY close to reaching 100% completion, I know that the sequel succeeds the original as my favourite indie of all time.Play it. Right now. I'm serious. Open your wallet, pull out your credit card, and throw your money at the faces of Sabrina DiDuro and her team at GalaxyTrail. They deserve it so much, and I guarantee that if you even marginally kinda like platformers, you will love Freedom Planet 2 like I did.

_childDocuments_.review: Freedom Planet 2 has been a great time and am very happy with how it turned out. I was and am a huge fan of the first game. I remember getting it on the Wii U back in 2015 and enjoying the hell out of it. Now we have a sequel and how does it far against the first? Well, there are certainly differences. The combat has had some tweaks, mainly with the addition of a dodge/parry. I think this does make the fighting overall easier, but more fluid and engaging.The Characters have also gotten some tweaks to their combat and how they traverse the stage. Lilac pretty much follows the same concept as the first game. Carol is still Carol, but instead of the move where she does a flurry of kicks, she now has a circular-bladed weapon that she throws, and can also jump too, giving her more movement options. I can't comment on Milla however, because I didn't play her through the first game. The visuals and art style have also gotten a huge upgrade, and I feel it helps to distinguish it more from Sonic games and gives it more of its own unique identity. It also makes the world feel so grand when traveling through the stages and looking off into the beautiful landscape. It's obvious a lot of love and hard work went into the pixel art and they truly did a great job. The story wasn't of much importance to me in the first game, and truthfully I vaguely remember what happened. What I do remember from the first game though was how corny a lot of the cut scenes were. In FP2 I feel like the story has improved simply from the fact that there weren't any cheesy lines that made me want to skip the scenes. In fact, there were a few moments that legit gave me a good laugh. Overall, I enjoyed the story well enough, and it was engaging enough to make me want to keep playing. Now one thing I did want to mention, is that the game feels really grand, almost too grand. I meant in terms of size. These levels are long with many different paths you can take. As a completionist, it can be rather daunting going through trying to find all the collectibles. There is so much to explore in each stage and can be easy to overlook a little nook or cranny where the item is hiding. This is one downside for me, but after playing through all the stages, I realized it wasn't as bad as I though, but still an annoyance, at least in regards to finding the collectibles. Overall I love Freedom Planet 2. It has fun, exciting and challenging gameplay with lovable characters (minus Neera) and a beautiful world. I think most people who enjoyed the first one will enjoy FP2.

_childDocuments_.review: I had fun with the first game, but with Freedom Planet 2 I reached a point very quickly where I just wanted it to end, because it was getting so tiring.The level design often gets confusing and doesn't convey well where you're supposed to head next contrary to the first game.A lot of times the levels are littered with enemies and traps, which make it impossible to not take a hit. You can also see the developers acknowledge this will happen by adding health petals close to those spots so the player can compensate for the hits taken. This is not good level design.The level design after a few stages feels flat out lazy and re-using gimmicks and enemies from older stages while the layouts get even more confusing, and the stages drag themselves to 10+ minutes each.I'd rather have less stages that feel unique, shorter and fun than a lot of stages that feel like padding and filler.The pixel art and animations are cute but the background gets overly detailed at times making hard to distinguish the characters from the backdrop elements.I don't know why they changed Lilac's model so much from the first game, especially when all other characters only got slight updates, she looks weird to me now, like if she's wearing a wig. Lilac's appearance was already established with FP1 and all the other indie projects the character is in, so what gives?Not fan of the bosses in the first game and seems they are even worse here.Bosses have very erratic patterns, spam the screen with projectiles, barely announce their actions and often jump offscreen making the battle a chore.I know there's a guard mechanic, but it's very finnicky and often results in you getting hit anyway, perhaps if they added a freeze-frame or a parry/counter mechanic then the guarding would make more sense.For the music, I don't know what happened here. The first game had some really nice themes, especially boss battle ones. Minus a few tracks, this soundtrack feels too "soft" and afraid to push the bar. Very disappointed with the music.The voice acting is better than the first game, but the cutscenes that they are used in are not very entertaining. Sometimes the voice clip quality sounds lower and more muffled for some reason.There needs to be a fix for the gamepad. Perhaps add some profiles for it to support DPAD as well etc. I had to wrestle around with fixing the controls when I first launched the game. Not a good experience, especially when the icons do not really reflect the controller buttons.Finally I got a few collision bugs, especially stuck when moving through loops or jump-through platforms. There's some instances where the collision area of some objects is larger than it should be and the character looks like they are standing on thin air. The game softlocked as well when I tried to pick the "Food" option in the inn at the palace area. I encountered a few audio glitches as well where a lot of sound effects were playing at the same time really loud. And in the final stages with the light on/off system the game lagged a lot and experienced graphical glitches (Had to restart the stage a couple times for them to be fixed).The game might scratch the "classic Sonic platformer" itch for a little bit, but I wouldn't recommend this game over the first one, that's for sure.
