_childDocuments_.review: I'm not big on the 2D Sonic titles (or just in general), but the first Freedom Planet really enamored me and the sequel is no different.The way you create speed and carry momentum in this game is so satisfying with your attacks generally having some sort of movement property. My favorite example being Milla's beam attack "Super Shield Burst" that's so strong, it blasts you in the opposite direction you shoot it. Learn to chain this attack together along with her Yoshi-like float that keeps your momentum, you'll be flying across the stage at mach speed if you're good enough. Legitimately some of the best movement mechanics and physics I've ever experienced in a platformer.On top of that you have the absolutely gorgeous pixel art and incredible soundtrack. Even if you're not a fan of the Sonic titles like me, I'd still 100% give it a try.

_childDocuments_.review: It's incredible how much they've improved on for the first game polish, level design, removal of bugs. I had a ton with the first one too.I don't normally write reviews, but I enjoyed so much of this game and had genuine fun all throughout. It's a Sonic and Treasure game combined and both parts are done extremely well. All the levels make you feel like you're going really fast and doing really cool an unique actions all throughout the levels. The Level variety is incredible so many familiar gimmicks and a lot of new ones as well, and none of them bog down the level. All throughout you're just blazing through the stages even while doing puzzles everything has this seamless and effortless feel to the gameplay. The difficulty is really well done never brutally hard, but in the perfect sweet spot that you'll lose all your lives, but still get a chance to clear the part you're stuck on.There's four playable characters so lots of replayability as well as time attack and a bunch of side things to do. The music is incredible fits the theming and has a lot of ear worms you'll want to listen to again and again. The only issue I have with the game is the story it's very corny and not serious, but the game play is so incredible and in a way the "Saturday Morning Cartoon" - esque cartoon is a nostalgic trip. Buy this game it's worth every penny at full price so much love and care went into the craft of this seamless experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Freedom Planet at one time divided Sonic fans into two camps. The first saw a solid game with their own style, the others turned on the morons and started yelling about plagiarism and parasitism on Sonic ... which, in fact, has long gone to ♥♥♥♥. However, Freedom Planet has received the recognition and love it deserves, building up a fan base that is finally looking forward to the sequel.The story starts three years after the first game. The grown up and prettier heroines are attacked by unknown robots that destroy their house. Forced to cooperate with the royal nobility, they investigate a series of incidents involving the same robots, which slowly but surely leads to key events.Compared to the first game, the combat system has been noticeably upgraded here, adding a defensive move, as well as lowering the limitation for old abilities, allowing the use of much more advanced attack combinations.The levels here are divided into two types:1) Combat - where we have to run through vast locations, making our way through their unique opponents in order to defeat the big bosses at the end.2) Urban - the most beautiful residential settlements with many characters who are ready not only to talk, but also to trade.In addition to the standard levels, there are also secondary activities, such as an arena with various modes, among which I especially liked a kind of PvP analogue that allows me to push the protagonists head-on.Stunning sixteen-bit visuals have been pumped to perfection here, giving out not only magnificent detailed cities with civilians, but also combat levels, each of which lives according to its own laws, always remaining in motion.The musical accompaniment of Freedom Planet immediately wanted to add its own playlist and the sequel took its well-deserved place in it. The soundtrack not only harmoniously combines with peaceful towns and dynamic levels, but also literally caresses the ear from the first seconds, and the sound effects are my respect.Freedom Planet 2 perfectly demonstrates to us those rare cases when the sequel not only does not lose the dignity of the original, but also multiplies them many times over, making literally everything better. This is a true creation of people who love their work and their project, and this same love does not let go even after a complete passage, as it was with the first Freedom Planet.

_childDocuments_.review: This game kicks ass, not just as a sequel to the already amazing Freedom Planet, but as a game in general.It's a massive improvement to the first game.The controls feel slightly better the first game. Not only that but you have a guard button now. And it fits extremely well with the game. At times, it feels like a fighting game but suited well with platforming, as the guard button do another action, like air dashing for the cool purple dragon. It also makes the boss fights feel even more epic and badass, cuz you can kick their ass hard if you learn the guard.Levels are also amazing. More has been done to separate one level from another. Each has even more distinct features and gimmicks to toy around with. Levels are also paced much better. Each level is shorter than the first game but it's a good thing here as there are more levels.The boss fights were fantastic in the first game and they are just as fantastic here. The added guard button and improved controls make the boss fights a spectacle to behold. The game also feels more fair to newcomers with certain mechanics that can caters to your play style. Music is just as good as the first game. Top notch. Feels the mood perfectly. Certain songs carry leitmotifs from the first game. Can listen to it anytime!The graphics are awesome as hell. Sprites moves beautifully and graceful. The background are some of the best scenery porn I have seen. Characters are really expressive too.The story is the biggest improvement over the first game. The story feels more complex. Some characters develop over the course of the game. Character interactions and story moments can be fun, goofy or serious when needed. The world building is also surprisingly great.There are hub worlds in this game. It makes the game's world feel alive. NPC's are great as well. They are harmless at worst and lively at best. They fit well.I really loved my first playthrough and I can't wait to play even more.November 2022 edit: This game also kick ass on the Steam Deck! Best action you can play on the toilet!

_childDocuments_.review: Big improvement over the first game gameplay-wise.Team Lilac has improved combat capabilities, especially Carol & Milla with their new and smoother moves. Skill level can be customized at any time in the game but you can still choose skill level at the start of the game & stick to it if you so desire.Fantastic and perfectly balanced bosses. At first, you might have hard time fighting them but the more you fail, the more you learn from it and it's a great feeling beating them faster & more efficiently. My favorite new feature is the guard mechanic that if perfectly timed, it gives you invincibility for a very short amount of time. It's quite satisfying to use it once you get the feel for it. Despite improvements, two things I'm not exactly fond of in this game. While the soundtrack in FP2 is fantastic, it doesn't exactly capture the emotional states of each stage like it did in the first game, thus making it not nearly as memorable. Few exceptions do exist, of course. That & the main antagonist isn't nearly as brutal as the first game's villain. I do love Merga's design & voice acting but she needed to be less merciful. Brevon reeked of evil in every way possible, from brainwashing to torturing, mutating, killing and tricking three kingdoms into war... basically anything so that things will go his way. He taunts you, laughs at you & spits out sarcastic one-liners. Merga just manipulates her enemies & takes over a kingdom without a scratch (almost) and leaves once she acquires an important key item.It almost looks like she was holding back the entire time.Story overall had some odd plotholes & it certainly wasn't the highlight of the game. I still recommend the game to any platformer enthusiast.

_childDocuments_.review: To be clear, I'm a huge fan of the first game. I called it "doing Sonic better than Sonic does Sonic". It was an outstanding game and this is a disappointing sequel.I'll start with the good stuff, graphics and game play. It feels really good to play, really snappy and fluid. And the pixel art is extremely detailed and looks like a huge amount of time, effort and love went into it. I'm particularly a fan of the sprite of one of the bosses which is a huge rabbit mech, which is just really impressive. In general the bosses are a highlight of this game.I want to say however that the game play suffers because of the actual level design. It's extremely unintuitive and confusing. There's too many puzzles. In the majority of levels I would be zooming around before realising either i'm going in circles somehow, or there's a sealed door or something else that just stops me dead. And I have no idea where i'm going or what to do. Honestly in this kind of game, that is a running, action spectacle, there shouldn't ever be a single moment where I'm trying to figure out what i'm supposed to be doing. To put things in perspective, Sonic levels average 3-6 minutes each. Want to know the longest time I spent in a level here? 63'25''13. Yes, over an hour. For just one of the 24 levels. This was due to it being an extremely unintuitive and complex puzzle heavy level. It was open in design and featured underwater sections and water level changing mechanics. Yes, 2D water temple mechanics. It should be obvious but it never, ever is. The levels are overly long, averaging over ten minutes, without being broken into two acts.Next, the music is bad. Pretty much every track from the first game was a banger. The music here is generic and doesn't fit the energetic nature of the game or the tone of some of the things in it. I can imagine in my head several of the bangers in the first game like i'm listening to them right now. I don't remember a single track from this sequel. With the exception of one or two remixes taken from the first game. So you know, another composers work. Garbage.The story even in the first game was divisive. But most wanted the option to skip it, which they added. it was called classic mode and just threw you into action packed level after level, with only the context of what happens in the stages. Bizarrely, this was completely removed in this sequel, which forces many many cut scenes on you and throws you into completely pointless hub worlds filled with NPC's. I watched the cut scenes during the first half of the game and it drifted between feeling aimless, boring or making pretty poor attempts at humour. Writing humour is difficult and so many things intended to be funny came off as irritating or cringe. Specifically there's a few whole characters who are intentionally obnoxious and annoying. They aren't minor characters either, they appear many many many times as bosses and in cut scenes with their catchphrases and shrieking laughter. I also don't want to sit down in a Sonic game with NPCs and study the games lore in a library (actual moment in the game). I get it, you made your expansive rich lore, but I don't care, I just want to play the game and I don't think many people do care about the war between the ancient war between the dragons and the snake mechanoids or whatever.I encouraged Freedom Planet 1 to branch out from its inspirations, because i truly believed it was better than them. Turns out a lot of people said that to them because they really did. They expanded the scope of absolutely everything. Everything is bigger, richer, more populated, more believable, more beautiful... More bloated. It lost it's way somewhere. I am imagining the devs of this game like a Game Master from DnD or another tabletop. Just writing and filling this game with so many ideas, passion and love. Some things work, most things don't, and there's a lot of it. And somewhere in the process the fundamentals of this kind of action game were lost.What would i suggest is this. Bring down the scope. It doesn't need to be bigger to be better. Shorter levels, or at least split it up into acts again. Every level should be linear. Splitting paths are fine, dead ends and a million puzzles aren't. If you must dedicate huge resources to your lore, characters, hub worlds, cut scenes, voice acting, make it optional. Or just don't and tell the story through game play, like your genesis inspirations manage. Less is more.

_childDocuments_.review: It was a long time coming, and arrived with little fanfare, but I'm happy to say Freedom Planet 2 delivers. This is a sequel in the classic sense, better playing, better sounding, more variety, better looking, and better acted. It still plays like a lost Saturn title, consisting of fast platforming with the occasional puzzle box, the original started life as a Sonic fangame and anyone familiar with the classic Sonics or Sonic Mania will feel quite at home here. The story is competent and fully voice acted in story sections along with a lot of incidental animations for characters that are well-timed, it's telling I didn't find myself skipping any of the dialogue.One major change from the original is the presence of items to make the game easier or harder, but as these reduce your rewards I tended not to use them. You might find them interesting or necessary and you can grind for them as levels are repeatable, with hidden items and soundtrack discs acting as incentive to do so.This game is not easy and a few key bosses took me around ten or so attempts to take down, thankfully it doesn't have the huge difficulty ramp at the end like the original's eye-watering final boss, but you will feel the escalation as the game continues. The guard/parry mechanic gets not one but two tutorials which should hint at how critical it is to progress, later fights feel like something from Platinum and I mean that as high praise.Frankly this is the best platformer I've played in years, don't pass it up.

_childDocuments_.review: This is my second time finishing this game and I’m convinced it’s one of the best platformers thusfar this decade. The gamefeel is on point balancing fast speeds with robust combat mechanics. Even though you zip through levels at breakneck paces, the camera readjusts itself for every occasion and there’s even an option to make it more or less adaptable to your speed. The presentation is delightful with bright, beautiful pixel art and excellent sound design with great music, too.I think the reason why FP2 isn’t more celebrated is because it’s a surprisingly dedicated experience. All the characters have robust movesets that get some taking used to, even if the basic control scheme is simple and intuitive. Despite the overt Sonic inspirations, the game is very fight focused– taking a lot of verbs from character action games (including a very necessary guard mechanic). Many levels are sprawling– a number of them clocking over ten minutes if you do a lot of exploring– and almost  of them feature a boss fight at the end. The challenge level ramps up quickly. The first time I played this game, I saw a lot of game overs.Those aren’t , but I think most people would be caught off-guard by the amount of Give A Damn the player has to bring to Freedom Planet 2. There’s an easy mode, and I haven’t tried it, but I think even if it makes getting to credits less of a trial, it’s probably an inelegant solution in which the ferocity of the game will still ebb on players. This game will take most 10 to 15 hours and by the end– partially in thanks of the game’s intense final act– the players will have had their fill.But I guess what I’m saying is: Freedom Planet 2 is a . It’s A Lot but what’s there is very good and will be an irreplaceable platforming experience for some players, myself included. Tackling this casually– it’s probably a good time but not something exemplary. I hope this game finds an audience with those that would really cherish, though, because it’s something truly special.

_childDocuments_.review: It took a while for the game to click with me, but once it did I grew to enjoy it even more than the first game which I already liked a lot! It's basically just more Freedom Planet, everything cranked up a notch, as any good sequel should strive to do.It's a big, BIG game. Almost 30 full stages with a smattering of towns, boss stages and optional challenges. I reached a point where I assumed it was the end of the game and didn't realize I wasn't even halfway done! The levels are huge and the pixel art is gorgeous to look at, all the levels have their own quirks and gimmicks, like one being entirely progressed vertically, one having you collect keys to proceed, yes there's even a water level but don't worry because it's not a slog like a lot of other games, there's a lot of boosters and the ability to swim to keep this sort of level from slowing things down.There's a few stages that are purely just long boss encounters, and the side-scrolling horizontal shooter stage makes a return here too. There are some arena gauntlet style challenges unlocked as you progress that have you do things like navigate a maze, defeat waves of enemies in a particularly cumbersome arena and basically show a mastery of the mechanics introduced in all the levels you've finished so far.Currency earned can be spent on items you can equip that either help or hinder your progress. The more hindrance you have, the higher your completion rank will be on the stage results and the more currency you earn. So for example, you could equip an item that gives you only 1 life, but doing so would give you more rewards at the end, which is a neat idea. There's also a museum you can spend currency in to unlock dioramas of all the bosses in the game, it doesn't serve any functional purpose other than being just something else you can work to collect. Some equippable items can only be found in hidden areas in stages, the stages with items unfound are marked which is helpful so you know what you're missing from where. The last collectible worth mentioning are the vinyl records which unlock music tracks.And on the subject of music, the soundtrack in this game slaps hard.Easily one of the best 2D platformers ever made, you won't regret picking it up if those sorts of games are your thing.The issues I do have are quite nitpicky and I fully acknowledge it's just me being a whiner and don't much detract from the overall enjoyment, but the three things I personally felt didn't work...1) The story. At best it's a serviceable way of tying all the stages together, but it's just not that interesting as a story and there's too much of it. As someone who is very susceptible to emotional storytelling and grows attached to endearing characters, I felt absolutely nothing here. It's not that it's a small part of the game, either. A lot of time and effort goes into the cutscenes which just makes it all the more grating because I see what they're trying to do and falling flat. Also, "classic mode" for playing without cutscenes is only unlocked after beating the game.Edit: Thinking about it more, it's probably less to do with the actual story being bad and just the way it's presented. It's way too dialogue-heavy and would have worked better with a show-don't-tell approach, because it's not an overly complicated plot once you trim the fat and cut the threads that don't lead anywhere.2) The main characters. I'm not big on their designs even in the first game, but even less so for their redesigns. What makes this worse is that pretty much every new NPC added in this game looks far better than all the returning characters. I imagine the idea was to try and distance the series from Sonic games by making the characters taller and without the big heads, which worked great for all these original characters designed from the ground up with this new style in mind, but makes the original characters stand out in a bad way.3) Lilac gameplay. This is more of a me-problem I guess, but I really dislike her cyclone ability. It's a double-jump that makes her spin like a tornado and cause damage as she goes and I have three gripes here. One, the tornado will keep spinning for a short while after landing on ground and if you try to jump before the spin animation stops, you only jump at around half the height as usual. Two, the constant voice sample when using a skill that you'll be using most of the time becomes annoying and there's no option to turn it off without disabling all voices in the game entirely. Three, it also seems to be the strongest attack you have and I spent a good portion of my first playthrough assuming that the super attack and melee combos would be the biggest damage dealers on bosses when I should have just been spamming double-jump.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely amazing. That's what the game is summarized in two words.The more I play, the more I like it. Is the dialogue cringe at times? Sure. (Update: Got further into the game. This dialogue and story writing is amazing!)Are some of the bosses jank or weird sometimes? Yes.But despite its flaws, I see so many major improvements over the first game. (A game which, by the way, I've finished at a 100% on the Nintendo Switch)The writing, the gameplay, and even the music are all better than they have ever been... and I love it. I'm so immensely surprised by it.At the time I write this review I'll have around 9 hours, but believe me when I say that it might go up to 40 or more when I'm done finishing this game at a 100%. Having a blast with it, even if the battlesphere's a bit wack.Heavily recommended if you like platforming games in general.Update #1: After exactly 17 hours, I have 100%'d the game with Carol (except for the museum, still gotta repair that). And my opinion of the game's... not changed much! It's still really good, I loved a lot of aspects of it. Some of the hub songs don't loop, and a lot of the voices sound quieter than others, but I'm sure they're working on fixing them, so I didn't mind that too much.Story-wise though, damn. I actually got engaged with it at the end, was pretty fun.---Update #2: I have 100%'d the game, having obtained every badge/achievement available, which also means having cleared all characters, obtained all S Ranks, Items and Vinyls.Gonna miss this game. It's been a ride. Sadly, after your second playthrough, the story begins to lose some of its charm however.While I did heavily appreciate the added cutscenes for Milla and Neera, they really felt shoehorned into the early conversations, ending up with some of their dialogues just straight up being ignored (mostly in Milla's case).But again, the added cutscenes made up for it quite well. I didn't think Neera would even have one at first! Ended up pleasantly surprised about that.Overall... I still heavily recommend the game! It's great! And the soundtrack's great too!Gonna be waiting for Freedom Planet 3, if that ever becomes a thing.Once that day comes, I will buy it on day one, and play it through and through as well.

_childDocuments_.review: It's so good to be home! Freedom Planet 2 is familiar, yet adds so many new things that are expanding on its predecessor's ideas and contribute to cement the series as one of the best Sonic-inspired games out there.Coming from FP1, the controls are refined, more responsive and as fast paced as ever. The levels are huge, sometimes intricate, and most often than not clever in their designs and gimmicks.  The true show stealer though is the world of Avalice itself, that can now be visited extensively through a Mario-like overworld map with hubs sprayed up here and there, filled with NPCs commenting on the plot and the state of the world, providing the titular Freedom Planet a depth that the original game could only scratch. So far, this is the sequel that all freedom Planet fans were waiting for, full to the brim with swift action, clever level-design, great music and, of course, a very corny yet lovable cast of characters.
_childDocuments_.name: Freedom Planet 2

_childDocuments_.review: Possibly my most favorite platformer of all time; everything has been expanded and improved over Freedom Planet 1. Stages are faster and more varied. Characters are more refined and a new character that's fun and fits the gameplay well. Combat is smoother, with a new guard ability adding more depth at the same time. A lovely artstyle overhaul, and the music is honestly even better than the already great OST of FP1.The story is much better. Merga is a more interesting and deep villain than Brevon, and has reasons for her actions instead of just a crashed ship (even if misplaced). The writing is more mature and the tone is more consistent than FP1. Humor is aplenty and personally lands much better.Replayability is extremely high. Each Character is different enough from each other to feel fun in their own ways. Stages now have rankings, encouraging you to play fast and play well. There are hubs where you can soak in lore and details of the world of Avalice. You can buy items in these hubs to customize your gameplay experience (like starting with a certain barrier, or a potion that fine-tunes your character), or make it harder with brave stones for a better rank and more crystals (or masochism).I've beaten FP1 many times and has always been a great experience. I see myself beating FP2 much, much more. And I will love every second of it.+5 Respect

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely incredible platformer and an even better sequel. I've been burned many many many many times by sequels that fail to live up to name of its predecessor, losing the charm that made the original so interesting/fun, and I am very happy to say that this game does not fall among them. While the first game existed mainly as an homage to the classic Sonic games, this game strikes further out from this material without leaving behind much of what was so good about its source, and I have to say I think it turned out pretty well. It certainly doesn't skimp on the length of the story as well, as there were several points where I was expecting the game to be drawing towards a satisfactory conclusion before having a whole new area open up with more levels. Upon writing this, I have only beaten the game twice in 30 hours (Lilac and Neera) without going excessively for collectibles or for speedrunning, so I think it's a pretty fair assessment of the games length. Speaking of the story, its quality hasn't changed much from its predecessor, so if the story/voice-acting of the original really turned you off of it, then I'm sure that this game will do much of the same. The voices are of noticeably better quality, but there are still a good few lines here-and-there that I feel had some odd-directions behind it. Regardless, I would overwhelmingly say that this game is worth playing, even without having completed the original, and I feel so sad about the fact that this game doesn't seem to be as big or popular as it deserves to be. There are so many aspects to this game that show the fine hand of detail that went into crafting these environments for such a diverse range of character abilities that no other platformer I've seen, AAA, indie, or otherwise, can compete.

_childDocuments_.review: Like the wings on its logo, Freedom Planet 2 soars above the competition as an outstanding high-speed platformer that improves upon nearly every foundation set by it’s predecessor. It is without a doubt my personal game of the year and a shinning example of both indie development and how to craft a killer sequel. The game’s story is heavily involved, taking place 3 years after the invasion of Lord Brevon and the shattering of the Kingdom Stone. An ancient centurion of a dead race named Merga has awoken and seeks revenge against the world of Avalice due to the genocide of her people long ago. Returning animal heroines Sash Lilac, Carol Tea, Milla Basset and newcomer Nera Li must confront her plans as well as intercept remnants of the previous alien invasion and friends turned enemies. The center conflict deals with heavy themes like genocide, cultural erasure, and the ethics of warfare without coming off as cheesy or edgy while greatly expanding the mythos, lore, and fleshing out the culture and identify of Avalice. Merga comes across as a cunning yet broken person with actual motivations for what she does rather than simply being the evil big bad. Despite the serious tone, the game features a lot of funny jokes and witty comedy that never breaks pace and helps to round out the mood in between drama. Each playable character gets unique dialogue and cutscenes throughout their own playthroughs that frames a narrative for their struggles and motivations. Voice acting is thoroughly improved in both delivery and consistency; everyone sounds fantastic without a single instance of wince or cringe and cutscenes don’t overstay their welcome. This includes the previous VA’s and professional talent like Christopher Sabat of Dragon Ball fame. A plethora of new and returning characters help to add personality and charm to cutscenes. Every criticism of the first game’s story was taken to heart here and for repeat playthrough the story can be skipped with classic mode. Like it’s predecessor, the game offers a mix of highspeed platforming, exploration, and combat across 24 levels and 4 playable characters each with their own unique movesets. Movement feels more fluid and easier to keep due to a reworking of the skill meter and abilities that allow for greater vertical height. A new dodge button allows skilled users to avoid damage and parry damage back if timed right. Lilac remains speed oriented with her dragon boost now cancelable, Carol can climb walls and use a throwing disc while her bike doesn’t break apart, Milla has a normal health bar and can quickly summon alchemy cubes, and newcomer Nera is slower but uses frost arts and focus to freeze enemies and unleash powerful attacks. This gives each character their own utility and playstyle which gives each playthrough a fresh but familiar challenge. Stage design feels better adjusted to player momentum, physics, and abilities which gives each level a more polished feeling. Unique environments, platforming gimmicks, treasure boxes and boss encounters make for a lengthy campaign with enduring replay value. Once unlocked, the battle sphere allows for unique challenges and boss rematches, which help unlock a special ending and secret stage. Bosses remain a key focus of the game, with most stages having at least one encounter and some stages being entirely devoted to boss fights. Unlike the first game, these are more strategic in nature with better attack patterning and a greater focus on movement. This results in many fights acting less as slug fests and more like combat puzzles. These are still very challenging encounters with later bosses offering exceedingly difficult fights. For several fights this does equate to chasing down the boss to damage it and overall, I feel encounters are weaker compared to the first game. This is especially true for the final encounter against Merga, which lacks the fast-paced frenzy of Lord Brevon’s showdown. It should be noted that boss encounters are still a fun challenge, just different from how the first game offered them. The block button helps to make encounters feel fair. In Adventure mode, levels are accessed across an expanding tile map that also includes hubs housing shops and interactable NPCs. They feature new dialogue after clearing certain stages and help to make the world feel more interconnected and alive. Shops are connected to the new item  and ranking systems; trinkets found in stages or bought at shops can either ease difficulty or increase the challenge. Examples include items that can increase player health or kill the player upon taking damage. Aid will reduce the gem payout after clearing a level while challenging items increase the payout and award a higher rank upon completion. Rank is defined from C to S rank, which is determined by items, the number of deaths and continues used, and damage taken. Potions affect gameplay statuses like shield points given or player speed without affecting score. This system allows for more robust playing options for casual and competitive play. Upon beating the game, a Museum opens that allows players to spend gems on models of bosses fought and trivia on the game’s development. Progression is more linear in Classic mode, with a basic level select and universal store option between levels. Lives reset each stage, with continues bought using gems after lives are used up. A new reviving system lets players restart after dying with only a sliver of their health left to clean up mistakes in a pinch. Difficulty options allow for the rules to be customized, like adjusting how many gems are used to revive or turning off these options entirely. The game features gorgeously detailed pixel art reminiscent of the Sega Saturn with a lot of rich colors and highly animated sprites and occasional polygonal elements. Character sprites in particular are much more vibrant and expressive with a lot of personality. This is seen in the game’s photo mode, in which any paused frame can be turned into a photo with unique poses available. Levels and hubs feature rich backgrounds which blend Asian and Filipino architecture and science fiction. Some sprite scaling can become blurry when the stage scrolls out, which adds to the retro charm but can be distracting and should be optional. With a greater focus on melody and atmosphere, the soundtrack offers a less high octane score compared to the first game. This will be disappointing for those that enjoyed the first game’s OST, but this is largely down to preference. The game’s score is still impressive with over 90 original compositions that offer a rich sound. My only criticism would be that many boss themes lack the same intensity found in the first game but overall, the soundtrack is phenomenal with many call backs and leitmotifs to the previous game. Personal favorites include Shade Armory, Ancestral Forge, Lilac’s theme, and the boss themes for Magma Starscape and Clockwork Arboretum. At launch, the game featured few bugs and an overall astounding level of polish. Updates for the game have been constant, with continued tweaks and bug fixes. A few recommendations I have would be for additional rank and par times to be present when selecting a stage, for classic mode to be unlocked by default rather than rewarded for beating adventure mode, and for greater item customization. A late game use for gems and currency would be appreciated as well. DLC offering more playable characters and levels would be a godsend.After nearly 7 years in development, Freedom Planet 2 acts as a near perfect sequel by expanding what worked and improving what didn’t in the first game. This title matures the franchise into its own unique identity that surpasses it’s own inspirations to become one of the best side scrolling platformers of all time. This game raises the bar for indie works and leaves high expectations for a potential Freedom Planet 3. Easily 9/10, please buy this game and support the developers.

_childDocuments_.review: I was definitely hyped for this game when it was announced on Christmas 2015. I had played the first game about 4-5 months beforehand and considered it among my favorite games of all time (and would at least place it somewhere in my Top 10 even now). Unfortunately this game did take longer to release than I was initially hoping (not that I was thinking it would come out the following year but I at least expected it around 2018-2020 lol), but now that the game released... I can safely say it was worth the wait.In a nutshell, everything that the first game did really well, the sequel does even better. Gameplay and level design is even more interesting and fast-paced, the characters feel even better to play as (though I've only completed the game as Lilac but, whatever), the story is more in-depth and the art style looks even nicer. Presentation-wise, if Sonic Mania felt like a long lost Sonic game on the Saturn, this game basically feels like a hidden gem platformer on the same system, to put it the best I can. There's a lot more detail in the pixel art between the character sprites, environments and backgrounds in a way that still stays true to the first game's general art style. I will say that I didn't quite like Lilac's redesign at first, but it's definitely grown on me.The plot is also a lot more in-depth than the first game. FP1 was pretty good for what it needed to do, but it didn't really go very far with things like character development or lore, in which this game... well, it does a lot more of. Not going to spoil it for those who haven't played it, but it adds a lot of worldbuilding, lore and history to Avalice with events that unfold in a way that helps the characters feel more fleshed out. On top of that I feel like this game does a better job of incentivizing playing through the game multiple times with the different characters - which I already touched upon but with how some characters go in and out of the story it does make me want to replay the game to see how those events unfold (on top of seeing if there were any levels I might have missed by just playing as Lilac). Plus it also feels a lot better paced in which the first did have an issue of overly long cutscenes that... really didn't do much to further the story (to the point where some of the original cutscenes were trimmed in an update lol).Gameplay-wise, there's a lot that Freedom Planet 2 does to build off and add depth to what the first game brought. The new potion and upgrade system is one thing which, while optional, does add a level of personalization to each person's playthrough and may offer extra assistance to those who need it or even offer extra challenge with some items that you can receive that limit your abilities, life or revivals - which also come with the benefit of extra bonus. That last point brings me to another thing - this game also adds a rank system similar to what the Sonic series has since Sonic Adventure 2, which further incentivizes repeat playthroughs to get the best rank in each level. Plus the lives/continue system isn't meaningless like it was in the first game - you are given continues but they come at a penalty of the amount of crystal shards you've collected, and when you die you're also given the option to continue right where you left off but with only 1 life petal, or continue from a checkpoint with a full life bar. You are given difficult options to choose from in the game's assist settings though in case you have trouble with the game.The game's also much longer than the first - containing 24 levels and according to HowLongToBeat clocks in at around 10 hours for a normal playthrough (albeit my first playthrough as Lilac clocked in at almost 12) compared to 4.5 hours for the first game - more than double the length. And if you think the amount of levels might diminish the quality of each individual one, you'd be wrong. Each level feels extremely well designed around the smooth, fast-paced controls, and each of them stand out with their themes, gimmicks, tempo and challenge. The game further builds off the Sonic-y level design from the first game combined with some added depth to the combat system, and overall creative, fun levels that reward replayability through the game's rank system and general mastery of the game's mechanics and controls, plus a few alternate pathways here and there.The only real negative I can think of is that I did experience a few bugs here and there - a couple of which that did require me to restart from the last checkpoint. First one was during the first Serpentine boss in which during the 'falling' section after the first phase I ended up somewhere offscreen and got stuck somewhere I couldn't recover my character from, and the second one I clipped into the floor when falling down after being blown upwards by a giant fan thing. Nothing too big of a deal, but did cause some slight annoyance. I guess also that some of the later levels went on for a bit too long but considering how much I enjoyed playing through the game it really didn't become much of an issue lol.Truth be told this game might be my Game of the Year so far, and depending on how Sonic Frontiers turns out, may even hold onto that title. I pretty much had a good time throughout it - never really feeling tired or burned out - and I can definitely recommend it especially if you liked the first game.

_childDocuments_.review: I've waited for this game for 7 years - and it did not disappoint.This really takes the concept of the original game and ramps it up by a hundred times. With a good mixture of stages ranging from fast-paced ones to more a bit puzzle oriented. The combat also feels more fluid and satisfying compared to the first game, and the Guarding and Revive mechanics are much welcomed additions. The fact that you can change the item loadouts before every stage, and thus alter the difficulty level also makes things more flexible.The visuals on this game are so beautiful, and there's so many attention of details I like (it's so nice that the game also has a Photo Mode for capturing those moments). That's some of the best looking pixel art I've seen for a while.The soundtrack is so kickass, that it might even rival the original Freedom Planet at a times. The fans of the original game should recognize some of the familiar beats on some of the tracks. ;)The Adventure Mode on this game feels much better than on the original game. The pacing has been improved vastly, and it definitely helps that there are Hub areas now, which the original Freedom Planet lacked due of the engine used for it being... not so good.The Classic Mode is still there (which is unlocked by clearing the game for the first time), but for me it kinda feels more negligible than in the first FP, due of how much improved the Adventure Mode is in this game. But it's still there in case you wanna speedrun through the game or something.The story feels more serious this time, given that there's been more than one writer this time around. The voice acting also sounds more clearer, although I did notice certain voice clips being more lower in volume, but other than that it's pretty good.It was also nice to see that the charm from the first game carried over to this, and that there's been certain scenes which just made me smile - and even laugh sometimes. XDThis game also has been pretty stable (for me at least) since Day One. There are some minor bugs, but they don't hamper the whole experience much, and I'm pretty sure they'll be fixed over time - this game already received several patches in just one week.Overall, this game is a real blast to play - the better sequel I could've ever asked for. Definitely worth the long wait, and just happened to become one of my all-time favorites.If you'd like to play some fast-paced action platform goodness, then I'll definitely recommend this with a heartbeat. (As long as you don't have a furro phobia or something. XP)P.S. Lilac is a real bab, you can't change my mind.
_childDocuments_.name: Freedom Planet 2

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not far into this game yet, and I do intend on continuing playing. But early impressions of this game haven't been great for me. The new pixel art is incredibly gorgeous and detailed... Unfortunately to the point where it's actually hard to see what's going on while playing. I've noticed far more bugs in the first 3 stages than I have in the entirety of the first Freedom Planet, frequently clipping through terrain and objects, weird audio quality drops in VO, and on the very first boss somehow triggering a bug that made me invulnerable after I was supposed to die. Most of these can be fixed with a patch, though the cognitive overload of the pixel art may be difficult to patch. The thing that I think can't be patched though? I'm just overall having way less fun with this game than I did with FP1. The level design and combat just *feels* off to me. Combat doesn't connect and have that same crunch that it had in FP1. The levels feel far more convoluted and frustrating to navigate than the first game; I find myself getting lost far more frequently than FP1. As a once or twice thing I'd say that's more on me, but this was a constant struggle for me in the first 3 levels I played.I really REALLY want to like this game and I'm going to continue playing it in hopes that maybe I'm being just a little too harsh with my first impressions. But I hope by leaving this review the devs can make some adjustments to the game to live up to the first game's greatness.

_childDocuments_.review: Probably one of the best action platformer titles I've ever played. Pretty hefty amount of content with lots of memorable bosses, locations, NPCs, and lore. Every single level has at least one thing unique to it that makes it stand out, and there are some moments and mechanics in the game that I've never seen done in any other game ever. I had an awesome time with this playing through as just Carol so far, and I'm looking forward to returning to get all of the achievements in the coming days.
_childDocuments_.name: Freedom Planet 2

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not sure how to put it into words but I love almost everything about this game. It's incredibly fun to play, all the characters feel different and the level design compliments them very well. I enjoyed the story, and the way it sets up some levels makes them far more enjoyable and memorable. The various hubs you can visit in Adventure Mode are great to hangout in and the npcs really make the world feel lived in. The world map is cute and also really helps all of Avalice feel connected. The music is absolutely amazing and adds a lot to the atmosphere of the levels. There's also so many fun side modes like sparring with other characters, boss rematches, and various challenges. Some items like the "Life Oscillation" one are pretty cool and fun to use. Dragon Valley is a fantastic starting stage, the level flows well and the art and music are phenomenal!The Floating Island Map has especially wonderful art and music, I could sit on that screen for hours! (to be honest most of the world map makes me feel like that, but the Floating Island map is probably my favorite)The in-stage character dialogue is charming and makes each stage it's in feel like an active part of the story.The ranking system is neat, but it could definitely use some changes to allow defeating enemies and collecting crystals to contribute to getting a high rank, as opposed to just using the brave stones and ignoring everything.I'm pretty sure the way you earn the time capsules was a result of running out of dev time, but it's still unfortunate they're only obtainable in the Battlesphere.Incredibly minor thing but I wish you could toggle whether the Battlesphere boss rematches would use the Battlesphere tiles and background or their original tiles and backgrounds. Some of the boss fights just don't look as cool and clash a bit with the Battlesphere tiles. There's so much I like about this game that I didn't mention here, I don't think a single review does it justice! If you're on the fence about this game, give it a try! I couldn't recommend it enough! (it also has a demo if you just want to try that!) Also GalaxyTrail is still fixing bugs and adding stuff which is awesome!This game makes me happy ^w^
_childDocuments_.name: Freedom Planet 2

_childDocuments_.review: I really, really wanted to enjoy this game. If there were ever a game to convince me Steam needs an "in the middle" rating, this would be it. I was given FP2 as a gift and I am thankful for it, but ultimately this game just did not click with me at all.+Game feels very good to play+Beautiful graphics+Creative stages and bosses-Level design is cluttered and long-In desperate need of polish-Marvel-tier writing-the music For all that I disliked, there is a lot that I did enjoy.The game feels  to control and play; everything just feels so right when you do things, and it is fun to run around and attack and smash enemies. It is fun! But then a nasty bug might show up and ruin your day, getting you stuck in a wall and now you have to restart to the last checkpoint.This game looks beautiful and has some absolutely brimming art. The scenery is pretty, characters and enemies alike are well-animated, and the "segmented" bosses are very impressive (major shoutout to Lemon Bread there especially) - everyone on the team did a great job on the project. However, there are moments - especially in the Shuigang hub - where things just look unfinished. NPCs missing shading, heavy sprite clash between the pixel art of Sabrina and Pixy versus TysonTan's binary art scenery, and some off-model art (Lilac's "shocked" portrait being the biggest offender). This game was in development for 7 years, and it's jarring as a result.There is a lot of creativity brimming with each stage; every level looks and feels unique from one another. Some of my favorite levels were the ones where you had to slow down and either engage or do some puzzle work. Shade Armory and Lightning Tower are two notable highlights in the pool of stages I really enjoyed - more of those levels, please! Unfortunately, the better stages come later in the game with some of the downright weakest stages coming closer to the start of things. If you're willing to get through the less interesting levels (and deal with the story, more on that later) then you'll probably have fun with some of the more intense stages.Alright. Now into the things I downright disliked.Levels overstay their welcome. I think everyone who has gotten to Ancestral Forge knows about it taking 20 minutes or more to complete... But other levels in the game take upwards of 8 minutes, at which point you start to wonder when it's going to end. Sonic games had their levels split into 2 acts to break up the stages, and notably in later entries, allow the 2nd act to throw new things at you instead of continuing to be the same level for 10 minutes. People complained about Battle Glacier for this reason but it seems that stage length is being doubled down on here.The writing is not good at all. The story's premise seems serviceable at first... Dragon warrior from the past that was sealed away is now free, and is out for the Magister's blood because of something that happened long ago... But then you get to the dialogue. Maybe it's because I just finished Xenoblade 3, but the dialogue gave me immense whiplash. Like, I'd compare some of this game's writing to the original "Golden Alpaca" scene from YIIK - going from absolutely serious to trying to shove in humor where there really, really ought to not be any. Characters ironically don't feel like themselves at moments. Simply put, it is not easy to get through.The worst part of it all is that you cannot skip the story; you are forced to play through the Story Mode on your first playthrough, which seems like a complete backstep from FP1 allowing you to play Classic Mode from the start. Weirder still, you can skip the cutscenes... But can't cycle through text? I read far faster than I listen, and even in games where the text is being spoken to me, eventually I just want to read it. It's really annoying and it makes the dialogue issue worse when you aren't able to skip through the parts that dampen the experience without sacrificing the entire cutscene in return.And the music... What happened here? Freedom Planet 1's OST is absolutely wonderful on the ears with music that gets your blood pumping and ready to roll - Sky Battalion, Thermal Base, Major Boss Theme... There is almost no bad music in the entirety of FP1.I cannot remember a single song outside of Globe Opera 1 in this game. The music here is just not memorable in the slightest - I genuinely have tried to remember other tracks and I just cannot, only bits and pieces. The music in FP2 is not strong and I do not know if it's a mixing issue or the composing being weak. I know Woofle can do some amazing work, not even including FP1 but also her arrangements for Bunny Must Die! were strong as well. But then you get to tracks like "Boss (Mega)" that are just... not good. But of course, I am just a dragon on the internet. Your opinion is your own, and mine is my own - just because I did not enjoy the game does not mean you will not. Again, this game does  do everything wrong, and I will reiterate that this game is an argument for Steam adding an "in the middle" ranking for games. It is not so awful that I hate it, but it is not a game I would recommend.If you're curious... Well, Steam has a 2-hour refund policy for a reason. Try it out. Maybe we'll get Spade DLC this time for real and it'll change my point of view.

_childDocuments_.review: I pirated the original game on my Wii U. I liked it a lot so I pirated this one when it came to Switch earlier this year. I loved this game so much that I knew I had to come back and buy both Freedom Planet 1 and 2 to show my support. These games are absolutely amazing and will not disappoint in pretty much any way. The music, the sprite work, the characters, all great, especially here in the sequel which blows the first game (which was already good) out of the water in my opinion. The combat is especially good here as well, giving a nice twist to the "Sonic" formula. All of the foes are formidable but never seem extremely difficult and are fun to take down, was was a slight issue I had with the first game (although it could have been a skill issue then. I should probably replay it to compare). The quality of the content and the amount of replay-ability here with the multiple characters with their own side-stories and extra challenges is insanely high for the low price they are asking for. _childDocuments_.review: This is a quick, dirty and early review because while I'm still working on finishing my Lilac playthrough, I've been enjoying the game a lot! It feels like a truly worthy successor to the first game and additionally follows up on plot points from it, letting it flow seamlessly into the new storyline. It's also just written and voice acted far better, making the story easier to get invested in with less distractions like Carol's bathroom mic from the first game.However, here's mainly why I'm writing this - I do recommend maybe holding off for a little bit because the game has been getting a LOT of patches lately, some of which are pretty major fixes like controller issues, save file corruption and music loop points. Playing the game at launch for me felt pretty good for the most part and I didn't have any real problems aside from weird controller binding problems (which were fixed!)I'll update my review later on when I finish playing the game as all four characters.(I got this as a gift from a friend!)

_childDocuments_.review: I remember when Freedom Planet 2 was announced. I was 17, and hyped out of my mind, as I adored the first game.I am 24 now, and so very glad this game lived up to the hype. An absolutely massive amount of stages, each different and distinct from the last. Tough as nails boss fights that made me tear my hair out in the best way. Better controls and combat. Banger music. Absolutely *gorgeous* pixel art, like ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Really clever callbacks to the first game that show the impacts it had; without indulging in Sonic's brand of "hey, remember this old game? Be nostalgic!" I've only played as Lilac but am so excited to jump back in and do the rest of the girls' campaigns.The story is a big step up from the first game too. I appreciate how it balances tone better, and how the presentation and voice acting is much improved. Galaxy Trail could've just lightened up on the plot, or made it just goofy and silly, but no. They kept it genuine and sincere, no fear of people screaming about the story being "cringe" for daring to actually tell a story that tries in a mascot platformer. Hell, in order to get the true ending you literally have to collect a bunch of lore time capsules. You can tell the story and hub worlds had a massive influence on the game, and I think you're robbing yourself of the full experience if you don't give the plot a chance at least once.Also the villain is, I ♥♥♥♥ you not, basically lesbian water dragon Shadow The Hedgehog, which kinda rules. Shout out to Sabrina DiDuro and all the folks at Galaxy Trail for making such a cool game, can't wait to see what y'all work on next after you give yourselves the biggest vacation; seven years of dev time sounds exhausting.
_childDocuments_.name: Freedom Planet 2

_childDocuments_.review: So, I've beaten the game with one of the four characters, and here's my summary:Fun levels, rich and colorful pixelart AND a great story!But on a longer note, this is one of the best fast-pacing, action 2D games your money can buy. You have over 20 great levels. Some are fast-pasted, few are puzzle-oriented and they are greatly made. After that, you can spend your time to master these levels and get an S-rank if you dare, especially when it all compliments the four characters' abilities, Lilac, Carol, Milla and the new playable character, Neera Li. They all got their own stories to unfold on this adventure, (I do recommend playing as Lilac on your first playthrough just for the sake of the story).You can also tell that GalaxyTrail got the experience on their belt when making this sequel. The pixelart for starters is amazing! So much so, you might get your eyes glued on it 0.0. Not just the levels, but even a handful of hub worlds you can explore. They are pretty distinctive too, depending on their themes and culture. You even get a whole lot of NPCs to talk to. Some have funny quirks, some are even making references you might or might not get. The whole world is just inspiring to see.And then the story. I won't do a spoiler, but I will say it's consistently told and got a tone that is more balanced out. You got some villains that you gotta stop or else we are all doomed and all that jazz, but you might like them too just for their characteristics, and all this will also impact the characters you play as and the ones they are allies with. Still, gotta play the game for yourself to know what it's all about. I bought it day one to support the indie team that worked 7 years on this and I promise you: You will get a heck of a time with this game! I highly recommend it!

_childDocuments_.review: This game took every minor gripe I had with the original and came out with an absolute masterpiece. I'm seriously blown away by the quality, the amount of content, and the surprisingly very enjoyable story. It masterfully takes the best of the genre and merges it all into a near-perfect package,If you're a fan of this kind of game at all, do yourself a favor and pick this game up. I guarantee at the very least you'll like it. Inherent to the sonic dna in this game, at first the game will be a bit tricky, but as you progress you'll have the movement and flow click with you and make you eager to dive back in and time-attack or play through again with the different characters.This really is more than that though, this game stands on its own two feet with a unique identity of its own, and with a game THIS good, I really look forward to whatever the days may be working on in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful story and voice acting that only enhances the experience of each stage. Great setpieces. Crisp and fun gameplay that you can adjust the difficulty as you see fit. Level design improved from the first game. A zoomed-out camera that can have all of the sprites in full-resolution with an easy to install mod. A great classic-feeling sonic-type game with active time combat and full movesets, works very well. The pixel art never misses, the game is drop-dead gorgeous. A must play that nearly perfects what the first Freedom Planet had. An ideal sequel that knocks it out of the park.Your first playthrough will easily hit double-digits in your playtime, which already makes the game worth the price for a single character. Multiple playthroughs, exploring, or speedrunning/S-ranking will all add lots of playtime to those looking for a deeper experience with the gameplay. I highly recommend to anyone even SLIGHTLY interested in 2D platformers.
_childDocuments_.name: Freedom Planet 2

_childDocuments_.review: An improvement on the original in every way possible. The game oozes polish, love and care all the way through. Gameplay has gone through a number of improvements to suit the chaos and better define itself as a mixture between high speed platforming and breakneck combat. Boss battles are as exciting as ever, and the levels are tons of fun to go through. Even the story mode, despite actually being longer than in the first game, is far better paced and is better at respecting the player's patience, on top of just generally having better written dialogue and dynamics. The voice acting I don't think was ever bad but it's definitely at its absolute best here.This time around in the art department, Tyson Tan lends his distinctive art style and designwork to Freedom Planet's cast and world, and there's never been a better fit- it's clear they want to use his work to help define the visual identity of the series. Overall, Freedom Planet 2 just reeks of "we figured it out" energy across the board- this is a good thing. The first game was an excellent experience that felt 80% there - but this game feels like it has properly realized how to establish its identity as something truly unique and remarkable in its own right. Everything feels more purposeful, planned, and adds up to one of the most fulfilling gaming experiences I've played in a minute.To say I'm addicted is an understatement. For anyone worried about a lack of content, don't be. This is 20+ full-fledged levels, each with their own themes and ideas they used to the fullest. Four playable characters all with their own distinct gameplay identities and feels - Sonic/Knuckles/Tails scenario this is not - the way you approach combat, speed, and platforming with each character is completely different. Items that allow you to customize your character's stats or play the levels with a tighter challenge. A "Battlesphere" mode which not only lets you rematch individual bosses but contains new arena challenges and obstacles courses for you to beat your records on. A sparring mode that lets you fight other characters in 1v1s or smash targets within a time limit. There's just so much here and it's all very well-thought out and meaty.I can see some not liking the "cringe" story like with the first game (read: they're boring people and just hate a fun time) or the long, highly involved levels, but everything comes together for me in a way that feels remarkably solid, refined, and entertaining. It's just a blast and I invite anyone who loves action platformers to give it a try. But please, I implore you, don't go into it treating it like it's Sonic, and don't play it like it's Sonic. Because it's an entirely different beast - some things in common, but it must be tamed anew.Mega Man Zero + Gunstar Heroes + Sonic the Hedgehog for people who wear thigh highs. play it.
_childDocuments_.name: Freedom Planet 2

_childDocuments_.review: I want to preface this with a little storyI loved freedom planet 1, and I beat it on the hardest difficulty on every character simply because it was really fun, and I have always enjoyed a good platforming challenge. The OST was incredible and the story even pulled me in a little bit (I was interested in the larger world they lived in.) However, it did have some frustrating moments, and I never did find every star card. But I did always remember my time in the game fondly.After freedom planet 2 was announced, I was excited. And that excitement was burning for years, as I figured the development might take a while. But after the demo drop, I became discouraged as months of waiting became a year. And another. And another...I began to lose hope, to worry the project was secretly abandoned and nobody wanted to say anything, as other games released (Petal Crash in particular) in the interim. It got to the point where I just...stopped checking.Last month, my passion reignited with a burning vengeance as I found out that not only had development continued, IT RELEASED! I was beyond ecstatic, but I had to wait for the funds to get the game. I thought 25 was a hefty price tag, but I was willing to give it a shot. I set aside a weekend, got the game, and I dived in.I was blown away. The story, the world, the new controls, the characters, the sprite work, the levels, the OST, everything hit me like a truck. I started my play on the hard setting, and I was blown away by how even that worked, and the menus assist settings to help newer platformer players get into it! (I love settings that help new players enjoy the genre, as I enjoy seeing new players succeed and get better!)I'm going to be honest, I have never had a game make me feel like a kid again before, and I don't know if I ever will, but this is a thank you to the devs for allowing me to relive those kid-like feelings of wonder and amazement, and even accomplishment at achieving victory. Even the final boss theme hit me different. It made the fight intense and sad at the same time, gave me the feeling of "this is IT, all or nothing" as I fought my hardest, using every trick I'd been taught to win.A satisfying ending to a seven year wait, this most definitely was.My list of Pros:-Difficulty customization is unique, and I think it's a great addition to the game. You can choose the way you want to S rank a level if that's your goal, or you can choose the best items to achieve your victory, or even to help you beat a level faster than ever before.-Level Designs are great. I never really felt like I had to slow down too much in a level. There were a couple puzzle segments that upset me a bit, but since I'm biased against most puzzles, I will abstain from judging that as a negative.-Boss Designs are incredible. All of the bosses felt unique to fight, and all had their own patterns of movement and attack, No boss really felt too frustrating for me, save one, It's mostly because the boss is frequently off-screen and that makes it hard to tell where the boss is. I had to use particles to guess the buss location and hope I aimed right. If the camera in that fight zoomed out a little bit to accommodate the boss's size, I think that would easily fix my negative view of that particular fight.-Lots of levels! There are an incredible number of stages, and thus content, in the game. I have put in about 20 hours on Lilac's story alone, and there are four versions, one for each character and their particular journey in the world.-The Sprites are very fun! I enjoyed the large variety of characters and sprites, and if I recall correctly, almost all were unique sprites, giving each character their own life and appearance! In addition, the stages are GORGEOUS. they look incredible, and the backgrounds are no different. Everything just feels and looks so good, I was never bored by the appearance of a level!-The story is good. They actually explain a lot more of the world's lore, and dive into the history of their planet. I had been curious about this since the first game, and I finally got some of what I wanted. Excellent execution and very good characters (especially the voice acting improvement! Great job!) help make the world come to life.-The OST is bangin'. I love almost all the music in this game, there was never a time where I wanted to mute the music. Sometimes I boot the game just to play some of the OST collectibles in the jukebox because they are so good. A certain boss theme really does it for me and hits me in the emotions.The Cons-There are still some bugs in the game. I've been thrown out of the level in a few maps and either got soft locked or just...arbitrarily cleared the stage by hitting some unseen flag. I'm unsure if this is an intentional "recovery" feature (no matter how good your programming and testing might be, someone is still gonna find somewhere to break your game! Hello, speedrunning community!) but it was a tad confusing/frustrating when it happened.-Some hitboxes are not obvious that they are hitboxes until you've died a few times to it. One particular attack that got on my nerves with this was an attack with a dagger that had shockwave clouds around it. Little did I know, not only did the line the dagger traveled hit you, but the cloud shockwaves would hit you too! (cost me my rainbow s rank a couple times and believe me, I was heated)-Some spawn checkpoints are a tad far, from bosses enough to be annoying, but not enough to constitute a game design sin. As someone who likes to go fast when I get good at something, having that delay every time I go to fight them was definitely something I found zero fun in.-some items are able to be selected even though they do nothing for you in that stage. I think the items should have a clear warning if you can't use them in the stage, or be locked. (Final stage Timer Badge is one I can think of immediately)TL'DRGame's really good, got a couple minor gripes but nothing too major, definitely worth your time for players of all skill levels. And I think the overall quality justifies your money expenditure, as well.Final Score: 9/10Very good job, devs.
_childDocuments_.name: Freedom Planet 2

_childDocuments_.review: Going into this, already being a massive fan of the first game, it would have taken something truly special to blow me away like the first game did. But, not only did Freedom Planet 2 live up to the first game, it surpassed it in every conceivable way. No, it went even beyond that.The genuine surprise and joy of playing Freedom Planet 2 doesn't come from saying "Wow! This is like if Treasure made a Sonic game" it comes from the realization that this game is BETTER than that hypothetical game! Every element comes at you with the energy of what had to be the happiest game makers on the planet. There's ALWAYS something new coming at you, and with the quality of the art, music, level design, enemies, and game feel, you'll be surprised to know the amount of content this game has. Freedom Planet to just about triples the amount of content from the first game, and that's not counting the fact that there's 1 more character, and 2 more adventure campaign stories than last time. This could have easily been a $40.00 price tag, but at it's current price, it's more than a steal.This game puts FREEDOM in Freedom Planet. The movement options and level design go together so well, you'll find yourself in a constant loop of speed, exploration, discovery, and combat ALL AT THE SAME TIME!To all video game fans out there, this is a genuine victory for the industry, and not something you should pass up. In a year with Sifu, Bayonetta 3, and God of War Ragnarok, Freedom Planet 2 will still probably speed away with my game of the year.

_childDocuments_.review: The sequel that got hit with 4 years of delays, maybe 5, it was so long I can't remember. With all that time, it had big expectations from me to live up to, and fortunately it came out pretty good. It's clear if you played the first game that with the sequel they wanted to set themselves apart a bit more from the spiky blue guy who runs fast, redesigning the characters and adding a little more focus to the combat. Fans of Sonic games or the first Freedom Planet should absolutely give this one a go... There's even a free demo!In general, the entire scale of the game compared to the last one is much larger as one would expect. While the levels are shorter, being comprised of one stage rather than 2 parts separated by a miniboss, there are a lot more of them. There's an additional playable character bringing the total to 4. There's an area you can freely revisit that has a bunch of short challenges and a few minigames to partake in. There's even a secret ending!Every character's mobility has been improved since the last game as well, so navigating the stages can be a little easier, and there's an ingenious option to zoom the camera out when you're speeding around! And there's a new guard feature, so incoming unavoidable attacks can still be dodged with some good timing.It's hard to comment on the game's difficulty, as it's tied to optional items you can equip/remove when selecting a stage. I found it to be pretty fair overall, though without the items I believe it's a little too easy, and using those items increase your rewards at the end of a stage, so they're worth using if you care about ranks or 100%ing the game.Possibly the most welcome improvement of all: The voice volume slider. No longer do you have to subject yourself to the sometimes grating voice acting this game offers, though you'll miss out on one NPC voiced by Chris Sabat if you do.Oh, the soundtrack is good too. It's a great game overall, and a worthy sequel. It may be even better than the first, personally I'd say are equal.
_childDocuments_.name: Freedom Planet 2

_childDocuments_.review: Freedom Planet 2 is amazing and better than the first one in every way. I have waited a long time for this game and i can definitely say that it was worth the wait. Freedom Planet 1 was pretty much my favorite game of all time and they managed to make something that i love even more and i'm very thankful for every hour that was spend with making this game!!The Levels are incredibly creative and every single one of them has something special that makes it stand out. The Leveldesign is also absolutely amazing, really intuitive and fluid. The controls are just as fluid and it's just fun to move the Character around. The Bosses are also really creative and can be a great challenge, once you've learned them you can whack them easily and that's really fun! So yea, everything about the Gameplay is perfection! The pixel art is probably the most beautiful pixel art that i have ever seen, espacially the Hub Worlds are so pretty. Same goes for the Character and Enemy desings, really detailed and you can tell that there was put a lot of love and care into designing everything. The music is just as great as in the first one, pretty much every song is a banger. Only complaint is that it often sounds a little too soft, i prefer the powerful songs with guitars in it and there was a little less of that in this game then i would have liked but it's still amazing. The music also often captures the feelings of the Characters really well in specific situations. Now to the Story. I already loved the story in the first game but they have gone wild with the Story in this one. I loved watching every single Cutcene and Learning about the lore. It's often really dramatic but also has a lot of jokes, sometimes it can also get really dark and i just love it regardless of what is happening right now, it always has my interest. The Hubworlds also have a bunch of NPC's that have a lot to say so yea, you can learn a lot about the world and their Characters and i love everything about it. The Game also has so much optional content that you can really spend lots of hours with completing it and every second of that was amazing for me. Now to some of the bad stuff, which isn't much. So the only thing about the Story that bothered me is that it kind of ends with a teaser for more of the story and it took 8 years for this game to come out, so i want to know more about the Story and how it will continue but there i will have to wait a lot of years until anything will be continued. I like the ending but i just want more of the story xD The other thing that is bothering me (mostly for the first days that the game was out) is the lack if polish. I encountered a lot of bugs and softlocks and i didn't expected so many bugs after the game was being worked on for so long, but they are fixing it faster than i can look so that isn't a problem anymore. So yea, the game is just amazing, amazing AND amazing. I want to thank Sabrina DiDuro and everyone at Galaxytrail for making this masterpiece of a game. I'm incredibly thankful for your hard work, thank you. I can't stop gushing about it, buy it, play it and fall in love with it. 10/10 My Favorite game ever.

_childDocuments_.review: Very Satisfactory this game is absolutely worth your time!Very Satisfied, it runs well even with Proton emulation under an obscure Linux Distribution.There have been FPS issues in the first Freedom Planet during certain scenes like when the bosses exploded or during certain boss fights, i am happy to Report that there are no noticeable FPS issues this time!My hardware:CPU: four core, Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-4670Graphicscard: GeForce GTX 1060 6GBRAM: 16 GB DDR3OS: Arch linux (proton was used to run the game)Same or even better then FP1, the Music is very nicely done and reminds me of games like jazz jackrabbit.You can choose between four different characters, each of them has different abilities and play styles.I also like to mention the way difficulty is managed in this game, because the player has a lot of options to tailor their gaming experience. You can either be the super hardcore player by actively sabotaging your health and lives with certain items to create an especially hard challenge for yourself, or you can also craft or buy certain items to make it easier on yourself. There is also a timer for each level and high scores which makes the game interesting for completionists and speed runners.
