_childDocuments_.review: Based on early impressions: Lovable heroines: CheckBangin' soundtrack: CheckTight controls and fast paced platforming: Check Brutal boss encounters that will keep you on your toes: CheckCheesy dialogue: Check It's a Freedom Planet game. The core mechanics of the original are improved and expanded upon and the heroines have been re-balanced giving Milla and Carol the same satisfying feeling to play as Lilac (who in the first was arguably the best kitted character by a long-shot) while retaining the unique play-style between all 4 playable characters. Neera's kit, unfortunately, I feel plays a little too stiffly for the high-speed action. For the platformer expert the boss encounters, so far, have been easier than in Freedom Planet 1 but it's definitely balanced out by the fact that the difference between a death and a game over is no longer mere formality. On expert mode a game over will leave you with the choice of either restarting the stage from the beginning or buying your way back to your most recent checkpoint with a not unsubstantial sum of your hard-earned crystals. There are items that can be obtained that can offer nominal improvements to your characters (or even add additional challenge in exchange for a higher bonus at the end of the level) but for the purist it is far from a mandatory part of the game and empty item slots give you a nominal increase to your end of level bonus so the item system is definitely balanced with the purists (who would probably rather ignore the item system) in mind- even to the point that two key bonus challenge items are automatically equipped at the start of an expert play-through. My two biggest complaints would be that Neera just doesn't feel anywhere near as satisfying to play as one of the original trio and on some of the longer boss fights the boss music will stop dead for a couple of seconds before restarting instead of looping smoothly. I will update the review later if the experience falls off, otherwise just assume that the entire game is rated: out of 10

_childDocuments_.review: It's been a long 7 years but it was worth the wait! I love the revamped artstyle, the plethora of stages (haven't even finished it yet and holy crap), and while I can see how the hub areas might be a nuisance for some I personally love exploring them and getting all the little tidbits from NPCs. _childDocuments_.review: Freedom Planet 2 is quite a beautiful and content-rich successor. It features astonishing BGMs and exciting stages with pretty details that make everything feel a lot more alive while also adding interesting mechanics to the gameplay. Stages such as Zulon Jungle, Zao Land, Phoenix Highway, Shenlin Park, Sky Bridge, and Globe Opera are outstanding and creative. On the other hand, I couldn't appreciate the red stages quite as much. They felt like shallow and repetitive boss fights that require the player to wait too long for an opportunity to attack rather than give their best. Even more if you're playing on Expert and looking for an S rank as Lilac, whose move set isn't as compelling as other character's. What's worse is a part of the game has quite the streak of red stages and cutscenes that would be a pain to watch were it not for the quality voice acting. Don't miss out on this if you're a fan of the genre, but expect to get dragged into dull fights and rides as you approach the lategame and the game decides to go longer than neccessary. I'd rather have a slightly shorter campaign to play and collect everything once as each character than having such an extensive one I don't feel like going through a second time.

_childDocuments_.review: Took me a solid 42 Hours to complete the 4 characters campaignsCarol was played firstMilla secondNeera Li Third Lilac 4thWill challenge the rest of the 17 achievements left (mostly speedruns and collectathons.) in which I will update this review.At the time I would say this.Its a decent game but it feels a little cut around the edges for some parts of the game especially art materials revealed in the past 7 years since the Freedom Planet 1 release (July 21st 2014). *A photo of Lilac's gang + Spade/Dail alongside Carozon Tea on a airship. Probably just for promotional sake to stir hype. Sadly the same event doesn't happen in the game.  Majority of the music is solid for the most part but it does not leave much of an impact as the first game. Sadly only 7 stages has leitmotifs from the first game. While the Soundtrack is indeed weaker then the first game, it makes up for it with nearly 17 more songs of the song-list (FP1:72 tracks / FP2-89 tracks) from the first game which is quite nice.Story Mode of Carol Tea is quite endearing but it leaves more to be desired with interactions to her and her sister. Only a few instances are just her meeting her sister and her sister just jets with a warning. I feel Corazon could've been made to be a more integral part of the game itself. But it be how it be I suppose. Not much of her past is revealed. Only references of her previous occupation before teaming with Lilac.Milla the Hound while her past is mysterious since the first game being adopted to Carol and Lilacs' care, it comes to light in this game. Which I believe is to be the most impactful of all 4 Plots within Freedom Planet 2.Story mode for Neera Li left more to be desired, hardly put nothing is revealed about her past, mostly a soldier through and through being quite focused and tempermental.Lilac story basically gives more depth to what Lilacs' motives are especially with her kind. But it falls a bit short somewhat as it just makes her more of a worry-wort instead of the determined and focused character from the first game. Though it is questionable of the *Past* of Lilac of how she became to be considering how the ages are. The new antagonist while the initial reveal shows them to be capable, gets a bit lamp-shaded being behind the scenes for majority of the game until 3/4ths of the way through the campaign. Brevon from the first game had more of a existent threat than she was as he was making loud moves between the three kingdoms of Shang Tu, Shang Mu and Shuigang. Not until the reveal of the antagonist of the second game to the cast did it felt that the world was coming undone.Strengths4 different styles of playA expansive world map that expands around world-building of planet Avalice.Bigger soundtrackSome characters backstory is revealed but not fully.WeaknessClassic Mode locked after first completion of Adventure Mode which can be a bit of a slow-going but I'd feel after first playthrough Classic Mode would be a must to play for a streamlined exp. without the padding inbetween stages.Soundtrack is less memorable than the first game with some tracks placed in, however there are quite a few bangers within the game.  Game feels a bit straightforward this time around which is quite weird. After you play through the stages first time around or so, you start to feel that the stages are quite easy to memorize and quite very so you can breeze through them quickly as possible. (Even one of the achievements is to beat the game in under 4 hours time from total time of the stages.) Still, longer than the first game which *CAN* be completed in under a hour or two if focused.Story seems a bit cut out. Some moments seems to be omitted out to make the game much more flow through. I prefer the first game story overall to be straight blunt with you. But personal preferences aside. Its serviceable somewhat.You will notice that the further you get into the game, the more enemy spam placement there will be. In most cases they are merely hindrances that you can ignore (however upon defeating some enemies you get Energy Cores in which you can redeem for Gold Gems to unlock items/potions to enrich gameplay.)Serpentine isn't a jobber anymore? Maybe? Maybe not? You decide.The new characters (outside of Carol sister) are questionable at best for their purpose and being in the game. They feel out of place and out of sorts compared to the other cast. At least talking to some of the NPCs is quite nice for the first romp through the game however on subsequent playthroughs I just wanted to blitz through the game to complete it. Would be nice to implement some additional effects from chatting with the NPCs such as quests and what-nots. Mayhaps for future implementations there would be a reward to enhance the game with more content? Who knows.For under $22 its a good game to get. $25+ unless it has further updates and DLC included within would be more appetizing. I feel the game is lacking quite a bit. Need more story implementations for the characters.But I recommend it if Spark 3 being 3D isn't good for you. Then the old 2D-platforming Razzle Dazzle would be perfect for you.*Update*70 Hours upon completion and I got my time in the game 100% with every achievement managed to unlock.My entire playthrough can be watched here. 13 Videos chronicled for the game. Mistakes were made, improvements were done, and shortcuts were taken. Regardless I had fun. Here's hoping you do the same if you purchase this title for its full amount that it is worth.

_childDocuments_.review: Basically everything there was to love about the first Freedom Planet, refined and built up for an even bigger, better, gayer experience. Shikata ga nai and such.On the whole it feels more balanced than the previous one, so no more having to stockpile extra lives for an endgame meat grinder. However, there's a lot more boss fights with multiple phases/enemies that can prove frustrating. There's also a new system of held items and potions that can be confusing at first, but useful for boosting your characters or providing different, additional challenges. It's completely optional too, so you can just play how you like.The soundtrack is as great as ever, sprites are detailed and well animated and backgrounds beautifully rendered, and the voice work is lively (admittedly some of it's pretty cringe but by now that comes with the territory. I accept and am at peace). This sequel isn't breaking a lot of new ground, but it's a solid and fun game regardless.

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing action platformer with blending its speed and characters' combat abilities for fresh feeling fast paced game play. _childDocuments_.review: Freedom Planet 2 is 50% a great time 50% unnecessary additions and bloat. It's clear that a lot of passion and time went into a dream game but the developer was never told what ideas might be working and what would have been better to cut.The template is the same as the first game. It's a heavily Sonic platforming game with some light combat elements. The core Sonic platforming is the strongest part and though the physics aren't quite as well tuned that's probably more of a consequence of more moving environment parts and it never broke in any significant way. There's a huge variety of levels with unique stage mechanics: one of my favourites being a giant bat that shoots you off a baseball miles across the stage. The main issue is everything else.There are some stages that have more of a puzzle element, collecting machine parts or keys etc and sometimes these are interesting diversions and other times tedious chores. My main contention is the bosses which are memorable artistically and often conceptually but just aren't fun to play. It's like you are playing Megaman Zero bosses but without the deliberate and tight movement akin to that series (point stolen from Stu Gipp). It doesn't help that boss stages are often so large the enemy moves offscreen, potentially throwing attacks at the same time. I think I enjoyed only one or two bosses throughout my entire playthrough.I should also touch on the story. It's very much bunk but unlike the first game which has a classic mode to skip through it, this one makes you play through the whole story first. I'm assuming you get classic mode after finishing the story. There is no option to fast forward the dialogue so you if the voices are driving you nuts, or you just read the text as quick as I do your options are either sit through or skip. I honestly don't think this games has a subtle enough touch to be talking about species genocide: maybe don't have the antagonist sporting Dr. Wily skull mechs as a minimum??I've played about 7 hours of the game with one character, Lilac. In terms of content that's impressive because there's still three other characters with unique gimmiks. This would be great if I wasn't dreading taking those characters through the aforementioned aggravating parts. I didn't enjoy taking Lilac through the mecha piece hunt, getting dogpilled with enemies and walls/ground of spikes; why would I enjoy it with Milla?There's some other issues to briefly touch on. The music is good but I don't think it's a cut on the original game. The pixel art is very detailed with wonderful animations but the background art can often be so cluttered that it's hard to tell what's foreground or not. It feels like GalaxyTrail is equally committed to undercutting it's great ideas as it to passionately crafting an engaging game. I really don't want to mark this down because it has so many fun ideas and level mechanics so I would say pick this up on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a much more fleshed out sonic game, that lets you go faster faster, with more flexibility.  Sonic was honestly always held back by its desire to keep things simple, and a bit of level design and screen size, sonic mania showed what really good level design and even a slightly bigger screen can do for the game.  Freedom Planet 2's addition of a screen that can zoom out really highlights how nice more information is in these games, though it's unfortunate that the pixel count doesn't increase as the game zooms out, as it makes some sprites look a little wonkier, but it's not too bad.  The addition of attacks, guards and some special abilities makes their characters feel unique and increases the things a character can do, at the exchange of having to use more than one or two buttons.  Playing as Lilac, you can use her Dragon Boost ability to speed up from a standstill, like sonic's spindash, but since it's assigned to a single button, seperate from the jump button, rather than a combination of down and the jump button you can use this ability much quicker, in addition in being able to do it while still in movement, even using it in the air and angling to fly through the air.  It results in a more flexible move, which will make obstacles easier to by pass, but,the move itself is insanely fun to use.  The invincibility on the move does have the potential to make it kinda OP, but the short cool down and direction lock on it is usually enough to keep you from spamming it and just never dying.The other 3 characters all offer their own unique play styles, though I haven't played much of them.  A big portion of this review is coming from my experience with the previous game, and finding this game to be a big upgrade to what they did previously.  The voice acting and story are a bit too anime and cutesy at time, but there is plenty of charm and the voice actors are actually quite good, just know if you're some hardcore cool guy you might feel like a bit of a weirdo showing it to friends.  I know playing it in front of my D&D nerd friends resulted in a bit of joking about the story and characters.

_childDocuments_.review: Ignore my playtime, almost all of my playtime was when I had no internet. I have finished the game as Lilac and Carol.I think for how closely I followed the development of this game, for how much of an absolute ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ reply guy I was in Sabrina DiDuro's and GalaxyTrail's tweets just expressing how hype I was for this game, I have done a disservice for not writing a review sooner.Let me start by saying, I do not consider either of these games 'Sonic' games, and their identity should not be likened to Sonic. They are wholly different experiences that only ultimately share the very baseline DNA of 'Going ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Hard' with the blue blur. With that said, Freedom Planet 1 was, for many years of my life, what i considered 'The Best Sonic Game'--if Sonic made a game exactly like Freedom Planet, just with a sonic skin and sonic-themed movesets, it would probably still not be as fun as Freedom Planet. I've played Freedom Planet 1 so many ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ times, at this point, it's probably more than I've ever played Cave Story.Freedom Planet 2 is  After completing Lilac's story, I said, holy ♥♥♥♥, I feel like I got my money's worth and a half. I can't bang out a run of FP2 in one day like I can FP1, but that's more than okay to me. The game is immaculate. If you played Freedom Planet 1 and you thought to yourself, damn, this can't get better, well, TOO BAD, MORON, because  The combat feels better, the characters have all received a massive glow up that makes them so much more fun to play that after playing this game, I don't think I *can* go back to Freedom Planet 1. Much like Freedom Planet 1, the crown jewel of this game is Lilac. With new moves that interact with her dash, the ability to uppercut out of a jump, and her cyclone no longer taking any meter, it's like Freedom Planet 1 was you playing the game with ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ training wheels. Carol and Milla are both very fun to play in this game, way better than they were in the first game. Had Lilac stayed the same as she was in FP1, I would not be able to pick a favorite. However, for all the improvements made to Carol and Milla, Lilac matched those in spades. If I had one complaint with this game, it's that Lilac is *too fun.* She makes me not want to play as the other characters, because even though they ARE fun, Lilac is so well designed I start to feel like everything in the platformer genre was just the buildup to Sash "Lilac Freedom Planet 2" Lilac.One other complaint I would say I have, unfortunately, I don't think Neera is very fun at all. The power character type is interesting, but I don't feel like she does anything particularly useful with it and she doesn't make fighting feel any more satisfying than it does with Carol, and neither of them are as fun as Lilac. Even so, at her worst, she is still inherently fun to move around with like the others.The soundtrack to FP2 is, much like the first game, an absolute ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ banger. Just amazing all around. Like, if I had to make any criticisms, it's that Merga's motif isn't quite as good as Brevon's. The storytelling in this game is also far better than it was in FP1, managing to stick a lot closer to the tone I think they intended. There are still a few moments, jokes mainly, that I don't think landed, but at the end of the day I think the game does a much better job, though I do think while Merga is a great villain, she does somewhat live in the shadow of Brevon and how perfect he was.My only other complaint regarding the story of this game is something I hope can be adressed in Freedom Planet 3, provided it happens. There will be some story spoilers for the ending of Lilac's story ahead, so just, you know, read at your own risk.The ending clarifying and establishing Lilac and Carol's relationship as a romantic one is something I'm sort of conflicted about. In my head, when I think about it, I like this relationship. It makes sense. They're cute together. However, unfortunately, this is only really something that extends into my head. Part of the plot of FP2 is based on Carol going off on her own and getting into trouble, and Lilac and Carol having these repeated disagreements that put strain on their relationship. This makes sense and I think is a good hardship that the two overcoming helps them understand their feelings for each other better, but my real issue comes in the fact that we unfortunately only see them disagree and fight. There are so few scenes in Freedom Planet 1 or 2 where the two of them are shown to be friends, to know each other well and get along in a way that isn't specifically a team rally declaring that they can do anything. Off the top of my head, I can only think of the scene where they're watching the movie in the first game, and even then, part of that is based on Milla, and more serves to establish Milla as a friend of Carol and Lilac, but not actually doing much in terms of the friendship between Carol and Lilac specifically. To be clear, I don't say this because I want to pick apart the writing of this game, I just want the relationship between the two protagonists to be as good as possible because I love these games. I hope for the future of the series, we can see more interactions of the two of them just being... friends. Lovers too, of course, but I think first and foremost friends.

_childDocuments_.review: In this spoiler-free discussion, I talk about why Freedom Planet 2 is the greatest indie game ever made! It's the best indie game of all time!This is a game where you control four anthropomorphic animals who have to fight off the robots, criminals, and invaders of Avalice by beating the crap out of them. It's basically a character action game similar in vain to Sonic the Hedgehog and Gunstar Heroes. The game is divided up into levels where players are tasked with fighting off enemies in close off encounters and then players are then ranked at the end of the level based off their performance. How ever unlike most speedrun action games where you play as a blue hedgehog fighting against robots by jumping into them, Freedom Planet 2 task the player to fight robots in combat by using a bunch of unique special moves. Lilac can speed boost and a spin attack, Carol can do claw attacks and rides a motorcycle, Milla can create cubes and use a shield burst, and Neera uses a spear and make some ice attacks. Unlike the first game where it's just a speed platformer, the sequel itself have put into more into that, like hub worlds, shops, and even battlesphere challenges. Not only that, but this game also added in some collectibles and secrets where you can find in the game like brave stones, power ups, music vinyls, and tons of other items which I don't want to spoil. The game takes the speed combat pushes it to it's absolute limits and creates some of the most unique gameplay mechanics to a video game I've ever seen, and while I can't spoil everything about this game in order to entice everyone to play it, it's best just to discover all of this stuff while you're playing the game yourself. I mean it's one thing to watch a let's play of Freedom Planet 2, but it's a completely different experience while you're controlling the game in motion. Now let's not to say that the gameplay is the only great thing about this game because the story and the cutscenes are really amazing. Even if you're playing the game on the lowest difficulty setting and fumbling your way through the combat system, you'll still be able to enjoy the colorful cast of characters and all the crazy set pieces. The entire game is heavily inspired by Dragon Ball Z and Sonic Adventure, it's like this crazy saturday morning cartoon where the stakes constantly scale up to borderline ridiculous scenarios. The boss fights are these mecha animal creatures where you need to fight a week point to fight off the boss itself, and the game just constantly one-ups itself until it escalates into one of the most over-the-top mind-blowing hype as hell endings to a video game I've ever seen. And you're just sitting there watching the end credits feeling incredibly happy, and exhausted like getting screwed. Still for the majority of players who will most likely put the game down once they've reached to the end credits, it's still a completely fantastic game that anyone can enjoy, and I highly recommend it to everyone. It's one of the greatest indie games I have ever played! In conclusion, Freedom Planet 2 was the best indie game on Steam, it's easily the best game of the year, and possibly most likely the greatest game ever made of all time!

_childDocuments_.review: (As of writing this I have only beaten the game as Lilac.) Freedom Planet 2 is more than just a game for me, it was an EXPERIENCE. This game is a prime example for how to create a sequel that's even bigger and better than the original. From the core gameplay tweaks, the level design bursting with really fun and creative gimmicks, more balanced bosses, the more appealing and improved character designs, the improved combat thanks to the new abilities and the guard move, and the gorgeous spritework--some of the best I've ever seen in a videogame--there is a lot to love about this game. It really says something about the game’s quality when I’d even consider the weaker stages to still be good at the first least. Combined with the items and the ranking system on top of that, you have a game that’s endlessly replayable. But the aspect that has seen by far the largest jump in quality in my opinion is the story and the overall writing. I'd say that the story is really good--great even this time around, thanks to the improved presentation, very likable characters (with Lilac being one of my new favorite characters of all time), great voice acting, tighter writing, fairly high stakes, really funny humor, and better cutscene pacing to name a few things. Merga especially runs circles around Brevon from FP1 when it comes to being the main villain due to how compelling her backstory and motivations were, and how the story explored her relations with Lilac seeing as both of them are the last known water dragons. The overall tone is much more consistent as well, as while the game has its fair share of comedy, it knows when to slow things down when it has its more serious moments, compared to the first game which had some serious tonal whiplash issues. The game even did a fairly good job at tackling more serious themes, such as the effects of colonialism, mass genocide, and historical revisionism to name a few. As for some other aspects, I even really liked the addition of hub worlds as a nice break between the main action stages and the NPCs as well! They also do a great job when it comes to the worldbuilding of Avalice, and how it makes the world feel properly lived in. When it comes to the soundtrack: while FP1 might have arguably higher highs, I still think FP2 has a really awesome soundtrack in its own right, and I really appreciate the wide variety of musical styles. Overall, Freedom Planet 2 is not only one of the best 2D platformers out there, but it's also one of my new favorite games of all time while probably being one of if not my favorite indie game of all time. 10/10, this game is absolutely worth picking up if you're a fan of 2D platformers and women. You don't need to play the first game in order to enjoy the second, but I'd still recommended playing it as it's still a great game in its own right, and it makes it easier to appreciate the changes 2 made. Definitely looking forward to doing future playthroughs with the other 3 characters at some point.

Ok, but it'll still get boring to-... is that items that make the game harder?All by themselves are nothing to write home about but combined!There's where your hours will go away.I feel like this is the type of game where you pick up where you left off, play for an hour, and then stop because it can be hard sometimes (especially the bosses).

_childDocuments_.review: I had high expectations for Freedom Planet 2, but the game somehow still managed to dragon boost itself past them! The game is full of little details that makes everything feel alive. You can really tell that a lot of love has been poured into it. Even just dashing around in the tutorial level is a lot of fun since the controls are so spot on! While it would have been nice with a native Linux build, the game runs great in Proton Experimental.The only issue I had was the frame rate of the final stages. I play using an iGPU on a rather old machine (Ivy Bridge, fourth generation i5). The game ran perfectly up until the final stages where it dropped to just a couple of frames per second. Changing the graphics form 1080p to 360p for these parts brought the frame rate back to more-than-playable levels. This probably had something to do with the combination of my old GPU and Proton, but it might be worth keeping in mind if you use an older machine as well.I found everything about this game to be top-notch. The gameplay, the artwork, the music, and the way the story brings everything together. The things I wrote in the first paragraph after a couple of hours still stand after having finished my initial play-through. The game kept raising the quality slowly all the way through. I don't think I've ever had such an intense adrenaline rush before this, even if Freedom Planet 2 felt easier than its predecessor!I strongly recommend both Freedom Planet and Freedom Planet 2 for everyone who enjoys side-scrollers!

_childDocuments_.review: Freedom Planet 2 is, in pretty much every conceivable way, a superior game to Freedom Planet 1. It took 8 years to develop, and it shows.FP2 is a speedy platformer with diverging paths and lots to explore. It draws heavily on influence from both Sonic and Megaman in pretty much all aspects. Combat is snappy--you never spend too long on a single enemy in the field--with just a pinch of depth that makes conquering boss fights feel rewarding. The stages are beautiful, with powerups and secrets to find. Difficulty in this game is easily modulated with helpful and hurtful items, so you can find that perfect balance of a playthrough or mess with fun, wacky combinations.The story itself is pretty middle of the road, which is fine. FP2, like it's predecessor, is dedicated to easy-breezy saturday morning cartoon vibes, and the story beats fit perfectly in line with that. The tone gives way for some moments of drama and tension which I personally appreciated.Like with FP1, the thing this game excels the most with is its visual story telling. There's a ton of dialogue to be had in FP2, but I found myself most engaged in the story and stakes in many of the later stages where GalaxyTrails' spark for visuals comes to life. There is a lot of care poured into each stage that tells its own story, so much that playing in classic mode with barebones story still contains the same sense of motion and tension.10/10 Best unexpected game of 2022
_childDocuments_.name: Freedom Planet 2

_childDocuments_.review: The game's genuinely fantastic. It's fresh, fast and fun!The graphics are more detailed and prettier than FP1, and are impressive in motion with how well-animated every single one is. The sound and music quality is AAA.Overworld map design is SMB3-like and therefore great. It's great how city hubs were implemented, and the NPCs therin were all funny, witty or both.Story mission being available in almost any order does wonders for replayability, and was a genius addition. Story pacing, along with tonal consistency, was an improvemnt over FP1, and the optional lore collectibles were a nice side quest.The difficulty curve is very finely tuned in the second half. The bosses stage bosses becoming cuphead-levels of hard near the end made me very nostalgic for the first game.(Don't know if the devs've said for how long these updates currently being released twice a week will continue for. But I hope they eventually include fixes for some some nit-picky details like:Remains to be seen, but at this pace they'll surely be done polishing this up before the summer 2023 console ports.)

_childDocuments_.review: Freedom Planet and Freedom Planet 2 are a masterpiece of platforming. This game offers more hours of exciting meticulously crafted game play from every last pixel to the entire humongous soundtrack. You cannot find a better $ to entertainment value in any other game of it's like. The story and voice actors are absolutely amazing, there will be moments you laugh, and others where you feel the tingling emotions and butterflies. These games are instantly in the all time hall of fame for me when it comes to expressing the pure passion of a development team it shines through in the game as you play it.  There is plenty of replayability, again more than any other games in the genre. I cannot stress enough to anyone reading this right now considering this game that you are missing out on a gem of a game that in my strong opinion is leading the entire platformer genre even with the small development team and funding they have to work with, this game is more than all Sonic games ever were to me, and I used to be a Sonic die hard growing up. This game series has easily replaced Sonic for me.Thank you GalaxyTrail, I love you all!

_childDocuments_.review: Upon completion of Lilac's story, my thoughts of the game have changed entirely from when I first played it.  At first, I thought Freedom Planet 1 was the better game, however, with more experience with this game, that was clearly wrong.  The only things I can say are better in the original are the level-to-level gameplay rather than a small hubworld, even though it doesn't really hurt the game, and theme song, which in my opinion is still better than this game's theme, but that is subjective.  In terms of story, this game takes what the first game did and amplifies it by adding more character drama, more intensity to the character interactions, and genuinely helping to make the villain more connected to the main characters, something that Brevon lacked.  In terms of gameplay, nothing bad to say, takes everything the original did and amplifies it ten fold.  The Sonic influence is still very much present in this game, even down to adding grinding as a mechanic, and I am truthfully a huge fan of this aspect of the game.  Sonic is my favorite franchise of all time, and to see those who understand the reasons why the classic 90s Sonic games' levels worked so well and apply them with a unique and fresh touch that not even Sonic Mania has.  Well Sonic Mania suffers from originality issues in terms of level themes, this game does not, which is awesome to see.  Bosses in this game are fun as well, retaining that classic sense of timing and waiting for an opening.  Music is fantastic, no complaints there.  Overall, this game takes everything that was fantastic about the first game and amplifies it.  The first game used to be my favorite indie game of all time, ever since I first played it 7 years ago, but now I am happy to say this game lived up to all of my expectations and is now my favorite indie game of all time.  I have huge nostalgia for this franchise and I really do hope GalaxyTrail continues with another sequel.  This game is not just a fantastic treat for Sonic fans, but fans of classic platformers as well.  Classic platformers in the vain of Sonic and Mario are my favorite genre and this game knocks it out of the park in that category.  Exquisite work GalaxyTrail, here's to hoping for more successes in your future!

_childDocuments_.review: Warning: This review contains major spoilers for the story of Freedom Planet 2. If you do not want to be spoiled, please avoid this review until you finish the game. Howdy! Player of the original Freedom Planet here. Cracking good game, that. And after getting the sequel, I can conclusively say it's a drastic improvement in a lot of ways. +Characters got a lot more moves and rebalanced mechanics+Soundtrack SLAPS+Story has a better time balancing the tone+Voice acting is better. My man Alejandro Saab still shines!+The art is gorgeous. Which art? Pretty much all of it. Sprites, backgrounds, you name it+There are a lot of levels.+Lot more stuff to do, such as the Battlesphere and purchasing items.And a downgrade in others. Allow me to elaborate:-A lot of the game makes callbacks to the first game, Freedom Planet 1. It's not detrimental to gameplay at all, but noticeable from even a casual glance during cutscenes and dialogue.-Difficulty spikes, the level where you  being a particularly bad offender. The enemies take ludicrous amounts of damage on Normal. The game is practically screaming at you to use the new parry/dodge system when this isn't normally the kind of game that has that and its predecessor didn't.-The levels are longer. That's subjective, but some levels were simply wayyyyy too long. Cripes, one took me upwards of 20 minutes because I just kept getting lost!-The items you can buy are uninteresting for the most part. Playing as Milla, the life-steal item is practically useless because her hardest hitting attacks are ranged or non-physical.-The characters are fun, but often are written pretty wonkily. There's also a distinct disconnect between how some characters are described (*cough*Astal*cough*) and how they actually act. The character dialogue is fun but can sometimes fall flat. Milla's dialogue is the biggest offender. I get she's a young girl, but she is older now. She doesn't have to speak like a five-year old all the time now. And now you're saying she's some kind of science genius? Please. I approve her character growth but this dialogue is just way too childish.-There's a hub now and that's great, but 99% of the NPCs don't offer much of value other than odd chatter. One may call it world building, but there should be some mechanics built in somewhere. Such as side quests or something. There's shops yeah, but you put a "quick shop" option up there to skip walking to the shopkeeper. Also kind of hard to tell who the shopkeepers even are.-Distinct lack of character growth over the course of this game.-The Story itself and how the characters act. Wow. Ok, that's really subjective, but let me explain. This game does a lot good in terms of story. Heck it doesn't even commit the cardinal sin of "gameplay and story are segregated". Seriously I absolutely LOVE how Freedom Planet 2 merges story and gameplay. Other characters helping you out in cutscenes? There's a good chance they show up in levels  All the playable characters have aged several years and are a lot tougher, represented by expanded move pools compared to the first game. All that is awesome. This is the biggest critique I have of the game--plot holes and the characters sometimes act or talk like complete morons, and the general disconnect between the background fluff and what happens in game. Massive spoilers ahead. Sorry that got lengthy but felt it had to be said. Overall this game is great and a definite must for anyone who played the first game or wants to play a hearty side-scrolling platformer action game. And at its current price? A steal. An absolute steal. Bless GalaxyTrail for being so generous. I mean it. 8/10Edit: Spelled Askal's name wrong and removed unnecessary ranting.

_childDocuments_.review: After several hours in I can tell you this is the epitome of what a modern 2d sonic inspired platformer should feel like. It mixes in stage elements from Sonic 3, Sonic & Knuckles, and even some aesthetic from Sonic Adventure 2 even though it's not a 3d game. The combat mechanics also have a modern feel to them where stage bosses feel like stage bosses, and it can take a little bit of effort to get the patterns & mechanics down. It's not as brutal as something like Hollow Knight, but brings that same vibe that has graced a lot of the platformer & metroidvania genres in modern time that makes the battling a part of the game. This makes a lot of sense from a design perspective considering that there is more emphasis on non-Lilac game play.This game was a solid buy out of the gate, and it remains that way as they have continued to drop patches to fix bugs and tweak based on feedback every day since the release. -------------- Original Review -----------------Freedom Planet returns for a 2nd entry finally after many long years. It still holds the same charm as the first game with a bunch of new features, a new character, and new levels. The game's medium difficulty feels right, and for players who struggle there are assist options available such as auto-guard to not exclude anyone. This makes this both an incredible throwback to the era of 2D Sidescrollers, but also an easy title to jump into, or even have children play if you set up the accessibility options for them. I did have a bit of an issue getting used to the default control scheme, since it feels like it's from the Playstation 1/2 era, but the good news is there are options for changing bindings if you're really frustrated as well! Worked out of the box with a PS4 controller directly connected.Additionally it seems like there may be some bugs that haven't been fully worked out - I killed the boss on the second stage & got the achievement for killing it with dragon boost, however the stage didn't end, and it was then further immune with no health bar. After letting myself die and go back to the checkpoint, killing it the second time worked without issue, and hasn't impact any other level so far.Overall, this is a solid buy and I'm glad I bought it at release, it was worth the wait!

_childDocuments_.review: SOME SPOILERS AHEAD IF THAT MATTERS TO YOU.Freedom Planet 2 is probably my favourite platformer i've played in the last few years. Being a mix of speed and action with the occasional precise sections, the game reminds me a lot of S3&K with a dash of Shantae, which is a great mix if you ask me.To start this off; the first thing I always look for in a game: music. It's great. All of it. Go listen to the soundtrack if you haven't, you wont regret it.The levels are all designed well with multiple routes through most of them.The 4 characters all control near perfectly. every issue I had with the control in the first game is gone (Milla is fun to play and wildkick is gone)boss fights are all very fun both the first time and the 5th. they're simple and can be cheesed but are fun no less, and the music is great. (Vs. Corazon my beloved)The story is engaging with a near perfect length. if you want more, each character experiences it from their own point of view and are all fairly different. It's essentially 4 for the price of 1.Merga is a great villain, and her motive is understandable and hell, even justified.the twist supporting antagonists were all great. (and one of them is Vegetable which is an automatic +1(5?) from me)As for the side content, it's there but not needed which in my opinion, is exactly how side content should be made. and the extra boss and ending for completing the battlesphere is a great incentive to complete it.TL;DR: If you like platformers, action games, or are just looking for something casual to play for a few hours every now and then, Freedom Planet 2 is a near-perfect experience that you're bound to love.

_childDocuments_.review: Perspective: Just finished the game on Normal (middle difficulty) using Carol earlier today. Still intend to play the other characters. I also played a ton of the first game and considered it one of my favorite 2D platformers ever. If you haven't played the original then this may not be quite as good a review for you, but if you're at all a fan of fast, action focused 2D platformers and don't mind a challenge then definitely go for it.Pros:-Music slaps as expected-Movesets of characters are expanded from the original, Carol's shuriken is very fun to use-Love love LOVE the level aesthetics and variety, every level feels super distinct and always challenges you in new ways, and some just look amazing-New interactivity with NPCs and world map is minor but helps make the game feel more grand-Nice ways to customize your difficulty and character using handicaps or potion buffs-Sprite work during story conversations are more expressive, and general dialogue is more enjoyableCons:-The story did its job but I failed to get too invested in it. This may be due to the character I chose (Lilac seemed to be more integral than Carol). The main antagonist's motivation was more relatable than the OG game's Brevon, but from Carol's perspective she's very one note-Main gameplay critique: your character's volatile moveset and the more intense levels backfire on the game a bit in that it makes the game very hectic. It's very easy to lose your bearings and struggle to find the exit to a level segment for a bit, or miss items like hidden collectibles or life flowers that you'll need to keep yourself alive.-Limited view around your character can make some bosses annoying to keep track of. One boss in particular I found myself waiting until they entered my view because pouncing around the arena looking for them would put me at risk of taking a hit.-This game is surprisingly difficult on Normal, partly for the reasons listed above. I would definitely recommend either playing on the easier mode or allowing yourself whatever buff items you can find on your first playthrough. The lives system is more strict this time as well so you may find yourself replaying some sections fairly often.Overall worth the 7 year wait and I am definitely looking up the soundtrack later.

_childDocuments_.review: It's hard to make a sequel. But even harder to make a sequel that's better than the original. I can confidently say this blows Freedom Planet 1 out of the water. The level design is awesome (only with a few nitpicks on certain levels), the character moveset is awesome (I've only played Lilac at the time of writing this though), the sprite work is beautiful, and the music is amazing. All of it comes together in an amazing 2D platformer package and I loved basically every minute of it. The game is challenging (I played on normal) and definitely took me a couple continues, but it's the fun kind of challenge and not the frustrating kind. The game also offers a easy and hard mode as well as an item system. I wish this game didn't have lives, I wish they'd be gone from gaming as they're a relic of arcades and it's 2024. Fortunately this game is very generous, checkpoints are wisely placed and after every death you can choose to continue on super low health (good for landing the last couple hits on a boss) or respawning at the last check point with normal health. And if you run out of continues you can use the blue gems (coins basically in this game) to get another continue. The items system also helps a lot, it doesn't feel tacked on but I didn't use until the last few levels. I never once felt like the game was blatantly unfair. It also contains a couple water levels and I usually hate water levels but they're done so right in this game. And the sprite work in this game is amazing, it's colorful and bright but not eye bleeding, the high detail pixel art is enough to make the characters expressive and give the game a nice look. it reminds me a lot of Megaman 8. The game also has a dodge mechanic the original didn't have and it feels so nice. This game makes you feel powerful for being good at it, it encourages you to dodge although you don't have to do it. The music in this game is amazing. The plot is fairly predictable, it's engaging and the voice acting is decent. It tends to pick up a bit in the mid game. The characters are likable but some of the side villains are under developed. I would say you don't have to play Freedom Planet 1 to enjoy the game but the plot is a continuation of the Freedom Planet 1 plot, so you may miss some references. Overall highly recommend if you like 2D platformers.

_childDocuments_.review: Back in 2015 the first Freedom Planet was a kind of anti-depression for me at the time. It was colorful, amazing soundtrack, had the pixel graphics I missed a lot and had a great personality to it. Sure, the dialogue oftentimes got a little cringe, but it was an indie game. Fast forward to now and in the sequel they improved upon pretty much everything. The dialogue still tastes the same as the previous game which may throw some people off, but it's cute if you try to embrace it. The graphics are bloody amazing. Some levels have like four levels of background scrolling and it looks incredible in action. There are sooooo many little animations and details. The water even has animations when you interact with it. I know how difficult it is to make pixel art and animating, so the fact they managed to cram so much of it in here is amazing, and with FOUR playable characters that are nothing alike. Even the music, just as the first game, remains catchy as heck. So yeah, definitely get this if 2d games are your thing, the levels are much bigger and more elaborate than the first game's, and overall amount of content and polishing is exactly what you'd want from a proper sequel. No wonder it took seven years. On Normal difficulty the bosses to my pleasant surprise actually get challenging too.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, the game was worth the wait. But did it live up to my personal expectations?Not quite sadly. It's still quite good but there are some issues that sadly soured my experience with the game especially nearing the end and prevented it from being great to me.Well let's start with some of the good:- The story is quite good, the comedic scenes made me laugh sometimes (otherwise atleast grin) but the serious parts were more earned than the first game- The presentation of the game is quite good, the artstyle is unique and really colorful- The game has loads of fun gimmicks that kept each level fresh- The hubworlds were a welcome addition which made the world of Avalice feel more alive- The game has a big cast of main characters and more minor charactersNow for the bad:- I like the new artstyle but it made it really hard to see what was in the foreground and in the background in some levels. Causing me to get stuck, not understand where I could land or even die- I ran into quite some bugs that usually were to my disadvantage (once it helped me beat a boss though) - though with all the patches coming out this should get better with time- The music clearly does not loop, which is very noticeable in some levels- Most of the hubworlds were fun but I wish there were some more things to do- Some parts of the story felt "off" to me (one choice seemed to lessen the impact of the main villain to me)- Some levels were kinda annoying to beat (the puzzle based levels mostly)Back to some great stuff to finish this review:- That title screen is just amazing, when a game opens up like that you know if will be good- The game is very well balanced each boss encounter felt like a threat but not straight up impossible (Playing as Lilac)- 80% of the levels were very fun to play and had loads of very cool features- The game has tons of moments where the WOW factor really was present (elevating it the best 2D platformer game you can find gameplay wise)- I like the episode format, gives more choice and personality to the world- There are loads of nice little references for long time fans, which felt very earned after replaying the first game- There are loads of fun levels making the game really worth the asking price (heck it may even be too cheap for what you are getting)If I would give this game a grade... I would give it around 7.5/10Definitely recommended

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could give some sort of "meh" or "10/20" review. _childDocuments_.review: The levels are all so much fun and enjoyable to get through, there wasn't a single one that I though was bad. The spritework in each of them is gorgeous, every song in every level is so insanely good and the level design is so well made. Seriously, there was one level in particular that was absolutely massive and had quite a lot of puzzles, and it took 28 minutes for me to beat it, and yet it didn't feel like it took that long at all, I was actually surprised when I looked at the timer and saw the time, I was having so much fun I didn't see it pass.The bosses are all so great and enjoyable to fight now, especially with the addition of the guard/dodge in this game. This one move completely erased all of the problems I had with a portion of the bosses from FP1. Now when I get hit by an attack I think "Damn it, I should have dodged that" instead of "There was no possible way I could've avoided that, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥". I also absolutely LOVE how, when you're defeated in a fight, you can use a stock to choose to either go back to the last checkpoint with full health to try the fight again from the start or you can revive yourself immediately with a tiny amount of health and resume the fight. This completely eliminates any kind of possible frustration that there could've been from nearly defeating a boss, but then getting hit at the last second and having to do it all over again, as it allows the player to have control over that and have him choose what would be the best play. I've never seen a game do that before and it's such an incredibly INGENIUS idea. The story is just SO much better than the first one. It's so engaging and interesting, you're just constantly at the edge of your seat wondering what's going to happen next and you just never know. The characters are all so well written and awesome, and the voice acting is so well done.I could go on and on about how ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ fantastic this game, it's seriously a masterpiece, and I'll remember it as one of the best I have ever played.HIGHLY recommend anyone to check this game out, it's an unforgettable experience.

_childDocuments_.review: This is probably the singular best sequel to a game in terms of sheer execution of the ambition and improvements. Considering FP1 was originally a Sonic fan game, and then comparing it to FP2, it's a straight 5:1 improvement on a galactic scale. Everything is leaps and bounds better: story, pacing, character gameplay, level design, enemies, graphics, art diversity, world expansion, and voice acting. There is no singular element that wasn't massively overhauled to improvement while fitting with their new designs.Gameplay:All characters--sans Lilac, I think--got overhauls to their gameplay kit to make them unique, but also much more fun and capable to play. Each character has various methods of attacking, and they all have different mobility options.While Lilac plays largely the same, she gained the Guard function like all of the characters, but hers comes with a character-specific dash attached to it.Carol got a *massive* gameplay improvement overall, primarily to her motorcycle functionality. She is also wildly faster than the first game, so she no longer feels miserable to play off of her bike. I actually played most of the game off of it, and didn't practice with it, and I never felt like she was 'slow' because of. I enjoyed her playthrough a lot.There's a big emphasis on speedrunning this game, as well as multiple difficulties, and further ways to challenge yourself or make it easier. If you are not into this game's difficulty, you can set it to easy and use items and potions to make it even more accessible. You will NOT miss any story if you decide to do this; nothing is locked behind Hard Mode, etc.Milla has also received gameplay improvements, though I didn't play her in the first game. She has a shield, multiple ranged options, a float, but is relatively slow on the baseline mobility. This isn't actually an issue, and she is actually capable of beating stage times faster than Lilac when you use the various techniques available in her kit to maintain speed. I'm not finished with her playthrough, yet.Neera is the new character, and her gameplay was actually quite enjoyable. She has the simplest method of acceleration, and an incredible horizontal mobility available to her. While her combat kit has more of a 'stand your ground' feel to it, she has some interesting tools that can help her out in situations. Like the other characters, she has variances in her kit that make her better or worse than others, depending on the situation/boss.Story:All cutscenes, and including in-between stage dialogue, are fully voice acted. The voice acting has improved a lot since FP1 for each character returning. There is some incredibly emotional deliveries by several characters, showcasing their range and skill. The story itself is quite expansive, namely building the world, and continuing from the first game with a lot of cohesion. The writing of the dialogue is strong to every character's personality and presentation, and no one feels "dumb" or out of place in how they respond to situations. This is used to be both comical, and serious, at times. Each character has special interactions with other characters in their own playthroughs, and additional cutscenes the others won't see. For example, Lilac has more/special interactions with Merga, while Carol has additional ones with Corazon. Due to some timing of how missions play out in the sequence in each story, characters will have perspectives from different cutscenes in different places, even. They really put a lot of effort into fleshing this out, and it shows. As for the totality of the story, it's not bad. Some might find it generic, but it's very polished otherwise.The addition of Neera was a surprise, but welcome design. She is actually a great character, and I think they did a fantastic job with her inclusion.Level Design:Some of the new levels are fantastic, both visually, and gameplay-wise. Some kind of drag, and how you feel about that will be subjective. I don't enjoy Shade Armory or Ancestral Forge that much, but Lunar Cannon is an absolute visual masterpiece and experience, and Weapons Core is incredibly sad in relation to the story. No level was absolutely painful to play, and due to the differences in the characters, they will each have varying levels of difficulty/ease in each one. I like this differentiation between the characters' kits actually making them unique to play.Art:You can just look at a screenshot comparison if you want to see how big a contrast is. FP2 has solidified new designs for every character, and they are fantastically detailed, with the sprite work going so far as conveying their emotions in tandem with the voice acting super well. The levels are pretty, and distinct, and the game never feels like it has a visual clutter to it. The bosses are also sporting fantastic designs, along with the visual effects. Truly one of my all-time favorite sprite-centric games.Music:This soundtrack is amaz~zing. Absolute bangers on it. Even the opening menu is fantastic, though I think Lightning Tower or the final two boss tracks might be my favorites. Seriously, give it a listen.FINAL WORD:If you are into action-platformers or any kind, I cannot recommend this game enough. Recommending FP1 is... hard, though the story is extremely relevant to this game. Whether you want to get the first is up to you, but I absolutely think this is worth a play. It spent a long time in development, but what we got is a masterpiece of a sequel through and through.I'm curious about the inspirations to this game, as Lilac plays most like Sparkster from Rocket Knight Adventures (2), though each character sort of functions like they have a similar charge system for their strongest abilities. Sometimes I also feel like Gunstar Heroes was an inspiration. And, of course, Sonic was the original inspiration.

_childDocuments_.review: Freedom Planet was one of those games I shaped a lot of my interests around, and it heavily influenced what circles I've come to hang around with to this day. However, I slowly fell off of the series over time, since I began to kinda see the cracks in the game. When FP2's release date was confirmed, I can't really say I was excited, but I did want to see how it came along. When it finally came out, I bought it, but to me, it felt like it was more out of obligation. Eventually I played it, and, well...My philosophy is that if you go in with no expectations, even the mediocre games are enjoyable. Despite having no expectations, FP2 was the biggest surprise hit of the year for me. So far, I've only cleared Lilac's story, but I went for all the Time Capsules too, and it's been a really fun ride.Here's what I'd consider the biggest pros:- Selectable story arcs. I like how you can not only set your own path through the story, but play with the difficulty in a way that still keeps every story beat intact.- The original game's levels felt like they dragged on a lot. However, this one's levels lean a bit more into the speed-based gameplay, likely a result of Christian Whitehead's assistance on programming and level design. A typical level in this can take 6 minutes to complete, which works perfectly for stages that combine a Sonic stage's two acts into one.- The voice acting is very much improved. In FP1, a good amount of the VAs were relatively new to the scene, or had come from the Internet. Dawn M. Bennett was a particular example, having no experience prior. However, in FP2, a lot more professional VAs were cast, and the VAs from the original game have hit the big time, having gotten a lot of training and more roles under their belt.- The story feels a bit more... direct now? The first game's story had a number of things that just felt unnecessary, and didn't do much other than show characters' personalities. This one still gives them plenty of character, but shows it more in how they react to situations in the story, and there's less that could be considered unnecessary. Even the Battlesphere episode, which seems a bit disconnected at first, turns out to be important to the story as it introduces Captain Kalaw.- All the characters feel far better to play as. Carol's Jump Disc is a brilliant way to give her a new ability on the level of Lilac's boost, Milla's combat has been heavily reworked while still keeping her primary gimmick, and Neera is great for the players who want to focus more on combat. Lilac has been changed the least, but the boost cancel ability is incredibly satisfying to pull off against a boss.- The items are fun to mess with, allowing you to create your own gameplay experience. While I haven't played around with them much, there's a lot of potential combinations I've seen.- Unlocking the extra final stage involves just playing through a set of short levels that play like the normal game. While things like Sonic's Special Stages can be a fun change of pace, they can sometimes be infuriating if you're not good at them. This method ensures that as long as you can play the main game well enough, you can unlock the extra final stage.- I enjoyed the extra final stage's aesthetic. That's all I'll say because of spoilers.While the game is fun, there are also some other things I want to point out. While they aren't necessarily bad, some may see them as such.- Some bosses, particularly in the late game, have too much HP, and can be hard for those who want to just play something Sonic-like.- The ranking system relies entirely on the crystal bonus percentage you get at the end of a stage. If you want to get a high rank, you need to use items to get a high bonus, instead of just going for a high crystal score.- The storyline feels like a lot was taken from Sonic Adventure 2. While this necessarily isn't a bad thing, it still comes across as somewhat unoriginal.- In a later level, a boss enemy appears as a normal enemy. However, its HP remains the same. If I were designing a game like this, I'd reduce the HP quite a bit. That's what makes it work in games like Space Invaders Infinity Gene: bosses appearing as normal enemies have less HP so that shooting them down makes you feel strong.- It can be easy to not realize the Time Capsules exist on your first run. I definitely wasn't aware myself. I'd probably add a post-credits scene showing the museum in Parusa where you can find the only non-Battlesphere one.- The museum side quest is fun, but it can be hard to get all the cores you need to complete the exhibits.- The game ends on a bit of a cliffhanger, and we don't know if it's going to be resolved or not. This is kind of unfortunate, especially after seven years of development.- One of my friends mentioned this, but I don't see it as much of an issue: the game's visual identity was made to set it apart from Sonic, but the levels and story still feel very Sonic-esque.All in all, I firmly believe the positives outweigh the negatives. No matter what, no matter how hard a boss was or how much trouble an enemy gave me, I kept going because it was an enjoyable time, far better than I thought it would be. Seven years of development may have killed my interest originally, but it's clear that instead of sitting and doing nothing the whole time, Sabrina spent a lot of time making the game fun and enjoyable.

_childDocuments_.review: The original 'Freedom Planet' was always going to be a hard act to follow, but 'Freedom Planet 2' somehow manages it. The controls are tight, with an interesting and diverse move-set for each of the four playable characters. Thoughtful level design makes for a varied gameplay experience that never loses its lustre - and with the sheer size of this game, that is quite an achievement. The difficulty curve is a little smoother this time around, simply owing to that increased scope - later levels present a suitable challenge. At two junctions, the player is provided with multiple branching pathways to choose between, determining which levels they will tackle next. While all paths must be explored in time, this does help provide a visible structure to the game; meanwhile, the inclusion of an arena area with a wide selection of challenges ensures that the player is not bound to a single path of progression for most of the game's runtime. While many of the game's (over thirty!) boss encounters refuse to pull their punches, I never found myself stuck on any one boss for too long - echoing the first game, they remain a real highlight of 'Freedom Planet 2', providing a number of jaw-dropping moments of paired spectacle and peril.The story has the same cosy nineties Saturday morning kids' TV vibe that the first game nailed, complete with the shockingly dark elements that characterised many examples of that genre. The hub areas are a sensible choice to help dispense with the long cut-scenes of the first game - here, players can more easily choose how much of the story they engage with. Some of these hub areas feel underutilised - while some offer secrets and mini-games, others are little more than vehicles for dialogue. The voice acting is, on the whole, enjoyable to listen to - it is clear that the cast are having a lot of fun with their roles. The dialogue is somewhat uneven, occasionally lapsing into clunky pop-culture references that suggest a lack of confidence in the franchise's own charms - at its best, however, it by turns warmly humorous, engagingly dramatic, and genuinely affecting. It is a pity that the tension only really starts to build towards the end of the first half of the game - the story might have benefited from a few more early hooks.This is a beautiful game - it is often tempting to pause just to admire the backdrop of a stage, or to appreciate the fluidity of characters' idle animations. While all character sprites receive a greater level of detail this time around, some have changed significantly - Lilac in particular has received a notable makeover, and while others have debated the relative merits of her old and new sprites, I did not find that such changes distracted from gameplay. Perhaps the most impressive graphical assets belong to the game's bosses, each of which is intricately created out of sets of moving parts that are fittingly displayed in a gallery in one of the hub areas. Sound design greatly enhances the game's aesthetic pleasures - well-chosen crashes, splashes, buzzes and booms help make each level feel more concrete. The soundtrack is huge and wide-ranging, although its forays between disparate musical genres never lose it its coherence. You'll encounter several remixes of tracks from the first game, each of which manages to innovate and build upon its parent track; meanwhile, there is a lot to like among the wholly new musical content - I look forward to listening to the soundtrack a decent amount in the coming weeks.Overall, 'Freedom Planet 2' stands as an impressive achievement, a sequel that outshines its rightly celebrated predecessor. While occasionally frustrating, it is perpetually enjoyable, with strong replay value and deft game design that leaves it practically unmatched among high-speed platformers.

_childDocuments_.review: So i picked this game up a few days ago and well now i got 27 hrs in it.but for a more detailed review-(at the time of the review, I only have completed lilac's story, plan to do the others soon)First up, negatives. Weird start but its short so who cares-The only true thing that id say could use a look outside of the odd glitch or two is specifically the world map. Now I like the idea of the map, making the world flow better and giving you a break in between stages and cutscenes. However later on, once I want to practice stages to get better the walking can get tedious. A quick solution would be a fast travel option through the details menu, where you could select a stage to automatically start.Now onto the things that I dont exactly feel strongly about:Story- all the subtlety of a sledgehammer, but honestly, Im no writer so I feel a  bit unqualified to give a detailed critique hereMusic- Now part of this is the hype I had going into the game and honestly, I think the music will grow on me over time. But as of writing, I feel the first game had a slight edge in the soundtrack departmentAnd now the positives-Level Design- Holy mother of something this is good level design. Each level sticks out in a way, and none of the level mechanics are quite what I'd call "gimmicks" as they are fleshed out enough within the level to make it feel right. As well, the level design quite encourages exploration, which is always fun in these 2d games that give you great movement options. The amount of goodies scattered around is insane and I love searching each nook and cranny of a level and getting rewarded for it.Physics- Now most of the time its not worth mentioning, but since the game focuses on speed, it is worth mentioning that the momentum feels great, but still feels very controllable. As well, gaining speed is easy to do, but keeping top speed is difficult, and the physics play into this with how everything just feels. Just feels right, yknow?Combat- Now the first game has some issues with combat imo, with some enemies just feeling far too bulky, especially in the endgame. It didnt help that bosses did not have health bars so it was totally up to you to track it. Now with healthbars for bosses and enemies feeling less tanky (or your attacks dealing more, idk it has the same effect in the end), combat feels satisfying enough to learn and try to get better at, especially since bosses are almost always vulnerable to attacks meaning you can really shred them if you know how to. And finally some attacks have utility during platforming which always helps things feel cohesive.NPC dialogue- the game made me spit out my drink laughing. Don't know if that means my humor is just bad or if the dialogue is good but I frankly do not care. Art-Every single sprite is super detailed and looks great. Special shoutouts to the bosses being made of multiple stitched together parts by how it looks, letting the bosses feel alive, and letting them do expressive movements with them.If you liked the first game, you will probably like the second game is all I have to finish this review

_childDocuments_.review: The tagline surrounding FP2 is "There has never been a game like Freedom Planet 2." And that's true, though not for lack of trying! I get the impression a lot of Saturn and PS1 games were trying to have this kinda of impact, to be this sense of scale, but lacked the technology. Even the original FP1 lacks the experience that pulled off as complete a package as this game manages.If you have a nostalgia or even a retro-fascination for the cool-factor stylings of Gunstar Heroes or Astal or even something more world-building focused like Klonoa or Symphony of the Night, Freedom Planet 2 puts the vibes of the era together in ways I've never seen before: Fun, fast-paced gameplay with extremely interesting gimmicks and environments, all wrapped up in a fun story that actually manages to feel poignant and inspiring in a way so few games manage.Bosses take a bit of time to learn and 2 doesn't pull its punches - especially where the achievements are concerned - but that only helps take me back to an era that games seem to think they evolved out of, when really they just shifted away from something fun to something else equally fun. Beautiful ost and passionate creatives behind every pixelated corner, I wholeheartedly recommend anyone who's been wondering where all the good 5th Generation nostalgia games have been give FP2 a go.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll make this short and sweet (aka tl;dr). If you like Freedom Planet 1, this gives you ALOT more to do. This game is an obvious pick up. That is just to get people caught up so that they don't have to play the first one, if they don't want to. I HIGHLY SUGGEST YOU PLAY THE FIRST ONE FOR THE SOUNDTRACK HOWEVER. PLEASE PLAY FREEDOM PLANET 1. HOLY DOG, THAT GAME SLAPS.If you don't want to play Freedom Planet 1, then the plot of Freedom Planet 1 is that This game plays like a combo of Shantae and Sonic. If you are a fan of those games, you'll love this game. Speedy platforming with large levels, player has a health bar and enemies that don't get taken down in a single hit.
