_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed the original Freedom Planet, so it's a shame to say I didn't particularly enjoy the sequel. While it's a decent enough platformer in its own right, it's a whole host of little things that come together to make the game an absolute slog to get through.Firstly, the game is long. I mean long! One playthrough of the game with one character, not going out of my way to find all the secrets and so forth, took 12 hours. There are FOUR playable characters. By comparison, for Sonic Mania I've done a complete playthrough with every character (Sonic, Tails, Knuckles, and Sonic with Ray and Mighty) 100% all collectables and achievements and that's taken just under 20 hours total.This wouldn't be such an issue if the game did anything truly interesting, but it doesn't. If you're a fan of platforming games - particularly Sonic - everything the game throws at you, you've seen before. That in and of itself isn't a bad thing, but the levels are way too long. The average level takes about 10min to complete. They would have benefited a great deal from being shorter and snappier. I also felt that I could never quite see enough of the stage area at any one time. If an off-screen enemy is able to shoot at you that's not good game design IMO. Worse still is that some of these are total filler. One in particular sees you having to collect several keys in order to rise a bridge to get to another area. If this level had been left out it would have made absolutely no difference. There are several levels like this.The enemies are all very spongy, even the most basic needing at least two hits, which is not great for a fast paced game like this. The further on you go the more spongy they become. And the bosses are absolutely ridiculous! Some fights end up being more like a bullet hell game and, again, they are spongy as a soaked matrass! The final boss has six phases - count 'em - SIX! It's ludicrous! Add to this that several bosses you have to fight more than once and it truly becomes a chore.While the story of the first game had a kind of cheesy Saturday-morning-cartoon charm, here it is dragged out so long that it just becomes boring and tedious. I almost never skip cutscenes in games, story is one of the things I really enjoy, but it didn't take long for me to start skipping them here. It's just not interesting.There are items in the game to buy and use, but I found myself basically ignoring them. Partly because they didn't seem to make any discernible difference to the gameplay, but also because the game is so restrictive over what you can use it's just not worth the bother."Tedious" is probably the best word I can use to describe Freedom Planet 2. It's like the devs took every single idea they had and crammed it into the game, resulting in a bloated, tiresome mess. If they had reeled things back a bit, ditched the extraneous levels and boss encounters and generally tightened things up this could have been so much better.Apart from the four playable characters and the items mentioned above, there are also heaps of collectables and a "Classic Mode" to entice you back to replay the game. However, after the absolute slog of getting through just ONE character's story, I can't see myself returning to this at all.

_childDocuments_.review: I remember when I first played the original Freedom Planet way back in late 2015. I was bored one day on the weekend after school, and decided to give it a try. I was absolutely blown away, and loved every aspect of it! Even after dozens of game overs, I beat the entire game in one day! Something I can only do for very few games. Somehow, Freedom Planet spoke to me in a way that no other game at the time did. But things were about to get even more exciting! very soon after beating it, something big dropped on Youtube. The trailer for this very game: Freedom Planet 2!This was the most excited I had ever been for an upcoming release EVER! Years passed, I grew up, went through phases, started jobs, ended jobs, survived a dreadful pandemic, started questioning my gender, but through that entire time, I never forgot about Freedom Planet 2.  Eventually, in September of 2022, it finally released, and I was HYPED! I bought it ASAP, on itch.io for ten extra dollars! But you know how hype works. It gives us impossibly high standards, and inevitably leads to disappointment......At least for games that aren't Freedom Planet 2! Seriously! This is easily the shining example of how to do a sequel right! Every aspect about Freedom Planet 1 has been improved! The music, for instance, is much more diverse! I'll admit that it needed time to grow on me, but this is one absolutely phenomenal OST! Leilani Wilson (AKA 'Woofle') did an amazing job here, and you should check out her Bandcamp albums, and her Novel series 'Elancia Chronicles' (The protagonist from that series also has a fun little cameo appearance in FP2)The voice acting here is also incredible! FP1 had some great acting that brought the cast of characters to life brilliantly, but this sequel saw a BIG improvement to the quality! Being recorded at Christopher Sabat's  (Voice of Kazuma Kuwabara from Yu Yu Hakusho, Vegeta from Dragonball, and probably a whole host of other anime tough-guys) Studio, the voice work is a whole lot more professional. Every line is delivered so perfectly, which is elevated by the more complex, mature story! The first game had the classic story of a rag-tag band of heroes uniting the nations to repel an evil alien warlord. Simple, but it's delivery was very ambitious and passionate! You can really see how much GalaxyTrail have grown since then, as Freedom Planet 2's story is much more mature and well realized! The antagonist of the game: Merga is a much more complex, and tragic character than Lord Brevon. The game has a much better balance between dramatic and light-hearted moments, a more fleshed-out cast of characters, more mature themes, and loads of lore delivered through the game's several hub-worlds. The art of FP2 is also simply magnificent! The resolution is very high for an indie pixel-art platformer, and they used this extra screen size to incredible effect, having vastly more detailed sprites than it's predecessor, while also being super expressive, fluid, and easily readable in the heat of the action! Big shout out to Tyson Tan who volunteered an incredible amount of work to give this game it's beautiful art-style!And now the gameplay: Yeah, it's also a massive improvement! Every playable character has a much more balanced, and powerful arsenal of abilities, while all still having their own strengths and weaknesses. Milla and Carol especially have seen a drastic improvement to their move-sets! Carol now has a proper ranged attack, which doubles as a great & super satisfying movement option, while Milla's Phantom cubes are now spawned instantly, and she's also picked up some new Kung-Fu tricks! The newcomer to the game's playable cast: Neera Li is also an excellent addition, sacrificing easy movement abilities for rawr strength, and a wide variety of ways to bust your enemies up good! The levels have also seen an astonishing improvement in Quality, Quantity and Diversity! From the journey through Dragon valley, to the daring raid on Airship Sigwada, to the visceral carnage of Zulon Jungle & Naolo Lake, and the dark, ominous depths of Ancestral Forge. There is something here for everybody!My favourite addition to the game is it's Hub worlds. Each one is packed full of so many unique, and colourful characters, who all have so much personality, and really bring the world of Avalice alive! Some of the game's best humour and lore comes from these NPCs! In conclusion, Freedom Planet 2 is an absolutely incredible hidden gem of a game that gets nowhere near as much discussion as it should, and you should definetely not miss it! I'm just as in love with this game that I'm playing as a proud 24 year-old lady as I was with the first game as an awkward 16 year old boy. This has to be one of the most ambitious, and beautifully executed games I have ever seen! No wonder it's among my all-time favourites. And I certainly don't expect any other games to surpass it any time soon (Unless GalaxyTrail blesses us with another sequel, that is...). Thank you Sabrina DiDuro, and your incredibly talented team for bringing this incredible game to life! Your games have made a huge impact on my life, and spoken to me in a special way that no other has! (By the way, Sabrina is now a V-tuber named 'Spacey Batotelli'. Be sure to drop in to her streams and say Hi). TL:DRFreedom Planet 2 surpasses the first game in just about every aspect. It has loads of incredible content, and is sincerely one of the best platformers ever made! You can feel the development team's love and passion all throughout this game! Buy it! Play it! Love it! Now!

_childDocuments_.review: Prologue  When Freedom Planet 1 came out in 2014, it quickly became my Game of the Year, and in 2015, a sequel was announced, but I never expected for it to come out seven ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ years later, after I had accumulated over 57 hours of playtime in the first title at the time of this writing, now, seven years is a long time, but was the wait worth it? Spoilers, it was, just look at my playtime for FP2, but now I'll tell you why this sequel works so well.Graphics  No joke, this is the best-looking 2D indie game I've ever seen. FP2 genuinely reminded me of Castlevania Symphony of the Night when it came to background detail and sheer amount of animation frames for anything, from the main characters to enemies and citizens you can talk to, every single level looks drop-dead gorgeous and even the most non-important NPC looks great and have way more frames of animation than they needed, but the artists went above and beyond anyway.  The first game already had a solid presentation, but the sequel improves on it even further, there are even some 3D models this time around, which made the SOTN parallels stronger, and just like in that game, they don't look out of place because they were used for things that would've been difficult if not outright impossible to pull off in traditional 2D, and if they could, wouldn't have nearly as much impact.  FP1 already looked like a Saturn game, but FP2 looks even more like one with the combination of richly-detailed 2D sprites and backgrounds with 3D models. However, my one and only complaint about the visuals would be the completely static water in Paradise Prime, considering how perfect this game looks, a small lake that doesn't animate in any way sticks out like a sore thumb.Sound  Woofle returns as this game's composer, and just like with the first game, she absolutely nailed the soundtrack, with catchier songs and now there are way more of them, you know it's going to be good when even the songs that play in the World Map are absolute bangers. I'm not a musician, so I have no way of describing what makes this soundtrack so good, you just have to take my word for it.  The sound effects are just as good, if not even better than in the first title, no complaints there, they're still very distinct and I would never mistake where they came from if I heard them outside of this game.Story  Now here's a surprise, the story in Freedom Planet 1 was a very contentious topic and I have good news for everyone, the second game has improved the narrative quite a bit, with dark themes but without any overly indulgent scenes like the infamous electrical torture scene in FP1.  It shows restraint, and I really like how playing as different characters led to different dialogue in some cutscenes, the first game already had that, but with the much lengthier campaign and more exclusive scenes, it makes playing as all four characters more worth it this time around.  The voice acting has also recieved a noticeable improvement, dialogue was recorded in a professional studio so no longer there are differences in audio quality, returning actors improved their performances even more compared to the first title and the new actors have very solid delivery.The only mixed bag for me about the story would be the villain, while her motivations are much more understandable compared to Brevon in FP1, in my opinion she is nowhere near as charismatic, Brevon was a bastard but he was OUR bastard, while Merga didn't really win me over. Towards the end of the game she also makes a questionable decision, especially considering her culture, but I won't go into spoilers.Gameplay  The high-speed action platformer formula returns in this sequel, with even more improvements, some subtle, others not so much. Starting with the obvious enhancements, characters control and feel even more responsive, the screen sometimes zooms out to give you a better field of view (and you can adjust it in the options menu!), a world map has been implemented, hub levels are a thing and now there is a dodge button, which gives you invincibility frames when you press it.  Not gonna lie, when I started playing this game, I almost never used the dodge, but as the levels became more intense and more stray projectiles started flying over the screen, I was constantly pressing that button, and the same thing happened with the bosses.  Level design became bigger and bolder, and for the most part, it works wonderfully, I can safely say that 95% of the levels in this game are a blast to play, and even the worst stages in the game are nowhere near as painful as, say, the worst levels in the Mega Man X series, if you're familiar with those. If not, then rest assured, you ain't gonna die a million times and spend an ungodly amount of time trying to get past them. Rule of thumb is, if the level you're in ain't called Inversion Dynamo, you're good. The other weak levels are just jank.  If 95% doesn't sound like a good enough percentage for you, let me put this into perspective: It took me over 10 (probably closer to 20) playthroughs for me to achieve my current playtime in Freedom Planet 1. In Freedom Planet 2, I got 49 hours on it (at the time of this writing, of course) after only four. This is a MUCH longer game, with a lot more content waiting to be seen by the player. Granted, I played on Adventure Mode, which has cutscenes, but even then, there are way more levels in this game and some of them can be very long - I don't have a problem with long levels as long as they're interesting and checkpoints are well-placed, and the long bois in Freedom Planet 2 pass that test with flying colours.  Aside from the regular levels, Freedom Planet 2 also added Hub levels, which have no enemies and it's just you, vibing and talking to NPCs (there are a LOT of them, too), and ocasionally, playing a minigame or just admiring the scenery.  No longer used just for extra lives, crystals can also be exchanged for gold gems, which are used to buy various items, many of which helpful in nature, such as giving you a Damage Over Time effect when you hit an enemy (particularly helpful for bosses) or giving you an extra life petal, while others increase the game's difficulty in various ways and give you access to higher rankings (without those items, the best rank you can get in a level is A).  The biggest addition in terms of side content, however, is the Battlesphere, which might sound familiar to anyone that played the Ratchet & Clank games, it's an arena with various challenges, boss rematches and a baseball minigame, and as the game goes on, more of those first two unlock, and in fact, beating all challenges is mandatory to obtain the best ending, but it's not the most difficult "good ending" to get I've seen in a game.  Speaking of difficulty, Freedom Planet 1 was a challenging game, and while the sequel might be easier in some aspects, it can be more difficult in others, such as boss fights, in my opinion some of these tough boys 'n gals can be harder than even the last boss of the first game, but at the same time, these fights are QUICK, if they last over two minutes, either the boss has a big health bar or something's going horribly wrong. You die fast, but so do your enemies, and that's exactly the kind of boss fight I prefer in games.Conclusion  I spent two hours writing this review just to try to convince more people to buy Freedom Planet 2, especially that coward Woolie, and the only way I have of finishing up here is, just try it - There's a demo and if you want to see more of the game, within the 2-hour refund period you can get a good glimpse of what it has to offer, especially if you skip cutscenes. Freedom Planet 1 is no longer my favourite indie game of all time because its sequel is now finally out.Can't wait to play Freedom Planet 3 in 2035!

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who not only enjoyed the first Freedom Planet game, but also gave it a  and considered it one of the BEST 2D Platforming games EVER, I was "beyond hyped" going into Freedom Planet 2 and had such high expectations for this sequel to be as good (if not BETTER) than the first game, but unfortunately, it truly saddens me to say that this sequel, in my opinion, is  compared to the first game in almost every way possible. The following points lists my main issues with this sequel: This is especially true for  who had such a GREAT design in first Freedom Planet (she truly looked like a character from the "Sonic the Hedgehog" universe), but in this sequel her re-design looks  and uninspiring whatsoever. What's worse is that another character,  who was my FAVORITE character in the first game both for his design and his "Shadow the Hedgehog-like" edgy personality, was COMPLETELY RUINED in this sequel with an AWFUL new re-design AND attitude that made him SO BORING that I lost all the love I had for him from the first game (I'm truly baffled by the developer's decision to change/ruin the cool personality that Spade had in the first game rather than building upon it). Much like the 1st point, the graphical look of this game as a whole is not as good as the original game which had WAY BETTER-LOOKING stages/backgrounds than this game. As a result, the stages looked (and felt) bland and weren't as memorable to me as the stages from the first game (the "16-bit" look of the first game was magnificent IMO). With maybe 2-3 music exceptions, the zones music in this game as a whole weren't memorable at all and most of them were "all over the place" in terms of how they play and none of them felt "catchy" at all. In fact, some of the remixes (e.g. Dragon Valley) were COMPLETELY RUINED in this game and nowhere near as good as they were in the first game. THIS point right here is, by far, the  part of this game for me personally. You see, I'm someone who always looks forward to boss battles not just for the fight itself but also the BOSS MUSIC that makes those moments so INTENSE/EPIC/MEMORABLE. And so, whereas the first Freedom Planet game which had EPIC boss music that  were  and gave you a sense of  as they play ("Prince Dail's" boss theme from the first game was in my "Top 15 all time favorite boss themes" too), the majority of the boss themes in Freedom Planet 2 however sounded  that you would expect in a boss battle and sounded more like "regular zone themes" than anything else. I am still beyond shocked at how the developer "okay-ed" these GARBAGE boss themes/remixes that were absolutely NOTHING in comparison to the AWESOME boss themes from the first game. (My rating for the boss themes alone in this sequel is , sorry to say) While having longer stages (compared to the 1st game) may sound like a good thing at first, the stages in this sequel are SO LONG that it feels  especially if you want to achieve a better stage completion rating or find hidden chests that you missed. It's even worse that there isn't an "in-stage map" and thus trying to find hidden chests in stages that take  to complete is just HORRENDOUS and very de-motivating to do honestly. While I never got a "Game Over" in this game, the fact that the lives counter RESITS every stage to "2 lives" and does NOT accumulate like in the first game felt like an unnecessary  to the player and many times I felt  so that I don't get a Game Over. I really think this was a BAD DECISION on the developer's side and feel that this should have been kept as a "Hard difficulty-only" feature (I played on "Normal" difficulty for the record). Additionally, I did NOT use those "helping items" that you can equip before entering a stage because it felt like a "cheap" way to make the level easier and I didn't want to feel "forced" to use them just because of this "always 2 lives starting" system. (And no, I never used that "instant revive" option when you die because that too felt like a "cheap" way to finish a level and so I always preferred to restart from the "last checkpoint" instead) Unlike the first game (which DIRECTLY took you to where you are supposed to go next), the so called "Hub" zones in this game felt like a CHORE to explore to progress the story. I didn't care about the characters there who provided USELESS text and the shops in there were also useless because I had no intention of using any of those items in-stage. There were many instances where I honestly did NOT know where to go next in order to progress the story. For example, after beating "Merga" the first time, not only did that battle end very awkwardly (i.e. without any subsequent cutscene to explain post-battle events), but also the game did NOT tell me where I'm supposed to go to next and there wasn't even an "!" mark to highlight the place where I was supposed to go to next. Needless to say, I much prefer the "directly taken to the next area" approach the first game had than this game's "hub approach" IMO. Many times I ended-up taking unnecessary damage (especially against bosses) because the "regular guard" and "dash" buttons were merged, which led to many instances where my character "dashed into an enemy/projectile" even though I did NOT intend for them to perform a "dash" command. The solution to this is to simply  through a future patch and that should significantly help in reducing unintended character inputs. Initially, when I saw the animated short video for this sequel when it was announced, I had high hopes for the main villain of this game, but sadly I was so underwhelmed by the main villain who was very uninspiring, all talk and nowhere near as VICIOUS/MENACING as the AWESOME  from the first game. I couldn't take the main villain seriously and was bored every time she appeared throughout this game (even the final boss battle was "meh" at best IMO). A  that was a blast to play and had awesome character designs/personalities, story, stages, visuals and ESPECIALLY boss battles/music, all of which should've been preserved going into the sequel. A  that opted to "try something new" rather than build upon the strengths it had established from its predecessor and thus resulting in a sequel that fell short in almost all comparable areas and was nowhere near as memorable (or worth re-playing) as the first game in the franchise.P.S: When the development for the inevitable  begins, I hope the developer goes back to their roots and takes inspiration from the  in making the next entry in franchise and focuses on what made the 1st Freedom Planet game so awesome while developing the next game, in particular the  that made the boss fights in the first game (especially the  so epic/memorable.

_childDocuments_.review: Freedom Planet 1 was really good, so I don't understand what happened with Freedom Planet 2. I like the pixel art, character design and overall presentation. The music is pretty good too. Unfortunately that's where my praise ends. There's no way to play the levels without being forced into story mode. The level design is rather long and boring. The story and NPC's really don't add any weight to the story. It reads like a sonic satam fan fiction and there's nothing wrong with that in itself but the tone is too inconsistent that I don't really buy it. Boss battles are very annoying, with very odd hit boxes and way too much HP, even on beginner mode. It honestly feels like a game that doesn't know what it wants to be, inspired by both MegaMan X4+ and Sonic. I really wanted to like this game, but the entire thing just felt like a chore to play.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game on launch out of excitement, which it had a rocky start which didn't help it, but once I was able to play the game, I stopped part way through only to come back to try and see what it was that made me stop, after going through the game I have multiple problems about this game which actually made me angry.This game is a great example take one step forward and two steps back.The art style is fantastic, Tysontan did a wonderful job with the designs and aesthetic, the problem comes in when the designs are put in motion they can feel really awkward at times, which if they're even given motion in some cases, making them feel too rigid in some scenes, not only that, there are multiple graphical problems that occurred from some things moving too slowly, and the absolute abundance of paper doll bosses that were used.The gameplay was really smooth and worked well, even adding some depth to the formula that was there, the issue was that the stages were not very well thought out and didn't have any flow to them what do ever, which lead to enemies being placed in blind spots and not enough visual range while playing, this lead to even some environmental blind spots while moving at high speeds, not to mention some of the enemies felt either forced or they were placed in a spot a speed traps to hit the player, which leads me to bosses being absolute damage sponges and have either literally no attacks that were a threat or being so loaded with attacks with barely any attack patterns to speak of working randomly with the intent to just pummel the player into the ground, this notion isn't made any better with the fact of the inclusion of augments to make you stronger, as well giving a retry that puts you at a check point which also includes boss fight phases that costs some crystals that can be earned from this punching bag, which implies they knew people were going to have problems.The sound design and music is great, at first, as time goes on some of the sounds start to layer in weird, the voice acting volume is way too high for default and some of the mixing feels weird, not only that, while I do like the music in this game, the later stages music did not reflect that I heard in the beginning leaving a quality gap between them.The last thing that was the last nail in the coffin for me was the story which was so horrible back loaded and ham fisted it felt completely out of place and could've used far better execution entirely to get the point across, which it ended up feeling completely preachy.While I understand game creation is not an easy task I wonder what actually went on during the duration of development, as this game feels heavily front loaded, and that it needed a year or two more time to thoroughly cook, I did not enjoy this game in the slightest.

_childDocuments_.review: I dont understand what the positive hype is around this game. Its an average one at best. Even though the game looks very good and has an alright story behind it. Its a 2D high speed platformer similar to sonic, but with fighting mechanics added into it. Now this is a really great idea and the boss fights can be fun, but GalaxyTrail messed up on one important thing. The Guard/Parry move. It has this weird delay to it where you have to press it before the projectile or attack hits you, not when its about it hit you. Your character will gain some I-frames and negate the attack entirely. It doesnt really help either when you are being attacked by multiple enemies or projectiles. I dont understand why they dropped the ball on this and they should look at other games on how parry is done right. Guard is useful in some situations but useless in most others. You might as well dodge by jumping over the projectile and not worry about guarding at all.Another issue is the level design. A lot of the level layouts can be confusing and very chaotic. There are also these mini puzzles that can be confusing or difficult to navigate. There were some levels that were done right and those being the ones with very long roads and few enemies in between. None of that jump puzzle BS either.The story is an okay one, but it kind of has a disappointing ending with a cliffhanger and it calls for another sequel to be made.  Is this included in the secret ending?  ♥♥♥♥ that, Im not playing through the whole game again to try and get it. Its been a frustrating experience for me already. Anyways, Freedom Planet 2 is mostly a frustrating experience. With its chaotic level design, cheap boss fights, and a broken guard move that is almost pointless. I wouldnt give this game a full recommendation. Hopefully the next sequel they will learn from their mistakes by making a functional guard move, and overall improve on the level designs and bosses so it can be called a fair challenge.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is good in the gameplay department. So, why the "no"? Well, it is because it crapped the metaphorical bed. Even thought this pushes the limits far above what was in FP1, by the end of this review, I will have either convinced you to never purchase this game or ignore my warnings because they don't matter to you. Sorry in advance for the angry late night ranting in this review that is half delirious. Here are some basic problems:1: The game is too darn long in the levels. Honestly, they should have split every level into two sections for ease of play. This is made worse by lazy level design in some cases. Not only did they reuse certain story moments involving villains from FP2, such as them appearing on the screens to alert their minions late game, but also various other bits. While there is definitely a ton of heart to it, the problem is that the former game also did these reused moments and their mechanics much better.2: The OST. Too many reused tracks, which normally is not a problem because I like listening to remakes of classic tracks in a series as everyone knows how many Sega has reused. However, what crosses the line is that a couple tracks seem plagiarized. The latter of these was an issue that even showed up in the demo way back, and clearly they did not care to fix it.3: Despite the gameplay generally being improved, they messed up by making the new dodge button mandatory. The fact is, the first game had issues because only Lilac was ever worth playing as, mostly because the others were a pain to play as. This was because Lilac was the only character who got enough iFrames out of her moves, specifically her dash attack, while the cat spent too much on their kick and the dog had less health and only that shield. In FP2, they added dodges, which grant you a blink of invulnerability to characters. Why is this bad? Because they also made it 100% necessary to use due to how certain boss fights work. What this means is that you have to dodge, and you have to learn to be good at it, despite it breaking the fun of the momentum in gameplay. If they just toned down some of the more insane boss attacks, then I could have gotten through without it, and honestly I hate this new mechanic as, again, it breaks the fun of the momentum and flow of a highly kinetic platformer game.4: The story....Here are the nitty gritty story sucking problems with as mild spoilers as I can:Okay, so let's talk about the first Freedom Planet game. Why? Because believe me, this is very relevant, and retroactively I must give FP1 a bad review because of what was in FP2.... So, in FP1, there were two characters intended to be playable that were cut; Spade and Torque, of those, Spade has a very important story that was clearly cut in FP1, and I know this because I have played FP2 and there is tons of backstory relevant to the character that would have really been important to him in 2. So, why the cut of this promised character? Well, I personally theorize the main dev of these games suffers from extreme selfhatred, which would not be an issue except that he/she clearly has other related issues often associated with selfhatred and suicide which I will not address here because IRL drama, which normally would not be relevant except it impacts writing and game variety. I wish them well, but honestly they are clearly psychologically unhealthy and I fear them projecting is partially responsible for the bad writing in FP2. In the case of variety, both cut characters from FP1 were male, and in the case of FP2..... ....yeah, there is another case of "lipstick lesbian couple" afoot in this game. It's just bad. It is not simply that it is cliche, but in all honestly, it's a bad cliche when done bad. This type of crap writing is why Dragon Prince season 3 was so bad, although admittedly that case was much worse than this one, until you get to the "relevant history of racism" subplot, because of course this game pulls that dumpster of a plot point out. The fact is, this alone does not make a bad story, but the way it is told is terrible. I enjoyed the way Star Versus the Forces of Evil handled this story concept, even if that cartoon was flawed about it, but FP2 fumbles the ball down the stairs and it hits every step on the way down to the ground floor. Of course, explaining this requires spoiling things, so I won't, but let's just say "and nothing of value was learned and everyone got off scot free because hate crimes from generations ago that nobody in the current day was involved with" sorta bullcrap happens. It's trite hacky writing. "Character X burnt a whole forest down after the kidnap scenario, and yep because some of my ancestors were bad, your war crimes are nothing so you get a couple months of community service". I was the guy calling bullcrap when Orochimaru survived he end of Naruto and did not get blown up for his Doctor Mengele level evil, so seriously don't handwave this stuff with "oh, but they meant well when they did evil, so it does not count"; trust me, when you kidnap people who have no involvement with the situation, it ain't meaning well, and this happened in FP2. You could have skipped this awful story, but the casual mode is unlocked after the game ends.Funny little detail about the "Battlesphere" area of the game. The things you unlock in that arena, at first I thought they were going to be neat accessories like those you find in shops. NOPE. They are the items that unlock the holorecords to the dang backstory involving the lesbian couple. Because, OF COURSE THEY ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ARE! Imagine saying "yeah, work hard for that unlock", only to unlock a heaping pile of crap. At least the turd quest from Breath of the Wild was not trying to pander towards me.This is supposed to be a game about a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ purple dragon speeding around and fighting robots; what the heck is wrong with you people?! Just let it be that, or make the writing not bad cliches of current day writing! I can read preachy writing and not have a problem, even if I disagree with it, if the writing does not suck, case in point all of my favorite RPGs which are filled to the brim with Japanese environmental messages and really oddball treatises on religious views both local and foreign to me; those RPGs actually conveyed these issues well, but FP2's writing is weak and seems only to suit the fetishes of the people who made it. Heck, I have even loved games with LGB characters and couple in them, including Undertale, which was amazing, and the reason that game's lesbian couple is not hated is because it meshes well with the absurd nature of that story, which also included a Tsundere Airplane, but also did not break the flow of the game. Also, just FYI, there are many people who would have not purchased this product if they knew the entire game's story was going to hinge and center around one lesbian couple in it. Like it or not, people have beliefs on that issue, and they also like to make sure their kids don't buy things that have that content either. I will argue that this is not a deception by omission, as the game pretends to be child friendly, but engages in both pandering and terrible story writing that makes it all about people paying for crimes based on their racial ancestry and not whether they were involved in it.

_childDocuments_.review: Version 1.1.8rSanik was advertised like gotta go fast. But when it finally came out people instead got a slow and tedious generic platformer with a lot of dying, slow moving platforms and even going left. No matter what it tries, the franchise still can’t deliver on their promise (if we don’t count the endless runners for smartphones). Even the best sanik games allow to go fast only to the peak sportsmen who memorized the layouts and are younger than mid 20s when the human brain stops developing and starts rotting into alzheimer. The general public has to stumble and fail and go slow across the stupid platforms.Freedom Planet was on the the right path of fixing sanik. The game made the levels almost play themselves on normal difficulties and offered a ton of HP. They still weren’t perfect choose your own roller-coasters, but you could go fast. To add more gameplay to the game it has tough bosses. On the normal difficulty you still can face-roll through all the levels yet be stuck on a boss-fight for an hour. The challenge was pleasant and offered a good contrast. Only a couple of bosses were drawn-out fights of attrition.Having a platformer about meaningful speed is what sanik imagined. But it never achieved it, and the popularity of infinite runners proves that people want that.Hope is the first step on the road to disappointment.People expect sequels to improve upon the game, to keep the good parts and fix the bad parts. Even the Assassin’s Creed‘s sequel somehow became a playable game compared to the first one. I waited 7 years for this game. But rather than improving upon the first game it went far in other direction. It’s not sanik-1-bad but it is very bad. Instead if making the sequel tighter they decided to make it phatter with unnecessary clutter.You were the chosen one! It was said that you would destroy the Sith, not join them! The entire level-design is unnecessary clutter. Instead of doubling down and making levels longer and even more streamlined, it made them into the giant buggy repetitive directionless convoluted slog of sanik labyrinth. There is a ton of dumb platforming and stupid no-brain puzzles. You don’t go fast to the right, you wander around in samey-looking rooms made of the same elements and hit the dumb walls all the time. There is a lot of precise platforming and waiting for the platforms to appear or move nearer.There’s a terrible mandatory scroll-shooter section, and your weapons are garbage while the enemies are giving you bullet hell. And everything is filled with unnecessary clutter, it’s impossible to read the screen behind all those stupid explosions and to see your hitbox in relation to dangerous bullets.When you get to play as a giant robot, instead of being the coolest part of the game like in Enclave or Psychonauts, it’s the worst part of the game. The robot can’t kill anything, the tiny enemies are not even damaged by it. It can’t traverse the level specifically made for it, it doesn’t fit anywhere and you have to get lucky to squeeze it through the narrow ways you are actually supposed to go through. It controls like an absolute arse.But well, all controls in the game are fiddly and unresponsive. Even if you get the result you wanted, you still achieve it not through synergy with the game’s systems, but by unsure suggestions and leeway.The levels are filled to the brim with stupid suckerpunch enemies and traps. Whose idea it was to add scam foes that kite you no matter the speed you are running at? They are always out of your reach but tie their damage output to your position. The game is dispensing unavoidable damage unless you slow down to a crawl. And not only you have to do that to avoid damage but to deal it too. All the enemies instead of dying from one hit are severe damage sponges. Even the first enemy in the game in the tutorial takes several hits on normal. That is if you can even hit it. And unlike sanik you don’t deal damage while jumping. You receive it. All of this is killing the pacing, who thought that adding a ton of combat into sanik can improve it? What is this, Freedom Unleashed?All of the combat is unnecessary clutter. Your boost deals barely any damage and it is hard to aim. It’s more of a traversal power than a combat ability, despite granting invincibility. The spin doesn’t drain the meter anymore but its attack is very weak too, and also it’s hard to hit anything with it. Well it’s hard to hit anything with anything because all the enemies have annoying hitboxes. Yet they all are made of lava and easily deal damage to your giant hitbox without even touching it. The stupid block button (because a sanik game needed a stupid block button) repositions you back into damage. And well stunlocks for 50% damage is a common occurrence.Most of the bosses in the first game were an enjoyable challenge. You can clearly see what you have to do and you are doing it. But this time the bosses are spazzing boring damage-soakers that are often turn the game into a bullet hell. A lot of them outright run away off-screen so you can’t even reach them while they pour death from above. They are plain not fun, starting with the first one, their patterns are primitive and there is no agency. But they have absolute tons of HP and just soak damage for an hour. The final boss is cancer. You have to beat her three times before you get a checkpoint while she fills the screen with unpredictable damage. Good luck fighting a one-armed bandit with ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ controls, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hitboxes, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ jumps and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ combat. The house always wins.And all of that is enveloped with a terrible unnecessary clatter overworld map. Like, okay, you want to allow people to replay the levels and you’ve added asinine grind for money and materials. You’ve added shops selling the collectibles and garbage skills that are mostly useless. But why the absolute hell the navigation on the map is so bad? Why the hell it is multiscreen and with terrible node positions instead of unambiguous orthogonal roads between them? Why it wastes so much time on walking? Why it locks you away from the shops and earlier levels during the mid-game? Why the hell you are offered to chose one of the three levels all the time, if you play all three anyway? If there’s an overworld why lock that choice instead of offering branching paths? If there’s an overworld why is there no character selection screen? Why do you have to create a separate profile and be stuck with your choice? And yes there is no pause button on the map screen it still blasts music on focus loss.The adventures of Lavaboy and Sharkgirl in 3-DThe story is unnecessary clutter. The first game featured teenedgy trash barely comprehensible convoluted story with terrible fandub voice acting. And it all is fitting and the characters are kinda endearing.But this time we have to suffer through barely comprehensible convoluted story with terrible fandub voice acting that thinks it’s Zookeeper’s Schindler visiting John Raabe in Nanking. It’s second-hand embarrassing baby hitler dindunaffin. It’s a boring and self-serious garbage with more holes than a black hole. I wanted to love this game, i went out of my way to purchase it by any means necessary once i saw that it was finally released. But before the 30% completion i realized that this is just mentally draining and embarassing, that i hate it and never want to see it again. And that’s before my life has turned into constant existential dread with me hoping for any game to be at least just a little bit not terrible so it can give me a small respite. I had to force myself to finish it, a level per several days.Unnecessary clutter out of unnecessary clutter.

_childDocuments_.review: Freedom Planet 1 is a game that is near and dear to my heart, so I'm going to be reviewing this primarily as a comparison to the first game. I've played 5 stages with Carol and tested out all the other characters within the tutorial and first level. 👎 The artstyle is very distinct from the first game. I can't really say that I appreciate it after playing the FP1 so much and associating all the characters and whatnot with the old artstyle. It doesn't feel like a natural progression for the series's artstyle in the same way that something like 2D Sonic games have evolved. I do think all of the new assets look great in a vacuum, but the first game's artstyle was so striking that this feels like a downgrade. It doesn't help that the higher pixel count sprites end up making the game blend in with other indie games going for a similar look. I get the impression that whoever made the decision on the new artstyle wanted to distance themselves from the Sonic and Megaman X inspired artstyle of the first game. I feel like it's kind of too late to do that though. 👎 The music is very much a mixed bag. Some of the songs sound really great like the new Dragon Valley remix and Shade Armory. Other songs though are either unmemorable or feel unfinished. The boss themes I heard in particular were quite a disappointment. Even with the songs that I like though they don't really have the same appeal as the FP1 OST. They end up feeling overly busy and not as cleanly mixed as the songs from the first game. It seems like some of the songs from the beta/alpha have remained unchanged in the final game as well like Bakunawa 3, which is still just a 46 second loop. The end result of all of this is that the music quality feels very inconsistent throughout the game.  compared to FP1, which I felt maintained a very consistent level of quality throughout its OST. 👎For the most part the entire cast controls really well. There's just a few mechanics that I personally disagree with. The game has a guard button. This was something that was in the demo I played a few years back and I hoped it was a placeholder mechanic but I'm sad to see that it's still here. I'm not a fan of "press button to negate damage" mechanics as I find them to be unengaging and promote a passive playstyle. And that's exactly what they do in this game. The timing for the block is  (despite NPCs dialogue's attempts to convince you otherwise). You can pretty much just stand in one spot and keep negating damage as long as your timing is half decent. I wouldn't have an issue with this so much if I could just ignore it like the bullet time in Katana ZERO, but it is ingrained into the game and so you will need to use it. FP1 did not have a block button (unless you were Milla, but that's a different kind of block), so all bosses were designed for you to avoid damage by moving out of the way or using invincibility frames. Not the case here. Boss design in this game is far more loose and cheap as a result of the guard mechanic existing. Pretty easy to design bosses that you can call fair when you give the player a get out of jail free button. I could harp on this mechanic for another paragraph, but I'll just say that I don't find it very interesting or engaging and leave it at that. 👎The levels don't feel as tight as the ones from FP1 from what I played, and you can feel it from the very outset of the game. They feel kind of empty and bloated sometimes, and convoluted and mazelike some other times. I think there was another review on here that echoed a similar sentiment. I do think the level design picks up after the first 3 levels, but I never really felt like it got as good as the first game's levels. The end level bosses also were pretty underwhelming from what I played. Apart from the boss of the 5th stage they all felt more like minibosses from the first game. Speaking of which this game doesn't have those. The structure from the first game of Act 1 --> Minor Boss --> Act 2 --> Major Boss is gone. You just have level and then boss here, and the bosses are generally just random big robot, while the bosses and minibosses from the first game often had a story reason for existing. Overall levels are shorter and more bite sized in this game, but they have a lot of empty space and glorified hallways. 👎I like the idea of FP2's camera as a proof of concept. FP1 had a single viewframe for the whole game that never zoomed in or out. It could be kind of claustrophobic in a few places, but I didn't find myself minding it too much. FP2 attempts to fix this issue by implementing a camera that zooms out depending on how fast you're going, allowing you to see more of what's ahead. You can adjust how far the camera zooms out in the settings or turn off the feature completely. The downside of this is that it makes those pretty hi-pixel sprites look like total garbage, and you often can't hardly tell what something even is supposed to be because the pixels are so crunched when it's zoomed out. I really don't think it's a good idea to put control over the camera in the player's hands in a game like this. A better solution would have been to handcraft the camera according to the level design: zoom in during the slow and complicated sections and zoom out during the high speed sections where the player is expected to go fast. Instead what they've done is implemented is a clunky system that tries to automate the hard work of proper level and camera design away and fails at it. 👎It's quite buggy. Within the first two hours I found more bad geometry that I was getting stuck on than in the entirety of FP1. There was also someone complaining about the controller glyphs, and yeah those are screwed up as of writing this. Game feels rushed despite taking so long to come out, and honestly that's what I was expecting. I'm not going to say it's Duke Nukem Forever levels of bad or anything but it feels like it's within that territory. 👍From what I played it seems like they got almost all of the original cast from FP1 back to work on this project. There are some replacements like Gong and Syntax, all of the major VAs still seem to be there. The VAs for the new characters sound good as well. I really liked the amateur VA cast from the first game and I'm very happy they've returned to work for this project. I think they do a pretty good job in their delivery for the most part. However I can't really say that the spritework always does the voiceovers justice. The original game had that problem from time to time as well, but I feel like it's exacerbated here because of the more zoomed out camera in most scenes. This segues into my next complaint which is... 👎👎👎The presentation in this game is a wreck when you compare it to FP1, and I think it mainly is due to the overambition of FP2. There are text only dialogue boxes now, which weren't a thing in the first game. In FP1 whenever a character opened their mouth you got voice acting, and they were able to pull that off because of the smaller scope. In FP1 you would go through a level and get a cutscene. Rinse and repeat until the credits. Here you also have towns segments (that feel completely pointless) and have NPCs to talk to. When major characters show up as NPCs to talk to they don't get voice acting either. You don't always get a cutscene after each level like in the first game, and some levels seem to have no place within the story of the game either (Tiger Falls is just a level you go through to get to another city). I can't make myself expect less when the first game set the bar for my expectations.Would you look at that, I’m out of space. Can’t fit anymore. No conclusion segment, sorry. I’m going to try and refund this.tl;dr go play Freedom Planet 1 if you didn't

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, this is kind of a hot take, but I think the only reason this game series didn't get more attention is mainly due to being perceived as "furry" on the outside, but trust me is pretty good. But yeah, this sequel is amazing, it does distance itself a lot from being a 'Sonic fangame' even if the first game had already lots of influence from other Sega Genesis/Megadrive vidya. This game pushes a bit more the beat'em'up feel, adding even a dodge button, and slowing just a tiny bit the gameplay sometimes. Speaking of it, many stages are way larger, sometimes levels not being as straightforward as in the first game, but I think this is actually a right step (one of many) in comparison to the first game, giving room for more complex elements and enemies. Overall this game has so much more content and the OST is amazing even if you'll miss a couple of the iconic songs from FP1. You're likely to finish your first playthrough in around 15-20 hours or so (including beating every level, battle-sphere, boss rematch, etc... but not 100% completion) and it does not feel draggy at all. If you played the first game, basically you'll be missing our lil' alien guy, Torque, and a continuation to the previous villain's whereabouts, which (spoilers from FP2)  , but to be honest, I think they did good with changing the subject of an otherwise predictable sequel, and giving us in exchange a pretty deep story and lore about almost anything that was rather unanswered in the first game and tons of new characters, including a new antagonist.TLDR; buy it, it's sooo worth and I love this game, there are very minor caveats but nothing is really stopping the fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Great sequel that manages to surpass the original.It has the same good gameplay and setting of the first Freedom Planet (albeit with a few design changes in the characters), topped with some more goodies.First, the addition of Neera Li as a playable character (who was a quite a challenging midboss in the first entry of the series) in which she functions as a power-type character.While not as a fast in movement and combat as the other characters, Neera possesses a variety of moves that can pack a punch to enemies; ideal if you're into a more aggressive, battle-focused style of gameplay.Also, the addition of the guard action for all characters adds more depth to the gameplay by providing you with a very fast and short protection for those moments when you get yourself into a bind (a bit comparable towards the insta-shield for those who have played either  or ).Furthermore, the game's difficulty is more customisable than its predecessor due to addition of items that can be held before entering a stage and either give passive postive or negative effects depending on the held item in question.The items are grouped into "boosters", "potions", "charms" and "brave stones".Boosters, charms and potions makes the game easier by granting passive bonuses when held, but at the cost of a penalty on your ranking and crystal shard bonus that gets granted by completing a stage (crystal shards are used here as a currency to buy items in the hub-stages of the game or to exchange into another currency to buy other certain items that are being sold in the hub-areas).You can also fiddle with the assistance settings in the options menu if you really want to play in easy mode.On the other hand, brave stones makes the game harder by granting negative effects on your character, but rewards you with a boost on both ranking and crystal shard bonus; if you play really well with brave stones, you may even get the highest ranking possible for clearing a stage: a rainbow S.The story is just as enjoyable as it was on the previous title and there is even some lore to be found in this entry.The only small downside is the lack of character-exclusive stages and that the difference in dialogue in most cutscenes can be minimal when playing with different characters.One thing of note: the game will reference certain elements, events and a certain character of the previous title, but I don't think it won't have too much impact if you haven't played the first .In overall: a great sequel to an already great sonic-like indie platformer with its own identity that also manages to succesfully expand upon it.Definitely worth recommending!

_childDocuments_.review: I had a very high opinion of the first Freedom Planet game so I was a little afraid that the sequel might not deliver. However it ended up winning me over to the point of not wanting to stop playing and getting all achievements.I wasn't the biggest fan of the artstyle change (specially Lilac's concept art. Sorry but I really like her OG design. She looks better in her sprite form though!). However comparing it to the first one I definetly see the technical improvements. Not to take credit away from the more primitive, cutesy style of the first one, it's just a different vibe. Also I'm really sorry to say but the OST is not as well recieved as the first one and I agree with that take. It's definitely not bad, it's just not as good. No offense!Some of the new gameplay elements such as guarding, items, revivals and boss HP bars made me want to try only a couple stages; however after taking a break and understanding how they worked it made the gameplay really flow (even though it made it feel easier compared to the first one). There's some fun rewards for completing the Gallery and getting the "True Ending" so look forward to that!I've seen some people not really satisfied with the story and I suppose I see their point, but I wouldn't call it a bad narrative, there's interesting worldbuilding and plenty of room to expand on it with other games. What really sells me on the game is the wonderfully responsive controls and the character's different platforming/battling styles. Not to mention the incredibly appealing pixel art.All I can really tell you is that I highly recommend this game. If you're expecting "Sonic but better" or a carbon copy of Freedom Planet 1 it is not going to happen. This game has its own identity and if you learn to play it you're not going to want to stop (well, that's my personal experience at least).

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: Oh, and well, if you haven't played FP1, and are wondering if you should buy this, you don't need to play the first one, and most people will enjoy this one more, since there's less chance of getting stuck on a boss and there's more content. You should probably try at least one of the games either way.I was sceptical about a positive review, because I felt like I enjoyed and remembered FP1 more by a bit. But it's still a good game, I've given positive reviews to worse, and will probably replay it eventually for other characters, so here you go.Despite being a better game in QoL, mechanics, content, voice acting etc, as a lot of other people mentioned, I'll just focus on my complaints:- the music wasn't as memorable as FP1.- the game has a lot more of speed sections compared to the slower platforming of FP1, and it felt like the stages were more empty as a result. Totally subjective though, most people seem to like this more.- I think I actually missed the FP1 bosses, because these ones were easy, probably because of the extra tools you're given - guarding (which might be overkill, since a lot of attacks seem dodgable normally) and Lilac's Dragon Boost being cancellable now. Maybe I should've used more difficulty raising items (especially since I think the game lets you switch items if you game over, and continue at a gem cost, so you don't need to reset the whole stage), and other characters don't have as much i-frame attacks (I think...), but I remember needing to learn patterns more in FP1. The arenas being smaller in that game might help it too, there's more safe spaces here.In particular, I preferred the final boss of 1 compared to this.

_childDocuments_.review: Liked:- Incredible gameplay, reminiscent of Sonic Advance games. There's also quite a few super-levels that feel a bit like a traversing through a Zelda dungeon that gave a nice amount of variety to the stages. Ancestral Forge was a pleasant change of pace from the high-speed stages from prior. Despite their size, these levels were designed very well, and I never felt lost. Certain levels are very memorable due to their length, like Globe Opera, Ancestral Forge, Lightning Tower, and Clockwork Arboretum. There's like one new gimmick per stage and you'll never know what'll be in the next one, which is exciting.- Guarding feels satisfying and you'll definitely be using it against the souped up bosses. A lot of attacks will track you and test your ability to guard, which I feel adds some extra complexity to the boss fights.- Plenty of replay value. It took 8 hours for me to beat the game on one character, and there's four characters, each of which have their own special cutscenes that get teased on other characters to encourage you to play them: I was playing Lilac and Carol's disappearance and what Milla promised to Serpentine were practically begging me to play their characters to find out what happened.- Story is great and the villain is multidimensional unlike from the previous game. You can really see their point of view and understand why they do what they do.- Characters, interactions, and dialogue is interesting (and hilarious). I think there's a perfect mix of old-school corniness, seriousness, and humor. I remember when FP2 was originally going to have VN-style cutscenes, but they decided to go for the more standard in-game cutscenes, which I feel was a great decision. This probably was one of the reasons why the game took so long to release.- Overworld and hub areas add a lot of lore and coziness to the game. Just walking around the different maps and interacting with things adds a lot of worldbuilding that the action-packed stages can't do.- Music is excellent and I bought it instantly after finishing the game.Disliked:- Choosing one of three stories to play for each act doesn't feel like a very exciting player choice. I recall they got rid of it at some point in development, and then brought it back. I feel the story could've felt more connected if they just forced a certain order on us. Players will naturally do the easier stories before the more difficult ones, so it feels a bit like an illusion of choice that isn't necessary.- It would be nice if long levels allowed saving at certain checkpoints, or if they were broken up into sections (but still preserving the togetherness). Something came up while I was playing Ancestral Forge and all I could do was leave my computer on and the game paused.- There should've been a hint at the existence of a true ending and how to get it, maybe a post-credit message for the player. I only found this out by looking it up outside of the game. Instead of Time Capsules I feel a better requirement would've been to complete the game with every character.Things I wish were in the game that the developers probably also wanted in the game but had to drop to avoid even more scope creep:- Another 3-storyline act between acts 2 and 3: It feels sudden that the villain's evil plan is happening and we're immediately going into space to stop her. Catching Dail, maybe gathering materials for the trip, and something else would've added a nice rest stop before the intense final act of the game. I was a bit disappointed when Dail's capture happened off screen and when Serpentine instantly built his ship to get us to Bakunawa.- More content for the secret ending: I feel there could've been at least 3 additional stages dedicated to building up the final, final boss, kind of like how Sonic games have a final story.- Character-specific stages, which would add even more replay value beyond just different dialogue and slightly different boss fights.- A post-game act given how the ending is so open-ended and there's plenty of unanswered questions. I wouldn't be surprised if this ended up as DLC.Would I recommend it to others?- Yes, you'll probably like this game. You can definitely tell why it took so long for this game to release when you're playing it.Hopefully, Freedom Planet 3 doesn't take as long to release once the developers start working on it. Maybe they can pull a Wizard of Legend 2 and have another studio helping them with it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is such a great sequel, improving so much from the original. It's an amazing game and might be in my top 5 favorite indie games. The smash bros x Sonic and other 16-bit inspired gameplay feels so much better with all of the tweaks and extra moves. The stage design has also improved, or at least changed with it now focusing more on speed instead of platforming like the first game did. There's more of an even mix between large stages with multiple routes and more linear or confined ones. I can definitely see myself coming back now and then to play a stage just to have some fun.The game offers a lot of content. There are like 30 stages and 4 characters to beat them with. The added hubs, npcs and world map also makes it feel so much more like an adventure and spending time interacting with the hubworlds' npcs is quite charming. Some may not care about the story or extra content however and just want to play through the stages. There is a classic mode where it's just the stages but you have to beat the game once while in adventure mode. I don't see the problem with that honestly as you should at least experience and understand the story. Unlike the first game, you don't have to worry about being stopped from playing the game because you're having trouble with a difficult boss. I myself never needed them outside the final boss, but you can buy gear and items via shops to make the bosses easier. With other extra help settings you can toggle, you can really tailor this game to your skill level if you so desire to.The amount of replayability is great. You are encouraged to explore levels to optimize your speedruns. You get a goal to beat the "par time" of a stage and also get achievements for getting less than half the par time. There is also a ranking system but it isn't tied to your speed. It is based on the combat of the game, and to get a perfect rank, you have to beat the level, defeat boss and also not get hit. It can be pretty brutal for some bossfights, but you can still get shields to avoid the instadeath, so it makes you have to optimize a route through stages in order to get as many shields as you can. The story of this game is honestly weaker than the original, I won't deny it. The main problem is that the game no longer has separate campaigns for each character unlike the first. Combined with a lot of extra villains, it makes it harder for them to shine. The main antagonist themself really suffers from this, as unlike Lord Brevon from the first game, they aren't nearly as intimidating or involved with the conflicts. They're supposed to be overpowered, but outside of the lore/backstory, there's only a single time in the story where that's shown besides from the final boss. I really wish they had divided the villains across multiple of the character's campaigns, along with making some stages more tailored to certain characters and their abilities. The dialogue itself suffers from them not doing this in some cases. Characters have unique dialogue or conversations you don't see in other campaigns, but then there are times where other characters who speak to your player character don't have unique dialogue to say to them. This creates some weird flowing conversations and is also disappointing if you wanted to see what is different ( Especially to me, someone who really likes a lot of these characters ).The music of this game will go down as being one of my favorite osts. The only complaint I have is that due to the amount of stages, some of them are less unique to others. This in turn makes some music themes less memorable or distinct. The ones that do stand out however I really do love. I also started to like some of the themes that didn't stand out to me at first the more I played the game across multiple campaigns. It is really down to your preferences whether some will stick out to you. If it weren't for the non-distinct campaigns and for the weaker story and characters, I would say this game is a perfect 10/10 platformer. Right now though, I'd say it's a very very solid 8-8.5. Even if you're not such a sonic fan, you should really try this game out. It's easier to get into than the first I'd say and is overall quite the polished game.

_childDocuments_.review: Freedom Planet 2 is a huge improvement over the first game.you have a few characters to choose from which all have different ability that reflect the different kind of archetypes you would expect from a sonic game , the soundtrack is fine even if It's not highly memorable and the story is good enough while being delivered by some decent voice acting.the controls are tight and the game mix platforming and fighting pretty well , the level design is well done and offer a good ammount of variety and the game is very fast paced. _childDocuments_.review: Having really enjoyed the first Freedom Planet and played at least enough to complete every character's path, I feel confident in saying this game is better by leaps and bounds. That's not something typically said about sequels, but it's true here. The main thing that really makes it, is that the developers took all the character abilities and dialed them up to 11, making all of them really and truly enjoyable to play. To a point that I don't really have a favorite or one I consider "the most fun." It's almost a miraculous thing, most single-player games don't do well with multiple characters and abilities that are too different, but Galaxy Trail pulled it off. The first game, while fun, was mainly made for Lilac-- unless you're one of those crazy speed runners. Seriously, check out Milla speed runs in FP1, you'll be blown away. Maybe even a little scared. o-o; I was.Speaking of Milla, she absolutely takes the cake for cute mascot characters, her idle sequences will make you go "awww!" I guarantee it. Sooo effing cute! ^-^ But overall the character designs I say, were vastly improved over originals. So much more detail, better movements, and I'm in the camp that strongly dislikes the over-sized head/hands/feet. It's a real turn-off, so I'm glad the sequel did away with it. Between this and the prior point, I just about can't play the original game anymore. Not to say it's a bad game, certainly not. And if you're new to the series I think you should buy it and at least play Lilac's route. But for me, it lives as a cherished memory and that's about the extent of it.One thing I would have liked to see carry over from the first game: Dedicated character levels. There were a handful of these mini-arcs across the game, each was 3 levels you could do in any order. Out of 32 levels, I think it would have been really cool, to have one mini-arc specially tailored to each playable character. Truly differentiate everybody's play-through, as well as flesh out more of their individual stories-- just a little. Cuz that is one thing too, the story was still largely centered on Lilac. There was some personal stuff with the others, ranging from "quite interesting" to "downright spicy," but none so poignant as "last of the water dragons business." I'm not set to complain about that in earnest, because in a game like this, the mechanics and "fun factor" are so much more important than the story. But there is very clearly an intentional emphasis on SOMETHING narrative-driven, which is fine-- great even. The cherry on top of a fantastic and fun game sundae. Not worth mention if the goal was "focus on Lilac" anyway. Usually nobody cares about sidekicks anyway, I get it.Lilac's final rant though. Gave me chills. I'll say this much: It's a bit too meta for real life social discourse right now, and I don't appreciate that. But it was handled well so, have a pass. And be more mindful in the future. I play games to ESCAPE reality, not be dragged through more of it, kthx.

_childDocuments_.review: A major improvement from the first game! The gameplay is soooo much better than the first game (the dodge mechanic makes things so much more fun! Mastering it makes you feel like a combat master and I love it!), sprite quality is much better now, the voice acting is so much better now, the level design is a lot more fun, and unpopular opinion but I think the music is a lot better this time around. There are 3 things that I don't like that prevent me from giving this game a 10/10. The story, yep another unpopular opinion I know but I thought the first story was better for my own personal reasons that I wanna get into here but i'm not saying the new story is bad it extremely well written, I just like the first story more (Well I was 15 when I played the first game so it be nostalgia talking). Lady Neera, yea I'm sorry but why was she the 4th character chosen to be playable? Who asked for this? We all wanted Spade not her *sigh* a waste of a cool 4th playable character. The last thing that prevents me from giving it a 10/10 is that some levels (despite me praising the level design earlier) can be confusing and tedious asf making them a drag to go back to when you're trying to beat the game as all characters. But despite this, its a major step up from the previous game and is easily a 9/10! Amazing job!

_childDocuments_.review: (comment changed after 3rd playtrought)This is by far my favorite 2D platformer ever.At first, I thought this was going to be a basic Sonic styled platformer with weird looking characters, but oh well that wasn't the case at all. The gameplay, the level design, the music (oh the music 📈📈 Leilani you cooked so hard), the visuals, the characters, the world, it's all so good.The playable characters all have their unique attacks and abilities that completely changes how you play the game. Of course that makes the game EXTREMELY replayable, and theres something for everybody like optional side story content, optional collectables, badges and achievements, and a rank system,  Multiple reason to replay the game again.The difficulty is also very well balanced. The system itself is pretty creative, you can equip and unequip items to change your level of difficulty on the overworld map, when you feel like it. Meaning you can equip items to make your experience easier or harder at any time.The only negative things I can say about this game is that:1- The cutscenes are uhhh... _childDocuments_.review: Freedom Planet 2 is a fantastic action platformer but also a love letter to 90s/2000s animated shows with an endearing cast of characters, a thoughtful story, and a truly memorable villain. Highly recommended if you like thrilling speedy action platforming akin to classic Sonic/Gunstar Heroes/Mega Man X, stellar boss fights that are challenging but always fair, heart-pumping music, or just hanging out in gorgeous, pixel art hub towns talking to cute, charming npcs.
_childDocuments_.name: Freedom Planet 2

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DRIf you enjoy the 2D Sonic games or just fast 2D platformers in general, you literally can't go wrong with this game whatsoever. 9/10TS;DRI was a bit hesitant on picking this game up at first, but one 100% run through the game later, and I can safely say this game is simply a god-tier 2D Platformer. The artstyle, music, writing, characters, controls, level design, and everything in between all fit neatly together to make an amazing ride from start to end. All 4 characters feel so fun and different to play that it honestly makes repeat playthroughs worth it and super enjoyable (It's also cool seeing your specific character's POV in the story). As with most Sonic games, there's nothing like mastering a stage and being able to breeze past obstacles at light speeds. All the stages feel like playgrounds all with different toys to mess with.Man. What a good game lol9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Returning to Avalice hasn't felt any better.  is how you do a proper video game sequel. The world built by the first game has returned, yet feels completely brand new. The environments are more lively, there is more depth and detail in every nook and cranny which is super fun to search for every hidden detail. The characters have evolved nicely, while they maintained their original traits this game expands upon their existing attributes and makes them even more lovable.  has grown up and evolved into a brilliant and caring leader,  is nuttier and more lively,  is cuter for no reason at all and she has more personality, and even  went from an absolute ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ to somewhat likable. Most of the past characters have returned,  is still the most enjoyable to me. He maintained his sleezy attitude and is now obsessed with finding a new something something for something I don't want to spoil. The only con that I have with the game is that Torque doesn't have any mentions or references in the game, I wish that he was mentioned vaguely, it would have been cool if Lilac kept in contact with him or something, just speculation.If you like fast paced platformers and retro goodness, Freedom Planet 2 is hella worth the money. _childDocuments_.review: Freedom Planet 2 is without a doubt an amazing game.
