_childDocuments_.review: My impression after completed this game is that, it's heavily geared toward young audiences.The game is rated PEGI 12 after all. And everything in this game seems to be appropriate to that age range;Like, fluffy character designs, story-book presentation style (a narrator would tell you story like how an adult would tell a child), child-like vocabulary, low violence, simple and easy to understand story line that focuses on morality and life lessons, low difficulty combats, basic colour matching puzzles.So, if you are older gamers, those things might irritate you, because you might perceive them as lacking when you compare to other action-rpg games made for older audiences or adults.Personally, I appreciate that there is more open-world action-RPG made for kids.And I recommend this game for kids or anyone that new to the genre.For everyone else, if you already played many open-world action-rpg games before, this game offers nothing new. And you should definitely wait for sale.Since the game is made for kids, it is quite basic in every aspects. Combats feel floaty and unsatisfying. Most enemies do the same attack patterns.Huge majority of contents in this game are fillers that designed to make you explore the world. And the world, while looks pretty, it's quite empty.The replay value is very low too; there is no new content to be found in new game plus.For game performance, this game runs ok. The most taxing graphic options are: Shadow Quality, Foliage Density, and World Draw Distance. On RTX 2070, in some of the worst performing areas, the different between Medium and High settings for Shadow and Foliage can be ~20 FPS each. And max World Draw Distance would cause a major performance hit in some areas when raining.Also, this game only use double-buffered vsync. That means when your PC cannot maintain vsync, FPS will drop to half of your monitor's refresh rate. For example, when using 60Hz monitors with vsync on, this game will either lock to 60 FPS or 30 FPS, nothing in between.

_childDocuments_.review: Biomutant is a very great game that I am enjoying the heck out of, so here is what I think of it:It's a very vibrant and pretty world and all its environments.It's combat feels clunky at first but after about 2 hours you understand how it works and is much easier to combat anything.The leveling system seems adaptive meaning all foes you come across are either about 3-5 levels above you and always around 3-5 below you. With the odd health bar bosses randomly around the world possibly being higher (I remember killing at least 10 skull "leveled" enemies around lvl 5-9)I picked saboteur and am, at current level of 28, nigh unkillable and deal 90% crits of 700-1200 to nearly everything.The game allows a great amount of min/maxing right down to gear and their parts you can find and always recycle your weapons by dismantling them and replacing part to make them stronger.The game's ui is simple and easy to follow, doesn't crowd the screen(especially at 110 fov) and inventory ui is a bit rough when using the mouse but only keyboard it works fine.There are a ton of quests in this game and many that are requires for getting into certain areas that are locked/blocked off.My favorite stuff is the story related mounts and other collectible mounts you can get.Some dungeons after 8 hours of play you'll notice are going to feel fairly samey(especially the sewers and nuclear plants.) but overall it just makes them easier to pathfind to get your loot and get out.The story so far since seems interesting however I have avoided nearly all of it and have just been exploring the world, like I always do with open world games. I'll do the story probably around when im out of side quests to do or hit level cap (if this game has one).The narrator, same one who narrated in vermintide games, is a man with such a great voice and even with most random world dialogues being silly is still great to hear and the narration of the npcs of the game since they all speak gibberish is good. It's like being read a story to you by someone when you're a kid.The overall game is great and i've experience no game breaking bugs or anything that is broken and cant be completed yet.

I'm 50, and Biomutant has become one of my all-time favorite gaming experiences.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm on an i7-8750H, 32gb DDR4 with a GTX 1060 6gb on m.2 SSD. Graphically this game is stunning, beautiful, adorable, and visually interesting. I've encountered no running bugs so far. Updates will follow below the original review. Final review TLDR: This game deserves a much better sequel where they learn from the failures of this one, because there is so much here that could have made this Fallout-level good. I plan to slog through and finish because the parts that are good are solid. This review will have spoilers. I mark as recommended, though I may change my mind in the future, despite many cons, which I will list first. If these are enough to turn you away, the pros won't change it. I still recommend the game as of this writing.Cons-Far too frequent interruptions for complicated, sometimes confusing and often nonsensical exposition-Complicated upgrade/level up systems that feel out of place-Unexplained events in game, like enemy faction leader having dialogue directed at you immediately after you choose the opposing faction despite not being anywhere present at the time, a creature in a wheelchair scaling out of a huge hole you had to climb to leave, talking about the tree of life without my ever having seen it directly, etc. (heavy ludonarrative dissonance)-Some controls are not as fluid or responsive as I might have hoped-Very repetitive world objects, the same broken down truck in every area you enter for examplePros-Awesome fighting, at least for the Saboteur class that I'm playing with-GORGEOUS world art, adorable characters-Ki power upgrades seem awesome and fun to use-A cool weapon and gear system I've yet to fully explore (sadly this long in I have no customization items yet...)I hope that some changes might get made moving forward to improve the game, even if they have to be big ones. I feel truly like it doesn't know what kind of game it's trying to be. There's a ton of promise here, and I've been keeping loose tabs on the creation of this game forever, so maybe take my bias into account. I think a fair number of people are disappointed in this game so far, and I too may reach that point (I'll sure update if I do) because of expectations of what this game would be vs. what it actually is right now, and I don't fault them at all given my list of cons. I will still give it a chance, and maybe the game will open up and be better as I progress.4 hour update: The game DOES get better. Lots of the mentioned flaws don't necessarily go away, but there's a lot more to do now. Though I consider it a hefty oversight that it took me 3+ hours to pick up customization items and stop having constant story dialogue interruptions, the game now is starting to make me think of a combination of Mini-Ninjas and Fable, but with a more fun weapon customization and crafting system. I'm liking it more than I was for certain, once you get some powers (though a few are confusing to use and not well explained before you unlock them) and weapons under the belt. Still struggling to incorporate the parry system. But now I feel much better about recommending it for sure. 14 hour update: There's so much to do in this game. Lots of territory capture. Factions. Crafting, upgrading, powers. Imagine if half a Pixar team got together with half of the Red Faction team to make a game, except they never quite settled on some details, got rushed in the 11th hour, and did the best they could to make it playable without everything quite in good order. That's about what this game is. Objectives have zero pacing, and zero time restraint. The narrator gives ominous warnings about night, and you can rest until morning at campfires, but night itself is no different than daytime. I've found the combat to be very fun if not always fluid, dialogue is fairly predictable and binary with lots of what feels like filler in absence of context or better words. Lots of things that give you the impression they make a difference actually don't. And the game DOES have some bugs. Changing out my top for example, on my avatar the upgrades I've made on my equipped top will remain if I change it to a new one. Shop selling lists often mark the wrong items as being equipped.  Small stuff. While lots of stuff feels unfinished though, what is finished is quite fun, and my honest review is this: This game deserves a much better sequel where they learn from the failures of this one, because there is so much here that could have made this Fallout-level good. Better even. I hope it survives the bad reviews to get that much.

_childDocuments_.review: Biomutant had a bit of rocky start with some bug crashes and other issues but currently its running very well for me on PC. I played on ps4 also with less success. It doesn't really invent any new mechanics but it combines elements of other games to mostly good effect. And it looks really cool. I'd say if you like open world action adventure and the theme of mutant kung fu animals appeals to you give it a shot. It's semi-open world really as you must methodically unlock access to most of the map. But it feels pretty open mid to late game with wide open areas to explore and a good variety of terrain. The strongest points I think are:  1. Combat. Not terribly inventive but it integrates enough different elements in a fairly intuitive interface to be really fun. You have guns, melee, wung fu powers, psi powers and mutant abilities from which you can tailor endless combinations and strategies. It rewards experimentation. 2. Crafting. The loot system is above average. Lots of open world games suffer from an overabundance of loot that eliminates the excitement. Or from an encumbrance system that makes collecting difficult. Here there is a good balance. Especially the spare parts. You can use the gear you find, buy, win in quests or that you craft yourself. It's not super critical to follow a curve and the quest lines supply you with what you absolutely need so, if you are like me, you can just have fun with it and dress your character in zany ways. 3. The world. The map,  enemies and NPCs are both clever, beautiful and consistently silly. Of course there are a few weak points also: 1. The game contains puzzles. They aren't good. Mostly they are easy but compared with other open world contenders out now BioMutant has some of the weakest puzzle challenges around. 2. The narrator. I can't figure out how to turn this off. It's incredibly repetitive and ceases to helpful after the first fifteen minutes or so.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think I have ever been more torn on recommending or not recommending a game. Not going to go super in-depth with this "review", but I will say - this is the best worst game I've played in a very long time. So much of this game has the potential to be a 9 /10 or even a 10/10 contender just due to how creative it's systems are. To explain the above a bit more - Biomutant has a LOT of well designed mechanics that are ultimate held back by the game itself in a way that end up being detrimental. If you take the game by bits and pieces, each individual mechanic would actually classify as "Great" or even "Innovative" but all together, the game is just repeatedly dragged down by a ton of small issues that eventually add up into a large detriment. For example, the game's Crafting System for Weapons is easily one of the most creative I have ever seen in a game, I would even go as far as to say it's very innovative - but the end result ends up being 2 detriments to the game itself and one that affects this system. First off, the combat in the game is hardly balanced properly, melee weapons are practically worthless outside a very specific scenario and Automatic Rifles are beyond broken, even more so when you unlock Perfect Reload. Secondly, same as before, not only are the enemies not able to deal with your onslaught of lead, the way the world continually scales to your character, is not balanced properly - enemies ONLY scale to your Level, meaning they do NOT scale according to the power you possess, which means you can end up completely breaking the game 2 hours into it if you manage to get lucky enough with an elemental base for an Automatic Rifle. The game also just straight up feels at times like it does not respect your time. I'm not sure why they thought giving you tools to unlock certain areas, like a crowbar to unlock doors, a big punchy fist to break down walls, a Jet ski and other stuff also require you to complete an asinine fetch quest to raise them to Lvl 2, just to use them in like, 4-5 more scenarios that you normally couldn't. Honestly, I could go on and on about how much this game just presents a very well thought out, enveloped system only to just severely undermine it with another mechanic. Not only that, the sound in this game is so, off putting. Even after turning the "Narrator" all the way down to 0, he would still find ways to just spit out nonsense from time to time. Weapons and guns all have different sounds for the most part, but feel kinda drowned out, like there's a lack of proper sound tuning. There's barely any music to speak of, and there is, I just barely remember any of them and certainly none I would pop in for a jam here or there.To give it SOME praise, this is one of the visually stunning games I've played in a while. The environments are all super detailed and just fun to explore. Plenty of vistas and sights to see, and just makes running around for hours a very relaxing experience for the most part.So, why am I recommending this game? Well, I personally got 30 hours of enjoyment from it and I may pop back in to get 100% eventually. I did really love some of the systems the game has. I think overall, I ended up walking away pretty happy from it despite my reluctance in recommending it. I will say however, that my review is a touch misleading. The reason for that is because I actually do NOT recommend the majority of you actually pick up this game until it hits a deep sale. I personally had a pretty good time with it but just as a one of, I know a lot of you will straight up not enjoy this game. Take that as you will.

_childDocuments_.review: Do Not Buy - I wish I could return but I am past my two hour mark. I regret spending so much money on a game. Ill break out some of my points below. This feels like a game that was never allowed to have constructive feed back on any mechanic. They got so caught up in what they were doing, and if anyone told the devs this featured seemed weird or clunky they ignored the feed back entirely. So the game looks awesome on paper, but when playing it there is no soul or fun to the game.- The story would be appealing to a 7 year old that has a hard time reading. I mean if you feel you kid is too young to play dark souls and want to prep them for Dark Soul, may do the trick. - This game holds your hand so much and explains so little. It is amazing the amount of time going through tutorials (beware tutorials and teaching mechanics will eat through 2 hours of play through which effectively makes the game nonreturnable) and yet there are hundreds of mechanics that come out of no where that do not make sense. The unexplained or explained mechanics are not intuitive. A great example is a fort raid. I walked up to some guys with an exclamation point outside a fort. Once I talked to them it initiated a raid on the fort, I could not back out. Not only that I was warned not do cause any collateral damage. There are only bad guys at staged levels. So you have lots of time to wander the fort. While wondering the fort, there does not seem a way to cause collateral damage to anything? There is no loot to find. It is just an empty fort until you reach these predefined stages where you fight people. During that raid on the fort I was exploring and fell out of the fort and took about 20 minutes to find another way to climb something to get back in.- The choice system feel inspired by fable, but somehow seems a lot more childish. Fable had simple mechanics and the choices were obvious. This takes the level of obviousness to a whole new level and the narrator explains the choice to the point of tedium. What is annoying, is sometimes the mechanics for showing which choice are good or bad take a while to appear on screen. I saw some weird mouse thing about to be executed on a stage outside. You could choose to interact with the mouse tied to a post or a stand which the executioner (or judicial authority?) was speaking from. I went to check out the stand, because I wanted to check for loot before letting the little creature go. After I clicked the action button on the stand, the icon showing me this was a "bad" choice popped up... Also This is an example of a mechanic that was not explained. I guess it is intuitive if I was playing slower?- The leveling system is annoying. Lets say I want to level up hand-to-hand combat. Well, after I level up I select hand to hand combat at level 2. All the items in hand to hand combat are already learned? Okay, I want to learn a Psi power. Oh those dont take level up points, I need to collect something else. - This is not an open world. I am 4.5hrs in the game right now. Not in the way skyrim is an open world. You have follow the quest line to progress. After the main tutorial being introduced to the world. You have to choose the path of peace or domination. You are given limited mobility and if you explore areas you are not supposed to be in, some locations are still on the map and explorable, but are entirely empty unless you at a specific point in the story where you can interact with the location. Even after you choose a path, you are limited in how far you can progress. It is annoying to find some place cool to explore and literally have nothing there because the location is entirely story bound.- Things to fight are scarce unless the location has some significance or you are at the correct point in time in the story. On other hand you can find a really cool looking location then out of nowhere a giant boss will pop out without warning. Literally out of thin air. The narrator will say something and if you are not prepared you will likely die fairly quickly. - There are side exploration quests. When you find Brick Town you have to find a loot to complete a quest. There is tons of loot in the location, no one to fight, and it is as boring as this sounds.- The world just is not interesting to explore. It was cool at first but lost interest quickly once you realize there are not hidden gems to find on your own. Everything explored through the story. This is not a BoTW type of game. At least 4.5 hours into the game. But at what point does it become an actual open world? 10 hours?- Fight mechanics are pretty cool. Fights take forever in a dark souls kind of way, but give you way to many healing objects. You could fight maybe 10 guys and it will take 10 minutes to beat them. 3 minutes of time will be spent healing. This may just be because I suck at the game. The fights just take to long and literally get boring.

_childDocuments_.review: This review will entail some tips and tricks + observations, l what feels missing from the game, and a mid-high level of how the game plays.Note: This game currently has a potential bug (at least for me) where with a 2 handed blade I am prompted for button presses but with my melee dual wield the most I get is the icon notifying me they are about to attack... if it is not a bug then depending on your weapon the difficulty could differ significantly based off of counter/dodge prompts or the lack therein.Sub-Genre Classification Summary:I'd probably classify it as an open world ARPG for people who like exploring within a new genre of Souls-Lite due to how dying isn't punishing but depending on your character/gear you can be 1 shot. Enemies across the map generally scale with your level. The difficulty on Hard, assuming levels are equal, reflects what if that giant monster hit me... you'll either will die or be badly hurt. You act like an damage sponge to enemies your size/level as much as your enemies your size/level act like a damage sponge to you.Mid-High level Gameplay Summary for Gamers:You can save often, the fights do get monster-hunter / Souls-likeish combat at times (you can be one shot by mini-bosses depending on level discrepancy and build). The game is harder than Batman on its highest difficulty and reflects most closely a marrying of the combat from (Middle Earth) Shadow of War without skill combo's counters/bonuses (nor allies) when you are fighting enemies in a non-siege battle on the highest difficulty... meaning that it can feel like your vs something impossible and it forces you to try new strategies... albeit this game doesn't adapt to your playstyle and the fort captures are overly easy (which is fine as they are not the focus of the greater game)... it is in the same vein of difficulty vs anything that is a group of enemies with a (mini) boss (which is frequent). It is as if Shadow of War's combat was mixed with Breath of the Wilds whimsy and vastness, in conjunction with some simplistic puzzles and art reminiscent of Ratchet and Clank. Per the 6/1 update the game is easier on Hard. My Psi Freak still rocking those starter electric gloves I can now more easily dodge and do noticeably more melee damage. Not sure how I feel about the loot changes as on my first character I wasn't getting crazy loot and my my 2nd I got 5 level 30 locked and a few level 20-29 locked gear pre level 15... but if that legendary gear is now going to be shifted to my level then I don't want to open red/pink chests until I am level 50... They also fixed more major bugs (that were still minor) and seemingly buffed equipment resistances across the board thus making exploration of the map possible significantly earlier (~level 20) without the specific environmental suits.Warning: It is easy to die if you build a glass cannon and if you don't build it it is still easy to die if you're not seasoned at combo based ARPG's (on Hard). Loss of attention in a fight will equal death. Levels feel like they have a big impact and you get the sense of your going up against of an army of equal leveled enemies at times, unlike Batman, DMC, Assassins Creed, etc. that all feel easier on equivalent difficulties... I find myself having to use items in this game whereas I cannot recall the last time I had to do that in any game including the aforementioned... also this game makes it really easy to quick heal.Tips, Tricks, and Observations:The Psi-Freak class defaults to unarmed combat and well.. Psi powers - your melee attacks will apply electric elemental damage thus they do not have to be only casters.Crafting comes early on if you follow the starting narrated direction. When crafting weapons note that you can craft ranged by clicking the "Ranged" tab at the top... it is easy to miss.Your abilities dictate how dynamic your gameplay is... I recommend the (bounce) shroom and fire dash abilities (not their actual names) as they help you get around the map if you do not have a fast character (mine has all its points into strength and intellect with some vitality as some guns require up to 50 vitality thus far (there are plenty of good ones that don't, especially if you craft). Apparently there are some clothes that require agility but I only came across 1 pair and it is lesser than other clothing without restrictions... so agility is not a necessity and if you side-quest Luck probably is not valuable past crit chance... you first have to do damage for crits to be valuable hence why I'd recommend investing in Strength or Intelligence.I played the Mercenary class to start, for those who didn't pre-order I'd advise character that boosts melee damage unless you are only going to play ranged (which is a lot less fun) and wont last once armored units that block bullets come into the fray... it might be feasible with Psi Powers or attempting to shoot a gap in armor (requires a rare weapon base to get lazer accuracy so I wouldn't plan on it being feasible even if possible).There are perks that use those dogtags (similar to biopoints and psi points) that are easily overlooked for both your class and general that play into chaining like attacks.The karma system systems to direct the player, through commentary at least, to balancing yin and yang rather than go to one extreme or the other and  I would recommend checking out this link for more on tribe allegiances if you don't mind not figuring it out for yourself (you may never figure it out): If you like exploring the fetch quests likely wont feel like fetch quests, especially as you'll find gear along your way to upgrade your gear... there are invisible walls and at least 1 place thus far you can get stuck... luckily the game autosaves often and fast travel is a breeze.Hit space as a character is talking to have the subtitle popup immediately, hit space again if you don't want to skip the narrators commentary.One may be able to play the game without doing the main story quest of allying with a Tribe, but one has to explore the rest of the world and it comes down to if one can proc the flashback when visiting your characters village between the two factions of which the narrator seems to direct you to ally with one of... I know I will be doing a 2nd playthrough and I've never done that for an open world game before as I am that curious as to if it is possible. I stupidly allied with a tribe but did not carry out the alliance before realizing these implications.What the game can benefit from:The game is lacking a combo number system from showing up on screen which other games leverage to incentivize the player to fight in more dynamic ways including attack chaining (bonuses)... the result is you have to challenge yourself to do this instead of cheesing combat. This is likely where a lot of people feel the combat is lacking.As the game lets you make your own character so dynamically, if you are unseasoned in Combo-System based ARPG's you can make your life a lot harder than it needs to be.The middle mouse button modifer needs a way to remap the modified keys, this is a significant feature that is lacking despite being able to bind everything else. On PC with keyboard get used to the idea of hitting E, Alt, Space, or Right Click.Ammo limits? I like what they did but I think people are cheesing ranged as they have unlimited ammo... I'd prefer combo bonuses and limited ammo that 1 can easily reacquire from drops post-fight as currently it seems to be balanced by reducing clip sizes and attack speed. Elemental ammo and its limits are nice but expensiveQuick Heal needs its own key mapping... you'll end up using a health pack you don't want to without this improvement.

_childDocuments_.review: It is a hardcore, all in wuxia story.  Don't be fooled by the cute animal characters or the post apocalyptic coat of paint.  The customization is hard to judge this early in...  Judging from loot I've collected, I think it might be more reasonable to look at the customization aspects closer to 30 or 40 hours in.  So far, there's quite a bit of stuff, but if it's like any of these other games, there is an enormous amount of stuff reserved for higher levels.There are some bugs.  The very first NPC you can talk to in the game bugged on me and I had go back to my last save.  Fortunately, the game autosaves all the time, so that's not as big of a problem as it could be.  Hope you have an SSD.  This may be the first game I've played that I feel needs that kind of disk response time.  My rigs internals are going on about five, six years now.  The game plays well on here, but there are other games that do not.  i7 6400k with 16gb DDR5 for ref.I like the story.  I'm a sucker for wuxia, but I'm hardly alone in that.  I really hope the automaton has a few more skins, and I hope they change what it is instead of just being different colors of grasshopper.  It's a very small thing, especially in the action sequences with everything that's rendering, so I would understand if modeling time went elsewhere.The political presentation is a little thick and heavy, but it's not as though anyone argues reckless polluting is bad.  I'd just say this is a game and while there are corporations as reckless and irresponsible as portrayed in the game, I hope people will focus their ire toward the countries that actually practice that sort of dumping.Good presentation of all themes.  I particularly like that people react to your reputation so it isn't a pointless set of points.  Looking forward to the updates!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good openworld game. As the first game of a new game studio, it's absolutely stellar, with wonderfully evocative graphics and great worldbuilding.Good game world designs all have their own "feel" to them (Consider "Stray", or any game by Bethesda) and this game has that in spades.While the ratings are "mixed", if you filter them to "English only", you'll see "Showing 10,089 reviews that match the filters above (Mostly Positive)". So I suspect their non-English versions may not be as good? I could imagine the narrator being not up to snuff in a lot of languages, particularly given how he's too much for some people even in English. [2024 edit: Even filtering by English, it's now still "Mixed". Ah well.]I've been playing it quite a bit, and just completed (100% achievements, all main quests, all locations and sub quests that I could find). This took, Steam tells me, a little over 87 hours (though about 10 hours of that was me deliberately darkening my aura, only to discover that was pointless, as NPCs who reject you due to a light aura don't change their mind if your aura changes).I'd recommend it, IF you're a "completionist explorer" player like me. From other reviews, there're definitely other categories of player that it doesn't cater to as well. I'd say that in terms of variety of activities, quests and locations, it's a little below Fallout 3, but a fair bit above Breath of the Wild.In terms of combat, it's... well, there's no one-hit kill sniper build, and monsters are levelled, so no matter how strong you are, they're still grindy to kill. You can just crank difficulty to "easy" once that starts to annoy you, though. Combat is fun, and (at least while you're trying to get relevant achievements) it has mechanics to reward you for using a combination of melee and ranged weaponry. Once you no longer care about the achievements, though, it's just easier to just strafe around with a machinegun rather than using all the fancy special attacks and ammo. If you enjoy combat in games you might get more out of that part of the game than I did.I like the setting and story. As is normal in open-worlds, if you are an explorer, you will want for nothing: all my armor and weapons and materials are maxed out, and I'm a millionaire in "leaves", the ingame currency.After 87 hours I'm at level 63, I've maxed all psi skills, all mutations/resistances, and all wung-fu/perks, but not yet maxed the stats... in fact, I'm not sure there IS a cap on stats, I've raised luck to 300 (which gives 100% crit chance), and could apparently raise it even higher: my "loot chance" is still only 75%.There are plenty of points to spend: I now have psi, bio and upgrade points I can't spend on anything - which I feel is fine, it means I got to play with all the abilities in the game, rather than only getting to play with the ubercool final abilities for ten minutes at the very end, or in New Game Plus mode. NG+ does exist, which skips the intro and gives you all your stats and inventory from the previous game, which is nice.So I'm not sure the level cap, but I assume it's Very High, if any.Loot is well balanced: you feel like there's way too much stuff you can't use, but you can sell or grind it up for scrap. And even if you are at max there's always slight incremental improvements you can make, when you find ultimate weapons that are slightly better, either for your primary weapon or your "sometimes, just for fun" weapons. There are also outfits you can create, so if you want to look like a spaceman with a jetpack, you can do it with a mouseclick: more importantly in the early game, you can make custom outfits dedicated for each resistance.I found that resistances were only a big deal in the early game: you'll very quickly be able to put together outfits that'll give you 100% for at least one resistance, and eventually you'll have 100% in all just in your regular outfit.There's no inventory limit so you can loot ALL THE THINGS. But (bizarrely!) mats that you decon them into are capped at 99. Game balance?The variety of clothing and mounts struck me as Really Nice, and I'm not even normally concerned about those things. Range of craftable weaponry combinations is awesome.I encountered no gamebreaking bugs, and fewer minor glitches than I'm used to in open-worlds (conversations sometimes continue after I say goodbye, not unlike talking with some IRL people; Steam achievements don't visibly track progression, but do unlock once complete; there was one minor sidequest that didn't mark itself as complete in the journal).If I have any complaint, it's that some minor locations (crashed cars on roads, etc) were often cut-n-paste, so if you had searched one, you knew where the loot would be at the next one.I can kinda see why people were disappointed at $60, but for half that it's about right-priced. For less than half, it's a steal. As an indie game, and the first game by the studio, "Experiment 101"? It's kinda wow :DI'm excited to see what else this studio comes up with in future! They were acquired by THQ Nordic in 2017, before even releasing a game: hopefully this is only one of many.

_childDocuments_.review: I am enjoying the game so far. It's basically Ratchet and Clank and Breath of the Wild mixed together with Borderlands/Diablo style looting and customization. The story is horrible and I turned the narrator off after about 3 hours. Combat is... okay. Melee is essentially useless, unless maybe you put all your skill points into strength. Guns seem to be the way to go, and the gunplay is solid. The world is beautiful and vast, and the game heavily rewards exploration in the form of loot. The whole light/dark system is essentially useless aside from a few powers that each give you, but you can just unlock all by the end of the game it seems. I chose the dark path and to save the worldeaters and let them destroy the tree, yet when it came time to confront the first boss, I still had to fight it and I killed it. But then afterwards it was just sitting on the root chomping away. Cool I guess? In short though, I am having a lot of fun just running around the world and looting and crafting gear. If you enjoy this kind of game, definitely buy it, but don't expect a good story. I would say whether it is worth 60 dollars is subjective. There are better games that have sold for less, but far more worse games that have sold for the same price.

_childDocuments_.review: This review will contain SPOILERS!Things I like about Biomutant:The character creator! It is extremely unique and I love how it determines how your mother and father look, as well as your child self. That was a nice surprise! Not to mention, your character looks really cute!The combat! It is really, really good! Very flashy, very cool! Fast-paced! I have had a great time unlocking new abilities and trying them out!The crafting! I usually don't like crafting in games, but this is very simple and easy to understand and I like that you can build your own weapons and that some possess unique powers! I have had a lot of fun experimenting with builds.The world. This is a beautiful game. The environments are very detailed, very colorful! It's all very pretty to look at! The sky, the sun, the fields, it is so very pretty! It is also HUGE with tons of things to do!The mounts!  I like the mounts! They are very cute and I am continually surprised by all the new ones I find.Things that I do not like Biomutant:Repetitive Dialog. After a while, you start to realize that talking to the NPCs is all kinda same-y. They all have pretty much the same things to say no matter where you go, and they are all based around the trope of their character. If you've played this game and listened to the dialog, you know exactly what I mean.Feeling overpowered. Maybe I just power-leveled, maybe it is the difficulty I selected (Normal) but the enemies seem to be unable to stand any chance against me. I completely destroy anything in my path just by firing my guns. I will sometimes switch back to melee just for some variety, but I feel the majority of enemies you come across are not really a threat. I will try amping up the difficulty in the future.A glitch, I think! I tried to switch tribes once I was able to, but I was not allowed. They were not my rival, but I was not permitted to switch tribes, which disappointed me. I hope it's just a glitch because I have seen videos of switching tribes being done, but that was my experience.Overall: I really love Biomutant. It might be one of my new favorite games, I haven't completed it yet but I am loving every moment I spend playing it. I love finding new things, becoming stronger. If you want a game that has good third-person combat, this is the game for you! If you like open world games with puzzle solving, this is the game for you! If you like crafting, looking cute and cool, this is your game! I am a long-time fan of THQ Nordic, Darksiders 2 has been my favorite game for years and this game I feel is exactly the type of game that I have been looking for. I wanted to play it since it was announced and I was interested in the years waiting for it to come out! And now that it's here, I am super happy with. I am just blown away that such a small team was able to make such a great game! They are truly talented and I love the final product. I can see now why so many years were needed to finish it, I can see all of their hard work paying off as I play.I hope my review helped you, and if it convinced you to buy the game, then please do! Support the devs!

_childDocuments_.review: There are a lot of mixed reviews for this, and I'll admit there were a few things I wasn't thrilled about at first. The storytelling could be better, especially with several "flashback" segments meant to provide some backstory to your character. I also don't really like how you are reduced to either the "light" or "dark" end goal. But as I've progressed a bit through the game, it's isn't much different than a "light side" or "dark side" theme that would feel fine in a Star Wars game. There are certain psionic abilities that you will be required to have a "light" or "dark" rank to unlock. So far, it has felt pretty natural playing a neutral or balanced role. The narration thing is unique, to say the least. I kinda like the David Attenborough feel to it. Hearing the little furry creatures speaking in their own language adds to the immersion of being in a post-human, anthropomorphized furry critter world. The more I think about it, having English character voiceovers coming from CGI stuffed animals probably would have felt a little more Disney/Pixar than I'd have liked, so it was a cool creative choice in my opinion that probably allowed for more budget options in different departments and spared us the agony of sub-par voice acting.  The combat took a little getting used to. The targeting system could be better. You don't really have the ability to lock onto an enemy or control your targeting very much. You basically target whatever enemy you are aimed at. As I've gotten more used to it, there is more of a natural feel to the combat than I had at first. I can't help but compare it to the Darksiders combat (because that is what I was playing before installing Biomutant, not because of any specific similarities) and while Darksiders had really satisfying combat and targeting, I couldn't help but notice that with Darksiders the enemies will tend to hold back and let me finish certain combos rather than attack often. Biomutant doesn't do that. Your enemies will attack whether you're in the middle of trying to combo their ally or not. Maybe that is partly because I'm playing Darksiders on Nomal, I believe, and selected Hard for Biomutant, but it is something I appreciate about the Biomutant combat either way. Some people might prefer having that bit of pause from enemies so you can do cool combos, but I really like that the Biomutant enemies are actually trying to kill me and not just hanging around for target practice. There are obviously bugs and flaws to the AI, but overall the combat is both challenging and satisfying once you get used to it and unlock the special moves used to charge the Wung-Fu system. Basically certain moves, which you have to unlock for each weapon style as you level up, will charge your Wung-Fu ability if you land them correctly. Once you land 3 (you have to vary them, you can't just spam the same move) you can activate Wung-Fu mode which is basically a few seconds of being able to do several special moves like a super combo, or firing your gun at a dramatically increased rate, driving enemies into the ground by bouncing on their heads, or flying up and smashing down with AOE shockwaves.  It can be decisive in small fights, but will not finish off bigger enemies or larger battles in one go.  The mutation mechanic is a bit less involved than I expected. It basically just unlocks special combat moves like shooting a green bioattack missile or spawning a mushroom that enemies bounce on (actually way cooler than it sounds, especially if you bounce on it with them as you can do a massive melee air combo). I think there is supposed to be more to it as I think you eventually encounter bio-pools that will actually change morphology to some extent. There are definitely things I haven't progressed to yet, like the mech and other vehicles. That's probably because my play style is to do a bunch of exploring before reluctantly following any main quest lines when I have the option, which fortunately you do in this game. The crafting had a mild learning curve. It took me a little while to understand what components I was missing in order to craft a gun, but once I understood what the different component types were, it is very straight forward. You can craft weapons from scratch, or attach add-on components to buff stats. You can also use a crafting table to upgrade the quality or materials. Crafting for armor/clothing is basically the same. Overall, the customization options and aesthetic to costumes and weapons are pretty great. The world and exploration is where the game really shines. The graphics aren't anywhere near photorealistc by any standard, but the environments are truly gorgeous, and given the mild eco-warrior theme to the story, there is a really nice balance of natural beauty and the post-civilization remnants of a forgotten world. The narrator has funny names for stuff like microwaves and toilets which serve as puzzles to unlock special loot. The environmentalist message is there, of course, but it's not so heavy-handed that it feels like you're having political BS shoved down your throat. It's mostly a sort of "matter-of-fact" approach to "the old world was interesting and its inhabitants made some strange choices" explanation for the abandoned cities or the landfill or biowaste biomes (both of which will require buffing resistances with special suits to visit typically). TL;DR - I think the game has a lot more going for it than what it's gotten credit for so far. It's far from a flawless game, and like any new release has a few bugs. But they aren't Cyberpunk 2077 level bugs, and the overall experience is a great balance between world exploration, character building, crafting, engaging combat, and a "mild sauce" weak, but not that weak story. It will forever be in the shadow of much better open-world RPGs from much bigger studios, but it hands-down outshines plenty of other games from the genera that were solid, enjoyable games in themselves.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite how incredibly rough this game is right now, I still can enjoy it quite a bit.Beyond the performance issues, nothing in the game seems thoroughly explored or done incredibly well. It seems that they had so many good ideas all at one time, but didn't fully deliver on any of them. It is shallow in all regards, but still enjoyable. The combat is quirky and fun, looting is intriguing (weird looking items, crafting potential) and... that's about it. The core game-play is engaging, but the elements that KEEP you playing and engaged are what's weak.The story is very plain, with every line of every interesting character being watered down by the narrator. In fact, every piece of information or dramatic dialogue is delivered by the narrator. It starts off as quirky and a bit fun, but quickly becomes terrible as moments that are supposed to be profound/emotional are just... read like a bad audio book.If that's not bad enough, the animations and cut scenes can often make these over the top, Oddworld-esque characters look stiff and inorganic. Recycled character animations, characters popping in and out of the blue... it's jarring and ruins the immersion. It makes them feel more like placeholders than characters.On a side note and while this may just be me, the responsiveness and lack of audio response for certain actions sometimes irks me. When you hit an enemy, you often don't get a meaty chunky TWAK when you hit an enemy. You have to look at the health bar to know your attack just wiped them out. It feels really wrong, and makes any attack feel very... floaty and wispy. It plays like an old PSOne or PS2 game. It doesn't fully realize everything it does, but has solid framework to build upon. While it is a singleplayer game and likely won't be, it still is an enjoyable experience. But wait to pick it up for like, $29.99. As it is currently, it's 100% not worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: Just leaving this review here as a placeholder for now, due to many people perhaps unfairly slating the game without investing much time into it. I am finding it enjoyable: exploration is fun in a world filled with wacky creatures, interesting terrain and wonderful views. A lot of effort has clearly gone into this title to differentiate it from its’ similar sandbox peers in terms of the aesthetic and writing. The narrator can get a bit much, such as announcing the very short day and night cycles constantly – however, you can turn down the narration frequency or turn it completely off in the options menus. Overall I wouldn’t say the narration bothers me or is grating in any way, occasionally breaking immersion when set at 100%.Visually it makes me nostalgic for games like Crash Bandicoot or Spyro the Dragon – it could be the palette or weird creatures. Gameplay is good fun, I’m level 11 at the moment and have a good range of skills, weapons, abilities and mounts: it creates quite a tailor-made and diverse playstyle. There is a wealth to explore here in terms of environments, enemy types and gear. Combat is fun, fluid but tends to feel quite repetitive after a while. The game is polished on release, which is not something to take for granted these days unfortunately, I haven’t run into any major bugs. If anything I’d say that a wider audience would be reached if the price tag was a reasonable $40 over a very cheeky $60. _childDocuments_.review: Well, unfortunately, this game seems pretty underpolished. I'll just bullet what I didn't appreciate here and you can look through and see if any of these are deal-breakers. Hopefully they'll release updates relatively soon and fix some of these issues, but regrettably, many of the issues are with the content.> Cutsceenes are jarring; the animation into and out of cutsceenes break immersion by wholly interrupting any current animations or circumstances of the surrounding area> The dialogue is incredibly slow. Although you can pace through manually, you'd otherwise have to wait for a 1 - 5 second blurb of Banjo-Kazooie-like babbling before a narrator tells you the INTERPRETATION of the dialogue, as opposed to translating it. Only in one underexplained case are characters voiced in English, and those characters are pretty annoying (trying too hard to be comedic)> Lots of the dialogue doesn't make sense, or flow. I'm not sure but it may either a case of hyper-affectedness, or bad translation.> SPOILER: Some dialogue doesn't make contextual sense, for example, you can save random citizens from a rival village who are due to be executed by their military, and afterwards, they'll say what a shame it is you didn't join the very tribe that was about to kill them.> The boilerplate dialogue to end generic npc interactions is nonsense.> The combat primer is way too fast to be made good use of. Mechanics are poorly explained in the 'tutorial' level.> Dialogue options and responses thereto are generally... nonsensical. They certainly don't flow like a normal conversation in many cases.> Too many made-up, unrooted names for varied facets of the story/world/objects make for a cheap-feeling plot and experience. Imagine how grade-school writers begin by writing a fantasy story: with little/no context and lots of obviously 'alien' sounding names, or; imagine rebranding LOtR, Harry Potter or the Wheel of Time but calling every creature, mundane object or other such fact-of-the-world according to some random-name-generator.> Aside from having too many combat mechanics that aren't explained well (or that we aren't give the option of practicing), the combat flow and difficulty is way out-of-whack. Enemies your size are numerous and just as hard to kill as giant 'boss' enemies, but much harder to avoid or address because you're ganked from all sides.> Neither is the combat system well-rooted in the story, so far as that exists.> 95% of the combat is scripted in the first few hours I played. Unscripted combat doesn't seem to be random-encounter combat, either. >The fur textures look like impossibly thin faux feathers, even sprites.>Re: the story and dialogue... well, you're given so little explanation or chance to flow naturally from one question to another. One of the most pivotal characters in your backstory just suddenly appears, hints at no intimate relationship with you, gets annoyed at you, and doesn't even swim to save you as you drown together.> Honestly I'm finding it really hard to get over just how sloggish and undetailed all the story and dialogue is, despite that this is an open-world game.There's a lot more to say, yes, even in just a few hours of gameplay. It could get better, not sure. But I wouldn't buy it at this point; certainly not for its price. All that said, and despite some animation and graphic qualms *not* related to the content of the story, it IS a pretty gorgeous and well-styled game. *****I think the studio must have spent a fortune on artists and nearly nothing on writers.***** Really, it feels like a gorgeous Chineese-apocalyptic reskin of Fallout with a gutted story, cumbersome mechanics and arbitrary classic RPG elements.I'm really let down by this game, but since it's just been released, I hope it'll be cleaned up significantly so I can play it again. I can imagine it being a lot more fun if the story and interactions were more cleaned up, and some more explained and polished mechanics were introduced.

_childDocuments_.review: The game took about 3 hours or so to get interesting, and I don't mean just the tutorial part. The entire starting area feels empty but after crossing the river and entering Bricktown (I think the name was) the game actually opens up and starts to feel like an open world game. I've ran into more quests than I can keep up and have enjoyed exploring the map so far. I was thinking a 6/10, but after a couple more hours it's at least an 8 so far from me. Is it amazing? No, I personally think games like Oblivion/Skyrim gave a lot more for exploration but I still find this game quite fun. I have very much enjoyed punching things with a rocket fist to death!Some more details I guess for anyone that may be interested, based off the 6 hours I have while writing this and 4% completion rate starting with the good.[Good]-I love this world it's so beautiful to explore and everytime you enter a new biome it feels and looks very different.-I know a lot of people seem to hate the combat but I love it. It's more on the simple side which, as someone with little action-rpg experience, I appreciate. But yes, there's maybe like 5-6 combos or so but honestly trying new weapons is fun in this game.-Crafting feels fun, with the ability to switch out parts like fallout 4 for new elements/effects.-Map feels big, which I appreciate even if the open exploration is a average/above average at best.-Enemy variety seems to be pretty high, and even older enemies come back in new ways at times so it feels nice being surprised with a new obstacle in combat.-Performance. I barely meet the min requirements and I've still had consistent FPS, besides a few noticable dips for a second or two every now and then (Prolly from my PC being on the low end with a GTX 960 Lol).-Story has me interested, it's less childish than the graphics may make it seem. Had me feeling sad at parts. So far I'm very interested.[Neutral]-Narrator is nice at first but they relied too heavily on him imo. He speaks randomly as you explore/idle, as you fight, as you do things and every single NPC dialogue. You can turn him down thankfully, but I feel they should have left him voice the story and general stuff but not NPCs and literally everything else too. I find myself reading subtitles and skipping him during NPC dialogue. Don't hate him though.-Open world is average/above average at best. There's moments where it's really nice, like activating a giant radar dish to pick up old transmissions or something to discover a new quest. But mostly it boils down to fighting random enemies for some quick loot or a brawl between NPC factions. So far, anyways. If I had to rate the open world by itself I would say a 7/10 at most. As in stuff to do and see, but nothing amazing or remarkable (besides the sights) so far.-Character Creator is... interesting. I'm not really for or against it though but it feels like the character editor is very basic and ties your looks into your stats. As a person who just wants a cute little furry I left my stats on default just for a look I like XP But in all seriousness it doesn't feel like it lets you be creative with your looks. I've heard stats don't matter, but I don't know how true or not that is. If so, can disregard this.-Your Good and Evil conscience. Maybe nitpicking here but their chatter gets cringe at times Lol.[Bad]-Game throws a lot at you tutorial wise in the beginning, I think. 6 hours later I honestly don't remember everything it said.-Puzzles so far are very basic and even when they're introducing a new puzzle... it's just a different way to do the same puzzles you've already been doing.In summary I think someones comment I read perfectly fits this. That, gameplay wise, the game is great but unremarkable in its greatness. It's fun, and I expect to play this game a lot, just don't go in expecting some 10/10. For a small and inexperienced studio though I think they made an excellent game so far. I have not fought a worldeater yet or ventured into an extreme biome since I still lack the gear and I've barely left the bottom part of the map but so far I give this game a solid 8/10, will be enjoying it a lot more at this rate ^^

_childDocuments_.review: Biomutant is an open world, action combat game, with a large amount of story and rudimentary gameplay.It can feel a little like a young persons game, with a naration style that is not too distant from watching a tv episode of Pocoyo (UK tv).The gameplay loop is such - explore, loot, craft, fight etc - with a nice array of mounts, gadgets, "spells" and weaponry to keep you constantly trying something new. The enemy types are varied, but similiar in nature - with alternate versions of colors and armors.The map is large, and full of interesting locations - some requiring resistances or gear to traverse and explore.Pros:You can play as you wish - creating your character isnt the final step - you can switch to swords or guns or magic at any point and play viably.  However, if you want to specialise, you can, and the gear supports this.Theres LOTS to find and explore.  This isnt a small game - you will be here for hours exploring.  If you get sidetracked easily, this is one of those games.  The music and sounds are pleasant, the animal gibberish is cute and the narrator is very chatty.  I did turn him off after a while however, but many love him.Controls are easy to use, hard to master - combos for fighting CAN be used, but if you cant use them, you dont get punished for it.Cons:The narrator is VERY chatty.  Its very childlike at times (ping pingety ping ping!) and sounds like a childrens program.  The story is quite complex in places, and the backstory is interesting.  I get vibes from MANY games, and i feel that some of them have been stolen slightly to make this game more interesting to many people.Its not always immediatly obvious how to work the inventory.  Items are not highlighted very clearly, and its perfectly possible to accidently sell everything you are wearing because its not obvious your wearing it.You can accidently sell or dismantle things because there isnt a 2nd "are you sure" option on legendary or ultimate items.  This is BAD.I got motion sickness from this - something i dont normally suffer from - i recommend a high FOV, and motion blur turned on to counter it.  I never use motion blur normally, but i believe the bright garish colors and fast movement cause it.Some things arent explained - if you complete a certain quest, you CANNOT go to some areas and aquire certain items.  This could do with a better explanation.  I get that it breaks game immersion, but a quest i got at the start of the game that i finished early locking me out of many sets of weapons and armor feels annoying.Rating:8/10Borrows heavily from many other game sources, to deliver a game thats many things all at once, that forgives alot of mistakes, has alot of content and alot of cuteness.  I like this game, because i can do anything i want - and ive got alot of room to do it - im not limited to "this power means this armor ONLY" etc. Id like a closer camera angle but more to the side to alleviate motion sickness, but thats my only annoyance so far.

_childDocuments_.review: This was the game that convinced me to build a PC. Offt! That's a big statement!I had this pre-ordered and I knew that I wanted to experience this in the best way possible - that was purely on the hype I heard. The graphics and story had me hooked before I even laid eyes on the game itself.Fast forward a few years...In all honesty, I'm now on my second attempt at this game. _childDocuments_.review: I play a ton of games, but I rarely review them here, but felt like I had to say something because people are review bombing this game, and I can't figure out why... granted it has a slow start where you're pretty weak.  Enemies feel bullet spongey for the first 2-3 hours, and your melee hits are pitiful until you start getting upgrades and understand/learn how to craft, and then combat is vastly improved and feels much more rewarding.  Once you reach mid game, the exploration and crafting systems start to open up to you more.  There are plenty of scavenging opportunities and side quests to do to make exploration worth it; especially when crafting/upgrading items is very powerful.  Planning out and building your character and equipment really matters.  Combat could be a little better, but works well enough and is rewarding if you actually learn and execute the attack combos and special moves rather than spam clicking.  I suspect many players with few hours were just spamming attacks and brute forcing their way through combat by chewing through consumables, which isn't that fun or interesting (because that's what I did for the first few hours).  But once you get the hang of it (and once that tactic stops being viable) character movement is fast and fluid and you're able to do some pretty cool things in combat.   The complaint that the game visually looks bad are just silly, you can see in the screenshots and videos how it looks its a very pretty game, sure, certainly not groundbreaking, but good enough that its not distracting from the experience.  I've also encountered no bugs or frame rate drops you'd get in a poorly optimized or unfinished game.  The only really valid complaint, that maybe bothers others more than me is the decision to have 2 different VO lines for all of the NPC dialog, the subtitles should appear DURING the gibberish language the animals speak, instead of waiting for the narrator's VO.  The way it's currently done, I'm skipping all of the gibberish VO, waiting for the subtitle and then just reading that before skipping again.  Because the conversations just take too long w/ too much downtime otherwise.  I agree it was a bad decision, but it's a minor annoyance you can work around, and isn't worth tanking the entire game over.  There are far worse open world/exploration games on steam that are reviewed/recommended higher than this.  There are terrible early access exploration/survival games that will probably never be finished recommended higher than this on steam. So why is this getting such a negative response?  Is it a 9 or 10/10 game?  No.  But it's fun, it's well made, and doesn't run like garbage.  That should at least be easy positive review.  Have some patience to let the game establish itself, and you might actually enjoy it.

_childDocuments_.review: There are a lot of down votes for this game that I just don't understand. Yes, the narrator gets annoying after the first couple hours. However you can turn him off for the most part in the options menu. (this of course isn't told to you until at least 50% of the way through the game) The game itself is beautifully done, I played mine on ultra so I could even make out individual hairs in the fur of the characters. Combat is smooth if a bit repetitive and there are plenty of busy quests to keep you exploring and finding new areas. It's a good game, and if you can catch it at 50% off (or better) worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: CONS:Story:There's so much potential here, the designs and the fighting style are so interesting. However, the game will force you to spend hours in boring, surface-level conversations with characters that you simply can't get invested in. You just decide that you're either a good or bad character from the first mission, there's no in between. The "tribe war" doesn't really feel like an on-going event that happens while you're not around. Pretty much everything to do with the story is rather thin and never fleshed out. There are so many funny quirky names, places and ideas in the world that elude to a living, breathing environment that seem like they may have interesting backstories, but most of it isn't explored.The game's story moves so slowly and makes you watch so many cutscenes and flashbacks. I've after 2 hours of playing the  game, and I still felt like I was doing tutorials. I don't need a whole 20 minute flashback mission to teach me how gear upgrades and searching trash piles works, perhaps just a pop-up when I'm near a trash pile or something. This isn't a complicated mechanic, the game does this with most of its learning opportunities.Graphics/Animations:When entering and leaving short cut-scenes like when your character opens and door or when you're watching your character doing an action, your model can snap back to its normal position when returning to play. Or when an NPC goes from one animation such as running or creeping to another like walking, they sometimes snap with no transition. There are lots of other weird cut-scene and model animation inconsistencies that happen, these are just two. After while these small things can build up and make you feel like the game isn't finished. If you've seen gameplay and watched cutscenes, something just seems a bit, off... It certainly doesn't feel like a game that came out this year.I also found that even when the draw distance is set to maximum, far objects are sill rendered with a really low polygon count, my PC is pretty strong and I think I increasing the max draw distance would make looking out on the landscape so much better. When at a high place, even on maximum draw distance, the environment has a low poly count and it's not very pretty to look at. These things could most likely be fixed with future patches, but without a guarantee of this I'd say I cannot recommend the game yet.Some areas such as indoor spaces feel empty and lifeless and don't feel "lived-in". There are vast areas with almost nothing interesting in them, entire woodland forests with just... trees...Missions:The structure of most missions is similar, they feel very grindy and aren't very engaging. Most of them involve talking to NPCs as well, and as stated before these conversations are surface-level and can take very long if you actually want to understand the story. You're almost punished for wanting to know more about this world, then when you spend the time, you aren't rewarded. The biggest thing I'd say that is wrong with the questing in this game are the tutorials, the game is so slow to start with, you're just dropped into this world and dragged through slow, boring cutscenes and very obvious, unsubtle game mechanic lessons. Feel like I'm studying a university degree with all this reading I have to do.PROS:Graphics:The game has fairly good graphical quality at max settings at close range. Considering the vast variety of different unique enemies and environments, the poly count is and detail of all of these places is pretty high on average. Most buildings and items through design and name appear to have unique and interesting aesthetics. But as I stated before, the actual history and story this world doesn't meld with these cool ideas.Enemies:Some of the enemy designs I believe are truly brilliant, the worldeaters look very cool and although the average enemy you fight isn't that interesting, the boss fights can be pretty cool (although chipping down a health bar isn't that engaging, the actual attacks and flow of the fights themselves is fun). Honestly, from a design aspect most of this game is genius, but it just doesn't save the game when seen as a whole.Overall I'd say that Biomutant doesn't feel finished and should perhaps have been delayed until animation quirks and story-writing had been fleshed out. There are games that were released years ago that do better than this game in almost every aspect, the main hook of Biomutant is the design, kung-fu aesthetic, combat and serotonin grind. Games like Borderlands (grind), The Witcher 3 (story), and Dark Souls (Skilled Gameplay, not stat-based) all do better than Biomutant in their respective aspects and more. Until Experiment 101 do some big changes, I'd say stay away for now, but keep an eye on it.

_childDocuments_.review: Think of Elder scrolls done right (looking at you Bethseda),toss in the end of all humans and replaced with a crazy mix of furry mutated animals, you got the protagonist that is a mutated furry. Trying to save there little part of the world from collapsing and throw alittle reclaimed tech, a tiny dash of Dark Souls combat, and Biomutant is what you get. How the terrain is varied, with no two places looking exactly the same. the terrain itself has verticality from the highest reachable point to the lowest reaches you can even break down certain walls with what I can best descibe as a power fist with mini thrusters connected to it (although I wish the more things were breakable) and It plays smooth. one of the few products that I can say is "NES cart ready" there might be some minor bug (nothing game breaking), but the game overall was properly done from start to finish with proper QAQC (quality assurance and quality control) before it was released. This is something us as gamers has been asking for, for god knows how long. This is one of those game you can get lost in for hours. as I played from install time till i went to bed. Very few games do that these days for me and to see something like this be made shows there are devs out there that actually care about there product and not let the bean counters take control of the project. This is a must buy in my book as I can see myself getting lost in this game for hours if not days weeks or even months. The character creation system is simple but when you creating your character how you distribute your stats changes your character's initial look and character progression comes in the form of leveling up and increasing your "Aura" to access special skills or fighting certain mobs or finding canisters with "bio sludge" of sorts which gives you access to skills you can buy and and tokens to purchase new combat skills, (spoiler alert) even the little grasshopper buddy can be upgraded to do various things. Gear customizing system is simple but well developed, you can build,modify or break-down the  various parts you find in the world, or buy them which leads me to the NPC vendors.The Market system in this game is somewhat different. Vendors have basic items and some gear but if you sell thing to them it shows up in that specific shop which you can purchase with leaves (or i think that is what it is) as currency in this game, you get for defeating or helping other mutated humanoid creatures or finding special leaf plants or from stashes found littered across the world. This is all i have for now as I am still grinding through the world discovering things also there are some areas you cannot explore without the proper gear as the area's is too harsh for your character to survive in. which is fine by me. All the more reason to go out and explore this world the devs have made.

_childDocuments_.review: ✅  Impressively made by a 20 person dev team✅  Major patch released just six days after release day. Not a late day one patch, but an update that addressed some of the biggest bugs and fan complaints of the game. The speed of this update is unprecedented, and shows how much the devs really listen to their audience.✅ Top-tier graphics and performance at a stable 60 FPS. Photo Mode lets you bask in the environment around you✅  Big and beautiful open world. I'm at 25 hours and taking my time on my first playthrough. My progress is at 8% according to the in-game Completion% and I feel like I have so much more ahead of me.✅ Customizing your character and selecting their perks is really fun. Innate aspects of your character can be changed after character creation later in the game, but there is no option to respec your perks. That's ok.🟨  I can't put my tongue on it, but the combat leaves a bit to be desired. Combat is for me, really one of the best parts of the game. I feel incentivized to fight every enemy I see. It's fun unlocking new Wung-Fu and other special attacks. But I give the combat an "ok" for "more of this please". More enemies, more combos, more ways to defend yourself against gunfire and ranged attacks besides having high agility would be super.🟥 Story really leaves something to be desired. As far as I know, the only voice acting is the Narrator and two NPCs you are introduced to in the tutorial and that later show up from time to time. Often times I wonder why the team didn't hire voice actors, because I thought they would have fit in just well. The Narrator though is cheeky, so he'll suffice.The game isn't for everyone for sure. Those still on the fence should wait for a sale. This is really the game for me though and I can't wait to hear and see more from this new developer in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Ah, so these are the adventures of Rocket before he met Groot. It looks like the Dark Souls of Ratchet and Clank.In reality it’s like Kung Fu Panda meets Fallout. It really makes you FEEL like a Biomutant.It’s a great game that’s not perfect. I felt like people have been overly negative. The world is fun to explore, the RPG character stuff is great, combat is fun but not hard. I didn’t mind the story, some people think it’s meh. I wanted to enjoy the narrator, but it got annoying for me, thankfully there are a plethora of options including changing the language, frequency or toggling it on and off. TBH I just wanted to hear the narrator say goofy things for as long as possible. I enjoyed the repetition, I’m weird like that.The game has a lot of flaws, particularly in regards to the storytelling, but I compensate for that by immersing myself in my character and imagining a slightly more personal narrative. Other than that, it is shallow but absolutely dripping with charm and a unique style that you can’t find anywhere else. If you need to be really invested in the story to like the game, maybe this isn't for you. But if you'll enjoy this world of wonky creatures after humans ruined the planet and you'll like the combat/crafting loop, this game is totally worth it.My favorite aspect of the game are the side quests, but it’s best going in blind. For me it is a great game. It's one of the best I've played in awhile, I haven't put it down since I got it and I think about it all the time. I have different tastes then some though I also thought Dragons Dogma and Kingdoms of Amalur were fantastic games, it feels similar to those titles. Big but still indie.I’ve enjoyed it for what it is, a fun sandbox to run around as a mutated rodent, build cool stuff and meet cute critters. People take it way too serious and thats why they are disappointed with it.Biomutant begs the question… Can any small team make a smash hit open world RPG like Fallout New Vegas? The answer is no, but its fun as f*ck to strap literal garbage to your character and role play as your average rat from New York. So I say wait for it to go on sale and then go wild.Better question is, are you worth it for Biomutant?10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Im very neutral on the game, Although i have been enjoying it enough. The beginning / tutorial is pretty painstaking and boring and when you think you're done theres essentially another tutorial. They make you do these quick time events somewhat often that force you to spam one button to open a door or dig through trash which feels really pointless. the narrator is either loved or hated but it really makes dialog very annoying to interact with because you have to hear the NPC speak gibberish for a few seconds then wait for the narrator or text to pop up to read (yes you can mute the narrator but it made the dialog very strange feeling like something was missing). This could of been WAY WAY better if they used a more gritty or serious tone rather than a man reading me a bedtime story to contrast with the almost childish nature of the game if they were to take an approach like bastion from supergiant it would of been actually incredible.  the combat is Fun but clunky and often times the camera angle and hectic mechanics make it feel like you were going to get hit regardless of what you do to avoid it. I think bigger / brighter markers showing what the enemies are about to do ( on the small mobs not the bosses) would be a great improvement because currently they are tiny grey lighting bolts over their head that are hard to see in an extremely vibrant and flashy world, guns and ranged really do feel a little too good making it hard not to kite even bosses and just blast them to death (although a melee only playthrough is possible). The exploration and general feel of the game is completely incredible wit ha story that so far is pretty lackluster (clear good vs clear evil make a decision 30 minutes in). The character design is very cool but can feel cluttered on your own character. i think a sequel can do this game wonders, throw me into a world that i must learn, let me discover a story rather than have it kinda spoon fed to me. Clean up the combat. Although i basically complained this whole review (and have a lot more to say) i for some reason still really do love the charm and want to keep exploring the world.

I never write reviews but thought Biomutant deserved some good press. 4/5 stars
