_childDocuments_.review: To start off this review - yes, I've only put an hour and a half into this game. This is because I intend to refund it, but don't take it as a negative sign. I chose to buy this game to see how it was, leave a review, and possibly refund - there are games I think would be a better money sink, but don't take my word for it. BIOMUTANT is a game where reviews are going to be wildly over the place. This might be the most subjective game of all time.Also, I played with an Xbox 360 Controller. I usually do with these kind of games.From what I'm reading, this game isn't necessarily getting horrible reviews. Most of the negative reviews are actual criticisms that I, personally, agree with. The combat is repetitive and somewhat boring, the little puzzles I found are a bit easy, but remember that this is Experiment 101's first game, and of COURSE it's going to have flaws. This game holds promise, however, since I have enjoyed what little time I've sinked in. I don't mind repetitive games, whether it be in combat or in exploration, but something about the combat does feel hollow. This may be a positive review, but let's start with my biggest complaints.Biomutant's storytelling method is a great way to move around the inability to access multiple voice actors. The narrator's voice comes straight out of a documentary, which is great! ...for some aspects of the game. I like the narrator telling you the general outline of the initial story, but as soon as I met my first NPC I immediately did NOT like that the narrator describes the gist of what one person is saying. A better solution would be drawing inspiration from a game series like Zelda and use chat boxes, rather then having the narrator describe how a person feels. Even in chat boxes and physical emoting, one can get a sense of how a character feels and reacts, whereas having someone else tell you kind of breaks the immersion a bit.My second complaint boils down to a couple of things - mainly, the flawed combat. Whereas I found it exhilarating to be a lil' squirrel-racoon hybrid and start blasting a couple of guys with my pistol, I felt the combat of this game could definitely use some polishing. The fact that I have to swing my camera around as much as I did feels unnecessary, and could easily be fixed with some lock-onto-target system. Maybe there is one later? I don't know, but adding one is maybe the deciding factor as to whether I'll pick up this game again.THIS GAME HAS MANY IDEAS, BUT IT'S FLAWS ARE IN-YOUR-FACE.BIOMUTANT is a promising game, one that could be fixed in a couple of patches. BIOMUTANT's biggest seller? By god is the environment gorgeous. Even in the one and a half hour playing I would say that this game maybe has the best environment of ANY game I've played so far. Below is a list of Pros.PROS.-Great Environment and beautiful scenery, which does not punish and in fact rewards you for taking it all in.-All the models in this game are unique, wondrous, and nothing like we've seen before. This severely impacts the combat.-While the combat is hollow, the combos you can do mixed with a gunslinging style makes you feel impactful and stylish.-Character Creator? Maybe the best I've seen in a game! It's not Cyberpunk's over-the-top creator, but maybe that's better!-Great controls that feel natural to play with, instead of jamming too much moves into one controller. However, could use a couple of reworks to fit newer mechanics, but that's just nitpicks.-If they had to go with the storytelling method they did, it could have been done better. But, the narrator does an extremely good job at his voice acting.-I found connections in the melee combat to those in Kingdoms of Amalur, which is fun. The adaption makes it even better. I found melee combat way more fun then ranged combat, but there is a con I have with it.-Oh boy, did I not expect the comic book style of this game AT ALL. The story is comedic, with the occasional comic book sounds coming out or your gun (Klink! When you reload). This was an EXTREMELY pleasant surprise, which really got me when you meet a person called Best-Before. Sorta spoilers, sorta not.CONS.-Storytelling method just HAS to be changed. The biggest thing about open world games is that they introduce so much land, but it all feels hollow when there are no NPC's to talk to and connect to. Zelda-Style chat boxes would definitely lent me a mile in rating this game.-Combat feels clunky and repetitive. Against multiple enemies, this doesn't shine through too much, but in one-on-ones I end up just holding the left analog stick left or right and holding the right trigger, which is ranged. Not too mention that I have to swing my camera around WAY too much.-Ranged Combat is infinitely better then Melee combat, which sucks. I chose to play a gunslinger, and I found it to be mostly holding the ranged attack button while there is a couple of quick reloads you can make. Melee combat felt fun, fast paced, and involves parrying and dodging with right timing.-The story tries too hard to be comedic in some places, and honestly this isn't exactly special to this game. Borderlands 2 did this, Fable sort of did this, etc. What we need from comedy is for it too be well paced, and not even necessarily 'comedic'. Darksiders Genesis, one of my favourite games of all time, does it's comedy between Strife and War VERY well. This game just kind of shoves it in and hopes we don't cringe TOO hard. Or, at least, I cringed hard. That might be a bit more of a personal thing.Overall,BIOMUTANT suffers from a lack of mechanics, but makes it up for a wide open world of exploration and wonder. The open questline to four different areas takes a major leaf from Breath of the Wild's book, but that isn't exactly a bad thing. In fact, I kinda of wish there were more then four areas to go to.If I were to give this a score out of ten, I might go somewhere along the lines of 7/10, with it's potential going to around 9/10. I hope Experiment 101 and THQNordic don't give up on this game, besides the negative reviews, because this hold promise. Right now? This is the game I might buy i again if it's on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Biomutant is a game unlike any other I have played before, and I mean that in a good way. Biomutant is a beautiful and charming post apocalyptic and mutated open world action RPG. The world has a spirit and pulse which embodies Kung Fu, magic, crazy weapons and other unique game play elements. These elements all add up to be an enjoyable game albeit some setbacks such as repetition in questing, lacking a deep meaningful story, and mediocre at best narration. The open world is a good sized map with colorfully diverse terrain and plenty of locations to explore and loot. The graphics are amazing, the world is detailed and characters pop into life with vibrant colors and textures. There are many character models in this game. NPC's and enemies are diverse and have their own distinct look and feel to them. The combat is fast, fun, and you have a wide array of weapons, magic, mutant abilities, and combinations to defeat the enemy. It's hard not to smile while you are flying around  swashbuckling enemies with cool Kung Fu combos blending chaos and elegance in combat. There are plenty of magic abilities and fighting combinations to be utilized, and a ridiculous amount of customization when it comes to melee/ranged weapons and armor. The world is filled with loot which helps you craft your arsenal and armor. The playful design of the game gives you a sense of place in this odd but magical world. There are a lot of quests and side quests however they do become repetitive after time and are not the most impactful. The story is light hearted and easy to follow however the narration feels not genuine. Also the dialogue between the NPC seems unnecessary at times and drawn out. Overall I enjoyed Biomutant despite some setbacks. You wont find a game similar out there and for what the games does do well its worth checking out at a discounted price. Score: 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: (11 hours in) I'm a person that usually try to enjoy the games I play instead of chasing bad things to point out so keep that in mind when reading this.I'm having an amazing experience with the game, here are some considerations if you are in doubt of buying it or not:-Prologue / Tutorial (2hrs) has a very slow pace and can be quite annoying, makes sense in a way cause the game has a ton of mechanics.- The narrator has a unique  "documentary" vibes, that at first is not clear it's supposed to be like that, so you may feel like, "wow this narrator shows almost no emotion" / "is this some disney stuff?", but after playing for a while you understand how it is and you may start to like it (the frequency of how much the narrator keeps talking is annoying, but you can lower that in settings and then you can set a perfect amount that keeps the vibe and don't overload you with phrases)-dialogs, OOF, this part is probably the one that I didn't like, they are veeeery long and slow paced, usually I read/ listen everything that the npcs have to say but this one is hard to digest, every sidequest has a long dialog, with some madeup words that very often you fail to understand if you are not 100% focused (which is especially hard when streaming and keeping up with chat)-gameplay: after the prologue the game gets a totally different pace, which for me, became AWESOME! the combat system is superfast and with a nice variety of movements depending on how you want to play.The fact that you have RPG stats to affect "meele/magic" damage AND can still use guns with every class without having to worry about "should I put point on STR or shooting ability" is amazing, cause the gun dmg is based on crafting and perks, not on stats that you add points from leveling up (as far as I know)- the craft system is amazing, allowing you to create some unique weird weapons- weapon (melee and ranged) selection / quick item selection / skill activation while in combat is super user-friendly (playing with mouse and keyboard here)- the visual of the game is stunning, you can spend hours just exploring and looking at the beauty of the world.-soundwise the game is basic, the OST is not involving (as far as I played) so don't expect some EPIC FEELING from the songs, but the relaxing vibe from the open world's song is nice.FOR ME: 8/10A game very fun to play once it starts, that you can go playing for hours with getting stressed or exhausted.If you wanna check my gameplay so far: IAMPEETZ on twitch.

_childDocuments_.review: I would recommend this game with a significant caveat. This game isn't polished, has some GLARING issues and desperately needs some serious TLC for making sure that MNK players have a better time with the skills you can get. Binding the skills options to a middle mouse/scroll wheel click and hold is just bad and the rest of the keyboard mapping isn't much better.Pros:Pretty world, good atmosphere, plenty of side questing to do (which is honestly more interesting than the main story missions), and a flashy aesthetic to combat.Cons:Floaty controls, bad mouse and keyboard mapping with almost no explanation of controls for MNK in the actual tutorial, railroaded introduction to the faction system, blatant vegetarian and eco friendly agendas are force fed to the player in a "You're a terrible person if you sympathize with the carnivores/people that want the tree of life to die" mentality, otherwise poor choices for optimizing moving through the world makes getting to the fun stuff (the side quests mostly) a chore, and finally the crafting system needs a rework ASAP the material requirements to make new weapons are so egregious that Warframe is less of a grind to make what you want. Oh and the light or dark requirements for psi powers? GET RID OF THAT ♥♥♥♥! Yoda can use force lightning and sith can use light side force powers. The arbitrary you have to be evil or good to use these powers is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and I hate it.At the end of the day the reason I recommend this game even with all of its glaring flaws is this.It has potential to be great, it has some really great concepts that developers can learn from, it has outlandish missteps that new developers can learn from, and the RPG elements can be fun. This is not a game I recommend to play for fun, this is a game I recommend to play as a learning experience for what not to do and in some (very niche) cases what to do right.

_childDocuments_.review: 100% Achievements - 49 HoursNot sure where all the hate for this game stems. It's a fun, often times silly RPG that gives nostalgic vibes in the vein of N64/NGC era games' charm. Did a melee playthrough and combat was fun, just smashing away at enemies and occasionally using super wung-fu for big aoe. Story is relatively basic, but there's enough there to be enjoyed, and your decisions do matter. It's just a fun game and I am hoping to see story DLC in the future.As far as complaints or downsides, it's a bit on the short side. Even with 100% achievements and completing every quest I could find besides two (which were bugged for my save), it took 49 hours. As far as bugs go, there's not an unbearable amount. The quests were the only major bugs I encountered, and afaik they've been fixed and are just a byproduct of having a pre-fix save. Edit: I got this game off GMG for $45 pre-order, but would have been happy if I paid full price as well. Would be understandable to wait for a sale, however, due to how short it is.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR This game, bottom line is fun after you break through that initial barrier that is the egregious tutorial and forced story points. Once you're let loose in that world it's guns blazing, building scavenging and cave diving to find that sweet sweet loot that will blow your enemies away.I feel obligated to throw in a positive review because this game truly is jsut something special. This game is a blast, exploration is satisfying, the combat is imo some of the best flowing combat I've experienced, and It's one of the first games to put a genuine smile on my face which I hadn't even thought about until playing it.Now to cut emotion out of the review, the game has some pretty obvious flaws here an there, or at the very least has some features that people greatly disagree upon. One person will say combat is garbage, the next will tell you it's flawless. One person will say the world is empty and uninspired while the next guy in line say's it's imaginative and expansive. These inconsistencies of opinion are the only consistent thing in regards to peoples reception of the game, and they are present from the gameplay all the way down to the price of the game.I should note that there seem to be a lot of reviews that are negative, and a majority of them aren't even past the tutorial, which admittedly is the first point of contingency. It's the opening of the game, it's hand holdy and doesnt let you breathe and it feels like it never ends while you have a beautiful world staring you in the face that you just want to go explore. There are some minor gripes people have which really shouldn't really define how someone feels about this game. Narrator can be turned off or you can change his language. Combat fleshes out the more abilities you unlock, quests are pretty fast and streamlined with picking up new ones and trust me this is the kind of game where you will get netted into like a 100 side quests before remembering theres a story, and those sidequests are rad. I don't actually understand the gripes on the graphics? theyre stellar, and any given screenshot of the game is amazing. Sound design leaves something ot be desired, but the devs have addressed this as a point to improve upon as well as combat flow and world difficulty.One take away I'd like to leave you with, the devs of this game are incredibly commited. They are communicating with us on various platforms and are keeping us in the loop about what theyre working on, and THAT is refreshing. I'd say give the game a chance, do your best to understand how the game feels during it's tutorial and really take your time with it.

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely wouldn't recommend this game, at least at the price it's at currently. Cons:It's just as short as everyone says it is, with lots of side-quests, fetch quests, and random collectables to pad it all out. The shortness wasn't the worst part though - the writing and dialogue are what is truly awful. Everything has these dumb cutesy names, like pianos and guitars are called 'string-plongs' and 'twing-twangs' and the bad guys are named ♥♥♥♥ like 'Porky Puff' and 'Jumbo Puff' - it's hard not to cringe when literally everything in the game is named like this.The very worst part though was the narrator, and tied in with this, is that all the npc's don't have their own voices but just have some weird mumbly, Sims-like language. So the narrator does all the translating for each character, but in that ♥♥♥♥♥♥ way where they can't translate exactly what the person is saying; he just gives you an approximation of what characters are saying with his own bland commentary. This makes every conversation a bore and i couldn't help but skip almost everyone's lines. I have 31 hours in this game and I felt like I was actively avoiding finishing the game - if you just did the main quests and threw in a side quest here and there, you could probably beat this game in like 10~12 hours. 60 dollars is asking way too much for what you're getting. Pros:idk, the combat is great (although you will get knocked out of your attacks constantly, and every attack feels like they lack substance), the crafting is legit great, lots of looting which is fun,  and the world is pretty and huge. Also the music is great, although tracks will start to repeat pretty quickly since it takes forever to get literally anywhere (even with mounts, and even with the speed upgrades) (this is probably just another way that they padded out the game time) Another good thing is that this game didn't crash on me even once, and i only experienced one actual glitch that was easily solved with a save and reload - this felt pretty impressive with how poorly some games run these days. Only get this if you REALLY need another game to scratch the open-world BOTW itch, and only on deep discount

_childDocuments_.review: I have never reviewed a game before because I just like to play and enjoy, however, this game is a unique experience so I wanted to share my thoughts. I was excited to play this game and was really bummed out when I saw all the negative reviews on steam. Do I think they are unwarrented? No. But I think they are specific types of gamers reacting to their expectations of the game, which makes sense. I actually made the decision to get it after watching many video reviews that included game play.Do I think the game is worth $60? No. But I do think this game has entertainment value and shouldn't necessarily be written off for it's short comings completely. I think that when this game goes on sale, many people could have a pleasant experience from it with the right mindset. Now if you are what I would call a more "serious" RPG gamer who enjoys picking the perfect class to make the perfect build, I don't think you will enjoy this game. Outside of a few class specific perks that impact combat on a rather minimal level, class and breed don't really mean much. If you are a more casual gamer who enjoys new experiences, flexibility, crafting, and more relaxed games I think you may find yourself pleasantly surprised by this game. I am more of a casual gamer and tend to only really get serious about certain games and I have had a good time with the game (though I do think it's worth closer to $25-30). Below are my pros and cons. Pros:I like that you can fight with any weapon you want at any given moment. I am a psi freak (focus on abilities aka magic) but I love being able to bonk enemies with a melee weapon if they get close or pew pew them when my energy runs out. I think the world is beautiful and I LOVE the creatures. Most of them are ugly or border on ugly/cute but I get a kick out of that. I love the variety of mounts. There are mounts in each area that are unique to that area. You just need to find a berry for that area and feed it to the mount. There are some genuinely funny moments (like the swimming animation OMG!) and I find myself actually interested in the character's story. There is lots to discover and do if you are patient enough to just check things out!Looting and crafting is super fun to explore and discover.Cons:The dialogue is repetitive and a bit silly at times (sort of stupid silly). I understand that they are going for the vibe that these animals are naming human artifacts but it comes off as goofy. It is true that the narrator translates everything for you and makes random comments but he really didn't bother me as much as the dialogue itself. Choices don't really matter for the story. I like the morality system and the idea of choices but outside of unlocking certain psi abilities based on how light or dark you are, choices don't change game play. The light side choice were usually too fluffy and often didn't result in anything. Example: one citizen asks me to help, I say sure, and end of conversation! That was the light choice. Later a citizen asks for help, I say you're on your own, and proceed to punch the citizen in the face. End of conversation but much more entertaining in my opinion. That was the dark choice. Choosing tribes doesn't really matter except to get tribe armor. You will get tribe weapons by conquering tribes. Some aspects of the game aren't explained super well and some important quests can be easy to miss. I would highly recommend looking up guides before you begin. The world story is confusing and mostly just hits you over the head with environment propaganda.Overall, I think Biomutant is a pleasant experience for the casual gamer who enjoys something new that they can explore and discover. I don't think more serious gamers will enjoy it and I think it's best to add the game to your wishlist and wait for it to go on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to give this game a chance, I really do, but as it currently stands this game just isn't worth the $60, or even $40. It tries too hard to be a deep narrative without being a well written narrative. story feels too forced and unoriginal, tries too much to hold your hand and make everything blatantly obvious, and there's nothing to care for in regards to the characters. The game lacks a clear identity as it tries too hard to be like other openworld RPG games instead of setting out what it was initially suppose to be.The mechanics are a mixed bag. The martial/weapon arts system, as well as the mutations, look a lot of fun but are jank as ♥♥♥♥. The gunplay is very disappointing and feels like more of a "shoot x enemy if you want" yet the reload mechanic is mars any sort of enjoyment you can get out of it unless you choose deadeye as your starter class or unlock the instant reload ability later on, meaning you're more likely to use the guns you get throughout the game as glorified finishers rather than actual weapons. The environmental resistances mechanic seems interesting, but I haven't even played the game long enough to really get a good look at it due to other aspects that make the game feel lackluster at the least, and downright annoying or disappointing.The artstyle is... hit or miss. The world looks beautiful, enemy designs are interesting, yet the photorealistic textures on what are otherwise cartoonish models and overly realistic shading really make the game unpleasant to look at at times. It's like the devs couldn't even decide whether they wanted the game to be photorealistic or stylized, and it really shows. The music is okay. It's not badly made or really annoying, but it also doesn't sound unique or identifiable in anyway.The world map itself lacks coherency and logic with how it's set up. It looks like the devs took a couple looks at a map from a battle royale and thought that was good enough for how to make a world. Trenches don't span a long enough area to be relevant or have any sense to them, NPC's are haphazardly placed in areas to try and give off the sense that the world is alive, when it really isn't. Some areas don't even look properly made, and it really shows.The graphics are bad, like really bad. I'm not even saying that from the standpoint of some graphics ♥♥♥♥♥, either. The graphics of this game are genuinely unpleasing to look at at times. The lighting is all over the place, the way foliage waves and moves is extremely immersion breaking, and the amount of stuff that casts shadows is absurd and could be what's contributing so much to the game's poor performance. The high quality, photorealistic textures stand out like a sore thumb and sometimes even make the game look like an asset flip.I started this game on normal difficulty, so I don't know what it's like on hard difficulty, but there just doesn't seem to be much of any challenge when fighting enemies. You could literally just spam your melee attack and haphazardly dodge and parry, not caring about enemies hitting you and you'll get out of most encounters mostly unscathed. It's the big dudes that pose a bigger threat due to being able to toss you around like an abused napkin, and even they feel like pushovers when you finally get the fighting mechanics down. On top of that, the game gives you more healing items than you'll ever need.There aren't many bugs from what I've noticed, but there is a lot of jank, like a LOT of jank. Combat feels off and adheres too much to where you're aiming when it comes to the melee, the swimming mechanic is extremely outdated and poorly thought of, and from what I've seen of gameplays, mounts don't even seem to care about the chaos going on around them when you fight enemies.TL;DR: The game doesn't know what it wants to be and lacks a clear identity. The devs seem to mostly be comprised of programmers, animators, and artists based off of the bit of good that the game does have, and it really shows. There's a significant lack of coherent writing and world building/setting, the mechanics appear to be more experimental than anything else, the music is good yet doesn't have much to yield but isn't unique or identifiable by any means, and the dialogue is extremely forced half of the time. It pains me to say this as I had high hopes for this game, but I cannot recommend it at all. If you really want to get this game, then at least wait for a 50% off or more sale for it, because it is not worth the $60 price tag, or even a $40 price tag for that matter. There's potential, but it'll require a MASSIVE overhaul to reach that potential.

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely an 8/10. Minimum.I've been struggling to understand the negativity around this game. I purposely sheltered myself from any hype whatsoever involving Biomutant, only looking so far into it to make sure it's not something like rhythm based or PvP (things I Personally do not enjoy). Aside from that, I seen "Ninja Kung Fu Squirrel" and that was enough to keep me interested and rather excited to play.I was Not disappointed.I personally really have a lot of fun with the game for what it is: a large, post-apocalypse open world for you to explore and loot. Fight random baddies like you're in a martial arts movie, attempt to get old machinery or devices to start working again and salvage what you can out of it. It's your character and the open road, doing what you can to survive against how hostile the world has become due to the past actions of the species before yours. If that sounds fun to you, then you'll probably enjoy the game like I have.But let's go through some of these common complaints I see to satisfy the goblin in my brain:-The Narrator Is AnnoyingHe... Really isn't. He's got a pleasant voice to listen to, and though he doesn't have a 'Lot' to say about the current situation, he does make the journey less lonely. If you weren't bothered by the narrator in, say, The Stanley Parable, then you should be fine here. If not:Options -> Audio -> Volume -> Speech = 0, Frequency -> Narrator = 0.You Can Turn Him Off. You Are GIVEN That Option.Does it stop 'all' subtitles? No. But the ones that remain actually feels like it's your own character's inner thoughts. Or perhaps your conscience wondering if you're doing the correct thing, but that could just be me.-The Combat Is ____The Combat is fine. Maybe it's not "Insert Your Perfect Game Here" (like Devil May Cry 3), but it's not trying to be. The game gives you enough tools, weapons, skills, points, etc. to play around with other weapon/gun types- On The Same Character. There's no reason to Min/Max here: If you find yourself bored, try something new. Did you find a shotgun barrel with ice element that seemed interesting to try? Do so. Use your scrap that you've collected and put one together and see how it works out. Play around with different melee/ranged/"tech" abilities to find something fun. Is it always going to be the best thing to mow down all enemies effortlessly? Probably not, but that doesn't mean it's not fun to play around with. It's kind of a sandbox game: you make your own fun here, and the game gives you plenty of opportunities to do just that. I've played games that are more expensive than this that have faaaaarrrrr worse combat systems, the one in Biomutant is good for what it's trying to portray.-The Story Is Weak.It kinda is, very Black & White. But that doesn't mean YOURS has to be. The story is just a baseline to give you an epic, that's about it. Your Story can be whatever you want it to be.... Within limits. Okay, look, it's not going to be Skyrim or Divinity: OS2 levels of choices here. You're not going to be able to kill the NPCs and steal their homes/stuff. But you are alive, I assume, so you have the ability to use that imagination of yours. Stop waiting for the game to carve your story out and make it yourself, it's not going to be able to read your mind. No Developer can. I personally would rather have the freedom to make my own vs being pulled by the nose through a horribly boring story that I'm not engaged in. If you don't like the story in Biomutant, you can basically skip through it without missing much.-The Tutorial Is Long.It kinda is, and it can be very hand-holdy in the beginning. But I believe they're working on changing this a bit-Actually, I just checked, and they apparently altered the Tutorial for the better in yesterday's patch. I personally have to play through it again to really see, but they've made several fixes that should make it better.-QTEs Suck....You can turn them off. 90% of them anyway. Look into Accessibility Options. Seriously, thank the Devs for putting this option in, because Bloody Hell, I'm so tired of QTEs...-The Puzzles Are Bad.They're not "Bad", they're "Easy". They're just there to break up the gameplay loop a little bit and give you something else to do. I don't mind the fact that they're easy, better than stonewalling all progress just to open a door for a quick exit. And they do spice it up rather creatively, I thought. I don't remember seeing anything like them in other games recently. I honestly welcome them.-The Price Is Too High.*Presses the space between his eyes*Okay... Look. People who work on things like this DESERVE to be paid for it. Especially if they're doing it for a LIVING. Considering the hours and sacrifices they make to their own lives for Your precious entertainment. As controversial as this is going to sound, I'd argue that games should be more expensive- but I won't do that here. A review is not the right time. Yes, it's decently expensive, but you're getting a lot of content for that price. And you don't need to "Buy it now while supplies last". If it actually is too expensive for you currently, save up a little bit more next month/whatever and get it then. This isn't a "Live Service" game here, it'll be around for when you have the spare cash on you. If anything you'll be getting any bugs patched up by waiting a little bit, but it is Not "Too Pricey" in general.Look, the game isn't perfect, but it definitely does not deserve all the hate and the mixed rating. "Not Recommended" should be saved for actual bad games and crappy business practices/scams, not "6/10"s. If you didn't enjoy the game, that's Fine, but Biomutant... FUNCTIONS. It does a lot of things well if you REALLY take the time to look at it. It's not some broken mess of a game like some of the nightmare stories you've heard before (and you know the ones I'm talking about). They delayed the release of the game to AVOID that! Maybe it's not what you were expecting, but that's hype for you: it alters your perspectives of what a game can/will be. Learn from it; don't give into hype or set your expectations too high in the future. And hopefully we won't have another casualty like this in the future, because a "Mixed: 67% Positive" is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ shame for something as good as this.

_childDocuments_.review: Biomutant. Good idea but has poor execution. The setting is beautiful, models look good, it LOOKS and SOUNDS great! But the actual game play, its unacceptable. The combat is like you are one of the cat-creature side kick in Monster Hunter with only that much power. You zoom and slide all over the battlefield and hit with all the force behind a half-assed first pitch of a baseball game thrown by some 80 year old politican. The dodge and parry times are unreliable, parry only works regularly on the mutation-giving enemies. The queue to parry comes too early for all other enemies. Dodge, as mentioned, unreliable. You could get the rhythm of a big enemy down to a T and then when you go to slide and are nearly through the animation, it picks you up and punts you down onto the ground, taking half your health bar with it. The Mounts are fine, better control than some games. I am really disappointed with the mech mount though. I was really excited when I saw the big guns and awesome melee and the ability to customize it too! But I was floored when I saw that one of my normal (not mech) punches could so more than its gattling gun or slam attack. In total, Biomutant gets a 4/10- good idea and design, bad execution. I wish I could still get a refund.

_childDocuments_.review: After two hours I'm already on the brink of refunding the game, and let me tell you why. Simply put, the tutorial is too long, Two hours in, and I'm still getting hand held at every junction or taught mechanics like "How to craft" not the worst, but the way they did it, by sending me back to my childhood just is not indicative of how tutorials should be done. Also, for a loot based open world game, they love to put you on rails really early on and not give you loot? I've been struggling to find anything that's not a health-kit and so far I haven't found guns, or armour.The combat is, brain-dead to say the least, half your hits seem like they don't do anything and giant monsters are a pain to fight because a good portion of their attacks will hit you multiple times, without I-frames so you will be near-half health and die in a single combo because the game doesn't give you a chance to dodge out of hits and will instead punish you and stunlock you to death. To consider balance as well, there is an over-emphasis on your FIRST class you pick, and I would even mention that some classes are just straight up better than others, as my limited time playing the game, I chose Commando, which had 2 useless perks and a perk that was good only accessible at level 15 or so, which in contrast being a dead-eye gives you multiple choices in your class to choose which do benefit you greatly in combat.They have ONE voice actor voice EVERYTHING David Shaw-Parker.Now the problem is, I don't know why but they've chosen to have David SUMMERIZE, what creatures just told you basically most dialogue you have with any other creature, in any story cutscene is voiced by David which is a struggle in it-self, and most dialogue options go as -Creature: "Bel boola bekala"(Unsubtitled) -David's Line: "He just told you Skreembo can be found over there"This bogs down the dialogue MASSIVELY, and I don't understand why the dialogue couldn't have just been subtitled. And this also makes important plot points a little ridiculous because I feel like I'm just being read the story instead of being told it by IMPORTANT CHARACTERS I am being narrated instead and giving summaries as to what they said.Eventually this culminated into me muting the narrator in every instance, which unfortunately also mutes the two angels that speak to you who AREN'T voice by David.Another massive problem this game has is simply TELLING YOU all the backstory of the game in the first 5 minutes, and I'm not kidding, this is THE definition of Tell don't show. In an post apocalyptic world, you'd imagine some things would be left to the imagination, but no they don't want you to figure out why the world's like this, they straight up plot dump you 5 minutes into the game, there's no intrigue, nothing to figure out, And they CONTINUE to do this, straight up telling you your childhood in more plot dumps to rush whatever story they wanted to push onto you, and mind you, this is 2 hours into the game. Also there's a very plain and clear theme on a Tibet vs Japan (based on themes and what clothing each side wears) where one side is absolutely "evil" and the other's absolutely "good" and you choose which faction you want to participate in a good hour into the game, where it warns you it will lock out the other faction completely.  Which is jarring to say the least, instead of opening your world to be more ambiguous, it's just straight up bashing you over the head of being good or evil. Unless the devs can address many of these problems, I would definitely save my money and wait and see if there's ANYTHING left to salvage, after 8 years of development time I had high hopes, but evidently it didn't work out that way and was greatly disappointed my one Pro is that I got to play as a small furry creature in the small time I had with this game.
_childDocuments_.name: BIOMUTANT

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who pre-ordered BIOMUTANT upon its release on console, I found myself deeply disappointed and I decided to abandon this game. However, when Humble Bundle offered a PC copy, I decided to give it another shot. Sadly, my excitement gave way to frustration once more.The game begins with such promise. The world is vibrant, the engaging gameplay with a potential for something truly special. Yet, as I delved deeper, that promise crumbled beneath the weight of repetition and lackluster mechanics. The game's ambitious ideas are evident, but it feels as though it bit off more than it could chew.  The tone can be inconsistent between seriousness and whimsy, leaving the narrative feeling disjointed. Dialogue, in particular, falls flat (THE GIBBERISH DOES NOT HELP AT ALL!)While the world is undeniably beautiful and expansive, it lacks the substance to make exploration truly rewarding. Quests often devolve into mundane fetch tasks, and many features feel unfinished or underdeveloped.After 20 hours in, I am ONCE AGAIN exhausted and disheartened. It's clear that the game has a solid foundation, but it's buried beneath a mountain of unfulfilled potential.
_childDocuments_.name: BIOMUTANT

_childDocuments_.review: I'm recommending this because I had some fun with it. If you like PS2 style platformer games like the Jak and Daxter games or Kya: Dark Lineage, this one may be work checking out. It is an RPG only in that it allows you to customize your main character though, so no fancy base building or companions. There's several mounts to choose from, you get customizeable weaponry, character stats, abilities, and so on. The world map is very large for this kind of game and that gives it replay value. There are some choices you can make that change the development of the plot. So it is clear that replay value is what they were going for. So is it good? I think it is if you approach it with the right attitude. The narrator can get annoying, but as soon as you're about to turn off the sound, the game informs you that you can turn down the frequency of his comments. The dialog is frustrating in this game. It give you redundant information over and over again from several different characters. So it is weak on dialog and lore. But the action platforming gameplay is decent. I got it on sale and I felt it was worth my time for the gameplay. The graphics are decent too with a very colorful world to explore.
_childDocuments_.name: BIOMUTANT

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know why people (especially reviewers) ♥♥♥♥ all over this game.  It is a good game and lots of fun.  - Environments are really gorgeous- Movement and responsiveness of the character is good- The weapon and clothing mod system is unique, creative, and cool- Mounts, mech, jetski-ish thing, air glider ability, etcUltimately, the game is entertaining.Yes, the combat can benefit from improvements like not (often) being able to dodge the 3 move combos in between even if you have the timing.  Narration and story style is different and can sometimes be a little too much, but you can skip through, turn off narration etc. Also early on in the game, your guns are not very effective so your combat sessions last longer than you would expect (or you will have to be more adventurous with melee), and there are probably a few other things that I don't recall off the top, but this game is NOT deserving of the ♥♥♥♥ people are throwing at it. The reviewers are doing a disservice to the game and potential players (and they should get off holier than thou pissfest - not all games can be Ratchet & Clank level but that doesn't make them deserving of 5's and 6's either).The game is also more expensive that I would expect.  I'd probably think it should be at the $49.99 price point.  However, having said that, I don't regret paying $59.99.  I am at around 25 hours currently and I can see myself playing it to the end and doing most of the side quests.  Some videos suggest that there is probably around 50 hours in there to play (and sometimes I just like to wander around exploring as well).  In the end I'll end up paying a little over a $1/hour for this game.  If you are looking for a good, fun, 3D platformer that does some new things, is beautiful, and quite a bit of fun, I think you would easily get that from this game.

_childDocuments_.review: A decent open world RPG from a newer studio.It's a very simple game that is easy to get into and fairly straight forward as everything flows together nicely. They use a lot of well-known systems & mechanics from other games, making it easy to get into the game quickly.The negative of this game is that nothing really stands out apart from the fact you play a midget fur ball. There are some parts that aren't explained well, and others that could be delved into more. But it is always for parts of the game that don't really matter. I'd believe it if the target audience was "amateur gamers who have never played an RPG before". So that they could then be introduced to better, more intense games of the genre like Assassin's Creed or The Witcher.It's a 6/10 game, 7 if you push it. So a very chill game that is enjoyable to play casually.This game is 100% NOT worth the full price ($90 AUD). I'd pay $40 AUD at most.

_childDocuments_.review: Thus far, the game exudes an aura of raw, unfinished craftsmanship, displaying a dearth of meticulous attention and an overall lackluster quality that fails to captivate. _childDocuments_.review: This most recent update brought a lot of improvement to the game and some essential elements to combat. My first playthrough I had used almost exclusively guns and played on normal, and everything had gone off without a hitch, it wasn't a super hard video game. For my second time through I tried to play a melee character on hard difficulty because I wanted more of a challenge, but I found myself being angry at how the game worked quite often. The ability to animation cancel with dodge is really the biggest thing for me because I can really play somebody like the saboteur or mercenary the way I feel like they're meant to be played with dodging around everything rather than being forced to get more tanky because the combat doesn't allow me to dodge properly. I preordered this game after seeing how incredible it looked and the amount of customizeability it had and have not regretted that purchase once. If you are the kind of person looking for an incredible story in a game, this isn't the one for you(not that it's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, just not a professionally written novel in game form). If, however, you like gameplay and visuals then I would say this is a great purchase. I am entirely sure that I will go on to get far more than 60 hours of enjoyment out of this game, which I think makes it worth the $60 regardless. As far as the gameplay goes, I think it feels great. melee combat makes me feel badass, doing flips through the air and the slightly exaggerated motions that the animations have. The ranged combat is good, but I think to enjoy the game properly you should play aggressively. I sort of broke the game my first time through by finding a good gun and maxing out my crit chance, and while that is a way to beat the game I think it is far more enjoyable when you are in the thick of it fighting a group of enemies. I think this is a self created issue and therefor I don't really think it's up to the developer to fix it, I like that there are ways to become completely broken and unkillable and that I can enjoy the game properly if I so choose. I honestly don't really have any criticism for how this game's combat feels and looks. Another thing I really like is the crafting system that is in the game. I really like the customizeability that it has and being able to create my own weapon really adds to the role playing part of the game, being able to add even more individuality to your character. The story, like I said is something a lot of people criticize, but I don't think it's that big of a deal. You are sort of able to craft your own story with the way it is currently. If you want story the game probably won't satisfy your every desire, but I am not entering games looking for an experience like reading a novel, so it's right up my alley.Visually this game looks incredible. The world is a great mix of stylized and real that just gives it a great feeling. Everything is quite saturated and vibrant and I quite like that. It's a bit hard to describe if I can't show you gameplay and screenshots, but really it is a stunning game. While playing this I said 'wow' out loud to myself on more than one occasion, and I am very grateful for the inclusion of photo mode. TLDR: The game doesn't have an incredible story, even if it isn't a bad one. If you are looking for an incredible narrative experience don't expect that of this game. The gameplay is great, the combat feels good and has been greatly improved with the latest update, and the amount of customizeability in this game keeps it feeling fresh over time. I highly recommend this if you aren't desperately wanting a superb narrative experience and just want something fun to play that you can make your own.
_childDocuments_.name: BIOMUTANT

_childDocuments_.review: I'll say that this game isn't for everybody, but I absolutely love it. It has a beautiful and huge open world, fun combat, and an interesting connection to the world via narrator. I've had a ton of fun just running around and trying to gather up crafting supplies from various places on the map, and the quests are also engaging and fun. Very few glitches, and those that are present are run-of-the-mill things like weapons loading in the wrong hand, nothing that breaks the game or causes performance issues.Not your average RPG, but a great experience with light-hearted tones in a not as light-hearted world.
_childDocuments_.name: BIOMUTANT

_childDocuments_.review: It's pretty fun. Definitely a smooth launch for day 1, which is sad that I have to bring it  up. Lots of big games have problems at launch. This one has no problems for me.I'm still getting used to the game, but it definitely feels like it's meant to be played casually, and that's ok. I've played enough "hardcore gamer" games, and it's nice to have a break from the sweaty games.If you like games that let you just chill out and beat the snot out of enemies, and then gather resources to make better gear, this game is for you. That said, it's not  casual that there's no moments you're on the edge of your seat. There's definitely some moments that can feel tense or even scary.The only major complaint I really have is that when you beat the last enemy of an encounter, it always shows them getting launched in slow motion. If there's a way to turn off that slow motion, I'm going to hunt for that option. It gets old fast, and just takes too long to watch it. It adds 5 (feels like 10) extra seconds to each battle, and doesn't help with the "awesome factor". The wow-factor should come from the moveset and combo timings, not from a post-battle "special effect".
_childDocuments_.name: BIOMUTANT

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start by saying I had a blast playing Biomutant. What I wanted by buying this game was to explore a beautiful and vivid world and it's just what I got. The world is stunning, it's alive and you can really explore every nook and crany and find something interesting. Finished the game in about 38h but I skipped a lot of side quest, if you want to 100% the game, I can easily imagine you can get 50h out of the game and even more if you take your time to explore. The world is quite big.There is a new game+ option too and if you want to explore different endings, this is possible. The game is far from lacking of content.Okay, so that was what the game made awesome, now what is okay-ish? The combat system ! While not bad, you can actually make some pretty cool moves once you get accustomed to the system but the fights are uselessly difficult and long, so much that it can be boring after a while. There's plenty of stuff to improve your characters (perks, psi-powers, bio-powers, wung-fu (that's their word for kung-fu) and equipment) which is nice but well, the combat is okay. While the character doesn't seem to have any physics while you move, it becomes quite good during combat.The story is okay-ish too and can be summed up by saying: Humans lived long ago on earth, a corporation full of greed empoisoned the land and drained it of it's ressources now their extinct and weird animals rules the land.You, you're a kid who got his mommy killed by a big baddie and you know seek revenge. You lost an eye and there's a prophecy about a one eye kid saving the world so while you get your revenge, why not also save the world, the save the world tree, unite the tribes and kill the world eaters (big critters gnawing at the tree's roots)? It's not bad, it's meh. Okay, why not?Another meh is how the world is quite hard to get into at first, it's just hard to invest yourself in the game, first because it's a brand new IP and the world is not explained very well to immerse yourself from the moment you start the game. Then because of the different systems explained too quickly and not well enough. Throughout the game, you have a hard time connecting with anyone, the NPC are bland, they talk and talk and talk but since it's always the same narrator talking for them, it's really hard to want to know them more. They're also too talkative but see the narrator paragraph below.Now, what does the game do bad and is irritating?First, the UI, the lack of mini-map, the quest tracking badly done and the fact you constantly need to bring up the full screen map to track the next close-by objective is tiring. There's a also some kind of slowness in the menu which doesn't fix anything. They're not very well imagined and inventory management is simply horrible. I had to search many time in the menu for what I was really looking for before getting used to it.Crafting and most system is underwhelming and badly explained. You cannot craft the most interesting weapons and cannot improve them which makes them really useless. (bow, boomrang, shuriken, claw, mechanical fist, ...)The mounts, oh boy, they're not really fast, making them useless most the time and the cool ones are limited to a specific environment. For example, the mecha can only be used in the tar area on the left side of the map, you cannot summon it anywhere else. The water bike only works on the right side of the map, meaning if you need it on a body of water anywhere else, you will keep seeing the message "cannot summon here". The cool hand? Well, I was level 40 when I got it and so were enemies meaning that mount was totally useless and not damaging any enemies around.Also, you cannot improve your mount but you can find parts to customize their look.The quests, they will bring you to explore the world and travel back and forth for hours but gosh they're boring, forcing to you find appliances like radio, micro-wave, washing machine, old computer, etc. and resolving a stupid puzzle to fix them which will then bring you to the next one. AND THERE ARE A LOT OF THOSE QUEST !!!! So many that I got bored of them, couldn't finish them because they were so frustrating. My quest log was full of quest I didn't complete when I finished the game. Find 8 micro-wave, 5 radio, 8 washing machine, 8 guitars, 5 piano, etc. -_- And free 23 prisoners which I did half way through. The quest are boring and badly designed.Even the tribes quest are always the same for all tribes. Only the 4 world eaters are a bit more original.Now, lets talk about the real problem of this game, the problem that discourage me from doing any new game+ ever: The narrator ! During the game, you will hear 3 voice actors, the narrator, the light and dark conscience. While your conscience are okay, the narrator is a huge pain ! The way everything is written is a pain. The text are worth of a 5 years old when you see a train is called a chugga chugg chugg, water is called the surf, brick brocka brooh glooby goolbah... Think I'm kidding? I'm not ! Worse is how the narrator keeps talking, you'll quickly shut him down because his comments are as tiring as having a 2 years old pulling your shirt while you play and talking in baby language. The game is full of those moments you want to skip but can't like cinematics, the same coming over and over and over until you start screaming at your screen in the hope the narrator will just shut his mouth. I can't describe enough how horrible this narrator is and how repetitive everything becomes. He's not a bad and sounds rather good, he's doing his job but hearing him so much and hearing that silly writing of booga boo boo is enough to drive you mad !!!! He really makes you hate NPC and you end up not caring what might happen to them. When a NPC talks, it goes like: "says there's an object he needs nearby, says it's very important, says the chubbah goobly is the main object he needs for whatever he's doing, ..." and it last for what seems hours, it makes you hate NPC ! Seriously !!!Otherwise, a few bugs, nothing really game breaking.Unprecise controls which makes you fail what you wanted to do (a bit frustrating).Why oh why do we come so many times in front of walls of rock and cannot climb it forcing us to run all around making us lose 10min for nothing? Why do we die so easily in water and tar also forcing us to walk all around it and make us lose time? TLDR: the world is amazing, the game is long, the combat is okay, the story is meh, the UI is horrible, the quests are repetitive and boring, a few bugs and frustrating unprecise controls along with annoying obstacles which are only there to make us lose time, the narrator is boring and tiring and you hear him WAAAAY too much, he's the worst thing that could happen to this game, he totally ruined it. Post apocalyptic (sort of) kung fu panda with weird critters wearing pyjamas for armor and without any panda.
_childDocuments_.name: BIOMUTANT

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute gem of a game, "Biomutant" takes a stand against the washed-up AAA companies like Bethesda and CD Projeckt Red and reminds us how, even on a smaller budget, a virtual world can be polished and immersive--even if it isn't stuffed with more systems than a nuclear power plant.Despite a few glitches here and there and somewhat simplified combat that still does at least require quite a bit of skill to master, and even with a mostly shoehorned-in story, Biomutant shines from its sheer world building and fantastic creature designs. The vast world beckons you to explore every nook and cranny, improving your skills and crafting delightfully makeshift weapons as you fight the legions of bandits and terrifying mutants you will encounter everywhere. "Biomutant" is single-player gaming distilled down to its core essentials. It doesn't need to tackle philosophy or society-shaking questions or literally improve your IQ by its complexity. It just needs to be a fun, well-polished escapist experience you can immerse yourself in at the end of a stressful work day.I look forward to Experiment 101 improving this concept even more in a sequel and getting lost in the post-apocalyptic beauty that has been reclaimed by nature. You've earned a hard-core fan, guys! Keep showing the Big Boys how it's done!
_childDocuments_.name: BIOMUTANT

_childDocuments_.review: So I will do my best to explain my feelings regarding this game and my opinion. I do not often review games but I will do a quick TL:DR and then you can continue reading if you want. Warning, there will be spoilers. Pretty game, bad story and many glitches. Pros- Pretty world- Combat can be fun- Lots to exploreCons- Story is honestly not that great, maybe a 3/10- Quiet a few areas glitched to where you cannot finish them.- Characters felt rather boring. Now the rest of my review and the spoilers. So when it comes to games like this I am a big time explore, like straight up just walk off ignore the main quest and start looting and exploring areas. I loved that so many areas had goals to encourage you to explore the area and get loot or other good things. I went through going everywhere I could to try to get as much loot as possible and see this beautiful world that was created. Problem is there are quiet a few zones that when you enter and try to complete they are glitched so you cannot finish them. Which frustrates me when I am going through trying complete all the areas. Now onto the story, you have to unite the tribes and kill all the boss monsters eating the trees. At the start you get to pick the evil tribe or the good tribe, no in between.  Each boss fight is going to require you to use the special mount for the area which is a nice touch and kind of fun.  So I choose the good paths normally, going through and exploring helping everyone and that good jazz. But what gets really old is the narrator just randomly talking about how you have to save the world, or when you enter a area you have to hear about how to corporations killed the world and this is all their fault. Gets really really old really fast. Each tribe did not feel really different from the last one, felt like a re-skin of the previous tribe and the same couple of things to be able to take a base and then the fort. For the bosses they felt the same for the most part as well, you shoot the boss use the special for the mount you are using and keep shooting between cut scenes. Over all I will say if you are interested in this game get it if it is heavily on sale, not a lot of replay value to it and not a lot to keep ones attention. That has been my opinion on it, as I said I do not review often but this game honestly just left me so disappointed I had to write something.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an extreme theme park game for casual console players. Whenever you feel like something exciting is about to happen, the design throws you into a unskippable cutscene. First 2 hours is just about spamming ESC key to skip dialogue to get into any combat. Combat isn't smooth, there are a lot of animation lock for move-sets, very clunky parry mechanic. I really wanted to give the game a chance for it's combat, unfortunately this isn't the one. Too much narration killed the game for me and lack-luster combat wasn't enough to keep me in. I felt like I was playing one of those Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtle games back in early 2000s where it's narration driven and having no enemies in open world unless I engage in a mission. Outdated game-play released in a time where people have expectations to match it's trailer.

_childDocuments_.review: No shame on this one. Do not get this game unless you *really* dig the core concept, especially if they're still listing this game as worth 60 dollars.An exploration game with fun combat, but a forgettable story that's barely there, a massive amount of padding, and a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ puzzle system that almost softlocked me multiple times all because of RNG. It kinda hurts to say all of this because I still sort of like the game, but there's so much that indicates that the people who made it, frankly, didn't know what they wanted the game to be. 3D platformer? A "Choices Matter" game with a karma system that reminds me of Fable? Some kind of fighting game? A BoTW contender with a large world to explore and many sights to see? And considering other reviews/discussions are saying that they've completely abandoned the game, odds are none of these are going to be addressed or fixed.Overall, a game with a few good concepts and many bad concepts put into a blender and mixed until it's a bitter slurry with a sweet aftertaste. You keep drinking it and hating the taste, but the aftertaste keeps you drinking. 4/10, would play BoTW with my cringy Sonic OC Coldsteel the Edgehog with two nodachis and a machine gun with telekinetic powers and STOP LAUGHING AT ME, CARL, HE'S COOL!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not bad at all. It's not the next greatest RPG of all time either. It feels like a true video game though. I feel like a kid again playing on my dad's ps1. _childDocuments_.review: When I was a kid, I watched Star Trek's "Wrath of Khan". I have almost no memory of it except a scene where it's described that Kirk is one of the only people to pass something called the "Kobayashi Maru" test. Now, in the mind of some ten year old, these were just sounds they said. It meant nothing to me and still barely does beyond a quick google search to make sure I spelled it correctly. Even though the scene stuck with me, it is the example I think about when universes just throw letters at the wall to make up random names for things. It is my chief concern with this game more than anything else. I will lead with this complaint because I don't have much else beyond mere petty annoyances, just in case you get confused at my thumbs up.Most parts you pick up are just random letters thrown around with the occasional vowel to at least make it pronounceable. I think I have a rifle stock named a "Skorp" or some nonsense. I cannot express how irritating this is. Why is it so difficult to just name it something like "Basic Metal Stock" or "Incredible Shiny Barrel". Nope, it's all Flips, Skorps, Smicks, Klobbs, Yrkums, Infs and Plockers. I literally only made one of those up. Some of it I can accept, like referring to the past as the "Once-was", but it's all so incredibly inconsistent. It'll call something the Once-Before and then go on to explain a polluting corporation destroying the planet in modern linguistics. Pick one, writers.While I do think the grumbling linguistics of all the NPC's should have just been subtitled than narrated, this little feature pisses me off a bit more than I think it should, but here we are.So what kind of game is this? It's an open world loot-shooter with some magic and melee thrown in the mix. It has the worldly vibe of a Chibi-Borderlands game while also giving me a Breath of the Wild vibe, though this game does marginally better at filling the world. Not necessarily with stuff to do, but more along the lines of hiding loot behind waterfalls. In BotW, I remember running across fields for minutes at a time, while Biomutant does a better job of giving me a reason to stop to explore some bombed out building because there is inevitably something in there to grab. I'm not fully sure what aligning the antennae on a television did for me (experience? I don't know!), but I still do enjoy running around as an adorable rodent to figure out how a toilet works as it spits legendary loot at me.I only have nine hours on it and some features still elude me, like crafting clothing. I'm not terribly fond of looking like a ridiculous clown but sometimes I sacrifice a few armor points so I can look like a fairly bad-ass automatic rifle shooting samurai warrior. The game honestly gives me the biggest BotW vibe but I think Biomutant does a few things better. Including the "more reasons to stop and run into those woods to see if that big mob will drop something good", but there's also a plethora of interesting hazard zones to give you a hefty risk-reward ratio. Do you have low heat resistance? Well, how's your move speed (upgraded through agility)? Because I've done a few encounters where I'd just do hit and runs on a hazard zone's perimeter, got some decent loot, dived into houses (which sometimes negate the timer), and shot mobs through destroyed doorways and windows as they chucked fireballs at me. I enjoyed that encounter.Another thing I don't always like are combo moves. I never got into street fighter arcade games when I was a child and I certainly don't have the memory to do it now. I've only once in nine hours been able to activate the "super mode" that you can get when you do three unique combos in a certain time frame, because honestly my two rats are just gunners so I just kind of click on everything until their health goes away. I will occasionally do a jump to get some bullet time in there but I mostly just rely on a couple of very specific combos that I can actually fulfill and they've carried me a decent distance so far. I have no real complaints on the combat. I've seen better, but I've seen worse.I'd say ignore some of the metacritic views and really base your purchase decision on what types of games you, the player, actually like. I see a lot of 6/10's thrown around and while I don't disagree with that numeric value, a 5-7 out of 10 always ends up translating to a "decent, with flaws" game and I've rarely been disappointed by a middle of the road type rating. I only get worried when I start seeing 4's, and this is not a 4/10 game. It's really not that bad.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to start by saying this game is nothing like the Negative Youtube reviewers have stated.This game is basically similar to Fallout 4 and somewhat similar to Mini Ninjas. The world is beautiful and huge, the gameplay is hard if you play melee even on "easy" its slightly brutal as the dodge and block tells are very hard to see. Just a heads up if you and your children can handle mild violence then this game would be perfect to play with them together, as its exactly aimed for all ages.+Exploration is huge in this game and really fun to navigate.+Character creation is amazing+The world does have lots of enemies but you must actively search for them.+The world is full of charming little puzzles all very similar but not exactly the same.+Side quests are everywhere which helps lead you to enemies if you are lost.+The stories are varied and two characters can have very different game plays+Loot is amazing every thing has a purpose even if at first you don't know what its for.+Crafting is humorous and fun at least i liked it+Ranged is a lot easier than melee+Gear is really strange and quite funny.+After the early tutorial the world opens up immensely.-The narrator is annoying to many (not me) but he can be disabled.-Enemies can be brutal for melee classes even on easy mode-Dodge and block combat tells are really hard to see mid fight which make melee very hard to play.-No motion Blur removal can make customers sick ((me included) is it being added)For myself on an older PC the game has run very smooth and sweet and my Cpu is below recommended Core i5 3470 but still runs this fine, my Nvidia GTX 1060 6gb has had no hitches or stutter and zero crashes so far on 460.97 drivers. I even run the game on a standard Harddrive WD 1tb blue.I would have loved a fog removal option to make the game less intensive on pc's.So if you are looking for a Samurai styled cutesy version of Fallout 4 pretty much down to the wire go no further than Biomutant, and for me i've had zero issues the negative reviewers have said.One last thing i'd like to thank 101 for this game, its been a few years since i've enjoyed an open world sandbox game this much thanks. _childDocuments_.review: It has all the potential to be incredibly enjoyable and interesting and funny and proceeds to capitalize on absolutely none of it. It isn't hard, it isn't interesting, it isn't clever, it isn't innovative. It's just the same thing you've seen a million times and all you really do is press a few buttons absent-mindedly. The environment seems dead and muted despite the colors and space. There is no wind, environmental effects, or interaction between enemies and the environment. The level design seems to consist of "walk through these 5 doors for no reason and, no, there isn't anything in any of the rooms either." Every mob is the same brain-dead AI shooting nerf darts. Despite the combat designer's intent to provide an engaging and fun game, all they've really done is create a standard auto-locking m1 and m2 spam fest similar to the Mordor or Arkham Asylum systems.

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR at the bottomAs much as I have personally enjoyed my experience thus far playing Biomutant, I cannot in good faith recommend this game in its current state. What upsets me the most about Biomutant is that you can clearly see how amazing the game could have been given the budget, team, and amount of time some AAA games are given. Don't get me wrong, there are plenty of amazing moments playing this game that have kept me playing as long as I have, but that does not excuse the lack of polish especially given the fact that this game currently costs $60. As someone who has been waiting since around 2016 for this game to finally arrive, I can appreciate the hard work and effort put into this game. I try not to compare games and their development to each other but this very much feels like early No Mans Sky. At release you could clearly see the vision of the developers/studio but it was clear that they had neither the time nor the money to completely pursue that vision. By no means am I saying that we were duped or lied to, many people clearly had higher expectations for this game while others were able to tame it a little better. I was part of the latter and still feel as though this game does not even come close to its true potential. Below are a list of some Pros and Cons that I found throughout the game so far. Biomutant receives a   TL:DR – It’s a fun relaxing game not to be taken too seriously. I would say that this is a fantastic game for a younger audience. 10 year old me would have absolutely loved this game. If you are interested in the game and don’t mind the $60 price tag, try it out. Otherwise, wait for a Steam sale, $40 seems a lot fairer for the current state of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: So, like many, I got this game in the monthly Bundle. I had heard that this game was a pretty big disappointment upon launch, but I wanted to go with an unbiased and open mind, so I dove in and... I agree with the general concensus.First things first, combat. It's the main part of your game, it's open world so it's going to be pretty damn frequent. And it. Frigging. Sucks. Balls. Enemies being "harder" means they become bullet sponges; status effects, spells, and the such are basically meaningless, defeating an enemy means emptying clip after clip of bullets on them until they go down. Oh but don't go too far because the kiting system is pretty damn stupid! I understand they don't want players to drag an enemy halfway across the continent slowly chipping away with DoT until it dies, but these monsters have a shorter range than a LoL camp; you move half an inch away from the very limited spawn location, and they turn back and regenerate all that HP that you took four clips and five ki bars to deplete. I'm aware Horizon: Zero Dawn is a very high standard to compare to, but THAT is how you make combat engaging; I was eager to fight new machines, not dreading "oh my god here comes another 15 minutes slugfest where I hold down RT until bullets are out".And the narrator... oh my god the narrator... gets old and obnoxious pretty ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ quickly. Returning to the LoL comparisons, it's like when Caitlyn shouted "Boom! Headshot!" every headshot she got, which to the ones not familiar, was about once every five to eight seconds. Gets boring pretty ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ quick. And I understand not having enough budget to voice act every single character, but you can like... just leave the subtitles, instead of the narrator going "he's saying that...". I don't know how it made sense to developers, but it's annoying.I wouldn't recommend this at anything lower than a 70% discount and even then, I would encourage to refund immediately if you don't like the first few minutes of combat. Gets boring real quick and the game is very lackluster.

_childDocuments_.review: While i hesitated to write a review at first, i feared it be more of a rant post. And that does not really help anyone. Truth: whatever you might have expected from it - Its not that. A few stat points here and there do not make a RPG. Fetch quests ... well some are ok i guess. Its not like i got anything more motivating to do. And mediocre Quests. Oh. Lots of them. While I liked the Character creation options they might not appeal for everyone since there is not much of a  role you are playing. Later on you can equip pretty much everything and also a Psi Freak will have to fummel at some enemies ala' Lee. Nothing i hold against it personally. Diversity can be fun. The crafting itself is solid, with a few Keypieces really standing out. If some People complained about Cyberpunks Dressing that was like " Tar yourself and run through Elton Johns closet" kind of style - wait what this Game has in store for you. Hilarious. Do not think of finding inspiration for Cosplay here. Please, do not try it - might end up becoming a meme, unless that is the intention.    Open world. Ok. Nothing huge - but very nice to look at. The visual aspect and appeal is certainly there, save that ruins could have been more detailed. Still solid. Very Few enemies far in between. Dont play this at 1AM and expect to be awake at 5 am. Eyes tire out and it barely has anything else to keep you awake.Verdict Visuals > 9/10 Some animations (like going up the ladder, walking, swimming -or drowning?) leave a bit to be desired but in combat, so far, very nice. Fluid.Verdict Animations > 8/10Sound. Well ... Honestly don't expect any earworms or Nier level BGM. Music does not intrude and most certainly does not makes itself felt. Cant even remember having heard anything at all. Oh well. Gibberish is kinda cute at the start but looses the appeal fast - since its also being narrated).A textbox would have been fine aswell - also might have pissed off someone else (not me, i am Textbox proof)The annoyance level certainly would be less, but at least its skippable. The ESC key suffered heavy abuse after the 5th hour of my playtime. Narration can be lowered to 0 so "This is a Bridge" is fairly phased out. But still the ever repeating dialog of when you catch fireflies has you rock bottom fast even with that slider down and does not help the immersion. While i can appreciate  healthy Sarcasm (Honestly i was expecting The Bard's Tale level of Narration (Sarcasm and etc.)  ala "Tony Jay" there given the game setting but i had to chalk it up to a missed Opportunity and a miss-placed expectation of mine. While not bad, but after 10+ hours the narration is all you will remember from this Game soundwise. Whenever this is good or bad i ll leave the judging to you.  They where NOT kidding with the description of the features of the game, that, "every step in your journey is narrated" and almost took that literally.    Verdict Sound 5/10 - nothing great to mildly annoying. The Fact that i cant remember the music is telling.  Steering > Keyboard jockey.  Chances are you have a Gamepad. You ll most likely use it. While you can rebind the keys (what a hassle) you notice the game design for combat and PSI etc. -  has controllers in mind for the Steering. Consoles.>.<   I play with keyboard and its nothing remarkable on its default setting, at least on my opinion. Workable, but i missed Alt sometimes and hit the "Win" key instead - for instant gratification, pun intended. Verdict Steering > 6/10Story. Well you ll be skipping most of it. So, errr, i dunno. Sidequests are abundant and few have something to offer entertainment wise.  The Dark- Light dialog and could have sort of just played in the head (perhaps) but no you get a A or B choice most of the time. Some PSI abilities are linked to the Alignment so well, so, you ll be doing quite a few of nasty stuff in order to get telekinesis. What has Telekinesis with Dark to do in the first place? You tell me. Another "take it as it is" Scenario that forces to either resign to its design or start complaining > A or B.  Light or Dark. Verdict Story > Sorry. I was too busy hitting the ESC key. It started out ok'ish i guess ... so. Cant rate this. I ll cut this short. The Game has certainly a few fleshed out features and others just bare bone or outright missing like voice acting that AAA games usually in this Price tag feature. Do you have a 10 year old Child? If yes - good. (Its tailor Cut and he/she will apreciate the Klick! Klick!) You might even get some enjoyment out of it as-well if not at least some Quiet hours. In THAT CASE i would recommend it then  at a 30$ price tag.Future DLC or Updates might change the Game somewhat or substantial, i hope for B.  So much for pre-ordering. Lesson learned.

_childDocuments_.review: Pleasantly Surprised! 9/10Whilst the game unarguably draws some of its influence from games such as Zelda BoTW and Oceanhorn, the developers have managed to make something that feels unique and enjoyable. I am not a big fan of the concepts of 'Light' and 'Dark' being tied to special abilities as it forces the player to play a certain way. I have found many dialogues to be cheezy, and many scenes that were intended to create an emotional response seemed to under-deliver, only making me sigh and hope that they are over quickly. The puzzles have been a breeze so far, even at the hardest difficulty, and have not provided the gratification of accomplishing something -  hoping they increase in difficulty (by a lot) as the game progresses. Those are all the complaints I could think of,  and if you can overlook some of its quirks, you'll likely have a great time playing this game.
