_childDocuments_.review: Like everyone else, I have to say that it's really difficult to review something in a binary rating system. Yes/No. Good/Bad. Positive/Negative. There's nuance needed. I'm putting this in the positive reviews as the good just edges out the bad in the current state of the game. I purchased the game for $43 CAD so I don't feel as irritated as those who spent $60 CAD or $60 USD. The game in its current state is definitely not worth that price. It's unpolished and clunky at times. I initially rolled a Psi-Freak and was completely useless. The damage of the character's main ability was negligible and combat felt tedious. After re-rolling a Mercenary, I started having fun. The world is gorgeous. I love vivid colours and this really hits the spot. The animals are (mostly) cute and amusing and there's just something cathartic about a samurai-weasel fighting off a band of baddies.  Exploration is interesting, but it does suffer from lack of enemy encounters and interesting quests. I feel that the glaring bugs in the game are fixable: lack of encounters, clunky combat, unbalanced abilities. They are things that  can be re-worked by the devs and brought up to snuff. I'm really hoping that happens as I'd love to see more innovation in games these days.  If you can pick this up for under $45 CAD, it's worth some entertainment that will likely come out to about $4 an hour.  We've all paid more for less (I'm looking at you GoT Finale).

_childDocuments_.review: Man oh man is this where I hate these thumbs up / thumbs down systems and long for the days of five stars. Nothing is binary and no-where is it more obvious than in games like this. A three-star, middle-of-the-road actiony open-world RPG with guns and wanna-be kung-fu action.It's self-irreverent, tongue-in-cheek, but holy environmentalism batman is it heavy-handed with the "humans are bad, we destroyed the world and now it's ruled by mutants what horrors have we wrought" BS. I love that the developers have been responsive and attentive. I love that they've done their best to give us a game that they felt would be enjoyable... but that doesn't make up for something that's, unfortunately, painfully generic and safe whilst at the same time not quite managing to hit that bar in a few places.Generic Ubisoft towers to gain visuals of a place? Check. "dangerous" zones that have been used before and were kinda popularized by Breath of the Wild? Check. Complete with specific armor that you have to get and wear in those areas to remain safe, disregarding any other gear you might have. Mutations can counter this, but there's little point when you can slap the armor on, duck in, do what you need to do, and leave. Combat is... unfortunately repetitive and tends toward spamming a few of the "Wung-Fu" or whatever they called it and - even then - the inputs can be finicky for pulling those off consistently. Would have been better off with them as. It simply feels like they tried to do too much with the combat and ended up making it a bit of a mess of one part action, one part fighting game combos, one part bullet time, and one part spamming the same three moves before activating you special mode and going ham on something. Overall TL;DR is that the game is perfectly average. It's perfectly playable, had petty visuals and playable combat, it's perfectly lovely, it's perfectly flawed, but I can't recommend it at asking price if you catch it on sale I'd say give it a go and enjoy the world for what it is for a while. Otherwise, you can have someone yell at you about giant gas plants creating "oxygenless" (read: "Air Made Toxic by Petroleum Fumes") environments, global warming making some places too hot to live, and improper dumping of nuclear waste leading to toxic environments on social media for free and you don't even need the $60 game wrapper for it.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wish there was a mixed mark because there are some really good elements to this game as you can see by my play time, but there are many different problems also with this game,. I haven't encountered any bugs but there are elements that I don't understand how the devs didn't see. Like i'm playing this and thinking of things they could have done which makes me think if they have even played their own game.The mount system is cool but why can't we have multiple mounts on the summon button, literally had a really cool skeleton horse but did a mission to get Mjut because you need it to open certain area. As soon as it was completed my other horse just disappeared which is annoying as I have no clue how to get him back. Why include sales vendors of animals if you can only have one at a time, it just makes all the other mounts useless if you need one to open certain areas.The mutations and psi powers are cool. But again, why include so many when you can only have 4 at a time, it's mind boggling. Could have included a system like assassins creed where there are two layers to the powers. I will guarantee you will only use a select few as there are others that are basically useless. The dark abilities are weak compared to light so keep that in mind.Don't even get me started on the narrator, honestly so annoying. The amount of time i've heard him speak about activating the mainframe after completing a puzzle, or if you fail the puzzle he will just speak again, this is with the narrator on 20. I turned him off from translating characters as the dialogue was irritating.Talking of puzzles, jeeeeeeeeeeeesus. Never have I ever seen so many useless repetitive puzzles in a game before, at the start I was like ok, this is cool. However the more you play the more annoying they become and you find yourself traversing the land just to do these puzzles.The open world and environment is the best thing about this game hands down. Although, there are so many copy and paste jobs it's ridiculous, like some buildings are literally the same layout which removes the fun from the exploration element as well as the fact that some superb loot are in silly places so a lot of time you just completely miss them so I had to do a Youtube job a few timesAt the moment i'm level 40 and each new item I get I have to scrap because it is useless. Crafting system is also very unique, however like I just said I keep finding parts way below my level now which means that the system becomes useless taking the fun out of that particular elementMissions in this game is lacking. Had to do 4 fetch quests from the same character at one point. Some are so close to each other as well so you find yourself back tracking multiple times which just makes you want to stop playing the game and very infuriating to be honest.The combat element is cool and fun, although the enemies get tedious and very boring after a while as they are re-skins and you find yourself doing the same thing. Some there is no point fighting in close range because they will just flatten you, especially if there is two of them so there are a lot of fights where ranged guns are best. Melee weapons are way too weak compared to guns, can literally run around holding the trigger. This is the problem, there are so many unique elements in this game which is great, however there should be quality over quantity. Bought this on CD Keys for like £30 and i've got my time out of it for that money, definitely not worth full price though until there are improvements in the game.As the aforementioned summon feature, this is the reason for this review. I think i'm going to stop playing for a while as that really peeved me off.Great elements and it is fun to play, however many systems rip the heart and soul out from the game. I'd advise you to buy if on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: It's ok. Mostly somehow boring.I don't understand why everybody is hyping the graphics. They are okay. But I 've seen much better. ESPECIALLY the fur - it looks like crap. The World is okay. It's "open" - but beside invisible walls it has many natural walls. So yes, its kinda open world for that par which is reachable.The dystopic background story is nice. But way too fluffy for my taste. So instead of deathclaws and bloodthirsty raiders you are fighting colorful teddybears. Its really hard to take this game serious. The RPG part is nothing really exiting. Craft weapons and use them - if your level is high enough.But what really kills the game for me is the way you solve quests. You run around a bit and suddenly you are told that you solved a part of a quest about a person you haven't even heart about yet. It feels like being married to someone before you even know the person. I don't think the (at least german) narrator was the best choice. Took me a while to figure out that it should be the voice of the little grashopper-robot. And the way he is translating the animals babbeling to words really bugs me, since its all told in 3rd person. Btw. there are sometimes just short comment which do not make any sense, because you don't even know what object or person epecially is meant (if you know the person already anyway).You can't compare the game to great titles like Fallout or Horizon Zero Dawn. I find the story telling way too shallow and non-linear to keep my interest.You can see the effort and the size of the world and everything, which SHOULD justify the price. But on the other side its simply too boring, chaotic and shallow to justify the price from the entertaining point of view. Maybe the half price (or a little bit more) would be a good standard price.

_childDocuments_.review: Here we go once again with all the people dropping negative reviews. So far I'm ~3 hours into the game and personally I'm enjoying it. Sure the narrator can get a little tiring to listen to but outside of that I find combat to fluid and fun. It somewhat reminds me of the combat from Kingdoms of Amalur. The world is vibrant and beautiful which is a refreshing take on a post-apocalyptic setting we don't ever get to see. The crafting, while admittedly I've only scratched the surface of, is a good touch without being overly cumbersome. If you're a fan of open world titles where you explore, gather loot, and get to decide on the morality of your character give it a try, you won't be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing 10 hours I can't recommend this game for full price. 60€/$ is way way too much for such an unpolished game. There are many people that complain the majority of bad reviews are of people that didn't evenplay more than 3 or 4 hours. And it might be true, but I will tell you why: the first 3-4 hours of the game are a tutorial, and they are absolutely awful. Like I don't remember being do bored playing a videogame ever before. However it is true that the game improves once you complete them and get out there into the world. And you will see a dead world where there are certain places where you can kill mobs and loot items. Rinse and repeat. Secondary missions are fetch quests. Or go find anoher NPC and do a fetch quest for the NPC. Rinse and repeat. The combat is incredibly shallow, you only have 2 combos and a few powers that are only usable if you play as a "mage" or psy-freak, because you need to use ki to use the powers. Plus melee is really clunky, you can't cancel animation, so you will find yourself wanting to block or dodge, but you will be stuck in the combo animation and will not be able to do so. You will be hitting the same 2 buttons throughout the whole game. Im pretty sure the only reason many people like is: the game looks quite good. It is very saturated, but it is a nice looking world. And that might make somethings, like the combat, look better than they actually are. It is like the last trilogy of star wars, completely devoid of logic, incredibly bad plot, but they are graphically appealing, so you might enjoy it in that way if you ignore everything else. Plus the story is super tipical, very similar to that of Zelda BoTW, but the game lacks everything the latter had that made it so good. In my opinion, do not buy this game if you don't like open world games, because this is the worst exponent of many bad things like repetition. If you like open-world games, do not buy this game for more than 30€/$, it is not worth more than that.

_childDocuments_.review: Charming, quirky, and fun.Biomutant is an open world RPG featuring an impressive amount of content and decent gameplay.The combat is not complicated nor hard and that is part of it's appeal.Game has a couple of innovative design choices like being able to craft on the fly (great) and scaling cliffs simply requires finding an anchor point and pushing in the direction you wish to travel with the thumb stick only.The RPG elements are levelling and investing skill points into different skills (these are quite limited so overly diverse builds aren't a thing but I don't think it matters). There is also a light/dark choice system.This game is more about exploring the map, meeting the quirky characters, looting/crafting better items and engaging in easy combat without any hardcore elements or pressure. A narrator gives voice overs along the way and adds positive comments that are young 'un friendly.A charming game that is as cruizy to play as it is fun.An easy recommend based on that.

_childDocuments_.review: I really really enjoy this game. It's one of only a handful of open world games I really enjoy! There is lots to do without feeling overwhelming, I love the various creatures and clans, honestly there is a lot to love about this game.The strong points for me:- World building. I know a lot of people don't like to be hit over the head with the "companies bad" thing, but I think it makes for really interesting and fun ways to ♥♥♥♥ up the world you're making. I like the various ways the company ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up the world in over the top villainous ways, I think it's fun and silly like a good b-movie!- Gameplay. It's as simple or complex as you want it to be. I like the combos and moves you unlock and how fast combat can be. It makes for very enjoyable gameplay. When outside battle you can really move fast, and exploring all the different environments is both easy to navigate through and super fun.- Graphics. Man I just love how this game looks, it's very beautiful, but then very ugly and decrepited when it needs to be. They struck a balance that I think is very fun to go through and keeps me engaged and excited for the next area.-Story. Overall I like the basic story. I do have some problems with it, which I'll explain below, but I like the basic idea of it. I've had fun so far!I do have a few issues. These aren't enough to keep me from recommending this game, but I feel people should be aware of them.- The narrater. I don't actually mind him too much, though I think this guy works better in a comedy situation then this big open world serious game. My only real gripe with this guy is that while you're exploring and doing other things off the main path HE WILL NOT SHUT UP. He's constantly reminding you that you have to do the main story. You cannot turn this off without turning off the whole narrater. I want to explore and have fun, I don't want to be constantly berated for doing that.- Light vs. Dark. This is such a tired and boring trope and I'm frankly tired of seeing it in games. The thing is that this game has a lot of potential for throwing out that concept completely and leaving it ambiguous to what is the "better" option. Both end game options can be perceived as overall good or bad, but by assigning this "Light vs. Dark" thing, it makes it obvious what the right choice is supposed to be. Also the light and dark pixies are annoying and I hate it every single time they pop up. I don't need to be hit over the head with this stupid concept when the core story of this game would be way better off without it. This also extends to the clear "evil vs. good" clans. It's annoying, get rid of this trope.- The clans. There are six in total, 3 light and 3 dark. I like this concept, it's so cool and could really show what each clan believes is the right thing to do. It simply doesn't though. Instead all 3 light clans are the exact same, and all 3 dark clans are the exact same. For example, if you go to the website talking about clans and read about the Netra it specifically says that the Netra want to defeat the world eaters but believes the clans (they're called Tribes btw, but I like the term clan so that's what I'm using) should remain independent and free. However, when you go to join them their goals end up being the same as the Myraid and the sifu's speech is the exact same, word for word. What your actually choosing between is clan weapons, which you get anyway by defeating each clan so there's no real reason to change clans.I know I went in depth about each issue here, but at the end of the day they really are small things in the overall enjoyment of this game. You can turn off the narrator. You can ignore the sprites. You can choose a clan based on which one you think looks neat or whatever. There's so much more to this game then three issues and I don't think they are nearly bad enough to take away from this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy this game. I wanted an exploration combat game with a unique world to be immersed in. I really enjoy the interactions with the characters, the way they sound, look, etc. <--- This and the narration are the reason for a lot of negative reviews, I just feel entirely different I guess. Narration can be tweaked down. I was glad that the beginning of the game spent a lot of time teaching, walking you through some concepts while still doing some exploring and interacting. <----- This is also a reason for a lot of negative reviews and the intro period has been shortened in the last patch. Guess I'm glad I got to do that part before the patch!I love the combat system. It's not just a matter of using different weapons that have slight variations. You unlock abilities for these weapons and more importantly, you build your weapons with found items be they melee or ranged. Ranged: pick your handle, stock, magazine, base, muzzle, add ons etc. Until you get the feel, just use the top found items and wala. You can completely combine melee and ranged in your battles. It doesn't even stop there, combine your unlocked Psi mutant abilities in battle, your unlocked bio mutant abilities and add special ammo to your ranged weapons. There is SO much to mix and match that it's up to player creativity to pick and swap battle style and go with what feels the most fun for you. <---- A lot of the negative reviews are because some feel battle is stale, etc. Again, I just feel completely differently. I love the exploration and how beautiful the world is. I admit the same buildings etc can get a bit repetitive but overall the world is lovely. The lack of more unique towns, point of interest layout, etc is somewhat offset by all the different biomes and the fun of trying to reach hard to get to places via things like gliding abilities or using your bio mutant abilities to conjure bouncy mushrooms to jump way higher than you would ordinarily be able to. <---- A lot of negative reviews are because some feel the world is beautiful but stale. I only partially agree with the sentiment. I feel that if you can enjoy the immersion of the game and get into the story where it even takes you back to childhood experiences that help shape and further the story, all the adorable creatures you interact with etc, the game is fantastic. If you're looking to just get l33t and constantly battle, unlock things, battle, unlock things, loot, profit: This game may not be for you. The creators took a lot of time to make a unique world and pace things out to make sure you can get the most out of immersion in this world. I even enjoy the little touches like lifting defunct couch cushions once in a while to check for loot, urinating on signposts to unlock them for fast travel, etc. I don't know if I have ever reviewed a game before but with as many negative reviews as this game has gotten, I felt a strong desire to do so. I bought the game on release day. If I had waited and read reviews, it's likely I would not have gotten it or waited a long time. As much as I am enjoying the game, I'm glad I bought it before all the reviews!

_childDocuments_.review: "Cute" Action RPG, where you have to unite the land against an ultimate threat. You get to choose wether you join the dark or the light side, which might influence the ending. Also your characters look changes, depending on how you allocate stat points, or learn mutations later in the game, which is in my opinion its strongest and most interesting point.The dialogue has lots of made up words like mooma and poppa, up to the point where it just gets annoying and confusing, almost like you're in a children's story. There's also lots of finger waggling and "pollution is bad" talk, which is just unneeded and gets annoying over time.Combat is fun so far, it consists of shooting, attacking with melee, dodging and using special attacks occasionally. It's prety well done action combat I'd say.Overall I would say that the look of the world and gameplay mechanics are done pretty well, while the storytelling, made up names and finger-waggling pollution-is-bad-mkay story is really not for adults and makes one want to skip those cutscenes. And fortunately: you can!

Yeah, it saves money to have one person narrate stuff so you don't have to pay people to voice all the characters but come on.. I turned the narrator off.Anyway, it's not worth the current price of £17.49 and definitely not worth the full price.Paid reviews/lies:4.5/5 – We Got This Covered - "robust character customisation" - You mean the very limited options? Ok.9.5/10 – GameSpace - "Frankly, I’ll be surprised if BIOMUTANT is not game of the year.” - It has to be good to get GOTY.9.5/10 – Game Revolution - "A true modern gaming miracle.” - A real miracle would be 90%+ off for this game(?)I need to pee.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game - it’s not bad, it’s just mediocre. Overall the actual game structure and gameplay feels very dated, continuing the banjo kazooie comparison, this feels like an N64 era game to me with modern graphics and open world - fetch and collect crap, defeat 4 mini bosses, best game. It feels like a throwback (so if you’re looking for that you might really dig it).This is overlaid with quite convoluted RPG character progression and weapon upgrades, but it all feels very meaningless and tacked on.Overall - I don’t hate this game, it’s not bad and if you want a nice easy going time you can do a lot worse…But the game is a lot like its protagonist - a slightly weird mutant mix of different parts. I’m not sure if it was just too ambitious, or the devs weren’t given the time to finish it properly, but it feels like there’s the makings of a great game here but it just never quite gets there.

_childDocuments_.review: This review turned out a bit long, so here's a short summary:Promising and ambitious but is ultimately incoherent and feels like a chore. Grab it if it's on a significant sale and the world looks interesting to you, otherwise don't bother.~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~Pros:- Art style is delightful, world is intereting enough to draw you in, and has a ton of charm.- Combat is easy to learn and feels extremely fun once you get the hang of it.- Giant open world with plenty content to do.- A lot of choice when it comes to progression AND story both, with a dark / light path you can choose between in most situations. This includes freeroam interactions or interacting with specific objects on the map that can tip the scales either side, making it very helpful if you need to correct a mistake or simply want to cap out one or the other.- There's a LOT in terms moves and special abilities to use and level, so regardless of starting class, you can deviate away from that and build your character how you feel comfortable, swapping spells around depending on combat or traversal, if it comes to it.- Very high amount of customizing possible including looks, armor, weaponry and mounts, with the ability to alter your appearance later on if you change your mind.Cons:- Narrative and story are disjointed, weightless and at times make no sense at all. Characters react seemingly at random to what you say, and your dialog options jump between straightforward and overly cryptic nonsense, making it impossible to discern what you're about to respond with.- Interacting with NPCs can get downright irritating; them speaking an otherwise charming gibberish with the Narrator voicelines overlaid 'translating' them (even if this can be finetuned in the options somewhat).- Some sidecontent doesn't give you a clue on how to figure it out, so you can be stuck near endlessly trying to find a key to open a door, only to find the monster that swallowed the key did not show up where the map tells you it should.- The above can mean you cannot complete one or two things on the checklist associated with a specific zone, which gets annoying for map completions' sake, besides literally barring you from possible loot. Sometimes loot you need to find for these checklists is also in unmarked dirt piles which are hard to spot and can be missed entirely.- Puzzles work on limited steps you can take, and if they run out, you lose health and have to retry. You can pump your intellect stat to get more steps, but even then some puzzles just can't be solved in the allotted number of those, forcing you to retry until you get lucky, and the puzzle starts in a state you can solve with how many steps you got. (This includes story-critical puzzles.)- Enemies and bosses do next to no telepgraphing to some attacks they do, nor do they have recovery time between them, but YOU do. This can result in getting completely obliterated by repeated combo spams by two giant enemies, while you were either animationlocked in a dodgeroll you might not even wanted to do, or out of stamina, unable to avoid anything. Did I mention some enemy grab attacks also ignore you dodging? Because we got those too.- The above point also means that some fights are nigh impossible with melee, making you have to kite and use ranged, which in turn can completely suck any enjoyment out of fights.- There's so much stuff lying around as loot that your bags will be completely full of useless equipment that you're forced to either sort through, scrap or sell every half an hour.- Crafting is made generally obsolete very quick due to loot that's just simply better and found out in the world. This only worsens the previous point, as now you have components to manage too.In the end, I really, really wanted to like this game, but it just turned so frustrating and confusing after a while rather than enjoyable. The style and premise made it incredibly interesting to me, and this weird, semi-magical post apocalyptic scenario is charming as hell, but there're so many things weighing it down, that for me it was disappointing.Like I said at the start of this (incredibly wordsy) review; if the initial looks from the store page are enough to draw you in, AND the game is on a big sale, give it a try. Otherwise, it's an over-ambitious but ultimately under-achieving game that isn't really making it worth the time, and especially not the default price it has.

Diving into bunkers to loot, finding what's left in there, and fiddling with old technology is awesome. Not to mention how GORGEOUS the world is, too! Not just graphically; it's a genuinely beautiful world full of color and amazing landscapes!The gameplay is great as well; having a melee combat system, but you also have a *GUN* is great. Crafting weapons is fun and wonderful, too!This game is not perfect, but it's great for what it is! The progression could be smoother, but the world and combat are really good. _childDocuments_.review: I know it has been a while since its release but I don't get all the hate this game has garnered. I suspect because it has a cutesy factor that turns some people off but it isn't meant to be serious. I enjoyed the expansive open world which is beautiful, the combat was fun and I found it engaging. The different environments ensured you couldn't blast through an area all at once since you had to build up your character and depending on what you find, you're forced to leave an area on part of the map alone and come back to it later when you're buffed enough for it.Cyberpunk could learn something from this game when it comes to crafting. I loved collecting shwack loads of parts and seeing what crazy stuff I could put together. There were so many options I could really customize different weapons for different encounters depending on elemental immunity of the opponents. I really enjoyed exploring to see what I could find and the menu improvements from release just made it so much better getting rid of stuff you don't want. Then there are the different powers you could get. Again, the different options and combos you could do were really varied and I made sure to get them all as some you do need to get really good stuff in hard to reach places even if you don't use them elsewhere. I feel like there were enough options for different play styles.Okay, the narration does getting annoying after a while so I just turned that sucker down so I don't have to listen to him yap so much. Some parts are repetitive but there is a decent variety of things to do and stuff to find I didn't get bored enough to stop playing (unlike Far Cry 6).The other thing is since there is no gore, the game is more accessible for younger audiences too, which again, may turn some people off but I accepted the game for what it is. I found it a refreshing change of style from so many other games that go all out on the gore. You want that, go play Doom Eternal.Although pretty light on plot, discovering the lore of the world and piecing together how it wound up the way it is added more dimension. Exploring the world as completely as you can makes sure you get the best stuff.Is it the best game of 2021, no. However, it doesn't deserve the hate it got. I think THQ struck on something even if they missed the mark on some things. The ending does set up for a sequel easily enough so hopefully THQ will accept the good feedback and improve on the 2nd outing which I hope they will do.

_childDocuments_.review: Look, the concept, world and scenery is amazing. The game is beautiful, and theres a lot to love here, hell theres an elvis in this game that had me laughing for 15 minutes.But...The character customization was super underwhelming, the creation of breeds doesnt really do anything, as they all look extremely similar and some options like the dart frog-esque arm are locked in. Weapon customization may as well not be a thing because there is a clear meta in the gun parts that leaves you little option. Basically, DPS is the only thing that matters. Guns themselves are an absolute joke and trivialize most of what i saw in 5 hours; you become a turret that can sprint from spot to spot while enemies dumbly follow you at a snail's pace and few if enemies have anything but a basic melee attack, and any special attack comes with huge warnings and is child's play to dodge, and I saw no ranged attackers at all. Even worse was that no enemy, even boss types, had any way to counter ranged spam. In short, machine guns make this game a cake walk.World is so empty but so beautiful, and the biggest sin by far is the lack of voicing. Characters make these jibber jabber noises and the narrator translates, but he never sticks to one way or style, so sometimes its third person past tense, other times its second person present tense, etc. This MURDERS the immersion and makes dialogue very boring and since its ONE guy narrating DOZENS of hours of dialogue, you will grow to hate this poor man despite his incredible storytelling voice. Sidequests have no depth being shallow enough to win a bethesda award, and like i said the world is just so darn empty, the only NPCs i ever saw were enemies at specific, scripted locations, with no faction system so everyone is just naturally hostiel because guess what, all the world NPCs are magically the faction you didn't pick in the over TWO HOUR tutorial segment.Melee combat is okay, its serviceable but nothing special. Combos are often a waste of time apart from the dedicated boss types as generic mobs have neither the health nor the threat to bother combo'ing. Vendors rarely have anything for sale, let alone anything GOOD for sale, i mean every time i checked a vendor they had a few items and it was stuff i was finding 20 minutes ago.The tutorial HOLY ♥♥♥♥♥ this tutorial, it is literally like 2.5 entire hours, and in the last 45 minutes you get stopped every minute or two for exposition, or rather for the narrator to either translate the annoying jabbering of NPCs, or to explain something pointless over a near static image, sometimes things we would be much better off not knowing as they don't matter or just dont affect you as a character. Morality system is just garbage, the entire game is only good or evil, theres no grey areas or third options and the choices are clearly defined, i mean the options literally have a LIGHT and DARK sprite over them to tell you which to pick, and thats the only RPG element since you can only talk to quest and vendor NPCs who dont have any dialogue options other than "continue".Game has a solid foundation with great core ideas and the devs clearly put their hearts and souls into this, but theyre an inexperienced first time studio so to speak, and the game suffers greatly for it, with janky writing, an empty world, a completely boring cast of characters with no personality on account of not being voiced, and of course, the most cut and dry "good guy v bad guy" story since superman first appeared on screen. Hopefully theyll continue updating it with fixes, (Update: all theyve done in YEARS was a few bugfixes) but as it stands i give it a 5/10 (Updating to a 2/10. This game is effectively a $60 PC equivalent to an art book from a comicon artist) pretty average, sometimes below average game that only excels in being really pretty to look at at running extremely well (I used an RX 580 at the time).Hope the devs come back in the near future to absolutely slam dunk a reboot or sequel-boot, or even a new IP, but this game aint worth it. Like i said, its effectively an art book with a few jokes that you get to press a few buttons while looking at it.

_childDocuments_.review: As my previous review stated, I was going to wait to see what 101 does before attempting a refund. Well, today we got our first patch.. One of the LONGEST I have ever seen.. To be fair, that is NOT a bad thing at all. The list is extensive. Ranging from quality of life, amplifying sounds, and fixing some jank. And so far? Very good! I have to give it to 101, they came out swinging and I am enjoying the game so much more. There are still some thing I would like to see added (lock on), and I am not far in the game (just took my first outpost) so things may pop up again. Just to note, one thing I did notice was right when I loaded in, before the first real boss, my FPS shot down to 30 FPS. Moving into the fight, it fixed itself and no issues since thank God. So nothing major.  However, I really kept the game because it seems they are open to criticism and this industry desperately needs more devs like this. I did not see ANY news from 101 after release. Some may say this is bad, but imo, it just means they sat down and got to work. They did not want to make empty promises, bash the community, find a safe space on some whack website. They knew it was a "nut up or shut up" kind of moment. And after this update, I truly believe 101 has a mural of Talladega himself. Honestly, I am still not the biggest fan of the lack luster story (I will continue to think rodents running around doing kung-fu should have a story to tell). But I like the graphics, the combat is flashy and fun, and the world is something new and fresh. I just hope 101 add to it. That being said, they proved they are not abandoning this game, and will continue to work on it. Hopefully they learn from Biomutant short comings and come back from that. But for now, they earned my money.

It was fine until the patterns and colors....then, into the game, it was practically a 2 hour tutorial, and I don't like how there is a 5-10 minute dialog for every inch of play. You want to craft gear? Listen to this guy talk TWICE (once for the character and another for the narrator to translate) just to learn you won't actually be able to craft for a LONG time because you have to find the resources. The combat system really threw me. Having to hold 1 button, in order to use 4 other abilities, instead of just using a simple 1-5. (Yes I'm aware you can change the hotkeys, but most of them are already in use.) It was just made to be much more complicated than it needed to be. I feel like the dialog really makes the game feel incredibly slow since you have to hear mumbles and then a translation. Would have been better to either cut the narrator, and just use subtitles for the character (similar to animal crossing) or just had voice actors for them. I don't really understand when people say the combat gets boring, I think it's more so just complicated and disorganized. It was a little lame basically just running in circles around rather dumb npcs and just go back and forth trying to kill a thing that basically just stood still. It wasn't challenging, maybe that's what they meant by boring.The story is also not anything super special, but I didn't think it was boring, just was a bit slow and unneeded to go back and forth in time, when a simple cutscene would've worked. They try and get you into this rpg, but when you're trying to get into the character, and talk to people in YOUR language but need a narrator to translate? Kind of takes you out of it.Basically after several hours in, I just had to stop because I was getting more upset than I was enjoyment out of the game. I think it has so much potential but I just don't think it's ready yet. This game is nice, but I don't think it's worth the $60.

_childDocuments_.review: An enticing universe I wish I loved.        Almost canceled my pre-order.. Said no I'll give it a shot. People are saying this is cyberpunk with fur but in all honesty i would pay for cyberpunk again, bugs and all before I recommend Biomutant at full price. It tries to be everything you want it to be but delivers on none of its promises. All the Story, Audio, and World Building aside ill just speak on the gameplay loop. Which at first seems great until you realize youre just playing a Loot box simulator with tacked on combat.          Somehow something as gratifying as loot becomes tainted with displeasure as you learn the addition of Add-ons to any armor renders its stats Void and will just straight up not apply them to your character.  There are also Vault weapon rewards that are so strong they just outright replace all your looted gear until practically max level.            Ability stats feel as though they have no impact on anything aside from crit chance. Even then being over 100% crit i still land white hits. Loot Chance stat feels useless as you never know when its actually changing your luck.. everyone i know has the same level or better gear and i have 228% loot find while they have maybe 40%. The Character screen that displays your stats doesnt take into account all of your collective talents, so you see a baseline number and have to do go back and remember all the additional perks you might have picked up to see total output.         All in all I enjoy the world and exploration but the constant recycling of objectives just makes further exploration a chore. Some exploration is locked behind level 2 Upgrades on your items and when you visit the character who can upgrade they send you on a fetch quest to another character who then sends you on a second fetch quest. And of course its an open world rpg so there are enemy forts to capture, but these are copy pasted as well. I found myself opting for the passive dialogue choice just to get it over with.        And thats what sums up playing this game, you just want to get it over with to get to the better gameplay and unfortunately that gameplay just keeps eluding the player. This game suffers from what many games this era suffer from, "Come back in two years and it'll be better"

_childDocuments_.review: For starters, let me tell you that this is not a perfect game. I CAN tell you however, that the Trailer for this game does not do it justice. Shocker right. We are all too aware of the fact that developers are gods at creating a good looking trailer, but the actual game tends not to match up. Its due to the creativity and misleading that they can use to hype their game up. Bio Mutant however, is not like that. The game starts out decent. The character creation is, in my opinion, one of the best. Its simple. You don't spend an hour making it perfect, and the choices you make with it are important. I chose to go with an Agility and Strength focus. I love hack and slash games like Metal Gear Rising and Nier. This is just like those. Now lets get to the details.Music:Lets start out with the worst quality. The music. Its not that its bad, but instead its that its underwhelming. I can't actually think of a moment where the music resonated with me and as I speak...I have no idea what any of the music sounds like. Its not bad, but its probably more along the lines of it lacking impact.Audio (other than music):The audio is great. The sound effects are very crisp. I love a lot of what the audio brings and the only complaint I have is that the combat lost weight on strikes due to the lack of what I can only assume is bass. When striking enemies, unless its with an ability, its very quiet.Although I say this, I actually enjoyed the game so much that I didn't mind it. Combining both CQC and Fire arms actually dampens the impact of this complaint.Graphics:Anyone who says that this game looks horrible or this game is not gorgeous...they are kinda dumb. I am playing this game at Max Visuals and its stunning. Im constantly looking around my peripherals to truly enjoy the environment. If people can agree that Breath of The Wild is a beautiful game, then this game is just as gorgeous.Open World:The Open World is pretty simple. It actually opens up quite well. As soon as the world became available to me in the beginning, I found myself so invested in just looking around and investigating whatever I found. I just experienced things as they came and somehow ended up across the map without even doing some of the first campaign quests. The Open World is nothing different per say, but that doesn't mean its the same. Its delivery and flavoring. They make quests and side quests short and sweet....but they give you a lot of them. You also don't have to follow any path. If you see something interesting you can go to it. If there is a quest you dont want to do, then just ignore it for now. Its freeing. Pairing the beautiful world they created with the graphics and art style they use is a recipe for success.Character & Equipment:They managed to actually make an enticing crafting system. The equipment is simple. You have the following: Head Armor, Torso Armor, Shoulder Armor (Both Sides), Leg Armor, Main hand (weapon), Off Hand (Weapon), and a ranged weapon (with the optional dual wield). You can craft weapons, while you find armor through various means. You can also use addons to your armor. These give you different stat boosts and alter your appearance. The best part about the equipment is the crafting. Its Simple. Each weapon type has a certain amount of parts you can use. You litterally buy or scavenge parts and put together and build your own weapons. I built a shotgun for the first time and forgot to put a stock on it. Totally missed out on an even stronger weapon because of that. The promise and let down that fallout 4's weapon crafting is reconciled when using this game's system. Its simple and fun.Misc: There are so many other details I want to include in this review.  I just want to point out that BioMutant is being given a hard time...and its understandable, but not deserved. I can see where the biggest critique is of the nararator who talks a lot. I however didn't see this to be a big turn away. In fact, I enjoyed many of his quips. The dialogue in the game is fair. It can be annoying and I understand, but I read so fast that I usually skip and just read subtitles. I personally enjoy and understand the importance of the narrarator. If they didnt have him, then the game wouldn't have a good story. It was a smart move in order to leave the game as open as it did. For a final note, I want to say that the game isn't perfect. That being said, I give a high rating specifically because I enjoyed the game a lot. I didn't harp on issues I had. Given that I have had like 100 gameovers to drowning...I didn't give in to my dark side and hate the game as much as it bothered me. Instead, you should try it yourself. Honestly, given the last 4 or so years of really garbage games that were hyped up only to be unfinished or just bad on release...BioMutant really knocked it out the park. It was a very good experience and Im gonna keep playing it and pouring my time into it. So even if you don't like the game or think that its using the same mechanics of any other open world game, I want you to just ask yoursuelf whether the game was fun or it wasn't.Overall:Music: 4Audio: 7Graphics: 9Open World: 8Character & Equipment: 9Score: 7.4/10This game utilizes the same mechanics we have seen in the past, but to a unique and different extent. for the past 4 years, I have gotten hyped for a game time and time again only for it to flop and really suck. Cought Cough 76....cough....Anthem....cough...CyberCuck....I think its unique and will be one of my favorite single player experiences. I expected something worse from this game and when I started playing it, I couldnt put it down....so If a Kung Fu, Action RPG, Nier Automata, Chaotic Fighting, Exploration, Puzzle Game sounds like it might be interesting...give it a try...

_childDocuments_.review: This is a hard game to review. I had a lot of fun playing, but there are also so many strange shortcomings or things that could have been great and just aren't. I hope more people play this game, but at the same time I wouldn't recommend this game to everyone. In the long run, a small team took some risks to make a new and fresh IP, and they've mostly succeeded - and they continue to listen to community feedback and make good revisions on an already strong start. So where does that leave us?There are some aspects of Biomutant that are done really well, some that are a stylistic choice and either will work for you or not, and other parts that are either just bad design or missed opportunities - your mileage may vary depending on how much you can overlook the bad and how you feel  about the more divisive choices. I have no regrets purchasing this game, and found a lot of the core gameplay loop to be quite engaging, while still relaxing to play, so overall this is definitely a thumbs up for me. That said, I think reviews should help others decide, and want to give a balanced take. Things that are good: Character customization is well done, with a lot of options (breed, class, starting resistance, fur colors, body shape) for personalization, and some areas in the game where you can revisit and tweak the cosmetic ones. Exploration is probably the game's greatest strength - a lot of beautiful environments with something curious to investigate everywhere you look. When this is combined with a fun and extensive looting and crafting system, you've got a good recipe for fun outside of the main quest lines - and at about 64 square kilometers, the map is big enough to keep you busy for dozens of hours just exploring. The variety of mounts and vehicles available in the game is really fun as well - while some of the best are unfortunately bound to specific map zones, it's still great to be able to have such variety (a jet ski, a blimp, a gliding bat creature, a robotic horse, a giant mech, a furry shark, a blimp, etc...). Movement is enjoyable, graphics look nice, and there's a decent variety of enemy skins (though less variety in actual enemy attack patterns). The general, mostly open structure of the main quests (that allow you to do them in any order, or ignore them entirely for dozens of hours) is also nice. The biomutations and psionic powers that are in the game are pretty fun to use, and sufficiently different from each other to make changing up those you've got keybound worthwhile. The general design of the assets overall - from the buildings, to the clothes and gear, to the biomes, and the enemies - all worked for me. Including a photo mode was a really smart move - it's a gorgeous, flashy, silly game, and it was really nice to be able to capture some of its better moments. I enjoyed the combat - I think it's the kind of thing that is as fun as you make it. It's pretty easy fairly early in the game to craft a gun that will melt anything quickly, but sitting back and mowing things down gets boring fast. If you learn the wung fu combos, make use of parrying and dodging, incorporate the biogenetics and psi powers, and even switch weapons on the fly, there's a fair amount of variety and it can be really fun to manage enemy mobs. This is no souls-like, nor is it quite as polished as a Platinum game, however - it's more like the combat you'd find in an action platformer or metroidvania, with a few elements borrowed from other fast-paced hack and slash games (like air juggling, bullet time, etc). This is also an important positive for the game - the developers have been AMAZINGLY responsive to community feedback, and have already at the time of this review (i.e. in the first month since release) put out two huge patches that addressed many of the most glaring quality of life issues and a good number of general requests. It's clear this team wants the game to succeed, and are doing what they can to make it as strong as possible. The bad: if you spend as much time looting and exploring as I did, the reuse of assets becomes very apparent. In some cases, whole quests and dialog are cut and pasted, particularly in the tribe wars and even in the 4 main bosses - while on the surface they have variety, it's the same fight with a few different skins each time. The morality system feels underdeveloped (and I personally found the little angel / devil exchanges some of the most annoying dialog in the game) and in general, while the game is going for a nostalgic, youthful vibe, the constant bludgeoning of the main themes and the heavy-handed moralizing gets tiring. The overall writing, combined with the lack of main character voice acting, means that there was no real emotional investment for me. If you're looking to play a game for story, this isn't it. General NPCs  are such a waste of time to talk to that I stopped bothering in the first few hours, even though there's a chance one might tell you about a "secret" location at some point - but all these locations you'll either find exploring or get a side quest chain that will point you to it eventually anyway. The fact that the characters speak gibberish, and THEN the narrator translates, also makes all dialog take way too long to be worth it whenever you can avoid it. Your mileage might vary: The narrator has been really divisive it seems. I do wish they had done voice acting for the main characters, but overall I didn't personally mind having a Fable-like narrator accompany me - and sometimes I downright enjoyed it. In any case, the narrator's voice actor did a great job, and the devs have added a number of settings that can significantly reduce or even disable narration, so it's up to you. The tone and gibberish-like names for everything might turn some folks off - I found a lot of the names pretty funny, and overall appreciated that this game feels like its channeling an older, colorful action platformer - but in terms of how the tone contributes to the sense of investment and the overall storytelling, that was a miss for me. The side quests are pretty basic, and mostly just checklists of repeated elements (find all of X in the world, etc.), which is fine if you mostly just want to explore, loot, fight, rinse, repeat - but disappointing if you want meaningful additions to the overall story. The puzzles are laughably easy save one or two - which didn't bother me, but also didn't add to my experience. If anything, it's the missed opportunities here that make this a good game instead of a great one. It's a game with a lot of breadth, but little depth. The systems (classes, breeds, psi powers, biomutations, environmental biomes, etc) all hint at a lot of choice, but don't matter that much in the end - you can get all powers, resistances, general skills, and wung fu easily in a playthrough and have many leftover points in a single game; after a while you'll have crafted the best gear you can and looting or shops return nothing that can compete; the tribe war seems like a great concept until you realize it's the same 3 campaigns over and over; the tribal weapons all seem cool but can't be upgraded and don't compare to what you can craft in the world; there's no real difference between most mounts except aesthetics. Despite all of this, I still found myself wanting to play every night I could for a month. While I started noticing a lot of repetition early on, I was still finding the occasional neat new element up until I finished the game. I had a lot of fun despite the flaws. I'd suggest watching some gameplay and seeing what you think before diving in - but if you like what you see, there's a lot fun adventuring to be had.

_childDocuments_.review: I refused to look at reviews for this game until after I had an initial impression on it. I was one of those people who thought "well, I am going to judge a game for myself and ignore the reviews." Not so much because I want to discount what other people are saying (and continue to say) but because I judge games differently than other people.I'm a very casual gamer. I don't play for the challenge, I play for the experience. IMO, Biomutant ticks off everything for me in all the right ways, and while there are a few things I don't like, I am not too bummed that I spent the full price of 60 on it.Things I love: -the story. It's simple, it's quaint, and while it isn't deep I figure it does what it needs to do. Love the flashback bits where you steadily recount the protagonist's history. -Like the morality scale. It's nice you can play a jerk, even though I never will haha-Love the narrator. He's cute. While I wish everyone had proper voice acting and the narrator makes it sickeningly obvious that there wasn't a budget for that, it does give the game a "story book" vibe and I personally enjoy it.- Lol you pee on signposts to mark them for fast travel- The crafting!! It's neat and easy to understand, and not too convoluted for idiots like me!- the setting. Beautiful world, interesting to explore, lots to see!-THE VEHICLES/MOUNTS ARE AMAZING HOLY ♥♥♥♥-The puzzles are easy. I'm an idiot so I am thankful for this.-Goofy ass dialogue. Sounds like it was made by people trying to sound fantasy-like. Taking it seriously is not what I think was intended; the silly words feel very cheeky to me.-The combat. Flows well, not too sluggish, easy to pick up and learn.-The enemy designs are a mix between spooky, cute, and really unique. Love them.-NPCs are pretty. Mounts are pretty. Everything's super pretty and I wish I could pet all the bang bang raccoons I find walking aroundThings that kinda annoy me:-The animations.. or lack thereof, in some cases.. are a bit jarring. Most bosses do the same thing. Attack patterns really don't change.- The character creator. Why is my appearance tied to stats? That's a no-go for me, joe.-The combat difficulty, or lack thereof.. I personally don't mind the easyness, but I know some people are going to hate it.-Wish the NPCs had more to say. They all seem to say the same thing, with some words switched around. They say you're a good kid and go on some annoying speel about how life is deep or some ♥♥♥♥. Wish they were less corny or at the very least had some differentiating dialogue.-Wish the NPCs were.. well, more. They look nice but that's about it. They have no distinct personalities or histories or anything. It's either "I'm eeeevul and want to destroy da wurld" or "I'm a piece of optimistic soggy cardboard with no decernable personality traits other than I'm trying to sound deep but I'm really not"-....Also the combat. Too easy. No difficulty whatsoever. Not a deal breaker for me but I know it will be for others looking for a more standard RPG experience.-There *should* be an option for more difficult puzzles for people who want them. Think puzzle difficulty from silent hill. Not everyone is willing to trudge through easy puzzles and some people just want a challenge, and there's nothing wrong with that.All in all? I rate it a 6/10. A little above mediocre, but still veeery enjoyable imo. not really worth the 60 bucks but def, DEFinitely get it on sale. It's such a nice little experience and I am hoping there will be more content for this game in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: The post-apocalyptic environment is gorgeous to look at, whether it's the lush wilderness or the remnants of a city that got me to sing City Ruins (Rays of Light) from Nier Automata. It's also diverse too, which is definitely a welcome change from desert-y wastelands found in Fallout, Mad Max, and Fist of the North Star. I never get bored from looking at everything while heading to my next objective or getting sidetracked to what's left of a convenience store, houses, and other structures humanity left behind. The critters' design may be hit-or-miss, but for the most part, they look absolutely adorable! Their fur is well-shaded, and the various animations that The Protagonist has can be charmingly cute (i.e proudly posing with their hands on their hips after acquiring a spankin' new set of clothes). Plus, I find it strangely attractive to interact with various modern day gadgets like washing machines or arcade cabinet from the perspective of a mutated critter. I love the inclusion of Chinese instruments in the soundtracks, and they definitely give me the right feels from time to time when exploring the New World. My only complaint is that it changes abruptly whenever you go into an indoor area from the outside and vice-versa. I wish that it plays without any interruptions. The crafting system is rad (pun totally intended), especially when it comes to making your own melee weapons and guns. I can't say the same for clothes however, seeing as how most of the addons may not match the overall aesthetics. Combat can get somewhat tedious and frustrating, especially when facing off against a large mob of enemies that can easily interrupt your melee attacks and knock you flat on your ass. It makes it easier to fall back on the dominant strategy, aka using powerful crafted guns or Super Wung-Fu, to take shots from a safe distance. It's fun at first, but then it gets repetitive the more you rely on it. The lack of a dedicated lock-on system like the one in Yakuza or Nier means that it's really frustrating when most of your shots miss or they hit the wrong enemy. The Narrator is talented and has a great voice, but when overused, he becomes an annoyance. Because of how he translates  of the gibberish that the characters speak in using a relatively neutral tone, a lot of their characterization gets lost as a result. I find it easier to relate to characters when they are speaking directly to The Protagonist (and by extension, the player) without an interpreter doing all the heavy lifting. One way to remedy this is to either have the gibberish subtitled or let the characters (and the Protagonist) speak in partially corrupted English/Russian/Japanese/etc. The Light/Dark Karma System feels too simplistic to allow a lot of room for creating nuances in characters' personalities, especially when I want to roleplay The Protagonist as a flawed yet compassionate individual. It doesn't help that the six tribes and their leaders are given shallow characterization, and they don't do much in the story aside from waiting and hoping for The Protagonist to join them so they can further their agendas. I wish that they were more active in the setting, and perhaps scrapping or hiding the Karma System so the characters will be given more chances to develop. The game's exploration of the theme of balance feels to me that it's hampered by the presence of a mechanical scale. The sidequests, like killing giant monsters or finding and interacting with modern day technologies, are fun at the beginning, but they become a slog later on the in the game. The puzzles also feel too simple to be challenging.  The main plot doesn't feel cohesive. After finishing a pure Light side playthrough, it felt to me as though the writers were having troubles deciding on how to tie up loose plot threads, and one thing ended just as it's about to become interesting.  Some of the invented words are a little over-the-top that they don't appeal to anyone at all.Biomutant is, for the lack of better words, a flawed game. It deserves a try, even if it's a wait-for-sale type of game. It has a lot of interesting ideas that are cobbled together, but sadly, aren't fully developed. I believe that a game like this could benefit from either a soft reboot, a much-improved sequel, or a more refined spiritual successor.

_childDocuments_.review: The game has a charming art style and overall pretty map to explore, but its honestly kinda terrible.My 3 biggest gripes with this game are the following:1) The combat2) The way dialogue and story is delivered, as well as the "lore" and naming conventions for everything3) The gameplay loop of explore > loot worthless junk > repeatCombatI played on Hard from the very start and have found the entire thing to be devoid of challenge and strategy.The AI will literally just walk towards you in a straight line, taking a very long time to react, attack you, etc, you can cheese literally every encounter in the game by just strafing backwards and in a circle around the enemy.Guns (not the weapon class, just firearms in general) utterly dominate combat, melee feels extremely ineffectual, clunky and slow by comparison. Even among guns, not all weapon classes are equal. Most guns can't hit the broad side of a barn, shotgun pellets will spread at 70 degree angles out towards the sides of the screen and deal pretty abysmal damage.For 80% of my time in the game every single combat encounter consisted of me holding down left mouse button while using an automatic rifle and walking left or right until all enemies were dead.Aside from this you just press the dodge button to instantly dodge virtually any attack in the game, and sometimes you press the parry key to instantly parry an incoming melee attack. That's it, there is no more to the combat mechanics here.You get access to a variety of generic perks (stuff like +% reload speed, fire rate, damage, etc) that only help make combat even easier. If you really want to, you can invest in psi abilities and all that, all of which seem to be pretty terrible and kind of a waste of time. None of the attributes or skills felt particularly useful to me, so I dumped basically all my points into Luck and increasing my elemental resistances (which mind you are worthless until you get them to 100%).Dialogue/Story/LoreAll dialogue is, and I'm not even joking, delivered to you by a literal third person translating in rough terms what the character you are speaking to is telling you in a hyper obnoxiously vague and patronizing way.This is the narrator, some random british bloke who will speak to you for the entire duration of the game.The way he delivers all dialogue makes it impossible to take anything seriously, and extremely difficult to follow along what it is people actually want from you, or what the plot is even about.As an example, lets say you meet an npc, the npc is trying to convey to you that this one monster has been causing problems, can be found in a bomb shelter and that he'd appreciate if you could go kill it, the npc is also dismayed that you have decided to join a tribe that want's to literally destroy the world.This is how the narrator delivers this:"Smogums speaks of the Garglam. The munster has caused a big meanie-peanie and so Smogums asks you to hunt the Garglam. Smogums says the Garglam can be found in the boom-boom cave in the nono zone. Smogums is saddened to hear that you have decided to help the Jiggamans, but says its okay and doesn't matter perhaps."Initially I wanted to assume that this was him translating things for you (because I think he's the grasshopper that follows you around?), but he also translates what your own mom and dad tell you in these annoying flashback scenes, what various characters you supposedly already know and have spoken to in the past tell you, and no one else in the entire world needs any devices to speak to you.On top of the awful way of dialogue delivery, the narrator will also chime in with the most agonizingly childish quips and descriptions for random things in the world. It's funny or insightful, I'm not 4 years old, I don't appreciate walking up to a toilet and being told that the Flushy-Wushy from the-time-before was used to do the boom-booms uwu.All the items also follow the narrators naming convention too, it's like the devs gave a bunch of drugs to the local kindergarteners and wrote down all the dumb things they said for inspiration. It's so tiresome and childish man.In part thanks to the intrusive narrator and the way the devs decided to deliver exposition and dialogue to you it becomes brutally difficult to follow along the story or to even glean what characters are about or why you're even doing anything, so most of your encounters with npcs will consist of you being spoken to like you're mentally challenged and being sent on some random fetch quest without context.You have "dialogue options" which all result in the same response.What these usually do is give you dark/light morality points (which do nothing and have no effect). Waste of time.Same with choices, you are often given the illusion of choice, but nothing really matters and nothing seems to really change.The lore of the setting isn't super deep either. The tl;dr is that civilization has gone under """"eons ago"""" because one singular corporation dumped toxic waste in the ocean. The entire world seems pretty green and safe by the way, food appears to be pretty plentiful, everyone is a vegetarian (i think?) and everyone seems pretty cool and chill with things. But they will still insist that the world "is ending", whatever that means. No, they will not explain more about the locations you explore, this corporation that caused all of this, or why the world is ending, it just um, it just is, okay!You have one antagonist, some guy nicknamed "the meat eater", but its unclear if he's even relevant to anything, I met him one time, shot him, and he ran away. Your character sometimes mentions wanting to kill or forgive him, because he killed your parents I guess? But it's not really a big deal to you or anyone.Your objective also seems to be to either destroy or save "the tree of life", which is not explained, and to either stop or allow the "worldeaters" (big monsters) to destroy the tree (spoilers, you have to fight them either way because... idk, the developers were afraid you'd miss out on the epic experience of strafing left and right until you win?).Nothing makes sense, nothing is explained to you, you are treated like a stunted child and dialogue sounds almost AI generated.Gameplay loopYou go from location to location exploring, but all you find at all of these locations is assorted junk items and random clothing and weapons that you use to craft things. The system isn't very deep or complex and feels extremely tacked on and last minute.There is a rarity system, of course, because every game needs loot with different rarity levels in the CURRENT YEAR, but these seem entirely arbitrary. I found a LEGENDARY ugly hat, which has worse stats than a common hat I found a few hours earlier.Wow a LEGENDARY automatic rifle base (which is worse than an uncommon automatic rifle base I bought a long time ago).The real challenge when exploring is not getting bored and also finding gear that actually matches and looks okay.You can find a variety of merchants throughout the game (and by that I mean 3 different merchant types with randomized gear), but they don't specialize, they don't carry anything of particular interest, nothing. They are just merchants that carry random stuff. Going to a merchant in a Jagis outpost doesn't let you buy gear specific to their tribe, the inventory is just as random and boring as that of the Plingplong Wing Wang tribe down the road.A lot of random "sidequests" you get also ask you to find/do X of Y."Pluck 5 guitars (pling-plongers!)", "free 23 captives!", "Touch 9 scrotums-smotums!", "Dingelidang 4 Bibbidybabs!"There is of course a LOT to explore, but its purely quantity without quality, the first 1 hour of the game will be the same as your 20th hour of the game.There is a lot else to touch on, but why bother, plenty of other reviews have touched on the many issues this game has.

_childDocuments_.review: It makes me very sad to have to rate this game negatively. I had high hopes for it for so long, but after completing the game it simply did not live up to the expectations they set forth from the trailers and teasers. I understand this game was made by a small and inexperienced team, however as a full price $60 game it deserves to be judged with the same criticisms I would judge any $60 AAA title with.I'll start by saying that it isn't that I necessarily didn't enjoy playing the game. I did have fun while playing. It is more so that the negatives outweigh the positives. The open world is vast, and it is beautiful. Stylistically the game looks very good. Unfortunately there isn't much to look at once you start to explore and look deeper. With a severely limited number of different types of enemies ( most just being recolored versions of others ) combined with the towns, tribes, bunkers, contamination/cold/hot/etc. zones, and all "areas of interest" having only one layout that is copy + pasted throughout the world you run out of interesting things to see exceptionally quickly. And though the game is stylized very well, nothing in the game is graphically impressive. The combat is severely lacking and the enemies all feel hollow and bland. Your attacks feel weightless and are interrupted by any move the enemies make as well as not changing much from start to finish of the game. As you level you don't feel any stronger or more impressive. The melee component is under-powered compared to the guns and it is noticeable from the very first encounter. Almost every fight in the game ( to include all bosses) can be fought with a gun exclusively and all you have to do in run in circles and shoot while dodging occasionally. The powers you get are underwhelming and once unlocked contain no progression. Powers don't level up, fighting doesn't level up, gun play doesn't level up and it leads to a stale feeling combat experience by the second hour of game play. There are also many bugs in the game. Sound effects don't play sometimes, bio points are incorrectly used while leveling up resistances, enemies glide across the ground to complete attacks that would otherwise miss and too many more to mention. While none of the bugs ruined the game for me they did lead to a much more frustrating and confusing experience. The last thing I feel has to be mentioned is the story and how it is conveyed to the player. About ninety percent of the story in the game is presented to the player at the very beginning. The beginning of the story is genuinely interesting however nothing after that point carries any weight at all. The morality system is a joke where when completing tasks or talking to NPCs they get as close as possible to literally asking you, "Do you want light points or dark points?". That is basically the gist of it. The NPCs all say the exact same voice lines, except the story important ones who have small parts of their dialogue tweaked to fit their part of the world. After defeating every boss (which is a series of fetch quests and then a very basic boss battle) the NPCs all say the same lines and if you don't complete the story in the exact order they expect you to the things they say might not even be true.A personal opinion of mine that might not be popular is that the choice to go with a single narrator who voices everything that happens in the game was a bad idea. After the first hour I was completely sick of him. Narrating me opening new doors, narrating every enemy that crossed my path, narrating which area I was entering. The narrator got so annoying by the end that I turned his volume almost all the way down and set his frequency to as low as it goes. It seems like someone on the dev team played The Stanley Parable too much and didn't really understand the relationship between the world, the player and the narrator very well. A narrator isn't a bad thing but having to sit through uninspired drivel while npcs make gibberish sounds for ten seconds, then the narrator translates with some dad joke tacked on is torture. TL;DRThis game under-delivers in every aspect it offers. A story that feels like it was written by a middle schooler, combat that only functions on the most simple of levels, a world where all the assets are copy pasted around it and it still isn't very densely populated, and an rpg system with uninteresting, bland looking materials and gear that are completely unnecessary and don't progress with you as the game plays out.If you want a gorgeous open world game with amazing combat play Ghost of Tsushima.If you want a fun to play RPG system where leveling up feels important and impactful play Skyrim, or Fallout, or Final Fantasy.If you want a game where you character mutates and grows and changes throughout the story to become stronger/faster/more interesting . . . well me too, but Biomutant did not deliver on that promise. If this game ever drops to $15 i'd say it's worth it to pick it up and give it a playthrough. I don't even think i'd be comfortable recommending it at $30. At $60 for this unfinished, uninspired and uninteresting game I'd say stay away.

_childDocuments_.review: After a rough start that is the tutorial, I found myself sticking around at what is now 24 hours in with only 8% of the game completed. Moreso as you continue to level higher and discover areas that require special equipment to access. Most enemies will have similar, if not the same movesets and most of the world inhabits items that you are rewarded for when exploring. The combat deepens as you progress your character and begin stringing different combos, mutations, and psi powers together. The gun crafting system is wonderful.It is not a revolutionary game changing video game, but it's a solid fun time. If you enjoy games like Outward, you will enjoy this one. _childDocuments_.review: I'm only playing this game as a form of self punishment and because apparently I hate myself. There isn't a single positive thing to say about it as of this moment.COMBAT: It is slugish, your attacks do not connect well with the enemies, there is no impact from the hits, the enemies bug more than half of the time and every fight, be it against a regular mob or a big boss, feels the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ same, they are all boring.STORY AND CHOICES: The story and lore are as shallow as it can get. The game follows a choice system where your choices are supposed to impact the story, and the choices are literally like "That person needs help, do you want to help them or slap their mother in front of them?" or "Those kids are hungry, do you want to share your food or explode their school?". There is no nuance, the choices are stupid and the impact on the world building is minimal because killing a whole tribe weights the same as petting and feeding a bird on the games morality balance.NARRATOR: So, if you don't know, there is no real dialogue in this game in the sense that during the whole game a narrator speaks for the characters, and I swear to god, there is a point (like 30 minutes into the game) where everytime this narrator speaks I feel a primal urge to kill myself and end the pain. It is bad enough that you only hear the same voice over and over through the whole game, but the narrator also tells stupid dad jokes for every single thing you see, keeps the same dead tone for every event and does not shut up for a second. You need to pull a lever to open a door? The game take a minute to pause and make a small cutscene to focus on the lever, then on the door, and during this whole time the narrator is telling you "Go to the lever", "Go to the door" and this goes through the WHOLE game, not only during a tutorial nor anything. Every time I hear a dad joke from the narrator while an enemy bugs mid combat I lose 1 year of my lifespan and pay for a sin commited in my past life.EXPLORATION: The world has nothing interesting to reach for, the items are mostly boring and all the objectives are already marked on your map from the start in the sense that, let's say you trigger a sidequest to find 15 items around the world, when you do this the location of all 15 items will be given to you instantly. There is no real sense of exploration and most of the time you just find yourself running in an empty land from point A to point B,  which is a shame because the world itself is actually beautiful to be honest. And about the mount that you get, if you spend 5 level ups on agility you run faster than your mount, I don't know why it is even in the game.I don't recommend spending any money in this game, I'm only playing it cuz I got it from a bundle and because I want to atone for some of the mistakes I made in life to maybe guarantee a spot for myself in heaven through self punishment. If you also want to get on God's good side by paying for your sins, than I highly recommend this game, but if you have some level of self respect than there are a ton of open world games that are just better in every aspect.
