_childDocuments_.review: Biomutant was an  title that had me excited since it's reveal in 2017. It showed up something for everyone. Fluid combat, comic art style, aura system, custom weapons, etc.Although, this game was made by roughly 14 people, and I'd be a little more leisure about it, if it was priced at a AAA release. So just as everyone, I'll be reviewing Biomutant as a AAA experience. Biomutant has a great open world, visually at least. It's got story all over and pretty much anything is lootable (as long as it's in an area designed to be looted). The story is linear and bland with nothing more than fetch quests for the entire experience. Meet new character, get quests, pick up object for boss, fight boss. Nothing changes, and the side quests suffer the same way.The map is barren, enemies are few and far between and there is never really any danger at any time. There's always something to look at but also nothing at the same time. Thankfully you're given mounts to travel around and speed up the movement a little bit. Enemies are interesting and I mean that lightly, there are 3 various of enemies. Beast, humanoid, and giant, which all have the same 3 attack patterns. You will either be shot at, swung at, or stomped on. Which would be fine if the various enemies were actually eye catching except for the names being funny sometimes. The NPCs are voiced in gibberish, with the narrator speaking and translating for them. A very unique thing we haven't seen often. Except for when you catch on that the NPCs say the say gibberish voiceline over and over and over and over and over and over and over again. It never changes, they will say the same line, while the narrator changes what they say slightly each time. Which also isn't very different. It's always something about either being a good boy, and that my mooma would be proud or that I'm evil and need to find a spark of light. Nothing changes and I ended up skipping the dialog most of the times from that point. The narrator is charming when you're just walking around, but if you have a setting to make him shut up, then you know it's annoying and not very good. The AI is kinda bad too, they get stuck in idle animations or in mid swings. All I can say about this fights is that the enemies do make combat fun when it works. Guns, swords and spells, oh my! That's the weapons you get, those are yours arms in the world. Weapons can be crafted from dismantled weapons you find or dismantle yourself, axe blade with katana hilt? You can make it. The only that ruins the combat is there's no impact, two handed swords have no thud to them. It's like a two handed noodle. The guns felt like you're spitting on them, even upgraded they just feel like stronger spit. Enemies don't stagger often enough and just power through your hits and keep moving, skills don't affect the damage either since weapons are how your damage is modified. The spells pretty much don't do anything either except mucus bubble which is the only power worth the grind. Also, PARRY DOESNT F**KING WORK. THE AMOUNT OF TIMES I PARRY A HIT IS SO LOW BECAUSE THE GAME DOESNT REGISTER THE PARRY UNLESS YOU SPAM THE BUTTON.  Sorry. But if you have a PARRY you need it to be the most responsive action in the game. Clunky, and wacky. The amount of time my character just freaks out because he doesn't know what animation to show and then it decided to dump the first one it can. Other than that you don't really notice much of the problems, unless the game freaks out and doesn't work. Biomutant is a masterpiece as an indie game, and would've been higher on my ratings and likes if it was for the fact the game isn't just an indie game. It's an experimental game, made by first time developers, sold as a AAA game. That's why I'm giving it a negative rating, it's not worth 60$ and is very unfinished, and unpolished. At best its worth maybe 30$, just due to the time it was given. Although it's not worth a AAA price point when what's given isn't a AAA experience. , just wait until it's dropped or if they update it and add more or fix the content they have now.

_childDocuments_.review: Gorgeous. This game is absolutely gorgeous. All of the scenery in all of the biomes never feels lacking for the amount of detail and effort that must have gone in to making it feel more real and organic. The world does kinda suck you in. Then it all gets ruined when.....yep you already know what's coming.....the narrator opens his mouth, and any degree of immersion you had is utterly destroyed. More on that later.I mostly came into this game blind. I remember watching the cinematic trailer back during one of the E3 events many years back and I kinda forgot about it till recently. I have heard many times from various other reviews though that the combat feels clunky and awkward. Honestly, my only complaint about the combat is the combos are the same no matter what weapon type you have. I feel this could have been expanded on to have different combos for different weapon types. It certainly does make the combat feel a bit samey. I went for the Psy-Freak class first though, and it added a much needed depth to combat, allowing me to do melee, ranged and 'magic' combat all at once.As mentioned before, the world is gorgeous and one of the best things I enjoyed doing in the game was just running around and exploring, doing tasks as I came across them rather than trying to complete one quest at a time. I think I would have very quickly felt overwhelmed at the sheer amount of things to do if I focused on finishing things. The main story is not terribly long, so don't feel any need to rush it.The crafting system was pretty fun, allowing you to create some silly looking weapons that somehow manage to kick ass and look good doing it. Especially nice is the ability to constantly switch out parts of your weapons as and when you find stronger parts, so you're always able to grow stronger if you find a favourite weapon type.Criticisms are few with this. I'll start with an easy one. There is a parry system in the game, and when an enemy gets a special mark above their head, you can hit the parry button to throw them off balance, allowing for a counter. This is nice when fighting regular enemies. This is not nice when fighting very large enemies, as their head is often off-screen so you never see the prompt to parry and so you spend a lot of time being paste under their feet.The story itself is short.....extremely short and lacking any real depth at all. You are constantly assaulted throughout with a pressing sense of morality. Good v Evil. Over....and over.....and over. It gets tedious to listen to very quickly and it often resulted for me in particular to just skip dialogue the moment an NPC would start reminding me 'my choices have consequences'. Yes. I get it. Put the point across at the start of the game as a forewarning for the end of the game, but don't do it with every....single....NPC.Finally the biggest issue. The narrator, and by association, the childish language he uses from start to finish. The mannerisms in his speech along with the baffling childish names for...well....anything, sounds like he's treating you like a 4yo pre-schooler and it gets super annoying very quickly. Yes you can turn him off, but you shouldn't have to. The NPCs speak in gibberish, so fine yes have him translate what they're saying, but just be normal about it. That wonderful world you're immersing yourself in? The enjoyment you're getting from exploring weird locations or kicking ass in a fight? The narrator will chip in anytime he likes with more child-speech to shatter any illusion of immersion you have. It's like listening to an episode of 'In The Night Garden' (It's a British TV show for little kids).All in all I will still recommend this game to anyone who is interested, but I would probably say wait for a sale before you buy it. And if you do buy it, for goodness sake, disable the narrator. You can thank me later.

_childDocuments_.review: More detailed review to follow after more hours in game but I can say for certain right now that anyone with less that 1.5 hours of playtime hasn't even finished the tutorial yet. That can either be a pro or con, depending on what you want out of early game, but if you haven't even gotten to the open world part of an open world game...well...your opinion requires a giant grain of salt to go with it. At 2.2 hours in (with a 10-20 minute break to let the dogs out) I just now learned how to craft. There are a LOT of people buying this game just to give up on it before it even opens up, be warned. Actual review based on playtime thus far: Biomutant's vibe HEAVILY reminds me of the early 00s era, back when publishers were willing to take risks on unproven game formulas, which is something I've really missed. It pulls a lot of ideas from its peers and (at least in early game) they all seem pretty fleshed out and cohesive. Performance can be...weird. One of the first big boss fights dropped below 50fps while the rest of the game runs at 80+ on my rig. Not ideal, but can be ironed out by the devs over time and the rest of the game has been smooth as butter thus far. Transitioning between melee and ranged combat is effortless and there are a ton of unlockable combos for both if that's your thing. The crafting system is surprisingly deep for both weapons and armor. The setup is a more narrative heavy BoTW affair (four big baddies with one gatekeeper for each with side missions, puzzles, and traversal filling the time between) with a heavy dash of martial arts cinema influence mixed in. Think Jade Empire vibes but simultaneously cuter and more bleak. There's also a dark/light morality system which is influenced by your narrative choices and effects which abilities you can use and how some characters interact with you.I'm interested to see how the experience is shaped along the way but the bones of the game are far better than most of the reviews let on. The culture of "buy game, play for 30 minutes, refund and then leave a negative review" is getting ridiculous on Steam, ESPECIALLY in open world/narrative based games that take time to build. Typically, I wouldn't post a sub-2 hour review at all unless the game was borked and Biomutant is definitely not, it's just being reviewed unfairly imo. Is it worth the $60 price tag? I couldn't say yet. For a lot of people, probably not. However, I can confidently say that most if not all of us gamers have spent $60 on worse (and infinitely less unique) titles. I commend Experiment 101 for their creativity and THQ Nordic for having the guts to take a risk on such a weird game idea. I genuinely wish more devs and publishers would follow suit instead of pouring millions into forgettable cookie cutter game ideas.

_childDocuments_.review: Biomutant is a decent game, but not without its flaws.The good:The world of Biomutant is really nice. The landscape is breathtaking, the wind ruffles the fur of your little creature and the customization allows you to create the furry you always dreamt of. The combat, even though the move set is very limited, is actually quite fun if you get into it and overall the visuals are very nice. The story is nothing special, but it's not bad.The bad:The game has no voice acting in the classic sense except for some weird noises the creatures make, instead the whole game, dialogue and actions (even during combat) are commented on by a narrator, who WILL ABSOLUTELY get on your nerves, no matter how patient you are.The customization and class selection have minimal impact on the gameplay. Every character can learn the same moves and perks except for about 5-6 perks that are class specific, but not enough to make the classes feel unique.Biomutant features a classic morality system, which means you are either a saint or a ♥♥♥♥. There is no point in balancing it out, since the game doesn't have neutral options most of the time and you need to have a certain amount of dark or light aura to learn most of the Psi abilities. The conclusion:Biomutant is not for everyone. It is a charming game with an interesting and breathtaking world, but it falls short in a number of ways. The main problem is the price tag. It is a nice game, but it can't keep up with other open world titles in the $60 price category. If you can get it on sale for like $40 at some point however, I would absolutely recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: SPOILER WARNING.I got this game for $20 on sale and played it entirely on Steam Deck. I played it on Low at 800p with dynamic resolution and a 40fps target. For the most part it felt smooth and responsive. You can definitely hurt the frame rate running around the world on a mount tho.I'm giving this game a thumbs up, but only just barely. I was hype about this game before it came out, but I have a habit of never buying games for $60 so I waited. I finally bit at a sale recently and purchased it because I thought it would be a great game for my new Deck.I'd be very upset if I paid $60 for Biomutant. The combat is okay, I don't care about deep complicated combat. I'm not a combo juggler. The shooting... is. The world itself is pretty interesting but if you look too hard some of the stuff is repeated like random structures. And some of the dungeons you come across are pretty neat.My biggest gripe is that the narrative sucks. Every time you talk to someone, it's not the person talking. It's a narrator. And not a good narrator, an often vague narrator. It removes any sense that you're getting to know characters. It makes it very hard to feel who you are talking to, when instead of quirks to their personality, you're getting "Seems like they might possibly want that" from the narration.And on top of that, dialogue between characters can often feel incredibly random. 8/10 times I get an option to input my character's thoughts on the subject, at least one of the options is a mystery to me because I didn't feel like we were talking about that. And the ending is just dumb. Like, I've busted my ass to save the world and then that happens? Why? Didn't I save it? Why can't i choose to stay? Where the ♥♥♥♥ are we going?And as a side note, probably play on Hard if you want any semblance of a challenge. I played on Medium because I don't really like punishing games, but if you craft yourself a decent machine gun, you can strafe murder the entire game. Doesn't matter what you're fighting.

_childDocuments_.review: Your mileage may vary -- people seem to be generally warm towards the game (outside of reviewers who are generally either "it's okay" or "it's complete ♥♥♥♥) so watch a good mix of bigger and smaller channels -- those like Cr1tikal miss the mark entirely in my opinion (way overly negative, gave it a lower score than CP2077) where gameranx and fextralife are much more measured in their response (if slightly negative), while TagbackTV and Khrazegaming both seem super pro-Biomutant.But as of this review it's at 68% positive, which should tell you that gamers are generally at least slightly warm, if divided, on it.What this means is, approach with caution but curiosity -- if you have the money and time to sink in, go for it. Otherwise, it may be worth waiting for a sale. Now, into personal opinion.-> For me it scratches the same itch of games like Genshin Impact and Breath of the Wild -- while the story in Biomutant is fairly bare-bones and "gets the job done" it's still decent enough to keep me wanting to help the characters involved usually. The main draw here is the exploration, side quests, looting, crafting, and general completion of the map.-> You can consider this like a large scale open world collect-a-thon where there's a ton of things to interact with and the game doesn't take itself too seriously, but some of the quirks (like unconventional naming -- fry-sparkers are microwaves, twing-twangs are guitars and up-and-downs are elevators) may grate on you. Personally I think it adds to the idea that *these are animals in a human-made apocalypse, they did the best they could naming things they don't entirely understand*-> There's a fair amount of variation in locations, with irradiated, dead, nuclear-waste-contaminated, on-fire, desert and water areas at various locations with larger sections of them in the corners of the map. You get a special mount for the dead / without oxygen larger area and for the water area. There's also a blimp later for the larger hot area. A lot of smaller / unimportant / not-lootable buildings are cut and paste, but there's enough variation in the ones you can actually enter than outside of a few, most locations at least *feel* unique.-> There's a nice cast of side characters in the side quests with all different personalities and things they're good at and different views on the world -- some like Jumble and Boom are enjoyable, while others feel samey outside their particular flavor-of-the-week views on the world (screw the world / glad you're saving it). Still, the differences are enough to carry their quests well enough at least.-> While at its' core crafting is just "attach the part with the bigger numbers that makes the bar more green" there's also unique effects some base weapon parts add that can change the way the guns work in pretty interesting ways, and can add big buffs to melee like "heal for double the damage you deal with this weapon" so there's a neverending quest for the best parts, there's always *something* better you can get, at least until endgame (level 30+). The armor add-ons really add to the whole "animals in the apocalypse" thing, like just putting screws on your armor and stuff, just random scavenged junk.-> Looting is as passable as can be expected, but it's definitely weaker sometimes with how meaningless the loot can feel especially at lower levels and before you get into upgrading the rarity of your weapons and armor and need to dismantle your spare parts. Even then, it's by far the most tedious part of the game so it can just feel like a grind -- fine if you want to shut off your brain and just go go go.The biggest con is combat - without some form of haptic feedback (woojer vest, haptic bass on headphones (or just really good bass), the rumble on a controller) it can feel like you're kind of just punching or shooting at air, and it's incredibly underwhelming. Combat with a keeb+mouse has no punch to it and is incredibly boring, but with an xbox one controller and the rumble even the general tedium of combat at least feels interesting enough that it doesn't bore me that much.Also, given that one of the most touted aspects was "wung fu" you'd think there'd be more unarmed attack animations, but there's really not and you can tell after a while. Also, the combat is really easy unless you're playing pure melee, and only gets easier as you level up and get better gear. The recently added "Extreme" difficulty helps that a bit, but it's still pretty easy.Basically, go in taking every bit of review with a pinch of salt, and if you're on the fence then buy when it goes on sale because it may just scratch that itch for you like it did for me.

_childDocuments_.review: NOTE: There was a major update that should have addressed some of my grievances below. This review predates that update. I am giving it another go and will update accordingly.It's clear that Experiment 101 want this game to be well received. The first post-release patch did improve things a noticeable amount. I haven't created a new character, so I didn't experience the improved pacing of the tutorial, but it was pretty agonizing before the patch, so I won't be commenting on that. One thing I want to add that was missing from my original review is a list of things that are good or great about the game:* The crafting system is pretty awesome. The user interface could use some tuning to make it a bit easier to navigate, and it would be good if it had a better display of what the different parts were doing, but the mechanics are solid. I would consider this the most complete feature in the game.* There is an inordinate amount of content that is not part of the main story. I completed the game in 14 hours, which included a little bit of side content. When going into New Game+, I just followed the side quests, and that's been another 7 hours and I'm only scratching the surface. I would estimate you could put in 100-300 hours depending on your own pacing if you were trying to 100% the game.Now for some more detailed critiques:* Dialogue: The new patch has added options to improve the dialogue so that you aren't clicking through two phases to advance. Unfortunately, there's still too much of it. It feels like there is a checklist of traits your character has (based on creation and your gameplay choices), and every NPC you meet has to make a statement about each item on that list. I don't need every character I come across to tell me that they don't like the tribe I allied with. Post-patch, dialogue still slows down the pace of the game. I don't see them being able to significantly address this, but I would be open to evaluating further improvements here.* Combat: The combat still seems to be a bit feast or famine if you are in close combat. Parrying can be very effective, but multiple enemies make melee combat exponentially more frustrating. Even with the damage rebalance, guns, and in particular automatic rifles (with Perfect Reload perk) are much less of a hassle. When using melee, every fight with a few enemies seems to either be me swinging and just dominating the encounter, or me trying to do just that but being hit by a constant stream of knockdowns. The balance is still off here, but this can be fixed.* Cutscenes: AAAAAAAAAA. These are still just the worst. They happen for all sorts of things. Some are skippable, some aren't. There are better ways to handle most of the cases where there are short cutscenes that don't interrupt the flow of the game. When raiding an outpost, you don't need a cutscene for every phase to tell you about the next line of defense. You can just spawn in the enemies with an animation, and still run the narrator's line, and it doesn't interrupt the flow of gameplay. There should never be an unskippable cutscene for something that isn't a major plot point (and even then, those shouldn't be unskippable), and you should be able to skip a cutscene as soon as it starts and not have to sit through an animation fading into the cutscene before the skip is active. I do not think this can be resolved without major changes to the game.Overall, while the patch has improved the playability somewhat, I still do not recommend the game at this time. As I said before, it looks like Experiment 101 is serious about improving the game, so I'm hopeful that I will someday revisit the game and change this review again, but I am doubtful that they can resolve some of the major flaws. There were decisions made about the design of this game that I don't think can be fixed.Original Review:This is a game that can't get out of it's own way.* Everything has a cut scene. Literally everything. Encountering five enemies? Better show a cut scene of the five enemies! Pick up an animal and pet it? Cut scene. Kill an animal? Cut scene. Looting a container? You guessed it! Cut scene.* Every bit of dialogue is twice as long as it needs to be. First, the character speaks gibberish, then the narrator translates it. Fortunately, you're given the ability to skip through, but don't mess up the timing, or you'll skip the translation instead of the gibberish! No way to go back and see what you missed.* Every enemy has interrupts and knock-downs. You can parry them, but not if you're actually trying to fight. If you encounter a group of enemies, it's just so annoying to fight close combat and it is slowed down so much. Not difficult, mind you. The combat is fairly easy, just a slog.The game also lacks depth in most areas.* All the bosses follow the same structure. Meet someone, do some quest to get a vehicle of some sort, then do another quest to get some super special ammo, then go fight the boss and use that special ammo to make them so you can do damage with normal ammo.* Character creation sure has a lot of options, but doesn't seem to have any major impact on game play. It seems to just seed your starting stats, and gives you an exclusive set of perks that you can unlock, though they didn't seem to have any major impact on the in-game systems. Within a few levels, any bonus from your starting stats is overwhelmed by what you've unlocked from leveling.* Money seems to be pretty worthless? You don't seem to get a lot of it, but that's fine, because you just spend it to buy items from vendors that aren't as good as what you can make.* Combat is very simplistic. You have one melee attack. You can't control what sort of attack it is, it's just sequential. You can perform combos, but good luck trying to pull some of them off in a crowd (see above about interrupts and knock downs).* The ending of the game is influenced by light and dark aura points. These are earned by doing good things or doing bad things, like punching someone randomly. You have few big decisions to make that influence this, and lots of decisions that really have no impact on the world. Most of your light and dark points will come from picking up critters and either killing them or petting them (both of which will present you with a cut scene of the top of your head!)After defeating the third boss, everything became a total slogfest. At that point, I needed to complete a different main story mission, which wasn't particularly interesting, and involved lots of running around. After finishing that, I go to do the same set of quests as every other boss to gain access to the last boss, but this one... this one is different. This one has extra quests, all of which are about 1km away (hope you unlocked some fast travel locations nearby!)Despite all of that, I did actually play to the end and was invited to play it again, to which I will decline. This game isn't awful, and I'm sure there are people out there for which it is excellent, but for me, and I would imagine most prospective players, the annoyances add up into an experience that on the whole felt like it was something that happened to me, and not something I participated in. Were the game not $60, I would probably be a bit more positive.

_childDocuments_.review: Holy crap, where to even start with this steaming heap. The tutorial (if you can even call it that) is WAY too long for what it's supposed to teach you, and frankly, unless you're 4 and this is the first game you've ever played, you aren't going to learn anything.The 'quests' are unintuitive, repetitive, and unrewarding. _childDocuments_.review: This game has many things going for it. The combat is fun enough, with a wide variety of weapon types to keep it intersting. I tried out a numerous amount of builds before finally settling on dual-wielding swords. It's fairly simple, but still satisfying. It can use a little work to smooth it out a little bit, but it's by no means broken. The world exploration is also really fun. The scenery in this game is great. I spent a decent amount of time in the game searching for some cool vistas to set up some screenshots. This is probably one of my favorite things to do in this game (but the photo mode could use a few more features for posing and facial expressions to make it more complete).Where the game falls apart for me is the interactoion with other characters (or more specifically the lack thereof). For some bizarre reason, the writers of this game decided to do away with regular dialogue in favore of a narrator that explains everything to you as if acting as a translator. This makes interacting with anyone seem so impersonal and lifeless. It didn't seem like much of a problem at first, but after the excitement of a playing a new game wore off, I realized that everything started to feel a little dull and it is 100% to blame on the narrated interactions.Every character is a boring blank block of wood that expresses zero emotion. Reliant only on the narrator to tell you if he is angry, sad, glad, etc. Nobody has any personality because they all have the same personality as the narrator. This begins to create a pervasive feeling of lonely meaninglessness to everything you do. Once you finish a quest, there is nobody there to thank you or react to what you did besides a generic voice saying "He thanks you for your assistance" or something along those lines. Every character is some kind of animal! This should be the perfect opportunity to have a bunch of fun and wild personalities. In the end, it starts to feel as if you are the only living person in a beautiful world. After a while, the beauty falls apart when you realize there’s no one else and everything you do is meaningless.

_childDocuments_.review: I believe that the developers worked really hard to make a game like this. And I commend them for that and for making this. Game developers work on tight schedules and sometimes to the bone. That being said, my experience with Biomutant has been strained. I want to like this game, I really do; but I feel as though I'm getting chicken wings with all the good, meaty bits already eaten.The combat in this system has the potential to be very, very fluid, but just does not have that "oomph" factor that makes it feel like I'm doing something impactful. The melee attacks are great and well choreographed on their own but connecting them just looks and feels weird. I have yet to see a random t-pose, but the fluidity between moves is erratic. The slow-motion elements are in all the right places, but where's the kick that makes it feel like countering attacks matter? I've been able to just run-and-gun and complete fights without ever having to worry about using melee, unless the enemy has a shield. Once I destroy that shield? Back to dodging and gunning.The game is actually gorgeous. Really, really stunning visuals. From the foliage the the way the lights hit, it's really good. I do get the occasional screen tear and hiccup in visuals but I suspect that's my own hardware not meeting standards all the way. Even dialing the graphics down to their minimums makes the game look a little above good, personally.The dialogue in this game and linearity of the story gives the illusion of choice. I thought I'd be able to have my own blended story that aligns with my own personal values (after all, it is a single player game), but I was left stuck between two choices and having to commit to the series of choices that follow. It's like choosing between water or soda. If you pick water, sure, you can add flavors, but in the end its just flavored water. Choosing soda means every choice later is some variation of a high-sugar drink. There's no back-and-forth here, really--at least not in the grand scheme of the plot.The UI is, dare I say, Fortnite-esque. Bright blue with comical impact-style font and bold shadows. Being guided through the UI for leveling up, the map, gear, and crafting is super clunky and does not feel at all intuitive. Visual customization is definitely top tier (imagine having a banana has a hilt with an electric blade), and I loved that. But the stats for any of these items (especially in crafting) just don't pan out so seamlessly. I can barely compare items without having to put an item on and then take it off. And mousing over them DOES show the change in stats, but sometimes it doesn't. Imagine if your current stats are X. If you mouse over item Y, it will show you what X would look like + Y. But then if you mouse over Z, it will show your stats as Y + Z. Why? If I stop mousing over Y, show me X, then when I mouse over Z, show me X + Z. I also barely know the emphasis of the different item types or rarities--I was encountering things like "Rare," "Legendary," "Abnormal," so early in the game it would confuse me. Why am I encountering high item rarities so early in the game?The dialogue in the game is a miss. Some of the dialogue choices I make don't get responded to accurately. It's like telling an NPC you're hungry, and they respond with "yes," rather than "what would you like?" Or if an NPC asks if you're hungry, and you say "no," they'll ask "okay, how many [food] do you want?" Also, the translator should just speak the entire way through what an NPC is saying rather than having to wait for the NPC to speak their gibberish.Guys, I really want to like this game, but it kills me to play it. It's a 5/10 for me. I'll edit this review when I finish the game--if I can. And I hope I can, because I want to.

_childDocuments_.review: A great game with a nice sense of humor, exploration on par with games like skyrim and fallout 3/4, i enjoy the weapon customization system, especially for ranged weapons. _childDocuments_.review: Honestly at $60 there's no way I could possibly recommend this game.Lets talk about the good first. 1: I love the setting, there's a lot of color, I think game developers are realizing that gamers are fatigued on games that offer nothing but  browns and greys.2:The game is very adorable and filled with cute fuzzy friends     Thats about it for me unfortunatelyNext well talk about what's just ok.Combat: While it's serviceable, it's not particularly satisfying. Enemies size and level's do not really seem to correlate to their combat ability, and neither does yours for that matter, I fought enemies who smaller than me and were 4-5 level below me that were absolute tanks and I've fought giant enemies that we're 6 levels higher than me that died in a few seconds, there really doesn't seem to be any real rhyme or reason, it mainly just seems like the level system is in place because that's how most open world games are. Also there's none of those satisfying moment's that make you feel like a total chad, you're not going to pull off an epic finisher and obliterate  anything, they'll all kind just fall down and that's the end of it, it's all very MEH. Gun play is also pretty lame, it works, but it's really just there to make ranged attacks so you don't have to risk taking damage, there's no real aiming or skill involved, just click the mouse in the general direction while the game decides if the bullet hits or not.Crafting: Poorly explained, extremely basic, and probably mostly unnecessary. I found this (Similar to what I said about enemy levels) to seem arbitrary. I would craft a new gun that was statistically way better than what I had been using and it seemed to make very little difference at all. Honestly it seems that the game scales so well thaat pretty much nothing seems to actually make a difference game play wise, just mentally which seems to be a problem with scaling in general, let gamers fail by trying to take on an encounter that they obviously aren't prepared for, just like letting gamers absolutely destroy that weak ass enemy who should have minded their own business, we want to overcome adversity, but also feel like a total Chad at the same time, do developers not know how boring scaling can be?Preaching: Yes climate change and pollution. We get it, and you're probably not going to change the minds of people who don't agree by smearing it in your game 50 times.Good vs Evil: Too in your face, you have a literal angel and devil that tell you if you're decision was good or bad, which is so painfully obvious that even a rat could have made the choices for me and I don't even thing it really matters so long as you unite the tribes and spare your childhood bully, Just seems like it was in there to make the game seem more dynamic than it really is.Let's talk about the bad.1: The missions are extremely repetitive, especially the main "world eater" missions which consist of; you need to use this vehicle, but it's missing parts! Spend the next 30-60 minutes gathering them and then fight an oversized monster that isn't much more difficult than anything else you've already been fighting. It's boring and disappointing, I didn't really find any mission in this game that felt genuine or original in any way.2: The dialog is so damn repetitive you will start hearing the narrator repeat the same lines in the first 1-2 hours and with every character you talk to. While I am sure they saved a ton of money by not having to hire 50 voice actors, and by having so few overall lines, it gets extremely boring and annoying quickly, characters in this game have precious few things to say, so it's sad that most of it is reused content. I honestly would have rather it had been Nintendo style where it's obviously gibberish and I just read subtitles, not that I want all of the narration removed, the narrator delivers his lines well, especially during cut scenes, but it's just rather obnoxious overall.Overall, this is probably a below average game for me. The extreme lack of variety, the unsatisfying gameplay, the unsatisfying crafting system, the boring level scaling, the repetitive boss sequences, the constant repetitive narrating, the preachyness, the lack of an actual feeling of urgency or importance. It's just not really that fun.Don't spend $60 on this please because honestly if this was like a $15-20 game, my opinion would be much higher and I'd tell you to buy it now, but it honestly lacks the care, attention and polish that is expected when you are paying $60 for a game .*I'll update my review when it's not 4am and I can check it for errors.* Hope this helps you,

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty much the only thing I like is the music. The combat feels awful, and the narration is really grating. I thought it would be more LittleBigPlanet style, but it's much more like someone actually reading a child a bed time story which, while I think that's what they were going for, feels weird. The story also feels like an advertisement for the environment, costantly reminding us it's our duty to clean and recycle. The message is fine, but again, it feels like they're talking to a child and it's grating. Parrying is probably the least satisfying thing I've ever seen, half the time I didn't even realize I actually parried something. The graphics sometimes look amazing but other times look really bad, which I don't mind, but you might. All this said, I don't think this game is a lost cause. If they can somehow make the combat not feel like two clouds trying to have a pillow fight, it would be worth probably at least $30. In its current state, I'd say it's worth about $10. They can't really do much about the story at this point, but with better combat you could at least skip cutscenes and enjoy the martial arts.Update: So this was written with the modern gaming mindset of "the devs won't care, it'll stay broken until they can sell a GOTY version or something, then maybe it'll be worth it for $20 on a Steam sale" but they seem to actually be listening and working quickly to try and fix what people are complaining about. This by itself makes me recommend the game, but only if you're either very forgiving, or wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of the 'puzzles' are overly simplistic and the morality system is overall not very impactful... But overall, I really like it. The core gameplay loop is fun, with deeper combat than a lot of people realize and an amazing crafting system. The environments are beautiful and mostly worth exploring, hiding plenty of high-value loot away from the beaten paths. The world and characters are full of quirky humor, but also a surprising array of philosophical profundity. Every boss fight and the prep time leading up to them offers a satisfying mechanical distraction (without spoiling too much: vehicles!).Bottom line -- if you like open-world ARPGs and don't mind a little jank, you will enjoy BIOMUTANT.Edit: An update on June 1st addressed one of my main complaints in regard to game dialogue, by allowing you to disable the NPC gibberish, narrator's voice-over, or both. Doing any of those will make conversations much faster to get through because the text appears instantly, rather than after a delay you previously had to press a button to skip. Same patch also appears to improve the somewhat lengthy tutorial section's pacing, which is something I also felt needed work but failed to mention in this review. So... Good job, devs, keep it up.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros- Visually interesting- Walking around and exploring feels very interesting and rewarding for the first 2-3 hours- Modular weapons with replaceable parts is coolCon's- Lot of copy and paste environments, mostly when it comes to indoor and underground areas especially- There is a severe lack of interesting abilities that are good, and especially a lack of abilities in general, I thought the mucus bubble would be cool but all it does is stick enemies to you and you pop it to make em go flying, doesnt do any damage or anything, lame.- There is a morality system but its extremely binary and all it amounts to is you gaining good or bad points so you can have enough to get the psi-power you want, spoiler, theyre all lame and not worth anyway.- Guns are overpowered and trivialize all encounters, so long as you keep upgrading the thing, or stumble upon the best one in the game, you can beat any enemy in the game with no issue at all.- Combat is just too easy in general, only thing that can kill ya are instakills- Game takes itself too seriously, but also is too goofy to the point its annoying, they come up with goofy made up names for stuff instead of just saying what it is. And theres also some story related to you about revenge and a cycle of hatred.......like a main enemy is called porky puff...cmon. - Narrator gets annoying since hes the only voice you actually hear besides the npc gibberish, and he comments on everything.- Looting actually becomes annoying after you get a good loadout since you need to watch an animation every time unless you spam the pickup all button, but it still takes up time when theres just so much to loot.- Not enough interesting enemy variety, theres small guys, big guys, and the handful of creatures that all kinda do the same thing pretty much.- All the boss fights suck, theyre janky, and are piss easy.- Charisma is completely useless, had base charisma and passed every persuasion check in the game, lets you skip fights ez pz.This game is charming in many ways, but janky, dumb, and obviously overscoped in so many others. Get it for like 10-15$ if you REALLY need something to play cause otherwise just go play a farcry game or assasins creed or something.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't trust the bad reviews. If those kids had reviewed Breath of the Wild, they would have given it a bad review because "Link is mute and it is annoying".Yes, the narrator gets old eventually. But that alone should not make or brake a game for anyone.I have over 100 hours on the game, not finished yet, just because there is so much to do and to see. Just when you think you did pretty much anything, you discover another XXXX that freaking XXX!. (no spoilers.You can see how much love was put into this game. The attention to detail  is impressive. The variety of mounts, the customization of EVERYTHING (gear, weapons, mutations, your automaton, even your body shape). I want to specially highlight the crafting system. It is awesome. Every weapon or armor is made of parts. So even if a new gun is not necessarily better than yours, you can probably use its scope/grip/handle/magazine/addon/etc to improve it. Also, at some point in the game I was able to add 2 rotating saws to a single one handed melee weapon. How cool is that?The game world is HUGE, so much that I could've finished the game without even visiting the entire northeastern quarter of it.The quest system is awesome, as the game does a GREAT job of showing you where you need to go, and also showing all quests that can be completed nearby on the map. Also, there is a list of any points of interest to all small areas of the world, so that you don;t miss anything, or don;t waste time searching for something that is not there.I played it on hard, and I loved the challenge. Eventually, I explored so much that my gear became godly and now the game is easy even on hard.My game never crashed, I never found a bug or got stuck anywhere. Only feedback I woul;d give the devs: Melee is VERY underwhelming when compared to ranged. I deal 2x as much ranged damage, and also melee puts you on harms way too much, and you get staggered too much, so your melee DPS falls even more. Ranged is too safe.Anyways, I love this game. If I have to chose the best game I played in 2021, for sure it would be Biomutant. So much that I am aiming for full completion. Let's see if I can do it.Anyone looking for a huge, beautiful world to explore, a great story and a lot of fun: This game will not let you down.

_childDocuments_.review: Reading other reviews I came in with low expectations for this game, but I have to say I was very positively surprised! I personally think it's fantasticThe game world looks absolutely gorgeous, that and the crafting system and combat variety are definitely what keeps it going for me. Exploring feels rewarding and whimsicalThe combat is a bit of a footgun in that you *can* make it very boring for yourself if you stick to just one playstyle - I recommend switching things up often and experimenting with new weapons and different combinations between gun/melee. That keeps things engaging and I feel that's how it was intended to be playedThe story is     what it is, I don't really care much for it, and I don't mind. I wish you could skip dialogue faster. The worldbuilding is definitely where the game's writing and design shines. The main quest is a bit meh, but gives you a good reason to Do ThingsThe general vibe really reminds me of games like Ratchet and Clank, both in gameplay and to some extent visuals. It's a great nostalgia trip if you played those as a kidOverall I think this is a fantastic title, especially for a small studio. From what I've seen the main gripes others have are mostly with the story and endgame, which I personally don't care much about in games anyway. Definitely worth grabbing on sale if you ask me

The graphics are nice, and the world building is really fun.The choice of narrating everything in third-person is an interesting choice, and to be honest does make the story and characters feel a bit distant, but honestly I don't care much for story in videogames much anyways.Overall, the game certainly isn't a masterpiece, game of the year quality sort of game, but it's fun, and if you want something to mess around with, I'd recommend it. If you want intense gameplay or super indepth story, this might not be what you're looking for.

_childDocuments_.review: Was looking forward to a single player rpg game. Don't even know what I expected but this is far from it.The combat feels awful and I found myself just making a fast firing high damage pistol so I could kill anything in max 10 seconds so I could get on with the game(other than armoured enemies whom I sadly couldn't take out with guns).The narrator... It really ruins the game when npc's speak gibberish and so the narrator has to translate it all to you for you to understand what's happening. Am I supposed to feel bad for this guy whose village was burnt down when he goes "tstthst toot spoot houngengya meow bark" which roughly translates to "oh no, everyone I cared for is dead and my legs are broken" but it's being told by someone who didn't experience any of that and certainly don't re-tell it with the emotions someone that's experienced it would have? _childDocuments_.review: I'm gonna throw my hat in the ring since I'm more than 0.5 hours into the game unlike the negative reviews. So what's good about the game?Graphics - Graphics are gorgeous, there are things here and there missing like when you swim the water doesn't flow. The grass doesn't perfectly rustle. But that's all a nitpick. I would very much put the graphics of this game close to Nier, but ascended a bit. There were at times that I wanted to keep moving my camera around just to get the view of the world. I see people complaining about the 'cartoon' aesthetic. I don't understand how they can, unless they bought the game without looking at literally anything. The game looks as it's advertised.Character Customization - This'll be debated but I like the concept. The game is very centered on the idea of mutation ( hence the name ) and evolution. First you pick your race or "breeds" which will grant you basic stats and act sort of as a second class of sorts. Some breeds are better at PSI others at tanking. It also alters your head from cat like to rat like.Next is more character design. Customization is basic, using a radar chart for most things including the pattern of your fur. Which I will admit is pretty stupid. However, what I really liked was your stats. If you wanted your character to be focused on strength the game will make them stout. Focus on agility? Lengthy and skinny. Intellect? Big brain. Much like you'd expect from basic evolution.Finally is the classes. It's a pretty basic spectrum like you'd find in MMOs, same with the races. Ya got your classes focused on melee, others in magic and some that are in-between.Story - I'll have to come back to this, but the story does have me intrigued. The game centers around you and your past with the overarching story about the Tree of Life and whether or not the world will survive based on its survival. The former had me interested because Gear Customization - I just reached this part of the tutorial. ( Yes, 2 hours in, and I'm still in the tutorial. I'll address this later. ) I can already see it's very in-depth like you'd see in the videos. The best way I can easily describe it is if you took the now retired game LoadOut and amplified it by 10. Rather than becoming a God by leveling up. The game presents itself that you need to become a God by crafting a God-Like weapon. Adding attachments, crafting, ect, so on. I'm excited to start going really deep in this part of the game.What's Okay?Combat - Another that will be debated, but hear me out. I see in the reviews, that no one likes it because there's no lock-on. I think lock-ons are a very outdated aspect of gaming. In the era of dynamic audio and ability to adjust your FOV. I don't have problems focusing on a single target and staying on them. It also adds a more real feel to the combat. Now, I picked DeadEye as my class. Because if it wasn't clear from my avatar. I like Nero from DMC4 and DeadEye sports both a huge sword and a revolver.Is the combat as bad as everyone is saying? No. Is it like Devil May Cry like everyone is saying? Definitely not. I'd label this game as a comfy hack'n'slash. You won't be blown away, but when you do pull off combos you will feel satisfied. Same with parrying. Enemies don't advertise their attacks like in Devil May Cry. If they're coming to attack you, they're going to attack you and you have to have that reaction time to parry. If you can, you'll feel on-top of the world until the second enemy elbow drops you into the concrete.Is the combat fast? Is it slow? It's as the game advertises it as. If you can get good at it, and work on gear customization. The combat can probably be boosted up to good tier.Enemies - Not much to say here, the enemies at least at my time in are "eh." Ya got your close-range, long-ranged, big boys, shield boys. Sometimes you'll face off against mutated wildlife and toxic bugs. Haven't reached the PSI enemies yet, so who knows.What's Bad.The Narration - Now, this is very subjective. I knew when buying this game the only voice is the narrators. I did not know he'd be translating the NPCs either. Which made it feel like I was relying on the Narrator ( which is read by David Shaw Parker who does a good job ) just to make it through the game. I think for the NPC's they should have done what Okami did. Give me the gibberish with the translated text. BioMutant will give you the gibberish and David comes in with "He says you're an idiot." How do I know that's what he said, David? It's like using Google Translate to get that Japanese Kanji tattoo. The Narrator should come in when he needs to, rather than every 2 seconds when talking to NPCs. It felt like the developers enjoys Davids work, slapped their hands on the desk, and demanded that he needed to be in the game as much as possible. Which fair play, but know the limits.The Tutorial - Oh. My. God. I am two hours in, and I think I'm finally at the end. For about an hour, you're in a linear tutorial teaching you to basic. When you think it's over, it kicks you into the open-world. Tells you to pick a side, good or bad. Then it kicks you back into a tutorial where you learn about crafting, mods, and all that jazz. It was there when I finally took a break to type up this review, so I pray when I go back into the game I can actually explore.In conclusion. Does the game deserve 48% Or whatever it is at when I finally push the 'Post Review' button? No. Additionally, I don't think it's fair for users to post a negative review for bugs for a game that released just 3 hours ago? No. As far as I'm aware the game had no Early Access, Alpha Test , Beta Test. So having a wave of players coming in with thousands of different devices. Steam has forums for a reason.What is my out of 10 for this game? A 7 out of 10 right now, and that's being frustrated that I feel like I'm stuck in a tutorial. Can it go up? Can it go down? Yeah. But it's definitely higher than a 50% for the amount of polish the game has.

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately I can't recommend this game. It starts nicely, the combat system is fun, the world is big... Just shooting is straight up better than any melee skill, magic or bio power. There is simply no deep in it, is always the same, it's extremely repetitive. The enemies aren't even different.* The game has no idea what it want to be. It tries to be an open world sandbox and an action RPG but fails at being both. It tries to be all in once doing poorly everything. The map marks never work properly, enemies level up with you, doing whatever gear you have pointless, I've been using the same rifle since lvl 20. Doing sidequests is just meaningful if you want to go for the 100%, which can be done in less than 30 hours. The game is just empty.* It has 5 music tracks, one of them is the main menu.* I've encountered more than one bug but nothing game breaker. I couldn't jump, use items or roll from time to time. * The game has a positive and good eco friendly message but the story is a mess that you end up rushing everything. if you want a casual game to play once in a while, BIOMUTANT can be a fresh thing. If you want a fun adventure, it isn't. It's just boring and, sadly, I can't recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: I felt I should get that out of the way, as it's important, because my review would be different had I paid full price. I'll continue where I left off by telling you what Biomutant is not:Biomutant is not Dark Souls, Monster Hunter or Skyrim. If you are expecting that feeling, or that combat, or that scale, you will be disappointed.What Biomutant is, is fun. As has been mentioned, the tutorial is oddly lengthy, and feels restrictive compared to the standard 'do what you want after 5 minutes' approach Open World games have always taken. When the game starts to amp up, I found it best to approach it more like "Devil May Cry", with the dual pistols to match. The combat isn't as impactful as some people may expect (especially the melee), but it bnrings back memories of Dynasty Warriors combo streaks, and the spectacle is definitely there. I am enjoying what I'm playing, and, to me, that is the most important factor. If you're looking for a serious epic adventure, look elsewhere.If you're looking for something your kids can watch you play, and doesn't feel like a second job after a long shift, you've found it here.

_childDocuments_.review: I would definitely recommend this game, just not at full price.  If you can snag it for $30-$40, I'd say that you would get your money's worth as long as you know what you're getting into.  This game is a solid AA experience and should be priced as such.  When I pay full AAA price for a game, I expect the polish that is worthy of a AAA game, which Biomutant just does not have.  A lot of the game is pretty janky.  Jank doesn't equal bad, but it's not something you want when you put down $60.  Animations don't flow into each other, instead just doing a hard cut between jumping, running, climbing, etc.  There's also a lot of "Hello, fellow kids" type of slang used, like "this looks stronk enough" and "it hits you right in the feels."  It has a lot of dated cutesy-meme terms that the game uses, probably leftover from when they first started developing the game around six years ago and terms like that were used often.  However, it fits in decently well with a lot of the weird names that the game gives items and places, so it's not as off-putting as it could be.The narrator is overused.  He absolutely nails his performance, and the way he reads his lines is done very well.  But the game relies on him way too much to tell the story and a lot of times he will end up pulling you out of what you're doing.  You'll probably end up turning him all the way down so he only narrates what he needs to.  Again, the actor himself does a great job, his work is just implemented in a way that doesn't serve the game very well.  They probably would have been better off just going with Animal Crossing-type dialogue:  gibberish and speech bubbles.  The open world can be a bit empty at times.  There are plenty of cool places to discover, but most of the time the only things you can do with them are either find loot or fight a boss, then find more loot.  This issue could be solved with some post release patches if the devs wanted to.  An extra pilgrim here, maybe a random bandit group there, just some more life to fill in the world in between locations would go a long way.With this in mind, you'll still experience a game with a charming setting and beautiful visuals and an entertaining, if not mildly repetitive, combat loop.  And don't forget about the loot.  This game is heaven for loot ♥♥♥♥♥♥.  Crafting is very entertaining, and if you're into that aspect, you'll be combing through every corner for another attachment for your gun, another handle for your sword, and all sorts of other stuff.  Like I said before, this isn't a bad game in the slightest.  Just overpriced for what it provides.  Definitely wait for a sale and (hopefully) a couple of post-release content updates.

_childDocuments_.review: Biomutant is a cool game, shame it got such bad reviews. Don't get me wrong, it's definitely flawed and underdeveloped in some parts - not a polished AAA experience. It's also a bit weird in general and not for everyone. But that doesn't mean it's a bad game and I'm tired of inflated video game reviews treating everything that's not at least an 8 (on a 1-10 scale!) like it's garbage. - Very fun and fluid. You have different weapons and abilities at your disposal. You can use melee weapon / ranged weapon / special (magic) abilities seamlessly during the fight. Also the abilities are pretty cool, like telekinesis, or mushrooms that bounce you and your enemies into the air. - It's very "stylized" and colorful.  Combat is flashy with comic book style text effects. Character design is quirky and cute if you're into that stuff (like monsters in onesies, lol) - The environment is done well, from various city districts like suburbs and industrial zones, to the biomes in general - forests, tropical waterways, mountains and also dangerous zones - cold, heat, biohazard, etc. Map is just the right size. There's a lot of loot and side quest NPCs scattered around the map that you can find by exploring. - Definitely one of the better crafting systems I encountered in a game. You get many different parts by looting and you can make things like a sword with a banana handle (lol) - Clothing items you can find are pretty good (especially the hats!), you can have a soldier furry, samurai furry, cowboy furry... - There are "regular" mounts, but you also get a mech, jet ski, submarine and similar stuff that can only be used in certain zones (they're customizable btw)Unpopular opinion, but I like . I only heard him repeat lines a handful of times. is not bad, but it's not particularly good either - the way it's presented is a bit off and lacks depth.Main storyline is not long but there's lots of side content (I'm 30 hours in and I can see it will take me at least 30-40 more before I finish the game).  are just ok - generic open world stuff. Most of them aren't too creative and there's a lot of "Find Item 0/10" type of missions. - Characters speak gibberish, so basically the whole dialogue is actually The Narrator translating what they're saying. I feel like that really detracts from the characters and makes them seem a bit shallow and generic instead of unique NPCs with their own personality? - The game doesn't really feel that challenging even on the highest difficulty (combat is still fun though). Also, puzzles are so easy that I wouldn't even call them puzzles.So yeah, the game is far from perfect but it's definitely worth playing. If you're looking for a cute furry character to customize, flashy combat and a beautiful map to get lost in, this is definitely the right game. But if you want a deep story, characters to get invested in or challenging gameplay, you should probably skip it.

_childDocuments_.review: I beat the game on my first character in around 9 1/2 hours, and there is a newgame+, if you like that sort of thing. I think that what Biomutant gets right, it gets almost perfect, but there are also a lot of flaws, some serious, and some minor. First, I'll talk about what I think it gets right. 1. The game is absolutely gorgeous. The colors are vibrant, and the variety from place to place is fairly decent. One of the more minor things I noticed was how good your clothes look when they are soaked by the rain. Note: This was with max settings, and I do not currently have any knowledge about how the game looks with lower settings. 2. Combat is very good in this game. Every character has access to melee and ranged attacks, as well as more magical attack if you spec into them. You'll generally be going between using the ranged and melee attacks in fights, rarely using only one. I purchased a few magic abilities, but rarely found myself using them, not that their bad, but I felt confident enough with just the ranged and melee attacks. I will say that I felt overwhelmed by enemies sometimes, when there were quite a lot of them. I played on medium difficulty, so you may get a different experience if on a different difficulty.3. NPC designs were very nice in this game. They are quite varied, in looks at least, and of good quality. 4. The crafting system in Biomutant is one of the better I've seen in recent games. It's fairly simple, but there is enough variety between weapon and armor parts to make each one unique, at least in looks. As for the abilities that the parts give you, I've only encountered a few that actually give some sort of ability, so I'm not sure how often they do. 5. Looting in this game is very satisfying. For the most part, whenever I saw a container I could open, I would do so, just to see what interesting things popped out.6. Character customization is something that I am actually split on. The good part of the customization, in my opinion, is your gear. You can make your character look wildly different with a few changes of gear, and there is a lot of it.Now for the flaws.1. As for the bad part of character customization, I felt that creating your character was lackluster. When I heard that your appearance would change based on your stats, I also thought that they would implement interesting abilities that would alter your appearance as well, but unfortunately, it is only stats. To add onto this, choosing a class feel utterly worthless, as all classes have access to all abilities. Even the starting perk that you get with your class is unlockable on other classes. The only things that are unique to each class are a few perks, that consist of upgrades such as "rifles deal extra damage", or "you reload weapons faster." It kind of feels like they didn't try to make the classes unique.2. Dialogue is awful, and impersonal in this game, as you have a narrator who translates the gibberish that NPCs speak in every single conversation. It makes it hard to connect with the characters, when you hear the same voice speaking for them all.3. Quests are super repetitive. Most of the main quests consist of multiple fetch or find this person objectives, and then fighting the boss with the new mount you get (we will talk about mounts later). I think on the final Worldeater quest, you do like five or six of these monotonous fetch quests before being able to fight the boss.4. Speaking of mounts, they are stupid. The very first mount you get is a giant mech, but guess what, you can summon it pretty much nowhere. You also what is essentially a jet ski, and at one point, I was in water, but for whatever reason, it wouldn't let me summon it, so I drowned. The optional mounts you find while exploring are also pretty lackluster, and for whatever reason, they feel slow, for a mount that is. There is one really cool mount, though, that I don't want to spoil.5. The story is meh. It kept foreshadowing an unexpected ending (it literally says the story will end unexpectedly multiple times), but it just wasn't. There are multiple endings depending on your choices, so maybe there are some unexpected ones, but it would have been nice if each ending had a twist with such blatant talk that there would be one.Overall, I think that this game is fun for what it is. I don't know if it is $60 fun, but $30 would be a good price if it ever goes on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: BIOMUTANT is a game that benefits from having some expectations before playing it. I had an excellent time with it after following it for a few months before it's release, gleaning a sense of what the creators wanted to accomplish with this release. It's exactly what I expected, though, inevitably lacking some polish as the team was of moderate size (~20 people). Anyway, the negatives are already ubiquitous within every review posted thus far, so I'll focus on the major positives.Ultimately, I think gamers with a proclivity for investigating every nook and cranny of an open world and a penchant for whimsy will really enjoy this game. The beautiful world of BIOMUTANT is filled with an abundance of life and charm if you care to look for it. It really scratched by exploration itches while still providing a rewarding and malleable combat system. But malleable, I mean that any way that you prefer to play the game, it will allow you to, with a real RPG feel to creating your character and specializing in the combat aspect that most interest you. I loved the Wung-Fu combo system. It takes some time to find your rhythm with the combat, as I believe everyone will feel there own subjective inclination to combine particular moves together. If you take that small time to play around with each type of weapon and ability I promise you will find a harmony, otherwise, you will likely just spam the ranged attacks which will get mundane fast, and is, unfortunately, effective. I had a ton of fun with the combat myself, mixing a number of ranged, melee, and psi powers into my arsenal. I felt the combat was far more rewarding than other exploration focused open-world games, like Breath of the Wild.Again, the world is lively if you allow yourself to embrace it. Although you'll reach a point (~20 hrs in if you are going out of your way to stop at every destination) that the areas will appear redundant, you will still encounter unique mini-bosses and spectacular loot; the loot and the crafting is truly one of the best facets of the game. I have spent an inordinate amount of time with the crafting system. Every weapon you create feels so unique and you have a personal connection to it, since you built it piece-by-piece. The armor, too, (especially the interminable list of hats you will collect) is so diverse. There is a menu where you can easily swap between 5 outfits you've put together, injecting a mutable personality to your character. The side characters are quirky and charismatic, though, your interactions with them are almost always fetch quests that will at least result in a cool reward. The lore, while superficially intriguing, does not have much depth and the main story is relatively short. However, the main bosses (the four world eaters and Lupa-Lupin) do offer some challenge and unique fights. Every world-eater requires a new, fun vehicle to defeat. I slowly progressed through the story, focusing more on the exploration and letting the excellent foundation of the lore breathe life and meaning to the world and its different biomes, tribes, and creatures. It's a charming game. One I had a ton of fun with. I'm not sure how it fares on a second play-through, and expect the games cracks to be accentuated then. But I'm very happy with what I got out of it, with just under 50 hrs at the moment. Objectively, the game is good -- slightly above average, probably a 6/10; that is, when including all of the negatives, which was not a focus of this review, as I'm sure you've heard them all already. There is a lot of potential here and I personally had a blast. That's why I'm giving BIOMUTANT, based on my experience and love for exploration heavy and zen gamer friendly games, an...8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Another poor port from console to Mouse and keyboard.Game says you can re-map controls, but what it doesn't tell you is you WILL lose a lot of functionality when doing so.For Example: The default button to toggle you powers is middle mouse.  Since I want to play pure mage I remapped it to E (E is normally interact).  BUT using E instead of middle mouse breaks the ability menu.  you can only quick cast whatever power is your 1st power.  This means you can't access the other 3 powers using E like you can if using middle mouse.  It also means you can't charge up your "Spark Ball" and can only quick-cast it.Q & E are arguably the 2 most important keys for ability's in PC gaming.   So these dev's hard-coded those 2 keys and switching them out will break the game.  But even switching the middle mouse and the right mouse button breaks things.  Using default middle mouse will bring up a menu that visually shows your 4 power options.  Switching the ability menu to the right mouse button and it breaks it.  The visual will pop-up for a split second and then disappear.Hard-coding things to specific keys and not allowing them to be changed is frustrating for PC players and our number one complaint when it comes to ported games.

_childDocuments_.review: Thoughts on the game so far:Positives:- Creative character design- Wonderful art design- Graphics are nice- Fighting is fun (especially with melee and your added psi,etc..)- No bugs or crashes so far- Lots of ways to customize your characters build- Has a nice Chill, Charming and funny vibe ala Fable 1/2- There is a HUGE variety of enemies to encounter- Enjoying the music so far- A nice surprise is the crafting, some of the best around!- Fun to rip around the game world, movement and jumping feels goodNegatives/Things to Improve:- The quest design is pretty generic most of the time, biggest issue for me personally- Performance isn't bad but could be improved- The audio for when weapons hit should be better (this is probably my 2nd biggest issue)- Tutorial might annoy some people who just want to jump into the open world right away- The writing is a missed chance, I like the overall idea for the story but not executed well- Some elements feel half bakedHonestly surprised at all the negative reviews this game is getting. It is exactly what I was expecting tbh, a Ratchet & Clank, Fenyx Immortals, Zelda/Kingdom of Amalar style game that isn't super hardcore. You can relax and chill out and play this without worrying to much. If you went in thinking this would be Dark Souls or Divinity OS 2 level of complexity or difficulty I don't know what to say, I love those games to but this is a somewhat more casual action rpg. Right now I would give it a 7/10, won't win Game of The Year or anything but its about what I was expecting, maybe even slightly better in some ways (the crafting,etc..).Won't be for everyone but if you go in knowing what type of game you are getting (go check out some of the many youtube videos out there showing its gameplay) or don't have crazy high expectations you will find a game that is fun, charming and alot better than many of the reviews have said.I have played around 2 hours and have not had the game for 14 days, i could refund right now if I wanted to but so far I have had a good time on the game and not even thinking about getting a refund, whats here isn't perfect but there is alot of fun to be had here and alot of things done very well.Oh yeah.. and my character has joined the dark side, he is now punching injured travelers, joining evil tribes and burning down villages, the evil run experiment has started lolThis is a smaller scale open world game, it is not trying to be super serious or crazy hard, its about relaxing and doing some leveling up, customization, crafting, flying around the map and riding mounts around the map and soaking in the beautiful gameworld. If I was scoring it I would give it 7/10, it is a smaller scale game and not a AAA game and the price reflects that (AAA games here in Canada are 79.99, this game was 59.99).This is a better Feynx Immortals or the last few Ratchet and Clank games to be honest, that game had much better puzzles but I find nearly every other aspect in Biomutant to be better.**Will add more thoughts after I finish the game**

_childDocuments_.review: Title: BiomutantRating: 6.5/10Platform: Steam DeckBiomutant is an action-RPG game developed by Experiment 101, consisting of 20 people - veterans of the Just Cause series. The world they have created offers a unique atmosphere through humanoid animal inhabitants in a post-apocalyptic setting ravaged by humans.What immediately sets Biomutant apart is its character creation system, which allows players to customize the appearance and abilities of their character to a wide extent. We can choose between various genetic mutations that affect our character's abilities and appearance. This flexibility allows for creating a character that precisely matches our preferences.Biomutant takes place in an open, fairly diverse (by which I mean varying biomes), thankfully not sprawling, post-apocalyptic world. I admit, it captivated me right away and drew me in for several hours. Picturesque landscapes - forests, hot deserts, icy tundras, or contaminated areas, each have their own atmosphere and require appropriate equipment for traversal. The characters inhabiting the world, much like the protagonist, are humanoid animals that have adapted to specific environments and settled there.The story in the game exists, and that's all I can say about it because it didn't interest me at all. Here begin to appear the main flaws of the production. In short, the plot revolves around avenging our mother's killer and saving the Tree of Life, with a war between factions inhabiting the world squeezed in between. Here it is worth mentioning the dialogues, which stand out from other games because the characters in the game speak in their own dialect, and everything is presented/explained by the narrator. Unfortunately, after a while, this becomes terribly tedious because the narrator has the same tone of voice, lacking any emotion.Now onto the combat system, which combines elements of melee combat, shooting, and acrobatics. The combat is dynamic and satisfying, especially when utilizing various skills and attack combinations. However, the combat mechanics can be somewhat imprecise, leading to frustration at times. The game features several unique bosses and fights with them in various ways, but they do not pose a significant challenge.Visually, Biomutant presents itself very well. The game world is colorful and full of details, creating a unique atmosphere. The music and sounds are also well-chosen, supporting the atmosphere of the post-apocalyptic world. The translation into Polish is solid but with minor errors.In summary, Biomutant is a game that evokes many emotions. Despite certain shortcomings, such as a lack of narrative depth and issues with the combat system, the game offers a unique world to explore and an interesting character creation system. For fans of action games with RPG elements, Biomutant may be a worthwhile choice.BiomutantOcena: 6.5/10Ogrywane: Steam Deck.
