_childDocuments_.review: I want to emphasize that I have NOT finished the game yet, and I may change my views on this by end of game (if I get there). I'll break things up into categories that hopefully won't give any spoilers:CombatBiomutant presents itself as a DMC-style combat system, but limits itself to very little combos and little variation in general. The flow between guns and weapons don't feel intuitive or synergistic, and I find it very rare to feel that satisfied "hell yeah" moment when I pull anything off in combat. Even if you get the super-fu, it's super limited and restricts you to a new (SMALL) combo set. Why? Why not make it like DMC and boost my moves and maybe have a couple specials? Or maybe give me a chance to bust out a new combo in super-fu form to pull off a cool move. It's also annoying that you have to pull off three different combos, when you barely have any combos to begin with (especially early game). I feel like the moves/combos that exist are aesthetic and creative, and the developers are definitely on to something, but it feels incomplete and half-assed. I love the customization aspect, and I'm hoping that later game I can see some seriously creative builds, as there's SO many items to choose from for your armor/weaponry. I like that there's multiple classes of weapons - but yet again, each one feels super limited by combos and thus, doesn't give me enough reason to want to swap between them. Swapping between weapons is also a HUGE pain in the ass. I'd love to be able to easily swap between weapons during combat to change up the combos and see more variation in combat. Story/ExplorationThe story is all over the place for tone and I absolutely hate that. I get the not-so-serious vibes the game is trying to present, but when the game's supposed to be serious, commit to it. The game goes open world too quickly when it still wants to be super linear and makes for empty pointless exploration. Once you go through the linear intro plot points you "unlock" abilities (ie. swimming) and items on the map (ie. materials). What's the point of opening the world for exploration if there's nothing there yet, that's completely limited by plot progression? Why not just force the player through the plot first to get the game going. And it doesn't stop there either - the game consistently stops you for long (and mostly pointless) plot progression. I never know when I can actually get in the groove of gameplay or when I should just get a bowl of popcorn and watch the endless talking. Also, why do I play a character that doesn't even have a name?? Am I the only one bothered by this? You play a character with significant background story and impact on the world. Why wouldn't you have a name?Lastly, why does the narrator wait until the gibberish is done? I don't think anyone sits there wondering if they can decipher the language over time or generally enjoys listening to it. Why not at least make theoption to have the narrator translate during, or better yet not at all, and just have subtitles?GraphicsIt's a new game in 2021 - it has good graphics. The aesthetic is great, the scenery is gorgeous, the animals are super creative... list goes on. I find some of the textures to be out of wack, hit-boxes are out of place, and interactions with objects (especially walls and trees) are all over the place making it confusing to know what you can and cannot climb, punch holes in, or interact with in general. The game gives you hints using yellow color on objects, but it's not always the case, and it just adds to the confusion for me.AudioI noticed a lot of glitches with audio syncing with movement and contact with targets/objects. The biggest issue I have with audio in this is the soundtrack is lame and lacks variation. Music for battle hardly triggers, let alone is interesting or moving. So far, I'd put this game at ~6/10. If the developers put out a MAJOR overhaul on the combat system, and some serious patches to fix the interactions/exploration in the world, I could honestly see this as an 8+, as there's SO much potential in this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I've never left a review on Steam before, but I feel like this game is getting a lot of bad press, especially just after launch.First off, the things I like:-The atmosphere is absolutely beautiful. It really is very fun to experiment.-Personally, I find the combat fun. It's definitely improved since launch, I focus on melee and do way more damage than ranged. The melee sound effects have also been improved, which improves the whole experience.-Finally, I feel confident in the developers to continue improving the game. They have already rolled out two large patches in a short space of time, and I don't doubt they'll have more on the way.It's not a perfect game, there are things I didn't like:-Fast travel points decrease in frequency as you progress-There's a lot of side quests. I'm a bit of a completionist, so it's difficult to get through all of them.-Narrator is a bit tedious eventually. But as others have pointed out, this can be disabled in the options menu and has been improved with patches.In general, a lot of the negatives can be patched out in the future and, at the moment, do not ruin a very enjoyable, immersive and unique game. I will say that the price point is a little large for what is essentially a big budget indie title, so wait for a sale if you're unsure.But overall, would thoroughly recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Almost every video game I have ever played has had at least one part that felt like a chore to me. You know - that mechanic or minigame that makes you groan inwardly and think "Crap. Another one of these." The unfun part of the game you muscle through so you can get back to the fun part of the game.Biomutant doesn't have any of these. The game is pure fun.The loot/crafting system, as well as the skills systems, make it incredibly easy to customize the game to your liking. The game is slightly repetitive, but only in the ways that all video games are (re-used assets, similar puzzles). And Biomutant is more creative about it than most. The world is vibrant and feels alive.The real selling point of the game, though, is movement. This is one of those rare games in which the simple act of moving through the world is a joyful experience. I am a lifetime lover of maps, but when I play Biomutant I hardly ever look at the map (in fact, an absence of a minimap is usually a deal breaker for me in an RPG). Mainly because the world is so full and interesting (and therefore distracting). You see a thing. You go to investigate said thing, and during the process you see another interesting thing. And from there you see another. And an hour later you find yourself wondering what it was you were doing when you noticed the first interesting thing.Biomutant is interesting and fun. And more. It is an absolute delight. I highly recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Just few hours into this AAA game and I already hate it.The camera doesn't feels right. It is way too close, so I can't see ammo (which is shown above the gun somehow). If I switch it to "vertical", then it's low way too far and I dislike alien-like vision. The player character is way too small and camera makes it hard to observe surroundings, which are often much higher. I believe this game could be much better as a first person FPS.I dislike combat pretty much, was hoping it will get more interesting later, but not, it's just constant running in circles and pressing dodge, despite I am trying to build ranged, namely mage-type character... there is no stealth, tactical approach or anything: the enemies simply spawn and run for you. Playing it batman games way (pressing parry when seeing attack indicators) is surprisingly hard and unreliably, perhaps it's just my poor skills, though I didn't have problem to do perfect parries in e.g. Assassin Creed games.The game performance is very unstable. Maybe my system is not top, but turning everything on "low" and having stable 60 fps, then suddenly it drops to 30 and stay there in the city.. same with "maximum" where it drops to 30 under the ground. WTF? Why is it 60 or 30? It must be something hardcoded into game engine, made for consoles...Big locations with nothing. Occasionally there are chests. Then city with hundereds of chests everywhere. Exploring is most of time not rewarding. It's hard to see if location has something hidden and map is surrounded by invisible walls everywhere, feels really poor with double jump to hit such wall.The loot system coupled with craft system is not interesting. The inventory UI has problems (e.g. selecting head slot).The dialogues are dumb, I need to press key 4 times to just listen a gossip or begin trading, lol. The choices are unclear, several times the NPC reply something totally unrelated to the option I select.The narrator voice is annoying in Russian translation. It comments everything and I dislike the style where narrator translates what NPC tells, wonder if someone actually find that good, to me it's just a cheap way to simplify translation, but lack of good voices makes story telling really poor, imho.Not sure if I continue playing the game, but perhaps my and others negative reviews will prevent someone from wasting their money.

_childDocuments_.review: I've never actually done a steam review before (and I'm by no means some professional review...er thing) but I felt the need to because this game was my first preorder. Normally I'm not a fan of preorders because of the history of money grabbing and dipping out into the darkness never to be heard from again but I had a really good feeling about this game! Or... maybe I just really wanted to be a mutant rat/raccoon/lemur thing kicking ass in a wasteland. And playing it now and reading the reviews, its feeling a lot like Cyberpunk. I've loved Cyberpunk and not had the "gamebreaking" issues there either but still people insist it was unplayable. But it wasn't (for me personally having no glitches aside from people in a sit pose walking once or twice) and this game is getting a lot of undeserved hate too I think. When I saw the Dev update, he said he'd call it a mix between BOTW, Ratchet and Clank and Devil May Cry and honestly? Yeah. I'd say that is pretty spot on. I've seen a lot of issues from people mainly against frame drops and sound for combat and while I did, for the first couple of hours, see the frame drops, fixing up my settings to what fit my personal (aging, yes) setup fixed that for me entirely. As far as the combat audio, I've seen people saying there is none or its too low to matter and personally, again, I've not had any issues with that. Its clear, audible and pretty great music to my ears with the combat. Breath-taking scenery, models are incredibly done, the monsters and characters are unique, the foliage is beautiful and duh, unique, the animation is insane, the landscape is anxiety inducing like I feel like it should be. Its a WASTELAND but there are beautiful little encampments and miniature townships.I can however see the issue with some people viewing some quests as "grindy" or "repetitive" with the quest for  . The only other issues I've seen (and it is purely cosmetic): The background blur in conversational cutscenes. Specifically in these scenes I've noticed the background blurring is... a bit off. There is something wrong with some further things being crisp edged, the blur not quite making it to some parts on the background. But again, purely cosmetic. Another huge complaint I didn't quite agree with was the narrator. First and foremost, his voice does to me what David Attenborough's voice does to me: it relaxes me and makes me beyond happy to keep listening. Its soothing, elegant and most importantly, I think its important to the story. The creatures are mutants. Animal mutants. I've not once been upset that a mange riddled rat didn't speak English to me from the dumpster but I have, in fact, wished I had a narrator to help tell me what animals were screaming at me about. It makes it much more immersive in that its helpful to the character and to me. It would seem odd if I could just understand what a bipedal rodent was saying to me.

_childDocuments_.review: I had this game on my wishlist for over 2 years, and I was getting a little worried about the mixed reviews, but honestly Biomutant is not a bad game. Yes, it is far more childish than I was expecting, and 'medium' difficulty is like any other game's 'very easy', but it is a fun experience nonetheless.The crafting mechanic is great, and this is coming from someone who usually ignores that kind of thing in most other games. Exploration is a major part aspect of the game, and piecing together the history and lore of the world can be so intriguing. The variation in combat styles is a shallow ocean rather than a deep puddle, so you can very quickly max out the rather samey abilities for your playstyle, but this does allow you to mix things up without having to worry about completely respecing.Some noticeable downsides though:- The combat can get pretty repetitive, even if you mix up your weapons- The narrator has been known to get on peoples' nerves when he chirps up unprovoked- The permanence/impermanence of your choices is not made clear, and it is difficult to tell whether or not a choice is permanent or can be changed at a later date- What was looking to be a more gritty post-apocalyptic game about mutations has turned out to be a casual 'Ratchet and Clank' style game- The puzzles are the easiest I've ever seen in a video game, and even if you fail one by mistake they can be immediately repeatedBasically, if you were thinking this game was going to be a souls-like, you'll be disappointed. It is, however, a great casual game for chilling out, and particularly a good game for young teens. So if you want a nice open-world game that isn't too big and you can relax while playing, Biomutant might just be for you.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the perfect example of why Steam could use a 'meh' option for reviewing products. For now I will give it a positive review because I am having fun with the game.The customization and exploration are really great and the world is graphicly impressive and fun to traverse. The combat is OK at best, but I think it's not that bad. The ability to collect different mounts and parts for the vehicles you can have is really cool.Now for the bad stuff: The story is a mess and not interesting at all, the good and evil system is horrible and not fleshed out at all (It's just always picking between a yes or a no and that makes you either more evil or more good), the puzzles or if you can even call them that are just the same thing copy pasted everywhere, the dialogue is also just the same thing copy pasted everywhere in most cases, the side missions are ALSO doing basicly the same things over and over again.This game would have been more acceptable for a 30 euro price tag instead of 60. Nonetheless it is a fun game to just relax and explore but don't expect anything meaningfull oitherwise.

_childDocuments_.review: Neutral would be a better option but since everyone who wants to give neutral actually gives a thumbs down I choose a thumbs up.Pros:+ beautiful world+ entertaining combat so far (nothing special but arcade-style on a similar level like Batman Arkham Asylum)+ fun to traverese the world+ humorous at timesCons:- empty open world (aside from "combat arenas" you rarely stumble upon enemies or npcs)- in a game with rodent characters i would expect them to be able to climb some walls at least (climbing is possible at certain points in the world though)- The game tries to hard to transfer a Yin-Yang message. Every second or third sentence is some stuff you could find in a fortune cookie.- to much handholding. 4 hours in and there are still tutorials popping up and the narrator interferring with simple actions like activating a switch (i will give turning him off a try though)Story:+- not really a pro or a con since it is really up to the individual player: Humankind was bad and the world suffered. Overall I will continue playing but it feels like this world could have achieved more. I am not attatching to any of the characters so far because everyone gives me the Zen / Yin-Yang vibe. Which is fine, if it  wasn't so "in your face!". No character in particular stands out. They all blend together to an overall message.If you are looking for this kind of refreshing message and some not so difficult combat then this game might be for you, otherwise be aware.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start by saying I had fun playing BIOMUTANT, and I don't think its an awful game. It wasn't buggy, it ran well, and there were some pretty cool aspects of the experience- but I still need to be honest.The story in this game is complete nonsense, at certain points it seems like it was just an after-thought. Someone made the strange design choice to have an omni-present second person narrator constantly chatter throughout the game. From the glimpses of a cohesive story that I could pick up, the pacing was extremely uneven.The gameplay itself is actually pretty fun. I played a high mobility rogue and enjoyed exploring different weapons and approaches to combat...for about 5 hours. Then it started getting a bit dry; there are roughly 5 or 6 enemy types, and for something based so heavily on rogue combat the enemies are flat out brain dead and the finer points of melee encounters seem blunt and numb (no staggering, parry's don't counter, etc.) A good way to put it would be a clunky Shadow of Mordor combat with guns.I got 10 hours of good entertainment out of it. I don't really want the hours back, and I'm happy with what I got overall. That being said, I don't think Ill play it ever again. If you like RPG's and have cash/are bored- pick it up. Otherwise, you aren't missing anything ground breaking.

_childDocuments_.review: It's boring and the way that they chose to tell the story through a narrator is possibly one of the worst ideas in gaming. I usually love stories in games but in this game i just find myself skipping every dialogue and every cutscene because i completely lost interest within the FIRST hour of the game, not only did i lose interest, i actively annoys me because the NPC or whatever will say something, you then have to wait for a solid 5 seconds and THEN the narrator translates. Seriously, every sentence in this game takes 30 seconds to get through, it's unreal. The combat is fun.. at first but i can tell that it's going to be a drag later on. The game doesn't run very well either, getting huge framerate dips (RTX 2070, i7 9th gen) at 1080p which just shouldn't be happening, i can run metro exodus 1440p with maxed out graphics, no problem. The world is beautiful, sure. But it serves no purpose, there is seriously no reason to explore this world because looting isn't fun and it isn't rewarding in the slightest. You can find hidden chests at obscure locations, and your reward? Probably a healing item, of which you'll have hundreds of. The flashback sequences are also, BORING and completely pointless. The second i enter one of these horrible sequences, all i want is to get out ASAP. I seriously closed my game over this last night, my time is better spent sleeping than being bored to death.

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of reviews have put this game as Game of the Year. Do I agree the game is decent. Yes, but not Game of the year worthy. I will admit that it is a fun game, but the repetitive locations and the lack of care for dungeons annoy me. For a game that was pushed back to be polished, nothing seems cohesive. I get so bored with the the tribe warfare aspect because it is the same thing. It is an aspect of the game that really sticks out to me when people ask about this game. All the camps are the same, you do literally the same thing to take them over. Blow up the front gate and run through killing 4 enemies at a time on the first one. Second one you do something outside the camp that finishes it entirely. Third one you just kill some big animal. Last one you take over. I don't even see the point of upping the difficulty level on the game, because this game is way to easy. You level up way to fast. yes the game has a ton of items to find, but the world is nothing exciting to go and explore. Its go hit this scrap pile or go open find some loot that ultimately makes not difference. Weapon crafting on the fly seems way to easy. You should be forced to go to a table to add items and create weapons. There is zero point to go into the towns and mingle with the NPCs placed in the game. I have not really experienced any bugs in the game apart from a quest I can no longer do because the boat will not move after already being activated once. Was this game worth $60. No not at all. Maybe 25 to 30. Yes I do have over 20hrs in the game and I will complete otherwise I would just of wasted money on yet another disappointment of the year. This Review was all over the place, sorry about that.

_childDocuments_.review: On paper I should love this game. But I really don't.I finished the main story and almost all quests but I never really felt engaged by anything.The combat gets stale very quickly. The weapons don't really feel different enough in practice even with the tribal weapons. The combos are more or less the same for all of them and the "Super Wung-Chu" abilities are weaker than just continuing to beat someone over the head with my regular weapon. In general the fights are too easy, but annoying. They take quite a while, most enemies scale with your level and at least in melee there's just a lot of abilities that knock you back or on the ground making the fights last even longer.A lot of content is repeated. Cutscenes for the tribal conquests are 1:1 identical. Entire points of interests are practically the same and realistically there's not much difference between the things you fight. There's two types of puzzles that are just mindnumbingly easy but get reused so very often. Voicelines from the narrator get repeated waaay to often, though you can admittedly turn the frequency down in the settings.Quests almost exclusively boil down to "go there, get/kill thing, come back, watch cutscene, repeat."The narration was offputting. Not having any of the characters have a proper voice removes most of the connection you might have with them. Their designs certainly are memorable. But I would have prefered no voice acting at all and just reading what they say in direct speech instead of what we got.The world is nicely designed, but it feels largely empty. almost none of the points of interest have anything interesting to do aside from walking into every corner, killing every enemy and opening all the containers.I liked the crafting system, but by the second conquered tribe the upgrades I got were marginal and at least with ranged weapons there's a clear best choice.The "morality" system is just weird with the choices. It's fine in general. And I understand why I get "dark aura" for killing an animal I caught or punching a pilgrim I saved. What I don't get is why my character would to these things? Why would I save someone just to then punch them in the face? There's no proper explanation for that outside of "being a ♥♥♥♥"Then there's the general Jank. There is almost no way to distinguish if a button needs to be mashed repeatedly, held or just pressed once during QTEs, and especially during combat you don't really have the time to look at them well enough to check. There's no good way to sort through the massive amount of loot you get outside of looking at it's value and rarity. Virtually all items have a rarity even when unneeded like for the different mounts or automaton skins.The display of materials only goes up to 99, though you can in fact carry more than that.And finally the story: There's really nothing of note here. It's just surface level, without surprises, interesting characters or memorable moments.I really should have loved this game. But nothing it did, it did well and some things it did outright bad. I really don't know why I played 40 hours of this.

_childDocuments_.review: 60 hours in on side quests alone & Not done yet..It's easy to get lost in this game, with such beautiful & terrible scenes to explore and fun game mechanics to do so with- Curiosity abounds!You'll enjoy creating your character (with an opportunity to modify your character later in the game)and see them become an ultimate critter of the land. For better or for worse, your choices impact how characters treat you and how the game ends.I went with "psi-freak" and maxed out my "magic" abilities. After experimenting with the wild abilities, each satisfying and useful in their own ways- I found I would use the water bubble a Lot, rolling over small enemies and lacing them with elemental damage, you can hear fire crackle on the ground beneath, electricity arcing from my characters hands and wisps of radiation energy stinging the water bubble transfixed foes.Elementary, Watson.The water bubble is good for traversal as well, when activated you bounce and jump higher.I recommend that you find "Pebble," do his quests, to help upgrade your "prybar" to help you get behind lv. 2 locked doors- it's the only way.additionally you will love the animal mount for water situations- I'm sorry to be blanking on the characters name you need to talk to for this quest line, but he's a fisherman and he wants to move his home.also, recommend the luck attribute, it can be very rewarding.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, I have been waiting for this game ever since they announced it. Who doesn't want to play in a vast open world with crazy weapons, enemies, vehicles, and character creation!? If that's what you wanted to get here that is NOT what this is. The whole world feels dead, it is so far from being immersive it forces you to not want to play it. Here are some of the reasons that I will no longer be playing"THERE IS NO DIALOGUE FOR NPC's. Well, there kinda is... its literally just random gibberish that took 5 mins to record, and a narrator explains what they said. It honestly rips all of the personality out of every character you encounter. Not only that, the narrators voice instantly makes you want to skip all of the "dialogue" scenes. If you still cant grasp how bad that is, imagine playing a game but the whole time you have an e-book playing. (The gibberish also makes you want to rip you hair out)THE COMBAT IS BASIC. I dont have much to say about the combat other than it feels like it was taken from Monster Hunter World and somehow made it worse. Its pretty much just an insane amount of button mashing hoping youll land your combos.THE LOOTING IS TERRIBLE. Its just opening boxes that have 1 or 2 items inside or maybe looting a body. The worst part of it all is the animation for looting takes up the entire screen and has like a 1 second animation for each item. You can take all at once but if you do, it doesnt tell you the items you received so you have to look through you inventory for it. THE ANIMATIONS FEEL OLD. The animations dont line up with items in the game and are overall bad. It feels like it came out in 2013. Just another aspect of the game that make NPC's feel dead. It reminds me of the NPC's in CyberPunk 2077.   Those were the immediate things that stuck out to me. For me, this completely ruined the immersion of the game and just disappointed me. Its truly unfortunate because I was looking forward to it for awhile now. Some things I enjoyed were the character creation, exploration, and a few of the enemies. Hopefully overtime this game improves with updates and I might repay it a visit if the price drops. If this game were listed for $30 this would be a completely different review. If i were you, I would do the same if I were you.

_childDocuments_.review: It is honestly very hard to rate this game. On one hand, you can tell the developers put a lot of heart into it. The graphics are stunning, the lore is interesting, the world is like a breath of fresh air. Of notable features, crafting deserves to be mentioned as it is a very fun system, giving players the ability to hand-craft their gear. I like the aura system, as it is possible to define your character in some way, and it comes with witty dialogue between good and evil (similar to Black&White game).Unfortunately this is all there is to this game. Most of the time dialogue is pretty confusing and the illusion of choice lacks any impact on anything. A missed opportunity is for characters to actually talk for themselves, as the game uses the same narrator everywhere, which breaks immersion to the player. Not the best developer choice, given that the world is beautiful, and the player would most likely love to immerse themselves into it. I think a big missed opportunity is with base building. There is a run down place, and it would be great to remake it. Alliance with another tribe is nice and well, but as a player, I would love to start my own tribe in the game, which would make it a much better goal.Overall, I won't leave a negative score for this title. From what I see, it has gigantic potential to grow into something more, because the vast game world while nice, feels a bit too empty now. The developers obviously love their game and my hope is that Experiment 101 will improve it, based on player feedback. Doesn't look like the game needs lots of work to make it better. Is it worth $60? For now, I would say around $40 and hope the game will improve with few DLC's that will make it worth twice as much.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted this game ever since it was first announced. It felt like some futurepunk kung fu panda fever dream that seemed so cool.I hate feeling disappointed and I hate admitting that. I wanted to love this game.When you see people say the beginning takes so long before the game actually lets you go out into the world? They're not lying. It took me about 2 hours before I felt that I was actually out of the tutorial. Then, I played for an hour more before I just couldn't do it anymore.Here's my personal reasons for just having to stop:1. The Narrator. At first, I was like ok, this is charming. I can deal. Then, when I realized I was reading the subtitles faster than he would begin to read them, I was like, "ok shut up. Enough of that." I couldn't just turn the narrator down to 0. I had to fully turn down voice audio to finally read subtitles in peace.Need to take a drink while reading? Oh, the game still believes the narrator is reading that for you so it'll just skip to the next line without a prompt. Nice. Thanks.2. The audio mixing. It was like the majority of my time was running around a (beautiful) waste land with sleepy relaxing music that never seemed to change. I never heard my footsteps or jumping or the foliage around me. It wasn't very immersive. It was weird. Also, the automatons sound effects were ramped WAY higher than any of the voices and that just JERKED me out of the relaxing music that kept me at peace.3. Go wherever you want? Yeah but here's an objective marker that won't go away and if you interact with something else then it'll replace that objective marker with a new objective? How do I go back to the other? Oh screw it.4. I couldn't get invested in any of the characters or story. It was so formulaic. You're an orphan who suffered a great tragedy that you're trying to remember and you've started your adventure by visiting a people in need of a great savior. Also, and I've seen someone else say this, the game harps on and on about morality SOOO MUCH. It's really grating. I'd like a little nuance. Plus, the dark and light characters? _childDocuments_.review: Note: I'm reviewing v.15 but I have been playing the game since launch.With that said, I'm posting this to let people who are on the fence about buying this game because of all the mixed reviews that the DEV ARE INCREDIBLE! They have addressed 95% of all the pain points since the game launched in under a month which is mind-blowing, not just because they are so responsive, but because it is quite a difficult feat to accomplish for such a small studio. I can wholeheartedly recommend this gem of a game in it's current state. It isn't perfect by any means but... well... I'll just make a list:PROS+ Runs butter smooth on PC.+ Has gorgeous visuals and a unique art style that is a mix between comic strip and cartoony animation. (I totally dig the vibe!)+ The story is just campy enough to be fun+ Combat has gotten much better since launch. There is now a higher difficulty and lock on system that makes for some sweet squirrel fung-fu.+ There is a true sense of exploration in this game world that I have not found in video games for a long time. I would suggest just picking up all the side quests you can and then sort of forgetting about the map markers. Just explore the world at your leisure and find all the amazing secret bunkers, caves, waterfalls, towns, etc. You will organically complete 90% of the game just by exploring. CONS- The light/dark system is pointless. So far the only real influence it has had in the game has been to choose which high level powers you can unlock. And even those aren't really gated. Once you're about 20 hours in you will have enough light/dark points (30 each) to get powers from both sides, so who cares really? Besides that, it is basically a simple binary decision that dictates which ending you will see without any real consequence.- The side quests are all the same kill-fetch-return or simple puzzle format. Which is why I suggest just picking them all up and completing them organically as you explore. Then it doesn't feel quite so mundane to do them one after another.- Game eventually gets too easy. I went out of my way to make it harder for myself and even then it is a cakewalk once you've got good gear, even at the highest difficulty. I was curious to see what a crit build would look like and I put even single level upgrade into luck. Every single hit is crit. I can take a large mini-boss down in 3 hits, 5 bullets and maybe throw in the occasional spell cast. Like 10-15 seconds per fight, tops. The trash mobs often go down in just a couple of hits.My suggestion would be to enjoy this game for what it is. A fun furry dress em' up adventure in a new world, full of places to explore. It is not a tooth-grinding hack-n-slash with thatrical character development. Don't be a completionist. Think of it as a Zen Squirrel Simulator.

_childDocuments_.review:
Biomutant is an open-word, post-apocalyptic Kung-Fu fable RPG, with a unique martial arts styled combat system allowing you to mix melee, shooting and mutant ability action. Your actions play a major part in the unfolding of a story where End is coming to the New World. A plague is ruining the land and the Tree-of-Life is bleeding death from its roots. The Tribes stand divided, in need of someone strong enough to unite them or bring them all down...
Although you are guided through the world by a Storyteller that narrates every step of your journey, it's your actions and choices that'll decide how your story of survival ends.

name: HUNTDOWN
detailed_description: In the mayhem-filled streets of the future where criminal gangs rule and cops fear to tread, only the bounty hunters can free the city from the corrupt fist of felony. Lay waste to the criminal underworld and make a killing in this hard boiled action comedy arcade shooter. KICK-ASS CO-OP, FROM NEAR AND FAR Hunt solo or give suppressive fire and advance on the enemy together as you run, jump, and take cover in the mayhem-filled streets of the future. Whether your buddy is in the same room or on the other side of the planet, wreak havoc as a team through couch co-op or Steam Remote Play. NEW ACTION-PACKED ARCADE MODE It’s you versus the world as you’re pitted against players from all corners of the globe in a brutal battle to pummel your way up the leaderboards. Innovate and invent new ways to pulverize your foes to rack up your score, whether you make use of combo-kills, quickdraw weapon-swap bonuses, or just hurl criminals off the rooftops. In this nail-biting race against the clock, collect as many bounties as you can while you watch the numbers roll and strive to be the apex bounty hunter. PLAY AS THREE LEGENDARY BOUNTY HUNTERS Anna Conda: Ex-commando, firearms expert, and full-time loose-cannon, Anna will assassinate without question or mercy, as long as you don’t mind the collateral damage. John Sawyer: Once a Special Forces cop who left the law behind. This scarred veteran has lost so many limbs in combat he’s practically half robot. Mow Man: Modified recon droid, stolen and empowered with banned software. Trades bodies for cold hard cash. Don’t expect to be taken alive if Mow Man’s on your six. OLD SCHOOL MODERNIZED Hand painted 16-bit pixel art graphics and hand-drawn animations combined with fluid 60-FPS gameplay and an epic synthesized soundtrack. 20 LEVELS Gritty, neon soaked, graffiti strewn 80s cityscapes to clear, each with their own infamous gang boss to terminate and bounty to collect. FOUR UNIQUE GANGS TO DISMANTLE Hoodlum Dolls: Violent feral punks winning the gang war with the toothless authorities Misconducts: Organised hockey hooligans, experts in robbery and extortion with a penchant for explosives The Heatseekers: Murderous motorcycle club. These rockabilly villains style themselves on the centurions of Ancient Rome NO.1 Suspects: Masters of discipline and organised crime. Martial arts experts, these slick psychopaths control the night through their casinos and nightclubs CHOOSE YOUR WEAPON Confiscate machine guns, laser weapons, katanas, grenades and more, and turn them on their owners. Stab, shoot and explode your way through swathes of gangs and bosses and collect your bounty.

_childDocuments_.review: Occasionally, I launch through RetroArch some old Sega Genesis / Mega Drive titles such as . While I enjoy the sprite work and feel, I only have fun for a couple of minutes until the approximate game design and dated level structure bring me back from the 90s. But now that I have , I can fully enjoy that 16bits era of time within a game that is undeniably excellent, benefiting from more-rounded modern design sensibilities... as well as from the crazy talent of the developers at Easy Trigger Games.You (and a friend in COOP) choose a mercenary upon the three available and get offered a campaign in the form of 4 consecutive areas each populated with a unique colorful gang. The backstory is minimalist, and there won’t be more than a few occasional lines of text or short cutscenes to introduce new threats. The end of a level is always crowned by a boss fight against a “bounty”, often a gang leader that marked the level with their footprints.While the story is appropriately barebones (and consequently will not go in the way of replayability), the world, rendered in gorgeous pixel art, is incredible. This is a perfect melting-pot of , , , , , , , and everything that is holy from that glorious era of science-fiction movies depicting an ultra-violent future. The references are everywhere, in the gangs and their style, in the cool one-liners from the main characters or their bounties, in the music, and of course in the dirty neon-infused levels, as the fights will be taken from the subway to the rooftops. Even the fonts are totally on point!Gameplay-wise, instead of trying to emulate the rough edges of old games,  removes multi-directional aiming to focus on horizontal aiming, but masters it. It is possible to dash or to take cover behind crates or within alcoves, allowing players to smoothly choose between frenetic jumping around in order to dodge, or smooth shoutouts from fixed positions behind covers. While these systems are often clunky in many games, in  the controls are very intuitive and there is little friction between what players want to achieve/what they picture in their mind, and what they can actually perform immediately in the middle of a gunfight.Each character has its own gun and an alt attack recharging quickly, so even after picking up a melee weapon there are options to deal with enemies farther ahead. Scattered across the levels are all kinds of weapons, from close-range shotguns that blow people to bits to destructive rocket launchers that blow people to bits; there are often several possibilities so players can pick according to their style or to their knowledge of the levels. I must admit that it is refreshing to play in hand-crafted levels rather than yet another repetitive rogue-lite game or a broken Metroidvania. Combined with tight level design and a huge variety of enemies and boss fights (each new boss encounter is pure bliss), we arrive at the best run and gun game that I have ever experienced since . Don’t get me wrong, this is not a replacement for  and its huge boss fights with spectacular levels at breakneck speed.  is another proposition, less free-form chaos and more toward grounded but tight encounters.Difficulty is a common hot topic concerning action platformers. ’s difficulty seems as well crafted as the rest of this superb game, with a campaign that starts relatively easy but gradually ramps up the challenge (I just hate the jetpack enemies that explode at my feet). Each level provides a fair amount of checkpoints, so you never have to go back too far when you die, although it’s still better if you can anticipate the threats ahead (damn those bikes). There are also secrets (3 briefcases to collect per level), and the extra challenge of completing a level without dying, to earn a medal. If you don’t want to occasionally have a hard time you can start the game on Easy, but if you are looking for a spicier challenge, there are more brutal difficulty modes with fewer health points, giving you little room for error and demanding that you both anticipate the threats and play more technically with the game mechanics. Finally, there is an Arcade mode, in which you get a finite number of lives (you can find a few extra lives in the levels and checkpoints still help) and you are tasked to complete one of the four areas. The levels have been slightly remixed from the campaign, your time is displayed, and skulls and other items are contributing to your score (with a satisfying “ting ting ting!”) as you compete in the leaderboards. If you just rush through the story on Easy, there will be at least 5 hours of play. But if you want to get all medals and play on normal, we arrive in the ballpark of 10-12 hours, and then quickly more as you get into the higher difficulty modes and the Arcade. Since the story elements and cutscenes are kept in check, the game is highly replayable, and you might want to invite a friend to share in on the fun.Once a player is down, there are 20 seconds to revive them by mashing the defibrillator over their fallen body. Otherwise, they simply have to wait until the next checkpoint. Coop is not available online (except through Steam Remote Play), only local. The keys are fully rebindable, and it is even possible to have two players on one keyboard. I just can’t find fault with this game.Oh, yes. The elephant in the room. First, this is an external issue and has nothing to do with judging the game on its own merits. Second, while it seems greedy for successful publishers with a hit on their hands to also take Epic’s money, smaller games and publishers always risk releasing their game in complete indifference on Steam’s overcrowded market, so Epic’s money is a safety net and a welcome financial security. At least, now the game is finally on Steam, and it deserves to become successful. Don’t pass on it, as even Electronic Art’s horrors find a strong audience on Steam despite forcing to install Origin: it would be unfair that the small devs get punished while the nasty companies thrive.

Think Elevator Action Returns (Part 2) meets Blood Dragon meets AD Police & Bubblegum Crisis Animes with a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥' soundtrack. Everything about this game from the 2D Pixel graphics to the music to the art is just amazing.  It's like someone hacked my brain and found my 14 year old self obsessed with William Gibson Sprawl novels of Cyberpunk meshed with Bladerunner.Don't hesitate to buy this game if you're a 2D freakazoid like me.  I could never really get into 3D (I play the games but never cared for it).  This is Phenomenal.

_childDocuments_.review: At first, I had my doubts. I kept getting killed constantly and I was scratching my head why as I've grown up on Contra, Metal Slug, etc so I should have this in the bag.But then I remembered when I played Broforce and did the same thing there- Stop trying to rush through and take a second to see what weapons are available, what's laid out ahead of me and move slower instead of trying to blast my way through. It has a lot of the older games DNA here for sure, but it's a approach is a bit more methodical. The pixel art is awesome and so is the soundtrack. They even have voice actors and they're actually REALLY good!!! Enemy placement and level design is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ top tier. Boss battles have their moves telegraphed like in the nes Mega Man games which is great so you can learn and adapt to their patterns. Everything felt very tight and fair on normal difficulty. And you can turn off screen shake thank God!!! The attention to detail is incredible all around.And one of the best parts is all the fan service to games of the era. And it's not the overdone stuff to death like, "It's dangerous to go alone" lines. I've picked up nods from Duke Nukem, Shao Khan from MKII and 3, and even movies too. It felt fresh to hear this stuff instead of the same old same old, and they were implemented well and not just shoehorned in. My ONLY gripe is the achievements. The ones here are...ok, but I wish it had more progression based ones after clearing levels, killing bosses, number of enemies, complete the game with x, y, z character etc. But not gonna complain about it too much since everything else is just damn near perfect. Hopefully the sequels implement this. They nailed it with this game 100% though. Please make lots of sequels, I will buy. My wallet is ready. My body is ready. Giant enemy crab. Riiiiiiiiidge Racer!!!!!

_childDocuments_.review: In the future, there will hopefully be no end to the flood of pixel art games reminiscent of the console era of the early 90s! But when a game comes along that is as rich in atmosphere and detail as Huntdown, then I can only be happy: The 2D action is rendered in a top-notch 16-bit pixel look. It perfectly matches the arcade-like gameplay and scenario.Huntdown sees itself as a declaration of love to the countless riot movies of the 80's. So you can expect a lot of explosions, noise and pixel blood, empty jokes, evil villains and a stylish synthesizer soundtrack that successfully accompanies the ballerfest. The story offers a loose framework at best, if you want to call it that. You play as one of three bounty hunters who earn their living in a dirty, futuristic metropolis. This means that you have to take on several brutal street gangs in a total of 20 levels, and at the end you always have a crunchy boss opponent to kill. Don't be fooled by the occasional short cutscenes with English voice-overs in between: The story clearly only plays a minor role.There is no online mode like in Streets of Rage 4, but you can play alone or with two friends in local co-op. My brother and I used remote play together and it worked great. You can switch between the three bounty hunters between levels, but the choice is secondary anyway. All three heroes play pretty much the same. The basics are always the same, even if they have slightly different standard weapons. You'll feel right at home if you've ever played Contra, Metal Slug, or its modern descendants like Blazing Chrome: In typical run-and-gun fashion, you can jump, shoot and dodge with a quick dash, which works well, but is nothing special. However, Huntdown also uses a handy cover system that is extremely rare in the genre: Your character can crouch behind crates or hug the wall to avoid getting hit. This doesn't necessarily add depth to the game, but it does slow down the action a bit. It also gives Huntdown a very unique feel.You'll collect many weapons along the way, in addition to the standard pistol. Once you've used them up, just throw them away and grab the next one. It's usually just around the corner. There are several shotguns and machine guns, as well as miniguns, rocket launchers, energy weapons, throwing stars, grenades, katanas, and so on. All in all, a great selection that will keep you entertained until the very end! The hit feedback is also great. You can clean the screen of your enemies, who are nicely animated in pixels: After a gunfight, bullet holes and blood splatters appear on the walls. When a street hustler is hit by a missile, the shrapnel literally flies. It is wonderfully over-the-top and not for children, but it is so satisfying!Unfortunately, the 20 levels are quite short. Many of them can be completed in a good quarter of an hour. I would have liked more scope, though, which is common in the genre. Because the action scores with variety, Huntdown never gets boring: You start your bounty hunt in dirty alleys, subway stations and sewers. Later on you can look forward to bars, garages, casinos, bathhouses, construction sites, factories and much more. There are no vehicle sequences or anything like that. But you'll have to fight in a moving convoy, take cover from helicopter gunfire or even flee from a monster truck. Not only the levels are varied, but also the different street gangs change several times during the game. They often appear unexpectedly and attack you with new weapons and tricks: In the beginning you'll only have to deal with lightly armed guys, but later on you'll have to deal with thugs with remote-controlled rocket launchers, automatic shotguns, hoverboards and exploding jetpacks, so you'll always have a challenge.The highlight, however, are the 20 different bosses. They've been implemented with great attention to detail. Giant mechs, attack helicopters, lightning-fast ninja sisters, mutated hockey players with mini-guns on their backs, or an Elvis impersonator with a flying motorcycle and lance - no two fights are alike. Most boss fights start out relatively easy. This gives you time to learn their attack patterns. However, there is usually a second phase that follows shortly after. This is when the action really picks up, and good reactions are required. Huntdown is surprisingly easy at the beginning on normal difficulty, but it gets much harder later in the game. To avoid frustration, there are relatively fixed checkpoints in every level, even right before every boss fight. If you die, you can try again immediately and don't have to repeat a long part of the level.A pixellated run-and-gun game isn't exactly the most fresh idea, to say the least. But who cares, if the resulting game is so much fun to play? Huntdown doesn't even have the pretense of being more than it is: You get 20 levels of focused, flashy sidescrolling action, great backgrounds, cool weapons, silly lines, massive bosses, and coherent 80s flair, all wrapped up in a really kickass pixelated retro style - no more, no less! Of course, I would have liked more scope, bonus objectives or replay value and for 16.79 Euros some games have already delivered more. But the overall package is still right: If Huntdown had been released for the SNES back in the 90s, I would probably be celebrating it today as a classic of the genre. In 2020 (2021 on Steam due to the EGS exclusive ....), however, it's simply a very good action game for retro fans. And that's enough.

_childDocuments_.review: Just when you think side scroll shooters were lame and belonged in the past, here comes Huntdown many probably confuse with another game. But let that be its only negative as the game really hits everything one could want in a simple side scroller modernized for people like me that didn’t grow up on these types of games. Don’t let this hidden gem pass you by for whatever reason you make up not to try it out.
_childDocuments_.name: HUNTDOWN

_childDocuments_.review: Huntdown is a side-scrolling action platformer with emphasis on cover shooting mechanics. It is set in a dystopian cyberpunk world, where crime is rampant and bounties high. That is all you need to know about the world. Well, you only need to know about the bounties as you take control of one of the three bounty hunters.At the start of the game, you get to choose from one of the three hunters. Each has a different starting loadout, which means a different gun and throwable weapon. A neat little feature is that you can change the hunters midway through a playthrough without losing any progress, letting you figure out your favourite while all hell breaks loose.On top of the characters, you can find various weapons ranging from guitars to heat-seeking missile launchers, which can either be hidden in boxes or secret caches or can be dropped by enemies wielding them. You can always carry your basic weapon as well as one extra you picked up. Found weapons have limited ammo so you cannot just spray willy-nilly even though you can find ammo for each weapon fairly often. These are accompanied by throwable weapons which include Molotov cocktails, grenades or throwing knives. All these things combined create a nice concise package where everyone will find a weapon that just suits their playstyle. is not a run'n'gun game in any shape or form. As already hinted, there are cover mechanics that you will have to use in almost any fight if you want to have a chance of surviving, especially on hard difficulty. You can duck behind boxes and cars or hide in the shadows on a garage, making you invincible to incoming fire but not explosions or melee attacks. Thus, even if you are hiding behind a cover, you are never truly safe.The game is divided into 4 major thematical sections, each divided into smaller levels. Each of the sections is based around one of the gangs occupying the in-game city. Those include brutal hockey fanatics, a biker gang or fashion obsessed crazies. And this is what made me fall in love with the game. You do not really get to know a lot in terms of story about these gangs or about why things are the way they are, yet these individual gangs ooze personality, mainly through the location and character design.Each of the levels is finished with a mini-boss fight against one of the side-bounties. These encounters are simple in terms of mechanics but fun in execution. As an example, one of the fights is against a hockey fanatic who just skates around and when she hits you with her stick, you just go flying around (and yes, you can end up in a goal). Another is against a biker leader, who has a huge javelin on his flying bike and behind him is a lady who keeps shouting how great he is. Simply put, the mini-bosses are a nice little treat after an endless gauntlet of enemies.Each of the gangs has their big bad leader and those are at the end of the final level of each of the sections. These are the big fights you were waiting for and they deliver. As the game progresses, each of the main bounties gets more complicated and challenging to face. Each of the fights has multiple attacks, special gimmicks and even multiple phases to keep you on your toes. If you are not careful, you will be demolished in seconds and have to restart the whole fight over. looks amazing. Even though it is a pixel-art game, there is so much attention to detail, from backdrops setting the scene to individual sprites. I am a huge fan of pixel-art and this game not only managed to satisfy that craving, but it also left a very pleasant aftertaste that I will gladly revisit.Same can be said for the soundtrack and sound design. The music has a cyberpunk feel to it and complements the atmosphere to a great effect. It is almost impossible to imagine  without its simplistic yet memorable soundtrack. Same applies to the sound design, where every single sound is distinct and by the time you are nearing the end, you will be able to safely recognize what kind of enemy is coming at you just based on the sound.It almost pains me to say but there are a few issues that the game suffers from. First, there is the typos and mistakes in the English text which are a minor oversight. When I first saw the main menu, I felt like I am about to play some random game made in 20 minutes during a lunch break.The second issue is that the game sometimes breaks the difficulty curve it created and leads to an unreasonable spike. A few moments ago, you were mowing down an army of gangsters only to get suddenly hit from 4 different directions, exploded, and hit with a baseball bat off the map. That is mainly the issue of enemy placement, which is fortunately not random, so you can create your own strategies, but some parts will feel outright unfair.Overall,  is an amazing title that I cannot recommend enough. If you are a fan of side-scrolling action platformers, this game will be right up your alley. At 16,79 euros, it is a fair price considering there are extra challenges for completionists as well as co-op mode, which adds more bullets and mayhem to the already existing one.

_childDocuments_.review: You feel under the weather? Peaky? Feeble?You're having a bad day, craving for some easy, self indulgent gaming, and remember when videogames were just a joyfull rush of pixel, digitalized music and guns, tons of guns?You lost faith in this terrible, terrible world? The crappy future imagined in the 80s seem more desirable than our actual crappy future? You wish that at least living in violence and chaos would have bring us legions of  punks, flying cars and pink neon bar signs?You need to Plissken-up your life?You want more Dredd on top of your Total Recall?Pal, please, leave this burning real world aside, have a seat, and enjoy a game in the burning world of some action movies future that never happened. Even hopeless futures were better before.

_childDocuments_.review: It's Broforce with dash & cover mechanics instead of mostly-destructable environments, or 1st gen Ninja Gaiden with guns. Or 2D Snake Plissken, for the men and women of culture. This is a neo-80s cyberpunk treat, retro feel without retro clunk. If you're a gamer of mediocre skill like myself, Hard difficulty will almost assuredly grant a death or two per level, but no rage. Boss patterns are intuitive to memorize, and attacks are a treat to perfectly i-frame like it's Soulborne at times. Unexpected deaths from new mechanics like attack dogs and molotovs being unceremoniously introduced inspire appreciation for the details rather than saltiness. It seems like this one was a labor of love; I would gladly have paid more for it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is truly awesome side-scroller with local 2-player coop. It's like modern Contra, for real.Pixel art, music and gameplay are excellent. Every boss is unique and interesting to master. Popular culture references here and there is a cherry on top. In the end you see my playtime which is way higher than the average on Steam. I'm missing a single achievement (to beat each of the levels with a single life), so I guess I enjoyed the game that much.Oh, and the game also runs natively on Linux, which is always a plus for me.TL;DR: superbly made modern Contra that you'll enjoy the most in 2-player coop.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best dystopian future 80’s shoot them ups in old classic style. You as a hired mercenary had to stop these psycho lunatics ruling over your beliefs. Its either you or them, and there will be a lot of bullet chewing time. Amazing art style design filled with many throw back 80’s era nostalgia and memories. Music makes this mayhem even more hectic and powerful, as if that’s not enough you will be surprised with many great level boss fights in the end. Combat feels extremely satisfying and rewarding in higher difficulties. Be prepared for smash hit cause this game will blow your head.  Masterclass/10
_childDocuments_.name: HUNTDOWN

_childDocuments_.review: It is criminal that Huntdown didn’t get more exposure during it’s release. Boasting an stylish, colorful and vibrant pixel art graphics, coherent cyberpunk aesthetic, awesome 80s synthwave with convincing voice-acting all round and gunplay that is varies between action-packed and tactical, Huntdown is a near perfect recreation of the old-school run & gun format that would’ve stood shoulder to shoulder with Megaman, Contra and Gunstar Heroes. Developers Easy Trigger has accomplished something remarkable here. If you love 16-bit Run & Gun, Huntdown is a worthy purchase. Highly recommended. No joke, Easy Trigger put a lot of love in Huntdown and it shows. Every single element in this game is designed to evoke that 80s Sci-Fi action movie experience and they nailed it. From it’s neon  light Robocop/Total Recall atmosphere, the catchy 80s synth-wave soundtrack, the badass playable characters with memorable one-liners and the mad max inspired villains, Huntdown oozes and drips 80s swagger. This, combined with it’s excellent gunplay that includes cover mechanics, dash and melee attacks makes a satisfying combat with great flow, rhythm and progression. The great amount of distinct weapons will vary your play style greatly, from assault rifles, carbines, pistols, shotguns, laser rifles, sniper rifles, grenade launchers, flame throwers to even baseball bats, crowbars and katanas. This game is a lot of fun and it’s a damn shame that it did not get the reception it deserves. If you have the chance, get this game. It’s worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: HUNTDOWN

_childDocuments_.review: -This game is like the combination of old PC sidescroller like Duke Nukem (pre-3d), NES Contra, and arcade Metal Slug with 80s /90s cyberpunk and action movie tropes.-The cheesy humor, plot, and music is top notch. Might look like a shallow nostalgia at a glance but once you played it, they even spiritually nailed the silliness of similar games/story in that era. The guns, the character acting and lines, the costume design, etc.-It's not as fast paced as I thought it would be. But actually that makes it relaxing to play. Easy to get into and the challenge is just right for me without being frustrating. -I like how the enemies and characters are pretty diverse. -I haven't finished the game but I feel like this game will have similar replay value like Streets of Rage 4. Not because of there are many things to do or getting better at the game but because it's somehow just simply tight, fun, and arcadey to replay.

_childDocuments_.review: Short form:- Synthwave soundtrack- Great sound and level design overall- Relatively fast-paced gameplay- Game is 3-5 hours long, but it's just enough to have a blast of an evening.If you fancy yourself some sidescrolling run-and-gun action like Contra or Metal Slug or even old Judge Dredd game (no longer on Steam btw), you are in the right place.10/10. Strong recommendation.Long form review part, so here's your only warning if you pressed "Read more".UPD: Fixed typos and whatnot.Story:Huntdown is a sidescroller shoot 'em up about bounty hunters trying to make a living by killing morally reprehensible gang members and their respective leaders. Clearly you are here for the action. However, you get an achievement by listening to all briefings, so at least for the first run just hear Wolfmother out. After all, she knows her children. All in all, it's an action flick type of story done in order to justify it being there. Glad that the developers respect their audience and aren't beating around the bush.Sound:First of all, gotta commend that there's voice acting present in the game. Even briefing parts are nicely voice acted and I feel like the VA part of the game is very good. Characters aren't shying away from throwing occasional one-liners akin to old-school FPS games. The lines are said with enough consistency to not be annoying, and somehow it's always on point, keeping that entertainment value along with giving characters enough of a distinctive personality, so it's worth replaying the game at least once per every character just to hear their lines, because even in briefings they reply to Wolfmother differently, even if they're essentially agreeing to take her contract. Still, it's a good touch. Over the span of the game you encounter different gangs, and each of them also say lines respective of the gang they belong to, and it's not just grunts saying those lines, even the bosses will occasionally say a one-liner that befits them as leader of their group, and I'm glad that small details like these are included within the game. It's full of these little touch-ups and I am all here for that.The soundtrack is superb. I know that synthwave nowadays is nothing to write home about unless it is done by some exceptional artists, or if it's a Furi/Hotline Miami OST. And yet it has enough impact in itself to perfectly fit within the setting. Makes me think of the montages by the 80's Guy where he edits footage from action classics of the 80-90's and puts synthwave on top of it. That's the kind of feeling this game gives me, and it's perfect for what it is, even if not specifically outstanding. There's a pretty wide array of weaponry in the game, each weapon sounds different and satisfying, as it should. Every weapon has a solid punch to it, not just in sound, but in animation as well. Animation and visual quality:Like I said prior, the game is abundant in details. I probably realized it later than I should have. At least the extent of the detail. I was just looking for stashes, minding my own business, and one of the sections had chain hooks. And when I jumped up to touch them and see what happens, expecting to phase through it like it's a piece of background, chains actually reacted to my presence and dangled. That's when I started paying attention to visual details and cues much more. And there's plenty of things to notice. Movements of hostiles, their jumps, idle postures whenever you're far enough or they don't see you, a character reloading each weapon differently (to name just a few, pay attention to rocket launcher and sawed-off reloads), it's all very dynamic and very reactive, so I encourage you to hunt for these details.Also, few extra details before I finish this section: First, this game has an achievement for making a dog fetch your grenade. Cruel, but funny. Second: gibs. Third: easter eggs to the action movies of the golden era.Gameplay:This section will be shorter because if you played any Contra game, then you already know the drill. You have your shooting button, your jump, your dash that has i-frames on it and acts like slide in Contra Hard Corps. The only difference that sets it apart is that the enemies drop all sorts of weaponry, and it's free for the taking. Sniper rifles, shotguns, sawed-off, assault rifles, SMG, flamethrowers, remote bombs. You even get to carry a portable howitzer on your shoulder at one point. Pretty impressive stuff. All of it serves only one purpose: making your enemies regret being on the other end of your weapon of choice. You have a choice between three different characters: Anna Conda being agile member of the group with fastest firing primary at her disposal, John Sawyer being the "heavy" class and having the most damaging but slowest primary in the game, and Mow Man being the balance between the two. Secondaries, those being whatever you pick up from dead enemies are the same for everyone.The only major difference from your "normal" run 'n gun is that this game has cover system. Approach any obstacle and your character will take cover. Be careful though, covers are destructible. Especially cars.And that's your gameplay loop. Difficulty:The difficulty is very fair. I'm not the one for ridiculous challenges or for extremely hardcore difficulties. With that out of the way, I found the game to strike the perfect balance between being challenging and fair at the same time. Deaths feel fair and I never felt like I'm at developer's wrath and that I should learn the trajectory of every bullet in the game to start enjoying it. No, in this game, regardless of difficulty, you're only as good as your momentary decision making skill is. Each attack and the appearance of every enemy is well telegraphed and I never had a section for which I wasn't prepared, because nothing ever shot me off-screen before I could even see it. The game prepares you for everything with enough timing. While not holding your hand necessarily, it's not beating you to a pulp either. One small complaint I got is that there's no player characters animated avatars in Points Shop. Perhaps something to consider? I'd love to have Mow Man animated profile picture! Wonder if developer is still reading these...Conclusion:Meticulously designed run-and-gun side-scroller with great pacing, great sound design, level design and balanced difficulty. A throwback done absolutely right. I wish I could have a "double recommend" button, or something that would express my satisfaction with the game in a proper manner, but alas. If you've made it this far, thank you. Have a good time of your day, and good hunting. The huntdown is initiated.Reminder: don't kill unarmed people and leave the cats be!

_childDocuments_.review: HUNTDOWN~~~~~~~~~~~Huntdown is a tip of the hat to a beloved genre of 16bit arcade shooters. And not just any arcade shooter, a proper 16bit, side-scroller action full of all features that we old-school arcade-goers love and adore. The game graciously sets up its tone for the chaotic nature of its gameplay and overall story-arc with a brief yet classic intro with one of the most 80s things imaginable; a heavy deep-voiced actor narrating a fantastic plotline.Plot: In the distant 21st-century nations have collapsed from the ruins of war. And from those ruins arose a society run by the mega-corporations. Fueled by greed and profits, these corporations provide jobs and security for those who obey their rules.An alternative path is one of crime and gang affiliations; a constant power struggle bowls for the control of the cities between these mega-corporations and the gangs. When the streets become too much for the citizens they call the authority’s ruthless law enforcers, who will go to any length possible. And when things become bad enough and the authorities are in trouble, the Bounty Hunters are called in; an elite group of mercenaries driven by profits and bloodlust. No matter how ruthless the gangs can be, these Bounty Hunters can go one up.Gameplay: This game is a benchmark of what arcade side-scrollers should be on PCs. The game starts off with a brief intro into the game's backstory; it pretty much sums it up and puts a great flavor into the overall theme and gameplay itself. The basic game is simple and tends to be greatly detailed after the old-school arcade, with its simple movement, jump, and cover machines. Thankfully the game provides much-needed key bind change for single and dual player modes. Although players won’t be able to use the same keys even when they use two different keyboards, which is such a bummer; it’s not the game's fault, it’s just windows. The game has two game modes to choose from: Story mode: Where you go after gangs in order to eliminate them and their bosses and sub-bosses, who count as a bounty. Before each mission and bounty, you are given a summary brief with Intel on each bounty. There are currently four unique gangs present in the game. The game does a great job at putting these different gangs and their bosses into different and sort of unique group according to their theme and outlook. The level progresses each time you collect a bounty by killing bosses. This trend will continue until you reach the final bosses and get to the end game where you beat his final form. Arcade mode: Basically the same as the story mode but here the motivation is very clear and streamlined. Kill as much as you can and get through all the checkpoints to get the game saved. You have a limited amount of lifeline and after you’ve died enough, you will need to pay from your profits in order to get back in the game with another set of lifelines.No clean bounties will be declared in this mode, but you will face the bosses and Level progression will mean leveling up the difficulty as well. Weapons: The game features a handsome quantity of weapons to go through. You will be given a primary weapon and a limited number of throwables, which are surprisingly powerful and balanced out to kill everything with enough shots. But the main fun and value of the game is where you get to use weapons dropped from the enemies; these are powerful, and some even come with a greater fire rate.Ranging from Katanas to Mini-gun-styled canons, they are balanced, powerful, and go great with the hectic gameplay. Bosses and enemy types: As mentioned earlier, there are four unique gangs throughout the city, and each has its own customs, style, and environment to rule. The gangs and bosses are very well detailed, and each can be easily identified. I can say the same for their fight style as well.  The bosses are really cool, with their own unique looks, play style, and abilities. As you progress through the game the bosses become more ruthless, powerful and altogether badass. World design: A fantastic looking, highly-stylized 16-bit aesthetic. The game pays great attention to detail and lighting. The levels are fairly spacious, although in certain areas and boss fights, I would’ve loved to have seen bigger arenas. Music and sound effects: The game features a banger of an intro music. The background music during the gameplay was great as well. The sound effects were bang on for the game's overall theme; from explosions to small arms fire, everything fits in perfectly. Positives: + Fantastic Story-arc + Shared/split screen co-op+ Fast-paced instance gameplay + Awesome music + Deep 80s-style narration and voiceover + Fantastic 16bit game design + Detailed environment + Unique and fun bosses Negatives: - I have no negative things to say about this titleHuntdown is just a perfect example of how great arcade titles can be on the PC side. From its fast-paced arcade action to its Steller authentic style.  This game is just perfect for arcade lovers. 10/10 Key provided by the developer/publisher for review purposes. Any opinions expressed are entirely my own!

_childDocuments_.review: I've spent (as of this writing) 57+ hours on this game. It is an absolute 10/10 for me. Arcade game of the year 1992 is exactly right, and honestly some of us have been looking for this game since 1992. Coop is rock solid, boss fights are fun (tiny quibble here: boss difficulty varies - still a 10/10, don't worry!), and the environments are dope. If you like any kind of dystopian science fiction media by way of Paul Verhoeven you really can't go wrong with Huntdown. Lately I've been listening to audiobooks and just vibing through levels, and it's perfect for that too.
