_childDocuments_.review: Before getting into my lengthy and especially incoherent "review" about Huntdown, let me share a personal story. I was born in 1989, in Eastern-Europe, Hungary. Growing up, I was surrounded and heavily influenced by media from the 80s. Despite I was an 80s kid for only a month and spent my childhood in the 90s, the newly formed TV stations, and VHS distribution companies (and sometimes even rural cinemas) financially struggled to get all the hot new media from the west, so they aired and published movies from the 80s a lot and I mean A LOT. I grew up on movies like Tango & Cash, To Live and Die in L.A., The Running Man, and so on. When the 80s revival happened with Grand Theft Auto: Vice City then with Hotline Miami, I fully dived into it, and as a fan and listener, I was there when the early synthwave records came out in 2010. Having this background, I have a special spot in for games inspired by the 80s DONE GOOD. Because let's be honest, the retro-futuristic aesthetic especially on Steam is over-used, and you have to search for great titles with a magnifying glass. But when I saw the first trailer for Huntdown a year ago, I knew there's something good going on. Although, the trailer looked awesome, to be honest, there wasn't anything special what previous indie titles like Broforce and Mercenary Kings haven't already done. But from the video, I immediately fell love with the game’s art direction; and the gameplay did look great too. I'm more of a beat 'em up guy myself, but I like some shooting too. So I bought the game day one, and after sitting on it for a bit, I played it through two streams on my Twitch channel. And boy, I loved this game. When you innocently start the game, you don't know what to expect, but the intro with the arcade styled menus with that amazing music theme caught me off-guard and gave me a huge smile which lasted through my playthrough. For some reason, I started with arcade mode and it was a good lesson, really. It helped me to develop the necessary basics on my own, and prepared my bottom for the frantic action that awaits me in story mode. You have three different characters to choose from, each coming with its completely different basic weapon sets, and your job is to rush into the three distinctive districts in a crime infected city. You play as a bounty hunter, and you have two easy tasks: to kill everything that moves and to not get killed by the crazy punks who are after your blood. Your basic weapons are always with you, equipped with infinite ammo, and you also have throwing weapons which are also infinite but are on a cooldown. You'll find an incredible amount of various and strong (sometimes OP as hell) weapons and grenades, but most of the time, you'll have to rely on your basic kit, and it's really important to try all three bounty hunters to find who's kit will fit your play style. For me, it was Mow Man, a modified droid, and he was the one I started the story with on normal difficulty. I'm far from 100%-ing the game, but I have the desire to do so, because this game nails everything! Honestly. First of all, the gameplay. The gameplay is slick as hell: you can shoot, you can jump, you can switch weapons, and most importantly: you can DASH. And the dash is AMAZING. With a tiny window of i-frame and with a small but sometimes crucial cooldown, you'll have to abuse dash as much as you can, and every time you do so, it feels amazing. A badly designed dash could've alienated me from the game at the beginning, but it's just so damn rewarding to use, and feel so great, that I immediately fell love with that and I can tell you, there's not much better feeling when you dash BETWEEN TWO BULLETS during a bossfight. The length, the feeling of it, everything hits that sweet spot. And here comes my hot take. The game is clearly inspired by Contra, but for me, the game felt more like Mega Man (to be exact: Mega Man X)! No, I'm not high while I'm writing this. How the stages start, the dash system works, and especially the single-screen boss fights, it's just feel more like a Mega Man game than a Contra. And do you know what is also great in this game? It's not rougelike! Don't get me wrong, I don't have any problem with that type of games, but to this game, I just don't see if it could've worked. One of the key elements why this game works so great, it’s because it nails the difficulty. Again, I only played on normal (yet), and this genre is not my main one, but I never felt unfairness, and whenever I died, the only one to blame was me. The difficulty curve is spot on and from stage to stage it helped me to enhance my abilities, knowledge and necessary skillset to proceed further, and with a trial and error mentality, you can easily nail every obstacle you might meet during a hard part. The pre-deployed /determined enemy layout helps a lot, because for a successful run, it's a key point to memorize the stage and enemy spots, especially on later stages. And those stages... my gosh. SNK may be the true masters of pixel art, but this game is just amazing to look at, I kid you not, every single screen is background material. It's incredibly detailed with every part of a stage being completely unique looking. You'll never see the same shop and neon lights twice, and the bit darker tone of the stages with almost everything being brown, grey and black (well, we're talking about a literal concrete jungle) makes a great chemistry with the bright colours of graffiti and neon lights. And you'll make the stage mostly red anyways, because the game has some sweet gore in it! And the three completely different gang (inspired by the cult movie The Warriors) who took over the city, are amazing. Every gang has multiple types of goons and some of them will make your life hard! Each goon also designed well, they almost look like Streets of Rage enemies, nailing the punk and gang aesthetics. And one part which might look trivial for some, but made the game so memorable to me: the voice acting! My gosh, the voice acting is AMAZING. The dialogues (of course almost entirely made of cheesy 80s inspired one-lines) are really funny and entertaining, and from the nameless goons you mow down in hundreds to the unique bosses, everyone is memorable, and it's mainly because of the amazing voice acting. There's a ton of various dialogues, shouts, every boss fight starts with some great lines. My personal favourite is Teddy Taxman, who during the entirety of the first cycle, when you fights against security cannons, gets interrupted by his boss via a phone call, and it's just so damn funny to hear him talking like there's nothing going on, when you are literally under him on a platform, shooting as much as an entire army. Every spoken line well delivered and memorable, and shout out to all voice talents, who really made this game worth its price! The synthwave music is also amazing! Great tunes all around, and wink-wink, it's also available on vinyl, which I frankly own already. The absolute banger of the OST is New Hunting Grounds, which is an amazingly produced 80s synthwave song, but the almost horrorish and disturbing Restless Nights as well Entering Gangland, the break and funk inspired The No. 1 Suspects, and the song Gathering the Armies featuring an amazing guitar solo is just as amazing to listen to. The game might feel short but in reality, it isn't. What content is in it, is 100% crafted (the stock weapon sounds being the only exception), and there's a huge replay value. Two game modes, various difficulty and objectives to complete, the game does offer a lot. I'd love to see a sequel because for me it's not just a great indie title I really enjoyed. For me, Huntdown is the game of the year in 2021. 10/10. I absolutely loved everything and I can nothing but recommend it, and with its really-really friendly price tag, it's a no brainer to get. So what do you waiting for? The city ain’t gonna’ clean itself!!!

_childDocuments_.review: One of my ultimate fantasies and one of the best games I've ever played. It's the embodiment of what I love about the 80s cyberpunk and retrofuturism greatness, with humor that fits the tone.The gameplay might feel a bit limited, but it's great by design, similar to old school Castlevania games. Plus, the variety of excellent level design and creative bosses greatly makes up for it. Arcade Mode also adds to replay value with new enemy and weapon placement and score attack challenge.The graphics make it feel like a Sega Saturn game, with stunning visuals and exquisite attention to detail and sound design - everything just feels right.The voice acting is great, and there are tons of references to 80s and 90s films, games and anime, which are too many to count. Some of them include The Warriors, Robocop, The Terminator, Running Man, Escape From New York, Blade Runner, Akira, Mad Max, etc. If you love these types of media, you will love this game.The soundtrack is legendary, and the game is worth buying for the music alone. There's a fantastic mixture of great melodic synthwave and rock music, with both head-bobbing tracks and more atmospheric pieces inspired by such fims as The Terminator and Escape From New York; some tracks even feature the sound of the good old Yamaha chip used in Sega Mega Drive. "The Troublemaker" is one of my all-time favorite tracks ever!10/10, will never get tired of this masterpiece. Please let there be a sequel (or at least some DLC with new gangs and such)!

_childDocuments_.review: Recommending with reservations. An arcade-style shooter but one in which your mobility and evasion is severely limited so your best bet in most instances is either hiding behind cover or ambushing enemies quickly before they can retaliate. In that sense it's less like contra or metal slug and more like a rolling thunder, crime city, shinobi, or elevator action returns, although it plays much faster than any of those games. It's kind of hard to draw a comparison because it doesn't have a distinct lineage, and that's what I like about the game. You have to work your way through incredibly dangerous enemies both tactically and efficiently, and moving down waves of bad guys feels good.I find the faux-80s aesthetic to be extraordinarily played out by now but the production values here in terms of graphics and sound are undeniably extremely high quality. I just wish the voice clips weren't so frequent, the repetitiveness gets very grating after a while especially when they're doing tired movie quotes.The difficult point is that I really disliked the boss fights - while most of them are fair, the bosses are extremely spongy and take eons to kill, even on the early stages. Given the limited life you have it means you have to dodge near perfectly for an extremely long time, and my hands would start to hurt after a while. I got extremely frustrated with some of the late fights which were impossibly tedious. With the bosses getting so much emphasis in the game that left me feeling a bit sour. It's possible the boss fights were balanced around co-op play? I never had an issue playing the missions solo though, so it's weird that there was always this extreme difficulty spike.I grabbed this on sale and felt I got fair value, but it wasn't something I felt strongly compelled to replay to 100% the missions or try on higher difficulties. Ultimately though it's a game that despite being retro-styled is distinctly different and I believe that sort of originality deserves to be commended.

_childDocuments_.review: Unlike what the screenshots may suggest, this is not a fast run-and-gun platformer, it's more like a slow technical sidescroller. It plays very similarly to the Shinobi or Rolling-Thunder arcade games. It takes a lot of level learning and memorizing.  It's not a movie game and the casuals will be filtered.The game saves after each level, and the difficulty ramps up generously for a very satisfying overall challenge. 100%ing the game on normal will take some dedication, but it's achievable to most gamers. Though getting all the achievements will be extremely difficult.The game is full of details, secret rooms, and little references to 80s culture.I like that they limited themselves to more or less megadrive graphics quality, which enabled them to create an ample amount of asset graphics with reasonable ressources. It's a good example of scope limiting. The pixel art is somptous although the theme is very banal and it's nothing that you haven't already seen before. And the over-use of pastel purple grades everywhere ruins a lot of the ambiance.I also enjoy the oldschool animations and movement speed, some will find them stiff, but I much prefer that to modern platformers where all characters slide and slash across the screen like hectic chihuahuas.The sound department is very rich with original music and voice actors, but nothing memorable unfortunately.

_childDocuments_.review: Instead of having a long walk in a level, Huntdown divided one area into different smaller areas, giving each one around 5 mins of gameplay includes a mini boss to battle at the end. I suck at horizon scroll arcade games, I find in shorter levels I make fewer mistakes.Huntdown has a good control, a good variety of weapons and enemies, one of the few games keep me hooked and want to keep playing. On easy mode (yea, suit  me in well) I get a good amount of health pills when making a kill, so I can stay calm. The game is generous on giving supplies, yet still challenging. There are suitcases to collect, at least one placed on a higher floor, one you need to quickly take from an escaping target, the last one can be anywhere. For playstyle, you can clean the area or ignore everyone and head all the way to the exit. There are crate to stop bullet but will eventually be destroyed, oil barrels, doors to hide. You can always see health bar on everyone, easy to make the next move.Last thing is game shows 1P and 2P. I haven't tried out co-op, but can imagine the fun play with a friend.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun and intense shooter in the style of Metal Slug and Contra, with a good 80s retro look and feel to it.When I say "80s retro", I don't mean that they just smeared neon lights on everything and noodled on a synth for a couple of tracks.  The game has a beautiful cassette futurist look to everything, right down to the small details.  Instead of just dropping a couple of references, they built wildly entertaining themes around old movies and cliches.  The top-notch voice acting only helps make the game as aesthetically fun as it is exciting to play.

_childDocuments_.review: WOAH DAMN THIS IS SO SICKA sidescrolling shoot em up with modern mechanics, and a high enough skill ceiling that you can do tons of cool stuff once you're good at it.Sprites and animations are fantastic, nothing clashes and everything fits just right. Lots of variations of sprites in each level, and tons of little set pieces so each stage feels unique. Weapons have some varieties you can only find on certain stages so are a treat to use when you find them, and EVERY weapon is fun to use with a good level of "oomph".Controls are tight and snappy, never have I fallen victim to an enemy due to anything other than my lack of skill.Music is suitably boss and goes perfectly with gibbing Many Dudes™, voice acting is camp as hell and... also fits perfectly.Once you reach the halfway point, the game ramps everything up a bit more and becomes really intense, but the difficulty is never unfair in any way.My only gripe really would be some parts go on a bit too long for how little challenge they provide, and the same with some bosses. There's one section in the sewers with a hovering car that is incredibly easy to avoid, but you spend a good 2~ minutes just plugging it with bullets which isn't great and slows the pace down to a crawl. Fortunately, any downtime is quickly forgotten as you're back to exploding idiots with rockets right after.Cannot recommend enough, can't believe how quality this game is for the price, can't believe how consistently good it is throughout. Simply amazing.MUST BUY.Only con - devs are afraid to call out any bigots on the forums. :)

_childDocuments_.review: Dear players,I would like to add my sand grain to the mountain of positive reviews.This game is a small master piece in many ways, but let's start with starters.Huntdown is a platformer beat them all. it offers you the choice between three unique heroes to venture with through the four chapters composed each of  5 stages and so many bosses to fight against.So why is Huntdown such a success ? Because of three main points (to me) :- Its atmosphere- its stages and bosses- its heroesThe above list is to understand as a "horizontal" ranking where all these points are completing the other ones and the whole give you the harmony of the game. Let's develop a bit each of them :Atmosphere : the game is really well made, from the level design to the music, we're making a happy jump in those beloved and famous action movies from the 80th-90th. everything just shout it out loud from the look of the enemies to the punch lines of all actors, we're in for a bullet hell (from your side at least) and a weapon fest. we're breaking cars, causing explosions and all of that in a very well made game. We are the star of a movie and the developers give you that to play ! The music is really well composed and dispatched. it's a bit repetitive, but not unwelcome and never did I lowered the volume !Level and bossesThe level design is really well done, sometime obvious and simple but clean. and the cleanness of the stages is met with the bosses. Oh god, I'm not a good beat them all player, not at all, but here I have to say that i had so much fun fighting every boss of the game. Their pattern is clean and you can beat them if you're good at it, if you take time to watch them moving and shooting around and when you're stuck with a boss, it's rarely on the devs side... And those bosses.... I could name a few of my favorites but Taxman is always one I'm glad to fight. It's a simple one, but his personality, for the few you discover about him is genius. Many bosses are charismatic because they impersonate famous characters from movies, music and video game from the golden 80th-90th. You have some who parody more recent movies and some who just have very good punchlines. it's a pleasure to fight most of them even if they get trickier by the end of the game (yeah, Final Boss, I'm looking at you :-P). All in all the Misconducts are, to me, a blast to play against. Heroes :One basic hand-gun for each and one bladed throwing weapon. And a lot of hilarious punch lines. each hero is a pleasure to play with because as the boss I mentioned earlier, they have their own personality and you discover them through playing and hearing all they have to say about the ♥♥♥♥-hole you're venturing in. The arsenal of weapon proposed to you through the various stages is also interesting as you may choose the weapons and throwing items (grenades, etc.) you take with you to fight the boss and if at the beginning it does little to beat them, by the second chapter you're starting considering which one will be better given the boss play-style. I've left a lot in the mist, but just go buy and play this game whenever the price is good enough for you, you'll  enjoy it and treat yourself to a fun and hilarious trip  to Gangsta' Paradise haha ;-) Have fun everyone !

_childDocuments_.review: While the game's themes are decidedly based on 1980s action films, its technical quality is much more along the lines of a AAA action side-scroller from the mid-90s, with the gameplay of something like Robocop Versus Terminator. And to that end, its gameplay is straightforward, with all complexity lying in the challenge and ability of the player to execute well without taking damage. No RPG mechanics, minimal power creep, just an honest-to-goodness old-fashioned action platformer / shooter. More forgiving than Contra, you have some HP, and levels have checkpoints. But it's still challenging.There's a bit of secret hunting, and optional challenges and 4 difficulty levels to keep you chasing higher expertise, should you enjoy pushing yourself. But really the reason to play this game is the beautiful retro audio/visuals and the turn-off-brain action blasting. Wouldn't mind going through it again in co-op.If you like Genesis-era action/shooter platforming, you'll probably get a kick out of Huntdown.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is one of the funnest games I’ve ever played. The campaign is a blast, and I’ve played it multiple times on multiple platforms. Then Arcade Mode is the icing on the cake, with endless fun and replayability. It is seriously so fun getting combos and collecting scores and bonuses. They really nailed arcade mode.Huntdown is fun solo or couch co-op. I’ve played a lot solo and enjoyed every moment, and I’ve played enough co-op to confirm that it is incredibly fun. It is like the fun I used to have playing Contra in the glory days of the NES, but with all kinds of modern improvements and enhancements.Some of my favorite things in Huntdown are the music, sound effects, satisfying explosions, humor and voices, Arcade Mode, and throwbacks to the over-the-top 1980’s. This game is highly polished and you can tell they had a lot of fun making it. This game is not afraid to just be fun, and I love it.What is my wishlist for the future of Huntdown? An endless arcade mode in Huntdown would be awesome with simplified boss fights. And every 10 or 15 minutes you could enter a little bonus round with a Spy Hunter type driving sequence where you drive to the next area and blow some vehicles up for bonus points by ramming them or firing rockets at them. I’m hoping the developers can put something like this together as DLC. I’d pay as much for that as I did the game itself!As it is I easily rate Huntdown as one of the funnest games I’ve ever played and without hesitation a 10/10.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to start by saying that I had no idea what this game was when I found it. I simply saw it was on sale, read some reviews (which were raving about how great it was) and said "Why not, it's on sale?"What I found is that Huntdown isn't just a video game - it's an experience that perfectly brings back the pure bliss that games used to be when we were kids. This isn't a game that you have to worry about "hopping in the server" or "readying up" or "micro-transactions", or anything like that. This is a game that you invite your buddies over, order a pizza, grab a couple of controllers, have some beers, and have a sleep-over as a grown ass adult (unless you have kids, in which case you can replace your buddies with your kids). It's like being a kid again, but with a beer. It's also plenty fun to play by yourself too (Pizza and beer and all).Gameplay wise - it's something out of the world of PS1 or Dreamcast pixel graphics (complete with CRT mode as well, which I prefer). The enemies are creative, the game itself is pleasingly challenging, and the weapon variety is satisfying as well too. Overall, this is "invest button meme" level of buy it now. It was on sale when I wrote this and, knowing what I know now, I would buy this game at its full price any day of the week. This one made me feel something again.

Extremely punishing and I have no patience anymore.Pros:- cool retro style shooter- pixel art style is visually appealing - sound design, game play has that old school arcade feel - large variety of bosses with interesting mechanics, figuring out how to defeat the bosses is fun (actually fighting them, is a chore because of clunky controls and things listed below)Cons:- visually chaotic when playing - often lose track of characters- in coop, during boss fights, players can go off screen - snipers from like four screens away can shoot you- game seems to go for quantity over quality in terms of level and enemy design - it throws everything and the kitchen sink at you- to revive a friend, you have to button mash - which is fine - however, there is a noticeable delay before your character can move again, given how hectic and fast paced everything else is (and enemy aggression) this just feels bad - when being revived, you can also just die immediately by getting stun locked before you even get control of your character again - explosions will cover your screen, which is cool, except you can't see your character who is likely getting shot, so you will die - the things that can hit you - sometimes don't look like they've hit you, but you will get hit anyway even though it looks like you have dodged it successfully

_childDocuments_.review: Huntdown is among a wave of contemporary, yet retro-stylized games, but sticks out for it managing to keep old school gameplay exciting as a result of it's modern additions, as opposed to those being what hinders it.In Huntdown, you take the role of one of three playable assassins, or hunters, tasked with completing 20 levels, divvied up into 4 rivaling gangs, each level having their own unique boss in the form of a high-ranking gang member. The levels do not overstay their welcome, which may give the impression that the game will let you off easy, but let it be known, Huntdown can get very tough, especially during the bosses. However, the vast array of weaponry, explosives, stage hazards, enemies, and scenery, stops the game from turning into a slog. Without having any hardware limitations of the run n' gun games of old means that there's no stopping the creativity of the developers, and the excitement rarely fails to persist. On the subject of scenery, the presentation in Huntdown is simply fantastic. Before even beginning the game, what probably struck you first into buying it was the sheer talent expressed in the pixel art. The dedication put into the design of this game really shows that a game does not have to be technologically impressive to be visually impressive. The inspirations are clear, many backgrounds resemble something you'd find in a movie like Bladerunner, but these references feel more like homages, rather than something of derivative nature. For that reason, I believe Huntdown captures the spirit of the 80s better than most, but also offers an original, modern spin on the classic cyberpunk look.It's actually the game's references to 80s media that got me interested in Huntdown to begin with, and it's clear that the developers had a lot of love for movies of the time period. I mean, Anna Conda, one of the playable characters, literally just looks like Snake Plissken from Escape from New York, and John Sawyer, another playable character, uses what is basically his gun. (Not to mention that ) Besides visuals, that inspiration extends further into the game's music. While still keeping present day flair, as not to sound archaic, many of the game's tracks emulate the sounds of old school synths, reminiscent of works by John Carpenter. They're simple rhythms, but not unpleasantly so, and they compliment the gameplay as they should. However, on the audio side is where I find faults in the game. As mentioned previously, Huntdown gets tough at times, and when fighting the bosses, you're likely to die a lot. And while each boss having a unique personality is, on paper, a good thing, they repeat a small list of voice lines quickly that, if repeated enough, can get really annoying. Sure, they're amusing the first couple of times, but for a few bosses, it just brought down the whole experience. And, as far as I can tell, there's no way to turn down the volume of the voice lines specifically. I do appreciate the work of the voice actors and actresses, but I just wish it was used more sparingly.And that brings me on to my main negative point, and it's a big one. Something you can't fix with a patch. Huntdown is a great game, but I think it really would've been made better by a more serious tone. I think as it is, the comedy can go a little overboard, especially when it's not the funniest stuff in the world, frankly. I think it is my fault for forming a preconceived perception of the game's tone based off of it's clear inspirations. When I see a game that reminds me of Bladerunner and Escape from New York, I make the assumption that it's going to have a similar, mostly serious tone like those films, but I can't deny that the game's setting and brief, but existent storyline intrigues me, and I do believe there were opportunities to build upon it.Regardless of how I am a little disappointed by the game's tone, it's really not a deal breaker, because I still managed to have a lot of fun with this game. If you're a big fan of 2D side scrolling run n' guns, and are looking for a contemporary spin on the genre, or even are just looking for an action packed game with simple mechanics that was actually made within the past 5 years, look no further than Huntdown. I don't remember how much I bought it for but it does go on sale for relatively cheap, but this one is really worth checking out, so buying it at full price isn't a bad idea. Check out Huntdown if you think it's for you, but most importantly, have fun!

_childDocuments_.review: An incredible game. Ripped right out of 1994. Could have come out on the tail end of the Megadrive or could be mistaken for an early Saturn release. This is quintessentially 90s, from the post-apocalyptic, neo-noir setting, over-the-top stage bosses, incredible synth soundtrack that retains that western "twang" of later Megadrive releases. Everything about this game is crisp, from the visuals, to the controls, the voice acting and the incredible art. This has been genuinely one of the best games I have ever played. It is punishingly hard as an old school side scrolling shooter should be, particularly on the Badass difficulty, but it is so rewarding. God I hope there's a sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: This Game is a blast, pure 80s action cheese.For difficulty, I am an experienced action platform player and I found normal mode to be to easy for me, so I switched to hard mode with I felt was a nice sweet spot for an experienced player. Basically 2 hits you're dead which is fine, and being forced to play to the mechanics without being overly punishing for a single mistake. You have unlimited lives and continues, and there are plenty of checkpoints.I wish there was more variation between characters, such as one character being faster, or able to jump higher, or maybe being able to hack a panel or something, this would add to the replay value where some characters can reach certain secrets and some can not. Right now the only difference between characters is their primary weapon and their projectile, which does add some spice, but not enough in my opinion.There isn't much though in terms of unlockables, there really isn't any reason to get all the collectibles or try to beat it on harder settings aside from just enjoying the challenge.An extra character or two, bonus stages, more story, or really anything of note would go a long way to make the challenge truly worth it.Overall though the game is a blast to play, controls feel good, and is definitely worth a weekend play through, either by yourself or with co-op. Pick the difficulty you are comfortable with, run through the game, have a great retro time.

_childDocuments_.review: I played the entire campaign in coop. Absolutely gorgeous art and music. The problem is the gameplay. The trailers make the game look way more fast paced than it really is, and my impression from the trailers was cyberpunk Contra, or Katana Zero with guns. That's not the case at all since it plays like a cover shooter. You walk up to a car or doorframe, hide behind, wait for enemies to stop firing, and then fire back. Repeat.The levels are short and easy, and don't offer any significant challenge or interesting platforming, which makes me question their purpose. They felt like filler in between bosses. The bosses were clearly the central focus and the highlight, but they significantly vary in quality and difficulty. Some bosses felt cheap and gimmicky, some had too much health, and the rest were boring and easy.In the credits, I noticed there was only one programmer but several artists, and that's really telling. I did enjoy my time with it because I was playing coop and everything is more fun in coop, but I wouldn't have finished the game if I played solo.

_childDocuments_.review: By all accounts this is a great game, it has beautiful pixel art graphics, it’s fast and frantic, incredibly violent, full of references of science fiction films from the 80’s, it carries the spirit of Robocop in its veins, and it presents a game that showcases the mood of that film beautifully.But it’s also a terribly difficult game, I bought it knowing that it had an easy mode, and I was hoping I would be able to play through it without feeling like I was spending way too much time with it, dying time and time again, it ended up turning into a horribly frustrating experience about halfway through.I don’t like difficult games anymore, and I think if developers implement an option to make the game easier then that option should work as such, otherwise you’re left with a game that arbitrarily has three difficulty options but that it might as well have none because of how freakishly difficult it ends up being in all of them.I ended up regretting my purchase because of this, because independently of how good everything else about the game is, and how much I love it, I simply can’t play it because of how difficult it is.I can’t even ask for a refund because I got past the 2hr mark, given that the game truly doesn’t become increasingly challenging until about the midway point.

_childDocuments_.review: You know those moments in gaming when you're craving a quick adventure, not a marathon quest? _childDocuments_.review: This game is so good, I bought it twice! First on Steam and then on Switch aswell. If you like the street-gang movies of the 70's and 80's in which society is somewhat overwhelmed by massive, merciless, criminal activity such as  or even , just to name a more modern example, taking place in a  setting then you'll love this game.If you like well-thought-out game design with tight, intuitive controls, easy to learn but hard to master level design, , superb voice acting and amazing, neo-retro pixel graphics then you'll love this game.Huntdown is in my personal top 3 games of all time! It's one of the games I'll always have installed even when I'm not playing it for a while. An absolute must-have. One of the best purchases I've ever made on Steam, regardless of the thousands of hours I've spent with other games. GET. THIS. GAME. ♥I don't need to tell you that Huntdown runs as smooth as it gets. You can probably tell just by looking at the screenshots. Your PC or whatever you use has to be from the stone age to not run this game. :pI haven't encountered any bugs or crashes in 63 hours of gameplay on 2 different gaming laptops, so there's nothing else I can add here!Ugh... it's beautiful! Animations as smooth, explosions are bombastic, the backgrounds are extremely detailed and somewhat immersive, considering it's a 2D game. Lots of little references and easter eggs can be found in just the scenerey alone!But let's just get to the point: the soundtrack. This game has one of the best soundtracks I've heard in the nearly 200 games I've played on Steam. It easily gets into my personal top 5 alongside games like Streets of Rage 4 and Orcs Must Die! 3. Every time I play the game again, no matter how many times I've already played it and how much time has passed, I'm always immediately pumped up by this banger OST the very second I start the first stage. It's not just neo-retro 80's music like you'd expect from many games, alot of the tracks and little bits and pieces of music sound like they're straight out of a  movie! F*ck they even got an actual, non-cover  song in it! 0.0And if that's not already enough, the voice acting in this game is supreme! I don't know why they decided to put this much effort into VA for a 2D shoot'em up that doesn't really require any voice acting at all in order to be good, but it brings the quality to a whole new level. From all the little one-liners that your characters make, to the screams and insults enemies throw at you all the way down to the dialogue you get from boss fights, everything is extremely professional and of outstanding quality. Heck, triple A titles rarely sound this good! Bigger studios can learn alot from Huntdown when it comes to the VA.Have you played The Messenger? Do you agree that the controls of that game are extremely tight, responsive and intuitive? It's the exact same with Huntdown. Once you get the hang of it you start blazing through stages like you're a god of destruction. It's a cover shooter so you'll often have to take cover behind cars, boxes, different elevations and even inside doorways and other niches and alcoves.The weapon variety is pretty good and fun to play around with. From your standard pistols and rifles to a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ PORTABLE HOWITZER CANNON, all the way down to a CYBER KATANA... every weapon is fun to use and there are plenty of them to discover!Speaking of discovering things... Huntdown is packed with easter eggs and secrets to find. And you'll actually spend alot of time searching for them, unless your a little pus... I mean bit... I mean true gamer by looking it all up. :p Whatever you prefer, it's always worth it. Some secret locations will reward you with bonus weapons that are often overpowered and will let you blow stuff to kingdom come, others are direct 1:1 references to popular movies, some of which I've already mentioned in the "TL;DR" portion of this review. It's fun and satisfying to find all secrets & easter eggs, so go for it!In all seriousness though... are there alot of neo-retro games these days? Sure. Do they all manage to make you feel like you're 10 again and sitting infront of your SNES or Mega Drive / Genesis from 30 years ago? Nope! Huntdown is a blast and it will leave a lasting impression on you if you have a similar taste than mine when it comes to movies, music & games. Get it, and don't forget to pick up the soundtrack aswell, because Easy Trigger Games deserve your support for making this absolute banger of a game! ♥

_childDocuments_.review: An enjoyable arcade throwback!Gameplay is fun with a fair amount of weapon variety, although it's perhaps a bit lacking in enemy variety at times. Movement is solid with fun little slides & quick snappy dashes that make evading even the most terrifying barrages of enemy fire possible, along with a smart cover system that never acts in a way you'd not want it to. This arsenal & movement combined with a good set of supplementary items such as Remote Mines, Grenades, Cluster Bombs, & Sentry Turrets, make for a game that's enjoyable on your first playthrough & beyond.The highlight of the gameplay has to be the bosses, however. A suitable jump up in difficulty that doesn't feel unfair but always feels rewarding when you figure out their little tricks & patterns & manage to down them for the first time. Higher difficulties (one of which is unlocked after beating the game) & the arcade mode should keep more challenge-oriented players occupied for a while! All that said, there was something about the gameplay that I can't quite put my finger on that keeps it apart from the absolute best of the best for me. It's not that the gameplay is poor by any means (as it's very good), it just doesn't do anything to a level I've not already seen in other releases - I enjoyed it, but it didn't "WOW!" me.Presentation is absolutely on point with some of the best layered pixel art I've ever seen in an arcade themed indie release. There's so much depth & quality to each scene that I found myself standing still amongst the wreckage I'd wrought just to appreciate it on several occasions. The accompanying soundtrack & sound effects compliment the OTT arcade absurdity perfectly, & the story, while intentionally short, adds its own bit of charm into the mix.Overall, Huntdown does a hell of a lot right without doing much of anything wrong. The brilliant visuals, banging OST, cheesy one-liners & sufficiently wonky voice acting make for an experience that feels both familiar & fresh, & while the gameplay didn't quite hit the heights of the best of the best indie titles I've played, it's still a damn good way to spend 5+ hours for a maiden playthrough. Oh, and huge kudos to the developers for actively promoting Remote Play for Huntdown - It's the perfect game for it!

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: I've played for multiple hours across different devices and platforms and I'm still fighting through the campaign. Huntdown is raw, unadulterated joy for the early 90's kids who grew up playing side scrollers. For everyone else, it's a chance to witness artistic and creative greatness that is far too uncommon. While Huntdown is ridiculously good and known to be super challenging, not mentioning the other highly polished aspects of the game is a massive disservice to what's been accomplished here and offered to the gaming public for often a very reasonable price.Huntdown reminds me of a time long ago where games were difficult to add longevity, and Huntdown is certainly a reflection of that time. While the game appears and feels "retro" at first, you'll discover that it's in fact closer to a what many gamers my generation wish our favorite games of yesteryear continued to be today, rather than raw reminder of their era, all to the joyous benefit of anyone playing Huntdown today with an appreciation for what has come before.First and foremost of note is the audio - once you hear it you'll understand. Even the title screen is delight in high-fidelity stereo. If you appreciate rock solid voice acting delivering classic action one-liners, mixed in with super clean and polished weapons popping off, shells hitting the concrete, wooden crates falling down in a pile, the thunderous fiery explosions of a barrel followed by the splash of gore against the wall, you'll recognize you're hearing best-in-genre audio. Huntdown is a treat for your ears as much as your fulfilled masochistic desire for challenge. It's not uncommon for me to hear a line delivered or effect that provides genuine surprise, delight, and disbelief at how high a level this has all been executed.If the goal of Huntdown's release was to show the world that 2D side scrolling still has untapped potential and deserves your attention, it succeeds wildly. If there is a god, and Huntdown 2 becomes reality someday it could take a leap into rogue-like in story mode without sacrificing the things that have served as the foundation of Huntdown's unabashed callbacks to a simpler time, including it's excellent Arcade mode. If you loved 2D side-scrollers growing up and are itching a return to that time, buy it now. If you're wanting a fun pick up and play action title that can be played co-op occasionally, wait for a sale. But either way, you won't be disappointed if you have an eye for the passion applied here by the developers.

_childDocuments_.review: THe HUNTDOWN is so much fun to play either solo or with a friend. There is plenty of weaponry, levels, types of standard enemies, unique bosses, and laughs. Also, you can play as three different characters with different starting weapons and different starting equipment. You can change your character at any time, but you will have to restart the level you are currently on (not a big deal). I initially was trying to beat every level by eliminating all enemies, not dying, and finding all of the secret stashes (completing all 3 simultaneously is a challenge as you progress). As I got closer to the end of the game and completed these challenges up until that point, I lost my progress. I'm not sure how, but I think my son might have accidentally deleted my progress. As a result, I ended up just speed running the game from the beginning. This is a game I intended to play on my steam deck (when I get it) and still will do so. After you beat the game, you unlock the badass difficulty (I have not attempted). I can see myself going back to play the game on hard and possibly badass.I have barely touched the arcade mode, but the game does recommend you finish the story before attempting arcade mode. Based on the 10 minutes I played of arcade, I can see myself repeatedly going back to play it. The game is great to play if you only have 15 or 30 minutes or hours to play. It is highly addictive. If you enjoy retro, side scrolling shooters, you should love this game. I can't think of anything I didn't like in this game.Please give us HUNTDOWN 2!

_childDocuments_.review: It looks cool, it sounds cool, the puns are terrible, so it should have been good. Not sure exactly what, but the levels with the controls you are given are just super awkward. I acknowledge I'm getting older and probably not as quick as I once was, but I haven't struggled this much with anything else, and I've played some much faster paced games. During the levels I keep finding myself stuck out in the open with no cover whatsoever and not much choice but to just take hits. There's "difficult", and then there's awkward design, and that's what this is. It's very odd. I expected the bosses to be even worse but no, they were just fine. The controls and level design seemed to match them just fine and made for a really fun boss fight. But the levels? Man. They were just getting progressively worse. The little miniboss fights with the hoodlums in the van were the worst offenders. It just goes:1) duck behind cover from shotgun blast2) return fire3) duck behind cover from one stray bullet4) return fire5) repeatJust....bleck. The levels on their own are fine, the enemies on their own are fine, and the controls themselves are fine on their own too, but put them all together and it just doesn't work for me on this one. Like I said, it's really strange. Also it seemed like it would be incredibly short, as well as repetitive. I played as Mow Man and cleared out the first gang/set of levels and went 1 level deep into the next world/gang. It was already getting a bit repetitive because nothing was really changing. It'd be alright just for a couple bucks, but even at the sale price of $6.79 I didn't feel like it was worth it. Definitely not a full price purchase of $20. Usually when I critique a game I like to talk about "how it could be better" but honestly this one kind of has me stumped. The only thing I can really get from the top of my head is some skills you unlock as you progress so the game play would change a little bit as you go, as well as more levels to allow more of that growth as well of more game to play. Some upgrades such as more health, improved base damage, or skills such as dropping down a temp piece of cover, some kind of better dodge. You get the idea. I don't think the game needs much, but it definitely needs something. It's so close to good it's aggravating.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent looking game (seriously, one of the best looking indies out there) with great, Genesis-feel soundtrack to support it, with mostly fun bosses, that is held down by incredibly shallow gameplay, braindead level design and extreme lack of variety.I don't know why this game gets compared to Contra, when only thing in common are guns and nothing else - controls are stiff and "heavy", which is on purpose just like ability to only shoot straight and every single thing makes it NOT Contra, it's everything but. More like maybe Elevator Action 2 or Bionic Commando minus the arm. My guess is reviewers calling it like Contra are the same people calling shoe lacing like Dark Souls. Unless maybe they mean like PSX Contra games, but less about those the better.Blazing Chrome is still the king of Contra games and as much of unofficial sequel as you can get.5 hours to finish on hard is not that bad for a game like this, but I have to say it felt boring and tiresome by the time I got half-way through chapter 3 (and only there game tries to do something to not bore you to death with some basic platforming).I wish there was mixed rating, but as it is, I sadly have to say no to this game, which is incredible shame, because it's almost good. It lacks the spice that original 3 Contra games had and Blazing Chrome tried to capture. It's "ok" for what it is, I guess and if you have nothing to play, I can say you can try it out, but there are better options. It's like 6/10, you can check it out, nothing really wrong, but nothing really good in gameplay dep. Just don't expect miracles and you could have fun.At the end of the day, best description I can give it is nice package, but nothing special inside it.Pros:+ great graphics+ solid music+ awesome sound design+ funny writing accompanied by great voice acting+ most of the bosses are funCons:- incredibly linear and monotone stage design, where you most of the time go from left to right with no variety at all (again, nothing to do with Contra, which had fake 3D stages, top down stages, 2D stages and go to the top stages with some of them having at least some gimmick, unlike here and don't get me started on Contra 3, which also had motorcycle level)- shallow gameplay with barely any depth at all- side objectives are the same for every level- for the most part difficulty is well balanced, but there are some awful difficulty spikes

NEEDS a dedicated weapon swap button (at least an optional bind)honestly the only one of those that I really give a ♥♥♥♥ about is the weapon swapping.  there should be a dedicated weapon swap button so I can switch quickly without accidentally picking up stuff.  if the devs patched this in it'd be 11/10 game.  despite this flaw, I can only give this game the highest recommendations for anyone who's a fan of run and guns and 80's-90's retro aesthetic loaded with fun and heartfelt references that pay homage to the genres it's inspired by.

_childDocuments_.review: Great retro, side scrolling action. Good graphics, perfectly suiting those of the era - along with solid and purposeful sound effects. Having grown up on the coin-op machines that this game clearly pays homage to, a lot of the references makes sense and are perfectly in vibe of what it is trying to achieve. If I were to have a small gripe, it would be the clearance of the character's jump arc, compared to the height of the enemies - especially in boss fights. Literally a pixel of your foot hits them and that's a chunk of your health gone right there.I enjoyed the boss fights so far, but you do end up on a precision-repeat course where at times having to replay them is a grind - not a challenge. More than once I've come off the game having lost a boss fight for the third or fourth time in a row - not in frustration, but just through the thought of having to do all that whittling down of their health again. Aside from that, it's nigh-on perfect and I would definitely purchase a sequel if one was ever released.

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the most detailed pixel art in pixel art games. It's so detailed and filled from front to back. Really neat in style. Good soundtrack blasting on top of that while getting city rid of all of the gang members and leaders.Gameplay and controls themselves aren't nothing impressive and pretty usual, but get the work done well enough. Moving, shooting, throwables and dodge/slide are basically what one has going on in Huntdown. There is wide arrange of weaponry to find and use, some are hidden very well in secrets and usually these include some reference/easter egg towards something else like Blade Runner scene.As well as weapons come in wide variety either melee or ranged, so does enemies and what they do. Some might run you over with motorcycles, while other run away with collectible cases behind other enemies. Then there's the boss at the end of each level. Totaling five levels per area and four areas which is total of 20 bosses. From which the Grandmaster Yuudai was bit of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ boss and needed pretty good positioning. Areas and enemies go hand in hand so first Punkrockers, then Ice Hockey Team, Greasers and lastly Ninjas/Samurais. These can be tackled with selected mercenary/bounty hunter that can be changed at any levels start to another, all of them have bit different base gun and throwable item which can be changed to the ones found from ground. Either making flames going higher or showing some slap tricks with hockey sticks.Overall good 5 hours of side scroll shooting, boss fighting and collectible looting.

_childDocuments_.review: A little Contra, a little Rolling Thunder, a little Elevator Action, a little Door Kickers: Action Squad. My sidescroller blaster ship rolled in. :)Great, gory fun with imho - Normal Difficulty at least - very reasonably placed checkpoint saves, challenging but fair bosses that won't make you tear your hair out too much, and you start every boss battle with full health. I recommend the game to the Easily Frustrated :) who want something challenging but not soul-sucking. :) Also, if you like to enjoy some adrenalized action fun for modest periods of time and then return to it later (at worst, you can return to that latest set of levels you reached, and very little backtracking is ever required).Tight controls on controller. Enough that clumsy me actually feels fairly graceful when the game requires dodging and evasion.If you're on the fence, look me up on weekends to try it in Steam remote play with me. :)Great weapons variety, everything satisfying to use whether ranged or melee. Each character has a unique special attack and some differences in base ranged weaponry.Memorable, challenging but not Brain Busting boss battles. Given that you start every boss battle at full health, and can replay it as many times as you're willing, it's not like these roguelikes that make you replay 30-40 minutes just to return to the boss battle. :)Lovingly hand-animated, cool pixel graphics, including visceral explosions and geysers of gore. I believe it has an optional CRT visual filter if you really want Full Retro. :) Playful music, great sound. The game supports online co-op through Steam remote play, and local co-op, and offers four difficulty modes.If I had a minor gripe, I've shared on forums that it would've been nice if each character had a unique movement ability (it's dash for each) to differentiate them more. And maybe some access to character-unique weapons. Most other weapons in levels drop from enemies, but it could be neat to sprinkle some weapons unique and only available to a particular character to use. For replayability's sake and to provide a bit more unique experience for each character.Great fun, and especially worth your time if you enjoy side scroller blasters and/or have nostalgia for old school (but with top notich modern production values), arcade side action shooter games. :)

_childDocuments_.review: Score: 9/10Nostalgic mechanics and art are combined with deeper nostalgia for a masterfully fleshed out 80s cyberpunk action thriller. While maintaining the obsolete run and gun methods hurts in some aspects, Huntdown accepts these as necessary and consistently builds levels and enemies around the limitations and framework it sets up. Barring a few minor hiccups, slight modernizations of these quirks makes for a surprisingly smooth combat system that, to the keen player (not me), can be utilized to avoid all damage with relative ease. Tight packaging of individual setting themes, combined with simplistic, unique bosses, with a very comforting spread of character, makes for a pristine sense of environment, even if the story, if there is one, is lacking. Art is very pleasantly cohesive and nearly top tier in quality, with highlight moments worthy of screenshotting. While the ending is visually spectacular, some odd difficulty spikes boss to boss can be a minor impediment, and the voice acting ranges from mediocre to terrible, though it's up to the player whether this befits the retro theme more than the alternative. Huntdown is pretty good, man.

Some platforming in the later chapters can be a bit clunky and are exacerbated by the 2 specific types of air dashes the characters have. Aside from the few set pieces and bosses, there's tons of style, fun, humour, and callbacks to Huntdown's inspirations. It's fun in solo mode, but I've yet to play co-op.

_childDocuments_.review: Huntdown is a very good side scroller shoot’em up and a very excellent love letter to the '80s and its cyberpunk dystopian cinema, so what is the story. In the not too distant future of the 21st century after World War 3 entire nations have collapsed and the world outside is ruled by mutants, but profiteering megacorporations have created a city for people seeking refuge from the chaos, but only if they abide by their policies and work.But for those who refuse there is another path, a criminal path. Gangs of all kinds have risen up committing assault, robbery and murder and regular law enforcement cannot stop them or are on their payroll. But there is a small group of people who have no allegiance to corporation or gangs, their only true allegiance is to the highest bidder, these people are called bounty hunters and they only live for one thing to hunt them down.Alright the likes, the gameplay is very good and for the most part it's hard but fair, it does have some bunk in it but I'll get to that in the dislikes. Anyway the gameplay has a sort of Contra kind of feel to it as you run around picking up weapons while killing bad guys and trying to survive the various environments and at the end of a stage fight a powerful boss nothing too complicated, while still very enjoyable. The weapons are all very good, you have your standard pistol to the shotgun, but we get more fantastical devastating weapons and they are some weapons that are more useful than others, it’s up to you to pick which ones to use and how to use them.The story is very good it's simple basically you're a bounty hunter and you have to kill the bad guys and collect their bounties, but it does a few things differently especially at the ending where it has the perfect setup for a sequel, It's also absolutely chalked full of references to the '80s action and dystopian future cinemas from Blade Runner to Robocop and Running Man, it was quite a joy to see.The pixel Graphics are really good very colorful with many great designs from characters, the city, the weapons, even to enemies and bosses, it’s a joy to behold with all the scenery and colors capturing the look of classic side scrollers, but with modern touches.The levels are really good very diverse with great little touches here and there that just makes each level and the city itself just stand out and being quite visually distinct and not wearing out, like they're also items that are specific to those areas like the subway station we see subway cars running about and we hear a woman on the loudspeaker talking about the various rules of the subway station, then junkyard there are burning pipes and destroyed vehicles, then to the rich upscale neighborhood with shops and museums, it's these little touches and attention to detail that make the whole game’s levels feel alive.The enemy and bosses are really good each one has their own unique looks, I especially like the fact that the standard enemies each has a specific look tying them to their gang, like the hoodlum dolls red jackets and more fashionable appearance to the final level’s gang The Number One Suspects and their Asian inspired attire and a lot of the common enemies have references to them like referencing greaser culture or Kung Fu black exploitation cinema.The bosses are spectacular each one has their own unique looks and attacks that really keeps you on your toes, also a lot of them are also references to different things, like one that's inspired by greaser culture, another boss at wouldn't be out of place in the warriors movie, we even have one boss that is a reference to RoboCop.The music is very good each track is a joy to listen to that fits with the game’s aesthetic very well. The game also has voice acting and the voice acting is really good, especially for the bosses each one despite having a few lines does a really good job.Alright the dislikes, I did say the gameplay is for the most part it's hard but fair, but it does have some bunk in it, like Suki the sniper’s level as it feels pretty unfair not only are you dealing with jetpack people you're also dealing with guys with homing missile bazookas.Some of the boss fight stages can also feel very unfair and pretty chaotic like Sunny Rooster’s when he’s in his second form as you're not only dodging him, but also lava and Grandmaster Yuudai as when you drain his health to specific point Chinese dragons with bombs start flying around the screen, that feels particularly unfair because not only are you dodging his shotgun blasts, but you also have to worry about those Chinese dragons.Alright with that done Huntdown is a very good side scroller shoot’em up and a very excellent love letter to the '80s and its cyberpunk dystopian cinema, it has very good gameplay, a very good story and really good enemy and bosses, so I definitely recommend this game if you're a fan of side scroller shoot’em ups or you love 80’s cyberpunk dystopian Cinema then I highly recommend getting this game and I really do hope this game gets a sequel someday.

_childDocuments_.review: Some games emulate nostalgia moments and try to re-capture that "magic" from the past but often just feel like "modern" copies of better games you've already played. But then some games take everything that made old games good and vastly improve on the formula, edging out even the classics. Amid Evil is one of these games. And Huntdown as well. This is arcade perfection with great level and boss design. It's properly challenging but never unfair. Four difficulty levels also help serve your individual need for a challenge. It's very stylish with great pixel-art graphics and a banger synth-wave soundtrack. With three characters with their own perks and tons and tons of weapons to choose from to wreak havoc among your enemies there is also a great sense of variety. Optional collectibles, a (local) 2-player-coop mode and hidden secrets also add to the replay factor after finishing the ~5 hours long campaign. Unfortunately the game has some weird performance issues on the Steam Deck, so that I switched back to playing it on PC.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent pixel art platform action game! Love the retro vibes and references to 80's action movies. The weapons feel punchy and the platforming is tight. The game is split into zones (think themes) with multiple areas per zone, each with an end level boss. Each level also has 3 sub-objectives besides getting to the end and defeating the end level boss. Defeating the boss is the only requirement to progress. The 3 sub-objectives are kill all enemies on the level, find all secret stashes and complete the level without dying. The sub-objectives are where the replay value lies together with increasing difficulty. There are also a few secrets/references to 80's movies hidden in some levels e.g., getting Snake Plissken's gun (Kurt Russel from Escape from New York). The game is fun and challenging and is highly recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: When I was a kid back in the 80's, I remember I used to ride around on my bike and daydream about my perfect game. Games were pretty primitive back then and nothing at that time was technically capable of pulling off anything close to it. It seemed little more than a figment of my imagination, but I had a vivid picture in my mind of that game and how awesome and fun it would be. I assumed it would forever be a fantasy, and as time went on it got relegated to the back of my mind.Well, fast forward about 30 years or so and here I am actually playing something that comes very, VERY close to it!! My dream game (!!) it's almost like they read my mind from back then, with everything from the futuristic theme, the backgrounds with flying cars and subway trains, the strategic hiding behind cars and crates to avoid enemy fire, the enemies bodies that stay laying there dead after you killed them, the movie-style quips, the arcade-style bonuses like 'double kill!' etc etc...The point of me telling you this story is just to highlight how utterly awesome this game is! It's pretty much the perfect arcade-style run and gun game, just like I imagined! If you are a fan of the genre this is a MUST-buy, everything from the graphics, sound and playability is absolutely top-notch. It's the kind of game that I could finish, and then play all over again just to take in all of its awesomeness.Can't recommend this enough. If you are a fan of arcade-style action games, you will not be disappointed. 10/10!!!

_childDocuments_.review: For the folks raised in the 80's and miss the classic 8-bit or even 16-bit side scrolling shooter, here's your chance to relive your childhood. The combat is fast pace, guns feel like they pack a punch and aren't just pea shooters. The one-liners your character pumps out from time to time, straight out of a 80's/90's action flick. The game has great controller support, and would recommend using a controller, keyboard isn't as enjoyable. Bought this game on sale, so for the price it was well worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: HUNTDOWN

_childDocuments_.review: If you like the side scroll shoot them all then you will like this game. The music is really good and immersive while the gameplay is basically a modern version of Rolling Thunder with a polished mechanic for 2021It's a nice game to play single player, best with a steam deck, or multiplayer with a friend with the ability to invite people in your lobby

_childDocuments_.review: The game play is side scrolling shootemup with a simple cover system that can be used, but many times it can simply be skipped to run and gun.  It gives me Contra vibes, but with more current quality of life improvements.  I'm only just scratching the surface of this game so I'll do my best to update the review as I progress if something jarring comes along.Helpful things that I've figured out playing just a bit more.  After you pickup a weapon with limited ammo, you can switch back to your pistol to save the ammo by pressing "B" on an xbox layout.Update 11/24/21.  Final boss is tricky.

_childDocuments_.review: Almost perfect balance, the game requires a lot of skill and concentration, and it gives you the right tools to beat it, you cannot run and gun mindlessly nor mash shoot to win at all. Music and voice acting are marvelous, pixel art is retro and appealing, characters are cool and interestingI think the game would benefit from a Boss Rush or somewhat of a challenge mode or endless modeAnd I personally would like to disable lifebars and button prompts. I feel there are not enough unlockables nor achievement
_childDocuments_.name: HUNTDOWN

_childDocuments_.review: Great shooter platform like Sega genesis's E-swat and Blizzard's Blackthorne.You cover and shoot through a dystopian cyberpunk society with a lot of 80's nostalgia and one liners.Every level culminates with a boss fight.Probabbly the best pixel graphics I ever seen.Totally recommend if you are a 80's child or if you just loved those games I've mention it.
_childDocuments_.name: HUNTDOWN

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:+ Superb pixel art / cyberpunk aesthetics+ Ultra-cool 80s synth soundtrack+ Vast, radical arsenal of weapons, both ranged and melee+ Tight controls (key rebinds allowed), precise jumping / platformingCons:- Extremely short levels, the game feels almost like a boss rush- Difficulty is rather high. The Hard and the unlockable Badass difficulty levels (and their respective achievements) might be out of reach for regular players
_childDocuments_.name: HUNTDOWN

_childDocuments_.review: Huntdown is an excellent old-school sidescrolling shooter. The focus is wholly on the action and the gameplay is completely unburdened by unnecessary complications like character progression or skill trees. It's all about your skill as a player.The difficulty curve increases quite steeply and I experienced a few frustrating difficulty spikes here and there. But the game almost always felt fair and rather than be discouraged by failure I instead wanted to try again until I could beat its challenges.While pixel art 2D games are a dime a dozen, the art direction in Huntdown is superb and evokes the 80's B-action movies that have clearly been a source of inspiration for the game.The story is simple but presented with such over the top flair that it immediately won me over. And the voice-acting is a really good, especially considering the type of game this is.And as a final note the game has couch co-op, which I consider to be a huge plus.If you like sidescrolling action games and want to just shut off your brain and get into the zone? Then this is the game for you.
_childDocuments_.name: HUNTDOWN

_childDocuments_.review: "Huntdown" is a great example of a "modern retro game". It looks beautiful, has a catchy OST and very responsive controls. Basically how we remember all games from our childhood ... until we dust a few of them off. ;) The game gets tougher the farther you get (who would have thought?!) but never feels unfair. You should have a fondness for 80s (action) movies to fully appreciate "Huntdown", though. There are countless references for you to discover.
_childDocuments_.name: HUNTDOWN

_childDocuments_.review: Man what a fantastic game this is. From the art to the animation, everything drips with 80's action style, and it's a brilliant homage to the movies we all fondly remember from that era. The nods are clever and plentiful, from a boss being named after an A-Team member and looking like one of the guys from Dutch's crew in Predator (he even yells "CONTAAAACT"), to a sign that says "H. Gruber Moving and Towing" and many, many more it is a fantastic love letter to the classics. The gameplay is short and sweet while offering a great challenge but never feeling unfair. I can't recommend this one enough. One of the first area bosses even talks using a Macho Man voice, what more could you want?!?!
_childDocuments_.name: HUNTDOWN

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10, outstanding in every way possible. A shining example of what video games can be, and a true modern classic, destined to be immortalized in gaming history by the virtue of it's pure awesomeness. If you're able to, buy full price - it's well worth it, and the makers of this game fully deserve such patronage. A lot of love went into their work here, and it most certainly shows.
_childDocuments_.name: HUNTDOWN

_childDocuments_.review: I have mixed feelings about it. it's a shame steam doesn't allow an "average" opinion. the game is sublime, both for the eyes and the ears, and the atmosphere is really perfect, a pure dive into the retro-cyberpunk universe, a real pleasure.the problem is that the game remains unfortunately quite repetitive. we move forward, they shoot, we take cover, we ventilate, they die, we move forward, and so on...very quickly, the only variety you can have is to find the hidden briefcases and the bosses which are very well done and varied in terms of the challenges they offerit's really a pity, a huge work has been done to make the game beautiful but on the other hand, we quickly feel quite passive as we have few choices. we would have liked to have the choice to be able to progress following different paths, either by the roofs or the sewers (if the level is suitable of course), to be able to choose our equipment rather than picking up what the enemies leave when they die and using it until the magazines are empty. in short, we would have liked to have had more choices in the game in short, it's a pity, I don't doubt that the game is a very good experience but I don't think I'll come back again and again

_childDocuments_.review: Easily a contender for best game of 2021. Just like with Katana Zero, everything in this game is spot on. Great soundtrack. Awesome retro pixel graphics. Smooth responsive gameplay with a challenging but fair difficulty. Not too long, not too short. You pick one of three bounty hunters, who have different playstyles, based on their primary/secondary weapons. Every single boss fight was original and uniquely challenging. High replayability thanks to different bounty hunters, four difficulties and Arcade Mode, where you have only 1 life to finish a whole stage.I never tried co-op mode yet, but I had so much fun playing just by myself. I'm sure it's a blast playing it with a friend. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: HUNTDOWN

_childDocuments_.review: Even though I myself have only done one playthrough on normal, I can tell this game has replay value in terms of aditional difficulty, arcade more, goals etc if you are so inclined. Impressive looks and soundtrack, very smooth and reactive controls. Very sensible checpoint placemetns, there's really no backtracking and silly bull**** like that. Boss fights are fun and unique. Even the normal difficulty was not trivial but not super hard, just the right ammount of challenge where you can get through everything in several tries before frustration kicks in. If you are a hardcore fan of 2d run'n'gun platformers you'll be happy as a pig in mud. Even if you are a casual I'd encourage you to check it out.

_childDocuments_.review: A game like games are meant to be made. Besides the good graphics and music, the playability is great and the gameplay very well balanced. The length of the game is also a good point. Shorter would have let me thirsty; longer could have started feeling repetitive. A masterpiece.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun for a bit of single player, though Huntdown really shines for co-op play. If you have someone to play with this is an easy recommendation. Unfortunately it's not that simple since this game has local co-op only. Steam's Remote Play feature was too laggy for us to get too far into the game's more complex boss fights and so I wish proper multiplayer support were introduced.I also wish there was a little more to chew on here, but what is on display is extremely tasty. Each of the characters has small differences that mix things up nicely. A reasonable variety of weapons and items to make each area unique. There are opportunities to feel powerful and opportunities to feel clever - excellent - mechanics are straight forward but with some nuance for mastery. The achievements are well designed - I always love finding secrets... but the big challenge is getting through the levels without dying. I imagine this will be particularly difficult in Badass mode. Boss fights all feel quite unique and challenging, they certainly make for a fun time - you will be able to crack the patterns and avoid most damage in each fight... as opposed to some random nonsense that leaves you feeling simply unlucky. Great!I like the restraint with 2 player only co-op... a perfect amount of chaos on the screen at any one time. Lovely, well balanced.I would be interested to pick up more content for this game if it were ever released, which is always a good signal. A fun time for some couch co-op... and I won't stop until Badass mode is complete!Recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: A delightful throwback to the 2D shoot-em-ups of the 90s, filtered through the grungy excess of the 80s. The look is wonderfully grimy; the music is propulsive; the gameplay is rock solid. It'll definitely push your skills to the max, even on normal difficulty settings, and the goofy story and characters, while not exactly groundbreaking, know better than to take any of this seriously. Well worth the price.

_childDocuments_.review: Huntdown is a 2D run and gun platformer stylized in a 1980’s gritty cyberpunk universe, and looks like it was made for the SEGA Genesis. While the platforming is a large part of the game, I feel like the 20 or so boss battles are the real selling point of the game. Each boss has their own unique pattern obviously, and can really have you sweating while finishing off that final chunk of their life bar. Using a controller with a turbo fire button for this game would be beneficial.
_childDocuments_.name: HUNTDOWN

_childDocuments_.review: Holy shoot balls this is a boss rage simulator second to none. If you feel like your diet is lacking in rageohol then this is the game for you. This is a hard game. On NORMAL. The best thing about this game is the cool scenery, music, and all the little touches that go into setting the atmosphere, It's 90s side-scrolling carnage in high res, and it's beautiful in its crumbling scifi dystopian finery, but ain't no one got time to look at the drapes when there are baddies to gib at 6 and 12, pointblank. That's satisfying. Fighting the minions is fun, if at times, overwhelming. Fighting the bosses (bounties) is not and you will fight them all. the. damn. time. Fighting bounties is all trial and error as you learn their patterns and work out the range of their attacks. Throw in the occasional spanner throwing minion and that's that. You would think a game that is all about the boss fight they would actually be fun. It feels like a lot of love and attention to detail went into the first levels. They are so dynamic with a lots of cool background stuff going on, and it feels like love at first sight, but this level of detail seems to drop off as the boss grind kicks in. I can almost nearly sort of maybe like you (Huntdown), but never love. I'm going back to bro force. That's a game that knows how to have fun 8) I would really love to get some more time to interact with the environment and more minion gibbing to pad out the aggravating bounties. Die you sonofa...!So yes, I recommend this game. BUT. Only if you are coming for the sights and staying for aggravating bosses. Hey, I'm not judging how you choose to spend your time. 3/5Edit: after playing on easy - it (easy mode) feels like you are a force of nature, mowing down your enemies with skill and ease. Bounty fights are sane, with less emphasis on endurance and perfect timing. I fought all the bosses I came against in normal mode, and after that nightmare of training I crushed it. That said, bosses will still cause pain while patterns and weaknesses are learnt, and I have only cleared the first two areas, so can't yet speak of later game difficulty. I am finding easy to be the setting of fun. Normal is for the insane, and I don't want to think about any settings beyond that. Rating is now 4/5.
