_childDocuments_.review: Huntdown is a 2D side scroller. The presentation is wonderful. While playing the first level, I knew this was going to be an awesome game. You step out of your car and kickass music starts. You pass by some cops that are arresting thugs and in the background police mechs are patrolling the street. Now this is how you make a first level. The level layouts, enemy design, weapons everything is masterfully crafted and when it comes together you get this amazing game. The soundtrack is catchy. Main characters and their one liners are great. Lots of 80s and 90s movie references. The cover system is a nice touch. Story mode is enjoyable, and it prepares you for the arcade mode. In arcade mode there are no cutscenes, there isn't any exposition. As soon as you start a level, game throws enemies at you and expects you to kill them fast and stylish. Killing enemies as fast as possible and making combos felt satisfying. Huntdown is an awesome game.
_childDocuments_.name: HUNTDOWN

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed the game well enough to play through it on  Badass (without dying) but it has some problems.The presentation is good, aesthetics are great. The references are entertaining. These are the best parts.There are annoying animation locks that can easily kill you in game. For example, if you were shooting a pickup weapon and try to go to cover, game will not let you until you have finished its shooting animation. You kick a dude and you cannot do anything until the kick animation ends, the kick also can happen all of a sudden if an enemy spawns next to you (coming from behind a corner or such). You'll suddenly be kicking them in the face while a dozen others aim their guns at you (the kick sometimes also plays twice and the second kick does nothing, the enemy will do their own melee animation and you'll get popped). Picking up weapons similarly locks you into a reload and switch animation and you cannot attack at all during it, the same animation happens when you run out of bullets for a pickup weapon.The cover system makes the game a bit slower than it needs to be, usually you won't need to use it, but sometimes there are scripted sequences where it's the only way to progress barring some really well-timed dodges.Compare this to Metal Slug, another run n' gun shooter, and Huntdown doesn't hold a candle to that game. Metal Slug does not have any of the animation locks I talked about here; you pickup a weapon and it's immediately accessible, you also can jump and run while doing a melee animation - no matter if you began slicing someone up on the ground or not, you can still jump in the middle of the animation and it'll switch to the aerial animation on the fly. I'd recommend trying out that series instead unless you absolutely want a cyberpunk themed shooter.Huntdown's a decent enough game but has some really annoying quirks and gets a thumbs down from me overall. I cannot recommend it as it is.I'd also like to add that the characters have different skins and different primary weapons, but do not differ in any other meaningful way from each other. I feel Jack Sawyer is best because you don't really need to keep your aim on an opponent to deliver maximum amount of damage. The others need to keep stationary to deliver their dps and each and every primary weapon does similar amount of dps, the difference is just in the "how fast can you move after shooting" department.
_childDocuments_.name: HUNTDOWN

_childDocuments_.review: Huntdown is an incredibly difficult yet fun side scrolling shooter that combines Contra, No More Heroes, Castlevania, Hotline Miami & more into a sci fi dystopian future filled with references (both subtle & not so subtle) for every movie you love from the 80’s. The game is fully voiced over, has excellent music, presentation & atmosphere that are all top notch….yet I am forced to give this a negative review…Steam reviews are simple, they fall into two categories: Recommended & Not Recommended. Despite me loving a lot of what Huntdown has to offer, some things I might even think they are perfect, this game unfortunately falls into the Not Recommended category for one big issue the game has...the current state of its Multiplayer. See the problem is Huntdown solely relies on Steam’s Remote Play feature to handle Online Co-Op & currently after a big update Remote Play is worse across the board for many users but honestly it was never great to begin with.Huntdown is a difficult game, you have limited health & the bosses are brutal. Twitch movement & learning every pattern to a fight is key here, old school difficulty. If you die you restart at a checkpoint but each level you will notice the bosses getting more and more punishing, that all changes when you add in player 2. While other games pump up their difficulty when they detect a 2nd player, Huntdown does not. You are doubling your firepower & adding unlimited resurrects between players on the same difficulty level, there isn’t more enemies, they do not even do more damage. Because of this playing Co-Op over Single Player is a night & day experience in Huntdown. Co-Op is always more fun but the entire dynamic changes with this game. So the game only supports Online Co-Op via Remote Play. If you go to the forums section you will find lots of people complaining about this & there is usually a mod on the games side saying something like “Hot Tip: The game works great with Remote Play”. It doesn’t….at least for me Remote Play is entirely busted. See they may think the game works great in Remote Play but if the devs are all playing in the same office together, the connection between users would be pretty perfect. Out in the real world that connection falls apart entirely between friends. As the Host my game runs fine, but currently the Client user seems to only work when Remote Play is set to Automatic….but that still means freezing, slowdown, delayed inputs all in a game that requires precision movement. Any other setting including Fast which should sacrifice visual quality for performance tanks Player 2 to 1 FPS. Is this the devs fault? Not entirely…it seems a recent update to Remote Play pretty much destroyed the service for lots of Steam users. So what is their fault? The game is infinitely better in Co-Op but they entirely rely on a poor service to handle their online connections instead of working on at least a Peer 2 Peer system.I want to love Huntdown, there is so much good here, but I can’t recommend it due to this massive problem. If Remote Play ever gets perfected in the future (doubt) or if the devs put in the work to have their own Online Co-Op system, I will happily swap this review to positive based on all the good I mentioned in the first paragraph. But sadly for now I cannot recommend Huntdown.

_childDocuments_.review: I have only just started playing this for an hour or so but feel I can recommend it already. Fantastic detailed and interactive environments, beautiful & stylish pixel artwork, superb soundtrack that carries you through the levels at a fast pace, every 80's/90's pop culture/movie reference is on point and there is excellent & sometimes hilarious voice acting.     I find the gameplay a good balance of challenge and satisfaction, and that's only the normal difficulty level. There is a great old-skool feeling of chaos and destruction as you fight your way through the carnage of each stage. Some of the bosses have been quite tricky to beat, and it takes a few attempts to learn their attacks and time your reflexes. I think the default keyboard controls are a bit difficult to use, but it's simple enough to re-map them.     In short: this game really hits the spot for me, you should give it a try.

The game has a good look and feel. Controls are pretty simple with or without a controller. I appreciate that they are customizable, such as the default movement keys are the arrows and through the options menu, I was able to key bind WASD. At the time I'm writing this, it is on sale for $3.99 and it's well worth the money. It's a lot of fun. I've started on the lowest difficulty so I can learn the mechanics of the game. The boss fights are all unique and engaging. I also like the Blade Runner vibe the game gives off. I can see why it is critically acclaimed. I highly recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting retro side scroller that harkens back to the Arcade games of the 90s.  The pixel art is fantastic, rivals metal slug in terms of quality.  The gameplay reminds me of a mix of Robocop on the Amiga, Metal Slug and Contra from my youth.You play as a bounty hunter, taking on jobs too dirty for the police in a future dystopian city.  There are three bounty hunters to choose from.  Each has a slightly different default gun (slow & powerful / average middle of the road / weak & fast firing)  you can pickup one additional weapon at a time, until you swap it or it runs out of ammo. You can also pick up various throwables for some extra fire power.Each level (bounty hunt) has three badges to earn; All kills, No deaths, All 3 collectables.  The bosses (bounties) have patterns that you'll need to pick up on, as well as tells, or you'll get hammered into the ground.All in all, good fun.

_childDocuments_.review: You'll know very quickly if Huntdown is the type of game you'll enjoy. The difficulty wastes no time ramping up. When it does, you'll find yourself attempting the same sections over and over. Some people will like that. Others will become frustrated. For me, it fell into the "frustrating" camp. For a game that demands split-second reaction time, the characters feel oddly sluggish to control. They move at a pace similar to Mega Man or Shovel Knight, yet there are bullets streaking across the screen, explosions, and charging enemies to contend with. A faster, nimbler character would have intensified the action and made the game play more hectic. But Huntdown infuses a Contra-style 2D shooter with cover mechanics instead. While some players may enjoy that, I found the two styles clashed with one another. There's a lot of time spent hiding behind boxes or in dark alcoves, trading fire with enemies. Since enemies take several hits to bring down, these firefights can last a while. A dash move helps speed up the action, but it's still not easy to dodge bullets since ducking can frustratingly lead into a slide that sends you straight into the enemy. Jumping is a little slow and heavy, too, and lacks the springiness of games like Bro Force. And the 16-bit aesthetic, while nice looking, is overdone by indie shooters. It also doesn't make much sense to theme a game around the 1980s and fill it with 1990s graphics.Overall, I don't think Huntdown does anything particularly remarkable. There are flashier and more exciting games in this category, and the sluggish movement, cover mechanics, and crouch slide are bound to turn some players off. It's probably a solid enough experience for anyone looking for an old-school challenge; but when it comes to high-octane fun, Huntdown falls short of its competitors.

_childDocuments_.review: I am going to recommend it on the basis that is a well worked game, the art style is great and well detailed for a pixelated game, full of funny references and obvious influences from action movies in the 70/80s (specially robocop and the warriors), BUT if you're looking for an "easy" game, this is not it. That is my main complain, it can get extremely frustrating sometimes, not only due to difficulty but also sometimes hit boxes don't seem to be that precise, giving you damage in situations i couldn't understand.If you want a challenge, achievement hunting, like detailed pixel art and run and gun humour, it's amazing.If you don't have the patience or just want and easy going a to b game, it's still good but you won't appreciate it.

_childDocuments_.review: Huntdown is one of those games that I enjoyed playing but will probably never go back to. The graphics are pretty good with lots of detail despite it being pixel art. The sound is great with meaty sounding effects and a fantastic soundtrack. The gameplay reminds me of the old skool Robocop videogame on systems such as the (showing my age here) C64 and Nes - side scrolling action and shooting bad guys except that its a bit more involved then that.It is pretty fun and the references to old 80's movies are cool. Some of the levels do feel short and the boss fights are a bit hit and miss (my favourite is "Unholy Goalie). There is 4 stages split into 5 levels each so isn't a long game (which can be a positive). I guess I just feel a bit meh about it really as I'll uninstall it and will probably not ever think about it again. If your on the fence about whether to buy this or not then wait until a sale. If not spending a lot of money on it then yes it's definitely worth it, I'm personally glad I didn't spend over £20 on it as I would feel a bit miffed!!!

_childDocuments_.review: It's a simple 2D game that's just really fun to play and really challenging.Every thing in here looks, sounds and feels fantastic.From the enemy placement to the sprite work, nothing feels rushed or underdeveloped.I think my only complaint is the lack of an autofire button, it kind of limits how much I can play this game when my hand starts to cramp up after mashing the living daylights out of the shoot button. But I'm sure younger players won't have that issue :)The story is just a bag of cliches, but they're enjoyable ones to be sure. I did end up calling the big twist in advance, but not the smaller follow up twist. So that's good. I love that each bounty hunter gets their own quips and lines in the cutscenes really gives you a good sense of personality.Game play is very simple. You ever play Contra or Metal Slug? It's that.A 2D side scrolling shooter with light bullet hell elements, although unlike those two Huntdown has a cover system and no aiming. Which means you have to put yourself in danger to hit your target and that is where I think most of the challenge comes from. Timing your shots between enemy volleys and sprinting for cover whenever you can. Maybe it would have been better to compare this to NOT A HERO which is another cover based 2D shooter.The bosses are great, only one felt kind of cheap because its movement wasn't telegraphed. But the rest are beyond solid. They're fantastic. Excellent displays of character and world building mixed with creating an enjoyable yet still challenging fight.

_childDocuments_.review: This 80s/90s action movie inspired arcade shooter wears it's influences on it's sleeve with pride, on ode to a simpler age where politics were sidelined in favour of fun, and masculinity was still an acceptable quality.Set in a familiar dystopian future where crime is rampant and law enforcement non-exisent, you play as one of three classic action heroes, delivering you own brand of vigilante justice (which basically involves shooting, stabbing and exploding everything that moves). If you assumed you'd be quipping one-liners like they're going out of fashion as you go, then give yourself a bro-fist.The pixel graphics are top-quality, with some impressive attention to detail, and although the shooting mechanics seem simple at a glance, there's enough wrinkles here to make for some surprising tactical depth which rewards good planning or quick-thinking.Tight shooting mechanics really pull this all together with a diverse arsenal of weapons to use, each feeling distinct and appropriately punchy. The combat moves at a brisk pace and can be difficult on higher difficulties, but doesn't feel unfair.With a good variety of locations, enemies and well-designed bosses to get through (including a couple of genuinely laugh out loud moments), a Warrior-esque syth soundtrack and some excellent combat, Huntdown comes highly recommended. The only real negative is the lack of online coop, but if you're determined to do this, there is always Steam Remote play as a work around.See you at the party Richter...

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent sidescrolling brawler with superb pixel art and character design. The enemies and bosses are so full of character. These are the four gangs you will be facing: - generic 80ies punks- ice hockey punks- gasoline/Mad Max punks - samurai cyber punksThe levels leading to the boss fights are adequately short - they never outstay their welcome and are also crafted with a lot of retro love. The many bosses themselves have some nice variety to them and you need to learn their patterns in order to succeed. I usually don't finish games. This is an exception. Huntdown is wholeheartedly recommended.PS: As a case in point for the retro vibes: In some scenes (mostly loading screens and cut-scenes) some objects (e.g. cars, heads/body parts) are improperly scaled. I don't think it's by accident - you can observe that quite commonly in games of the olden days. :)

_childDocuments_.review: One of the main problems with this game is the huge difficulty gap between the levels and the boss fights. The levels can easily be torn through without any real thought. I found on normal difficulty using cover was completely unnecessary as you could just spam your way through the level, but there isn't much appeal to using the cover either as it quickly falls to just being a case of slowly pushing through the level whilst you peak and shoot over and over. The argument could be made that I should put the difficulty up, but as someone who enjoys difficult games, I found the boss fights atrociously monotonous. The bosses are unique from one another but the individual fights are way too repetitive which makes it feel like an absolute slog when you die and have to go back to the start of the fight. Another issue is the lack of options you have to creatively overcome obstacles. The game just doesn't have enough mechanics to feel like you are playing in your own style. Everything is so rigid and limited and repetitive… and writing this review has made me realise repetitiveness is a key gripe with this game.Then there is the humour. The bosses are normally based on some 80's reference like the Macho Man or Ultimate Warrior or Elvis...that should be enough of an indicator to know this game's style of humour. On the flip, the visuals are incredibly detailed and cleverly put together, but there are a ton of other reviews talking about that so go read those.

_childDocuments_.review: 5/10I found this game more frustrating than funThis is a pretty standard side-scroller shoot em up, with some over the top weapons and violence, that encourages you to use whatever weapon pickups you find as soon as you find them, similar to something like Hotline MiamiNow, the game is well made in a lot of waysThe sound design is good, although I have to admit I turned everything down so I could listen something else, but from what I heard nothing was at all badThe core game mechanics - the Movement, the Shooting, Dodging, and Taking Cover, worked smoothly. Nothing is broken, exactly, but I WOULD say the melee mechanic feels like it occasionally just doesn't workI WOULD say everything with the visuals is good to perfect, except...Well, the visuals aren't bad because they look ugly(I think they nail the aesthetic perfectly). The visuals are bad because they often make it nearly impossible to perceive incoming attacks(which makes it nearly impossible to AVOID incoming attacks) due to over-cluttering and poor telegraphingIt's one thing for a situation to be hard to overcome because there's a lot on the screen and it's hard to keep track of so many things. It's a whole OTHER thing for there to be a lot of things and I can't even SEE half of them because there are a bunch of overlapping spritesFor instance, on the final boss fight there are a bunch of boulders falling past you while you're on some floating platforms. When the boulders hit the platforms, they bounce, give off a boulder-colored cloud of dust, and keep falling. When the challenge is 'avoid the boulders' and I can barely tell which things are boulders and which are clouds of boulder dust...idk, it just didn't work for meAnd all that being said, while the gameplay was solid(most everything worked well), I wouldn't say it ever really felt engaged; most every fight just felt like moving forward blindly shooting until everything died or I died, and only about half the times I died did I have to think about how to get past that section.And most of the time I DID have to think about how to proceed the answer was usually 'go really slow and kill everything you can from a safe distance'The final thing I'll say is that the boss fights, while often visually impressive, were either tedious and easy or tedious and a giant pain in my assThe bosses either have a few easy to dodge attacks and 2 minutes of health to chew through, or the bosses have a few difficult to predict attacks and it takes longer to chew through their health because you're always preemptively dodging.But what's worse is, none of them really did anything I found interesting, and there was nothing that made me use the core mechanics in any fun way: nothing that made me feel cool for doing something well. But maybe the game lost me early on and I had a bad attitude from there, it could be different for others I imagineI played through this on normal, and feel no desire to go back on any other difficulty, or ever play the game againI will say I played this solo, and I bet it'd be a lot more fun with someone elseBut if you want an action packed, over-the-top-violent, 80s themed side-scroller I'd recommend Broforce over this any dayP.S.Also, at the end of each mission it gives you a 'score' - Pass/Fail on 3 things: Enemies killed(Pass is All enemies in level)Secrets found(3 secrets in every level)Deaths(Pass is 0)This score doesn't seem to affect ANYTHING, and there are no upgrades or anything like that, so there's no reason to even TRY to get a perfect score other than a steam achievement

_childDocuments_.review: The bosses in this game are either non-entities or are absurdly unfair and haven't been playtested at all. Unfortunately, this game is wall-to-wall bosses. None of them are any fun, even if some of them have funny personalities. All of them have an instant melee attack that hits you when you enter an invisible field around them, which is shockingly terrible design. It's not that you touch the boss, it's that you touch the VICINITY around them. An easy way to tell this hasn't been playtested is sometimes the boss arenas have melee weapons in them. These literally cannot be used to beat the bosses.Now, their melee attacks are pretty bad, but nothing compared to how every boss can (without warning or animation) shoot a volley of fast projectiles in your face. For most of the bosses, you can learn to work around these design flaws. For others, they're bullet sponges and fill the arena with randomized hazards that often create no-win scenarios. Going through the process of trial and error in these special few have drained any remaining bits of fun out of the game for me.If you want to enjoy the amazing pixel art, go ahead. That part delivers. Just set it to easy I guess, since the game itself is an unbalanced mess.

_childDocuments_.review: As far as retro games go, this is a gem. The attention to detail, the gameplay, graphics, sounds and overall theme is perfectly executed. I guess there's a nostalgia factor to it too, but if you fondly remember the Amiga days and if you've played and appreciate the gameplay in those side-scrolling shoot'em'ups, I doubt there are better options out there. It's not too long, it has three characters to choose between and while some bosses are quite tough, it's not overly difficult in my opinion. To be fair, I've played it in coop, and we still got a couple of stages left before we've beaten the game. There's extra content for those who are inclined to climb a scoreboard. For us the game has worked very well with the 'remote-play' Steam feature, which kind of doubles the value of the game if you looking to co-op. Both on controllers, although I've seen some players on the forum struggling with it.Overall it's a great game for what it is. High quality and not very complex or long, but just right for this kind of game. It's decently priced at 16.79€. I'd recommend it, but of course it's a better purchase on a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, here's a zoomer review.It's good, presentation is cool, gameplay is like an arcade game, who woulda thunk it?The level gameplay is really fast paced, so playing like a completionist is easy once you get used to the slightly odd controls, the Heatseeker levels are the hardest, I would say. The boss battles, though...The boss battles, they're not bad per se, just so drawn out. The patterns are easy to learn but hard to execute, I guess. Maybe I'm not old enough to have nostalgia for games that extend their playtimes by making you shoot a thing for 7 minutes straight, but they really turn me off of the whole game.Let me end this off on a positive note, the world, though limited, feels genuine. This legit feels like it was a game made for an 80s action movie that never existed, the plucky grime of the Hoodlum Dolls, the cultlike sports culture of the Misconducts (Unholy Goalie is cooler than Shogun tho, shoulda been last), the charismatic violence of the Heatseekers and the slick, funky brutality of the No. 1 Suspects, it's great for real. Part of me feels like the game and the world is limited by the devs dedication to making a "retro" game, but that's just me.Also the dash mechanic is so unnecessary that I genuinely forgot about it. The weapon switching system is lacking a lil bit, I think that a melee button would be a better alternative, maybe allowing the player to have a melee slot alongside a ranged weapon slot.All in all, 7 or 8/10, really good, but lacking in ways that might be intentional. _childDocuments_.review: Huntdown is a fast-paced, retro-inspired action-platformer that combines classic 8-bit and 16-bit visuals with modern mechanics and an over-the-top, action-packed story. Developed by Coffee Stain Publishing and Easy Trigger Games, Huntdown draws heavily from the arcade games and action movies of the 80s and 90s, delivering a thrilling ride for players who enjoy a mix of old-school gameplay and intense combat.In Huntdown, players take on the role of one of three bounty hunters: Anna Conda, John Sawyer, or Mow Man, each with their own unique abilities and weaponry. Set in a dystopian, gang-infested city, the objective is simple: eliminate dangerous criminal syndicates and restore order, all while engaging in explosive gunfights, dodging enemy attacks, and navigating challenging platforming sections.The game is packed with colorful pixel art, fluid animations, and a vibrant, dystopian world full of personality. Its action is smooth and rewarding, with tight controls and a variety of weapons to choose from, including pistols, shotguns, and rocket launchers. The level design is diverse, taking players through gritty streets, abandoned warehouses, and underground hideouts, each filled with enemies to dispatch in stylish combat sequences.With its relentless pace, charming retro aesthetic, and satisfying gameplay, Huntdown is a love letter to the golden age of arcade action games. If you’re a fan of side-scrolling shooters with a heavy emphasis on action, style, and humor, Huntdown is a must-play experience that will keep you coming back for more.

_childDocuments_.review: Dang solid little arcade run n' gun.It's short, and on a deep sale I think it's an instabuy if you even sort of like the genre.The design is more cerebral than I was expecting from a contralike, and I'd compare it to Flashback. You can't really twitch out of the way of bullets, so you have to be somewhere else before they're fired. Cover exists, but isn't great, and weapons run out of ammo fast, so it kind of plays like a high speed puzzle where you're constantly managing a dozen different factors.Add to this gorgeous sprite art, deliberately paced levels, a nice soundtrack, and an extraordinary number of pulls from 80s films, and the game as a whole walks a careful line between nostalgia and innovation, feeling engaging as hell all the way.If I had to critique it for something other than being short, I think it fails to thread the needle on one of the blaxploitation / hong kong cinema gang bosses, and Yuudai comes across like a Shadow Warrior character. I don't think this is a thing that will irritate most players (tbh I think folks who like Shadow Warrior will like Huntdown's setting a lot), but it stood out to me so I guess it goes into the review.And on the subject of standing out, the voice work and sfx design in Huntdown is unusually good. Every performance is taken 100% seriously, even the goofy ones, and Wolfmother's voice actor absolutely kills the line delivery for what is otherwise kind of uninteresting text.I think if you want a 2D shooter that forces you to get a little cerebral sometimes, and Huntdown's on sale, and you have an evening to burn, this is absolutely a title to pick up. I'm stoked to check out whatever the developers release next.

_childDocuments_.review: "HUNTDOWN" – the ultimate blast from the past with a futuristic twist. If you're into pixel-perfect action and retro vibes with a modern punch, this game is your jam.First off, let's talk style. "HUNTDOWN" rocks a classic 16-bit aesthetic with a cyberpunk edge that'll make your inner '80s kid fist pump with joy. Every pixel is dripping with coolness, from the neon-soaked cityscapes to the grungy back alleys.Now, onto the gameplay. Get ready to kick some serious butt as you dive into fast-paced, side-scrolling shootouts. With three badass bounty hunters to choose from, each with their own unique skills and weaponry, the action never gets stale. It's like "Contra" on steroids, but with more attitude and explosions.But hey, it's not all mindless mayhem. "HUNTDOWN" brings the challenge too. You'll need lightning-fast reflexes and strategic thinking to outsmart the ruthless gangs and mega-corporations that run the show.And let's not forget the soundtrack – a synthwave masterpiece that'll have you nodding your head and tapping your feet as you mow down baddies like a boss.In short, "HUNTDOWN" is a retro-futuristic delight that'll scratch your itch for old-school action with a fresh coat of paint. Grab your controller and get ready to unleash some pixelated fury!

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who experienced Contra thanks to flashgames and has not played many other sidescrollers, this is the peak of this genre, for me.From visuals to audio to balance, everything is just so  right.The short main menu intro is so nice, with the 3 playable characters wreathed in shadows, lighting up the title and the absolutely stunning synth trumpets roaring up.The soundtrack is incredible: dark synth undertones telling you that youre the prey or upbeat tracks infusing a sense of godlike invincibility.It sticks to its genre, but is still unique.The difficulty is somehow perfectly managed in this game.The addition of cover seems to be something quite new in this genre and I think it absolutely positively enhances such a games balance and tactical depth.Even when the section of one level feels hard to beat at first, it is super easy after knowing the ins and outs.It is definitely learnable as the controls are kept simple, hud elements are not intrusive and all enemy spawns are predictable and not randomized.The weapons in the game feel powerful, but not too easy as they spend ammo quick enough.Every level shines in its sharp detail, be it background or foreground.NPCs vary from melee units flushing you out, to shotgunners waiting behind cover to blast your head off.Every boss is different from the other, aesthetically and tactically.You must employ different strategies to beat each: quick shotgun blasts to the back of Psychonaught, stay away from TNT Randy and attack from afar, dodge Sids quick melee attacks.And those are only from the first area.And oh my lord the one liners.Criticisms:I think John Sawyer might be too OP, mainly because of the boomerang.It hits, and staggers, multiple enemies and you can catch it to nullify the cooldown.Mow Man gets 3 throwing knives and Anna gets a tomahawk.Neither of these two throwables seem to be able to penetrate multiple enemies and/or recollected as opposed to the boomerang.Some hitboxes might be a little unfair, such as Sid.When dodging into him early, before he intends to punch you he still hits you even the player character is mainly behind Sids body and fists.Some bosses are way too easy, like Bad Boy Bob.He does not nearly have as much depth as other bosses in the same area and the strategy to defeat him is really simple.Explosion sprites are way too obstructive, covering up an entire radius around your character model making you unable to see anything beneath it.This is a huge problem in the Heatseeker area.Conclusion:Clean up on aisle my pants. This is the ♥♥♥♥. This is _The_ Side Scroller.Also thanks for native Linux build.

_childDocuments_.review: People compare this game to Contra, but I think it's a lot more like Rolling Thunder (or maybe Metal Slug). The pace is slower, and there is a focus on using cover instead of dodging bullets. Your character isn't highly mobile, which means you can't just nimbly jump over every projectile. You also can't shoot up or diagonal. That being said, I like Rolling Thunder, so this game is fun for me.There are four buttons: shoot, jump, throw grenade, and switch weapon. _childDocuments_.review: Pretty good run-and-gun in the vein of Contra/Broforce/Ninja Gaiden/etc, i.e. move forward, kill bad guys, collect different weapons and health, etc. I played this solo but would definitely play it with my friends. I enjoyed the visuals: the gangs had pretty interesting themes and looks (although the first gang was sorta meh), and the levels were all pretty cool too. The soundtrack and sound effects are all pretty good as well. There is a reasonable increase in difficulty as you progress further. The game felt fair; there is no "game over", there are no lives. You can just keep trying until you beat each level/boss/area. There are checkpoints scattered throughout the levels that help with that as well. Overall I enjoyed it. I feel like there is potential for expansions or a sequel; new areas of the city, new gangs, new weapons, etc.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, very fun. Pretty difficult but not insurmountably so, even for me. _childDocuments_.review: - If you've ever wondered what the 16-bit bastard offspring of Robocop and Escape from New York would look like, it's probably Huntdown. Every screen of this game is home to some snazzy pixel art full of neon signs, urban decay, and lots of explosions- The music follows the theming perfectly. Be prepared to hear what could easily be an 80s action movie soundtrack. Driving synth beats and percussion will ebb and flow in tempo until you reach the final credits. I was not expecting to hear a licensed song as the credits started to roll, especially not my favorite Twisted Sister track. Out on the Streets is awesome and you should probably go listen to it right now- There's also voice acting, and it's very well performed. Sure, some of the bosses have that phoned-in "tough guy" voice, but at least the protagonists are voiced well. It was fun to mow down enemies with a minigun while my trenchcoated robot quipped action movie one-liners- The presentation isn't perfect, however. Some of the animation is pretty awful. I thought it was a framerate issue, but even capping the framerate didn't resolve anything. There just aren't enough animation sprites in the game to make. It was distracting enough that it did affect my enjoyment: it  looked like I was playing a flipbook at times- I'll explain the setup, but don't go skipping the intro movie (a mock movie trailer complete with the expected overly serious voiceover). In any case, this is a post-apocalyptic cyberpunk game. As is often the case in such dystopian settings, the world governments have collapsed, and the power vacuum  has been filled by private corporations like a libertarian wet dream. Meanwhile, street gangs have taken over the cities and war openly in the streets- That's where you (or, rather, one of 3 playable characters) come in. Instead of seeking corporate citizenship or gang membership, you're a bounty hunter who's been hired to clean up the streets--and make a pretty penny while doing it- Keep an eye and ear out to 80s movies references. They're everywhere- There's a lot of words you could use to describe the vibe of this game, but the most appropriate is "rad"- Looking back at my SNES days as a kid, I don't recall playing many 16 bit platform shooters outside of Mega Man, but Huntdown doesn't feel much like those games. Contra III and Judge Dredd are more similar. Metal Slug a little less so- That is to say, you're going to be jumping through, between, and on top of a lot of crumbling buildings while swapping weapons to dodge and precipitate opposing hails of gunfire- The platforming feels pretty tight, but there's nothing too difficult in that respect. Just keep an eye out for secret areas and destructible parts of the environment if you want to find powerful weapons and collectibles- All the difficulty in Huntdown comes from the combat, and it is notably difficult in the same vein as the Contra games it draws influence from. Fortunately, your movement options include the ability to slide (handy for dodging bullets coming from offscreen as you charge ahead) and duck into cover (either in doorways or behind boxes). You'll need to keep tabs on your available cover options if you want to avoid damage- Weapon variety was way better than I expected. Each of the three selectable characters had a unique sidearm and projectile to start, but you'll have way more fun with the melange of melee weapons, assault rifles, machine guns, shotguns, rocket launchers, lasers, remote mines, etc. that litter each stage. If you find yourself still wanting variety here, you're too hard to please- Each of the five levels in each of the city's four gang-controlled areas is capped off by a boss fight. These felt varied enough mechanically and visually that no two felt overly similar in spite of there being 20 of them in total- I can see myself playing this again down the road, partially because I didn't even touch arcade mode and partially because I'm disappointed in myself for having to lower the difficulty to Easy in the third area (The Overseer stage). Huntdown doesn't mess around- With robust challenges, eye-catching pixel art, and genuinely fun run-and-gun gameplay, this is an easy game to recommend to anyone who has a soft spot for titles like Contra or Metal Slug. I just wish the animation hadn't been so distractingly choppy. Seriously, compare a clip of Huntdown to Metal Slug 3; the difference is substantial- It ran without bugs or other technical issues just fine on the Steam Deck- . Buying a game simply because it looks cool turns out to be a great idea sometimes, apparently. Maybe wait for a sale if you're not going to delve into the arcade mode as the story is only 5-7 hours long depending on difficulty

Unless you try to get the survivor medal, then some enemy placements can feel frustrating. A lot of gun variety. Enemies feels different enough for a 2d game. Every gang and place feels live,different and pleasing to look to point 2-3 times I just stopped playing to look at the scenery for a minute.
_childDocuments_.name: HUNTDOWN

_childDocuments_.review: I thoroughly enjoy Huntdown, the way it merges nostalgia with sci-fi punk vibes and smooth mechanics is great. The game play is fun, while also quick enough that you can jump in and out, and not be punished for leaving it alone for weeks. Solid work and worth your money if you like the setting, genre or game play style.
_childDocuments_.name: HUNTDOWN

_childDocuments_.review: This game is excellent, maybe the best side scrolling shooter I've ever played. I love the world that the developer has crafted, it's colorful and creative sci-fi 80s future is a joy to shoot your way through. Boss fights are unique, challenging and fun. _childDocuments_.name: HUNTDOWN

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing side scroller. Combines some of the best elements of classic games and adds an insane level of detail and top-notch sound, music, and voice acting. Runs fantastic on steam deck and consumes little battery. My only quibble would be that I wish the levels before the boss fights were just a little bit longer. The gameplay is so great and I would love to just blast some more baddies before I get to the next boss.
_childDocuments_.name: HUNTDOWN

The difficulty grows linearly as players get familiar with the mechanism. The boss fights are designed in very high quality. I will recommend anyone who gets bored in 3D ACT to give this game a try.
_childDocuments_.name: HUNTDOWN

The secret stash and level clear stats also don't mean anything, so it's just shoot and scroll. The graphics and sound are gorgeous, but i wished for a better story and more diversity in gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: HUNTDOWN

_childDocuments_.review: Great little game. There are a ton of 2D side scroller retro games like this. This one stands out with the best mechanics (the kick is a game changer!) and the most entertaining presentation. It seems like they borrowed from "Door Kickers: Action Squad" a bit, another nice little 2D shooter with similar vibes.
_childDocuments_.name: HUNTDOWN

_childDocuments_.review: Instantly became one of my favorite games. Cyberpunk is my favorite setting, I grew up with retro games and i adore 80s style music. So, I love this game!This game is hard, completed my first run on hard and it was a challenge. Not only is it skill based, (easy to pickup and understand, but gets more challenging real quick) but you also really want to memorize bosses their patterns and level strats. Playing singleplayer on hard sometimes makes the game feel tactical, and slows the pace down sometimes, though gets fast at sections with many enemies.But play on normal mode alone or with a friend (yes this game has a classic couch co-op experience!), the game gets way faster and chaotic. It feels amazing to dodge around attacks and troll your friend with melee weapons.Anyway, buy this game if you like retro games! Music is great together with all the sfx and comical voicelines, visuals are top-quality pixel art, and the gameplay is retro but very modernized!
_childDocuments_.name: HUNTDOWN

_childDocuments_.review: - very good graphics,- detailed environments,- low hardware requirements (steady 60 fps with integrated gpu and i3 cpu),- thought through level design,- vibes of contra, metal slug, old arcade games, Tarantino action movies and bladerunner,- good platforming,- amazing sountrack,- crisp sfx,- broad arsenal changing in each act,- challenging but not overwhelming bossfights reminding me of dark souls (fixed movesets easy to recognize and dodge after a while),- 5 hitpoints on normal mode and plenty of scattered healing items and checkpoints,- ability to dodge and take cover,- 3 slightly different joke-cracking headhunters to choose from,- funny, not cheap and straightforward humor,- great gameplay solo, even greater in coop with the ability to resurrect the second player when downed (helps with bosses),- secrets are not absurdly difficult to find and can contain generous rewards or cool easter eggs (like Bladerunner or Gremlins references)Overall a very solid game, quite refreshing and not frustratingly hard. Maybe a little short, but that's the price you pay for overwhelming quality and that I prefer over games that on paper have content for 100+ hrs and get boring after 10.Huntdown is easily a 10/10 material in my book.
_childDocuments_.name: HUNTDOWN

And for £3 ish , you be mad to miss, if you like these type of games...Pixel art, music and game play are excellent. Level design is great and re-play is a 10..  One to buy !!
_childDocuments_.name: HUNTDOWN

_childDocuments_.review: This is the best run-and-gun game I've played in recent memory and even rivals Blazing Chrome. The pixel art graphics are extremely polished, soundtrack is full of bangers, and gameplay is precise. I love the retro-future theme as the overall setting of this game is great. Boss fights are difficult, satisfying to beat, and add to the game's over-the-top character. There is a  solid level of replayability if you want to kill every enemy, collect stashes, or attempt deathless runs of each level. This all proves to be addicting as I've doubled my playtime since the credits rolled.
_childDocuments_.name: HUNTDOWN

_childDocuments_.review: Super fun game but it needs an infinite play mode. While it has multiple difficulties, they all feel like some variation of "hard". "Easy" is not easy, by any means. Regardless of difficulty, if you get hit five times, you die...period. The difficulty also ramps up after the first boss, so be prepared. Just don't expect the game to hold your hand or be a walk in the park.

_childDocuments_.review: It's awesome. I would love to see more like this. Talented dev team, looks like all their games kick *ss and I would love to see more from them with a similar genre as this game.I was amazed that I plugged in 2 controllers and immediately was able to play with my buddy, he had never even seen or heard of the game before but he loved it and we had a great time. _childDocuments_.name: HUNTDOWN

I wish more studios had this use in mind instead of forcing themselves to use all gamepads buttons for nothing.Hope we'll hear from these guys with another game soon!
_childDocuments_.name: HUNTDOWN

_childDocuments_.review: At $20 this best-in-genre near-masterpiece is worth every penny, at $4 you should only avoid it if you're incapable of enjoying a run & gun.  If you have a friend to play with its even more of a no-brainer.-The game is polished to a shine.-the thematics, including VO, character models, environments, and even the appropriately light story are amazing.-simple but still engaging gameplay; it's not a bullet-hell experience like Metal Slug, you have to think more tactically, utilize cover, etc. especially at higher difficulties.-I mostly but not entirely reject the complaint that it gets redundant.  Yes, the game is not dripping with differentiation, but the core experience is so good and I think there is plenty of variety in the enemies and bosses (the weapons probably lack a little diversity for some, but its part of the game just overall being so elegant and clean.  Jump, Dash, Shoot, Special Weapon and I never wanted a fifth button personally.  The gameplay isn't wildly varied but it's SO compelling and satisfying.

If you're not up to trying again and again and getting angrier and angrier because you keep progressively taking damage from the same ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ thing because there's no cooldown on damage to the player, then this is not for you.
_childDocuments_.name: HUNTDOWN

_childDocuments_.review: I LOVE THIS GAME. A platform action shooter that puts you in the spot of a Corporate Mercenary tasked with bringing the LAW ONE BULLET AT A TIME to social degenerates. There are 4 locations and each location contains 4-5 miniboss along with a final boss at the end of a given location. Each individual miniboss level is about 10-15 minutes of gameplay and can be longer depending how many times you die to the miniboss. And let me tell you, YOU WILL DIE, up until you learn and deliver lead justice to your bounty target.The gameplay is simple enough, run and gun any goon in your way. You start with a pistol and a rechargeable throwing weapon but as you progress through the level you can gain access to Miniguns, grenades, shurikens, hockey sticks, UZIs, AK-47s and a whole plethora of weapons. You can choose between 3 playable characters, I think each has a unique throwable and basic weapon but I just played as MOWMAN the entire game cause he's designed to MOW DOWN ORGANIC LIFE (literally his in game description)The whole 80s action cyberpunk dystopia aesthetics are exactly what I crave and I wish there were more games like this. Each enemy faction has a unique strange twist and feels very Mad Maxx/ The Warriors.Soundtrack is fantastic and you'll love ripping through hordes of criminals to john carpenter-esque rock/synthDon't know what else to say, it's such a fantastic game and it's criminally unheard of. If you happen upon this gem of a game, BUY IT no questions ask and SWEEP THE STREETS CLEAN OF THOSE FILTHY GANGBANGERS
_childDocuments_.name: HUNTDOWN

_childDocuments_.review: I initially bought and played this on the EGS (spare me), and it rules. killer combat, tunes, sound effects, attitude, pixel art, and sheer sense of style. cannot recommend it highly enough. hell, it is so good, I bought it twice, just to have it on Steam too, which I think says enough of how great it is c:for more thoughtful recommendations of the best games on Steam, check out my curator, .
_childDocuments_.name: HUNTDOWN

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful pixel art, and has a simple and arcadey gameplay so that you can zone out and just enjoy the art and mood of the game. It veers very close to the "TOO much neo-80's" but just manages to avoid it due to the excellent production quality of all aspects of the game. Don't get me wrong, the game is 100% full of references to 80's action movies and such, and heavy on the synth and neon, but it doesn't get to the point where it feels cheap or low effort (this game is very clearly carefully crafted).
_childDocuments_.name: HUNTDOWN

_childDocuments_.review: It took me around 6 hours to complete a run on normal difficulty.The 80's style that the game is dripping with lifts it up significantly, the gameplay under the hood was decent enough though.  I'm assuming the harder difficulties will make Huntdown a little closer to Contra, as it spawns more enemies and gives you less health, though I did not dabble with it.If the 80's style looks appealing, and you like Contra/Metal Slug type games, and you don't mind the short length (Note: Harder difficulty would probably take a lot longer than 6 hours to master) then this is well worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: HUNTDOWN

_childDocuments_.review: Huntdown is fantastic! The gameplay is simple like an old arcade game, but has huge variety in levels, enemies, settings/backgrounds, music, and unique bosses. Like literally SO MANY unique mini and full sized boss fights. The bosses really feel like weird unique enemies that a devious creative GM would think of for their Cyberpunk Red or 2020 campaign. (Which brings me to my next point). While the gameplay is fun, the real MVP here is the amazing pixel graphics and super knowledgeable 80's cyberpunk references. EVERYTHING in the world would exist in a cyberpunk Red game (ttrpg) and all fits very well with older 80's sentiment around dark future, crime, and other cyberpunk themes. Can't recommend enough for fans of old arcade games and 80's cyberpunk specifically.
_childDocuments_.name: HUNTDOWN

_childDocuments_.review: One of those games where the sum of its parts exceeds the value of each individual element. gameplay is refined, the game is bloody hard, but never really seems unfair, the soundtrack and sound design is great, the graphics are just so, it's this pixel art that would never have been possible on old hardware. Love it!
_childDocuments_.name: HUNTDOWN

_childDocuments_.review: Great game in so many ways, but there are a few levels where it just feels like they had hired help instead of their A-team doing the work, with instant death pits and enemies that do 4/5 of your life in a single hit as filler rather than actually making the level more interesting.  It's bad enough I'd give this game a "maybe" instead of a yes if it was an option, but the levels that are good are fun enough to make it worth grabbing on discount.
_childDocuments_.name: HUNTDOWN

_childDocuments_.review: Perfect run and gun with that smooth 80's Bladerunner aesthetic. Satisfyingly challenging with enough variety in enemies and environments to keep you coming back. Simple but rewarding level scoring with collectables to find and challenges to beat. Each boss is unique and reflects their level design. Replay-ability is high with three different characters to play as with their own gimmicks.Just a great game all round.
_childDocuments_.name: HUNTDOWN

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful pixels. Great soundtrack, fantastic VA (fully voiced). All three bounty hunters are cool. Big guns that sound great (Anti-materiel rifle <3). Very stylish. I love this game. Easy 100% recommend.Minor cons: it's too short (but that feeling just proves how great the game is), some enemies are pretty annoying with no obvious way to counter them (jetpackers), few boss fights drag on (Ringo Road Rage) and one particular boss is a certified scumbag. You'll know which one once you meet him.
_childDocuments_.name: HUNTDOWN

_childDocuments_.review: We've just beaten the game with my bro. It took for 4 hours that we didn't expect from "run and gun" game. And It's just story mode, as we know the real deal starts in the arcade one ha-ha. Generally we're satisfied, it's rly decent arcade game from setting till gameplay. The only confusing thing which you'll have use to is friendly fire by explosive staff, what's the strange decision? xD
_childDocuments_.name: HUNTDOWN

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely incredible. Graphics touched my 16-bit heart, but the gameplay is better than most 16 bit games- this is a polished game made with love and nostalgia. Part beat-em-up, part run-n-gun, and wholly true to its ancestry, Huntdown rewards you for learning the game, slowing down, and outsmarting the challenges- I'm not a great player, but I had a great time on normal difficulty, and now I'm looking into the developer. If for no other reason, you should give these guys money so I can see what else they make.
_childDocuments_.name: HUNTDOWN

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing run-and-gun game with fast-paced gameplay that I can't recommend enough, especially if you grew up enjoying the likes of Robocop vs Terminator and Judge Dredd on the Megadrive. The pixel art is downright excellent, particularly the highly detailed backgrounds that ooze life from every pore. Heck, even the voice acting is suburb, which is something i wasn't expecting given the nature of the game. The soundtrack is the cherry on top. Yeah, I can definitely say I love this game from start to finish and only wish I had bought it sooner.
_childDocuments_.name: HUNTDOWN

_childDocuments_.review: Even though it's a bit on the short side (around 6 hours for a straight playthrough, but double that if you're out to complete everything), don't let this game's length throw you off. It's jam-packed with an amazing mix of baddies and bosses to tackle. You've got three classes to pick from, each with their own cool stock gun and special ability. And don't think it's going to be a walk in the park - nailing all three challenges in each match can get pretty tricky, even on the normal setting. Plus, the game's got some solid controller support, which is always a bonus.I snagged this gem on sale for just 4 bucks, and I've gotta say, it's a total steal. If you spot this game for less than a $10 in a sale, I'd say definitely grab it.
_childDocuments_.name: HUNTDOWN

_childDocuments_.review: Huntdown's a very nice modern-retro arcade run-and-gun with a gnarly 80s gang theme. Smooth controls and very polished overall. Mechanics and enemies somewhat limited/repetitive but great boss fights.Worth a look if you love the old 90s-era arcade run-and-guns. It's very polished and the artwork's amazing.  Gameplay's fairly basic and can get repetitive but the boss fights are excellent, worth playing just for those. Much better in co-op than solo.For more niche curation, follow me at:
_childDocuments_.name: HUNTDOWN

_childDocuments_.review: Huntdown is a cool retro action game that takes you on an exciting journey through a cyberpunk world. It's got awesome pixel art graphics and a killer synthwave soundtrack that'll transport you back in time. The gameplay is fast-paced and intense, with tight controls and satisfying shooting mechanics.However, the boss battles in Huntdown can sometimes feel a bit tedious. They can be tough and require a lot of patience. Some battles drag on and can get repetitive, which might frustrate players looking for a smoother experience.But don't let that discourage you! Huntdown's strengths outweigh its boss battle flaws. The stylish visuals, fun combat, and well-designed levels make it an enjoyable game overall. If you're up for a challenge and don't mind the occasional slog, Huntdown is definitely worth checking out.In a nutshell, Huntdown is a rad retro game with a few hiccups in its boss battles. But with its cool vibes and exciting gameplay, it's still a wild ride that's worth taking. Get ready to dive into the cyberpunk chaos of Huntdown and have a blast!
_childDocuments_.name: HUNTDOWN

_childDocuments_.review: The detailed artwork, classic game play, and quick controls made this a terrific romp. I very much could see something like this for the Saturn or Dreamcast being borderline revolutionary back in the day.However, the profanity was not helpful to the game, and if left out, this could have easily expanded its audience. I can understand trying to be 'edgy' for a cyber-punk atmosphere, but much of this dialog was hilarious, clever, and quite witty. I'm sure there would have been a creative way to write around using swear words in the voice samples.
_childDocuments_.name: HUNTDOWN

_childDocuments_.review: Huntdown is a retro style shooter in the same fashion of Contra or Metal Slug, but with many more mechanics and more complex enemies. Overall I think this might be the best game I have played in the genre.The good:+ Three different characters with different mechanics+ A good ammount of levels for a game of this kind+ An unlockable extra hard difficulty mode+ Some achievements to keep you playing a little bit more+ Multiplayer supporting remote play together+ Cool secrets in every levelThe bad:-If you make use of checkpoints and ignore the 1-life per level achievment, the game can be rather easy (at least compared to the retro games of its kind)
_childDocuments_.name: HUNTDOWN

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing. This game really takes me back--back to when videogame arcades were a thing, and most of the games had that Reagan-era "Winners Don't Do Drugs" announcement. It has all the buzz and excitement of stepping into one of those arcades, and all the retro-futuristic grit of N.A.R.C., Robocop, Final Fight, and Vigilante; but it's also a parody of them, and the wittiness and absurdity has me laughing out loud, even when I'm dying for the 12th time at the same hard as Hel checkpoint or boss. Thanks to the devs for giving me joy I haven't felt since the '80s.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game!  Timeless in style!  Flawless in execution!  Instant Classic!  Absolute must have!This game has some of the most amazing lore building and environmental story telling, which easily pulled me into the world.  It felt lived in and added to the excitement vs all of the visuals being just set pieces.  The levels, enemies, enemy placements and challenges were intelligently thought out, making for a challenging, yet fair and very VERY fun experience.Also there are some fantastic cameos from other famous cyberpunk and distopian media.  This game is an instant classic and isn't just a cash-grab play on the cyberpunk/distopia genre, but is a very VERY well polished and crafted experience!

_childDocuments_.review: This is going to be a weird review...but it is hard to really describe an experience with this game. I sampled it on Switch a while back, and have been waiting for a good sale to get it. Obviously that sale came or i wouldn't be playing and reviewing the game.When i stepped into this review, I thought: what makes this a good game? What could be done better? Why would I give it a thumbs up? What let me down?And that is where I ran into a problem....I really can't answer those questions in an effective way.But that is ok....because if you were to ask me the same thing about a game like Contra, I would be the same. Is Contra a masterpiece because of its difficulty? Or because of the weapon options? Or the level design? Really is it all of these together, but done subtle enough that the game just comes off fun?And that is what Huntdown does.it is like Contra + NARC + Blackthorne together in one game. And it is put together so perfectly that you can feel each ones influence, but it becomes its own thing.So if you are looking for something like: This game is fantastic because of the way the physics for aiming and recoil is built from the ground up to take into realistic blah blah blah...you aren't going to get it.Huntdown is fun because it just is. It isn't trying to redefine your gaming experience. it is molding all the good into one solid game where you can't single out a specific thing. Everything just works well together seamlessly.You are probably thinking I wrote a lot and said nothing. Or did I actually say enough and it looks like nothing? If you are not sure after reading this review, then define the greatness of the first Contra...and why to this day it is still loved. You are looking at a game that could be just as loved 15 or 20 years down the line. So get Huntdown.
_childDocuments_.name: HUNTDOWN

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an absolute masterpiece and a total joy to play if you're a fan of classic run n' guns like Contra, Metal Slug, etc. The audio and visual presentation has far more life than most contemporary AAA games and the boss battles are so good they reminded me of Gunstar Heroes and Contra: Hard Corps but a bit less predictable. The shooting and cover mechanics are flawlessly done and the three different playable bounty hunters have a nice variety of unique weaponry and great one-liners. Getting 100% and beating it on Badass Mode is difficult but well worth the effort, especially once you master some of the exploits in each stage. My sole criticism of this otherwise perfect game is that there's no online co-op and it's handled through the iffy remote play system if you're not playing couch co-op. Other than that, this might be the best run n' gun released since Shattered Soldier and I highly recommended it unless you're averse to challenging games.

_childDocuments_.review: If you ever wanted to play a Contra clone with superb pixel graphics, a rocking 80s synth score, oodles of B movie personality and just the right amount of challenge, look no further.Some knock Huntdown for its short length. I'm gonna paraphrase something I read years ago: I'd rather take a memorable 5 hour game over a 50 hour UbiSoft open world slogfest any day.Others might not like that this game follows the Megaman rule of 2D shooting, in that you can only aim left and right. The game is designed in such a way that you don't need to aim in more than 2 directions to win.And what design! 20 levels that never drag on too long, each ending with a unique and fun boss battle. There are 3 achievements for each level that add replay value. If you're really daring, you can play arcade mode, which throws out the balance of the main story mode in favor of tons of baddies and finite lives.Not to mention this game's personality, which I can't stress enough. Each playable character has countless one-liners. There are tons of references to cyberpunk movies of the late 20th century. The voice acting is ace, especially for the announcer, who sounds like he's imitating Don LaFontaine. This game does not take itself seriously, as it should; it's a throwback to early arcade shoot 'em ups that were all about style and edge. I'd buy that for a dollar!
_childDocuments_.name: HUNTDOWN

_childDocuments_.review: Never been a fan of 2d shooters but this one changed that. Gameplay, although simple, challenges you with complex -but never unfair- boss patterns. Now, what really make his game, is it's style, aesthetics and well crafted universe; a perfect blend of 80s cyberpunk and nostalgic references (from Blade Runner to The Last Dragon and everything in beteween). The nostalgic world is concieved in excelent pixel art paired with a fantastic OST (synthwave) and good sound desing. To people that like 2d shooters this is certainly a solid 8; to people that also like 80s cyberpunk it's an easy 10.

The only thing that changes is their starting weapon and their utility item. You pick up secondary guns which have limited ammo. Could be a baseball bay or a guitar, or it could be a rocket launcher or gatling gun. Grenade items can be picked up and replace your utility until you're out of ammo. I've only seen half the game, there are "worlds" which feature a different gang and increasing in difficulty from easy to very hard. If you like side scrollers, this is worth your time. _childDocuments_.review: A pretty enjoyable but somewhat difficult side scrolling shooter.Pros- Great selection of sound effects and music, it's like being back in the 90s again playing Contra 3.- Excellent variety of weapons and enemies, keeps you on your toes and gives some small room for player expression.- Playable characters are charming and as a fellow 80s kid, highly appreciated the little references dropped during gameplay.- Movement overall felt smooth, liked the idea of the dodge and being able to do that from the air was a good touch.Cons- Late game difficulty felt a bit lopsided, I understand increasing the challenge so that the player doesn't become comfortable but the last 2-3 stages were simply not enjoyable despite having some rather interesting bosses.- Having a cover mechanic frankly felt weird, it was generally fine except for the one or two instances you were actively punished for using it instead of simply air dashing to attack at close range.- A more explicit section in the "how to play" explaining how the dodging mechanic works. It seemed consistent against gunfire but against some attacks appeared to be unavoidable which doesn't sit right with me, same goes with the slide.- An autofire option for your default pistol would have been nice, my fingers would definitely appreciated it if there was a sequel or spinoff released.Tl;drPick up this game on sale if you like Metal Slug/Contra style with some added replayability thanks to the different difficulties mode and clear challenges (Took me about 3 hours to complete on the Second difficulty setting, first playthrough).

_childDocuments_.review: Huntdown is an amazing Cyberpunk-oriented game where you play as a band of bounty hunters out to lay vigilante justice for society. Taking down ragtag bunches of criminal gangs in a very dystopian future.This game is fun as hell and I praise it for having a very digestible pace in the gameplay. You have your stages that are littered with small bosses that represent each gang you'll be up against, providing their own fair share of enemies reflecting their members. It will take you under a couple minutes to confront the boss, it's really that quick and depending on your expertise, you could readily beat this game in short order.The visuals is fantastically well detailed for pixels, capturing that cyberpunk aesthetic we all love and adore. The music accommodates along with it, grabbing and pulling you into it's settings. Huntdown simply just oozes with character.You owe it to yourself to give this game a try if everything Huntdown advertises gives you an itch to experience what it has to offer. It's quite a gem to be found. It's so good, I actually bought the game twice on two different platforms.

_childDocuments_.review: NOT IRONIC -- NOT RETRO -- ACTUALLY BADASSThis game is not a nostalgia trap, you're not paying to go down memory lane and have a laugh. There are funny parts in the game, and it obviously apes some of the future-retro-whatever vibes, but in every aspect the love and care Easy Trigger Games poured into it outshines the "jokes".Huntdown is is better than old games, and new ones. If this had come out in 1997 arcades it would be world famous as one of the CLASSICS, but unfortunately the market for it has shrunk as people forget that this is a legitimate genre. It deserves the "Overwhelmingly Positive" reviews as far as I can tell.It is tough, but checkpoints are fairly distributed. The game does allow different "styles" of play, even though the levels are laid out with a certain logic. Picked up a cool weapon? Don't waste it on the losers, swap it into your backpack and save it for later, you may need it. Found some cover? Don't run around like a fool and act like it's brainless. If you do run around, make sure you also slide, dash, and throw your secondary weapons enough to create havoc.I haven't played a lot, and I've only played single player, but I beat the first entire level and I can confirm that the mechanics are rock solid, the weapon selection is fun, and its presentation is slick. You just become a better player and choose a harder difficulty if you think you're a badass.*PRO TIP: If you're like me and hate screen shake, you can turn it down in the options. So glad devs are including this.*

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty fun game! Variety of schlock, 80s and 90s pop culture references. Weapon variety is rather fun as well.Admittedly, even on normal, toward the end enemies go from fun and challenging to feeling a little bullet spongey. Takes what was a frenetic, aciton packed arcade experience into a different sort of game.Now, I loved Blackthorne, but that game had a deliberate pace to its gun play. _childDocuments_.review: Run and Gun has never been a genre I've played so I wasn't sure what I was getting myself into with this, but man this game is something special. The best way to describe Huntdown is Metal Slug with some cover elements, though that would be doing the game disservice since it is so much more than that. The graphics are beautiful, some of the best pixel art I've seen in a while, the story is fairly interesting though not that amazing, but this is because it is supplementing the gameplay. The gameplay is simple and yet it's a joy to play, the controls are tight and fluid, running through levels hiding behind cover and swapping between guns is incredibly fun, not to mention the voice acting from the main characters and the enemies giving the game a very fun vibe. There are bosses at the end of each level and they typically are very fun, not every one hits home, but they all bring something new to the table which can be said for the whole game, every world has it's own gimmicks and general feel to it making the experience very fresh. The game isn't long, it'll probably take you less than 6 hours on a first playthrough if you're good, but that's because the game wants you to replay it on harder difficulties and go for 100%, mastering each character and each level is really a great experience if you have the patience for it (though extremely difficult later on but never completely unreasonable) so I'd recommend at least trying, it's how you get the most out of the game. The only actual criticism I have isn't even with the game, it is quite obvious the dialogue wasn't written in English, and while the localization is great most of the time, there are some lines that are obviously translated weirdly, but it doesn't harm the overall experience. If you couldn't tell so far I highly recommend playing this game if any of what I said interests you, it is insanely cheap for the quality and time you can get out of it, and based on a Youtube search, not enough people know about this indie gem.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is kind of like a slightly slower paced Contra, with funny Duke Nukem jokes (as the metal-jaw character), and a retro theme that pays homage to 80s~90s games & movies. You can shoot, duck, dash, and air dash (down, and diagonal down in the air). You can pick up an assortment of limited weapons to use (ranged, melee, and explosives), with unlimited use of your main ranged weapon and special move. Has two player co-op. Enemies will often talk ♥♥♥♥, but the playable characters, especially the metal-jaw guy, have funnier/wittier comebacks. The game has a checkpoint system that is very forgiving on normal story mode, and it also saves your progress after each stage. Is it fun? Abso-♥♥♥♥♥♥-lutely. If you like games like Contra or Mega Man, you'll probably dig this. I cannot think of any flaws, this game is perfect. A gem that should be in your collection, and worth every penny. Get it.

_childDocuments_.review: Depends on what kind of player you are.If you like pixel style, you like retro horizontal action games, you don't hate cyberpunk style, you like 80s sci-fi action movies, you have to play, you can't miss.As a reminder, characters can only shoot left and right, not up or diagonally, and there are no training elements. But I don't think it's a weakness. Because like board games, the point is that the rules are well-developed, self-contained, and fun.I think the jumping, dodging, melee system and maps combine well in this game. BOSS fights are also in the good tradition of old arcade games -- even memorizing levels requires concentration, hand-eye coordination, and even a certain amount of patience.Games are pixelated, the style of the levels varies greatly, and there are very few repetitive elements. 20 bosses, full of sincerity.As soon as you start playing, the details of those old movies come up, but it's hard to put together a list of the movies this game pays tribute to.I love it.From China.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't say enough good things about this game.You've probably heard already it's a Contra-like shooter. That's true, but it's so much more. Unlike Contra, the levels have tons of variety. The environments change, new enemies come, a new weapon drops, an NPC antagonizes you; the levels never feel repetitive and all the bosses are mechanically unique.Gun play is fun, and the assorted weapons have the weighty impact we'd expect from a rifle or grenade launcher. It's everything you'd want from a run-and-gun shooter. While some enemies can be difficult, nothing seems cheap or unfair, and if you plan your actions all damage can be avoided.And this is without even discussing the 80s cyberpunk aesthetic they've completely nailed here. Everything from punk gangs, Verhoeven movies, Blade Runner, one-liners, blaxploitation movies, Kung-Fu; this game has it all. All the sprites look incredibly, and the game cutscenes some how manage to be both old-fashioned and gorgeous. Voice acting is excellent for all the bosses, each has their own unique but carcicaturized personality.On Normal Difficulty you are probably looking at around 4 hours here, but Normal is pretty forgiving. For the experienced players "Badass" mode is the hardest, not even allowing a single hit before restarting at a Checkpoint. And the ultimate challenge? 3-medaling Badass mode, which means no checkpoints, all secret stash items, and all kills. This would be a monumental feat and likely lead to a lot of controller throwing, but it's for masochist only.If I had any quibbles it's the lack of anything to do outside the campaign. Arcade mode is simply the standard levels with a score instead; it's not especially unique. But what you get for your money is still very worth it and I highly recommend Huntdown.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Potentially the best side-scrolling shooter there is. (Also, why are you reading reviews if you don't want to read reviews?)if you're into SIDE-SCROLLING OLD-SCHOOL ACTION GAMES, this is as good (and I believe better) than it gets. I don't like the "11/10" cliche, I think it's hugely overused and un-creative, I think it dumbs down criticism to an embarrassing degree sometimes. but . . . this game hits every mark it tries to hit, it succeeds on every level it was going for and more. it's FUN, FUNNY, CHALLENGING, WITTY, GOOFY, FAST, SLOW AND TACTICAL. it's obviously made with such JOY that it's infectious as hell. okay, how's about this: this game, and only this game, made me take a look at "DEEP ROCK GALACTIC", as it had the same publisher, Coffee Stain. and DRG is absolutely *amazing*, another absolute ringer. To whoever made this game, THANK YOU. it's not just one of the best I've played in my 2018 - Current middle-aging return to gaming, I will absolutely say it's one of the best games I've ever played. and calling it "Great" on some dumber, lower "Action Schlock" genre is a total disservice. this game is DUMB ACTION SCHLOCK done SURGICALLY perfect. it never takes your intelligence or time for granted, it never wastes your time or your energy, and I bought it for less than SIX CANADIAN DOLLARS while on sale (AGAIN, this is my SECOND PURCHASE AND PLATFORM for this game), so about 6% of the amount I'd pay for "Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2 Part II", which I haven't played, but is virtually assured to be WAY lower on quallity, craft and care. way lower. they may have the budget, they do NOT have the PASSION. absolutely absurd old-school action platformer shooter thing. it's at least as good as any other indie game out there. I can't say enough good about it, so I'll quit now.

_childDocuments_.review: Am only sorry I've taken this long to finally play this. But there are lots of these retro titles around and it's really tricky for developers to make a modern game in that pocket that people actually want to play now.But here we have a truly beautiful mix of sound, image and gameplay. It's not just copying Blade Runner (movie) elements on to a dull game, which far too many of these are.They've got voice actors here, great animations, and a soundtrack that is like The Terminator (movie) in the best possible way. Nice shades of Escape from New York (movie) too, especially with this setting.The influence pool is wide; in terms of gameplay it has a feel of that rapid fire splatting you get in RoboCop versus The Terminator on the Genesis/Mega Drive. Shades of Flashback because it's future shooting with good animation. Some Bitmap Brothers style choices. But actually it's more a of a coin-op feel to it, thinking NARC 1989 cabinet.Aesthetically, it's all about trying to get to 2000 AD (comic), that's what RoboCop (movie) was doing and so games had a massive injection of all of that in the era Huntdown pays tribute to. I think the only thing which was taken in more by games in the late 80's and early 90's was Aliens (movie)... the poster for which is in here, along with Akira and The Thing. And there's Gremlins here too :DSo yeah, floppy discs, synth, irreverent humour and the villains are punks... if that formula were easy to get right, Huntdown wouldn't be as good as it is. But it nails it, head and shoulders above most that try it - hope the team behind this do some more
