_childDocuments_.review: Anyone who has worn out their copies of every XCOM game, as I have, knows there is not a wealth of new games in the genre. I appreciate what the Romeros are trying to bring to the table with Empire of Sin, but for now the game falls short in core aspects of execution. Hopefully, this will someday be a game that I feel gives me my money's worth. 2/5 stars.Last month I bought and completed Hard West, a game I greatly enjoyed for its combat mechanics and level design. A few days after my interest in HW ran its course, I saw Empire of Sin in the store. It seemed to promise a lot of the things I loved about games like XCOM and HW, but with an innovative scalable strategy layer and an emergent narrative based on 1920's Prohibition Chicago. Being a Paradox game I somewhat expected it to come out half-baked with a ton of issues, but this is a rare effort at an XCOM competitor and Paradox are generally good about supporting games for a long time.I hope that continued support is the case here, because the tactical gameplay in this game gets old very quickly. At the outset the game shows a ton of promise, in 3 attempts at starting a campaign so far my favorite part each time was the solo missions at the beginning. The "boss" character of your gang really lives up to this name, and taking down 5 or 8 enemy thugs in just a few turns is a great introduction to the combat system. After taking over a few rackets, earning a few made henchmen, then assaulting a rival gang's safehouse to overpower their leader and seize their territory, you can really immerse in the game's promise of being a criminal overlord with an empire.What follows is where the game becomes bogged down in itself. Running multiple gang wars when you own a sprawling empire is an exercise in tedium. Your racket guards are hopelessly inept at lower levels, and when a racket is raided by the enemy you're ripped away from your boss character and are stuck controlling "60 hp woman with lead pipe" or "55 hp man with short-barreled shotgun", typically against an equally inept force of random enemy thugs. Then, when your guards lose you immediately get to repeat the experience inside your racket.The tedious gang wars also highlight the repetitiveness of the different buildings. Each building can be "small", "medium" or "large" and the interiors of each racket type do not vary much. So, in a short span the game goes from being a very enjoyable stint as the baddest guy in town, to fighting through a hopeless slog with no-name characters in the same environments over, and over, and over. This is not an enjoyable experience for a turn-based shooter.The strategy layer provides more scale than depth, which would certainly be forgivable if the combat sequence was more engaging. Owning 30+ rackets in a neighborhood, each with 20+ upgrade levels, with 10 neighborhoods as default, quickly becomes a chore when the ultimate outcome is that each time you make slightly more profit or the guard battles become slightly less tedious due to upgrades. Immediate improvements to the tactical layer that I would suggest are:-Make the player character and their made men essential to the core game mechanic: turn-based tactics. It is not as enjoyable to fight battles where they are not involved, and these should be automated 100% of the time. It might be workable to give the player a way for responding to such events, such as posting made men at the neighborhood safehouse and having them immediately respond to help the guards against any raids in that neighborhood.-Make combat involvement mostly line-of-sight based rather than area based. Having a random group of thugs in an alley around the block or a faraway policeman become mandatory elements of combat because they were within X tiles of the ambush is never an enjoyable surprise.-The controls sequence for fighting battles with a controller is not intuitive to work through, and sometimes limits player options compared to KB+M. In my opinion, XCOM: Chimera Squad is the gold standard of intuitive controller support in the tactical layer and I think it would be a good thing if this game had a similar controls sequence.-Speaking of XCOM:CS, their breach system was a fantastic innovation in the genre. I think that a similar mechanic for raids in Empire of Sin would provide a sorely-needed breath of fresh air to the short roster of interior combat environments. Breaching from outside in would also help solve the disconnect between the outdoor and indoor environments in this game, which at present feel like different worlds (see: no-name guard battle progression).

_childDocuments_.review: I know, I have 300+ hours on a game I don't recommend. It's cause I'm a sucker for steam achievements.PROS: - I like the combat itself. I think I may just like tactical RPGs, though, since I haven't played a lot of them. - The period details are nice, they definitely did their research on the storefronts, weapons, etc (not so much on the factions, as half of them are fictional). - The equipment system is very RPG-like and works well.- The boss fights are satisfying, fun, and challenging. CONS: oh boy, I've thought about these for a while. Essentially, Empire of Sin doesn't know what it wants to be. - It seems to be leaning towards a tactical RPG since that's what the combat is, but once you play you realize you have to employ 4X tactics to actually win. Maybe 4X is a bit inaccurate, since you can't really "expand" peacefully; somebody has to die, but when it's thug rackets that don't pose any actual danger to you it might as well be. The problem with this isn't that it's mixing genres, but combining lots of combat with how granular squad-based combat is makes the game extremely tedious. You're going to be taking over about 30 or so thug rackets, none of them are going to be remotely challenging, and it's going to be boring once you've seen the handful of building designs they have for each size racket, if not before.- The 4X nature of the gameplay gets worse when you realize there's only one way to win: the equivalent of a domination victory. Even the original Civilization in '91 let you win the space race if you didn't want to nuke everyone. Sure, you can buy factions out if you're protecting them, but this leads to a lot of thumb-twiddling while you save up the cash and have to do dumb stuff to get them to like you. You also won't be considered enough of a threat to get protection from until you've killed at least three bosses in vanilla (I only had to kill one when I played with Make It Count).- So in other words, you are going to be fighting a lot of barbarians (thugs) and other factions. And it's going to get boring. Really boring, really fast. I get that any kind of strategy game is going to have a degree of repetition when you've got multiple factions to play as, and that's not necessarily an issue. But in Empire of Sin there's really no reason I should be fighting this many battles where no one is taking damage, it's just a waste of time. I believe they foresaw this and added the "auto-battle" feature, which would be nice if it didn't massively underrate how likely you are to win a fight and required saving before/after to avoid a game over.- The game plays out almost exactly the same every time. Sure, the bosses have different abilities that are mostly pointless (we'll get to that later), but what you're doing is the same every time. You're killing a few bosses (or all of them), you're buying the Golden Tommy Gun, you're hiring Norah Quinn because you have to have a doctor, etc. Nothing changes but the layout of the neighborhoods, which may be of minor tactical importance but is ultimately nbd. Let's look at some other strategy games: In Civilization and EU4 (New World), you can randomize the map so resources and strategic points are different every time. You can't do this in Crusader Kings, but the game world is so vast that playing in sub-Saharan Africa is completely different from playing in the Mediterranean which is completely different from playing in Siberia. There's also different eras you can start in. Something like this is BADLY needed to preserve replay value.- The side quests are way, way, way too easy. Talk to your crew member, kill a guy in a completely pointless, one-sided battle (sometimes you don't even have to do this), collect a few thousand bucks. Probably takes less than five minutes even if you read all the dialogue. The only ones that are a little better are the boss quest lines, which are both more challenging and more interesting story-wise, but there's still maybe on the level of a randomly generated Skyrim fetch-quest.- There are probably dozens of mechanics that just do. not. matter. at. all. I almost feel bad saying this because I'm sure some poor Irishmxn or two probably spent months coding these but here's a short list: honor, hunkering down, brothels, BOP raids, Chicago PD raids, alcohol storage, morale, loyalty, gangster roles, neighborhood lieutenants, the gangster rating system, any of the gangsters that cost more than $3-4K to hire (about half), gangsters hating/loving each other, the "worried" status effect, and temporary business arrangements. A lot of these things feel sophisticated until you realize they don't matter at all; it almost feels like the team that came up with them had a different vision entirely and thought this was more of a sandbox strategy than what it was.Conclusion: not worth it in its current state. There's definitely some solid potential here, and I think a fun sequel could be made if they ditched all the higher-level strategy (neighborhoods, weekly income, rackets, precincts) focused on boss fights and actually doing something challenging in the quests, but I think you'd also have to ditch the whole multiple playable factions thing. Make it more like GTA or Mafia but a tactical RPG, and make it absolutely nothing like Civ.

_childDocuments_.review: So this game has alot of promise. As with most paradox games I am excited to see how it flushes itself out over the next few years.Right now I would say there is a balance issue as far as the economy goes. There is a depth there for the player who wants to go in and flush it all out and make a min/max approach to a small area.  But really for my first play through I just hammered at size over quality and suffered no real draw backs from it.The combat systems weak point when talking about balance is centered around the ambush ability in street fights, it allows for a rude combo when used with mabel. The fights are a bit of a grind, but seem quick enough once you have a solid combo working. I want to see more events, and a change in the UI when it comes to quests. but overall no game breaking bugs, (a couple crashes related to the revenge perk when triggered, and the game once deleted my boss some how but a quick reload and all was well)Visually it is a pretty game, I enjoy the sound track and feel of the city.it looks like there is an option to play as a anti hero in some ways, where you can gain access to the cops but I had no luck in getting to that point. _childDocuments_.review: I think it has a lot of potential, but it needs work. My biggest gripe is during a gang war when your establishments get attacked one after the other. A lead pipe is the best available weapon for a gang controlling several districts of Chicago?The combat has issues. Sometimes the enemy fighters just move and move again to better positions, running straight past suitable targets and never firing a shot even as they are slowly killed. Another problem with the building attack is that the game just picks up your characters and the enemy's characters and basically chucks then up in the air. Where they land, that's where they are when the fight starts.  So you can easily have one of your team in a room with two or three enemies, which is just stupid.A lot of potential, but it's a typical modern Paradox product, superficially full of options but very shallow below the surface.

_childDocuments_.review: Empire of Sin.... a 1920's prohibition / mafia themed, x-com-like strategy game that has a lot of potential but at the time of this review (about 39 hours of play time) I simply cannot recommend the game in it's current state. This game should have released into Early Access. The cons at this timely, simply outweigh the pros.Pros :- Game looks nice and plays smoothly- Mafia theme- Varied characters to choose as your boss / avatar- Nice variety of weapons- Gangster Roster - plenty of minor characters to choose from as your hired thugs- Music / Soundtrack really fits the themeCons :- Too many bugs and glitches for a full release- Unbalanced abilities - Repetitive combat at times when the AI attacks and you have to complete fight after fight- Game mechanics too bare bones- AI needs working on- Mission / quests badly paced outThis game has only been out for a couple of weeks but really needs some patching. Fun enough to play, assuming you can get past all it's current faults. Current recommendation : wait for a sale and/or for the game to be fully patched / updated before buying.Rating : 5/10 Average (but on the bit disppointing side).POST PATCH :  Devs have done some work to this game so it's time to change my review a bit :Pros : - Safe Houses are now hidden and you can't bum rush your rivals any more :)- A lot of the quests seem to work fine now- The "loot boxes" you can find all over the map have been re-balanced and are more rare- 12 different 'skins' for all the generic thugs makes for a better experience, rather than all 1 generic type- weapons and bosses have been nerfed a bit and difficulties have been adjusted- Ability to skip 'non essential' fights- Guards get better 'upgrades' for each upgrade levelCons :- Rackets are still a bit bare bones - need more variety- Animations of the in game models still bug out from time to time- Quests still seem to be assigned all together 'in a bunch' rather than spaced out more- Some bugs for first version of the game still persisting- AI still needs some workOverall, the new patch shows alot of promise. I hope the devs continue supporting and working on this game. It definately has improved since launch, but there still is a fair amount to do for it to be a truly GREAT game.New Rating : 6 / 10 - still wait for a sale or for further patching,

_childDocuments_.review: The boss I picked has an ability that lets him run to someone and perform 3 melee strikes; if he gets a kill his AP is refunded and he gets a pretty serious stacking movement/melee skill debuff.  Despite the debuff, I can pretty much always use the ability twice in a row at the start of every fight and instakill two enemies with it.  Once I got him a blue machine gun, I could then blow away a third guy with his refunded AP, no matter where he ends up.  This means every single fight starts with me doing the exact same thing with my boss which gets me 3 kills on one turn 99% of the time.  This tends to leave my boss standing out in the open somewhere, but since he has 2-3 times as much health as everyone else and the generic thugs are incredibly weak and stupid (even on hard difficulty), this doesn't actually matter.  Of course, once a gang war started, I did get to start playing fights where my properties were attacked and I had to fight back with 2-3 generic-ass boring guards, which was even worse.  Seriously, these generic guards can't get above like 55% hit chance even under optimal conditions, which means your generic thugs and the enemy's generic thugs just sit there and blast away at each other for 10 minutes.  Boring.I think this game has a lot of potential and if they hit it with some patches that improve it I will revise this review, but right now the business management part is confusing and not very rewarding, the RPG management is wonky, the UI is clunky and hard to navigate, and the tactical combat is repetitive and easy.

_childDocuments_.review: Is this the spiritual successor to Omerta city of gangsters? I'd hoped it would be.Well it added almost everything missing from Omerta;- Expansive Maps (which are very pretty)- Multiple factions- Diplomacy- Relations between charactersBut unfortunately it is missing almost everything else a now seven year old game will offer you.The business side of the game is about as strategic as FarmVille. All the upgrades to business are a simple linear progression and there is little to no synergy between businesses or options to different strategies.The dialogue between bosses is slow and clumsy. Dialogue options often consist of antagonistic comment or a different antagonistic comment, but down worry there is nothing to indicate your choices have any effect on relations with other bosses.The combat mechanics are fine when compared to other squad based games of the past decade, but no improvements of innovations. However it’s averageness is let down by;- Random placement of characters at the beginning of encounters.- Bosses so poorly balanced that you can often kill only enemies before they get a turn.- Diplomacy and trade is shallow and often useless in seeking victory.- Very few maps for combat encounters make for repetitive game play.- Enemy npc’s have little variation and make already repetitive even worse.The game is currently also very buggy, about 20% of missions have glitched out and I’ve not been able to complete them.TLDR: Buy Omertà, it’s a unfinished seven year old game that’s in better shape than this.

_childDocuments_.review: High Buggy & Unbalanced Game is good . Keeping negative review because I'm tired of the ♥♥♥♥ game launches with patches to fix games. It is getting old.There still isn't a 2nd DLC. I bought the premium edition and was promised 2 post-launch DLCs. Only one has come out. It's been over 2 years. Guess this is an example of why you shouldn't pre-purchase games and content even from developers and/or publishers you trust. Unacceptable.The game seems pretty good after the launch of their first DLC. I considered updating my review to recommend Empire of Sin; however, I am tired of games launching like crap and then players having to wait for a decent game. For that reason alone, I am keeping it as "Would Not Recommend". The gameplay is pretty good now though.Patch 1.03 is in beta right now and it seems to have completely changed the flow of the game. Many of the bugs and exploits have been fixed and I'm enjoying it quite a bit more now. This should have been the launch state of the game, I am growing tired of video games launching it a crap state and then patching it out months later. You want your money? Give me a quality game from the start.1. Battle will start, but the first character's turn will never begin. Game and save breaking.2. Animation bugs where a character will be stuck in the shooting and downed pose. When animation bugs occur the time to take an action increases dramatically.3. Occasionally, you won't be able to attack a building. You confirm when prompted and it just sits there.4. Hotel Synergies go all crazy sometimes. I've had to SELL a racket to get all of the synergies before.5. Battles don't end when you kill the last enemy if 2 friendly factions are at war with each other.6. Death animations do weird things when using melee attacks.7. Sometimes the UI shows an action unavailable (no color) like you don't have action points, when you're full action points and can execute the action anyways.EDIT: I just want to say, this game was the first game I received all of the achievements. It is incredibly unbalanced, resulting in a strategy game that requires no strategy.1. AI will accept absurd trades. There are a lot of exploits that stem from this issue.2. You can trade for the AI faction's unique weapons and they'll never equip another one, leaving them weaponless in battle.3. Quick travel takes no time. This allows you to explore the whole map, meet all of the factions, and collect all hidden stashes in one in-game week.4. Stashes are on the map from the start of the game. This makes the game trivial. Collect a few good stashes, equip your team, kill every enemy. Why interact with rackets, synergies, trade-deals, or quests?5. Healing can be done instantly by quick travel to safehouse, which costs nothing. It can also be done using skills by starting an ambush, using healing skill, cancelling ambush, and repeating. This makes the doctor passive heal pointless.6. Weapon type traits can be earned by accumulating kills and thugs are crazy easy to kill and plentiful.7. Rifles shadow sniper rifles by doing similar damage for 1 AP instead of 2 AP. Same with Submachine guns and Machine guns. Shotguns spead shot has the same accuracy and damage as the single-target shot. Why even have a single-target shot? Just use the multi-target one every time.8. Explosives (excluding time-bomb) have no counter-play. Spawn into a fight, enemy gets their first turn, throws bomb into the pack where you spawned and you've lost multiple gangsters. All explosives should be timed or not an instant-kill.9. Better gang members shouldn't cost notoriety AND money. By the time you can hire the better gangsters, you've already trained up your cheap gangsters to be very strong. Additionally, 10% income cost is insane enough, but another $30,000-$70,000 on top of that? Never going to be worth it.1. No window-borderless option in 2020. Single person made early access games even have this.2. The hotkeys are dynamic and it screws me up constantly. One minute the [3] key is swap weapon, the next minute [4] is swap weapon and [3] is reload. This screws me up CONSTANTLY. Please make these static.3. The Escape key unpausing the game is annoying. I'm just trying to bring the menu up to save and you unpause it and then something always manages to pop-up at that very second. Let me bring up the menu while paused.1. Repetitive dialog option variety. I am tired of hearing Al Capone say "What's this a free lunch?" I don't need variety for everything, but the dialog options that are common, like making a deal, should have some variety.2. Thugs are all the same, weak and boring. Add more enemy types, both graphically and mechanically. They don't have to be strong, since they're thugs, but at least have them do something different.3. I would like to see more depth added to mechanics around rackets. Hotel synergy is nice when it works. Add more things like this.4. No more DLC weapons. Those things are OP and I would love an option to make them basic guns instead of legendary, aka basically a weapon skin instead.I'm going to keep playing this game. It can be enjoyable, but commonly comes with frustration. Please fix the bugs and balance!

_childDocuments_.review: Empire of Sin: Badaboom.Way back in the day of the forgotten PC demo, I played the snot out of Omerta: City of Gangsters. A clunkmaster of a game pushed out by Kalypso that died on the vine. But I did always like the concept of a game where you manage a criminal empire with XCOM stolen turned based combat. However the management was just Monopoly with extra steps and the turned based combat was jank. How do you fix a problem like that?John Romero, apparently. And giving the game about half a year to iron out the issues it had on launch.Empire of Sin is half crime syndicate management and half turned based combat where the game itself has a story that stretches for maybe half an hour and the rest is spent pummeling the AI for constantly starting gang wars with you. It hits the clicky part of my brain where I get sucked in and start slowly encroaching upon every district of Chicago and by the time I snap out of it, I have three districts on lock and it's 11:43 at night. I don't know how I got to this point but I certainly got there.It's not perfect. It still has the Omertas problem with the strategy starting to peter out by the late game. Once you get to a certain point, you don't have to worry about raids or anything and you have money to burn so you just buy and make criminal syndicates for funsies. Turned based combat is at least better with actual classes and weapons to choose from, and even the Rare guns aren't going to keep you from getting clapped if you aren't careful. The only con I can see is a lack of being able to drag your goons into fights, meaning you rely on the Black Book list of expensive hires to fill the blanks. And while I like the whole "like/hate" system requiring you to think before hiring 5 new expendable pawns, I'd like them to stop forming love triangles every 10 seconds. My criminal empire shouldn't entirely fall apart because of someone screwing someone else.If you want a good way to kill weekday nights and want to play a game that's half Monopoly and half XCOM with more jazz music and art deco everything, then Empire of Sins is your go-to game here. I would wait for it to go on sale however, as is the rules with any Paradox property. I'm glad it's at least now more functional then it was on launch, but still.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm quite sad to not recommend this game.I could not rate it and just stay silent, but honestly, this game, as it is and probably will stay forever, is rather bloated and lame with very shallow gameplay mechanics, almost without any substance besides sheer size of the world map. I've been a big fan of Gansters 2, which is many years old.I can't comprehend how they could have messed this up so badly in comparison.The whole game is more of an atmoshperic slide show with some minimalistic turn based battles in the same environments over and over and some repetitive, generic and lame economic fiddling.Everything feels isolated, game mechanics do not multiply, it has no flesh on the bones, it feels uninspired, it feels like the person in charge does not even bother with gameplay but aims for some success metrics in some rather 1 dimensional cognitive model.That resulted in throwing some cool assets in a stylish setting with some adequate voice acting and well made music at the player.Maybe they are hoping players imagination takes over and will make up for the missing mechanics because everything sounds and feels so cool ?Imo nope, this does not work or not for long at least. As soon as you realize there is nothing more besides learning some simple routines, it looses all of its charm and becomes just annoying.The current version is the best iteration so far, some annoying disruptions and triggers where adjusted or removed, constraints on economics where adjusted.Overall not very much has really changed in regard to core gameplay loops and interdependent mechanisms that could give a feel of accomplishment, challenge, progress or even a slight sparkle of the feeling of a living world with real feedback that captures the player.The game world itself shouts "I'm so stylish and elaborate" very loud but the game itself is rather void below it's artistic user interface. Honestly, do yourself a big favor after reading this words and skip this. For the future wait until a real game designer takes over, e.g. John himself, because i doubt that he was in charge of this shallow experience.I bought it, because I "worship" this man and his legacy. But he should not allow something like this to happen in his vicinity with his name put on the package and so on ...Sad and hard to understand. Sure it is an accomplishment and it could be worse, but what are legends good for, if they deliver at best mediocre, shallow asset showcases which run as executables and clue together minimalistic mechanics with some realtime rendering, some menus, some sound queueing a.s.o ... It is sad, that something obviously crippled this game. Maybe my assumptions regarding overall design failure is wrong, maybe other reasons compromissed the dev lifecycle, maybe it is exactly they game they wanted to make ?!Idk and in the end I gave my money and do not really care what happens to this game anymore, it does not seem to change substancially in any realistic future scenario as I strongly doubt they invest the resources in remaking their own game. I also doubt they will do better in the next iteration, because if you listen to what they say, they seem to focus on everything but not the real problems of this game. Just my take on this. If you like the style and it is cheap, or you love John and don't care, get it =)

_childDocuments_.review: Edited after more time in game..THIS IS NOT A 1920's gangster Sim, this is a Modern take of what the 20's could have been.Pros: Gameplay is pretty solid. I enjoy the fights and the abilities of my team.Beautiful and detailed cityInteresting Bosses and Gangsters to hireEvery character is well rounded and has a backstory.They put in a huge amount of time developing and creating a large pool of gangsters (and bosses) to hire (with backstories, likes and dislikes.). Almost half of which are female. more than a third 1/3 roughly are minorities (by todays definition of the word.) Everyone is very well represented. There are even LGBTQ+ gangsters that you can hire.  Also, I've had many instances of same sex relationships forming between my shooters in my gang. Cons:There are still a lot of bugs and balancing issues.AI is ...special. From walking back and forth between points for no good reason during combat, wasting obvious combat opportunities and general weird behavior, Its obvious that its bad AI and is immersion breaking.You can never have the Mob family by 1920's idea of gangs.This is by far the most heartbreaking meta issue I have with this game. The ethnic gangs of the time were formed for a reason. It would have been awesome if they would have used this game as an opportunity to point out the faults of the era and the resulting violence and why we need to come together.  It would have been timely at the time of writing this. All of the gangsters that you can hire have others in the pool that they like, love or hate. Many have 4 of these in different combinations. It makes for super a interesting thought, but if you add in, that the opposing AI Bosses (14) also hires out of this pool, it stops being about building your crew and starts feeling like a high school popularity contest. Also, if you go to fight another boss and one of your peoples "Friends or Lovers" is on the opposing side, they wont fight that person and most likely will leave your gang if you win and their friend dies (unless you leave them out of the fight, which deprives you of one of your possibly expensive shooters.), so the magic hoops follow you around even if / when you can jump through them the first time to get a solid team. You are forced to take whomever is available, Not who you think is cool or build with a theme (Like the Italian Mob or Madam Queens Harlem Raiders (although she is done very well in the game as one of the bosses.)) This could have been a cool game idea, but in practice its terrible with such a small pool of talent, the pool needs to be about 2 times bigger to give you any actual choice or freedom in building a group you want to use. On the upside, all of the people you wont be able to hire, have backstories and mission statements.  Oddly only about a dozen have missions you can go on to get cool loot.All of them that can are the lowest quality level at the start.  This game desperately needs a way to (hire) create generic gangsters that you can change the look and skills. No Legitimate Businesses (Fronts) that you own and make money, only illegal rackets.  If you take over an area, there are probably going to be about 15 to 25 buildings you can make into whatever racket you like, or you can raze them to the ground so no one can move in, like your enemies. You cant have too many rackets or of a type of racket (you can have 25 speakeasy's in an area with 50 buildings and thats okay. Theres no such thing as too many in an area.)  You can ransack thug owned buildings / 'smash up' them, but you have to do this constantly to keep people from moving in. Its not a one and done until later. Theres so many that you would spend all of your time re-running the same buildings to just to keep it locked down.Spreadsheets, for the love of god spreadsheets...EVE online shed a tear of pride when this game came out. The menus are a pain to navigate and not at all intuitive. Weapon and item balance. I'm not talking damage, I'm talking about supply. My last run I had 3 gangs of 12 that had all of the rare and epic weapons available but 9 that barely had any or all that they did have were common or uncomon. The blackmarket is there but it doesnt have anywhere near the amount / variety that you actually will need, or all of the things that you were looking for and it takes forever to restock.You cant rename buildings so if you take over other bosses territory you will have rackets titled "Available Racket Building" and you cant do anything about it.More than half of the customers in your rackets when you go inside are wearing trenchcoats for some reason. You cant change the color designation of your buildings or choose one you want. Its all static. Overall, its a playable game that theyre updating a lot. Pick it up if its on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely not as bad as people make it out to be but not perfect either. Gameplay is serviceable, if a little basic. There's really only 3 things you can do: Take over territory, build businesses, and manage your relationships with other factions. To take over territory, you have to send your crew to the enemy's depot, either taking out all their businesses first or dealing with a wave of reinforcements for every business they still have running. The combat is just a basic turn based system which is fine at first but gets boring after a while, which sucks considering you have to do at least 3 or 4 fights for each territory you want to take over (until the mid-game when your crew is so powerful you can basically rock up and take whatever you want). There is an "auto-resolve" button you can use to skip past the smaller fights, but there's always a chance that your entire crew will die so you'll basically never use it.Building businesses is about as exciting as it sounds; click on a building, choose what kind of business you want, and you're done. There are 4 types of businesses in the base game: Breweries, speakeasies, casinos and brothels. Breweries produce alcohol, speakeasies sell it, casinos sell half as much alcohol as speakeasies but generate a random amount of money per week, and brothels consume no alcohol but also make basically no money. With DLC you get access to loan sharks, which require a large investment up front but generate stupid amounts of money.Diplomacy, in my opinion, is where the game needs the most work. Your relationship with a faction is basically inconsequential. In the 20 hours I've played, nobody has ever declared war on me, no matter how bad our relationship was. I have never had my businesses raided by the police. None of my friends have ever joined me in a war I declared. The only useful aspect of diplomacy is trade, which you can use to buy alcohol or items from different bosses or, more often than not, just give all your excess items away for a huge opinion increase. If you have a good relationship with a faction you can have them assassinate literally anybody in the game and you can do this as much as you want, which is completely broken and I'm kind of shocked it made it into the final game.In short, the game is fine. Just fine. I picked it up hoping that it could capture at least a fraction of what Gangsters: Organized Crime did (since I can't get it to run on Windows 10) and it scratched that itch for a while, but I can begin to feel myself growing bored. If you're a nerd for prohibition era mafia stuff like I am, pick it up. But if you're not, maybe give it a pass.

_childDocuments_.review: So, full disclosure. I bought this game at launch, but got it refunded because it wasn't doing anything for me....but I could see it had real potential. So I closely watched the development of the game over the next 12 months or so, and was very impressed with the improvements I saw....so purchased the game a second time. I certainly am glad I did, as its a lot more entertaining now. Locations feel a bit more varied, and the mission system is much more fun to engage with, as is the Empire building side of the game. There are additional improvements I'd like to see in the future (more character abilities, even more combat locations) but the game is a real hoot as it currently is.....especially for the asking price. Just don't go in expecting Game of the Year material, and I suspect you won't be disappointed by this game!

_childDocuments_.review: Very much a game that tries to do way to much at once, and as such it is unquestionably shallow. The management part lacks any strategy, and mostly consists of waiting for money, buying a few upgrades and then more waiting. The turn-based combat is the now standard XCOM-style. The RPG-elements and relationship-system also feels undercooked The AI barely seems to do anything and is rarely a threat. So with all that why the hell do i like this game. Well, the theme does alot of heavy-lifting, they nail the feel and look perfectly, everything about this has that wonderfully cliche gangster-film feel. And while the combat is basic, i still did enjoy it. It has a ton of weapons and they are fun to use. I also enjoyed recruiting and trying out the diffrent gangsters you can hire, and that does have a real feeling of them getting more powerful. I do like the fact that it does actually have a story, each mobster you can play as i think has a diffrent main one. It's just kinda cool for a game like this to have that, and does add alongside the opening conversiation a more character and story-focused approach which games like this never really does. Yeah, there aren't really that many of those missions and it doesn't really matter that much to the overall gameplay, but it still is pretty cool. I can't fault the game for it's ambition, even if it falls short. I hope that with time and expansions they are able to really add depth and fix the problems it has. Because i did enjoy what i have played. For now i recommend this for people who really love the gangster setting and enjoy fun, but basic, XCOM-like turn-based combat.

_childDocuments_.review: The biggest sin in empire of sin, is that of publishing this game as a finished product rather than an Early Access. I don't know whether the onus is on the developer or the publisher or both, but it's a blatant lack of ethics  and of respect for prospective custommers. Sadly, it is increasingly common in the gaming industry.The game is a bit further than one might expect from the initial release of an Early Access in that the storyline for each boss is already in, but as far as bugs and game mechanics polish go, I've played Early Access games that were further along the development line on day 1 of their Early Access (props to Fell Seal: Arbiter's Mark team) than Empire of Sin is on an official release.So if you chose to buy this game in the state as of this review, beware that you are buying into an Early Access for a game that will hopefully meet it's expectations only several months from now.I can't endorse this product because of the unethical marketing strategy. I would've paid full price to participate in an Early Access if it had been properly advertised as such because the genre is right up my alley and the game looked (and still looks) like it could have a lot of potential down the line.That's the end of the short version. Details below.As for appreciation of the game in it's current state:-The atmosphere and music is great albeit a little repetitive.-The voice acting embodying the personality of the bosses is enjoyable, although limited in scope.-The graphics are fine although still bug-ridden e.g.--Attack animations causing characters to go through walls or shoot through objects--Certain characters end "frozen" during some or all of their animations and when this happens, it appears to slow down the execution of actions.-Given the prevalence of tactical combat in the current state of the game, the fact that buildings where combat take place only have a handful few layouts for each building size quickly becomes very repetitive.-There remains a lot of gameplay bugs, even after 2 big bugfix patches. I have only experienced one that was gamebreaking and forced me to restart a new game, and it was in the intro tutorial with Goldie. However I've had to reload to last save for a couple of bugs, or save and reload right away for a handful few very annoying ones, and there are others you just accept to playthrough however annoying.-Gameplay is very shallow. And this is well above bugs as to why I feel this should've been released as an early access game. There are 2 main game systems, the tactical combat system and the empire simulation system. They intertwine by allowing you to hire better mercenaries or purchase gear or by hostile acquisition of revenue-generating buildings.--The game can be won while ignoring the empire simulation altogether. You can kill every other boss and win the game, no matter how well guarded they are, with your own boss alone on max difficulty. Part of this is game balance. Another part is heal/sustain mechanics and most likely a bug with a healing item. And an even bigger chunk is terrible combat AI.--The combat advantages gained from a good empire sim are very marginal, unless you purposefully stretch the game to wait for later game mercenaries to catch up and be fully upgraded as the cheaper/early game ones are. Gear from merchants is generally worse than the random loot you get from thug hunting/box farming.--Even with self-imposed rules or boundaries to try and explore empire simulation, the max difficulty AI is quickly outscaled. I won my second playthrough with self-imposed rules by 1923 because I had nothing else left to do than finish the bosses off. By contrast, prohibition lasted until 1933. Eventually you just realise that you would need to self-impose a lot of idle time to try and reel the player's growth potential in line with the poor AI and the simulation mechanics are neither sufficiently complex nor varied to where even very casual gamers won't figure enough out within a few hours.Despite all of that, I still have mild enjoyment playing this game because of the laid back jazz atmosphere and some of the more corny dialogue and the sheer laugh of breaking the game so hard.

_childDocuments_.review: I just wanted to take some time and say I truly love this game. Mafia/mob themed games are in short supply these days. The theme of the game lends itself wholeheartedly to the systems of the game, Think Monopoly meets xcom and you have yourself Empire of Sin. Running around the city with your ragtag band of hired guns taking over abandoned buildings from squatters or knocking over businesses of your rivals to make your income go up is cathartic. This has become my "chill and vibe" game. Sometimes I turn up the volume and listen to the jazz soundtrack while I play and sometimes i turn it down and flip on a podcast while I play and just enjoy myself.I hope that the game does well so we can get more expansions for it. this game truly is one of my favorite games in recent years. It doesnt try to be a bombastic AAAA game. it is a systems heavy mafia simulator and in that regard it does what it does very well. My two knocks against the game is that the random events you run into seem to be very similar regardless of what lead you pick you will probably check off the same list around the same time in your game, and the "misc" equipment slot doesnt seem to have a real purpose. i found a car battery and i can equip that on my character but it literally does nothing stat-wise.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played a full campaign as Frank Donovan on medium difficulty over roughly 20-25 hours of gameplay.Pros:*Graphics are beautiful 9/10*Sounds are fantastic 8/10*The map is great to look at when zoomed into a neighbourhood*Potential for 100+ hours of game play*ITS A DAMN MAFIA GAMECons:*The sound would get 10/10 if it wasn't for the shabby voice acting in parts which almost ruins the experience.*I've personally had some "game breaking" bugs, upon restarting the game or something significant happening in game, the bug will usually resolve itself but i'm aware this isn't the same for everyone and there really are A LOT of bugs, mostly minor.*Diplomacy is fairly pointless other than trading your excess guns for moolah*BUGS - i can't stress how many bugs there are, mostly graphical and minor annoyance bugs, this game needs a LOT of polish still in that respectSo here's the big one for me, the game play itself, it's great to start off, very much Xcom inspired gameplay but with a Mafia styled skin. It's fun for the first couple of hours but it does indeed get repetitive later in the game. After something like 4-5 hours of playing (this was my first play through) i could have easily "completed" the game but i decided to go and take over the whole of chicago instead hence the 20+ hours of playing. The mechanics to earning money are pretty straightforward and are also fairly shallow. Upgrading buildings are almost a wasted investment, besides guards, as it's far more lucrative to simply take over other established rackets.Shortest version, yes there's bugs but if you like mafia games and think it would be fun playing one Xcom style then get this game, there will be updates to squash the bugs and update the gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: Sometimes you go into a restaurant and order chicken, it looked good on the menu and when it arrives it looks as good as it sounds, then you cut into the chicken and its a bit pink because it hasn't been cooked long enough, maybe the chef was busy, maybe the restaurant was busy sometimes you will say "oh well it's probably ok" and eat it anyway, some people may even send it back and order something else...This game is like ordering chicken and it arriving clucking with feathers. Missions are broken, stats mean pretty much nothing and bugs break the game constantly, not to mention the economy.But damn it I still want the chicken so I will wait until the chefs sort their stuff out because it still looks good on the menu, and I'm hungry.Update: Never have I seen a premium release so badly done on Steam. A post in December a couple of weeks after release saying that fixes will come in Q1 of the following year. End of January and not a single Hotfix or further communication about a terribly broken game. This already feels written off by the developers, the fact that they have a "roadmap" for dlc is laughable. I am shocked that Paradox would put their name on this steaming mess of a game. Go to enemy base kill boss, ignore everything else repeat half a dozen times, game done.Awful mechanics, voice acting, gangster costumes that look more like superheros from Watchmen and a script that is so embarrassing its bordering on racist. This is broken to the point it should almost be recalled and rebuilt from scratch. Like many others I was optimistic about the game, love the concept and the era but this it my most regretted purchase ever, and I pre-purchased Stronghold 3 and Duke Nukem!In short avoid at all costs, uninstall if you already have it and to the developers may god have mercy on your souls.

_childDocuments_.review: So i got this one despite all of the mixed reviews because again, i'm just a sucker for mafia-related media and paradox-published games like Cities, Stellaris, HoI etc spoiled me too much i guess.People are comparing this game to XCOM a lot, and well, so will i, because thats the game that always springs to your mind when playing this thinking "why isn't this and that just done like in xcom??"First things first:- Graphics are fine. Everything looks grimey, theres smoke hanging in the air, the streets are littered and reflect the dim streetlights on a rainy night...just like you would expect from a 1920s Mafia-Movie. Nicely done.- Music is KICK ASS. So flippin catchy i got it stuck in my head for quite a while, fits the scenario very well and really gets you into the mood for beeing a wise-guy from the second the menue starts up.- SFX are...ok. Every SMG sounds the same, so do the MGs, the Shotguns, the Handguns etc...seriously? there are so many classic and iconic guns in here, you couldn't bother to get at least like 3 different sounds for each subtype of gun? Weak. Don't you just love when you are playing a game and can tell "Oh that guys got a (insert gun)!" Just by it's sound? well...not here.- Still on the Sounds-front, after hearing your boss saying his lines for the 1000000th time, it gets old. Even worse with some npcs that seem to have like 2 lines shared between them. So get used to hearing "Ahhh damn it..i'm ♥♥♥" A LOT.Now to the Characters, which like in xcom, is a huge part of this game.- The Bosses are all unique and interesting enough, though i would have liked some more "classic italian mobster" types. Really don't see myself running a Crimesyndicate as a petite burlesque dancer you know..- With that in mind, it's clear the game wants to push everything in a more "colorfull" and kinda funny(?) way with the bosses and squadmembers. Which is fine if you are into that but not so fine when you really want to roleplay as a classic mob kinda guy in this ROLE PLAYING game. There is absolutely NO character customization, so you have no choice but to have a squad of people cosplaying as cowboys, butchers, soldiers, indians and lunatics etc. In XCOM, you can FULLY customize every little thing on each of your soldiers. So you can go full lunatic with pink camo shorts and green iros, full simp by having your females running around the battlefield in hotpants and sportsbra or, if you want full tryhard and have everyone in buzzcuts,camo-facepaint and SpecOps-Uniform and Helmet. Well...not so here.- Your squadmates level just by existing. Excuse me?? _childDocuments_.review: This game has great potential HOWEVER, I will not be playing it again until a much needed patch is released. it should not have been released in this state - far FAR to buggy and just......empty.My main concern is that the overhauls this game requires are too far too many. It basically needs the below to make it playable:- DIPLOMACY OVERHAUL -. I rate games like this straight away on how they handle diplomacy. The sit downs are a great idea but are terrible. They should have functioned like an interactive story book with many unique situations coming from them. Also, you shouldn't always have to come off as an arsehole when speaking to other factions.....that is what diplomacy is! (Cant see this being fixed due to the costs involved with getting voice actors back).- AI - The Ai is shockingly bad. Standard issue in games but can be fixed- COMPLETE PLAYER / AI INBALANCE - Games like this desperately need to feel fair and that both AI players and you are doing the same things to reach the ultimate goal of winning the game. For a start, the AI player just constantly throws generic gangsters when at war - something you cannot do except for when defending. Any unique gangsters the AI may have will always be waiting for you at their safe house. The Black List of gangster shouldn't even exist, it should be that the generic gangsters evolve into RANDOMLY generated gangsters that can be customised like X-com - a game this heavily takes from. Doubtful this will get fixed due to the sheer balancing issues this would cause.- HEISTS/ROBBERIES - Why oh why are they missing in this game? You should have had to start at the bottom and work your way up. Simply to fix.- AUTO RESOLVE - I do not understand how this game is missing an auto-resolve option? Something i have no doubt will be added in the very next patch. With the constant generic gangster spam being thrown at my buildings - this was the main reason i stopped playing. Utterly game breaking.- LACK OF PLAY TESTING - I played on the medium difficulty and had three times more points than any of the other 10 AI players. Seems you can just take over buildings constantly with 3/4 strong gangsters and make money that way. Use the money to buy other buildings and you will then take over whole neighbourhoods shortly.  Rinse and repeat then expect the inevitable spam attacks...which is when you turn the game off. if you manage to stay sane enough to continue playing....use the shallow booze system to make the booze you need and then where it should be distributed. I can just imagine raising the difficult wont improve AI....just add cheat modifiers to the battles and stupid percentage hit chance increases. _childDocuments_.review: Firstly - im not a fanboi so this review is genuinely unbiased and based on my current gametime having bought it in the last 24 hours.Firstly - Ive been following the game since announcement. I havent bought it until now which speaks volumes as this was based purely on steam reviews. Having seen it on sale and with very little else on offering i thought, screw it lets have a punt even with mixed reviews.Summary:Ive got almost 12hrs game time which i understand isnt like 100+ however, i dont understand the negative reviews - and trust me ive read many reviews, hence why holding off buying. Yes the developers have only recently started pushing updates/patches  however in the last 12 hours game time, ive not experienced any bugs AT ALL. <touchwood>The game is very much a nostalgic nod to the old games of Gangsters: Organised Crime, Mafia and Omerta as many have said before me. The game is not designed as a quick fix. Its a slow burn. From my take im game its very similar to the old school strategy games - i say this due to the nature of jumping in game, spending a few hours sorting some business stuff  and enemy take overs and then coming back to it in a few hours or even a day or 2 and picking up where you left off. I remember fondly how i used to do this with The Settlers on amiga - player 3 or 4 hours solid gaming then come back in a day or 2 and carry on as if there was no interruption. If you play the game the way it is meant to be played  then you wont be completing a playthrough in quicktime. In my 12 hours, i own 1 neighbourhood and i find myself playing politics with the other 9 factions whilst im desperately trying to single out a specific weak link faction that i can eradicate. This isnt an easy feat by the way, unless of course you  get some intel on a boss safehouse - and even then, it takes some planning and purchasing of consumables to attack a safehouse and come away with all your capo's!I dont understand the moanings of people saying its broken as you cant get gold henchman - gold henchman are top tier. Why if you are a scrub mafioso would any gold henchman ally with you - doesnt make sense. Therefore the whole "endgame" henchman argyment is a moot point to me. Higher henchman are scaled for notoriety as they should be. I am still grinding loyalty with a linked henchman to get my first gold henchman - and i like that fact you have to work for it. To put in simple terms, since i clicked play, i went to the black book and began picking my endgame henchmen and have started my affiliation with lower henchman as a result. I love the fact you have to plan for long term in the short term  - amazing mechanic in my view.Imagine Shadows of Mordor's nemesis system whereby guy A doesnt like B but wouldnt have an issue working with guy C. However guy C is best mates with guy D who hates guy A - and each of guy A,B,C,D all have differing abilities. The possibilities are endless. Im currently using a demolitionist, 2 doctors, 2 enforcers, 1 hired gun and 1 con artist. The mechanics of the fights are drastically different depending on who you take and each fight can be totally different. For example one fight which was listed as a medium location ended up having 2 guys that could throw demolitions - when my team are huddled near the door as ranged characters - it was painful! The only gripe i would say is that auto resolve for fights is a total lottery. One of my brewery's got attacked by 5 enemy players and i had 2 guards. It was a clear loss so i clicked auto resolve just to get rid of the conflict and much to my amazment. I won /facepalm (clearly i pay my underlings too much!!) On that note i would suggest the enjoyment of the game is actually playing the fights anyway, rather than auto resolving - but each to their own.Pros:Games a slow burn - and it should be. (i bought settlers in my early teens and it lasted me well over a month or 2. nowadays im buying games once a week)Depth of companions and choiceAbilities and story of your main character choice (genuinely going to play a new game with a new character - which is rare in modern games for me)Graphics are solidPolitics with other factions Companion questsCombat escalates quickly - especially safehouses (took me 5 save reloads to drop my first boss with each fight lasting 20 minutes+)Cons:Doesnt suit the generation of completing a game within 20hrsLoot drops can be a bit rubbishAuto resolve is laughable so avoid itTravelling can be time consuming (use the taxi's they are there for a reason)Not many businesses to createSave system is a bit meh - would prefer ability to name saves and auto deletion of out dated savesOverview pages can be confusing and awkward to locate quickly a business you are looking for unless you remember the name of it (my naming of businesses aint the best - my latest brewery is called Capone Kissma Nads)All in all, this game is pretty amazing and considering there is little other choice in the genre and whilst its on sale, SNAP IT UP - you would be mad not to.Finally there is something special about hearing your irish main character saying Gobshite in a true irish accent as he hits someone in the face with his Shinty stick!

_childDocuments_.review: This game could have been very good. The potential of the game is obvious. However, potential isn't what people are looking for, or at least not what I am looking for. I like my games to deliver. Despite entertaining enough gameplay, albeit repetitive, there is one thing that screws this game over far more than anything else. That is the bugs. It is rare for me to encounter so many bugs in a game, that I feel it is game breaking. Here is just a few of the worse ones; -Some missions do not resolve properly, you get the rewards, but the missions do not clear away. Eventually the bad consequences of missions with limited time will happen as well when missions fail to complete properly. - Gang members, or the entire gang, including your boss, can disappear if you are inside a building while upgrading it and rushing the upgrades. I found this particularly true of breweries. The only character you can get back without loading is your boss character, by "travelling to", the other gang members are in limbo. - Enemy gangs can acquire characters without having raised their Notoriety Points sufficiently. All recruitable characters have a minimum demand for how Notorious you are. However the computer can recruit characters ignoring this, meaning the entire point of raising your Notoriety faster than everybody else is gone. The AI cheats in crew recruitment. - Once a Cooperation Deal was cancelled by a rival gang the dialog box refused to close. When this happened for me that last quick save was also corrupted. Progress was lost. Basically; the game has game breaking bugs.I rate games on a die of 1-6, but with 0 for absolute failures. Minimum for recommended is 3. This is a 2. Not complete crap, but it fails to reach the minimum, I do not recommend you buy this game at this point in time. Wait a couple of months and see if it gets patched up and fixed. If it is fixed, it can become a solid 4. Currently though it is a 2.

_childDocuments_.review: Jeez, this is bad.I was so into this game. I had it preordered and it was a tossup whether I'd be more into this or Cyberpunk. After all, it's a management sim with a mafia theme and tactical combat. It's basically made for me.Except it's not. It's not for anyone. Its initial strong charm wears off quickly when you get into the flow of the game, which it's clear nobody put much time into. Your character's unique traits, promising a customized experience, aren't particularly useful, coming in randomly once in a while, but never telling you exactly what happened. The sit-downs, supposed to be a clash of personalities, are invariably an exchange of zingers followed by an offer of sharing bonuses. The management part is fine for what it is, but traveling around the world map is an infuriating exercise in zooming out, zooming out some more, sometimes zooming out a third time to go to a place and then you can interact with a building and do your talking or fighting. There are a zillion missions that come in from nowhere, far too many to track, and all of them basically have the same flow. It quickly becomes clear that the game has shown its whole hand in the first minutes and you're just going to see the same things over and over again.Speaking of repetition, there's the combat. The thing you spend most of your time doing. You can essentially win any fight by just shooting over and over and over again. Terrain doesn't matter, placement doesn't matter beyond line of site, AI is terrible, and everyone is outclassed. And combat is the endgame of every interaction, as far as I can tell. There's no autoresolve; it's just endless fight after endless fight.If there's violence in a mob game, it needs to be visceral. And it's not. It's a sanitized gunfighting game where there are dozens of people standing in the line of fire, who you can't hurt. There are no civilian casualties. You can only hurt other criminals. Even accidentally. I don't WANT to kill civilians, but the fact that I never accidentally hit one in dozens of firefights kept taking me out of the game. The game might be fun enough without the combat, but the combat kills fun as efficiently as your gangsters kill nameless thugs. I want to wait and see if this gets patched into something good. But there's a fundamental sloppiness, from the animations to the systems that don't really interact with one another to the deluge of repetitive quests to the wasted subject matter and bland writing, that makes me think this is the game we get. Which is ultimately the sin this game traffics in.

_childDocuments_.review: With a decade's worth of competition behind it, Empire of Sin attempts to copy everyone's homework while trying not to make it too obvious. Players of  and  will immediately see the similarities, and along with it, every issue that riddled this game's predecessors.Its initial hours are to be praised; With a large cast of unique characters that all come with their own initial story, it's easy to get immersed in your narrative while short-and-sweet alternative missions keep you occupied between the game's progression loop. It only takes your first or second run of this loop, however, to spot just how shallow the ocean is... Its management aspect is almost identical to an idle sim, and its combat variety and difficulty scaling immediately default to more red shirts that take slightly more damage.The Bosses mechanics quickly boil down to traits and bonuses tier-listed into game-breaking or not worth playing at all, only serving to slightly speed up or slow down the monotonous board game format, making anything but smaller, faster playthroughs an unrewarding grind. Your , as the ability to hire lackeys or goons is barred for you, and only available to the opposition, try their best to tear you from any semblance of realism; Adamant to bloat the game with horribly inaccurate portrayals and tokenism while swearing they're a hard-researched, deeply historical game.With everything falling short of the mark, the developers attempted to fix, it and soon after abandoned the title. And it's only DLC showing a clear Paradox-style marketing scheme of selling you basic functions for a price tag. And even if they were to continue development, you'd still find more authentic and varied gameplay from a 2001 game than this.

_childDocuments_.review: As of me last playing this on 12/13/2020, this game did not stand out at all. The game was simple to grasp, and might give you enough bits here and there to keep you going. Those bits are just distractions to the giant lack of features and mechanics that helps make the core gameplay interesting and exciting.* The core gameplay mechanics center around property management and turn based combat.Turn-based combat: It feels pretty ok at first but as the amount of enemies and tougher gangsters appear, it feels drawn out and unnecessarily long. You're also forced to manage the defenses of your own property when an enemy gang decides to invade you, which can feel frustrating if you don't have one of your tougher underlings stationed nearby. The generic units you get and face in the property defense feels boring and more of a numbers game, which further unnecessarily extends the length of the fight.Property Management: The concept feels pretty ok, but I don't think I've been able to generate enough money off the property and have been spending more time raiding and invading. Although I've only had a short time playing it, the upgrades don't feel impactful for the defenses and the payout isn't noticable in the long term for profits. Also there's a constant change in the areas that can affect the amount you can make, which is to deter you from monopolizing on a single product line.They have posted that they created a community group to gather feedback and directly influence the development, but I am still waiting to see something that changes to jump out at me. I'm sure that alot of people are enjoying what it has to offer, but it doesn't really make much of a good impression for me, and feels more like an early access game.If i had to give it a rating: 3/5There are some interesting concepts that they want to do but it needs further fleshing out to make gameplay more interesting and less of a chore for certain core mechanics. There is definitely room for improvement.I would not recommend this game in the state it was in, since I last played.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, I got this for free through my wife who works at Paradox. However, I've got nothing at stake here personally.I am still undecided what to say about this game, or if I want to recommend this game or not. After 17 hours, I just finished my first playthrough... first 15 or so hours I took it slow, then I got a bit bored (and overwhelmed with the management), so I just went around and killed everyone in a row, winning the game. But let's take a deeper look in things below.---The game's premise is pretty interesting. I like a bit of management, as well as good old turn based combat. The theme is also close to my heart, so I was very tempted to buy this game. Luckily I ended up getting it for free, so I launched the game and dug in.Within the first 20 minutes I realized that I am not actually playing a game made by an AAA studio headed by John Romero - I was playing a sort of an indie dev game that somehow had big names attached to it. The game feels like a small studio game, where the publisher has pressured the team to make a game too complex and too fast, without enough playtesting.The game is simply clunky. From controls to camera to combat to management, everything feels like there's a good IDEA behind it, but not enough testing and not enough planning actually went in to the features. You'll very quickly realize that the AI in combat is wacky to say the least and very easy to exploit. At the same time, the management of different rackets is a bit confusing and extremely cumbersome. The story is explained through quests, but they are not very well presented, they get a bit confusing and in the end I completely ignored them. They need to be paced a lot better.Once you snow ball in this game even a little, it's super easy to just go and take over everything, while ignoring the story, police raids etc. You just go from a generic battle to another. There's also plenty of weird little bugs that occur pretty much all the time. However I did not run into massive game breaking bugs, unlike some other people have.There's a few longer, better reviews that outline my feelings towards the game very well:---With all that being said... I wish I could go into more details about everything. With less than 20 hours though, I don't feel I can do that properly. The game has many glaring, major issues and it doesn't feel like a proper, released game. However, with all its faults it is a playable game and has a certain charm to it. Of the 17 hours I have played so far, 15 were somehow still enjoyable and kept me engaged. I had fun and I didn't hate the game, even with all its faults. In a way it felt like a game that was just deep enough to interest me and shallow enough at the same time to allow me to enjoy an hour or two after work.Even though the devs have announced that there'll be DLC's coming, I don't think anyone should bother with them. Get the game in a sale, hope the devs abandon this after a few patches. I hope - and so should you - that they'll get enough money and goodwill out of this demo of a game to get funding for Empire of Sin 2, which would be properly planned and tested before release.At the moment this game is only worth about 10 USD. I can recommend it at around that price range, and if you have tolerance for small issues. And if you like the theme. But it's not an AAA game. It's a game that feels like it's done by industry beginners.

Also every bug that currently exists that I have seen has made the game easier and not harder which is only a problem if you want the slightest amount of challenge in your games.Just wait to buy it.Edit: Steam keeps asking me to revise review, not realising the additional hours of gameplay are just to kill time before CP2077 comes out. _childDocuments_.review: 14 Hours in and I was pleasantly surprised. The key elements of Paradox games melds into an interesting tactical game. Nothing game breaking however.... I found the game to be one that draws me right in, setting up raids and managing my empire. The respect to Chicago's layout is a nice touch as well, although its not truly localized so to speak. Ten hours later and I found the bugs, and noticed how absolutely repetitive the game is, and how many absolutely game breaking bugs there are with no support in like the last 5 or so months. Its really frustrating as the little bit of historical narrative they tried to put into these characters was what added life to what becomes a one dimensional slog without it. _childDocuments_.review: Well it's XCOM minus the stuff that made XCOM special.  You don't really have the care for your random gangsters like you do the soldiers when they are cut down.  What Empire of Sin does right is the look.  The game setting looks good, the concept of a open world meets XCOM style turn based game is very unique, and playing the mob boss from a more strategic level is neat.  The police and feds as a third faction that comes out of nowehere seemingly to ruin your day is a nice touch and the in game missions aren't bad either. That said it has some odd hang ups that prevent it from being a cult classic.-unlike other paradox games where historical accuracy is aimed for and alternative history is played up for a joke this game really mixes things up.  Example Hymie Weiss, the man alleged to be the only man Al Capone feared is someone you can just hire off bat.  -the gangs are very inclusive and open minded despite what history says, I wouldn't mind this if they did it like CK3 where I have options to play historical or non historical but a lot of these gangs won't even allow you to be in them unless you're of a certain ethnicity or race unless you're the bottom level guys-There's some sort of relationship system between your henchmen which is mostly just annoying.  I get the concept was some henchmen would not attack each other but mostly it comes off as strange.  Seemingly ALL my henches are bisexual evidently and I've had such strange parings as the black and proud harlem hellfighter and the refuses to be reconstructed ex confederate solider. I mean being gay in the era is wild enough much less the age and race issues going on in that relationship.  But it seems to happen with EVERYONE.  Everybody is just itching to get into some sort of sexual relationships seemingly just as an annoying game mechanic which is all it becomes in the end.  -Oddly enough the mechanic as progressive and ahistorical as it is, it also hinges entirely off mongamy.  Evidently all my bisexual gangsters refuse to share with anyone.  We run brothels, they're all bi, but no one wants to share or even consider a orgy.  So instead I have to keep my drama queens apart or my XCOM game becomes a slap fight between my crew except with guns.  It's beyond pathetic and really makes me feel like Al Capone should have been questioning his actions long before he had the mayor of Chicago murdered. -Honestly all the business management seems really secondary to the turn based fighting.  It's what earns you the money for vests, guns, etc but your best gear comes from other crime bosses which you get by killing them so really the money is just to buy better bisexual hench persons. -Oddly about every race is in this game minus hindus, arabs, and islander types...there are two full blooded indigenous Americans as well which can only seem so progressive about a game centered around illegal alcohol trade. Again it's an attempt to be progressive but at what end if you're also trying to be historical?  Henry Hill wasn't exaggerating about the whole not being full blooded Italian means you can't be made, ironically crime is not that open minded about race in fact they're the opposite but won't let it stop them making a buck.  -The rival gangs are mostly made up which I can somewhat understand but all the legit organizations should be in game.-All organizations cops, gangs, etc have females in them.  Again I get the progressive tone but it makes the game look more like Michael Jackson's "Smooth Criminal" because they all wear the men's attire regardless.  Only female henchmen, gangbosses, and prostitutes can dress like women.  The 20s must have been a strange time with bisexual criminals who are only into monogamy but have very odd dress code rules.  Overall it needs work and I think a historical option playing up the more edgy less progressive aspects of the organizations would be interesting as well.  So far this feels more like CK3 when you make everyone bisexual and XCOM combined.

_childDocuments_.review: Generaly I love Paradox games. This game however has been a bitter disappointment. At the beginning the game seems like fun. Combat is sort of challenging especially when you are not using any of the golden weapons that you get for buying the delux version. Soon after that you and your companions will become stronger and pretty much all the challenge goes down the drain. Having an AI that seems to make worse choices in-game then my Tesla on FSD in traffic doesn't help either. Then we come to the management side of EoS which feel even more rushed to the shelves then the combat system. There are a few options to make money, all don't require any interaction and aren't very interesting. Basically you claim a building and upgrade it to either a brothel, casino, brewery or speakeasy. The first two are nothing more then money overtime. The speakeasy is a little more interesting because you need a brewery to produce your own stock. Depending on the local economy you need to produce either low quality for poor towns and better quality for areas with a richer economy. All in all this has been a very big disappointment and feels like a big money grab where Paradox uses up it's  somewhat good name to make a quick buck. That being said, there is still hope for the game when more content will get added.
