_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun game for a few hours, but then just falls flat on its face. After about 5 hours, my first playthough was done (I didn't even realize it at that time). There are some deep mechanics, they don't really have any actual impact at all as some are just not meaningful in any way, not complete, or do absolutely nothing. Below I will list the issues I have noticed, and will not include any bugs I encountered. I tried to play like a non-threatening boss at the start. Go to sitdowns rather than the other options. In the end I was always offered a business proposal, they would admire something about my empire and offer me some small perk. In return they would say something about "cheap muscle" and I can't figure out what I am supposed to do to hold up my end of the bargain.. I assume it has something to do with my security level, but I don't see any interactions that would let me do anything to help them. So that was a bunch of negative honor for failing to do my part. I started off doing the quests (which were overwhelming at the start as I didn't realize some were timed - which caused an original "made" person leave the crew - no problem I instantly hired them right back). But then once I took the first neighborhood, money (and thus making trades) was a non-issue. Also, CPU "Hey help me in this war" Me. "Whats in it for me?" and proceeds to check off everything the enemy owns.. CPU: "Sounds fair".. Me: does literally nothing, CPU wins war and gives me the entire empire they just took. o.O Along those lines too, once I started exploring other neighborhoods- since I was getting rackets in them from the CPU wars, I realized Chinatown was totally desolate besides minor factions. The CPU never expanded there or really at all. After ~8hr my first game, I had 60 rackets and the next closest boss was at 12. My money is over 10k per week that I just reinvest in upgrades to make more, and a ton more security. The interiors are just there for looks. I'm not sure why there is mechanics like hired people can get STDs or drunk depending on if they are in one too long. I hung out in one to see if eventually they would go do their own thing, nope, everyone just stayed by me. I then thought maybe you were supposed to leave them there to defend, as some have perks that benefit a particular racket.. But why? Only being able to hire 10, I couldn't cover everything.. On that note, the defenses are a joke and you are forced to do them.. "X is attacking your building!" /fight  Cool my 6 guys Vs their 3, using just generic sawed off shotguns and pistols mostly. So boring and you have no chance to get yourself or any of your bosses to that random location - so again it is boring and basically pointless. At least let us Sim it when the odds are like that. Once I took safehouses in other places, it asked me to make someone a Lt. I did, but they don't actually get promoted to that position and has no impact on gameplay since they still just follow me around. I also inserted someone as a Mole into Capone's group - 3 hr later no clue what impact that had. There was no additional options to have him do something, and I didn't get any secret info. You already get all the info you would need, down to "their plans" from the 1000 panels in game.Looking at the black book, I have 7 people from there. The AI owns 3 total, through all the other bosses.. The cheap people are decent, and get pretty strong when leveled up. But once they like you, then you can recruit their friends without reaching that notoriety level - and the higher level ones are gods, and the drawback is they are very expensive up front - except money is no issue. 99 marksmanship, just give them a sniper rifle - or regular rifle, and GG. They 100% whatever they can see.  Plus my entire crew likes each other besides one guy who loves someone who doesn't love them back. So the biggest mistake is to injure/down one of my guys because then everyone else goes into a rage and unloads on anyone they can see. It pretty much wipes the entire enemy squad and I did nothing at all. Finally the RPG elements feel shallow. Nothing has a meaningful game impact here either. It is basically if YOU want to roleplay a character a bit and self impose rules to follow. The sit down dialogue just makes no sense.. The last person I met was Sai Wing Mock.. His attitude was "who are you, why should I care, you are nobody etc" Well.... I have 60 rackets and you are down to your last safehouse.... soooooo... ok bye. Im sure the AI stupidity in combat has been beaten to death.. But I will add that during street fights, there is always some random thug or 2 virtually out of vision that gets involved in the fight. So after 3 rounds and everyone is dead, im like... Whaaaaaa? Oh, dude 2 blocks away is still running up.. Don't worry we'll wait.. Along those lines, when you attack a building, most of the safehouses seem to be the same map and everyone spawns at the door. but the other buildings? Why do some of my people start in a bedroom half way into the building? It isn't xcom where you can scout and setup before you are noticed/attack. Right now I am at 480 notoriety - nobody else in the game has 100 yet. I saw some smashed rackets but really, they AI just doesn't try to "build an empire" as much as they just chop each others legs off. I was hoping that it would be viable to go smash their breweries so they can't make money in the other rackets, but what is the point? There doesn't seem to be any reason to attack their economy over brute forcing shooting them in the face, ever.. Even if you raze it, it disables the building for a year - but in a year I could turn it into something useful.. And for what it's worth, I'm only 1.5 years into my game and it is LONG over. So that option basically removes the building for the entire game. Overall I'd give it a 6.4/10. Do I regret buying it? Not to the degree of "I wish i refunded it" necessarily - that is extreme for me. But would I recommend it to someone? No. Maybe if it was $20-30 and after seeing what they address.. But realistically I don't see a real reason to play through a second time, unless you really just want to be another boss or try a different strategy to win - which will probably work because the AI can't tie its own shoes, much less run an empire.

_childDocuments_.review: I think Empire of Sin is a very interesting mix of strategy, RPG and turn-based combat like in XCOM.The fights are fun, but quite tenacious. I'll compare here with XCOM, where you need like 3 shots, maybe 4 if you're unlucky, to kill an opponent without armor. In Empire of Sin you don't hit the enemy more or less with your shots like in XCOM, but the opponents have a lot more life in relation, so it takes many attacks to kill an opponent, which makes the fights unnecessarily long. That's why I mostly use the autobattle. Some of the mechanics weren't immediately clear to me personally at first even after the tutorial, but after I clicked through the menus after the tutorial and looked at everything myself, the picture became clearer and clearer.In the conversations with other gang bosses, it was not always clear what bonuses you get if you accept their offer.But nonetheless, it is no online game and it's only to play for you maybe after work for one or two hours and for that I find the game fun.I can understand why a lot of people don't like the game.I personally wouldn't recommend buying it at full price. Rather wait for a sale or buy a key for it.I got the game for 5€ as a key, so it doesn't annoy me at all that the game is rather mediocre.You can definitely have fun with the game, but it's not worth the full price.

_childDocuments_.review: - especially if you like turn-based combat (XCOM-Style).  However, no story means no drivers to push you forward.  The main premise of taking over buildings gets highly-repetitive, only to open up yet another casino, brothel, distillery, ect.  How many brothels (or other rackets) do the devs expect the player to invest in a small block radius, and then limit the hotels to 1 per suburb?  Rolling around the streets with all your recruited gangsters [spolier](12 it seems is max)[/spoiler] makes it too easy and not worth really moving on to other neighborhoods - .  Gangsters come with preferences in player behavior and the company they keep (gangster choices) - but it has little to no consequence on the game play at all.. to include long-term loyalties as you can just pay someone off to shut up and keep coloring if you made them mad by offing someone they wanted to kill themselves.  Mechanics: Attack a rival building, take it over, work to upgrade it.... rinse and repeat 100 times.  I held on 10 hours, which is long enough to gain control of the entire south side area before I lost interest. I might be back for an expansion or major game play update.  I recommend getting it on sale, as it is arcadia-like gameplay, and lasts as long as your quartered interest does.Having said that, art style and graphics are nice, and the voice acting is somewhat humorous and stylized to the expected gangster/prohibition era. Nice to haves would include a character generator and real consequences based on actions/decisions made. No one tried to 'wack' me once, no one interfered with my business, deals and alliances were not necessary to survive, no double-crossing, and no collateral damage which could alert the police/feds, civilians, rival gangs, newspapers, or even spark in-fighting within your outfit or rackets.  Empire of Sin should be re-dubbed, "Empire of Murder and Hostile Takeovers" to get a better sense of what to expect from this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Reminiscent of Gangsters: Organized Crime (a classic from 1998) in a very fun way, so in that sense it feels like I've been waiting on this game for 20+ years. The combat is repetitive but still fun for me after @40 hours. The faction AI is solid and can be very punishing if you start a war before you're well prepared. Resource management is pretty good, although some additional nuance and complexity would be nice. There are numerous quests that pop up during play and these are fun. Many of them are tied to the particular gangsters you've hired, so there's good motivation to try out different people. Gangster relationships remind me fondly of Jagged Alliance 2, another of my all-time favorites. The city looks great and has a lot of wonderful immersive touches. Room for improvement? Sure. Playing on default difficulty the police/feds seemed like non-factors and the dynamic mini-factions -- while cool additions that make the city feel more alive -- feel easy to exploit to get ahead of the other major factions. Another exploit-y thing is fast travel (done via taxi) which allows you to respond too quickly to enemy attacks, thus nullifying their danger to a large degree. There are bugs as well although after @40 hours I haven't seen any of the game-breakers mentioned elsewhere.All in all, I'm really enjoying this game and am looking forward to continued refinements.

_childDocuments_.review: 2 main reasons why this is not the game quality we expected from this game.1. Terrible AI. Will run from cover using all their actionpoints (not shooting, just running) and leave the cover to end their turn in the middle of a room.2. Bad UI design. The management tabs are a hassle since they dont do what you expect them to do. No simple menus for upgrading your rackets. The tab named "gangster promotion screen" is not where you promote your gangsters, it is a place to admire your maffia tree, with no interactions possible at all. No button to find your gangsters in the world, dubble-clicking on a character portrait is usually standard for centering the camera on that character in the world, but nope does nothing. These small things shows that the game simply is not tested enough by actual players, probably only the developer themselves and it is very easy to be blind for these things when you are the developer of the game and know how to find everything.I am still enjoying this game because I have paid for it (I feel forced to enjoying it because otherway the money is lost for nothing). I even bought the deluxe version because I love XCOM-series and thought this would be a "modern" take on it, and there is some cool stuff, like the abilities of the bosses etc. But would I recommend it to someone else, definately not. Keep your money and buy XCOM 2 instead, it's sadly a better game in every game mechanic. This is the 2020-version of XCOM, I'm hoping Paradox gives them time to make this right by bringing it to new light next year.

_childDocuments_.review: I do not feel that this game deserves most of its negative reviews...Yes it feels a little bit janky at times, and the combat camera can at times be an annoyance, but this is a pretty solid grand strategy/turn based RPG.The only real negatives I have stumbled across so far are small UI glitches and occasional awkward camera issues.As for the gameplay, i have found the combat to be up to par with XCOM....it doesn't set the world on fire or bring anything new to the genre, but it is solid and enjoyable, however I do feel that the different classes do not really feel unique enough and there could be tweaks to make each class stand out, but as a counter to that, every character in the game has a set of personality traits (similar to crusader kings) which does add a lot of strategic elements to building a team of mobsters that can not only bash skulls but also run your businesses whilst managing to get along with each other...its a nice touch and, for me at least, it made the world feel a lot more alive. If you are looking at this game because you were a fan of the old Omerta or Gangsters series, just buy it, this game will scratch the itch for a modern Organised crime empire building sim!I will conclude by saying that, if you are looking for the "next gen" groundbreaking, game changing turn based strategy game...this isn't it, but if you are like me, an old dude whos into strategy games looking to kill a few hours while scratching the nostalgia itch (this game feels like the Gangsters 3 we never got) then theres easily 20-40 hours of fun to be had here before it gets old.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to start this by saying I truly wanted to like this game more than any other I've played. I love the setting of 1920's Chicago, mobsters and love the genre of grand strategy. However, even though for these reasons I'll probably still occasionally play it, I would advise all others not to buy Empire of Sin in its current state. The issue with the game is not the ideas and concepts, rather, the execution. While combining business management, Paradox diplomacy, turn based strategy, and an RPG looks good on paper, they all have their own issues that break the game. Business management aspects are rather dull, requiring massive amounts of capital to upgrade businesses anywhere from 2-6 thousand an upgrade, while the income may only be a few hundred. The same applies for purchasing weapons, a normal pistol may cost as much as an entire brewery of yours. Diplomacy is fairly meaningless, as deals that are stuck are comically meaningless. The combat is alright, not new or innovative or bad and buggy, just average. RPG aspects are dull and lacluster, as character developments don't have much of an inmpact and negative effects can be easily circumnavigated. While these are all poor in their own right, what ruins the game is the AI. The AI won't attack, expand, or do much of anything. They just kind of sit there. As the player all you have to do, is kill an enemy boss at their safehouse and you win all of that gangs possesions, After killing two or three boses, you basically win the game. This coupled with completly dumb AI strategy ruins the game. This game is much closer to being in Alpha compared to a finally release state. I"m not one for complaining without offering solutions, so here are a few suggestions that I would make to improve the game. Overhaul the economic systems Completly fix the AI Make gang wars feel realHave enemy bosses switch locations, so you have to gain on intellegence first for a suprise hit Perhaps require a certain ammount of captured businesses before confronting a boss? Give other ways to win the game besides killing boses Overall, there a tons more suggestions I could make but I'm sure many more players will make them as well. This game is in need of a No Man's Sky type overhaul. The foundations are there, yet this game needs to work out all the kinks, bind the systems together, and vastly improve the AI's strategy for this game to become the ultimate gangster game it was marketed as and I hope it can become.

_childDocuments_.review: Empire of Sin is a combination of  a gangster management sim and an x-com-like turn based strategy game.Neither are deep enough to really feel satisfying and both keep getting in the way of each other.I finished an entire playthrough out of spite.On the management layer, you open new illegal ventures, upgrade their security, profitability or discreetness with the push of a button. The numbers change slightly and you build up a criminal empire over time.You also manage relations with the police and other gangs, but often these appear only as pop ups with X gang requesting Y treaty with you, often at the expense of your honour because they previously broke an agreement with you within the last 30 days, which the game does not communicate to you in any meaningful manner. In fact most of the inner workings of the management layer are obfuscated.Lucky then, that you don't really need to pay attention to the management beyond ensuring you are making enough money and booze to fuel your empire.The other layer of the game is the turn based combat game.This is where the management becomes mostly irrelevant. You can attack venues run by common thugs for an endless stream of extremely easy battles and resources, all without upsetting rival gangs. This creates a fantastic risk free infinite funds tap to keep your gang well supplied. Also, no matter how easy these battles get, you can't rely on auto resolve. A battle that when played manually ends in a single turn will still result in injuries and risk for your gangsters when auto resolved. Go figure.The two games that EOS is trying to be get in the way of each other. The management game becomes pointless with the infinite funds injection from the combat. And the combat isn't varied or rewarding enough because it's just there to prop up the management side with something to do while you wait for your working girls to bring in that cash.EOS is a fantastic example of a developer spending far too much time polishing a bad idea rather than just making sure the game design is solid before pushing forward. Also most of the bugs the game had at launch (and there were a LOT) have now been fixed. You can't fix bad game design though.Skip this one. Wait for the zombie/ghost of Eidos to release a worthy successor to the original Gangsters.

_childDocuments_.review: Bottom line up front: Paradox already made buckets off of everyone that has bought this game, and they really don't care about the state of the game.  This is an MVP; the execs know it (and don't care), the product owners know it but pushed for something half decent, the devs know it and are slaved with work, and the playtesters know it sucks.  We'll only start getting quality games at launch when people stop pre-ordering/buying them at launch.The game is fun, but too easy.  XCOM but the aliens are Italians is perfect, except the Italians are fat and weak.  The game has long-term potential, but the economy isn't thought out and the fights are too easy.  There's so much that could be had with the alcohol procurement/delivery process, but instead there's a shell of a system there.  Additionally, I was really hoping to be able to customize the different rackets, but instead it's a phone-game-esque "upgrade this but oh wait you can rush it immedately for .5x!' ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.  And why bother since you can just take something else over in 10 minutes with little combat skill.The game was certainly released too early--but all the negative reviews surprised by that shouldn't be.  This is, after all, a Paradox game, and this has been their M.O. since Stellaris originally launched (if not before then).  It will eventually become a strong game.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game — I really do — because I actually enjoy these turn-based tactical combat games such as XCOM, Fire Emblem, Wastelands, Gears Tactics, Age of Wonders:Planetfall, Phantom Doctrine, Phoenix Point, Mutant Year Zero: Road to Eden, Battletech, Shadowrun series, and of course Final Fantasy Tactics. When I saw this game had that combat style AND it let you run a criminal empire that expanded into a living world in a deeper strategy game sense I was excited for that experience. Then I played the game. TLDR: Overall my initial reactions are the game is a really shallow experience. That empire management stuff and the economic systems in play are very shallow in particular. After combat you get to take over the buildings. There is little to no difference between the rackets though. When it asks you what you want it to be there is really only three choices. They each make you money, some more than others, they each have an upkeep mechanic you gotta pay, and that's about it. No difference between the three (Speakeasy / Brothel / Casino) though and you can literally spam only one type and be just fine. The Breweries are needed or you won't make any money in your Speakeasies. They need you to supply them with alcohol. You can trade excess booze for cash too which is a broken exploit right now because you can disguise it as Whiskey. From there you just spend the cash you make on more speakeasies (or upgrades) to make more money until you need more booze. And do the cycle again and again. It always seems to be the same repeat. Not a lot of depth here. It think the game's economy would be way more interesting if there was some kind of supply and demand system that is more robust than the preferred booze type that changes each month. Where if say your neighborhood of Chicago was oversaturated with speakeasies then it would become harder to attract customers and booze would have to be sold cheaper. Which means lower profits if you invest in only speakeasies. It would incentivize players to then try to monopolize a particular business in that neighborhood and cut out the competition maybe choosing brothels, casinos, or something else instead of a speakeasy. Hotels bring in more customers and double your synergies. If you have say three of a kind of the same racket type they give you like a 10% bonus. I think you can only have one Hotel per neighborhood though. The other thing you spend your cash on is hiring henchmen. Though the combat is so dull you really don't need a full 10/10.The game revolves around the combat and that isn't even all that special. The maps are tiny first of all. The combat is over in a matter of turns even when you're trying to take down a bosses safehouse. This is because the OP boss abilities. The other major flaw to the combat is the lack of environmental interactions. They are virtually non-existent. You would think people would be climbing over benches or vehicles to scramble to get out of the way of a gun fight that just broke out. And the player could be using the vehicles or other things in the environment as explosions or using explosives to destroy cover. It's very basic half cover, full cover, and flanking the enemy. Half the time there is no penalty to just running up next to them to get 100% and the kill but leaving yourself outside of cover. The AI is not very good. And when you kill a boss the game doesn't even replace the dead with procedural generated one, or even lesser factions. One would expect some lesser criminal would at least try to take up and assume the mantle and seize control in that power vacuum. I honestly think the combat is a step back from previous games in this genre. Instead of improving upon games like XCOM or Gears Tactics even Empire of Sin just does the bare minimum. The characters ( think xcom soldiers) do have classes and each class has different abilities you can choose in the skill trees but there is a lot of overlapping abilities even amongst the classes.  They badly need an auto resolve function for the combat because you'll get sucked into repetitive fights back to back to back when you're trying to manage your empire and forced to fight as your guards. I don't mind this every now and then I would even choose to fight the fight but you have no choice. It's every time you gotta go in and fight the fight.Also they really need a better way to compare weapons. Since your constantly upgrading and changing it's not a fun experience.  The UI functions and information is actually really shoddy. For being a strategy game and a Paradox published game you would expect more. Half the time I was scrolling over symbols and couldn't find a way to tell what it did or explain it and where i was getting it from. Not even a name to let me know what it was. Did I mention there is no manual even?I haven't even encountered any of the game breaking bugs reportedly out there either. The game is just a hot mess but there's hope that they'll fix it in that it just released and by and large it's been negatively received by the community. They got to do something. What do I like about the game? I love the setting and the theme. The time period of prohibition-era mobster ran Chicago has always been a fun time to play around in. The violence and intrigue of backstabbing and killing former partners in crime. The musical score is pretty good too.  It has a lot of style going for it and you can tell it was a labor of love for at least some of the devs. The game has it's potential but that's where my praise for this game ends. The theme alone doesn't even come close to outweighing the issues I have with it's design or mechanics. Which leads me to leave this game with a negative review rather than a positive one.

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay is way too basic, disappointingly one-note, you basically do the same thing over and over again. The environment on the surface looks pretty good but when you look under the hood it starts to feel inauthentic (were there really that many lady cops and male strippers in "1920s Prohibition-era Chicago"?) Not enough gangsters to choose from to keep things interesting, the interactions between your gang members are extremely lame and limited given how few of them there are (there should be a lot more, as a trade-off for such a modest roster) and the fact you can't send your no-name thugs out on patrol missions and such like the AI can do just feels like a missing functionality. Can't recommend this game in its current state, certainly not at full price, but there's definitely a good game hiding in here somewhere if it was given some serious work. (But I understand it's not being supported anymore so I wouldn't expect any improvements.)

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoying the game, notched up the difficulty one above the preset as i think people are playing on regular and finding it too easy, started out easy but difficulty definitely picks up once you start going to war with the real gangs.Not had any issues with being able to rush bosses, attempted it after taking most of their rackets in a neighbourhood and found they had guys with extra armour and half decent weapons, I actually had to flee. Regular thugs seem a bit dumb, however they tend to be melee and shotgun users so try get close range, but the tougher mobs have a bit more about them.Side missions add a nice bit of variety, trading and doing deals is quite interesting to build rep with gangs you may wish to keep at bay.Only came across one bug, which looks like a bit of a UI issue but didn't impair my game play.Overall this is enjoyable for what it is, I'm not looking for X-Com or some other comparisons when playing this, I'm enjoying this because I have a fondness for organised crime and strategy and this ticks both those boxes. I can only imagine this will improve in the future.The animations etc don't bother me, I knew watching the game play what I had to expect and they ain't that off putting. If you buy this game, notch up the difficulty and it will be way more enjoyable, don't expect to steamroll through everything and prepare for some real struggles.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not sure what other reviewers are so disappointed by - I love this game! It's exactly what I was expecting. Xcom style turn-based combat, with a good amount of challenge but not so much it gets impossible.  Fun characters with several very different feeling gangs/bosses. Yes, it can get a little redundant as far as the later game neighborhood takeovers/development goes, but that's true for a lot of these types of games. _childDocuments_.review: This game has potential, but I do not believe you should pay full price for it at it's current state. While the core game play loop is solid it becomes noticeable fairly quickly that there is a general lack of depth to almost every system this game has. At the end of the day it feels empty and repetitive, and It didn't take long for me to lose all desire to continue playing, especially with other grand strategy games available that are fully realized.I have high confidence that in time this game will improve. Almost certainly at the cost of the consumer via DLC, and probably some free content and updates as well. But, overall you will  be getting a better value a year down the road or even longer, when you can buy the game and necessary future DLC on sale. If you want to support the developers, by all means, I did and will wait out more content. But do not feel obligated to play an incomplete product, it just isn't as fun as it should be.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: I have not quit this game via the menu once. It was always ALT+F4 because it locked up. I really want to like it, but it's almost unplayable.Not a great game in its current state. And since this is a full release for $40 or even $60 if you get the bigger versions, I expected a lot more from it.The worst parts for me:- Soft locking bugs that pop up out of nowhere. If you begin a sit-down, chances are the game bugs out and you have to ALT-F4 it. If you start combat and two people have the early overwatch skill = soft lock. If there are animations that are supposed to be played, but they can't for whatever reason = soft lock. - No idea whats going on in gang wars. If you end up in one, your properties are suddenly swarmed by goons not a second later. And you can't bring you boss to a fight once it already started, leaving you with a few ill equipped guards. There is no auto-resolve, so you HAVE to fight manually 10 guys, with your 2. I also ended up in a war with some obscure faction out of nowhere, even though there was never a screen showing me this. When I tried to sit down with that faction leader to see wtf is going on, the game soft locked. - Weapon balance. Shotguns are effing useless, submachineguns overpowered.- Businesses have a weird cash flow, hard to read. But its certainly not enough money to do anything. If you want money, buy swill, disguise it as whiskey, sell it to a minor faction for brutal profits. They wont even care that you swindled them. And even if they did, they are never doing anything. There is a solid game under the hood here, but even the simplest quality of life improvements are not available and the bugs are horrendous. A lot of care has been put into the dialogues, probably curtesy of the Romeros, but most people skip excessive dialogue anyway and it's a very, very minor part of the game. The time and money would have been spent better at literally any other area of the game (bug fixing, polish, management, combat...you name it). I hope we will get a GOOD gangster simulation eventually, but this aint it.

_childDocuments_.review: Do not buy this game, it's a serious rip off, especially don't pay for the second DLC, it doesn't exist, and never will.This game is a complete rip off, and the developer, publisher, and even steam should be ashamed of the way they are still selling this product with a 2nd DLC that the publisher has already stated will never be delivered as the game has been "archived". For those, like myself, that pre-order this game having already paid for that second DLC. which as I just said they have no plans to ever deliver. They took money from people and never delivered the product that was paid for.The game itself isn't terrible, but yet at the same time isn't great either.Positives:- The visuals are nice.- The sound is good.- Combat is okay, fun at first.- Skills/Upgrades - it has a reasonable list of skills you can learn as each member of the team levels up. I won't go into detail, but some are useful, others not so useful.Negatives:- Combat - as I said it's okay, but it quickly becomes repetitive - AI regularly makes very poor decisions during combat.- - At the start of combat, they won't enter via the door you actually clicked on, they'll be randomly placed inside the building. Randomness in a game like this isn't necessarily a bad thing, but to me being essentially teleported to the opposite side of the building is a bit jarring. To me there are better ways to create randomess to this type of game. It also kills any real ability to try different strategies/tactics in combat, since you're just randomly placed, you can't choose how you want to approach combat.- - As combat triggers, they'll scatter, but the places they choose to take cover in often make no sense as they provide cover in the wrong direction, and leave themselves completely exposed in the direction fire will actually be coming from.- Businesses (legal/illegal) - too limited, not enough variety.- The city/map felt like a bunch of disconnected towns rather than one large city.- It HAD potential - however as noted above this game will never reach its true potential, it's been abandoned.- Dialogue is terribly cheesy, and the same lines a repeated over and over again. Not sure if it was bad writing or bad acting, I suspect a combo of both. As an example, you can fully upgrade one of your own businesses, and still, when you walk in with your chosen boss they'll regularly say "What's this dump?".... it's one of your own businesses you idiot, or worse, it's your home/safe house you dumbo.- What is there is good, but ultimately it lacks content and would need a few large DLC updates to be a worthwhile game.Would I recommend this game to others... NO, NO WAY!Paradox and Romero should be embarrassed to have released this game in the state that it was in. They should be ashamed of themselves for taking people's money and then running away without delivering what was promised, and yes, it was officially stated two DLC would be delivered. Avoid Romero games at all costs, a game about criminals, and in my opinion, made by a bunch of criminals. Will not be buying a game by Romero ever again.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: neither the combat or management in this game is good or innovative. It's not worth its price. I'm just glad I made that decision fast enough to get a refund.This game is a real flop on release, which looks like it might be becoming a trend for Paradox games. I don't have the faith that this game will be fixed like they're currently doing with Imperator though.In short, the game had a great premise but completely failed to innovate. It's buggy and quite dull compared to similar games, and certainly not worth its price point. The only way I'd recommend this game as-is is if it cost peanuts. The combat is in the realm of X-COM, but so much worse. Enemies routinely leave full cover to charge right into your guys. Bosses are OP, I played as the Vice Kings boss whose special ability allows him to unload an entire pistol clip into any enemies in range and killed the tutorial boss in 1 turn. You mostly expand early on by attacking unaligned thugs. The generation of these fights is tedious at best, you'll be plopped down (probably surrounded) in a construction site with a bunch of thugs who will try to rush you. There are two resources to manage in Empire of Sin. Money and alcohol. You start out with barely any income in either of these and are expected to expand. In the tutorial you are immediately pushed into the red by hiring 2 underlings, each of which has a minimum wage of $300. You don't need them this early. Paying to upgrade your rackets doesn't pay off nearly as quickly as going around fighting thugs and establishing new ones and you don't need hirelings to do this.Diplomacy is handled quite poorly. Every time you meet a new gang they will threaten you, and you have the option to threaten, negotiate with, or attack them. If you choose one of the first two then they will invariably demand that you pay them $2000 to avoid a relations penalty, possibly in addition to the penalty from threatening them.The voice acting is ok I guess. I wasn't really interested in the characters but I didn't have very long to get to know them. Story richness is probably the strongest suit of this game.

And some dumb decisions, like how you can click on a slot to promote someone but it does nothing. Instead you promote them from a small key command written in text on their character screen? Lots of overlapping information, most of which is useless, and other major rookie level problems. Overall, don't bother with this game. It never goes deep enough in the moment to moment play, nor in the strategy elements, to be worth your time. It will be really fun for a couple hours and then you have seen everything.

Overall I'm rather disappointed for having pre-purchased the premium. And I highly suggest waiting for a discount, maybe holiday sale or something.Overall what could make this better to start with? Aside from the clamoring bugs (standing deals being stuck ongoing even after killing the boss of the mafia you had the deal with), or lacking sense of progression, I suggest devs extend the parlor types you can have --businesses and rackets extend further than just 'brothel' or 'casino' or 'brewery' or 'speakeasy' I mean really, flesh it out and give us more in the realm of depth... _childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Not a great buy, but you may consider it if you want xcom tactical combat with a mafia atmosphere, and you are not bothered by this studio's political agenda. Dont buy if you expect a well finished nicely designed game with replayability, or if you are bothered by SJW themes.Visuals are on par. Sound effects are acceptable. User interface acceptable but console friendly and not optimised for PC. Story is average, slightly disconnected from the actual gameplay and unrelated to xcom type 'challenge' based on time and escalation. Those are your 'ok' parts of the game.On the pros side of things, we have to admit xcom based tactical combat is still a great thing. The mafia 'build your empire' genre works and leaves plenty of room for a violent ambience.Now, onto the bad, the sad, the horrible, the unforgivable parts: the game is glitchy, buggy, unfinished in many ways; progression is not well worked out; characters are 'set in stone' leaving no room for customization; replayability is limited; difficulty level unmanageable; repetition is everpresent (same maps for each building size, yes thats 3, plus one for safehouses); poor class design; poor economy design (could have mattered but not here); strategical layer inexistant.Now, this game also has a rare personal agenda. The sexualization of grandmothers (and everyone else even when you dont want to hear about it), the presence of unsanctionned homosexual relationships (constant amongst your own crew) along with a ridiculous emphasis on race and gender 'inclusion' makes it very hard to be honest about the game but also progressive in ones mindset. Comon, just let players choose the gender and race of whoever it is they want to play as and with. I usually have no problem with sexual content, but this game forces on me a lot of stuff that I didnt pay for, and thats unnacceptable. After doing research on this, I found out sadly the studio's owner is a woman with her own agenda. I dont recommend getting involved with any comments on this game and studio, I felt I had to do it because I have nothing to lose.Look, I am just a player, just a gamer, keep your politics out of my games. I hope you guys enjoyed my HONEST review of Empire of Sin. I did play and finish the game, am glad I did, and I would not recommend it unless you really miss XCom combat and dont mind a little 1920 prohibition era atmosphere. I was very aggravated by the hidden political stuff in there, and midly annoyed at the lack of polish of the game. Also of note is the fact that everything 'art' is a level above everything 'game design' which can be surprising.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, took a bit to come to a consesus about this game so let's get to the parts that matter.  Empire of Sin is a very simplified Gangster style XCOM, set in the 1920s during the Prohibition Era: Your goal? Conquer Chicago.  If a combat heavy (not even joking about this part) game of such style is of interest to you, then yes, I do recommend it.If you are however interested in a management focused game, or perhaps not having to fight (every) engagement all manual like, then I recommend sticking clear.  It's a game with a lot of potential, but I personally don't see going past more than one full run before moving onto something else.  Maybe only coming back once in a few months during a dry spell with other games.Each boss you can choose feels somewhat unique, even if their conquest of Chicago plays out largely the same.  While you certainly can spend time upgrading your empire's businesses, there will eventually be so many, and virtually no difference between them, you'll just want whatever increases profit enough to equip your gangsters for upcoming wars with your rivals.  Which can be short and brutal by essentially going straight for the leader, a departure from the methodical approaches of the old Hothouse Gangsters games of yore.Overall I'd say the game's relatively average, but definitely something you can sink hours into and have a degree of fun with.  Whether you'd have the endurance to take each boss onto the path of glory as Chicago's rising kingpin, well that's up to you.I myself, did get my money's worth, even despite various bugs showing up.  Not that detail counts for anything. :PHesitant buyers I strongly recommend waiting for a sale first.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, 7 / 10. Most annoying bugs were resolved in the first few days and the game runs just fine now. Its XCOM-style turn-based combat, fighting for control of illegal businesses, getting into wars with other factions, and ultimately trying to come out on top. You run a crew of 'real' gangsters, up to ten, and from 5 'classes', which can be further customized with a tree of talents to choose from, and further with their gear, weapons, etc. You manage various seedy businesses, but there's not much depth there. Missions drive some storylines, but aside from the first few that give you alot of cash to initially get started in the gameworld, they don't do much. The real fun is in taking over existing businesses from other factions, and growing your own empire. Hired Gangsters are powerful, and expensive, so your main goal is to have enough businesses to support both hiring, keeping, and outfitting your gangsters, so that you can stand up to the other major factions.Atmosphere is high quality, theres fun diversity in gangsters including their dress and special abilities, and the combat is challenging at higher difficulties. I'd play on the standard starting difficulty if you're not familiar with XCOM style games, and a higher difficulty if you are. The navigation of the world and in combat is a bit tricky to learn, but once you do you'll appreciate why they did it that way - becomes very easy.Big Pros:* Combat is fun* Leveling up and diversifying your crew's abilities and equipment has depth and value* Visuals and navigation are clear, clean, and useful, once you get used to them* Obvious room for growth in mechanics through future content/DLCs from great initial frameworkBig Cons:* AI on lower settings atleast, is weak, both in combat and their management of their businesses* Police don't seem to do anything but slightly annoy you, no matter how many of them you shoot* Current Balance around Safehouses is broken and allows too much progress too quickly* Too much of the game is not skippable, which is especially annoying at the start of a game talking to all of the factions and getting raided - an autoresolve would be niceIf development is continued on this game, the Con's can disappear quickly, and the Pro's will expand, so I recommend this game in its current state.*Says 56 hours but it was just running in background - more like 20 hours.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game quite a bit, as I'm a pretty huge fan of XCOM-style turn-based strategy games. However, I have three pretty major complaints with it:1) The game is too easy. Like, waaaaay too easy. I love Paradox, and have a long history with their games (particularly CK2 and Stellaris). Empire of Sin follows in their footsteps in that you can reach a position that is essentially unassailable very quickly relative to the overall length of the game. I know AI "cheats" are annoying to some strategy game players, but the AI in Empire of Sin really needs some hidden bonuses to money/alcohol production and/or free facility upgrades. The AI is also pretty weak in the tactical aspect of the game. Even on the hardest difficulty, the enemy AI is not particularly tactical. They don't attempt to flank. They often use suppressing fire or overwatch when they could take a killing shot. In fact, the only difference I observed in different difficulty levels is that enemies have (slightly) more armour the higher the difficulty. Enemies should get a bonus to hit chance at least, even if it's not possible for them to get "smarter" on higher difficulty levels. 2) There's a lot of stuff you can do that should have a strategic effect, but literally none of it matters. You can just hire 10 gangsters and run around town steamrolling everything. You can upgrade your security, but it doesn't really matter. Just find the enemies wandering around the map with the rat icon above their head and kill them with your 10-gangster goon squad before they can take out your facilities. Cop activity is tracked, but even on the highest difficulty, it's no problem to operate at full capacity without the cops taking any real interest in your businesses. There is no strategic element to expanding your empire. Just... keep some money in reserve (usually 1 weeks' earnings is enough), and upgrade as many facilities as you can. That's not strategy. It's just busy work. You can assign a lieutenant to a safehouse, where they give a very minor bonus to the neighborhood's production and exist as a last line of defence if your neighborhood is attacked, but gaining money is not challenging (so you don't need the bonus), and your gangster is more valuable as part of your hit squad than waiting around playing defence. You can assign a mole, but that takes your gangster out of commission for six months and the effect is incredibly minor. Your mole can potentially steal some funds, damage a racket, or even assassinate a rival boss, but the % chance is incredibly low relative to the long time you lose a gangster to being a mole and in the six months a mole is gone you can easily (you guessed it) take your 10-man hit squad and take all of a rival gang's money, rackets, and assassinate their boss. Your gangsters gain loyalty and morale so quickly and easily that those numbers never made a difference to the game.There's a diplomacy screen, but it's also mostly pointless. Theoretically, you can buy other bosses out without fighting them, but you have to have been protecting them for 3 months first and the AI is (surprisingly) smart enough to break protection agreements when it gets close enough to possible to buy them out. There isn't really any consequences for refusing another boss. You might lose rep or honour, but those are again one of those numbers that appears like it could do something strategic, but doesn't really. Enemy bosses propose business agreements, but then rescind them randomly a few weeks later. 3) Game-stopping bugs. I only encountered the one, but it was enough for me to give up on the game. There's a story mission where you go to a casino to meet the mayor and chief of police. Then the game locks. It's a known issue, and has been a known issue for several months. I feel like a game-stopping bug in the middle of a main story quest is a pretty significant flaw.Suggestions:-Notoriety gain is too fast. I've maxed my notoriety after taking over a single neighborhood. Notoriety gain should be significantly slowed, and, in addition to controlling the power of the gangsters you can recruit, it should also control the number of gangsters you can have in your hit squad, starting with 3 gangsters at the start (so you can have a team of 4 with your boss), and expanding to a squad of 5 at 500 notoriety and maxing out at 6 with 1000 notoriety. Only being able to bring 6 gangsters into any combat would significantly up the challenge. I'd slow notoriety gain by capping some sources of notoriety. Like, after 100, you no longer gain notoriety for killing random thugs, or after 500, you only gain notoriety for killing enemy bosses and completing quests.-Take a page from Stellaris and give some enemy bosses an "advanced start" (use a slider at game creation so folks who hate AI cheating can turn it off). These bosses should gain more territory to start, as well as a huge bonus to their racket upgrades, cash earning, and booze production.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, so having played 10 hours of this game, I'm still somewhat torn whether or not I'd recommend it. I think I'll start from the top and slowly move my way towards the bottom and be ready for plenty of "however" or "but!"I really like the games style, music, atmosphere, and the various mob families and I do enjoy how each of them come with their own perks in terms of combat and business wise. However, I do kinda wish they also had some negatives like if you play as the Tong mob family you'll have tougher times making friends with the Italian mob or they might demand higher prices for specific things you wanna trade with them. The gameplay is a mix of X-com and business management, you need to buy/take over buildings and thus establish various rackets from speakeasies to casinos, it's pretty to wrap your brain around it. But! I do wish there was more nitty-gritty to this setup, like say allowing players to pick a branch of how they wanna further progress a specific type of business say turning a simple brothel into a strip joint or maybe a small-time casino into a poker club or betting house, because as it is you are given a progression but it's simple upgrade stuff that you just need the right sum of money for. Now, this game isn't exactly plot-driven, it's more close to Hearts of Iron or Crusader Kings in terms that you pick your starting family, you get a line of quests to do, but also get various side quests and I will say from the 3 families I tried out the main quests do indeed differ, when it comes to sidequests it's kinda wonky I've seen a few different ones but seems some do indeed repeat. Since the combat is Xcom style, it does present some challenges, I've seen people claim it's too easy and I dunno what I was missing but the more high-level soldiers of rival families can def put the hurt on you, especially since they can hire other "elite" mobsters as you can and if you're playing on normal difficulty. But! With that said, the AI does sometimes pull pretty dumb moves by either going into the open or hiding right next to your guy where you can land clean shots on them. Oh, yes, this game has elite mobsters you can hire as you level up your notoriety, however, some mobsters won't work for you if you have a specific guy they dislike on your team and some can build relationships and even open some sidequests for them. Which I must say, adds a nice flavor but you'll probably pick your favorites pretty early. There's also various weapons/gear you can obtain by either searching for Big Jim Colosimo crates, during missions or buying from the black market, usually, it's guns (the rarer the weapon the more damage it does), gear, or trinkets that add some bonuses. Now, I did run into some glitches during my playthrough, one was a game-breaking one that happened during me playing for the Tongs for some reason, I couldn't find a way to progress after fighting off the attack on my safe house. I didn't find the mechanic for the market all that hard as well, since it's just about making sure your breweries make the right type of booze and making sure you have upgraded the production and storage capacity but again I do wish it gotten more detailed when it came to working on your various rackets. Now, would I recommend this game? Mmm...Hard to say, it's not flawless and there are def bugs that need patching up, graphic wise it looked fine and its combat isn't bad but can be given a challenge on a higher difficulty, I like how each family has various abilities and the characters have their own special skills, but kinda wish there was also negative trait aspects that would make you decide how to balance your alliances properly. I do wish the business mechanic allowed for more choices on how to set up the business, I've seen people that we're hoping for Gangsters game, but as I said it feels more like a more compact version of HoF and Crusader Kings since you can even set how many families you wanna face off against. I will say this if you wanna have a Mobster Turn-Based/RPG/Bussiness management type game, give this a shot. If you're hoping for a Gangsters type game? Sorry, this ain't it and I fully admit I want a similar game (for me it would Chicago 1932 Don Capone though), but this game isn't bad. I'd say it's def more fun than Omerta City of Gangsters was, but if you think a price for such a game is too high then grab it on sale and may enjoy yourself and prob have fun trying the various families or seeing if you can beat 'em all or not.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright...Where to start? a couple of months ago I reviewed a similar game that I was expecting called Company of crime that is the same gangster setting but with a different timeline and in England. One of the biggest concerns was the bad design of combat and the fact that you can't explore the city like Empire of Sin. You might ask why I am starting my review with this, and the answer is that people like me that use to play Gangsters Organized Crime back in the day have been waiting for a solid game that can bring that amazing concept once again. On that note, let's start with what I think so far about the game and why I would recommend it. First and foremost, even with some people saying that is null and gets repetitive the game is still fun. The diplomacy might not be relevant but you do enjoy the sit-downs were you can actually negotiate booze, war with factions, and much more. Now the con on this part is that the conversations are too repetitive and the animation sometimes feels not real. For example, Capone always raises his hand the same way for all threatening responses and that feels really simplistic. I do hope this gets fixed. Again diplomacy at this point might not be very efficient, but I do believe it makes the gaming experience more meaningful. Please Devs, if you are reading this, work more on this and add more victory conditions. At this point, the only one you can have is by killing all the gangs and there is no fun in having alliances because they are meaningless. You have rackets, but there is no front for them. How are you going to have an illegal business without any legal business at all? There should be interactions with more NPCs like city officials, judges, witness and such that would add more immersion to the game. The game does feel like a strategy game but sometimes is too cartoonish. For example, some gangsters really don't make sense and this I know can be done better. Also, please add: banks that we can rob and make business in, hotels with more meaningful management, and more rackets. The combat in this game is good but sometimes is dumb. For example, the AI does need some work but for the major part is solid. One issue that combat has is that when you have a lot of guards and gangsters in a small speakeasy, it is very hard to tell who is who because the colors are not very helpful and all the guards look the same. It would be nice if the game could add some type of drive-by feature to kill the guards in front of a building, which would add more to the immersion of the game. Finally, and I don't want to sound that I'm complaining too much, but the game can add the stuff I mention and deliver a true 1920 gangster experience that will make fans of the genre like myself happy. On the bug notes so far I haven't had any issues on my PC, no issues with corrupt save game files, and crashes so on that part I can't say anything bad about it.so I must say at this point 6/10. It is a fun first version of the game but It could be way better. It is a bit pricey, so f you are looking to save money, wait for more work to be done on it and then go for it. But do I recommend this game? Yes, it is a solid concept that just needs some work. Hope this review gets to someone in Romero Games. Thanks for getting this far on this review btw. Cheers and remember power is taken never given!

_childDocuments_.review: Right now, as of 9th Jan '21, the game is not something i would suggest to anyone.The game has a lot of things i love, starting from the fact that's in 1920's Chicago, in the heat of Prohibition-induced criminality. It has the same combat style i love from XCOM and such, with different classes bringing different ways to play encounters. It alsohas the management side of the coin, bringing somewhat intresting combinations of rackets you can stack up for different and better bonuses, all the while choosing who to assign to each different neighbourhood to boost its capabilities.All of this and i still wouldnt suggest it to a friend.The game SUPPOSEDLY has an AUTOSAVE feature. It's ♥♥♥♥. Plain and simple. In nearly 15 hours of game i have seen it work TWO times, while it also takes a few seconds to save. The autosaves are WAAAAAAY to far and few for the amount of times the game crashes.I'm fairly sure i've lost ATLEAST a third of the progress i made in those near 15 hours due to random crashes/softlocks: the game will engage you in a fight and magically it soflocks, nothing you can do. Captured a racket? the game might softlock. Ambushing someone? game might softlock. Entering a racket you own? 1/5 chance it softlocks. playing your combat round? guess what, it probably will softlock every few hours or so.There is nothing you can do. There are a thousand instances in which the game might softlock that will screw you over ROYALLY, expecially considering the game probably autosaves once every few hours. _childDocuments_.review: This game- Wow- I would like to start the review by saying it is not as terrible as people say it is, there is the basis and concept for a good game here. But it is not very well done. So instead of following what everybody else is saying, i'm going to write down my own personal issues with it.The game plays a lot like Xcom, I have never played the game but looking back on it I should of played that instead. The game is not as large scale as you think it is, as you start out with one gangster who had a ominous reputation. I started out as Al-capone because its a game about gangsters. Now, here is my main issue with the game. You start out with one guy and if you finish the tutorial three. The people you can hire are effected by your fame, or if you help them with a boring side-quest that allows you to get them earlier or for cheaper. This sounds like a okay system, a lot of games use it like Fallout New Vegas, the difference being that the game was story focused and you got invested into the people in your rag-tag team. In this game, they are not designed to be disposable- However, they feel disposable. If one dies they are gone forever. If you loose a good team mate this can be a issue or if you loose too many early game you will have nobody. If your boss dies then you loose so this leads to a spiral where new players assume you can hire the bodyguards (which the AI use as a replacement for the people you can hire) so you can end up either in two situations, the boss is the only one left (which is basically a game over) or you have AI on your ass because they have a infinite number of attacking forces. You have three people. The game tries to counter this by letting you have guards which can level up scattered around your large empire. Mid game-The main issues with mid-game is that by now the early game gangsters that you can hire are probably all dead. Either by your suicidal hiring system or maybe even the AI might of hired some they are set to hire. At this point you probably have a crew of 4, not including you, if they are high level enough maybe you are even at war with some AI factions- This is personally one of the biggest problems I have with this game, the AI has a infinite number of troops against your ill defended speakeasies and breweries. This would not be a problem if you actually levelled up your breweries however chances are that you have not. Another problem is that when I played this game there was no actual auto-resolve meaning you had to fight every single battle, even the ones you were going to loose. The AI can send out a ridiculous number of auto-scouts, and I have no idea why they even made that a thing because if they choose to attack you and you are on your own you are royally ♥♥♥♥♥♥. Seeing as we are talking about the way you make money in this game, its pretty broken. The more footholds you have in your owned territory such as speakeasies, brothels, hotels and breweries means the more customers are likely to visit. This makes it a race against time as you try to fight against the infinite AI troops to settle as much speakeasies or casinos as possible, since those are the only ones worth placing in my experience. I will give credit where it is due, hotels are pretty well done. They are a total gamble as they can either result in a big win or a big loss. As they attract more customers and can provide a bonus if placed near a brothel (; . But that does not really ease out the fact that if you don't place them, there really is no consequence. At this point in the game I controlled a entire neighbourhood and was in the process of taking over another, and I was rich, all this just placing speakeasies and the occasional casino. Really shows that it does not matter what you place. Another thing that just does not matter is the quality of the drink. I had the worst quality on my most recent save, the worst quality is so bad that is called "piss" yet this did not effect anything, in my eyes it just cut costs.Late game-Late game is uneventful, by now you probably control 2 neighbourhoods, maybe 3 if you are better than me, and are virtually invincible unless you get caught out on your own by a AI scouting party, this is where the real issue with the game became so much more obvious to me- Bugs, lots and lots of BUGS. animation breaking, sometimes just a game crash while trying to auto save. The game almost became unplayable at some point for me. e.g- the turns would take so long for some reason, that I thought the game had froze. Especially in big battles, which will happen often thanks to the amount of dumb AI ramming into you non-stop. It would give you a two minute breather sometimes, but considering you could not autoresolve at the time I was playing the game (even now the autoresolve is so clunky you will probably either win or loose based on a single thing) it was a nightmare. At one point I got sick of it and took a break- Such a long break that I never actually came back to it. Ever.Conclusion- The game is pretty sucky, i'm also going to mention the fact that they are releasing DLC and the most of the issues mentioned here are still not fixed. In conclusion, this game is not worth your time, I wish this 15 hours could of been claimed back, I could of got a girlfriend, talked to my family, maybe even got better grades- But since i'm writing this review to you right now what do you think my grades were /: . 4/10, go check out my friends review on Evil Genius 2 instead or maybe buy a decent game idk

_childDocuments_.review: Review 3.3/10.I really wanted to love this game. I'm still going to play it because I like the genre- but buyers need to have expectations of an early access title as opposed to a released game. This is the reason you don't rush a game to hit a deadline. I will update this review with more information as I play the game more and the clear bugs get fixed. Combat is buggy, sometimes causing you to have to restart the level/load a save. For example, even playing the tutorial my combat screen failed to load in so I was just staring at the characters unable to move/shoot or do anything. Playing as Al C. you will inevitably end up firing into the wrong direction with your special without a foreseeable cause, as seen in the developer stream. What a shame.As other reviewers have discussed, the game is a rinse and repeat with little depth. Empire building is essentially walk up and down the block taking over every business you see followed by the same activities the next block over. Combat is compared to x-com; however, I find the percentages to be incredibly off within this game to the point that they can essentially be ignored.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games where it's hard to decide whether to recommend it or not.  The game itself, in my 2 hours of play, didn't have any bugs or weird issues but the structure of the game itself makes this a lot less fun than I was hoping.I came into this hoping for a strategic crime family simulator with x-com style combat.  You sort of get that from this game but it's rendered a lot less fun by confusing menus, too much stuff going on, and a frustrating real-time with pause feature.In the game you control a squad of mobsters and can run around a map to attack other factions or neutral thugs to either ransack, destroy, or take over their rackets (the games term for illicit businesses falling into one of five or six varieties).  All of that is, in theory, good however the financial aspect of the game is pretty confusing.  The game seems to favor rapid expansion into rackets rather than upgrading the rackets you have.  I made this mistake early on by spending my early game cash improving my rackets rather than expanding and was stuck in this cycle of having to assault and ransack neutral locations to earn money or go to war with an enemy faction with my 3 gangsters.  The game's tutorial has you recruit two additional gangsters and that ends up costing you $600 in wages when my rackets (2 speakeasies and a brewery) earned somewhere like $400.The financial aspect was manageable but what really frustrated me was the absolute constant bombardment of missions and communications and events.  Within the first 20 minutes of the tutorial ending I was invited to war in conjunction with another faction.  I assumed it was in the neighborhood I occupied but, no, it was in fact a separate neighborhood I'd never been to.  I then was getting attacked in new businesses I got as a result of the war and didn't even know where they were and didn't have the ability to pay to upgrade them due to cashflow issues.I fully admit part of my issues are due to poor play and lack of familiarity with all the systems but the game honestly came off as a convoluted mess that couldn't really decide if it was a strategy game or an X-com game.  I know a lot of reviews have complained about bugs but I didn't really encounter any other than the game seemed very particular about clicking and sometimes something wouldn't work for no apparent reason and then all the sudden start working.  To me, the bigger issue is that the game itself feels haphazard and chaotic in an unfun way.  I never got to feel like I was a crime boss.  I felt like I was a street thug surrounded by bigger fish with the game constantly trying to pull me in 15 different directions and me having no clue what was happening half the time.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a great potential, however it is ruined by utter repetitiveness.The start of the game is nice as you establish yourself as a gang in the city, going through main & side quests. However suddenly the main quest line ends (or was this a bug?) and  the game just tells you to wipe out the other gangs to "win" the game. Which takes you ages compared to the quest lines you want through. It is a total imbalance of playing a story & just running around and taking everyone down to end the game. It was one of the first games of which I was glad I finally made it to the end, as you are doing the same over & over for hours to make it there.Also for a game which is over 2 years old it still has quite some elemetary bugs which should have been solved in that time (counters which are not right, NPC's & gang members bugging out etc.).Better balance, less repetitive & fix obvious bugs, the game would be so much better (+ we could recommend it)

_childDocuments_.review: I grew up loving the game Gangsters: Organized Crime.When I first saw the promotions for Empire of Sin, I pre-ordered without thinking about it. It struck me that this could be an updated, prettier, worthy spiritual successor to one of my favourite management games of all time.Five hours in on day one, I'm not disappointed, but I will say that we're still at the "could be" stage. As in: this could be a great game, and I have high hopes for it. The state of it right now is okay - but pretty bare bones. Being a die-hard fan of all things under the Paradox umbrella, I'm kind of used to this - I'm hoping that this game winds up being more than what it is currently. It's enjoyable, though even beyond initial battles it seems almost absurdly easy to beat most of the battle scenarios. I'm also not stuck on there not being a way to speed up the pace of the game even a little bit: I'm not sure if QA and Alpha testers decided that they liked twiddling their thumbs waiting to upgrade every single building (one at a time) or not, but I can say that I'm not really enjoying it, even though I keep a book beside me for just such occasions in real-time grand strategy or management games.Give this game a chance. It's a little slow at times, a little hammy at others, but you can tell that the people who developed this game have a love of the period and this game has the potential to be an absolute gem.It just has to get past that "can be" stage.

_childDocuments_.review: This game deserves it's mixed reviews. It's got some great concepts at its core, and cool ideas, but in its current state it completely fails to be a good gaming experience.Empire of Sin looks like it started as an ode to mafia strategy games like Gangsters: Organized Crime, but quickly got taken over by X-Com. That actually seemed appealing at first, but the two genres never really seem to mesh. Your criminal empire is made up of various "rackets" that generate different amounts of cash depending on various upgrades. There's a deep menu explaining the desires of each ward in the city, and how well the rackets are fulfilling those needs. There are bonuses for adjacency. There are special Hotel rackets that don't generate much income, but do generate more demand. There's a system of prosperity in the wards that changes what people in those wards want at different times in the game.None of that matters. None of it. There are just tons and tons of systems built for a Mafia strategy game that just simply don't matter at all to your success. The real game is in the turn-based combat. Using just a few men, you can easily take over most enemy rackets as they only start with 2 guards, and upgrading security is expensive, and takes a while. That means that most combat is a breeze, and by the mid-game you'll be dominating almost all battles.When you get to a certain point you'll be able to reliably take down enemy safe houses, which are the only challenging battles in the game. Once that happens, the game is just a few battles from being over, as taking out an enemy safe house nets you their entire empire all at once. That just makes the game feel like it could have been re-tooled to be a story-driven turn-based squad combat game, and strip out the totally unnecessary strategy sim. I don't know how to fix this. Maybe it's just core balance issues. Maybe Rackets need to start with more defenses by default so you can't just plough your way through the game with combat, but as it stands right now the game doesn't "work".That being said, I see a lot of complaints about bugs, and I only ran into one bug while playing, and it was fairly minor (a character always appeared to be dead, but functioned properly otherwise). Maybe some of the bugs are under control now.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't let the mediocre reviews from the critics turn you off the game, most of them got their copies before the Day 1 patch.  But is this a good game?I would say yes, but needs to be fleshed out more.  The XCOM fights arent difficult by any means unless you crank the difficulty, but not everyone (myself included) needs a strategy game with soul-crushing difficulty.  Management of your businesses is mostly fire and forget, unless you piss off the wrong person - then you need to scramble to take out their guys before they take you out.  The missions arent noticable or exciting most of the time, but you really should do them because they give you some very nice rewards.Edit:  Bugs are also semi-prevalent, but nothing moreso than annoyance as of now.  Characters have an irritating habit of not moving a long distance once you have a big enough group, but it can be fixed by "waypointing" (making multiple shorter moves) or by just skipping it using the fast-travel to a closer point you want.All in all, this game has a huuuuuuge amount of potential, and i would totally recommend it to anyone who likes strategy games in the vein of XCOM, especially if you happened to like Chimera Squad.  I do hope the devs decide to keep pouring their love into this game, though.

_childDocuments_.review: About 12 hours played as of review in March 2021.Initial impression: 6 out of 10, based on potential. Unless you are bored or super curious, wait another 6 months.Game is passable but needs more improvement. Has the potential to be a lot better: key issue is to remove the tedious repetitiveness after a few hours.Some suggestions / weaknesses at the moment:- Need more ways to make money. The current way is to either go to war with another gang, take over their racket; or create a new racket from scratch by seizing an abandoned building (more or less the same thing). This gets repetitive. There should be a way to, for example, raid rackets of other gangs (without automatically starting a war), rob a store, and collect passive protection money. - The economy and $ values are a bit nonsensical. I could buy a crow bar or other melee weapon for approx 7,000. It costs less to open a new business, or even hire someone. Gangs will offer to pay you protection money of $70 a week. Why bother. It also feels like income from rackets is a bit low.- Combat: Not bad, but not exactly Xcom. A few things scream out to me: melee seems far too inaccurate to be useful and guns are too accurate. Some of the physics is crazy; I am shooting people with 90% accuracy across impossible angles, but i have less than 50% accuracy when trying to punch someone in the face at point blank range? Executing people seems to have no benefit at all.- to break up the monotony, they should have some combat missions to be timed (similar to xcom). Eg rob a bank and get out in less than 6 moves. - fewer gangs so defeating someone feels meaningful.- The grappling hook is immersion breaking and should be scrapped immediately. It also allows you to drag people through walls, which is absurd.- diplomacy: While at war, the only option is to seek a truce. If I am winning by a lot, I should be able to force a concession on my opinion (money, territory) on the loser (just copy the concept from other paradox games).- lieutenants: you shouldn't lose a combatant for appointing one-encountered a few bugs. Eg at war with someone but impossible to initiate combat, or it says I have lost a battle when in fact I have won.- automate explore function for gang members. AI does this, but human cant- right now one ends up spending too much time on combat, but combat is fairly boring. I would push the game towards more management and less combat and it'll be interesting.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a hard game for me to not recommend it combines a cool theme of the 1920's underground liquor criminal system, XCOM like combat, and a Civ like map. I thought it would be a recipe for success, however, the game falls short in practice. The economy once figured out mainly circulates around having well off breweries and investing heavily in keeping a good stock of booze. You have three ways to make money Speak Easies, Brothels, and Casinos. The first two scale with upgrades which are expensive and honestly are rarely worth the time investment. Casinos make money on an RNG factor and can sometimes break and net you a crazy amount of money if you scale them all the way up though they are frankly useless early on. Though you can pretty much ignore all of this since any game can be ended within an hour since capturing enemies’ breweries will kill their economy and you can just invest in guards and snowball the game from there. The diplomacy system is there but rarely if ever nets you any serious gain and killing an enemy faction is too easy to do. Declare war, Assault Safe house, Murder enemy boss, and now you own their empire and your economy is through the roof. Why pay for upgrades and wait when you can just lose your small business and kill their leader and get them all back and more. That’s what the game boils down to in any given campaign save up money buy gangsters get early kills on gang boss leaders. Then rinse wash and repeat. Any other method is slow and time consuming and doesn’t net the same efficiency. I like the idea of this game but the execution is shallow and feels repetitive after the first couple of campaigns.
