_childDocuments_.review: I kept coming back to this game because I love the genre. And to be fair, I think  has an overall aesthetically pleasing set of presentation values. From the music in the background to the sound effects to the styling--you name it, this game brings a lot of style to deliver on its promise. I just like the look, feel, and so much about it. I think that's why I couldn't give up on it. I bought it and refunded it at least twice before finally picking it up as cheap as it's ever likely to get during the 2024 summer sales.Beyond mere looks, I can also say there's a fair bit of compelling game play to be had here. The turn-based combat portion is enjoyable to a point. I like the variety in classes of criminal and the different skill trees they bring to the table. I don't think it all works quite as well as some other games with similar mechanics, but I've tried a couple different bosses and can honestly say there's room to play in different ways. I think my favorite is Sai Wing Mock for his ability to throw devastating poison bombs. It's such a powerful skill, especially when you can make him a melee brawler and do it again after three turns of cutting down fools with single strikes.But here's why I have to give this game an overall yet qualified negative review: it just doesn't hold up for long. For the first six to ten hours I was still running into new things, learning, and enjoying finding my way in the gangster world. But somewhere around that time frame I'd pretty much seen it all. I hung on until hour fifteen because I'd basically been screwed over by Al Capone and swore myself an oath I'd put him in the ground. Doing so was very satisfying, though it was as long protracted battle that cost me one good gang member to wounds and another due to affairs of the heart.But beyond that, there's honestly little to no reason to keep playing. I'm already clearly the most powerful faction in the entire game. Expanding into other neighborhoods and taking over more rackets has essentially become grunt work. And the promise of what's left for me is... well... doing that same thing over and over again in the next neighborhood and the next and the next and... I just don't think it holds up for long.The bugs and obviously re-worked systems don't help either. I've run into a few real show-stopper bugs along the way. And I hate how some of the mechanics--like the adjacency requirement for precincts, the lines connecting one neighborhood to another, etc.--feel like they were added simply to pad runtime. For crying out loud, I'm playing as a criminal: I'm  to ignore rules and red lines in the sand! Sheesh.In the final analysis, I absolutely got my money's worth. I paid something like $10 for the game and had a solid 10+ hours of genuine fun. I'm a real sucker for this genre of games, so if you're like me and are desperate for another title in this under-served field, then you could probably have fun with it too. But I think for most players it's just not going to be worth your money. There are plenty of better games out there. Especially now that the publisher and/or developers have basically stopped working on the game, even screwing people who bought the promised second DLC out of their money. The game isn't great as it is, and it's just not going to get any better it seems. What a pity.

_childDocuments_.review: The game itself is quite enjoyable.  Interesting enough character design and boss progression.  The development team did some research into various backgrounds of different nations immigrants that lend into the feel of 1920s prohibition era USA.  I've only played as Al Capone to start off with and get a feel for basic game mechanics, but am interested in additional play through as the other available syndicate bosses.  While there are a noticeable amount of bugs and glitches, the autosave feature as well as ability to manually save help mitigate any significant setbacks should you need to exit the game and reload.  Alot of the negative reviews don't have any notable feedback of worth, primarily just kids crying about how their toaster PCs can't handle the game, or otherwise just being sad salty children without any impactful feedback for what they feel makes the game "bad".The tutorial seems lacking and the business management aspects of the game seem to be not fully fleshed out.  The combat mechanics are simple and pretty much the standard you would expect for tactical combat based fight system.  The city map seems unpolished and rushed to have been dumped out with simple geometric graphics which is a real shame.  The standard view when wandering the city is nice to look at and runs smoothly at 120 FPS in 4k resolution.The game seems to be mainly story focused more so than on the difficulty of combat or the city builder/ management features.  I'm interested to see what future updates bring, hopefully some touch ups on different graphic elements, some more quality of life improvements like equipment comparison tooltips, and potentially more mob boss selection.For the $40 price tag, and the future promise of additional campaign content, I'd recommend the game.  Once it has been released for a while and inevitably goes onto sale in one of the countless Steam sales that occur every other month, a discounted purchase would definitely be worth the investment if you enjoy tactical combat games, historically inaccurate but clearly inspired prohibition era games, and a little bit of business management/ lemonade stand type games all mixed into one neat package, then this game would be a winner for you.7/10 enjoyable game with an interesting enough story to keep my attention.  Graphics are nice but not the most beautiful thing to come out lately.  Recommended machine specs are not all that demanding, and so anyone giving negative reviews for poor performance must be playing on a early 2k macbook or other overpriced paperweight.

_childDocuments_.review: I played around for 11.2 hours on the lieutenant difficulty. Beating game on the in game date of Sep 14 1920 by just clearing out the other mobsters. I beat the game without doing the quest the game gives you at the very start. Even beating the game the day I got it. You have a number of different bosses to chose from. With there people being from Hungary to China available for you to play as. Other bosses willing to team up with you more if you come from the same place as them or your personality match theirs. Which is what I saw in one youtube video on the game. Gameplay wise I love it. You have these different abilities to play with from your boss’s special ability to hinchmen’s abilities. With pistols to machine guns. Semi-autos to fully automatic weapons. The people you hire can be formed up how you like them to playEach henchmen have different relationships with other characters. Which may cause them to leave if you shoot the people they love. Which happened to me once in the game. The racket system is rather simple. You produce liquor for your speakeasy. Liquor to make your Casino visitors not be able to think. And you have hotels to bring people into your neighborhood to increase the amount of customers. If the customer’s tastes in liquor change, you can change the production of your breweries. I love the naming feature as it's fun to name something you owned after taking it over or buying it. There is diplomacy from trading to allying yourself with others against other bosses. I barely used it except for declaring war on everyone.There were only a few issues I had with the game. Fast Travel was too easy to use since there are taxis all over the place. My run as Sai Wing Mock Usually involved me fast traveling and poison bombing the guards out of nowhere. Another issue is that the boss' abilities are op. Sai Wing Mock’s ability can allow you to throw three bombs which poison an area for the rest of the battle. I usually clear out most of the guards in the battles thanks to me having three bombs. This would be more balanced if Mock could only throw two bombs. The third issue is that the unique items you get from the bosses are worth the risk of killing the bosses. Unique items pretty much turn your Zeros into Heros. I gave my mercs the unique items and they easily did their jobs well. It makes me wish the items could only be obtained through special side quests or could only be found in random locations. Another issue is that the other bosses very little through the game use their abilities. The only boss I saw use theirs was Genna after I ended most of the other bosses. When he threw knives at my gang during my raid on his safe house. Another issue I had with this was that you could beat this game with low tier mercs. The bosses only have one merc with them. With them usually being a medic. In the end I never got my hands on the best mercs and just swarmed the last bosses with low tier mercs carrying unique weapons.There is one issue I have that is a single glitch. The first one and only one I encountered was that gangsters from other gangs stick around after their bosses are dead. I had an encounter with the Vice Kings long after their boss was dead. By this time I’m pretty sure there was already a funeral for Jackson. It didn’t bother me much until I raided Colt’s safe house. After I defeated the White Circus while they were at war with Colt. I got war declared on me by Colt. I went in and the White Circus had the last laugh. As the White Circus guards teamed up with Colt and his gang. Making it impossible for me to take over Colt’s Safe house. So reloaded a save and waited for Dyer to kill Colt before I killed her.  Also during the lieutenant mode, I spent little on my rackets and never got raided by the police. I wish the game rewarded you for spending time waiting for more money even though you are strong enough to end the other bosses careers.Despite the issues, this was a fun game to play. It's a lot easier compared to Paradox’s other games like EU4 or HOI4. Though it could use a lot of additions to make the game a bit more complex then how it is. Which can be added over time with DLC.

_childDocuments_.review: I hesitated on buying this due to the bad reviews, but I'm loving it.  You can set the game to have 1 neighborhood up to 10 neighborhoods.  Each one can have dozens of ownable business locations to fight over.  I'm guessing around 60 gangsters or so, each being their own unique character having their own skill tree and gear/weapon slots whom you recruit.  There is a relationship factor there, some gangsters do and/or do not like some other gangsters and recruiting them to your gang, putting them together can cause issues if they do not get along or if they are in love and one dies.  There are about a dozen or more gangs and you play as the gang leader of which ever gang you choose. If you like XCom like combat but with a business building simulator twist, I'd grab this. _childDocuments_.review: On my 3rd playthrough I thought I'm trying to accomplish total control of the city, solo."this may take a while"So I'm taking it easy, trying to avoid the bugs mentioned on this forum and elsewhere, but that's (like many have said before) impossible. SO I try the 2nd best option... play with the bugs. Not all of them break the game entirely, and with careful saving and loading most of the bugs can be 'reset' and some even help the player, untill fixed.- For example: I'm getting the +20 health recovery from melee weapons, on my rifle shots.I managed to turn Angelo Genna into a solo beast. With all weapon-proficiencies maxed, this isn't that hard on any character I supose.All-in-all, I'm having a great time, between a couple of bug related reloads.SO far, perhaps nothing new for a couple of players that may just have been faster with the battles and conquering all 10 neighbourhoods. During all this I used the run to get a better feel for the economic side of things. Getting the racket bonuses, figuring out that upgrading ambience in them helps, run down, dangerous neighbourhoods back up to a more profitable level.And all this time I'm wondering how many of the players, have actually taken the time (and plenty effort) to work through the obvious flaws (bugs etc.) to do this as well.I've taken the challenge and came out the other end with a whole bunch of quests I had not seen before during the more "safehouse storming, boss killing, taxi teleporting" playthroughs I've done and read about, here.I'm going to put it out there...I think this is a solid game, that may or may not have been rushed near the end of production coming up on a releasedate. So it misses the finishing touches to make everything run smoothly. It may not be of the same caliber as, let's say "cyberpunk" but suffers from what I gather, a lot from the same production issues. Too much hype too soon, potential buyers, seeing all that good PR stuff roll over the Internet, wanting a piece of the action. Studios wanting to keep the fleeting attention spans of the Social Media Generation, focused on their product. Saturated Steam libraries with hundreds of games to choose from and nothing is up to the high standards of the "hardcore" gamers. Besides they probably already bought 3 new games on the next steam sale. Played those for half an hour and bash the producers and studios in the same manner, they do for this game.Nobody wants to accept that todays endless options lead to even more desire/greed, on both ends. Producers and studios feel the pressure to release a new title, in fear of losing their fanbase amongst the tons of other studios. The gamers have so many games to chose from, they throw any new title in the bin as easily as a banana with 1 little brown spot.Because we throw our money at the screen, we feel entitlement, the screen shows our wildest dreams and deepest wishes. And then anger, when it doesn't live up to our expectations.I, for one, enjoy this game thoroughly and don't regret the money spend. A little regret perhaps, that I fell into the trap of buying a new game on release, that obviously should have been given more time to be finished. But willing to support the designers with feedback, other than the profanity filled stuff I read elsewhere.If you beat the dog too often, he's not going to listen, or behave better.Let's hope Romero Studios and Paradox, are still willing to listen, and help the players to a better gaming experience. Then perhaps we actually get to enjoy the game they intended to make.

_childDocuments_.review: This game broke my heart a little bit... It's bad.I love gangster themed games. I have a particular love for the "management of the business" type of gangster game. Much like many of the other reviews, I was excited for a "Gangsters: Organized Crime" successor. This game promised that, throwing in some tactical turn-based combat (which I love too), as well as characters/stories to drive forward a motivation and a story (although not necessary, as I would prefer to write my own gangster story).This game pretends to do a lot of different things, and spectacularly fails at all of them. The "management" is laughable, the stories/voice acting is comically poor, and the turn-based combat is an abject failure.It's still buggy too in it's early state (so these will likely be patched after the time of writing this review), I have already had to restart the game twice as certain actions were not progressing (in a 90 minute run). The pathfinding is also a joke, with characters often not moving at all, and preferring to get intimate with nearby wall. This game feel like it was made to bank on a subset of interested fanatics (people who love gangster themed games), instead of being made to satisfy a particular itch that many of us have had for years.Paradox are really "Hit and Miss" with recent game launches. In some instances reading their target audience with lazer point precision, and others completely missing the mark and sparking anguish in their attempt. This one is a bit of a step too far for me. And I will not be pre-ordering a Paradox game until after user reviews are in. Paradox employee a fantastic team of creators to peddle their rubbish, so I cannot even trust some of my favourite channels to provide me with valuable consumer advice until well after the fact.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to like this game, I really do. I love Paradox Interactive, I think they're a fantastic studio/publisher. They've got some of my favorite games under their belt (Surviving Mars/Aftermath, Stellaris, etc), and I like the setting, music, and ambiance. The primary problem, in my opinion, comes from the game play. It's part of the core game play loop so I'm not sure if or how it could be fixed. The combat in this game is the turn based, grid based, isometric style any X-Com player would recognize. It is significantly simpler than X-Com2, which came out almost 5 years ago.  It gets repetitive, quickly, and there is a lot of it. Oh boy is there a lot of it. Seems like, with few exceptions when you're focusing on base building for a few minutes, there is a generated fight every 5 minutes or so. The maps get repetitive (you'll see repeats within the first 5 fights), it's basically the same 3-5 bad guy set up each time. It just is too much of the same thing. I would have liked to see this game focus a greater emphasis on base building / empire management. I'm sure the world opens up more as you progress. I've got 9 hours logged on the game in two playthroughs (I restarted after realizing it wasn't a great idea to pick a fight with Capone as a newbie, but the combat is easy enough where you think it might be.) I don't know, I want to like this game. It's got great flavor and the world building based on characters' backstories slowing coming out through interactions with other bosses is an interesting set up. It's just that you see that combat screen way too frequently for how simplistic the fighting actually is. Hopefully the fighting gets more complex, or the frequency gets turned down, but I cannot recommend this game in it's current state. Go find Omerta: City of Gangsters (Kaplyso Media game from 2013) for a few bucks on sale somewhere and you're getting a lot of the same game for 90% cost reduction.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, First review here we go!i absolutely love this game, the aesthetic, the music, the concept is all in place and match the time period, while giving it a great X-COM feel. however, at this time, it is VERY unpolished. in the span of 22 hours i have come across 3 bugs, with one being a game crashing one. the gameplay at the standard rule-set of lieutenent difficulty and 10 factions is easy to handle. gang fights get easy to handle and Joseph Saltis +speakeasy spam is win. the game is easy to comprehend and easy to figure out.here is my issues with the current form of the game:the diplomacy needs work, and plenty of it. the A.I is intransigent and the moment you do something mildly rude to them they decide that you and your extended family will be murdered, burned and dragged through Chicago. there is very few options to get them to like you or to interact with them overall, the business agreements are rarely worth using due to the bonuses being so small (but that may be the bosses needing a Buff), as far as iv'e seen there is no way to lower the A.I's threat of you, the Chicago police bribe function does too little to matter and ultimately, you get to the point that the most viable option is to just kill them all, which i did in my first play-through. after i bumped it up to the under-boss difficulty, most of these issues were fixed, money got harder to come by, the A.I is alot more aggressive, diplomacy is very much more viable and you cant just kill them all, but that comes back to the big issue of there not being alot of diplomacy.Overall, this game is great and has tons of potential, what i'd like to see later on is:a Multiplayer added, either turn based or real time, make it stable and make it WORK.more options for diplomacy and to make diplomacy more viable, tune the A.I to be more agreeable depending on who they are, add more options like proper alliances, gang merging/vassalization, favors: loaning out guards or giving a temporary upgrade to rackets, promising to stay out of your neighborhood, demanding a racket or to allow me to sell a racket to a potential friend over just selling it and removing it from the map.Slight tweaks to abilities and combat, kill chain and the perk that lets you move after killing a enemy is essentially Big Joe Saltis clearing huge warehouses full of thugs with a tommy gun and one turn, allow you to place your gangsters in designated places of buildings you want to take over, instead of breaking into a brothel and your starting spot is some room with a couple getting it on. expand the arsenal of thugs and guards so its not just 80% shotguns and 15% pistols.Ultimately, i love this game and would recommend it to anyone who loves the 1920's gangster theme, anyone who loves X-COM or the style of combat, or "up close and personal" strategy over the disconnect of the standard paradox map game (still love those as well). as far as recently released games go, i give this a 7/10 with a potential 9/10 further down the line.

_childDocuments_.review: So its been several months since this game has been released. I have come back to make some updates.While they have addressed a lot of the issues and concerns with this game there are still a lot of things left on the table that could have made this a much better experience.There are still a lot of bugs, especially those regarding your rackets and synergies. Tons of animation bugs, and various others. Nothing seemingly game breaking, or at least not quite as much as there was before.Some issues I have with the game...Maps are so small, and so repetitive. There are only a hand full of maps for indoors locations, and they get repetitive pretty quick as they are generally very small, and the enemies can just run from one side to the other in one turn to melee you. Some of the bosses will still continually spam you with standing offers even when you consistently decline them. The AI is pretty dumb, they tend to always rush you, it would be nice to see something like Omerta, where they would actually hold cover. Speaking of cover, its about the dumbest thing ive ever seen... When someone is hiding behind full cover and you target them to shoot them, they will just lean out of cover to let you shoot at them, kind of defeats the entire point of being in cover. I know this is done to make it look realistic when you hit them vs hitting them through a wall, but why would you hide behind cover just to stand well out of it every time you are shot at?Just about every one use item has the same one or two animations. If you use a healing tonic, you drink from a big jug, if you use SMELLING SALTS, you drink from a big jug. A little variation would have been nice.The very limited amount of dialog lines for the enemies to speak get very old very fast. When you're in a fight with 10 enemies and they all say the same 2 lines when the battle starts, and over half of them say the same thing when they die. Id just as soon have them say nothing at all. Nitpicky, but every sit down scene with a boss runs through the same couple animations, generally hand waving everything said by the other boss.Not getting into great detail, but its improved slightly over the launch offering. Hopefully it gets better.

_childDocuments_.review: I really do wish they had a neutral/check again later option vs Yes/No.  For now though, I have to vote no. I like the concept of the game, it just feels really unfinished.  Like it's an early access or beta.Combat feels like they tried to mimic xcom style games, but maybe haven't quite played those games.  It needs more polish and variety.  Strategic layer is both insanely overwhelming and underwhelming at the same time.  I know right? The overwhelming part is there are so many things going on and at such a frantic pace, you cannot keep up.  I ended up ignoring the some 50 missions I had simply because everything else was going on.  Forced to meet bosses from 10 factions despite only just visiting my burrow.  Forced into wars, a few missions etc.  Maybe if the speed could be adjusted on how many things are thrown at the player at once it'd be a good thing.The underwhelming part... You don't have to bother taking pieces and parts of another bad guy's area. just go take his safe house and you get everything he owned.  I took two guys like this before I really ever understood the complexity of how my own structures work with one another. Heck I still don't really, but I'm in the process of taking over a 4th bosses safehouse and territories. I think the team has something that could potentially be an amazingly fun game to play, but it needs to have some more thought put into combat, strategic layer and the speed at which a human can actually process and think about everything thrown at them.  Hoping they can re-evaluate, re-engineer and fix some of these issues over the next year.  Then maybe it'll be worth the $.  Certainly doesn't feel worth full price atm.

_childDocuments_.review: Ooof, this game caught me with some really sharp barbed hooks.Imagine, you vs 13 organized crime factions. X-Com Style Combat and Tycoon Management.Sounds great, but isn't really what you're getting here. Fighting is OK but some bosses have overly powerful abilities.Rival Gangs have nearly zero agency.  Compared to the player they are helpless idiot children.  You'll never be threatened or challenged by them.  Two examples of this:  There is a large pool of unique recruitable gangsters you can hire for your 'crew'.  You can hire a max of 10, while the enemy only recruits one.  You send this crew to do your dirty work or bolster the defenses of your business.  The one recruited gangster stays in the HQ with the boss.  Yes the enemy sends out parties of generic mooks to attack you but they're always easy, and you also can see where they want to attack.On the defense the rival AI is also atrocious.  I've never seen them upgrade their business' security - which means all fights when taking over a rival's businesses are just too easy.Voice acting is good.  Music is nice some times  but often repetitive.  Like at your own HQ I think it's on a 30 second loop.Animations are often broken but the ragdolling/machinegun dancing is funFor some reason the game bombards you with quests but they aren't very interesting or they lock you into long conversations (which in game time last days) when you are probably needed elsewhere.Multiplayer of this would be hilarious. _childDocuments_.review: I think the main take away from the game is that depending how you feel it is either not sure what it wants to be or it was a gamble that did not entirely pay off.The main systems that I view in this are X-Com (Remake) combat, Gangsters (late 90's game) concept, along with some very light business management, and quest and RPG elements.  On it's surface, those are all very good ideas and if they're put together, I would absolutely adore this game because it's what I want.  However, it suffers from 'just missed the mark' on every one of the things it sought to bring to the table and it leaves one wanting.X-Com style combat?  Unpolished and inconsistent with damage, character ability, mechanic function, item availability and trait development.  I'm not sure how the X-Com turn based firefight which has turned into the new standard could be so glitchy and difficult to implement for the studio.Light business management?  It's not as deep as the number of screens likes to make it seem.  It lacks any refinement and the depth of interaction that the Gangsters Game had with it's industries and businesses.  All money is the same, any structure is the same, the five illicit businesses are the same no matter where they are.  You can stick five casinos next to each other and they function the same with the same income, ditto with brothels, or speakeasies.  Fifteen illegal bars on the same block have zero impact on how much they earn.  Changes are incremental at best, and have no real effect.  There's no real techniques to hide anything other than investing in 'deflections' nothing as refined as Gangsters of hiding brothels in legit hotels, or speakeasies inside of resturants...just click the box and you're good.Quest and RPG Elements.  The game wants you to think that you're an RPG, that you have dialogue choices with other gangsters, make deals, have an effect on them.  Wants you to think that they might actually act differently depending on how much they like you and your behavior towards them affects the relationship you have.  Nope, someone can be polite and professional in a meeting, or act really friendly, and have MASSIVE debuffs towards you that makes war inevitable.  Your character can only click on tribute and hope that will help.The game wants to be far more than it is, far, far more than it is.  And while it's not a horrible game, it just does not really nail anything so well that you overlook the exceptionally mediocre other aspects of the game that miss their mark.  It might be worth getting if you haven't played the other games that this one is borrowing from, but if you're here, you already have.  It will get better when there's a modding community, and probably after the standard Paradox DLC business plan kicks in, until then, give it a pass.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is... amazing. Simply amazing. You get a vast number of mafia bosses to start with, most (if not all?) being historically based on a real person, tasked with dominating the entire town of Chicago starting with one small brewery, speakeasy, and safehouse. While I am typing this, I only have around 10 hours in-game. It's a very well thought out idea in general, and has so much potential, but in it's current state, it still has some issues that end up being just a bit annoying. First of all, the beginning of the game is always the same/very similar, spawning usually in the same areas and with the same power. Next, on most difficulty levels, unless you're really avoiding it, it's pretty easy to take out other factions, by just fast travelling there and walking in with 3-5 guys, which makes it a bit tedious instead of action packed and interesting. Why not have hidden safehouses so you actually have to put great efforts into defeating other prominent mafiosos?Then last but not least, the mixing of the voice acting is simply terrible, some characters are too quiet and others too loud (Example: Angelo Genna is rather quiet while some companions are far too loud) and in execution scenes/other special moments, you can hear whoever is executing is clearly saying special dialogue, but barely hear it with the fact that whatever stabbing/shooting/other noise is 125% louder.Tl;dr: Empire of Sin has great potential and I'm very happy with it, but it has a lot of issues that need to be addressed, too easy to play, not a lot of variation at the start, and terrible sound design. I wish the developers the best of luck going on with this game, as this game is very promising.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is quite repetitive, you will spend time killing mindless thugs to build up cash or take over buildings. You can never call a meeting from behind your desk in your safe house and carefully plan your next move and send out your lieutenants to carry out hits. Everything is the character you pick running full sprint about the map doing same stuff basically. The business management aspects are bland as it can possibly get, and honestly you never at any moment feel you're running a "empire" but you will begin to feel a land rush attitude to take turf/new buildings constantly, least enemy get the upper hand. My biggest beef is the playable characters besides a couple aren't interesting at all, everytime you click them they repeat same cheesy phrase. Example Dion will repeat stuff like "I will be there in 2 shakes of a lambs tail!" Yeah he is a true gangster, I get shivers just listening to his corny 1 liners. The fact we have to use and look at our characters a lot and frankly they're bland. We can't gain outfits nor gear we can see visually change their appearance. Also some characters look as if they've had more TLC like Al Capone, he looks nice with nice strong details on his outfit/face. You can tell time wasn't taken for example Frank Regan whose 1 color outfit looks rushed down to his blurry MS paint tie. Then there's the voice acting or lack there of... its just not good and characters like Reyna are just plain bad with voicing. The dialogue isn't great either and I never felt like at any moment it even mattered, again bland. Its not terrible its just not good.The game gives you a list of characters you can hire at a big cost and a cut to your business earnings. They will run with you to fight etc. they're like crew members like in XCOM, but they're premades with small stories, background, traits. A lot have goofy outfits you can never change like a nurses outfit or ww1 style military officer outfit. They don't give gangster nor everyday vibes, they're very cliche. The world seems bland and everything seems like a rehash or a copy same object gives little reason to look at your surroundings because you've seen them all so many times in first hour you don't care anymore... this includes building interiors.Honestly there's little going for this title beyond 15 hours I'd probably put into it. The game does alot of things, but none of these things are great. If you feel spending $40+ on 10-25 hours worth of content is for you? Go for it, everyone is different. I mean this game could be good with a lot of content patching, DLC, and dev love over next 2 years for now I can't play it.. this is bugs aside, it's just not good. I will come back and check the game out in future, I love gangster movies and was hyped for this game but I fear if I keep it I will play 10-15 hours. Anyways, helpfully this bit of rambling helps someone out, I am not expert its only my humble opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: A lacking turn based strategy.  I was really looking forward to playing this after waiting on the big patch.  I'm a big fan of this genre, however Empire of Sin has all the pieces but they are not put together well.The battles are fine, but you don't get enough information on flanking or why your hit % is low or high.  Also it only sometimes shows who you'll be able to attack at new positions.  The consequences of a battle don't feel meaty enough when there are too many of them when at war with another gang.There are plenty of non-combat side missions, diplomacy, and unit leveling & setup decisions but none of them feel fun to make. _childDocuments_.review: I waited to give a review on Empire of Sin until they were done patching in the initial months.  Past reviews you can see its buggy and crashes with saved games being lost and you can't progress certain missions.  Since the game has been patched and there is another one coming soon, the game is living up to what I had hoped when I prepurchased it and anxiously awaited its release.The game now is solid.  I have beaten it on two different bosses and have not had any crashes.  Combat is Xcom like but I would call it Xcom like.  Yes combat is turn bases but in Xcom you make a mistake and will dearly pay for it, Empire of Sin I feel like is better (for me) as it doesn't punish you hard for making a tactical mistake.The tycoon aspect of it is fun trying to take over neighborhoods and the story of each character is unique with many side quests.  Also there are different arcs for the bosses so just when you think your boss's story is over the one person you spared may come back and be a friend or foe. Auto resolve is coming in the next patch which is nice because there is nothing worse than having one enemy boss left and spending 30 minutes battling out in them attacking your brewery when you are just about to attack their safe house.  While I don't think I will use the feature for 90% of the game when it comes to the end game I think it will be a nice feature to have.  Other things I would like to see adjusted is in the neighborhood if there is peace your alcohol quality just keeps going up for what people want, I would like this to be dynamic and have some randomness to it.  Overall its a fun game and enjoyable if this is your genre.  I consider this a fun casual game to take over chicago.  It can be challenging but its more fun and casual to me than that, but this is also my niche type of game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is inherently flawed.The major gameplay and the economics are not at odds with each other, but they're essentially two passing ships in the night. I could probably play this game forever without having to spend money. I never would though. The combat is shallow. Some brand spanking new director said "hey we can do isometric turn based combat" and they made the basic implementation, brought in some cool, historically accurate firearms, then ♥♥♥♥♥♥ off to god knows where while the animation team was struggling to fix everything when this game first released.The combat is a pale imitation of the combat loop from a game like the XCOM reboot. It copies essentially all of the mechanics for the combat classes from that game, but without any of the depth to the combat encounters. Every single combat starts with you knowing exactly where the enemy is, the enemy knowing exactly where you are, and you are more often than not, in one of several incredibly repetitive and claustrophobic. The enemy is limited to the exact same classes, meaning you lose out on things like the asymmetric combat against the aliens from that game, or the mission variety. I have ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ never been able to finish the story to one of these boring ass characters, so there might be some tiny amount of variation, but I doubt its worth suffering through.There is also an incredibly pointless and essentially out of place RPG mechanic. Your Gang boss and hired hands all have stats, modified by their backgrounds, but almost all of them are safely ignored. Its not that there is absolutely nothing there, but they're so varied and so ticky tack that my mind smooths over. The only useful non-combat skills are the ones that you can use in the story missions to avoid the combat or avoid paying people to do ♥♥♥♥ for you.I think the worst system here is the districts and neighborhoods. Each district represents a famous area of Chicago, like the Loop, and each district is cut up into neighborhoods, which are the arbitrary blocks where you are going to have your various rackets. You have to ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ fight for each ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ block. If another main character gang doesn't have it on lockdown, it'll be controlled by generic "thugs" with enough firepower to shift the Somme. You need to take the central safehouse/alcohol store in order to take the block over and even begin to profit from it. There are like, 10 neighborhoods in a district, give or take. You can see what I'm getting at. Its a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ repetitive slog.The second most annoying ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ system is the notoriety system. In order to get effective gangsters on your payroll, you need notoriety. Notoriety is gained mostly by completing missions, cornering rackets, and murdering more schmucks than were ever involved in racketeering in Chicago. Unless you kill another boss, you'll have to commit a Valetine's Day massacre every month for like 8 years to even hire the people with decent stats. Watching that number go up is like watching my life tick away.Its like someone took Saints Row 2, then decided to make it a procedurally generated rogue like with the main character being essentially a Civilization 6 leader for their little gang. Except Saints Row 2 was more emotionally impactful than any of the story on display here and was actually a decent copy of what it was trying to ape. Its not a game where you go from small time gangbanger, controlling a block, to kingpin, controlling industrial crime in the city. Its like Dark Heresy in a Hiveworld without any of the things that would make a Hiveworld fun. No highrise firefights, no fancy balls, no huge warehouses, no docks, no variety. You fight on the street or you fight in an indoor dumpster.I can't even damn this game with faint praise. Its a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ chore to play. Every 20 feet some random ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ is telling me, whoever random mad bomber/mass murderer/war criminal I am playing as, that I need to do the random ♥♥♥♥ they tell me to. Its like watching my attention being split thinly with a razor like that scene with the garlic in Goodfellas.Avoid this ♥♥♥♥ like the plague. Do not waste your money or time.

_childDocuments_.review: So much unrealised potential. There's something there to build on, but currently the game is quite shallow and bizarrely balanced. Bad economy design, bad strategic UI. Combat is "ok" but some bosses are so incredibly powerful off the bat that they trivialise 95% of the fights you encounter.The default game settings has 10 districts with ~20-40 potential rackets in each, where there are only 4 varieties to build from. It gets tedious and overwhelming very quickly. It doesn't help that they don't have anything to interact with to help make them stand out. There's no reason to even visit them once you have them. Much like your own safehouses.Management/Empire UI is poorly thought out. Having so many gangs, including small mobs, but only being able to scroll through them one by one, without a list or search is again tedious. Minor factions don't even have unique portraits, they are all the same and blend together. Not being able to go to diplomacy or info pages on a faction straight from the map, or even by clicking on their portraits in other menus also seems like a glaring oversight.Game economy is really unbalanced. There's no real reason to bother upgrading your rackets apart from alcohol quality in breweries. Firstly because there are so many of them that it's just not feasible to cover the costs, but also because the costs are so high compared to the income each racket generates that the ROI is terrible. Negotiating "business proposals" with other factions for 2-4% discount buffs is almost useless considering the drama it seems to cause.It's more profitable to just mask cheap booze as whisky and sell it to factions. Also just selling whisky outright to minor factions is a faster way to make money than relying on your rackets. Item costs and sales prices, and the way your relationship score changes from trades is easily abused and mostly nonsensical. The cache drops across the maps at the start of the game allow you to decently kit out your entire gang before you even start a war, if you want to bother running around everywhere for 30 minutes. Gear seems to hit a peak relatively early as well, so you quickly run out of upgrade opportunities.The enemy factions also appear to struggle with the game economy, as they tend to constantly be almost broke and as such barely upgrade anything apart from their own safehouse security. Which means you can just declare war and blitz everything they have without much fuss. The only "challenge" is that there can be so much happening across so many districts that you can't keep up with any roaming gangs on the streets to cut them off before they attack your own rackets. Even that's not a big deal, as savvy players will just pause the game and rush security upgrades as needed before the building is stormed.Lieutenants, underbosses, moles etc all seem like cool ideas that never got past the first cycle of workshopping. You can't even use lieutenants again without "demoting" them and losing morale. There just doesn't seem to be much benefit of making new safehouses and paying to keep someone locked in there for the rest of the game, when you could keep them in your party and use the extra muscle to take down all the other factions faster.The story and side missions are all fine, nothing outstanding. It seems you generally receive the best outcomes by showing mercy or "being good" at every opportunity, which is a bit odd for a hard boiled gangster-themed game with a cast of sociopaths.I haven't experienced any particularly big bugs, so at least recent patches appear to have stabilised the game considerably.All in all I want to like this game a lot more than I currently do. It needs more flavour and more balance. I was holding off on getting it for a long time but finally caved. It was a mistake, as it will need many updates to really find some soul.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed it at launch, "playing" for hours at a time. It was more of a grind and one heck of a struggle to see any sort of progress. The missions felt lackluster, the characters didn't have any real significance, and the combat was... lacking. You'd think that unloading a tommy gun on a room full of underling mobster wannabes would be satisfying but it was basically just some generic gun sounds and an underwhelming display of damaging firepower.I kept struggling to make things work and, while it was supported, the updates were frequent and significant enough that they would throw my save files out of whack by virtue of correcting items or tactics that I had come to rely upon to progress, causing me to adjust my play style mid-campaign and screw myself over with the next patch.Frustrated, I abandoned the game until the devs could sort it out and/or add some more content. Unfortunately, the devs have abandoned it, too. This was a massive waste of money and they're still selling DLC that they will not be delivering. How this "game" is even still on Steam is beyond me, when it's basically just a trap to steal your cash.The real criminals aren't the ones you boss around in the game; they're the ones who developed it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game lacks content and will keep you busy for about 15-20 hours. After you took your first whole suburb, it´s repetitive and grindy. The storytelling is excellent and shows how much better this game could have been.The pillars of the game are story, economy, diplomacy and combat. While combat and storytelling are very well implemented, the economy and diplomacy system is broken.You can completely ignore economy because you get all your income from combat. Upgrading your locations is unnecessary, unfortunately. Diplomacy is a waste of time because you have to wage war against every other faction and kill them off down to their last warehouse anyway.That being said, if you play it as a sandbox game and take your time, you can have fun building up alliances and wage war together. The game spams you with popup missions, yikes.The combat system is well done, but in the end, you wanted to manage a crime syndicate, not go from one combat screen to the next.Get it for 5-8€, it´s not worth more and lets not give them money for DLC when the base game is broken. Thumbs up for the well done stories!

_childDocuments_.review: In it's current state, no.Empire of Sin has 3 main problems:- Bugs: Encountered a good amount of bugs, some gamebreaking. Definetly needs a couple of patches.- The Menus: Just feel too clunky imo. I'd give money for a neat empire-overview so that I can see where my money is coming from and going to.- The Content: There is just not enough to engage you. You have seen everything the game has to offer within an hour. Sure, EOS is half management game, but the mechanics just don't run deep enough to engage you for a longer period of time. You have different venues to create and upgrade. Diplomacy is shallow, you can only trade, declare war and ask for non-agression pacts or alliances. After you've scratched the surface, you realize that the surface is the entire game, and that there is just not a lot of new things to explore after a while.Yeah, the Atmosphere is nice. The characters and Chicagos districts do immerse you up to a point in this 1920 prohibition scenario. The fighting is Xcom-esque and works well. And the management part, while terribly shallow, does hold potential.Empire of Sin is a big Meh. While the game does show potential, the execution is sloppy. If Paradox wants this game to turn good afterall, they have a lot of work to do. Bugfixes are the most needed part right now, but in the long term, they need to overhaul the menus and add more content. More venues, more diplomacy depth, more options on how to manage your empire.Don't buy it now! Wait for patches and content updates and get it on sale, but don't buy it in it's current state. Imo, the game is barely worth 20 bucks at this point, much less 40.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, so let's be honest, and real here, to help you sort out all the hate here.  Does the game have a lot it needs to improve on with fixes and DLC? Yes.  Did Paradox already state the first DLC is announced to be released in 20 days on Dec. 30? Yes.  I feel like the majority of the hate here from people is equivalent to buying Hearts of Iron 4 when it came out and expecting it to be the same game as with all the DLC.  Is it a money grab to not give you the perfect game and encourage DLC purchases? Yes, welcome to the 21st century lol.The game outside of that is fun, and those that say it's no challenge, and "it's repetitive"...here is a secret.  Don't play on the default difficulty. Play on Boss, or Underboss to start, and after you playthrough the game and finish the base tutorial quit and start again.  The tutorial gives you 2 free gangsters, when if you skip it after you learn the bare bones basics its just you and have to build, oh and increased difficulty means your gangsters also die and get injured easily on a difficult take down.  95% of the hate stems from default difficulty, which admittedly is basically like "easy" for most games.

_childDocuments_.review: I pre-ordered this game for full price and afterwards they seemed to have cut it down by 70%, but anyways here is the review: This game advertised cool and new systems, good graphics and a lot of replayability as well as customizability that would make each playthrough feel unique.Playing it through I immediately drew some comparisons to games like Omerta City of Gangsters and initially I enjoyed it; the good graphics and dialogue between the Gang leaders, with some small story details about the relationships between who we hired to be in our crew, but after a few hours I realized that this was all the game had to offer, repetition and grinding that does not seem to reward any progress, I felt like I had the most fun in the first 2 hours and the hours after that were spent repeating the same things over and over.Below that gameplay there were a myriad of bugs during the missions, crashes and a feeling that some of the playable boss characters were worked on more than others. Personally, when I play a game I like to pick characters that I can relate to and I believed I would relate and enjoy playing as Sai WIng Mock the most, but not only was there an impossibility to do his quests due to bugs in his early missions, but they also recycled his brothers entire character image to be a stock grunt, imagine playing a game like the Witcher and seeing a bunch of Triss and Yennefer clones running around everywhere fighting and dying (simply unimmersive).I would not have a problem with this if they simply told people that they did not work on certain bosses as much and that for most bosses the only thing they have different with each other are their skills, voices and character models.

_childDocuments_.review: I must admit I do like this game but it seems that it is missing alot of things, the fact that your hired gagsters cannot level up as well as your boss , you can’t improve their  stats or your own,unless you speak to the reporter and even that only happens once and it happens early in the game.Other then that I do wish there was some form of clothing customization, or character customization in genral, it is classified as a  RPG but lack a fundermetinal  thing that all Rpgs have and that is character customization. I also wish it would go down the godfather route and make it so you have to take down rackets and building of a specific family before you can attack their safe house, just allowing you to attack a safe house and remove the boss is way to easy. _childDocuments_.review: You can teleport to any boss fight at any time. There is no character progression so you can fight them from the beginning of the game. The only way to win is to fight all the bosses. The entire game is filler that you can, and should, literally skip.Here's some easy to read bullet points.-The best way to get new gear is by shooting groups of 2-3 of the weakest enemy in the game, who guard chests you can teleport to at any time, are visible on the map, and aren't affiliated with any faction-There's 2 "resources":               Booze limits how many places you can own but 1 brewery unupgraded is worth like 10 places               Money limits what combat troops you can hire (of which you'll need 3 tops) and otherwise only exists to feed into               the worthless city management systems that only exist to minor increase these two resources by tiny amounts               despite needing a huge time and resource investment-You can just steal existing buildings at 0 cost to gain infinite production of both these things-Several of the playable Main Characters have the most broken OP moves ever in an XCOM game from the start, letting you 1v20 unharmed but most fights are against 2 people you could one-shot without it, on the hardest difficulty-There is a total of about 10 maps to house your 100+ fights, most of which end in less than a turn, no matter where in the city you are.-Learning new skills takes in game time rather than experience. I never learned a third (or higher) skill on any character before beating the game and only got a 1st and 2nd by dragging ass and exploring all the non-content trying to find a use for it-Enemies never get any stronger, only 1-3 people during boss fights don't die in one rifle shot on the hardest difficultyAnd now a short list of the systems in this game that don't do anything and should be ignored, as it's as useful to you winning as playing cookie clicker on your other monitor.Managing customer draw and capacity at owned placesManaging tier of booze dependent on sector prosperityDeciding which building to make for highest profitsManaging sector prosperity by building qualityManaging your threat level versus other factionsTrying to not draw police attention (I shot every cop and never did anything to hide and they never did anything about it)Managing relations with other factionsBalancing security against likelihood to be raided (you never get raided, minimum security can beat any actual attack if you decide to not teleport and kill all 3 attackers with your Main Character)Hiring troops based on bonuses, traits and relationshipsInstalling troops in businesses to increase building statistics slightlyQuests

_childDocuments_.review: At this point what you have is the foundation for a great game, but it isn't there yet.  The inclusion of Boss-specific storylines and missions is cool, while the relationships and background of all of the gangsters you can hire adds another dimension to picking characters, as different combinations will open up different missions, in theory anyway.  I've loved Xcom since the original, but this is closer to a simplified knockoff like Hard West.  The game is incredibly buggy, with the entire marketplace disappearing in some saves, or characters locking up in a single stance, or unable to enter buildings, or missions crashing...Its Paradox though, so you know it'll be updated, it'll be supported, in about 6 months it'll be a completely different game, in a year it'll be another completely new version, and so on.  For now, it's fun when it works, you can see where it might go, but it isn't a finished product or really worth purchasing... yet.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm so disillusioned with this game. It's sad that Gangsters and Gangsters 2, PC games from 20+ years ago, offer a more complex, in-depth, fun, and more complete experience than this game. Empire of Sin is interesting for a short few hours when you first get into it and are learning the system. It's clear that the devs borrowed numerous elements from previous mob games before it, but that's the problem. It borrows them and doesn't do much to integrate these elements into the game resulting in a game that has what feels like cobbled together systems. A 'fast-travel' taxi system, but no cars that you can buy or use to travel and explore faster. Henchmen for buildings; but no way to bring henchmen into your group for extra muscle or even send them out to explore (but the computer mob bosses can send out henchmen to explore the city). An interesting system of loyalty and notoriety, but so poorly implemented that it requires intense grinding for hours before you have enough to recruit more mobsters. By the time you can most are already hired by the other gangs. Hope you like those first two mobsters you pick because you are going to be stuck with them for a long, long time. It really is a disappointment as everything Empire of Sin tries to do and wants to be, has been done before and done better by older games.

_childDocuments_.review: Take the turn-based tactical combat of XCOM, combine it with the management elements of a tycoon game, and slap a mafia skin on it, what could go wrong? Well, as it turns out, a lot of things, actually.So let’s just start this off by saying that I’m disappointed more than anything. This is a game with a fantastic concept, a game that could have been good. However, the execution is just shallow, nowhere near enough to really sell the experience.I have two major problems with Empire of Sin: its combat elements and its management elements. Considering that those are the two major areas to the game, we’re already off to a bad start, but I’ll talk about the combat first.This is a strategy game that has combat done in a turn-based tactics manner, similar to the XCOM series. You get your group of gangsters, enter a building, and have to eliminate all of the opposition to win. It’s pretty simple, but the real experience lies in the depth of that combat. I will admit, my first couple hours with the game, I was actually satisfied. The combat was fun and I was having a good time going from building to building growing my empire.However, I quickly found out that there is really nothing beyond that. The combat does not really evolve, it kinda remains static throughout the entire game, whether you be 2 hours in or 20. Despite going into different buildings, you’ll start to notice the exact same layouts, the same enemy types, the same weapons, and the same abilities used in every single fight. Sure, you unlock more abilities as your characters level up, but it’s only like four or five until they’ve maxed out, nowhere near enough to offer the combat depth required to avoid that feeling of monotony.Due to how simple it is, the combat eventually devolves into this repetitive sequence that you can apply to every single fight and win without issue. In fact, once I had a group of six or so gangsters, I pretty much steamrolled any competition. Whether it be a simple building takeover or a boss fight – they all felt the same and this alone honestly kills the overall experience.There is another side to the game though through its management elements. And unfortunately, those management elements are equally lacking. I would go so far as to equate them to a clicker game, as all you’re really doing is applying upgrades, switching which alcohol your establishments serve, and waiting for money to apply even more upgrades. There really is not much to do here, and it was so bad that at one point I was literally sitting there fiddling with my phone while I waited for money to come in so I could buy more upgrades so that the money would come in faster so that I could buy more upgrades and you can kinda see where this is going.However, all of that goes out the window when you realize that the entire management aspect is kinda pointless. Why spend time upgrading stuff or changing what alcohol your establishments are serving when you can simply waltz into an enemy safehouse, kill their boss, and acquire all of their buildings with just that one battle. Do this for each boss in the game and you’ve won, without ever needing to really engage with any sort of management.Really, the most management you get is with your characters themselves. They each have their own skill tree, a bunch of different equipment slots, and even traits and relationships. For example, a character that is in love with another gangster will not attack them even if they are on the opposing side in a battle. And sometimes a character’s loyalty to you will unlock gangsters for hire that would have otherwise been unavailable. Playing around with the characters was easily the best part of the management side to the game, but unfortunately the bulk of that side is managing your establishments – the boring part.During my time with the game, I ran into plenty of animation issues, clipping, and freezes during combat that would hang the game for seconds at a time. That and the AI is not the greatest either, oftentimes putting itself in really bad positions during combat or just acting in a manner that actively ruins their chances of winning. I was fortunate to not run into any crashes (the game has been patched up a bit since its rocky launch), but it’s still not an entirely smooth experience.I cannot recommend Empire of Sin. Patches may be able to fix the technical problems, but the core to the game is just far too shallow to be worth the time. Repetitive combat, lackluster management elements, it just loses its appeal after those initial few hours. A shame, as I really like the concept here, but the execution just doesn’t cut it.Follow my  for more reviews + videos!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a real toss-up for me. I'm basically 50/50 on it, and I wish Steam would allow me to post the review as neutral with information in here instead of a 'recommend' or not... because the game has the bones of something really cool. The structure is there. The visuals are wonderful. The systems in place have potential. The idea is great, and 'almost' executed well enough for a recommendation - but alas, the details were ignored, the pacing isn't right, the entire concept of the AI having even a 2nd grade reading level was overlooked, and the trade/barter/negotiation system is all one-sided. You have no say over the core of what makes this game great, and therefore, it becomes mediocre at best. It's an economy driven game, without the need to build much of an economy. It's a business simulator with no control over your prices. It's a multi-agency strategy game with no say over trades or negotiation terms (it's take what they offer you, or piss them off). It's a turn-based tactical combat game, without the need for proper tactics, even at Boss difficulty (the highest). It has many screens of in-depth information, but doesn't give you what you want to know when you want to know it. It'll interrupt your gameplay entirely with repetitive noises and loud crashing sounds for things you don't care about, and then fail to notify you on things you do care about. Even things like quest markers take an unusually long time to find on the map. It's as if they never thought allowing interaction with a quest would make the player want to know 'where' it takes place. A simple button to zoom in on the location would be best. Information such as what you're currently producing has no mouse-over at all (is that barrel swill or rack? I really don't know unless I go to another screen to find words next to the symbol. Why can't there be mouse overs on this stuff?).Also... the strongest weapon in the entire game is the taxi. Don't bother investing in security. It's not needed. Just pause, taxi there instantly during pause with your hero, and blow the enemy up. It needs improvements, and perhaps due to it's extensive modding capabilities, we'll get even more than the devs have planned... assuming they have it planned. I wish them well on their journey to make this game the great game it was meant to be. I hope they see the criticism in the reviews as an opportunity to improve it to something awesome, like No Mans Sky has done, and not something to abandon, like say... Phantom Doctrine. Overall right now, I give it a 6/10 -- and at $40, that's just not good enough. Wait for a deep sale now, or evaluate when it's had some patches, has improved it's AI greatly, has expanded it's availability of information, and hopefully has fixed Salazar's voice... because... well.. that voice has got to go. It's basically a non-native Spanish speaker trying to sound Mexican in the form of a TTS readout. I'm not kidding.

It feels like I'm breezing by killing everyone and everything in my way with no actual strategy needed in attacks, who I ally with or who I make an enemy of - because I can legitimately just squash them all like ants with absolutely zero repercussions, as long as I don't just do it all at the one time. Combat has no difficulty, the AI is absurdly bad and opens itself to easy attacks like they're just begging you to kill them. There's no real strategy in what is supposed to be a strategy game.The characters themselves have no personality, which while isn't necessarily important for a strategy game, I feel that if you're going to give us the ability to become friends with and enemies with the other gangsters within Chicago, it might be best to ensure that they all don't feel like the same cardboard cutout with a different paintjob.Now, this game isn't terrible, it just gets really boring incredibly fast. I just can't recommend it at full price, but on sale? Absolutely. I put hours upon hours into other Paradox Interactive products (mainly Crusader Kings II), so I have faith that they'll eventually get around to adding things to make the game more interesting, so hey maybe even wait until then. The idea of the game, being a gangster and building up your empire brick by brick is a good foundation and I really wanted to like it (and I am going to keep playing it, so this review might change!). I just hope they can bring this game to the full potential that its bland self just can't seem to reach as of right now.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a pretty solid foundation for a turn based tactics game. However it is not very polished and has a lot of minor issues and a few major ones. For instance my best campaign so far was ended because I destroyed a faction, and that dead faction would try to talk to me later which would immediately freeze the game, forcing me to Alt+F4 it and restart. Loading back into that campaign would lead to that same thing happening soon after the save, so a multiple hour long campaign is just ended due to a bug. The minor issues include things like unskippable conversations (which are about the same between every boss, so get old fast), character pathing getting stuck while exploring on the map, and the game hanging mid-combat while it seems to be calculating something. The game is basically still in a beta state with many bugs, some of which are game breaking so I cannot recommend it in its current state.However, the game has a lot of upgrades over Xcom 2 which is the closest game I have played to this style. There is a percentage chance to hit predictor that updates as you mouse over tiles a character can move to. The percentage chance to hit does not lie from what I can tell, whereas in Xcom 2 the player will miss more shots the better they do in missions, so the RNG is wildly inaccurate once you get into a campaign. You recruit the same basic soldiers early, but with their relationships you can recruit some late game people earlier in the campaign so you can recruit a wide variety of people. You can also influence how their traits are gained to an extent, making each soldier slightly different in every playthrough. If the developers work on this game it has a chance to be great, it is just not currently in a fun state as players will just get frustrated with the glaring bugs and other issues.EDIT: As an update to this review, the bug that initially prevented me from progressing was fixed, and I was able to finish my first campaign. However upon starting a new one on the next higher difficulty I was unable to attack any territories as whenever I clicked to attack the game just ignored my input. The devs have been releasing fairly quick patches to fix bugs, however there are still some that break the game so my overall review still stands.

_childDocuments_.review: Sorry for my english in advance.I will tell about three things that mattered to me.1. Combat/Global War.It has two stages.First - you paid for two mercs and you steamroll everything. Thug buildings, enemy rackets, random guards on the street, you name it.Second - when you attack enemy safehouse game suddenly boosts guards stats and numbers. Which is understandable since you're coming for their boss. But there is no difference between boss with 100k cash, 100k hooch and 100 rackets, and boss with nothing. Number of guards, their toughness will be same.Which means when you can crack one safehouse without losing anyone in the process - you just won the game.You don't need to slowly bleed your opponent out of money, muscle, hooch or whatever. You just go to safehouse, win boss fight and that's it. You just got what he had.2. Management.Prices in game have no sense in terms of upgrade. Meaningful (and there are not many) upgrades cost almost as much as full new racket which is x4 times more effective.Then you realise that it is not effective to spend money to buy buildings when it is far easier to just conquer every minor faction you come across cause they can't defend themselves.The only upgrade i did in my game is to get increse quality of hooch. that's it.Guns and everything war related is found in crates in your starting neighborhood, so you don't need to buy them really.Just buy some med kits before safehouse mission and that's it.Playing "tall" like getting your neighborhood only for youself and getting upgrades is basically non-existent unless you are really forcing it.3. Diplomacy.Ever played any Civilization?)Same here. Like really same.Constant changes in the mood day by day. I had moments when two factions were in and out of their alliance daily for a couple of weeks.Bribing police for relationship is super expensive. And you will basically win whole game before being able to really have this money to spend on this.Summary.Bugs aside game is mediocre at best. Repetetive with copy-pasting from X-COM/Civilization and very basic management.I really hope that there will be workshop support (cause i can't return this game after 14 hours of play) and some enthusiasts will make needed changes to the game design.Love Paradox and hope this game will turn into something good.

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of people don't like this game and I can kinda see why, but at the same time I think its the most fun I've had in a while. You can be allies with someone who goes to war with someone in a different district, and you can ask to take a few buildings in that district and then you can get a foothold in there and its just you and your ally. You could then betray your ally with outside help and take over that district. I get why everyones disappointed with the racket system, I am too, but I think its a little too much to ask to have a system similar to Omerta: City Of Gangsters which was extremely in depth with several different forms to make the same kind of money. If they could do something like this, maybe in a huge update or DLC or something, I think this would be the perfect successor to Omerta, as this game is obviously heavily inspired by it. Anyways, I think that you should buy the game and try it out, I really like it and its probably one of my favorite games this year. If you're looking for a semi-casual exaggerated mafia experience similar to Omerta, this is a perfect game. It may not be ALL perfect, but I still think its worth atleast trying it out.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a well researched visit to roaring twenties Chicago.  Unfortunately, every time I have played, the game session has ended in a crash.  That is at least ten sessions by now..  The mechanics of combat are smooth enough, the engine seems to have trouble managing itself.  A rival gang started a war and hit three of my business one right after another just as I had entered to clean out a third gang's 'racket'.  The engine froze.  If I play for over three hours, chances are I will have to 'end task' and gripe about not saving.  Autosaves seem arbitrary, too.  It just wasn't ready.  This is poor quality control on a game that doesn't seem to be too involved.  The database management could be smoother and the interface less obtuse, but they did a good job of keeping it from being a spreadsheet management game.  I look forward to the next six months of patches that will address most of the issues as that seems to be the industry model.  I had high hopes for this game.  It delivered as promised, mostly.  Its instability is a turn-off.

_childDocuments_.review: Updated review as of August 25, 2022Came back to this game after a while and it's been improved slightly. However, not enough to the point that I'd say it was worth the price. Upon some reflection, I recommended the game initially due to what it potentially had rather than what it currently has. I haven't bumped into any game breaking bugs anymore so I guess that's a plus. Otherwise, it seems like the game has stayed nearly the same with some minor changes to combat, quests, and the businesses.In conclusion, I've changed my review to 'Do Not Recommend'. Additionally, the dev updates have stop and, newsflash, it's been 9 months since the last official update (last one was November 2021 and it's August 2022) so take that as you will. Do I regret purchasing it? A little but I did have fun for the most part. Probably will come back to it once in a while when I get bored.-----TL; DR: Bugs (quests, mechanics, and dialogue), repetitive visuals and combat, and feels like it's missing key features. Graphics are fine, has not crashed yet, stable frames, foundations for the game seem like they're there. I recommend EoS but only when on sale. Otherwise, just hold on to your money and hope it gets active support.First of all, some background, I only heard of this game through CallMeKevin and pre-purchased it after seeing Blitz and CMK's sponsored videos on EoS. I liked what I see from the videos. Two other factors that affected my decision to purchase the game were that a.) it was developed my Romero Games (I'm more familiar with John Romero's work) and b.) that it will be published by Paradox Interactive. Knowing Paradox Interactive their games (developed or published by them) tend to have long lasting support and DLC with two already slated to be released in the future. In its present state, the game has bugs, mostly found in quests, diplomacy, and combat. The quest bugs are really annoying and game breaking. It's either you can't find the NPC (High Roller Heaven quest) or the mechanics of the quest are broken (breweries remain closed after finishing the quest for Jacques). It needs quite a few quality of life improvements (like a better way to filter properties in your empire and a way to see the day progression maybe a clock or meter). The tutorial is solid enough though I had to figure certain things out myself. The economy and management aspects are pretty easy to understand but makes it feel lackluster. As for combat, it's pretty repetitive and loses its flare after a couple of fights. Diplomacy and interactions with the other factions are bland, making it feel unnecessary. Properties and the map could really do with some changes. It gets repetitive. One thing to note is it hasn't crashed yet, at least.It's not all bad. Even if combat is repetitive, it is currently not buggy (the same can't be said for the rest of the game), the existing aspects are decent. Map is big, even if it's repetitive like the combat, a single playthrough could potentially last hours. A decent number of mob bosses to start with (still hoping for custom character creation). Frames are stable for me. A few things that, in my opinion, could help make the game better, adding more roles and actions you can take as the boss, adding more kinds of businesses, and interactions with local politics (this happens through a quest and ends there). Just my opinion, won't really affect my review.I enjoy the game but it feels like it's missing a lot of features which I hope get added in free and not tied to DLC. Unfortunately, it feels like a game that could pass up as an early access game. I heard modding tools will be added which will, most likely, make it better off.  I recommend it for the potential and the foundations are there I can see that there are building blocks to make it a good game. However, in the state that it is in, I only recommend purchasing when it is on sale. I will probably update this review when I feel like enough changes are made or if I find anything else to add during my playthrough.Edit: Added quests can get extremely buggy and some are game breaking.Edit (August 25, 2022)
