_childDocuments_.review: In my experience, game sequels that come out many years after the original usually fall into one of two categories:1. Development Hell Garbage2. _childDocuments_.review: The rare sequel that manages to live up to (and in some ways surpass) the original, but 20 years later.  The fact that they managed to pull this one off after so much time is incredible.  The platforming and combat feels smoother and tighter thanks to a modern engine, but all the imagination and creativity of the original is still here.  If anything, there's a bit of a darker edge to this one and the game is willing to confront some questions/issues that the original didn't.  This is an excellent platformer about mental health.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoy this game for a variety of reasons.Easier use and selection of psychic powers in comparison to Psychonauts 1, which was a bit of a rollercoaster for me in finding out how to switch and bind abilities to a certain key on a controller.Beautiful graphics that fit in with the theme and artistic intent of the game. One qualm is that Double Fine didn't make the interns or any of the workers at HQ look anywhere near as hideous as some of the designs in the first game, which is a pity because I was looking forward to gawking at some absolute monstrosities in the sequel.The levels are large and challenge you relatably to the psychic ability you've most recently attained while also making sure that other powers aren't sidelined, I also like how the game isn't quite linear in the choices you can make in fights and level exploration and completion with your psychic abilities, leaving nigh all of them quite viable in most levels and circumstances.I think the VA for Raz (Richard Horvitz) did an incredible job returning to a role from 2005 (though production on the first game begun pre-2002 based on E3 footage from the time).One really essential change from the first game is the ability to 100% the game after finishing it, which was a luxury those who did Meat Circus in the first game did not have, thanks Double Fine :)

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked the original Psychonauts then you'll probably enjoy this one. Overall a good game. Strike City and Compton's Cookoff were my favorite levels. It was nice to have Lilli along in the Fatherland's Follies level.Some minor nitpicks: Bob Zanotto's turnip persona when he's being carried by a bird and Doodle Raz get pretty annoying, very quickly. Turnip Bob quips get repeated and loop frequently when the bird is circling around with him. Use gag order pin on Doodle Raz to help alleviate his talking.The items/places that are locked and need Mental Projection could have just used Telekinesis instead. Combat use for Mental Projection differentiates at least with it being a distraction for enemies.Cosmetic pins and power buffs compete for the same 3 spots. The game is easy enough where power pins aren't needed.More involvement with the interns in the story. It doesn't have to be every single mind or use every intern. Maybe have one of them help traverse a specific mind and/or fight the boss by dealing with a mechanic or supporting Raz during the fight. Psychic Six presence in final battle instead of or in addition to the interns since they felt more earned.Have something happen after the initial spat with Hollis and the Aquatos, specifically the mother. More of the family involved in general. If there's another game, it'll be nice to explore the world and adventure through minds with Lilli, Agustus/Frazie Aquato family members, Senior Psychonauts like Sasha/Milla or whoever the next set of side characters would be. *Spoiler* Use water as part of the platforming in the next game using Hydrokinesis. *Spoiler*

_childDocuments_.review: What an incredible game! Honestly, after waiting so long for the sequel to what I consider a near-perfect game, I was worried it might not live up to the huge shoes the original Psychonauts left to fill. With excellent level design, writing, humour, and phenomenal style, Psychonauts 2 absolutely delivers and adds to Double Fine's impressive catalogue of outstanding games. Exploring more themes of mental psychology including depression, loss, addiction, grief, and others, Psychonauts 2 expands on the ideas of not "fixing" people, but helping them with their mental damage and confronting things that have hurt them. It's so rare to find a piece of media that so carefully considers the mental state of characters all while throwing in tasteful humour from likeable characters. On top of everything, Psychonauts 2, like the original, is a fantastic 3D platformer/collectathon that is more than worth the time of anyone that loves games. Please play these games! (Rhombus of Ruin can be watched if you don't have a VR setup)

_childDocuments_.review: I'll be quick, without many spoilers, because a lot of people have already given so many awesome reviews.It's one of the best games I have played in recent years. At its core it's an indie game, crowdfunded by the fans and supported by Microsoft. The story picks up where the first game left off and offers a lot of closure to the story of Raz Aquato and Psychonauts as a whole. It dives deeper into minds of human beings and explores mental health issues themes, just like the first game. This time tackling (among many more) loneliness, split personality, addiction and anxiety. It's told in a creative cinematic way.The world and level design are amazing. I'd say on par with the new Ratchet and Clank game. The only thing that differs here is the fact that there's no ray-tracing. Sticking to the OG artstyle, but using UE4 was a well thought-out decision. Sadly, that same decisions had its downfalls. Like stuttering issues and occasional framedrops. While well optimised, I had some problems with low framerate in some areas of the game. Granted, I do play at 1440p so those playing at 1080p might not have the issue.Worth playing for fans and newcomers alike. Even if you haven't played the first game, there is a quick "Last time on Psychonauts" video that catches you up to speed with the overall story.Truly, a gorgeous and intriguing adventure that everyone should go on, even if they don't like platformers or adventure games.I give Psychonauts 2 100 brains out of 10 brains!And with my whole heart I hope for a remaster of the first game sometime along the line... And perhaps another sequel? Please, daddy Schafer?GIVE MOREEEE

_childDocuments_.review: Psychonauts 2 is the type of sequel that greatly expands and elevates the ideas of its predecessor.Visually the game has improved on a technical level, of course, but it still retains the same overall art style. There is a shift in focus between the first and second title. Environments are much bigger both in the overworld and within levels. There's also more obligatory verticality which is nice. The levitation ability has been nerfed which is welcomed because it makes platforming more engaging.The first game was a blend of platformer and adventure game, while Psychonauts 2 is firmly a platformer. There is an expanded focus on combat with many more types of enemies as well as specific weaknesses for certain foes. Abilities are also upgradable in an order that you choose. They can allow customization in how you go about combat.Story and plot take a focus, continuing off of the end of the first Psychonauts game and their VR-only adventure (I suggest you look up a playthrough if you don't have VR and want to be informed on the plot). Returning characters are present but not the focus with most of the screentime dedicated to introducing and developing the new characters we meet at Psychonauts headquarters. There's an engaging mystery, callbacks to the first game, and a couple key memorable moments between Raz and the characters from the first game he idolizes.As for critiques I have there's one big gameplay one and one big story one, both spoiler free. The gameplay gripe I have is the pin system. It feels needlessly restrictive to have only three alterations to your abilities via pins active at a time. Some of these are just cosmetic and should not occupy a slot. Pins are also expensive so unless you spend time grinding for currency as well as prioritize the pins that generate extra income or earn discounts you won't have access to even half of the pins before the final levels. The story gripe is that specific characters are neglected and could have had more screen time. Returning characters have a lot to do at the start of the game but for most of the rest of the game they stand around in a way that feels quite static. The new characters like Raz's new piers are more dynamic but we don't get as much time to spend with them as I would like. There are also far fewer than the large cast of campers for the first game so there is a slight feeling that headquarters is somewhat underpopulated.Despite small criticisms, it is an amazing fact that this game exists. After the financial failure the first was and the decade it took to get another game the fact that this game isn't a cash-grab or a pale retread but rather a shining examplre of how to make a sequel shows that there genuinely is a spark to this franchise that makes it unique. Psychonauts 2 delivers not just on the premise of being more Psychonauts but also a solid 3D platformer in this age of the genre's revival.

_childDocuments_.review: There is a lot one could say about this game. It truly shows what kind of masterpiece a video game can be when the right people come together. Just like the previous installment, this one continues to be passionate and well-executed. Comparatively, there is a significant difference due to the nearly two-decade gap. Let’s start with the obvious, the visuals are drastically enhanced. I’ve rarely seen such a fluid and expressive animation. Especially the faces manage to convey a lot of emotions. The world-building in this one manages to be not only great on it’s own but also expand upon its predecessor’s. They even keep a lot of memorable characters from the previous game while also introducing us to new ones. And just like before, the relevant characters are not merely one-note but have a certain dept to their personalities.Although the story is a bit predictable in certain regards it still managed to keep me hooked with a certain level of mystery. I believe it may be a result of the frequent foreshadowing that the player tends to get spoiled a lot throughout. There is also the occasional pacing problems due to the game shoving multiple objectives onto you before you can proceed with the story. And while each objective contributes to the overall narrative, it does tend to break up the pace when you’re forced to enter multiple minds before being able to reach a turning point in the story. Nevertheless, I have to commend the writers, they managed to whip up a story that goes hand in hand with the previous game and has multiple layers to it.The gameplay also experienced a major improvement. They trimmed some of the unnecessary abilities and features from the previous game and kept the good bits. While I’m not a huge fan of the strong focus on combat I can’t deny how well they managed to implement it, with each ability serving a purpose when fighting enemies. They even introduce a lot more new enemy types in this one which prevents the combat from being monotone. While gathering the collectibles wasn’t as stressful this time, I still ran around a lot, looking for the needle in a haystack. They should consider providing the player with some form of detector for figments at least. But I suppose it’s overall a good sign that I only needed a guide to find a single collectible in the hub world. Speaking of which, the hub world is great and very lively in this one. Truly makes me feel like I’m playing an actual video game and not one of those awful simulator games. The individual minds you enter are also amazing, both visually and from a gameplay perspective. Each mind manages to stand out on its own with a unique feature or design. However, certain ones tend to overstay their welcome due to being a bit too lengthy. I will say this though, there is one mind that dumps so much exposition at you in such a creative way that I can’t do anything but praise the people who came up with that idea.What else is left to say? Perhaps some of my highlights. If you’re a fan of Invader Zim you’re going to get a kick out of seeing a reunion between Zim and GIR. The comedy in this game is also superb with occasional adult jokes thrown it at times. I remember overhearing a conversation between two employees, indicating that the woman was cheating on her husband with a fellow coworker, only to be revealed that they are planning a party for the husband. Or how Raz’s dad is told to think of something hot to set a pinecone on fire, just for him to reply that he will think of Raz’s mother. And for music fans out there, Jack Black voices a character in this one who even gets to sing a song. Truly a work of art overall, I’m rooting for Psychonauts 3.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: Psychonauts one was a magical game and honestly, creating a sequel? I can't imagine much more difficult tasks. That being said, they really did hit the nail on the head with this sequel. I felt like I was back in a new adventure with raz but the world was much bigger, more monsters, better platforming, bigger brains, and cooler powers. It took a while but we got a cool continuation of the story and the whole ride was fun from start to finish. The movement is fast and fluid and making raz jump off trees and hop from tight ropes to swinging on bars was fun as hell. Not to mention the story and how it turns mental issues into something imaginative and interactive blows my mind. 10/10 worth full price.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: A solid platformer with an excellent story, dialog, and quirky humor. Combat can be a bit basic, but there are plenty of in game modifiers that can be obtained to customize powers to be more towards your liking. Very creative level design and exploration opens up after the first few levels.If you played the previous games, this is a must have as this is an improvement over the original. For those of you that haven't played any of the other games in the series, the first boot of the game has a short summary to cover the basics References and callbacks to the previous games and some of the game mechanics may seem even odder without the context.As far as negatives go, finding collectibles in the levels can be bit of a pain as there's no easy way to know what specific items you may be missing. And for anyone finding the game too difficult, there are readily available difficulty accessibility settings to mitigate damage or boost your own.If you aren't interested in collecting every little bit of everything, this game will probably clock in at a solid 20 or so hours.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a true sequel, fulfills the promise of Psychonauts 1. Does everything a sequel should, expands on the world of the original while remaining faithful to all of the lore and essence of the series. I was honestly worried that a game that cleverly utilized the polygonal nature of 2005 platformers could feel the same with a modern sequel, but it did extremely well. There are a lot of references and nods to Rhombus of Ruin, rewarding players who bought the VR bridge game. Great work and real heart was put into development. _childDocuments_.review: A worthy sequel to the original - not better, which is likely partially my own fault.Pros:* Signature DoubleFine humor all over the place.* Great level design and music.* Great plotlines and voice acting.* Nice wrapping-up of loose threads from the original.* Mostly great re-implementation of fundamentals, to streamline the game.* Excellent new enemies and groupings of same, requiring switching up strategies on the fly.Cons:* Freeze bug when examining objects in inventory system; gotta kill  the game to get around it.  WTH?* None of the levels are quite as... bug-f*ck nuts, as the original. (which  based in an asylum, though?)* Levels seem a little more... formulaic, than in the original.* When replaying a level, I miss the teleporters at the end of the level; instead, have to either retrace steps to a teleporter, or jump entirely out of the "mind" then go all the way back in.* The game's just not as... original?...  as the original.  Likely just because I've played the 1st one to death.* Lots of missed opportunities with the other interns - the "fellow kids" shtick was done much better in the original.* No longer can punch while on a levitation bubble. Ditto w/ gliding indefinitely. WTF?* Cosmetic changes (bubble color change, idle dance, etc) now need to occupy an equipment slot I'd use for fighting enemies... which means I'll never use them.* $60.  Really?TL;DR: If you merely liked the original or never played it at all - and it's not on sale - then 5/10.  If you loved the original it might be worth your cash at full price, else if it's on sale, 7/10.Edit: Added more details and dropped scores by 1 - the nerfs (cosmetic & levitation) and high price are serious dissatisfiers.

_childDocuments_.review: While the game has some really great moments, for every smart level there's an equal amount of content that feels overtly designed by committee, or some awkwardly non-intuitive platforming puzzle.Worse is the game's ideology. While the gameplay conceit of using what amounts to psychology to solve individual problems in order to fix wider issues carries an inherently neoliberal rhetoric of individual responsibility for global welfare, this is unpleasantly an ideology the narrative and themes firmly grapple onto. The plot is ostensibly in favor of 'peace keeping' foreign interventionalism and forgiving war criminals for their past actions; and the narrative is told entirely from the perspective of the invaders with the locals being set dressing for the story. This makes the seemingly checklisted approach to cast diversity feel rather offensive, as despite clearly strained efforts towards inclusivity the game tosses away the script time of its more diverse cast in favor of the hegemonic elites which dominate the narrative. The beginning hours are also particularly rough, strangely committing a lot of narrative weight to the mediocre VR exclusive marketing-gimmic game that came out last year.All that said the game is often enjoyable and occasionally very smart, were it not the sequel to a superior title I may have given it a thumbs up.

_childDocuments_.review: Psychonauts was one of the first games I have ever played. It brings me so much joy to know that this underrated classic got a sequel, knowing that it might have never even gotten one. This game is what I think makes a perfect sequel. It carries a lot over from the original game like abilities, collectables, and the platforming. It also features newer abilities, and an enhanced combat system which I thought the first game really needed. It just feels so good to bash through newer enemies, and using a bit more thinking to which powers would come to use during combat. I love the level designs, and visual aesthetics all of them bring. Also, staying true to the games original surreal experience. It's also great to see a bunch of returning characters such as Raz, and all of the Psychonaut Agents from the previous game. Even expanding upon some of them and making more room for story telling. This games story does a good job carrying out the first games plot, and dives deep into the origins of the Psychonauts agency as a whole. A minor complaint being the protagonist Raz, not being as snarky, or smug which made his character in the first game. Though, it is very nice to see all of these characters set in a new environment, and we get to see more of them in action. It's amazing to get to experience this franchise again. I would definitely recommend this, and the first game to those who enjoy platformers. It's such an amazing experience to go through first hand, because of how unexpected the game can be.

_childDocuments_.review: An improvement on the original in some ways, and a huge letdown in others. If you want more Psychonauts, this is for you, but if you just find the premise and story interesting, the first game is a better bet.While this sequel does make the platforming less frustrating, its combat is almost unplayable, and large parts of the game clearly haven't been tested. The side characters also aren't quite as interesting as they were in the first game, and you'll find nothing here as iconic as the milkman conspiracy or lungfish city.On the other hand, if you've been waiting a decade plus for a Psychonauts sequel, you largely won't be disappointed (as long as you can make it through the train wreck that is the first level). However, coming from that end, you'll also be utterly lost if you happen to be one of the vast majority of people who doesn't own a VR headset and was unable to play the (story-essential) Rhombus of Ruin spinoff.Ultimately, this review is marked as negative simply because I think the people who would enjoy this game won't be deterred by anything I have to say, and those who might not enjoy it should know up front what they're getting into.EDIT: It turns out you can (and, frankly, should) essentially turn combat off in the accessibility options--both by making yourself do extra damage and/or by turning yourself invincible. This definitely makes the game easier to recommend, but still leaves me recommending the first game over this one, as while its combat could be frustrating, I never felt the need to do anything as drastic as disable it completely.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely a great sequel to the first game. If you enjoyed the first one, this is right down your alley. For those who haven't played the first game:  If you enjoy platformer games, a lot of puns, play on words, backtracking through brilliant zones, collect-a-thons, bacon, quirky art designs, and a well thought out story to tie it all together, then you'll enjoy this and the first game. (I'd recommend checking out or at least viewing the 2 - 3 hr VR 'Rombus of Ruin' to help clue you in to the start of the game.)The humour is kid themed, but has that same sense of awareness as a parent does, knowing that kids will inevitably encounter some subjects through their lives as mentioned in the game, and doesn't shy away from presenting it. I appreciate their willingness to touch on dark topics with a whimsical veneer to make it more palettable.The controls are great  (using an xbox controller) and only a few times when you feel like you should have interacted with a ledge/rope/enemy but didn't, and perhaps one or two spots in one level where I suspect I shouldn't have been where I fell through an invisible pit a few times. The auto-aiming can be a bit of a struggle to get it to work right sometimes, but most of the time auto-aim makes targeting/shooting insanely easy.The only thing I'd wish to change is having a figment locator, I love the zones, but you can only spend so many hours in one psychedelic brain for the last fragment for so long.

This means in tight situations, you'll find yourself constantly rolling off objects or platforms you want to stay on which is really annoying. I'd love to have more action oriented controls, so if I'm facing forward but move the stick left, snap Razputin to the left immediately rather than make him rotate. Sure, it's not realistic, but neither is the game, so this control feature would be just fine.Since I switched to KB+M, the difficulty in controlling Rasputin decreased immensely and I'm way happier with the game. But there is one problem though...The M button is hardcoded to bring up the menu. There is no way to re-map this button to something else. It's not in the control settings. _childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game. Remembering the first part almost 20 years ago, I do remember some tedious parts about this as well. Walking around the summer camp has always low-key bored me, searching for psi cards and other gimmicks and finding ways how to reach difficult spots - not really my jam.What was pretty cool were the minds of people, carefully designed levels, each on their own pretty cool, with interesting and unique gameplay parts and differing greatly in style. The milkman conspiracy, Black Velvetopia, the theater, the Napoleon guy - it was epic.What have we here now? A bunch of the same old mechanics that weren't fun for me back then and aren't fun today. Boring and large hubs. Yes, they are beautiful, but I simply do not enjoy exploring them. They're too normal. The mind worlds I have seen so far were pretty lackluster but they would be okay if there were more of them and I could explore them more often. Instead I have to walk around a hub and finish tedious tasks, and between every single step, there is a cutscene.This should be called Psychonauts 2 - the movie. I hate switching between the psi powers because it feels annoying, here you need to burn something, here you need telekinesis, it's all always pretty obvious and I have to switch powers using some mini menu. It's not TERRIBLE but has me roll my eyes. Then there are tons of parts where I am not sure - can I go there? Will I slip? Am I supposed to jump on here?The jump and run mechanics are partially annoying and tedious but manageable *cough cough comb tower* Wish it was less of "here a platform and there some moving thing pushing you down and here some obstacle and here a bomb" and more of "wow this looks actually amazing and going there feels like actual fun and like it belongs to this level design and isn't just here because platform platform jump jump curse curse"So it's basically all the parts I disliked about Psychonauts 1 minus the cool parts of it. I've seen that there are not that many minds to explore and some seem to be about war. If it continues like that, I might not even finish this chore of a game. Cutscene 2.

_childDocuments_.review: This will be a comparison to the legendary Psychonauts (first game), for everyone who wonders if it lives up to its predecessor! I recently finished both games, so this is from fresh memory. No particular order to the categories below.Graphics/Level Design: Obviously MUCH better graphics. Great animated cutscenes, cleaner effects, BEAUTIFUL environments which fit every mind just as well as the original game. Still true to wacky character designs, non-Euclidean world, it just looks much better. Psychonauts 1 did level design extremely well, and Psychonauts 2 is a worthy successor. Very unique levels, always appropriate to the mind. See it for yourself!Sound/Music: To be honest, Psychonauts 1 didn't have very memorable soundtracks, just very atmospheric background music. (Great exception is Waterloo OST.) Psychonauts 2 has some very beautiful OST, especially in the lategame minds which tone down the pure wackiness. Wonderful!Dialogue/Voice: I'm torn on this one. Psychonauts 1 was FULL of great lines and great voice acting. Psychonauts 2 is more of a hit or miss: Sometimes, it gave me a "isn't this cool, kids?" vibe, but other times, it was back to Psychonauts 1 quality. Milla talks very slowly, for some reason. Also much more toilet humor than in Psychonauts 1, but to each their own.Story (no spoilers): Psychonauts 1 had a pretty silly story/plot, but it fit the levels and dialogue very well. Half the levels have no direct relation to the main story. Psychonauts 2 is less silly and designs levels much more closely related to the main story. It depends if you like it or not. I liked both!Combat: No contest, Psychonauts 2 did it better: no more shield, timed dodging, earlier (but less overpowered) area attacks, all abilities can be used for combat, more mobile melee, far bigger enemy variety (while staying somewhat in-universe). You get access to Blast, Levitation, Pyro, Clairvoyance, Telekinesis in the tutorial. Each ability has their own energy system: You can blast much quicker, but you need a little time to recharge. You can use other abilities in the meantime, so you are basically encouraged to use as many different abilities as possible during combat. Confusion grenades and Invisibility were scrapped, sorry if you liked them. Definitely higher difficulty: some enemies are fast, many enemies are ranged, etc. No more one-blast-everything-explodes.Game length/Achievements:  I took about 23 hours to 100% Psychonauts 1 (but I've played it before) and about 26 hours to 100% Psychonauts 2. I always took my time to look around for secrets and collectibles in every level, then guides for the last 5% I missed. Psychonauts 1 unfortunately has multiple points at which you can no longer get a specific achievement - since I planned to 100% from the beginning, I had to inform myself beforehand. Psychonauts 2 only has two relatively early achievements you can miss out on, and features post-game exploration of all areas and levels you've finished before. This is necessary too, since you can only 100% in post-game. You can see a great overview of all collectibles for each area from your menu too. One downside: figments of the same shape are grouped together in the overview, if you miss one you may have to visit all their locations.Play Psychonauts 1 first! If you have VR, play Rhombus of Ruin too, it's canon. And then play Psychonauts 2! You are allowed to ignore the previous games, but there are plenty of references you'll miss out on.

_childDocuments_.review: This is, hands down, my new favorite game ever made. It is expertly crafted and made with an utterly absurd amount of love and care. Each and every moment of playing this game felt like a gift I waited a decade to receive with every moment being entirely worth it. Never before have I played a game that made me feel like this game does. To start this review, I'll go over changes from the original:Raz is much snappier to control and almost all of the awkwardness with his Levitation ball, pole/swing bar interaction, and camera issues have been eradicated in this game. Whereas the original Psychonauts controls as you'd expect (a semi-early 3D platformer), this one absolutely crushes it in the control department. The only changes I can think of from the original I truly dislike are Raz's double jump and the Levitation float.Double jump has been drastically changed to be more in line with platformer expectations whereas the original had a floaty double jump that had Raz dip down before rising back up. It was bouncier, and felt somewhat defining to that title. The Levitation float has been eviscerated. No longer can you float forever nor fly with the speedrun exploit. While I expected the exploit to be removed (sadly) I did not anticipate the forever float being taken away as well.Figments are easier to grab, are more visible, and are less hidden on average. Collectibles in this game tend to not be hidden behind stationary objects but rather out in the open, behind a puzzle, or near some sort of interactive object. This makes finding everything relatively easy for those scouring about and makes full completion more of a time-based endeavor rather than one based on scrutiny/attention to detail. The Scavenger Hunt items do not require the quick puzzle-solving of the originals and feel like a bit of a downgrade on that front. Almost all of these are either out in the open or behind an ability gate and is slightly disappointing as someone who was a fan of the original's mini puzzles. The new collectibles are top notch.New enemies! Psychonauts had an EXTREME lack in enemy diversity which has been remedied almost entirely here. Each enemy functions differently and is many times more interesting than just the standard Censors. Many function essentially as mini-bosses if there's enough support surrounding them though are easy to beat on their own. It's well worth experimenting with abilities on them as the devs made sure to include multiple ways to fight and interact simultaneously.Level-ups function much differently. Rather than periodically getting enhancements to powers or new powers altogether periodically Psychonauts 2 gives four upgrades per ability you can buy with your levels. Powers unlock at set intervals in the story now and are not level-related. There are some powers missing from Psychonauts but there was a distinct effort to make the new ones feel just as, if not more interesting and even an attempt to combine older powers together in the new title.Now, onto the new stuff:The game leaves an incredibly strong first impression with its stylized opening that does a serviceable job of catching new players up and a nostalgia trip for existing fans. I'm going to be entirely honest here. I cried. I cried during the opening cinematic because I was **actually playing Psychonauts 2** and I couldn't believe this game was real. The score at the beginning (and throughout) is fantastic and is littered with leitmotifs and themes from the first game that pull me back into the world with ease and elicit old memories. It felt like coming back to an old friend anew. I can't think of any other way to describe it.Each and every level has a wonderful theming and is delightful to play... barring one. But, I will fully admit that one level is more than likely going to be enjoyable for the majority of players and it just didn't tickle my fancy. The mental issues presented are still very welcome choices even when the first Psychonauts took the lion's share of the big, well-known illnesses. The levels twist and turn on themselves with frequent use of impossible architecture, world-bending pathing, and straight up impossible changes to an incredibly impressive degree. I remember circling around in one of the late game levels and immediately realizing I was curling in on myself and I started giggling like an absolute idiot. It was bliss.The new characters are overall very well-designed aside from one of the interns whose name I consistently have to look up as he's just that forgettable. The writing is pretty great all things considered. I actually had to look up if Erik Wolpaw worked on this title as well and apparently he did but was not credited for it so I'm not entirely sure how much of the game he contributed to. In any case, if your game's writing makes me look up if one of the main Portal 2 writers was involved you've done something very, very right.The story is sublime and dives into the heart of the beginning of it all. I won't say more so as to remain spoiler free but if you pay attention and collect the Memory Vaults you will walk away with a pretty comprehensive history of the Psychonauts, their world, and how they fit into it. All of which is ridiculously satisfying for someone who had questions about all that subject matter after/during the first game. I, again, cried multiple times throughout the story both due to plot points and from joy that I was **STILL** playing the sequel I had waited so long for.Visually the game is certainly up to snuff. It's not groundbreaking or anything but it doesn't need to be. The world design, concepts, and how the devs play with the idea of being inside a mind was always the main draw to Psychonauts and it's here in spades. It's beautiful to look at with many areas/enemies having detailed flourishes. I should clarify that when I say "groundbreaking" I mean "this title's visuals will shake the industry or entirely revitalize a style of graphics". That word comes with revolutionary standards that Psychonauts 2 doesn't meet, even though it still excels.All in all, Psychonauts 2 is an enthralling experience through and through. Nothing quite measures up to it and it is wholly unique to the point of standing in its own field. I sincerely hope the success and popularity of this game motivates Double Fine to add to this franchise every 4-5 years rather than leaving us all high and dry for so long.I highly recommend it to literally anybody. There is not a soul on this planet who should not play this game.The original is a cult classic, and this one is a modern masterpiece.

_childDocuments_.review: Psychonauts 2 picks up right where the first game/VR title left off in more ways than just its story. All of the platforming/basic psychic powers are available right after the first introductory level, unlike a lot of other sequels that wipe away the main character's progression from the previous game. However these powers have been expanded upon with the introduction of the upgrade system, and each tier of these upgrades feel impactful to gameplay. There is also the pin system, of which 3 can be equipped to give cosmetic or functional effects to your psychic powers. These systems add linear depth to previously simple abilities without making the base abilities weak or the fully upgraded varieties too strong.The depth of these powers as well as other improvements play an important part in the much improved combat from the previous game, which was the weakest element. The biggest improvement to the combat is by far the enemy variety. Rather than having just censors populating every mind in addition to level-specific enemies, there are now 7 more consistent enemy types with their own weaknesses. This further elevates the upgrade system by allowing players to make reliable decisions in regards to making certain enemies easier to deal with. Changes to Raz's abilities also make combat more engaging, such as the addition of dodge attacks and making the PSI Blast on a sectioned cooldown instead of using ammunition. The addition of new powers also helps give the game its own identity separate from the first. The controls for PC also feel much more streamlined than the original game.Excellent level design and pacing make the game a joy to adventure through and explore. Every area of the game oozes style, personality, and care, while maintaining unique challenges and visuals that keep things fresh. There was almost never a moment that felt like it dragged on or was too confusing. Every mind and area outside felt memorable, and made me intrigued to keep looking for nooks and crannies I had yet to see even without collectibles to incentivize me.Part of this interest in discovering all of the level is due to the interesting character designs and interactions with said characters. This applies more-so towards the main world than the minds, but there are well-written and humorous characters in them as well. There are many optional conversations Raz can have that world-build and are just entertaining to listen to. Some conversations also give Raz side quests to further incentivize world exploration.The writing of the game's main story is an excellent expansion of the first game's loose ends and mysteries. Just about every major character from the first game makes a return, and maintains their defining attributes. New characters are introduced when necessary to create new plot developments and dynamics between characters, and while they have a minutely different style than the original cast they are just as well-written. The Psychic Six are a good example of introducing new major characters without sidelining the original ones.Every moment and area of the game has an excellent soundtrack backing it up, composed by Peter McConnell. The music reflects every situation perfectly and greatly helps players feel immersed in the emotions of the story and the environments. The sound design is also top-notch, with every important sound being recognizable and identifiable to the player for good flow, all while sounding good on top.Psychonauts 2 is just as good, if not better than the first game. It improves upon aspects such as platforming precision and combat depth while maintaining the personality of the quirky psychological collectathon the original set out to be. Psychonauts 2 is the perfect example of what a sequel should be.

Going in to fix the mental disorders of the many people around him along with his crew of other 'friends' in this incredible 3D Platformer with its bringing back much of what used to be time when 3D Platformers much like its prior title was released in right at it's tail-end of a constant rush of titles much like it. _childDocuments_.review: Tim Schafer, and his crew over at Double Fine have made one of the best sequel games I've played in a long time. Broken Age really put a bitter taste in most fan's mouths, but this game is so sweet. I really enjoyed this game, but I won't exclude my critiques. It's been about sixteen years since the last full fledged Psychonauts title has been released. There are a couple blatant cracks at that, and by the second time it got old.As for graphics, there is quite a variety of settings Raz traverses. The rendered environments were beautiful and left me wanting to explore more. All are quite vibrant and nostalgic notes of the prior games hold throughout its style. Although I wish there was more variety to Raz's outfits while in levels. The visuals have gotten a huge upgrade, but there was something I missed. The faces in the sky. The ones that the clouds formed to be exact. I may be just overlooking them, but I never saw them. They were so perfect for the game's tone when the player notices them.I should mention at this point I 100% completed this game at around 60 Hours. I genuinely believe that this game feels short. I can almost overlook it, but there is really nothing to do in terms of endgame. It is very linear, but has a very open feel to its play-style. Going back to previous levels is easy, but some objectives are unrepeatable. Those are ways to lose out on collecting some figments. Some Psy Challenge markers require some really skillful jumps. Specifically the one in the main Atrium. This was the last item I collected in the game.There was some hate with the LGBTQ+ cast characters in some Steam reviews. The story in the game was genuinely organic, and it's nice to see a studio getting with the times. Their implementation of the story arcs are as genuine as any other video game.To end this succinct review, Psychonauts 2 was well polished and ran beautifully. A very refreshing game in a year with many disappointing releases. Definitely get this game on whatever sale comes your way, because $60 seems like "a fan of the series" kind of price.

_childDocuments_.review: Psychonauts 1 and 2 are games that are very special to me. This one went above and beyond to deliver a fantastic sequel that felt so fresh and so familiar at the same time.For returning players, this game remains faithful to what you experienced before with the original characters being just the same as they were before. And you're actually not set back too much as far as your powers go. Most of what you had in the previous game are granted to you very quickly in this one.For the new players, you get caught up to speed pretty quickly in a fun and entertaining catch-up video. Though I will admit when I first played Psychonauts 1, plenty of concepts went over my head and it took a little while for me to get the hang of this strange world.Now this is for ALL types of players. This game has many important things it wants to teach you about loss, healing, and mental health in general. It illustrates so many ideas in brilliant ways that make them thought provoking concepts. I think this game has many subtleties that deserve to be recognized as the profound ideas they are. Throughout the whole game though, I was invested in the mystery and the adventure. I was caught off guard by twists and I laughed the whole time.For the completionists out there, this game is actually very easy to get 100% achievements for. Even some of the grinding ones took only a few minutes with the right upgrades (pins in the Otto-Shop). There are no ridiculous challenges that would take hours of practice and grinding and [NOT REALLY A SPOILER BUT IF YOU WANT TO BE SURPRISED AT THE END OF THE MAIN GAME] I personally am looking forward to what will happen in about 2 months. Cause I know for a fact that I am going to start a new save then, just to experience the whole game again. It's that good.The only other thing that I can say is: This game should've actually won more awards instead of just being nominated for them.

_childDocuments_.review: As a long awaited sequel many were concerned we might not get; without a doubt Psychoanuts 2 is further proof how good a concept the first game was and how much more interesting the series can get if it is allowed to keep going. The worlds continue to impress with more interesting puzzles and better use of your psychic powers, more charming characters are introduced as well as bringing back plenty old ones. _childDocuments_.review: I'm about 36 hrs into the game and nearing the end, so I'll prob need to update my review later. But holy smokes, what a ride it's been so far. I'm astounded by the psychadelic visuals, heartfelt writing, and the humor of this game. I adore its world and characters, and the beautiful perspectives it presents on life, mental health, and human relationships.The stories behind each mission truly touched me, causing me to reflect on my own life and some of my own mental health struggles. There are some heavy topics tackled in this game, each approached respectfully IMO. While I think the writers did a great job of balancing out the tragic/sad with more lighthearted moments, there were times where darker scenarios could weigh me down emotionally. So I'd advise to sensitive souls: if you start to feel depressed or anxious while playing Psychonauts 2, take frequent breaks! Go to a different room, relax for a bit, or find a quick distraction before picking the controller back up again. Your mind will thank you later!Gameplay-wise, I feel like the platforming and controls are incredibly fun and intuitive. And even when I felt stuck or like I'd forgotten how to solve some environment puzzle, there was usually some conveniently-timed reminder to set me on the right path. I've been having a blast with my PSI powers and exploring every nook and cranny of the game. The environments are gorgeously detailed, and I get a kick out of all the NPC dialogue.On a personal note, the story of Psychonauts 2 has made me want to try harder to keep up with loved ones, especially in the face of a worldwide pandemic. I feel like the stress, absence of communication, and distance I've spent away from friends and family is causing the erosion and breakdown of relationships I once held dear. Like some of the game's more broken characters, I feel I've become somewhat despondent and disconnected from others. And though part of me is filled with regret, guilt, and shame for letting these relationships atrophy, this game has taught me that it's ok to feel these things! If someone is important to you, you should do what you can do make them feel appreciated and loved--even through small acts of kindness. It's never too late to show that you care.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: It's really good and it's exactly what I wanted as a longtime Psychonauts fan. As proof... it's been out only a week and I already spent 30 hours playing to 100% the game. This game is the first game in a long time that I can say is completely worth buying at full price.It's more of that Psychonauts platforming goodness with a few extra mechanics/psi powers thrown in the mix to add a little more variety. For completionists, the collectathon gameplay is still there. With hundreds of figments to collect, mind vaults to punch open, emotional baggage to sort, and nuggets of wisdom to find... there's plenty to keep you occupied for a good chunk of your time. The platforming feels nice and Raz controls really well.This is where the game really shines... just like the first one. As fans of the original know, the levels themselves give you insight to various characters because of the premise of the games (You are diving into various character's minds and the levels themselves are a representation of that character's mental state). There are a lot of really great levels here and while the first game probably had some of the wackiest levels out of all the games, I would say that a lot more of the levels in this game come to a heartfelt conclusion on various characters. If you are looking for trippy levels that play with the laws of gravity, physics, etc. this game has that in spades. I can't really go more in detail without spoiling anything, but if you liked the levels in the first game, you will like them in this game.Wow! Everything about the world is expanded on! We meet new characters. We get to see Psychonauts headquarters. We see more of Raz's family. We get to see the origins of the Psychonauts organization. And more! And it's all a really well told story too! While I liked the story of the first game a lot... this one took it up a few notches! They really spent a lot of time on trying to convey why characters were the way they were and the way they dealt with revealing this information always felt sincere and heartfelt (sorry if I am using that word too much). Every story character was treated with respect by the developers and no one was really "the bad guy". Everyone had reasons for why they did what they did and the developers really tried to make you understand how that character came to believe what they believed or do what they did. Like it states at the beginning when you start up, the entire game is about empathy and thus understanding others and their own motivations is a big part of the story. And the developers also tried (and I think succeeded) in clarifying that Psychonauts is not about "fixing" people but about helping people address their own personal demons. All in all, the unique premise of Psychonauts allows for some really interesting stories to be told and the writers took full advantage of that!It is very stylized and faithful to the original. They stylized art helped make sure that the original still looked pretty good even after all these years... and this game is just that but with an upgrade.

_childDocuments_.review: THIS IS GAME CHANGING MIND BLOWING GOOFY GOODNESS!In 2020 I was introduced to Psychonauts (2005) and although the graphics were a bit old, it was the most refreshing game I had ever played. The character models were ridiculous, and the concept- what sort of mad brain does it take to envision such a bizarre world? Yet through all its absurdity, I felt it portrayed mental health struggles in a really endearing and validating way. Everything about Psychonauts was novel and my only disappointment was that I would never be able to experience another game like it. Then out of no where I heard Psychonauts 2 was being released! I’m happy to announce Psychonauts 2 is just as quirky and fun as its predecessor. It stays true to itself while expanding upon the world and introducing some QOL improvements to the original.

_childDocuments_.review: Psychonauts 2 takes place directly after the ending of Rhombus of Ruin, a sadly VR-only game that takes place also directly after the first game. So despite the 16-year gap the games only take place between the span of a few days. In this game, Raz is finally able to join the Psychonauts as an intern, and after his supposed mentor turned up brainless, he investigates a possible case of having a mole. It is pretty similar in tone and atmosphere with the first game, but not too similar, just familiar enough to be good and nostalgic as well as adding unique touches.Gameplay is pretty much the same, an open-world platformer with several levels that takes place inside some character's minds. Unlike the first game, there is postgame free roam, allowing you to wrap up collectibles and sidequests as well as having new dialogue. There seem to be several point-of-no-return warnings, but none of these are permanent, just some areas you cannot return to before you complete the story. In fact, some collectibles can only be acquired during postgame because you need an ability that you get very late.The mental worlds are also pretty well-designed, each having a unique theme and aesthetic fitting the character whose mind we dive into. Some examples include a hospital-casino, a psychedelic music festival, and a historic amusement park ride. But most of these levels are linear platformer/combat ones, the more puzzle-centric levels such as the theater and suspicious neighborhood in the first game don't exist. Instead, we have quite many, perhaps a bit too many, ball-rolling segments. Whether its an upgrade or downgrade depends on you, but the neighborhood is one of my favorite levels.As you would expect, there are also some changes in the game's mechanics. While most powers return, there are some new powers, like creating a mental projection, but some powers don't return such as invisibility. One I really miss is the ability to use bacon to ask Ford Cruller for helpful hints, here you can only rely on Raz talking to himself if you take too long, or other characters if they say something. Collectibles are also easier to find, as there's a checklist if you collected everything there as well as adding a photomode filter that reveals every collectible once you finish the game.Overall, Psychonauts 2 is a really great game, just as great, if not better than the first game. It also explores several events and characters mentioned only in previous titles, like the Psychic Six and Raz's family. A proper continuation of a good game, retaining all the great aspects while adding some more and making it in HD graphics. If you liked the first game, you'll definitely like this one as well due to the similarities it has, while still being fresh enough to not be boring.

_childDocuments_.review: +++++ : Levels or "brains" are what puts Psychonauts apart from other platformers. Always visually interesting and always goes deeper than it looks. Allowing experimentation, combinations and requiring dodges.++ : Also known as "Pins". Not many of them useful when you have 3 slots but some of them can change the game. I am especially fond of "Glass Cannon" Pin.+ : Developers did everything they could to make the experience smooth as possible. For example in Psychonauts 1 when you missed an easily missable "figment" of /300, you had to replay the whole level and your best bet was to watch a "All Figments Walkthrough" 1:1. Now, you can skip to points in a level and also the camera highlights the missed figments. This time the game gave more emphasis to character developments and the conflict in our own minds and addresses some sensitive mental health issues which were really refreshing to see!Praises aside the game felt it could have expanded and explored more with the story-line and there are too many new characters who quickly go into the background without too much emphasis to the story. _childDocuments_.review: I've never reviewed a game on Steam before, but Psychonauts 2 is the sort of experience so fantastic that I genuinely wish I could forget it all and play it for the first time. If you're a fan of the original game, rest assured that this sequel is likely everything you hoped for and then some. The levels here are insanely creative - all visually and thematically distinct from one another and delightful to explore. The controls in the first Psychonauts could be mildly janky at times, but that's been ironed out here and it's a lot of fun to move around. The story and characters have a surprising amount of depth and I was surprised at how emotionally invested I was in how things would turn out. If I had any minor nitpicks I'd say that while the enemy designs and weaknesses were conceptually neat, the basic combat encounters aren't quite as impressive as the rest of the game, and a lot of those encounters are easy enough to get through by moving around and spamming attacks, so I didn't make much general use of the pins you could buy. Even then I can't say this is something that really bothered me. Overall, the world of Psychonauts -from its humor and passing conversations to its art direction - is vibrant and memorable, and when the credits rolled I still didn't want to leave it behind.

_childDocuments_.review: This one was a long time (5 years since the crowdfunding campaign in 2016, 16 years since the first Psychonauts) coming, and the wait has absolutely been worthwhile. Double Fine have taken the gameplay of the original Psychonauts (Story-heavy 3rd-person adventure 3D platforming) along with its charming characters and wonderfully colorful, surreal, and cartooney art design and brought the experience out of the 00's, into the '20s, and for the better. The control scheme and feel of Raz's movement in the first game was a pain point for a lot of players, since his movement could feel at alternate times too loose and too sluggish. That complaint gains less foothold here; the movement scheme has been honed to be more fluid but retain much of its feel from the original. Complaints about infrequent punishing platforming sections in the original (merited, to be sure) and frustration with extended collect-a-thon patterns have also been addressed.Psychonauts 2's story feels like a step forward as well -- 2005's release had excellent theming around persevering through and overcoming individual trauma to be healthier and more whole as an individual, while this outing focuses more on community/friendship/family and being accepting and caring as support for mental well-being, and it feels much more cheerful and encouraging for that slight shift of emphasis.Double Fine have outdone their first release, and without diminishing the original's appeal. Yes, 2 is a mechanical and (arguably) thematic improvement but the original had so much charm that the small improvements here feel like they are hardly changes at all. This makes me want to invent a new term for simultaneous experience of nostalgia and novelty just to put a term to what it evokes.

Through out that time many people would discover the gem that was and still is Psychonauts.Over the course of 2 weeks I not only played the game from start to finish but also 100% the game, all with in a play time of a little under 2 days.When this sequel was announced about 5 years ago, I was instantly hyped for it like many were. Unfortunately a lot happened in that time. Many games were announced, came out, and were just one disappointment after another. Game companies bumbling into any number of scandals ranging from intentionally shipping bad games, intentionally shipping incomplete games, or intentionally violating the rights and sense of safety of developers.It was easy to grow bitter and distrusting of any upcoming video game and the people that made/published them for that whole time. Even when game play of Psychonauts 2 was shown off, I still had my doubts about it.To say the least, it is truly a breath of fresh air to have in my possession a game that honestly feels like the people worked on it actually cared about it as much as I did. I honestly can't be happier about this.Sappy stuff done and out of the way, what's my review?Pros:1. It's Psychonauts through and through. If that is what you expect to get when you buy this game, that's what you will exactly get.2. Game play is tight across the board. You'll find it hard to point out moments in the game that you feel like you have no control over Raz.3. Fun every step of the way.4. Funny, even when it gets too cheesy you can't help but laugh.5. A true collect-a-thon done right.Cons:1. Steam version is a bit buggy. You'll find a few issues as you play but all of them sort themselves out in the end. One in particular though quite literally sort itself out but the end of the game for me to finally go back and finish that one level.2. Easy to sequence break in a few places. It's not too bad but it did throw me off when Raz said something that I didn't know anything about until I made my way to where he was supposed to go first to learn that information.That's about it. This was an amazing ride and a satisfying ending to a long waiting part of my child hood. Hope you all find the same satisfaction in your own ways.-Gently

_childDocuments_.review: Haven't beaten the game yet, but I'm at the point of no return and it lives up to the creativity and fun of the first game. A tall order to fill for sure, but this game does that and then some. Feels like the first game with a lot of good balancing and improvements, but leaves room for replay. Each character has a fun schtick and is fun to talk to. I don't usually exhaust all dialogue NPCs, but in this game I absolutely did and enjoyed almost every minute of it. The level design is creative and connects to it's theme and character it's attached to VERY well, while also having fun challenges. It's challenging, but fair, the ques to find collectibles and guide you along the right path are there, but not shoved in your face hard. Music is also nostalgic as all hell as it borrows themes and motifs from the previous game, but the change of feel and instrumentation to distinguish setting was well done. Haven't even finished the game yet, but I can't wait to see the ending and how it all wraps up. Hopefully it's not as hard as the Meat CircusEDIT: Just got to rank 102 and the game continued being just as fun through 100% completion. The last figments are tedious to find though
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: I backed this game back in 2015 (wow it's been 6 years). Just got finished getting 100% and wow what a ride indeed. A perfect follow up to the original game. There are certain things that I do miss from the first game like the infinite glide and bouncier psi-float, but the game was designed around the newer physics so it isn't a huge problem. They found uses for a lot of the abilities that I felt were underdeveloped in the first game. Just an amazing game that took 6 years to make and didn't end up being broken on launch. Hats off to all the fine people at Double Fine.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: New Review: This game is truly one of the best platforming games I have ever played. It has the same charm and feel of the original game and just expands on it. I played the entire time without feeling bored or like the game was getting monotonous. There are so many ways to use your powers and go through fights with different combos and strategies, as well as using your powers to solve many puzzles that leave you thinking.Pyschonauts 2 is easily my GOTY 2021. It has beautiful graphics, very fun and fast paced gameplay, great level design, interesting and likable characters, fantastic story, and made it easy to relate to parts of the story.If you are looking for a new platformer, it won't let you down. If you are looking for an enticing story, you'll be hooked fast. I myself have suffered through my own tragedies and the way this game handles mental illness, regret, and doubts and other feelings really hits home and left me with a very wholesome experience.Early game: Wow this is very entertaining. Starting after the story of 1 and the VR experience Rhombus of Ruin (which I have not played), Psychonauts 2 jumps right in without skipping a beat. It feels like a sequel game in true fashion, and has the exact same feel that the original did for me. It's really neat to see the original cast and personalities are back along with the powers and gameplay of the first. Just about 2 hours in and I am thoroughly enjoying the game. The level design is already fun and trippy. I can't wait to play more and discover what else this game has to offer
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: It's Psychonauts, but more. The original still mostly holds up after all these years, and now we have this one too.If you're not familiar with the original, bummer. This takes place like, 2 days after the first game, after returning to base from a mission. It's probably not impossible to get into if this is your first with the series, but it's going to make some of the surreal elements even more surreal. I really recommend starting with the original.It's some crazy-good writing, incredible level design with multiple aesthetics, solid platforming, combat, exploration and... "puzzles". I use quotes because the protagonist will prompt you with what you should be doing, because it won't be obvious the first time you run into a thing.Worst I've faced is a camera in a cramped combat arena not letting me see a symbol over the enemy's head. And the best... ah, that'd be spoilers.

_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: This is probably one of the most fun and new experiences I have made in the last 10 years. After playing the first game in the series, I was intrigued how the second one would improve the formula.I was not ready for a game that one-upped the previous one in every single category.Granted, it is probably a bit hard to get into the game at first, especially due to its design, characters and things that just feel off, but once you are in the world, it all makes sense somehow. You care for the people, you want to help them and you want to know their history.The different levels and abilities all work together really nicely and promote exploration. Whatever mind you explore, it will be different than the one before and every one will feel unique and cool.I am not sure, whether there is anything I could complain about in this game apart from me wanting more of this, but that's a compliment, I guess!Play it.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: DoubleFine doesn't disappoint. They are truly masters at creating living, breathing characters and unique settings that totally immerse you into the game. The story is well written and woven seamlessly  into the level design. Be prepared to be bombarded with the artistic diversity spread across the game levels. Don't let the simplistic/childish design aesthetic fool you, it is in direct contrast to the darker aspects of human psyche that the game deals with such as loneliness, abandonment, regret, shame, and guilt. The gameplay is possibly the weakest element in that it is fairly rudimentary for an action-platformer, Towards the end it clearly takes a backseat to the narrative experience. Music and voice-acting is excellent throughout. Not recommended for play on keyboard/mouse - Use a controller. No bugs at all the entire play through. Personal rating: 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: If you haven't played the first Psychonauts, start there. The storytelling in this series is amazing and is worth playing in order. _childDocuments_.review: After a long struggle with tooooo many cut scenes, especially in the beginning, I am starting to enjoy this game ... somewhere half way through or near the end ...Also: 🇺🇦 Slava Ukraini 🇺🇦==================================================My old review:"I mean, you can't lose forever, right?"Yes, you can. Because Psychonauts 2 is 99% cut scenes, 1% game play.In some places, there are consecutive sequences with a few seconds (!) of game play, followed by a long cut scene, a few seconds of game play, a long cut scene, a few seconds ...Other places, after a loooong cut scene, you walk a few steps, only to trigger yet anther cut scene.Heck, they even replaced literal jump and run sequences with cut scenes! The cut scenes are jumping and running for you. Degrading the player to a spectator.Sure, the game gets (much) better after the first few hours of play time (not game play!). I loved the Psi King Levels. But the cut scene madness just never ends. We do get to experience a moving story. Although the game often feels like an interactive movie instead of a game.

_childDocuments_.review: Psychonauts 2 is a great game, and a good sequel to Psychonauts. While the graphics and gameplay have been updated, (the game looks great), it retains the uniquely odd art style of the first game. The story continues from "Psychonauts in the Rhombus of Ruin", a short VR game set between the first game and this one. A short comic-book style introduction recaps the story so far, and Psychonauts 2 drops you straight back into the adventure. There is really no need to have played the first game prior to this one, but I think it does hold up well and is worth playing as well. I think the first game did better in two areas, firstly the "mindscapes" that form the platforming levels in the first game were less censored in terms of mental illness, and I think dealt with the issue better because of it. In Psychonauts 2, the mindscapes are beautiful and fun, but I think fear of being accused of not taking mental illness seriously has reduced the creativity of the scenarios slightly. The second area is that the platforming feels a little more random than the first game, sometimes multiple attempts at a jump will produce different results, so it can be easy to think something isn't possible, when it is. Although I'm not very good at this type of game, I was able to complete it without much difficulty, and for anyone worse than me, it has a few options to make things easier, (switching off fall damage and such), and combat difficulty can be increased or reduced.

_childDocuments_.review: 9/10There are VERY few games that exist in the same realm as Psychonauts does. In fact, the only game I can think of is A HAT IN TIME. It has a good amount of platforming without the intense acrobatics of Mario. It has a very thick story with great characters without the muddled mess of Kingdom Hearts. It.. has... atmosphere.The combination of music, open exploration, unlock-able secrets, skills, and story driven by mystery gives the entire game this overcoat of intrigue that keeps me hanging on. I don't know how to describe it besides that feeling you get when you are in a game and you discover the "backdoor" at "night" to the places you've seen a million times. About to find out some secret that has been hidden from you. I have a few issues. I wish I could have seen more of that backdoor at night feeling. There are plenty of points where that could have been implemented but instead they stuck with the psychological development for characters or more platforming. I think more of that was present in the first Psychonauts. One of the most disappointing areas was the Cassio Pia (book) level. This was the least developed character that also had an unclear mental condition, only made worse by the strange bootlegged backstory, and the worst voice actor. I heard a young woman reading lines and not acting, and a terrible old person timbre. Otherwise the visuals are AMAZING, the gameplay smooth, and the script and acting superb.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: This is a perfect sequel, keeping what made the first game great while adding on to it. Kept flickering in and out, but not so much that the area was unplayable.The other being the Raz's face polygons's colours breaking. But simply shutting the game down and re-opening it fixed it.Over all great game, 10/10!

This one is perfect so far, has all the humor of the first, but way more expansive in every category of gameplay.  The animation style is Disney/Monsters Inc in quality but with its own quirkiness that makes me want to explore every nook and cranny.  10/10

_childDocuments_.review: The first half of the game felt almost perfect. But then:OMG! Really?! Another "make 3 things" mission inside the same kind of one?OMG! Really?! You tell the answer to the puzzle after 10 seconds of trying to solve it?OMG! Really?! Why did he do that? It doesn't make sense!OMG! Really?! He just stays and sees?OMG! Really?! Do I just need to fight with someone who frightens the most powerful psychonauts?OMG! Really?! Are they all promoted? But they did almost nothing!Well, this game is a big disappointment to me.
