_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: This was EXACTLY what I wanted in a Psychonauts sequel after all this time. I played and beat the first game way back on the original XBox and have since purchased it a few more times on several other platforms, just to keep reliving that experience which I found again in Psychonauts 2. The story and comedy is on point and just as silly. I absolutely loved the references to the first game because they felt well timed in game and didn't hit you over the head just for the sake of being there. All of Raz's PSI powers and move set feel polished and ready to take on the various new enemies that pop up and new environments to explore which are just as brilliant and rich to explore as the first game. I tried hard to not rush through this, but I just could not put it down. I wanted to find every last figment, unlock all upgrades, hear all the dialog I could find. No spoilers but, the Archetype has to be my favorite new ability due to the functionality AND the voice for it (which I sat and talked to for some time after I got it, before I continued playing the game), SO GOOD! After 36 hours and all achievements unlocked, my only complaint is that it's over. Hoping there will be some DLC and in that maybe there will be more Psychoseisometer challenges, but not holding my breath. Either way, this is gonna be one of those games that'll show up remastered on the PS7 years from now, and I'll buy it just because. Thanks Tim and Double Fine for another masterpiece.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly this is one of my favorite games to date. I never really felt like I was bored during the story nor thought the combat was too easy or too hard. Me and my friends honestly had such a fun time with this game as I played through it. These characters are just so interesting both in and out of their minds. I couldn't recommend this game enough for those who want a fun and interesting story told in a weird and creative way. I can't wait to 100% the game fully. not there yet though I'm on my way.The only problem I've had was more so a technical one; that being my game crashed every so often though that may just be my pc. I'm staying just as a heads up though.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: A absolutely fantastic game to play! It could have been a little harder at times but I really enjoyed this game the same as I did the first one all those years ago. Usually I aim to try get 1 hour per 1€ for what the game costs but this game was well wourth the full price tag for me!If you liked the first Psychonauts game or any other platformers then this game is definitely for you!
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: DoubleFine signature wholesome humour is present but it is not as prevalent. The whole story structure, writing and issues presented are much more generalised and feel kind of directionless. Apparently, recognising the problem magically resolves it.Psychonauts are not precision platformers. Wouldn't that offer some leeway in terms of exploration and freedom?ㅤI don't know how true that is. Seeing Raz bumping into thin air, unable to jump around or over to a thing he wants to see or pick up in a literal arms reach.I loved the inertia in the first game. It still feels nice here but is limited. You won't be able to gain enough traction to catapult around large platforming chunks. ㅤUnfortunately, this concept wouldn't even be able to take advantage of the crammed, corridor or spiralling design of P2.P2 is much more streamlined overall, supposedly less jank. Yet somehow not as fun.The 'real' world was the highlight for me in the first game as well but P1 also had some memorable brains too.ㅤP2 level design is by enlarge unremarkable and a chore to get through.It started out with me thinking I'd 100% the game for sure. Growing tired of it around half-way through, just like the first game. Difference being, Psychonauts was worth it in the end and has had me thinking of it every now and then throughout the years. 2 caused me to go Psychonuts. Outside of a few interactions and Questionable Area world hub, it'll fade in memory.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing platform game for adults. Environmental storytelling at its peak, full of charm wherever you look at.Dialogs straight out of Lucas Arts' best titles. And the subtle yet on point referenzes to human psyche make you wonder if they actually hired professional psychologists in the making of this game.Fully recomended.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: Psychonauts 2 took what worked in the first and made it better astronomically. Its much more clear what your supposed to be doing at any moment without feeling handholdy. The collectibles are not used to collect items that make it possible to do levels in the first place. All of the sets are amazingly well designed and the story is even elevated further here. And the movement is so much more polished and serviceable. it isn't something to go writing home about but the improvement in combat is. The sheer difference in how combat works in this game is amazing. I recommend this game wholeheartedly as I still believe both of these games have one of the best stories in media today.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start by saying this game delivered on everything I hoped it would, I'm honestly sad it ended and that there isn't much more after the credits rolled. And while I did run into some issues here and there, these are mere nitpicks in a largely extremely polished experience.The game takes me back to a collect-a-thon mindset that I had missed for so long. I played the first Psychonauts fairly recently and loved it despite the faults it had, of which most were a byproduct of the time/zeitgeist the game came out in. And when you drop into the sequel it really feels like not much has changed between the characters, both narratively and visually. And don't get that sentence wrong, the game looks absolutely stunning in UE4. They just translated the artstyle so well (and improved a lot of it's aspects, like animation) into the "next-gen" space. I also need to add that the music and voicework is once again top-notch, with lots of returning roles which really helps move the experience forward that much more. It takes me back to the cartoons I used to watch during the early and mid 2000's.My only real issues with the game were me getting stuck between bits of scenery about 2-3 times (particularly in the beginning, the casino levels) which forced me to restart a checkpoint. The fact figments were hard to keep track of (returning issue of the first game). And I found the (SPOILER ALERT maybe) final boss, while well presented and told, a bit of a pushover. But the game makes up for it with some extra bits that help bring closure to the whole thing, so it's easy to forget.A must-play for fans and newcomers alike. I'm really hoping they get to do that remake of the first game they were spitballing around in several interviews. I think it deserves a proper makeover.9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: Positively fun gameplay! Fans of the first Psychonauts game will feel right at home, but the control scheme has greatly been streamlined. If I'm not mistaken, the original cast have all reprised their previous rules. Certainly, some attacks should be better telegraphed and there are times when the difficulty sometimes spikes suddenly, but it's never been enough to dissuade me from enjoying the game to its fullest.As for visuals, it's pure eye candy. The unconventional art style for the characters may take some getting used to for new players, but I bet that you'll be won over quite handily by each character's charm.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: A really great sequel to an awesome game. There a couple of references to the VR title in this series early in the game which I had to search to know what they were talking about, but generally they were just mentions, and not details, which is great for me who has no VR setuppros:- really solid gameplay- story is rich- large open-ish world and- easy enough to try for a 100% completion after finishing the storycons:- the price is a touch steep, but the game is getting discounts on certain sales now so if you're not willing to pay full price just wait for one of those- platforming can be a bit weird, where I got to places a way I don't think the developers intended- no milk man
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing game for sure, just as good if not better than the first with a story that at least personally hit quite a few chords.  The gameplay is tight with no level feeling repetitive to any other, most obstacles are challenging without being overwhelming.  I never felt like I was simply handed a win but never died once, but even if that's too much their is an immortality mode in case you're a game journalist.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing game through and through, and almost certainly my game of the year. In most games the levels are like “the dark cave” or “the erupting volcano”. In P2 they’re like “let’s splice someone’s gambling addiction into the anxiety of their medical career” - and I’m not talking about cut scenes - the level is a physical manifestation of their storyline!It’s also not a one trick pony… each level is just as creative as the last and it’s just a series of slam dunks until it ends. Amazing.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: This game... is good, I do not think it is better than Psychonauts 1 but I still like it. At sometimes it feel like its being drawn out for no reason but you won't notice half the time because the amount of character and personality in this game. Some of the people's mind give you some deep messages and also try and teach you things as well. My only real complaint is that the Milk Man didn't return (nor did the other asylum patience). I would recommend to anyone because I feel like any one would love this series.8/10 Would think again.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: was good. not as good as the first one. it felt so... empty and short. it felt less like psychonauts 2 and more like psychonauts 1.5. theres so little to do, nowhere near as much content as the first game. to me it just didnt have the same... depth as the first one. felt more streamlined for mainstream audiences. the brain worlds felt so much less open and so much more restricted and linear. i wish there was more "game" to the game, even if it was just padding. the graphics are great but it just didnt feel like a true sequal to me.i sincerely hope this game gets some major dlc. it left me thinking: "that was the whole game? theres no more collectibles, no more side areas, no more physical world areas?" i think if the game had more openness, and had more areas and depth, it could go a really far way. it feels like it was a "safe sequal" in that it didnt really try many new things, didnt add much to the formula, didnt take any risks to try anything majorly new. it was great to see, and great to play, but it just felt too... safe. a lot of the darker humor and charm from the original is missing. it feel slike the kind of sequal that would have been made a few years after the original, not 15 years later if that makes sense. the graphics are like next gen though.tl;dr: wish it had more to do and took more risks, still decent though, for whats there.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute masterpiece. I fully expected this game to disappoint me. I didn't exactly expect it to be bad, but Psychonauts 1 is one of my top 5 favorite games of all time. How can any game live up to such lofty expectations? Well, someone Double Fine did it. I only hope this isn't the end of the series. I would LOVE a part 3.Edit: Well, I beat the game and 100%ed it. I'll say it again. What a masterpiece. Just buy it. The level of creativity here is astounding. Every corner of this game has a story to tell. It's games like this that make me love gaming. The only fault is that it's not long enough, but honestly, being this good, I don't know that it ever could have been. I could have played this one for a hundred hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: This is a faithful, impressive and beautiful continuation of a beloved cult classic. It expands upon existing characters and lore while keeping, and even improving, the core aspects that made the first game so good. The stylised design is a treat for the eyes and the writing is a delightful homage to the older generation of games. I highly recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: Power Of Whale!It's a 3rd person adventure and collection game. You level up and become more awesome as you find stuff so exploration is rewarded. And, the humor is on point!+ Works perfectly with 21:9 super-wide screen.+ Awesome graphics in a familiar style.+ Bizarre puzzles in complex environments... Or is that the other way around?+ Fantastic writing and voice acting.+ Bigger, better and more grandiose in every way than Psychonauts 1.+ Unlimited Power! Gotta find it all!- Combat can be a bit awkward, but it's also not the main loop.- Healing items have to be bought.It's totally worth it! It was a joy to play and shows both old-fashioned design and modern conveniences.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: Great game! It manages to simultaneously feel like it's been 20 years and just a couple days since the first Psychonauts game. It also really feels like the people making the game have matured, while staying essentially the same. I had a little bit of PTSD reaction when the Aquato Family Circus music started up, but fortunately there is no equivalent to the meat circus level in this game! It deals with more mature issues than the first game, in a more mature way, but is still outrageously fun and weird. I'll definitely be replaying it regularly.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: Doublefine did it again! If you've never played a Tim Shafer game, this is a great one to start with. There is _very_ little I don't like about this game. Let me think.... sometimes the platforming is a little janky and takes a couple of tries, but nothing to really break the flow. Oh and there's some places where the signposting got me confused, but not enough to really annoy me.Other than that: Falling into pits cracks me up everytime, I can't unhear Invader Zim's typical voice screaming. The acting in this game is just GLORIOUS, a cinematics cut of this game would already be worth the time.Did you notice this game is WEIRD? Just when you thought it couldn't get any more outlandish, something stranger happens, but somehow it's all grounded in familiar themes and so recognizable at the same time.Anyway, what a fun game, I want to play it again, just buy it and have a good time. :D
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: Fun and charming sequel. I do have a handful of gripes with the story. Side character felt under utilised with no plot reasons to justify their absence which is disappointingA main character does something truly reprehensible and at most other characters just act like they're slightly upsetPolitical messaging that isn't pushed far enough to actually say anything.Still a good time.

_childDocuments_.review: 16 years of waiting for the long awaited sequel and it was definitly worth it! Still the same formula from the first game with more additions. The worlds and story were all interesting and breathtaking. I would definitely recommend the game to anyone, even pick up the first game if you get a chance, still holds up well today and more things in this game will make sense as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: It's not for everyone, but if you have the taste for a story oriented lite-platformer, lite-collectathon, it's very good. It was very fun seeing a PS2 game lifted right out of the early 2000's into modern day graphics. The story, characters and voice acting are all top notch. The gameplay could have been much better. Particular problem I've had with it was that you've got more abilities than what is assignable to the controller, so you're constantly pausing to re-assign new abilities that are needed to the shoulder buttons. That doesn't sound so bad if you've played Ratchet & Clank or something, but it doesn't feel ergonomic at all in practice. It made me wish some of the abilities were context sensitive and automated. Like, imagine if you played Ratchet & Clank and you had to manually select the slingshot every time instead of it automatically equipping when sling targets are near. At any rate, I recommend getting on a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: The first game, but without the bad parts! In other words, a masterpiece. People give away the term "Super Mario Galaxy 3" to any good 3d platformer, but THIS game deserves it. It actually uses non-planar gravity, like galaxy, and quite a few mechanics are similar to ones from Super Mario Galaxy. Sure, you don't go into space, but going into people's minds is also very interesting. The hub world feels like a theme park, with themed restaurants, learning centers, and bowling. There's a bunch of other locations you can go to outside of the Motherlobe, too, of course. And if you don't want to explore, you can use the fast travel. The Cosmic Observatory wishes it could be this cool to walk around in. The game looks beautiful, the humor is fantastic, the characters are great, the story is interesting, the gameplay is engaging and smooth. One of the best 3D platformers I've played in a while.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: I was so sure this was going to disappoint me, given my attachment to the original. It didn't. It keeps the quality writing, delightful characters, and the creative level design (it doesn't have a standout on the level of The Milkman Conspiracy, but that's just too high a bar to clear), and irons out a lot of the janky platforming.It is a bit easy, though.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible all around!Played  and beat the first Psychonauts game the day I bought it - had so much fun with the original game that I decided to pick this one up right afterwards. If you want to see if you'll enjoy this series, I'd recommend picking up the first - as you'll want to know what happened to understand some parts of this one.For Psychonauts 2, I cannot recommend this game enough!- Incredible art- Incredible level design- Lovely voice over work from all actors- Fun all-around enjoyable plot- Interesting characters that I felt invested in learning about- Entertaining game play - though overly easy at times, I was more invested in the story so it didn't really detract from this point much for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: A worthy continuation of the great game. So many years of waiting were worth it. After completing the game, I did not want to believe that this is the end, I want to play again and again. This game will make you return to it and go through it more than once (like the first game). All the levels are very cool, it's hard to choose the best one. I want to explore the locations in more detail. The characters are charming and attractive, as are their stories. The plot of the game is also great, at the end it is able to break through to a tear.This game deserves the Game of the Year award. (IMHO)
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: I played Psychonauts 2 to completion on Xbox (approximately 22 hours gametime) and am replaying it now on Steam. This game is incredible. I went back recently and replayed Psychonauts 1 and this is one of the rare occasions where the sequel is just as good or better than the original. I've had a strong urge for more PS2-like 3D platformers lately, and this game is a modern take on it. A lot of the mechanics from the original have been refined and the platforming overall has been tightened. The story, humor, and art design are fantastic. There are some snags: the controls for your powers can be a bit cumbersome as you sometimes need to manually switch them out and the boss fights are somewhat underwhelming. Some of the platforming sections can be occasionally confusing. But, that's all the negatives I can think of. This game gets everything else right. Not playing it should be a crime.Now all I need is a good Sly Cooper continuation...
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: This is not a real review, it's really just me gushing, an appreciation piece and not much more. Psychonauts 2 is easily my Quarter 1 & 2 game of the year. Very likely to be my game of the year overall. (At the very least I can't see it being beaten but I welcome any game that I enjoy as much as this one). I got into Psychonauts just two weeks before 2 released, I loved it. It oozed charm and character that I wished I'd experienced when I was younger. Still even in my 20's it's humor and charm didn't age poorly even after 16 years. So I was really happy when 2 released to jump right back in. It did not let me down. While I would have liked to see more of many of the characters this series has to offer, what was there was almost always charmingly funny, or eye-rollingly amusing. The game is full of the clever writing Double Fine is known for. Everything was enjoyable and often defied my expectations. I truly love this series- It holds such a strong identity and quality that I seldom see in games nowadays. It is not without it's flaws, but it's amazing design and writing make the few that are there easily forgivable. Loved Psychonauts and Psychonauts 2. I know Double Fine probably wants a break from the all the pressure of making such a long awaited sequel- and I look forward to their future titles- I just I hope to see another sequel to this series before I die. TLDR: Buy this game if you like 3D platformers it's better than most Mario entries. 8.9 psycho's / 10 nauts
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: If you haven't played Psychonauts 1 and are reading this review, just stop now and play that game first. At this point, EVERYONE should just play it, even if you're only slightly into platformers. It's funny, strange, laugh out loud funny, and a work of art unlike anything else. Psychonauts 2 is pretty much a direct sequel that delivers a great experience, but it's not the work of creative genius that the first one was. DEFINITELY play that game, and if you want more, then come back to get the sequel. Psychonauts 2 could be better, the gameplay hasn't really evolved at all and it isn't as imaginative as the first one, but it's still a great sequel.The story is great. We see much more the world of the Psychonauts, the real one, not just the summer camp, and we also see more of Raz's family and the mystery of their family curse. We learn more about Ford and how his mind shattered, and we see into the minds of more messed up people. I feel like Raz did a lot of growing up in this one.Unfortunately, a lot of the strangeness of the series has been toned down for this installment. Psychonauts 1 had a lot of iconic levels inside the minds of people around camp. And those levels weren't just interestingly themed, there were some real interesting mechanics in there as well. Of course, everyone knows about the infamous Milkman level, but I also loved the Waterloo level, where you were able to move between levels of abstraction on a board game. You could be on the board itself, moving tokens with telekinesis, head up and talk to the people playing the game, or go deeper and the board game became a living world and the game tokens people with problems to solve. A lot of the brains you entered had strange and fun mechanics like that, but in P2, you're pretty much just doing normal platformer things. Jumping to ledges, using a grappling hook-like power, grinding on rails, etc. The levels still have some interesting set dressing on display, and there is one standout level that comes close to the genius of P1, but otherwise it's pretty standard fare.The brain worlds are a little less strange and colorful. That might be a side effect of trying to make a more mature game that plays better for a 2021 audience. A man with a split personality who sometimes think's he's Napoleon in P1 was straight out of a book of cliches, and the people you encounter have more genuine mental woes. I think it's great that they're taking mental health a bit more seriously and respectfully, but I think they could have injected a bit more whimsy in there too. Nevertheless, I left each mind feeling pretty empathetic for the person I just met and felt like I really helped them.Mechanically speaking, the game plays about the same as P1, or maybe a bit worse. I know P1's platforming was a bit rough around the edges, and it seems like they didn't spend much time trying to fix it. It still works, but you'll be continually frustrated of things like changing your power loadouts on the fly because you don't have enough buttons for all the powers you need to explore AND fight, and there are some collectibles that you will really struggle to get, and not in a fun challenging way, but in a frustrating way. It's not a deal killer, but it lacks elegance, and that's kind of a big deal for a platformerI could nitpick and dissect this game all day, but the bottom line is I truly loved it and returning to the world of Psychonauts. As frustrating as I found it at times, I found myself trying to 100% the game, just because I wasn't prepared to leave it. The emotion the story kicks up makes up for the lack of gameplay refinement and while there's nothing quite as memetic as the Milkman Conspiracy, you will still frequently be left in awe of the worlds on display. The world of gaming is a little more colorful and special thanks to this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: Unconscionably good. This game feels like a dare to other games to step it up just by existing. Detailed, psychedelic world-design is married beautifully to a heartfelt and surprising story, all traversed through with some incredibly smooth 3D platforming. If you have any interest in the genre, play the first game and play this one too. Lightning, improbably, struck twice.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: So I played the first Psychonauts in 2012. I generally dislike platformers and am absolutely terrible at them, but it gained a spot in the list of games I periodically replay anyway. Yes, I have voluntarily subjected myself to Meat Circus several times, I love it that much. I say this in order to emphasize the following: Psychonauts 2 is everything I hoped and more. This game basically radiates joy. It is a precisely-engineered joke machine that dispenses humor and emotional sucker punches. I admit I was (briefly) disappointed that none of the memorable campers from the first game reappeared, but I got absolutely sucked into the story of the Psychic 6, and the Sensorium might be my favorite level in basically any game, ever. (Also, Sam. I adore Sam.)I will say that this feels different from the original, in one distinct way: the first game felt, fundamentally, like an adventure game, because a lot of its interactions were based on "use X on Y." As funny as I found it to use random items (tickling everyone with the crow feather, introducing Mr Pokeylope to the camp, showing literally everything to Crystal and Clem to see if they had new cheers), generally refining/streamlining narrative and character elements into more of a pure platformer makes for a much more cohesive experience overall. This isn't a complaint - far from it. The original game (and I say this with nothing but love for it) is a strange and often janky grab-bag of things. This game, for me, maintained much of the weirdness, that sense where you never knew what would happen next, and it does so in a context that feels much friendlier and more polished to actually play.I went in absolutely blind, knowing nothing about this game other than that reviewers I trusted thought it was great, so I'll limit my comments on the narrative to this: I loved the way it handles mental health, which reminded me of the best aspects of Gloria's Theater. Sometimes I use "dear universe, please shut up" as a weird little mantra when I'm stressed, but there isn't a single level I didn't adore. The balance of humor and compassion felt spot-on - sweet without being saccharine, funny without punching down.I wish I could forget it so I could experience it for the first time. But I know I'll be going back, and I look forward to seeing what I missed the first time through.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: This is EVERYTHING you want from a sequel. It expands upon the ideas of the first, beefs up the details, softens the edges, and keeps it just as fun as the first, if not more. The graphics and run smooth as honey and it suits the distinctive art style, the voice-acting is PHENOMENAL; as in SO consistent with the first game that it really does feel like a couple days instead of 10 years (plus Jack Black and Elijah Wood I mean come on), the gameplay is incredible to the point where the diversity of play allows you to breeze through the game quickly or take as much time as you want (combat included). The story itself is honestly beyond perfect in my eyes. They expanded the universe and its lore, whilst also expanding what we know about established characters, and it's all done in such a way that it's never overwhelming or jumping the shark. It's just.. Ough... Perfect is a strong word, and I get that, but I feel the writing and design of the script couldn't have been done better from an artistic standpoint.It's got COMBAT, it's got PLATFORMING, it's got COLLECTABLES, it's got STORY and LORE and INTERESTING CHARACTERS and an ESOTERIC ART DIRECTION.It's a good game and well, WELL worth your money in my opinion. <3
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: Everything about the first game is improved here. It looks and sounds GREAT, and the story's pretty interesting. While the new characters aren't super fleshed-out, and the story does get very jumbled up later on in the game, it's a great game to play, especially if you prefer gameplay to story (like me). I would recommend getting it on sale, though, and make sure your PC is above the proper minimum requirements before playing the game. Have fun! :)
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: Presentation (3.5/5) - visually creative settings for a game with creative world building and theme. Cartoony 3d style with some scattered 2d textures mixed in. Music is pedestrian, sound goes well with the graphics and also has character. The visualization of mental health concepts as enemies to fight is cleverly executed and rather amusing. Voice acting is good, sometimes overenthusiastic to a fault.Story/Dialogue (3/5) - Heavy on exposition at times and backstory briefly explained in still images. Story and dialogue resembles a merely above average children's cartoon with hit or miss humor that overemphasizes puns and gross gags. Story seems oddly paced because its progression centers around 'let's get into this person's mind'. Sometimes game does get into very dark territory though without matching visuals (let's have a crying pursetag while discussing death or alcoholism). While the story is likely great for most, I found myself disengaged and even checking my phone at times.Gameplay (3.5/5)  - A mix of adventure and platforming mechanics where you gain a larger number of skills as you progress that can be exploited in some platforming scenarios, These skills also have their uses in combat, excelling in specific circumstances. Boss fights are complex and require you to adapt to what is being thrown at you. The gameplay is in other words adaptable, if a bit easier than it should with no difficulty options for a bigger challenge. The gameplay suffers from having too many cutscenes, often interrupting the flow.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: The game is great visually and really pulls you in form the beginning. It's easy to play and has enough differences throughout to keep you entertained and prevents the game from being repetitive. The puzzles make you think but don't require that much brain power. What I really enjoy is the ease to find most of the items on your first play through so you don't have to spend hours searching for one little thing and miss out on gameplay or the story
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a sequel to an early 2000's cult classic -which you should absolutely play, it's like $5- and it has made improvements in every regard compared to the original.The story: not going to spoil anything, but to say that the writing is incredible would be an understatement. There are few moments in this game where the writing is anything short of stellar, and when you do see the points where the writing is not up to the highest standard that the rest of the game exudes, you will be given the contrast of great game versus best game ever. It's that good. Also, the ending isn't a mess like the first one and is actually a great conclusion to the story. Overall story grade IMO: 9.9/10, nearly perfect.Mechanics: This game has a lot of really fun abilities that will all be useful at multiple points in almost every level. The abilities are all really fun to use and feel mostly quite responsive and interesting... I rarely used only a few of them. The only one that feels anything short of incredible is the last one you get, but it's fine; it just doesn't feel as polished and well-integrated as compared to the other ones, but it is voice acted by the same voice actress that played Gir, so it technically makes this game an Invader Zim fan game, so it's alright I guess. Mechanically very good, an 8.7/10Visuals: The game is ugly. That is a good thing. The art direction of this game has many different ways that goes in and they were -no doubt- the most demanding part of the pipeline since they are all very, very, very well done and give the game cohesion despite the many different directions the art goes in. Every level's art style is unique and beautiful and it never feels like an afterthought; instead, it generally feels like the nexus around which the level is made. Art direction, 10/10. A masterpiece.Music/sound design: This game sounds great, the voice acting is all very well done, and each character is brought to life through their voice. The characters are highly expressive and funny and they all feel like someone that you could meet and have a long conversation with. The music is incredible and always very fitting for the mood of the story that is taking place. The sounds of the game are all very well put together and are just the right mix of unsettling, silly, and fun. 8/10.Now down to the brass tax. This game is incredible and I want more. If the developers do end up reading this, this is my suggestion to you guys.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: I really loved the original Psychonauts. I replayed the original prior to playing the sequel, fully aware that I may have been setting myself up for some huge disappointment. But this game fully lives up to the original! I love it so much, I wish it were 3x as long. I don't want to beat it! They put a lot of work into the story and level design, and it SHOWS.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the sequel I waited over a decade for. The first game was one of my favorite platformers when I found it, and when I had heard there was a sequel coming, I was READY. Now, when I had heard this game was coming, all I wanted was a follow-up to the cliffhanger from 1 (and Rhombus, after that came out). It could've played the same, and I would've been fine. HOWEVER, not only did the story surpass my expectations of what they could build off of from the world the first game created, the gameplay received so many major improvements. Each power was improved, and could be leveled up after unlocking. New features left and right, each of them incredibly useful and creative. Mental cobwebs were replaced with collectibles that were much more fun. And the devs are always listening to feedback, and that meant so much to see. Given the game's themes and the target demographic, it deserves that accessibility and attention to details and playerbase. This game blew me away, and while it will never replace the original, it certainly lived up to it.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: Psychonauts 2 is an amazing adventure from start to finish! I bought the original Psychonauts several years back on a whim and I am ever so glad that I did! Both games are a joy, but two takes the fundamentals of the first game and improves on them in every way! The game starts you off with a nice recap of the events from both Psychonauts 1 and the VR game; so you don't need to play them to enjoy Psychonauts 2, but they definitely enhance the experience. If you enjoy puzzle-platform collect-athons with light combat elements, give Psychonauts a try!

_childDocuments_.review: Being a sequel that's coming over 15 years later, I had little hope. But after having played it, I can say I am truly in awe. The writing is even more refined, it's dark, witty, and has an extra layer of depth we hardly see in gaming ever. Its truly a masterpiece and a very worthy successor of the original game. Probably the best game to come out so far this year, a breath of fresh air compared to the boring open-world games devs puke out year after year without any soul.I would honestly recommend you play the first part to enjoy it more, but it goes without saying that you can easily play it without havent played the first part.

_childDocuments_.review: A truly wonderful and high quality game. It is quite funny, sometimes a little silly, and always has a lot of heart. The amount of effort in this game is truly staggering, all of the levels feel fantastic, and the game play is solid. Tim Schaffer's Magnum Opus, and there is no contest. A must buy. Only downside is that this game picks up immediately after a VR exclusive, but luckily they explain the plot quickly. A profoundly sincere game about empathy and caring for others.

_childDocuments_.review: In short, this game lives up to the original and was a great experience. The writing and especially the combat have been improved and, although there are a few things I prefer about the original, I'd say this game is marginally better overall.  I do have two major complaints about P2, which you can read about below. I'll list the ways in which I think each game is better:Ways in which P2 > P1:- Combat. Not only are there now far more ways to fight enemies, but they've introduced upgrades to your powers which unlock special abilities that allow you to create your own playstyle. There are also now far more enemy types, so you're no longer just fighting hundreds of censors and those screaming cat suicide-bomber things (the latter of which has been removed). The new enemies are named after mental afflictions (e.g. panic attacks and depression), and the way they fight actually reflects what they're named after.- Getting 100% completion/achievements is no longer the insanity test it was in P1. In P2, it can be done without too much difficulty in about 25 hours, particularly because figments no longer blend into the background or fly in annoying patterns. There isn't a point-of-no-return in P2, and all achievements and items can be obtained in the endgame if you miss any (there's one or two moments where you're locked into the story, but they're only temporary).- Writing. The tone is much more serious now with a bit less humour overall, but the lines which are meant to be funny are much funnier in P2. I thought P1's humour got quite tiresome as it felt like every single line was trying to be some quirky one-liner, so I prefer the more serious tone. Furthermore, the depiction of mental illness is much more real and serious in P2. In terms of characters, while the interns in P2 are nowhere near as good as the campers from P1, I preferred the other characters in P2 in general to P1 (I loved most of the new characters in particular). In terms of story, I think P2 is slightly better as it has more mystery and goes into people's backgrounds more, but I think P1 has a better written villain. The side story about the mole in HQ has a really good ending, but it gets forgotten for most of the story for some reason.Ways in which P1 > P2:- P2 is much more linear. My first major complaint about P2 is that while it has a big, open overworld as expected, the levels themselves are far more linear than in P1. The devs weren't necessarily wrong to go for more straight platforming, and the platforming is probably better in P2, but it's disappointing that other than the overworld, there's only one big, open area to explore and do tasks in any order in.- Pacing. My second major complaint is that there are so many subtasks within subtasks within subtasks in P2 that there are times when the game grinds to a halt and you lose all perspective of what you're meant to be doing. There's a particularly bad point about one third of the way through the game where I was getting bored and genuinely didn't want to play on. I'm glad I was able to get through that part as the pacing picks up and the later levels are some of the best in the series, but it's a major problem when the player is thinking about putting the game down so early on.Other differences: - Level design. As I said earlier, I don't like the over-reliance on linear levels in P2 but there are still some great levels, with Cassie O'Pia's library possibly being my favourite level in the series. When it comes to integrating the subject's personality into the level design, I think P2 does it better artistically but P1 does it better in terms of gameplay and level-unique gimmicks.- Music. The music is more ambient and more subtle in P2, so it's a bit less distracting than in P1, but consequently there are far more memorable tracks in P1.

_childDocuments_.review: Psychonauts 2 is awesome! It has everything a great 3D Platformer should have. Fun traversal, a deep combat system, visually appealing artstyle, smooth animations, expansive areas to explore, a large variety of levels, interesting characters, witty dialogue, and an exciting plot. I strongly recommend playing it.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: From someone that didn't really vibe 100% with the first entry, Psychonauts 2 grabbed me from beginning to end. Art direction (and the variety on offer) is the main standout, with palette choices and composition constantly forcing me to stop an gawk in fear of being overwhelmed (in a good way). Animation is a close second for me, with all of it actually being animated by hand rather than supplemented with mo-cap. Most of the animation work is great (if stiff at time in regards to the canned stuff during dialogue scenes), with several fantastic set-pieces sprinkled throughout that genuinely floored me. Blizzard's top dog in video games for animation and, at points, Psychonauts 2 approaches that level of quality.Voice cast is stacked, which seems to be the norm for Double Fine. Music pretty nice as well, and as varied as its settings, but not as memorable for me. In fact, the only real knock I can give this game is it's bizarre audio mixing during a few cut-scenes, where it seems some foley effects are missing or muffled.Everything is wrapped together in a surprisingly personal story from the expected psycho-spy adventure. Truly, just fantastic, from beginning to end.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: Well, After a good 30 hours of running around and seeing what there was to see, I have finally managed to gather all collectables and achievements this game has to offer.So the controls are a bit off, nothing too bad. But it is something you will notice if you played the first game and got used to how Raz used to move. Some of his powers have been obviously nerfed, but its kind of understandable why. Other than that raz moves smoothly and is fairly comfortable to play with. The key-binds were also very kind, but then again i played on controller.The story, I will not go into as i dont want to spoil anything about it, but the game itself along with it's story, world building and how everything is laid out along with all the dialogue the NPC's have will keep you running around for an age. The story has good twists and turns, and looking for vaults will give you information you might have missed or give you something to think about. The figments always tell a story of their own in each mental world and completing them actually seems to give the person we explored closure or relief of a kind.The achievements were all VERY easy to get. Granted, some figments were a nightmare to go back and find. But progressing with a steady stream of achievements i never had to go out of my way to really get any in particular. Just wanting to get all collectables, you will get everything naturally as you progress!Overall the game was a pleasant experience and will do quite a few more runs. But for collecting everything and doing it all, it is completely possible and within a small period of time. Hopefully others think the same. 9/10 - Would Set Fire To The Wildlife Again!

_childDocuments_.review: ---Psychonauts 2 is the long-awaited sequel to the cult classic Psychonauts. Historically.. games with that much of a legacy behind them have been let-downs. But Psychonauts 2 takes everything that the beloved platformer set out to do and improves upon almost every aspect by leaps and bounds. As someone that probably wore out their blockbuster’s copy multiple times as a kid, coming back to this world has been like coming home.Psychonauts 2 takes the glimpse we saw of the world in the first game and pulls back the curtain to give us the full view. In every way, the game expands upon the criticisms its predecessor faced and gives us a deeper, more emotional narrative as a result. But don’t worry, it retains ALL of the clever humor the original was known for. It’s just more.. Tasteful. The story is set mere days after the first game and the underrated VR pre-sequel (thanks for the term, Borderlands) with Razputin and his mentors trying to break into the mind of the recently-redeemed Dr. Loboto. From there, Raz makes it to the Motherlobe, the Headquarters for the Psychonauts.. Where he’s made an intern. From THERE, Raz experiences the job from the bottom of the barrel and learns the real ins and outs of being a Psychonaut. And of being a boyfriend.The game gives us a beautiful look at trauma, empathy, and therapy. Instead of barging into any mind he wants, Raz has to learn to /ask/ to be let inside. As an adult who grew up with this game, I felt a connection with a lot of the lessons this game talks about. Regret, self-forgiveness, introspection. It’s all very human.The writers do a good job about not forgetting the core of mental health: we’re all flawed, *very* flawed human beings. And no one, no matter who they are, is free from that truth. But understanding goes a long way with helping us put our imperfections back into that metaphorical bottle.The gameplay surprised me a lot! It’s much, much more fluid than any other platformer in the genre. And it builds upon the mechanics of the original game in ways I didn’t expect. The ability to switch powers is quick and responsive, and they can all be customized with pins purchased from an in-universe psychonaut vending machine.Each fight is fast-paced and can be completed in SO many different ways. It’s definitely fulfilling, and a huge improvement over the first game.The level design was one thing I was *greatly* concerned about.. Would this game end up being a disappointment? I can safely say it didn’t end up that way. While the original game’s levels will ALWAYS hold a special place in my heart due to how many times I’ve completed them, Psychonauts 2 builds upon the formula in sensible ways  and gives us so many incredible minds to explore. The Psi King’s mind is definitely one of my favorite levels in the entire series and shows me that Double Fine never forgot the heart of Psychonauts.However.. I will say that I feel the original game has much better control when it comes to the acrobatics portion of the platforming. Tight-ropes and trapezes feel so far and in-between, but I might’ve been relying too much on the Levitation Orb.Dialogue is a lot more in-depth than the first game, with Razputin able to ask a /lot/ more about the world and how characters feel about things happening around them. One clever addition is that some of the questions Raz can /ask/ Lily will.. come out differently than the player intends, because his character hasn’t fully come to terms with their relationship. It’s adorable and adds layers to his interactions with Lily.While I’m not a huge fan of the intern menu and feel the original game’s journal was so much better, it does its job and isn't a terrible change. Its design even makes sense in the environment Raz is in.The original Psychonauts was known for its unique artstyle and I’ve always felt that was the game’s BIGGEST strength, providing the first game with a timeless look. This aspect has carried over into the sequel seamlessly, with the new engine making everything look as great as any modern day game WITHOUT sacrificing the original game’s charm.If you’re looking for more of what you saw in the first game, you WON’T be disappointed. You’ll be amazed.At the moment, there’s a bug where the main menu gets stuck if you look at the unique items in your intern menu. It’s REALLY annoying, but it can be solved by rapidly alt-tabbing or using escape to back out of the items instead of clicking “close”.I’d easily recommend this to any fan of the first game! While it does have imperfections, it delivers a sequel that easily builds upon the original’s legacy and gives us what we loved in spades.

_childDocuments_.review: WARNING! THIS GAME IS HIGHLY ENTERTAINING AND MAY CAUSE SEVERE ENJOYMENT, ENTERTAINMENT, AND MANY GOOD LAUGHS. SECOND WARNING. JACK BLACK IS IN THIS GAME.This game is absolutely phenomenal, and it's visual and verbal storytelling is revolutionary. Though the artstyle initially caught me off guard, it's wonderfully unique, and the atmosphere of the game tied with Raz's adorable personality is a blessing I never knew I needed.Gameplay: Excellent      The mechanics of the powers are super fun, and jumping around all the levels is a (PSI) blast! The momentum you gain with the lev ball is great to play around with, especially in the brain tumbler. Not only that, but the parkour in the real world is also amazing! One of my favorite areas to explore was the Questionable area, due to all of the fun parkour challenges to get psi cards and challenge markers.Story: Phenomenal      From heartwarming to extremely dark, it caught me completely by surprise and had me rooting for everyone involved. We are human, and we all have our own demons to fight. Sometimes we just need a seecond chance to regain our ground. Genuinely perspective changing on a few things despite the overall friendly and lighthearted presentation of the game. It ties perfectly back to the original game's story as well as Rhombus of Ruin, and it's just a feel-good experience for any new or long-term Psychonauts fan.Aesthetics:     Out of this world. It is a game full of more colors than there are colors that exist in the world. Most strikingly, the level for Jack Black's character. Absolutely stunning from beginning to end. The level designs for characters' minds were unique for each one, and the world as a whole is fun to explore for hours on end.     Overall, a 100/10 experience, and one that I will forever adore. Also, for completionists like myself, when you go back to levels to get all the collectibles, the game makes it very easy to track what you are missing and marks off each of the minds in small areas. It's something that makes even the largest of levels much less overwhelming to fully 100%. Fully recommend this game to anyone who enjoys fun, and who likes watching a loveable 10 year old dork kick major ass. Hats off to the devs for an amazing experience, way to go Tim Schafer and everyone else on the team!

_childDocuments_.review: There's a lot to truly love about Psychonauts 2. The aesthetic and the characters within this world charmed the bejesus out of me, a hallmark of Double Fine. There are some smart moments of writing too, especially in the way the game addresses mental issues with a gentle humor and underlying seriousness.  And as a complete package, this might be the meatiest Double Fine game to date, with lots of levels and exploration to be had. But.But like so many Double Fine games, this is a chore to actually play at times. Platforming elements often feel just a hair off, like the main character Raz should either magnetize better or make easier connections with the next environmental object. There are also some bafflingly difficult portions of the game that are only that way due to the controls or frustrating elements within the environment. For example, a clever bowling alley-themed level is nearly ruined by having to negotiate a bowling ball like a marble through jumps and turns meant for a game that controls better than this.That too is a depressing hallmark of Double Fine games. They're often very clever but hampered by having to actually play them. In Psychonauts 2's case, that cleverness and the sense of love that went into this game are enough to pull it out of the fire, but there really needs to be much more playtesting and a general questioning of "is this element fun?" in future games.

_childDocuments_.review: Very few games have ever taken more than a decade to release it's sequel without it being terrible. It is a testament to Double Fine's commitment to its fans that Psychonauts 2 has even been published. The original Psychonauts game did not have a great initial release and became something of a cult classic, beloved by those who actually did stumble upon it.I must admit I was one of those fans of the quirky original, but Psychonauts 2 has proved itself to be one of the truely incredible games having received overwhelmingly positive reviews both from original fans and gamers who are new to the franchise. Psychonauts 2 is that rare thing, a sequel that is not only better than the original but stands entirely on its own. The original was great (yes it had flaws, but those were largely the same flaws all games of its generation had), and this sequel is even greater than the original without requiring the nostalgia of playing the original. In many ways, Psychonauts 2 resembles a scrappy underdog, well liked by their small group of friends, after going through multiple intense training archs and finally gains the respect and adoration of of their larger community.If you have not played Psychonauts, but are considering playing Psychonauts 2, do it. You do not need to have played the original. As well loved as the original game was, Psychonauts 2 is so good it turns the original game into a worthy prologue. If you are seeing this because Psychonauts 2 was nominated for a Steam Award for Visual Style, understand Psychonauts 2 has a higher review score than any game that won any of the categories. While I might argue that the wrong game won the Visual Style category purely due to the size of its fan base, I wouldn't necessarily say Psychonauts should have won that category. It however, should have won Outstanding Story-Rich Game, and should have been nominated for Game of the Year, though I will admit Resident Evil Village is also an incredible game and I don't know if I could argue that one is objectively better than the other.If you need to know what you're getting into before buying a game, this is an exception platforming game centered around the psychology of people that have been through various kinds of trauma. You will help them come to terms with those traumas, though you will not do so entirely alone, or without making mistakes. You will learn and wield incredible powers, discover long hidden mysteries, and even discover secrets hidden in your character's own history. You are not some destined hero, you have your own reasons and motivations for what everything you do.While the story is exceptional, the game play is just as good. You will explore many unique worlds, each an inner mindscape reflecting the distinct personality and experiences of the character it belongs to. You will re-master abilities from the original game, but you will master even more new abilities in pursuit not only of helping those around you, but to become a true Psychonaut!

_childDocuments_.review: To start off, the original Psychonauts was my favourite game of all time. To this day, if I'm particularly stressed or overwhelmed, I'll load up a save I have right at the level start of Lungfishopolis and nyoooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooom. It was always fun and engrossing, with savvy humour and sly commentary. Oh, it had problems, and Meat Circus is a forbidden word in this household, but it was always just that comfortable pair of bunny slippers you slip into and sigh happily.But my dudes, dudettes and gentlethems, Psychonauts 2 is straight up the game that character and storywise... Psychonauts wanted to be. There's still the moments of cackling laughter and absolute spectacle from the original game. And there's still moments of shrieking because you overran and platform and HAVE TO WORK YOUR WAY ALL THE WAY BACK UP THERE #$@$@#$!!!!! The difference is every head you go into, I've had at least one moment of just quietly and often solemnly taking in what they've put on the plate here. There's a thoughtfulness and empathy here that while was there in the first, is now sharpened to an exquisite knife. I'm not done playing yet. But I had to stop and write this. Even if the last bit of game goes wildly off track, I highly recommend this game for what I've played through so far. I backed it ages back and forgot it, but THIS is what it is to really, really take the time to develop a game to perfection.That said, there are some HILARIOUS bugs, where effects stay, especially if you get nailed repeatedly by a few. And the age old psychonauts YOU SHOULDN'T HAVE JUMPED THERE!!!! is still there. And the game does hit some pretty strong phobia and triggering material. If you've got some tender spots, seek out some spoiler free content warning lists before you put your cash down!

_childDocuments_.review: is a fantastic follow-up to the cult classic original. The best way I can describe the game is an interactive Pixar film. I was glued to the game from start to finish, although there were some bumpy patches along the way. Raz finally arrives at Psychonauts HQ, the Motherlobe, after his misadventures at Whispering Rock and the Rhombus of Ruin. However, he quickly finds that his promotion to Psychonaut isn’t official and is demoted to an intern. Now he has to climb back up the ranks, all while dealing with a whole new work environment, the other interns, his estranged family, and a new psychic conspiracy that threatens to drown both the Psychonauts and the world. In a world of psychic espionage, there are some secrets best left buried…The story was pretty great. There were multiple twists and reveals that had me eager to see what the next bend had in store. While nothing terribly new or innovative was used in the story, the execution was exquisite and I rarely felt bored. PN2 has a huge cast of new characters and continues the witty writing from PN1. However, I feel that some of them could’ve used more time in the spotlight as they quickly became background characters. Nonetheless, I really liked everyone and they all contributed something to the journey. This time around, a greater emphasis is placed on mental damage and how Psychonauts can help heal people. While specific disorders and diseases aren’t directly mentioned, their inclusion helped make their owners feel like more realistic and relatable characters. Healing, growth, and connections are central themes, and PN2 does a nice job exploring them all.      PN2 is a massive glow-up from 1. Essentially, every area has been refined and polished, making PN2 a blast to play. To start, platforming is much more engaging and challenging, mostly due to great environmental design. Often times, navigating the terrain is a puzzle in of itself. For example, trying to navigate a cave network via wall ivy, stone platforms, mine rails, and more. As a result, each new real-world zone was thrilling, with different terrain challenges and nooks and crannies to explore. Thus, you're always on an adventure, even when just wandering around the real world. I’ve spent a lot of time just wandering around the real world, scraping around for collectables and enjoying the views.In order to compliment the platforming, Raz’s powers have been refined and the game truly feels built around them. You can find challenging far jumps requiring skilled Levitation jumps and tight hovers, or use Pyrokinesis to clear areas or even create new pathways. As a result, you'll be tested on how well you can use your powers, and some interesting puzzles are made around them. Additionally, every power has combat applications to make your toolset more versatile. On that note, combat is very engaging and involved. Encounters are pretty frequent, each containing multiple enemies, and most enemies take some time to put down. While they all have pretty straight-forward tactics, getting swarmed and having to counter all their strategies at once is an exhilarating feeling. Since all your powers are usable in combat, you’re free to create your own strategies for victory. Raz’s powers operate on a cooldown system, so knowing the proper time to use a power always feels rewarding. I'm pretty conflicted about most boss battles. On the one hand, their presentation and thematic mechanics are excellent. The sheer scale of the fights is amazing, and each boss feels truly personalized to the person they torment. On the other, the rule of three is heavily used, so encounters feel very scripted and rigid. Certain gimmicks are also really annoying to deal with. For example, digging specific items up to use against a boss as they attack you. All in all, I think the style outweighs the substance. Collectathon elements felt like they could’ve used some work. There are 5 types of collectables and their main purpose is to allow Raz to level up. However, keeping track of them all can be a hassle. The completion page bundles all the areas of a level into one page, making tracking down missing items downright painful and annoying. Likewise, since the scope of each level has been immensely increased, finding those very last collectables can easily get tedious and frustrating. For a casual playthrough, this is a minor inconvenience. For completeionism, this is a nightmare.  I did a lot of collecting and exploring, so I finished in around 18-ish hours. 100% completion took around 25 hours. While the game is of moderate length, I feel the ride was enough to justify the price. There's also a proper free-roam mode after completing the story, which is a very welcome addition.I absolutely love PN2’s visual design. Modern graphics elevate the eccentric design of the series to a new height. Mental worlds are the clear winners here, each being whimsical yet profoundly telling of their owners. While I described PN1’s worlds as “unique amusement parks”, PN2’s all feel like different planets due to their wildly different themes, scales, gimmicks, and more. The visual design is marvelously done and I found myself enraptured in quite a few. Character designs for the series are rather unique, taking a 3D approach to cartoony designs. Admittedly, some designs look a bit strange, but the sheer diversity helps create memorable characters. Overall animation quality is pretty good, aside from clipping and lip synch issues distracting during certain cutscenes and talking segments. The soundtrack really hits all the right notes while playing. From nostalgic remixes of PN1 tracks to new and emotional ones, I always had a smile on my face when taking in the music. Many original voice actors also reprise their roles, which is phenomenal. Newer voices were also great as well, although some lines felt weird from a directing or quality standpoint. Sound effects were pretty solid across the board.  Overall, the Steam version ran pretty smoothly. There were some stuttering problems, but they seemed to smooth out after a while. I also experienced one "Fatal Error" crash. However, people have been reporting various other issues, so your experience may vary.A nice amount of graphical and audio options are available for tweaking. You're also offered an impressive amount of accessibility options to make the game more approachable, such as larger fonts and colorblind filters. I played with a Xbox controller and everything functioned well. You are able to rebind both controller and KBM controls.  I am in love with what PN2 has achieved. The 16-year wait was well worth it and the product is something I feel anyone can enjoy. Practically everything is an amazing step up from the first game, and I thoroughly enjoyed the journey as a result. Replayability is a bit limited due to its linear nature, but collection completion will take a lot of time and effort in the meantime.

_childDocuments_.review: "Psychonauts 2" takes players on a whimsical and mind-bending journey through the imaginative landscapes of the human psyche. Developed by Double Fine Productions, this long-awaited sequel to the cult classic "Psychonauts" delivers an experience that's as charming as it is inventive.The game picks up where the original left off, following the adventures of Razputin "Raz" Aquato, a young psychic acrobat who joins the ranks of the Psychonauts, a group of psychic secret agents. As Raz delves deeper into the minds of various characters, players are treated to a colorful array of levels, each with its own unique theme and gameplay mechanics.One of the game's greatest strengths is its creativity. From a twisted dentist's office to a psychedelic casino, every mental landscape Raz explores is bursting with personality and surprises. The game's art style is vibrant and expressive, perfectly capturing the eccentricities of the human mind.Gameplay-wise, "Psychonauts 2" offers a mix of platforming, puzzle-solving, and combat, all of which are executed with polish and precision. Raz's psychic abilities allow for a wide range of gameplay mechanics, from telekinesis to pyrokinesis, adding depth and variety to the experience.But perhaps the most compelling aspect of "Psychonauts 2" is its storytelling. The game tackles themes of mental health, identity, and belonging with nuance and sincerity, weaving them into a narrative that's both heartfelt and humorous. The characters are well-written and endearing, each with their own quirks and motivations.That said, the game isn't without its flaws. Some of the platforming sections can feel a bit clunky, and there are occasional technical hiccups that can disrupt the immersion. Additionally, while the story is engaging overall, it does meander at times, with certain plot points feeling underdeveloped.Despite these minor shortcomings, "Psychonauts 2" is a triumph of creativity and storytelling. With its charming characters, imaginative world-building, and heartfelt narrative, it's a must-play for fans of the original and newcomers alike. The characters are endearing and the mystery plot is engaging.For completionists, there are numerous collectibles but there are a number of handy features in the post-game to help you find any you might have missed.

_childDocuments_.review: I simply can not emphasize how much I loved this game. I absolutely adore it. Its a must buy for any fan of the first game and the best platfomer I have played in recent memory. Just buy the game. Theres no reason not to; I dont care if you dont even have a pc.
