_childDocuments_.review: I want to update this once I'm farther in, because I am enjoying the game and intend to finish it, but there is stuff I gotta get off my chest...The performance... It's not good.  This is a stylized, "cartoonish" game and it just cannot keep a stable framepacing.  I thought something was awry when choosing the highest graphical settings still sets the render resolution to 75%.  I wouldn't realize how necessary it was until I got to the first large hub of the game.I have a 5800 X3D and a 7900XTX and plenty of fast RAM.  Most recently-released games I can play at highest or "perceptually the same as highest" settings (except RT, of course) and get well over 100 FPS most of the time and often max out my refresh rate of 144.  My system *struggles* with this game.I've found that in most small internal spaces, I can get away with all settings High except for Textures, which can stay at Very high no problem, and render resolution at 100%.  Not too bad.  There is fairly frequent stuttering, but it's not game-breaking.  Some early bosses were giving me a bit of trouble.  There were serious frame timing issues if I didn't cap my framerate at 60 and/or use VSync, though.Once I got to the campground, though... it was bad...  Almost no amount of settings changes could get it to run stable frames at 60fps.  It stayed at 57-59, reported, no matter what, but it was perceptually a slideshow and the input lag was awful.  I had to lower the render resolution to 60% and drop all the settings to medium to get it playable.  Fortunately, because of the stylization of the game, it doesn't impact visuals too much.  The render resolution does, though, because everything is super blurry now.  It's really unfortunate as everything else about the game makes sense as to why it's so beloved, but the performance issues are a really big hurdle for me to get over.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: A quick, spoiler-free review... Level Design: Brilliant. The platforming and puzzles are fun and challenging. Psychology is creatively integrated into level design. Graphics: Gorgeous. They preserved the art style of the first game and polished it for modern systems. Music: As good as the first game. In fact, they even reused some pieces from the first game. Voice Acting: They got ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Jack Black. Dialogue: Witty.  Characters: Colorful, both literally and figuratively. Plot: Messy, anti-climactic, and disappointing. Had some good moments, but when the credits rolled, I felt unsatisfied. Length: I finished it in about 20 hours. 100% will take a little longer. Audience: Appropriate for kids, but intelligent enough for adults. Kind of like a Pixar movie. Portrayal of Mental Health Issues: Accurate, respectful, and creative. Controls: Use a controller, the keyboard controls are ♥♥♥♥. Bugs: I haven't found any. Do I recommend it: Yes. Should you play the first game: If you want to get all the jokes. Also, the first game is a masterpiece and you should play it anyway. Value: Just buy it.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: They kept this game in the oven long enough that it came out well-done.I like the new abilities, they all give the feeling of power without still being OP. Keeping the most significant powers from the first game unlocked from the beginning was a very good idea.I liked the levels with the exception of the overworld, which felt empty and the collectibles were incredibly tedious and difficult to find. But the levels themselves were very pretty and creative, and enjoyable to play through.I especially liked the new system to finding missed collectibles, thanks to which 100%-ing the game was much easier and felt more rewarding.If you liked Psychonauts, then this is an improved version with new levels, new story and new characters. Definitely worth playing through.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not sure which one I like more among the two games, but Psychonauts 2 is exactly how a sequel should be made, being its own thing.It builds up on the prequel (though it can be a standalone experience as the game starts with a recap of Psychonauts and Rhombus Ruin but I'll still urge you guys to check out the original like seriously it is needed for the "experience"), and does so much more, tackling a more varied spectrum of the human psyche, dealing with mostly severe issues, yet neatly coated with a spice of comedy and playfulness which I'll never get over and forever adore.The story is also more immersive and detailed with lots of twists this time around and it was an amazing and fun journey. Post game grinding for the completionist run was a treat, just be sure to get those two missable achievements beforehand.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: I don't even know where to begin with my praise. I loved the first game as a teenager and have always hoped for a second part. And what an amazing game they have made! The level and character design is just top-notch, the fights are challenging yet totally manageable (also for a younger audience), they have kept their great humor and there are new. fricking. POWERS!! Just the sequel I hoped to see and a plot I didn't even dare to imagine. The display of human minds with their fears, blind spots, emotional baggage etc. is so artistic and deep at the same time. Tim Schaefer and his team are geniuses for this.If you like innovative plattformer-puzzle-games with room for exploration and a good dash of crazy, this is for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: Great sequel!!! Gameplay has been improved a lot!! The things we loved in the first game are here too: good storytelling, great characters, humor and beautiful art! Visually, this game is amazing! There were only a couple of things I didn't like: 1) the story is very good but it suffers a bit from having too many characters and not enough time/room for handling all of them correctly. 2)The level design is great when it comes to visuals, but I think that when it comes to structure and gameplay, no level here is as good or memorable as the best levels of the first game.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: I only have two negative things to say about this game:The game is not quite as funny as the first one which still makes me laugh with its cast of awkward weirdo kids and spot on dialogue straight out of classic point and click games.Obviously, humor is 100% subjective and it's hard for the writers and voice actors to replicate that.Raz is less of a lovable ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and more of a lovable optimistic friend, which didn't bother me, but might not be everyone's cup of tea.The slightly more linear level design makes backtracking less enticing and I honestly haven't bothered. There are less figments but they are still kinda of a hassle to find (Always fun to see you're missing one after combing the entire stage). Those are small complaint to a fantastic follow up that absolutely lives up to the original.Combat is fun, the controls are great and all the levels are fun and varied.It's even more trippy than the original and has an absolutely stunning presentation with great sound design as well.The story is pretty good and I love how positive and uplifting it is despite some the themes that are explored. As cynical as I can be, this genuinely put a smile on my face at times.I think they did a great job appealing to both the older and younger audience, because it never dumbs anything down but doesn't get too depressing or explicit either.I had my doubts ever since this was announced, but Double Fine went all out with this one and nailed it.Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: Having Played The Full Game. I can definitely say. There is no milkman in this game! And its a crying shame!But its also a really good game and you can tell a lot of love went into it. Would be nice if they could patch the bug with unique items freezing up the game if you investigate them but. And give more missions involving the fellow interns. It felt like I didnt get a chance to learn about them at all.Get it on sale and enjoy.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: I am a huge fan of Tim Schafer's games and Double Fine in general. Psychonauts is one of my favorite games. I played it multiple times on multiple platforms, renting it on PS2 back when it came out. I still remember getting the Demo disc in OPM.Psychonauts 2 really holds up. The writing is top notch, the gameplay is near identical, and the graphics were updated flawlessly. The game does suffer from the classic 3d platformer problems like issues with camera angles and confusing controls when said camera goes wild.No game, NO GAME is without it's flaws, but hot damn if this isn't as close to perfect as a sequel can get.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent sequel.The worlds are more insane and random, but the story isn't as tight as the first one.  Starting things off where some VR game nobody played left off was a mistake, but it soon finds its footing.  The lighting is also kind of cold and harsh at times, was less cozy feeling than the first game.  Very good music.  Too many cool environments to list.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: This game kicks ass.Some might say that this game doesn't quite surpass the original.  I think they're crazy. To me this game is an improvement over the original in pretty much every single way.  The mental worlds feel just as fresh and creative, the platforming is more stable smooth, the combat is significantly less stale, every psi ability feels like it has a purpose, etc etc.  We are pretty lucky that this game even came out looking at its development history - which is something I can't be more grateful for.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked the original or have any interest whatsoever in 3D platformers, get this game. The traversal of space is amazing with enough variety that you won't ever be bored getting from 'A' to 'B' and (unusually for a 3D platformer) the combat is actually fun.Where the game shines in particular is the incredible variety of levels and the creativity on display. Levels are creative, present a wonderful variety of environments and gameplay styles and the integration of story beats into the levels is remarkably good.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: This game is more than I could've ever expected. It managed to make me feel the same way I did when I first played Psychonauts, 16 years ago. The atmosphere, the personality... the puns. Most importantly, representation done right, showing characters of all sorts of origin, background, sexuality, all in a very tasteful way. I know the developers to be very inclusive, but it's still really heartwarming to see. This franchise will forever be my favorite. There's so many elements to it, so many details, it's very obvious the people making it had fun, and that's one of the many reasons it's so great. The sequel in particular (since that's what I'm commenting on) was an incredible adventure with a great story, and an important message behind it. It's made improvements to an already extremely unique game and made it even better, which I didn't even know was possible. My only complaint is that it doesn't last forever.Thank you, Double Fine, for this unforgettable experience, looking forward to whatever the future holds, I already know it's going to be great.

Gameplay doesn't stray away and still embrace the original formula while modernizing it to the current standard. Also I found it pretty weird that the final boss didn't have its own stage, especially since the one in the first game was reallly well done imo. But yeah whatever, games good.

_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: One bit of advice: I started with a keyboard and mouse because that's always my default control scheme and to be clear it's fine that way, but it seems this is best experienced with a controller.I can't believe it's been 5 years since I backed this on Fig, and over 15 years since the original.I've got dozens of development updates that I haven't read, and I've avoided the trailers and reviews because I didn't want any spoilers - I wanted to go into the sequel to one of my all-time favorite games with fresh eyes.It has absolutely been worth the wait!  It's exactly what you'd want in a sequel - the same heart as the first game, but more and, frankly, better.  The story respects and expands upon the groundwork laid in the first game, while delivering a depth and complexity that was frankly surprising given the generally whimsical tone of the game.  The minds are creative, varied and compelling to explore. There's tons and tons of well-voiced dialogue with that characteristic Tim Schafer\Double Fine wit. The combat has just enough depth to be satisfying to master, but you don't HAVE to master it.It's good.  If you liked the first, it's a no-brainer.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: A simply delightful game.  Wildly creative concepts and level design, beautiful art, animation, and sound, and a touching story tying everything together.It can be played without playing the first one, but you'll definitely be a bit lost by the opening of the story if you haven't played the first one.It's slightly let down by controls that can be a little janky, and (at least on the linux version, which I played), some small bugs that kept cropping up (for example, mouse control would sometimes just disappear until you went to the menu and then resumed game).  Overall, I loved this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: In my opinion a complete upgrade to the first game, and that one was already really good.It should be noted that this game often references the first game and also the small VR game "Ruins of Rhombus".I recommend playing the first game  and Ruins of Rhombus first (Ruins of Rhombus of course only if possible, but you probably know how to catch up with that, it is fairly short).
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: If you played the first game and liked it, you will love this game. Relatively bug free. The controls are super well defined as opposed to the first game. Other bugs have popped up for others, but they are actively working on patching the game. I ran into one tiny issue myself at the end, but you can reach out to Double Fine support and they'll help. If you didn't play the first game, I'd still recommend this. Again, it's way more controllable and has all the wit and charm of the first. I've waited over half my life for this game (no exaggeration), and it was worth the wait.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved every second of this! I was a huge fan of the first one, and have 100% completed it a few times. Rhombus of Ruin was also a lot of fun, especially in the new medium of VR. This was really nostalgic for me and is everything that I think a good sequel should be. Upped the ante from the original, kept the same feeling, and humor as well. Added new gameplay elements that felt at home in the world and to the character. Also, loved the creativity in the world-building as you jump mind to mind. I will definitely 100% this game, and then await announcement of either a DLC or a sequel. Another great Double Fine game.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: Having enjoyed playing through the first Psychonauts game this year (2022) my expectations for the long awaited sequel were quite high. I can say with confidence that Psychonauts 2 absolutely delivers as a sequel to its predecessor and even exceeds it in many ways.Quality-of-life experience is improved across the board and the production value is comparable to many 3d animated films. I also found myself more attached to the cast than the original game and the environments are full of various, eccentric NPCs that establish a more immersive environment than ever before.Psychonauts 2 isn't perfect: combat can become a juggling act with PSI-powers, Raz's fellow interns become less involved and underdeveloped despite their importance during the game's climax, and the final portion of the game is underwhelming despite how brilliant everything leading up to it is. Some may also find disappointment with the more platforming-focused level design compared to the more experimental level mechanics of the first game.Regardless, I consider Psychonauts 2 a must play and the best 3D platformer I have played since Super Mario Galaxy.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not kidding when I say I'm one of the people that have waited 15 years for this game and even though I already beat it just a few days after launch, I  can't believe this game exists.  Double Fine did so much right with this game that any negatives I have feel like nitpicks   What can I say that hasn't already been said? The tight platforming, the funny and clever dialogue, the lovable and unique cast of characters, the rock solid level design, just the unbridled charm and love this game exudes? It's all been lauded time and time again.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most gorgeous games I've ever played, in nearly every aspect. Design and gameplay are flawless, each level is unique and surprising, and the game is engaging the entire way through. Not to mention the different areas of the hub world, each feel alive and vibrant in their own way. Imma say it, I enjoyed this game more than even Mario Odyssey. Tim Schaffer, you are a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ genius. Thank you for knocking it out of the park once again.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: A true sequel in all ways. While the game could be burnt through in a small amount of time just like it previous entry, the charm of Psychonauts 2 is the life it breaths into everything. I know alot of people are probably not one for all the small talk in between major events in their story but it flushes out this world so much its enjoyable seeing how the creators made the environment tell the story too.The game flushes out alot of the clunkier parts of the first game. Powers can be used mid jump, the upgrade system is more player controlled, and the worlds/minds can be visited in an order the player choose for the most part. Overall would recommend for any fan of the first one.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: Talented, brilliant, incredible, amazing, show stopping, spectacular, never the same, totally unique, completely not ever been done before, unafraid to reference or not reference, put it in a blender, ♥♥♥♥ on it, vomit on it, eat it, give birth to it.I love this game and the company so much, playing the first game made me so hype for this one and I feel bad for not making a review to show my absolute love for this game and it's amazing characters and design
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: It's a solid 8/10 in my opinion.I loved the original Psychonauts, I loved the world, the art style, the music, I loved everything about it. The platforming was never the best though, and in general the combat and gameplay mechanics ranged from "pretty good" to "can we move on now?" I don't think that's too crazy to suggest, just some bits where the controls maybe weren't great or the platforming was a little janky.Psychonauts 2 is... more of that. They tightened up some of it but it honestly just feels the same. So, if you liked the first one, you'll like this one.One minor complaint I personally have is the voice acting performance from Horvitz and about half of the rest of the cast, because honestly they seemed a little checked out most of the time. It wasn't a disaster, but it did really take me out of it at points. And there's something... off, about some of the facial expressions on Raz. I don't know, somethin' funny going on there. Makes me uncomfortable.So yeah, great story, excellent world, just long enough to not overstay its welcome, good replay value, just an all around good experience.As an aside, I saw some stuff in the Discussion forum about the game's political commentary and I wanna say, I usually complain about that stuff, most video game writers just don't know how to work a political issue into their story without directly referencing recent events or getting angry. But Psychonauts 2 did a really good job of divorcing those issues from reality and working them cleanly into the world they created. I won't say more about those issues, and if you disagree with their opinion about those issues that's fine too, but if you see anyone whining about them bringing those issues up at all then that person is being a butt.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic follow-up to the first game!  Psychonauts 2 takes all the action and platforming elements from the first game and improves them in various ways.  Every ability has its use both in and outside of combat, especially the new and really cool ones.  Not only will you explore dozens of new and unique locations, but you'll learn the story of many new characters, and tie the loose-ends that were presented in the first Psychonauts game.For the achievement hunters out there, this is how long it took for me to get 100% in this game, and I'd say that it never dragged on.  Some figments may be tough to find, but I assure you that the gameplay is engaging enough to make it worthwhile.Double Fine has done it again! With games released these days, I usually have low expectations, especially for sequels. Despite this, the developers have managed to stay true to the spirit of the original game.  In many ways, I'd say this game is superior to the original!I recommend playing through the first game's story before buying this, since it will greatly improve your experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: it's very rare to see a sequel to a 16 year old game pull it off THIS WELL, the charm known from the first game oozes out of the sequel. The music, the writing, the voice acting, the LEVEL DESIGN are all finely crafted to create an immersive experience on par to the nostalgic trip that is the first of the series.great ♥♥♥♥, shouts out to the devs
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game. Even better than the first one. Has a lot of those classic adventure game stuff that made 2000's games so great, with great visuals and an epic story which will take you for an emotional ride. Highly recommend it to anyone looking for an interesting game to play through and definitely pick it up if you played the first Psychonauts, you won't be disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: Easily my favorite game to come out last year. I'm still catching up on some of the hits from 2021, so there may be a hidden gem that I have missed, but I honestly doubt anything can be this good. It's an hysterical, brilliantly written, fantastic story with amazing, fully realized characters and classic 3D platforming that holds up very well by today's standards... and, on top of that, some of the best levels I've ever played in the genre. I mean it's Psychonauts 2. It was some of the most fun I've ever had 100%ing a game 10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: From what I have played, the game is pretty damn perfect. It is hard to quantify how many things Doublefine does right in Psychonauts 2. The story is well written and interesting. The gameplay is enjoyable, fast paced, and charmingly irritating at times. The music sets a great atmosphere. The visuals are incredibly enjoyable. Most importantly, the game is designed and created by people who actually wanted to create something special, and it constantly shows. The cohesion from the story elements to the enemies to the type of challenges is really a treat. Everything (as in game elements) seems so obvious, but it's really not, it's just how hard the creators worked to get it to that level.My recommendation is to not read many reviews, don't watch gameplay or anything, just play the game and enjoy every aspect of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr - Buy Psychonauts 2 with money.Just as excellent as the first game for different reasons. Where it lacks the same sharp and relentless sense of humor from long ago, it makes up for it in well-explored poignancy of its characters. Perhaps at the risk of losing some memorability or opportunity for creative puzzle-solving, the gameplay is much more streamlined and will never leave you looking up guides--a lack of obtuseness I welcome after a certain amount of frustration with lack of clarity in the predecessor. And dear god, the presentation. The soundtrack is a standout of the experience (the way the orchestra swells during the late-game combat theme, WEW.) Higher fidelity models and textures are one thing for enhancing the visual style, but the animation is what really gets me--fundamentally, Raz doesn't look too different when standing still, but in motion the kid's got a better energy about him than ever before. Some character designs look more in line with the likes of Broken Age this time around, and I welcome that eclecticism. It shows how much the studio has learned and grown over the years. They did a double fine job on Psychonauts, yet again.

_childDocuments_.review: Great writing, creative levels, and some of the absolutely worst 3D platforming I've ever encountered.Most of it is OK to mediocre, but occasionally the levels feature very difficult to execute jumps. It's absolutely clear what you have to do, there's no puzzle, it's just a matter of the jump being so unforgiving that you have to time several key presses exactly right, neither too fast nor too slow, or you fail. The jump is right on the edge of what's possible, so if you're off by of fraction of a second, you fall.Which is bad enough, but it's pretty common for making a mistake on a later jump to drop you back earlier in the level, so you have to go through attempting the same <expletive> jump again. And again.After a while I just reached a point with one of these jumps where I didn't want to play anymore, and couldn't see myself ever trying it again. The reward of getting to see new funky levels just wasn't worth the aggravation of the actual gameplay.

While I have my misgivings, Psychonauts 2 is a worthy sequel, and I certainly wouldn't complain if someday we miraculously were gifted with the announcement of a  Psychonauts 3. Psychonauts 2 is a great, charming, sometimes surprisingly emotional journey, and one that I recommend to fans and newcomers alike. Final score: 4/5

_childDocuments_.review: My current time with the game (17.4 hours) isn't entirely accurate as I've left it open once or twice and spent a LONG time exploring all the stages because I like the art so much.Basically I waited until I was at least 4-5 stages in before deciding to recommend the game. I've been waiting for this a long, long time and have avoided all media about it. I was both excited and worried because how it was a crowdfunded game to begin with and how, while I love Double Fine's work, traditionally they struggle with compelling and polished gameplay even with a normal budget.I'm glad to say it looks like my worries were unfounded. This is easily Double Fine's most polished game to date. It's super fun to control Raz, and you don't lose any of your abilities from the last game, you just get more and upgrade the old ones, all of which feel much better to use.Everything's just as good as ever and in many cases better than ever. Voice acting, animation quality, music, stage design (good lord there are some amazing transitions/special effects) and all that good stuff.I'm not done with the game so I don't want to write a comprehensive review or anything, but I think if you enjoyed the first game, this game should feel even better. Some of the new levels are instant classics, and small things like little 2D representations of Raz as he's viewed by other characters/enemies/critters (with updates depending on how far the story is of course) have not been forgotten at all.I'd say the thing that took me the longest to get used to was a few of the new characters, namely the other kids. Now that I've played for a while and had more time with each of them, they've grown on me, but my initial complaint was that they were introduced too quickly and that they have "normal" voices. Rather, in a game full of cartoon character voices, it's weird when someone sounds normal. That said, they're not the only "normal" sounding characters but there's also still a ton of cartoony voices, so at this point it just makes the world feel more varied and I don't mind anymore.At this point in time, I highly recommend the game.

_childDocuments_.review: ~ DIFFICULTY ~🔲 My 90 year old grandma could play it🔲 Easy✅ Normal🔲 Hard🔲 Dark Souls~ GRAPHICS ~🔲 MS Paint🔲 Bad🔲 Meh🔲 Graphics dont matter in this game✅ Good🔲 Beautiful~ MUSIC ~🔲 Bad🔲 Not special✅ Good🔲 Eargasm~ STORY ~🔲 This game has no story🔲 Like playing Temple Runners for the story🔲 It's there for the people who want it🔲 Well written✅ Epic story~ PRICE ~🔲 Free🔲 Underpriced🔲 Perfect Price✅ Could be cheaper🔲 Overpriced🔲 Complete waste of money~ REQUIREMENTS ~🔲 You can run it on a microwave✅ Average🔲 High end🔲 NASA computer~ LENGTH ~🔲 Very Short (0 - 3 hours)🔲 Short (3 - 15 hours)✅ Average (15-50 hours)🔲 Long (50-90 hours)🔲 Extremely long (90-110 hours)🔲 No ending~ FUN ~🔲 I'd rather watch paint dry🔲 Hard to enjoy🔲 Repetitive🔲 Actually pretty amusing✅ Ride of your life~ REPLAYABILITY~🔲 It's a one-time experience🔲 Only for achievements🔲 If you wait a few months/years✅ Definitely🔲 Infinitely replayable~ WORTH BUYING ~🔲 No✅ Wait for sale🔲 Yes----------------Psychonauts 2 is a long-awaited sequel to the cult classic Psychonauts, a 3D platformer that lets you explore the minds of various characters with psychic powers. The game follows Razputin Aquato, a 10-year-old aspiring psychic spy who joins the Psychonauts as an intern and gets involved in a conspiracy that threatens their existence.The game is a delight for fans of the original, as it brings back many familiar faces and locations, while also introducing new ones with their own quirks and secrets. The game's humor is witty and charming, with plenty of references and Easter eggs to spot. The game's story is also engaging and emotional, as it explores themes of family, identity, trauma and redemption.The gameplay is mostly similar to the first game, but with some improvements and additions. Raz can use his psychic abilities such as telekinesis, pyrokinesis, levitation and clairvoyance to navigate the levels and solve puzzles. He can also equip pins that modify his powers or give him cosmetic changes. The levels are varied and creative, each representing a different aspect of the character's psyche. Some levels are whimsical and colorful, such as a psychedelic music festival or a cooking show; others are dark and twisted, such as a hospital full of nightmares or a casino full of bad luck.Overall, Psychonauts 2 is an excellent game that lives up to its predecessor's legacy. It is a rare example of a sequel that improves on almost every aspect of the original without losing its charm or identity. It is also a game that celebrates diversity and empathy, as it shows us that everyone has their own struggles and dreams inside their heads. Psychonauts 2 is not only one of the best games of 2021; it is also one of the best games ever made.Psychonauts 2 gets an 8/10.For more reviews check my Steam profileHope you enjoyed my review, god bless you

The humor isn't as crude or mean spirited as in the first game (which was a bummer), and though there is a lot of creativity in the art direction, and plenty of surreal visuals, it doesn't quite get as surreal as the first game either (nothing will top the Milk Man Conspiracy). I also don't like the interns nearly as much as I liked the campers from the first game. The game still gets REALLY dark at times, but it's more serious instead of played for laughs. Still I appreciate that they didn't sacrifice gameplay in favor of narrative, a trend all to common these days... The platforming is still a blast. There's still a lot of fun things to collect. _childDocuments_.review: What can be said about Psychonauts 2 that hasn't already been said in every other positive review? Every part of 1 that was frustrating has been polished up and the new powers are a treat to use. I do have some complaints, the story feels a tad short for how much is thrown at the player in the last act and there's a lot of new characters that don't really get much room to breathe. Raz's peers have gone from deep characters that we constantly see around and learn something new about, to people who turn up when Raz needs someone to be mean to him or embarrassed around. They're fun when they ARE around, but we just don't see them do enough to make them as great as the peers from 1.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR Overall I believe the rose tinted goggles many of the fans of the cult classic are wearing means that I won't influence those who've spent hundreds of dollars on the crowd funding campaign. They need the game to be what they invested into. For everyone else, get the game on at least a 70% sale if you feel you want to play it, or watch someone else play through and save your money for a game worth your time. Review:Personally, I think that there is nothing in this game that will draw people back to replay it after beating it, that the poor writing/pacing are only appealing to fans who already beat the first game and are able/willing to fill in the gaps themselves, and that the game is either blitzed through just to beat it and not worth your money, or you'll play trying for 100 percent completion, you'll reach a point of boredom and then rush to beat it or stop playing. The attempt at continuation after the VR only sequel to 1 is recapped in game with a regression in most of the character's personalities away from being fleshed out to becoming rather bland and plain. The story as other reviews will note is worthwhile only if you've been invested in the series, which is there is a mole in the psychic spy agency, and the only one who can save the day is the mentor character and his friends. Notice I didn't say main character there, your role in this story is to fix bolster everyone else, be subtly considered the mole, and be the hypocrite who is told not to try to “fix people”, who then proceeds to fix people to help magically save the day. The game itself is combat focused and the humor is at best a sad chuckle at random one liners that are as forgettable as what you had for dinner a week ago. Don't expect this game to pander to anyone not already a fan. The sad reality is that if you remove the collectibles (which are only needed if you like seeing the numbers go up and have the tacked on “upgrades” to your moves), you have no reason to appreciate the interesting and pretty visuals, and will get just far enough into the game to get bored and be unable to get a refund. I will say after reading many of the positive reviews, that the “focus on the healing of mental damage” is a theme in this game, literally to a cliché degree that makes Saturday morning cartoons feel like adult themed content. It does tickle a nostalgia bone for many people, and it does tackle adult problems in an almost naive and joyful happy ending redemption way. Many of the “plot twists” aren't really unexpected, though some of the clues are really obvious when doing one of the side conversations that aren't needed to advance the game. As far as aspects that don't really fit in anywhere else. There are only 3 or 4 side quests in the whole game. The music is orchestral, and can either be amazing or just boring depending on how you feel about that type of thing. Anita Sarkeesian was a consultant on the game, and while no politics are preached, sudden moments like a gay wedding scene or the fact that many diverse strong female characters are being more capable or show affection through punching all seem like ways to try to subtlety point out “Hey, we're not going to cram our beliefs down your throat, but this is what we think, it's normal to have it this way now”. There are game breaking bugs still, there are many places that you can get the main character where he shouldn't be, some people have lost progress, and this game appears to be console focused. There are options to become invincible, do extra damage, and basically skip combat. There is a point of no return for the first 3 areas that you can't go back until after beating the game. There is a reference to Gir from Invader Zim.

_childDocuments_.review: Psychonauts 2 doesn't quite have the freshness of the first game, and I also think the self-contained world of Whispering Rock Psychic Summer Camp works better than the Motherlobe, the Psychonauts HQ introduced in the sequel. Nonetheless, if Psychonauts 2 didn't quite bowl me over the way the first one did, it's still a more than welcome return to this world and its characters. I have some quibbles - one or two levels are less inspired than others and border on the incoherent, there's no utter standout like the Milkman levels in the first game, and the final confrontation and aftermath seem a bit rushed - but Psychonauts is still one of my favourite games of the year and absolutely a virtual world I want to hang out with. Double Fine has clearly put a lot of love in their game, and it's impossible not to feel this love when running around as Raz Aquato once again. And while the story comes to a proper end, I do hope that this isn't the last we've seen of the Psychonauts universe.

_childDocuments_.review: I feel that I was fortunate in just playing Psychonauts for the first time a few weeks ago - I only had to finish that game before I could play this one, instead of having to wait for 15 years. I very much enjoyed Psychonauts 2, but to be honest, if I had waited that long for it, I probably would've found it to be fairly underwhelming.To be clear, I had a lot of fun with Psychonauts 2! It was absolutely gorgeous, the levels were bright and crisp, and the visuals were truly a delight. The music was wonderful, and the story, though simple, was engaging enough to keep me interested. The platforming was fun, the combat was adequate, and the collectibles and side missions were usually fun to hunt down rather than frustrating. All in all, it was everything I would want in a platformer/adventure game.However, I do have a couple of fairly major grips with Psychonauts 2. The levels themselves were a bit hit or miss - I feel like sometimes they went for quantity over quality. While the visuals and stories of each level were great, I felt that the gameplay started to feel a bit same-y after the first few. There just wasn't enough variety in how the levels played.Additionally, I thought that Psychonauts 2 struggled with tone at times. This game deals with some pretty heavy topics. I wish that they would have let those hit a bit harder, it's a little difficult to take a discussion about alcoholism or depression seriously when its interrupted by a "witty" quip or the kazoo sound of picking up a collectible. I think the topics discussed could've been better utilized if they leaned into them a bit more, but I do applaud Double Fine for broaching these topics in the first place.Overall, I found Psychonauts 2 to be a good time, but I don't think it's better than the original. If you're a fan of the first game, I think you'll enjoy it - just set expectations accordingly.

_childDocuments_.review: Story spoiler-free review below!If you're coming straight from playing the first game, there will be a bit of adjustment to the controls you'll need to get used to, but I believe the changes make it overall a tighter platformer. If falling off of ledges makes you frustrated, you can turn off fall damage. If you feel the enemies are being absolutely relentless, you can turn on invincibility. I never ended up using these, but I can't say I wasn't ever tempted. It's nice that they're there for people who are struggling, or just want to chill out and enjoy everything else this game has to offer (which is a LOT). The game feels, for the most part, fair in its challenges though. Leveling up abilities is satisfying in how much stronger it makes you feel, and between that and buying pins you can really choose how you want to buff combat strategies for different enemies. Or just pet the animals and have rainbow trails on your punches. Whichever. It's a bit more linear within the levels compared to the first game, so collecting everything your first time through a mind is often impossible (many areas seal off when you enter the next one as you progress). That said, cleanup is way easier when you do get to reenter minds, since the areas within each brain are fairly self contained as a result. I think the impact this design decision has on the story each mind tells is worth it. My advice if you like to 100% collectibles? Play through each mind as you want the first time and enjoy the story beats fully without worrying about grabbing everything. Then come back to collect the rest. There is a post game too, so though there are some "point of no return"s (and the game will warn you!), you're never truly locked out from 100%ing the game. In fact, there are some overworld collectibles that you CAN'T get until the post-game (looking at you, doors with mailslots).The story and writing is again A++. Talk to every NPC at LEAST once - some of the most unexpected will have dialogue trees of absolutely hilarious content. The endgame twists and turns are surprising and satisfying, while feeling connected to everything that was set up earlier in the game. Many heartwarming and wholesome moments throughout, but some absolutely dark ones as well that ground the story and make it feel meaningful. I absolutely devoured this game. I'm sure I'll come back for seconds, once my memories fade a little, so I can discover it all over again.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow. The first Psychonauts is a pretty formative game for me. I first played it on release more than 15 years ago as I was exited by a console platformer from the people that made Full Throttle, one of my favorite classic Point and Clicks. Psychonauts stuck with me because it was the one of the early times that a console game showed heart and humor above anything that had come before. Then Brutal Legend and a host of Double Fine productions came out over the years and were just that... fine. By the time Psychonauts 2 landed and was on my radar, I had zero faith that Double Fine had it in them to attempt to reignite a classic. Well they did it, and they did it well. I'm genuinely gobsmacked. The core of Psychonauts is still there. DF did not attempt to break the wheel and reinvent it at all. They made a genuine sequel that builds on the original in every way possible. Gameplay, innovation, creativity, character, and story. All there and better than ever. Rarely has a fun family platformer captured the same spirit, humor, and tenderness as some of the best Dreamworks/Pixar films out there, but Double Fine did it with this sequel. My only complaint is that P2 nearly felt too long, but humor and heart for miles isn't a bad thing. 10/10, well done.

_childDocuments_.review: I think my biggest mistake was to play this right after finishing the first one. It makes the flaws and issues so much more apparent. Here's a summary;Pros;1-Vibrant, colorful world2- fluid gameplay, responsive controls3-  Interesting story and intriguing plot twist. I got the feels in a few of the Ford quests.4- some lovable and unique character designs, and it was nice to see the old characters back!5-  Sound design is spot on and fits very wellCons;1- The newly introduced sidecharacters are lackluster, mean and boring. I felt nothing for them, and wanted to skip almost every dialoge they had. Most of every other character without a role looked like a muppet.2- The game has gotten much more child friendly, which isn't necessarily a bad thing since it is a game for children... But most of the humour the old game had is gone, and you're constantly handheld and backseated the entire game. 3- The levitation skills have been so nerfed it's almost sad. Even fully upgraded, there's hardly any difference...4- The game felt short, and it felt like there was nothing to do but the main story most of the time. I might not have been able to trigger some events, but honestly the game felt so empty..5- I began getting bored early on, but the main story kept me playing. It felt like such a dissapointment considering how much I enjoyed the first game.---So, honestly? I was pretty bummed out. But for a child, or someone who hasn't played the first game in a while, I fully reccomend the game!There was so little to do. So few minds to explore. So little character interaction with anyone, and what little you got were just Raz being belittled or abused by almost everyone around him. When the other 'interns' were redeemed, I still fully despised them, and felt nothing for them. The same goes for the older siblings and your mother.  In the first game, you were basically only bullied by two people, but that was the steriotypical bully pair. Even though there was a lot of side characters, you still wanted to save them in the end, or listen to their dialog.  I can still remeber half of the names of the people you met in the first game, but nobody in the second, at least the side characters.I have a lot more to say, but I feel like it'll be too nitpicky. so I'll leave it at that.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: This is probably the closest thing to a perfect sequel I can think of. Everything I loved about the first psychonauts is here and some more. All the dialogue that's somehow sarcastic and sincere at the same time, the goofy character design, the amazing environmental storytelling. Honestly the way this game handles not only mental illness, but relationships, group dynamics, and coping mechanisms I'd be suprised if this wasn't referenced in some type of psyche class. The weakest parts of this game are probably the combat and platforming and they're not even bad, the writing just outshines them.The platforming can be hit or miss sometimes but I was never bored or majorly stuck in any area. it all moves at a very good pace and is constantly introducing new elements and aspects, its just no Super Mario or anything. When it comes to combat I've heard in other reviews that its nothing special, and I'll admit its not the hardest, But the amount of enemy variety and the way each power factors into combat I was always happy to jump back into it especially in the latter half of the game. Also pretty much every boss is awesome, can't really think of a bad or lame one.The only two "complaints" I have is there are WAY too many fragments and the pin system is a little under-cooked but still cool nevertheless. I think two more pin slots would've helped and maybe cheaper prices. But bedsides that this game is stellar. 8.5-9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game, I really did. I did a 100% run of Psychonauts just before playing this, intending to play them back to back. After playing this game for several hours (I was offline on my Deck for most of it, so it doesn't show on my profile), here is my conclusion....If you liked the first game, don't ruin it by playing this one. I don't see why this game is so well received. It's just a mostly typical 3D platformer, running on Unreal.The music uses motifs from the first game, which would normally be charming, except they're used for mostly unrelated things, which kills the effect.The story.....oh where do I start. It's basically a cookie cutter style checklist. Cringe moments with family members that don't have a good reason to be present? Check. Tough boss? Check. Very obvious plot twists? Check. School bullies? Check.Speaking of school.... The psychonauts are an elite group of secret agents. Why are they somehow a school now??When Raz is bullied or mistreated by anyone, he doesn't even react. He just acts like it's all normal and fine, and still hangs out with the bullies afterward.The game will also force you to do things that are clearly bad, and that you may not even want to do. Bad design, in my opinion.And finally.... The level design is pretty bad, too. Many of the levels are small but very tedious. They are also not very friendly to the Steam Deck, as some things are pretty hard to see. The level designers also have an odd obsession with the....grotesque.Overall, the game just feels uninspired and subcontracted. It's a harmless game to let a child play, but there's little value for anyone older. I would say the original game is superior in nearly every way. And that's saying a lot, because I had to fight to get it to work on my Deck. But it was a far more enjoyable experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: I have been one of the biggest fanboys of Psychonauts ever since my mom got me the first game for the Xbox when I was a child. I grew up always thinking that there was no way in hell that they would make a sequal to one of the most unique and enjoyable experiences you can have because of its cult status. Even when they announced it was in development years ago I still was in disbelief, especially seeing how long the game was delayed.But here we are now, the wait has finally paid off. The game so far has shattered my expectations into a million beautiful pieces. It still holds the original spirit of the game but improves upon its predecessor in almost everyway possible. It shows that the extra time and money that they spent on this game was well worth it. The level of polish and detail is incredible. By no means could you compare it to the new Ratchet and Clank games in terms of graphic fidelity, but the art and design in Psychonauts 2 is a shining example of creativity and genius that is not seen very often in the cookie cutter game industry that we now have.You can notice the love and devotion that Tim Schaefer and the rest of the Team at Double Fine put into this world, and it really shows even a few hours in. I'm more than happy to support a game studio that supports their team. Here's hoping that more studios follow suite with a no crunch policy because I genuinely believe that having a mentally well team is the secret ingredient to success when all of your resources are tight.Thank you Double Fine, I think this game is something that a lot of us needed recently. I haven't played too much so I will update my review as soon as I finish.

_childDocuments_.review: I played and loved the original Psychonauts when it was released. This is everything a sequel should be. It improves on the original while maintaining the environment. The game looks fantastic and plays like a dream. I am tempted to fire up the original again after playing this.So what is new? There are a couple of new powers. I particularly liked the little clone you could make, that solved a number of puzzles. If you play the game you know something like this is going to happen, but when the ability finally arrives it is implemented much better than I expected.Level design is just incredible. You can see why the game took so long to make. There is just so much detail in so many locations. The quality is just phenomenal.And guess what? The game doesn't crash! Yet that's right. I played this game all the way through, and am still carrying on after finishing the main quest, and it hasn't crashed once. This is the first new release I have bought in years that hasn't been full of bugs. So well done to the team led by Tim Schafer. He can be justifiably pleased with himself over this game, he has done the original proud.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the few games where I had so much fun and enjoyment I was genuinely smiling most of my playthrough. I can't believe they've done it and made a sequel that's a genuine improvement on everything that made the first game so memorable.Probably the most amazing thing about Psychonauts 2 is that compared to its' predecesor, its' quality and creativity is consistent throughout the whole adventure. There's never a dull moment, a level that feels weaker. While we may not have standouts like some of the popular 'brains' from the first game, it just means in 2, they're all fun to play through and memorable for their own right. So much care went into making sure that these levels are not also enjoyable but also woven into the story and this game does it with a lot more confidence than the first game which speaks a lot about its' improved writing as well. Seriously, all the characters and their dialogue are great (Raz is still one of the best if not the best video game protagonists), there are so many moments when I ended up chuckling!If you are a fan of the first game, don't even think about it and grab this, you will not be disappointed. If you are and you are looking for a cool platformer with a focus on exploration and story with themes of psychic meddling and solving mental issues, mixed in with Bond-esque spy bits and a soundtrack to match, give this a shot (better yet, start with the first game).Psychonauts really is the Incredibles of gaming.

_childDocuments_.review: I've 100% completed the game with all collectibles with rank 102. There's nothing left in the game for me.This game is probably one of the better games I've played the past few years. The dialogue is fantastic, the story is gripping, the gameplay itself is fun and entertaining. The analogies being made throughout the story, the environment that plays into it, the small subtle things that you could very easily miss but love when you don't... they're enough to make you cry your heart out or laugh depending on the who's consciousness you're in.The game isn't long per say. You could probably rush through it in a few hours if you don't care about collectibles. I think it's about the right length honestly. It doesn't drag on when it shouldn't and it does when it needs to for effect.The music and sound in this game is ridiculously good. I can't think of a single thing they did wrong or could have done better.The story is extremely well-made, especially considering the first one. They tied it together better than I thought they would. But it's not without its issues... For example, Loboto is supposedly scared to reveal his plan early on in the game and it's speculated it's because he had "help" and that he's scared. Later on in the game, this becomes sort of questionable. Unfortunately, that's never truly resolved and it's left up to the player to speculate instead. There's a couple others that are sort of questionable but reasonable. It's just enough to not make it perfect (but still very very good).The gameplay is most certainly fun but... and I hate to say this... it ends up being a button masher to an extent. There are certain enemies that you simply cannot do that with which is fantastic. It forces you to use all of your abilities. There's really only two enemies that are like that, the rest you can just mash your face into the controller. However, that doesn't happen until a bit later in the game. In addition, the bosses often don't encourage button mashing and actually encourage you to use your brain a bit. However, they don't totally disallow you to button mash and you'll defeat the boss either way. The platforming and the dialogue are both much stronger suites in this game. The environment itself has puzzles that aren't kidding around in how to do them, they'll make you scratch your head for at least a few minutes. Because of the allowed button mashing, the score lowers a bit to an 9/10. Fun, rewarding, but not perfect and hard to lose.The collectibles in the game are... okay. Some of them you'll probably never find no matter how hard you look. I will say that the two collectibles I *had* to look up were exceptionally difficult to find. The rest I think were fairly reasonable. The biggest killer I think is the figments. I can't remember what the original game did here, but if you are missing one figment in the whole map, good luck finding it. It might not be listed in the figment book (it only lists specific types of figments, if you haven't gotten that type, you won't know what type of figment is missing). The figments are also not very context bound. For example, a figment that looks like a cake might be in a Backstage area or the Concessions area (you would think it would be in Concessions). I wish the figments were a tad more intuitive but it's a niche part of the game ultimately.The dialogue is the best. The delivery of all the dialogue is perfect, especially in regards to humor. It makes you want to listen to all the dialogue options while forcing nothing onto you (though, see the Lili caveat below). The map / environment has one big issue and that is it's too easy to manipulate. You can accidentally skip over sections of the map and not even know it, to the point it causes bugs. Speed runners will have an absolute field day with it, but I don't think it should have affected casual players. In addition, you can get to portions of the map that just feel empty. Things in the map can be very well hidden but if something is just difficult to get to, they won't put anything there. I understand why but there's a distinct lack of easter eggs to fill in the blank space. I wish they put team photos, some neat non-collectibles there, or something so it felt like you achieved something while not actually being required to 100% the game. While I'm giving the story an 8/10, the creativity in some of the maps are through the roof, to the point of being beautiful. I just don't know if they contributed as much to gameplay as it should have is all. The game also has a few noticeable invisible walls where some can be a bit frustrating. You'll see something you want, try to get to it, but blast it, there's an invisible wall and no obvious signs of how to get over there otherwise.And lastly, I don't like Lili as a character. I wouldn't mind if she's childish (because she's a child) but she's frankly stupid and annoying. She does things in the game that makes you place your palm to your face. She is the "most fake" character in the game if you can relate to that. All the other characters were distinct and the intention seems to be that their personality had traits that you could relate to or at least try to understand. Lili has none of that. This applied to the first game too and I don't really want to take too much off of the score for it since she's the only recurring kid from the first game (aside from Raz) and it takes place days after the first game... not much they could have done there if they wanted to keep consistency. She's not a large portion of the game either, but she is important to the story.Overall, this game should more than qualify for Game of the Year.Overall: 9/10Characters: 9/10Gameplay: 9/10Graphics: 7/10 (feels a touch dated but still very much has charm, I don't grade graphics heavily here)Audio: 10/10Environment / Map: 8/10Story: 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of the original game, I enjoyed Psychonauts 2, and it wasn't much of a pain to 100% during the first playthrough and didn't make me tired or sick of playing. As someone who suffers from color deficiency, there were some fragments that I had difficulty seeing the first time without a guide, but I still managed to find them in the end.The only thing that I didn't like was that they changed Raz from being confident and sure of his choices to being a meek pushover. Having watched Rhombus of Ruin on YouTube, due to not having a VR Headset, I do not believe that anything happened to Raz to cause this change in personality.I also feel that the studio was trying to be  careful with trying to make sure that the mental crises that Raz encountered weren't offending. Psychonauts 2 didn't feel as free and whimsical as the first game did, but I would much rather have this Psychonauts 2 than nothing at all.All in all, 34+ hours very well spent. I don't know that I would recommend anyone else spend $60 on this title, but at the same time, buying at full price may lead to Double Fine working on more of their historically fantastic games.

_childDocuments_.review: Spectacular game, all around.  There are plenty of reviews that go into all the detail - but some of the "little things" I found most welcome:1)  No part of the game was frustratingly difficult.  Challenging, yes.  But unlike the game's predecessor, there were no points that put me in a "ragequit" mood.  The most difficult portions of the game took me perhaps three or four tries - but never more than that.2) When you quit the game, the interface displays the expected "You will lose all progress since your last save" message, like any other game.  However Psychonauts 2 also tells you how many minutes and seconds it's been since your last save.  So simple, and so useful.3)  Holy hell ... Psychonauts 2 lets you PAUSE CUTSCENES!  Yes!  If you're in the middle of a long cutscene, and the phone rings, you can PAUSE the cutscene, and resume!  I've literally never encountered this in any other game.Seriously -- I cannot recommend this game highly enough.  Graphics, story, dialogue, gameplay, characters ... it's all there, and it's all amazing.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely incredible sequel ripe with highly memorable artistic worlds, characters teeming with personalities, and one of a kind designs and creativity. This game's wordplay, symbolism, and thematics are some of the best and most unique I've seen in any game to date - even when compared to its predecessor. There are non-euclidean environments and weird concepts that expand in bizarre and allegorical ways as you progress, always hiding collectibles and lore to those with more keen eyes. This game - in my opinion - is and has been heavily slept on by the gaming community. In some ironic way, this game was memory holed and I'm genuinely surprised that it hasn't generated memes or content publicly stirred from this series in any mainstream way. I know people who loved the original, and didn't even know a sequel existed.Jack Black makes a VA return, along with all of the wonderful voices from the original series. Tim Schafer hit a grand slam with this one, and I hope they continue on with this project, and/or Brutal Legend. While the combat isn't the most interesting, and there are areas I wished they would have expanded upon further (more pin options, more equip-able slots for loadouts, Easter eggs impacting gameplay, etc.), the set-pieces and bosses more than make up for it. Definitely give this game a chance if you love scavenger platformers with quirky gameplay mechanics. It's short and sweet, and really highlights what a talented non-artistically bankrupt studio can commit to reality when supported and fostered.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

Just remember, the main character is a kid, and you may connect a few dots before he does, despite his advanced psychic abilities.I may be biased, but I liked this game enough to 100% it, despite the figments being a pain in the butt to find. They really should have had some collectible finder that you can buy at the end game. I don't see why Otto couldn't make something.

_childDocuments_.review: The perfect sequel to the original! To make a new game, on new technology, and make it feel sooo much like the original in terms of controls, is mind-blowing to me. Now imagine making a game, but every "level", you throw out all your artwork, and make a complete new set? That's Psychonauts!  A lot of work went into this one, and it shows. All the different characters are well developed, and interesting, and piecing together all the different details of the main story, through the experiences of everyone involved is a lot of fun. And then there's all the "extracurricular" stuff you can do outside the missions, just like in the original. Pros:* More Psychonauts! A worthy successor. * Interesting story* Very creative, and interesting level designs. * Good atmosphere* More dynamic and interesting combat.* Plenty to explore, and secrets to find.* A whale called "Esmerelda"Cons:* Controls can be a bit frustrating sometimes: for instance, jump distance can be hard to judge at certain spots. * Lacks some more "puzzle"-like minds, where you go back and forth finding a solution. Most minds in 2 are fairly linear.To me, psychonauts 2 is a game about compassion, and I think we all could use a bit more of that right now.

_childDocuments_.review: Still got some ways to go in the game but I think I’ve played enough to make a preliminary review.To put it succinctly, Psychonauts 2 is a fantastic sequel to a beloved cult classic that I’ve been waiting over a decade for. The most impressive thing is how even after 16 years Double Fine didn’t skip a single beat, this feels so much like a natural extension of the first game, just picking up where it left off. Like I feel in some alternate timeline where we got this game a few years after the first during the 360/PS3 gen it wouldn’t have been too far off in spirit.The game is a bigger, better, and more polished follow-up to the first in every way and is one of the finest 3D platformers in recent years. Definitely one of the must play games of the year, I couldn’t be happier.

_childDocuments_.review: A truly joyous game. They don't make them like this anymore. No season pass, no micro-transactions, no bullsh*t. Just true old school platforming joy. Great graphics, great story, and full of charm. If you loved the Nintendo 64 days of platforming (Banjo-Kazoo + Mario), but want a modern polish, then you'll love this. If you played the first Psychonauts, then don't hesitate to buy this. It's a worthy successor.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: It's a really interesting companion piece to the original game, simply put, but it has a different overall feel tonally as well as a different set of strengths and weaknesses. I think it's better written but less funny than the original - if the original was like a really good episode of Invader Zim or The Grim Adventures of Billy and Mandy (edgy dark humor that is still appropriate for kids though a little lol so randum at times), this is much more like modern Pixar - Inside Out is a pretty obvious reference point, but I think pretty obvious comparisons can also be made to Up, generally there is a darker and more mature / sincere coming of age story at play about personal responsibility, though it is very impressive in how it seems to manage to tie up all of the plot holes the original game had while seemingly potentially leaving room for a sequel (though I would be somewhat surprised). It's also nice that even if, like me, you didn't play the VR game they made between this and the original, it doesn't really matter all that much as you're able to get the gist of it. Other strengths the game has over the original are in regard to it's music and visuals. Obviously it's a much prettier game than the original - the original was often ugly looking for a PS2 game, forget by today's standards - but they did a great job with trippy visual effects and cutscenes here too, and the music is a lot more memorable than it is in the original, with everything from Jack Black doing psych rock musical numbers to beautiful acoustic folk BGM and the most intentionally annoying fake national anthem I've ever heard (still stuck in my head days after completing it). However, I don't think it's actually quite as good a game as the original. It can be a bit rough around the edges at times - The game glitched so hard I had to exit and re-enter it twice from me just doing ordinary stuff, which is something that never happened with the original for me (I am, however, glad it has a very generous autosave feature) and there are numerous physics-based jank issues here and there - but my main issue is just that the levels themselves aren't quite as memorable as the highlights from the original game - cool moments are usually down to the aforementioned visual effects as opposed to actually interesting level design decisions, like in the Milkman Conspiracy or the Risk / Spanish Art-based levels, so if you're looking for more of that, you're not gonna find it here. In addition to this, I didn't find the collectathon elements as compelling this time, which is down to a few different factors (lots of backtracking involved once you get the last two PSI powers, hub world being way bigger than in the original, there just being much more of them in general etc.).In saying all this though, I still think it's a pretty essential companion piece for all but the most retro-purist fans of the original game, but you absolutely should play the original first.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing sequel to an amazing game. A game that explores adult themes of alcoholism, drug use, depression, sex, love, war, etc. and their impact on our state of mind through sadness, loneliness, fear, judgement, anxiety, and more. All wrapped up in a story that delivers and dives into those topics using a cartoon-like art style, abstraction of themes, perspective changes and clever game mechanics.A superb and unique game that will for ever be in the gaming history Hall of Fame.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: This Is indeed what we were waiting for!My favorite character is the goth chick who's creepy and knows it, but ultimately has a great heart, Lizzie.It was a blast to see Raz working side by side with Ford and Lili in the last two levels, and of course one cannot leave without mentioning the total Feast for the Senses that was Psi-King's Sensorium (I especially loved the Yellow Submarine references).Not to mention, using the mental metaphors presented in this game has made it easier to sort out my own emotional baggage (Dufflebag tag, anyone?)Fanfic writers, get your pens out! Anyone who was a fan of the first, or just loves a good platformer in general should thoroughly enjoy this romp through the minds of Schafer & Co.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: BEST GAME OF ALL TIME. the first Psychonauts was a perfect game. Then they released Rhombus of Ruin. BANGER. Then they top it all off with the perfect sequel, bringing back EVERYTHING THAT MADE THE ORIGINAL GOOD, GETTING RID OF EVERYTHING THAT MADE THE ORIGINAL BAD, AND ADDING NEW THINGS TO MAKE IT EVEN BETTER. _childDocuments_.review: This game is a near to complete Masterpiece. I loved this game from the beginning to the end and I believe that it's a perfect sequel to the Original Psychonauts. _childDocuments_.review: Psychonauts 2 is a masterpiece. Amazingly fun and inventive. Actually funny, even despite the usual Doublefine puns. Perfectly stable, even when playing in widescreen or when using 5.1 surround. The music really makes this game special, I don't think I've ever heard such a diverse and entertaining score. I still have the Grulovia song stuck in my head. The game feels like just the right length, and well paced. The one improvement it could easily make is having a harder difficulty setting - I figured one was unlockable at the end, like a new game + mode, but there wasn't any. _childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: Psychonauts 2 is a very well crafted sequel to the nearly 20 year old first part. The very anticipated sequel holds up really well, and introduces fun mechanics paired with a well crafted story.Gameplay wise, this game is a simple platformer and collect a ton. The gameplay is rather slow paced compared to other similar titles. The movement and combat feels fluid and is easy to control. There are a bunch of different abilities for Raz to unlock, I would have wished to have a different way of accessing them, or to equip more simultaneously.Story wise the game is quite interesting, it picks up right after the first one, (and a VR title, that can cause some confusion for other people if unknown). It features a wide cast of likeable (and unlikeable) characters and ties back nicely into the whole family plot that the first game set up.The levels in this are somewhat weaker in my opinion, if compared with my favorite one from the first game, the napoleon level. While it doesn't reach the same heights as the first one, the levels and their design are still really well done and polished and offer a lot of variety.I'd definitely recommend this game to everyone that enjoys quirky platformers
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: there are no words for how perfect this game is even on its own, but it is an absolute gold standard for continuing any piece of cult classic media. it's very clear that the team that worked on this game not only loved what they were doing to death, they also listened very closely to what the fans loved about the first game and then expanded on all of it. in fact they learned from and fixed so many of the short comings of the first game (seriously the conveyance in the first game is a mess. i didn't have to google a single thing just to finish this one, though!)its hypocritical of me to say since i waited for a sale but i think this game is fully worth the $60 price tag. _childDocuments_.review: Extremely well polished. Has plenty for old fans to lean on whilst also allowing new players to join the story without having massive exposition dumps thrown on top of them. Its a fantastic melting pot with absolutely nothing forced! I am a VERY huge critic of games that USE their games as a platform to share their views, this game actually just creates a fantastic story that just so happens to have humans who do human things without going "HEY LOL OMG WE DO THIS AND THAT TOTALLY ACCEPTABLE LOLOLLOLOLOLOL TOTALLY INCLUSIVE!!!!" Nah its literally just a emotional and VERY well written story. Please support them and get ready for a psychedelic ride which i personally believe has been missing for recent released games. TY for reading. Be well. It is worth every penny.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, I loved this game. Well worth whatever price you can get it for. You got Jack Black, very crazy easter eggs, literal giant eggs, madmen in shower caps, and enough psychic baggage to make YOU wanna go to a therapist.But joking anecdotes aside; this game is a real page turner. Each person you can enter the mind of has a unique mental drawback that is almost line for line actual mental issues. The game has you work through the issues of others and is a good self reflection. _childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: This game has been stuck in my library since Jan 2, 2023 and I have finally finished it. But before playing this game, I wanted to play the prequel which I enjoyed so much because the humor, the character, and the story that I experienced made me feel like I was a kid again on my Playstation. It had such a nostalgia feel to the game.Now after fully completing Psychonauts 1, I started Psychonauts 2 and some of the dialogue did not make sense to me. That was when I realized there was another game (for VR) in between which was the Rhombus of Ruin, a very short game so I just watched a playthrough online. But if you want to play Psychonauts 2 for the first time WITHOUT playing the prequels, it's fine. The game gives you an animated recap at the start of your adventure.Psychonauts 2 is the perfect sequel and a masterpiece of a platformer + collectathon. It works on everything that the original had to offer and adds on to it with an amazing spin on the gameplay and story. PROS:- The characters are all unique, most have good writing, they have extra dialogue that expounds on the story and they also banter with each other.- Character development especially with Raz (Asking for consent after the Hollie incident)- Plot Twists (Mostly good)- Platforming aspect is always fun along with the PSI powers.- People who would want to 100% the game have an in-game checklist and you'll know if an area is cleared of all collectables. (A completionists dream)- Being inclusive to the LGBTQ+ community- Level designs and map transitions - UPGRADES UPGRADES UPGRADES- Wonderful take on what goes on in people's minds (Mental issues/illnesses)- A lot of humor and meme references- References from the previous games- Esmeralda the WhaleSo much moreCONS:- With what Psychonauts 1 and 2 had to offer for story-wise, I don't think we'll be getting a 3rd game.- Combat can be a clunky at times.- The Infamous Bob's bottles banana figmentOverall - Slightly better than a mouthful of nails/10
