_childDocuments_.review: A very worthy successor to everyone's favorite psychotherapy simulator, Psychonauts 2 brings back all those fun mechanics from the first game and many more, such as modular, equippable upgrades in addition to the normal leveling upgrade system, which has itself been tweaked such that you can now choose what order they come in. Get to know Raz's family, the history of his homeland (or rather, the country his family most recently lived in; the thing about the Roma is that they don't *have* a homeland, you see), and just how much of a *negative* impact a psychonaut can have if they aren't careful.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game very much. The story line is absolutely the best part of the game with twists and turns that even if you can predict some of them somehow find a way to subvert the expectation through the ride along the way. The Game play has many great elements and features that are modern and feel like a proper sequel. The introductions of new thematic enemies is really well received, and is a fun premise. Now this is the part where I mention the games biggest flaws. The gameplay is good, but I'd honestly say I prefer the first game much more. Several mechanics are introduced in interesting ways only to seemingly be ineffective or outright meaningless later on. Along the same line, some advancements seem to have no flavor to them asides from being #Different. Several Abilities were scrapped from the first game to this one as well, including the ability to use and cycle through items. Dialogue feels almost entirely optional, the fighting takes a lot longer and doesn't seem as effective, and you're left constantly switching abilities in the middle of battle or tanking damage.The Supporting Cast is very Very flat, but tries very hard to convince you they're interesting and memorable to the point I'd literally entirely forgotten one of them existed until the showed up at the end of the game. The Map layout is REALLY GOOD, but the collectible placement leaves much to be desired being very difficult to find without google, but absolutely not impossible. Speaking of Collectibles! The Pins, and Other things available through the Otto-matic (the in-game shop) are entirely flavor text. They don't feel like something you'd have any real desire to try out unless you're like me and 100% the game, Even then I only bought them all for the achievement, ESPECIALLY THE CAMERA! Which has no other use than to take screenshots!Everything being said, I would play this game through again. The Main characters are absolutely lively, relatable, and so very interesting (though perhaps suffering a little sequelitis). The Story is top notch. The Art is true to the original, and I had fun playing and Streaming this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Psychonauts 2 is the long, long, long awaited sequel to the 2005 classic and it delivers. The creative level concepts of the first game are still on the table but bolstered by a much stronger art style and level of detail to the visuals that's equal parts beautiful and disturbing. The gameplay is a HUGE improvement from the original with much finer controls for platforming and an actual combat system. But the thing that caught me most by surprise was the story. The different mental disorders explored in this game are handled with great care and there's multiple emotional moments that have really stuck with me.It makes me extremely happy to see that Double Fine was able to fully put to page what they've always wanted to with this series. The first Psychonauts was this mangled web of quirks and fun ideas that when mixed together was a unique experience, but one that I thought could be so much more if given the time to grow. Cut to 15+ years later and I think they finally nailed it with their... second entry into the series. Glad to see that the time was well spent.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll swing back around and give some commendations because Psychonauts 2 has plenty of positives, to the point where if you just made a list based on pure good vs bad, the good would seem to completely eclipse the short comings. HOWEVER, it feels like this was made by someone who forgot what a video game even is. Barrelling past some smaller gripes, the central issue with Psychonauts 2 is the sheer pretension. Every five seconds seconds of gameplay is interrupted by cutscenes. I'm not talking about over world story progression, I'm talking about the levels. Play a small segment, get a cutscene. Walk literally five feet quick cutscene to establish the new scenery. Cutscene for set pieces, cut scene for you name it. It's mind boggling how obstructured actual game play is at any given moment, and even more infuriating, the levels are designed around this segmented design. Most--not all-- levels are short sixty second obstacle courses and then you get telaported to the next one. I was curious how you could even replay levels designed like this, and it turns out you just get a teleport option to play each tiny chunk. The core design is so grand, so up it's own butt. The first, what? Three hours? The first three hours of this game is completely on the rails with no overworld exploration, no stage that attempts to be cohesive. I was actually miserable at first. And while it gets better, you better beleive it never goes away. There was such an emphasis on produtction value and constantly showing you how crazy and weird the world are that the developers literally forgot to let you play the game. Which is highly ironic because being up their own butts made me hate the levels. I really want to emphasize this. There were sections where I could not possibly explain why control was taken away from me. Dialgoue? I can listen as I platform? Want to show me a view? I can see it; you really don't need to. Past that, the overall pacing and structuring is janky. Like I mentioned, the first three hours was on the rails. And even when you unlock the over world, it's structured around 3 stages. This means the majority of powers you have going into it, and by the time you get additional exploration abilities, you're locked out until the post game. You lack that joy of exploration where you see something and you can't get it and then you come back stronger with new abilities. A collectathon is thrust on you for two hours and then it's over. And again I emphasize, there was no reason for this. It's unconscionable that the developer thought: let's make sure they can't explore for most of the game. So focused on their own vision how they wanted the game experience they forgot to structure it like a video game. We're almost done with the negatives. I'll also throw some general negativity toward some stage design, combat, and difficulty. The game is very easy with a lot of what's being asked of the player not properly balanced around your powers. But combat gets ratcheted up which is an abysmal choice. It's not deep, just annoying. Time for some glowing praise:1) The ambition of the game is insane.2) It's gorgeous and creative, especially the stages. 3) The way powers are implemented as a sequel is refreshing. You don't have to reearn anything and they still found an on rap to create progression and make it not feel like you started on the plateau. Not perfect, but still a bold choice that worked. 4) The story. If there is one thing that didn't work about the first game, it was the story. This game takes it past competent to surprising. It's still relatively simple in the way a game structured as this is can be, but I give full points to what they worked in here. Overall, so many elements that are sterling on their own right fall flat and I put the fault squarely on the game direction. Not to get too personal here, but it feels like a George Lucas situation with the natural restraints and needing to rely on others. You write that man a blank check and it's a nightmare. Which isn't even to say that this director's track record is impeachable when working on smaller projects. Brutual Legends is just a cocophany of: "Why would you design this."I digress. As someone who loved the original (I say as someone who isn't nostalgic because I played the original three years ago) I'm not sure this is worth you're time. It's fine. There's some cool stuff to see, but you'll be trudging through it. 5/10

_childDocuments_.review: I played Psychonauts 2 right after the original game, and the comparison between the two despite the amount of time between them is an interesting one. As a side note that span of time is is even lampshaded in game somewhat, which is funny. But when looking at the two side by side, as well as how much I enjoyed them, I'm forced to confront the question: is Psychonauts 2 a better game than 1?I would say yes. 2 fixed a lot of the issues 1 had, using a lot of modern sensibilities and quality of life while still maintaining the cleverness, imagination, and heart of the first game, although not to the same degree. I missed a lot of the side-narrative in the first game so I didn't realize it at first, but the original did a lot more in terms of the other kids and their own little storylines, providing a bunch of fun, optional content to explore and enjoy. 2 introduces the interns, but despite their prominence their presence seems mostly cursory, relegated to little moments at the start and end and one or two appearances somewhere in the middle of the game. 2 is also easy even compared to the first game, so easy that you could probably stumble through it even if you sneezed out your brain. That said, it doesn't necessarily need to be that kind of game, and is plenty enjoyable regardless.I would definitely say I enjoyed it, altogether. The mental worlds are almost unilaterally great, with excellent, highly imaginative elements blended together seamlessly. It was difficult for me to choose a favorite, and unlike the first game, there weren't any that I really disliked. Fighting is more fun, and the bosses are almost all quite good. I find myself more drawn to familiar characters and their stories, story being a much bigger factor in this game overall. 1's story was very self-contained, mostly a premise, while 2 gives more insight into the world itself, into a present shaped by the actions of a few in the past who must still comes to terms with their fears and traumas, with your help. It tells more of a complete story, with a more solid mystery and development, while still having the cleverness and humor of the first game. Some of the powers seem a little underutilized, and one of the few leftover gripes I have from the first game is a couple powers being so indispensable that we're left with only a button or two to cycle between the rest, but I'm pretty happy overall.Psychonauts 2 feels sort of like three steps forward, one step back compared to the original, doing a lot of things better but also missing a thing or two that helped make the original special. While some of its features and elements are underutilized in my opinion, the things it does well I feel it does even better than 1. All the  comparisons aside, I would say that Psychonauts 2 is a great game, full of creativity, empathy, and wit, and something that it would be hard for just about anyone with a heart to have a bad time with.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: Its been nearly 17 years since the release of Psychonauts 1. Thats a lot of time, and with all the numerous delays and changes in the production of the game, it was honestly going to be a wonder if this released at all. So with that out of the way, does the game hold up?Hell yes it does, I am so happy to say that for once an anticipated title in 2021 ended up actually meeting and even surpassing expectations. Psychonauts 2 fixes a lot of the horrible stuff from the original. The platforming feels more robust and well constructed, trying to 100 % the game is a breeze and the game is super forgiving with only a couple of exceptions, the story feels much more sensible and logical. Going into the game it felt honestly incredible how well they picked up where the previous 2 games left off. The game just oozes quality, from its fun and emotional voice acting to the energetic and beautiful animations. I was able to 100 % complete the game in about 24 hours. If you are just focusing on the main game you can probably finish this in 14 hours. For a game that is 60 bucks that can be a relatively hard sell, especially because the game sadly doesn't have a lot to offer once you collected everything. It thankfully does mean the game respects your time, those 24 hours are packed with content that is fun to finish. It might not be a long game, but its a game that will stick with you for a while.Now onto the negatives. Besides its game length, the game just doesn't have a lot of depth or variety. One thing I really appreciated in Psychonauts 1 is how many different people you get to meet and really understand. It feels like you don't really get that a lot in this game. Everything feels like its based around 1 central subject which I won't spoil. And as a result a lot of story lines can feel a bit similar. Also the game introduces a ton of characters early on, but it feels like a lot of them barely get the attention they honestly deserve.The other thing that feels lacking is the combat and pin system, the combat looks incredible and the enemies are super fun in terms of design, but fighting them feels incredibly similar, once you get a bit of extra hp you can pretty much beat all enemies with the same strategy of just headbutting and spamming a couple of abilities. I never even felt like changing my pins (your equipables) into anything besides the currency earning pin types. The game also gives you a lot of cosmetic and fun pin options, sadly there aren't a lot of equipment slots and as a result these fun pins get left to the wayside really fast. The progression and combat sadly ends up feeling pretty shallow as a result of all of this.But those things don't take away from the main experience. Just jumping around and exploring is a ton of fun. The main story might be lacking in some ways but it still tells a pretty engaging and fun story, with excellent dialogue and animation to boot. Its a game filled with charm and love. If you are a fan of platformers you should do yourself a favor and just play this game. If you are a bit hesitant, maybe because you dislike or are bad at platformers, then I recommend you wait for a sale. Its an extremely accessible game, even if you are bad at platformers, there are a couple of options in the option menu to help you still be able to play the game. To conclude: 3D platfomers nowadays are rare, let alone ones that are this polished and well made. The game is a ton of fun and a big recommend from me.

_childDocuments_.review: A sequel that takes its cult classic predecessor and improves on its best qualities. Hasn't fully escaped some of the first game's problems, but does alleviate them to a degree. A game you can easily sink 20+ hours into, especially if you're a completionist. If you liked , chances are you will love .  is an adventure-platforming game, and the long-awaited sequel to the cult classic . If you haven't played the first game yet, I highly recommend stepping back and picking that up before you jump into this (though you can get away with not playing the VR-exclusive ). If you have played it, though, then you mostly know what to expect: a mix of platforming and exploration, tons of collectibles, wacky characters, psychedelic levels, a story of secret agents that's full of twists and turns, and a whole lot of imagination throughout. All of these were staples of the original game, and each one returns with at least some improvement in the sequel:I managed to sink over 20 hours into this game, and I definitely feel that it was time and money well spent. Searching every nook and cranny for 100% completion made things start to drag at times, but playing through the main story and just grabbing whatever collectibles caught my eye along the way was a satisfying gameplay loop that never stopped being fun.  I'll admit that I was very skeptical of this game before it launched due to Double Fine's more recent track record with games, especially crowdfunded games that undergo years-long delays. That said, they managed to live up to the hype and make the long wait worthwhile, and I hope that this game is just the start of an upward trend for Double Fine and their future projects.

_childDocuments_.review: I was worried when this first released; it's been years since the first one, fans have asked and been promised before, it's a sequel-those are never as good. Though this is a PHENOMENAL game.Whether you've played the first Psychonauts or not I'd recommend this game. The game does a good job at recapping everything you would need to know and making it a fun experience for new and returning players. It makes fun of a few things old players might get a laugh at while new players probably won't even notice.The game feels smooth and nice to play, it doesn't have any mandatory tedious quests (a few side ones that might be, but those don't do anything for the story), and I LOVED the story.I don't want to oversell it and have it be something that could never reach expectations. Though I will say, after a streak of sequels making me wish they hadn't even bothered this was a delightful difference. It keeps a lot of the same fun, quirky, and sometimes pleasantly bizarre atmosphere the first one did, while also making it new and "up to date." It feels like a genuine continuation and like it's own original game at the same time.Cons: Not a lot honestly. I think there were two or three places where the wall jumping mechanic and the camera didn't play nice. The camera would get in a fixed location so you could see everything you needed to, however, that would mean not being able to get the clearest indication of whether or not you were wall jumping at an angle or not.I'm a rabid completionist, so the only other complaint I have might not even be a bother to others. However, I like being able to grab everything in a stage before proceeding and the game is made so that certain beginner areas you have to go back to (I'm okay with that tbh), OR you have to wait until you finish the game and are released with total free wild abandon upon the world. Not a big deal to I imagine near everyone, but if you are like me, then just get prepared to know where something is, fully understanding how the game WANTS you to get there, and accepting that you don't have that power yet so you have to move on.Though really, those two things are pretty minor. The wall jumping mechanic still feels nice and is really fun to screw around with. And, the game does let me grab every unnecessary thing I want to pack rat away once I'm done with the story.TL;DR: Definitely worth every penny. It's good for both those who played the first Psychonauts and those who have never heard. It's fun, wholesome, an honest continuation that doesn't alienate people who've never played the first one. Only one minor complaint, and one "I like to 100% games before fighting the final boss and was only allowed to get to 99%" irrational completionist grumble. 10/10 was worth the wait.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: Most others reviewing this game have said that it lives up to the original, a claim I'd disagree with. I'd say that it manages to surpass it on almost every count. The level design starts at the peak of the first games quality and manages to surpass it on multiple occasions after that fact, the story here, while thin at some early points, manages to be much more emotionally resonant than the first games whilst retaining the humour, the psychic powers themselves are much better this time around with no powers I never felt I wanted to use (looking at you, invisibility from 1) and the soundtrack... well, just listen to the Brain in a Jar theme if you need proof of how good that is.The only area I'd say it suffers is with some members of the supporting cast. While most of the cast are fairly well characterised and entertaining the recruits that make up Raz's peers feel like they don't have enough time given to them to be particularly entertaining or cultivate depth (with the exception of Sam). This can be a bit of a problem for the game as even without that necessary focus it still leans on them for some moments that can fall a bit flat.Overall I'd say this game is an easy recommendation and a competitor for the position of my favourite platformer.

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot praise Psychonauts 2 enough- it's been so incredibly long since I played the first game, but PN2 has been able to suck me in completely. Every single part of this game is just oozing with personality and humor and emotion, including the incredibly expressive character facial/body animations, the extremely inventive and unique levels that are chock-filled with details reflecting the characters' minds, and the well paced and very personal stories being told and interwoven with each other.The only thing I can complain about is that some movements are finicky- e.g. jumping when pressed right up against terrain objects that aren't perfectly vertical (because the environment is so stylized) can fail, and sometimes jumping while climbing depends too much on the camera being mostly straight behind your character. Beyond that, this is simply a masterpiece.

_childDocuments_.review: Psychonauts 2 is a fantastic sequel, which anyone who enjoyed Psychonauts will love. It builds and improves on the original in many ways, and is a great game in its own right. Impossible not to recommend this one.The idea behind Psychonauts 2 is that you are a psychic agent, tasked with entering people's mental worlds and clearing up their problems from the inside. Every level immerses you in a wild metaphor for an individual's psyche. Things which are important to that individual may appear huge in their mind, and enemies which you battle represent doubts, regrets and so on. It's a terrific idea, which worked well for the first game and continues to be used to great effect here.The world-building, game design, and overall story is just brilliant. The whole game is wildly imaginative from start to finish, Every single new area I wanted to poke about and see what was going on, and every time I did so the game hit me with a cool idea, great characters, a fun game mechanic, a minigame... The game never drags as a result - I never wanted to put it down.The gameplay is significantly more platformer-focused than the original, which wore its adventure game influences more proudly. Inventory has been removed, and most puzzles are very simple. Instead, there are more open arena-like settings for combat, tricky platforming segments, and rewards for exploring off-the-beaten-path. I would say the difficulty is greater than the first game, but accessibility options mean this can be adjusted down if desired.The game smooths out two big issues with the original. The first is figments, which are little doodles of imagination in a person's mind, and serve as collectibles in both games. In the first, they would frequently be rendered invisible by the surroundings, and so it was frustrating to try and collect all of them. In the sequel, their visibility has been greatly improved, and they also have a glowing aura so they can be seen from any angle. The second is balancing out psychic abilities. In the original, certain abilities were rarely used due to being pretty janky (Telekinesis) or pointless (Clairvoyance). In Psychonauts 2, however, great care has been taken to make all abilities fun, easy to use, and useful, so I spent a good amount of time on every ability.Despite all its successes, there are a couple of points on which Psychonauts 2 does poorly, or at least doesn't live up to the original. The first is that Raz is *way* too forthcoming with "hints" that it almost seems like he is nagging. For instance, a gate might open, and I'd rather spend some more time looking around the area I'm in - While I do that, Raz will be badgering me the entire time saying things like "I should go through that gate!" and "I wonder what's on the other side of that gate!". He also says "I can hear emotional baggage nearby!" which is awful, and destroys the joy of exploring and discovering emotional baggage for yourself. The other issue I have with Psychonauts 2 is the writing just isn't as good as the first. I can easily think of loads of little lines from the first game which are very funny, and stuck with me. Pick any level and I can instantly come back with a line I really enjoyed, and some levels (Lungfishopolis, Milkman Conspiracy) were bursting with great writing. With Psychonauts 2, I have to think quite hard to remember knockout lines from any of the levels. It's much similar in vibe to Black Velvetopia from the first game: the world building and ideas are what it relies on, with the sharp writing taking a bit of a back seat.Overall, Psychonauts 2 is excellent. It's very easy to recommend this one.

_childDocuments_.review: I was very skeptical going in. The goofy graphics, the dated combat, the floaty platforming. They all looked like deal-breakers to me. Yet, I heard so many critics singing from a rooftop: "The level design and artistry of this game are unique, lovely, exceptional." It pulled at my interest just enough to get me to buy the game. And you probably saw it coming: I'm extremely glad I did. I haven't quite finished it yet, but I feel safe singing Psychonauts' praises as follows:This platformer is more about exploring and enjoying a piece of art than it is about game mechanics or snappy controls. If you are at all interested in games as a form of (artistic) expression and story delivery, this game is for you. The story is thoroughly compelling: up there with the best in gaming and refreshingly unique in its themes and subject matter. The artistic execution and creativity of the Psycho-premise is great. But the way that level design is leveraged to execute that same artistic premise is *second-to-none*. Best ever I've seen in a game. I now understand the GOTY nominations.Is the *game* the best ever? No! The combat? Passable. It's like Fable games back in the day. RPG elements? Bulk-standard: little bit of respeccable customisation and some perk points. Platforming? Fun, but nothing spectacular - though its worth mentioning that the floatiness isn't bothersome. Remember the difference in snappiness between Gamecube Smash Bros. versus the later ones? Psychonauts' platforming is like those later, floaty Smash Bros, where the snappy platfomer would be like Ori or Mario. Fortunately, the slowed down pace is matched by the pace of the obstacles, so it doesn't bother you at all while you're playing. And if anything, its actually a sort of boon: it gives you more time to appreciate the environments. The same can be said of the Ubisoft-esque collectible scavenger hunts: I don't give a sh** about collecting cards and markers and blah blah blah... but that busy work is fine if its just a byproduct of exploring these excellent levels. I think the developers also understood this, because the collecta-thon is pretty easy to complete. It's just a way to get you to look around. At the end of the game, this game does 1 thing great (story) and 1 thing exceptionally (artistic level-design), and rests those on a foundation of unobtrusively adequate gameplay mechanics.To wrap this up, it bears repeating: This game is a beautiful piece of art you play a game inside of. I highly recommend spending your time enjoying it.

_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: A game that had a lot to live up to. The original Psychonauts was a fantastic game with a creative premise, interesting and funny characters, and great art direction. It was criminal it wasn't more on more people's radar. When a sequel was announced, I was very excited as well as a tiny bit apprehensive. After all, revisiting a project you did more that 15 years ago always runs the risk of missing what made the first game great by relying too much on nostalgia and playing it too safe. Thankfully, Psychonauts 2 avoids these pitfalls, and improved upon the original in every way. The main story is more streamlined into every level / brain seamlessly, the comedy feels better than the original and the themes hit harder. The old and new cast are great and a higher emotional and philosophical depth is achieved. The combat and platforming are a massive improvement. The visuals, sound and level + World design are technically and artistically brilliant. Two smaller things to add is that it's a breath of fresh air that the team making this game were not subjected to crunch times, and they knew when to delay the project to avoid it. And the LGBTQ+ representation was handled really well. Overall, it feels as if the second entry blows the original out of the park, and cannot recommend enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: The most important thing to note here is that Psychonauts 2 tones down the edgy, early 2000s cartoon feel of the first game in favor of a lore-heavy drama about mental health.  In other words, there's some heartfelt moments and clever twists but the humor isn't quite there. The interns are also some of the most underdeveloped and downright unlikable characters I've seen in recent years and I constantly wanted them to leave. However, it definitely tops the original regarding visuals and playability. The mental worlds are beautiful and just as imaginative as ever. There's a stronger emphasis on platforming and combat, which are both simple to pick up and surprisingly complex. The glaring gameplay flaws of the first game have also been stamped out -- looking at you, Cobweb Duster. It's a thoroughly enjoyable game overall, but certainly not worth the $60 price tag. Since the writing was always Psychonauts' strongest aspect, I would recommend the first game if you haven't played it. Psychonauts 2 is still a very solid package overall for Psychonauts fans, but I'm less inclined to suggest playing this instead of the original.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: So, downsides first: You'll probably want a guide for all of the collectibles, some of the puzzles and bosses require a specific combination of lateral thinking to solve that aren't always obvious, you'll want to watch a playthrough of the previous two games if you haven't played them yourself, and if your friends want to avoid spoilers it will physically hurt to not talk about this game because HOLY MOLY this is a good game.I'm not great at Platformers, but the game gives you accessibility options and doesn't shame you or gate off achievements if you use them. The game gives adequate trigger warnings without spoiling, and it goes way, WAY out of its way to remind the player how dangerous it can be to play around in someone else's head.The cast is charming, the voice work impeccable, the art style complements the tone and theme of the game well, and the levels are all polished. Some of the powers are a little more useful than others, but none of them are completely useless, and the music is great, even outside of the stage absolutely devoted to musical theatricality.

_childDocuments_.review: Like it's predecessor, Psychonauts 2 is a great throwback to the platformer genre.The humor, animation, and character design is absurd and zany, and it works perfectly. Everything about the game is just a little off kilter in the right ways. The hub world is expansive and features lots of areas to solve, and each of the levels (which similar to the first game, involves solving the psychological issues of various characters by literally hopping into their brain) is uniquely styled and thematic to the mind of each character you delve into.Like most platformers, in addition to just figuring out how to make their way through each level, there's plenty of interesting combat, puzzle elements, and collectibles. In addition to the Figments which return from the first game, there's a lot more collectibles that work more towards improving Raz's abilities. Speaking of which, Clairvoyance, Levitation, Psi-Blast, Pyrokinesis, and Telekinesis return from the first game,  but now in the place of Invisibility, Confusion, and Shield, we now have Mental Connection, which allows you zap yourself from mental node to mental node through the air to reach areas you otherwise couldn't jump to, and also to pull enemies toward you for an extra punch. And then there's Time Bubble, which creates a bubble of bullet-time slowing down faster enemies allowing you to attack them while they are slowed and can't fight back easily.  And lastly there's Mental Projection, one of my favorites, which creates a little 2D version of yourself which distracts enemies and slips through hard to reach places, and is voiced by Rosearik Rikki Simmons, who also did the voice of Invader Zim's GIR alongside Raz's VA who did Zim, which was a combination I was surprised and overjoyed to hear.All of those abilities can also be upgraded with enhancements using skill points RPG-style. There are a few other trinkets you can acquire along the way, along with pins that you can swap in and out for other smaller abilities and bonuses that are useful in different situations.The story itself continues from the first game (and the VR game, Rhombus of Ruin) pretty much immediately after, so Raz is still much the same 10 year old Psychonaut-in-training hoping to become a famous psychonaut like his heroes, the Psychic 6 (err... 7) which feature prominently in this story, tho I don't want to give too much spoilers, but it delves a little bit into Raz's backstory, as well as the history of the psychonauts.I did play Rhombus of Ruin part of the way through, though I never finished it, but its not at all necessary to enjoy this game, as this game gets you up to speed on what happened in the VR game pretty quickly (which wasn't all that much, basically you rescued Lili's Dad and brought him back to the psychonauts HQ.I will say though, I feel like it would be difficult to get too into this game if you haven't played the first one, storywise, since this is really just a continuation of that story, and while the game does summarize things in the beginning, the first game does a lot to setup the world and what the psychonauts are.I only have a few complaints with this game. Firstly while the graphics have improved since the first, and its cartoony aesthetic means that it won't necessarily be going for anything hyperrealistic, I found a lot of the textures seemed very low resolution and grainy, even on the highest settings.  It's using Unreal Engine 4 but I didn't see any evidence of tech like raytracing or more modern illumination and shading effects, so the game looks a bit dated for something that came out in 2021.While I still loved most of the levels in this game, a few were pretty dull and monotonous. They seemed larger than the first game, with more collectibles and things to find, but that resulted in even more backtracking and running around to try to find what I missed. Fortunately once you complete a level you can go back and find a fast travel system implemented, but there was still a bit more backtracking than I would have liked, since there's a lot of content you can't even reach until you unlock abilities only available much later in the game.I'm hoping if they do make another psychonauts game we see Raz's character aged up a bit, as one of the drawbacks of this one picking up precisely where the last games left off is that he's still just a 10 year old and there hasn't really been much character development other than his gaining new abilities and becoming a more skilled psychonaut.  It would definitely be cool to see a psychonaut game playing as a young adult Raz. Who knows if they'll ever make another though.That all being said, I enjoyed the game thoroughly, enough so that it's one of the few games I've nailed 100% of the achievements for, collected all the collectibles, and acquired all the items and abilities. And it didn't overstay its welcome after playing it for a casual 26 or so hours off and on. I imagine you could have gotten through the game a lot quicker than I did if you just focused on getting through the story and not so much 100ing each level.Overall, I certainly recommend this game to anyone who enjoyed the first! Though I do recommend playing the first game too before this one. It's fun, psychological, psychotic, and psychedelic.

_childDocuments_.review: When I heard my favorite childhood platformer is finally getting a sequel, I've  my dudes. The game was officially announced after a big crowdfunding effort. As a huge fan of the original, this review might be biased due to nostalgia. If you want to hear me out anyway though, get comfortable. 	The story picks up right after the original (except for the fact that the VR title “Psychonauts in the Rhombus of Ruin” explains the small, but pretty important gap between the two games). The Psychonauts try to find out who was really responsible for the incident at the Whispering Rock Psychic Summer Camp and the abduction of the head of the whole organization, Truman Zanotto. In the meantime, Raz finds out more about himself and his family, and delves into many interesting mentalscapes and their backstories. Although the game tries to recreate the atmosphere of the original to some extent, it mostly does new things. We still have mysterious campgrounds inhabited by mutated psychic animals to explore, but the campers have been replaced by a completely new cast of characters. That’s not necessarily a bad thing though, considering all new interns have pretty colorful personalities and we’re getting to know them fast. There are also some reoccurring characters such as Lili and Ford. The minds themselves are where the game truly shines. All of them are unique and amazing, resembling the character's mental state, and so, the turmoil within. Unlike the first game, this time Double Fine consulted actual psychologists to ensure the adequate portrayal of various mental problems in their product. The way it handles mental health is very interesting: problems are shown in a comedic, cartoonish manner, fitting in the game’s atmosphere and aesthetic, but still designed in such a way to give you an idea of what a person experiencing, for example, sensory overload or a panic attack feels like. I recommend watching “Psychology of Psychonauts” series by Gaming University for cool breakdowns of the individual levels of both games and issues they portray. I really enjoyed shining some light onto Ford’s backstory and other founders of the organization. Story ties up a lot of loose ends from the first game leaving us with a complete and satisfying journey. Although I'd love another sequel, I was actually surprised when Tim Schafer said that they aren’t currently working on the third game, instead of saying something along the lines “That’s all the story Raz could tell us and time to move on” or something. I guess there is hope. Platforming is even more fluid than in the original and it’s just a pleasure to jump and bounce around with Raz. His move set makes it really fun to move around. In terms of abilities they kept the best in, while getting rid of some less enjoyable ones replacing them with new stuff. What’s really cool is that every ability in addition to just being useful in exploration and moving around is also functional in combat. An exception from that is clairvoyance. It may be funny using it on some of the characters and puzzles, but in combat it’s only useful with one specific enemy. Speaking of combat, it’s a lot more dynamic and engaging now. Game encourages you to use everything you have at your disposal. Different powers are more effective on different enemies. The only drawback I see is the fact that you can equip a limited amount of your powers at once. Switching back and forth between abilities by a radial menu is annoying, especially when you’re playing on keyboard and could map everything if only given an option. Music is amazing, probably on par with the original, but again, I'm blinded by nostalgia. I’m going crazy when they play old tracks, but the new ones are incredible too. Personal favorites are probably “Maligula Unleashed!” and “Fight in the Library”. Generally good sound design. Graphically the game has a very unique aesthetic and design. The reflections, lightning and stuff look very good, but similarly to the first game it will probably look good years after anyway thanks to the characteristic art style.  Game has lots of accessibility options. Achievement-wise it’s pretty straightforward. You can do everything on the same save and nothing is missable. Pretty chill to do a 100%. 	My final thought is that it’s a perfect sequel. Ties up a story that has been incomplete for the past 16 years. Does improve gameplay and leaves you satisfied. It owes a lot to its predecessor, but is a great game in its own right. Again, it’s probably thanks to nostalgia, but it has been a long while since I was smiling every minute of playing a game, 10 hours into it. And it’s not only because of hilarious jokes, but also out of pure enjoyment. This was a real treat.
_childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: I really had to formulate my thoughts after playing for twenty hours and beating the game. I had to 100% Psychonauts 1 to remember what it was really about. But after coming back for 13 more hours to 100% Psychonauts 2, I realized that this game lived up to the original in ways of how it treats its themes. The relationships of parents to sons, the insanity of emotional baggage, and the hidden little treats that we've all come to love- all come together in Psychonauts 2 to create emotional catharsis for the viewers and the characters inside of the game. The best therapy 60$ can buy in a game, one that promotes healing and fun, to whatever that means to you.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best action platformers ever made, if not THE best. Period. Just like Psychonauts 1, it's overflowing with character, humor, creativity, but all of the factors that made Psychonauts 1 memorable and lovable are cranked up to 11 in Psychonauts 2. The platforming is much more tight, and the combat is far more engaging, encouraging you to mix and match your psi-powers to deal with enemies in whatever way you want. Exceeding the first game, the soundtrack is PHENOMENAL in Psychonauts 2, and it makes revisiting minds to gather 100% of the collectibles a treat.The story is also much better than the first game. Every character is written like a real person, with flaws and mental disorders, and thought processes that are both unique and completely understandable. I won't spoil too much, but the story is also much more personal to Raz, and as a result will get you much more invested and immersed.Each level is entirely unique and enjoyable in its own way, from its music, to its NPCs, and (of course) its distinct aesthetic. You'll jump into levels that look almost exactly like how you'd imagine the concept art to look like, with their tall and twisted heights, their curving roads, and their mind-bending illusions that shift gravity and bend reality in a way that isn't nauseating, really pulling you into a world beyond reality: the mind.With the Quality of Life patch released in November 2021, 100%ing the game is also much easier, making collecting all the figments manageable and easy, but without entirely trivializing the difficulty of exploration. The only problem is that the X-Ray/collectible finder lens doesn't work on aforementioned reality-bending impossible rooms that are bigger on the inside, but it makes sense as to why. With how colorful and lovable this game is, with its wonderful soundtrack and unique characters, you'll want to 100% it just to spend more time in the seamless, perfectly-executed world Double Fine has crafted.This game is nothing short of art. The level designs are like paintings, the story is like a book, the music is fantastic, and each mind -- the way thought processes and disorders are translated into physical objects, worlds, characters, puzzles, and enemies -- is like poetry. I cannot recommend this game enough, and with the accessibility options that are provided for people who aren't looking for a challenge (invincibility, removing fall damage, etc.), there's no reason NOT to play this game. Buy it for full price, or wait for it to go on sale like I did, I guarantee you're going to enjoy every second of it.

_childDocuments_.review: Big fan of the first game. Glad I backed it up during the campaign. Everything is amazing and I am happy to finish the game. I only had a few shader bugs, so I think it is safe to say that it is fully playable at launch, which is rare these days.If I really have to critique it, there are only a few things:- A lot more cutsenes. It's great, but there is a lot less combat and it kills the replayability. I can pick up and play the first any day, but I am not sure it will happen with this one- There was more game design risks that they took in the first one. This one feels "safer" and more linear. Great for casual players, but I miss the hardcorness of the circus finale or just confusing levels like the milkman.- Feels a little short.I hope they make a DLC or a 3d one. Do not mind diving into the psychonauts again! Big thanks to the team.

_childDocuments_.review: A game I have waited a long time for, and I have to say that I have mixed feelings right now. The gameplay feels more varied but is not as fun as the first game that came out over a decade ago. The upgrades used to be given on level ups and frankly over powered Raz by the end, but almost all of the upgrades now kinda suck or are something that you could just have because you already had it in the first game. Perfect example you need to once again acquire the ability to chain hit enemies with you PSI Blast. You can also modify powers with badges but they (again) are mostly useless. The only two that are truly worth a damn are the glass cannon and the fist power up. Another problem for me is the story is kinda meh. The overall story is fine but the beats in between are not fun to play through.  I did not care for almost any of the new characters outside of the Psychic 6. They just were not all that interesting when compared to what we had from the first game. Two of the many standout characters for me in the first one were Clem and Crystal, two cheerleaders that tried cheering everyone on while secretly holding suicidal thoughts. If you just did the story you would not have seen any of that but I liked them so I kept checking in on them only to see one of their attempts. This was missing in this game to me. Characters that I actually wanted to see out of the story beats, and the ones that where there just deus ex machina themselves into whatever situation need at that moment. The game I wanted to like is in here but all of the bad drags it down for me. Off sheer value that the levels were neat (nothing comes close to Milkman or the Waterloo levels) I will recommend this game but DEFINITELY not for $60. Barely $30 and if you can get it lower you should do so.

_childDocuments_.review: A few years ago I purchased the first Psychonauts game after having seen a few youtubers gush about how great of a game it was and after playing it for myself I would still absolutely recommend that game as well as this one. The original release date for the first game was over 16 years ago so the wait for this game has been long and though I never played the original I believe the wait might have been worth it for those that played the first game all those years ago. The controls are tight and responsive with challenging and fun platforming as well as combat using the full array of powers to tackle situations in each, the writing and script for the story and interactions between characters is hilarious, tragic, and engaging, and each level has felt unique and incredibly well designed so far. As of yet I haven't completed the story mode but I would certainly recommend this game to fans of the first game and if you're new don't worry they have a recap of the first game at the beginning but you'd be missing the great levels that game has to offer. Over all if you want to get this game now it's well worth it and an incredibly well crafted game in every aspect.

_childDocuments_.review: I do recommend this game and I do love it but after all these years it does feel like they tried to appeal to a more modern audience.The writing is still very sharp, the game is gorgeous, the platforming is fun but throughout it all something felt... missing.The interns are a really bad replacement for the campers. During the casino finale sequence Gisu says "Remember what I taught you about grinding, Raz." I don't know if they left that line in there by mistake but you meet the interns and then go into Hollis' mind the line just makes no sense as if they forgot to include a whole part of the game where you connect with the other interns.No "puzzle-box" levels and no inventory - this game is a straight platformer. No puzzles. All levels are (albeit still really good) "point A to point B" which makes the different minds just not feel truly unique from each other like in the first game.This game is still a really good sequel and it solves the questions the first one brought up and is probably one of the best games of the last few years but due to "modernizing" some of the best parts that made the first game so great are just gone or watered down.Play this.

_childDocuments_.review: Feels just like the original in terms of core gameplay, very nostalgic and a ton of fun, but with some key drawbacks. Psychonauts 1 had much stronger level design with Lungfishopolis, Waterloo World, the Milkman Conspiracy, levitation ball races, which all had unique gameplay mechanics that set them apart from the rest of the missions and kept the game feeling fresh the whole way. Most missions in Psychonauts 2 consist of pretty simple puzzles that all kinda feel samey. The only thing that really sets each mission apart from each other is visual design. Otherwise, they all feel very similar. The levels aren't poorly made by any means, just very repetitive. There were a couple good standouts though, like Compton's Cookoff. The combat is a lot of fun but there isn't nearly enough of it. Overall, it's a good game and if you liked the first then you'll like this one too. If you're new to the series, I would highly recommend playing the first game despite its age.

_childDocuments_.review: If you loved the first one, you'll be mindblown on this one. I loved the open-world exploration feel, the unique and fun characters with their witty banter and interactions, the rich and ever-changing inner mind-worlds, the gradual increase in difficulty that is challenging but not punishing. This has it all. I'm probably only about 30% the way through the storyline, but I am 100% confident that this game is everything that I had hoped it would be. The game feels like a continuation of the first, not a shoe-horned repetitive call back to the original, and stands on its own in its own right (though you should probably play the amazing first one too). Everything that was great about the first, they brought it over and continued it. The controls feel smooth and camera is much improved from the first. They've somehow kept the graphics seamless with the first without making it feel dated. I am savoring this game and taking my time through the game, cause I don't want it to end.Edit: Finished the main storyline and am continuing finding all the secrets, it's so good! Also I should probably mention that I am not typically a fan of platforming games, but this game is sensational and I love it. Nominating it for 2021 GOTY, it has my heart.

_childDocuments_.review: Psychonauts 2 is a rare perfect sequel to an already outstanding game. It has improved every issue I had with the original, and kept the charm, humor, and wild imagination. The mental worlds continue to be some of the most fascinating locations in any video game I've ever played, and the art style is so good!However, the part that I really need to talk about is the narrative. The story hits emotional heights that Psychonauts hadn't managed to achieve before. Don't get me wrong, I still love the first game, but the plot was kind of a basic "villain trying to take over, go stop him" setup and didn't do much to build up anything thematically. This is where Psychonauts 2 shines for me. It uses all of it's parts to construct a more cohesive whole, and has a lot to say about mental problems, trauma, recovery, and empathy.My personal Game of the Year for 2021!

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game for it's story, characters, and gameplay. _childDocuments_.name: Psychonauts 2

_childDocuments_.review: oh my gosh this game is so goooodThe first Psychonauts is a pretty good game. It blends incredibly creative levels with superb writing, but it's held back by an annoying leveling system, bland combat, and some pretty meh animation. Psychonauts 2 took  a very bold approach called TAKING EVERYTHING THAT BROUGHT THE FIRST GAME DOWN AND MAKING IT ALL 100X BETTER. Everything is polished to the extreme. Movement is snappier, combat is deeper and feels much better thanks to the incredible animation. Like, this game has some of the best animations I've ever seen in a game, and that doesn't even take into account the cutscenes which could basically just be a Pixar movie. In fact, the entire game could be a modern animated movie. This is one of the most gorgeous games I've ever played. Every mind has its own distinct artstyle and all of them look incredible. From the cel-shaded psychedelic mind of the Sensorium to the Lady Luctopus Casino to Compton's Cookoff, every mind is brilliantly designed and really helps you differentiate between them. Each mind also features the amazing writing Psychonauts is known for, blending humor with thought-provoking depictions of anxiety, depression, multiple personality disorder, and alcoholism. This game takes the mental issues it depicts very seriously, and it makes the story of the second game much more personal and gut-wrenching than the first game and its very...loose depiction of mental disorders. The game does falter in one area, which is the bosses. I really didn't think many of them were that special compared to the first game, although at least none of them reversed my controls (I'm still angry at that tank from the first game). The leveling system is also very improved. No more do you need to reach a certain level to access the next mind. Instead, levels are used to upgrade the abilities you already have to allow for more power in combat or more movement. The abilities from the last game are also much better implemented. While most of them felt a bit janky in the first game, here, they're all wonderfully implemented and feel great to use. The new abilities are also excellently melded into the platforming and the combat, and they all felt like great additions to Raz's arsenal. Everything in this game is just amazing. This might just be my favorite platformer ever, and it definitely is one of my favorite games ever. If you ever want a fantastic platformer with incredible writing, wonderfully charming characters, and some of the most creative platforming ever, pick this game up. You won't regret it. I give Psychonauts 2 a Where did you get the milk/10

_childDocuments_.review: Psychonauts 2 is a game of the year contender. I remember playing the original game (Psychonauts) way back before the it even hit Steam, all the way back in 2005 when I bought it brand new, and I remember being heart broken that this great game probably wouldn't  have a future.  It's been a wild ride watching Double Fine emerge from the ashes of near collapse. While I didn't have the money at the time or the Psychonauts 2 funding campaign, it feels good to have funded things like the Double Fine Adventure. This game will probably be the highlight of my year.The story of the game picks right up from the VR game, Rhombus of Ruin, but it's not required to know the story as the game gives a good recap of the events of the first game. You could probably play this game without the first game too, but you lose a lot of neat references and emotional attachment. Sadly it's kind of hard to write more than the plot synopsis without spoiling the game. If you're on the fence though the writing is both thought provoking while also meeting the full range of chuckle, snort, and laugh out funny. The game does deal with a lot of family related issues as well as dealing with the results of political destabilization if that's something that could bother you. I'd also warn there might be some stuff close to body horror as well.The gameplay of Psychonauts 2 is a well refined version of Psychonauts 1 if a bit striped down at its core. Some powers are missing despite being important, canonical abilities from the first game (Shield, Invisibility, and Confusion). Each power is upgrade-able and thankfully there are plenty of points to get the powers improved enough there's no pressure if you feel like you messed up. Improving some of the new powers right away though is kind of a must, sadly. The new pin, side grade, system is interesting, but the extra effects aren't really used all the much. I'd had preferred a point system where cosmetic pins were zero points and didn't compete with combat abilities. I only cycled through about five of the pins at any given time. My biggest grievance with it is there are hardly any over-world use cases for a lot of pins. For example in the first game you'd use Invisibility to sneak past things. I saw there was a pin that gave you the ability to speed up things, thinking it would be used for a collectible I bought it, but it wasn't used for anything. I also couldn't find any use for the ability in combat either. Getting money can be a bit of a chore as there's no dowsing rod so you'll get betting money in 1-50 chunks. Wasting it on pins that do nothing can feel kind of bad.When it comes to collectibles I found them refreshingly less frustrating than some of them were in Psychonauts 1. There's no Millo's Race Track shenanigans this time around, but please stop putting figments on perfectly arked jumps. I got most of the collectibles on my first run through of levels. Though, there are still some super tiny figments (like coins in other games) that are hard to see physically, which is kind of annoying given how well done accessibility is done in other parts of the game this time around. I was kind of hoping for a figment finder or an in-game list where you found each collectible, even if you get it was super late game item. Hunting one figment of 200+ in some levels or a single card is literally the worst. My biggest frustration was missing rank 102 (100% completion) before the final boss because of a bug. In one of the levels that if you fail one of the challenges' time limits you're locked out of 100% that level until you beat the game. The last level seems to force you to come back post game to get the last few figments. You do get a post game to wander around, so no real Point-of-No-Return, but you won't get to use your infinite ammo and skills on anything important.All-in-all, this is still a great game. 100% completion in 25 hours. I'd actually love to see something like DLC for challenge rooms or something. Really I'd recommend the whole franchise to people. This is pinnacle game writing. I want to see more stuff like this in the medium.

_childDocuments_.review: The unique aesthetics and approach to storytelling of Psychonauts have benefitted quite a bit from being brought into the modern sphere, and this sequel improves on its 2005 predecessor... a lot. The combat is more fluid than the original's, with a variety of psychic powers that can be used strategically against the uniquely themed enemies like "Doubts", "Panic Attacks" and "Judges", and these abilities also tie into the level design and platforming in all sorts of creative ways. The colorful modern graphics accentuate the unique character designs and trippy mental worlds. The puzzles are far more intuitive than the original's obtuse puzzle logic, while still being thought-provoking. And the constant stream of collectables (all of which tie into the different level themes) are woven into the upgrade system in a way that encourages the player to look for secrets and rare items hidden in these intricately designed worlds.There are some rough edges to the movement and animations from time to time, plus a few tedious sections of the game, like missions in the main hub world that involve lots of drawn-out dialogue options. Even with these occasional annoyances, though, I had a blast playing through Psychonauts 2. For anyone reading this who's new to the duology, the first one still holds up well today and I would recommend playing the original first - but this sequel outdoes the first game in a lot of ways, and this has got to be one of the most freakishly creative 3D platformers I've ever played. 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't finished the game yet, but I can say with 100% certainty that this game improves on just about everything Psychonauts 1 had. While not as funny as its predecessor (It has its moments), it has a much heavier emphasis on mental health and the issues that everybody faces. The new psychic abilities you get are all incredibly fun to use, and what's even better is that every psychic ability has a use in battle, so you're not just spamming your fists and psi blasts everywhere. All the new enemies have a weakness to an ability you have, which makes combat all the more interesting. That was probably one of the best changes this game has made. The environments you explore are colorful and memorable, the characters are just as lovable, and the game is just overall fun to play and explore. The only thing I wish was different is the first new ability you get. Without getting too spoiler heavy, you mainly use it as a source of world traversal, but you see at the beginning of the game it can do something much more drastic to people, you do it once, and then never again which I found disappointing. I would have loved to be able to use that ability more. Overall this game is DEFINITELY one everyone should play, even if you're not too big a fan of 3D Platformers. Hands down one of the BEST games to ever come out of 2021!

_childDocuments_.review: A great game.  It keeps the style of the old one, The new psy powers are great, and while I do miss some of the old ones, I think that I prefer the new setup. Railslides, telekinesis, pyrokinesis, and the new powers were things I was always using, so I didn't have an issue where I forgot that I had a tool, or wasn't experienced in using it.  I miss the asylum crew, but the new minds are interesting, and dealing with their problems was a lot better integrated into the story.A few small problems stood out, occasionally getting stuck on geometry, and I'm used enough to the originals' controls that I sometimes had trouble using levitation.  Mental projection also sometimes feels a little bit like a gimmick power, but one of them isn't so bad.  The plot also had a bit of an issue where the twist is very obvious if you've played the original recently enough to remember certain aspects.  Raz also will sometimes forget details that you've learned from dialog or other brains.

_childDocuments_.review: Super good, honestly lives up to the original, which I did not expect. The artistry in this game is incredible and they cranked up the wacky level designs to 11. Took most of the best parts of the first game and made them even better, took most of the worst parts of the first game and fixed them. Solid story, solid characters, solid all around, and extremely creative and simply a joy to experience. I spent so much time playing this game with a stupid smile on my face.There are a few negatives, firstly: the game is extremely easy, and as far as I know there's no option for harder difficulties. I didn't ever die or even come close to dying during my entire playthrough, and I'm not particularly good at video games. The only exception was the final boss fight, which I did die once during, and I might just be salty but I think it's because the boss' reach is bugged to be too far during the second phase haha. The combat in general can feel good sometimes but be pretty janky feeling other times, but in either case it remains true that you don't exactly feel much of a threat from the enemies. Some boss fights were fun but some got old pretty quickly. The design for each one was super interesting though and the art team really knocked it out of the park.The puzzles aren't really puzzles, and any time there is actually a puzzle the characters just tell you how to solve it, so you don't really often have to think through things on your own. The game is just a bit of a walk in the park in this regard, it takes you through a lot of fun experiences, but you don't actually have to do much beyond press buttons in order to progress. The only time you have to figure things out on your own is for getting certain collectibles, which I have to admit are really fun to hunt for, at least in my opinion. The levels are so fun to be in and look around that it never gets boring to look through all the nooks and crannies.Sometimes things just take too long when you are at a critical point in the story. You're getting an exciting story beat but then forced to play through three separate 10 minute segments in the middle of it that maybe aren't super fun. Not a huge deal but it can interrupt the pacing at times and feels like they included a gameplay segment just to pad out the runtime of the game instead of adding something interesting or fun to the game.My only other main critique of the game is sometimes characters just get annoying. Not because they are written that way, but when Rasputin repeats for the 5th time in the last 30 seconds that he hears a collectible nearby, it's like, alright game I get it. Or when I go off to do a sidequest and Rasputin feels the need to remind me that I should actually be doing my main quest. Mainly it's Ras getting on your nerves by constantly talking during gameplay, but that seems to be an issue for single player RPGs across the board. What really gets me are during boss fights, hearing the bosses repeat the same 4-5 voicelines over and over and over again during the entire bossfight. It's just irksome and there's no reason for it.Over all super positive experience, just hope for the next game DoubleFine tighten up a couple of things and spend a little more time asking themselves "is this going to be fun the third time?" before working really hard to implement something.

_childDocuments_.review: Psychonauts 2 is a truly remarkable game. The original game, Psychonauts, was a crazy platformer with some of the craziest and most remarkable levels in videogames, packed together with a great storyline full of good humor. Psychonauts 2 takes everything that made the original game a cult classic, refreshes it, fixes some bad aspects and adds more good stuff. A result is a game that in almost every aspect is at least two times better than the original.Let's start with a storyline. The game starts right after Rhombus Of Ruin, a VR-spinoff. Razputin Aquato, or Raz, main character of the series, arrives to the Motherlobe - a psychonauts HQ, where he becomes an intern (while in original game he received an offer to join psychonauts, Ford Cruller, who made an offer, actually didn't have an authority to do so). Yet something is not quite right - after saving Truman Zanotto (which happened in Rhombus Of Ruin) they learn that the mind of a kidnapper, Dr. Loboto, was booby-trapped, and they don't know who hired him, but all they gathered points at a mole in the organization and the fact that it somehow is connected to Maligula - a former psychonaut, who killed a lot of people and was stopped by Ford Cruller 20 years ago, which resulted in Ford losing his mind. Raz forced out of investigation, but of course it wouldn't stop him.Main problem for new players would be the fact that this game is heavily connected with previous games. While original is 16 years old and another game is a VR exclusive, it doesn't look good. The good part is that there's an intro which will describe basics of what happened prior to Psychonauts 2, so if you didn't play the first one or VR exclusive game, you won't be out of a loop completely. While in the beginning you won't see more than jokes and references, the more you play, the more you'll learn about what exactly happened in the series - and it's not as simple as you might think.As it was in the original game, in Psychonauts 2 you will not act in a real world only - quite often you'll have to enter someone's mind to get answers. Or change something in their behavior or perception of reality. The story focuses on mental health - and you'll get to see the minds of characters who suffer from different mental problems - addiction, panic attacks, stress, anxiety, depression, PTSD, etc. While the game is very humorous and lighthearted, it doesn't make fun of those mental problems, and they are never a punchline to a joke. The story itself also has a lot of plot twists - and while some are not exactly hard to predict, there will be some twists that you won't see until they'll happen. To put it simpler - the storyline is wonderful.Yet, there are some things that players might not like. The first problem is politics - while there are no specific real-world countries, the story focuses on a country called Grulovia - which is, IMHO, reminds of a history of a pre-revolutionary Russia, with some things changed and/or renamed here and there. IMHO, it's not a problem at all, but some people might find not like it. Second problem is a story of a married gay couple. Frankly, I don't have a problem if it is written good enough. The problem is that in this case it seems EXTREMELY forced - even if it is actually kinda matters to the story. Anyway, I warned you. Personally, I still find the game's story to be excellent, I just believe it would be better if this exact substory would be handled better than it is in a released game. Oh well, let's continue.How does it play, anyway? Well... Good. In terms of gameplay, it plays pretty much like the original game, but with some things changed to be better. For example, telekinesis becomes much more useful, and its usage is similar to Control - you can grab something and throw it into an enemy. Fighting system became better and faster than before. Some powers were nerfed for the sake of balance, but there are no useless abilities. Some powers (like shield and invisibility) were removed, but there are some new powers. You can also upgrade your powers and your gear, or buy pins that will change some gameplay aspects or visuals. In terms of movement - it's much more fluid now and Raz learned some new tricks. Basically about gameplay - it's kinda same but new. Since the original game is still good in terms of gameplay, this one is even better.What about visuals? Oh, you shouldn't worry about that. The game looks wonderful, sometimes looking like it's a playable Pixar movie. Graphics, animations, textures - everything looks great. The main part of visuals it this game is, of course, worlds within heads of characters. All those worlds are unique, some offer a change in aesthetics, some offer you new gameplay features, some levels do both. I'm afraid I won't be able to describe some best parts of the game but believe me - levels are unique, crazy and great.Ok, now sound. Damn it's good. All actors are back again, and it's like there were no 16 years between games. There are also new characters and new voice actors - and of course Jack Black is here too. And he's singing. Do you really need anything else, really?Joking aside, sound is good, voice acting is good, and music is good too. A lot of music you might recognize from the original game, but there are some new songs and new music. New music fits without any dissonance, new songs are great, AND there's a song by Jack Black. So you shouldn't worry, it's all good, even better than it was before.In the end, is this game good. YES. Should you play it? YES. It's one of the best games in a current year! Yep, it's not absolutely perfect, but it doesn't matter. You really should give some attention to this game. It fully deserves it.

_childDocuments_.review: i really enjoyed this game, i am a huge fan of the first one, so it should come as no surprise that i liked this one a lot. now, that being said there are a few issues ive had with this game that i feel need addressing-mental illness portrayal/enemy varietyi feel like they really pushed this aspect of the game in your face a lot. every new enemy would be some spin on a mental issue. for example, the enemy named "judge" was meant to represent self judgement, etc. now, there is nothing wrong with these enemy types, and i think they add a lot of good the the game, but i dont see why they had to push the mental illness narrative to 11. also, there arent unique enemy types for each brain. every time a new enemy appears, from that moment on, it is in every brain. there were no "unique" enemies like stage actors or the rainbow squirts. both of which are unique to certain brains you visit. overall, i felt this could have been done a lot better.-level designthere were some levels that were absolutely phenomenal in their design, but i had issues with a lot of them. Most levels boiled down to "this character has this problem, lets make that the basis for our entire level". for example, there is a gay alcoholic character in the game. half of his brain is platforming over alcohol bottles, and the other half is platforming, but on gay wedding cakes. Overall, just waaay too on the nose, and not interesting. i felt myself missing levels like "the milkman conspiracy" where, the whole level wasnt giant milk bottles, but instead, an entire journey through twisted streets and eyes looking at you from every angle, blending in with secret agents to figure out who the milkman is. this game just isnt the same.-charactersohhh boy the characters. a lot of them are from the previous installment, all of which keep their original charm, but are now background characters (except for 1). a few of the new characters are good, but overall, the new characters are mostly just annoying to be around. -ploti dont actually mind the plot. theres a few good twists.i rate the game a 7/10. might be lower if i didnt have such a love for the first game. you should still get this, but wait for a sale. (GET THE FIRST GAME ITS SOOO GOOD)

_childDocuments_.review: Even after seeing bits and pieces of this game for a long while up to launch, the one thing that made me pick it up wasn't gameplay or writing, but the fact that it's also preceded by a mental health advisory. This advisory, well-written and considerate, is the start of the game's rock-solid core of care and consideration. Where the first game stumbled in how it showed the mentally ill, and ways of "treating" their illnesses, this game shows how- even in a world of bizarre psychic brainscapes- it's possible to be sensitive in how you show and care for these people. And as a bonus, that level of care and extra attention extends to the rest of the game too, from the creativity in the art and level design, to how good the game feels to play. One of the very few games I'm more than glad to have paid full price for, because it's been worth every cent for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Psychonauts 2 is 3D adventure platformer about the human mind. The game takes place literally right after the VR game, Raz finally arrives at the mother lobe, but quickly it's known that there's a mole in the Psychonauts. The story is very good, that wraps up the plot nicely. As good as the story is, the main thing that makes this such a great game, is that they actually brought in a mental health expert to help design the game to depict mental issues as accurately as possible, and it does it well. Not to mention, the they improved on the art design and the levels so much. They bring back the old psychic powers plus two new ones, time slow and a mental archetype. This game out-does the first one by miles, very few sequels can do that, and you can tell that developers cared about making the best possible game. And I give this 10/10. *Possibly 2021 GOTY*

_childDocuments_.review: My expectations for this game were pretty low to start (I've never had a good experience with a game that came out 3 years after its original release date), and slightly lower after a short tutorial I didn't care for, but once I got into the second level proper, it became wildly obvious this game is even better than the original. With more in-depth writing, a somehow more vast overworld (though it takes a while to unlock the overworld), and a POST-GAME thank you for not forcing a reload of an old save at the end of the plot, it's honestly a great adventure.Though they made it harder to abuse the psyball in this one. I think I only did a few unintended routes I was supposed to have a different power for, and none of them were particularly level-breaking (sorry Tim I am NOT riding the venicular more than once). In the first game you could use the psyball to do some real unintended platforming

_childDocuments_.review: An incredibly worthy sequel and a great game in its own right.I consider the original Psychonauts to be one of my very favorite games of all time, and this is pretty much a perfect way to continue the series. It's a thorough and imaginative expansion of the original world, mechanics, and cast. All the new powers have interesting uses in and out of combat with plenty of old favorites returning as well. The mental worlds are quite varied with some very unexpected theming and clever ideas, while still working in callbacks to the original (my personal top 3 being ). The new and returning cast of characters is quite good, with Forsythe, Lizzie, Adam, Frazie, and Gisu being particular favorites of mine. Even the trademark Psychonauts attention to detail with things like character reactions and ability reactions is also back in full force, along with original's great sense of humor. The story was great and twisty as well, and while I called a few of the turns it was still fun to see them through and certain ones still caught me off-guard. And that whole ending sequence was phenomenal, just about the perfect way to tie everything together.
