_childDocuments_.review: This game is really great, with one glaring flaw that prevents me from recommending it. Until you notice this flaw, you will be having the time of your life, and after you notice, all enjoyment is sucked out of the game.The slipstream.It gives you so much speed and works from such long range that it creates a super strong rubber banding effect. There's no point to being in front, as everyone else can just catch up to you in no time. There's no point to use a boost, as everyone behind you can steal your speed. There's no point in even trying to be fast as nothing you do matters until the very end.This effectively means that the best strategy to win is to race meaninglessly with the rest of the pack for 2 laps and a half while saving boosts, and then pop them all at the end to get first right before the finish.There's also a distinct lack of a risk-reward loop. Once you get a feel for the game's handling, there's nothing to really do besides drift corners, as the tracks are so wide that you can pretty much co-exist with other drivers.If this one issue were fixed, I would recommend this game, but as it stands it's a no from me.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: A good arcade racer with some weird design decisionsLikes:I love the whole retro arcade vibe. From the clean untextured graphics, to the catchy music and the overenthusiastic announcer. It captures the aesthetics of a 90's era Sega cabinet perfectly.The driving itself is very intuitive. I play with a gamepad and never had to lookup the controls. Right trigger to accelerate, left trigger brake/drift, and A to boost. You gain boost by drifting and lose boost by crashing into things. Boost can be activated once your boost meter reaches a certain threshold.This is a interesting system, especially in time-trial (my favorite mode) where optimizing your boost usage becomes extremely important in order to do well.Dislikes:The global leaderboard for time-trial only shows the top 10. Come on guys, everyone (including me) wants to know their global rank. Improving your global rank is one of the main motivators when trying to improve your times.There is no replay feature in time-trial, whereas there is one for normal races... why?There are several characters in the game, each have 4 unique cars. But it seems like one specific car from one specific character is the outright fastest, making all the other cars and characters essentially useless.Racing and time-trial use a different driving model, so the skills you build up in one mode don't translate one-to-one to another mode. A baffling design decision. Overall:Whether you will enjoy this game depends on your expectations. The gameplay is fine. Personally I don't care too much about racing others, either AI or online. I prefer to race my ghost and try and set the best lap time possible, and for that the game (barely) works well enough. In combination with the overall look I would give it a 7/10.However the game is quite light in overall content/features, so maybe wait for a sale or some future updates.

_childDocuments_.review: For the 20 euro you're supposed to pay, you don't really get a lot with this game. The core gameplay mechanics are weird to learn and definitely hard to master, albeit because of the wrong reasons. Tracks are often nothing but a NASCAR 0-style plucked into different scenarios with drifts that feel really stiff and awkward. And if you don't have boosts on your hand, there is no way to win a race with good skills. I'd rather wait for a sale or buying another racing game instead.

_childDocuments_.review: Nothing good to say about this game (but the drift, drift is OK).- Rubber banding is a plague. The races has a "Groundhog day" feeling, You always compete against 2 to 4 opponents (based on difficulty), you will always pass them and then they will pass you and try to ram you. If they succeed your race is over (but in normal difficulty). The most convenient way to win races is to build your booster level and boost 2 or 3 times on the final straight (just lame).- Nothing screams retro or arcade to me. Not the cheap placed "Easter eggs", reminders of other arcade games like Daytona or hydro thunder, not the use of a Sega-ish announcer not even the Virtua rally aesthetic, because the game-play is mediocre at best.- Use of bad cheap stereotypical humor.- Main "career mode" is meh at best, normal tournaments are boring, hard and expert difficulty are irritating, and the fact that you can't restart the race (it restarts the GP) is frustrating. They could implement the progression system into the game instead of making a shop to buy skins.- Bad optimization with choppy framerate on high settings and in some circuits on medium (Ryzen 5 5500U and RTX 3050).Avoid this one as a plague.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been keeping an eye on this game ever since it had the working title as "Racing Apex". It originally hinted at having VR support, weapons, and a unique co-op vehicle combat mode where one person could drive while the other player was a gunner on the roof of the car. Unfortunately, none of those planned features made it into the final game, which is now named "Hotshot Racing". I was still eager to play this game because of the retro polygon art style, which reminded me of Virtua Racing and the original Ridge Racer. My main problem with the game right now is how poorly optimized it feels on my PC. My specs are a 4GHZ AMD FX, 16GB RAM, and a Nvidia GTX 1070. You would think that a simple looking game such as this would offer silky smooth frame rates on my 144hz 1080p monitor, but no, for some reason the game randomly stutters and freezes constantly throughout a race.All technical hurdles aside, I stubbornly played through a set of races, which reminded me a lot of how Mario Kart games are structured. You play 4 consecutive races and try to win a gold cup. Cool, whatever. Something seemed off about the way the game played though. It reminded me of Road Rash 64, where all of the racers where tightly grouped together in an invisible bubble. No matter how terrible or well I played, I was always in close proximity to the other race cars. Even if I stocked up on the boost meter, which refills as you drift, I couldn't get very far ahead of anyone else.This type of gameplay mechanic keeps races close and "interesting" in theory, but it ends up feeling frustrating to lose a race because the AI is always rubberbanding back and forth. Even if you race flawlessly and time your boosts perfectly, the AI is always right behind you in your slip stream. Running into walls or knocking other cars into them seem to have very little effect as well, since you basically bounce off everything and recover instantly.Overall, I am left feeling very underwhelmed by this game. If you play it split-screen for a quick arcade-like experience with friends, there is some fun to be had, but there isn't enough here to differentiate itself from the sea of other generic racing games. As of now, the game is barely playable and very ordinary regardless.

_childDocuments_.review: It is a fun and simple racing game, easy to pick up and a little difficult to master. The mechanics are exceptionally arcade-y. And going for 1st place from the start doesn't guarantee win because the slipstream is very powerful.The NPCs love to ram tho, sometimes mess up your racing line and punt you to the wall, very typical of average drivers. The Drift cars are almost irrelevant due to their poor speed and acceleration when racing in Expert mode (unless you master the game REALLY well) so there needs a slight balancing issues.Also I can't seem to play Online mode on Steam Deck; the game exits out when I tried to play it.Overall, a very fun, very simple circuit racing game with very fun mechanics used, and that's purty much it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really really fun but the multiplayer is super broken, even for private games which is a huge bummer because me and my friends used to have so much fun playing this. The AI can also be really unapologetically rubberband-y they almost never fall behind and wrecking them does almost nothing, boosting does next to nothing to catch up to the frontrunners unless the AI decides it does. They can outpace you with boost even while not boosting but only when the game decides. It can be really jarring. But at the same time the music, the character, the cars and the generally arcady vibe is really unique especially nowadays. It's still a really fun game despite its flaws, I just wish that it was better because the game got next to no updates to my knowledge and seems to be abandoned by its developer.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, but definitely not perfect. It's super fun and I am totally happy with my purchase, but it has some glaring issues. GOOD - looks great, controls great, very fun. BAD - Difficulty controls speed and is poorly balanced (Normal is so slow it's boring, Hard is fast and fun but still really easy, but then Expert requires absolute perfection). THE AI - I'm OK with the AI being a bit aggressive, the problem is when they even tap you, it sends you flying into last place, so they either need to dial the aggression back or make it so that you aren't penalized as severely for bumping and grinding.  TRACKS- as I said , difficulty controls speed. So all the people complaining about track design are probably playing on normal, which is so slow its boring and you often don't even need to drift. On Hard or Expert (or in time trials and other modes) the track design is great.Edit: After some more time and practice with it, I'm changing my review.  The AI just pisses me off.  I'm beating staff ghosts in time trial no problem but I can't beat the damn Expert races because the AI just runs me off the road. BS.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: In spite of the discount-bin name and unimpressive branding, it's a fairly convincing arcade racing game. It kinda throws you right in, but pulling off drifts and making comebacks through slipstreaming and boosts makes for well-executed gameplay. The dynamic, pumping music and snappy sound effects/UI give the whole affair a sense of high energy. Details such as the way the cars make collisions help to sell their physical presence. The 'retro visuals' can often cut corners, but the jagged scenery and unimpressively-shaped cars are passable once the world starts whizzing past you. Just don’t let the polygonally nightmarish humans get under your skin. The game would be worth picking up during a generous sale if some no-questions-asked fast-paced racing seems appetizing to you.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: This is not a great game.Mind you, I'm not *panning* it: for people like me that hate the super technical "take the curve at that precise angle and use digital controls" races, Hotshot racing is nice, especially at the start.And yet...I'm writing this review after the equivalent of throwing the controller at the screen (fortunatly I play with a keyboard and that helped me save both...).I'm trying hard to be equanimous but I can't ignore how, the game suffers from 2 problems mainly:- if you are trying to get something more than the "bumper cars" feeling you got when you just started playing, the cheating AI becomes increasingly taunting- most cars become complete trash at expert difficulty, leaving you a selection of 3-4 decent car at maximum. Mike cars, in particular, look like a bad joke.Hotshot racing is all about diminishing returns: you start full of enthusiasm and anticipation, but when you reach Expert the game doesn't give you anything (but rage...) anymore.Thats said, the graphics are nice and very retro, the characters entertaining and I spent 22 hours on this before hating it with all my guts, so I'm giving it a regretful thumbs up...2.5/5

_childDocuments_.review: Played this game in the beta testing phase as well as now. I can only say it is one of the most fun experiences in an arcade racing game! No race position is certain because of how powerful slipstreaming is. Drifting is so much fun! Cars have quite a nice variety to them and the characters interactions are nice. However, the game can be called rather short, as its grand prix championships can be done very fast. But hey, there are 763 customizable parts ready to unlock so it is a nice achievement to work for but it will take you probably more than a hundred hours. Online is where the fun is at, since you have cops&robbers and "drive or explode" or normal races to compete with your friends. There is also a ranked system, not sure how it works yet. It gets super satisfying once you get good at the game, however there will be many pushes from other players from behind because of slipstreaming, so don't blame them if they can't avoid you. Overall, the game right now does not have much else to offer, but I heard there will be more game modes & free DLCs coming, so in the end it will be worth it.Noticed some problems with controllers, however I had a generic controller that I managed to make it work from the Steam controller settings screen. I saw it can be fixed for all if you unplug every controller except the one you want to use. So maybe look around more out there how to fix the problem yourself instead of leaving a negative review with 0.1 hours of playtime because the controller doesn't work. There are solutions.

_childDocuments_.review: Not recommended, but just barely.I love racing games of all kinds and wanted to enjoy this one more than I did. The graphics have an appealing low poly charm and the feel of the vehicle handling makes for great arcade racing on the surface. There is an interesting drift mechanic to charge your nitro boost that could be a great concept, but it leads to the game's downfall. The excessive rubber banding, which seems to be intentional, forces you to drift needlessly and excessively to have that boost to pass at the very end. That sort of defeats the purpose of any strategy if you are always doing the same thing to win. If this were to be balanced better, then I would enjoy this much more. Also, the overall amount of content is very lacking for the price. This one was so close, but misses the mark for me.

_childDocuments_.review: WHAT I LIKED--Has that fun arcade racing feel! -Races are short and sweet-Good variety in vehicles. -The AI in cops and robbers is RELENTLESS and very fun. -Lots of customization -Colorful environments. -16 maps and 16 mirrored tracks are plenty. -Cops and robbers and drive or explode are actually fun game modes. WHAT I DISLIKED--Its very hard to distance yourself from other cars since the catchup system is very forgiving.  It can get pretty annoying when you boost 4 times in a row and the person behind you that didn't boost once just has to follow your tail and they'll be right next to you seconds later.  This is the case for easy and hard difficulty.  In expert mode much this is much less noticeable.-While I have been able to find lobbies frequently, i'm sure the longevity of the game is not very high as it has low players atm. -Every time I turn the game on it sets volume to maximum again.  Very annoying. Its pretty fun for an arcade racer and will definitely satisfy you if thats what you're looking for.  It really reminds me a bit of Motorstorm without the destruction, crash focus, or environment changes in the race.  It will not take long to complete all grand pris and online can only keep you satisfied for so long with the amount of cars and maps in the game.  This game will most likely need content to keep it fresh as this is a racing game and the gameplay is repetitive in nature.  Hotshot racing is worth the pickup if you see a sale or need that Arcade Racing kick.  FINAL RATING: 7.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Hotshot Racing is exactly what I wanted out of an arcade racer. Sumo Digital's done it again!First the driving physics. In many arcade racers the physics are usually an after-thought, where the steering and the grip levels feel weird, flimsy and inconsistent, and how and when your car decides to drift feels completely random. In Hotshot Racing, everything feels consistent and understandable: Every car can has a good sense of momentum, and they can throw their weight around satisfyingly, causing your grip levels to vary depending on which of your tires are loaded as you're manuevering. And when they drift, you can *feel* that it's driven by a proper physics system, so you can actually have nuance in how and when you drift.Just to give an example, one track has two sharp right-hand turns, each separated by a brief straight (like this: ┌-┐), and you have to really manage your momentum and drifting to get through them. If you drift too sharply into the first turn, straighten out, and then try to drift again through the 2nd turn, you'll probably just hit the wall. With the reason being that your momentum from the sharp turn/drift overloaded your leftmost tires, briefly causing too much overall grip, and thus causing a slight delay in your ability to get into that 2nd drift in time. The solution to this is to either enter at a much gentler angle so that your weight distribution is even across your tires, or to try to do a very gentle drift through the entire thing.So now that's two entire paragraphs on the driving physics. I place a huge amount of emphasis on this because the physics makes or breaks any arcade racer in my opinion, and it just feels so damn good in Hotshot Racing. It's a pleasant mix of being exagerated arcadey nonsense, and yet it's nuanced enough to make it challenging and fun to experiment with.Physics aside, everything else is very well put together. The tracks and locales are all detailed and memorable, and the AI is consistently fun and sweaty to race against, each and every time. The AI can also make mistakes and there can be quite a variation in where each of them'll end up by the time the race ends, making the races feel lively and dynamic. No AI conga lines here like other games, where an algorithm pre-decides how well each racer will do before the race even starts!More on the AI: I honestly can't tell if the AI uses Rubber Banding or not (maybe they're just very good at drafting?), but it works well. The AI is always just behind you, and they're incredibly aggressive, and can put a fair amount of effort into trying to screw you over. I hate it, but I love it. And it makes every race feel all the more exhilerating, because you know there's always a chance of victory being snatched away from you - or from your enemies, since they screw up too. And I don't mind that, because each race is an average of 2 to 2.5 mins long anyway, so restarting a grand prix isn't the end of the world.And finally, the standard blargh about "muh presentation, muh music, muh characters" goes here. All I'll say is that it's modeled after dat mid-90s flat-shaded polygon charm, and it feels nostalgic and authentic.So overall, I'd very highly recommend this game. And while the aggressive AI might make the game inaccessible for some, for more patient people like me, I think it'll make for a really fun 5-hour romp. It's just the right mix of arcadeyness, nuance, challenge and style.

_childDocuments_.review: If Slipstream was a way to enjoy classic racing action in a modern title, then Hotshot Racing is the ability to play early 2000's arcade racers without spending any quarters. The game is clearly inspired by the early 3D arcade racing cabinets of the late 90s and early 00s. Regardless of the source material, Hotshot Racing is an incredible racing title in its own right. The game is graphically gorgeous, representing the absolute pinnacle of low-poly, color-blocked 3D modeling. The cars are good looking, the environments you drive through are inspired, and the whole aesthetic is perfectly put together. You drive through all of the various trope tracks that you expect - a casino, a desert, an alpine forest, etc. The devs pay true homage to the classic racing arcade games of the past. The cars drive like they feel like they should - you have or don't have control when it feels right. Slipping around corners and slamming into walls teaches you about racing lines and braking techniques while slipstreaming teaches you how to pass cars. The racing feels tight and engaging all while being wrapped up in a nostalgia-bating aesthetic. The soundtrack is awesome, reminiscent of late 90s, early 00s Sonic titles. Overall, the game is an absolute blast and I love picking it up again every few months to play through a cup or two. Certainly a good casual racing game for those who don't mind throwing on the nostalgia glasses every once in a while.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is exactly as advertised. I love the old, blocky "Virtua" art style from the Sega era of arcade racers. It has a nice compliment of characters with their own cars to choose from and customize; to which earning your customizations is a nice touch. The soundtrack is very upbeat and reminiscent. The controls are easy to grasp and the drifting is very fun. The AI seems to have a sort of "speed compensation" for when you're leading, so you don't get too far ahead for it not to be a challenge--which isn't necessarily good or bad if you're already used to that gimmick from other games. All-in-all, a very solid title! Nice work!

_childDocuments_.review: Fun enough to be worth it. After anticipating the release of this game, I held off when some reviews were meh. I found the game selling for a price I was willing to pay to try it. The AI definitely is rubber-bandy (it's basically a game about making sure you have boost for the last leg of the race) and there are some performance issues and stutters on certain tracks. I believe the AI makes sense for a game like this, it would be boring to get ahead and never see the AI again. I had no issues using a controller, X1 controller on PC worked immediately. I have had a lot of fun finishing 2 single player GPs on expert so far. Yes there are only 2 more GPs for a total of 4 right now. There are a few other game modes and online as well. But they have said there will be free additional content (cars + tracks). I fully believed the reviews that suggested to skip it, but I found a price I was willing to pay for it and discovered that the fun factor is there. If they smooth out the performance and add more content it will be well worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: Ive waited so long for Hotshot racing. Jimmy Broadbent renewed my vigor and made me excited to finally lay my hands on it. I love it. There are parts I'm not too keen on. And I do have some pretty nagging complaints. Overall though, Im really enjoying it. Firstly. I really do struggle to call this a 90's style arcade racer. This is very much a modern racer. I always remember those old arcade games being somewhat heavy. This game plays physics fast and loose. Now, that isn't a complaint. I enjoy how light and responsive the cars feel. I do have a complaint in the art style. In particular the character models. I enjoy low poly art, I do, but...I dont know. I always remember 90's arcade racers having a sorta "smudged" look to them. Low poly mixed with zero shading or texturing leads to some of the cars looking non-descript. For example, at some angles I can tell a certain car has a wheel well, but at others the car just looks like a solid square racing down the road. Next are controls. You have to drift. You have to. You cannot win unless you rip that car sideways and send it. Cars do not turn. You can beg and plead until you go blue in the face, but the only way you are getting around that corner while still being able to keep up with the pack, is to Tokyo Drift the ever loving hell out of that car. If you are into drifting, this is going to have you salivating all over your keyboard. If you dont like drifting...well...Im a sucker for a good racing line. Arcade or Sim. A good racing line gives me the biggest of virtual boners. But the drifting is so well done and fun that I can over look it. Rubber banding, oh holy rubber banding. Like. Good lord. I know that the point of rubber banding is to keep the action flowing and that is important in an arcade racer. But, by god, do I despise rubber banding. It just sucks so much fun out of racing. I can yeet my car into a wall at speed and fall to the back of the pack and still have a decent chance to regain my position in that same lap. Meanwhile, other drivers will rocket past me then suddenly come to a screeching halt and allow me to pass them again. Its really jarring at times. In my experience, playing on expert does ease this considerably. I cannot tell you how cringe worthy the dialogue is. The drivers talk NONSTOP. Thankfully you can turn it all off from the options, but this also disables the announcer. Which depending on how your race is going, may be for the best. Overall, Im still having fun. If rubber banding was removed and an option was added to suppress dialogue, then this game would be great. I think adding an option to remove boost, thereby making drifting slower, would be going a bit far, but hey, could be alright.

Both modes which are chaotically fun and gives you a nice option besides just the normal racing.The only problem I have is that the AI could use a bit of work. _childDocuments_.review: A fun racer paying homage to the arcade classics, Hotshot Racing is a charming and accessible ode to games like Daytona USA and OutRun that has enough personalisation and variety to actually keep it interesting. Swap out visual elements of 32 different cars, divided into categories based on Speed, Drift, Acceleration, or a balance of the three. Change steering wheels, spoilers, liveries, exhausts, headlights and tail lights, etc - a neat extra touch of customisation. Races are heavily rubber-banded though, meaning your opponents will frequently overtake you and then slow down after disappearing down the road for a little bit, allowing you time to catch up with relative ease. This isn't actually quite as annoying as I thought it was going to be, primarily because you're also able to catch up at the same rate as everyone else and you spend more time jostling with other drivers, as opposed to vanishing ahead never to be seen again. However, one downside to this is that little noticeable difference can be felt in the game's three difficulty levels. Anyone acing normal races will have no problems on expert. Despite this, the visual style is cute, multiplayer adds to the overall race variety and there's enough fun in the drifting alone for me to warrant a recommendation.

I'd probably put about $2 in it and never play it again. $20 may be pretty cheap for a game nowadays, but it's hard to swallow for... this.

_childDocuments_.review: Charming arcade racer that provides a satisfying feeling of speed. The cars feel surprisingly different. This allows you to pick the playing style that suits you best: drift wildly around corners and use the earned boost on straights, or try to drive a bit more precisely along the imaginary ideal racing line. The rubberbanding and aggressive AI is bearable in this game. I also appreciate the broad choice of camera positions (I prefer the bonnet view) and the option to turn controller vibration off.

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels fantastic to play. I admit, I'm really not a racing game aficionado unless you count Mario Kart, but I haven't really been able to put down this game since I bought it. I saw some people talking about performance issues and controller issues, but I haven't had either. In terms of controllers though, I'm using a Dualshock 4, which usually has problems on Steam but has been perfectly fine. To those of you experiencing controller issues, it's likely not an issue with the game itself, but with Steam's native controller support trying to keep you in a menu configuration. I have had this issue with even well optimized games like Dark Souls 3. I  have experienced one bug in my almost 4 hours of playing, and it was just a visual glitch. This is a day one game. If you like the gameplay (which is fantastic), give it some time for the kinks to be ironed out. The performance issues likely aren't poor optimization, they're way more likely conflicting with your hardware in some way. This is an independent developer, they don't have the resources to individually check for optimization issues on every hardware configuration, and will need normal bug reports to iron it out instead of trying to kill a great game day one. Thank you.

_childDocuments_.review: A great throwback to the classic arcade racing games like Virtua Racing, Daytona USA and Outrun. The art and design is thick with that 90's arcade aesthetic. The track designs are interesting, exotic and easy to remember. The roster of drivers, cars and customisation is great. However, I do have a few issues. Rubber-banding is incredibly prominent. No matter how fast you go, how many times you boost or take corners perfectly, you'll always be battling for first place. It's not a massive issue, it does keep things interesting, but it can be incredibly frustrating. You'll always have somebody on your tail, no matter what you do. Each driver has four cars, each divided into a separate category: Balanced, Acceleration, Speed and Drift. However, the only two that seem to matter are acceleration and drift. A car's speed rating doesn't seem to matter in this game. Combined with the rubber banding, you'll constantly be battling for position with one or more cars that will be ranked slower than yours, which can be incredibly frustrating when combined with my final issue.The AI drivers are RIDICULOUSLY aggressive. I've seen this mentioned in a few other reviews. They'll just throw themselves into you regardless of where you are on the track. They'll sideswipe you, punt you from behind, push you into walls, spin you out and it can get really frustrating. I've had a few races ruined because of AI drivers just t-boning my car out of the blue while I'm drifting around the final turn of a race. They can knock your car about like they're Mohammed Ali and trying to retaliate is like being a one-legged man in an arse-kicking contest. You can't knock them about like they can do to you. I get that it's an arcade game, it's not meant to be simulation racing, but even in games like Daytona, I don't remember the AI drivers being as aggressive as the AI in Hotshot Racing.Despite these issues, it's a really fun game. It's a great love letter to the classic arcade racing games and it's a good dose of nostalgia which contrasts today's abundance of more realistic racing games. It just needs a few issues sorted out.

_childDocuments_.review: Hotshot Racing isn't particularly deep, but it does scratch that itch for a quick and fun, arcade-cabinet style race. The way the AI all bunch together and constantly boost around the track is pretty silly, and it's easy to win the Normal mode just by boosting past the whole pack right before the finish line. Turn up the difficulty, though, and you get a much more tactical and satisfying experience, even if the AI are a bit aggressive and can end your grand prix with a well-timed ram from behind.What Hotshot Racing lacks, in my opinion, is a proper campaign, something to really sink your teeth into and keep you playing from more than a few hours. The current grand prixs are just four races that only last two or three minutes each.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun game for what it is, I think it's worth its price but don't expect anything really crazy or out there. The handling physics suit the style, it's fun to slide around the pretty wide tracks (in most of the cars). The customization is also pretty fun and I will get a lot out of doing the challenges to unlock and buy all the options for each car. The real letdown of the game is the lack of real variation in both the tracks and the cars. While the tracks have some pretty zany scenery, the problem is that all the zaniness is in the scenery, not the tracks -- and all that scenery is going to waste as you're focusing on the road. Some 90 degree hard turns and maybe two actually hard hairpins -- the style easily would have supported more craziness like loops, almost-vertical banking turns, more changes in track width, crossroads, shifting grip levels (e.g. ice, snow, grass, rough terrain, or even slime or something), or even some intersections for some destruction derby, etc. The "Jungle" tracks have some changing surfaces but even that has less effect than in more realistic circumstances like for example Rallycross in the Dirt Rally series. The cars are also confusingly almost realistic to a fault (not counting the drift-happiness and nitrous boost). First I found this delightful, trying to find out the real life inspiration for each car. But overall this coupled with the drifty handling means there's not really that much "personality" to the vehicles, they're not that memorable. Again, a more realistic game can have a touring car with a lot of grip but not much speed or something like a Koenigsegg which has speed for days but can't handle the slightest turns. And after all this the cars are horribly unbalanced: two of them are completely OP because out of the three attributes "Drift" is pretty much useless (the car with a Drift stat of 4 can take a turn as good as the one with 10) and these two have the most Speed & Acceleration, while some are almost useless because of incredibly soft suspensions as if made from rubber bouncing around and making them hard to get out of a corner straight (and not balanced enough with acceleration or speed). The worst thing about the game however for me is the AI which is almost incapable of handling an overtake without contact (either when they overtake when they're being overtaken). From my overall experience there's no rubberbanding, strategic slipstreaming will help them enough in catching up (useful trick for the player as well), which is a plus. But their sometimes bafflingly aggressive driving style has left me (sometimes along with them) a lot of times in the wall and/or spinning out and dropping to last place because instead of taking the turn right they go left into me. I'd add that this also helps in catching up, as they do this with each other as well (so it's not just about picking on the player as some other games can feel), but as it's pretty much 7 against 1 it's mostly just frustration. And all this is also made worse by difficulty which is a shame as difficulty level also increases the overall speed of the game -- so I can choose to play on Hard and win but feel slow or go for Expert and satisfying speeds but get frustrated by the AI. Combining the last two points are the two extra modes, Crash & Burn and Cops & Robbers. These are almost okay in adding variation to the game, but as both rely very heavily on damage-by-contact, the AI's aforementioned aggressive driving style makes them incredibly adept competition. Played them until I managed to end up first and never wanted to play again. I hope there will be some more extra modes in the future -- even the first image in the "About" section on the Store Page shows a mode that's not in the game! -- but because of the AI I'm not confident they will add enough longevity. Final point: currently the player base seems very low, I haven't managed to find any online games to join. The devs have noted that "Quick Race" has bugs but I'd say for now only count on the single player modes.

_childDocuments_.review: It's an arcade racer in every sense of the word. If you were there in the early 90s with the Sega/Namco arcade racing revolution, this is that in all its low-polygon, fast visuals, limited tracks, obscenely rubber-banded Ai glory. It's a game designed for short, sharp bursts. Handles like Ridge Racer, on tracks like Virtua Racing, with cars like Scud Race. Go in expecting something you'd pay 50p a game for, and you'll be happy. The only complainers are youngsters who don't remember tight checkpoints and AI that adhere to the "somebody's right on your tail!" coin-eating ethos.

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of Outrun, Lotus II, Horizon Chase, Virtua Racing and other Arcade Retro Racers,I had high hopes in Hotshot Racing.So far, I had to admit that I am dissapointed, and here is why:1. The technical problems: -----------------------------------It kinda suprises me, that even though the game was in alpha/beta testing, the team obviously never tested if controllers work properly with their game. For me, (and many others) the game is unplayable with controller, since the mapping (which cant be editied) of the accelerator button doesnt work (only opens the pause menu). Other do not get their controllers to work at all. I cant believe no one noticed that during alpha/beta testing.The second big problem is the performance and lack of configuration options. On Laptops, the game runs without making use of the 3D Nvidia GPU and uses onboard instead. A problem most devs have solved by implementing a config menu where you can choose which GPU you want to use. In HSR, you have to manually configure that using the NVIDIA drivers tool. Something, not many people are aware of.Even with a proper Geforce 1060 and a i-7 CPU, the performance of the game is a nightmare. Yes you have 60FPS and more, but a little bit of smoke or spark effects or other randim things will cause stuttering and slowdowns. For a system running games like Forza 7 on high details, this is a no go. To get the feeling of speed, which is essential for an arcade racer, this needs a lot of optimization.2. Content / Game Design--------------------------------16 Tracks sound alot, but the track design is poor. Since the corners are not that sharp at all, and mostly s-corners, you can simple drive through them in a straight line. So there is no need to drift or to steer at all in nearly 50% of the corners, which is kind of boring experience.Overall, the game lacks content or features are just unfinished or half-baked. You can earn credits in the game, but you can only spend them for useless cosmetics, some totally rediculous. Why should I buy a new front bumper? 99% of the game, I see the back side of my car.Verdict:----------HSR isn't a bad game. If you are one of the lucky ones to get the controllers working and wanna go for a quick round, this is quite entertaining. However the game fails to resemble the old 90s arcade racers. The feeling of speed is bad due to bad optimization, and music and characters aren't convincing either.This become a awesome game, but lots of work is to be done to really finish it.

Cars are also extremely aggressive, trying to tailspin at literally every turn.These two issues combined make the game very frustrating as no amount of boost banking will stop enemies from clipping you as soon as the boost ends.Sumo Digital made some of my favourite games of all time with Outrun 2k6 (no longer on steam, due to licensing) and Sonic Racing Transformed but, since then, have seemed to really fallen off. It seems they misunderstood why those games were so great - with both sonic racing and this game having so many weird balancing issues that make the game unrewarding to play beyond a casual level.

_childDocuments_.review: While it's not the game it probably wanted to be (other reviews have likely mentioned the features that were removed over time) it's still a wonderful little racer. Glad to see that the arcade racing genre isn't stuck in the recent wave of Need For Speed/Forza Horizon clones.This game OOZES 90s-era flash and fun. No nonsense garbage social media story, no performance upgrade grinding for minor handling improvements, no barren open world to waste your time. Just a great, straightforward, lap-by-lap, speed-focused racing game. Love it.For the negative reviews:Anyone complaining about the strength of the rubber band AI don't really remember what arcade racers were like back in the day. This game lays somewhere between Burnout and the very EARLY Ridge Racer titles (Ridge Racer 1 and 2, particularly) with the visuals taking more inspiration from Virtua Racing and Daytona USA (the ports, not the arcade titles). Controller compatibility:Check your steam controller settings, the game was literally plug-in and play for everyone I know. No issues with gamepad (or even arcade sticks and keyboard)What it needs:More tracks, especially more varied ones. The tracks are great but there are very few "technical" courses, just a lot of ovals/wide circuits.More stuff to use your cash on:Earning money in game makes it super easy to buy anything you want. But once you get the customization stuff you want for each car, it's pretty much collecting dust. Some super expensive "prestige" type items or something would be very cool. Maybe vinyls or more customization options like boost fire colors, new music, or horns even?Better performance optimization:Experienced a couple of frame drops, running on a 2070 Super and i9-9700. That probably shouldn't happen considering the game's low-poly look.Lost Features:I remember following the game when it was still "Racing Apex". Hopefully some of the features lost along the way will make their way back in post-launch updates. Namely:-VR Support-More fully fleshed-out wheel and pedal support-More gamemodes-Visual damage (This is probably one of the more difficult ones. If it was brought back, I'd prefer it placed in the Cops and Robbers mode)Overall I'd give it a 7.5/10 (Far above average) for the excellent core gameplay and overall quality, but that could go up with some post-launch updates. Points lost are for inconsistent performance, limited content, and the significant amount of features cut that would've elevated the experience further. (Special thanks to whichever developer made Keiko's ending the same as Ryu's from Street Fighter 2, great touch.)

_childDocuments_.review: Racing and handling is pretty much what you'd expect from a game advertising itself as an arcade racer with boosts and drifting galore. Though simple at first, as is typical with any racing game this also has a skill ceiling that some may wish to explore. , AI drivers have a tendency to aggressively occupy the player's space and this is generally more prevalent on lower difficulty levels but is apparent across all. Often mirroring your movement, position and even boost timings at the start and throughout a race.Recall that above I mentioned Mario Kart? That's because the difficulty settings of medium/hard/expert correlate to 50cc/100cc/150cc that you get in Mario Kart. Meaning, playing on expert is actually a speed increase and not necessarily an increase in AI difficulty. You may find racing on 'harder' (read: faster) difficulty to be more of what you'd expect from an arcade racer, with drivers generally spread wider apart throughout a race track compared to them all huddled around you on the normal difficulty.I feel that the visual style of the game along with the colour palette used severely limits the overall variety and uniqueness that each level can achieve - but can appreciate that this is the style they chose.While there are six different race modes, without online multiplayer* you'll most likely settle on Grand Prix, Arcade or Time Trials.*Audio wise it sounds like something you'd hear at your local arcade (and that's great) - menu selection sounds are loud and crunchy, tyres screech every two seconds and the announcer shouts "Checkpoint!" each time you pass one.Music is actually pretty good too, especially the theme played on the main menu.It's worth noting that progression (in-game cash) is used purely for buying cosmetics (rims, spoiler, paintjob) which do not affect a vehicle's performance, as each vehicle has its own unique stats that cannot be changed. But beware, this game does not have cloud save so you will lose all progress when changing PCs!

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: I personally love this game. It's fun with friends and can be very enjoyable as a solo game. I do think it needs some balancing, but it is a fun time all around. To get into more specific stuff, the vehicles have three different attributes that affect how well they drive.Speed - Affects max speedAcceleration - Affects the rate at which you get to max speedDrift - Affects how sharply you can drift around cornersThese cars are characterized into Speed, Drift, Acceleration, and Balanced cars all which prioritized the attribute that they are named after. Balanced cars are meant to be the a Jack-of-All-Trades without being particularly good in any one area. All 32 cars have variations on these three attributes with some sharing the same amounts of these attributes. Most maps don't have that many sharp turns. From my experience, cars with lower max speed have a very hard time catching up to opponents compared to Speed cars. This is far more noticeable on Expert difficulty.There are three different difficulty levels that affect how fast your car moves (Normal, Hard, and Expert). There is contact in the races, so it highly incentivises you to put your opponents in the wall or pit them to crash.  That being said, the same can happen to you.Focusing on Arcade Races and GP's:The Grand Prix races consist of four races that put the player against 7 different computer players. The AI is fairly consistent between all three difficulties and can be both very forgiving and very punishing. I've had races on expert difficulties where I burnout on the starting line and 5 AI characters burnout with me. I've also had races where the AI puts me into a wall three times and forces me into lower positions. Thankfully, you don't need to finish first every race in a GP to get the gold. You just have to perform better than your opponents across all four races. The main mechanics that I think is the biggest downfall of these gamemodes are the boost mechanic combined with the slipstreaming mechanic. By slipstreaming and drifting, you fill a boost meter that stores four charges that you can use at any point in the race. As pointed out by other reviews, these boosts are better used at the end of the race in GP settings against AI. I have not had the opportunity to test this out in multiplayer games, but based off of time trials and racing with a friend, games that do not have AI will not suffer this problem. One thing that will be an issue is the slipstreaming. 2nd place has the biggest advantage going into the final turns in both multiplayer games and solo games. They fill their boost while gaining on the person in first. If they fill one bar of boost, they can rocket ahead of them. This is what I have noticed to be the biggest contributor to rubber banding in races. I have had only one or two races where I was a full checkpoint ahead of AI opponents, but I firmly believe that the slipstreaming mechanic makes it much worse.Other Game Modes:Hotshot Racing has four different game modes outside of the traditional Grand Prix. Vehicle attributes are less obvious in these game modes with the exception of Arcade Races.Arcade Races: 1 map races that function the same as GP races.Barrel Barrage: Races that allow you to place exploding barrels on the track. Each player has a health bar that goes down whenever they are contacted by players or the wall in certain areas or if they run into a barrel. Last one surviving or first to finish is the winner. These races become very chaotic with more laps.Drive or Explode: All racers must maintain a certain speed. This speed increases as the race progresses. There are health bars that function the same as in Barrel Barrage with the addition of losing health when you fall below the target speed. Last one alive or first to finish is the winner.Cops and Robbers: The weakest one in my opinion, but still a great amount of fun if you aren't focusing on score. Robbers must cross checkpoints in order to increase there bounty and not become a Cop. Cops must chase down Robbers and decrease there health to 0. When a Robber's health reaches 0, they become a cop and chase down the remaining Robbers. All surviving Robbers gain a survival bonus that increases their bounty. When a Robber becomes a Cop, the Cop that caused the Robber to turn gains the bounty of the Robber. Any assists get a partial reward. Cops are better rewarded for chasing down the robber that is further ahead since they will have the highest bounty, but the real winner is either the Robber with the highest bounty at the end of the race or (in the case that no Robbers remain) the Cop who took down the Robber with the highest bounty. Not a bad game for an $20 dollar price tag and a hidden gem in the March 2021 Humble Bundle. Edit: Small change for the price of the game. I would pay the $20 dollars for it due to the amount of content it offers, but it goes on sale for $8. If you are willing to wait, get it when it goes on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Hotshot racing is very much what it says on the tin - a take on those mid to late 90's arcade racers where the mechanics were go fast, drift and go faster.  The drifting reminds me a lot of the likes of scud race and outrun 2006. If you approach the game with the mindset of this effectively being an arcade racer (as what the name originally meant) it is great - you should not expect massive single player championship modes that are dominant in modern racing games but rather a more restraint approach where the fun comes from simply racing.There isn't too much content in the game as as far as I have found the unlockables are minor cosmetic items and new paint liveries but getting all of them does sort of busywork to pad game length which is a negative in my opinion but this is balanced out simply because these unlocks are so minor (the liveries are just different combinations of racing stripes at a core level for example).The track design is solid and so is the associated art but you can see where the incarnation as apex racing lingers as tracks are very wide so you have lots of space for nothing. This isn't an important criticism, just a point of note.I would say this is a solid 7/10 game. The game mechanics are polished and work as you expect, the environments are interesting and the a.i poses a good challenge but its certainly not excessive.Edit 11.09.20 A note to all you playing on normal - as far as I can tell increasing the difficulty also gives your car a faster top speed (along with the inherent tougher a.i) so playing on expert gives you maximum speed, maximum challenge.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the very definition of "flawed".The good:- Mechanically, it is very solid, drafting, drifting, and boost mechanics all very functional.- Visuals have a nice clean retro-3D style, which is a welcome reminder of great games past.- Giving each character 4 cars instead of 1 is a great idea, as is the visual customization of them.The bad:- Within under an hour of play, I encountered 3 glitches: The first was a frozen screen that crashed to desktop, the second was when an AI racer rammed me into a wall, I became "welded to it" and could not re-join the race, the third was a network error that kicked me from the party.- The game's AI rubber-banding is HARD, as in; at one point I had 3 AI racers in a perfect formation infront and then behind me; and in the results screen we were seperated by single-digits of micro-seconds.- The WORST element to this for me, is the outrun-style mechanic of just taking the game away if you don't cross a checkpoint in time.  This meant that, of the 12 races myself and friends played, for about a third of them, I didn't get to play for some chunk of the game.  Yes, you can say "git gud scrub", but how can I get good when I've just started the game, and I'm having the controller knocked out of my hands for screwing up once?  This mechanic is terribly implemented. The end result: I refunded the game.  There's certainly potential here, but the game needs polish, and I'd suspect; more to do for players to stick around long-term.

The background for these tracks are meaningless, as are the themes, because at the end of the day you're driving on tarmac in a circuit, rinse and repeat 16 times.Now for the characters. They've got little messages they say during races in response to stuff like getting hit or driving into a wall, which is pretty cool, until you realise they  and there's no option to turn it off either. _childDocuments_.review: [Scroll down to the bottom of the review for the TL; DR]   Come on devs you were on the right track to create a fun old school racing game of yesteryear! This game looks like it was created based on great games like Ridge Racer, Sega's VR Racing, and Daytona USA, all amazing games for their time!  The problem with this game is while it does bring all the good things those previous mentioned games had, it also brings the bad as well.     First and foremost, why would you ever purposely choose to bring back "rubber band" AI?  That was literally the number one thing all racing fans complained about in racing games of that time.  Second, why are all the AI drivers in this game super aggressive regardless of the difficulty level setting?  I have tried going around all AI drivers with a wide berth and, regardless of who it is, the AI will literally crash into you. This will always, at the least, slow you down or, at the most, straight up cause you to crash into something like a wall and come to a complete stop.  Depending on where you are in the race this will determine if the race is even possible to finish in first place and that is not fun at all.  Third, why does it seem like races cannot be won unless you save your Nitrous for the last quarter of the last lap for every race?  Again, this probably harkens back to the original issue of "rubber band AI", which if you fix that problem, it will also likely fix this problem.   Now while I did mention the main things that are making this game bad, there are some good things to the game as well.  For example, I love the old school arcade graphics and sound!  That echoing voice telling you your time has been extended is exactly what you would hear in an old school arcade racer, again I absolutely love it!  The graphics are a kind of mashup between Ridge Racer, Sega's Virtua Racing, and Daytona USA, as well as mixed in with cell shading textures.  All in all, it looks good, although some of the characters could use a little more detail.  The gameplay is almost an exact copy of the old school Ridge Racer drift style gameplay.  If you loved how Ridge Racer used to control in the days of the arcade game and PS1/PS2/PS3 games, you will love how this game controls.   TL; DR This game has some good pros and a couple of really bad cons.  The pros are the game has old school arcade graphics and sound with fun Ridge Racer style control.  The cons are the game has really bad "rubber band" AI as well as the AI is always super aggressive regardless of difficulty level.  This can make the game extremely frustrating to play on even the easiest difficulty level.  I really wanted to give this game a thumbs up, but until the devs fix the "rubber band" and overly aggressive AI, I just can't give it my recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: Dear arcade racing fans, Give the game 10 hours of your time before you judge it. It requires this playtime from you, the more you play the more you realise what this game is trying to give you: an orgasm Think back to the times of the early noughties when you were a kid and played through that racing game despite the issues in difficulty you had, you played through it, grinding on it and found out, guess what? THAT was Awesome! I'm satisfied! This is like one of those times. The golden era!Recommend for: Fans of the genre who think this is what you've been waiting for all these years, yes it's good in that way. Driving physics impress me, it's good, All Audio does in a way too. Sounds fun. Fun fact game runs on the infamous outrun engine. The driving physics/mechanics remind me a lot of driving in Burnout 2 and the boost chaining! This is good. I'll probably end up getting a lot of replayability out of it just for this to see how far I can take it. And see if boost chaining the whole track is possible whilst looking stylish. Customisation is nice and varied. This game has good content and will keep you busy. Personal gripes:Flat wide tracks for the most part. Yes there are subtle elevation changes on all and it fits the style they're going for, but I'd KILL for even more elevation change sections overall and varied track width on some. I love me some rollercoastersWhy don't we get good AI for this? To push the genre? If we had half-decent modern racing AI, I'd literally have my review changed to recommended. Not recommeded for: casuals, here's why:Piss poor controller config support, no rebindings in game unless on keyboard, unless using steam controller mappings. Wth! I did finally manage to utlize steam controller mappings to work flawlessly but for a casual, they won't be able to figure it out, but yes you can make any controller work, including the analog and vibration, works flawlessly but you might not have vibration adjustment.Straight up Bad Rubber banding AIKind of Bad optimisation depending on your PCDead online I think...Game substitutes unlocking content for the difficulty in earning all GP trophies. Kinda worksEverything else is ok.Reviewing this game has been difficult since I decided to review it way too early in my playtime(almost unfairly so for this game). And have changed this review from Not recommended to recommended solely because it does the nostalgia fans justice.TL;DR If you haven't refunded it already I actually think this game is only a problem for modern casuals who have never played a 90s game or Ps1 title to date. Hardcore racing arcade fans will happily ignore what the minor "problems" are cause everything else is solid. Amazing game.

_childDocuments_.review: + Beautiful PS1/N64 era aesthetic with lots of detail in the environments.- Circuits are flat and bland, and too wide in my mind. OG Ridge Racer, Daytona USA had more complexity.+ Nice selection of cars.- Cars locked behind characters, more on them in a moment to see why that is a negative.+ Wonderful car models.- Ugly and scary looking characters, less detailed models would have been better.+ Some fun visual customisation unlocks.- No performance customisation at all.+ Car sounds, soundtrack, and announcer are spot on and suit the 90s vibe.- Character voices and personality are awful, one of the worst elements of the game. Can't mute them as it also mutes announcer.+ Works fine on gamepads. I'm using a Wireless 360 pad myself, no issues. Those who are having problems is probably down to Windows 10 or Steam settings, not the game itself.- No gamepad remapping. No issue for me as I prefer the triggers accel/brake and shoulders for gearing style. But many are moaning that it does not match NFS and similar.+ Runs fine at 60fps on my Win 8.1 i7 4790k 4ghz, GTX 970 4GB, 32GB DDR3 ram system at 1080p.- No support for fancier monitors, have your 144mhz at your peril as it induces screen tearing and some physics issues.+ Great base look.- No visual options at all other than "Low" or "High" and Vsync. I mean, is this a mobile game?+ AI is tough, making use of some rubber banding and the games OP slipstream mechanic.- AI just wants to pit and punt you, in all modes, not just Cops and Robbers. And that slipstreaming really is OP and needs to be toned down a little.Is it fun? Sure, kinda. Do I like it? Ehhhhh, mayyybbbeee? Doesn't feel the same as the 90s era titles that it is trying to emulate. The courses and the characters are the weakest points for sure. is to wait for updates and pick it up at 25-50% off. I have refunded it once already, but I'm keeping it for now as it isn't expensive. But, still, not really worth the money.At this time, it is too on the fence. I am going to go against my earlier statement regarding recommending waiting for updates and a sale. Simple reason is that it is clear that the dev team are not really capable of bringing the enjoyment to this title, like the 90s racers we all loved did and which they are trying to emulate.Even with patches to remove the punting AI, even if the Cops and Robbers mode got a massive overhaul or got replaced completely, even adjustments to the stupidly overpowered slipstreaming I doubt this title could get it right. Go on to YouTube and look up gameplay from the classic Ridge Racer titles,including Rage and Rave, take a look at Daytona USA, Cruise N' USA, Virtua Racer, Sega Rally, then take a look at gameplay from Hotshot Racing.Notice anything missing? Beautiful environments aside the racing is all flat and bland. At this time the dev team simply does not seem to understand what is lacking from their title. Their promise of more content is all well and good, but if it is more of the same then what is the point?While the project idea has been going on for 4 or more years, this game, this variation of the idea is only 18 months old, and it shows. I have a copy of Ridge Racer V in storage (alongside most of the series, no doubt), I could put that in an emulator right now and get a more fun, thrilling, and challenging experience. Hotshot Racing has it everywhere expect for where it matters; fun and challenge. It lacks both.

_childDocuments_.review: A terrific arcade game that is feels as great to play as it looks. It takes many aspects of other well known arcade games to make a game that I think is worth every penny.The driving physics is definitely reminiscent of Burnout and the (very) strong slipstreaming/drafting mechanic very much feels like Ridge Racer. All in all, execution was really done well.Clearly the aesthetic was based on Virtua Racer, mostly due to the textures used... or the lack of. Virtua Racer used only flat shaded polygons to "texture" the game, unlike Daytona USA.In the way the game plays, I can't really say anything in particular.Nothing revolutionary or new makes this game distinct to arcade games of years past, but that isn't necessarily a bad thing either.It's definitely what I looked forward to while waiting for the game's release, and pretty much why I enjoy this game as much as I do now.Many do complain about the AI though, but I think the way the AI is designed is purposeful.Much like in Ridge Racer, the AI takes advantage of the strong slipstreaming to "rubberband" when you're ahead. So, don't expect to lead the whole race. Just keep drifting and boosting whenever you can. This is where the real challenge lies.There are also complaints about a ridiculously aggressive AI, but I think it was meant to be that way. At one point, this game was supposed to be a combat racer, so that bit was probably left in tact in the way the AI drives.I guess the description could have been written better to take into account this aspect of the game.One genuine complaint I do have are the collision physics, short race lengths and somewhat bland course designs.Getting hit in the right angle can spin your car around (which is beyond frustrating, even in combat racers); I'd think making the car turn less severely in collisions will solve this problem completely. Races as short in duration as each last about 1.5 minutes and design-wise the tracks do not have any unique identities that would make them distinct from each other. A few more laps would make each track more enjoyable I think, and also allows space for comebacks. As for the course design, the ones in the "Boss Level" DLC pack are well done IMO, especially the first track. I'm looking forward to future tracks with that kind of style.But all in all, I don't think this game has many outstanding flaws that would hinder you from having a terrific experience.There are very  few racing games out there of this kind. Simple arcade action and terrific local multiplayer.I'd give it an 8.5/10: Terrific execution, but somewhat bare track designs and very unforgiving collision physics.

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately, the game just isn't good.The visuals are amazing - the low poly aesthetic is a nice throwback to old racers of the 90s.But that's pretty much it for the positives. There isn't a lot of content, not really anything to unlock outside of skins for the cars and outfits for the characters.I could look past all of that but the way the game plays is also too poor and unpolished. On higher difficulties, no matter what car you drive, the AI can easily spin it out often leaving you in a position there is no recovery from. Meanwhile, you can't really do that. I once managed to send an AI car flying but it still caught up to me within like two seconds despite being airborne and crashing into a wall. The races don't really feel like races either. Almost all AI cars (save for one most of the time) drive together very close. So instead of having like 2-3 groups of racers like you would in other games (like 1st, 2nd, 3rd place warring for the first spot, then there is another pack in the middle, like 4-6, and then there's the last places), everyone is just cramped. Get spun out once and there is a very high chance you will immediately be second to last or last place. The reason why this often means game over for the race (and grand prix) is because of how overpowered slipstreaming is. Compared to drifting, you get way too much nitro (as well a speed boost...) from simply driving behind someone. So that means when you're in first place, the AI will get a lot of nitro and a speed boost which is why it's almost impossible to stay ahead of them. At the same time, fall too far behind (as mentioned before) and your sole source of nitro will be drifting (which actually feels great but is too unrewarding). This means that the best strategy will be to hold onto your nitro while being in 2-4 place and then use it during the last lap, ideally shortly before finish line.While a lot of racing games have somewhat overtuned rubberbanding that makes the races feel too artificial, this game is definitely in a league of its own. There is hardly any thrill in the races because your driving skills simply don't matter as much.

_childDocuments_.review: Poorly optimised and pointless "catch-up and ram" AI mechanics ruin this game.Visually it looks like it could have been a more advanced throwback to Outrun, and the cosmetic unlocks for the cars are pretty impressive for a racer in general, let alone a throwaway little arcade racer like this (you can change steering wheels in your cockpit view... change the cluster type).BUT... the game is kind of unplayable.On a machine that can run Cyberpunk 2077 on maximum insane settings at 1080p and produce a very stable and consistent 60fps. Think about that when you scroll down and check the system specs, I'm talking about running it on a machine with an RTX 3080 rockin' 12GB of VRAM... with Hotshot here, I have to reduce the game to 1080p maximum, Vsync OFF... and if the graphics quality is anything other than LOW, the frame rate drops to single digits.  Even on low, when there are multiple cars on screen and particle smoke coming off drifting cars, it still feels like the game is dropping to sub 30fps. Try raising the screen res even a tiny bit higher with everything off/Low... you get the same single digital frame rate issue. Very weird.Then you have the driving. What chance I tried to give this game, every time I felt like I was getting into the groove of how the physics worked for the varied car types, an AI racer would magically come screaming up with these old style "catch up" mechanics, but instead of focusing on racing the AI would make it their priority to shunt you from behind, side swipe you, or magically go so fast as to do a clean overtake only to brake check you (usually 2 of them trying to side swipe each other while brake checking you).It makes any sense of skill usage feel utterly pointless and unsatisfying. It also makes you feel cheated whenever you a have clean run and distance yourself from the tards, only for them to always be there, performing impossible slingshot overtakes.A real shame because it looks like a lot of quality thought had gone into the variety of racing modes (cops & robbers is a cool, though ultra simplistic mode), the specific car selections available to each driver avatar, and the track designs are pretty decent for what it is, with off-track traction/speed penalty mechanics that could have been great... if you weren't constantly dealing with psychotic bumper car AI drivers. That psycho behaviour also makes it impossible to drive from cockpit view, because you end up struggling to figure out from what angle you were just king hit, and it is hard enough to recover from those unavoidable rams as is when you see them happen from a distanced cam view.I had to turn the music and dialogue off as well... all the voice acted comments are just.... it's dumb kids game stuff that just added to the frustration and desire to send my controller into a death throw against the wall.The world is pretty well populated in terms of polygons, but they're not complex models, and we are talking barebones flat/cel shaded surfaces... there is not justification for the lack of optimisation.

_childDocuments_.review: Hotshot Racing is a throwback to the arcade racers of old. Scud Race, Virtua Racing, Daytona, the list goes on.This is within the very specific realm of games that Sumo Digital operates, with one of the single best arcade racers ever made, Outrun 2, under their belts.I think, for this reason, it's hard to look at this game and not compare it to their other offerings. With the scores of side content and extreme quality of their previous titles, what would be a hit for most developers comes across as a bit of a miss.There really is no bonus side-modes or career. You have half a dozen GPs with 4 tracks each and that's it.The AI of the rival racers feels like it was copy & pasted from a 15 minute Unity tutorial on Youtube.Which makes playing any of the side modes in the game besides Time Trials feel like an absolute chore.The tracks all feel the same, there's no difficult corners, verticality or narrow sections on any of the tracks.I'd say they're almost all 50%+ 6-lane wide straightaways which just gives the AI ample room to rubberband past you.That isn't to say that the game is unsalvagable, just that playing the game in single player is almost entirely unbearable.There is 4-player splitscreen support and online play available, which is where the game is clearly meant to shine.There's also a huge variety of cars to choose from and customise, with body kits and dozens of different colour options to unlock as you play the game.I think, for me, as someone desperate for this kind of game after all the indie developed arcade racers have evaporated, it's certainly going to fill that gap until something more fun comes along.But if you're expecting the usual quality Sumo delivers or even something you can have a bit of fun playing solo, you're not going to get what you want.

_childDocuments_.review: The mechanics and game-feel are pretty great to be perfectly honest, and this would be a very serviceable arcade racing game.. If the AI wasn't so frustratingly basic.The sole purpose in their artificial life is to ram you into oblivion (you can't return the favour, mind you. Their cars are made of depleted uranium, while you're piloting origami), and I genuinely burst out laughing on two occasions at the horrendous, absolutely-egregious rubber banding. It's literally the worst I've ever seen.The slipstreaming's a really cool idea, but it works at all speeds, turning the start of every race into "get the boost or face a complete clusterf*ck for the first 20 seconds". No big deal, but it's wasted an otherwise awesome mechanic.The characters are colourful, with lots of customization options for the racer and the car.The drivers also have plenty of voice lines, but you only ever hear your own driver. This not only gets stale quickly, but also reminds you of how lifeless the game feels. There's lots of bright colours and some beautiful maps, but it's just so sterile as you race along, hearing your character quip the same quips every lap with nobody apparently listening.I got it for 80% off, and I don't feel ripped off, but I  surprised that in a game that's not even a year old, the multiplayer's completely broken. I don't mean somehow unbalanced, it's literally dead.I wish they would have the courtesy to take "online multiplayer" off the store page, guys. Come on.

_childDocuments_.review: It's incredibly fun for a few hours. The controls are great, the aesthetics are top tier and the overall aggressive vibe is amazing. That being said, it does have some issues that keep it from being a really good game, but the potential is there.The main issue is how the AI opponens will likely always be on your tail, no matter how good you are. It's impossible to shake them. This means that, due to the ability to store boost and go faster with slipstream it's always best to be in 2nd place until the last few seconds of the race. There also feels like there's a lack of variety, despite the game actually having a lot of stuff in it. In terms of maps, this is mostly due to most maps looking pretty similar, with similar colors and similar style, all daylight, all with a mix of saturated and pastel colors, and with vaguely similar race layouts. The characters and vehicles aren't too varied either, although there's a lot of them. The only thing that changes from character to character is what they say and, due to there being so many of them, they repeat their voicelines A LOT which gets very, very repetitive. imo Steam Workshop support for custom characters, maps and vehicles would pretty much fix this lack of variety, but they could also develop the characters a bit more, perhaps having less characters to compensate. I'd gladly take fewer bettter developed characters than a lot of bland ones with repetitive voice lines.Overall, the game is still pretty fun, but it just feels it could be so much more.
