_childDocuments_.review: Take a trip back to the mid to late 1990s and early 2000s, and step into any arcade.  Past the pinball machines, light gun shooters, and crane games, you’ll find the coin-op racers.  Racers that provided high speed thrills for a couple quarters out of your pocket, and a chance at bragging rights against your buddies or holding the course record on a highly used machine.  That was my jam.  Time has not been well to arcades in America, and the frequent sightings of classic machines has dwindled.  With console and online play taking over the need for hot-spot gaming areas, the classic arcade racer experience is held onto by new developers with the urge to burn rubber much like myself.  And while some recent iterations don’t quite nail the complete experience, Hotshot Racing can stand tall as one of the best arcade racers to grace any platform.Let me explain.  Hotshot Racing is an arcade racer in its purest form, with industry vets Lucky Mountain Games and Sumo Digital, the former having its hands dipped in several racing titles, looking to nail the early 21st century need for speed for the modern times.  All the normal fixin’s are present: single races, grand prixs, and time trials hold the fort.  But what really needs to be explained in fine detail is everything else that was meticulously crafted into a seemingly homogenous racer, because it’s hard to really understand how much love and time was spent showcasing the history and love of the sport until you start peeling back some of beautiful inclusions.For starters, Hotshot Racing handles its speed like a dream.  There are two main components to keeping your car in first place: drifting and boosting.  Drifting will be the most common tactic around each track, as a simple tap of the brakes will push your car as close to sideways as you want.  Drifting feels super rewarding, and can be an absolute trip on other vehicles, which I’ll get to in a bit.  Boost is accumulated through successful drifts and slipstream, or drafting, opposing racers.  Each vehicle can hold 4 bars of boost, and is an instant injection of speed to push past the competition.  Some racers will push drifting to be an absolute to where if you ain’t drifting, you ain’t winning.  Hotshot Racing smartly doesn’t combine a good drift with an immediate boost as sliding across the track will deplete your speed, and you can and will get passed.  It’s a fancy risk-reward tactic where drivers have to choose whether to sacrifice a lead and top speed for more boost, or take the fastest way but lose the chance of filling up for later.That boost can be an absolute make or break when you start to get comfy with the game’s racer AI.  To say the AI is aggressive is an understatement, but I absolutely love it.  Arcade racers of old have this natural tendency to put the player against the clock (to get all your quarters of course), and instead of having difficult opponents, AI racers will be slapped on in large numbers and players have to dodge and weave while running clean enough laps to not get timed out.  Hotshot Racing has you duking it out with racers that legitimately feel like they want the win more than you do, and they will bump and slam into you to make sure they get it.  What’s ingenious about this is that Hotshot’s options to gather boost would require the player to drift around unnecessarily to just to grab boost if the player had a big lead.  If the AI racers are on your tail, boosting past you with their own boost, and forcing you to either spend or save your boost, it makes every race intense.The aggressive racing also ties into Hotshot’s eight selectable characters.  For an arcade racer, I was not expecting this much character in these guys and gals: from American grease monkeys to British playboys, to a literal Android but no he’s a human participant what are you talking about.  Racers come with their own backstory, giving a normally non-included reason for their will to win, and even giving each character a special cutscene when winning a Grand Prix.  Each racer comes with four vehicles to choose from, each a different style of driving: Balanced, Top Speed, Acceleration, and Drift.  The little easter eggs tied to each racer are a blast to see included: James Bond-esque vehicles for Aston, Initial D-like drift machines for Toshiro, and Cole Trickle’s stock car ala Days of Thunder for Alexa: don’t think that reference was lost on everyone.  Beautifully specific details like right side driver seats for foreign vehicles and rear wheel and rear engine vehicles drifting differently due to weight distribution and turning style is such a compliment to fans of the craft that I can’t help but applaud the extra effort.Each vehicle boasts a staggering amount of customization: different hoods, spoilers, colors, steering wheels and dashboards for the cockpit view, and accessories are available to unlock.  It took me off my seat seeing nearly 800 pieces to unlock, which are unlocked by in-game money earned by completing races and specific challenges; with how many challenges there are, it would’ve been nice to have had the option to see which challenges were left, but as far as I saw the only way to check is to finish a race and see the updated numbers there.Once your car is set, Hotshot’s courses capitalize on that fresh low-poly slathered in beautifully rich tones that are a feast to indulge.  4 courses on each of the 4 categories round out the 16 stages available, each stage being able to be mirrored out the gate.  Race through bustling downtown cities, to Jurassic Park styled jungles and mountaintops that you’d see on paintings.  The music accompanying each stage does well to keep up with the speedy tone of the cars, and keeps a beautifully electronic vibe in 6th gear.  The course designs could do with some more varieties in difficulty, but each track is still a thrill to play.Alongside Single Race, Grand Prix, and Time Trials (good luck with those staff ghosts), Cops and Robbers and Drive or Explode complete the playable modes.  Cops and Robbers have robbers driving laps collecting cash for speedy runs while avoiding the cops who are there to destroy the robbers.  Robbers are given 100HP that depletes on hit, and cops get a serious increase in boost so they can try their best to T-bone the living Hell out of whatever poor soul is in the way.  Drive or Explode has vehicles draining the HP of other drivers by hitting walls or other drivers, while also maintaining an ever increasing top-speed.  Stay under the desired speed, and your car becomes a ticking time bomb that’ll explode.Don’t think I forgot to mention the buttery smooth online play, because this is the cherry on top for Hotshot Racing.  Complementing a 4-player split screen that is compatible with Steam’s Remote Play Together, Hotshot piles up to 8 players in one lobby to play any track or mode minus Grand Prix and Time Trials.  AI racers are available to fill in the blanks if wanted, and any changes made on your vehicles are carried online.  A couple hours of playing online garnered no hiccups or lag, and playing with friends in such a tightly contested style of racing is incredible given how much can be going on.Hotshot Racing pulls no punches in solidifying itself as one of the best Arcade racers ever made, but combining all of this with a price tag at $19.99 and more content coming in a free post-launch update soon is even more ridiculous.  With blistering speed complimented by genius design choices, an absolutely absurd amount of customization, and the beautifully crafted love letters to the four wheels of racing and its arcade predecessors, Hotshot Racing places itself valiantly alongside the best games of 2020.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game, i think its a great game, very wonderfull, very fun and enjoyable. One caviat i have to say is, the game is the most fun at the lowest difficulty, as difficulty only increases the speed of the cars, so the higher the speed, the less fun it is, its not even that its hard, because its not, like, you lose the lead, you lose, period, theres no comebacks here on medium and definetly not on hard, its kinda wierd how they did the difficulty but yeah, easy maybe slow but its fun, maybe it doesnt matter so much because you have to complete every race on every difficulty with every character anyway, so again, like i said, quite grindy if you wanna chase that completionism. _childDocuments_.review: It's simple but excellent. It's an arcade-style racing game that's been done very well.I really don't have much more to say about it than that. And that it's really, really fun. When my brother showed it to me through couch co-op with my best friend involved as well, I was instantly hooked. It's fun solo or with other people.There are a total of 8 characters to play as, each handling differently when driving, and it feels like each have a different weight. They also have a variety of fun voice lines they can say when racing, including witty remarks.There are 3 difficulties that you can choose for any mode except time trial. The difficulties increase the maximum speed as well. The difficulties are as follows;Normal- Pretty standard. You'll notice AI are really competent in this difficulty; they will manage to keep up with you despite you boosting a lot and generally having a faster car than them.Hard- Little faster, but still tons of fun. AI still competent but not as much as in normal difficulty.and Expert- I actually consider this the easiest difficulty in terms of AI skill, but you go a  faster, which means you will most likely crash harder and more frequently. But since it's very fast, it's also very, very fun.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is boring and unengaging. The driving physics feels as if its not responsive enough to feel like a true arcade racer. In Daytona USA, SCUD race, even virtua racer you will instantly steer left or right as soon and as brief as you want and you feel like you're in control of the vehicle. In this game, you'll turn left or right but with a delay whenever you switch your direction which makes you feel like you're driving a brick and the sense of speed is equivalent to a golf cart. Drifting is not hard to do which makes sense for an arcade racer but at least the 90 racers they are paying homage to have a decent learning curve to keep you engaged to learn how to maintain as much speed through the corners but the driving in general has no depth at all. Drifting is needed for any semi sharp turn and since it feels like a chore more than a fun mechanic it makes the gameplay loop more tedious and boring than it should be. Graphics and presentation of this game feels like a lifeless, ugly and cliched modern throwback to virtua racer and 90s arcade racers. Also, if you don't have a potato pc and you disable v-sync so you can have your 144hz refresh rate, you will experience the most egregious screen tearing you'll ever see. Music is ♥♥♥♥. Pick this game up for a dollar.

_childDocuments_.review: Hotshot Racing is a lovely looking game. The problem is, it's a bit boring. The tracks are easy, with no shortcuts, big jumps or anything else exciting that I would expect from an arcade racer. And whilst rubberbanding is not necessarily a bad thing in racing games, it's turned up to 11 here. Simple strategy - drift, save boost, boost to the end to win. A shame, really.

_childDocuments_.review: i wanted to like this game because i've been looking for a cool retro type racing game for awhile now and this one seemed to have cool graphics and an old school feel.  i've been playing racing games since pole position for the atari 7800 but i've really only ever been average at them, they're just fun to play.  this one is just super frustrating though, i've only been playing for half an hour and i'm going to uninstall.  i like the graphics and the physics seem fun, there's lots of cars and the tracks seem relatively easy.  but the drifting in this game is very hard to control, for me at least, compared to other drifting type racers.  basically my drift button might as well be a "spin out of control" button because that's what happens whenever i try drifting.  tried different cars with higher or lower drifting values, but when i tap the trigger my car just spins in a circle, there's no control at all.  i figured i would just try to race without drifting, but you need to drift to gain boost.  and as many other reviewers have noted, the other cars are always right behind you, you simply cannot gain a huge lead no matter how fast you race.  i think i attempted the first race in the first grand prix about a dozen times before i finally managed to get in the top 3.  so i went to the next race and was in last place (of course) so i restarted the race, and it RESTARTED THE ENTIRE GRAND PRIX.  you can't restart the current race when doing a grand prix, it restarts the whole thing from the beginning.  that was the final straw for me.  not being able to restart just the current race is a baffling design decision.  i could forgive the difficulty otherwise, as long as i could attempt each race multiple times until i got better at it, but making me replay the entire grand prix is annoying enough to make me quit playing.

_childDocuments_.review: Works fine using Proton (only 20 minutes playtime) but cutscenes have minor frame-timing issues. Menus are very buggy, e.g. pressing down will not cycle through an entire menu but pressing up works fine, e.g. 1->2->2->3->1 versus 1->5->4->3->2->1. Ultrawide is not supported, the display is 16:9 stretched to fill the entire screen. I've only completed the first GP so far and found boost to be a bit useless. On normal difficulty the slipstream effect is so overpowering you will easily catch and pass a car in front of you who is boosting; the opposite applies to, cars behind will easily catch up to you as the speeds achieved from being in the leading cars slipstream exceeds the maximum boost speed.I'm leaving a negative review for now due to the lack of ultrawide support and buggy menus. I'll update my review once those are fixed.

_childDocuments_.review: I think I first found this game back in covid days. There is nothing ground breaking in this game - a decent arcade racer that tries to capture the feel of the original low polygonal blocks from the era when gouraud shading was still a luxury. An obvious homage to Sega's Virtual Racing and maybe Namco's Ridge Racer. Acceptable physics + drifting mechanic you can easily adapt to makes it a decent experience for a few runs. However, rubber banding here is somewhat ridiculous.Be aware that the game is basically abandoned, there is no online and it might not even launch on your machine due to some specific windows 10 conflicts nobody gonna fix, but if it runs, it's okay.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: The controls are god awful. Shame on everyone who played this in the dev team when there are Need For Speed games like Hot Pursuit 1 and 2, Underground 1 and 2, Midnight Club and more.Notable mentions Ridge Racer 1- Type 4 at least and Outrun 2004 run circles around this game. You can not change the controls at all and are bad. There is no dedicated break and drift (handbrake) button which make the game just a arcade  cashgrab for people buying this unknowingly. Who thought that PS2 games and even PS1 do have custom controls in some games and at least 3 different presets which a modern game lacks. PS3 / 360 was the era of the lazy devs struggling to offer any settings in games and now with indie games on Unity (mostly).You can ram people from behind and get no penalty for playing unfairly / traditionally. I lack the term to categorise this pushback and deceleration / slow down on ramming cars from behind that was a standard in even NFS games for a long time.Last edit: The game can not even teach you the basics. I complain about these controls because you get a Mario Kart-esk engine breakdown when you red-line the car before the race starts which is considerably bad because you use the triggers which have no real feedback. I'd prefer X for acceleration and square for braking but no chance for this badly made game. Sadly the other two good games in this genre are on the NS handheld only.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: Almost all the negative reviews are just saying "ooh rubberbanding ooga booga" but in all honesty, you just have bad wifi. All iv'e done so far is online, and not once have I experienced any lag or rubberbanding at all. Besides the rendering distance and anti-aliasing being so bad, I have nothing but good things to say about Hotshot Racing. It's fast as all hell, it's super intense and definitely raises the risk of stroke, and it really peaks that sense of pure madness and fun. This is absolutely the most entertaining racing game I have played, by no means realistic but that wasn't the aim. I will say though, the price could be lower considering the minuscule playerbase and slightly small amount of content. But if you are considering buying Hotshot, I would say go for it. Full price might be a stretch, but I can almost guarantee that you will still have a blast.8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun arcade racer like the good old days before all the racers became sims.  The drifting and drafting mechanics are great fun and tracks are fun and vibrant.Music is decent with some standout tracks such as on temple run that really get you in the racing mood. The characters have quirky personalities and have some funny sounds bites.Only fault is that  online multiplayer seems to have some issues at the moment as I'm not seeing any matches but hopefully  this will be fixed.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: Got this in a bundle a while ago and forgot to leave a review. Hotshot Racing is an arcade racing game that is sort of a modern take on retro racing games. The art style is simple but looks good. The maps are interesting, got lots of great scenery.The gameplay is simple. Normal racing game driving controls, and you drift to build boost charge.I tried playing multiplayer but nobody playing it.The vehicle collisions feel very artificial and weird. You kind of just bounce off of other vehicles and the environment. I know its an arcade-y game but I think a little bit more physics would be nice.Not a bad game but also pretty forgettable. Once you have played the 20 maps, tried the different modes, and experimented a bit with different cars, there isn’t going to be much to do. I don’t really see why I should play this game over other racing games. With nobody playing it and better racing games out there to play alone and with your friends, this one will probably be played for a few hours and then put on the metaphorical shelf.

_childDocuments_.review: charming but ultimately pretty shallow, even for an arcade racer. it falls into that trap of nothing mattering except boosting right at the end to make sure the AI can't catch up AI their way in front of you and make you lose. racing lines barely matter beyond not hitting walls. mistakes are basically not punished at all when you can just draft and immediately be in first again. it's fun for maybe an hour or two. the driving model itself is nice at least.

_childDocuments_.review: 2/10Usually when I play racing games I'd prefer to have a button that, like, starts the car. It would also be okay if the car starts automatically and just never stops. But having no accelerating button is basically the only thing I'm complaining about. Maybe someone else would be perfectly fine just hanging out on the starting line 'till losing game.But yea, I was using ps4-controller and am way too inefficient to actually try to solve the problem.

_childDocuments_.review: Garbage: if you're interested in this game you probably love games like SEGA RALLY 2 or OUT RUN 2006. This game won't offer anything but a low quality copy of those games. _childDocuments_.review: When I was a child, my father never took an interest in my hobbies. He was always out, at work, or just doing ‘adult’ things. Due to this, I vowed that when I had kids, I would take an interest in their hobbies, whether they be sports, gaming, or whatever else! And that’s why I became a 45 year old father, probably one of the oldest people playing this game. I am the father to my son, Mike, who is now 14. Recently, my son downloaded this game and in less than a week, he had already played for over 20 hours. This was devastating for me, as instead of bonding over ping pong, he was locked away in his room. As a result, I decided to make a Steam account, and get this game and take an interest in his hobbies, as my father had never done. I loaded into the game, and had no clue what to do, so I asked my son for help, and he hosted a game for me to join. I loved it, as he hadn’t seemed this happy since we went rock climbing together in 2018. This game has ever since brought my son and I closer again, and now we spend time together on hobbies that I grew up with, such as fishing. This game reminded me that there’s fun to be had in everything, and it has brought both I and my son many happy memories.

_childDocuments_.review: It's nice to find a arcade racer that doesn't try to work in sim driving and beat you over the head with a thousand different driving mechanics. The other racers are overly aggressive and will always try to come up behind you and clip you sideways into a wall, or slam into your side on purpose. However the way the game works is that any time you are slipstreaming you build up nitrous so you can always stay in the race with nitro boosts. It also makes you think twice about boxing out other racers because you are giving them nitrous buildup any time they are behind you. Cool cheap arcade racer. Worth $20? God no but $4 on sale heck yah. Or get a copy outside steam even cheaper.

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun arcade racing! Playing this on expert though can be a difficult (and sometimes unfair) challenge since the opponents rubber-band a LOT but it's possible to squeeze a win once you learn the track and how to handle the car you are using.Content-wise it offers a good amount of stuff to do for the price and you can play split screen with a friend. I haven't checked the online stuff but you can also play online multiplayer if you like that stuff (you will need to find lobbies though).Really fun game overall!

I think it's less that there's rubber banding, and more that the slipstream is just much stronger on lower difficulties.Would love more updates for this game. It handles great and multiplayer is fun.

_childDocuments_.review: The handling physics, vehicle customization, and overall presentation are pretty well done for a game that's meant to capture the feel of Sega's racing games from the 90's.The game's biggest issue is the rubberbanding. It's fine on the lower difficulties, but the races become very frustrating on hard mode and that's about the time I stopped playing. The voice samples get grating after a while but they can be muted at least.It's still worth grabbing on sale if you're looking for an arcade racer to play in short bursts.

Nothing fancy, just slight tweaks to allow for zero deadzone etc., to make wheels usable - it's a real shame.Would even pay for 'wheel support DLC' if it was a thing. :)
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: This game is certainly something. It's almost got everything I could ever ask for: a great visual style, fun physics, and a very good boost system. But the tracks... just what even happened? Only about a fourth of the tracks are good, and those are REALLY good. Most others feel empty. Just highways with the occasional right turn to complete a lap. Another problem is the AI. They behave like Mario Kart AI where they zip past you and slow down because of the terrible rubber-banding. It's fine on the easier difficulties, but on harder difficulties it's nothing short of pain trying to grab a podium. Last issue is the grinding system needed for modifying cars. Swapping parts around is VERY fun in this game, but you're never going to be able to unlock all of them. In the end I'd recommend grabbing this game on sale with a 100% save file. That's how you'll get the most fun out of this game.

_childDocuments_.review: By far the most exhilarating and immersive racer I've ever played. The vividly colourful low-poly visual style is of exceptional quality and detail. The racing tracks are lavishly abundant, astonishingly diverse, and ceaselessly challenging. The wonderfully varied environments are lovingly crafted, imaginatively fun, and surprise you at every turn. The gameplay is thrillingly addictive with precision controls, adrenaline-fuelled cornering at blisteringly breakneck speeds, explosive action, a wealth of alternative game modes, funky music and crisp sound design. The ultimate dream racer. Love it.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: 8/10A fun yet janky little arcade racing game, which is best enjoyed with friends. I purchased this game on a whim to play with a friend, and we ended up getting the whole friend group to play it with us. This has led to some downright hilarious races, with quite literal photo finishes. The maps are all pretty fun, and some are enjoyably challenging to complete on harder difficulties. NOS is so fun to use in this game, but be warned that at least among my friend group, a meta developed where we all just saved our NOS boosts until the last lap, so keep that in mind.My only real complaints with the game are that the online servers are extremely janky at times, and there have been several instances where one of us lost first place last second despite finishing well ahead of another player in all POV's. The singleplayer experience isn't anything to write home about either, it's pretty standard and kind of forgettable for the most part. Oh, and the AI on expert difficulty are actually really mean, which is usually amazing, but can become super frustrating at times. Due to their unapologetically aggressive nature in expert mode, expect to lose entire tournaments because they take turns trying to make you crash into walls one after another during one race until your last place, which costs you just enough points that you lose the whole tourney. This is especially surprising because on all other difficulties the AI is almost entirely docile.Despite these minor complaints, I cannot stress enough how much fun I have had playing this game. It is super fun if you enjoy simple arcade racers, and don't take them very seriously. I have played this game so much I have acquired every ingame unlockable (as of writing only 1.4% of players have the achievement for doing this), and even purchased the soundtrack to support the devs. If that doesn't establish how much I enjoy this game, I have no idea what would. The game may not be for everyone, but I have certainly enjoyed my time with this product.P.S. While unlikely, I do hope one day we get a DLC that adds more maps, I think having some night maps would be an incredible addition!

_childDocuments_.review: Hotshot Racing is a delightful throwback to the classic arcade racing games of yesteryears, and it's a breath of fresh air in the world of modern racing titles. Developed by Lucky Mountain Games and Sumo Digital, this game delivers a dose of nostalgia while also offering a thoroughly enjoyable and engaging racing experience.One of the standout features of Hotshot Racing is its charming retro aesthetic. The vibrant, colorful graphics and the character designs evoke a sense of nostalgia, taking players back to the days of arcade cabinets and pixelated visuals. It's a visual style that not only pays homage to its inspirations but also adds a unique flair to the game.The gameplay in Hotshot Racing is fast-paced and exhilarating. The controls are intuitive, making it easy for players of all skill levels to pick up and play. The sense of speed and the thrill of drift-based racing are executed brilliantly, and the variety of tracks keeps the action fresh and exciting. The game's power-up system adds an extra layer of strategy and unpredictability to races, ensuring that every match is a thrilling contest.Hotshot Racing offers a well-balanced roster of characters, each with their own personality and driving style. This diversity adds depth to the gameplay, allowing players to choose a character that suits their preferred racing tactics. The multiplayer modes, whether local or online, provide endless hours of competitive fun, making it a fantastic game to enjoy with friends.Furthermore, the game's soundtrack is an absolute standout, featuring a fantastic selection of retro-inspired tunes that perfectly complement the racing action. The music enhances the overall experience, immersing players in the arcade racing atmosphere.In addition to its gameplay and visuals, Hotshot Racing offers a well-rounded package with multiple game modes, including Grand Prix, Time Trial, and Cops and Robbers, ensuring there's something for everyone. The progression system and customization options add longevity and replayability to the game.In conclusion, Hotshot Racing is a delightful and addictive arcade racing game that successfully captures the essence of classic racing titles while delivering a thoroughly enjoyable modern experience. Its charming visuals, fast-paced gameplay, and engaging soundtrack make it a must-play for fans of the genre and a great choice for anyone looking for some high-speed, nostalgia-infused racing action.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the ONLY racing games that i ever felt the itch to keep playing,let alone maybe get 100% achievement's-No Microtransaction-It has Catchy soundtracks-It has (Arguably) good characters voice acting, and Silly lines-The art Style just grabs you in, i love it (Deep rock galactic is a huge influencer for my love for polygon shaped art)-it has a Incredible balance between Racing and Drifting, most racing games i have played were either too focused on the top speed or too focused on drifting, and this one strikes a VERY satisfying balance for both!-The racing tracks (Not music) are all very distinguished from one another and very pleasing to the eyes-Drifting while going over 175 speed is satisfying as hell AND smooth (depending on your car)-Bots will provide challenge (so long you play on expert)the only 2 sad things is that multiplayer is..., dead unfortunatlyand Drift focused cars seem a little underpowered, But after playing a bit more with them, i can see SOME (Mainly marcus) of the Drift cars being alot more stronger than they lookoh, also, it can get annoying sometimes when bots RAM your car when you are driving, especially on drift carsyes there is collision and no you can't turn it off unfortunatlyWHERE IS THE SOUNDTRACK ALBUM FOR ME TO BUY?!

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best racing games I've ever played.Normally I do not like racing games because I am terrible at racing.This arcade game I picked up for free is one of the few racing games I actually have ever enjoyed.The boost and slip streaming mechanics make it possible for even the worst racers to keep up with the best.This makes for Hilarious situations playing with friends via online.There are several game modes:Arcade: Regular racing, if you don't go through a checkpoint in time you dnf but it is pretty generous.Cops and Robbers: Zombie type mode, one player starts at the cop and kills others to convert them to cops. Robbers must pass through a checkpoint in time or will be converted by dnf.Drive or explode: Stay above set speed limit, limit goes up every lap, try to survive or take out the competition with ramming.Barrel Barrage: Lap racing with damage, place barrels to damage your enemies or just outlast them in the race.All gamemodes are quite fun, the A.I. are very "rammy" on single player and multi player but they can be turned off in multi.I usually HATE racing gaming but this game had me plastered with a huge smile for HOURS.Even streamed it and people loved it.Graphics: 10/10 - Arcade style advertised, arcade style achieved. Love the art style.Gameplay: 8.875/10 - Single Player: 8/10   - Grand Prix: 10/10 Good fun, you get to do 4 maps per cup, 5 cups total. Difficulties are noticeably harder as you go up.   - Time Trial: 6/10 Functional but has issues. Chiefly the "Developer ghosts" are using advanced strategies to get great times. Making it demoralising to figure out how they even achieved such speed to begin with. Once you get the strat, it's trivial to beat them. Still a fun challenge and great way to learn a map. Knowledge does not transfer to multiplayer. - Multi Player: 9.75/10  - Arcade 9/10 - Good fun. Great racing.  - Cops and Robbers: 10/10 - Don't give your friends the idea to drive in reverse direction as cops. That would be funny. For best experience, set lap count to 7 (Max).  - Drive or Explode: 10/10 - Now this TeACHES you to drive like your LIFE depends on it.  - Barrel Barrage: 10/10 - I would give it 20/10 if I could it is SO MUCH FUN. Great DLC.Customisation: 9/10 - You can customise your cars a little, with unlocks but best of all they are only cosmetics. - Cars are unique and fun, pick the one that works best for you and shop around a bit to find a good car.Punishments: - Always online DRM, can't launch game if not connected to steam AND in online mode.Remarks: - No modding. But the infrastructure seems there. Perhaps if it was more clear how to mod it could be done.Final Score: 8.29/10 (27.875) Graphics: 10 Gameplay: 8.875 Customisation: 9 Punishments: 1A damn good game worthy of your money. I wish I bought it instead of getting it for free. And my friends are intent on buying the sound track JUST to support the game a little. We are sad we did not pay full price for this gem.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is great for a nostalgia kick where you can remember the times you played similar racing games at the arcade, but it doesn't go much beyond that. The levels are all kinda samey, there isn't a large variety of modes, and the car customization is nice, but a little lackluster, but if you don't expect a really in depth arcade driving game going in, the experience is still a lot of fun. A lot of others talk about the rubber-banding being kinda bad. I personally think it's somewhat realistic seeing as drafting gives you such a massive speed boost in this game. Staying just behind the leader for most of the race is actually a tactic at higher difficulties, and it just doesn't feel right to play it that way. The music is great, absolutely nails that arcade feel, but just like at an arcade, the time enjoyed is short. Playing with your friends (which I unfortunately haven't had the opportunity to do) is another great way to expereince this game. A few things this game could really benefit from is vertical track design (giant jumps and ramps etc.) and a destruction/crash system. These would make the game feel a bit more "arcady" and fun. Definitely a fun game to spend a few hours on every so often, but probably not worth 20 bucks. Wait for a sale though and then your money is worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game surprised me. I expected very generic arcade driving, but I was dead wrong. It pays homage to multiple different racing games and I was able to very quickly figure out each one they were trying to do. This game has the art style of Virtua Racing, the presentation of Daytona USA 2 and SCUD Race, physics that are similar to Project Gotham Racing 3 and 4 and Ridge Racer, and AI that feels very much like FlatOut. I can't really remember what game has music similar to this, it's not as good as Sega's killer OSTs or Ridge Racer's. With that out of the way, to the actual review.Physics: Shockingly, this game feels very much like a simcade despite having nitrous and brake to drift! And not only that, but you sometimes end up slower if you choose to drift. The game seems to balance the two better than the NFS series as of late. Obviously this is no proper sim or even as realistic as something like Gran Turismo for simcades, but I'd say it's slightly more realistic than the majority of GRID games in terms of the cars actually having mass to them. You're not going to get demolished if an AI hits you nor will you be able to destroy them from hitting them. And you do actually have to brake in this game, despite the drifting. Sometimes you have to let off the gas rather than brake.AI: Probably the weakest part of this game. I've not seen rubberbanding this bad in ages. It borders on NFSU/2 levels of craziness. On normal difficulty the cars are slower and the AI are passing you going way faster than they should without even using nitrous. It very much reminds me of FlatOut, where particular drivers and cars are going to annihilate the competition. I understand why they didn't go for Sega AI where they're more like decorations than actual opponents, but this is just ridiculous. Needs fixing. On higher difficulties, it's not as much a problem. But that's best covered in the next section.Racing: Aside from overly fast AI, pretty decent. The ironic thing about this game is that the difficulty settings are akin to FlatOut 3 and Mario Kart. Normal is much slower cars and will have closer packed racing. Higher difficulties will have way faster cars closer to what you'd expect in arcade racing games. Obviously being in the style of an arcade game, you're very limited in what you can do and set up. There's only a few locations and different layouts. There doesn't seem to be rhyme or reason with which cars to choose for each track since any of them can be pushed hard enough to be competitive. Obviously has your traditional grand prix modes and whatnot. But don't expect a laid back game just because of its appearance. Just like more hardcore racing games, you will be on edge due to the AI, however it's harder on normal difficulty. If you're experienced like I am, it makes for an addictive challenge. Oh and the characters have one liners, which is something every racing game should have, even sims like rFactor and whatnot!Cars: 4 per character, your typical "one is balanced, one is faster, etc". You can see they drew tons of inspiration from real life vehicles. You can customize them somewhat, some can be made to look closely like their IRL counterparts, others are more generic. Really sucks that you're extremely limited to paint and liveries, having to choose between existing color choices. Each car has an interior view and they even seem to model stuff like suspension and exhaust headers.Graphics: Not talking about the actual graphics here. It looks great, just like some of Sega's earlier 3D racing games. What I'm actually talking about is the camera views. This is probably one of the best parts of the game. For a game that's aiming to look arcadey, they've done something you'd expect in more hardcore racing games, which is to have the FOV set lower for the interior and bumper cams, which makes driving much easier if you're using a computer monitor (go look up racing game FOVs and why it's important). Of course, you can't adjust it. But it is rather neat, reminds me of Project Gotham Racing's lower FOV, which makes cars look "slower" in exchange for being far closer to what your eyes expect. Hell, you can even look around in the interior and it has that famous Daytona USA 2 styled "clip through the roof" camera view so as to not get in the way.Overall, I'd say this game is worth a shot (buh dum tis). If you like your racing games to be more of a challenge, this game certainly fits the bill (albeit sometimes unfairly). It's definitely a unique take on paying homage to racing games as a whole, even if flawed sometimes. Long time racing game fans will feel pretty at home playing this, but I do say this might be too difficult for your average player.

_childDocuments_.review: I really don't want to make a negative comment on this game, 'cause I had a lot of fun playing in solo mode for the 6hours I played. And I'm certainely gonna have more in the future. The game is, like description say, pure adrenaline. It has a mechanic that don't let you win the game until the last second, 'cause staying in second position and then use the turbo at the correct time is the key to win. It's not a con, I really like it. It might seems easy but it really isn't. I love the look of the game, the music and the sounds. There are only 8 racers but it's not a big problem, having 4 cars for each of them. The physics Is also really really good. This game is true fun. There's actually one simple only thing that make it impossible to raccomend: it's not online as it claims to be. I don't know why but servers aren't working. Well, to say the truth, there aren't even server. And it's not like there's to few people playing this, it's just that there's no way to play online. It wouldn't be a problem, if only Online weren't in tags for the game. And it's really a pity cause this game online probably would be more much funnier than other racing games could ever imagine to be. It's really a pity. _childDocuments_.review: Heads up: I don't play online or multiplayer in general & and hence do not care for the problems of THESE PEOPLE (we all know they're monsters) concerning this title. Online doesn't seem to work, boo-hoo. So this review is about the single player experience in the first 2 hours or so.Don't buy it full price. Pay a fiver or sth like that & its totally worth it (paid 4 Oiros I think, thats fine)The arcade driving mechanics are awesome & feel really great as soon as you get the hang of it (try the drifting focused cars) which needs a bit of getting used to, but generally: never let go of the accelerator & learn when/how to use the drift/brake. Save most of your boost for the last round (if you can without loosing the crowd) & you'll have fun. That drifting mechanic is so satisfying, it really can put a big smile on your face if you get it right.And if the AI doesn't ♥♥♥♥ it up.The AI might be a little (too) aggressive for some people - they like to ram you off the street, which can get really annoying, fast, borderline frustrating especially in GPs. Kind of a stupid decision to make them this way, as the drifting here can get you in a real nice smooth flow around the track which just feels awesome. But then some asswipe cancels it by ramming in your back or your side. Repeatedly. Why? It totally kills off your flow and usually isnt even especially helpful in terms of getting ahead of the opponent, because thats what the boost is for...So you might have to be in the right mood for this kind of ♥♥♥♥ if you want to play for a bit longer without killing your controller or rage-quitting. Doesn't help that if you play GP you can only only restart the whole tournament not the individual race. So if the AI ♥♥♥♥♥ you up by ramming you straight ahead into a corner or sth like that, you might drive behind trying to catch the others the rest of the race without a chance to retry. Doesnt happen frequently but sometimes & can be really frustrating.That's one reason why this is definitely not a game I'll play the whole day, but a few races/GPs are fine at the time. You know, like how you play an arcade game, if you have enough other stuff to play/watch/live - a game for in between things.In typical arcade fashion, none of the cars feel real, but all feel different & most of them good. There are 8 drivers with 4 cars each which aint a lot, but enough for this kind of game. Lots of unlocks for visual customisation as well, if you care for these things. Don't know why there are drivers to choose from, cars would have been enough & they're all stupid. Possibly they should've been funny or sth, but they're just too boring & too cliché for that. I take it as motivation through hate as I want to see all of them suffer. Except the driver I chose for the particular event obvs. I hate those next time again.Number of tracks is a bit lacking as well, it's essentially just 4 themes with a lot of very different layouts, but this doesn't change the fact you'll only see 4 backgrounds.Music is forgettable & not very good in general, I recommend using your own playlist instead (as usual I suppose). Sounds are boring but alright.Graphics are, well, of a certain taste. Personally don't find them that appealing, especially not the colour palettes, but it works. Well, except that there's screen tearing sometimes, which is weird as my PC is above recommended specs quite a bit, but maybe I'll have to re-check the options or sth. Or the developers are not that great in optimisation, who knows? Usually its smooth.So this doesnt sound too "recommended", does it?Well, if you know all that stuff & can live with it & you'll pay a reasonable price while its on sale, its worth it.Because its really fun to drive this thing here. And there's not too many simple fun arcade racers on steam, right? And it has split screen for if you find friends someday, so that's nice. It's certainly no Forza, Wreckfest or Codie racer, but I like it. Could've been a lot better I guess, but it is what it is. Just fun to play. And in the end, thats what matters, right?So buy it. Or not. It is your money after all.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm kind of on the fence about this one. I'd rather do mixed but since I have to choose between thumbs up and thumbs down, I'm going to go with thumbs down. It's fine if you catch it on sale for cheap for hour or so of fun but it's certainly not worth the full price tag.Hotshot Racing simulates the classic days of arcade racing. I'm talking about when 3D racing games first became a thing and it does a fine job at it. Everything is low poly to fit into the aesthetic. The driving mechanics feel pretty good.My main complaint about this game is the content. There are 20 tracks all of which a lap time will not surpass a minute. Most races are 3 laps with only the last cup having 4 laps each. You'll complete the entire career mode in about an hour. There are some interesting arcade modes if you want to jump on for a race to kill a few minutes.My main complaint is the AI. They're very rubberband-y. It does make races a bit more interesting but you find yourself just sticking with the pack, saving your boosts, to use them all on the last half of the final lap to pull away and make sure you cross the finish line first. Furthermore, it's like the AI are driving concrete blocks on wheels that are just as fast as you. You can slam into them and it won't do anything but they'll be able to spin you out with ease and it gets very frustrating when they actually get you to crash to a dead stop. Overall, there's not much content and the AI can be very frustrating. If you're looking for a game like this, wait for a sale or look for something else. You'll probably find yourself done with it after an hour or so.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: In the beginning, I wonder how good can this game really be when it's a low-poly game that looks like it's made in Unity (it's actually made in the NOESIS GUI engine)? Well, let me tell you some of my thoughts after playing several hours.The racetrack and environmental design with location-based audio cues from the drivers are phenomenal. With 8 unique drivers with a selection of 4 cars each, which can be cosmetically customized, across a beautiful array of 20 racetracks (4 new from Free DLC) with drifting controls that make it feel genuine all come together to make a truly wonderful experience. Not to mention the first time I stepped foot on the course I was blown away from the fact I recognized originally styled music from the legendary WaterFlame himself.On the flip side, what makes this game fall flat from a wholesome racing experience is the mechanical direction of the AI. In an arcade style racer game, such as Mario Kart where items are involved, a certain aspect of your placement is based on skill, while attaining a bit of luck. When you fall behind in the race, you are rewarded with items to help you catch back up to the pack. And, when you are in the front, are only given items to try maybe help you maintain your lead. That is known as rubber-banding.In a competitive racing game, such as F-Zero-GX, your placement is purely dependent on your skill of taking sharp corners, hitting all the speed boosts, and avoiding getting blown up by the track or other racers knowing exactly where you are both in front and behind to minimize your lap time. If you are able to lead by a huge gap, you can guarantee (unless you crash, or fall of the track) you'll maintain it. You don't have that same assurance when you get hit by repeating blue shells in Mario Kart.Anyways, both games mentioned above are fun because they put everything together so crisp it makes sense in the spirit and style of the game designers intentions. If you want to do better, you practice along with learning little tips and tricks, and shortcuts, along the way intuitively as you watch the CPU accomplish things you didn't think of while on the highest difficulty setting.Now back to Hotshot Racing. As fun as this game is – if you were to play locally or online without the weirdly scripted AI with their cheating techniques of always having a boost when they are behind without the need to drift, or not wanting to boost in the front of the pack so they can wait for their tailing friends to catch up – it is also frustrating with the lack of a dynamic race in any of the 3 difficulties. Where the game really shines is how the CPU can ram you, get rammed by you, or crash into a wall with their speed and pathing unaffected.So, with that in mind, the independent time trials racing against the dev ghost times is where the real challenge comes into play. This mode let's you learn and appreciate the racetracks in combination with the drifting mechanics to achieve a new course record.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels like it came straight from the SEGA DREAMCAST. Its a classic arcade game. it feels like it could be one of those late 90s local arcade machine games where you have to drop some coins to play.the artworks is really nicethe music is feels really nice. its not your typical indie game music. i think it has this housey and techno feel to it.the cars handle well. you have options for cosmetic upgrades. those however does not affect the cas stats.the voice acting is really good. it fits the game. i especially like the announcers voice.the whole game feels like a revisit into the oldschool days of arcade racers.

_childDocuments_.review: All I have to say is I'm having a blast. Fast paced engaging game play, tons of unlocks and tracks, cars, and characters to master.AI rubber bands a lot but it is possible to fend them off and that could be just slip streaming and even then if they didn't rubber band would it really be an arcade style game?That's it, that's my only criticism, go buy the game already, god's sake.
