_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: I went into Hotshot racing not knowing what quite to expect. I loved the classic arcade racer style of gameplay and the low-poly graphics style which really makes this game a joy to see and play. There are a few different game modes (my favourite being barrel barrage) and characters, each with their own set of 4 customisable vehicles. This gives plenty of room to play it how you enjoy whether that be classic Grand Prix racing, time trials or playing cops and robbers where you can drift or speed you way to victory! This can provide you with hours of entertainment before you get bored of it. With regards to the controls, they are easy to learn, yet hard to master to get the best lap time out and can differ wildly between cars. Doing the same thing with two separate cars can give you a really quick time with one, then mean you hit the barriers at every corner with the other. This was definitely one of my favourite parts of the game, learning each car’s quirks and adapting my driving style towards it.However, it does have some key issues that if resolved, would really make this a 10/10 game. Unfortunately, the AI is far from the best and they rubber band like crazy which can be annoying but does make it more challenging, often adding to the appeal. Now at this point multiplayer would be the perfect suggestion to get away from rubber banding. Unfortunately, online multiplayer does not work so you are limited to local only so I never got to experience what I’m sure would have been great online racing and I think that would have been the best part of the game. The final slight bad point from a completionist’s perspective is that there is a lot of forced replaying with each car in order to get all the customisations which is what I spent a lot of my time on this game doing (however still enjoyable for the most part), and from my perspective the achievement  “The Destroyer” is insanely difficult to get during gameplay and also a bit buggy as to whether you will get it when matching the requirements. Overall Hotshot racing is a really good game, but with some tweaking and fixing, it could be a superb game. I would recommend getting it, but it can go quite cheap when on sale, so definitely wait for it then!
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: If you just want to sit back and relax while playing a nice arcade style racing game with different modes and race cars that don't fly off the road every time you turn or touch a gust of wind, then this is the kind of racing game for you, you race and are incentivized to drift in order to collect towards your boost gauge to give you short bursts of speed to either catch up, pass, or keep in front of your competition. fun and simple game that's not trying to be so realistic that it ruins the experience of trying to be an entertaining game.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good arcade racing and graphics run super smooth. Content is light though, in 45 minutes I had cleared 3 of the 5 grand prix circuits (each of them are a collection of 4 tracks). There are cosmetic upgrades but not really a whole lot or really all that remarkable. I think this game is asking a bit much at 20 dollars for the amount of content it has, but on a deep sale price its a fun game to jump into for a few laps.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: Fun little game to play alone or with your friends, it's an arcade type game so if your looking for something more realistic this is not the game for you, but if old arcade racing games are your go to, than this game is perfect for you. It really did remind me of the past racing games i used to play and have lots of fun on, being able to customize your character and cars is also a very good feature.I can also drive listening to eurobeat so its worth it!
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: Hotshot Racing may sound and look beautiful, but its hindered by roughshod gameplay. It just goes to show that a great art department can't make up for bad programming.First, the positives. Hotshot sounds great and has well-written dialogue with a comedic bent. There are even unique endings for each character after winning a Grand Prix. The polygonal art is colorful and detailed, for the most part. The exception is when it comes to the natural landscape. You may find mountains or canyons with only a few different polygonal textures. I don't know if this was a design choice or cost-cutting measure, but it makes some of the tracks a bit lifeless.Now the negatives. As others have written, the rubberbanding is horrible. The easiest (and most boring) way to win is to simply stay behind the first or second place cars until the last checkpoint and boost to the finish line. The aggressive AI is annoying because you'll shake and spin like a top if they hit you but if you hit them you will bounce off like a polarized magnet. Other AI advantages exist, like when you are one second away from missing a checkpoint (and losing a race) and yet the AI cars behind you don't get timed out. Cars can be selected based on three skills: speed, acceleration, and drifting ability. Speed is useless because of the AI rubberbanding. if you're in the lead, the AI will soon catch up. If you're not, you can easily catch up through taking advantage of other cars' slipstream, which is nothing like the mild boost you might find in Mario Kart. You'll often need acceleration from all the times the AI hits you off course or to speed out of a drift, which the tracks are designed for. Drifting has a learning curve and is quite finicky for a game that touts itself as an arcade experience. It's more Gran Turismo than OutRun. The lack of a tutorial doesn't help the fact. While a reward system exists, it is largely useless and confined to minor changes to car and character textures. "Wow, I can change the color of some polygons, woo hoo!" The DLC has added a few minigames but the same AI problems reduce their enjoyment.  For instance, you will lose health in Barrel Barrage if hit by the AI, but the AI won't lose health if hit by you.Overall, this is a thumb sideways for me. I recommend it only because a lot of effort appears to gone into some aspects. You might get something out of it if you buy it in a game bundle or on sale and think of it as a "movie-night" replacement.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: I didnt have any trouble with controls, and the AI can be annoying when you're not paying attention to what you're doing. The AI aren't pushovers, they're designed to be rival racers not just punching bags for you to ram off course.I would love to see something with this art style and arcade fun mixed with a jet racing game (Like Jetborne but with controller support)
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: Think of this game as Arcade racing meets excessive violence. It's a low-poly arcade racer game set on several tracks in 4 different landscapes. It's not a perfect game by any means but its got a lot of cliche glory that a lot of arcade racers these days fail to miss the mark on. And if the standard racing scene isn't enough, you've got the opportunity to shoot explosive barrels at your enemy or go Demo Derby on them and smash them into walls, cones, guardrails, etc until they explode in a parade of low-poly fiery beauty that would please even some unnamed Movie producers. Its quick, easy-to-learn, senseless fun that anyone could have. I've only played an hour and its bringing me back to the days of ridge racer.. just with a lot more traded paint and explosions. Yes... Yes I do recommend
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: Great arcade racer! The game is a homage to the 80s & 90s arcade racing cabinets with some really cool modernized additions. It features local and online multiplayer with a variety of modes: Arcade, Time Trials, GP (a la Mario Kart), Cops & Robbers and other goofy stuff! Very entertaining and lighthearted! The handling feels weird at first, but once you understand the intended (drifting-and-boosting-like-crazy) way to drive, it becomes really satisfying and fun!As expected from an arcade racer, all A.I. cars are affected by serious rubberbanding, but that just makes the racing always feel neck-to-neck. This could be frustrating for some, but for me, having played too many hours on various Mario Kart games, it just felt fun and thrilling!This is a must play for arcade racing fans. If you are not sure if this is for you, a gameplay video will be enough to make you decide. If the chaotic driving nature of the game seems fun to you, definitely buy it, otherwise try something else.The full price of the game is also pretty fair, with a pretty wide variety of tracks, cars, characters and customization items to  spice things up and keep the game fresh. The awesome game modes are also a strong aspect of the game. On the downside, the car sounds and general sound effects are pretty boring, but are accompanied with a pretty fitting soundtrack which has come straight from an arcade cabinet. Another problem I noticed was that even though the frame rate was always stable, at specific points of specific tracks it felt like the game was slowing down. Pretty weird, especially since the game runs very smoothly 95% of the time!As an arcade racer, an easy 7/10.The -75% sale which is often applied to the game is seriously a steal. Give it a go!
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: HOTSHOT RACINGA Pixel style racing game.. honestly.A very simple game, fun for a short time, nothing unique.The game serves well as a fluid and responsive racer, the cars and drivers are not anything special, I just think this game has a hard time finding where it fits in.. there are only two types of racing games.Arcade and simulation.. this is arcade but stuck in such a crowded Genre with better titles..I say pick it up very cheap5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: Not a terrible game, but a bad PC version. There is a problem with freezing on even very high end PCs. VRR are not supported, and I never was able to get framerates higher than 60fps to work on my PC. Basically bad technical work.The game is reasonably fun to play, but the tracks aren't great. The music sounds like something designed by someone without any training in music. The visuals a interesting, sort of a very-high poly version of what we actually got in the very early 90's.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: *I play arcade racers for the time-trials or as single-player only.If you really want the best arcade racer in the cartoon art-style then I would look no further than Sonic and All-Star Racing Transformed with F1 Race Stars as a possible alternative. As an indie developed arcade racer, this has clearly been inspired by the former title but stands more as a rival to Horizon Chase Turbo. Its low polygon count won't win any awards in the graphics department but it's certainly brightly coloured and vibrant. It has a good atmosphere, you get to choose a decent variety of cars (with their own attributes) and tracks. The gameplay is solid reminding me a little of Rise: Race the Future. The good news is that it displays your personal best for each track; the bad news is that it doesn't tell you which car you achieved that time with. If you own the previous titles mentioned, this offers nothing new and will not blow you away. However, if you're looking for a change this is solid enough to be given a spin.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun arcade style racer, fun with friends, but multiplayer has a lack of players, but single player is fun on its own with interesting tracks highly recommend.Edit as of 1/3/22: The Game has been abandoned and the servers have been shutdown. Do NOT purchase this game looking for an online Multiplayer racer. The Single player is still playable, that is the only thing this game has left.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: I like the driving part of this game, it's arcade, simple and fun. But I can't recommend it due to the lazy AI. Instead of making them drive better, they just have way better cars. Better speed, acceleration... even seems heavier. It gets really disheartening to make that perfect turn while the AI in front hit a wall and then being barely able to keep up in the straight, with slipstream, on a car with a full speed stat, without them using boost.Also why forcing those cheesy lines of dialogues at character select? It is an arcade game which is supposed to be replayed a lot. Adding clutter to the car selection is just wrong to me.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: Hotshot is a nice acrade-like retro racing game.You have a great variety of maps, 4 game modes to choose from, interesting low-poly aesthetics and a good soundtrack. Also, there are 8 pickable characters, which each 4 cars to choose from. They are all unique, can be modified and have different stats.Race your way to the top in the grand prix or play online against friends and strangers. You can do simple races, cops and robbers, last one explodes or throw exploding barrels behind you. If you drift, you gain boost. That’s basically the whole game.Simple and fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: For those who love old arcade racing games where physics be dammed then this is the game for you.Simple, frantic fun that despite the short races can turn into absolute chaos at the drop of a hat thanks to the feisty AI.Combine that with a fantastic retro polygon style that pops off the screen, great tracks and an awesome soundtrack this is one I highly recommend picking up.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished every GP including the newer boss GP on expert and got 1st in each one with Keiko's Initial D meme car. Far from a max speed car people say you "need."I really love this game. I dont even remember where I got it to be honest. The graphics aren't bad, I turned off the ingame music and just played my own (really helps get into the zone) and the controlling in this game is near perfect for what it is. I 100% recommend this to any casual racing fan that just wants to load up a couple tracks without thinking too much, but also have a challenge and a good time.The only complaint is the rubber-banding of the AI on expert. Not impossible, but a bit annoying. Normal and Hard should be no problem even with the AI.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT : Multiplayer servers seem to be up again!Nice arcade racing game. The various cars feels different to drive. Supports 4 players in local-coop, as well as online (sadly no one around).My "negative" issues with the game is that car customization is not saved in local-coop, so local players cannot enjoy the very wide range of car decorations available. I would suggest creating "User profiles" that stores Driver outfit, Car customization and "Last Camera angle used" (I always drive in first person because the feeling when DRIFTING is AWESOME from behind the wheel!).
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: This scratches an itch that, until Daytona USA gets republished, is going to have to suffice.  Pros:* Honestly just fun.* Quite a bit of variety.* Kinda Daytona USA.  Kinda Mario Kart. * No silly powerups.Cons:* Every race seems to end with me hitting the boost button and just narrowly beating 2 people that have been with me the whole time somehow.   I can't say there isn't rubber-banding AI, but it sure seems like it.* Sometimes queues for the directions the turns are going to go just doesn't carry the articulation ---- or I'm getting old.  Just could use some shading and most turns do have signage.   There's a weird depth perception thing I'm having an issue with here.* The 'extreme' AI really is pretty brutal.  ...and by brutal I mean, aggressive and s**ty.  Fast, too, but it's frustrating to be slammed into a wall the second you get near them.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: This game is for you if you loved classic Sega arcade racing games like Virtua Racing! It feels like a natural evolution as if Sega kept making sequels and made good improvments to the formula, all while keeping with the awesome visual style and arcade sound effects! I blasted past the wirth GP race and I had a blast. I can't wait to play the others.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: I got this as a gift, so im not complaining. But.. theres absolutely nothing new to see here..The game is super bland, and follows a formula that we have seen a million of times before.Replay value is close to none, specially if played as single player.It reminded me alot of Outrun 2006, but less exciting. (and that its probably abandonware nowdays.. go get that instead)Think like this.. back in the day you would go to the arcades and spend a couple of dimes to play this game from time to time... looking at its price.. i dont think this game worth that many dimes
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: Pure arcade fun and a great little game! Captures the arcade look and feel perfectly and has intuitive and responsive controls that fit the game. Races against the AI were some of the best I've had in ages, in any game - every race felt really exciting, tight and not over until the finish line. There's not too many driving games like this on a PC, highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: Fun retro racer that's probably only enjoyable for those of a certain age who remember pumping quarter after quarter into games like this at an arcade. The recommendation is for the nostalgia factor. Beyond that, there is a lot wrong with this game. Aggressive AI and rubber banding impacts game play significantly. Online racing seems dead, as I've never successfully found a match. Customization is purely cosmetic. None of the upgrades change the stats on your car, so why bother other than to hunt achievements? And many features should have been implemented that aren't there. For instance, each car has challenges, like "drift for 250 seconds total". You cannot easily see the progress against these challenges without actually completing a race in the car and looking at the progress at the end of the race.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: Everything about this game is FANTASTIC except for one single little thing which can ruin the entire game, depending on who you are.Extremely unfair rubberbanding.If you're unfamiliar with the term, rubberbanding essentially means that the AI can catch up to you no matter what. This can be extremely frustrating as you can use four boosts in a row and be half way across the map where you  be extremely ahead of the pack. But for some reason, the enemy AI will be right on your tail without using any boosts, which can make the entire game seem pointless until the final stretch of the last lap where you can use a boost and win the race.But other than the rubberbanding, the cars are diverse, have great customization, and the game has a diverse set of tracks and characters. And best of all, in my opinion, this game has LOCAL CO-OP / SPLITSCREEN! Making it absolutely worth it on sale!Overall, it is not the perfect racing game, but it would come pretty close if it weren't for the AI rubberbanding and borderline cheating. But it still is a whole lot of fun and even more fun with friends.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: Ok arcade handling.Cons:Frame rate stutters despite running 90FPS. It's stretched on an ultrawide monitor, you can't even run it pillarboxed!Distant lines on the road are flicker with horrible aliasing.Default WSAD steering. Back in my day we used the arrow keys.It just feels like a cheap retro-styled cash-in.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: This game handles like a dream! And from the team that brought you Sonic & All-Stars Racing Transformed, I expect no less.Yes, the game has some insane rubber banding, and it may rub you the wrong way, but a friend of mine presented a case for it specifically for this game and it's stuck with me: Because of how intense the rubber banding is in this game, you will always have an opponent to slipstream against, which will allow you to earn even more boost to complete tracks faster.I'm normally not a fan of rubber banding, *especially* of this severity, but because of how the game rewards you fairly generously with boost for slipstreaming, it actually makes burning through GP races more interesting, in a different way. Give it a shot!
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: Let`s just say if you are a fan of multiple classic racing games like Daytona USA,Ridge Racer,Burnout/FlatOut,the 90`s NFS games,I think you are gonna enjoy the hell out of this game.The only problem is the rubber banding of the AI,doesn't matter what difficulty you play on.There is a car type for everyone some work better on some tracks than others tho:1: Balanced (self explanatory)2: Acceleration based3: Speed based4: Initial D based styleCars feel different depending on the camera you use,it even includes a first person camera which makes the game more challenging but feels better to drive imo.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: I got Hotshot Racing with the humble bundle and I was surprised by how fun this game turned out to be. It has very arcade handling with a boost (nitrous) mechanic but it's far from an easy game. The AI on the hardest difficulty are brutal and in order to keep up with them you need to be almost perfect. This involves full power drifting around every corner...which is very hard to do on a lot of tracks! The game really pushes you to improve.I've seen a lot of people complaining about the difficulty of the AI, but I love the challenge and think they did a good job with it. The retro artstyle the game uses is very cool, as is the music. By far my favourite thing about this game however are the cars. They're not licensed, but they clearly take "inspiration" from cars in real life. I'm a bit of a car nerd, so looking through the car list and recognising a lot of the vehicles used (especially for some of the more obscure models, like the old LeMans endurance race cars) is really cool.Unfortunately, the playerbase for this game is non-existant so the online is completely dead. I'd still recommend the game but be aware of this before buying.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: Best arcade racing game imo. No story, no free roam in between, no traffic in the road, the drifting feels as good as a drifting only game but it's being used to race instead of just collecting points. My only issue (not really an issue) is that the lighting and other visual effects are not all that great or smooth, playing in a 165hz monitor didn't feel much different than 60hz.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty cool game with nice colorful graphics. Played it with an XBOX ONE S controller via a USB cable and it works flawless. Has a decent difficulty balance and plenty of tracks to play. I can see myself playing this every now and then to satisfy my gaming thirst. Completed the GP4 races and I had fun racing in hood view mode. Didn't feel a sense of speed in chase mode so hood mode works best for me. I recommend it, especially if you get it at discount.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: There's no benefit to being good at this game, cause the rubber-banding AI will not care and constantly keep up with you. It's not enjoyable to race like that, it's insulting.Shame, cause the gameplay is genuinely fun.If players have the skills to be 3 minutes ahead of the pack, let them be 3 minutes ahead of the pack, don't insult their skills like this.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: Yeah, it's good.No fuss. Bright colours, going fast, doing cool slides. Pick a goofy international stereotype, pick a car, drive around the track three times. It's extremely polished, it's tight, it feels good to nail a drift. Sensory feedback joy.The AI seems pretty rubber-band-y and will pretty much never let you breathe easy in first position (which, I dunno, I guess some people might hate? I can see the benefits) although it feels like the game is self-balancing to a degree anyway, since slipstreaming behind someone provides both a noticeable speed boost and also bonus nitro. Difficulty is also a little strange; it feels like the 'normal' difficulty has you moving so slowly that engaging with drifting is almost a hindrance. I feel like 'hard' provides a much more satisfying experience, and isn't noticeably more challenging.Also I highly recommend turning off the character voiceovers. They all get grating pretty fast and one of them has a 'cake is a lie' joke.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: This game is arcade arcing done right. As someone who don't really enjoy most racing games i can fully say that this game is a joy to play.For an arcade racing game the key mechanic a developer needs to focus on is simple: Drifting. And my oh my does the drifting feel incredible in this game. The cars feel like they have real weight that you need to manage in a swing as to not crash into the sides. If you, like me, enjoy "sonic and allstar racing transformed" you'll most definitely like this game!Git it.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, a very marginal thumbs up because I'm feeling generous today.The good:A fun pick-up-and-play arcade racer, for the most part.Colorful, Sega Saturn-esque graphics.Sound effects and music all spot on.Tracks aren't super exciting, but colorful and playful for the most part.Drivers have some modicum of personality.The bad:As others have mentioned, there seems to be rubber-banding where you can really never develop a substantial lead.You'll often get rammed from behind, which will send you into a spin that you'll never recover from.There's no indication whether car customization effects your cars' performance. If it's not all cosmetic, it's certainly not clear.No real difference in drivers' skills as far as I can tell.I have not tried online, so I can't comment.I got this in the Humble Bundle, and I think in that context, it was a fun 3 hours or so of cartoony racing (on Easy - I shudder to think how bashed and bruised I'd be on Hard).  I would wait for a sale, though.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome, just started playing. Makes me feel like I'm back at the arcades.Wish they'd fix the Online mode though, especially if they wanna keep this game alive. It seems to freeze and crash every time I try to start an online Quick Race.Also, another pro being this game's requirements; even a potato can run this without making the game look like ass thanks to the low poly visuals.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: I will give this a thumbs up but would probably pick a "meh" if it was an option. Worth grabbing on sale.This is a super arcadey racer and has all the brightness, pace, and electronic music that comes with the territory.  Some other reviews had compared the handling to Burnout which isn't really true. Yes you can drift round corners, but the handling is far more twitchy.There are a few cool game modes beyond your regular race, plenty of cards and characters to choose.  I will say that the harder difficulties are pretty unforgiving, you will pay dearly for any mistakes.Also note that in my experience, online PvP is empty, so you're buying a single player game.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: It was fun until Boss map session came.. uncontrollable cars, sand makes it even worse. Buy Horizon Chase Turbo instead. It is capable for everything this game but doing it way better.. There is something I miss from this game the most, handbreak.. impossible to stop the car before the collosion if you are already lost the control.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: First impressions so far:++ Big variety of cars with 4 classes++ Characters with small background stories, which is kinda rare in racing games++ Good visual design+ Different modes+ Car customization+- Tracks are pretty easy, because they are wide- AI, while I haven't experienced a lot of rubberbanding, they seem to really enjoy smashing into you
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic love letter to retro Sega racing games. Characters look eccentric have cool quotes to say during racing. Each characters' vehicle roster is great and each of them work very differently in on each track. You can also customise them the way you want them, which is a neat touch. Didn't expected to have so many tracks to race in.However the game does show huge difficulty spike if you are race on the hardest difficulty. Even the opponents can bump you hard and throw you off the course. It is painful since you can't retry the race, you can retry the whole championship from the start.Overall, it is a fun and fast paced racing that should be in your library.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: Before writing the review, I just have to say: Having been just playing this for the past hour together with my brother, we both feel satisfied and having the urge to play more. It just honestly was a good fun for both of us, with both of us trying to outrun and outsmart each other in this exhilarating and chaotic racing game.If you see the complaints from others that this game is full of rubber-banding, I believe you would need to understand that this element for arcade racing games: especially such as this game that unabashedly pays homage to the racing games in the 1990's. I understand why many see rubber-banding as a terrible thing in a racing game, but honestly I think it is applied really well. I think it keeps you on your toes to always keep drifting if you are ahead, just to build the boost that you will need to retake your lead should you be overtaken.I mean, it is an arcade racing game. This game is not meant to be played with sim racing approach.If you grew up with games like Virtua Racing, Daytona, etc., you would spot several objects that truly captures the nostalgia of those games. I even almost believed that there is a track that is a carbon copy of a track in Virtua Racing. I initially wanted to buy the remastered Virtua Racing on Switch, but cancelled it when I saw this game. From a review I found on YouTube and the videos that show how this game looks, I can immediately see how this game tries to capture the feeling of Virtua Racing and other games that were inspired from it. In all honesty, I believed this game is worth every penny I spent. I am eager to find more content that the developer is seemingly developing. If it is sold as a separate DLC, I think I would buy one.

_childDocuments_.review: Puts the fun back into racing and a smile back on my face!A fun racing game reminiscent of Ridge Racer, Sonic Team Racing and almost every retro racing game ever created. If you like arcade style racers then this is for you. It's such a pity the (PC) online part of the game is virtually non-existent, however, the single player modes are great and dual player setting works well. For a casual way to spend a few hours I could not recommend this highly enough... but remember I was brought up on Ridge Racer, Virtua Racing and Sega Rally Championship... so I can't be wrong!
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: A game worthy of being called an arcade racer. Bright colourful visuals, an upbeat and energetic soundtrack and a driving model that puts an emphasis on fun over simulation. Yeah, back when the ideal method of getting round a corner was to drift around it and to catch up by injecting a little extra horsepower into your car with boost. On top of a timer that will end your race prematurely if you aren't driving fast enough. If you love arcade racers as much as I do, I can easily recommend Hotshot. Though, like any arcade racing cabinet, best played in short bursts or you will exhaust the game as fast as you cross the line.The only thing that's missing is a "de-de-de-de-do-dewe-da!" or "HOT-SHAO-OWWT.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: Before anything else, this game has a dead multiplayer community. That being said, the game is really fun, and brings back a lot of nostalgia for Daytona USA, SEGA Rally, and other retro arcade games. My main hope for this is they add crossplay and revive the multiplayer community, but the singleplayer seems to have enough to be fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine if Polyphony Digital had made Crash Team Racing in 1991.The makers of Hotshot Racing clearly have a deep love of real-world cars and motorsport. Every one of these cars is recognizable even when beautifully rendered in low-poly form.The four game modes each have their own charm and provide a variety of things to do in the game.And that soundtrack. Wow. It fits the game perfectly.I just bought this today — well, it was yesterday back then — and am now up entirely too late still playing it. Well worth the cost of entry already.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: Game is a lot of fun in the standard racing modes, but some modes don't work or need some touch ups. Drive or Die is particularly ridiculous. I'm sure it works okay if you're playing online with other players, but the AI isn't able to make the mode work. You can't get enough separation due to the rubberbanded enemies and the slipstream mechanic so they'll always be on your tail. Additionally, they hit you from behind often in every mode, but in this they deal damage without receiving any of their own. Nearly unplayable offline in that mode.I was able to load into the final Grand Prix at last, so now that's done, but there's just not much else to do. Once you have the skins and colors, the only thing left to do is unlock all the outfits and mods, but as they're only cosmetic, there's little interest to the player. I would love to see additional drivers or cars in the future, but for now, I think I'm done. 27 hours of play was all it took to complete the game on nearly all modes and beat the Grand Prix with all characters. There is some decent replayability, but without friends or online PVP, this isn't going to hold anyone over for long. 6\10.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: It's the perfect balance between oldskool and modern arcade racers. It's fast, simple, stunning andlots of fun. It's the first game after Ridge racer 7 that feels like Ridge Racer again, even harkening back to the Ridge Racer Revolution days. Simple, smooth, speedy gameplay on colorful and fast tracks with a lot of silky smooth driftwork. The graphics are simple yet very detailed and the framerate is what tops it off. One word of caution: this is not a game for days on days of straight up racing. It's more of an hour a day at most, just for the kick and the fun. But it will pull you back in regularly, because it races so damn good :)

_childDocuments_.review: HIGHLY RECOMMEND THIS GAME!!  This game taps into the arcade racing games of Sega's Golden Age (late 1980's to early 2000's) with one of the most visceral racing experiences to date.  On Expert (aka "150cc" mode), this game makes Mario Kart look like a kiddie game.  There's no reason NOT to play this game on Expert.  This game performs wonderfully at a near constant 60-fps which helps that sense of speed really kick in.  The environments are colorful and laden with landmarks to accentuate the grandeur of speed.  There's a wealth of cars from all walks of life worth appreciating--F1, Prototypes, GT, NASCAR, European exotics, muscle cars, JDM. The list goes on.This is honestly one of those rare games that both appeals to gamers and car guys alike.  It's a celebration of what makes racing so joyful and enthralling.  It's all the good stuff you like about cars and racing condensed into one package.  It's definitely more on the "shallow" end (since it is an arcade game after all), but if you must have the exemplar racing game, it's this one.  Everything about this game makes me smile (except maybe the VA's which can be muted).  This is an "easy to learn, hard to master," kind of game, so you can get a lot of replay value out of it if you are interested in competing.If you do play this game, play it with a USB controller (Xbox 360 or Logitech), or better yet, a steering wheel.  If you don't know how to configure the game to use a steering wheel, hit me up and I'll tell you how to set it up.  It makes the experience a magnitude better!

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic experience for any retro arcade racing fan. Interesting, colorful tracks, fun characters and exciting gameplay, all topped with an energetic, pumping soundtrack. Much like the retro racers this game pays homage to, there is a strong emphasis on drifting; and mastering those mechanics is essential if you want to play properly. I was, like some other people, annoyed that I couldn't change the steering to the d-pad; but, as it turns out, the thumbstick is very much necessary to perform proper drifts, since applying proper pressure can make or break your drift.The tracks all have some memorable moments and pretty much every turn has something beautiful to look at - whether it's a volcano ready to erupt, a casino-style stage straight out of the Sega racers, a water park with dolphins jumping out or literally driving through Jurassic Park with dinos roaring at you. Even Optimus Prime is hidden in one of the tracks - see if you can find him.Once you make your way through the default, racing mode, you have two other modes to have fun with: cops and robbers, where some characters play as the cops and are trying to stop other racers by depleting their health, thereby turning them into cops as well; and race or explode, where you need to keep your car above a certain speed limit, or - you explode.However, this game is not without its faults. I had some technical issues during playing - most notably, there were sudden framerate drops, seemingly out of nowhere. Also, for 20 euros, there's a surprising lack of content in here. Sure, racing on the great tracks this game has is a ton of fun and its 3 game modes definitely help with variety; but outside of some decent customization options, there's really not much else you can do at the moment. You have endings for finishing first in Grand Prix mode, but those are pretty lackluster and you get no bonus if you complete it on expert difficulty. I should also mention that expert difficulty is the way to go, since it's the only one that offers any kind of challenge and learning curve - other difficulties make the game way too easy. The AI can also be an absolute pain with how aggressive it is; there's nothing more frustrating than being first throughout the whole race, only for the computer to run you off the road and put you back about 5 places. With the huge amount of rubber-banding this game has, that's a big problem, since you are literally always neck-in-neck with the other racers. This is a double-edged sword to be sure, as it makes for some tight and adrenaline-filled gameplay, but also makes the whole experience needlessly frustrating at times.A free patch is supposed to come out soon, which will add new content; but until then, I'd wait for a sale before getting this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Next best thing to Outrun 2006: C2C, which is my favorite racing game. Sad to say my CD copy doesn't work on WIndows 10 and that FXT mod didn't appear to work for me either when I tried it recently. Still regretting not buying the game on Steam before it went away. The overall driving experience of this game has that arcade feel and similarity to Outrun and Daytona USA. The in-game control system needs work as I had to adjust my settings in DS4Windows for it to work properly with a PS4 controller. You can't re-map any controls in the game.* I'm not a fan of this art style. It's difficult to recognize the track vs. walls and other obstacles.* The looping courses feel limited and nothing like that feeling of that scenic selectable journey in Outrun 2k6. There is no traffic or other considerations in the game besides the competing racers. * There is occasional slowdown on my i7-6700 and GTX 1060 system even in low quality 1080p mode. I'm not sure what's happening giving the blocky non-textured style of this game.* The characters seem very stereotypical. Kind of awkward to see and hear constantly. * The AI is extremely basic. Expect Mario Kart 1 level of cheap if not worse. It appears impossible to win by a wide margin unless you save your boosts and spam them toward the end.* There is a definite difference between the classes of cars for each character. I've been using Keiko and the F1 style car a lot, though I did use the Android quite a bit too. The drift car seems extremely difficult to win anything at expert level. So far I've gotten all golds in the first and second tiers, and one gold on expert. Haven't tried the tracks in reverse and haven't looked much into the two other modes.Very much not a replacement for my favorite racing game, but it gives me just enough of that similar driving feel to like the game. I'm overall happy with the game for what I paid at less than the already pretty low price. That said, I really wish Sega and Sumo Digital could somehow take the source of OutRun 2006 C2C and remove/replace the Ferrari stuff so we could have an updated improved version of that game. That's the game I really want...

_childDocuments_.review: This game has great graphics that capture the Virtua Racing style feel perfectly, and the music is OK, but this game would be much better without the rubber banding.I'm don't proclaim to be the best game player in the world, but I'm not totally crap either, and I absolutely love racing games, the Outrun series, Virtua Racing, Daytona, Sega Rally etc, but I found it very hard to win races in this game, even on the easiest difficulty setting due to the rubber banding, and any time I did happen to win seemed to be more by pure luck rather than any form of skill. And I can't believe this game commits the cardinal sin of racers barging you from behind, sending you flying and straight into the side of the track while they go through as if nothing happened! How is this STILL an issue in a modern racing game?The Cops and Robbers mode is awful too, and I couldn't find any way to select which one I wanted to be? It just selected whether you were a cop or robber at random, and then the second time I played switched from one to another half way through the game! wtf? The Need For Speed Hot Pursuit series did the cops and robbers thing far better than this,If I see this game in a 80% or 75% sale in the future I might get it again but at full price I just can’t find any value for money this in game. The rubber banding kills it for me.

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of mixed thoughts in this comments section, here are my pros, cons, and whatever in between. I'd give it a 7/10 for solo content and 9/10 if you're derping around with other people. Man is it old-school. Love the design, bright palette, music, the feel. It's primary goal was to be an arcade-racer and, as for the theme, they nailed it. The driving is smooth and the AI is challenging (maybe too much so - more on this later). I play with an Xbox One controller and have had no issues, so I'm not sure what the deal is for other people.The characters are comical and the voice acting, be it for the announcers or the racers, is all top notch. I found myself laughing aloud at some of Viktor's lines.There's a fair amount of rewards to unlock, all cosmetic related. That's fine by me; this game was clearly made with multiplayer in mind and upgrading a car to give an advantage doesn't fit that vision (especially since there's no career mode).The additional game modes are all really neat. The cops and robbers "tag" game mode is a standout idea executed perfectly for multiplayer madness. Additionally, being able to download others' ghost times in time trials adds a fun competitive edge to a group of friends playing this game. My one wish here though would be that you could sort the times by your Steam friends list. The tracks don't feel all that different. I suppose that's a critique about a lot of old arcade games too - Cruisin' World maps were all pretty generic with layout, for example. Nonetheless, for a game with Mario Kart Grand Prix events on maps that lap, some additional hazards or challenges across maps would be welcome. Some people have complained about the AI "rubberbanding," which is not the case. The game actually uses a slipstream mechanic. The speed you gain while slipstreaming is incredible and can be more than a boost, which is partially how the AI keep up so well. Additionally, while  slipstreaming, you charge  your "boost" meter. So, if an AI is in your slipstream, not only are they outpacing you even if you're boosting, but they can dance around you and use their newly generated boost to plow past you.On one hand, this mechanic helps keep races tight and interesting, but it the raw power of slipstreaming seems overtuned to the point where good driving and being in first place doesn't feel rewarding. Sure, it can narrow the gap in multiplayer to ensure exciting races, but the handicap from slipstreaming is too strong.All in all, I think it's a pretty game that nails its core identity, creating an enjoyable and nostalgic experience. Again, I'd give  it a 7/10 for solo content and 9/10 if you have friends.

_childDocuments_.review: Hotshot Racing is a fun little arcade racer that takes me back to the days of my childhood. Hotshot Racing's visual style is low-poly, obviously inspired by arcade racers like Ridge Racer and Virtua Racer. It's hyper-fast and it has a bangin' soundtrack that sounds like it would fits perfectly on any SEGA racer from the 90s. Each track has it's own theme, and while they aren't wildly different in feel, they are vibrant and have a fun charm with animated background props that you'll notice as you race, such as dolphins jumping over the track or a dinosaur roaring at you as you drift around a corner. There's a simple Grand Prix mode, with various difficulties to play through as you go for the gold in 16 different tracks that are split up between four cups. There's also 'Single Race', 'Time Trial', and a couple other modes "Cops & Robbers" and "Drive Or Explode", both which seem to boil down to the same goal 'drive fast, don't crash'. There's also multiplayer (offline and online) for these modes, though I don't have anyone to try the offline multiplayer with so I can't speak for how well these run. Online seemed to work great, when I was able to find a match. You can customize the handful of drivers you can play as (each with their own personalities and phrases you'll hear during the races) and each racer has their own set of cars to pick from, each with their own stats. As you play, you'll be unlocking more cosmetics as you make progress on achievements that are specific to each car. The cosmetics don't affect performance, however, but you want to look cool as you're drifting at high speed! Overall, I'm happy with this game so far, I hope to see more added in the future, and I recommend it to anyone that enjoys simple arcade racing games.

_childDocuments_.review: There is a really amazing game underneath some technical and day one issues. I personally have not had any technical issues but I understand that it is a problem. More customization and more tracks are required but for $16, driving mechanics this smooth and fun are worth it. This might change in a year if the devs don't fix issues and don't add content.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: This game started out with tons of potential. It was a wonderful throwback to classics like Sega Super GT (SCUD Race) with tight driving dynamics and lots of personality. It was buggy and the online multiplayer had weird issues, but I left a pretty thorough positive review at the time.Sadly I'm returning to change my positive review to a negative one, for two reasons:- At launch, there was one car that was overwhelmingly dominant in the time attack meta. A few months later there was a content update; while the new courses were welcome, instead of rebalancing all the cars or nerfing the fast car, they made every single car in the game faster, which ruined the great driving dynamics in the upper classes.- The multiplayer is now completely non-functional. It had some issues at launch but it was at least possible to play online through the bugs. Now this is essentially a single player-only game.RIP Hotshot Racing. You had so much potential.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: Plays good looks nice sounds goodYeah its good.....but....Bit disappointed if i'm honest, there's like 4 tracks with 4 variations of each really, and to get any sort of challenge out of them you have to play it on hardest difficulty other wise you'll just go through them all only braking once per lap on average. Its basically a mario kart 50cc-150cc setup in the difficulty. but with mario kart 50cc still has weapons to make things interesting, here its just racing with no challenge.Also using manual gears is basically out as the 1 locked pad config is triggers for accelerate and gears on the buffers. seems a really stupid basic mistake.Sounds like i'm on a downer but i was really looking forward to this and its just disappointing is all, not bad but not great either. Its the tracks really, nothing matches up to the challenges of the old sega ect games from the 90's too many of them are flatout. hopefully they'll add a few more later. Personally as far as playing im not running into any of the problems a lot of people seem to be having. I'm using an xbox one original pad working fine (apart from the dodgy layout)games running fine using an old 1080 gtx and an even older 2 series i5 im running 4k at 60fps not a hitch
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: I see a few reviews saying their controller doesn't work.  My XB1 controller works fine.  There is not button customization in-game, but it works fine still.  Overall, a fun racing game.  Cool look, some nice character/car customization options, and pretty easy to handle gameplay.  Well worth the price if you're looking for a more "casual" racing game.
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: View my full review here:For fans of arcade racers (Sega Rally, Virtua Racer, Mariokart, etc...) You're going to love this!In the package you're getting Grand Prix (4 to play through, 4 tracks a piece), Single Racing, Time Trial and Online Play. I was able to play everything except for the online play, as this was pre-release.First things first, the cars control beautifully. There are several characters to pick from and play as and each character has  a distinct personality (complete with voice overs and phrases they say during races) and they each have 4 cars you can use. Each car actually does have it's own attributes for things like Drift and Speed and believe it or not, you can actually feel the slight difference from each car!The boost system is something I really like in this game too! You get 4 bars of boost but you have to earn them from drifting and slip streaming behind other cars. you get to choose when these are put to use, usually during tight sequences when it could mean the difference between 1st and 2nd place.The track variations are really fun! There is a dinosaur track, a casino track and an ancient ruins track - just to name a few. No matter the track though, the dev team did a great job of making all of them fun to drive on!Back to the characters themselves, the game features more story and characterization than I was expecting for them. Not only do they have voice overs as I mentioned above, but they also have stories! You won't really know what their background is until you finish with them in Grand Prix mode, but I was surprised to see that each character gets a cutscene, complete with some background about them and what they did after winning.The game also features an unlock system for each character and their cars. As you accomplish things in each car, like drifting and what not, you will unlock these accomplishments and then unlock money to buy customizations for all your cars! This also brought on one of my only complaints about the game, which is that I wish the accomplishment stuff was a little more "in your face" before you start a race. The accomplishments are buried in the menus if you want to see what else you have to do for them, which is annoying if you just want to get started.All in all, great arcade racer, recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Hotshot Racing

_childDocuments_.review: Hotshot Racing is a blisteringly fast arcade-style racing game fusing drift handling, razor-sharp retro visuals and an incredible sense of speed to create an exhilarating driving experience.

name: Desperados III
detailed_description: Desperados III is a story-driven, hardcore tactical stealth game, set in a ruthless Wild West scenario. In this long-awaited prequel to the beloved classic Desperados: Wanted Dead or Alive, John Cooper will join forces with the runaway bride Kate, the shady hitman Doc McCoy, the giant trapper Hector, and Isabelle, a mysterious lady from New Orleans. On Cooper’s quest for redemption, his adventures lead him and his gang from rural towns, over swamps and riverbanks, and finally to a dramatic showdown worthy of Wild West legends. Play smart if you want to succeed. A good plan can make the difference between survival and finding yourself at the business end of a pistol. Drifter, gunslinger, and natural leader Cooper can kill quietly with a knife, or take out multiple foes with his revolvers. Strongman Hector carries a giant bear trap and can slay the toughest opponents with his trusty axe. Cold blooded bounty hunter McCoy likes to be methodical, using lures, knockout gas, poison syringes and a custom long-range pistol. Kate can fool almost any man with the right outfit, and kills discreetly with her hidden gun. And then there is this mysterious woman from New Orleans, Isabelle… Combine your team’s special skills to overcome each tough challenge in your own style. Play five unique characters, each with a very particular set of skills Experience true freedom of choice with countless different ways to overcome any obstacle Defeat large groups of enemies with careful planning and execution Witness the glory of classic Wild West scenarios like frontier towns, mysterious swamps, sprawling modern cities, and many more Choose between non-lethal and deadly attacks, stealth and blazing guns Adjust the game to your playstyle with various difficulty settings and special replay challenges The Showdown mode allows you to pause the game anytime and react to ambushes or surprise attacks

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:+ nice graphics and animations+ quality themed music and sound+ great UI+ smart designed locations+ various types of difficulty from simple to crazy challenges within different locations+ variability of characters abilities and their synergy+ more types of opponents with different reactionsCons:- Reactions to environmental killings have a peculiar effect- Some characters and their abilities are very strong compared to anotherMimimi Games has already been scored in their previous game, Shadow Tactics, and Desperados 3 continues the trend. It is the same genre in the setting of the wild west, where the authors have brought many things to almost perfection. Here we have a group of characters in the observable story, who communicate together in the mission in well-spoken dialogues and voices under tones of a quality western soundtrack. The authors managed to achieve really nice graphics and quality animations within the unity engine.The player has a very well UI available for the elimination of enemies with various options for displaying patrol vision zones, there is also a time stop where you can plan the simultaneous execution of several character actions at one time. However, this option is not available at the highest difficulty of the game. The difficulty of the game ranges from a relatively simple to an insanely difficult challenges within individual 16 story missions or special baron challenges missions.The variability of the elimination of opponents, attracting them, hiding bodies, use of the environment are wide, but sometimes it is more interesting and challenging not to use some of the strong abilities of the characters, e.g. I used the mind control of the native Isabelle only in the turtorial of this ability.The reactions of the enemy camp for environmental killings does not work well (they look at it for a while and then it works as if nothing happened), as well as searching for lost mates does not end with an alarm but just returning to the loop. On the other hand, it is basically a puzzle game and not a simulation of reality.Desperados 3 is a great game, a must for fans of genre fans, where everyone can find their own challenge.
_childDocuments_.name: Desperados III

_childDocuments_.name: Desperados III

I'm still not fully finished with the game, so far the story has been extremely entertaining, but I am heavily biased as I love most wild west themed games.Would recommend to any fans of strategy tactics games.

_childDocuments_.review: Full review: TLDR: An engaging story and near-impeccable gameplay mechanics combined with AAA-like presentation makes Desperados III a must-play for strategy lovers.+ Manages to feel like a successor to both OG Desperados and Shadow Tactics at the same time+ Engaging story+ Absolutely amazing stealth mechanics+ Awesome AI+ Each character is unique and fun to play+ Big open levels for such a game+ Mission structure is varied and allow for lots of experiment and creativity+ Lengthy single player campaign (20+hrs)+ Lots of ways to customize difficulty settings+ Looks great, runs great, sounds great- Micromanaging multiple characters can be frustrating due to the controls - Takes a long time to fully open up- Forced to play certain missions with certain character combinations (that's just a nitpick)
_childDocuments_.name: Desperados III

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of the Commando's series and Desperados from years ago I was really looking forward to this and have not been disappointed. This is a stellar game, you can really feel the care and attention that the devs put into this, from the mechanics, to the story, the mission specific and action specific character commentaries and diverse level design it all combines to make a really memorable and enjoyable game that's part puzzle, part strategy, part reflexes and part adventure - very much enjoyed it.
_childDocuments_.name: Desperados III

_childDocuments_.review: The game is an absolute must have for all Commandos-style lovers! One of the best releases of 2020. Great job Mimimi!The mechanics is basically the good old Shadow Tactics with a couple of refinements.It's pretty polished and stable (finished half of the game so far) and can be enjoyed right after the release - a rare thing these days..I absolutely love the difficulty of the game and the fact, that it's doesn't follow the trend to simplify everything. I play on hard and sometimes you have to really think how to clear/pass a sector.A few things may have been done better or to improve laterr:1. The graphics looks a bit blurry and simple for a game with AAA price tag in 2020, the game easily hits 165 fps (cap for my system with rtx 2080) in 1440p with max settings. On the other hand, it's should be playable well on potatoes.2. It's not possible to queue more than one action in showtime mode, which limits the tactics component a bit.3. The subtitles don't always show on dialogs and sometimes it's hard to understand what npc's are saying.Can't find any more negatives about it. Just buy and enjoy it!

_childDocuments_.review: Even better than the already-stellar Shadow Tactics: Blades of the Shogun. Desperados III is basically the same mechanics, with a few adjustments, and in a whole new genre: the Wild West. Most the abilities from ST:BotS carry over in some form or another, such as a thrown coin instead of a thrown rock, or a bear trap instead of whatever Yuki's little trap was.In addition to new maps, a new story, new characters, and such, there's also lots of cool new features. After beating a map you can see a time-lapse of your progress through the map for a cool little review of it, which is a nice way to round it out. There's also actual nonlethal options now: you can knock people out and tie them up, which not only is an option for pacifist runs or being able to deal with civilians, but some missions and their objectives rely on it. Guns play a bigger part and are more versatile than the flintlocks in Shadow Tactics - as they should be in such a setting. The planning mode now pauses the game, though the highest difficulty undoes this to make the planning mode act like it does in ST.Not only that but there's vastly more content. In addition to having more maps than ST, there's additional challenge maps to spice things up, and DLC if you want even more maps than that to play with. Everything that made Shadow Tactics excellent has remained, like the optional challenges (that are only revealed after you beat the game once).Definitely recommended, even if you're new to the RTT genre, as it has flexible difficulty settings.
_childDocuments_.name: Desperados III

_childDocuments_.review: ♥♥♥♥, this game's good. It's a stealthy strategy game, and what's great about it, is the options it gives you to approach finishing the levels. It also gives you quite a few challenges. After you finish a level, the game goes "Oh you made it? Great, now you can replay it and do it with this very ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hard limitation, good luck". My hours right now are at 25, that was only the campaign, without any of the challenge runs, it has content for days if you're into the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: The game very much follows the same concept as the old Desperados, Commandos, etc. but adds some nice additions and innovations. Graphics are good for this type of game but nothing exciting. It feels partially a bit repetitive to kill and hide opponents, while sometimes it also only works by trial and error. 8.5/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Desperados III

_childDocuments_.review: If you've played Shadow Tactics then the short version of this review is that the game is a direct upgrade to SS as far as most aspects of the game are concerned. Gameplay is better and has a lot of Quality of Life upgrades, maps are bigger and have more approaches, animations both in-game and in cutscenes are better, the medal challenges per mission are harder and more interesting, and graphics received an overhaul too. The only thing I feel is worse (but not bad) are the characters which aren't as fun/interesting as the SS group.  My time spent on each mission is pretty much the same as in ST so expect the same game length  (edit: finished the story at 19 hours on Hard, so it was longer than SS in my case, still not done with medals and the Baron Challenges though). It's well worth the purchase if you liked Shadow Tactics since it's pretty much Shadow Tactics But Better: Cowboy Edition.For anyone that isn't familiar with the genre, Desperados III is a RTT Stealth game where you control a group of vigilantes/bounty hunters/bandidos as they take on a greedy railway company that's too lazy to build its tracks around people's homes. The story is fairly simple and mostly acts as a backdrop to move characters from set piece to set piece, it's a solid story but it won't win any awards, the characters are fairly likeable and have unique quips for every missions which helps make them come across as proper characters. The gameplay is pretty great, it works like a Hitman game but with Real Time Tactics gameplay, you have a map, your targets, and must find the best way to deal with these targets (or the one you prefer). The game is fairly good on its own, and I recommend it for that alone, and if you're interested in getting into the genre then this game is a great starting point before getting into the harder titles like the Commandos series.
_childDocuments_.name: Desperados III

_childDocuments_.review: Just got back into PC gaming after 10 years and came across this gem of a game after watching Mack (Worth A Buy) on YouTube. The voodoo lady is totally OP in my opinion lol. I see the DLC is on sale today as of writing this so will have pick that up! Cowboy up mothe... 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: "Real-time stealth-based old-west action CRPG" is a bit of a mouthful, but the game is effortlessly accessible to new players and seasoned veterans alike. Each and every stage is a lovingly crafted diorama of seemingly impossible stealth challenges that, after some thought and whittling away over time, are conquered utilizing the vast array of useful and unique abilities and tools the devs provide.Though definitely following pretty closely in the footsteps of Shadow Tactics before it, the Desperados legacy can be felt, even by new players, as it elevates the proceedings with unique and beautiful miniatures of the old west.Part Hitman, part board game; it's great fun through the campaign and has a generous offering of extra challenges that are, honestly, more fun than they even need to be.

_childDocuments_.review: As expected from Mimimi Games, and more! After having played Shadow Tactics for over 70+ hours, buying this game was a foregone conclusion. And boy, am I glad! So far, 6+ hours into the game and 5 missions down, I'm only getting started. The characters (have not yet met Isabelle Moreau) are well-written & interesting, with their varied skills, items and weapons. Love the replay browser (a top-down overview of all your progress after finishing a mission). One thing I love about games like this is that you can take your time, plan your course of action according to the environment and NPCs around.A must-buy for strategy fans! You won't be disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: Desperados III

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed my time with Desperados 3 a lot. If you want a quick opinion then I would say that this game is definitely a buy. At first I thought that the price is unreasonable, but after beating a game and discovering so many unique locations and a 30hr long campaign I think that 50$ price is totally justified.So, here is an in depth look into the game from my perspective.I would like to start from the story and I see a lot of progress compared to Shadow Tactics. The motivation for our main protagonist is clear as  a day. Yes, everyone is tired from revenge stories, but here it is only a boost for Cooper. I would say that this is more like a road movie, which concentrates on relationships between very distinct and unique characters, which I have fallen in love with. The dialogues, specific phrases for each of them, reactions when they meet each other and show their skills, all of that is top notch. By the way, the color identification of each character is a cool feature. They went so far, that tone of the characters voices changes depending on the current mood in the band. Considering the gameplay-centric nature of the game I would say that everything about the characters and the story is executed perfectly.Let's bring the big elephant in the room, which is gameplay. I highly recommend you to start your playthrough on a HARD difficulty, cos then you will have the most from satisfaction of executing a perfect plan. As you probably know, each character has a set of different abilities, which tie them to a unique play style. The balance is almost perfect and you need to use all of them on HARD in order to succeed, which is wonderful. You gain the most from using characters in synergy in tactical pause mode and the only feature that I miss is creating a few actions for one character in a row. Of course, some locations are created more for some characters than the others, but with enough creativity you can play as wild as you want. At first I thought that this will be less of a stealth game and more action based, considering the addition of the guns, but it appears that these are more of a ranged stealth tools. All the gadgets are extremely fun to use and some of them have a specific bond with the owner, like Hector and Bianca (loved these two so much). The enemy variety is almost the same as in Shadow Tactics, which is fine, but the cool addition is consideration of an enemy gender, which creates fun situations when you play as Kate in her disguise. The one enemy type that I didn't see enough were dogs that push you back from hiding spots and adding more tension to gameplay. Overall, I can't praise the core gameplay enough and knowing that there aren't really any alternatives in this genre I would say that it is the best of its kind.Finally a bit about the visual and soundtrack beauty of this game. First, in almost every location you feel the atmosphere of cruel and lifeless wild west, but the location variety doesn't stop there. You will travel across multiple biomes which sound and look nice. The esthetical part of myself was pleased every minute of playing. The sound of the game hits splendidly both purely technical, like sounds of abilities, and the artistic parts. Some of the melodies still play in my head, which is a defining factor here.In the end, Desperados 3 is a game like no other(not counting Shadow Tactics) and it perfectly hits the real time tactics niche. I am incredibly happy that there are still developers that are able to create such great games in this genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Desperados III

_childDocuments_.review: Such a fun game. This game brings back the nostalgia. Really well made missions and refreshing look at characters keeping some elements from the old ones. Thank you for making this game and the additional content. This game genre is seriously underrated and I will buy every such game that comes out new.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a real surprise; I didn't expect it to be anywhere near as good as it ended up being. I got about halfway through Shadow Tactics (by the same developers) before finding it too frustrating to continue.Desperados III is just an improvement in every way. The story is enjoyable and satisfying, with a zany cast of varied characters with a healthy dose of moral ambiguity about them. The overarching tale is of five people with almost nothing in common except a shared desire to take vengeance upon the bandit leader Frank, but the cast get into all sorts of amusing scrapes along the way. This story is mostly told via cutscenes at the beginning and end of each level, leaving the excellent gameplay mostly interrupted.Each of your five characters has a very different playstyle. It's quite rare that you're in control of all five of them in the same location at any given point in time, so you often have to experiment with synergies between pairs or trios of characters as well as with the layout of the levels and the characteristics of each environment. All of this succeeds in making every level seem completely fresh. You even learn to work with aspects of your characters that may initially seem like a disadvantage - Kate is much slower to move bodies than Hector or John, but she does so from a crouching position, which can help her to evade the gaze of nearby enemies.The difficulty is set just right. Many of the scenarios are pretty challenging and will take you several attempts to work out, but between the pause button (sorely lacking in Shadow Tactics) and generous quicksave/quickload functionality, you'll eventually be able to muddle a way through each of them. As you progress through the game's campaign levels you also unlock Baron Challenges, which I found significantly more difficult - it may be better to leave them until the end of the game, when you know your characters back to front and are able to co-ordinate them effectively.Desperados III is enjoyable, satisfying and full to the brim with varied content. Any fan of real-time tactics games should give it a try.

All in all, this is a nice game, but hell, these simple mechanics that don't work can piss me right off.

_childDocuments_.review: Didn’t play their first game, but after playing Desperados III I’m going to have to go back. Desperados is simply fantastic, it never becomes too difficult to manage, but forces you to plan and perfect your maneuvers. You simply are not going to ever pass through without failing, that’s what makes the quicksave/quickload system fit so well. Sometimes you can picture what you want to happen, you’re just going to need to perfect the sequence of actions you will take to get there, and there is little penalty to experimentation. Of course, if every level required the same strategy, then you wouldn’t need to utilize that experimentation, but this is where the designers really show off their skills. Each level has varying objectives and the cast changes so you’re never quite comfortable.  The characters are of course varied and each one is capable enough to not allow you to bench someone. Those synergies are the real core of what you are going to be perfecting and where each character’s strengths are going to shine. Not to overly gush here, but even the story is fun. I really expected to skip most of it, but it plays out in such a way that it keeps you interested, and the characters are just fun to hear.  I would highly recommend this game to strategy fans or really just video game fans in general, it’s my GOTY so far.

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely, one of the best games I've ever played. The first Mimimi game I've ever played was Shadow Tactics: Blades of the Shogun; loved it, finished it, and totally had fun with it. Then, I heard the developers came out with a new game, hence, why I'm writing this review, to recommend this other game titled Desperados III. I'm late to the party, I know, having played only two Mimimi games and starting out the Desperado franchise with the third installment, nonetheless, I will definitely recommend this due to the fact that it carries with it the same narrative-driven strategy game that I've come to love from Blades of the Shogun, albeit a Western setting this time.The characters and their motivations are well thought out and the mechanics are innovative in their own way. Each character has their own set of skills and abilities, and using them in sync with one another creates multiple options for the players, in terms of carrying out the mission objectives (and the hidden ones as well).  This freedom implemented by the game provides countless hours of replayability and challenge, urging the player to try out other ways to finish the mission the second time around. Aside from that, the developers were generous enough to create DLCs and challenges which can be unlocked per level progress. Now, isn't that amazing?!Overall, Desperados III retains the charm and replayability that Shadow Tactics: Blades of the Shogun was able to offer. Hopefully, Mimimi games would continue to develop more Desperados games in the future, continuing where the story left off. Don't get me wrong, the story of Desperados III is already complete and compelling enough, at least for this particular installment. Perhaps, they can introduce new baddies and additional game mechanics in the future to keep it all fresh. But for now, I highly recommend this game. Kudos, Mimimi Games!

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic Sequel to one of my favorite Strategy Games - Nostalgia Galore included.The Characters are hillarious clichés and even more over the Top than in the Original, but i love it. Their Animations and Sounddesign are smooth and really satisfying to pull off (e.g. Knife / Buntline / Pistols / Bianca). The Soundtrack is an absolutely fantastic Mix between Rock, Western, Swing and Soundtrack. Although it can feel a bit repetitive in certain Levels and / or Situations if you spend too much time on them. While the Story is a bit lighthearted and overly dramatic at other times - and seems to be mostly about having reasons why certain characters are in certain Scenarios for the players to beat - that's not what the game really is about. It's about the great tactical riddles you have to solve however you want to. The Ingame-Banter on the other hand is fantastic and hillarious at times, with the Doc-Hector-Bianca-Love-Triangle taking the Cake. The well cast Voice-Actors make this ragtag posse a family I definitely didn't mind to revisit for Post-Campaign-Gameplay. It ONLY has 16 Levels - compared to the original that had 25 - but those 16 levels are almost all killer, No filler. On Desperado i needed 30 Hours on my first Playthrough and am still working on beating all the extra challenges, finding new ways to tackle the Levels included.  The extra challenges completely change how you have to approach situations and give this game around 100+ hours of Gameplay.If i had to criticize things it would be, that the AI has a few glaring flaws that can be abused once found out, making playing on the extremest of difficulties way too easy. They are generally way more predictable than in the original Desperados, where they would just frantically roam around in terror making life uneasy and the Gameplay more unpredictable for really long times. Also the Patrols are really easy to wear down (Bianca / Knifethrow / Voodoo) and never really make your game harder - Just artificially longer.The Game has some weird bugs that rarely happen, where it will just refuse to save a mission. I only encountered this once in my playthrough, which was a game breaking bummer and had me restart the mission.Overall it's a 9/10 from my side and i am really hyped for Potential DLC or Sequel!
