_childDocuments_.review: F5 Simulator, western edition!Heads up, if you take away anything from this review, let is be this: NOT worth 60 bucks. Not at all worth 60 bucks!If you ever played a Hitman game, it's basically that, without the nice perspective, variation and decent AI-Enemies. Otherwise it's a Hitman-Ripoff: There are stealth kills, accident kills, disguises, the whole shabang. Once the alarm is raised, you lost.The graphics look like a mobile-game from 10 years ago. A real missed opportunity. Get it? Missed opportUNITY? That explains the washed out, rough graphics.I don't know why they did that. The levels aren't big and there are no demanding effects whatsoever.Gameplay is fun, story is okay. In the Hitman games, you're one assasin with all the skills. Here, it's hero-based. They broke the skills up between 5 heroes.Also, the game is VERY challenging for me, for all the wrong reasons. Enemies have these (immersion-breaking) view-cones. Enemies spot you if you step into their view-cones.The most challenging thing in this game, is overlapping view-cones. You can't take out one enemy without being spotted by the other.I hear you say "But dude, that's the game!". Yes. But these enemies always do the same route, repeating every 30 seconds tops. They are dumb as rocks otherwise. And the ONLY challenge is their inconvenient placement. What I'm saying is that this game might as well be a chess-puzzle. There's no need for the "western" theme, you could just reskin it to a ninja themed game. Which the developer did: It's called Shadow Tactics! What a coincidence! Also: The "big map" is NOT BIG. Let me explain: You start a level, and there's a big map. On this map, you have 4 targets to kill. Those targets don't interact with each other. They are each in a separate part of the map, repeating their 30 second routine. These targets function completely independent of each other, in their own little segment of the map.Think of the map as a square. Divide this square into four smaller squares. Place a target in each smaller square. This is how the game works. The graphics make it look like one big interconnected map, when in fact, it just consists of little boxes holding one target each. Those little boxes are placed next to each other, giving the impression of a big map, which it is not, because the "boxes" DON'T interact with each other.One last point, because some neckbeard will come out of the woods and say "But man, stop comparing this to Hitman. Hitman is a Triple A game, and MIMIMI studios are a small indie-studio".Listen up, friend: If they charge me 60 dollars for their indie-sausage, it means they charge a Triple A price for it. And then, I expect Triple A value of a game. Which this game clearly does not deliver. Not at all.I love anything western-related, that's why I bought it. But you can buy the new Hitman games for way less money, if you're not into Westerns, DEFINITELY buy those!

_childDocuments_.review: Desperados III is a prequel game to the franchise, which makes it great entry point to the game series. Mechanics are pretty great and there is different ways to play, pure stealth and mix of action/stealth. Each character has their own strengths and abilities which make them differ from others. While this game doesn't have the greatest voice acting (Southern accents totally gone and mobs keep spamming "who finds them gets their stuff" and that is very repetitive after a while). Also i do want to stress if you have played the previous game by Mimimi Games (Blades of shogun) this game is almost reskin copy of that game mechanically, so there isn't much new really added in. However setting is new and so is the story..
_childDocuments_.name: Desperados III

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome game. Real time tactics commandos feel and slick controls to boot.  Game encourages meticulous planning and experimentation.  The tutorial encourages save scumming but I do not find that to be a bad thing is this case as the game's intent is to facilitate and engender experimentation via trail and error. Although certain perfect star conditions require no saving, you can do practice runs before retrying missions with no-saves in mind. In short, the game cultivates tactics and practicing such tactics to refinement.That leads us to this: the game is very open ended with how you complete objectives. You can do objectives in any order and you are really not forced to go on certain stratagems. Although there are maps that points out specific strategies, you are technically not forced to do so and you can even renege on these instances and do something entirely different from that was intended.Overall, I highly recommend this game as a worthy Real Time Tactics game and a solid experience in its own right.
_childDocuments_.name: Desperados III

_childDocuments_.review: For some reason these viewcone-dodging stealth puzzle games always get my heart rate up, more than even most FPS. And this is one of the best, for sure. The story is full of all the usual Western cliches, but it's fun and knows what it's about.And yeah, it's so very satisfying to play. What could easily have been a tedium of identical takedowns, feels instead like each new set of guards is a completely different puzzle, well-thought-out and requiring new tricks and timings. And it's difficult enough that even though I *know* there are plenty of ways to navigate the maps, sometimes just finding *any* solution that works is a great feeling. Plus, it's pretty and ran well on my laptop without any jagginess despite all the pausing and planning I did, so that's the first couple hurdles right there. Finished it in 35 hrs and it felt very doable (though I was obviously not going for speed) and the little extra quests they've released are also quite fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Desperados III

_childDocuments_.review: Playing it during free weekend on a whim, and totally enjoying it. I've got it on my wishlist now. I've never played a "real time tactical" genre game, and it's a fun twist on the FPS and RTS games I already play and love. Fun storyline so far, decent graphics, fun interactions. No complaints. I'll look to get the game in the future!
_childDocuments_.name: Desperados III

_childDocuments_.review: If you only watched trailers or a part of the gameplay you might think to yourelf "this game is just Shadow Tactics pt.2". I honestly bought it because I was thinking that, but I was so overwhelmingly surprised I had to make this review.This game picks up on that legacy and presents a very polished version of the mechanics presented in Shadow Tactics while adding a few features that give the game a few more possibilities for the player to experiment.If you expect to be using guns all the time you couldn't be more wrong: guns are loud as hell, and when you trying to sneak through, that's the last thing you want. Interactions between characters and abilities are way more fluid, and feel nicer compared to ST. Also the feature where there are "neutral zones" where you can walk unnoticed is also a very cool addition. I could go on and on about new features that fit the game very nicely, but I'd rather let you figure them out yourself.To me what speaks the loudest here is the maturity they have gained in the storytelling departmentShadow Tactics' storyline is quite predictable and a bit bland, but you really don't care because of the awesome mechanics the game brings, even if they are a bit clunky at times. In Desperados 3 the storytelling is very compelling, and the way the story unfolds really puts you at the edge of your seat at each new chapter. Also, the voice acting has sure been a point of improvement from ST, which helps charaters have WAY more personality.I'm looking forward to finishing this game and if you liked Shadow Tactics for the genre/mechanics this is a must play. If you like the Wild West, give it a try, because getting out of the fps/tps niche in this theme and doing a good job at it is a very hard thing to do.
_childDocuments_.name: Desperados III

_childDocuments_.review: Desperados 3 is a Real Time Tactics game developed by the same group that did Shadow Tactics: Blades of the Shogun, so if you've played that you'll feel right at home with Desperados 3.The first thing I'd like to highlight, is despite Desperados 3 being the "Third" main entry into the series, the game is actually a prequel/soft reboot. You do not need to play any of the other older Desperados games in order to understand the story, this game is rather self-contained and doesn't require any prior knowledge of the other games; thus making it easier to get into.The game itself is very Trial and Error, you will be using Quick Save and Quick Load a lot, which isn't as bad as it sounds, to complete missions and have everything run smoothly. For those who have played Shadow Tactics you will notice that a lot of the abilities from that game carry over to this one.The cast themselves are all interesting characters in my opinion, to your standard Cowboy main character archetype, to the seductress all the way to the voodoo woman, utilising their abilities and having everything connect together to complete missions, is nothing short of satisfying; especially after you pull off all five people doing something at once using Showdown Mode.The story isn't anything to write home about but this is one of those games where the story merely serves as an excuse for the enjoyable and interested gameplay, it's unlikely you'll care about what's going on in the story but you'll be more interested in the set-pieces and enemy locations as to rack your brain to figure out the best solution forward.There are dozens of ways to complete any given mission, different routes, who to use, what abilities to prioritise, this for me is what makes the game enjoyable; you can play the same mission twice but you probably won't accomplish it the same way twice.Of course in games like this there are challenge modes, DLC missions and what not which are also enjoyable, I only just completed the main story when writing this review but I know some of them are effectively; "Do this mission with only these characters, instead of the original ones." And some are just brand new missions entirely, which means you can get a lot of time and content out of this game for what you pay for it.To complete the main story it'll take around 15-25 hours at best, since there will be times where you're just staring at the screen, watching guard patterns and thinking. "This is bloody impossible." Only for something to click, an ability you rarely use becomes feasible and then you've got it.Overall, this game has my recommendation, although I did prefer Shadow Tactics: Blades of the Shogun (Purely because I prefer the Japanese Sengoku Era aesthetic) This is a fantastic game and a great entry into the Real Time Tactics Genre and a must have for any stealth game enthusiasts out there.7/10, fantastic gameplay, lacklustre story.

At the same time, nearly nobody offers free demo version to try out, but I think it shouldn't cost extra and all companies should adopt demo versions as a commercial part for their own job. _childDocuments_.review: Don't take my words likely: This game is  tactical. People who don't like tactical games (TRPGs) will hate this game. Just killing a single enemy often takes a minute or more of planning and when you're talking about 50+ enemies per level, you can see that playing this game is NOT fast and there is NO 'run-n-gun' option in this game at all... You literally are forced to play tactically or you'll just die. So, don't even try this game if you don't like TRPGs because this game makes somebody like me feel a little weary of playing this game for a couple of hours, and I'm somebody who likes XCOM2 and other TRPG games, so that's saying something. This game is easily 5 times more tactical than XCOM2.With that being said: If you love TRPGs then this will be the game for you. It has very smooth gameplay and it looks very nice. I'm particularly impressed with the fact that it only uses 50% of my 1070GTX, despite looking very nice. Each different character in your squad has various different strengths and weaknesses. Some of the characters can't even climb ladders, or swim, which I found very strange, but although it's not very realistic, I can totally understand that by them doing that, they make the game much more difficult and tactical, since you can't just use a single character to do an entire mission because of it.Overall, it's a very good TRPG. The two BIGGEST issues I have with the game by far is the fact that you cannot have dual-bindings for keys.. this fact irritated me constantly and often caused me to press the incorrect key as a result. If only they allowed you to have dual-bindings for a single action, then this game would have been amazing. The other issue is the fact that there's  character progression or character customization, meaning, your characters can't equip weapons, skills or abilities... they don't gain experience and they don't 'get stronger' in any way (like they do in XCOM2 for instance). These two issues takes this game from being a 10/10 to only being an 8/10. Still pretty good and well worth the money, but it could have been so much betterFor more reviews, visit my curator page: For my full recommended list of games:

_childDocuments_.review: In the wild west, there are only two things you can rely on, your gun and your friends. In Desperados III the only two things you can rely on are F5 and F8. The reason this game is hard is not because of the amount of skill you may need, but the number of times you would need to reload and try a new tactic.In this classic western themed game you play a bounty hunter on a vengeance quest. You meet a classic group of characters, who aid you in this endeavour. If you're a fan of cowboys, and tactical games then this definitely needs to be on your playlist,
_childDocuments_.name: Desperados III

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, the mechanics are amazing. I love it. Before even perform any action on the map you gotta think - who sees me, whats my time-window, what can i do to get from A to B... and you have so many ways with all your unique characters. Will you just throw a coin for decoy? Will you stun him and quickly dispose him? You decide.The story, of course, is that of a classical revenge arc - not the most innovative - but it nicely implements all the different characters on your way and the game really gives you a nice tutorial on what their skills are on the way. i can recommend it!
_childDocuments_.name: Desperados III

_childDocuments_.review: I decided to buy this game after playing Mimimi's newest, Shadow Gambit, as I liked the mechanics of sneaking and using different character's skills to get the job done while having the option of "showdown mode" which lets you line up a sequence if you have to take out more than one enemy at a time. The top down asymmetric view works extremely well, I've played 100% on controller, it works fine on steam deck, its a western version of Shadow Gambit (and I'm told their first game like this, too, name I can't remember right now) and if anything its a little harder than Shadow Gambit - the enemies seem more keen to see you, the guard dogs can sniff you out, so be careful and plan or indeed just try out different ideas to get to the next stage - the instant save/reload mechanic works well here although if you've picked this up after Shadow Gambit be warned there are not as many active save slots (3x total in Desperados III)Its the kind of game you'll be thinking about when not playing - an idea will come to you about how to get past some enemies and you'll be keen to try it out as soon as you can.Overall a good game, not overly repetitive, the character voices are not too annoying (I found some in Shadow Gambit a bit grating) and for me a pretty much perfect sneak-em-up with just the right balance of sneak vs. kill. Its a shame Mimimi studio are closing as I loved both Shadow Gambit and Desperados III so would have bought whatever they came up with next in the same sneak-em-up genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Desperados III

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a pretty reasonable implementation of a 3rd person isometric squad stealth game. It's just that it is too tedious. If you just play the game, it's pretty easy and not that interesting. if you do the extra badge challenges, then it's not exactly hard, it's just incredibly tedious, e.g. things like a 20+ minute mission with many points where someone might spot you and then the badge says "don't save for the duration of the mission". The game is balanced around constant saving, the tutorial even teaches you this and the timed speed-run challenges include the time for failed attempts where you loaded a prior save to undo whatever happened. I just didn't have enough fun with this game to recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Desperados 3 is a great game! You should buy this if you like tactical stealth games like Commandos and Shadow Tactics. 8/10There are 16 main missions and some of them took me 3 hours to complete and this is okay for me. _childDocuments_.review: As someone who spent countless hours on the Commando series in my youth, it’s a true joy to rediscover a game of this kind, especially one that is such a masterclass in execution! The maps are vast and intricately detailed, with scenarios and dialogues meticulously crafted to fully immerse you—an amazing job all around! However, to fully appreciate this game, you need to enjoy a slow-paced experience where multiple tactics are required. It may not be for everyone, but if you loved Commando, dive in—this might be the best real-time tactics game you'll ever play (along with Shadow Tactics from the same studio). It's truly unfortunate to hear the studio is closing, given the incredible quality of their games and how rare this genre has become...
_childDocuments_.name: Desperados III

_childDocuments_.review: I had high expectations for the game since Shadow Tactics was such a masterpiece. Truth to be told, I am a bit disappointed. My disappointment comes from a weak story and a bit of boring gameplay in the first chapter. At the start of the second, you'll get your fifth character, Isabelle, which is essential, overpowered, and simply fun to play with. On the other hand, there are things which went great. The level design is amazing! In sixteen maps, you don't have a feeling of repetition. Voice acting and soundtrack are both excellent. Overall it's a good game, but I have trouble seeing it as better than Shadow Tactics. And I like the western theme way more than the Japanese theme. (15.08.2021)So I returned to do all the additional content, Baron challenges, and the DLC. I have to say I had more fun playing those. Baron challenges are surprisingly unique and indeed bring a challenge to the table. I have a slight issue with how much freedom and possibilities you have in the main story, and Baron challenges fix exactly that. The mission with train and shooting only was the most memorable. Badges try to solve the same issue, but the execution is horrible. There are two types of badges without any distinction, and the list is hidden in the first playthrough. Plus, I really don't like the speedrun one. While it is justifiable, it's still a tactical game. Anyway, the DLC brings back freedom, but I liked the story. I just wish there would be more character development, interaction, and, hell, even cinematics. I simply want more story, because the characters are fantastic! Overall I have now more positive experience with the game, and I can say it's on par with Shadow Tactics.
_childDocuments_.name: Desperados III

_childDocuments_.review: Nice game with beautiful visuals. Graphics, environments and visual is nice and theme is set to wild west, known mostly from movies and books. There is a nice balance between different map environments. Music is relaxing and sounds are good. Game play is really tactical and strategy based. Everything is about right positioning and timing. True challenge is playing without any alarm. Playing without killing anyone is nearly impossible. Different characters have different skills and everything feels well balanced. If you are into real time, stealth strategies, this is the right game. Just stay in the bushes, hidden in shadows, use your skills and enjoy the stealth.

_childDocuments_.review: A great tactical stealth game - difficulty is pretty savage on hard mode but very satisfying when you finally pull it off.My main complaint is that many of the enemy layouts feel like there is an optimal way to proceed, with most other methods resulting in an alert.Game length is probably 25-40hrs on Hard mode - with plenty of optional challenges for further playtime and replayability.

_childDocuments_.review: You just have to command them on an excellent game.Story is engaging (you really wanna know how it continues/ends)Characters are lovely (I found them all interesting in their own way)Game Mechanics are wonderful (You can execute what you have in your mind, at no point, was I fighting the input)Approaching the game is diverse (there are so many ways to solve each level, just wonderful)Presentation is sublime (Grafics/Sound/Voice acting it all fits together for a wonderful experience)Billing Model is straight forward and honest (I very much dislike lootboxes and the likes)I can wholeheartedly recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Desperados III

_childDocuments_.review: Mimimi have taken everything that was wonderful with Shadow Tactics: Blades of The Shogun, and made it better. I enjoy every single reload, as I learn another enemy pattern and a better strategy. Characters are great, story ain't anything groundbreaking but works perfectly for what the game is, and the character interactions are awesome! I am looking forward to more games in this genre made by Mimimi!There are similarities in characters between this and Shadow Tactics, but they're shuffled around enough that it feels fresh. One of the characters (Isabelle) is particularly new, bringing some mechanics that weren't in Shadow Tactics at all.While I like the setting of Shadow Tactics more as I like Sengoku and Edo Japan, I must say this is the better game. The devs really improved upon every single aspect, but both are highly worth playing, and amazing in their own right.There's enough variety here to keep you going for a long time, if you're into achievements/badges/challenges too. They've also got the setting really well. It's a thrilling cowboy revenge story, with compelling and believable characters, just like Shadow Tactics was in its own right.The music is damn nice, and really sets that wild west atmosphere. All in all, very great stuff.
_childDocuments_.name: Desperados III

_childDocuments_.review: This is the first review I've written for any game and that's because this game is amazing. If you played Shadow Tactics you may think this is just a reskin but there's a lot more to it than that. It is similar in that it's a RTT game made by Mimimi, but I think the 4 years in between Shadow Tactics and this shows in this game. The graphics are significantly better, the UI is a bit updated with the replay at the end of each mission being a nice touch, and even the characters' portraits look really nice; Isabelle's being my favorite.I think the gameplay is a bit more varied than Shadow Tactics too since this is a western as opposed to a stealth samurai game. There are still heavy stealth mechanics but you can choose to shoot your way through a lot of situations. I had a lot of fun with Hector's shotgun and Cooper's dual pistols, and Isabelle's voodoo mechanics are awesome. There's a lot of replay value too if you want to challenge yourself and go after all the badges and/or beat the levels on Desperado difficulty.To me, this is one of the most enjoyable gaming experiences I've had in a longtime and it reminds me of classic computer games.  If you enjoyed Shadow Tactics I think this is a step further than that, and if you enjoy strategy games that require some thought you will definitely enjoy this. I hope Mimimi keeps making these amazing games.
_childDocuments_.name: Desperados III

_childDocuments_.review: I managed to complete the game in Desperados difficulty first play through. I was blown away by the good level design. it always kept me at the edge of the seat as their are always unexpected challenges. Many parts of the game was so hard I had to pull out my hair. But it was so satisfying when I managed to get through the level. The story was a bit meh, nothing too special. i did not watch the cut theme but did not feel I missed out muchOverall a fantastic game, def the best game I have played for a long while.
_childDocuments_.name: Desperados III

_childDocuments_.review: I have played 60 hours so far of Desperados III.  I have only finished 1/5 of the game, and I love every minute of it.  It is a stealth puzzle game, like Hitman, but instead of a third person view, you run a crew of little people in a Western trope setting using a top-down isometric view.This is a game made by a little company Mimimi Productions, who intimately know what fans of the genre are looking for.  You can tell that a a lot of love and passion went into designing of this game.  Their game is inspired by the old Desperados series and iconic games like Commandos II of the early 2000s.It is an great improvement of the old Desperados / Commandos games, and even more expansive and polished with improved mechanics compared to their excellent, previous title, Shadow Tactics.The different mission layouts are very thoughtfully designed, and the developers have provided a wonderful sandbox of approaches to tackle each mission.  The badge system is designed to force you to replay the missions in a completely different manner, exploiting different characters, tools and approaches to each mission.  It is a game requiring patience and sometimes you are lead down a path to exploit the advantages afforded in particular pixels on a large map, and a real-time coordination of actions between multiple characters, aided by the showdown mode.I hope that Mimimi productions continues making similar games, and I hope that this game sells well.

_childDocuments_.review: Desperados III, from the creators of Shadow Tactics: Blades of the Shogun and Aiko's Choice, stands as a testament to refined tactical gameplay and engaging storytelling. With improved pacing, intuitive mechanics, and a plethora of diverse levels, it surpasses its predecessors in every aspect.-  Desperados III boasts much-improved pacing compared to its predecessors. The inclusion of a shadow mode that pauses the game, a suggestion from the community, enhances tactical decision-making.-  The story in Desperados III is not just coherent but also deeply engaging, drawing players into its Wild West tale of revenge and redemption.-  Dividing levels into sub-levels with cinematics in between adds depth and excitement to the gameplay. Gone are the days of grinding through lengthy, monotonous levels; instead, players are treated to short stories, small locations, and limited goals that keep the experience fresh and dynamic.-  With numerous levels in the main game, additional DLC levels, and a plethora of "extra" levels offering special tasks and alternative completion methods, Desperados III offers a wealth of content for players to enjoy, ensuring a long and fulfilling gameplay experience.Desperados III excels in delivering a refined tactical experience, blending intuitive mechanics with strategic depth. From its enhanced pacing to its diverse level design, every aspect of the gameplay contributes to a truly immersive Western adventure.The abundance of levels and additional content ensures that players will have plenty to sink their teeth into, offering countless hours of tactical enjoyment and exploration.Desperados III is a masterful blend of tactical prowess and narrative excellence, surpassing its predecessors in every regard. With improved pacing, engaging storytelling, and a wealth of content to explore, it stands as a testament to the evolution of the tactical genre.

Shadow Tactics looked amazing, but the devs from Mimimi (sorry for killing so many of you buddies) made their new product look absolutely breathtaking despite its lack of AAA, high budget and ray tracing - needless stuff that is in fashion these days. The story may not be mindblowing, but it is really well-built, every character has a voice and personality, you can't help but fall in love with them. _childDocuments_.review: Unknown to the vast majority of the world, "Desperados III" is not just a tactical stealth game set in the Wild West. It's actually a coded message, revealing one of the biggest secrets of our modern age. The developers, in collaboration with an ancient secret society, used the game to pass on a hidden message to the chosen ones about the world's water supply.In the game, players might recall the numerous instances where water bodies and sources play an integral role in either helping or obstructing the characters. These aren't just gameplay elements. They're allegories.The secret society, known as the Aquafarians, believes that in the underground caverns of the Wild West, there exists a source of 'Elixir Aqua' - water so pure that it can grant extended life and unparalleled intellect. This isn't just any water; it's the primordial essence of life on Earth.Why connect this with "Desperados III"? The Aquafarians' symbol, a droplet within a hexagon, is discreetly placed throughout the game. The game serves as a map and a series of clues for those deemed worthy to find this source.But here's the kicker: modern-day drinking water companies have been on this trail for decades. They are attempting to monopolize the Elixir, diluting tiny amounts into their 'premium' water brands to keep the world hooked, coming back for more, and paying top dollar, without revealing the source's true power.Only by mastering "Desperados III," understanding its intricate web of coded messages, and following the trail you will also find the truthDon't forget to drink water

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful game from Mimimi, and a terrific follow-up to their break-out success, Shadow Tactics. Largely the same formula gameplay-wise but set in the West, this game tells the story of one's man's quest for redemption, seemingly at all costs. Gameplay consists of controlling multiple protagonists in real-time with a myriad of skills (each has their pros and cons) that can be enacted in real-time or queued up for simultaneous stealth/carnage. Varied maps and objectives, plus the forced use of a combination of 2-5 of the characters on each map means there is a varied challenge with limited scope for overusing a particular character/play-style. That said, Cooper and Isabelle are going to do most of the killing/incapacitating. Badges and "Baron" challenges keep replayability high.Thankfully there are also a number of quality of life improvements, like group movement, that enhance the formula. However, there aren't a significant number of new gameplay mechanics. If you're looking for the developers to push this genre in a new direction, then this won't do it for you. If you wanted more of Shadow Tactics, then you're in for a treat.Arguably plays better with a controller than keyboard but YMMV!

_childDocuments_.review: Desperados 3, prequel to the rest of the franchise and a mighty fine one at that.  Any concerns that Mimimi might've missed the mark bringing the unique Wild West spin of the original Desperados title back to life in a Real-Time Tactics game, or tried to make it more in line with their previous works were thoroughly dispelled within minutes of entering the game proper.To make a long story short, if you're the type of person who can devote entire hours to analytical study and stealthy trial and error gameplay, then you will feel right at home.If you're the type to get impatient with real-time puzzle strategy games, well, it's probably not the game for you.Moving on, there's no denying the attention to detail the developers have provided to the game, especially for a known IP with an existing fanbase at that.  If anything this game serves as a proper successor to the legacy of the old development team.  This isn't just Shadow Tactics or Commandos in the Wild West; this is its own piece of beauty, it belongs in the setting, from the audio and visuals, to the characters and tools at their disposal, it's all fittingly part of the setting for the most part at the very least.Gameplay wise, it is very much a fluid improvement over previous entries, perhaps even better than Mimimi's previous work with Shadow Tactics even.  Every character pulls their weight, every level can very well keep you invested for hours studying, preparing, and gambling the pros and cons of every action.  Even going loud isn't off the cards either, with helpful hints from the interface helping you plan your every move, it's not really a question if you'll solve whatever level you're on, but when.Every level feels delightfully hand-crafted too, with puzzles that keep you at em with lots of replay value if you're into the challenge this game provides.  The options for creativity are incredibly flexible too, so experimenting is highly encouraged.Relatedly, I feel non-lethal approaches have been vastly improved in this compared to ST: Blades of the Shogun.  The simple ability to tie enemies and unhelpful neutrals up? So much cleaner. ^^Having said all these positive things, I must point out that there are issues with the interface when it comes to movement, with it sometimes being obsessive with jumping down Z levels rather than using the stairs, and other such unusual behavior.  Furthermore using the in-built tactical mode can be hit & miss, especially since far as I know, there's no way to tell characters to rush to their assigned melee targets, which can make things awkward if they notice their buddies getting punched.  Overall the design is sleek, but improvements still could be made.So in summary, I highly recommend this game, especially to fans of the older parts of the franchise, they did it justice, it cannot be said enough.

_childDocuments_.review: After an excellent Shadow Tactics that probably resurrected the commando genre, we now have a sequel to the Desperados franchise. Character were more interesting, environments had more variety, and the few new abilities in Desperados 3 are so overpowered that I spent the game avoiding to use them. Also, I would say Desperados got slightly less challenging, while still being a good challenge obviously.Anyway, one can only enjoy more content of such a quality.

_childDocuments_.review: This is very well put together game. Often, strategy games focus much more on the strategy and gameplay than on the story and the characters, but the characters in this are VERY good, with some of the best voice acting I've heard in a game for a long time. McCoy and Hector are absolutely excellent in that regard.It's also a game that can be mentally taxing - trying to figure out how to achieve an objective is often difficult, let alone trying to achieve it while getting badges as well...but not so much that you get frustrated. Thankfully the quick load is very quick, and 'save-scumming' is actually an integral part of the game - but it doesn't feel like cheating.A minor gripe is that coming from the Jagged Aliiance series of games, I was hoping for a more detailed/elaborate timeline-style mode than what Showdown Mode currently delivers, but the dev's reasoning for not going down that route does make sense. You can get through the whole game without needing that detailed level of planning, although I do miss some of that 'YES, THIS WHOLE THING WORKED!' feeling that the JA games give you. Desperados III is much more of a real-time experience, versus JA's more 'plan it all and hope for the best' approach.Special mention goes to the music too, it's perfect for the game and setting. In fact the attention to detail in this game on every level is absolutely perfect, it's one of the most polished games I've ever played.As for bugs...there has been the odd time when a character hasn't quite done what I asked them to (it's possible some of this may have been user error), but nothing that really pissed me off. No CTDs or other major bugs. Certainly nothing that a quickload couldn't fix.The tutorial could probably spell things out a little better, and there are a few features that don't seem to be documented anywhere, but google quickly sorted me out.Overall a recommended game for anyone who likes strategy/tactics/stealth games and/or wild west themed stuff.I'll be checking out Shadow Tactics after I've completed D3.10/10 would play a map with hungover characters waking up in stupid places again.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr - An excellent modern take on what made the original game legendary! Highly recommended!I'm a huge fan of Desperados: Wanted Dead or Alive and as such am extremely happy it finally got a worthy successor after the two miserable attempts Cooper's Revenge and Helldorado.Mimimi Games proved themselves with Shadow Tactics: Blades of the Shogun, which I can't recommend enough for fans of the genre and when I heard they were assigned to do Desperados III I was overjoyed, because I had great faith in their talents. I tried the demo as soon as it was released and, upon finishing it, immediately pre-ordered the game.The campaign consists of 16 missions (including a tutorial), which are very well designed. The story, however, is a little flat and parts of it seem to only exist to justify a certain kind of gameplay. It's not bad by any means though! It's a very entertaining western romp for sure!In addition to the classic characters of John Cooper, Doc McCoy and Kate O'Hara you get to play as Hector Mendoza and Isabelle Moreau. Hector is the equivalent to the original game's Sanchez, an immensely useful strongman whereas Isabelle has elements of Mia Yung to her, but overall plays quite differently.The game is all in all very well balanced and you will only occasionally get a feeling of strong superiority to the enemies, usually because of Cooper's knife, Kate's luring ability or Isabelle's voodoo shenanigans. There are 4 difficulty settings, by the way, and you can even tweak them to your liking regarding the amount and kind of enemies, amount of ammunition, enemy reaction speed and even the number of save games you can use!Other than the main story you can also play challenge missions, which take place on existing maps of the campaign and are really fun as well. They add even more replay value to a game that is already incredibly replayable due to achievements, other challenges during the story, easter eggs and the overall map design.My initial playthrough took me 24 hours, but I have played it way, way beyond that since! I think that speaks for itself.

This variation gives you a multitude of ways to complete each mission.You can use 'Shadow mode' to pause, then plan a sequence of actions for all of your characters before executing the plan (and executing all the enemies at the same time) - super satisfying!).There is lots of replayability; you could do a no-kill run or try to speedrun it. Still, I think the game is at its best when you fully utilise all the fun tools and abilities on offer - at least for the first play-through.Recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: was very good, but  is fantastic. Just about every part of this style of gameplay has been perfected with this instalment- excellent level designs, fluid animations, powerful and unique movesets for every character, and a massive amount of very welcome QoL mechanics. The game also has a massive amount of meat on it's bones for the price on offer. My amount of hours played at the time of this review betrays just how much playtime you can actually get out of this experience. While the main story will run you about 20 hours, there's the Baron's Challenges (optional "What If?" missions that either remix the levels from the main story or change up your objective in a suitably unique fashion), Bounty Mode (which lets you replay every level in the entire game with every character), three excellent DLC missions that are all worth your time and money, and even a "level editor light" of sorts to mess around with (not a true level editor, but rather dev tools and the ability to share your save file online, which can allow you to make your own custom levels). All of this could easily triple time spent with the game, and this isn't even counting the  intense stuff like hard mode challenges, or getting every badge on every level. Seriously, this is a game stuffed with excellent, engaging, and creative content.The only real issues the game has are balancing ones: every character has some ability that is blatantly overpowered, like Isabelle's Connect, McCoy's sniper pistol, and Coopers dual pistols and knife combo. While this opens up a lot of creativity with how you approach certain situations, it can also mean that you fall back on specific strategies to solve every problem you come across rather than branch out into more creative solutions. Once you've gotten the taste of Hector being able to knock out his allies and toss them up to places they shouldn't be able to reach, or Kate dragging enemies away from their friends, it's hard to go back. Perhaps that's the reward for experimentation though, the ability to gain a dominant strategy that's effective to use? There's also the story, which while not being terrible in any stretch is a fairly cut-and-dry revenge story. It's mostly saved by the main character's fun personalities, the good banter between them and their great voice acting (and the incredible audio mixing during cutscenes), but it's nothing too groundbreaking. It does motivate you to keep playing and is presented fairly well, so it serves it's purpose. And if this criticism has taught your anything, it's this- even in areas where it needs to improve,  still does incredibly well. Either way,  is a phenomenal game that shows the stealth genre still has some life left in it. If you're a fan of stealth, a fan of the  I.P, or just wanting to try something new and unique, this is absolutely the game for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Mimimi have done it again.With the final release of the 3rd DLC on this cursed day, Mimimi's Desperados III finally gets my approval as GOTY 2020. You can grab all 3 DLC from today until 6 Nov. at the same discounted price as the pre-order people.Desperados III is a clear improvement over Mimimi's previous Shadow Tactics: Blades of the Shogun while still remaining familiar. Brown nosing out of the way here is the real review.Desperados III is a prequel to the previous 3 games in the series (so really should be Desperados IV), but back to the classic isometric view in the RTT genre, where we discover more about Cooper and his gang prior to the events of Wanted Dead or Alive. The Unity engine poses its issues but we have the game being able to run at a locked 144fps with close to non existent hitches. 99.9% of the time you won't have trouble when carrying bodies / crashes / jumping off a ledge into an execution / characters patrol routes messing up. The environments are rich in colour and variety but just don't look too far off the edge off the map to see the low res rocks :P.The game time wise takes a similar amount as ST, between 25-35 hours depending on player skill. Other than the purchasable DLC, akin to the bonus missions in Commandos 2, there are FREE "remixed" levels too after beating the main game, changing the layout and playable characters of familiar levels, increasing playtime and replayability.My personal pros for this new title are responsiveness and well done animations (other than for the DLC, no body capture animations were used there for CUTSCENES only), allowing both beginners and veterans to have a great time thanks to fluid gameplay. Other pros are the banter (improved from Shadow Tactics by a country mile, both in writing and voice acting), the soundtrack and the improved "Showdown" mode. In ST the Showdown mode felt a bit clunky and didn't pause the game, in D III, other than on the highest difficulty, you can pause and the UI is intuitive. One feature that I think all patrol-based stealth games should have are D III's fast forward mode which does what it says, and works in tandem with the showdown pause allowing for precise executions. Also more "in-doors" gameplay is appreciated, other than that it's a good modern RTT with many gameplay and decision choices. God bless bringing back the ability to tie people up and shove them all in bushes and the like.Now it's time for the D E B U N K section, especially for reviewers like Ranton. D III is not simply "Ninjas in the wild west" or "Cowboy Ninjas". While it's true again that only when carrying bodies and only on specific surfaces do your characters make noise, running past someone requires pristine micro executions and even though previous kits are utilised, the gameplay remains unique. Pretty hard to make innovative abilities since stealth is not new (Hayato and Cooper, Yuki and Hector, Katie and Aiko). There is however a very unique character, Isabelle. Isabelle was seen as divisive among RTT fans as "too overpowered" and "Voodoo not belonging as it's not a fantasy game" but her kit remains balanced and fitting for the game's Southern theme, especially in the swamps of Louisiana. Not like previous existing stealth games did not have something absurd going for them. As it stands Mimimi is the modern standard for RTT games and their new upcoming game should be great... in 3 to 4 years' time. For RTT recommendations see the end of my Partisans 1941 review.

_childDocuments_.review: This review goes full western cliché.- Storytelling, atmosphere, animation, presentation, liveliness. Sterling all.- Good interface, improved from Shadow Tactics (which I thumbed down,) notably the gamepad controls, not perfect yet but adequate with some practice.- Amusing gimmicks, abilities and tactical options, either shared by some (climbing, swimming) or unique (traps, weapons, even magic,) including the reactions, comments, animations and frequent laughs that go along with them.- Excellent cast of characters (and of voice actors,) with clear personalities and attributes.There is someone for every player to like, to favour. Some might do the same job quicker than others, but none is either weak or indispensable.- Excellent level design.Not only are the maps gorgeous, they vary vastly in visuals and vibes, accentuated by local features and mechanics.The line-up of enemies is cleverly optimised and never feels small. Individual narrative roles help with that, as much as they build the environmental storytelling.- 1st-class save system.Manual saves, auto-saves, and cycling quick saves.Furthermore, all states are restored, be it point of view, paused mode, combat statuses, etc.- Sticky feet.My main cause of death, possibly.There's nothing like a timed sprint on a narrow strip in a narrow time window being stopped clean by an impassable pebble on the ground or a bulge in a wall.This is the one imperfection of level design. It ignores visibility constraints. A rush requires full view of the surroundings, hence a zoom out, but at such distance tiny obstacles are invisible.- You can have a good camera, and a good camera control with the gamepad, only not at the same time.When you toggle Follow Mode in the options, the input is also changed, against your will, and it shouldn't.- The contextual action prompts are clunky.They change in the millisecond before your button press. Hence an awful lot of jumping in front of enemies instead of opening doors, for example.When several actions are possible, the UI should open a radial menu on click, instead of relying on other buttons and labels that fluctuate between pixels.- There is an issue with the synchronisation mode.It works just fine for group orders.Individually, however, new orders for 1 character will interrupt the flow of a previously automated companion, who will then stop and stay in the open.Took me a while to figure it out, the hard way, and learn to avoid the practice.- Badges, namely the fact that they are only revealed after map completion.Players should always be pampered before replayers; there are many more of the former.The quirk partly achieved its goal; I did uncharacteristically replay a couple of maps to take on certain challenges. If I ever replay this title, however, it will be because it's a fun game, not for participation trophies asking me to forfeit fav mechanics.As a side note, it's odd that each map offers a speedrun challenge, antithetical to the genre, but no ghost challenge, fitting and expected.- As far as I can tell, the only use of RNG is to determine in which direction an alert NPC will move or look next.- If only we could zoom a little closer...In summary, this is the best entry in the Mimimi Games catalogue. So far.

_childDocuments_.review: There aren’t any rootin’ tootin’ cowboys here. Follow Cooper and his gang of misfits as they beat the odds in a heart wrenching story that take place in lovingly crafted levels.  The player is able to control up to five characters based on the specific encounter. Each character has a unique speed, carrying type, and special abilities. These abilities are introduced gradually so as not to overwhelm the player and it was fun to have every ability from every character, but the limitations created by only having certain characters required new strategies to be developed. A lot of the special abilities combo quite well, and the game is happy to allow the player to combine them however they see fit. One such example that I found quite interesting was the ability to connect enemies that makes them share state. This means that if one dies, the other does as well. There were two guards that I wanted to take out that were connected. I mind controlled one, which is unrealistic but has many uses that stretch the player’s imagination, and was unsure at first how to make him kill someone but have him perish in the process. It then occurred to me that my target was linked with the one that was mind controlled, so I had my puppet shoot its compatriot causing them both to die while looking like some insane suicide that didn’t create suspicion. This sense of freedom is what helps the game feel so fresh as a lot can be done with the tools given.Stealth is a big focus in this game as the player’s small group of vigilantes is quite outnumbered when compared to the forces that they are up against. To stay in stealth, each enemy has a view cone which can be viewed at any time. Viewcones have two areas, one is solid and the other is striped. The solid one means that any character within that space will be spotted quickly. The striped area allows for allies to stay crouched to avoid detection. Many times, these viewcones will overlap which requires the player to take enemies out of their defensive formation one-by-one. The tools given to enhance viewing areas to stealth are quite fair. A viewcone can be viewed, but only one enemy at a time. To get more info, a marker can be placed that will tell when an enemy is looking at a specific place but this doesn’t show exact viewcones so a player wouldn’t know what it looks like with without research beforehand. Breaking stealth causes a player’s trouble to triple in most cases, which is why it is important to use the quicksave quickload system that is recommended ingame by the developers themselves. It allows for experimentation without punishment which makes the game quite a bit more enjoyable. If stealth is broken then enemies will start pouring out of the closest guard post. There is a limited amount that won’t respawn, but the same can be said about the player’s ammo. Not only this, but every guard in the area will try to gun the player down.There aren’t a lot of enemy types, but they do their jobs well enough and more enemies would simply cause confusion in such a hectic game. Simple guards will be tricked by everything, but they can be killed instantly. Poncho wearing guards can’t be tricked by distractions and won’t let their nearby simple guards to get tricked easily either. Thankfully they die just as easily as their weaker counterparts. Finally, there is the long coats. These trench coat wearing mounds of muscle don’t get tricked at all and can be killed under special conditions only. There aren’t a lot of them, but they create quite the challenge to get around, thankfully the environment allows for some great opportunities for death and destruction.The environments in the game use their own art styles and layouts without any reuse of assets. This provides a handcrafted level that has love injected into every inch of it. Traps can be triggered to help get rid of pesky groups of enemies with enough planning. Environments are also quite vertical which allows for side paths which open up only more opportunities to the player.Side content comes in the form of some challenges which are difficult, but there aren’t a ton of them. The main side content that is offered is the challenges called “Badges” which are revealed after a first play of a level.The story is a hero’s journey full of twists and turns that I didn’t see coming. It is one that kept me riveted. The story is woven well into the gameplay as some of the exposition is provided by the characters as they enter a new area that they are commenting on. It makes the world and characters feel full of life. The game also flows seamlessly into the first Desperados game as this one is a prequel.The sound is top-notch with shots having powerful sounds to match their lethality. What surprised me the most about the sound design was the voice acting. I expected it to be cartoony and corny, but the voice performances found in this game are serious and heartfelt.The graphics are gorgeous. The three-dimensional models are intricately detailed and give great visual feedback. Every enemy has a piece of red clothing, with a red band around the hat being the most common. Every player character has a unique color scheme which helps identify them when the action gets crazy. The cutscenes are long sequences of animation that one can tell was mocapped due to the realism present that is usually unable to be achieved otherwise.The controls work well and there are quite a few customizable shortcuts that make the game quite a bit better. It can get a little difficult to click on specific objects in the game world due to the perspective being shown at the time, but it is simple to rotate the world : The game runs exceptionally well which surprised me based upon how many objects are on the screen at one time.One playthrough of the campaign on normal equates to about 30 hours which only an okay amount of value. If the player plays levels multiple times to get more badges, replays the game on hard, and finishes all of the challenges, then the playtime is likely at least twice that. There are so many different ways to solve all of the encounters so if a player enjoys this game quite a bit, there is a lot of replay value inside.👍  👍Great storyAmazing gameplay choiceIntricate detail in graphics.👎  👎Annoying hitboxes

_childDocuments_.review: Desperados III has so far been surprisingly good and exceeding my expectations. As a kid I played through the original game from 2001 many times. Here, the developers somehow managed to completely revive an almost 20-year old franchise with great graphics and sound, beautiful and challenging level design, while at the same time capture the look, atmosphere, gameplay and overall feel of the original game. It's also got the same cheesy American cowboy dialogue as before, which for me adds to the nostalgia. The user-interface and menus are intuitive and well designed.The story is built on the original characters. I believe this is a prequel, as characters you'd expect were familiar with one another are faced with their first introductions to each other. This means new players don't need to know anything about this franchise beforehand, anyone can jump right in. Besides, these games are not very story-centric, but more focused on the strategy gameplay - which they do remarkably well!I highly recommend this game for any real-time strategy fans.Mimimi Games has made a product with a quality level that fully defends it's price.

_childDocuments_.review: A masterfully executed tactical RTS infiltration game in the likes of the Commando series, and a worthy sequel to the Desperados franchise. The story is good, but what takes you into the game is the mechanics, the great amount of content and the amazing puzzle-like design of the levels. The maps are huge but very detailed and well designed, from a graphical and a game-design viewpoint, the characters each play very differently (although if you played some games of the genre you might recognise some common abilities).I highly recommend this if you're looking for a good single player challenge, however if you're just looking to relax this game might be a bit hard or frustrating at times. These will probably get patched soon but I encountered some bugs, including one time a character teleporting from inside a building to a waypoint every time I pressed Enter from showdown mode, a few other pathfinding bugs but the game is pretty stable in general.If you're wondering if this game is for you, try the demo. _childDocuments_.review: As someone who has always claimed that Desperados: Wanted Dead or Alive is in my top-3 all-time favorite games, I'm super happy that Desperados is being seen by so many people and it's getting this much love. Not only I loved Desperados but I always thought the original game was the most underrated game I've ever seen (the original one, not Desperados 2. That was the worst).I loved the gameplay, the mechanics, and the level design. It was perfection. I enjoyed every second of the game and I don't think I've ever seen such a well-designed game in the genre. I can't express enough how much I loved their showdown mode and how satisfying it was to pull off a successful one. Oh, and the game summary at the end of each level was lovely.But, there were 2 things I didn't like about the game as a Desperados fan:1. I wish they recreated the amazing cutscenes the original Desperados had. Those were one of my favorite parts of the original Desperados as a kid and since I heard the news that Mimimi is developing Desperados 3, I was hoping they do the cutscenes again.(They did a similar one for their announcement trailer a few years ago). I mean the isometric cutscenes were cool too, but it was far from those magical cutscenes from the original game.2. The story wasn't good at all. I know that the original Desperados didn't have a superb story either, but at least it had some interesting twists and the theme of each mission was much more interesting than this new version.Overall, Mimimi Games did a great job with this game and I can't recommend this game enough if you're a fan of the genre.Bonus point: Their soundtrack is 10/10.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this genre of games. I've gone out of my way to find games of this type and have played every one of them multiple times over - even the weird obscure ones like that Sherwood one.I loved Shadow Tactics, but after viewing the release trailer for this, I was very worried that this was just going to be another Shadow Tactics game with a reskin, just using the Desperados IP with a name-only cash grab. This thankfully wasn't the case - the writing is great, the banter between the characters is natural and pretty funny, and you can tell that whoever was responsible for it knew the original games well. The story, while a fairly generic revenge arc, was fairly engaging, and the levels are large, complex and challenging. I was also pleasantly surprised to see that while they've definitely kept a lot of the Shadow Tactics engine in place, there have been a bunch of improvements to it as well.The only thing that I didn't like was how many of the original Desperados characters were replaced. Don't get me wrong, I get it - all the mysteriously missing characters were basically racist stereotypes lol, from the dumb tequila-drunk Mexican to the Native American who kept talking about 'collecting scalps for his wigwam'. But I suppose I have a lot of nostalgia around those games, so to have half of the familiar characters removed left it feeling like there was a piece missing? I don't know. I did like the new characters though, so it worked out.Anyway buy the game.

_childDocuments_.review: For any fan of Commandos type of games this is a must-have. Desperados 3 is a worthy successor of the original Desperados:  Wanted Dead or Alive. Its probably at the pinnacle of its genre. Desperados 3 is a massive improvement from Shadow Tactics, a game that introduced Mimimi devs to the broader audience.Its a prequel to first game of the series, focused on John Cooper forming group of bounty hunters and fighting few demons from his past. Its a solid story with few interesting twists, but I found the characters to be the best part of it. Before and after each mission there are cutscenes that introduce you more to the characters and help to understand their motivations. Each member of the group has different personality and game is good at combining them all. For example we have jovial, a bit bruttish, but symphatetic Hector confronted with secluded, reserved and arrogant McCoy.Gameplay is probably the biggest strength of Desperados 3. Each character has unique set of skills that allow you to accomplish mission objectives on many different ways. The game itself encourages you to take different approaches. Each mission has multiple badges for completing level in certain way, but you can't see those badges untill you finish the mission for the first time. Level design is another asset of D3. Most of levels might even seem intimidating because of how big they are or how many enemies are on the map, but usually game presents you few approaches so you don't need to eliminate every adversary to progress with your objectives.There are many difficulty setting which allows you to have fun no matter if this is your first experience with the game or you are a vet that played every game in the genre. You can even made your own custom settings where you can set number of enemies, supplies (munitions and equipment you find on the map), detection speed and your characters health. You can even limit your amount of saves or even turn off saving at all. Didn't I mention there are different types of enemies? Each of them forces you to take different approach and makes it harder to stick with only one viable strategy. For example Ponchos are guards who never abandon their post, no matter what so don't even try to lure them with Docs bag. You can try to turn their strength into their weakness. If there are multiple guards and you whistle with Hector you know that they will remain at their place and won't join their regular comrades to investigate the noise.Desperados 3 audio part of the game is excellent. Starting from voice acting which is top quality to music which somehow manages to combine old western themes and adds a bit of electrical flavor. It sure helps you get in the mood while playing game placed in Wild West.My only complaint might be that the game is not longer. Its still almost 30 hours of gameplay on hard difficulty, without even touching Barons bonus challenges or attempting to unlock most of the badges. With doing this I expect it to be twice as long and the game is great to come back after a while to finish it again.I can highly recommend it to every fan of the genre or any fan of the westerns. Game is also great for newcomers with its multiple and totally customizable difficulty level. I can't wait for new DLCs for it and for next game made by Mimimi devs.

_childDocuments_.review: Desperados III is quite the rollercoaster of a game. The difficulty level is no joke - it often feels like I'm trying to crack some complex puzzle with each mission. While this can be frustrating at times, it's also a big part of what makes the game so satisfying. Every successful strategy or clever maneuver feels like a hard-earned victory.What really keeps me going is the quicksave feature. Seriously, this is a game-changer. Being able to save my progress whenever I want lets me take risks and try out different approaches without worrying about losing a ton of progress. It's like having a safety net that encourages me to experiment and come up with innovative ways to tackle challenges.The Wild West setting is beautifully realised. The attention to detail in the environments, the characters, and even the sounds immerses me in this world. I find myself getting lost in the dusty towns and feeling like I'm part of a classic Western movie.I won't lie, though - there are times when the difficulty gets the best of me, and I need to step away before I throw my keyboard across the room. It's a game that demands patience and careful planning, which might not be everyone's cup of tea. But when I do manage to pull off a seemingly impossible mission, the sense of accomplishment is incredibly satisfying.All in all, Desperados III is a tough nut to crack, but it's also a lot of fun. The quicksave system is a game-saver for me, making the challenge more manageable and allowing me to explore different strategies. If you're into tactical games and don't mind a steep learning curve, this game might just rope you in with its Wild West charm and satisfying victories.
_childDocuments_.name: Desperados III

_childDocuments_.review: That's a great game! :)  I had played both Desperados I and Desperados II (which I probably like the least amongst all Desperados games so far) in the past. Although Desperados III was released, I didn't buy it for about 2 years. Perhaps I was partially sceptical whether the game would be good enough and similar to the orignial Desperados. Now, I have recently bought it and I endorse the good reviews the game has received! :) I enjoy it. The graphics are lovely. If you played Desperados I, you will probably like Desperados III as well. A little expensive (compared to some other games), but I think that in the end it's worth buying it. It has a good/decent  a) story, b) replayability, c) grapihcs,  d) level of tactics required  and so I have had fun playing the game. It's quite nice that they tried to "respect" the basic principles of the original game and to bring back the feeling of playing a Desperados game. Quite happy that they did Desperados III, perhaps one day they might make an equally good Desperados IV.

_childDocuments_.review: I love stealth games and this is one is an absolute bless! The music, the atmosphere, the graphics, the story, the very hard gameplay  (on desperado mode) . It can be very frustrating , but that I guess also has to do with the fact that I instantly started on Desperado mode.  Which means A LOT of trial and error.   On average a mission takes me between 2 and 4 hours to finish in the first play through.  Which makes finishing them truly feel like an accomplishment. There are so many ways to do the missions , that  the game has a high replayability value.  10/10!

_childDocuments_.review: Mimimi have done it again! Another brilliant title under the niche real-time tactics genre that appeared to be gone and forgotten only a few years ago. Mimimi had found the right formula for Shadow Tactics and have only improved upon that with Desperados III!This game has it all – interesting storyline, great level design, challenges that can be approached in a number of ways, memorable characters with diverse skills which allow for a myriad of combinations. Difficulty options make it accessible for newcomers to the genre. And while that’s not really my cup of tea, there’s a great potential for doing speedruns or trying to take on one of the challenges that get unlocked only after you complete a mission for the first time.One thing Desperados III really stands out for is that it came out as a fully completed and very well polished game. From day one, there were no non-negligible bugs/issues and having already completed it, it never felt like it would need to get DLC-ed before you can really enjoy it. While that used to be the standard some 15-20 years ago, all that is very rare nowadays so kudos to Mimimi for taking the time and effort to polish it that much before releasing it.Following the free content update released a few days ago, I’ve now invested 40+ hours in it. And that’s before the DLC’s that I’m eligible to receive having pre-ordered the game! While I’m certainly a completionist type of player, that’s definitely impressive for a single playthrough, i.e. no level re-runs, taking on challenges, etc.Overall, the game is very much worth the price. Can we have more of the same, please? It’s already perfect as is!
_childDocuments_.name: Desperados III

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game. Got it on sale for 25 dollars, was worth every penny and more. If you're only peripherally interested in this genre or stealth games in general, get it if you can find it on sale and you'll still likely be satisfied even if you never pick it up again. At 25 dollars its damn near a must-have,. If you love this genre or stealth games in general you shouldn't care about whether or not its on sale, just get it. You won't regret it. Pros:-Phenomenal gameplay, extremely satisfying to pull of group executes and trick gaurds. -Great characters and character chemistry/dialouge-Perfectly follows golden rule if bought on sale, Main story 25 hours -Probably 25 more at least for a completionist run.-Highly replayable, wanted to jump right back in after beating. Cons:-very basic, but serviceable story.-soundtrack is great but gets repetitive.-Edge of viewcones can sometimes weirdly ambiguous and hard to gauge.-Quicksave reminder is far too frequent for a first time playthrough, cleverly designed though.

It's really quite satisfying changing the course of a whole war or trying to free a friend in stealth ninja style from a bombastic Japanese fortress with overwhelming number of bad-ass samurai guards. Killing a bunch of random cowboys strolling around my dusty backyard, only because my friend fell asleep in the nearby fisher hut and I "want" to see what he has been up to lately - less satisfying. _childDocuments_.review: Mimimi Games has shown their niche expertise with the masterpiece that is Shadow Tactics, and this game cements it. While it is definitely a very polished and rewarding experience, it does borrow a lot from Shadow Tactics. By a lot, I mean A LOT. Most of the skills and enemies are the exact same from ST, just named different things to fit the Western style.Do not get this game if you do not like save-loading, as it is crucial in this and ST. It's an issue that I had with ST, and, sadly, it is the same in this game. This can make the game a drag when stuck in positions of RNG, such as when guards roam around while confused.Regardless, the game does stand up on its own, and you could easily play this without having played ST. I was just expecting more new content aside from the obvious (Isabelle, who is the most fun character in the "franchise"). _childDocuments_.review: Excellent in every way. Atmospheric, as well as rewarding gameplay. Some enemy positions feel impossible at first, but pulling of a well thought through maneuver feels just as good using that old RTS micro to your advantage and it never feels too hard or too easy thanks to the adjustable difficulty with different aspects. The AI also works pretty decently, and though you sometime feel as if the NPC walked into way to obvious a trap or went way too far to look for their friend you have often forgotten (due to all the reloads you've made) that they haven't even discovered that there are hostiles in their territory. Speaking of reasonable NPC:s the use of voicelines is both well done regarding to quality and timed very well with regards to gameplay actions. The music is nothing to gloat over but it surely is atmospheric, though in such a replay friendly game there could have been longer and more varied scores, for example when you are discovered and all hell brakes lose it always seems as if it's the same theme playing.All in all a great buy, even if not on sale. (But if you are on the fence and want something cheaper, check if you like shadow tactics. Also think there is a demo to try out somewhere)

_childDocuments_.review: Desperados Wanter Dead or Alive is quite possible my favourite game of all time (definitely top 3), so I had high expectations. Although I wasn't too worried as Shadow Tactics from Mimimi was superb, too.To some degree this is western-Shadow Tactics. If you liked that, this is a no brainer, just buy it and you will love it.Tbh, there were a few weird things for me at first. Why reset the relations between the original characters? Why only three of the old characters and two brand new ones? The new voice actors are totally understandable but man did they sound weird saying those well known old phrases!The story, while not a masterpiece but it is very good, did justify the choices around characters. And I did like the variety in the way the characters talked to each other and about the missions. Some of their sentences made me LOL, and I don't do that too often. So, all the weirdness I ended up liking quite quickly.From gameplay POV this is a masterpiece. Desperados and Shadow Tactics already were, so no surprise here really. The one thing I missed is the less predictable behaviour of the enemies from Desperados. But I also understand why it was easier to just use the enemy classes from ST. Would I have liked the game more with less predictability? Absolutely! Do I still like the game regardless? Absolutely!Desperados 3 does live up to its name. And from someone who loves the original, this sums it up all really. Must-play for the fans of its genre.

_childDocuments_.review: The strategy is perfect, the characters are very different and all offer a different approach, allowing us to play and replay this game with several different strategies.Replayable not just for the fun, but also for the challenges, but mainly for the fun.The story is great and the characters all have strong personalities, with lines that fit the mood perfectly.Desperados is a western version of strategy games, from a period of the United States that is always very captivating in terms of ambiance.The traps used to kill enemies are very clever and fun to watch.Many gamers are put off by the trigonometric view but it's perfect for strategy games and the graphics in desperados 3 are wonderfully well done, the devs have a very good mastery of this art.The missions are very long, with lots of areas to explore and enemies to kill. If you take the time to play the game 100%, you'll get as much enjoyment out of it as the price demands.

_childDocuments_.review: A game worth recommending. If you liked the old commando games, this is for you. If you enjoyed Shadow Tactics by the same developer, this is for you. If you don't know those games but enjoy tactical decision making at your own pace, this is for you. It has a nice cast of characters with different abilities, a fairly simple  but enjoyable storyline with a nice finish.I finished the main story at a normal difficulty, which for me was a perfect mix of being challenging enough and also not becoming frustrating, when I made mistakes. But I have yet to try the 'Desperado' difficulty, so I'm unsure about the difference. When you're done with the main storyline - or also during if you'd like - there's the option to do several challenges to get more gameplay out of it. While - in my opinion - not as interesting as playing a new level in the main story, it does scratch that itch when you want to play more. Also there's the option to get badges as rewards, at first what these are are unknown, after you've played a level you'll know and can play it again to get these badge rewards. While they're just for fun, they often do make you play differently, sometimes it requires you to take a path you didn't take previously and other times it restricts you on using specific abilities. The ones I don't care for much - but that's just a lack of interest - are the speedrun badges, i.e. finish a level within 15 minutes; To those who care the speedruns are probably the most difficult badges to obtain.

_childDocuments_.review: A very good game in a genre that is almost gone. RTTs are rare nowadays and for players like me, who grew up with the original Desperados Wanted Dead or Alive, Robin Hood Legend of Sherwood, Commandos series etc, this is such a great experience. The game is punishing, challenging and a lot of fun. I recommend it to everybody, even if they have never played anything like this.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun and a difficult stealth based western isometric game. Similar to playing with heroes on old RTS games, with a nice "pause" feature like red dead's dead eye. _childDocuments_.name: Desperados III

_childDocuments_.review: So far having a really great time, was just gonna check it out quickly tonight and ended up playing 5 hours so that's great. I would say it feels even more nicely progressive in the story and missions than Shadow Tactics so far. I like that wedding mission where you first play as the bride sneaking around then it switch to Cooper the gunslingers perspective and you play him and eventually you meet up and play both. It just felt more glued together and fletched out than what I remember Shadow tactics was. Both games amazing so not saying anything bad about Shadow Tactics just an observation and you can tell they definitely learn things with each game. Graphics are fine nothing groundbreaking but they fit the theme and are convincing enough, sound as usual is also really good and the music was really catchy, felt like Clint Eastwood movie at times. Something I really love developers doing is the small stuff most might not know could be in the game but when it's there you wonder why not every game have it. Like the achievments you can get in game for the missions, kill no guards, don't hide in bushes, complete it under 5 minutes, use no disguise etc. Then the replay function so you can save your run if you liked it, just genius and it tells a lot about these developers understanding on what their players want and expect from their game.The fact that you can actually click through game hints yourself at your own pace instead of missing it every time since your SSD loads the screen too fast. It's just small things but not many developers get these minor things correct. It made me happy seeing the UI and how they introduce you to the game. You can tell it's passionate gamers and not microtransaction designers in charge here.I'm sad to hear that they're shutting down the studio, Mimimi games were so great, even their logo is so unique and cute, it sucked you in at the loading screen the first time I saw the crying baby. It's just brilliant and you knew straight away a company that has such an original logo will make great games as well and I was not wrong. This is a gem just like their other games and I definitely recommend buying all of them, these games are so rare these days and this style will always have a place in my heart growing up with Commandos before them.
