_childDocuments_.review: Desperados 3 is not that bad of a game. It's a top-down tactics game whereby the objectives are clear and the area has multiple routes for you to choose how you achieves these objectives. Every character has different abilities, strengths and weaknesses. You could almost classify it as a puzzle game becasue once you get spotted you might as well reload the save. Don´t expect to just go in guns blazing and win it, the enemies are perfectely capable of killing you before you even have your gun out so a more thoughtful approach is often the best and the zerg rush tactic is best reserved for when you are close to the end.The reason why I don´t recommend it is thus: I have some experience with the developers of this game. Shadow tactics: Blades of the Shogun was a pretty good game and Desperados 3 is basically that but in the wild west with some tweeks and improvements to the UI and more options. The problem with that is that many of the bugs and annoyances are also transferred. Characters sometimes not running even though you double clicked or run when you only clicked once. Characters standing right up when they exit a ladder or a river are just a few. The greatest reason why I don't recommend this game is that one of these bugs doesn't allow me to progress the game. In the mission Mississippi River there is a pop-up of one of your new skills. You can't close it, the pop-up doesn't show anything and the game crashes. You can't reload the save and have to replay the mission only to end up with the same pop-up and the same bug and the same crash.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a completely different game to my usual games like call of duty and gta but I have found that I have liked the change in genre. This is a real time strategy game where you play as a cowboy and possibly other characters depending on the mission and you can control what each character does and how they will kill their target or just an enemy whether it be with a gun or a stealth attack. I haven't played the game for very long yet but already I have really enjoyed the difference in genre and the game as a whole.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolute must play for anyone that played the old Commandos games or enjoys challenging tactical games. The stealthy real time tactical formula was not only seamlessly preserved but polished to perfection as well, meaning you can solve the tactical mission puzzles in as many ways as your creativity allows, especially with the introduction of the occult tactical options (don't want to spoil anything beyond that) so the tactical combinations are endless. You can also go in guns blazing if that's what you prefer. Slap on a good story with top notch voice acting and extra content in terms of bonus challenges or missions and this game is the complete package. Mimimi Games have done a brilliant job, just like they did with Shadow Tactics, so I'm looking forward to what they come out with next.

_childDocuments_.review: Desperados III is a tense, challenging, white knuckled real time tactics action adventure which combines Shadow Tactics with the versatility and replayability of the Hitman series. Visually portrayed from a top-down view, the player controls a total of five characters throughout the game (though some missions will vary these numbers depending on the event in the plot) to complete the objectives of the mission. Each character has their own unique inventory of weapons, gadgets and abilities which boast their share of strengths and relative limitations. It is this character diversity that allows for a substantial amount of the replayability because, like the Hitman series, it allows the player to experiment with different ways as to how they accomplish tasks. Such methods include direct assault, stealth, guns blazing and the staging of incidents to give the impression that the opponent death was an accident. To add to the replayability, the game offers various challenges and alternate modes to go about the various challanges offered by Desperados III.Visually, Desperados III is simplistic beauty by offering a clean and crisp top down perspective of gameplay. As far as soundtrack is concerned, it's barely noticeable but that isn't necessarily a flaw given that it keep the gameplay at the focal point (this is important since a mission can be ruined by the most miscalculation of space or time). The seemingly minimalist art-style of the game, overall is a strength. Specifically, I refer to the fact that this game features no pre-rendered cut scenes or cinematics. All of the gameplay is told from within the immersion and is very effective in doing so as the flow between gameplay and story is never broken. Desperados III is unapologetic in its difficulty but pays off by allowing the player to vary the level of difficulty along with a save system that outright reminds you to save - it doesn't hold your hand, as such, but is at least self-aware enough of its difficulty to not shame them into using the save system. While the year is far from over, Desperados III is shaping up to be the game of 2020. I enjoyed the tense and frustrating moments, I loved the way the game looked, the story had me immersed from the beginning and I thoroughly enjoyed playing as all five characters because each offered a unique gaming experience. A modern classic.5 out of 5

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: After some thinking, I actually changed my opinion to a thumb down. While there's nothing really wrong with the game, I feel like the full prize would just be too much for a game that is essentially the very same puzzle game that Shadow Tactics was, but with slightly different graphics. It has the same issues (some people may actually think of them as features rather than problems, but I don't), and it's doesn't feel like the Old west any more than ST felt like Old Japan. If you're interested, wait until it's properly discounted, that's the best way to get real bang for your buck, otherwise you're just in for a bit of a disappointment unless you played ST previously and are still having wet dreams about it.Original: Does what is says on the tin. Yet perhaps a slight disappointment, if I'm honest, but as there is nothing essentially wrong with it, I don't want to give it a thumb down. It is a Commandos-style game, but it shares some of the same issues it's predecessor, Shadow Tactics had: the various characters are not really THAT different from each other. All but one are capable of doing the melee kill, which it what you'll be using 98% of the time. The system is utterly merciless when it comes to your dudes getting spotted, it's literally 1 millimetre or 1 fraction of a second that separates a clean kill from an ALARM that practically requires you to reload the quicksave since the UI and the game mechanics don't allow for a very flexible combat to occur once you've been spotted. At least this time the map design is slightly better than what it was in Shadow Tactics, but still I often get the feeling it's simply an exercise in getting from A to B and killing all the guards in between. The biggest issue is that just as in Shadow Tactics it didn't really FEEL like I was in Old Japan, Desperados III doesn't feel like I'm in the Old West. Both games are just too sterile somehow, they feel like puzzle games (which of course they are) with really pasted on themes that fail to fully immerse the player. If you're looking for a proper Commandos-style game, go for the Partisans 1941, it's captures the feeling much better and feels much more like a TACTICS game instead of a PUZZLE where there is only one correct solution.

_childDocuments_.review: I adored Desperados. It was one of the first PC games I played and a huge part of my childhood. Then came Desperados 2 and I didnt like it at all. Until recently, I wasnt even aware Helldorado existed. So the franchise eventually died, both for real and in my memory. And so did the entire subgenre it represented. Fast forward more than a decade later and out comes little game called Shadow Tactics, from an unknown developer. Seeing those cones again woke up memories of Commandos, Robin Hood and especially Desperados. I had to play it. And it was phenomenal. And then those same devs announced Desperados 3. And it is glorious.This is the finest example of tactical strategy you can find. Everything great about Shadow Tactics has been improved upon and cranked up to 11. Every of the 5 playable characters is unique and combining their skillset is key to success. There is a huge amount of ways you can complete your objective and dispose of your enemies. One character in particular offers possibilities I didnt even think were possible in the genre. Each level is huge and methodically crafted to offer maximum amount of challenge and most of the levels take hours to complete (for us mortals). Story, although cliched, was surprisingly good and I loved seeing these characters again. Besides Story, which will take you 20-30 hours to complete, there are also badges to earn, baron's challenges and bounty mode. There is a lot to do and replayability is impressively high.Edition I bought also came with 3 dlc missions and I'm working my way through them now.The only issue I can find in the game is AI, which sometimes reacts in bizarre ways, but its an issue that still plagues entire stealth genre.To say the least, I'm impressed. Thank you devs for bringing this series and genre back to life. After Shadow Tactics and Desperados 3, I'm 100 percent behind whatever Mimimi do next.10/10

You really just end up doing the same thing over and over (stealth knife throw, long shot -run hide) ... with limited ammunition one is forced to run too much until find more.  Concept is fine, just think way too many enemies on some of these missions and would like to fight back more vs. always run and hide. _childDocuments_.review: On the positive side, the game looks great. The character animations are wonderfully detailed and the terrain is wonderful. The music is also very enjoyable. It was not long before I saw it simply as a series of puzzles to solve with the five characters as different operators. That may be for the best, because the game essentially has you playing five characters who murder hundreds, maybe thousands, of people in pursuit of vengeance against one man who killed one of your characters's father and another man who tried to steal the farm of another of your characters. This is my first game from the "stealth" genre, so I can't compare it to others, but I would recommend it to fans of that genre. Overall, 3/5.

_childDocuments_.review: My first play-through of the Desperado games. It's a fun game with solid gameplay. Main story took me about 45 hours to beat. I feel I got my money's worth especially with the sale discount.Pros:-Lots of planning, timing, and execution of stealth kills. Like solving a methodical puzzle.-Satisfying to clear areas of enemies.-If you like Shadow Tactics you'll enjoy this gameplay.-Playable characters have interesting skill to play around with.-Good visuals and sound.-Level design is varied.-Only encountered one bug late in the game but it resolved itself.-Isabella has fun abilities. I wish the entire game was a voodoo theme.Cons:-The story never really picks up intrigue. Skipped cutscenes halfway through.-You're constantly saving the game every 1-2 minutes.-If you don't like constant trial and error gameplay you might not like it.-Western setting doesn't feel fully explored.-Not as much "gunslinging" as expected.-Only three enemy types.-Controls can be a little finicky.-Environmental kills don't feel as satisfying as you'd expect.

_childDocuments_.review: A top-down stealth/shooter/strategy game where you play as a ragtag band of misfits in the West. There's a lot of depth to this game that, even on the second mission, you're looking at how best to approach each group of enemies. This only gets amplified with each character you add to your roster.One example of this, Cooper can do stealth takedowns at a range by throwing his knife, while Doc can throw his bag out to be seen on an enemy's patrol pattern to lure them in. Once they open that bag, it blinds them, and Doc can ambush. When you mix these two options, you need to weigh which one is better to use where, or if it'd be better to use in tandem with the other. If there's an enemy wearing a pancho, they will not go for Doc's bag, so it's better to use Cooper to take them out. Putting this in action, I used Doc's bag as a distraction for one enemy to pull his patrol pattern away from a Pancho that I had Cooper kill while the patrolling guy was distracted by the bag. When he got blinded, Doc stealth killed him.This game has many ways to approach each group of enemies. Stealth is the main focus so far, but is pretty satisfying to do. You could also just ignore a lot of them if you move right, and then there's going loud, which you'll find there's a time and place for.All in all, the game is beyond what I expected of it so far after picking it up for the sole reason of it being reviewed as overwhelmingly positive on here, and I absolutely look forward to whatever comes next.

_childDocuments_.review: After having both the games "Commandos: Beyond the Call of Duty" and "Desperados: Wanted Dead or Alive" as some of my favorite games of all time buying this game didn't require much thinking. Is it as good though..?I am not sure how many who knows about it but the first Desperados game had TWO sequels that tried something different. It was good ideas and fine stories but rather lackluster in execution and definitely not worthy sequels as a whole.This game is more back to the original style. Offcourse the original came MANY years ago. Some who will be buying this game wasn't even born yet so naturally it's not exactly the same but I think they got most things right.Unless you are really talented this game does require more patience than most games out there. It's not about being the fastest or smartest it's more about seeing the whole picture and figuring out your next move. It is certainly not a style of game for everyone. Compared to food GTA is pizza and this is more like something your grandparents love that you don't understand at all. Thankfully.. Some of out there are "grandparents".The game does look like a better version than the original without taking it too far to the left or right. It certainly has a lot more details that I enjoy and I believe most others would too. Both in story of the missions but also small things in the gameplay. I remember Commandos 3 took some elements too far hoping to make the game better than the previous games but it didn't work. Here it's just enough.I don't think many play these types of games for the story but I do like what is here and most of the characters has very entertaining personalities. Most characters..? Yes, there is one brand new character which has some features I thought was a bit off. It is sort of a voodoo woman I don't think it really fits. Her abilites is too strong and make some things too easy. A minor issue for me but in future games I hope to find other characters or that she is changed up a bit. One thing missing is also the ability to have smaller characters for singular missions. They could easily worked in a couple to spice things up. Someone you meet along the way and after one or two missions their off somewhere. The levels are fun and creative. If you have played the game "Shadow Tactics: Blades of the Shogun" you will see that some levels are very similar. But it's the same type of game from the same company so I can't really blame them. Only positive things from me here.I have to be honest though. I never did finish the game. Just like in the original there is a odd "last battle" (the very end of the game) that in theory is very cool but just didn't work this time around either. I hated it back then and don't care for this even though it is a different type of challenge. It is the only time the game changes format and in my eyes doesn't do it well. Please! If you guys and girls do more sequels.. Just make the last level be a normal one, lol.So.. Is the game as good as the original? In my nostalgic mind? No. Because of one thing. This style of game is about slow strategy and should be a challenge. In this game you can often use your gun and get away with it. Which rarely was the case in the original. I might be in vast minority but I prefer the old style. This does look exactly the same on the surface but both here and there it's easier to push forward. Besides that complaint, which I don't think would occur to many at all, this game is stellar. I might not love it like the originals but I do like it a lot and looking forward to other similar games by the same company. I hope they don't go "Commandos 3" in the future and similar games might be even better!Grade? Easily a 8 / 10 game for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Graphics are good for its style of game. Works well on a Steam Deck at max settings for 90 minutes on a full charge. Saves sync with my Linux desktop running the game on max 4k using an RTX3090.Western themed top down tactics game. Most of the action happens real time but there's an added Showdown mode that allows you to pause the game and plan a single action per character then trigger all queued actions at will.  This allows a lot of inventiveness in gameplay as you can create some crazy chain of events that unlocks a blocked path of guards that would have been impossible to sneak past. Each character has their own style of stealth   based on their unique abilities. When mixed together, you feel like you're in control of a Western SEAL Team Six.This soundtrack oozes that Western cowboy vibe. Uses a Leitmotif in the main theme song that gets mixed into other songs. Such an earworm of a theme.If you enjoyed Shadow Tactics, this is an easy recommendation. It's the same formula of game, just a Western setting instead of the Japanese theme with some additional improvements. If you like stealth games like Metal Gear  Solid, and RTS games like Starcraft/Warcraft, this game is a fusion of both genres. Also has a great story to tie all the great gameplay together.2 thumbs way up.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok full disclaimer, this is my first ever desperados game and i am LOVING it. Ive done about 9.5 hours so far and enjoyed every second. I have not really played a game like this before although I am a big fan of beautiful isometric games. personally I find it very challenging. but that is not a bad thing! Usually if a game becomes too hard that it requires multiple attempts, i start to lose interest and say to myself "ill pick this up again another time and really give it a go", but not this one. the quick save and quick load buttons on screen are a great way to just reset and try a different tactic. it makes me want to try again, with a different approach, right away.I forget to save sometimes if im really in the moment and can see my next move right away, thats gotten me in trouble a couple times, such as not saving when you begin a new level. i had to keep going back to my last save toward the end of the previous level, but thats just my own forgetfulness. You have to really pay attention, think, study, plan your moves. Its so tactical, that a lot of the times it feels like a puzzle game as you stare at the characters on screen and watch and learn patrol routes and enemy behaviours to plan your strategy. Something i really like is the map replays you get at the end of each mission where you get to see the exact path and all the actions you took on an overview map of the level. One of the levels so far took me almost 2 hours to complete ( I know, i suck. ) but i enjoyed every second of it. to watch my movements and tactics play back on the map when i finally finished it was so good, i was remembering all of my actions and what i had done, even impressed myself a couple times haha.Anyway, this is a great game, really makes you step back, watch and think.  oh and the graphics are just beautiful! ive been looking for something that graphically rivaled Divinity Original Sin 2 and i think ive finally found it. its a different style of gameplay but that graphical style is just gorgeous. the levels i have been through already have been so intricately beautiful with so much going on, so many props and set pieces, it really feels like looking down on a miniature western world. I would highly recommend this to any fan of isometric rpg games looking for something different and more focused on strategy and tactics, but still with that beautiful graphical style. Id also recommend it to fans of puzzle games, people who like to sit back and study before making their moves, and of course fans of stealth, strategy and tactics. being able to pause time to plan your next move really allows you to think every outcome through before you execute it. Im having a lot of fun with this, I hope you will too! I must now go back in time and check out the other desperados games because clearly, i have missed something very special here.

_childDocuments_.review: This is what Desperados II should have been.I am a great fan of the original Desperados : Wanted Dead or Alive. I have played it again and again and again. I can still play it anytime I want it and it never gets old. Then came the abomination called Desperados 2 : Cooper's Revenge. Don't know what happened but the voice acting was horrendous. Absolutely sickening! It's like they hired some fish market sellers and drunkards for voice overs. And whatever happened to the animated cut scenes? The original Desperados had great CG cutscenes. Desperados 2 had stop motion frames which reflect on the laziness of the developers. Or lack of funds? And the move to 3D was bad. Really bad. Others would have reviewed all that made this game a shame for the original Desperados. And finally now, we Desperados III. To say the least, this is a true work of love and pays homage to the original Desperados. This is how 3D should be done in a stealth tactics game. It's the same engine used in Shadow Tactics by the same developer, and hence, many of the elements of the game might be familiar to those who have played it.Due to the similarity with Shadow Tactics, some may feel a bit "been-there-done-that" but the game still is as involving and as addictive as ever to get that special final finishing touch and doing the "clean-up" work of disposing the enemies one by one, and clearing area by area. The textures and graphics are different to reflect on the wild west theme. Pros :------+ Huge Maps. (Playing at Hard Difficulty first time took about 2.5-3.5 hrs for each map for me.)+ Deep game mechanics, requires thoughtful planning + Smooth graphics even at 4K on a moderate range Radeon 5700XT.+ 3D implementation put to good use in an isometric game+ Addictive gameplay+ Multiple ways to complete a mission+ High replayability+ Stable and no crashes+ Has a polished feel+ Good voice acting and good animations+ This is what Desperados 2 should have beenCons:------- Gameplay is too similar to Shadow Tactics due to using the same game engine- Almost no Mexicans in this game, no Mexican slang, no Tequila, and no Sanchez! (I'm Asian, btw). I felt the original Desperados blended well with the southern states and border towns which gave identity to that game.- Inclusions of missions dealing Red (Native American) Indians would have been better- I find characters in the original Desperados other than Cooper, Kate and Doc more interesting. I really missed Sanchez and Sam.- The death animation of enemies are purposely made slow, so, when playing in harder difficulties, it can be frustrating to avoid the enemy line of sight within the given short period of time- Not for those who are not patient with thoughtful planning and execution. This game relies on trial and error. You really need patience to play this kind of games.This is one game that I really added to my wishlist, because I've played Shadow Tactics before and I had a feeling Mimimi Games would deliver and uphold the legend of the original Desperados. And it didn't disappoint. In fact, it's a blast to play.

_childDocuments_.review: 60 hours of enjoyment (and glorious frustration) in the main storyline alone. I haven't even touched the many additional challenges that unlock throughout the first playthrough. Desperados: Wanted Dead or Alive was the first PC video game I ever played as a kid, and I was genuinely scared to get this because of how special the first game was to me. I also found the 06 sequel clunky and second-rate. Even after I read some of the steam reviews, I was surprised and blown away within the first 20 minutes of play. Mimi Games has created an absolute masterpiece. Beautiful, genius map designs. Outstanding dialogue, cutscenes, and music. They managed to build upon, modernize, and honor the original in storytelling and game mechanics. It's also hilarious and features 5 characters that are ALL fun to play as and a necessity to utilize for each mission.My style of gameplay for the missions is ALWAYS stealth. I tried to take out every guard in every map (which is why the first playthrough was 60 total hours), but the badges and challenges encourage and incentivize the player to revisit each level. I did a lot of exploring and screwing around, but most players won't have to spend this much time in their first playthrough. An absolute must for anyone who loved the original. A great game to start with if you've never played this style of RTS (haven't played Shadow Tactics yet, but heard this is a little easier due to the updated "Showdown Mode" which is badass). Frustrating as hell? Absolutely. Rewarding, fair, fun, and nostalgic? Absolutely. One of the best games I've ever played.

_childDocuments_.review: In case the developers read these reviews but not if TLDR, I'll start off with, PLEASE GET THE COMMANDOS LICENSE and make COMMANDOS 4. If anyone can do right to that franchise, it is these guys. They know what they're doing.Ok, with that out of the way, I was introduced to this genre, from Commandos. Had a blast in those games during my younger days once I got the hang of the gameplay style. It was highly unique and different for it's time. Super frustrating but once you learned that Quicksave and Quickload were your best friends, it just got a whole lot better. Nothing like making a mistake, but being able to instantly go back to right the wrong. From Commandos, I discovered Desperados which came out some time later.I initially was never into the Wild West theme in games in general. My only thing going for Desperados was that I heard it was Commandosesque and this drove my interest to give it a shot. Sure glad I did. It plays splendidly into the formula of real time tactics and the Wild West flair just adds character to this particular genre.If you are already familiar with the genre and played Commandos, Robin Hood Sherwood Forest, Samurai Tactics (also awesome game from these guys), then Desperados will feel right at home with you. Control a range of characters that each have their own strengths and weakness with an assortment of gadgets to get through each stage. The typical route would be using stealth as this isn't a game you want to just go guns blazing and making everyone come at you because you will not live long. That is where the beauty of this game lies, in the matter of how many ways you can come up with to get by against all odds situations. Every stage you will be outnumbered dramatically and it's up to you to figure out the best ways to lure the enemy to kill, hide, or ultimately remove them from the situation. Each enemy represents a thought on how you are going to take them out or lure them. This is where the fun begins. A lot of trial and error but again, back to the top, quick save and quick load are your friends. You can have the greatest plan set, only to realize 1 guard you never noticed hiding in a spot just witnessed everything and now your bust. Quickload! Okay, now you know where that guy is, time to alter the strategy because of him. This is rather addictive as easy as it sounds because it is not always easy to alter the strategy you came up with to just take into consideration this other guy you never noticed.Listen, I can ramble on forever about how great the game is and talk about how it plays, but you just need to try it yourself and determine that. It's not for everyone, but it is very rewarding for those with the patience to give it a shot. A single stage can take hours as you carefully plot your course but completion feels amazing. The graphics are superb, the music, sound effects, and everything just fits together flawlessly. I can't think of a better job they could have done here and is why I'm giving my endorsement (lol) for these guys to take control of the Commandos series. They can do it justice.
_childDocuments_.name: Desperados III

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of the RTS genre and you like stealth mechanics in games, Desperados III is definitely worth buying!The level design is excellent. Each level has a special theme. The mission objectives can be approached in different ways. Each playable character also has different strengths and weaknesses. This means that strategies have to be constantly rethought. Desperados III is basically a prime example for the trial-and-error method. A western film or game stands and falls with its soundtrack. An epic soundtrack is therefore essential. Desperados III delivers that. You only have to spend a few seconds in the main menu and the soundtrack pulls you into the Wild West.Each character is interesting in its own way. However, I would have liked longer and more cutscenes to introduce the characters in more detail. It took me several levels to develop empathy for The Magnificent Five.The story starts slowly, but really picks up speed in the middle of the game. The ending, however, has no depth at all. More emotional character development or a surprising plot twist at the end would have helped here. Besides, some elements of the story were quite predictable.Nevertheless, Desperados III is for me one of the best games of 2020! I hope that we'll see more games like Desperados III and Shadow Tactics from Mimimi Games in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Desperados III

_childDocuments_.review: Mimimi have improved so much since Shadow Tactics: Blades of the Shogun.Characters are likeable, they interact perfectly with each other. Every one of them act according to their established character(maybe they could've improved Isabelle's story arc a bit more).Story is nothing special but the way they integrated these characters into it is amazing(there are some well done twists). Voice acting is on point, you can see that they wanted to make a perfect product.Music is breath taking, capturing wild west spirit perfectly + capturing mood of the gang most of the time.Everything looks amazing. Big improvement from Shadow tactics(it looked great too).Gameplay wise, damn. I felt that it was easier than Shadow tactics(even on hard difficulty), but there is another difficulty "Desperado" which is great if you want to challenge yourself. They have also implemented new challenges which are so much fun. Main story tho, first few missions are really easy, untill you pick up all skills with characters. Then we have classical: find one weak spot in an area and exploit it, which is sometimes really hard on first playthrough. Last couple of levels require of you to think hard, to plan out your every move(if you are playing on hard difficulty or doing badges, it requires of you to think even harder because you won't get away with some shenanigans).I really like what they did with characters.Cooper is really strong. You will end up using all of his abilities very often + he can swim, climb vines, climb ropes and has ~1s kill with melee.I found Hector useful only for carrying bodies, disposing of Longcoats and sometimes for sawed-off or Bianca.Kate is good for blinds and obviously distractions with disguise. She also has almost silent short ranged pistol which i didn't use often.McCoy is good only for sniping and occasional use of sleeping gas or dr. bag. Can't climb vines or swim, same as Kate and Hector.Isabelle...so broken. She is by far strongest one. She is fast while crouching, can climb vines, can swim, she can link 2 enemies(what happens to one happens to the other), mind control(used it maybe once per map but probably would end up spending hours figuring out how to pass guards), and cat as distraction(double distraction if you use link). I said that she is most broken because you can basically take out 3 enemies without raising alarm in area where there are 10 guards with link + mind control.Overall, game is amazing. Main content will take you 20-25+ hours to finish on first playthrough and there is bonus content with challenges and revisiting main missions for badges(which are well thought out).Also, you don't have to be RTS fan to enjoy this game or Shadow tactics.Definitely worth a buy.

_childDocuments_.review: Desperados III is an excellent follow up to Mimimi's 2016 release, Shadow Tactics: Blade of the Shogun. The game builds and expands on the previous title's mechanics, so experienced players, as well as new players looking for that Commandos (1998-2006) nostalgia will feel right at home.Level design, character design, and voice acting are impressive once again.Similar to Shadow Tactics, replayability for Desperados III is all about replaying levels to accomplish various challenges, which encourage different play styles. Each level can be completed multiple ways, encouraging players to experiment. Later in the game, you unlock challenge maps. These return you to previous maps, but will all new challenges and restrictions, such as no weapons and environmental kills only.With Desperados III, Mimimi has another Stealth RTS gem on their hands.

_childDocuments_.review: Very interesting fluctuation of emotions about this game. Started with excitement since I saw it announced maybe a year ago, since I loved the original, and still play it occasionally. Then moved into severe disappointment when first playing, particularly with the lack of infinite gun reloads which made the first game so fun, with the sort of blend of abilities from Shadow Tactics and Desperados, and with the fact that as soon as an NPC notices a body, the alarm will be raised sending tons more guys out patrolling so you can't just make a pile of bodies to lure everyone into a death pit like the first game. However as the game went on, I started also to feel positive about the changes, as it makes for not only a slightly more challenging game, but also it's done well. The balance of the game is good, and the final, fifth character's new abilities are seriously dope. The final challenge is really taxing, as it should be, but not so much that its unpassable, I managed it on the first go (I mean, of playing, not reloads haha, there was probably about 30-50 reloads just for that part). And at that point, I realised I loved the game.So that was my range of mixed feelings about the game.Some pros, cons, and deets i didn't get from the store page:pros:-characters feel balanced, all are useful in someway, more difficult to just smash through a level with just one of them-the map replay of characters and actions after completing a level is pretty dope-with achievements/goals for each level, plus the barons missions, there is tons of replay.-animations are realistic-storyline is good enough-the prequel that should have been like 18 years ago-characters conversations actually made me lol a few times-Hector's love affair with his bear trap Biancacons-mass killing is less frequent-setting off alarms is a lot easier-sometimes you have no choice but to set off an alarm-you can only really use characters skills to distract/move NPCs (which in some ways is also a pro, as it requires tactical thinking something something)-still one or two minor bugs, nothing game-changing or ridiculous though.deets-5 characters-barons missions: when you've completed enough of the game, you get special missions which are replays, but with different characters and with parameters like, only environment kills etc-17 story missions I believe.-the story of how john, kate and mccoy first started out together, plus two new characters-speedrun seems ridiculous. 15 mins for a mission that took me 2 hours to complete.... like whuuut

_childDocuments_.review: The most silly fun in stealth since Hitman: Blood Money. Want to not kill anyone? Go for it. Want to trick enemies into the same trap, one after the other? Have fun. Want to kill everyone on the map without anyone noticing? Yeah, why not? It's this sort of emergent gameplay I love in stealth games with clear, exploitable AI. Desperados III is also significantly improved from Shadow Tactics, with a ton of animations, level variety, and most important, quick loading, which is a pretty important thing to do right when you're expecting people to do a lot of it. I have some criticisms with the voiceover work (I'm not sure what accents a lot of the cowboys are supposed to be), but other than that, I really, really like this game. It has rough edges, absolutely, but I love those rough edges. I love that there's a power that lets you psychologically link two enemies, so if you have one pet a cat, the other will replicate the motion without a second cat. This is just intentional, stupid fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Once again we are back in the western era in United states, much like the setting of red dead redemption which we all have at the forefront of our memory.The game is a pretty decent and addictive piece. It can be frustrating at times, but very rewarding all the same. Much like dota 2, but without the hate and furiosity which is so common in online games. Clarification: I'm not saying it's like dota 2 gamewise, just what the game makes you feel.The game is stealth/strategic/puzzle/western-story, quite similar to commandos which you have probably heard of or even played some years or even decades ago. I don't think you will be disappointed picking this gem up, though the prize can come across as somewhat high for a game which is obviously not a Tripple A production, but rather a Double A one.The good+ Nice atmosphere+ Executing combos which works out well, is a total blast+ You will most certainly get a few elevated heart beat moments+ Nice voice actors and above average likeable characters+ Lots of replayability thanks to different challenges+ Gamepad and mouse/keyb-support which is well optimized for either setup. I play with both gamepad in front of TV as well as mouse/keyb in front of computer depending on mood and playstyle. The latter being somewhat more precise for challenge hunting.The bad- Graphics can feel somewhat dated and the character models a bit recycled for a 2020 game at almost full price tag, but the aesthetics are pleasing.- It feels as if the game sometimes doesn't execute the commands you intended which results in long series of quick loads. Thankfully, your last three saves are always available in case you accidentally save after you have ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up.- The controls can be quite clunky, even though it's probably hard to perform it otherwise.- Even though there is potentially 100eds of possible strategies to use, one tends to (I at least) fall back on what is tried and tested, resulting in problems being solved almost identically on every map. This esentially makes the game feel a bit repetitious, even though the difficulty bar constantly rises and the margin for error shrinks incrementally.Final score: 8/10 GreatGuide:1 - Abysmal2 - Miserable3 - Wretched4 - Bad5 - Half assed6 - Okay 7 - Good, 9 - Incredible, 10 - Amazing/Outstanding)

_childDocuments_.review: This is the first Desperados game I've played. And it's awesome. I love tactical stealth action games and this fits the bill perfectly. Stalking around in the shadows, hiding in bushes, or donning a disguise, in order to sneak up on baddies to slit their throats, or bait them into stepping onto a giant bear trap (lovingly named "Bianca"), or cast voodoo mind control magic to have baddies shoot each other is all par for the course. Though if you want or if needed, you can always go in knives out and guns blazing. Though you probably won't have enough ammo to kill everyone, which necessitates the stealth part. But there are times it's necessary. Just try not to raise any alarms. Or do; that's more baddies to kill.The built in save-scumming feature to quicksave and quickload is a godsend. It's easy to make mistakes in planning, so the ability to quickly reload is greatly appreciated. Though if you don't want to use that, you don't have to. While I wish the scenery was a little more varied, the Western environment is well done. You also do get a chance to explore the swamps of Louisiana, along with Baton Rouge and New Orleans. The story is interesting enough to keep you moving forward and the characters develop enough to keep you interested. Each has their own reasons for joining the ragtag gang of desperados and you'll find out through the game. Which is a lot longer than I expected, not even including the other game modes and challenges.In many ways, this is another take on the Hitman series or even Splinter Cell series. And Desparados 3 does a great job on that take. So if you're into either of those games or other tactical stealth games, Desperados 3 is the right choice.

_childDocuments_.review: on the one hand, it's beautifuly made and carefully designed. every enemy stands right in the place to make your life harder, the picture is a pleasure to look at, but, well, I dropped it right after the first act. the whole gameplay quickly becomes stale, because every new mission doesn't offer much new mechanics, and then you realize: «oh, sh#%, here we go again», save and load for hours, yay. seriously, sometimes I played a mission for an hour, saved, quitted, then continued the next day (the same freaking mission), and then one more time in the third day. This kind of genre isn't engaging enough nowadays, even though it would blow my mind in my childhood, probably.For a tactical gameplay, I'd settle with turn-based combat older fallouts style. If stealth is crucial… maybe «Hitman»? it's also full of scripted NPC behavior which I'm not really fond of, but at least you can make it fun any time you want when your cover is blown: not because I like action/shooters, but because it nudges you to improvise, especially if you play without saves. The combined option here is the excellent «Invisible Inc». In case of the wild west setting, we always have «RDR2» and, let's say, «Wierd West». Overall, I wish it to be a game in a different genre allowing you to explore this beautiful world in a realtime and don't plan every move you make. Or, if you remember the good old isometric game «Robin Hood: The Legend of Sherwood» (made by developers of «Desperados 2»), it could have alike metaprogress features to make your life easier in further missions by doing specific actions or earning the sheriff stars (they don't do anything here, kind of achievments). In the «Robin Hood» title of yore it was possible to build up your forest base, recruit followers and make them produce helpful items, just for example. What we have here, in «Desperados 3», well… you just want to trigger the end of your mission, no matter how, because in the next one you will have a specific team/pre-defined ammo anyways.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent strategy game, old West style (even though the majority of the game takes place in the Southeast!). Starts off a little slow but stick with it...the missions become very involved. You have to plan your moves carefully. If you make a mistake and wind up dead, just restore your last quick save and try again. If you're new to Desperado, Beginner mode is definitely recommended. This game is challenging even on beginner and many of the missions take well over an hour to complete successfully. Graphically pleasing, great dialogue (not family-friendly so play this one with headphones if younger kids are around), lots of action, and dozens of different ways to proceed through each mission successfully. Strategy guides will help when you're stuck but most of the time you'll figure out your own strategy to get through a mission. Highly recommend!

_childDocuments_.review: I've played through Commandos I & its DLC, Commandos II, Shadow Tactics: Blades of the Shogun, and now this game.This is the best RTT game in the market as of Dec 2020. The story of the game is at about 8.5/10, music is at about 9.5/10, and it's graphic is at about 9/10. The mechanic of the game is quite similar to the Shadow Tactics: Blades of the Shogun, but the level design has been the best for all the RTT that I've ever played, which is the most important part for this genre at 11/10.Each of the 5 characters have his/her unique abilities, and advancing every corner of any mission requires the development of cleaver strategies to utilize them. This is not a type of game for every gamer, but if you enjoy RTT games and/or their elements, this is the game that can't be missed. The German developers has done a awesome job of keeping this genre alive and making it better than ever. Watching/reading different coverage of them makes me think that they really treat this game with good passion, knowledge, and seriousness, and that reflect perfectly on the game.  I streamed and completed the game and its 3 DLC missions on the Desperodo (hardest) difficulty while killing all enemies melee with no injury and no alarm. I met some awesome people while doing this challenge, which includes the voice actor of Hector (a character in game). It was a very memorable 60+ hours.Special thanks to my friend Rexgar, who gifted me this game and its DLCs.

_childDocuments_.review: Deperados 3 is an absolute gem of a game that I would highly recommend to any fan of the tactical strategy genre. From the intricate level design to the satisfyingly challenging difficulty, every aspect of the game is crafted with a level of care and attention to detail that is truly impressive.One of the things I love most about Deperados 3 is the diverse cast of characters, each with their own unique abilities and personalities that make them fun to play with and easy to become invested in. Whether you prefer the stealthy approach of Kate, the brute force of Hector, or the cunning trickery of Isabelle, there's a character to suit any play style.But what really sets Deperados 3 apart is the level of strategy and planning required to succeed. Each level presents a unique challenge, requiring careful consideration of your team's abilities, the environment, and the behavior of enemy patrols. The game rewards creative thinking and experimentation, and the feeling of satisfaction that comes with pulling off a complex heist or taking down a tough boss is truly exhilarating.All in all, I can't recommend Deperados 3 highly enough. It's a masterful game that showcases the best of what the tactical strategy genre has to offer. And, with the way the game ends, I can't wait to see what the developers have in store for the next game in the series. Deperados 3 is a true triumph and a must-play for any strategy game enthusiast.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a marvel to everyone who loves games of this style. I just finished it, and want to write a positive review right away, so I don't forget it.I want to write a detailed review, not just good words.This game is a prequel to original series, it shows the past and not future of famed John Cooper. If you played original game, you'll recognize two old heroes, except cooper, and there are also two brand new. Yes, there are five characters instead of traditional six. All of heroes are very useful, you'll want to use all their abilities, none are just to occupy skill slots. One of new characters has two skills that I've never seen in other games and I am sure the majority of players will appreciate them. The difficulty is fair. The start is very easy, and the further you progress the harder missions get. Yes, towards the end, there are some very hard places. But if you like games like this and have any experience in this genre, you'd never get frustrated enough to abandon the game.Some missions have different approaches, I mean not the variety of skills, but the physical approaches - like the final base can be attacked from the east or west, and both roads have their own difficulties. Or in another mission when you need to block the railroad, the game will offer two options to do this, each with own consequences. I liked that the game allows to cause "accidents" in the way of "Hitman" series. In many missions you can kill the "tough" enemy by dropping something heavy on him. So, not only you'll avoid fighting him - which is hard, but also "accidents" never cause alarm.As a con, I can only notice that the game only has cinematics with in-game engine, it won't show any full scale video like original Desperados. That's bad, but I can live with that.So, here's summary: if you loved original Desperados, don't skip this one.10/10

_childDocuments_.review: A majestic masterpiece in this underrated game genre.Like a lot of people, I discovered Mimimi developers through Shadow Tactics. I love strategy and tactical games and I love Japanese culture (the real one, not the weeb ♥♥♥♥), so it was a great game for me, who perfectly portrated this dark time of the country. If I talk about it, it's because I recommend it just as much.Then came the trailer for Desperados III, and I was so pumped until I saw that it was yet another game set in the Old West period (such an overrused time period, it's annoying at this point). But Mimimi had completely earned my trust after Shadow Tactics and I was ready for it.Boy was I not disappointed when I played it. Everything is amazing, and I'm being objective. The gameplay is exactly the same as in Shadow Tactics (at first I was almost let down), to the point that some skills are just a copy paste. But that's not really a bad thing, even if you played the previous game.The story is incredibly deep, I really get attached to the characters, and the motion picture was the perfect idea for it. The ambiance is very immersive, be it in the graphics or in the soundtrack.There's not much to say, all I can say is, just let yourself drawn to it! Every mission is different, the replayability is at its best, and if you're a completionist, it's both easy AND fun to 100% (it's rare!)I also encourage you to buy the DLCs, they add more to the story, and hopefully it will convince the devs to keep going on this genre, because one thing is certain:Mimimi are the new masters of RTS games.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd describe this game as "Good but not great" If the price point were lower I'd have marked the review positive, but it doesn't live up to the expectation set by a £45 price tag. I passed on getting 2-3 other games to get this and having played the final level I don't feel like that was a great choice. If you're lucky enough not to have to care about money treat this review as positive.In a line this game is a very typical example of the isometric stealth tactics genre that delivers solidly on the key parts of the genre without doing anything outstanding.Compared to Shadow Tactics the interface is slicker, with the ability to speed up the game so guards move on their patrol paths being particular highlights. They've also added a challenge mode with special levels designed to make you use abilities in different ways or to avoid relying on your tried and tested solutions, which feels like a neat idea, but showing they're capable of making levels that avoid you relying on the same repetitive approaches just makes me question why that didn't happen more in the main game.The mechanics suit a western genre less than they suited a ninja genre. In Shadow Tactics creeping around stealthily taking people out makes you feel like a ninja. In Desperados refusing to use your guns in 95% of situations makes you feel like maybe you're not very good at this "western" thing.The characterisation felt a lot weaker. In part this is down to having established characters, while it's a reboot they're not going to do anything that surprising. It doesn't have any moment that comes close to the peak of Shadow Tactics, it's most dramatic moment felt more like "You appear to be acting differently to every other decision you've made so far in a really stupid way in order to have a dramatic moment". It also does a thing where it sets itself up for a little payoff (in a clumsy way but suited to the genre) and then squanders that in having one of those awful cutscenes where an arbitrary problem is introduced and then resolved without the player really being involved.I'm not sure that this is a genre that really suits sequels, getting to know characters and their personalities and capabilities is a big part of the game. I'd be much more interested in seeing a new isometric stealth game than either Shadow Tactics II or Desperados IV. Sticking to the established Desperados characters definitely hobbled it and it might meet a more positive reception from someone new to the series.Some of the design choices seem a bit poor. There's a tool to tell you who's watching a particular guard, but it doesn't work because a guard can stand on the edge of a vision cone such that they're technically not in vision but their hitbox changes slightly if they're dying so they're spotted by people who the UI said couldn't see them the moment it becomes important - the pixel perfect positioning in guard placement required to do this suggests bad UI has been implemented as a difficulty choice. Towards the end there's a section in which an action is queued by the game which will cause you to lose the level if it's carried out early, which is then triggered when you do anything with showdown mode, including clicking "Execute only this action" on a different action. Since there are some things that can only be done from showdown mode this arbitrarily limits a few abilities. There's not loads of stuff like this, more levels than not you won't encounter a single thing like it, but it comes up enough to be a ♥♥♥♥♥♥.It's still got very solid gameplay for the genre it's in. There's plenty of watching guard routes and forming a plan of attack and trying to figure out the perfect execution. A mix of guard types, terrain features, and player abilities stop it being as samey as it could've been. The new character introduces an ability I've not seen in other examples of the genre that opens up some genuinely new and interesting tactical options and is definitely the (mechanical) highlight of the game.If you liked Shadow Tactics, Desperados, and Commandos you'll probably have a decent time with this. "Good not great" means it's still good so if the genre is your cup of tea then you'd miss out not to play it, but maybe wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Greatly improves upon Shadow Tactics in every aspect. The best RTT yet. Gameplay is at it's finest, way more polished than in ST, doesn't have the same indie feel as it had. Better animations and overall smoothness. Situations are also a bit more difficult sometimes, but all in all probably not much has changed in that regard. Next big change is the variety of guns. It improves on ST concept, makes them more unique and fitting to Desperados franchise. Cooper can shoot two revolvers at once, killing several enemies. Hector's shotgun has a big aoe and opens up a lot of possibilities. Kate's small pistol produces almost no sound. And Doc is a sniper, unchanged from ST. They are both great for stealth approach and are easier to use. Showdown feature compliments them greatly. Opposite to ST it now pauses the game, popular feature in western setting games. Isabel's Connect\Domino is my favorite ability. Loved it in Dishonored 2, and loving it in Desperados 3. This and mind control ability make her great addition to the game. Biggest improvement is the writing. ST had very banal story and cliche characters. In Desperados 3 they made the jump from terrible to average. And it is good enough. Writing doesn't distract as much as it did in ST. Desperados 1 also worked because it had memorable characters and they were very well written. Hopefully in next game Mimimi will get to it's level. Looking forward to it. Must have for those who loved Shadow Tactics. Well worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: Desperados 3 is a great game for both old, and new fans of the real-time tactics genre. First and foremost, if you are interested in playing this game, download and try the demo out! Desperados 3 is in essence a great combination of old and new. While the developers Mimimi games borrows heavily when it comes to both gameplay and aesthetics from their previous game Shadow Tactics, they still manage to combine this with the feeling of the previous Desperados games. The world is portrayed in the same grim, but also humoros way as the original games and the characters are fleshed out in the often hillarious banter between them during missions. The gameplay is essentially the same as in Shadow tactics. The characters control nicely, and the skills given to each one of the characters feels different enough to make them all unique. Mimimi games makes both the characters and the missions of the game feel fresh by splitting up the team, forcing you as the player to reevaluate and use your characters in new ways when the composition and challenges of your team changes in between levels. This felt really refreshing to me, as I had to learn new combinations between my team members throughout the whole game. The maps are great creations, and always give you several options of how to take them on. This truly does invite the player to replay the game at a harder difficulty, trying out new routes and tactics. My one and only gripe with the game comes down to the enemy variety. While the combination of, and amount of enemies keeps increasing as the game goes on, the game basically consists of just a handful of different enemy types. This does in no way make the game easy, as the combination of enemies still makes them hard to take down, but it does at times make the encounters feel a tad bit predictable.All in all, Desperados 3 is a great and challenging strategic game which makes me incredibly excited for the future of both the franchise of Desperados and the developers Mimimi games.

_childDocuments_.review: Really cool game, having a lot of fun with it for the very most part+ like the graphics and the scenery+ very cool mission design with great variety+ cool and creative indiviual character design/abilities+ cool features like showdown mode and lots of different interactable stuff+ quick save/load with automatically keeping last three quick savestwo things though i really don't like (sorry, second is a long one...)- badges should be visible sooner. maybe not before the mission so they don't spoil anything but maybe after the mission intro or once they become relevant within the mission. just feels like a really cheap and obvious way by devs to make you play each mission again ...- the difficulty of obtaining  the speedrun badges is just sooooo much higher than anything else in this game. now i personally don't like speedrunning at all, but i guess that's personal taste. i like watching them though. the game genre is however what i would consider the extreme opposite of a fast paced game. you often have to and are intended to take your time and observe situations precisely to come up with a strategy, even by going through many trial and error loops. speedruns of missions feel like you're playing a completely different game and i wouldn't think people playing mostly games of this genre are used to it/skilled at it just by default. i think in the last ten years i've only played two other games of this genre, which were one single playthrough of shadow tactics and desperados 2 (which i mainly played as a third person shooter). still i was able to beat this game on its highest difficulty on my first playthrough after ~40h while clearing ALL enemies on the maps. going for the speedrun badges however, even when i set the difficulty to lowest is just sooooo much more demanding and absolutely frustrating. it feels like you have to plan out the whole mission from start to end beforehand and have to time everything so precisely because you simpley do not have the time during a mission to plan anything or look at situations since time is always running even in showdown mode and the mission timer does not go back when loading. also it is just so frustrating if you realize near the end of a long mission that you barely cannot make it i time and you cannot even load a savegame but have to start the mission completely from scratch. the speedrun badges in general are maybe a cool idea for this game, being like "hey, just try this completely different approach to the game" and introducing players to it that otherwise maybe wouldn't have thought of trying it, but as it is so different to how the game in its "intended main mode" plays i think this should not make the very very very far most difficult challenge the game has to offer. in all honesty, when i've been playing through this game on desperados difficulty i've sometimes been playing for 6h straight and still wanted to go on. when i'm going for a speedrun badge (on beginner, with reading guides, etc.) i get sooo frustrated that i cannot play the game for longer than maybe 20min max and makes me want to uninstall ---> in short i think the speedrun _childDocuments_.review: Lets get TL;DR out of the way before the long review cause I never understood why people put it at the very bottom cause if people going for ain't nobody have time for scrolling.*** TL;DR: Definite buy if you have played games from this genre before. More like a reboot instead of a sequel. Pays good homeage to original Desperados but more similar to Shadow Tactics Blade of the Shogun which is not a bad thing since that is a good game by this same developer *** Disclaimer ! Long-ass satire based, story-telling syle review beyond this point. Proceed with caution.Still here ? Ok lets carry on. Stay a while and listen, *insert meme quote from that game you can relate to"Good old me is no professional stream reviwer so don't expect bullet lists and other fancy bells and whistles. What I can provide you some ye olde style views so gather'round you young snapppers for the story.Out story takes place in the mythical BS ( Before Steam ) era...... Vicious times when poor players were bereft of the light of Almighty Gaben, Praised Be His Name, an era when internet connections were dial up and if you wanted a game you had to get them from those places called stores. Your hard saved allowances were laid before the altar of luck as sacrificed because you never knew if your offerings were going to be answered with good games or be struck down with crappy games or scratched CDs.I still remember seeing Desperados 1 on the cover of a gaming magazine and playing the free demo. I was mesmerized with the characters, maps, mission designs. I still remember the loading screens for the game being a picture of John Cooper slowly fading in and found it so cool. It is a blessing I loved that loading screen too  because I had to see that ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ loading screen so many times, rember this was the age before the fabled SSDs was bestowed upon us mere mortals, because you know...gitgudscrub, l2play noob, etc.  Being the connoisseur I am I later on went to enjoy more games in this genra like Commandos Series, Robin Hood The Legend of Sherwood and Chicago 1930. You could say I was like Robert Downey Jr. of this genre of games. If it existed I definitely did it, some more than once..... Hell I have even played Desperados 2.... Not a high point in my career but whatever.After the Commando-like genre more or less sputtered out following the flop of Commandos 4 I was left with nothing but good old memories but I was happy. After all my Desperados and Robin Hood were like a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ bottle of quality whiskey. I knew that I could always reach into the ol'cupboard and take a few sips whenever I needed that hit of nostalgia to escape the grinding gears of being an adult. I could always get my fix of nostalgia, taking me back to more innocent times... Times when our rigs had less RAMs in total than some cheap-ass smartphones nowadays, RGB was nothing but dreams of a mind on an acid-trip but we loved our games not because they had über graphics but because they were good.Later on Almighty Gaben, Thrice Praised Be His Name but not his games, came and delivered upon us a new age. We were saved by the chosen one and safe in his bosom we laid our guard in bliss.Then the DLC nation attacked. Followed by the evil games as service. Like a plague it infected many of our loved ones.... Many fell during these times... Some survived albeit forever tainted by their infestation, a mere shadow of their former glory...... Some of our numbers sought refuge in the Groove of İndies while others offered sacrifices at the Kickstarter Temples to mixed results.....As time went on this pestilence grew and morphed, taking the form of Lootboxes. Just when we thought we were brought to our lowest a new hope rose. Like a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hobbit army showing upto mordor and beating up ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Orcs and big-ass evil elephants, us mere players rose up and start to resist.Just like godrays piercing through dark clouds, good games began to flourish once more. Even though some usurpers try to lead us astray from the Steam Engine of Glory, it feels like we are catching a glimpse of the lost Golden Age.Now...... Back to the topic.... This Desperados 3 is a salt of the earth game. It may not be like those games of yonder I have mentioned but it pays good homage to its elders. Some lines like "Enough dilly-dallying" or "Someone called for a doctor" are examples of showing respect to good old Desperados.... Some of the skills on some characters like Doc's stink bomb, Kate's super charm and Cooper's coin toss stayed same. Some characters were changed with or merged into one.In an ideal world where your clock rate would be high and your CPU temps low I would expect to have the original sound actors for the remaining characters but new ones did an okay job as well. Shuffling around of some skills and some new additions were cool as well. My only gripe is with the addition of voodo stuff...... I mean mind control thinga majick is kinda similar to crazy poison dart of Mia from original game but the whole connect thing is kind of a deal breaker for me and takes away from the immersion in the game. I admit it makes for some fun and creative tactics but still, it kind of feels out of place..... Like a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ demolition derby consisting only of Smart cars...... Does it get the job done ? Sure. Is it fun ? Yeh sure..... still feels kinda too odd for this old fellow.New maps look really nice and environmental kills are funny as well but missions and maps kind of lack the pizzazz Desperados had. No more breaking a gang member out of prison, no missions where you could hide in dark shadows, no missions where you could hide your gunfire by standing near loud noise sources, horse stealing... Yeh you have different ways of interacting with maps in Desperados 3 like swimming etc but they kind of lack the charm of those from Desperados 1 and the final map is quite lackluster compared to the last map of Desperados 1, a mothereffing cave with a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ lake in it !! and a bloody puzzle based on tiles on ground as well !! You either had to be a nerd about it and solve the puzzle or just go yolo save scum like the chad I am.........In summary, Desperados 3 is good but it kind of feels like a cowboy version of Shadow Tactics Blades of the Shogun. That game is a good game by the Mimimi Games and I enjoyed it as well. Same goes for Desperados 3 as well. It is a good game and money well spent. It is no aged whiskey like Desperados 1 but a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ good craft beer.Sure your craft beer may have all of that hops and stuff and get the flavour from being aged in barrels like a whiskey as well but all I can say agains that is "Get out of my saloon you hipster.... We don't need none gentrificating train company coming here and stealing our town"Still here ? Well thank you for taking time to read this performance. Please like, subscribe, upvote, whatever.... Hope you have as much fun playing this game as I did playing it & writing this review being totally sober. I swear.

_childDocuments_.review: I was lucky to get an early copy of this game thanks to the guys at THQ Nordic (Thanks for hooking me up with the key!) and I’ve been playing this game steadily over the past month, while embroiled with editing and other projects.Made by Mimimi Games and published by THQ Nordic, Desperados 3 is an excellent sequel in the series, and by the same awesome guys who made Shadow Tactics.The gameplay…my word, the gameplay! You get a bunch of different, fleshed out characters, each with different and specified abilities, and you’re thrown a gauntlet of challenging missions to test your skills on. From Cooper’s knife throwing, loud guns and coin distractions, to Hector’s traps and axe play, to even some mind-♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ with Isabelle, you get a ton of options for completing the levels. The characters are well designed, and while I haven’t found anything particularly enthralling about the story, it’s serviceable and keeps me entertained.Shadow Tactics was known for it’s difficulty, and Desperados III is no exception. I’ve never been one for difficult games like this, so I look at my 38 hours played (by this article) and barely halfway through the game as a kind of humiliation. But it’s a good difficulty. The game blesses you with a no-penalty quick-save option and pause to plan your moves real time, and the sheer versatility and options it gives grants you a lot of replayability. I know i’ll be replaying this game on completion to try and get the achievements.As for flaws? There aren’t many. They did a really good job here. I have seen a few instances where my game refuses to load saves, forcing me to backtrack (though it may be to repeated quick saving and saving over them, causing corruption. Don’t abuse that mechanic like I have). The repetitive dialogue of the enemies when looking for you can also be a bit grating, but these are minor nitpicks. This is a chunky, well made game, and well worth its hefty price tag. Don’t be put off by that, give it a try.I rate Desperados III an easy 9/10. I’ll update the score when I finish the game, but I can already see this making my GOTY list in December. It’s that good.

_childDocuments_.review: Good:MusicVoice ActingLevel DesignCore GameplayGraphicsPerformanceAttention to detail and polish (did not encounter any bugs).Not so goodThis section is quite subjective, as I thoroughly enjoyed the game in its entirety, but people should probably consider a few things if deciding whether to purchase it or not.The story is fairly generic and not particularly deep, although I did find I enjoyed more as it went on. The gameplay is repetitive (as you get taught all the basic stuff early on) but I believe is carried by the level design and solid mechanics, which keep it interesting - almost turning it into a real-time puzzle game once you have a few scenarios under your belt. There isn't really any customisation of characters or 'rpg' elements to the game. You have access to 5 unique characters that are well written and very well voice acted. Each character has a unique set of skills and they work together to move through each level.Other commentsBecause the core mechanics are executed really well, there are a lot of potential ways to approach most situations in the game, which gives scope for replayability, along with some challenges and medals you can earn for doing things a specific way. I played through the game on Hard difficulty and got about 35 hours worth of gameplay out of it, which I was really impressed with for a single player campaign game these days. It could probably be done in around 20-25 hours with a bit more emphasis on haste or perhaps a lower difficulty, and certainly having gone through the scenarios once each now they would be a lot quicker to solve again, but some are very tricky the first time around. I certainly see myself doing another play through at some point to check out their hardest difficulty, so will likely end up getting a good 60-70 hours out of it at least.I would love to see a level editor where people could create their own maps and allow others to try them. It will be interesting to see what additional content becomes available in future, and I think the core concepts could be applied to many different genres and settings.It's a relatively simple concept with a great execution. It was refreshing and compelling to not have all sorts of skill trees and experience points, unlocks and upgrades, or to worry about min-maxing or grinding. It kind of goes 'This is what you've got, go enjoy yourself'. If you're more on-the-fence about the gameplay, I'd still recommend giving it a go but perhaps waiting until it's on sale. However, I do believe it's worth the full price for what the developers have delivered, which I can't say for a many games at that price point and above these days.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun enough game, lots of enjoyment, but clearly a reskin of shadow-tactics. The story is cool and fleshes out the characters better than the original desperados and its interesting to see more of their back stories. The missions are interesting and trying to clear the maps is fun. Be prepared to reload a lot!Here are my complaints / room for improvements. Note that this doesn't indicate that I dislike the game. I would still recommend it. Maybe some fans of the game would agree with me below.1. Number 1 biggest complaint of this game. This game is fairly new but the AI of the enemies is quite awful. I am really bringing this up because the first game was made in 2001 and it had more realism in the AI than this 2020 game. Enemies would patrol around the map and would rally - it would really want you to prevent alerting anybody ever. Now in this game the AI pathing is pathetic. Like, I'd be embarassed to have programmed it if it was being compared to the game made 20 years ago. The complete randomness of the enemy patrol is unthreatening and braindead. Bottom line. Biggest disappointment.2. Minor, but some of the challenges can be soft-locked in missions or require many re-runs in order to complete. When I have to speed run a mission multiple times to get to the one part with the challenge, I get bored.3. Witch doctor that can possess people. Witch doctor doesn't really feel like she belongs in this genre or atleast in the period. Its a HARD sell for there to be magic in this game. I'm just not buying it. She's too overpowered too.4. Where was samuel? We get every character but him? What do you have against him?5. minor: I don't understand the healing mechanic of this game. by this I mean, why have it? Why let almost very character be able to do it? Why no resources and put it on a cooldown? This isn't call of duty and I found myself never using this mechanic ever.6. Why put weapons on a cooldown? What the hell? How does it make sense to only allow someone to shoot a gun once? I understand it would break your game the way you designed it, but maybe you shouldn't have made a shadow-tactics reskin and actually programmed something new?7. Glitch: I found this out by accident but it always works. If you are ABOVE a bush (like, say you are on a roof or a higher-up balcony), you can deposit bodies into the bushes without actually being anywhere near them. Simply rotate and position the map in a way that makes it LOOK like you are hiding a body in a bush and the body will disappear as if you are actually in the bush! Game breaking.

_childDocuments_.review: This review is specially made for those who like indie games and completing all the achievements and have this game in their backlog. (minor spoilers ahead) Desperados 3 is a Real Time Tactics game where you control a group of characters in a wild west setting. The core gameplay revolves around completing mission objecting while eliminating threats, with lethal and non-lethal weapons and skills.  36 Achievements, only a few are story related, a few others will be achieved naturally while playing the game. It took me around , but my first playthrough was in the hard difficulty and I played very cautiously and with no help. Playing on Medium and using a guide will probably cut the time by half. Medium. If you played this kind of game before, the medium difficulty won’t be much of a challenge. I played on hard. Hard, or very hard, depending on your skill.  You might also need to grind a bit, depending on how you play the game. You’ll need a guide to know the location of some characters and objects, for a few achievements, figuring it out on your own will take some time. I recommend this game if you like RTT games, this is probably the best one ever released. Even if you don’t play this kind of game very well, set the difficulty to beginner and enjoy the story and characters, which are top notch. I can’t recommend this game as an easy one to get all the achievement because it will require a lot a time, guides, and some skill/strategy to complete.
