_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely one of the best games I've ever played and the definite crown jewel of the real time tactics genre. If you played the old Commandos and Desperados games: this is that but much better executed thanks to a ton of gameplay and UI improvements. If you played Shadow Tactics: this is that but bigger in scale with better, more confident gameplay design and a bunch of new features that greatly improve the experience.I could get into detail on how great the gameplay mechanics are but I think that depth is best experienced through playing the game. Let's just say that experimentation has its rewards, I kept finding new ways to solve problems up until the last mission and I don't think I've found out about everything yet. I will have my chance at digging deeper though since most missions offer at least 2 main ways in which you can complete them (and you also get quite a lot of remixed challenge maps) so the replay value is very high here.These are also long missions so when I say "bigger in scale" compared to Shadow Tactics I really mean that. When it comes to map size the game very much reminded me of Commandos 2, another RTT game with giant sized scenarios but Commandos 2 achieves most of that through busywork (useless interior areas, a ton of looting, searching for bonus books etc.) while Desperados 3 offers "real", more meaningful minute to minute gameplay.I really mean that this is the best RTT title I've played too and yes, that means it's better than the original Desperados. The main reason for that is controls and UI: for anyone trying nowadays Desperados is pretty much a nightmare to control efficiently thanks to its low fps, unintuitive hotkeys and its weird UI and tech shortcomings. In Desperados 1 you can never be sure of for example Doc's sleeping gas vial hitting the intended spot if there's a wall near the arc of the throw, you can never be sure of height based cover because of the limitations of the old 2D engine etc. and that results in an insane amount of trial and error nobody these days will put up with. In fact even returning fans can suffer, like if you look at my Desperados 1 review here you'll find a negative one from a man who gave up at the halfway point because he just couldn't take the frustration anymore.That jankiness simply doesn't exist in Desperados 3, this is a game where 99.99% of the time what happens on the screen is what you intended even if you made a mistake. Trial and error is still part of the gameplay since that's part of the genre itself but you'll reload a save because of your mistakes here and not because things don't work as they should. That fact alone is a game changer.And on top of the great gameplay you get an excellent visual style that avoids every single trap that top down 3D strategy games can fall into. The graphics are beautiful, the visuals are readable (though with the great enemy / object highlight feature turned on), the art style is a stylized version of the wild west but it's not cartoony and it just has a great sense of visual continuity with the previous games. In short the game looks like Desperados instead of trying to copy what's currently popular.To my surprise I really enjoyed the story too even though I generally don't like prequels. It was fun to see how Cooper's and Kate's backstories unfold but more importantly the game just does storytelling really well. There is just a lot of recorded dialogue for the missions (the characters even have mission specific lines for acknowleding your commands) and generally the whole thing just feels like a good western narrative with nice stylistic choices like how even the motion capture cutscenes stay true to the top down perspective.Negatives? I dunno, I think the right mouse button is a bit too busy with multiple functions and that sometimes makes cancelling an action harder than it should be... and that's all.

_childDocuments_.review: is a real-time tactical stealth game developed by Mimimi Productions and released on 16 June 2020. In  you play as Cooper and his band of outlaws on a quest for revenge. Desperados 3 successfully expands on 2016’s ’s commando-like mechanics. While it doesn’t revolutionize the formula, it polishes and improves upon its predecessors on level design, map density, extra features, graphics and audio. In short  is a stellar successor to the genre. Players control between 1 to 5 people (depending on the mission) to achieve certain objectives. The objectives vary from eliminating enemies on the map, reaching a certain destination or interacting with certain objects in the game. Players control the characters in real time, with a pause button that allows them to queue actions to execute later. Enemies have a vision cone. If you right-click on them, their vision cone will appear on the ground. There are 2 types of detection areas: clear and striped. Clear green areas means any characters and objects are visible to the enemies. If you stay too long inside the green area, enemies will attack you and raise an alarm. Striped areas means your character can move through it safely if they are crouched. Striped areas are usually the spot behind short objects, or unlit areas at night. Some enemies might carry torches that turn striped areas into green one. Bushes are safe areas you can never be detected unless the enemy is directly touching you. Almost every action creates sound. If enemies are within the sound circle, they will be alerted even when you aren’t in their vision cone. Actions such as shooting with guns will have a large sound range, and throwing knives are more silent and attract only enemies in direct vicinity. There are surfaces that make loud sounds so even walking can attract enemies. Stealth is a very crucial part of the game. If you rush into enemies’ dens they will take a short work of you as you are outnumbered heavily. There are several types of enemies. Regular enemies are weak and distractible. They can be lured out of their posts and patrol. Enemies wearing ponchos are more disciplined so they cannot be lured or moved. Heavy are tough, and can only be taken down by one particular character or you need several characters coordinating. to take them out. Dogs can sniff you out even behind bushes.There are 5 playable characters each that bring their own array of tools and abilities to your arsenal. Almost all the character’s abilities can be separated into 2 categories: Offense and Distraction. Offense are the abilities that allow Cooper and .co to remove enemies from the level. These abilities can be lethal or non-lethal.Non-lethal attacks will leave enemies stunned for a time and if you don’t tie them up, they will wake up and resume their routine. Lethal actions are faster and safer. The game never forces you to use either of them nor it has consequences narratively. Non-lethal actions have their practical uses in certain situations, but the choices are mostly self-imposed restrictions by the player for either completing extra challenges to earn badges or just role-playing. You can hide bodies in bushes or throw them into wells and water to remove them permanently. Distractions are skills that allow the characters to attract attention, lure them to certain positions so it gives you time and opening to either take enemies out or slip past them. The 5th character has a slightly different, powerful skill set aside from offense and distraction. One of them is a “link” that allows 2 enemies to be linked, so whatever happens to one (like dying or distracted) happens to the other one. She can also take control of an enemy. The environment can be used to kill or distract enemies. Examples of these actions are dropping a boulder on top of their heads or putting off lamps and torches to lure enemies to light them back. Some levels also contain areas where you can leave footprints. If these footprints are within green vision cones, certain types of enemies will come and investigate your steps. Lastly, you can distract enemies with bodies. This is where the mechanical usage of non-lethal takedown comes into play. Upon discovering dead bodies enemies will immediately raise alarm and take more aggressive behavior. Discovering a knocked out person, they will just untie them and investigate around the perimeter but don’t raise alarm. All the elements combined create a fun, challenging gameplay. There is satisfaction in seeing your plans executed successfully. While it requires a lot of trial and error, the game has an easy quicksave and quickload option where you can easily access the last 3 quicksaves you made. Combined with outstanding level design, and even denser enemy population compared to previous games,  is a worthy successor to the long line of commando-like games. My main criticism is the fifth character’s abilities are too powerful and make trivial of most areas she’s in. The other 4 feel fairly balanced and each brings and complement each other, so the balance of the game can feel off whenever she’s usable. None encountered and ran 60 FPS perfectly in any situations.Overall the game looks good. It’s not fantastic, but it is an improvement over  by a huge margin. Character models look good at the distance you're looking at them from. they are animated well especially in cutscenes. Environment looks great and there is a good amount of variety from towns, to swamps and train bridges. There might be some spot on rocks or ground where the texture looks low resolution, but mostly the game looks good.The game sounds crisp and well-done. Several characters wield different weapons and their sounds are noticeably different, footsteps react to the surfaces you’re on and the ambient sound effects are spot-on. The named characters are well-voiced, but NPCs can feel samey like there are only 4 voice actors to fill the whole game. It can feel a bit jarring because there are at least 2 dozens of enemies on the map. Music is fantastic. It really depends on how you like western cinema music but the tracks are great in my opinion. The story is a typical wild west revenge story. It’s nothing special, but I like the chemistry and camaraderie between the characters. Desperados 3 is a fantastic stealth game, and improved upon every aspect of its predecessor. It is polished, challenging, and importantly fun. The gameplay is flexible, replayable and filled with extra challenges if you crave more challenges. If you love the stealth genre, this is the game for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Desperados III is among the best games i have played this year and saying that after beating 125 titles during that timeline with few of turdaloos which did remove from the account.If you loved Shadow Tactics or even liked it, Desperados III will feel the same for the most part while feeling improved variously in gameplay. _childDocuments_.review: Mimimi nailed it again. Everything about the game is great...so far. If you have played Shadow Tactics and liked it, this would be a must-pick. It has more 'personality' than the Shadow Tactics, which shows the devs are learning from their experience. If they can keep this up, we may find even better games from them next time. So what does this game have:+ Beautiful characters with unique abilities (just like commandos or shadow tactics). + Varied environment and interactive world. Learn to observe, adapt, and execute moves to dispatch enemies or get past them without being seen.+ Objectives (i.e. fast run, don't do dis or dat) make the missions more challenging if the higher difficulties aren't doing much for you.+ Beautiful character interaction makes the world feel lively and not just "okay, going there," "Okay sir," "Can't do that sir," type deal!+ Some missions will surely remind you of missions from previous titles like Commandos 2, but with a different twist to them. Day-night cycles included.+ Pathfinding for each character is great. I had occasional trouble with this in Shadow Tactics but here they ironed it out just right.+ The Slow-mo mode makes action theatrical and fun to watch.+ The end of the mission gives you a full playthrough of your movement and action on the map, showing how you executed each and every move. This is perfect for those who want to hone their skill and curve out the flaws in their plan for a perfect run. First time I've seen (correct me if I am wrong) this in this genre of gaming. The other really good version similar to this I've found is in Digital Combat Simulator with a separate software called TacView, but that is a whole different genre (simulation). Seeing the devs put effort into making this show great care and dedication for casual and hardcore gamer. + Music is..well western style as you would expect. It's a like or hate scenario with this one. Overall great composition that draws you in but nothing too fancy that your ears would have orgasm. So far I have not come across serious bugs, crashes or something along those lines. Game runs smoothly. Now to hope that Mimimi will deliver us a new game with even greater potential and expanded universe than this. Perhaps they will make a sequel to Desperados III, or come up with a whole new franchise of their own, or perhaps continue the story from where Shadow Tactics ended.

_childDocuments_.review: Desperados III is one of the best games I've played in a long time. I pretty much loved everything about it! When it did end (after about 30 hours of playing) I felt entirely satisfied although if you are a completionist that is only the beginning of this wild journey that spreads out it's Sudoku-like strategy goodness across 16 intense and fun-filled levels! Go play, you won't be disappointed. 9/10!

_childDocuments_.review: Desperados 3 is the second Stealth Strategy game from Mimimi´s 4 games on the genre, and you can feel what they learned from the previous one. Despite the name it´s a short of pre-quel to the classic series, which already had 3 parts. But don´t let that name THQ probably forced, this is a stand alone game and you don´t need to know the series to enjoy it.The level design is fantastic, and there´s a lot of detail all wrapped with fantastic lighting, the game looks amazing. The puzzle nature of this genre is very well balanced, and with patience you always get that "eureka" moment, and then the satisfaction of excecuting it. The characters are fantastic and their interactions really enjoyable, even when the story is a little basic and weak they make it work. And as for difficulty, there´s always the badges, some are easy some are devilish, but overall it´s more welcoming and forgiving to players than their first game on the genre, Shadow Tactics.In most fronts (except story) it´s an improvement on ST, and you can feel the love Mimimi had for this super nitche genre that it´s quite frankly very underrated. If I were to have a criticism it would probably be on the DLCs, it´s really just for people eager for more D3 with a weak story and not that interesring maps. The Baron Challenges are far better despite recycling maps. Overall another fantastic game from Mimimi, I rate it 100% chance of 100% chance that I cry tonight once again thinking about Mimimi not making any more games. YOU WERE THE CHOOSEN ONE MIMIMI!!

_childDocuments_.review: For some reason these viewcone-dodging stealth puzzle games always get my heart rate up, more than even most FPS. And this is one of the best, for sure. The story is full of all the usual Western cliches, but it's fun and knows what it's about.And yeah, it's so very satisfying to play. What could easily have been a tedium of identical takedowns, feels instead like each new set of guards is a completely different puzzle, well-thought-out and requiring new tricks and timings. And it's difficult enough that even though I *know* there are plenty of ways to navigate the maps, sometimes just finding *any* solution that works is a great feeling.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Great game, worth the buyWhen it comes to gameplay, Desperados 3 is much the same as its predecessor, Shadow Tactics. Don't expect any major new features. Isabelle is the only character with abilities veterans won't be familiar with, but then again, why re-invent the wheel?Where this game shines is in the areas of level design, atmosphere and content. The story mode consists of 1 tutorial and  missions that vary in length, but all were somewhere between 1 and 2.5 hrs for me. _childDocuments_.review: I want to start off by saying that I usually hate games that make you control multiple characters. I knew coming into this game what I was getting myself into, but even so I just couldn't get myself to play the game for a week or two after I had done the first (real) mission. The second I had to control a second character I just wanted to quit the game and never think about it again. Still, that week or two where I was not playing the game I was constantly thinking about the amazing sound, voice acting, graphic style and the small bit of gameplay that I had gone through and what the game might offer if I just force myself to play it for a little longer.Fast forward a week or two and I finally sit down and get myself to play the next mission, this time telling myself that I would go through that mission no matter what. Well let me tell you that was one of the best decisions I've ever made. Not only did I start enjoying both the gameplay and story, but I basically got addicted to the game. Even though I was playing on hard and sometimes got stuck it usually just got me more excited and determined to finish that mission. It's been a long time since I've actually played a game to enjoy it and not wanting it to end, instead of mindlessly rushing towards the end.If you enjoy the tactical stealth genre there is no question that you will enjoy this game. It provides a good bit of challenge on the higher difficulties and has some nice extra challenges in each mission if you want to challenge yourself even further. For those either new to the tactical stealth genre or are like me that either don't like the genre or don't like controlling multiple characters; try it. If you are playing it for the gameplay I very highly suggest playing on either Hard or Desperado difficulty as it becomes a completely different game. Other than that - just enjoy the ride as I have.

_childDocuments_.review: I liked it. I had recently finished shadow tactics and was afraid it would not have enough original content. Happy to say the gameplay is different enough to make this enjoyable. The level design is very intelligent, I like the fact that the game allows you many opportunities to fire your guns, even though it is a stealth game. *minor spoilers about game mechanics below* Your ammo is 'limited' in theory though there are many ammo drops around the map which makes it not be a bottleneck at all. I also like that every gun is different and has its specialized usage. Kate's gun one shot kill silenced and short ranged, cooper's gun medium to long range but just as loud and Mcoy's gun a sniper rifle(heh, a silent sniper rifle, makes it unnecessarily OP, you could have added more sound to that) and hector sawed off short range shotgun that blasts and kills many enemies. Too much talk about guns which is one of the many mechanics and it is not even the most important since this is a stealth game.The story is quite nice as well. The dialogue is a bit hit and miss, the 'forced conflict' between your characters that is meant to create humor does not always land for me. The western atmosphere is not done super well. There are as many women gunmen as men gunmen, I don't mind that and in fact it was done well enough. What I do mind however is the choice words for cursing, I do not think they used to say wtf in the ancient west.Overall I liked it a lot, it's a no brainer on a sale and a fair deal on full price.

I really enjoyed that last stage.- The Baron Challenges was fun to do after finishing the base story (I only played two though)Cons:- Few stages. _childDocuments_.review: I recommend both Mimimi Game's Shadow Tactics: Blades of the Shogun and Desperados 3 as excellent additions in the stealth RTS genre, in line with the memorable Commandos series and Spellbound Entertainment's Desperados 1 and 2.Upon first playing Shadow Tactics and Desperados 3 it might feel same-y to its predecessors with their same-y view cone mechanics, but if you made the mistake of trying to replay the Commandos or Desperados 1 & 2 for the sake of comparison, you’d lose a lot of the nostalgic reverence you had for them because ST and D3 does improve a lot in terms of both gameplay, and presentation.If you have never played one of these before: in every level/chapter you load into a relatively large map with guards whose locations and patrol paths are predetermined, you are given a certain combination of characters with their specific toolsets to play with, and you basically spend most of the time avoiding the guards’ view cones, while utilizing your characters’ toolset to remove/distract the guards in order to reach the objective’s destination on the map to progress (with tons of quicksaves and quickloads in between).I love the optional challenges given after the first completion of a level, which are a great way of incentivizing repeat plays with different strategies and goals in mind. Though you do lose a lot of the level replay incentive upon finishing all the goals, there’s still a fair amount of entertainment value in a game without infinite replayability.Compared to its predecessors, ST and D3 have optimized a more streamlined control scheme for the modern era with character abilities accessible with asdfg/qwert keys (customizable in options), as opposed to Commando’s insistence to use the entire alphabet list. Characters and abilities feel as fun and well balanced as they were, with good map design which gradually becomes more challenging. I remember being able to cheese Desperados 1 by revealing your position on a rooftop and unloading your party’s bullets on all enemies who climb up a ladder 1 by 1, severely limiting ammunition for guns in ST and D3 was a good call.Both ST and D3 makes great use of their respective time period settings (Edo Japan/Wild west) beautifully, with well-detailed levels, decently likeable characters and engaging story. It isn’t particularly fair to compare the visuals to games from two decades ago but it does have gorgeous visuals, with Shadow Tactics: Blade of the Shogun being the stand out in particular, probably because its Edo period setting allows for more prettier architectural designs and environments compared to the stereotypically brown dusty aesthetic of the Wild West or the olive-green military bases aesthetic of World War 2. Love the big city night levels in both ST (Matsuyama City) and D3 (New Orleans) in particular.

_childDocuments_.review: Thanks to its attention to detail, fun mechanics, memorable characters and fun dialogs, Desperados III is a stellar entry in the real-time tactics genre that's faithful to the original, with finely tuned stealth action. Picking apart patrol routes is addicting, even after many blunders. And the presentation is quality, with detailed towns and bayous on top of some great music. It is hard to say which of Mimimi’s two games is better, but Desperados III offers plenty to sing about.

I would recommend this game above any else that I have played, and highly encourage anyone reading this to buy it as soon as possible.

_childDocuments_.review: Welcome to "Shadow Tactics 2: No Guns Allowed"!There are other much better reviews that outline what I don't like about this game but let me summarize it for you:1) Guns have limited ammo. I can deal with that. What I can't deal with is the low amount you are allowed to carry. Would it have been too hard to give each gun their seperate chamber? Or too easy if we had more?2) Guns have cooldown. You are forced to go the stealth route. No quickly shooting three guys that inconvenience you. Nope.3) The skills are almost carbon copies of the ones in Shadow Tactics. Cooper has a Ninjato (Knife), Shuriken (Throw Knife), Throw rocks (Coins) and has two (wow) guns that share ammunition (Whole 8 shots! How generous /s). He probably doesn't have bandages because that would be too obvious.I thought playing a younger John Cooper would be a neat idea and it is. In theory. But if you take pre-existing characters and change them because they wouldn't fit your contrived stealth game otherwise than why not just create a whole new cast in the first place?Nostalgia makes a lot of money and this game is not worth that money. At least for the price they are asking.Don't get me wrong. The game is good. And I would like to play it eventually. But I will wait until the price is lowered. Because to me, this game is not fun. There is nothing "Wild" in this West. Please give players the option to go loud because that's what made the original so great. Maybe introduce a skill tree where you can tweak your characters towards a certain play style and watch them grow as they are becoming the bunch of badasses I know and love from the first game.But for now I will play the first Shadow Tactics again. The gameplay fits so much better with ninjas against muskets.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly one of the most entertaining stealth tactics games I've ever played.The controls and mechanics are so crisp for executing a synchronised plan, it never stops being satisfying when you line it all up and trigger a domino chain that takes out half a dozen guards out of commission before any of them can raise the alarm. Lots of effort has clearly gone into the QoL side of the controls so that executing your plan isn't a far bigger obstacle than thinking up the plan in the first place.The story and voice acting are also great fun. It's all very classic western; avenged family, train heists, showdowns in the church yards. Full of tropes you'll know well, but done sublimely well so you can just enjoy the ride rather than roll your eyes.It's got a good pacing to the progression too, there's not only a goodly number of mission missions but they're also generally very distinct from each other, with new enemies, challenges, tools and combinations of circumstances introduced all the time. So you don't end up with the feeling of just going through the motions of doing more of the same waiting for a new mechanic to be introduced.

The cinematics for the story are short, but keep you invested and are filled with shock factors that really carry the story, I never found my self predicting what was going to happen next. _childDocuments_.review: And so it ends. After all main missions, all challenges and all dlc missions, this game has given me all it gots. Now, we're going to compare it a lot to the first Desperados, which I played over and over again in my youth.+Everyone has rope (except Kate) and can carry bodies. Practical that you don't have to use two specific characters to do the other.+Ammo is limited. Good choice since guns were and are tad overpowered.+Environmental hazards. Sand leaves footprints, water makes noise. And chickens. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ chickens.+Guard houses are a nice compromise; you can forgo stealth if you are ready to tackle extra guards for it. I for one preferred sneakier playstyle.+Story is plenty good, if maybe short, and characters are intriguing. With what little screen time he has, Frank is pretty fascinating villain.+Voice acting. It's plenty good. And not only do characters have dialogues during a mission, they have unique voice lines on missions that reflects their current situation, like when everybody has a hangover. Same goes for enemies; when they're bandits, they'll shout death threats, when they're deputies they call you troublemaker. This keeps the voicing fresh.+Unique enemy types. One won't follow lures and other is immune to Kate's seductions. Pairs and patrols share their interactions.+When I first tried Challenge mode, I hated it. But after completing the main story, I gave them another go and found the  variability satisfactory.-Decrease. There's less player characters, enemy types, character skills and levels than in the first Desperados.-Characters aren't unique enough. In the first game, everyone had a firearm and 4 other skills which were more or less unique. Some even had more than one way to use a specific skill. In addition, characters had unique strenghts, like only two characters could carry bodies, only two could use machine guns, only Cooper could climb and so forth. This brought variety to the game. Now everyone has lethal/knockout melee (Kate only has knockout) and can tie (not Kate) and carry bodies, 3 characters has healing as skill, Cooper's 5th skill is, (drum roll) another gun. This would have been better if devs would have complemented characters with more one-of-a-kind strengths and weaknesses.-Only 4 enemy types, with 2 having a female counterpart. In the first Desperados, a new enemy type appeared nearly every level. It was good that the enemies we got had their unique gimmicks, but there was room for more. Where were the fat mexicans and instakilling demonios?-Civilians were heavily nerfed. I barely noticed them being in the game.-By the end of the very first mission, I decided not to pursue any of the badges. They seemed a tad annoying for my tastes. Especially the speed runs.-DLC missions did not bring anything new to the game. They were just missions like any other.*Cooper, Kate and McCoy sounded nothing like they did in the first game. This was bad at first, in time my ears adjusted. I can accept that they were younger in this game since it's a prequel.*While I liked the character of Isabelle, I did not like that she was a real witch with real supernatural powers. Would have been fine if it was hinted she was, but I think mind control and connect were too over the top for the spirit of the game.*The game warns you not to try Desperados difficulty on first playthrough. Well I did, and I think that's how the game should be played.  *I would have liked more references to the first game. Kate sucking at poker at first when she later becomes professional cheater was a nice detail,  but devs missed a chance to implement more.Overall, this is a very good Desperados game, and I'm satisfied with what we got. It is not, however, as good as the first. And now that I'm through with it, I don't think I'll replay any of the missions, one playthrough was more than enough.

_childDocuments_.review: Desperados 3 is the prequel to a classic series of tactical stealth genre which thanks to Mimimi Games, has been successfully revived, and just like Shadow Tactics, Desperados 3 is an incredible game.👍 +Tatical stealth gameplay done perfectly right. +Fantastic soundtrack+Missions are long and offer multiple ways of being tackled.+The main cast is nicely voiced.👎-The main story is pretty much the average revenge story.-The variety of objectives does get repetitive around half the game.Desperados 3 shows us the story of John Cooper and how he met his band of misfits made of Kate, Doc Mcoy, Hector, and Isabelle. Each of the characters you meet has their own issues to deal with and as you progress through the game you form a bond with them. John's main objective is to get revenge on the person who killed his father and he'll do whatever it takes. It goes pretty straight forward from here with the usual, arguing, disbanding, and making peace again with one another of his group mates and there really isn't anything that will shock or impress you. It's a standard story of revenge and comradery but even in its simplicity, you slowly start to like one if not all of the characters in large thanks to the good voice acting. I personally liked Doc the most. Don't buy Desperados for the main story. It's not what it was made for but who knows, we do lack simple cowboy stories in games these days and you might enjoy it a lot more. Story rating: 7.5/10If you've come for the gameplay well you're in for a treat. Desperados 3 does tactical stealth almost perfectly, so good that I just can't imagine what else can they cook up in future games to impress me. If you played Shadow Tactics then you know what to expect from Desperados 3 and if you haven't then what the hell are you waiting for? Just like their previous game Mimimi has managed to revitalize a dying genre which was no easy task. You're playing as 5 unique characters each with a set of abilities that will help you kill or knock out enemies in your path towards the objective. Enemies around the map and even the level design is masterfully crafted so that you'll always need to use your available skills and tools. For example, Doc Mcoy which as I've mentioned is my favorite character, can easily dispatch enemies from far away and quite silently with his sniper rifle or you can throw a decoy to attract and separate wandering guards from the rest so you can silently dispatch him. I can spend all day writing and describing each characters unique skills so I will just say this: not only you can freely use each skill but the game also has a number of hidden and fun ways of using some of the skills you have at your disposal such as combining them with the other characters or even allowing you to carry out multiple attacks at the same time with the showdown mode. Each level takes around 1 to 2 hours to complete depending on your skill and whether you're going to play stealthfully as it should be played. Playing this loud is a waste of time in my opinion but you are indeed offered that option. I also did mention that the objectives are quite repetitive after a while seeing how this game is a 30+ hour long however you are given free reigns on how to proceed with the entire map minus the tutorial parts and some small linear missions. You're also going to be rewarded at the end of each level with a star-based system where it shows you what you could've done to achieve those special objectives. I personally would've loved to see them all the time but I suppose this is a good way to increase replayability. Overall the gameplay offers a lot and it's fun, hard, and a lot of times nerve-racking which requires a huge amount of patience but I just could not put it down. Fantastic experience.Gameplay rating: 9.5/10The moment you boot up the game the first thing you'll notice is the fantastic main menu theme and just like that, you'll know the rest of the soundtrack will be great. It's a long game, no doubt, and many songs will be repetitive but not once did I get bored with them. The voice acting is another great aspect and it's honestly what makes the story tones less boring. Every character in the game is voiced and the main cast does a fine job at immersing you in the experience. Their banter is especially funny and great during missions. As for the other sounds, there's absolutely nothing negative to talk about. Guns, enemies talking, environmental sounds are all perfectly fine. Audio rating: 9/10Visually the game looks pretty decent and the way the levels are constructed and enhancing the gameplay is top-notch. Sadly the textures and on rare occasions, the lighting effects are not that great. They do not ruin the experience at all though it felt weird how those huge mountain rocks passed Q&A as they were quite in your face and looked pretty bad. Luckily these occurrences are rare and overall graphically speaking the game looks fine and the missions are very varied from deserts to crowded cities. Performance is perfect, at least on my machine. There were no frame drops ever and besides some minor enemy AI bugs I had no problems playing the game. Graphics, performance and tech analysis score:  8/10I don't know what to expect from future Mimimi games but along with Shadow Tactics and now Desperados 3, it's clear whatever the developers make I'll be there day one. Desperados 3 is a masterpiece in gameplay and hopefully, I'll see the same characters again in future sequels. Buy the game at all costs.

_childDocuments_.review: The best example of a Real Time Tactics game I have played since the original Commandos franchise which began in the late 90's. The developer Mimimi games have created a RTT gem. Their first RTT game was Shadow Tactics which was a great homage to Commandos series though a little rough around the edges but they have taken Shadows Tactics DNA and refined it to create Desperados 3. The game play is so addictive it's a game you don't want to put down. It's challenging especially on the hardest difficult "Desperado" but the sense of achievement when you crack a difficult mission or scenario is fantastic. I can only compare it to the feeling you get when you defeat a tough boss in Dark Souls, you feel so good about yourself like you're a genius. The game controls are very intuitive and the levels are super detailed, really high end visuals for a RTT. it's a very accessible game easy to learn but a brilliant challenge to master. The game is well worth it's triple A price tag due to having 50 hours plus of content especially on Desperado difficulty which I played it on and for it's high quality production. The game works perfectly I haven't experienced any bugs on PC and the game is extremely well optimised, my I9-9900K/RTX 2080TI machine can run the game at a rock solid 120 FPS at 4K resolution. I am now tackling the bonus challenges which are still keeping me playing even after spending 58 hours on the campaign missions. The story is good if nothing exciting but works for the narrative. There are only 4 different enemy types including guard dogs, I would have liked to see more variety. The voice acting is excellent with some funny one liners from enemies. The sound effects are high quality and the music is catchy I would usually turn it off to concentrate in Commandos for example but this soundtrack is worth listening to. Shadow Tactics came close to taking the Commandos crown as the king of RTT's but with all due respect to the 90's classic, Desperados 3 is the new king.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: thumbs down because D3 level design is apparently doing away with the ability to sneak through or punch through the clockwork, and instead seems to force the player to disassemble the clockwork gear by gear, the tedium of which is described well in this review: I loved Shadow Tactics so much that I put 400+ hours into it. People say Desperados 3 is a re-skin of Shadow Tactics, so why the thumbs down?It’s because the level design of D3 is contrived and amateurish compared to that of ST.As I wrote in my review of it  when you become more advanced at ST, you can afford to leave more guards alive on the map because you’re stealthy as a ghost. Or you can just become a tornado of destruction and rapidly obliterate everything, while still being stealthy enough to avoid alarms. Between these two extremes is the sneak-wait-kill-repeat approach, which in my opinion is the beginner’s approach to the game.D3’s tendency to make everyone always take this beginner’s approach is caused by pervasive use of complex cover formations, layered and spread out over large distances. This means you will have two, three, or four guards all watching each other, and one or more of those guards will be watched by another guard that is far away, and sometimes that guard is watched by another guard, etc.There’s a big piece of evidence to support my assertion that D3 level design only accommodates the sneak-wait-kill-repeat play style, and that is Isabelle’s connect ability. I was getting pretty frustrated trying to play D3 until I realized that these multi-cover guard formations are really designed around Isabelle.Her connect ability is tailor-made to address these formations, because when two guards are watching each other, you need to kill them both at the same time.Also, Isabelle’s mind control ability allows you to remove a guard from one of the complex cover formations, making it more manageable.I think the mind control ability captures the essence of the thinking that led to D3’s level design: why does it really matter where the guards are placed, if the player has the ability to just move a guard anywhere they want?The guns mostly just feel awkward. Kate and McCoy’s are a bit better, but the maps are just too crowded to use Cooper’s and Hector’s guns without setting off alarms. The obvious answer to this problem is to simultaneously kill everyone in hearing range of the gunfire, but then you’ve got those distant cover formations, which just makes the whole thing seem awkward, forced, and even cheesy, rather than the smoothness that I found so pleasurable in ST. Concluding thoughts… I heard something about Mimimi working with a certain “narrative development and consultation studio” known for their political ideology. I also noted there are some lines in D3 which seem to imply that Isabelle has a sexual interest in Kate. Whatever, I couldn’t care less, but when the game also seems to be lower quality than ST in level design, it all starts to have a familiar stink to it.
_childDocuments_.name: Desperados III

_childDocuments_.review: + Awesome real-time tactics mechanics+ Stealth approach is more than rewarding+ A huge amount of the content+ Five different well-written characters with useful abilities that the player has to use wisely depending on the situation+ A captivating story that is interesting to follow+ Thoughtful level design+ High replayable value+ Challenges that are really interesting to complete- Some levels take a lot of time complete, around 2-3 hours- Reloading saves feel tedious sometimes - Repeating character replicas can become a bit annoyingPlaying Desperados III was a really exciting experience for me because the original game was one of the first games I have played on PC when I was a kid back in 2001. As you can probably guess, gaming then was completely different than it now - we never had a library with thousands of different games, usually, we were limited to a few games, that we had to replay again and again and again. I never had the luxury to rage quit the game, so I had to think a lot of how in order to progress with the story.And Desperados was my first ever experience with real-time tactics games and I will never forget those moments. Constantly saving and loading, trying different approaches, consulting with my schoolmates - it was awesome. The reason why I am telling you all this, is because Desperados III brought me exactly the same experience, same memories from my childhood and I couldn’t be happier in this situation. Everything that I used to love in the original games has been saved in this prequel, so if you are the veteran player, don’t you dare to miss Desperados III.Desperados III tells us the story about John Cooper, a rough bounty hunter who has to revenge for his father’s death. During his journey, he meets a company of desperate characters with their own story, motives, and the reason to stay with John Cooper. So, in terms of the story, the main goal of Desperados III is to tell the player how everything started and how John met his gang members. The game is presented as an isometric real-time tactic game, where the player has to control different characters in order to complete the level. Each level can be completed in a loud or in a quiet way, however, the stealth approach is much more rewarding and it causes fewer problems for the player. During certain levels, the player has to control only one character or it starts with one character, and then another character joins a bit later. Every single character has their own unique abilities that are hopeful during certain situations and the player has to figure out how to use them properly. The way the game introduces the new character to the player is magnificent: it starts with a short story of what happened to them and then, the whole level is dedicated to that character and it’s designed to be completed by using the abilities of this character. This kind of approach lets the player to learn the character and to understand how to play with him.My favorite part of the game is the design of levels - they are extremely huge and thoughtful, the developers made everything to let the player finish it in a lot of different ways using different methods, where the player can go quietly or go loud. Most of these levels take a lot of time to complete, around 2-3 hours and this can be a problem for some players, I believe. Usually, the main reason why it takes so long to complete the level is probably the mistakes that the player will do during the playthrough. Speaking of me, I was constantly spamming F5 and F8 buttons that are obviously responsible for quick saving and quick loading respectively, simply because there were always some enemies that were appearing out of nowhere, spoiling everything for me.After the mission is done, the player can check on the results of the mission: the map with the movement of the characters, the number of saves and loads that have been executed and how many enemies each character killed. For example, one of my games has 103 saves and I loaded the game for 79 times. I realized that the whole concept of the game and my approach to it didn’t change too much since I was playing it as a kid back in 2001: I kill one, maximum two enemies and then I do an emergency save just to make sure that I won’t be forced to do it again if I fail on the next pack of the enemies. I can’t even describe you how satisfying it is when you can’t understand how to fool the big pack of enemies and to bypass them and then when you finally find a solution. Every single enemy has a cone of their viewing area divided into two parts: a solid one closer to the enemy and a striped one, a bit distanced from the enemy’s eyes. The solid area is the place that has to be avoided by any means if you don’t want to be spotted by the enemy and the stripped area only lets the character move around the enemy in a crouching position. If the player will stand for a long period of time in the stripped area, the enemy will trigger the alarm. Desperados III has a huge amount of content, including 16 long missions and 5 challenges that can entertain the player for a few more hours. This game has a pretty high replayability value, because it really differs a lot when the player switches to the higher difficulty. Every single level has special badges and unique tasks that the player has to complete in order to get them and this is something that will make the player stay in the game for a few more hours. I finished the game on the normal difficulty, some of the missions I was able to complete on the high difficulty and when I finished the game completely, I instantly started it all over again to try it on Desperado difficulty. Frankly speaking, after finishing the game and knowing everything on each level, I found it much easier to play even on this highest difficulty.Desperados III has a pretty pleasant graphics, this game never tries to impress the player with it, but it just the does the job in the right way. The game has short cutscenes during the levels and between them, however, they are all made on the source of the game.  The soundtrack in this game is simply amazing and it definitely fits the atmosphere of the game. Every single character of the game is dubbed by the professional actors. My biggest issue with this game was repetitive replicas of each character which became annoying especially after loading the same save for a few times in a row.Desperados III is an extremely quality game that is definitely worth picking up especially if you tactical games heavily based on stealth mechanics or used to play Desperados games in the past. It can be challenging at first, especially on the highest difficulties, but once you get into the mood of the game, it will become much easier. The great thing is that it has pretty high replayability value and it’s interesting to try new approaches in completing the level.

_childDocuments_.review: - I used to be a huge fan of "Commandos" 1 & 2 when it came our 20 years ago... Since then, I was looking for similar strategy stealth games and finally found it in "Desperados 3"! The fact that it was well-reviewed on Steam made it a no brainer for me.- I personally really enjoy slow-paced stealth gameplays where you plan out every actions using logic from observations or eventually trial and error :-) Since I also like western themes it was a good combo and did not disappoint.- Most missions took me about from one to two hours and I enjoyed every last minute of it (completely lost track of time which is a positive). I only wish there were more included with the base game but I'm being greedy :-)- I had low expectations and really did not expect anything from the story. In the end I was pleasantly surprised. It was good enough for me to keep going, and grab onto something that was artistically speaking coherent & "believable" with even some twists in between that I did not always expect.- Using "showdown mode" also gave me oddly gratifying coordinated kills (really liked that mechanic).- Sound design passed my expectations- I enjoyed the cast of characters, the way they were introduced and the little depth developers added to them given the somewhat short storyline they were working with.- Good Job developers (keep it up)- Great strategy stealth game- Definitely was worth a buy for me (would recommend)- Very good replayabilityLastly, I'm a firm believer that an overwhelmingly positive review must contain at least a negative/ area of improvement in order to be legit :-) Thus, the only thing I would improve are the graphics in general. Again I'm really nitpicking, it's not a AAA game, it's a genre not focused on graphics, but it's 2020 and a little more character details (with better creative zooming options at hand) or dynamic scenery could be worth it.Hopefully Mimimi Games makes another title like this one soon!Following this game completion, I'm strongly considering buying their previous title of this genre "Shadow Tactics: Blades of the Shogun".9/10

_childDocuments_.review: This is exactly the case when all the stars came together at the only right moment, giving us a miracle. Incredibly talented developers from Mimimi Games, who created «Shadow Tactics: Blades of the Shogun», were called to work on the continuation of the legendary title Desperados, and, «unexpectedly», created a great product. And if in the nomination “Game of the Year” it is too early for her to win, still there is still a lot of time and serious rivals (we believe that Cyberpunk will be released THIS year, right??!!), then for me it is the best tactical game it will definitely be. The game perfectly understands the most important idea of the best tactical games - providing freedom of thought to the player, the absence of linearity chains that hamper the possibility of improving it. We once again find ourselves in the deadly Wild West, in the company of old beloved adventurer heroes, who are threatened by many threats, including wild gangs, dirty businessmen with their mercenaries, and flocks of loud, annoying hens. Oh, how deadly these noisy hens are, and those who strive to get the attention of a random patrol. The story here is told incredibly skillfully, a fully-fledged western is unfolding in front of us, in which great attention is paid to both global events and small details that enliven the surrounding world.Each huge mission of sixteen available is not only large spaces, but also an incredible amount of opportunities, and this is incredibly important. The plot of each mission is almost a separate film, with a well-developed exposure, competent development of the action and an explosive climax. The respect that the creators give to the iconic spaghetti westerns and classic American westerns is palpable, in the game you can easily find references to many masterpieces of the genre. The player can complete missions in various ways, although it should be said right away that at serious levels of difficulty you can’t run with pistols, you have to wait and plan. Planning here is generally important, because enemies always have an advantage in quantity, they are keen to respond to any wrong step by the player, so you need to use the entire arsenal of tricks - distraction, adjusting accidents, calculating timings, using all the characters' capabilities. The game is difficult, but it does not break the player’s neck with something intentionally complicated, but simply gives him opportunities for improvement. You really feel the growth of your skill right in the course of the action, which creates simply magical sensations of unity with the game. And for even greater variability, the game has a system of stars that make them pass missions with certain conditions (they open after the first passage), which makes them even more varied.With the naked eye, the warmth with which the creators relate to both their project and their players is noticeable. Every detail of the design is made with love, many easter eggs are hidden in the game, which the player may not even find, but if he does, he will feel himself in seventh heaven. You see, even secret scenes, which almost no one can possibly find, are worked out with manic thoroughness and attention - is this not an indicator of incredible love for your creation. Desperados 3 is a diamond that deserves the attention of all players; games of this scale are not released as often as we would like. A stunning well-deserved success and an unconditional recommendation for a purchase

_childDocuments_.review: It's the typical, dumbed down successor of an old series. The game removes everything that made Desperados 1 and Commandos great: Variety, creativity, and sandbox gameplay.You could play the mentioned games in any way and you always had multiple paths and options, including the option to be more aggressive.D3 restricts the player in everything. It's a puzzle game, not a stealth game. Your ammo is limited to remove possible offensive approaches, levels are very linear, and situations require specific skills in specific orders to be successful.In D1 you had to weigh your options. Lure the first guys with Kate, then kill 2 via knife throw, then a dose of Doc's balloon, topped with a stick of dynamite? Nah boi, that'd be too fun. Now you are forced to do the same 3 actions in the same order in every mission. Throw coin, set bear trap, whistle. Most skills are similar and a re-hash of Shadow Tactics anyways so it's always the same setup and routine.And what's with this voodoo crap? Desperados was not a supernatural, weird west, occult story just because the final boss in 1 was named El Diablo.It's a soulless 60$ re-skin (or mod) of Shadow Tactics, which had the same issues but where it was OK since it was their first outing in a long forgotten genre. Now was the time to remove all of the past's shortcomings, such as A.I problems, pathfinding or level design. But nope, the A.I has become even worse. They are now a hivemind legion. If you alert one enemy then the whole map will know where you are. Also, if context sensitive actions overlap than you'll have to switch between them, which is horribly indicated in the game, so you'll probably pick up an enemy 3x instead of actually open that one door behind the body. Every character has less skills than previous entries as well. Desperados 1 and Commandos are basically Splinter Cell Chaos Theory, while Shadow Tactics and Desperados 3 are the linear SC 1 and Pandora Tomorrow.You should check out this small game called Intravenous. It's more like Splinter Cell meets Hotline Miami with a touch of Commandos but it's fun and the A.I is more advanced than in this triple-A priced product.

_childDocuments_.review: I love Desperadoes III.  (I might love its predecessor, Shadow Tactics: Blades of the Shogun, to which it is so very similar, just a little bit more, but that's neither here nor there.)  Mimimi's stealth-tactics formula is immensely satisfying.  I love stealth, I love tactics, and I love Mimimi's level design.  Each level is like a puzzle made of smaller puzzles, each of which usually has multiple solutions.  That allows for a lot of player creativity and does a much better job of making me feel clever than a more traditional puzzle with exactly one solution where I feel as though I'm expected to read the designer's mind or guess what he was thinking.In short, Desperadoes III is very, very good and you should definitely play it.  My only caveats are that the controls can feel a little imprecise at times and that unless you are sufficiently clever you may occasionally run into situations in the later levels where, due the real-time nature of the game, you will have to perform a bit of quick finger gymnastics.  I confess I am not always sufficiently clever.  Fortunately, the game has extremely fast quicksaves and quickloads.

_childDocuments_.review:
On his epic journey through 1870s USA and Mexico, John Cooper will have to take responsibility for mistakes that have been made in the past. On his quest for redemption, Cooper joins forces with the runaway bride Kate O'Hara, shady Arthur "Doc" McCoy, the giant trapper Hector and a mysterious lady from New Orleans. They make their way from the mountains of Colorado to the heart of Louisiana, then finally to New Mexico, right back into Cooper's past.

You take control of this ragtag band becoming a highly functional group of unlikely heroes and heroines. The leader of his team is Cooper, drifter and gunslinger, who can kill quietly with a knife or take out multiple foes with his revolvers. Strongman Hector carries a giant beartrap and can slay the toughest opponents with his trusty axe. Cold-blooded bounty hunter McCoy likes to be methodical, using lures, knockout gas, poison syringes and a custom long-range pistol. Kate can fool almost any man with the right outfit and kill discretely with her hidden gun.

Combine your specialists to overcome tough challenges in many different ways. Plan your moves wisely and execute them perfectly in real-time to sneak past your enemies while remaining undetected.

_childDocuments_.review: A quick and simple review just to throw my thoughts into the sea of red.GameplayPlays a bit like a half baked pc port and it really shows when you look at the controls.This probably wouldnt have been that much of an issue if the targetting worked properly,getting some of the moves off was a pain in the ass and some dont even respond to the correctinputs from time to time. Another thing about the targetting, i hope you like tunnelvision,The targetting zooms the camera so far into your character you can see every individual polygon, but heyatleast itll make the inputs for your moves easier.And if that isnt enough the amount of times youre gonna get hit because youre locked into attack animationswill eventually frustrate you. And no, you cannot animation cancel attacks into a parry, that mightve been a massive redeeming factor for this game if it was possible.EnemiesEveryone complains about the AI being less than ideal, yet people do not mention themeat shield big boy enemies that usually have a wake up attack that can hit youeven though you are behind them, wich will deal about half your hp in one hit and staggerlockyou into death even on the easiest difficulty, there are also normal enemies fully capable of doingthis in the later stages of the game.Not to mention the lovely bosses with their invulnerability phases, very fun boss design there.EnvironmentI liked the environment, reminds me of running around looking in every nook and cranny forhidden stuff just like i did when i played the old dnd games on xbox. Lovely trip down memory lane.I actually dont have any gripes with it, except for the invisible walls spread sporadically out everywhere.MultiplayerSo peoples main point about this game being fun, is it being best enjoyed with friends. We'll you see if youare one of the unfortunate people out there you might get hit with a disconnection bug, and thats frankly alli can call it. Even though ive got good ping and a decent PC setup, though that shouldnt really factor in the slightest, i all of a sudden started disconnecting constantly when starting or joining lobbies. Sometimes i could get into one just to get disconnected during the loading screen when we were about to start with a mission.I wouldnt try your luck with this if i were you.End note?Just wait, please just wait with buying this game. It is the best thing you can do for yourself.There is no reason at all to buy this game for 40 euros or whatever the price is where you're from.There is frankly nothing that this game offers in its current state that makes it worth it, and i do notbelieve one or two patches will be enough to make it worth it either. Try your luck somewhere else.Or rather, do not try your luck ever again. Trust the negative reviews from time to time and just wait for more updates and content, rarely do these types of single/multi player games get worse with time.Side noteThis text format looks like ass, but i cant be bothered fixing it. Just think of this review as early access.

_childDocuments_.review: Early Adopter ThoughtsDon't expect another Dark Alliance game as release on XBoxImagine Vermintide meeting The Lord of the Rings: War in the North.In theory this could be a great idea, but here is why it doesn't quite work in this game. You will also notice these issues link together in the perfect storm1) Solo feels unbalanced - if you can't find players at a similar level you play alone and are unable to rez in boss fights etc.2) Most players were highest level after a week - Got the game but was unable to play until weekend of release. Big mistake as enemies are levelled with characters for all maps3) Inactive Player Base after a month - Good luck finding anyone!4) No Bots - If you've played Vermintide you will know sometimes it is a better option over random players5) Clunky, boring solo Combat - To me it seems slow and clunky, if they have an arrow sponge boss, get ready to yawn6) Irritating environmental effects - Warmth to combat 5 times in one map or you die quickly7) No progress for failure - Got fed up with Vermintide runs where you lose at the last hurdle...8) Takes ages to level up on lower difficultysIn all fairness the story map and characters are nice and the game looks and plays fine except for the above. Unfortunately it becomes more frustrating than fun.If you can put together a team of like minded people, I'm sure it would be a lot better

_childDocuments_.review: Dungeons and Dragons: Dark Alliance is possibly the worst game I've played all year. I jumped into it with zero expectations and still came out disappointed.Let's start with what I found to be the game's two most egregious issues: the AI and the difficulty scaling.The AI has to be some of the worst I've encountered in any game period. Enemies do not react at all to projectiles or any character that seems to be outside of their combat arena. Not only this, but even when standing next to them, the AI takes several seconds to even react to the player's presence, and even then, occasionally during combat will seem to forget the player's existence at complete random.The difficulty scaling works on two different extremes: you either play the recommended difficulty and melt everything you come across in seconds or play even just one tier above that and every encounter takes several minutes to clear while almost if not every attack one-shots you.Something that I haven't seen mentioned much in reviews posted prior to making this one is the game's feat system, which is about as dull as one could possibly make a feat/perk system aka it all comes down to is minor stat upgrades (ex. 10% crit chance).Combat is unsatisfying and incredibly repetitive, at least as the archer character. As the archer, you will be spending almost all of your time holding down the aim button and spamming the shoot button for about 95% of your time in combat since doing literally anything else outside of your two specials will quickly bring your max stamina down to 50% leaving you constantly starved for said stamina. In combination with the AI issues mentioned above, it feels like the game was not built with the archer in mind and that the devs really REALLY don't won't you to play as her.Combat in this game takes up about half of the gameplay. The other half is running through empty hallways, occasionally solving what I could barely even consider "puzzles" and grabbing dull loot that's likely only a minor stat upgrade compared to what you're already wearing.To add on to all of this, the game is super buggy. My personal favorite that my group ran into multiple times was a bug where whenever we wiped on a boss, we'd end up stuck on a loading screen as we hear the boss kill our respawned selves and thus freeze the game, causing us to have to restart the entire level.I'm typing all of this up in a rush on a late night juiced up on three cups of coffee. There are a myriad of other problems like poor animations, bosses reusing normal enemy models, poor sfx, horrific lock-on camera, etc, but I don't have the time nor patience to go into detail about them especially since what I did talk about at some length should be enough to get the point across. It's not like I'm getting paid for this or anything.Some might say that the game is at it's most fun with friends, but that could be said for everything including watching paint dry. If you're looking for a co-op game to play with your friends, then there are better places to spend your money and your hard drive space.

_childDocuments_.review: At this time, I can't recommend the game for a few reasons. - With the name D&D: Dark Alliance, it is implied that it is at least a spiritual successor to the BG:DA games, however it doesn't really correlate at all. It's one of those games where you have a lobby and pick a stage from there, much like Vermintide or Left 4 Dead, making what little of a story it does have mostly meaningless- The combat attempts to be souls-like, but is clunky and doesn't respond correctly most of the time. Also, even playing in modes designed for your character power level, you will be killed in 1-2 hits on some enemies that aren't even bosses.- The matchmaking isn't optimized. I was level 2 and matched with max level characters, allowing me to attain legendary level equipment, but not allowing me to gain any XP to level up. I understand the reason behind stopping power-levelling, however if I want to get XP, I have to play alone.What we wanted was a modern update to the Dark Alliance series. A good, simple D&D Hack N' Slash. What we got is nothing more than a generic time killer.

_childDocuments_.review: the difficulty is sporatic, the bosses are bland, the enemies' AI is on par with Alien: Colonial Marines, and the combat is button-mashy as all hell. Do not, and I repeat, DO NOT buy this unless you are DESPERATE for a Dungeon Brawler. There are so many games that do this better, and this does the Dark Alliance name a disservice. I'm sure it was rushed by the higher ups, and I don't blame the programmers at all for, what feels like, the most rushed bag of mish-mashed ideas.EDIT: Feel like I gotta elaborate on the difficulty and the combat. The enemies are either A: Childishly easy, who take 1-3 hits before dying and they can't do enough damage to kill you or B: Damage sponges who one-hit no matter what.As WhimsicalPlushie said, the feat system is bland as all hell, with basic stat upgrades being the peak of the system. In addition, certain characters feel more finished than others. Drizzt and Battlehammer feel fluid and playable, while the barbarian and archer are janky and, honestly, need a lot more work to make playable. To summarize, this needed another year in the oven and a whole lot more prep time to make this playable. Oh, also, the netcode kinda sucked during early review time, the bosses would kill us and then continue to kill us on the loading screen (causing a crash every time), and the archer is busted to all hell and back. 3/10, nothing feels good about it. at most, it feels neutral and passable.If you want a good dungeon brawler, either wait for the Dark Alliance remaster that's supposed to land on Steam by the end of this year, or tackle Remnant: From the Ashes, Outriders, Destiny 2, or Path of Exile/Diablo 3. It's unfortunate, but it's the reality we've been dealt.

_childDocuments_.review: It has bones, but arrived version 1.0 dead on arrival. Its design is pandering. It plays like a kids game, or a mobile game, often holding your hand with elementary school puzzles, terrain management, and platform jumping. A kids game would be okay it if were a kid's game, however it has a confusing dark tones regarding its subject matter, themes, and targeted audience of PC gamers and R.A. Salvatore fans. This game would blow my mind on playstation2 in 2004.  the gear grind feels basic, and RNG stats are uninspired. No micro transactions (good thing), but it still reveals loot drops like a loot crate game, which again, kind of feels out of place and really arcade/mobile for the themes of the game. Much of the set piece bonuses are just specific elemental resistances, but i've yet to identify an elemental damage theme by level with that would matter, which would make preparing an armor set for an specific level more meaningful. Sure, you can learn which levels have what enemies, but i don't see a real point in changing armor for the encounters when you can just stun lock the ai. Mundane gear can be transmogrified, but the Legendary gear can't be transmogrified. You start getting epic drops immediately, so after three missions, i was no longer wearing any gear that could be transmog to customize my style. in other words, my character in his best gear looks like my highschool "tacky day" on spirit week, and the gear is sort of out of theme for a grim dark tale in the great north of "Icewind Dale". My Drizzt Character has no hip bones and looks like david bowie in a tesla coil marvel super hero suit and yellow rubber gloves. My favorite outfit was his starting gear, but i can't transmogrify my epic gear.Levels are pretty., albeit pandering. They felt designed for a different game altogether, such as a souls-like, or a bullet hell game. AI logic doesn't know how to adapt to a terrain. so they can't follow you outside a certain aggro arena. You can't knock them off a cliff. The level designer seemed to work independently of any game play concepts.  Boss battles have no stages, no MacGuffin objectives, no strategy required, no witty banter or plot points. Bosses have the same move set as their lesser minions and can be stun locked just as easily. The hit detection feedback can be confusing, when you feel like you dodged something but get hit, or feel like you should get hit but dodged. Camera lock feels like it was designed for a different game. Stamina management feel like it was designed for a different game. The resting mechanic has little impact since you can run past almost every encounter if you reset before the ai responds to your presence. I say it has bones because some of the characters play style is under-cooked, but some of the characters combos feel fun and have a cadence/pacing to them. Drizzt is really fun to play when you unlock all his move sets. He's very mobile and it feels good to pull off a huge combo uninterrupted. I think this game was originally meant to be a "god of war"solo player game with drizzt-only campaign to honor the source material, since drizzt seems to be the most fleshed out with his combo attacks and animations. Somewhere along the line this was re-purposed into a loot crawl brawler with RA Salvator's name on it.  There is a chance for a redemption arc with patches and updates, maybe perhaps even mod overhauls if there were a community for it?  but if that happens, it would be probably 2023 or later before it would be worth buying on a reduced sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Do not buy this game.I am and Idiot, I bought this game despite all the terrible reviews.Don’t be like me. Solo Gameplay:+ Ok graphics+ Drizzt+ UI is pretty nice- All the levels are basically the same. - The monsters are spammy and will stun lock you, or body block you into corners.- Difficulty scaling is basically like the lottery. Completely RNG- There is no character customization aside from feats which feels like you’ll end up with all of them anyway.- Bosses are usually repurposed normal Mobs with more health- There are no new mechanics after the first level. It’s just the same stuff over and over. Bugs:- AI will just stop working- You’ll hit buttons but they will just not register .. no really. It’s worse than you think- Your specials will be consumed without triggering randomly- Character models will have gaps you can see through depending on equipped armor- Bosses will despawn randomly- Major issues with skills and mobs when verticality is involvedThis is not a comprehensive list of negatives, and bugs. This game is so frustrating it’s almost beyond words.If this was an early-acces game it might be acceptable but at this point the game is too far gone (they’re releasing DLCs). It’s fundamentally flawed, and they’ve had a long time to fix stuff, and they haven’t really despite their obvious efforts. I can’t imagine how bad this trash was at launch.If you’re looking for exactly this game but really good, Vermintide 2 is what you want. Go play that, no really. If instead you want something a bit more indy, and roguelike check out Barony. I’m compelled to finish this game, but we’ll see how long that lasts.Finally, look at these patch notes: They speak for themselvesEdit: Played through about half the base game levels with 2 of my gaming group and here's the list we came up with so far. - Voice lines aren’t synced across clients- One player canceling a cut-scene cancels it for everyone- Interactables don’t always become interactable when you get close to them- Crazy warping to boss when they activate - Occasionally, the character will just stand at the entrance and the game will not accept inputs.- Enemies falling through the ground- The characters say their kill lines when you break breakables- Poison plant aoe lasts even after the visual disappears- Character icons don’t show current gear- Catti-Brie can drink potions in very rapid succession. VERY rapid.- You can’t see the potion other players are drinking.- Special effects are very low FPS for some reason.- Even if a monster is frozen before it pukes, the acid will still appear on the floor- Gweni;laksdf;j (cat) doesn't attack training dummies- Boss voice lines are mixed really low, and spatial audio is way off for them. Catti-Brie seems like she was implemented completely different from other characters. She has a whole different set of bugs, like loading screens disappearing, the reward screen at the end of the mission goes away, etc. It's weird.

_childDocuments_.review: I got a few problems with this game.1. There's an annoying delay on some button presses, like when you open your menu, shop and character sheet screen.2. There's an annoying delay on item pickups that will sometimes make you come back to do it again because the loot just decides it didn't want to be picked up right that second.3. Combat is a bit weighty, and that wouldn't be a problem especially for the more beefy characters except there isn't much feedback and communication that you should be getting when you hit a goblin ( even that seems delayed).4. Combat can be devastating and satisfactory, but it also commits to that animation to do the attack, and there are only a few moves in your line-up that will allow you to react to an oncoming attack while you're the one attacking. I'm not sure if was trying to replicate the Souls combat style, but it doesn't really work for most encounters that are more unforgiving, and are often surrounding you if you choose to solo the dungeon.5. AI is like a trail mix bag if it also included melatonin and barbed wire. They stand around and do nothing if you are not in their immediate vicinity, and their damage can vary wildly depending on the difficulty you selected. I'm talking the difference between a tricycle and a 18-wheeler.6. Respawning is perhaps the dumbest I've seen in a video game. The party leader is the spawning point, so when you get incapacitated and decide to force a respawn, you at first get thrown back to the beginning of the dungeon, which sucks but the game sends you back to where the party leader is after 10 seconds. This is all fine unless the party leader is downed, and forces a respawn themselves. Excluding the boss fight at the end of the dungeon, all party members will get thrown back to the party leader's location, forcing the entire party to make the long trek back to where ya'll were last. 7. Disconnections isn't an unexpected occurrence in a multiplayer match, but when the games themselves are about an hour long with spongy trash and even spongier bosses even on easier difficulties, it just puts a bad taste in my mouth when  I can be disconnected even in a post game summary screen, and still lose all of my progress and rewards for completing the match (one of my achievements on the game turns out to be a farce because i lost connection at the very last second of the post game summary, I'm not kidding).Overall, it's a game that I can definitely see the potential to become a satisfactory game that most definitely needs to be smoothed with a steamroller. preferably if they can get rid of all the delays, breath a little more life to the monsters, and fix the respawn system they got, then i could see my self spending alot more time seeing what this game has to offer.

_childDocuments_.review: I normally don't review games, and definitely don't normally leave a negative review, but I just have to be honest for the people who are interested in the game.· I played this with a friend, and we didn't even realize there was a tutorial until we were reading the reviews.· Combat and movement feels very clunky. I had to change the camera speed to 100% so it wouldn't take me 5 years to turn around. You're basically limited to left and right for your camera. Up and down is very slow and very limited. Lining up for attacks is a 50/50. By the time your attack hits (Unless you're playing Drizzt and have a faster attack rate) there's a chance the enemy will move out of the way.· Enemies do weird amounts of damage. We did a campaign on a difficulty less than 50 above our power level. Mobs were easy, but the boss did some combo hit with no warning that one-shot.· Navigation felt off. Maybe it was just us, but it was hard to tell where we had already been.· AI is bad. If one of us got knocked down the enemies would just continue to target that person, leaving the other to do whatever. This really just made things easier because the other player could continue fighting their mobs before resurrecting, rather than having to fight more mobs.· In the settings, even though you have a cursor and the setting have arrows that appear to be clickable, most of the options require you to use your keyboard. This was really confusing for us.Honestly has a really similar vibe to Vermintide, but isn't nearly as good. I wanted to like this game, since I loved the Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance series as a kid. I wasn't expecting it to be like the old games, but I wasn't expecting to be this disappointed.
