_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like Dark Alliance. I really did.I've been playing D&D for several years now, and I've played the previous Dark Alliance games too. When I first started playing this game with friends from my D&D group, I was hoping for a fun, fast-paced co-op experience set in the Forgotten Realms setting. Unfortunately, things went sour pretty quickly.First, there are the bugs. I know the developers have been fixing many of these, but from the first session we played, my friends and I have experienced game-breaking glitches that wasted our time and even caused us to lose progress. Sometimes, early on, my character wouldn't change levels with the rest of the group after a boss fight. More recently, one of my friends didn't get credit for finishing a level at all. Issues like these meant we'd have to replay an entire level, something that we didn't enjoy having to do.That brings me to the second problem. The game is just not very fun. You control your character in third-person perspective, and have various attacks and combos you can pull off. The combos almost remind me of a fighting game. You can also level up to unlock new moves, and pick up better equipment while playing to increase your character's effectiveness. This all sounds fun, in theory. In practice, the majority of the combos don't really matter--gameplay generally devolves into using the few really short and effective combos, or just mashing the attack and dodge buttons until enemies die. It's sloppy, and not satisfying.Also, the randomly-dropped equipment is rarely good for anything other than being sold to a merchant. Even after finishing several 'chapters' of the game, my character was still using the same old, weak gear.And the chapters feel pretty long. Each chapter has several levels, and each level is about 15 minutes long, on average. It does feel like there's a lot of content, which sounds good at first, but it doesn't feel satisfying or exciting to play through. It feels mindless.I will say that the art style is very interesting to look at, at least. Seeing the game artists' take on well-known D&D monsters, cultures, and locales was one of the few highlights of my time playing this game. Reading the in-game lore collection was another. It seems the developers paid attention to the source material, and I appreciate that.I think the game would have greatly benefited from reducing the scope of the moves you COULD potentially use in combat, and the options of the loot you MIGHT randomly pick up while playing, in order to ensure that you'd always have a small number of fun moves and interesting gear that you actually WOULD enjoy using. Maybe reduce or even remove the items that differ only slightly in their statistics. And test out a smaller roster of available moves for each character in different areas of the game. Maybe even shorten the levels! It's possible this game just tried to do too many things and ended up doing most of them to a mediocre degree.Ultimately, though, as it is now, I don't think this game is worth your time or money--let alone that of several people buying the game to play co-op together. There are better games using the D&D license out there, and better 4-player co-op games as well.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me preface this by saying I really enjoyed the small amount of time I put into this game. That said, I can't recommend it. I come from the land of terrible free to play MMOs, so when I heard that this game was bad, I took it with a grain of salt, and I'm glad I did. It was not nearly as bad as I expected, and I was able to pass off some design flaws as a "D&D-ified" quirk, like how you have to stop attacking to get your character to turn around, as something like that would affect combat in the tabletop version as well (at least the way my DM played).First off we'll cover the good. The locations are stunningly beautiful. The writing feels very on brand for the different enemy races, and each mission is written like an in-character DM narrating (in a good way). I only played as the Ranger, and I enjoyed the combat, it was a fun mix of dashing around the battlefield and brute force stunning/fighting some larger enemies. Each fight you have to consider what enemies are attacking in what way and dash past some to kill one that is more dangerous. I think with a full group of 4, this would be an even more fun dynamic, however I only played solo so it got frustrating sometimes when a single enemy would wipe the floor with you from behind 5 others.Now the bad. The main issue is a lack of polish. After a while it can start to feel like you're doing the same thing over and over. Almost every boss is a very generic enemy that has more health and hits harder. The bosses that are unique have really weird gimmicky mechanics that feel almost like a chore rather than an epic fight. The gearing system feels awkward, it plays like a gearset-based MMO, where certain sets will drop in certain zones, but on the lower difficulties they really don't matter. And once you hit the higher difficulties, it becomes so hard that the only thing you can do is focus on gearing. If there were an open world I would love this style, but it's a mission based game, similar to Vermintide. As such the gearset system just doesn't feel right, and feels like a way to artificially inflate the endgame. It feels like you have to grind missions you've already completed just to have a chance to attempt the hard version. At least in an open I could be exploring while I power up.Overall it's not a terrible game. If you don't mind less-than-great games, I would recommend trying it. If you have a few friends who want to play, I'd definitely recommend it. But if you're like me and just wanted a fun RPG to grind for a while, this isn't the most interesting one.

There's no reason to expect an attack cause it just looks like it's getting up.The last boss can spam an ice beam that will stunlock you to death.Drizzt is absolutely busted, pretty early on he unlocks the ability to have 100% crit rate when he is behind an enemy and will outclass anyone in an online session.You can't sell junk equipment all at once, if you've amassed a lot of common gear, get ready to hold down your confirmation button for minutes after every few missions. You will stay locked on to dead enemies.Some enemies will drop loot, if you manage to knock one of those monsters into a hole, the loot will forever be stuck hovering above that pit, unreachable.Any loot left on the ground before a short rest will disappear after a short rest.Loot can seemingly spawn in any direction around an open chest. _childDocuments_.review: 16 hours between Wulfgar / Drizzt Solo and Multiplayer before deciding to put my 2 cents.First I'll start by saying that two main complaints are legitimate but pretty exaggerated.- Netcode does need work and diminishes the value of twitch mechanics which otherwise work flawlessly Solo but at the same time you're in a group so unless you're the type to scream "But I pressed the button!" and rage. It's mostly an annoyance right now and not bad enough to kill enjoyment of the game.- Enemy AI is indeed a bit derpy taking "Action Movie" turns to attack the player. This is most notable Solo. At the same time if the enemy were to aggro stick the player all at once I doubt it would be Solo'd above 2. Hero difficulty. Far as I've seen the issue with hitting enemies from range, esp bosses is generally fixed and in the end this isn't a competitive game. I've seen 5/5 star games where the AI is still easily exploited. Just play the game and stop trying to break it.- The meat of this game is it's combat and in that it does a great job. The aforementioned twitch mechanics work great. There are a lot of different combo types that take talent to use properly well as different ways to open into those combos. There's heavy emphasis on positioning, timing and whether or not to dedicate to certain attacks. Some attacks are slow and you should not use them at the wrong time or you will be punished. Don't put yourself in a corner then complain you can't dodge out like some. That's dumb.- Enemy Telegraphed attacks are spot on but janky Multiplayer. It's quite easy to see these attacks coming and when / if the netcode is fixed there should be no problems.- Character Building. Feats and Attributes don't amount to much. In general each character plays like they're intended. However Armor and keeping different sets is where you can get some customization and on higher difficulties it's pretty much needed to keep different sets based on encounters in the mission. ie Resistances, support health drops, Reflect Damage, Lifesteal, Condition Afflictions and sets based on boosting certain skills.- Graphics are Basic. Draw Distance is short for ground objects. Distance LOD and texture are Average. - Atmosphere is Good. Each map captures a unique and interesting environment.- Sound Effects are Average. - Music is Good. *When it's playing.The main thing that bothers me as a PC gamer is neglect for PC UI interface. Thankfully menu interactions are done outside of missions. However a lack of 21:9 support and re-bind on WASD is a problem. Maybe not you though. Overall there need to be about 20+ more graphic & config options going on here that are missing.If they manage to check some of these boxes which I imagine they will then I can recommend the game. It's not bad by any means and I've been enjoying it despite these launch flaws. It just needed more time to cook. If you're curious still and esp if you're familiar with NWO combat this is essentially a new and more in-depth version of that which you might find worth your time. Otherwise just wait for some of those improvements.Hope this was helpful.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been desperately trying to enjoy this game for the past 2-3 hours. I adjusted the settings getting rid of the annoying HUD so that I could feel more immersed, so I could just focus on the "hack and slash action-adventure" game that I was promised. Maybe it could be fun if they had taken the time to actually finish this game. The combat is laggy, unresponsive, does not flow and that makes it rather frustrating, (especially for a game that is supposed to excel at hacking and slashing). Up close hack and slash combat wasn't even the worst part I noticed, the worst part was trying to use projectiles. Drizzt's sword throw? Forget it, a pathetic move in the state it is in, it has no stagger impact, super slow, passes right through enemies as if they were bloody ghosts, you can just sit there and spam his projectile while the enemies stand there like monstrous vegetables.This leads into my next criticism, a lot of the enemies I encountered don't chase you if you're standing far enough away, even when you're throwing a blade at their skulls they just ignore you like everything is fine, they don't even try to dodge your attacks. If I throw a sword at someone's face I expect them to at least have a shred of a reaction, stagger backwards, hold your face in pain as you bleed, something like that is to be expected. Speaking of violence, sure this game can be bloody as it should be for an M rated D&D game, but I was expecting better gore detail, like limbs and heads flying from bodies as I cut down monsters.It's clear to me after only playing a couple levels that this game fails to satisfy in its current state of development. Really hope Dark Alliance gets finished in future updates, but I'm guessing that will take another year of "patches" to even get this game to the state it should've been on release. Considering how hard this game has bombed I'd say we all deserve a refund for those of us who payed 40-60 dollars, this game certainly isn't worth that much, maybe in the future when it is fixed it could be worthy of a 30 dollar price, but maybe isn't this moment, and at the moment I feel cheated out of 60 smackaroos.

_childDocuments_.review: After finally finishing the game, I feel like I can accurately provide a review for this game...rather than just a list of gripes an complaints. Let's start with the Cons first. Because that way we can just rip the band aid off. - Glitches and bugs. Enemies fall through floors. Bosses become immune and prevent you from finishing a boss fight. The shields off of key items don't drop even once you try to trigger them. Some.... well.... almost all of these incidents require you to restart the round. Others are minor and merely warrant you jumping off a convenient cliff to reset your character. - Matchmaking. I am lucky enough to have friends to play this with which make all the difference. Randoms wont sit through the wipes and the frustration. No matter what you do, they just wont. The game needs help from a bot support system. Also FOR THE LOVE OF GOD, untether the party to the party leader. That is the STUPIDEST, LAZIEST mechanic to include in this game. This isn't early 2000's. Lets move on from that. - Enemy hit boxes are purely suggestion and sometimes... they teleport. Yes. Teleport. And sometimes the Veerbog will redirect in midair from a flying belly flop to land on your face. -Linear and Redundant level design. The levels are quite linear with only the illusion of branching paths. And there really isn't a replay value. If you want to grind for gear, that is about the only reason to replay it. And now for the Pros. - This game is a good 40+ hour distraction with friends. Just make sure they have a good sense of humor. - The characters do play differently, but I would not recommend playing them outside of how they were intended. And yes, CB is broken as hell. Play her first :)- The game is challenging and unforgiving, but you can dumb down the difficulty level to your preferred liking. So overall, if you have friends and you like dungeon crawlers, I would try this. Maybe if its on sale, probably not at full price. The cons alone don't warrant the price tag. But I think if this is your genre, you will enjoy it enough to ignore its flaws.

_childDocuments_.review: DO NOT BUY THE DELUXE EDITIONIt's a classic beat-em-up brawler, nothing fancy.  It's fun for what it is, if a bit tedious.  It's meant to be played with others and I recommend doing so, as trying to solo your way through each level- while possible, can be mind numbing at times if not overly difficult.  As it is still new, there are some glitches that I, for the most part, can ignore and don't mind but some do make progression impossible, such as not being able to interact with ladders or portals just not working.  This can be resolved by returning to camp and restarting the level but these aren't small levels that you can bust out fairly quickly, they take a decent investment of time to do, making having to restart the level halfway through frustrating.Some of the bosses I feel could use some re-balancing, I don't mind having to absorb an attack that can almost nearly one-shot me (just don't get hit by it) but when I can one-shot a boss that comes after that one?  The damage that you deal out feels inconsistent at times.One of my biggest gripes is having pre-ordered the deluxe edition, I was expecting access to special, unique sets of equipment as advertised in the store.  Come to find out, they were skins.  This was not mentioned and I would not have purchased the deluxe edition had I known this.On the note of skins, changing the skins of equipment can slightly but randomly impact the stats of equipment without any consistency.  If you were to cycle through the skins you would observe that the same skin will produce different results, if any at all.  I personally feel that skins shouldn't alter the stats of equipment, it's a deviation from the cosmetic nature of skins.Anyways, great fun overall, play with friends, don't buy the deluxe edition expecting to get actual equipment sets

There are  of people downing entire dungeons (bosses included) as Catti without them even reacting to her shots. _childDocuments_.review: I reviewed this for  and gave it a 5/10. There's lots to love about the setting, the comedic asides from enemies, and some of the expanded movesets you can unlock for the four pre-made characters. But make no mistake: this is a broken game that will frustrate you and waste your time.Enemy leveling is incoherent: there's no way to tell whether a trash mob is going to fall over in a couple hits or tank tons of damage and potentially one-shot kill you. Hitboxes are nowhere near the models on screen. Gear and stat adjustments make no difference in terms of how you approach the game, which doesn't change at all over the course of 21 campaign missions + dungeons.The levels themselves are occasionally interesting but ultimately they're all linear corridors that will sometimes stall you with a fight in a wider arena area. Most of these, it turns out, are entirely optional - you can run through straight to the end of most levels without fighting at all if you want to.Bosses are boring - they're mostly repurposed, larger versions of the handful of enemy types you encounter ad nauseam through the rest of the missions, just granted huge health pools and additional magic attacks in some cases. Don't worry though, since they'll only occasionally take note of your presence, and at no point will they attempt to avoid any environmental hazards that might be in their area.This is just an unfinished, broken game. If you want to play co-op, pick up Vermintide, Deep Rock Galactic, or even Outriders.

While the plot is as straightforward as the novels it's based on, the voice acting, music and overall presentation largely stand out. Underneath the occasional glitch, the AI hiccups and lopsided balance, there is a game that is easy to pick up  with a very high skill ceiling. My hope is that people will give it a chance and support the better game that it could become.

Movement- overall movement feels bad sure, Hard to be too specific about it, but you kinda feel like your moving a truck, made even worse when your attacking, its like a guiding a truck to its targets and 'attacking' to slowly ram them. However a specific thing to note, you can only dodge forward, back, left and right,(M&K) you are completely unable to dodge diagonally for some reason. I mean it might sound like a small thing but it just feels wrong, my mind is all confuzzled after playing this garbage. I don't know where to begin or end. Its a lot easier if you just try out the game for yourself and experience it unfortunately.... watching videos helps but it doesn't allow you to experience the full '????' thats going to be going on. Camera- movement for mouse...... its horrendous, no... stupendous, horrendously stupid. Like many console port lazy garbage. You gave no care for how it feels to have simulated stick camera movement. For those who don't know what i mean by 'simulated stick camera movement'. imagine your mouse as the center point of a stick and you move it in the direction for the stick to move that same direction, THAT is not the same thing as a camera moving based on mouse movement. Infact i could swear that sometimes moving the mouse diagonally, didn't input at all and it would mostly just move the camera literally up, down, left and right. Controls/inputs-...................Jesus Christ, who slapped the default inputs together, was any of it thought out? lets just skip the usual controls, people change and put their own custom stuff for the most part anyway however lets address the things that you get taught in tutorial at least. Even after changing almost everything to what i could to be as comfortable as possible, because you could not do multiple key inputs or hold inputs. your left with gaping problems. First up to mind, though you can totally get by without it, 'lock on' hey... you guy over there, who thought pressing lock on with 'tab'(default), and cycling through lock on targets with left and right button(thats right left and right arrow keys) was good, you do realize.. the average person has 2 hands....  what am i supposed to do, slap the cycle target with my ♥♥♥♥? i mean sure if my left hand occupies my movement and my right occupies my camera..... guess ill slap it with my ♥♥♥♥ in combat, why not. But to change these buttons to a functioning set to my own customization? is that possible? OK so lets assume I like tab as target lock, what do i make my cycle target when everything around my fingers for movement are already taken(QEF123 lets say, there is also technically ctr, alt, shift, capslock, ZXC but ill admit they don't feel quite right to use in this situation AND as said earlier they are used for other things the game has, special attack, ultimate, team attack? block/parry, sprint, interact, pots/usables) and remember you cant have multiple inputs or hold inputs? WELL guess ill use mouse wheel right? wrong(bug? never seen a game not allow scroll wheel but here I am), scroll up and scroll down do not work. Guess ill stick to slapping it with my ♥♥♥♥ if i ever use it... Oh and another not really problem but small thing, because you can only scroll left or scroll right through targets. it means it actually does require 2 separate buttons, again not a problem usually if you have ways to account for it but the game doesn't allow for it thus the need for ♥♥♥♥ slapping or more realistically- taking one hand off an area and moving it to a new area, mid combat. Minor issue i know but was a lol.Combat- ..........................................lets get onto clunk. your attacks are static and often miss the target even when aiming directly at them seemingly because of a soft lock on system going on. Not a bad system usually, infact many games have this, its often fine, batman, spiderman, biomutant to name a few. But its definitely not a good feeling one in this, often makes you swing and miss, sometimes cant figure out which target your trying to attack and leaves you open to the next problem which is- Attack canceling for dodging/blocking are inconsistent- Sometimes i can cancel an attack for a dodge or block mid attack and sometimes i cant. why is this? i cant well figure it out at all. I've tried doing it early in animation, mid and late in animation. it sees to be a 30%(pulling a number out my ass because i don't really know but i'm sure you get the point) chance that it would, but i know for sure it is possible as it does happen? The attacks are just so static, enemies also static, yet if you look at the character and them closely it looks like they are just sliding along the ground like a capsule(those in the know, know what i mean) AI is missing the I, ♥♥♥♥ i only got through the tutorial played a bit more and i have 0 intention of playing longer. The controls alone were enough to make me question if i really wanted to do this any longer, in the end i made the decision to refund. I really feel that even if i used a controller for this, it would still feel just as clunky and dry. Proof is in the movement and attacks themselves. It feels like i'm attacking the air slowly, step by step while fighting the camera to move better to reach my target, that's already right next to me and me STILL looking directly at it, -somehow miss them completely, WITH SOFTLOCK systems i don't understand.... oh and given that aiming on controller sucks anus folds, i would imagine 'aim' shooting wouldnt feel any better than it did on mouse? on a mouse!!! it felt like crap, how do you do that? how??? HOW??? a mouse is made to point and click, even simulated stick camera sometimes feels passable.... Nioh and darksouls when they first came out didn't feel this bad. And they were baaaad on release in terms of specifically mouse camera/controls/inputs.The UI- Hmmm. Honestly not gonna say it was bad or good here. It was serviceable, did its job but it wasn't exactly eye popping, kinda ugly honestly. Doesn't hinder my experience any less than everything else did. Infact as you can tell from my low gametime, you can tell i barely had the time to delve into it, i got my first couple bits of gear and equipped them. Looked at stats and skills + feats, that was it. Grain of salt.Given the reviews ive seen i should have known better but i wanted to give it a try for myself.... holy crap was i wasting my time. There are literally people defending this game for being broken and saying give it a chance, it will be fixed later on other places, and in this review section there are some saying ignore the bad reviews. Hey good on you guys for enjoying the game, honestly. But this is not at all the $80 Australian worth game, spend elsewhere. Who knows, it might get reworked and fixed up later. _childDocuments_.review: As the fan of Robert Salvatore's works, I am extremely glad I finally decided to buy this game despite many negative reviews. The game might have had issues at launch, but many of them seem to have been addressed.What I enjoyed so far (please, note that I have finished 3 chapters solo and played only one of five characters):- Lore: I like to listen to the introduction narrated at the beginning of each act. It reminds me of playing the "Legend of Drizzt" board game (the D&D Adventure System), where I used to read aloud the introduction to each adventure. I like reading the collected tablets, scrolls, and quotes on gear. The paintings and reliefs also add to the story.- Graphics / World: The locations are truly beautiful and provide grand views. The level design is relatively simple but allows both vertical and horizontal exploration. Locations are not unnecessarily convoluted. I like exploring and discovering hidden chests, collectibles, and secondary objectives before continuing down the main path.- Combat: The combat system is fun, satisfying, and challenging. Even at level 1, my character had a wide array of moves and skills. Unlockable moves add to the depth of the system. Combat mostly feels fluid and natural. Moreover, almost all moves, even the ones ulocked at lower levels, have their use. Blocking, parrying, rolling, sidestepping, and jumping are present as well.- Progression / Leveling: While not overly complicated, progression is present. Feature / skill trees are not elaborate but provide choice.What I found strange:- Itemization: While the set system is interesting in terms of set bonuses and appearance, items seem to have random attributes. Two items with the same name may have different characteristics. In my opinion, it would be more logical if sets had a range of dedicated attributes.- Story: While the chapters seem to be connected in terms of plot, the final task or even direction of the player is not apparent. It is not clear what exactly the player is supposed to accomplish. AI: Sometimes, enemies are excessively idle, particularly when there are many of them. Some monsters seem to be waiting for their turn to engage in the fight. However, when playing solo, that is a welcome feature.- Occasional texture issues: Sometimes, the bodies of slain monsters are slowly drifting away. When landing on a object after a jump, the character may be floating in the air above that object before touching the ground.Overall, despite some flaws, I enjoy playing the game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just not fun in its current form, and it will need a massive overhaul before it ever is.  Soloing in this game is just plain awful, and I would not recommend.  Loot in the game is one of the worst offenders of just being plain boring and no fun. Gear is few and far between, and it is only awarded after clearing a stage and never during.  You can forget about ever equipping that new legendary sword that just dropped, unless you can successfully clear the stage.  The multiplayer for this game was basically ripped off directly from Vermintide 2, and it's plain that this Left4Dead style multiplayer does not work here.  There is no way in MP to search for sessions, or to even select which act you want to play unless you're the host. You're only options are either to host, have friends to play with, or join a random group. Finally there's the combat, prepare to be one hit killed by everything, as there does not seem to be any thought to enemy balance or tuning.  There are some seriously broken mechanics here, from enemies spawning and straight up not moving, to enemies being able to knock you to the ground and killing you before you're even able to stand back up.  I really wish these publishers would stop releasing these half-baked games, as this probably could have been a really fun game otherwise.

_childDocuments_.review: I don t know why all the hate. Bought this game for me and my friends and we are having a blast playing it. First of all some recommendations: 1) Fix the evade and the block buttons to the mouse, it will be easier to remember in the heat of battle. 2) My wife got dizzy when she reduced the movement blur... do not reduce the movement blur.3) Don t do the tutorial, you can learn the game on the run (yeap it s that easy).4) Play on level 1 (at least in the beginning). The game is punishing if you do not have some initial loot. Once you do a couple of runs you will be ready for other levels.5) Do not lock on targets. For some people the sudden move of the camera can cause some discomfort. I play with keyboard and mouse so I don t need to lock on enemies.6) Be afraid of Ice if you do not have Heat from a source. You will surely die without it.7) Use the resting places to increase the loot if you still have potions. On the first levels sometimes you can get a gold piece of equipment or weapon that can totaly make the difference in the next run.Ok, now that those bits of wisdom are out of the way, go and buy these awesome game. We love Diablo 2 and this game has vibes that resemble the atmosphere of that game plus the loot and the rpg elements are awesome.Graphics are fantastic, granted I do not play in 4k with a mega monitor but ♥♥♥ that. To me this game is beautiful. One of the main things I learned to love is exploration for loot. It is awesome to deviate from the linear path to fight some mini boss that is guarding loot or to avoid traps in order to get some chest in the middle of nowhere. Look for the clues and get some nice loot.And... evade... evade... block... evade. Even the biggest bosses can be evaded. its the nature of the game and it is the best mechanic ever created for a fighting game. Only wish diablo 3 has this.We have a lot ahead in our path but so far this game is not only way better than any mediocre review says but way better than the best reviews I ve seen. Give it a try. It took me a couple of years to get it due to paying attention to the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ reviews in steam from lousy players that go straight to level 9 without gear thinking they can beat the game with their wits and resourfulness and they die miserably trying. This is D&D. Your character needs to grow, needs to find awesome loot and you need to learn how to play the game before joining the ranks of the bad losers that wrote so many bad reviews. _childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot of mixed reviews and I see why. It's not deep, its not nuanced, and it doesn't have much to offer in respect of RPG elements. It has nothing to do with D&D gameplay or the typical ARPGs that Wizards of the Coast are known for in their video games. In my opinion it plays like a cut-rate, bargain-bin Shadow of Mordor without any of the charm. There is a lot of emphasis on building hit streaks and executing special moves for your chosen character. There is a clear emphasis on multiplayer, but the community interest is not their to sustain it and I've not been able to experience it. I'm also willing to bet that 90% of players main Drizzt, although I've not personally managed to find the statistics. I'm guilty, I've been playing as the drow ranger myself. The missions are short and shallow and all access is from a central hub area. The only NPC is a merchant with no real characterisation and limited utility.  All missions boil down to go to "x location" and kill a thing, great now go to "y location" and kill another thing. What there is of the story appears not to have much continuity from mission to mission, or (if there is) the story is not compelling enough for me to care and I have been skipping all cutscenes even on a first play-through - not a good sign.  Also, on the subject of cutscenes they seem to be the only medium by which the "story" is told. There's no dialogue trees, there's no player choice and there's no interactions outside of the aforementioned combat. As a fan of the books, it is nice to see much beloved characters in this game, but the story does not do them justice and the "story" (such as it is) does not fit with the continuity of the books. The characters come across as shallow and do not have any breadth of character. There are also changes in appearance for several of them which is not congruous with the descriptions in R.A Salvatore's novels or wider D&D lore. However, I would still recommend the game for a casual gamer. As button-masher brawlers go, you could do worse (although you could also do better). The missions being short are in some ways a blessing when you have limited free time but want to jump in for a 20 min game of something. I work long hours, have little time for gaming, and come home exhausted. Sometimes I don't want an immersive, deep, genre defining game of the year. Sometimes I want to mindlessly hit light and heavy attacks - and you know what, this game scratches that itch. The loot grind and core game-play loop, though nothing to write home about, is implemented well enough to keep you wanting to play a little more, and surprisingly I have actually found myself having fun, despite it's obvious shortcomings. I'm now about 9 hours in so it clearly must be doing something right, and I am finding myself playing a quick mission when I have a dull moment. Is this going to be the best game you ever play? No, absolutely not. Is it good enough to kill a few hours here and there when you are in the mood for something casual? Yes, and I'd recommend it for that reason. Consider picking it up when it is on sale or if any of the "positives" speak to you otherwise it's probably one you shouldn't lose sleep over if you give it a miss.

_childDocuments_.review: Atrocious game, its a discgrace to Dungeons & Dragons franchise and Companions of the Hall. These are one of the most beloved characters in D&D and this is the game they get? I gave this game a fair shake, just for the characters alone, but I will not finish it, as its such a horrible experience.Everything about this game feels amateurish, broken and unfun. Combat is stiff, with unresponsive controls and poorly designed enemies with unclear hitboxes. Bosses are one of the worst I have ever experienced, they are just buffed versions of regular enemies, to the point of being huge damage sponges or gank squads. Fight with The Chef was the straw that broke the camel's back, his hitboxes are huge and he constantly knocks you down or kills you with 1-2 hits (on recommended gear level). Not to mention his arena is constantly sprayed with flames that don't damage him.Entire game is buggy, janky and oh so poorly designed. Nothing about these locations is interesting and you constantly encounter the same props and enemies. It wouldn't be so bad if at least combat was fun, but it isn't, you don't feel like these mighty heroes at all. Attacks don't properly lock onto enemies and there is no animation cancelling, so you are constantly flailing around hoping your dodge will become responsive when you need it.There is an enormous potential in making an action RPG with these characters, or at least with Drizzt, but D&D Dark Alliance doesn't come close to realizing that potential, its galaxies away. Its one of the most unfun, broken and janky games I have ever played. Stay away from this piece of ♥♥♥♥, believe all the negative reviews, yes - its that bad. Its high time Wizards of the Coast gave D&D license to good developers that can realize its potential, not a bunch of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, that don't know how to make a half decent game.

_childDocuments_.review: I saw this game advertised initially in the early part of 2020, perhaps 2019.  I kept an eye on the site and Facebook page because The Legend of Drizzt is one of my favourite book series ever.If this had been a hack and slash game in the vein of Demon Stone or even Dynasty Warriors, it would have been acceptable.  Listening to the Companions of the Hall banter as they sliced through hordes of enemies?  That would be awesome.Instead we get a sort of Vermintide knock off.  As my friend and I went through the levels, we could see and point out the spawning locations of monsters and what would trigger them.  Every single troll comes out of a hole in the ground.  Every. Single. One.  Verbeegs have out houses.  Sometimes there is a hole NEXT to a random wooden outhouse and BOOM, troll and verbeeg, right on schedule.The Akar Kessle fight (why the heck is Akar even in this game?) was a disgrace.  He just stood there and let us kill him.  Three times.  In the same fight.  No ads, no special magic mechanic, no thing.  Just slapped him three times.The cosmetic system would be better off not existing.  All, with very few exceptions, of the armours and weapons look silly.  I did not find ANY gear I could imagine any of the companions wearing.  Drizzt very quickly just became a drow assassin in all black or purple spider pattern gear, as if the development team were given a generic rundown of drow lore.Cattie's bow is so short it may as well be a toy.  That is all on that point.There are huge amounts of visual and game play bugs.  Sometimes the 'activate' button just breaks and you can't loot in this looting game, or pick up friends if they should somehow go down.The higher difficulties are beyond stupid.  Every weak goblin is now a near immortal god that will take combos of your whole stamina bar to murder, whilst his two godly brothers whack you from the sides.  Sadly, this applies to bosses too.  Their mechanics are so simple that it would make even Akar Kessle look competent, so the devs just gave them an extra few bucket loads of health to soak up the damage as they glitch around the combat arena.All you had to do was let us play as the Companions murdering DnD monsters.  Not try to retell the Shard's story as badly as you possible can.The environment design is awesome, very pretty, the guy that designed that needs a gold star.  Everyone else can see me after class.My friend and I plan to continue this game and finish it, as well as return when the free updates happen.  If things improve, and I hope they do, I'll update this review.  Until now, stay far, far away.

_childDocuments_.review: Given the bugs that currently exist in this game, I cannot in good conscious recommend this game. The fact that this is marked as a full release title shows us how low our standards for games have become and how meaningless the words "early access" and "full release" really are. It's clear that there either wasn't proper QA testing, or someone greenlit this for release despite these flaws.- Infinite loading screens essentially requiring you to restart resulting in you losing 1+ hours of progress (and any XP/gear you've obtained) just isn't acceptable. - Loot rarity has no meaning. Receiving an epic/ legendary item in the 2nd second stage makes the rest of the loot feel subpar. - Forget playing co-op because the desync is god awful. Enemies will teleport randomly, attacks will hit you before the animations even start, sometimes there wont even be an animation at all! (this isnt an issue playing solo)- Enemy AI is absolutely brain dead. Often times they will AFK as you're rezzing your buddy, or just sit there and watch you attack them. Others wont even move toward you until you stand still.+ Combat was pretty fun when the game worked.+ Decent level of customization with gear, consumables, unlockables, and combos make your character feel like they're progressing.+ Cutscenes were enjoyable to watch+ Exploring feels semi rewarding Supposedly there is a mage character coming to the game #SOON but who knows when you'll get that. There is "potential" (I dislike this word) in this game, however by the time a game reaches said "potential" it's often dead in the water. I understand there is a thing called a "marketing budget" but maybe instead of spending that money on hiring celebs and streamers to play your game, and invest a LITTLE bit of that on development we could have a solid experience here. Buy at your own risk.

_childDocuments_.review: After diving in all morning since launch, I can say that this game should've waited just a bit longer. All the parts are there, but with key components being very buggy, laggy, or downright not working at all, it's hard to recommend the game in its current state.NARRATIVE-It's no shocker that you're thrown into a virtual D&D campaign. You're not really given a large focal direction of a linear story, instead thrust into a D&D world halfway through and expected to understand where everything's expected to go. Backstory was either very limited or nonexistent. Each act you perform seems to operate on its own and has no direct connection the preceding or following acts at all.ENEMIES / BOSSES-Enemy & boss names either look like they came out of a random name generator or complete the phrase "(blank) the (blank)." Attempt at originality is there, but names don't really match the characters since all enemies statically move with the same personalities across the board.-Focus on the popular D&D enemies were very apparent from the beginning. Trolls, goblins, orcs, and the occasional wizards, all of which carry similar or almost exact enemy design.GAME / LEVEL DIFFICULTY-The difficulty setting for acts is a good touch. Being able to adjust your difficulty to increase rewards creates that high risk/high reward scenario that many gamers enjoy.-Despite the ability to set your own difficulty levels, there's basically only 2 difficulty settings: You become a tank and mow everything over, or you get 1-tapped by anything that's not a regular goblin enemy. Large-enemy or boss stomp mechanics and AOE range are beyond troublesome, if not impossible for close-range players who's characters, you know....have to be up close to do damage like the barbarian or assassin. Essentially, you will never do enough damage at higher difficulties before a major enemy or boss 1-taps you, making your character choice worthless to your party since you'll be spending your entire engagement trying to draw enemies away just for a chance to revive your teammate.-Act III boss battles are the standout encounters in each world area. They actually have somewhat different mechanics aside from other levels...until you realize that the majority of boss encounters in each world area are simply killing smaller enemies to open up the boss for damage. ENVIRONMENT / WORLD DESIGN-Players really do feel like they're immersing in a D&D world - caves, rocky mountains, glacier caverns, etc. The design of each level is unique to their own, but it's apparent that the developers attempted to make each level feel so similar that they almost look the exact same in aesthetic and design. Originality in level designs honestly leave little to be desired - smack a wood fence, blow up a door or two, jump and grab onto a ledge with a red cloth on them to guide your way, avoid damage areas on the ground, rinse and repeat. It's the same designs, reused in every level.LOOT / REWARDS / ITEMS-Loot feels damn good to pick up and receive when you complete a level. The tally screen at the end of an act makes you feel like you accomplished way more than you actually did. The game itself almost makes you feel like it's a looter shooter without the shooter aspect. Think Diablo hack-and -slash.-Rewards seem very limited to simply finding them in chests only. Rarely will you find any enemies that drop loot for you, and even then your loot is tied to the difficulty you're on, so if you're not the party leader of your group and they chose a lower difficulty, the chances of you getting gear in every encounter that you'll upgrade and/or use becomes slim to none. You'll most likely be spending your time in the merchant store selling every piece of armor you were rewarded.-Item builds in comparison to their actual use is nonexistent. The amount of stats you receive for a character are very reminiscent of a D&D campaign, but in a hack-and-slash design such as this they're basically not needed. Your life bar & stamina bar are the only things you're going to focus on during your entire gameplay. World design is so limited to enemy attacks and AOE pools that the amount of resistance traits seems needless.COMBAT-Combat is at its absolute best when you create attack chains and open up different move abilities, such as barbarian hammer swings shifting from light to fierce and spelling doom for enemies. However, it quickly shows when you become reliant on the same attack patterns over and over because the enemies are only one of two thing: Shielded or non-shielded. That's it. You'll find yourself becoming very repetitive very quickly.-I hate to bring this up, but combat, unless required to progress, is almost pointless. The amount of times I had an entire party down only to simply run back to where we were while avoiding encounters entirely was almost insulting. Enemies sit there completely oblivious to the fact you're running past them. The amount of experience you get for enemies in the tally  screen just isn't feasible enough to justify reengaging or even pre-engaging.-The frequent safe zone mechanic that pops up after specific encounters is awesome. You have the option to choose to save your checkpoint and refresh, or risk it all for a loot rarity bonus. Realistically though, if you're running 3 or more party members in your group, there is absolutely no reason to checkpoint. Battle are solid enough with 3 or 4 people in a group that the difficulty vs revive ratio makes checkpoints worthless when better loot is in front of you.AUDIO-Audio is traditional as to be expected for a release game. Sliders make the game easy to adjust from its preset ear-bleeding level.-Cinematic audio is not applied to audio levels and act independently, so they always remain extremely loud.QUALITY OF LIFE (QOL)-The combat tutorial was great for learning combat, but the absence of any other tutorial makes the navigation of the UI, menu, market, etc very difficult for players. It's literally a "pick it up and figure it out" thing at first glance. It's not "difficult" per-say to figure out how to navigate the game menus, but the sheer design alone makes a tutorial a needed thing that was never implemented. You're not told about adding moves, feats, or other character customizations such as equipment upgrades in the market or other vital gameplay options.-Keybindings on launch do an excessive amount of reversion to default settings. It doesn't happen in-game by itself, rather when the game is restarted. You'll find instances where any keybind changes made will not appear in the game U/I during play so you may find yourself accidentally hitting the wrong button because you either forgot that you changed it or it reverted and didn't revise itself.-The ring and necklace equipment options in the market rarely ever work when clicked on to either change, sell, swap, or upgrade your equipment. I found myself clicking endlessly on each 50+ times before they finally load the next screen.-Selling equipment requires you hovering over the item you want to sell and holding enter rather than mouse clicking, then if you attempt to sell another item you have to move the cursor away entirely and then back to refresh the market list so you can sell again.-It's extremely obvious that this game was made for priority controller use. The chest in the middle of the home area, nearly all menus and the trophy section of the game were clearly meant to be used with a controller stick because clicking on anything menu-related will have no response. Instead, you have to use WASD to move and navigate.MATCHMAKING-Two options: You host, or someone else does. Only available in the home area, never in-game. This creates extremely long wait times & sometimes severe in-game latency.OVERALL: 5/10It's got all the makings of a great, fun game to play with friends, but the repetition, QoL issues & matchmaking restrictions are holding it back.-Jake

_childDocuments_.review: This feels like a third person action game from about 2012 in a lot of ways, which I mean as high praise because I really liked those. You choose a character, choose a map, go there, kill dudes, hoover up some loot, tweak your gear and do it again. The maps have a pretty high density of secrets, but they're usually pretty easy to find with a little attention, it's enough to keep you clued into the environment but not enough to turn it into a puzzle game. There's also a fair amount of character in the environmental design and enemy chatter, which is funny to listen to. The combat system is surprisingly deep, with a pretty wide variety of moves for each character; if you keep the difficulty low you don't really need to worry about it, but higher difficulties reward understanding how to chain moves. Unlike a lot of similar recent games *coughEldenRingcough* combat is fast paced, and you're usually fighting lots of enemies at once, which definitely sells the whole playing as Drizzt fantasy. There's boss fights, but they aren't the focus of the game, and don't generally feel like you need to learn some dumb obscure gimmick in order to beat. Graphically it isn't the greatest, but once I'm playing, I really don't notice. If you're expecting something really recent and cutting edge feeling, this isn't it. If you go in wanting something that feels like it would be at home on the XBox 360 or so, you will be very happy.

_childDocuments_.review: To start this review, many of the first negative reviews, and highest rated ones, are both much too critical and based off of a low amount of hours.This game is marvelous, but it would be ignorant to write this review and say there are no issues. Of course, there are some glaring issues. But many of them are no where near as detrimental as some of the high rated negative reviews make them seem. The worst issue in my opinion is the lackluster AI. Many of the enemies, simply won't attack you, if you don't start attacking them. And you get warmed up to that very fast. However, there are some AI, who are very aggressive, and being warmed up to AI not generally attacking you, it makes it feel like... a normal game. However, if you're playing with a team, I have not yet encountered an enemy who will actively attack you whilst reviving a teammate. THAT BEING SAID, the monsters are VERY fun to fight against, when they actually fight back. Except for some. Namely, Verbeeg, Stygian Riders, and Trolls. They're simply bullet sponges. But, their attacks make it feel like an actual dungeon brawler. You have to actively dodge and evade and make use of it being stunned, to get hits in. There are some very enjoyable fights with enemies in this game. And it feels very satisfying to get off a long combo and kill an enemy. To go over the pros and cons;PROS:- World building and design. It's breathtaking. It's exceptional. Every map has some winding paths to follow that reward you with more loot and optional quests, or you can stay on the main objective and fight fun enemies, and reach the end goal. The design of maps, the look, being able to look out into inaccessible areas and see, for example, the bones of a dragon. It's great.-The music and audio. It's DND. What did we expect? The music is FULL. It's an entire orchestra, giving off the energetic highs and the scary lows of a battle. It makes the music fun to listen to while running a dungeon... for the 7th time. Trying to get your gearset.-The story! It's enthralling. Fighting giant monster after giant monster trying to reach the end, where your met with Icewind, the ice dragon trying to make good on her vows to destroy the party that killed her partner, Icingdeath. Fighting Ice Trolls, flaming verbeeg, goblin emporers, and finding yourself trapped in this magical world where you just want to keep going.-The endgame loop, it's just like any other arpg and hack and slash looter. You grind x dungeon for x hours to get x gearset to raise your overall "gear score" by a small margin. but its fun! The dungeons have some good repeatability that actually make you want to play the game after beating the 15-20 hours of story.-The promise of MORE. two free dlcs over the summer, a paid expansion with a new character in the fall, the fact that they actually ACKNOWLEDGE the community and have responded to known issues and are constantly looking to fix bugs. It's great and it makes me feel like there will always be more to the game.CONS.-Finicky AI. As I said in the first few lines. It is sometimes good, and sometimes it won't notice you.-The scaling for FIRST TIME PLAYERS, from CR1 - CR2, can be difficult, but also, its because the CR1 enemies fight back less, compared to CR2-6. I've tested it, and in my experience, the enemies are actually easier to face in CR1, not considering the lack of health compared to others.-Lack of content, kind of. It's no secret that for this game and many others like this, there is not as much BASE CONTENT as people would prefer, and some people who get these games don't have the mindset to max every character, get everyone good gear, etc. So if you're looking for something with 100s of hours of story, this, notably, isn't the game for you. -The community. The subreddit discord for this game is horrendous. People complaining about every single little aspect, saying how this is the worst game they've ever played and then going on to say that they only have 2 hours. Saying the game is insanely laggy and then mentioning they barely meet the minimum requirement for specs. Sure, it's not as good as Baldurs Gate Dark Alliance 1-2, yet. But it can be. And it is good to know the Devs are hard at work trying to make it the best game it can be.TL;DRThe negative reviews are much too critical, but the game is far from perfect. High potential, but also very good right now. Definitely could be better, but I would 100% buy on sale, and if you have the money, buy it now. Very good game with a good endgame loop. World is great, music is great. Ai could get some work, and some more base story would be nice. It's good to know the devs care about the game. Good amount of planned content for the next 1-2 years.Buy the game. It's great. :)

_childDocuments_.review: I really REALLY wanted to enjoy this game, mostly because it was set in the Forgotten Realms, but also because of its price. I still haven't completed it but I don't think it's gonna work out for me. Forgotten Realms is a great D&D setting to base a video game on, so a lot could have been done with it. Even though I didn't expect something like BioWare's golden age entries, since this game obviously had a different vision and audience, it still could have been better. But apart from some fairly impressive cutscenes (and there's a bit too much of them) and map designs, and obviously Drizzt and his companions, the game has very little to offer in terms of lore, which is quite a bummer. Well made cutscenes contribute to the storytelling in a game, sure, but when it's too much... It's just too much. It gets so incredibly boring after a few fights. Because all you do is fight the same types of enemies, loot, fight more enemies and boom, cutscene. So naturally you lost the fun. Which is what disappointed me the most in terms of gameplay. Just how much it looks like a generic hack & slash game and feels like one too. And that's not even a pro by itself since the combat and the enemy types is almost completely repetitive. There are some small moments that the combat gets a bit creative, but, it's mostly a small detail so it doesn't make the entire game enjoyable. If you still want to play and just looking for a reaaaaaaally smooth sailing game that you can just play to spend time, you can give it a go. I'd say preferably, wait for a sale though.

_childDocuments_.review: Controls are stiff and janky. You can't change direction while attacking, you can't cancel an attack into a dodge or block, so defensive reactionary play is non-existent. Combat is more fighting with the camera to line up attacks than actually doing cool things.Edit (Elaboration):You can't do anything once you commit to an attack, not even change directions. This is a third-person character action hack-and-slash. Having even a modicum of directional control during an attack string is standard design, yet this game lacks that. The camera is too slow, even at max sensitivity. Trying to aim a character's attacks is obnoxious due to the lack of ability to adjust direction after making an attack. The character will constantly try to attack in direct line with the camera facing, mostly regardless of what direction I'm pressing at the time of initiating an attack. Only once was I able to get the character to attack away from the camera, but I was not able to repeat it in combat. Combine a stiff inability to change your attack string's direction with an inability to cancel out of an attack in any way and you have a rigid, janky feeling combat flow. Further, the camera rides too close and zooms in off-center from your character when you lock-on, to the point of removing your ability to see anything the left or behind you. Lock-on is also mostly useless as it breaks when your character is barely a brisk walk away from the target. Even when lock-on stays it messes with your view and makes attacking or reacting to anything else a hassle.

_childDocuments_.review: So, I got this game as a gift. I only knew it was based on DnD has some kind of co-op brawling gameplay.I was genuinely excited, as I love the DnD setting.If you're looking for a DnD game, look elsewhere. Also look elsewhere if you want to play any kind of dungeon crawler.Seriously, I'm not the guy to jump on any kind of bandwagon, I really want this game to become good, eventually.You probably already read the other reviews, and to be honest, I can't anything new to the list of complaints. But I want to try to give you more of a "feel" for the shortcomings of this game.The most glaring issue: The game feels clunky/sluggish. I played as the archer class, and the only thing that really felt satisfying to do was her primary arrow shot, which isn't bound to M1, as you'd think - you have to hold CTRL, which puts you into an aiming mode. In this mode you're just plain slow. On top of that, the arrows don't do a whole lot of damage. Sure, you have a charged shot, but the charged shot takes a pretty long time to prime and is bugged. Sometimes when I shoot a charged shot and try to charge the next one I get locked into the charge animation and have to cancel the charge. You're able to do a fair bit of melee fighting, especially after you unlock some fighting skills (by the way, for all arrow-related combat techniques, you have to reach Lvl. 7 first, which is kinda dumb when playing an archer). The main problem with the melee fighting: It feels . The animations have an awfully long windup and cooldown animation. Most of the archers meele attacks consume a HUGE amount of stamina, and you're also loosing max stamina when depleting your current pool, which just ends in you waiting after performing a single combo. Enemies react with generic and equally slow recoil animations, making hits feel weak and disconnected. Also, you can't really "aim" your animations, so your character just pushes through the enemies, making the last hits of your combo miss.Speaking of enemies: In combat, enemies tend to warp after they finished their animations. It looks like they're lagging, which only adds to the sluggish and weird feel to the combat. Also, the animations sometimes don't really match up with the actions. In some cames, the enemy model was facing me and charging up a projectile attack, but the projectile flew backwards to the other player in my party. It's not really detrimental to the gameplay itself, it just looks bad and makes the game feel so unfinished and unpolished. Players and enemies snap into long winded animations all the time.All of this just makes the core loop of the game just not fun to play. Sure, other games in this genre are grindy and you have to put in a fair amount of time to unlock cool abilities, but those game have an engaging core loop. Dark Alliance feels like waddling trough mud.

_childDocuments_.review: So this game is sort of a mixed bag, On the one hand it's looks and feels like you expect Icewind Dale to be. The characters have a lot of moves and you can free form them together into combos. I did notice looking at the skills I can buy with the different characters, that the videos of celebs and such playing the game, were given all the skills. This is why I think the combat feels clunkier than what we see in the videos. They were fully unlocked.Even with only the base skills though, and spending time with the various characters practising on the combat dummies, there is a ton of moves you can do. From short combos, to very long combos, to mixing various hard attacks that will knock down enemies or knock them away, giving you some breathing room.I don't know why everyone thinks every game should allow you to animation cancel, this game forces you to think when you attack. You can't just swing away like a madman, and then vault away at a moments notice. You have to plan your attacks, make sure you don't start a big move, while a Verbeeg is trying to slam the ground. The characters are also all designed to play off of each other. Meaning you can have Bruenor up front, parry an enemy, which then allows Drizzt to come in and backstab them, which then allows Wulfgar or Catti-Brie to use their team attack to do big dmg. Obviously if you are soloing, that's not an option.The other thing I noticed people complaining about was enemies stopping their attacks, well they have shields, and they are blocking. Just like you can block the enemies attacks, to avoid dmg. Most characters have some way to deal with the blocking enemies, for example with Drizzt jump at them, and attack from midair. His dual ground stab, will knock down an enemy not blocking, or stun and break through the shield enemies. Leaving them open to a back stab.As far as controls, I found a setup that works very well for me on keyboard and mouse, I rarely feel the need to lock on to enemies in these kinds of games, so I really don't use that feature, except when the tutorial made me. =)I use space for blocking, e for jumping, r and g for the specials, 1-4 is potions, 5 is ultimate, (because it doesn't fill fast enough you'll be hitting it all the time) I use mouse wheel button for dodging, q for aim. I use F for interact and shift for sprint. I never ran into any issues using my attacks, and found it very responsive. This may be because I have played games with similar locked animation attacks, such as Neverwinter mmo.I have not encountered any bugs or slowdown or anything like that, so for me this has been a fun game to play.I still recommend trying it out, the majority of the complaints on here is the AI which is being patched, and the lack of animation canceling, everybody wants to have no risk for their combat, dodge out at anytime. The combat takes time to learn, to get used to when to attack, or when to block, or dodge. A note about the AI, when I played enemies didn't stand there, they came to me if I damaged them at all.There is definately more they could do with the feats and skins function, I am hoping they will eventually expand on it.

Unlike some games where you can see what games are available to join and what quests / dungeons those people are doing, you join blind.  You have no idea what dungeon / quest you are about to join and no way to control it.  You also have no way to control what level ranges or difficulty ranges you will be joining.  I've joined into several games where the party leader was 15 levels above me and playing on very hard difficulties and I was being one shot-ed by everything and barely doing any damage. _childDocuments_.review: Since launch, this game has been a disappointment. I have played it on and off again for a few years, because I love The Legend of Drizzt novels and this is the only game that I can find and access that has the Companions of the Hall as the main characters. With that being said, even that can't save the game in my eyes at all.It runs like crap, it's not fun, it's completely abandoned. You know what other game is the same price as this? "Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance" or "Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance II". Both of these hack-and-slash/ARPG titles are a tonne of fun, they're available on Steam, and I've been enjoying them thoroughly recently. That's why "Dungeons & Dragons: Dark Alliance" tried to cash in on the name recognition. Also, both of these games have Drizzt in them as an unlockable character!Seriously, spend your money there and PLEASE do not waste it here!Update: I recently decided to play through the games entire story, as I'm almost stuck with owning it now. The game had a few things I want to mention, some are good but not amazing. Spoilers ahead, if you care.GOOD1. The size of the Frost Giants feels good, they definitely tower over you in an accurate manner (I believe).2. The Stygian Goat Tribe is interesting, seemingly a barbarian tribe similar to where Wulfgar comes from but they made a deal with Levistus that they fell through on so the whole tribe now wanders Stygia and heeds the call of Levistus to do his bidding. Very interesting lore.3. The setup for the boss fight with Kelvin felt awesome, him inhabiting his own descendant and sucking the life from all the nearby Frost Giants to empower himself definitely built some intimidation.4. The game has ONE boss fight that has more to it than just, hitting it until it dies!COUNTER TO GOOD1. Nothing interesting is done with the Frost Giant size, you just wack their legs until they die.3. The boss fight is like every other boss fight, wack them until they die.4. The fight with Icingdeath had more to it than "wack them until they die" but... its mechanics feel like a boss from a Spyro game. You wack it, it becomes INVINCIBLE until you activate a thing around the arena. Repeat 4 times, through in some mooks that spawn. It was the most interesting boss fight in the game, but still not very interesting.BAD1. Almost none of the bosses felt like YOU killed them. You wack them until their health bar drops, then a cutscene plays with NONE OF THE CHARACTERS IN IT (until the very end, where it has ALL of them) and the boss dies. Sometimes it'll even die from its own stupidity rather than anything you did. Yippee...2. I played as Wulfgar in this playthough, and now I'm playing as Catti-brie. One is "wack-till-death" and the other is "shoot and leave combat area".  I played Drizzt off-and-on for years, but because the combat is so slow, and locks you into animations, you can't react a lot of them time when something is about to attack so playing him is torture. Not the mention the parrying system is sometimes do-able, but often times god-awfully specific. I admittedly haven't tried Bruenor, but though he can likely handle himself it seems some of his abilities gear towards working with a party. And I played Auralla for all of 10 mins before putting her down, because I have no idea how she works, like she is a magic-user but has melee ranged abilities and needs to get in there? Maybe I'll give them both another go, who knows.3. Building off the previous point: I would play with friends, but they all despise this game. I would play online, but there is no way to communicate with others online? And often times the connecting is too piss poor to actually play!4. This is a "fan of the books" issue... WHY THE HELL DOES WULFGAR SHUNT LITTLE MAGIC HAMMERS AS HIS RANGED WEAPON?! WHY DOESN'T HE HAVE AN ATTACK WHERE HE THROWS HIS MAGICAL WARHAMMER! IT'S LITERALLY BUILT TO RETURN TO HIS HANDS FOR THAT REASON! HE EVEN THROWS IT IN THE REVEAL TRAILER BUT NEVER CAN IN THE GAME?! Oh, but I think I may know why...5. I don't think this game has physics. The only time physics do anything, is when you kill an enemy that doesn't IMMEDIATELY TURN TO ASH and what happens? It f***ing shoots itself into space! _childDocuments_.review: Currently in the process of getting a refund for this title. Here's why:I purchased this title (deluxe edition) the night before release, because I honestly had no idea it was so close to releasing, and that it had pre-purchase options. I did so simply because I felt somewhat confident that this title had an opportunity to be the "Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance" sequel (spiritual or not) that I've been waiting for, for years. I was firmly, and sorely, disappointed. What were my expectations? A continuous hack & slash romp through various locations across a multitude of Act's, filled with player-friendly combat, smooth third person gameplay, and mass loot collecting, all in a nice D&D package. Instead, this game is an unconfident clone of Warhammer Vermintide, done poorly. Sold at half-price no less (unless you purchased the deluxe edition. Why am I unwilling to give this game a chance to hold onto my money and grow? Simply because, I can already see the systems that are in place, and how they're all going to be fundamentally damaging to enjoying the game long term. I can almost guarantee you, there will be microtransactions in its future, and an immense grind that will require constantly replaying the same parts of the game over and over again (instead of allowing you to do so at your leisure and enjoyment). This is most certainly not what I was hoping for with this title. Why is it fine that Warhammer Vermintide works with this format, but not this title? Simple, and two-fold; It's namesake is Dark Alliance, so it's in no way wrong to hope that this title would have followed more closely with it's ancestral titles, giving players more freedom to change equipment on the go, gaining in strength during gameplay, instead of mirroring Vermintide and only allowing equipment changes between missions. Where Warhammer Vermintide gets it right by making the gameplay more enjoyable in it's format, and allowing player progression between missions to be meaningful. Yes, there is upgrading and material requirements, none of it is slapdash, and is designed to be significant, and player-friendly. If you are upgrading with one character, much of that same equipment can help you to boost another character significantly, making progression tied more to the player themselves, rather than the character. Using materials you've gained to improve other characters isn't a hindrance, it's an enjoyable part of the game.D&D Dark Alliance gets all of this wrong. Character Progression is tied singularly to the character. This game flies entirely in the face of its predecessors; it's not a Dark Alliance sequel, it's a bad Vermintide clone. The loot system has a thousand red-flags of microtransactions incoming. The gamplay is stilted and uncomfortable, the enemies are copy-pasted entities with no character besides random one liners, and aren't fun to fight. Every action your character takes seems to stop you in your tracks, meaning you have to anticipate everything, instead of being able to enjoy flowing through combat in a flurry. I honestly don't know how many times I can restate that this is a Vermintide clone done poorly, and adequately get that message across. Even with the "speed" characters, it seems like you move fast, and then stop dead to do anything. The forced third person perspective means forcing yourself to adjust to the strange angles you're being attacked from, instead of being able to switch sides, or move the camera to the back, or god forbid play in first person. Usage of the controls just seems... poorly designed, like aiming just seems finicky, the block and parry mechanics feel unwieldy and like they have a mind of their own, and swinging your attacks just to feel like every move either comes up short or flings you into the enemy doesn't make any sense. I really wanted to love this game, I'd been waiting for it since it was teased a year or two ago, yet I kept not hearing anything about it until it was literally the day before. It's almost as if the developers and publishers had no confidence in this game, and are just rolling it out so all their effort doesn't go to waste. I'm disappointed, and I honestly don't usually give bad reviews. Hell, I didn't even rate Cyperpunk this poorly. You know what this really is? It's a child trying to describe to you Lord of the Rings: War in the North, as if it was Warhammer: Vermintide... poorly.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing and finishing the 2nd act, the goblin one, I can't suggest the game to anyone at this price tag right now. The game is fun with friends if your group is just looking to find a janky game to mess around and laugh at all the bugs this game has. Balance is iffy, at one instance, we're just cruising along the level having an easy time, then when we jumped at our recommended level with a 100 level difference below us these mobs are 3 shotting the dwarf tank. Also the dwarf tank is a better healer than the archer that is supposed to be a support due to having an unlockable move that fully heals anyone that has no cooldown, only a stamina penalty. Go figure.Bugs. Lots of it. Some of it game breaking. You can get stuck on a dodge when there's no enemy besides you. The archer can bug out on a lock on making you unable to turn your camera until she finds a new enemy to lock on to. The dwarf can be stuck on a recovering attack animation and CAN'T PICK UP ITEMS until he fully dies. At one point my friend got his character reset to level 1 with a combat ability of 5 and the only working solution was to reset the game and join back again. You'll get frustrated at some of them or laugh at the absurdity of some of them. Servers. We're playing in SEA and our ping is always in the 200's. What's with that? Our internet is good enough as it is that we can play any multiplayer game no problem on the 50 or 70 range. Anyways if you have 4 friends to play with try it out first on the Xbox game pass if I recall it's only a dollar now. This is an early access game at best and I'm disappointed by it but we're having fun messing around with the bugs and we're planning to continue.Edit: We finished the game. Above review still stands. The bug where the dwarf can't pick items is so prominent in our continuation that it was just annoying and not fun anymore. Bosses are just "stunlock this man to oblivion" levels. If they can't be stun locked and has a big hitbox i.e. Kelvin, just bring the archer and she'll do the work. Icewind as a boss is bad, the mechanic involved firing 4 ballistas at Icewind to kill her, which is just padding to make the boss longer. Remove all the ballistas and she still falls like any other boss. Overall a really meh experience. The only good things I could say about this is that the overall design of the maps are gorgeous, some of the puzzles are interesting, and the combos are nice. It's still not worth the price.

_childDocuments_.review: So, first the good stuff. All the potential for a good game are here. The environment is beautiful, the detail on the characters is amazing. Cattie-Brie's fighting style is gloriously fun in concept. The monster designs are great and the dialogue is pretty amusing.On to the neutral, the death animations are extremely goofy, and some of that I think is from bugs. Sometimes it's like the monsters pop like a balloon and go sailing into the sky. Sometimes they just stop existing. Other times they flop down like a proper corpse. And sometimes they jutter and shake like a phantom from a horror movie. This really does look like a lot of bugginess, but it's amusing in some ways and is a tolerable bug. Something of a quirk for the game that is going to be loved by some and hated by others.Likewise, while the characters and environment are great, some of the interaction pieces look a bit rushed. Treasure chests in specific look pretty rough in places.Now the bad that is a bit my bias. Cattie-Brie's run animation looks a bit sluggish, the sprint is a bit better and her dash is great, but her common walk looks dumpy. And her passive stance looks like she has a broken back, it's painful to look at.And finally, the REALLY bad, the enemy AI is terrible. They give up on fights too easy. They don't press advantage. This wasn't as bad at Hero difficulty, but at adventurer, they basically waited in line to be killed. The verbeeg attacks were almost never a threat. The guy throwing bear traps and the optional boss The Sticker never really got close to me. Between all Verbeeg, I got hit by that harpoon attack exactly once in 3 hours of play. The thing separating this from being a fun experience with a few bugs vs a veritable cake walk is fixing the enemy AI and animation speeds. Hopefully that will be fixed quickly because right now it is a virtual cake walk.My next preferred priority would have you fix Cattie-Brie's model to look less like she had the stance of an old woman who badly needs a chiropractor. Then the worst of the death animations (juttering/flickering corpses, stuff like that).After that... I'd hope the effort would be on adding storylines and releasing new characters from the list of Faerun greats. Maybe a Darkwalker on Moonshae story arc with Robyn and Tristain Kendrick. Or Liriel Baenre and Fyodor of Rashemen. Or a rehash of the Azure Bonds and Wyvern's Spur with Alias, Dragonbait, Giogi, Cat, and Olive Ruskettle. The battle for the monastery that occurs in the Cleric Quintet.I'd love to see lots of classic TSR stories told in this format maybe with opportunity for weird crossovers like Liriel and Drizzt working together finally (they'd hate each other probably). But before any of this potential can be realized.... Enemy AI absolutely has to be fixed.
