_childDocuments_.review: This is a heartbreaking disappointment for me. If you desperately need a good Dungeons and Dragons beat 'em up, pick up Dungeons & Dragons: Chronicles of Mystara on Steam. Two great arcade ports for $14.99. It's an even better deal on sale, and you can get a 4-pack for about the same price as this base game. Give 3 copies to your friends and have a great time leveling up, fighting over treasure, and engaging in a campaign with branching story paths. I have no idea how a pair of arcade games from the 90s are a better co-op D&D beat 'em up experience than this game.On the surface this game sounds like a dream come true. I love a good fantasy setting, and they don't get much better than the D&D universe. Classic characters such as Drizzit have stood the test of time for a reason. This game has everything going for it; not only does it have a great setting with great characters to build around, but its core design philosophy is just as great. It's a 4-player co-op beat 'em up, with loot drops emphasizing replayability. Therein lies the rub, they focused so much on replayability that they neglected the playability.The AI problems some reviews mentioned weren't as horrendous in my time venturing through the Dale. Though that could be due to the fact that I stuck with Drizzit, who really highlights just how awkward the core gameplay really is. For starters, you're going to miss a lot of attacks-- and it's not your fault. Attacks have a lot of wind up, and every combo is a lengthy commitment. This makes combat feel like a dice roll, not to mention the fact that the incentive to button mash is abhorrently blatant. There's not much depth to the combat. Enemies will either throw out attacks without telegraphing them or accept their beating like a 1940s housewife. There's no incentive to change your strategy. Enemies with shields are just a basic enemy with two healthbars instead of one. Bosses-- or rather, the one boss I fought-- are simply uninspired. This doesn't even scratch the surface of how dissatisfying the game is.There are design flaws from top to bottom. Even though I didn't have a terrible experience with the AI, they are still bad. Perhaps you'd be kind enough to give this game the benefit of the doubt-- maybe this is a design choice-- but you can stare an enemy down and count the seconds before they actually aggro on you and swing in for a hit. I like to think that the AI is actually built around dice-rolls, as if the game itself is being run by an inexperienced DM who is struggling to roll their D20 in time to keep up with the players. Enemy AI isn't the only thing that seems... slow. The aforementioned wind up time is even worse when you pair it with the odd delay in your roll/dash. Movement as a whole feels sluggish. The lock-on, which some would think is a fix for attacks missing, is actually the worst lock-on I've seen in a while. I tried locking onto an enemy once, only to find that my character's back took up half of the screen. I never tried it again.Presentation is where the game shines. The areas look great, the characters look how they should and there's more than enough eye-candy to trick you into wanting more. While the sub-missions and exploration feel tacked on, I still enjoyed running around levels and finding "hidden" secrets and solving "puzzles" to get more loot. Yet the enjoyment fades quickly due to the lack of diversity. The problems with this game are visible when you peer beyond the surface. If this game were a cake, then it's moldy, damp, rotten and oddly crunchy with a beautiful outer layer of icing. This game desperately needs patches to improve its flaws-- from basic game feel fixes to complete overhauls into core game mechanics. I'm hesitant to refund on the basis that I desperately want this game to be good. However, at its current state, I can't call it anything more than just an average beat-em-up at best-- a fundamental failure at worst. Perhaps it's worth a shot with friends, but I still would suggest you get the D&D arcade games instead.

_childDocuments_.review: Nothing about this game is horrible. But everything about this game is just. . . distinctly subpar. The mechanics are a bit shoddy and the game as a whole is just limited. General advice: if you can get it for 10 or less, go for it. Otherwise wait to see if they turn it into an actual game.The biggest issue with this game is that nothing particularly stands out. The story is pretty tangential and underwhelming. Also a massive deviation from the books. Combat is similarly underwhelming; mechanically challenged with serious inconsistencies in hitboxes, aiming, dodging, aggro. . .and pretty much everything. Even setting aside the mechanical issues, the combat is fairly repetitive and uninspiring. Looting is distinctly limited, both in the number of drops and the variability. Each class has a handful of gearsets, and that's about it. Skills are similarly limited, each class getting to choose 2 active skills out of 4, and combo skills being railroaded. Feats operate the same way, with a max level character unlocking all feats, which are pretty much the same across characters. Ultimately, your build comes from which gearset(s) you equip, and with only a few to choose from, it's not terribly exciting. Further, enemies types are pretty limited, you'll mostly just be fighting the same things over and over. Finally, it just feels like they didn't put a lot of effort into making it seem like a full game. You go back to camp and you're greeted by the exact same dialogue, every single time with the exact same soundtrack playing. The maps, while well designed, don't have a lot of variety. I bought this game to play with my brothers (we loved the OG Dark Alliance back in the day) and unfortunately this is nothing like that. _childDocuments_.review: Ok.... All i have to say is WOW.  Beautiful visuals, potentially deep characters, good story backdrop, good voice acting.  Unfortunately, the people who worked on gameplay must have lost the concept of what fun is.  Those in the story department for character development must have been on half days.Why do I say this?  Well, this game has a lot of potential but it has been restrictive to promote its multiplayer experience which has hurt the storyline and all the potential to be something truly special that pulls a player in regardless if they want to play online or not.  This game has made me miss a similar game called Demon Stone.  It’s a much older game with pretty much the same concept of this but the storyline and character development are so much better than this game.   For gameplay.  The controls are not fine tuned and everyone feels like a tank that wants to move fast to keep up with the action.  This got a little better since I went into the settings and adjusted the camera sensitivity but it still feels like a lost cause.  The combat is not smooth at all, I keep finding myself hitting an enemy just to find myself swinging at air (in a straight line) when I knock one enemy down and I am fighting a group of them.  The loot.  Ummmm does the loot system for Anthem ring any bells?  Yup that sums that one up.  I was super disappointed and let down by this game.  Its easy to see who cared and who did no care about the project.  The best thing to recommend is to release a remaster expansion and completely rework the party system so all team members are engaging during levels and have more character development.  Also get rid of the loot system; have small cosmetic and stat upgrade gear that you don’t get very often.  The loot feels cheap in this game and not very D&D where when you get something you feel like you have earned it. Also COMBAT, COMBAT, COMBAT needs to be fixed along with the camera so you really feel like you are handling some of the most well known and deadly characters in dungeons and dragon. _childDocuments_.review: TL:DR This game is a fun hack and slash adventure game starring the characters of R.A Salvatore's novels set in the D&D universe. It has issues and is by no means perfect but a lot of people are reviewing this after less than an hour of gameplay. Keep in mind it is an Indie developed game built for co op. It CAN be played solo however it is built for multiple friends to play with. Dungeons & Dragons: Dark Alliance is a game I've wanted for years and have even discussed about many many times over those years. I honestly just wanted a Drizzt Do'Urden game in any way shape or form. When this was released however my expectations were a bit different than what was delivered. I automatically assumed it would be a Left 4 Dead clone based off the many similarities shown during marketing. I was pleasantly surprised to find it is not that. There's no horde timer, no frenetic pacing in the level, no panic to get through the level fast. Rather it has the hub and mission select of vermintide as well as equipping loot and customizing in the hub between missions with the level set up of what feels like WoW dungeons to me. A sprawling huge map with mobs of enemies, checkpoints, hidden loot caches as well as hidden objectives for a majority of the levels. Each campaign consists of 3 levels with 4 campaigns on launch as well as 3 dungeons which are campaigns only harder with massive levels and massive bosses. The amount of content available for 40$ had me happy with my purchase. As of review I have beat the game on 1 character and have played 2 of the other 3 about 1/4 the way through, took about 30 hours for 1 character to beat all content. Next I will tackle what a lot seem to overreact to. As stated, this game is not perfect. 1:Janky combat- The janky combat boils down to being very precise and deliberate meaning each move you make will lock you in. You can overexpose yourself by being greedy causing you to take a hit. It takes some mastery as well as progression. Like a lot of other RPG's this game takes cues from the D&D playbook adding moves to unlock as well as abilities, feats, and attributes. All of which are game changers and can vastly improve your character in combat.2:Bad camera-The camera is plenty fast for me. I've tweaked the settings to my liking, however I am playing on controller as the game recommends. My only complaint is the intense zoom on the focus system, yet I feel the focus system is not ESSENTIAL for 3 of the 4 characters(exception being Cattie-Brie cause she's ranged). The melee characters will attack the enemy near you that you are pointing at with the left joystick. At the point of this review I've beat the game with Drizzt not using focus at all during packs of enemies, and even quit using it in solo enemy fights due to adds possibly popping in and not being able to see them.3:Waste of a License- R.A Salvatore is by far one of the most influential authors on the Dungeons and Dragons table top universe today. Writing multiple huge events in the table top universe as well as creating backstories for huge events. His characters are some of the most well known by people who don't even know dungeons and dragons and if you feel like this game is a waste of the license then you clearly have no love for these books. ANY game doing something, not just with the universe, but with these characters specifically is anything BUT a waste of a license.4-Brain Dead a.i- The A.I on early difficulties is brain dead however as you amp up the difficulty their aggression amps up too. As well as damage and health. Their a.i too(i'd assume) is modeled after the creature counterparts from D&D, for example goblins are a fearful skittish lot who run from fair fights. They often will pack together in groups to take down one person which is why they are often used as front line fodder by other monsters. There's many layers to the game that most players will not know about and I find it funny so many negative reviews have less than an hour of game time. Now here's the real cons with the game as I see them as well as how it could be improved.1. Hitboxes. There is a few enemies that have wompy attacks that will hit you when you can't visibly see getting hit. It doesn't happen often but when it does happen you will notice this. Some Area of Effects like poison clouds can also be deceiving, poisoning you long after the cloud disperses. 2. Input seems a bit off with Drizzt and Cattie-Brie. Sometimes I will intend to do something and something entirely different happens. Things like shooting with Cattie-Brie holding LT and pressing RB to shoot will cause me to kick instead of shoot. Some small things that do need smoothing out.3. LAN LAG! Online works perfectly fine for me. Very minimal drops and kicks from me or others online. Some things like invulnerable buff being permanent, being permanently silenced, enemies teleporting around. There's a few things I can point to as being online bugs.4. Some creative liberties taken with the characters. Wulfgar doesn't REALLY throw his hammer. Drizzt REALLY isn't a battlemage. Gwen ISN'T an ethereal Space Panther, Some characters playstyle(as well as look) is a little divergent from the novels. Drizzt's skin is purple rather than ebon, wulfgar has a bald head rather than long unkempt barbarian hair, bruenor rarely has a red beard and hair, cattie-brie isn't voiced by a scottish woman. Some minor things I can forgive but things that just stood out to me being an avid reader of R.A Salvatore's Novels. People who don't know the source material won't even care about this stuff.Suggestions for the game. Some things I'd like to see added are a combo list. Something that shows your basic combos and what your character can do at level 1. Because there is no way to see what can be combo'd together your left kinda just pressing buttons around to figure out the combos yourself. I'd like a combo list for learning and mastering those combos as well as a more detailed tutorial showing what executions are as well as other game mechanics which are very very obscure til you just figure it out. Let us skip the tally screen at the end of the mission. Let skipping cutscenes be a group vote thing. A randomized playlist of missions with endgame modifiers would be cool and this game would definitely benefit from something like this. I'd also like to see more abilities as well as ultimates for each character.Overall I whole heartily recommend this to anyone. Even people who don't know the novels or source material. This game is a blast with friends and has a decent amount of content for 40$. Overall I was surprised by how smooth it did feel(Knowing it was an indie dev building an unauthorized Drizzt game til Wizards of the Coast slapped the name on it), surprised at how unique it was(expecting a vermintide clone), surprised that the humor wasn't immature and over the top cheesy or flat out cringey like a lot of other games on the market. I was surprised at how well the devs nailed this game. If you are looking for a fun Co-Op game to play with friends with an engaging combat system as well as a RPG-esque progression that will have you fighting many famous monsters from D&D lore, this is a game for you. Just don't expect it to have the polish of a AAA game and don't cry about the difficulty, there's varying difficulties, go as high as you dare and quit complaining about brain dead A.I on the easiest difficulties. Buy It, Love it, if you enjoy it, read the books. Need more Drizzt everywhere.EDIT: Quit complaining about this game and comparing it to Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance. Those games are top down ARPG's. This is a 3rd person hack and slash brawler. This was also developed by entire different dev studio, authorized by WotC during development.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has some severe issues. It's nice-looking, but the combat is clunky and hard to enjoy. Characters learn new moves, but the controls aren't responsive and the moves are annoying to pull off, so most of the game is button-mashing to kill the same tiny handful of enemies over and over again. Collision detection is wonky and hitboxes are weird as well. Sometimes beating a level won't actually let you finish and you'll have to start over and lose all of your loot and gold. I've had issues playing with others, as basic functionality has vanished during co-op, leaving my teammates unable to pick things up or use skills properly.Levels are insanely dull and you've seen practically everything the game has to offer after the first few hours. The camera is weird and hitting enemies is awkward, as the camera is better suited to a third-person shooter than a melee action game. All of the levels feel the same and the game gets insanely boring very quickly. Levels end in boss battles that aren't boss battles, you just need to kill a regular enemy with a larger health bar most of the time. There's barely a story and the characters are also horribly underutilized, as they don't appear in cutscenes. Cutscenes look good, but instead focus on enemies goofing around. This game has nothing to do with Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance. They just reused the name because they figured people would buy it for that alone.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start by saying that I don't ever write reviews for games. But this one encouraged me to because of how depressingly bad it is.My boyfriend and I have been excited about this game for weeks. He pre-ordered it for us, we played it Day One, and let me just say, I am SO. INCREDIBLY. DISAPPOINTED. The combat is janky as hell, it feels slow and unpolished, key presses take about a million years to actually register in game, the characters are so difficult to actually control, and the animations are SO slow. This feels more like a demo you'd play at E3 as a preview instead of a fully finished, fully released game. It honestly feels like they've spent 90% of their budget on graphics and music, and left the other 10% for combat, animations, and everything else. The archer character, Cattie-Brie, is who I started with. Right off the bat, there was no reticle for aiming. So I'm running around for half the level trying to shoot at things and missing half the time. I then discover that you have to hold down the CTRL key to go into aiming mode. And keep holding that key the entire time you're shooting. I don't know who thought this was a good design choice, but I think this is one of THE MOST ridiculous things I've EVER seen in a game. There's a stamina system in game that is tied to attacks, so once your stamina bar runs out, you can do absolutely nothing until it recharges. Granted, it doesn't really take THAT long to recharge, but in a game being marketed as an "explosive action brawler," there should be NO downtime. I shouldn't need to run away from enemies because I'm out of stamina and therefore can't attack them at all. I'm not really even sure where the stamina mechanic came from, since in actual tabletop DnD, there is no such mechanic, at least not that I'm aware of. It just feels like something they implemented so players wouldn't be able to take enemies down in seconds. When playing in co-op, your attacks can actually stumble your allies, which in normal tabletop DnD terms I can understand, but should really not happen in this game, especially if you're marketing this as a mostly co-op game over single player. In addition, at the end of missions, your characters are pitted against each other to see "who did better." I'm sorry but in a co-op game where you're supposed to be working as a team to take the big baddies down, this shouldn't even be a thought. In a competitive game like Overwatch, sure, but not here. The end screens aren't even skippable, so you have to just sit through the 5 minutes of "look how much damage you each did," and "this is all the gold you got," or "this is how many crystals you found," which is SO frustrating. Let me skip through these parts, because honestly I don't really care. This game is not a "dynamic co-op." This is a button smasher beat em up, AT BEST. There is no "explosive action" in this game. Unless you call watching enemies stand there not attacking while you smash buttons to death to try and kill them "explosive action." This is an incredible disappointment with the Dungeons and Dragons name unfortunately attached. I really can't believe Wizards of the Coast let this game be released in it's current state, because it's honestly laughable.

Lastly there is an interesting interaction with group play vs solo play in regards to the difficulty rating. When there are more people the enemies split attention making it easier to manage the field. in solo play having all those mobs on ya makes that management more challenging. For new players i highly recommend going through the lowest difficulty, leveling up a bit, gettin the gold for abilities (substantial amount of avg dmg), and most importantly collecting the set pieces. I highly recommend not giving up on the game!

_childDocuments_.review: Could this game be better?  Yes, it could. Is it the worst game of 2021?  No. Not at all. Is it worth 39.99 ?  Maybe, if your a DnD lore fan and enjoy a story and murder hoboing your way through a dungeon with friends. Otherwise maybe wait a few months for a sale and grab it then.I will recommend it though, its good, it could be better, but its not junk.I have 13 Hours in the game at the time of this review.3Things I like1}Scaling difficulty , you can make fights at lower levels extremely hard, almost Dark Souls hard..and if you win you get better loot.2)Attacks, combat is as fluid as YOU make it. Learning your key presses and combos is important in this game. A team that is in sync and working together can melt difficulties 4 or 5 times above their recommended gear score gaining 3 or 4 levels a mission.  A team that is not working together can still win, its just gonna take them much much longer.3)The story, I know its not a book, its a game, but the characters and setting are one of the, if not THE, most written about in fantasy lore.  The story, the cut scenes, the journal entries are all amazing to me as a long time fan.3 Things I dislike1) The fact that I cant make my own character.  Yes, the 4 we get are lore based and their skill sets are made to compliment each other, but if players could make their own characters to join up with the fab 4 or to run with their gamebros that would have been awesome.  You have 4 party members and its the SAME group makeup every time. Should have released with at least 2 more Characters to play.2) User Interface, I play mouse and keyboard, and have no issues in combat at all, BUT when I am in the hub the User Interface is a pain in the ***.  To many dead zones for my pointer, holding key presses to make a selection? come on...3)The animations for the Archer,  first of all , she looks like a 12 year old boy, second, her animations are  stiff and repetitive.  Gameplay with her is fine, shes a beast when you play her right and build her.  Those motions though,  its like watching a kung fu movie where the bad guy falls down from a kick, only then you see the kick after...and the kick looked like some Napolean Dynamite/Master Ken youtube martial arts mashup.

_childDocuments_.review: I have mixed feelings about this game, maybe it's much funnier to play with friends. Mostly playing solo BUT my first impressions of the game it's fun, but buggy as hell. Menu (pressing escape for example) or inventory has a slight delay and can be annoying. It seems like the game is supposed to be played with a controller as well, because when I connect a controller the menu management has better respons. Visually could be better, the cutscenes are great but the character looks bland and "shiny", they don't really blend in to the world. Some scenery are not that great either. Some armor makes my head disappear or chest disappear. Some enemies are invincible, don't know if they are supposed to be that, you can only see a health bar floating towards you, spooky stuff. After you clear a level one can see healthbars on the floor and in the air some times, restarting the game works but gets old after a few.Sound it's a bit weird, when an enemy is in front of me I hear him either to my left or right, not in the center area. I don't know if it's my setup, but no game has done that to me before, except this one and that is really strange and breaks the immersion, it's just weird. Tried switching to surround and headphones but no fix there.  The combat in this game reminds me of Monster Hunter and Dauntless, very sluggish and you get stuck in animations. There is very short time to dodge in some cases. For Example when I was in a middle of a flurry (Drizzt Do-Urden) a big dude had plenty of time to pummel me and throw me around, even the standing up animation is slow. It doesn't really flow with the enemies really.  I tried to play as Wulfgar but the animations where even slower, I had to change because Drizzt is a hard character to solo, better off playing Wulfgar or Bruenor if you are a solo player, at least they can take the hits. And there is this thing with some enemies even if you dodge they manage to get a hit and that can be frustrating at higher levels.  Some climbs are also buggy, I got stuck in a loop where my characters falls down then climb and then falls down again and climb, that bug happened several times, got stuck in the air while performing a air downward smash and had to wait for my character to die in order to get it fixed. Now the enemies in this game are stupid, some bosses does not react when I hit them, they really seem to like my pummeling. One boss even stayed still until he was dead, really challenging.. Some trash mobs don't react in time when I enter the room and can easly wipe out at least the first group. Been cheesing the game thanks to this though. I've learned that A.I has a aggro range, if you play as Catti-Brie you can charge your ultimate and easily clear almost every level on hardest. The mobs stand still when you are in the perfect range, just get your combo to 15 and repeat until Ultimate is charged and you are good to go. It takes time though but the loot is nice. Now, this is only 10+ hours of the game and I've seen a lot of bugs in a short time span. I would recommend to wait untill they patch Dark Alliance if I where you. It has potential but unfortunate its very buggy at this state. I will though struggle through and clear the game just to see where the story goes, it has humor, some cheap some good, it's a mix bag of frustrating combat and joy from clearing a level. I have to say no though if you are thinking of buying this, just wait for some patches like I said for a better game experience for you. Or take a leap of faith and go for it.Finished of the game a few days ago, but sadly no relief feeling except that it's over and I can finally move on to the next game. No big patch changes no nothing to this date. Controls still have input lag and the A.I is still a no brainer. Bad character development or should I say it doesn't exist in the game, recently got to know you need to read the books about the characters, I don't like when devs force you to read lore about character when they are already in the game, why seperate them? Save time? There is no character development what so ever and that is a big no-no.I get it, if you are a hardcore Dungeons & Dragons fan, sure you might think this is cool, but as a novice D&D fan, I've only watched Critical Role and heard or awesome games people have had, good for them. But the game is still bad for people who doesn't know much. There is replayability, sadly no harder difficulty than Rank 6, no more new levels after you beat the game. Sadly this is a  situation and that it cost $40 is a disgrace, it's a $10 game for sure. Also i think they put "Dungeons & Dragons" title so it would sell more. But what you get is a whole other thing. Sorry readers, I'm at my limit with this one.

_childDocuments_.review: PC controls are a big issue at times on keyboard and mouse, and feels like traditional PC play is an afterthought.  Playing Cattie-Brie with keyboard and mouse has lead to many cases of the game just ignoring my inputs.  Spamming left click for rapid fire lagging on firing at times.  Holding right click to charge up the multi-shot ranging from doing nothing, sometimes only shooting the weakest charge upon holding it for seconds and releasing, and sometimes getting confused about firing exactly as I make the next click attempt rather than charging up.  It has nothing to do with stamina, as I've had it just not charge up at all even when my stamina bar is full, and there have been times I'm at 50% temp max stamina that even before I have enough stamina for another fully charged multi-shot, it will sometimes begin charging again when I technically don't have enough stamina.Also, the menu for PC keybinding doesn't allow certain keys to be rebound, like M for opening your character menu.  And if you do like I did, and jump straight into multiplayer, and your friend plays exclusively with controller, you'll never even know that M is the key to open your menu to change gear or distribute points, etc.Even on a controller for Drizzt, I had issues with how this game forces all your attacks to be aimed at the center of the screen.  Any other game remotely this style, my character has always performed attacks in the direction my left analog is aiming, unless locked on.  This results in an issue where you always have to use the right analog stick or mouse to target things without lock on.My god the lock on, kill something while locked on and odds are you'll be targeting an explosive barrel a second later.  And getting a new target can be a pain if you unlock from something, as if you're not dead center middle of the screen enough on the enemy, it just won't latch onto a new target.  And some might say just hit right or left on the analog, but the lock on indicator is very hard to seeThere's a good bit of graphical jank in this game, like a troll hiding under ground will briefly pop into existence above ground, then disappear to crawl out of the ground as intended.  Given some old issues I know have been fixed, this graphical issue is just more of icing on the cake of despair of not giving a damn about quality than anything else.I've really only committed to playing with my friend more than anything due to going over he 2 hour limit.  The experience is tolerable enough for that, but I can't actually recommend anyone bother until things are fixed much more.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit:  I came back to this several months later, looking for some improvements and the promises made at launch, and found none.  In fact, not even the fully promised expansion was released, say nothing of the cross-play promised, issues rendering particles, janky elevators, and enemy response time.  It is a shame,  It is a small studio, so I gave them time and the benefit of the doubt, but alas, this will be a thumbs down for me.It's okay, and perhaps I am misguided, but I have faith they will put some time into fixing the bugs and creating more content.  The graphics can be beautiful, until you're on a clunky elevator that reminds me of Mass Effect 1, and that sometimes yeets you.  Not me, but two of my friends went, literally flying, into the air, only to end up back on the lower floor, several times.  It was hilarious, and therefore, a feature for me, but probably not great for a first day launch (see what I did there?) bug.Many negative comments are valid.  From AI's sometimes not responding, to the console port not being done very well (for example, the potion icon still had the directional pad and not numbers on them to say how you use them in the UI). Finally that combat is clunky, which, is unfortunate and true.Some negative comments should be ignored.  These include "what an awful sequel".  While the name is confusing and often associated with Baldur's Gate Dark Alliance I & II, this is not Dark Alliance III and this has been made clear since the beginning of production. And "the lore is awful", there is plenty of lore if you're willing to read, which, you should be a fan of, or at least used to, if you ever played Dungeons and Dragons.I have not played single player nor will I, but the multiplayer was fun.  We ran around and smashed things, and that is what me and this particular group of friends sought to do.  We got some loot, and we laughed at the bugs, which, luckily for us, were never game breaking.  I recommend this, purely based on this experience.  If you have three friends, looking to chat and just have a stress-free night of smashing things, I recommend.  If you're looking for in-depth true DnD style game-play, this isn't the game for you.I will say, one of my friends had less fun then the rest of us, and so, unfortunately, we likely won't touch this until some patches come, but hopefully they do.  The game has potential and just needs polish (maybe a few gallons, but nothing determination can't fix).

Forget balance, forget most DND mechanics or archtypes, this is a video game, through and through, with DND more as a setting than any actual impact on gameplay.Still, again, a lot of fun, especially if you have friends that enjoy playing otherwise sub-par games with each other and the various goofiness that results.

_childDocuments_.review: *I have changed my stance to Not Recommended. The game has good points, but overall it's disappointing to see such a waste of a good story and combat mechanics go to this nasty release. This was clearly still in alpha development.*Intro: I have played Dark Alliance for 7 hours, and have a solid idea how it is in it's current state. Also, I love the Drizzt series, so this review is something I hope the devs take with a modest amount of seriousness. I don't recommend this game, but there are things I want to clarify. (Edit: DO NOT BUY @ FULL PRICE!!!! This is like a mobile Drizzt game ported to PC)(Double Edit: >>>I DONT recommend to non-Drizzt fans.<<< The current state is haphazardous to your day. I only recommend it if you are diehard fanboys like me lmfao)  First, I want to address the issues with the game thus far in my own words, with my own experiences. ---The game has a bug that prevents you from completing a mission. This bug is most likely to be repeated if you skip enemies right before the boss arena, and are considered infinitely in combat. This happened while my friend and I defeated the boss in the mission "Order of the One Light".---PC controls are super janky. Especially the camera, and the way to rotates independently of the character 50% of the time. At least you can keybind.---(unless Im blind) while in a mission, you can't view your character sheet, switch gear (that you already have, Im not talking about the rewards of the mission-though I will discuss what i would have done differently with the game design later), review Moves (I cant remember how to perform 60% of my fav character's moves lol.---Battle Power warps difficulty way too much. I had roughly 50 less BP than recommended, and was getting 1 shot every time. I wasn't playing Bruenor (He tanky). This is obnoxious with the way stats work. You equip yourself towards a build you intend to path towards, but stats mean jack diddly squat if you decide to try anything not in 'White Lettering' in the mission selection.---The most oppressive issue is the netcode. Playing by myself was amazing. 100% smooth combat and adventuring. Trying to play with my best friend who only lives 2 hours away causes massive desync. >>>I can't confidently Dodge/Block/Parry without knowing I will be oneshotted.<<<---Exp for levels is mission completion earned only. Nothing from enemies (EDIT: This is only true if you do NOT complete the mission. Enemies give Rewards ONLY at end of mission, including EXP) but the occasional crappy common and few gold pieces---Transmog is sort of in the game. Almost like an unfinished decision. You can transmog stuff like color, but only on specific pieces of gear, and from ehat I can see, only weapons change entirely. Whats the deal with that?---AI programming is unfinished. Enemies reset, act like they arent being hit while you chuck your ranged attacks outside their designated aggro range.   Second, I will address the fun stuff.---Moves expand your characters combat prowess and options. Purchaseable with gold, Prerequisited/Gated by Character Level.---Feats, like moves, expand on your character prowess by adding stats like Crit, Armor, Health, Damage, etc. Or even doimg things like adding an extra useable consumable (i.e. Health Potion 3/3 default becomes 4/4)---Gear Progression pretty straightforward, but needs more work. I'll explain later--- Team Attacks are sick, but also need more variety. Parry prerequisite is a good  thing. Keeps things interesting and rewarding for skilled play---Attribute increases due to Exploration/Side Quests---Forgotten Realms lore super great to know about before. I read up to Book 6 of the Drizzt series. Best fantasy storytelling period. The game obviously follows the primary characters of those books. No need to read them, but maybe then people will understand why this isnt a Character Customization friendly game?---(Edit: Same 'Name' Armour has different cosmetic looks based off rarity)   Third, I will explain what I would have done differently in game design.---No Mission-based system<Open World adventuring with quests---No Reward chests<Gear equippable upon acquisition---Increased Variety of Stats/Feats/Gear/Customization/Transmog/Team Attacks---Remove Hub>Replace with Ten-Towns or include many other cities with NPCs and lively populace---Enchanting implementation  Finally, (Edit: Rewrote conclusion due to confusion of my opinion/stance on the topic) I want to state that I am having fun despite these backlash and problems the game has. It does feel like a mobile game ported to PC, and that's unfortunate. For what it is though, I like the combat and story enough to keep playing. Looking forward to seeing what happens in the future. At least the lore is fun and the characters are great. Too bad Drizzt looks weird (Not the same facial design as intended by Salvatore). >>>I DONT recommend to non-Drizzt fans.<<< This game can be fun, especially with friends once this netcode gets sorted out. Maybe wait for a sale though. Worth $25 maybe. Baldur's Gate games did a better job with their approach. At least you get to choose to be 1 of the 4 Companions :DThanks for Reading!

_childDocuments_.review: So- I have 30 hours. I completed the game primarily with Drizzt, playing with friends. I've beaten all the scenarios on all difficulties. They don't scale well and neither do the rewards. The higher levels should guarantee 1 Legendary at least as a completion reward.In short- the game doesn't seem to offer much customization of your character short of choosing what gear set you want and what 2 abilites you have equipped and then praying to RNGeezuz that you get drops with non garbage stats. Gear should have had some standard stats tied to them- why on earth do games still have weapons where they can possibly double roll extra damage on them? Just give them a damage type based on the tier and rarity and then randomize the bonuses. No one wants to see a blue with a double dmg roll on it out dpsing a legendary because it rolled no dmg bonus as one of its stats. That's just silly.Catti Brie is easy mode. AI is so dumb they just dont know how to deal with you and you do just as much damage- if not more than the other champions.The gear needs some type of customization option for stats. Maybe you can replace 1 stat with a random roll  for gold and shards.Abilities needs morphs or some way to level and customize. The cooldowns are too long. Maybe gold and exp dump to level them up and reduce cooldowns/potency/duration.A lot of the combos are super janky and just dont work well together. There are awkward delays on some that will cause you to get hit by a massive attack you are stuck in an animation for and get one shot.Bruenor's buffs often get bugged and just never fade. The set bonus that makes you invulnerable when you whirlwind? Yeah, that persists for the rest of the game until you whirlwind again...AI is very slow and unresponsive. You can literally run up and to them and start wailing on them before they even turn at you and you can stagger them until theyre dead, unless theyre a giant or something.I just cant get over all the combo attacks they have in the game and they gave them massive drawbacks with stam costs and you get animation locked for like 5 seconds in some instances to do them. Just make them instant and let us have some fun with them. Let me toss enemies in the air with my dark hand uppercutting and following up with a air spike strike into a shadow grasp or something. Literally the only moves worth doing are the quick and hard hitting attacks. Drizzts best attack is like one of the last ones where you just dash once then do a jump attack into a forward flip where you spike the ground and you can just spam that.I'm severely disappointed in this game at the moment. Maybe they will fix it. Hopefully- I never want to see a game fail. They have some DLC planned that was included with my edition so maybe that will improve the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Man... I never post reviews, but I feel the absolute need to in Dark Alliance's case. Firstly, I want to say not to let the extreme negative reviews sway you from trying this game yourself. The game is not perfect, but I've found there are only a few minor issues right now that even make my list. And none that I would deem making the game "un-playable" in any way. The amazing story-line, character roster, loot mechanic, and dungeon crawling make this game probably the best D&D game I've ever seen or had the pleasure to enjoy. Cons: -There are glitches. Some are small quirks that I find entertaining, like CRIT-ing a goblin and watching it fly far up into the sky on KO. Some are more inconvenient, like the one time a lich-cult-dude I was about to merc got stuck inside a wall and just decided to live there forever. -When at it's peak hours, the game can disconnect. This is by far the most frustrating thing, but it's only happened to me once out of the 9 hours I've been playing. And nothing was lost, it looks like it mostly happens only when you're back at camp and your loot has already been saved all nice and neat in your chest-box-thing. It can still be quite annoying to have to reconnect, especially if you have a full party of 4. -The characters are pre-made, set characters, and NO THERE IS NO MAGE. Not really a complaint for me, but more for others seeking to get a real custom experience out of this. This game is based directly from RA Salvatore's Forgotten Realms novels, starring Drizzt Do'Urden and his buddies. There is no technical "mage" in their party in the books, and therefore there isn't one now in this game. (Note however that each character does have customization in terms of loot/equipment, and each char has some sort of their own magical abilities.)-The combat is challenging. (Also see pros)The combat can be very difficult, especially if you're a loner and/or are too cool for friends. Don't expect to easily get through higher challenge ratings, even with a souped-up party of 4. Trying to do this can lead to irritation, sweating, nervousness, anxiety, and eventually rage-quitting. Pros:-This game is damn beautiful. The attention to detail in the characters, history/lore, loot, and monsters makes the game worth almost any quirk it could possibly have. -The dungeons are epic. They start off small (as in 30min-1hour each), and get more and more intricate. Eventually you'll be solving puzzles, digging for loot at every corner, and defeating mini bosses at every turn. You and your party could spend hours in one dungeon if you really wanted. That is, if you're a bunch of completionists or loot goblins like me. -There is a short rest mechanic, and it's so dope. You just defeated your first mini-boss. He was kinda tough, but your party got through it. A camp appears, asking if you'd like to take a short rest. Heal up, refill your potions, have a sit. Or... Give it all up, and go for glory? Meaning, of course, skip the rest and increase your loot rarity. Taking the loot upgrade will cost you a checkpoint if you die, and you may have to start all over, but hey... What's a little glory without some sacrifice? This is one of my favorite mechanics, for sure. -The equipment upgrading mechanic is really great. If you didn't get that legendary loot you were looking for, it's okay. You can upgrade your equipment up to 3 times in order to get through dungeons a bit better. Most games I've seen just offer better loot to replace it, and while this does do that as well, the option to continue using the loot I have and just make it better really appeals to me. Especially since there are set bonuses for every single piece of equipment in the game. You may not want to give up a set bonus until you finally get that legendary you've been looking for, and upgrading is a great way to make sure you live long enough to get it.-For the costume peeps, there are tons of skins for the equipment in the game. And they're kinda epic. So while you may not get to design your ultimate-fantasy-elf-waifu, you can always make Catti-Brie your majestic-battle-hardened-redheaded-SMASH-princess. -This game is the epitome of "working with others". And if you thrive on social games and co-op with the boys, this one is for you. Anyone who plays D&D IRL as well, if you are looking for a D&D based game to play with your group in between sessions to get that lootin' & hollerin' craving out of your system, I believe this will be the closest, most enjoyable experience for you. -The combat is challenging. (Also see cons)This is going both on the cons and pros list. Because while this combat is hard, and I mean HARD, it is so rewarding. You cannot just click buttons and hack and slash with ease like a normal dungeon crawler. The combat in this game takes some strategy, practice, and a bit of precision. I found that because I am used to quicker paced fighting games, turning the camera sensitivity all the way up helped me a lot in order to get used to the way combat works. But I highly recommend doing the tutorial stage with every character, figure out which one you like best, and practice with lower challenge rating dungeons until you feel comfortable with it. It can be difficult, but it feels so much more rewarding to kill bosses and get that loot. Like, I didn't just button mash till they died, I earned it by thinking my combos through and obliterating them from this earth. The fact that your party has combo attacks as well just makes it even better. In conclusion:This game is mostly everything I have wanted from a D&D themed video game, and I honestly believe I'll be playing it for quite a while. The lore is epic, the characters are iconic, and the combat is fun as hell. If you just want to turn your brain off and play a hack and slash with a Mary Sue type character, then this game is not for you. If you get annoyed by game glitches and are too impatient to wait for patches, this game probably isn't for you. But if you love D&D lore, enriching combat, and dungeon grinding, you definitely need to give it a go.TL;DR:You like D&D?Ignore every review you've read and just go play the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Purchased the game right off the bat and began playing it last Tuesday. Have played approx. 7/8 hours now and am still enjoying it. However, I'll be as upfront as I can about the current state of the game.The game is entertaining, the levels are beautiful and so are the graphics. The gameplay itself punishes button mashing and specifically punishes people who attempt to animation cancel. Once you lock in a move, you've locked it in and you cannot dodge or block in the middle of it (you can however time a block to parry). This can be quite annoying if you're not used to it, but with some practise it comes pretty quickly.The developers were, in my opinion, lazy with enemy designs. A lot of enemy models are re-used and just re-textured. Even some bosses use the same moves as some normal enemies which, quite frankly, is lazy and rather upsetting. In it's current state the archer is absolutely broken. The AI does not respond when you're out of the aggro zone, so the archer quite literally can clear the entire dungeon without ever actually fighting. I cannot imagine this won't be patched soon, as it LITERALLY breaks the game.As for the melee classes, they work as intended and are a lot of fun. If you're playing in a team of 4, be prepared to have 1 person to be bored as hell, because he/she is never getting attacked....ever....at least until they fix the aggro issue.The AI itself also needs some tweaking, as right now the AI feels a bit sluggish and sometimes it feels like they let their mind wander quite a bit, as if they momentarily forgot that you were there. Besides that, combat to me is still rewarding and fun (except for the archer). It requires some planning rather than just running in and button mashing. It's no dark souls either. You cannot dodge nor block during a started attack. You have to complete the full swing, keep this in mind while attempting to kick the enemies green behinds. Rewards are satisfying to get and completing armor sets, increasing your attribute scores and feats have a noticeable effect in both increasing your damage output and reduction.All in all, I'd say: It's a fun game that needs some fixing, was it worth 40/60 euro's? No. Would I recommend buying it? Yes, but either wait for the game to be fixed or get it on sale/cheaper.  If the developers fix the AI issue and the archer issue, I'd recommend getting the normal game for 40 bucks (or waiting for a 20/30% sale).

_childDocuments_.review: Short version: Passable in multiplayer, could be actual fun in a few month. Horrible in duos, impossible in single player. I tried to like it, I really tried, as the general idea, the love for details, the beautiful maps and little riddles are a perfekt combination to just enjoy while slaying some monsters...Skill and Progression system? A bit weird but nice. Classes with different play styles? Jepp. A lot for you to learn as a player about synergies and of your and your companions skills? Challenging and fun! A couple of bugs in AI, Netcode and animation? Not great, but sth you can fix over time, no biggie. There are people complaining about the enemie logic when you are outside the direct combat zone. That complaint is accurate, though if you choose not to exploit it and get into the fight, it doesn't really matter.But the horrible fighting mechanics, wow, you would really think they did some sort of tests beforehand or applied effort to make it interesting. Difficulty scaling happens by giving monsters ridiculous advantages, and later on more health and single shot damage (up to a point where dying and getting revived in MP becomes preferable over resource management and staying alive). Can they stagger you and interrupt your attacks? Jupp. Can you stagger them and interrupt theirs? Nope. They just do their thing whether you are there or not. And of course, your recovery time ist just slightly longer than theirs, so once you are down, you are down, as you have no chance to get out before the next attack(s). Can you just evade from an already started attack with visible aim and direction? No, of course not, silly you. The enemie just retroactively turns on the spot in your direction without any animation or time penalty. Thrown rocks literaly change direction in the air. It's beyond stupid. Controls are mushy at best, (or asynchronous?), with evasion of your character not always corresponding to your movement direction. I get the feeling there are very few directions allowed, at least nothing seamless. To be fair, this hurts most if you play single player. This game is clearly meant for full party or maybe 3 players, below that difficulty goes up crazy and any fun evaporates due to fluctuating enemy difficulties that can be somewhat alleviated in a party.

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE: I originally recommended Dark Alliance due to my hopeful nature that issues I mentioned in my old review would be fixed, but I cannot recommend it as things stand. This game has been abandoned by developers, and I only continue to play this game to get all the achievements so I never have to play this game again, and even then, I can only get through the levels by heavily modding it. If it goes on sale for $5, it might still be generous to call this game "worth it." Stay away from it.OLD REVIEW:This game still has a few bugs to work out(ragdolling, clipping, loot hitboxes, nonresponsive commands, potions being used twice, the keybinding menu doesn't show all keys) but is an overall fun hack n slash. This game seems to be balanced around having people play with you online, but as someone who doesn't have any friends, this game is extremely unbalanced, as I usually can only really get through levels with half my XP rating, and I usually die more than once a run. I'm hoping this is fixed in the future, as only two of the four characters can "sustainably" handle a single-player run (Wulfgar and Bruenor).I think my only gripes at the moment are that not much on how to play it is explained, and it was frustrating trying to use the shop and ended up accidentally selling gear I actually wanted more than once. The recommended XP to play each level doesn't really mean anything, as I am playing single player and it's balanced for four players. It would also be helpful if there were little text windows that popped up when you hover over something(stat, gear, ability, etc) to learn what it does or is.There's not a lot of accessibility settings that can be changed for people with special needs either. I have a couple of processing disorders and it would be really helpful if I could change health potions to automatically use themselves if your health gets to a certain point. I usually only notice too late how low my health is and, even when I do remember, the animation takes too long/the command is unresponsive and I die anyway. The way the loot is balanced doesn't really make sense, either. I played one Act on first level and got a Legendary piece of gear, while I'm currently playing an Act on third level and am only getting Common.Another thing I'd like to see is when you pause the game during an Act on single-player, it would be nice to be able to see what loot and how much coin I've picked up. It would also be cool to have the codex list every variant of monster you come in contact with, and manipulate the models so you can see them from every angle.Overall, I really like this game, and I love the setting. You need to play a level multiple times on different difficulties in order to progress, and good gear is pivotal. I would suggest figuring out your play style before spending your Feat points and Attribute points, so you can use them economically according to how you play. There's still some bugs and accessibility issues that I would love to see addressed, but it's very fun and addictive.

_childDocuments_.review: DO NOT and I mean DO NOT buy this game in it's current form. It's not worth the price tag, I mean even if it was free right now I'm not sure it's worth playing. It was clearly rushed out of the door too soon. Range fighting is broken, you can kill things without them aggroing on you. Melee is too clunky, you get locked into animations that leave you swinging off in the wrong direction or end up taking damage from attacks you can see coming from a mile away but can't do anything to stop it. The AI scaling goes from too dumb/easy to insanely difficult. I really want this game to be good and perhaps with another 6-12 months of rework it could actually be a lot of fun and enjoyable, but man right now it's a complete mess. I rarely write reviews and usually only positive ones, but this one is bad enough to warrant the warning to possible buyers. Wait for a re-release or something or maybe some major patches to fix most of the mechanics.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, a lot of negative reviews have less than an hour played and are just expecting the game to be mind hack-and-slash Vermintide sort of combat. If you like a bit more nuanced, pseudo-fighting game style (Shadow of Mordor is a good comparison or Assassin's Creed in some ways) with the traditional third person Action-RPG type of combat system, you'll enjoy it. Visuals look great and the voice acting is top notch, the soundtrack exceptional as well. Minor criticisms towards the AI (leashing, some issues with aggro in some places), but a patch can fix that, and another minor criticism is that you need gear to do any of the harder difficulties early on (scaling of enemy damage relative to your reduction/health is rough at first, but it evens out fast).I'll avoid rambling and leave it here: currently on June 23rd now, I'd give it a 7.5/10 (half a point for the soundtrack/audio quality, the rest for the gratifying feel and nuanced combat system). If you want to jerk off to a horde of slaughter, this isn't the game for you, but if you like relatively thoughtful combat mechanics and some deep "adventurer" feel in your gaming, you'll like it quite a bit. Can't wait to see the updates.

_childDocuments_.review: I was hoping for a nice single player game RPG that if I wanted to I could team up with friends.  I'm finding that playing alone the game is either too easy or too hard.  There isn't a good balance.  Sure you can pick different levels of difficulty but the game allows you to be swarmed too easily when you try for a challenge and you just can't dish out enough damage without running out of stamina.  The limit on health potions requires you to rest and give up the bonus loot.  I don't want to have to play every mission at the lowest setting but there doesn't appear to be enough balance.  Perhaps it's because I'm trying the tank and I should playing the barbarian or something.   Already tried the ranged fighter but she runs out of stamina and requires her to go into melee where she can only kick and gets killed with one hit.   This game needs a lot of work before it's ready

_childDocuments_.review: I'm trying so hard to like this game instead of just liking it naturallythe combat is so weird with most attacks coming out after a delay, a weird jerkiness to the combat flow, no ability to cancel out of insanely slow locked combo animations, almost no physics aside from final blows, a ♥♥♥♥ ton of enemies that drop martyr bombs on death, a lock-on camera that zooms in so close that it turns into the worst combat camera ever if there is more than one enemy or any hazards around you, almost everything that hits you throws you into a knockdown mini juggle status, don't even get me started on the nigh unavoidable elemental debuffs you will eat all the time or the one shots that can come from off camerait seriously feels like it was made by an indie team without a lot of combat experience. It is so bad that you can run off edges due to the crazy bad zoom camera from a long combo animation and the devs just reset you to the middle of the room because they are clearly aware of how cheap a death it isthe networking can do some crazy stuff at times, despite double low latency wired connections we'll see things like rezzing someone and then it says they died from the rez running out 3-5 seconds later or using a potion and then it still says you died even after watching your health go back upthe levels are kinda cool with some side paths to explore but jumping is crazy unintuitive with it constantly looking like your guy will never make the jump but miraculously connects to the ledge. The levels have some of the most annoying damage zones I've ever witnessed in a video game and they do crazy damage.and sooo many heavies are straight up damage sponges with bosses being redonk, the combat just isn't fun enough to make it so tediousenemy variety is minimal in appearance with the devs focusing on largely new cheesy abilities to frustrate you rather than challenge or entertain youthe story is kinda cool but has very little relation to the actual levels that coulda been swapped in for almost any story as there are very very few level moments that anchor any of it to this storyleveling up is a bit tedious as the devs clearly said to themselves 'ok we've got a solid game now let's add some super long grind system so they can play it forever' but they didn't finish the 'solid game' part first. Vast majority of players will see the story one time or never finish it and will never participate in the grinds. I honestly can't imagine why i'd do it again after finishing it once, there are just better games to play if I wanted grinds.also annoying is no auto pickup of any form of loot, you have to hit a button to pick up everything individually even in a cluster and some of it isn't super obvious sightwise - some loot is shared acquisition when coop and some isn'tdevs clearly didn't want anything slowing down coop so they don't let you access loot, progression or gear in a level - you have to wait until you are out. And you lose everything if you don't finish the entire tedious level, cuz that is such a fun way to design an rpg focused on progression dopamine. Nothing like spending time to get zilch in a game that can't be relied upon for solid networking or combat mechanics.my recommendation is to watch an entire level on youtube or play a demo somehow or keep razor sharp track of your 2 hour 2 week limit for a refund from steam.

_childDocuments_.review: We'll start with pros first:This game is actually really really fun. It's a great mix of a hack and slash and a souls-like game.There is so much detail in this game and it really shines at times when you least expect it. A good example is the level of detail on most pieces of armor/weapons that you get. Really cool textures!So much fun to play with friends mostly, and decently solo. If you have a player filling every role, it's perfect for having a great time. Even the glitches are hilarious with friends.A huge amount of variety in combat!! Yes you only have two "active" "abilities" but you have a ton of other abilities and combos aside from that. This isn't Dark Souls, you don't have 3 things you can do. You have TONS of combos and it's really fun to remember them and use them on the fly without having to have them equipped as abilities.The story is so great. Cutscenes are amazing. Really excited to keep going on it and see where it goes.And of course some cons:Nothing big really, but some typical day 1 bugs. I'm sure they'll work them out over time.Don't expect to use mouse/keyb for this game, but I highly doubt you would use it for Dark Souls either.Netcode isn't great, but it actually seemed to get better throughout the day, or with less than 3 players, which makes sense. Still some work they could do on that.Overall the game is really solid and super fun with a decent group of players. If you like action rpgs and D&D lore, specifically Drizzt story, you'll absolutely love this. The missions are built in a very curated way and the environments are really cool and fun to play in. Bosses can be tough, but they have mechanics you can learn, souls-like, and get better to beat them :)Just stoked to play some more with some friends!

_childDocuments_.review: Yes the game has it's glitches, AI has some blind spots and it is not well balanced yet.But I saw worst games at launch and this one is very playable so far.What I think we are all seeing is a rushed game to meet a deadline.But, if you take the game as a Beatm'up with RPG progression/loot/craft you will enjoy it better. Either solo or coop you will still get fun. This is why even if the game received bad critic reviews, many players are still enjoying it.Personally I will keep it.Hopefully it will be getting fixed and polished and additional content will surely come.UPDATE: Got hooked by the combat and the rpg mechanics. Loving Drizzt gameplay, my Lightning Fast Ninja Elf.He is a "high risk high reward" character but when you learn gradually it becomes more than a Assassin, he is a  Frenzy Killing Machine.The game works with VorpX for VR and you can play it in a giant IMAX cinema screen with 3D depth supporting Z-Normal/Z-Adaptive and Geometry 3D. I uploaded a profile but I will try to improve it.The entire game is very appealing visually.The fights look awesome chaining crazy moves. If you love DMC, Batman and good brawlers in general to name a similar range of styles you will enjoy this together with a great main story and RPG progression.The AI needs to be fixed on certain specific issues, like some enemies being able to hit them from a far point without reaction.  In the meantime you can use HONOR and trigger the fights directly. I jump into the battle directly or sneak but I start the combat chaos and problem fixed :)Devs are already fixing it and the first day patch already helped.The game will receive further content as characters and couch coop so I confirm my recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: The game itself feels much like a classic dungeon crawler from back in the day. If you're looking for fast paced action. This probably isnt for you. The pace itself isnt slow per say, but not as fast as some of the A-RPGs we're used to such as the new generation of MMORPGs. This is not a hack and slash game at all. There's a lot more that goes into combat than that and it seems like theres tons to master from Blocking, parrying, triggering team abilities, and other strats. Its pretty simple to learn and pretty fun to play. So far, Combat has been difficult but not impossible, but it seems like every group I've joined has taken on missions higher than our collective item level. Quickplay works well, but sometimes will throw you into a game with someone already taking your character and ask you to choose a different character. I've clocked in about 5 hours and 4 missions. Its a Yes for me so far. Just dont buy this expecting MMORPG type fast paced a-rpgs11.5hrs playedSecond part of review.It seems like I've reached end-game pretty much, Maxed out my Dwarfs move list, maxed out potions and anything I find I can use can be upgraded to max within 1-2 quickplay runs. This game is short and the replayability as an individual is pretty dismal. Combat is unforgiving with most monsters able to kill even the Tanky Dwarf within 2-3 hits. Combat is rather slow, think World of Warcraft Global cooldown, but no indicators. One attack after another, execute an attack too early? not even going to happen because you're still in the middle of the previous attacks animation. Move list is very limited as well. Overall 7/10 Graphics 8/10Gameplay 6/10

_childDocuments_.review: As a D&D game this falls way short. Game is worth $10-$15. 20-30 hours play time finished the game and not much I want to repeat. Super lame lets get this figured out or maybe I don't play your games anymore.I was level 20 for 1/3 of the game with no need for gold or experience. Some AAs here could make that more interactive. More than one voiceline from the stupid ass merchant per champion would've been a nice touch. Or just stop doing it after the first few times you enter the hideout.The loot system is pretty bad. _childDocuments_.review: This game is impressively bad.  Combat is extremely limited, attacks lack impact, AI is a joke and apparently it was even worse on release.  Enemy attack animations are poor, the tutorial is a by the numbers player controls explanation and nothing else (why are enemies outlined in red/yellow?, environmental hazards and how to negate them?, why did Wizards of the Coast greenlight this?), damage from and to the players seems to be all over the place.  On top of that this game is designed to be played with multiple people; enemy health pools are seemingly only affected by the difficulty rating you choose when starting a stage and they are all ridiculously large, but the online is so laggy as to make it unplayable.  I played with a friend on another computer in the same house on a fiber connection and the animation delays and enemy reaction delays made it like playing a slideshow.  This game is a joke, and it's a good one, it's just too bad it got played on everyone who bought this.

_childDocuments_.review: I am absolutely devastated.I bought this for myself and my partner after seeing the trailers and Gameplay Trailers and i have to say i am severely disappointed.Let's get the good out of the way first. It looks BEAUTIFUL. The soundtrack is amazing and got me hyped before i started the game. That's.. that's really it. It's made with Unreal Engine, so you'd expect it to be pretty.The best way of describing this would be to say they spent 80 percent of their budget on graphics and sound design and the combat in this game is incredibly lacklustre. I played both the big hammer dude, and the rogue, while my partner played the archer and the dwarf. First of all, having a button you have to hold to aim your bow is just a bad design choice. Holding a button down to attack is boring. She spent most of her time kicking enemies because it was, i quote "more fun than using the bow". Arrows shot by the bow chick have almost no impact on enemies. By that i mean there is no stagger or anything to even hint that she is doing any sort of damage, and i imagine it makes the character feel pretty useless. Also the starting sensitivity is insanely low.. also also, why when i move my mouse more, does it move the camera less? Please stop doing this, it's infuriating.The hammer dude's attacks are slow, sure, as they would be.. but the Recovery Animation frames are killer.. it takes so long to recover from attacks, it pulls you right out of the "ass kicking immersion", forces you to stop attacking for like, a month which means you can barely hit enemies before you need to stop attacking, just so you can wait out the recovery frames, so you can dodge. It is not fun combat at all, but this may just be due to the difficulty. And, the difficulty seems to be linked to how much the enemies attack. I know it sounds stupid when put like that, but they just taunt all the time.. it's just a button mashing, boring hail of attacks until the enemy stops moving. It was great being hit by an enemy that was nowhere near me too, that was fun.i will say, the rogue is BY FAR the most fun to play, and that is only because he is quick and nimble. You can press Mouse3 to aim at a enemy, but it puts the camera so low towards the ground i'm practically inside my characters Arse. When you attack from the air, you must make sure you don't jump on the enemy, because if you do, you will just float there for about 5 seconds before you finally hit the floor and do your attack.. this is very, very annoying, especially when you get hit by something else, and it breaks you out of your attack. Also, the more time you spend in the air, it seems the more stamina is spent on  the attack. Another thing about attacking (especially the rogue, with it being a close combat character) is almost every hit sends the enemy flying back.. And like i stated before with waiting for the character to stop doing his animation before you can do ANYTHING, you have to wait until the animation stops,  hope you didn't click again so he can do another attack just to wait out the animation, and run over to the enemy so you can hit him again. The just doesn't seem to be much flow at all.This game is way too unpolished for a final release. I wouldn't be bothered as such if it was early access or beta testing, but the fact this is a full release.. it's depressing. Put it this way, the characters feet don't even touch the ground.. Who tested this game? Why was it released like this?Also, multiplayer is so janky and the sync issues are bad. But, i did get thrown about 100ft into the air when using an elevator. i was tempted to give a good review just for that. Please make menu buttons way more noticeable, or at least let the player know they can press their arrow keys to show the next reward!. It took me 2 missions to realise when i was checking my rewards, there was literally a down arrow to go to the next reward.. I then spend a further 5 minutes running around the lobby looking for a way to open my inventory, only to press N accidentally, and it opens.. this is not good UI design!This game NEEDS a tutorial to let the player know how to attack, block, dodge, open inventories.. All in all, i was absolutely sucked in by the visuals and the gameplay trailer. And the way they showed their combat (in an empty arena.. with nothing around.. on their own..) to make it look really interesting is almost criminal. I also, don't think it helped that they literally took the title of "dungeons and dragons". I'm sorry, but who in their right minds would take a title as MONUMENTAL as D&D, try to make a game around it, and release it in this state?i'm so sorry i got this. and i wish i could leave a good review. But i'm so sick of being let down by trailers making a game look amazing.. when in reality it's barebones, janky and, quite frankly, boring.

_childDocuments_.review: Just to put it out there. This game has its ups and downs. It is a very aesthetically appealing design inside and out, the mechanics are pretty cool. But the bugs are sooooooo annoying I can safely say the game is not worth even remotely near what they charge for full price. Notably, there is a few quite game breaking bugs/glitches I have experienced first hand that would deter alot of people from playing right off the bat until these are resolved with patches by the DEVS at a later date. Some of the bugs I have experienced I will list below.The first one that alerted me was the joining a friends game feature, the connection and discovery process of finding and connecting to your friends game, including invite only modes are very unstable and will take you many tries just to be in the same game with even one of your friends. The second is upon finishing a level to its completion and seeing the "Tally Screen". Waiting for all of the stats to run its course and display until you are given the option to fast travel back to the camp. Instead of it working as it was supposed to 100% of the time. My friend was sent back to camp and I was stuck running around in the boss room with no way back out of it. Even escape didn't work. Nothing would happen, the only way out of the completed boss room was to Alt-F4 the game. Loading it up after I was greeted with nothing gained from completing the mission unlike my friend. I did not have any earned XP from the mission, no loot or level completion status on the map. Simply just a brand new, clean Level 1 character that I started with and all of my keybindings I spent time configuring to a place I felt content were wiped with it and set back to default as well. This was confronting. But still not the worst thing to have happened. That comes now, be prepared....Thirdly. And this is my pet peev so far. I had my Dwarf character maxed out, Max level is 20, I managed to reach (Done), all Feats and Moves obtained (Done), all potion buffs (Done), a Rank 4-5 LEGENDARY ITEM equipped in every wearable item slot which took me over 25 hours to collect just by grinding purely for Epic and Legendary loot only. (8 in total of these Legendary items were equipped on my Level 20 Dwarf when everything was wiped from existence). Then the game decided to freeze for whatever reason between Tabbing between programs I had running at the time. Tabbed back, oh wonderful the game is not responding. End the task in task manager, as this was my only option. Then booted up Dark Alliance again to continue my game progress. Oh cool. I NOW HAVE ZERO CHARACTERS ON MY ACCOUNT!!!! What the hell happened, and why are my key bindings and in game settings also set back to default, without me touching anything at all??!! I had 4 characters I made to play with friends, and also Solo characters just for myself to play as that are now just poof, Gone, without a trace they ever existed. But thanks for not wiping my achievements as well. How good.......Now, what kind of game apparently backs up game saves to the Steam cloud but also deletes them when something goes wrong, both locally on my hard drive and also the cloud save. So how is it that when something goes wrong, it just straight up deletes everything saved, characters, items, progress and individually tweaked settings. I'd love a developer to explain how everything I ever did in my game is now just permanently GONE, LIKE FOREVER!!?? So did I just waste my time playing and building characters built to a point I felt happy with? Those many hours of time and stress invested into getting to a point I was very happy with, for it to just freak out, stop working entirely and destroy all of the progress I made since playing the game from the date it launched? Why? Just why? Imagine this game had micro-transactions for items, skins whatever.... not just you grinding for literally all of your gear like you have to do anyway which everything drops at random and the rarer the gear the more time it takes to have the chance to possibly obtain something that works well with your characters setup. Then imagine, out of nowhere your game crashes spontaneously, you lose everything you ever did, all those hours spent, everything you ever spent money on if hypothetically they had micro-transactions for stuff. And the best answer you could get is, oh yeah wow yikes, there is no known fixes for these problems...sorry (says the developers). In no way is any of this okay? If you invest time into something, especially a game you enjoy, you want security knowing things will be backed up by your connection to the server passively in the background as you play (you know, like every game worth playing these days), or even multiple instances of the local save files updating over time, in case these things happen, which they do and absolutely have done. Its not a difficult concept. But losing everything from game errors is a big kick in the guts, no matter how far into the game you are.How do you justify selling a game with BUGS THIS EXTREME?! I was going to originally give this game an 8.5/10, if those problems weren't apparent. But after these things happened that have directly affected my game and more importantly my Game Save without warning, and with ZERO known fixes for any of these issues, including forums and information based help sites. To put it simply, I wouldn't want anyone to play it in this state, to enjoy yourself, be happy with your progress, then suddenly having it all ripped away because of already present issues that are yet to be resolved. I don't want anyone to be turned off a game that has great potential because of problems that can do more than just be a minor bit of lag here and there. Losing all of your hard work to a bug with no way to get it back, that's not a finished product, and shouldn't be released as such, not yet. I'm reluctant to give this game over a 2/10 at best. Save your money and wait for these issues to be patched, then I can be assured you will enjoy playing this game. But until that day comes, its just not worth investing in as of now.
