_childDocuments_.review: This game was released minimum 6 months too early without enough experienced gamers in the room or QA. It's a glitchy disaster wrapped around a love story to the Forgotten Realms. There's so much missing, there are so many bad design choices (targeting POV, hello? What?) and it feels just overall unfinished. I want really badly for this game to do well enough that content keeps getting made for it as a fan of the lore, but you need to fire anyone who greenlit this for release. I don't mean they made an oopsy, I mean they fundamentally don't understand videogame design in 2021. What I will say is, there's fun in this game. There is a kernel of something good in there, at least as a multiplayer experience, even among all the glitches my friends and I had fun in the scramble. Also, the music and visuals deliver, and the RA Salvatore fans will find a lot of fun nods to the universe. But the AI, limited 'moves' trees and feat trees, the balancing, the sound design (impacts are kinda awful), it just.. goes on and on. The VO is also a bit of a mess, a mix between awkward writing and awkward VO (Is Cattie Brie someone's niece or was she just sabotaged by direction?). Also, Bruenor is literally written in the books with a Scottish accent, like, phonetically written out. Soooo, who's the 35yr old pretending to be old and gruff with a whisper soft english accent? Please don't abandon this title, there's definitely a game worth reviving from this dumpster fire.

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute tragedy. The AI that the enemies operate with is, in the nicest way I can describe, incomplete. Enemies will loaf around, forget you exist, not react to projectiles (or even melee in some cases).This game is terrible, do not pay for it, and if you already have, refund it while you still can.Pros:its pretty (they took their time making the environment look good and forgot to make a game I presume) the voice acting is solid (I'm not a great judge of actors but I wasnt disappointed)the goblins have neat dialogue (the game is fairly well written if you view it from the perspective of anyone but the main characters)Cons:everything that is not the environment and/or the small snippets of conversations between characters.absolute trashfire. _childDocuments_.review: Online multiplayer is like playing D&D with a drunk DM. In both the good ways and the bad.Melee attacks land somewhere between before the animation starts and after the animation finishes. Seemingly at a random point somewhere therein. This basically renders the parry a useless gamble. The networking code needs a good rework, as well. Enemies skate across the screen, jitter through the world when killed, and attack in directions they aren't facing. Oh, and they'll hit you with a melee attack when they aren't anywhere close to you.The game's combat system was clearly set up for a flat world. Standing even two or three feet up a ramp makes you immune to ranged attacks, including the big guy's grapple.Combat is basically you fighting a couple different types of enemies on different maps and in different groupings. There are puzzles, kind of? and secret things, kind of?Look, I'm having fun with my friend in this game mostly by joking about how the DM is a drunk a--hole. Sometimes it works out for you, and sometimes it doesn't. If you kill the enemies too quickly, he'll spawn more. If you kill them too slowly, he'll laugh about how he thought you could take it while he resets the board. Enemies clipping around are him drunkenly reaching down for the tokens and dragging them across the board, knocking around all the others in the process.The game itself isn't that great. The combat system doesn't really fit with the platforming system, which doesn't really fit with the style of the game as a whole. It's really like a bunch of unrelated dev teams were all working on unrelated games, then some manager pulled it all together, barely tied it together with a few lines of code, dumped the D&D logo on it, and shipped it.

_childDocuments_.review: Full game with all bonus objectives w/ time stamps here (when it uploads)Review:I'm not going to lie I was greatly disappointed to find out this was a fantasy deep rock galactic spin off with a D&D/Gauntlet legends twist. I was really hoping this was going to be a Dark Alliance top down adventure game with better graphics and a great story like the original which didn't happen, you choose missions and you go through the stage. The first stage of every act has a cutscene and every act has a big bad which drops a trophy. I didn't play the multiplayer yet, but I have played the full single player difficulty level doesn't add harder mechanics, the game just straight up tests your patience as the enemies are the same and heavily abuseable, if you need to the enemies can be leashed away from their starting area and you can kill them as they go back to their area minus of the final boss of the stage every area should actually block the player in like the final boss does temporarily to avoid cheesing the enemies. You can use terrain to abuse them as well which actually adds strategy so that's pretty nice and some of the bosses at the end are slightly difficult on the easiest game mode. It's not a bad game, but it's definitely not what I was expecting it's good, not great. The Game being under the original dark alliance banner is just a bait to get you to get the game, there's not much in common, in this game you're already a well accomplished hero I'm not even sure what the story at the intro of the game comes from tbh I'm not sure if it's from an established module or dark alliance 2? I feel we should have started a brand new adventure with fledgling heroes even if it was the beginnings of the companion of the hall and an adventure type game. It doesn't deserve the immensely negative reviews the game has received, it's completely beatable, the graphics are nice, dialogue is kinda entertaining, it has a ton of unlockable lore, and some cool boss fight, but again it's not what I was expecting and a huge let down for me personally. EDIT: I was also thinking about it and something else that really grinds my gears is you literally get no cutscenes of the heroes after the introduction to the game before you play, which is lame you see them do nothing awesome outside of your own play, you don't see them grow, you don't see them show their relationships I think that's actually the biggest miss and most annoying thing of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: The game seems really cool and has a lot of concepts i like. it also has enjoy loot grinding if you like that sort of thing, which i do. however, i cant say i recommend it. i have a bunch of things i dislike as well as a few nitpicks that ends up being death by a thousand cuts for me.as a number of reviews ive seen say, the difficulty is a little silly. at recommended level you are nearly unstoppable, but any difficulty above that and you will often get one shot killed. this makes me assume, (though i havent played in a group so i cant confirm) that the games difficulty is based entirely around group play. so while you can play solo, it feels lackluster. like you are noticeably missing out. which creates a catch 22 where i could recommend my friends buy it and see if it gets more fun with friends, but since i dont feel its currently recommendable, i wouldnt feel right doing so.combat early game is also lackluster. you have light attack, and heavy attack, and two abilities on cool downs. this magnifies the feeling for me that the game is only meant to be played with a full group of players. you can unlock more abilities as you advance to add a little variety, which is standard for the rpg experience so no complaints there. however after unlocking three new abilities i found myself having to make an effort to remember to use them, which also leads back to the first thing i mentioned which is difficulty, and on normal difficulty enemies are so easy you need not bother.couple other small nitpicks that arent game breaking, but again just compound the large gripes; your loot/gear affects your appearance and your stats. this is very common in games like this so i dont fault this game in adopting it, just wish games would stop using this because i have to choose between having my character look cool or have good stats. and sadly this game does have an appearance feature for your gear which i was really excited about at first when the tooltip popped up, but it was another let down as all it does is change the color pallete and not the actual appearance. the hub where you upgrade your character, shop at the merchant, etc is very bare bones. it gives me a monster hunter world vibe where i start in the hub, select my mission, go do said mission than return to hub. however there is nothing to do here. it might as well have been a menu for all the features of it. the only npc is the "merchant" which they didnt bother to give a name. and strange complaint here but his animation isnt synced up to his random voice overs. i honestly spent a few minutes trying to figure out who was talking to me/where the source of the voice over was before i realized that it was coming from the merchant and they just couldnt put in the effort to animate mouth movement.my last nitpick is that i would have preferred not to have the character pregen named characters. i get that many people are excited to play as drizzt, and that playing as these characters fits the narrative of the game, which is why this is the lowest gripe on my list. but i personally would prefer in a rpg game based on dnd that i would have a little more agency to create my character(s). also, am i the only one confused by the fighter class character being the archer/sniper?

_childDocuments_.review: To note, I am a huge fan of action games and I huge fan of the Dungeons and Dragons franchise. I DM two games a week and read the entirety of the Legend of Drizzit series. I'm not unlike any of you. I played this game two patches in so I did not have as many A.I issues so I won't be speaking of those.I wanted this game to be better than what it is.This game reminded me a lot of Borderlands 2. Borderlands 2 is a good looking game with many gameplay mechanics. Borrderlands 2 is also EXTREMELY hard to play solo. Without your teammates you tend to struggle fron the get go. Dark Alliance is no different. Dark Alliance was made with multiplayer in mind, meaning that the solo experience can be extremely challenging as you play the game. "Get Gud" or whatever, it gets to a point where the game stops being fun due to mechanical difficulties and not game challenge. You have a block and a parry while being attacked on all sides. Unlike a game like Dark Souls where positioning is important, positioning matters little in Dark Alliance. You will always have ranged enemies striking from behind while enemies you're parrying are up front. Meanwhile, there will be enemies with unblockable AOE attacks near you. Every enemy is centered upon you at the same time. Going back to multiplayer, this wouldn't be the case when paired with playing with others, as the aggro is split among the players. The damage ratio also needs work, as your damage even at the lowest levels does very little in comparison to enemies. Oh, and the fact that there are status aliments that prove to be a constant threat throughout the levels granted by the environment and enemies alike keep you constantly on edge. The game is hard, but not in a satisfying way.\To compliment the above, I also feel the need to mention that the hit boxes on many enemies and their attacks also have their issues. Case in point, the frost giants. They conduct an attack where they slide their axes to the ground towards you. I have dodged this attack, even have gotten behind them, and still took damage. Trolls act in the same manner as well as the harpoon attacks that some characters have later on.  A harpoon can miss you by a mile yet still grab you and pull you in. My most egregious complain lies for when you're prone. Case in point, you are susceptible to damage while prone. To get up it takes roughly five seconds, during which you can be attacked my multiple enemies. I have gone from full health, prone, and then dead within that five second period. That is not a challenge that can be learned and overcome by the player, it just sucks. The game however is extremely good looking and the cutscenes are fantastic. If you have a group of friends willing to buy this alongside you then you will have fun. This is not a game for a solo or quick online experience (The reviews saw to many others purchasing this game).Hasbro and Wizards have money. They can afford a better studio than Tuque games.

_childDocuments_.review: Have requested a refund. Wanted to like it. Wanted to ignore other reviews, and wanted to enjoy it. Couldn't do it. While the game is pretty and has most of the 'mechanics' that you'd want in a game of simple hack & slash with a tiered loot system it doesn't have much more going for it than that. And that includes things that it should have that it doesn't.It's simply unpolished as a lot of other reviewers have stated. What does this mean? [Here's where the ramble begins] enemies are slow to react - when they do react it doesn't matter what direction they're facing they're going to hit you anyways (ever try to dodge in pokemonGo? yeah it's like that.) - you can't access character menu while on missions (but it doesn't tell you that? I probably spent 5 minutes thinking it was user-error... before realizing it's intentional, but opaque) - input latency (push a button and it takes a second and not in a PC problem or a 'working as intended' type of way) - loot is just.... places? feels like an early 90's game where the devs took a map of the level and threw darts to determine where coin purses were (side of the road randomly with nothing around it rather than on a table in the base? Although there's some in the base too occasionally so there was SOME thought into it... but then why the schizophrenic placement?) - remember that you can't get to your character menu in a mission? that means no moveset list either. Bought a new technique? hope you memorized it already. I swear I found a ring in a box during a mission... but you can't see it (even 'undiscovered') so when I hit the end of the mission... no ring? Can't tell if I'm crazy, or I misremembered, or it's a bug. There's no transparency. You basically have to ignore whatever you THINK you got during a mission and just be surprised at the end. This ramble isn't comprehensive... but it gives a 'feel' for the overall lack of polish. It's not worth the price tag, and it's not honestly worth the headache.Overall I'd say... imagine the LOTR game for the PS2 (LOTR return of the king?) from around 2006 ... but clunky and MORE button mashy (and I LOVED the old LOTR games and WISH this would have emulated them) ... instead it's 2021 and given the choice of the 2006 game or this one... I'd buy the '06 one twice.I have low confidence that the dev's will fix this, but hope I'm wrong. There's too many things that if I was a dev/publisher and had play tested it halfway through the development I would have gone back to the drawing board on that piece and feel like it's too fundamental of a problem to patch out. Maybe I'm wrong and they'll refurbish it. Have seen other games do it... but wish it wasn't such a pervasive problem in this title.Glad people enjoy it. It frustrates me too much to play it and that frustration makes it very unfun. There's too many other games out there that I get more enjoyment out of for less time commitment that are everything that this game tries to be.

_childDocuments_.review: I find this game to be quite interesting and fun. Is it perfect? what game is... if you play this game for what it is and stop comparing it to every other damn game that comes out or has been in existence...you might actually enjoy it. There are quarks where the AI is kinda dumb and just stands there, but to be honest, it was in our favor when people kept dying so much and allowed us to rez our party members. The cut scenes are actually very well done and look beautiful. There is a little bit of levity in there when dealing with the Goblins and Orcs too and I find that funny as hell. Some purists would argue that it should be more dark and sinister. Well, let's go down to the local goblin village and just see how REAL this interpretation is...I'll Wait.... THATS RIGHT....ITS FANTASY MAN! Just because it doesnt fit YOUR perception of what YOU think Goblins and Orcs should act, doesnt make it a bad game. I loved it. It caught me off guard and really got a chuckle out of me.The combat can seem a bit slow and clunky as they say, but not horrible. Playing Drizzt, sometimes my skills were firing and I was a virtual windmill and other times I felt my attacks were quite slow. This is WITH my stamina bar full, for those who are about to ask.  Characters, like DnD itself were weak and kinda meh at the beginning levels (as one would expect), but as you leveled and got gear, skills and feats. Holy smokes, they really came alive and were amazing! So anyone who hasnt leveled past say... level 10 and says the characters suck....prolly never played DnD before and knows how to level and gear a toon. Give it a chance, level that toon, get some gear, you'll see.Playing solo is very underwhelming. Each character has their strong points and as a team, are GREAT together, but solo.... not so much. You would probably have a decently hard time do anything past tier 2 or 3 unless you were a gaming god.One of the complaints is how can this be DnD and NO MAGE CHARACTER!!! My reply.. READ A DAMN BOOK! This game was modeled off of the novels by R.A.Salvatore and in the books, THESE are the 4 main characters. Now there are more and they could put them in at a later date, but no mage as of yet. So keep your pantyhose on people. If you want the whole every class available and character customization, go play Baulders Gate 3 or any of those games. This game reminded me a lot of Vermantide in many aspects, but in third person. I loved that game, but the first person killed me. So for me....this is a bonus. I love the game and I think that it has a lot of potential. I cant wait to see what they come up with next. Keep up the good work and tidy up those things that you have noticed and are mentioned in numerous forums and you will be on the right track.

_childDocuments_.review: Advice for Game mechanics1.	The matching mechanism needs a complete overhaul. Added custom rooms and lobbies, allowing players to select some of the rooms. In addition, let the player choose whether to exclude the same hero from a room. And “quick match” automatically excludes the same hero so that the player can find the room faster.2.	To make combat more balanced, the damage of monsters need to be adjusted. And some boss are too weak, and some are too OP.3.	Monsters should be balanced on a per-player basis to make sure players don't get too easy or too hard quest. Also make the Quest difficulty applicable to the map (Just like 《Dying Light》, Pls developers, you guys really need to take a look at mainstream games how to do it ) 4.	Added new servers, Asia, Europe, Middle East, etc. At the moment, a lot of players have to live with the high PING, and most players will only play offline mode in this situation, which is very bad.5.	Adjusted all monsters' Hitbox so that their attack actions match their true range.6.	The damage caused by the environment to the player is too high and should be reduced. In addition, werewolve’s “bleed state” so much OP that let they can kill players instantly, It's unbalanced.7.	Please Fixed 5 classes of gear on 4000(Red 6 difficulty) power missions. Right now, class 5 gear is just too hard to get. Because it's so hard to "graduate" just one hero, it makes players less inclined to play other hero.8.	Added random gear entry system, which allows players unlimited to be changed gear entry on merchants using gold.( Late in the game, the player's gold becomes meaningless )9.	After the player reaches the upper limit of level (LV20), the hero can still continue to level up, and after leveling up, the hero can receive some of reward(Coins, materials or gear and something else). It also displays on other players' UI (like the HR level in the MH series. Represents how long plays in the game).10.	Add more help and explanation to game terminology so players can understand the meaning of various states.11.	The scarecrow cannot be attacked from behind, it should be placed in a wider area with more detailed Settings (e.g., scarecrow does not get stuck in unusual condition, armor value adjustment and resistance adjustment).12.	Add more maps. And make the rewards of all maps balanced. The Boss quests should be able to earn higher individual rewards (exclusive equipment or something), rather than relying entirely on bonfire loot rewards. Whether a map with attribute point bonuses has already been claimed should be displayed in the map selection UI.13.	Added reset options for attribute/actions and passive ability (can cost the player gold).14.	Added chat box for players. And let players can communicate with specific emoji or something. In addition, in the base, add some players can interact with the mini-game(It's like a dice game).15.	There should be no waiting time when a party is wipe. At the same time, Settlement reward should can be speed up UI (calculated individually per player).And there are a lot of bugs out there, but I'm not in the mood to mention them because there are so many things that don't make sense that I'm not going to pay attention to them.I don't recommend it because it's an unfinished game.

_childDocuments_.review: I was hopeful that all of the negative reviews and YouTube content was overblown, but after playing the game myself for about 45 minutes I refunded it. Controls are choppy, with an input delay between button press and in game action, another delay between animation and hit affect, and a noticeable lag between enemy animation and in game affects. The UI makes it obvious that this was poorly ported for PC, with slider bars that can't actually be dragged and default keybindings that make no sense (left and right on arrow keys to change lock on targets, but middle mouse button to lock on and WASD to move. Guess I need 3 hands to play this game). I had to set my keybindings 4 times in my less-than-an-hour playtime because some or all of them would revert, got stuck after hitting a training dummy before even starting my first mission (which has to be done before playing with friends, yet it doesn't tell you that so you have no idea what you're doing until you go back to offline mode and try again) and had a blue outline artifact stuck on my screen for 5 minutes. I wanted to love this game but it's a hard no in its current state.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played roughly 27 hours, hopefully this review will help anyone interesting in purchasing.This game has a few minor glitches that made early game a bit frustrating, but after working through it, the game is pretty fun! At first I didnt like the game at all, and that was a 'me issue,' I came in expecting it to be more like the old school Baldurs Gate, or Champions of Norrath. This game has similarities, but not quite the same. At first I didnt like the combat system, mostly because it felt a little clunky and reminded me of Elder Scrolls online with the attacks and skill trees, at least for Catti.1) early game, it was difficult to work out the combos because the game just showed pictures of arrows for key presses, and going into the controls, it didnt say which key went to said picture. After some head banging, I realized it was tab. Tab to parry. Freaking tab. Im either THAT blonde, or the game could give a bit more for less user friendly peoples.2) Running missions at the board is great, but after the missions, while trying to equip your sweet sweet loot, you'll find it darn near impossible to click on your necklace and the ring, unless you find that sweet spot. I kept closing the inventory over and over, trying to get it to work, til I accidently discoverd you have to click the bottom of the necklace and ring icon box to get in. After that discovery, easy sailing.3) I absolutely do NOT like the lock on skill. Maybe with more practice Ill get better, but for now, no. With Catti, when you lock on, it zooms you in on said target and you have some significant blind spots. Ive died more from those blind spots than anything else. Also, the key function to switch between targets is the arrow keys by the num pad, and that cant be changed in the options. So, if you want to use the skill, and you want to switch targets to cycle through enemies to the boss, you have to either be a monster and release your precious mouse and risk a smacking, or a psychopath and use your left hand which prevents you from moving and dodging. Overall, I hate this, and I highly recommend NOT to use it. Especially in the later, more difficult, runs.4) Sometimes the enemies health bar doesnt pop up. Here's where this gets annoying, especially on Catti. You pop your ultimate skill to summon your awesome bow of doom, your melee characters are knocking the boss around, and youre panicking to see where the stupid little goblin boss is through your bows blinding light, you shoot towards your melee friends, miss, desperate, you shoot again, a hit, and the skills done. FU*K! Now. You can lock targets, you psychopath you, or you can shoot "in the dark."5) The ranged bow skills, volley ect, are NOT fun to aim with on Catti. Again, it may be a me issue and my silly depth perception, but I cant ever seem to get my range right. One time I shot and it went over some wall into the abyss, which sucked and took away precious damage. It would be awesome if, eventually, the game could impliment a circular graphic for the shots, or at least when focusing an enemy, the skill hits said enemy instead of going waaayyyeeee over there. Till then, all my Catti friends, CTRL + LMB power shots = AOE win.Conclusion: This is a new game, its not even been out for 2 weeks, over all, getting past my own biases and expectations, this is a really fun game. Right now, armor sets are a little lack luster, the element armors are useless stat set wise, but pretty. I'm one of those players who really want to min-max my favorite character, so its both a blessing and a curse that the maps are exactly the same. Blessing in that, I can roll through 6s and get that sweet sweet loot from chests, cursed because it will eventually kill its replayability for most. This game has some bloody awesome humor in it at random intervals that makes me chuckle and give thumbs up to the Chefs Bird.I know there's a lot of mixed reviews for this game, and Im trying to be as honest as possible, because at first, I wanted to say "Fu*ck it," but give it a chance. Read my review, see whats up, and if you're a fan of DnD, give it a shot. This game can only get better, with new maps, new lore, new gear (drool). I really cant wait to see what else this game has to offer!!

_childDocuments_.review: At the current state, the game feels unfinished.I played with a friend through the first level and the difficulty varies wildly.  Enemies are almost oblivious to us, but at the same time there's not an easy way to dispatch them.  The combat system doesn't lock on properly and feels like it's missing some elements.  The combos are not intuitive and the delay in attacks feels a bit odd.  The issue we both encountered was the janky controls.  There's no way to really explain how that feels until you play it. Difficulty spikes insanely with the different options.  I played each character through the first level or parts of it.  Catti-Brie is definitely a bit cheesy with the ranged attacks.  You can dispatch the entirety of the first level with no real challenge with her, however, bump up the difficulty and be prepared to just rage.  The difficulty is based more on gear/stats than actual challenge as enemies do more damage and have more health.As it currently stands, I'd recommend a pass, but worth watching to see what develops with this.  If you have a group of friends the game seems like it's catering towards that, but solos should avoid in my opinion.

We did this over 10 times before we had to tab the game closed to get out. I am very disappointed. The overall design and graphics are really well thought out and we both enjoyed finding loot, this game has great potential so I hope they work these bugs out. I am definitely not a gaming expert but even for me i found Dark alliance to be like a seriously bad relationship, looks great on the outside but on the inside its just consuming all your humanity. I definitely will be keeping an eye on this game for updates and if Tuque can turn this game around I will play the crap out of it!

_childDocuments_.review: ok. so a lot of reviews for this game have been extremely negative. i wanted to put my perspective out there. these dungeon crawler/ rpg games are really high up on my list. i love these games and the way they feel. i loved vermintide, minecraft dungeons, diablo, etc. but this game being tuques second game to release was expected at least from me to be a little rough. ok so lets get the negatives out of the way first. the game is rough and unpolished. the animations could use a little work, for example, katabries bow animation. her head and body stay completely still while her arms are in full motion. for me its unrealistic but isnt anything game breaking. so far i havent seen any "game breaking" bugs. the worst i've seen is while me and my friend played he had to return to his own camp to retrieve his gear and this only happened once. the game is a little clunky but over time i think this game will have all of these issues fixed.the good news. people say the gameplay is repetitive but when you get into a game like this its something to expect, especially in the first hour or so when you havent unlocked many abilities. the game is fun and you shouldnt expect to be able to play a  difficulty up when its meant to be for higher level players. one of the biggest complaints ive heard is that its very hard if you dont play the recomended difficulty. these games are like that and you should expect it. overall i think the game is rough but fun and can use some work but is definetly worth the buy and or wait for when they polish out the game.

name: The Invisible Hand
detailed_description: The Family Office Update NOTHING SUCCEEDS LIKE SUCCESS. As a trader, you’ve amassed enough wealth for FERIOS that somebody in the Miller Family Office has decided to retain you as their personal financial advisor. Will you fail miserably, or will you be so successful that even more powerful and shadowy members of the family make you their golden goose instead? In this update to The Invisible Hand, explore a new and improved Endless Mode that will allow you to gradually control entire percentages of the global economy on behalf of the wealthiest people nobody has ever heard of. As an Endless Mode player, your options are immeasurable. Do you have what it takes to make the numbers so big that it forces us to patch the game to allow for even bigger numbers? Can you delay our future projects and ruin our lives for the sake of a pointless abstraction? Can you test the implied warranty of the word ‘endless’ for some indecipherable purpose? The choice is yours. Of course, Endless Mode will be accessible to all players who purchase The Invisible Hand whether they begin by playing through the original campaign or not - just don’t say we didn’t warn you. About the Game Congrats on your new job! Welcome to the first-person world of a mid-level stockbroker, as you begin your very first day at the trading firm FERIOS. You’ve probably wanted this job since you were six, right? Well, so have a lot of people… so you'll have to fight for it and prove that you're the top dog for the job! Just remember: profit is all that matters, the rules don’t apply if you’re a winner, and only losers feel guilty for the pain, loss and poverty that are the unfortunate but unavoidable by-product of the critical and important work we do here. It’s simple: your job is to make money for FERIOS. Buy the stocks going up, sell before they go down. Short the ones that are going to fall (or the ones you’re going to make fall). The more money you make, the bigger your commission. And you want that commission, don't you? Well don’t worry, the rewards are limitless, if you’re hungry enough. If you’re really smart, you’ll find ways to influence the market to your advantage. Think you can lobby an influential group to affect the market? Do it. Get an opportunity to acquire majority shares to move the needle? Take it. Drive down the currency of a foreign country to improve the margins of the companies that import their products? Why not? The only consequences that matter are the ones that impact our bottom line. Every Joe Schmo has access to the regular news. If you want to get ahead of the spikes and crashes you’ll need to find the inside line from more, shall we say, “exclusive” sources. And definitely don’t let those rumors of a financial investigation get you down. No one employed by FERIOS has ever been found guilty! We’re one big happy team here at Ferios and nothing brings the team together like competition. So in the spirit of togetherness you better meet your daily profit targets and beat your coworkers’ results if you want to keep your job. We won’t hesitate to fire anyone who can’t or won’t do what it takes to succeed... The fruits of success are yours for the taking. Fast cars, lavish parties, fancy apartments filled with beautiful furniture and artworks. Of course, for any truly successful trader, work is its own reward and their true home is the office so it’s a good thing you can decorate your desk with photos of all your wonderful things to remind you they exist.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really entertaining and makes a good caricature of finance culture. The stock market mechanics are satisfying and I enjoyed playing that out. However the campaign is really short and doesn't actually take into account what you did. I was making a killing by playing it straight so I never used the cheaty tools but the game just assumed I was and doing it poorly. I'd love a version where playing the market takes longer and is more challenging OR one that actually reacts to whether or not you are breaking the law.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invisible Hand

_childDocuments_.review: The game needs some work thats for sure. Genuinely, surprised the creators of the game didn't make the game a lead up to 2008 financial crisis. This would make for a very interesting game as it would get harder and harder to make money... Genuinely devs, if you want to create an expansion that revolves around this idea I would buy it thats for sure!Rating this game is difficult, but I had no bugs, I had zero issues, really the only problem I'd say I had was it was a bit short, and theres no endless mode. Oh, and theres no save option which seems like a horrid choice. The story really isn't that great either which is sad. But honestly, if you're here for the story... Why? This is a stock market game...Anyway, 7/10, great idea, could have been implemented better, and had more content.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is dull and has no content. Everything the game has to offer gets shown to you within the first hour or so. The gameplay consists of you looking at the games version of tweets and then buying or shorting stock accordingly.There is no tactics involved with it at all. Tweet say stock go up? Buy stock, then sell it a couple ingame hours later.Tweet say stock go down? Short it and buy back the position a few ingame hours later.You can influence the price of certain goods / materials via lobbying but the mechanic essentially is just you spending cash to make the price of something go up or down. None of your actions have any lasting consequences. Within an ingame day everything is back to normal.You can't destabilize another ocuntries economy and there are no dynamic events such as forest firest or similar that will impact you in the long term.At the end of the day you get paid  private money that you can use to buy houses that will generate you additional private money whose sole purpose is to... buy more houses. You can't upgrade your workstation, you can't get your own office. Nothing.The UI is atrocious. It takes up way too much space. It's a shame since the game gives you 4 monitors. Two of which are useless, the other one you only look at once per day, if at all.The devs easily could have implemented a system that'd let you buy monitors, view multiple monitors at the same time and put the information you want freely on the monitor to let you customize your workspace but no. None of that is in the game.After the day ends you can spend cash to increase the friendship level with your co-workers. As far as I can tell, this does nothing. All it does is be a cash sink.The last goal of becoming managing director is literally not achievable. The goalpost gets moved further and further back whenever you are about to achieve it.The game isn't even giving you the satisfaction of owning everything. No, when you reach a certain amount of stocks owned the game resets your progress, forcing you to do the dull grind all over again. Your reward are upgrades such as "25% more dividends" or "50% increased trade volume" - The trade volume one feels insulting because really the default trade volume should be much higher than it is. It's just more padding for a game that consists of only padding.On top of that, the game doesn't follow its own rules. It introduces "Danger Zones" but then prices don't rebound or crash when you purposefully navigate the prices inside of them, the danger zone just "vanishes" and nothing happens.Sometimes you lose public order despite not even using lobbyists. In my last playthrough I got game overed because somehow the game thought I lowered public order, when in truth, my public order went UP because I DIDN'T USE ANY LOBBYISTS.So either the game is buggy or it doesn't follow the rules and boundaries it sets. It's frustrating.This game is one wasted opportunity. It would have been nice if you could have worked your way up into owning the company, paying off politicians, influencing politics and the world at large. Instead what you get is a mindless clicker game that has you achieving absolutely nothing.Buy this game when it's on sale for 3€ or so, it hardly is worth more than that.

_childDocuments_.review: Read the full review here: Invisible Hand is a screed against the financial industry dressed in black humor and then further wrapped in the guise of token gameplay to get players to sit through the story the game was made to convey to players.  The gameplay elements are mostly what you would expect - stocks go up and down in value according to random events in the background you can follow through a Twitter analogue on the left side of your screen.  You can buy stocks low and sell high normally, called a "long", but you can also "short" stocks, borrowing and selling high then trying to buy them back low to make money at someone else's loss.  (Whose loss?  Who cares, probably some guy thinking he could retire's retirement account.) This means that if you're on top of the trends, you can make money both with stocks going up and down.You can also make those trends, because you can lobby governments to either help or harm a given industry or even a whole nation's economy.  This is the "Invisible Hand" the title refers to, and the main argument above and beyond the usual arguments to more heavily regulate the financial industry that this game makes. By deliberately tanking a market, you can make money shorting it, profiting off of other people's losses, or even outright destabilizing whole nations or even the global market while doing nothing to help the economy, yourself, all for your own personal profit.  [Insert Bond villain laugh here.]The game is also highly critical of the toothlessness of financial regulators when the people who make the laws are in the pockets of the same big-money industries they are trying to regulate.  The game starts you off with an ethics questionnaire where the firm has already pre-filled in the correct answers so you can just punch "continue" without even bothering to read them, and further has the woman overseeing your taking of the test insult you if you do take the time to read them.  It helps set the tone for the game overall.Significant spoilers follow: At the end of the game, after letting the player do many terrible things, it holds its metaphorical trial for the financial industry There's a total lack of subtlety in what the game is doing... that said, looking at the other reviews, it seems no amount of bluntness is blunt enough, as people still seem to be rating this game purely on whether it is a good stock broker simulator.  I have to admit, there's a certain line you have to balance between spelling it out for the kids in the back of the class and ruining the tone for the people paying attention, but this still feels like it stepped too far on the speaking VEEERY LOOOUUUD AND SLOOOOW side.Another major tonal weakness that the game has in trying to make its criticisms land is that the game only lets you see things from the perspective of the guy staring at a stock ticker, flushing economies down the toilet to see his own personal number score go up - which is part of the point of the game, for sure - yet it needs to do more than just tell you that bad stuff happened somewhere else in a news report you don't even have to pay attention to, you need to see the actual negative consequences of your actions for them to connect the way that the game seems to want them to.  As it stands, you see far more consequences to your rival co-workers that all wind up being fired for failing to make as much money as you do, and they're basically all psychopaths played for laughs.All told, as a game, it's paced well, in that it rolls out new mechanics fairly regularly and doesn't overstay its welcome, but you probably won't get more than about 10 hours of this game before feeling bored.  As a story, it has a message worth telling, and makes some decent jokes in furtherance of that goal, but it really doesn't stick the landing.

_childDocuments_.review: How to start describing this game...? I might as well start with the setup for the first day: You're given a quick "ethics test" at the start of the game, with the correct answers already marked. While you do the test, your boss remarks on each question on the test, setting up one fact in particular: None of those rules will apply to you.Once you start your first day proper, you end up in a situation where the market is on a downward trend, your options for making a profit are limited, and you're trapped in a contest with an expert to decide who gets to stay with the firm. On the other hand, you have insider information telling you that if you wait for just the right time, Coffee's going to have a boom. The tutorial's already forced you to buy coffee anyways, why not just go with what it says and let it all work out...?As the intro of the game establishes, while this is technically a game about buying and selling stocks, the emphasis on the game is more on  than truly understanding the market.Your primary tools to understand the market come in the forms of two things, which I'll class as "Unreliable Information" and "Reliable Information". Unreliable Information primarily comes from short messages from various analysis groups of dubious quality, who may or may not affect the market for a limited period of time. You can guess their accuracy by how many "likes" they've gotten, but by the time they've been verified as correct, you've also missed your best chance to earn a profit, so part of the game is trying to figure out when to try to go with the flow to make a profit and when to completely ignore the tips altogether. Reliable Information on the other hand, comes in two forms: "Insider Information" which generally gives an indication of a massive change in things at a preset time which can be leveraged for profits if you're prepared, and "News Articles" that indicate 3 trends that will persist throughout the day. You only get one of the two each day, with Insider Information mostly being plot-related. My own personal experience of course, is that since Insider Information tends to invoke a quick profit at a single point in the day while the news articles give us trends that continue throughout, you'll generally make more profit with news articles than insider information.But rather than dealing with all of that, what about if you can just... Change the market however you like? And this is where most of the gameplay is focused: Early on in the game, you're given the ability to make use of Lobbyists, which you can use to drive the stocks up and down to achieve your goals. You can only have up to 16 lobbyists working at a time, and they cost money to hire, but they allow to direct the market as you will, barring the fact that if you do it wrong, it can have disastrous effects on the market, and get people very upset with you personally.Every product on the market has a limit to how high or low it can go: Once it reaches that point it triggers a rebound, which increases people's distrust in you, and eventually results in fines. To make matters worse, some products on the market use other products on the market as materials, so the prices of products further down on the supply chain can have effects on everything higher up on the chain. The game is thus about deciding about how to manipulate the markets: Are you going to play it safe, or take the risk of collapsing the market to help push your plans along?Either way, I found the main plot enjoyable, though the main story did end surprisingly quickly; While apparently the game can last until Day 37, I made it to the "ending" by Day 16 on my first run. The better you are at making money, the faster the plot goes by.

_childDocuments_.review: Cool game but:As someone who is in institutional finance, this isn't how modern trading is done at all; Lots of QoL missing. Instead this is very much a simulator for "unsophisticated retail" finance, where you trade based off of gut instinct. This feels more like a simulator for guys who trade from their phone on Robinhood who are on FinTwit.You can't employ even simple well-known finance trading strategies like mean-reversion or momentum since the longest lookback period is simply 1d. Instead you are simply trading based off of "social media" posts and news information. No institution with a few billion dollars of market cap, like Citi, Blackrock, etc. works like this - only small firms with a few hundred million might (and these are not the firms who comprise "the invisible hand").The absence of other instruments like derivatives, hedging, etc. but the explicit inclusion of dividends is also strange, considering the market price movement mechanics seem pretty developed - buying stock drives the price up, and selling stocks drives the price down, and they seemingly obey a random walk with some level of covariance where it's logical to have. Derivative pricing would be simple to implement with what is here.The tools for learning how to implement information arbitrage is here, but slightly lacking. The niche for this game is for people who are interested in market dynamics, but I frankly think this needs more options (no pun intended) for me to recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: The game looks promissing at first but quickly turns repetitive.The economic model is horrible broken. You can short an umlimited amount of stocks in a given company without considering the companies networth. Combine that with companies paying out unlimited dividend percentages and you have a money printing machine on steroids. Short one unlucky business and go long on another while signing a dividend contract. On day 3 you have billions and billions comming in from your million dollar investment. Go figure how a business stays afloat paying out 300000% dividends.After that there is absolutely no challenge playing this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game a masterpiece? Well, it is a broker simulation. Not a completely realistic one, of course, but you won't understand much of the game if you have no idea what going short or buying long positions means. Basic stock market knowledge is highly recommended, even though everything is explained to you. You are a broker, and do what brokers do. Buying and selling shares or currencies. And conducting a few insider trades, of course.The game starts with a (very) little test with realistic questions to determine your ethic qualifications, but even dummies pass it because it is a multiple choice test and the correct answers are already pre-selected for you. Then you start in your new job as a broker in a trading firm - in front of your computer, trading stock. You also have access to frequent insider informations, which makes your job so much easier. Watching the news ticker and share price development is still recommended. If you want, you can drink a coffee (to accelerate time), but you might miss important things that way.Be successful, and the company unlocks additional transactions you can perform and showers you with bonifications (that you can spend with the help of your company to buy useless status symbols). Miss your daily profit targets, and you are on the street. The game is not limited to just sit in front of your computer and watch your monitors, you can also walk around the office, talk to colleagues and deceive them, manipulate stock prices... do everything necessary to be better than your colleagues and make the most profit!A sarcastic, exaggerated and not very subtle simulation of the career of a (dirty) broker in a trading firm. Profit is all that matters.

_childDocuments_.review: Could be good but seriously bizarre choices. I bought this on recommendation from pcgamer which makes me question pcgamer honestly. I played an hour and half until the game bugged out and I couldn't access the computer in game. Went back to menu to try to reset it and apparently there is no save game as the game just restarted. Honestly kind of baffled, how could this be released and recommended by pcgamer when there literally is no saved games?It's possible there is one saved game slot and it just didn't save for some reason? But then there's no place to see saved games or a "start new campaign" feature which makes me think there is no saved games.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fun, but whether it's worth $13 USD is debatable. Why? The story is barely there and is EXTREMELY short. It took me a whopping 3 hours to "beat" the game, after which you try and try in an endless mode to reach a promotion that they never give you because they keep moving the goalposts. I've seen a developer on the forums mention that this is actually intentional because real companies do this a lot. It might be realistic, but take a little creative license guys, especially when it's implied that you're supposed to get closer to the family that runs the company and you're well on your way to doing so. Seriously, that's where the game ends: Right after you're told that.Do I recommend this game? Yes and no. Yes because it is in fact fun, but no because of the price versus the content you get. I got it at $10 USD or so during a flash sale and still feel a little ripped off. If you can get it for $5 or $7 (or if you don't care) then I'd say go ahead and get it. Any more than that? Not worth it. The game's sole intent seems to be to get the player to spend more than 2 hours playing it so they can't refund it.As a response to the developer, who said "We have added more content to the game with the latest update, I hope you'll enjoy !": Adding a couple of perks to allow you to fly through the endless "Prestige Mode" (as apparently that's what you call the boring, story-less endless mode) faster does not a content update make. Flying faster through boring repetitiveness for no reason is still going through boring repetitiveness for no reason. You just get to do it faster, that's all. Not gonna be checking that out since I play games to be entertained, not bored out of my skull.

Right now this game is like Gamestop's 2021 ascension to the moon...short lived. But, be like me, a retarded ape & YOLO your $12.99, and have some diamond hands and support the devs.

_childDocuments_.review: I played the story twice. The first time, I was very happy with my purchase. On the second, I couldn't help but be disappointed.For what appears to be a responsive story-line on the first play through, this game does NOT have replay-ability. The story is not actually responsive to your actions. There are a few scripted endings depending on if you , but that's it. Whether or not you manipulate the market, or use the "cheats," it doesn't matter. . This is a railroaded story with the guise of being responsive to player action on the first play through, and I feel cheated.The AI is also laughably easy to beat. You would think with your colleagues also manipulating the market, that some of your trade would move suddenly without a justification, but they don't. It's as if the AI isn't actually doing anything except buying and holding stuff for small changes in their portfolio's worth. They aren't competitive even from day 1. This makes the game remarkably not fun to play, as you are essentially playing against yourself for how much profit you can make trading, and not actually fighting towards any goal, except maybe the daily goal (which is also remarkably easy to hit every day, even without manipulating the market).Overall though, if you are looking for a chill game to waste a night on, this will suffice (one-off play-through). I got it on a deep discount sale (-70%) and feel like I got my money's worth. Still, it is just a disappointment that the game fails in certain capacities, when it could be so much more (cf. Suzerain). I have no idea if the developers are still working on the game or plan to release updates, if they do, I hope they can address these problems. Until then, I can't recommend this game to anyone looking to play a competitive "strategy" "economy" "trading" game. This is more-so a game for a short comedic story about capitalism, without providing anything else.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invisible Hand

_childDocuments_.review: A great game, from the perspective of a financial student I certainly enjoyed it. It pushes a narrative which brings into question how bankers or traders may effect the world for their own gain, and potentially get off with a slap on the wrist. It's a narrative that we see real world effects of constantly.

Make billions to pay thousands of fees - keep the rest. Free-mode is a relaxing thing to do when it's wekend and the real markets are closed. AMC to the moon!

_childDocuments_.review: I only just barely recommend this game. The game play is good, and the story is good. The problem is the game is unfinished. The story ends on a cliffhanger which goes nowhere.Spoiler alert:This is why its bad - You can never get to managing director. I know the excuse is that in real life firms exploit their traders in such a manner, but by that point in the game my character had over a billion in cash. I'm sure developers are aware that with a billion dollars I could start my own firm and become one of the "names  behind the names." The player could have pushed the moral aspects to the extreme by making the player become the ultimate exploiter, but it falls short.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invisible Hand

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game but just barely. I love the concept behind it and wish there were more games like it.In the game you become a stockbroker for a hedge fund company and your goal is to make as much money for your employer as possible. You get daily challenges and the better you do at those, the more bonus money you get on your paycheck. The storyline has a few possible endings depending how you react to certain situations, you can also get fired if you don't reach certain goals or lose a lot of money in a day etc. There are 2 modes, normal mode and story mode. Normal mode should be named story mode and story mode is like a casual mode, the naming doesn't really make sense to me. Even in the casual "story mode" the game is not endless or still does end if you abuse your power too much , which sort of bothers me.I wish this game had a sandbox/freeplay mode where you could tinker around with controls or limits yourself and see what settings are most enjoyable to play for yourself, like setting a custom amount of lobbyists, starting capital, enable/disable public opinion, etc. The developer claims after you finish the game "endless mode" starts but there are still too many limitations to what you can do, a fully separate sandbox mode would be a great addition to the game.Some of the controls aren't very intuitive, the 2 tracker monitors above your workstation only work with up and down clicks, why wouldn't they use like a scroll wheel or drop-down menu here? When you start the game, even if you played before and you want to start a new play-through, there is as far as I know no way to skip the tedious 5 minute long stupid intro before you can select your game mode and actually start the game, would be nice to have an option to skip all that when you want to start playing immediately in stead of watching an unskippable cutscene for the 4th time. Also stuff like coffee/tea takes way to long to brew for no reason , there's just several annoying things like that.For this game being the first release of the developer Power Struggle Games I have high hopes for their future games and hope they don't leave this game as-is. I do hope the devs release some QoL updates because otherwise this game has 0 replay-ability after you finish it with every possible ending.- - - Review update November 2021:Last game update/patch was 6 months ago and I don't see the devs adding more features or changing things that would provide QoL content for the game. I don't blame them, it's basically a finished game but I was just hoping for something new, maybe even a DLC with new features. Nevertheless, it's still a fun game and worth playing.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun "Wall Street" kind of game with a dash of .You start the game as an analyst, move up the ranks as you make money against competitors, to your help you have an insider channel telling you what to expect on that day, as well as being able to buy tips. You can also manipulate currency and commodities to boost/sink their value.You make money by either investing or shorting, there are multiple factors that happen that you get in form of a trade tracker, one factor can be "Coffee shortage" and if that also is in the same region that has an economic boom, then that are two factors that will boost coffee companies. Your insider tip can also be nullified by negative factors so keep an eye on the tracker during the day.The game story line is somewhat interesting, i wouldn't say it's necessary to play it, but it adds a bit of atmosphere. Every day you arrive at work, you get a bit of conversational pie from the receptionist (or the company solitaire expert, or whatever he is) as well as a boss. If you do something stupid, like ruin a financial sector, you get a mouthful at the end of the day from the boss that hired you in the first place. You also get emails and messages and in the story line there is also some kind of Mr Robot reference popping in.No bugs, but some annoyances, like once the story line is complete the receptionist keeps yammering on about events you already done, until some line says that "it feels like our story is over", after that he keeps quiet. But there are also emails that repeat, in my case it was "How badly we got hacked" that kept showing up every day before 9 am. Nothing game breaking but annoying.Is it worth it? Yes, if you like stock market sim games and making money like a wall street sociopath. I just wish the game was a bit more developed and had a few more game play mechanics, it feels unfinished, like a raw diamond that needs a bit more polishing.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Choice for May 2023, this is part of my coverage of the bundle. If you are interested in the game and it's before June 6th, 2022, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.Being a stock trader, only here you can’t lose. The Invisible Hand is another Simulator game, this time it’s the stock market.  You are supposed to compete against other stock traders, because… reasons, but all you’re doing is day trading and while the game starts hectic, it’s pretty relaxed for the most part, even having the ability to drink tea to slow down time or coffee to speed it up.  The controls are pretty simple to learn, and the game has nice shortcuts so you can just click on the names of items to get to the correct sheets. But man, everything here feels like a cheap simulator game.  The models feel like they’re straight out of an asset store.  The characters make an annoying sound to the point where I would have preferred silence, there are a few clever lines but nothing important is ever said.  In the first hour of gameplay, the game makes it blatantly easy to make money, it tells you which stock is going to go up, and when.  It gives your “hints” with indicators telling you whether it’s real or not.  There’s almost no challenge whatsoever, and I think I’m almost halfway through the game.  I’m at the third level out of probably four or five. Pick this up if… Honestly, I wouldn’t pick this up.  There’s a game called Space Warlord Organ Trading Simulator that’s equally short, but at least that one has some fresh ideas. There are a lot of good economic trading games, but The Invisible Hand is just too easy and cheap to be worth the time.   I’d probably recommend skipping this and looking into something with a focus on economics, maybe Offworld Trading Company, or god, I can’t believe I’m saying this but Capitalism 2.  Yeah, those aren’t about sitting at a desk day trading stocks, but nothing is interesting here about that either. If you enjoyed this review or want to know what I think of other games in the bundle, check out the full review on or subscribe to my Youtube channel:

_childDocuments_.review: Great Concept, But Not Great ExecutionPros:I found this game very relevant given the recent activity with stocks like Gamestop and AMC. People are really hyped up on stocks but many don't even know what shorting a stock means. This game can provide you a basic education on stocks and some insight on what it is like to be a stock trader which is really pretty cool. You will learn how the world is interconnected such as when lumber prices go up housing prices tend to follow suit or how a war in a country can affect the prices of certain goods. This game also hints that there is some manipulation in the trading world and quite frankly I absolutely 100% agree with that.Cons: This game was very short, didn't quite go far enough and parts of it were extremely sloppy. I think it would have really helped if there were maybe some company statistics like long term debt, beta, or other financials that would impact the game. The graphics were mediocre and I really thought the people could use actual voices. I really hated the events that took place like the "hack" where essentially you couldn't play the game for 2 days and just had to drink coffee. Honestly most of the events detracted from the game. _childDocuments_.review: Interesting concept, but flawed execution. The writing should have been done by real writers, as its about as subtle as a sledgehammer driving a tack through a wall, but I'm glad it's there. This is the only stock sim game that is wrapped around any kind of narrative, to my knowledge (aside from Wall Street Kid on OG Nintendo). The game is very, very light on realism, as all you can do is buy at current price and short at current price. The markets are quite reliably predictable, as well. If you want something like this but that feels somewhat more like a sim and is more difficult and complex, check out 'wall street raider' or 'speculator' by roninsoft. There's some ludo-narrative dissonance here. Even without 'cheating', (which the game 'suggests' to you constantly, gotta love that subtle writing), the core gameplay loop is ridiculously easy. I won't describe it here, but the trade feed is all you need to pay attention to.  The problem with this is that even if you try to be a good trader and not intentionally manipulate anything, you will still be treated as if you are Bernie Madoff. Nobody likes illusion of choice. Everyone wants to feel as if their choices matter in a game. I get why they do this though, it's to hammer home their message that the financial industry is cartoonishly evil.. These kinds of messages are far more effective when better written though. I would have enjoyed this game much more from a role playing standpoint if it was nearly impossible to make money the traditional way, but cheating allowed you to win big bucks. I also got wrapped up in an endless mode without realizing it for a while, which was annoying, but they fixed that today according to patch notes. The most annoying part though is a bug that will sometimes sell and buy your stocks in ridiculously small increments, per 'tick'. Other times, the full amount will post in one tick, as you would expect. This is more apparent later in the game, during the 'vice president' sections (math errors using larger numbers I guess?). If I have 900m, sometimes the game will sell or buy only a few million per 'tick'. This means you're completely helpless if an event occurs that tanks the stock, as you're not able to sell off quickly enough to not lose a fortune. Still, this isn't much of a problem since it's so easy to make money. In short, I love the concept of a stock trading game wrapped up in a narrative, and it's a topical game given the whole GME/dogecoin etc... thing, but the writing leaves much to be desired. Still, it was worth the money for the novelty of it.

_childDocuments_.review: Video Review:  8/10 The Invisible hand developed by power struggle games has you play as a stock broker, trading to the top, use everything at your disposal even if it's not total legal to become the best trader at the office. The invisible hand, right from the get go is a terrifying game, having you at a desk with numbers flying by, buying and selling not knowing what it is. Your fired from said job and now work for Ferios as an intern but this won’t last long. Teaching you the ins and outs of trading and inside trading, Buying & Selling stock, shorts, and dividends will be your weapons to out compete your fellow employees to continue to work at Ferios.  The invisible hand keeps info short on what all the buying options are but makes up it with practice. At first, I had a hard time understanding what everything was but after trial and error and Luckly not with real money. I figure out what each option was and its basic meaning, I think this is a nice touch and maybe a good introduction to people who want to get it to trading, not the whole game but the basic understandings of Shorts & Dividends please do not try insider trading it’s a hefty fine and a few years in federal prison.  Speaking of the illegal bits you have a dark web page that gives you the inside scoops, and lobbyist to help raise or lower overall stocks by affecting the product stock, the country's currency, or materials stock. I wish this was just a fun part of the game but it's also a sad fact of the world that a single person with enough power can topple one's economy. But you want to be sparing when doing this or perception of the company will falter and will need to apologies for your actions. You may get fired but I don’t know I did this 5 times and he just keeps ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ so just be careful.   Adding to the fun at the end of the trading day you can buy items and houses with your commission, the houses can be used as rental houses and items to stock the houses to increase its price per day. Also, with the ability to throw parties for you work mates, and get some perks for the next day.  I like the Idea of the properties because many people don’t think when they start to have money, they really need to use this money to make them money without them needing to work. And this Kinda gives you that feel. But again, please get your money legally. The last stages of the game are going to push you to the max, I still haven’t beat it and it's because the game is forcing you to reach the top position to make at least 5 million plus in one trading day. This comes with its pros and its cons. Pros you get better at manipulating the stock and con its gonna take some time to get there. Every time I would end the day the closest I would get was 4 million and the limit was pushed higher. I would say this is annoying and it is but the profit you gain that day will be there to trade the next day so eventually you can diverse in enough stocks to reach it but you need to repeat this a good bit of time. I personally enjoyed The Invisible Hand. The jumps in stocks and seeing you profited over 1 million or rushing to sell because the price is plummeting is slightly exhilarating.

_childDocuments_.review: "The Invisible Hand", which is a title that really has nothing to do with the actual game, is a game all about Maths and Economics.There is really not much to say about the game; it's a Simulator game that has you do stock market investments... I can see this game actually appeal to Economics majors, but I majored in Literature so, it's a big no no from me.Now, if you've read some of my reviews (I've got a ton), I'm a guy who gives a game a chance... everytime, even if it's full of Maths and Economics that I haven't looked at since I graduated highschool. Having made it into the rank of associate, I can attest that the game is pretty accurate for what it's worth. Some days you gain, some days you lose big time. Other than that, there are a bunch of "quests" in Career mode you can do, some of course landing you in literal prison like the corrupt stock market investor you are. However, the lack of voice acting and a real purpose for the game leaves this one quite lame and repetitive."The Invisible Hand" is a hard pass; even a harder pass if you hate Economics and you have no buisness doing stock market revenue. ; the worst part about it is it reminds you of your part-time shifts that were so boring they would never end lol

_childDocuments_.review: I am financially ruined (agricultural futures)I have lost everything, and I'm not sure how to continue. This summer I invested $17,500 (six months salary and my entire life savings) into ornamental gourd futures, hoping to capitalize on this lucrative emerging industry. After watching a video about Vincent Kosuga and his monopoly on onions, I decided I'd try to do something similar with another vegetable. I did some research and found out many agricultural forecasters expected this year's gourd yield would be far smaller than the past, due to deteriorating soil conditions in central Mexico and a warmer-than-average spring. At first, demand soared around Halloween and prices skyrocketed, but the gourd bubble burst on November 12th. Unfortunately, the coronavirus caused a massive drop-off in demand due to fewer families decorating their tables for thanksgiving, and prices plummeted. I had invested early enough that I thought I would still be fine, but then on the morning of December 2nd, a new email in my inbox caused my stomach to turn into a pretzel. The massive gourd shipment from Argentina, scheduled for early March, had arrived. I was planning on selling off my futures right before this, in February, but this ruined everything. To top it off, the gourds in this shipment were absolutely gargantuan, some topping 4 pounds each, causing the price-per-pound to drop like an anchor into the range of 6 cents per pound. I am ruined.

_childDocuments_.review: Just requested a refund. Had I known it was there, I would have downloaded the demo first. I figured this game would be a lot like Papers Please, or Death & Taxes. Instead, there is way too much going on and it's just hard to focus on. Green and red arrows, constantly changing colors, up and down, new stocks popping up, too much text going on, then if someone is talking to you that shows up, along with the talking sound they make, with the background music and ambient sounds on top of that. How am I supposed to focus on all these things all at once, while also learning what all the stock trading terminology means?You know how in Anchorman 2, they decide they need a bunch of information scrolling on the tv, with ads, and it's obviously parodying Fox and CNN? That's exactly how it felt to play this game. Way too much ♥♥♥♥ going on to be able to focus on just one thing, couldn't understand what was going. _childDocuments_.review: You probably have to like finance to find this game "fun", but it is definitely not a simulator and can be very easily exploited. The story is mildly interesting, just enough to keep you intrigued . The writing is witty but leans very far into the anti-capitalist "you are a soulless cog in a machine" jokes, but it makes sense why.The gameplay can get challenging if you challenge yourself to constantly day-trade the news but as i said, you can easily just do meta stuff, however, the daily challenges shake it up a bit.Although what i said might sound negative, overall i would recommend this game. I had fun for a few hours and that's what games are for, but don't expect more than 6 hours of content from the game, maybe 7-8 if you take a while to get promoted and/or try 100%The game has a decent price point and i got it on sale for like €4 so i'd say it was a good deal. So yeah, I recommend!

_childDocuments_.review: The game makes you hate all people who stay with you in that company. The first one to get fired is someone who does not want to cheat.You trade depending on different sources and you can go long (you just buy it) or short (some trick where you will get money if the stock falls but lose money if the stock goes up).It is all neat and funny and you have a nice UI and you could feel like a trader.The problem is... in the real world you never know the outcome of anything.Rules like "if this goes up then that goes up too and that goes down" do just not exist. You never know what will happen.So I feel completely disconnected from the game, sit there and watch it unfold and just don't care because I hate everyone and I hate especially cheaters and I don't care about these millions of currency because with just one million I would have enough for the rest of my life in real life. I can't connect to this kind of personality where you never have enough.So, I think it is a good game, if you want a game.Don't use it as "I will now learn how to trade stock". This is not it. Not at all.If you never did stock trading then it is good to give you an idea how it works.But it will NOT teach you real stock trading. So.. after an hour of gameplay I had enough for now. This might not be because of the game, but perhaps it is more because of me. So judge me, not the game :---)If you want a game with a story and with stock trading... try it. If you just want stock trading... not so much.There are free interfaces - connected to the real market - out there where you can use fake money to buy and sell and trade stocks and see how it would have been for real. But these are not a game. They are not fun for most people.If you want a game, try this.

_childDocuments_.review: My time played is not accurate - Steam tracked an initial session as being a minute long.The Invisible Hand is fine. Admittedly, I've yet to find a trading game I thought was super-interesting but it's largely the same issue with all of them - information is presented to you in ways which makes it fairly easy to deal with once you find that information. The Invisible Hand has the potential to do this if you ignore the core 'tips' mechanic of the game by outlining the core inputs and outputs of each stock in which you can trade, but those tips are so important to a good strategy to win that, given they exist and are as frequent as they are, they should be presented to players prominently (and are).You also sometimes run into an issue where the game can't decide whether it wants to be a satire of capitalism or a well-executed trading game. The narrative is too basic for the former, but certain mechanics (lobbyists spring to mind have little place in the latter.Do I regret playing it? No. Do I regret paying for it? Yes, absolutely.4/10

_childDocuments_.review: I came into this thinking the game was going to be about how the stock market is hard to manage, so you resort to illegal endeavors to gain an edge. While that's certainly what the story is about, the gameplay doesn't really back it up. Once you understand the connections between all the parts, it's relatively easy to predict the market even without the illegal tools given to you. It makes the illegal endeavors your character is forced to do feel somewhat pointless as you could do just as well legally. The story is funny though in a sardonic sort of way. It makes for a fun experience but lacks in replay value. I'd recommend giving it a try, but it certainly won't be your new obsession.
_childDocuments_.name: The Invisible Hand

_childDocuments_.review: Let's state this up front, The Invisible Hand has spot on pacing and humor. I finished a play through in roughly four and a half hours, and that length gave the satirical narrative a fast and punchy feel that was supported by a game play loop I found surprisingly stressful.  That loop makes the game deserve an RPG tag because I felt like the stock analyst main character: under immense arbitrarily cruel pressure, coffee addled, entirely out of my depth, but with enough introspection to know I absolutely should not have been given the phone numbers of all those lobbyists. By 5 o'clock many peoples lives have been ruined, but I was also broke since I had accidentally hit the short sale button...again. It was actually stressful, so this might not be the for you if you want an immediately laid back stock trading fantasy.The Invisible Hand left me with an itch to play a bit more, so I will probably enjoy more hours of stock trading entertainment by continuing on to it's endless mode. That said, I can see how the game play loop will eventually wear out it's welcome in the not too distant future, so I am glad the story did not outstay it's novelty. Just to reiterate one point, the game landed it's jokes. Kudos to the writers of these insufferable characters.Disclaimer: I received this game as a bit of a surprise through Humble Bundle, so the price of the game was largely absent from my thoughts as I wrote this review.
