_childDocuments_.review: A fun "little game" featuring exactly what you can expect from a stock trading sim.Little as in there isn't much things to do appart from exponentially growing, which isn't a bad thing if you're into that kind of never ending grind/Clicker experience.It does feature a short but fairly alright story, and is packed with humor everywhere.The size of the story isn't a problem since the real game starts after the end of the main story, revealing the sucession mechanics and such.Trading is fairly easy but hectic and fun in this game, which is obviously a great thing.All in all, if you're looking for a "clicker" game that requires you to actually play the game instead of looking at numbers growing, and that you enjoy stock market related shenanigans, you will definitely enjoy this game.

_childDocuments_.review: A good, short, funny story driven game. Is it realistic? No. does it need to be? Hell no! It gets the central point across and made me laugh. To the institutional finance reviewer, that's not what this ever set out to be. And if it was, we'd both probably hate it on account of being more work, after real work. Not that the mechanics are good, but they don't detract from the (at least story) experience either. They break down into endless mode. I give it a 6/10. _childDocuments_.review: Imagine Tyler Durden created a game about the stock market.Not the way the stock market actually works or real issues - you won't find anything like "Liar's Poker" or "The Wolf of Wall Street" here.Instead you get a game that beats you over the head that the only ways to win are either to cheat the system or not play at all. Insider trading, magically teleport lobbyists, and more. By the end you'll have less idea of how the stock markets (and the game's mechanics) work than when you started.Mostly, this makes me wish it was a good, realistic, interesting game about being a day trader, or a stock broker, or even a member of the US Congress (who are legally permitted to engage in insider trading.)But, for all its faults, it was reasonably enjoyable to play, and I'll probably play it more in the future.

name: Hellpoint
detailed_description: Featured DLC About the Game Hellpoint is a dark sci fi RPG that takes place on a derelict space colony in the aftermath of a massive quantic cataclysm. You play a Spawn of the Authority brought to this world to investigate the circumstances of this event and unravel this deep interstellar intrigue. You will explore the open world of the Irid Novo colony, orbiting in real time around an enigmatic black hole which triggers all sorts of dynamic events to keep you on your toes. Build your warrior according to your play style, and venture alone, with or against friends in online or split screen multiplayer. Once a pinnacle of human achievement, the Irid Novo space station has fallen. Its ruins are now overrun by cruel interdimensional entities acting as puppets of the malevolent Cosmic Gods. You have been created by the Author, organically printed on Irid Novo and sent on a mission to find out the unholy series of events that led to the catastrophic incident known as the Merge. Irid Novo is a massive interconnected world full of mysteries, hidden passages and secrets within secrets - all for you to explore in any order you like. More dread and shivers awaits you as you travel deeper into the darkest corner of this forsaken colony. Dozens of melee and ranged weapons and armor pieces to suit your playstyle. Every weapon has unique special abilities that unlock the more you fight with them. A fascinating new sci fi universe reminiscent of classic sci-fi movies, set in the aftermath of a massive quantum cataclysm and complete with a deep lore and goosebump inducing soundtrack. The space station orbits in real time around an ominous black hole that triggers various dynamic events such as boss appearances, horde assaults as well as modified enemy stats and positions. If you are struggling, ask a friend to press Start to join in a couch coop session, or call for assistance online. The entire game can be completed uninterrupted in coop. The loot is shared, and the experience of local player two is saved and not watered down.
about_the_game: Hellpoint is a dark sci fi RPG that takes place on a derelict space colony in the aftermath of a massive quantic cataclysm. You play a Spawn of the Authority brought to this world to investigate the circumstances of this event and unravel this deep interstellar intrigue. You will explore the open world of the Irid Novo colony, orbiting in real time around an enigmatic black hole which triggers all sorts of dynamic events to keep you on your toes. Build your warrior according to your play style, and venture alone, with or against friends in online or split screen multiplayer. Once a pinnacle of human achievement, the Irid Novo space station has fallen. Its ruins are now overrun by cruel interdimensional entities acting as puppets of the malevolent Cosmic Gods. You have been created by the Author, organically printed on Irid Novo and sent on a mission to find out the unholy series of events that led to the catastrophic incident known as the Merge. Irid Novo is a massive interconnected world full of mysteries, hidden passages and secrets within secrets - all for you to explore in any order you like. More dread and shivers awaits you as you travel deeper into the darkest corner of this forsaken colony. Dozens of melee and ranged weapons and armor pieces to suit your playstyle. Every weapon has unique special abilities that unlock the more you fight with them. A fascinating new sci fi universe reminiscent of classic sci-fi movies, set in the aftermath of a massive quantum cataclysm and complete with a deep lore and goosebump inducing soundtrack. The space station orbits in real time around an ominous black hole that triggers various dynamic events such as boss appearances, horde assaults as well as modified enemy stats and positions. If you are struggling, ask a friend to press Start to join in a couch coop session, or call for assistance online. The entire game can be completed uninterrupted in coop. The loot is shared, and the experience of local player two is saved and not watered down.
short_description: Hellpoint is an intense action RPG taking place on Irid Novo, a derelict space station soaked in an intoxicating dark sci fi atmosphere. Fight dreadful creatures, face the Cosmic Gods and unravel their twisted story. Should the challenge be too great, play with a friend in local or online coop.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all it supports 21:9!  That out of the way I gotta say the game is a ton o fun once you get some decent gear.  (sort of like most games I guess) I found a good grind spot and 9 hours in I'm level 65.  The game doesn't hide the obvious influence of DS, but I don't think it should.  I see it like a fan of DS made a game and added things that they liked to it.  There is the obvious allusion to Miyazaki's obsession with black holes, and the visual element of eclipses, accretion disks, fiery rings you get the picture.  I'm obsessed with that iconography too haha.  I have been enjoying the levels and the aesthetic.  The weapons feel as one would expect so far with me mainly having melee weapons. I guess I should progress a bit.   The fighting mechanics are pretty good with a few bugs that I think just got patched out.  I am leveling in anticipation of co-op working so I can play this with friends.    I dunno if everyone will enjoy it, but if you're looking to scratch that itch for a game that teaches you to get better, experiment, and explore i think you should give this game a try.Oh and can JUMP!  Plus riding zoomy ladders is dope.UPDATE AFTER 47 HOURS IN:  This game has so many secrets and hidden places!  Also the weapon mechanics are super neat.  It took me awhile to get it all but there are two different weapon mechanics for each weapon.  The catalysts you level up separately but install in weapons, but they can be swapped into different weapons and maintain the catalyst level.  It's cool because you can use a catalyst to improve weapon speed on a heavy weapon and increase stagger on a light fast weapon.  Or just buff the existing stats of a weapon's strength.  The weapons themselves unlock new movesets the more you use them up intil the gauge is full.  Most people probably got this pretty quick but it took me awhile to get it as I didn't want to risk any spoilers that may have accompanied tutorials.  I am still having a blast at 47 hours in I'm level 120 ish and looking forward to co-op to share all the cool stuff I found with friends.  I really think folks should ignore negative reviews and just try for themselves if they like difficult but rewarding third person action games with tons of hidden locations, items, weapons, armors, and things to find.

_childDocuments_.review: Hellpoint has a huge world to explore and lots of hidden secrets, puzzles, and mysteries. With a non-linear story line, the player forges their path through the game! Its up to them to seek out and piece together whats happened to humanity and whats become of this advanced civilizations AI. Find terminals with excerpts of the past, commune with beings outside your understanding, or find NPC's to bring you up to speed.  Fairly difficult combat reminiscent of Dark Souls 3 and a fairly diverse pool of weapons and armors. For the aspiring mage or gunslinger, there are catalysts and firearms found throughout the game- not to mention the many weapon skills available that explode, buff, shoot, and heal. For the good ol' hack and slasher or simple barbarian, there are a number of unique long swords, great swords, axes, clubs, A WHOLE PILLAR. Good times.  Awesome movement mechanics, the platforming gives exploration more depth. There are tons of challenging puzzles and secrets that require utilization of the players jump, and finesse. Dodge mechanics feel solid, there is an iframe stat which means the player can have items/armor either increase or decrease their dodge margin. Its a nice balancing feature. If you wanna dodge like its Dark Souls you better get stacked.  Which brings me to my next point- the leveling system. Near identical to the souls series- Axioms are the currency and XP in Hellpoint. When the player dies, all their Axioms are dropped and they spawn at their last visited 'bonfire'. Remember that 25k Axioms you just got off a boss but forgot to spend? BETTER BE CAREFUL ON YOUR WAY BACK!!  Hellpoint has a really sound online interface. Having trouble beating a boss or clearing a new area? look around and find a blue hand on the wall. Interacting with it will summon a player into that world. Alternatively a player can place a blue hand to be summoned. RED HAND! Now were talkin PvP- seeing one of these bad boys slapped up on a wall that means they wanna fight. Interacting with the red hand accepts another players challenge and summons them to that world as an enemy. Now featuring a ranked arena system!                                                                                 Final verdict: 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Really great atmosphere, wonderful exploration, interesting lore, tons of customization and some really great boss fights. That said, those really great bosses aren't the majority. There is a lot of filler, and the combat can sometimes get to feel repetitive with some of them. All in all a really great experience. If you're familiar with Souls games you'll pick up on the basics quickly, but there is so much here that feels alien to the genre you'll stay interested for sure. Figuring it all out without a wiki feeding me information has been a real treat.

_childDocuments_.review: The last true ending BOSS IS GARBAGE, ABSOLUTE TRASH, I had great fun playing this game, going for almost 100% completion, then this spit in the face appeared and made me consider sending hatemail to the devs. I officially give up and will watch the endings on yt, ♥♥♥♥ it.So I really recommend this game, but either skip the true ending bs, or make sure you have a good build to live through that.So hellpoint is a very soulsy game, no question about that. Almost all mechanics you'd expect are here, builds, secret passages, this doesnt open from this side, roll dodging, stamina management, renewable health items at checkpoints, and currency to be retrieved on death.The interconnected world with a very labirynth like layout is a huge highlight of this game, definitely reminding me of exploring DS1 for the first time. There is a lot of obscure stuff you can miss, so you can go through the game normally for like 7 hours and complete it, but if you're exploring all branches, all secret passages, then that really adds to the playthrough, easily doubles that.The levels have a really good sci fi horror atmosphere to it, with a religious art deco district as well. Probably the biggest gripe I have about the atmosphere is the enemy variety, especially all those recolored fish enemies.Visuals are good too, works silky smooth on my PC in 144 fps, and looks appropriately flashy. Animations are also well done, I see that the kickstarter money was put to good use in this department.Sound is off unfortunately, soundbytes sound ok, even if they're not really varied, music is ambient and suitable as well, but there are constant issues with it cutting off, drowning out instead of overlapping, as well as bad audio mixing at parts. Audio is also terrible in that aforementioned last bossfight.Controls are responsive for the most part, but platforming in the soulsy games apparently must have jank and awfulness to them. Sprint trigger is inconsistent on platforms so small, jumps may have oddly varied distances sometimes, and on landing there is a slight slide, the absolute worst thing to put in in a precision platforming. A small nitpick is an odd and small window of animation cancelling, I understand why it might be small for attacks, but cancelling healing to dodge could've been much easier.So the combat for the most part is pretty good, I haven't used to many ranged weapons, but no doubt the biggest cheese potential is there. All weapons have also very varied movesets, even if similar to DS3, straight swords and other fast weapons like that are clearly the best melee choice. Especially weird for me were halberds, their standard attack is stupid slow, has almost no stagger to it as well, while sprinting and dodge attack are better in both those aspects. Armor also is kinda secondary, you will probably just go for best defense to physical and other common damage, if equip load allows it.While the regular enemies are easily dispatchable, while still posing threat, the most interesting fights would be with the bosses, and here a financial shortcoming is bright in display.There are only 3 unique bosses, 2 final bosses, and rest is reused assets, that is 11 reused enemies, that is a very disappointing thing for a game like that, variety in bosses is something that may keep you going back to the game after completing it, and here that is a one less reason for it too.So the 2 final bosses I didn't really count as the same as unique 3 bosses, I have a very simple reason, they are completely terrible. To let you visualize it - first end boss is like a bed of chaos, while second is like shadows of yarnham combined with wintern lanterns in there too.To say it disappoints me, is putting it lightly.The first awful one I can manage, but second is just a nightmare, here's why:It consists of an npc that chases you, hits you and stuns you, it is a nuisance, but the most managable part of it (even though the arena is so dark you barely see that idiot). And then the biggest fnnnnn a-hole floating in the back.It's a teleporting boss who's got it all, unlimited range, as well as AoE, on all "melee" attacks, a laser projectile spawning every 15 seconds as well, most of the attacks have high radiation (basically poison), so you're limited to heavy armors or dodgin perfectly all that stuff. If it wasn't enough, 2 of his attacks are an almost instakill, they have very little tell, to easily differ them from others, not to mention those attacks have heavy stun, so if the one hit kill attack didn't kill me instantly somehow, it put me on the floor, then the follow up killed me with no option to dodge. There is also the sound mixing part of the problem here, the attacks have unlimited range, but they have barely audible sounds to them, and the one shot attacks don't have special sounds either, not to mention those sounds being so quiet, that I had to mute the song to actually dodge them better.The devs will probably not read this but PLEAAAAASE, change some stuff about it, it's just a furstrating mess and a combination of all the worst elements in bad bosses from the souls series. Just nerfing the circle of laser projectile barrage would be nice.

_childDocuments_.review: This one really took me by surprise in a very possitive way. I had heard that this souls-like game was buggy and glitchy as hell, and impossible to play without controller.. Nothing could be more wrong! first of all i want to adress the many reviews saying "jumping in this game is awfull, and almost impossible" Well i can honestly say that its no harder than timing your jump in the darksouls series, and way easier than in DS2 -to give an example. Also K +M works perfectly fine with this game, and you def dont need a controller to play it, but I have to mention that theres one achievement you can not get without a controller connected, but im thinking this can be fixed in the future, specially because the devs are still fixing small issues, and are very present in the steam forum. they listen to their players and always reply, which is a great +. Bug & glitches wise, I havent experienced anything out of the ordinary, and im in ng+3 now. a few glitches yes but you find that in all games. SO whith that being said let me talk about the game itself. This is definitly among the best souls-like games ive played, and i have tried quite a few. The exploration feeling of this game is through the roof! Its all the way up there with the dark souls series, and it reminds alot of ds1 in the way its build, the way you need to constantly back-track & tons of "this door opens from the other side", bonfire mecanism, yellow fog gates that you cant enter in the start game, npc side quests and so on.. so if you like the exploration part of the dark souls series, looking for shiny's, finding new paths and so on, this game will def please you. Its packed with secret walls, hidden items and secrets in general. The bosses however are pretty easy, you might have some challenges with one or two of them, but in general the bosses are the least of your worries. Its more about placement of enemies on the way to the boss, and about gravity messing with you. You'll find yourself falling over edges, or down in a hole, you'll get lost and stuck for a while but its all your own fault and you know it :)  Stay focused or you will die again and again from gravity and stupid mistakes. whats not to like right! Also many of the mechanics in the game are really brilliant, and I would go as far as saying that this game has some features and mechanics that ive missed in all other souls-like games. Such as the concept of "time" being intergrated into the game. Without spoiling to much let me explain real fast: you have a clock in the left corner of your screen and as time pass while you play there will be moments where you enter "horde hour" and "black (hole) storms" where you can collect special items, get access to otherwise closed areas, and even unlock stuff by doing certain things on the right location at the right time. Also several of the location gives you the possibility to enter "the underworld" where the area you are in gets mirrored, and new pick up items will appear + enemies will change & extra optional bosses and sidequests will be available!  going into ng+ is just as rewarding, new bosses, new paths, new items, new endings. And yes theres tons of dark souls references (and other reference for that matter) but I def dont see this as a dark souls ripp off, but more like a tribute to dark souls, by some Devs who loved the ds series themselves.If i shold compare this with other games i'd say this is dark souls meeting remnant from the ashes, but ofcaurse with a smaller budget. You can complete the game/your first run in like 25-30 hours, but if you wanna get all items , bosses, weapons, achievements etc. theres atleats a good 60 hours gameplay (and you do because the game constantly keeps you interested through those 60 hours!) On top of that there is co-op , grinding, pvp, arena battles etc ..The visuals works, is not astonishing or breathtaking, its simple in design, and reminds more of remnant from the ashes than dark souls, but it works. it gives you the feeling of being on a cold and dead spacestation, circling around a black hole in cold empty space.I really loved this journey! 8.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: If you ever wanted to play souls-like game with Co-op partner then check out this game. Hellpoint has amazing Sci-Fi atmosphere comparable to Dead Space series which fits my taste. I loved the design of levels. You can encounter many secrets, even more than in Dark Souls games. There are lot of paths to go, many places to visit. Overall Hellpoint is really fun game to explore.Unfortunately I encountered some problems:- Lack of information that should be in the game. If I remember correctly Dark Souls had similar problem.- There are still couple bugs but nothing gamebreaking. The last boss fight was bugged, he didnt attack us at all compared to what we saw on youtube videos from other players playthroughs.- Lack of monsters variety. Lot of them were reskinned. - Coop partner who joins the game doesnt lose souls when killed. I feel like in mid our playthrough he was too strong because of that. Despite of mentioned problems I really had great time finishing Hellpoint and I recommend it if you are looking for coop game.

_childDocuments_.review: It needs a bit of polish but I think it does what it sets out to do. It's a solid souls-like and adds some of it's own ideas. I hope people that like the genre don't overlook it, there is enough here to scratch that itch and the potential to become even better. The combat is what you would expect, different melee weapons (that each gradually unlocks passive and active skills as you use them), "spells", ranged weapons, armors, etc. Manage stamina/ block/ dodge/ hit, etc. It works pretty well, normal enemies even 5 hours in are a bit too easy though, personally I'd rather there were fewer but stronger enemies, but that's personal preference.There is a lot of exploration to do, maps are rather intricate with a lot of secrets and shortcuts to findThe environments could be more varied, but there is so much you can do in a spaceship and at least the atmosphere is good.I can't comment much on build variety and balance because I haven't played enough yet, but there seem to be enough moving parts in regards to stats, abilities and equipment to support several different playstyles. Then again, we'll see.Things that I think should be polished/ improved: There are some objects without collision, some weapon movesets feel a bit janky, some bosses need better sounds and visual effects when they hit you, they can feel like they don't have impact even when they smack you for half your health. Will update if my feelings change as I play it further, but atm I think it is worth playing.

_childDocuments_.review: There are times when I hate reviewing games I'm not good at. It can make for the live broadcasts to get dull do to repeating the same thing over and over again... like 30 deaths in a 4 hour stream. But this was not the case. I had an absolute blast playing Hellpoint. The controls are smooth and reactive, the artwork for the different areas is stunning in it's bleak sci-fi temperment, and then there's the rag doll. Oh yes... unlike other souls-like games, when you die, your body rag dolls all over the place like somebody forget to program that part of the game. In Hellpoint: it's a feature.There was something about the game that I really loved and hated at the same time. the addition of a "ghost". Not so much an illusory image of yourself or someone else beating a stage. But an actual tainted ghost with your stats, attack style, equipment... everything. It even attacks in a similar style to you. And if I am being honest, I have probably died more times to my ghost than any of the denizens in game. Even the first boss! Normally you die to a tougher enemy, so now you have to fight yourself AND that enemy at the same time. HUGE, but welcome challenge .I really enjoyed playing this game and I am looking forward to dieing over and over and over again as I push towards the DLC that's already out!

_childDocuments_.review: Before playing this, i played it's other demos (you can look at my review for the thespian feast) and i was interested to play the full game so i did.To start off, Hellpoint isn't perfect and it's because of it's enemy repetition (which i got used to), bosses being recycled to enemies or vice versa, some bosses being ridiculous at first but managed to beat or some easier than others, and i used maps online because i wasn't sure where to go next. Although there are some positives as well such as, interesting worldbuilding, lore, and visual designs, however playstyle you desire to play, variety of weapons and armor, and some bosses felt good to fight.Overall, this is an okay sci-fi horror souls-like that has good gameplay, story, and worldbuilding but has unpleasant design flaws and minor bugs. It's definitely better than its demos and there's a difference between the thespian feast and the full game but i wouldn't recommend it to everyone, its a 7/10 for me. get it on discount.

_childDocuments_.review: Decent indie souls-like game but there's so many things wrong with this game's system that could've been easily avoided🟢 Similar to Dark Souls🟢 Exploration is rewarding, lots of secret paths to find🟢 Heavy, fast or ranged build🔴 Lightning system is utterly horrible in this game. It's so dark that you'll have to max gamma and light setting in order to see anything in front of you🔴 Fast travel requires a special item to activate and not only it's hard to find but also very limited in quantities. With so many fast travel points, you can only activate a few. Why the heck can't fast travel be free? This forces you to needlessly walk back and forth so much🔴 Resetting stats is extremely grindy and expensive. Game forces you to make a melee build at the start due to strong melee weapon early on and it gets hard to switch build as you've already invested in a melee stat🔴 Status effect does not go away at resting points, only way I found to cure them is to either fast travel to another location or quit the game to menu and loading again🔴 Polarize can entirely ruin the game. It makes the game harder, enemies and bosses have massive health and damage. You do get more souls and level up very quickly. When you recess, the game becomes way too easy as you've leveled up too much. The balance gets lost. Polarize only makes sense at NG+ but manually being able to change too easily was a really bad idea🔴 Fall damage is stupid. You can jump two flights of stairs without dying but when you jump from 1 floor, you instantly die even if you have full health. Heck, when a elevator is going down and you jump up, you'll also instantly die. It's just ridiculous 🔴 Number of health potion does not refill to max at resting point/dying and can only be refilled to max at specific heal station. Mindbogglingly terrible design. You've to repeatedly travel back to base to refill it every time you die and it's a nightmare to do it before every boss battles or else you're just handicapping yourself for no reason🔴 Whenever you die, a doppelganger with the same equipment as yours spawns and it becomes annoying to deal with it repeatedly🔴 Printing is way too expensive. Why do we even need to craft weapons to get them which aren't even that good🔴 Performance can be very inconsistent with stutters and FPS drops🔴 No cloud save

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a mixed bag except all the things in the bag are pretty great. They did a good job of capturing the unease and intense loneliness that makes space horror so potent. It's only partly about the monsters (which are pretty cool). A large part of the horror is that helpless feeling. It's about being alone and feeling tiny in a seemingly endless universe. Souls mechanics work so well in space because it's just so damn scary. Hellpoint is a struggle uphill against an unknown enemy, and so much of space is completely unknowable. Every hard-won victory brings you a moment of relief before you remember that every second is a fight for survival. The messages are cryptic, and the few characters who can talk don't feel any need to give you helpful information. When you struggle through, you know that you did it all by yourself, and it's incredibly rewarding.Suffice to say that I like this game, and I really hope you do too.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic souls-like title that is a perfect example of how to make a souls-like the RIGHT way. A lovely blend of Dark Souls and Deadspace, Hellpoint has a lot of great potential and fun.Exploring:Took me a while to complete, I like to explore everything before going down the 'right path'. Only this games map is so huge and seemingly interconnected that I found myself finding entirely new areas to explore every time I went down the beaten path. Turns out there is no 'right path', and you can find another way to get to where you need to go most of the time. Truly, this was a fun and enjoyable outcome for me, I felt blissfully overwhelmed and constantly had to plan and think about my path, especially since there is limited fast travel. Combat: The combat is familiar if you have completed a dark souls title, feels very similar to DS1 in my opinion with its low complexity. Weight matters, builds matter, and there are guns too. Its a little unpolished if you're coming from a newer title like Elden Ring, but still very enjoyable. There are some bosses that become enemies types, but there are a handful of very unique and interesting boss designs as well. I did encounter a few bugs, such as a boss that dodged through a wall and fell to their death, or myself falling through the floor to my death; but these bugs where minimal and not game breaking. Weapons and armor are pretty slim pickings in the early game, but later on there are several different builds and styles you can pick and choose from to round your character off. Lore:This game has some crazy lore, and the environments fit the theme and story telling very well. Being on a dying space station that orbits a black hole and has 3 demi-gods on board is something I was not expecting going into this game. The  usage of time was also a very unexpected mechanic, where we orbit the black hole and even have two times a day when the station goes through the accretion disc of the black hole, creating a nightmarish skybox and spawning some unique encounters across the map. I especially enjoyed how the story unfolded as we learned more and more by exploring the environment and reading notes, wall markings, items, etc. This title is a must play for Souls addicts like myself, and has quickly become one of my top ten souls likes

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, so here we go. Hellpoint.... Do you like Dark Souls? Do you like The Surge? Do you like Sekiro? Do you like Bloodborne? Do you like Remnants from the Ashes? Do you like Any Soulslike? You'll probably then like this game....Probably. I say this not to be condescending, but to give you more of an understanding of how this game will play for you. It's got a hell of a good feel to it with a great sense of progression (once you understand it), a great aesthetic, if you pay attention, a great lore, and overall just a great game. Though with my optimistic tone, and high regard for this game I also must be frank. It is wonky as all hell, with some serious bugs in multiplayer, and an even more serious issue in level design and exploration. Lets get into it.Pro's- Combat - The combat for this game is similar to Dark souls, with a bit of extra speed, so maybe even say Elden Ring, or Bloodborne. You roll when not targeting enemies, and quickstep when you do target em, so I guess more like Bloodborne. All fights are mostly fast pace, with your toon getting incredibly overpowered towards end game if you really explore all the nooks and crannies, so fights become whatever. Personally I love it, because it shows me that not only am I actually progressing in the game, but progressing my toon towards godhood. - Aesthetic - This game is sci-fi as hell. Seemingly taking much inspiration from Dead Space, and Event Horizen. The look of the weapons, armor, enemies, and some zones (Especially the DLC) are incredibly original for the most part, so nothing ever looks same....however on the contrary.....- Weapons/Armor - The base game came with a decent amount of weapons and armor, not alot, but a decent amount either way, however with the DLC (once again) about 9 sets, and 14 weapons were added to the game with interesting ways of obtaining them further creating a better fashion souls, and ways for combat. - Multiplayer - I played the entire game with a friend, and co-op was implemented amazingly. Summon your friend and they stay in your game the entire playthrough getting loot, leveling up, and also creating their own personalized character. The only loot that your coop buddy cant obtain are the boss artifacts, but there are so few that it doesn't hinder the game whatsoever.-Exploration - This game has secrets upon secrets, upon secrets. There are so many ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ secrets in this game it could be called Hellpoint: Bet you Didn't find this. Luckily there are messages players can leave behind revealing these secrets, so it's not too overwhelming or anxiety inducing thinking you'll miss something.....but you probably will. - Leveling - this game has the easiest leveling system i've ever seen. Its just like any souls game where you have multiple stats, and based on those stats you can equip certain types of gear, as well as focus on a certain build. However weapons dont get upgraded, but an interchangable component can, so say you're using a hammer, you find an amazing sword you want to use. Simply exchange the component onto said swords from your hammer, and it will be current towards your players level. So trying out new weapons is definitely not a hassle or detrimental towards your playthrough.- Weapon skills - Most weapons come with unique skills that can be obtained through just using them. Using a weapon unlocks specific passive abilities, as well as usable abilities that can change how you play entirely.- Music - The music in this game is great. From what it seems, most souls like have incredibly music tracks. This souls like is definitely one of them, especially with those little juke boxes. Con's- Level Design - So as I said previously this game has a really unique look to it, however unfortunately about half of the base game looks sooooo identical that it gets mindnumbingly easy to get lost. Also it gives  sort of cheap feel to the game. I don't blame the devs due to their probably low budget for the game, however copying and pasting square looking designs is not the way to make your game vast. - Sound Design - The game uses alot of stock sounds that get very tiresome to constantly listen to. A small change for how weapons sound when hitting enemies would be very appreciated. Some sounds just well sound absolutely abysmal, and ugly. - Enemies - even though the enemies all look great with incredible imagination needed to create, the base game has veerryy few unique designs, so you'll be fighting alot of the same things. - Exploration - Even though the exploration is great, its only great when you know where you're going. Unfortunately since the level design is so same-y looking exploring can easily get you lost, and overwhelmed.- Multiplayer bugs - So even though multiplayer is very easy to do, right now the game has maaaaannyy bugs, and I wouldn't mind it if some werent soft-locking your playthrough which can only be resolved by killing yourself ( Friend locked me out of a room that was needed to progress the game, but since an option to open the door wasn't available to him and only be I had to kill myself to progress). There are a few bugs which aint too bad, but the bugs themselves are gnarly. I know I didn't really get too detailed about the game, I feel as this review lends a good mind on what to expect. A pretty damn good Souls-like which can sometimes feel a bit cheap, but overall fill that void in needing a new souls like to play. getting this game with the DLC for 40 bucks is a perfect price, especially with these devs. They seem to be very very passionate about their game, and continue to update it, and stay in the loop with their community. So overall i give this game a solid buy now and enjoy, especially if youre in a need for a good souls like.Personal Rating : 9/10Overall Rating: 7.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: This is definitely one of the best 3D souls-likes I've played. I've tried a bunch of them, and they're usually pretty disappointing. This is kinda like The Surge but good.Overall the game is a little bit buggy and unpolished. Some gameplay elements are a bit janky and confusing, sometimes enemies or bosses will get stuck on the geometry or start T-posing.  Sometimes the sound will drop out into awkward silence. But it's all pretty rare, and it's not bad enough to ruin the experience. The game is definitely 1000% improved compared to the demo a few years ago.This game really shines from the lore, the characters, the environments and enemies. A really haunting atmosphere, like Dead Space meets Dark Souls, or with Event Horizon/HR Giger vibes. The combat is really smooth and enjoyable, and that's the most important thing. Usually this is where souls-like games fail.My biggest frustration is the infuriating labyrinth of the game world. I was constantly lost, and it's very hard to get your bearings. Lots of dead ends, and the game doesn't really tell you where you're supposed to be going. It's also filled with some platforming puzzles and secret doors. Very confusing at times, but maybe I'm just bad at navigating.Overall it's a flawed gem but I loved it. Worth playing if you like a challenge and enjoy this genre, but just be prepared to wade through a little bit of jank.

_childDocuments_.review: I've just beaten the game on splitscreen with my friend, and I need to leave this review...First, this was an excellent split screen choice to get into with a partner on a single machine. PC games just don't like to offer that kind of experience nowadays with some titles literally taking their already split screen titles on the console editions and simply disallowing the already existing feature on a PC. Cradle Games? Thank you for your contribution to the classic couch co-op.It's all downhill from here.The game play was relatively good as we worked tirelessly through many deaths and level resets to achieve our end goal of what we weren't sure. In classic Souls-like fashion, you spawn knowing nearly nothing and travel through a challenging but possible gauntlet with enough perseverance and skill.The boss fights are also satisfying. Very challenging, but possible once you learn the combat patterns.I don't recommend the game to the general public for these reasons:It's buggy, almost unplayably so.We had to do a full restate halfway through the game because a crucial peace of gear was bugged, and we needed it... literally required it... for protection from the environment. The gear would not function, and this bug just happens to some characters. Flip a coin. Good luck.Both myself and my friend have had our split screen characters reset entire 6 hour sessions. We don't get to sit down this long very often. Many people don't. A 6 hour reset would sometimes be weeks and months in real life for us. We alternated being player 1 and reset the story an additional time so that we could progress evenly again for attempt number 3 through this game.Lastly, we went through some major boss fights. We have sat down for an hour and a half for our longest and most satisfying boss fight in this game. It was glorious. After all of this pain and struggle, and all of the boss fights beginning to become a legendary endeavor, we stumbled upon the last boss in the game... The final boss in the story... Where the legend comes to life and you achieve something great before finishing your gaming experience... And we killed it in, not even slightly joking, 30 seconds. Roll game credits. You win. It's over.My friend and I finished this final boss fight and were both waiting for the next step to begin when the credits rolled and both of our shoulders and jaws begin to rapidly drop. The journey to get here was fraught with peril. Perseverance and determination abound to get us through this game 2 and a half times so that we can finally get far enough to beat it on split screen with an even playing field between us, and we received this as a closing to all of our effort?Cradle Games... Guys... You've wounded me...

That is the most succinct description of this game i can think of.For a souls-like this is not as grindy as one might expect but every aspect of the combat slows the player down. _childDocuments_.review: One of the best games I played in 2021.If you enjoy souls-like games, this is for you. If you enjoy puzzles and hidden secrets, this is for you. If you enjoy space fantasy, this is for you. If you enjoy 'humanity truly screwed up this time' then this is definitely for you.This is a fantastic action combat game where you passively discover a really interesting story while trying to stay alive. The game is not easy. In a lot of ways it's harder than Dark Souls. But like Dark Souls, it gets a whole lot easier once you realize what's going on, the boss mechanics, etc. The combat is very satisfying. It is a solid mix of 'crafting' vs. skill.The only place the game falls down a little is in the middle of the game, where it's possible to sort of out-run the story and wonder what the heck you're supposed to do next. But that's kind of how it is in Souls-likes in general, I guess. There's no hand-holding at all in this game. And if you are like me, that's going to be just fine.

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game perfect? No, but few games are. Is this game a good horror souls-like? At least for me, hell yeah! I didn't have many problems with bugs like other players, and I played the game for almost 40h. It was a lot of time that I didn't enjoy a souls-like so much. Everything you hope for a good souls-like is there: huge interconnected levels, a lot of weapons and armors, cryptic secondary quests, many secrets, and huge-challenging bosses. The space station is full of secrets, dozens of secrets walls, switches, and hidden pathways This, combined with an oppressive horror sci-fi atmosphere, makes the exploration so rewarding. There are also many mechanics and improvements not common to souls-like games. The station is orbiting around a black hole, and this has an effect on the levels, with new and powerful enemies appearing, secret doors opening, or tough challenges against hordes of enemies revealed only at a specific time. Also, there is the possibility to increase and decrease the overall difficulty using rare items. Some areas have a parallel universe to explore, with powerful items to collect in a limited amount of time. But be aware that dying in this underworld means losing the items collected there.Weapons and armors are what truly shine here. Many souls-like end up with very few elements, and all very similar to each other. Here every weapon feels completely different, both for shape and moveset. From the backbone of a space-whale, to the animated severed hand of a grotesque flesh god, every new weapon is a joy to discover. Plus, the more you use a weapon, the more it levels up unlocking new skills. Sometimes the skills are huge magic that will completely change your approach. This feature increases a lot the depth of the game, and sometimes you just want to level up a weapon to use the cool skills it unlocks, like generating a small black hole. Playstyles are also very diversified, and if strength-based players will have a tough time, using magic and firearms is instead very rewarding.  But for sure you will find a strategy that will suit your style.If you don't mind some bugs and a modest but satisfying graphic-style, and you love souls-like, Hellpoint has a lot to offer in terms of atmosphere, exploration, and mechanics to reward even the most exigent player.

_childDocuments_.review: Hellpoint is a pure and simple “souls-like” in a science-fiction universe.It stands out for its gripping and distressing artistic direction where solitude is our only friend. Additionally, the "black hole" clock system can make combat difficult. At the same time, the equipment is very similar to Souls with statistics to be assigned to equip or use weapons, but we have the possibility of crafting items or improving them. Its level design is well thought out and well articulated, it is possible to go wherever you want. The healing system is ingenious, you have to hit to regenerate our healing vials (system inspired by The Surge) and which works very well and also with the appearance of a ghost when we die with the same trick as us. It is possible to customize the difficulty to suit our needs, which adds an interesting risk-reward.But Hellpoint has flaws that can frustrate: tortuous level design where you no longer know where to go; uninspired boss enemies with a limited bestiary; little challenge present; sometimes very long boss fights. We can blame an absent soundtrack, which could have reinforced the solitude or the strong moments.To conclude, Hellpoint is a good game with very good ideas but the execution leaves something to be desired. I liked the universe and the very gloomy atmosphere and its grandiose level design. In comparison with The Surge or Souls, Hellpoint lacks its own identity to be futuristic “souls-like” in its own right.

_childDocuments_.review: Really don't understand why so many bad marks on this game; for a "Souls like" made by an indie studio it displays a lot of love for its creative gameplay roots by managing at the same time to convey an awesome dark sci fi horror atmosphere in the vein of Event Horizon. Sure it's a little bit clanky and buggy but an honest kudos to developers: the figthing mechanics are more than decent, there's tons of secrets to discover and the show don't tell typical of From Software games mixed with (implicit) item and environment storytelling makes this small homage really worthy of the "Soulslike" surtitle,

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine the slow mobility of DS1 mixed with the bosses of Elden Ring doing 25 hit combos that can end or continue seemingly at random, as well as having very few open windows to counter attack. also the bosses deal way too much dmg when compared to the amount of enemies in each area and how many axions (souls) they drop to "farm", which leaves the impression that you are supposed to farm every area 10+ times and lvl up or stick with the starter items and only lvl health. Often times when I beat a boss I don't feel like I "got gud" and learned the bosses attack patterns it feels like I got good RNG and that the boss decided to use attacks that weren't BS. I looked up an online guide to make sure I didn't accidentally wander into the harder area early(the catacombs in DS1) only to find out I was in not only the right place but in area 4/14 3 of which are DLC... I really want to like this game but when I walk through a boss fog and get half of my health bar obliterated While wearing full armor by either a ranged attack or a BS move its just not fun. I can't recommend this at $35 with a $8 DLC. but I will absolutely recommend this if its on sale like an 80% sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Hellpoint is quite the indie gem, i was very impressed with how much they managed to cram into this game. If you're a souls fan this one is definitely worth the money.+Amazing atmosphere, with impressive lighting and sounds, giving Irid Novo a sci fi horror vibe. I like this a lot +While the soundtrack is a bit on the small side, what is there is very impressive. From boss themes to just crafting in the observatory, It does a great job of making you feel like you are isolated.+Graphics are very astounding once again showing what Unity can do. Amazing lighting effects, and shadows.+Level design for me was a plus here, got lost a few times, but eventually you map everything out, this point will vary between players though.+A nice variety of builds, from Strength,Dexterity,and mana based weapons and styles to pick from. +Performance wise the game ran very well i only had 2 crashes in my entire playthrough.FPS was pretty solid as well+Boss designs were fantastic! Love the animations as well, very unique.-Had an instance of a major boss glitching on me where he just stood still and basically let me chop him down. This was a one boss incident though, i have no idea how it triggered either.-Camera sometimes spun itself around while moving into a new area.-Platforming was fine, just sometimes my character kept running after sticking a landing, fortunately my deaths in this manner were low.-The game could have explained the dark hole mechanic earlier on, this isn't a huge gripe though. Just small feedback.In closing. If you're a souls fan or just looking for an action RPG to sink your teeth into. Hellpoint provides a ton of great quality and quantity gameplay for your dollar. The aesthetic is incredible, there is a lot of love put into this game. And you support a great indie dev team. Also, hopefully we get a sequel :D

_childDocuments_.review: **This game is a Hard sell, Had to retype after some more gameplay**Tl;DR: This game feels early access, Parts are not working right, portions seem unfinished & there's frankly a lot that just annoys me in its current state. Including bugs & limited features.If you're cool with that buy this, but this game is pretty much ball torture for me & playing it further is only me trying to get a reward from a game that constantly punishes me.So i enjoyed the concept originally. "Hell souls" & playing it is more like Doom Slayer-souls with that robot 'Mister Deadly' who wants to explode from Archer season 10. But after 15+ hours..things have started to bother me. The following things in mind, i cannot recommend this game to 'souls' fans. Unless you enjoy torturing yourselves then go ahead & leather up.Controls:So theres some input lag on some controls, Ground smashes with R2 repeat sometimes making the idea currently unusable unless you're always on point with them. There is also some input lag in regards to spamming controls.Bosses:This game seems primarily designed for the dark souls fans who enjoy just boss fights. I like time to breathe between boss fights, i like to be able to explore & Farm & get better gear before i am forced to fight another boss. I am up to the third boss & i really cannot beat it with its nonsense, nor do i seem to have any gear to counter it(Such you'd expect from a souls game)Enemies:Enemies have a weird scaling, its essentally the same zombies (At least early on) for awhile & they don't really change. You then go around the corner sometimes & there are 'mini bosses' that are always present that are leagues ahead of the enemies around them (or if you are in an unlucky location during hell hour)Lighting:Game is dark, Really ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ dark. So dark i had to bump brightness up to 90. Its so dark they even give you a flashlight?? Weird design choice.Hidden doors:So it wasn't until a few hours into the district around the third boss that i read online there are secret doors that you have to find, I thought all doors would be the breakable doors you find in the first area. This is frankly confusing to me to give us an example of 1 doorway & then use another.Pathing: The pathing is so damn annoying. I can't make a clear mental map of where i am going sometimes as theres just so many dead ends & locked doors. Not to mention the amount of BACK TRAVELING. The idea of a shortcut is to make travel short, not just more..tedious.Teleporting:So you can teleport through the rifts, but only if you have synced them using an uncommon item that i have only found about three of...Whats worse is you have no idea when to use them or when you SHOULD use them, making me wish to go back & undo my choice.Builds:So like most souls games you make a build, you get weapons that help that build & you go a long way. Hellpoint doesn't really give you any gear for your build. I have found more reflex weaponry than anything (I went Str build) & there is no way to Undo your choice (at least this early on) So i have a str build with 1 str weapon & i had to grind to 'fix' my build into a reflex build with a reforged glaive.

The "interface" does an attack that one shots you and i only beat it cause i survived it somehow by a pixel in my lifebar and the boss though that i was dead and literally stopped attacking me so i wacked it till it was dead.And then the true final boss came and it is by far the worst boss in the history of any decent soulslike game. _childDocuments_.review: I've played a lot of souls-like games, as well as every Souls game and Bloodborne as well.This game is amazing. If you enjoy souls-like, absolutely grab it.What you've got is a huge open world of a souls game. You have an incredible amount of freedom of where to go, and the game is pretty brilliant in how it paces you. You wouldn't be the first to think the game is linear, but some of branching paths are hidden behind secret walls and such.There are secrets EVERYWHERE.  Hidden walls, small platforms and rooms tucked away, edges hiding above and below, and they'll contain either useful items or paths leading to entire new areas sometimes.There's a huge amount of areas. The game reminded me of Hollow Knight in you'll keep thinking you'v run out of new areas to find before stumbling upon a new one.I really like how the weapon system works. Instead of directly upgrading your weapon, you install a chip inside and upgrade that, which you can pull out and replace in another weapon. Allowing you to play with new weapons without worrying about upgrade materials. These chips also have a progress bar attached to them, unlocking various skills associated with them. Using the catalyst weapons with these skills is how the magic builds work in this game. As a cool method to keep combat flowing: melee attacks will give you some mana back for your firearms/catalysts to use. It's a small but smart choice.Another smaller smart choice is having parrying not be attached to its own button, instead on having you time the bringing up of your block with the enemy's attack. It frees up the trigger, which is then the sprint button. What would normally have been a sprint button is now its own dedicated jump button. This allows for some more creativity in level design.I haven't even touched on the setting or the world yet. You'v got a giant space station,  orbiting a black whole, and some occult shenanigans that happened long before your arrival. It sounds a bit familiar when put like that sure, but I'm simplifying it.The sci-fi setting and the design of the space station is awesome. You'v got crazy looking gardens, a giant research facility, an underground mine full of blue liquid radiation, a golden pyramid like technobase, and an abandoned quarantine zone, just to name a handful. The ambient sound design for the game is incredibly well done too. It's creepy as hell the whole way through. Now, at the current moment, the game is a little on the buggy side. Constant work is being done, but just know it is a little rough around the edges at the moment. It's still one incredibly awesome gem, and I know the devs will make it ever better.Something I feel should be mentioned, the team that made this game consists of SEVEN people. That's it. And if I'm not mistaken, all the programming was done by just 1 of them. Considering the size and scope of the game, it's INCREDIBLY impressive how such a small team was able to make it.This is one lf my new favourites for sure, and I know I'll come back and replay it many more times.

_childDocuments_.review: Re-writing the review, as I've had a ton more time in it.I enjoy it a great deal, I recommend it still - just wanted to contextualize some of the pros and cons a bit.1- the game is rather janky at times, you can get stuck in geometry, or get the camera stuck in an odd place, making you die unfairly.2- the world is MASSIVE. maybe TOO massive. I am still finding new areas, still finding new weps and enemies and ways to die. I've only taken out 3 bosses so far, the game is big to the point where you aren't fighting 40 bosses. They're mostly spaced out pretty well.3- perfromance for you may vary, keep in mind you can only set graphical options in the main menu, not during game[play.4- the weps you find can be upgraded with " materia like " stones that you can find or craft, and you can upgrade those stones, unequip them from a wep, and place it on another 0 decent systemI addition to this, weps have an experience meter that gives you latent or active skills just by using them for awhile.5 - when you die, your ghost goes after you - these are literally your character - but they have seemingly unlimtied stamnina, much more attack and generally have the best AI out of all the enemies i've faced so far - they can path find you from alarmingly far distances to the point where you died. 6- bosses are fun, if too few ( so far ) My original review cited I didn't know if there were checkpoints ( ala bonfires ) there are, and you can connect them to each other using items ( which kinds sucks ) as the world is so large, you're gonna wish you could remove the links you've made, for future ones you discover. ( ie; fast travel is a bit of a pain ) there's some terrifyingly bad platforming, but that's always for additonal secrets and loot, you're not forced into precarious platforming to progress (not yet, at least ) The lighting may be too dark for some, and I agree - you can also adjust the power of the light sources in game, but I feel when you brighten it up, you lose atmosphere, and things get TOO bright for your eyes in some areas.few more minor things, no char creator, online is currently out of service sadly - but it does exist. The world is labyrinthian in nature, so it's easy to get lost. You can craft weps and armor, but not very often.I love the art direction, creature design, and mood the game presents in it's appearance. is that enough to justify it's shortcomings? no, but it's worth keeping in mind this is an indie team's first game, I've certainly played worse " souls like " games.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed the combat system, it is better than Dark Souls. Simply because you can jump on command. Also the co-op function is spectacular. Sadly, this game is very confusing as far as where to go and what to do when you get there. Most of the levels are restricted by locked doors or otherwise impassable obstacles.Every attempt at communicating with the user online sucks. Just a stupid gold handprint that upon inspection shows you an assortment of symbols that could mean nothing at all. There are very few NPCs to interact with, making it even less human, if that was possible. The story itself is dark, and a little hard to follow due to a mixture of dates showing up at random times due to a library level.Visually this game is very dark all over, it gives off a spooky vibe. One level in particularhas a terrifying sound track if you give it some time and a dark room with headphones by yourself. The graphics add to that spooky atmosphere and a thought that you are the last surviving human in some kind of future apocalypse. The bossfights are interesting, and the regular fights will tear you up if you have never played a Dark Soulsgame.  The jump puzzles are absolutely the worst, your character has butter on his feet for some reason. Because you will always slip and fall off a platform after jumping a 5+ foot gap in front of you. _childDocuments_.review: I'm having a great time!Dark Souls, the Surge and Dead Space all lost their big budgets but made a baby.Has all the Souls-like features we have come to expect, but the package is actually good.The level design isn't as amazing as the Surge 2, but it does have secrets everywhere, and the zones are quite vertical so exploration is fun and tense.Combat feels good (I'm playing on mouse and keyboard) and when I get hit or killed, it's because I wasn't quick enough, not because of dodgy animations.The graphics are passable, but the sound is magnificent. The developers really took care in crafting the sounds. Weapons feel impactful and meaty, footsteps and groans are clearly audible and overall the sound effects are brilliant enough that I haven't noticed the lack of ambient music.There are a wide variety of character build possibilities, just in weapons alone there are strength based melee, dexterity based melee, firearms, magic and all sorts of hybrids. Hitting enemies with a melee attack recharges your mana/ammunition and estus flask which leads to fluid engagements and huge potential for all kinds of builds.I mentioned above that there are many secrets, but I want to touch on this subject again because these locations don't take the easy way out of hiding a bunch of souls or crafting materials, they can contain valuable things. Blueprints, shortcuts and even items like keycards. There are entire areas that some players will never see even after completing the game because they didn't notice a suspicious looking wall and pickup the key hidden within.So far, fighting mobs and exploring take centerstage over frequently fighting bosses, so players who loved the Surge will feel right at home here.The game is very dark and it is certainly a horror game in the same vein as Dead Space, but not quite as horrific.Also like deadspace there are opportunites to do spacewalks around the exterior of the station, which is cool.Story wise...I have no idea what the story is, what happened or whats going on, but I want to know, so in that case the passive storytelling of the game is working.Overall I highly recommend this game to any souls-like fans. It's not a cheap cash in, Hellpoint has been made with love, it is fun and worth the time.

_childDocuments_.review: At the time of this review I'm maybe a third of the way into the game, enough to have an adequate impression of the game's performance. I mostly agree with a majority of the existing reviews, that it should be bought at deep discount. It's a decent game if you are itching to have a little guy to run around through a convoluted and interconnected set of secretive mazes, finding loot, leveling him up and dressing him in the latest fashions. It does fine at that.There are a few neat systems to play with. Upgrading weapons works a little differently in this game, where you slot interchangeable modules into weapons and thus are free to swap them around and experiment without a permanent commitment of the upgrade to a single item. You upgrade the slotted material, not the weapon, and you can simply transfer that upgrade to the weapon of your choice at a weapons bench (although these are rare locations, there's one in the main hub area).There is also a sort of day cycle where the black hole which the space station is orbiting changes position as the station rotates, causing more powerful monsters to spawn in when it is facing your location. A few special vaults scattered around the levels only open during this period as well. Additionally there are "accretion storms" which trigger other challenges when active. This is actually a pretty cool feature of the game, which keeps encounters interesting when revisiting familiar areas.The mag-ladders are also cool and zippy. There are also sections outside the station where your survival greatly benefits from wearing an EVA suit, although gravity is still normal somehow.The UI could be a little better, as you need to review multiple panels to really get a complete read on your weapon damage and the effects of certain items. In particular, a valuable tip to remember is that modules (read: rings or amulets) which increase a base stat such as Health or Strength actually temporarily boost your level in that stat, which increases your overall character level, and therefore the cost of leveling up. Remove these items before leveling up to avoid "overpaying" for additional stats. It's very easy to overlook and waste axions (souls) on, if you are not aware of this.The game feel and presentation is a bit rough around the edges, and while the combat does have the basics of Dark Souls melee, it lacks the versatility of its well-rounded move-sets and attack animations. For instance plunge attacks and backstabs do exist but do not reward you with a satisfying kill animation, it's just another type of hit you can land. That's okay though.Platforming is a nail-biting proposition in this game, and you even have a dedicated jump button and the tiniest amount of mid-air control, but the movement controls are a bit more fiddly, and you will die more than once from over- or undershooting a jump that you feel like you should have been able to make. Sometimes sprint does not engage promptly, or you may get snagged while jumping too near to a corner. Add to this, that these jumping sections can often be very far from a respawn point, placing successful retrieval of your "souls" at greater risk if you die.The camera is also wonky at times and will clip your view in tight spaces, sometimes due to the lock-on marker.The level design to me is the least appealing aspect of the game, as others have mentioned everything feels pretty samey, without much in the way of actual set pieces or landmarks, mostly some bigger rooms connected by a bunch of twisty passages or bridges, mostly diagonal or straight angles so the actual modeling work for the environments feels a bit uninspired and elementary. Graphically it feels more dated than even Darks Souls or the original Dead Space, and the layouts feel more like the arbitrary chaos of a Doom or Quake map, but huge. There's not much of a sense of place early on, although there are still some "a-ha" moments when you open a shortcut and realize where you are. The locations do become more interesting and detailed later in the game as it turns out, nothing I would call spectacular, but serviceable.Then there's the lighting. Many rooms and corridors are just murky brownish barely-lit metallic boxes. Though you can find light sources to equip later on, your first impression might be that they just wanted to hide as many of the bland textures as possible.As of yet I have not tried any of the multiplayer features, but it seems like co-op would be fun. I'm not convinced that the combat system is versatile enough to make for deep interesting PvP, but summons and arenas are there to bop other players with your stick of choice; if that's your cup of tea, might be worth trying out. The player hint system works similar to Dark Souls, providing helpful hints and trolling taunts.In summary, Hellpoint does have its charm, but it takes a while to really feel it. It does not put its best foot forward and initially may be off-putting. Proof of this is that in the Steam achievement statistics, less than half of all players even bother to beat the first boss, the very first achievement, and he's not hard. Many of the games systems are opaque as to how they function, and the early experience is riddled with confusion. I mean that's very Dark Souls in itself, maybe what is lacking at the beginning is just that critical first impression that draws you in. But if you stick with it past the first couple levels it begins to click, and if you can see past the shortcomings, there is fun to be had.

_childDocuments_.review: Kind of alright Dark Souls clone, with some design choices that make it objectively worse than the game it wants to be. The difficulty is higher than any fromsoft game (well maybe on par with Sekiro) which is fine, no complaints about the difficulty from me. Where it goes awry is in the details. Animations aren't as polished as they could be. Resting at bonfires (sorry--breaches) doesn't refill your health potions. Losing all your stamina is too punishing, and breaks the balance between difficult but fair to frustrating. I don't know why these tiny details are intentionally the way they are but the ruin an otherwise enjoyable experience for me. If you are one of the 'git good' dark souls fans (as I somewhat am myself) you'll like this game, but if you're one of the dark souls fans that touched a guidebook during your playthrough (no judging from me) then steer clear.

_childDocuments_.review: I had, oddly enough, discovered this game a few months after launch and seeing as how the file size is so small, I was doubtful, but nonetheless I tried it on a friend's console; I was not disappointed! This game is glitchy as hell, which makes sense because of the tiny file size, I guess, but man, I felt so silly for doubting what an awesome title this is! The combat is awesome with a rewarding sort of "regain" system that is reminiscent of the offensive healing tactics introduced in Bloodborne. Visually, the style is great, it feels like the Aliens movies and Dead Space had a baby and out popped Hellpoint. The music is great, I'm simply impressed by that itself! As for the story, it's vague enough to truly sit among the other great souls-like titles out there! The black hole mechanics really add an extra fun layer to the mix and I found that using the effigies was a great addition, much like the bonfire ascetics from Dark Souls II. I really wish there was a wider variety of enemies and armors, but to be fair, I'm really impressed with how much content is packed into this title! I know there's the standalone game "The Thespian Feast" that takes place 50 years after the initial events of the base game, which I will play, but I really really hope the team puts together some huge, awesome DLC (Or multiple DLC!) packed with new content! If you like challenging games that are filled with style then Hellpoint is for you!

_childDocuments_.review: Take this game for what it is, a Dark souls like game but set in space. I strongly emphasize the word 'like' in the previous statement. This game isn't Dark souls and if you want an exact copy of Dark souls then you will probably be left disappointed. If you can get past the fact it isn't and never will be as good as a souls game then you will thoroughly enjoy this game just as I have done. It isn't as long or polished or detailed as a souls game but it also doesn't come with the same price tag so what did you expect? I found the core gameplay to be solid and fun despite lacking a bit of creativity at times. There is plenty to do and lots of little secrets to be found. I didn't encounter any bugs that other people have mentioned in their reviews so maybe they have been patched out now. Give the game a go with an open mind and I think you will be pleasently surprised. Special mention for the lifts in this game. They are simply cool.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd love to tell you how this is sci fi dark souls and its amazing, but i cant because after you put in several hours you'll get a UI glitch that makes the game impossible to play cause you cant see or interact or navigate any menu. So 12 hours ruined in one moment...maybe this is just a new level of the soul experience idk but getting 12 hours and lvl50 yoinked for no discernable reason is pretty upsetting.update: had to reinstal the game but i got it fixed and did not loose my save so all is well. but yeah its sci fi dark souls except cooler and more challenging in some ways while distinctly different in others. it feels good and plays well. pretty heavy emphasis on 3D platforming in many places in order to move forward and that is very challenging (as is all platforming in all souls games) but the challenge is welcome and is far from insurmountable. also people saying they are having a hard time navigating just got no sense of direction and no breadcrumbs for thier cube. that said i get lost plenty but that is part of the desperation and overal stress of good ol souls. as for people complaining about the game being to dark, there is a cube for that to ;) pitfalls hidden in darkness are like this games version of traps. lastly, some state poor design of gameplay and QoL due to healing charges not being filled on death etc. this game requires you to earn everything and is merciless and adaptive. reclaiming lost points from a death is more involved than simply going and finding the dropped little nugget of light. feature scaleable difficulty/rewards similiar to DS3. one stark difference from most soul games ive noticed is that there are no single opportunity encounters. everything can be undertaken at your leisure, but still lots of time sensitive and cyclic "events" to chase down.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR:I love the idea and the game feels true to a game a souls player can expect. However, shoddy/incohesive level design, game-breaking bugs (ex. disappearing projectiles, buggy hitboxes, invisible enemies, projectiles), and piss poor bosses hardly justify the $35 I paid for it. In it's current state, it's not worth any more than $15 max. It has so much potential and I hope the cons can be addressed and the game tightened up.Pros:- Feel is familiar to a souls game with secrets and interesting lore.- Cool setting- Overall interesting art styleCons- The level design is HORRIBLE. Arisen Dominion is one of worst of them and I couldn't wait to get out of that level. It's also super out of place to the rest of the game. The developers shove in jump puzzles everytime they run out of ideas in a map, there are long empty passages with no added purpose other to exist. For example, when taking the tram to Port Issoudun, there's an enemy right when you spawn in so while you're loading in, you're getting attacked before you can even see anything. I spawned in dead and lost all my axioms. There's also a ghost spawn next to the rift so you can die over and over before you ever finish loading.- $35 is WAAY too much for this game, especially in the state it's in.- Buggy hitboxes. Watch an enemy 10 feet away swing their sword and blood fly out of your back.- Invisible bullets, especially on the final boss, but you'll still feel the damage from them. Only reason I knew they existed was that the other player saw them. - Weak enemy variety- Poor boss design- The hardest battle is fighting against the ♥♥♥♥♥♥ level design.

_childDocuments_.review: Only buy it if it's on sale and you don't care about the bugged achievements.Despite having many many problems and bugs and typos, it's a very fun game.The multiplayer features suck and barely anyone plays the game. There are 4 endings and you are forced to play the game at least 3 times to get all the endings (unless, like me, you back up your save games and edit the files). Everything is a mystery and nothing is explained so you'll spend lots of time googling around.There's an achievements that's meant to be unlocked only by googling it and using a controller (not keyboard) and took me forever to unlock it. I was also only able to unlock the "coins" achievement by cheating because who has that kind of time to find all the coins.I also don't like the fact that there's a dlc coming when there are so many bugs and problems to fix instead.In short, it's full of problems and bugs but it will give you a lot of hours of fun.

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic game that works much better than I thought it would be. It's quite eerie, a great sprawling world with creepy and mostly fun-to-fight enemies and combat is honestly quite fluid.There are a few hiccup and bugs - like NPCs not moving to where they should - and the world being so massive that its very easy to get lost but I feel like this doesn't detract from the experience as much as I thought it would. Honestly the getting lost can sometimes actually be beneficial when you stumble upon some really cool hidden area or discover a new weapon, it kinda makes up for all the times I got lost running in massive circles of corridors because I'm blind and didn't see the super obvious door...Lastly, calling it a souls-like is somewhat accurate, but doesn't really do justice just how good it is. It really is its own thing and while I can see the "Dark Souls roots" it adds that extra little something that makes just calling it a "souls-like" almost insulting.Overall, I'd highly recommend it, though only if you've got lots of free time as this game is good enough to easily sap away days of your time.

_childDocuments_.review: Dead Space + Souls-Like, Inspired by the film Event Horizon, with a world that shapes and shifts similar to Demon Souls, for $30.....
