_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; Great game to play coop and actually has a functional splitscreen. Second player won't get kicked from your session after beating a boss and generally has some super smooth multiplayer. Just join and go! Solo on the other hand is very frustrating.. not just because it's a soulslike game, but Hellpoint has a lot of bugs and balancing issues that can ruin the experience. Highly recommend if playing multiplayer, if playing solo wait for a sale.Now that I've had some time with Hellpoint I can share my honest opinions about it.. keep in mind my entire playtime was splitscreen coop, and while there were a few bugs that I'll mention, the overall experience was great up to a point.See, the problem with Hellpoint is the level design. It starts out simple enough with a bunch of secret branching pathways, but then out of nowhere you hit the observatory and the game leaves you with no direction / goal. I'm sure some people will enjoy this aspect, and for the most part we were excited to play a soulslike game coop that we pushed through, but from that point on the rest of the game just gets more and more confusing with multiple pathways that lead to bosses which lead to other bosses.So after playing for so long we managed to track down most of the world bosses by accident by just wondering around and finding different paths we hadn't explored, some taking hours to complete with no payoff while others might unlock a useless shortcut and some lead to the final boss of the area.As far as I can tell the goal of the game is to kill bosses to collect passes which allow you to access areas you couldn't, but how do you know what pass goes where? You don't. The worst part is there's no in-game map to speak of which sucks because I feel like this would really help this game.. or if there was like a "Boss List" somewhere, or any type of objectives really.After about 5 hours of playing, we were pretty much done, the last 2 hours was wondering around trying to find some paths we hadn't explored or aimlessly searching for items required to progress when we finally decided "what's the point?" and stopped.Up to this point, it was an enjoyable experience that I can easily recommend to play with friends, but playing solo? No thanks, this would've been awful. Hit detection, auto-aiming enemies combined with brutal damage amounts don't really add up to a challenging experience you might see in other soulslike games, this just becomes cheap shots and luck.. luck whether your hit registers, or your dodge avoids damage etc. In coop, you can usually just have one person lure an enemy while the other one attacks, which didn't always result in a win, but it was a fun casual experience without much frustration.Hellpoint also has a dedicated jump button and boy does it use it.. there's TONS of platforming and some of them are brutal.As far as we're concerned, we beat the game. All that was left for us was to find some armor required to explore an icy area so we didn't freeze to death. At the end of that zone is some key item for a good ending apparently, but frankly there's not enough people playing this game to find enough info online about how confusing some elements are.Overall it was a blast playing a souls game coop. Unlike Dark Souls, the second player won't get kicked after you beat a boss and can simply continue playing. In fact, if the second player dies, the first player can bring them back to life at the cost of half their health, but if player 1 dies you both respawn at the nearest Breach (Hellpoint's Bonfire) and since player 2 didn't technically die, they'll keep all their XP, meanwhile player 1 will have to grab their death pile to reclaim lost XP.. Player 1 will also create a clone of themselves to fight where they died which is pretty fun...I hate to nitpick, but the game also has a space theme near the beginning, which is cool, but right away the enemies, bosses, weapons and armor turn into Dark Souls stuff.. my coop buddy kept asking "why do I look like a Dark Souls knight instead of a cyborg?". I would've liked to see Hellpoint do a few things better than Dark Souls too, because honestly with this being such a clone, the best weapon is the medium speed longswords since heavy weapons are too slow and fast weapons too short-ranged. Everytime we got a new weapon we were disappointed it didn't compete with the swords.Weapons also level up as you use them which is a cool mechanic, but the game won't calculate leveled stats correctly.. the only way to find out if a new weapon will be higher damage than your current one is to level it up and 90% of the time, the new weapon might have higher damage but has a slower attack animation or takes too much stamina or something and we'd swap back to the longsword.RECOMMENDED if playing coop / splitscreen. Solo isn't awful, but it's pretty pricey for a Dark Souls clone and has quite a few bugs that become more obvious the further you go.

_childDocuments_.review: Hellpoint is essentially Dark Souls, but with an aesthetic resembling a mix of Alien and Hellraiser.  The gameplay resembles Dark Souls to a tee, with similar movement, blocking/dodging, leveling and death penalty systems.  If you enjoyed any of the Soulsborn games, you will get some fun out of Hellpoint.  The mood and environments in this are great.  Taking place on an immense derelict station infected by madness and dark gods, Hellpoint is filled with gigantic rooms built in a grandiose architectural style.  You really get a sense of the scale, with enormous pits, drop-offs and a feeling that--at any moment, you could fall to your death or get sucked into the vastness of space.  Unlike Dark Souls, this game features a jump button, along with a number of harrowing platforming segments that are both nerve-wracking and potentially frustrating due to so-so controls.  While I enjoyed the Giger-esque style, the creature designs did not have much variety, and I did not find any of them to be particularly threatening or creepy.  The same goes for the environments.  While I loved the expansive abandoned station, I feel that Hellpoint could have used a few more really weird alien areas to fully take advantage of its theme and style.  The weapon/armor sets and build options were fine, though nothing remarkable, and I feel that the game could have benefited from a more robust character build system, with a some more interesting options.One fun aspect to the game was the secrets; with items hidden behind secret doors, or along barely-visible (or even normally invisible) ledges.  There were hidden codes for optional areas, multiple endings, and more.Overall, this was a fun game and I would recommend it.  While it's not anything revolutionary, Hellpoint is a fun soulslike game that will entertain any fans of the genre.  7/10

_childDocuments_.review: Not recommended. There are better alternatives for a similar price. Here's just some of the problems I had with the game.I experienced a game crash the reverted my character file back a whole session. I lost 4 hour of gear and axioms. Do NOT alt-f4 out of the game, as that can cause you to lose progress.While playing multiplayer, the final boss broke during the last battle and the co-op player wasn't able to target them or take damage from them until we did a full reset.  is a huge problem in multiplayer. Enemies that are knocked down or stunned don't appear to be on the other player's screen. Bosses that move around quickly just teleport all over the place.  Some levels were pretty okay, but by and large it is a mess. Most maps are labyrinths that lead to dead ends (sometimes literally rooms that serve no purpose and have no loot, or stairways that go nowhere) with repeating items and gear sets that make exploration mostly meaningless. Lore is spread all over the map in text files that dump exposition on you in the worst way. You will unlock many pointless shortcuts, sometimes going through elaborate dungeons only to pop out in the very first area of the game to unlock a single door so you can ... idk, back track all the way to the start for no reason at all? There are no mini bosses, and only a handful of NPC's to interact with. After you defeat a boss expect to see them copy-pasted all over the map for the rest of the game. There is little to no enemy variation at all. The enemies you fight in the first few seconds of the game are pretty much the same enemies you'll fight for 80% of the game.Most weapons and movement don't seem to have any weight to them. If you lock onto an enemy, your character snaps onto them and all your attack animations just spin around at light speed to wherever the enemy is located. This is true for enemies as well. Massive bosses will spin on a dime to attack you if you get behind them.The floatiness is excusable with combat, because, well, no one is expecting this game to be AAA quality anyways. But for some reason they decided that this game needed to be an action platformer. Your character jumps 8 feet in the air, and slides on the ground like butter. If you've ever played crash banditcoot, it is sort of like that, which is totally out of place for a souls-like. You WILL jump on tiny platforms and slide off of them. You WILL watch your friend bump his head on a ceiling and die. In Co-Op the bosses are all trivial. 90% of the bosses will only aggro on one player, which allows the other to follow along behind and kill them without any effort at all. In my play-through with a friend, we defeated the final boss by: player one dodging attacks while player 2 used a catalyst to kill him. Player 2 did not even move during the whole fight with the FINAL BOSS. The single player experience on the other hand is atrocious, especially if you make the mistake of using a slow strength weapon like I did. Almost every boss past the first two will one shot you, or use a combo to kill you with no chance to put an input in to escape. If you plan on playing solo, I don't recommend playing a str. build. With a weapon like the column you can only land about 1 light attack safely in most boss fights before you have to run away, unless you get a lucky stun. Heavy attacks are almost always punished by an instant death. I ended up having to find a kickstarter code for a long-sword that swings much faster in order to even stand a chance against most of the bosses.There is no cheat protection in this game and it is trivial to boost your stats. Take that for what you will. Player characters will never have enough health to survive more than a few hits from another equal-level character even with the best armor in the game and a large healthpool. Playing pvp at the end of the game was a game of who could land a single melee attack first. Not fun. There are two separate crafting tables with large menus to craft items. You find blueprints around the map and huge amounts of materials if you explore. No problem. Most of the materials you need to craft the actual good weapons are not dropped by enemies, but are a single item sitting somewhere in the dungeon. Get the wiki out boys.There is only one single weapon upgrade bench in the whole game, and it is in the hub. You put a component in the weapon and now it has an ability. Awesome. But, what you probably won't know or figure out intuitively is that you can press right and left on the arrow keys to upgrade the weapon to more than +1. The game's only tip about this is the word "increase" on the bottom of that crafting menu written in 5 point font. Ok here is where the real salt comes into play. There are two key items in the first area that you will almost certainly miss without a guide. Both the EVA suit and a key to the horrible flesh hand boss area are behind hidden doors. If you don't grab them, tough ♥♥♥♥. Your only hope is to run around the whole game mashing interact on the walls (specific ones that have two black vertical bars) if you want to be sure you can play the game.The EVA suit could be a topic on its own. In order to get it, you have to find a hidden door, find a hidden elevator, go through an airlock, and do a suicide dash out to it. You MUST have this item to go to an entire area of the game. FUN.Last thing about the hidden doors. They are hardly hidden 90% of the time. If you play in offline mode, the devs have put yellow handprints around the doors so you know where they are or instructions to unlock them. What is even the point of the hidden doors if you are going to make them mandatory parts of the game AND display where they are with neon lights?This is the nitty gritty stuff but: in the final few areas of the games you fight enemies that drop 500 axioms each. Why am I still picking up axioms off the ground that are like 200? Why? Why? Why? Catalysts and reflex weapons are the best in the game by FAR. That would be okay normally but there is no way to reset your stats, so you either have to start the game all over again or just tough it out. I went with the latter and surprise surprise I had a terrible experience. The art was okay so basically 2/10. Still better than anything Ubisoft has put out in the last 5 years.

_childDocuments_.review: First off, my friend and I are kind of suckers for the souls-like formula which is why this game caught our attention but here it goes.Pros :- Great aesthetic for pretty much everything (armor sets, enemies, general environment, bosses and weapons).         - Intricate level design with a lot of interconnectivity and secrets that will make you want to either take notes or draw a map of your own (big Bloodborne and Salt& Sanctuary vibes on that point).          - Interesting story and world to discover (well woven into the original's game ending and NG+ mechanic)Cons: - Extremely janky co-op sessions; enemies suddenly turning semi-invincible (only the host could damage them and yet the partner can still be hurt by said mob), random visual glitches where one of us would completely disappear apart from our shadows, getting stuck in a falling animation when walking on solid ground. Plus the longer we were in a co-op session, the more these bugs would happen.           - Horrible boss design; most of them end up just being damage sponges that penalise you if you do not have a specific build to counter their elemental weakness. They all have big AoE moves that will do half if not more of their arena. In that regards, the game nearly forces you to spec mainly for a ranged build with your melee weapon being there solely for the leech mechanic (which is pretty neat I won't lie).            - Unbalanced items/abilities; my friend went caster and I went melee. He would melt bosses in a couple seconds with most, if not all, of his caster implements whilst even if I went full glass cannon and with the heaviest hitting weapons I could  find I would barely tickle them. Some weapon abilities are downright useless in certain conditions because they would glitch on the surroundings and simply not work or output damage.           - Anti-climactic DLC; apart for the armor sets and weapons you can find in it, it adds nothing but frustration to the game. The bosses are even a worse offender in that vein.All in all, get it on a sale without the DLC if you're a fan of the genre. Otherwise don't bother

_childDocuments_.review: A really impressive Sci-Fi Soulsborne experience - tiny bit janky in places (whenever I die my character clips through the scenery and then flies off into space rag-dolling furiously), but weirdly these bugs made me fondly remember the days of roll-tossing enemy corpses off cliffs in Dark Souls 1 and helped break the tension of dying for the 15th time.I'm not a huge way in, but already the game gets the fundamental joy of the Soulsborne: exploration and constant reward for progress. I spent most of my play time just wondering an area trying to find all the little items and secrets - I still haven't succeeded in this. And it's great fun. Combat is pleasantly fluid and the dodge mechanic works significantly better than many other 3d entries into this genre, which alone is enough for me to press on.Like many, I am... struggling to fathom why quite so many of the areas contain jumping puzzles when these are NOTORIOUSLY fiddly with this kind of game, BUT I have to credit that at least they help give the areas a real feeling of depth and cavernous space. Tip: if you're struggling, unequip all your armour, that seems to help me massively xDWould have liked to have seen a slightly more varied landscape BUT I can see why they have gone for the aesthetic they have, and it works very well in a lore context and to help the oppressive nature of the game. Really nails the themeOverall, I will definitely be playing more and can solidly recommend to anyone who enjoys Dark Souls 1 especially: you have to be a tiny bit forgiving of odd flaws, but the result is an absolutely enjoyable tumble head-first down the sci-fi rabbit holeP.S. Dear Devs - please: give us some single player/story DLC for this, I want to give you some money since this was gifted to me. And quite frankly I never bother with PVP until after I've completed the full game a few times

_childDocuments_.review: Second playthrough (thanks again for the extra key) and there's a good deal of improvements. To be honest, I was spurred here to say something positive for once because of the negative review today from Jim Sterling, whom I generally agree with. To think this was done by such a limited team, I thought it was rather clearly a work of love.He thought this was a rather shoddy tribute and to be honest, after playing a good deal of "Souls-like" games, this really nails everything you could want and...want them to experiment with with a Soulslike. I've gone through the Surge series, Nioh, and Mortal Shell within the past year and while Nioh nails the combat feel and puts more emphasis on the RPG/weapon systems, Hellpoint feels so much more focused on the FEELING that was invoked with the original Dark Souls game on your first playthroughs: Wonderous foreign atmosphere that rewards and asks for exploration, tons of obscure data and a storyline that isn't forced upon you more than can be drawn from data you both seek out and things just shown/experienced by you, and combat incentives that continually grow (even if movesets feel pretty barebones) as your arsenal and stats grow, including a much more limited estus flask system that regains charge by you aggressively going after a foe.Yes, there's some jank, but I found it all charming and in tribute to the Soulsbourne series. There's nothing revolutionary here, there doesn't need to be but there are enough surprises and secrets to justify multiple playthroughs and I'm happy to be back.

_childDocuments_.review: "Hellpoint" is an indie RPG that strongly adheres to the formula of FromSoftware's Dark Souls series. It offers a fascinating blend of science fiction and occultism that, despite some shortcomings, provides a captivating gaming experience.The game begins with a cloned body on a massive space station where you must fight against demonic beings and god-like creatures. The narrative is cryptic and leaves many questions unanswered, leading to constant tension and curiosity.The graphics of "Hellpoint" are impressive. The interiors are stylishly designed and the exteriors offer breathtaking views of outer space. Despite the dramatic changes in color palette and lighting, the game feels consistent and coherent.The combat system is solid and the enemy designs are interesting. The bosses are challenging and the music contributes to the atmosphere. There are many unique weapons that unlock great abilities with increasing use.However, the game also has its weaknesses. The controls can sometimes be a bit clunky and the performance could be better. The space station is a labyrinth of interconnected passages and regions that are confusing to explore. There are little to no signs of where to go.Despite these shortcomings, "Hellpoint" is a worthwhile game for fans of the Soulslike genre. It offers a satisfying adventure experience and can captivate you for several hours. So if you're a fan of challenging and merciless action RPGs and don't have too high expectations for the graphics, "Hellpoint" could be a good choice for you.I must mention in conclusion that Hellpoint was my first Souls-like game and thanks to the game, I have developed a fascination for the genre. I would like to thank the developers for this. I love the game and its atmosphere so much that I start crying just from the title music because I'm so happy to finally take a look again. Sometimes I listen to your soundtracks on YouTube, just to lose myself in them. When it comes to sound and atmosphere, probably no game has ever touched and captivated me as much as Hellpoint. I would be happy if this game and its developers received more attention. Thank you for this great game.

_childDocuments_.review: If there was ever a game that I did not expect to resonate with me so much, it would be Hellpoint. When I tried the demo; The Thespian Feast I thought "Meh it's okay I guess", but I decided to take the plunge and bought the full game a couple of days after release to give it a real honest fair shake, and to support a new up and coming developer. And oh my did I fall in love so deeply with this game as it has become one of my all time favourite games ever. Yes it is a Souls-like and yes it is rough around the edges with some balance issues and bugs but it's one of those games I found myself continuously coming back to and loving every run I do because it always felt fresh and different trying out new builds, routes and seeing the game world change around me all the time as I discover new thing.However it's definitely far from perfect and as usual I break things down:Pros- Weighty, challenging and methodic combat- Beautiful surreal art style with a dark dreamlike quality- Huge interconnected non-linear world with lots of find and explore- Loads of secrets- Lore, lore, lore! There's lots of interesting lore to find- Tons of build and play style variety and viability- Excellent soundtrack- Almost every weapon has unique, interesting abilities- Enemies are very varied in appearance and fighting styles- Platforming that works surprisingly well in a Souls-like- Perhaps the best rendition of teleporting in a Souls-like, forcing you to use precious resources- Great multiplayer with co-op, PVP and splitscreen play- The clock mechanic can cause interesting world events- Daring and Fearful Effigies to change the New Game cycle are excellent additions- Every time you die the world can change in subtle or overt ways- A bunch of content, a first run can last 20+ hours- Insane amounts of replayability with different endings and new things to try out- Runs incredibly well even on low end hardware- Heaps of options to get the game looking and feeling just right for you- Plenty of fun Easter eggs and references hidden throughout the gameCons- New Game+ is sorely lacking with no new additions, changes or goals whatsoever - it really needs spicing up- The clock mechanic isn't dynamic enough, accretion storms and black hole hours could be far more dangerous with more high level spawns and environmental hazards - I'd love to see the world change in far more drastic and challenging ways- Eliminating cosmic gods doesn't have enough impact on the world, again I wish this could change the world in more varied and interesting ways - Outer space sections are underused and disappointing- Can be incredibly buggy at times albeit nothing gamebreaking- Sound and music frequently cuts off on all machines I played on- Two incredibly important NPCs are bugged to some degree, one randomly running around while the other randomly returns to the Observatory despite having never spoken to them- Certain elemental damage types are overpowered while others are underpowered- A bunch of enemies feel too weak in standard NG, especially the upgraded victims- Some weapon abilities are near useless- The Interface boss kinda sucks and is incredibly easy to cheese its AI- Lack of proper mod support- No map to any degree; while I know my way around the game, it would be a welcome addition-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------These next two paragraphs are directed to Cradle Games, the developers of Hellpoint: While it goes without saying that I want to see all the issues I mentioned ironed out, I do believe shaking things up completely for New Game+ would make me care about NG+ a lot, perhaps with random elements that change up enemy spawns, item spawns, NPC locations and perhaps a new goal to achieve that's different to the first NG cycle. Making the game clock and cosmic god kills have a far greater impact on the world in interesting ways would also help to make the game so much more dynamic especially for replays. For example a list of potential changes that could happen: more varied enemy spawns, new enemies in previous areas, ghosts spawning across the whole game like the one in the High Ateliers, opening the player up to invasions, gameplay modifiers e.g. mirror mode, enemy buffs, player debuffs, random elements, new gear, new NPCs and sidequests and so much more that could change the game in so many fun ways - even if it's just a separate game mode in the main menu if you'd want to keep the vanilla game intact. All of this would make Hellpoint even more special via forcing the player to adapt to new and different rules in the game world.I also believe adding proper mod support with the right tools and Steam Workshop to truly change every aspect of the game to whatever the player would ever want with new locations, enemies, gear and so much more created by the community would elevate Hellpoint to even greater heights and would likely keep me constantly playing non-stop. Making said tools as open as possible would allow the community to really fix the issues I mentioned and didn't even think of too. I would also love to see some more content updates and paid DLC too wink wink nudge nudge Cradle Games and TinyBuild bat eyelash bat eyelash.-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------As you can tell, I absolutely love and adore Hellpoint on so many levels but I do feel it was released before it was finished as there is still quite a bit of work the developers could do to make this diamond in the rough really shine and be hailed as one of the best Souls-likes out there. So yes, it's definitely not for everyone but if those issues I mentioned are something you can deal with and aren't enough to deter you from this gem then I think you will enjoy Hellpoint a ton. It's a game you can really lose yourself in, I know I often do.

_childDocuments_.review: If you need a game to scratch that Soulslike itch, Hellpoint has you covered – but anyone looking for a completely fresh take on the genre likely won’t find it here. There are some intriguing mechanical changes and the sci-fi setting mixed with splashes of cosmic horror do make for a delightfully spooky combination, but one can’t help but feel like a bit more could’ve been done with it, especially in terms of visual design and enemy variety. Having said that, I can still more or less recommend Hellpoint if you’re a diehard fan of this genre – it may not reinvent the wheel, but it certainly hits all the notes needed to be a sufficiently solid and worthwhile addition to the ever-growing Soulslike family.Curator page:

_childDocuments_.review: A fairly good souls-like game. There have been quite a few updates that fix the majority of thew bugs and issues that were initially present (Primarily with online connectivity). So the game has had some good support from the devs post launch. I played this solo all the way through and then played it a second time through with a buddy and both times it was incredibly fun. Think dark souls with the ability to jump. There are a lot of easter eggs present throughout the game with hidden paths and bosses as well. The combat is fairly solid too, might not be as much to offer in terms of move sets like dark souls, but there is still a good amount of flexibility. Pros+co-op (you won't get dc'd if the host dies, and the host can revive the summoned player)+sci-fi souls-like (this may be a con for some people)+Difficulty (you can scale the difficulty up and down with certain items)+Boss Design (a lot of care felt like it went into these designs over normal enemies)+Easter Eggs (Konami Code and I'll leave it at that)+multiple play through (new game +)Cons-Normal Enemy design (now this is absolutely the worst, but you will notice the same enemies frequently with minor variation)-Level Design (mainly the paths seem to be a little peculiar, for the most part I didn't have any trouble, but I could see a lot of people becoming frustratingly lost. It's a patience and careful awareness of paths and area scanning. More so than Dark Souls)I drew a lot of comparisons between this and dark souls, and it's hard not to. My bias is that I tend to enjoy souls-like games and this one still managed to fit the bill. Not a bad price for potential time and enjoyment that can be had with this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Most Souls-like games do some things well, but fall short on others.While that's also the case here, I'd say Hellpoint is the closest to the "feel" of Dark Souls.Gameplay loop of this game is just Dark Souls. You kill enemies which nets you souls, or AXIOMS in this case. You unlock breaches that act mostly like bonfires. You can rest at them to fill your healthbar, but it will not fill your equipped healing items to maximum. You gain healing items (and energy) by dealing damage and you will respawn with 2 no matter if you have upgraded yours to +5. You need to earn those heals.You need to fast travel or die in order to respawn the enemies.Fast travel works between these breaches, but you need to connect them together in order to use them. Breach synchronizers are items that allow you to do hit. These are limited so you need to think a bit when to use them.Breaches also allow you to level up your character (does not require you to use a Breach Synchronizer) and to Increase or Decrease the difficulty of the game with items.The atmosphere is something closer to the grimness of the first Dead Space gameand Alien. The mood of the Irid Novo space station is fantastic. The soundtrack also relies on ambience and is missing some of the more epic tracks the Souls games have but keeps the tension alive while not being distracting. The Level Designs of this game is phenomenal. So many secret routes that connect different areas together. This is what most Souls-likes miss. The interconnection of different areas makes the world feel well designed. While not everything is connected, and there are loading screens between different areas, the way everything is linked together is so masterfully done, and in some parts it matches (or even surpasses) the source material. While the level design is one thing I praise about the game, budget of the game does affect this in a way. Many of the areas look the same, and while it does make sense (as the game is set on a space station after all), I wonder what wonders the team could have done with more money. There are few areas with different themes, but many places just look like dark corridors without soul. Thankfully the level design more than makes up for it. Other strong aside from Level Desing is the combat. While the animations might look a bit clunky at some points,the feel of your attacks if satisfying and doesn't feel janky at all. Many of the weapons will be quite familiar with anyone who has played other souls-likes, so when you get your hands on them you should feel right at home.Upgrading said weapons requires items, but those are not tied to weapons. You can remove those upgrades and put them to use on other weapons too which encourages trying different weapons and playstyles more.Most of the enemies in Hellpoint are well designed and look nice visually. There are a few that look out of place in my opinion, but other than that no complaints. There is enough variety when you move from different areas to others, and none of the enemies feeloverwhelmingly difficult. While most of the basic enemies are great, the bosses leave a lot to be desired. Many of the first bosses are later reused as enemies and I would classify as mini-bosses more than actual bosses. The "Actual" bosses are more special and I could see them appearing in Dark Souls. They do lack different phases but offer some challenge with their different movesets to dodge around.Just like the father of this style of games, Hellpoint doesn't explain it's story too much. Slightly more than Dark Souls, but most of the lore is up to the player to find and understand. Doing some sidequests also allows for true ending, which is a great way to get people to play your game more than once. There is also a new game+ mode, so you can continue where you left off.There are few things I didn't mention here, but I feel like that's the most important stuff out of the way.I hope more people give this game a change, it's much better than it might look at first glance (many saying it looks clunky).Cradle Games has created a fantastic game and I hope they will continue and make more games like this, since they clearly excel at it.

_childDocuments_.review: Easily the best Souls-like (since surpassed by Lords of the Fallen from 2023) and I personally like it more than Dark Souls itself. However it is a little buggy, but nothing I encountered that breaks the game.+I totally love that with every melee hit you refill your mana and health injections, based on your weapon's leech stat. This gives you great sustain. and is a huge quality of life feature.+I like the sci-fi setting and weird monsters.+Combat feels responsive and great. Enemies and bosses (except for the final boss) don't spam bs AOE attacks constantly coughEldenRingcough.+Your melee weapon doesn't bounce off walls. Sounds insignificant... until you play Dark Souls and get killed repeatedly because your attack doesn't land because it bounced off the wall letting the enemy wail on you. Or worse, the bounce, which causes knockback, knocks you off the edge and you die.+I like that you can increase and decrease the difficulty at any save point (breach) using certain effigies. With higher difficulty the enemies are tougher but drop way more axions (exp).+If you want to you don't have to fight the final boss. You can just surrender your data and go to a new cycle.+I love the maze-like levels and how interconnected they are, like Dark Souls 1.+-Story is meh and almost non-existent, and told in a terrible way. I beat the game and I still have almost no idea what's going on. For some reason this seems to be a requirement for Souls-likes. Just because Dark Souls had a meh story terribly delivered doesn't mean you have to copy them there too.+-I would have liked more weapon and moveset variety, especially for the guns and catalysts (magic).+-There's a bunch of armor, but most of them have crappy stats. Aegis Armature is easily the best set and it's definitely worth it to increase your load stat for it regardless of build. Unfortunately you can't upgrade your armor like you can your weapon, so eventually you're going to be getting one-shot on the higher difficulties by the bosses anyway.+-I would have liked changes for new game plus, like the items found are different, change in enemies, and so on.+-The Omnicube is cool, but most of the programs are junk and you'll never use them. I don't even know what you're supposed to do with the cooling and warming programs.+-I hate when these games have secret walls. Worse, you're almost required to find these secrets to progress, at least in a timely manner. But once you learn what the secret door looks like it's pretty easy to spot. This is in contrast to Dark Souls that has illusory walls that are impossible to discern and you must read a guide.+-At first it really annoyed me that in order to warp between breaches you needed to find and use a breach synchronizer. However by the end of the game you have learned the hub areas and used your breaches there and have some to spare. Annoying as a newb, not so bad when you're experienced.+-I wish the game had a map, even a simple one that showed you what areas connect to what other areas. Expect to be lost for a long time.+-The black hole clock is an interesting idea, but unfortunately the game doesn't really explain what it does. When the orange symbol is at the 3 or 9 position that's when hordes will appear, behind an orange barrier like a boss, and reward special loot. Areas also have a gray circle and when the orange and gray circle meet then I believe enemies are stronger and reward more axions. Also that's when black hole (white) barriers are lowered. However some barriers need you to also input the correct eye codes (located at a certain place), and it's unnecessarily convoluted. Most of the loot behind them is uninteresting. Only bother with it to kill the First Archon Knight and the only if you care about the achievement. It also sucks that there's no way to speed up the clock.-The game is buggy and unfortunately the dlc introduced new bugs. The devs are supposed to be looking into it. The worst ones are you can't move after dodging and your character stands there waiting to die (only happened once), and the other bad one is your healing doesn't work (happened to me several times).-Stagger builds are useless on difficulties higher than 1. As you increase the difficulty all stats of the enemy increases, including its resistance to staggering. Stick to fast weapons.-Almost all of the melee weapon abilities are useless. You're almost always better off using an elemental conductor and activating its special ability to enhance your weapon with that element doing a lot more damage, especially if the enemy is weak to it.-------------Ultimately worth a buy, especially on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I do this review letting you know that I have not yet completed the game. Because the game won't f%#$ing let me.This is a soulslike game, and a pretty easy one at that. I died WAY more times to janky platforming than I ever did to actual combat. Speaking of which, whomever decided that platforming should be a major element of this game, should be demoted or fired. Your character platforms like a concrete shoed zombie, and the game expects competent platforming out of you. You can get it done, but you'll be fighting your character and constantly getting caught on terrain that leads you to your death.Am I rambling? I believe I am, because there are good things about this game. They are however, completely overshadowed by all the bugs and very questionable design choices along the way.Doing an escort quest? Gee I hope the NPC you're escorting doesn't bug out twice, causing me to need to reload the entire area and do it all over again losing me about 30 minutes of my time due to no fault of my own.Doing some combat? It's all fun and easy until you get knocked down, and then you realize, " ♥♥♥♥! I don't know where I put all my I-frames!." Causing you to get wombo comboed to death off of one hit.Status ailments? Mostly ok, except for cold and radiation. Cold as an ailment is fine, until you realize everything that inflicts it does so through a chain combo melee attack. What does cold do? You move more slowly and can barely dodge! Leading their easily dodge-able multi-attack to now be a wombo combo until death that you can't do anything about. Radiation (think poison) is just as bad once it hits it's second tier, because it starts lowering your maximum health. This would be fine, if it didn't persist until the next LOADING SCREEN. Seriously, resting doesn't solve it and neither do the anti-rad injections they give you. It's just GONE, until you reload everything.Sound would cut out, items went missing from my inventory, once I just died from full health while just traveling through a cleared out area, and I've fallen through the map more than once. It's just SO MANY BUGS and it's CONSTANT.The environments are super easy to get lost in as well, partially due to what I assume is an intentionally confusing layout tacked on to environments that basically look the same with the addition of secrets being ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ everywhere so you are never sure what path to take, you end up getting lost constantly or worse you know where you are but have a vague recollection of a place you need to go now where you've been before but that was 40 bland tile sets ago.Now onto difficulty. The game for the most part was piss easy. It was challenging at first until I was able to cobble together something of a build and then it was easy street with the occasionally insta death combos from enemies and bosses, very frustrating when are getting hit on the ground or are just stunlocked until death, but I've played and beaten a lot of souls games, so I expected the occasional jank. It was for the most part easy though, I died maybe about 7-10 times to bosses and enemies (around 50 or 60 to jank platforming or bugs though), and then from left field comes the final boss. Holy %$#@ is it frustrating. You get staggered or knocked down once, you are probably dead. Just one shot kills left and right, and if you survive you get crippled with radiation lowering your max health and doing damage over time. If you did your due diligence and did story stuff you have an NPC who will also fight you at the same time as the boss! Leading to even more frustration. Oh, and on top of all that, you will deal absolutely nothing for damage. My character is about level 80 or so, with a +11 espadon, and it took me about 80 or so hits to down the big boss, and then another 20 or so to kill the little guy, all while dodging one shots coming from all directions with some having little to no start-up animation.Do you know what happened after I beat the boss? I floated through ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ space forever because the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ game bugged out AGAIN. I, so far have beaten this boss now 3 times, and each time my effort is wasted since the game refuses to acknowledge that I've emptied the health bars.If I hadn't played so many hours, I would refund this garbage. This game lacks polish on every single level except the visual. Did I mention that a good chunk of the equipment legitimately does not work either? The game in it's current state is an embarrassment, do not buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: DLC July 12th boys!This is my favourite Souls-Like (yes, even Nioh 1/2). I personally loved just about every minute of this, while giving it leeway based on the small team. It captures all the important aspects of Souls-proper games IMO. Intriguing lore, rich atmosphere/environmental storytelling, deep exploration (stellar level design) and solid combat with an addictive game play loop.My biggest gripes are some enemy attacks going through cover, namely the Arisen bros boss fight ranged attacks. I took my vengeance on them grinding through Arisen Dominion several times to punish them.Platforming was frustrating at times too, but I welcomed the dedicated jump button. I'm so glad Elden Ring gave us a proper jump.I loved the majority of the environments and level design. They described it as oppressive brutalist architecture, which feels appropriate. Despite being rather empty at times, some of the levels are ominous/awe inspiring. Outside the underside level , the short cuts and hidden pathways with loot to find is insane.The soundtrack is outstanding too, especially the Observatory theme.I pirated it, finished it, then bought it to support the devs and played through it again. I explored every inch of that station, doing/finding everything including the proper ending, while ignoring the golden doors. What a mess those codes were.There is some jank, but the combat feels good, especially when you factor in you can earn health by fighting. You only have to pause to level up/cash in Souls, which really pushes the risk/reward in Souls games to deeper levels of anxiety.The ending was disappointing, but hopefully they expand on it in the DLC.I absolutely adored this game. After i wrap up Surge 2 on my Steam Deck, this is next on it, all in prep for the DLC.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a Souls fan this is a no-brainer. It's obviously much more rough around the edges -- attack animations and hitboxes take a bit of getting used to, and there's generally a light scattering of jank throughout. Level and encounter design is also weaker than a true Souls game, particularly the environments (especially early on) all feel very samey and that can make navigation tricky sometimes. Enemy variety is also lackingSouls veterans will probably find the difficulty a bit gentle, at least after the initial adjustment period. But if what you love is just that feeling of probing deeper and deeper into an enigmatic world, growing in strength and knocking down bosses, this will absolutely scratch that itch and I really enjoyed all ~18 I spent with it. There are four endings total to see if you have the time to play through it that many times.Vastly superior to awful cash-ins like Lords of the Fallen -- this game is clearly made by people who love Souls games and actually understand what makes them so appealing. Grab this cheap while you wait for Elden Ring.

_childDocuments_.review: Souls-like with a Sci-Fi/Occult blended theme.  If you've ever seen the movies Event Horizon, Pandorum and the Hellraiser series, that's kind of what the blend is like.  Also plays perfectly on keyboard + mouse, so not sure why the dev recommends a controller.Current "top" review by BiteMexD is highly misleading.  (They) disabled comments on their review this morning after people were pointing out all of the information in it is wrong.  There is an ESC menu, and keybindings can be changed at any time.  You get a weapon before meeting your first enemy.  The "tutorial" area enemies before you get to the safe hub (Observatory) are plenty forgiving, and there are plenty of places to stop and go through all the menus and keybindings. _childDocuments_.review: One question: Why?Souls-like in space? Sure, go for it, I guess, but at least put some effort into it.In the hour I've played I'm just turned off by how "bare bones" this game is.The UI is straight out of hell, combat feels "alright", enemies are so far "alright", level design is ... "convoluted", "resting" does not exist apparently? Then the game throws enemies at you you likely can't defeat, so just run past them ... oh, for some reason you are getting attacked by your "ghost" if you die and revisit the site of your gruesome murder. That ghost is a lot stronger than you and a lot more agile. Nice.Then you get to the first boss, no rest area in between, alright just rush through it, call the elevator for the umpteenth time and have at it.Boss is easy.Now, the big BUT ... everything is unpolished. From animations to sound design to actual graphics. Sounds cut out 80% of the time when running, when fighting ... the Boss didn't really make a sound at all. Attacks were barely telegraphed at all, I just chanced it proactively, because you have no idea what or how sth hit you.And the story... well, I dunno, it's some Russian space souls with so far little cohesion.Dark Souls 1 came out years ago and is still playable and enjoyable today. Not up to Dark Souls 3 or Bloodborne standards of course, but still. This though? If your very first boss seems more like an afterthought than an actual boss ... nah, I dunno. I'm not really interested to see if this gets marginally better.If it was at least polished, I might stick around, but it doesn't feel satisfying playing it.

_childDocuments_.review: Dark souls with crafting set in a DeadSpace like environment. About 20-30 hours worth of content if you do everything in the game, with a well written guide this game would incredibly short.Pros: A mixture of different souls game mechanics plus its ownCrafting is interesting weapon upgrades are different I personally enjoy the level design (a ton of hidden areas and optional platforming)Combat is amazing (Bloodborne dashes combanied with Darksouls rolling)Healing is unique (you only get heals back on death or killing enemies) no "bonfire refill"Cons:Some areas lock you to that area (cant go back) (no warning either)Difficulty spikes (went from getting the first 3 bosses in one try to being destroyed)Map layout, its super confusing and requires you to back to areas alot.very few bosses, you will be killing mobs 90% of the game.Biggest issue: The game can be complete in less than six hours if you dont even know where to go, my first and still  running playthrough I almost "accidentally beat the game" This game uses a weird feature that measures your progress in Data Percentage %. Dark souls games feel more challenging then this and have more verity and bosses, this game also does not have NG+ items or requries X runs to collect every boss weapon or spell. _childDocuments_.review: I tried HP: The Thespian Feast and was not impressed.  Despite that, the main game seemed pretty appealing from the streams I saw so I decided to get the main game.  I don't know what it is, but the main game feels better than TTF and I am quite pleased.I've played all of the Dark Souls entries, Bloodborne, and Sekiro, but never made much progress.  I appreciate and admire soulslikes, but I just haven't been able to 'click' with them gameplay-wise - until now.  Hellpoint comes along with a great aesthetic and a soulslike experience that finally resonates with me.  Learning enemy attack patterns and strategies/weapons to approach with are much easier to grasp so far than other soulslikes and environments are open to plenty of exploration in a much more vertical manner than I expected.  Difficulty is fair and there's way more than enough room for exploration and discovery to keep things interesting when I run into a wall in on route.  I like it.There are still a few bugs in the game, but I haven't encountered anything game-breaking.  Aside from a few instances with bad hitboxes, everything's been good.I'm only 7 hours into it, but I'm thoroughly enjoying my time with this.  The demo/Thespian Feast doesn't do justice to the main game.  In my opinion, it's an excellent entry point into the souls-type genre with a forgiving and well-scaled difficulty and a big map with a great atmosphere.  I still haven't gotten through it, but Hellpoint has renewed my enthusiasm for the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: + Interesting setting and decent atmosphere (spooky space station and etc)+ Gear variety is good+ Using the same weapon makes it stronger (or grants abilities)+ Exploration (and platforming) is rewarded+ Enemy/Boss designs are neat+ Armor and weapon designs are cool as well+ Healing system is well done (you fight to get more healing)+ Enemies drop currency (Axions) in form of items once in a while which are not dropped upon death+ Split-screen coop if you are interested in that+/- You can increase or decrease difficulty by using consumable items at any time (Fearful Effigy and Daring Effigy)+/- Platforming may be frustrating for some people (personally had no issues myself)+/- Enemies can spawn after a certain time passes given that you didn't die. Connecting to a Breach ("sitting at a bonfire") does not reset enemies+/- The time system is original BUT one whole cycle being 2 hours is an effing joke+/- Enemy placements are nothing original+/- Visually doesn't look great (in terms of graphics) but it does run well+/- Death by falling is the most common cause of death in this game- You can't use a weapon with both hands even if the said weapon is pretty much a 2H weapon- Basically no classes or customization (no class selection or char creation of any sort)- Very stiff animations to the point of being comical (my favorite is the block animation which I spam once in a while for fun)- Game loves putting chasms in front of you (more wasted time backtracking because you held Left Stick for an extra 0.2 seconds before you saw the chasm)- Breach placement is simply bad. Sometimes you don't find one for 30 minutes and sometimes 2 of them have a 30 second walk between them- Sound design (volume, frequency and variety) is absolutely abysmal. They underpaid the guy who made the sounds I bet- Janky as hell and has minor issues like sound cutting or your corpse ragdolling like crazy when you die- Timer cycles take 2 hours for one cycle which is too long and wastes even more time- Ghost mechanic is more frustrating than challenging (you leave a hostile 1:1 clone of yourself near where you died and usually have to deal with it)- Rest points (Breaches) are not connected by fast travel by default and you have a limited amount of connection items. They reset every NG cycle as well which means you prevented wasting time only temporarily (and have to do it again if you want to save time again)- Backtracking is cancer (it's not hard to backtrack despite the labyrinthine maps; it's a waste of time and it's tedious)- Elevators are way too slow (I had to speed it up via Cheat Engine to actually make it bearable)- The "hardest" achievement is about collecting 66 coins and you can permanently miss one of them if you are not careful which means you wasted a whole NG cycle. Progress isn't saved between NG cycles as well- "Bosses are normal enemies now" or "Normal enemies are bosses now" is common (causes lack of variety in means of enemy types)- There is no "get all achievements" achievementI connected to someone (by coop connection) who was 3-4 areas ahead of me and racked up like 50 levels worth of currency because of the mobs the host was killing. To be honest, the start was so slow that those 50 levels worth of Axions actually made me viable by letting me use the first armor set I found and have some extra HP/Stamina. I never liked playing Deprived in Dark Souls games anyway so it saved me time.Certain items should have been non-consumable and should have carried over NG cycles. Notable examples are the Effigy items and the Breach Synchronizers. In fact, I think Breach Synchronizers should have had unlimited use (or had a shop which sells them with unlimited stock).Enemy placements never surpise me after Nioh games. Hellpoint has the exact same crap case of "enemies around corners" syndrome.Ghost system could have been better if it held your dropped currency instead of being just another lousy roadblock which can be ignored entirely since they drop next to nothing.Half of the time the game feels unfinished. Hell, it sometimes feels like a tech demo!

_childDocuments_.review: So, I picked up this game almost at random and thought about it approximately not at all for months. I only picked it up a few days ago and found a game that was a passably enjoyable Souls-like, with a decent enough story, a solid enough art style, and some fun mechanics and gimmicks, with tight combat and characters I did have interest in. but one that slowly wore its welcome from me accepting it with open arms to "I'll probably finish it and never play it again". Above average for an indie soulslike but only a little better than mid overall.As the fact that: most bosses were bigger versions of normal enemies with an extra attack or two, which was especially apparent when I went even slightly out of order and ran up on bosses I had already seen the enemy designs for, areas had load screens between them, some areas have screwy geometry, near the arena tower in the Sohn district has a ledge you can drop onto that looks like there should be something there but there's no way to return from, and the walls of the outside of the temple I would get consistently stuck on, an invisible wall or two and other assorted jankiness. also I really just, personal preference, didn't like the fact that an AI ghost of your character spawns on where your souls dropped.All became apparentI was still enjoying it, especially as it it had that feel of clearly being a game the developers cared about, but I couldn't recommend it to anyone who wasn't already very versed in the souls-likes already out. Out of the people who were watching me stream on discord and the people who owned the game, I was probably the only one willing to finish, but I found it honestly pretty enjoyable despite the intense jank, and sometimes even funny because of it. This was the limit of my review until someone watching me who had the game and was more down on it asked if I wanted to make a new character and just run the game as best we could together, see if it was more fun that way....I am now a massive fan of this game, not just out of "jank is more fun together" but because the multiplayer experience is outright *phenomenal*. Compared to your usual soulslike, this game's ease of co-op is unheard of, but it even stands out as easy to use across the entire indie market, You just have a code for your play session in your multiplayer menu, you share it, your friend heads into the multiplayer menu, hits join match and inputs it while you're connected.They can connect to you and join your game from pretty much any point in the game, wherever they are and wherever you are.You don't HAVE to set yourself to be invaded if it's just you and a pal playing.Both players can pick items up, and both players get a copy. P1 is the only one who gets key items, however.The netcode is more than enough to get the job done, I haven't once questioned getting hit and we've only had DC issues once in the 16+ hours we've played so far.You can change areas with your partner, no being cordoned off to x section of the mapYour visiting partner goes down? you can revive them where they died for half your total health pool, you go down? they don't get ejected, they teleport back to the most recent rift or area change with you.Also it has local co-op and steam remote play together just in case you needed that as well or your friend doesn't want to buy it themselves.Just the sheer simplicity and friendliness to the multiplayer experience changed this from a solid mid game I'd wait to see if there was a sequel to, and recommend, but only if you were a person into Souls-likes who was done with Fromsoft's offerings alongside the Nioh 2s and maybe even Code Veins in quality (or was SPECIFICALLY looking for something more akin to Demon's Souls), to a game I can honestly recommend a playthrough to anyone who enjoys action games and has someone to play a game with, that I genuinely can't wait for the DLC for.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has one of the coolest premise and setting in the Souls game genre. You spawn in on a colonial space station orbiting a black hole after a cataclysmic event resulted in a parallel universe colliding with our own. This event obliterated everyone on board both physically and mentally, turning them into deranged feral mutilated souls, and if that wasn't enough such an event attracted the attention of Cosmic Gods. You wake up in a vat and are basically told you are a human clone and some messed up things happened here and are then given liberty to figure out the details on how and why this all happened.The one thing this game does a really good job at is intriguing the player on exploring and discovering what happened on Irid Novo. Just like any souls game the story is not fed to you. Typically when I play DS I'm mostly focused on just beating bosses and clearing areas. I know theres a way more intricate story than the face value of your 1st playthrough but I never felt compelled to "understand" the lore as much as simply beating the game. Hellpoint actually makes this a part of the game by incorporating the lore into "data." You want to collect as much "data" to  understand what happened and you will miss A LOT if you do not look for secret rooms and passages. This game takes illusory walls to a new level. Sometimes there are secret rooms within secret rooms so the game encourages observation. All the information you can find is considered data that is broken down in bits of percentages. You obviously want to acquire %100 but there is more than that, I'm not sure how high you can get so don't think you found everything if you made it that far.The gameplay in general is great. Fighting feels like a mix of both Dark Souls and Bloodbourne. Is it hard? Yeah. Is it Dark Souls hard? Hmm I dont think so, but I don't see that as a detriment to the game. Interesting thing is the difficulty can be changed but not through the menu but rather through "effigies" you find in the game which are rare to find. One of the coolest things about this game is its co-op. You can play an entire game with a friend if you chose to do so from literally start to finish or anywhere in between either online or split screen which is really cool. Overall for its price I think it's well worth it for those who love this kind of genre of games, and its not that bad for someone who isn't sure, especially if they can get someone to play with them either online or split screen. It doesn't have great graphics like compared to DS3 from 2016 but they aren't bad. You'll still end up at some point just fixated at gazing into the black hole when you can. To me this feels like the movies "Event Horizon" and "Hellraiser" were made together into a souls game which is something I never asked for but I'm super glad I stumbled across.

_childDocuments_.review: The eye divine cybermancy of soul’s like’s, keeps coming to mind now i finished my first run through. It's just as deeply flawed, overly ambitious but has atmosphere, gets enough gameplay right and you can tell it's been made with heart that i really enjoyed it despite itself.It's story is solid and told throughout with a nice mix of exposition and environmental details that felt a good balance of being explicit with what's going on but also telling it with different characters so you got some flavour to what's happened. Dealing with a neat mix of theme’s so it's not just a re-hashed doom demons in space story once you get into it. Topping of with a neat ‘true’ boss that ties up the story, themes and game systems.Combat wise it's let down by a lack of variety in enemies, you get like 3 or 4 per the 3 different archetypes linked to the story. With multiple also being palette swapped for bosses with little difference other than bigger numbers and mode, including the same movesets. For the most part they are fun to fight, with a handful of hit boxes feeling inconsistent or unfair, or some attacks feeling overtuned. But enough that felt right that I still enjoyed the combat, with plenty of options of weapons and types to use.The levels I'm conflicted on. Overall they have the sort of interconnectivity, hidden off shoots and spots to explore that give me vibes of demon souls and dark souls 1. Loads to explore and see, but the quality of the places to explore is a bit hit and miss. Some zones feel tightly designed and have a good pace to explore through, then you take a turn and it can end up a bit barren and sparse, but in an unfinished sort of feel rather than what feels intentional? Like there's a zone with a large park in it, but it's mostly barren and has the same creature 10 times followed by a large barren road with nothing at either end, followed by a large building with one fight followed by multiple large rooms with nothing apart from some text and a location for a npc if you deal with them. But then at the other end a zone called the arisen dominion, it's fantastic, visually and the spaces you explore in it, fantastic, top to bottom, just enough things to fight throughout that's tense when first exploring. Multiple points whilst exploring it just stoped and though ‘man that looks cool’. When they nail it, they nail it really well, but when they don't, levels never felt broken just like stuffs missing.Visually, it's not gonna win awards for technical prowess. Even with settings maxed, some textures are a bit interesting and the lighting has that flat unity light engine look to, it's fine but never great. But what I found great is it's art direction. It reminds me of Blame and other works by Tsutomu Nihei. That far future stark dark concrete and steel brutalsium, it's not pretty but at times striking. And this game at times captures that feeling at it's best moments. The main character and several npc’s even have that far future transhumanism look very reminiscent of niheis work. Some people are gonna hate it, but if you can put up with dark future sci-fi corridors, they have some serviceable ones and some really good ones with what they could do.Systems wise, it's a darks souls mostly. You got your not-future-souls currency to spend on stats to boost health, damage weapons usage ect. That you can lose on death, save them from your corpse or lose them on death before collecting. The fairly standard solid system. It's bonfire equivalent with it's spin on it having a consumable allowing it to become a stop to teleport to other bonfires that have also been connected with the consumable. Also you can raise or lower the new game plus stats of the world with consumables at the bonfires, that's a cool idea. For the most part it's nothing new but solid with some new ideas here and there.It's also a bit janky bug wise. Audio levels would peak and blow out on foot steps. Corpses would play audio constantly when dead. Menu ui selection would flicker, sometimes select, sometimes not. Enemy ai would spin on the spot looking very daft at times when trying to track you behind a pillar. Ragdoll on deaths can sometimes be very funny, multiple of my deaths or kills just seeing a body crumple into a jittering ragdoll mess as if stuck in geometry. Mostly not game braking, but noticeable in that janky unpolished sort of way. I did have one full unity engine crash to desktop, fortunately with no progress loss. But other than that one crash I never had anything game breaking.This isn't a great game, it's got a bunch of flaws. But I really like it, it's got heart. It feels like this was a first attempt and I want to see what a second try would be like. They tried and got a bunch of stuff right with some cool ideas and art direction.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm having serious difficulties enjoy this game. Though I love the theme of an occult scifi game with a (literally) cosmic horror touch and have had thousands of (successful) hours of other Soulslikes on my track record... I think Hellpoint overdoes it.I cannot claim that I even laid one boss in this game or explored more than Pond + Embassy. And you'd be right by saying that I cannot possibly give this game any justice due to this. But: whereas other games of the same genre will gradually increase the difficulty and give you time to die and learn things step by step, Hellpoint doesn't. Even the tutorial area is already complex enough in layout to fully confuse you with extremely bad lighting choices, has tons of enemies and a prominently patrolling bully tank enemy that one-hits you if you don't constantly backtrack to level up. To get to the next area, you basically alert everything on the entire floor and have your first gangbang you'll likely not survive. Then you return, everything is back but there's also your green shade which spawns on death and pulps you with unlimited stamina as well as perfect knowledge of ALL the moves, stats and skills that your player character had at that point. And it also comes back again if you get killed by it. So even if you grind and level up, it's still better than you at this point of the game.Seriously, come on! This isn't even a difficulty curve, it's an overhanging cliff for crying out loud. I played Dark Souls II in Company of Champions mode all the way without even knowing and it was FINE. Combine this with really janky dodge mechanics and fancy but way too useless lighting if it comes to gameplay and you get a big gloomy mountain of frustration you need to -somehow- beat before even getting to the more interesting parts.And, again, you'd be right by saying that I'm not giving the game justice by not even mentioning the gorgeous architectural and cineastic moments it has. Or the soundscapes. If you've ever played E.Y.E: Divine Cybermancy - it's exactly there and gives you the same kind of awe in concept and flair. But to get there? Enduring all the uneven initial difficulty that doesn't care about ANYTHING that previous game did right? Sorry, no. Even Nethack did better and that's a masochist joke to begin with.TL;DR - the initial difficulty is so ridiculous at this stage that I'm about to get a refund. There's imho more rewarding games out there considering. Even if you enjoy a bit of masochism in your action adventures.

_childDocuments_.review: This was a pleasant surprise, that came at the exact right time for me.I just played (and reviewed) a soulslike that ended up being the quickest a soulslike (or perhaps, any game for that matter) made me feel it wasn't worth my time. So I'm going to do something different in this review, list the major things I felt were wrong with that other game, and how these DON'T apply to Hellpoint.In order of least to most severe (for me) these points were:4. The game was trying so hard to be Dark Souls that it didn’t have it’s own identity, and yet…3. it managed to fail completely at creating the experience you hope for in a soulslike.2. It was loaded with artificial difficulty, the bosses I fought were only difficult because of their large health pools, and because...1. the combat was extremely sluggish and unresponsive.Hellpoint, on the other hand, is incredibly unique aesthetically; it's scifi, but that kind of far future scifi where things are almost (but importantly, not quite) magic. It also has a few unique mechanics, rather than naming them all I'll just mentioned my favourite; your healing items gradually restore as you deal melee damage. This is a small change that quite drastically changes the way you play in an interesting way, as the lower you get on healing items, the more you're actually encouraged to play aggressively (somewhat like the newer DOOM games). Yet despite managing to be unique, it absolutely nails the feeling you'd hope for in a soulslike, in fact I'd go beyond that and say it actually feels like closer to an actual soulsborne game than any other souslike I've played; sure the lore isn't as deep, and (as I'll get to in a minute) the environments are built different, but it absolutely nails the atmosphere and the feeling of the gameplay itself.I also don't think there was any artificial difficulty in this game; it absolutely gets right that feeling a soulslike should have, where you might describe the combat is tough but fair, and that if you're struggling it's because you (or your character) need to improve. In other words it doesn't feel like the game is 'too hard', it feels like you haven't yet mastered it. Most of all though, I don't think anyone could describe the combat in Hellpoint as sluggish or unresponsive with a straight face, it is perfectly responsive and gloriously fast paced.Don't get me wrong, I wouldn't say Hellpoint is perfect but any negatives I could list are basically nitpicks in the grand scheme of things, and pretty much all of them are a matter of personal preference. For example, my opinion on soulslike environments is that they should somewhat mirror the combat, you enter an area and it seems impossible to learn (in the same way a boss might seem impossibly to beat), but by the end of the game it's hard to even remember a time where these seemed that overwhelming. Hellpoint however is just an outright maze from start to finish, I'm fairly confident if I jumped back into NG+ right now I'd still get lost in the majority of areas.I also found the difficulty a bit weird, progressing through the actual levels was almost exactly the level of difficulty you'd expect, but then the majority of the bosses were quite easy for a soulslike. Then if you attempt to go for the true ending of the game, the true final boss amps up the difficulty to insane levels; I actually think I might literally have died more to that boss than all the other bosses in the game combined (and also once you start the battle, you're locked in to it, so no heading out to improve equipment or farm some levels).There's a few other small things here and then, minor glitches and that sort of thing, but again I think these are all nitpicks. At the end of the day, I thoroughly enjoyed Hellpoint and can easily imagine myself playing through NG+ in the near future.
_childDocuments_.name: Hellpoint

_childDocuments_.review: There's a lot to like in Hellpoint, but after 33 hours played I just can't find it in my heart to truly recommend it. The final boss fight highlights everything that is wrong with the game, from janky angles and camera work, to hitboxes that simply don't connect despite them clearly passing through each other. With an unskippable cutscene before every boss attempt. It just isn't FUN, and isn't that what games are supposed to be? Being spammed by locked on attacks from offscreen just isn't fun. It's the kind of artificial challenge that you can't "git gud" past. If I ever install the game again to try my luck against the boss one more time, it won't be skill that gets me through, it will be luck. A real shame endcap to a game with a lot of full elements, but between this and the third boss, I can see now that these are intentional design choices not bugs.I am happy to report that after 11 more hours of play, I've not found anything as janky or broken as the boss in Sohn. Enemies and bosses seem much better tuned over all, areas have got lots of cool hidden things, and there are sections of lore to read if you hunt them down. The game is EXPANSIVE and open, and I've regularly gotten lost or played for about 30 minutes to finally die and realise I haven't got a clue how to get back to my bloodstain. All in all, a solid indie experience that I can recommend — except for that damned twin boss.Really enjoyed the Thespian Feast, despite it's sometimes janky camera, but currently cannot recommend the full game, as much as I'd like to.Positives:- lots of exploration and secrets to find- while not amazing graphically, the game has a DOOM-like hell-on-Earth aesthetic that I really like, and it has great atmosphere- enemy design is decent, albeit mixed in places (what's with the green floating fish?!)Mixed:- controls are a mixed bag. Plunging attack seems wildly inaccurate, shield smash doesn't seem to do anything (unless it's just supposed to be 'running with your shield up' which you can do anyways.- areas just aren't super memorable. They have the really twisty maze-like style of The Surge 2 but lack a lot of the visual distinctiveness to pull it off. Many places with similar neon signs, for example, offer little more than confusion and dull backtracking.- some of the run-backs to bosses are too harsh and crowded by enemies. Yes there are shortcuts and closer breaches, but some of them are hidden behind secret walls that you might literally only find because someone else in the game has left one of their gold handprints on it.Negatives:- hit boxes. They're all over the place.- status effects. No idea what any of them do and there's seemingly no help screen for them. Two of the first three bosses have an affect that slows you down and I have no clue which resistance might help counter it.- collision. The pair of enemies that make up the third boss encounter are either really bugged or just plain badly designed. The one with the censer can stunlock you to death through scenery because his ranged attack (and they both have ranged and melee attacks) goes through all the terrain. The one with the staff can damage you by hitting his staff on the ground even if you're nowhere near him and are shields up.- clock thing. I get the idea that the black hole influences what is going on in the game world, but there's zero explanation of how any of it works and in a game like this where the difficulty already seems to vary wildly, a little bit more knowledge would help.- the ghost. I don't mind the mechanic, but they feel like a real waste of resources to beat, don't offer enough of a reward to compensate, and often ignore attacks after you've parried/shield-blocked them.All in all, with a few patches under its belt, Hellpoint will hopefully live up to the promise that I saw in the Thespian Feast, but right now it is more on the frustration end than the fun end, and no amount of cool secrets to find will balance out poorly-balanced combat and bosses.
_childDocuments_.name: Hellpoint

_childDocuments_.review: I initially played Hellpoint on PS4 when it released but moved to PC for the DLC because 30 FPS is hard to go back to. It's both incredibly unique and also very obviously derivative by taking a sci-fi, cosmic horror themed story and placing it in a challenging Souls-inspired gameplay loop mixed with an environmental design that calls back to the sense of dread and isolation from the original Dead Space. It has a jank-filled charm and creates a really unique feeling that's difficult to describe. It won't be for everyone, but I absolutely adore Hellpoint.Pros:- Absolutely drenched in atmosphere. Hellpoint has a bleak, surreal, otherworldly futuristic visual style that really gives the game a really awesome immersiveness that I haven't experienced since the original Dark Souls or Dead Space- Fantastic level design that encourages exploration with tons of secrets to be found- A minimalist but very haunting soundtrack- A slower, methodical combat system, again channeling the original Dark Souls feel and (mostly) gets it right- Some really fun boss fightsCons:- Floaty jumping and forced platforming are a terrible mixture- Some bosses are more frustrating than challenging, and some bosses later are reused as normal enemies. - Random sounds not playing during combat- Occasional weird feedback during combat where the only indication you've taken damage is your decreased health- Some input buffering oddities where at times it can feel like you've queued up 2-3 actions instead of one on the next input- Some of the water reflections not only don't match the room, but look like they are stretched from 64x64 resolution even in the highest quality settings. It's the first thing I noticed after starting a new game since you're surrounded by water.Overall I'd give it a 7/10 for a general attempt at an "objective" review, but for me personally it's a 9/10. I love this game.
