_childDocuments_.review: Hellpoint is a crudely polished gem in the rough.While this title may not have all the resources to become a masterpiece, it certainly makes the most out of what it has. It is a damn solid souls-like with a fresh atmosphere, engaging lore (albeit not entirely fleshed out at times) and a variety of different builds to play around with. My only two complaints are the bugs and some combat animations. Don't get me wrong, being an avid fan of Bethesda games and Cyberpunk 2077, I am no stranger to bugs, but at times these ones can hinder your expedition if you are unlucky enough experience them. Most notably, NPC's can sometimes get stuck before they move to their next quest location or you might get stuck in the floor and die, with no checkpoint for miles around. That being said, nothing was really game breaking, even when my nerd rage warmed up to a light simmer. As for the weapons, some feel weirdly janky, while others had a much better handling (cheers to you, spears and halberd gang)  though none of the equipment felt ineffective.The setting of this game was fresh and varied, you could be slaying a highly advanced army of monastic hell worshipping robots, in their pristine halls while their golden pyramids tower overhead. Or you could be wading through a valley of blood and viscera, while some skinned torture victims (of a demonic cannibal cult) eagerly wait to punch the ♥♥♥♥ out of you if you wander too close.If you get this game, make sure to get the DLC's too.Is it Elden Ring? No.Is it absolutely worth your time and attention when it goes on sale? You bet!All in all, a small studio brought us an entertaining sci-fi horror/action game and I will eagerly await a sequel.(P.S There are multiple endings, though witnessing them is about as unceremonious as an escort splitting as soon as you pay them. The journey up to that point is a wild one, but you'll be left with a yearning for a deeper connection.)

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE: My complaints for this game still stand, with even more attention to even more bugs that cropped up during my playthrough, but I finished the game. This game is much more enjoyable in co-op.-----At its core, Hellpoint is a copycat. The combat is reminiscent of Dark Souls, its dodging mechanic almost identical to Bloodborne. In ways, its lore is hidden, just like Soulsborne games, if not a little more direct in its delivery. Bonfires in this game are known as breaches, and serve the exact same purpose as their counterparts.Orbiting around this core, however, are features and details that separate Hellpoint from its peers, make it a game of its own. Most people are quick to dismiss Hellpoint for its similarities to -- let's face it -- superior games, but those who give it time and attention will notice that it does tend to stand apart and establish its own identity.So, why am I giving this game a thumbs down? Poor game design and bugs, much like everyone else who finds themselves ultimately not liking this game.A fairly big bug that tends to get me killed more often than not is when the lock-on refuses to switch to enemies that are close to me. I've encountered this more times than I would have forgiven and, as of the time of this review, am dealing with it in a particularly frustrating boss fight.Another example of poor game design is the stamina drain. When dealing with stronger enemies, it feels like it takes two hits to drain your entire bar and, if you happen to be stunned, a full five seconds or longer to recover and move again, but in that time, you can get stunlocked over and over until you're dead. This is the most debilitating issue. Decreasing the difficulty often doesn't help because, even if the damage is slightly lessened, the stamina drain and overlong stun-state will just kill you anyway because everything's hitboxes are strangely wide.I want to like this game. I think the atmosphere and the setting are pretty great. The story is interesting as well, but it's hard to like a game whose design actively fights against you every encounter in which you find yourself. I'm not done with the game just yet, but if I can't find a way around issues that should have been fixed a while ago, I might have to drop the game for good.

_childDocuments_.review: There have been plenty of souls like clones all over the internet lately, which have been nothing but a copy-paste of multiple art styles, combat, or even the weapon UI. Glad to say that Hellpoint is not one of those clones. It is an inspiration taken from Dark souls for sure, but it stands out entirely on its base with proper and profound lore and its world build up.After several years into its development, Hellpoint finally releases today on Steam and consoles. Special thanks to Tinybuild/Cradle Games for providing me with a key early to do a proper in-depth review.I always wanted a soul-like game in a futuristic space setting for a long time, and I finally got to experience it. The game feels exactly like dark souls in both combat and visual aid, with its own futuristic/cyberpunk-ish vibes and colors with black contrast to complement its visuals.Hellpoint is set at a space station called Irid Novo, where you take the role of a 3d printed pawn of your creator whose agenda/scheme is unknown to the player, and you are given full control/freedom to do whatever you want.Your primary mission is to collect a minimum of 100% of the data by going through different areas and exploring the deep space station and opening up breaches for checkpoints for easier traversal. There are multiple endings in this game and after you have beat it once, you will be taken over to New Game+ where you will have your current arsenal and weapons and would continue with your old knowledge of things to trying out different dialogues/ pathways leading to newer areas or even more unique enemies.Several boss battles feel easier than the dark souls games, at least the early few enemies are more manageable for those who play RPG/soulslike games a lot. It will be a decent challenge for new players but would get easily adjusted to their attack patterns since most of them have 2-3 unique attacks and skillsets.The attack animation, the enemy hitboxes, and the boss locations are well thought out with excellent visual fidelity. The entire Irid Novo and the surrounding areas in the space station have their designs and live characteristics, which makes it seem unique in its way.Hellpoint has its weapon variety, including melee weapons, ranged weapons, and magic weapons. While opening breaches, you will be greeted with the character augmentation screen where you can level up your character in whichever way you please.Read More by visiting Us at :

_childDocuments_.review: Ok wow, first of all. Ignore the negative reviews.People see things through rose colored glasses, no one remembers how the first Souls game was actually like...Now, onto this game. I played the beta over a year ago and loved it, and it was super unpolished, the controls weren't too responsive, the attacks felt floaty(like dark souls 2 cough cough) I am happy to say that it's been addressed. The combat feels great, there's weight to the attacks, it doesn't just feel like you're waving a weapon around the dodge feels sooo good, think Bloodborne. The graphics are not some omg out of this world graphics, but they're really good for what it is, people are expecting some insane budget from a super small studio here, they are good, shadows look great, it's detailed enough to appreciate the art and locales. I really think the style of graphics suit this game perfect.The exploration, the exploration is really good, there's a lot of hidden passageways to be found and shortcuts galore. I accidentally fell somewhere and turned out to be great as I found a weapon in some nook, exploration definitely pays off in this game, and the ability to jump around allows you to get to a lot of places, I love the vertical exploration aspect. The skill system is pretty good, usual build situations, strength for heavy weapons, their version of dex for quick weapons. The death system is interesting, it spawns a ghost that you can kill and should kill before it kills you(think Hollow Knight). The music is good when it's there, again, it's the usual gloomy type of environmental music you'd find in this genre. The gameplay overall feels very very smooth, again, this is coming from someone who played the beta and found it wonky and janky.  It's good, the controls are responsive, and I do think that with a couple of patches they can fine tune them even more, but it's not like you press a button and the character doesn't  move right. This game has definitely scratched that Souls itch. Honestly, it feels like a DS in space. I honestly hope it sells well because I'd love to see what they can do in the future with a bigger budget. And finally, I can't complain about the multiplayer because I haven't tried it nor am I going to anytime soon. I love soloing my games, as I like to say "git good" and very good job peeps at Cradle Games. This game was well worth the wait, just a tad more polish and this gem will shine to bright. Now, back to playing, I'm spending precious time away from this baby<3

This includes boss items but unfortunately you can only talk to the npc who turns them into boss weapons in your own game which is the only flaw with that.... There's also a split-screen option though it would be nice to be able to swap between vertical and horizontal since larger weapons can block the screen. I truly believe that the only thing this game is really missing at the moment is a little bit of polish and I'm very excited to see more content in the new dlc. Fantastic souls-like, 10/10, just want more.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really surprised that the game is as good as it is. I initially dismissed it as a crappy souls clone but there are some fantastic aspects to this game. I think its biggest achievement is exploration - you will likely enjoy this game a lot if you're a completionist and like searching every nook and cranny for secrets (because 95% of the time you'll actually find something). There's good world interconnectivity and verticality - you'll constantly find shortcuts to unlock as well as different ways to enter areas you've previously explored, often to blocked off sections that contain secrets, gear, etc. I haven't explored too much into it but making different builds seems to be pretty fun and encourages multiple playthroughs. Weapons have a familiarity system which unlock passive buffs (e.g. increased health, stamina) as well as active weapon skills. you gain familiarity by hitting stuff with said weapon. Melee weapons seem to get 2 active skills (for example, the ceremonial dagger has a backstab ability and later on the ability to throw it) so it's basically the weapon art system from dark souls 3 but with more variety. Combat is decent. It's not amazing but not terrible either. Thankfully the controls are for the most part responsive. Enemy and boss variety aren't as good as they would be in a souls title but it's not really to the point it's egregious.Also this probably goes without saying but there's quite a bit of jank - I believe this is the first game this dev team made. Personally I'm not too bothered with a lack of polish in certain areas but I just wanted to make clear that this game is rough around the edges in certain aspects.Overall I've really enjoyed my time with the game so far. I usually stay away from alleged "souls-like" games like the plague but I think this game deserves a spot in the pantheon of souls-like games that aren't a complete ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ along with salt & sanctuary lol

_childDocuments_.review: Have not yet finished Hellpoint just yet, but am close enough to give a review. Would say something like 7 or 8 out of 10. The game is fun, longer than I thought at first, and while it can be a bit maddening (like souls games, though I feel some areas you need to do a lot between checkpoints/breaches/bonfires) - I really only "rage quit" for a few hours after losing 120k axioms due to platforming being a bit tough sometimes - like trying to jump to the left onto another zipper rail from one you are already on, as you are "stuck" in the take-off direction (basically - beating an area backwards is harder navigation wise for some areas).The short-hand, is that this game is an interesting souls-like with many of the same features and stuff, but it also has it's own "persona" that shines through the entire time to remind you it's not an exact copy, and sometimes even steps far outside of the normal "souls-like" box to nail home that it is something else.Combat is similar enough, but it is also different in the included "gear leveling" system where you master the weapons you use and can gain new weapon skills. Some also just double damage, or increase your stats a little, so building a "kit" may also include using a weird weapon because it adds 7% to your life total when maxed for example. The 2-hand combat is also a little less involved than Souls games, but in it's own way that also works really well. Your off-hand is more staves/shields/guns while your main hand can be all but shields. The weapon types also blend nicely enough that only some weapons just feel inherently "not good" (like daggers with short range, but against some bosses this is not going to work too well). Additionally - in regards to the "magic" items, there is one of each type for 3 of the 4 or 5 "elements" (cube/staff/hand and Induction/Nihil/Light); and so they are just palette/damage swaps, but you don't need to comply like "Ohh, I want a laser, only fire has that so rip Nihil Sorceror". There is however 1 thing to get used to - being how your healing items work - think about it more like Bloodborne, where weapons "bloodlet" enemies, and the more you bloodlet the faster you recharge healing items and Energy. Dying will also refill you to the default 2 (which heal all the way, and buffing it gives you the ability to store more); options are also very unique with 1 seeming quite "OP" later on.Movement (and combat) are also a bit clunkier feeling at times, so certain elements (mostly platforming) can be a bit of a chore. Have died more times due to run/jumping (which you land and take 1 step guaranteed) because my guy takes the one last step off a cliff, or I hit one spot where it was 5 normal jumps and then 1 running jump (which I didn't expect and just missed the landing); easily died more to gravity than all enemies combined. Otherwise though, it feels like it fits well; attacks are locked in and you have some "dodge attacks" to also help, otherwise roaming around is fun and combat is still good.Enemy design is neat - each area more or less has at least 1 unique duderino, and some are time sensitive to an area; so to a minor degree the areas feel "alive". One of the experiences I remember the most being when I went to an area to get my Axioms/Souls back, and then a new mini-boss like guy was there and completely surprised me.Speaking of dying and getting your stuff back - they actually upped the challenge from your normal Souls experience in a great way. Everything is about the same, except now you need to fight a mirror image of yourself, which is a great test to see how your build is doing.Lastly - I will touch on the ambiance a bit. The game has a lot, and manages to also explain some things more than Souls games traditionally do, but less simultaneously. I imagine this is where the multiple play-throughs would come in handy, but some secrets and stuff are buried DEEP. Some of it is stuff only the beta testers would know a lot about (like the codes right at the beginning, and the secret door behind another secret door style stuff). Additionally - there is more to do in the "Underworld" than one traditionally would imagine; figured it out right before fighting my second major boss, and enjoyed the detail quite a bit.The way everything pairs, the visuals, the music, ambiance, hell - even the way the levels interconnect and the sparing use of the "zipper" lines; this feels more like a strange blend of Dead Space (level and enemy), Metroid Prime (Level, collecting data, Elements and traversal - the zippers always remind me of Morph tracks), Dark Souls/Bloodborne (general gameplay and vibe), and then small portions of Eternal Darkness (more weird enemies, 3 gods theme, some "revelation" moments), and finishes with it's unique flair being stuff like the magic system (it goes a little nuts, but beams are not as OP as they appear which is great) and it's "omnicube" utility that I really wish I got to know immediately (warps "home" are FREE - I thought it would 0 me out like the base ones in souls games).There is more I could mention, like you can level gear, this game has a new/fresh take one elemental damage (radiation poisoning is spookier than poison, nihil makes your screen FOV get all weird), some quest-lines are hard to find but have cool rewards, but honestly there's already too much here lol. Am interested at eventually getting into the DLC also, as I am almost done with the story (I imagine), but it is fun enough to want more.

_childDocuments_.review: Review title: A very mediocre Dark Souls experienceSo I just sunk my first hour plus into Hellpoint, and I have to say it's...so far it's not really impressive. While I can appreciate the fact that the makers of Hellpoint were obviously big fans of both Dark Souls and Dead Space, their execution leaves much to be desired. The game isn't a complete trainwreck, however from what I saw of other reviews of this game, my expectations were much higher.Hellpoint starts you off as a nameless mass-production model clone that awakens inside a literal vat of goo (ugh, THAT tired trope?! Really??) on board the space station Irid Novo, and a mysterious voice known only as The Author directs you to meet up with them "at the end of the Embassy Hall". After that, the game provides you with no further instruction or guidance and leaves you to fend for yourself, as is Dark Souls tradition. Clearly something has gone wrong, because the station is infested with freakish bloodthirsty monstrosities that exist only to end your pitiful existence (and more often than not they succeed at ending your incarnation). The game quickly gives you a crappy melee weapon and a pitiful shield that might as well be made out of cardboard and tasks you with exploring the rest of Irid Novo, which is a very frustrating endeavor due to the sheer size, scale, and complexity of the station. There are many different twisting paths to follow, some of which loop back upon themselves, while others either lead to hidden secrets/goodies or simply become dead ends. There's also no automap, which normally isn't such a big deal however it's virtually impossible to keep everything straight inside your head once again due to the sheer size of the maps. Normally having big areas to explore keeps the game nice & fresh, however in Hellpoint's case it becomes a case of repetitive run down space station corridors and rooms filled with repetitive enemies (oh noes, I've encountered that same exact zombie wielding a rusty pipe or sharp poking stick for the umpteenth time, whatever shall I do??). Combat feels very clunky compared to Dark Souls. For one, the fodder enemies easily get stun locked. So rather than attempting to analyze each enemy's move set and figure out a strategy, the most viable strategy is oftentimes just spam light attacks until the enemy dies, rinse & repeat for each enemy in the room. This obviously doesn't work with the bigger/tougher enemies & bosses, however the normal enemies become very boring & stale after just a couple encounters with them. Also, your healing injections (think Estus Flask) only replenishes from killing enemies or dying, it doesn't recharge at Breaches (aka Bonfires from Dark Souls). Connecting to a Breach does heal you, fortunately, however you have to kill many enemies before recharging a single healing injection which means it's very likely you could wind up with low health and not be near a Breach to heal.Speaking of Breaches, let's talk about placement. In my entire hour plus of wandering around (and dying!) inside Irid Novo, I found precisely ONE Breach: the initial one that shows up right at the beginning of the game. I took my time and carefully explored, hoping to find another Breach but alas I didn't. Bear in mind that there are liberal amounts of enemies in each area, I wound up killing somewhere in the neighborhood of like 40-50 enemies and didn't encounter any Breaches beyond the first one before meeting an untimely death at the hands of some angelic-looking knight wielding a big bonk sword and board. The game is very stingy with Breaches, which makes healing and progressing through the game's complex and mind-boggling mazes that much more difficult.To Hellpoint's credit, the devs did attempt to shake up the standard Dark Souls formula a bit. Enemies no longer respawn by resting, instead there's an in-game clock displayed in the HUD and enemies reappear at certain intervals. This mechanic is meant to encourage players to hurry, however in practice it just leads to frustration because of how easy it is to get lost or not be able to figure out where to go. Another idea that sounds cool on paper but totally fails in practice are player ghosts. Upon each & every death, the game spawns an NPC clone of you that you have to fight along with enemies that might already be present. Your evil ghost clone uses the same exact weapons as you do, however its stats are a little higher and it fights a lot better than you. Do note that this applies even during tough boss battles, so if you're having a tough time with a boss you might have no other choice but to summon a friend for help rather than try to complete the battle on your own.My final gripe lies with the atmosphere/environment of the game itself. Part of the appeal of Dark Souls isn't just the punishing combat or stiff penalties that come with death (which ultimately lead to a sense of triumph when you do finally succeed), it's the world and environment. Dark Souls is a dying world that's very interesting to explore, the people you meet are dripping with character and flavor, and there's a lot of lore & backstory to discover on your own if that's your thing. Hellpoint is just a run down space station full of deadly creatures and that's about it, it's absolutely lacking Dark Soul's heart & soul (no pun intended). Without that crucial element, the game feels more like a drag than a good time. I do plan on playing a little more, however this review constitutes my first impression of the game and I'm definitely not holding my breath. Is Hellpoint a terrible game? No. But I was expecting much more, and so far I feel very disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll hesitate to recommend this one to Soulslike generalists, but push it more heartily if you're okay traversing massive, labyrinthine, brutalistic architecture a la NaissancE (a free platformer here on Steam) and like your plot to be about as well-spoken as EYE Divine Cybermancy's (a cult (or occult?) classic). It's also got a fair amount of that EYE-tier jankiness, which can try on one's patience.Warnings aside, I am enamored with Hellpoint.The world is massive and sprawling (if you can find the key items to let you get to different areas of course), which means that the route you find and take is likely to be different from the route the next player takes. This also means that it may take you a fair while to find new equipment, or end up rather out-of-depth if you take a wrong turn. It's, well, it's bleak and crushing in a way I find difficult to describe. There's a keen, peculiar sort of dread knowing that each room leads to two more rooms, and each to two thereafter, and then splits into three, never knowing which turn takes you to the tram to another zone or breach (this version of bonfires). This is honestly the game's strongest offering in atmosphere, besides the failed-state space station of occult power hovering around a black hole thing. Everything is sharp angles, shiny metals and obsidians, monolithic, bleak, and you, this wretched amalgamation some something calls 'human' are an insignificant visitor, a mote swirling in the cascading apathy of a structure ceaselessly reveling in its state of catastrophe. Every place is a liminal space because nothing belongs there, least of all you.The rest of it, though, well, it's jank, and if you have no patience for jank, or for environments that just don't respect casual or sensible player routing, you're going to struggle to enjoy Hellpoint. There's not a huge variety of enemies, bosses get recycled into common mooks depending on where you go, you may not find a set of armor or equipment to fit your stat set for a while (there's a few that require no particular stats), nothing is particularly well explained. Music cuts out immediately at area thresholds (well, ambiance, not music), some enemy animations are bizarre or not well telegraphed or just look awkward, your character spaghetti ragdolls out if you die while wearing the scrap shield. Laugh, sigh, move on, respect that the big bad you faced in the second zone becomes a casual mook later (as emphasis you're getting stronger, perhaps), and try a different path. Maybe you'll find a weapon to suit your Reflex/Foresight stat aspirations over there.Combat handles okay, though there's nothing exceptional to write home about. Dodges work, some attacks are worth blocking, back attacks do more damage, certain damage types are more effective against certain enemies than others, etc. I like that it's not the standard spread of fire/ice/lightning/etc, or at least it's decorated differently- you have induction (fire), entropic (cold), radiation, light, nihl, and physical. Killing walking aberrations of flesh and bone with the power of nihilism (assuming that's what nihl is) is pretty rad, in any case.The platforming is on occasions kind of touchy or kludgy (yeah, there's platforming in this soulslike). Oftentimes some clever jumping leads to a secret area with a secret collectible coin, new piece of equipment, a key item for cutting corners around the station, or just more axions (souls), but sometimes your inquisitive platforming takes you out of bounds and you clip through objects and fall to your death. It does take my immersion out a fair amount when the game is rewarding curious acrobatics without taking extra precautions to keep players from getting too inquisitive. Some thought went into making sure you try and see if you can make this or that jump or what might be around that cliff, and that scratches an exploratory itch something fierce.Bottom line is this, really- if you just want more Souls, pass on Hellpoint, it's just too divergent from what makes Souls a cohesive experience. If you want to get like SUPER lost and are totally down to clown with a game that doesn't tell you jack squat about where to go or what to do, Hellpoint looks a lot more appealing. Make sure you know you want this before you buy, and make sure you've got some patience to spare, but if you know what you're in for, you'll probably enjoy it. If jank scares you, wait 'til it's on sale. If you want it sooner, it's in Humble Choice for May.Edit: Doubled my playtime, got all the achievements. Every point made stands.

_childDocuments_.review: Surprisingly good.  I saw the mixed reviews when the demo came out and thought: 'maybe not.'   The good reviews I see everywhere today made me decide to give it a go anyways and I am glad I did.  Yes, the graphics are not AAA but they do the job - the immersion is great, level design top notch, enemy variety and difficulty good.  The combat is very dark souls - a little clunky but lots of fun.  The price is just right.  The story is just...barely  there.  It would be nice when devs start to treat stories in game as more then just flimsy excuses for the gameplay.  But when you are rolling fighting exploring honestly you forget about it.  Yes it doesn't make any sense that everyone in this far future space station fights with sword and shield, the secret defense of the space station is a weak human clone etc.. but really who cares? - huge station to explore, bosses to put down, secrets to find. _childDocuments_.review: Avoid this game if you've played Dark Souls, Nioh, or even Code Vein. Hellpoint does not live up to those titles polish and general design philosophy. If you've never played a proper "souls-like" title, you might find this passable if you are interested in a different angle of ARPGs. Equip a glaive, throw away your shield and stunlock enemies to oblivion with your overhead L1 strikes.A Souls-like game with a futuristic setting on a spacestation where strange, hellish creatures warp in and cause chaos. You have just awoken on this station and are trying to figure out what exactly is going on. It's a combat-focused game with sparse narrative tid-bits strewn around in forms of messages left on walls, text dialogues from computer terminals, and conversations with a few NPCs you'll meet along the way.I like the setting and situation you find yourself in. Feels a bit like a blend of Hellgate London, Dead Space, and Dark Souls. Although a very misguided and ill-tasting blend. Beyond this, I can only say the crafting mechanic was a bit interesting at the start. Mostly since you could upgrade and refurbish old pieces of a set into a better, and more effective set. I also like searching for hidden rooms, even though most of them are easy to spot once you recognise the copy-pasted wall asset.The visual fidelity seems fine at first, but later you realise the environments are mostly in grayscale and/or very low saturation, with lots of copy-pasted structures. You will find segments of walls you saw in the early game in every single locale on this space station. Not only are many assets reused, but some have low texture resolution even on maximum settings. (I play with a water-cooled RTX 2080.) The lighting is hit-and-miss. It works in some environments when it's a bit varied, but when it's a flat light level with no variety the scenery feels very empty and soul-less (hah).It's your standard souls-like control scheme with the twist that you have a dedicated jump button. The combat animations are stiff and has a very awkward delay on . Trust me, it's not because of the anticipation frames. You frequently make an extra attack, or two, by accident and if you are unluckily positioned it'll cause you to tumble into a death pit.The battles themselves are either a stunlock fest (both ways), a horde of enemies piling onto you, or getting juggled into a corner and locked in. Shields are obsolete since most large enemies can hit you through them and stun you for three whole seconds. Bosses can combo you like it's Marvel vs Capcom since you have  meaning you may get unlucky and get caught in a high-damage combo with no hope of getting out. Many powerful boss attacks doesn't even knock you down, instead you're locked in regular hit stun until you die.Many weapon movesets are reused for other weapons in it's category and the glaive (even though it's a one-handed sword) was the one I found most serviceable, but not good. Most movesets are delayed, sluggish, jerky, and has abundant action queuing to a fault.This is the absolute  aspect of this game.Depending on how meticulous you explore, you'll encounter some platforming sections with great items hidden away. You'll have to climb the environment to find these treasures. That's fine by itself, but the controls are so painfully stiff and the momentum is so awful that you have very little control over your jump velocity. More often than not you will fall to your death attempting these stunts. Many times you'll walk through a doorway only to find yourself falling to your death. Lots of sudden drops where you cannot see past corners or slopes because of terrible camera angling/lighting/room design.Tiny rooms, narrow hallways, small arenas, and miniscule platforms.The entire game is very claustrophobic. Every single locale is built out of tiny rooms and narrow corridors and lots, and lots of doors. Majority of fights are a struggle not to collide into walls or fall off ledges while trying to dodge sweeping attacks from enemies of all kinds. All areas look very similar and It's easy to lose track of where you've been since most assets are featureless. Lots of locales loop into each other several times over with the exact same door+button combo that you'll be unsure if you've already been there or if it's a new area within the locale.Many sound effects are missing completely.Running has no sound effects at all, some enemies' attacks (including bosses) produce no sounds at all, the very aggressive object culling in the game engine cuts away sound effects coming from outside your viewport.Many sounds are horrible mixed/normalised. One example, a thrall's unarmed swiping attack has a higher base volume than bosses large slamming/exploding attacks. The voice acting are just incoherent mumbling causing you to only read the text and not get any sort of emotional reading out of any NPC.Bipedal xenobytes convention.Almost all enemies you encounter are bipedal humanoids with four body type variants and palette swaps. After 15 hours I only encountered five enemies that weren't bipedal. Even then, two out of those were disembodied humanoid torsos. Extreme waste of potential to throw yourself to creativity and create any amalgamations of horrible hellish creatures.This game had high potential, but it was utterly wasted on repetitive locales, bad/forced platforming, confusing level design, awkward combat, and really uninspired enemy designs.

_childDocuments_.review: Again I wish for a thumbs sideways, because this is right on the fence for me for recommending. On one hand there were many enjoyable elements and improvements on other souls games, but on the other hand some design choices and bugs detracted from the experience. TL;DR more enjoyable co-op than DS3, but not nearly as good as Remnant: From the Ashes.Hellpoint starts off strong, and for the first third of the game I was hooked.The combat is solid and the co-op was not janky when compared to other soulslikes. You're not constantly being invaded because there is a matchmaking option for co-op and pvp separately, or you can invite a friend and they progress with you and the loot is shared (for the most part, and the exceptions to this are aggravating).The weapon variety gives more builds viability, and many builds take advantage of the unique ranged weapon integration (melee hits charge your ranged weapon of choice) but this is squashed by the inability to respec so you are locked into one playstyle and lose the ability to experiment at all, so 90% of the gear you get you will never be able to check out.Lastly my favorite part of Hellpoint and the most unique is the time-related difficulty. There is a clock in the upper left at all times and when your orbit around a black hole aligns all the enemies get harder and some special events spawn. It really mixes up the gameplay just a bit which is enough to keep engagement and freshness. Really should have taken advantage of this aspect in naming, something like HellHour or HellTime... Hell O'Clock.... obviously something better than that but I never formed a connection between the game itself and the name Hellpoint...   Hell Noon!!! Boom perfect name.The environment looks good and enemy and level design is not bad, but that's where things take a turn.The biggest issue is not being able to teleport freely between bonfires (data breaches). An item is required to link a bonfire to the network for teleport-able ones, and those items are very rare so you're hesitant to even use them at all. This makes forming a cohesive layout of the world much more difficult than it needs to be. There is no map, which would be fine if areas had distinguishable landmarks or features instead of labyrinthine indoor corridors. Some of the connections between areas are not obvious, leading to substantial searching for where you need to go next which is very difficult if you don't even know where you are and have no way to return to anywhere familiar.The second factor that made Hellpoint slip for me is the difficulty curve. It was not super difficult to start but I attributed that to going through the game with a co-op partner. About midway the enemies and bosses started to get even easier... and at each bonfire there is an option to increase or decrease the difficulty of enemies "in this area" which I did not want to mess with because I would like to experience what is laid out as it is intended not trying to predict how difficult I think each encounter should be.. Towards the end of the game we were splitting off from each other basically unkillable even though we never grinded for level ups, and my friend killed the final boss in three seconds with magic before I was even able to land a hit. We had more deaths to falling than to all enemies and bosses combined.

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: I finished the game with the default difficulty setting, you can increase or decrease settings with ingame items called effigies, you can find them in the world lying around. Co-op also didn't work at the time I finished the game, was really looking forward to playing it with a friend and do some PvP, but aight, sometimes it be like that.Summarized:- sci-fi souls like game- responsive controls, platform/jumping sections are scuffed- combat is FUN with fast weapons, slow weapons seem to lack the impact you'd expect, I didn't try catalysts (magic) or rifles/ranged weapons- some boss fights are heavily telegraphed and thus pretty easy (except the golden twin boss, which was actually challenging, that's about it though... can't say anything about the final boss as it bugged out for me...)- a lot of exploring available, however most of the time it felt pointless and dragged out- story is semi-interesting, there's a couple sidequests you can do- level design is hella confusing after the third boss, I recommend to not hesitate to look up a guide if you hit a wall... if you don't want to run around aimlessly for hours on where to go next- quite a lot of bugs at launch, visual glitches (menu and crafting values), enemy AI, ragdolls etc- sometimes I couldnt get rid of the feeling that no one play tested the game before launch- lack of music/OST? most of it just sounded like ambient. you can find some juke boxes though, which was pretty funny for the moment, they have some cool tunestldr; Combat made me stick around til the end, but not enough for NG+. Buy the game when it has gotten some updates/fixes. If you are a souls gamer, please increase the difficulty, the default one was very underwhelming. It's a good entry to the series, so I'd recommend it when it's a bit more polished compared to launch day. The devs seem to work really hard on it right now, which is great.

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE: I have now finished the game, including getting the "true ending". Overall, my opinion is about the same, but there are some more gripes that have arisen. Notably-Many bosses are recycled smaller enemies with big health pools (though the bosses that are unique are fun and cool, I just wish there were more).-Some secrets yield the same rewards as other secrets, like armor sets and weapons, making them less rewarding. However, I think this was the devleopers' intent, as the game is EXTREMELY open in terms of exploration. I mean, you can go basically anywhere from the start of the game if you know what to do.That leads me into some more positives though!-Repeat playthroughs are fun due to being able to explore the world in a different order that you didn't know of before. My second playthrough ended up being even more fun due to knowing how to access a sort-of-later-game area early on and getting a good "magic" weapon. BTW magic is broken and super powerful. I melted the "true final boss" with a magic build in like 10 seconds, even with the difficulty increased a bit, so while that's not exactly a positive, it is nice to have a bit of a power fantasy after getting stomped by it for a while with a different build.-Build variety in this game is nice, if unbalanced, which is fine. Strength builds are viable and fun, but lose out to magic/dex builds easily. I haven't tried guns yet, but if they function similarly to magic, even if not as overpowered, they are probably really fun to weave into combat.Overall, I still really enjoy this game and will probably do a playthrough using guns. I might see about speedrunning it casually too, but not sure yet. The openness of the game could make it a fun speedrun game.ORIGINAL REVIEW:About 7 hours in now, and I am thoroughly enjoying my time with this game. It's definitely taken a lot of inspiration from Dark Souls in the best ways. Not just in gameplay, but also in level design. There's lots of interconnecting paths, TONS of secrets, like holy cow there are so many secrets that reward exploration generously. There's also platforming due to the game having a dedicated jump button, and it's pulled of better than you might expect! They seem to know what they're working with, and it honestly elevates the exploration (pun intended) and makes it even more fun and satisfying. The atmosphere and art direction of the game is extremely good, and it's exactly what I've been craving in a souls-like. Sci-fi horror is a fantastic combo, and they pull it off well. The lore is interesting, nothing mindblowing yet, but keeps me wanting to learn more. There also appears to be good build variety, which I absolutely love, as that will keep me coming back for more playthroughs.Also, this game has not only online co-op, but couch co-op as well! That's crazy and always an extremely welcome addition for people like myself who love playing games in-person with friends.The game isn't perfect though, and I will say my biggest gripe is the UI. It's not bad exactly, but there are things that could be communicated better, streamlined, and some things that you cannot even see. For example, the "tenacity" stat on armor doesn't have a sort of "total" amount on the stats page, which is pretty annoying due to it being poise. There might also be  some questionable design decisions with some weapons, but that's kind of always going to be a thing in a souls-like it seems. The only one instance of this that I've come across is the "Infused Column" weapon. It seems to make it into a hyrbid strength/magic stat weapon, but it doesn't seem to scale well off magic and makes it less worthwhile to use than the base weapon.Overall, I'd definitely recommend this game for fans of the genre. I can see myself enjoying the rest of this game and doing numerous playthroughs. Hats off to the developers for making a great game!

_childDocuments_.review: -------------------------------------Scroll down to the next line for the review--------------------------------Just quickly wanted to say that you shouldn't listen to a lot of the negative reviews, especially the ones that are complaining about level design and co-op. If they're complaining about the level design then they don't understand what good level design is. Yes, there are a lot of ways to go and you do get lost sometimes, but whose fault is it that you can't remember what way you went? Yours. That's your own fault. And the Co-Op is fine, yes there are some bugs with it but you guys have to understand that this isn't some massive AAA developer with hundreds of millions of dollars to throw at the game. The coop works just fine, the worst thing that can happen is that one of you have to reconnect. Seriously just how spoiled are some of you. Some guy was even suggesting that this 20+ hour game with tons or replayability should be priced at 15 bucks. Seriously if you're mad about spending 35 bucks on a great game then go get a job. Ridiculous. -----------------------------------------------------------Review-------------------------------------------------------The game is amazing in my opinion. Some bugs here and there but i haven't found a single gamebreaking bug thus far.What you get here, for 35 dollars is equivalent to a souls game in length. It also has high replayability. +Fun combat+Lots of weapons+Decent boss fights+Not a lot boss fights with ads/more than one boss(!!!)+Interesting story/lore+Amazing map design+Loot, LOTS of loot+A ton of hidden/secret areas+Multiplayer that doesn't despawn the other player on death or boss completion (It works great after the patch)+ Amazing, very immersive atmosphere- Some minor bugs here and there- Some of the bosses are a bit easy- Increasing the game actually makes it easier- Magic is overtuned, it is way to strong imo (But using it is optional, obviously)- Some puzzles i hate, i'm looking at you double artillery in Alma MaterOverall you get SO much for such a low price. I can see myself easily getting 100+ hours in this game. And even if you just rush through the game you're going to get a solid 20+ hours out of it. I've paid 60 bucks for less.I think the devs did an absolutely outstanding job with this game and it can only get better from here. I am hoping that this game gets at least one decent sized DLC. And i am looking forward to Hellpoint 2 if that ever happens. This is the best Souls-like i've ever played.

_childDocuments_.review: A middling-bad soulslike. Boss designs range from boring to broken (especially one DLC boss in particular).Still, the plot is unique for a soulslike, and the atmosphere & art are pretty good too. Gameplay is not bad, per se, just nothing to write home about. Exploration is fun, and most levels are laid out to encourage poking around in the nooks and crannies for every last secret (and there are many secrets).Grab it if it's on sale and you're curious, but otherwise hold off on booking your vacation stay on Irid Novo.

_childDocuments_.review: Seems I'm about at the end of this game which makes this a good enough time to leave a review me thinks... Overall I want to say this game is an AWESOME Souls-like experience that succeeds rather well with the ideas it brought to the table.This game is all about exploration and very little hand-holding after it gets you started. Discovering things for myself with little to no guidance is pretty gratifying given how much each area is interestingly woven into itself and other connecting locations. Some locations feel a little dull and visually similar to others at times but that's hardly a problem in this game if you ask me.Combat is smooth and still remains challenging enough for a likely more casual player like myself. Weapon customization is simple but that's fine given the different skills you unlock for each weapon the more you use them. Weapon play is fun and satisfying overall. Enemy placement early on gets a little redundant at times but that changes for the better pretty smoothly as you defeat bosses and progress. Bosses are great too! None rely to much on gimmicks and make for some straight forward, intense, game-play.I have a bit more to discover and do in this game as of this review from what I can tell and I'm looking forward to every bit of it. $35 for this game on release? Pff, you don't need to wait for a sale. Show this game some love and buy it at full price. Every penny is worth it. Every minute is worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: It had some problems and bugs in Co-op at its launch, but must of them were fixed a few days later. I really liked the trist, dark atmosphere (especially the ambient music) and the overall setting of the game as well as the - in its functionality - better made co-op experience compared to Dark Souls. We didn't find all of the hidden things, but it was a fun searching for them as the space station is like a mostly very logical labyrinth of sorts.A little tip for immersion: If you arrive at the hub (you will recognize it) then better take the big elevator down to the Arcology instead of going to Port Issoudun if you managed to find the key. It will be a much better experience lore- and immersion-wise. My friend and myself found out really late that we totally mixed up the whole experience by accident. _childDocuments_.review: Pros:-Interesting story that is fed to you by small snippets you find in the environment.-Fun combat, cool looking weapons and armor.-Interesting enemy and level design (dark souls on a far future space station)Cons-Bad collision, you'll find yourself getting stuck on random things.-Truely terrible platforming, like it's actually the worst part of the game because you have...-Clunky darksouls movement-Fast travel clearly limited for padding purposes.Seriously though, it's a fun soulslike from an indi studio, so give it a try. Unfortunately, fast travel is limited by items with which you can connect the bonfire analogues, which means that there's quite a bit of backtracking on foot. Truly unnecessary amounts of backtracking on foot, there's no reason that you can't have these points connected except to add hours of padding to the game. It should also be mentioned that this is one of the few 3d souls likes that has a jump button, you can in fact jump on command whenever you want. Unfortunately, this actually detracts from the game as there are platforming sections because of this, they are by far the worst and most frustrating parts of this game. Word to the developer if you're reading this, in the future for Hellpoint 2 take out the jump button and put the development time you put into platforming over instant death pits into something else. Over all though, I would recommend it to anybody who loves souls like games. Despite all my criticism this clearly has a lot of love put into it and its a really good game. It just turns out that there's a reason that platforming usually isn't a part of 3d soulslikes.

_childDocuments_.review: It's Dark Souls meets Dead Space. What's not to like?Pros:A true Soulslike - large but tight world with rest points, shortcuts and different path choices, player/equipment upgrading, secret areas, collectibles, interestingly vague story, and unforgiving combat.Great graphics - looks great while keeping very low VRAM usage & GPU temp, with very high FPS on max settings on a GTX 1650 Super. Other developers should look to Cradle Games to learn how to have great graphics without the horribly common sacrifice of performance so many other games have.Probably the only Soulslike that actually plays very with with a keyboard & mouse, despite for some reason the store page strongly recommending a controller.At least 20+ hours for a first playthrough if you like plenty of exploring and uncovering secrets but aren't a completionist.Cons:Movement and combat are sometimes a bit too clunky and actions sometimes don't immediately register, especially with non-default controls.Custom keyboard controls still reset upon exiting the game.Basic graphic options - the game looks and runs great, but it would be nice to have some better or more options.

_childDocuments_.review: Hellpoint is a worthy entry in the soulslike genre - smooth, responsive controls, plenty of interesting mechanics/depth of play, and an awesome, dark scifi atmosphere - it feels like Event Horizon/Dead Space had a lovechild with a souls game. Just a heads up - the game starts fairly simple, but it doesn't take long before interesting gadgets, abilities, crafting and upgrades become available. I mistook pacing for simplicity when I started Hellpoint - that's not the case.Cradle Games has definitely proven they're capable of punching well above their weight with this title - a small developer that can hold its own in a genre dominated by massive developers with big-budget titans like Sekiro and Dark Souls is one to watch, without a doubt. All told, Hellpoint is a distinct, attractively priced Souls experience that's well worth your time if you're a fan of the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, this type of game is rough with reviews... cause depending on when one reviews it the feeling can be completely different. Did you just rage quit cause you felt you got smoked by some mob in an unfair way?  Or did you just down a boss on your first try and are feeling mighty?  Truth be told, if you have either of these feelings chances are its a good souls game.  Cause both will inevitably happen.  I'm not far in but i can honestly say that the controls are tight (though sorta janky... hard to explain) and once you learn to be patient combat is really pretty fluid.  I played the demo and wasn't very impressed, mostly just cause it wasn't a good way to give people a true feel of the game.  Starting out with nothing and growing from level 1 is the only way to learn a souls game.  This also feels far more polished and "finished" (rightfully so) than the demo. Update after 8 hours in. - Still really enjoying my time.  Very pleased so far with the balance of this game.  It's been very hard at times and then also very easy.  The easy parts are nice breathers before the usually difficult but very fun and once learned, simple bosses.  So many satisfying feelings that remind me of the OG dark souls days.  Thanks Devs!Overall i'd give a 8/10 so far.  I certainly want to play more!

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR It is an atmospheric game, but is it a good one?Wot I liked- Dark, gloomy grimdark techno atmosphere - pitch black dark sky with blinking stars and that humongous black hole;- The great maze of a map - there're quite a lot of ways you can explore Irid Novo space station;- Dark music ambience is one of its saving graces; - The story, or what glimpses of it I learned, is pretty fun and reminds of Event Horizon meets Pandorum; - Those black hell whatever hours, eye codes, secret doors & walls reward you (mostly with useless junk) for being on the lookout;- There're some decent monsters out there (zombies, cyborgs, robots, mutants, demons, gods, ETs), just don't expect to meet them right away; - There're even a couple of tough bosses - you just have to look for them;- It's pretty addictive for a short time;- Pummel guys with a stone tp roll or skewer them with a demon poker.Wot I disliked- I very rarely complain about graphics but the game just looks too unimpressive - everything's blurry, contrast is all messed up - you either don't see anything or are blinded by the white shining;- Most mobs (and a good chunk of bosses) have 1-2 attacks, they have no AI to speak of and would quite often get stuck or just plummet to death from some ledge without any encouragement from your side;- Combat, the spine of this whole game, is broken. There's no blocking, no dualwielding, no backstabbing, no stances, no special moves (to speak of). Jumping attack / kick allows you to stunlock most opponents, sometimes even bosses!- The weapons are sameish, the armour is even worse. Spells and ranged options are few in number and lacklustre in performance; - Levelling your character adds little - my level 1 character killed mobs with 2-4 hits of his pipe, my lvl 80+ character killed mobs with 2-4 hits of his stone tp roll. You might say that my opponents grew in strength, but not really. In the first couple of hours of my playthrough I had access to the mobs I was fighting at the end of my playthrough;- There're only 1-2 attack patterns for your weapons. There're more attack animations overall, however its number per category is nothing to be excited about;- Everybody's animation is stiff;- That clock mechanic, while being an interesting twist, forces you to waste too much time waiting for the clock to strike - the devs should've introduced a timeskip mechanic as there's literally nothing to do while you're waiting;- There're few items, what's more - there're even fewer useful unique things which would give game some flavour;- Missing textures pop up quite often; - Shortcuts kept resetting each time I started the game; - Controls in menu and game are different;- Menus are unhelpful and look too small in 1440p;To sum it all up, after playing the game for ¬10 hrs I found that it's bad, then I played it some more 20 hours and found some redeeming features. The combat is bad, however the story is pretty entertaining and the space station of Irid Novo is an interesting locale one wouldn't mind to get lost in for a couple of days. I wouldn't recommend the game, though, due to its current state and the quality of combat.

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't had so much fun exploring a souls-like since Dark Souls. The world seems huge and the level design is just amazing, with secrets within secrets and cryptic stuff tucked into every nook and cranny. When I entered the Observatory, the games main hub, I peered down into the abyss of what I thought was just lod scenery, but no, loot was shimmering down there. Then I looked up at the distant ceiling structure, realizing I could get up there as well. This has defined the whole experience so far - much of what I think is just scenery turns out to be clever level design, reachable, somehow, either by ways of agility or ingenuity.Unlike most souls-likes the game also sports a jump button, that helps take the level design to the next, vertical level. Some jumps can be tricky, but I personally like it tricky, and controls feel just precise and responsive enough to make me feel like it's my own fault for missing a jump.While you've probably seen "cosmic horror on derelict space station" before, it does a good job to set itself apart, both tonally and visually. The writing/story bits are good, leaning more towards interesting obscurantism, than lazy techno babble. The black hole/space station setting is intriguing from the get go and a lot of the cosmic horror enemies are genuinely creepy to a point where I ran past the first many heavy hitters, not due to fear of combat engagement - I was simply intimidated and unnerved by how they looked.I'm still in the somewhat early game, but so far, combat seems fine and bosses are nicely balanced. I've died a couple of times on each, not enough to be frustrating, but just enough to be satisfying when you finally put them down. They don't feel like Nioh/Sekiro-esque skill-gates to slam your head against 40 times to unlock the next wee bit of locales. Some people may not like this, but my aging fingers and affinity towards exploration loves it.Finally, I know a lot of people's experiences differ from my own, but I haven't encountered a single bug so far, no dips in performance and nothing in the world that seemed so bare-bones as to feel unpolished. I could nitpick a few nuisances, like lighting could be a bit better overall, having to move your hand to press "enter", when all other keys lies comfortably within hands reach and maybe most irritatingly, ambient/atmospheric sound is tied to the same mixer as combat sound, so if you want to take combat noise down a notch, you mute the entire thing instead.But those are minor complaints in the grand scheme of things. This is a big, satisfying AA title, made by a tiny indie-sized studio. Technical difficulties aside, Cradle Games should be satisfied and proud of what they've achieved here. Brilliant game.

_childDocuments_.review: Mystifying, cryptic, strange, and I can't have enough of it. Hellpoint is a soulslike which doesn't deviate from the formula. It knows what it is and it doesn't pretend to reinvent the wheel. It's as solid and sturdy as it needs to be, with its own variation to make it feel truly like its own game and not just Dark Souls In Space. Where Hellpoint shines the most is in its lore, in the themes it chooses, the unraveling of the story, the exploration of every nook and cranny of Irid Novo. There's so much going on that -even if the answers were to turn out ridiculous - I still enjoyed the feeling of the mystery, the intrigue and the sensation that we are here just to take notes after the apocalypse and have a chat with [one of the last remaining] god. It's buggy af and it needs some good polish in the multiplayer department though, but so far, we still haven't found anything that stopped us in our march.

_childDocuments_.review: Hellpoint ends up being for Soulslike fans who are just dying for more experiences within the genre, but if that doesn’t describe you, then you’ll be disappointed. The sci-fi nature of the game and its story offering allows it to find its footing right before it ultimately falls apart from its uninspired gameplay. There’s a decent experience to be found during some late-game plot offerings, but that will require you to be invested past the first boss, which is asking a lot.

_childDocuments_.review: While many might describe this game as a "cheaper" Souls-like this game has an immense amount of depth. The combat may not be quite as tight and satisfying as Dark Souls it DOES have an enormous catalog of weapons and armor. These can really change how the game feels and allows you to tailor your experience within to your liking. What this game does have is exploration and a sense of being lost in an alien landscape. There are so many secrets and alternate paths to find I'd be surprised if you ever found them all. Add to that seasonal updates with holiday themed mini-quests there always a reason to return. Made by a small team of developers this game is under near constant improvement. While I had minor hiccups at launch recent updates have dramatically improved my frame rates and stability leading to an incredibly smooth experience. Give this gem a shot, under the surface you'll mind plenty to keep you occupied.

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't reviewed a Steam game in years, but I feel like I need to give this one a nod.To be frank, I expected to buy this and refund it within an hour but something about it truly did grab me. As someone with at least a thousand hours across the Souls series across multiple platforms, I've been extremely disappointed in Soulslike attempts like The Surge and Lords of the Fallen with their odd, floaty combat. Somehow, Hellpoint's weapons feel the more DS1-accurate than any other game I've played to this point.It's far, far from perfect, with glitches and somewhat easy bosses abound, but something about its weapon feel and its sincerity has kept me glued to it. I love the strange story of the station and some of the art on display is top notch. I finished my first place through and immediately started going through NG+  to aim for a few areas I know I missed, and I'm looking forward to spending a lot of time just being summoned to help when the multi comes up.Keep your expectations in check regarding this $35 indie title and you'll really have a neat time. I hope they get the buzz they need to continue supporting it.

_childDocuments_.review: Hellpoint has a fairly unique plot and world for the soulsborne genre. The plot is probably the best part of the game as it's a good mix of science and science fiction. It's closer to Resident Evil in the sense of a dystopian yet semi-believable future. It also focuses heavily on platforming and hidden secrets. Although this may make it unique, it does add a lot of frustration.Where the game suffers most is in the combat. Although the weapon variety in the game is quite good, the enemies do not require anything special thought to kill them. In other games you are required to punish certain attack patterns. Hellpoint doesn't really have this. You can mostly get away with pre-emptively attacking smaller enemies or backstabbing larger enemies.  Once you get past the first two bosses the combat stops being interesting.

_childDocuments_.review: Short Summary: Made by a group of 11(!) people, Hellpoint is a wonderful game, and as someone who played the soulsborne games for thousands upon thousands of hours, I can holeheartedly recommend it to anyone familiar with the genre.PROS:-Probably the most awesome ladders in any game I've ever played.-Fluid and satisfying combat (just like combat in Dark Souls 1, just a bit faster paced)-HUGE interconnected map (just like Dark Souls 1) with an almost endless number of fake walls and hidden things to find and actually good platforming.-Almost perfect difficulty, not too hard and almost never unfair but still can sweat even veterans of the genre (exceptions listed in cons)-Interesting and cool enemy designs with competent AI (although you can still trick NPCs to roll into falls)-Fantastic fashion and extremely varied and cool weapon designs, none of them being terrible for combat. Weapons also get passive and active abilties, all of them different ones, if you use them for a long enough time (not that long).-Very unique game mechanics with the blackhole and the clock which are a bit difficult to understand but once you do it changes your view of the game completely.-Splitscreen and online co-op just like in Dark Souls: summon,invade,duel. (didn't work at release but fully functional now in my experience)CONS:-(MAJOR SPOILER) The bigest fault of this game to me is , which I really hope is not intended because it literally stunlocks the player to death if not dogded perfectly (I had 20 vitality + Deamon Scythe passive health bonus). This to me is the biggest stain on the game's difficulty which is otherwise impressively well done.-Enemy variety is a bit lacking but hey this is still an indie game-There are still some minor bugs and glitches that don't impact the gameplay but still could use some fixing. Most notable bugs at the time of playing: some missing textures/voice lines, enemies sometimes start spining in place when you engage them which is quite funny, killboxes when falling are missing in some places.-Environments can get a dit dull with mostly everything being grayish metal panels but yeah this is still a indie game

_childDocuments_.review: So my first thoughts about this game were good but hesitant. Its a souls-like, set in a sci fi universe with a 'clock' that affects the gameworld. Theres a dedicated jump button and floaty air controls, but its only needed for getting little extra pickups so far. Overall though its a good dark souls vibe on a space station with aggressive health recovery sort of like bloodborne, ie you attack enemies to refill your estus.The more I've played though the more I like this game. There has been obvious work put into this and while there are bugs, i expected that on release for a smaller development team. having been on the discord server for a small while i can say they are very active and bugfixing is getting done quickly.Worth the £20 i put into it, and i know I've only scratched the surface.

_childDocuments_.review: I tried to like this game but ultimately I can't recommend it. The biggest issue is a general lack of polish for a game that's been out as long as it has. The game runs super poorly, apparently on any platform. I had turned off the blood effects because they looked so bad but then had to turn then back on because its sometimes the only visual cue that you are hitting something. The whole disk clock thing in the corner seems to not be explained anywhere and even after reading a guide on it I don't understand the point. The enemy design is OK for the mobs but then the bosses feel very lazy with narrow movesets and just spongy health pools.The hit boxes for you hitting enemies seems fine but hurt boxes from enemy attacks is awful. There were far too many times where the enemy was clearly out of range or their weapon clearly missed me but the game decided I still took damage.This game has an issue i also had with Dark Souls 3 and Eldin Ring where sometimes it queues your inputs, so if you are mashing the heal button during a boss then stop mashing after your heal goes through you will still sometimes healagain because you had previously pressed the button resulting in just wasting your limited heals.This might have just been me but at the end of the year they put a winter aesthetic on the main screen that caused nothing but the snow and xmas lights to display. I couldnt find anyone else complaining about this and it didnt resolve until after the event was over and the game updated again. On the pro side i do like the setting.The future outer space thing all looks neat and is intriguing.I like that what i saw of the story was intriguing and now the tired dark souls thing of being over ambiguous for no good reason.I enjoyed the idea of the crafting system even though I kept getting recipes for which i had no where close to the resources they needed. The areas are large and the low stamina consumption from running was an awesome idea over similar games. This also helps mitigate the common issue with this genre or the unnecessary and annoying "boss run"Movement feels really good for the most part and the ability to dodge cancel helped to make combat feel much faster.I can definitely see the makings of a good game in here but it really needs a once over to fix its issues before i could recommend it to someone. I am sure a hellpoint 2 would be killer

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: Very fun gameplay and immersive atmosphere. As a Soulsborne fan that'll try anything that's compared to the series, this is my favorite non-FromSoft attempt at the genre. Very obviously "inspired" if not "all-but-copied" Dark Souls but in a space station in orbit around a black hole. Combat is tight, music is engaging, visuals are pretty good but I would expect a bit more detail and thought into the environment. Cons: BUGGY AS ♥♥♥♥. I've fallen through the floor. I became invincible to damage. I had NPCs spawn in random places (this could be intended, I guess. I don't know what the NPCs are supposed to do, really.) Ragdoll about 90% when I die. Music just stops sometimes.The mechanic of losing your axions/xp/souls is the same as other games but in Hellpoint there have been several times where I go back to where I died and there is nothing to be found. From a design perspective a lot of things in Hellpoint are kind of ugly to look at. The menus are very uninspired and as nitpicky and pedantic as it may sound, I HATE the font that is used in this game. It looks so out of place and makes me feel like I am on the PS2 or something.Other thoughts: Not sure how I feel about the story. I love cosmic horror and this game has been giving me that feel since the beginning but it is hard at this point to see where anything is going. Overall: If you like Soulsborne games and are okay with playing with a decent amount of bugs, get Hellpoint.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an *excellent* game, I was recommended it by a friend of mineThis brings me back to the Dark Souls trilogy in the best way possible. It is not a pale imitation, these developers took all the right lessons from those games. It's not "hard", it's *unforgiving*.  This is a spiritual sequel in the same way Alien is like the spiritual sequel to the Texas Chainsaw Massacre.I read early reviews. Sadly, games like Cyberpunk 2077 and Bethesda releases get a pass to release a broken game on release, and smaller games like this do not get the same luxury. But regardless, it's been *fixed*. Give it a try, you will not regret it, and it is well worth your purchase, you will get at least as many hours out of this game as you have each of the Souls titles.

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay for the most part is pretty good.  But holy hell are there some despicable design flaws.  Platforming is needlessly difficult and leads to more deaths than any mob.  Sometimes move to jump in one direction and the game just chooses a completely different one.  The ghosts that spawn when you die make already difficult corpse runs even worse, especially since they play by different rules entirely (no stagger, can dodge out of being parried).  The huge window you get staggered into when out of stamina wouldn't be so bad if stamina didn't run out absurdly fast. At several points, I've died while standing still in safe environments just because (no oxygen/cold/heat etc. meters).  Some enemies are invincible for several seconds when you approach them just because.  If you join a multiplayer game before you finish a corpse run, your hard earned souls disappear.  At times it literally feels like this team wants you to hate them, more than any FromSoft game I've played.  "Difficult but fair" this is often not.  "Artificially hard for horribly designed reasons," it is.That said, it's still pretty fun when it isn't being mindlessly horrendous to the player.  It scratches the itch when it plays right.

_childDocuments_.review: Tried it for half an hour. Not getting that time back unfortunately. The fact this is a Dark Souls clone is not an issue. What is an issue is the drab aesthetics ranging from characters to locations (I looked some more up before writing this... later game doesn't seem to improve much). Equally, the controls are pretty floaty and generally unpleasant to play. Equally, the new user experience here is hilariously poor. Moving onto some misplaced expectations on my part. I thought this was a melee or shooting style game and that certainly doesn't seem to be the case. Equally, I would have thought the pc controls would be at least manageable. They were not. Use a pad. It doesn't fix the jank and floatyness, but it makes the game playable. All in all, a resounding "meh". If you want to play something like Dark Souls... replay any of the FromSoftware titles or the Surge or Nioh or any other clone. This ones really only if you have a spare copy lying about and have absolutely no other game to play.

_childDocuments_.review: So far, game seems decent for the price of it. Animations are pretty fluent and enemy movement can be reacted too, most of the times. While it's not much, it definitely has some use.Let me list some bugs i found for now though, maybe devs will find it helpful:- Messing with graphic settings reverts resolution window to default resolution of the screen- Audio of in-game sound effects seem to be way to high by comparison to everything else- I was able to use saves from Thespian Feast, which caused infinite loading screen- Flickering and disappering textures on, for example, banners in room with Sacrifical Dagger- Shield Bash either doesn't work, doesn't have animation or is not what i understand as bashing something with a shieldAlso, a small suggestion: Perfect block/parry should prevent damage on hit from at least small/regular mobs.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:+ Gameplay is fun+ Graphics and art style are nice+ Devs are updating and fixing bugs regularly+ Game is more fun (and easier) with friends in multiplayer+ Ability to change game difficulty up or down on the fly (with required items)+ Interesting storyCons:- I play with a controller and the game will not allow me to remap a button to a LS/RS press, even though actions are already mapped to those buttons- Combat can feel clunky at times- With two people, it is very easy to defeat bosses. Once a player holds aggro and tank the boss, the other person can just go to town with damage and destroy him with little to no worry of getting hurt- Deaths are still glitchy, if the second person dies near a ledge, more often than not the resurrection point is off the ledge, unable to be reached, OR when the person resurrects, they immediately fall off again and die- Fall damage does not make sense at times, falling from the same height at different points causes different damage- There is no ability to respec currently, and as someone new to this game, it's hard to know what build to go for until you've already put in a decent amount of points- Several aspects of the game are never fully explained and hard to understand for a newcomer (black hole hour doors, accretia storms/hordes)- Not necessarily a con, but i would not call it a pro: level design can be EXTREMELY confusing at times. Backtracking or remembering which room you need to go back to can be unforgiving, as a lot of the rooms look similar, or corridors/hallways can be hard to remember maze-like directions. There is an item to combat this, but the pathing power needs to update faster Verdict:+ Fun and interesting take on a souls-like game, better with multiplayer. Learning curve is fairly steep as not everything is explained or given a tutorial for. Worth the money the devs price the game at.

_childDocuments_.review: I tried really hard and waited a long time... but I came to the conclusion that I can't recommend this game even to die-hard souls-like fans. The game was seemingly only made worse over time. Especially the release of the DLC made everything even more janky.The game has a great atmosphere and some interesting monster, weapon and armor designs. The gameplay systems are overall quite nice... if they worked properly.Let's start with clunky combat. Imagine Dark Souls 1 but with clunkier controls and everything is trying to hit you through a wall, will then actually glitch through the wall and then fall through the floor. That is not a rare occasion in this game, something this happens every 15 minutes. That's something I could still deal with even though it is annoying. How about you are in the middle of a boss fight and suddenly can't do anything anymore? Happened to me 3 times in 1 day.The world in the game is okay. It looks good if you don't look too closely. Lots of blurry textures, invisible objects and seemingly random level design at times. Jumping puzzles that will ruin your day due to the clunky movement and terrible collision detection.The game also has some quests. Like kill 10 enemies of a type. Also some well hidden quests that would be quite fun, if they didn't constantly bug out. I just wasted 3 hours on one of those hidden quests because enemies fell through the floor or it was just impossible to complete for no reason.A word on the balancing: It's terrible. Really terrible. I can see why so many people quit in the first few minutes of the game. And I'm not talking about the tutorial boss itself. It's not that difficult if you are accustomed to souls-like combat, but enemies mixed in that will kill you instantly on level 1 and a 5 minute walk to go back to where you died because you tried to explore. This is not just in the beginning of the game. Especially in the DLC there are enemies that will randomly one-shot you. There are bosses that are insanely weak and other bosses that are complete damage sponges and require specific items to be able to stay alive long enough.But hey at least the game never crashed for me. I'm not even sure if I will ever 100% this... it's just so exhausting to play when you get so many bugs and such annoying gameplay.
