_childDocuments_.review: In short, great formula and some interesting ideas buried underneath a ton of minor issues and probably a lack of budget to flesh them out. Personally I had fun at start, mid game I was annoyed by technical issues and backtracking, by the end I just wanted it to end ASAP.ALTHOUGH, If you are looking for sci-fi soulslike on a spooky space station just to have some fun for a few hours then go for it if you can get it for cheap somewhere.If minor issues like stuttering, falling out of bounds sometimes, npc escort that sometimes buging out, audio not playing or cutting out sometimes or ragdoll on death being broken irritate you then stay far away. This game is very rough around the edges and I mean very.PROS:- setting and atmosphere- plenty of weapons and armors + weapon leveling unlocking new perks for it- many secrets to discover- enemy design and boss design (but not true final boss)- the "clock" which is a fun concept on paper, it introduces some variety passively (black hour, demon spawns)- cosmic gods take over mechanic, if you kill one of them his minions get replaced with the other god's minions, fun idea but could be fleshed out more- 3 bosses can give you quests, this was a fun and unexpected discovery- mirror world, a great idea (timer sucks tho)- easy to change difficulty, the effigies are a nice idea. game is too easy, pop some daring effigies, it's too hard - fearful ones. Very user friendly difficulty system (you have to find those tho and be careful to not overdo it)CONS:- too much f***ing platforming, really, and it is not fun platforming like in an action game, your only tool for platforming is a jump and that's it. If you jump during a sprint tho the character does a stutter step forward which mostly kills you. Easily 70% of my deaths in this game were fall damage or instant death pits.- the "clock" and locked black hole doors, who thought waiting for this garbage would be fun? do devs like wasting people's time? full cycle of that clock is like what 2h? terrible idea- if you want to go for 100% achievements be aware that one of those is locked behind a controller or twitch integration + coin collector does not carry over to ng+ and you will have to start all over again with the whole 66 coins set (there is a tram section that can f**k you over and block a coin for a playthrough)- tons and tons of small issues, stuttering in many spots (mostly when looking in the direction along the location's length), falling out of bounds when doing special moves, audio cutting, stuttering or not playing sometimes, ragdoll is broken because apparently some cretins found it funny and now it is a feature, getting blocked by seemingly nothing sometimes (esp. on the pyramid), some elements of some armor sets disappear when you look at them at certain angles, npc can get stuck on some wires during escort (and btw his questline might just reset like out of nowhere) etc. As I said before, VERY rough around the edges.- Only 5 bosses (3 gods, 1 robot and 1 true final boss), all other bosses are literally just big versions of common demons walking around the station, same movesets, same look, just bigger.- Enemy variety is on the low side,- It is a worse maze than The Surge 1- Station is big but that means there is a lot of empty space and you will have to walk and backtrack a lot because...- bonfires (breaches) are not connected to fast travel system and the items you need to connect them to fast travel system are limited and usually well hidden so better look up which ones are crucial and activate those first,- elevators are too damn slow, like really, why? there is a lot of elevators in this game and it is a pain to take them- environments are kind of the same which makes remembering the way harder- no real voiceacting which is even worse then they say the same gibberish line multiple times in a row + kind of boring NPCs and quests,

_childDocuments_.review: Recommend to developers: fix gameRecommend to players: Play at your own risk, 35$USDAs of 2020/08/12 this game should be in early access. It has been released for a couple weeks, and it feels...so broken. I've played mostly co-op with a friend and we have experienced numerous, persistent bugs. I'll list some below:When I host and he joins:-We can play for some amount of time with frequent problems.-Enemies respawn "invisible" to him. They can hurt him, but he can't see them.-Enemies can't be damaged by him. They appear to take damage to him, but they don't take damage in reality (my server).When he hosts and I join:-I randomly disconnect.-Damage I do is "laggy", meaning they appear to take damage from me, but he always has to finish them off, or they appear to me to die and don't.Hardware:-Both our computers are fairly good, ryzen 5 3600, xmp enabled, 2070 Super (overkill for this game), NVME drives (blazing fast)-Both our connections are 100meg+-We play many games on Steam, Epic Store, Xbox live together, seamlessly.To put this in perspective: I have had Satisfactory Early Access, for a period of time, never experienced issues like this. This game is extremely buggy, to a fault, and frustrating to play online. We have played tons of Dark Souls 3 online, Division 2 online, the list goes on. Hellpoint is very broken, and should not have been released, because it isn't finished.I appreciate that the developers update this game regularly, but it is not nearly finished. The broken co-op is the most frustrating, because we were looking for a new "souls-experience" to enjoy together. We've both beaten DS3 numerous times on Xbox and on our new, beefy PC's. We are huge DS fans and wanted a new game to scratch that itch...this is not it, unless you love encountering hours of bugs, and chatting in discord while reloading. Maybe the game works better in single player. I don't really care, because when a game ships with co-op, I expect it to work. As a stand-alone single player game, it's probably more playable. If I have the time to check it out more in sp, I might. It's more on the Bloodborne-end of the DS series, but it lacks the polish and perfect-parry timing that that game (and ds3) embedded). If you're going to buy and play it: ranged combat is necessary. Use guns or magic, and use them frequently. The game builds your "magic" meter back by hitting w/ melee, so you absolutely want gun-play or magic. Otherwise, you'll spend a lot of time whacking away at enemies that can attack with their own ranged abilities. I'm not saying you shouldn't buy it ever. However, you definitely shouldn't pay $35USD for a game that doesn't work as it is described, and is fatally flawed in one of its best playstyles: co-op. Oh, and before the "git-gud" crowd arrives: yes, I love a challenge. I beat ds1r and ds3 numerous times without co-op help. However, I also helped my friends beat it, and they joined in on my many successive runs for new builds and boss runs. We were looking to play the game as advertised, with co-op. I don't mind extra enemies and enemy respawns to crank up the difficulty -- but it doesn't really matter if they're invisible, or you disconnect. FIX IT.I'll update if the game is fixed.

_childDocuments_.review: 4.1/5 :  Amazingly robust 3D world, FPS.  More Z (vertical) in each zone than any game I've played before and I've played a lot.  We played entirely on macos 14.  Ran fast and clean most of the time, but had to restart after 3d errors cropped up after hours of play. If we'd judged it based on the first few hours of play, it would have been a thumb's down. There's something deeply wrong with the balance in the first zone.  The opening is fine, the tutorial method (green hands on the walls) is good, but the first zone boss is impossible to beat without a LOT of grinding and the first zone is too small.  I played it side by side with my partner (each on our own machines) and we would literally just stand waiting for the MOBs to replot. It was super tedious. We almost quit several times.   Also, the inventory system is a disaster. It is way, way too easy to accidentally destroy unique items and there's too much garbage not to 'disassemble' things consrtantly or the inventory becomes overwhelmed.    One can replace unique items if one has  a friend with the game. Player1 creates a new character, which re-generates the universe, then the player  (Player2) missing the item connects to player1's "match", runs through the world to get to the item, picks it up, both players in that universe get the item, then Player2 disconnects and can go back to playing their own universe with the item.   Without that, it seems impossible to finish the game if one accidentally destroys the wrong item.Also, I accidentally killed a key character and there was no way to recover from that. I have read it's possible to finish the game, so I'll continue through, but it's an example of some of the flaws with the game.But for a very strong 3D run-around, detailed, hack and slash with big distant graphics and amazing vistas, Hellpoint is fun.  I was re-reminded how strong the human vertigo and dizziness at heights .  Uncontrollable yelps as one unexpectedly comes up to a 500 foot drop. The game isn't perfect and there should be more story, but it's fun to play co-op.  For those, like us, who strongly prefer desktop games, Hellpoint is very strongly designed around controller play and there are a lot of controller-type special fight actions using quick key combos. Takes a long time to learn them and each weapon is unique in some way. I broke my alt / windows key on my keyboard bashing it to pop my shield up.  oops.We haven't finished it yet, but we've been to every major zone and are now tying up loose ends as we kill each of the top bosses.  There's still grinding, but it's fun to get tough enough to be able to beat the impossible bad guys from the early part of  the game. The in-game mechanism to increase and decrease difficulty is interesting, I'd not seen it before. I wish it were slightly more granular: changing to a more dangerous universe changes the difficulty A LOT. MOBs go from easy to almost impossible.  I'd rather the jumps up and down in difficulty were 50-60% as big as they are in Hellpoint.Definitely recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: (tl;dr version)This game is legit. It gets a lot more right than it gets wrong. This is your sci-fi Souls that you've wanted all along.---(Longer version)You know how a lot of Souls-likes try, but ultimately kind of fail at really capturing that "Souls" feel? Usually due to overly janky and/or unsatisfying combat, milquetoast level design, tepid atmosphere... there's always something that's missing, that makes you think "yeah, no, this just doesn't cut it". Hellpoint... is on point. Despite being crowdfunded project made by an experienced, but small, indie team, and not a high-budget endeavour, it gets a lot more things right than it gets wrong, and is overall on of the better Souls-likes I've played.But, naturally, being a budget game and all, it does have a fair bit of jank, I can't lie. So let's start with that and get it out of the way:- Jumping feels clunky at times, and a missed jump usually means certain death, which can be frustrating. I would say that easily 80% or more of my deaths have been through falls. Some of them were my fault, but some of them were, IMO, annoying camera or clunky jumping mechanics. The upside is that the more annoying platforming parts are completely optional.- It has a number of small bugs that can be annoying, though not game-breaking fortunately. - The UI, especially to manage inventory, is not great. There is no "storage" option to stash away gear, making equipment clutter a real problem especially in NG+ and onwards.- Some mechanics are poorly explained. I didn't realize I could upgrade weapons further until someone in their Discord pointed it out to me, for instance... eep. 😅- Enemy variety could be better.So, what's GOOD about it? Well, quite a lot:+ Level design. This is the strongest aspect. I was surprised to see a few reviews panning this aspect. The world itself is fully interconnected like Dark Souls 1 (though some areas are still separated by loading screens). Individual levels vary in quality, but some of them are completely bananas... in a good way. Loaded with verticality, secrets, looping shortcuts and all that good stuff.Arisen Dominion, for example, is a huge, huge maze-like area, full of verticality and filled with secrets to find. Some of those secrets I found in NG++ despite thinking I had already explored the whole place thoroughly already. And just when you think you explored a huge chunk, it just keeps going until you get completely lost, which can be daunting as you carry all those axions (equivalent of "souls"), and then you end up looping back to a familiar place and go "ahhh, this place again!" with that familiar sense of relief.+ Fast-travel is limited; "breaches" act as the "bonfires" somewhat, but outside of a few specific ones, you need to use a semi-rare consumable item to make it "warpable", so you sometimes have to really decide if you keep going or backtrack and retreat to a safer area. It's also interesting that resting at the Breach  respawn enemies (nor does it refill your Healing; more on this later), so sometimes you can just retreat there to refill your health. (Yes, turns out you  need to copy bonfires and Estus to make a Souls-like, who knew? /s)+ Atmosphere. The game is set in a hellish, derelict space station set in the far future, with the dark occult sci-fi mood reminiscing of Event Horizon and Dead Space. There's a lot of really cool futuristic space vistas and impressive brutalist and alien architecture, with lots of suffocatingly dark and creepy areas making you rely on your Omnicube Light tool to navigate.+ Combat is pretty tight. Controls are responsive, the dodge is generous (similar to Bloodborne, it's a side-step when locked on), there's a decent variety of weapons and builds, some weapons have really cool and satisfying abilities. I played a Reflex (dex) / Cognition build, which focuses on faster weapons and a firearm as ranged support, and it worked well for me. In NG+ I experimented with "Foresight" abilities (basically magic), and found them fun and quite powerful.+ Build variety and depth. There's lots of options and possible combinations in there. I barely scratched the surface, honestly.+ Secrets. Soooo many secrets. Exploration is very rewarding in this regard. But hell, if you enjoy the obtuse Dark Souls secrets, you'll be spoiled by Hellpoint there. Some doors only open when mysterious conditions are met (and good luck figuring all of them out on your own xD). I even missed the "true" final boss because of one secret I missed and had to try again in NG+.+ Cool unique mechanics. For example, the Accretion Storms and "Black Hole Hour". The game has an internal "clock" in the top left corner, showing the station's current position in the orbit of a.... black hole. :D Depending on its current position, sometimes, special events happen, spawning enemies in places where there wouldn't be (such as during Accretion Storms), or unlocking chambers that are otherwise locked. Another cool mechanic is how you refill your Mana bar and your Healing items by attacking enemies (how much gets refilled depends on your Leech stat). I wasn't sure about this Healing mechanic at first, but it grew on me as I played more. You can find weapons that have extremely good Leech properties, so for example you can have a loadout that focuses on guns or magic and melee attacks are mostly support for refilling your mana.Honestly, if you crave a sci-fi Souls, I think this is the best you're going to get at the moment. The Surge didn't do it for me, but this one ticked the boxes.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; Bit low budget souls like that has some great unique ideas and does enough things really well to be worth a look. I don't think it is going to change anyone's mind on the genre but it is a very good one if you want more souls and are ok with a little jank. Very fluid combat system with many tools at your disposal. There is dodging, running, light/heavy, mid-air light/heavy along with special abilities that cost mana. Combos often carry progress between light / heavy attack chains so you can go light attack -> second hit of the heavy attack chain. Many special abilities are attacks you can use even without stamina as long as you have the mana to spend. You always have a lot of options available to you at any given time and it just feels good to hit things. Also rather than backstab attacks being big lock-in animations you just do significantly more damage to enemies backs. This encourages aggressive forward dodges with high damage but doesn't give you any invincibility frames for the attack. There also is a nice variety of daggers, swords, staffs, magic catalysts guns etc.  A key part of what made this work so well is mana and healing items recharge on melee damage. This means that you do not have to really save your powerful attacks. While it hurts to miss these moves it doesn't feel like you are screwed if you are out of mana without a nearby resting spot. This also lets you expend all of your mana on say ranged shots to kill a problem enemy without feeling busted as restricted until you get more melee in. Healing items being recovered on melee damage also is great as it lets you keep exploring as long as you don't take too many hit in a row. It also has a nice ebb and flow where you can play aggressively when when at healing cap or more methodical if running out. Frankly I hope future souls like games take this idea it just works so well. weapon upgrades are tied to an item which you slot into weapons. These change the stat scaling on weapons and provide a stat boost. They can be transferred somewhat freely (at the firelink equivalent main area) so if you find a cool new weapon to try it can be upgraded very quickly. Also as you use a weapon you unlock new passive and active abilities. These include things like lower weight, different firing modes for guns, ranged attacks for melee weapon etc.   Enemies have sweep attacks you can jump over and levels are designed with a lot of verticality and interesting platforming required. This is reflected in the level design and is just a nice feature.  the areas in this game are choked full of secrets. There are constantly hidden doors, items over gaps, secret elevators etc. The game constantly taunts you with items just out of reach encouraging exploration to find these hidden areas. The levels are also often have multiple paths through them, interesting shortcuts and are visually pretty cool. One of my early game favourites is a city district; as you enter the area you see an overhead view of tightly packed buildings before having to descend into the city streets fighting through narrow narrow alleyways full of ambushes. You eventually can climb through and jump in between buildings. So many levels are just really fun to explore and I think they nailed a lot of them. You also often have multiple accessible at any given time so if you are a bit stuck of feel under powered can go try somewhere else. There are many places in this game where you can feel that this is not an AAA game. Many regular enemies in the game are fought as bosses, you will find duplicate weapons and armour sets or weapons functionally the same with a different element, some of the animations are a little wonky, etc. Finding hidden paths and secret areas is a really fun process but it is a bit of a let down finding a duplicate. I also think the enemy variety issue was a bit exasperated by a design choice as well. As you progress through the game enemies are replaced with harder ones. While a neat idea, it meant the last few hours I spent secret hunting I fought a lot of the same enemies repeatedly. Perhaps instead they could've gone with some random replacement to add unpredictability to play into the horror theme a bit while keeping variety up.  I ran into a few bad ones including: unable to use or change left hand weapon until returning to main menu and rejoining, an NPC who`s dialogue indicated we`d already met on first time meeting him, an NPC`s quest progress reset to an earlier stage and steps had to be re-completed, a hard progression lock preventing going to a particular area. Props to the dev they have been very good about quickly fixing the worst of these which would break save files; my particular progression issue was fixed within a day but the game has some rough edges. There are some more minor things like getting caught on terrain and needing to jump out.A very good albeit a little rough souls-like with absolutely stellar level design, great sci-fi horror theme, and fast varied combat. I liked this game a whole lot and will be keeping track of what the dev puts out in the future for sure. The big stand out for me was just how great the level design was; I loved exploring these areas trying to find all of the secrets. This game has a lengthy demo so would recommend just giving it a shot. It has some unique areas not present in the final game version of the level + has split screen co-op. I hadn't heard about the game before trying the demo in the steam demo festival a couple of months ago and I'm glad I tried it

_childDocuments_.review: Glome here--This is my new favorite indie Soulslike. It channels the spirit of Dark Souls particularly well; the real meat of Hellpoint is in the atmosphere and exploration. The combat is solid and fun as well -- I especially enjoyed the weapon familiarity system which definitely added a lot of depth to the combat in the later game. Ultimately, it's the presentation of the game that really hooked me. Irid Novo is a bleak and beautiful place, and a totally original one as well. You can get lost very easily in the labyrinthine levels but I loved this. This game is a dream come true for completionists and secret hunters. HIGHLY recommended for any and all Souls fans. 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: For the love of us all, PLEASE FIX THE PLATFORMING.If you're going to have a jump mechanic, make it work.Especially when it comes to invisible platforms (using an in-game item, you can see invisible platforms).Two instances:At one point, I was jumping from invisible tree to invisible tree. These trees are not like the rest that have a flat platform on top. No sir. These trees are insanely easy to fall off of because you have seemingly less surface area to work with, coupled with only being able to see in a flashlight-shape cone in front of you. And of course, the trees are high enough in the air and inconveniently placed enough that whether or not you die from the fall, you have to trek back to them repeatedly. It took more attempts than was fun/interesting. I succeeded, but it sucked.Now the worst offender.At a certain point in the game, you'll find yourself in a decent-sized room, being shot at with giant blasts from two mechs on either side of said room, high above where you seemingly cannot reach them. Well, SPOILER, you can. You run through the room, dodging blasts, as you make your way to one side, where, after a couple jumps, you'll find a "ladder" to climb up to one of the mechs. You need to kill this mech, all the while being shot at by the other mech on the other side of the room. It takes more than a few hits. There are then invisible platforms to jump across while being shot at by the mech across the way. Of course, the platforms are high enough in the air that if you fall, maybe you'll just lose some hp, but it's also very possible you'll die. I've found that performing a dive attack sometimes negates/minimizes fall damage, but it's frustratingly inconsistent.Here's the issue. Not only are you being shot at, but jumping is WILDLY INCONSISTENT. You may RUN and jump, and overshoot. You may WALK and jump, and undershoot. If you get hit by a blast, you may fall, and if not, you'll LITERALLY be pushed to the far right edge of the platform. And I don't mean you'll be pushed when you're hit, I mean AFTER. You'll get hit, start to move, and your character will MAGICALLY warp to the right side of the platform, which just adds to this inconsistent mess and mentally throws you off further. Add to this a brief pause when changing your character's direction from standing still after sprint-jumping (which is an annoying issue on its own), and it is seriously nearly impossible. I've seen a player message on the wall across the way, so at least one person suffered and conquered this rage-inducing jank. Just imagine doing this over and over and over and over and over and over and over and over. Death after death to literally BROKEN MECHANICS.Even if, for this situation, there is a way to kill the mech that shoots homing blasts while you attempt traversing the invisible platforms (like with a ranged weapon I'm not spec'd into), or items in the game I'm unaware of that decrease aggro range or lower/nullify fall damage, the fact remains the platforming is overall atrocious.There are things to enjoy about Hellpoint, and I applaud the effort that was obviously put into this game. The Souls series includes my favorite games of all time, and I'm not referring to a "git gud" situation. An integral game mechanic is broken. It needs attention. I cannot recommend Hellpoint to anyone until the platforming/jumping is fixed.Perhaps allowing us more mid-air control of our character would be a helpful step to a resolution? I don't know; I'm just spitballing.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is good, very good, but with some caveats and much room for improvement. Don't get me wrong, this game is a jewel as it is (although still a bit rough around the edges) and should be played by souls-like fans and "not-so-casual" gamers alike. Casual gamers... beware, thread carefully. Difficulty is never "easy" but it is significantly harder in the first parts of the game, and is reasonably "lightly-hard" for the rest of the game. The setting and world are intriguing, the narration is minimal but it gives some clues to the whereabouts of the story. Overall is really a mix of Dead Space with a sprinkle of Doom, presented in a souls-like fashion, and it works very well. The combat is solid and is very open to experimentation with different weapons and styles. The ability to also mix ranged weapons in a hand and a melee weapon or shield in the other is cool, although the usefulness of ranged weapons is limited. The weapons themselves are good, different from each other and allowing you to improve them with either mods or level-ups that add some passive or 2 active abilities (usually powerful and very impactful), so you are always tempted to try out new weapons. Visuals are also very good, and a lot of work as clearly been poured into the creation of this world. I played most of it in split-screen coop without any major issues (mostly some sporadic camera issues, the bosses that don't handle the second player well, and some quirks with the second player management of xp rewards after boss fights), which is pretty cool. There are some negatives, though: as of today, there are still some bugs to fix (but the team is working on it, with daily updates). Furthermore, there are some things that I hope will be addressed so that I can enjoy more the NG+: falling is maybe the greatest threat, because it kills you on the spot, sometimes you don't even see it coming and other times you have to do some jumps for which the control system is really not well suited. I hope that they choose to make you lose some health and respawn on the ledge when you fall, like in other games like this, and maybe improve the precision of the jumping mechanics. Another gripe is with the area maps: they are huge, with very big halls and very long corridors, but most of the times those are just empty, although nice to look at. When the "awe" settles off, you remain with the boredom of having to run through vast distances. To make things worse, maps are extremely intricated and lacking landmarks, so exploration is both time consuming and confusing, at times. On occasion, there is also a certain lack of direction, although I never truly felt "lost" because I kept track of things left to do. I think that a good 3D map system could fix this very easily (or at least in a much easier way than to modify the maps themselves, shortening corridors and so on) and allow players to actually enjoy and take advantage of such complexity. I know that this is not very "souls like", but I think it will be for the better and, in the end... who cares, this game is unique in its own way. Also, boss fights (mainly ) need some more work, they are either too easy or difficult for the wrong, unfair reasons. Another thing: many of the details told/shown around in the world could have been exploited/expanded more throughout the narration, but maybe I missed something (although I explored a lot). And please, allow us to respec in some way and to disable the other players marks from showing in the world. It may seem that there are as many negatives as positives, but they just pop out as the little stains on a white shirt: they are not so bad, overall, but they spoil the experience to some extent. All in all, though, the experience is very positive and the game is very recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay-wise, it's great. Relatively forgiving for a "Souls-like", with the option to increase difficulty at any time. The layout design is phenomenal. Environments are interesting and different enough where you won't get lost... and there are enough secret pathways to make backtracking much less cumbersome and boring. I really only have 2 complaints, and they are *very* minor ones. 1) There is a certain... lack... of variety when it comes to creature design. This becomes even more apparent when you run into your first boss... who then re-appears as a regular (A.K.A less threatening) enemy later in the game. 2) The story was a bit lacking as well. I get that a lot of it was meant for the player to figure out... but it all felt a little too disjointed. I don't know, it's a little hard to explain. With something like Dark Souls, you felt like you were dropped into this new world. It felt mysterious and wondrous. But the world of Hellpoint is... nothing but a puzzle. A problem that needs to be solved. It doesn't feel lived-in, if that makes sense. Still, I've had a great time with it so far!

_childDocuments_.review: I would recommend this game for anyone looking to scratch the souls itch.  There are some differences, but a solid game overall.  The scifi atmosphere and gear are a welcome change.  The healing mechanics are a little different and I absolutely LOVE IT!  You can carry more than three injectors to heal yourself, but only three are refilled upon dying.  Weapons have a Leech stat which is used to refill those extra injectors, so you have to inflict damage to get more injectors.  Not a groundbreaking idea, but it's well implemented here.  Overall, worth the money.  My favorite part was finding the Prying Tool.

_childDocuments_.review: This really is Indie-Souls in space!The game is not perfect, it's clunky and not very impressive in terms of graphics fidelity but they more than make up for it with stellar art direction and level design.The atmosphere is eerie, alien and creepy. From the very first moments you feel lost and it's up to you to travel through the massive space station on your own, with multiple possible paths, having only your thirst for finding out what happened there to push you forward.There's no annoinyg cutscenes or npcs with quests. You interact with the story at your own pace by reading texts and conversations left by the former inhabitants of the station. It's up to you to make sense of it all. I love it!To me this game perfectly captures the spirit of original Dark Souls, letting you loose in the intricatly built alien world and letting you make sense of it.

_childDocuments_.review: There is fun to be had in this game but it suffers a lot of issues.These range from bugs where you insta die randomly just walking along, bits of terrain being missing or black hole doors not opening when they should to npcs dying which breaks your progress in a quest.The weapons are also massively unbalanced and most of them are crap. They have a gimmick of a timer that triggers certain events at certain times but some of these are bugged and tbh they dont really add much to the game.The area layout isnt great for each map and can be pretty confusing sometimes. Also fall damage seems pretty random i can make a jump and take no damage my friend can make the exact same jump and instantly die forcing a return to checkpoint.Weapon variety is also pretty slim most weapons use the same animations and if they have extra abilities these will likely occur on other weapons of the same type. The magic is basically the same thing repeated for each element and tbh only 1 of them is really useful. Guns are the same with not much variation and only one of them i found useful, they also tend to be outclassed by the magic staff.The game on the whole is really easy and pretty short, thats even including the fact i accidentally did the game on ng+ difficulty from the start and skipped the early game areas and went straight to the later areas. The lack of difficulty doesn't even come from damage or hp which increases via ng+ it comes from the enemy ai being laughable and even worse when you add additional players as it just outright ignores them even if the host isn't around. Most of the deaths i've had that weren't falls or bugs were from me being trapped in terrain and wailed on or when the difficulty was to the point i could be one shot and a particular enemy would pull out a cheap glitchy move.I don't know why the devs decided to add pvp multiplayer before they got round to fixing the bugs that are in the game personally i would of preferred a less buggy experience to being able to fight pvp.Overall you can still get fun out of it but at the current price point it seems pretty steep for what you get and how buggy it is. I'd wait till it drops below £10 if i were you.

Being made out of inspiration from Dark Souls, you'd think there would be a copy of it with little deviance required in plot or anything else from the tone and atmosphere, but this game is a wholly unique experience, and it owns it. _childDocuments_.review: I have many good things to say about the game - but to truly recommend it I have to note a few negative aspects.For my personal tastes - the levels are too big and the enemies are too few and too often re-used. Huge levels - because they are soo huge - they become bland. There is a ok amount of memorable areas - but they are drowned by the same old corridors/etc. The levels themselves don't have a great deal of actual function/distinction.Enemies - too bland for the most part in terms of their attacks and strategy needed, or maybe just too easy for me to mostly attack spam them. The enemy visual design for the most part is good/great.-- Here's the good - energy/"health potion" recharging due to melee attacks. Weapons leveling up to reveal new abilities. These to me are highlights of the game.In addition the armor sets are cool and the bosses have a really neat visual design.--Basically it's a good attempt at making their own version of Dark Souls without the Dark Soul's teams budget/skills, so very commendable and I hope that there is a Hellpoint 2 for me to buy.

_childDocuments_.review: It's very reminiscent of Dark Souls 1 - hits the same vibes of wonder and exploration. The level design is very good, with tons of secrets and looping corridors - the only downsides are that the areas do not transition seamlessly (loading screens), and maybe that it's not landmark-oriented which makes it very hard to predict where certain paths will take you. Though the sci-fi horror setting kind of necessitates this type of a claustrofobic design. There's also lots of very good ambience and stunning art direction. There's a system which you could call 'dynamic weather' which influences the game world (enemies, open locations etc.). The game is just as enigmatic with its lore as DS, maybe even more so. It's all interesting, and the setting really sells it. Overall, if the above things are what you are looking for in your Soulslike games, do not hesitate and play it already.This game can get janky at times but I wouldn't say it's much jankier than the first DS was. Combat is fun, with a pretty basic but sound souls core, and with some welcome twists (like ranged weapons actually belonging in your rotation). There's crafting and a good amount of equipment to use. The default difficulty is ok for me so far, and there's also a system similar to the bonfire ascetics in DS2 if you need a greater or lesser challenge.So far I'm very impressed. I would totally recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: A kinda janky and weird but nevertheless deep and enjoyable sci-fi ARPG/Soulslike. Strong on exploration, lore, and mystery, but weak on combat, build diversity and polish.I certainly did have a lot of issues throughout the game: in particular, I don't recommend you come to this game for combat as both the enemy/boss design and weapon build variety is a bit lackluster. For enemy design, it didn't take long for the game to start recycling normal enemies for boss encounters which really let me down, and most enemies were either just too boring or too annoying to deal with. For builds, while technically there are a lot of weapon choices, they are highly unbalanced with tons of trash choices: for example, I highly recommend avoiding heavy slow str weapons as I found them to be absolutely terrible with neither the damage, stagger or ability to make up for the slowness of their animations. There were also plenty of weird glitches and physics oddities for jumping and movement, as well as systems that were not explained well that really made it rough to get used to.But where I think Hellpoint stands strong is the world and how interesting it is to explore. Unlike a lot of other games, I found this surprisingly easy to build a mental map for as the game was good in building diverse environments with lots of unique structures and such to use as landmarks. Also there are tons of secrets to be found, both in terms of lore, characters and quests, as well as treasures hidden in nooks and crannies and hidden paths. It ain't perfect: I certainly wish someone would turn the damn lights on since so many of these maps are so dark, and there were some instances of blank/recycled rooms and assets. But overall, I found myself enjoying myself when it came to exploring every new area I came across since the game does such a good job of having so much to see and find.Having said all that, I still have a big grudge with this game, and how it screwed me out of an ending and boss fight because I didn't talk with some dude locked in a cage off in the corner where no one in the right mind could even notice he was there in the first place. The nerve! The temerity!

_childDocuments_.review: Hellpoint is the best souls-like game I think I've ever played, and I have played many, as I am a true Dark Souls fanatic. I believe this game is definitely a worthy purchase for a die-hard fan of the souls genre. However, if you are not familiar with Dark Souls, this would be a pretty rough introduction to this type of game. In short, it feels very faithful to Dark Souls yet brings a lot of creative new ideas to the table. On the flip-side, I am writing this review over a month after the game's release - and although a lot of the bugs that were present on day one have been resolved, the game still feels rough.___________________________________________________CONS:-The controls are quite sticky and sometimes feel downright unresponsive. This, combined with the necessity of jumping and platforming to progress through the game, creates a pretty aggravating experience. I love the platforming aspect of the game personally. It seems that the developers are having a technical challenge in getting something that works as a hack-and-slash action rpg, but also a sort of Banjo-Kazooie-style exploration platformer.-There are some frustrating quirks with the combat mechanics. On my second play-through, I decided to go with a foresight (magic/caster) build. If you hit the cast button during a casting animation, it will cause a second cast to be queued. "Queued actions" are very counter-productive in action-rpgs, where split second changes to your tactics often need to be made.-Early game feels quite dull, especially for a first play-through. When you create a character, there are no starting classes, which are one of the cornerstones of Dark Souls games, and really RPGs in general. Starting classes in this context are a mechanic that distributes your beginning attributes in different ways and typically determine what your starting weapons are. In Hellpoint, your character will start with all attributes at the lowest value of 1, and because of this, many of your early levels need to be dumped into health and stamina stats to keep you combat-ready with a melee weapon since there are no guns or catalysts to be found in the first few zones, so I imagine a majority of players would opt to start focusing on a melee-build out of necessity.___________________________________________________PROS:-The small team that created this game are Dark Souls lovers and I can feel it when I play this game. The attention to detail in story elements, gameplay elements, level and sound design, all resemble Hidetaka Miyazaki's desire to make an amazing gaming experience. I really feel the spirit of a souls game when I find myself wandering around a gigantic space station, where something cataclysmic and undeniably mysterious has obviously happened right before I got there. I find myself wandering through mazes of dangerous enemies only to find a shortcut that brings me back to familiar ground, or sometimes a path that will lead to a zone that I haven't seen in hours. I can feel my heart beating out of my chest when I'm sprinting from a horde of space hollows, trying to get back to my space bonfire so I don't lose my space souls because I've run out of space estus.-I love the addition of weapon "experience". As you kill more enemies with a weapon, more "experience" will be gained on the weapon. Once it reaches certain thresholds, different abilities and boosts are unlocked for that particular weapon, often with the final ones being the most potent. This is a mechanic that I believe accommodates players who like to try a lot of different weapons but also players who like to stick with one or a few "ol' faithful" weapons. -Another excellent new innovation is the weapon upgrade system. In Dark Souls, sparse and hard-to-find upgrade materials are scattered throughout the world and must be collected and then spent en masse along with souls to increase the damage of weapons. In Hellpoint, the only resource needed to upgrade a weapon is an enhancement chip that can be attached your weapon of choice. Once the chip is attached, you need only spend your souls currency (axions) in order to unlock higher tiers of the chip, which will in turn increase the damage of the weapon. There are different types of chips for different types of weapons, and some melee chips have additional augmentations that affect your attack properties. The most wonderful feature about he chips is the fact that they can be detached and reattached to other weapons at your leisure. This is amazing, once again, for putting an interesting new spin on an old Dark Souls convention.-Multiplayer has been streamlined for a much simpler co-op experience. I personally am very thankful that in Hellpoint, co-op and pvp are finally separate entities, and don't need to necessarily go hand-in-hand. You can join a friends game, and stay joined, no matter who dies or whether the boss has been killed. Another great aspect of multiplayer is that there is very little messing about with soapstone items, or soul memory, or any other tedious mechanics that get in the way of jolly co-operation. You simply have an 8-digit multiplayer code for your session. Your friend can join your world just by inputting your code._________________________________________________If you are a fan of Dark Souls, this game will definitely scratch your itch. If you have never played Dark Souls, play Dark Souls right now, and then play Dark Souls II, and then Dark Souls III. Then once you have become hopelessly addicted to Dark Souls, you can find a lot of hours to sink into this charming little space souls.

_childDocuments_.review: Really exceptionally well-done for this studio's first foray into the world of games!Action RPG in the Soulslike box, really interesting designs, fun and enjoyable weapons with a knowledge system for each weapon that really adds a lot to things, world design is fantastic and the lore feels absolutely perfect for a Souls fan like myself.My only gripe, and unfortunately a big one, is the platforming. There are some platforming sections in the game and it is definitely not the game's strong suit. Moving through the air feels far too floaty in comparison to normal movement, sometimes jump inputs are stored resulting in a death, and there are literally a few spots where it seems like they didn't really test out the platforming themselves as the character clips against objects and plummets to death when trying to jump to the intended ledge. That being said, there aren't too many of these moments, and most are just optional paths for random loot so you can avoid them mostly.If you enjoy soulslike games, get this one, it's absolutely a treat and the "anger" it has made me feel at times, due to my own mistakes, was one of the closest to the "anger" that Dark Souls made me feel.Can't wait for their next project!

_childDocuments_.review: If you need to scratch that Dark Souls itch, this game will do it! Combat is the tried and true formula of most Soulslike games. There are a few twists, like gaining energy and healing uses back by dealing melee damage, but the core principles are the same. You have a decent-but-not-huge variety of weapons and armor, which is perhaps one area the game could improve on. Large maps with plenty of secrets and alternate pathways to explore.It's a pretty solid-looking game considering its light install size and the fact that it runs well on my 4+ year old gaming laptop. The space station setting is appropriately spooky and atmospheric. Great sound design and space visuals will have you stopping occasionally just to soak in the ambiance. The story, like Dark Souls, is mostly obscured and left to the player to piece together, which is fine. It's definitely grim and unsettling enough to fit the genre.TL;DR: it's a well-executed Souls-like game with a great creepy space atmosphere.

_childDocuments_.review: Hellpoint : By Triple F"Hellpoint", the 2020 action RPG from Cradle Games, throws players into the derelict space station Irid Novo, a labyrinthine monument to a fallen civilization. Borrowing heavily from the "souls-like" genre popularized by Dark Souls, it offers a challenging experience steeped in a nightmarish atmosphere and cryptic lore. While "Hellpoint" delivers moments of genuine brilliance, its execution is often hampered by technical shortcomings and uneven design choices.The game's greatest strength lies in its visual design. Irid Novo is a masterclass in oppressive world-building. Brutalist architecture, rusted and decaying, looms over the player, creating a sense of claustrophobia and isolation. The bioluminescent flora and twisted, grotesque enemies add a layer of unsettling beauty to the otherwise bleak environment. The art style, heavily inspired by H.R. Giger, evokes a sense of unease and dread, perfectly complementing the game's narrative themes of cosmic horror.Combat in "Hellpoint" is deliberate and unforgiving. Unlike its inspiration, the focus here is more on mobility and strategic use of stamina than slow, methodical attacks. Dodging and parrying are crucial for success, and mastering these techniques is essential for overcoming the game's formidable challenges. While the core mechanics are solid, the hitboxes can occasionally feel inconsistent, leading to frustrating moments of undeserved punishment.Exploration is a double-edged sword in "Hellpoint". The interconnected world is vast and full of secrets, rewarding players who take the time to delve into its depths. However, the lack of a proper fast travel system and the repetitive nature of some areas can lead to tedious backtracking, especially after death. This is further exacerbated by the confusing map design, which can leave players feeling disoriented and frustrated while navigating the station's labyrinthine corridors.The narrative of "Hellpoint" is fragmented and cryptic, pieced together through environmental storytelling and cryptic item descriptions. While this approach can be intriguing for players who enjoy piecing together lore themselves, it can also leave others feeling lost and disengaged. The lack of clear direction can be particularly frustrating, especially for those unfamiliar with the "souls-like" formula's tendency towards minimal hand-holding.One of "Hellpoint's" most unique features is its local and online cooperative multiplayer. Teaming up with a friend can significantly alleviate the game's difficulty and provide a welcome sense of companionship in the face of overwhelming odds. However, technical issues like occasional lag and connection drops can disrupt the cooperative experience."Hellpoint" is a game of contrasts. Its captivating atmosphere and challenging combat are undeniable strengths, but its technical shortcomings, repetitive level design, and cryptic storytelling hold it back from achieving true greatness. Ultimately, it caters to a specific audience: players who relish a high degree of difficulty, cryptic lore, and the satisfaction of overcoming a brutal but rewarding experience. If you fall into this category, "Hellpoint" offers a dark and compelling journey through a derelict space station, but be prepared for a challenging and sometimes frustrating one.

_childDocuments_.review: IF YOU WANT TO BUY THIS GAME FOR THE CO-OP EXPERIENCE, I HIGHLY RECOMMEND YOU STOP...I bought this game because it looked like it could be fun co-op (and eventually singleplayer maybe, like Dark Souls) but was disappointed to find a major co-op issue in the short time I played it. The major issue is that the enemy only targets one player (weird aggro system?) and ignores your co-op partner. This means that your co-op partner can just hit enemies from behind with no repercussion. This kills the atmosphere for co-op. In the short time that I played co-op I noticed this with two enemies, one big guy with a cross shield and the first boss. Yes, the boss... Very fun. This issue may've occured with all monsters I met but I just didn't notice because smaller monsters died quickly.I've since stopped playing and tried to get the devs on Discord to acknowledge and (hopefully) fix this problem. I've yet to get an answer from authority saying whether or not they'll fix it. Maybe it's not a major issue? I'll keep waiting.I can't speak for the singleplayer experience. But since you're alone this issue enemy targeting won't be a problem. Other than this a very minor issue I had with it (which could easily be ignored) was that in co-op only the host will receive achievements.

_childDocuments_.review: Hellpoint, game that just came across and didn't really have almost any expectations of. Knew it's souls like set in space and that it certainly was. You can expect weird NPCs, locked doors, secrets, boss fights, mobs lurking in the dark, getting a space suit or dying outside of space station and more.Gameplay felt quite fluid and jumping mechanics are quite much used if you go out of the beaten path. It's much easier that your original Souls game and that's good things, as some of the routes are quite treacherous and look like where one shouldn't even try to go, but in the end there is path and there's a way to get those shiny loots from far away places. Combat was also quite familiar and felt responsive and fast enough to deal with. This time though mainly had melee weapon in main hand and blaster in the other. Blaster and the like use energy or what ever the blue bar is and you can recharge it by hitting enemies, which was pretty solid idea. On top of those things you have floating bot with different mods like in Nier Automata, but it doesn't really have damage mod, instead of different lights and the like, so those hidden paths are possible to find.Locked doors and opening routes play big part along with those breaches which open like eye of universe before you giving sight on how to improve yourself with quite familiar stats. Think mostly the dark halls and futuristic space station gone to hell was pretty fine to look at, but some of it was pretty ugly to look at, especially own character which looks quite something you wouldn't most likely create in character creation tool, but at least can cover up that mug with armor. About armor and weapons, think armor variety is pretty low in game, but all builds/stats should have their respective set, though felt that game served you better by balancing the stats. Weapons have usually hidden abilities which come out after whacking enough enemies and then give out solid bonuses or charge hits, buffing weapon or character.Variety in areas and enemies is solid enough though it's shame that most bosses are pretty much your average enemies after first encounter. They should have given them unique skins at least and something more over the normal mob. Though it makes sense that they would be similar looking in a sense. Areas change from mostly dark alleys and cities to brighter regions and each of the god bosses who are the most unique in this game tend to have their own theme going on. There are some locked black hole doors around with secrets, also blackhole hour is a thing and was wondering what the heck is going on when it first hit, as whole space station was vibrating and soon noticed how big ugly mutt was clanking it's big metal staff in midst of familiar mob, black hole open invasion possibility for daemons during it's hour and you get bit more aggressive and stronger enemies around it around several places challenging your progression along with arena fights with mobs that give rewards for completing them. _childDocuments_.review: Yeah, so... Barely an hour or two in, and I've come to the stunning realization that this game wants to be Dark Souls, but cannot achieve what Dark Souls did.To explain: COMBATThe combat in Dark Souls (to me, other's will have different opinions, and as such will be respected by me while writing this) feels grounded, a bit slower paced but also methodical. You learn your opponent's moves, you fight them, you die, you come back with that knowledge, and you do it again.This game? This game feels beyond floaty and doesn't feel nearly as fleshed out as Dark Souls was. The game is okay, at best in terms of combat, but nothing makes sense. Enemies turn around without warning one time and start swinging without any regard for their wellbeing or yours, but the next time you fight them, they just sit there. As if they had been here before, agin and again and again. There doesn't seem to be consistency with the grunts that you start with, BUT, I will say for the larger enemies (looking at you, sword bastards) they have a "moveset" but that set of moves doesn't feel like that means literally anything.STORYDark Souls has a story, yeah I know. Do I know it? No. Do I understand or pretend to? Nah. I tried, didn't work, I just played the game. This game's story? Uh... Where is it? Where actually is the story aside from an unseen "guiding hand that created you" that actually explains things along the way? You know what I learned from him? I am the perfect specimen and I live in Irid Novo. THRILLING RIGHT? Except it's not. Being told "you are the perfect specimen because I created you" just kinda... Ruins it for me. Why am I perfect? Why do I look like a prototype sex doll? Why did Dark Souls literally make you a dead person just to come back but this game's approach seems 100% memier? Nothing makes sense.In short, I genuinely cannot recommend this game unless you want another Souls Like. It's okay, at best. That's about it.

_childDocuments_.review: Hellpoint is a soulslike action rpg set at a derelict space station Irid Novo where things have gone horribly wrong, you are a spawn created for the purpose of investigating the station and uncovering the truth of what has occurred on the station. But to do that, you need to survive the horrors that now stalk the station.Gameplay and combat are similar to the original Dark Souls and features several familiar mechanics, although on a smaller scale, less polished and often feeling a little clunky which is to be expected as it is an indie title with considerably smaller dev team and significantly less resources.But there are differences such charging up your healing items by killing enemies, weapons having familiarity experience which in turns improves the weapon and in some cases unlocks special abilities, a real time black hole / storm mechanic that spawns powerful enemies, new encounters, allows you to access some areas and even rewards you with some additional items and of course, the futuristic dark sci-fi setting with things such as no oxygen areas, firearms and advanced tech.Graphically the game is average at best, even if the art direction does a good job of nailing down that darker atmosphere - enemy & armor designs range from futuristic, disturbing, demonic and even at times venturing in the realm of body horror, be it in amalgamations of flesh and metal or things similar to Hellraiser. Environments range from somewhat bland space station corridors to larger/open and architecturally pretty interesting looking areas.One particular aspect that Hellpoint really nails down is its level design and perhaps even more so how rewarding exploration is. Levels are often interconnected although with loading screens in between, feature multiple shortcuts to unlock, optional areas with bosses, hidden doors and plenty of secrets to discover such as areas that are accessible at specific times to actual vertical exploration that leads to hidden sections of a level. For me, it managed to capture that same sense of mystery and the thrill of exploration I had when playing FROMs souls games the first time.That being said, the exploration aspect does have its flaws especially for completionists as you'll see plenty of duplicate weapons, some armors and items as loots due to some areas acting as sort of like alternative routes through the game. Additionally towards the end of a completionist playthrough, you'll be way too overpowered.In terms of audio design, I think the game is somewhat boring. While the sound effects do their job, nothing really stands out and sometimes it almost feels as if some of the sound effects are entirely missing. Music is rarely used and isn't really something that stands out.Aside from that, Hellpoint does have some general issues:- Bugs: While I didn't bump in to any game breaking or otherwise serious bugs, I experienced things such as missing collision, getting stuck in geometry, falling through the world, environment not rendering and some enemy attacks ignoring collision along with myriad other small issues. But I've read reports about some more serious bugs.- Weapon balance: In particular heavier melee weapons feel extremely weak compared to the faster weapons, especially when taking in account the required stat investment.- Difficulty curve: Could use some work, as you end up getting a bit too powerful towards the end and even by accessing some areas too early in the game (such as Port Issoudun) you can trivialize a great deal of the game.My first playthrough of the game took slightly under 20 hours and I had plenty of things I planned to explore, but accidentally ended up finishing the game instead and was put straight to ng+. Fortunately I had so much fun exploring the sprawling levels, surprisingly interesting lore and even the gameplay despite its flaws that I'm eager to do another playthrough.So would I recommend the game? Yes, but with some caveats. I think if you're a fan of the genre, have played and enjoyed other soulslike games (apart from just FROMs output), have a tolerance for some amount of jank & slightly clunky combat and enjoy exploration - it is pretty likely you'll get some fun out of Hellpoint. For everyone else, I'd say go in with tempered expectations - it isn't a AAA title. That being said, in general it may be worth waiting a couple of weeks while some of the bugs are ironed out.

_childDocuments_.review: Some advice:* Invest in more health and stamina before anything else. Then put the minimum number of points towards whatever weapon requirements you need. * Upgrading your weapon conductors influences your damage more than leveling up your stats.* Shield bashing is a reliable way to stagger even the larger enemies. Parrying is trickier to pull off, and the parry window seems to depend on what shield you're using, but it's also quite powerful.  * Two-handed weapons aren't really better than one-handed in terms of DPS, but they are *much* better in terms of staggering. * Guns use Cognition - they are relatively common and useful. The humble railgun is a reliable weapon for much of the game. Catalysts use Foresight - they're somewhat rarer, but also more powerful. Putting points into both Foresight and Cognition would be expensive but also give you a huge range of options for combat at any distance. Or you could just focus on one of them, and make sure to have more than one elemental weapon at any given time.

_childDocuments_.review: Hellpoint is if anything solid, fun and successful in its goal. It is not without flaws and I know I've found a few. However, these kinds of things did not detract from the enjoyment I had with playing the game. The weapons have a unique 'proficiency' system. The utility of the omnicube from an enemy tracker and a pathing orb so you know where you've been help to mitigate the limitations of its level design. Tonnes of secrets with a very non linear progression that, for the diligent explorer will yield paths in various directions. Don't expect this to be an experience identical to dark souls; enemy variety is indeed limited and I would like to see some boss changes just to give them some variety. However, I had a lot of fun simply exploring and discovering new secret paths. Hellpoint in my opinion takes some of the focus away from simply bashing the heads of everything you see and gives back in the form of exploration and discovery. I mean the primary goal itself is to collect information of the space station you reside on. Support the dev and give Hellpoint a go, I have faith that if this game meets the success that these developers deserve then we may hopefully see an improved sequel that addresses everything that limited them in this game.

_childDocuments_.review: 4 / 10.  Skip this game. I've now played through 14 souls inspired games and this one was the worst of them.  I very rarely finish a game that I'd score under a 5 but I powered through this one hoping it would get better and it didn't.   What worked is the core combat.  Its also why I played to the end.  The player controls well, it was fun going around zones killing dudes and the RPG systems work.  I especially like energy system being similar to the Surge in how it converts to more healing letting you stay out longer.   There was a also maybe 3 bosses that felt pretty fun to play and elevated themselves beyond 'meh'.  What didn't work for me personally was just about everything else: - Environments were bland to the point of confusion.  So many locked doors in a way that didn't feel 'fun' to unlock down the road but just added to the confusion of the area.  This is especially true when you go long periods of time before unlocking a door you forgot existed.- Areas lacked cohesion...I didn't feel like one space connected to another and when it came time to backtrack I was completely lost as to which area was where. - The fast travel system being linked to rare item drops is HORRENDOUS.  As a player you don't know the map or what areas are worth returning to so this idea only brought the game way down versus simply letting people fast travel freely.- Enemies were extremely dull.  Most stagger on first hit so 90% of this game is just getting the first hit.  You do NOT need to learn patters in this souls game and that's a huge fail.- This game doubles down on platforming and its just not a fun thing within the souls formula.- Most bosses felt generic and ultimately were generic due to re-use as monsters- Gear upgrading led to a feel bad moment for me where I dismantled old versions only to find out they were requirements for gear I wanted later in the game.  I was then at a total loss on how to get that gear again.- The 'other world' gimmick that's used in this game was a creative idea but felt like padding ultimately and did not serve to make the overall game more fun.

_childDocuments_.review: That was a fun ride, although a bit rough around the edges.If you like Sci-Fi with Eldritch-Horror and some Occultism sprinkled in there, this game might be interesting for you just for it's atmosphere. Movies like Event Horizon, Manga/Anime like Blame!, Warhammer 40k, and some retro-sci-fi Movies/Series come to mind.The gameplay is okay. Combat feels good, albeit a bit clunky at times. Many different weapons, but not an obscene number - you don't get showered with new shiny toys all the time basically, but every now and then. The energy system is a nice touch, and gaining healing-charges via dealing damage is also neat as it promotes an aggressive playstyle.The Leveldesign is interesting yet a bit maze-like (reminded me of The Surge 1). There's a lot of connected maps and passages, and a lot of secrets (or hard to reach places). Exploration feels rewarding. Sometimes it feels like you don't know where to go next or "is this the right way i'm heading?", however, there's multiple ways go through the game and you always end up progressing. There's no long one way roads that just lead to some random, non-progression thing - as far as i'm aware.There aren't many NPCs or Quests, but that's fine, as you don't get sidetracked a lot and just focus on exploring the space station by yourself.The Story & Lore is nice, IF you like to piece things together yourself and IF you can accept that by the End of the game, you'll probably only have "a good idea" of what this all was about. I enjoyed the mysterious vibes that came with exploring places and reading messages, figuring out what the hell is going on (where are we even? what is this space station? black hole? demons?!).The Artstyle varies from great to "you tried", but it feels surprisingly cohesive. Animations can be a bit rough. The music and ambient sounds are great and set the mood without much effort - it just works. However, some sound-effects can feel like they haven't been mixed well (too loud foodsteps, and god forbid that concrete-pillar-weapon smash sound).There are platforming elements to this game. They work, IF you take a moment to figure out how different jumps work and that mid-air attacks can help you with controlling your jump. I have maybe died a handful of times due to not making a jump. I do get why people dislike it though, but for me it worked and gave the game a sense of variety.All in all it was a really enjoyable game and I do hope there'll be a second installment. Excited to see what the DLC will be about.

_childDocuments_.review: DOOM meets Souls, in essence. I won't spoil anything, but if you like the general story of those two, you'll appreciate the writing of this one. It has its flaws - it's certainly the "worst" soulgrinder I've played - but it is by NO MEANS a bad game. Weapon variety is limited in terms of basic moves, but it makes up for that with an evolving weapon system where your favorites get better the more you use them (some minor exceptions). Exploration is detailed with very good level design that loops back on itself with an appealing aesthetic, plenty of little nods to "Ahh, you managed to actually GET here? Good job." Unfortunately, many of the bosses are just recycled basic enemies with an extra move or two. I think that's somewhat made up for by the main bosses of the game, including the potential endings.All in all, worth the time I spent, worthy of sequels or spiritual successors from the developer, worth the price of admission, but not a game I ended up sticking with beyond my initial playthrough. See the playtime for how long it took me, including thorough exploration and the completion of all the side-quests I found.

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome! I am having a blast. Still early, but this is Dark Souls meets Doom and Event Horizon...incredibly unique and fresh formula for a souls-like. The atmosphere is top notch and the combat, where souls-like games tend to falter, is superb. One of the better souls-likes I have played. That said, it could use some polish. I don't get the complaint about there being "nothing new here". That's really comical. It's like Dark Souls on a space station orbiting a Black Hole! Nothing new? Really? There are also really cool mechanics around weapons and the black hole that are obviously new and add to the formula...totally not getting the nothing new grind.   However, it's not perfect. The fast travel system is horrible and will have you covering the same ground over and over. The level design is top end, but it would really benefit from unfettered fast travel. The fact that they added jumping is really cool, but some of the jumping sequences feel like you have to be more lucky than good...which is the cardinal sin for souls-likes, imo. Simply dying a lot is not what makes a souls game. It has to feel fair, and while the combat here is fine in that regard, I died way too many times to jump falls rather than enemies, and I died at least 10 times on 3 specific jumps in the game. Basically, it just feels gimmicky in a game like this, not unlike the fast travel mechanic. Falling from the same distance will also do different amounts of damage. There doesn't seem to be a real formula to it at all, it just arbitrarily decides if you will survive or not. Finally, I don't even want to remember the final, "real" boss.   Hellpoint is awesome and feels like it could have been a gem on the same level as its inspiration. Hopefully it will continue to be patched and improved. I expect that it will only improve because the devs have done an awesome job supporting it thus far. Prepare to be frustrated, but it will keep pulling you back in. Well worth the price, solid 8 as it stands now. Solid souls-like!

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start by saying I am a huge souls-like fan so this is not an unbiased review, but on the other hand it also does make me more critical. This game has its PROS and CONS and this review will include some spoilers so TLDR: overall good game: satisfying combat, upgrade system, some environments, disappointing bosses and plenty of glitches.-Satisfying combat- Multiple weapons with different movesets, although i found a weapon i liked quite early and stayed with it throughout the game.-Interesting upgrade system- Upgrading in this game works by adding a catalyst to your weapon of choice and then upgrading your catalyst by pouring currency into it. Catalysts can enhance scaling based on different stats as well as to different damage types, making multiple builds possible. You can take the catalyst out of a weapon without losing any upgrade and put it into a different weapon, which allows the player to try out different playstyles without losing viability in their current area.-Some environment- For a game that does not look as good as many souls-like counterparts ex. the surge, this game has a few beautiful areas with great level design. Variety in asthetic as well as interesting jump puzzles made exploring great fun. Some great hidden gems and rooms throughout the levels made the level design stand out.-Bosses- Okay spoiler alert from now on. ONLY 3 BOSSES IN THE ENTIRE GAME WERE UNIQUE. One was the same as in the demo, with literally 0 changes. One was a huge fire demon that was literally the easiest boss to beat. The last was the final boss, who was a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ computer with a really bad arena design and boss mechanics, not to mention glitching out every other attempt. Every single other boss was repeated later in the game as a normal enemy, making the encounters with the boss not memorable and souring the experience. I can appreciate one or two slightly harder versions of the normal enemies as boss, BUT 6+ BOSSES???? That is just bad game design and lack of originality or creativity. The first three bosses were the only decent ones with decent mechanics (all 3 showed up as normal enemies later on). -rotating black hole and storm thing- An example of a great idea executed very poorly. To be fair I did not find many of the secrets during the black hole time, but the cons of this outweigh the possible pros. The mini dungeons that spawn during the storm do not spawn minibosses or new interesting enemies, just a ton of the same boring old normal enemy. If you have a weapon with a wide quick swing able to stunlock them, you win, if not, you get buried in a wave of bodies in a tiny arena. Secondly, its such a burden when you are trying to fight a boss which you may be having trouble on. I experienced this with the twin boss, the 3rd one. I did not want to fight an empowered version as I was having trouble with the normal one, so every time I had to wait for the dark hole or storm to pass, spent much time just waiting around.In summary, its an enjoyable game with fun exploration but forgettable and some poorly made bosses. I still recommend it as it is fun and the world is interesting to explore. I bought it for 20% off right before it launched, and I would recommend waiting for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Hellpoint is a wholly different souls-like when it comes to character progression. It took me until my 3rd playthrough to figure out that leveling up isn't really part of the progression system. You only want to meet the bare minimum stat requirements for your gear; after that raise Health, Stamina, Energy, & "Load" to preference. Beyond those only put your Axions [this game's version or Souls] into upgrading weapon/shield/firearm/catalyst chips. Upgrading these chips is very important for gameplay. The minimum for a shield chip is "+8 chip" on a Tribal Shield(DLC) [any other shield needs higher rank] to not lose Stamina while blocking. There is no upper limit to chip upgrades [Ex: I have a +744 Martial Melee Weapon chip].

_childDocuments_.review: Genre - Sci-Fi Budget Dark Souls LikeI am late to the party, but that isn't always a bad thing. I have finished the final boss on difficulty 1 with much co-op play, and here are my thoughts.Hella fun, the game has some of the dark souls elements but with a reliable co-op and fair breach (bonfire) spacing it doesn't become frustrating. You can increase/decrease difficulty at a whim allowing for a more sandbox play style.The bosses are varied enough and offer a decent challenge, but have clear weaknesses. There are also multiple ways to defeat them (Sekiro!). The mobs are quite varied and offer variable difficulty. Some are like mini bosses, whilst some are cannon fodder.The travelling around can be confusing at first due to there being no map, but with co-op you can always get a 2nd pair of eyes. Your skill allocations are locked so you might need to create multiple character builds though as I can't see a re-spec option yet.Weapons, Armour and accessory drops seem fairly unique and will encourage you to collect them all. There are also at least 2 different ways to heal (flasks), which allows you to customise your build more. Ranged is key and also varied from staffs and guns to laser cubes.I think this game has become a gem in the rough over the time and deserves a look (especially on sale).
