_childDocuments_.review: + Extensive, interconnected levels. Interesting and diverse levels. I am on my second character and already found a whole different area, another door to which I need the key and whole lot of shortcuts back into known areas (playthrough #1), you can NOT teleport to breeches (they are like bonfires) but there items that give you the ability to activate travel for one breech at a time. Some people are complaining about that, but there are many of these items hidden behind secret doors, breakable walls and just in the rest of the world. The DLC also added a way to farm them from an enemy-type! There are plenty of interesting puzzles and gimmicks!+ A fair amount of different enemy-types, some of which are used as bosses. The main-bosses are all unique and fun to fight! The DLC adds quite a bit onto the table and even has hidden bosses.There are also events that happen at set times every "day" on the station where you can encounter hordes of enemies, you can get nice rewards from these events just check the surrounding area for the loot!+ Weapons are a little bit different than other games, you can level them up (not upgrade, thats a different mechanic) and they unlock multiple bonus effects, for example +6% health, grenade-launcher round, reduce weapon weight and more! Yes you can unlock new abilities!+/- There really could be more weapon variety (the DLC added some more) and the scaling should be easier to understand, there are upgrade-chips which you can use to alter the scaling and upgrade the chips. You can also remove the chips and just slot them into other weapons and there is no limit to upgrading them, you just need to pay the price!The one thing I hope will be added is more weapons, can we have a weapon that scales with cognition and foresight? Give us some stuff to experiment! If you do a reflex build you can find one of your final weapons in the first area, before the first boss... come on devs! Some enemies dont drop anything.... Pls?+ There is a crafting- and restoration-system which lets you turn scrapped or old pieces of armor into better pieces, just find the recipes and materials!+ The story is interesting and engaging, picks up a lot of topics which are important in todays day and age... really underappreaciated! I am not going to spoil it, but be prepared to get only bits and pieces in the beginning and depending on how your exploration efforts go you can suddenly find large amounts of information at once and get a fuller picture of the world. Oh and I didnt explain it properly there is a mechanic to collect information, if you get enough you can enter the final area and try to get one of the endings!- There some bugs, in my nearly 30 hours of playtime I encountered a glitch that freezes you movement 3 times, I am unsure about what exactly causes this. It seems to be a combination of certain animations on your characters end and being hit while doing so. Nothing gamebreaking, but when it happens it is very frustrating. Dying solves the problem.Another glitch I have seen is the world not loading properly, everything is just grey and you cant see structures anymore, happened 2 times. Leaving and reloading the save fixes this, the game saves when exiting and you respawn at the last breech you visited.Jump attack is a little bad, its animation is too long and you cant get back up before the enemy recovers.Also the heater spear has the weirdest hitbox when enemies get to close, pls fix.Very minor problems most of the time.Yeah check this out if you are looking for a good soulslike with a lot of original ideas and concepts!

_childDocuments_.review: Pros- Aesthetics/lore are the standout aspect here: a mix of cosmic horror, Cthulhu stuff, space and tech- A lot of different influences: Dark Souls 1-3, Bloodborne, Dead Space 1-2, Hollow Knight, Metroid Prime 2, Grim Dawn, maybe The Surge?- Inherits the NG+ system from Dark Souls, but IMO has a really cool lore-friendly implementation (certain progress also carries over, not only your levels/equipment/the usual stuff). Also there are Bonfire Ascetics from DS2, but they're a little more flexible here.- Certain boss designs and arenas are pretty cool.- Lore and implications are really interesting, philosophically.Cons- CLUNKY CONTROLS. IMO this game feels terrible to play, and many boss fights come down to poor AI and obvious tells. I finished a lot of fights feeling accomplished, but also annoyed.- Non-obvious controls: upgrading conductors at a weapon bench, and leaning left/right on ladders- Certain boss fights ruined by sudden OHKOs, _no sound effects_ (which is incredibly weird), lackluster camera, and additional enemies.- Very indie. Leftover bugs never patched, including bad/wrong hitboxes (i.e. your weapon swinging thru an enemy doing no damage, or taking damage from a projectile a mile away... happened to me a lot, in a certain fight in the Port)- The space station looked a lot bigger w/ more variety when I started the game, but ends up feeling like a long corridor. I often felt boxed-in.- Critical NPCs can die even though they might not show a HP bar, so your playthrough is screwed. (You could redo it on NG+ and reduce the difficulty to NG though.)- Blue Sun (DLC) is tempting if you want to fully experience the game, but allegedly it's of mixed quality... read reviews carefully.Tips- Victim Poker weapon is good IMO, I liked STR build and upgrading the Strength Conductor to +2 and beyond.- Check Steam Guides for the "Stat Breakpoints" guide, but I kinda wish I stopped upgrading STR at like... 20-25? instead of 35 which is suggested.- Ignore Coins- Use a guide for the ending you want, *however* i admit the game felt more natural when I didn't get that ending on NG but got it in NG+. To repeat what I said earlier, the NG -> NG+ transition is really lore-friendly.- Certain rewards for hidden content are.... terrible. Use a guide to see what you'd get.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played, finished and gotten every achievement in every Fromsoft game since Demon's Souls. I've tried most of the not-souls and bounced off each one for some reason. This not-souls is the best one I've played.It absolutely captures the sense of mystery and discovery of Dark Souls. Every area is jammed full of passages to explore, with strange things, people and loot.The combat is excellent, taking the quicker style of Bloodborne but keeping the possibility of slower, more methodical combat if you want it. It has streamlined a few things, making it easier than a Souls. You gain back your Estus charge equivalent through combat, resulting in fewer trips back to the not-bonfire and less overall difficulty. The sound design is excellent, perfectly emulating a dark, spooky, empty space station. The place groans and echoes as you wander in the dark.I haven't run into any bugs. I honestly don't know where the claims of jank are coming from. Could it be better? Sure, but it doesn't need to be. We don't get spooky games that aren't about running away from boring things anymore. This is the direction horror gaming should have taken.

_childDocuments_.review: It’s Dark Souls in space. No pause menu, a small nudge in a singular direction that can spiral into several paths toward an unknown goal. It lacks the polish that would make it a pretty good game, but this lack of polish does not hamstring a competently made Souls-like.The sound design of this game wobbles back and forth between awful and just good enough to be useful in combat. Most of the things that need sound queues, like attacks from giant bosses, have those and were what I used to avoid/guard against their strikes. At other times the sound is either absent, too quiet, or horribly inconsistent. The lighting works very well with the ruined derelict space station you are tasked to explore, almost excusing how the sounds do not work all the time.It’s Dark Souls, but with less options that are locked behind a needless crafting system. To get most of the interesting weapons require crafting, which means finding useless items in the field and bringing them back to a 3D printer with a specific blue-print and spending Space-Souls to get a new item. Upgrading said items requires upgrade chips which then can be boosted with more Space-Souls.Your three methods of damaging enemies is to bonk them in melee, shoot them with a space gun until you run out of energy, or shoot them with a space-magic stick until you run out of energy. Considering the main way you regain your energy with which to shoot the guns or space-magic is bonking the enemy with a space-stick, you will always be reduced to cave-man bonking with various degrees of sharp space-sticks.Unique to this Souls-Like, as far as I am aware, is that weapons earn EXP when used to bonk/blast things. These unlock passive perks granted when the weapon is equipped, and special attacks that are assigned to the special attack button. These attacks also consume energy.Healing in this Souls-Like is restrictive, and you never have as much as you’d like of it. Healing has its own resource which is only replenished in three ways:All of the healing methods in the game, sparing your Omni-Cube’s very slow heal, fully heal you with varying degrees of speed. The blue med-hypo, which also purges Radiation from your system, is arguably the most important healing item as Radiation is the most deadly status effect in the game. You will not find enough healing upgrades to max out your healing capacity in one playthrough, so you are better off committing those upgrades to a single healing source.There is a jump button in this souls-like, and the game’s tips encourage you to use jump/dodge attacks to deal extra damage. This extra damage is significant and the extra finesse needed to get that extra damage is engaging and needed. The jumping is a pseudo-commitment; you cannot adjust your jump after leaping, but that means with practice you can gauge how far you can jump. Jumping about can lead to interesting places, and potentially interesting loot.There is a clock in the game that has unique bits attached to two specific time frames. Whenever the clock’s fast moving circle is at the 3 or 9 hour position, the chance for loot or better loot from enemies increases. And when the Eclipse Hour occurs, special passages or things open. I did not discover these things, but the loading screen tips suggest as much.There are also secret doors that are opened by smashing your face into a suspicious wall and pressing the interact button.Finally, there is only Opt-In PVP via duels. You will never experience a player purposefully invading your game to impede your gameplay.Your space-man protagonist is a synthetic human-being created by the space station’s AI for the task of figuring out what the heck is going on. This encourages you to sniff out logs and situations that help explain what everything on the space-station when to pot.Much like all the other Dark Souls games, you can completely ignore the plot and still beat it. But finding info can give context which can enrich the struggle. If you’re into that sort of passive, subtle story-telling.It’s Space Dark Souls, without the hateful PvP griefing but with a needless crafting system. The healing in the game is hamstrung compared to other souls-likes I have played, which did not allow me extra time to better learn the bosses’ attacks before a death. The combat gravitates heavily to melee attacking, so any character build is going to have melee be at the core. Dodging is more encouraged than using a shield, as dodge attacks have extra damage and your dodge mobility is faster and greater than that of a super cheetah. Additionally, hitting things in melee replenishes your healing resources, ensuring all combat will have you hitting your enemy with some sort of stick. Translate this to a New Game+ where enemies hit even harder and the only means of defense are dodge or grind levels until things do not hurt as much, and there is little reason to play after the one go.The story is there. I did not find it engaging or satisfying.I would only recommend this game to diehard Souls-like fans that need to scratch that difficult combat itch. The game is competent enough to do that, but does not do enough to innovate or break from the Dark Souls mold in battle or story.

_childDocuments_.review: What a tough game to recommend. It's very rough and has a lot of faults. If you like the look of the setting and have already played all the FromSoft games and still wanting more then I say give this a go. It really is a cool setting and every time I thought about stopping it surprised me with something that kept me going.The enemy variety is really low. Not only do bosses get reused as regular enemies but the more you play the less variety there is as enemies actually get removed from the game. Due to the more open design I ended up fighting mini mob versions of a boss before the actual boss itself. Really disappointing when the movesets are exactly the same with only a health bar to mark the difference. None of the bosses were memorable. Only the final one was even a little interesting and that was a negative because it had too much going on (if you're going for true ending).Exploration started off really great. I appreciated that they wanted to encourage this. But the jumping was horrible and you can't fall far without dying. I had more deaths from falling than from enemies. That's a bad sign when you're not playing a platformer. And when you finally made it, the reward was hardly worth it. Some of the rewards I got near the end of the game which were also hidden behind long secrets were duplicates of things I had been using for most of my run.Combat is janky. It felt like the Elex of souls-likes. Telegraphing felt pointless when you couldn't tell when the attacks would come due to long wind-ups then quick releases. Then even if you dodge the attacks will often track you anyway. If you do die to enemies then next time you face them you also have to contend with a ghost of yourself. Super cool idea that just ended up being annoying. I got that feeling a lot playing this game. Things that made me say "wow I would really like that if only...".Yet after finishing Elden Ring which I thought was great and having these complaints (and so many more) I still somehow recommend it. Maybe it was the obvious Hellraiser inspiration letting me play as Pinhead with my own cube.

_childDocuments_.review: Hellpoint, although it falls short on a few elements along the way, delivers a satisfying RPG/dungeon-crawling experience. The lows are unimaginative and confusing level design, nauseating visual effects with no accessibility options, and a vague sense of direction. Fortunately, these lows are countered by the highs of incredible science fiction visuals, a unique cosmic horror theme and a visceral combat loop that will manage to keep most players hooked. Hellpoint's draw is complete with it's splitscreen local co-op and replay value. If all this sounds good to you, then give it a go (but use a controller, because apparently every studio taking notes from From Software refuses to address the horrid keyboard playability of the genre).

_childDocuments_.review: Version played: Steam Build 357 - Server 1.03 - Excellent atmosphere. It's Dark Souls meets a tamer version of Dead Space.- Game has an decent-sized arsenal and armory for a indie souls-like.- You won't feel guilty for using the same weapon over and over. The game has a reward system on each weapon that gives passive buffs and/or skills after you hit enemies a number of times. - Weapon upgrade system is neat. Instead of grinding for upgrade stones for each weapon, you have chips that enhance certain atributes. You can equip and unequip the upgraded chips from your weapons and put them on new ones. No more regrets from upgrading weapon x and then finding a weapon y that is cooler to use.- A fair amount of content to consume because of level secrets, multiple endings, collecting items, co-op and duel PvP. - Game's music is forgettable.- Too many bosses are reused as normal enemies.- The game is quite janky. Examples: Many animations from the characters are weird; The UI for your items when you need to pick one for crafting/upgrading is just a list of all your items that you need to scroll through again and again; Your inventory can't be sorted and you can't drop your items.- Game has a lot of bugs. Examples: Sound effects become mute for no reason; Certain loot will vanish from the game after a certain point of the game is reached; Enemies pop up in your face or become invisible; If you hit the final boss as soon as its speech ends, the AI turns off; Running sometimes isn't activated when you hold down the running button.- The game has a platforming system that seems either bugged or badly crafted in regards to fall damage. Some jumps to other platforms will kill you while others with same height from other areas will deal a small amount of damage. Some jumps will kill you if you press the jump button to leave the platform your character was standing at but if you just drop down, you recieve a small amount of damage instead.- I'm not that much of a fan of this game's Fast Travel system. You need an item called Breach Syncronizer to connect one of your checkpoints to the others that can use fast travel. If you search every nook and cranny, you can find enough Syncronizers to connect all the important checkpoints. If you don't, you're going to have a bad time with the long backtracking in certain areas. Also, the checkpoints need to have their fast travel capabilities reactivated by Syncronizers each time the character starts a new game cycle...- Game has 66 coins scattered throughout the world to collect. Getting them all doesn't give you any rewards besides a Steam Achievement. Really lame to get just an achievement after all the effort.TL;DR - Recommended but i would wait for a sale. It's better than most indie souls-like games that i've played but the bugs and certain design decisions would make me hesitate picking this game up without a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: While there's a lot of smaller issues (with hit detection, weightless feel of swings, enemy and equipment variety, platforming issues and more) and some major problems (the true final boss, online mode not working), Hellpoint is still an absolutely engrossing experience due to it's enticing secrets filled environments. The set-up is intriguing, it's got an interesting concept in it's approch to difficulty, while the melee-to-magic integration is an unmitigated success. Combine that with a stunning setting, that artistically does a lot with a little and always leaves you wondering what's around the next corner and Hellpoint is something every Souls fan should experience at some point.It respects the player, trusts them to find enjoyment in exploration of convulated spaces often hiding secrets in plain view, which feels liberating in a way most games don't today, but most importantly of all - despite the polish issues - it always manages to feel like a passion project that the developers cared deeply about. It's got heart that reaches far beyond it's budget, which is always worth supporting.Oh, and it also has split-screen co-op!

_childDocuments_.review: Full disclosure, I have not beaten this game yet, but after 9 hours of playing, there are a lot of glaringly obvious things about this game. Hellpoint is an absolute mess. TL;DR: Decent combat, lackluster bosses, some of the worst map designs I've ever seen in a Souls-like (maybe even a paid game in general), a slew of bugs, and incredibly poorly utilized mechanics that only aid to muddy the game's decent core mechanics. I'm a huge fan of souls likes, and I've played quite a few that left me in awe, and even more that left me with an awful taste in my mouth. Hellpoint falls somewhere right inbetween both of those categories. The graphics aren't anything special, yet on my 2080 and i9, it still makes my computer run almost as hot as Cybeprunk. The frames also manage to drop from. Considering the graphics that often look like a game from 2015, this shows a lot about the lack of optimization. That category definitely doesn't win it any favors. The combat, being a souls like, is definitely something of import. All in all...it's eh. Initially, it felt really great hitting the first enemies you're shown, as the sounds were punchy and satisfying. That, sadly, didn't last, largely thanks to one of the most frequent bugs throughout this game. I'll get more into it later, but put quickly for this, you often don't hear anything when hitting enemies later in the game. Weapons stop making noise on impact. The combat really comes to a crawl when fighting bosses, however, and this is where the game seemingly falters the most. Many amateur takes on Souls-likes struggle with creative bosses that have a balance between difficulty and diversity. Hellpoint dropped the ball entirely and decided to just make bosses kill you in 3 hits regardless of stats and armor. There is seemingly no balance between good and bad bosses in this game. Some you can literally circle around endlessly while they just attack where you were several seconds ago, and others will attack without end until you get hit once, and you're then chain stunned to death. The bosses go from low tier sponges to god tier enemies on a whim, and never is it because of creative design. If a boss is hard, it's because it will 1, 2 or 3 shot you regardless of how far ahead you are. It's not satisfying to overcome the bosses in this game because they're just so mindless. It's not skill that ends up beating them, and when you do, the rewards are always lacking. Map design. Souls-likes are notorious for having relatively complex maps with branching paths to make sure you explore everything, lest you miss out on important loot. The developers behind this, sadly, held an ambition leagues above their capabilities. Never in my days have I seen more complicated maps. Rarely do I find myself lost in a game after passing through the same area three times, but with Hellpoint I found myself hoping to stumble onto success after looping back through the very samey corridors of the station. This would likely not be so much of an issue if a Dark Souls style teleportation system was in place, but one of the peak examples of this game's eagerness to stand apart was taking the worst part of Dark Souls 1 and then making it even worse.  You need a single use item to allow 'bonfires' to function as teleportable waypoints. "Breaches" take the place of bonfines, and you need an item to turn each Breach into a point that you can teleport TO and FROM. This would be less of an issue if the map design wasn't so horribly sloppy. I've come across 15 breaches, and after very, very indepth exploration, 6 items for connecting those breaches. This means I can teleport to 6 of those 15 breaches. I have almost no access to anywhere on the map. Now ideally, you'd think that you could strategically choose these breaches. Sadly, you'd be wrong in this. The game will put two breaches almost directly beside each other, often separated by a mere elevator. It seems almost random how these breaches are placed, and it's baffling to think that they'd place them so poorly with maps designed so terribly. To finish, the map design of Hellpoint would be much like a visualization of Metal Gear Solid's plot using only arrows. Bugs. Oh bugs. The most annoying bug that happened for about 7 of my 9 hours playing came in the form of audio glitches. Elevators will make ear piercing screeches while cutting in and out completely, some armor sets don't make sounds while you're sprinting, some maps remove weapon sounds all together, and of course, sometimes the audio just cuts out. I truly cannot believe that this game isn't early access. A more pressing issue, in terms of playing the game, is how you can find yourself falling forever on flat items. Land wrong on a piece of nearly flat rubble and, uh oh, you're not stuck free falling in place. I waited a total of 7 minutes falling on one piece of rubble and, be it through luck or me mashing buttons, managed to escape. The second time I got stuck on a ledge (that I NEEDED to go up to progress) I wasn't so lucky, and had to manually shut down the game. You can't access the pause menu while falling, so it was an Alt+F4 moment. For a game with positive reviews that managed to leave early access, I'm genuinely befuddled that so many people are okay with these issues. A quick google search assures me I'm not the only one, yet apparently I'm one of few to take a real issue with it. In conclusion, between the droves of audio bugs, never ending awful map design, and god awful bosses, this is truly an amateur souls like. If this game were early access, I think it'd be a middling "Maybe", but with it not being such...this is a hard pass for anyone intending to spend money. It's commendable that the developer tried so hard to be original, but as is so often the case, struggling to hard leads to an absolute mess clinging to a fleeting idea of creative genius. This game being as small as it is also makes finding out information on the very, VERY cryptic elements within often impossible to find. There are a slew of mechanics never explained at all, and no matter what I searched, I couldn't find anything on it. Found some codes for free weapons though, so that was nice. This isn't an awful game for 10$, MAYBE 15$, but it's just so poorly polished that it's hard to claim the developer really loved their creation. When the audio is cutting out more often than it's on, that's a serious issue. When 5 bosses I encountered all became normal enemies to save on creating other enemies, that's an issue too. Reusing a few is fine, but every boss I've encountered thus far when I'm supposedly only 30% through the game? That doesn't bode well for the future. This game cuts a lot of corners, often cutting off crucial components of good games with it. Buyer beware, but if you still choose to go with this game anyways, I wish you luck.

_childDocuments_.review: I've put seven hours into this game over the past three days and I wanted to put down my tentative thoughts on the game. I'll change this as I play more.Okay, I hesitated for a long time on this game. I was fairly intrigued by the Kickstarter. A game promising a soulslike experience with influences from Event Horizon, Lovecraft, and Giger sounded right up my alley. However, I've been burned before on that platform. I backed Stonehearth and Chasm, two mistakes that still haunt me to this day. So I didn't back it. What's more, the reviews on Steam didn't seem promising. The good reviews seemed lukewarm and the negative reviews looked downright damning.I can now say that I regret not backing it or buying it sooner. This game succeeds because of two elements: level design and world-building. I almost wanted to say that, in this game, they're one and the same. You see, the abandoned world of Irid Novo feels like a breathing corpse. The sounds, environments, and characters paint a picture that, true to the Souls formula, could not be told otherwise. The level design allows the world to be an interconnected maze that genuinely feels like a monumental space station.And speaking of mazes, there are secrets galore thus far. In just seven hours I've stumbled across at least four secret doors. A quick google search showed me that I have missed a fair amount already, so I'm excited to retread or replay in the future. This brings me to my final point for now.The comparison to Dark Souls will be inescapable. I'm a fan of the genre. Hell, Bloodborne is my favorite game of all time. I firmly believe From Software pushed game design into a different direction for the foreseeable future with their work. In the case of Hellpoint, the comparison to Soulsborne is fair and accurate, but there's a nagging thought I keep having. When Miyazaki made Demon Souls and Dark Souls, he achieved the, up to that point, impossible: he and his team made some good 3D Metroidvanias. And that's why Hellpoint works for me so far. This game reminds me of a Metroidvania in the best way possible. There's a breathtaking world to explore and unravel at your own pace.Wanna grind into until your character is as powerful and destructive as a black hole? Why not! Wanna poke around in everyone corner? ♥♥♥♥ it, you do you! Wanna speed run the game as fast as humanly possible? Go to town!So to wrap things up, I have to mention where I started this review-in-progress. This game isn't for everyone and that's totally fine. However, if you want to explore a mysterious haunted space station, take the leap. I didn't regret it and I hope you don't either.PS: Hellpoint and Sekiro have officially convinced me that more Soulslike games need a dedicated jump button. It allows for whackier combat and better exploration, end of story.*Edited for typos*

_childDocuments_.review: The dated visuals could be forgiven if the gameplay was somewhat decent. Things I don't like about this gameNonsensical level and redundant level designs. Huge areas and paths that end up to completely empty places with nothing to interact with. Rooms with a short set of stairs that lead to walls. Darkened areas in the first part of the game designed to make you fall to your death (if you think this is to teach you to watch where you step you're wrong, because this kind of trap doesn't come up in the later levels which are more well lit)Getting stuck on geometry, especially annoying when it happens on narrow ledges.Movement lacks weight/feedback, it almost feels like your character is ice skating.Platforming. Absolutely terrible. The number of times I've fallen to my death because the sprint in a sprinting jump didn't activate. The level design that has 1-way platforms where if you've landed on the wrong platform you have to either die or teleport back to the last checkpoint. The forward momentum on landing that makes your character unresponsive for a brief moment which can cause you to walk off a ledge. The lack of mid-air control to correct a jump if you overshoot it.There is currently no way to respec your character if you didn't like how you levelled them. Kind of dumb considering a first time player wouldn't understand where to put their points on the first playthrough. Punishes players for not looking at a guide before they play.You character going in to a frenzied break dance every time you die. Seriously Cradle Games, I know you seen this during testing. Just play an animation if you can't make the player rag doll properly.There are just too many little things that spoil the experience before I can recommend this game.I got this on sale for 1/2 price and I still feel ripped off.

_childDocuments_.review: The game was fun and had an interesting story - I really did enjoy the time I had playing. However, I can't recommend the game to people because of the sheer amount of game breaking bugs! The following are the most consistent bugs I ran into, constantly:- Enemies (including bosses) knocked me down and, upon getting back up, I couldn't move at all - unless I got knocked down again or died.- Sometimes, when swapping to another weapon, you get stuck in a loop of swapping weapons. As a result, you can't do anything and need to force close the game.- Somehow, quite often, dodging outside of the game/scenery and falling to my death. - Entering a room and moving the camera too fast causes everything but the UI to disappear - the fix is to find your way out of the room and re-enter. - This game has parkour elements, except jumping is really inconsistent - randomly over jumping or randomly just hopping slightly forward.If you have the patience to deal with these bugs, then go ahead and give the game a try! Also worth noting, the co-op is highly unreliable and almost nonexistent - you're better off trying to form a group with someone but you will still face connection problems.

_childDocuments_.review: - Atmosphere- Sound Design- Combat- Boss Design- Exploration (There are secrets and secrets within those secrets)- At the time of this review optimization is great and the game runs smoothly- Enemy types are repetitive (Early game at least)- Enemy AI is easy to exploit and overcome (As far as early game mobs go)- Too many pitfalls in overly dark areas (Bad game design in my opinion)- Some environmental pop-in here and there- Speech audio bugs out sometimesOverall enjoying the game so far. Feels like a Dark Souls 1 level of clunky when it comes to movement and combat, which is acceptable. Don't be expecting Dark Souls 3 level of fluidity in player movement. Boss designs are cool so far. Music and sound design are superb. Graphically the game looks great, it's no jaw dropper by any means but they are nice to look at aesthetically, but if you're buying a game solely on graphics then you're playing the wrong game here. As for what I've played so far, it looks like the story will mostly be weaved into pieces of lore found throughout the world, which is fine. I'm not here for the story, I'm here to immerse myself in this dark, spooky world with creepy space monsters. This space station is pretty large too, so be prepared to get lost and explore, which is another thing this game has a lot of.As a Kickstarter backer who has been here since the beginning, I'm happy with the final product. _childDocuments_.review: 7/10 - Fantastic cross between DS and DSp(Dead Space) with great elements from both with more than a few flaws+ Truly unique world building and design unlike anything else. _childDocuments_.review: A really solid entry to the souls-like genre that's worth checking out if you're a fan. If I had to make a quick comparison it's somewhere between Dark Souls 1 and Remnant: From the Ashes (leaning more towards the former).While it lacks the polish or graphical fidelity of something like DS3 or Sekiro, combat still feels solid with only a handful of hiccups, and a very strong art direction makes the game interesting to look at and dripping in atmosphere despite some relatively dated texture work and VFX.The space station is expansive and an explorer's delight, those who enjoy scouring every nook and cranny will appreciate the sheer amount of hidden goodies tucked away, and you're encouraged to return to areas as you get new tools to find even more.There's a surprising amount of platforming too which helps to make the environments feel a lot more open as you can freely jump about and are often required to do so.I appreciate that ranged weapons and the sorcery-equivalent feel more viable as main weapon choices due to the replenishing energy system and the ability to equip catalysts or firearms as an offhand weapon. Less restrictive stat requirements than a souls game also means I have more build flexibility and am more freely able to try new weapons I find, instead of most of them being completely useless if they don't align to my stats. Weapon upgrades are also more flexible with a system akin to Bloodborne's gems - rather than level up individual items you invest in chips which can be freely swapped between weapons.One of the major downsides is a gated fast travel system. Any breaches you find can be turned into nodes on the fast travel network but you are required to expend a limited item. At first I appreciate this as it encourages you to explore and use these more thoughtfully, balancing between resting now or going deeper, but later in the game it can make backtracking a chore - especially if your early ones were used carelessly. I would appreciate a way to craft this item or something to alleviate this towards the later parts of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: First i would say any Review that is below 3-4 hours is invalid. The game gets much better after the first 1-2 areas. I guess most people got smashed hard by the Sentinel enemy on the first level and rage quit.In my opinion if they removed the 2 Sentinels from the first level the game progression would be nearly perfect.Pros:-a LOT of levels that are interconnected-diverse Areas, most have their own charm/atmosphere, i love the art design, it gave me Bioshock in space vibes-Levels are logically designed, and memorable for the most part, many souls like dont achieve that-the backstory and lore is interesting and does a lot for the world building and atmosphere-weapons, all your weapons have exp bars and can be upgraded by killing enemies to unlock more powerful active and passive abilities, i absolutely LOVE this system, it is amazing, not only can you upgrade your weapon stat wise like dark souls but you have an alternative progression, it keeps making me want to try them all and see what i unlock next-so many hidden secrets and loot, i loved the exploration so much, if you explore all in your level or looking up a guide now and then, you really appreciate the art and level design-steady good progression, i dont know if it got patched after launch, but i never felt overwhelmed or out matched, if you do your exploration, slog through the first 1-3 levels, it has a great difficulty curve(as in most souls/like games first few levels are hardest then it gets better)-sound design is great, it makes you really feel like you are on that alien space station, with creepy sh*t around every corner-a lot of replayability, trying new builds, unlocking different encounters in NG+ and so on, i will continue my journey sooner or later-the black hole clock is a cool idea, and unlocking those secret gates was also a nice exploration, i just wished we could skip time/fast wait, sometimes i just stood around waiting for the clock so i didnt need to go back and forth again-art and graphics are decent and clean, not next gen but good enough, the atmosphere and design makes it even better-THE GAME ONLY NEEDS 6 GB, ALL DEVELOPERS SHOULD BE ASHAMED BY THEIR 100GB+ GARBAGE GAMES FFS-jumping puzzles are fine after you get used to, all people who fail, get gud, same as combat in souls likes-long game, depending if you kill optional bosses, do exploration, side quests, black hole events, use guides or not, this game can easy take 30-45 hours for one playthrough, and then you get more with NG+ and other builds-great art design on weapons and armors, i just wished we could upgrade all our armors as we do weapons, unlock abilities or sets gave us boni-Catalyst weapons are f*cking amazingCons:-the Space background when you look outside is too low res, i dont know who did this , but please just exchange a high res picture, the galaxys/stars look awful-the Sentinels in the first level are just bad, yea you can kill them if you know how, but still... many people got problems with them, they are also one of the few enemies that have "cancer movements" what i mean by that is that they can change their attack movement mid flight/jump/dash by being locked on to you, like an aimbot. Its just bad design, but fortunately its maybe the only one who does this-the "true secret" final bosses arena gave me vertigo, its super dark and those lights moving around very fast and radical. _childDocuments_.review: You know your game is pretty good at copying Souls games when the best you can make is a boss with a ton of target points that make your camera completely ♥♥♥♥♥♥ and when you die the camera janks into oblivion. Amazing job with this one.The fact that when you get knocked down you can still get infinitely hit is amazing, borderline the most amateurish game I've ever played of this kind.As an avid lover of souls-like games, I don't recommend this game the slightest, it's riddled with bugs, bad level and game design, and I would have requested a refund if I could (my playtime exceeded 2 hours). Having defended this game back when the Thespian Feast was released, it is a dissapointment to see the game has barely improved (if at all) and the final result is pretty bad.EDIT: after writing this review I started over with a different build (i was doing reflex and conjecture or whatever the tech one is and instead just went full STR and used the tutorial level column for the rest of the game up to the final boss). I got to the true ending of the game completely by accident, I met NPC's that acted as if I had already interacted with them, only to find them in previous areas and acting as if we had never met. I did everything completely out of order, I did not understand anything about the plot, but it seems to be just a bootleg version of Event Horizon.Nothing I wrote originally changed throughout this new gameplay, with the only difference being that I could now effortlessly stunlock bosses and even strong enemies into dying just by mashing attack. The damage I was dealing with inferior stats on STR were drastically super by second compared to my original build, and the difficulty of the game overall changed drastically from way too hard to way too easy at some times. I understand this is more or less common in other souls games, but I never saw the disparity this hard, and being someone that usually replays souls games multiple times with different builds (rogue, warrior, sorcerer, nightblade whatever) I never felt the difference this hard.Overall the ending was lackluster, and I left knowing the same as I started, and honestly only finished this game out of the habit of finishing games I start. I hope the devs can learn from whatever they learned technically, and actually make a solid game with a solid storyline next time.

_childDocuments_.review: I beat this game in local co-op and can't really recommend it. It's not *terrible* but it's extremely mediocre with several glaring technical and design issues. My partner and I were pushing to finish this game ASAP once the end boss was in sight.Pros:- Pretty cool atmosphere and lore- The combat ..feels OK outside the often poor AI.- Local split screen coop is rare for this sort of game and was appreciated- Some of the environments were visually pretty impressive for an indy gameCons:- This game has a debuff, "insanity" which I ♥♥♥♥ you not *zooms your camera way out + fish eyes it* for several seconds. It's never explained and is very common. This coupled with the already poor camera and smaller view in split screen made me wonder what the devs were thinking...- Terrible lock on system (the "lock on" indicator is tiny and hard to see in the dark which is where you spend the entire game, the right stick switching enemies often won't work or will lock onto mobs through walls). The camera will flip around or stare at ceilings / floors very often in all sorts of situations.- Coop has all sorts of bizarre design issues like if player 1 dies, player 2 dies instantly too. However, player 2 doesn't lose their "souls" if this happens so by end game player 2 will be several levels higher than player 1. - Player 2 also can't interact with quest items, npcs or doors.- Map areas are huge mazes that branch off constantly, and all the corridors look the same. You're going to get lost and waste time. Walkthroughs online were mediocre.- Many of the map branches just lead to dead ends or have very little payoff- Most of the weapons and armor you'll find will be useless, there's way too many stats to pump  points into. I think maybe 10-20% of the equipment we found were equipable, the rest were utterly useless besides scrapping.- Too many places to fall to your death right around corners or due to darkness. The jumping was kind of awkward, the amount of HP you'd lose from falls was wildly inconsistent too.- The levels are insanely dark and your flashlight takes constant energy to use (flashlights in the future go out in 15 mins? what?). Energy is also how you use your weapon's special move, so.- Energy and healing pots won't recharge at checkpoints- You seem to gain both heals and energy from damaging enemies, but in co-op it doesn't share so if one player is in front getting all the kills, the back person gets nothing (you can't swing through partners and there's a lot of narrow corridors so this happens often).- The bosses and enemies in general have AIs that simply can't handle 2 players, one player can literally just kite them while the other wrecks them from behind. We beat the entire game this way and the bosses were mostly a joke. Considering tough bosses is kind of a cornerstone of soulslikes, this was pretty disappointing.- Had random game stuttering on a high spec systemTL;DR: if you're desperate for a co-op soulslike and have a ton of patience maybe this is worth it on sale. Overall the terrible level design, camera (featuring "insanity") issues, bad / easy AI and other weird design decisions hold this game back from being anything other than a mediocre souls imitator. Would not recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Needs more work in my humble opinion; Spawn timers should be shortened as farming is a chore right now. Blocking should be instantaneous (ala Sekiro -> it should be about when you push the button, not when the shield comes up) and / or there should be a dedicated parry(kind of standard in a 2020 souls game). Combat for the moment is really just about either A) killing the enemy before they can attack  you, or B) waiting for them to overextend - I know this sounds fine, but Sekiro really raised the bar in terms of active engagement in combat. Theres a lot of minor tweaks that should have been done before this was released but I couldn't possibly give this a thumbs down. Its fun in spite of its problems. its a 6.5 or 7 out of 10 in its current state. the atmosphere and world to me is a 10, and whoever did that alien voice should win an award - so awesome. Give it a shot if you're a die hard souls fan, its definitely not easy and u'll find it refreshing, in its own dysfunctional sort of way. Just don't expect the polish and consistency of a fromsoft game.

_childDocuments_.review: A highly enjoyable souls like. So far the areas are all really well interconnected, like the first half of Dark Souls 1. A lot of hidden stuff to explore and shortcuts to unlock. The atmosphere is incredibly well done with the sci fi architecture and ambient noises, and the enemy design is varied and a lot of detail went into their models. Combat is a little faster than DS1 and a little slower than DS3. The bosses are challenging and need strategy to tackle. IMHO Co-op is better than most soulslike games because you can follow the host across multiple zones, and you share resource pickups.There is a little jank in the movement and some invisible obstacles (very few I've noticed), and sometimes the netcode is kind of funky. The only real problem I have with the game is that in some cases you need to set up port forwarding to enable co-op, and not all players know how to do this, so sometimes it's hard to find a co-op partner. I've enjoyed my time so far. Not sure if this will hold up for the entire playthrough, most games start to peter out a bit by the 3rd act. Will update this review when I complete it.

_childDocuments_.review: Things I do like about Hellpoint:• The art direction. Looks like a mishmash of Synth, Hellraiser and Renaissance and as weird as that combo might sound, it works pretty well. Really cool and unique.• There is some level of challenge to it, you can't faceroll enemies like you can in most other Souls-likes if you go for a non-magic/ gun run, melee can be pretty challenging.• The soundtrack doesn't stand out outside of the game but while you are playing, it does its job well enough.• The upgrade system is split into stat leveling and weapon leveling, and the weapon leveling itself is split in two parts as well - conductors, something that you slot into weapons and is what you actually upgrade to + the weapons, and familiarity. Familiarity unlocks extra weapon-specific passive buffs and skills, and it builds up as you use the weapons. Conductors on the other hand give the stats increase and can be removed and re-slotted in at any given time. This means you don't have to upgrade every single weapon in the game to use it, you just slot an upgraded conductor into whatever you wanna try and it instantly gets the + level of the conductor. A pretty elegant solution to weapon upgrading that even Souls games get wrong.• The narrative and dialogues are interesting. Surprisingly it isn't a riddlefest or edgy as ♥♥♥♥, like other souls-likes tend to be (Mortal Shell and Lords of the Fallen I'm looking at you), so reading and listening to audio logs is enjoyable.• Platforming. I love jumping puzzles in games that have them. In Hellpoint, it is a love-hate relationship and I will elaborate on why that is below.Negatives:• Optimization is kinda ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥...• Bugs. It is extremely buggy. Hellpoint was released 3 years ago, received many patches since as well as a "Next Gen" update alongside its DLC and yet it is still buggier than your average Early Access title...• Level design. Some moments and shortcuts are memorable, however the design leans heavily on being convoluted. I've seen some compare the levels to those of Dark Souls, which I totally disagree with - shortcuts in DS are kept to a minimum and they all serve a purpose. Level design in Fromsoft games in general is complex (complex =/= convoluted) but clean in design and full of landmarks that help you memorize areas. In Hellpoint, most levels are pretty much labyrinthine corridors that look samey. It can be extremely tedious to navigate this world.• Mechanics and progression are obtuse and convoluted. When the community has to rely on the devs' Discord posting "Spoilers" so the player can find pathways, items and even bosses, you know something has gone wrong in terms of making an intuitive game.• Fast travel is tied to something called Breach Synchronization, which is done through a limited (per NG cycle) item that you'll always find far less than there are Breaches (bonfires). This will create a situation where you can unknowingly mess up your mid and late game as you won't be able to synchronize later bonfires. This issue is further compounded by the convoluted map design I mentioned above, as well as that Synchronizations are undone and don't carry over to NG+ cycles. Mind you the DLC does fix this problem by making the otherwise extremely limited items reliably farmable, but it never feels right to me when devs create a problem and then paywall the solution.• The combat can be a bit of a mess. Attacks, especially ranged ones (magic and guns), will miss constantly because the lock-on system is unreliable and enemies' hitboxes seem to bug very often. Some enemies have really goofy combos that go on and on, some of which can stunlock you (hello mindflayers). Attacks that clearly didn't make contact with you, will register as hits. Sometimes during combat everything glitches out in a way that freezes you in place. The game doesn't accept any inputs afterwards, only dying or task manager "fixes" the bug.The worst and at the same time most unique thing about Hellpoint is its platforming. There is a dedicated jump function here, which already sets it apart from other soulslikes and even most Souls games. There's lots of platforming and jumping puzzles and in theory, they are well designed. In practice, because of how buggy and glitchy it is, you will grow to loathe the platforming and JPs. Invisible walls that clip you and bounce you to your death, dubious ledge placements where you'll clip your head and your jump momentum will disappear, inputs lagging out of nowhere after landing (I'm talking 2s delays), losing momentum randomly as soon as you jump, getting stuck in terrain... When latched onto lifts, jump direction doesn't depend solely on the movement button input, it sometimes also depends on where the camera is facing, which will bug things out so badly that you'll jump off the lifts in completely random directions, probably to your death. It is unfortunate that the one feature that helps Hellpoint stand out from other soulslikes, is the most poorly executed aspect of the game that might just make you hate it.If you are interested in Soulslikes, Hellpoint is definitely worth a playthrough. Maybe buy it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: After cca 70h played only with keyboard and mouse i have to review it. Despite overall positive feeling i have to start with cons as there are things new player should be aware of. - Exploration      Hellpoin is fairly large game and exploration is at least 30% of playing time but it so unrewarding and dull. There are many istances where level desing it done well to encourage you to look there and there, sometimes they also throw little puzzle at you but after you get there the item what will you find will be:  1. Duplicate item you have already found few. And it even happens in puzzles which that type appear only once. I remeber once after finishing puzzle located in the final parts of game i got same item as i found just lying on the floor in early game.  2.  Axioms ( game´s currency for leveling up ) which are pretty useless coz in the most scenarios you can find 100-900 of these but what for when to lvl up i need 20 000.- Platforming     There are load of platforming segments but platforming itself is exremely simple. Just jump and land. If you will miss plaform 0,1 mm further you will fall , there is no edge grabbing ,nothing. And most of the time it leads to death as if there is no death pit, platforms are so hight  you just cant survive it with some character builds. Cherry on top , prize at the end is the item you have already found.- First ending       I am not talking here about overall story but there is ending which is really simple to get without even having beaten all bosses and explored all areas. And you dont know that end is coming. It is so anticlimatic you dont want to believe it is the end.  , at this part player is expectig twist. Not the end. When u will finish the game , there is no asking you if you wanna go to NG+. They will yeet you right there and will take some collectibles from you which were pain to find as i mentioned exploring becames really repetetive.- Bugs     Yeah , there is still load of them. Updates every now and than but u know , its just too much. Biggest shame is that multiplayer is hardly working now. Second player do not have animations , he is naked , flying or stuff like that happening. From PvPing you get nothing, not even those measly Axioms. I tried PvE , enemies werent losing hp despite i was hitting them. After dying my camera just stuck there and i had to alt-shift-delete. But i havent crashed once, thats good i guess. Devs are releasing patch every week, i believe they are working hard. - Tutorial     Except that right mouse is for attacking , space is for jumping game doesnt tell you much. Which is good but there are instances where it at least could warn you.   + game universe     I didnt expected it to be so deep as it is. I mean it is not abyssal zone depth type of lore as in dark souls but every character you meet has his purpose , his reasson to be there and mostly his goal. You can help NPCs ,you dont have to. At the end it leads to many different endings. Which except for the first one are really good. That one is probably for speedrunners i dunno.+ Story    Story type of hell let loose on space station is excatly my cup of tea. Plus it is combined with paralell universes ideology. It adds more to already good story. Some characters are even aware of the fact there is same thing with few alterations happening right now in oher universes. Some are obliviouse to it, it adds such diversity. Multiple endings , even multiple intros which depend how did you finished your last playtrought. I havent seen this yet in other games so it really suprised me in good way. Dialogs or monologues are interesing and well written. Some tell you where to find good stuff or how to get somewhere. Some of them expands the story to next act. Some tells you about the lore. Some of them want to abuse you , some them want to be abused. I feel like hellpoint have 5 writters and one programmer, again referring to those bugs.+ Combat    Someone actually finaly did it. They made combat fluid and fun, can compare it to dark souls. Althought , enemies can get cheesed in most of scenarios but at the end you are the one benefiting from this. I playd as heavy weapon guy and kept smacking monsters to the floor, it was fun. There is jump button , and its real jump button in contrast with dark souls where you can jump only while running. You can combine jumping with your fighting style. Its fun until you get to platforming as i menioned higher.+ Atmosphere   Great, walking in cold iron corridors of Irind Novo is so immersive. Its dark and depressive and i love it. Altough if i am mentioning station itself there are some typical " only in game" desing stuff. Like, why are there falling platforms like in Indiana Jones movie on this space station. I understand it is part of a puzzle but still it makes me giggle a bit.+ Builds     Big weapons , daggers, mace , scythe , swords, guns , artillery , mage weapons , catalysts. Fire damage , dark damage , radioactive damage, physical damage , explosive , heavy armor , light armor , magic armor...etc. The amount of builds you can do is something this game definitely does not have to be ashamed about.   + And now they added PvP Arena with prizes day before christmas. What a great gift.-+  Bosses     After few bosses i found out that all of them can be beaten by circling around them with a shield.-+  Shield     Shield with 100% physical resistance or others makes game so easy. Even if there is some attack you cant shield game do allow you to dodge while having shield up, so even when you miss dodge you will not get damaged badly. I am not sure if dodgeing while having shield up is a bug or feature.-+ Getting from point A to B when you already explored them.     There are no enought breach synchronizers ( thingy that lets you teleport from bonfire to bonfire ) I meant there are load of them but they are usually clustered at one place so I instinctively use it one bonfires in that location that are already too close to each other so there is no need for it and than i dont have it when i need it.-+  Bonfires     Sometimes there are two bonfires centimeters next to each other, sometimes there is none where it should be.-+ 2 handed weapons controversy    You cant two hand weapon in this game which is no biggie. It expands the things you can hold as there is useles to be empty handed. But, if you really want to do that heavy guy big weapon build ,pity, he will hold it with just one hand no matter how heavy it is.

_childDocuments_.review: This is going to be a weird one. Quick note, love Soulsborne games and have I don't even know how much time I spent on them. I've seen a few videos of Hellpoint, and figured after seeing the overall ratings, decided to give it a try. Played the game to a completion.Story, you're a Spawn created by the Author, a super AI. You are created for the purpose of collecting data and finding out what happened to the station Irid Novo. That's about as deep as I was able to tell: There's some cult stuff with Cosmic Gods but I never could find anything deeper than that.Gameplay, it's a Soulslike:  You start as a clean slate character with base stats, no classes to choose from. This gives you the freedom to create your character exactly how you want: Pump it in Strength and wield big weapons (what I did) or focus on occult things with Foresight and have access to unique tools.Healing and Energy (Mana) regenerates with melee attacks, kinda similar to Surge 2. It's still a good system and works well here.A neat thing is that various weapons can be passively upgraded just by using them: You start using a Demon Scythe and it's alright, but more you use it you can unlock unique passive and active abilities. Not all weapons have this, but a good number do.In addition, you can 'transfer' weapon upgrades between weapons. You put in condenser to increase the scaling of a certain stat, and then you can upgrade the condenser itself. Then, if you get a new weapon you want to try, you can, for free, yank out the condenser and place it in your new weapon. This makes trying out new weapons a breeze and is a great change, as Soulsborne games require you to upgrade new weapons from scratch if you want it on the level of your currently equipped one.One complaint about weapons: There's such a small variety. I'm a Strength build kinda guy, how I did my first run. However, I only found around four Strength weapons? All of which paling in comparison to my big greatsword that gave more Stamina, increased Strength scaling, and a run/dodge attack that hardcountered almost all the enemies in the game.  Think there's two Quality (Str/Dex) weapons. Total. Probably don't go that build.To build on that, there's duplicate loot. Near the start, I found an armor set that I couldn't use. That's fine, not expecting to use everything. Then, 30 minutes later, I found the same exact set! Why is there two? It makes finding loot, one of the most exciting things about Soulsborne exploration, feel lackluster. It's like finding Havel's set, then going to Archives and finding it again. Even some KEY items are duplicated!The UI is messy: Inventory cannot be sorted, meaning you have to dig through it every time you get something new (Even more of a pain with duplicates). If you want to break down materials (for crafting) or gear, you have to select the item, then confirm it with a different button, and then you are booted back to the main crafting menu. You have to break down every piece of gear individually. I tolerated the duplicate items because navigating the UI was just that annoying.There's a TON of secrets, some involving puzzles that you have to find clues for. I know I didn't come close to finding everything my first time. There's some really obscure stuff to figure out, which is really neat! What isn't so neat, are items required for progression hidden in super secrets.To access a new area to complete the game, you have to first find a hidden door (It's Dark Souls 2 rules: Interact button against doors). You access a hidden area, get some stuff and a crafting station. Did you know, though, that there's a SECOND hidden door in that hidden area that contains a key to a late game area containing one of the three big bosses you must fight? This kind of exploration should be for secret areas, items, or encounters, not for progression through the game.You are given no actual direction. "Go out and collect data" doesn't help when I'm wandering a hyper huge area looking for the one button, item, or trigger I happened to miss. Sure, being lost is part of the experience, but even Soulsborne games at least point you in a direction. 30-35% of my gameplay was just wandering around completely lost, fighting the same enemies. This is made worse by fast travel being a consumable item you use on Breaches, 'syncing' them to other Breaches you used the item on. This item is very rare, and of limited supply. Also requires knowledge of where best to use them for convenient travel.Enemy variety is extremely weak. There's some neat variations (especially later on) but even they get old fast. Get ready to fight the same zombies, fishes, and demons, especially when you get lost.Bosses range from absolute jokes to good to cheap as hell. There's a boss that 'poisons' you with radiation with a single hit. Not only do you take damage over time, your max health also starts to decrease. The chances you found the radiation cure item before this point is very unlikely. Another stuns you with a single stomp and then swipes at you before you can recover, likely cleaving your life bar in a single combo with you helpless to stop it.The final boss I fought, it's own arm blocked one of it's most powerful attacks, and I was out of range of it's melee, meaning it could only zap me with a weak beam as I just chopped it's arm. Another boss literally died in 4 hits. It's all over the place. There's good fights, of course, but the extremes really stand out.Finally, this game has a healthy amount of jank. Your character 'getting down' when they die, enemies getting stuck on terrain or flying at hyperspeed through walls, you getting stuck on invisible walls (fun when doing jumping puzzles), had a boss not move or react to me...There's a lot of weird stuff that happens here. It's a smaller studio, but man, the jank is hard to overlook.I missed a lot, and want to play again just to see if I can get another ending with a different build, or find some of the secrets I missed, and it will be better since I know my way around more, but I don't know. My playthrough was one of annoyance until I got my super sword, spammed Run/Dodge R2s (which pancakes 90% of the enemies and staggers bosses quickly) and found that key hidden behind two secret doors. Then I just didn't really feel much of anything. Some neat things at the end, but that's it.I don't think I can recommend Hellpoint for the $35 it's asking for. Unless you're really hungry for a new Soulsborne experience (And already played the heck out of the Cinders mod) and can tolerate/laugh at jank, I would recommend picking it up on a sale, if at all.Better than Lords of the Fallen, though. By multiple miles.(RE-EDIT: Experienced online, expressed views in the comments. Doesn't really change the overall tone of the review, sadly.)

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly I was pretty excited for another Sci-Fi  "Soulslike" game, but this one had been a disappointment for sure.  This game has some issues for me personally that make it entirely boring and annoying to play.  I think the controls are not responsive enough and are at the bare minimum needed for a game called "complete".  I think that the map designs overall are boring to look at and have the issue of all looking similar so no only is going through the world boring, it is far too easy to get lost or turned around.  I feel like a good portion of the early game bosses are either 2 extremes:  either way too easy with little thought put into how players would abuse them or way too unfair for early sections of the game.  I don't say too hard because in my opinion as soon as a boss is unfair its no longer "difficult" if that makes sense.    The bosses early in the game presented no challenge whatsoever when the environment they are in can be used to abuse them.Early in the game you get a way to choose which district of the station you go to, I haven't started over to pick a different district first to see if its possible, but if it is I think forcing a decision on where to go and not allowing back tracking at that early of a point in the game is a pretty poor game design.Overall game experience is just OK, with negatives on level design and exploration.  I don't know if bosses get better later, but it doesn't matter much if the game stops being fun before you reach that point.  Definitely not worth the 30 or so dollars I spent.  I think my biggest gripe is the overall game play experience so far for 30 dollars when Mortal Shell is coming out at the same price point, or lower, and is fundamentally better in every way from graphics, combat, and level design just from what I saw playing the demo.I would recommend for people to wait until its on sale later down the road.

name: Maneater
detailed_description: Wishlist Killing Floor 3! About the Game Become a MANEATER Experience the ultimate power fantasy as the apex predator of the seas - a terrifying SHARK! Maneater is a single player, open world action RPG (ShaRkPG) where YOU are the shark. Starting as a small shark pup you are tasked with surviving the harsh world while eating your way up the ecosystem. To do this you will explore a large and varied open world encountering diverse enemies - both human and wildlife. Find the right resources and you can grow and evolve far beyond what nature intended, allowing the player to tailor the shark to their play style. This is fortunate, because to get revenge on the cruel fisherman that dismembered you will take evolving into a massive shark, an apex predator of legends. Eat. Explore. Evolve. Unique Story Play through a full narrative, story-based campaign narrated by Chris Parnell (Rick and Morty, Saturday Night Live, 30 Rock) and set against the backdrop of a reality TV show. Diverse, Compelling Combat Battle fierce wildlife including other apex predators or fight against various types of human hunters ranging from town drunks all the way up to the Coast Guard. Evolve Into a Legend Feed on humans and wildlife to grow your shark, and find shark loot to evolve your shark down multiple possible paths. Explore the Gulf 7 large regions including bayous of the gulf coast, resort beaches, industrial docks, the open ocean and more. Experience a living world with a full day/night cycle.

Not bad, but kinda ruins the "shark feeling".Overall I would really recommend this game if you can pick it up on a sale somewhere. Keep in mind the game has some serious performance drops once in a while which quite annoying!overall a 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: Let's get out of the way first: this game is far superior thant SoT. It has a revenge story that hooks you, upgrades, evolutions, side tasks, etc. Maybe SoT has all of that (except for upgrades, I know that for a fact), but this is simply better. Not as AC4, but better. ♥♥♥ off Carlos, give me back my 50 dollars mfer.Now, after the previous totally correct statement, I will flex a little about my PC specs:- Motherboard B760M DS3H- 48GB DDR5 5600MHz- RTX 4070 Super- Intel Core i9-14900F - XPG Core Reactor 850W - MSI MAG CORELIQUID E360Now, I know there's better builds than this, but I should suffice the needs of a 2020 game. Well, I had to reopen this game because of crashes about 40 times in all my playthrough. Some tutorials suggest updating drivers, lowering CPU priority, windowed mode, lower graphics (which is a total waste of modern GPU capabilities) and whatnot. My most efficient method to solve this was to restart my PC after all the previous failed, only to happen again about 15 minutes in. This happened to me when doing human missions and using the tail to get several of them at a time. Also, the most frustrating ones where when trying to access the DLC, as I felt I lost my money for some unreal engine misuse, which fortunately I could solve.So, the thing is unoptimized for some of the most basic quests. All and all, I have such a blast with the game, that's why I'm giving a positive review.I have to say that it's more appealing at the start, when you're but a pup feeling like a god aftear defeating your first alligator just by mere frames. After that, I have to admit that it becomes a little too repetitive, and the fact that you can kill a whale only with your tail is ridiculously hilarious, for good or for bad.Me personally I like achievements sometimes even more than the games themselves, that's why I got the DLC even after reading the reviews, but yes, it's repetitive, the final boss is just a little bit harder than the main story final boss and the decision to throw all mutated enemies at once seemed like an excuse to justify the short length of "new" content. The atomic evolution set is inferior to the electric and shadow ones, so I'd say just get base game and buy the DLC on discount if you have curiosity for it, I did that.So, in summary, Carlos smd.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely simple and gory fun. Like the in-air tilt of the shark is opposite of the camera controls and I could never get it right. I also had issues with the in-combat status never going away, I had to quit the game and restart to rid of whatever fish was trying to hunt me across the map probably.

_childDocuments_.review: A fairly humorous yet exciting "collect-athon" that reminded me of classics such as Feeding Frenzy. It isn't perfect, but the flaws can be easily disregarded.Click  to see my other Reviews or follow my  for more recommendations.The thing I didn't expect from Maneater, was for it to be presented like some kind of fishing show you'd watch on TV, ala Deadliest Catch. To top it off, the narrator is funny and there's a lot of small references and originality scattered all throughout the early stages. Especially enjoyed the Lovecraft references.There is a lack of polish, however, as I ran into bugs and frame-drops/stutter during the entire playthrough. Some animations (not limited to your shark, but everything), are very janky. In a few instances I got stuck in geometries and was forced to quit and load. The mouse in my UI wouldn't always be able to click on the things I hover over. Near the end of the game the narrator started skipping sentences or just cutting them short. Audios overlapped, and it was a mess in cutscenes. Restarting seemed to fix this, also. To top it off, there were periodical crashes, especially when alt-tabbing.The gameplay itself was fun. It took a lot of adjusting and getting used to, but it soon became simple, although aerial controls are quite a mess and I hated doing it. The best way to grow quickly was to collect POI's and caches - with this method I found leveling up to be fun, instead of grindy. There's a decent amount of mutations/parts, but not all seem very useful.I love the fact that eating animations don't slow you down or prevent you from acting, and there's some neat indicators for things, such as the red cables leading to the grotto, or orange corals marking exits and such. Unfortunately they don't have any indicators to track stuff such as stacks of poison or other effects, and fast travel is horrible because it keeps telling you you're in "combat" - and by the time you're out of it, you've already gotten to your destination by "fin" (heh, get it?).It feels like there's a huge hole in the variety of edible critters. It's really unfortunate they didn't add anything like large crabs or lobsters on the sea floor to change things up. Perhaps some rare jellyfish as well, and big birds like pelicans, or even seagulls, as edible creatures on land/bridges. With such minor additions it would've truly brought the game to life.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Maneater is one of the most unique games you will likely ever play. Playing as a shark and going on a rampage while levelling up your abilities and finding secrets is tremendous fun. However, it sadly does not last, and there is little replay value aside from starting again on a higher difficulty. I did 100% of the achievements in 9.5 hours in the primary mode and 4.5 hours in the DLC. Based on this I think it is too expensive for what it is. 29.99 for the base game is reasonable, and 9.99 for the DLC is also acceptable. Get it on sale if you want it. Also the CEO is undeniably based. Garden tools mad because they need to have some personal responsibility for their actions. Shame on Tripwire for caving to the woke mob.Full Review:For me, one of the most unexpected parts of the game was the attention to detail the developers paid to getting all the information on the sea life you encounter in the game. When you combine it with the announcer, give you a play-by-play of whatever you are doing, be it eating everything in sight, fighting one of the apex bosses or just swimming along taking in the scenery, it makes quite the combination. Maneater is one of the most unique and enjoyable experiences I have ever had as a gamer. The visuals are vivid and crisp, and the combat is fluid and well designed. The quests are unique, named in very humorous ways and fun all around. I would recommend allowing players to lock on when tail whipping to destroy the towers in the DLC and putting options so players can adjust the HUD clutter. You can get very cluttered with all the sea life around you in the underwater biosphere, and when you are looking for hidden objectives, it can be hard sometimes.My main complaint is that Maneater is just too short for the price. I completed 100% of the game in 15 hours, with no new game+ or any incentive to go back and do it again. I hope the developers come out with more DLC as it is a great and enjoyable game, but I can't help but feel that it is a wasted opportunity.I give this game an 8/10. You may not go through Maneater more than once, but if you get it on sale, you will not feel bitter about it. It is a gratifying, fun and unique game like no other.

_childDocuments_.review: Didn't think I would enjoy it as much as I did.Menus are good and easy to understand at a glance. I do have to point this out because certain games just lack any UI/UX creativity and simplicity.Graphically, it's in tune with about what you'd expect. The graphics are obviously not ultra "realistic", but it's good.Gameplay is basic but fun. Obviously no shark is going to go around on a man-eating rampage like the one you play as in this game, but I think they brought some touches of "this is what sharks actually do" with the tail whip and a sort of echo location.The evolution mechanic is pretty great and adds a sense of progression. Over time as you do different tasks, you unlock different types of parts that you can interchangeably evolve on your shark at any time you want by visiting a grotto. You can also level up these parts which will also change aesthetic the higher you get.Overall, pretty good fun. I hope they add more content to the game at some point, because it is pretty short considering the price.

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked the hungry shark mobile games, you'll love this one. Fantastic story, plenty of gore, beautiful aquascape. There are a few problems though. Firstly, the game crashes a LOT. Fortunately it seems to save basically right up to the last minute, *so far* I haven't lost any major progress. Secondly, the "bosses" are a little too easy to beat. The alligators are more difficult than the shark hunters, even as an adult. All you have to do is target the "big hunter," bite em, drag em below, then hide from the others and you've just defeated a boss. Maybe it becomes substantially more difficult after the first half but I think I've been killed one time during a boss fight, and that's because an alligator got me below the surface. Otherwise, I do love the game. I actually felt super sad (no spoilers) in the beginning and I love that it gives you a good reason to go on a killing spree. Overall, the problems do not negate the fact that this game is fantastic. I do love it, it's unique in that you play as the villain with a good purpose, yet get to have unbridled fun being said villain.
