_childDocuments_.review: By all rights, I should hate this game. I'm one of those people who has a grudge against Jaws for what it did to the public image of sharks. This game is in that same vein - you are a shark and you are violently hungry and angry at all times, murder humans for fun, and never stop eating, but honestly? I can't hate it. The game doesn't take itself seriously enough. There's enough distance between what this shark is and what an actual shark does that I'm okay with leaping out of the water and over a bridge to consume the human on it. I'm okay with grabbing a turtle and tail whipping it into a sperm whale's face because honestly, screw the both of them. I love the character of Scaly Pete. Not because he's particularly deep, but he is interesting. And also hilarious. And for all that wackiness there, there is even some depth. At the end of the game, the narrator says there's "something to be learned here", but then cuts himself off because it's "just a show about people killing sharks, and sharks killing people." But he's not wrong! Man Eater is a game about the cycle of violence and revenge. Both Scaly Pete and The Bull Shark (who I have affectionately named Shania because MAN she eats all the humans) lost their parents to the Port Clovis Man-Shark War, and they’re both literally scarred by it. It’s really interesting to me that everything bad that happens to Pete is his own fault. He loses his hand because he just has to mutilate a newborn shark - something he only did because he was trying to avenge his dad. He loses his leg, his son and gets half his body exploded because he then needs to get revenge for losing his hand. He then dies because he wants to get revenge for the loss of his son. At any point, Pete could have stopped and saved himself more grief.But that’s the rub, isn’t it? He can’t. He’s a shark hunter, through and through, born into this life and more than happy to die in it. It’s almost a classic tragedy in that way. Had it been anyone else, none of this might have happened. But he can’t. So the cycle continues.As for Shania, she’s a hoot to play. At first I didn’t think she had much of a personality, and in the same way that Samus Aran or Gordon Freeman don’t, she doesn’t. But that doesn’t mean she’s an empty blank slate. Assuming all the missions you do are things that Shania is interested in doing, she too is focused only on vengeance. An entire category of her missions are called “Revenge”! And a lot of the revenge missions don’t target random humans, they specifically target places Pete likes to visit or deal with. She wants to take everything from Pete, and then kill him. But she’s also a shark, so she’s interested in defining her territory - the entirety of Port Clovis. Her slaughter of the Apexes is something she does to set herself up as the Apex. But then you get things like the license plates, and it seems like she has hobbies. Maybe that’s why she lives at the end? Shania has something to live for, Pete doesn’t. Or, maybe, it’s just a silly action game about a shark going ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ because that’s fun. And on that level, it DEFINITELY succeeds. The controls are ever so slightly wonky - mostly in regards to trying to fight near the surface when you suddenly start knifing when you certainly DO NOT WANT TO - but I don’t entirely know how to fix that? I feel like having a button specifically to enter knifing would be even clunkier. I also would’ve liked a lock-on mechanic instead of a focus-threat mechanic. Also, jumping out of the water is…weird. I never really figured out how to get Shania to go where I wanted her to when getting air, which became especially frustrating in the time trials. Lastly, other people have told me they felt the game got samey towards the end, and I can definitely see why. A good example is the bounties. Fighting boat after boat after boat after boat to then fight a bigger boat can get really boring. I avoided this by diversifying my activities. Instead of leaving the bounties for the end, for instance, I’d work my way up to the next bounty boss while clearing the Revenge mission, and then take them on roughly every time I cleared an area, letting me do other things in between to keep things interesting. Pace your playthrough and you’ll be fine.FINAL ASSESSMENT: If you’ve ever wanted to play GTA, except you’re a shark violently mauling people in an attempt to seek revenge, then play this game. If you want a fun, over-the-top action game, then play this game. The high points way, WAY out pace the few lows. The only reason I can see people who like action games not liking this is that they think it’s too crazy. But then, if you feel that way, why are you here?

_childDocuments_.review: Peter Benchley, author of Jaws, spent much of his life campaigning for the protection of sharks. His book, and the subsequent film adaptation, changed the public perception of sharks so wildly that it led to mass hunting. In fact, shark attacks are incredibly rare, and deadly ones almost never happen. 2019 saw an estimated 140 worldwide human/shark interactions according to research conducted by the Florida Museum, less than 100 of those were unprovoked and most resulted in no injuries at all. More injuries are caused each year by staplers. The point is, sharks aren’t anywhere near as dangerous as you might think, but Maneater isn’t a realistic game so none of that matters and you can have plenty of fun chomping on humans.The premise of Tripwire Interactive’s latest title can be pretty much summed up in the simple phrase “♥♥♥♥ you, I’m a shark”. It doesn’t come up in the game, but it’s the ethos behind the game. You start out as a cute little shark pup, and through eating lots and lots of fish and random seabed junk, you grow up to be a bigger and bigger shark with more skills and plenty of over-the-top enhancements like echolocation, electric teeth, and the ability to jump higher than Kriss Kross and Van Halen combined. The developer describes the title as a “ShARkPG”, and it delivers on that promise. This isn’t just a chaos-causing sandbox like Goat Simulator or Untitled Goose Game, but a full-fledged open world adventure with a storyline, missions and a detailed levelling system. The aforementioned enhancements are earnable through gameplay and changeable depending on your tastes, meaning you can customise your shark to your particular playstyle. You are the daughter of a shark killed by “Scaly Pete”, who is a legendary shark hunter. Your task, in the long run, is to defeat Pete, but along the way, you’ll be eating basically anything that fits in your mouth in order to level up and collect nutrients to spend on upgrades. The game also throws nutrient caches liberally around the seabed, which give further boosts to spend on making yourself the most powerful fish to grace the ocean. There are various sections of ocean you can unlock as you progress through the game. Usually these are kept shut with gates that you need to reach a certain level to be able to bash open with your tail. Each area contains different fauna to swallow, as well as various quests, usually surrounding the consumption of either fish or people. There are often “boss” type quests with larger predators such as Mako or Alligators to go after. In addition there are 10 landmarks such as statues or shipwrecks to visit in each section. There’s certainly a huge amount of content to see, and completing it gets you ever closer to the final showdown with Pete. There’s an air of cartoon-esque horror in Maneater, but at the same time, there are some gruesomely realistic moments. When you grab a human from a boat and drag them under water, they often continue screaming below the surface, making distressing gurgling sounds along the way. I felt bad for finding this to be amusing, and there’s a reasonable chance that you will as well. I don’t think there’s any shame in it, just keep reminding yourself that they’re not real people. Also, a lot of the time, the people you will be eating are shark hunters anyway, so they kind of deserve it. Visually, it’s a nice but not amazing game. Graphics are solid, but not groundbreaking. Some of the underwater vistas are lovely, though I wish little bits of my shark didn’t keep clipping into them every now and then. It’s not a gamebreaker, but don’t expect to be wowed by the visuals. The style is realistic but with some exaggeration such as with ridiculous amounts of bleeding from anything you attack (even empty boats for some reason).Combat is a little bit repetitive after a while, with most fights just being a case of evading an attack from an enemy, chomping on them for a bit, then repeating. You might also nip away to eat a fish to get health back in the meantime. It’s still good fun to partake in, but don’t expect to find a huge amount of tactical depth. It’s more about brute force than elegance, and this wouldn’t be so surprising if it wasn’t for the fact that the initial gameplay turned out to be a lot more involved than first expected. You can rush through the main missions in about ten hours too, but there are enough side missions to keep you occupied for a while.There’s a danger with this type of game that the novelty factor becomes more important than the gameplay itself. My time with Maneater showed that the developer was clearly aware of this danger, and did their best to avoid it. With no multiplayer and a relatively short campaign, it could be said that there’s not enough time for it to overstay its welcome, but nonetheless, I do feel that enough was done to avoid the problem of the novelty wearing off. Overall, it was good fun to play and exceeded my initial expectations for the game, and my only criticism would be that I wanted to rule the sea for just a little bit longer.8Maneater (Reviewed on Windows) This game is great, with minimal or no negatives.With more in the game than the concept might suggest, this is a fun to play title and exceeded my initial expectations of how the game would be. It’s a little short and I would have liked more of it, but this is definitely worth picking up.SummaryOUR VERDICTManeater is a fiendishly original concept that just about lives up to expectations when it’s focused on chomping humans. However, its formulaic open-world design and repetitive mechanics don’t sustain for a deeply satisfying experience. You’ll still enjoy having your fill but it won’t be long before you depart for new waters.PROSGreat varied and gory visualsAttacking and eating humans is a devilish good timeEntertaining narrationA few absurdly fun abilitiesCONSMissions quickly get repetitiveArbitrary progression systemUnderwhelming underwater combatPlease give me award

_childDocuments_.review: Maneater. A game developed and published by Tripwire Interactive.Over the course of millions of years since the age of dinosaurs, there is one fact in the animal kingdom. That the greatest killing machines of the world, need no improvement. The Crocodile and the Shark being the most prominent creatures of this fact. Which leads us to this, Maneater, a game where you take control of a bull shark pup and begin the process of growing her, and evolving her until she is the epitome of destructive capability. You start the game as a fully grown Bull shark, and you will control this until you learn the controls and subsequently begin the "story" where your mother is killed and you are left to fend for yourself and seek vengeance for her death. A fairly standard revenge story, where you continue to get stronger until you finally face off against the ones who wronged you except this time you're a shark. The game taking place in Port Clovis, a fairly diverse biosphere of varying flaura and fauna. Long story short here though is that there really isn't a story, and definitely not enough to pay attention to, It earns a five which is about the borderline between horrible and okay. As you can imagine in a game like this (If you can imagine it at all!) the movement has to be fairly on point, as it'll be the major mechanic for you to traverse this world at all and there really isn't another mode of transport to use. Thankfully Maneater pulls this off extremely well and in a fairly seemless and fluid manner. There are a few short comings in this department mainly relating to speed as the map is quite large and even at maximum evolution the Bull shark isn't very fast at all. I think a major aspect with any game like this, is the biome diversity as it can make or break the game as a whole. Half the fun is exploration and finding new biomes that you haven't seen before or wouldn't have experienced or thought you'd experience. Maneater sufficiently provides enough sustainability here that you can get to the end of the campaign without running out of things to experience. The map isn't amongst the best maps i've ever seen, but it does make navigating the game ALOT easier. Clearly the shark doesn't have a map in it's pocket but the developers obviously chose ease of navigation over realism in this regard, the map helps find objectives in the world, paths to use and also gives you important information about the development of each biome as the game progresses. Not to be confused with customisation and Evolutions which i discuss a little later on in this review, i really liked the premise of starting off as a pup shark and growing older, learning from the enemies i've fought and growing stronger with mutagens and evolving my shark. I wish this premise was expanded upon though,which i touch on later as mentioned above. And now we've stepped into the negative points. The quests, oh dear god the quests!!! If you really want to call them that. Maneater does so much of its base concept so exceptionally well, and then completely goes numb on the pulse of keeping the game interesting, The quests essentially boil down to the fundamental, You go here, eat a few of these and you're done, rinse and repeat possibly 7 to 10 times per biome, and eventually face the "Apex Predator" of the zone which is essentially just another quest where you fight a slightly higher level version of the same threats you've faced in the zone already. Extremely disappointing as the options here could have been phenomenal. In a game where the sole premise is to evolve your shark to astronomical levels, you would imagine or in the very least hope for a Baskin Robbins array of choices, flavours and options. Where in sad reality the games maximum amount of mutations/evolutions and customisations sits around 25 or 26. This is extremely sad, and really broke my heart as a player hoping for more, Not even the capability to choose colours of your shark or skin patterns. The bosses are lackluster to say the least, they are extremely simplistic in their design and their diversity, They all have some sort of weapon they shoot at you with varying basically from pistols in the early stages to shotguns, assault rifles and some kind of basic missile launcher, they don't do anything particularly special, and realistically by the time you've evolved as much as possible, they won't cause you any issues anymore in the slightest. I honestly don't know what the intention here was, truly. Because it almost seems like games like Carmageddon back from the early 2000's did a far better job creating a fearing civilian AI. The human AI here is stupid, incapable of anything but screaming and huddling down into a ball as a giant shark comes bounding toward them, the wildlife aren't much better, seemingly swapping between bite attacks and tail swat attacks to throw you off guard which is extremely easy to learn as every single enemy does the same combo and has the same tells for what is coming. If you're willing to grind for achievements you might spend at most 20 hours in this game. 20 hours for at full price a $57 game....The hours don't equate well to me and probably won't to you. I wish there was more to do, more to explore but once you've finished the story and maximised your evolutions as much as you care to, thats about all the game will offer you unfortunately.Maneater is far from the best looking game on the market, and i think it was made that way specifically to take away from the severity of the subject matter, too much realism and viscera in a game of this calibre would be hard to push over the line for most viewers. However, the game does still make you stop occasionally and absorb the atmosphere of the environment you're in, the days cycling into afternoon and night is pretty stunning and the overall underwater effects of this game is fairly sensational, There were very minimal graphical issues here such as tearing or glitching. And i sat a fairly comfortable 60 FPS throughout the entire game on my system (See profile for specs).Much akin to the visuals, the audio doesn't take itself too seriously which is good due to again the subject matter here. The bright poppy sounds help elevate the experience as well as a fairly atmospheric ambience to help keep you in the feeling of being underwater, the sound of waves crashing and tides rippling around is really quite stunning, There really isn't a soundtrack here though and doesn't really have much music at all, there are the occasional bursts of music when you activate some abilities to make you feel powerful, very DOOM-esque but otherwise focusing much more on the atmosphere here.I waited a long time for this game, and sitting here now upon it's completion i can't quite comprehend why, I guess i was  hoping for something more along the lines of Hungry Shark, a mobile game that i truly adore to its exploration, its vibrant world, its intense boss fights and its replayability. However i was given a fairly bland interpretation of it. That's not to say this game is bad, but its extremely short and feels like its missing a lot of what could make truly astounding. More evolutions, more growth, More exploration could all lift this game to a truly amazing standard. In its current state though, its hardly worth its full price, and its not worth much more than a 50% discount. Hopefully with time this game is given the love it deserves from the developers to add what is missing and to make it what it should have been all along. "Welcome to Port Clovis."

_childDocuments_.review: It's a generally amusing game but you really have to buy it at the right price. 12 hours is enough to 100% the whole thing, so keep that in mind when you consider what price you want to buy it. This might last you a chill weekend or a week at most. I really wouldn't consider buying this until it's under 15 bucks, and absolutely don't buy it until it's on sale at minimum.It's an RPG, but a bare bones one. You have 3 builds (chosen via armor sets) basically and a couple options for powers like echolocation or damage resistance, etc. You have to eat creatures for resources (there's 4 max) and just doing the side content is enough to get you most of what you need for the entire game.The story is goofy, which is to be expected, and the mock "Deadliest Catch" style keeps it entertaining.Few minor criticisms - the random dialogue is fairly repetitive, and this includes the narrator. t's noticeable but not terribly annoying. The jumping mechanic is really janky, which becomes annoying the handful of times you're asked to use them. It frequently doesn't do what you want, either leading to a really shallow jump, or a back flip. Coupled with a camera flip when this happens, and you might be able to land where you want, but then accidentally jump back in the water because of the camera lock.Buy it for cheap, play it over a couple days, then go back to playing something more substantial.

_childDocuments_.review: "Maneater" is a unique action RPG where you play as a shark on a quest for revenge. The game shines with its open-world exploration, where you can swim freely, hunt, and evolve, gradually transforming from a small pup to a terrifying apex predator. The mix of dark humor and brutal gameplay makes it engaging, though the missions can feel repetitive.The DLC, Truth Quest, adds new areas, mutations, and tougher enemies, expanding the storyline with a conspiracy twist. While the added content is enjoyable, it doesn't drastically change the core gameplay. Overall, it's a fun, tongue-in-cheek experience for those who want a break from traditional RPGs.

_childDocuments_.review: Maneater only eats your time.There isn't one.  You play as a baby shark that swims around eating things and growing until some credits role.  Then you do it again.The game involves swimming around and mashing the bite button on one to twelve creatures, then swimming somewhere else and doing that again.  This is the entire game.  There is a basic dodge button, a mostly useless tail whip move, and a small pile of body upgrade and evolutions that somewhat change how the shark kills things. _childDocuments_.review: I purchased this on sale after a brain numbing night class, hoping to tune out. Perfect choice. If you're looking for a unique game to zone out, mash some buttons and have a good time with, I can't do much better than suggest Maneater. Growing and evolving is the core of the fun but even finding all the landmarks is rewarding due to all the humor and pop culture references they hide (IT, Rick & Morty, the banana stand from Arrested Development, Spongebob, Pacific Rim etc etc). Evolving to the point you can fly through the air like a rocket or breathe and bounce along land is great fun. Chris Parnell does so much amusing voicework, he's kind of an unsung hero for this title. He really ties the package together well. The level design is interesting, each area is different than the others; from the deep ocean to the bayou, to a Palm Springs style ritzy neighborhood. The areas are full of interesting things every where you look, so traveling never gets old. Level design is also considerate, there are locks you can open later in the game to make travel to earlier areas easier. Grottos are easy to find thanks to the neon lights that lead into them. Underwater caverns which had the potential to be disorienting have a familiar orange light around entrances and exits to rooms. The only thing I would say is it is short and sweet. I'm glad I waited for a sale because you are going to get roughly 10-15 hours until you have 100% the game. I wouldn't blame anyone for buying it at full retail bc its a good experience, but the cost/playtime math isnt as favorable currently. I would happily pay the 40% discount I got, for 40% more playtime. I wish there was an endgame difficulty to unlock. I cant wait for the DLC in August though!

_childDocuments_.review: Basically you play a shark and eat things, grow evolve into some horrific monster. It is funny at points, but the problem is well you're a shark. The problem there is that because its open world you can't progress until you've completed specific story missions. Which means to progress the story you'll be told "Kill 10 baracuda" except it has to be in a specific area, but there's not really a reason why except because that's what the mission says. You go to new locations because of the same thing and just yeah there's some decent laughs, but its hard not to feel the game forcing the matter when your objective marker goes "Right go 2000 meters that way to swim by the story's over arching antagonist without him knowing you're there in an area you've never been before."The grind is just rough.

_childDocuments_.review: Maneater is an open-world action-RPG (ShaRkPG) where YOU are the shark. Starting as a small bull shark pup you are tasked with surviving the harsh world while eating your way up the ecosystem to become the ultimate apex predator. Eat. Explore. Evolve.As you explore the large open world locations you will be faced with some of the harshest predators known to man from small muskellung to enormous sperm whales, and it’s not just limited to the creatures of the sea being a threat, you will also have to face off against 10 of the toughest hunters to really crown yourself king of the sea. As you chew your way to being the fiercest predator you will need to find and collect all the right resources to be able to defy nature by growing and evolving far beyond the average shark. Each evolution types tailors to all types of players being able to mix and match to create the ultimate beast. All these perks are to get revenge on a cruel fisherman that goes by the name of “Scaly Pete” which killed your mother and left you with a nasty slash to remember him by; revenge is a dish best served cold and it’s never been sweeter.When controlling your shark it really makes you feel like you are the ultimate predator, grabbing small fish in your giant teeth absolutely tearing them apart with one bite to special moves like breaching out of the water spraying your victim’s blood all over the ocean. One of the abilities you have access to is the “Sonar” which is used to track both prey and collectable items throughout your searching allowing you to see who is, and isn’t a threat nearby allowing you to avoid possible bad encounters with larger species early on before you’ve had the ability to evolve and conquer all. The collectible items include POI’s (Points of Interest), Nutrition Chests and Licence Plates. Some of these collectibles aren’t easy to get to and do require you to be at a certain level to reach them. But don’t worry, you can go back to any area of the game you’ve been to at any time. Everything you do, collect and eat all goes towards your XP bar, so it’s worth collecting everything.There’s also 3 incredibly large doors operated from a switch at the very top making it near impossible to get through but with the ability of grabbing larger prey you can hold and precisely launch them in any direction you want with the force of your caudal fin whipping into the victim. With each evolution (Bio Electric, Bone & Shadow) they all have their own perks to help in different situations.I have found that when encountering boats/hunters the bone evolution is best due to its course body and brute force it provides allowing you to strike right through some vessels at an alarming rate, whereas the shadow evolution makes for more of a swift getaway after mutilating your prey at the bottom of the sea. Of course as mentioned earlier, you can mix and match these abilities to whatever best suits your play style.Maneater is a really good looking game and Tripwire have done an amazing job. The crisp look of the creatures and atmosphere really makes it feel like YOU are the shark. The deep scar that was left from Scaly Pete really gives it character and reminds you of how much you want that revenge. Whilst rummaging through the swampy type areas, the murky waters surrounding you keeps you on edge from the aggressive alligators that lurk close by, though making for an easy escape from the hunters once you start adding to your infamy rank. Each area you reach and unlock is far different from the one you just came from, with one section being the waters.This was one fantastic game taking me around 13 hours to complete to 100%. While it is a single player based game, I think there is plenty of opportunity to open it up to an open world multiplayer or at least a 4 player private lobby style as once completing Maneater there is a substantially large area not used that could incorporate a multiplayer section to take out numerous apex predators with levels that are far beyond you alone to take out and require a group to take them down. Players could then be rewarded with prizes for your efforts such as a whole new style of evolution for your shark.The only downside I have found with this game is that once completed there is no incentive to play again. As sad as that is, Maneater is everything and more that I have been looking for in a single player story, it grabs my attention and wouldn’t let me go until it was complete. I grinded hard for the 13 hours and I even completed it twice because I ran into a glitch that stopped me from acquiring 100% on my first save.Overall, Maneater is a game like no other and I would 100% recommend to anyone, I got so lost in the scenery and evolution once I completed the campaign I would often find myself just rampaging at the bottom of the gulf trying to take on multiple high level threats at once proving that I am the ultimate apex predator.

_childDocuments_.review: This games premise is pretty simple, a power fantasy from the point of view of a shark. For the majority of the game I really enjoyed the collecting and gameplay loop, the only places that it hung up with me was the Truth Quest missions where you had to strike the antenna with objects or people, which I ended up cheesing with the shadow tail whip or atomic tail whip. The core game was what I expected for the price, and I thoroughly enjoyed a lot of the grinding for materials. The DLC felt a little lackluster in many regards, a lot of the best upgrades were cool, but came into the game so late that they weren't very useful, there's also so much more the developers could have done with it.Bottom line, if you're like me, and want a reasonably short time-sink, this is a really fun game with a pretty fun loop, but you could pass on the DLC if you really don't feel like it, the dlc area is fairly small anyways.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're big on marine conservation, this is a satisfying way to take out your rage against humanity while also enjoying some 'tongue and cheek' humor about the said atrocities of humanity. Pros:gorgeous game, smooth animations.Fun narration and humor.combat is relatively fluid (although it can be a bit nausea inducing)Cons: Game play can feel a little monotonous and grind-y at times, especially if you're big on 100%-ing.If you are prone to get motion sick, be aware this game will possibly cause that. The chomp n' thrash for controller can get a little  repetitive motion injury, who is she?The game kept crashing on me during loading sequences; nothing I could fix on my end.
_childDocuments_.name: Maneater

_childDocuments_.review: What a day to become a shark!If you like the idea of munching on people and smacking turtles with your tail this game is for you! The game feels slow at the beginning but it really ramps up the tension when predators come to play, requiring you to either grind your levels on optional stuff or having enough skill to take the biggest creature in that area. The environments are beautiful and expansive, rewarding the player in exploration. I highly recommend this game to anyone who likes the idea of becoming a shark and eating pretty much everything.
_childDocuments_.name: Maneater

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a lot of fun and does capture what I imagine it might be like being a shark. People swimming look like clunky wooden puppets, barely moving, as you glide effortlessly through the water- no wonder we get bitten sometimes, it's just too easy. Hunter Boats and divers are easily evaded in the depths. Everything ends up being your prey. At the beginning, an encounter with an Alligator is challenging, and by the end you're eating them for a snack. The environments are great, with plenty of exploring to do and secret places to find, the upgrade mutations are fun and I enjoyed the random commentary from Chris Parnell. I played through the DLC too and enjoyed it, I dare say I will play it again.
_childDocuments_.name: Maneater

_childDocuments_.review: A game born in the wrong generation, but a fun ride all the same. Simple, gory fun. Spent like 15ish hours on the base game, and 5ish on truth quest. The game has a 'this is a TV show' gimmick that doesn't get cringe but is a little misplaced. There's some message about environmentalism that gets lost in all the zany ironic humor. There are some great lines, though, and some good deliveries by the narrator. Dont go in for the story and dont expect a 10/10 experience. Go in for eating people, upgrading your giant shark, and watching your shark gradually become an anti-boat killing machine, and you'll have a pretty great time. Good stuff.
_childDocuments_.name: Maneater

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game to just shut your brain off and de-stress with. The basic gameplay loop is not complicated. I didn't need to look at a WIKI once on this game. The story is engaging and entertaining, though the game is very short. 14 hours of play, and I have just about 100% it.Gameplay wise, this is what I thought Depth played like, though I have never experienced it, with a little bit of Feed And Grow Fish thrown into the mix. As for RPG mechanics, I came into it the combat expecting a challenge, like Dark Souls or Monster Hunter, where if you don't time you dodges correctly, you will be greeted with a death screen. What I got, however, was much more forgiving. The combat portion can be solved with "dodge if they are bigger than you, thrash if they are not."As for experience and leveling, "XP" is broken down into 4 different resources you use to level up your abilities. Every resource is used to level your shark, which leads to some level cheesing very, very early on.All in all, I would highly recommend this for anyone looking for a casual game to unwind with.

_childDocuments_.review: Maneater + its Truth Quest DLC was a fun and enjoyable ride. The game's essentially a giant weird open world rpg shark simulator game with lots of dark/cruel humor. You play as a shark out for the revenge, trying to find the man who killed your mother. While doing so you'll level up, unlock new abilities n upgrades to you stats and your shark's appearance. There's a ton of mild boss fights in this game (I don't know if any boss in Maneater can really be considered a boss except the one at the end of the base game and at the end of the DLC). The difficulty scale for this game is like a 3/10. I think I died a total of maybe 5 times at best? It's all rather easy. The only difficult part about the game is playing around the dreadful auto targeting system that decides who you attack. The atuo targeting system is fine for the most part, but when you need to attack a very specific target in a group of 20 targets then good luck hitting the right one! The base game never gets too, it's as if JAWS was a video game but it's also a comedy instead of horro/thriller. Truth Quest (the DLC) takes the game in a much better direction, here they don't hold back and the enemies and storyline gets way too crazy for anyone to believe. This is what the base game should've done too. Overall the story's alright, it's just humor mostly, the combat's okay at best, the rpg elements are neat and the game looks beautiful. I'd recommend Maneater to anyone who just wants a chill time without a challenge. Oh yeah and the collectables in this game are nearly impossible to miss. Overall it's a 6/10 game, nothing too special but not a bad at all! only slightly above average. If it wasn't for the auto targeting system I'd give it 8/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Maneater

_childDocuments_.review: Janky but fun shark power fantasy. Climbing the food chain and becoming able to devour the predators that gave you trouble before is the core of the game, and it feels very satisfying. The game can feel grindy (there isn't all that much a shark can do, between eating things, fighting things, and finding collectibles) but as long as you find the core gameplay loop fun, it'll keep you entertained. The DLC is fairly short (~3 hours) but has a ton of fun mutations, and takes the power escalation to ridiculous, over the top levels. Definitely worth it if you enjoy the power fantasy.

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyable, but extremely short and very repetitive.Overall it's a nice, easy-going game, the narration is very good, it looks pretty, sounds decent, but there isn't much to do.The main quest is about 5 hours, and in my 15 hours I completed both the base game and the DLC to 100%, and it's not like I was speedrunning it or wanted to get it over with. Even on current 50% sale that's 25.63 euros for 15 hours of gameplay.There is no difficulty setting, very easy overall. The only difficult fight I had in the game was going against a lvl 8 enemy right at the beginning when I was lvl 2-3. But soon after that nothing can stop you. The DLC does provide some challenge, but again: not much.The evolutions (special parts that you can add to your shark) are fine, but since there's no difficulty they're not relevant enough. They're nothing mindblowing either. The problem is that your main damage is your bite against most enemies, and you get that right at the beginning. This means that besides small increases to your bite damage, damage resistance or movement speed, you won't really get anything exciting or useful.Nothing even close to what you experience in Evolve or Prototype. In fact if you like this evolution thing and killing stuff in open world, then you're better off with Prototype.. they're probably cheaper as well.The 3 kinds of quests in the game are eat 10 fish of a certain kind at a certain locations, eat 10 humans at a certain location, and kill some enemies at a certain location. And you're in water mostly, so while the environment looks nice, mechanically it's irrelevant, you're always just fighting in water.Again, everything in the game is at least decent, but there isn't much in there.

_childDocuments_.review: Not a bad game, not great either. Worth it on sale, not full price.+Boss fights are fun and everything feels smooth playing. +Had a single crash on my play through. Cutscenes aren't bad and the basic story is fine. Game obviously isn't really about the story though so it's limited.-Missions are very repetitive. Besides the select few story missions, most things you'll just repeat throughout the game-100% completion within 10 hours for me (Didn't get DLC)-Movement and especially being on land or jumping out of the water is clunky and sometimes unpredictable.

_childDocuments_.review: This game did something for me that few games do nowadays, perhaps because I'm a gamer of older generation: it kept me hooked until I did every single trophy, around the 23 hours mark.I have to be honest: I loved the game! I really did. I was a pup shark, which kept growing into this behemoth of the sea, the one and only true apex predator, the Mega Shark! The original game is really well done, graphics are beautiful and the game ran smooth as butter on my r7 5700x,  RTX 3070, 32 gigs of RAM. You get a lot of activities, which you do, uncovering the areas and leveling up, and of course, ALWAYS eating every creature unfortunate enough to run across your path. The main villain is also really well done.Than... there's the DLC. I just don't know about that, I'm afraid. They added more of the same, however the main villain is now a generic NWO organization and the new things they added, consisting of time trials, crushing towers, looking for tinfoil head men, just feel out of place. I don't believe time trials, which demand of you to do some quite hard jumps, are something most people would enjoy. The last boss isn't as much hard as it is annoying, especially in phase 2, where he calls all other DLC bosses, which you have already beaten, to his aid. SO yes, I recommend buying this game, absolutely, just keep in mind that the DLC is hardly an improvement.

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: I am not a native english speaker so mistakes are bound to happen, not just that, but I'm lazy and I got the ADHD thingy so yeah, I sometimes don't care enough to correct my mistakes. That being said, let's get started: Pros:-Fun Power Fantasy-Goofy Story for inbetween gameplay-Has Eastereggs to other Tripwire games (such as Killing Floor)-Easy to play, especially with controllerCons:-Short-Not soo serious-gameplay gets a bit boring over time-Weird level designI got this game ages ago in my Humble Monthly and installed it on my Steam Deck to play it occasionally and then went to finish it.On the deck it works pretty good, even with medium graphics, the controls are good and reactive, so I also played it on PC with a controller.The game doesn't really take itself serious, starts kinda as a documentary and becomes a conspiracy theory simulator, but it's humor - not strong - hit me several times. I did enjoy it. The Story follows a shark, whose mother was killed by someone that this sharks grandpa has killed. It's a revenge fantasy just as shark, no morale, just crunch. Visually speaking the game has quite some diverse landscape and it really doesn't hurt the game. The gameplay mechanics are also pretty decent, feel good and you can - tho limited - customize your shark to your playstyle and it's pretty good. The music, however, was not really too good and after a short time I deactivated it. Besides the main Story you have side objectives where you have to find containers, number plates and attack beaches and ships or other predators to level and continue further into the story. It was easy to complete, however to 100% the game on steam, you need to buy the DLC. I bought it for 5€ and it was okay. It extended the gameplay loop but really did not add significantly anything, besides  a higher max level and some better upgrades for the shark. Oh and a new bossfight.So overall if you get it for cheap, it is a great experience, I don't know what full price is, and I am too lazy to check but no need to buy the DLC, the base game is enough.

This is the best bad game I've played, I 100%'ed the game and mostly enjoyed it but I just like being a shark. The gameplay is SUPER shallow, controls are pretty mediocre, the story is horrible, the missions are recycled at every single section of the map, and the DLC is kinda just more of the same but more grind. The best part of the game (aside from the main gimmick of "Me Shark Me Bite") is the narrator. The commentary is pretty great and the DLC in particular has some funny commentary on conspiracy nuts. If you want to chomp people and chomp fish a lot like I did this game will satisfy that itch, but I cannot say this is a good game.
_childDocuments_.name: Maneater

_childDocuments_.review: I had fun.... but.....I have very mixed feelings after 100% completion of the base game and DLC.It took 13.2 hours to complete everything the game and DLC have to offer. For me this is an extremely short amount of time, as I tend to take the scenic path in games. I didn't follow any guides, and to me this just showed a lack of gameplay.Sure, the game was enjoyable and both the storyline and narration were always funny. However controls were clunky (keyboard and mouse) and the lack of depth in gameplay really sank in about half way into the experience. There is a rinse and repeat cycle of 4 or 5 different tasks in each area of the map, and other than evolving your shark which is admittedly satisfying thats it... Nothing else to the gameplay at all...The reason I am leaving a negative review despite having fun playing the game was that it was just too expensive for the lack of gamplay available. Even having bought it on sale I feel a little ripped off. This game feels like wasted potential. It looked amazing, and was very fun but was lacking overall.
_childDocuments_.name: Maneater

_childDocuments_.review: Just.... What?I was expecting a fun and short romp through the world as a shark not an action RPG. Why do I have to dodge attacks from enemies? Why do I have to grind through level locked areas? I'd rather just go play the old IOS shark games. They got to the carnage quick and weren't bogged down by silly gameplay mechanics that don't really work.
_childDocuments_.name: Maneater

_childDocuments_.review: The game including the DLC is about 12 hours long; I've got 100% on most areas and spend around that time in the game. The game is alot of fun, but it gets very repetitive. New area - Collect stuff - Kill stuff - Kill Apex predator - move on.The shark customization is limited (Up to 5 sets with the DLC). The higher your infamy rank, the more fun and difficult it becomes.I recommend it, but beware that you'll be doing the same stuff over and over and over.The DLC is fun, but the same collecting from the main game comes back. The DLC shark set is amazing aswell.
_childDocuments_.name: Maneater

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just okay. I bought it on sale because I really wanted to play it and like it, but the game mechanics leave a lot left to be desired. Too many times I found myself getting stuck somewhere. The auto-surfacing/jumping really got annoying throughout the game. The inconsistency with wiggling forward, jumping, and lunging. The game doesn't do a whole lot so it's tough to excuse. The story was non-existent for me. I didn't play it for the story, but I initially tried to at least pay attention to it but by the end I was just skipping it. The RPG elements are alright, though there really isn't a lot of variety. I pretty much used one set the whole game.All in all, it's a fun experience if you think you'd like the game and it's on sale, but I would not buy it at full price. If you're going into this thinking "RPG" you should dial back your expectations because it's barely that. At the time of this review I've 100% the achievements for the main game and DLC so there really isn't a lot of replayability for this game and it's easy to 100%.
_childDocuments_.name: Maneater

_childDocuments_.review: The game itself is pretty fun, and I was able to get 100% completion of the main game. Didn't buy the DLC.The biggest problem was the random crashing. Sometimes within a minute of loading in, usually about 30 minutes of game play before a crash, and sometimes as long as over an hour before crashing. I can count on one hand the number of times I chose to exit the game, vs the ~50 times it crashed during my playthrough.
_childDocuments_.name: Maneater

_childDocuments_.review: This was a really fun game, albeit a bit repetitive, until the frame drop kicked in. It got worse the longer I played. Lowering all settings did not help. The fps got worse and worse until I just could not put up with, and I am willing to put up with a lot of jank in games. The poor optimization of this game is inexcusable.
_childDocuments_.name: Maneater

_childDocuments_.review: I'm seriously not feeling it. I don't think I've given up a game I'm otherwise interested in so quickly.But it is just extremely repetitive, a bit boring, and honestly quite unfunny. And I'm not even two hours in...The controls feel thoughtless.I prefer most games with a controller, so I tried with that first, and I hate it. Generally the buttons are assigned well, but the extremely repetitive biting is wearing me out. It wouldn't be so bad if the combat was more varied, but since 95% of your time is just spamming RT/R2, it's pure suffering.So, I switched to a mouse. And the incessant clicking is a lot better than trigger presses, so no issue there. The problem is with everything else. No button feels deliberate. I have trouble finding the "rhythm". And I'm also annoyed by the buttons in the menu: any game that only accepts Enter/Return - which is a right-hand key - for certain actions get put on my ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ immediately. Why? I don't understand...I don't feel like I'm doing what I'm supposed to.Take the "sprint" for example. The game tells you what button does what, but you have no idea how anything works. It doesn't teach you anything. The problem is that nothing feels natural.I think what's happening is when I starts dashing, I get really fast, and then gradually slow down over 30 seconds. And so, it'd be ideal to re-sprint each 15 secs. But that didn't feel right either.Not to mention that sometimes, I'm unnaturally fast, and other times there's barely a difference between when I'm pressing it and not.And one more (big) complaint: I'm pretty sure vertical travel (without the "dodge" buttons) is only possible when holding down sprint. But again, I'm not sure. And the game definitely didn't tell me if that's the case.All this game did for me is appreciate how well other games (like Subnautca) are doing 4DoF, or even 6DoF movement.
_childDocuments_.name: Maneater

_childDocuments_.review: It's pretty fun, for the first few hours. The objectives start to feel like chores because it's the same thing over and over again. I'd recommend it while it's on sale. The DLC is worse. Again it's fun for a little bit, but quickly becomes a serious grind, and there isn't enough content between the base game and DLC to justify the full price All in all I put in about 16 hours to 100% the base game and DLC and so SO much of it was just repetitive grind. I can't see the replayability value unfortunately either. . If you like sharks though, like really love them. You'll have fun just stalking the reef for a bit like I did.
_childDocuments_.name: Maneater

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start by saying this game is not going to make you feel like it's the greatest most awesome thing ever to be created. It's a shark game where the mechanics feel slightly off for no good reason. If you ever played Tony Hawk and remember the feel when your trying to do some board tricks and it just feels a bit off. Same thing. Cool being a shark but executing the motions does not always work right. Also the game feels like it was rushed. Bosses and abilities don't feel like they were designed with a proper game flow. However the game is fun to explore. Lots of hidden items to find and the general creative structure feels good. Almost a bad game but it's passable ... slight time killer. I'd try this if your REALLY bored.
_childDocuments_.name: Maneater

_childDocuments_.review: A fun concept and some good writing and voice acting, but the core gameplay is unpolished and frequently frustrating.The hardest enemy in the game by far is the camera, everything that I attack responds by swimming beside or behind me, and spinning to be able to lock target over and over gets old.The big thing was that the game doesn't really tell you how to do anything from mid game onward, from not explaining chained jumps to not telling you how to open gates (bite another predator, jump, and tailwhip to throw - absolutely not intuitive either), to all the license plates require jumps that seem insane until you go on youtube and see how easy they are, none of that is clearly shown or explained in-game.The narrator lines include some surprisingly good jokes, but they repeat far too often with a relatively small number of possible lines, and the story is surprisingly good for a mayhem simulator, but the frustration in the core game coupled with the tedium and grind of the DLC make this a "wait for the next big sale" title.
_childDocuments_.name: Maneater

_childDocuments_.review: (Oh here she comes)Watch out boy she'll chew you up(Oh here she comes)She's a maneater.The game is decent for what it is, probably not worth the asking price.Try to buy it on sale, because the playtime is on the shorter side, and even though it was fun, it also started to become repetitive in the end.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun, fast paced exploration/collectibles game with perk/upgrade progression where you play as a customizable shark and kill everything on sight. I picked this up on sale, and recommend others to do so as well if they are unsure they'd enjoy it. While buildcrafting my shark and unlocking new perks was enjoyable, there ended up not being too many of these to choose from, even counting the ones added from the expansion, Truth Quest. The maps are quite beautiful and detailed, and cool landmarks and references are strewn about, making exploration easily one of the highlights of the game, though the presence of invisible walls blocking off sections of the city, and the lack of an option to disable antialiasing detracted from the freedom of movement and visual fidelity aspects for me. Honestly what kept me going probably was the movement tech and high apm potential in combat. And playing as a shark. Although, I wish there was just a bit more depth to combat other than bite/tailwhip/evo ability/sonar. As for replayability, I see myself coming back now and then if I'm bored to try doing stupid ♥♥♥♥ or take screenies, perhaps more if there is an update or new expansion.The story was really meh, the missions were repetitive and uninspired, and there was so much unfulfilled potential. But...Pretty cool game--pretty much what I expected, plus a bit.

_childDocuments_.review: Everything this game does Jaws unleashed (released in 2006 on PS2 and Xbox) did better.  I'd like to say they at least upgraded the graphics, but the setting is a swamp.  A heavily polluted disgusting looking swamp.  The gameplay is grindy because there's very little content.  I spent an hour unlocking a skin.  That's it.  Swam around and ate random things passing by and occasionally killed some marked fish and alligators.  That's all the early game has to offer.  This game makes me want to go see if my ps2 still works so i can play a real shark game.
_childDocuments_.name: Maneater

_childDocuments_.review: Maneater is a wonderful Sharkventure.It is so good in fact that after beating the game on Epic Games I decided to buy it on Steam to do 100%.After 25 hours I now finished everything the game has to offer and it was a blast.The Game has some flaws however:- Underwater Combat can be sometimes confusing due to fast camera and the softlock on enemies- Sometimes crashes because of U4- Presentation can be lacking sometimes or feels unfinished- The developement and story felt kinda rushed could've been a longer journey imo- some DLC late game ships are kinda unfun to fight against What it does really great:- Beautiful underwater locations (except the Gulf, was a bit too foggy)- Sound design, especially the transition betweeen being under water/on land is great and feels immersive- Sonar makes the collectibles actually fun to collect and a part of the game instead of just being a unnecessary addition- The speed challenges, Bosses and Humor in the DLC was great and a lot of fun- A lot of ways to "build" your shark which is insanely funWhat I hope to change for a possible Maneater 2:- The Nemesis system from Shadow of War would be perfect in this game and could be implemented for Shark Hunters and Underwater bosses, could improve the sometimes rushed character development and adds infinite replayability- some more factors regarding the horror you bring upon humans like a scare scale or something to give more ability to immerse as a maneating shark- More possibilites for modifying your shark (coloring etc.)I would recommend this game to anyone who has fun developing and upgrading your character and anyone who likes to feel absolutely OP.8/10

_childDocuments_.review: I will HAPPILY change my recommendation on this game, once a fatal flaw is corrected/removed.I honestly REALLY enjoy this game.  I think it is well thought out, well designed, has solid graphics, interacts/reacts well with what you do as the shark.BUT - I keep having repeated, and consistent, freezing issues when the apex foes appear.  This is a game breaking flaw.  You cannot progress the story without fighting and beating these foes.  As such, I have done everything else in the game up to this point....and am now stuck.I have reported it to the designers, I have tried every work around I have found and read about.  Nothing is working.So until such time that this game-wrecking flaw is corrected, I cannot recommend playing a game that I will never be able to complete.IF they correct this flaw, I will absolutely revise this review - and recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: There is an old game called "Jaws Unleashed" and chances are, you are thinking about buying this game because of it. If you liked that game and how it allowed you to destroy ships, eat and dismember people and sea life and allowed you to upgrade your shark and gain new moves / skills then you will like Maneater, and will find it does many things better than Jaws Unleashed.The game plays as this: You start as a baby bullshark and eat / destroy your way up to becoming an elder. The game world is split into areas with different settings that has different types of sea life. You have collectables, bosses and sidequests to keep you busy in each area. The more you kill people the more you get infamous and shark hunters start looking for you. There are ten infamy stages which spawns a boss hunter when you hit it. Killing each hunter grants you a new upgrade for your shark.Some keypoints I want to mention:- The map is split into sections and each section has a boss battle with the "apex predator" of the area such as an irradiated barracuda or a great big whale with many spears and wounds on its body (basically Moby ♥♥♥♥). When these bosses show up there is supposed to be a cutscene introducing them with their name presented after a freeze frame effect like Borderlands. This never worked for me. Everytime the name popped up but the game softlocked and I had to go back to the menu and try again. It seems to work after the first time, no big deal for me but the issue is there. - The game is pretty unrealistic and doesn't take itself very seriously, in fact the whole game is about a show called "Maneater" with a man called Scaly Pete hunting sharks and you, a bullshark, find yourself forced to star in it. There is a campy show narrator that has things to say to your actions and you can make your shark spit poison, attack with electrical shocks and do double or even triple jumps in the air. With that said, the tone isn't overly wacky. The narrator doesn't speak after your every action and the jokes aren't that bad. The graphics also has a cartoony style, especially on humans, mentioning this because screenshots doesn't really reflect that.- This isn't an overly long game, I finished it 100% after 10 hours and I took my time messing around too. Not a bad thing in my opinion, it ends when it just starts to get a bit boring.- The animal variety is okay but isn't anything special. Most of the fish you encounter are tiny and not very interesting. There are one, maximum two new animals for each section and many of them are nothing special. You mostly deal with barracudas, groupers, catfish, muskies, seals, swordfishes and other sharks with sperm whales and orcas at the final area. There are no dolphins, squids, octopuses, elephant or leopard seals, walruses, narwhals, manta rays, whale sharks the list goes on.- It's an easy game, there are some sections that might give you a hard time, especially in the beginning where your shark hasn't got very good stats but generally you have to make an effort to die in Maneater. I died four or five times and everytime it was battling hunters.And that's about it, if you liked Jaws Unleashed or simply want to wreck havoc controlling a shark, buy this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Maneater

_childDocuments_.review: Do y'all remember Jaws Unleashed, and how awesome that game was?? Well, Maneater might be its true successor! It has the same feel, but updated graphics. It is a TON of fun! ( However, you may want to check your specs first before buying. Yeah, it only requires 8 GB of RAM, but it will use up EVERY. SINGLE. BYTE of that requirement. I am not joking. I would recommend getting a RAM upgrade FIRST if NECESSARY.) 9.3/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Maneater

_childDocuments_.review: I'll be honest I had my eyes on this game for some time, though, I waited until the Steam release as I'm currently not too keen on the Epic Store. However, I think the wait was worth it. I did get this from the last Humble Bundle Choice. I was quite stoked to see this game in the Choice rotation.Maneater is a game where you're a shark and you do shark things. You start as a pup, then the more you consume and collect things around the world, the more you evolve. You have 30 levels to progress. (You do get higher levels and an extra Evolution slot at Level 35 with DLC Quest) You have special traits that can be Passive, or to be Aggressive.Maneater is one of those rare good games we see where you play as an aquatic creature, this reminds me of Jaws Unleashed, which I still have a physical copy of for Playstation 2. I felt like there may be inspired by that game. Maybe, maybe not. Either way, it was a positive for me and I do love aquatic creatures, this was enjoyable to play. It was fun enough I 100% the game, which is rare for me. I completed everything in 16.5 Hours. I still have the DLC Quest to complete with that. So in terms of content, you got a fair amount.Mentioning of content, this game narrates you (Though I could say the narration does get repetitive but isn't a big deal for me.) But the game has cliche humor, pop culture references, memes. Honestly, I loved it, all of it. It even got crazier with the DLC Quest. I will say thank you devs for the chuckles, there were some things I did not expect to hear from this game. The story is pretty fair, I mean, honestly, I was just looking into being a shark and eating people and stuff...but the story is a generic or parody of some sort of Shark Week documentary. To put it simply, if you're expecting anything serious from this game...look away.Shark Designs are pretty cool, loved the locations that were featured. To Swamps. Toxic Dumps, Golf Courses, and the Gulf itself. Locations were pretty distinct to seeing new types of fishes, enemies, Killer Whales, Blue Whales, etc.Overall for $40 full price, I think it's fair, though, for the DLC I would suggest a sale. I don't believe it's worth the full price. But you can get both Base game and DLC on sale. But overall, if you're linking into a casual game with no serious stuff, I can recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Maneater

The collections/quests/combat are very repetitive. I wish they put as many resources into gameplay as they did production value. Overall a pretty average forgettable game.

_childDocuments_.review: 30 minutes in and so far the game is good. Similar to Jaws Unleashed, the game has more content and storyline, therefore making it more fun than Jaws. Being underwater and play as a shark is no brainer because you work your way up in the food chain. _childDocuments_.name: Maneater

_childDocuments_.review: Maneater was a game I desperately waited for and anticipated but sadly I just can't recommend it. On paper its a solid idea that sounds genuinely fun and at first I did find it quite enjoyable but an hour in I knew that this game was NOT worth the 40 dollars its priced at, thankfully I didn't spend no where close to that thanks to Humble Bundle but still if you spent the 40 or 20 dollars on this game you would feel a little betrayed. For a game that has an "open" world it doesn't have much on offer that keeps it interesting. Yes there's collectibles but they add very little value outside of one of them offering special upgrades that more or less don't feel worth it. I spent 10 dollars on the Truth Quest expansion which does add some more enjoyment thanks to a new evolution for your shark but besides that it again relies on the same formula of go from point A to point B, I mean honestly I felt like I was led on a leash most of the time. The one thing I really commend however is the inclusion of Chris Parnell as a narrator because anytime I here him speak all I can imagine is either Jerry from Rick and Morty or Cyril Figgis from Archer but not even his inclusion makes what feels like a mid-tier experience any better.
_childDocuments_.name: Maneater

_childDocuments_.review: The game does a very good job of making you feel weak and scared to confident and finally simply like the Apex that runs the water. It has a great feel to it.Pros:- The story is good- Chris Parnell's narration is great- Combat is fun- Good enemy diversity and challenge at times- The development of the shark is actually awesome, though you get OP very fast even if you gimp yourself to basic build.Cons:- Game drags with some repetitive tasks to unlock new areas which are not fun (eating people, finding chests, etc) and I feel like if this was just purely 100% optional it would be fine, but you need to do some of it to unlock areas which is annoying.- Build options are a bit limited- Infamy mechanic could be better. It would have been better if it was less enemies and more challenge per enemy, as right now I felt like I was breaking my keyboard mashing dodge and attack to clobber ♥♥♥♥ to death over and over.Overall, this is a great game. You can clear main campaign in 10-12 hours and expansion in 4-5 hours. If you have a fear of water or sea creatures, this is a good game to get over it, or at least try.
_childDocuments_.name: Maneater

_childDocuments_.review: Maneater is fine, $40 is just overpriced. You can finish the main story in 5 hours and complete almost every achievement in hours, that means total game play should be around 10 hours. Though repetitive task wouldn't be boring that much on the fist run, there is definitely no replayability. Should wait for the sale or go Game Pass.You might think human is your main villain, most of time you fight sea creatures such as a crocodile or some aggressive fishes. The difficulty is easy, and you have few ways to attack them so the combat is pretty simple and repetitive.The map is open world like. There is over 5 sea areas and you can unlock each area step by step, each area has unique color and city vibes, those are relaxing and enjoy to explore.The mission is problematic. Basically to unlock each main/boss mission, you have to finish bunch of same quests like "killing some fish" or "eat human". The enemies attack patters are very similar including bosses that makes you bored after defeating a few of them. Other quests are collecting items/signs that give you few rewards and no fun. The combat and missions are not great though, this game is very fast paced that you can level up quickly and beat enemies and finish quests so easily. You would have no regret if the price was low, so wait for the sale if you interested.
_childDocuments_.name: Maneater

And it wasnt too much of a big deal. Still it was a bit of a bummer.despite all that i still recomend!

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: If you like violence simple games, buy this.I didn't think I would enjoy this game this much; I had seen it on sale a number of times and deliberately passed it by. The game play is fairly simple, and while its goals/missions are repetitive, it's repetitive in a way that still feels very satisfying. There is a simple story that's still engaging enough to be interesting. I particularly like that the whole thing is  set as a reality TV show, and the social commentary and easter eggs you run into are fantastic.I picked it up for half price. Sometimes the thing bites back. It isn't compelling. The game is narrated by Chris Parnell, which is fun right up until the point where it becomes grating and repetitive.
_childDocuments_.name: Maneater

_childDocuments_.review: Whenever I would hear someone talking about Maneater it always left me with the impression that it was a trashy satire game with little enjoyment to be had as a "real" game. As it turns out, this isn't the case at all. Maneater is absolutely a satire game don't get me wrong, but it's unironically really fun and holds my attention for hours too. The camera and lock-on system could use some work, and it's not very long, but if you just want something simple and fun to sink your teeth into (ha) for a day or two and then uninstall, you could do far worse than Maneater. Highly recommended, especially on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Its just fun to play as a shark: attacking things at random and eat whatever you want. The different parts you could equip were probably the best part to me, putting on all parts of a set makes you feel invincible.The humor (mostly from the narrator) borders on cringey (especially in the DLC), story is fun but not much to it, and not much post-game unless you wanna do the Infamy stuff. The game play gets repetitive after a while too. Verdict is it's good, just wish there was more. Wait till it's on sale to get it. Same with the DLC.

_childDocuments_.review: Craziest monster power-trip game since... I guess Prototype?  In both games, your start out weak but lethal, but by endgame, you're damn-near unstoppable.  It's a blast to play, and I highly recommend it for anyone that's wanted to take a swim in a shark's scales.Pros: Beautiful underwater world, even the parts blighted by humanity and it's disregard for the ocean.  Underwater enemies are surprisingly challenging.  Playing as The Shark is fun as hell.Cons: Sometimes wonky aiming of The Shark for attacks, human enemy AI could use a tweak or three (dumb as a bag of hammers, outside the Boss Hunters).

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome game, just don't buy the DLC.Let's get this off my chest right away: This game has blood. Not drops, not even pools, but oceans full of blood :DIf you can't live with this violence, this is not your game.So, the pros: Open-world. Not a very big world, but a nice one. Different areas have different vibes. And different difficulty levels, but the game won't stop you from advancing if you'd like to wander off. Only limitation is that you have to hit "Teen" level to get out of the first zone. And you're free from there.Cons about the world: World of the ocean is... underwhelming. No octopi, no strange eels or anything. You have aligators and fish. And that's it. (and cetaceans, but those also kinda look like fish... )I liked the game controls... not the battles every time but i general it's good. It's fun to swim around.Also the collectibles are fun, especially the signpost-things.Graphics and also good. Game looks nice. No weird glitches most of the time.Bad stuff: a bit repetitive. The story (which is actually kinda deep and good) only covers about 5% of the gameplay. Mostly you kill 10 X and cosume 15 Y...Humor: Top 10. Especially the miillion little mentions of other pop-cultural stuff.(the 3 shells and the toilet thing... that's an ooold one :D ) Bad stuff: The DLC: Don't activate it. If you have it, skip it. It's insanely bad.
_childDocuments_.name: Maneater

_childDocuments_.review: This is an absolutely fabulous game. I cannot recommend it enough, if its on sale, if its not maybe read further.Maneater has you running around as a bullshark with sharp control and excellent fluidity. I never felt like someone playing a shark, I was the shark and had full control. Its visuals are colourful and vibrant from the murky bayou to the sparkling white beaches. Having old mate Chris Parnell as the narrator will keep your ears engaged with his crisp and clear dialogue. For me the only problem this game has is that there is not enough to do, and too much of the same stuff repeating. Don't get me wrong, the collectables were fun and there weren't too many you see early on and have to go back for later but especially the locations. you go there, you find it, thats it. you don't really get to interact with them or have a funny thing happen, they just are places to go and get the tick for. There is also a period in the very late game where you need to get more upgrade points and you have to get on that grind of just eating that certain colour fish for them and that gets abit tiring. But don't let these cons make you hesitate on buying the game. it is still very much worth it and very enjoyable for a full days worth of fun
_childDocuments_.name: Maneater

_childDocuments_.review: Great fun, lots of enjoyment! Who doesn't want to be a monster of a shark and decimate all of humanity in a hunger fueled rampage? Unfortunately, it is quite short. _childDocuments_.review: I could not recommend this game enough. To start with, its pretty. _childDocuments_.review: Maneater: A brief reviewPossibly like many people out there, I came to this game to look for a "shark eating things" game for P.C, because Hungry Shark World was way too much fun than it should have been. Did it satisfy me?Graphically speaking, it's acceptable, but not something I would write home(or to other gamers) about. Think better than Assassin's Creed Black Flag, but less than A Plague Tale: Innocence. But it's well-defined, the objects are clearly realistic, and the shark itself is a marvel to look at. It's not bad to look at(the game), but not very impressive either.Surprisingly, this game has a story. And like the graphics, I'm not much impressed by it, but only by the fact that it has one. It's quite enjoyable, I think. It's like watching a horror-comedy film from the perspective of a shark.And not surprisingly, in this game, we play as a shark. Although different from Hungry Shark World, in which you progress and then jump on to the next shark, this game tied you to a specific one(hence the story mode). The game offers different customizations and abilities for your shark, and you also progress by leveling up your shark by consuming organic materials(although for a game titled "Maneater", eating a human is not that much fun; it's quite tedious). The game itself is a never-ending GTA-esque cathartic rampage, in which your trigger-happy-free shark swims through the water, jubilantly destroying/ consuming everything in its path(and is subjected to human punishment, as usual) while accompanied by the dry and transgressive comments by Nature television host. The swimming control is fun and easy to master, although the 360 degree angle camera is quite bad since it always trying to screw up your fight with superior prey or human watercraft).And if doing all these things aren't good enough, then I think just being able to prowl in the blue ocean's water as a shark like in an aquarium is definitely an experience to be had.Overall, "Maneater" is fun to play, and fun to immerse yourself in, but it's not perfect. It's good in a few aspects and quite lacking in several others. It's certainly a good shark game for consoles and P.C, although I think it's optimal to buy it on sale. What I want you to know is Shark game is quite a unique concept for a niche market, it's not a game for everyone since not everyone cares about sharks(while also a game for everyone at the same time due to its sheer stupidity and zany idea). If you think you like playing as a shark chomping things, go for it. I went for it and got what I wanted (a shark game). I like it and enjoy it. Certainly there is fun to be had.Also, I think this is definitely a holiday game since you could just sink into it for a good couple of hours and then forget about it until the next play.
