_childDocuments_.review: This game is the most fun i have had in ages! Been playing it 10 hours straight :kekw~2:  I'm a shark swimming around eating people in an epic adventure to avenge my beloved sharky mother Killed by shark hunter "Scaly Pete".The humor is very enjoyable and narrated in an Attenbouroughesque style by Chris Parnell (Jerry Smith from Rick and morty / Cyril Figgis from Archer). It's intense in combat and the power scaling feels ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ awesome with level ups, rank ups and Evolution body changes, I had to hide from crocodiles as a newborn shark, now when I return to my old spawning grounds as a mutated elder shark i gobble them up and barely even notice it
_childDocuments_.name: Maneater

_childDocuments_.review: The objective of the game is to go from little fish to big fish by eating other fish, humans and random junk. Grinding (killing things for currency), collecting and doing other repetitive things like kill x of x or kill the Apex predator (boss) is how you progress. You just swim, eat, collect and grow bigger. That's the whole game pretty much. Grind and repetition. The novelty of playing as a big, bad shark and eating humans wears of pretty quickly and you start off as a baby shark anyway so it takes a lot of time to get there in the first place. There's a story tacked on (avenging your mother or something) but again it's just travelling from area to area, killing things over and over again, getting bigger and stronger and then taking on more powerful foes until you finally avenge your mother I guess. The game has a habit of crashing randomly too. For the asking price of £33.99 I'd absolutely not recommend it lol! Graphics are pretty nice and there's some Killing Floor references which are a nice touch if you like that game. An alright time waster but with so many games to play and so little time who actually has time to waste? Not me.It would've been nice to play as other predators, more customisation and really just more to do apart from killing things and levelling up. May as well go back to playing World of Warcraft. More variety in the type of quests would be a good start.
_childDocuments_.name: Maneater

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could give a middle thumbs up. The game's okay, I did have my fun with it but there's too much grinding. Took me about 10 hours to finish the main game. The story is all over the place. Are we supposed to feel empathetic to the shark hunters that kill for fun? Shouldn't we just focus on killing rich people for ruining the environment? Aren't we supposed to be empathetic to the shark we play as and understand why it must kill humans? Put a little logic and depth to its motives from birth to adult life. It tries to set up the villain and make him empathetic but he's just a shark hunter that (again, just kills for fun) tries to find the shark that killed his father (and he never does).I adore sea life so exploring it was nice, but I wish there was more to do in the open waters. It's just barebone and finding collectibles. The busyness of it all is in the crammed beginning areas for some reason.Overall, okay game. Not really worth $40. Get it on sale. I have yet to try the DLC and I'm seeing that it's pretty mixed.
_childDocuments_.name: Maneater

_childDocuments_.review: Nice lite Action-RPG where you control a shark and make it evolve while wrecking havoc in the surrounding waters of a coastal city.Controls are great, you really get the weight and power of the shark increase, feeling like an untouchable king of the sea. Just a complain, the Trash system is a nice idea but shaking frenetically the right stick to shred your adversary into pieces is more destroying your gamepad into oblivion.Graphics are good and magnified by a nice art direction and level design, do not expect to be wowed it's just good.Sound design is great , you're really feel in immersion and I often found myself just chilling around listening to the song of a whale, or just biting human and to hear them scream their lungs, bubbling in excruciating pain.Overall, this game is pure dumb fun, one that must be consumed wisely though to avoid getting bored 'cause shark life seems to be filled with the same repetitive tasks.Hoping for a MEG dlc, I want to be a MEG.
_childDocuments_.name: Maneater

_childDocuments_.review: A spiritual successor to Jaws Unleashed. This would have fit in well with the PS2 and Xbox era of villain games like Destroy All Humans and Stubbs the Zombie. While it shares the same dark humor, over the top action and colorful settings as those games, it also features the same downsides. Such as repetitive game play, a shallow open world and short playtime. That being said it's a very enjoyable and unique game, definitely good for killing a weekend. The art style is beautifully grotesque and there's a surprisingly engaging and conflicting story being told. Chris Parnell is a great narrator.I'm actually hoping we see an expansion and sequel as there's a lot of good game play and world building to add on to. It could use some more enemy types, upgrades and cosmetic options. It is also a bit short ( I beat it in 8 hours. I wouldn't recommend it at the full $40 price, but It's one of the more enjoyable new IPs I've seen in a while.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros-Playing a shark - Getting to play a bloodthirsty shark bent on revenge.-Narrator - While you play your actions are narrated as if it is a nature documentary and I love it.-Size increase - As you kill and feed you visually increase in size and through enough feeding you reach different stages and increase your stats and you can reach new areas.-Visual upgrades - There are different evolutionary sets that not only change your appearance, but as you upgrade them they continue to change appearance though it isn’t scientifically accurate. -Rewarding exploration - Doing the side objectives and collectibles generally reward you with new mutations to get stronger.-Carnage - If sharks like this actually existed I would be fine living in a mountainous area. Cons-Too much land carnage - For a shark game you spend a lot of time hopping around on the ground munching people.-Repetitive gameplay - A lot of the gameplay is repetitive like the bounty hunters, most of them are pretty much identical until much later.-DLC advertising - After beating the game it plays a short mission for the dlc and asks you for money to play the new area. When a game advertises inside the game it is a bit annoying and immersion breaking.The game is worth a try and if you don’t mind the repetitive nature it is a fun and enjoyable experience.

_childDocuments_.review: "Maneater" promises an intriguing premise: embodying a shark and wreaking havoc in the waters sounds like a novel concept. However, the execution of this idea leaves much to be desired, drowning in a sea of technical flaws and repetitive gameplay.Let's start with the most glaring issue: the camera. It's like trying to wrestle an eel underwater. Constantly reorienting itself, particularly when near surfaces or locked onto targets, the camera becomes an adversary in its own right. This makes navigating the game world and engaging enemies an exercise in frustration rather than enjoyment.Controls don't fare much better, feeling sluggish and unresponsive. Combat, touted as a core mechanic, devolves into mindless button-mashing and sporadic dodging. Attacks lack impact and consistency, often resulting in either overpowered dominance or negligible damage, seemingly dependent on arbitrary factors like your shark's level or upgrades.Speaking of upgrades, while the concept of enhancing your shark with different organs and abilities is intriguing, its implementation falls flat. Many upgrades feel insignificant, merely boosting experience gains or minor stats, rather than significantly altering gameplay dynamics.Quest design doesn't fare much better, serving up a buffet of uninspired fetch quests and repetitive objectives. From mundane tasks like consuming a set number of fish to dispatching generic apex predators, the quests quickly devolve into a monotonous grind. The narrative, if it can be called that, is further weighed down by incessant and often grating narration that fails to add depth or humor to the experience.Technical issues plague "Maneater" as well, with frequent crashes and the need for compatibility mode just to run the game. These issues undercut any semblance of immersion or enjoyment, leaving players stranded in a sea of frustration.Despite these substantial flaws, "Maneater" isn't entirely without merit. The bold choice of premise deserves acknowledgment, offering a unique perspective rarely explored in gaming. However, novelty alone cannot salvage a game so heavily weighed down by its own shortcomings.In conclusion, "Maneater" swims in promising waters but ultimately sinks under the weight of its technical deficiencies, repetitive gameplay, and lackluster execution. For those intrigued by the idea of playing as a shark, it's best to approach with caution or perhaps wait for smoother seas in future updates or sequels.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good fun, but has lots of flaws too. The narrator's goofy enough not to make you feel awkard while slaughtering hundreds of innocents sea creatures and humans, the world's pretty beautiful and the story, which is mostly centered around your nemesis, is pretty captivating. But collecting things on hidden and hard to reach places isn't least bit fun, the controllers are pretty clunky when you have to jump to a high place (and you do that a lot), and the leveling goes too fast, making every enemy pretty underpowered halfway through.As for the DLC, well, they give you a taste at the end of the game, and that combined with its reviews are enough for me to call it a day after 100% the base game.Overall, I'll give it a 6,5/10. Playing as a shark is plenty fun, but it had many game mechanics I wish were not implemented.

_childDocuments_.review: Maneater is actually a social critique/commentary, about human intervention in wildlife and society’s  at solving the impending ecological crisis of our time. It’s all delivered tongue-in-cheek, though. It works mostly because the narration by Chris Parnell is pretty good by video game standards, but in general terms I’m not a huge fan of this approach. If I had to choose, I much prefer  (a game I have also reviewed) style messaging. I think it gives the weight these topics deserve their due gravity, but I don’t think Maneater’s is terrible, either. It’s comedic at times and it fits the tone the game is going for.The sequences with the antagonist, Scaly Pete, are actually pretty good in the first part of the game. His initial motivations aren’t exactly explained, and  doesn’t really match up with his early game characterization, but they are such a great break from the monotony of the  when you’re still not very fast or strong or capable. It’s a shame that there isn’t more substance to these cutscenes. They’re well done and awesome.It’s a shame the other characters have practically 0 defining features or moments. The hunters who come after you as your infamy/bounty level grows are introduced like they’re game-world established folks, but not only do they die as fast as they arrive, but they don’t even put up a fight in any real distinctive way, both in terms of difficulty or approach. There’s very little  about anything. The environments are gorgeous and diverse, as is everything in the game, visually, but from a gameplay perspective the game doesn’t really , which is a bit odd considering the basis of the game’s progression is you as a shark evolving and having adaptations to allow you to do different things. These adaptations hardly change the gameplay though, and the  fights, which pretty much serve as zone boss fights, don’t evolve much either.The final boss fight is unique among them and is actually good! But after 8ish hours of doing the same thing it’s a bit of a weird feeling in your mouth, like One thing that you absolutely never tire of though is  They are  cool. The leaps, the barrel rolls, the final hit animations, the people flailing in your jaws. They’re all elite, and the apex predator  are sick. This helps a lot in the mid-game when the missions becomes a major pushover. If you do any side-mission accomplishing at all you’re bound to out level the main story by a large margin, and things become a complete joke until pretty much the very end, when the game arbitrarily caps your level at something less than the last few major enemies.The music and sound are nothing really to write home about, but they’re not bad either.  For some this is perfectly fine, and for others it’s a disappointment. I am pretty much square between these two camps. However, I can’t say I’m not surprised this game has a  recommended rating on Steam. I  would not recommend this game for full price, both for the enjoyment and the length. It seems like the DLC adds some new ways to play and some additional length, which seems like it might be good, but it’s hard to think about shelling out more money for a game that is lacking on value in the first place. I may pull the trigger, though.Anyway, Maneater is fun. The visceral carnage is enough to keep your blood pumping and you engaged to get you through most if not all the game. But as much as I’m left with a smile at what a stupid and ridiculous slamfest this game is, I’m left with a twinge of disappointment for what it could have been if the devs had been more ambitious with the story building, mission typing, and creature expanding.If you wanna have fun playing as an all-powerful shark, I would still recommend  far more, even knowing it’s a game that has been  and is no longer receiving updates.

_childDocuments_.review: The Idea behind Maneater is absolutly solid.The World looks very pretty and areas are distinct.Sadly the game itself is absolutly lacking.The Leveling happens way to fast (got level capped in 3 hours) making the game itself laughable easy.The "Items" you can get are sadly way to few (though pretty)The Story is forgattableThe quests simply boild down to kill x amount of yalso there are some anyoing bugs that either crash the game altogether or softlock you (switching to main menu and then continue) that often happen with "boss" enemys(mostly reskinned enemies that become laughable easy because you overlevel to fast)All in all Maneater is a Solid shot fun game but at most worth 20€ if not less

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a lot of fun. The biggest flaw with it is simply that it doesn't take long to complete. I've played it for 15 hours as of this review and I have 100% completion in the entire map. There's lots to do, but you can do it quite quickly. Another of the reviews complained about the camera directing where you look and where you attack and while that is true, I don't think it takes away from the game. The combat can be a little dull when fighting creatures your size or bigger but that is made up for by how much you need to pay attention to your opponents moves so that you don't get hit by a heavy attack. TLDR Good game with lots to do, but can be completed quickly if you don't mill around doing nothing.
_childDocuments_.name: Maneater

_childDocuments_.review: It's if they were trying to copy Burnout Paradise in style, but you're a growing/evolving shark monster thing. Exploration is bland in general, there are landmarks to visit that are all parodies or references to other things, but they don't really add too much to the overall game. The navigation and combat on mouse & keyboard is weird but better than gamepad controls (for me). Combat is fairly repetitive, most of the time you clamp down on something and shake them until they're gone. Fighting with boats could have been more fun, but it's just 'there'. You have to flop around on land as well, which is a bit of variety, but it's only really to collect collectables, or have a feeding frenzy with beach goers. I got to the last boss, after multiple frustrating attempts, I decided it wasn't worth the annoyance to finish the game. Also, the DLC adds extremely overpowered evolutions that essentially make all other evolutions useless. Not recommended unless it's on sale for about $10.

_childDocuments_.review: I Think you should do some research before you purchase this. I have to give this one a thumbs down guys. I just cant recommend this game. I wont throw any more money at this or any other of your products if this is the way you all want to do business. Give your customers a finished product, Then ask them for more money when you have new content. I bought this game during the summer and I had a blast with it initially. The game play is fun and solid and you do indeed get to feel like a shark (granted it may be a shark on some kind of psychedelics). The collection aspect kind of feels lame though. _childDocuments_.review: While I did enjoy my time playing this game, I would probably say that was due to the fact that you get to play as a shark and you get to grow and eat larger fish like classic arcade games. The evolutions/mutations are interesting and provide some variety of gameplay, but overall you'll just be following a path to an objective with a world full of filler content (Consume 10 Sailors / Kill this Animal / Destroy this Ship).The saving grace of the game would be the narrator, but that's about the only thing that made me truly glad I kept playing a little longer. Although, once the prerecorded voice lines ran out it got old and I stopped playing after 100%ing it in around 30 hours. So maybe get it if you truly want to experience the old school "small fish grows to be the biggest fish and eats everything" kinda arcade games, but otherwise I can't recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Someone finally made a good shark game! I don't want this to turn into a back-handed compliment(this game will likely not melt your mind with glory),but this is a solid, open-world RPG. Collect stuff? Sure. Do ya gotta? Nah. The tourists spots are the only things you need to rope in their entirety to see all of the upgrades.          Doesn't take itself seriously and the voice work certainly reflects that(in a good way). You can stick to the story and burn your way through,as the devs seem to have a healthy respect for your time.         The jumping can get wonky,and the game did crash once,but only once,so the rest of it is more good than not.Pick it up and enjoy an underwater dogfight with a sperm whale.

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: ★★★★☆ (4/5)Maneater is a unique and delightfully absurd take on the action-adventure genre, and my 18.8-hour journey into its chaotic waters has been a mix of aquatic mayhem and offbeat humor.The game casts you as a ferocious and ever-evolving shark, driven by revenge against the menacing shark hunter, Scaly Pete. Your goal is to grow in size and power while exploring the open-world waters, feasting on unsuspecting prey, and occasionally terrorizing the human population.Maneater's most striking feature is its tongue-in-cheek narrative style, presented in a reality TV show format. A witty narrator provides humorous commentary throughout your aquatic adventures, offering quips and exaggerated tales that enhance the game's comedic charm. It's clear that Maneater doesn't take itself too seriously, and this lighthearted approach is a breath of fresh air.Gameplay revolves around exploration, combat, and progression. As you devour smaller sea creatures and humans, you gain experience points that allow you to evolve and unlock new abilities, such as improved stamina, electrified bites, or a tail whip attack. The game encourages experimentation with different abilities, which can lead to some absurd and hilarious encounters.Maneater's open world, set in the fictional Gulf Coast, offers a colorful and detailed underwater environment teeming with marine life. The exploration aspect is quite engaging, as you uncover hidden collectibles, caves, and various underwater locations. The game's world is surprisingly rich in detail, considering its unconventional premise.The combat system, while simple, is satisfying. Chomping your way through schools of fish, snatching humans from their boats, and battling other sea predators is a visceral experience. As you grow, the battles become increasingly epic, with you taking on everything from alligators to giant squids.While the game's quirky humor and unique premise are major selling points, it does have some downsides. The gameplay can become somewhat repetitive over extended playtime, and the camera can be a bit finicky, especially during intense battles. However, the occasional absurdity of these situations often serves to add to the game's comedic appeal.In conclusion, Maneater is an offbeat and enjoyable gaming experience that offers a fresh perspective on the action-adventure genre. Spending 18.8 hours exploring the game's absurd waters is a testament to its entertainment value. Its humorous narrative, chaotic gameplay, and vibrant underwater world make it an excellent choice for those looking for a break from the conventional. While it may have some minor shortcomings, Maneater's unique charm and comedic flair are sure to leave a lasting impression and a smile on your face.

_childDocuments_.review: Great power fantasy game where you play as a shark!This game does something new and lets you play as a shark that grows up and evolves as you make your way to the top of the food chain.There's a story in the style of a Shark-Hunter TV show, where the main antagonist is trying to hunt you down, and you want to get revenge on. The story is fine, but not the main focus.The game itself is on a big map that you keep unlocking more parts of by leveling up and doing missions and collecting things. Most actions you make are being narrated by a pretty entertaining narrator, as if you are being watched by a documentary film crew.The game also offers some shark upgrades that you will be able to equip and unequip at any time. These upgrades effect the visuals, speed, damage and defense of your shark. Most pieces are also part of a "set" that will provide extra bonuses when equipping multiple set pieces.Generally speaking, this game was a very fun experience. But I will say that the main thing that kept it fun was the satifying gameplay loop. Eating and destroying things is simply satisfying, and that's what keeps this game from becoming boring.However, the game does have a lot of the typical "open world pitfalls" that it could improve on.Don't get me wrong, I fully enjoyed this game. But a potential sequel would really need to add a lot more things in order to not become boring.Basically: If this wasn't a game where you play as a shark, but instead you'd be a soldier with a gun, it would pretty much be like a bad Far Cry clone. It would be another typical open world game filled with busywork.And most of the missions and collectibles are kind of busywork. And as I said, the satisfaction of destroying and eating things is what stops it from becoming boring. Since we haven't really had games like this before.The amount of equipable shark upgrade sets are somewhat on the low side at 3. 4 if you count the DLC.And as I just stated, most of the missions are just busy work, meaning copy-pasted missions of "kill this, kill that, destroy this, go here and kill that". Again, it only works because being a shark is very fun.I'd love to see a sequel, but it would really have to innovate on a lot of things.More indepth missions than "go kill this". And definitely a lot more possibilities for upgrades for the shark. It has the potential to become an in-depth shark RPG with new mechanics and playstyles.There's a lot of stats that get changed around with certain upgrades, and some passive upgrades also buff certain abilities and such. But it is very unclear what some stats directly effect. And there is no screen to see your total stats all added up for example. It doesn't matter that much, but it's definitely something that could be pointed out that could be improved on.The visuals of the sharks and their upgrades are beyond stunning, and make me excited for any potential future game that could be made with a ton more content.A sequel would be awesome, but really needs a lot more innovative improvements and more content and care.All big franchises thankfully started somewhere smaller scale, so here's hoping!

_childDocuments_.review: I like a good stupid game. Something with a simple silly premise, easy to get into gameplay, good length. Something to just sit down, play, enjoy and move on, maybe replaying it again a few years later. And Maneater turned out to be a pretty good example of a game like that. Less than 10 hours of simple gameplay loops of swimming and chomping fish and people, upgrading the shark to be more ridiculous and finding secrets.Maneater is an action adventure with light RPG elements set in a big open map that opens up bit by bit as you level up and progress through the story objectives. It’s extremely simple – you’re a killer shark, you swim, you eat, you gain levels and upgrade your abilities and you also mutate into more horrifying forms, gaining special abilities. The map is divided into several zones and each zone has several activities, like “eat x humans in y area” and some collectibles. Eating anything gets you resources that you use as upgrades and also levels you up. And that’s about it. It’s this simple gameplay loop that’s repeated over and over as you go to newer areas and get more ridiculous abilities.It’s fun as is. It would get boring if it lasted longer, but luckily it last just enough to be fun. It’s a bit grindy. It’s very stupid. The whole “cable TV show” style of the game, with a narrator commenting things that you do, isn’t as funny as the developers thought, but does have its moments. And did I mention that it’s fun?Even apart from its repetitive nature it has some weird issues. Controls are a bit off, sometimes the game can’t load areas seamlessly and gives a short loading screen, combat with more resistant enemies can become boring rather than challenging and the upgrades don’t go quite as ridiculous as I would’ve wished. The game is, in fact, surprisingly restrained in its stupidity, despite the premise.But it’s some good silly fun. A lot of people might not find the game to their liking or grow bored. Some might find it just a bit too stupid. But I enjoyed it. And if you like a bit of simple underwater exploration and a lot of shark chomping, give Maneater a try.

_childDocuments_.review: Maneater is a 2020 action role-playing game developed by Tripwire Interactive and co-published with Deep Silver. In Maneater, you play a female bull shark out to get revenge for your mother’s killers while exploring the open (sea) world and completing its various quests and hunt for collectibles.TL; DR – You play as an angry shark in an ocean open world and get to eat everything in your way. It’s loads of fun on top of having a keen eye for detail.Story (3/5): Played out from the perspective of a documentary, players assume the role of a female bull shark that was brutally separated from her mother at birth and now seeks revenge against the shark hunter responsible. Along the way, you will climb up the ranks ascending to greater levels of shark maturity and face tougher opponents. Cutscenes placed at the end of each chapter help to flesh out the story from the shark hunter’s perspective. Meanwhile, the game/documentary’s narration is provided in real-time by the excellent Chris Parnell.Gameplay (5/5): Maneater has a large sprawling open world map in the form of a large body of water with the occasional land dwelling. Transitioning between land and sea is surprisingly seamless. Role playing elements come in the form of “upgrading” your shark by way of mutations. While enemies you face range from ocean predators to increasingly difficult shark hunters. Side quests come in the form of hunting humans/sea creatures and obtaining collectibles. They help progress the main campaign which helps to not feel like a chore to do. Highlights of the campaign include the Apex Predator quests and the hunt for Landmarks around the open world. Controls (4/5): With a control scheme that feels like a hybrid between an aeroplane and a submarine, Maneater’s shark controls do that a fair bit of time getting used to. Playing with a controller is highly recommended due to the finer axis of controls provided by the analogue sticks. Once you get the hang of things though, this shark handles like a finely tuned machine.Graphics (5/5): Next to the audio, this is one of Maneater’s stand out points. You can tell that the team put a lot of effort and research into getting every detail of the ocean world right. From the animation of the shark in motion to the refraction of the light as it breaks the ocean’s surface, Maneater is a stunning game to behold. The art style is still heavily stylized but, there are some moments (especially in underwater tunnels) where the game is shockingly photo realistic. Audio (5/5): From Chris Parnell’s excellent narration to the visceral sound effects when your crunch down on a turtle, Maneater promises aural satisfaction. More than superficial satisfaction, the audio ques are pivotal in dodging potentially deadly attacks in the more difficult boss fights. This is one title I would recommend playing on speakers especially if you have competent setup with a powerful subwoofer that can really emphasize the lows and bass. Issues/Optimization: For a PC game that looks this good in 2020, Maneater is very well optimized both in terms of frame rate and game stability. Bugs are very far and few in between with only 2 instances throughout my 21 hours playthrough having game breaking bugs. Overall (4.5/5): One of the hidden gems of 2020 game releases, Maneater is a true labour of love by developers Tripwire Interactive who have done a fantastic job of what’s perhaps the only open world shark simulator to date. Highly recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: So this game is barely 8 months old and they released a dlc 3 months after release and locked achievements and content that should have been base game. I played mostly offline due to sharing my library but I put a good 20+ hours on it and 100% "base game" For what it is, it was a good game but due to the DLC being cut content I just won't rate it worth while if you didn't already purchase it. Story: good until the end, sucked. Real BS. The dlc sounds more interesting but as mentioned above, I'm not gonna get it. Game: Overall it was fun and challenging at times, the progress in the beginning is really slow and perhaps had a little too much grind for how repetitive the dialogue gets, actually by far the worst part of this game outside the DLC being cut content is how repetitious the voice acting is. I mean I love the guy who voices Jerry from Rick and Morty but holy ♥♥♥♥ I will be hearing him in my dreams. I'd suggest turning off the voiceovers when getting the nutrient chests and general eating and faffing about but unfortunately there is unique dialogue for everything else so I kept it on for the most part. There are loads of easter eggs and they are basically an integral part of the game as you level up quicker finding them all but I feel like it was more of a chore than it was fun, I liked each one but the radar and finding them wasn't fun as the radar had a cooldown and took a slot on your ability bar which is limited and one full slot gated behind the dlc.

_childDocuments_.review: Are you scared of the ocean because of sharks and other wildlife that could potentially hurt you? Well, this game will help you get over your fears. You play as the shark, going from a pup to adulthood, you explore different lakes, grottoes, and food sources. There is so much to explore, the game is developed really well (assuming you have a good enough graphics card) and it encompasses everything a shark must know. The best part, for me, is that it even includes educational narrative every once in a while so you can learn about sharks and their feeding habits. Honestly, this is a great game if you want to spend time being the predator, instead of a human. The evolutions are amazing and customizable, and it consumes your time. Before you know it, 5 hours have gone by and it only feels like a few minutes. It is well worth the money!

_childDocuments_.review: So this is going to be a long review if you just want to know if you should buy the game or not read on below.While the game does become a bit grindy / samey after awhile its a nice time waster to pick up for a couple of hours and here and there. You're a shark you eat fish and people and destroy boats while steadily evolving into a megashark with super-powers and making the ocean your ♥♥♥♥♥. If that doesn't make you want to play it then skip it or grab it on sale. You'll get about 8-10 hours out of it. The game's story is pitched around a Shark Week style TV show where a crew follows a shark hunter named Scaly Pete who kills your mother, scars you and then throws you into the water to grow, evolve and seek revenge.As a plot device it serves its purpose to drive the story forward but I feel they kind of missed an opportunity with the antagonist. You don't feel his presence in the world at all and for most part he feels far away and not really attached to what's happening. Maybe he could have come out at night to hunt you or setup traps for you on certain maps or taunted you Jack from Borderlands 2 style. In any case they could have done more. You're a shark, you eat smaller prey to gain nutrients and evolve into a more formidable shark, these start out somewhat realistic but quickly become ridiculous. Which is where I feel the game missed the mark a bit. You can either try to be realistic or embrace the wacky nature of your game. They had an opportunity to essentially make GTA: Shark but they fell short. I say double down on the wacky evolutions, give the shark wings, a laser, centipede legs go nuts. Make the missions more interesting then simply eating people, make them stupid and over the top. Embrace the wackiness I say. The game looks about on par for something built with UE4. There's some jank here and there with entities spawning in late or rapidly shifting animations sometimes but TripWire aren't a billion dollar game studio so you can forgive the occasional hiccup. The underwater areas look quite nice and are fun to swim around in. There are moments where you're just swimming and the sun hits the water and everything looks amazing so good job environmental artists looks great.There's a few slow-downs and frame drops occasionally when just starting the game, leaving the grotto and entering new areas. They're brief but they do happen enough to be noticeable.There's a crippling SOFTLOCK when entering areas where the Apex predators spawn. Basically the name of the predator comes up and then nothing happens the game becomes softlocked. It didn't happen on every single encounter but close to 80% of them. The only way to fix it is to exit and reload the game and re-enter the encounter. A once off would have been fine but this happened at nearly every apex encounter in the game. PLEASE FIX THIS.

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine Ecco the Dolphin (back on the Mega Drive) meets Grand Theft Auto, Saints Row, Far Cry ... but you're a baby shark. It's an action RPG where you get to choose how you evolve as you literally eat everyone and everything on the backdrop of some beautiful scenery. A game where despite having a lot of busy work quests and collectibles can be finished in less than a day, which is a good thing.Disguised as a B grade 'sharknado' game, every opportunity is taken to remind us of the impact we're having on the world beneath us.No music stands out, though they do use a subtle "Jaws" cue during some sections which is a nice touch.Also the sound of a turtle getting eaten (the pop at the end) #FeelsBadMan.But be warned though, memory leaks and an unstable engine means you will get your CPU maxing out at 100% after exiting AND several crashes.Luckily the game saves after everything you do so you shouldn't lose much (if any) progress.

It doesn't get too boring, but it is quite repetitive. All the upgrades basically improve the same basic attacks you have from the start, and are mostly visual besides that. I managed to hit max level at 6 hours and beat the entire game (with doing literally everything else on offer such as collectible hunting and side quests) in 9 hours, after which there isn't anything left to keep me playing. So if 9 hours of a fun shark game is what you're looking for then go right ahead and get it on sale!

_childDocuments_.review: Grade A certified to drastically reduce the lifespan of your controller.Tl;Dr; I went in pretty blind, I had heard about there being evolutions and the sort, and that's pretty much what I hoped for in this game. I was immensely disappointed. It's 5$ or 10$ at most, and the thought of someone paying 40$ for this is genuinely appalling to me. Ironically has extremely shallow gameplay and progression, while also being painfully repetitive. Just watch highlight clips on youtube or just a compilation of all the landmarks, you'll save on time, money, and your controller/keyboard will thank you.  - GameplayPlain and simply, it's controller-abuse, drastically overstays it's welcome, barebones, and the amount of things to do is greatly underwhelming and pitiful. The entire game is a slow grind at it's roots. It takes FOREVER to get enough materials to upgrade. The core flaw however, the things to actually do.There is a SINGLE mission. It boils down to going to place A, kill 8-15 of a specific animal or humans, mission done. That's it, that's 90% of the game. The wildlife diversity is immensely lacking, and the humans are boring and mind-numbingly boring to fight. The combat is painfully lackluster and lacking any real options. 99% of combat against wildlife is biting a couple times and backing off to dodge an attack, and thrashing is simply just masked controller-abuse. Fighting humans is boring doing the same thing over and over and over and over again. You either leap out of the water to grab someone out of a boat or you ram/bite the boat to damage and eventually destroy it, it never advances past being more than that, boats are far tankier than they have any right being, and destroying them takes soooooo long, even with the full bone armor set. - Collectibles There are 3 types of collectibles, and only 1 is even remotely interesting. -License plates, which offer absolutely nothing, uninteresting, and are literally just filler. They are littered everywhere and look amazingly fake and out-of-place, and you collect them by biting them, nothing happens when you get them, absolutely nothing noteworthy, I think they just give a tiny amount of exp, if even, honestly never noticed if they did even that, because of how worthless they are.-Material Caches, these are scattered everywhere, you get them by biting them, and they give small amounts of all materials and a decent bit of exp. That's it.-Landmarks, these are by far the most interesting, they are more-or-less what you'd expect, just random unique landmarks or quirky things the developers modeled and put in, and each one has unique narration. They range from literal trash thrown underwater to man-made statues to random references. At it's best, these are just "haha look, I got that reference" low-effort referential humor.  - EvolutionsVirtually identical to armor sets in any other game. Except THERE'S ONLY 3, or 4 if you buy the lackluster and overpriced DLC. THERE ARE ONLY 4? Really? Calling them evolutions is also quite an overstatement. They're functionally identical to armors, with armor set bonuses.The most unique one lets you shoot a projectile using your tailwhip, and another one visually changes your dodge into a lightning stream, but it's still functionally the same. That's the best it has, ALL the other 'evolution' parts are boring as heck stat buffs. I expected a cool evolution-tree of sorts, or anything to do with picking and choosing from multiple branching paths, and instead got three boring armor sets with boring attributes. An extreme letdown.

_childDocuments_.review: Very glad I finally played this. It's like a cheesy but charming shark movie, except you get to play the shark. It might make me a little biased, but I always enjoyed those movies even though they were terrible. A little janky, some bugs - had a "boss" / elite mob fly into space and it eventually came back after re-opening the game, and towards the end of my playthrough the audio just started cutting out with dialogue overlapping itself or just not playing at all. However, the game's movement and your progression are what really sold me on the game. It's fairly short, I 100% the base game in a little over 7 hours or so, but the pacing is wonderful, and I always felt motivated to grind towards something and continue evolving the shark. The missions that pop up are simple and repetitive, but it sort of works given the whole "turn your mind off and have fun" feel the game has.Some stuttering as well but it's a UE4 game, nothing new there. Besides those issues, it's a very fun game from start to finish and I think the game actually lives up to its self-description of being an "ultimate power fantasy as the apex predator of the seas".

_childDocuments_.review: An okay little mayhem simulator. Clearly could've used a few more honest months in the development oven since, during the few days it took me to finish the game in its entirety, it crashed a couple of times and I also experienced some other oddities and glitches, including enemies just yeeting off into space all of a sudden, the shark making a sudden 180 degree turn out of nowhere, and a bunch of graphical hiccups where the textures wouldn't load.Despite these smaller flaws I had a good time for the vast majority of the time as developing your very own Garbage Disposal Unit of the Sea was fun; watching it grow and evolve into this absurd monster with a helmet made out of bone. Missions got a bit repetitive and combat mostly boiled down to mashing the attack button and dodging button in sequence until either you were dead or the enemy was dead. The narration was the best part of the game by far.
_childDocuments_.name: Maneater

_childDocuments_.review: Like many others, I got this as part of the Humble Bundle Choice pack. At ~9 hrs in, I've cleared the base game 100% and upgraded all the shark bits to max. So, that's basically everything I could do other than swim around aimlessly.Was it fun? Sure, it was fun.Was it challenging? Uh, not really.Maybe there are ways to do combat or upgrade combinations that I didn't explore, but overall the "combat" is really repetitive. It pretty much boils down to whether you're fighting fish or not fish, there aren't really diverse enough enemy patterns that I'd say anything else stuck out to me.Some of the environments are pretty cool, I think a lot of it is ruined by your fishy body though so if you'd be looking to purchase it to get some of the scenic views they show in the slideshow...I'd skip it.I would pay probably $15-20 for this. Overall it's a fairly entertaining 9 hours of hitting the sonar button constantly and chewing on things as you swim around. If you skip some of the collectibles, I'd expect to only need about 8 hours to clear this. If you skip all of them, you could probably clear in 5 hours or so but would likely require more strategy against bosses.I think they missed a lot of potential replay/added value areas by having very limited upgrade choices and locking you into growing bigger. I would've rather seen "size" as something that could be upgraded or left as-is in exchange for something else (speed, damage, whatever) and it would've been cool to see a bunch more upgrades early on and as the game progressed, I think the last boss was the only time I swapped out some parts specifically to do something.
_childDocuments_.name: Maneater

_childDocuments_.review: It brings back the nostalgic feel of Jaws Unleashed, which was probably one of my favorite childhood games. The open under water wold is amazing and the enemies are just as impressive. Like many other games you "level up" so your ability to fight opponents becomes easier as you progress in the game. I liked that you start as a shark pup, the strategy in the beginning is to evade and hide from enemies and once you level up or grow big enough there's no more need to hide. I also like the abilities that you "evolve" in the game, which is apart of your level up experience. The only dislike is the amount of abilities you can apply to your sharks body. This however, does keep a certain challenge to the game .

_childDocuments_.review: The obvious sexism/misogyny of the game’s title aside it’s actually a decent experience. Although the gameplay is very repetitive and increasing infamy is a horrendous grind, it managed to keep me engaged for the majority of it. The leveling system, perks, and gameplay mechanics encourage the player to continue by providing a sense of progression. Even gathering collectibles was entertaining since it was kept to a healthy dosage and didn’t require looking up much of a guide. What could use a bit of tweaking is everything centered around out-of-water gameplay. I understand that it’s intentionally made to be difficult to navigate outside of water given the theme of the game, however, it becomes infuriating when half the missions take you out of water. Either to devour humans, gather a collectible, or even jump across an obstacle for a time trial. It’s vastly inconsistent and reaching high places is incredibly tedious.Something else that slowly got on my nerves is the narrator. I didn’t mind it at first, it’s actually a clever way of filling an acoustic void that the game creates by having it take place underwater. But having the narrator comment on everything you do and not even shutting up for a minute truly drives me mad. At the very least they didn’t pick an annoying voice to accommodate it. It began grinding my gears during the Truth Quest DLC where his entire presence just serves to mock conspiracy theorists. We get it, people with tinfoil hats should be wearing a restraining jacket to match their attire. Now please shut up and let me finish this game already. A minor nitpick I would like to add is how the humans during gameplay cutscenes lack facial movement and are generally animated weirdly.Let’s address the elephant in the room, a game like this shouldn’t have a base price of 35€ when it merely took me 11 hours to acquire all achievements within both the main game and the DLC. The game itself is just too repetitive and doesn’t offer much variation. The main objective of this game is to grind. And while the approach had me hooked, it doesn’t justify such a price tag. I personally don’t hold a major grudge against the developers for being openly sexist/misogynist with their game's title. It may have been a marketing stunt altogether to boost publicity and potentially gain a bigger player base. Regardless of that, the game itself is an above-mediocre experience. Having the game be called ‘Humaneater’ wouldn’t have changed what we have.

_childDocuments_.review: Story: Very short, but very enjoyable. Characters have personality, good ol' southern boys out hunting sharks. Music/Sound: Enjoyable sound design, did get jumpscared by enemies occasionally but I was playing with loud volume, badass music when activating special abilities.Gameplay: Shark is extremely fun to control, with ability to use both bites and tail to destroy your enemies, enemies present a challenge, and each one has its own mechanics, alligators have a nasty roll, barracudas are fast and move like torpedos. There are several sidequests and main quests to do as well as an infamy system that rewards you for beating bosses. Overall a very fun game that I enjoyed, total playtime was about 10-15 hours depending on your skill.

_childDocuments_.review: Awful, repetitive combat. Very little story - the vast majority of the quests are "Kill X number of Y mob" or "Kill Generic Boss Z." The thing that saves this game is the narrator. Its the guy who plays Jerry from Rick & Morty. He does a very good job... but honestly, you're better off watching "Best Narrator Comments Maneater Compilation" on YouTube rather than actually playing this game. What would've saved this game is more evolution variety - evolutions in this game is essentially gear, and while its all unique, there isn't much of it, and it doesn't impact combat enough. The DLC some unique gear that adds a more powerful ranged attack that's actually worth using, apparently, but a game shouldn't need a DLC to have actual variety to the combat.  3/10.

_childDocuments_.review: While an interesting concept--and featuring fun narration from Chris Parnell--the game requires you to purchase additional DLC for what should be core, basic upgrades.  A level cap is also imposed that you reach very quickly without purchasing additional DLC.  It is unfortunate that developers continue to release partially finished games, or only portions of games, while requiring that you purchase DLC in order to play the full game.  DLC should add optional or alternative content, not be a portion of the core game you must purchase separately.

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine one of the many shark evolve mobile game and then imagine someone who turned that into a proper PC game. That is what this game is. The gameplay is simple enough, yet it's fun and addicting. No doubt it's the fun narration and, surprisingly, the story that keep this a fun game to the end. If you like to complete this game 100% you well still quickly find yourself putting 10-15 hours into the game, and it sure is fun to replay it once a while.The only negatives I would point out is that the game isn't optimized too well. You can still play on older PC's, but there will be frame drops (10-25 fps) regardless of PC and graphics settings, especially towards the end of the game. It's annoying, but manageable. Other then that I would get stuck on rare occasions, but I was always able to unstuck myself after some trial and error.If you like a casual game where you play a shark wreaking havoc anywhere from the ocean to the golf course, you will enjoy this game. A bit expensive at full price, but for sure worth it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: It can feel like a bit of a grind at times if you're trying to get certain upgrades maxed and Jaws Unleashed probably did a better job with the eating mechanics since you could target body parts in that game and rip things in half rather then constantly doing an eating animation on kill, but it's certainly fun to control the shark and very few games give you the chance to play as a shark in the first place so it certainly gets points for novelty as well. Also, just as a heads up, you can press the jump key in mid air multiple times to get extra height, not sure if the game tells you that and I missed it, but it would have been useful to know in order to get some of the collectibles that unlock new shark parts, so there you go.

_childDocuments_.review: I got Maneater on sale for under $30 and the DLC for 50%. For that price, this is a great game and a fun, solid experience through the entire main campaign. While the game can feel pretty easy, it does a good job of making you feel like some sort of SyFy channel movie monster, the transition from baby shark in the bayou to super-powered megalodon bodying sperm whales in the gulf feeling satisfying. Story's clearly secondary, but shows that the team cared, as it's a step or two above story for the sake of it, with the Moby ♥♥♥♥ inspiration coming through well. Gameplay is solid, though lock on can frustrate as it's more of a soft aim-assist, but gets the job done 9/10. The other obvious flaw is how janky land movement is, sometimes taking away directional control or throwing you random directions. Despite that, the base game doesn't ask much of you on land, and with 90% of the game in the water, you'll find the game is controls to generally be tight and consistent, with movement underwater letting you really feel like a giant underwater death machine. If you're looking for a rampage game crossed with a collectathon, get it, especially if it's on sale. Don't bother with the DLC if you don't feel like fighting the jankier parts of the games controls.P.S. Would love to see more games with this concept, normal animal becoming a big monster. Cool ♥♥♥♥

_childDocuments_.review: Right off the bat I'll tell ya, this is a pretty good game, short and sweet are the words that will define my review. This game makes you want more, and I missed playing games like this!It's a different take on the Shark games you know, definitely not what you'd expect. RPG like with a level system, upgrades and a bunch of collectibles for you to find! And a fun narrator to listen to.I love the shark design, and how you can grow accordingly to your level, besides all of the beautiful gear you can get, which looks astonishing when fully upgraded, they also come with custom effects, abilities, and even great music once you use them.If you're someone who likes to explore, then this game is for you. It will heavily reward you if you get all collectibles, which is also a good thing if you're a completionist.Besides collectibles, there are lots of fun challenges to work on, from fighting apex predators to gaining infamy.Also, I love the soundtrack, ambiance, and every single small detail, from sea creature noises to music.Now, personally, the main downside of this game is that, it is a short experience, especially if you're not going to collect everything (Including DLC) I managed to complete everything under 15 hours. Personally, it would've been amazing if they made 3 large maps with the same size as the main one, which has around 8 areas.. As well add more gear and everything, maybe make other creatures playable. I'd pay extra money for that amount of content.Also, we don't get enough time trials (Something you can only get from the DLC) One last thing, when you jump out of the water especially to reach collectibles that are high, it can be difficult. There's this thing the game doesn't teach you, but if you jump and constantly look up, your shark will do a backflip. The trick is to look down after a high jump and center the shark, so it won't backflip, making it easier to get some collectibles and go through time trials. This could be somethinig to work on, if they make a sequel.Overall, great game, the price is not bad for the amount of time you'll spend playing, but still.. I'd get it on sale, same with the DLC (You'll need it, great extra content)I already miss this game </3

_childDocuments_.review: Poorly implemented Denuvo, if your internet is nonexistent or unstable, the game may crash. As mentioned elsewhere, overgrinding may cause game instability. Probably the biggest concern is the save destruction that is commonly reported. Upon crashing or dying, especially at higher levels, your save may corrupt and you may lose your save or respawn incorrectly. Backup your saves regularly if you decide to play.Controls can be somewhat awkward on the m+kb and there is no lock on option (the best you get is button mashing the focus button repeatedly to act like a lock on). Personally, not a huge fan of the m+kb controls, such as for thrashing. Certainly, the controls make sense, but when you have wrist pain, the back and forth movement can make it hurt worse.There are plenty of QoL stuff I wish there was in the game, such as lock on (as mentioned, the only lock on is to spam the focus button) and auto sonar (you will likely be using sonar a lot) and smarter map icon identification (if I can see that the icon is a landmark when I jump out of the water, the ? icon still won't change until I'm in range - even if by being in range, I wouldn't be able to see it when it changes).

_childDocuments_.review: Maneater has been a pleasure to play. It managed to be super fun and challenging without being utterly insane and frustrating. The only downside I could say is that the end-game replayability isn't as strong as I had hoped, as at about 27~ hours I've managed to beat the base game and the DLC, with a handful of side missions left and one more Steam achievement to earn. Of course one could always try new playthroughs, but I tend to be a stickler to my original playthrough, and plan to just relax in the game on and off after I collect everything.But while it may not have hundreds of hours of content, I've thoroughly enjoyed every minute of playtime! The combat system, the abilities, evolution mutations, etc make it a very unique experience. The game also rewards you for being both creative and exploring the available mechanics. Here's an example;When I was faced with ships that fired torpedoes at me, I was delighted to find that the unique electric-based dodge ability I had disabled the torpedoes and was basically a counter to them. And later on in the dlc quest, it finally clicked in my head that I could bite onto those disabled torpedoes and fling them with my tail at boats to make taking them down less tedious.I really love that the game's combat system is so fleshed out and rewarding to play around with. And I'm really hoping there's more planned for the game! I did wait for a sale to buy Maneater and its dlc, but after how much I've enjoyed it, I'd buy another dlc in a heartbeat!

_childDocuments_.review: Review Note: I do not own the DLC this review is for the base game only.Gameplay: Maneater is truly a collect-a-thon experience where you go from one distinct area to the next performing the same actions/missions in context of the new area. These missions will primarily have you go to a location and eat X amount of a certain sea critter or people. There are also caches, license plates, and landmarks to collect scattered around a pretty good variety of areas. The pacing of the game left a lot to be desired though as I found myself relying on the first powers I was given and the rate at which you gain powers vs complete the game means you likely will not unlock the sharks full potential until it is far too late. Over all I was able to 100% the game in just under 11 hours making the game not very long and easy to complete in just a few sessions.Graphics: I was surprised at both the variety and how often I found myself in wonder at the underwater environments and then found out how ugly everything was above the surface. The game can be hit and miss but at highest settings the game runs like butter even on a lower end system and is more than passing by today's standards. Audio: Uhhh...there was some kind of dubstep when you use the shark powers but besides that nothing stuck out. The underwater audio was weird at times being reversed on my desk speakers when underwater but returning to normal above land. I do not know if this was intentional or not but as someone who relies on sound in games this made some fights really confusing. Honestly nothing remarkable in this department. Story: I honestly felt like there was potential here. You have Scaly Pete who is a deranged fisherman and the in game lore seems to imply he is known to the area as being pretty aggressive and violent. Contrast to Pete we have his son Kyle who is a marine biologist and it's made clear that Scaly Pete did not have a good relationship with his father and is trying to reconcile that with Kyle in a fashion. But these story clips are brief and really only appear to move the shark along to the next area. There is some emotion to a few of Pere's audio only clips but honestly there was a lot to be worked on here that is just untapped potential. Action Value: So the actual action in this game comes from fighting humans or other predators. Both sort of boil down to some pretty frantic and mindless combat which is frustrating in the beginning and just cumbersome towards the end. With the basic electric teeth it is possible to stun lock most Apex Predators and simply chomp them to death. Be prepared to do a lot of chomping and tail whipping as your attack set in this game is sort of limited. There is also a weird non-lock on system where you have to click the right stick in every few seconds to stay orientated on your enemy. Once again nothing really special here but you do get to play as a shark and swimming around the reefs and hunting smaller prey can really put you in the shark mindset.Other Comments: Chris Parnell narrates the game. Wonderful to listen to but some of the voice clips repeated too often for my personal taste and made me more annoyed with the narrator at times than not.Overall I would recommend this game if you can get it on sale. Worth sitting down with for a few days on a weekend and just living out the fantasy of being a vengeful mutant shark.

_childDocuments_.review: Solid 3/5 game. Pretty fun gameplay and the ocean design adds to the immersion. I like the variety of animals included in the game, plus the land mobility feature is quite entertaining. Some areas of improvement though: 1) Lack of replayability. After completing all optional and main missions, since there is a level cap on the shark which means no more skill increases, there is really not much to do post game. It would help if the level cap was removed so it feels like you are embarking on a journey to become a true monster shark, if you get what I mean.2) Lack of character variations: I like that you can upgrade your sharks using these genetic modifications like bone armor and shadow skins, but I think it would be cooler if you could play as other sharks. There are many different marine predators shown in the game so I think it would not be hard to include them as playable characters as well!3) Combat is not smooth at times: This might just be me but I find the fish to fish combat to be hard at times due to the camera constantly moving away from my target. Sometimes in the midst of an underwater fight, my shark would breach the surface during an opportunity to attack the target which makes me miss the chance to damage.For its price, I would say I am a little disappointed from the content provided by the game, After 17 hours being put into it, I no longer want to play the game anymore due to the lack of replayability.
_childDocuments_.name: Maneater

_childDocuments_.review: I have unlocked 100% the main game and started Truth Quest. It's still a very repetitive experience. Hardly any variety to the content. Each area of the game has the same mission types. Mostly kill/eat a bunch of marine life or people. If you aren't doing that you are swimming around finding collectibles. I've maxed out all the main game's evolutions and at level 30 I still don't feel like a dominant ocean predator. Humans have ridiculous auto-aim that hits you every time. Fighting them mainly consists of ramming their boat. Ram, ram, ram, spin, ram, ram, ram, spin. As a mega-shark I should be able to completely decimate them with just a few bites. Fighting boss creatures consists of the same patterns. Bite, bite, bite, dodge, bite, bite, bite, dodge. Starts glowing, dodge and bite. Rinse and repeat. The only variety to the enemies in Maneater is aesthetics. The game really needs some patches to allow you to dominate after you have put in the required time to max out everything. Also a patch for the swimming function of the game. My left trigger finger is sore from repeatedly holding L2 on the controller to speed up. This could be fixed with a simple toggle-speed mode feature.  I will say that the narrations from Chris Parnell of "Rick and Morty" fame are hilarious and basically the only thing that kept me motivated to play the game to it's entirety. Overall Maneater has a great sense of humor and it's the levity that makes it an enjoyable experience. I'd only recommend buying this game if you can get it and the DLC for $10-$20  on a Steam sale. Otherwise don't waste your money.

_childDocuments_.review: ahh yes, my favorite clicker game. in all seriousness i loved the game even though it was REALLY repetitive basically wanting you to kill a few fishes, sharks, humans or just destroying a boat then comes a boss after that they throw some story at you. my main enjoyment about the game was collecting all the collectibles which there is 11 conspiracy theorist (that you need to eat), 90 license plates, 133 nutrient caches and 69 landmarks (nice) including the truth quest DLC which has to be one of the best DLCs in my opinion mainly due to the amount of content it brought to the game and the best part about the DLC was the mutated versions of the current existing enemies for example the great white shark that can be easily defeated has turned into the electric great white that can stun you but later in the story of the DLC you can encounter a atomic version of the electric great white which brings even more challenge. maneater also has one of the BEST progression ive ever seen in videogames, this game prevents you from exploring too far and getting vanquished by the stronger enemies you're not ready for. overall the game is a 9/10 from my perspective due to almost zero replay value but i would highly recommend this to anyone that ever plans on buying this, is unsure if this game is worth it or just wants to play as a shark that brutally murders multiple hundreds of humans.

_childDocuments_.review: The first 15 minutes seem a bit unnecessary, until you realize that this is just the tutorial and intro...once you become the shark for real, it's all an uphill battle from there, in the best way imaginable!Skins, Mutagens, Mutations, Upgrade systems, and a mission/sidemission/collectathon XP system makes for a very entertaining and engaging gameplay loop.My only gripe so far has been that enemies will respawn/despawn at a relatively unfair distance (i.e. I could start battling a Croc, and swim like 5 yards away, eat something, turn around, and the Croc has either come after me (which is good), OR it de-aggros me, swims back to where it was and despawns completely!).If this was fixed/tweaked somehow, I think this would be a helluva game! Definitely not worth the 40 dollar mark, but definitely when it's on sale. Wish I'd paid 25 or 30 bucks for it, not 35 or so, but really: it's a 5 dollar difference, so I can't complain too much.8/10, would listen again to Jerry from Rick and Morty explain how odd of a fish I am.EDIT: Also, the game seems to crash at strange moments, but so far they aren't a big issue as it pretty much saves all your progress when you die/crash.

_childDocuments_.review: I literally just completed Maneater after 10-12 hours of gameplay.I collected everything and I scoured the deepest depths of the ocean.So what is Maneater? It is basically the best "shark simulator" (fish simulator?) out there right now. I know there are a few "fish eats fish to grow" games out there, but most of them back from the Flash days.This game is on a different level, while essentially using the same mechanics.I felt the balance of the game was pretty good, the controls felt a lot better than I thought. At first I was annoyed that I got out my PS4 controller, yet the game just wouldn't recognize it. But it is a lot easier to play with mouse and keyboard than you'd think.Now this being a PS4 (PS5?) port, of course there are some drawbacks.There are both neutral and aggressive fish in the waters. One thing I don't understand, is how a lvl 1 muskellunge decides to attack a lvl 30 Mega-Shark. But oh well. Logic programming aside..The game design is pretty nice and the different types of fish are too.However one thing that really annoyed me:There are multiple stages: Pup, Teen, Adult, Elder and Mega.I was swimming around in the first two areas of the game until I turned into an Adult. Being the achievement ♥♥♥♥♥ that I am, I of course proceeded to collect everything, given I had access to it at the time.I hit level 30 as an adult, only to realize, I just completed 2 areas of the game and maxed out my level.I really feel having the cap be at 30 is a bit low. Especially with all the collectibles that also give you EXP in this game. I'm not kidding when I say, I could've probably hit level 60 from doing all missions and collectibles alone. Yet here I was, pointlessly collecting caches for achievements. That is a bit demoralizing.The second one, also probably port-related: Over the course of these 11 hours my game crashed 10 times. Every time was either while loading a cutscene or triggering an event. I hope there will be quite a few bugfixes in the future.Anyway, to sum things up, I definitely recommend this game. It is both fun to play casually and has enough content to tickle your inner achievement hunter. But given the current state of the game and my experiences, I'm limiting the score to a 7/10 - 8 if they fix the crashes, the rest maybe if they add more late-game content.It's just weird jumping from Adult to Mega within one second.

_childDocuments_.review: I had a ton of fun with Maneater. Two things I didn't expect to appreciate as much as I do are the game feel and the writing. This game could have been a frustrating and janky experience, but swimming around feels so absolutely natural once you get down the controls. I never feel like I'm fighting the camera and I'm always immediately able to gather my bearings after getting turned around. The combat also feels very satisfying and easy to overcome. The game progresses at an extremely comfortable rate, never forcing you to grind for xp or something since the game's mostly balanced around a very streamlined experience. Doing sidequests and spending more time beefing up your bull shark is more rewarding as a result. Also the writing is really amazing. I can't believe I was genuinely laughing at the dialogue as much as I was. It's surprisingly in-touch with modern social politics in a tasteful way, and very well learned in the sciences behind the game's genetic mechanics and marine biology. I have a lot of respect for Maneater after spending as much time with it as I did. My only complaint while playing was how collectables and landmarks disappear from the map after you find them, but after 20 hours I realised you can actually toggle them to be visible while on the map. I guess that means, aside from the fact it crashed twice, it's basically a perfect game in my books. My only caveat is that you have to be the type that actually enjoys doing sidequests, otherwise you're gonna get real bored real quick.

_childDocuments_.review: It tries to be grand theft auto with the ocean and in some ways it succeeds, but overall I'm having a very bored experience with it.No, you don't get to explore a vast ocean, you get to explore a small map. Getting bigger feels awesome but it's simply too slow. Game won't respect my time.Controls are the most awful part of this. The camera is tedious and annoying. Every time I charge I do practically no damage and need to realign the camera at the rapidly moving large fish I'm fighting. It makes the combat weird and annoying because we can't simply lock on continuously.Alot of the game is fighting. Most of the first 2 hours feels like you're just driving this shark to have tedious combat, then looking around for the checkpoint to the next location and have another weird combat over and over again.Overall a tedious experience for me. _childDocuments_.review: Maneater is a good choice of game if you want a few hours of causing some mindless chaos.It's a pretty cool idea for a game. You start off as a shark pup and through the course of the game your shark will grow as you level up and you can add mutations that you unlock to beef up your sharks attacks and defence.The sense of progression in levelling up your shark is pretty satisfying as you outgrow the predators that would have caused you trouble earlier in the game and the hunters become the hunted. You can level up your mutations which improve their stats as well so you can turn yourself into the perfect killing machine whether thats a bone covered battering ram or a bio electric shark.The underwater environments look great and theres a nice variety of areas you'll explore from the swamp you start in, to quays alongside wealthy mansions and eventually out to the ocean.While initially the game is quite fun it does start to get repetitive after a few hours. You basically follow the same pattern every time you progress to a new area. It usually goes enter new area, find cavern which acts as your respawn/upgrade point, do a few missions which are usually kill a predator/ consume humans/ hunt a set number of fish, kill the apex predator for that area and then move to the next area. The lack of variety makes the last few hours feel like a bit of a chore.I found playing this game in short bursts of about an hour to be the better option, as it helped alleviate the repetition a bit but I did find, even doing that, my interest waned for the latter parts of the game. Fortunately it's not an overly long game so it doesn't become a major downside.So while it may not be a particularly deep engaging game it works well as a game where you can just shut your brain off and cause a bit of chaos as a mutated giant shark.

_childDocuments_.review: If 3-4 hours of repetition + 6-7 hours of fun is a bad deal for you, then you won't like it. If you don't mind that and like some stoopid fun with the in-your-face cynic subtext social commentary plus the occasional 4th wall breaking, then this is for you.That's it. What they show on trailers is exactly what you get. Simple to play. Feels exactly as trailers show. There is little technique involved in playing, so it's dumb fun. Only the last bosses require not munching something (an explosive) and then slapping it with your tail. Everything else is "bite till you eat it or it explodes" and "if it can hurt you, dodge, if it hurts a LOT, come back later".The devs really should've cut back on the repetition side of things. Didn't overstayed its welcome, but it would be much more fun if it lasted 7 hours than 10 hours. Just because you've put more water on the lemonande and now you have more lemonade, that doesn't mean it's as good as it was.Oh yeah, curses are bleeped out. Kinda silly, but matches the television program format. Just wish there was options for "Uncut (You naughty boy...)" and the "Dophin Laugh You Know Well (that actually is a Kookaburra call sped up)"

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game. I love sharks, and I love open world games.Unfortunately, an hour into the game and I had seen everything. This game's quests make Ubisoft games look 12/10 for variety.Every single mission is 'eat X humans', 'eat X fish', or 'destroy X boat'. It's just so lazy. It's a shark, so there's only so much you can do, but there's so much more than just this.The concept is great, and parts of the execution are really special. The evolutions, while a bit limited in number, look great visually and for the most part affect gameplay in meaningful ways, such as the abilities.The game can be very fun when you're engaged in a fight with the local militia, and with careful use of resources you could almost go forever without needing to run and hide. That and the power fantasy of eating silly humans in a single bite was the most fun I had with Maneater. The on-the-nose references to other media properties all around the game can be charming, but mostly just make me want to play those other, better, games.The shark controls are decent.Especially at higher levels she controls like a big, dumb, hunk of meat, which I suppose is on-brand.In the 9 hours (nine!!!) it took me to beat the base game to 100%, I experienced seven crashes. Other than that, the game ran pretty well for me, barring a few stutters here and there (rare).It seems like the developers may have run out of time late into the development cycle.In the later areas, the narration that played with every landmark discovered were absent.I was playing with subtitles on, so it wasn't just bugged/missing sound, they simply weren't added.This made the short cutscene when you discovered each one rather awkwardly silent. Other voice lines were missing as well, including one in a cutscene, where the final boss spoke, but no words came out.Overall, there is some fun to be had, albeit with a big helping of grind.The price tag is unacceptable for what you're getting as well.Wait for a deep sale, or get it in a bundle like I did to avoid buyers remorse.The game also comes with DENUVO built-in, so if that is a problem for you (it should be!), steer clear.

_childDocuments_.review: It’s like GTA but you’re a shark. It’s better than GTA because you’re a shark...The main game is a lot of fun. At first it’s a grindfest. But when you’re still a small shark it’s also the hardest to fight other larger predators. As you unlock upgrades it becomes noticeably easier as long as you use the correct upgrades. After understanding the basics of the game (use that sonar!) I went back to previous areas to complete side objectives which weren’t that hard anymore by then.The main storyline was also entertaining enough to keep me going. The cartoony art style went well with the cartoon violence. This game keeps realism far away. Some of the narrators comments were very funny like the one about sharks attacking ancient humans on land.Completing the main game doesn’t take that long. I was near 20 hours. Part of that was spent on grinding early in the game but I also wasted hours killing hunters and randomly messing around later. The controls take some time to master but in the end I was tailslapping other sharks into humans on land just for the heck of it.The DLC storyline was a bit underwhelming and there were no cutscenes like in the main game. Hardware performance also seems to have taken a hit. But the missions were fun enough. Particularly the end bosses act better and it’s a bit less of a straight forward bite fest. Shark hunters will eventually have helicopters which are a cool addition. After all there was one in Jaws 2 as well...The side missions are more of the same with the exception of racing. But I was pleasantly surprised that eventually you also unlock a number of side missions taking place in areas from the main game. Even if the side missions are repetitive at least there’s something to do again. The open world is large enough and the areas are diverse so I wasn’t bored with traveling around yet.The DLC also lets you upgrade your shark to level 40 which is worth it if you enjoy the free roaming. But the total price of the game and DLC could be a bit lower for a game this short and repetitive. The addition of a multiplayer mode might have justified the 44 euro price tag. The combat system isn’t fleshed out enough for serious deathmatches but just hosting a private game to freeroam with friends could have been fun.
