_childDocuments_.review: I own the XB1 version of this game, picked the PC port up in a recent sale as I thought it would be fun to play at 60 Sharks a Second.And yes, the game is fun. It is repetitive, it is a bit grindy, the targeting could be better, but it is just good silly violent fun. Never takes itself too seriously, some funny dialogue, a decent gameplay loop that makes you feel like a beast. And you cannot deny jumping about the beaches eating humans left and right is a great laugh.But. This version of the game is riddled with problems.Many 12th Gen CPU owners simply cannot start the game. There has been no official patch for owners of today's current tech and the workarounds vary greatly in success. I was lucky enough to not have this problem but instead have another.I can only play for about an hour at a time before the game crashes with an Unreal Engine error. My guess is that it is a memory leak. So far nothing else has happened, but other users have reported game save wipes and even total PC shutdowns from the game crashing. So not good really, is it?I understand games, once done, are done. We're not asking for content, we're just wanting to be able to play a game on current hardware technology without issues. The game is still on sale, any stability problems should be addressed or the game should be taken off the store front.This isn't some retro Win 95 classic, nor are we running the game on outdated hardware, customers are moving with the times yet the game is not.However the Devs/Publisher seemingly do not give a damn. No mods active on these forums, nothing about hotfixes or similar. Zilch. Yet, the game is still on sale.A super fun and bizarre "rage em up" akin to early GTA or Destroy All Humans, but a technical experience that really isn't worth the effort.Only buy if these issues do not deter you, and really consider refunding within that 2 hour period.Win 11 i7 12700k 3.6ghz, RTX 3070 8GB, 32GB DDR4 Ram

_childDocuments_.review: I completed all main/side quests and found all items in a little over 20 hours of play. I'm a strategy gamer, so this was a bit fast especially for a game at this price tier. I admittedly figured this could be the case heading into this purchase with this kind of game, but it looked rather unique and I loved the idea and genre. The graphics are quite good, and while the controls do take some getting used to, I found I got the hang of them quite quickly. The narration and story line were also enjoyable, and the game does strike a nice balance between humor and gore.Overall I would recommend the game to others, but I do find the replay value to be quite low. On my first and only playthrough to date, I was able to easily acquire enough nutrients to upgrade all three evolution shark variants. If I needed to fight a ship, I'd change over to those upgrades and if I needed to fight some wildlife, I changed over to a fitting combination. I'll probably pick this up again in at least a year from now when I don't remember everything, but there's very little incentive to go through the game using a different strategy or evolution chain. The story indicators are nicely implemented, but it also means finding all the items is just a matter of spamming the sonar as you cruise around. I already found everything there is to find.I also thought the tutorial and some game mechanics could use additional explanation. I had to play the tutorial at least twice to quickly read all the explanations on mechanics. Would be nice if these could be viewed after the fact. Some other aspects are not even mentioned such as whipshot slo-mo aiming etc. Making full use of the bonuses afforded by evolution upgrades took more experimentation than it should have. As an example, lunge bonuses are usually only active in the first few seconds of lunging and not active just from holding lunge and swimming around fast.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is one of the best power trip fantasies made playable. You play as a shark that gets unceremoniously put into a very hostile environment, slowly but surely work your way up the food chain and eventually become the ultimate apex predator. The game has a pretty good progression system, a nice, big open world to explore, and plenty of action to feed all your hungry shark fantasies. All the different "Evolutions" you collect on your journey to dominance adds a lot of options for creative play styles and adds quite a bit of reply value as well. Overall, a great game to play straight through in one go or in several short bursts through the week because playing as a super predator is never not fun.Story-wise the game doesn't have much to offer. The main character of the story (who is also you main antagonist) is a flat, one-note caricature of hunting stereotypes. Every one else gets next to no characterization at all and are kinda just there. The lemony narrator provides some much needed levity though, even if he eventually starts repeating a lot of lines if you play long enoughYou won't really care for the story that much because you're too busy having fun being a shark that eats anything and everything in front of it. And the story is really just a paper-thin excuse for the game to throw objectives at you. If you do care to really look, there is a deeper lore in here, but not of this actually affects the gameplay. Plus, the game itself pretty much hints that you should not to take it too seriouslyWord of warning, this game as a reputation of being a bit buggy, with some people reporting a crash can even wipe your save file. My personal experience: in about 30+ hours of gameplay, I've only crashed twice, neither affected my saves though. Maybe I'm just lucky.

_childDocuments_.review: What did I like? The game has an interesting premise for sure. You play as a recently born shark and you have to grow and evolve to seek revenge on the fisherman who killed your mother and injured you as a pup. So you go to different biomes and pretty much eat everything that moves. Turtles, fish, alligators, people are all fair game to you as a shark. The graphics are also very nice and have a 'cartoon' feel to them which means they will age much better than many other graphics heavy games. What I did not like: Length of the game, repetitiveness, simplicity of story.  The game is around 12-15 hours long depending if you decide to 100% all the different areas. However, when you reach a certain level (level 30 in the base game) you are capped and the difficulty takes a massive plunge. Most other animals are no threat and you can just cruise through game from that point. Only humans remain much of a threat. The game also has very simple mission structure. It consists of: 1. Swim to area. 2. Consume a certain amount of food. 3. Profit. That is all you do. Not very engaging. Worth buying while on sale. I did not buy the DLC.

_childDocuments_.review: Make no bones that this IS a fun game. So why the downvote? Well if you look at achievement percentages only a little over 1/3 of all players made it into the 2nd half of the game. This is because a single piece of the electric set you get through killing Bounty Hunters makes you op and then everything is a walkover. Attack, swim off, grab some nearby feeder fish to stay alive - rinse and repeat.Amusing then that I saw several reviews saying the game gets too hard the more hunters you kill. I can only suggest that those people didn't understand upgrading and changing evolutions (equipment).You've seen pretty much all the game has to offer well before hitting 15 hours play time. This doesn't mean the game is too short though because it's a wild ride that is already overly bulked with grind quests. But there are so many of these quests that you will hit the lvl 30 cap long before you complete the story and from that point it's kind of disappointing. The DLC is more of the same but harder and even though it IS more of the same the game isn't really a complete game without it. It's also kind of irritating that the 30-40 cap change doesn't come into effect until you complete the main story and move on to the new area.If this were £25 including the DLC then I'd give it a thumbs up for novelty value and pure visceral fun. If it's on sale then it's certainly worth having. At the full price that many paid though it needed something more.Regardless of the overall negative for the reasons mentioned above I have to give Kudos for making a pretty cool game that dares to be different. Once again proving that Steam needs a neutral sideways thumb for reviews.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok so i went on this game with no expectation, i bought it on sale for 4€ i have to say i really enjoy my time on this one taking 16hours basically too beat 100% of the game. Now lets talk on what did the game brings to you. U start as a little shark and u will be challenge trough maps to beat bigger predatores and generating threat on the population making so that the AI attack u too with boots, and they also have some bosses that u have to beat while u gain reputation. While u progress u will unlock several mutations that can allow u too build your shark on different ways and let me tell u that each one of them provide diferent uses for sure! Some of this mutations comes from finding "Secret Places" that are not that secret since when u upgrade your sonar all the loot is really easy too find and the maps in my opinion are really a pleasure to explore. Now i saw alot of people bashing this games cuz of the controls and crashes and i will give my honest opinion about this one! !! I DIDNT USE A CONTROLER !! i play the whole game with mouse and keyboard and never had any problem with the controls of the game or controlling the shark even on the time trials that alot of people complaing on the DLC but i will get on that part too. Its true that sometimes when attacking humans the aim/control looks a little junky but overall i enjoyed my time playing and had no issues with the control itself. Now lets talk about crashes i had 2 crashes playing the whole game and never had my progress deleted as some players talk. One of them when fighting peter for the first time it did crash when i smashed the cage, and i had another crash after purchasing the DLC on a time trial. So lets talk about the DLC.I definitly feel that the game was a little bit more "clunky" with the DLC not sure why but u can really feel some optimization issues when playing on the DLC but like i said never had any really problems and i think that the whole DLC adds some new interesting fights from new predators with same mechanics and mutations that u have to some new AI fights on some crazy boats withs nukes and helicopetrs and as expected some more normal missions but overall i think if u grab the DLC on sale too its defenitly worth the time and i did really enjoy the challenge of the time trials that werent really a challenge but it was fun having a new mechanic on the game(where the shadow build/speed build trully shines). Now i have to bash the dev's for 1 thing only that i cannot agree on any game and that is putting DLCs achievements to force players buying extra content i never agreed with that and i think thats not the way things should work.But overall its a fun game to spend some hours if u like the sea theme while being one of the biggest predators that exist definitly worth a pick up if u grab it on sale on my opinion!

_childDocuments_.review: Really Fun!I'm about 7 hours in and I already completed some of the map sections to 100%. So I can tell it's not gonna be a super long game and I think that's a good thing. Let me explain why.The game is really fun, it's a bad-ass shark RPG, what's not to like? But the overall premise of the game remains the same for each section of the map.There are shallow swamps to super vast oceans! The map is great and really compliments the game and the way you play it.So each map has a few collectables, some side missions, a main mission and a boss battle. It works and its fun! You're welcome to free roam between all of the connected maps, but in RPG fashion, the enemies are level based so you can't just diddy daddle where you want. You need to be prepared. If the game had more content than it currently has I feel it would have started to become repetitive but it's just enough content per section to keep it fresh for the next section,The main story is actually really neat. The game tells its story through the eye's of a shark hunter in a shark week documentary fashion and it really works. You start as a cub and work your way to become THE MAN EATER!The game has n skill tree which allows you to upgrade your teeth, fins, tail, DNA ect. And it really delivers that satisfying sense of accomplishment you know and love form an RPG.So overall, the is really fun. And as Shark Game, I really can't think of anything they could have done to  make it better? They pretty much nailed it.Its not a full priced game, even if its not on sale so I really recommend that you give it a try if you are interested.I'm currently playing this as a side game to take breaks from my main game and it works perfectly for that.8.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: It all comes down to price, this game is not worth £30+. _childDocuments_.review: Despite billing the game as the ultimate power fantasy even at the end you don't feel all that powerful, smashing and biting boats at full speed while one of your buffs are active still takes way too much to destroy them. The pacing is just off, at the beginning you're scared of alligators and barracudas and at the end you're maxed at level 35 biting a level 75 boat for 5 minutes taking a sliver of its health each time. It's not that it's hard it's just everything is time consuming and everything takes too many bites to kill and even when you min/max your build you can only be so powerful, even with the DLC. But, despite that, it's good, controls are great, exploring is fun, being a shark is cool. The narration is occasionally funny and the rpg mechanics while a bit basic are good enough to keep you going. It's just I think the Devs haven't left themselves much room to expand on, they can't make the shark any bigger than it is, otherwise, it would prevent you from exploring early areas. They can't make you do too much more damage, otherwise, you won't be able to use the Whipshot which requires you to hold something in your mouth and shoot it with your tail, can't do that if you eat everything in one bite.

_childDocuments_.review: It's fun, brutal and fast. Once you hit critical mass getting resources for upgrades is trivial and you can eat almost anything with impunity. I wouldn't recommend doing this tho since every time you eat three humans you'll get the full wrath of the hunters, which can make the revenge missions a little more bothersome.The controls for the most part are smooth. Once you leave the water however it can get quite irritating. Breaching seems to be a 50/50 on whether you'll jump full height or just backflip and kill all momentum. It makes doing some of the "trick jumps" for the collectables way more frustrating than it needs to be. Luckily the collectables can be targeted with your bites so if you get close enough you will lunge at it. Overall it's a lot of fun. Narrator is probably the best part about the game honestly.

_childDocuments_.review: Maneater is a great game that I was thrilled to see be brought to Steam after its initial release on Epic Games. This game is a spiritual successor to a game called Jaws Unleashed that I played on the original Xbox, where you play as Jaws and go around eating people and fighting shark hunters, and it was an amazing game. This game is very similar to Jaws and is a lot of fun to play.In Maneater, you are a baby shark that's mother is killed by a fisherman and his son that are the stars of a reality television show about shark hunters. There is a narrator that speaks throughout the game as if the events are occurring within the show, including interviews with the human characters the shark goes up against. The game is set in New Orleans, and you explore the various areas of the city from the swamps to the open gulf ocean that each have their own unique species and types of people to eat. Your shark grows up as you explore the city and set out on your revenge against Scaly Pete, and you develop your attack abilities and other upgrades as you age. The upgrades consist of more realistic looking ones, but also special radioactive mutations like bioelectrical teeth, bone-like skin, or poisonous capabilities.There are various types of fish, sharks, whales, and humans to eat. Humans will be in many different types of boats, from kayaks to yachts, and will also be swimming and playing along the beaches. Each area has its own sea creatures that are difficult to kill, like other sharks or whales, and you slowly become the apex of the sea as you defeat them. Your shark can go on land and grab people or items and bring them back into the sea, a funny thing players of Jaws Unleashed would do that was given its own mechanic in Maneater. There is an infamy system depending on how much destruction your shark causes, and the human response to attacks increases with each level. Humans will send out under-equipped mercenaries and increase their ships and weapons to the US Coast Guard. There are famous fisherman and sailors that can be killed for each infamy level that unlock special upgrades. The boats are a lot of fun to fight, and have great destruction physics. It is always satisfying to hop onto a boat and grab someone off of it to be eaten. The game world has many collectibles throughout, some of which require abusing the mechanics or certain upgrades to accomplish, but even with this replayability design the game is still surprisingly short. The game can be played after completion to finish the collectibles and attack people for fun, but it is limited in what you can do. The combat and exploration are a lot of fun, and the game's atmosphere of being presented as a reality television show is a great framing device. The narrator is really funny to listen to, and makes great jokes that keep a lighthearted and ridiculous tone that fits the story. The game is worth the fun it provides, and for the nostalgia for those who have always wanted another shark game, but is really short and maybe better left to a sale for those that are not really interested in the premise.

_childDocuments_.review: I never realized how much I wanted to play as a shark until this shark game. And boy did they let me live my dreams. _childDocuments_.review: Play if you like:- Brutally murdering ocean life to permeate the grim circle of life- Brutally murdering humans who fail to respect how much of a threat you can be- Sharks- Conspiracy theoriesAvoid if you dislike:- Water levels- Sharks- Conspiracy theoriesIf you complete all the content and objectives, that's about 10-12 hours of game time, plus 3-5 hours for the post game ("Truth Quest").Worst thing about the game I'd say is it can have performance issues, and the variety of content is not that broad, like after you've completed two or three areas you may feel like you're not gonna see anything new for a while beside different scenery. Fighting the human boats especially can feel a bit repetitive and grindy to rank up your threat and infamy.So basically you a shark and you eat a lot of stuff to grow bigger and stronger. You roam around waters looking for smaller fish to eat and other sources of nutrients. Once you've eaten enough nutrients, you level up, and at some specific levels you advance one step in your growth stage from pup to teen, then to adult, and beyond. Growing bigger lets you reach more places and fight bigger enemies. If at one point you get stuck like me wondering why you don't seem to be able to progress on the "Check on scaly pete" objective: remember going on a frenzy on humans builds up your threat level, and higher threat levels unlock new things.There are objectives you can complete in each area, either involving exploration, reaching difficult places, fighting other marine predators, or eating up humans and destroying their naval forces.When completing objectives and advancing the main quest, you unlock some evolutions and mutations you can equip to different part of your shark: body, teeth, head, fins, tail, and "accessories" organs. Each mutation grants bonuses that helps you fight against certain types of enemies or makes exploration easier and faster. You can also upgrade each of these part and organs by spending the nutrients you've collected. Quick tip: don't sleep on the sonar upgrades, they help you find things you've missed or haven't found yet so much more conveniently.The combat system is mostly based around either carefully analyzing your enemies patterns and dodging correctly to retaliate at the right time, or you can also mash the bite button and guess when to dodge, or not dodge if you're big and bad enough to handle your opponent's damage (some body parts help cheesing bosses). Some dodge timings are very tight and require good reactions, or anticipation.The grinding isn't bad, if you take some time to complete objectives you come across you'll be generously fed in bonus nutrients to upgrade your body parts, and if not then you'll just have to choose your body parts more carefully and be more patient against bosses and big enemies.The controls are good, but you may have to remap a few keys for convenience, or having a mouse with extra buttons: you'll be pressing the bite button (left click by default) and the lunge button (shift by default) an awful lot just to roam around and get rid of other predators that attack you and require multiple bites to kill and eat.Performance are overall good, but some specific things cause frame drops, such as swimming right between the border of two areas, or looking around a lot in the open ocean with lots of terrain to render in the end game. This can be annoying when it happens during important fights. And during these frame drops, the physics engine behaves weirdly and causes some teleports if things are moving quickly during that time. I had a boss get teleported out of bound once because of this, but was still able to kill it with chip damage on the part of its body that was sticking through the wall.The Truth Quest post-game content adds interesting stuff, but it gets a bit repetitive by the end of it. The type of tasks you're asked to complete are nothing new, and the new area it adds being bigger than the other ones has some performance issues because just pausing the game takes forever to load the map of it. The new mutations, new area to explore, and new final boss are the biggest interest points in it.

_childDocuments_.review: Maneater doesn't really do anything that revolutionizes gameplay to make it stand out nor does it have any special mechanics. It's an arcadey game that is purely driven by mindless fun and it does exceptionally well at doing that. I think the devs knew exactly what they were aiming for so the game is very self-aware and that does add a bit to it. You are a shark and you eat and create havoc, if you played that Jaws game back on ps2 i think, you will know exactly how the gameplay loop will pan out except you can customize the shark. All that aside, I really enjoy turning my brain off and playing this game. The constant quips from Chris Parnell can be a bit excessive at times but for the most part, it isn't completely overbearing or bland so they're fun to listen to. The one thing I think this game did REALLY well was it's world. I was utterly shocked at how interesting the underwater world of Port Clovis was. The regions are surprisingly distinct and detailed, that's not to mention the plethora of parody landmarks dotted all over the map (Spongebob's home and Fyre Festival were my favorite). Overall, all you need to do is understand that this game wasn't aiming to be your next Triple A experience, it's just dumb fun and it does that incredibly well.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: #1. The game runs very well#2. The graphics are pretty good (above average certainly)#3. The narrator actually sometimes mentions some cool facts about fish#4. Starting out as a wee-fishy and becoming a 10metre (33feet) chompy-boy is fun#5. The shark design is really cool (especially with the different augments)Cons: #1. A massive and constant stream of overlapping dialogue by the narrator#2. Jumping into the air is extremely finicky and the game actually requires you to get to high-up places very often, which exacerbates the issue#3. I'm not joking about the Thalassophobia. If you suffer from fear of deep water, then you will absolutely want to avoid this game. I personally don't suffer from it, but my heartbeat CERTAINLY shot up a couple of times because of the deep water#4. The game is very short. $40 for just 8hours of gameplay is bad (and the DLC costs $15 and can be finished in 3hrs)#5. No multiple save slots (you just get ONE save slot)#6. No UI options whatsoever (no colorblind or opacity options)#7. No photomode#8. There's quite a lot of 'walking simulator' stuff going on. Sometimes you travel multiple miles just for the narrator to spew out a few one-liners and then it's off to the next location, which is again miles away#9. The narrator being a conspiracy theorist in the DLC isn't exactly funny. The devs tried to squeeze some humor out of the premise, but none came out.#10. I wish there were more types of augments (4 different ones isn't enough)#11. The game is quite grindy, especially in the mid-to-late game#12. The fact that the hunters from their boats can shoot you with bullets while you're 100feet below the water is counter-intuitive (haven't the devs watched Mythbusters ever?)Overall it's a really cool game, and the devs can absolutely turn this game into a mega-hit, if they allow you to choose different starting predators (instead of just a shark). Like, starting out as a Crocodile or an Octopus, would be super, super, super cool. Anyways, at the end of the day, if you're OK with paying $40 for just 8-10hours of gameplay, then have at it... it's a good gameMy wishlisted games if you wanna be a bro: For more reviews, visit my curator page:

_childDocuments_.review: This game is like the best examples of the straight-to-DVD monster movies and the trashy wildlife hunting shows it parodies: Fun, cheesy and doesn't overstay its welcome! The gameplay doesn't change much, but it is a constant source of fun, fighting other animals, exploring the world with all its sights, and eating humans just never gets old! I spent a lot of time just swimming about, enjoying the scenery, which I would have not expected from a game where maiming beachgoers is the main focus point! The progression system is a bit weird though, since you are basically finished with the game by the time you manage to make proper use of your arsenal of mutations. The optimization for the game is also a bit lacking, and it of course always is at its worst when you are currently fighting and have absolutely no use for stuttering, but it's never too bad or spoils the enjoyment of the game. And some of the cutscenes could do with a rework of the lighting. But these are in the grand scheme of things just a few details that absolutely do not stop you from having lots of fun with this game, this is certainly one, if not the best games where you can play as a shark or animal and kill humans - its pure entertainment and understands itself well.Absolutely worth the 9$ on sale and the 36$ when it is not on sale too!

_childDocuments_.review: Maneater is a bit of a guilty pleasure of mine. It is the essence of the cathartic, visceral violence I crave in combat; to the point that I can just zone out and enjoy the grind. It can also be pretty comical and the plot is not a bad one (though a narrative game, this is not).I certainly enjoyed it enough to purchase and play it twice. Once through on the PS4, and now on PC for Truth Quest. It is also surprisingly good on Steam Deck.This all said, if the thought of a super mutant shark rampaging across a port city does not sound like pure dumb fun then Maneater might bore you. You eat, fight, and find collectibles across several map regions. That is the game, cutscenes aside. So no grand RPG here, just an oceanic mayhem sandbox.

_childDocuments_.review: This game isn't all that long, even to get to 100%. But every minute of it is amazing fun. Maneater is surprisingly beautiful: it's got a really gorgeous aesthetic that combines undersea lighting with saturated neon cities. The best way I can describe both this style and the gameplay is, "GTA but as a shark." Gameplay-wise, you're following a solid storyline while a. collecting collectibles that can be a challenge to find/get to; b. eating to empower yourself and mutate specific body parts to customize your powers and appearance and c. doing missions around the map. Non-required missions include killing swimmers, beachgoers etc. (the humans in this game have wrecked the environment and you're a sort of accidental force of natural retribution). During those missions, the GTA style comes into play: a bounty/chase system where increasingly difficult shark hunters come after you in groups, including progressively harder bosses. But you can flee and drop your bounty if you escape.The game's hugely satisfying, beautiful to look at and just generally lots of fun. I definitely recommend it for a few days' happy relaxation!

_childDocuments_.review: I am going to recommend this game because it was a lot of fun to play but there is definitely some glaring issues and it feels more like a 20 dollar game than a 40 dollar game.  I will start with the good things.  The game play is fun and that is the saving grace of this game.  Tearing up boats, fish, people and other predators is exciting.  The map is unique and fun to explore.   The game is not really story rich but the story/narrator are entertaining.  The bad by no means ruined the game but is pretty obvious.  The quest you complete to finish each area is exactly the same.  Different enemies and locations but exactly the same quests.  There is only three different body variations.  I was maxed level and had my body modification maxed out after 7 hours.  The last 3 hours of the game involved vary little actual growth or change which is critical to an RPG.  The biggest problem is the game is only 10 hours long and this is not to beat the game but to 100% it.  I did everything in 10 hours and there is not a lot of reason to replay this game.  I don't think i have ever 100%ed a open world RPG and I have put 100+ hours into some of the best.  My advice buy and play it because its a lot of fun but wait for at least a 50% sale as that is what this game is worth.

_childDocuments_.review: Really funny and original game. It's a very relaxed Metroidvania-style underwater exploration game, where you can relax and work on getting to each collectible and each trick jump at your own pace. The combat is really satisfying, especially with a gamepad which gives force feedback, but it's great with keyboard and mouse too. The story is funny and intriguing, and the world is constantly narrated by a sarcastic narrator voice as if it's a nature documentary. There are tons of pop culture references to find under the sea, with references to popular movies and games.One of the most unique and entertaining games I've ever played. Reminds me of Subnautica, if you were the monster instead.The base game is the best by far. The DLC goes in a totally different direction, and mostly consists of artificial padding (going back to all previous areas to collect items) but at least offered some really fun and intense boss fights. It's worth having the DLC.The game is definitely pretty long if you do everything in the game:- 100% base game with all achievements, all quests, all collectibles, at casual pace: 15h 21m- 100% DLC: 6 hoursMy only wish is that there was something else to do after 100% in the game. Such as random encounters with mutated fish that have random boss abilities, so that you could fight endless bosses in a roguelike way. Sadly there's nothing like that. When you've done everything, there's nothing left to do but swim around as the apex predator with nothing threatening around anymore. I hope they create another DLC or sequel for this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Hello, Kiba Snowpaw here. This old ice wolf has been through many gaming wars, watched countless anime sagas, binged series till his eyes froze over, and has probably read enough manga to have turned every page into a snowflake. I've been around since the Atari 2600 days, friends, so when I give a review, I do so with the weight of those decades behind me. Buckle up, and let's talk about Maneater, a game that promised a deep dive but ended up beached.Maneater. As soon as I saw the words 'shark' and 'RPG' bundled together, my ears perked up more than when I hear the rustle of a takeout bag. As an apex predator myself (albeit a snow-bound one), the concept held a unique appeal. But sadly, my friends, this game is to a fulfilling RPG experience what a goldfish cracker is to sushi - a pale and uninspired imitation.The gameplay premise is simple - eat, grow, and evolve to exact revenge on the fisherman who harmed you. Sound straightforward? Yeah, it is. Almost too straightforward. The game's objectives revolve around devouring specific numbers of marine life or humans, which at first, seems thrilling, like finding the last piece of pizza in the fridge at 2am. But eventually, it gets repetitive, much like eating the same pizza for breakfast, lunch, and dinner for a week straight. And if you're thinking you'll get a dose of captivating story missions to make up for the repetitive objectives, prepare for disappointment, my furry brethren.The world of Maneater is rich and beautifully designed, like a lavishly garnished seafood platter, but it's frustrating to see that many of these 'set pieces', like the cruise ship, serve no significant role in the story or gameplay. Like those plastic lobster decorations on said seafood platter - nice to look at, but lacking substance.Maneater offers three sets of upgrades that promise to enhance your predatory prowess, but they, too, are a letdown. As varied as the toppings on a Margherita pizza - as in, not varied at all. If you're looking for in-depth customization that impacts your playstyle, you'd better swim on, fellow furred gamers.Even the game's length feels like a deflating beach ball. Most players seem to reach 100% completion within 10-12 hours. Now, I don't mind a short game if it's packed with quality content, but Maneater is as thin on the content side as a malnourished herring. The asking price of $40 is as steep as trying to climb an icy mountain in flip-flops.Let's talk about the elephant seal in the room - the PC crashes. Imagine this: you're enjoying your swim, minding your business, and suddenly - BAM! - your PC crashes with a UE4 error message. If you're lucky, it's a gentle crash, merely booting you back to your desktop without erasing your saved game. But if you're unlucky, it's like a full-on belly flop, deleting your save game in the process. Despite the problem being reported back in 2020, there's still no fix. That's like promising to do the dishes and leaving them till they grow fur - unforgivable.The game is not without its merits - the concept, narration, and aesthetic are all pretty cool, like the other side of the pillow on a hot summer night. But at the end of the day, a game is not defined by its cool concepts, but by its execution. And Maneater's execution is about as effective as a cat trying to catch laser pointer dots.In the gaming world, Maneater is akin to that charming rogue who talks a big game but can't deliver when it counts. As much as it pains me to say this, I cannot recommend this game at its full price, or until the crash issues are addressed. If you're really curious, wait for a deep-sea discount before diving in.And here's a little Ice Wolf wisdom to remember: "Gaming, like life, is a balance between holding on and letting go." So let's let go of the disappointment that is Maneater, and hold on to the hope of better gaming experiences.

_childDocuments_.review: The game starts off the rails and then doubles down, then triples down on its ridiculousness. The ridiculous and stupid story may not be for everyone, but for those who appreciate the humor, it works quite well.While the combat may seem simplistic at first, there is more depth to it than meets the eye. Although spamming the bite attack may work in some situations, certain fights require a more strategic approach, and you can unlock other abilities to aid you in combat. Beyond combat, the game offers a variety of activities to keep you entertained. You can explore on land, searching for license plates and boxes in caves, or even take on humans dancing on the beach. While some of these activities can feel like filler content, they do add some variety to the gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a solid and enjoyable experience worth the price when it's on sale. + It was fun playing as a shark.+ I enjoyed the tongue-in-cheek style of humour.+ Cool evolution system, I particularly enjoyed seeing how things changed as I went up the tiers. - The missions felt like mostly repetitive eat X number of creatures.- Fighting felt like wrestling with the controls in the early-mid game. - Equipping a whole set confers additional buffs so it felt sub-optimal to mix and match evolutions.
_childDocuments_.name: Maneater

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the game a few minutes ago and i'd love to say a thing or two about this superb game!Evolution:When the game starts your mother gets killed by the hunter called Pete, who is assisted by his son. He is not fond of fishing, but thats not the main detail here. Pete gets you out of your mother's womb, which sounds weird but thats how it is. He scratches your fin, so when you grow up he will hunt you down and basically will reminisce the time, when he murdered the "mommy shark". You play as a bull shark. Start off small, but as the time progresses you gain evolutions, level up, obtain new body types, fins, jaws and so on. There're a few ages: child, Teen, Elder and Mega (if i am not mistaken those are the ones). Different body types and other armor can be unlocked by playing the game, visiting new locations, searching for underwater sightseeings, killing different types of Apex predators and etc. If you are into games where you evolve and go from child to an absolute monster, this game is genuinely amazing at it's job. I was thrilled to see the same enemies i was scared of being scared of me! Its not even a big game. 10-11 hrs and you will finish the whole story with all the side quests.Story: (no spoilers only the beginning part)As said, the Hunter cuts the bull's belly and you are there. As Pete scratches your fin you bite his hand off, but he gets a new one. You are in a swamp, small, helpless, scared of it's surroundings. However, environment is full of different types of fish, that are small and can be devoured by the small bull shark. As you level up and gain more evolutions story line progresses. Each time you explore a new location a cut scene appears, that shows what Pete and his son are up to. Once you've finished the particular location at 100% or 98% you unlock another cut scene, which, again, shows their work and where they are at. Trust me when i say this, i have never played such an immersive game ever. Oh, forgot to mention, Pete is being recorded by some studio (not sure which), i would assume they are creating a documentary about shark hunters, but it did not go as it had been planned. Excessively heartbreaking story, which i did not expect from this game. When i finished it, i did not want to do what i was supposed to, but, unfortunately, i had no control over a cut scene.P.S this has nothing to do with story, but since it goes along with the game why not elaborate for a bit. During the gameplay one person talks over and gives you details about the bull shark, different ares and all about ocean life (not literally everything but you get the point). This will help you learn more about Sharks and sea life. For example i've learned that Sperm Whales eat sharks!Enemy types:When it came down to potential preys and predators of the sea, i did not expect such a diversity. Now, i know ocean is full of undiscovered creatures, places and what not, but this game had it all! You start off being scared of alligators, then Mako sharks, Humans, Great Whites, Orcas, Sperm Whales, Hammerheads and some other. Best thing about enemies is that, you'll encounter buffed types of the predators. For instance, once you've finished exploring the area you'll have to go against an Apex Mako shark, or Apex greatwhite which adds up to the game. Killing humans can get you in a huge trouble too, as you kill hunters your bounty hunt levels up (not sure what its called exactly, but basically stronger people start to come at you), it can go up to 10 and at that point if you dont possess the bone armor there will be no chance of surviving Pete or ordinary hunters! Furthermore it has its own twist, you must get to lvl 10 in order to obtain unlockable evolutions, hence you become stronger!What is left to say? the game is fantastic! as long as i know it is also getting an expansion. I am extremely hyped about that too!Things i did not like: The game glitches out rarely and it does not work untill you quit it and turn it on again, Apex predators dont show up on the screen which also bugs out the game and you have to go to the main menu then try again, It has quite a lot of stutters and frame drops but dont take it from me, it may be just my PC. Thats about it.I would give it solid 7.5/10, because of the bugs.
_childDocuments_.name: Maneater

_childDocuments_.review: Fun to me but others might considered the mandatory "missions" tedious.To get to the boss for each area you need to do Kill/Consume X creatures side missions, sure they aren't much fun but each can be done in a few minutes so not too bad.Playtime heavily inflated as i leave games on standby often, can only play in short bursts due to eye problems.Had 4 crashes during 100% completion of the main story, not great and with ridiculous stuttering, if i had a worse pc it probably would have crashed more.Overall really decent, heard some issues with Dlc missions, seems the time trials there are really bad but can't judge them yet.Edit: Races weren't too bad, only one had some bad jumps (gates under a bridge with narrow pillars that got in the way)Mission design weren't any better either but they again are short enough that it's fine.Would look forward to another game like this, either Maneater 2 or a sidegrade with a different gigantic predator, just make the missions less tedious, instead of consume just have kill instead, opens up options rather than just mash one button for all of them.

_childDocuments_.review: Rather short (can be completed under 6 hours) action game where you play as a shark. As you progress through the story and gain levels you'll unlock mutations and passive abilities that will allow you to customise you playstyle. It is a solid game with great visuals and fun gameplay.The Truth Quest DLC continues the story after base game and adds ~3h worth of content. There's new area to explore, new mutations to unlock, new boss fights and increased level cap. I enjoyed this expansion but I would recommend waiting for a sale before purchasing it.

_childDocuments_.review: >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>            6/10!!!            <<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<Game is AMAZING, but the lack of upgrades and other cosmetic makes this game feel very boring. It's a grind game that doesn't reward players for the grind. Despite the huge potential to become one of the best shark game ever, it failed to meet the mark by just barely. _childDocuments_.review: This game makes you feel like a shark and you have a mission. It is somewhat open world and wilder than an aquatic Rick James party. Now, I don't know about you guys, but I don't like Sharks, I know they only attack you if you are wet but some part of me hates them instinctively. Despite that I always wanted to be a shark. Not just any shark, but a giant, ferocious one that eats everything in sight. And that's exactly what you get to do in Maneater. You play as a bull shark, the game lets you explore the underwater world like never before. You can eat anything from fish to humans, and chomping on some unsuspecting beach-goers is one of the most satisfying experiences you'll ever have. And if you're lucky, you might just find yourself a little cat named Fluffy that makes for a tasty snack (and you get to call yourself replace the word "man" in the title with ♥♥♥♥♥).The game has it's fair share of memes narrated by Chris Parnell (so hide the women-folk). You've got the "Shark Week" reference that will have you laughing your dorsal fin off, and let's not forget about the "Maneater" song that will have you humming along as you devour everything in your path.Maneater is a fun, easy and short game but well worth you sinking your teeth into, if you catch it on sale. It's got everything you could ever want in a shark game, from the humor to the carnage, and it's all wrapped up in a nice little bow of memes. For a more in-depth take please check out my video review here:

_childDocuments_.review: If you ever wanted to be a hungry, mutated bull shark that gets beaten up by whales, here is your chance!  This stunning game comes with scary attack sounds; annoying edgelord muskellunges that inexplicably attack sharks in The Gulf region by pairing up with adolescent alligators; spring break tourists, and gun-crazy idiots on fishing boats.  I love that the map is separated into salt, brackish, and freshwater regions with (mostly) different enemies.

_childDocuments_.review: I looked forward for this. Bought a first day, when it was released on PC after have it on wishlist since developer place a game on steam. Had my fun, even if I expected little bit more.+ Perfect PC controls and camera, no butchered console convert.+ Graphic is nice, everything on max, V-Sync locked on 60fps on my GTX1080 - very smooth gameplay.+ Gameplay perfect, I really enjoyed manipulation of elesmobranch fish. Remind me my favourite old Fish Frenzy game in 3D.+ Eeach region is unique and have his own charm.+ Difficulty is somehow balanced, not too easy, not too hard. I do not even realize if there´s possibility to make a game harder for second play. - After 6h in game I really wish for option to turn off commentary (at lest you can turn his volume down to 0%)- Somehow I expected more options in Shark´s evolution tree (basically there is bone, electric and shadow modification), with so many kinds of sharks it is shame game allow to play only as bull shark, I wish there would be option for hammerhead, white etc.- I totally miss some "panic" factor between people on beaches. After first attack there should be panic and everybody try to get out of water. I guess same reaction is normal also between sea animal after shark attack.- Constant spawning of new hunter ships right after you destroy one is annoying7/10 - In overal I´m very happy, but there is still some potential for this game to be even better.

_childDocuments_.review: Great open world exploration game where you get to eat everything in sight, ocean life and humans alike.Level/world design is really well done, especially under water. I had a few legitimate jump scares from predators hiding out of sight; so I would say atmosphere and sound are spot on. Mutations and perks keep the game refreshing as you go through each location, evolving and growing in size.The missions in each new zone are repetitive (like far cry games).  DLC added some cool mutations but the level was small.  The final apex predator was very awesome and a lot of fun to fight.  Overall a very fun enjoyable game.

_childDocuments_.review: Love it, like what most other reviews say, roughly 10 hours to 100%, so not really a long-term kinda game.Very repetitive in its tasks, (Eat x amount of humans, eat x amount of fish, kill the big chungus of the lake, repeat), and there's not a whole lot of replayability. If you have issue with the controls, or combat, might want to refund though.Aside from that, if you do like the controls, or just, playing as a shark and the things you can do, you likely will enjoy the game. Due to its overall short playtime, you never really play long enough for the gameplay to become boring, unless you were already sick of it. A fair few people find it "grindy", but personally I didn't find it so, since just chomping whatever's in your way between A and B will generally be good enough, although the collectables help a considerable amount in your growth.TLDR; the ~10 hours story of the oceanic chonker of legend, if you don't enjoy your first 1.5 hours, refund it or smthing. Get on sale, $25 max really.

_childDocuments_.review: Shark go chomp. More chomp make shark big. Big shark chomp bigger. This game is a fun break if you're looking to just eat everything as a genetically questionable shark. _childDocuments_.review: If you played Jaws as a kid and enjoyed it, then this is for you.It's basically Jaws but with shark upgrades and Jerry from Rick and Morty commenting on everything your shark does in a national geographic narrator styled voice.The game itself feels a bit lackluster, there aren't that many places to explore or that many fish to eat or that many upgrades for you to obtain, and the humans are dumb as ♥♥♥♥ and the gameplay gets repetitive quickly, but if you enjoy "fish eat to get big" type of games then you can't really complain as there aren't really any alternatives available.If I could refund it I would because content wise its lacking, but would I play it again if they added more content definitely yes.7/10 would listen to Jerry narrate my life again.
_childDocuments_.name: Maneater

_childDocuments_.review: A fun and relaxing time causing havoc and sea based terror. This is an entertaining game that takes only a little skill to enjoy. For sure one of those games you can log onto at the end of a long day and just eat fleshy beachgoers to your hearts content. Story does seem a little short and some of the leveling and tasks can seem a little repetitive. But not so much as to disenchant you from booting up and vegging out

The only real downer for me was the story, I just felt real sorry for Pete, and the ending was a bit depressing, especially since the voice lines in the game lets you in on Pete and Kyle's relationship.Overall, you play as a killer shark, what more can you ask for?

_childDocuments_.review: I like the theme and the presentation, everything is super pretty and stylish. The problem is that the entire loop is "go and kill x number of creatures in this location" and all the combat is either trivially easy or charging fish weirdly telegraphing their attack (there are only one or two attacks a fish can really have) and everything feeling super imprecise. it's a basic numbers game wrapped in stylish packaging. There's very little skill or nuance to be had, it's just a question of whether you have grinded enough quests to be larger than the enemies.
_childDocuments_.name: Maneater

_childDocuments_.review: Do you ever feel your faith in humanity close to the bottom of the sea?Do you ever get sad about sea pollution?Do you just ever want to have fun by unleashing carnage in a game?Do you have ever felt that you don't belong as a human, I'm sorry about that, but there is hope!You'll go on a human-hunt as a man-eating shark, and you may sometimes hunt for other predators of the ocean.It's over the top, brainless carnage and fun, that is portrayed and narrated as a shark-week TV show. Where the jokes are very much cheesy "dad-esq" jokes in the style, and from the voice actor of the webs newer favourite bottom of the barrel dad, Jerry.It's not a long game at any stretch of the word and I've 100%'d it twice already, and have just started a new playthrough of it now. So I'd say it's well worth it at full price, but at summer sale and up to 50% off, you'd be a fool not to take the plunge and swim a mile in a sharks fins.This game is well worth a playthrough, and I'd give it a recommendation!I will most likely play through it again after I'm through it for the 3rd time, although it might be a few months in between each playthrough.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun for an hour or two, then it starts to get repetitive. The combat isn't exactly challenging, requiring you to simply mash M1 with some dodges thrown in between, and gets insanely boring over time.The missions simply consist of "Go there", "kill that" or "eat that." Even though the evolutions provide some variety, they don't offer any great active abilities, simply making you mash the same buttons with different passives.While most "Feed and Grow"/"Evolution" fans like myself would be willing to accept mediocre gameplay or worse in exchange for a big map with some enemy variety and decent graphics in this beloved niche genre, the devs made an apparently conscious choice to rob us of our favourite gameplay aspect: Limitless growth. There is a pretty low level cap, which increases throughout the story (and DLC), but it will always stop you from becoming significantly bigger than the enemies in the area.All in all the game provided me with 12.5 hrs of gameplay (which included boring 100% grinding in both base game and DLC) and I can confidently say that I will never touch it again.The best part was having Jerry as a narrator.Do not buy at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely cannot possibly overstate how enjoyable and fun this game is.  It's a game that lets you PLAY AS A SHARK!  Those types of games are so damn rare, only other ones I can think of are the Hungry Shark games, and Jaws Unleashed.  The story is a cheesy revenge plot, and the narration can be hilarious; but it's very satisfying watching your Bull Shark grow from a little pup that gets cut out of their mothers womb, to a fully grown terror that can destroy entire fleets of shark-hunting boats and eat pretty much anything in the ocean.  If I must criticize the game, the camera is quite awkward to get used to, there's an annoying bug that affects 10th, 11th, and 12th gen Intel CPU's that causes a majority of crashes (there's a fix for it), the game gave me a weird bit of Thalassophobia, and some of the collectibles are a tad annoying to find.  Overall, I really enjoyed the game, and I PRAY that we eventually get more games in the future that let you play as a shark.(PS: Please protect the ocean, and treat all ocean life with respect.  We have ZERO reason to kill and maim sharks as often as we do.  The ocean is their home, not ours.)

_childDocuments_.review: The only other game, that I'm aware of at least, that has attempted this concept before that wasn't multiplayer only was JAWS Unleashed almost 20 years ago, and it was pure garbage. Maneater is pretty much what that game SHOULD have been. You play as a Shark terrorizing a Southern port town. If that on its own appeals to you, you can stop reading here and just buy it. The game is really fun if you can just enjoy it for what it is. It doesn't over-complicate things, which is both good and bad. Youre playing a shark and youre going around eating people and other sea creatures, that base concept never changes, and while thats fine for the most part, There are times where it can get repetitive and some of the progression feels needlessly grindy. The controls can also be a little awkard at times. Its not game breaking and you can play this just fine with a mouse and keyboard, but it was pretty clearly made with a controller in mind. Bottom line, if youre looking for a game where you get play a shark, basically playing the main role in a b shark attack movie story, this will scratch that itch.

You do not need the DLC to have fun but I would still recommend it!I did find the game wanted to crash a lot. It seems to be tied with Unreal 4 but the game saves so frequently I lost no progress. Bare this in mind.Otherwise 10/10 wish there were more games like this!

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR wait to get it on sale if you really like sharks. (Note: no DLC was played prior to writing this review)From the slow beginnings of a Shark pup in a grimy bayou, to an amusing spectacle of a full grown “Mega Shark” (as the game calls it) reducing an army of Hunters and their boats to pools of tomato paste and scrap metal heaps in a clear gulf. This game’s presentation unquestionably lends itself to forming a visually satisfying and entertaining montage of carnage. However, this game has a combat system more button mashy than the Batman Arkham series and a Ubisoft-esque open world. A pretty art style can only captivate for so long before the brain starts craving for more engaging mechanics. It’s great if you have an hour to kill, but so is Batman Arkham Knight’s challenge mode. At least the ladder has more enemy variety.

_childDocuments_.review: I had no idea that Prototype, except you're a Shark, would be so much fun. As with Prototype, the game is all about a power fantasy where you rip through scores of enemies, eating them to heal. Any dodging mechanic is made superflous as a result, but I'd say the game is better for it. I wouldn't say it's difficult at all; I haven't died even once yet and I'm almost done with the game after beating all of the named hunters and the apex predators.I don't expect much replay value out of this game, and the timings of the special sets could be made to be a bit earlier (you don't get complete sets until you are mostly done with the game) to give us a bit more time to use them, but I also won't begrudge the devs for not cluttering the game with tons of useless items that won't ever be used; I've tried 2 out of the 3 sets so far and I'd say they're both equally viable, giving you the chance to pick based on your aesthetic and playstyle preferences.Overall, I'd say, buy it, it's a solid 8 hours of fun at the least. Or maybe I'm just under the influence of nostalgia for that shark game whose name I can't remember I played as a kid. But yeah, as long as you don't go in expecting a shark simulator, Shark Prototype is a great game accentuated by the documentary-voiced narrator with good and witty writing.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm recommending this, but with caveats.I really, really want to love this game. It's a fun roaming, chomping game where you grow a bull shark up from a brave little pup to the ridiculously absurd 9 meter "mega" shark. Along the way you swim through a variety of environments from bayou swamp all the way out to the deeper waters of the Gulf of Mexico, hunting for food, fighting with competitors, and, yes, eating man, just like it says on the title. Along the way you get to engage in a ridiculous set of mutations and run into a variety of ridiculous pop culture references. The narrative conceit of this being some sort of nature documentary is excellent. The game is narrated by the ever-hysterical Chris Parnell, who manages to deliver the lines with just the right mixture of seriousness and amusement. The other voice actors you hear are pretty solid as well, and the shark hunter, Scaly Pete, is surprisingly well-executed for how thin and light the plot actually is. A full movie of the cut-scenes, start to finish, will run you less than 20 minutes. This is not a game for those looking for dramatic story.The graphics are fantastic. The fish all look incredibly realistic, and it's easy to while away some time just swimming around and watching the fish of all kinds swim to and fro, and occasionally scarf one down, or fend off a predatory barracuda or hammerhead, and just chill.It's almost a great game, and that makes where it falls down that much more painful.1. The AI is abysmal. Prey fish ignore your presence until you bite them; hostile fish, no matter how large you are compared to them, attack you relentlessly once you swim within their attack bubble. This means that you have individual barracuda lashing out at your megashark, when you literally rip them apart in a single bite. 2. Nothing recognizes each other. Makos, hammerheads, and swordfish will all combine to attack you on sight, but ignore each other. None of the sharks, gators, or anything else will actually EAT any of the small fish. Other sharks don't react to blood in the water. While human hunters will come out in force, wave after wave of them throwing themselves to their deaths to kill you, they will ignore other sharks completely and focus on you. You can even end up being attacked by other sharks WHILE the hunters are after you!3. The controls are a little fiddly. At times your shark will bite the wrong thing, or suddenly spin about to attack back at you, and it's not quite clear why.4. After 18 hours of play, I think the game has crashed to desktop at least 20 times.5. The combat gets a bit boring after a while. The individual mutations change things up a bit -- giving you bio-electric powers, or the ability to drain blood, or poison your foes, or what-have-you -- but ultimately it's a set of three or four maneuvers that you need, and button-mashing will suffice in many combats. 6. The lesser shark hunter bosses are terribly boring -- you get the sense they were supposed to be a bit more developed, but they hadn't gotten their hands around it by the time they had to go to press.Like I said - it's ALMOST a great game. I certainly enjoyed it -- but I wish it had spent just a bit more time in the studio. More voice acting, better AI, and a bit tighter code, and this would be as close to perfection as could be.

_childDocuments_.review: Maneater geniunely sounds and looks like fun on paper, and it is - for an hour or so. Then you have a good idea of what the game has to offer: mindless ‘fun’, frustrating controls and extremely repetitive gameplay.It’s a shark’s revenge story in which you start of small. Growing up can be done by feeding on wildlife and humans that will earn you experience, therefore making you bigger and stronger. Eventually you will also unlock more skills. It’s all still pretty good for now.The levels themselves are nicely made, with plenty of details, plenty of ways to get around and a good population of humans, wildlife and vegetation. The activities you can do are okay to do, but since you’re a shark there’s not all that much variety. These activities range from finding landmarks and treasure chests to finding license plates and more.All still kind of good here.But then the combat: it is repetitive and frustrating, having you mash buttons to attack other smaller (underleveled or equally leveled) wildlife and humans. And there are overpowered (higher level) species lurking in these open waters that are tough(er) to take down, naturally, and give chase (but they give up rather easily). Same story goes for human hunters, and they’re even harder to take down because the target lock system doesn’t work properly (or for me anyway) and they’re naturally above water (until the boat is destroyed), meaning you have to use the previously mentioned frustrating controls.The combat is so mind numbingly simplistic because of the (initially) rather limited moves of your shark and the button mashing just doesn’t help either. The whole thing just doesn’t gel together as it should. Here’s when the game is at its worst. Unfortunately, it’s also the most important aspect of the game.Your shark can also be leveled up by eating wildlife and humans. Eventually you will unlock some skills that can make things a little easier and less stale, but for me it just wasn’t enough to keep my entertained. It’s a very superficial game and I think it knows but that doesn’t make it any better in this case.Graphically it’s kind of a pretty game. As I mentioned the levels are pretty open, with wildlife and humans swimming around, humans in boats and on land and lots of vegetation that make the levels look natural and semi-real life.The voice acting is over the top, but it fits the (narrative) style the game is aiming for. The screams are fun at first and then they’re not.Would I recommend this? I think you already know the answer: it’s a definitive no. Would I recommend it in a sale? No, unless you can maybe get it for $10 or less. I didn’t have fun with it, maybe you will, but I can think of 10 different games that *are* fun instead.

_childDocuments_.review: I would like to preface this review by saying I picked up a key for $15, and you should take that into account while considering my thoughts. At the time of review I have gotten 100% on the game and have done everything there is do do even outside of that including maxing out all of the mutations. So as far as a price to playtime ratio I cant recommend the game at any price over $15. Keep in mind there is a DLC coming out soon but that'll set you back an additional $15 so I would hope it adds a good sum of content. Having said that its be hard not to buy the DLC because I have to admit regardless of the short length, this game is a ton of fun!Okay with that out of the way lets briefly touch on the sound design and music. As far as music is concerned its basically unnoticed. Now I don't say that to bash the music as it fits the game well but its semi-infrequent and played at a low volume. Its more atmospheric music than something your meant to focus on, and it actually makes the collection process really relaxing.  Now the sound design itself is pretty good generally speaking and it gives you satisfying feedback when chomping into a crocodile or whatever else you decide to eat. This also goes for the water and boat sounds, it all sounds as it should. I think my only real gripe is the humans yell the same one or two things every time you attack them, which you will do a lot while going for completion. Now i'll go over story, which I actually thing is a highlight of this game. I wont go into specifics to avoid spoilers. The basic premise is there's a show Called "Maneater" and we as the shark pop up in the show here and there. You go about your business completing your quests and objectives then once you reach a certain point in each part they will play a cut scene involving the full cast. Its really goofy and over the top but i couldn't wait to see it through!Alright on to the meat and potatoes, the game play and controls! First ill mention that I played the game using mouse and keyboard. I would imagine it works great on controller but all I can say is that it was a great mouse and keyboard experience. You get to hold on to your prey and thrash around your mouse to tear them apart. All the keys are able to be rebinded. I personally changed the dive, active ability, and sonar keys due to the frequency in which I used it. It may feel slightly clunky at first but once you get into a grove it feels super smooth and surprisingly tactical. The game play itself is focused on two main things, killing targets and collecting various items. The combat difficulty can be made very easy if you feed often to level up or very hard if you opt to rush through. I enjoy the combat but again it can feel spammy or chaotic until you learn to properly employ your doge and active ability of choice. The collection aspect is pretty fun too in my opinion. Its organized very well and going around the zones checking things off till you see the 100% completion is very satisfying. If you like open world games I wouldn't be surprised if you come out with a 100% too! Don't overpay but if you can get it for cheap you will have a lot of high octane fun!

name: Risk of Rain 2
detailed_description: SURVIVE AN ALIEN PLANET Over a dozen handcrafted locales await, each packed with challenging monsters and enormous bosses that oppose your continued existence. Fight your way to the final boss and escape or continue your run indefinitely to see just how long you can survive. A unique scaling system means both you and your foes limitlessly increase in power over the course of a game. DISCOVER POWERFUL NEW ITEMS More than 110 items keep each run fresh and full of new challenge. The more items you collect, the more their effects combine, the more surprising some of those combinations might be. The more items you encounter, the more lore (and strategy) you’ll discover through the logs. UNLOCK NEW WAYS TO PLAY Unlock a crew of eleven playable survivors, each with their own unique combat style and alternate skills to master. Learn the secrets of the Artifacts to toggle gameplay modifiers like friendly fire, random survivor spawns, item selection and more. With randomized stages, enemies, and items, no run will ever be the same. PLAY SOLO OR CO-OP Tackle the adventure solo or with up to three friends in online co-op, or compete in the rotating challenge of the Prismatic Trials. Brand new survivors like the Captain and MUL-T join classic survivors such as the Engineer, Huntress, and--of course--the Commando.

_childDocuments_.review: Risk of Rain 2 is, despite all it's been through in the past few weeks, still a unique game with incredible, engaging gameplay. It is still worth the money and I can't call the game "ruined" due to Gearbox's delivery of the update.HOWEVER, I can't help but notice that the game feels very different with the release of SotS. It's no longer as smooth as it used to be, plenty of new bugs were introduced and the game does not feel as satisfying to play as it used to:- a lot of audio feels gutted- many mechanics are now tied to FPS (which is constantly changing due to how performance-heavy RoR2 gets at certain points like multiple loops)- UI feels alien and unresponsive (like, how in the world do you ♥♥♥♥ up what tab does??? why cant I sprint now??? why do I not see my money while pressing tab?? huh???)- many features (like one-shot protection) are just straight up broken for some reason, changing the way the game has to be played now with this in mindNaturally, these are BUGS, they are to be expected with new updates and will probably be fixed soon. The update also brought many positive changes like new environments and killer music. The game is nowhere near "ruined", but the direction Gearbox seems to have taken with RoR2 makes me scared for what the future holds for this beloved IP. TL;DR: still a great game but I beg Gearbox to not strangle my dear baby with another bunch of poor corporate decisions.Thanks for reading xoxo

_childDocuments_.review: OK, this thing didn't need another positive review since the day one due to the hype, so I didn't recommend it at first, just for the sake of lowering the expectations. Now, for the first time ever, I decided to delete my first review and replace it with a big thumbs up, even though I'm usually too lazy to write something, let alone re-writing.Basically, two things work for me here: diversity and exploration.While you usually have one playable hero and a bunch of items in a typical roguelike, Risk of Rain 2 already has eight characters to provide you with different playstyles (and that's an Early Access!). Moreover, they also got alternative skills to choose from in the latest update, so you have even more options now. Literally everything in the game tries to work towards variety: weapons, abilities, carriable items (including game-changing ones), achievements that unlock them, altars, monsters and bosses of different types, and what I love the most about this game is the obscurity of everything around. Sure, you get some general idea, like the characters being called survivors, all wearing the same kind of helmet and trying to escape from aggressive monsters. However, the rest is largely a mystery, and you only get slight hints about the purpose of things and what's going on. This allows developers to unleash their imagination at its full potential, and having a chamber pot with legs as one of the most dangerous bosses is the thing that I truly admire, loving and hating it at the same time.It's all drawn in single style, however, and doesn't look too absurd, which is a good thing. It's just mysterious, and fun. Besides, being in a full 3D makes it perfectly fit for exploration, despite the levels being hand-drawn instead of procedurally generated. In fact, remembering them and learning their well-hidden secrets provides the sense of progression, yet there are so many randomly placed objects and monsters that you do not tend to get bored for a long time. In addition, the game already has a number of mods around, if you wish to make your experience even more diverse.My first complaints were about the somewhat ascetic level design combined with too challenging geometry in a number of places. However, as the game keeps getting filled with various content, this is getting fixed by itself, and right at this moment there's basically nothing left for me to whine about.Still, I should also add a couple of words about the soundtrack. That main theme is great, but... to be honest, the overall quality is far below the bar set by the prequel (which is an awesome game, too). So, let's just believe in Chris and remember that it's an Early Access. The game is already a masterpiece in its current state, and having some friends to play this in co-op makes me love it even more than I could imagine.

_childDocuments_.review: I was a bit skeptical when I heard risk of rain was going 3D, but this game has proven how very wrong I was.  The combat feels fluid and fair, and the devs took verticality into account as an actual mechanic, and a nice world.  Overall, there are only 2 real problems I have with the game right now:1) Only 1 character on startup for a multiplayer game is risky.  Having at least 2 means that players can look at eachother and think "wow, he's better than me at X, but at least I do Y. We both do our own thing."  While I expect this to resolve itself over time, as the average unlock number rises, it's still a bit rough starting out.2) Navigation in the world can be awkward.  While I don't expect a full minimap with pointers to everywhere you want to go, it takes much longer in this game to explore an area than it did in the first game.  Since the timers are still relatively similar, this means that if it takes a while to find the teleporter, it can be much more punishing in the first game.  I'd like if teleporters had a space ray that grew as the level progressed, becoming easier and easier to see.  That way, it sets a soft limit on how long the player can go without finding it, while still keeping that element of luck/skill in tracking it down early.  Additionally, boxes should be a bit easier to see.  This could either be through making the colors pop a bit more, or even just letting pings be permanent, so you can always see them through walls.  Overall, I've been having a lot of fun with this game, and really look forward to where it goes in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATED REVIEW ABOVE THE LINEThe patches since the update dropped have course-corrected the game in a very positive way. The major problems have been eliminated, and I actually have faith in the ROR team at Gearbox now. I fully believe the update release was rushed by the higher ups, and that things were able to slip through the cracks because of this. I can now recommend this game once again. -------------------------------------------------------------OLD REVIEW, WILL DELETE LATERThis update (not specifically the DLC, but the overall patch) has broken the game in ways I would never have thought possible. This was one of my favorites, but now the game is plagued by bad coding. I will keep issues with the DLC out of this review. This review is for the base game.  Almost everything about how the game works is now tied in some way to the frame rate. Weapon spread, damage, player momentum, enemy health, enemy damage, enemy pathfinding, enemy behavior, player ability range, player ability duration, damage taken, etc... None of this was an issue before. The new health bar UI is atrocious and makes it a challenge to see how much health you have at that exact moment. Take a lot of damage and want to see your remaining health? The bar now slowly drains to where your current HP is. Even worse if you picked up an infusion item. Now your healthbar is red, and the damage taken section of your healthbar is also red, making it literally indecipherable at a glance. The final boss can be invincible now. Acrid's leap is unusable. Pressing tab interrupts sprinting and hovering. Tri-shops don't show item outlines. Aspect drop rate was multiplied by 100. Getting certain aspects causes your item pickups to be multiplied by 1000. Projectiles now fire from the center of your character model regardless of what the attack animation looks like (This results in, among other things, Artificer killing herself when using her Ice Spear, as it spawns inside/behind her head.) Anti-aliasing is now permanently enabled and Gearbox even removed the AA options. There is never a good excuse for removing options like that. There were some genuinely good changes made, such as being able to inspect items to see the actual stats. Blind pests and brass contraptions not being able to autoaim if you have not yet seen them. But these changes are vastly overshadowed by how bungled the coding of the whole game is now.I sincerely hope the Risk of Rain team at Gearbox can swallow their pride and work with the modding community to fix these problems. The modding community has already worked out where the code goes wrong and ties everything to the framerate, for example. Please fix our game, and please do it right.
