_childDocuments_.review: I've been waiting till I got all the achievements to write this review, and well today is the day. Long story short, this game is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ amazing. Buy it, get some friends to buy it and you will have a wonderful time. This game is a 10/10 in every category and everyone needs to experience it. But, personally I feel this game isn't deserving of such a short review so here we go.-Gameplay and CharactersThe initial gameplay is just amazing and borderline addicting. It, of course, is a roguelike so you will be trying and dying and trying again but that death is almost never frustrating, especially in the early game. This is because you will be getting item after item, working to unlock everything you can and every run feels like you are making progress even if you didn't get much further than the last run. And the main gameplay elements feel amazing because of the great cast of characters. They all feel unique with their own advantages and disadvantages and the feeling of finally unlocking a new character is unmatched by any other roguelike. In other games, you may unlock another character but many times they just feel like a reskin of the first character with a different weapons but here each character plays so vastly different from one another it is incredible. The cast of characters range from a gunslinging dude in a space suit, to a lizard dog thing that shoots acid at people. Some of my favorites include Mercenary - a samurai who while very tough is just fun to play - Captain - who has an amazing primary shotgun but is bogged down by lack of mobility - and Loader - who is basically spiderman mixed with the prawn suit from subnautica. The best part is that no character feels really bad. Some are worse than others to me but it allows everyone to find someone they enjoy playing and stick with them. Plus they all have more unlockable skins and abilities which makes you want to play them all. -Atmosphere music and GraphicsThe atmosphere in this game is top ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ notch. Each area is distinct with a certain style that is only helped by the amazing score. When I first heard it, I likened it to a mix of celeste and subnautica. An oddly calming and alien blend that I know see and distinctly risk of rain. The music in the final level is downright a masterpiece,  and after playing the first game, I can say that the music is some of my favorite rivaled only by celeste and the doom games. The graphics likewise, are amazing. Compared to the low res pixel art of the first game, the models here looks so damn nice. The characters and items fit perfectly in these truly breathtaking levels. Scorched Acres, Titanic Plains and Sundered Grove are just beautiful and a joy to explore and look at. Then you have the more alien worlds like Gilded Coast and the Bulwark Ambry which give you such a good sense of atmosphere and make me wish I could just teleport there and listen to the soundtrack while reflecting on life as a whole. -Level design The interesting part about this game is that while it is a rogulike the levels aren't completely random. They are always pretty much the same with some areas not being available sometimes with bridges being out or tunnels being blocked. This does wonders to the gameplay because you can become familer with the stages while also having variety from run to run. Plus there is the fact that there are an average of 2 different locals you can visit for each of the 5 stages. This does lead to some flaws with some being better than others but on the whole it is very nice and I hope to see more stages added to each level. As for each level, They are all very good but have a few flaws. Some are much harder to navigate if you character doesn't have any mobility and some are harder to find the teleporter, but on the whole they are all quite good. -Enemies and BossesThe enemies in this game are just great. You have certain enemies like beetles and hermit crabs that pose no threat but on the opposite side of the spectrum you have the most terrifying enemies like parents, greater wisps and elder lemurians who I still have nightmares about to this day. These enemies all spawn in different ratios and certain enemies only spawn on certain levels which adds to the variety and uniqueness of each stage. Having different types of enemies makes the player think but there aren't too many overall types as to overwhelm the player. The extra variety comes in the form of elites which can make even the most trivial enemies forces to be reckoned with. Then there are the bosses which come in 10 forms and spawn as teleporter bosses or as regular enemies in later stages. They are all unique and pose different challenges. There are also more formal bosses like the Alloy Worship Unit, Aurelionite and the Final boss. The first 2 are just reskins of other bosses but the Final boss is something special. I would say he might be the weakest part of the game but that is only because I have only fought him a few times. When the 1.0 update first came out, he was almost impossible on monsoon but now I feel like he is a little more balanced. Again I would have to fight him more to develop a final opinion but as for a final boss, he fits quite well.-DifficultyThe challenge this game poses can be quite daunting at first but I feel like on the whole it is perfect. To start there are 3 difficulties to choose which affect enemies, regen and other factors which lets players choose how they want to play but there is also the time mechanic. The longer you take on a stage the harder the game gets. This means that you have to balance your time between looking for items and beating the stages and progressing. This makes for a great difficulty curve and I would say the only spike in difficulty is on stage 5. It is insanely hard and will be one of the biggest roadblocks in any run. But there is also more choice in difficulty, because you can end the run by beating the final boss or looping which sends you through earlier stages with much much harder enemies. I prefer to loop because it allows for crazier god runs but overall it is amazing to have so much choice.-Fun with friendsBefore I wrap this up I want to touch on how amazing this game is with friends. Most of my playtime was with my friend who had most of the stuff unlocked already and it made the game easier to get into. Now playing with 2 or 3 other people is just great. Failing over and over again is much better with friends, and it works just great here. The only issue is that it is much much harder in multiplayer but I would prefer that to it being a complete cakewalk. -Final ThoughtsOverall this game has been a joy, and though I have most things completed I still want to keep playing. I may try it with mods or might just stick to vanilla and see how good of a run I can get. I would also like to point out artifacts which I am very mixed on. They can make the game hectic and amazing but sometimes command just breaks the game to a point where is gets stale. That is to no ones fault but my own but I can't help but feel like I'm cheating. Hell, I didn't even beat the final boss on monsoon without artifacts till the time I'm writing this review. Anyways, I am extremely excited about the future of this game with more updates and DLC and I hope the next one will be able to rekindle that magic of unlocking a new character for a first time. And if you made down here without buying the game, what is wrong with you?!

_childDocuments_.review: I never do this in roguelites, which I have played a ton of over the years, but I just quit to desktop out of a strong run. How do I know it was strong? I wasn't taking noticeable damage in boss fights and enemies died when I clicked them. I don't really know why this was happening, but it was. Why did I quit to desktop? I loaded into what might've been the 5th or 6th area, after about a 30 minute play session, saw some familiar, boring enemies spawn, and said to myself, "I'm tired of this."I dont get the goal of this game. Is it 'be a badass spaceman'? Is it 'carefully concoct an efficient build'? What's the end-game? Are there 7 levels? 12? The answer to my questions about Risk of Rain was constantly, 'I don't know'. Why does my spaceman have no map? Where's the teleporter? Is now a good time to do the teleporter? What do the items do? What does leveling up do? Why do I have to move so far, so slowly, when there's so much empty space? How do I spend this 1,200 dollars? Where is the FUGGING TELEPORTER? Why don't I keep money between levels? Why do my support units never lose HP? I don't know. I don't care. There'll be no joy in finding out.An absence of information makes this game feel empty and cynical. It is torn between 'frantic shooter' and 'Walk through empty space until you see the next loot/macguffin/money.' Chests good, going slow bad. There are all these beautiful environmental installations and life-forms which end up feeling like so many miles of pavement. When I loaded into a new area with a bunch of chests nearby, my reaction was to stand still until enemies auto-spawned, so I could get money to spend on the chests, which give... random buffs. Fish after fish in a barrel. Something was lost when I realized I could hold down primary-fire. Something was lost when I stopped checking my cooldowns and instead just periodically hit every ability key as I dodged around. You just keep shooting guys, that's it.This is one of those roguelites where I kept restarting in hopes of reaching the fun part but it was always just out of reach. Didn't hold my interest.

_childDocuments_.review: is everything you hoped it to be. It has the same feel and gives off the same vibes as the first game, there's just an extra dimension added. Even though the game is still in Early Access, and it needs some additional work, probably what needs to be said has already been done so through more than 6000 reviews in the first 3-4 days after release. This is definitely indie gaming at its best.Whether you played or enjoyed the first game, you will find that this game to be refreshing experience. The same ideas of progressively increasing difficulty and needing to manage resources and time are kept intact. Adding the extra dimension means that you have to worry about a few extra things while playing, namely, aiming with a mouse and using the keyboard for movements, instead of using a controller (which I find to be nearly impossible at the moment to play). I would just advise you to go in with a mindset of playing a brand new game instead of a sequel. If you expect to cheese your way through some of the enemies by standing where they cannot seem to reach you like in the first game, you will need to change up your strategies a bit. If you have no expectations, then just dive in.After taking a quick try at a single-player game, I quickly dove in with a friend for a co-op session. He's from Eastern Europe, I am in the USA. We played 3 hours straight and saw lag maybe once during that whole time. I saw a review posted just now about someone saying online multiplayer not working, I suspect it is not because of anything actually broken in the game.The concept behind the game is very simple, the game starts on Easy and gradually increases in difficulty with a set timer. Spend time to farm coins so that you can use to open crates/chests and gain power-ups before trying to engage in the boss. (Keep in mind that after you activate the teleporter to begin the boss fight, the remaining unclaimed boxes/crates/etc. will no longer be available.) The simple concept gives you a clearcut goal to work with, because the timer continues even as you move into the next area. This is just like the original game, so people familiar with the first will feel right at home in terms of the idea. You can farm money and try to open up all of the crates and gather all of the loot from one area before engaging in the boss. But the time wasted might mean disaster immediately or in subsequent area(s).As I already mentioned, the controller is practically impossible to use at the moment. The button configuration is the same as the first game, but there's added aiming componenent in 3D. There's no aim-assist, and I couldn't keep my finger off the jump button to avoid enemy fire while running around. But seeing as the right thumb is used for jumping and aiming in different locations, I was constantly sacrificing one basic necessity for another. Of course I didn't try to remap anything and switched to KB+M, which offered better gameplay experience, so I stuck with it. So if you are someone who absolutely must use the controller, I would say wait for some kind of aim-assist to be implemented before you take the dive.I think because of the game being in Early Access, we should expect to see improvements in the future. The biggest drawback right now is the lack of procedural generation of levels. If this game were to maintain that rogue-like feel, it will need more than just permadeath. The levels are the same currently, the only changes from run to run seems to be the spawning locations of the player(s) and the teleporter. I am unsure how many bosses the game currently cycles through, but in our 3 hours of playing, we saw at least 5-6. So the runs will definitely have some variety, but just not the terrain changes that you might also come to expect from a rogue-like. Also some items and enemies may need to be rebalanced, but that comes with Early Access territory. There are so many different things to learn and so many different things to see, I am really looking forward to playing more really soon!My biggest gripe with this game right now is finding that silly teleporter. It's so difficult to see it, especially in the darker levels. It's nearly impossible in that level with the dimly-lit caverns and dark-colored water. Couple that difficult-to-find teleporter with the enormity of most of the levels, we would find ourselves running right past it at times. Even though it is your choice to activate the teleporter whenever you are ready, we often were ready but really wanted a navigator to the teleporter instead.Definitely a KB+M game at the moment, despite full controller support available.Risk of Rain in 3D, it's amazing.Soothing, relaxing, and chill. It slowly lulls you in before raining a bunch of enemies to blow you into bits.The 3 difficulty selections in the beginning plus the uptick in difficulty gradient during each run based on a timer works well to introduce new players as well as those who want a challenge. Intended difficulty is pretty tough, but still fun.Totally worth the asking price, currently at $19.99 USD. And if you caught the deal when the game was BOGO, then that's a total steal, in my opinion.+So much fun!+Online Co-op that worked really well.+Same basic and fantastic concept, reworked into 3 dimensions.+Fantastic music to set the atmosphere.-Where is the procedural generation in levels in my rogue-like?-Where's the teleporter? This often invisible but crucial part of the game should have a slightly more obvious appearance.-Some characters/enemies/items probably need to be rebalanced, this will probably be driven by the community.If you haven't played  yet, you definitely should. It's action-packed fun and works so well in online co-op, so grab a friend or two and take the dive!

_childDocuments_.review: Risk of Rain 2 is the sequel to its older, 2D self of the same namesake. This one features 3D, open areas, and a lot of new ways to play the game. You can pick from a variety of various characters to play as based upon your personal play style, and there's a few variations of abilities per character. It keeps characters feeling fresh, and since this game is a rogue-like, it has plenty of replayability.The game features a standard difficulty mechanic with your typical Easy/Medium/Hard, but newcomers to the series may not know that it has an ever-increasing difficulty naturally. The longer you take to complete each level, the more difficult it will get. You'll want to grab as many items and whatnot as you can before it gets too hard or you may find yourself struggling. In co-op, I personally find that the difficulty spikes aren't too bad. This leads me to my next point.Risk of Rain 2 has wonderful online co-op. You can play with up to 3 friends in each of your runs. It helps balance out enemy numbers and even bosses. I personally think it makes challenge totems easier and more worth the effort. It's also a great game to just generally kick back and enjoy with some friends if you're looking for something to do and burn some time.Overall, I think Risk of Rain 2 is a steal, and for the amount of content they're adding/already have added combined with the near infinite build possibilities circa Binding of Isaac, you'd be silly to pass this up if you're a fan of roguelikes or looking to get into the genre as a whole. If you want to wait for a sale, that's even better because you're REALLY getting a bargain at a sale price.

_childDocuments_.review: As of writing this review, Risk of Rain 2 is still in effectively an Early Access period, with its planned June update on the near horizon. Despite being someone who abhors pre-orders and shies away from early access titles, as a huge fan of the first game I couldn’t help but see if the stellar game that was Risk of Rain 1 survived the shift to 3D. And I can happily say the series has not survived…it’s absolutely thrived. Risk of Rain 2 is a gorgeous love letter to the first game, with gameplay arguably better than its predecessor thanks to the third dimension, visuals and music that are a joy to indulge in, and an insane amount of potential and promise that I have no doubt the tiny team of Hopoo recognizes and will capitalize on, if the sampling we already have is anything to go off of.Risk of Rain 2 is a class-based, third-person, action rogue-like. In most ways, it is exactly like its predecessor. There are different characters with unique abilities that emphasize different playstyles, a variety of interesting enemies and bosses, chests randomly stocked with a plethora of different items (many of which unlocked through performing different tasks on your runs) that enhance you in various ways, and perma-death. Just as in the last game, you spawn in different lands scattered with chests, shrines, enemies, and the teleporter. Activating it starts an event where a big boss and lots of enemies rapidly spawn while you stand nearby, ‘charging’ the teleporter. Complete the event, hop through the teleporter, and go to the next area—rinse and repeat as you get more powerful to match the increasingly-strong enemies and bosses.However, the third dimension introduced in Risk of Rain 2 adds an incredible amount of depth (pun intended) to the combat of the game. Whereas I-frames and tanking were your only real options for evasion in the 2D predecessor, in RoR2 evasion and mobility are shining stars. You can run around enemies, leap over them, dive out of the way of projectiles; the movement of RoR2 feels satisfying and works perfectly with the re-designed enemies and mechanics for the 3D space.The rogue-like aspects of the series are also fantastic. This was largely to be expected—Hopoo really nailed that satisfying feeling of growing in power with random items providing tons of unique effects, and fighting powerful monstrosities. Item selection is still sparse compared to the finished first game, but I have no doubts we’ll be getting a ton of fun new additions to add to the already-passable arsenal. I’ve got over 100 hours in the game and can assure you, there’s already enough variety now! Bosses and enemies are very unique and interesting; again, more would be much appreciated, but with that promised already I have no real worries there—I’m already enjoying fighting what we have.Balancing issues aren’t too prevalent, though hopefully as development continues a few small gripes I have will be addressed. Damage does get a little absurd late into runs, to the point where only one-shots are realistic threats—the addition of armor mechanics from the first game would be great. Fire damage is also still over-tuned in my opinion, and some enemies need slight reworks. But overall, the game is in a great state balance-wise.Sadly the weakest aspect of Risk of Rain 2 thus far. As it’s in Early Access, most of the item and enemy descriptions are blank, and it lacks the final stage that Risk of Rain delivered. These all are promised to be finished by the end of the year or so, but it is definitely a problem at the moment. However, I will note the few things that do have descriptions paint an arguably more interesting story than even the first game had, so I’m extremely excited to see how this aspect will grow and development—what we have hints at an incredibly strong aspect of the game to come.Just like its predecessor, Risk of Rain 2 boasts incredible replay-ability. The RNG nature of the game means no two runs will be alike, and combined with the unique playstyles of the several different characters we already have (with more to come!), there’s a ton to see and try out. Maybe one run you’ll blast everything away instantly with a crit build with Commando, the next you’ll develop an obsession for fungus as Engineer, and another you’ll be zipping around the map swinging a samurai sword like a madman. The Red and Lunar items especially contribute to this, as their rarity means each one will change up the run substantially with their unique and powerful effects (Except for H3AD-ST v.2, they need a massive buff ASAP!). I will admit, I was skeptical of how good the visuals of Risk of Rain 2 would be. After all, I had fallen in love with the gorgeous pixel art of the original, how could that possibly translate to 3D? Well, I can happily say Hopoo absolutely blew me away with what they came up with. The game’s cell-shaded style looks positively amazing, with stark and vivid colors being a feast for the eyes. I especially enjoy the slightly dark nature of the lands themselves, which make your colorful-item-covered character seem all the more ‘wrong’, in a good way! Enemy designs translated fantastically as well, especially the Magma Worm, a classic staple from the first game. There are few games that have genuinely taken me aback with a particular visual; some games have certainly wowed me with their overall design, but very few have ever made me pause and just say…woah. This is one of those games—standing at the mouth of a frosty whitish-blue cave and staring out towards a frozen beach in the distance, and staring as a blinding white-orange enormous Magma Worm erupted from the ground and soared high into the air with a deafening roar, spewing firey rocks around it—yeah, it’s safe to say the visuals are better than they’ve ever been in the series.This of course goes hand-in-hand with the visuals, but the stages we have so far are absolutely beautiful. Each has their own unique design, and the later levels perfectly emphasize the growing hostility of the land itself towards our character’s continued journey (and slaughter). There are some problems with the gameplay design thus far however—the Roost feels a little boring and uninspired compared to the other levels, the Abysmal Depths have a lot of empty space and just get way too dark when enemies start messing with the lighting (Looking at you, Overloading Worm!), and the Gilded Coast is just a absolute pain in its current design for basically no real reward. There’s definitely some room for improvement on this point, and more stages are definitely needed, but what we have right now is by no means bad gameplay-wise.Just like the first game, the muted music of Risk of Rain 2 is fantastically chill. No one track is very special in my opinion, but they all perfectly set the tone for each level and menu, often without you even explicitly noticing them. In addition, enemies sounds notably great and in some places even improved—wisps and especially lesser wisps are not nearly as annoying-sounding as they were in the first game, for example.Overall Risk of Rain 2, even in its current very incomplete state is an absolute blast. Every aspect of it that’s complete is, in my opinion, a improvement over its predecessor—visuals are gorgeous, sound design is a bit more polished, gameplay is undoubtedly more nuanced and interesting—and the aspects that aren’t yet complete—item/stage/character/enemy variety, storytelling—already show incredible promise. Even if Hopoo were to announce this is actually the complete game, I would still be able to recommend it, and given I have absolute faith in them to flesh out the game further I am unable to recommend it enough.

You can customize the difficulty to an extent to be as punishing as you really want it but this is by no means an easy title regardless. To supplement the ever increasing difficulty is the various items you can collect throughout the levels to increase your odds of survival. This game is hard and it can get repetitive since it does not change much throughout playthroughs. Personally I did not like the title due to how grindingly repetitive it got after a few difficulty (to me frustrating) rounds. However, I can respect the vision of the developers as well as its affordability. Just because this title was not for me does not mean its not for you. _childDocuments_.review: As an avid Risk of Rain player who has invested hundreds of hours mindlessly mowing down Lemurians, Risk of Rain 2 is a game in which I have waited patiently for ever since its announcement. Needless to say, I was not let down. Risk of Rain 2 carries over the original Risk of Rain experience perfectly into a 3D setting. With a good balance of new and old, Risk of Rain 2 highlights exactly what a good sequel should be: building upon a previous game with some spicy new flavor. Perhaps the greatest part of this style of execution, is the sheer amazement created from seeing old 2D enemies in a new light. Although it may seem like the art style is a bit lacking, its reference to the original game absolutely perfect. The less detailed 3D textures pays homage to the low quality 2D sprites of the original game. And to be honest, I prefer this art style over the realistic style of a majority of triple-A titles. The unique effects accompanying elites also is masterfully done. With smaller monsters receiving more mild changes to large bosses becoming drastically different, it's clear that the emphasis placed on certain enemies is well calculated (the overloading magma worm is insane). Additionally, a lot of items now add visual effects and changes to your character which is wonderful. It's nice to get some feedback for your in-game actions, which is a significant  change from the original. The map design in Risk of Rain 2 clearly reflects the design of the original RoR. As for now the map pool might be low, but it’s already at a sizable amount to be more than playable without getting boring. And of course, nobody can forget the legendary music. Hiring the same musician that made the bangers in the original, Risk of Rain 2 has a top tier soundtrack.Unfortunately, Risk of Rain 2 is not for everybody. In my opinion, the game is worth 20$, but some of my friends think it’s not worth anywhere near that amount. One even thinks Risk of Rain 2 isn’t worth a penny and should be a free game. According to him, the game is "stupid" because you just do the same thing over and over. I fail to understand his point. Every game in existence revolves around doing the same thing over and over. But I guess for some people, the idea of permadeath and starting from the beginning could be daunting. Unfortunately for them, permadeath is a staple of roguelikes and it is what makes the "Risk" in Risk of Rain.Plus, there is a clear incentive to continually play. Risk of Rain 2 has a vast array of new items and characters to unlock through play and when artifacts get released in the future there will be even more ways to spice up gameplay.Because Risk of Rain 2 shares a vast amount of traits with the original Risk of Rain, it should be noted that anyone who likes the original will love this too. Likewise, if you believe that the original is boring and repetitive, then this game won’t be right for you.I’d recommend giving the original a play before hopping into Risk of Rain 2. You’ll understand the game a lot better and have a lot of fun in the process. The original Risk of Rain also has a lot more content than Risk of Rain 2 as of now, so you'll have more to go through at a cheaper price too.Of course, a lot more content is going to be added to Risk of Rain 2 in the future which will only make the game better and better. That being said, the price of the game might be raised in the future as more content gets added so pick it up early!

_childDocuments_.review: First off: I love RoR2! I've played hundreds of hours. If you haven't played it, buy the base game, right now!!! The reviews used to be overwhelmingly positive, until the new DLC tanked it. The base game deserves a high rating. Survivors of the Void DLC is also pretty good, and adds a fair amount of fun content. I recommend it as well. BUT....DO NOT BUY Seekers of the Storm DLC. Yes, they fixed some of the bugs that were glaringly apparent at launch, but it's still completely under-cooked and uninspired. First, let's talk about the price. $15 is insane for an expansion of a handful of maps, 3 half-baked playable characters, and however many items (17 I think), when the base games is around $25 or less.  You aren't getting anywhere near double the content of the base game, yet they're asking you to pay more than half of the base game cost. The new maps are just okay, but probably the best part of the DLC. A couple of them are well designed and fun, and a couple are the opposite. The new characters feel like modded characters. Modded characters aren't polished, many of them are still fun as hell to play, but they all have one thing in common that makes the lack of polish acceptable; the're FREE!!!!!!!!!    The new characters are severely lacking in creativity and polish. Worse than that, they aren't really unique. They all kind of feel like an amalgamation of already existing characters, but not in a fun way. I found them boring. For me, the worst part of the DLC is the new items. They aren't fun. Most of them are defensive, so you almost don't even notice their effects. They don't make you feel more powerful when you get them. Some of them are just objectively pointless. For example: Knockback Fin. Causes enemies to pop up in the air like 5 feet when hit. What could possibly be the purpose of this? If anything, it's a hindrance. More often than not, an enemy is launched and then you miss them with subsequent shots. Dumb. I find myself avoiding almost all of the new items. Again, there are a ton of mods for items if you want to spice things up, but for FREE. To be clear; I don't mind paying for content. I want to support games that I spend a lot of time playing. But, nobody wants to be taken advantage of, and that's what this feels like. It feels like they leveraged the community's love for the game to price gouge and put out a product that would take just long enough to realize how bad it is that you won't be able to refund it. You'll spend 2 hours hoping that there's more, just to find out it's too late, and you're a sucker. I see myself as one of RoR2's biggest fans. I've loved it since early access, and I still do. Corporate greed has just gotten the better of the new DLC. Yes, Gearbox released a statement promising to make it right, but don't give them your money until they deliver. They've done literally the bare minimum so far, which is fix stuff that shouldn't have been released in the first place. The sell now, fix later model has got to stop. It's BS. I'm tired of it. You're tired of it. You're going to see a lot of reviews saying to cut the devs a break and it's going to get better. I'll cut the devs a break when they give us $15 of content. Right now, I see it only as a cash grab. I will change my review to positive if/when the devs deliver on their promises.

_childDocuments_.review: Risk of Rain 2 is largely an improvement to the first game, which was already very fun.I think Risk of Rain 2 is worth the purchase at full price ($20 at time of writing) if you think you'll get at least 20 hours out of it.What might be an indicator of this?First, you should be generally interested in the main mechanics of the game. It's focused around killing enemies to obtain loot while finding and activating a teleporter to go to the next stage. When the teleporter is activated, a boss is spawned, and you have to beat the boss and some more enemies to go to the next stage. At this point in development, there are 4 types of stages you visit in order, each type of stage has two possible maps that you can go to. You can keep going through the loop of stages indefinitely, or you can end your run when a celestial portal spawns after you activate certain teleporters.The game is played as a third person shooter, and you can choose one of nine survivors who all play differently from each other.If you are generally interested in the mechanics of Risk of Rain 2, then I would say it's worth a buy if any of the following describe you:1. You liked Risk of Rain.2. You like rogue-likes or rogue-lites.3. You enjoy grinding to beat specific challenges in order to unlock gear (this will certainly get you 20 hours in the game).4. You enjoy games that you can play for 30 to 60 minutes.5. You are enthused about this game and are looking for confirmation that it's good for some definition of "good".Risk of Rain 2 is in early access, but even in its current state I think it's a good enough successor to the original game. The devs are actively tweaking and adding content, so hopefully it only gets better. I would not let the early access tag push you away from buying.One great improvement over the first game is dedicated multiplayer support (you no longer have to go through the trouble of hosting your own servers). The game is good solo, but even better with friends.The main difference between the two is movement and scale. RoR 2 is 2D instead of 3D, which makes dodging enemies and traversing the map more complicated. It also allows for some characters (e.g. Loader, Mercenary) to have even crazier movement options than they did in the first game. It's very satisfying to swing around the map as Loader. Maps are much larger and take longer to traverse. You need to be much more focused on your surroundings, both enemies and chests are harder to visually keep tabs on than in the first game.

_childDocuments_.review: This review is hard for me to write.After four long years being quite possibly my favorite game of all time, Risk of Rain 2 has been disgraced in it's most recent update.If you're a fan of this game and have been following it even half as much as I have, you understand why I have to make this review negative, but for those out of the loop:The original owners of the Risk of Rain IP, Hopoo Games, sold their IP to Gearbox Software after the release of Survivors of the Void in 2022.Ever since then, we have been patient and optimistic; waiting for them to fix the broken state of console, bring the Survivors of the Void DLC we already had on PC to them, and finally, release new content and streamline the experience to be equal on all platforms. All of these things were promised and eagerly awaited by the absolutely incredible community this game has fostered over the years.The monkey's paw curls.We now have a downgraded, buggy, mess of a game (with a subpar paid content drop, Seekers of the Storm, yeah its kinda mid) with a new codebase (that's ♥♥♥♥) on PC that is on par with what the console experience has been for years.Let that sink in. Knock Knock, open the door, its the sink:The PC version was DOWNGRADED to match console, not the other way around.But wait there's more! Now we have some shiny new critters! Such as but not limited to:Tons of collision issues, clipping, visual and audio issues all of which were not present before. (this is a LOT in one line)Physics and GAME DIFFICULTY being tied to FRAMERATE.Broken survivors that previously had absolutely no issue.A singular common item that makes the final boss unkillable.One tiny, innocent little bug where connecting a second input device will delete your entire save file.An ENTIRE CONSOLE edition that is UNPLAYABLE. Xbox players cannot even navigate the menu.And on top of all of this, we have a team of people behind the scenes at Gearbox Software and Take-Two Interactive that are not acknowledging the problems and the upset they have caused.I do not simply wish to be atop a pile of hate that this game does not deserve, but I feel like this is one of the only ways I can help. New items such as the one that lets you fly temporarily bring excitement and old items featured in the game also please players of the previous.The controls and HUD is great, and QoL changes such as a scrolling difficulty bar and the way you can move to the next level without killing all enemies is really nice too, however the game becomes much more difficult due to being unable to open chests while the teleporter is still charging (I'm not complaining, dying is all part of the journey).The skill ceiling is raised far higher than what the first game offered, and even then, the hitboxes are very generous for targets further away. _childDocuments_.review: In Risk of Rain 2 you start as your chosen survivor, landing on a bizarre planet. For the entirety of your run, you will be fighting for your life. As with other roguelikes, there's a number of commonalities you can expect to see: upgrades to pick up, a horde of enemies to fight, a boss to cap off each level. However, unlike many other roguelikes, the levels aren't procedurally generated (but the sequence of the levels do vary somewhat). As you complete achievements, new items and artifacts become unlocked and useable for future runs.You can spend hours playing a run, or beat the game in under 1.5 hours. You are largely playing the same 20 levels over and over, but the way in which you play within each run varies. This variability and versatility is what gives it such a strong replay value.RoR2 is not an easy game. Sometimes you find a good combination of items; sometimes you don't. Sometimes, you juke left when you should have juked right, and you're dead. RNG hits pretty hard and regularly crushes you. Despite this seemingly frustrating description of the difficulty, I implore you to stick with it. Play on easy mode for a while. Learn how the items interact with each other. As you start unlocking new items, characters, and artifacts, your possibilities branch out, and the enjoyment goes up. Default RoR2 will always be hard (and darn near impossible on the hardest difficulty, "Monsoon"), but after the first several runs, I almost never played it "default" from that point forward. I always played it with some combination of artifacts, most importantly the "" artifact. This single artifact changed the game for me, as it gives you much greater control over how you upgrade your character.Besides the base difficulty you set for the run, there's an enemy difficulty scale within the run, which slowly increases over time. It creates quite the interesting dilemma: Complete the levels quicker to ensure the enemies you fight don't get too hard, or spend more time collecting items to make your character more powerful. It's a delicate balance you must continuously maintain, because if you swing too far in one direction or the other, you're dead. Keep in mind this a general rule. As you experiment with other artifacts and game modes, you'll notice that some rules go out the window. It's a design that broadens the more you play it.One drawback to the continuously scaling difficulty, is that you don't get much time to plan. You're always on the run. You can't view your inventory when paused, and in multiplayer, you can't even pause the game! The only exception is when you choose to go to the shop between levels. This will be a drawback for those that like to do a little more planning with their roguelikes. Better take a bathroom break before starting a run with your buddies!Throughout each stage you'll pick up items to boost your character during a run. Duplicate items can be stacked (e.g. each additional 'boiler plate' you pick up gives you +5 more damage reduction). Items often synergize with other items (e.g. an item that gives you extra crit hit chance + an item that gives you some benefit every time you crit hit). This is the foundation of much of the versatility of RoR2. When you're playing "default" RoR2, it is possible to get bad loadouts. Some items are lame and almost completely useless. But most items are at least useful in certain combinations or contexts.There are over 100 different items and equipment. It will take a while to learn what they all are, and how they help (or even hurt you). To make it harder, the items are sometimes nonsensical in their effects. A ukulele?  Well, that zaps adjacent enemies with electricity, of course!  A slug? That increases your heal rate, naturally!I was pleasantly surprised that in certain modes, this game doesn't hold you back. Your character can be grossly overpowered. I even pushed it so insanely far as to cause my PC to crash. I love that it lets me do this without limits. It's a refreshing contrast to the thousands of games out there that throttle you back just as you feel like you're gaining some momentum. Sometimes it's fun to simply annihilate boatloads of enemies with little effort. However, in most other modes, there's a great deal of balancing mechanisms, where if you are getting too overpowered, it can come back to haunt you.It's really hard to sum up all the different angles and strategies for such a seemingly straightforward design. Even 100 hours into the game, I was still discovering new ways to do things, and new ways to combine items for specific effects. You'll frequently be referring to the very extensive wiki to refine your understanding of every item and character.Despite being known as a co-op game, I didn't find the co-op portion to be that strong. It was ok, but I mostly preferred solo mode.Some downsides to co-op:Having said that, there are some benefits for playing co-op:The soundtrack is absolutely amazing. I would even say it contributed significantly to how much I enjoy the game. I bought the OST at full price.It took me 174 hours to get all achievements. There are some challenges that you can do that aren't related to achievements. For example the "logbook" which requires you to basically encounter every possible item and enemy. I completed logbook entries after my 200th hour of game time.As mentioned earlier, the achievements are all tied to unlocking items, which I think is a great way to add significance to achievements. You not only earn the achievement, but get a new character/weapon/item for doing so.The goals for every achievement are quite different, and will require you to pursue various combinations of items to get there. Some goals will mean you have to forgo getting  normally helpful items that you typically want to use every run. The achievements often require such radically different approaches that the 118 achievements don't feel that grindy. Difficult yes, but not grindy.

_childDocuments_.review: As a newcomer to the Risk of Rain series, I was attracted to Risk of Rain 2 because of its co-op online, horde-like shooter structure with a fresh 3D perspective compared to its predecessor's 2D format. Just like other horde-like games, it follows the "loop" design of kill mobs, collect loot, defeat the boss, and rinse-repeat.The gameplay is simple, intuitive, yet challenging all at the same time. The gameplay is brutal, but fair. It is challenging but not in a frustrating way. I just want to play more. It is the kind of challenge you can appreciate and learn from your mistakes. I'm new to rogue-likes-lites and I was able to solo for more than an hour. As far as unlockables, there are six characters to unlock, four zones, and 99 items with more on the way. Items that you collect along the way are adorned on your character like trophies. Despite all the unique passive abilities you get from each item, I want to see more items with cool powers and abilities that I can summon. For top-tier players, they may feel content-starved. Personally, I feel there is enough content here in Early Access to keep you coming back for more. Playing with keyboard and mouse and the controls feel slick, snappy, precise. Items and abilities complement one another, making for a perfect formula for mayhem. Aiming and gunplay are precise and accurate. Enemy hit box is fine-tuned. Using terrain adds another layer of dimension to combating enemies.  Discovering new items and experimenting with them is extremely fun. And using them on enemies is even better. One of my favorite items is the black hole. Needless to say, it speaks for itself. Visually, Risk of Rain 2 sticks to what its good at, and just like the original it sports a very similar coat of aesthetic that is hauntingly beautiful and minimaliistic. The game runs extremely well @ 3440x1440 on my ultrawide and doesn't miss a beat. As you well know by now, Risk of Rain 2 is in 3D. Unlike its 2D predecessor, the third-person perspective and added dimension does not take away from what makes RoR great. Enemy attacks and projectiles now come from every direction instead of a lined approach, which changes things up for the series.The soundtrack is superb. If you like listening to soundtracks from "Deep Rock Galactic", "Blade Runner" or the movie "Drive", your ears will be pleased. The soundtrack is calm and soothing to the ears against all the chaos on the screen. There's also some rock, too, that goes well with some intense play sessions.Online multi-player consists of co-op online featuring quick play or simply hosting a game and inviting your friends. It has a  Some of the issues I experienced were some rubberbanding and the "Unknown Lobby ID" or "Invalid Lobby ID" when trying to use QuickPlay. Other than that, it has been pretty smooth for an Early Access game. Another feature that I really liked was the option for players to vote on difficulty level in the lobby. In the past, I have found too many games fall into the trap of map selection based on difficulty, which can really split the community. On the other hand, this may cause some players to quit because the difficulty level is too hard. One draw back is that it runs on peer-to-peer online connection. I had a few great "monsoon" difficulty runs end because the host quit. My one caveat with the online portion is that any player in co-op is able to click on teleport prematurely which transfers the entire group to the next area before looting everything. This causes some players to miss out on collecting the remaining items on the map. On easy difficulty, this isn't much of a problem. But on harder difficulties this can present an issue. Some players have complained about the visibility of the teleporter. I do not think it is all that bad. The teleporter visibility and randomization varies. Sometimes, I would go rounds finding it rather too easily. Once in a while, it feels like it doesn't even exist on the map.Another issue are how boss drops are distributed. The boss will drop at least one item per player. Sometimes, the boss will drop more items than there are players. In my experience, some players would grab more than one item or all of them, possibly to troll others in the group or they just do not want to share. Also, because the items drop very close to each other, it is easy to grab more than one boss drop item by mistake. The levels are hand-crafted like the original. While they are designed well, there is not enough randomness. The teleporter is randomized, but you can expect the rest of the levels to be the same.It was not until recently that I got into rogue-likes, thanks to some Steam friends. Usually, I would play co-op, horde-like games such as Deep Rock Galactic (excellent game btw), Vermintide 2, Helldivers, and so forth. If you like any of those games and you like some rogue-likes, or you are at least open to them, I think you will probably like Risk of Rain 2. I was not too fond of the original RoR, but I felt right at home with RoR2. It is like a love letter to co-op, horde-like gamers.Risk of Rain 2 was a pleasant surprise. Rarely do I instantly like a game this much within the first hour. Its simplistic and elegant design has a mild complexity when it comes to its challenging gameplay. It consists of smart design that allows any type of player to jump right in, so long as you have the patience for it. In the future, I would like to see more rogue-like-lite titles become 3D games. As long as it makes sense and works well with the gameplay style. Hopoo Games has shown that indie titles such as RoR can be a 3D title and still retain all the aspects that made the original a great, fun game.RoR2 is in Early Access and kicking with overwhelmingly positive reviews and it is well earned. The developers plan on adding more characters, bosses, items, a true endgame boss, and a true ending when the final product releases. Game modifiers that can be found in the world will be coming soon as well. Furthermore, I want to commend Hopoo Games for doing the "Buy One, Get One Free until 3/30" promotion. That was a very cool thing to do. Ultrawide 21:9 Support: Yes.i5-8600K @ 4.6 GHzGTX 1070 Founder's Edition (stock)16GB DDR4 RAMSamsung 850 EVO SSDLG Ultra-wide 34UM69G @ 2560x1080

_childDocuments_.review: This game reminds me what is the purpose of any game - to have fun. And Risk of Rain 2 delivers that just perfectly. No vertical progression, no leveling (your characters do not get stronger permanently after each run), no experience represented as numbers, no story (not needed). Just entertaining gameplay that allows you to jump in and relax after a long day. Each run being an unique experience and horizontal progression (items, skills, characters, skins are unlocked through achievements) keep the game fresh for a long time. You can share the action with your friends, although the game becomes more unbalanced in team than when playing alone (still fun though). And if you are feeling bored after playing a while, that's okay, take a break and be back later - gameplay will not change.First expansion lives up to the base game and delivers even more variety to the game with new void mechanics (enemies, items, events, maps and game modes).

_childDocuments_.review: I confess that I did not like the previous version - Risk of Rain. I am not good at roguelike games and I just couldn't go far with that 2D game. Soon I lost interest despite the fact that almost everyone who plays that 2D game loves that game.Fast forward to Risk of Rain 2. I am a fan of third person shooter. And the co-op option is good. I am still not good at roguelike games. At least, now I get to play with my wife. So far we have a lot of fun with it. RoR2 certainly has exceeded my initial expectation. Pros and considerations of this early access version as follows.Pros===+ Very fluid game play. Camera setting is perfect. Mouse and keyboard setup is very responsive. I have played many third person shooter games. RoR2 is among the best when it comes to control and camera.+ Very colorful. Love the cartoon-ish backdrop.+ Boss fights are epic.+ Very fun when co-op. The difficulty does escalate. There is a constant sense of urgency.+ Very much the same game design as RoR. While I am not a fan of RoR, I must admit that the game design is very good. There are different loots, different buffs, turrets / healing bots etc., different maps that make the game unique for each round of play through.+ There is an easy difficulty for more casual players.Considerations============- If you are not good at roguelike games (like me), you would probably get frustrated with the default difficulty setting. I don't think it is a game whereby you can get better as you go (e.g. past success doesn't get carried to the future games). There is a limit to what you can do with experience and awareness.- I wish there is a slider to adjust difficulty setting. I find that easy mode is too easy when a game can last like an hour. But the standard mode is too hard (yet to pass the first round). This means the fun part for the easy mode only kicks in after 45 mins of game play while the standard difficulty is just way too frustrating.- There is no revive. At least I don't seem to be able to find one. If your partner and you have a difference in terms of skill or in terms of loot progression, one of you may end up in spectator mode after his/her character dies. That is not really that fun after a while. There should be a way to revive because watching someone plays is just not as fun as playing the game with someone. Or some ways for spectators to participate in the game.- Teleport is a small device in the map that spawns the stage boss. It also helps to clear a stage and progress to the next map. The goal is to find the teleport. The challenge is that it is rather tiny and is not that easy to find, especially in a 3D world. In some maps, it may take a long time to keep circling the area and still not finding it. With experience, it does make it easier. Still, some maps are just harder than others (I guess one could say this is good design as this should give you a more varied experience).Game Video=========For those who are interested to see how this game plays like for two newbies to this game / genre, this are 2 videos for you!

_childDocuments_.review: I would like to start off this review by saying that Risk of Rain has been a franchise that I’ve held near and dear to my heart for years now, I still remember finding the game initially through Chris Christodoulou‘s music (specifically the rain formally known as purple <3) in the original risk of rain. And I want nothing but the continued success of the game no matter who is currently developing it. However the recent release of seekers of the storm is nothing short of a disaster that should have been delayed, and the fact that it was released in this state is unacceptable. I have never seen a game that was so fundamentally sound and stable so brutally dismantled by an update that had received nothing but unparalleled hype and praise before it’s release. The whole laundry list of game breaking bugs and poor design choices that were introduced in this expansion is mind boggling, I genuinely believe that this update was not playtested OR that it was playtested and known that it was horrendously buggy but shipped anyways because of higher ups at gearbox. Randy Pitchford went on record saying “This is some jank we’ve just sort of tolerated.” when discussing the new dlc and that is by far the most baffling statement I’ve ever seen said about a disastrous content release. How can you in good faith say that there is just some “jank” in the game when the game is currently unplayable on console, or that the flag ship feature of couch coop can permanently corrupt your save data if a second controller is plugged in. The current major issue of your FPS being tied to almost every form of physics in the game is game breaking on pc, I genuinely do not know how this got past QA unless they only tested it on a 60 fps locked ps4 and nothing else. The new content that was added is the only saving grace this update has, as the new stages, survivors, and items are all awesome and welcome additions to the game IF THEY WORKED! Warped echo making the MAIN BOSS UNKILLABLE is a laughably pathetic bug, seekers meditation is terribly inconsistent and buggy, chef does not feel good to play on higher refresh rates and ends up being a clunky mess because of it, and the new secret survivor (no spoilers :3) feels very unfinished, playing more like a low effort modded character than an official survivor. In its current state, I do not think anyone should purchase the game or it’s DLC expansions, it really pains me to say this because this is one of my favorite franchises and games of all time. But gearbox has horribly managed this update and put the game into the worst state I have ever seen it in. I genuinely believe that if swift action isn’t taken to address the laundry list of game breaking bugs that this game will not see the successful future that it deserves. I hope for the best, but with gearbox and it’s misguided management at the lead I do expect the worst.

_childDocuments_.review: First, I want to say thank you to the Gearbox developers for letting the community know that they have a passion for not only fixing the game, but seeing it thrive. Its very rare for a company to admit their content has balancing issues or straight up flawed design. Hopefully this sentiment sticks around for future patches and updates. If it does, my opinion will certainly become more positive.  The new Seekers of the Storm DLC is in a bad spot. I know most people believe this to be because of the bugs, and yes the bugs are rampant throughout the game and are diminishing the communities enjoyment significantly. But there is a bigger issue with this DLC that the majority seems to either be turning a blind eye too, or is just completely unaware of. I'm talking about the games Item Balance and how the majority of the new Items destroy the games Item Balance and are just simply not well designed. Items are the core and pinnacle element of Risk of Rain 2. In Risk of Rain 2 your power is predominantly measured by your items, a lot of the best items are the most basic ones that give you: Crit, Movement Speed, Bleed, Attack Speed, etc. And the more unique/situational items having more complicated or interesting effects. Generally the basic Stat Items, (White Common Items,) have positive synergies with the higher tier unique/situational items, (Green Uncommon Items,) that creates a positive feedback loop for the player to continue power spiking and progressing through the stages. (Ex: Gas & Ignition, Crit & Predatory Instincts, etc.) It feels like these new items were not designed for what the game needed, but more like the new developers had a wild hair of "...you know what would be cool?" and just ran with it. The items range from completely useless, literally broken, or detrimental, to straight up instantly run winning. The worst part being, because certain item types are so limited within the Item Pool already, such as movement items or healing items, the new items this DLC added that don't benefit the player in any meaningful way still negatively effect you every run by making your chance of getting useful items worse overall. (Because your percentage chance for an item goes down with every new item of that type added to the pool.) I cannot stress enough the rough shape that the Item Pool is in because of these Items. Lets look at some of the worst offenders. Antler Shield - relies on the player taking damage to be useful. Risk of Rain 2, on Eclipse 8, hell even Monsoon, is a game about not getting hit. The difficulty ramps tremendously and attacks begin to deal massive damage to the player. From a design standpoint, Movement Speed is better defense then... well actual defense. Why bet on tanking a hit when you could just be fast enough to never be hit in the first place? Not to mention the damage it deals back is percentage based and monster health scaling is multitudes larger than the players, so this item becomes exponentially less useful as time goes on. This item needs to be completely redesigned. Knockback Fin - not only is practically useless on ranged characters, but its actually a detriment to melee and short-range characters. Pushing an enemy away from you as Mercenary or Acrid or Chef only makes it harder for you to kill them quickly and move on to the next objective. If they are a ranged enemy, its even worse because it gives them a better chance of landing an attack on you. Even if a single character could use this item, its too niche and should never dilute the common pool of items. Warped Echo - is interesting on paper because it synergizes with medkit. Finally an item that has synergy! But... it makes your Rejuvenating Slug and Personal Shield Generator take longer to activate their effects, and this might be a bug, but it also allows certain damage types to pass through your One Shot Protection such as debuff damage. So it has one synergy and adds three detrimental effects. No Item in the game should make other items worse. Simple as that. If the interaction isn't positive or neutral at best it shouldn't be in the game. It doesn't service the player or the feedback loop of Risk of Rain 2. Noxious Thorn - looks terrible. Its a giant green blob that has a description which the Pentagon couldn't decipher. It just feels so... unfun to play with. Why is it also based on getting hit? Why not make the Item with 'Noxious' in its name deal Poison Damage instead of Bleed? We already have multiple sources of Bleed and only Acrid can use Poison. It would synergize well with DoT builds, Acrid, and Death Mark. Unstable Transmitter - might be the worst offender. Its explosion is pointless at high time or stage counts. and its effect is buggy and weird. It takes 3 to 4 seconds to activate and doesn't flow very well with the speed and feel of the game. Basic Movement Speed Item are already more effective at getting away from things like I said above about Antler Shield. Why is this DLC trying to push "Defensive" Items so hard? Defense in Risk of Rain 2 is: Don't get hit. Kill stuff before it kills you. Sure there are times where nobody is perfect and takes a hit, but that is why Healing Items and One Shot Protection exist. Plus, what Unstable Transmitter does... already exist in an item combo! Old War Stealth Kit paired with Power Elixir will proc simultaneously to let you get away at low health, without breaking your game. This bootleg combo has a surprisingly similar effect to this new DLC Item without being buggy, awkward, and taking up a Green Item Pool Slot.Sonorous Whispers - This item is broken by concept. No amount of balancing could fix this item. Risk of Rain Returns has a similar item called the '56 Leaf Clover' which grants Elites a 4% Chance to drop an Item on death. Of course its all RNG, but this averages out to about 3-5 Items in a standard run depending on when you obtain the item. The reason it works in Risk of Rain Returns and not Risk of Rain 2 is that there are no Hidden Realms that stop time completely in Returns. In Risk of Rain 2, if you ever pick up this Item, you can find the Lunar Altar on a stage and repeat until you obtain Gilded Coast, where time is stopped and you can farm large monsters, bosses, and elites indefinitely. If you get this Item, even on Eclipse 8, you instantly win the game. This should never happen. No Item should ever instantly win you a run. The simplest solution to this would be to disable the Item in Hidden Realms, but I still think it would be to powerful. This item needs to be reworked entirely. The biggest thing that I can say is that items in Risk of Rain 2 are deceptively simple. Its very easy from an outside lens to think of so many items that could be good for the game, but when they are actually implemented do not fit in to the ecosystem in a useful, fun, or meaningful way. Items need to feel good, be at least somewhat useful, and play/interact well with one another and the survivors, without getting in the way of other items or diluting the pool, the enjoyment, or the balance. Item Balance is probably the most difficult aspect of the game. Items do not need to be overly complex. The complexity creates itself through the items synergies with one another and how each individual survivor interacts with these items. This game is Item Soup, but the Soup has been carefully crafted and maintained. You can throw a lot of basic ingredients into a soup to make it taste slightly better, like potatoes or carrots. But if you start throwing in random, complex ingredients that you like, like gummy bears or beef jerky, the Soup can quickly begin to sour and lose what made it so special in the first place. Even if you fix every bug in the entire game, if the items and item balance are not well designed, then the game won't ever feel 100% right

_childDocuments_.review: I remember a lot of apprehension when Risk of Rain 2 was announced. It wasn’t unwarranted, either, as the jump from 2D to 3D has been dire for more than a few franchises. I wasn’t super hot on the original Risk of Rain either, owing to how sloggy the combat could be if your build didn’t keep up with the hordes. But all those concerns melted away in my first few minutes with the game. Risk of Rain 2 benefits so much from the move to 3D that it’s almost hard to believe it started as a side-scroller, with free movement and open arenas allowing you so much more control over encounters. And I can only assume it’s going to get better from the handful of foes and levels it has now.The story in these games is always a pretty big question mark, but the premise at least is simple enough. You’re some kind of space badass, landing on a bizarre alien world full of things eager to teleport all the way over to kill you. The only way to progress through these realms of slaughter is to find and power up a teleporter, which of course will attract the attention of things far worse during the charging phase. On a happier note, the planet is dotted with mystical shrines, drones in need of masters, and cases full of suspiciously powerful items, all of which can enhance your survivability if you can wrest enough coins from your foes to pay for them.At this precise moment, Risk of Rain 2 is a loop of six levels, each a wide-open space of fields, cliffs, walkways, ruins, and other features to explore. The map itself is always the same, save for minor differences like some doors and caves being open, but the layout of loot and the location of the exit teleporter is always different. You are free to explore to your heart’s content as enemies teleport themselves into your vicinity to murder you, but just as in the first game the difficulty rises as time passes. The main challenge of the game, then, is balancing your exploration for more powerful gear against the need to press on as your foes become stronger and more numerous. Once again, this is a balance that will take time to learn, and may end with you dead in the very first stage a few times as you seek to find it.The big difference between the first and second games now is the pace of the action. In Risk of Rain you often found yourself corralling foes into a stack to whittle down, boxing in enemies and chewing through them gradually. Part of the reason for this was your low movement speed and lack of mobility options in platforming. All that is out the window now, and not just because of the addition of a third dimension. Relative movement feels so much faster here, with a dedicated sprint button and more dramatic movement abilities for the different classes. Items that add additional jumps are also pretty common drops, but more importantly enemies can no longer box you in. You’re free to circle around foes, weave through crowds, and retreat in any direction if things get too intense. You have to stay in the vicinity of the teleporter to charge it but that’s still a sizable arena to work with.For the most part, the grinds against enemy health bars are gone as well. There are certainly some enemies that need further adjusting but the overall experience feels balanced more for cutting down big groups in a hurry. This is facilitated by the builds you can get going, featuring powerful pickups that conditionally enhance your damage or add leaping electrical attacks or explosive effects, all of which can be stacked with themselves. They say it right on the store page, they want you to exploit these items, creating builds that will tear through your foes like some kind of super-science reaper. These items will be familiar to fans of the first but it’s easier to get a build rolling in this one, possibly due to your greater relative power compared to your foes.There are six classes to unlock and use in the game now, from the familiar shootyman Commando to the nimble Huntress with her homing bow to the absolutely mad techno-magician Artificer. More levels and classes are coming prior to the full launch early next year, as well as the game-altering Artifact system from the first. Right now you can enjoy some wonderfully chaotic drop-in multiplayer (which works like a dream compared to the first game) and daily challenges, the staple of modern roguelikes. All you really need is that core loop of looting and shooting, though, because it’s absolutely sublime here. I never expected Risk of Rain 2 to outperform the original so completely, but the move to 3D has treated it incredibly well. For wild arena combat and fast-paced adventuring, this one is hard to beat.Did you enjoy this review? I certainly hope so, and I certainly hope you'll check out more of them at  or on my !

_childDocuments_.review: There is a cancer at the heart of Risk of Rain 2: it fundamentally does not respect your time.I think this is a symptom of it being developed in Early Access for a long time. There used to be only a couple levels, and looping through them to get more and more powerful was basically the entire game. But now that we have a final boss and enough levels to get to him without repeats, the game still expects you to play in the same infinite way: you get stronger, the enemies get stronger, until you're committing genocide with every mouse click, but also can potentially be two-shot by dozens of enemies at any given moment. This might sound thrilling, but the visual noise and sheer chaos means that focusing any specific enemy is often impossible, and you just find yourself going through rote motions. Depending on your character, that might be simple (Huntress), complex (Loader/Mercenary), or somewhere in between, but it's never actually challenging -- you just either have the damage and survival to make it through, or you don't. I've never been as bored in a game while simultaneously being moments from death.It's a real shame, because there is a fun action game in here, but once you've played for some hours it becomes equivalent to sitting at a slot machine. You're just gambling for the right set of items which makes you absolutely unstoppable, but simultaneously makes the game play itself. Death comes quick and almost never feels like it happens because you made a legitimate mistake. 95% of the time I can only identify what killed me because the game identifies your killer, but it could have been any of the hundreds of projectiles, damage fields, lingering DOT effects, etc. that were on the screen at the time. There is now a final boss, but he feels bad to fight, tests skills that you're rarely asked to demonstrate in the entire rest of the game, and the biggest sin, he takes away your items for a while. This could be cool if it was a normal boss fight, but because this is a permadeath roguelike, it's infuriating. To get to the final boss you're looking at a minimum of a half-hour run, but most players will want to loop through the level set at least once. I've seen people play single runs in this game for upwards of three hours. That's insane to me. I guess if you're the type of person who just loves to watch numbers go up, that could be awesome for you. It's like Cookie Clicker with much more involved gameplay... but yeah as a big fan of Roguelikes, this just isn't doing it for me. You can see how much I've played, yet so little of that time has been really *fun*. Similar to something like World of Warcraft, it's compulsive. And the lack of a save-game feature between levels, which almost every other game in the genre has had for years now, just multiplies all these complaints.

_childDocuments_.review: Risk of Rain 2 is an absolute blast for group play, offering a chaotic and entertaining experience filled with silly shenanigans that keep players coming back for more. From the moment you drop into its procedurally generated worlds with your friends, the mayhem begins. Whether you're frantically fighting off hordes of alien creatures or strategizing how to take down towering bosses, the cooperative gameplay fosters camaraderie and laughter as you navigate the chaos together.What sets Risk of Rain 2 apart is its unpredictability and the sheer variety of items, characters, and environments that ensure no two runs are ever the same. The game's replayability is off the charts, as each session presents new challenges and opportunities for experimentation. Whether you're unlocking new characters, discovering powerful items, or pushing the limits of your survival skills, there's always something new and exciting to discover with each playthrough.But perhaps the most memorable aspect of Risk of Rain 2 is the sheer absurdity that ensues when playing with friends. From accidentally activating game-changing items at the worst possible moment to narrowly escaping death with a well-timed ability, the game's unpredictable nature often leads to hilarious moments that you'll be reminiscing about long after the session ends. Whether you're a seasoned player or new to the game, Risk of Rain 2 promises hours of laughter-filled entertainment that makes it a must-have for any gaming group looking for a good time.

_childDocuments_.review: So sad to see another favorite IP of mine get Gearbox'd. Pretty sure they just hate the number 2 for some reason after how they trashed both BL2's good traits moving forward and RoR2's. I guess we can look forward to an awful movie adaptation with geriatric Huntress though! New characters feel bad, even if you get good runs on them the abilities don't feel right together or couldn't be helped by each other (life chef m1 and m2 being so janky I'd rather just use the mod version of the character and I've heard that same sentiment echo'd pretty much every lobby I've been in with or as a chef). Seeker is a cool concept but feels bad especially with how janky the ult is, Paladin wannabe is just a worse feeling modded character, and chef got cooked so hope you enjoy paying for a worse version of 2 mods and 1 bad feeling original concept when it comes to that. New enemies are bad. We got Child, the only new enemy that's not annoying or recycled content but I have yet to notice the impact they have. We have Wurm, 99% underground 200% too much hp for how little time you have to attack them. New boss feels like Mithrix reskin with none of the interesting mechanics of the phases. Worst part about him is by the time you reach him you're fighting more bugs than enemies. Last but possibly least we have Stone Golem + Stone Titan who can't even stay consistent with his cyclone attack, he might stand still and aim at a wall, he might run towards you while cycloning, he might tp on top of you and cyclone, it's seemingly random but possibly tied to fps (more on this later in the features section).As per usual with games nowadays, the art/music team did great work. Everything looks cool especially the new stages. They sure feel bad but that's primarily due to the bugs, enemies, and changes that plague this update and dlc. The 2 new elite variants of enemies are both crazy overtuned and just feel bad, not sure what the thought process behind them was, or if there even was any. Gilded and Twisted. Both have way too much HP and damage increase, not that they'll kill you with their hits anyway it just makes the bigger issues with this update even more apparent. Gilded steal your money and reduce their damage taken pretty often, often by stage 4 they take longer to kill than any end boss would at stage 5 with full phases with animations. Twisted reflect damage in a MASSIVE radius so enjoy one spawning on top of you and your proc chain coming back to end your run.   New features: everything is tied to fps. Items, enemies, abilities (both yours and the ones enemies use), the director that spawns enemies, if you can name it, it's tied to fps now. Enjoy inconsistent everything including some enemies being invincible or hitting exponentially harder (including mithrix 0.5 aka the new boss where his laser stats are tied to fps). 2/4 bosses are just straight up invincible if you have one of the COMMON new items. Sure hope you didn't wanna play with the new content you paid for! Honestly I already deleted the review I typed up once because just listing all the bugs went over character limit. A good list of the primary categories exists on any and every RoR2 content creator's channel by this point so refer to those for more of these "features". Lastly they backported outsorced console code to pc, really digging deep for how hard they could ruin a beloved IP. Overall avoid the game currently, or at least mod it to run on patches previous to the new dlc, don't buy that garbage, and mod in better versions of the dlc content you like the theme of, most of which existed for free before this dlc. Gave it too much time to form my opinion so I can't refund the dlc myself but in the current state it's one of the few examples of pay to lose out there. Hopefully it changes but given the direction it's taken and how this company has shown itself in the past, it's probably gonna get worse. Edit: I left out item reviews as so many are either not working right due to bugs like the fps tying or are seemingly not working so no point going over them. Most of them actively hurt game balance in a lobby though when they seem to work right so I guess new items are generally bad too. One of the new reds (War Bonds) just straight up giving someone free chests but not spawning more so one player will snowball harder and everyone else will fall further behind them, fun to carry with though I guess. New blue has a downside for you, and an additional extra one for the rest of your team, doubling their chest costs.  :)Thanks Randy for another banger of a dumpsterfire. You kill off games and franchises like they're GoT characters and that's kind of impressive, in it's own way.
