_childDocuments_.review: If this was merely last week, I would've said this game was absolutely worth every penny and hour I spent on it.But I cannot in good faith recommend this game in the current state is in now thanks to the newest DLC and patch Gearbox released.I cannot fathom how you could take a game that, while a little rough around the edges, was a very streamlined and absolutely blast of an experience and turn turn it into an buggy mess that feels AWFUL to even play. The amount of issues I got in merely the first few hours of the DLC is so egregious it makes me wonder how it was even playtested in this state - let alone shipped.By trying to make console and PC versions """consistent""" with each other, Gearbox just broke both versions. Misery loves company, I guess. Every tiny little thing that you wouldn't expect to annoy you now does. The health bar looks awful, pressing tab to look at your inventory now stops your character from sprinting, terminal shops have broken shading that looks poop brown (fitting), and EVERYTHING is now tied to framerate! You know, the ONE THING that's prone to drop when your run gets a little too silly? As much fun as looping can be, it's now just no longer an option (funny considering the new boss practically necessitates looping if you don't wanna die instantly). And you better have it capped to 60 fps like the consoles or else everything BREAKS. Fantastic. I love it when a product that used to work that I put 300+ hours into suddenly doesn't.This game was prided on EVERY character feeling clean and smooth to control in some capacity, but with the new patch so many skills just feel horrible to even use. Collision is wonky, hitboxes disagree with the animation, it feels AWFUL. I should not be fighting against the game physics themselves.And then the DLC itself is just aggressively average. Stages are alright, but only 4 new enemies is disappointing. Music is INCREDIBLE, but that's Chris not Gearbox (shoutouts to Chris). The new boss just flat out ending your run also sucks especially when it can end as early as Stage 4. And then some of the item choices convinced me that nobody who created these items actually played the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ game because how the hell do you make me wanna consider Low Quality Speakers from Starstorm 2 over some of the stinkers they added to item pool???Honestly speaking of mods, the microsecond the wonderful and talented modding community fixes all of the mistakes Gearbox created I will be playing that instead. I thought going back to vanilla risk would be rough with the long scrapping times, but I didn't expect everything to just be broken? But knowing Gearbox, they'll probably just wait for modders to fix everything then yoink the code and claim they fixed it themselves.Fix the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ game and I'll recommend it again. For now, I award you no points and may Providence have mercy on your soul.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me preface this by stating this I have and will continue to play this game, and I adore it and it's community; it is a mainstay of both indie and roguelike games, but to tell you to buy it and taint your experience with the buggy and unpolished game it's been botched into would be wrong of me. In all good faith I cannot recommend buying it in it's current state.  I have gotten countless hours of enjoyment out of this game, in both single player and multi-player but the fact is that with the newest update with the DLC the game is broken. I've been able to enjoy the game despite it's issues but I would not tell any of my friends to buy it in it's current state in fear of their first time playing the game being this update. I do not think it's a bad game but I cannot recommend it to others until the issues plaguing this game are fixed. If you're unaware of the situation that this game is in: (eg. finding this in your steam recommended and this being the first review you've read or something along those lines.) It is a shell of the masterpiece I would have called it just a few weeks ago.  , Hopoo Games brought us this game and it's precursor, along with the first DLC for Risk of Rain 2 (Survivors of the Void), all of which were amazing content especially for the small indie team of  and the freelance composer that they brought on who has brought a distinct sound to the series and helped format it's identity. They spent a huge portion of their life working on this project and were ready to move on, . Hopoo reassured the community that the two would be in contact with each other and that they would overlook and assist Gearbox when needed to make sure quality stayed the same and that the game would not lose it's sense of self. We were all hesitant at first but trusted Hopoo and Gearbox with hope of things going well. Gearbox announced it's plans for the IP by showing off  (a remake of the first game) in late 2022, and we got basically no news aside from the fact that there was something in the works until 9 months ago where  was announced and we learned the name of the second DLC for ROR2, Seekers of the Storm. Okay so, Gearbox wasn't pumping out exactly what everybody wanted but it was clear they cared about the IP at least and were excited about what they could do with it. Then they were bought out by Take Two. Hostile worlds was cancelled 2 months later (just half a year after it was announced). Sad to see that Gearbox's first try on making something new with the IP they bought was cancelled but it was a mobile gacha game... Then 3 weeks ago we got the first survivor of the new DLC revealed! On Aug 22nd we learned it was releasing in... . So we finally learned what it was about, and then shortly after we're told it's releasing. It's released and the base game itself gets updated to prepare for it. The game is awful. They rewrote the framework of the game and now it's a buggy mess, there's so many issues with the game that you literally need to DOWNPATCH to the previous version to enjoy it. The DLC itself is alright? One of the new enemies breaks the game and literally requires you to scrap all of your damaging items if you don't want to instantly die from the damage it reflects (through walls), the new boss has some pretty bad bugs in his fight, the final boss fight is broken and he becomes invincible in his final stage, the new items are pretty bad and don't compliment current ones, so they end up diluting the item pool making it harder to get any movement and making runs worse. And the bugs are still there and cannot be turned off like you can with the DLC. I'd say the new stages are the best part, but with the huge size of them, it also means the loot in the biomes are more plentiful so to effectively get the best value out of going to them you need to spend more time than needed for other biomes to get everything, along with enemy pathfinding and attacking being broken due to the size of the new maps. This is the steam version so I don't have to describe the fact that it erases your entire save file if you try to play multiplayer (one of the key features of the new update) on Xbox. To get the experience that I would praise this game for before the DLC came out you need to actively go and preform the act of downpatching your game which is not made easy by the developers unlike other games on steam where it's as simple as launching an earlier patch. The modding scene is one of the pillars of the community but a bunch of modders have simply refused to update their mods to this newest version because it's so stupidly broken (they made everything dependent on FPS???) and it'd require way too much effort to rewrite their entire mod (I don't blame them, don't look in the code for this version it is stupidly obtuse.) If you wanna play ROR2, you essentially have to downpatch your game to get the core experience. I wish I could leave a positive review on this game I love but it's being ♥♥♥♥♥♥ over a desk covered in nails right now by suits forcing deadlines, pushing out unfinished products, and calling for changes that they don't understand.  I hope this review ages poorly and I'm able to update it to say everything is better in the near future, but even with the major bugs being patched I still think this game has had a downgrade at the hands of Take Two and Gearbox. If you want a good roguelike go play Dead Cells, unfortunately it's also being ♥♥♥♥♥♥ over by stupid corporate changes but that's another matter.Still an amazing game.

_childDocuments_.review: Risk of Rain 2 is a third-person shooter roguelike with a distinct art style.Features:- At the time of writing this review, there are 10 characters to play as, each with different play styles and unlockable abilities earned via completing specific achievements.- Stages are procedurally generated, where chests and other interactable entities spawn randomly across the stage.- The difficulty is always increasing, with enemies gaining health & damage modifiers as well as rarer and more dangerous enemies being added to the pool of possible combatants.- At the time of writing this review, there are 2 alternative game modes; time trials and 'Eclipse', where the game becomes harder each time you beat it.- 'Artifacts' which dramatically change the way the game is played, with some Artifacts allowing you to choose your items, enemies exploding upon death, enabling friendly fire etc.- Can be played solo & offline as well as up to 4 players.My only quarrel with Risk of Rain 2 is that the update cycle is slow, with content updates coming every ~3 months

_childDocuments_.review: So, I'm returning this game after about an hour of playtime.  In my second run, I made it to the 4th world and killed the first 3 bosses.  So, I wasn't bad at the game at all.  I also own Risk of Rain 1 and have spent a decent amount of time playing it. First off, I can understand why people like this game.  This is a GOOD game, for sure.  The action is cool and the controls are great.  I am giving a Thumbs Down because this game is not for me, and I want people to have a perspective on why this game might not be for them.Basically, it boils down to intensity.  This game is intense.  It's like Doom.  When the action hits, you have to be right at the edge of your seat, with non-stop focus and intensity, for up to several  minutes at a time.  There are short breaks between action bubbles, but the intensity in this game just keeps ramping up and up and up. And unlike Doom, you can't quickload, so there's no room for slacking.Now, there are other games I have that require focus like that, games which I really love right now, like Spelunky 2.  But the nature of a shooter like this, and also the graphics they've used here, really makes this game feel super intense and demanding, and at times a strain on the eyes.  To succeed in this game, you basically have to sit up and play right at the edge of your seat, like you're in an FPS tournament.I'm sure a lot of people, probably a lot younger than me, love this, but for me the intensity was just too much.  By the end of the 3rd world, I was really just wishing I could save or take a break...  Ultimately, I just can't see myself really putting in the time with this one.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun game but there are a couple of issues that make it not as replayable as it seems. The bottom line is the skill expression is lacking. It's not completely absent, but the game doesn't reward you for playing it a lot. 1. The power creepI understand that the game is PvE but that doesn't excuse at least trying to balance the survivors.More recent survivors like Railgunner can achieve consistent runs every single time yet characters like Artificer and Commando are more reliant on item RNG. RNG should make the game more replayable, not make you feel like you were put in a scenario where there is nothing you could have done. At some point you will realize when the run is dead no matter how well you manage your time. Sometimes you don't get a single damage item as Commando or a single utility item as Artificer and your 15 minutes of that run is wasted. If all the survivors from the beginning were designed have the same consistency as Loader, Railgunner, Acrid, Bandit etc. then it would be fine. However, Hopoo seems to randomly decide when to balance survivors instead of it being the core focus. A good example is Mercenary gaining the expose mechanic. A bad example of this is with the new burn changes added in the latest DLC, Artificer's flamethrower now does less damage. I understand some survivors should be more difficult to play but that comes to my next point.2. The difficulty is mostly fake.There are some things you can react to as a player but a lot of times your death is going to be from a random stack of collapse or overloading orb or a blazing stone titan. Mechanics that either have very little counterplay or no counterplay at all depending on the survivor you play as. One shot protection is designed to protect players against these kinds of interactions, but more and more effects are added to bypass one shot protection. Yes, you could just get a raincoat every run or a blast shower, but itemization isn't something to rely on in risk of rain. Dodging in the game isn't difficult, you can circle strafe the majority of the enemies in the game and the rest are hitscan with no way to reliably dodge their attacks. This is also probably why there isn't a true melee survivor in the game. The attack that ultimately ends your run is something that isn't under your control most of the time. Mercenary is the only melee survivor in the game, yet the only solution was to add i-frames on a 5 second cooldown or don't even play him as a melee survivor. The first 5 minutes of every character all have a fun gameplay loop, but as soon as you enter mid-late game things start getting stale. Eventually every character plays the same as soon as the run gets good. You're only going to be pressing 1 button (usually your safest yet still most damaging ability) while running around in a circle. The uniqueness of each character is lost the further the run goes. Which comes to my final point - There really isn't an incentive to master a character when item RNG is so important. Mercenary is probably the most complex character yet this is probably all by accident. Cancelling skills probably wasn't even an intended feature. Even if you are very good at playing Mercenary or any other character, there aren't really many ways to express your skill. The difference between a Mercenary that is mechanically skilled at cancelling vs a Mercenary that simply understands when to play safely is marginal. The difference between a Loader that has mastered movement vs someone just picking Loader up for the first time is negligible. In the end, optimizing your play doesn't increase your chance of success in a run by much. Not every PvE game needs to provide dedicated players with the ability to show off their skill, but the best PvE games reward you for the time you spend in them. It's games that properly reward you for mastery that keep you coming back for more.

_childDocuments_.review: A really fun roguelike experience and an excellent sequel from a 2D game, which is quite impressive. It's really nice how they managed to make the game feel about the same despite going from 2D and 3D.Fun as Singleplayer, and even better with friends. It can be as challenging as you want and once you have learnt what items should you pick, that's when the fun starts. Also, at least for me, I think it has a very low "frustration" factor and most of the time you die, you just wanna try again, right away and that's the best compliment you can make to a game like this.Music is great, graphics are clean and they do a great job in keep things clear even when there is chaos going on. Sounds are nice and controls feel quite great. Lots of unlockables, secrets to discover and a ton of replayability. Just be aware that it might need a decent machine to enjoy it at it's best since despite running well most of the time, when there is too much going on, expect the framerate to dip quite hard. Goes from 144 stable to 60 and even a bit lower sometimes in my Ryzen 5600x and a RTX 3070, at 1080p.TL;DR : Great game, definitely give it a try specially if you enjoyed the first one. Or viceversa, the first one is worth revisiting too.

_childDocuments_.review: As far as I’m concerned, Risk of Rain 2 is as good as gaming gets. Unlocking items, discovering new synergies, planning out builds — it’s all immensely satisfying. Make no mistake: This is a tough game, and the randomized nature inherent to roguelikes just won’t click with some people. But, for players with a taste for escalating action and challenge, this game stands as one of the very best in the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: Got this game from a friend when they had "Buy one, get one for a friend" deal back when it first came out.I've been watching this game's progression since it first came out, and I can confidently say that it's worth the money. Hopoo clearly listens when it comes to the changes they make to the game, and I enjoy that a lot. Roguelike is possibly the best phrase that could be used when coming to describe a game such as Risk of Rain 2, but there's a lot more under the hood to it than just being "procedurally generated".To start, the only things that are really procedurally generated about runs of this game are the locations of important things such as chests, shrines, 3D printers, and the Teleporter, as well as the enemies and bosses you will counter along the way. The most important out of these are the chests. From them, you will get a completely random item that will help add onto your "build", granting helpful effects that will allow you to progress easier. Money obtained from defeating enemies will help you get more items, that will in turn help you progress.It's a very fun game with an interesting gameplay loop. The multiplayer component will often make playing with your friends more fun than playing by yourself. As you continue to complete runs, you'll have to chance to get different and new items from chests you buy, changing the way your builds work. You'll get more characters as rewards for your progress, giving you new abilities and playstyles that will change the way you approach enemies. You'll get new abilities FOR the new characters you get that will add even more diversity to your characters. As well as that, you'll get other little rewards along the way such as lore for certain stages, items, and enemies that you can read on your free time.Unlocking different characters and experimenting with new items has been a blast, and I'm confident that going into the 1.0 version of the game and coming out of Early Access, this game will be fun to anyone who enjoys rolling the dice and doing your best with what you were given. The gameplay of this lovely game is just the beginning. This game also has a stellar soundtrack, artstyle, and background story that makes it really entertaining. I'd suggest giving it a try!

_childDocuments_.review: Risk of Rain 2 does much more than only introduce the classic multiplayer roguelike to an extra dimension. It enhances and balances many aspects that felt odd in the first game. Moving, for instance, feels much more natural, and aerial enemies are much better to fight. Whether you become a war tank, a glass cannon, or a racing car out of control, the game's pacing remains incredible.There are also new unlockables such as character loadouts (which allow for different playstyles on the same character) and skins. Oh, and that's not to mention one of my favorite soundtracks and setting ever. If you like action roguelikes, replayability, and unlockables, give Risk of Rain 2 a try.

_childDocuments_.review: Solid 9/10. For me to give a game a 9/10, it has to be extremely fun and fresh (originality is a myth, freshness isn't) with no glaring flaws in the gameplay experience. Risk of Rain 2 is a roguelike (fight me) action game where you go to a strange new world and kill its god. The core gameplay loop is exploring a level, killing enemies to get money (and xp but eh) and using that money to open chests and the like to buy a variety of items to help you on your journey, then activating the teleporter and fighting a boss before moving onto the next level until you eventually get to god, at which point he kicks your ass because he's god, but after a couple more tries you eventually manage to kill him and escape the planet. It's got a wide variety of characters who all play in very different and interesting ways even before getting into the items you collect, which vary from increasing stats to making it so that you're immune to damage on Tuesdays, adn sure it's Wednesday, but the damage doesn't know that! and everything in this game stacks, allowing for some truly crazy ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Difficulty increases as time passes, pressing you to find a balance between being fast and being thorough. The variety of characters, the variety of items and enemies, and the depth of the aforementioned balancing act adds an immense amount of depth and replayability even before getting into the artifacts and the loops and the alt gamemodes and the skill unlocks and the like. I'm nearly 400 hours deep, and the game's still getting more and more fun. Also i ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ love the lore, but i'm not gonna factor that into the review

Examples being CC items like the Chronobauble.- Some bugs, bugged items and bugged mobs.- Frustrating late game where everything that is blazing can oneshot you unless you play mul-t/engi with health/armor/shield items and a lot of healing.Most of the negatives I have listed are going to get fixed soon so i can't wait to take this game to the next level.

_childDocuments_.review: Risk of Rain 2 is a godamm Ethereal ExperienceIf you're the type of gamer who plays Hearthstone all day, no friends, and says Poggers, i suggest you run, far awayNo, this game is for the pure Gamers, the upper crust, the ones who go fast, smoke grass and eat ass. RoR2 is a Dungeon run game, where you have to survive a hostile planet, where nearly everything wants to kill you.The only way to survive is to become a well oiled machine of pure genocide, killing your way to the moon. The game is based around stages, with you going through multiple areas, all expertly crafted. They can vary from Frozen Bases, to floating fields in the sky, to The Hell dimension of pure suffering.You can pick from a myriad of Survivors, ranging from a magic welding astronaut, to a Slimy Plant robot. Each survivor has a vastly different Playstyle, from up-close melee with high movement and I-frames, to a Attack Speed based monster that fires devastating primary attacks from any range. Each Character is very polished, and i love to play nearly all of them. And each character has different unlockable Loadouts, to customize your playstyle and fill different roles. The loot is randomized, which can be annoying some times, but it leads to fun and exciting gameplay when you get a god run with your own luck. Items stack to absurd levels. And factor in that you can find 3d printers, which give you a set item for a random one of your items of the same rarity, You can build your loadout off one incredible item, or, say, 50 attack speed items, to take them to ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ sprinkle town. This gets even more crazy when you loop the teleporter, playing the other levels over and over again, until you can make the final boss into a stain on his arena.This game is a drug.Please help me.

_childDocuments_.review: Risk of Rain was a great game. It had an excellent soundtrack, enjoyable gameplay, and was able to appeal to several audiences (as long as they were fond of difficulty). I enjoy the game so much, I speedrun it. So when I heard they were making a sequel, and it was in 3D, I was very excited and only slightly anxious that it wouldn't work as a 3D game.It followed the path of Super Mario 64 and Metroid Prime. It worked really well.This game improves on the original in every way. The soundtrack is even cooler, the graphics are very stylish, and the gameplay is super fun. It's the first game I ever bought on early-access launch day, and I have absolutely no regrets. In early access, the game was already very solid and enjoyable. Now that it's been fully released and updated, I can say for certain that it's one of if not the best game this year.Of course, it's not perfect. It took some doing to get used to the graphics having absolutely no anti-aliasing, and some of the artifact codes are annoying to find. Plus, there can be infuriating moments where you're having a really good run and then get obliterated by a Clay Dunestrider because you were playing a melee character.But I firmly recommend this game. It's an amazing experience alone, and even better with friends. Plus, check out the original, which is still good and different enough from 2 that it has a unique experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Note: This review was made before the 1.0 version of the game.No other game has gotten me to play this many hours in this short of a time frame. Gameplay:Risk of Rain 2 has all the parts about rogue-like games you actually like, and actually manages to avoid many of the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ traits rogue-likes have that nobody likes. Obviously, since you'll have different items and, by extension, different strengths and weaknesses every run, the game has a lot of replay value. There are also new items, modifiers, skills, and characters you can unlock to change future runs, for better or for worse. You'll always be kept on your toes, as you never know what to expect because each run is completely different from the last in regards to the stages, boss fights, etc. But this is all stuff you've maybe probably definitely heard about any other rogue-like game that's ever gotten any praise from anyone. What makes this one any different from the rest of this super over-saturated genre? ...Well for starters the game doesn't ♥♥♥♥ you in the ass at every twist and turn.Sure, being a rogue-like, RNG is absolutely a factor that largely influences the outcome of each run, but the fun part about this particular game is that if you're good, you don't need Godlike RNG to win. Each survivor (edit: most survivors) has all the resources they need, in order to actually complete stage 8 (the earliest point at which you can complete a run) right from the start. Hell, the game even encourages you to rush through stages quickly without picking up all the items, because rather than getting more difficult each level, the difficulty in Risk of Rain 2 scales as time passes. If you dwell on one stage for too long, it will usually hurt you more than it will help you. Each boss also drops a green or yellow (higher rarity/power) item upon death, further encouraging you to progress through each stage quicker for the promise of a strong item. There's even an achievement for completing a run in less than 25 minutes. You don't need an amazing combo of items to carry you through each run. This game encourages this quick progress because it is designed in such a way that the player's skill will almost always matter as much or more than their luck, and that's what sets it apart from most other rogue-likes. Sound:The sound in this game is both the best and worst thing about it. For starters, the music is fantastic. Chris Christodoulou really went all out when making these songs, following suit with his amazing work on the first game's OST. The main stages all have a similar vibe to each other while still being different enough to have their own musical identities, while the secret areas tend to seem more ominous or mysterious. The "void fields" theme in particular gives me chills when I hear it. But... despite these tracks being arguably the best part of the game, you'll probably have to turn them down a bit when playing on the hardest difficulty or when going for a very long run. Due to the nature of how enemies spawn and attack, you'll need to listen for audio queues to avoid a strong one sneaking up behind you and obliterating you and your will to live. Now, save for a couple exceptions, these audio queues are all very unique and usually not hard to pick out from all the other noise that comes from combat (except maybe during boss fights because the bosses are very loud). The ability to recognise the moment an enemy spawns isn't the problem though, it's more so the fact that you have to do it at all. This means you'll have to turn the fantastic soundtrack down or off to perform optimally. Perhaps the addition of a minimap that display nearby enemy locations could help with this problem? Maybe it'll happen in a future update. Nevertheless, this problem is pretty minor overall, and it certainly doesn't make the game less fun. Visuals: The art style is overall pretty aesthetically pleasing. Sure, it looks a bit basic, and it isn't the most unique-looking game out there, but this style is perfect for what this game is. It allows the player to instantly pick out a particular enemy they're looking for from everything else on screen, which is essential once actual threatening enemies start spawning. So even if the visuals aren't your cup of tea, you'll probably appreciate the simplicity once you actually need to shoot things. Story:This is probably the game's weakest element, as the developers have taken a "let the player figure it out for themselves" approach, but to be honest, you're probably not playing this game for the story anyway. Verdict:Buy this game. Now. Even if you don't like rogue-like games, I think you'll find this one might be an exception.Edit: Nominating this for the labour of love award in the 2021 steam awards.

_childDocuments_.review: "Just One More Run" Syndrome: You'll say you'll play for 20 minutes, but suddenly it's 3 AM, and you're still battling waves of monsters. Time flies when you're trying not to die!Picture this: you've been fighting your way through hordes of enemies, barely surviving, when suddenly a giant, monstrous...thing appears out of nowhere. Your heart races as you realize you're about to face the ultimate test of skill and teamwork. Or, more likely, panic and chaos. Ever wanted to experience what it's like to be a hamster trapped in a wheel of death? Well, look no further, because Risk of Rain 2 has you covered! The game throws waves of enemies at you faster than you can say "I regret my life choices." And just when you think you've cleared the horde, the game laughs in your face and spawns an even bigger, angrier boss. It's like a never-ending cycle of pain and suffering, with a sprinkle of hopelessness for good measure.The vibrant colors, the detailed environments, and the way my character flails around while getting pummeled by enemies... it's all a visual feast for the eyes. I particularly enjoy how my character's expressions perfectly match my own when facing a horde of alien monstrosities: sheer panic. My partner and I had a lot of fun going through the game. My best advice is: Just be prepared to die. A lot.I understand that games are supposed to be challenging, but Risk of Rain 2 takes it to a whole new level. I also struggled a little bit with the controls, but nothing we can't overcome. We had issues with the multiplayer aspects, 2 or 3 times. The respawn system is not my favorite. You basically respawn at the same place you die... to be killed again a second after respawning.Risk of Rain 2 is like a rollercoaster ride through a hurricane—it's chaotic, it's unpredictable, and there's a good chance you'll end up soaking wet and questioning your life choices. But hey, at least you'll have a good laugh along the way. I recommend this game and I want to play more with my partner in the future. :-)

_childDocuments_.review: Summary of all the stuff below: This game is an addiction and for all the right reasons. Risk of Rain 2 is a sandbox of chaotic fun, its sights and sounds are stylish and unforgettable, and the quality-of-life is pristine to a point I’ve never seen achieved anywhere else. It takes a little while to learn how to play it, but once you’ve been hooked, you’ll be playing it for months. If you enjoy roguelikes, shooters, or multiplayer PvE games, this is a must-play masterpiece I can’t recommend enough.More detailed review:Starting off with technical stuff, I want to talk about Risk of Rain 2’s quality of life. I’m not sure if other players had problems with this or not, but I adore how easy it is to learn everything on your own. There’s no pop-up screens telling you why you should kill enemies, no NPCs stopping you dead in your tracks to tell you how the levels work, you learn everything on your own without interruption. Other quality-of-life stuff includes no loading screens, a non-intrusive story with hours of optional lore, and hand-crafted levels with procedurally placed loot and objectives to keep everything familiar but still engaging.While it works totally fine as a single-player experience, the game is at its most fun when you’re playing with friends. Another example of this game’s super friendly quality-of-life: if the host of the party has stuff unlocked, new players can have that stuff too while also working on unlocking it for themselves at the same time. It’s still a fantastic game on your own, and even though everyone will have to own a copy, I highly suggest grabbing a friend or three for this.Onto the gameplay, your job is simple: investigate an alien planet via violent greetings and pile on enough junk onto yourself to make it back into space. Each level, you take the locals’ life savings, spend it on chests scattered around to get items, and then head to a teleporter to face a boss. The items range from the expected to the insane: you could find a syringe that boosts your attack speed a bit, a ukulele that grants chain lightning, or a bazooka that makes all your attacks explode. You will have to memorize the items, but thankfully you get a little description telling you what you just picked up and how it works every time you find it. And even though there’s almost 200 different items total, most of them are simple enough to remember the second or third time you find it. But since there’s so many, that special Roguelike addiction keeps you coming back to try out different builds. Especially when you realize that items can stack, leading to all sorts of power-hungry temptations. Even better, few items can’t be stacked infinitely. When the potential for a god run is so high, while also keeping the game an engaging challenge simultaneously, that’s when you know it’s gonna be a good time.Speaking of challenge, the difficulty balancing is incredible. You see, the longer you take to clear a level, the stronger enemies become. So, it’s this balancing act of taking the time to find items while also frantically finishing the levels to keep the upper hand. The easy mode turns the game into a fun sandbox experience (especially when you get that one cheat code), the normal mode keeps you on edge but plays fair and consistently, and the hard mode is great for the usual Roguelike masochists. When it comes to the characters to brave this planet, they’re all fantastic. Each one’s a sci-fi spin on the traditional class system opening whole new opportunities for experimenting with items and builds. You got your archer, rogue, mage, dog, Spider-Man mech, etc. Some classes can overlap each other when it comes to item priorities, but not too often enough for it to become annoying. There’s this great feeling when it clicks into your head what stacked items can make which classes become overpowered death brigades.One of RoR2’s most impressive feats are its 3D visuals. So many Roguelikes are built off sprites and pixels to save time and energy on the gameplay. It’s a perfectly fine compromise, but this game went above and beyond these common restraints. Many of the designs for the models and environments choose vibrant colors and minimalism over details and realistic features, giving a cartoony yet surreal look to everything. This is probably the least best aspect of RoR2; it’s impressive and perfectly serviceable, but not as outstanding as everything else.I’m not gonna talk much about the music since it speaks for itself but this a rare time when a game’s soundtrack is as stellar as the game itself. If you take anything away from this review, give a listen to the music, both from the base game and the DLC. I’ve heard tracks like ‘The Rain Formerly Known as Purple’ and ‘They Might As Well Be Dead’ dozens of times playing this game, yet they hit just as hard as when I heard them the first time.The only major criticism I have with RoR2 is unlocking new character abilities. I really like how you need to learn and experiment with items to solve most of these, but some are just way too much of a hassle. It’s not that they feel too impossible, but that they can feel, ironically, restraining at times. It’s only a handful of them, but it’s annoying how I can get all of one class’s abilities in two runs while another takes ten due to bad chance or strict guidelines. In a time of predatory monetization, unpolished releases, and uninspired ideas, Risk of Rain 2 revolutionizes both its genre and recent gaming as a whole. If you’re thinking about buying it, get the DLC too! It’s just as high quality as the base game and I can’t imagine playing without it. I’ve barely played the first game or tried RoR2’s modding, so I can’t say much there, but as for Risk of Rain 2, it’s a smart game that encourages fun and creativity unlike any rougelike before it.

_childDocuments_.review: Risk of Rain 2 is incredibly fun.It's a roguelike based around the concept that you're stuck on a planet and need to get off. You collect items, power up a teleporter and kill bosses to progress to the next level, all while the game ramps up in difficulty. What can seem like a serene walk in the park during the first few minutes can quickly turn into a festival of chaos where you have no real idea why you're still alive.RoR has tons of items that can all be stacked and used at the same time, often leading to overpowered builds if you're lucky enough or can create a build that suits your playstyle and your character. Whatever you get can be useful if used right and your experience is different with every playthrough.Outside of the gameplay, the game has hundreds of challenges and unlockables as progression. You can do easy things up to downright insane challenges to unlock new items that you'll encounter in your runs, or entirely new characters which you can use.The playable characters are all incredibly unique with their own skill sets with secondary skills that can be unlocked via challenges that replace certain skills, allowing you to create the character you want to play as. There's the Artificer, a glass cannon that can be stressful yet engaging, the Commando, an all round character that anyone can understand and play as, and a myriad of others.And it's still in early access, with frequent updates. 1.0 is just around the corner, however, but even when it is released the devs have stated they won't stop support and will continue adding characters and other features.It's also friendly to new players, with an easy difficulty to help you get into things, and the locked items help new players slowly get introduced to new mechanics as they unlock new items and characters over time. It's also co-op, so you can have a blast with your friends, newbie or veteran. (items aren't shared though, i'd recommend installing a mod for that)The game has it's charm and it's very unique. Even if you spent 2 hours on a run just to die, you'll still want to play another round.that's the basic gist of it i guessgo shoot a crab or something idkalso it's in 1.0 now and the music is probably some of the best i've heard even if you don't play it give the soundtrack a whirl

_childDocuments_.review: Risk of Rain 2 is a true testament as to what could be achieved by migrating an already well-polished and hard as balls game from a platformer into 3D.Being a direct sequel to the story and mechanics of the original Risk of Rain (which recently got a remaster, RoR Returns, highly recommended, too!), it is a roguelite shooter set on the surface of a fictional planet of Petrichor V, where up to four (the game supports cross-network online co-op, more on that later) from a pool of eleven crash survivors attempt to traverse four deadly zones in order to get to the planet's moon, where a rescue ship would allow them to go back to the safety of space.The gameplay loop is simple, but immensely satisfying. Each survivor gets four skills: regular attack, secondary one, mobility skill, and a special, all complimented with a singular slot for additional equipment. Over the course of the game, killing monsters earns money which can be utilized to open chests scattered across the semi-randomized environments. Said chests contain items that enhance the surivors' basic abilities, such as attack speed, movement speed or ability cooldowns. Additionally, some items, such as will-o'-the-wisp or the ukulele allow single-target attacks to attack multiple enemies via post-mortem explosion or arcing eletric shocks. As such, earning gear is necessary for progression, which is done by finding and activating a teleporter hidden away somewhere on each stage, noticeable by floating red particles in the air.Activating the teleporter doesn't mean a character is instantly transported to the next environment, though, as it needs to be charged beforehand. The shockwave emitted by the teleporter activation summons a boss monster which needs to be taken care of in order to allow the device to fully charge. At the same time, the enemy spawn rate is increased dramatically, which, coupled with the limited area that the player has to stay in for the teleporter to charge provides a stimulating, nail-biting experience to both fresh and experienced players alike.Another important factor of the game is the difficulty. In the menu, the player can choose one of three base difficulty levels - drizzle (easy), rainstorm (regular) and monsoon (v. hard). All those affect spawn rates, player health recovery speed, and difficulty ramp-up speed, which brings us to another gameplay loop element that leads to the breakneck pace of the game: the timer.As the timer ticks up, enemies gain experience levels, their spawn rates increase and their damage output rises.  This forces the players to make their way as fast as they can, as lingering on a single level can make the difference between having to defeat a single boss enemy or three of them during a single teleporter event.The game's fun factor rises immensely with the addition of four-player co-op. The game is adjusted accordingly, spawning more chests and enemies the more players are on the server. Additionally, the game supports cross-network play (unfortunately no cross-platform), meaning Steam players can join in on the fun with their Epic games acquaintances. It needs to be said that this feature is opt-in: having cross-network disabled routes the gameplay through the steam relays, while with the option enabled, Epic Online Services are used instead, and the implementation of Epic services in this particular game is... shoddy, at best. With crossplay enabled, expect frequent disconnects and server crashes that rise in frequency as the game progresses, none of which happen when using Steam Networking.Risk of Rain 2's performance is nothing to scoff at, lending itself in no small part due to the minimalistic graphic design, but also the the optimization made by Hopoo Games and Gearbox Software, who now owns the game and provides support for it. It is not without issues, however. In later stages, or after looping the game a few times the enemy AI count can, may, and will bring even the most powerful machines to their knees. With my rig, an Intel i7-9700K and an RTX 2070, having a run last more than 100 minutes brings the frame count to a movie-like 24 fps. This is most likely caused by a QA oversight, as the enemy stat changes are calculated each rendered frame, proving to be a bottleneck for the engine more than the device it's running on. In normal gameplay scenario, even on a mid-spec device like a Steam Deck, the late-game performance is quite acceptable, as, at that point, it is not the player who will be doing the most damage to the enemies around them.The game is constantly developed, too - as of the time writing this review, Gearbox offers a DLC pack to this game, Survivors of the Void. This expansion adds new environments, two new survivors, entirely new gamemode and new "void-corrupted" items, which provide new twists to an already established formula of the game. Currently, another expansion, Seekers of the Storm, is announced and in active development, which I, personally, am looking forward to.All in all, Risk of Rain 2 is an immensely satisfying experience with tons of replay value. If you're looking for a great roguelite to play with up to three friends, great community support with tons of gameplay mods and ongoing development worthy of the "Steam Labor of Love" award (for real this time), don't wait and hit that "purchase" button. It's highly likely you won't be disappointed in the slightest.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been a Risk of Rain fan for a decade, the first game was my favorite game of all time for a while, I used to play it on my mom's laptop sitting in our living room. I can remember where I was when I got the notification announcing RoR2, I can remember making a tumblr account just to ask questions on Hopoo's blog, I remember the day it launched in EA and rushing back to my dorm to try it. Suffice to say the series is very close to my heart. When they announced Gearbox would be publishing RoR2 I was concerned but I trusted Hopoo and figured it couldn't be that bad. 5 years later when they announced GB would be taking over the IP I was VERY concerned but tried to stay optimistic. When GB’s very first action as owners of the IP was to announce a free to play mobile gacha game, I realized it was over. GB did not care about the game or the IP, they had no intention of respecting, and wouldn't even do us the favor of leaving it alone. Despite that, some small ignorant part of me wanted to believe the base game would still be there to enjoy. That part was wrong. The new DLC feels underbaked and unpolished with items and characters that clearly had zero playtesting and even less thought put into them. The new boss and characters have reused abilities and animations that look worse than a mod. While the DLC being bad was essentially a given, GB decided to ruin the base game too. They brought the code of the game in line with the console ports that they had made, the ones that had been famously broken for as long as they have existed. There are literally hundreds of game breaking bugs, soft locks, and general jankiness. A lot of it is caused by the fact that many things in the game are now tied to your FPS (you know, that thing every game dev knows you're not supposed to do). This includes things like Loader’s grapple, enemy attacks, and enemy spawn rates. GB says they are working to fix these things, but remember that they created the console ports that have been broken for years. If they couldn't fix the issues then why would I believe they can fix them now. They have demonstrated that they do not care about RoR and are too incompetent to fix anything even if they did. At this point I would be shocked if their bug fix patch does anything other than add more bugs. The future of this franchise is bleak and will only get worse.  Hopoo sold out, they are still saying they believe in GB which is essentially proof they were lying from the start. I love this franchise and this game, but it is dead and GB will continue to beat its corpse.You can still have fun with Risk of Rain. This game can be downpatched, Risk of Rain Returns is still untouched and great, plus many similar games exist. Roboquest is an incredible arcade FPS roguelite, Gatekeeper is a top down heavily RoR inspired game in Early access right now. Go do those things, don’t give GB any money. Goodbye Risk of Rain, its a shame it had to end like this.

_childDocuments_.review: The original Risk of Rain was one of my first experiences in PC Indie Gaming, and it left quite an impression on me. From its stylistic character design, to the 2d side-scrolling ability spam fest, and an ending with music so beautifully appropriate it ended up permanently etched into my mind. So, when Hopoo Games, a studio of 4!!!! Individuals announced they were making a 2nd game and it would be 3d, I was all for it. I haven't written a review for this game yet, but I've owned it since it was first available in early access and with its first DLC on the horizon I think its time. Theirs a lot of reasons why I think this game is one of my favorites, and why it succeeds so much over its predecessor, which in its own right is fantastic:The transition from 2d to 3d while keeping its style is incredible. From the ability usage, to the items, it all feels amazing as your character transcends into a beast until you either beat the game or loop until you die.With the items you can feel that rush of getting a red on stage 1, or simply feeling happy at finally getting those damn crit glasses for when you desperately need one. Every item serves a purpose that benefits you in a very direct, observable way.Plenty of secrets to unlock and explore, from hidden stages, characters, and items, it can keep you busy for a long time.A wide variety of characters that all allow for a distinct play-style while also having switchable abilities that changes elements of their kit. It is one of the best soundtracks that I've ever heard. From the active teleporter boss jams, to the quiet serenity of the earlier stages, to the absolutely fantastic finale of  it's an incredible listening experience, every time.Easily accessible coop through steam, alongside the new addition of challenge modes for people who want that extra difficulty or variety in their runs, So, should YOU buy this game? 100%. Play a few rounds on your own to get the hang of it, then once you inevitably get hooked, tell all your friends to buy it, and jam out with them. Your music will be electric.

_childDocuments_.review: You should probably read some other reviews if you want a more in-depth analysis. I just wanted to share why I find the game so enjoyable :DRisk of Rain was a phenomenal game which included a refreshing item mechanic and diverse range of interesting, characters, environments, and enemies. It's you against swarms of enemies accompanied by music that makes you chew bubblegum and kick arse. It consumed a fair good amount of my time for the game it was, and it was the absolute bomb when you grabbed a couple of mates. Hence, I felt I got the 'complete experience'. I was fully satisfied, not feeling disappointed in any remark. Risk of Rain 2 (ROR2) however...WOW! This is an amazing entry to the franchise. A 3D ROR?! I mean killing enemies in the first game was fun and all... but now that it's in a 3D vibrant, traversable environment, it's on a whole other level. Also, as this is only in early access, the developers have lined up a string of new content, which is really exciting. As we'll be introduced to new content, whether that'll include features, characters, enemies or maps. This game has a lot to offer in terms of improvements.Basic Overview:VisualsThe visuals are a major obvious step-up from the original 2D sprites. However, they still somehow capture and embody the nostalgic essence of the predecessor. This title is accompanied by an amazing palette that I find really aids in the enjoyment of the game. Watching the effects and animations within this game is so satisfying. It has an amazing visual aesthetic which complements the mechanics of the game smoothly. Everything that happens looks like how it should happen.GameplayPlaying this game, you'll experience a fast-paced gameplay, that's complimented by tight, concise and engaging player/environmental mechanics. You are able to select from a range of unique characters all having exclusive (and might I add, freaking awesome) abilities that make your experience 10x more engaging. The AI will progressively overwhelm you, but it will offer challenge rather than a chore, this being due to your characters progression in-game. The item mechanic is so refreshing compared to other titles. I don't think I could find this as well executed anywhere else. It offers a range of unique items that enhance your character and overall experience playing. Adding explosions, electricity, visual changes to your character and just so many more elements to the gameplay.  I'd recommend this game to anyone who loves a fast-paced, action packed shooter and enjoys rouge-like elements. I'm not too good at reviewing, however I am really passionate about this franchise and want to try to express how amazing this game is and that others should try it!  Thanks for reading this far, I appreciate it!

_childDocuments_.review: In case you are reading the current reviews and deciding if you should purchase the new DLC then let this be a median as to why the reviews are mixed. To start, the base game and Survivors of the Void DLC are amazing. Absolutely worth the purchase. The Survivors of the Void adds new item mechanics and characters that make the game fundamentally play different, however you can't really say the same about the Seekers of the Storm. The main reason the DLC is getting negative reviews is because of the lack of polish it seems to have. The latest update introduced a TON of bugs that make the game feel more "clunky" than it ever has before. As for the DLC content itself, it's not bad, but it's not spectacular in any way. A lot of people like to blame Gearbox publishing because they have no frontal lobe control, but in reality there are less than three developers working on this game and just a year prior, they released a remaster of their first game. While it's possible Gearbox may have rushed them to release this DLC, one way or another, it's not polished or ready for publishing at all.The new items are "bleh" at most. The new boss is fun, as well as the three new survivors but overall it feels less innovative than Survivors of the Void. Is it worth it? Well yes if you are a die hard fan of Risk of Rain and no if you are just a casual player. Overall the update shouldn't deter you from trying the game out (despite the newly added bugs) and I believe the devs have a lot of work cut out for them; but for now it could be a lot worse than it is and the game is still one of the best Rogue-Likes out there.

_childDocuments_.review: GAME IS GOOD. No, but for real this game stands out as one of the best examples of an early-access game ever, up there with the likes of dead cells, factorio and subnautica (and of course the original risk of rain!!) I have to say I was super sceptical about this game when i first saw the blog posts about it around a year ago. I genuinely thought there was no way they would be able to pull off transitioning such an iconic, tightly designed 2D game into a 3D environment, i thought there was no way the unique feeling and rush of the first game, but i have to humbly admit; i was wrong. The game feels amazing to play, the movement and the animations of everything feel absolutely fantastic, and so satisfying, dashing in and out of combat, carefully managing not only your health and your abilties, the ebb and flow of combat, but time itself and the money you have to earn to buy new items. the game feels extremely oppressive, even when you are STACKED with heaps of powerful items, you still feel like you could die at any second if you're not careful. The enemy variety is impressive for an early-access game and I assume it can only get broader from this point on, and they also read extremely well against the background and environments, which is something i was worried about, and im utterly surprised they managed to make it work, as in, you can tell that there's a brass contraption 30 meters away from you readying up to transform you into a red splatter across the ground, you can tell that there's a burning greater wisp in the distance or around the corner because of the uniquely coloured glow;  nothing ever really gets lost against the background... until the screen inevitably becomes a flood of numbers and particle effects a couple hours in.I am a massive fan of "survival" games where the only objective is to last as long as you can in a state of constantly increasing difficulty, and to date no game has ever more perfectly captured this concept than this one. It does an even better job already than the first game, because everything is coming at you from every direction, even in the sky. There is something deeply and viscerally exciting about dashing through hoards of enemies, barely surviving, knowing you could be dead at any second if you dont move perfectly or you get too greedy attacking a boss, and once youre about an hour into most runs you get to the point where you are slaying literally dozens of enemies every second with your abilities that launch missiles, chain lightning, runic explosions, sticky bombs and more. Pushing yourself to survive for longer and longer only to get brutally cut down each time, and don't let me sully your expectations; this game is absolutely brutal. But you live for those rare times when you get the perfect combination of items which lets you ascend into godhood, becoming practically invincible and making the planet fear YOU for a change. The only real reason i wouldn't recommend this game to you is if you aren't a fan of a game where you have to sit down and play functionally the same thing over and over for quite a long time, a single run can be upwards of an hour, with the really crazy ones being upwards of 2 or more, with no option to save and continue later. currently the levels are quite samey, each of the 5 or 6 levels is much more static than the original, largely the same map with small variations like an open door or not (i assume this will stop being the case later on, as the game is in early-access), though obviously the loot is randomly placed.But yes, overall I am extremely impressed with the game and it is an utter joy to play. i truly believe that this could be the next great rogue-like now the age of isaac is coming to a close, since hopoo have made clear their intentions to constantly improve the game like the first one.

_childDocuments_.review: A game that I would probably never have looked twice at, if not for recommendations from friends that had already played it. Don't make the same mistake I did - the reviews do reflect just how great the game is!Gameplay consists of being dropped into a world that is beautiful and crazy. It's slick FPS shooter with roguelike roots that is a blast to play both single player and with up to 4 friends. A multitude of classes, playstyles, abilities and items will make every playthough different and keeps things fresh and fun every time you play. It's fast-paced and unrelenting, but rewards smart decisions, exploration and PEW PEW.It has a novel graphical look that is surprisingly good and great music alongside it. Things can get very chaotic as you advance through the levels, yet the game always seems to maintain a nice balance and not go over the top to a point where it's a lightshow. There are plenty of unlockables - in the form of abilities, characters and artefacts. Some harder to figure out than others. Exploration is key here. As you begin to understand the systems in play, you can start to work out a character build that fits the way you play - and luckily there is plenty to chose from. Fancy a bow and arrow huntress with seeking arrows? Got you covered. Fancy a mercenary with a lazer sword that dices enemies at close range? They got you covered. They have engineers, gunners, aliens, robots and more. Sufficed to say, you will find more than one way of playing - and all of them are fun. Where it shines, however, is multiplayer - where teamwork comes together to form a really slick and enjoyable game to play.

_childDocuments_.review: Risk of Rain 2, while the price may seem daunting, is a game that will be worth your money as long as you make efforts to go for useful unlocks and learning the game's items, mechanics and maps.For starter, the game does look very nice and colourful, maps such as Rallypoint Delta and the moon look amazing along with the scores that accompany it. OST is definitely top notch. The sound design for movement and weapons of characters is great too, bandit's "Nights Out" ability comes to mind.The only character I do not enjoy playing is Commando, while this might sound deterring as this is the character you start off with, just know you also get the fun yet challenging to play Huntress and some of the characters such as MUL-T are very easy to unlock. The rest of the characters are good and it is important you start to experiment and determine what is important for the character and what is not, this is important mostly with playing with others since if you want the best chances to win you need to know what items your teammates need and what items you need. A lot of the items are understandable, there is no flowery flavour text it will usually just tells you what the item does and while you can become extremely powerful, you cannot necessarily break the game the same way you might in Binding of Issac for example. There is always an underlying challenge no matter how small. Can the game be customised and challenging? Yes. Plenty of mods for the game, there are in game artifacts which are modifiers to the game too. The base game has plenty of challenges for players depending on what difficulty you want to play at, the game has loads of enemies, bosses and elite variants to be a challenge. If you want more of a completionist's challenge the achievements are many and by no means impossible or bs to accomplish, the thinking involved in some of them are creative and intuitive. Isn't just for bragging rights either, some of the achievements carry unlocks to help make your game more fun.Are there problems with it? Yes. It can take a while but if you play the game too much in a short amount of time then the repetitive nature hits fast and can burn you out very quick and not touch it for periods of time. The game is also very unforgiving at times and you could be 60 minutes into a run, die to a singular attack from a small enemy and then you have just spent 60 minutes of your life with nothing to show for it. Like all rogue games there will be awful rng at times. And seriously, play with friends or at least people you know, makes the game so much more fun, I would not recommend just playing this game solo, make sure there is at least one or two people you can play it with.

_childDocuments_.review: Read more of my short essays on video games at Time always moves forward whether you like it or not. In the blink of an eye, the present becomes the past and the future becomes the present. Every moment spent standing still is a moment not spent moving forward. We've all been standing still for far too long, until we can move around again, let me tell you about a game where you won't be able to stop moving.Risk of Rain 2 is a game that forces you to come to terms with the passage of time. Each decision you make has to be evaluated against the time it'll take to follow through with it as well as the expected value of the rewards you'll get.Risk of Rain 2 asks you to be quick on your feet and to think strategically, by working with what you're given and making the best of it. The core gameplay loop involves killing monsters, gathering items which make you stronger, activating the randomly placed teleporter on the level, triggering a boss fight and finally teleporting to the next level where it starts all over again.Imagine if you took a dozens of hours long Diablo-like game and condensed that entire experience into tight forty five minute runs of pure third person shooter action; that's what Risk of Rain 2 feels like.Playing well means getting as many items as possible as fast as you can because as time passes, enemies get stronger and more of them start showing up. Each level is randomly populated with chests, containing items, that you can open with the money you gain by killing enemies.Risk of Rain 2 requires you to use your big brain as much as your quick hands. Although, you have to rely on your intuition more often than not because of how fluid and random number generator dependent many of its systems are.Should I stay and gather more loot or travel to the next level? There's rarely a right answer to this question, and it's a question the game keeps asking you, forcing you to make risk vs. reward choices constantly and having you face the consequences.Risk of Rain 2 makes this question even more difficult to answer by allowing you to play as one of the ten different characters who all play quite differently from one another. Each character has four basic abilities; these abilities can be swapped in and out with a few more abilities that you can unlock by tackling tough challenges. Although the game doesn't feature much player progression outside of each run, players can unlock characters and secondary abilities for the characters they already have through play.Yet another example of a risk vs. reward choice present in Risk of Rain 2 are the Scrappers and 3D Printers spread across the levels. Scrappers allow you to convert items into scrap, which have no tangible benefit on their own but can be used on 3D printers, each of which can build one kind of item. Through this process you can convert situationally crappy items into great items. This gives you some power to influence the random number generator, and strikes a good balance between throwing random items at you while giving you enough agency to manipulate what you get and turn it into what you want based on the items you already have.Figuring out which items you want is already hard, but imagine how difficult this gets when playing with other people. Although Risk of Rain 2 can be played alone, it really shines in multiplayer. The game makes you feel a constant sense of urgency, encouraging you and your friends to stick together, cooperate and move toward your common goal quickly. Sessions are short enough to be easy to fit into a busy schedule while being long enough to feel meaningful. The default difficulty is "just right", it's not too easy, it's not too hard; but if it isn't to your liking then you can tweak it. There's minimal player progression outside of a run and so players can play with each other no matter how much time they've put into the game.Even though playing in multiplayer is my preferred way of enjoying Risk of Rain 2, I should mention a few of its downsides. Players can't jump into the middle of a run and runs are long enough that this becomes more than just an annoyance. Also, dying in multiplayer is painful because you can miss out on loot which leads to you dying again and this negative feedback loop repeats itself over and over again.Despite these flaws, I prefer playing in multiplayer because the game doesn't seem to be built from the ground up to support my playstyle in singleplayer. For example, my favorite character is Loader. She's a melee brawler who swings around with her hook shot, unleashes gigantic punches and generates a barrier whenever she hits an enemy giving her a lot of survivability.Although, theoretically, she can handle any kind of enemy the game might throw at her. In practice, dealing with strong flying enemies or fireball spewing lizards by yourself is quite hard. I've found playing alone as Loader to be quite deflating unless I get some very specific items. Then again, playing in single player makes getting the items I need even more unlikely because there's less variety of loot and less of it. In multiplayer, I can play to her strengths while other players cover for her weaknesses. There's more loot to go around, so we're more likely to find the specific items I need (eg. Focus Crystal, Soldier's Syringe) to make Loader strong.Whether you're playing in singleplayer or multiplayer, Risk of Rain 2, for better or worse, keeps you engaged by never letting you know what to expect around the next corner or in the next chest. One could say that Risk of Rain 2's main game mechanic is the Skinner box.In a world where Skinner boxes in video games are mainly used to scam kids out of their parents' hard earned money, I'm not offended by Risk of Rain 2's use of the Skinner box. Unlike many of its AAA brethren, it's a cheap game with no microtransactions. I'm a "human being" twenty four hours a day, I don't feel bad for activating the primal part of my brain for a few hours here and there.That said, addiction is addiction, and so I wouldn't recommend Risk of Rain 2 to someone with an addictive personality or with a history of addiction of any kind. The cost of becoming "addicted" to games like Risk of Rain 2 might seem relatively low, compared to the alternatives, but as someone who dove out of the womb and immediately started smashing open chests in the original Diablo game, I can't help but wonder what my life would be like today if not for the Skinner box…Risk of Rain 2 is a great game, and a great sequel. It smooths away the rough edges of the original Risk of Rain, adds another dimension, literally, by making the game 3D instead of 2D and makes the game playable with friends online. I haven't gotten tired of listening to the electronic prog rock soundtrack yet which is surprising because I've spent dozens of hours in the game. And, I intend to spend many more hours playing Risk of Rain 2 as long as I've got people to play with.

_childDocuments_.review: before i start the review, i want to say this: DO NOT BUY THIS GAME. ITS OWNED BY GEARBOX NOW. BUY RORR, OR ROR1, BUT GEARBOX DOES NOT DESERVE YOUR MONEY. now, to the review:Despite being riddled with a lot of questionable, if not bad design choices, this game is incredibly fun and will make your brain rot. (DLC is not necessary for the best experience, btw. I would instead say that in its current state, its clearly too buggy and rushed. Maybe pick it up while its on sale.)The music is as usual great, the characters all feel pretty diverse and have their quirks, the gameplay is overall very enjoyable although i think that hopoo should really try to add features that the players have been asking for YEARS- a restart button, ways for dead players to keep up with the others, the ability to drop items in multiplayer, as well as small reworks of older survivors like commando and huntress, that really need some sort of buff. They are both fun in their own way but are completely outclassed by every other survivor in the game.Changing the final bossfight a little would also be welcome as it can be cheesed with enough mobility and i guess a bit of experience. Funny moon man literally cannot touch you if you are in the air, and i believe that he should have a (reasonable) attack that can inflict pressure on high mobility players as well.Maybe remove the final countdown before leaving the moon and make the ending cutscene trigger once you have reached the spaceship? Having to run from void reavers and moon explosions(?) is already pretty exciting by itself, i dont think that having to do ANOTHER useless "teleporter event" is very fitting, besides, the reavers cannot get within spaceship range, and if you dont attack them, you have no way to die. So, what is the point of the timer? Maybe make it shorter or make the players do something else instead of just waiting.Some lunar items would also definitely benefit from a rework, for example gesture and brittle crown have NO drawbacks and can be picked up whenever, it really doesnt matter. I would mention the autoplay issue, which is a big one, but honestly as this point its useless because the devs would have to spend ages to completely rebalance the game from the start in order for its gameplay to feel more skill based than rng based. And i dont think they have the time, or the motivation for that. I just wish lategame was fun and didnt break completely with you killing all enemies on the screen just by looking at them.Aaaaand many more problems.I have to mention a last thing; one of the main selling points of this game is its multiplayer element. Yeah, a multiplayer that is only enjoyable with friends, because random lobbies are not fun. Please do consider adding the changes i mentioned at the start of the review, as the multiplayer experience really needs some extra polish.Though, to be fair, you will only start to notice the games design issues once you have several hours into it, and at that point you will most likely be too addicted to care. Its still a fun game that i enjoy very much, so i still recommend it, despite probably sounding very judgemental in the above paragraph.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is overall pretty good, if you're looking for mindless-- (except not entirely, because there are tactics you can apply for better survival, even down to time management) face rolling combat and monster mashing then this is a pretty fun way to do it. Of course, you're going to have to accept the game is a roguelike... meaning that your character and all their items will be gone once you die, and then you start all over again... so please understand what you are buying into before you buy it! Luckily, I myself was able to get my copy free through a friend because of the buy 1 get 1 free deal they had until the 30th, which was absolutely an amazing deal and more than worth. That being said, the game doesn't just leave you with nothing to gain from your adventures, there is a sense of accomplishment to be made through unlocking new various characters, obtaining lunar coins to use in your adventures further down the road (won't spoil as to exactly what they do), and for you completionists there is a logbook in which you can fill by way of obtaining new items, monster books, enviroment datas.... Your presented with 4 varying skills to use per character, all of which are unique to each and vary wildly different than the last.. and each skill and character serves a certain role in co-op play, though of course each can still lay down the pain on monsters as needed, some just possibly might serve that role better but also might not be as good for raw survival... you get the idea. At the same time however, so far from the characters I have played I wouldn't say that any one is just inherently "Better" than the last, they all feel pretty well balanced *in the roles they are intended for*.. it really comes down to learning how to play them well and whatever suits YOUR play style the best, so don't let anyone tell you "Oh, pick X character because they are the best."... no, it's the best for THEM.The game being an early access title, of course naturally is going to harbor a lot of suspicion and caution.. and well, you should be! However, let me at least put some wary to rest in that reassuring you that in the games current form even, it is quite enjoyable and replayable to an extent you can well worth get your $20 out of it, after all... most $60 campaign games run a storyline of usually between 20-40 hours and then you're done, which you can easily get out of this! Save for the enemies mostly, no two runs will be the same either (the maps ARE mostly the same, but they have different a few different versions you might end up with). The game seems like it still has content it wants to expand upon too, so hopefully we'll see more of all of this soon (new characters are definitely confirmed).Definitely give it a try, I think you'll enjoy it as long as you are into face pace smash-em-up combat games! I would also like to point out that earlier I said I'd got this for free from the 2 for 1 deal from a friend... don't let that be a discredit to what I'd left you with here, believe me... I regret plenty of money I'd spent on absolute garbage throughout the years, and if only I could get that back to make up $20(s) to buy the game not even for myself (since I already have it), but even for some other friends I would do it.

_childDocuments_.review: I can safely say with a doubt that Risk of Rain 2 is a fantastic game to play. The unique cast of survivors, the different skills you can unlock for said survivors, and all of the items in the game have different impacts in which you can play every run in this game.One thing I can say about the survivors is that they are all fun to play. I can't really say I got bored of playing one specific survivor in the game. There's just so many ways to play certain survivors that every time I've played, I've had a new experience for a certain character because of the blessed RNG I have in this game. Some of the survivors from Risk of Rain 1 return to this one with some new additions like MUL-T, REX, the Captain, and Artificer. The new survivors in this game are really fun to play, especially REX and MUL-T in my opinion, you can easily get overpowered runs with these 2. For the returning survivors of the game, they are still a blast as well. Of course I have only 7 hours in the first game compared to my 400+ hours on the second but I still liked the reaction from my friends on the returning characters back when this game's early access released in March.Very, VERY, solid gameplay. I can't say it enough, I love the game's gameplay so much. I really like rouge-like games and Risk of Rain 2 has not disappointed me in the slightest. From it's enemies, to the maps, to the items that you get, all of it is entertaining to play. One slight problem I have is just the lack of alternate 2nd, 3rd and 4th stage layouts (like the 1st stages have) but this game is getting future updates so I still have high hopes for it. The final stage in this game is very nice to look at and the final boss is pretty bs but that's what you kind of expect for a final boss, always have to have some bs in your game.  This games music is amazing, kudos to Chris Christodoulou because they made a GREAT  soundtrack for the game.The various items you collect and unlock in this game (in my opinion) have a good purpose for any survivor. Bustling Fungus? Give that to Engineer. Runald's and Kjaro's band? Give that to anyone who can do a big strike of damage like Loader. Backup Magazine? Give that to Artificer. Anyway, you probably get what I'm saying, all of the items have a good purpose, it just depends what survivor is better or worse with it.I recommend this game if you like rouge-likes, a ton of RNG, and if you like a little bs here and there, of course rn there is a few bugs with the 1.0 release of the game, but give Hopoo Games a break here, it's a 3 person dev team, any for that many people, this is an outstanding game. I know I got the game for free because of the early release deal but this game is worth every penny. Give it a try, if you don't like it, you can always refund as long as you didn't do a 2+ hour run. ;)
