_childDocuments_.review: Asian food is not to everyone's taste but give these spicy and sticky Korean chicken wings a try, they make ideal finger food for a buffet, but don't forget the napkins!Recipe:Sticky Korean chicken wingsIngredientsFor the chicken500g chicken wingslarge chunk of ginger, finely grated50g cornflourvegetable oil, for fryingsesame seeds and sliced spring onion, to serveFor the sauce6 tbsp dark brown sugar2 tbsp gochujang (Korean chilli paste)2 tbsp soy sauce2 large garlic cloves, crushedsmall piece ginger, grated2 tsp sesame oilMethodSTEP 1To make the sauce, put all the ingredients in a saucepan and simmer gently until syrupy, so around 3-4 mins. Take off the heat and set aside.STEP 2Season the chicken wings with salt, pepper and the grated ginger. Toss the chicken with the cornflour until completely coated.STEP 3Heat about 2cm of vegetable oil in a large frying pan over a medium/high heat. Fry the chicken wings for 8-10 mins until crisp, turning halfway. Remove from the oil and place on kitchen paper. Leave to cool slightly (around 2 mins).STEP 4Reheat the sauce, and toss the crispy chicken wings in it. Tip into a bowl and top with the sesame seeds and sliced spring onions.Nutrition: per servingkcal487fat24gsaturates4gcarbs48gsugars35gfibre1gprotein20gsalt1.8gThe game is also good, a must play if for whatever reason you haven't already.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: Well, a few years later and I finally came back to this one after playing a bit right when EA started. Pleasantly surprised at the amount of content that was delivered yet baffled by some of the weird game design decisions.Really wish there was a neutral or mixed review option here as the game is mostly good, but the few flaws that are there are glaring.- the levels are too big and the teleporters are too hard to spot. There is no map. There isn't even a minimap. Seriously? The levels are quite large, tbh, excessively so, so this is a puzzling omission.- This means that a large part of the time is spent being in that annoying state of "Where the heck is this thing??" searching high and low for the teleporter and generally not being a pleasant game flow.- forced platforming in some spots is pretty clunky. You can prioritize items that boost your jumping though.- The final boss is straight out of dark souls.. the problem is not every character has a dodge roll type movement option that is fast enough or on a low enough cooldown to keep up with him making it rather unfun with some characters. Again, trying to build for mobility will solve that issue but it's either RNG or relying on the 'cheat' relic that lets you pick your items.- Runs are very time consuming, often upwards of an hour or more. There is no save and continue. Again, NO MID RUN SAVE and runs are 1hr+ ?- Character balance seems pretty out of whack. Some characters (Engineer, Artificer) seem to just do way more damage than everybody else. Other characters (mercenary, loader) are just a chore to play.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Choice for June 2024, and this is part of my coverage of the bundle. If you are interested in the game and it's before July 2nd, 2024, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle. A strange sequel. Risk of Rain was a sidescrolling rogue-lite with tiny graphics that was amazing, Risk of Rain 2 is a third-person rogue-lite and while it’s a similar game, and I can see the original here, thus doesn’t feel like a sequel… This is so much better.  In Risk of Rain 2, you’re running through multiple vibrant worlds, hunting treasure chests, finding the damnable teleporter that will take you to the next world, and fighting a boss while it charges up.  All of this was in the original.But if you ever played the original, you probably know this is different.  There are so many beautiful worlds, multiple fleshed-out classes, interesting enemies, tons of combat here, and a freedom of movement that feels like a massive upgrade.   There’s multiplayer that works very well, though I think it is harder than single-player.  There are also tons of items to find. Which is also one issue I have.  The game doesn’t tell you what an item does, so quite often you’ll have to use a mod to show that or look online for info.   I also got stuck twice while playing for over ten minutes in two different levels hunting for the teleporter that I couldn’t find.  Even knowing what to look for didn’t help.   Also, I struggled with the multiplayer but devastated the single-player, and maybe that’s a mod issue, but it did seem easier in a single-player. Pick this up if you like rogue-lites, if you are going to play with friends, I can tell you this is a lot of fun, and I’ve had a group of four that I’ve played with multiple times.  While playing this solo on stream this is the first time I remember winning so… yeah maybe it’s easier solo. _childDocuments_.review: There's always at least one game each year that comes completely out of nowhere and cements itself as one of the most memorable experiences said year had to offer. Risk of Rain 1 was one of my favorite roguelikes when I was younger, so seeing a sequel I thought would never exist pop up on the steam store got me very excited to see what Hopoo had come up with. Then I saw it had switched dimensions to 3D, bringing me even more excitement, but alongside a fear that the first games original charm would be lost in the transition. Regardless, it was pretty much an instant purchase, and I have no regrets.Risk of Rain makes one of the most seamless shifts to 3D that I've seen in years. I'm surprised just how little was lost in bringing the game to this new perspective. Almost everything that made me put 50 hours into the original is here, and I suspect everything and more will be integrated by the time this game comes out of early access.+ Port-Forwardless Co-op, even though pretty much no game in 2019 still requires portforwarding i'm still very thankful that its so easy now. Having to portforward just pushed my friends and I toward choosing a different game, and I never got to experience what the original co-op mode was like. That probably doesn't matter much anymore though, because I'm 99% sure RoR2's co-op completely outdoes the original's. I'm having a blast playing this game online finally, and I don't expect to drop this game anytime soon. Plus you can queue with randoms online.+ Some of the most unique characters out of any roguelike I've played. By that I mean that even though there are only 6 characters, each one feels so radically different that they completely change the way you play the game, and I wish I could say the same for games like Binding of Isaac or Enter the Gungeon.+ Fluid, exhilarating, fast paced combat, backed by solid controls. While the game is lacking some content right now, the core gameplay is already amazing.+ Lots of ingame achievements and unlockable items for earning said achievements, probably adding the most replay value out of anything in the game currently.+ Another great soundtrack. If you loved RoR1's music like I did, then you'll love RoR2's just the same. + This game excels at making every run feel different. Not only can you select different characters to mix things up, but in you'll be able to jump 4 times and run across the map in mere seconds, another you might have an army of phantom daggers homing in on enemies and multiplying as they rip apart anything in your path.+ Daily runs/challenges. They feel unique, shorter than a regular game, and challenge you to go as fast as possible. There is no reward for getting a good time currently unfortunately, but the addition is still appreciated.+ Pretty great performance for day 1 of early access. Not perfect, but more than acceptable.+ No game breaking bugs, at least none that I have found so far. No crashes either.+ Much more content, improvements, etc. to come.-Pretty unfair to call this a flaw in the game, but just be aware that the game is, as you probably already know, in early access. This means that there is no final boss or ending yet, not all of the characters or items are finished yet, the artifacts from the first game aren't implemented yet, there are some frame drops (especially when there are tons of late-game enemies or you are fighting a boss like the Magma Worm) etc. - Sometimes it will take a while to find the teleporter and that might be annoying. The teleporter can also spawn under shallow water sometimes, making it hard to see. Overall I think they should make the teleporter easier to see when you find where it is.- no rain, misleading titleOverall this sequel is looking up to be everything I wanted and more, especially considering I never thought Hopoo would even make one. It's well worth the 20$ already, and I feel like it's shaping up to be one of the best games of the year. Also a buy one get one free deal at launch was great and allowed my friends to get into this game really easily, thanks Hopoo!

_childDocuments_.review: Steam really needs an "on the fence" or "mixed opinion" option for reviews. But we don't have that so I'm gonna go ahead and say I don't recommend this game in its current state. It's not because the game is bad, not fun, buggy or anything like that, but simply because it's the most repetitive roguelike I've played. The music is cool, I love the way the levels look and the characters pretty much make this game fun. The big problem I've found is that it's not random enough. I've found myself getting bored cycling through the same six worlds over and over. Additionally, while the items are cool, they hit a point of diminishing returns around level 25ish and just don't make characters feel different enough. With all my runs using the same character, the experience felt very similar after I'd cycled through each world despite picking up different loot.Having said all this, it's a great early access game and the roadmap looks very promising. I'm greatly looking forward to seeing how the game develops and changes all the way up to release.

_childDocuments_.review: Risk of rain 2 is possibly the best example of how one should do sequels.It retains all the feeling from the first game despite transitioning into full 3d, and that is a unique feature very many games can't seem to get right, but this one absolutely knocks it out of the park. Currently in early access, the game is absolutely blowing me away in terms of how good it feels. It's risk of rain, but in 3d and everything resonates extremely well with it.The art direction for enemies, items, the environment and so on is magnificent to say the least. It retains that feeling you got when exploring a new map in the first one, but amps it up by being an almost metroidvania level of progressive exploration.Soundtrack is once again one of the best ones out there, though personally doesn't have the impact the first game did, but that's fine.And the gameplay itself? Its awesome. So far all hours played are in coop, but everything about this screams fun.There's a few minor things like some interactable objects not appearing for the other player(s) but bug wise that's about all i could find, and i looked quite hard. Enemies can get stuck in places as well, but not enough to really warrant outrage.Overal a solid 9. Can't wait to see how this goes moving forward :)

_childDocuments_.review: I have not played a game this much in a long time. Over the past 2 years I've been struggling to get into a new game and Risk of Rain 2 does just that for me. Its fun to play solo but its also really fun to play with friends. I really love the mysterious aesthetic where you don't completely know whats going on with the story but you go along with it and find out more. I would highly recommend this game to anyone and everyone. You can get a lot out of this game no matter what your preferences are. If you do struggle to get into playing it consistently it might be because you havent found your character yet. All the characters offer drastically different playstyles and finding the one you like is a fun journey.

_childDocuments_.review: A piece of Art! I love playing this with or without my friends or family!This game seems perfect on all sides : -Gameplay : the rules are simple : Explore, Fight, Loot! Every game is a constant rush of adrenaline!-Optimisation : With everything that happens at the same time it's crazy how this game runs well! Even on my old pc I have no issue of performance!-Content : With more than a hundred different items, 10 survivors, More than 10 different zones, 12 unique mutators, 3 difficulties,... The possibilities are endless! And despite the amount of content, The balancing of every item is on point!-Graphics : A really cartoony and simple style that give ROR2 a quite surreal look that fits perfectly with the "alien ambiance" of the game. This simple look help greatly the optimisation!-Music : The score composed by Chris Christodoulou is, in my opinion, a complete masterpiece. I'm listening to most of it almost every day. Some songs are beautiful progressive rock while others are in the style of punk rock and metal.-Lore : With a game without any dialogue, you would think that there's no lore at all. Despite not being lore during gameplay, there are logbooks to find that make us understand why we are here! Some players don't like this aspect of action games which Hopoo Games understood! That's why they didn't throw lore at our face! But lore is there for us to find it and the story is brilliant!-Community : The modding community is very active, you can have so much fun with any non-vanilla content! But for accessibility, Steam workshop support would be really nice!TLDR : Buy this game, go listen to Chris Christodoulou music, Get involved in the community! You won't be disapointed! It's worth every penny (even more)

_childDocuments_.review: I've been looping the OSTs for Risk of Rain for a decade now. In the game, computer, phone, and in my mind when I turn in to sleep every night. But what is sleep but another moment in which to appreciate the subtle tones of "Petrichor V" or the gradual buildup in "Nocturnal Emission".There's two interactive music videos (Risk of Rain and Risk of Rain 2) that offer up nice visuals to look at while listening to Chris Christodoulou's immaculate work. They even offer the option for co-op listening sessions with your friends. We use this time to discuss our favorite songs, especially when the game is kind enough to slow down to where we don't have to interact as much in later stages. While we lament the visualizer outputting a frame every other second, it does allow us to appreciate the music that much more.I sometimes wonder what a world without Risk of Rain would be like. But not for too long, after all "The Face of the Deep" is next in the queue and my air sax needs a bit of polish.

_childDocuments_.review: The art style is easy on the eyes early on, but as the run continues and your screen starts to fill with clutter, the diarrhoea christmas lights at later stages can be seizure inducing. RoR2 doesn’t hold hands and guide you through its story because honestly there is not much story going on here. There is rich lore to explore for people who want to. The lo-fi melody perfectly fits the perilous environment and matches the gameplay with synced rhythm and tempo. Sound design is good too.Drop into a planet, kill monsters, get money, buy items. Rinse and repeat until you become powerful to one shot God himself. Fast paced with constant running, jumping, sliding and juggling between primary weapon, secondary weapon, abilities and equipment. In each run the difficulty increases over time, which is an innovative approach to deal with difficulty. The roster is filled with unique characters who each have their own gameplay mechanics, making the game feel completely different. Most items can be obtained by completing specific challenges. You can also unlock game modifiers to make the game easier or more difficult to your liking. The challenges are one-of-a-kind, and the rewards are meaningful enough to keep players interested.There is no limit. It stops being fun when you decide so.There is co-op to enjoy with friends and difficulty scales with the number of players. And if you have no friends, rest assured because all achievements are attainable through single player.No bugs or technical issues. Without a decently powerful PC the game faces severe lags and occasional crashes in long runs where you loop multiple times and a million things are happening in the background. Lowering graphical settings can help to an extent.Survivors of the Void DLC adds excellent new characters, stages, items,  enemies and alternate endings.Worth every penny. The Devs are continuously supporting and updating the game which is commendable. The community is very active and you can add tons of community made  to breathe new life into your game. I highly recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Risk of Rain 2 is perhaps one of the most, if not the most polished Early Access titles in recent memory. The game feels like a finished product, boasting a lot of content for roguelike fans while attracting new kind of players with its charming visual style and engaging gameplay. Going into RoR 2 after playing the first game I was pleasantly surprised at how well the gameplay translates to a 3D environment. It feels fresh yet familiar, and improves a lot on the limitations of the first game.The star of the game is obviously the gameplay. You pick one of the several characters in RoR (you start off with 1 but unlock more through gameplay), and starts off in a level with nothing except your abilities, but you get to improve your character through purchasing items and equipments scattered throughout the levels. Collecting items is the name of the game here, as there are tons of different items in the game, each having their own unique traits that will improve your character as you purchase more and more items. That's the core loop of the game, just keep purchasing more and more items until you went from a weakling to a gun-toting ultramarine that can run faster than Usain Bolt himself. As this is a roguelike, a playthrough won't last you that long, and when you complete a run, you usually get achievements that unlocks new items in the game, attracting you to play through another run. The game is addictive and engaging, and does not have the slightest hint of microtransactions. The devs are also releasing a stable stream of updates that keeps the game from being stale, and they even announced the Full Release date.Risk of Rain 2 is a wonderful gem, a shining star amongst other Early Access titles, and one that I will keep returning to play. If you're a fan of roguelikes or just good old fun video games in general, get this game. You won't regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: I believe that the core of what makes a rogue-lite addicting is the power fantasy. When the RNG hits just right during a run, you become a God... and becoming a God is fun! Risk of Rain 2 understands this concept so incredibly well. In other rogue-lites, a good run means you feel powerful. In this game, you have the capability of becoming so insanely overpowered that you can barely even comprehend what is happening. Hundreds of enemies will spawn only to be instantly killed with a casual glance in their direction, exploding in a fountain of coins. On your tenth loop, you become essentially omnipotent - flying around the map at mach speed, thoughtlessly burning everything in your path as you stack another teddy bear on top of the pile and put on your 10th pair of red-tinted glasses. Until finally, like Ozymandias, your empire collapses in an instant when you greedily stop to scratch your nose, atomized into a million pieces by a random flaming jellyfish.In RoR2, chasing that power fantasy dragon is so addictive on its own, but this game also happens to have the added benefit of featuring extremely engaging combat, interesting enemies, intense boss battles, awesome level design, a ton of fun items, a diverse cast of playable characters, multiplayer, challenge modes, and to top it all off... what I would consider the greatest video game soundtrack of all time. The music is just so incredible that I can't really put it into words.Risk of Rain 2 is hands down my favorite rogue-lite, and one of my favorite games ever.

_childDocuments_.review: I typically don't write reviews, so bear with me here.Risk of Rain 2 is a phenomenal experience. From the art style, the music composed by the wonderful Chris Christodoulou, the gameplay, and even the complex lore, there's not much I can complain about in this game. I'm not a huge fan of rogue-like games, but Risk of Rain 2 has always stood high at the list of my favorite games of all time. The gameplay consists of you dropping into one of various stages, and battling monsters to get experience and money. You can spend money on things spawned with you in the stage, always changing location every run or visit to the stage. This will be spent on chests which will give you a random item, terminals which allow you to choose a certain item out of 3, and various drones and turrets. Alongside these, you can use items on certain interactables like 3D printers, which exchanges an item for another. Each item comes with its own unique and interesting lore, and each one is iconic in its own right, even ones as simple as "Gasoline".The monsters that you'll encounter are all also quite unique, and all have different things you need to watch out for. Even after learning about monsters and their attack patterns, an "elite" version of them could spawn which switches how you need to play around them. At the end of every stage, there will be a teleporter which you need to charge to reach the next, and charging that will spawn a boss, or multiple bosses. All bosses can be very deadly, especially in the late stages of the game. You could be having a run which you felt invincible in for the entirety of, and then make one false mistake near a boss and die instantly saying "What?". Progression in the game feels seamless, and being able to see the scaling difficulty in the top right definitely feels nice. At the start of the run you won't encounter many monsters, and you won't be gaining that much experience or money. As the game goes on, you can see in the top right a difficulty meter that goes up the longer you stay in a run, starting from Easy, to the game becoming sentient and laughing at you for the hell you're going to endure. The enemies will continuously become harder as this meter  goes up, dealing more damage and taking more hits, with items helping you scale alongside the monsters. More elites will spawn, and even harder variants will show up further into the game. You could even encounter a teleporter boss as a normal enemy on a stage. During each run, it's likely you'll unlock something new, such as an item, which could be found in your next run. Each unlockable has its own unique challenge that is required before you unlock it, some being easier than others, and some being incredibly difficult and requiring some effort to obtain. Alongside item unlocks, you can unlock new survivors, and even new abilities and skins for those survivors. Most of these unlocks you'll naturally obtain simply by playing the game, and rarely will you ever need to focus on that one unlock just to get it in a run.Risk of Rain 2 has no definite story to follow that's easily found just by playing the game, and requires some looking into if you want to learn about it. Each item comes with its own unique lore, and secrets found in game help build the world. Additionally, monsters can drop logs which detail things about them, explaining what they do and some behaviors of them. If you don't like worrying about lore and having to constantly remember it, this game would be perfect for you! But, if you do enjoy lore and story, you also have the option of looking into it and having a pleasant time doing so. Each entry has a unique feel, and doesn't just feel like a wikipedia entry, as most of the time it's written by a survivor or some other entity. The music. The entire soundtrack was composed by Chris Christodoulou, and there is not one song that I dislike. Of course, music is quite a subjective topic, but I feel most will find the soundtrack to be stellar. Each song that's placed in a stage or a boss fight fits seamlessly, each song managing to fit that alien-like feel that they're supposed to be giving. The song that plays can go from beautiful to intense in seconds, my favorite of this showing during the battle against the final boss. I myself can easily listen to the soundtrack on my own time outside of the game, and while some may not be able to do that, I'm sure  they'll enjoy listening to the soundtrack in game.I'm sure I missed quite a lot of key points, but this is what I could come up with. Risk of Rain 2 is in my top 3 games of all time, and I highly recommend it for everyone. Even if you aren't a big fan of rogue-likes, I recommend you give it a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: Risk of Rain 2, the sequel to the beloved classic. As a Decepticon who loves a good challenge, I was pleased to see that the game didn't disappoint.The graphics may not be the most impressive, but as a seasoned warrior, I know that graphics aren't everything. What really matters is the gameplay, and Risk of Rain 2 delivers on that front.The game offers a variety of characters, each with their own unique abilities and playstyles. I particularly enjoyed playing as the Huntress, her speed and agility perfectly suited to my combat style.The levels are procedurally generated, ensuring that no two playthroughs are exactly the same. This makes for a fresh and exciting experience every time you play. And as someone who is used to fighting on a grand scale, I appreciate the fact that the game has no shortage of enemies to face off against.The only downside is that the game can be quite challenging at times. But as a Decepticon, I embrace the challenge and look forward to honing my skills.All in all, I would give Risk of Rain 2 a solid 9/10. It's a game that's sure to keep you on your toes and provide hours of entertainment. And if you're a fan of the first game, you won't be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: I went into this game having practically 0 experience or knowledge of how the first one played, only knowing it had a garnered a great amount of positive reviews and a dedicated fanbase. I knew a lot of people were hesitant about the new one going into 3D and since I had no idea how the first one really played, didn't have an opinion on it. It wasn't until the game's surprise Early Access release that I began to look it because of all the glowing reviews. I honestly wasn't sold completely yet, while it didn't look bad by any means, the game play footage wasn't really doing much for me and I already had a huge backlog of games to work on.Well, I am ever so thankful that a good Steam buddy bought me this game because ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, is it some of the most sincerely fun games I've played in the last couple years. Everything about it feels so smooth and well thought out, which is insane giving how early in it's release we are. The gameplay loop is satisfying and leaves so much room for replaybility because of the sheer amount of items and weapons at your disposal, not to mention the ability to stack them all. The game developers practically encourage you to be an overpowered unstoppable killing machine, but thanks to an innovative and dynamic difficulty mechanic, the game keeps you on your feet while still making you feel like your making progress. The worst thing I have to say about the game are things that the developers have already acknowledged, such as some minor networking issues that cause disconnects occasionally and the somewhat lacking of variety of levels/biodomes, which are currently being worked on. Lacking in content in some ways is pretty expected from a newly released early access game so that's fine. I honestly can't recommend this enough, THIS is how Early Access games should be done. A perfect example of using the platform to both the advantage of the consumer and the developers. I cannot wait for more content and patches to make this already great experience an even better one. +Addictive gameplay loop.+Smooth and slick artstyle+Nice background music and satisfying sound effects+Insane amounts of replaybility thanks to vast amount of items and classes to play.-Some networking issues cause disconnects midgame-Crazy amount of stuff stacking in later game can cause some UI issues (being able to tab to see allies health bars would be ACE)-Lacking variety in stages. (as one would assume though in early access)9/10

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to wait for the full release to have my final say about the game but honestly with how each update has been and how amazing the game is even in its uncompleted state, I feel confident enough to say this is probably one of my favorite games of 2019. The original Risk of Rain was such a great and addictive game, when I heard about a sequel happening, I was both excited as I was skeptical. How would a game like this even work in 3D, and would it make the transition well? I can safely say yes, absolutely. I'd go as far to say this is even better than the original which I loved quite a bit. In terms of art direction and graphics, the game looks fantastic, it's great to see the old cast updated in 3D along with cool new classes, and the entire roster of enemies just look fantastic, and the various areas you find yourself exploring are vast and have a decent amount of hidden goodies to warrant getting creative and making sure you check every nook and cranny. Performance wise the game runs fairly well on my 1660 Ti but considering the main gimmick of the game, pushing runs over an hour and a half the game will understandably dip into lower framrates considering the amount of enemies, particle effects, and a bunch of other nonsense is on the screen at once. I play with the Ultra settings so if I really cared, I could reduce some settings in order to maintain a consistently high framerate even after 20 or so stages, but I was never bothered by those performance dips enough to really caring about reducing graphics settings, especially since if I'm playing the game for that long, the game becomes therapeutic in its insanity. Before that tho I used to run the game on my Ryzen APU with low-mid settings and still got decent performance out of the game even in late game portions of my runs, and it was just as addictive back in its initial release. To get it out of the way, as I'm making this review the game is not finished with about 2 or so updates left to be released. Aside from a minor delay, everything has maintained on schedule and there's always consistent feedback and updates from the devs, this game has lots of love and care put into it and its easy to see that they're putting their all into this game. I'm only noting this because as you can expect, changes may occur in the future regarding the game that will be different from the version I'm playing (The Hidden Realms Update). Honestly, the content is stacked with tons of characters to choose from,dozens of items to use and unlock, 8 or so levels with two level receiving alternate formats for the starting areas, as well as a few secret locations too, and unlockable character weapon loadouts to change a class's play style a bit. All the characters have their ups and downs, with some needing a bit more work to be made more worthwhile to enjoy (Rex and Mercenary are my least played of the bunch). Characters get their own batch of unique abilities that generally manage well for single player, but combined together in multiplayer, there's a bunch of ways to tackle co-op sessions and allow for great enjoyment with friends. Multiplayer is probably one of the best incentives to get this game if you're looking for a new co-op game to check out as it offers lots of variety and challenge, and thankfully I've never had much issue with online connectivity with others. So the game looks great, plays great, and is great with friends? Is this just a perfect game? Of course not, a lot of the issues that persist in RoR2 are in regards to some balance issues with character abilities, items, tweaks to level design to kink out minor imperfections in the randomization aspects (I've had teleporters be completely out of sight or spawn in strange locations making it difficult for me to make progress in runs because I check entire levels only to be dumbfounded where the exit is), there's also the addition of items, enemies, character loadouts, etc. to be added to the game that are still under development but the biggest issue of all..... there's no end game portion...kinda. You can sacrifice yourself to a obelisk but that's really it at the moment. All you can really do is complete objectives for items/character loadouts and sacrifice yourself or see how far you can get before you die or when things get way too mind numbing, the game is still very addictive, but I would like something a lot more satisfying to look forward to when ending my run that isn't just killing myself, the original game had a pretty fun final level followed by a multi phase boss fight that was satisfying to complete, but we won't see something like this until this game's 1.0 update in Spring 2020. That being said, this game holds lots of great qualities that warrant checking it out now, especially for the co-op, or if you just want a video game equivalent of crack to distract you. This is very well worth the $20, its a phenomenal game with tons of great qualities and replay value that even in its incompleted state will have you returning to complete another run over and over and over and over again. If you like games that encourage speedrunning, unleash your inner kleptomaniac, give you a difficult challenge, or just play with friends, this is a must buy.

_childDocuments_.review: This is coming from a place of love. As someone who's put hundreds of hours into the game, and purchased it for others to let them enjoy it. I love this game dearly. But Gearbox dropped the ball with their latest DLC + Patch.With bugs ranging from missing sounds, to epilepsy-inducing visual bugs, to breaking nearly (if not every) character in one way or another, to immortal bosses, to deleting people's save data, the game has become practically unplayable.I'm not able to confirm this particular detail one way or another, but people are saying it feels like the PC version was removed, and replaced with a 'patched' version of the console version. Which, for those who are in the know, know just how awful that is.The content the DLC promised to bring itself isn't the issue, mind you. It all looks wonderful, and seems very fun. But that is not worth completely (and potentially permanently) destroying one of my favorite games of all time. I'm afraid that due to the nature of the content this update came with, that being a paid DLC, Gearbox may not be able to make this right. Somehow I don't see them delisting the DLC and refunding it, before proceeding to revert the game back to the version it was in before the patch. But that would be the best way forward. Doing this, apologizing to the playerbase, and going back to square one and developing the DLC again properly would be the best way Gearbox could approach this.The only real hope we have for this to happen is to make ourselves heard. For those that already have the game, make it heard through your reviews, discouraging new folks from buying the game. Refund the DLC if you bought it. For those that have not yet purchased ROR2, please don't. DO NOT buy the game in its current state. It's in shambles.For obvious reasons, I'll change this review if Gearbox fixes things. Because I love this game, and I want people to be able to enjoy it as much as I have. But right now, that's simply not possible.

_childDocuments_.review: Hey there fellow gamers! Today I want to share my thoughts on a game that's been keeping me up way past my bedtime lately: Risk of Rain 2.First of all, let me just say that this game is addictively fun. The gameplay is intense and challenging, and I love the fact that it's a rogue-like game, so every time you play, it's a different experience.The graphics are stunning, the soundtrack is epic, and the character designs are unique and fun.One thing that really sets this game apart is the co-op mode. Playing with friends is an absolute blast, and it adds a whole new level of strategy and excitement to the game. I've spent countless hours playing with my buddies, and we still haven't gotten bored of it. The bosses in Risk of Rain 2 are no joke. They are tough, and they will punish you if you're not careful. But that just makes it all the more satisfying when you finally take them down. And let's not forget the power-ups. Finding new and exciting power-ups is one of my favorite things about this game. It keeps things fresh and interesting, and it always feels like you're making progress. Now, I do have to mention one small issue I have with the game. Sometimes the difficulty spikes can be a little frustrating. You can be cruising along, feeling like you're on top of the world, and then suddenly, BAM! You're dead. But honestly, that's just part of the fun. It keeps you on your toes and forces you to constantly adapt and improve.Overall, I would highly recommend Risk of Rain 2 to any gamer looking for a challenging and exciting experience. It's a game that will keep you coming back for more, and it's definitely worth the investment. So grab some friends, gear up, and get ready for some intense, non-stop action!

_childDocuments_.review: Risk of Rain 2 is the sequel to one of my favourite rougelikes: Risk of RainThe core mechanics are the same, with changes to fit the translation to 3D. You spawn with no starting equipment, and buy your items as you go along. The items are randomised, selected from a pool.The Lore is rather light currently, but there is a goldmine to be explored, with the actual gameplay providing the diorama which is backed up by the Logbook.The premise for this game is the freight ship 'The Contact Light' has crashed on an unknown planet, with it's cargo being spewed all over the planets surface. You start as The Commando, one of the survivors who was on the ship, and your main goal is to try and escape the planet. Along the way you will rescue other survivors, gain items, and explore the many areas of this planet.The Logbook is your main source of Lore (and mechanical knowledge) for the game. When you pick up an item, you find the shipping details for it as well. This provides you with some context as to what the item is, and how it came to be on the Contact Light, and as such the planet. Some items will have rather amusing logs, some that are adorable, and some that will just break your heart. It's a rather good way of giving you a story for each individual item.This game is addictive. Whether you had a good run that ended by obliterating yourself from existence, or a bad run that saw you killed in the second level, you will always find yourself thinking "Maybe just one more".The items are infinitely stackable. This means you can have insane combos, where opening a chest releases a barrage of fireworks that will seek out an enemy, hitting them and causing lightning to chain between nearby enemies, killing them and releasing a flock of spectral knives, which themselves in turn seek out enemies, exploding for each hit which chains lightning and kills them releasing more knives causing an explosion of fire...You will reach a point in the game, where you obtain THAT run, the insanely overpowered one, or the one with the most insane synergy, or the absurd amount of gold.This game is just . I nagged some of my friends to get this game. They agreed to get it, somewhat reluctantly, and within about, an hour they were saying "yeah this game is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ fun".You will love playing this game, and before long, most of your runs will end, not with death, but wi-

_childDocuments_.review: Holy Cow. Never have I bought a game in Early Access that i've been so impressed by in it's "Released as is" state.I picked up the game Immediately because I had played the previous Risk of Rain and knew that any new form of that would be enjoyable even if it wasn't quite polished yet, and the 2 pack was available so, hey, that was the prime time to do it.After playing for a day I decided to pick up ANOTHER 2 pack for two of my friends, because I liked it so much. It is unexpectedly polished and working quite well for being Early Access!Okay, let's throttle off the Praise and actually give you an idea what you are getting into with this game.So, if you have already played the first game this part is mostly pointless to read, but to anyone new to Risk of Rain, it works like this:You spawn into a map, and there are chests and interactables scattered around the map to pick up. Most of it is purchased with gold that you earn killing the enemies that spawn gradually here and there. Everything you pick up collects as passive bonuses. These are all basic things you see in most roguelikes. Area transitions involved activating a Teleporter that spawns a boss and several small minions to challenge you before you make it to the next area, and staying in that teleporter's radius (visual AoE, you need to be near it to charge it). It won't finish charging and enemies will keep spawning while the boss is alive.Here's where things really twist: As you play, you have a timer and a Difficulty Gauge underneath. The longer you survive in Risk of Rain, the higher the difficulty gets. Each rise in difficulty means more abundant enemies, tougher enemies, and higher chances to encounter "Elite" monsters that deal more damage and have special properties (As of now there are Fire, Ice, and Lightning). This means that as you keep going and grab more things in an attempt to grow as powerful as you can, you are also constantly facing bigger and tougher swarms of enemies popping up and trying to end you. This means it's a race to get as many items as you can find, activate the portal, kill the boss, and move on as far as you can go, before you inevitably get completely swarmed by 7-8 Elite Golems that all have their laser sights on you at once.This make the game extremely addictive in nature and incredibly fun to play with your friends. Most of what was in the original 2D Risk of Rain has been implemented while remaining true to it's origin, but now in 3D, with many extra things added to spice things up.Another important note I think anyone considering this game should know is the Devs are extremely in touch with their community at this time, and through both their Risk of Rain 2 Discord channel and their forums are actually actively looking over observations and suggestions from their player base. This review is being typed out right after their latest patch, build #3731106. Looking over this patch, a majority of it is changes made either by community suggestion or something reported by them. This gives me a lot of hope for the future of the game so far, and I really appreciate this kind of relationship with Developers. Thank you for your hard work thus far, Hopoo!So, if you haven't guess it by now I highly recommend this game to anyone (who enjoys surviving until they get ridiculously overwhelmed and die horribly to a Kamekaze Elite Jellyfish swarm, like me).

_childDocuments_.review: GameplaySee also: Risk of Rain § GameplayRisk of Rain 2 follows a similar approach as the first title, in which one to four players must progress several levels while killing enemies. On each level the goal is to locate a teleporter, randomly located on the level; once activated, the players must defend themselves from an onslaught of aliens, including bosses until the teleporter is fully active. Killing aliens gains experience and currency; the currency can be used to open chests that drop random items on the level. These collectible items offer a wide range of boosts to the players carrying them and provide both synergistic effects and the potential to stack their effects if multiple copies of the same items are acquired. However, the strength, difficulty, and numbers of aliens increase every few minutes, thus making the game harder the longer the players stay on any level. In the metagame, players unlock access to new playable characters, items, and game modifiers by completing certain in-game achievements; once unlocked, new characters (called survivors) or modifiers are available to select from at the start of the game, or the new items can start appearing randomly in-game.Risk of Rain 2 features several of the same playable characters, creatures, and items from the first game, but transitions the game from 2D to a 3D environment.DevelopmentWhen they started development on the sequel, Hopoo started with a 2D-based prototype with the player in control of one of the monsters in the first game, as to mix up the formula for the sequel. [1]The transition to 3D was partly inspired by fan art for the original game that showed the various objects the player collected shown on the character. Hopoo wanted to use this approach for the sequel, but the 2D graphic approach did not give them enough visual space to work with. They transitioned the prototype from 2D to 2.5D, representing the character in 3D graphics but otherwise playing as a 2D platformer, however this did not work to their satisfaction and felt it was better to move the game fully to 3D, with the transition being relatively quick to complete.[1] Hopoo Games noted that the 3D option provided "much deeper design spaces and more possibilities for cool gameplay" as well as more ways to artistically express themselves.[2] The sequel was first announced in May 2017, at which time the team had already been working on the game for 6 months.[1] The sequel uses the Unity engine, which Hopoo had to learn to use, and 3D levels which the team spent a long time making.[1] In designing some of the returning monsters Hopoo noted that they had to design new attacks to make them more challenging in a 3D space.[1] Items also had to be redesigned to deal with the dimension change.[3]Hopoo released the game into early access on Windows on March 27, 2019, at the time they estimated that the full development process they would take another year.[4][5] During the early access period, Hopoo signed with Gearbox Publishing to release the game on Nintendo Switch, PlayStation 4, and Xbox One.[6] It was also released in early access for those platforms on August 30, 2019.[7] Its full release was initially scheduled for Q2 2020 but was delayed in order to expand the scope of its 1.0 update.[8] A free content update titled the "Anniversary Update" was released on March 25, 2021.[9] A paid expansion for the game called "Survivors of the Void" is currently under development, slated for release on March 1, 2022 for Windows, and Q2 2022 for console versions.[10]

_childDocuments_.review: This is kind of a weird review to write, because among both my close friend groups and the internet at large Risk of Rain 2 seems to be one of the most beloved titles out there, but it just never clicked for me. Despite having over 60 hours in the game, I've never once wanted to go back to the game after getting all the achievements. For a while I've struggled to realize why, but after playing some other games I think I have it.In short, my main complaint with Risk of Rain 2 comes down to two problems, or rather lack of game systems that I'd expect from a roguelite: lack of progression, and lack of variety. One other seemingly repetitive game I've been playing a lot and having a ton of fun with is Deep Rock Galactic, and I think one of the reasons why is that there's so much to do: resources to collect, upgrades to buy, dwarfs to promote: there's always a reason to go for another dive. Risk of Rain 2 doesn't have this: once you've beaten the game with a character and unlocked its 3-4 alternate abilities, there's virtually no reason to go back into the game, unless the basic gameplay loop is fun enough to justify it, and for me it isn't.The other issue I touched upon is variety. Risk of Rain 2 consists of the same 5 stages repeated in a loop, with a couple different hidden realms. Once you've played through a stage once or twice, you've played through it a hundred times. While this is not unlike the aforementioned DRG or other roguelikes like Isaac, I think the thing that separates those games is that I enjoy the basic gameplay loop in those games a lot more. The reason for this is that variety is not limited to just the stages, but also the items. In Risk of Rain 2, you are on the lookout for largely the same items every run, that are very strong when you collect them en masse, and everything else is just kinda there. This leads to a lot of runs feeling very samey to me, where I collect a lot of speed, fire rate, bleed, and win the game. There's no crazy builds like in Isaac that you've never seen before; again, once you've beaten the game once or twice, you've beaten it a hundred times. I think the third and final problem with the game that prevents me from playing it more is the pace. The beginning of the game feels excruciatingly slow, with no real "aha!" items to make your run feel fun from the get go, unlike in a game such as Isaac. I also find the base movement speed of a lot of the cast too slow, making them very unfun to play for me, as they need a couple or more movement speed upgrades just to feel like you aren't spending the best years of your life walking from point a to point b. However, my issues with the pace don't stop there. After a certain point (especially exacerbated if you go for a certain tonic build), you become nigh unkillable except for extremely strong two-shots later in the game. This creates a weird nebula of feeling too weak into feeling too strong, and when combined with the lack of variety mentioned earlier meaning you can just go kill the final boss as soon as possible (stage 5), or just wander aimlessly around the same levels until you eventually get hit two times in a row and die. This feeling could just be me, but there's never any sense of "how will I make this build work?", it's either "wow I found the same five items on every character and will now win" or "this is so boring I want to exit the game and restart". Overall, I find the pace of Risk of Rain 2 lacking extremely, which prevents me from wanting to do repeated run once the aforementioned few progression systems are completed. While I've been talking very negatively of the game so far, I do want to highlight some of the things I did enjoy. The characters all feel very unique and (besides having the same builds being universally strong for 90% of the cast) play differently. I also do enjoy the environmental design and the music is pretty good as well.In summary, I cannot recommend this game, as I personally do not have fun with it. However, with that being said, I do want to draw attention to how much universal acclaim this game does receive from other sources. Maybe you reading this will have more fun with the game than I did, and I encourage you to look into the game further if you're interested in playing it. However, my opinion of the game is, in whole, a negative one.Edit: A couple of people have commented on my playtime, saying 60 hours is plenty of time for a game of this price. I should clarify that almost all of these hours were playing with friends during which I only played the game because I was hanging out with said friends, the game itself was painfully unfun, but it gave me an excuse to chill with friends. The rest are from doing small solo runs because I am an achievement junky.Edit 2: I am aware DRG is not actually a roguelite, mentioning it was supposed to be more oriented around the idea of a seemingly repetitive game being very fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Do you enjoy multiplayer co-op and/or singleplayer "player vs. game" experiences? This game is perfect for you, even if you think you're not good at FPS games and it is worth every penny. The totally insane over-the-top hectic action with explosions, rockets, and  while headbanging to  might make you forget you're even playing an FPS. On top of that, forgiving aiming mechanics and large enemies take the focus away from twitch shooting and puts it on character abilities and movement, where it belongs. The game developers are so confident in their core gameplay that they created a character that uses only a sword, and after playing for about 9 hours I believe that confidence was well placed. The game runs very smoothly even on limited hardware, the soundtrack is , and the controls are tight. The maps are fresh, large, and conducive to player exploration -- there are no invisible walls and you can get outside of most maps.Multiplayer is quick and easy compared to the port-forwarding nightmare of the first Risk of Rain. This game is essentially the same as the first Risk of Rain with some minor character, monster, and item tweaks and additions. That being said, adding the third dimension makes for a completely different game stylistically and mechanically, so you're still in for a new yet familiar experience.I cannot comment much about replayability because I need more hours in the game, but I imagine there is a maximum of 50 to 100 hours of fun time. It's still early and tough to tell, but again, those 50-100 hours is worth every penny they're charging, and it will still be one of the best experiences you've ever had playing a video game with friends.

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute blast to play.Have you played Risk of Rain 1?  It's very similar in almost every major gameplay mechanic, except one main difference.. it's a 3D 3rd-person shooter this time.  This is enough of a reason for me love it, because I always liked the idea of RoR, but felt limited by 100's of enemies crowding around me in a 2D space.   The transition to 3D is done very nicely in my opinion, similar aesthetic is maintained through the genre and graphical shift.  Multiplayer is also much more functional this time.  No IP addresses and port-forwarding or finagling with tunneling services like Hamachi to make it work.  Steam is integrated and provides not only an easy way to join your friends for a private match, but also matchmaking with random players.Haven't played RoR1?  This is a good place to start.  It's a great game in its own right, even without borrowing off the success of the first title- and I can say that confidently, as I wasn't a super-huge fan of the first one.  For a quick rundown, you can play alone, or in groups of up to 4.  You each pick a character class, each of which has their own weapon(s) and set of abilities, which have cooldowns.  You're spawned into a world and roam around killing enemies and collecting loot while searching for the portal to the next world.Loot works similarly to Binding of Isaac items, adding passive buffs, special effects upon hitting or killing enemies, random procs chances of special things happening, etc- which all stack and synergize with each other.  It also has a fairly heavy emphasis on stacking up large amounts of these items to improve their capabilities.  Finding fun builds as you play can be as easy as seeing what happens if you trade in all your common-tier items for gasoline cans, or sticky bombs... There are also equipment items, which you can hold 1 of (with the exception of one character so far that can carry and swap between 2), and are used with a hotkey, usually with a cooldown.  There are also turrets and drones you can activate for money, different kinds of altars that will take your money, your blood, or present you with a greater challenge, for a chance at items or monetary rewards, and all sorts of other optional twists and turns along your run.There are already so many secret things to uncover, challenges to strive for that actually unlock new items to find in your runs, and plenty of room to have fun already.. There's more to come, and this developer will almost certainly deliver, having already proved themselves with the first title, and the amazing early access release of this one.Anyway, check the early access information area on the store page in blue to find out what is currently in-game, and what is planned for the future.  I personally think this game is already great, especially if you have at least 1 friend to play it with, or enjoy getting matched up with random folk from the internet.EDIT: Just wanted to update my review after several more hours of play.  I just want to reinforce how addictive this game can be.  There are already so many unlockables and secrets, and the game isn't even finished.. So many cool builds to end up with depending on the RNG of the items you find along the way (or even a certain shrine that can leave you with an awesome build, or destroy your run, if you're willing to take the risk).  Even without all the characters and items implemented yet, there's dozens of hours of fun to be had here.  My friends and I have been playing for at least a few hours every day, and it's been a big hit in our online group.  It's fun to play alone, too.. Almost as fun as multiplayer, if I'm honest.. but I'd still think your purchase would be best made if you had at least 1 friend to play with, or you're comfortable using the matchmaking to play with some random people.

_childDocuments_.review: Simplicity at its best! You only learn by playing again and again. This is not something you can compare with other titles available in the market. It’s unique on its own. Give this game a couple of runs, and you will fall in love with this masterpiece. Grinding gaming hours was never that easy before.Risk of Rain 2 follows the experience of the crew of UES: Safe Travels who are trying to find UES: Contact Light and any survivor along the way. Their search leads them to an unknown planet where the environment is full of hostile wildlife, and the increase in difficulty over time.. The crew will search through multiple environments accessible through different portals. Will they succeed in the mission or face their Malheur? The story is just an excuse to justify your creature slaying thirst. The moment you land with your space pod and exit to synchronize the territory, the action starts. Get ready to face a constant spawn of enemies as the clock is always ticking and difficulty is increasing with every passing second. Utilize this time to locate the portal and open crates to gather items from the gold dropped from dead creatures. It’s just that simple. Kill the mob; earn some gold and XP; open crates; upgrade the character; open portal; kill the boss; teleport to a new area. The route is simple, but the surprises it showcases are beyond explanation. There is no chance of staying AFK and not getting killed. Sprinting and jumping are the core mechanics. It doesn’t matter how strong your character is or how many drones you hold. If you don’t sprint, you are probably gonna die in an instant.Remember not only your character gets strong, but all the enemies at each progressing second buff themselves to face you with a full blow. With all this ongoing madness, it well executed the variety aspect. The items are distinguished between quality, from common to legendary items. There are currently 102 items and 31 types of equipment to choose from. And as there are 10 playable characters, their loadout opens up the tactical aspect of the game. A jump boost might not be beneficial for an already fast-paced character, but mandatory for a tank-based slow character. No journey can be complete without unpredictable secret portals and surprise item drops.It doesn’t matter how many hours you played this game; it’s going to feel fresh every time you start your run. The game manages well with the player's skill-ability too. If you think you are struggling to cope up with game mechanics, then how about starting the journey with easy mode and climb your way up to the max difficulty. Now some might wonder, what’s the point of replaying the same thing again and again without any progression? Well, don’t worry, as not everything is unlocked. Completing challenges grant you achievements and unlock new character too. Plus, you can learn more about the items using the logbook option from the main menu.Overall, all my time spent was indeed a fun experience. Another best thing about the game is- multiplayer lobbies are chill, and they are playing for a fun experience too. No kind of toxicity and regular updates keep the game well over the line.Talking about unique art styles, and here we are! Not only the game looks amazing, but it’s amazingly optimized even with constant spawning of hostile mobs. One of my last runs included 6 stages at hardest difficulty and at least 60+ drones. But there was no sign of fps drops even at ultra settings (1650 super GPU). Every level has unique topography along with a wide variety of creatures and their hostile nature. Animations are on point and looks extremely well.  Don’t stay on the same island for too long, as with each passing second, the difficulty increases. If you are a horder who likes to open every single chest available on the map, then be quick about it. A single run on one destination should be between 4:30 mins to 10 mins max. Learn the firepower of your character and stack the types of equipment accordingly. There’s a full-fledge tier list available on the internet.Even though the game doesn’t lack content, but the devs are ready to present new surprises for the audience. By the end of 2021, you can expect a new paid expansion pack containing multiple facilities like- A hidden realm that can be accessed through a blue portal only and a place to purchase various items with lunar coins or exchange items for better ones in the two crucibles. The time and difficulty are paused until the players leave the blue portal. If you enter a blue portal, then your stage is looped back to 1. If you see below BBT, you can see a Null portal that takes the player to a hidden realm where they need to survive 9 waves of the enemy for extra rewards, but they can leave it anytime they want.If you want something different from the main campaign, how about alternative modes?Risk of Rain 2 is a must have game for your Steam library. Probably the best time killer light-hearted game even with a crapload of action going on. Slaying the God-like creatures with varied firepower and smoothening background music was an immersive gaming experience. Buy at any price possible, but make sure to give it a try, solo or with a squad.Rating: 10/10Reviewer:  Drones are like my babies.

_childDocuments_.review: Risk of Rain 2 is an incredible game. I have played a lot of different genre of games in my life and one of my favorites is the genre rougelike. Risk of Rain 2 is a game where the sheer numbers of items never feels enough. You play a game on any difficulty weather its on Drizzle(easy), Rainstorm(Medium), or Monsoon(Hard). You jump into a 3D world and all it says in the top right is to activate the teleporter. You are given basic info on how to play the game and it highlights that the game gets harder the longer you play.  When you first play you are just trying to grasp the games mechanics and the Commando the first character you have. You aim and shoot, can roll and have stun ability and higher damaging shot. Naturally you shoot then enemies that spawn in and get money. You find a chest buy an item. That item gives you more attack speed or more movement speed. As you learn the game and get more and more items you start to feel pretty good. Then you find the teleporter and the boss kills you. You are like "i'll just play another round" You start the next game and feel bad because the items you had disappeared. Which means you don't shoot fast or move fast anymore. You play and get pass the teleporter boss for the first time. Then you go to the next stage and get more items. Little did you know that in Risk of Rain 2 items stack infinitely. This factor when getting into the late game of Risk of Rain 2 becomes ridiculously fun. If stack attack speed you can reach thousands of attack a second. Or maybe you take the games warning of play fast literally and get a ton of movement items and become so fast that walking around with out hitting walls or flying of the map is impossible. Not to mention this game has a bunch of characters to select from. You do have to unlock them which is in my opinion the charm of this game. To unlock character or different items you need to complete a set of challenges. These are fun and give goals to aim for in game. You can explore the maps and find hidden codes which can be used to unlock relics which change how the game is played. Want to have elite monsters be the only thing that spawn to make the game harder because you find Monsoon easy. There is a relic for that. "I hate that items are randomly generated." There is a relic to make it so you can pick and item. I personally think this makes the game too easy because you can go for crazy builds rather than letting the rng gods give you the proper items. However, it is a fun relic because you can just choose to build crazy things like 60 war banners so when you drop one on level up it covers the whole map. Not to mention every character has challenges to unlock new abilities that can change the way you play a character. What makes Risk of Rain 2 a great game is the fact that as it is right now the game always has an objective or goal to push for. If have trouble pushing for it by yourself, you can play with up to four friends or strangers if you want. Steal your friends item and have them get angry at you because there is nothing they can do about it. They move at snails pace and you move at mach 10 so you can steal your friends items from cross the whole map. I don't usually review games, however this game is really great and only in early access. Its worth $20 especially if you have friends to play with or they are willing to give it a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: A thrilling rogue-lite experience, tolerably marred by its own clumsy implementation of difficulty.The base combat system is engaging and well structured, featuring a broad cast of unique characters each with their own distinct abilities and unlock requirements. Battles feel lively and quick, players chunking through swarms of enemies and dodging about as they unload their special attacks. There is a decent amount of item variety and most have distinct compounding effects when a duplicate is gained, allowing for all manner of extreme builds to emerge as the player stacks more items together. The graphics, animation and music are all nice to experience; giving the game a decent sense of polish and style. The world is interesting, offering a solid amount of area and enemy diversity along with written lore that can be acquired in various ways. A multitude of secrets and unlockables provide an extra layer of intrigue to the experience beyond simply finishing a run; which has multiple different conclusions based on the route taken. Despite how gripping the game can be it unfortunately does include recurrent moments of forced downtime, as players get currency by defeating enemies; yet those enemies do not appear at a reliable rate. Thus the experience has random moments where the player must wait for enemies to actually show up if they want to get more currency for acquiring items.While the game does well to keep the player active and engaged much of the time, its general difficulty is extremely precarious. Outside of obvious mistakes or trial and error many threats are simply a matter of bad luck. Various enemies have attacks which can obliterate the player if they do not react in a very specific way at a very specific time, which may be impossible if the surrounding terrain prohibits such. Characters with ranged attacks have the sometimes monotonous option of shooting these enemies from a safe distance away but melee characters have few ways to survive if the enemy shows up in a disadvantageous place. Meanwhile the accuracy of some enemies can seem totally inconsistent, with them missing or landing attacks regardless of how mobile the player is being.Although the game does have a mechanic in place to protect the player from getting instantly knocked out from full health, it does not stop them from getting instantly knocked out from high health; or getting instantly knocked out by multiple attacks in quick succession. As the difficulty levels increase and players get swarmed by foes, avoiding damage quickly becomes virtually impossible due to the sheer amount of incoming damage; and the distinct limitations on evasion and mobility in combat. The danger of a given enemy may also be obfuscated by how much their damage fluctuates with the level scaling and elemental variants, preventing the player from reliably predicting which incoming attacks they can absorb and which may instantly wipe them out. If they can even see the attack coming amidst the visual clutter of massive enemy swarms, or alternatively the player might just get hit from behind.The threat of being knocked out in either a single moment or a single chain of sudden events by an attack which may or may not have been visible or avoidable is a constant and pervasive issue; particularly in the higher difficulty modifiers. Fortunately this problem is not as prevalent if the player sticks to the default difficulty setting and avoids extremely prolonged runs, but even when playing on the easiest setting unfair scenarios do haunt the experience.Despite how generally fluid and comprehensive the game system feels it randomly becomes unhinged by compounding, unregulated factors that emerge as the difficulty amplifies haphazardly. Fortunately these issues can be mitigated by playing on the lower difficulty tiers, which makes them not entirely mandatory to this otherwise enjoyable experience.If you're interested in finding more games like this I've probably reviewed quite a few on my curator page .

My friends and I have been getting together and having a blast since we all got it years ago, and have made too many memories to count in the late nights we'd just be ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ around. Every new update that's came has been met with excitement and interest, especially Survivors of The Void, but this new update has completely and totally changed that.I don't have the same horror stories a lot of other reviewers have here right now, but the Gearbox change tying almost everything to the framerate and the few UI/Gameplay changes are some of the most useless and infuriating changes I've seen in a game like this. When it comes to being just flat-out annoying, the change to the health-bar and highlighting of multishop items is just plain pointless and only serves to make things much more difficult than they need to be. Other than that, the few gameplay changes they made regarding inspecting items, multiplayer pause, and being able to see the teleporter from further away are actually great.Slightly annoying things aside, the framerate thing and character/enemy scaling has been no short of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ horrible. _childDocuments_.review: They added a whole third dimension; it just feels so fun shooting things from a third person perspectiveMost of the familiar items and mechanics return, though some have been tweakedCharacters are distinct and each are a pleasure to playAmazing boss fights and game mechanics (including the wacky Artifacts)Multiplayer works out of the box and even allows for online matchmakingChris Christodoulou knocks the soundtrack out of the park againInability to save and resume runs for laterThe necessary switch to the Unity engine means that PCs have to be built to a minimum spec for this to run smoothlyOh man. The audacity of Hopoo Games and Gearbox Publishing to surprise release this into Early Access on the day of the PAX East stream. It was something that was hyped up since its announcement, and the BOGO deal for the first 2 days of launch pretty much sealed the deal. As far as marketing strategies goes this I feel was a tactical masterstroke. Just look at how many reviews this game has gotten, and a significant proportion of them are Steam-purchased reviews, which is an absolute necessity nowadays.Enough comment on that, though - Risk of Rain 2 neatly transitions the game into a full-blown 3D roguelike looter shooter, and it's totally a blast. You'll meet enemies old and new, and they all have a bunch of new abilities. Maps might be the same (the choice of artstyle is great, the colours are vibrant and is generally easy on the eye), but loot and teleporter location isn't, and there's enough variety with levels switching between a few different ones. Occasionally finding the teleporter is a bit of a chore, though.Risk of Rain 2 also sports a vastly improved multiplayer system. Setting up sessions in the old game was a chore due to port forwarding, but that's a thing of the past. A quick play mode even matches you up against random other people. The fun and excitement (as well as the teeth gnashing when a greedy teammate steals all the items) is all there.The current character classes that are playable are all neat in their own right. Old favourites like the Huntress and Engineer have their own new twists to help with the transition to 3D. The Mercenary's transition to 3D is an especially interesting one, and has shades of 's Genji, in my opinion.Of course,  holds it all together with his usual masterful command of polyrhythms and weird time signatures, all while retaining the famous motifs from the first game's soundtrack. All of these factors have combined to immediately skyrocket the game into one of my favourites to play.Chances are if you're reading this now, you missed the day 1 BOGO deal, sorry! But I can unabashedly say it's still worth the price even now. For the penny pinchers, get in quick before it gets raised; still a fair and justified increase, in my honest opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: I really tried to enjoy this game, I really did. Unfortunately, you can only slam your head into a brick wall so many times before you realize you aren't getting through. Risk of Rain combines two genres which I love, shooters and roguelikes which makes it all the more confusing that this game fails to impress.    - One major problem I noticed was that the combination of these two genres somehow managed not to take only some of the highlights of each genre, but also almost ALL of the lowlights. While many modern shooters are fast-paced with great movement, Risk of Rain somehow manages to feel slow both in pacing and in movement. You often have to choose between being fast and being powerful if you even have a choice.    - Another major problem is the simple lack of variety in gameplay. Unlike most modern roguelikes, the maps are repeated as opposed to generated meaning that every time you go to a map, it's almost the exact same map as last time. It's much akin to listen to a great music playlist over and over, it's cool the first couple of times but after a while you can't help but feel like you need more variety.     - In Risk of Rain, there is almost no critical thinking required. Great roguelikes such as Hades or Enter the Gungeon require players to think logically about whether or not it's worth the risk to get a new item as well as weigh different options to try to get items which synergize well with the items you already have but Risk of Rain is *mostly* absent of these mechanics. If you have the money, open a chest, if you don't, don't. There are a few places where you can decide what you get (outside of Artifact of Command) but these too leave little option in what to get meaning that you can lose (often) due alone to not getting lucky.Overall, I'm sure a lot of people enjoy Risk of Rain for it's unique characters and gameplay style, but for me it fails to impress. Risk of Rain fails to innovate and somehow manages to capture neither the charm and excitement of roguelikes nor the fun face-paced feel of a shooter. Despite this, I'd say the game is well designed and developed so I wouldn't blame anyone for enjoying it.

_childDocuments_.review: With a heavy heart, I can no longer recommend this game. Gearbox have shown time and time again they do not care about Risk of Rain as a game. On Christmas day of 2020, I bought Risk of Rain 2 on Xbox after having vague memories of ChilledChaos playing the first one and remember finding it interesting. After my first run, which ended preemptively at the first teleporter, I was hooked, demanding all my friends purchase the game so we could all play together. I sunk hundreds of hours on the console version despite its clear flaws. It was riddled with bugs, and even though SOTV was delayed for upwards of two years, I held out. When the first dlc dropped finally, I bought it on that day, having followed every word the dev team spoke about its release date, and it was worth it entirely. Sure, it introduced some new bugs, like multiplayer not working, but being on console, I was familiar with those already. It came with a brand new recoding of the whole game too, which had progress change over as well. Now, you may wonder what this has to do with the pc version. I say that all to show that not only did I love the game, I also could deal with buggy experiences and still have fun. It also shows that gearbox, the group associated with the console release were clearly incompetent before this dlc release, mishandling the console port for actual years before Hopoo handed over the reigns to them. From what I read, they sold the ip for 42 million dollars, which is not a number to scoff at. This dlc has ruined the game for not only the console players but also the pc players as well. When I bought this game back in December of 2023 and played it February of this year, even while heavily modded the lack of bugs was a new and exciting experience. You could boot up the game and play it, multiplayer or single player, going for as long as you wanted (or as long as the game engine allowed). That is no longer possible. Bugs riddle this game because low and behold, the console port's terrible new code was brought over to pc. It is so bad that people, including myself, recommend you downgrade to a previous patch to be able to enjoy your experience.You can patch the bugs, gearbox, but you'll never be able to patch the mark of shame on your company after so many catastrophic failures. Also, the new dlc just kinda sucks. The items feel ai generated and whoever made them clearly had no idea about the core gameplay look of Ror2. It's unreal.EDIT: Instead of fixing the bugs in a timely manner, they released a roadmap detailing how it'll take them several months to make fixes any semi-competent dev could do in less than a few weeks. This game is dead and gearbox killed it.

The transition between animations, or even when scaling a wall (which the game often encourages players to do) is not smooth at all and it interrupts the flow.
