The game also doesn't offer much content out of the box, with a plethora of characters having to be unlocked via paid DLC, and the missions offered become repetitive very quickly. There is no way to fight one-on-one with or against famous Naruto characters like in a lot of the previous Naruto games. PvP is a no-go because you will get rolled immediately by all the hackers who have seemingly infinite uses of their ultimate abilities and don't flinch from any of your attacks.Overall, I'd say this is an okay game for the current sale price of 5 bucks if you're a fan of the series, but otherwise this game is just a quick cash-grab with zero soul to it. Whoever developed this game seemingly doesn't care to put out anything that actually explores new territory or really anything fun at all.

_childDocuments_.review: As a huge Naruto fan, I've always wanted a game that you can build your own ninja and extend your abilities in a hierarchical way just like in series (Genin to Hokage ) as you progress in the game. Shinobi striker first seemed like to me as a game that I described, but it fell short of my expectations. I've recommended this game(not in full price) because it's fun in general but there are more cons than pros for me.  Lets start with cons;- Altough there is a rank that goes up by completing VR missions(PVE), this rank only unlocks some gear to purchase from store for your character as you go up but doesn't have any effect to your abilities, which you unlock from known characters in series by choosing them as a master. I'd expect more "meaning" about ranks.- The game is not built in this way but it would be interesting to have a concept of Chunin exams with PVP involved that benefits player with new features as you climb up. It is a nice-to-have thing but the reason I added it to cons is the game lacks feeling of progress after you learned all jutsu from masters and this would also bring matchmaking a new perspective of matching the players with the same ranks.- VR missions are boring / repetitive. - There are lots of costume/gear with features (like boosting damage / heal etc.) but these features have a little variety.- Roles in a team is a good concept but unless you play without friends, most of the things that are happening in a battle feels like completely random. Game is strategy forced but it doesn't go beyond jutsu/normal attack spam in %80 of games.(In some battles I witnessed some well-thought and calculated moves)-The comment above brings a "relative" lack of content compared to the other battle arena type games; Tide of battle doesn’t change from early game to late game. Fight until your ultimate jutsu is ready, use it and then start over. It’d be good to have some additional abilities / features as the battle goes on. Like having an awakening state just like in other Naruto games which can bring different skill set, spree-based rewardings or giving an advantage to losing team (the list can be extended).-There are 4 battle types in PVP but the game chooses which you will play in tournament mode when you enter queue. -Some battle types are not enjoyable in my perspective. Flag battle lasts 2 mins max in 3 of 5 games and in base battle (which you own sites and gain points if they belong to your team) the players with  Gaara’s sand shield jutsu (impenetrable – unbreakable) blocks all the site until they own them. A rework both to the battle types and particular jutsus might be useful.-There are 5 maps since the release of the game.Pros:-Battles are fast-paced, Wall-running and wired kunai (like grappling hook) contributes to heat of battle.-Although I stated lots of cons, the game itself still enjoyable at one point in this current state. Especially if you come up to a good team.-Everyone is shouting jutsus. SHINRA TENSEI!-It is related to Naruto.TL DR: I recommend to those who like not-so-time-consuming and fast-paced PVP. There are lots of combination of jutsus(techniques) that you can try for each role and find your own style. Also new masters are being added as a DLC, you can play with those masters for free but you cannot learn jutsu from them. Still I wouldn’t recommend at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: ▷ This game is not worth over 25(euros/dollars/quids) but on sale you can pick it up with just 5€, I absolutely recommend doing so if you have the chance. You're also going to want to buy those DLCs due to that they give you massive advantage in PVP.▷ Naruto to Boruto: Shinobi Striker has many of the familiar characters from the anime and you start the game by creating your own character; character creation is very limited but in my opinion it offers enough options to be satisfied with. You unlock hairstyles by choosing your sensei and leveling up with them or by purchasing them from Tenten.▷ This game has very small hub in which you manage your character and builds, from there you go to main mission (pve) or queue up to pvp fights.▷ Main missions in this game are very very boring and you can't skip the horrible scenes that happen before every mission you go to, mainly in all of the missions you just beat up a lot of enemy ninjas that spawn in waves in different locations. This mode will show you how little money was put into making this game. But completing missions will eventually increase your ninja rank which unlocks new stuff in the shop so you should do them.★ PVP is the main stage in this game, where this game shines and the reason why I am recommending this game. You can choose 4 roles, (healer, attacker, defender or range), each role has their own jutsu styles, and weapons they use. for example defenders use heavy weapons with protective barricade jutsus etc, healers use jutsus to heal allies or buff them in various ways, attackers excel in hand to hand combat and get jutsus to support that aspect, range type gets jutsus to spam from further away with very heavy damage. Many of the best jutsus are unlocked with DLC characters, when you purchase the DLC you unlock character you can choose as your sensei and then level with them to get their jutsus. What gear you use matters a lot in this game as clothes gives you passive attributes to boost your fighting style, for the fashion gamers I have good news as this game allows you to pick up the gear you like for it's looks and then you can purchase what attributes that piece gives you.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot of potential, & I have to say, it's amazingly fun. Except....it has a LOT of problems. First off; the game's balancing needs work. Like, excessive amounts. It is way too easy to spam attacks, and some classes for some reason get skills that make them infinitely, excessively more powerful than the other classes. Specifically, the Attack & Range classes get most of the moves from the masters. Defense classes get nowhere near as much in terms of usable skills as the attack classes, and ranged class gets moves that can be spammed to the point of game-breaking strength from level one.Attack class' skills are also extremely overpowered, able to ragdoll you to death so fast the Flash would wonder 'what the heck just hit me?'On top of that, there's the DLCs. The DLC masters can be used freely with levelup, but they only give you skills(or literally anything other than the ability to play as them) if you buy said DLCs, and said DLC skills are MASSIVELY overpowered, moreso than most skills in the basegame, making the game Pay-to-Win.Apart from skill issues, the game is peer-to-peer in battle servers, meaning you will find lag. a. lot. And i'm still half-convinced that 90% of it is artificial, used by other players to give themselves an edge.There's also the problem that the voice chat systems don't work properly, and that's only when they work at all. The menu chat systems are almost as bad, being so minimalistic they're basically useless.So, to sum it all up; This game has amazing potential, but it's ruined by the game's lag issues, lack of any even remotely proper balancing, lack of properly-built communication systems, and pay-to-win tendencies.If you can stomach going into a battle and finding yourself dead in ten seconds flat because every other player does nothing but use the most broken, unbalanced, overpowered skills in the game, some of which they probably bought their way to instead of earning it via hard work, by all means, you'll enjoy this game. Otherwise, don't buy it. It'll save you money, as well as stop you from breaking your keyboard via pure frustration.

_childDocuments_.review: The Game is pretty good, but instead of praising it the whole time (which is something i could very much do since it has quite a few good parts) i would rather count out some of the negatives so that you can actually make a decision if you want to buy the game or not, would still say i recommend this game to all Naruto fans though.  ONLY BUY THIS GAME ON SALE! So the first problem i have with the game is that it's really hard to get into now, since it has been out for quite a while, and there are a lot of really good players that you will match from time to time, i also dislike that there is no "true" story, but just missions that don't really have any connection to eachother.The next problem would be the Pay to win features, these being the DLC having characters that are obviously better than others, and their jutsu not being able to be unlocked for free in anyway, and the lootbox system in form of "moonlight scrolls" which is just a different name for the best kind of loot boxes, being the esoteric scrolls. These moonlight scrolls are about a euro each if i remember correctly, but of course you can't buy them 1 by 1, you have to buy 2 at minimum. Now how is that pay to win? While a lot of Loot box items are cosmetic only, there are also some Perks on these cosmetics which you can only get from these cosmetics, and those are only avalible in the lootbox system. Then there are also weapons with unique move sets, some being extremly powerful, that are also only avalible in the lootbox system, and these items are always very limited timewise. Meaning this game has both a pay to win lootbox system, and a FOMO (fear of missing out) system, very questionable.Next, you won't find beginner matches, there just aren't enough new players. So as a new player the only expierence with online you can have of the bat are quick play matches, and that mode is filled with good players, making some of your first matches really annoying, and also, queue times for quick matches are very longso if you want to just get on and play some matches very quickly you might have to play the Ninja world league mode, this mode is in a way ranked, though it isn't quite. You do earn points and get higher ranks, but you don't lose rank points if you lose, and you even gain a few every match even if you lose.But since it does have rewards there will be a bunch of sweaty players, that only play the best Jutsu with the best classes.My next problem, i shoul've named at the start probably, would be that the village you choose when making your character doesn't have any change to your character or anything as far as i remember, the only difference is what cosmetics you start off with, you can still get the other village items through playing the game.Well anyway that's all the negatives i can think of right now, i won't list the positives in this review. I am sure you can find some in other reviews.Thanks for reading!

All updates just add some new characters (whose equipment and skills you can unlock, if you buy them ofc) and that is all. I really hope that developers will add some new missions or online-modes. But for now, I'm tired of this game. If you want to buy it, expect it to become boring in 2 weeks (just my opinion).

_childDocuments_.review: As an avid Naruto fan, I was SO excited for a team based game like this!Too bad its a GARBAGE HEAP to play alone.Pros- Its Naruto!!!- Custom Shinobi creation is SICK. It's so cool to have so many of the iconic looks of the Naruto franchise at your disposal to mix and match.- The masters and learning their abilities is a neat concept seen in past games.- The VR missions are super fun to run Co-op with friends! Definitely the highlight of the game experience.Cons- There is NO Matchmaking. Enjoy being level 10 vs the level 50s.- There is no true story mode experience. Just the VR missions. In order to unlock VR missions, you must wander around the central hub to find a character who then tells you to walk back to the VR missions person to get back into gameplay.- There is no warping, which means you must walk to each menu slowly but surely. You also can't enter a menu while in queue for matchmaking.- All the outfits have stats on them!! Did you want to make your own custom look? Well too bad, you chose wrong, you're gonna get beat so bad online.- This camera HATES you. To look around, it's right stick. To lock on, it's right stick CLICK. Once you lock on, if you flick the stick at all, it just switches who you're targeting so you must un lock on to be aware enough to move around.- When you get out of a match, the game requeues you but it requeues you into the SAME LOBBY. You must unqueue, which is a menu. Then you must re-queue, which is a menu that leads you to another menu. Speaking of...- There are SO MANY MENUS YOU HAVE TO WORK THROUGH JUST TO CHANGE THINGS. You cant' change your clothes, your weapon, your Ninjustus, your Ultimate, without going to a menu, which leads to another menu. Its tedious. You must WALK to the place that lets you get to the menu that leads to the menu to the next menu.- The lobbies are BARREN. _childDocuments_.review: Alright, so I figure I'm at a decent point in the game to make a solid review. I've played for 27 hours over the past 2 days and I am at a point where I can see the pros and the cons. If you would've asked me to review the game in the first 10 hours, it would've been a positive recommendation, no questions asked. And I will still vote this game yes, but not without detailing the flaws that I've found.Pros:- Character customization is great, it feels good to be able to make your own character and tailor their style to how you want your ninja. My ninja is the ultimate edge lord, and I love it.- Combat feels great. Some of the ninjutsu feel a little underwhelming compared to the anime, but hey, if all of the jutsu were as poweful as the anime, people would be dying left and right, so I get it.- Missions are exciting and encourage you to replay them, to get cool new accessories.- The game forces you to get good at the game, and it feels rewarding when you feel yourself getting better.- Overall fun factor of the game is very high.These pros are very strong, in my opinion, with a couple things that I go "meh" about, but it's no big deal. The cons are very disheartening though.Cons:- Matchmaking takes forever, probably due to the lack of active players.- Lag is unreal. I have lost matches and gotten draws on matches that should have been easy wins but when I use a ninjutsu my character lags over the side of a building and unloads his wrath on a wall. Happens pretty regularly.- The increase in difficulty from C rank missions to B rank missions is ridiculous. I mean, maybe I'm crazy, but I think the A rank missions are considerably easier than B rank and I have even done an S rank mission that wasn't as hard as some of the B rank missions. It's extremely frustrating.- Lack of communication with teammates. I have had so many matches where I want to tell someone to heal, or signal there is a potion, or just tell someone to quit being an idiot and knocking the boss over the side when we only have a minute to kill him and he's at 80% health. I have used Discord to converse with my teammates that are friends, but not being able to speak with randos on my team can really get upsetting.The fact that I got this game on sale for $20 was amazing, because I wouldn't have gotten it otherwise. I'll still play the crap out of it and I aspire to become a Jonin, but there are definitely cons to this game and I wouldn't recommend it at full price.TL;DR - The game is extremely fun, but problems with matchmaking, lag, and lack of communication bring it down. I'd wait for a sale to get this.EDIT: There is voice chat, but it is extremely hard to find. For others who don't know, you have to go into sound settings, turn on voice chat and then turn on microphone. What a pain.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played quite a bit of Naruto games in my life, most of which are apart of the "Ultimate Ninja Storm" family of fighting games. Every Ultimate Ninja Storm game that's been released in the US has offered pretty much the same thing: three-dimensional combat using Naruto's cast of copyrighted characters. Because I've always been a big Naruto fan and enjoyed playing the games with friends, I would generally purchase each installment and sink maybe 70-100 hours in with some friends until we got bored of it. When Shinobi Striker was announced and some footage was shown it looked really incredible to me and my friends because it looked like something that I feel a lot of Naruto fans wanted: character customization. I feel like Naruto's whole concept and the amount of world building done in the manga invites a lot of contemplation on what the fans would be if they themselves were in the Naruto universe, and it's pretty evident that this is the case in the community when you look at the thousands of oc's that have been created since Naruto's conception. I figured that this game would try to encompass all of that, but I was worried that it would be a little bit shallow, as the class system seemed limited and the Bandai Namco branding sort of carried some negative connotations with it concerning the game's longevity and overall depth. As it turns out, I was exactly right. The game is actually a whole lot of fun for the first 30 hours or so as the player picks a mentor from the Naruto universe and designs their own character, picking their own move combinations to use in 3v3 battles against other players online. But, like I thought would happen, the lack of real depth really made this game's concept become boring pretty quickly. I think that this would definitely be much more apparent to the players if the game's "hub world" was replaced with a menu (that's really what the hub is when you think about it) because if you take that area away, what this game really is is just a whole lot of 3v3 battles and some simple story missions with your own character, which is just fine. TLDRThe game is not going to blow you away with thousands of customization options or compel you with it's depth, but that probably isn't what you were expecting from a Bandai Namco Naruto game, so it's just fine with me. The 3v3 battles are a lot of fun and one could theoretically spend a whole lot of time unlocking each of the moves and clothing items available in the game, but there isn't a whole lot of depth there. It's pretty simple and shallow fun, and a really good idea for a spinoff series of the NUNS family of games, and I honestly hope they continue it. If you buy this game, you'll surely enjoy it, the combat and overall design is decent, but you probably won't be able to spend a whole lot of time with it because it's plagued by the same thing most anime games are. If you're willing to sink your teeth into something pretty cool for just a short while, I think you'll enjoy it, but if you're looking for something with more depth to it, I would pick something else.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun and actiony game where you can create your very own character, but Steam reviews aren't asking me if I like the game, but if I RECOMMEND IT, and quite frankly, I can't recommend it to solo players like myself. Especially those who wanted to create their own ninja and see awesome feats done by them.My main issue is a minor gripe, but for people like me it might be relevant. I enjoy character creation games and injecting myself or my own characters into a game to watch them interact with other characters and the world. Unfortunately for this game there is no story mode really. ANY cutscenes you see in this game don't even include your main character in them (I could be wrong, but this is just based on the first 2 hours of playing and it doesn't take much to realize this is a multiplayer focused game). This sucks because I was really enjoying the idea of maybe having your character in cutscenes with your favorite Naruto characters doing crazy jutsu all over the place like how DBXenoverse 2 had you shooting ki beams in cutscenes and punching holes through people. This issue means you don't have anything really engaging you to continue playing the game unless you're a competitive pvp type which this game seems heavily aimed towards. No problem with that of course, but for solo players this game isn't really for you.There's also the big killer which is that this game is ONLINE ONLY. Meaning that even if you were okay with the no story mode and you simply enjoy playing the solo missions with your created character, then you'll have to be sure you're online to enjoy that experience. What's worse is that automatically gives the game an expiration date since, once Bandai Namco decides to shut down servers (as they will eventually in the future whenever it doesn't seem profitable to keep them up), the game will be unplayable. I've read on the forums there's a way to play offline but it involves deleting a file, so since it's not an official feature that the devs have and it's outside help you need I still remove the points from this game.Ultimately I will NOT be refunding the game, as I find it to be a very fun and enjoyable experience having my own ninja running around and fighting other people and doing missions, but this is a NOT RECOMMENDED for solo players and also a message to the Bandai Namco that I'm disappointed in them. When I see Bandai Namco games I have some expecations of quality from them due to previous games I've played of theirs that I enjoy like God Eater and DBXenoverse and such. Those games I mentioned allow character creation that feels meaningful as you progress through a story and your character forges bonds with some of your favorite characters. In this game you just get dumped into the hub world and do some tutorial stuff and it all just feels so joyless and mechanical without a soul. I know these guys can do better and I honestly hope they do. I know this might be flamebait to say, but I'd honestly be okay with paying +$10 for a Story mode DLC where they add cutscenes where your character shows up in doing action scenes and of course missions where you impact the story. Either way I like this game but solo players be aware of what you're getting yourself into just in case. Not a bad game, but a loooooooooot of wasted potential here.

_childDocuments_.review: So I've played this game a lot, I bought it out of nostalgia for old school PS2 Naruto games.-The game delivers a very fun gameplay, that you can master easily, which is always nice. Ninja parkour, jutsus, parrying... Very efficient and fun.-Creating your own ninja. It is every boy's dream, I used to be one, so I'm happy with it. Unlockable suits, complete custom character creation, Selecting the class AND the jutsus that fits your playstyle. It's complete, fun to use, just a bit sad to not be able to color your gear, but hey, you need to have unlockables for this game.-Characters from every eras, entertaining bossfights that are a bit challenging, fun level design. Plus you can choose your sensei and learn his jutsus, and that's a nice touch.-Visuals nailed the anime vibe. Shadows that are hand-drawn textures, oil paint textures on the levels, SFX, camera movements, well done.-I remember the communication of the game being really vague about it being an open-world. It is not at all. It would have been the bomb if it had been, but it's an arena fighter. They are big, you got space, but I would have loved it to be like  : free-roam arenas open-world.-Very well made maps, but not enough of them. You can make strats thanks to the wallrun and the intricate level design, and it can be really dope, but you end up playing in 5 maps over and over again.-A lot of missions... that tends to repeat themselves. It is sad really, because it is the majority of what you do ingame. The PVP section got lil to no variety, it's deathmatch, grab the flag and control the zones... thrilling. And the PVE missions got the same structures most of the time, plus they repeat themselves in higher difficulty when you gain ranks, and when one is done you go back to the generic placeholder lobby, being here just a plaza of Konoha.-(EDIT) I add this now because it has gotten on my nerves : loot f*ing boxes. And not a balanced system. To be clear, you'll have to open scrolls to unlock 85 percents of the gear of this game, it's random chance, gear is ranked by rarity (which means that there are some you cannot unlock with low type scrolls). So already, this type of system rewards luck instead of commitment to the game, so I already hate it. But hey, I would digest it IF you were not able to unlock ten times the same piece of outfit, like the dam face piercings, and if they were not selling scrolls to you. You can play the game, end up with twenty rolls on you... and unlock nothing new ! It happened to me on multiple occasions. Because unlocking a new outfit does not alter your chance of having it next time ! It really is infuriating.The body of the game, core mechanics, is good but flawed. The heart of the game, content, is good but too repetitive.To me, it is still a good game, because it is fun, and I go back to it with pleasure, but it's a game I play in short runs before boredom starts to set in. I launch it after months or weeks, rediscover the lil amount of content there is, gain XP, unlock things, and when it becomes repetitive again, I turn it off and forget it for weeks.Good fun from time to time.

It is by and far the LEAST CREATIVE THING you can possibly add. You're basically untheming the game the more you add. Stop ruining my investment. It's extra-dumb to see a gattling-gun wielding Ninja fighting a ninja with japanese throwing knife. Even Nabari No Ou didn't go that far. These are not super sneaky hackers. There are level 1s with Jonin and their money is all 9s. The most basic of logical deductions programmed into the base game could catch half of these hackers. But the developer doesn't seem to care. They have been hogging the industry's ability to make naruto games so they could slowly drip-feed minimum-effort DLCs. Each DLC is more powerful than the last, to ensure you can't compete without continuing to spend money. I now have a button I can press as a defender to just shut off enemy ranged attacks around my team. So for more than 50% of the time enemy ranged characters are "noped". There's also now a jutsu to "nope" healers in the same way where your target can't be healed or debuffed. Not very fun to have someone switch to "nope" your type, and bully you into switching ninja on your next death. This game is unfortunately 4v4. This means most wins/losses have nothing to do with your actions, and rely mostly to do on which teammates/enemies you are paired with. Most of the time, there will be hackers or someone will disconnect and Bandi Namco couldn't rub two braincells together to anticipate this and allow reconnects, requeues, surrenders, or anything else to save me from 20 minutes of unwinnable 2v4/3v4 due to disconnecters. However, when you do get a playable match every once in a blue moon, you are such a small amount of the total number of players your own skill doesn't determine your win or loss. This game would be so much more fun 2v2, or maybe 3v3. That would also be mean less disconnects immediately one-siding the match, since there are less total players. But I think they're going for that league of legends style balance where there isn't any, and they obscure it with large player counts and extremely vague poorly translated descriptions. There are still to this day, years after release, the most basic of bugs that anyone who played their own game would notice. For example, if you play Ohnoki and cast Super Lightweight Boulder, you say "Super Heavy Boulder Jutsu!!!" when you cast it. And when you cast Super Heavy Boulder Jutsu it says "Super Lightweight Boulder Jutsu!!!" The fact that the developers have not noticed this and taken the 30 seconds to switch the audio files years into selling patches is pathetic, and really shows how little love the game gets. It is a cash grab.Lastly, IS IT REALLY NECESSARY to unload and load the map every match? It takes like 5-10 minutes to get into a match because none of the loading is done beforehand, and all the loading done is undone after the match. Playing the same map next match? Too bad, unload it and load it again. Waste of fossil fuels powering the pointless recalculations. Save the environment Bandai. Get someone who isn't retarded to plan your game to avoid these obvious pitfalls I would expect from a highschooler's first project.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the most anomalous games I've come across. I really only played this game back on Playstation when it came out in 2018 and it was fun, but left very much to be desired. So how does it hold up today?Going over the game, there is a LOT to unlock and grind for. Multiplayer modes that incentivize constant grinding and are actually quite generous with it's ranking(essentially there is no rank lost on loss, only gain whether you win and gain less when you lose.) The rewards are great and the customization is great, and the grind to each master that gives you meaningful skills and cosmetics are much appreciated and valued. While some of the DLC abilities fall off, I think this is one of those rare instances where a good player can truly appreciate the quantity matching the quality. The game is still dominated by a solid meta and you're going to see the same stuff but there's definitely value in each DLC(for the most part.) However, it took me nearly $150 for all the content that this game can offer even with a sale. If you don't have the DLC, there's pretty much nothing to really use or gain other than the base abilities, which are strong, but clearly not as exciting or grandiose as the DLC. It's pretty disgusting that they have so much money without even tapping to this game's atrocious monetization system, which is even questionable on what it provides for this game still being supported at this rate other than the DLC. It must be good, right? Well what if I told you the monetization model quite literally has p2w weapons and ninja tools behind it that quite literally affect how some game-modes and players can fight? Defense players have access to a weapon that gives you super armor while creating an AOE around you that gives heavy knockback. You are basically screwed unless you have a specific move against it, and you only get two, and that's not even mentioning the two moves they have in tandem with the weapon. Maybe some of the p2w ninja tools could also help, and while there are ways without DLC to combat it, obviously the DLC moves are better than vanilla, as I've mentioned. Oh, and attackers have 2 versions of a p2w weapon that requires very little effort compared to some of the combos you're FORCED to learn on the other weapons otherwise you get bodied essentially. It would be nice to actually be able to gain these weapons somehow, but the shop rotates every few months or so, and the gacha mechanic is quite pathetic with it's rewards. It practically just gives you reskins and nothing meaningful, even with it's "S" tier drops, which are just the same outfit or weapons with different colors or styles. Most of the items have been in the game since vanilla, but of course, they wouldn't put the actual good stuff from previous banners as a side feature, they mostly save it for the main pulls of a banner; which ALSO only get updated every few months. Maybe you've tuned your brain out to this long explanation; but the surprising thing is that it gets even worse. The players have been so whipped by this game's horrible practices that there are content creators for the game that ENDORSE a tool that gives you all the items and moves in the game that costs $35. Just look at the player data of who you're playing with and against and most of the time you're gonna see its some dude with not even 10 hours using one of the weapons I mentioned earlier. Even the players who have been playing for awhile use it, and I've been told constantly about it's use and effect on this game's community.And now I get to the community and playerbase. I haven't interacted it with much, and for pretty good reason. It's the typical competitive toxicness of most games these days. The best "players" have giant egos and think they're good at the game, but mostly just cheat or are just...not even people? There's like no quantitative or qualitative features of the players to even critique because it just feels soulless. Proof of this is that I have added a ton of high-ranked players I fought in my matches on my grind to the highest rank(S1) you can get in the main ranked 4v4 PVP mode, and sure enough, I only got legit answers from maybe 3 of the 20 people I asked. They actually have no gamesense or knowledge about the game itself, they just push buttons with melted brains, dodge the question, don't even speak english so those guys are excused, or give some really weird cringy 2012 anime roleplaying-forum response. The last one is actually pretty entertaining to maybe get a laugh at, won't lie. Oh, and I didn't even mention the fact that there is a whole clan of people who are dedicated to use hacks and cheats against other cheaters to combat the game's lack of protection. That's a whole can of worms too.Despite all of this malarkey though, I do find the game fun. And despite what I said about the game's community, there are good people and you definitely WILL have fun with the game. I still think that with the game's flaws there's still something to gain out of playing it. But I don't recommend this game to other players at the very least. Unless you hate yourself. Then please buy this game and it's hundreds of dollars of DLC! :)

_childDocuments_.review: I grew up watching the Naruto anime and playing the Naruto games like many others my age, so when i saw this game my instinct was to dislike it. This game is so different than any other Naruto game that has been released before. I grew up playing the fast paced, 1v1 fighter games they released for each season, the type of games where you followed the storyline for a bit and then could play as your favorite ninja against your friends and I remember loving this concept and thinking it could never be improved on. A couple weeks back Shinobi Strikers was available for only $10 and while i knew I wouldn't like it I chose to buy it anyway, it was worth a shot. BOY WAS I WRONG! This game is incredible, if i felt like a ninja playing the past Naruto games these made me feel like I was a member of the hidden villages. The ability to customize your own character is so fun and I enjoy that you can create your idea of a perfect ninja the more you play the game and unlock rewards. I feel an addictive pull to play this game whenever I'm not simply because of all the new things there are to unlock and equip. VR Masters is a great concept to use as an intro for those who didn't grow up on the manga or anime and its a great way to please the long time Naruto fans with some nostalgia. I would highly recommend getting this game especially on sale. The only negative I see that many may feel is the lack of a real 'story mode' that many of us are used to is replaced with VR Masters and, while it's a cool concept, there isn't very much material to work with for very long so it ends up being really short in length. This game is sort of what you make it, you can play whatever way you want using your favorite shinobi's jutsus to win matches. It's incredibly unique and it is difficult for me to name a game similar to it, it took a great anime and turned it into an incredible stand alone, online game. DON'T MISS OUT!

_childDocuments_.review: One of my first reviews, so bear with me.This is definitely a solid game. If you're looking for a semi tactical, objective based, multiplayer game, and you happen to be a fan of the Naruto franchise this game is in your favor. It's not a straight up fighting game, so if thats what you are looking for try out the Naruto Storm series. The combos are are simple and the game relies more on positioning and timing on your jutsus. If you have a good team composition and everyone communicates you will see a lot of wins in the future. (Especially if you get a decent medic and defense style ninja on your squad). And even though the game can lack in a in depth combo system it excels in naruto immersion. It is absolute insane to traverse the walls and jump around the many open maps, while laying traps in this high action game. You really can lose yourself in being a shinobi.The game also has some single/co-op missions that aren't exactly story driven, but feel more like random tasks. You will find yourself not caring about the objective at all, but you will also completely forget about the lackluster story telling because the gameplay is just so damn fun. So the missions are not perfect, but they make up for it as a good time killer.Customization is more than decent as well. the big con is there aren't enough original designs like the Xenoverse series (which seemes to heavily inspire this game). All the customization items are just outfits and hairstyles that main characters in the series wear or have, but if you try hard enough you can still find a way to make your ninja stand out from the rest.Overall the games multiplayer is what will hold your attention the longest. The hight action and strategic gameplay will keep you engaged. And even though the mission system isn't the most interesting mode, it's still something you will see yourself playing as a time killer, or if you need to take a breather from multiplayer.game is a definite 7/10 in my book. Not perfect, but if you're a Naruto fan and enjoy multiplayer you will find a place here to spend quite a few hours.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, I'm not a Naruto fan. I liked the series when I was younger and forgot about mostly.So this game comes around it and it looks fun to do with some friends.I played Dragon Ball Xenoverse without much knowledge of the series so I thought this might be some sort of the same good stuff.Sadly this game is downright broken in its design, fails in its execution and is lackluster in content.I have a soft spot for character customization in general. I played many bad games just because It has a good creator but this is awful. - Very limited option. Most F2P mmorpg have better ones- Over 4000 Outfits Choices. About 40 to 60 outfits, all the rest is just reskins. I had duplicates in the first hour of playing.- There are passive attributes on those outfits, but only about 6 to 7 exits in total. Most aren't even useful at all.But hows the gameplay? It is even worse.You have 2 modes. Coop missions and MultiplayerCoop is one of the worse modes I have ever come across- There are ranks, from D to S. But the is no differents in content in them. S mission just hit harder- Most bosses are 3 of the tailed beasts. The others are a snake and 2 frogs. Now the problem lies it its design   All of them aren't made to fight fairly. All of them have a insta-kill laser the go's through walls and buildings.   This isn't intentional. It doesn't feel and looks right. 9 out of ten times you can't dodge it ether.- All mission your are fighting against the timer more then the enemies. Since you can   respawn infinitely, there is no reason  to play healer or tank.   Death is meaningless. This throws defensive tactics in the dumpster   right away, you don't have that time to play defensive at all.  There is even a passive clothing skill that reduces the respawn time...  This only proves my point even further. The other mode in Multiplayer which is at its best decent and at its worse ok.- But there resists the same problem the other modes has   There is no point doing it in the long run.Real rant comes hereThere is no progression. When you level up you get a lootscroll to get more useless outfits.Jutsu's are learn by your master or playing a class repeatedly.But there are barely any jutsu worth unlocking. Most do ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and have little visual impact. E.g Kirin or Kamui look lazy and loss to Pain's ultimate.And the biggest problem is their take on a class based system.Every class has their jutsu's and weapons. A healer class can't use a attacker class weapons or jutsu. Also only 2 normal jutsu and 1 ultimate jutsu are allowed. Very barebone.This is broken and destroys any creative builds instantly.The game even contardicts itself. E.g Melee fist based weapons are attacker class only, yet Sakura who is a healer use her fists. Healer can only use katana's, yet Sasuke is a ranger who uses a katana.Forcing people to play classes doesn't work when your game doesn't even follow the rule it makes. And last THERE IS NO POINT PROGRESSION THROUGH THE GAME- No progression- No creative builds possible- No story or concrete narrative- Your CaC HAS NO IMPACT ON ANYTHING. Everything is VR so nothing happens or changes the slighted.In Dragon Ball Xenoverse your CaC is a time patroller. A character that go's through time to help and save the characters and makes sure everything happens as it should. When you battle a God like Beerus, you actually fought Beerus. They even comment on that and remember you.It isn't a grand story but there is a narrative. It gives you motivation to learn and understand the game.In Naruto To Boruto you're a nobody that has never gone on a real ninja mission since you spent all your time fighting VR version of characters that are dead and/or don't remember you or give any ♥♥♥♥♥ about you. You are as much a ninja as a pilot that has 300 hour in a flight simulation and never flew a real aeroplane.There isn't a narrative. If the game doesn't care, why should I...Also Denuvo (See EULA - 24. THIRD PARTY SOFTWARE)

_childDocuments_.review: its a decent game, but not worth this price tag. buy it when its on sale and force your friends to play with you.i wouldnt reccomend making it 'your main game' due to how repetetive it is, but you can still have some casual fun with it for many hours.the game is fun. but it got its number of flaws you wouldnt expect in this price range.logging it for the first time, you make your fanfic self insert uchiha oc - please do not steal - with a tragic backstory. the tutorial is decent, basics are easy, you play some vr missions, they are charming - you think at first. they feel, well, naruto. we know those locations, music, characters. there is lots of fanservice - we are able to learn most iconic jutsus, the enviroments look great and polished. but then you do more vr missions - which you are forced to do, if you want to unlock more masters and abilities - and thats where the problems begin.even if areas are pretty, uhh, theres only 4 of them. i was not expecting the story to be main point, but i wish there was more to it than go on mission, mindlessly kill enemies, repeat. its grindy, its boring, it doesnt hold much of my attention. i really hoped pvp would be a different story. and it was different, but not enough for my liking.i am not very good at pvp games. my decisionmaking in wack, my reflexes are even worse, and lets not talk about sense of direction. but the game, after few hours of playing, was quite easy to understand. the gameplay is simple, yet engaging. the game is definition of easy to learn hard to master. and i quite enjoy it. i hate having to play 200 matches before understanding whats going on my screen, but after a few matches you will most probably get the hang of it needed for casual play. sure, sometimes you will wonder 'hello why i cant use my jutsus now?' or 'whats this and why it bursted my whole health?' but core gameplay is straight-forward even for novices in the genre like me. i reccomend watching some gameplay on youtube tho, to see how to move more optimally and learn most of jutsu.you are free to make a build to fit your playstyle and mode youre playing, even without dlcs you got your fair number of possibilities.thats the only thing keeping this game fresh. i think the most fun in this game isnt meta building and winning every game, but trying different loadouts. even if theyre wack its way more fun for me. i can only wonder how fun would it be with friend group on the voice chat, making stupidest team comps in existence.and thats what i would reccomend the game for. some casual fun with friends. youre having fun alone, sure, but i believe solo gaming isnt doing this system justice.however, the similiar problem from pve missions occur - its repetetive after a while. its not mindless enemy killing, it actually requires braincells and stratedy and teamwork, but theres only 4 maps - same as pve ones, i might add (5 with chuunin exam arena, which is just. a circle. theres also a tree or two i think) - and 4 game modes. 5 with deathmatch thing. petty number, ngl. its not as exciting as it was at first. sure, the builds make game fresh-ish, but logging into fourth base-race mode in row, well... the community is not that big, so you often run into the same people, running same builds (or just different people, with meta builds). just add new modes please.the devs seem to be focused on adding more paywall content than updating the actual game. no new modes since release? yikes. i know company has to make money, but i truly believe this hurts the game. its getting repetetive after a while, and i know i am speaking after 3 days of bingeplaying, but remember why fall guys died so quickly?theres apparently a problem with hackers, but maybe i just had some luck and never faced them. or maybe im just horrible at spotting them. devs aknowledged the problem some time ago, so it might be fixed for the most part.connection tho.... its not uncommon to be kicked like 5 times in lobby in the row. sometimes even from the match. and its not my connection, other people seem to have similiar problem.i wish the game had more going for it. its like a good beta thats not quite there yet to be a good full game. the lobby is just here to make an illusion of a community and belonging to shinobi world. i want it to be more than it is right now. i want to explore more places, even if only konoha village, make it so people can free-roam a bit and hell, even role-play with others! theres many fun emotes you can do and the lack of space (and chat) feels like they scrapped the roleplay idea halfway through developing. i think its the closest we ever got to naruto online roleplay, ever. but maybe i am the only one who thought about that. i am just mmorpg roleplay enthusiast so it bugged me. the chat is non existent. you can only send pre-made messages. if you come to this game in hope of socialising, turn back.lack of chat also makes it so noone can flame you if you screw up, so im leaving it out of pros and cons, you decide.- naruto.- pvp modes are fun.- easy to learn, hard to master- matches are found rather quickly.- u can make some fun builds, even without dlc.- u can change your builds as much as you want, even in the middle of the match- customisation of your ninja.- gameplay is mostly smooth.- its pretty, fully voice acted, the enviroments and music fit naruto theme.- cat ears.- getting randomly disconnected from lobbies and games.- overpriced imo.- little content - game modes are getting repetetive after a while.- its pay to win, balance issues.- lock on function is SO BAD................- camera does weird things sometimes. (in mouse + keyboard setup at least)- the pve story missions are grindy and boring as heck.- lootbox system. ew.- no free-roaming and things to do outside pvp and pve instances.- no report system.7/10 if you get it on discount

_childDocuments_.review: I can't tell if the mechanics of this game were meant for an online, or offline system, but either way it works terribly on both ends.I'll make this short and quick, going straight to the good and bad points of this game, or at least my experience so far.Naruto Shinobi Striker is a Multiplayer PVP based arena brawler game, with the main focus being team based combat with your favorite ninja, or custom character with your favorite jutsu. It has a variety of modes ranging from Capture the flag, team deathmatch, control the points and "Barrier battle". Basically an attack / defend system.Starting with the pros:     - Interesting visuals on effects     - Fun mechanics and modes     - Very nice lobby with all other players     - Interesting take on classes and roles     - Great animationsCons:    - Incredibly unbalanced    - Cluster♥♥♥♥ of a mess both online and offline (Cant do much without getting interrupted all the time)    - Glitch abusers and no punish system do disconnects mid game    - Lootbox system to unlock items    - Very poor visual outside of effects. Characters look made out of wood and overall ugly. (Forgivable with the good animations and such)    - A lot of down time during combat, in a fast paced game. (Stuns and stagger last way too long)    - Combos and moves feel very unrefined with how often they drop    - Camera man feels like he had too many drinks and is trying to fly a hellicopter without prior knowledge.BIG CON: - There are hackers everywhere and nothing can be done about it (efficiently) - Report system very unintuitiveOverall, the game is fun and had potential to be something better. However with how it stands, Id say its only worth buying during a big sale, as full priced, the game is absolutely not worth it. Its cool to make your own ninja and use your favorite moves, giving that power fantasy we all love. However, besides that, the game is lackluster with mediocre visuals (excluding effects) with unbalanced mechanics and a crappy system.I cant say I recommend this game, but I can at least admit it has its fun moments. _childDocuments_.review: Wanted To Write A Honest Review For Once.Lackluster Graphics and Animation:Right from the start, it's evident that Shinobi Striker lacks the visual flair that fans have come to expect. The character models are uninspired, animations are choppy.Repetitive Gameplay:The gameplay in Shinobi Striker is shockingly repetitive. While the concept of team-based ninja battles sounds exciting on paper, it quickly devolves into mindless button mashing and tedious grind-fests. The limited variety in combat moves and tactics makes battles feel monotonous, leaving players craving depth and strategy.Broken Balance:The game's balance issues are a major turn-off. Some characters and abilities are overpowered, while others are downright useless. It's frustrating to see the same overpowered abilities spammed in every match, leading to a lack of diversity and meaningful strategy. It's clear that the game's balance was not a priority during development.Lack of Content:Shinobi Striker also suffers from a lack of content. The game feels like it was rushed to market, with a limited number of maps, game modes, and customization options. After a few hours of play, you've seen all there is to see, leaving you wondering why you invested your time and money in the first place.Frequent Connection Issues:Multiplayer is a significant component of Shinobi Striker, but the experience is often marred by frustrating connection issues. Frequent disconnections, lag, and matchmaking problems plague the game, making it a headache to play with friends or against others online.In conclusion, Shinobi Striker is a prime example of a game that had potential but failed to deliver on nearly every front. It lacks the polish, depth, and respect for its source material that fans deserve. Save your money and invest it in a Naruto game that truly does justice to the beloved series. Shinobi Striker is nothing more than a missed opportunity and a disappointing addition to the Naruto gaming franchise.

_childDocuments_.review: As a long-time fan of the Naruto franchise, I had high hopes for Naruto to Boruto Shinobi Striker, but sadly, it failed to meet even my lowest expectations. Here's why:Lackluster Gameplay: The gameplay mechanics are clunky and unpolished. Movement feels awkward, and combat lacks depth, making battles feel repetitive and unsatisfying. It's as if the developers took a step back in terms of gameplay compared to previous Naruto titles.Limited Content: Despite the vast world of Naruto to draw inspiration from, Shinobi Striker feels empty and devoid of content. The number of playable characters is disappointingly low, and the game modes are uninspired and quickly become stale.Technical Issues: From matchmaking problems to frequent crashes, Shinobi Striker is plagued with technical issues that hinder the overall gaming experience. It's frustrating to invest time and effort into a match only to be abruptly kicked out due to server instability.Questionable Design Choices: The decision to focus heavily on multiplayer leaves solo players feeling neglected. The single-player experience is lackluster, with a shallow story mode that fails to capture the essence of the Naruto universe.Microtransaction Madness: Like many modern games, Shinobi Striker is riddled with microtransactions that feel predatory and exploitative. Progression is heavily tied to purchasing in-game currency, creating an unfair advantage for those willing to spend real money.Overall, Naruto to Boruto Shinobi Striker is a disappointing addition to the Naruto franchise. With its lackluster gameplay, limited content, technical issues, questionable design choices, and excessive microtransactions, it fails to capture the magic of its source material and is best avoided by fans looking for a truly immersive ninja experience.Cheaters : When you are in the lobby there are lots of beginners who get rare skins with very low skills and levels, when playing with cheaters you feel very bored because when on a mission it is so easy to be defeated by casting the ultimate many times without cool down, this is very disturbing for beginning players.Not recommended to play 2/5

One, because the difference between a premade group of players and a team of randoms is immense and you dont have a real chance of ever even killing someone. This is somewhat excuseable, it does state on the steam page that this is Coop orientented. Fine. But why in gods name are there ZERO options to form a group inside the game?You cant friend a player after a match if you played well together, you cant talk to people in the lobby, you cant invite them to a group and to nobodys surprise theres no LFG tool either. Not even after you played a VR mission together. Even after that, you have no option to communicate with that other person. For a game that is supposed to be played with other people this game has far too little options to do so. Another thing that bothers me is that you cannot report people. Ive seen more than enough people with an "interesting" username, going by that I dont assume theres any sort of moderation going on. I also assume leaving a game early goes unpunished. Make that graphics just a little bit worse and this could qualify as a mobile game.

_childDocuments_.review: Please finish Naruto & Naruto Shippuden before thinking of buying Shinobi Striker as there will be many spoilers and characters that you may have not met yet. The fighting mechanics in Shinobi Striker are really solid with satisfying combos that you can perform on others with a vast array of weapons from the Naruto-verse itself. The gamemodes are based around working as a team and having people use different classes to contribute to helping each other. There is one or two FFA gamemodes which allow you to fight in the chunin exams arena with any class that you have created and test it out which I personally really enjoy .The jutsus in Shinobi Striker are great; the animations to them are not extremely overwhelming which is good as you can still see whatever is going on around you. The attention to detail is also amazing in Shinobi Striker as you'll see throughout. I don't want to say to much as it I might include things that may be spoilers so I'll let you see for yourself.Although Shinobi Striker is a great game to purchase for Naruto fans, it does get repetitive, sure the developers are quite active adding DLC's once in a while and starting some limited time events here and there. This repetitive gameplay is especially true in the PVE "VR missions" that they have, the "VR missions" are very fun for sure but there is just so much a game like this could have come up with.What I think they could add: Clans - allowing you to choose a clan whether it's Uchiha, Uzumaki, etc and once you've selected your clan, you can only change it through spending ryo on a clan change once every month. Every week or two, there could be a "spin the wheel" type random picker which chooses which clan's week it is. This will give people of that clan additional rewards that they can earn by completing fights together and bonus XP whilst it's going on. For the people who are not part of that specific clan, they can also participate in similar gamemodes but just earn less rewards (still good rewards but just less). More maps - I feel like by adding just one or two more maps it would create a fresher feel for those who still play the game every day. They could be significant places that occurred during some of the arcs which I cannot say as it would come as a spoiler. Shinobi Striker is a great game buy it if you want, you can get it for much cheaper on websites such as fanatical, that's where I got it from as it was a great deal.

_childDocuments_.review: Worth the £10, no way at full price.It's a very barebones Zenoverse. The hub area is tiny, which is fine cause it is faster to get to places bu you can't move quickly. You can only move at one speed, no jumping, which is annoying when in the VR missions you can walk on everything.There's no story mode, I liked Zenoverse's story. This doesn't have any. And the context is terrible.The big talk of the game is the Ninja League, which they say you got to train for, you train doing VR missions. There is no missions outside VR besides the PVP. Which means your not doing anything, just VR... Your playing a Naruto cosplayer living their dream of being a ninja in VR and getting arcade tickets that look like scrolls to turn in for new cosplay toys and clothing. If it wasn't for PVP I would have no idea that your character is actually learning to be a ninja. But your definitely not being a ninja because your not doing anything for your village, just VR missions, besides spectator sport I guess in PVP.You learn ninjutsu from masters like you learnt ki techniques from masters in Zenoverse. But these are VR masters, makes sense for any dead ninjas like the hokages but not sure how much you can learn in virtual reality and just by watching your master, you haven't got the sharigan, you can't see his techniques when everyone is ninjaing around a small rock formation. In the introduction Sasuke is asked to train you and he says "why train him? if we can use the VR to give him masters from the data we gathered?"... Not word for word but it's very close... And that appears really lazy. Maybe Sasuke thought being lazy like Naruto would help him be hokage.Matchmaking, this seems to be very important for the game... it's poor. If you need to do a mission it'll be lucky if you get more than one person. I've played a few hours, only really stopped once I hit a error that closed the game. I've probably had 5 or less games with a full team. Seems to be a lot of people running around but still not really had full team. Does the same thing as Zenoverse, you can talk with predefined messages... And you can spam them, damn can you spam them. the chat box was filled with one guy's spam for people to join his team since I joined that day through to doing a mission and I think going on a different server.For a few missions running around having some fun with people, and learning moves from masters, my favourite thing to do in a collectionist kinda way. £10 is all your getting from me.Full price, £40, for this little game is ridiculous.UPDATE: Reached chonin in about 15 hours, credits rolled so this is I guess offiicial game over, the rest of the missions but two have unlocked and they are repeats of missions. I counted 30 unique missions in the game, and these are repeated with stronger enemies for the higher ranks. Which is very annoying and disappointing.

_childDocuments_.review: To be honest, I was hoping this would be more like Xenoverse, but, really, it's kind of a downgrade from it, and Xenoverse isn't even all that impressive either so yeah, this game's pretty meh. Character customization is limited, but slightly less limited than Xenoverse's, technically. Basically, you get hairstyles that are all from pre-existing characters, as well as facial features and stuff, you cannot make a unique character on this game.  Considering this game's slightly younger than Xenoverse 2, I was hoping it didn't have that god awful archaic chat system that doesn't allow you to actually chat, but nope, it does, so... yeah, that sucks if you don't have a mic and want to chat with people.Combat's pretty okay, a bit harder to manage but it's fine. However, it's much harder to manage because the cursor won't stay in the game and that can really mess you up. Story... Technically, there is no story, the story is basically just side quests that have no impact on your character other than levels and gear. It feels rather dull, to be honest. It's disappointing. Also, the DLC characters are only trainers, you can fight as them but, that's pretty much it. So just buy the ones you really want or wait until there's a sale. Which, honestly, just wait until there's a sale for this game, it's not worth the full price, if you want something better, just go for the Xenoverse series or play previous Naruto games.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, this game grows on you after awhile.At first I was iffy, with the negative reviews, the backlash towards BANDAI NAMCO for matchmaking issues, trust me it seems very fishy. Hell I even sent a refund request, only to play the game more and fall in love with it. If you're expecting loads of conent, right now its just multiplayer with the ability to do solo training missions. The concept is really good in fact, the system works well and the only stipulations in my eyes that it has is only being multiplayer. If this was somehow incorporated into a singleplayer campaign, oh my god it would be amazing and would knock these reviews out of the ballpark.This games price is too steep, at most this game should be 35$ for the content its selling, I would not believe the community who constantly write on the discussions on why BANDAI hasn't commented on something thats just happening today (as im writing this review), its not like the majority of their audience are english speaking americans and their own company is situated in Tokyo.Like ive seen with other quotes, issues do vary per person, and some people are just to idiotic to update their own reviews. So far ive gotten no lag from servers, except one time where I had a moment of rubberbanding, that was it. I don't matchmaking issues either, even whilst solo, it takes about 5 minutes (if you complain about 5 minute matchmaking wait times you're greedy) to get players and join a game, and I get excellent ping and excellent FPS.Overall, you should buy this game, the only thing lacking is content, however updates will further come as this game only released barely a month ago.

_childDocuments_.review: I have a pretty fun time playing this. It's pretty simplistic in terms of gameplay, with a strong focus on pvp with a side of pve for missions. There's a couple of different gamemodes, some kind of event always running, and a lot of customization in terms of avatar. Events are mostly the same but provide unique cosmetics, weapons, and outfits to unlock.However, most of the jutsus are locked behind DLCs -- you have to buy characters or season passes in order to unlock more jutsu and some cosmetics, though the base game does have a fair selection of characters. If you're eyeing this game but aren't sure, buy it on sale. It seems to go on sale semi-frequently, up to 80% off. Wait for a sale to buy the game or DLC, you'll really save a lot of money.Regardless, I absolutely have a blast playing this. It's super fun to play and I enjoy making builds for different gamemodes. You don't have to buy the DLC to enjoy it, although you would likely get more out of the game for doing so.

_childDocuments_.review: NARUTO TO BORUTO: SHINOBI STRIKER, developed by Soleil Ltd. and published by Bandai Namco Entertainment, is an exhilarating and action-packed multiplayer brawler that allows fans of the Naruto universe to immerse themselves in epic ninja battles. With its dynamic combat, strategic team gameplay, and faithful representation of the beloved Naruto franchise, SHINOBI STRIKER stands as a captivating title that brings the spirit of the anime to life.One of the standout features of NARUTO TO BORUTO: SHINOBI STRIKER is its fast-paced and dynamic combat system. Players can choose from a wide range of iconic Naruto characters and engage in intense 4v4 battles in various arenas. The game's fluid and acrobatic combat mechanics allow players to unleash impressive jutsu, perform high-flying maneuvers, and engage in exhilarating close-quarters combat. The combination of melee and ranged attacks, as well as the ability to seamlessly switch between vertical and horizontal gameplay, adds depth and excitement to every encounter. The combat system captures the essence of the Naruto series, delivering thrilling and cinematic battles that fans of the franchise will thoroughly enjoy.The team-based gameplay in SHINOBI STRIKER is a standout aspect of the game. Players can form teams of four and participate in objective-based game modes, such as capturing bases or securing flags. The strategic cooperation among team members is essential for victory, as each character class brings unique abilities and playstyles to the table. Communication, coordination, and mastering team synergy become key factors in achieving success. The team-based approach not only fosters a sense of camaraderie but also encourages players to experiment with different character combinations and strategies, enhancing the overall depth and replayability of the game.Visually, NARUTO TO BORUTO: SHINOBI STRIKER does justice to the vibrant and colorful world of Naruto. The cel-shaded graphics capture the distinct art style of the anime, bringing the characters and environments to life in stunning detail. The arenas are beautifully designed, faithfully recreating iconic locations from the Naruto universe, and the character models are highly detailed and instantly recognizable. The visual fidelity, combined with the flashy special effects and cinematic action, creates a visually captivating experience that immerses players in the world of Naruto.The game's faithful representation of the Naruto franchise extends beyond visuals. SHINOBI STRIKER captures the essence of the beloved characters, their unique abilities, and their distinct personalities. The voice acting, character interactions, and the inclusion of iconic jutsu all contribute to an authentic Naruto experience that fans will appreciate. The game's progression system allows players to unlock new jutsu, costumes, and cosmetic items, further immersing them in the Naruto universe and giving them a sense of progression and customization.In addition to its multiplayer modes, SHINOBI STRIKER offers a robust single-player campaign that allows players to experience a unique storyline set in the Naruto universe. This provides a well-rounded gameplay experience for those who prefer solo play or wish to delve deeper into the lore of the series.In conclusion, NARUTO TO BORUTO: SHINOBI STRIKER is an exhilarating and faithful adaptation of the beloved Naruto franchise. Its dynamic combat system, strategic team gameplay, and stunning visuals capture the essence of the anime, delivering thrilling ninja battles that fans will thoroughly enjoy. Whether you're a fan of Naruto or a lover of intense multiplayer brawlers, SHINOBI STRIKER offers an immersive and action-packed experience that will keep you engaged for hours on end. Embrace the ninja way, join the battle, and prove your skills in the captivating world of SHINOBI STRIKER.

_childDocuments_.review: To be honest, I bought this game fully expecting to refund it after an hour and a half. After seeing the gameplay footage and heavy reliance on online matchmaking I really wasn’t interested leading up to its release. Being a fan of Naruto (Storm) games, I figured I'd try it out anyway, have some fun making a character, and end up hating the game.And so it turns out, the game is… not that bad? As others have mentioned, it does feel pretty empty at the moment, with only a few things to do in the desolate plaza of a hubworld. I expect (and hope) that more content will be added in this area, as the space is needlessly large for what’s currently in place. It would be nice to have more options for offline play too, especially in the almost inevitable event that the online scene dies out. Other than that, the combat feels satisfying and the matchmaking is fast paced, making it a good pick-up-and-play team fighter. The character customization is decent too, and probably the main reason I’m deciding to keep the game and hope for more updates. If you’re a fan of Naruto and had fun with the Dragon Ball Xenoverse games, you’ll most likely enjoy Shinobi Striker. If nothing else, try out this game for the character creation and just play a few matches. Pros:[+] Fast paced, high action gameplay[+] Solid character customization with plenty of cosmetic options[+] Basically fanservice for fans of the Naruto seriesCons:[-] Fairly empty world outside of matches; not much else to do[-] Potential for matchmaking to die out after a while[-] Somewhat overpriced in its current state

_childDocuments_.review: Alright first serious review. NARUTO TO BORUTO: SHINOBI STIRKER is awesome. I picked this game up not expecting that much but after playing 3 matches I was hooked. I got 24 hours in almost 4 days and I really enjoyed the experience. May aswell get all the positives out of the way now and get into the negitives later. Positives: Character creation gives you a perfect amout of creative freedom but not to much to the point where your overwhelmed with dozens of different options for like bone structure and useless stuff like that. Afrer you create your character you can edit it at any time but things like height and body shape you will need ingame currency to change but your not stuck with anything. After buying the game you can get anything in the game without putting money into it. Perfect amount of different ways to play the game, there are 4 classes (attack, range, defence, and healing) and each of these classes as up to 13 different abilities you can mix and match which makes you feel like your not bound by the default abilities of your class like in many other games. More on the abilites (jutsus). You can combine these jutsus any way you want which feels really fun and gives you reasons to keep playing and strive for your dream ability set. The VR Master leveling system is very rewarding and fun to use. Masters are unlocked through playing other masters or taking quests from npcs around the lobby and getting all of them and all they have to offer takes a long time and keeps you wanting to play. The gameplay is a balance of simplicity and skill. Skill in this game does not revolve around aim or mastery of controls, skill in this game is experience, coordination, and game sense. Negitives: The game requires coordination and is a big part of "skill" in this game but the game makes it kind of hard for you to do this. There is no clear understandable voice chat system that you can strategize with your team with. There is also no chat box where you can type to your team or the enemy for that matter. The game servers for online play are bugged and sometimes it will take over 10 minutes to even get into a game even though the game is pretty populated. Balanced matching can also be a hassle sometimes because you could have a team with 4 level 10-30s and the enemy team could have people level 100 and above. The VR missions can be boring and repitive sometimes too easy somtimes too hard. The tutorial says the VR missions will be from the "famous battles" of past ninjas but none of the missions connect to the anime at all and let down alot of people. Yeah thats about it, alot of the issues I have can be fixed easily so I hope they will be and yeahhhhh. I would rate this game 8.5/10 (currently rating may change).

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:+This game looks absolutely gorgeous and brings the Naruto unviverse to life once more.+The character customization, while limited at first, ends up being very fun and allows for a lot of creativity!+Gameplay can be solid at many points leading to high-octane fun.Cons:-The camera is atrocious, there will be many times when you get hit (usually out of nowhere) and then be unable to actually find your enemy. The lock-on feature does very little when there are four people fighting in the same area. This doesn't even take into account how often the environment obscures your view making those blindsided shots all the more common-The matchmaking is horrendous. No joke, in almost every ranked match I played, I was up against people who already prestiged (I was only around level 20) This is just annoying, the game can be really fun, but whenever you get paired up in one of these games, you often get walloped from the start with no chance of recovery.-The mission content is lacking. If you feel like teaming up rather then going face to face, you'll find that there is a pultry amount of missions, many of which are basically copies of eachother. Conclusion: All in all, Shinobi Striker is no doubt an alright game, made better for Naruto fans who dream of living their dreams as their own personal shinobi, but it suffers from multiple issues that plague the multiplayer. Don't pass on this one just yet, but wait for either a price drop or for a patch to the camera and matchmaking issues.

_childDocuments_.review: So, here I am, giving this game a recommended rating. How did it come to this? Okay, cliche movie lines aside, I never expected I would give this game a recommended rating.Hear me out here. Is this game basically "bad Naruto fortnite"? Yes. Does it have server issues which show blatant lies in interviews (Such as no lag)? Yes. Does this game have glitches and shallow combat? Hell. Yes. And despite all of this, I'm still recommending it.Why? Well, it really comes down to what this game is trying to accomplish. Contrary to the Storm games, this isn't meant to be a competitive PvP game, it's meant to be a co-op action game. In that sense, I expect there to be lenient timings, major use of auto combos, insane combo extensions that make no sense, and other crazy unbalanced mechanics.Pros:- Movement is actually pretty decent for an action game- Character customization is serviceable for a Naruto game- When the servers work, they .- The graphics took getting used to, but they're not bad by any means. As more stuff happens on screen, it gets more stylistic.- The gameplay overall feels fluid and free-flowing- While I haven't played with random players, the co-op experience is pretty good.Neutral:- In doses the combat is fun, but it also is pretty shallow and simple- When enemies get hit, their hurtboxes just kind of disappear for a short moment. I know it's to avoid overlapping attacks, but it feels like they disappear for too long.- The audio is basically the same voice clips used in Storm.Cons:- Difficulty scaling. The game is too easy most of the time, but sometimes mid-mission they just give the AI an ability to instantly set your HP to 1. The first time this happened to me was on Sai's mission chasing Kabuto, I didn't even know what went on until I realized Kabuto cast that jutsu, and it didn't even have to hit me to activate.- When the servers don't work, they . Server Maintenance is common, and sometimes the game will randomly kick you out. I was in a Discord chat and got kicked from the server .- The game isn't optimized for different hardware configurations. I know people who physically cannot run this game on more powerful hardware than me simply because they used "the wrong GPU model".- The game is pretty inconsistent on how it wants to present itself. A small example of this is how the flavor text for the DLC purchase links aren't at all consistent with each other. A large example of this is how the DLC buttons only lead to the DLC Store Pages, even if you .

_childDocuments_.review: is a high-energy, action-packed game that brings the world of Naruto to life in a whole new way. As a fan of the anime series, I found myself quickly immersed in the game's storyline, which offers a wide array of missions and challenges that provide hours of gameplay. However, despite its many strengths, the game's repetitive nature may be a turn-off for some players.One of the best things about the game is the graphics. The visuals are striking and well-designed, with a high level of detail that brings the characters and environments to life. The sound design is also impressive, with music and sound effects that perfectly capture the intensity of the battles and action sequences.The game's combat system is also a standout feature. Players take on the role of a ninja and must master a range of moves and abilities to defeat their enemies. This requires a combination of strategy, skill, and quick reflexes, making for an engaging and challenging experience.That said, the game's repetitive gameplay can start to feel stale after a while. While there are plenty of missions to complete and challenges to overcome, the core mechanics of the game don't change much over time. This can make it difficult to stay engaged with the game for extended periods of time.Overall, I would recommend NARUTO TO BORUTO: SHINOBI STRIKER to fans of the Naruto franchise or those who enjoy fast-paced, action-packed games. While the game may not be suitable for everyone, it offers a fun and immersive experience for those who are willing to put in the time and effort to master its mechanics.
