_childDocuments_.review: Honestly terrible, I got the deluxe edition for 8 dollars and still dont want to play it. So much is different than the older games but i wont necessarily count that against them, however i do feel that the combat pacing felt worse to me. Customization options are absolute ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, you have to unlock them with almost rng scrolls and you cannot change the colors of items you get, you just have to hope they are what you want. Similar to DBZ xenoverse 2 you have to pick a master and grind to unlock jutsu for your custom character, honestly not a fan of that. Part of what makes it feel so terrible is that everything is so slow. I play all my games on ultra 144hz so I know my pc is decent at least, but the load times are slow, even if you skip dialogue there are 2-3 second pauses between quips and sometimes the characters dont stop talking. As far as multiplayer goes I was kicked out of every one of the 11 battles I tried so I assume its nonexistent. As far as combat goes, the "A" button that was either a short dash or extended "run/dash" in the previous games is instead some obnoxious double jump that accomplishes next to nothing, and if you run on walls its an absolute hindrance. x/y/b have the same functions as previous games. Blocking felt unresponsive  but i decided to chalk it up to being slow. there is a parry that i dont recall being in other games but im not sure how much use youll get out of it(i only played 1 hour). I disliked the substituion jutsu teleporting you so far away from your target, I assume you are able to change it but again you have to unlock it somewhere and it felt bad enough to make me not want to play. Ultimately I have decided to refund the 8 dollars, this is honestly a game I dont think id play for free

_childDocuments_.review: The game's graphics and optimization are great for the most part, however this game still has a lot to work on. For one the VR missions are just a cluster♥♥♥♥ of enimies that you fight on the same 4 maps over and over. The combat system in this game feels like it wasn't ment for this game mode (which it really wasn't because the dev's focus was on the pvp but it's still in the game so this has to be said). When focused on an enemy your combo is always stopped short because of another npc that attacks you from behind and my two problems with this is that there is no back hit in this game (like in xenoverse) so when you are attacking one enemy the only way you can stop attacking them is if you dash mid combo and lock on to the enemy behind you which can be very tedious. My other problem with this is that the other npcs dont attack you until you start attacking the npc you are focused on which can be very annoying. There is also no need for lower level enimies to be present during boss battles seeing as they are already a hastle to deal with on there own and they make the boss battle more frustrating especially in the case of the Deidara mission. Ultimates also seem to have no affect on giant bosses and Kurama and The Eight Tails have a glitch where there beams/beast bombs will clip through structures. Most people will just strictly play the pvp mode which is better but if you want to unlock masters to get more moves for your character you will have to play the VR missions. On the pvp side of things, this is where the game shines with it's unique style of gameplay however there are still things that could be improved on in this gamemode aswell. The camera in this game NEEDS to be fixed. I cannot stress this enough. The lock on also needs working on because on multiple occasions I find myself locking on to an enemy that is behind the enemy I'm fighting or trying to go after. There are also some glitches with the wire kunai where it will hit a wall and not pull you in. Other than that besides maybe a few balance tweaks the pvp aspect of the game is fun, if you have a team... DO NOT PLAY THIS GAME WITHOUT FRIENDS. If you solo que in this game you will not have a fun time. This game really pushes the whole team based gameplay which can be a good thing and a bad thing. Good because the game's focus isnt really about who has the most kills on your team but bad because you can't carry meaning if you play with bad team mates and you go against a team that knows what they are doing there isnt much you can do so you'll end up losing. The customization in this game aesthetic wise is good but my issue with it is that clothes have stats attached to them so if you're going for a good build on your character you can't truely look the way you want to look. The last issue I have with this game is that there is no voice chat or even text chat in this "team based" game so if you solo que you have no real way of communicating besides holding down on the d pad and using a preset call out which isn't really viable because you have to stop in place and then press the d pad. My verdict for this game is to wait for a price drop or wait till they improve and add more content to the game which will probably come in the form of paid dlc seeing as the game has a season pass.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game on sale for 13 dollars, and I have to say, it is amazing. There is a variety of different jutsu for every playstyle, and it hits hard with nostalgia, from rasengan to planetary devastations. The missions each have a rich, unique objective, and I can say the same for all the bosses too. What I find best about this game is the combat system. It is super smooth and incorporates different techniques very well into battle. Combat varies between the four different classes, and the interactions are different each time. Against a swarm of enemies(White Zetsu for example) the targeting system and your attacks transition fluidly between the different enemies, making it easier to lock on to an enemy and not jutsu the air.Each class in this game is balanced, and serves a different purpose. And by balanced, I mean insanely balanced. There is no broken op class, and most of it relies on pure skill. In a pvp situation, there will obviously be a rift in strength (Rangers at a distance can shred an attack class, however if the attack class gets close goodbye ranger), but it is overall very balanced.The sale is over and I don't suggest buying the game for full price(It simply isn't worth that much money from a gameplay aspect) but if Shinobi Striker ever goes back on sale, BUY IT. I highly recommend this, Naruto fan to Naruto fan.

This is a quest, PVP, PVE game. The game is also pay to win so if hoping for PVP games you will be outmatched if, you don't have DLC content.Recommend this game: for players that are anime fans or Naruto or Boruto fans. Gamers that love online pvp or pve games.Pros: Network is really good. Some Bandai games I have tried had little, to no PVP games. You create a character and train with VR masters (not virtual reality) for moves to custom your created character - moves list. The quests are fun and PVP has rankings plus rewards.Cons: No story. As I said Pay to Win but the game is still fun if you just do PVE quests.Explaination: You make a character at the start of the game - which can be 1 of 4 types (Attack, Ranged, Defence, Heal). In pvp you can pick characters on the anime Naruto/Boruto anime roster. As you complete quests and level up you unlock trainers - that give you more moves for your created character. Also note that in the game you don't have custom chat but use dialogue from a menu in game. 5/5 Graphics - Has an anime likeness to being in the Boruto/Naruto world.4/5 Sound - Good music and good voice over so has the Boruto/Naruto theme.5/5 Gameplay - I use a usb controller on the pc. Controls are good 1 button moves so easy to do. Of course cooldowns  of jutsu moves are in the game. I like.5/5 Difficulty - The quests for solo or  PVE are ranked so if you want to try a high difficulty you can. PVP is always challenging.2/5 Story - There really isn't any main story. The quests though have objectives and cut scenes. Rating: 84% out of 100%. Shinobi Striker as of 02 october 2021 is my favorite anime game currently for PVP. I like the game very much.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a Naruto game that has many fun elements to its combat and customization. The combat is mainly PvP focused, but there are some PvE missions that can be completed for accessory items. Customization is done in an RPG-like fashion where clothing and accessories can make your character move faster or do more damage with abilities. There are some clothing and accessories that are tied down to specific classes. These classes consist of Attack (Damage), Ranged (Damage), Defense (Tank), and Support (Hybrid, Healer).  Attack gets up close while doing a lot of damage. Ranged keeps their distance while attacking from a distance. Defense takes hits and thwarts enemies. Support hinders enemies and benefits allies. All of the classes have different types of weapons available to them. These weapons have different attack patterns for their light and heavy attacks. Attack is the only class that go into a fight without using a weapon.  Abilities are locked to each specific class. Two Jutsus/Ninjutsus, one Tool, and one Secret Technique. Ninjutsu is used to damage enemies and protect/heal allies. Tools are class specific items that can used to start combos, prevent enemy movement, or even stop a Secret Technique from activating. Secret Techniques can be game changers that each class can build upon by doing their designed role. Examples of this would be doing damage as Attacker, hitting enemies with Senbons as Ranged, reflecting attacks as Defense, and burdening enemies/providing boons to allies as Support. There are are some Secret Techniques that can be charged faster than others.  This Naruto game is online focused. The servers are maintained, at the very least, once a week. An Internet connection is needed to play. The servers tend to kick people back to the lobby. This happens when in the process of joining a match, while on the loading screen, and even while in a match. There is no matchmaking thus there will be a good chance that a group of new players will be fighting against a group of highly skilled veterans.  The combat in this game consist of Combat, Base, Flag, and Barrier. Combat has fights with a set amount of points. During Combat, if a teammate falls off the map or gets knocked out then the team loses a point. Base contains areas that can be captured and defended. Points are gained if your team has at least two bases while having three will give points faster. Flag is a mix of combat and base where if an enemy is defeated then their flag becomes easier to capture. The flag is placed on a pedestal near each teams spawn point. Four kills can make the flag easier to pick up. There is also the option of taking the flag without any points, but this will take a while to capture. Carrying the flag slows your character to a crawl. Barrier gives us a boss battle. This boss battle is done through an Attack or Defend style of gameplay. Attack must pull up pillars and then attack the boss. Defend will try to prevent the pillars from being lifted and attack the Attackers while defending their boss.  I have had fun playing Shinobi Striker. However, I can not recommend this game as of this review day. The main reason for this poor recommendation would have to be the hackers/exploiters that are currently parading the game. There are hackers that will use Secret Techniques at the start of a fight and will use them every second. Alt+F4 will be your friend if your matched up against these types of players.  Regardless of the parasites currently eating away the fun that this game is trying to provide. If your up for some Naruto based PvP with a customized character that can use your favorite Naruto character abilities then this might be the game your looking for, but I do recommend getting this game when it is on sale. Main reason I recommend getting the game this way is because of the season pass characters. They can still be played without buying them but their abilities, hair styles, clothing, weapons, titles, and lobby actions will be unavailable.  Starting out in Shinobi Striker I  recommend not doing the VR missions first. Focus on the PvP Rookie matches until account level 30. The reason for this is that the Rookie matches become unavailable after account level 30, and the VR missions give account experience thus making your time playing PvP less enjoyable.~Edit: 10/2/2021~Action is being taken to help the games overall enjoyment. They're banning hackers and the like. I have switched to Recommend due to these actions being taken.~Edit: 12/31/2021~I want to enjoy this game for what it is, but the constant hackers that pillage this game are strangely increasing after actions were taken by the company. I'm going to leave it as a down thumb. If there was a middle thumb then my review wouldn't keep getting edited. This will be my last edit though for it seems that there will be no way for this company to protect their game from these types of people. Recently learned that this game does not have dedicated servers. Meaning this game has peer-to-peer which can and will disconnect anyone that can not connect to the designated host of the match, or if the host of the match is running on poor internet connection. That does not mean that the game is unplayable with poor internet though. There are still players that are using exploits too, but they are few and far between.

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot recommend this game to Naruto fans, online fighting fans, or solo players. This game is an imbalanced struggle to enjoy and I'll go into detail as to why.I give my personal experience and thoughts on:Balancing (there is none)Gameplay (defense, movement, etc)Online componentsIf that's not something you want to read, thank you for your time and hopefully a different review can give you what you want to know!I still play for the co-op VR missons, those can actually be a lot of fun.I must say this first and foremost because  My first few experiences were grating, to put it lightly. At the time of writing this review, I was only maybe level 15, having only played offline VR missions, as they're known in the game, and thought I had a decent chance online. I first tried to enter the beginners matchmaking, but waiting for half an hour during the height of most games player count (between 4 and 6 PM) wasn't something I was willing to do so I decided on the main quick match.I was teamed up with fellow low level players and was pitted against a party of level 200s with master rankings. Needless to say we were absolutely butchered with no contest. I thought that was a one off and went back into matchmaking. Same situation, same exact players. I thought "third time's the charm" and was actually met with a fun game, but was disconnected for no definitive reason. Okay then, let's try again. Same low level team, same exact high tier party (legitimately the same exact players, too), same exact result.This game will not allow a new solo player any time to get accustomed to how it works without throwing them against literal god tier opponents who have all the DLC and strongest moves. The player base is also so low that you will frequently encounter the same exact players. First impressions matter, and this one left me in a state of confused anguish with no learning experience. It was just join a game, get wrecked, rinse and repeat. There is no way to "train to get good," there isn't even a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ training mode. The VR training is worthless, it gives you absolutely no way of experiencing the high speed bully sessions of the multiplayer. Throwing a literally freshly born baby into the depths of the ocean tied to a cinder block. Good luck. It didn't have that, "huh, maybe I can switch my strategy and try again," feel to it. It was just getting beaten to a pulp and nothing changes. Throw money at the game to get the best trainers, spam VR missions with your god squad, get the best jutsu, bully everyone in multiplayer. This is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Shinobi Strike me dead please.Amidst the chaotic agony of the sorry excuse for a PvP game, the lack of control over your own character became more obvious. Once you are juggled, you are dead. Once you are against two or (god forbid) more people, you are dead. If you are one-on-one with someone, but they have stronger moves, or a direct counter to your class, you're dead. So, essentially, especially if you're new, 90% of the time, you're dead. Team work is emphasized, but non-existant when playing solo. I repeat; The only real way to defend is to block, but a good chunk of moves are guard breakers, and the game seems proud of that. Other than that, you have the substitution jutsu. Useful, right? Well, not when it takes 20 seconds to recharge, doesn't bring you far enough away from the enemy so they can just rush you again, you can't block right after using it because you appear in the air, and oh yeah, the enemy can flat out disable it and pound on you until you throw your control/break your keyboard. There's a dash, but it's slow and goes nowhere, better off holding block until it breaks.Even moving around feels like agony. Running is super slow, dashing gets you nowhere, and your attacks often fling you in the wrong direction. Did I forget to mention there's no way to stop a combo once you've put in the inputs? Yeah, so while you're attacking nobody because they used the substitution on you, they can throw a Rasengan right into your back. It's especially frustrating since your attacks  at all once they get out of it, or in VR missions when you kill an enemy, you keep kicking the air around you rather than lock onto the next guy.Lock on, that's also horribly broken. The camera itself is a travesty, it's impossible to keep track of everything when there's so much happening on screen, let alone trying to find a person. So lock on is needed, but it doesn't stick to them as nicely as it should. Instead, it offers a side angle for a cool look that the enemy can dodge out of, set up an attack while you can't see them, and destroy you. Not locked on? Attacks fling you around, they do that for the enemy too, they'll be dashing passed you in every direction for those 5 grueling seconds until the sweet release of death.The audacity of this design choice is so astronomically awful that I can barely put it into words. Ya know that awful situation I described above of being unfairly matched? Wouldn't it be great if you could just quit and match make again while that god team is busy so you can maybe find a good game more your level? Too bad. No. Wrong. Bad thoughts there, pal, because you are stuck being bullied into the dirt with no means of escape aside from outright closing the entire game. Even worse, throw some hackers into the mix and that's a whole new kind of "I hate it here." That leads me to:There's no "recent players" either, so you can't find them post game.If the examples above weren't compelling enough, the combat itself is all about stun locks. A stun lock meaning  That is a huge chunk of this game and something mind numbing to be stuck in, especially when the substitution takes so long to charge. As a new player in PvP, you will spend far more time running, being stun locked, and dying than doing any damage yourself, let alone getting a kill or two.The game revolves around two attack types, strong and weak, as well as ninja tools and jutsu. Jutsu are there, they function well enough, but some feel obviously better than others, making DLC trainers, i.e pay to win, that much more overpowered. Ninja tools are just as bad in this game as other Naruto games, except they're on a cool down, like your jutsu, instead of some kind of limit. Doesn't make them any less worthless. Ultimates function as well, but suffer the same pay to win bias as the base jutsu. The weak and strong attacks can be fun, but they don't combo too well and can easily send you passed the enemy or into someone else's attack. Don't rely on them. Yeah, don't rely on your most basic of moves, the literal foundation of a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ game, which are supposed to be something useful.I mentioned the atrocities of the defensive systems above, but will reiterate here. The blocking is useless and easily broken, the dodge shouldn't even be there, the substitution jutsu is laughable, and there's this deflect move that doesn't work because the enemies attack registration lags, and even if you successfully deflect, they can rush right back at you again and break your guard. So, stop playing literally anything but mashing all attack buttons until you die. Because, ya know, playing a game to keep yourself alive long enough to play the objective is stupid.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't get me wrong. The game can be fun. If you enjoy constantly running into the same people who haven't stopped playing this game since its release. And I genuinely mean the same people, day in and day out. I woke up randomly one night, hopped on this game for an hour. Said nah and tried to go back to sleep. I kid you not, I got back on later in the afternoon, to still see the same few people queuing for survival matches. It's rather rare to run into more than around 20 different people queuing for survival matches and the normal matches are literally unplayable solo as it's once again, people who never stopped playing so they all are teamed up in 4 queues with real communication and know all the exploits.Which is my next talking point. The exploits. This isn't a true fighting game. Too much ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ that's abusable, horrid game balance. Absolutely awful exploits with animation canceling infinite combo type stuff. Not to mention the amount of people running cheats, be it they are blatant or just running something simple like the ability to have infinite subs or jutsus and use them sparingly to appear legit. You will see a cheater in almost every around 7-8 games or so. Sometimes more often.Once again, this game has potential to be very good, and can definitely be fun at times. It's very addictive to find combinations of clothing, jutsus and weapons that look and feel nice. But then just when you feel like you have found a cool combo and will look cool doing it, you go into a match to see someone easily gliding around the map using weird movement bugs and then just spinning with their sword infinitely with super armor constantly taking attack priority and never getting hit.Sure, you could just switch classes to try and hard counter what people are doing. But then what's the point? I want a game where it's balanced enough to use mostly what I enjoy and still be able to play against people. In this game, that mostly isn't possible. Not to mention a matchmaking system is completely absent. you will even as a bronze 1 level 1 get paired with huge prestige 15 mfs that haven't ever stopped a day in their lives.So in conclusion, I do not recommend this game to the general population. I will continue to hop on the game here and there. Considering there are rare gems where I can find lobbies where there aren't insane people who abuse everything under the sun. But in general if you are looking for a fair experience that doesn't require you to learn how to abuse random exploits and obtain carpal tunnel doing it. I'd say steer clear. Unless you do happen to have a gang of 2-3 friends willing to play with you. Then it's generally alot more fun.Also side note. They really need to rebalance survival mode. Like they need to disable some jutsus. I get the point to a supporter class is to heal. But it's more meant to be for the team as a whole. There is no team in survival, so you just have a busted class with infinite hp. As well as with all the movement exploits, an infinite number of ways to run away to heal yourself. Defense can be pretty strong as well but not nearly as bad as healer. And I won't even get started on how annoying it is that attack type can lock up your subs with heavy attacks.

_childDocuments_.review: -no story mode-awkward menus and dialogs*-re-used outdated engine**+customizable characters+co-op and PvP+okay-ish fightingBought for: 25€Playtime on time of Review: ~2 hoursThis game feels just like Dragonball Xenoverse with the sad difference that there is no story or relevance in shops.If you haven't played one of the Xenoverse games I break it a little bit down for you.In Xenoverse there was this nice little possibility of doing Side-Quests, which you select and get sent to. After completing the demanded objectives you the mission is complete and you get back to your hub with NPC's for shops or main quest.Sad thing in Naruto to Boruto: Shinobi Striker is that the whole game seems to be just a quick copy&paste cashgrab from bandai. While cutting out any sort of story mode and removing a lot of gameplay functions that worked well in Xenoverse you get a game that let's you: customize your character (optics), pick a role (melee, ranged, defense, healer), choose your jutsus (2 slots, 1 ultimate, split on the 4 roles)visit the shop npc to buy more optical improvements,grind your way through about 2-5min long sidequests to get some jutsus from your self-choosen master (grindy af)While this doesn't sound that bad I have trouble in seeing how they come up with a price higher than 20€ / 25$.I'm still remembering playing the first Ninja Storm and beeing psyched of finally having some okay Naruto game to play - sadly Naruto to Boruto: Shinobi Striker was a let down.*you have to confirm talking to npc's (useless), get locked into mission complete screen for about 15seconds after every mission, forced tutorial (don't get me wrong, I don't dislike tutorials at all, only if they rape you)**practically copy&paste of Xenoverse (no joke, same menus, fighting is same, hell even selecting abilities and whole sidequest thing)I would really love to recommend it, while 2h playtime may in many cases not be enough for me to downvote a game, this case made it clear to warn everyone who's thinking about buying it.It takes a lot before I go to such lengths, and I'm a big fan of Naruto, but I can and will not tolerate any $$$-grab games!

_childDocuments_.review: A fun and competitive team-based fighting game based in the Naruto world. There is a decent roster of characters to choose from, each with their own set of jutsus that you can integrate into your own. The combat is fast-paced and movement-oriented, but it can feel clunky at first. The learning curve is steep, but it gets really fun once you get used to it.There are 4 different game modes for multiplayer PvP, and they rotate each season on a bi-weekly basis. There is also a solo/co-op set of missions you can do if you want to get certain jutsus first before touching PvP. However, they are not as interesting as the PvP modes.Equipment matters, and the best ones are locked behind a gacha. However, you can easily farm the currency used (scrolls) by playing a lot. The game lacks polish in some areas, but overall, it's a decent Naruto game. The only downside it has no matchmaking so prepare to fight against group of sweaty players and it crashes a lot. A LOT. If you are a fan of the franchise, I would recommend getting it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Before we start, do note this is a online multiplayer focused game before you buy it. If you're wanting a campaign or anything like that, this is not the game for you. Though there are "missions" you can play alone with bots if not with other players, you do have to be connected to the servers to play this game overall.It's a new experience for Naruto. It's not Ultimate Ninja storm, it's obviously not the classic 2D fighter. It's an semi-open world 4v4 PVP (or PVE for co-op missions) fighter. You have the ability to jump very high with distance, run across walls, ect. The fighting mechanics is like a classic fighting-adventure style game, mixed with MMO elements. You have your light/heavy attacks, two jutsu for abilities, ninja tools to help you and or your team survive, you can kinda make builds so-to-speak, and so on. It's basically something like Paladins or Overwatch, but it's a fighting game.The gameplay is fast and very fluid. Overall combat and stringing combos feels nice, movement across obstacles is nice... How the game feels when fighting and doing other certain things; everything feels pretty good and to me, it drives me to keep playing. The controls in my personal experience took me a bit to get used to, but they're not bad at all. The one complaint I do have is the blocking/dashing mechanic. If you want to block, you have to make sure you are standing still, not moving your character at all. Pressing the block button while moving will execute a dash. In general games, when moving, pressing the block button will make your character block right on the dime, while dashing is executed by pressing block twice whilst moving your thumbstick to your desired location, or maybe tapping the thumbstick whilst blocking. How blocking/dashing in this game works is unnecessarily difficult. Not to mention I feel like dashing doesn't have enough invisibility frames and it doesn't travel far enough. Also on that note, the lock-on system. Again, comparing to other games, when facing an enemy which your camera is focused on, you should automatically lock onto the next enemy after defeating that one. After you defeat one in this game, you'd have to turn your camera and spot the enemy who is still within your range and possibly is going to get the first hits in on you since you'd have to re-lock to that enemy. Despite these two annoying problems however, it's still fun.Customization...You create your avatar from the start, completing missions/multiplayer battles and training with "Masters" will earn you more cosmetics, weapons, jutsus, and so on. Cosmetics is not just for show though. This is one part where making your "build" comes in. Each cosmetic item has up one or two bonus effects such as boosting your maximum HP, break opponents shields easier, more damage, and so on.Multiplayer? Considering this is a multiplayer focused game, it's seemingly a bit unoptimized. Matchmaking in my experience takes a very long time to find players. Though it's clearly showing many people are online, I have to wait over 5 minutes to find a match sometimes...and sometimes it's instant. My experience in-game isn't very good either. Opponents hit me before they are actually close to me, and delayed inputs sometimes happen. These in-game problems aren't too bad, as they only occasionally happen, it's still playable. But they are flaws nevertheless and need to be fixed, especially the entire matchmaking.This game looks really great, graphically. The art style is the same as the UNS series, but with some additional textures, shadows, special effects and whatnot, everything looks so much better than UNS imo, and it's beautiful. I am running this game with a GTX 1060 3G, i7-8700, and 16 GB of ram. It's running at a stable 60 most of the time...most. Frames will drop when I run on walls for some reason. Not all the time though, just sometimes...it's random. It could just be my pc, but it is strange...Sure, this isn't UNS and it doesn't have a campaign. But if you are into multiplayer MMOs, like modes such as deathmatch, capture the flag, king of the hill, ect, and would like to create your own Deviantart Naruto OC? Give it a try. It's really fun. But again, matchmaking has issues. So be prepared to wait some minuted before finding a match. However, once you do, you'll typically stay with those players the next match or can easily find another. Not all the time, but it's something.

_childDocuments_.review: Naruto: Xenoverse, this is not.For what it's worth: What IS there is quite solid and could form the foundation of a genuinely good game. The problem is - there's very little there.First off, the single-player experience is unfun at *best*. It consists of the same 5 or 6 missions repeated at higher and higher difficulties until finally the credits roll, and there's nothing to them. Just spam buttons until the mission is over, and don't worry about dying because your only "lives" are the time limit, which you have plenty of time in every mission to finish.But of course, the main draw of this game is the multiplayer, so it doesn't lose that much for the single player. However, the player vs CPU just consists of more of the same missions over and over, just with 3 other human players with you. And what's worse is, as much of an afterthought these PvE missions are, you're REQUIRED to do them to actually unlock all the trainers that you have to go through to unlock more skills.As for the PvP...it exists. A grand total of 5 maps, with 4 gamemodes, 2 of which are locked in quick play and *3* are locked in ranked. The skills are all basically the same exact thing from a small selection of skill types, there's no matchmaking whatsoever, some skills are downright broken...again, the poor single player is excuseable because that's not the main draw of this game, but to compensate the multiplayer needs to *actually be good itself*, and it's not.Even character creation just amounts to "how tall do you want to be?" and "pick from a selection of very slightly different faces". There's no interesting outfits, nothing new to the game itself, every outfit is just the clothes from a canon character, and even that selection is relatively smallAgain, what is there is good - mechanically things are smooth, for the most part. Traversing maps with wall running and super jumping is easy and enjoyable, but you can't have a good game with just the foundation. I've seen game betas with more, and more varied, content than this

_childDocuments_.review: Heres the thing. Don't come into this game expecting it to be like storm. Storms a great game, and comparing it to any new naruto game will just make the new experience seem like a$$. As for the game itself, there are some very cool things and some disappointing things. It being a create your own character type rpg game where you can grind your ass off. Pulling off a good combo also feels great. The co op can get repetitive but its fun with friends. Another disappointment is that the customization is fairly limited. With a game like this, youd think that you can make your character look exactly like you always imagined. Thats not really true. Most of the customization is taking different tops/bottoms from existing characters and mixing them around. You can get different color variants, some having really cool designs, but its not how youd imagine a "Custom avatar" kind of game. This games combat, movement system, ability use is pretty unique. It has storm visuals, with its own twist on fighting classes. The PVP is a team game more than anything else, but it influences alot of play making. Winning when your down feels great. although, loosing feels pretty bad. Some moves are also only attainable through DLC so there is a "pay to win" aspect. But its not so huge that you need it. If you get good enough, it doesnt really matter what jutsu's the enemies are using. Theres a pretty nice learning curve when playing and when you get good enough, just winning duels feels amazing. Outwitting your opponent and destroying them with mechanics is a great feeling. At the end of the day, if you want to play the naruto version of xenoverse, with a bunch of its own twists, buy it. Highly recommend getting it while its discounted, the game simply isnt worth at full price with all of the DLC.

_childDocuments_.review: It is time for me to rate this game with all its aspects.After 50 hours of playtime, I have gotten to level 1 prestige 2 without any extreme amount of grind, although you will get free jutsus, secret techniques etc. it is most likely that you will have to spend money on about 3-5 DLCs one being of course Madara (majestic go brr). To get your first jutsus you just have to finish the “storyline“ aka. talking to NPCs, they give you a VR mission and you do it. Congrats you got a VR master, thats where more grind comes in. To actually get all their jutsus, you have to level the VR master to 10 stars, which alone takes about 5 games of multiplayer (from my experience). Now that you have done the storyline, you own the majority of free VR masters. After that all you mostly do is collect cosmetics and weapons and play multiplayer (with bad matchmaking) and play more VR missions. Once you play multiplayer you see people clapping you with jutsus you havent EVER seen in the game, and then comes the final act. The DLCs. Although, when on sales, the DLCs are very affordable, you wont be finished with just one of them. So lets say you buy a few DLC character, then you go to your mailbox and claim them, well guess what you still have to grind the VR masters to level 10. It isnt that hard, and usually, if you have a good build, you are having a tad bit of fun grinding multiplayer, but for some people it can be annoying.Ok, now enough of the stuff about grinding, heres some aspects that I think are excellent about the game:4 Classes with different playstyles.Satisfying movement system.Epic and very iconic ninja customization, with voicelines.TONS of jutsus and combinations with awesome VFX.Very nice combat system (except for fighter, just LMB)More than just one battle mode (wow, filler)Ranked system, that is pretty fun tbh.And the excitement of when you get a good S/SS from a scroll is just heavenly.And finally, the atmosphere in the lobby is very very nice.So a summary if you should buy this is:Yes - If you can withstand grindNo - If you cant buy DLCs and cant grind all the time :)

_childDocuments_.review: Normally don't bother writing reviews but here goes;I personally LOVE this game.  I feel it has a lot to offer as far as team comp and the combat is fun as hell.  I'll address the complaints for anybody on the fence.**Camera and Targeting**People complain about the targeting system and say its the worst in they have ever used.  I say, they have no idea how it works.  When somebody uses a substitution or escape jutsu, they become unlocked.  This is done on purpose.  Otherwise, why would it even be in the game?  It's a jutsu thats SOLE PURPOSE is to confuse and allow you to get the jump on your opponent.  HOWEVER you do have time to react to it if you are good enough.  The way they time the animations in this game, you will know you have been juked before you get countered.  As soon as I see the puff of smoke or the wood start to form on somebodies body, I just dodge blindly.  Sometimes I nail it, sometimes I dodge right at them.  What I will say is, if I use my camera correctly and look around to see them, I usually escape.  It's not easy BUT THATS THE POINT.  ALSO, PRO TIP: Put the camera on 10.  Its the best sensitivity for the frantic play style.  When you lock on somone you dont even need to use it and its best for situations i just explained cause you can sweep and snipe lock on in a fraction of a second to succeed in avoiding getting ambushed.**Combat And Combos**Another area where people are talking nothing but garbage.  I say, Get Gud Nerd!I play defensive style and I can formulate a TOD (Touch Of Death) combo if I can corner one or two people.  Yes its situational, but so are most TOD's.  If you can bait the sub jutsu, you can then try for huge damage.  That's most of the game.  Spacing, neutral, and trying to get people to mess up so you can punish.  Sounds a lot like a fighter.  When you add the smite style jutsu tug of war in the beginning, it makes for a solid 5 minutes of frantic fighting.**Content**Right now, it does seems a little lacking in content BUT, that's opinion based and honestly is really about whos looking at it.  For me, there is more than enough when I figure in the amount of masters and how much I would have to play to unlock everything to really start formulating serious builds.  I like multiplayer and picked this up with a MOBA mentality of "there is probably no story".  Those looking for traditional Naruto games, keep looking.  IMO, this was the way to go.  The original story has been done to death and trying to create something from scratch leaves us with DB Xenoverse, which I believe is an utter mockery of the series.**Improvements**The one and only thing I would improve on is the ability to form groups to play with and maybe an in-game friends system for guilds or the like.  It's possible that I just don't know how to do it but, from what I can see, it doesn't look "friends" friendly.  I am actually going to go open a discussion about that right now.  Even if it is just incorporated into steam.  Thats fine too.  With discord being the golden standard I'm actually okay without having a voice chat.TL;DRThis title is a solid 8.5/10. _childDocuments_.review: I don't know why, but this game scratched my splatoon itch. Does it involve inking the ground? Absolutely not. Instead it has a customizable ninja with insane movement options, 2 ninjutsu and 1 ultimate ninjutsu that you can customize, and a 4 v 4 format that works surprisingly well with the 4 "classes" in the game: Attack, ranged, tank, and healer. I've put in almost 20 hours into this game and I can say for certain that if you want to get good at this game you should at least get a basic understanding of each and be able to switch if your team needs it.Let's start with the attackers. Quite simply they hit hard but are thin as paper. At most this class is going to be in the face of the opponents spamming attacks and the usual kunai. It has a mixture of semi ranged ninjutsu that can counter, stun, or take a massive chunk of health from the opponent. Next is the ranger. It's kinda like attacker, but as the name implies deals with range. Their attacks and tools are mostly centered around range, but I've found that the rangers kunai does more than the attackers and can sometimes juggle enemies to death. As for ninjutsu goes, rangers do get some close range options, however most of there ranged attacks take a while to activate, so I wouldn't recommend pairing them. Next is the tank. They are built different and will eat most attacks coming their way. With the most defense and the lowest speed, they fit their role perfectly as they swing a massive great sword that plows through waves of enemies. As for ninjutsu, they specialize in making walls and making AOEs. Surprisingly, they also have a few ninjutsu that heal them, making their survivability almost as good as the healers. And speaking of which, healers. The game says that healers aren't suited for combat, but how boy are they suited for combat. With the fastest attacking weapon and their kunai replaced with a portable health potion, with the right ninjutsu you become nigh immortal. Yes, they have ninjutsu that can heal nearby allies and themselves, but they also have abilities that seal the enemies ninjutsu.Now, wants the best class? I don't know. With the amount of customization (I'll be it, most are locked behind a paywall, but I think they're worth it) your allowed to mix and match with, you could find something you like about all the classes and end up switching them in the middle of a match.Try it out for yourself. If you don't like it, refund it.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a long-time Naruto fan, and when I heard rumblings of this game back when, I was slightly excited, to have the opportunity to create my own ninja, and share a world with my favorite characters, doing missions with my friends and things of the sort. After I've learned what the game was and what it included, my excitement waned until it vanished completely. So after waiting for this game to go on sale and playing through most of what the game has to offer, these are my thoughts.If you're hoping for an epic Naruto story that revolves around your development as a ninja, don't. This game has no real coherent story, as you're introduced into the game and made your character, you'll be greeted with a boring dialogue that introduces you to the world and it's facilities where you'll do your missions, PVE, PVP, customization and all that. After that small introduction you're on your own. While the gameplay itself is fun, the missions are repetitive and get boring eventually, being redeemed only when you do them with friends. The missions offer no real story and just serve as a platform for you to level up, get scrolls (that net you customization items, like loot crates), and advance your master level which gives you all sorts of rewards.Now, in the customization part, I was very disappointed, with the lack of optional clothes and original content, what's the point of making my own ninja if 85% of the customization items are based on the original characters, like don't get me wrong, it's cool to look like them, I just wish there were more options for individuality, and this goes for hair-types, Jutsus (which is alright, I guess) and "make-up". In addition, something that really annoyed me is the recoloring of outfits, and by recoloring I don't mean you get to pick from a palette of colors or a slide system, oh no, they have made original palettes with color combinations that they chose, and let me tell you, I'm not exaggerating when I'm saying that the choices they give are some of the worst color combination I have ever seen, ugly can't even begin to describe them, so most of the time, you'll find yourself sticking to the original palettes as they look the best. Not only that, they added *some* differentiation to the costumes, adding ugly-ass patterns to already existing outfits, there's really nothing to look for when obtaining these items from scrolls and you're better off just earning cash to buy what you want straight up from the store.Now I know, there's season two yet to come, but I don't really see them adding anything original apart from more "masters" and a couple of missions, another lazy thing is, at first I had the idea that you would've picked your village at the beginning of the game and start there as you go through the villages for different missions. Nope, you get one boring and small map of Konoha, I can't even call it a map, it's pretty much a tiny lobby, where you can't jump on top of buildings, can't interact with almost anything, it's just bland and boring. The animations for walking around in the lobby are horrible, like the adventure mode in Bandai's Naruto games, and I guess it shouldn't surprise me that they've essentially ripped them from the games, while the game itself is graphically inferior to those games in every aspect.Overall, this game is disappointing, and as someone who hates live-service games, I guess I should've known, but my love for Naruto got the better of me this time, with the anime and manga ending, and Boruto being sub-par, who knows when and if we'll get decent games in the future.-sigh- 4/10 because you CAN find a cool look (it's hard), and there's a lot of Jutsus to choose from, and the game-play itself isn't that bad.

However i dont think it would hurt to add more supers and ultimates that aren't from the show but our unique (similar to how not all supers and ultimate's from dbx2 are taken from dbz but just follow the fundamentals of how attacks in that universe work).Gameplay in itself can be a bit rough at times and needs be refined a bit more but overall its alright and doesn't effect the gameplay experience too much.Now this is where things being to fall of, in terms of content this game is VERY limited. To begin with there need to be some offline content and we need more story based content (those mission just aren't it), so there should be an offline story mode wich is a unique story to your character (it should work like the Dbx2 story mode or the halo reach campaign, or even halo 4 spartan ops), for this just make up a villain and story, maybe add some cutcenes with our characters in and give it the option to be co-op. Also some 'what if' missions like what if madara won would be sick as well (we've seen time travel in the boruto movie so just do what xenoverse does and a game mechanic) the onlines alright but i feel as tho there needs to be a matchmaking lobby before the match so you know who your playing with. Also needs more online game modes, as whilst what weve gotten is alright it gets boring quick.The home lobby is too small, it needs to be bigger and mssions + mentors should be scattered around it like in xenoverse 2 as whats currently there is just borning and lazy, shops should be something you go find, imaging as your ninja traveling round a composite leaf village jumping from houses to go meet up with your mentor, it would be sick and would add SO much more to do and have fun with rather than just standing there running in circles. also there should then be an online and offline lobby.the amount of stuff the game wants you to buy is frankly ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, why do i have to buy so many characters. like they dont even try and hide how much they want to drain your pockets, like DLC like in xenoverse is fine as it adds enough content to be worth the buy but doesnt spoil anything if you dont want to buy it. but you lose out on so much of you dont drain your pockets in this game.In summary, the games is good if you are a naruto fan and want to make your own character in that universe however it feels so bare bone, like the game is just the minimum they needed in order to give it the go ahead and lacks any additions or world building to the game that makes it feel alive and like a world (something xenoverse does well). honestly the game constantly feels like its in its beta or alpha stage wich is frustrating as all it need is a sequel or major update that gives the game some love, development, time and a bit of money and it could be SO much better but maybe a sequal will come as the game has done really well and made them money for a game that feels like its had minimal effort put into it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game saved my life.I am 25.My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and adopted our son together. They are now both 4 years old.When we were going through our separation, I found myself lost and miserable. I was self destructive. I got so mad one day from everything spiraling out of my control that I punched some concrete in a moment of overwhelming emotion. That caused me to break my 5th metacarpal in my right hand... my working hand... my games hand.. the hand that I held and carried my children to bed with.. The hand I desperately needed to make sure I could continue to provide.After learning of the severity of my self-inflicted damage, I was borderline broken. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man with no history of depression or anxiety. I have never had fits of rage, or been one to break down and cry, but I was in a low spot that just really buried me from being able to see the light on the other side.Having nothing better to do, I searched for a game I could play, ONE HANDED while I recovered. I somehow stumbled upon this game and read some of the reviews. I decided that it had to be worth a shot... I must admit, I didn't beat the game, or play nearly as long as some of you. In fact, I may have only played this game a day or two.. With that being said, after doing so, I had a new found joy and hope for life. I was able to put behind me the pain and suffering that had been cast over me. I was able to experience other peoples joy and happiness. I was able to see the fruits of my "labor". I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥ing minutes to this music long enough to realize that I was going to be okay.After coming to that realization, I turned the game off, and I went back to work. It hurt my hand like hell but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so damn sorry for myself, and I became the father I needed to be in that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving as.Today, I am close friend with my kids mother. We don't fight, or argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents, and friends.I now have 3 kids. My third child is, wait for it, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my own separation, and we just stumbled in to each others life unexpectedly. We have been in a relationship for a year now, and are very happy together.Moral of the story, you never know what life holds in store for you, and if I would have given up when all the odds were stacked against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.Thank you

_childDocuments_.review: It's disappointing because there really is so much potential.  The combat and character customization are a lot of fun but, beyond the beginning missions (D & C tier), most remaining non-PvP content involve never-ending mobs that easily stun-lock solo players. It seems there was little effort made to effectively balance the game, because a lot of content is near impossible alone, which is a shame, because a few tweaks would make a big difference. When the odds aren't stacked against you, the combat can be a blast and involves a lot of spectacle.  I can't not enjoy jumping off a wall I was running on, and shooting a fireball on opponents below. There are just so many collective annoyances though that have been voiced since launch, years ago, that you can assume they will never be addressed at this point.  Some issues are rather deliberate. Character customization, for example, is tied to loot boxes called Scrolls, and while many are supplied, more so in the game's beginning, you'll commonly get repeat items or appearance options tied to the character gender you didn't choose.  If you do get a piece you like, it may not have a skill you want for your character build, so you have to spend in-game currency that takes several hours to gain if you wish to change it.  Point being, if you want to pursue that fashion game as a Naruto fan, there's no clear track.  It's random chance or throwing open the wallet. Player versus player, which is the game's biggest focus by design, is dominated by broken abilities tied to a paywall. There's still a online community playing, that's quite alive, but matchmaking does not balance veterans with new players in a way that anyone's ever seemed happy about. Being competitive in PvP requires spending some money for the overpowered abilities, and requires researching what DLC characters have said abilities to limit spending. While the community is alive for match-making, there's no auto-queue after finishing a match, it's back to standing next to the NPC who can take you to the match-making menu.  There are other issues as well that add up. These are hoops to jump through that you just wouldn't expect when you want to enjoy a Naruto fighting game.  But maybe some of these issues won't be as critical to you, just be sure to wait for one of the many sales this game has.  Often the base game is less than $10, while the season passes (additional characters and their more powerful abilities) are typically $15-20 even during sales.

_childDocuments_.review: I really feel like i should give this game a review, because many people are talking nonsense about it.So, Naruto to Boruto: Shinobi Strike. Or, if you'd prefer, the Naruto Xenoverse game.It's the first multiplayer Naruto game, or even the first Naruto game ever, to let you create your own ninja, and that alone is really awesome, and something i was really looking forward as both a gamer and a long time Naruto fan. The customization of the game is really good, many people will say it's not, but you'll see the same people making cosplay characters of Naruto or Sasuke, or terrible mashups like Madara + Kakashi, and not really putting some thought into their OC.But the aspect of character creation goes much beyond cosmetics. You are able to freely combine jutsus, or at least your class's jutsus, and make creative and fun combinations. And, again, most people will just use the skills that everyone thinks are OP, and the same people will, again, complain about the customization.The graphics are ok, but what really catches me is the movement. The movement is so fun and fluid, it makes the game really fast paced, and you WILL FEEL LIKE A NINJA.But nothing is perfect, and this game is no exception. It lacks a custom match lobby, a story mode, the aim lock system is pretty bad, PVE really sucks, and the hub world is kindda small. Yet, keep in mind that this game was released not even a month ago, so i'm sure we can expect both fixes and content updates.All in all, i've played about 15 hours so far, and i'm far from getting bored.It's really fun to learn all the jutsus and try different combinations against different opponents, and i'm looking forward for what the devs are planning on the updates, especially when it comes to new weapons.Is the game worth it? YESIt's a really fun game, it still feels like a beta, but so what?People give up on great games too early, and that's why good games die.Don't let this game die.

If you want to spend crazy money buying every single dlc pack, you will get the experience that you wanted from this game, minus the fact that if you dont count repeating missions, there are genuinely only about 15 missions in the entire game, even if youre max level. Also only a few multiplayer pvp gamemodes. Thats it. They added a ton of pay to obtain characters, jutsus, and cosmetics, then put almost NO content both single and multiplayer into the game. Servers are also extremely laggy if youre in the U.S. Dang, this game really couldve been great, they had everything they needed but they made the worst decision any devs could make by getting insanely greedy and demanding lots of money for very basic elements of the game. _childDocuments_.review: To be fair, this game honestly has one of the best combat mechanics in any game I've ever played thus far, and I'd wanna see more games with similar mechanics to it. The game also features some neat character customization and give some cool rewards for events which are completely achievable for anyone. So with those said, the problems lie elsewhere.1. There is a jarring amount of bugs - although you cannot expect a game to be completely bug-free, this game has jarring amount of it. Examples include but are not limited to a) Screen dimming after a cut scene b) Ability indicators would display cooldown when inflicted by certain skills despite being entirely unaffected and c) Severe latency issues with the host.2. There is a severe lack of PvE contents -  PvE contents are only significant in early game, for unlocking some of the more generic gears and for accomplishing some weekly objectives. Otherwise there would be no reason for putting too much effort on doing PvE unless you don't mind doing extremely repetitive stuff.3. The game is pay-to-win - you can purchase the base game at up to 90% sale but you also need to buy enough DLCs to at least be competitive enough not to burden your team. While the game allows you to customize your costume to a wide extent, the best gears can only be obtained through gacha mechanics and would force your character's appearance to look more from a Wuxia or Scifi game than a Naruto character instead.4. The connectivity is terrible - the matches employ peer-to-peer connection and can be horribly laggy and can be very prone to disconnections depending on how bad your connection with the host is. You would expect an esteemed publisher to provide a good server for their matches than to trust their players to have good hosting capabilities. The game cannot and should not even afford to punish players for disconnection due to how bad their match connectivity is.5. The matchmaking is imbalanced - The solo matchmaking is horrible as it is- putting players with high deviation of experience and performance in the same team just to balance it out with the opponents (if the game even actually try to balance out solo matches), then pre-made teams breaks all the balance. A full stack of elite players will often be matched with a random group of players that just happened to queue at the same time with them. This game basically heavily encourages you to play with a pre-made team and will punish you for trying to queue solo.6. The recap screen is very unhelpful -  What's up with the 15 second match recap? The game should let the players scrutinize the match stats so they can contemplate on player performance, including finding suspicious activities. If the game thinks that allowing the team leader to queue quickly outweighs the importance of a good recap, then they have their priorities wrong.7. An abundant population of cheaters and hackers - while it is not the game's fault that hackers exist, the game features give hackers some good level of opportunity. The game doesn't even have an in-game report function for suspicious and disruptive activities, and the game does not check for suspicious codes upon boot up (but will continuously bother you about the anti-cheat failing to properly load itself). The reporting system would give you much more of a hassle than just swallowing the bitter pill that hackers have an unfair advantage.So to recap, the publisher and devs should:1. Fix annoying bugs.2. Give more incentives for playing PvE or playing solo in general3. I think pay-to-win is tolerable for a premium game, just maybe lower the skill floor, give more f2p options, and/or give some premium-level incentives that doesn't include gacha mechanics.4. Stop being so stingy and give players some proper match servers.5. Balance the matchmaking process. Make it less traumatizing for new and/or solo players.6. If the game cannot provide a more meaningful game recap, at least remove the ridiculous recap timer.7. Developing a PvP intensive game should come hand-in-hand with a good and accessible reporting system, otherwise the game would be a good breeding ground for abusers and pave way to a more toxic community.Personally I'd want the devs to be more "in-touch" with the game and experience it a bit more, but maybe that's asking for too much.

_childDocuments_.review: - Great concept, poor execution. Unpolished.- Pay to win (lootboxes and pay to unlock best abilities)- Lobby is terrible. It is small, completely void of purpose (all the things you do on the lobby, on a any other game, would be in a simple menu for quick access. Lobby is there to give an illusion of an open world and to make players waste time traveling just to change one combat ability)- Chatting with other players is impossible, besides a few non-customizable pre-defined sentences- Combat is fun, but the camera is really clunky.- Impossible do fight a 1 on 1 match- I know the game is destined for multi-player, nevertheless the lack of single player content is just sad. The bare minimum would be to be able to play in normal matches (ie. CTF, combat, etc) with bots if you want to, but this is not an option. All the single player content comes down to a few boring and repetitive missions. The argument that this is a MP game and doesn't need any SP features really seems dumb to me. Many MP exclusive games give you the ability to play alone with bots if you want to (Counter Strike, League of Legends, etc). This does not hinder MP gameplay whatsoever and more features in a game is always good IMO. - The game looks like a poor man's Xenoverse and it would be that much better if it had drawn more inspiration from it. It has many of the same concepts, except poorly implemented and a lot less content- This is the only Naruto game with a decent CAC system, and the devs know it and take advantage of it by selling a game for 50€ with a handful of characters and making you pay 4€ for each extra character (which unlocks not only abilities, but customization options). The main problem with this game is that there is no competition for it and that's the only reason why people play it, not because the devs did a good job in creating a game for the fans.- In summary the game really feels like an early access game, but at full price and with microtransactions (then again, this seems to be the norm nowadays). Another game with huge potential that was screwed by greedy devs/publishers.

_childDocuments_.review: This is, without exception, one of the most pretentious games I have ever played, to the point where I thought Kojima was involved in some way, but there is actual "gameplay," so that rules him out. And you know what? I hesitate to call it "gameplay" because it isn't anything special; it is a very boring walking simulator. Truly one of the worst genres in all of gaming. Sure, the graphics are pretty, but when that's all there is, then it's not really worth it, is it? The game also fails to leave an impression in any meaningful way; there's no gameplay segment that I can point to and say, "That was cool." The levels are bland and forgettable on account of their little to no interactivity; isn't that the whole reason why we play games? People say the soundtrack is good, but nothing really sticks in the mind. The "story" is so lame and appeals to the lowest common denominator because "iT'S A MetAPhoR FoR LifE HuRR dUrr."  You gotta love how pompous and condescending some of the reviews of this game are, calling it "aN exPeRIeNCe" rather than a game. I hope I never get to that point where I think my farts smell good. Another thing I found funny is that there is an achievement for not playing the game for a week. Yeah! They literally reward you for not playing the game, as if I needed a reason not to play this game. Also, the complete game time comes right up to 2 hours, so I can't get a refund.

_childDocuments_.review: As an avid, long time enjoyer of Sky: CotL, I was ecstatic when its predecessor went on sale last year for Black Friday. Mind you, I had just set up a PC for the first time, and was completely unfamiliar with any PC games than HER interactive’s Nancy Drew mysteries from the early 2000’s, and a childhood spent playing Animal Jam on my parent’s ancient dell laptop- most of my gaming experience had been acquired from the comfort of my iPhone’s App Store- and to be honest, I really do think that Sky is quite an improvement on this game.  Don’t get me wrong, I loved Journey. The character designs, the scenery- and nothing gets me better than a sand sliding mechanic. However, it lacks the sense of joy and freedom that Sky has. Journey has an altogether more melancholy feel, a very lonely and lost vibe that made me very emotional toward the end- which is certainly not a bad thing, especially if that’s your cup of tea- but there is something so tragic about the loneliness of never being able to find a traveller you spent time with in game after having gotten used to the ability to add friends and communicate through emotes in its more recent counterpart.  Aside from these very obvious personal preferences, I also found that the ending left me with a distinct sense of “that’s it?” I was able to complete the game in less than a day, and was surprised that it wasn’t longer. I likely won’t replay it soon, as I wouldn’t want it to get old too quickly- but I’ll certainly pull it out again someday if I feel the need to kick back and play something atmospheric and calming.  To put it simply, this game is comfort food, but don’t expect it to keep you occupied as an open world forever. There are definitely defined levels in this game. I would, however, recommend playing this, and then downloading Sky on your phone (It’s free!), especially if you are looking for something with a more open world that constantly changes and updates seasons and cosmetics. I love both, but I think playing Sky first spoiled me.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't even begin to describe the magic of this game. You never know who your companion is - only their symbol. You form attachments to these players without even knowing who they are, and I just find that amazing. The story, the co-op and the little teaching moments between you and your companion just add to the joy of playing through this Journey. It brought me to tears when I first played, and coming back after a year just deepened my love for this game.

_childDocuments_.review: This review might contain what some may consider spoilers. It's hard to truly spoil a game like this but consider playing the game blind.Journey is a one of a kind game.The first maybe half hour I was wowed by the visuals, and meeting others along the way was very cool, but a small corner of my mind was thinking about if this was all it was blown up to be.Then, I got to the surfing sequence and decided that yes, this game ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ rules. It was a joy and awe that's extremely rare to find, I was smiling like an idiot the whole time. This and the viscerally terrifying section right after that would alone be enough for me to recommend this game to anyone with no notes.I got to the final mountain not long after. It was past midnight, and I considered leaving it for the night to finish tomorrow, but I'm so glad I didn't. I decided to finish it in one sitting since this is a short game and I thought the end wouldn't be too far.Eventually I reached a windy area where someone else was trying to push through. I slowly but surely caught up to them and from that moment, for about half an hour, we stuck together to the very end. They almost got killed at one point, and I was so worried when the wind pushed them off a ledge before I saw the other ledge underneath. The relief I felt for meeting back up with a bunch of polygons controlled by a stranger in the safety of their own home was incredible.I don't know who this stranger was. I don't know if the list of companions met at the end is in any particular order, and either way both the first and last names were series of random numbers, but I know I'll never forget them. I've played plenty of co-op and multiplayer games but none have made me so attached to a complete stranger before, and I don't think this is something you can get in any other game.Thank you, friend. I hope we meet again.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is quite short. Finish it in just over an hour. It doesn't explain anything at all to you, but it's not difficult how to grow your scarf, power up your scarf, or anything. Other than that, there is not much you can honestly say about it. It's called "Journey" and that's pretty much all it is.It apparently has a story line, though I had no idea what it really was, as it just shows it to you in cut scenes between each "zone". And they really don't make that much sense.It looks as though the developers wanted to do something "artsy",  and this is what was produced. Personally, I find "art", the way is applied to today's "styles" pretty pretentious, and completely full of ♥♥♥♥. To me, these so called artists, painting a blue square in the middle of a canvass and then just splashing red or some other color across it, and then giving it a name like "Swan's in Flight"... it's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, and a way from the pretentious elite to display how much better they are than anyone else.To me, art is a painting with a subject you can actually see and not just paint smeared around on a canvass. And frankly, I don't really get this "game" as "art". I just don't buy it. A personal taste. To me, this was just a boring walk across a desert.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; A pleasant engaging experience that is brief yet immersiveThis game took just under two hours and for ten dollars (the sale price) it was satisfying enough. The best way I can describe this is like going out for a show or movie, perhaps a ballet or a play. I think a ballet is most accurate.This Journey is just that - a journey following the protagonist through an elegant world with simple controls and a lovely soundtrack. You will neither hear nor read a single word as you travel through this world to your destination and journey's end. You will see small clips and markings as your story unfolds. It is very reminiscent in style for me - in that sense at least - to games like Limbo and Inside. After two hours you will have quietly, through music and movement, taken a journey.If you are looking for a simple, pleasant, and peaceful way to spend a couple hours and clear your head, save this for that moment. It will do your mental health wonders.

_childDocuments_.review: Tl;dr: Though I am an uncoordinated ogre, this game made me feel like a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ballerina.Journey is a walking simulator with plenty of platforming elements. It has fantastic visual design, great level design and a fabulous musical score. The mechanics are minimalist. The game is short - about two hours. I strongly recommend playing the entire game in one sitting, ideally with headphones.The controls are simple and progressing through the game poses little challenge even for hopelessly uncoordinated players like me who constantly end up pressing the wrong button. Despite my lack of skill I was treated to fluid, responsive movement that allowed me a level of immersion and control I very rarely get to experience in games. It's a rare treat.The only negative thing I can think to mention is that the camera struggled occasionally - I had one instance of clipping though a rock face that I found surprisingly jarring. This was most noticeable in the beginning of the game and caused little issue.I can see how one may balk at the cost knowing the game is only two hours long, but in this case quality far outweighs quantity. Not to mention that I find Journey to have excellent replayability value. For me, the game costs about the same as a cinema ticket, which made the choice very easy.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, so I'm not sure where to even start with this so I think I'll start from the beginning. I'm someone who really doesn't review games in general, but this game has made me want to share my experience with it. So this will not be very focused in the gameplay, graphics or any of those aspects, but mostly how this game has... impacted me, as cringy as it may sound.The first time I knew of this game was many years ago, my father had installed the demo for the PS3 and he was enamored with the visual style, the simplicity and the vast world that made his imagination go wild. I found certain charm within the game as well, but nothing that made me too invested in it. Fast forward to this year I was dumped by my girlfriend (I know, I know, drama queen yadda yadda) and I had a void in me. I saw the game again in steam and since it was pretty accesible to me I decided to give it a shot.Long story short, I loved it. The simple but charming visuals, the scope of the world that while not completely explorable it gives that feeling of sheer magnitude that makes you feel small in comparassion. Those sliding moments in the desert felt like rejuvenating joy from childhood paired with fantastic music that simply got you rushing.I am someone who likes rpg lite focused games like Dark Souls and Mount and Blade. Levels, dungeons, quests, combat, conquest. But Journey is nothing about that. It is as its name suggests a journey. No grand bosses, no powers beyond gods, no urgency, just you going from point A to point B. And I wouldn't want it any other way. Journey really makes you feel like going from one place to the other as a beautiful and impactful story either solo or with the people you meet in the way.The first time I finished this game was a couple months ago while encountering other players throughout the journey, it was a marvelous experience. But today... Today I started another journey after feeling blue because of life. And I finished it alone this time. I think I can count in one hand the times a game has made me bawl my eyes out, even more strangely for those tears to be of joy. The final segment made me feel happy, hopeful and left me with the sensation that life is beautiful. Art is beautiful. And everything will be ok. It may sound like I put this game on a pedestal, but honestly I kinda do. I wish to make my own games one day and the sensation this game gave me is one I wish to be able to recreate for other people and myself. As short and relatively simple as this game might be, it is a beautiful and soothing experience that I will hold close to my soul.I look forward to sitting on the couch and watch my father play this game from beginning to end. I know he'll love it probably even more than I did.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: I've known of this game and yearned to play it for as long as it has existed, but unfortunately for me it never seemed to get published on platforms available to me... Until recently. It's not every game that makes you confidently say that the ten whole years of waiting for getting to experience it were absolutely worth it, but Journey definitely does! It's just breathtakingly gorgeous in every way. In the beginning I was a bit unsure of the multiplayer aspect of it, but even those fears were unfounded: after meeting many travelers along several journeys, I can safely say that this is likely the most wholesome online multiplayer in existence and it might've restored my faith in humanity a little bit. All in all I can't think of a single thing I would've disliked in this amazing game.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could recommend this game and write a positive review.  As I like the concept, artwork, and really enjoy these experience type of games like Abzu, Firewatch etc. However, the game freezes randomly.  Which I have read is due to new players entering the server.  It's not my settings are too high as I'm hitting high FPS steadily until the freeze which lasts a second or two, then it restarts either ahead of where I was previously if moving or avoiding being killed.I've tried everything and all the advice online, with the only advice that would appear to work being to play in offline mode, which takes away from the experience of sharing the journey with someone else.I managed to complete the game with someone who joined me, and they must have thought I was a complete idiot, as the game would freeze at the worst moments and they would have to either rescue me, or they would hang back while I sorted myself out. This game freeze on the PC is unacceptable, and I would never play through again because of it.  It ruined Journey for me.Without the freeze problem I would replay the game every time I wanted an uplifting relaxing experience, because every other aspect of the game when it ran normally looked absolutely gorgeous, and as mentioned I love the concept and have been looking forward to playing on the PC as a none PSP owner for a long time.What a shame. _childDocuments_.review: It's a dreamlike experience that goes beyond the confines of conventional gaming. Since its 2012 release, players(including me on 12 years later) have been enthralled by its remarkable graphics, moving soundtrack, and insightful narrative. Every second seems to be an artistic creation. Also Dune seems like a fitting parallel to look up to. These pieces take you to distant places and engross them in a complex web of mythology and culture. Journey dives into existential concerns about life, purpose, and the ties that bind us all, just as Dune does with themes of power, destiny, and the human spirit. There are no words to describe my excitement for Journey. Every time I listen to this gem, I become happy. I cannot express how beautiful its scenery are, how melancholic its soundtrack is, and how deeply emotional its narrative is. Playing Journey is something you're really missing out on if you haven't done it already.
