I didn’t like the multiplayer system, while nifty that it is seamless, the drop in players can affect your game, preventing you from experiencing first time activations of what I feel are important story telling devices, thus losing the impact of the story. Besides that big issue, and it’s short length, there are a few spots that force you down snow boarding sections that I feel make you lose the ability to explore, kind of forcing you to speed to the next level. Good things about the game though is that it is beautiful. Extremely well done visually and the music is top notch. The “creatures” are very interesting and I liked that a lot. A few moments of the game have real terrifying spots and it was fantastic for that. Short length and drop in multiplayer are why I wouldn’t recommend this one.

_childDocuments_.review: I was astonished to discover that the fellow travelers encountered along the journey were all real players. This realization transformed the experience into something truly remarkable. Encountering fear in the darkness, overcoming obstacles on snow-covered mountains, and witnessing players disappear midway through the adventure were all part of this unique experience. There were moments I wanted to give up, especially after being attacked by monsters or feeling overwhelmed by the stress of navigating through the snow. Yet, when my character finally succumbed to the elements, collapsing into the snow and the screen fading to white, my thoughts weren't of defeat or sorrow, but a serene acceptance: "now you may rest in peace."This game is a profound journey that evokes the full spectrum of human emotions: curiosity, happiness, fear, and joy, akin to being part of a movie where you're both an observer and a participant. Although I had heard about this game years ago, completing it in just a few hours marked my first foray into its depths. It's not a game for everyone, nor is it something I'd recommend universally. Instead, it feels destined for those who find it, offering an experience that is as unique as it is memorable.

_childDocuments_.review: *This review contains spoilers*Journey was released 10 years ago for the PlayStation 3, and with the traction received by both outer wilds and stray also published by Annapurna Interactive, I think its time to see how this game holds up. Initially, Journey feels very slow, and that's largely due to the very slow movement speed of the player. Luckily, a power mechanic is later introduced where interactive objects, made up what seems to be the same fabric as the players clothing, allows you to glide, albeit a limited number of times. Compared to the slow moving nature of the game on foot, the flying mechanic feels almost liberating once you get to it. In terms of mechanics, there is very little other than this, although the game does find interesting ways to use them. The level design is very linear, and there is no way to fail a level. Holding the W key throughout the game is enough to get through most of the levels, but some problem solving is required here and there. The most interesting part of this game is the way you can meet other players while travelling. This is pretty much hidden, so most players don't know they are playing with other people until its actually revealed at the end of the game. In terms of game mechanics, this is probably the most interesting one, as not only is it cool to see who you've interacted with, but it also ties into the theme of the story.The story itself is kind of interesting. Although its may seem very cryptic and odd at first, slowly as you play the mystery of the game starts to reveal itself. While the story isn't the best thing in the world, it does fit the style and game play nicely and is interesting to think about. The nice looking graphics, while being low poly, do make the game interesting to look at. The story is, while relatively simple, very nice to experience. While there is definitely very much to read into, the simple and short nature of it does leave much to be desired. The soundtrack is an absolute delight and enhances every single part.The biggest downfall of the game (at least in my opinion) has to be the price. The game is very short, maybe spanning 2-4 hours of content depending on how much you're willing to play the game over again. It shouldn't take more than 2 hours to complete, and should be done so in one sitting. The problem is, this game costs 20 dollars, and barely has enough content to warrant that price. If you're looking for a simple and short interactive story, then the game might be for you, however even then I don't recommend buying it at full price. Journey, despite its downsides, will never not be an at least somewhat pleasant experience for anyone with an attention span and 2 spare hours. The game is very immersive, but the length and cost do make me feel like this story would work better as a movie than a game, if it weren't for the unique multiplayer aspect. Still, anyone looking for a decent yet short interactive story game would not be disappointed, just wait for a sale.Thanks for reading.7/10

_childDocuments_.review: Journey is a special game. One that if you play in the right mindset, is hard to forget. But it has a very simplistic & short setup & has been lauded for over 10 years now, so it can be difficult to look past all the hype & praise & just find a way to enjoy it in your own way. But you should try. Maybe buy it on sale, but don’t play it for a month or two. And maybe only after you’ve played something chaotic, aggressive, or violent so that you can treat yourself to it as a palate cleanser. Because even though it’s aged in some respects & has inspired dozens of similar games that you've prob played, I think going through it with as blank of a slate as possible will be a rewarding experience. So if you haven’t played it yet but are now interested, scroll away little fish. Treat yo’ self to Journey without my words in your head. Be gone!…Ok, so Journey is a kick ass lil game (maybe like 3 hrs top per go thru) about a thing in a robe going on trip to a big ole’ light on top of a mountain. Why? Who cares, just get up there. Because as it should be pretty obvious by the title itself, it doesn’t matter where you end up. What matters is the... Naw, I’m not doing it. But along the way of this adventure, you’ll be treated to beautiful music, gorgeous visuals & brief but authentic moments of interpersonal connection. And while it’s not a mechanically complex experience by any means, it’s one that evokes raw feelings of joy, fear, wonder and sadness. But let’s talk about how huh?So to start, the game’s aesthetic leans toward the simplistic side of the spectrum, but not without letting some flecks of detail shine through. Yourself & the beings you encounter are mostly depicted in ways that emphasize shape & movement, through lots of flowing fabric-like appendages. In fact the only time when something doesn’t move in a wave-like way is when it violently attacks, sending a message that rigidity isn't a friendly attribute in this world. These hostile beings are interestingly made of hard surfaces, seeking to literally destroy those who don’t conform into their solid shapes. This diametric theming also extends to the environment, most of which consists of malleable materials like sand & snow, leaving hard surfaces to make up long abandoned structures or obstacles that are slowly being swallowed by the environment. But plastered onto these surfaces are intricate textures that highlight important areas & effectively add to the feeling of forgotten history. And even though the large majority of each section is dominated by sand, their colors differ fantastically to fit the desired mood. The folds & waves of grains can be tan, pink, blue or bronze and are a sight to behold in the context of their respective parts of the trip. Each almost forces you to accept the feeling the developers want to impart on you. The lighting setups in each of these sections also work towards accomplishing this goal. Sometimes the sun will beat down on you from directly overhead, making you feel dominated by the desert. Other times it'll set itself just below the horizon, silhouetting you & emphasizing the beauty & elegance of your movements. But then in rarer times, in the darkest moments, you’ll only be treated to a few slivers of light scattered through the space, or even have them disappear completely, leaving you feeling abandoned & lost. It’s just all-in-all, a real treat for your eyes.So now that we’ve received the delivery to those eyes, in what’s best described as a left-hand jab, we’ve gotta prep for the strike to our ears. And that’s gonna come at us in the form of a right-hand cross that if we’re not ready for, is gonna hit hard & dampen the effect of the music & the sound design. Now, it's pretty well known by now that Austin Wintory’s score has been universally praised & even earned itself a Grammy nomination. But what’s more important is how that score & EQUALLY (& I’m stressing that so hard b/c I really don’t want the sound devs to be overlooked), the sound design is so complimentary to the aforementioned intensely moody areas & your own movements. In the areas where the tone is light & easy, the music is full of light stringed instruments that flow from bridge to chorus in an airy way, motivating you to move forward with at a brisk pace, punctuated by the sounds of your own dainty steps & smooth sliding action. On the opposite side of things though, when you’re in a tough spot, there’ll be loud & long blows from bassy horns that'll try to make their way through the windy and/or combative sounds echoing from the environment. But, even though they’re in competition, they’re really just working together chaotically to give you as much anxiety as possible. And then finally, there’s the moments where little bits of the good & bad are mixed together. When the game decides it’s time to smack you in the face, real quick, just to stun you for a sec. This is where the set piece moments happen. Where everyone involved in the making of this game is doing their absolute best to make you sit up & feel all the things they want you to. Where the light of the strings meet the dark of the horns, but instead of clashing, they swap sides to make your brain scramble for a moment. And that’s the exact moment when your thing in the scarf starts to travel across the screen with such strange artistry that you didn’t think anything on two legs could move like that. And that’s obviously because it couldn’t in real life but because the sound of its steps, spins & slides sound so damn good, you can’t help but accept the possibility for a little while. And that’s why the sound of Journey is so important.Ok, so we’ve now survived the one-two punch of the boxing metaphor that I created & now deeply regret. But it’s too late to stop now, and that’s because the final challenge is here: the surprise roundhouse kick, the gameplay loop itself. And I actually like how me from 5 seconds ago chose the word “loop”. Because that’s exactly what this game is, a circular experience which is meant to be “journeyed’ through multiple times, preferably with a stranger for you to share the whole experience with. Because the world you get to travel through is a lonely one full of world-building elements that prefer to prompt more questions than answer them. And so it feels good to have someone by your side to help anchor you and share in the amazement with, even if you can only communicate through chimes. And as for the loop itself, I’d describe it best as an adventure gamesque experience, with the majority of gameplay being of the puzzle, stealth, and platforming varieties. And while none of them provide much of a challenge, they’re really just meant to enhance the mystery of the world by encouraging exploration and, more importantly, to strengthen the theming for each section of the adventure. The dark and oppressive segments lean more into restricted stealth gameplay, while the ones that are light and jubilant only consist of some of the easiest platforming ever seen. But because these actions are so well matched to the respective sights and sounds you’re taking in by doing them, they fade into the back of your mind and become instinct, allowing you to engage almost seamlessly with the whole experience.So, all-in-all, Journey is really just an adventure game centered around LOTS of complimentary aesthetics which try, with fine-tuned details and techniques, to make you feel feelings. And I think through the combination of those beautifully crafted visual & audio touches, it easily accomplishes that. But once again, I think it's very important to approach this game openly, with as little skepticism to its reputation as possible. Otherwise, you’re just gonna scrutinize all the details to death & lose the magic. Because while there are dozens of games that have done what Journey did, it was a truly remarkable piece of art for its time & still can be today if you approach it with the right mindset.

_childDocuments_.review: If you’ve spent any time in the indie scene, you’ve surely spent part of it wandering through some beautiful, thoughtful landscapes. Narrative adventures that let their environments do the storytelling have indeed become quite popular over the years. Their origins can be traced to several sources, but a cornerstone of the genre has to be Journey. Originally released in 2012 and only recently freed from exclusivity on the PS3, Journey set the style and the tone for so many games that came afterwards. It suffers a little, then, in the comparison if you happened to play its successors first, but even so it’s not hard to see what makes this such a magical… well, journey.You awaken in a vast desert, clad in crimson robes and driven by a vision of a distant peak. Setting out towards your mysterious goal takes you across a land of ancient ruins, strange machines, and breathtaking vistas. Towering gates and cliffs may stand in your way, but you can do more than simply walk, slide, and hop. Tattered tapestries found along your path can boost you high into the air, and some will join with your own robes to let you jump higher and glide further. They’ve got a mind of their own as well, which will become more apparent as the other inhabitants of this land return to life. And even when these beings are out of the picture, this is not a journey you’ll need to make alone.It’s easy to use a lot of grand language to describe the places and scenery in Journey, because grandeur is easily its most striking feature. The desert you start in seems to roll on forever, with massive structures poking up from the ruddy sands. You can venture far afield from points of interest, farther than I expected, giving the place an enormous sense of scale. This sense only grows as you move on to new areas, with even larger landmarks and bigger spaces to explore. The graphics are simple but purposefully so, focusing on bold shapes and contrasts to draw the eye towards the most impressive forms. It’s a style that’s been widely adopted in Journey’s wake, so much so that I’m sure you’ll be immediately familiar and comfortable with it from the start.As a founding member of this genre, you can expect to spend most of your time wandering these beautiful places. Your character moves at a decent clip, and the features and landmarks you find tell an interesting, subtle story about the world you’re travelling through. You can jump and glide as well, and both of these are enhanced by finding special scraps of cloth that join with your scarf to make it longer and lovelier. Other banners and tapestries of similar material recharge your floatiness, as well as exhibit some interesting behavior of their own. Your one other ability is to speak a sort of tone, which can be charged up to make it louder and interact with fabrics and other objects in different ways. There are some minor puzzles that make use of this, but mostly this is a game about making it from point A to point B, and enjoying the scenery along the way.I mentioned before that this is not a journey you have to make alone, and that’s probably the most unique aspect of Journey. There’s a silent multiplayer system running in the background that pairs you with other players, providing you with a real-life partner for each leg of your trip. They’ll wander around the world the same as you, interact with the same things, and fade out if you stray too far from them only to be replaced by another later on. With no chat of any kind, the emergent communication that springs from the simple gameplay mechanics are a real treat, and I felt an actual kinship with some of the folks I traveled with. You can even boost each other using your voice which can make some sections easier or get you to new places, or simply help you move around faster with long glides.I wouldn’t want to play Journey without this system, but it does have its drawbacks. There’s one puzzle sequence in a tower where my partner at the time ran ahead and did everything for us, which prevented me from exploring or interacting with the mechanics there. I feel like it’s probably the only place in the game where that could happen due to how the puzzle works, but it still dampened the mood. It’s also worth noting that, as strong as the game’s aesthetic is, it’s still a game from 2012 and this is not a remaster. This means there’s a fair bit of outdated design like invisible walls and poor collision in places, as well as some graphical roughness and blurriness in places. My graphics card didn’t seem to get along real well with it either, leaving a few areas blacked out when there was supposed to be some sort of environmental effect.Journey is a landmark game, make no mistake, and a major reason we have so many great games like it now. It naturally doesn’t hold up quite so well when compared to more modern titles, and for my part it isn’t really the religious experience some people seemed to feel it was. I had the same experience with Abzu honestly, which is fitting since it was made by some of the same folks. Journey is beautiful and woven full of meaning, but I enjoy it more for the atmosphere and the relaxing gameplay than any sort of revelatory experience. Definitely check it out if you’re a fan of the genre and missed it before, and then join me in hoping that its clever multiplayer scheme makes a comeback someday.Did you enjoy this review? I certainly hope so, and I certainly hope you'll check out more of them at  or on my !

I don't recommend it to someone who is looking for more of a interactive-taking action/getting quests kind of game. Yes- you are collecting stuff/activating it and jumping /flying around but if I didn't feel so depressed playing it I would consider it to be a very boring game. _childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game. The whole experience was very nice, but there was a stretch while playing the game that felt like it was exactly what the designers intended. You'll occasionally find that you come across another explorer who is in the same area as you. During that shared experience, you can't really communicate other than through sounds, but you can follow each other or show each other around.I went through several levels near the middle game, including one of the creepier ones (no spoilers), and we stuck together and helped each other along in a way that was genuinely moving. Eventually I had to leave to go help my kids with something, and I legitimately felt bad to leave him after 3 levels of dedicated cooperation. It was awesome to go through the journey, have some passing interactions with some, and some great cooperation with others, and then to see them go and never know who they were. It was a really cool experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: This game was truly an experience; I don't recall the last time a game hit home on such a genuine emotional level.  I cared when the other person struggled or got hurt; finding secrets or successfully making it past the more difficult bits resulted in elated chirping from both the stranger and I that felt truly joyful or that we were happy for one another. We were invested in finishing the journey together, making sure not to leave the other behind.  The first person I met logged out and I was genuinely sad they left; the game paints the feeling of isolation and connection, The 2nd person was clearly someone that played before, but they were very patient and made a point of showing me things or what to do if I didn't see it myself.  The end stage evokes a joyful feeling and I honestly regretted that my partner and I were soon going to part ways. I don't know about them, but I felt a genuine connection during this experience. I think that since they're lost in the shuffle of anonymity it adds to it in a way, keeping the memory distilled to the pure and evocative experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly... I never thought I'd play this game because I didn't think I'd ever get the original console it was on, or the game itself... It was a work of Art that brought me to tears, because I related so much to the Journey.Everything I was trying to accomplish,My greatest sorrows and pains,My wishes,My desires,My fears,My ultimate Love...All of it was condensed into about an hour... I saw it, and was somewhat doubting what I had been told in my mind...Was I crying because seeing the mission fulfilled was beautiful? Was it relief? Was it mixed anguish that it would never be accomplished... I wondered... and.... right now I'm kinda crying... but I'm trying to hold it back...It's a beautiful game... If you do play it, please take to heart the message...The current system humanity depends on has already done this... But you know... What does it matter? They'll never learn anyways... And stressing about it the past decade has really made me feel bad...I guess... I guess I can just hope in one thing....There's a Love grander than anything we're capable of seeing on the surface of reality...I just wish one day I can help those who never had a fighting chance...The ones who never knew freedom...The animals in the factories...The Fountain of Life...And to one day meet with the Spirit.

_childDocuments_.review: I played Journey a couple of years ago and recently rebought it on Steam. Although the game is quite short, it always managed to fascinate me. The story and the gameplay are simple, but combined work really well together. Even when you play this game alone it is, but when you find other people the game becomes magic. Throughout my first "Journey" (pun intended) I met several people. Without being able to communicate apart from using meaningless symbols, one bonds with another. The aspect of not knowing who you are playing with is quite fascinating. Example given you could be playing with a child or an adult but in this game it just doesn't matter. The depth of the bondage with players differs every time. In my first playthrough I met somebody who just rushed and didn't take time to explore. Because I wanted to take my time, he soon vanished in the horizon. However, one time I met a white robed person at the very start of the game. I wasn't planning on playing the game entirely, but I didn't want to leave him. So we actually played through the whole game together, and he waited for me and sometimes showed me symbols I had yet to find. It was an amazing adventure with him and at the end it was kind of sad when it ended. I now aspire to be like my previous partner and made it my task to guide lost travelers  when I meet them.Overall, I can only recommend this game. _childDocuments_.review: Quality time.Quite often a thing hard to come by.It's elusive, even planning for it may fail.Journey gave me just that - while it may be short, it felt like quality time.It has a simple beauty to it, both graphically and 'story'-wise. The sand, in particular, has a dreamlike reality to it that I haven't seen very often. The simple character-models, both player and other, are strangely expressive, especially since they have neither faces nor arms with witch  to convey expression"Life is a journey, not a destination" - has never been more true. Especially when what little 'story' there is is somehow turns accomplishment on its head and transforms it into a Sisyphean task. (Ok, choosing between rolling a boulder and playing Journey may seem a no-brainer - but eternity is a mighty long time.)In the final moments of the game - final as in after it, in the credits, came the revelation that elevated Journey from 'good', 'beautiful' and 'zen-like' to something lightly touched by Awesome. Go play it. Soon!

_childDocuments_.review: At 3 am, curiosity led me to try a new game. Initially, it felt slow and uninspiring at first. Then, unexpectedly, another player appeared. I assumed it was an NPC, moving alongside me. But there was something different. This "NPC" wasn't behaving predictably.Puzzled, I wondered if it could be a real player. Yet, I hadn't logged into any account, nor chosen a multiplayer mode. Perplexed, I continued. Unfortunately , in an underground level, we lost contact, making me question if it was just an NPC after all.Emerging from the tunnel, a player greeted me and it surprised me. This time the signs were clear: I was not alone.Overjoyed by seeing each other , we sang for a few seconds together and continued our journey. We journeyed together, sharing the path and its wonders, reaching the end side by side.Having been without friends for years, this unexpected companionship brought a warmth I hadn't felt in a long time. The beautiful scenery of our final journey, experienced with another soul, moved me to tears of joy.After i finished the game i searched online, and confirmed this game is indeed multiplayer, but unlike any other. It's a rare gem, a beautiful blend of solitude and connection, bringing strangers together in an unforgettable way.

_childDocuments_.review: I think there are two slightly different games here. I had the luck to meet someone on the first level and we journeyed together. That took an hour, partly due to not wanting to hold the other person up. It was sweet and nice. The slightly different game would be a solo play-through when one seeks out the hidden things and explores a bit more - that'll probably take ~2 hours.How people went on about it when it first came out about being the new gold was a bit much - but it is nice.I'm a bit of a tight wad - so half price was a bit much: 2/3s off would be better. I suggest getting it on a steep sale - as then other people will be getting it too and the chances of having a play-through with someone will increase (playing at peak times will help too).

_childDocuments_.review: The story line is left intentionally vague, but if you really think about your "journey," you'll realize how much meaning it actually has. You'll have some solo parts, and some parts where you run into random people, and you'll like every second of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely, short-ish, and oh so scenic game that lives up to its name perfectly. Beautiful visuals and audio combine to make for a very evocative experience, rich in atmosphere and discovery. This is a good job as there's not really that much to do besides an inevitable push towards the mystery mountain, peppered with some light platforming and stealth-like moments. Like the winds that can sometimes engulf you, you can easily get swept up in it, thanks to a wonderful realisation of a world after the fall, with the mysterious history of the civilisation revealed by progressively finding and activating murals. If you enjoyed a game like Gris, then I think this should also appeal on a similar level. Thay have similar vibes, especially in the music, and Journey focuses very much on an experience over a multitude of game mechanics.There's a good chance you won't journey alone as you can meet other travellers along the way, communicating to each other by way of chirps, and abstract vocalisations. Whilst it is nice to meet fellow wanderers, I'd recommend taking Steam into offline mode for your first journey so you can experience it in your own personal way without another dictating the pace by doing and/or activating things in the levels that you should probably discover by yourself initially. I think it's best suited that subsequent journeys can then be partly or fully enjoyed with others if you wish to before going separate ways (world's apart).It doesn't offer much of a challenge but that's not the point. I think this will be a lovely, cozy one to just return to with open arms every now and again purely to soak up the world and get wrapped up in its magical tapestry all over again.And if you doubt you can make it to the end, just, er, don't stop believin',

You wait for them and they wait for you, and in the end this game truly is the definition "The destination doesn't matter, but the journey there does" 5/5

_childDocuments_.review: WOW.First of all, I want to deeply thank my friend for gifting this to me. I didn't even know it was on Steam 'till it was gifted to me...Again, WOW. This game is... truly an experience. There's no dialogue, no words, no nameplates, no chat, no emotes. A story told through imagery and nameless companion(s) that accompanies you along the way. It was tense, beautiful and an absolute joy to play. When I buy games, I normally buy it based on the amount of enjoyment I'll get out of it. (I like to follow the $1 per 1 hour rule as a guideline). _childDocuments_.review: Journey feels almost literary in a sense, like immersing yourself in a hieroglyphic script. It's really a marvel how intelligent and carefully designed the experience is, especially for such an (unfortunately) short game. I found the controls to be slightly frustrating, but I can forgive that for its wholly unique style and emphasis on intelligent, minimalist storytelling.

_childDocuments_.review: I first played Journey on its initial release on the PS3 way back in 2012, and immediately fell in love with the quiet, solemn gorgeousness of it. I remember putting many hours into my travels with companions, some frustrating and some fantastic, but always peaceful in the end. Journey became something of a means of meditation for me, I think. It was a soothing ritual to set out time and again on the familiar road to reincarnation; a small sort of comfort in crossing paths with another traveler and finding immediate connection in the wordless communication of chirps and hops. I played Journey again and again until I no longer had the console to play it on.So it was a surprise and an absolute delight to find it re-released onto Steam some 8 odd years later, completely by accident. Playing again felt like returning to an old friend. Warm, nostalgic, joyful. The simplicity of controls and stylized art give the game a feeling of timelessness. An experience I know I can return to whenever I'd like, still finding the same sense of heartfelt wonder with each pilgrimage to the mountaintop. Thatgamecompany will always stand as my champion for showing just how artful the experience of video games can be.

_childDocuments_.review: Journey is one of the greatest games i have ever played.The game in itself is quite simple, just go towards the shining mountain,but as the saying goes: It's not about the destination, it's about the Journey.During your travel you will meet other players that will accompany you throughout the journey.You are not able to talk to them, hell, you don't even know their name (Although, you CAN get their name after beating the game)The game shows that despite our differences, despite the language barriers, you can still get together and understand eachother, learn about one another, without a single word.For me, THIS is the best thing about Journey!Without companions, this game would not be the same, it wouldn't make me feel as much without them.I have managed to grow such a bond with some travelers and it was always so heartbreaking having to leave them behind.Some of them left early, and some stayed until the very end and I will never forget my first few playthroughs of this game. Actually, I don't think I could really call this a "game", it's more of an interactive art piece!If you do end up playing Journey and want a similar experiance, albeit with up to 8 people, I strongly recommend you play another TGC's game, Sky: Children of The Light! (Please actually play it, it's free!)

_childDocuments_.review: It's just a chill adventure.I've been told so many times how it's some sort of a unique meditation on the nature of human connection, a milestone in non-verbal storytelling, a deeply original experience, but... it's just a chill adventure. It has puzzles, enemies, little comics, and everything. It doesn't do anything unique.I guess you had to be there and play  when it was just released. It was original back then... except it wasn't. It was released in 2012;  did great non-verbal storytelling in 2005.  did great meditative non-verbal multiplayer in 2005 as well.I can't give  a thumbs down because it's a well-crafted and pleasant game, but it seems like my expectations were completely off the mark. Recommended to people who just want a chill adventure.

_childDocuments_.review: (Attention, the review may contain spoilers)The way was always the goal ...You begin your journey in a desert and explore the surroundings, which are peppered with ruins, perhaps of a long-dead civilisation, a mountain in the distance probably indicating the destination of the journey. Graphically alone, it's an incredible experience. The music is also excellent and the end credits in particular are musically very special and touched my heart so much. On your journey you can randomly meet other travellers, which are other players. Sometimes for a shorter, sometimes for a longer time. You can't chat with them or anything like that, you don't know anything about your fellow player. However, you can emit melodic whistles and communicate with each other in this way. You wear a scarf that can be "charged" on the way, with pieces of cloth that fly around in some places. You can then fly a bit yourself and reach higher places. If you are accompanied by a fellow traveller, you can "recharge" each other and thus reach unreachable places alone. In this game, you dive down into questions of meaning, where does the journey lead to, is the summit really the goal, what lies beyond it. And even after the end of the game, I felt that the game continued to have an effect for a long time, because the summit was never the goal, the path, what you experience and with whom, alone or together, was always the goal. The second time I played the game, I was only alone for the first few minutes, the whole rest of the journey I was with a fellow traveller. You don't know anything about the other person, gender, skin colour, age, but none of that matters. You experienced this wonderful journey together and that's what counts. I was shown places I had never seen before. You could communicate with each other through the melodic whistling, towards the end of the game even in the same beat. When we reached the top, we knew it was the end of our journey together and we would never see each other again ... we both didn't want to go any further, running around each other and whistling and flying a bit at a time. We both drew a heart in the snow almost at the same time ... then walked through the mountain together ... I never had such a beautiful and at the same time sad ending as in this game. In the end, all I had left of my fellow traveller was a rune with letters and numbers ... Thank you for this journey.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an utterly stunning game that evokes a wide range of emotions without even using a single word. Either written or spoken. That a lone is a great marker for how well this game was designed and made. While I am sure there will be a slight difference for everyone who may play this in terms of events due to the nature of how it works. I still think at the core of it people will genuinely have felt a lot of things during it and be left with a great impression of their time in the game.It's an incredibly simple game. With practically only a basic movement system, you can jump and glide and ring a bell while also pinging in an area. It has a beautiful artistic style and really works simplistic pallets to their best without having to overload every area or moment with too much visible clutter. It doesn't lack for beauty and really works the camera and the environments to great effect. Small touches to signal things like health, or being under the effects of something is so intuitive the game basically just leads you with no real interruption to the gameplay nor story.I highly recommend playing this game at least once. It may well be an experience you remember fondly and at worst you'll waste very little time completing it. But you'll support a great game and potentially have a great unique experience that you'll not find in many other games.

_childDocuments_.review: I do not own a playstation 3 nor 4.About 5 years ago I started listening to Journey's Soundtrack by coincidence, on youtube. I immediately fell in love with it, and It has been, since then, one of my favorite albums for listening while studying or relaxing. The landscapes were beautiful, and mixed with the soundtrack, it was a pleasure to adventure in this small world. In the middle of my Journey, I have found my first co-op adventurer, and the way they implemented co-op was by itself another wonder.In 2 hours of gameplay I was able to be happy, sad, frightened, and most of all, constantly fascinated.This is a beautiful game, If you can even call it a game.To me, it was a Journey.

_childDocuments_.review: The game itself is alright. Nothing life-changing or incredibly emotional as so many have put it in the past. But having gotten it on sale, it's good value, and I finally got to experience a game I had wanted to play for a long time, precisely because of the high praise it had received. I'm sure those high expectations did not help.However, the port itself is terrible. Strangely, I get great performance with graphical settings cranked up to the max, but after suffering several crashes during the Underground Passage section, I dropped everything to the lowest.  After this, the game runs terribly, but at least I managed to get past that section. Having so many frame stutters muddles the experience.And now that I'm trying to get all achievements, still running with lowest settings, I'm again crashing during that section. Unfortunately, the game is not interesting or fun enough to put up with this or look up a patch. In conclusion: get it on sale, temper your expectations, and hope you don't crash constantly. Hopefully you get more fun out of it than I did.

_childDocuments_.review: First things first, lets talk about what makes this game so great.Journey is one of the most beautiful game ever, by it's art style and it's story. It will take you on a unique experience that you will never forget if you like this kind of game.The game is gorgeous, and will get to you without using any words or text.However, I cannot ignore how poorly it was ported.Performance is really not where it should be for a game released on a PS3.A lot of users reported high CPU usage, crippling performance, where there should be almost none for a game like this.When turning the MSAA to max, black halos form around the menu text and performance drop to unplayable levels. Trying to reverse it causes the menu to glitch and the game crashing when clicking apply (using a 7700HQ and a GTX 1070).Releasing a game with this kind of obvious bug is unacceptable and they should at least remove the option if they can't fix it.Lapotps users beware, the game launches on integrated graphics, be sure to switch it to your dedicated graphics card.To wrap it up, Journey is one of the best game out there, who will take you on a chort, but unforgettable adventure.It's just a shame to not be able to enjoy it as it should be because of a rushed poor pc port.

_childDocuments_.review: Journey is a sublime, beautiful experience that you can share with a stranger (or multiple strangers). the desert landscapes, the ancient ruins, and the mountain summit are all gorgeous to look at, and the amazing music adds to the already gorgeous atmosphere. i don't really have words to describe it or the emotions i felt whilst playing Journey, so i'm going to make this review a thank you letter to the person who travelled with me on my Journeyto Green Brick,thank you for travelling with me. i never thought a chance encounter in the desert with someone else going up to the split mountain would wind up with me becoming terrified of not catching up with you in the ruins. i never thought that a 1.5 hour game would see me worry about what happened to you when we got separated again in the snowstorm. i never thought a game that serves as a metaphor for a spiritual journey would see me hope for you to make it to the summit before me. i never expected this game to make me so happy when i saw you waiting for me after we got passed the leviathan. the flight up to the summit with you was surreal, and i felt genuine joy and sadness when we went into the light together, knowing we made it yet we would probably never cross paths againi wanted to thank you from the bottom of my heart for making an already a amazing experience even more amazing. i only hope i made the journey as memorable for you as you made it for meyour desert friend,Shield

_childDocuments_.review: I remember when this game was released I wanted to play it but I didn't want to buy a PS3. Well 9 years after I finished it and I am not impressed at all.I will start with the negatives since I started this review in negative tone. The game feels and looks dated,I played many games similar to Journey and most of them are better...I know that Journey was one of the first games that went for this artistic life journey experiment but games followed that formula and evolved over 9 years. I am not saying Journey is a bad game it is just old and thats it. In my opinion porting  a console game 8 years after is just to grab the money because the port isn't that good to be honest (awful audio bugs).The game is a walking sim and if I hate something about walking sims that would be walking at a snails pace for more then 4 minutes(plenty of that in this game) . This game is at its best when it flows and I did had few WOW moments and I created my version of what the story is about. The thing that I didn't know is that others can join my game ,I found that annoying at times but also great at times...interesting decision by the developers,almost like a social experiment.Conclusion - Joureney is a good game but dated, a classic for sure but didn't age that well. _childDocuments_.review: One of the prettiest games I've played in a while. The story was a bit awkward in my opinion because I couldn't really understand it my first playthrough, but maybe I'm just a bit stupid. The underground part with the stone creature? And my flying pal? Yeah, genuine emotional damage done to me right there. I'd rate it a solid 8.5/10. I wish it was a bit longer, but I have a lot of fun replaying it.Met up with a random near the beginning of the game on my 2nd playthrough and we stuck together through all the trials and levels. Every time one of us got attacked by those flying stone creatures, the other would chirp until we got back together again. We led each other to fabric places to lengthen our scarves. When we climbed the mountain together, they fell from the staircase and I leapt down to join them. At one point they sat down in the snow and I assumed they were just meditating for a while, so I sat down next to them, and waited... and waited... and waited...... Over 15 minutes of being tabbed out sitting next to my companion, wondering if they would ever come back at all but DETERMINED to not be the one to leave them, they finally returned... and we finished the game together. It's much more emotional to finish the game with a companion than on your own, I must admit.RiotoSato, whoever you are, wherever you are... I hope you know I would die for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, over 17k reviews at the time I'm writing this. Not much more can be said, Journey is an incredible game. But I feel that many Steam players are kinda missing out on some of it's best aspects.1.  Yes you *can* play with kb/mouse, but you won't be able to do any trick moves. Even the simplest trick like doing a faceplant requires spinning the left stick, which of course is impossible with a kb/mouse. Advanced tricks like boosting are also impossible without a gamepad.2. . You just need to work around the games matchmaking. Coordinating with a friend so you both enter the first game level (the bridge area) at the same time usually works.3.  All those areas in the game that you can see but can't reach, like the far off bridges and buildings. You can reach all those places. Journey is the only game I know of that has such a rich abundance of exploration out of the restricted/designed play area. You can spend hours and hours exploring, and every single level has it's secrets, though some require advanced flight techniques to access.After you've played through a few times, you'll unlocked the white cloak. That's when Journey begins to open up like an oyster revealing it's pearl.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: There are games that let you spend a few hours of fun, and there are games - rare, rare gems - that allow you to feel something you've never felt before, to grasp concepts that seemed very distant just before. Journey is a masterpiece that everyone should experience at least once; for me, it rekindled a little hope in the bonds we share with all our brothers and sisters on earth. Don't expect a long game, for the whole experience can last between 1 and 2 hours, but there are elements of replayability thanks to the online interactions and collectibles. Also, the game features some surprising skill elements and a wonderful, wonderful community. I'm sure I'll spend many more hours on Journey.

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished my first playthrough and I want to start by saying thank you.The first thank you is for the team working on this game: The ambiance was grandiose and the music excellent. Each scene was a piece of art: The discovery where a lot of guided freedom is given. Then the ingenious puzzle that makes the player invested in the game. The slides mechanism that is fully mastered and is only able to give a feeling of joy, satisfaction and speed.The enemy which is at no point omnipresent, but have enough influence to give the player a sentiment of tension and powerlessness. A wonderful storytelling and sufficient lore to invest the player even more. And finally the last level being in a league of its own (I don't want to explain and those who played the game know what I mean).The second thank you is for the random stranger that I came across and ended my playthrough with. Being thrown to the unknown, but together is a total other experience that just being alone. We discovered the game and its implication together from the beginning till the end. Helping and waiting one another even when there is no benefit nor gain from it, just the beauty of a human interaction.I don't know who you are, how you or even where you are but the only thing I know is that this game made me fall in love with a stranger.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: A lovely little game (only takes 1,5-2h to complete) with beautiful art and music and (mostly) cute creatures where the protagonist travels to the top of a mountain through different landscapes, learns about the history of the world and meets companions (other players) on the way. The story leaves a lot for the players to interpret and the game is surprisingly emotional. Some players might rush ahead, making it easy for you to lose track of them, but others will continue travelling with you for the rest of the game, helping you along and waiting for you if you have trouble getting ahead or just want to look around. Fun to replay, as you can then help others on their journeys.I've encountered some bugs, but nothing major, though if you're an achievement hunter, one achievement might require you to adjust graphics settings for the game to register the achievement.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: Journey is an experimental surfing game with soulslike coop sprinkled with phallic symbolism. Themes somehow fit the modern ethos well.I like the idea of the ephemeral multiplayer component, which is integral to the experience but not to the play. At its best it reinforces positivity and thoughtfulness.I waited 8 years to play this game. It was a fine act to bring it to the PC.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: My teachers at my game art study highly praised this game for its visual storytelling and design and I get why! The environments are simple yet beautiful and the music completes it all, I felt very immersed. I do have to say though, it is more of an experience than a typical 'game'. There are some puzzles and flying mechanics, but it is fairly minimal (though flying around is really fun). Would love it if there were more complex puzzles you needed to solve with your buddy or so to bond with them even more!
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: First, a very small note of critique, I would just say that having to rely on one point of reference to find everything out in the desert can be hard, but that is more of an issue for anyone trying to achievement hunt in the game. Now for the praise, which I have large amounts of for this game. I am a very antisocial person, but in the vast nothingness of the dunes, just knowing someone else is there with you is a very comfortable feeling. I've finished the game twice so far, one run completing it alone, and the second was with someone with a white robe, and I can not emphasize how amazing and bittersweet the ending becomes with someone else. I don't think you can truly experience "Journey" until you have completed this game with a companion that you had from the very beginning, and while it is hard to manage in a game where there is no real communication with your partner, I think when you finally get the chance it will make the end all the sweeter, and I think that feeling would apply to anyone else. For a game with no words, it speaks to the soul in a way very few games can, and that seems to be the general trend for the games put out by this developer. "Journey" is a story, but more than that, it is an experience, and a great one at that.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game because I heard of the connectivity feature.When I first loaded into the bridge area, I was disappointed to see no one nearby, so I closed the game.Then I re-opened, now with the knowledge of the "white glow" and almost instantly noticed it, seeing someone sat in the sandUnfortunately they left meA few levels later however, I met someone that stuck with me right until the end, we completed the game together.Thank you Brananarama for making my Journey more fun. I had a smile on my face every time we interacted, and I got scared when I would lose you on certain levels thinking we would get disconnected10/10 game
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: Journey is one of my all time favorite games out there. With a scenery that will make you stand still and just take it all in, to a story hidden within the ruins of what once was. You connect with players from all over the world as you make your way to Eden. With the only way of communicating being chrips and calls you have to explore and trust one another to make it to your goal.  Note -  that this game is meant to be played multiple times, Trust me it will make sense when you go through it once. You can recognize Vet players by their cloaks having more rows of  simbols on the bottem. So dont be afraid to run off with them as they ( mostlikely) only mean for you to have the best experiance you can have in the game.With the sad undertone and new found connection you will only find out who your new found friends was that helped you along the way at the very end, So dont forget to write down a user name or two or 7 when you go to the ' Thank you or traveling with me' thread here on steam.Happy exploring -x-
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: Even if I completed the game in under 2 hours it is one of the most emotional games I've played. It's amazing how the game is able to tell a story with only visuals and music and not a single word. The soundtrack is unbelievably good and hits just the right time. I really like when I meet another player and experience the game together. Unfortunately that player left before the ending but the way it's executed is good that you can not see the name or communicate. The only thing you can do is make sounds to each other and it makes you care for that completely strange person. The end left me with a lot of thoughts and emotions. This is truly a masterpiece, it's a must play in my opinion.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: Love, love, love this game. Did I mention that I love this game? I usually go for survival/exploration games but a friend recommended I try Journey and I'm so glad I did. On my first play through I met several fellow travelers and while I'm late to gaming (I'm 59 and just really started playing games last year) I can say with 100% certainty that I've never felt such a connection to players that I've just met. I struggled with learning how to fly and they waited patiently while I plowed into walls and ceilings. They would chirp what I think was encouragement since they didn't leave me behind. And when I got to the stairs in the snow level and couldn't figure it out they wouldn't leave me behind. I finally had to quit the game so that my fellow travelers could finish their journey. Last night I finally made it to the end of the game. Wow was it amazing.This is the only game I've played where I felt deep emotions, met players who were selfless, and immediately knew it was a game I could come to to be uplifted.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: Journey is one of the most beautiful experiences since the creation of video games as a medium. The atmosphere/music/aesthetics are just all perfection, throw that in with some wholesome co-op with strangers where you can easily find a nice person to chime all game with and then just be sad that it all ended. Journey is a must if you believe games are an artform!
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game with a very clever incorporation of interactive sounds and music.The rewards for sticking to an unknown fellow companion is very rewarding in the end.There are very few games that can elevate the emotions that comes with it. Journey is such a game.I keep returning to this classic. Any self respecting gamer should have a copy of this gem.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: A game that made me laugh, scratch my head and afraid all in one.Journey ... It is in the name, isn't it? Once is enough to experience the whole game but the achievements are fun to do. Singing to one another as you slide down a dune, reassurance as the machines fly by, babysitting a single patterned companion and the end. The sands of this live will return to the dunes and i will be shaped once more.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: Why do people like this game? I'm not trying to be rude, I just really don't understand.I picked it up due to the overwhelming number of positive reviews that now seem like they were talking about a different game entirely.The Story was supposedly special and meaningful. I found it remarkably flat and predictable. I wont spoil it for any who still wish to discover it for themselves, but to be honest, it was basically exactly what I was expecting from the cover art and no more. The music did a good job of conveying emotion and the storytelling style was well executed, but unfortunately that doesn't come anywhere close to making up for the lackluster, played out content of said story (in my opinion).The gameplay was smooth and mildly interesting, it wasn't trying to be groundbreaking, and was mainly a storytelling device, so I can't fault it for being a bit... lets be kind and call it 'understated'.  It did have a distinctive dragging feel to it though. Maybe the devs were targeting a group with a longer attention span than I possess, but I felt like the levels were much wider and stretched out than they needed to be and the lethargic movement speed left me bored/frustrated and staring off into space for the half-minute it took to cross an empty stretch of sand. There is a flight/jump dynamic that made things interesting, but with a limited charge and a long space between recharge points, it felt just interesting enough to make me want to get to the next recharge place, but not interesting enough to prevent me from resenting the trek.The multiplayer dynamic was not something I was expecting, and solved a few of these balance issues. BUT I usually prefer to explore every corner of a space looking for secrets, view angles, and collectibles. I didn't feel free to take my time and explore while there was another player accompanying me and wanting me to follow them in order to progress. Especially when going over that ridge over yonder took a solid 2-4 minutes of them either following to pick something up they already had, or waiting around for me to return, pinging relentlessly. It was very short, which isn't necessarily a bad thing, but I was left with a feeling of waiting for the game to pick up, or the story to become something I hadn't seen a dozen times before, or to get another movement dynamic that would make things less draggy, or, or, or...... oh. its over. well. I guess no one can say I didn't give it a fair chance....All in all, I'm disappointed. Would not recommend. I apologize to any die-hard fans or Devs I may be insulting, but to me, it felt lackluster, poorly balanced, and led nowhere.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: Journey is a beautiful game with a confusing story that I found near impossible to discern.I had no idea quite why I was wandering through the deserts, valleys, and snowpeaked mountains of the game, but I knew that the game was quite pretty and had an amazing soundtrack to go along with my gameplay!Not a bad game, worth the 11$ and you get Flower free too!8/10edit: i also really enjoyed the random encounters with other players, waiting for them, doing the little "sing" mechanic to get their attention.Journey really is a good game, I urge you to get it while it's on sale! Give it a try! Pretty replayable game, too! Even if I don't see myself replaying it for quite some time... I won't be refunding it!
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game in a bundle since the difference in price was very small, expecting for it to be a short game that I will play once. It was  worth it, and even though game play is limited, it will take you a few run-throughs to get used to all the ways you could optimize the mechanics. I finished it at least 3 times now and will definitely come back for the rest of the achievements.I have never heard of anonymous mute co-op, but this is it. Doing it with a partner and no ability to communicate makes it more fun. It's definitely on the easy side and even easier if both players know the mechanics well, but the difficulty is not the point of the game as much as fun and wonder are.It's a delightful experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: An interesting and bliss adventure.It's quite difficult to not hate this game and the main reason why is the co-op. I would have given this game a dislike easily, but the co-op made my experience special and gave me and my character a reason to push on because I wasn't going to give up and on my partner.Without the co-op implemented this game would fall flat because of activities you can do and the graphics. By all means it looks good, but it ain't on the level of ABZU. ABZU takes the cake for this genre and it has more to offer.On sale this looks to be reasonable deal. I wouldn't get it at full price, sorry.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best games ever. Despite its short length, it has great replayability, and I'm sure the strong emotions felt during the initial playthrough will carry over to future ones. It moves you with its art direction, music, the feelings of power and hopelessness, birth and rebirth... Words fail this game. Buy it and try it yourself. You won't regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: It's cute. Much shorter than I expected (I expected it to be short, but I was thinking more along the lines of 3 hours), but it does make the most of its play time.+ Really beautiful+ Not a dull moment+ Gameplay varies between exploration, puzzle, stealth, platforming and... just sliding down dunes very fast+ Good environmental storytelling, does a lot with no dialogue- A little too short- Anticlimactic ending- Seamless multiplayer. One of the gaming industries' current obsession, and I really wish it weren't. Controversial, I know, seeing as most reviews are saying it was amazing how they became best friends with someone the other side of the world without being able to talk at all, but that wasn't the case in my playthrough. It was just annoying. I had 4 people pop in and out of my game - The first one was at the very beginning, and they just rushed forward, ignoring all collectibles and chirping aggressively, and then abandoned me when they got too far ahead. The second was just... standing still and not responding at all, and then disconnected. The third stayed with me for about 5 minutes, then I lost them somehow. The fourth disconnected almost immediately. I wouldn't say this completely ruined the experience for me, because there isn't much other players can do to interefere with your game, but it was pretty damn immersion breaking to have some other Journyer pop in and out and run around me when I'm finally starting to get invested. I would have just played offline, but there isn't any way to do that other than literally disconnecting my computer from the internet, and I didn't wanna do that.- Hidden collectibles. That's a pet peeve of mine. I hate it when games try to extend the play time by just placing a whole bunch of collectibles in various hidden places like behind columns or under the floor. If the collectibles are important, the result is I have to completely ruin the flow of the game so I can thoroughly search every room. I hate it. In this game the collectibles are only semi-important - they extend your scarf length, meaning you can fly for longer, but it's not actually  to be able to fly longer, so when I realized that I just stopped collecting them, unless I just happened upon them by chance.Bottom line - It's a cute, short, pretty game that's probably best bought on sale, and probably best played offline, unless you really like multiplayer.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: Bought this game because it was on sale for under $10. Had no idea it was multiplayer, no idea about it other than it got positive reviews. Went in totally blind. I ended up spending 4 - 5 hours playing and enjoyed it! Took a while to figure out what was happening, but it is interesting enough that I'll try again.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: I liked that this game metaphorically explains life, in general. You start out with nothing, small and innocent like a baby, as you collect scarfs in the game and gain the ability to fly as you progress through your path to reach the mountain. You might bump into a person, a complete stranger, while you travel with them throughout the game and become great companions. You face danger and difficulties but also experience joy and euphoria simply through singing in rhythm and always looking out for each other while it gets cold or they get attacked. In the end, through the short yet nostalgic or loving memories that you created with your friend, you become weak, slowly dying in the snow together. Having lost your ability to move around more, unable to sing, not having a scarf anymore and no more flying, it seems you are vulnerable again, just like how you used to be when you started out but this time, wiser yet fragile, like the elderly. After death, you seem to ascend up in the afterlife, reaching out towards the light as you and your partner say goodbye while parting their own way, having lived that amazing journey with someone else. This game had brought so many feelings in such a short amount of time and its truly one of the best games i have ever played. This game requires no dialogue to understand the story which is mind blowing because, you make your own journey in this game, just how you make your own story in your life, not in the game, real real life, your journey from being a juvenile to an elderly and the amazing memories you create, while overcoming challenges and obstacles that are being thrown at you are relatable in this game and in life. What i have learnt from this game is that it doesn't matter what happens to you, e,g, lose your powers throughout your journey, because you will lose your powers anyway during death, but the most beautiful thing about it is that you will regain them back in the afterlife and reunite with your partner once more. 100/10 Best game ever
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: 10000000/10. Walking simulator so beautiful you'll be crying at the end.I fell in love with this game back when it was released on the PS3, and I still love it all these years later. It's short, sweet, and poignant. Whether you're a seasoned white cloak or a first-time red cloak, the journey will always be a joy.

_childDocuments_.review: Journey isn't just a game, it's an experience. _childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: If you are looking for a challenging game, this is not it. This is not a game, this is an experience. You will meet companions and have a moving unspoken story. This game is like a living piece of art. I, as I was journeying, met companions, and then got separated from them. I was knocked down, got lost, had some setbacks, and felt like giving up at some points, but I kept on persevering. This is a game everyone should play. You won't regret it. It is short and sweet, which in my eyes is a bonus, but if you are looking for a long story then you, again, are looking in the wrong place. The story is simplistic, but beautiful and moving in a way. All this to say, buy this game, play this game, and start your journey.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: There's not one single word that could describe Journey. Amazing, fulfilling, mysterious, so many words could describe your experience with Journey. So if you're curious about it, play it. It's a very calming experience. Maybe I'll see you on your journey sometime.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: All I can say is WOW. This game is truly amazing, a piece of art. The adventure we partake in, is nothing compared to the graphics and sound design... _childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: What a wholesome game.You might not be able to start the game with a friend (as a party) but you might make some on your journey. In fact you can meet several companions before you are even ready for it. So did I. I wasn't sure what's the deal with the rest of hooded weirdos and why they would disappear in the wind until one of them really actively tried to help me with very high jump. And then... I had to alt tab to confirm... you can meet OTHER PLAYERS in game! You don't know their names and there's no way to talk to them (except short or long beeps but obv I knew no universal codes as what can each mean) and yet... you find yourself caring for this newly discovered friend, looking up if you fall if at least they made it, looking back when you find a safe place to stand... and journey stops being about finding the end but making sure you both get to see it.Thank you for your kindness each of you who helped me and the one who made it to the end!First run thru takes about 2 hours and not knowing what to expect while finding out it's better not to stop I'd say it's a good thing. But what do you know I only got 3 achievements and I bet that's where remaining 22 hours are at >:DIf you look at store page, art style, tags etc and think you might like it, you'll probably give it 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: Journey is one of my all-time favorite games, and for good reason. It captures a sense of wonder with a simple yet profound story that draws you in without a single word spoken. The stunning visuals and mesmerizing landscapes feel alive, while the ethereal soundtrack perfectly complements the emotional depth of the experience.The beauty of Journey lies in its ability to evoke powerful emotions through minimalistic gameplay and design. Each step feels purposeful, and the multiplayer component adds an unexpected layer of connection without saying a word. Whether you're gliding across sand dunes or ascending the mountain in the final moments, the game's atmosphere leaves an indelible mark.It's a short experience, but one that stays with you long after it's over. Journey is more than just a game—it's an unforgettable experience.

_childDocuments_.review: JourneyPositives:+ Beautiful and artistic+ Very atmospheric+ Nice sound and fantastic music+ Make you reflect about life+ When you fly or slide+ When there is some variation+ The creatures and travelers you meetNegatives:- Should have had more variation in landscapes and things too see- You walk a bit too much (there should have been more flying or sliding)- The few places where you must go a long way around if you're unlucky when jumping- Some parts are too cloudy and foggy- Some of the visual effects are a bit too much- Only 2 hours longI hoped this game was as fantastic as my favorite games in the genre, but to my surprise it was not.Dont get me wrong, the game is good, but its not fantastic. _childDocuments_.review: Can't believe now it's 2024 and it's still one of my favorite games to relax - breathtaking graphics, easy controls, interaction with other players and my favorite sounds effects (similar to thatgamecompany's Flower game). Most importantly, the philosophical thoughts on life. There is so much to discover, to admire, to enjoy and to love, while I'm flying my way to the destination as a white robe. Life is a journey and every chapter is uniquely charming in its own way. Thanks to those who joined my journey at various points of each chapters, and those who walked with me till the every end.

_childDocuments_.review: Buy it when it's on sale. It's only ~1.5h of content but it's definitely GREAT content. _childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: Journey while short and simple, pans out to be one of the most beautiful games you could possibly add to your library. It displays audibly and visually how video games can be experienced as an art form. Looking deeper, it allows its players to experience the game with a global communication. _childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start off by saying that Journey has been one of my all-time favorite games since I first played it back on the PS3. It's a travesty that such a sloppy port has dampened the experience of this beautiful, awe inspiring piece of art. Although the pace is not for everyone, this easy-going ambient adventure is one I will treasure for years and I implore anyone who enjoys this type of zen game to pick it up... on the playstation.Though I heard musical cues were broken, I haven't experienced that except maybe once in the very beginning of the game and it was more like a brief hiccup in the audio files. However, I've experienced far worse and jarring bugs that disrupt my nostalgia chasing time in Journey. It's easy to tell that very little- if any- work went into porting this over. Which that fact in and of itself is a slap in the face to the developers who worked so hard on it. To tarnish this gem of a game with such lackluster effort really is something to be ashamed of.My character wigs out a bit in the beginning- jittering as the camera struggles to find its place- the camera of which is almost perpetually off-center and giving me a slight right lean when trailing through the sand dunes or walking through the gates to the next level of the zone. But perhaps the most disgusting thing to me about this port is that it has determined my computer can only handle MEDIUM settings... from a PS3 port. Let me clarify here:The Recommendations:- 64-bit (check...)- Windows 7 (I have Windows 10)- Intel Core i3 (I have a 9th gen i7)- 4GB of RAM (I have 32...)- NVIDIA GTS 450 (I have an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2070)As you can see, I clearly meet FAR beyond the requirements here, and yet if I so much as dream of upping the graphics on the game, it decides it can't handle it. The frames (even at medium recommended settings) get extremely choppy during certain scenes and this simply should not be. This game is NOT optimized by any means and what you remember it looking like on the PS3 will only tarnish your memory upon booting it up on your PC. On a rig that FAR outdoes what the PS3 once was, this game looks as if it were early PS2 graphics. There's really no reason for this. Also upon attempting to up my graphics it cuts out the backdrop of cutscenes, showing it as a black empty abyss and completely ruining the atmosphere.Now, I did complete this game again on PC from start to finish and it is PLAYABLE. But it's incredibly disappointing and lackluster to my vivid memory of the original release. As an avid fan and someone who has played hours upon hours of this game over the years just to relive the wonderful experience, I'm begging whoever is responsible for fixing and polishing the port.PLEASE fix this game. It deserves to make as deep an impact on new players as much as it should the nostalgia chasing veterans. If these problems are addressed I will change my review- it is with a heavy heart that I leave it on a thumbs down when I love this game so much- but this sloppy port doesn't do a fragment of justice to the original work. Please, Annapurna. Fix this.

_childDocuments_.review: one of the best ambience games I have ever played in my life. I have been waiting for a pc release ever since I played the demo on ps3 a long time ago. Highly recommended with headphones on. This is not a game you dash through, because it's not hard if you want to finish it, you can do in 2hours. In this game you need to relax, get yourself a controller, sit back and enjoy every corner the game offers you!
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: My Experience was immaculate. I walked through the sand. I walked through the snow. all of it was beautiful. I ran into a fellow along the way, something I didn't think was possible in this game till now. We ran along side by side, learning of each others backgrounds and history, his name was Jim. He had a wife and kids, and was doing well in life. One day he had an off day and was fired from his job, the reason was that he was seen tripping a homeless woman. As he was on his way home he was furious, and decided to do another unlawful deed when he was suddenly transported to here, what he thinks to be for his crimes. While I enjoyed his company, I realized what a fool I was to trust him and I went along to sled down with him. When he flew past me, he had swung out his arm and stole my wallet, after that he gained massive amounts of speed and I never saw him again. As I felt hopeless with nothing to do, I had met another fellow by the name of Bob. We rarely spoke to each other at first, but quickly realized what danger we were in. In the end we became friends, and even closer brethren. No matter what we were here for, we realize the place we were transported to, this journey, will change you for the better. Even if you are a bad person like Jim, you will find peace within yourself like this game brought me and Bob. Still missing my wallet though.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: Found someone at the start of the game, stayed by each other, never left ones side. 2 hours of pure connection.Credits rolled, life crumbled before me, thought id never see my new friend again. A part of me had been lost.Saw the "people met" section of the credits and it was one name, his name. It was only then i felt true happiness.It was some 30 year old Japanese bloke. Still love him though
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best adventure game I have played. If you are looking for a game to enjoy and relax, this game is a very beautiful game. The total runtime of this game is just right with optimal amount of stages for you to complete. Truly an art! However, if you like fast paced game. This might not be for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing game. The perfect combination between music and gameplay. The soundtrack from Austin Wintory is out of this world.I played it in Playstation 3 many years ago and I was amazed. How this game without a clear story and with a character without a name and without voice can drive to your tears.At the end, when your character reaches the end of the pilgrimage I was completely moved. You encounter some characters like yourself along the way. At the end I understood that there were other players playing at the same time like a multiplayer game. Thats a nice touch, I dont know if it was the same way in the PS3. This is a must have experience. The only indy game that is between my top favourites games of all time.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: one of the most important games of the last decade imo.the multiplayer component is truly one of the best choices they could've made, no game has ever made me feel so attached to a complete stranger.can't really put into words how much this one means to me and I don't think will ever be replicated again
_childDocuments_.name: Journey
