_childDocuments_.review: First time I played Journey was on the PS3 when it was first released. Enjoyed it so much it easily became one of my, like, top 5 video games of all time. It's been quite a while since then and I simply remembered it as a ''very good game I remember loving'', but started wondering if it's still worthy of the ''top of all time'' list. I wasn't going to buy it for PC because honestly why would I if I already have it lmao BUT I am lucky enough to have friends who hate having money and got it as a gift. Of course I played it and all I have to say is yes, it very much deserves a place on the top of all times list. 2012 me had a good taste in gayms after all.god the snow part still gets me every time, especially when playing with people who also try to stick together and make it super sad :''') Which is really interesting because Journey doesn't have chat or much ways of interacting with the surrounding and players. _childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: It's funny. I like this and I like Sky, but I have little patience for the Journey-likes that have come out since. You know, the linear, level-based puzzle platformers with an "emotional" story told through silent cutscenes (and in some cases, diaries scattered around the levels) and an "epic" and "emotional" soundtracks definitely not composed by Austin Wintory.Yeah, I'm not a fan of this type of game. I avoid them like the plague unless they have something interesting to show for (e.g. Jusant with its rather fun climbing mechanic and compelling world building). Journey (and by extension its little sibling Sky), however, stands out for not overstating its welcome and having a multiplayer mechanic that ties to that """emotional""" storytelling. That and flying around is actually rather fun.This is definitely one of those games everyone should play at least once. Its gimmick is a rather good implementation of online multiplayer and yes, it's a gorgeous game. Can't say I love it for spawning a deluge of copycats that don't come close to to it, but alas.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely beautiful. Beautiful graphic, amazing gameplay and more. At one point it even gets a tiny bit scary. Also your stealth is being tested and more. And you can also meet new friends along the way! I met one person and we were together for the entire journey. And now we're friends here on steam :DSo yeah, this game is absolutely awesome and I would recommend it to everyone to at least give this game a chance!
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: This just goes to show how a game can be really thoroughly enjoyable, even if it is only 2 hours long, has no dialogue and has no clearly defined story. It is just you, jumping, navigating, flying through your environs, with a beautiful soundtrack.NB: you need to play with Vsync on or you seem to get crashed at the "underwater monster corridor".
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so beautiful and haunting!! I found it very interesting from a social/psychological standpoint which is why I initially picked it up, but it's so much more than that. It's very evocative and it made me feel very alone but also very connected to others at once, and most of all very human :)
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: This game is such a unique experience. No NPC's, no character names, no quests, just shown a mountain top and you're off on your Journey. It was so interesting exploring the game and finding out things I could interact with by chiming some notes. Eventually I managed to run into another person and the game just felt so much bigger, just randomly running into someone like this and continuing your adventure felt so genuine. Your only form of communication is just chiming out little notes as well, it felt so wholesome to see something really spectacular(which you will find a lot of in this game) and watch my partner burst out in excited chimes like "DID YOU SEE THAT?!".Somehow they're able to pack such a genuine and spiritual experience into just two hours through amazing level design, incredible music, and the ability to share this all with a random traveller you meet along the way. Unfortunately I wasn't able to finish the game with anyone as they all seemed to leave during this one part in the snowy area after not being able to make it a couple times. Regardless I felt myself smiling through the whole thing and really enjoyed my time in the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: Hello, my friend in America (you may be in America, but I'm not sure. I wrote China on the ground first, but you crossed it. I wrote US again). I am the white robe that I painted with you in the snow mountain at 11 a.m. Beijing time on May 12, 2022. You wrote me the contact information many times, but I still didn't understand it. I deeply regret this. I hope you can see me. I think we will become good friends with each other if we can.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: An incredible metaphor for life. Visually amazing (thanks to the lighting), great sound design and a perfect musical score. Its themes and message about the "journey" through life are rarely done so perfectly in a video game. Even though it's only two hours or so it will resonate with the majority of players and they will think about the game for weeks (I know I will).

_childDocuments_.review: I've never publicly made a review or a recommendation of any game before, really, but with Journey it's a bit of a different story.I won't go into too much detail here, because fundamentally I believe Journey to be a piece of art you yourself have to experience. This wordless story, a metaphor that will undoubtedly leave a personal impact on every single individual who plays this game, is beautiful. No matter how big or small the emotion, the things this game is able to evoke is stunning. From childlike wonder, to joy and excitement, calm from beautiful scenery, anxiety and confusion... _childDocuments_.review: Journey is nothing less than visual poetry. From opening on rolling dunes and wind-swept stones, to the closing of a golden star, arcing through the night sky, this game had me holding my breath. Paired with a random other player with no way to communicate but your chime-like singing, you forge a bond with this unknown traveler as you explore the beautiful ruins, filled with magic scarfs and old stones. My first playthrough took 2 hours, and that was with me jerking my companion around to explore every ruin on the horizon's edge, and stopping for a potty break. The levels are linear, but wide enough to allow for progression at your own pace.((Note: I received this game as a gift for Christmas, but having played it would highly recommend anyone picking it up when it goes on sale. Heck, if I get as much enjoyment out of a second playthrough as I did the first, I'd say full price - $15 - is a bargain.))

_childDocuments_.review: It’s… an experience more than anything. The game itself is a walking simulator where you press forward. There is light platforming, some timing for a section or two, and some collection but overall, it’s not the focus. The game is really about moving forward, absorbing the world, and trying to piece together the story while pretty music plays in the background. It’s more about experiencing emotions instead of comprehending a story which is either going to work for some folks or not work for some folks. It was… OK for me as the story it does have is pretty simple. Although, even without the backstory presented in the world, you can understand that there’s a character going on a journey through a strange world with struggles and guidance along the way. The visuals and the music itself are really good so it’s just going to come down to if you get into it or not.The co-op mechanic is fantastic and the way it melds two players together who mostly just want to help each other in this journey without a single word is great. Hats off to that.

_childDocuments_.review: Very boring game. I have no idea why this game gets such high reviews. It's a walking simulator. You spend 90 to 120 minutes pressing W. There is a flying mechanic where you can glide for a bit with red cloth throughout the game. It doesn't help much because it runs out quickly. There is also a button that emits a chime sound. I kept trying to use it at various places to try to figure out what it does, but never discovered any use for it. I kept hoping some plot would emerge or the little bits of content in the game would be revealed to have some meaning. There are these stones throughout the world that I was expecting might be revealed to be gravestones, but that question is never answered. There is also a larger version of your character dressed in white that you see very briefly in cut scenes. It's never revealed who that is either.This feels like an unfinished game. It's as though it's just flat out missing entire mechanics or pieces of story. I enjoyed the art style. The music was okay. It wasn't great music, but it wasn't out of place either. I never encountered any bugs or crashes, so it's not unfinished in that sense. It just feels like the developers realized they couldn't meet their deadline, so they wrapped it up with what they had. Not worth the time or money.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: At the time of writing this, it is currently June 15th 2020 at 5:15 PM, 7 minutes after the completion of my play through of this game.Let me tell you a story, dear reader, a short one, don't worry.I first saw this game on Steam's news page, and was instantly hit with a wave of nostalgia, having played a small portion of this game on the Play Station 3, I was happy to buy this game in order to live some of the joys of my childhood. I booted up the game thinking it'd be a simple console port, with the same graphics, same look... I could have never been more wrong. This game isn't just a console port, it's far from that, Journey is a beautiful game that blew my eyes away, gave them back to me, and then blew them away a second time. The graphics are simply stunning, and as a person who hasn't dusted their computer out in a couple months, i was running on the low end settings. That's saying something!The subtle music, the drifting winds, the calm serene atmosphere... all of it comes together into one to create this masterpiece of a game, this game isn't just something you look at or compete in, it's an experience. Exploration is awarded, and although it does do a slight bit of hand holding at the start, you're allowed to freely explore the majority of the world show to you. It's everything that my inner childhood was expecting, and so much more.A feature that I didn't know about before hand is the almost seamless transition into multiplayer that this game has, you'll be surfing the sands on your own, and then suddenly there's another person waiting for you at the next checkpoint, you each get to beep at each other and help the other through the game bit by bit, I walked through the final passage with a companion of my own, of which I stuck with thick and thin. We ran, we flew, and we surfed, the both of us having a completely new experience, just because the other were there to play too. There's no chat, no names, nothing, the only form of communication is the soft beeping of the other player. Anybody that you meet on the journey you take is unknown to you until you finish, where they are finally shown to you at the very end.This game is truly memorable to me, and will always have a deep place in my heart. It's worth the price, and so much more. It deserves the recognition, and it deserves all of the love that me and the fans of this community give it. I hope that i've helped give a good view of the game, and maybe even persuaded a few of you to buy it for yourself. Come join the fun! Maybe we'll meet each other in our travels, who knows! Have a pleasant evening folks, and happy surfing!
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: A metaphor for living, and for living with others. Reincarnation is an important part of it, but that could also be seen as a model of what it means to be old or young. You don't get that if you only play it once.The thing about multiple runs is that the early runs are mostly about exploring and learning, the later runs are really about helping the less experienced. All of which is like being young and being old, respectively. The middle runs are a mix of purposes.The value of the game is really in the relationships you have with utter strangers who just appear in your game (one at a time). You'd expect that some would be mean to you and out for themselves (as in life), but that generally doesn't happen. It has the effect of restoring your faith in humanity, and that's really the point. The game doesn't so much assert or impose this. It comes from fellow wayfarers, other actual human beings on this Earth now.The destination of the journey itself is death, but along the way there is beauty, fear, companionship, failed companionship, agreement, disagreement, opportunity, missed opportunity, frustration, fulfillment, bleakness, confusion, certainty, splendor, exhilaration, adversity, and achievement. Much like life itself.

_childDocuments_.review: "Journey" is a profoundly magical experience.I jumped into the game not knowing what to expect.  I knew the gameplay was similar to that of "Flower", which I had played before, and I did glimpse in the discussions that one could meet other travellers (players) on the way, but apart from that I had no idea what "Journey" was about.The simplicity and the alien feel of the game world is impressive.  But above all I was awestruck by the interaction with other players.  There is something extraordinary about meeting a stranger in this unfamiliar world and to then ally yourself to them in the common purpose of reaching the end of the journey set out before you.  This is done without clear language to communicate with (no voice server or texting).  All you have are chirp sounds, an accompanying visual sign (acting as a form of identification) and your movements to convey thoughts and feelings, wonder and appreciation, a warning or encouragement, a "Come over here!" or "Look, I found a symbol!"  I found that having this basic system is actually enough; it fits with the simplicity of the world around you."Journey" reminds us that there are others on this trek through life.  We are all on this same road that we have to figure out as we go.  There may be wonders and joys along the way.  Sometimes the road is filled with dangers and we may experience set backs.  But in the end we have a common goal: reaching or realising the destination, becoming the person we want to be, finding meaning in struggle, testing our resolve, and very importantly, sharing this experience with others, helping them or getting help ourselves, or simply just enjoying good company.  It seems a journey worth taking. In the end this journey is what it all comes down to.I loved the experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I have, in my life, been perturbed by video games. I have been shocked, excited, and certainly addicted. But there is no game that has quite brought the depth of feeling to me that Journey did. I had never been moved. I say had because in two hours, Journey completely broke me. I started skeptical of the game, not believing that it could possibly live up to its hype. The confusing control scheme and lack of plot left me feeling directionless. But some stellar level design pointed the way. It was good, but not great. And then, after a brief meditation, I got up, and there was someone standing next to me. I made a sound. They responded. And immediately I understood.I proceeded through the game. I lost some companions - one literally vaporised in front of me. One I was separated from by a great beast. And near the end, I surmounted what seemed to be the final hurdle with a companion, only to have my heart torn from my chest as they fell off the mountain below. I could not fetch them. I must not.And as the game ended in a great swell, I found, on the final screen, that there were two more companions I had been sharing my journey with along the way. I had never seen them. I had never talked to them. I did not even know that they existed. But, for a brief moment, they and I had been sharing an experience across cyberspace, wordlessly. Alone but together. Separated but connected. This was, I will confess, the moment for some tears.I cannot recommend this game enough. It is an astonishing accomplishment.Addendum: I still do not understand exactly what the control scheme was. I understand which buttons I pressed to make noises, but I don't understand precisely what they did. That in itself is a testimony of the utmost power to how profoundly intuitive and gripping this game is. Bravo.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't have many hours on the Steam edition of this, but upon release on PS3, and then the remaster on PS4, I have logged several thousand hours on this game. The flow of this game allows for hours of nothing but pure bliss and ecstasy from the breathtaking visual aspect, to the absolutely wonderful musical score by Austin Wintory. The music has become a guilty pleasure, and would just love to wonder if there ever was more music for the game that never made the final cut.Journey is an absolutely wonderful game that tells a simple tale of how technological advancement can cause war between to factions among the same race. The game has you traveling through an arid desert as you slowly come to find out that the entire sand used to be open fields and the living cloth, that of which makes up your scarf, used to grow in the open. Something wonderful about the game is it shows how quickly the civilization had fallen due to their greed towards trying to be on top and instead it ended up costing these people, so to speak, to be killed by their own very creations. The constant visions that you are shown are the elders, the white-cloaks, trying to convey the message down to you, the red-cloak, the error in their ways in hopes that you (all players)can possibly fix the damages that they caused their world.Probably the best part of this game's co-op experience is you cannot have anyone join on you, and you do not know who you play with until the end of the game. Mind you, it can possibly be multiple people, because it's almost a bit like a drop in/drop out co-op but it's completely randomized at just about any point of any level. it's absolutely hysterical to play and it is absolutely a blast to constantly just roam about with new players or long-time players. The game never loses its touch, in my personal opinion, but I advise you give the game a chance in case it is good for you too.

_childDocuments_.review: Somehow, without a single word, Journey provided the most profoundly emotional gaming experience of my life. I went in about as blind as I could for a game that came out over a decade ago, and that's absolutely the way the first play through should be. I found this to be a game where I often forgot I had a controller in my hands, multiple times IRL distractions broke my concentration and made me realize I was just witnessing the game with my jaw dropped, mouth open. As my final companion and I pushed through the last act, I realized I was actually crying. Just weeping as I pushed the joystick forward. There was a shocking level of catharsis for me, and I absolutely never expected that from this experience. It's not a game for everyone, but it was absolutely the game for me. My next play-through (once I've had time to process and reflect - which probably sounds so incredibly dumb if this game doesn't hit you the way it did me) will definitely be cozied up in a dark room with good headphones and no distractions. I rarely finish a game and immediately want to jump back in, but I'm really genuinely excited to explore this world again.

_childDocuments_.review: Maybe, just maybe, my favourite video game ever.I can comfortably and confidently recommend this to literally anyone. If you have any concerns about whether this is for you, even if you normally don't like or play video games - lay those concerns to rest for this game. It can be experienced  by just about any demographic I can think of - I think the target audience must have just been "humanity" or something. I'm not a bucket list or "100 games every person should play before they die" kind of person, but this is one of those rare works that I really feel like everyone who has a chance should experience it.Only know that it's short, you're getting an experience you can complete in around 2-5 hours. It's also profound, and definitely should not be spoiled. Go in as blindly as possible (but not deaf, if it can be avoided! The audio experience here is as touching as the visual one).There are a lot of imitators and other games that try to do the "video games as art" thing by being either very on the nose about it, or just super duper abstract. Journey is much more subtle and sophisticated than a lot of other games trying to do what it does, and while I've played and enjoyed some of the things released since, it's actually difficult to capture in words how much more this one manages to draw you in. A lot of the emotion comes directly from the game experience, not from set-dressing trying to tell you to "feel" a certain way before getting back to the gameplay. The game gives you a title card - "Journey" and then no further written, spoken, or sung dialogue right up until the credits. Even if you haven't like a lot of the other sorts of things of this nature, I'd still suggest you give Journey a try.The PC port is ever-so-slightly more clunky than the original PlayStation3 release, so if you can play it on a PS3 or newer then go out of your way to do that. But for those who don't have access to a PlayStation system, the PC port is perfectly acceptable - just with some very slightly clunkier integration of the (ABSOLUTELY INCREDIBLE) soundtrack by Austin Wintory. The choppier bits aren't really noticeable unless you're very familiar with the original.I'd also recommend this educationally as a study on story structure for anyone interested - whether that's a highschool student trying to pass their short story exam or someone who wants to get into writing professionally. It's the most distilled version of the "12 stages of the Hero's Journey" you'll ever find.Genuinely a remarkable title. I cannot recommended it enough. Absolutely worth the asking price, stop reading reviews and just purchase it if you haven't already.

_childDocuments_.review: To my friends Zoloft and Jobodo,I was excited to start my important Journey by myself. Proud and fearless. I start confidently repairing the giant bridge and see someone else dashing across it. Letting me do all the heavy lifting! Eventually they plopped down to help. Zoloft chirped at me, I chirped back and, eventually, I begrudgingly made my way with them, soaring across the bridge. Somewhere along the way Zoloft left on a different path and I ran into Jobodo. After being wary and annoyed of strangers I first tried to lose you in the desert. No dice. Looks like we were stuck together. I am so happy glad we were. You helped me discover, helped me hide, helped me learn to trust. We laughed, sang, surfed, got gobbled by stone dragons, cowered in fear, but persevered all the same. When the snow came and the dragons returned to blast your scarf into pieces TWICE I was so scared I would lose you. Watching you solemnly and silently press forward, tiny tail in tow, to meet back up to me filled me with so many emotions. I was relived, proud, scared, and protective. We went as far as we could, me trying to keep you warm with my scarf as best I could. Eventually it was too much. Our chirps faded, scarves shriveled, and our bodies succumbed to the cold. Suddenly, I rise vibrant as the sun, and to my absolute delight you are still there with me! You were soaring and filled with life! I didn't have to keep you warm any longer. You left me in the dust as I tried to keep up with you as we flew higher and higher, riding the backs of so many of the creatures we saved together. Such a beautiful sight! As we ascended to the top, our final steps all that remain in front of us, I can't help but think how lucky I was to have shared this experience with you. Our silhouettes slowly fade into one, and then diverge once more. Kindred and enriched spirits who shared a wondrous experience and who now must go their separate ways to help and improve others' journey's.What a game. So happy to end 2020 on this delightful little high note after so many ♥♥♥♥♥♥ lows.I will always cherish this experience and never forget you Jobodo (or you Zoloft...). I hope our paths cross again.

_childDocuments_.review: The wheel in the sky keeps on turning. I don't know where I'll be tomorrow.Isn't that the truth. This is the type of game I never really expected to pick up and play....and well, lets get down to it.First off this is less of a game and more of art. It delivers a message more than wows you with extreme gameplay. So be ready and know what you are going into....or it won't last long on your screen. Art gaming isn't necessary bad (and in the case if Journey, it helps). It just makes the game a little more niche. But that brings about a big problem with it: being an art game, you probably won't get much more than one play out of it...maybe more if you really want to revisit. So to put it bluntly:You know I still love you, though we touched and went our separate ways.I got this on sale for a little less than $6, and i really recommend you do the same if you want to pick it up. Really this would be the perfect rental game, if that option was possible...because you will probably get about an hour to an hour and 1/2 out of it in one sitting, and then move on for a while. It doesn't feel like it drags on really, but it will be a one sitting game.The mountains we have climbed to get this far....On my journey, I actually ran into a player that helped me through about 85% of the game...which was interesting. It was weird seeing the screen name of the person that went with me during the credits...especially when we can't message each other. I wasn't sure if it was a real player or some crazy good AI. Sadly if you don't encounter anyone else....this will probably be more of a let down trying to figure out what you are supposed to do.But if you are in the right mindset for it...it will be an amazing experience. Just don't swallow the "I got so emotional" stuff...its really not that over the top like that. And in the end:Don't stop believin', hold on to that feeling.Streetlights, people......

_childDocuments_.review: Journey is one of those games that can't be defined by a review but hopefully, this will suffice. Even though the game is a walking simulator of sorts it happens to say a lot without saying anything at all. Even from the very first moments of the game, you'll be able to see the end in sight. I think everyone's experience with Journey will differ from what you take away from the game. The impression I got was of going into a world that you didn't know and discovering finally who you were. Ultimately you complete your quest and are finally able to pass on to a higher plane of existence. Again everyone's interpretations will be different and mine as well the more times I play it. Journey is an open metaphor most people can on some level relate to. Even if you don't relate to the story the visuals in Journey at times are just stunning. Some scenes almost feeling like you could've ripped them out of an art piece. The only problem I had with the game is that it's really short at about 1.5 hrs. On the other side of the coin that's probably the strongest aspect of the game since it only says whats necessary. One of the most enjoyable aspects of the game is joining someone else in their Journey. There's an odd dynamic when you try to converse with another player since you can't directly communicate with them. The only thing you have is little chirps and jumps to communicate some kind of message. I've never been so amazed but a simple mechanic before but this is by far is my favorite. Journey is an amazing game but the price of $15 is fairly steep for the length. I'd highly recommend picking this game up during a sale if possible. Hopefully, if you're reading this you'll discover your own Journey while playing. 85/100

_childDocuments_.review: I'd like to tell a story about friendship—a friendship that will never reveal a true identity...I decided to launch Journey a week after my last play to get that achievement. And I thought, since I launched it again, why not try to get all of the achievements? They are quite easy to get, and there are plenty of tutorials. I already had unlocked a lot of them by just playing the game 3-4 times, but I still hadn't found a lot of secrets.So I launched it, went to the first story location with those carpet bridges. My first goal was to cross them, but one shouldn't be activated. I went straight for the last two and was afraid to meet anyone so that no one would ruin this achievement... but after the second bridge activation cutscene... boy oh boy, who I met!It was a full white person, with a little longer scarf than I had, and this guy was a freaking legend!(Because of his outfit, I figured that he already did what I was only going to.)In an instant, he understood what my goal was. He helped me climb up to the bridge, and...That's where our great journey begins!On each level, he showed me where all the walls, scarf letters, and secrets that I missed were located: the secret flower, the mysterious creature, and more. It's amazing how, in a game that only has a little song for engaging, we understood each other perfectly.My level of pure joy and excitement was off the charts. We helped each other the whole trip. A couple of times, he missed some letters, and I showed them to him, which added a little more of a teamwork feeling.A couple of times, he sat, and I figured that he wanted to make another achievement (which I already had at that time). Maybe he was hunting this achievement too, I don't know.But the funny thing is that I forgot which button to use, so I was furiously tapping every button on my keyboard, but NONE of them worked, and I don't know why!!! I mean, COME ON!!!Only two levels later, where for the first time you're hiding from the strong wind, it finally worked! :)There were a couple of "scary moments" when he was attacked by those things, and the most scary episode was when he was blown down by that strong wind in a staircase, but he quickly met me next to the next entrance.I think he was hunting some rare achievements too because at some point (a couple of times) he was spamming the "song" button like crazy and running around, the same way I did when I got that last "letter," "wall," or that mysterious creature achievement, so I think we definitely helped each other.And after all of this walking, sliding, flying, climbing, losing and finding each other, dying and resurrecting... when the only thing left was to walk into that mountain peak light, we sat for the last time for about half a minute in silence just to enjoy and to remember all this journey that we had, because we both knew that we would never meet here again.I was fully convinced that after the end credits, I would write down a nickname, to find and thank this person (doesn't matter if it is a guy or a girl, old or young person) for the help and for this journey that we walked together, from the very start to the finish.I waited for the end credits, then the black screen before the list of people you met, and finally...I saw my desktop wallpaper... (which is my profile picture)the game had crashed, leaving me with a bunch of mixed feelings and experiences.I didn't know if it was better this way or if I had lost an opportunity to meet someone interesting. I was a little confused if I can say so :)But what I knew for sure was that it was a great experience, and I loved it.I launched the game one more time, chose a white cloth, and walked a little in that hub location.After that, I didn't launch it anymore.Sure, I will do it at some point, but for now, I think it is not necessary.And that is my little story of a great Journey.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't really know where to begin with this.This game is great and it should rather be seen as an experience rather than a game actually. _childDocuments_.review: A really nice and short journey to experience in one sitting. You will meet random people through your travels ( you can only have 1 companion at once; if he leaves, another should quickly take his place ).The point is to travel with strangers, having just a chime to communicate. You can play alone or with a friend but it requires specific steps that you can find in guides.You quickly form a bond with your newly met companion and you can help each other reach the end. It is truly heartbreaking to lose your companion or say goodbye... if you finish the game you can see who you've travelled with and many people take this opportunity to thank their companions on the steam forums.But that's also the problem : in my first playthrough I only got great people so I was really enjoying the game. But on my other playthrough I encountered either annoying people or people that would leave after 5mins. If you're unlucky and you don't get the great people, it could really give you a bad impression instead of the good one =/I think the game's length is fine for this type of game but too short for the price, I would recommend waiting for sales. ~2 hours for the first playthrough + you can replay it to try and get all the collectibles and robe embroideries ( you get a new line on your robe everytime you finish the game, up to 3 times ). You start in a desert and are trying to reach the top of a mountain you can see in the distance. While you try to reach it, you will get visions showing you this world's past. The story is a bit vague but you get the gist of it and there are paintings scattered in the levels that give you other clues to what happened. You have two actions : chime and fly. Chime is used to communicate with other players and to activate pieces of cloth that allow you to progress in the world or you can use them to recharge your flying power. Fly allows you to reach places; you need "charges" to fly, those charges are represented with a scarf that glows and everytime you use a charge, a piece of your scarf stops glowing and you have to recharge it to use it again. You can make your scarf longer and therefore be able to fly longer too by collecting symbols throughout the game. You can also recharge your scarf just by standing next to another player, which is really useful.When you finish the game, you are brought back to the beginning and gain a line of embroidery on your robe, you can have up to 3. When you collect all symbols, you can choose to wear a white robe which starts with a longer scarf and said scarf recharges by itself when you touch the ground; you can't play with 1st playthrough players when you have the white robe.The gameplay is really smooth and it's pleasing to go from cloth to cloth, using your chime and flying to rise higher and higher. ~4 hours to get all achievements depending on your luck because there's an achievement where you need to complete most of the game with the same player ( you can also just select the last chapter and finish it with someone =P the game will consider that you've played the full game together ) + you have to sit and do nothing for 20s with another player.You have collectibles but you absolutely can get them in several playthroughs and there's a "chapter select" option to quickly go where you're missing something.You also have an achievement where you need to play again after 1 week without touching the game; but as usual with this kind of achievement, you can just change your computer's clock if you don't want to wait.

_childDocuments_.review: Not the game I expected, but I was pleasantly surprised nevertheless. True to its title, it's about the Journey and not the destination, so while the game requires you to solve puzzles, try not to blaze on through or you will miss things. _childDocuments_.review: I wanted to write this review for a while now but somehow never did. This doesn't make a lot of sense taking into account the impact this game had on me. I've never had this kind of experience with a game before and it's truly unique.That said, let's go from the start: I discovered Journey back in December 2020 and when I bought this game I didn't know anything about it. The only thing I've heard was that it's supposed to be beautiful. I haven't done any more research on it beforehand and when this game was released in 2012 I haven't been that much into gaming yet. So it was basically a blind purchase. In retrospective, one of the best decisions ever.In Journey you go (surprise!) on a journey, travelling towards a mountain far away in the distance. It is a beautiful and very emotional game, that's the least I can tell you without spoiling anything. If you're interested in those kind of games buy it and don't do any further research. It must be said, though, you might need to play Journey more than once in order to grasp the concept and see what makes this game so special. Plus, stick to it till the end, don't skip the credits! Reading some of the reviews here, I feel like that's what some people overlooked and it makes me sad to know that they might have missed out on an amazing experience. I also recommend to play Journey in one sitting, it probably won't take much longer than two hours.Journey brought me to tears, made me laugh and feel happy and vulnerable at the same time. It evoked feelings of loneliness, warmth and curiosity, in a way few games can. As by now, I've played almost 150 hours already which might seem nuts taking into consideration the length of a single playthrough. But I can tell you, this didn't make certain runs less memorable. Every playthrough stands on its own and some I will never forget.

These were quite irritating to me when I was aiming for leftover achievements.After I beat the game, I didn't actually think it was the end till the credits started rolling and I was left with a feeling of "That's it?" I think reading all the reviews of people speaking of having zen like experiences, and achieving higher levels of consciousness and whatnot raised my expectations waaaaay too high for this game. It's a decent game but the repetitive game play and anticlimactic ending wasn't as life changing as I thought it would be.Having read the overwhelming amount of positive reviews for this title I came in thinking that I would experience something deeply emotional and moving and yet I felt nothing. Apart from pretty landscapes and occasional interactions with strangers Journey really does not have anything going for it.I firmly believe this title is severly overrated. Because of the initial influx of positive reviews describing Journey as a thought-provoking masterpiece the more recent reviewers are unwilling to say anything but that for fear of being called shallow and basic. So let us be real here: this is a very mediocre game with almost no gameplay, shallow and vague story and short longevity.This game is absolutely underwhelming.I definitely do not recommend buying this title. _childDocuments_.review: Journey is an amazing game at non-verbal storytelling, not having any dialogue uttered over the game's 2 hr runtime and I think that's what makes the game work so well. It's a "Journey" and the contents of it can be left up to the player's interpretation. There's some guidance in the form of drawings and glyphs that appear in certain chapters but that's really it. I'm not really a fan of this amount of interpretation in a game's story but this game is an exception. It sets itself up to be a canvas for the player's mind to paint.On to the gameplay, it's simple and effective, only requiring two buttons to activate the character's abilities, and the rest is just walking. For a game entitled "Journey", they did a good job at making you feel like you're making this journey with your characters. The camera angles are wide, showing all of the land your person has to wade through. It adds to the immersion of the experience.Finally, my favorite feature of this game is the matchmaking system! I love how you can get into games with random strangers and they can become friends for the time you see them. You can add them after the game is done but I think the brevity of these tiny exchanges is enough. All in all, excellent game!P.S. If you like this game, check out ABZU. It's made by many people in the team who made this. Their 2nd title to come after this got shelved but if you want something to give you the wonderous fix, ABZU is your game.

_childDocuments_.review: I remember how stunned everyone was by thatgamecompany’s Journey back in 2012, when the game was released as a PS3 exclusive. I didn’t have that console and missed it entirely, but knowing Flower and flOw, I planned to definitely play the game some day. Well, now that the game is on PC that day has come. Except, it’s 8 years later. Does it matter?Journey is a very simple exploration-based title with simple controls and simple mechanics. You play as a mysterious robed traveler in a desert land trying to reach the summit of a mountain. You can chime, you can fly (depending on how much “magic” you have, shown on the scarf) and you can move around. The story is told via simple cutscenes that show a wordless story. And occasionally you may find yourself not alone but joined by a fellow traveler – an actual online player that you may travel with for a bit.It’s extremely simplistic and holds almost entirely on the game visual style and beautiful soundtrack. The colours, the shifting sands, the floating cloth creatures and great level design make this game work. With the online element being a really cute and surprisingly emotional cherry on top. And if you want something more, or dislike these kinds of ambient exploration titles, this might not be for you at all. But if you can lose yourself in these beautiful levels, this game still holds up and lasts exactly as long as it needs to, without outstaying the welcome.But we did get some beautiful games since 2012 that scratch the similar itch, yet might work for you even better. For me, for example, Abzû was a far more emotional experience. That game, developed by some of the same team from Journey, switched to the underwater setting and added some light educational elements to its world and to me that just made for a far more exciting experience. Perhaps, for you a more abstract experience of Journey will be more enjoyable, however.Whatever the case, though, it’s not an “either/or” question. Unlike Flower, which has aged a bit more poorly, Journey still feels amazing. And even though this new PC port isn’t as great as it could be (it can have bizarre hitching or audio glitches), it’s a wonderful way to experience this title. If you have a couple hours to lose yourself in a journey through a beautiful world, this game is definitely worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful and relaxing game from start to finish. The music is very good, and the game's story says a lot without saying much. It's definitely a great experience, however, my main problem with the game is the excessive crashes. Concerns for this PC Steam port date back to release at 2020, and according to the forums, not much has been done on thatgamecompany's part since then. Unfortunately, I can't recommend it because of it's playability on Steam specifically. Try a different port (console, maybe emu?). It's still worth a playthrough.Edit: Not all is lost, YMMV. After some research on the forums some say that turning V-sync on and lowering the graphics can help (it helped me, but it didn't help everyone). The forums were explaining that the problem lies in the frame rate. This is probably because the game was originally optimized for 60 fps (console) and the excessive fps of a high end rig causes artifacts, glitches, and crashing.

_childDocuments_.review: Journey is a 2012 adventure game, developed by thatgamecompany. The game was originally a Playstation exclusive, however 8 years later, the game finally saw a port to PC. And what a painful wait it was, as this game has been heralded as one of the greatest of all time. Multiple playthroughs later, I can certainly affirm that this is the case.Being dropped into a strange, magical desert land where not a single word of speech or dialogue is uttered, and not a single word of text is shown (minus the minimalistic, bare-bones title/pause menu), you take the role of a robed being, with one clear goal in view and in mind: Reach the summit of the looming mountain in the distance. And so your path across the landscape begins, surfing down sand dunes and riding alongside cloth creatures as you drift ever closer to your goal, as well as discovering the tale of the race that once inhabited it, and what befell them.At it's core, if one were to call this game a walking simulator, it is somewhat justified, as a majority of your time will be spent roaming the desert, exploring the buried temples and ruins, in a semi-linear fashion. Areas are self-contained with a few secrets, puzzles and achievements dotted around them, with them all eventually connecting to the next area.Graphics are clean with a cartoon-ish look, assisting the environmental storytelling in a grandiose fashion.Sound design is also on point as well, hearing the howling winds rustle by and shift the sand you're standing on, however I've noticed that the audio quality seems to take a dip in some segments, as if it was slightly bit-crushed. I believe a recent patch may have addressed that, however if it has then I am unable to tell the difference.And I haven't even touched up on what makes this game so special and what elevates it to an emotional level unlike most games I've played.At any point throughout the game, so long as you're online, you'll run into another robed figure just like you. That's not an NPC. That is an actual living breathing player, and fate has decided the two of you are to share the journey together.While you're unable to directly communicate with each other, only by small chirps and whistles, the way the game's experiences are structured push an amazing, undescribable feeling of companionship that stays with you throughout the game, as both of you face obstacles, overcome perils and push towards your mutually shared ultimate objective.The connection that is forged between the pair of you is something that lasts for ages, even well after you finish the game. And you only ever learn their name once it is all over, something I wish more games would do, as it helps break down the bias and misconceptions that people may have towards players. There are no arguments of differing opinions, no disagreeing on which path to take or how to take it.Just you, your partner, and the shared driven passion to attain your goal together.Austin Wintory's beautiful score also helps elevate the storytelling and important moments.Personal favourites from the OST are by far "Apothesis" and "I was Born For This", with a heavy emphasis on stringed instruments and a deep cello resonating all throughout.The game is certainly on the shorter side of a spectrum, with a normal playthrough only taking 2-3 hours at most, however secrets, achievements and even a sense of duty to guide the newer players through the land is what keeps me coming back every time, to assist others with their journey.Journey is also pretty well optimised and runs well, however I have noticed a problem where the game process decides to hog all of the CPU power available on your system, causing temperatures to rise quite a bit even though all that spare processing power isn't strictly needed. As such, I found it necessary to limit the game's amount of CPU power it can have, so my FPS does drop a bit because of this, however I would much prefer this than it conking out my fans because it's whirring all the time. I do hope they release a patch addressing this.That technical issue aside though, Journey is an extraordinarily unique game with an emotional and unforgettable way to connect players together as they travel through the land. What may seem like a stranger at first glance may very well end up being your best friend by the end of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Journey: Journey is one of the most beautiful games I've ever played. This game's artstyle is consistently jaw-dropping and had me taking ample screenshots of almost every single level. This game came out before but constantly reminded me of two games. Gris and Abzu. I think that this game has some of the best elements of both of those games, but doesn't have either of what makes both those games so so so incredible. For that reason, I really do like this game. It is a 'journey' that is borderline-unforgettable and treats the player to innumerous beautiful sights, but just doesn't quite scratch the itch that the very best walking sim/ artstyle extravaganza / puzzle type games like Gris, Abzu, and Journey do. The narrative was also not even nearly as profound as you would find in Gris, and while an enticing narrative with heart-striking beats is certainly not a requirement for a game such as Journey, but it is just another way that Journey has been passed by its successors. Don't get me wrong, Journey is still an excellent title with a really fun and interesting adventure to go on. Also, the addition of having other people join your Journey along the way is super super cool. More thoughts below. Feel free to comment if you have questions/ would like to discuss. Sights/Sounds/Performance- An incredibly beautiful artstyle with an incredibly beautiful soundtrack	- Textures/Graphics are not particularly stunning, but the visual style and amazing landscapes are bafflingly beautiful- I took a stupid amount of screenshots	- Such a beautiful artstyle and game- Sound design does feel a little muddy, however not a big deal- Flawless 144 frames at 1440p on a 3060 ti- 1 crash, nothing major- An incredible pause screen btw	- And the credits... DAMNGameplay- Gameplay loop is simple, effective, and very palatable- Movement feels quite smooth and fun- The addition of other players to kinda guide you around is really cool- Gameplay isn't really what's important	- It does what it needs to do		- Sits back, works how it should, and lets you experience the game- I am a sucker for varying cool environments, and this game (a lot like Gris) did that incredibly well, keeping the environments fun, engaging, varied, and interesting Narrative/Story- The goal is very clear from the beginning; make it to the top of the mountain- There is something so incredibly beautiful about going on this free, silent journey though the sand	- Incredibly fun to just run through the dunes, brings a smile to my face- While i didn't really understand the cutscenes all that much, the character progression was really cool to see- The darker undertones of the big stone dragon things destroying everything was super interesting and spiced up the 'journey'- The end was a really nice finish, capping off the journey by making it to the top and then watching your character ascend? and head all the way back to the beginning through all the rooms

_childDocuments_.review: 8 years and counting, Journey is a timeless classic based around something simple: the .  For those who don't know what the monomyth is, it's that underlying positivity/time correlation that makes so many movies and stories and epics so impactful.  Each area corresponds almost directly to a stage of the monomyth.  I'll let you research the details — to say more could well be to spoil the game.  In a way, however, this game is not exactly about emotion, but about   This is more or less the exact same awe that every religion in the world aspires to (NB word has it that even atheists can enjoy this game)....and if you don't know what Journey is, yes it's a game, but it's not a game.  Like so many games that came after it (e.g. GRIS, RiME), it is , first and foremost.  To judge this game is to judge art, so to judge this game for its gameplay would be wrong (granted, the gameplay is fun too).  And if you think this game is pretentious, then perhaps all art is pretentious to you — may as well stick to your pixel graphics games then.  Meanwhile the rest of us will take a moment to meditate in this game when we're feeling stressed (you can actually do that: press  to meditate).With breathtaking art by Matt Nava, a fine concept by Jenova Chen, and gorgeous music by Austin Wintory — 2 of these 3 are also behind ABZU — what's not to love about this game?  This is a game that turns strangers into friends.  Love and Peace are eminent...

_childDocuments_.review: Another banger from Annapurna Interactive. If you liked their game Flower, you'll love journey. It has the same beautiful storytelling environment and simple puzzle solving with the added feature of subtle co-op. I didn't even know until I finished my first playthrough that I was actually playing with other people and not just AI. Very few games can execute the same level of enjoyable teamwork with little more than a 'whistle button' to communicate with. A whole new level of meaning is added to the cliche saying "it's about the journey, not the destination" by completing this game, especially since we're never given a clear cut answer as to what exactly it is our character is trying to reach on top of the mountain. Overall, I highly recommend this game to anyone who can take the time to look around them and appreciate the natural beauty in things.

_childDocuments_.review: As a game designer myself I've always heard a lot of praise for this game from my peers. However to my shame I have to say that I never really touched the game outside of giving it a look or 2 on YouTube for reference material.However, this Steam Summer Sale around I gave it a shot, it's been on my to-do list for a while now and I figured I'd give it a shot!Wow... Just... Wow... Journey is an absolutely amazing game. Gameplay is buttery smooth and super simple to wrap ones head around. Level design is superb and I saw a lot of interesting takes on certain design principles; some really being stretched to their limits, yet they always manage to make it work. The game oozes dedication, love and attention to detail without losing sight of the bigger picture and packing it into a reasonable playtime.Aside from me fawning over all the technicalities and me going "oooh! aaahh! hmmmm interesting *scribble notes scribble*" I will have to say the game did touch the feels. At first I thought this was a solo game. And when I saw a carbon-copy of my player model appear out of the distance and pinging me in the Bridges level. I thought this was an enemy or something at first. I genuinely  had a "all hands on deck and focus" moment as the clone approached me. After it seemed that they were friendly I assumed it was a bot, which I found funny. But as time progressed I became more wary of the fact this "copy" might not be so much of a "copy" as I initially thought. In fact, it was another player. To say that my mind was blown was an understatement. Journey is yet another game that has a super unique, interesting and lovable play on multiplayer that reminded me of the way Dark Souls handles it's multiplayer (also a unique take on MP). Albeit this game does away with the murderparty and the like and is just pure jolly cooperation.However, due to the mute- less is more -nature of the game, the bonds you forge with the other players are quite unique. You really bond with the other player over your shared journey. Making sure they are okay and always try to stay close together, progressing together and enjoying the game together; as you can tell on almost a metaphysical level that the other player is enjoying the experience as much as you are. This along with the fact your only real means of communication being various degrees of pinging makes for an extremely unique MP experience. This will especially lead (at least it did for me) to very cathartic moments when you both reach the end goal. I had this experience 3 times now with 3 random players and it never failed to leave me with a bittersweet moment.But the Journey goes on even after "the goal" is reached, which ties in with the other strong point of the game. Symbolism. This game just oozes it left, right and centre and will leave you with much to ponder and philosophise about.This game is a defo recommendation from me for everyone that wants to experience a game that's truly outside the box and leaves you with something to think about.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played a lot of games in my life but this one is completely different. So respectful, so loving. It manages without any dialogue and still tells a story that picks you up emotionally. It's so relaxing, it brings you completely down. I think the last time I was this relaxed was after one of my yoga and meditation sessions. And as crazy as this may sound, I think this game is perfect for people who want to calm their monkey mind. Because many people who also like it have already played it umpteen times.If you get involved in this "Journey", have a decent pair of headphones, which are an absolute must here, and switch off all sources of interference for a moment, then you dive deep into a world that seems almost poetic. The game lasts just under an hour and anyone expecting a typical 0815 game will soon be disappointed, because:You don't die, you can't achieve any challenges, you don't get any names, no story, tasks or anything like that. But that's exactly the point! During the hour you experience wonderful scenery, music that has been thought through down to the last note and, at best, another player with whom you can share this experience. But without any chat or voice function. You only communicate through your actions and the other person's response.Maybe I've shed a tear and maybe the start screen with the sound is still playing in the background as I write this review (my first game review). After you have played the game, perhaps you will understand me a little. If not, that's fine too. I wish you wonderful moments with this game and other players.And if you like other games of this kind, then have a look at the developers page of thatgamecompany. Have fun!

_childDocuments_.review: I *definitely* didn't get the intended experience for this game, because I have annoying fickle, shaky internet. So this goes out to all of those other folks who also have shaky, fickle internet: don't play unless you got some stable internet.-------spoilers ahead-------From my understanding, this game is, in many ways, supposed to be joyful and heartwarming in the way it connects you to your mysterious "buddy" with whom you go on a roughly 3 hour journey. Even when things are at their most arduous, you and your companion pull through, for that companion to be revealed to be a fellow human being on the other end. Once the game is over, you've built an ephemeral, yet somehow lasting connection to another person who you might never ever meet or interact with again.This was not my gameplay experience. In fact, I had the opposite gameplay experience. The game was downright depressing. For me, I had a buddy for the first part, before my shaky internet basically disconnected me from anyone else after the first segment of the game. After that, it was a lonesome, fearful solo climb. Like, "you start the journey together, but you will die alone in the end" levels of depressing.-------spoilers end--------------so in any case, if your internet isn't entirely stable, avoid this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Polargamer101, this is for you, wherever you are.I started my journey as many of you did, confused, but intrigued. I sang to all around me, and watched as the wind and sand flowed through the cloth around me. I found small companions, and just as the gloom came, I sang once more, and my friends were freed.But then I saw one more friend. Who was that, in the distance just ahead of me? They just went down the path I was going to... I sang out, sang out as loud as I could to them, and at last, as we looked into the dunes to slide down below, they were there, waiting for me.We ventured, we slid, we bobbed and weaved together. It was a time of joy between both of us. Nothing could go wrong... And then we found the darkness. We were scared, we were afraid, but we still had each other, as we took each step side by side.We saw as the monsters took our joy, our hope. We could not let them snuff us out, so together, we made our way to freedom from the dark caves of misery. We cheered, as we had reached safety! We were still together, through all they searched to snuff us out.We climbed, climbed together into the light above us, seeing as our fate was laid bare in front of us. In our vision, there was only one of us, to start. As the vision carried on... There they were! My friend, we were destined to climb to our destination together, through all our struggles.As the winds blew, we pushed each other on, continuing to give our songs, to share our warmth. And that... is when disaster came.The monsters came, and my friend... was gone, swooped away, as I saw the sparks of life fade in the air...But wait, in the cover ahead! There they were! They were... alive!We kept pushing, kept going until we could not take one more step... so close to the end, they fell, and in the next step, so did I.Then hope shone on us, as we rose to the heavens, we didn't just sing, but we FLEW!We had made it. Together. Side by side, as it was meant to be. Our songs turned to hums, as we walked together into the light...Polargamer101, I couldn't find you when we were done, but I sing out now into the winds, that maybe, just maybe, you will hear me. I hardly know you, but I feel like I love you like a brother or sister. All I want to say is thank you for taking this Journey with me.

_childDocuments_.review: The setting of this game is a barren desert. As a result, gameplay objects are scattered across huge distances. 90% of the gameplay consists in holding W to get between landmarks. Not platforming; just walking forward. Normally I have no problem with games where most of the gameplay is just walking. However, games that de-emphasize gameplay do so to enable the player to focus more intensely on the environment and atmosphere of the game. Unfortunately, Journey has almost nothing to offer in terms of environment and atmosphere. Like I said earlier, the setting is a barren desert. The entire environment is one consistent dull orange color and some hills. The ruins are boring, uninspired, and sparse. Even when the atmosphere is boring, walking games can find some salvation in engaging movement mechanics. But the movement in this game is atrocious. You can't jump. There is a flying mechanic, but its use is limited . There is a mechanic to slide on hills, but it only works downhill. The walkspeed is agonizingly slow. You could recite the complete works of Shakespeare in the time that it takes to walk up a small hill in this game. The fact that the environment is so barren leaves you no choice but to focus all of your attention on these ♥♥♥♥♥♥ movement mechanics. If the walkspeed were tripled and flying and sliding were less limited the game would perhaps be bearable, but in its current state I find it actively painful to play. After 30 minutes of torture playing this game I watched a playthrough to see if anything changes later in the game. It does not.

However I'd recommend being a team player, it makes the game a bit more fun. It just becomes a bit more tedious and time consuming if you do it solo (getting punished for not being a team player).4. Bad co-op communication system (Not really, except in a specific situation. Read what I wrote below for more info on that).My food arrived the same time as I was doing a "puzzle" with someone. I had a choice to make there, either abandon the random person I was playing with or eat my food while it's hot. I'm not a fan of cold sandwiches.This is where I stumbled upon my first problem with the game. I stop walking and so does the random co-op player, and I have no way to tell them to go on, because I'm going afk for a bit (Unless I learn Morse code).I know if the person keeps going on for a little bit, then they'll get another companion, but what if someone wants to get the achievement for completing most of the game with the same companion. It seems like an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ thing to just stop and ruin it for them. Even when I pause and the character sits down, they still would run into me and spam right click, which flashes a little light.

_childDocuments_.review: Plays great on Steam Deck, and I have played and completed many games on Deck using my phone's hotspot to connect with other travelers, and finished the games with no problems whatsoever. Now that I have gotten all the achievements in this game, I would like to leave a thorough review.  I played this game over 10 years after its release, and I always meet companion travelers, so this game is definitely still beloved by many new gamers to this day. It's a very unique online gaming experience, and one that every gamer needs to have.  You won't get a more pure and enjoyable online gaming session than playing Journey and meeting up with someone to join you to head to the end of the game.When the credits roll, you get a beautiful song, and you get to watch all the places you walked through as your spirit goes back to the start of the game.  A real cycle of life, and as far as games go, it doesn't get better than this.  Journey is a world-class masterpiece from beginning to end.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a piece of art. In my opinion the ideal of what art and games should look like. This game respects your time and gives you the ability to communicate with other players on a deep, emotional, unique level. A absolute masterpiece that will hopefully remain for eternity. This game takes about 1,5-3 hours to play through, but that value of that expierence can not be measured in trivial things like money, at least for me. My favorite game to go to when the end of the weekend is near. Perfect for calming down if you have played the game at least once. It absolutely suprises me how people come up with always new ways to express themselves in the game and reach areas that one player alone could not reach without help of another. I believe this game can teach you how to truly love. I can not imagine any mentally healty person that plays this game not to feel anything while playing this game. There are only a few pieces of art that can match this game that i know of, namely another game named GRIS, which also has a unique artstyle. Both these games belong in a digital art museum if you would ask me. What makes Journey a unique expierence however is every person playing and interacting with each other. So i hope we see each other on the other side, my little cloth creature friend. I will be waiting on the end of the hallway for you.Thanks for every JourneyP.S: if you know unique pieces of art, that evoke positive emotions in you or give you a feeling of enlightenment, please share that knowledge in the comments. _childDocuments_.review: One of the most beautiful game experiences I have ever had with a game that based on exploration of a vastly unknown realm! You are tossed into a strange alien world, or more like a realm within an astral plain of higher dimension. The world seems like it was once a lush living world, now a desert wasteland after something bad must have happened to the people, and cities once there thriving. It is up to you, and possibly a companion will meet you along the way "another player" to travel and discover mysteries to solve, and uncover what has happened from relics from the past, and guardian souls. I don't want to ruin the experience for anyone by saying more than that. What I will say is, I had a wonderful time. Magical experience, & lucky for me I had a companion greet me early on, and together without a word "just chirps, and calls" we helped one another to discover things, and get past areas together with teamwork. _childDocuments_.review: I completed this game when it came out on PS3 and recently picked it up to replay on my Steam Deck. It’s just as beautiful and haunting as it was when it came out. I find it an important game when I’m struggling with depression and anxiety in life. The journey will be difficult. Sometimes you’ll feel alone. But you can do it. You can make it to the end. I have greatly enjoyed revisiting this game and at a difficult point in my life where I have been struggling day to day. It isn’t for everyone and people will pick it apart but if you’re willing to just go on the journey you will be better for it. Truly a masterpiece and deserving of praise. Highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: Beautifully simplistic art, which is accompanied by a soundtrack that is fitting for each individual fragment of the game that  the player will experience.The story is never explained to the player throughout the game, nor is it at the end. The player has to formulate it's own interpretation of the story by experiencing the various spectacular events within the game, it has an allure which makes the game unique and powerful. Whatever you decide to settle with as your conclusion to the game's story, another player might have an extremely disparate interpretation, furthermore, due to the game's non-restrictive story telling, no interpretation is wrong, each is viable and of varying amounts of effort, all of which are nonetheless, feasible and satisyfing to the player's mindAnother delightful addition is it's co-op: throughout the game, you are able to encounter multiple players who - just like yourself - are on a journey, attempting to unravel the intriguing world laid before them. If you were to experience it with a friend, a beautiful dichotomy of theories and interpretations could shape which is even more interestingAll in all, the game is unique, intriguing, short and simplistic and often during the playthrough, your mind is on a longer journey than the character which you control.
_childDocuments_.name: Journey

_childDocuments_.review: Just another sob story from another emotional player who takes everything personally...This game means a lot to me. I played it alone countless times without any goal in mind. I would launch it and I'd just walk, surf on the sand, 'sing' with the clothes, fly with them, feel the music, take everything in until I get lost in the atmosphere. It is a safe place for me.It helped me get through some of the loneliest days of my life... only to be left alone again by my companion! Ha! Man did it hurt! One time, I waited for hours, no one came. I just want to finish it with someone! Why is it so hard? Am I playing it wrong??? Am I really that difficult that even in a made up world no one wants to be with me??? I felt so discouraged but... it's still beautiful.Still I tried and tried and tried, I memorized the map, I worked hard to get the white robe and I wore it all the time because I thought that would make them want to finish the game with me. It still did not work... but to my surprise, it's still beautiful.And through my despair, one time, I chose to leave a companion on purpose. . . "Now, how does THAT feel?!" . . . only to... immediately regret it right after. I still feel the lump in my throat from that time. I paid for that by dying alone. I would never do that again.I have finally completed the game after almost a year. What a journey.I want to cry. Thank you to all of the companions I have met along the way.Finished the game for the first time: August 12 2021 @ 10:05pmFinished the game for the first time with a companion: August 2 2022 @ 1:32am

_childDocuments_.review: A brilliant and beautiful telling of the archetypal hero's journey. Attempting to sum it up would take away the magic of discovery. If you like original indie games with beautiful art, short but great gameplay, and meaningful connections then stop here and go play it. I'm personally not one for anything resembling a "platformer" but I'll set it aside to try something that otherwise looks interesting. And in this game? The movement through levels serves to set the tone wonderfully: You'll trudge through sand in your humble beginnings, learn to fly, scamper to hide from threats, soar with friends while empowering each other to go higher, and struggle through harsh lands with each others support. The presence of companion players makes it so much more poignant and rewarding.

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful, thoughtful, and despite not uttering a single word to my companion I was devastated when he disappeared just before the summit. _childDocuments_.review: This is a masterpiece. There's no other way for me to describe this. An absolute masterpiece.I think the power of Journey lies in how every single piece that makes it clicks just right with the other. From the beautiful visuals, through the wonderful soundtrack, to the simple yet grasping story; Journey combines them all together into a marvelous experience that feels flawless from start to finish. There aren't many games that leave me speechless as the credits roll, but Journey certainly left an impact on me.It's short - two or three hours at best - but that's all it needs to achieve its goal. In fact, I'm pretty sure that adding any more length to the game would've taken away some of its charm. Journey lets you peek into its world, experience it, enjoy it, and then lets you off to your own conclusion. It's very important to know how long your game should run for, and the devs nailed it just right.I think the best part for me was the surprise of finding someone else alongside my adventure. I didn't know this game had online co-op until that very moment. We went a few levels through until we had to part ways, but I kept thinking of this fellow throughout the rest of the game. Where are they now? Did they finish it? What did they think of it? Will I see them again? Then, when the credits rolled and I saw their name, I felt great. I don't know why... I'm just happy I found out who they were.Journey is one of these rare gems that leave you truly wondering at the end. I feel like there's a much deeper meaning to this tale than one might see on the surface, and I'll certainly ponder this for a while now. But for me, a game that leaves me with this feeling is a fantastic game - and Journey is, by all means, a true masterpiece.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: -Easy-Nice visuals-Lovely musicCons: -Very repetitive-There are probably only about 5 total actions you can take in the game, give or take-No clear purpose, story, narrative, objective, or goal; very abstract (judging by other reviews, fans of this game consider this to be a pro, but I found it to be vague, aimless, and even confusing)This game is pretty nice to look at, but that's about all it has going for it. The premise of the game is that you are making a journey across a post apocalyptic landscape, at points you are randomly partnered with another player who is also in the game. You can only communicate with this partner using short or long chirps. There are about 4 types of creatures in the game, one which is hostile, and which are re-occurring throughout most of the levels. As you journey towards your destination, you collect pieces of red fabric which lengthen your character's scarf and allow you to multi-jump or "fly." This in turn allows you to reach greater heights, but aside from the appeal of just jumping/flying higher, there is not much benefit of this from a gameplay perspective. It's just personally gratifying.I've asked a couple people what they like about this game and the general consensus seems to be something to the effect of "exploring for exploring sake with a stranger." Some feel that being partnered with someone you can't talk to or know their name heightens the sense of camaraderie. I can get that, but I don't think it's enough to redeem the game's lack of content. A good friend of mine said "the story is up to you to create." I don't understand this because there are no elements of this game that I would consider to be sandbox-like. Maybe they just meant it's up for interpretation.It's wholesome enough, but there's not much to it, and unless you are easily moved by pretty music and visuals, I don't understand how this is considered to be an emotional game. I found it to be a bit boring. It is a journey without purpose or explanation. And that's fine if that's what you're into, which obviously a lot of people are, but any of this sounds unappealing for you, I wouldn't bother with this game.

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic experiment in human social interaction.This game boils down communication with randomly assigned players to movement and simple audio chirps. What results is an improvised interaction with another human unflavoured by name, gender, speech pattern or fame. Language is constructed on the fly. How do you indicate excitement with such a simple lexicon? How about danger? You'll find that humans are naturally very good problem solvers in matters such as these and you'll build your own bespoke communication method with each player almost unconsciously.You may spend hours of quality time with someone only to find they are the kind of person you wouldn't ever seek out in real life.You might spend almost the entire game alone, only to be saved in the final hour by an experienced player who helps you push forward.The feel of the game changes each time because the human the game matches you with is different and the time you meet them varies. Even the most toxic of player will be hard pressed not to feel passion and empathy for their partner on their first few plays.It doesn't always work as it should, but if you get the right person at the right time, there is no equivalent in gaming as it stands.

_childDocuments_.review: Enter the world of Journey, the third game from indie developers thatgamecompany (creators of "flOw" and "Flower"). Journey is an interactive parable, an anonymous online adventure to experience a person’s life passage and their intersections with other’s. You wake alone and surrounded by miles of burning, sprawling desert, and soon discover the looming mountaintop which is your goal. Faced with rolling sand dunes, age-old ruins, caves and howling winds, your passage will not be an easy one. The goal is to get to the mountaintop, but the experience is discovering who you are, what this place is, and what is your purpose. Travel and explore this ancient, mysterious world alone, or with a stranger you meet along the way. Soar above ruins and glide across sands as you discover the secrets of a forgotten civilization. [thatgamecompany]
