_childDocuments_.review: UPDATED. At first this was a positive review.---IMPORTANT: You can't tell the game is bad unless you invest quite some time into it. This is how the genre works. So, you spend couple of hours into it, find it's flaws, understand that it's as raw as chicken in Ramsey's shows and BAM. You can't refund it.---So, if there was some sort of a book called "Action Rogue-lites: Do and Don'ts on example - this game would have a whole paragraph. Let me explain.The game is great: art, music, general ideas, mechanics. At first glance I gave Undermine a positive review. But as longer you play - the more you understand what's the difference between good game and "good looking" game.I don't want to compare it to mastodonts of genre like Isaac or Gungeon in this review, because this game is different (but I bet those two were the inspiration for Undermine), but I just can't. So...1. Item powerups. On each level there is a treasure room. Starting lvl 2 those demand a key. (just like in BoI) Each room provides you with an item that is supposed to aid you in your journey. But, there is a HUGE difference. - Item pool is really small. There are like 25-30 of items and 80% of them are useless. For example you can be on some deep level with a pool of: Item that expands the shop variety (useless, as shop doesn't provide any game changers), item that let you find leftover food in chests (though chests may contain food anyways), item that let you jump on oil (absolutely useless unless there is an oil spitting boss which I didn't find yet), item that does minimal damage to mobs as you pick up gold and so on. There are no items that affect your walking speed, there are items that were borrowed from other games without proper understanding on how they work in whole balance system.... Aaah!- Game advertises that there are item synergies. Well, yeah. There are. You have 30 items in game. I've unlocked like 75% of them. I got synergy. One! Two bomb items fused into one bomb item. That does pretty much exactly the same what any of the fused items did. Great job!- Item power levels. There are bunch of things that add X when you have Y: keys = damage, health high/low = damage, etc. They just suck. Do you remember "Money = Power" from Isaac and how it works? You get it, then you get some coins and suddenly you are a DEATH MACHINE! Here they do some really bad thing, for example: keys = damage. Having 6 keys at time makes you "wealthy" on keys. This adds something like +12 damage to your swing. How much is that? Well... Basic rat has something about 40-50 HP, and that +12 refers accordingly. +12 HP damage dealt each swing.I could go more with in-depth analysis, but no. There's too much to it.2. Whole progression. You're a dude, hunting for gold. Whatever. The aim is - travel deeper and get more. Ok.First boss (not the golem joke) is a giant centipede. It has some short cutscene and introduction. (Apart of thing, that it has some attacks that you just can't dodge and the whole combat mechanics... Whatever).So, after quite some time you kill it. And guess what? A ladder appear. Great job! Now go back and follow the rails. You get some money and unlocks. That's it. Why did I even had to fight it, anyway? Did it unlock another passage or biome? No. Did it give me some ability? No. The boss gives you an item (spawn minion at entrance of the hostile room. But it sucks, as it's blind and rarely hits the enemy.) and a potion that... spawns the same minion but once. Wow. Do you want me to avoid all bosses from now on? What's the point?- Leveling up is ehrhmahgerd. Let's say you start with 100 hp, 10 dmg and 10 range. You fight for your gold, over and over again. You level up everything once for the sake of it. Nice job! Now you're 120 hp, 12 dmg and 12 range. Try our new level up. We have like 40 levels of them. It feels exactly like playing one of those mobile RPG without donating for crystals. What can I say? I've spent almost 11 hours in game and all I did - killed two bosses and found a key that I can't get, as I need to spend another 3 hours on gaining gold to level up enough to make it happen. Nice!- Stats. Game has physical, lightning and fire damage so far. Is there a way to armor up yourself? No. Is there a potion? NO! Can I do anything to get less damage?! Well, you can get better at game... No armor. Period. Logic sometimes just leaves the room silently. You can pick up "flying boots" that let you levitate over pits. Oh, wow. So it's like flying, right? Now I can fly over those spikes... Whatta?!You can't affect speed of your character, you can't affect speed of your projectiles (which makes the upgrade of throw distance quite questionable), you can't affect critical chance, attack speed, anything that would make huge difference. Health, damage, distance and gold lost. All you have. And those are increased in 120 easy steps.- Damage. At first you'll be like "Oh, ok, I see". But then you'll get angry. The game has a jump as a dodging mechanic which is really questionable. Why not a simple dash, that would suit the game much more. As by jumping you really have no idea what you can jump over, and what will hit you for sure. So imagine this: you're in a rush, you storm the rooms. You aim for that left passage and you enter. The spikes at the VERY entrance greet you with -29 HP and send flying to that rat on tracks that gives you another -20 HP and then the incoming sawblade deals another -25 hp and sends you flying to a pit. It makes you fall to the room entrance with another -20 hp and since life didn't ready you for this you still hold "w" to run forward in attempt to escape and the spikes say "hi" again. What the hell? I've played  some IWTBTG and Boshy and those looked more honest in terms of damage dealing. Just why?I believe it's time to stop, though I'm not done yet.The folks that did this game are really passionate about their child, I believe. On all other aspects - the game is great. Those mobs dying gave me a feel as Paul Robertson walked in to the office and said: "Guys, I know a cool animation you could use". But the actual gameplay is so bad it made me create this wall of text. No hard feelings. I really hope the game will improve. Cheers!

_childDocuments_.review: There are aspects to like about this game and there are some issues, but honestly, this is more of a side-way thumb.The core issue I have with this game is a lack of focus and variation, as well as just annoying meta-progression quirks.Presentation (sounds, music, graphics) is pretty good.Please stop having perks or upgrades in games like these that boost your progression rate. In this game, there's a perk that increases how much gold you keep on death. Gold is used to buy upgrades and is accrued throughout a run. This means that this perk is generally speaking always your absolute top priority.Just tie it to general progression level in terms of perks or don't have it. It is basically always the optimal choice in games like these and that's kind of boring.Runs feel very much the same all the time. The game offers area skips if you've beaten the boss, but that's generally not a good idea because you kind of want the upgrades you'd get along the way to those levels.There needs to be more level-branches and stuff like time-challenges.In my general opinion, rogue-lites ought to fit in one out of two categories (with minor variations).- The clean rogue-lite where there's a few well-polished systems (examples: Binding of Isaac, Receiver, Ziggurat 2, Dead Cells).- The complicated rogue-lite with 15 (okay, maybe not that many) status screens and  a lot of different systems to interact with or handle (examples: Dungeon Crawl Stone Soup, Heat Signature, Caves of Quad).This game is definitively trying to be the former, but the gold gathering mechanic is frustrating. If you leave gold on the floor, slimes show up and start picking it up. You have to bash them away or have a canary with you to help you chase them down during combat. It is at the same time frustrating and generally free of consequences. The slimes might steal like a couple of percent of your gold, but having that task in the game of having to focus on getting the gold too is just annoying.
_childDocuments_.name: UnderMine

_childDocuments_.review: Undermine is a stellar game that suffers from one big flaw – lack of content. One would think that with all the beautiful pixel art, huge amount of items, and fun gameplay it could easily stand next to greats of this genre of games (rogue-lites such as Binding of Isaac and Enter the Gungeon), but only 4 bosses and biomes (5 if we count the conditional one, and 6th boss as the campaign end boss), coupled with such achievements as “beat the game 30 times”, really does no favors for Undermine. Had the developers gone that extra mile to at LEAST introduce one (or two) more bosses into the mix, this game would have been much better and more enjoyable, without egregious repetitiveness that I’ve personally experienced. This is one of those rare moments where I’d like to have a third (“mixed”) option instead of “thumbs up” or “thumbs down”, as the game can be enjoyable, yet becomes stale after some 50 hours of gameplay (and it is a general consensus that roguelites should be enjoyable for much, much longer).EDIT: oh, and ignore that "Story Rich" tag the game has - there is 0 story to this game, and what little lore there is is mostly item descriptions (it's hard to make another gem like HADES, after all)
_childDocuments_.name: UnderMine

_childDocuments_.review: In a genre where 95% of the games blend together and feel the same, Undermine manages to stand out. You've no doubt seen the core gameplay and mechanics elsewhere but only here will you see it so polished. My only complaint is that I started to lose interest around the 50 hour mark, but the devs are continuing to update the game and you can tell they're passionate about this project. This is a game you will not regret picking up.
_childDocuments_.name: UnderMine

_childDocuments_.review: Well, I'm having a blast with it. (A little over 9 hours in)I don't really understand the people saying it's like a poor version on Isaac. Imo, it's not trying to be anything like Binding of Isaac. Also, people saying they don't like running after gold, that actually turns into a really cool mechanic. (Small spoiler here:) Once you get Geckos Foot (One of the very early permanent upgrades you can buy) You can throw your axe to pick up gold (Given, that's not actually explained, but again I kinda like the discovery aspect of it. Like, hmm, what does this new item do) Anyway once you figure that out, it's really fun. When you mine for gold little weevle things come out of the walls and try to steal it before you can pick it up, if you've killed all the enemies first then that's easy, but sometimes in the chaos of the room fight the gold might get sprayed everywhere and you've got to make a quick decision as to continue the fight and lose the gold or take a chance dashing for the gold but possibly taking damage instead. Equally, if you're nearly dead, you might just want to rush to pick up as much gold as possible before everything gets you, or play it safe in the hopes there's health in the next room. It's definitely an intended thing that adds risk/reward to the game, not just some lazy oversight.Also, I love all the little secret puzzles n stuff.  I personally love the way the game slowly drip feeds new stuff and makes you discover the next bit. Some people might find it obtuse. Though, I would definitely say (Again, minor spoiler:) you should absolutely buy the bomb upgrade as soon as you beat the first boss. It is pretty unforgiving, and the air controls when jumping are donkey ♥♥♥♥.I don't know, it might become repetitive, but I doubt it. Will update this review after another 10-20 hours in anycase.

_childDocuments_.review: "Delving into Delightful Depths"Rating: ★★★★☆Introduction:"Undermine" is a hidden gem that shines brightly in the ever-expanding world of indie roguelike games. As a dedicated fan of the genre, I found myself pleasantly surprised by the depths this game explores and the fun it consistently delivers.Gameplay (★★★★☆):The core gameplay loop in "Undermine" is addictive and satisfying. You play as a lowly peasant armed with a pickaxe, delving deeper into a procedurally generated mine. Each run offers a unique experience, with a variety of enemies, traps, and treasures to discover. The blend of real-time combat and resource management keeps you engaged and challenged. The frequent upgrades and power-ups add an element of strategy, making each decision count.Graphics and Audio (★★★★☆):Visually, "Undermine" has a charming pixel art style that feels nostalgic yet polished. The environments are filled with detail and personality, from the bustling hub area to the eerie depths of the mine. The audio design complements the game perfectly, with a catchy soundtrack and satisfying sound effects that immerse you further into the experience.Story and Narrative (★★★☆☆):While "Undermine" isn't primarily a story-driven game, it manages to infuse its world with subtle lore and amusing character interactions. The witty banter with NPCs and the occasional surprises hidden within the mine add an extra layer of enjoyment to the journey.Replayability (★★★★★):One of the standout features of "Undermine" is its exceptional replayability. The game encourages multiple playthroughs by offering an array of unlockable characters, relics, and secrets. The constant sense of progression, even in the face of defeat, keeps you coming back for more.Cons (★★☆☆☆):While "Undermine" excels in many areas, it's not without its flaws. Some may find the difficulty curve to be a bit steep, especially in the early levels. Additionally, occasional technical hiccups and minor bugs can be a slight annoyance.Conclusion:"Undermine" is a delightful roguelike that manages to strike a harmonious balance between accessibility and challenge. It's a testament to the potential of indie game development, offering an engaging experience filled with surprises and moments of triumph. If you have a penchant for roguelikes or are simply looking for a game with substantial replay value, "Undermine" is a worthy addition to your library.Overall Rating: ★★★★☆

_childDocuments_.review: I'm getting to the end of the base game now and I have to say, this game is insanely addictive. The curse/blessing mechanic is challenging yet satisfying when you amass so many. Until you fully upgrade your gold pouch, amassing gold can be slow going at first but the diverse range of enemy types and powerful relics makes each dive feel unique.
_childDocuments_.name: UnderMine

_childDocuments_.review: Short story is it's just a Binding of Isaac rip off with melee capabilities but worse overall quality, not worth the price or time spent in my opinion.Definitely would not recommend unless you want to waste your time and money playing a game that only really gets good in the late game and late mid game, before that it's just a snail's pace of a grind to collect gold only to lose most of it when you die, and what little gold you save up gets spent completely in a matter of seconds on one purchase due to overpriced "upgrades". The upgrades are really not worth the price at all because they are very very minor but cost hours of real world time to obtain. If this game enabled you to change difficulties, adjust settings such as gold drop rate or disabling pilfers, and had workshop/modding compatibility then it would be worth the price tag. However, as of right now it is just a worse overall version of Binding of Isaac. Check back a few years later and if they've added the above features or better, then I would recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: UnderMine

_childDocuments_.review: It's a pretty game but there are too many frustrations for me. The controls are a fine in principal, but they lack the affordances you might have come to expect; no coyote time over pits, being able to start the jump animation and still fall down pits, have jumps animate but cancel movement. The bigger frustrations, however,  are around the unfulfilling reward scheme. Losing some gold on death is pretty much par for the course now but the miniscule incremental upgrades that give you minor number improvements feel like a fruitless grind which is only furthered by that loss. Not to mention the critters who constantly try to steal it from you in the first place! Then there are the dungeons, where you will often find yourself using a bomb to get a bomb, or an empty room, or trapped chest. The few decent rewards you get are, within the first few hours at least, pretty dull for the most part, consisting largely of simple stat changes. Simply put, the enjoyment of playing is limited by frustrations and the desire to keep playing is removed from the unrewarding process.

But I like that the mechanics and controls are relatively simple,  there are tons of relics and blessings to experiment with and the curses add interesting challenges.  I don't know if I'll ever get good enough to beat the Othermine, but I've put over 100 into the game and I'm probably going to keep playing for while.

_childDocuments_.name: UnderMine

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fine, I guess: it works properly and there seems like a decent enough amount of content and the rogue-lite progress pacing isn't bad, but I just can't really say I actively ever found myself actually enjoying playing it.There's no story to speak of and the mechanics have simply been done better in other games, so there's little to keep me playing and when there are so many other games, I'd rather go play one of them.I know this isn't very constructive criticism, so if the devs read this then I apologise: it's hard to put my finger on precisely why, but I simply didn't enjoy playing this game and thus cannot recommend it to others.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh boy, what a great game. _childDocuments_.name: UnderMine

_childDocuments_.review: This game starts in out in long tutorial style where you have to defeat 4 of the 5 bosses to unlock Othermine (roguelike mode). You keep a portion of your gold after dying to unlock upgrades to make it easier to win.  The bosses on Ascension 0 (when your just starting the game) do not respawn after you kill them once to make it easier for you to complete your first run. After you defeat the 5 bosses you reach Summoning Stone 1 which respawns all of the bosses and makes the game harder. Also the Din, the Old King fight is unlocked.The true challenge of the game is Othermine (roguelike mode). Try to beat Othermine with Siegfried's Aegis for a real challenge.At the time of this review only 1.7% of people have beaten Din, the Old King and only 16% of people have even tried Othermine. So take these reviews with a grain of salt because they barely even played any of the content available.

_childDocuments_.review: A super generic mine themed roguelite. It's doing a lot of stuff but none of it feels new or creative. _childDocuments_.name: UnderMine

_childDocuments_.review: What a game!The games developer (Thorium) has managed to create one of the most addicting dungeon exploration games to date. The blessing and curses system is perfect, each choice can either make or break a run, enemies are creative and simple, yet put a few different enemies in a room and suddenly it can be challenging or easy to make a mistake that will end that trip. Along with this the bosses are fun and challenging and if your new to the game can take multiple tries to defeat. The fact that the games does not make everything available and you have to find blueprints and then buy the blessing or potion makes the grinding feel very rewarding. Finally the dungeon itself constantly feels new, this is achieved by making the dungeon layout, chest locations, shops, power ups and enemies constantly different, after 22 hours of game play so far i can safely say that i'm not bored of this game and don't think ill be getting bored any time soon. Would recommend to anyone who wants a fun, interesting and attention holding indie RPG!

_childDocuments_.review: Heading into UnderMine, I was expecting a roguelite that wasn’t too bad but wasn’t anything great either. The sheer attention to detail is staggering from both a visual and gameplay perspective, with so much to earn and look forward to. Combined with its high level of replayability, I found myself quickly addicted. It may have an issue in regards to a lack of high-tier passives, but the rest of the game overshadows this flaw greatly to still offer something equally engaging and endlessly fun. If you’re looking for a great roguelite, UnderMine is an adventure more than worth mining away at.If you'd like to read the rest of this review and more like it, check out . _childDocuments_.review: Game's a scam. Undermine has such a high potential for greatness, and yet there's little issues that keep it from being the greatest thing since Nuclear Throne (Or the Roguelite Standard Supreme: MONOLITH. No game's better than that yet.)PROS:+Graphical Style+TRANSPARENCY OF ITEMS (Like damn I wish every crappy procedurally generated piece of junk showed me and outright told me what items did before I picked them up)+Jump function makes sense overall, is nice+Non-Boss/Big Enemy combat is fun.+Difficulty is WAY HIGH starting out. It's kind of stupid that such a thing is locked behind a slog of grind just to unlock another NPC that is USELESS until later. I've spent 3 hours just making my pickaxe good, and..it doesn't matter since OOPS RANDOM MINEFIELD LOL RUN OVER / OOPS MADE ONE MISTAKE DUE TO A CURSE THAT YOU CAN'T STOP FROM HAPPENING WHEN YOU PURSUE AN UPGRADE!!!!!!!! _childDocuments_.review: I bought this game on launch because of the comments that it was similar to The Binding of Isaac, and that it was a "roguelite" with itemization and combos much like the formerly mentioned game.I bought this game mostly to play a few rounds in between my ever growing backlog of games that I keep telling myself I'm going to prioritize and clear up.Well, after 7 hours in two days (which is not a lot for some, but quite a bit for me) I can safely say this game is "it".  Do you wish you could find a game that makes you go "one more run" and then you realize you've spent the past several hours telling yourself that?Do you want a game that is difficult, but overall fair?Do you want a game that moment to moment has more to keep you engaged instead of zoning out during your repeated runs of the first several floors?Keep in mind, this is early access, there are a few bugs and a few strange interactions in the game.  But the devs have already put out a hotfix on Day 2 of the game's cycle and have been very active in Discord in talking with the community.This is a roguelite that is already well worth the admission cost.  The fact there is only more to come has me very excited for the future of this game.Highly recommended for any fans of Isaac, Enter the Gungeon, Nuclear Throne, the whole nine yards.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot of heart and style behind it. From the overall light hearted story with a serious undertone to it, to the smooth gameplay that really is tightly tuned. This is just my synopsis based on what I've gone through so far. What I have played, however, is enough to encourage people to dig into this one. The price point is nice, the music is good, the gameplay is excellent, and the rogue-like build up is steady enough where each run through feels like your accomplishing more. Some runs seem to skimp on keys, some deaths are frustrating from how many things are shooting, exploding, and charging at you with pitfalls all around, and while the music is passable it really never sucked me in. That's probably the least I could say about the game. The most I could say has been stated in the first paragraph. The random dungeons keep a good variety and the evolution of the game is well balanced. In all, I encourage this to fans of Rogue-likes, Isometric overhead adventure games, and also fans of old school game design. A solid buy for the price tag at face value. A steal if you wait for a 50% off sale. P.S. So much love for the pilfers. They're just doing their job.

_childDocuments_.review: I collectively have around 5000 hours on roguelite/likes and I think that this is one of the best I've played, it has so much to offer and its not even a fully finished game yet! If you like games such as The Binding of Isaac and Rogue Legacy then you'll love this!First off, a little overview of what you can expect, you are a miner hopping down into the depth below to defeat evil and collect sweet sweet gold. Armed only with a pickaxe and a small familiar, you must make your way through the mines collecting gold and killing bosses.The game has many interesting systems, some most roguelike players will be familiar with and others that expand and evolve from what you are used to seeing. The first is the games permentant progression systems, while in the mines you may find recipes and blueprints for new items and these can be unlocked to appear in future playthroughs by crafting them using a rare gem known as thorium which you will collect alongside gold as you make your way through the mines. The interesting part of this mechanic that differs from most games is that when an item is crafted it can be taken into the mine on your next run, so you get to try what you just unlocked straight away!The game also offers a permantant upgrade system, the gold that you find while in the mine can of course be used on that run in shops and such but a portion of that gold is also taken back to the surface when you die, this can be used to purchase new and more powerful equipment like better armour for more HP or a new pickaxe for higher damage, these upgrades last for ever and effect every run.By far my absolute favourite system in this game is the risk/reward system, all good roguelikes have them, the best example of this is The Binding of Isaac deal with the devils where you trade HP for powerful items. This games system is much much more advanced and really become the core of the gameplay in most runs. After a you save a few of the townsfolk while in the mine you will unlock the ability to find alters with in the mines, these can be prayed to for a blessing of you choosing for a number of random option but with every time pray you gain a random curse, some curses arent very harmful, others will destroy a run if not taken care of quickly but do not fear because those same alter can be used to remove curses but at the cost of HP. Now there are many other ways to gain and remove curses such as special shops and potions but the alters are the central piece.Having the blessings, curses and the option to use HP as a resource really makes for some very interesting gameplay where maximumising value and thinking carefully about the risk vs the reward pays off in a big way.On top of all of this amazing content, the newest Update to the game just added an alternative gamemode called the OtherMine which makes the game into a much more traditional roguelike where all of your permentant upgrades are gone and you start from nothing each run, with each floor giving you a drafting stage to pick and item, curse and blessing!Overall I highly recommend this game to any fan of the roguelike/lite genre!If you want to see gameplay of this amazing game then please do check out the multiple series I have on the game here:

_childDocuments_.review: Undermine is an action roguelike with smooth gameplay, beautiful pixel art, varied randomized gameplay, and a solid meta progression system that provides long-term motivation.As typical for the genre, the game takes place in a randomized dungeon of connected rooms, with each room taking up one screen. If you enter a room with enemies, the exits get sealed until you have killed them. Not all rooms contain enemies though, some feature puzzles, shops, or treasures. The dungeon currently features 5 distinct biomes, and each biome stretches across 4 levels with about 15 rooms each, has its own set of enemies, features specific environmental challenges and opportunities, and has an end boss with unique mechanics. All bosses except the last one can be skipped if you don't feel ready for them.When you die, you automatically start a new character on the game's top level, which features a number of shops. You keep some gold from your previous run, and can use it to buy permanent upgrades for your characters. Another resource (thorium) can be used to craft powerful artifacts, potions, and blessings, provided that you found the respective blueprint / recipe / formula at some point. Most shops will be empty at the beginning of the game, but you can free their owners from various parts of the dungeon in a series of quests.I found the combat exciting and engaging. Each type of enemy has its own perks, and it was fun finding the best strategies to counter those. The game may feel a bit difficult at first, but actually becomes fairly easy as you keep upgrading your stats. If it gets _too_ easy, you can increase the dungeon's difficulty after beating all of the bosses. This will respawn the bosses, populate the dungeon with stronger enemies, and can be repeated indefinitely each time you beat all bosses.Meta-progression systems such as this one can feel a bit grindy, but Undermine implements it pretty well. You can find dozens of artifacts, blessings, and curses in each run, and many of those have such a profound effect on the gameplay that each run feels different. Also, after unlocking a new artifact / potion / blessing, you start your next run with it. For me, the curiosity of how a new artifact might work and how the next run might unfold, kept me engaged and interested. I had a steady feeling of progress.If meta-progression is not your thing, or if you'd like to shake things up a bit more, you can alternatively play a different game mode where you always start rather weak and face a dungeon with even higher degrees of randomization.Undermine won't revolutionize the genre, but is so well designed that it has quickly become one of my favorite entries. I also very much appreciate the focus on user-friendliness: the game controls very well with mouse and keyboard, all controls can be rebound (including an alternative key for each action), and mouse aiming can be toggled on or off. The game also autosaves at the start of each level.At the time of this writing, Undermine is still in early access, but it's almost complete and will soon have its full release. At that point its price will rise, so getting it now (or in the upcoming Summer Sale if it gets a discount) might be a good idea. The current price already looks like a bargain to me, considering how much fun I'm having with this game.

_childDocuments_.review: UnderMine is one of the better Roguelike/lites from this year and there's still quite a bit of content left to go. The gameplay loop is very solid, I do wish there was more randomness, but the progression feels good, and other than a few janky gameplay things there isn't much BAD to say. _childDocuments_.name: UnderMine

_childDocuments_.review: After beating all the bosses in the early access I can say this game definitely has potential. it truly does scratch the same itch as binding of issac but still lacks some of the polish that would make this a top tier game. Pros include a nice system of discovery, amazing pixel graphics and a worthwhile progression system. Some things that irked me were the jumping mechanic, too often I felt that I didnt have control over my character while jumping and sometimes felt I didnt deserve to end up in a ditch. The other improvement that I really would love to see is visual changes when you pick up a powerup/curse/blessing. Definitely on its way to being an amazing game, kudos to the developers.
_childDocuments_.name: UnderMine

Tip: You can enable the mouse aim in your options, this improves the game and makes it more fun.
_childDocuments_.name: UnderMine

_childDocuments_.review: I've been looking for another Roguelite to play and this game certainly fills that void. I started UnderMine up today thinking I'll just check it out, and ended up logging 12 hours in a day. Yes, I have no life, but the fact that I was able to keep playing that long says a lot about the game. If you like Binding of Issac and Enter the Gungeon, give this UnderMine a shot. I will note that it seems like some rooms are impossible to get through without getting hurt, but I feel the game makes up for it by providing plenty of ways to heel yourself.
_childDocuments_.name: UnderMine

_childDocuments_.review: At first I was unsure if I wanted to buy Undermine because people complained about stuff. There are so many mediocre roguelites out there but now that I've played Undermine a bit I think it's a good one. There are things I'd like to see changed like the thieves just annoy the hell out of me but so far I have really liked the game. Grinding for upgrades doesn't bother me because I grinded Isaac for 1k hours without any rewards.
_childDocuments_.name: UnderMine

_childDocuments_.review: So, I got this game because I was in a procedurally generated dungeon crawler mood and it does not disappoint. I've seen comments suggesting that this game is deceptively difficult, and I'd like to explain that its all depends on where you are at in the game. If you first start, then hell yeah damn straight its hard but that’s because it’s a new game and you have to hone your skill. However, for me around the 7th hour I started to really get the hang of it along with the upgrades and while I died to each boss I encountered at least once I came back with a new strategy and eventually succeeded.Gameplay is similar to binding of Isaac which in itself my opinion infinitely harder but some basic mechanics remain the same like for example bombs and keys finding secret rooms floor vendors etc. However, it is also in itself an entirely different beast, so same but different and inevitably enjoyable for it being early access I was very impressed. Of course, there are difficulty settings that I have yet to overcome and challenges that I still need to accomplish but I figured I’d drop a review. Would recommend if you wanna play something different and unique. Also, who would have guessed it doesn’t take 4k graphics to make an enjoyable game maybe The Last of Us 2 studios could take some notes and make something everyone can enjoy.
_childDocuments_.name: UnderMine

_childDocuments_.review: This game is crazy fun to me. I have never played a game like this honestly. Somehow it is amazingly fun even though you are essentially doing the same thing over and over again endlessly. Just working towards that next objective or that next boss keeps it enjoyable hour after hour.Edit 2023: Still stand by this 100% with 120hrs now.
_childDocuments_.name: UnderMine

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good for a game with only one weapon and two attacks. I should be bored AF with how little meaningful variety there is in the gameplay loop but I'm still having fun. I couldn't tell you why, exactly, but I am.There are a lot of 'upgrades' you can find in a run but 99% of it is boring crap like extra attack damage or extra gold drops, stuff like that. Some relics add graphics along with the increased damage, but they don't change how you play. Basically nothing you find anywhere changes how you play the game. There are potions that are mostly boring, giving you a buff for a short time, or rarely, doing something interesting like dropping a chest. I guess it's more fun to find a potion that creates a chest than just finding another chest. Whatever. Honestly, all this game has going for it are two things: The engine is smooth and well-developed, leading to responsive and satisfying gameplay, and the graphics are great. Music is boring. The visual appeal goes quite a long way, though--there's a ton of very, very good pixel art here to enjoy. Playing in 4k has caused me no FPS issues, which you'd think would be the norm for pixel art games but it isn't. If it looks like fun, you'll probably enjoy it. Lukewarm recommendation.
_childDocuments_.name: UnderMine

_childDocuments_.review: A genuinely delightful game.I'm enjoying this game so much. Gold collection can be a little slow, but all the different relics, blessings, and curses you can get along the way do a good job of keeping the gameplay fresh and interesting each time. It can be a bit of a grind sometimes, but not a boring one! Kind of wish there was a multiplayer version of this where you could mine dangerously with friends, but I'm still enjoying it without.Wholly recommend getting this game!

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy grindy dungeon crawlers then you will love this. Does it get repetitive? yes, if you don't enjoy that kind of thing this game will get old fast. If you do enjoy grindy games though you'll love this,pretty cool graphics, lots to discover and unlock, overall if its your kind of game it is definitely great value for money.

_childDocuments_.review: *SPOILERS* I would recommend this game except for the fact that the "last boss" (idk i cant pass him) is next to impossible because you have to face him as the "peasant" which has base stats and during the fight you get random useless items to pick up while you have to dodge the boss who hits you even in mid air, killing you in less than a minute. The whole game up until this point is easy mode, and then the final boss is next to impossible to create the sense of accomplishment, when in reality you are tasked with dodging heat seeking missiles with a piece of toast for a character, and you get items that are passive for a boss fight pool, not to mention he can hit you while in a freeze frame picking up items, which results in your death anyways. _childDocuments_.name: UnderMine

_childDocuments_.review: UnderMine has definitely been one of my favourite games to play of late. Good for if you just wanna zone out and game for a bit, made all the better by the soundtrack, with a surprisingly strong collection of NPCs and overarching story. Progression is a bit more permanent with basic items, special items, and potions all getting upgrades that stick with you no matter what, which is definitely helpful if you find yourself struggling here and there. _childDocuments_.name: UnderMine

_childDocuments_.review: I do love Rogue-lites (games where you die and come back, and get stronger each run till you beat it) but this combat/gameplay-loop is just not fun.  If the mechanics in this game was attached to something with more fun combat, this would have been a winner.I really tried to hang on, went about 5 hours in but the character-improvement is just happening too slow to keep me interested.
_childDocuments_.name: UnderMine

_childDocuments_.review: Everything feels unrewarding about this game. Firstly, it is not a rogue like in any way, but more of an RPG. The game is very easy and the only thing preventing you from beating the game at first is your very low health and lack of gear. From this point, it is just a matter of die-and-retry.  You unlock all the items in a very definite order and you get to keep most of them for your next plays. Chest rooms and secret rooms feel so cheap, providing basic power-ups, potions and gold. There’s really no outstanding item, you never get this kind of excitement after discovering a new item. And you don’t really mind losing to the game because, anyway, you know you’ll get the same kind of items next try.Secondly, the jumping system is the worst. It doesn’t fit at all the weird top-down perspective. You never really know where your character will land. It feels also very unresponsive and sluggish. A very bad attempt at renewing the roguelike genre with a little bit of a platformer.Good graphic design and concept, but terrible gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: UnderMine

_childDocuments_.review: The more I play this game, the less I like it. The first few upgrades you find are interesting, but then you realize that that's basically *it*. The "hundreds" that the game advertises includes linear stat boost items that persist through the game (+1 swing damage, +2 swing damage, +1 throw range, etc.). The fact that you really only have two main attack types (swing, or throw pickaxe) also limits the build variety and upgrade possibilities. The weapon synergies are lacking the excitement of say, Binding of Isaac.The game also plays waaay too long. Each level has four stages, ending with a boss that you only fight the first time through. There is a fast-forward mechanic a la Spelunky, but given the massive item deficit you take by bypassing the first X many levels, it's not worth it. So instead you are forced to grind through the first half hour, only to have a realistic shot at the level's boss. The graphics are great, though the mustachioed man "diversity" gets a bit stale (I imagine they will add more enhancements in the future), but I find myself increasingly playing fewer and fewer runs per day, and imagine I will probably fall off completely soon. Hopefully updates can address the grind and tedium, but for now I'd say this game is only worth getting if you need something for a long weekend.
_childDocuments_.name: UnderMine

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed this in early access and played it so much I had to quit - I wasn't sure if full release would be fun to play through after having "beat" the early access game quite a few times - but as I'm getting to the end of tier 4 and things are snowballing - it's so much fun. The new relics and curses and everything else is fantastic. The game performance is also very nice (it used to get quite laggy on long play sessions).  So addicting and so fun!  I appreciate these devs and can't wait to see what else they turn out.  Wish more indie games were done like this!
_childDocuments_.name: UnderMine

_childDocuments_.review: I will recommend this game if you truly love roguelikes, I will tell you though do not listen to the reviews that say its too hard or you can't find ____ easily, YES AT THE BEGINNING YOU WILL 110% STRUGGLE. It does not just hand you everything. With only 63 hours or so in as of 11/03 I still have so much to do. The game does become easier, and it does become harder. What do I mean by that?At the beginning you have no way to buy items to start with, unlock more items, potions or unlocking permanent upgrades, after a few runs you get the hang of it and if you get to the end not only does it make subsequent runs harder but there are more things to unlock like little pets to take with you for example, you can unlock hex runs which give you different achievements. There is also the othermine which you unlock to unlock separate pets and there's a hard challenge you can do to unlock an item for other runs :) If you like roguelikes I highly recommend this game. I love binding of isaac, moonligher and enter the gungeon to name a few if you like any of those you will love this game but give it more than like maybe 2-5 hours theres a lot to unlock once you get the hang of it, it is SUPER addicting.
_childDocuments_.name: UnderMine

_childDocuments_.review: UnderMine is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ gem of a game.Get this game. See the Pros and Cons below for the Short Version:PROSApproachable and fair in its difficultyPolished in its mechanics and presentationMusic is absolutely stunningThe story and the characters you meet are interestingThe cultural references and humor of the game are hystericalThe order in which you address how you complete portions of the game depend on you as the playerUnique boss encounters that make the player adjust their play style to the gimmick of the bossCONS - all these can be remedied/improved upon in the coming weeks; some are just what I wish was in the gameBugs with swatting back the bone projectile that the skeleton throwsProgression does not reflect a visual change to the peasant or equipment; it'd be cool to see upgrades to the pickax yield a different pickax, etc.No female peasant; lets get some inclusivity in here! Make it randomly generate which one you are too!There are a few recolored sprites reused through the game; this could easily be remedied with simply more enemies and more complex enemy design.If you have played bullet hell genre games like Enter the Gungeon, this game is going to feel very easy to you, perhaps too easyLong Version:I have three files open on this game; myself, my wife's, and my son's. My son is 7 and an okay gamer, but not good enough to really make much advancement in a game like this. My wife is a pragmatic puzzle solver who doesn't like being too stressed by video games, so much so that she will put it down if it gets to be too much, but she will whoop the ass of a game like The Room. I am big ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Papa. I will ♥♥♥♥ all your games up.I am telling you this so you understand the perspective of my review and how that may relate or not relate to your own opinion.UnderMine is the kind of dungeon crawler that is equal parts personality as it is challenge. The game will absolutely floor you with its unique art style and presentation, catchy tunes, and voluptuous cast of characters to talk to and interact with. The gimmicks in the game feel so directly tethered with the central themes put out there that nothing feels out of place (e.g., the peasant dying and you playing as a new one every time, the progression systems in place, etc.)The game itself is incredibly approachable; as stated above, you can see that my family consists of a varied group of gamers. Despite what makes us different, I am fully entertained as a hardcore gamer, my wife is still very much so interested in the game despite its challenges, and my son loves the presentation of the game. For some, this game will be challenging, but it is fair. I see some reviews on here complain about the slimes, the progression system, or the combat. I find this interesting because the slime mechanic turns out to be one of the funniest ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ things I have seen in some time; wacking those little bastards and listening to them do a Kirby-esque scream as they projectile off the screen is hysterical. The loss of gold upon death is part of the experience; upgrades start cheap enough to help give you the necessary buffer to learn how the game functions within, but the progression to be had here is truly on you as the player. You can bump up your damage or have a higher HP count, but if you really can't deal with the dynamics of the game, you aren't going to progress. Also, you can upgrade your bag, so you don't have to lose as much gold each time you die! As for the combat, there are literally three mechanics: swing, throw or bomb. Time your swings with the behaviors of the enemies, use the throw for long distance combat or to kite enemies around, or bomb stationary targets. This is a simple system with not much strategy involved despite how fun it is. If this challenges you to the point that you are not having fun, this genre in general might not be for you.On the other side of the spectrum, gamers who frequent games like Enter the Gungeon and other titles in the Bullet Hell genre are going to feel like this game moves a snail's pace. Even the most frenetic moments can be boiled down to patterns that all the monsters behave in, and a smart gamer will be able to predict, and outmaneuver these moments. I have found myself most frequently dying when I, the player, am tired and not paying attention, not because the game outpaced me or caught me off guard. That is what will kill these kinds of players, not the game.For an early access game, this title has a lot of content. I have made it to the bottom of the UnderMine and beaten all of the bosses; I am currently working on rescuing everyone that I have missed and re-beating the bosses that are now alive again. Some additions I hope to see in the full game are: female peasants for the player to play as, progression in the form of gear changes to clothing and items used as you purchase better equipment, and maybe some more variation in the sprites used (recolors always make me laugh, then cry a little). Overall, it's already an amazing game. I would recommend this title to any player looking for a game with a hell of a personality :)
_childDocuments_.name: UnderMine

_childDocuments_.review: Generally content-bare. Item unlock progression is painfully slow and bound to an extremely rare resource. I assumed most of the major content would be in the post-game but, surprise, it is just the normal game but with added difficulty modifiers and seemingly no kind of increased rewards. It seems like they wanted to do interesting item combinations and synergies, to the point that a handful of items will get an animation and new icon to denote their synergy, but it is so rare in an already very limited item pool as to seem like a waste of the graphic artists' time.I initially appreciated the jump feature as a breath of fresh air in a world of extremely boring and overdone I-frame rolls, but this soon proved to be a major annoyance when I realized items as well as your character can be bounced into pits and most damage can be dodged just by jumping so the addition of a height variable doesn't seem to add anything positive to the experience.The most interesting and charming thing about the game is the slimes that appear to steal your gold, 10/10 for this concept and its execution
_childDocuments_.name: UnderMine

_childDocuments_.review: The more i play the game the less fun it is because you realize there are a million different tiny bugs and rules to the game that just don't make sense like enemies having their attack damage you 1 second after completely disappearing from the screen and your hurtbox being taller than it is wide to certain chests drop their contents when being destroyed and others delete the contents Maybe If you put 100 hours into the game or if you enjoy eating poop and kicking yourself in the balls you can enjoy the game but other than those types of people you might as well not play it
_childDocuments_.name: UnderMine

_childDocuments_.review: Very good roguelite game. so good that i had to repurchase this on Steam after putting hours into the Nintendo switch version. System progression for your profile, meaning each run and each death will reward you as you level up  abilities. The longer you last, the more you play the better your character will get. The game still require skills and fast reactions, though. Be ready. Well worth owning and playing.
_childDocuments_.name: UnderMine

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not that skilled but this game isn't too punishing of that and it lets me go far in the game by grinding, which I really enjoy. I don't always have a lot of time to dedicate to games but this is easy to play in small chunks and pick back up again later. I love the art style and while the game can be repetitive it's also very rewarding
_childDocuments_.name: UnderMine

_childDocuments_.review: Very underwhelming and first impressions are you literally grind while smacking things with a pickaxe for marginal upgrades. Less like a roguelike, more like a RPG with random dungeons and runs, I feel like the gameplay loop must just be getting more gold to be stronger, rather than "getting lucky" like most roguelikes.
_childDocuments_.name: UnderMine

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. Any time I'm in a room with a bunch of enemies, I feel like I'm more than just a man with a plan and a pickaxe. I'm able to dodge attacks coming from melee and ranged, jump like a madman, and like CaptainSparklez once said, "Got [my] pickaxe swinging from side to side." It's really fun to progress in this game, and I like the concept of having a new character each time I go through a new run (as overpowered as you can become, you are still mortal, so it makes sense) and the only thing I wish for in this game is to be able to enjoy it with 1-3 other players. I think a multiplayer setting would make dungeons even more exciting because each member could specialize in a different playstyle and work as a team.
_childDocuments_.name: UnderMine

_childDocuments_.review: This caught my eye a while ago but the summer sale price was too tempting to pass up.  If you want a mashup of Zelda, Spelunky, Binding of Isaac, and Rogue Legacy this is definitely the game for you.  The addition to a jump with the top down view gives the combat a unique and dynamic edge, just remember that for once in a game like this you CAN jump.  Great game, if you were thinking about it, go ahead and get it before it's out of Early Access.
_childDocuments_.name: UnderMine

_childDocuments_.review: I take back almost everything I said about this game in my previous review. This is just BAD! I previously didn't realize why people were saying this has bad combat system, well now I do. You literally play as a miner but you're supposed to now fight enemies underground with JUST the hammer with swings and throws. An utterly lack luster boring combat system. This is the first game I've ever played where dying is actually a feature. How so? If I supposedly find an npc underground and free it, apparently I can't have access to it because that npc goes back to the surface but the player can't do the same unless THEY DIE and lose 95% of the loot they collected. The character selection is basically random characters entering the cave which are just forced upon the player, no customization or choice. Sometimes chest are covered in stone, guess what? You can't break those with the hammer. Also with my almost 16 hours gameplay of this, it seems to me it is trying to make players keep dying until they up their stats to max. This game is named Undermine but according to me this should've been named Underwhelm, because that's what it does really. I can't believe I rated this 6/10 before, now I'll give this what I think this truly deserves. 0/10. I wasted my 4.09$ on this rubbish. Yeah sure that amount might not be much for westerners but I live in the sub-continent and with 4.09$ I could've had 4 days worth of meals. Since I've bought it and I can't return it, I plan to FINISH this game anyways. I know this will be lots of mental torture for me but I'm prepared to handle it.Don't buy this game, it's a total waste of your time and money which you can spend on much better things.
_childDocuments_.name: UnderMine

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun "rogue like" game. Seemingly Endless adventure, it rewards skilled players, but allows those that are maybe less mechanically inclined to grind up to the point where loot makes up for part of the skill gap. Very fun, and offers end-game challenges for those that feel the need to take their gameplay up another tier. Very fun, Easy to spend endless hours grinding away in.
_childDocuments_.name: UnderMine

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR - This game is not worth it's 20$ price tag. Maybe worth it when it’s closer to 5$.Pros -It's really fun starting out and getting some cool things that constantly change your game and surprises you with some cool mechanics.The sprites and the music are very well done. I have the Bathcat/Toadvine track stuck in my head right now.Cons -Very repetitive overall and even though it seems like the rooms are random, you really start to see that they are not random but randomly place pre-made rooms. Very short game that gives the fake sense of content by ‘hexing’ you after you beat it and you do it again but harder.RNG is not your friend and it never will be. I went almost 5 floors without finding a single key and only 2 bombs, and on a few runs I was completely locked out of any sort of path forward and had to use the ‘give up’ option in the menu. This should never happen.The jumping mechanic feels extremely clunky and a huge problem being that it is your primary way of dodging attacks.

_childDocuments_.review: Tried it out on Game Pass, and came soon after to buy it here.  Undermine is a charming entry into the Roguelike/lite genre.  Solid graphics, music, sounds, and controls.  It's fun to start, but once you unlock the priestess and can fully dive into the blessing/curse mechanics, things can get crazy cool.
_childDocuments_.name: UnderMine

_childDocuments_.review: I have a soft spot for dungeon crawlers, Undermine is no different. The amount of relics, secrets, constantly changing rooms, curses, blessings, and items gives the game a metric ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ of replayability. Extremely luck based? Absolutely. Does skill still matter? Of course. Even though it's still early access I could see this being the fully released product, although I remain excited for what's to come.
_childDocuments_.name: UnderMine

_childDocuments_.review: A good game should get a positive review. It's early access. But at it's best.I run in no bug even after playing ~50 hours.Seems to be updated constantly. A graphic style I like. Upgrade system so u get stronger each run. A lot of items/relics blessings and curses. Makes nearly every run unique.Pets with unique skills.Makes fun. If u like games like binding of Issac the chance is high u will like this one too. For the road map see the homepage.I can't await the next update. 😁
_childDocuments_.name: UnderMine

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good game and very fun, but is incredibly flawed.After 10 hours it feels like I made no progress. I can see what people mean now when they say it feels grindy, you almost NEED to upgrade all of your tools, armour and gold supply in order to feel like you are powerful enough to continue on.You can be 30 minutes into a run and you will only be in the dungeon area and judging by the big rock with the boss medallion things in it, I am assuming there is a few more areas I have yet to even look at. To be fair, you could just rush your way down the pits (It works like Stardew Valley if you mined in that game, area progression works the same way), however you will have to be god tier with your pick axe where you can only swing a few pixels in front of you.Also with your relics, there isn't a single relic that I am hoping to get. The one thing I love about rogue-likes is that there is usually a few different power ups that you are just hoping to get that helped a ton in previous runs. In this game, maybe the most useful I have seen is the axe that makes your swing bigger. The rest that I have seen so far almost feel like they just deal with annoyances rather then actually help with a run. Like that bomb that explodes in 4 different directions, its nice to destroy as much rocks as possible for powerups but I can't say you really need it as bombs are so RNG to the point where some runs you feel absolutely rich with explosives and others you feel like your desperate.Also... oh god the pits in this game are the dumbest thing ever. They are only there to annoy you. I would have rather the devs make the pits have invisible barriers and remove the jump mechanic all together. The jump mechanic is incredibly pointless and just doesn't work with the top-down camera view. It is so incredibly frustrating to being almost an hour into a run and you accidentally fall into a pit when trying to grab a steak and die. Dumbest thing in this game.That being said, here's some positives and general notes- Combat is fluid and fair, although not very interesting. Still fun and satisfying to hit things though.- The art style is charming, maybe a bit too generic and doesn't feel like it's own thing but still nice to look at.- I like the music, although that shop theme drives me nuts.- There are characters with names and such but they feel flat and uninteresting where you don't really care at all about them and just use them for their resources.- I think curses are a bit much sometimes and only 1 curse can destroy a run which sucks (There's one that takes away your potion slot, there is one that makes all locked doors only open with your health, there is one for when you get damaged there is chance you will lose a key... which happens a lot etc.)With all my negatives, it is still a generally fun game but I would 100% wait for a sale. As rogue-like it is an incredibly frustrating experience and progression feels slow and tedious at times. The game is still very addictive and will continue to play and at least see what the ending is.
_childDocuments_.name: UnderMine

_childDocuments_.review: I typically like rogue-like games. This one is simply not fun at all.  The game pacing make it practically unplayable when you get dropped into a small room with 10 fast-moving nasties--which is a very common occurrence .  Losing items on death isn't that big of a deal, but considering you need gold to purchase items and then lose at a minimum half your gold on a death, you end up spinning your wheels and making no progress for the most part. 90 minutes in and deleted. Sorry.
_childDocuments_.name: UnderMine

_childDocuments_.review: Undermine is fun and slightly addictive. I really enjoy leveling up. You cannot expect to live at first and you have to work at collecting as much gold as you can so you can level up. A lot of the collected gold is lost when you die and buying things on the surface is the only way to permanently level your character, so save up before  you do die. It is frustrating sometime when you cannot find the food or items you need in the level you need them, but such is life. _childDocuments_.review: Overall Undermine is a promising game that plays almost exactly as advertised. The RPG elements and steady leveling are highly reminiscent of Rogue Legacy. Rooms are fairly varied in design so it takes a while for them to get repetitive. It looks like there is a lot of room for growth here, with multiple types of minions/familiars and many different types of artifacts to be unlocked.This is a very polished game, especially for an EA title, and I found no bugs or game breaking concerns. It is fun and held my attention for a good 16 hours.  Ultimately it got to be a bit stale, but I think that it will only improve as new content and features are added. _childDocuments_.name: UnderMine

_childDocuments_.review: As a veteran fan of both traditional roguelikes and roguelites, I can safely say that Undermine is an average game at best. If this game is your first game of this genre, then yeah I can see you getting hooked, but when compared to some of the offers out there, it falls quite flat.While on a first glance, this game seems to have all of the markings of an indie gem: cute and appealing art, polished interface, catchy music, etc. But the truth is that Undermine doesn't bring anything new or even interesting to the table. Many other games did the same gameplay loop much better, either with more interesting mechanics or more compelling randomization.Even worse, this game pads out and tries to hide its barebones gameplay with the grind of the meta progression: all of the progression costs a hefty amount for what you can reasonably gather in a run, and of course you need it because by the 3th and 4th dungeons the enemies start hitting like a freight train. And therefore you'll have to run the initial dungeons over and over, engaging with the repetitive, uninspired and limited combat. As I mentioned in the 2nd paragraph, despite its aparent well polished aesthetic, once you get past that veil of lies you'll see the souless core whitin.If you're young or new to roguelites then yeah sure give this a try and honestly I won't blame you if you have fun with it. But for the veterans like myself I can safely say to skip this one.
_childDocuments_.name: UnderMine

_childDocuments_.review: A great rogue-like with a unique combat system and story.Out of all roguelikes I've played, I think this is one I've enjoyed the most followed closely by Risk of Rain 2. This game has a great combat system that becomes most comfortable and natural as you play the game, allowing you to dig deeper and deeper into the story and collectibles as you learn and adapt. The characters, items, curses, blessings, bosses, and pets help to make this game feel less than a typical rogue-like and more like its own unique game. I've done most things you can do in this game (If we are referring to Steam Achievements), so I can say there is a lot to do in the base game and a lot more if you want to pursue challenges and achievements.If you are looking for another rogue-like game with a lot of replayability, I think you'll be surprised by what this game has to offer outside of its cover. I am looking ahead towards Undermine 2 with all of this in mind. I know Thorium can reproduce what made this game special and I hope they can add more to make it a unique installment.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who's typically put off by pixelated games (personal preference) I was surprised by how much I loved Undermine. I think it might be one of the best-paced games of its kind - you get enough roguelike randomness to make each run feel fresh and unique, but there's just enough similarity between each run for you to learn from the previous run's mistakes and apply those lessons to your current run. If you're struggling and are waiting for that next upgrade to make things easier, the amount of time required to get it will be similar to the amount of time you'd need to outskill the place you're stuck in so you often end up with the satisfaction of beating a challenge and an extra boost on top. The power ups are nice and diverse - you can try and "spec" into a specific build (e.g. ranged or melee) or have just as much fun with the pure random ones.Overall, I'd highly recommend this game. It's made by people who clearly love playing Undermine themselves and it shows in the patch notes - they focus on improving the gameplay every time instead of broadening the appeal, so if you like the game during your first few hours, you're only going to like it more two months in!

_childDocuments_.review: It isn't fun?It markets itself as a quirky, fun rouguelike with a lot of variation. Unfortunately, lack of variation is exactly what kills this game for me, and probably many others.One of the problems this game suffers with the most is that you (effectively) only have two weapons, melee attacks, and a thrown pickaxe. You can upgrade those, kinda, but those are the only weapons you will ever get, compared to many other Roguelikes with hosts of unique guns or swords or whatever. But it gets worse - You really only have one weapon, because attempting melee astronomically increases the chance of taking damage, and in this game, where healing is sparce, you can't take that risk. This leads to only throwing your boomerang-pickaxe, and constantly spamming the throw button as you frantically dodge bullets. Additionally, the rooms are nothing special. They are fairly varied, but only in ways that give you more things to worry about - holes you fall into, water that can be electrocuted, oil that slows you down and sets you on fire, and just random bomb barrels. A good 50% of the damage you take in a run will be ambient room damage, which is really, really annoying. Also, the game is unbearably grindy. Each run, you take all of your money with you into the dungeon (Why? who tf knows), and when  you die, you lose 20-50% of it, the idea being that each run, you get enough new gold to cover the losses of the  gold you just lost, and then you can use that gold to buy permanent upgrades. But, sometimes you just don't. Bad luck might have you die on lvl 1 with 100k gold from you last run where you got to lvl 12 or something, and you lose an astronomical amount of money. And because you constantly lose money, you have to grind the game over, and over, and over, to get literally anything. I had no idea a rougelike could be so grindy.ALSO, another issue is the upgrades. In terms of the relics, 40% of the time, the relic you get is just useless, 55% of the time, the relic you get is just +throw damage or +melee damage, and only in the final 5% of relics is the relic actually interesting or changes your playstyle at all. The +damage relics are incredibly monotonous, too - - More damage for each key you have!- More throw damage!- More damage the lower your health is!- More melee damage the more health you have!- More damage after throwing your pickaxe!- More throw critical damage!Soooo many of the relics are just mindless increases in damage, which really don't make for interesting runs. Anyway. Overall, the game is monotonous and grindy. It is fun to play for the first ~6-10 hours, but rapidly spirals downhill after that. I would not recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: I liked Undermine, still do, in fact. This should come as a surprise as I hate platformers, didn't like Binding of Isaac nor most roguelikes (except the originals, like, well, Rogue). But Undermine has a nice mix between simple but mechanically polished combat and well-managed RNG that keeps runs fresh while avoiding an overly binary role in which a run's success depends solely on RNG. I've found that you can have great runs despite having a bad start. Skill matters, decisions matter, even if they're decisions between bad choices.It's also a beautiful game, with good art, interesting character models and a great deal of visual clarity (this is important in a game that sometimes turns into bullet hell). I liked the sound design, the depth and a large variety of different items and mechanics (the blessing system is especially fun as every  bonus always comes with a malus - which, though, you can remove eventually.)It's not an especially long game. It has 5 levels, which you probably want to replay several times, and there are additional mechanics that facilitate this, including the fact that you probably will have unlocked a small number of items on your first few runs, and haven't played around with all the possible builds yet. As you progress, you can increase difficulty with each successful run, although, you don't have to. There are small gripes. The final boss feels quite tacked on, and goes against much of what made the game great: you don't get to make a build or bring items. It's just two back-to-back boss fights that you have to win naked. This has the notorious flaw of having to go through the cut scenes, albeit brief, every time you want to attempt the boss. It took me about 10 tries, and I was already sick and tired of it. Besides this, the runs still remain fresh and fun. All in all, I think this is one of the most polished and accessible roguelites, and from the games I've tried, only second to Slay the Spire in this genre.

_childDocuments_.review: Great graphics, but a fundamentally flawed game. While I did play through it, and beat it. I can't see myself playing it any more. While it's a "rouge-like" it actually isn't, while I enjoy rougelikes, this borrows some elements from the genre and doesnt do a good job balancing them together. Ill give a couple examples.It's a game where you have to build up gold per run then to spend on upgrades. The thing is though, its not really possible to beat the game until you've died a bunch of times. So it forces you to rerun it over and over, which is fine for a roguelike, but the problem isn't that you're getting better exactly, you're just playing for long enough to have the game lower it's own difficulty for you. So in that sense, a game like spelunky where you can beat it all the way through in a run, is nice, and in theory something like this seems nice. But then once you're close to beating the end boss and have maxed out all your upgrades, all those lower bosses that were enjoyable boss battles once, just become chores.Lack of clarity for a variety of complex mechanics. I was on a good run recently, I picked up a "curse" bottle. thinking it was something I could drink, or swap out, I went ahead and picked it up, anticipating I might find a "clear 5 curses bottle". upon picking it up, I got like two dozen curses. it basically ended my run right there in the most painful way possible. What the game made seem like a slight debuff was a slap in the face. While roguelikes are painful, and unforgiving, they are at least fair generally. Well, at least the good ones are (which is why I'm saying no on the recommend)Uninspired procedural generation. Collecting gold, running through maps, its all just a huge chore. The game was fun for a little bit, and if you enjoy a grind then get a playthrough out of it, but it's all just so grindy, and unrewarding at the end. I'm kind of left with, why??I hate to say it, because the art is great, and I feel there was a ton of love dumped into that. But unfortunately, amazingly smooth pixel art doesn't translate a quality game. The guy has some great pixel art of his dogs. That's cute and all, but I was left asking myself when seeing those. How many hours went into this art? and how many hours went into game design? I feel like the relics obviously had a ton of game design theory put into them for all the ways they affect mechanics, but then the problem is that it's all just a slot machine. You're just hoping for a lucky run where it drops the right combo of items and doesn't hit you with too many "gotcha" situations for a win. It's a roguelike in the worst ways in that, it's not skill can prevail a bad run, it's that a good run is dependent upon your lucky pickups, and maybe you can win off of that.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing rogue like capturing everything that I deem essential in a beautifully wrapped package.  The unique mobs, combined with interesting choices in itemization and character development make for a very replay able experience.   The procedural generation for the rooms and layout is very impressive to me and works in synergy with the abilities of the mobs that may spawn at that location. _childDocuments_.name: UnderMine

_childDocuments_.review: Looks like Zelda Links Awakening meets Enter The Gungeon. If you liked Gungeon then this good to get. Has a lot of similarities as gungeon; runs to unlock characters in your base [smith, potion maker, ext] sometimes these runs need to be done over and over to find and gather certain items to then give to an npc to unlock another. A slew of different perks in the way of items and treasure you collect. Also has curses.Hidden levels and bosses. Hidden rooms galore.Doesn't have the bullet hell part of gungeon however. The meh:I've seen the game cheat on me 3-4 times; entering a room and it pushes me into a pit or spikes. It tends to chain attacks which leaves you open to get mauled by nasties. There have been death rooms, which are small rooms with a lot of nasties and high level nasties. One of the achievs is beat 30 times in a row, each run averages about 45-60 minutes. _childDocuments_.name: UnderMine

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly good in the early, mid and late-game. It is only after unlocking all of the content that the game falls short, where other genre-defining roguelikes shine -- the end game. After unlocking all content, you've likely already seen most of the combinations as cycling through 60-70% of the items in a single run is not uncommon, nor is it difficult. This is still a home-run of a game, with remaining opportunities to enrich end-game content with rare encounters and even more difficult enemies (and proportionally epic rewards). The art style is pixel-oriented but still has its own character. The music is charming and appropriate.The extremely early game and extremely end game both could use difficulty tweaks:- early game w/o blessings and w/o familiars or good items seems not very fun (fun measured in this case as discovery and progression in mechanics of the game). Runs tend to be cut extremely short and gold cannot be retained. It is a grind but not a particularly fun grind- Very late game with familars, blessings, items, potions, experience of the game, and upgrades is entirely too easy. As I mentioned before, where the great roguelike titles shine is the ability to maintain a challenging and enticing run after thousands.If you're a fan of Roguelikes, buy this game.Recommended price range: 20-30USDRating (03/05/2020): 4/5

_childDocuments_.review: One of my favorite rogue-like/lites. There's an old saying I heard about creating things: You basically have two choices. Highly polished, entirely replayable, good stuff, amazing version of a song you already know by heart. Ain't nothing wrong with that at all.10/10, would mine again.

_childDocuments_.review: Not a fan of how the game feels like doing whatever it feels like doing instead of the inputs I press to do a certain action.Like maybe it's just visually incorrect, because it doesn't look like I'm standing in oil, but I still can't jump.Or the game being inconsistent on how far you can jump because sometimes with a running start I'll jump two blocks, and others I'll jump one. So it's this game of wondering if you'll jump 2 blocks away and avoid taking damage, or jump 1 block and take damage which isn't very fun. I don't understand why you would have multiple outcomes for the same key presses. It's like RNG on whether or not you dodge, rather than being unable to jump two blocks if something is in the way, which wasn't the case, ever while I was playing this game.Like that would also be a strategy to stagger your dodge to avoid getting too far away, but this isn't the kind of game where it takes that into account. You're airborne the same amount of time regardless of how far you jump. It doesn't make any sense. The input necessary to jump just one tile is so finicky. Because most of the time I jump what seems to be less than a block, and the hitbox of a spike is more than a block. The game also sometimes decides that I wanted to pick something up, or wanted to click on something, even though I didn't. It just so happens that the action button for interacting is the same as the action button for attacking, or rather defending yourself. So even though you wanted to kill something, you accidentally interacted with something and it ate your swing input and you take a hit or you interacted with a hole and went deeper into the mines or dungeons rather than open a chest that spawned right next to it. Like this game's been out for a while, and man, oh man, did I not miss this kind of game.  The indicators for half the things are nonexistent so it's annoying having to guess rather than predict. Like even an audio indication of where on the screen the worm boss will appear from would've gone a long way, instead it's just mono audio and it could literally appear from anywhere. Like, I don't care if this boss is piss easy and I've already killed it three times in a span of twenty minutes.It's still f*ckin annoying dude.Get it on sale. F*ck the base price.
