_childDocuments_.review: Bugsnax is probably one of my top 5 favorite games in recent years. This game not only has adorable graphics, fun and varied environments, a plethora of cute and silly creatures to discover, and interesting mechanics that allow you to experiment and find your own methods of progressing - it also has one of the best stories in a game that I've seen. The developers also added free DLC earlier this year - the Isle of BIGsnax - which added even more story content, lore, and cute game features at absolutely no extra charge.The story topics are presented in a way that is approachable for older children and adults alike, with humor mixing in perfectly alongside more serious discussions that don't talk down to their audience. The characters feel real and have real issues; difficulties with intimacy, with their self-worth, with their mental health, and with their place in the world. Through the course of the game you are able to follow the characters in how they try to confront these issues, and there are some extremely good life lessons in there which I think anyone of any age would do well to think on. And, of course, the characters are funny muppets eating food-shaped creatures with googly eyes - the game knows this and knows how ridiculous it is, and isn't afraid to poke fun at itself at times. All in all, it's a wonderful experience and well worth the time and money.

_childDocuments_.review: Let's dive into Bugsnax. This oddball odyssey by Young Horses serves up charm and humor that keep its gameplay engaging over its 9 to 10-hour duration. Despite the baffling trailers, Bugsnax is a story-driven first-person adventure with light puzzles, surprising depth, and delightful character development. It might not flaunt PlayStation 5's power, but Snaktooth Island is a must-visit—just be cautious about overindulging in its wildlife cuisine.In Bugsnax, you're a news reporter brought to Snaktooth Island by explorer Elizabert Megafig to cover its edible creatures. Yep, Bugsnax are animals that mutate consumers upon consumption. Totally normal, right? The island's inhabitants, grumpuses (fur-covered humans), add to the delightful chaos.Bugsnax are a visual treat, with distinct appearances from flying pizzas to swimming soda cans. The Spuddy, a butter-topped potato charging at you, is a personal favorite.The main task is rallying Snaxburg's residents back home for interviews. But each grumpus has requests, and Bugsnax, being the primary food source, are crucial. While the missions follow a similar pattern, top-notch writing and voice acting keep each grumpus unique and engaging.Bugsnax is absurd but also meaningful, touching on subjects like relationships, mental health, and loss. The humor keeps things light, and the game is full of laughter, both from the creatures and the grumpuses.Catching Bugsnax involves scanning them with your camera and using tools to nab them. The metroidvania-like elements add depth. However, the real magic is in Bugsnax's storytelling, keeping you hooked with its characters and narrative surprises.Bugsnax is odd and delightful. Its gameplay might have moments of repetition, but its heart—its story and characters—makes the journey worth it. It's a story with over 100 Bugsnax to discover, somehow making you care for these quirky critters.Anyways this game is a trip, have fun!

_childDocuments_.review: I know that the Pokémon comparison with this game is worn out by now, but the best way to break this game down to one sentence is that it's Pokémon if it's main focus is catching creatures and ditches the battles entirely.The gameplay loop is fantastic. You get simple but fun quests, you go to an area to catch whatever wacky creature (called Snax) you need, then you go back to town and feed caught creature to one of the goofy village people. It's a game that thrives on variety, with each new area introducing a new batch of interesting and memorable critters to catch.The story and characters are also unexpectedly great. It's not groundbreaking, but considering that I went into this game only really expecting a bug-catching adventure, it was a genuine surprise to me that the narrative was more than decent. It's also surprisingly quite mature at some points, especially at the end.Controls can be a bit annoying sometimes. Some of the Snax you have to catch require good timing, and I wish there was a separate button for closing the net instead of me having to awkwardly scroll to the net while the little guy I have to get skitters away. The Trip-Shot also feels a bit off to use sometimes, like sometimes it just doesn't work or won't attach. The game is also not really replayable. Once you're done with the content on your first run, you don't really have much a reason to play it again.The game is very much targeted to kids, so it might not be for everyone, but I love it to bits personally.

_childDocuments_.review: Talkin' bout bugsnax~The representation in this game is really well done. lgbt characters are obviously lgbt, but aren't highlighted and shoved into the players face as some kind of trophy or abnormality. no, instead, these characters are introduced the same way the rest are. Most movies, games, etc, treat lgbt+ characters as if they are unique, that it isn't common or normal to be part of that community- Many only include gay characters simply to say that they, in fact, included a gay character. _childDocuments_.review: This is one of the strangest games I've played in a while. It's a creature collector, but there's no combat. Instead you actually find creative ways of using different hunting tools in combination with the environment to find a way to stun or otherwise capture each of the creatures. That's not what makes it weird though. The story behind this game is that these muppet monsters found an island where all of the animals are hamburgers, baked potatoes, birthday cakes, pineapples, and cheesy poofs. Those are bugsnax. They're the most delicious things ever, and eating them turns the muppets' arms, legs, teeth, and eventually their whole body into the bugsnak they ate. You're the local bugsnak hunter, so you just go around mutating the whole town willy nilly just to make them look stupid. It was delightful.

_childDocuments_.review: Kinda bug and kinda snack Bugsnax is what I personally want from gaming; just devs having a great time making something fun, with a lot of heart. You can tell a lot of effort went into crafting the Grumpuses (Grumpus’?) personalities and the Snax. Each character brings a lot of, well, character, each bringing a different personality to the table and maintaining good (or intentionally bad!) chemistry with the other characters. (I personally believe in Snorpy and Chandlo supremacy :D)THE SNAX:The best part of the game. Goofy lil dudes with goofy little designs. I caught myself smiling many times upon seeing new snax for the first time. Also, shout out to the voice actors for the snax, because they sold those lines. Very goofy, and obscenely silly. I often think fondly of the sounds Bopsicle and Scoopy Banoopy make.THE STORY:You play as an investigative journalist who’s on a last ditch effort to save their job after receiving an invitation from Elizabert Megafig on Snacktooth Island. A bit of mystery, a bit of seriousness, a lot of fun ensues. Your job is to find out what is going on on the island, as well as finding out what happened to Elizabert. Without spoiling anything, do all the loyalty missions for your buds in snaxburg (why wouldn’t you? They’re your buds!) for the best and happiest ending. Overall, this game is fantastic and if you’re looking for something short, sweet, with a lot of heart, buy it. I was not disappointed, and would gladly pay full price again.

_childDocuments_.review: I went into this game not expecting much. My girlfriend mentioned it, I got it on sale for her to play, but apparently she'd already played it. She also said it was a horror game, which kept me from refunding it. Let me just say, this game is 100 percent worth playing. It starts off a little cringe, the characters all suck in their own ways, whether they are annoying or just irritating, but the game goes out of its way to humanize them all. It gives them all traits and backstories that explain these poor behaviors, and you can help them all better themselves to become better people. Like one character is obsessed with getting bigger and stronger, but never seems to be able to, and you have to help him learn to accept himself and improve other aspects of his life. One other case is a washed out pop singer who had a one hit wonder and never made it big again, and you have to help her learn how to stop living in the past and move on. The game appeared to be nothing more than telling a message about how the worst people can still be fixed, with one character who seems a little crazier than the rest less than subtly hinting at a major plot twist in the end. I didn't believe that character, she genuinely seemed like a loony, so when the plot twist she was warning about came it caught me so off guard and fully explained the "horror" aspect of the game. You're basically conditioned by the game not to pay attention to the very obvious plot twist that's building up, every chance the game gets it would downplay it. Someone asks something like, "Where do the bugsnax come from?" and someone else basically says "It's just a game it doesn't need an explanation." Stuff like that is said so often that you actually start to think its true, until the truth thats being teased right under your nose is exposed and the whole game changes. You play the game the first time thinking it's just a cute creature collector, and the second playthrough actually feels eerie, knowing exactly what the bugsnax are and all. I've said too much though, the Grumpinati is listening, you'll have to play the game for yourself to learn more.
_childDocuments_.name: Bugsnax

_childDocuments_.review: Everything in this game lacks depth. The creature-catching mechanic isn’t particularly challenging and involves no real strategy. After catching a few Bugsnax, it quickly becomes repetitive and uninteresting. The characters are very generic, have the emotional depth of a puddle, and are generally annoying, failing to create any meaningful connection. Technically, while most of the game ran fine, I experienced a significant number of bugs with the game's scripted events, and the boss fights with the legendary Bugsnax are poorly executed.Also, I don't understand why people describe the game as horrifying. There's nothing remotely scary or macabre here. It honestly feels like I played a different game than everybody else. I don't hold this against the game, as it doesn't market itself as such, but I'm genuinely confused by the experiences others describe.With that being said, and while I don't recommend this game for the reasons described, I don't want to be completely negative. It’s not a bad game. It's cozy and cute, and customizing your villagers with the Bugsnax is amusing.This game might be really good for children or someone looking for a limited, chill game to scratch their critter-collecting itch. However, if you're looking for a game with more substance, this is certainly not it.

_childDocuments_.review: The story of this game is captivating and has meaningful side quests to it. There's a few on-running jokes in the game and callback humor. _childDocuments_.name: Bugsnax

_childDocuments_.review: It is quite rare for me to thoroughly enjoy a game as much as I did this little gem. Bugsnax is a creature collector game, that focuses a lot on the methods and ways you catch these creatures. The game gives you tons of different tools and traps to catch the various different types of Bugsnax with, and the true of fun of this game is figuring out all the different clever ways the game wants you to capture a Bugsnax. I've seen a lot of people compare this game to Pokemon, but it is much more in line with something like Ape Escape in my opinion. Pair this game's charming writing with it's addictive gameplay loop, and the rather cute Jim Henson inspired art design, and you have a game that is more than worth the price of admission. Delightful experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Bugsnax

_childDocuments_.review: I've just finished the game, so here are my thoughts. Bugsnax is a psychological horror game dressed up as a cutesy, fun adventure. Without diving too far into details: You're a journalist that goes to an island to find another character that has gone missing. While there, you end up receiving the aid of (and aiding) the other characters that have settled there. You catch "bugsnax" to feed the others  I enjoyed the story, and all the aesthetic cuteness of the bugsnax and the art style itself. The soundtrack is fun and energetic, and all the lines are well voiced and well written. The characters are interesting and each have their own depth and fun stories.  My one complaint is probably the amount of steps it takes to catch some of the bugs... I'm embarrassed to say I had to look up quite a few of them to understand how I was supposed to go through the process. In any case, I certainly recommend it. All of the achievements can be done fairly easily, with maybe only a few select ones being "out of the way" of the main story line.
_childDocuments_.name: Bugsnax

_childDocuments_.review: Bugsnax has quite a bit in common with Slime Rancher, IMO: - Gameplay focus on exploring biomes to catch weird but cute creatures. The main thing players are meant to do with these creatures, is kinda gross in both cases, but also kinda addictive (at least to me)- The story and NPCs start off seeming like they'll be just be cute, funny and simplistic, and at first there's only hints about how they'll not be entirely happy. And then the games start sucker punching you with assorted existential crises. And the NPCs and story turn out to be deeper and sadder than what might've been initially expected (though in Bugsnax the NPCs get more fleshed out than in Slime Rancher, and unlike Bugsnax, I doubt that anyone could really call anything about Slime Rancher horror). Both games give a lot of bittersweet vibes. - They both have some quite a bit of diversity in their cast of characters, in different ways, and as far as I can tell, they both do pretty well with their main diversity focus? While Slime Rancher has some POC characters and just a few hints of LGBT+, Bugsnax has some very clearly LGBT+ characters, and a bit of racial coding. - They both have some pretty scenery, and very nice soundtracks, and it's fun decorating your placeDespite it's child-friendly look, Bugsnax has some adult themes sprinkled throughout it, but I think it's about the same level as an average Spongebob episode. Other than the level of tragedy that Bugsnax can reach. I guess if you're thinking of letting a little kid play this, you might want to watch a playthrough first - or maybe even do a quick playthrough of it yourself - including checking the possible bad endings, by leaving side quests incomplete. Then decide based on that. You could get through the game a lot faster than I did, there's just a lot of optional content.

_childDocuments_.review: I am pretty sure I did not "get" this game and I really tried too as you can tell by my playtime. However, I can not recommend it and I wish I could give a "Maybe" as a review instead of a "Yes" or "No".  There is surreal and then there is Muppet people with complex adult relationship issues who eat bugs that look like snack food. Figuring out strategies to catch bugsnax is satisfying, because some of them are actually pretty challenging and require planning and patience.I was drawn in by the cute food creatures, but got much more than I was expecting. The character design in this game is great, each of the bugsnax feel unique (with reskins between regions, which I thought was perfectly fine to do). All of the grumps have clear personalities even before you hear them talk. The voice acting is great. Paired with the great character design, the voice actors bring even more life to each character. I got this on sale, but I think it would be well worth it at full price.Replayability: I don't think I'd play this game again, but I could see someone wanting to go through at least one more playthrough if they didn't catch all the bugsnax on the first run.

_childDocuments_.review: I think the worst thing you could do to Bugsnax is discredit it as some kind of "Knack 2 baby" type joke game. A lot the reviews are just "bunger", and while its funny, I do really want to stress that there is actually a really lovely game here.A nice little ~8 hour experience, Bugsnax is a tight cozy little game that feels like a PS2-era title in all of the best ways. On release it was nicely polished right out the gate back in 2020, and the version now available on Steam is its final form with the free expansion that adds a bit more to do in terms of optional content.The cast is really great,  being my personal favorite. If you engage with the optional sidequests, the characters all have a bit more emotional depth than you would expect from a game like this, and you can tell the guys at Young Horses really wanted to pump some life into these characters. They actually handle a couple of themes in a really mature way, and I respect the heck out of them for sticking true to their ideas. Not to mention, their voice acting is really superb. Heck, you've got Ryuji and Morgana from Persona 5 voicing a couple of the grumpuses, and Shinji from the Netflix Evangelion dub.Main plot-wise, the obvious weird body horror of the bugsnax leaves you intrigued enough to see the story through to the end for sure just to figure out the mysteries. I think its a nice mix of charm and intrigue that this game's story will please most enough. I do think that the relationships between the other characters are really where this game shines though.I would describe the game as maybe a mix of Pokemon Snap, and Slime Rancher. Its pretty unique though. Imagine if instead of battling pokemon to capture them, you had to solve a little puzzle. With half-dozen gadgets, its surprising how many ways you need to utilize them to capture every single bugsnak.Beyond that, I actually really like the speed of your character in first person. The movement is surprisingly snappy and feels good. Heck I speedran this game back when it was only on Epic Games store. There's plenty of optional challenges and things to collect if you just wanna keep playing like I did, so everyone should be pleased.Random aside: I would describe the game as having a colorful PS2 aesthetic. I think a demake of this game would be really neat to see, honestly. The character/bugsnak designs are all really charming as well.The music is surprisingly great. Hits a nice chill semi vapor-wave feel thats just nice and cozy.With the main "Brokentooth Island" content spanning about ~2 hours, I think it was just a nice little extra piece. I really like the designs of the dozen new bugsnax, and they have a couple fun gimmicks. I also appreciate that they got to give some extra time to a few of the characters that didn't get quite as much limelight or instant love. As a returning player, I did really enjoy the 100-ish challenges that they added to unlock pieces of furniture for you house. Its a nice throwback to old games to actually give you rewards for challenges that aren't just "currency" of some sort. The house/furniture bit adds nothing to the game, but its just a really fun little bonus for people who want more time with the game. On top of that, the hats were a cute little touch too. I think their additions with this expansion were super smart, in that they added stuff to collect that was just fun enough to actually feel worth collecting, but not game-changing.The expansion was free, but I loved the additions. Great work.Said most of this at the beginning, but the game is really special. Its unlike most other stuff you can play these days, and I think basically anybody will have a great time with it.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, so looking at this Steam page and at the screenshots, you can probably conclude that this game isn't worth your time if you're above the age of 12. However, due to the writing and charm of Bugsnax, this game can be worth anyone's time.The characters were the biggest highlight for me. This game tackles some very serious themes and presents them in such mature and insightful ways. It was very off-putting to just to see how skillful the writing really is. When you meet all the characters, they start out as stereotypes, but as you get to know them, they begin to feel more like real, breathing people. There wasn't a single character I hated or even disliked, at least once I got to know them better.With the gameplay, it did get a bit boring for me. It started out great at first, where it treated the capturing of bugsnaxs more like puzzles. However, as you get all the tools (which happens really soon), it felt like 80% of the bugs can be simply caught with the use of a single tool (which I won't spoil here.) The game gave me so many options, but yet, I barely felt the need to use multiple tools together, which is a shame.Other than that, the only other flaw I can think of is that the AI of the bugs can break at certain points. It's nothing too bad, but I had a bug get stuck in a tree or even zoom into space.Overall, I recommend Bugsnax. If you're unsure about the gameplay, then I'd wait for sale. The writing made it worth it for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Bugsnax was quite fun. A remix of Cloudy with a Chance of Meatballs 2 where the bugsnaxs have to be caught to be eaten by the starving villagers of Snaxburg. It took me 24 hours to complete (it may take less time if you aren't interested in all the side quests and the mail quests).Story: You are a journalist and want to investigate the new discovery from Elizabert, an island with bugsnaxs. When you arrive on the island, Filbo is the only Grumpus in Snaxburg. You have to convince the others to come back, catching bugsnaxs with new equipment along the way. There are four bigger bugsnaxs that are part of side quests, and a big showdown at the end requiring a new variant of the equipment you've used so far. You do find Lizbert eventually, but she (and Eggabelle) won't be coming back with you to the city.After the credits (with pictures as a sort of epilogue), a conversation can be heard which might points to a sequel? Maybe? Pretty-please?

_childDocuments_.review: GAME OF THE YEAR... ok not really, but it was a great game. The gameplay is mostly about doing quests for the characters, which usually involves finding and capturing Bugsnax. Each Bugsnax has their own quirks and patterns, and you must use your tools, the environment, and other Bugsnax to capture them. The Bugsnax themselves have simple yet creative designs based on food and googly eyes, and they are very cute thanks to the excellent voice acting.This voice acting also helps with the story and character development, which is top notch. Each of the characters has well defined personalities, and the game explores their personal and psychological problems. Progressing on the main story and the sidequests makes you feel like you're helping them towards overcoming their problems, or at least, helping them understand them.The main story involves finding all the characters that are scattered through the island, interviewing them and gathering clues on the dissapearence of the town's leader (Lizbert) and the nature of the Bugsnax themselves. There's quite some lore, and the big mystery isn't revealed until the very end of the game (try to avoid spoilers!)Be warned that, while the game is overall very cute, the final segment of the game can be a bit disturbing, so I don't recommend this game to little kids and people who can't stomach abrupt changes like these easily. Otherwise, I highly recommend checking it out.

_childDocuments_.review: A strange but enjoyable game that I'm having a hard time classifying. You play as a journalist that's trying to get an interview with a renowned explorer but your boss (Laharl) is having none of it. You decide to find them anyway and go to an island that has an abundance of these adorable small creatures known as the Bugsnax. When you eat one a body part becomes whatever it was you ate. Well not you personally, you can't eat.  The game is a loop of finding someone, getting them to come back to the town that has been established, then a new area opens  up, rinse and repeat. While going to new areas you will complete side quests to better get to know the inhabitants and their overall point as to why they came to the island. Some stories didn't really do anything for me while others where oddly gripping. Not to spoil anything but there was a guillotine in one of them. The main story itself was interesting enough and by the end I was pretty happy with what I got from the game. Gameplay wise aside from the side quests you will essentially play Pokemon and catch all the Bugsnax to fill up your book full of entries. Not much else. That being said I was happy they let it come off of being an exclusive and put it on Steam. For $25 I can say it is worth the time to play. Also once you get an ending it unlocks a new island as DLC so don't think it's over just yet!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is one of my absolute favorites. While streaming Viva Pinata a friend said "What in the Bugsnax is this game?" and thus I was introduced to Bugsnax. This game is very similar to games such as Viva Pinata, Slime Rancher, Animal Crossing, and one could even say maybe Disney Dreamlight Valley. It is an adorable game where you collect Bugsnax and figure out what has happened to the Grumpuses (aka our main characters) that are living on Snaxtooth Island. Each Grumpus has such an in depth personality which makes them so lovable and able to connect with. I think having these diverse and in depth personalities is what kept drawing me back to the game. Each one of them is different, yet utterly adorable, and the sass that they can have makes interacting with them just that much more fun. I also liked the relationships between the characters themselves, including the development between a few (wink-wink). It was fun to see them gradually grow into their personalities and made the connection the player has with them so immersive. The graphics for this game is amazing. I would say that it is extremely similar to Slime Rancher in style. The graphics are astounding for this to not be a Triple A game and I appreciate the detail that went into creating this masterpiece of a game. Seriously so visually appealing. Artists, ya done good!The story line for this game was so fun and I had NO idea the ending that was going to take place! While 100% the game was a lot of running back and forth, everything from the graphics to the Grumpuses to the cute rewards you would get made it worth it! The story was coherent and made sense and the twists and turns along the way were shocking and exciting. The ending set it up to possibly be getting a Bugsnax 2, and I for one am screaming TAKE MY MONEY!!!! Young Horses, you did a great job with this game! I cannot wait to see what you give us next! (:

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so good that I bought it at full price on Steam despite having it on Epic Games.Gameplay wise, it's like a mix of Pokémon and Ape Escape, using one or two of six tools at your disposal to catch over a hundred unique creatures. The twist here is that these creatures are food as much as they are animals, so you're able to feed them to one of the many townsfolk and turn their body parts into these snax. There are so many to mess around with, so you could turn your friends into utter health hazard disasters, just a singular food, or my personal favorite, try to replicate their original look as close as possible using snax of similar colors and shape.Speaking of the townsfolk, you have 15 friends to accompany you, and they're all endearing and fun in their own ways. Some of these examples are a mayor who's trying his best while constantly being scrutinized, a stubborn farmer and a nihilistic archaeologist in a struggling relationship because of their different priorities, a very shy and paranoid animal husbandrist who refuses to eat any Bugsnax, a snooty valley girl who thinks everyone has a dirty secret, a washed up singer who has one single hit she isn't proud of, a grimy salesman who resorts to scummy tactics because he thinks that's the only way he can get by, a friendly and surprisingly wise jock, a conspiracy theorist nerd who has feelings for said jock, his scientific sibling who has scorn with everyone else and has morbid tendencies, A meditator who despises bugsnax and tries to stray people away from them, a doctor with serious self esteem problems, and her adventurous wife who mysteriously disappeared, of whom everyone wants to bring back to keep things together again. And while these characters look like weird muppets and may seem one note at first, as you delve into their side quests you can see just how deep they are, find answers as to why they act the way they do, I won't spoil any of them, but even those who might be your least favorites have a sympathetic reason for their actions, will improve by the end of the game, and overall I just came to love each and every one of them for who they are,Overall, while it might not be everyone's thing, I highly recommend this game to people who love upbeat cartoony games and story driven games with character arcs. It's one of my all time favorite games, and it's made by the same people who made Octodad, so you can't go wrong there!Cinnasnail is my baby and I love it so much.

_childDocuments_.review: Come for the cheerful visuals, fun creatures, and catch-em-all gameplay; stay for the shockingly deep and emotional stories of these strange muppet creatures as you gradually learn of the sadness that pervades their lives. Seriously, the characters in this game feel surprisingly human with their respective situations and complex relationships. I'm not usually one for narrative-driven games, but this game kept me invested all the way through and beyond.The free Isle of Bigsnax add-on adds an extra chapter that isn't super long, but lends even more insight into the characters and their lives before the game's events, which is always welcome. This was my third playthrough of the game after 100%-ing it twice on PS4, and I was never bored thanks to the new stuff. It even adds some new secrets to discover on the main island itself...I like the LGBT rep in this game. There's a lesbian couple, a gay couple, and a non-binary character, and it's all just part of the world without waving virtue flags or drawing attention to any of it. Which is how it should be if we want to normalize it in real life, IMO.One of the most pleasantly surprising games I've ever played. A must-have if you like deeply engaging characters and having the ability to transform them into food-based abominations.

_childDocuments_.review: isn't a perfect game, but it has a lot of heart.You play as a reporter who has answered the call to Snaktooth Isle, the supposed home of the titular, legendary Bugsnax, creatures that are "half bug, half snack." Not long before crashing on the island, you find out that the residents of the island are having problems and must help them to pursue your story. This, of course, mostly involves catching Bugsnax.The characters all have a charm once you get to know them, and the Snax themselves are all creative and cute. Some more so than others.Now, whenever a game like this comes out, the inevitable happens: comparisons to Pokémon. Other than being collectible critters that say their portmanteau pun names, there isn't much else that's similar.Unfortunately, the game does get a bit repetitive. In order to catch a Bugsnak, you need to figure out how to do so. Some can easily be caught by laying a trap in front of their path or even just walking up to them with your net. Others require using your different tools together, but none of them are truly that hard to get. The game is definitely geared for younger audiences in this regard.In the end, I overall enjoyed playing , and I would love to see the series expanded into something more.Also, *ahem* BUNGERBUNGERBUNGERBUNGERBUNGER!!!

_childDocuments_.review: This game isn't shy about the fact that it's heavily inspired by Pokemon. (One of the achievements is even called "gotta catch em all".) But at the same time, it's not remotely a rip-off of Pokemon; the gameplay style is completely different.So here's how the game plays out: You go out into one of several gorgeous biomes in search of Bugsnax. You employ a variety of tools, bait, environmental elements, and other Bugsnax to help you incapacitate the Bugsnak you want so you can capture it. Then you take your Bugsnax back to town and decide what to do with it – whether to have someone eat it, or just have it be a pet. You check in with people to get new requests for specific Bugsnax. And then it's back out to the wilds for your next hunt!If your favorite thing to do in Pokemon is catch new Pokemon and fill out the Pokedex, I think you'll like this game. There are no RPG elements in this game, which leaves room to flesh out the catching experience for all it's worth.I won't say anything about the story other than that it has layers. It's an iceberg - how far down the iceberg you delve is up to you.

_childDocuments_.review: Bugsnax is a cute bug collect-a-thon where you hang out with a group of misfits on a mysterious island. Using a wide variety of traps and tools, your goals are to catch them all and use those caught Snax in order to complete quests and unlock more and more of the island and more people to hang out in your village.Bugsnax is also a horror-lite. The creatures have the effect of transforming anyone that eats them, giving the game a light cover of body horror, and the further into the game you get, the more the horrifying truth of Snaktooth comes to light. Each person that lives in the village also has their own issues, from depression and anxiety, to not being able to bring back the old days, to feeling like they'll fail at everything they do, and the sidequests both touch on those topics and help put some resolution in them.If you can handle a bit of body horror, unsettling truths, watching cute furry critters discussing heavy topics, and don't mind a gameplay loop that consists of figuring out what tools you need to use to catch the critters in this game, I highly recommend giving this game a try. At the time of writing this, I have caught every single Bugsnax, completed every sidequest, satisfied every request, unlocked every achievement, and even finished the Isle of Bigsnax free expansion.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall impression: 9.5 out of 10. A great buy at full price. Bugsnax is clever, fun, and well designed all the way through. It is one of the best all-round games I have played in a long time.I will try to do a quick breakdown of what makes the game great without giving too many details. Players should dive in with little knowledge about the game and enjoy the ride.Pros: Deft writing that makes you care for even the more distasteful characters. Catching bugs is fun and requires a bit of puzzle solving without being overly complex. The overarching story is great. Learning about the various characters, their relationships, and the secrets of the island and the bugsnax is a great trip.Cons: I am having to nitpick, since the game is so good. Some of the mail challenges are either too obtuse or require way too much running around the island. The bugsnax on the DLC island are clever, but they lean too much toward being annoying in how you have to puzzle out how to capture them while avoiding the other bugsnax in the area.Conclusion: I read the great reviews and went in without spoilers. I am glad I did. Bugsnax is one of the best games I have played in a very long time.

_childDocuments_.review: Close to perfect. It's tagged psychological horror due to the tone being that it's all cute and carefree eating bugsnax, but it turns out there are some grim consequences of eating them . Gameplay is you learning the various strategies needed to capture each creature(there's a 100 unique creatures) in order to decorate your grumpus back at town, fulfill quests, and donating them to increase bag space for holding more bugsnax. You the player character are the only grumpus who can't eat bugsnax with the reason being that you're allergic and it's never discussed how the player charater could've sustained himself for so long without bugsnax.Going in blind and trying to capture some of these bugsnax for the first time can be quite a headache to learn each and every strategy as you're just given the tools and their basic use before having to figure out the full scope of possibilities. Some creatures require using several tools in conjunction with each other in order to capture them which is not readily apparent for example putting the snare trap on the launch pad and launching the snare trap at the creature on a wall or flying in the air. These more advanced techniques are something you'll learn after many attempts or just watching how to catch one of the bugsnax online, heck your method might be more efficient than the ones you found online.I completed the story and all side quests, but there was still very many tasks to complete which are more like challenges in order to get the rest of the decorations for your hut. Everything about your hut besides the bed is purely decoration. The 11 grumpus in your town are at your mercy in regards to how you want them to look as there's 14 areas of customization on each grumpus tthat you can place a bugsnax food at and with the 100 different creatures they can all be pretty unique from each other. After the credits they leave the door open for a sequel by .

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to enjoy this game, but the amount of tedious troubleshooting I've had to do just to get it to function has left a very, very bad taste in my mouth. I have never in my 10+ years of gaming been pushed away from a game due to technical difficulties, but I don't think I'll be returning to this game any time soon.The first hurdle I hit was that the game wouldn't utilize my GPU if I looked around at all. It worked fine as long as I didn't touch my mouse, but as soon as I looked in any direction the frames plummeted.  After about an hour of troubleshooting, changing to directx9, updating drivers, etc etc, it finally starts working and I begin to make my way through the game.The next hitch was just a hard crash to desktop without a warning, which was just weird but since it autosaved I wasn't really too bothered by it. The next time it happened, however, it decided to really screw up my audio. I use voicemeeter to split my audio tracks for streaming, so I don't know if it had to do with that or not, but it scrambled up my sounds so that discord/chrome worked fine, but the discord and windows notifications were going through a channel that by all means should have been audible, but wasn't. Same with the game, on the next launch I couldn't hear a thing, even though it was in the same track as audio from other applications that I could hear.. At this point, I'm through with it, maybe I'll give it another try in a little while but this has taken entirely too much troubleshooting for me to want to continue.That being said, I did enjoy the few hours it was functioning properly. And, for the record, I have a mid-end rig, so maybe I'm not up to the Bugsnax™ standard, but again, this is the first game I've had problems with in years.

_childDocuments_.review: Bugsnax is an adorable little game that adopts the 'catch them all' style of games like Pokemon. However, it is rich with lovable characters, all with their own relatable traits and issues. The story is delightfully simple and easy to follow but does have it's twists and turns here and there which will make you see the story in a whole new light! In addition, the character side quests gives you more time to bond and understand the character's passions and conflicts.For what it is worth to some, a handful of these characters are LGBTQ+ and the game handles them respectfully by not objectifying them by making their entire personality revolve around their sexuality - a rare feat in modern day media.

_childDocuments_.review: an extraordinary game that seamlessly combines whimsical charm with captivating gameplay. With its stunning graphics, immersive storyline, and delightful character designs, Bugsnax has undoubtedly established itself as an amazing and unforgettable gaming experience.From the moment you start playing Bugsnax, you'll be mesmerized by its breathtaking visual design. The game boasts a vibrant and colorful world that feels like a living, breathing ecosystem. Each area is meticulously crafted, featuring lush landscapes, detailed textures, and stunning lighting effects. The attention to detail in the environments and the bugsnax themselves is truly commendable, making every moment of exploration a visual treat.Bugsnax presents an intriguing and unique premise that keeps players engaged throughout their adventure. As a journalist invited to Snaktooth Island, you'll uncover the mysteries of Bugsnax and their transformational effects on the island's inhabitants. The narrative gradually unfolds, revealing surprising twists and heartfelt moments that leave a lasting impact. The well-paced storytelling combined with charming dialogue and memorable characters ensures a compelling journey from start to finish.Bugsnax features a delightful cast of characters, each with their own quirks and personalities. From the curious and adventurous Filbo to the enigmatic explorer Lizbert, the characters are brought to life through fantastic voice acting and endearing animations. Additionally, the Bugsnax themselves are creatively designed, featuring imaginative combinations of bugs and snacks. Their diverse appearances and abilities add an extra layer of excitement and discovery as you encounter and capture them. The gameplay in Bugsnax strikes a perfect balance between exploration, puzzle-solving, and creature capture mechanics. As you traverse Snaktooth Island, you'll encounter various Bugsnax species with distinct behaviors and characteristics. Strategically using your tools, you'll need to devise clever ways to lure, trap, and study these creatures. The game's mechanics are intuitive and easy to grasp, allowing players of all ages to enjoy the experience. Beyond the main storyline, Bugsnax offers plenty of side quests, secrets, and hidden collectibles to discover. The island is filled with intriguing mysteries and puzzles that encourage exploration and reward curiosity. The game's replayability is further enhanced by the branching narrative paths, which provide different outcomes based on your choices, inviting you to embark on a second playthrough to uncover all its secrets.Bugsnax is an exceptional game that excels in every aspect. Its stunning graphics, engaging storyline, and charming character designs come together to create an unforgettable gaming experience. The game's whimsical charm, paired with its solid gameplay mechanics, make it accessible and enjoyable for players of all ages. If you're looking for a unique adventure that will captivate your imagination and warm your heart, Bugsnax is an absolute must-play.

_childDocuments_.review: Its strongest selling points are its visual charm, voice acting, and simple but compelling gameplay. When you get right down to it, this is a game for kids; but adults can find a lot to enjoy here too. _childDocuments_.review: Quite literally one of the best games I've ever played. It's such a fun game with creative art direction and characters you genuinely care about. Even the characters that your supposed to hate are likeable, it's incredibly hard for me to dislike any of them even if they sometimes do some very morally questionable things. Not to mention the absolutely stellar voice work across the board, it really brings the world of Bugsnax alive and, again, helps a lot with making these characters likeable and easy to root for.Gameplay-wise, this game is super fun. I've already completed this game a few times over on my PS4 and I have a blast every time, especially when I discover a new way to catch a bugsnak I hadn't previously discovered in other playthroughs. The new update that came along with the Steam launch adds to the fun factor for me, with so many new optional quests giving me the opportunity to discover new hidden secrets and gameplay elements I would have never discovered otherwise. I particularly found the missions that came along with a certain doctor's letters to be very very entertaining. Nothing quite like the experience of intentionally putting your character in dangerous (and realistically speaking, very very deadly) situations just so you can get some new furniture for your hut.Without spoiling too much, the plot twist is hinted at very effectively, yet somehow caught me completely off guard my first time through. After replaying it a few times, I really began to notice that the plot twist has always been implied and hinted at from the very beginning, and yet it's done in such a clever way that it isn't super obvious immediately. This adds a lot to the replayability, seeing how many hints you can pick up on that you missed on your first time around.So yeah, great game all around. I feel absolutely no regrets purchasing this game 3 times as well as purchasing the Bunger plush literally the second it was up for sale. Bunger my beloved.
_childDocuments_.name: Bugsnax

_childDocuments_.review: I have loved this game ever since I saw an ad for it before it was available on steam. The characters are lovable and their relationships with each other are interesting but not overwhelming. The gameplay is simple enough to not need a guide but exciting enough to keep you hooked (especially if you have a short attention span and suck at finishing games). The creatures are cute and their voicelines will be stuck in your head for days. Wambus is so funny and Filbo is my bestie, sorry Beffica. So much to do but it isn't all tied to achievements or completing the game. Took me 22 hrs to complete but if I did every single mission it would have taken a lot longer, for me that is a good thing. Totally underrated masterpiece, definitely buy if you haven't already. Keeping my eyes peeled for a sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: Didn't expect to enjoy it as much as I did, but honestly the gameplay is a great break from your usual story shooter. Characters are decent, story is decent (nothing groundbreaking and pretty short), the environments and creature design are amazingly endearing though. Has the same sorta draw as something like Stardew Valley does for me, just relaxing and fun.Gameplay is very simple but very enjoyable tbh, gives you that satisfaction of completing your collection but doesn't make it impossible to 100%, just challenging enough to be fun without being super frustrating.The "horror" element that I've seen a few people mention is a bit of a stretch. There is a twist, but it's pretty predictable and nothing super out there. So don't go into it expecting things to take a turn towards lovecraft or anything.Regardless, very fun little game, gave me a good amount of enjoyment for 3 or 4 days. Definitely worth it on a good sale if you're looking for a nice singleplayer experience to spend a few days on.Most important note, Bunger and Bunger variants are the GOAT (luv me BBQ Bunger).

_childDocuments_.review: Where do I begin? Bugsnax is absolutely incredible. From its design to the story, there is something in Bugsnax for everyone. This game is a blend of adventuring, puzzle solving, and collecting that is fun rather than challenging for the average player to complete. The added DLC, mail quests, and achievements also enhance the game for players who have already completed the main story line and provide more challenge for those who seek it.As far as design, the art style is super colorful and cute with the Muppet-like characters you can meet, interact with, and complete side quests for. This also applies to the Bugsnax you catch as well, which have Pokemon-esque voice lines and clever environmental design.Overall, this is a must have for your library and you will find yourself humming the credits song on a random Tuesday at 1:36 P.M.
_childDocuments_.name: Bugsnax

_childDocuments_.review: In Bugsnax you play as a journalist muppet who captures sub-sentient organisms that move like animals and look & taste like food, but are widely acknowledged to be something else entirely. This is not cause for concern.If you like creature collectors, then this one comes with some fairly unique mechanics in the genre. Some snax are captured by simply setting a trap and lying in wait, others must be stunned and then scooped up, and some require you to lead one snak to another via a trail of sauce (bait) and cause them to collide or have one grab the other to stun.Well I found it unique anyway, given that so many games in the genre are turn-based games or employ a simple net/vacuum approach. A lot of work was put into the story, which is somewhat narrative-focused and largely character-driven. There's no reason to not do all of the side quests (it's a decent chunk of the content). It's got some cool twists and character moments. There's also the new Steam-launch DLC. I won't say much to stay clear of spoilers.Overall the game is a purely for-fun experience. There's no threat of progress loss or death even during the boss fights. I'd say it respects the player's time. Will take ~10-12 hours to do just about all of the content. I went for 100% completion, which took a little longer. Good game.

_childDocuments_.review: A real delight, this game poses a wonderful hunting/exploration theme, with creative monsters and characters to guide the way. The game is jam-packed (pun intended) with additional content, from side-quests to exploration puzzles to hidden secrets that either advance the plot or paint a better picture of the world and its inhabitants. The story is much deeper than first impression might lead to believe, and the character's fleshed-out personalities help give a realism that the game may be lacking with its cartoony aesthetics. The game's closure, if a little corny, wraps the story together nicely, giving the characters an ending that feels deserved, if a little flat compared to the depth shown throughout the rest of the game.It's a little disappointing that there's no reward for full completion beyond the main storyline and its side-quests. A final reward for completing all optional mail missions or fully stocking the farm would have been a nice final touch, especially when some of them require a lot of work. With that being said, the game does a good job of rewarding players along the way, so the offence isn't too terrible.Highly recommended to people who want to try hunting/exploration games without being too overwhelmed during their first venture, with fun visuals and a compelling story to boot. Played casually the game can be fairly simple and straightforward, but delving deeper and clearing out the game in its entirety is a welcome challenge that isn't too daunting to players unfamiliar with the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: You take one look at Bugsnax and you expect the absolute worst from it. And why wouldn’t you? It’s 202x and children’s entertainment is more annoying than ever. You’d think Bugsnax would be another one of those filler games only meant to milk money off kids. Just another kiddy game filled with bad writing and dull mechanics. And I honestly wouldn’t blame you, as it’s something that everyone has thought about this game. But Bugsnax isn’t part of this garbage children’s entertainment junk, it is so much better than that. I wanted to play Bugsnax the moment I heard it far exceeded others’ expectations and I’m hoping you will too.From a gameplay perspective, Bugsnax is fairly simple on the surface. It’s a first-person adventure game with a heavy focus on creature capturing. There are little over a hundred of the little critters to capture and while they do repeat some of the solutions, they used quite a few creative ways to figure out how to capture them. You’ll be setting traps and baiting Bugsnax into them in a large variety of ways. A big portion of this comes from the number of tools you have and having to combine them for certain captures. One example that comes to mind has to deal with capturing bugs that are frozen or on fire. You could lead them into a fire or pond with some bait, but you could also knock another Bugsnax into them and capture them both at the same time. The gameplay doesn’t just revolve around capturing insects though. The game’s quests mix things up enough to prevent the capturing from getting old. Some of my personal favorite sidequests involved spying on certain characters and others had me dressing up the characters in a specific fashion. That’s another big part of the game. Feeding a character a Bugsnax causes part of their body to become that Bugsnax. This resulted in the grossest game of dress-up that I ever found myself enjoying. I made one dude entirely out of popsicles and I made his wife entirely into pickles. There are also 5 optional bosses to fight, although 1 is part of the free DLC. The bosses all bring their own unique puzzle to solve to beat them and I’m glad they’re there as sort of a final test for the game’s simple gameplay loop.I found myself enjoying the quests, catching, and dressing up enough that I 100% the game. And there wasn’t a single dull moment.But the gameplay isn’t even the biggest selling factor for me. One of the strongest points of Bugsnax is, surprisingly, the writing. The characters may all look like discount Muppets, but the game’s cast is one of the most human ones I’ve seen in a video game in a long time. Let alone for a kid’s game. Bugsnax may have a cutesy exterior, but that never stops it from dipping its toes into more mature topics. One of my favorite examples would have to be Triffany’s questline. Her plotline revolves entirely around her obsession with leaving an impact on the world before she dies. Other characters delve into issues like depression, abandonment issues, and severe anxiety. Considering the kid-friendly aesthetic, this may sound jarring, but I promise you the game handles it well enough that it never feels out of place. And the more adult themes never stop the game from having a sense of humor. I think my favorite joke has to be that one of the characters keeps a cactus replica of his wife because he gets lonely sometimes. That and the absurd names like Gramble Gigglefunny and Wiggle Wigglebottom. I mentioned earlier that the lack of repetition helped me do all the sidequests, but seeing the conclusion to everyone’s arcs helped with that as well. I don’t think the characters would’ve been such a selling point to me without the voice actors though. Bugsnax has a shocking catalog of incredibly talented voice actors. Just take a look at the backgrounds of some of them, you’re bound to see someone you recognize. Roger Craig Smith and Yuri Lowenthal are the big standouts to me. They’re the voices of Sonic the Hedgehog and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Ben 10 respectively. All of the voice actors are really good is the point I was trying to get at. One quick look at some of their resumes is a quick way to prove it and I applaud Bugsnax for putting effort into its voice acting.My biggest complaint about Bugsnax may seem incredibly nitpicky, but I promise it’s not minor. The world map may cover a decent amount of biomes, but they’re all so enclosed and tiny. Every area is so small that a quick stroll throughout the island results in dozens of loading screens. I really feel like both the beach areas, desert areas, mountain areas, etc. could’ve been put together as one area. I don’t want the game to become open-world, but the number of loading screens between areas gets pretty tiring. I can imagine it’s going to be more of a problem for lower-end PCs. I just feel like the PS5 launch title could’ve gotten a little more intense with the map size. That and I feel like biomes get a little repetitive. As I mentioned earlier, half of the biomes just feel like an extension of the previous one. And it’s a little disappointing that the final area of the game is effectively a straight line. As some quick round-up points on my thoughts on the game: the soundtrack is pretty good. I don’t think I’ll be listening to it outside of the game too much, but the interview theme is an exception to that. A lot of the creature design is pretty cute and creative with the constant blending of bugs and snacks. I found the pineapple tarantula, hot dog worms, and sandwich centipedes to be a few of the pun names that stuck with me. I can not say the same for the Grumpus design. I just really don’t like the way the default characters look. Like I glossed over in the introduction, they look like discount Muppets. Oh and as a final positive note, I really appreciate the free DLC campaign. Too many game companies lock additional content behind a paywall and I always have to applaud companies that choose otherwise.Overall, I greatly enjoyed my 12 hours with Bugsnax. I completed every sidequest and the free DLC in that time and it never got repetitive.  I’m hoping to see more like this and less like Octodad from Young Horses in the future. For $25 it is definitely worth the price.

_childDocuments_.review: Bunger?!Ok but seriously, I love this game so much! I'm currently almost finished with my second playthrough. I initially discovered Bugsnax through RTGame, and I just had to try it myself. Everyone likes to talk about the twist at the end, and although it certainly threw me through a loop, very few seem to acknowledge just how great the core gameplay mechanics are. It was really fun trying out different combos of tools to try to catch different kinds of Bugsnax. I also liked that there were multiple ways to catch most Bugsnax, further encouraging creativity. Even the most ridiculous of strategies can work. The Bugsnax are also very cute, especially Hunnabee and Our Lord and Savior Bunger.The Grumpuses and their relationships between each other are surprisingly fleshed out as well. Sure, some had better character arcs than others, but each one has a distinct personality that makes them iconic in their own way. My favorite Grumpus has to be Chandlo because he's an absolute chad and a nice deviation from the typical jock stereotype. Snorpy's a close second because he's silly, gay, and mentally ill, he just like me fr fr.Overall, don't let the cutesy graphics fool you from thinking this is a simple children's game. It's so much more than that. I'm excited to see what the devs are cooking up next

_childDocuments_.review: This is one if not my absolute favorite game of all time!!! I love the little bugsnax with all my heart and I really hope even MORE are added!! I have this on nearly every console I own and let me tell you it's WORTH IT!! The soundtrack is amazing and the voice acting is top tier. It might make you hungry though but you can always combat this by having some snacks near you. I CANNOT Get over their little googly eyes!! This game always makes me want to doodle some silly bugsnax of my own and has helped me figure out what I want in my own game design journey. If you don't have this game yet GET IT!! The plot is good, the characters are a bit campy but in the best way possible. The controls are consistent and transfer well across platforms and they are also easy to learn. _childDocuments_.review: Of all the games I've played, Bugsnax might be one of the more unique ones. Even the premise sounds ridiculous on paper; catch bugs made of food to feed them to muppet-like creatures so that they too will turn into food. But despite the ridiculousness, the game is cute, silly, and charming. In terms of presentation, the game is lovely! The character design is simply but visually appealing. The characters really do look like muppets, with flappy mouths and exaggerated body language at times. Meanwhile, the titular Bugsnax resemble insects and other animals made of food, with googly eyes on them. Absolutely everything in the game is charming and visually appealing to look at. The environments, while a little on the small size, all have a good amount of detail and environmental variance to make them stand out. There may not be a ton of areas, but the ones there are all feel unique. The gameplay loop for this game is very simple; catch the Bugsnax using one (or more) of your six traps, and feed them to the Grumpuses. Every so often you have to complete a puzzle (especially in the DLC), but by and large 90% of the game is catching those Bugsnax. Once you do catch them, feeding them to the Grumpuses cause their bodies to change into the same type of food that you just fed them. There's not a whole lot more depth to the gameplay beyond that, but there is an odd sense of satisfaction mixing and matching food parts to create the most ridiculous looking Grumpus you can. The one thing that sort of takes away from the experience is the complete lack of any threat. You don't actually take damage in this game, and it's not possible for your character to die. You can get knocked aside, frozen, set on fire, but you'll always recover after a few seconds. Is it a bad thing that there's no threat? Not at all! It creates a very relaxing environment, but at the same time, it causes some serious moments to lose a bit of tension since you can basically sit there and face tank anything the game throws at you. The highlight of the game is probably the writing and voice acting. Each character is charming with their own vibrant personality and motivations. The writing made me actually care about the characters, and had some moments that were just downright funny! The voice actors absolutely nail each character... but perhaps my favorite bit of voice acting is the Bugsnax themselves. They just... say their names over and over in an exaggerated voice, and it is seriously funny. I found myself saying it along with them because it was just so silly that it was fun! Ultimately, the game is fairly simple. While it doesn't have a ton of depth and there isn't much challenge, it's still a lot of fun and deserving of a playthrough. If you want a silly game where you can just vibe and chill with low stakes objectives, then Bugsnax may just be the game for you. Also, Chandlo is best Grumpus.

_childDocuments_.review: Graphics: 10/10 *super cute animation style that is so unique and works perfectly with a goofy/emotional story*Voice Acting: 10/10 *Honestly surprised at the quality of the voice acting; there's singing (actually quite catchy original songs), and the reactions fit the character design to a T*Control/Mechanics: 9/10 *TBH the controls were often goofy with some glitches; however, most of the time it works in your favor and its pretty fun to be thrown across the map*Quality: 10/10 *Art is unique and the style is consistent throughout the game.*Personable: 10/10 *I wasn't expecting to be able to customize anything but you can! You can pick the color of your fur and decorate your own house!*Bugsnax is a phenomenal game that everyone should get! It's cozy and really a play at your own pace type of game. However, there's drama, emotional baggage, betrayal, and more. I didn't expect there to be plot but the story is structured beautifully where it ties up loose ends and builds upon everyone's stories. I went in disliking most of the characters to adoring them by the end. The character development and issues that arise are great to investigate and watch. I felt like a detective for most of the game, so this aspect added to my experience. Although catching bugsnax became a chore three quarters of a way in, I can't believe how time slipped away from me as I would play for hours just figure out how to fulfill quests, challenges, and bugsnax captures. The puzzles were clever but not too hard. I had a pleasant time learning each region and uncovering its secrets. Moreover, each region comes with new characters, tools, backstory, bugsnax, and environment. I enjoyed figuring out new mechanics of the game. It really doesn't just throw you in. You have time to learn the game and its story. I'm not one to typically 100% games but this is the very first game that compelled me to do so! I captured all bugsnax, completed all main/side/mail quests, and found all secrets. For most of it, you don't need a guide (although there are plenty if you get stuck). However, unlike a lot of games, you don't need to really 100% the game to have 100% completion (for instance, once you have all of Gramble's upgrades, you do not have to keep donating other than quests).Overall, I truly would recommend this game to anyone who likes cozy games with good plot and fun game play. The silliness of it all added to the game as well but, dang, did it get serious everyone now and then. My end time was 27 hours but, assuming I didn't 100% everything, it probably would be a 15-20 hour game depending on how fast it takes you and how far you want to go in the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm torn between writing a funny review or a legit review. The bugsnax are great and made with love. It's fun to figure out how to catch all of them. The story is intriguing enough to pursue while finishing the main goal of collecting all the bugsnax. And now after playing it I am questioning all things inside of my life. 10/10. Bugsnax is great.

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful voice cast, fun graphics, lovely gameplay, great story, I mean I can't find anything bad about it. It's just so weird and charming that I can't help but to love it. It's also notably one of the most polished games I've played. I've played games newer and way older than this that have more akward edges, annoying mechanics or a bunch of bugs that never got fixed. _childDocuments_.name: Bugsnax

_childDocuments_.review: GODDD this was such a good game~! A friend of mine gifted it to me & I have been obsessing over it for days, Just finished it today & I wish wish wish I had moreeeee granted, I entirely missed the bigsnax section of the game as I kind of rushed the quests & ended up not finishing everyones but maybe I'll get back to it one of these days :]] Bugsnax is definitely going in a list of my favorites & I'll remember playing it for years ahead.bunger bunger bunger
_childDocuments_.name: Bugsnax

_childDocuments_.review: Overal, it is not a terrible game. Bugsnax is cheesy, weird, and relaxing to a fault, but i cannot recommend it to anyone who likes games that demand you to care at all. Graphics are fine, everything looks cute even if unoriginal, just food with googly eyes stapled on it, you can find them pretty funny at times, like the most aggressive pile of spicy food thats literally on fire.The game has many issues that make it just monotoneus in the end though.Music feels way too generic, not a single track stuck with me, most sound like elevator songs you'd just forget as soon as you hear them.The game has also a huge issue with janky controls, especially of trip wire and the launcher which must lock on to something, but the lock-on is very inprecise and either snap or something you do not aim at at all, or refuse to snap onto anything unless for just a shortest moment.The writing also requires some work, as characters end up being pretty much just stereotypes with a "Oh so grown through the story" approach where they learn to appreciate each other, but don't really do anything to stick with you. Not to mention game feeling like it needs to remind you over and over that half of the island is gay and it couldn't decide on gender of one of characters. It got annoying as it continued. Ended up liking pretty much just Chandlo by the end.But the biggest issue, since writing can be ignored if gameplay is good... Is that all sense of danger or urgency was removed. The game does not feel like a game, more like an unfailable qte at times because you just cannot lose. You do not take damage, you get put right back in place after falling off a mountain, lava is only an inconvenience, it was relaxing, yes, but being too relaxing ends you up being boring.  Overal, can only recommend if you really need to de-stress and prefer to de-brain yourself for relax rather than focus on something fun as a way to chill.In the end, its just a walking sim with bad food puns.
_childDocuments_.name: Bugsnax

_childDocuments_.review: I LOVE BUGSNAX!! I don't play too many games, but for people who are pretty new to gaming or like creature collection games, I would HIGHLY recommend they start here. The tools are easy to learn, there's a fun, heart-warming plot, and it's always fun coming up with different ways to catch these dubious little creatures. I didn't think I'd fall in love with these strange muppet looking characters, but I did. It feels like Slime Rancher, just a little less lonely :) Great game, I can't wait for more updates.

Explore whimsical Snaktooth Island in search of answersand a snack, maybe. 

In this first-person adventure, you play as a journalist who receives a mysterious film from the disgraced explorer, Elizabert Megafig. name: Boyfriend Dungeon
detailed_description: Date up to nine-ish weapons, from dancing swords to heart-piercing daggers Generated action-combat dungeons and challenges! Stay sharp! Various combat styles. For example, hit hard and dodge quickly with the dagger, or take on crowds with Lasersaber Inclusive, tasteful approach to gender and sexuality - male, female, and non-binary romance Let's get to the point: take your weapon-babes on romantic outings, such as to the club or the beach You move into your cousin's old apartment, rent-free for the summer. Plus, he'll help you solve your little problem... you've never been on a date in your life! To get some confidence and meet people, plus earn a little cash, you’re tasked with clearing the creatures in “the dunj”. Soon you discover weapons you find transform into cuties… and they’re SINGLE! (What a craaazy coincidence because you also happen to be up for grabs yourself.) But someone's abducting weapons and leaving them damaged in the dungeon! Who could do such a thing? Will you solve the blade-napping mystery? Will you find love? Or, friendship, at least? Craft gifts for your bae blades and give them when the time is right, whether it's in the dunj or out on the town. After all, a couple that slays together, stays together. Estoc (Isaac): the sharpest dresser Dagger (Valeria): tired of backstabs Talwar (Sunder): worried he’s becoming an antique Lasersaber (Seven): hard to get a handle on him Glaive (Sawyer): awkward in the wrong hands Scythe (Rowan): reaping what they sow Brass Knuckles (Pocket): loves cat naps Axe (Jonah): surfer sweetie Hammer (Leah): fashionable and cute Whip (Dr. Holmes): Cannot be wielded Date them all without a care, you polyarmourous dual-wielder, or just be best friends. Either way, you can reach max Love Rank, because platonic love is also real love. (Besides, you can't be romantic with the cat anyway. Calm down.) If that's not enough for you, mod your own! The devs have already added basic support for changing out weapon looks -- keep an eye on updates for more features to help you blacksmith your own sharp cuties and trade them with your friends.

short_description: Date your weapons! Romance swords, daggers, and polearms to level them up in this “shack-and-slash” dungeon crawling adventure.

_childDocuments_.review: A Dungeon Crawler merged with a Dating Sim sounds like something that would be impossible to pull off. However, Kitfox has done it so damn well! Creating charming and truly inclusive characters for a Dating Sim is hard enough. But, they also managed to fill this game with evolving combat that makes each character (weapon) feel worth dating to level up their skills and learn more about them! I discovered this game back at Twitch Con 2018 and have been so hyped to finally try it and can say that it was worth the long wait because you can seriously feel the love in the game! If you are debating picking it up I do recommend it! Now go smooch some swords silly~ <3
_childDocuments_.name: Boyfriend Dungeon

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun little game! I enjoyed the various characters and their personalities, and getting to know them was fun; the dating was a bit linear for all of them, and it might have been nice to have more branching or varied outcomes, but I enjoyed things as they were. I appreciated the variety of dates, and the different things they're all dealing with and the themes they each represent were surprisingly compelling and introspective at times, even though the story overall is still pretty simple. The final boss feels a bit tacked-on and I would have liked that fleshed out more, but the rest of the story is fun.The combat side of the game is pretty basic; eventually I got the hang of it and just sort of hammered (ha) my way through the game. It mostly helps space out and prop up the dating side, I think, which is fine. Overall it's a cute little game that I enjoyed my time with.
_childDocuments_.name: Boyfriend Dungeon

_childDocuments_.review: Exceeded my expectations. I was expecting this game to feel either like a dungeon crawler with a dating sim shoe horned in or a dating sim with a dungeon crawler awkwardly jammed in there. However, I was very wrong. Breaking character scenes with dungeon crawling does wonders to enhance the experience and my affinity towards characters I normally wouldn't be that interested in. Either I would not care for the characters personality initially but liked their play style, or the other way around. I really hope games like this get made more! This is such a fresh and innovative way to improve the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Boyfriend Dungeon

_childDocuments_.review: It has the charm and wholesomeness of Dream Daddy with a little extra plot. There was a lot more seriousness and moving ideas woven into some stories.Most of the narrative intrigue lies within the characters personal stories though. The "main plot" isn't bad necessarily, the writers were just really good at writing an unlikable antagonist.In terms of being a dungeon crawler:If you don't normally partake- like me- Boyfriend Dungeon does a good job making the gameplay laid back yet entertaining. Otherwise, it's just a really simplified hack and slash.It is also important to note that this aspect of the game if very short, the game is far more a dating sim than a dungeon crawler.Overall, as a dating sim enjoyer, Boyfriend Dungeon is definitely a must play.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a bit shallow an experience, but it's sweet, short and to the point... like a dagger to the heart. Some tropes get bucked, and it makes a lot of the characters feel more human as a result. It felt good, didn't overstay its welcome... but man, I am looking forward to whatever these folks do next.

_childDocuments_.review: Boyfriend Dungeon is a great game. When I say that I really mean it. Usually, games don't effect me that much. I play them, I finish them and move to next one. But Boyfriend Dungeon really made a special place in my heart. I can compare BD to Persona. When I first started playing Persona, I wasn't expecting too much. I was assuming it was a simple JRPG but Persona surprised me and captured me. The same thing happened with Boyfriend Dungeon. First of all, if you are thinking this is just an average +18 visual novel, you are wrong. This game has so much depth to it. The characters, your interaction with them, special moments... everything is presented in such a unique way it is impossible not to love this game. The art style is fantastic. The game is eye pleasing to look at from beginning to end. The soundtrack is amazing. I finished the game, but I'm still listening to it while writing this. Tunes are so catchy, and lyrics for some songs are such a joy to listen. The gameplay consists of two parts. Dungeons and dating. Dating stuff is your usual thing. Your partner messages you, you go to a place, talk with them and end the day. You can give gifts to increase your love with them. Now, let's talk about the dungeon part. This people you meet and get acquainted with can turn into weapons. Dagger, scythe, estoc, lasersaber... variety is very good. Every weapon behaves differently and has unique skill set. The more you use a weapon the more love points you gain. Increasing your love rank unlocks new combos and abilities for that weapon. Other than that, you kill monsters, collect loot and recipes and gather money. With money you can buy clothes, gifts and crafting components. You can use your workbench to craft the recipes you've collected. Every dungeon has multiple floors. You can leave early by using the elevator if you are low on health. But in order to progress through the story you have to kill that dungeon's boss. Every dungeon represents your character's fear. When you kill a boss, you overcome that fear and move to next part on the story. Overall, Boyfriend Dungeon is a unique game, and I'm so glad I found it and played it. From start to finish it is masterfully crafted and deserves all the praise. I wish it didn't end but I guess every good thing eventually ends.
_childDocuments_.name: Boyfriend Dungeon

_childDocuments_.review: I can't remember the last time I have laughed so much in a game!! Have only had it for a day and have (quite shamefully) already played it for 8 hours. Love the characters, the music and the dungeon crawling. I really hope they add more content in the future.10/10, would recommend to any fellow slasher <3
_childDocuments_.name: Boyfriend Dungeon

_childDocuments_.review: Hmm ... What about this game? The music is very pleasant to the ear and can be listened to in a loop. The graphics vary between the cute and the gorgeous. I particularly appreciate the different personalities that are presented to us, although I am insatiable and I would have liked there to be more (but I am patient, I would wait for the next two!) In general, all the characters are endearing (except Eric ...) and makes you want to discover them all. A relaxed game very pleasant to play, the fact of replaying the dungeons "often" to increase the "levels / love" of the characters, is done very well and quickly, thus avoiding falling into the vicious circle of repetition! I am very happy to have supported this wonderful team from the start!

_childDocuments_.review: I think there's something short on the game play - It's decent, but less than what I expected. But it's fluent and very accessible. It's not roguelike though, there's hardly random generation nor stuff to build around. Everything else is very enjoyable though, the blades are sweet as hell and the story is what keeps me playing.
