_childDocuments_.review: I have mixed feelings, but I don't have such an option on Steam.tl;dr: dungeon crawler part - good. Otome part and plot - bad. Game short.Contains spoilers. It will be long.On the one hand, we have a decent dungeon crawler. Its strongest sides are for sure creativity with both ideas about enemies (as a manifests of player's fears) and about weapons (gameplay-wise, they feel original and I absolutely loved the idea of gravity skills on a scythe). It isn't difficult, so it is accessible for everyone - better player's will just progress faster and there is no skill-wall for the rest. The painful thing is that everything is short and can get pretty boring when you have only 2 dungeons for the entire game, but I will return to that point later. For me, this part was at least nice overall.And then came the otome part of the game... And its plot. I will divide this part on 2 sections: Rowan’s route case study (cause they are the only character I had a romantic relation with) and overall plot.Otome part feels just rushed. It doesn't give you a time to get used to a romance/friendship option; to spend time casually; to wait a bit with opening. We have only 6 meetings per character, so the writers had to pack a relation into these 6 meetings. And it was a tiny, tiny box. Valerie's route has the best pacing, I think, but for 1 Valerie we have 6 other characters, like Rowan. Then it turns out we know almost nothing about past of these characters, about their memories, dreams, favorite places – things lovers and friends should have an idea about.About Rowan’s route: its pacing is totally wild.First meeting: I want to kill you.Second meeting: I’m sorry I wanted to kill you.Third meeting: Eric is stupid.Forth meeting: Oh no, Crowley is gone, help.Fifth meeting: We will medidate. And, btw, I don’t want to date you, cause I will lose you just like I lost my grandmother. (what was their relationship with their grandmother even? All we know is that she was named Alice and was a witch!)And in the end they decide to stay with the relationship, because they met their grandmother… It doesn’t feel right. How about their feelings? Their own development as a character and growth as a person? About overcoming their own fear of intimacy, because they love player’s character more than they are afraid of losing someone once more?Also, Seven’s route has the same problem as Rowan’s route – a serious problem gets intoduced and just passes by with a divine touch of player’s character. Grief and depression aren’t things that can be easily overcome. Portraing them like that is simply wrong and misleading.Overall plot… It was just shallow. We have The Villain TM, who is So Evil! The game just shows Eric from the worst side all the time and it is boring: he dislikes cats, he wants to buy cheaply blades from Rowan, he is racist and most of the time will speak about it. Also, he exists to show how cool our love interests/friends are. It feels like a story written by a middle school girl, where a plastic barbie is a must-have villain. Eric’s motivations also aren’t explained well, we don’t have any reason to understand him or feel for him.Shortness of the game: it has around 10-15 hours of gameplay (I am not a dungeon crawler expert and I finished it with 96% achievements, so I suppose it is a normal time), which may be a reason why writing is so rushed. The writers may have interesting, complex stories in mind, but without enough time to expose them correctly… well, it hasto end up like that.A special mention: soundtrack! It was modern, fresh and it fits well to the game.In the end, the dungeon crawling part manages well, but is pulled down by the plot.

_childDocuments_.review: What a fun little game! I intended to just casually play this an hour or two at a time, but I got super drawn into it and wanted to see it through to the end, so I finished it way faster than I intended to. It's a simple game. The characters aren't particularly deep, but still plenty enjoyable and it's fun to date them (shoutout to Valeria and Seven for being lovely, and also (spoiler) ). The roguelite dungeon gameplay isn't particularly hard and I could get away with mostly buttonmashing even to finish the hardest content in the game (albeit with a few tries in the worst cases), but that's fine, I wasn't looking for anything challenging either. It's genuinely just a nice and casual game to get through, which was pretty much exactly what I was looking for. A huge bonus for me is also that it is just a delightfully queer game, and though that wasn't the way I played, even seeing the dialogue options where you can choose to just be friends or have an asexual romantic relationship was very appreciated. There are also a great amount of quite sensitive details put in by the devs, for example, you are asked in the beginning of the game if you are comfortable receiving supportive messages from your mother, and even though all those details aren't for me, it's still nice to see in the game. But here's the big one that this game has gained some notoriety for: as the warning informs at the very beginning of the game, it 'references stalking'. Only it doesn't just reference stalking, you very literally gain a stalker and the fact that you have this stalker is a significant part of the story. While they I think succeed in making this a deeply uncomfortable experience, it is an experience I honestly wish wasn't there in such a large capacity when I go into this thinking it's just a fun game where you do dungeons with weapons you can also date. I'm not inherently opposed to such a story being told and they did handle the storyline with care, but I do wish that the focus of the main story were on something else. But besides that: I genuinely had fun here and I'm glad I put in the time to see all the content.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: This game is gay as heck. The cast is great, gameplay is fun, there's a good but not excessive amount of collectibles, and the devs did a good job job of having a story that works with whoever and however many of your weapons you decide to date.  Definitely worth the $20, while short and pretty easy by dungeon crawler standards it's a fun and pretty unique experience. The gameplay isn't super deep, each weapon has a set of combos consisting of mixes of heavy and light attacks but almost none of them are more complicated than: press light as many times as you want, then heavy for the rest of the 4 or 5 hit combo. Each weapon does have unique abilities that unlock as you improve your relationship such as chain lightning on hit or critical hits if your enemies are confused. Combat feels satisfying and there's enough loot keep completionists occupied without being overwhelming. For the dating part of dating your weapons, you've got guys, gal (just the one for now but another is coming in an update or dlc), and non binary pals, and you can set your own gender to one of these options as well. You'll have a good mix of personalities amongst your arsenal, each with a pretty interesting and unique story to explore. There's no punishment for polyamory and there are aro and ace options for each partner. Although each of these "options" are set by a single dialogue choice each and you cannot change your mind afterwards. Started a relationship with Isaac because he was the first character you met but later decided that Rowan is the nb of your dreams and you'd like to be exclusive with them? Not today. Also depending on the character, platonic relationships can feel kinda weird in this game, sometimes feeling like your dates (spending time with a character is called a date regardless of what your status is with them) have only had one or two bits of dialogue modified ever so slightly to account for your decision.There is a disclaimer regarding this at the start but this game has some uncomfortable stalker moments in it and I'd strongly recommend treading lightly if that's a subject that you are sensitive to for whatever reason.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. The dungeons are a fun dive and the music to go along with it is soooo good. The art styles and colors are incredibly well done. Each and every one of the characters felt like real, complicated people. This is more than just another visual novel meets dungeon delver, this is a journey into our own self worth, self confidence, and self identity. Yes the main villain is a creep but I disagree with the hate that this game has been given because of him. The content warning at the beginning was more than enough to sway someone away who might be triggered by his unwanted attention. They state outright: “play with care.” I don’t know any female friends who have not had an “Eric” in their lives. I myself suffered from this exact kind of manipulation and mental assault from an “Eric”for many years. When your character meets Eric in game and he begins to disregard your requests for him to quit his advances, I was audible with disgust because it brought back awful memories and made Eric feel even more like a real person. This is painful but exceptional storytelling. And that’s what video games are about: storytelling. This is the story these artists wanted to tell. It’s a real story that many people can relate to. But there are extremely kind characters to help you on your journey. The story is not about how Eric is an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, the story is about the friends you make, the strength you gain, and your newfound confidence you acquire through the trials that you conquer. My eyes welled with tears as I finished the game. My heart felt full and light. I felt like I made a difference. I felt like I had conquered my own fears once again. And THATS what this game is all about.

_childDocuments_.review: : A quick and cute fusion of both dating sim and Roguelike where you can make as many friends or more-than-friends as you want, and still get all the achievements easily. Take the "may" in the game's trigger warning as a "does" or "will" for the main story. Really hope to have another game at Verona beach soon....The game is a fun little hybrid of a dating sim and a Roguelike and I'm all for it.- Each "dunj" was a fair challenge. Not too hard, and didn't get too easy too quickly when levelling up.- I found the characters themselves to be a lot of fun to interact with.- Both the music and art style are great.- There's someone for everyone in this game, and you can choose if you want to just be friends with them, date one person, or date them all at once. This doesn't make the game easier or harder, and you can still get all the achievements, even if things are just platonic.- On top of saying the right thing or giving them gifts, you can bond with your preferred weapons by fighting with them "in the dunj". It makes sense to me, and it also makes it easier for people who aren't used dating sims. You can make up for wrong answers by just fighting together.- Voice acting in dating sims is always tricky to get right without making me, at least, feel embarrassed. I tend to turn it off, but I kept it on because I found  of the voice acting to be quite fun. Still cringed in most of the romantic bits, but that's me.- Weapon transformation animations were a nice treat. Hope we can see updated animations if the game ever gets a revamp.- Too short? The game is meant to take place over three-ish months, but It felt like maybe a couple of weeks. As a consequence, I feel like the characters kind of suffered for it.- Characters were deeper than many in dating sims, but because of this, I feel like the creators could've gone a lot further. I feel like more interactions with them really would've made them shine. This resulted in next to no heart-flutters for me, which I think is a significant goal for dating sims like this one. .- The auto-save was a champ, but I do like the multiple save file feature that most VNs have. If I could, I would've had a save especially made so I could repeat the last chapter for my favourite suitor. As far as I could tell, there was no way to go back to certain beats of the story.- For me, a couple of characters didn't have voices that suited them, which lead to me being taken out of the atmosphere and just thinking about them in the booth. No hate to the VA, but Holmes had the voice I took most issue with.- Didn't bother me, but it may bother others. Game has already faced controversy for this, but trigger warning needs to be rephrased. It effectively says you "may" encounter certain triggers, but they're all in the main story. Most of which are unavoidable.

_childDocuments_.review: SUMMARY: An accessible and surprisingly deep and emotional fusion of roguelike, datesim, and social sim.  Date living weapons, explore procedural dungeons, face your fears, craft goods, and find love (or just lust).  Boyfriend dungeon is the weapon-dating alternate-modern world dungeon crawler you didn't know you wanted - until now.Boyfriend Dungeon sounds like a bit of a joke - "Date living weapons to explore dungeons."  Though it will poke at some tropes, it's a fully-envisioned game that fuses Datesim and Roguelike with an actual plot (and many subplots), great art, and a lot of heart.  It's Soul Eater meets Persona that then goes beyond its simple premise.You're a visitor to a California City, Verona Beach, in a world of both modern technology and commonplace mystical happenings.  Some people can become weapons, magic is real, and dungeons made of twisted fears pop out of the ground.  You're in town to face some fears in the depths of the mind and maybe meet someone - fortunately plenty of attractive living weapons are here to make life easier.So let's get to the game:THE CHARACTERS: Most of the cast are living weapons, but they also have complete stories and personalities.  Don't expect to fully understand, like, or predict everyone.  Also expect to find that you have favorites as the cast is fully realized, and full of surprisies that may make you laugh, think, or feel your heartbeat speed up.  The writing is excellent and the characters compelling.THE DATING: Dating happens in various choice-driven segments and some random dungeon events.  Expect some pretty complicated plotlines, deep choices, revelations, and cuteness.  Give gifts, make choices, and be ready for surprises . . .(The game is inclined to those attracted to men, and even if that's not your preference, there are plenty of options.  Also, its a very RP-driven game, so it's fun to create a personality for your character and follow that!)THE WEAPONS: Most of your life revolves around the living weapons.  As you build relationships, new abilities come out.  Each plays radically different.  You'll find favorites, least-favorites, and plenty of strategies.THE DUNGEONS: Face weird monsters in procedural dungeons - that are also outings.  Beat monsters, stop for ice cream, find treasures and blueprints.  You may just learn more about your character.CRAFTING: Of course there's crafting!  Make gifts, clothes, and magical zines.  These affect the game of course, and are fun to try and collect.DRESS UP: Honestly, you want to be able to dress up, right?THE PLOT: Yes, there's a plot - multiple ones, really.  Don't think you know everything, and small and large revelations will challenge you.  The game INVITES you to role-play and be in character because actions have consequences and choices may be difficult.There are a few flaws in the game:* The in-dungeon fighting is a little "floaty" - aiming and play isn't that precise.* There's not a huge variety of dungeon levels or monsters.* It's relatively short (maybe 6-8 hours).  However, if you want to be a completist, there is a lot to do.  There's also a LOT to it, so in the hours you spent with it, it is very fulfilling.* You may have to grind a bit, but that's part of the gernes.  And yes, maybe grinding is a bit of a metaphor too . .Boyfriend Dungeon is worth your time if any of this intrigues you.  A fusion of various elements that we don't often see together, well-written, and heartfelt.  Hopefully, we're seeing the launch of a franchise of gorgeous weapon-people having romance and fighting monsters.

_childDocuments_.review: Boyfriend Dungeon is a short, sweet hack-and-slash game that you can easily finish within a day if you dedicate yourself to doing nothing but playing it the whole time. I completed it in about 8.5 hrs, and it was an overall fun experience. The keyboard controls were rather unpleasant for me, so I opted for a controller instead and found it much easier to wield my weapons and defeat monsters in the dunj (dungeon). I thought this would be a simple hack-and-slash game with some dating elements and was surprised when each romanceable character came with their own storyline. The player's own character also goes through growth, and it's satisfying to see how it wove in with the overall plot. I admittedly didn't like all of the romanceable characters because I found their personalities grating, but there's a lot of variety in who you can date (or just want to have as a friend!) and the inclusivity in the dateable characters is refreshing. The gameplay itself isn't difficult, especially after I switched to a controller. I do wish there was an option to just leave the dungeon after a floor is completed rather than having the option of swapping weapons and then continuing. Sometimes I would just let myself die in the dungeon just so I could get out of the dunj and go on dates so I could further my relationship with characters. I also wish that the player could make some craftable items more than once. Otherwise, a really pleasant game. Time flew by as I was playing it and I was surprised whenever someone in the game mentioned that my time with them was nearing to an end. If you want a short, creative game to play and the premise of Boyfriend Dungeon appeals to you, go for it!

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed all of my time with this game. Even getting to see the stories of characters I didn't really resonate with, and re doing floors in the dunj for love rank/ level was enjoyable. Just maybe not repeatable. I spent 13 hours with the game and could have easily spent 13 more. Pros:*Variety of characters and play styles- you have a weapon for every dungeon crawling preference, and a personality for every dating type. *Dating more than one character is okay- this is an odd one to considered a pro for most dating games, but it is nice to not have to replay the game over and over again to see the different character development paths. *Time restrictions- there aren't any and I love this. If you agree to date go on a date with someone but decide to spend the evening doing the dunj- its okay. The date is still there for you without a negative consequence.*The cell phone- usually reading text messages in games gets old but the conversations keep being interesting, and who can turn down cute cat pictures*Combat- tying back to my first pro, there is a weapon you will enjoy using no matter you play style. Don't expect the challenge of Hades, but do expect to enjoy yourself.*The option to be friends- some reviewers have claimed you can't be friends, even when given the option but that is only with one character and it is plot related. Every other character has friend paths, and you have enough variety in responses to decide later on that you might want to be more that friends, or you want to call it off and do your own thing. It nice.*Collectables/ customizations- you can find, and craft so many things. From gifts for your love interests to outfits you wear out and about town/ in the dunjCons:*Music- Although the music is good, there are a very limited number of tracks and if you take you time trying to max out multiple love ranks you will be tired of hearing the music in no time*Game length- Its short. I didn't want this game to be over. The beginning felt rushed, and the end did too. I had hoped for more dungeons to open up, and I really wanted more options concerning where I went after my experiences of the game. *Challenge level- I didn't mind the challenge level of the game, but I did wish that a difficulty level had been an option at the beginning of the game. The devs were thoughtful enough to ask if it was okay to receive texts from Mom, but didn't give me the opportunity to challenge myself in combat. Overall: great game that is worth the money despite the short length of the game. The variety and thoughfulness that was included in the game was fantastic, and I really hope that DLC content or something similar adds something more to the game later. I would love a reason to come back to VB.

_childDocuments_.review: I backed this game the first day it launched on kickstarter, so I've been excited for this game for a long time. Mostly I was interested in the combination of the two genres - a dungeon crawl and a dating sim all nicely rolled into one. I enjoyed it! I would recommend it if you're looking for a fun casual dating sim with some RPG elements and light crafting.It's LGBT+ inclusive which is a big plus, you can chose your pronouns and style your character however you want, it even includes two nonbinary romance options, and you can romance anyone regardless of your pronouns.However this game didn't really live up to my hype. It kind of seems like the two genres this game is supposed to represent didn't quite live up to either of their potential. The RPG elements are especially simple, I didn't have to mind or take note of any of the weapon combos in order to win, I never had to swap out my weapon abilites for anything that might be better suited. Honestly the combat is easy once you get used to the enemies and how they move. The game only has a handful of enemies, the stronger enemies are just stronger versions of the old enemies. And there are only 2 dungeons in the whole game, I guess with maybe a dozen enemies each and with a few unique bosses.What initially attracted me to this game was the idea of a fully fleshed out dungeon crawler with the added bonus of the dating sim on the side, and the dungeons were just super underwhelming. As for the actual dating sim part, I enjoyed that quite a lot, because I liked most of the characters. It's also very surface level. Your dialogue options really don't mean much and the dates are going to go how they're going to go. There's no branching paths or stories with any of the romance options as far as I'm aware. I'm not even sure if it's possible to reach max level with them platonicaly because the only romance option I turned down continued to persue the player character romantically anyway. I just gave in and decided to romance everyone for the achievement after that.That doesn't mean it's not fun, most of the romance options are a lot of fun just to go through the story with and find out more about them, you just don't have to think too hard. My main complaint is Sawyer, I skipped most of their cutscenes and dialogue because they felt a walking stereotype. They act like a child. As a member of the LGBTQ+ community myself, I'm glad Rowan was added to offset that or I would have been really annoyed.The "main story" of the game is completed within a handful of cutscenes. I know it's more about the dungeons and the romance options, but when both of them were kind of underwhelming it was a super bummer that the main story was so short! I felt like I had only just started the game when all of the characters started texting me that I'd be going home soon since the summer was coming to an end! I hadn't even maxed out a single character before I hit the final mission. Overall I just didn't feel like every character got to be explored deeply enough, ESPECIALLY the character that the main story sort of revolves around.Overall, I had fun with the game, but I am disappointed. I know more content is coming in the future, and maybe that will iron out these issues, but I kind of would have just preferred they waited to release if that's the case. I guess I expected too much, or something different, to what this turned out to be.

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely loved this game. I never play dating sims but the dungeon delving aspect drew me in, and I'm glad it did. All of the characters feel real even when you're talking to a dagger, and I love the flexibility it gives you in how you develop each relationship. It's not about sleeping with everyone, you can grow closer just as friends, or even have a platonic romance, and you never feel like you're missing out on anything or like that sort of relationship is any less important.I'm not sure if "enjoyed" is the right word for it, but I appreciated the rougher aspects the game touched on as well. Unhealthy relationships and stalker behavior are covered in what feels like a realistic way. Well...besides the whole weapons and dungeon delving being literal, but they serve as good metaphors. On that though, I've seen in other reviews that you have to interact with the stalker, but you DO NOT need to ever go on a date with them to finish the game. You CAN ignore them and shut them down at every opportunity and never need to pursue them except to confront the problem. If it ever feels like you don't have other options, just spend some time with your other friends either dating or in a dungeon.-SPOILERS FROM HERE ON-I think my main complaint is that there were only two dungeons.  technically three, in that it seems to count the final boss fight as a dungeon. With how it was set up it really felt like there'd be more. Also, while I do love being able to guide relationships towards just friends, platonic romance, or sexual romance, I feel like that gets locked in very early. Like if early on I don't go full in on the romance or choose to start just friends, then it stays just friends with no way to change my mind later. So, be aware that if you get an option to say anything that says you'll be just friends, even if for just one event, that means you do not want to go further than that for the rest of the game.It can also feel a bit directionless at times on how to progress without interacting with Eric and it wasn't really clear that it was purely a progression event to "shop" at his store, and it's never really a shop. Also would have appreciated calling the cops on the guy or him having any retribution whatsoever for what he'd done, instead of just being forced to trust him at his word and let him walk away.Overall, though, it was a great experience. It really felt like I was saying goodbye to dear friends when the game came to a close.

_childDocuments_.review: I normally avoid throwing my hat into the ring when commenting about games as there is generally a large discourse around them already, but since I backed Boyfriend Dungeon, I'd like to place down my two cents.Currently the game does not have enough content to justify the price tag it comes attached with. I "finished" the game in around three and a half hours (there are only two "dunj"'s and a totally-not-slapping-you-in-the-face-obvious final boss fight), before doubling back to round out the rest of the romances and craft the remaining items I had missed. I think this game suffers from an identity crisis: it is effectively a combination of dungeon crawler and visual novel, but without doing either remotely . Gameplay in the dunj is, kindly put, bland. While each weapon does attack differently, at most you will be alternating LMB and RMB clicks (the game does list "combos" for each weapon, say LMB RMB RMB, but all this does is let you swap in to the RMB attack string from the LMB attack string. Only Sawyer and Rowan get different moves available to them by doing this, as their RMB attacks are standalone moves that do not chain unlike, well, every other weapon), dodge rolling, and occasionally shooting out whichever generic special move you've chosen from your collection of Zines--super powers in this game being determined by which 'zine' you have equipped and whose effects range from things such as breathing fire, summoning a decoy, or releasing a shock field. They're fine, but they're uninspired and don't contribute much to making the gameplay flow different or exciting.Alright, so maybe the dungeon crawling is a little tacked on, maybe the characters make up for it, right? Well, no. Boyfriend Dungeon uses the trope that Everyone Really Likes You that crops up in romanceable character games occasionally. Your sharp heart throbs do have some potentially interesting issues: Recently coming out as non-binary (...but the fact they can't cook seemed to be a larger plot point than that.), how do you find love and connection when you've lived for 200 years already (something many of us will obviously go through), coping with depression (by falling in love obviously and not seeing a therapist).On the flip side then you have things such as: rich attractive man disappoints his father by being philanthropic and "breaks away from him" but still seems to keep his expensive and cushy living arrangement...?But all of the potential interest, the good work in offering you platonic relationships as being equally important and healthy as romantic ones, pales in comparison to how little your input matters. All of the characters like you, and often times not for any explainable or obvious reason. They just happen to think you're neat, so neat that they're happy to pash you. I think the  with the setting of Boyfriend Dungeon remains largely untapped. What would it be like to actually wield another being? How would that impact your relationship with them; how would it grow that relationship? Is it comfortable or uncomfortable for the weapon-turner? Alongside this, text messaging system which is used to continue conversations with your bae blades outside of your heart dates/events is inane, slow, and does its best to reduce any connection your might be building. How are you supposed to be seriously invested someone when they send you four multiple paragraph messages in a row to which your response options are a single sentence, a single word, or a series of emojis? Despite being eerily reminiscent of what online dating can be like, it makes the situation even more unbelieveable that these characters are often entirely delighted and content with your measly responses, an experience which is repeated on your in person dates. How am I supposed to care about a person whose response to me, not matter which option I select, is approval, love, or wonder? What is heartbreaking about all of this though, is that Boyfriend Dungeon has style. To take a swipe at the low hanging fruit here: Boyfriend Dungeon is a good-looking bad date. It is well dressed, it sounds nice, it looks good, but when you talk to it you quickly realise that there's just... not much there. It is distressing when the only nice things you can say about a game are its art style, user interface, and music. It's like looking someone up and down before smiling and saying, "Your outfit is vibrant today."I'm not sad to have helped in some small way to bring Boyfriend Dungeon to be a game in the world; respectful and representative queer content is still sadly sparse, especially non-erotic content, but I am sad that the experience is so flat. I find it interesting how much Moon Hunters (one of their earlier titles) and Boyfriend Dungeon have in common. They are both rich in setting, visual storytelling, and appearance. But they're also sparse, and kind of empty. Outside of the dunj, and being texted by five people at the same time for a date, there's just not much to do in Boyfriend Dungeon, so there's little for you to fall in love with.

_childDocuments_.review: Boyfriend Dungeon is an absolutely delightful short dating sim in which every character feels like they have depth and their own quirks and secrets. There have been several times that the game surprised me, and others when I was simply delighted by what I expected. It has a silly premise, and it leans into that, making fun of itself and using the space that creates to have an absolute blast with the game that results. I'm not normally into dungeon crawlers or dating sims, but apparently when the two are combined, I'm smitten. The dungeon crawling has a bit of a Transistor vibe, for fans of that game, and everything in the game felt like it was designed with convenience in mind - the dungeons give you teleport points in the form of elevators, so that you don't have to start from the top every time you re-enter. The game was thoughtfully written, too, with bits of dialogue in one route being influenced by how far you are in a different route. Even the game's villain is well-written and well-conceived. Also - how could I forget? - the game mentions ethical polyamory, which is absolutely phenomenal, and allows you to choose friendship routes while still maxing out each weapon. I only wish it was longer, but truthfully, I think it's a pretty perfect length for what it is. Highly recommend checking it out, and supporting some lovely indie game devs.

_childDocuments_.review: How do I describe BFD? Well, mechnically, it's a hack and slash with very basic combos (either 3 or 4 string, depending on the "weight" of the weapon) and a pretty basic dungeon crawling aspect that becomes even more basic after the first dungeon. Every monster you beat, floor your clear, etc grants you XP at the end which contributes to your level, which not only gives you more HP, but improves your damage with each weapon.There's also the crafting element, where you use items you either find in the dungeon or purchase in or out of the dungeon to make recipes you also find in the dungeon. For what purpose? Getting to that. Point is it's really basic and you can only craft recipes once.Then there's the dating sim element! The characters are well written by all accounts, each with their own distinct personalities, traits, and flaws that, over the course of a playthrough or two, you'll either fall in love with or not. That said, it is limited to brief interactions in the dungeons, giving gifts, and 6 dates that, at least to my knowledge, result in a "Love Rank" increase regardless of what direction you take the relationship, but that's kind of necessary as these rank ups also add to what the your weapon partner can do down in the "Dunj".Over all, you might notice that I use words like "basic" and "simple" a lot. And that is gonna continue, because the game's setting feels a lot like if you simplified the dungeon delving and premise of the Persona games, and did something similar with the Soul Eater anime series for the characters and setting, but threw in a huge helping ton of realism, LGBTQ+ themes, and made a game that is dripping with charm, promise, and love, both in the narrative sense and in the meta sense.For those who haven't paid much attention, this game has been in development for *years*, struggling due to all manner of things, and I'm sure a lot of more advanced or ambitions elements had to be left out just to get the game out at all; two characters are going to come out as DLC specifically because there just wasn't enough time to include them in the game.And this is the part where I feel the need to point out the game's flaws. While the game stresses a Personaesque ticking clock of "you're only here for the Summer", and certain events and looming ends are brought up in conjunction with that theme, the truth is that you can freely ignore that time limit and max out all your relationships before you finish the second dungeon, or conversely not enough finish one before beating said second one.The game also requires a certain level of acceptance for themes, terms, and slangs that more than a few players might find "cringey" or "too SJW-y". And while I disagree with that notion, I can see people being turned off by the game referring to dungeons as Dunjs.Finally, I hate to say this; the games boss fights feel weak. I'm not sure what about them makes them feel that way to me, what design choices make them like that, but I can say this much: Do not make boss fights where the boss talks to you through text bars in a hack n slash action game. No player is going to have the time to read those. Either have them be voiced, or slow down combat somehow during the speeches.That all said, I've played through this entire game twice, with my first playthrough happening in basically the first evening I played it. It turned an awful day into one of the better days I'd had in awhile. I've written 80 pages of fanfiction about this game since the second completion.This game has inspired me like very, very few games or other media have, period. It's characters have my heart, and its world lives inside my head.If you're at all interested in dating sims, but not willing to dive into the deeper visual novels, or hack and slash dungeon crawlers but don't want that to be the *only* thing you're doing, then this game is a beautiful entry into either genre that'll leave you hungering for more.

_childDocuments_.review: Verona Beach – a chill place to spend the summer. Especially in a rent-free apartment previously occupied by your cousin. Kind of him to offer you the space, even if he’s one of the most obnoxious and interfering people you’ll ever meet. But hey, families – can’t pick ‘em.But you can pick lovers, and that’s part of the reason you’re here. See, you’ve never had a date. Not even once. Your cousin, under some duress from your mother, has been assigned your wingman, but it won’t be long before you’re able to make connections at your own pace.Connections that lead to a very interesting quirk: your ideal love interests are all capable of transforming themselves into wield-able weapons. Cue  core premise. Namely, dating the weapons you will take into dungeons – or ‘dunjis’ – to do battle with a host of monsters that reflect your deepest fears.It’s a neat, clever premise – the kind ideally suited to gaming’s specific narrative and  gameplay strengths, successfully mixing the dating sim with hack-and-slash (or "shack and slash") dungeon combat. Successful to a point, anyway.Throughout your summer in Verona, you’ll meet a host of potential love interests. Each character feels unique, carrying their own baggage, harbouring secrets, and needing you just as much as you need them.There's Valeria, a dagger, who also happens to be a talented artist in need of a new direction in life. Although initially resistant, your developing romance eventually allows her to open about her rather extraordinary talents. Then there’s Sawyer, a glaive, and to them you are a lodestone in their young life. They really did entrance me! There’s plenty more, too – seven, in total – and each feel fully alive, their personal dramas unique to their own lived experiences.Your time together is either spent on dates across Verona’s lovingly drawn romantic hotspots or in the dungeons.Dungeon combat is pretty basic, settling for fun, engaging encounters that are never too taxing. Each love interest transforms into a specific weapon – a glaive, a scythe, and so on – and as your relationships deepen, you’ll unlock more abilities, transforming you both into an increasingly powerful duo.There’s items to pick up along the way, most of which you can take home and craft into gifts (flowers, cupcakes, pizzas...). Like the combat itself there’s no real depth to the crafting process; all you need do is find the right materials and put them together at home. That’s not in any way a slight – just an observation on the game’s breezy and poppy tone. I wouldn’t have it any other way!I liked my dates. Their dialogue was thoughtful and considered, probing the complexities of modern love, sex, and desire. I’ve seem some reviewers lauding the ‘great writing’, but I can’t agree with that. They probe the complexities, sure, but the game never digs very deep. It’s  good, so let’s not get carried away, yeah?More importantly, this is an inclusive game with stellar representation. Proudly LGBTQ+, I was so heartened to see these characters represent our diverse and developing understanding of gender. It’s arguably the writing’s greatest strength.Yet, when it comes to the ‘game’ bit, I can’t help but feel  is lacking. I mentioned earlier that the game’s tone was poppy and breezy, and whilst that did work for me, I felt like  was in order in some crucial departments. There’s only two dungeons to complete, a singe villain to defeat, and, dates aside, that’s sort of it.As the dungeons are representations of the protagonist’s fears, it’s disappointing to see it handled in such a cursory manner. Sure, it's not meant to be a complex drama, but by the time the second dungeon concluded, I didn't feel like a complete statement on the game's many themes had been reached. There’s much more that could have been done to create a fulfilling arc worthy of the game's thematic interests. It’s fine that the combat and crafting are kept minimal, but I walked away from the game feeling like there wasn’t nearly enough done to properly capitalise on such a clever premise.Even if it did let you date a cat.But whatever misgivings I have about the game’s overall execution, I had a super fun time. The characters are likeable and compelling, the combat enjoyable and simplistic, and it’s loaded with positive vibes: a welcome relief in today’s angry world, drunk on hate and eager to lash out in fear of diversity, of difference.  emphatically embraces our differences, and for that reason alone, it’s worth giving it a try.And you can date a cat.

_childDocuments_.review: It's fun for a short night long play through, but lacks a lot of player agency and depth that I'd expect from this kind of game. If you're looking for a small self contained experience and nothing more, it's well worth the price tag, but the game itself left me feeling both sad and unfulfilled.For how beautiful the art is and how cool the concept may be I find it really depressing that nothing you say matters. You try to say no to someone? Ignored. I told several characters I'd prefer to be friends and yet the game FORCES you to continue going on romantic dates with them and flirting. The game lectures YOU the player about consent and then ignores your own consent later into the game. Maybe, you might think, you can just romance one person and ignore everyone else? Nope, you HAVE to romance everyone at least once for the story to continue. Your dialogue choices don't matter, your dating choices don't matter, nothing matters. It's an illusion of choice.And this goes for the ending too; this is going to dip into SPOILER territory so beware.  You have no impact on your relationships or the world around you, forced to follow the story directly. Either you ignore a character or you pursue them, there is no in between.This kind of spamming issue happens in the dungeons as well, the weapons all follow a basic combo of clicking that lacks a lot of variety. I didn't mind this as much myself but I know some people may find the basic nature of the combat and how easy it is boring after awhile. Doubly so since this game doesn't have difficulty changing options.To any looking to buy this game, I think it is very worth it if you're going to play it with friends, or if you want to appreciate the beautiful art/soundtrack this game has to offer. Otherwise, I would hold off to buy it when the game has more DLC or additional content to offer like more dungeons or female romance options (since there's only one as of right now.)

_childDocuments_.review: In a world of time-sinks, here is a game where you can experience almost everything in under 20 hours. Platonic and romantic options for every character relationship, among a cast of various genders and sexualities and species, with game play that is compelling without being overbearing and an excellent soundtrack. As someone who identifies as a heterosexual male, I found playing this thought-provoking as the game makes no assumptions about gender and sexuality for your character - only the choices you make can articulate those preferences. A wonderful, refreshing experience in a world of bloated, all-consuming sandboxes, this game respects your time and rewards you abundantly. I highly recommend it!*One warning - though I think there is now a CW in the game - not every relationship or person is healthy, and this game is authentic in that respect. If you have dealt with harassment or abuse in your life, consider whether you are in a place where you can deal with media concerning those themes.

_childDocuments_.review: This game takes a visual novel and a dungeon-delver and somehow blends the two together just right.  They never feel like they've overpowering each other.  The romance interests are mostly okay, and nicely written.  I like that you can tell the characters that you just want to be friends, but that doesn't necessarily lock you out of their content.  Platonic love is just as important and powerful as romantic love, and the devs seem to recognize that.  There's a cat you can befriend, that's also important.  The art and music are very nice.  My main complaint is that it feels like they tried to cram too much into too short of a time.  I'm three hours in and it feels like I'm at the endgame...but I still haven't found all the characters, let alone maxed them out.  Each character has six chapters to their story, some of which feels like a lot of filler (did Sawyer's cooking shenanigans really need to go on so long?).  They set up some of the more fantastic elements, but don't have time to really go into the lore of it all.  It just kinda...exists.  And I mentioned the friendship mechanics, but some characters feel like they were written specifically for romance and get passive aggressive when when they're delegated to friendship (Sunder, throwing a hissy fit in a romantic area because you were friendzoned isn't going to make me like you).  But at the end of the day, it's a very nice little romance game.  Even with the stuff I didn't like (which most of it boiled down to Sunder and Sawyer, so that's just a personal taste thing and not an over-arching problem with the game).  I do recommend it, especially if you're looking to add some romance to your gaming habits.Isaac best swordsbando, fight me.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to start off by saying i ultimately really enjoyed my time with boyfriend dungeon and look forward to any new content they add in the future. the game's writing and art style are phenomenal and, for the most part, the characters all endeared themselves to me really quickly. the gameplay isn't difficult at all, to be honest, and I suspect it would be disappointing to a hardcore rogue-like fan. i rarely play those kinda games and i was able to almost 100% the game in around 10 hours. the controls aren't as tight as some of its peers, a little more slow and floaty than i like, but i still enjoyed it.the game's story does have some dark elements that could make someone feel uncomfortable, especially if you're sensitive to stalking. it warns you before you start and you should take that warning seriously. it also give you the option to turn off texts from your "mom", a feature that i want more games to include. otherwise, my biggest complaint is that there is only one female romance interest. i love the enby rep but it would have been nice to see one more lady round out the cast.

_childDocuments_.review: These characters talk a good game about consent and communication, but the game doesn't care at all. Isaac thinks we're Together Forever and I have no idea what I did to make him think that; he definitely didn't ask me. The scythe asked me if I wanted to try sex/romance/sex+romance at like heart level 3, and that was apparently a binding contract I never got a chance to back out of that wasn't "be an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥." Another character "broke up with" me and my only options are to be different flavours of sad+outraged, but I'd been looking for a way to tell this guy to chill and not been seeing any options that weren't "express disgust at his plotspoiler secret." Also, this character might have murdered or assaulted someone and I never get to care about this?!? But I got a lot of opportunities to tell the graffiti artist her ♥♥♥♥'s illegal, because I have Priorities, I guess. The dungeon crawl part isn't long enough to fit the story, even if you don't "date" all the weapons. The two dungeons are really simplistic, more like a dungeon-crawling minigame. The weapons get more interesting as you level them up, but by that time you're out of dungeon to fight, so I'm not sure what the point of having more powerful weapons is.Sawyer is so, so awkward. I don't mean "adorably awkward." I mean "it is deeply uncomfortable to play this storyline." This character is a literal child. They're an undergraduate and you teach them how to cook and they hero-worship you. It's gross. You shouldn't be this kid's romantic or sexual interest, and you shouldn't be their friend either. If you're young enough to be involved with this kid, most of the *other* characters should not be involved with *you*. If this is really supposed to represent a 20-something, well, big yikes. And *really* bad gender politics. AFAB trans people and nonbinary people get infantilized enough without being cast as "adults who are basically children."The concept here is wacky and fun enough that I'd still have been happy with a simple game, or a game that looked like it could have been more but was ultimately scaled back to get it done. This is both of those things, but along with being unsatisfying, it's gross about consent in nearly every way it could be.WARNING: the content warning at the beginning says something about how it "may" involve stalking. Your game WILL involve stalking. STALKING IS CENTRAL TO THE PLOT.

_childDocuments_.review: Started playing the game because a friend had recommended it to me and had absolutely fallen in love with it! Everyone's visuals and characterizations are so diverse and downright lovable; the game's entire vibe is a well-curated combination of calming (with its ambiance and soundtracks) yet thrilling (the dungeon crawling) and energizing (the incredibly cute character interactions) all at the same time; the theme songs are incredibly gorgeous and utilized at the most appropriate of times that it greatly affects gameplay so beautifully (I can never shut up about how certain songs pop up so perfectly at key-scenes with the romanceables that it made me fall for them and the game deliciously deeper and how I'm well into making them my nightly lullaby by this point); and, the diversity of activities the game offers are all top-notch! _childDocuments_.review: I was really excited about this one, and while it looks slick, and everyone is beautiful, of course--even with limited time with it, it just feels pretty empty. The characters have no real 'hooks' to them, everyone is a slightly different flavor of smarm and/or already in love with you, and for all that there seems to be a sweet core to the interactions, it already veered into preachy from your very first interaction, maybe for fear of being labelled problematic (a common problem for LGBT+ VNs in my experience, as the call often comes from inside the house these days to rip LGBT stories to shreds for daring to have anything short of squeaky-clean Disney romances with perfectly upstanding model citizens as characters). With no risks, and pretty characters with no substance, it just feels like unprofessional writing with a nice package. Also the dungeon-crawling controls are extremely bad. They're too slow to respond, even for a mini-game, and as it is the 'main' mini-game, it seems like it should be more polished! The enemies are boring, the dodging is not reliable, and I had no fun at all. Gonna pass on the rest of this one. Sorry, guys. The idea is still so good, but the execution didn't hit for me from the get-go.

_childDocuments_.review: kickstarter syndrome strikes againIF YOU LIKE: Supergiant (Pyre, Hades, Transistor, Bastion), Dream Daddy, Stardew Valley, Monster PromSEE ALSO: Hatoful Boyfriend, Going Under, Unpacking, Moonlighter, HuniepopPROS:- LGBT + PLATONIC RELATIONSHIPS: huge dub. breaks heterosexual AND monogamous frameworks, going so far to talk about polyamorous relationships and includes explicitly stated "we are good friends and are ok with romantic/sexual tension because we talked it out" scenes. heavily appreciate the nb and ace options/dialogue- TECHNICALLY POLISHED: little to no bugs, game runs great, loading times are quick, transitions between dungeon to overworld to visual novel is smooth and charming, controller supported and easy to switch to K+M or vice versa; game autosaves frequently and i never needed to worry about the game's performance for any reason- FUN AND CHARMING CAST: everyone is HOT and memorable, even if on screen for only a moment. there is great attention to keep characters consistent and the attention to detail in little decisions being remembered later is always a fun touch. while hinging on tropes, it's not a bad thing, and it was clearly thought-out and fleshed to be more than a surface level quirk.CONS:- TOO SIMPLE, GAME-WISE: it's sometimes hard to distinguish enemies from environment in the cell-shaded art style the game uses. there's no outlines between PC to enemy to environment, or other visual cues; i relied on the sound cues + dialogue more than looking at the actual environment to expect a fight. i have a gripe about variant enemy types only being distinguished by one/two (sometimes unnoticed) visual quirks. as a self-advertised "shack-and-slash" dungeon crawler, i would have liked seeing more completely new enemies rather than another slightly bigger recolored foes.- TOO CLEAN, STORY-WISE: interactions or entire arcs end up too clandestine or had realism hand-waved away. i sadly include the main story in this. story is subjective to people's taste, but multiple instances felt like talking to characters was a formula. meet, date, level up, some conflict happens: "haha see you in the dungeon, same time next week!" - some conflicts being solved in one or less conversation with little chance to be explored felt jarring and i had to coax myself into suspending my disbelief more often than not.- OTHER:- ACCESSIBLE: contains story content warnings, easy to understand combat mechanics + handicap considerations, relatively little to no penalty for "wrong" date choices, change your character's pronouns/appearance anytime- EASY FOR EXPERIENCED ROGUE-LIKE PLAYERS: dungeons are piss easy; baby's first isometric roguelike. every run felt like "go to dungeon, go through 12 premade levels, also we gave you 2x xp for whatever reason and now every enemy is a oneshot". weapon combos are not particularly spectacular or varied. you can travel to any checkpoint floor a la Stardew Valley dungeon-elevator. i was having no trouble walking past enemies if i didn't want to fight. this is a con for me as someone who plays a lot of technically demanding games, but shouldn't be considered an "always bad" trait as this allows for more people to play and choose to take it at their own pace.- INCONSISTENT: sometimes i can't tell if this game is meant to be funny and light-hearted... or serious and introspective. i honestly can't tell if the dungeons are randomly generated or not. some character portraits don't match with the rest of the game's artstyle. a whole metagame-y and completely bizarre character interaction is fully forgotten and forgiven in literally a sentence? sometimes an enemy telegraphs attacks, sometimes they just hit me as they fly into me? some characters i intended to have a platonic relationship with, instead were written almost entirely from a romantic perspective and made incredibly awkward scenes??? the cat said WHATNOTES:back in 2018, i backed the kickstarter for this game. the expected delivery date was uh... 2019. hm, steam page says the game was released in 2021... (not that it mattered, it took me until 2022 to actually boot it up lmao) but now that i've finally played it, i say "yeah, it's another kickstarter game!"it's rare for me to find a game to play that i won't close in an hour. i definitely didn't expect to finish the entire thing, especially in an impromptu stream call with friends ending with 12 hours of talking/laughing with the game, 9 being actual game hours - but it's hard to recommend this game when, in the end, i don't feel it's a "good" game. there wasn't anything that stood out to me, which is a shame considering that it's very clear that the devs put a lot of thought and love into this. it felt like a lot of concepts were presented with efforts spread too thin to in order for anything in particular to shine. i don't like any of the datable characters to be dedicated to them, which is a big flag for me in a dating sim. it's just a "fine" game; i jokingly give it a 6/10 if people had to ask, then steeple my fingers in a big grin and say "you wanna know why?"the stalkeri had no problem with them (thankfully w/ the CWs, was prepared to encounter) and had no intention of mentioning this element of the game, but seeing other reviews and talking about this created great discussion that i hope more people consider. i see players considered the stalker as distasteful, sometimes triggering, sometimes annoying (same for me) and wanted this to be completely cut out of the game or skippable. i disagree with this wholeheartedly (there's plenty of access ALREADY, considering *gestures at the first half of this review*) - aside from asking devs to completely rework their plot since uh, the stalker is the driving point and climax of the main story, feels unreasonable. and just. feels wrong. i don't want to play a game that always "plays safe" - i want to play a game to have fun, win, interact with characters in a thrilling way. there is no thrill without a little danger. the stalker ends up being real and valid motivation for the story to move forward. why the heck are people asking the devs to remove them? what else are the characters supposed to do? why the heck are people asking an indie game studio founded on diversity and exploration to... not be diverse and explore? this character was a highlight for me in the game as someone who (sadly) has had so many similar conversations and situations from that kind of person, and i sure wish my situation ended as happily and healthily as it did in-game. having that kind of closure, artificial and incredibly lofty as it is, is still nice. it's personal, and i feel more connected to the game even if by a tiny thread. i feel like the people who fight against "problematic" material lose sight of the main point; to repeat myself, removing that aspect of the game would have not made this game so heartfelt. i enjoyed the fights and annoyance that this character brought, and i fight for them to stay in the base game. i say all of this because if given the choice and the devs did remove them, i would have chosen to do so - and would have had a lesser gaming experience and impression of the game because of it.in the end i had fun! i see the love from kitfox and it's admittedly validating to see the LGBTA+/platonic rep in modern games. i ultimately want to support indie devs to make games, especially without having to worry about conforming to people's (corporation's AND fan's) will.

What I found was a really easy going intro to the genre for a newbie like me. The combat, rogue-lite, dungeon crawl part was major chill and shouldn’t be much of a challenge for most folks but if it is you can turn on easy mode. _childDocuments_.review: TL:DR: Good game, graphics and sound 10/10, ending kinda meh, funny weapon dating.I love this game. Always enjoyed dating sims but they can feel "idle" a lot of the times. The music is peak, the style is pretty and easy to look at, only getting overwhelmed with too many monsters on screen, but that is hardly avoidable gamedesign wise.Very inclusive and considerate. A lot of different characters, male, female, enby. Also covering some serious tones about self-care and self-growth. The characters don't feel flat, they have personality and often feel like real people, not just a cliche or steriotype of character. However wished your choices mattered more, but who plays a dating sim for the story anyways?Gameplay is great, feels fluid and every weapon has a different style, however that makes it difficult to progress with a character you like but hate how the gameplay aspect of the weapon is feeling. In my opinion every weapon has pros and cons, making this somewhat balanced, but if you really hate how the weapon is playing, chances are, you're not having fun in leveling their relationship. All of them are sweethearts.The ending is very underwhelming, feeling like the story is going too easy on the "antagonist". Disregarding my personal opinion of him, he comitted multiple criminal acts, many of them probably resulting in jailtime, yet he promises to do better and go to therapy? I understand the message of giving people a chance to better themselves and not to lose faith in someone for mistakes but he literally commited crimes. At least make him face those consequences too. Other than the ending, I quite enjoyed all the story around the characters and it feels like a world with lots going on, even if we "just" see into the characters lives. _childDocuments_.review: The short version: There's nothing incredibly negative I felt towards this game so generally I'd recommend it, but more so if you like dating sims and less so if you like rogue-likes. Playing for almost 9 hours got me nearly all of the achievements. For me that makes the 20 dollar price tag fairly worth it, and any sale price even more worth it. The long version: Pros: There's a lot to love here. This game has a lot of fun queer representation and a very unique cast of characters. All of the weapons felt good to use in dungeons, and I didn't feel that any one weapon was more powerful than the others. Gameplay is pretty easy, maybe even accessible? Normally I don't learn combat very quickly in video games but after running the same dungeon floors twice or so it was pretty simple to get through. This may change player to player, but I was really appreciative of how the dungeon pacing matched the story pacing pretty well. It gets frustrating in games where you're left grinding for several hours to get kinda close to being prepared for a plot battle, and on the other side it's kinda disappointing when your combat is so far ahead of the plot that you two shot the big bad boss in the finale. The "final boss" here had good timing with how quickly I arrived to having a weapon close to love rank 6. There's only 6 dateable weapons, but I think it's safe to say that their personalities are varied enough that there's more likely than not a character you will be very attached to. The early game is a little rocky, because I felt that the combat was kinda clunky at first but once I got over that it was easy to put in the additional eight and a half hours. The cons: spoilers ahead. I will cover the plot related ones, but not the ones that deal with dateable weapons/the dates.A lot of the weapons definitely feel like shadows of characters rather than characters. I'm not sure if I'm just that far out from dating sims, if it was intentional since the story only takes place over a summer, or other constraints, but it made trying to get through some dates kinda painful.  I think the fun I've had with other dating sims was meeting a character, having a general feel for a character, then having some sort of wrench thrown in that mix, whether that be something very bizarre like being a secret candle reviewer online or having a double life, literally anything. The characters in this game definitely felt like the proverbial wrench was simply that they have fears and doubts about their life/career paths, which is realistic but really left me feeling like they didn't do much else. In the same vein, I kinda liked that all of the dates kinda flowed together into a cohesive mini-story, but I also kinda didn't like that. It goes hand-in-hand with what I said previously. I don't think it's a bad thing but I'll put it in this section anyway: the combat is kinda just button mashing most of the time. Sure you can do cool stuff, but usually if you mash Y instead of X. I think my ultimate disappointment is that I feel like the game could've done just a bit more. There's no penalty for just getting every weapon to rank 6, I guess I'm supposed to presume every character is polyamorous even though only one explicitly states it? You can even switch weapons between floors, so wouldn't it have been interesting to have the current weapon comment on the previous weapon you held in some way, not just jealously but admiration or even ambivalence? "Ah I see you wanted to use a *real* weapon this time" or anything like that?  Am I just supposed to believe that even though Verona Beach seems fairly small, that most of these characters have never interacted in any way? I was really left wishing that each weapon wasn't so...compartmentalized and boxed off from each other. Now...for Eric. More minor, but still worth mentioning: You're immediately dropped into the game and told that fighting through dungeons is how you can deal with your fears. Not only is it literally stated as plainly as that, it's not really explained further as to why dungeons manage to be both your personal therapy-through-fighting-cell-phone-monsters, and also a genuine hazard to the general public of Verona Beach. Also. They shorten dungeons as "the dunj." As texting slang, fine, but I'm pretty sure characters *say* dunj instead of dungeon. Maybe I'm old but that word is not hardly worth shortening...Even after all my complaining, I do still recommend this game, I think the 20 dollar price tag is fairly worth it and honestly, my complaints exist more because I liked the game enough, and not because I disliked it.

_childDocuments_.review: Boyfriend Dungeon is a unique twist on the dating simulator genre. You explore dungeons armed with your weapon of choice, but you also get to date your human-like weapon. While the game presentation and soundtracks are impeccable, the dungeon crawler aspect of the game can feel a bit repetitive. Overall, Boyfriend Dungeon is very engaging and fun to complete but way too short. With only three dungeons to explore, you can only wish that such a unique experience would have been longer. The dating sim aspect of the game is quite inclusive and well written which makes you even sadder that the experience lasts only 10 hours at best. Boyfriend dungeon is quite charming. It mixes different art-styles to create a cozy experience. It is quite similar to “Kitfox Games” previous entry: Moon Hunter. The main gameplay happens in a simplified and stylised 3D sprite work. Although simple, it still brings a certain charm and atmosphere to each dungeon, everything is clearly visible and still detailed enough to have its identity. The Datin Sim part of the game uses gorgeous illustrations for the characters and the backgrounds. Overall, the game gives a very warm and cozy vibe. Another very strong point of Boyfriend dungeon is its soundtrack. Most of the tracks have that “indie” vibes to them that really fit the “a summer abroad” setting. The simplicity of the tracks doesn’t take away their quality and they really fit perfectly with the art style. Moreover, of the 26 tracks, 14 have lyrics and singing on top of them. They are usually used during particular dialogues to reenforce a particular feeling. I personally think they are quite enjoyable. Those tracks are worth a listen:Boyfriend Dungeon is a unique mix of different genre. The first part is a dungeon crawler type of game where you dive into a dungeon with one of the different weapons at your disposition and the second part is a dating simulator where you date... the weapon you used in the dungeon. Don’t worry, those weapons can transform into human form so it’s... not as weird as it sounds. The dungeon part consists in exploring around 12 levels of a randomly generated dungeon, defeating enemies, collecting recipes and material for crafting and of course gaining love level with your weapon. This is however a bit repetitive and not really that challenging. By gaining levels you will quickly overpower everything in the dungeon, and you’ll just go through them without many thoughts. The same way, crafting is very barebone, each recipe can be used only once, and you’ll never have to really farm to get the materials needed. This part was still fun, but it lacked depth. With only three dungeons, you kind of miss some variety and challenges that a game centred on that aspect would have had. The second part of the game, the dating simulator is quite okay. You have a phone and periodically receive (A TON) messages from your lovers/friends and with each love level you gain in the dungeon you can further the relationship with a particular weapon. You can also offer gifts to strengthen your bond with them. Quite an important part of any dating sim. Here you can date 9 weapons and befriend a cat-weapon too. Kitfox tried to be as inclusive as possible while creating their characters. You can date any of the characters regarding of your gender. The roster is composed of four men, three women and two non-binary people with quite different personalities. If some of them seem a bit one-dimensional at first, they quickly show a bit more depth. However, I’d say that some of them can turn a bit annoying the more you date them. It’s very much a question of taste and what you like to talk about. I found some dialogues to be a snooze fest while others got me completely invested in them.  I also appreciate that a lot of the characters discuss important topics regarding dating such as consent, honesty, or even obsessive behaviours. Story is both predictable and trivial. You see it coming from the very beginning, but I don’t think that it was meant to be the centre of the game. It is a bit sad because the final boss is just as bland as the main plot. I would say however that I really like a story where the main character spends a summer abroad searching for themselves. You know you’re going to have to say goodbye at some point and every time someone mentioned it during the main game, I just didn’t want summer to end. You can 100% the game in one playthrough and in the span of 10 hours. I don’t really see what you could objectively do differently story wise except dating another weapon or friendzone some others. It is perfectly possible to date everyone in a single playthrough, so you won’t miss many things. I enjoyed the dungeon, but there’s nothing quite different about them once you collected everything to motivate you to go back to it.  The 45 achievements are quite easy to get. You receive them for collecting recipes, and basically dating the weapons. You can’t really miss any of them.

_childDocuments_.review: Having been waiting for this game ever since it was first announced years back, it did not disappoint. Though it's a short game at launch (almost 100% clear in about 7-8 hours), the characters are all interesting in their own way, there are a lot of branching paths, and there's plenty of room for replayability. The gameplay itself is sort of awkward on keyboard unless you remap the controls, and the glaive is not great without the mouse or a controller, which is unfortunate, but each weapon is equally good in most cases and although the second dungeon can be pretty hard, you're only really likely to actually die at the start of the game, after which there is a generous leveling system. There are some issues with the game that can be rectified - in town, some things have collision detection when they clearly do not need to, making things a little annoying. Also, I experienced a softlock on the final boss, which sucked, but it's only a day or two after launch so I can forgive that.Overall, short but sweet and I highly recommend it. Not just for the duck jokes or the 'use a whetstone on a lasersaber' or the cat.

_childDocuments_.review: is a rogue-lite/dating-sim. There are 3 dungeons, 5 bosses, several equipment pieces. The MC's name and appearance are customizable, level progression is completely automatic and linear (higher level = more HP and higher damage). Difficulty depends on the PC's level, because nothing scales and it is easy to out-level everything. There are no penalties for defeat in dungeons, XP and loot acquired are kept.The controls are responsive and rebindable, 5-button mice are supported. The game uses 1 auto-save. There are 9 weapons that are unlocked as the story progresses. It is impossible to alienate or antagonise them, they love the MC no matter what and always available to use after acquiring them.Dialogue choices are rather limited, but often reflected in following dialogues. The main story itself relies heavily on the MC's passivity and lack of attention, while the main antagonist is extremely obvious and ridiculously incompetent. There is no in-game journal or log. In general, clearing 1 floor of a dungeon is enough to trigger next event. I have not encountered any significant bugs.Recommended on sale, because the game technically achieves what it states on the store page - there are weapons who are possible to date, randomly-generated dungeons offer action-based combat, despite both aspects being shallow.

_childDocuments_.review: It made me smile, it made me laugh, and, when it was over, it made me cry.Action Roguelikes are not the sort of game I typically play, but hearing my friends gush about the game and learning about its character customization (Unlike 99% of games on the market today with character creators, the game allows non binary people to actually play as themselves and have both the game and its characters refer to them with gender neutral pronouns) I decided I had to give it a try. The combat is fun, the dialogue well written and voiced, graphics charming, music's a bop, and the boys... They're good boys, Brent. Except the ones who aren't boys, but they're also good and I love them.I recommend it, even if you're not into guys, in which case you have the option to simply play this game as "Friends with Boys Dungeon" and hang out with them instead.And yes, you can pet the cat.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game; though a little on the short side, so maybe wait for the upcoming DLC to come out.Turns out Dating sims and roguelikes go pretty well together! The variety of cute characters to date and a decently fleshed out dungeoneering really help breaking up the monotony and faffing about of each genre. The dating aspects are quite engaging and  give you some goals to work towards where roguelikes can feel a bit aimless at times, and the dungeoneering add some game and actual test of skill beyond picking dialogue options. The way your dating progress is tied to the leveling the weapons in the dungeon also helps you feel like you're constantly making progress.For the Dating Sim there's plenty variety of characters to romance, each with pretty interesting storylines. The roguelike portion of this game is pretty reminiscent of Hades (in a good way), though perhaps a little light on  replay-ability. Not a real issue, considering the Dating/Story aspect is the focus of the game, just don't expect to sink hundreds of hours into it.:This free update is maybe not monumental in extra playtime, but does add a nice chunk of extra content in the shape of a new area, a new bossfight and three new characters (as well as some new collectibles). For old players this gives a nice opportunity to return to this game and for new this should simply weave into the main game seamlessly.The new area definitely provides a bit more of a challenge, and the boss fight has a nice scoring mechanic that provides a nice opportunity to get A+ with all weapons (easier with some than with others).I don't know if any new content will still be added, but all in all I definitely enjoyed this game and the update. Well worth a try!

_childDocuments_.review: I was one of the Kickstarter backers, and they did us really dirty. There's are two weapons that were fully funded (A Hammerbabe and Axebro) and should of been in the game at release. One of which is the Surfer Axe guy who clearly was coded to be in the game, has UI and sprites, but the character just abruptly leaves instead of staying in the game. So they took peoples money saying you could use Jonah, but just gave him a little cameo instead. They took our money, went dark for some time, and then cut content before release.The writing in this game is pretty bad, characters are as deep as puddles. Everything is about your feelings and magic and other crap. You can sum up the essence of every character with one sentence. The main character is a total loser that can't talk to an attractive person without freaking out, their cousin is obsessed with wing-manning us, Isaac has daddy issues and does not want to run his Conservative dads company, Sunder is a lazy ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ vampire, Valeria is your standard street kid artist from the barrios, Seven is whiny famous person that does not like being famous, the only regular smith in town is a human supremecist, etc. The problem is that every datable character is either a horrible person or a walking stereotype. As mentioned, there is a smithy character who exists to act racist towards weapon people so that you might be tricked into liking them more. This game can be summed up as "Trying to be Hades and failing" in that it really wants to be Hades but will never get there. BFD want's to do the same thing, where sexy characters explore a randomized dungeon to grow deeper relationships. The problem is that the modern setting of Verona Beach legit makes no sense, there are places in town that turn your worst fear into monsters that can kill you, this is a major plot point. WHERE IS THE NATIONAL GUARD, WHERE ARE THE COPS!? The game never addresses what weapon-people are, why they can do it, and why/where Verona Beach is like it is. The aformentioned monster place is... THE MALL AND NIGHTCLUB? So you are telling me that all of the social hotspots in this city feed on your dark emotions and breed monsters? No seriously where are the freaking cops. The other thing is that there's no real call to action, you just randomly start finding weapons down in the Dunj, who then hit you up for dates the second they leave the screen. Also, I refuse to interact with any person that calls it "The Dunj" like fighting monsters in bloody combat is some kind of quirky sexy modern activity. Now let's talk about the REAL reason I am not suggesting this game: It's too easy. Every dungeon run gives you XP depending on how many floors and monsters you fought. Even though the game offers you elevators to start deeper down THIS IS A TRAP. Because the game puts so much weight behind XP and leveling up, it behooves you to just start from the bottom every time to rack up fat XP with almost zero danger behind it. This also allows you to power through the XP you require to level up your weapons... I mean living people who we are dating.... and thus be able to do a dungeon run, do everybodies events, then power back down there. There is an your face gameyness here that drains any fun or romance out of it. In general this was an indie attempt to copy off another indie's homework, and it failed.
