_childDocuments_.review: A nice short game if you want to chill for an evening or two. The dungeon crawling part can be a bit challenging at low levels, especially if you're using a weapon that doesn't suit your playstyle, but once you level up enough it's not too bad. The only dungeon I really hated was the third one because it had a really annoying gimmick, but even then the game is short enough that I managed to complete it without hitting the rage-quit point. The dating sim part, on the other hand, can be a bit hit or miss. On the plus side, there's a good variety of people/weapons to meet, all with their own quirks and interests. You probably won't like ALL of them (I honestly kind of low-key hated the scythe), but odds are at least one will catch your interest even if you just want to stick to being bros instead of boinking every person you meet. All in all, a nice, comfy game that lets you pretend to have friends that actually care about you - at least for a day or two.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh gosh oh gosh oh gosh where do I begin.So I am fresh off my first playthough, and I hope this is coherent. I love this game. Unabashedly. The characters are lovable and their character arcs are accessible, AND I got to smooch all the smoochable ones. The dungeon hack and slash was fun (and with 7 weapons to rotated through, I didn't get bored), I got to dress up my character. Pretty much everything I wanted from this game. AND TWO NONBINARY KISSMATE OPTIONS.That said, there are a few critiques I have, mainly about the storylines/dating parts [so possible spoilers ahead]! A handful of times, I would select a line and it felt like I was being responded to as if I'd chosen a different answer. And it didn't feel like there was a difference between the romance and friendship paths (ie, someone I had gotten full ranks with and invited to come home with me kept calling me "mon ami"). Just little things like that that made it feel like it didn't matter what I chose, which bugged me. I can only hope that it's not the other way around too. And just like there didn't seem to be a difference between friendship and romance, there didn't seem to be a difference between monogamy and polyamory. I chose full polyamory and I would have liked there to be a discussion with the characters about it; one of the characters makes it seem like they'd prefer to be monogamous, but it's never brought up again and they don't get bring up you dating other people. To me, polyamory is very much about open communication. Everyone needs to be on the same page, and the fact that it wasn't discussed at all did bother me. I wanted to make sure everyone was okay with it, and I wanted to see the other characters interact more!The character plotlines also weren't as... ironed out as they could have been. I don't know if I was pressing the buttons too fast and just not absorbing everything, but there were times when a character would say something about their lives, and I'd be surprised, because it felt like it'd been going on for a while and that was the first they'd mentioned of it. It felt like rather than an arc, I was getting little blips. My last critique is of the plotline behind the smooching. I know some people are bothered by Eric and his arc, and that's valid (I for one wish I could have been harsher to him), so if I'm in the minority that's fine, but I actually wanted more. Possibly more dungeons, more delving into what drove him. I wanted a real villain out of him, and I didn't get that. I understand why we don't dwell on it, this is a game of smooching sword babes, not delving into some weirdo's obsession, but the fact that we only got a taste made me want more. Anyway, for all the things that bugged me, and the interesting things that didn't pan out, I still enjoyed it for what it was. 7.5/10 for this game, I am still very satisfied with having backed it. Can't wait for the DLC! <3

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game on a whim and then forgot about for months, then decided on a whim to open it. AND IT COULDN'T PUT IT DOWN. I finished it in about 7.5 hrs, then went back in a 2nd playthrough to see how choices impacted play. One of the first things I noticed is that this game has some pretty incredible music that absolutely HITS at all the right times, I seriously recommend checking out the soundtrack. Past that, it does a very good job of... being exactly itself. The concept is incredibly cool, and if you don't take it TOO seriously, you'll have a lot of fun! This may be one of the few games I've played that featured romance-able characters where I actually nearly wanted to date everyone -- that never happens to me! Each character was unique, engaging and interesting. My main gripe is that I wish there was more content. Feels odd to be called Dungeon Boyfriend with only two dungeons. _childDocuments_.review: Boyfriend Dungeon is a game I picked up because I thought it looked cool. A dating simulator where the people you date turn into weapons and then you build relationships by taking them into the dungeon? That sounds pretty neat!! Except the execution left much to be desired. In the initial version of the game, there were two dungeons. That's it. Two whole dungeons in a game about dungeon crawling. The combat in the dungeons can feel shallow, with your moveset changing between your various partners. Speaking of whom, though the game is called Boyfriend Dungeon, you'll be met with a cast of men, women, non-binaries, and a cat, all of which you can swing at monsters with. The strength and abilities of each weapon are dependant on your relationship progress with each character, meaning the new weapons you pick up later will be weaker and harder to use against the current dungeon, forcing you to find a way to cope with it or to move back to an earlier section of the game. As for the bosses of each dungeon, they range from "incredibly boring and straightforward" to "how the hell am I supposed to even approach this". That mostly covers the Dungeon part, so moving onto the Boyfriend part; The game will not shame you for polyamory, though you do have the choice to keep a relationship platonic when interacting with the cast, which I appreciate. At a certain point, they released a free DLC that added three more weapons (only two of which you could wield), and a whole one more dungeon. For a total of three dungeons. In a DUNGEON CRAWLER. Yes I am still bitter about this. No matter which sword you choose to smooch, you will be harassed by a blacksmith that your cousin tries to set you up with. He is, undoubtedly, the worst part of this game. Using the game's texting system, he pesters you constantly, even after you tell him to go away. I wish you could just ignore him, but you are forced to answer to every one of his messages in order to move the game's plot forward, and watch as he stalks you on dates and harasses your partners. Then, during the final boss fight (spoilers, by the way) you are forced to tell him that he isn't a horrible person and that he's trying to become better in order to weaken the final boss.Overall, it feels like a waste of an interesting premise.

_childDocuments_.review: Since they've updated it a ton, even though it's still got the same issues I see it's not abandoned so lets give it a likeMy review used to be positive but I have changed it to negative after a replay and my initial giggle passed. (Will put updated at the end)I loved the game!There is space to improve but here's the good and bad sides for me personally.PROS: - A lot of puns, so the dialogue is fun- Fun combat system which is easy yet satisfying- You can romance more than once so you don't techically need to do multiple runs just to see what each character has to offer. However it makes me feel slightly guilty, despite the characters being okay with poly I IRL am not comfortable with it.- Wacky conversation option which are funny- Overall cool characters with lots of diversity- Good musicCONS:- Doesn't offer many chances to reject/friendzone characters. I wanted to go for a single person near the end but no longer could turn down other romance options- Only two dungeons, would be good if more were added with an update- Each dungeon only has one (or maybe 2) soundtracks, so it becomes slightly repetitive after a while, could do with more music optionsOverall Score: 5/7 :DSo, after sitting on it a bit and replaying the game...I've come to realise how the game is actually very railroaded. Your options, although often funny, always lead to the same outcome. Even if you attempt to friendzone them, they'll still love you. For no good reason. The PC can do nothing and still be loved. Nothing much changed with the ending, everyone still showed up and partied like we were friends. What really also bothered me was the inconsistency. For example the  and that even when you reject them, or friendzone them, they still act as if you're lovers and basically it is like they do not take no for an answer.For my second playthrough I wanted to do an experiment to see if anything would change if There were so many missed opportunties to make this game a replayable dating sim jewel. However the game ultimately falls short after you try to play it more than once. There's nothing more to do.There's only two dungeons which I have managed on my second playthrough to go through them whole in a single try, without extra levels or weapon upgrades. From what I could see, there were supposed to be even more romantic interests but they probably cut the game short just to release it, so hammer and axe got....axed.All in all, I had some mindless fun, just...disappointed now when I look at it again and see what it could've been.I hope the game recieves a content update with more 'dunjs', fixed writing that respects 'no' as a no, friends being just that, and actually makes your choices feel more relevant overall. When that day comes, I'll happily change my review back to positive and replay it all again.

_childDocuments_.review: After making your character, you arrive at Verona Beach so you can spend your summer there, with the help of your cousin Jesse letting you stay at his old apartment as the lease isn’t up until summer ends. However, this isn’t a summer that you can lay back and chill inside or soaking up the rays. Your mother has decided that this would be the perfect time to solve your problem of not dating anyone, not going on any dates, and your confidence problem (which is all true for me irl). Jesse has the solution for both of them: set up dates for you and have you go into dungeons that often appear at Verona Beach. While Jesse’s meddling resulted in some horrible dates, one of which proceeds to be a jerk stalker that doesn’t get the hint that you want nothing to do with him, the dungeon part actually works out. For both of the things Jesse is trying to help out with. You learn that there are some people (and animals) that can turn into weapons and you are sadly not one of them. But you can wield them. You meet Isaac first, an Estoc, that is happy to show you the ropes. While this is a great way to get some exercise in and make some money, Isaac also explains that these dungeons manifest based on your fears and insecurities, and the monsters there change their shape based on it too. It also seems like there isn’t a set amount of floors as it also depends on how deep your own fears or insecurities run (though both dungeons are both 12 floors). It doesn’t take long for you to meet another weapon, though it’s not in the best circumstances as he mentions that someone abducted him, chipped his blade, and left him in the dungeon. And you’ll meet the other weapons in the same predicament. Good thing that all they need is to have a day outside of the dungeon to rest to heal the damage and that they’re pretty open to letting you wield them and date them.In terms of the characters and the dating aspect, they’re both fine. The characters are the types where you’d like some of them, rather than liking all or most of them, but they are well written from what we got. I did enjoy the vast majority of the interactions and getting to know them. Past the initial meeting and the dialog you’ll get in dungeons (and the two parties where one weapon will come with you), they don’t interact with each other and you’ll really only interact with them when you rank up their Love Rank which they’ll text you and you can find where they are on the map (which your character can run on to get where they are) to get to their date (or it’s automatic once you reply if it’s happening at your apartment). However, they only have 6 ranks each, which can result in some of them feeling rushed, and you’re more or less pushed into accepting them as your romantic partner each time even if you want to keep them as a friend. This may be due to the game letting you be poly and date all of them at the same time, which none of them really care if you do and don’t tell them, but it is a weird choice considering the game says that it’s fine if you want just a platonic relationship with them.Anyways, onto the dungeon crawling part. There are (sadly) only 2 dungeons here, representing the fear of change and the fear of intimacy, that you can unlock and go to. And when you dive into it, it’s pretty easy to get the hang of it. You’ll choose who you’ll be wielding before going in and all the weapons are handled differently. They excel in different aspects based on their weapon type and have differences in their combos. They all are best or not so great in certain situations, like Isaac isn’t that great when surrounded by a lot of enemies (which happens a lot in the second dungeon), but they all handle pretty well. This is also a first for me where I was fine using any of the weapons and not dreading using one. Granted, I’m more of a person that like weapons (/characters) that are focused on attack fast and not the slow, but powerful, ones. You’ll also be able to dodge, which is best to get the hang of, and you’ll have several drinks (which depends on what you pick as a preference) that will heal you as well as zines that act as another way to hurt enemies or delay them. There are also certain hats that will give you an effect bonus like stunning enemies or having drinks heal more. Though, it does become easy enough to where you can just wear whatever you like best.Once you complete a floor, the weapon you were using gets some EXP for their Love Rank and you can switch it out for someone else before you get to the next floor. As extra EXP doesn’t overflow to the next, it is best to switch them out so that EXP don’t go to waste. You can also gift them something, each they all have gifts they hate, like, or love, to help them rank up, but there are only certain situations that the game will let you. Although, it has to be said that once you max one weapon, you are given an item that gives you double EXP and EXP overflow for the rest (which either was planned or is because it feels like one more dungeon was supposed to be included). When a weapon ranks up, this unlocks a date for the next day and a skill that will help you in battle. So the more you rank them up, the more helpful they are. Like Isaac will get the ability to riposte and charged attacks, Sunder will be able to inflict bleed, and Valeria can inflict Confusion. Some ranks will also have two different variations on the ability that you can choose to reflect how you wield them.You level up as well, but it’s only when you’re exiting the dungeon. This gives you more health to work with and, I believe, lets you hit harder so if you find yourself not doing a lot of damage when you encounter the tougher variants, you might want to exit so you can level up. Certain floors will have an elevator so you can exit early and let you start the dungeon at that floor (though you might not want to use this to skip floors so you can rank up the weapons and get money early on).There are various shops around, both on Verona Beach’s map and a secret shop in dungeons, that will sell different outfits for you to wear, crafting resources, and gifts. The crafting resources will let you make the various recipes you acquire. The best outfits and hats you’ll get will be from these recipes, you can only craft the different zines, and a lot of the gifts are from recipes (and aren’t as expensive).However, this game is missing some content and has the underlying feeling that it could have benefited more by having more time. 2 weapons are not implemented, Leah the hammer and Owen the axe (though Owen does appear briefly), and have already been mentioned that they will be added as DLC along with some additional stuff (though as far as I know, it’s not clear whether it’ll be free or paid for those that aren’t Kickstarter backers). It would be interesting to see how they would be implemented though. Would it be weaved into the main story where it supposed to have been or would it be in a post-game where you’d be visiting for a week or two (or full on moving there)?While I looked forward to Boyfriend Dungeon for a long time, I did enjoy my time with it, and I had fun playing it to where I barely convinced myself to complete it in 2 sittings, the more I thought about the game to write the review, the more I just found disappointing and wanting more of. There’s a lack of dungeons and there’s a lack on the dating sim aspect, so unless you’re someone that didn’t have big expectations and fine with this being more simple than it lets on, it’s going to feel a bit disappointing. I still recommend it, as it still is a fun game to play, but some might want to wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Boyfriend Dungeon offers a unique concept, mixing two improbable genres together in a very silly story about weapons turning into hot people. It sounds like a concept of a game you joke about with friends but never get to actually making. Well I'm happy the developers took the plunge and made that unlikely game.I found the core loop really engaging, and would find myself telling myself after every dungeon run "ok let's just have some date", and after every series of dates "ok let's go for one more dungeon run". The alternation between both kept the game from becoming repetitive.I'm happy with the care the developers took to make the experience both accessible and inclusive. They give content warnings, give you an option to opt-out of interacting with a secondary character called Mom, allow you to choose your pronouns, include non-binary characters (plural! a rarity!), and so on and so forth. I felt amazed by all this, and I really wish more games were like that.The soundtrack is catchy, and I kept listening to it after I've completed the game. I love playing a game with original tracks that have vocals; it's not common and it gives it a certain charm.I didn't feel like all the romance options were as interesting and likeable. For example, Valeria and Sunder are quite flirty with you, have some depth, include you in their hobbies and have some twists in their story. On the other hand, you get characters like Sawyer, who doesn't really have much to offer as a lover, and whose story evolve mostly around you helping them out to learn how to cook because their skills are very lacking. You don't need to go on all dates with every weapon, and even if you do you can do so platonically, but still in a dating sim I would have preferred if all dateable characters were romantically interesting.The fighting is not the most exciting, but it serves its purpose and it's decent enough for a game with more than one focus. I think it's a good thing that it isn't too complex or too hard, because otherwise a lot of people who came in for the dating would be stuck because of the fighting.Overall, great experience, do recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a delightful and lighthearted game! I wouldn't recommend it to someone looking for a hearty rouge-like or dungeon crawler, nor someone interested in an in-depth dating visual novel, but anyone who enjoys both those types of games and is looking for something to sink a weekend or so into would have a great time with this game.Combat: The combat is simple and easy to pick up, but I recommend trying it with a controller, as I found that much more intuitive than keyboard and mouse. It's not very robust and there's not a great deal of strategy to it, but the combinations of weapons, zines, and headwear could shake things up and it was fun trying out new things. Again, if you're looking for a game where the combat is the main focus, I would look elsewhere. It never hit a point where I was sick of it, but it can get repetitive, especially when getting everyone to max love level and finding all the blueprints (but that's not required to beat the game, so I did that willingly).Story: Avoiding spoilers, I thought the story was good. The main plot was basic, but it's clear the main draw of the game is the dates with the other characters, which shine. I appreciated the options for platonic or romantic relationships and how the game doesn't make you pick a single character and ignore the rest. Getting to max love with all the characters was great; their stories and lives were made with care and the writing is excellent. It's the kind of game where everyone who can be romanced is attracted to you and (mostly) never oversteps boundaries, so not the most realistic in that department, but this is also a game where people turn into weapons and the mall has monsters in it, so realism isn't really a big concern here. The more serious elements that they do touch on are largely handled appropriately, but I've seen some comments about the shifts in tone being a little strange, which I can agree with. But considering the nature of the game and how you can jump around between characters and quests at your leisure, I can see how that's hard to avoid.Value: I picked up the game shortly after the big secret weapons update, so I can't speak to what the game was like before then, but with it I thought the game has a good amount of content for the price. Not much by way of replay value, outside of going down different paths of friendship or romance with people, but the game leaves things open-ended enough that you never lock yourself into someone's route, which I appreciate as someone who doesn't have the time to put into replaying a game over and over. All in all, a lovely game! I hope to see more of it in the future!!

_childDocuments_.review: Boyfriend Dungeon is a story about you and several weapon-people who you get to know over the course of a summer. It's filled with funny, ridiculous and stupid moments. Some characters are great while others need as much therapy as feasibly possible or jail time. But let's not dwell on that as I go into more details!There's a lot I could say about the art style, mainly that it's distinctive and gorgeous. A lot of the backgrounds make you truly feel like you're there. The attention to detail is incredible!The animations are stunning for when a weapon transforms back into a person (or cat) and vice versa. It takes me back to watching anime with magical girls except less sexualised.I also love the design of the characters (even the ones who I felt awkward with). The highlight was definitely  because it showed one of the weapon-people in another getup that is very them.Speaking of which, let's talk about them! I'll try to keep my descriptions short and to the point as there are quite a few characters to get through.Isaac – Overall nice and polite despite having family issues. Valeria – Cool with an intriguing past.Sunder – Too much in every way.Seven – Distant but not rude. I'd say more like cautious and kind of cute.Sawyer – Filled with energy all the while being clumsy as they try their best.Pocket – Wary of strangers (as most cats tend to be) but also a sweetheart once you get to know him.Jonah – Sweet and respectful.Leah – Overall lovely.Dr. Holmes – Weird and reminds me of Director Qi from My Time at Sandrock in the way they speak. However, I much prefer Qi as he's adorably awkward whereas Holmes is just odd.Then there's also your cousin Jesse, his fiancée Samantha and the blacksmith Eric. Jesse is cool and Samantha is sweet. Eric on the other hand… I despise him. For obvious reasons. There's also another person named Olivia who is a worker but she doesn't play a huge role. She's the most side character to ever side character. There's also another weapon-person who I didn't get to know well and since I don't like their weapon style, the chances of me learning more about them is very low.It's smooth and quick but also challenging. Now, I'm not too well-versed in dungeon crawlers or roughlike games but I've played Pokémon Mystery Dungeon, Skul: The Hero Slayer, and Hades.I'd say this game is pretty up there in terms of enjoyment. I had fun trying out the different weapons and abilities unique to each character. Some may not like the repetitiveness in enemies but I don't mind it. For me, it makes it easier to learn their pattern (which is a saving grace when you're highly under levelled).I adore the music in this! It's a mixture of bouncy and chill. It evokes the adventure you feel when slaying monsters in the dungeons but also reminds you to take it easy every once in a while.In most soundtracks, I find one or two songs which to me are mediocre. Not in this though! I can confidently say I liked them all and will listen to the music for the next few weeks or months.The story in this is very simple: You're on summer vacation in Verona Beach where you meet up with your cousin and then date a lot of people. There's not much else to it apart from getting to know said characters. That's the meat of all this.If they weren't present (and the choice to date them), the entire thing would fall apart. It would be just another dungeon crawler. But it's not. It's a dungeon crawler with some interesting twists and turns.I have seen some pretty bad literature in video games. Sometimes I truly wonder if people even bother to have anyone edit or proofread anything before they publish. Other times, it's quite nice. I can tell a lot of work and love went into the making of the game.This one strangely fits right in the middle. Overall, the literature is enjoyable – it's funny, punchy and doesn't overwhelm you with descriptions. It gives you more than enough to make an image in your head.However, there were times where the text looked gross, namely from the overuse of two dots instead of three. Or just overusing in general. I also found a few sentences which made no sense whatsoever or when it should have switched to description but the dialogue box of the character persisted. That's probably more a design nitpick but I'm still including it!In its entirety, I'd give it a 6/10.Boyfriend Dungeon provides a wacky adventure filled with lots of dating and some internal struggles.

_childDocuments_.review: I would say I am about middle ground with this game, but I'd overall give it a recommendation for more reasons that I'd say I'd recommend against it. Here are my general opinions of the gamePros:-Really great LGBTQ+ representation in the game. Pronouns are a part of the game and can be changed at any time for your PC, and does not affect who you can date. Dialogue options make room for people of ace/aro/poly identities to be supported as well, and dateable characters are of differing gender presentations: some cis men, some cis women, some non-binary.-Great artistic style and great music soundtrack. Art is more unique for some games I've seen and music is generally pleasant and fun depending on where you are in the game. -Simplistic and easy-to-follow controls for combat, unique styles for each weapon used that give great versatility to each of the weapons you can wield.Cons:Storylines for each of the characters, and the game as a whole, lack depth and don't entirely make sense all of the time either.  There are separate romance and friendship tracks for each of the characters, which are mixed in throughout their storyline, but it's not always apparent which is which, and it doesn't always make logical sense why some characters would react the ways that they do to certain responses you can give. Sometimes, as other commenters have stated, it's a choice between the obvious positive and obvious negative choice, which gives the storylines too much of a railroading feel to them.-This is more of a middle ground depending on what you're looking for, but this game is *very* short. I'm typing this at about 8 hours of gameplay and I have completed the main story and maxed out all storylines for the characters. _childDocuments_.review: This is an absolutely fantastic game. I literally bought this like yesterday as soon as I got the email notification that it was available on steam and then did an 8 hr run straight through. While a game with some heavy themes, they are integrated really well, and the dating feels rather real too. Boyfriend Dungeon provides the autonomy that I really desire from games with dating mechanics. Here, you get to set your boundaries with the romance interests, so that if you want to just be friends, they understand that and respect that. Sure, they may question if one day you'd entertain the idea of being something more, but overall they respect your choice that maybe you don't want to bone every single weapon at the exact same time (although that's totally game as well). It's really nice that you can remain just friends with a weapon while still getting to know them, still seeing their stories, and not getting punished because "this secret is only revealed to romantic partners". Moving on to the combat-it's super fun. The different weapon styles match the various personalities and weapons you're fighting with, and it's a great mechanic to unlock more weapon skills as your relationship levels up with that particular weapon. The dungeons are fun to go through and your strength increases at a good rate so that you never feel like you really need to grind. Overall, seriously. An amazing game. The only real downside is the overarching theme of being stalked during the story (which is included as a warning prior to starting the game). So if you that's too much for you, then maybe be cautious. But other than that, 11/10 game, the only game on Steam that I've felt passionate enough to actually write a review for.

_childDocuments_.review: GAMEPLAYBFD is a dating simulator with a unique twist that takes you on a summer journey of love, laughter, and self-discovery. Instead of dating humans, you'll find yourself swept off your feet by a cast of charming swords, each with their own distinct personalities, backstories, and emotional baggage. As you progress through the game, you'll embark on romantic dates, engage in witty banter, and uncover the hidden depths of each sword's soul. The game's branching dialogue system allows for multiple playthroughs, ensuring that each interaction feels fresh and meaningful.ART STYLE:BFD's art style brings the world of swords to life. Each sword is meticulously designed with intricate details and vibrant colors, showcasing their unique characteristics and personalities. From the elegant curves of the talwar to the rugged edges of the katana, every blade is a work of art. The backgrounds are equally stunning, immersing you in lush landscapes, cozy cafes, and visually pleasing dungeons. The game's overall aesthetic is a testament to the developers' passion and creativity, creating a truly immersive experience.CHARACTERS:The characters in BFD are the HEART of the game - pun intended. Each sword is fully fleshed out with a rich backstory, motivations, and desires. You'll meet the charismatic, shy, mischievous, and even downright sultry blades testing your resolve and your will to not "catch them all". As you get to know each sword, you'll discover their vulnerabilities, dreams, and personal struggles. The writing is refreshing, delivering witty dialogue, heartfelt confessions, and moments of genuine emotional depth. You'll find yourself genuinely caring about each sword's well-being, even the side characters push to warrant your attention in the midst of your decision-making.REPLAYABILITY:BFD has a mild replayability factor as it depends on how you progress through the story. I am a goal-oriented person so I tasked myself with reaching each goal and gaining every achievement before realizing I needed to complete the MAIN STORY. So if you want to choose one character, go through the story, and complete the game; you can! I proceeded to "catch them all" before returning to the MAIN focus... Slight spoiler as yes, you can, very well indeed, catch them all... I will leave that up to interpretation~ :3 TLDR - Worth the Buy?!:Yes! BUY IT!!! BFD is a heartfelt and unique dating simulator that stands out from the crowd. From the BOPPIN' music to the DELICIOUS characters and then the GORGEOUS art - It's a no brainer~ Whether you're basking in the warm glow of summer or seeking a romantic escape, BFD will transport you to a world where love knows no bounds and swords are the key to your destiny. Game has potential so I'll keep an eye on this one~

_childDocuments_.review: I struggled on whether I should put yes or no. I want to say that I was excited for the game. I followed the developers on tiktok and have been hyped for its release. But the best way I could describe this game is "almost enough." My time logged is the amount of time that it took me to 100% the game, all achievements, all character routes. -The art is beautiful, and while the moments of animation are short and far between, they really do add a lot to the game.-The characters are quite diverse, and the inclusion of nonbinary characters as someone who is nonbinary myself is quite refreshing. I appreciated that you could date anyone freely. I know LGBT friendly dating games are becoming more frequent, but I'm still happy for every inclusion there is.-You can be fully polyamorous with no consequence. Which means if you want to be like me and delay the end story point until you kiss all the characters, you can! Which is very very nice.-Your cousin Jesse. I love him. I love him so much.-The freedom you're given. Outside of tutorial segment, you're free to explore the dunj at your own pace. You could focus all your time on one weapon, or split it evenly amongst weapons. There's no real rush to finish the game, regardless of when in the summer the text messages say it is, so you can go at your leisure and really ensure that you see everything.-The length. There are only 2 dunj's in the entire game. Honestly I was expecting a lot more. My personal experience was having my birthday party, being told its the middle of summer, then immediately being told after one more dunj trip that my time was almost up.-Your choices don't matter. Now there is branching dialogue options a little bit, but 90% of options as far as I could tell lead to a few lines different of dialogue. Even if you choose an option a character really likes while on a date with them, it doesn't give any additional affection or change the ending at all. Which plays into my next point.-The surface level writing. There is a lot of diversity, yes, but the problem with the amount of characters is that if you were really only here for one, I feel like you'd be quite disappointed. Each story is very predictable, and it feels like you're going through a checklist of basic date ideas or story points with each character instead of delving deep into their psyches. Which for a game that has one of the main points being "overcoming your fears" really surprised me.-The simplicity of the gameplay. It was hard to tell if this was a real con or not, because I don't really mind easier games, but overall it was just a bit meh. It felt very barebones. I appreciated the different play styles with the different weapons, but this game felt like an emptier Hades, gameplay wise.-The way you unlock Rowan. This is more of a personal gripe. I believed I would encounter them like every other weapon through the dunjs, only to discover that I was supposed to run North past my vision at the beginning of the game. A lot of my playtime was just grinding their affection to catch up. A dialogue queue mentioning the mansion to the north would've been nice.-THE STUPID BUG RACING GAME. It took me an hour to finish it. Which doesn't sound like a lot, but it was only 3 races. F*ck those bugs.-Your inability to say 'no' to romance. You can deny the sex scenes in the game (their very PG anyway, so you're not missing out on much), and insist on friendship. Yet despite that, the characters still continue to regard you in a romantic way most of the time. The biggest example of this particular gripe is Sunder. I'll explain in detail below.Spoiler warning from here on out but these are massive cons to the game.Overall I'd say this game is almost enough. It should've been expanded more, given more time to breathe or had more people working on it. I imagine with the kickstarter and tiktok fame though, the devs probably only had so long they could work on it. That leaves the game feeling very shiny and polished, but overall hollow. Like empty calories. They're sweet, and I enjoy them, but it doesn't take me long to get through it and doesn't leave me feeling full for long, if at all. If the devs ever come out with expansions tot the game, such as additional dunj's or weapons, I'll certainly check it out, but outside of that, I don't feel any desire to replay it. If you believe that you'd enjoy this game, I say still go for it. Just be ready for a very short experience, and one that's very bare bones. I think with more time and experience under their belts, the devs can do a lot more, and I'd still be happy to watch their projects in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderfully enjoyable queer game made by queer developers. It's a fun concept, the gameplay is satisfying and doesn't overstay its welcome, and the story wraps itself up about the time I'm ready to leave. I'm so happy to see a game like this not only being made, but being made to such success. A few years ago, something like this would be unheard of.This is a game made by people who understand what it's like to be queer in the modern day, it radiates the energy in every facet and it really gets it. The characters are genuinely lovable, the chemistry ranges from being spicy to adorable, it's just an across the board great experience. I love that you can pursue multiple routes at the same time to no real ill effect.I'm excited to see that they'll be adding more routes too. I was a huge fan of each one presented, especially Sawyer and Rowan. As someone who is nonbinary myself, seeing two characters like me, and such wonderfully caring depictions warmed my heart. Sawyer is such an adorable and fun character, I loved every moment I got to spend with them and my only complaint is that I didn't get to hang out with that adorable little disaster for longer.I think this is a game that can help a lot of people become more comfortable and confident in their identity simply by seeing characters who remind them of themselves. Characters they can see themselves in. As someone who had only really recently come out, being able to see myself in people like Sawyer and Rowan was truly comforting. Characters who not just happen to be like me, but get my whole vibe. I'd also like to take a moment to talk about how well realized the male characters are as well! I was recently having a conversation with a friend of mine who likes to DM tabletop games, and a topic that came up was that he understands how to make a likable and attractive female character, which is not to say 'aesthetically pleasing' attractive, but in that he, as a largely straight man, understands the aspects he finds attractive in femme-presenting characters. With that conversation fresh in my mind going into this game, I was able to really appreciate just how much this game understands what people who are into men and masculine-spectrum people are into, what they find attractive about those kinds of people, down to personality quirks and the ways they show affection. Every character, from the men, the woman, and the nonbinary folk, are written by people who clearly understand what aspects make those kinds of characters particularly attractive. Again, not only in that they're handsome, pretty or whatnot, but in the unique ways people of those gender identities are attractive.In summation, this is a wonderful little game that I highly recommend to anyone looking for a fun spin on the roguelike and dating sim genres, especially people looking for LGBTQ+ games made by LGBTQ+ creators.

_childDocuments_.review: Queer players! Dating Sims fans! Hear ye, hear ye! Your search is over! I will go off and rant about this absolute gem for WAYYYY too long  but the TL;DR is: FUN! FUNNY! SWEET! ADORABLE! BUY ITTT.This game honestly taught me a valuable lesson in that you can find connection, warmth, kindness and depth even in the silliest of places. And here you can find it all while fighting a flip-phone in a shopping mall wielding your casual vampire situationship or your emotional support idol tsundere husband! The first obvious merit of the game is the game play loop. Being half dungeon crawler, half dating sim, the two halves complement and feed each other in really refreshing ways. The dating elements help vent out and air out the frustration of the dungeon crawling part of the game, while the smooth sword swinging (not that kind) mechanics help break a little of the monotony of only reading through pages of text. That way, the around 15 hours you take to beat it are barely felt at all! It's cutting edge, really (badum tss)And if they’d stop here, they’d have a fun engaging game. But then they had the gall to care! And now look at where we are! The first choice you make in the game is whether or not you want to enable a “Mom” character to send you supportive texts. Right then and there, 5min in, this game showed more care for the comfort of their players than anything I’ve ever played. Not only for making adorable mom texts a main feature, but even allowing us to choose our own relationship with something that is so often taken for granted as a good thing. It allowed me to have my own relationship with a thing, and respected my choice with no question. It's like... What if a game suddenly cares about your boundaries?! And this philosophy follows you all through the game!?You get to customize your pronouns and change them at will, your relationship with food, with gender, with relationships, with sex, with intimacy and have them so effortlessly respected that it felt... refreshing. You can even choose the drinks you like! When the game has this agency and comfort taken from you through the plot it hurts, and players should be mindful of the Trigger Warnings before playing because it does have a recurring character overstepping your boundaries. But even that to me feels in theme with themes of love, the softest and sharpest sides of it. I honestly couldn’t believe this level of thought was first displayed in the video-game world in a game about kissing sword-turning people! It sounds like a joke! All the love interests in this game feel unique, both for the dating sim and dungeon crawling portions. Each date felt nice, even the LI I cared the least about made me chuckle and smile to myself at some moments, and the ones I cared for have broken and mended my heart in ways that will always be treasured. In a game about, yes, kissing swords. How dare the developers make me embarass myself by talking to my friends about how a vampire sword broke my heart?The soundtrack is amazing, the art is absolutely adorable, the writing is hilarious, and the overall message of the game is the absolute sweetest. But my favorite thing about it is that it exists, unceremoniously, and it will deliver either a fun time or just the gentlest embrace that only a thing made with the utmost care can give someone. In my case, both! I’ll be on the lookout for more things like this on the making, and I hope you (the reader of this way too long review) can find the comfort i found ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ kissing swords in some game, any one! And maybe this one is it for you too! Take a stab at it!

_childDocuments_.review: I originally backed this game on Kickstarter, but waited to play it until the DLC was available so that I wouldn't have to remember to go back to it later.  I'm glad that I waited; I think that the DLC adds important content to the game, and getting a year's worth of bug fixes along the way was also nice.  Overall, I enjoyed the game very much. I think without the DLC it would have felt a little on the short side; I was able to get the maximum romantic level with all the weapons (including the three in the DLC), 100% all the collectibles, and get my PC to a level where the final boss fight was trivial, all in 17 hours; that would have been 11-12 hours without the DLC, as the newly-added "dunj", boss fight, dates, and "walking around town" character events add plenty of depth. The combat is, I would say, more comparable to Bastion than to Hades, but there's plenty of variety in how the weapons play.  I might have liked one more full-length dungeon, but then again, I don't think I needed another 15 hours of this combat, either, and what's provided is enough to max out all the characters' abilities and play through all the storylines, so I think the length is sufficient without overstaying its welcome.Really the only downer was finding out after I'd finished that there were videos for the character transformations that I wasn't seeing because I played on the Steam Deck, but YouTube mostly helped me out there. I'm not sure why those don't play on the Deck.  I did experience a couple of hangs, but nothing that couldn't be overcome by restarting the game, and I didn't lose any meaningful amount of progress when that happened. Overall I found the game quite playable on the Steam Deck, and although I didn't try playing the mouse/keyboard version, it's the sort of game that I think wants to be played with a controller.All in all, great job!  Whoever wrote Pocket definitely has had a deep and abiding relationship with a cat, which is something I can appreciate.  :)  I loved the art, the characters were all interesting, and the ones that either weren't my type or that I wasn't comfortable romancing were all cool with platonic options without taking away the ability to unlock all of their weapon abilities; indeed, a primary reason the villain is the villain is because that character doesn't understand the concept of consent or boundaries.  I know there was some controversy over the story but I can't speak to it.  I thought it was obvious very early on who the villain was going to be and why, and that's how it played out.  I am sure that people who have been through toxic relationships of the sort depicted here could find that part of the storyline triggering, but I don't have the personal experience to say any more than that.  The game has been out long enough and enough has been written about it that I think you could determine whether it would be right for you before buying it.Finally, the soundtrack is great.  I'm listening to it right now!

_childDocuments_.review: Not the most detailed dialogue routes, but the mechanics and overall story are funny and cute. I still found myself genuinely invested in my favorite characters and genuinely annoyed at the ones I didn't take to, so I have to applaud the writers' ability. Not a fan of the final scenario/ultimate ending, but the rest of the game is a surprisingly solid play. I genuinely enjoyed the whole thing and actually laughed out loud a few different times.  It's also really thoughtfully designed in terms of warning you about potential triggers and asking your permission before engaging you in certain game elements, which I frankly really appreciated even though I'm not the target audience.Spoilers Below the Cut:------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------I wish the polyamory aspect was more fleshed out, you have the option to see multiple people and can tell "mom" that you aren't monogamous, but you never really get dialogue to officially tell your partners about eachother and they don't interact on dates. Hopefully an expansion down the line will offer a more concretely poly play style.I also wish they'd been a bit more subtle about Sunder's vampirism. Your first exposure to it, you catch him feeding on someone with exposed monster-eyes and fangs, though it's played off as a casual sex encounter. Then he has to be formally invited into your apartment every time he visits. Then he accidentally mentions being immortal a few times. Then someone references a dead body as a "messy meal" of his. Then, after all of that, they act like his vampirism is a HUGE SECRET that he's revealing and your character's responses are limited to one of two forms of surprise. It just felt like being bashed over the head and a bit clunky. It was still an interesting story element, I just think the dialogue around it could have benefited from a lighter hand.Sunder is also clearly and openly pursuing you casually, but they don't really give your character the option to express that their interest is purely casual too. The endings for him are all considered "bad" and act like he's breaking your heart, which is a little frustrating when he's very obviously the "fun ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ who isn't serious" route.Valerie I thought was handled very well, her dialogue involves slowly opening up to you and trusting you with more emotional intimacy over time as she's been burned before. As a bi/pan person, I would have liked for her to not be the only romanceable woman, but I understand the devs are a small team and the other romanceable female character had to be pushed back to an expansion down the road due to time constraints.I don't have any major critiques for the other routes, they were all fun stories and the weapons had enough concrete difference in-dunj for it to be worthwhile to master the different playstyles. Others have also mentioned this, but I genuinely dislike having to interact with Eric to advance the storyline (devs are apparently already working on a patch that allows you to ghost him, but as of my December playthrough you still had to talk to him or the game wouldn't advance in certain stages) and was disappointed that I didn't have the option to redeem Katana instead. Last, I know your character is supposed to be socially inexperienced and an introvert, but I found myself frustrated that a lot of the dialogue involved choosing between two nearly identical nonanswers rather than more decisive language. There are times when your options are between things like "sure." versus "okay.", or "Thumbs up emoji" versus "okay". With all that said, I genuinely enjoyed the game and I sincerely hope the studio makes additional expansions and/or additional full games in the franchise, the art was cute, the soundtrack was great and the whole play experience was enjoyable.

_childDocuments_.review: WARNING: Some vague storyline spoilers.I followed this game from its kickstarter days, reading the dev blogs and first person character emails. The game combines my love of RPG hack and slash with my love of visual novel romance, but in its present state is unable to satisfy my hunger for either.Tl:dr – The game is unsatisfying and shallow in most criteria, failing to fulfil either a desire for a good and varied RPG experience, or an engaging, intelligent (see adult level complexity), immersive, romantic graphic novel experience.Overview:Considering the amount of time the game was in development, and Kitfox's refusal to announce an actual release date, stating only it would be released when the 'weapons [were] beautiful enough', I wanted to believe the story side would be meaty enough to offset the largely repetitive combat. Unfortunately, the end result is very shallow, and it's a shame because people-weapons being wielded by dungeon crawlers is a neat and unique concept. I may go back again and try to master all the weapons just out of sheer OCD, but given the unsatisfying ending to my first mastery and that the game cuts you off once you finish the final mission (rather than allowing you to continue crawling and develop relationships with the other weapons), I really don't fancy starting from scratch.Aesthetic:I like the art style of the characters in their cut-scenes, but the top-down style for movement and combat is a bit cutesy for my tastes. I suppose given very vague sexual descriptions at various points in the game I might have expected a little more maturity in the graphics, but then again the descriptions are VERY vague in a fade to black way. The music fits very well, but is quite repetitive and not really my genre.The voice acting is actually pretty natural and fitting for each character, but engagement could have been improved VASTLY by voicing all narrative dialogue.Combat and Movement:Left button. Right button. F to heal. Q to special ability. Space to dodge. That’s it. While the game does include combinations, and levelling up your relationship with a weapon unlocks new effects, you’ll be madly clicking your mouse buttons over and over again with little strategy required. If you’re looking for a challenge, you will not find it here at all – the ‘dunj’ crawling really is a mini-game to the relationship stories, levelling them up to max in order to unlock the next dating scenario.Storylines:I completed Sunder’s storyline well before the final overall game mission was available, and that left me pretty pissed off. It was a full stop to all development with that character, who I could still use in dungeons, but could take no further in a relationship sense; and the ending had me groaning a long fuuu$%uck oooooff and sneering “NOT a better story than Twilight”.  As an author myself, I recognise there is so much potential, but I suddenly found myself involuntarily taking the ice-bucket challenge.I got most of the way through Isaac, Seven and Valeria, and all but Seven had a curtain-fluttering, chime-tinkling, off-screen sleep over, but none of their stories were especially inspired.Sawyer is a nice addition as far as non-binary inclusion is concerned, but looks like a child, so ew, no, no romancing there.I did not unlock Rowan or Vitas Varnas.For the amount of potential the concept has, the world’s context and the world in general is sparse, and feels like, ultimately, they decided to release the game with super short, flaccid stories on a stage dressed with cardboard cut-out scenery. Tastes a bit like cardboard too.Adult Content and Questionables:OMG they said sex! Mwah mwah kisses happen! That’s about it. Nothing truly risqué happens. Honestly, the only thing that made me feel a teensy bit uncomfortable, was some none-to-subtle racism (in this case weaponism?) from one of the characters, who funnily enough, turns out to be the same type of hypocrite as those religious evangelists spewing homophobic hate out one side of their mouth while sucking a c0ck with the other.Conclusion:This game is rated D for disappointment, and I get the distinct impression, D for future DLC which I will not invest in without more confidence in Kitfox’s ability to deliver stories that rise beyond cliché.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm recommending it with caveats:  (Edited to add detail)This game is a bit like Hades, and a bit like a dating sim, with a little bit of crafting thrown in. It's all fine. It's not great, but it's fine.  Ultimately, it struggles with being shallow versions of better games. However, the mechanics are fun, and satisfying, if simple. However, the game is hugely problematic in the narrative. It presents as progressive, and in some cases, it is, but it also has major problems. Some of them:1) You start the game of with your cousin tells you that he's worried about you because you don't date.  Clearly you can't be happy unless you are dating someone. That's a problem. The cousin then sets you up on dates that you don't necessarily want -- basically forcing you into it "for your own good".  So... that's a major red flag.2) Pretty much everyone that you meet have major red flags. The most egregious is the stalker, but they are all problems in some way.  I believe you are supposed to help them, but I only played through a couple of stories. So either you should ignore red flags or try to fix people. Either of those messages are terrible.  As an example: one of the first characters you meet has their business partner mention that he has a history of violence and you should be wary.  This isn't something that you should teach people to ignore.  Another of the characters appears to be underage. I'm not sure if they are, but that I even thought that they were, based on appearance and how they act -- that's a big NOPE. 3) Near the end, you fight to overcome your fear of intimacy, where you are accused of being asexual like it's a bad thing. So, much as this game is progressive on gender fluidity, it's not great with asexual being a viable lifestyle choice.The cat, on the other hand... just be friends with the cat. The cat is awesome.

_childDocuments_.review: As a bisexual woman I really appreciate having a game with such a diverse romantic cast like this game so thanks so much devs! The game is a ton of fun and it was great being able to date so many interesting and diverse characters along with playing through the dungeons. The game was challenging while not being too hard and it was fun getting to try out the different weapons and see their stories. The main complaint is that the game is too short for my taste, but with the new DLC coming out it feels like the game has a lot more to give and I'm all for it. What I really appreciate more than anything was also how the relationships were portrayed realistically and even allowing you to call out toxic/unhealthy behavior and how realistic some relationships felt as a result. I feel like too many games romanticize toxic behavior/relationships so this was massively refreshing!

_childDocuments_.review: An interesting concept with charming characters and designs to match, but after beating the game and playing two more times to see if my choices have any impact to the story, it falls short.For it being a dating simulator, the stories for each individual romantic interest are linear.  What I mean by this is that no matter what choices you make in interacting with them, their story doesn’t change.  You can reject a character’s advances and they will still try to make moves on you.  This is not to talk ill of any of them as they each have their own unique charms that compels me to know more about them, but if I want to stay friends with someone or give consent to pursue them romantically, I’d like to explore those different outcomes.I come into this game wondering if I, as the player, can dive into a story and change the world around me with the choices I’ve made while also creating deeper bonds with the people I come across on the way.  I didn’t get any of that.  The ending was shallow and lackluster.  My relationships with the characters left me rather bitter and emotionally scarred (looking at Sunder who's the poster boy for the game's promotional material btw), and on top of this, it feels like me as the protagonist did not experience any actual growth.  It was like I was put in a movie and forced to ride it through without any means to change its course.  The game warned about elements of stalking and emotional manipulation.  These are integral parts of the story, they're triggering topics and I’m glad to see it.  But I wasn’t emotionally prepared to see the level of those elements into play, it left me scarred and uncomfortable that’s for certain.  I see the direction they were going and it’s a good concept, but the delivery hits home and not at all in a good way.Perhaps if the game receives future content that adds more depth and writing to the story (perhaps even fix some of the romance’s personal storylines to cater to player needs and satisfaction such as branching plots in choices), then I’d be all for it.  If you’re looking for a casual hook-up game with mindless dungeon crawling elements, go for it.  However if you’re looking to make meaningful connections with some hotties and explore a deep, rich story to boot, as it is right now, I cannot in good conscience recommend the game to anyone.

_childDocuments_.review: A mostly pretty good dating/dungeon crawler.I find it hard to recommend though since this is a very niche since you need to have like dating sim sort of games, dungeon cralwers and isometric hack and slash style combat. Which I have at least some interest in the first two, but isometric combat is kind of annoying, perspective making it hard to hit targets; especially with the Estoc weapon which is a thrust attack and your going to miss a lot at first. But the real problem with the combat is it doesn't really know how to make combat harder other then to just spawn more enemies. Which kind of sucks and I just ended up spamming Area of Effect attacks since I was constantly surrounded.Also the spell books are kind of useless. Like I get what the intention was, but most of the spells are meh at best and are out done by the weapons with AoE attacks. Also there is two hats that double damage and that just breaks the games tactics down to "melt the enemy before they can even attack"The love interests are... mostly fine. I did get through all the romance paths except for one, which was Sunder the guy on all the promotional stuff. But these aren't really characters I'd gush over how much I love. Also it feels weird, normally dating games tend to go through a number of archetypes that appeal very broadly but boyfriend dungeon kinda doesn't, which is kind of refreshing but also gives a sense of more limited options. Let that colour your opinion as you will, just something weird I noticed. Also it feels like they ran out of ideas since one of the "boyfriend weapons" is just a cat.Overall pretty good. If the concept sounds interesting then I'd say it will hold your attention, it is rather short. I wasn't really rushing and it took me less then 8 hours.

_childDocuments_.review: Right off the bat, I wish this game was longer, had more to it in main-story-plot and in relationships; The game isn't cut short in a negative way by any means, I just enjoyed it so much that I wanted more!!!The characters are all interesting and distinct, regardless of whether I actually liked them or not. The dungeon crawling portions of the game are actually really fun and the fighting mechanics are super smooth - there wasn't a moment where I was unhappy about either having to grind or choosing to focus on the story. This is a really well balanced game where nothing ever felt like a chore.The only thing I can comment on is that the shops in game seem rather useless - I went maybe twice when, in all honesty, I didn't really have to - I'm just obsessive about crafting items the moment I get blueprints in games. Honestly, you could play the entire game without using a shop for anything more than aesthetics (clothes); Even the gifts that are sold in the shops aren't necessary if you focus on crafting (actually, the gifts are just a bonus, not even required at all for progress). Honestly though, the lack of necessity for shops isn't a bad thing, it's just something I noticed. Overall, this was a really fun game, and I'll definitely be putting more time into it to play through all the possible story lines. :)

_childDocuments_.review: There is so much to love about this game, especially if you're LGBT+As far as the combat goes, it does a great job of giving each weapon their own intuitive fighting style that seems to really fit each individual's personality. I'd go into detail, but I don't want to spoil.As for the dating sim aspects of the game, there are men, women, and non-binary people to romance, which means there's something for everyone and it's great if you're pan. You can change your appearance and your pronouns anytime at your apartment, which makes it fun to play with your avatar a bit, and the pronoun flexibility is great if you're questioning or gender fluid. You can seemingly date everyone, simultaneously, and no one seems bothered by it which feels so great if you're poly, and you don't have to pursue any of these relationships from a romantic or sexual angle if you don't want to. You can just form a close platonic relationship with any or all of them, which is great for aro and/or ace folks.Love this game. 10/10 will play again.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted this game to be a lot better because of the controversy around it. Things that I personally experienced that I'm not nuts about:- the combat system isn't particularly robust- choices in your relationships don't really seem to matter- you can't choose how the M/C feels about people so it feels a little restrictedThings I researched before deciding whether or not to stop playing but have not seen for myself.- The game is apparently not complete. I would rather pay more for a complete game later. I'm personally not a fan of the installments model in games. Other people might not mind this though.- Choices continue to not matter.- I'm not nuts about the two nonbinary character designs as a nonbinary person. There's not a lot of representation for us in games like this. There's nothing wrong with people (esp other nonbinary people) liking the characters but nonbinary people tend to get perceived as either soft boi trans man lite or spooky witch enthusiasm trans woman lite a lot by cis people. I think if there were either more nonbinary and trans characters in the game it wouldn't feel so bad, but it just feels kind of weird for me.- I think regarding the above point and also some reflecting I was doing on Seven's plot, I feel like the game is marketed as and tries to present itself as socially aware (the economist is interested in addressing inequality, a character who believes in a system that's a metaphor for racial purity is a villain, LGBTQ options etc), but it gets complicated when marketing these characters in game and out of game has to do with desirability. These characters being diverse is in someways a commodity to sell a product and I was expecting some commentary on that in game (especially with how NPCs treat Seven and the way white people interact with K-POP as a commodity), but felt like that ultimately didn't pull through. I was hoping that maybe the writing on a character like Sawyer would be teaching people not to fetishize nonbinary people as certain tropes, but what from I've researched it doesn't turn out that way.In case the devs bother to read this I'm going to say some nice things as well because there's clearly a lot of love in this project and I don't want to trash it.- I appreciate that the game has an ambitious concept for people who are not accustomed to this genre to maybe play more (I've played a decent amount of VNs in my life).- the art and stylization looks great- Jesse being bisexual slaps- I want to date Noah so badly but I'm afraid of him being unemployed or fat being treated as a joke, and if he wants to resist capitalism and find his purpose through surfing and being kind to animals ♥♥♥♥ yes.- side note: frankly I don't need my dating sims to be progressive. I play a lot of ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up and weird games. But if that's your goal you have to fully commit to it.- back to compliments!! the break stops in certain levels that heal were a great mechanic and helped game play a lot- the idea of combos is good, they're just a little too unchunkable memory wise to be practical rn! Great concept to mix up combat though.- the monster design was very good and I enjoyed them- the rest spots in the dungeon all slapped

_childDocuments_.review: First and foremost, I recommend this game if it's on sale. At it's current stage, I do not believe it's worth the full retail price. I beat this game at almost 11 hours and about half of my hours in the game were being idle.However, I do think it's a great game that has a lot of potential. First, the soundtrack is absolutely amazing. The songs would constantly get stuck in my head when I wasn't playing and I loved it. I also like the dungeon part a lot. I'm usually not for roguelike button mashing games, but I loved this and how each weapon had a different feel of a play style while you were travelling deeper in the depths of the dungeons. The dating part of the game...feels kind of meh right now. There's a few characters when you get farther down the ranking path with them you just start to feel annoyed with and you're choices don't feel unique. I just wish there was more impact choices or situations when it comes to that part of the game or get a more unique ending with them. And then of course, my biggest gripe right now is how short the game is currently. 2 dungeons and then a final boss. I overpowered myself by going through a dungeon to it's completion before heading to the final boss and it needed a requirement of at least 1 rank 6 weapon and. Well. After that it was very easy to beat the final boss.I don't know if more content will be released, but I am crossing my fingers for that as I think a lot more updates could help this game out to just feel more complete.

_childDocuments_.review: I did enjoy the game despite my problems with it. My main problem with the game is the Protagonist is a major jerk, from the first meeting with Eric your Protagonist seems to dislike him for some reason and just *will not* treat him with civility, courtesy or kindness... My next problem is that the game is far too short, and my last problem is that Eric is not a romance T_T. /RANTI decided to check this game out after the "controversy" and I discovered that I had absolutely no problem with it that people were "all in uproar" about lol XD. Maybe because I thought Eric was treated entirely unfairly from the very beginning of the game by our Protagonist. I don't think Eric is a stalker like the game is trying to write him as, his advances were never unwanted for me. I was only upset that not once in the game could I ever just have a friendly conversation with him, the writers are dead set on making our Protagonist hate him. WHY?! Why do you want us to hate him writers?! I felt like I was resigned to romance the shirtless wonder instead of romancing Eric. /RANTAnyway, I read that the dev team is planning on additional content for this game, so I want to recommend it so you can support the game and the team for that content <3 ^^. If you want to love Eric like I do, watch the BBC Pride and Prejudice and imagine having a conversation with him cause the game won't let you have any civil conversation with him... EDIT: Also Sense and Sensibility, Downtown Abbey, Frankenstein or Psycho Pass(you'll see a properly villainous character in Psycho Pass.)EDIT: Eric is not completely hopeless that everyone is hating on him about. If you've played Dragon Quest XI then you know of a character called, Vince Vanquish who abducts challengers and gives them to Arachtagon; before the Hero arrives on the scene, Vince won the tournament, so for a full year he abducted and let people *die* due to his actions. What Eric does is similar to Vince, I don't understand why the dev team and Boyfriend Dungeon are so keen on hating on the poor man.  Also dev team, please make him a romance. It is not impossible to keep everything exactly as it is in your story *and* have an Eric romance. For one thing, if your protagonist shows him kindness and a keen interest in Eric, then he will be pleased but feel extremely guilty and probably want to break off the relationship. At the end of the game when everything comes to light, you should be given the choice to accept Eric for every one of his faults, or stay with one of the other romances. I think that would be the best story for him <3. EDIT: Changing my review to "Not Recommended" because the dev team looks like they have no interest in adjusting their writing to make the Protagonist not be a total C-word and to treat Eric with civility, courtesy and kindness. If the dev team surprises me with an update to their writing in regards to Eric, then I will recommend it again. The story has strengths, but the writing team is much too heavy handed in forcing young people to *hate* Eric. The poor guy doesn't deserve the reception he gets. Eric needs our love <3.

_childDocuments_.review: I had a blast playing through this game and will likely play the entire story again at some point. The characters are interesting and the dating sim part is very fun, but simple. The majority of the story takes place through those "Dates" and one can always choose not to pursue a character further by simply not going on further dates with them. Unfortunately though all the "dating paths" are pretty linear with only slight variations here and there and only minor impacts on other "dating paths". The dungeon crawls are fun with each weapon feeling quite different and unique. The monsters are interesting but lack a bit variety with each dungeon coming with a handful of monsters, that then have a stronger  variant to them and one boss. Its also interesting to play around with different "spells" and strategies, though I found myself trying to maximize love with as many weapons as possible per run. Within the different Levels you sometimes find a place to interact with your equipped weapon - which is nice and flavorful, whit each weapon reacting differently to each possible place.One thing both the dungeons and dates have in common, is that there is not a lot of them. There are 2 dungeons that are really fun and each weapon has 6 Levels you can reach, which translates to 7 dates including the date in which you first meet them. There are a few events in between - but while being crafted beautifully, they do not add a whole lotta game to play. This might change a bit in future and mod support is in its way - but those are might and maybe. Overall I finished the main story and maxed all love ranks in about 8 hours, without too much grinding or time optimized gameplay - which left me wanting more, though I think replaying this game will be fun.Overall I can really recommend the game and think the price tag is good for this somewhat smalller unique fusion blend of genres.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a bullet hell game with little in the way of gameplay customisation, propped up by a barebones dating sim with a lack of actual varied dialogue choices, ranging from enthusiasm to teenage ennui and indifference. Dating is the usual pastiche of tired conversation options, affinity raising and wanton bribery.The gameplay is passable if basic, the content is so intrinsically Californian that I feel that the game is two steps short of asking consent before dealing damage to you. The character creation is possibly a hidden social commentary on how despite all the options available to you and your identity, none of them actually have any practical value. Certainly subversive, but it can't carry the plot by itself.I was hoping the content would at least be humorous, tongue-in-cheek and witty the way Monster Prom is, but this game currently reads more like a hormonal angst-fest with little in the way of plot (it has opt-in content warnings for people who are triggered by interactions with their mother, for goodness' sake). Perhaps that isn't entirely a bad thing, but I'm probably at an age where I find it a trifle tiresome. Did not live up to my expectations of something more in the vein of Hatoful Boyfriend (the pigeon dating sim).

_childDocuments_.review: This is a quick game, a dating sim with a dungeon crawler mechanic rather than the other way around.I love that some of the boyfriend's are just ♥♥♥♥♥♥ people who behave poorly. I can't tell if it's poor writing or a similar intentional statement about how ♥♥♥♥♥♥ people can be, but some of the people you say "I just want us to be friends" with make moves on you repeatedly anyway, or even wake you up with kisses. The game tells you explicitly you can be strictly platonic with people, but some of them will repeatedly try to re-negotiate that. My list of "characters in this game who are not ♥♥♥♥" got smaller and smaller over timeWhich is good. If you give people what they want, of course they're nice to you. You only really see how nice someone is when you see them facing rejection or other anger. People who romanced some of the people I think are gross, probably think they're great bois. They didn't see how they were when you weren't interested.At the same time, that is a bit too much realism for some people. So the game might be for you.The dungeon crawling is fine, especially as the weapon styles branch out from progressing each relationship.It's worth a shot if you want to play a dating sim with more three-dimensional people than normal. It's just, you can't just pick who you want and fix them. They stay who they were, and sometimes that means you get bit. Which to me was neat and a good truth to reflect in a game. To others though, dating sims are escapist fantasies they want to go well, and this doesn't always go well for you.
