_childDocuments_.review: I've had this game on my wishlist for a while, so when I saw that it was dropped suddenly, I was ecstatic! The game was actually gifted to me from my partner because they know I'm very heavily into romance novels and they like dungeon crawlers, so having this on an account with Family Share is a win-win! Onto an actual review: COMBAT: It's really simplistic but not in a negative way. I'm garbage at most dungeon crawlers because I struggle with timing my hits and dodges correctly. This game is super merciful and allows for beginners to get a sense of the genre without feeling like they're too in over their heads, which I enjoy wholeheartedly, and the different weapon types allow for several alternate styles of gameplay as well. My favorite weapons to use were the brass knuckles, the scythe, the dagger, and the laser saber. Each weapon has different abilities and as you level up, you can change the build your weapon has to be either more tactical or more damage-oriented. I picked the more damage-oriented skills most of the time because I personally just think they're really neat. Also, giving some hats some bonuses to combat is fun! I like that some of them obviously go with craftable outfits but do not strictly have to be with those outfits. Using the fox hood with the leather jacket or the bucket hat with the cultist robes is extremely fun to me. The zines are also really creative and clever! My personal favorites to use were Spooky Zine and the bug one (can't remember the name, sorry!). STORYTELLING: I. Love. This. Story. I really do. The characters are all so well-written and there's a LOT of side twists within each individual character's storyline, which is super enjoyable, and some of the characters overlap in strange ways which is cool too! The usage of the text conversations to advance the story is clever and the responses are super witty. Every character has their personality shine through and it's incredibly refreshing to see enriching characters portrayed so wonderfully. The voice acting is nice as well! I'm also going to mention that there's a few spots in the story where there are some hints towards characters making a return, or the player character also making a return back to town, so I am hopeful that this game will eventually make some DLC for the holidays or something. The game doesn't lock you into dating anyone. You have complete freedom over who you choose to date or not to date, and that's really nice to see. It's a fresh perspective for a dating sim to have a lot of inclusivity like this one does. Part of me is also really endeared that the developers chose to make the player's character model as androgynous as possible, because that way the outfits just appear as clothes, and are not specifically gendered. The flavor text on the hats/outfits is wonderful, too! SIDE COMMENTS: Truly, this game is worth the purchase! I think the big baddie was pretty obvious from the start (though part of me thought it was going to be a side character that ended up being a one-off...) but I also enjoy the curves and twists the story takes as you romance or befriend people and try to get through the summer. Sad it's such a short season though!! Also, the soundtrack is absolutely bopping. The headphone and ear pod hats change the music and I am so in love with all of it. Rating: 10/10, please buy the game. please.

_childDocuments_.review: Finally, a game that let's me smooch a sword! As far as the dating/visual aspect novel goes, I'm really impressed with the variety of characters (weapons?). They all have unique personalities that seem pretty darn realistic as far as how people actually behave (one character uncomfortably reminds me of an ex-boyfriend and the game lets me be as snotty to him as he deserves). Definitely A+ for the dating sim parts.As for the dungeon diving? I like it too! I appreciate how character growth is tied both to the standard experience points (killing monsters), as well as the progress of relationships with weapons. Combat is simple (combos are made with just two buttons and there's two more buttons for healing items or attack items), but effective, and the scenery in the dungeon is visually interesting.And now, the art and music! The backgrounds outside of the dungeon for all the date spots are detailed and really well done. Character portraits are fantastic and some of the best I've seen in any game, let alone visual novel style games. What's particularly cool is that all the major characters get animated introductions similar to the Sailor Moon transformation. Some of the non-character cutscenes are animated, too, and all high quality! As for the music, soundtrack is poppy, upbeat, and entertaining. I've yet to encounter a piece of music that's obtrusive or annoying as a loop. It's the kind of music you'd put on in the background while studying or doing some sort of hobby craft.TL;DR: Smooch a sword in a dungeon to the sick beat of a pop jam.

_childDocuments_.review: I... want to like this game, but I don't. I really, really don't. It doesn't have any ability to refuse dates, or turn people down, or set boundaries and then have them respected. I say I don't like dancing? Too bad, I must dance. I say something isn't a date? Too bad, everyone but me agrees that getting coffee with that guy was a date. I think my cousin's quest to make me have a date right now is kind of dumb, I'd really rather just chill and go slay monsters in dungeons? Too. Bad.More than that, though, it genuinely made me uncomfortable in a way the warnings didn't prepare me for. At the start of the game there's a warning "This game may include references to unwanted advances, stalking, and other forms of emotional manipulation. Play with care." which sounds fine, but in actuality it is not 'references.' You, the player, acquire a stalker. He leaves a rose on your doorstep. He follows you when you go on dates to other people and comments on them through text message later. He keeps calling you pet names even though you ask him to please stop.Stalking is horrible, and consent is important, and I can tell that this game understands that. Clearly a lot of thought went into it, because the interactions ring true. But I really feel like if you're going to confront something that strikes so close to home for a lot of people, you need to both warn them in advance better, and always directly show the difference between 'Okay' and 'Not okay.' Because having my stalker presented as messed up while I am incapable of refusing dates, or refusing to dance, or whatever else confuses the entire experience. I just feel trapped in every single interaction I'm having. The game will ask me for my preferences, and then completely ignore them.And that's not the kind of game I want to play, and it's not the kind of game I'd recommend to anyone.

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting genre mix for a game. Never knew hack&slash could work with visual novel. Turned out really fun actually.Music is amazing and fits gameplay perfectly. So much so, that I literally got goosebumps sometimes. I also love how it changes depending on how much enemies is around.Gameplay is not too hard, can be relaxing actually.Love the whole style. Very cute, very chill.Story is simple and kind of absurd, but pretty fun. Ending was cool, a bit bittersweet, but fitting.Characters - mixed bag. I guess it just makes them for every taste. Eric can burn in hell, Valeria and Sawyer are annoying at times, Sunder is kind of a ♥♥♥, Seven and Isaac are for the win, Jonah and Rowan are pretty cute actually, Leah is just ok and Dr.Holmes are fun. But oh my god, Pocket. Pocket! My MVP. My bestie. My partner for life (his owner doesn't exist, be quiet). Figures, that in the romance (kinda) game, my favourite character is a cat. But what a cat he is. Perfect, everything about him is perfect. His design, his soundtrack, his "dates", his resting events at the dungeon. Also, for some reason I expected him to actually talk (like a human), I mean, it does look like that kind of a game. But I'm really glad he doesn't. And, oh lord, he's ending is 100% the best, stop arguing, I can't hear you and you are wrong anyway. For god's sake, no joke, the  part - I never felt more touched. Brought tears to my eyes, smile to my face and peace to my heart. He is just the best cat ever and I would die for him.I enjoyed this game a great deal.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr: It feels rushed.When you start the game, it instantly charms you. There's so much to do! The visuals are pleasing, and they added some quality partial voice acting, to spice things up.Unfortunately, you quickly run out of content to do, which is a sin for anything that attempts to call itself roguelike. The dating part doesn't fare much better.There's only 2 dungeons for you to clear, and I managed to finish the crafting part of the game before even finishing the second one. That makes further re-runs pretty much pointless, from resource gathering perspective.The only issue I've encountered in the first dungeon, is that it doesn't seem to know how to handle the player surviving part of the tutorial, where you're supposed to die. Second dungeon is more buggy than the first.Once you reach max love level with one of the weapons, you get x2 boost for any love points you get with others, literally allowing you to speedrun the rest of this fairly short game.The dating aspect is diminished in its charm by how Everyone Is Totally Into You. You don't have to do much, for the weapons to throw themselves at you.While the possibility to pursue a platonic relationship is mentioned in the beginning of the game, if you do not choose "I want us to stay friends" as soon as it is presented to you, the game will proceed with understanding that you want a sexual relationship, with no option to back out of it.Some of the platonic relationships can be awkward. I'm looking at you, Sunder.And since I mentioned Sunder, spoilers for how his story ends: As for the game's ending, it's so heavily charged with combat, you may want to run it again, just to see what you missed the first time, by focusing on not dying, or maybe take another weapon with you... and the game doesn't let you redo the ending. Despite allowing you to continue playing after the ending, to deal whatever it is you didn't finish.All in all, I expected more, back when I saw this game on Kickstarter.

_childDocuments_.review: I think this game is a solid game, especially for the price. You have a little gender neutral sprite type character, and you can choose your pronouns out of the three basic ones (she/he/they). All of the chars could be attracted to you, so no matter what gender you are, the options remain the same. In the menu, I discovered you can reduce the damage you take, so if the dungeon style intimidates you, know that you can make it easier on yourself. Try it out!Each of the characters are unique, and they each of good and bad qualities. The game gives you a warning at the beginning, because it does have stalker types, and if you are an estranged kid, you can opt out of texts from "Mom." The game deals with how parents can be ♥♥♥♥♥♥, so there is a clear acknowledgement that the character may have a decent parent, but not everyone does. The clothing choices, just to start, are minimal but offer two different types of head coverings, for those of various faiths. Some of the dialogue is acted out, and done fairly well. I almost wish all of it could be, but I don't mind that it isn't. Characters are well designed, and generally very attractive. I have yet to see a character who is not able bodied (or at least doesn't show it physically), and who is not, in some way attractive. I'm not that far into the game though!The game also deals with social anxiety very well. The main deal with your character is stepping out of their shell and dealing with their issues. I def feel called out  LOL. So if that is something you don't want your character to delve into...be warned.Overall I absolutely adore this game. I highly recommend it. Just know there is, as one would expect, some seriously sexually charged dialogue, references to trauma, and overall deep topics it delves into.

_childDocuments_.review: First, the positives. Very inclusive, (ace, aro, nb and poly friendly options and 2 enby love interests. Rarely ever see that kind of inclusion and ALL for it). The premise is interesting and the dungeon and bonding mechanics are hella fun. Loved the intro animations and the art looks good for the most part. Some of the faces seem a little off at times though. The crafting and outfits are all really well done. The game has lots of charm and I desperately wanted to love, but also has a lot of missed potential and things that can feel...lacking story content wise. I really hope devs consider adding more plot content for all the main love interest, but ESPECIALLY Sunder and Jonah.My main beef is with Sunder who's basically a cheese grater for your emotions in the worst way possible. In short and without spoiling the details, he's a bad end only character. Tried two different playthroughs with the same result and as far as I know, no other players have found a good ending for him. I'll add more with a spoiler warning further down.As an enby I was so happy with Rowan's character and that there was more than one enby romance option, even if Sawyer wasn't my type. Rowan was incredibly well done, but like the other love interests, their route felt too short. As an ace I was thrilled that sex was opitonal and not required for romance. On the other hand, many of the romances felt very rushed and like there should have been more to them so much so it almost felt like a hookup focused game over a date sim. To be frank there's a lot that felt rushed or cut short to the point I feel the game's release should have been postponed a few months. There's only two dungeons with less than 15 levels each and they go by pretty quick. Didn't feel like there was enough time to flesh out the story and worldbuilding either which is a shame because I wanted to know more about the weapon people. Spoilers for Sunder ahead.Now for Sunder. Hoo boy, the man single-handedly soured the whole game for me. Everything else, I was willing to overlook til this point. Having one of the main love interests in a date sim exist only to break your heart in the most callous way possible with no options to discuss or address it or get a good ending is a very poor design decision imo. Especially since he was one of the main reasons I bought the game. If I wanted to simulate having my heart broken and reliving an extremely painful experience (charming older guy toying with my feelings and stringing a younger, more inexperienced me along as a way to pass the time), I wouldn't...be playing a date sim. I felt extremely emotionally manipulated by Sunder only it was worse because he had spent so much time gaining my trust and trying to convince me he was worth giving a shot. I expected it from the antagonist, but again, NOT a main love interest in a date sim. Despite other characters warning you about him. I thought it was just the vampire thing keeping him from intimacy in the past, not...him not having his $h*t together as a human being. If he was aromantic and wanted a queer platonic relationship with your character, I would've been fine with that. If he was poly? Would've been fine with that too. If he was both and just wanted a platonic, but loving relationship with you while sleeping with other people, I might've been fine with that too. I just would have liked the option to discuss it openly with him and explore it as an option together.. Not be strung along, jerked around, then dumped with no real explanation or closure.As for Jonah. for the life of me I can't figure out how you're supposed to unlock his route. You meet him, he texts to say he won't be there the rest of the summer, but he feels you'll meet again real soon...except you don't. That's literally all I can say about Jonah which is too bad. All I can think is that maybe it was the devs way of hinting they'll release content for him soon?Jessie also became extremely annoying because you couldn't say no to the pointless awkward dates with non love interests. The first one I get since it's essential to the plot, but the rest was just like "LEAVE ME ALONE AND LET ME DATE MY WEAPONS JESSIE." Even Jonah, is kind of forced on you by Jessie as a third wheel if you invite one of your own date's to an event later. For a game that has the sensitivity to ask about whether it's okay to send you texts from a character called Mom (which I was incredibly grateful for as I don't have a great relationship with mine) and brings up the importance of consent at multiple points, it's kind of jarring when you realize you can't opt out of or say no to Jessie about any of the dates he sets you up on.Also gonna repeat what other's have stated about the content warning. It's not adequate as written. It makes it sound like you can opt out of the stalking and emotional manipulation or like their sort of in the background, but doesn't tell you it literally forces you to keep engaging with an incel, "nice guy" stalker type in order to progress the plot. I know it's a game and not real life, but I found it implausible that your character wouldn't just block this character's number. That said, the devs have announced they'll be updating the content warning to reflect this, so hopefully that's in place soon.I feel like this game's release date should've been pushed back a bit and that there should be a good ending for Sunder, literally any content for Jonah and at least 10 heart levels and dates with each love interest,I'm hoping devs release a future update or DLC with more story content as this game still has the potential to be incredible, but in it's current state, I can't quite bring myself to recommend it to others. The outifts are cute, but the game really doesn't need more of them and I would have been fine with half as many and no craftable racing game, if it meant more fleshed out romances or at least getting a positive end for Sunder. Currently you can date every character (save for Jonah) and nearly 100% this game in about 6 hours or so.

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked Dream Daddy, you'll most likely enjoy this game too.The dungeon part has a nice difficulty curve to it and never becomes frustratingly hard (minus one very rare enemy near the very end that hits like a truck), in part thanks to the generous amount of healing sources available and the quick leveling. The way you acquire most craftables can be a bit annoying since it requires a bit of grinding, as you find practically all the recipes in random chests. There's only one I never really got into, it doesn't bring me the same level of enjoyment as all the others.My only con: depending on some of the very early decisions you make in your playthrough, the main plot point of the story may get spoiled. _childDocuments_.review: Such a great premise! Wish there was a bigger fandom for it! Really adore the queer/inclusive range of characters and options for the player character. It's a queer friendly Canadian indie game. What more could I want? <3<3Do wish there was a bit more polish re: game mechanics and difficulty, but it doesn't diminish the game enough to be a game breaking issue. The combat could be way tighter and less clunky honestly, and the levels could be better laid out/stick to cleaner metrics for use of space/where the PC and enemies can and can't move through at the very least.Above all else though? I just really REALLY wish there was a hard mode!!! I mean, whaaaat??The present difficulty level makes the game SUPER short!! The whole thing seems balanced as if it wanted to shepherd players out of the game as fast as possible! 100% Achievements in like under 10 hours if your trying for it. But I WANT to spend more time with it! I wan't to replay, try combos, grind and get recipes or dialogue with my fave weapons! (Without having to start a whole new file, and dumping said file if I DO die in the middle of a dunj and level my way into the difficulty being way too low again literally from that one, MAYBE two runs. ='( )Fantastic setting/idea, fun characters, inclusive and caring company, needs better balance, and to feel able to take up more space/time?? Honestly it's like it lacked confidence in itself!

_childDocuments_.review: Creative, visually stellar, and left me wanting more.The game description is exactly as it sounds - you run some dungeons and you can date your weapons. Or most of them, at least. For a short game, it packs a story that keeps you engaged. You want to continue progressing in the narrative to reach that supposed satisfactory conclusion.Pros:- Great visuals and animations for the weapons.- Dungeons were fun and liked the concepts of the bosses.- Variety of dateable characters, or can keep thing platonic!- Crafting system was simple and felt rewarding, not a chore.- Music is banging! I'm still humming the songs weeks later.- Inclusion of multiple pronouns, ability to change your avatar how you see fit.- Developers are listening to peeps and made effort to update content warnings and address concerns.- Story was alright. Some tweaks could be addressed, but appreciate the devs pushing the narrative into areas rarely discussed.Cons:- It's a bit too short for how much you pay.- Replay options are limited. it's easy to get most of the achievements in the first play through, and you can date multiple weapons at once.- Only 2 dungeons! I had a lot of fun running the dungeons, so I was a bit meh when a third wasn't available.- There are some problems with how the last boss is handled in terms of mechanics. It's a little cringy from a narrative perspective. Also not a fan with the conclusion of the overarching nemesis. It felt rushed.Something I hope Kitfox will do:- Add an "Endless Dungeon" mode! Instant replay value. With each floor increasing in difficulty, I would easily spend hours running the dung and be satisfied.Overall, I genuinely enjoyed playing the game. Though I wish there was more dungeon content, the core of it was fun. I'll be playing again for the soundtrack!

_childDocuments_.review: 6/10Overall a very enjoyable and sweet game, I definitely recommend it.Highlights first:- This game is inclusive as heII- The sprite artwork is gorgeous and the simplified character style in the dungeons and on the map is adorable- The music fits well and I liked the score a ton- The game makes you aware of its trigger warnings and overall makes you feel very safe- Every romance option has its own appeal, I didn't feel like any character had less depth than the other, they feel about equally as developedSome things that contributed to the low score to be aware of when picking up this game:- The voice acting isn't perfect: It doesn't align with the text boxes at certain points and characters are not fully voiced(which isn't an issue, but worth noting). There are scenes where one character has full voice acting, while others don't, which feels dissonant.- The game sets up themes and doesn't quite deliver on them (To remain spoiler free, I won't elaborate, but I'd have liked my choices to be viable and have actual impact on the story a bit more, especially during the finale.)- Although all characters are developed equally, they don't have many layers, which isn't bad, but in general leaves me lukewarm about them.In spite of all this, I had a very fluffy time with this game, 10ish hours of gameplay well spent. I don't regret picking this one up.

_childDocuments_.review: I had been looking at this game for a bit and picked it up on sale out of boredom. I wasn't expecting much.  I was hooked a couple hours in, but near the end I was bored. Starting off, I was impressed by everything it had: character customization, crafting, interactive texts, and a good variety of romances.  It has all the right mechanics and a great foundation, but the writing needs a lot of work. There are all these characters, platonic or otherwise, and this great little world the writers have created, only to have the story go nowhere when it hits the climax; then the story resolves itself quickly and VOILA you've hit end game :\  (Also the "twist" with Sunder? UGH, WHY. This felt like pandering to fans of that aesthetic, and it added nothing to the story line -- not even HIS story line.)The pacing through me off a bit, too.  Maybe I didn't dungeon enough, but it didn't take much to get 6 romances maxed out, so all I had left was the 3rd dungeon.  I didn't end up beating it because it got too boring.  I romanced a 7th character just to give me something else to do.Overall?  It's an okay game geared towards casual players, with underwhelming and uninspired writing.  If you're someone who likes challenging gameplay and a little more from your dating sims besides just, "Hey I'm a nobody that's new in town and looking for love, but no promises 'cause I'm leaving in 2 months anyway", then look elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun, witty, medium-length game (I beat it and completed every character's story in around 12 hours, and I'm a slow player) with dungeon crawler, visual novel and dating sim elements. If any two of these elements sound like your type of genre, I highly recommend checking this game out. This game will make you interact multiple times with a person who will later turn to stalking, threatening and then trying to more-or-less kill you. You have no choice about whether or not you interact with this person, the game makes you do it to advance the plot. Their antics  quickly dissolve to "how dare you reject me, you're a f*cking c*nt like everyone else". I don't mind the inclusion of such characters, especially because the game judges them HARSHLY for it. But the game also, at its very start, lets me choose whether a friendly parental figure will send me encouraging text messages in between, because that may be upsetting to some people, yet the game did not warn me about the stalker character, at all.(I went back and checked the game trailer and store description just to see if I missed out on any warnings, but no.)After starting the game and being pleasantly surprised at the opt-in option for the parental figure, this felt like a punch in the gut. I have not had stalkers literally trying to kill me IRL, fortunately, but I have met lots of people who raised red flags for me all over the place which made me get the F out, and I saw that reflected in this one character's writing. Kudos to the writing staff, but just please warn me first. Fiction is all about safely exploring (dangerous) concepts and that includes knowing what you're getting into.- the art is GORGEOUS! Not only the in-game avatars for everyone, and the cute outfit options for your character, but especially the animations that play when a weapon first transforms into a human- the dialogue and characterizations of everyone. The romantic partners are wildly different and all feel authentic, as in: They have their own goals, motivations and developments. Even your bystander cousin and your (if you opt-in) parental figure have distinct personalites I couldn't help but want to see more of- there's discussions of depression, of discovering yourself, of societal expectations regarding gender expression and it felt very diagetic and "this is this one person's opinion" instead of a lecture on how to do stuff, applicable to All People- you can freely choose what gender or sexuality you are (but the game is a bit weird on letting you express the latter, see "the negative" below)- the music is a vibe (I have not much clue about music, but I liked it, it felt very fitting for the setting)- as I've mentioned above: The stalker character.  Afterwards, there's more positive interactions with all the other characters and the game finally starts dropping hints and comments that the stalker's actions are messed up, so I felt more comfortable going forward. And I'm glad I did, because this game has a lot of good scenes where characters with anxiety or depression express their thoughts in ways I had not considered before, and I am glad for getting this experience. But I was really thinking about quitting this game . Which is a shame, because all the gripes I had, the games addresses eventually.- the dungeons are kinda boring. Combat isn't hard and after you've figured out how to play every weapon, the game becomes really easy- you cannot tell the game what your sexuality is beforehand, you can only choose in the moment. Which, I think, is a pretty great idea for factoring in that not everyone is always down for everything, but then the game also jumps ahead and makes conclusions like "You don't want to engage in sex on your nth date with this person? I guess you dislike sex then and I'll make this personwho asks to spend the night specify that they do it on the couch, far away from you."And then you get a tiny sad smiley from that character, sort of disappointed but NOT judging you, that you didn't want to have sex with them on that night (and for the rest of eternity, as the game presumes). Pro-tip: Track the PC's actions across multiple playthroughs, not just the one romance route they're currently playing. Also let us actually say aloud if we hate sex or not etc., please.I've ranted a lot about my perceived inadequecies of this game above, but I want to state: I recommend this game, whole-heartedly. I went into it expecting a whacky, campy, gay dungeon crawler, but then I also found glimpses into depression in ways and especially sensitity I had never expected it to address. This game made me tear up and reconsider how I have and will handle other people. If that isn't an indication of empathetic quality, I don't know what is.If you get this game: Go into it expecting it to be cute and then have your world shaken just the tiniest, good bit.

_childDocuments_.review: It's hard to know if this is a visual novel or a very light twin-stick slasher - there's a strong "what if Hades but way less roguey and way more dating" vibe! But whatever it is, I had fun.It's pretty short - I finished it in maybe nine hours? - and you'll only see four tile sets, six? monster sets and three bosses. That doesn't *sound* hugely replayable, but I'm still replaying it. Also, there is apparently DLC in the works.On the VN side: Everyone is bisexual, and it's notably not just "playersexual" in a couple cases. There's also some explicitly polyamorous characters (and "Mom" is supportive, if you tell her you're dating multiple people, "as long as you're honest and on the same page dearie" iirc). Dating options: three guys, one gal, two enbies, and one cat (cat route best route!) You can keep it platonic and still get the achievements.On the combat side: The weapons all feel nicely different, and there's some combos to learn - though I'm  more of a buttonmasher than a careful combo considerer, and I still got through. You do have to use each weapon to its strengths - e.g. the estoc has a unique 'block' ability you need to remember, or you'll have trouble getting mobbed when using it.Overall - it *does* feel a bit short for the price, but part of that is how refreshingly low grind it is. I definitely think I got value for my money and value for my time. Do recommend!

_childDocuments_.review: What do you get when you mix a dating sim, a roguelike dungeon crawler, a mystery, psychological baggage, and anthropomorphized weapons? Clearly, the creators of this game were set on finding out. This game is just . It's not too challenging, not too stressful, and not too serious, but still holds your attention with an entertaining (if kind of bananas) premise and enjoyable, easy-to-learn combat. You play as [insert your own character name here], a young [woman/man/enby--choose your pronouns] who is visiting Verona Beach to stay with their cousin for a summer. You have crippling anxiety over dating, something you've never done before. So your cousin sets you up with a few dates, but you find yourself falling for weapon-people: which are exactly what they sound like. But, lo and behold: you're a wielder! You take up the hobby of bringing your dates to the "dunj," where you can fight off monsters that take the form of your own insecurities. But something is happening to the weapon-people you find: many of them have mysteriously gone missing and turned up in random spots in the dunj. Can you solve the mystery while battling your inner demons  having the best summer flings of your life?That answer is yes. Yes times seven. (Well... six + a cat.)You should absolutely play Boyfriend Dungeon. It was a great 15 hours. Alas, summer's over far too soon.

_childDocuments_.review: A very good dating sim and a decent dungeon crawler/rogue like. Most or all the characters are very entertaining and likeable. The dungeon crawling has a variety of weapons with different combos and strengths that can be expended depending on which character you go out with the most. You also unlock new swords by progressing through dungeons which adds more playstyles to experiment with. I also like how the game focuses on repressed emotions and developing the main character throughout the dungeon with the monster designs and environments layouts. Through the halfway mark this aspect of the game does get repetitive and tedious as most of the weapons have been unlocked, enemies generally stay the same level, and no new mechanics are introduced. I feel that the playtime for the game being around 10 hours could be extended to add more content for the story and the overall pacing of the game. The visuals are great and the cutscenes of getting a new sword are a pleasure to watch. Although I do wish they add more portraits for some of the characters for more expressive scenes. The music when going through dungeons and dating characters is a groove, with the vocals being the cherry on top of it. This game has already a lot of potential and I am eager to play more if more content is introduced and I will update this review if things have improved or not. Overall the game is fun and would recommend it if you're into dating sims. Also Valeria is the best.

_childDocuments_.review: So originally I wish-listed this sucker for lonely b!#% reasons. And eagerly waited while desperately looking for other games to fill the void.Trying the game out after all the waiting was as fulfilling as getting a penny trick or treating as a kid. (Seriously Screw people that do that!) Characters and dates The art (janky in places) and animation is nice but I couldn't care less how pretty something when character development doesn't exit. I guess if you have time to kill and money to burn this might be a reasonable purchase but there are so many visual novels out there you can get (especially on those juicy sales) that'll give you hours upon hours of meaningful, memorable content and they are often pretty too. It's harder to find LGBTQ+ friendly polished work but that doesn't mean you should settle for mediocre. Oh about the stalker warning. It's a topic that's meant to be uncomfortable. I don't mind tense and traumatic experiences in a game/media (Psychological thriller/horror manga and Berserk fan enters chat) but if you dislike that sort of thing it's an unavoidable part of the story. And your character deals with it and typical fashion for them in almost every situation they are in - doormat. No matter what your illusion of choice is you often don't do much.I had a rough time relating to the mc and immersing myself. That's the reason I play a game where I can name my character. I enjoy placing myself in their shoes and I hoped there would be a variety to our options. Usually are shoehorned into what the story wants you to do. You have the illusion of choice. Make a choice that's wildly different from what the story wants - nope not allowed. Want characters to back off because you are uninterested? They'll nod, smile and keep hitting on you. I dabble in the video game harem lifestyle so while I'm cool with hoarding a bunch of romantic interests like Pokemon I send off into Mortal Kombat  it may not be your cup of tea. _childDocuments_.review: A B/G/NBxB/G/NB dating sim/dungeon crawler where you play as an individual (you get to choose pronouns and appearance) visiting your cousin's place for the summer in an attempt to gain some confidence in dating. To gain that confidence you have to literally fight your fears inside dungeons using a cast of conveniently single human-weapons. While I did enjoy playing this game for the most part, it ultimately feels like it was released in an unfinished state. There are a lot of great ideas here, but none of them are fully executed to the extent that I believe they should or could be.There are 7 romance/friendship options available: 1 female, 4 male, and 2 nonbinary. As far as I can tell each romance/friendship only has one ending and the overall story has a single ending. There might be different endings for friendship vs romance but I couldn't really determine which characters were on which ending if that was the case. It took me about 8 hours in total to complete all romance/friendships, both dungeons, and the main story.If there was a neutral rating for reviews I'd use it for this game. Since that doesn't exist, I'm going to be optimistic and give it a thumbs up based on what it could become in future updates. I paid full price $19.99(USD) for this game, but in it's current state I'm not sure I could advise spending that much on it. Perhaps wait for a sale or for more content to be added/updated first.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a cute little dungeon crawler and dating simulator I had fun with for the few hours it took me to play it through.Even though I'm not that good at dungeon crawlers it wasn't frustratingly difficult, so, for me, it has well balanced encounters. I got behind the combinations the different swords have, which also have different focuses regarding range, attack/defense, etc. But the combinations aren't so different that I had to remember a lot of combinations, at which I'm bad at. I'm usually a button smasher in these types of games, but in this one I wasn't so uncoordinated with the combinations after a while (I prefered gamepad over keyboard). Finding the zines and clothes didn't feel like work, but is just something that happens alongside. Some of the zines  I found a bit annoying, but I didn't have to choose them.Other than the title might suggest, you can romance and/or befriend sword characters of different genders. Each of the characters has their own arc. I liked all of the sword characters, some more than others, but the cat, Pocket, is my absolute favorite one, regarding fighting style as well as plot-wise: he protec, but he also attac. That the different answering-options indeed make a difference in how your relationship with the character unfolds is integral and well-made. The overall plot is good too. You get a content note for stalking, emotional manipulation, and domestic abuse before the start of the game. You have three different pronoun options (she/he/they) in your character creation and I deemed the varieties of possible styles for my character to be adequate to create a .I had a few problems in that I wasn't able to launch the game through steam, so I didn't get all achievements or only a random few, but I was able to resolve the problem by playing around with the compatability settings. This is why I played it again and, tbh, I hadn't as much fun the second time. I think with a bit more experience the dungeons and the dates felt a bit tedious and the music, which is good, became repetetive and annoyed me a bit. So for me it's more like a one time game. Or I just need a bit more time between replays. I'm still looking forward to the new sword characters though, one of which is already teased at.It's cute, it's fun, it's quite wholesome, it's queer, so it's right up my alley. ^^

_childDocuments_.review: The over-the-top, insane, steamy, sensational fantasy of this game is not romancing the hot vampire sword guy or the uber famous k-pop idol, it's living in a sane world where people are generally nice and treat each other with basic kindness and respect regardless of your sexuality or gender. Combine that with having a mother that loves you unconditionally and an entire village that cares about your emotional well-being and I was hooked.Partially kidding, but I truly did not want the game to end and was kind of sad to wave goodbye to Verona Beach. Even if the romances aren't that deep and the tropes were... well tropes... the game made me feel "normal" and happy in a world that always wants me to feel lesser for being my authentic self. This game is so committed to this that you can even change your pronoun selection during your playthrough without it being a world ending event. I started the game with one set of pronouns and ended with another and the game never comments on it being a big deal, everyone immediately understands and no questions are asked and it doesn't limit your dating pool. There's even two non-binary romance options with Sawyer and Rowan. Sure some of the enby stereotypes are a bit over the top and dated but I think it fits with the universe and overall vibe the game was going for. Outside of dating and romance, the game itself is actually surprisingly fun. It manages to find that "just right" Goldilocks spot of not too challenging but not so easy that it's a total cake walk. There can be a grind to it if you want that and that's how I played because I wanted to 100% it, but you don't have to do it that way if you don't want to. Overall a super fun, cute, lighthearted experience that lightly touches on some important themes like fears of intimacy and change.

_childDocuments_.review: This isn’t a complete do not recommend but more YMMV.Overall it’s a well thought out game with a good idea but I didn’t find myself enjoying it and wanted it to be over more than I wanted to keep trying to make it work for me.Combat: Felt to weightless and I didn’t feel like attacks or even dodging had any impact to it. That made a little difficult to get into the zone when in combat.I ended up prioritising who could get me through the dungeon and mobs the fastest rather than trying to get more use to the combat. Which doesn't sound bad, but I wasn't enjoying the encounters at all. The enemies are not particularly difficult but since combat didn't feel good it wasn't fun to play.I also forgot about the books half the time and rarely used them in combat until I was panic button mashing in a challenge room.Dating: Everyone seemed pushy/forward from minute 0. Other dating games start out with your candidates being more neutral toward you and it gets built up to romance or friendship route. But since everyone in this game, including your mom, starts out on a mission to get you dating all interactions = romance?Even the dialogue options that seemed more friendship (or flat out rejection) get you romance responses.At least for the first 3 (4?? If stalker lad is an option) I wish stuff started more casual. The dates and interactions feel forced, even more so when I choose “this is not a date” options. It felt  like working in reverse, instead of building up a relationship to romance I’ve got to convince them I just want to be friends.But I also was not a fan of the first available candidates. I ended up wanting to be their friends instead. A lot of their dialogue ignored my attempts at “let’s just be friends”….but that’s also probably because those options mostly trigger more pink/red hearts and rarely the yellow ones. That made it difficult to enjoy since I was trying to reject/neutral them and they stayed flirty at every turn.Even though I was interested in finding out about the other available candidates, I couldn’t stand the interactions with the first 3 and dreaded any dates. Dates are required for weapon level progression so I couldn't get away from them if I wanted. I was annoyed through most of my short playthrough and didn't want to keep going to meet the other candidates or unravel the story.Also, as nice as the game is to give you a warning about some aggressive interactions (à la stalker lad) his interactions and any extended dialogue with him is stressful and tanked the game experience for me by a lot. You may want to watch an LP or play with a friend first to get a good feel if you’ll be comfortable having to interact with this guy. Especially since he is also one of the shop owners. Though his shop dialogue is neutral-ish and (so far) you can get what he sells via dungeon grind instead.Other:- I kinda wish there was a day/night cycle. As far as I know you only sleep once and from then on it’s just go out into the overworld whenever you want and hit up shops or dungeon. I think it would help the pacing for when you go on dates. Especially when the dialogue is see you tomorrow or this evening, but it doesn’t match up with when you can go do activities. But characters will text you when a location is available to visit for an activity, most of the time the unlock is instant.- Navigating the overworld with your avatar seems unnecessary? Personally just cycling through buildings with a list or bright outlining the location you want to go would be just fine and simpler.- Too many text. I was getting overwhelmed with how much the characters text you. Going home I just wanted to see what I could craft or try on new clothes but the text were so much. There was a little downtime to not text but it just felt like a lot happening and waiting for them to finishing typing to see if you can respond or not.I don’t know if I could have just left people on read or if they’d continue to text you if you were in the overworld or dungeon. If there was a better or easier way to manage the text I didn’t see it.- I needed an option for everyone to just say dungeon. Every time I saw or heard “Dunj” was a cringer.

_childDocuments_.review: I left this game feeling very mixed. I really enjoyed most of it, but it feels like the beta version or play test of a game rather than a completed game. Starting with the areas without issue, the music is very solid, the zines are all fun to use, the crafting is excellent, and the enemies are all really fun to fight for the most part. Next, the problems. The combat, while fun at times, has so many interesting ideas that feel almost finished. Out of all the weapons, the only one that feels finished in combat is the dagger. Every other weapon lacks combos or synergy with it's abilities. The axe for example has only two combos which get boring really quickly.  Leveling up also feels lackluster when all you gain is health and monster damage scaling causes that extra health to be unremarkable. A stamina system or character abilities would make each level feel more impactful. Finally, there is no wave mechanic to stagger monsters spawning in and add extra strategy to combat. Monsters spawn in all at once and are mainly difficult because they swarm you.Then there's the dating sim side. Though the story is mostly fleshed out, it doesn't feel like you have much of an impact on it. Rather than having a major impact on how the story plays out, the story happens to you with you only getting to choose which parts play out around you. Each character is fairly flat, with a few exceptions, and any of the dialog choices you make don't seem to make an impact on the story. You can give people gifts, but there is no in game system to track their likes. Though such a system is not needed as each character's likes are extremely basic and easy to guess. The cat gets the cat toys, the surfer the surfboard, the business man the cuff links, and so on. Those things wouldn't be big problems if any of the character's were fun to date. The minimal voice acting and lack of diverse character sprites results in you seeing and hearing everything pertaining to a character after an hour or so. On top of that, the dates are all boring, predictable, or cheesy in a bad way as it feels like minimal effort was put into the writing. A final thing to add is the lack of character customization. While the clothing options are all fun and there are plenty of them, there's a disappointing lack of hair styles and no way to customize your body type outside of gender. All in all, I enjoyed my first play through, but won't be playing Boyfriend Dungeon again and can't recommend it. If you can get it half off like I did then it might be worth it for a lot of people, but there are also finished games you can get for the same price. Go spend that money on something like Cosmic Wheel Sisterhood or a better dating sim.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game, I truly did, but I just... didn't.I love dating sims with wacky premises. I love dungeon crawlers with rogue-lite elements. I'm VERY gay.But the writing in this game was just... not good. I didn't feel connected with any of the characters in any meaningful way. Most of them had a single one-note 'problem' that wasn't really explored in enough depth to make an impact on me.The only one I liked even a little was Hato Moa's doing, and that just made me wish I was playing Hatoful Boyfriend again instead. This is very much a personal taste thing, but all of these characters were too damn nice, and the only exceptions to that were: 1. a guy who stalks you. 2. the bisexual bad boy who only wants sex archetype. Neither of which do it for me. Robert from Dream Daddy did and subverted the latter with way better writing and more complexity. Where's my gay weirdos?Aside from that, there's only two dungeons in a game that's supposed to be equally about dungeon crawling AND dating. Once your character gets even mildly powerful the dungeons are completely trivial and basically a repetitive chore you have to do to get more story content. Combat isn't particularly deep. Having to use weapons I hated just to see their dates was annoying. The art style in the Dungeons is also completely different from the rest of the game and not in a way I like - I'm not expecting mind-blowing hand animated 2D art, but I would like it to remind me less of goofy party games when the 2D art in the game is so gorgeous. Yeah, the art's nice. Can definitely say that. Backgrounds are pretty, 2D animations are beautiful, portraits of the characters are visually lovely. But it absolutely cannot save this game from being a 'kind of okay in parts, wouldn't recommend'.TL;DR: Just buy Hatoful Boyfriend if you want a dating sim with a wacky premise that has deep characters and emotional writing in it. Just buy Hades if you want a dungeon crawler where you also get to date. This is less than both.

_childDocuments_.review: So I loved this game but I feel expectations need to be set in order for people to enjoy it:Difficulty is low so if you're someone that enjoys games like Elden Ring and Dark Souls this will maybe be boring for you.The sickly sweetest and earnestness of the games writing may also alienate people that don't go in expecting it, or just don't enjoy that kind of writing.Its also very very short, which the free-DLC should fix by adding an extra dungeon, but even then the free-DLC is only going to bump it up from 13 to maybe 17 hours of content.I do not care about this cause I have barely any free time to play games and 20 hour games pretty much suit the time I have available, but if you expect or enjoy long-ass games then this will disappoint you.The game also likes to have its cake and eat it to.There is the escapism of having 7 (soon to be 10) ultra-hot, ultra-charming, gender-diverse, polyamorous bisexuals (including a K-pop and a SPOILER) all romantically pursuing consistently and respectfully, initiating dates with you so you don't have to do that labour or try gage whether its okay or appropriate for you to initiate with them.And then also your being stalked and harassed. And then also you have one random date where the person isn't interested you just to remind you how 99% of your dates go in your real life. And then one character breaks up with you on reaching "Max Love".I'm not against any of this, it just feels really dissonant as it breaks the escapist vibe. The underlying message the game carries regarding relationships needing to be built on trust and vulnerability is important and it requires the stalker plot-line and instances of rejection to hit home. I just think the writers maaaaaybe needed to polish the scripts a bit more as there are tonal shifts in the game that (while do not justify the outrage and harassment that has been generated from it) are genuinely very upsetting.BUT - if you understand all these things going into it and still are interested in playing it then most likely you will also love this game. Great characters, great story, great art and designs, great game play. It basically succeeds at all the core things it attempts to be.FYI - Rowan is the best character in the game, make sure to visit the mansion in the top-right corner of the map after the 4th of July barbacue or you'll miss them.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a little strange to review but I will definitely try my best to encapsulate everything it seems to offer. Here are a few key points I made note of as well as a list of pros and cons in general! Hope this helps! This point is pretty tough to describe as the writing in the game does many things well and almost an equal amount of things wrong. First off, a lot of the interactions are weirdly both meaningful and shallow at the same time. It really feels like the writers wanted to make the interactions more realistic and deep but barely scratched the surface in their execution of it. This point is shown even more through the characters themselves as (once again) they are clearly very fleshed out in the creators minds' but unfortunately it does not seem to convey that way in its final execution. If I had to choose one phrase to define the writing it would be this: lots of potential, not a lot of results. The gameplay is very simple and relatively well-executed. This is an example of great execution but not a lot of creative thinking unfortunately. By no means is the dungeon crawling poor in my experience with it, but I did find myself constantly wanting more and knowing the team could have gone so much further had they taken more time and been a little more ambitious with the system. It always felt like there was a certain flair that was missing to it after the first few levels. Redundancy is not the worst thing to feel in a game, but it certainly does not help a game either. Ultimately, the dungeon-crawling is a very fun system with great mechanics and great execution, but could definitely have done more to differentiate itself and live up to its full potential. This was yet again a hot and cold situation for me. While I enjoyed most of the characters and believe almost all are very unique and clever (especially for a dating sim; i.e. the cat character is literally a cat), I also wanted a more characters in general. The cast is relatively small for my tastes. Perhaps the bigger issue for some is the pacing of a character's arrival. After 4 hours, I was still being introduced to new potential dates. While I personally liked the idea of some more spread out pacing so you can really learn more about a couple characters before choosing to move on to others or not, it will definitely be a turn-off for some people. I got somewhat "lucky" in that my favorite potential date was introduced very early for me (Valeria) which really helped to keep me engaged early on. This game really struggles to be a "dating sim" at times as the player rarely makes any real meaningful decisions when it comes to dating the weapons. In a game where the writers clearly wanted a more realistic dating approach, I was surprised at how even the worst answers just led to a successful date by the end of it all. Again, this is not to say the dating sim part of it is bad, but more so it was a massive missed opportunity that could have tied into the gameplay and made the game more challenging (where it can struggle at times). Ultimately, this game had so much potential and I was thoroughly excited to play it! Unfortunately, the game does not live up to its full potential. All is not lost however, as the execution of most of the game is very well done and it was clearly crafted with a lot of passion all things considered. PROS-Very unique characters-Fun dialogue-Well-executed dungeon-crawling-Great character designs-More realistic dating and characters (you know, with actual flaws)CONS-Many missed opportunities to better the game-Lack of meaningful choices in the dating sim portion of the game-Could have executed some of the writing a little better on certain portions of the game-Gameplay CAN get somewhat repetitive and redundant after awhile (particularly in long sessions)-A couple other characters would have gone a long way7/10 (Above average, and one I would still recommend for players who already enjoy dating sims and/or dungeon crawlers, but not many others.)

_childDocuments_.review: At present, I am very happy with this game. It is exactly what I have been looking for for years. A Persona-esque life simulator/RPG, but is written with the contextualization of adults rather than teenagers. Meaning that your waifu won't freak out when holding hand, but instead might even wanna head down to freak town on the first date. And as much as I love anime, Japanese culture, and visual novels, it is refreshing to break away from those archetypes and troupes, to a more western style'd game. I really like how flawed some of the characters are, to the point where you may not even like them until you get to know them. They feel like real people. Really thirsty people. The soundtrack is also banging. The combat is tight and snappy. You know you've got good combat when rolling just feels great to do.I am sure a lot of people will inevitably compare this game to Hades, and while it has similarities, this title has been in the works years before that game came out. I will say if you liked Hades you might like this, but at the same time it it should be measured on its own merit. Just so good. So glad this finally came out. Much love, and thank you!

Despite the places where the writing falls through, I still find myself really enjoying the gameplay and the heart in the relationships. The one thing I think that has stuck with me, is the theme of healthy relationships being what helps a person to grow. The inclucivity and GNC characters made me feel rather seen as well. _childDocuments_.review: It’s summer vacation and your absolutely amazing cousin Jessie is offering up his old apartment room rent-free for you to stay at while he and his fiancé live together and prep for their summer wedding! Verona is a gorgeous town with malls, museums, art studios, a college and cat cafes! Capulet Beach is a popular tourist spot with the Verona Lighthouse as a scenic landmark, and best of all, there are dungeons! The three dungeons are super popular dating locations between wielders and weapons, to clarify… people who wield weapons and people who transform into weapons. This summer, it’s time to be brave, step out of your comfort zone, identify your fears and literally fight them head on as you dive deep into the Labyrinths! 5-11 hours to complete, Boyfriend Dungeon is a Roguelike Dungeon Crawler that’s also a VN and LGBTQ+ friendly with non-binary options. There are 3 procedurally generated dungeons and 10 dating options  that can turn into various weapon types that leave a lot of room for creative and diverse playstyles that you can level up and unlock new skills! There are also plenty of customization options and outfits to wear, things to craft, and skill books to use. The music is notably made by Marksye and songstress Madeliene McQueen and is honestly really good to dungeon with. I only really have two complaints. Let me mute my phone! I get it! You have a lot of dating options. That’s great. But when you step out of a dungeon and you have like, 9 people blowing up your phone trying to get your attention and set up dates it just makes me not want to come out. This is made significantly worse by accepting the “Encouraging texts from mom” option when you start the game, which you can’t turn off unless you make a new game btw, who absolutely has no idea what moderation or personal space means. My phone was constantly popping off and it drove me ******* NUTS. Secondly, not everyone is super comfortable with polyamory! I only tried to date like, 2 people and one of them I decided I didn’t like later on, but I ended up pulling like, 6. If you don’t immediately tell the other person on the first date that you just wanna be friends, I think you just straight up get locked into the romance route; which is a bit terrible because at that point you literally do not know anything except a brief summary and first impression of the other person.

_childDocuments_.review: Boyfriend Dungeon is a gem of a game where you face your inner fears and dungeon crawl your way to romancing not just beautiful people, but the very weapons you're relying on to stay alive as you forge meaningful relationships with them.You choose your pronouns (she/her, he/him, they/them) which doesn't impact your relationship choices and can dress your avatar any way you want from dresses to suits or costumes. There's a fair range of skin tones, hair colors, and hair styles (curly, short, long, bun, kinky, etc.)When it comes to capturing hearts, options include 3 males, 1 non-human male, 1 female, and two non-binary characters. (Additional 1 male and 1 female to be added in the future). The characters are sincerely interesting with hopes and flaws that left me looking forward to more after each interaction. Boyfriend Dungeon shares the good and the bad of not just romance, but many kinds of relationships. And you'll see  reaching the end of your summer in Verona Beach is just so bittersweet. Gameplay is roguelite with generated dungeons, monsters, and treasure, but forgiving with the ability to jump to certain levels you've already reached and no other progress lost. You can make combat easier for more casual play via settings and wearing a hat with 1 extra benefit (more healing items, more damage, extra life, etc.) or unequip the hat to maintain pressure in your hack-and-slashing. The ability to swap weapons between floors reduces grinding and lets you try different weapons often - highly appreciated! Each weapon has its own quirks & fighting style where you make some choices how the ability changes (stunning versus more damage, bigger area of effect or more targets, etc.). The weapons' fighting styles change when you increase intimacy by experiencing the dungeon with them, giving gifts, and going on dates. What I appreciated is that not all relationships were forced to be romantic and I could choose to be friends with a character rather than kiss and romance everyone. Besides lovely art for the characters - including captivating animated transformation scenes for all the weapons - the game's soundtrack is a great one! I do wish the game were longer, as I did 100% the game in about 10 hours. However for the price I am satisfied. The game only has two dungeons with less than 15 floors in each. I understand the monsters in the dungeon are currently about the main character, but it would have been nice to have additional dungeons related to the other characters' fears and anxieties to get even a little deeper into their stories surrounding commitment, grief, independence, validation, etc. For example, I thought the second dungeon would be related to Sunder in a deeper way (but was mistaken) and would like to see more dunj appear in other locations related to some of the weapons.Overall I highly recommend the game and I'm very excited for the additional characters coming in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr Get Boyfriend Dungeon for the Boyfriends, not the Dungeons. 7.5/10Boyfriend Dungeon is great. Like a warm hug.If you think a simple dungeon crawler where you get to progress a relationship with a character by wielding them as your weapon in battle sounds interesting, don't be afraid to try it.The hand drawn introduction animations for the characters are gorgeous, the art style for character portraits is unique and different, and the game tackles romancing people in a way I've never seen before, and I'm more than grateful for the option to just be platonic with them. However, there are some drawbacks, mostly technical.- The combat is probably the game's weakest point. It's hard to explain, but it doesn't feel 'tight' enough. There certainly isn't a delay in input, but it feels somewhat sluggish at some points.- Smoothly flying through the dungeons fighting enemies is sometimes tripped up by awkward obstacles in rooms and unnecessary feeling walls.- The dungeons start out difficult, then when you get a few levels on your character, it becomes painfully easy.- Despite the weapons all having different mechanics, ultimately it feels like you're smacking around enemies with the same thing, just reskinned. (This doesn't carry over to the characters in each weapon though, thank goodness.) ps. pocket is best cat.

_childDocuments_.review: Short and sweet visual novel with an excellent soundtrack. The art is lovely, the characters are fun, and the combat is expressive if somewhat simple. The main event here is--perhaps unsurprisingly--the visual novel elements. It's light, breezy, sincere, and funny. The uses of text messaging as an intro and outro to the various date scenes is excellent and the game gives you a lot of control over when you engage with the dungeon and the various characters keeping the games pacing largely up to you. Don't go in expecting some sort of torrid relationship simulator that tests your ability to guess what the characters (or the writer) are thinking. Everyone's here to have a good time with or without the main character, and your interactions are part of that not a challenge or obstacle for the player.While the writing is largely interested--like the soundtrack--in good times and chill vibes, there's a creepy stalker fellow who turns up as a foil of the supportive supporting cast. It gets darker than I expected, but unless you're particularly sensitive to themes of stalking and incel rhetoric it shouldn't detract. I'm not sure how much the game benefits from going there, but the tones are blended well enough that it didn't strike me as a jarring misstep either.In principle, combat forms the other half of the game. In practice, it feels like less than half regardless of time commitment. Combat is fine. The game has the decency to stop before the simplicity of combat overstays its welcome though some of the late-game weapon upgrades are a lot more powerful than the enemy simplicity really deserves--it doesn't feel quite as good to go ham with late-game Pocket or Rowan as it would with a more sophisticated opposition and just adding health or damage to existing enemies wouldn't fix this. Dodging isn't quite effective enough and attacks can cancel all projectiles so its more about timing when you push into a crowd of enemies than movement or attack execution. Within the simple framework, each of the weapons has a reasonable amount of personality in combat--they require different footwork (WASD work?) and expose you to different amounts of risk even if they create unique tactics. Making any bumps in this road more palatable is the insertion of VN "hangout" scenes into the dungeons--they can be ignored if you've seen a particular location/weapon scene combo before and they add a nice breather and a reminder of the game's strengths that keeps the combat feeling a little fresher than it might otherwise.The soundtrack is also fantastic.

_childDocuments_.review: I understand the controversy of the premise of this game.Storyline was hit or miss, depending on your perspective. I found the games progression to be pretty simple. You can max out your characters pretty easily in the game before progressing to the end of the actual story. I ended up maxing mine out that way at least. The gameplay was fairly straightforward, in the beginning I expected to be overwhelmed a lot more but it wasn't as bad as I thought it would be. For people looking for a challenge, I wouldn't add this to your wishlist, its definitely a more casual type of game. The characters you meet are robust and distinct in both their personalities and abilities. The game doesn't make it as clear whether or not your romances affect your endgame... but I can say, it doesn't seem to affect it much. I kinda wish it did so I could have made different choices. You can gift items to your characters also, but it didn't seem necessary since I maxed the characters out and still had presents I could have given away.The music is awesome, and the reason I ended up clocking 10 hours into the game. It doesn't take nearly as long as I put into it, I just found myself listening to the soundtrack in the background as I browsed the net. Sounds and such, like attacks were fine and felt weighted enough so no complaints there.The graphics were alright, I definitely enjoyed the introduction animations for each character you meet. The end animation was pretty great to see also, slightly bittersweet.I think the best part of this game for me was the mixture of gameplay with visual novel. It allowed for a slightly more diverse type of game. Now as for the controversial stalking, Yes there is stalking in the game and no it is not horrifically excessive. However it is there and it is understandable for anyone who has been in a situation where that may have happened to them, it can be uncomfortable and I probably wouldn't recommend someone with that issue to bother with the game.For those who haven't and are looking for a simple game to sink some time into, I'd recommend this game to them.Overall rating 7.5/10. Needed more content and more weight to your choices to get a higher score from me.

_childDocuments_.review: Been waiting for this ever since the Kickstarter, and it did not disappoint! It's innovative and different, as well as feeling very, very real in the character interactions. _childDocuments_.review: TLDR: This game is SO MUCH FUN! If you even just remotely enjoy anything in the direction dating-sim and/or dungeon-crawl, you will enjoy this game!So, I've just got this game on 100% (with the steam achievements, my wielder lvl ain't maxed out yet, but psht!) and honestly? And even if they are, they still have some sort of detailed-ness about them so that they don't feel... one dimensional, if you know what I mean.The trigger warnings at the beginning are an important addition and should be considered before playing and the fact that the game asks us if messages by someone called "mom" are okay is phenomenal too!These little details (asking for consent, the option to chose between platonic and romantic attraction, the fact we can chose they/them pronouns, polyamorous relationships etc. etc.) make this game phenomenal, plus the intuitive and easy gameplay make it a wonderful game to play casually!So, all-in-all, a truly amazing experience.I am very hyped for the DLC Kitfox announced a while back and will definetely keep an eye on the studio in the future.with kind regards,a queer person <333

_childDocuments_.review: The devs did a good job of making an enticing story to accompany the concept of a dungeon-crawling dating sim. I don't think people realise the character development for each character, including yourself (except maybe Jesse): it's very well-written. There's a focus on boundary setting and regulation which is something I appreciate. You can see that primarily in Rowan (Scythe) and Sunder's (Talwar) stories, where they attempt to establish a boundary with the player or take accountability for the fact that they made a mistake which could have overstepped your own boundaries. It's not specific to certain characters but those were the instances that stood out to me and it's something that really made me appreciate the game even more.Other than that, I really appreciate the inclusion of non-binaries in the player customization as well as the characters, Rowan and Sawyer (I may have missed a few others but they are the mains). I also noticed the headscarf and turban in the character customization: a suggestion I'd have is to make those a hairstyle as opposed to a hat. Aside from the hats that offer full-coverage for their hair like the Fox Hood, a lot of the people that want to wear a headscarf will have to sacrifice it in-game in order to reap the benefits of the hat that they want to wear. I know it's a lot that the devs would have to work on just to accommodate the hats to the headscarf and the turban but I do think it helps with the inclusion of these people that wear them on their day-to-day (and want to wear them in-game). I thoroughly enjoyed the graphics, art, and just everything in between. This game is so beautiful and there's a nice attention to detail in all of the explore-able places, as well as a careful consideration to the player's interaction with it. The dungeons aren't extremely difficult but they are challenging enough to do where it still feels stimulating even if you're maxed out on all of the swords. The inclusion of supporting characters like Olivia really helped with aiding the storyline (as supporting characters are intended) and providing a laugh: when Olivia was offended about the player and Seven being out together, I thought it was so funny (although, there is a lesson in that story for her to learn). All-in-all, a really well-done game and I look forward to seeing what else these devs come up with!tl;dr: Worth buying the game if you're looking to play a dungeon-crawling dating sim with some smooth voice acting and cute game design. :)

_childDocuments_.review: A very interesting concept for a dating sim game. I loved all (well, almost all) characters. They can get a little cheesy sometimes, but each one has a lot of depth to them. The main villain can get a little.... too much exaggeratedly villainous, but the romantic options (more like relationship options, really) more than make it worthy. The main plot is a bit nonsensical and you can see the twist at the end coming from a mile away, but it is also charming in its simplicity.The gameplay is nice, the way it combines dungeon crawler and dating is refreshing. The dungeon part can get a little repetitive and too easy towards the end, though, since enemies tend to just swarm your devastating area of effect attacks, the healing items drop multiple times in the same room sometimes and you just level up too fast. I barely used my special "magazine power", since I never seemed to need it. I understand though that the main focus here is the dating part and the dialogues, and they are very well done. The gifts and the social triggers each dungeon floor really add to it.All in all, I think the only actual fault that made me a little disappointed is the length of it. It's just too short, with only two dungeons. In the end you might find yourself grinding a bit just to evolve the relationships and play through their cutscenes before the final fight.It's a very creative and decently done game with a reasonable price tag on it, so if you're a fan of dating simulators I surely recommend it. Oh, and the soundtrack is just superb, seriously.

_childDocuments_.review: As I thought about what to say on this game, I realized a lot of it came off as pretty negative, so I want to start by saying I enjoyed this game, and I recommend this game. I took the time (~8 hours, maybe less if you're faster than I) to get all the achievements, and I'd play more of this if it were available.I can't speak to the developer and if this really was their goal, but this game felt like an attempt to pay homage to Hades* and/or Persona 4. If one were to take Persona 4's social systems and its general idea about enemy/dungeon themes, but then try to layer them atop Hades gameplay, you might get this game. The trouble is that it doesn't do either of those two sides of the game as well as those examples. Several other action roguelikes offer sharper gameplay, especially if you're looking for any sort of challenge, and other VNs offer arguably better stories and romances.Somehow it works, though. It's a pretty short game, especially if you find a weapon you like and level it a couple times - the content becomes trivial, more of a farm than a challenge. You get several romances with a pretty varied harem across genders and styles, and a lot of it is very charming. The look and sound is solid. I finished the whole thing in two sittings.*Post-review Edit: I realized after posting this that Hades is actually a pretty poor comparison for the gameplay this offers, but had been in my head due to the weapon system, which is something it does a bit better than this game to be honest. However, I realized there's actually another Supergiant Game that this resembles more closely - Transistor, in both the themes of romancing your weapon, and in your weapon having a personality that has certain skills tied to it. I came to the conclusion that the gameplay more closely resembles someone attempting to turn Transistor's systems in to an Action Roguelike than Hades itself, despite the similarities in weapon systems.

_childDocuments_.review: Number one complaint I saw about the game in reviews was that people felt like there wasn't enough content on offer. Each of the dateable characters are charming and engaging in their own way, and you're not forced to date exclusively and replay the game several times over if you want to see everyone's story. The game is LGBTQ+ friendly and it's very easy to tell characters you just want to be friends, if you'd rather explore a purely platonic relationship. Mechanically speaking, the relationship building is super low risk, you don't have to worry about min/maxing dialog choices or optimizing gifts, just spend time with them and you'll get there.My parting advice to any prospective players is to max out your favorite blade early, rather than spreading your time out amongst everyone - and to make sure to keep an eye out for a date opportunity at the big house to the northeast of town!
