_childDocuments_.review: I can honestly say i regret buying this game. It was a fun 6 or so hours of my life but for as much as it costs when I'm pretty poor it was not really worth it. It's a really great concept, just really poorly executed. 2 Dungeons (I refuse to call them what they call them in the game) and a very lackluster final boss fight were done in no time. The romances/friendships felt very stilted and somewhat confusingly written. I felt very forced to only do certain things, like being at odds with one of the friends of the character i was mainly dating, for example. With another character i kept telling him to back off but when I wanted to know why he was gone for so long, out of curiosity, ingame it turned into a moment of jealousy and supposed insecurity? Suffice to say, I really did not enjoy the writing very much either. I really wanted to though. There were a few moments i loved the writing, like how sawyer was so happy to know another nonbinary person. It felt like  a real human piece of dialogue, partially because that's the kind of thing i would've said in a similar situation.One of the main parts i didn't like was when the "main antagonist" rather patronisingly called another nonbinary character an enby, and no one called him out on it for being infantalising and that grinded my gears a bit. A lot of Nonbinary people don't like being called an "enby" and while i'm not one of them i do believe its a term others can use to be infantilising and it should only be a term used when its absolutely okay by the person in question. In that vein, i just hated that the guy who said it wasn't called out. I was ok with how the "stalker" character was portrayed he was oddly the most 3 dimensional feeling character in the end. While i liked how everyone reacted to him it all still felt like it was handled rather oddly. But really, as i said before, the writing was not very enjoyable.If the characters were rewritten, made to feel more human and 3 dimensional that alone would honestly make me want to play the game again. i really did love the concept and i loved the concept of the characters too, they just really didn't feel right. More dungeon content would also be nice, but i had some misgivings with the combat albeit that might be more the fault of my controller, but it felt clunky so beware of that possibility.I read that they were planning on adding dlc/more characters. If it was free dlc or just an update, I wager it would make the game more worth it, especially if the writing improves.All in all it was an ok game with a lot of downfalls, but definitely some bits that made me smile. I can only recommend you buy the game when its on sale though if after reading this review you still think you'd enjoy the game. 6 hours and completed is not a lot of time at all for a game that costs this much.

_childDocuments_.review: Well.  As far as realism goes.  This game nails socialization.  Being overwhelmed by text messages all coming in at the same time from different people.  Having to keep track of a lot going on.  Characters having real personalities with flaws and all just the right way to make you feel uncomfortable all over the place.  Game was totally right to recommend taking breaks as needed- and I was only 48 minutes into the game before I needed one… as someone who usually binges games and books for hours at a time, I feel like that’s saying something.  Even taking breaks, it was a bit too much.  I kept struggling to figure out what to say to different characters while worrying I said the wrong thing- which is realistic as well but perhaps too realistic.  Especially since sometimes the options are ‘be rude’ ‘be even ruder’ ‘agree to something you aren’t comfortable with’ in the dialogue options.  Instant stress.  The game is… kinda heavy.  It’s not casual, mentally-emotionally speaking.  It’s a lot.  No, but, really.  This triggers social exhaustion like crazy if you’re an introvert.  That’s pretty rare for a videogame of any sort, even one that’s mostly an interactive novel.  And the content warning isn’t really enough, I don’t think.

name: Werewolf: The Apocalypse - Earthblood
detailed_description: You are Cahal, a powerful Garou (Werewolf) who chose to go into exile after losing control of his destructive rage. On a quest for redemption and blood, Cahal plays a crucial role in the great war between the Garou and Endron, a powerful oil company that serves the Wyrm, a destructive entity ravaging the planet. • Transform into a wolf and sneak past enemies... • Or into Crinos, a ferocious beast that can rip those enemies to shreds. • As a human, interact with people, machines, etc. • Learn new abilities through the skill tree and perform devastating combos to exterminate all your foes. • Let the rage flow through you, channelling your rage into frenzy, turning you into the ultimate killing machine A unique experience full of savage combat and mystical adventures, inspired by the famous role-playing game

short_description: You are Cahal, a powerful Garou who chose to go into exile after losing control of his destructive rage. He can transform into a wolf and a Crinos, a huge ferocious beast. Master your three forms and their powers to punish those who defile Gaia.

_childDocuments_.review: Here's the thing. I really really really wanted to give this game a thumbs up.I mean its a werewolf game where you hack and slash your way through evil corporations. Whats not to love right?Except its not like that. Not really. You mostly sneak around from level to level until you reach a certain point. Then your character, sometimes for no good reason, will get enraged and turn int oa werewolf and THEN you finally get to rip and tear your way through badguys. But if you happen to get caught sneaking around before its time to change, its game over. You don't get to change if you get caught, its just game over. I feel like that was a very poor decision.Plus the graphics only look great in the opening cutscene and during werewolf fighting scenes. FOr the rest of it the game looks really shoddy and a little sub-par.The voice acting is bland and boring and its just not very good. I mean there are some serious dramatic moments that happen to these characters but their tone of voice is like they couldn't care less.The story itself is pretty unoriginal, just another revenge plot. But the idea is original and nice. I want more werewolf games but I also want better werewolf games. When you get to actually be a werewolf and do some fighting, its pretty fun I guess. But all the other stuff around it was so boring and so grindy that I found myself more bored than anything else.Maybe wait for a big discount before buying.Thanks so much for reading and if you want some more in depth info with actual gameplay then please check out the video on my youtube channel (link below).If not then I hope I was able to help some of you out there to spend your money wisely. Thanks for reading.

_childDocuments_.review: Contrary to what some people are saying in their reviews, you *CAN* absolutely skip stealth. You are *NOT* locked into stealth, and if you just want to rip and tear your way through nearly every level in the game as a 9 foot death machine engineered specifically to murder in the name of mother earth, you absolutely can.Anyone who says you get locked into stealth hasn't played much of the game at all. After you get to the CEO of the arms dealers, you are no longer locked to stealth. Everything before this is more or less a prolonged stealth tutorial. I urge you to KEEP PLAYING past this. The game begins to shine.Granted, a lot of people's complaints are valid. The cutscenes can use work, the voice acting is only passable, and the game feels like it should've come out ten years ago. I don't believe these are reasons to skip on this one, though. There are numerous more technically impressive games that are far less enjoyable.It's a setting worth looking into, a safe (albeit dumbed down) introduction to a compelling world, especially in today's environmentally conscious climate. Showing devs that this is a setting we want to see more of is worth the time. It's not a triple A title, and it won't play or look like one. It just needs to be fun, and this is fun.So allow yourself to fill the role of the Garou. You were born and blessed by the Moon as a Warrior in a warrior's culture, into a war that has been raging for thousands of years. The enemy has poisoned humanity. They're poisoning the earth, your mother. They're killing your brothers, your sisters, your family. They turn you against your own, against yourself. They are everywhere, behind every corporate corruption, their venom bleeding through the cracks in the world. The Earth bleeds more and more each day. It is time to answer the only question remaining.When will you Rage?

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to give this game a thumbs up, but I really can't do that if I want to remain honest.TLDR: A LOT of wasted potentialPro:+ Finally a game set in my favorite pen and paper setting+ A lot of Easter eggs for those who know what to look for with the companies shown and mentionedCon:- terrible camera controls- looks and plays like a PlayStation 2 game (and not one of the great ones)- annoying checkpoint saves- bland constrained levels- flat voice acting- bland boring combat- bland boring stealthThe worst part for me is that some of the potential that this game could have had shines through at times:- downgrading from five to three forms makes sense for a video game and their roles are set alright, but in practice, it feels like two games, a stealth game like so many sections in way too many games and a bland action brawler where you defeat scores of enemies which you can reduce by being good at stealth.- the idea that you gain spirit powers by helping the spirits just beyond the reach of regular humans is good and as an idea a nice translation of the role playing game, but in practice, it just means running around an area, hoping to find them so you can get generic upgrade points to spend in a bland and uninspired skill tree- seeing into the spirit realm is a great idea, but instead of making it a game of shifting between worlds to avoid obstacles and enemies and seeing the destruction wrought by the Wyrm on both sides, this wonderful power is reduced to being a generic detective vision like in so many other games.- being a lone werewolf who tries to help his people sounds fun, but this is once again a letdown for those who like the setting, where the pack and its totem spirit are so important. And now for the ranting part of a long time storyteller and player of the pen and paper:- Why on earth way such a bland main character chosen? There are thirteen interesting and diverse tribes to choose from! I personally love the Fianna tribe, but why is he so bloody bland? A rough man who actually cares for his family instead of abandoning them would have fit, so would a man who stands apart because of the fae blood in his veins. - From what little I have seen so far, a member of the Wendigo (Native American werewolves who follow a great cannibal spirit of winter) could have been a far better choice and could have lead to interesting conflicts of whose land that actually is- By the same token, a roaming Silent Strider (Egyptian werewolves who have been forced to roam the world after loosing their homeland to vampires) would have fit just as well- Why did you make him a warrior if half the game is going to be stealth focused? All garou are capable of ripping enemies limb from limb, but a Ragabash (tricksters born under the new moon) would have fit so much better for a lone wanderer who infiltrates- The inability of shifting between worlds annoys me to no end, this can be such a cool mechanic as seen in so many other games.- Instead of a stealth-action mix, why not make it a party based game with a rag tag group of garou from different tribes who have to work together? Yes, they are killing machines, but with the right enemy design that could be a lot of fun.- If you need to make it a game of a single character infiltrating then why not go for one of the other Fera( werecreatures)? A rat could have made the stealth part more interesting and focused it more into that direction. Want to keep it the same ratio? Use a Bastet (great cats), there it would actually make sense that the character could not cross into the spirit world and that they are on their own.In the end, I am mostly saddened by this thorough disappointment of a game and I sincerely hope that a far superior game in that setting can be made some time in the future.I will probably force myself to finish this game and will update the review at that point, but I highly doubt that I would ever recommend buying it unless you want to catch a glimpse of a really cool setting that was done a great disservice by this game.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all I think it's important to note that the top review which states that stealth is an instant failure, is not entirely true, it's in the game yes, but only in the first couple missions, once you've spent, oh I don't know maybe 40 minutes in the game there's no such thing, you can go into full werewolf mode whenever there's enemies, zero restrictions, and just rip and tear your way through them.I'm a big fan of werewolves, so when I discovered this game naturally I had to try it out right away, and I'd say it's somewhat of a mixed bag, if what you like is just some dumb action and ripping your way through enemies as a werewolf, then this game is for you, because that's what it is, dumb action, there isn't much nuance to the combat system, but for me there doesn't need to be.If what you're looking for is a in-depth combat system then keep looking, the combat is very simple, there's a grand total of 3 combat combo's, if you can call them that, you got left click and then right click, left click twice and then right click, left click three times and then right click, very basic, yes you can switch between agile and heavy stance but that actually take away 2 out of the 3 combos you have, in agile you only have 1 combo and you move faster, in heavy 3 combo's but move allot slower.Surely that can't be all there is to the combat you ask, and well there are also abilities, but they are limited by ''rage'' which you obtain by attacking and killing enemies so don't expect to use them a ton, 3/4 times a fight, you have a heal, a long range jump, long range projectile, a roar, and a couple others, honestly it would be far more entertaining if they were part of the combat system in some way instead of limited abilities as they don't feel impactful enough.But that's just the werewolf, what about the wolf form? Well supposedly the wolf form is for stealth, sadly enough when you perform a stealth take down while in the form of a wolf you turn back into a human, boy did that ruin stealth for me, here you have the fantasy of performing stealth as a wolf and then taking enemies down as a wolf but then I just turn back into a human? Missed opportunity.That said stealth isn't anything to write home about, expect to maybe be able to take down 2 enemies before you get discovered, because it really wants you to rip through allot of enemies and not walk back and forth to enemies all the time as a werewolf the rooms to fight tend to be rather small, so enemies are very close to each other and will quickly spot you.And lastly the human form, required to interact with objects, outside that useless, when you use your stealth crossbow after firing it you stand still for roughly 2 seconds reloading the damn thing, not optimal when the point is to try to sneakily kill someone and then walk away.The werewolf model itself, actually looks fairly good, this isn't some AAA studio we're talkign about so you shouldn't expect some insane werewolf model but it's still pretty good, the fur could use some improvement and the tail's movement is rather stiff, doesn't move much at all, could have been a bit longer as well.I've done a fair bit of complaining, and yet I would still recommend the game because this kind of dumb action as a awesome werewolf simply is just right up my alley. You may have noticed I didn't mention the story, and that's because it's a rather generic revenge + big bad evil corporation story, besides I didn't buy the game for the story, I Bought it to play as a werewolf.So basically in short, if what you're looking for is a dumb and simple game as a werewolf and nothing else give this game a try, I certainly enjoy my time with it and I don't think I'll ever get tired of being a werewolf.

_childDocuments_.review: This game looks like something you would rent from the Blockbuster bargain bin circa 2005.Werewolf the Apocalypse is that game that grandparents get you because they don’t know any better and you love them but you’re just a bit disappointed that they didn’t ask you what game you really wanted. “It’s got Werewolves, they’ll LOVE it!”Sadly I had more fun playing as a Werewolf in Skyrim, hell I had more fun playing as a Werewolf in Don’t Even Think, and that says a lot. I enjoyed the game but I can understand the criticisms. Still played it, but maybe up the difficulty to make the combat more interesting. The game would have been a masterpiece if it had released in 2009.Despite that I personally had fun with it.  Sure, the voice acting is lackluster, but the gameplay was just what I wanted when I got the game.  I played on normal, started areas being stealthy then tore them all apart when I was busted.  The game makes turning into a Werewolf feel like a Super Saiyan transformation. It's not a perfect game by any means, but it was exactly what I expected it to be so I don't regret the purchase.Werewolf Earthblood is a good game but just not a great game. If you're a fan of action beat'em ups and werewolves and aren't expecting the next God of war, it's a good but not great time. The comparison with Vampyr made by some is spot-on. Will it be an amazing game? Probably not. But it's not bad. Sure. It's not the greatest. But it never claimed to be either. I loved Vampyr, I love the Prototype games, and as a filthy uber casual White Wolf interested person I'm glad to get a game set up in the Werewolf camp.I still hope it has a modicum of success that might encourage the development of other products - Werewolf is a rich setting and deserves a bit more consideration.6/10

_childDocuments_.review: I have not finished this game.The Wyrm has been more powerful than me, but I got so bored that for a moment I fell into the Harano. I've failed the Garou Nation, but not as badly as this...thing.If any of the above terms ring a bell, congratulations, you know one of the most special games ever published by White Wolf in the 90s. Werewolf: The Apocalypse was, is, a role-playing game with a wonderful background that brought together spirituality, ecology, epic, tragedy and a stark (not always elegant) critique/parody of industrialised capitalist society. As of today it is clear that as a species we have sold out to the Wyrm and are killing Gaia, we live in the world that Pentex wanted to create and it is quite depressing. But that is not the point of this review. I just wanted to make it clear that I love Werewolf: the Apocalypse.And that's why I hate this game. Not only does it not take advantage of the universe it exploits, nor the very concept of the game. Garou herds hunt together, but in this product they go alone and it doesn't exploit that aspect of the universe at all. Garou are stronger when they work together, but here the Garou are stronger by collecting random spirits that are scattered around as collectibles.There is no exploitation of the fascinating spiritual world at all, no threshold travel, no garou rites, no use of the terminology of that rich universe, no spiritual fetishes or klaives. The character himself seems to ignore 99% of the aspects of the world in which he lives despite the fact that he is originally the second of an Alpha in charge of a very powerful Caern. Nothing. You have a hand crossbow, because they've decided this has to be a stealth game.And this is where the problem of the game really begins. Its gameplay is boring, very boring. Cyanide Studios seems to think that Styx: Master of Shadows was a great stealth game, it wasn't, but it was pretty fun, and they've decided to do it again. This thing has the WORST stealth design I've seen in a long time, with broken AI, surveillance patterns and mechanics so badly broken that it just manages to be frustrating. Metal Gear Solid, the one that came out on the PSX, is better designed and more fun than this game. The stealth mechanics are there, and you can skip them most of the time, but if you do, the combat arenas start.And the poo hits the cake.The combat, which you would think would be important and well-crafted, is the most basic thing that could have been programmed. Strong attack, fast attack, jump attack and a few powers that are triggered by Rage (if you're going to play, power up the healing power). It's a bland system, with no depth, that achieves something impossible: making a combat system where you're a giant werewolf boring. That the enemies aren't funny at all, that the camera goes crazy and that there's no interesting addiction to combat just makes it worse.If at some point in the prison part they put in some addiction, that's welcome, but my brain couldn't take it any more.And he's ugly to boot. The game is from 2021 but it looks like a mid-generation Xbox360 game. The designs (with the exception of the Crinos forms and some spirits) are ugly and boring, the animations are pitiful, and the voice acting of the poor actors who had to read the worst possible expository dialogue is pitiful. The story...as a kid, when I was DM of Werewolf: the Apocalypse and thought the Raven was the coolest movie of all time I directed much more interesting Chronicles.But the music is cool. That's true. Especially the more powerful themes.Conclusion: Cyanide Studios is a subdivision of Pentex, possibly belonging to Tellus Enterprises, which has created this mediocre and boring (I don't even know how many times I've written that word already) game to turn the garou into victims of the Harano. To avoid. And I hate to write this because I know it's a small game and not a big production, but honestly they could have done better with the great material they are working with. It could and it should.Remember the Litany: Combat the Wyrm Wherever It Dwells and Wherever It Breeds.

_childDocuments_.review: The reason I recommend the game is because it has no competitor. It's the only werewolf-centered game within its genre that I know. Overall the game is a bit mediocre and if it wasn't for the werewolves I'd recommend staying away from it, but I've got to admit that the game has its high points and they surprise you in very nice ways (I'm not going to list them because the whole "magic" of the moment was not expecting them).Now, to list a few problems as a warning:- The level design is pretty dull. Specially at first where every facility you sneak into feels almost copy-pasted. Later on it gets better, so hang in there if it feels a bit repetitive at first.- The stealth part of the game is bad in many ways. It's as easy as it's unnecessary. The good part is that you can ignore it and brute-force your way through. In my humble opinion, it would've been much better to focus more on making a better TPA or beat 'em up even if you're not in Crinos form (the werewolf) all the time. I understand the idea behind it all though. Turning into a wolf to sneak around, maybe take down some guards and build up tension for the climax of turning into a killing machine... That all sounds good in paper but in practice is not well delivered in my opinion. You get used to it though.- You gain most of your skill points by... Sniffing plants?- Animations are a bit bad. The Crinos animations are decent, the wolves' are somewhat alright, but every human including the MC move very oddly.- There is nothing half as good as the intro cinematic in the game.- Executions and other moves feel unsatisfying. Like you can grab a human and squash it but you don't really see or hear what happened so you're left wondering if you killed him or not.- Camera work is bad sometimes.And despite all those flaws I still had fun. The game gets better overtime and Cahal grew a bit on me (all other characters not so much). All in all it laid a good foundation for a better sequel. I liked the story too, it's easy to empathize with the cause and it doesn't feel preachy. Even as a unique experience I'd say it's worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: I like the tabletop game and its lore, but when this was announced I was skeptical. I wanted to find some reason to like this game, I really did. I decided to wait until I'd finished the game to give it a review. This was a frustrating experience, and I have a lot of thoughts. I have no intentions of playing any more, but maybe I'll come back to it.First and foremost, the game is not pleasing to the eyes (or the ears), even on max settings. The wolf and werewolf form are cool enough visually, but everything and everyone else is just... Hard to look at. The NPCs, the enemies, the environment, all of it. A large majority of cutscenes look like they were poorly animated in SFM and some of the voice acting is just jarringly or laughably bad. The maps are serviceable but bland and quickly start blending together. The music is just the same couple of songs on loop so at some point I turned it off and started playing my own playlist.Stealth in this game isn't just "optional", it's outright pointless and frustrating past the tutorial. The small size of most rooms, enemy placement, lack of any actual cover, and enemy pathing basically made it actually impossible to go through most rooms without tripping the alarm. Even in big rooms enemies could just see you over the short cover, especially during takedowns. I actively TRIED stealthing for most of the game and eventually gave up because there was no real reason to do so, and it was more frustrating than it was worth. Just walk into a room, press the rage button, go sicko mode. Ignore whoever's talking to you on your earpiece, move on to the next room. Rinse and repeat. It left me wondering why there was stealth to begin with, it seems like they just wanted you to focus on the werewolf stuff and the stealth was an afterthought. Combat felt good at first, but as the enemy strength rises you begin to feel less like a powerful werewolf and more like a pain sponge unless you find ways to cheese the enemies that constantly block your claws. Also get used to seeing the same 3 final kill animations all game, including for bosses.The story is a completely predictable train wreck. Nobody you talk to actually matters in the long run, even your allies. Combined with the bland voice acting and terrible animations, I couldn't find myself getting invested in any of the plot or anyone involved and just pressed the designated rage button whenever I could to get out of having to talk to anyone. I just didn't care. Every enemy with dialogue is just a plank of nameless wood for me to break over my knee. It's like the game had an identity crisis before release. At times it feels like there's almost something there. Then it immediately fizzles out and you're once again left with something that just feels unfinished. If you're dead set on playing it anyway, I hope you have more fun than I did and genuinely enjoy the experience despite its flaws. I'd recommend waiting for a sale to avoid buyers remorse, if possible.

_childDocuments_.review: As a WoD fan, this game is a huge disappointment. The story is flat. I was hoping for a game that followed the mechanics of the TTRPG in some way but no, it just lightly borrows from the lore and then goes off on its own tangent. As a gamer, the saves are frustrating. I've accidentally hit "restart level" instead of "load from last checkpoint" more than once and had to repeat a lot of content with no way of going back. The gameplay feels mediocre, the combat feels kickass for all of 10 seconds when you burst into Crinos form and then lackluster when you realize that it's repetitive and not very involved. The graphics feel dated. The voice acting is terrible. This would have been a decent game 10 years ago.I'm going to finish the game because it's WoD and I waited so long for this game to come out, but unless you're a die hard WoD fan or really want to play a werewolf game don't bother.

_childDocuments_.review: Oof, I hate to say this, but I have been highly disappointed by this game.This needs a modder's touch because it feels like it is a great concept but is missing a lot of what would make it great.The game portrays itself as a story driven action-stealth game along the lines of Shadow of Mordor or Assassin's Creed with elements of Arkham Asylum (Only Asylum though). It takes place in a classic TTRPG setting and uses that to lend itself an air of legitimacy in that area, and just falls flat.The story is boring, the gameplay is flat and generic, and the main elements I was looking for from a Werewolf the Apocalypse game are missing. I'm not normally one to criticize graphics, but these look like ten year old visuals. Add that with the gameplay and this may have been a top 50 game of 2012.If you want a mediocre and outdated hack 'n slash with some neat concepts that aren't fully explored, this game is for you. I hope that the mod community can bring this game to its full realization, because the Werewolf property deserves more than this.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm very sad about this.  I used to play Werewolf the Apocalypse way back in the 90's, and was a big fan of the universe.  I was very happy to see this story get a modern game treatment.  And boy did it look great. But unfortunately, it just wasn't that fun to play.  I'm sure there are cool moves and combos you can pull off as a werewolf, but there's no real opportunity to hone these skills, as combat doesn't occur that often, at least if you're playing the game as intended, which seems to be mostly a stealth game. I'm also very much missing the Glabro (Wolf-man) and Hispo (Giant Wolf) forms.  It would be so cool to have those as different "stances" as well.  And no attacking in Wolf form?  After that sweet opening cinematic?  C'mon.  The human form should be able to use everything that humans have too.  Just a Crossbow with 3 shots?  Well ok, but you can't pick up an enemy's rifle or handgun or anything?  Please.  The RP elements are nice....if you're a fan of the WoD already and know what they're talking about.  I'm not saying you need the characters to keep spitting exposition every scene, but even in The Witcher series, which also had an older more established fanbase, there were Glossary Entries for anyone who wanted to learn more about the world to read and unlock as you encounter them.  Not having this makes this seem very FFO (For Fans Only.)And finally, the transformations....  One of the coolest things about werewolf characters is that transformation, it's part of the fun.  This "Poof" puff of smoke transformation is very off putting.  I realize in the TTRPG, you can in fact do instant transformations, but it still should be more than a puff of smoke.  Anyway, as a huge fan of the Werewolf mythos in general, and Werewolf the Apocalypse at least from the 90's, this game just didn't meet my expectations.  Granted, they were probably too high in the first place. But Skyrim had better Werewolves.  There, I said it.

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't like this game at first, but it grew on me after I realized how it was supposed to be played. It's part tactics, part beat-em-up in the form of an angry guy who changes into a werewolf. Immediately it feels like the game Prototype, but this is not an open world game and in most areas you are confined to a small section of a building interior.Supposedly this takes place in the same universe as Vampire the Masquerade: Bloodlines but I couldn't tell that at all from a playthrough so it's irrelevant. There's no mention of vampires in the game as far as I know. There are references to wolves and worms, or "wurms" as they call them. First off, the intro cutscene is very impressive, but the in-game graphics are a little disappointing. Especially since you have sequences in the wilderness and you encounter things like bears that don't even acknowledge your presence, as though they are animatronic placeholders for real things. The story isn't bad, it's your typical vengeance save-the-girl nonsense, but the game takes itself WAY too seriously. It's a game about a man who changes into a mutant wolf, a little comedy would've made it much easier to digest the dialogue sections. At first I hated the game play, but that's because I didn't understand it. Basically, you have a number of different enemy types, mostly humans but also mechs, turrets, etc. They are never alerted to your presence, so you can skulk around in a very bad steath-type scenario until one of them gets alerted and then they all attack. The game then shifts into an action beat-em-up, and while it is repetitive, I must say the combat is a lot of fun. There were many times when I was within an inch of my health so I had to run to the opposite side of the map and carefully build up a powerup to avoid dying. The stealth sections suck, but you can get through a lot of them without alerting the enemy. You can also do things BEFORE the enemy is alerted, such as take out some of the infantry with silent kills, fire an arrow to disable turrets and cameras, break panels to weaken mechanical enemies, etc. This is where the game gets interesting, because you can carefully analyze each room to determine the specific plan of attack. There are also oddly placed AC vents on the floor that are the perfect size for a wolf to fit through. It doesn't make any sense, but it is fun trying to navigate around the mazes without alerting the enemies. If the enemies are alerted, then you into kind of a beast mode where you can switch between two forms, use powerups and build up a "rage" meter. When the meter is full you can basically bludgeon everything to death with no resistance. I was really bad at this game at the start because I didn't realize you can heal as an ability, so you want to heal 2-3 times every battle since everything resets after the fight.The camera is a pain though, almost game breaking but not quite. You can lock onto enemies, which makes it easier when you're fighting one, but when you have a dozen or so enemies and need to move quickly you will probably find yourself rotating the camera constantly to make sure it stays behind your character. It's unfortunate. There are a number of decent boss fights, two endings, and a lot of collectibles. If you get the collectibles it gives you points towards perks that can drastically alter the combat. This I really liked because the perks create legitimate strategies you can use to beat the game. In some games the perks are useless, but the fights are hard enough in this game that picking the right ones quite often means the difference between success and failure in combat. Overall, a pretty cool game, the music is repetitive but it gets you pumped up, and it's nice that someone actually created a game where you play primarily as a werewolf, as I don't recall a single other game that does this.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the many times I wish there was a "maybe" option for reviews. This game at full price? No. This game on discount? Yes. Its a real mixed bag of good and bad that's hard to summarize when you get down to it. When Werewolf came out, I had the expectation it would have the loving care of another World of Darkness game you might recall as VtM: Bloodlines. Of course, both games are practically separated by a huge span of time, VtM being the earlier game, and a different dev team and perspective would provide a different kind of game than Vampire no doubt. That said, differences aside, they are not the same caliber of game. You want more of a WoD experience, play Bloodlines. That said, you want to play a monster in the same vein as Prototype? This is worth a go.Combat and stealth are the highlights of this game, hands down without question. Not terribly challenging, I had to crank the difficulty up to hard to really feel stoppable, your werewolf form starts strong and just keeps getting stronger as you put in points to developing your abilities. With a quick form and a slower stronger bruiser of a fighting style, theres some value in switching things up on the fly but it can get super easy at times to just dart around the map picking off people systematically as they try to gun you down. Stealth is an option, a doable option in most situations but certainly unneeded; just letting you set the fight more in favor to your advantage by sabotaging gear and reinforcements or altogether dodging the encounter completely. Enemies have a set and predictable route that if you wait around enough you can ghost on through but between the two styles the combat is probably going to be the more engaging option.The story is........ not great. It does root itself in WoD's lore, but it just doesn't do it for me. Maybe its predictable drama of the protagonist, or maybe how the villains are just one seal clubbing away from being 2D edgelord captain planet villains, I just can't take much of it as seriously as they are trying to sell it to me. Easily the weakest element to this game. The side quests in finding spirits and stuff through your special vision were obnoxious too, especially since I couldn't walk while having it enabled forcing me to flash them on and off as I search the map. The campaign itself is pretty linear too, having progressed a huge way through the story with little to explore off the beaten path aside from your occasional spirit to gain points from.In short, don't expect a VtM: Bloodlines kind of experience with this one; but then again its probably the point. Werewolf should be expected to run different than being a vampire. That said, its not nearly as enjoyable with its atmosphere and characters as the former. Still fun though, even with its linear design. For the discount I got it at for ten bucks? Definitely worth picking up.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not Bloodlines. But you know what else it isn't? Heart of the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Forest. Ugh.I was told this game was disappointing as Hell, and even as a WoD snob, this game was actually surprisingly good. The traversal feels ridiculously smooth, and honestly, with the toggleable wolf/man form and the open-ended maps, I am BLOWN AWAY at just HOW smooth the moving around feels. Not only that, but the models actually do an impressive job of conforming to their footing (that is, feet actually stand on uneven ground like they're supposed to rather than floating a model or clipping through a texture). I know it's a weird thing to get hung up on, but it's seriously cool, and just, like, way more than I expect from AA Eurojank.What else is surprisingly fun is the combat, honestly. This game actually does a pretty solid job of emulating being a 10-foot-tall, 1-ton engine of destruction. It also does, for my money, the best demonstration of why Kindred are ♥♥♥♥ scared of the Garou. I know all the fluff and lore by heart, but really getting to see it shown off in a game that's trying to showcase the destructive potential of werewolves, I have to say: a Raging werewolf makes a Frenzied vampire look like a wet book of matches. I know the Griffith Park encounter, and I've played Redemption a few times, too; I know there have been WoD werewolves in games before, but not like this.<Switch from The Matrix>"Not like this."Dialog? Terrible. Models IN dialog? Terrible. Acting? Terrible. Writing? Terrible. Story? Negligible.Get it on sale ($10 or less), expect *nothing* from it, and just accept the little werewolf experience for what it is. I really didn't think I'd like this as much as I did. A very solid 7/10 AA game.

_childDocuments_.review: Werewolf: The Apocalypse – Earthblood – an Action-Adventure/Brawler, based on the Pen&Paper “Werewolf: The Apocalypse” (first published 1992), part of the “World of Darkness”.Before I start my review, two things up front: 1.	There are other reviews claiming that you instantly fail if you are caught during stealth. This is nonsense. Whoever claims this, has not played past the first mission, which is still part of the tutorial and the “don’t be caught”-mechanic is just relevant in the first half of that mission. After that you are mostly free to choose how you want to approach a situation: Stealth to take out as many enemies as possible before the bloody fighting starts or go in “Red in Tooth and Claw” right from the start.2.	The game developer, “cyanide studio”, is a rather small company and not a big shot with a huge amount of budget. So this is NOT an AAA-Game made by some huge studio and it is their first brawler game (other games by cyanide for example are “Call of Cthulhu” and “Styx: Master of Shadows”). So don’t expect top-notch-graphics by today’s standards and huge diversity in gameplay. This is a classic (some might even say “old-school”) Action-Adventure/Brawler-Game set in the World of Darkness. So keep that in mind.About the game: As a huge fan of the original Pen&Paper I was thrilled to hear that we would finally be getting a game based on “Werewolf: The Apocalypse” (there were two other attempts many years ago, both failed). Knowing it was a small studio and following the marketing and information about the game closely I checked my expectations concerning the graphics and focused on the gameplay and how the lore it was based on was treated.And I was NOT disappointed. I had a lot of fun playing the game, I enjoyed the story and characters, the stealth parts (although the AI could have been a bit more challenging), the ability to change between Human- and Wolf-form, but even more so the fighting style in the 9-feet-tall Crinos-form (the “warform” of the Garou). The animations and movements of the Werewolf- and Wolf-form are great and the setting, tone and music capture a lot of the atmosphere of the original Pen&Paper.*Maybe I should mention, that I bought it on Epic Games when it came out in February 2021 and played it various times before I decided to buy it here on steam a second time to support the developer*The story is fast paced and straightforward but decent and the depiction of the lore is mostly pretty accurate when it comes to the adaptation of the original source material. There are a lot of details that players of the Pen&Paper will recognize and it is clear to me, that the team of developers, though definitely limited by budget and time, truly love the RPG their game is based upon.That said, fans of “Werewolf: The Apocalypse” will indeed understand a lot more of the hints and details of the story and about what is going and why it is happening, than the average gamer. The developers present the quite complex lore of the Pen&Paper here in a more simplified way and let some aspects of it unmentioned, so anyone who is completely new to “Werewolf: The Apocalypse” won’t get “lore-bombed”. And they converted a usually pack-oriented RPG (Garou gather and fight in packs) into a straightforward single-player campaign.I recommend to every player: Talk to the important NPCs, and not just once but on several occasions. Gather as much information as you can, explore the hub areas and levels, look for spirits, read the documents and listen to the conversations of other characters. It pays of and you get a better understanding of the whole background of the story and feeling of the setting, which benefits especially those who don’t know the RPG. Is it a perfect game? No. Is it the Open World-I can choose my own character/breed/moon auspice/tribe-kind of game that many fans of the Pen&Paper wished for? No. Would I prefer if it would have been way bigger with a longer story, wider areas, more background and more lore? Absolutely. But it is a solid AA-game with a lot of passion for the source material, a fun hack-and-slash combat system and a great soundtrack. If you love Werewolves, Wolves or are a fan of “Werewolf: The Apocalypse” you should definitely give it a try.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game. I had it on my wishlist for months because the trailers for it looked good! The characters move like something out on an early 2000's game when developers were first getting their feet wet with 3D characters. Mouth movement doesn't match the dialogue, there was a lot of clipping in the mouth area, and creepily of all the characters had this blank stare that looked through the person they were talking to - if they looked at them at all. The pack leader had this distracting blue glow in his mouth.The pacing was terrible and confusing. The voice acting killed any distant hope of making the emotional scenes interesting. Instead, they are about as heart touching as a Monday morning conference call. I was really hoping for a hack and slash type of game where I could ignore the cliche plot and focus on massacring some corporate scumbags. Nope. The werewolf thing feels like it's supposed to be your handy dandy pocket knife rather than the .50-caliber rifle it should be. Instead you sneak through levels and use a piddly crossbow to take out enemies. Wow, exciting.jk. I'm sad. This game is sad. My wallet is sad.Thank you Steam for giving refunds so effortlessly.

_childDocuments_.review: I couldn't possibly not recommend this game.While vampire sympathizers have a myriad of titles to choose from, there is an undeniable drought of werewolf-focused narratives in the videogame industry.That said, having played until the very end, it's not as if I think Earthblood is anywhere near the concept of "perfect". A predictable storyline, subpar in-game cutscenes (nothing that lives up to the cinematic trailer), rigid animations in dialogue and overall repetitive gameplay add up to what you'd likely deem "mediocre".Despite all that, I believe this was an important step in bringing more attention to this otherwise underrepresented supernatural creature.I absolutely would buy a sequel.If more thought were to be put into the story to offer branching paths with consequences to Rage, a less linear world or levels design, and a greater range of skills to allow personal expression would make for a rather promising next iteration.My advice is to get this game if you're  into werewolves, the first couple of hours can be quite fun. On the other hand, if you're only mildly interested in the concept, wait for a good sale.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; Get it on saleWerewolf the Apocalypse: Earthblood is one of those games where most of what it offers is either mediocre or just a bad experience. However the combat does not fall in this category as in my eyes the team was able to convey the power and feeling of playing a Werewolf really well. The story is bland with no real attachment to any characters. You don't get to explore who anyone is, not even the main character Cahal. The only dialogue that comes up only involves 1 of 3 topics which is either, Endron is definitely the bad guy incase you somehow forgot,  , or  . You can also ask them to give you World of Darkness lore dumps. It's not that the characters shouldn't talk about this stuff or inform the player on the setting, it's the fact it's ALL they talk about besides the mission objective. I think just simply trying to explore characters emotions and motivations would have at least made this not such a big deal. Not to mention the story itself is very straightforward and is just meant to guide you from level to level. So the game doesn't have a compelling narrative, and it doesn't do a great job having you get attached to the cast. At most you get a decent idea on the Werewolf lore in the World of Darkness universe.You'll also notice real quickly that this game added stealth segments that are incredibly unrefined. When you move into a stealth segment, Cahal will automatically crouch. The stealth gameplay you get from mission 1 is what the rest of the game offers up to the end. Now if the levels had interesting design then maybe they could have salvaged this but this also suffers from the type of stealth design that ignores the puzzle-esc aspect those genres introduce. You are able to completely move passed guards without issue and can ignore whole segments within seconds if you wanted to. Not to mention it's even worse when the only advanced things guards can do is detect bodies (that you can't move at all). You then get to see how when alerted, most guards in the room will just casually walk to whatever location Cahal is hiding in if the ai knows that Cahal is currently in the room. The "stealth" doesn't need to be in this game, and luckily outside of the tutorial levels, it's optional and doesn't effect anything. However the action Werewolf combat is a full 180 from this.When Cahal get's caught or during designated segments he will transform into his Werewolf state. The first time I was able feel how the Werewolf is controlled, I was taken back by how well the dev team put it together. It's by no means innovative or a unique twist, it's just designed really well. You can earn new abilities with different purposes, you can (kinda) juggle enemies, and Cahal has stances that completely change how the flow of combat is going. The music being played and animations make it the icing on the cake for that Werewolf power fantasy. However like I said it's not innovative or a unique twist, if you play a lot of different action games then this won't surprise you in that regard. The only actual issue I have for combat is that stunning any enemy is extremely easy and removes any tension in boss segments or in areas with a high enemy count. However despite this, enemies that go down easy actually add more to the fantasy since you are able to pick them up and execute them while running by either tearing them apart, chewing their face off, or any other animation they have for this, with some enemies having unique executions. These executions are available for every enemy and boss with the only exception being a specific boss. If you also end a fight with an execution you get a cinematic view of what is happening to also add to the intensity. Honestly the ability to switch between a stance that makes Cahal fast and nimble with quick attacks that do little damage, or a Slow but tanky stance that does really high damage and more visceral moves. Not to mention both stances have unique abilities, specifically 2 that are only for that specific stance, one that works differently depending on the stance, and a healing ability. They also gave Cahal a rage that let's him have access to both stance"s benefits at once, and has a moveset that combines the best parts of both stance's basic attack strings, at the cost of being unable to use abilities. The combat has a great foundation and I would love to see this dev team just expand on what they already implemented. The only things that holds this game back is it's writing and odd choice of stealth gameplay.Overall the game is mediocre at worst and at best it's an enjoyable action game with a Werewolf flavor that can be really fun if it speaks to you. I would definitely recommend to only get this on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I am cautiously voting to not recommend this game, not because I don't think it's a fun game worth picking up on sale, but because it really does have a lot of quality-of-life issues that take away from what could've been a solid B-rated experience.I disagree with many of the really, really aggressively negative reviews (also people need to unclench, it's just a game). Definitely buy on sale so you don't feel cheated out of your money's worth. But yeah, little things like being able to move and have Umbra vision on at the same time would've been beneficial. Action was fun, you can tell most of the small budget was spent making sure your lupus and crinos forms felt slick and moved wonderfully. It's a shame that the budget wasn't greater or we could've gotten more detailed character models. The difference between how good the werewolf combat animations are and the awful NPC animations is palpable.There were little things too that I wish we could've seen more of, like the ability to interrogate people and flip out mid-conversation at a hair-trigger (if you so desired). But ultimately, if you're looking for stealth, there are far better stealth games out there. You want Splinter Cell, not WTA Earthblood.Finally, environments are lovely, and the Patron Spirits legitimately look incredible, but unfortunately for the first half of the game you're stuck repeating Endron HQ over... and over... and over. Take it for what it is: a low-budget rage-filled werewolf romp. 5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't have high regards for this one, because I believed all the big reviews and such when it came out. In a way, I can see their perspective, but Wowzers, I had a loooooot more fun with this than I thought I would. But some of that is because Earthblood was exactly what I was hoping for: a freaking WEREWOLF game! It's crime there's not more of these.Okay, I'm going to be absolutely blunt with you here. Are you looking for a good stealth game? Being able to ghost through levels without leaving a trace? One with interesting characters, dialogue choices, and heart-felt moments? Challenging minigames and puzzles to break up the main gameplay? Then move right past this game.Are you looking for a "Be The Monster" game? Something more akin to arcade and "Character Action"? Where you can just say "FISH THIS!" at nearly any point of the gameplay- even in the middle of dialogue circles, to 'Enrage The Beast' and rip and tear? Not to mention one that doesn't 'Scold you' or 'Give you the bad ending' for actually having some damn fun? That's Earthblood. That's this game.In the introduction, you are going to see why the reviews were quite poor. I swear that this game starts on its worst foot (or Paw) forwards; a few bugs, 'First-Take' voice acting, borderline 'bad' looking human models. Hell, I spotted someone T-posing and sliding in one of the cutscenes in the early game! It looks Rough, and again: I can see why the reviews didn't like it. The first hour is probably the worst.But I paid for the game so I kept going. Just taking it a few bites at a time, putting it down and returning to the game in a day or two; where the gameplay of just tearing through enemies didn't get tedious. Because of this, I had a lot of fun with Earthblood than probably a lot of other people did. The more I played the game, the less bugs I found, the less the voice acting and models annoyed me, the more I found the story appealing, and I still just found myself enjoying the game for what it was. People's reviews here are not "Wrong" or "Off". It just really depends on what kind of games you enjoy (and how you choose to consume your time with this one). This is a power fantasy, where humans are struggling to take your Lycan-self down and they're putting up quite the fight. It half reminds me of CARRION in a way, that "Monster Massacre" overpowered style. If you ever played Skyrim and loved the fact you could play as a Werewolf, and wanted an entire game based upon that: here it is. If that idea bores the fish out of you, you have your answer.

_childDocuments_.review: If this game still had mixed reviews I probably wouldn't have written a review. But at the time of writing this this game has mostly positive reviews, which I don't think it should have. It's not a bad game, and I did enjoy playing it but it is pretty mediocre on every point and if you do plan on playing this game you should go in with the right expectations.- The stealth is incredibly bare-bones, there isn't even a mechanic to hide bodies, enemy pathing is extremely basic. - The combat is serviceable and at times fun, the last two boss fights were challenging but the combat never really clicked for me.- enemy design is pretty lackluster for the first half of the game.- the story is pretty meh until the end, important deaths fail to have a proper impact- as far as I can tell dialogue options basically don't matter and there was only one choice in the entire game that had any impact on the story.- It's really short- the wolf form sometimes feels like an afterthought with the only thing it does is allow you to go into vents, even absorbing spirits transforms you back into a human.Again, this isn't a bad game, but it's not a good game either. There are so many aspects that could have been improved. The characters needed more time to be expanded upon, most of them are just sorta there. There's no character development. Cahal's whole story of giving into rage and going back to his Caern in their time of need goes nowhere.  He seemingly gets over his anger and sadness pretty much instantly when the moment passes. And again, stealth needed to be fleshed out. This game does not feel finished. I'm giving it a negative review because I know that with more time and effort this game could've been so much more than what we ultimately got.

_childDocuments_.review: Bought this at a sale long ago and decided to finally give it a go after running out of vtm games.I've seen a lot of reviews complaining about the graphics and they are indeed outdated for a game from 2021, but I've played games from the 90s so I can deal with it. Once I got into the game, I was surprised to find that this game was actually very fun. While the combat isn't my favourite, I did get a nice enough build towards the end. What I really enjoyed was the stealth portion and I'd reload the checkpoints quite a bit to get as far as I could without combat. One thing worth noting is that the studio did their homework with regards to the lore. While I had not played other wta games, I knew enough from reading to recognize most references down to even some of the background props mentioning pentex subsidiaries. It was quite refreshing to see them come to life in a game like this, even if it's far from perfect. I think my biggest complaint is probably split between the plot and the length of the game. _childDocuments_.review: Werewolf: The Apocalypse - Earthblood is a third-person game with light elements of RPG, stealth, and hack-and-slash. Set in the World of Darkness like Vampire: The Masquerade games, you play as Cahal, a werewolf who with his pack tries to stop Endron, an evil megacorporation from tainting the Earth which upsets the balance of nature. It might sound silly, but it actually works. You will travel to Endron's industrial areas and sabotage them.Gameplay-wise it's quite fun, you can sneak to avoid combat, or to slowly thin out the amount of enemies later. In werewolf form it plays like a hack-and-slash, chaining combos and it has a skill tree. Most levels can be stealthed through, but I don't feel it's a "complete" stealth since sometimes there are the big enemies which can't be stealth killed, and areas that where combat is necessary to progress. I recommend trying to stealth first as its more fun, but I do wish there was an option to stealth kill the big brutes or at least move dead bodies.My problem with this game is honestly the saving. It's checkpoint-only, and that kind of saving in a stealth game isn't really a good idea since you'd have to redo quite some more if you got detected. I know stealthing is not the only way, but it's my preference. And I experienced a bug trying to reload during a level change cutscene, it loaded me to a broken, locked-out version of a hub level in which I cannot progress or restart the level and must start a new game.Overall, I think Werewolf: The Apocalypse - Earthblood is a pretty okay third-person game, and if you're a fan of playing as fantasy creatures or the World of Darkness franchise you might want to give this title a try. Don't expect the same length and quality of their most popular title Vampire: The Masquerade Bloodlines though, but the setting might be able to scratch that itch.

_childDocuments_.review: I just want to say, I feel like werewolves do not get enough love in the videogame world, there is only a few games I know that you can even play as a bad ass werewolf. In my teen years I learned about Werewolf The Apocalypse and World of Darkness series paper and pen tabletop and I fell in love with the world, and loved the concept of the werewolf games. I was so happy to see that they made a videogame based on werewolf the apocalypse. I'm a little sad though that this was not the werewolf game I had hoped for. Id love to play a open world werewolf game where you build your character and choices matter, like a skyrim but with werewolf the apocalypse. If you are buying this game in hopes for the same thing you will be disappointed. That being said the game is not all bad ether. If you are not familiar with werewolf the apocalypse or any of the world of darkness this game gives you a little taste about the world.First of all, you play as Cahal, a badass werewolf. The combat is completely action based and honestly easy to abuse. There is a skill tree to upgrade your character a bit. Pretty environments. Overall it is a fun game if you like beat'em'ups.The downfall, the game is barely werewolf the apocalypse. It uses the concept but its a action beat'em'up first.Almost no reason to use stealth in this game. There is no reward for stealth killing enemies. Pretty much only reason to stealth is to ether A bypass whole rooms or B to sabotage the room to make the combat easier. Skill tree is lacking, although you can upgrade your combat abillities to help, there not very much reason to get anything else. You find spirits and huff them like a drug to upgade your skills in the skill tree which is a little weird. The pen and paper tabletop you had gifts which are basically powers, you had weapons, ect this game you get pretty much none of that. Like i said a beat'em'up.My biggest complaint is that the game has autosave and only autosave. If you reach a checkpoint, good chance your path backwards is blocked locking you from any spirits you could have found earlier. In fact I suggest going into the game knowing you will probably miss a lot of spirits along the way. Some are so well hidden that even with the spirit sense ability its hard to tell if there is a vent you missed or if its something you have to grab after a checkpoint. I just excepted that i was never going to get them all and just enjoyed the beat'em'up.Story is pretty meh. Dont expect a great story. Its predictable and just overall meh. The cut scene animations in this game are also very janky. Characters like to flail there arms around for no reason and seem a bit robotic in their animations.Overall the game id rank maybe a 6 or a 7 out of 10. Its not bad, but its not great ether. Very mediocre. However you play as a a big badass werewolf thought and thats pretty awesome. Id say if you love werewolves even if you never heard or played the tabletop, id still pick this title up but maybe wait for a sale first.

The werewolf combat wasn't super intuitive and took some getting used to, but it was sick as hell and had crazy metal playing the entire time. The story didn't grab me at first, it was pretty bland and predictable, but I found myself getting more and more invested as the game went on. It was super stupid and fun and exactly what I was looking for. If that sounds good to you, I would suggest picking it up, but for the masses? Steer clear.

_childDocuments_.review: Diseases? Curses? Forget everything you heard about the werewolf mythos for this is a different take on it.Earthblood is based on Werewolf: The Apocalypse series which are pen n' paper RPG's set in the World of Darkness universe, created by White Wolf and acquired by Paradox.In such universe the werewolves (or rather, the ) are born that way and can shapeshift at will between three forms: human, animal and in between. They are also one with the earth i.e. it's protectors and can also see, hear and speak with spirits (sometimes even travel to the spirit realm).In Earthblood you're in control of Cahal, a garou from the Fianna tribe (which were pretty much bards in times long past, but not anymore). Cahal and his brethren (among some regular humans) are fighting against those who taint the earth, an oil company called Endron (reminds you of something else?). And with all the environmental destruction also comes evil spirits to feed off of all the suffering and controversial experiments so you can probably picture how everything is ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up. It's a losing battle for the garou but they don't give up.The game is a nice mix of stealth and hack n' slash and it's conversation bits reminds me a lot of the modern Deus Ex's. It's soundtrack is 99,9% metal as ♥♥♥♥. Voice-acting and graphics are alright and the length is just fine (with the ability to choose between two paths, in the end of the story). You spend most of your time in enclosed areas (Endron's turfs) but there's also a forest, a desert and a prison, as levels. Never had any bugs nor glitches but the game crashed on me twice.Overall, though, I had a blast with it. Give it a try.

_childDocuments_.review: Before you buy.It's important to note that I bought this game with the impression that it is a story driven game. The game is marketed as such, or perhaps that is what I wanted from it.Werewolf: The Apocalypse - Earthblood is better described as a hack-and-slash game.The story is horrible, and it is a shame, because there was good potential. You are thrust into the game without much context and back story, the first mission is a horrible setup. Your wife dies by a an apparent antagonist because she was sent in on a solo mission, but you don't really care because there was no time spent to showcase her character or make you give a ♥♥♥♥ about her. And then they proceed to let you kill the werewolf/antagonist immediately after he killed her. He also doesn't have a backstory, his only purpose was to kill your wife for no reason and die???The main character also has no backstory other than being a father and a werewolf. No backstory of how he became such. The setup is horrible, the animations look like they came from 2005. The gameplay is mediocre and the graphics look good until you see it's just pretty textures. The soundtrack is cool but repetitive.I actually immediately stopped playing the game after the first mission. This game is a scam, the marketing is the only thing good about this product. Don't buy it, not even on special.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd only recommend this for fans of the franchise or werewolfs in general. Fights are nice and gameplay is ok overall, but very repetitive. One feels very powerful as a werewolf and that much is fine really, but aside from that, about all feels wrong. I'm 70% of the game done after 10 hours (says my save file) and I feel like I've only done 2 things in the game :1- walk in a room, (weaken the enemy with sabotage, optional) kill everyone there. Again, nice fight, but repetitive, and in small rooms the camera can really be annoying.2- walk around as a wolf (human moving is really slow and unsatisfying), hearing myself pant every 5 seconds, and activate "vision" to search for spirits. And there are...tons of them ! Think 10 to 20 per section of the game. Really mind numbing after the 50th time. It's a real shame because the ability to search was a great idea, because it makes the search easier than say looking online in a guide, so it helps reinforce the immersion ; the amount of spirits to find and their stupid locations sometimes really kill the vibe around it.Sneaking in is not really a gameplay element, first it doesn't work that well at all and anyway is slow and annoying, but also, you don't get xp to improve your skills by doing so, whereas killing everything in sight will give you xp.Story is very basic and expected so far. Acting and voices is good though, MC especially.I would NOT recommend at full price, even for a big fan. 8 to 10, ok for a fan, but more than 10 £/$/€ is a steal. Important to note that although graphics are ok, it is limited to 1920x1200, so if you play on a big screen, it'll look fairly meh.Progress is very linear. This feels very old school in it's approach. It's :-Main quest (corridor, room with enemies, repeat until mini-boss/boss, next objective)             -1 secondary quest at a time, that will only reward xp if you do, but won't change anything if you don't.Don't get me started on programming laziness, eg a dialogue that triggers each time you pass in a specific vent. So if you pass it back and forth X times, indeed, there is no "achieved" marker, and the same dialogue may in certain occasions trigger X times (big yellow fans, to quote only 1 occurrence).I'll finish the game now that I'm there, but had I know before, I wouldn't have started at all I think, and I used to play vampire/mage/werewolf RPGs, and I'm a big fan of the franchise.

_childDocuments_.review: Didn't expect much from the game, bought it as it looked like the first 'serious' WoD game focusing on werewolves, trailers were fine and was really cheap but unfortunately the gameplay gets boring really fast due to how repetitive it is. We often have two ways of pushing forward - brute force or stealth, while combat can be fun for a while I find stealth really bad, which is a surprise as I enjoyed both Styx games (created by Cyanide), limited paths to take, skills not changing much, dumb enemies, not rewarding. Everything felt really old school, room -> kill/sneak -> next room -> rinse and repeat for entire game pretty much.Graphics and audio are fine, music during combat/menu actually fits the game really nice, liked the main protagonist, most NPCs are shallow and if they tend to disappear/die, no one really cares. Will forget plot next week, side missions were also boring and pretty much copy paste (either find something or kill), everything takes about eight hours to beat.Bugs, yeah bugs, couple times I ended up in a wall or floor and had to restart from last checkpoint, but once, when I was mid game after completing a mission I ended up in a closed room I couldn't leave, there were no objectives, mission description was suggesting it's 2nd mission and guess what? Had to restart ENTIRE game thanks to absolutely horrible save system, which lets you only use last checkpoint or restart mission. For achievement hunters it might also ruin your playthrough, when let's say you were getting all the collectibles (spirits that are easily missable) but for some reason you noticed one just after some door that just got locked for good, solution? restart level or entire playthrought if it was a spirit in previous level -> top tier design.Concluding I'd recommend the game only for WoD fans AND on a high discount, otherwise don't bother.

_childDocuments_.review: For me, this game is ruined by way too many forced chaotic group battles and checkpoints that are insanely far apart. The stealth sections are quickly stopped down because you enter a room with too many guards all standing around facing directions that encourage you to morph into a werewolf and destroy everything. _childDocuments_.review: So this is quite an interesting one. Since I pretty much played all of the games that Cyanide Studios made so far (except the cycling ones), I'm familiar with what they do and how they do it. Their games are often a bit janky, often a bit rough around the edges, but you can always see what they intended to and that the effort is there. They are, to me at least, the definition of a AA developer. Werewolf: The Apocalypse - Earthblood (what a name...) is no different.This game would have definitely been awesome in 2009 or so. For a 2022 game though, it's a bit of a disappointment. The basics are all here: solid technical side, solid mechanics in terms of character development and, for the most part, gameplay. The latter consists of dialogue sections on one hand and the stealth-action parts on the other, and those last ones are the main problem for me here. I like stealth games and I love action games. Cyanide themselves made some very good stealth-action games with the Styx series. But Werewolf lacks the clear and clean design that Styx has: Styx is almost purely a stealth game because the main character can't fight very well, while in Werewolf you have the ability to transform into a very powerful beast form, so they couldn't do the all-out stealth approach here, obviously. They want you to use the werewolf form regularly - and they designed the levels accordingly. That means, that there are sections in the game where it's almost impossible to get through in a stealthy manner and you're pretty much forced to do action sequences. And they're not the strongest part of the game. They're pretty messy with the camera, and the controls are not as smooth as you would expect. Also, basically all of them are arena-based, so kill a certain number of enemies (which you can sort of control by sabotaging the enemy spawn points beforehand) and then go back into the stealth part. Rince and repeat. And this gameplay loop gets kinda old kinda fast. I would've much preferred if you indeed had the option to go pure stealth, but that doesn't seem to be there.Giving a recommendation here is really hard for me. I really do like much of the game. But I just can't get over the fact that the gameplay design is so forced and restrictive. And that's why I can't really redommend the game to other people.Similar games I would recommend instead, in no particular order: Alice Madness Returns, Styx: Master of Shadows, Darksiders II, The First Templar and maybe also A Plague Tale: Innocence. Most of them are quite a bit different to Werewolf, but I feel there's some overlap in terms of mechanics etc.

_childDocuments_.review: I played better and I played worse. The game has significant weaknesses but reminds me of similar old-school games I enjoyed a lot around the 2000-2010s. For the nostalgia alone, it get's a freepass for a lot of nonsense from me (like semi-ideal graphics, wonky mechanics etc). The story is based on a pen&paper game that emerged in the 90's, so if it feels like a 90's plot...it pretty much is. It can get a bit jumpy from time to time too, but it's coherent enough to know at all times what's going on.Problem is, it won't satisfy people who expect a lot more from a game that was released in 2022. It's not bad and you'll get your wolf action - just not the way you probably expect it. It's biggest crime is the lost potential in that regard imo. If you're a diehard werewolf fan and just want to smash enemies wolf-style, then it's definitely worth a try on a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I would give this a mixed review since the game has plenty of good and bad things about it, but overall I enjoyed it more so despite some of its flaws. If you are looking for a werewolf hack and slash game then this will fill that void nicely. On the other hand if you are a fan of World of Darkness looking for an RPG game then you may find the story lacking, predictable, and doesn't use a lot of mechanics from the core game.The story follows a garou pack with their never ending struggle against the corrupt human companies destroying earth. Thus aiding the Wyrm and harming Gaia and her spirits. As a warrior of Gaia, you must sneak into facilities and destroy these companies from the inside out while trying to save your pack. What I love the most about the game is that it lets you choose how you want to play. You can either sneak around, or brute force your way through each room. The later being a lot more fun and more effective to cleanse the Wyrm taint.Issues I had with the game was the way it saves onto one file. Once you hit a checkpoint it auto saves, meaning you cannot go back further unless you want to redo the entire chapter. Another issue is that it will lock you out of certain rooms and areas. So if you forgot to grab something too far back, you can't get it anymore. I didn't have much of an issue with the story other than it was super predictable with how it was going to end. I was able to figure out what was going to happen half way through the game.
