_childDocuments_.review: The idea is great, a Deus Ex style game with sneaky werewolves in the World of Darkness setting. It's got evil corporations, cool powers, a mix of stealth and action, etc. etc. If that sounds amazing to you, you might enjoy it despite its flaws.The problem is not just that the budget is low. Lots of "janky" AA games surpass their origins and offer great gameplay (Elex for example). However this low budget is paired with a general lack of quality development, leading to a game with no heart or great gameplay to match its jank. At the end of the day you get a simple, low rent version of the genre in a cool setting. Maybe that's enough for you. It was enough for me for 10 or so hours, before I ditched it.
_childDocuments_.name: Werewolf: The Apocalypse - Earthblood

_childDocuments_.review: There are good games, there are bad games and there is Werewolf Apocalypse Eathblood. A third person action game with stealth elements. Story: Story is you are a shape shifting werewolf who choices to abandon his pack and family after he goes wild on a mission and kills one of his own pack and after the death of his human wife.  He comes back five years to find his pack under attack by the same evil corporation that he was fighting against then. Now he must make amends by destroying the evil corporation. He must slaughter his way through endless waves of guard, mutant experiments, turrets and big robots from Aliens. The story is utterly terrible. Everything that happens is very predictable (With the exception of the ending which I'll get to in spoilers). Not only that but these characters have some pretty dreadful voice acting. The main character for example has the most monotone "What have a done? I've killed them" I've ever heard and its hilarious. There is an even better example later on when a character dies off screen and he says "No" in the same monotone voice and it's never brought up again that they died or were even involved in the story. Some of this dialog is so bad it honestly wouldn't sound out of place in Daymare: 1998 or Hunt Down The Freeman. VisualsThings don't get much better in the visual department.  Models and textures look like they come from a mid budget xbox 360 game. Many textures and blurry, lacking detail and look surprisingly dated. Not in the charming way like a throw back boomer shooter but rather that they just look old and cheap. There are sections of the maps which have these ugly dark patches through doors and in huts where the devs didn't have time to finish modelling these are super frequent given enemy's spawn in these dark areas when they attack you. The game also can become somewhat samey looking in areas with the same lab and industrial areas repeated over and over. What doesn't help is these areas also use a lot of premade assets which just makes it look generic.As for character models, it's a mixed bag. I actually think that the werewolf's look pretty decent. They might still have low res textures but the models actually look like werewolves and there are a few nice looking animations on both the full werewolf form and the normal wolf form. I also like how the spirit gods look. There are two in the game and the second one which looks a bit like a bird snake hybrid actually looks really cool design wise. However things take a massive downfall when we look at the human characters. These people are ugly with some very cursed faces and super robotic animations when they are talking. Ganeplay:Now as for game play that's where things get interesting. The combat is split into two types. Brawler and Stealth. The Brawler sections have you tearing through large groups of enemy's as a werewolf in two forms, Agile and Tank. Agile is faster and Tank is slower, more defensive and deals extra damage. You have ability's such as a leap which lets you get through the environment and pin down enemy's. You also have a dodge to avoid shotgun blasts which have a visual cool down. After you've done enough damage you can go into rage mode which makes you much faster and more aggressive. Combat is brainless and silly, but it is kind of fun. At least at first. I know it a basic system but tearing through enemy's as a werewolf is still satisfying, even if it's rough and I don't see any other games that let you do it. As for stealth however that's a another thing entirely. The game lets you switch between two forms, human and a normal wolf. In normal wolf form you are faster and can slide through little grates into vents. Once inside vents you go into first person like it's metal gear solid 1. In human form, you can climb over bits of the environment and take down enemy's. Sadly you often have to switch into human form to do anything relevant like taking down enemy's, interacting with PC's to open doors or switch off camera or do other things. Personally I'd have liked it if they had animations for the normal wolf doing guard take downs or smashing the controls. I know they could have done it because the wolf has some surprisingly good animations when sneaking around. For the first few missions if you fail stealth you get a game over, but later on if you get caught you just go into brawler mode to fight enemy's. Personally I avoided stealth because A: Why would I want to be human in a game that's sole selling point is playing as a werewolf and B: The stealth is awful. Enemy AI is super inconsistent. Sometimes it can't see you stood next to them and some times it's got perfect vision from through a solid object. There is also no way to drag or move body's after you knock someone out which often means you'll alert guards even if you are super careful. How such a basic feature of stealth is missing I have no idea. Plus there are even enemy's you can't stealthy take down like the big robots which you have to ether shoot with a crossbow three times or go werewolf on. Even the game seems to know it's stealth is bad because it forces you into combat in some rooms.You also have a skill tree which also lets you upgrade both for stealth and combat.  However here's my tip, ignore the entire stealth section. Outside of the ability to shoot cameras nothing here is worth the skill points and you'll be better off inventing in combat for the later bosses.Speaking of bosses, most of them are super easy. Go into tank mode and spam left click. Occasionally heal and use your rage mode and that's it. Most of the time you can out damage them. There was only one boss in the game this didn't work for and that was the two werewolfs you fight near the end. Even the final boss dies using this trick. At first I still liked the gameplay despite it's many flaws. Being a werewolf slashing apart evil guys is just so conceptually fun. However by the halfway point, that fun had faded. The game took like 10 hours to finish including most of the side quests but it runs out of any new ideas before the 5 hour mark. You'll be stuck fighting growing numbers of the same enemy's over and over and it eventually becomes tedious rather than fun. Speaking of side quests one of the literally broke on my in the second half and wouldn't let me finish it so unless you want the extra skill points don't bother.Spoilers: (Skip to conclusion if you want to avoid)This games ending is awful. After being dragged to four different locations to find you're daughter you are forced to kill her in this big monster form. Then you are given a choice, kill the annoying bad guy or save your friends. As far as I am aware this is the only choice in the game. I picked to save my friends which started a long wave of the same enemy's over and over until my friends got away. The bad guy left alive, my daughter dead and finally to twist the blade a cliff hanger of the corporation trying to group back together as if setting up for a second game. Perhaps If I had killed the guy it would have been different but to be dragged on for so long only to achieve literally nothing left a real sour taste in my mouth. Conclusion:When I first started playing Werewolf I actually still kind of liked it in a "So bad it's good" kind of way. I've often said I miss the older AA style of mid budget games with wacky and strange concepts that you won't see in other games and even if it was janky I was still exited to finally have one again. As the game progressed however the "So Bad It's Good" faded away into just being another bad game. Whilst the price I payed on sale might be fair it's still a very rough game that's carried by it's concept alone. The saddest part however is the fact this still might be the best werewolf game we've ever gotten. That alone is the real shame of this entire adventure. One day someone will finally give me that dream werewolf game, but for now this is all we have.

_childDocuments_.review: Werewolf: the Apocalypse – Earthblood manages to marry action and stealth in a manner where neither is slighted, but action is the real deal here. Werewolf Cahal returns to his Pack after five years of exile following a disastrous mission only to see they've gotten in deeper fighting an evil corporation out to endanger the world. Get ready to hunt for spirits throughout levels with magical vision in order to upgrade your skills, skulk around as a wolf and cause havoc in werewolf form once the alarm starts blaring. Story is there with all its “save the planet” glory, but it's the freedom to play your way that sold Earthblood to me. Even if you'll mostly fight similar enemies for a while and monotonous warehouses and office locales. Good pinky dip for the franchise and here's hoping for more.Compared to World of Darkness' better known vampire counterpart, Werewolf: the Apocalypse has flown under the radar as far as video games go. Now finally Werewolf: The Apocalypse – Earthblood gets to take center stage. There's a matter of tempering expectations first as Eartblood is not an RPG some were lead to believe, but rather action meets stealth. Was it worth the wait, though?It doesn't take long for disaster to strike our protagonist Cahal of the Fianna tribe as he loses his wife in a raid on an evil corporation called Endron. This results in him abandoning his own pack as well as his daughter, and going on a five year self-imposed exile after losing himself to Rage. Until he hears they, now operating with human activists, continued to fight the good fight and his daughter Aedana had stepped into her mother's former role – being an inside woman. Looking to redeem himself Cahal returns and if there's a chance he gets to avenge his wife all the better for it.In this setting werewolves, or Garou, fight to save the world at the behest of its very own spiritual representation called Gaia. This “saving” takes place in many shapes, but is primarily characterized by maintaining the balance between material and spiritual realms. In modern times this tends to effectively mean becoming eco-terrorists who fight polluting corporations, literally or otherwise seeing as everything has a spiritual equivalent in the realm of Umbra, acting under the auspice of less well-meaning spirits. These entities seek to unbalance the status quo for their own benefit all the while Garou serve as Gaia's warriors combating such incursions.There's a metric TON of lore to all of this and I've given you the cliff notes version which is more than Earthblood does because it aims to keep your focus grounded. This can be somewhat jarring as you get to interact with your pack's spiritual Totem spirit, for example, but still.What struck me as strange is just how minimal the experience you're getting here is. For example, Cahal's tribe? Game will barely even mention that unless you read the notes scattered about. That's not even getting into his character. He's a gruff and almost stoic type which seems to be at odds with Fianna image of warrior poets or loud braggarts, depending on who's answering. Characters themselves never really get much attention and it's fortunate that goes hand-in-hand with a likewise simple approach to story game has. There's two pillars to it: avenging those you cherish and saving the planet. It just so happens that, be it your hacker Kinfolk or Silver Talon pack leader, everyone can conveniently direct their anger at Endron. I did like how there were some attempts to ambiguity later on, but it's portrayed in such obvious manner you can immediately figure out something is wrong. Only people who may be fooled in this instance, ironically, are fans of the property who know about a certain anti-human tribe's ways.Enough waffling about the story bits because it's time to get into gameplay. This is where I got blindsided by how the game approaches action and stealth so they work perfectly together. You have three forms to work with, after all.Stealth in a game driven entirely by turning into Crinos aka hulking wolfman destroyer form dedicated to combat alone, which comes with its own Agile and Heavy stances, is tempered by the presence of Lupus form where you assume the shape of a regular wolf. Now that I think about it Cahal's human form is mainly there to press switches and talk to scant few other characters, it's the action and stealth ones pulling most of the weight. So how does an action game manage to integrate stealth without it feeling tacked on? Simple – by making stealth entirely optional, but beneficial to engage in all the while keeping the doors ajar enough so stealth can always escalate into action. I had a good laugh when the only mission where Cahal is seemingly set for a stealthy approach can just be hacked and slashed through leaving your contact wondering what you're going to do now. Protagonist answers he'll think of something.I wish Earthblood had more there to work with. For me it boiled down to “stealth became too cumbersome, combat became too annoying” as game kept throwing more obtuse level layouts and enemy compositions at you. Probably not helped by the fact you're largely confined to corridors with plenty of chest high walls to hide behind, cameras to avoid and fuse boxes to sabotage incoming reinforcements with. Reasoning behind why you would want to do SOME stealth has less to do with thinning out enemy ranks, as they'll send waves of reinforcements, and more with building up your Rage which lets you use special abilities. You can also generate it in combat, but why not prepare beforehand? Cahal can also use a crossbow to deal out damage and flasks to increase Rage, but I honestly never found much use for either. On normal difficulty cameras were never an issue because combat isn't really an issue to begin with. Sure, some enemies are trickier as silver damage can limit your max health until you upgrade your skills a bit, but nothing you can't work around with some dodges or target prioritization. I also wish an action game like this had more worthwhile bosses instead of couple I actually remember.Skills? Yes, I've saved the best or worst for last. Further enforcing the whole “play it your way” is the way in which progression via Spirit points isn't at all tied to how you play. You get some from mission completion, but 90% comes from tracking down vagrant spirits scattered throughout levels. This means regular backtracking throughout the level to find the ones you've missed with your Batman, errr, Umbra vision and Lupus form's detection upgrade should be the first one you buy. These points can then be spent on Tactical or Combat skills. Just keep something in mind – Earthblood doesn't feature level selection. Make sure you get them Spirits as you need them if you want to get ALL the skills by end game.In conclusion I can say game had me hooked enough to not only collect all the Spirits along the way, but also to replay the final mission to see both endings. Amusingly enough side missions ended up being the most frustrating aspect of a game that teaches you to rely on Umbra vision only to expect you can locate things without reliance on it. As far as soundtrack goes I cannot remember much, but sound effects were crunchy enough even with general lack of gore. I'd say they nailed the overall feeling of Werewolf: the Apocalypse down to how the game ends.

_childDocuments_.review: I probably would have really liked this about 10 or 15 years ago.  However it coming out in 2022 does make it feel very dated.   If I paid $30 for this in 2022 I would have been pretty pissed and much harsher in my criticisms.  I paid $3 in 2024 and think its money well spent.  If they were to develop a sequel and improve on it a lot then I would happily pay full price in the future.The game is fairly short and a lot of the gameplay is repetitive; however, I did have a lot of fun with it.  Imagine every stealth game you played, sometimes you fail the stealth section and think "ah screw it, im just gonna go loud and kill everyone."  That happens in this game except its to an absurd degree.  If you are a fan of the tabletop rpg World of Darkness setting and more specifically that of its Werewolf gameline then you kinda know what to expect from its story, its fairly straightforward and a little basic, but basic isn't necessarily bad.  If you are a newcomer then there will be a couple of headscratching moments where you don't know what is going on.  For example the Black Spiral Dancers, newcomers will probably be confused about why some wherewolves are working with the bad guys, but long time fans will understand.

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay: So this game tricks you into thinking its going to be a stealth game with some werewolf combat elements. The intro and the first mission force you to like stealth around and then shift gears into fighting hordes of enemies with potentially the best werewolf based combat in games. The contrast is hilarious because this game has the worst stealth game play in all of gaming In not sure if that is hyperbole. It may actually be the worst. THIS STUDIO MADE "Styx: Master of Shadows!?" Guess what though, the stealth game play inst just "optional." You flat out don't have to do it at all. You don't have to do it, and then fail to start fighting.  The second you're in a hostile area the game lets you "Press Q to Enrage" and yeah your basically playing a better version of the Venom portions of "Ultimate Spiderman" for the PS2. Some people might find it boring or repetitive, I am aware. I do wish there was more enemy variety, but I had a blast. Leveling up the skill tress and shifting between stances.  I love games like  "inFamous" "Marvel:Ultimate Alliance" "Batman: Arkham City" or "Spiderman:PS4" its fun to feel powerful, and enjoy your powers. This game does that. Seriously, your dodge and jumping animations have active hit boxes, so you can maintain juggling enemies and keep combos going by jumping or dodging into them. I think that's pretty cool! Reminds me of Devil may Cry kind of.Story: The story is cringe-worthy nonsense. Any story about werewolves where its not an infection but some bloodline nonsense will inevitably be trash and uninteresting. I'm sorry a bunch of grown adults referring to themselves as "pack" and "warriors of Gaia", is so lame and this games story takes itself seriously. The shear amount of times you will hear the words, "Wyrm," "Cairn," and "Gaia" used  un-ironically will make you want to stop. Now me personally I enjoyed the story because the way the dialogue is read in conjunction with the poorly animated cut scenes. I'm going to be honest in terms of story I think this game is "so bad its good." It actually made me laugh a few times, and I see that as a positive. Given the choice between laughing at something when its bad or rolling my eyes and groaning I'd choose the former.  Its all funnier when you realize they're using these very European folklore terms even the characters have odd Eurocentric names and this game takes place in the state of Colorado.Glitches and low quality areas: I'll start this section by saying I am aware this is not a full priced game. I do have to mention on one mission I loaded a checkpoint into a hard lock. I was stuck in an elevator and had to restart my mission progress to keep playing. I mentioned Arkham city earlier this game rips off the hit counter mechanic for how many consecutive hits your landing, doesn't do or mean anything. I was getting up past 100x hits as far as I can tell its just fluff. The lore stuff like the random readable pieces of paper and data logs? There is no Journal or anyway to read them later not that I cared that much but the whats the point though? All the cut-scenes are weird.. Also lots of re used animations and bosses. Oh and the games short witch is good and bad it doesn't over stay its welcome but I beat it in around 7 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Werewolf: The Apocalypse - Earthblood

_childDocuments_.review: If you're not dealing with lamentable voice-acting, a plot that's drier than the Caern of Southern Dakota, and cookie-cutter world hubs with meaningless side quests and no world-building, then you're dealing with janky combat, an AI whose sneak detection flip-flops between potato-brain and god-mode, a character that doesn't do what you tell him to, and glitches that prevent you from completing the combat encounter. If, by some miracle, you're not dealing with either of those, then you're sneaking through bland environments with seemingly random level design that are-- in some cases-- meant to force you to enter combat. The only redeemable quality of this game is the combat, which sucks because half the time, the combat is unrewarding, repetitive, and buggy.

_childDocuments_.review: You start the game with 15 minutes of lore dump via two cut scenes that doesn't tell you you could skip.Then, I got the crossbow and right clicking while covered blocked half my vision by clipping my camera into the object, so you can't really sneak/stealth behind obstacles intuitively. Breaks game immersion right off the get go.Another part that irked me was the voice acting. I usually don't really put too much attention to voice actors, but my god was it bad. Dude kills a packmate and goes "oh no what have i done" and I'm like, "not a very good job on the dub that's what you've done." I can't even find who did his voice on IMDB because Cahal isn't listed. I don't need you to be the best VA on the planet for every role, but I do need you to not make me question whether my 10 year old niece can do a better job than you.The initial lore dump was the worst part. The writer should have led with less fancy schmancy unexplained wyld/worm lore and more on Endron being an evil capitalist corporations that's hellbent on persecuting werewolves. I the player neither cared for the little girl nor the woman that died in the tutorial and nobody was memorable or stood out. Maybe there'll be a hook that catches my attention later, but you've already lost me if you can't convince me to like or care for your characters within the first couple minutes.I'd be excited to play this in maybe 2001. For a game released in 2022 by friggin' CYANIDE STUDIO this was a massive disappointment. Other games that Cyanide made include Styx: Master of Shadow and Shard of Darkness, both of which I loved. I had expected a similar experience for a stealth action game, but ultimately this game fell short whether it was the janky controls, the less than desirable voice acting, or the crawl-slow pace that it started off of. 20 minutes of this was all I could take. Praise steam refund.

_childDocuments_.review: I went into Werewolf Apocalypse Earthblood with no real high expectations. Most reviews already spot on said it all. If you're expecting a AAA game, this is not it. HOWEVER, that being said, I still had a lot of fun with it! For starters, it has the most wicked cool looking werewolves in it! I mean, heck.. it has WEREWOLVES in it. I am pretty sure, sadly, that this IS the only werewolf game out there. And for that, it's doing a fine job. The combat is wild and ferocious. The only thing that bugged the wolf outta me was, that quite often, the mouse wouldn't respond. Not enough so that it was a hindrance but rather, extremely annoying, especially in the heat of the battle. There are stealth aspects to this game. They are not greatly developed BUT they are there and do help thin out some of the enemies. Personally, as someone who sucks at stealth anyway, I very much appreciated that there were zero penalties for saying 'screw this' and going full Werewolf. The story was okay. Nothing fancy but interesting enough to keep you going throughout. All in all, it feels like it had excellent potential but got cut short. The graphics are mediocre, though the cinematics are pretty awesome! All in all - it's an enjoyable game. Not too long, but with so many huge, massive open world games out there, it's a nice little change of pace.

_childDocuments_.review: I would say that objectively, this is not a great game.  It's not great at stealth, and it's not great at combat.  The dialog choices aren't super interesting, and you can only play a male werewolf.  The story line is pretty meh and is all about eco-terrorists.  What does make this game great in my opinion is the lore.  The creators of this game paid very close attention into keeping the lore as close to Werewolf: The Apocalypse RPG as they could.  The Red Talons were perfect, having the wyrm and the formori were great.  It touched on the weaver, which was pretty cool.  Exploring the unchecked werewolf rage was good to see.  The downside to all of this is that none of this lore was explained well.  Some of it was in all the little text notes scattered about, but unless you actually know the RPG you're missing out on so much.All together, I would say this game is fun if you enjoy Werewolf: The Apocalypse RPG, just being a werewolf in general, or really like watching a werewolf put extra effort into keeping his eye patch when he shifts.  All the other werewolves don't keep their clothes when they shift, but  keeps his eye patch, like the boss he is.

_childDocuments_.review: I feel sorry for anyone who paid more than 20 €/$/£ for this game. The trailer sure made it look very cool, but beneath the surface this is a very mediocre game.The good stuff:- It has werewolves. How many games are there about werewolves? If you're a werewolf fan, you're probably going to get this and enjoy this game for that aspect alone. The wolves are very cool and shifting and fighting is decent enough.The bad stuff:- Sometimes the graphics look okay, but generally, they are very outdated. The werewolf looks cool, but all the facial animations are stiff and sometimes bugged and would have looked okay some 20 years ago. Your model clips through surfaces constantly and walking through a water puddle is like walking on ice, with no water effects whatsoever.- You get two places in between missions, a forest, and a desert, but otherwise all you do is sneak around and fight in these compounds that all look alike. It gets boring and repetitive really fast.- The AI is poor. It doesn't see you if you are in a different room (different 'area') and jumping up and down, but the moment you step inside the other room, they can spot you. These days I think players are used to pretty decent AI and actually needing to take care of not being noticed when sneaking around.- The plot is super generic and not very exciting. You get some conversation options but they don't really matter at all.- The voice acting is wooden. The guy voicing Cahal was okay, but otherwise the characters sound kind of amateurish.- The enemies are a few different kinds of soldiers, a few werewolves and Wyrm-infected soldiers. That's it.It's too bad this setting wasn't used more effectively. Get it if you are a werewolf fan and can get it cheap, but definitely don't bother with the extra content. It doesn't make your super mediocre experience any better and you'll just be wasting your money. This game is worth 10 eur at best.

_childDocuments_.review: It would be a good game on paper.A stealth and hack&slash game centered around werewolves and an extensive lore. The best part is that you can choose if you want to stealth the game or go all claws swinging. Unlike some people say, the game does not force stealth on you and you are not deadmeat if you fail to stealth until the end. You can just smash your way across the levels as a werewolf if you want. I loved this freedom. It meant I could spice up the levels by stealthing one part and just smashing in skulls in the next.It was great.Now onto the bad part. You knew it was coming.As I said before, it would be a good game on paper but sadly it does not work with the current glitches and issues it is having.1. Saving is a nightmare. There is no manual save and the game only, strictly only saves at checkpoints. So, if you do some side missions, collect some stuff before a main mission and die before reaching a checkpoint... good luck collecting all the spirits, reading all the notes, and redoing your side missions again.2. Stealth is a glitchy mess. If as a lupus your tail sticks out from the mesh of a cover, the enemy will spot you for some reason. If you stealth kill someone, the body might glitch out and go crazy. Like, falling through walls right onto the path of a patrolling enemy, or flies around the floor like possessed by a demon and alerts the entire level of its presence. Yes, both happened to me multiple times.3. I would have no issues with graphics if it was properly optimized. I mean, it looks like a game from 2010 but requires a PC from 2030 to run it without issues.The only reason I am even daring to give it a thumbs up is that I enjoyed the gameplay, despite these issues and gave a nice 20 hours of entertainment. Ignore the 1,5 hours, though. That was due to me redoing side missions and collectibles because of the terrible saving system.

_childDocuments_.review: I find the critics harsh on the game. It is not a masterpiece but it's another solid game by Cyanide. Forced stealth seems to be a big complaint but it is barely the first hour or so of the game, you have a good 7 hours of mayhem if you wish so after that. Closer to 5 hours if you put it on easy, ignore stealth at all beside the early mandatory part, and have some mindless destructive fun. Ironically enough, I think there are more encounters in the whole game that force combat than stealth. I'm not sure if it is bad game design or people having too short attention span, I'm pretty sure you can finish the "tutorial" in the 2 hour Steam refund period and actually see what the game really is.Voice acting is not awful but bland, graphics even on maximum are rough for 2022 and gameplay remind you of old PS2 action-rpg but it is what I expected controlling a fearsome werewolf. The skill tree is simple and does not offer game changing skills but it allow you to focus on your favorite playstyle. The game is quite linear, mission based with very few sidequests and while you can have a couple different way to explore the areas it's pretty much a series of rooms. Open or Semi-Open World would probably have been too much for Cyanide but it would have been great for this game.My knowledge of the Werewolf part of the World of Darkness is on the low side so I can't say how faithful it is but I enjoyed the nature and spirit lore. Plants and other natural trinkets being your source of experience is a fun idea and does not penalise stealth since combat does not give experience at all.The only reason I would not recommend this game is because of Nacon and the one year Epic exclusivity. The game itself is fine if you buy it on sale because it is a solid 7/10 for me but too short for the full price.

_childDocuments_.review: A really fun hack and slasher which lets you take on the role of a big, furry killing machine. The best bit about the game is the combat in which you turn into a monstrous werewolf and rip and tear your way through rooms of humans, mechs, and later on sort of demonic possessed people. The game does an amazing job of making you feel powerful. When you transform you'll send civilians (mostly scientists) fleeing in terror and becoming catatonic whilst you rend their allies limb from limb. By the end of the game I had improved my fighting stances so much that even bosses didn't stand much of a chance - especially with the levelled fury\rage mechanic that heals you as you fight.There's some very simplistic stealth mechanics, but don't expect to go through this game without fighting. Hell, some areas demand you kill everyone. I found the stealth fun at first, but it quickly just got in the way; though I did enjoy turning into a normal wolf a lot due to increased movement speed rather than being sneaky.You can't do much in your human form, but you're constantly shifting back into it to talk on your radio, open doors, and collect spirits and stuff to gain spirit points so as to improve your abilities. Oh, you do have a crossbow, but I didn't use it after the first few missions, I enjoyed just going loud. lol.There's also some very, very minor RPG elements, but you'll have levelled up everything you wanted long before the game has ended. Story is kinda crappy and predictable. You are Cahal, a werewolf fighting for Gaia against cartoonishly evil mega-corporations. You could take this story, hell the whole werewolf setting, and put it into a cyberpunk world and nothing will have been lost. Cahal is a man doomed to play out a predictable story in which the events of the past happen again as he wages his nature themed cyberpunk anti-corpo campaign of terror. Be prepared to be hit over the head with themes of "mankind is bad!" and "businesses are so evil, guys!" and for it to really go no deeper than that because in the end they're all serving some evil apocalyptic entity named the Wyrm. Not too familiar with the source material so I have no clue if the themes in that are this shallow and silly; only played Vampire and Demon myself.Anyway, if you can pick it up during a sale and, like me, like the idea of rampaging around as a nigh unstoppable killing machine, then check this game out. I got it for roughly £2.50 during a sale. Game really isn't worth full price, in my opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: If you were to ask me what my favorite game was before I played this game, I would've been torn between half a dozen games I love to death. If you put a gun to my head, I would've reluctantly said Kingdoms of Amalur. Having finished my first play through of Werewolf: The Apocalypse Earthblood, I can now say without any hesitation or doubt this my favorite game I have ever played. If there isn't a sequel, I expect it will remain my favorite game for the rest of my life. I have only two complaints: first, there was a little bit of jank with a few side quests (you could complete the objectives on a few before picking up the quest and you would be locked out of completing it.) Second, I NEED MORE! Let me put it this way: if I won the lottery, I'd spend millions funding a sequel. From start to finish, I loved everything about this game! I love World of Darkness, and for me this was a wonderfully faithful and creative adaptation. Reading some of the other reviews, I genuinely don't understand what people are upset about. I think a lot of people expected something like Vampire: the Masquerade Bloodlines. That would've been incredibly awesome without a doubt, but I love the path this game took just as much, which is really saying something! Or maybe it's plagued by the expectations tabletop players went in with. Whatever the case, the negative reviews leave me absolutely baffled--it feels like other people played a different game than I did.Seriously, I could write a dang novel on everything I love about this game. It brought me joy unlike any other game, including Kingdoms of Amalur! It kept me on the edge of my seat. The villains made me furious. It made me laugh, it made me cry. The characters are fantastic. The designs are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ AMAZING! The environments are breathtaking--and heartbreaking. The themes and story are both a really cool concept to play out in World of Darkness, and a depressing portrait of our real world. But the best part is, at least in this world, you get to fight back! Seriously, it's cathartic ripping those corporate goons apart! In an effort to keep this a length people might actually read, let me conclude by saying this: this game is truly unique, and I really mean unique. Sure, there are other games that are similar, and yes, a lot of the game play mechanics have been done before, but at the end of the day nothing does what this game does. It provides you an experience you cannot get anywhere else. Again, there are a lot of games out there that are similar, but what this provides really is truly unique. Everything just feels so GOOD! This game is not just a great time, it's a work of art!

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know what people have a problem with with this game, really.I do wonder if it's insecurities, I mean... Cahal is a kickass Irish bard with feelings who could rip you a new one regardless, and he's putning around the usual sorts of men with guns that gamers play as. So this is something I can't ignore. They just can't deal with a tree-hugging furry punting around white, gun-totating dudebros like ragdolls.I, on the other hand, love it. I also like that instead of being some kind of greedy psychopath who's doing things for loot under the flimsiest of jutifications, I'm taking down a fossil fuel corporation. I can imagine that makes some uncomfortable too, but I bloody dig it.The characters are a delight, Yfen I could just listen to reading a dictionary (his voice-actor was also responsible for Legion in Mass Effect), and while the voicework is very... European? I wouldn't call it bad, it's just more emotional than your usual AAA(A?) American fare. I'm a fan, I like it.Running around as a wolf is a delight, the animations are well done and it's fluid. Wolves are a liquid. I mean, perhaps not as much as they are in Wolfwalkers but Cahal's woofly form is still quite fluid and a delight to just bound and parkour around with. Being open to new experiences and not wanting the same pasteurised, homogenised mush fed to me all the time, I enjoy movement as a wolf. I wish there were more games that allowed us to utilise different body types beyond the obviously familiar.There are lots of neat little things, like snooping around for computers, notes, secrets, and hidden spirits, but the star of the show be crinos form. The werewolf! It's a really enjoyable brawler. I come from an oldschool background and sometimes I just like a video game that's a video game, rather than a "play to earn" grindfest with MTs and the exuberant and multitudinous forms of exploitation that work their way into so many mainstream games these days.The brawler is just... fun. You know, fun. We used to have that, before everyone got brainwashed to think that games are jobs. It's a blast just bounding around the battlefield and the levelled-up crinos heavy form is one heck of a power fantasy, the catharsis is real.I don't mind the writing either. It's very cheesy '90s action film with a very left-leaning intent and I kind of dig it. It's kind of like those gun films but if you were a tree-hugging werewolf rather than a fascist cop with a machinegun. So I really dig that, actually? Plus, Cahal has real dad energies and I like that he actually cares about things. As I'd already mentioned, so many "heroes" in modern video games are just gormless and unempathetic psychopaths who care only for their own gains.It's just... It's refreshing. You'll either love it or you'll hate it. If you just want to be a consumer who consumes more of the same, you'll be very alienated and possibly even upset, confused, and disquieted by Earthblood. I mean, look, let me sum it up this way...Would you rather...a.) Be a musclebound, psychopathic barbarian in a fantasy setting, murdering likely innocent orcs for their loot and making flimsy essentialist justifications for your actions;b.) Be a faceless white soldierboy with a gun, working for some kind of fascist institution or other, murdering people without ever wondering why you're doing it—but you obey anyway because that's what you do;or...c.) Be a tree-hugging, Irish dadwolf who's tearing up a fossil fuel corporation and hunting down evil execs to try and do whatever he's able to to protect the wild?How you answer that will really tell you whether you'll like Earthblood or not. It's very left-leaning, it's very cheesy, it's unusual, and it's a bloody delight. It isn't every day that something like this comes along, it isn'f for everyone, it's janky (the best games are), and it doesn't have the soulless polish of the AAA(A) sludgy gruel that makes up the gaming diet of so many buuuut... It's unique, it's actually fun, and y'know what? I like it! I do. It's pretty great.It's actually nice being a real good guy for once who does something about an actual evil. Plus, that dadwolf swagger. The heavy stance of the crinos form is so hilarious to me, I love it. It's also rad that the hero is a left-wing old fellah, rather than the fetishisation of youth that happens too often in video games. That's a European developer for you, though. Appreciably progressive.

_childDocuments_.review: Werewolf the apocalypse is a hidden gem of a game I’d argue that the game is even underrated I’ll go ahead and break down what I liked and disliked about this game please note I will not be spoiling anything during my review!#Story issuesIf you are coming into this game with the mindset that this game is going to have a complex and ground breaking story then you are not going to enjoy this game for that aspect because the story never really allows you to connect with any of the characters emotionally in the story meaning you will meet a character the character dies and you just don't feel sad that the character died because the game never really allowed you to form a connection with any of the characters. I definitely would have liked if the game provided backstory about Cahal as when you first boot the game up it feels like the game just started you in the middle of the game not the beginning as the game doesn't give me a reason to care for any character which sucks as you will see many scenes where you think i should be sad for this character however why am i not feeling sad and it all goes back to the game failing to give you a reason to feel invested and connected with any of the characters. #Graphics/glitches/AiThe game definitely could have used a little polishing when it came down to the Graphics now the graphics are pretty good however I feel that the graphics could have been a lot better as character models aren’t amazing looking in this game especially that one character model of the business suit dude near the beginning of the game his head model low key looked like clay. Some objects don’t have any collusion so you can phase your character through the object.The AI could have been improved as the AI feel like robots instead of dynamic humans walking around during the sneaking sections. I hope the devs update the AI as it's very bare bones when it comes to the stealth sections as the AI will either stand in one spot forever or a AI will walk around in circles forever which kinda breaks immersion for me seeing how limited the AI was during stealth.#GameplayThe game play is very smooth and responsive i would hands down have to say the gameplay is very good this is the part of the game where it shines the most you are sadly limited to a bow as your primary weapon as a human however you can choose to switch between human and lupin at any time both lupin and human offer a good mix up of gameplay/tatics. However the best form is of course the Werewolf when you play as the werewolf you can feel the weight behind the werewolf movement and attacks you can upgrade the Werewolfs abilities via the perk tree in the main menu however in order to do so you will have to collect spirit points from smelling plants that you will bump into randomly during your journey to beat this amazing game!!!#Game pretending that your choices matter.One slightly annoying thing that this game does many times is it makes you think that if you pick the wrong option that your actions have consequences but in reality your choices really don't matter like at all when it comes to how you answer back via the wheel of options i would have liked if my choices did matter and had weight behind them. The only time that your actions have weight behind them is when you get to the end of the game where you have to choose between two options which is a shame. Furthermore i found the dialogue wheel text to be a little confusing as you don't know exactly what cahal will say basically we have the fallout 4 dialogue issue in the game sadly i would have liked more context when it came to choosing the dialogue options from the wheel.#Conclusion But with all that said I don’t regret buying Werewolf the Apocalypse Because I bought the game for 1 reason and that was to play as a werewolf and slaughter human beings in the game and it’s very enjoyable. If you don’t have a love for werewolves or don’t like fast pace combat then I wouldn’t recommend this game to you however if you like werewolves and enjoy the fast pace combat then I would 900% recommend this game to you definitely go and get this game during a sale or even buy it at full price even with the issues I listed above they don’t take away from the overall experience of just slashing people apart as the werewolf every level was fun and I can see myself replaying this game a lot. I give werewolf the apocalypse a solid 10/10 for it’s amazing werewolf role playing experience you feel powerful and plus the werewolf model is THICC.Game of the year for me for 2022

_childDocuments_.review: "The game literally makes you feel the exaggerated swagger of a garou treehugger."Game is alright. If you love Werewolf: The Apocalypse and the World of Darkness tabletop RPGs, I recommend getting it (preferably on sale like I did).Gameplay is pretty basic. You've got a basic skill tree with two path Tactical and Combat. Tactical handles all your stealth based elements and Combat handles when you have to go OwO mode and giving everyone "a little looksie here" by tearing their guts out.Combat has two stances, one fast and one strength. Fast lets you pull off, well, quick but low damage combos and you move really fast with the trade off being you're weaker to damage. Strength lets you tank hits and deal massive damage with the trade off being your movement is slow. You have a frenzy mode that let's you go ballistic and deal massive damage in either mode that you can upgrade to make you stronger.Stealth is pretty basic and all of it is auto-crouch in certain areas to stealth and you can either find a gap in enemy patrols or take them out with headshots from you crossbow or do stealth takedowns when no one's looking.You can also turn into a normal wolf for more stealth shenanigans but you can't operate technology, but you can auto turn back into your human form when you interact with doors, do takedowns or need to aim your crossbow.This was an Epic Game Store Exclusive for a year and it's now on Steam. Having seen a lot of the reviews in that time, most people act like this is the worst thing ever, when there's honestly worse games out there. It's a pretty basic stealth/action-rpg game that is set in one of the World of Darkness TTRPG games.Really I would recommend this to fans of the games who don't expect this to be some high-budget AAA experience and see it as an indie game with pretty bare-bones, but serviceable gameplay, graphics befitting of an early 2010's Xbox LIVE Arcade game, are not expecting some deep philosophical "we are the real monsters" storyline or whatever mumbo jumbo.7/10 I want a werewolf mommy GF or whatever review score is popular with game journos these days.

_childDocuments_.review: Werewolf: Earthblood is a straight up 7/10. It's absolutely a good game, I enjoyed my time with it and I'd probably watch for a sequel. That said, its worth explicitly saying it's not a great game nor is it must play.Werewolf is best described as a modern beat-em up. You'll enter rooms, slaughter everything that moves and then move to the next room. You've got 3 combat stances (Heavy, Quick, and Frenzy) that each have their own combos and special moves. Depth is added with things like avoidable telegraphed heavy attacks, silver that reduces max health, and a decent assortment of enemies with unique behaviors. I also want to specifically call out the bosses as a high point. The first werewolf I fought amazed me and I can honestly say that to the end... they stayed enjoyable. They could have used more variety and the camera absolutely didn't always play nice... but they were good.So, the combat is very well done. Everything else... was not. The save system is literal garbage saving automatically after key events or at a random intervals. This means that it'll save before long, slow conversations... on the wrong side of the map... before elevator rides... 50% of the time after a hard combat... and basically never in the "open world" quest.  I can't tell you how many times I needed to talk to an NPC multiple times or pick up the same collectables because the checkpoints are awful.The stealth was an early frustration until I realized it's intentionally broken and that you are expected to fail most rooms. Instead, its used as a way to weaken the upcoming battle by either taking out key targets or sabotaging reinforcement points. Ultimately, the stealth is barely functional and things became more fun when I accepted that it's just letting me start the combat rather than avoiding it.And as mentioned before... the "open world" sections and "side quests" actively hurt the experience. Half of these involve tracking down invisible spirits in decent sized bland earth mazes or fighting waves of scattered foes. The open-world itself isn't bad, but the rest of the game isn't compatible with it... saving in particular.I can honestly say I enjoyed my time with Werewolf despite frustrations and jank, but I do recommend playing it on an easier difficulty. It was a blast on hard, but the risk of death and balanced enemies put a focus on the problems with Stealth, Camera movements, animation bugs, janky controls, saving, etc. It's definitely worth a sale price so long as you keep your expectations in the right place.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has received a lot of mixed reviews, but having played it more than most I would personally say that it is very much an enjoyable game, although at times a bit confusing, simple and unpolished. It's kind of an odd experience in how some things are very well polished while others are rough and a bit confusing. I'm guessing the devs had somewhat limited resources and decided (appropriately) to prioritise the important aspects of the game.+ Very faithful to the source material+ I liked the fast-paced combat in werewolf form, it's very satisfying.+ Most gameplay elements are very smooth, especially the combat, stealth works fairly well, most forms of movement are solid and fluid and look very good.+ Solid performance overall, pretty much free from bugs beyond the occasional NPC getting stuck.+ Good design for creatures and most environments.+ Much more depth than most people realise, decent bit of lore and conversations to be had with NPCs.+ I liked that this game isn't afraid to go all in with the player being a literal eco-terrorist, while still being fairly believable. Some people have reportedly found the story underwhelming but I thought it was pretty decent and very much appropriate for the setting.- Some acting / dialogue is very wooden, especially from unnamed NPCs and earlier on in the game.- Very little information / guidance to find non-main objectives. The game has a lot of side objectives and 'collectibles' that allow upgrading your abilities, but it doesn't really explain these very well and finding them is way harder than it should be.- Gameplay can get somewhat repetitive. It worked for me because I very much enjoyed the gameplay overall, but if you don't enjoy the combat and stealth as it is you're likely to get bored.- I'd love to have seen the game be even more violent, since that's a pretty strong focus. More gore would have accentuated the otherwise wonderfully brutal experience.- Some character designs, especially for friendly NPCs looks sort of bland and like they're probably stock assets.- Facial animations (esp. outside of cutscenes) aren't great.- Lore can be somewhat confusing to those with no prior knowledge of World of Darkness.- Kind of short. Most players clock around 10 hrs, though I managed to rack up 30. This was mostly from re-playing the start several times as I realised I would need a guide to find the 'collectibles' and side objective, which also made the game take longer for me.Overall, I liked this game. The gameplay loop is pretty simple but there are remarkably many abilities and moves to keep it interesting for the duration of the game. The story was also alright in my opinion. Nothing award-worthy but perfectly alright and above all else, both fitting for the theme and very much faithful to the franchise, so anyone who likes the source material will likely enjoy the story too.The biggest issue with this game is how tricky it is to find a lot of the side objectives and various pieces of lore and experience bonuses scattered around the world. These do add a more depth both to the story and gameplay, but since they're just oddly hard to locate I think the game suffers from the fact that most players won't find them on their own. The game really should make these things more obvious, be that showing them on the hud, a map or just making them visible in "spirit vision" mode.The only other issue I had is minor odd design choices such as requiring to shift from wolf to human every time I open a door, and some less polished elements, particularly the look and voice acting of allied NPCs. Everything else is a fairly solid indie game experience in my opinion.Overall I'd say the game is definitely worth it for someone who likes World of Darkness, werewolves in general, or thinks the combat system and overall gameplay loop looks fun. It's not a perfect game, but damn if it isn't enjoyable.

_childDocuments_.review: Ah yes, the very first game from White Wolf's Werewolf content. While detractors will keep talking mad nonsense about "muh graphics, looks bad, not as good as X or Y", I'll go beyond these pitiful and superficial details. Graphics may be important, but if you're playing a game just so you can cry like a little girl about textures, then you better go watch porn and jerk off to some dude's shaft. Bunch of degenerate wankers.The story is on-point with the World of Darkness lore and the Werewolf world, the spirits have their good designs based on nature, and it screams supernatural when I see Yfen, a gigantic humanoid creature with a head made of tree branches and a white void of air, or Pachu'a and its multilayered skull, bones and wings, representing animals from the Nevada desert. The werewolves themselves have great designs, not only in Crinos form, but in human form, giving their personalities and "ways to fit in" pretty well. The combat? Such a delicious power trip I have never felt before playing any other game involving werewolves (this being the ONLY one I can remember of, Altered Beast for the PS2): you run, you slash, you bite, you slam, you break, rip and tear, you howl and roar, you bleed and make bleed, all attuned with a banger soundtrack by the incredible band Alien Weaponry, the absolute tribal beast killing machine mood that I have yearned for so long...I do hope to see a sequel of this, because Cahal still has scores to settle with Wadkins and Pentex.

_childDocuments_.review: This is another game that seems to struggle with identity, plot, and pacing. (I played this on the hardest difficulty). In this game of Lovecraftian-Ecoterrorism, you are shown fairly early just how little the voice actors cared about the scripts they were reading. You are delighted to know that an apparently-successful Ecoterrorist organisation has the same cognitive dissidence as the Lovecraftian Megacorp they are fighting against.Starting out with the tutorial/prologue, you are pushed to do things stealthily. Instant failure states, complex vision puzzles and a low amount of ranged take-downs and later to be followed up by a significant lack of punishment for failing. The number of stealth abilities is lacking, with the best making you harder to see in wolf form. Now if only the protagonist Cahal could find a way to take someone down with wolf-teeth. Instead, every time you perform an action that isn't 'look around in red vision' or effectively walking around, you will be forced out of wolf form so that human can perform a lethal attack. In addition, there is a 'civilian' status on some enemies that only serves to point out that EVERYONE should die, because these guys effectively act as alarms with a neat achievement attached. An achievement I assure you, that I have no interest in acquiring.I get that an employee might sound the alarm on someone in their area, but most work places don't mandate EVERYONE to have a radio, The actual security personnel, sure, but Dave and Cindy who are scientist no doubt under a strict company leash are probably not even going to be allowed cell phones in their Corporate Black Ops site job, but hey, here they are being given a radio.Making this worse, there is a function in the game's stealth department that just doesn't work. You are TOLD that breaking certain monster-boxes- I mean security panels, that you will stop people from spawning at them when you inevitably are either forced to fight, or just get caught by intern Lisa. The problem is, even if you hit ALL OF THEM, you will notice that those doors will still have plenty of monsters to spawn - I mean armed employees standing just on the other side of them.One last thing about stealth is the large enemies. In many cases you HAVE to kill them. The problem, you can't take them out outside of combat. So yeah, have fun with that.If the game's oil-platform level has done anything, it's reinforce just how little the Devs know about pacing a fight to make it interesting. What ever happened to the rule of 3? Or 5? Or a time limit or progression bar or something? When the only thing that is a threat to your werewolf character is an army consisting of dozens of convict-experiment-private-military-security group(?) with explosives and mech suits and immunity to friendly fire... well, simple to say, it is more frustrating to be killed towards the end of a no-checkpoint grind-fest than it is compelling. I asked for a challenge when I selected my difficulty, not a grind. Cut the fight after the 2 mechs fight and die side-by-side. Or better yet, just give a heads-up as to how many more I might have to kill.Effectively, you have two stances. One is where you're speedy and should be able to dodge around easily, but you hit like a wet noodle. The other is strong an sturdy, but you hit like an absolute truck. Technically there is a third mode with his just both merged together, but with none of the abilities of the other two. So far, makes sense.The problem with combat is that dodging in agile form is passable, but the flash-step of powerhouse mode really can't get you out of anything. If power-mode had a block instead, it would make a lot of fights less annoying. Another problem with combat is that it almost always feels like a test to see if you can survive long enough to go Frenzy-mode, at which point you hope that everything is dead enough that you aren't going to need to do it again.The game shows you a hit-streak, but with no score-attack or bonus beyond maybe an achievement, it serves no purpose. In addition, there are times where you can try to dodge, but thanks to the enemy having somehow occupied the same space as you, you can't. Oh, and the numerous times late-game when you can be chain-stunned because dodge has no priorities, only some of your other skills do.Perhaps the one thing that I actually like in the game is the dialogue, when it happens, and I'm not talking about the plot. About 5-10 times in the game, you will be given an opportunity to talk with one of your enemies. Half of the time, this is while you're pretending to be human, other times it serves as exposition dump. But, while it is an exposition dump, it gives you an actual choice that might cause you to get angry. Get angry enough, and you hulk-out and start combat. It seems to be leftover from when the team thought they were actually making a stealth game.Sadly, that's not really enough to make the game good. And the story doesn't help either.SPOILERS!?As stated earlier, you are Cahal, who lives in Washington State Park with the rest of your Eco-Terrorist werewolf family. Your clan is full of idiots with talents and magical teleportation abilities that only enter into the story once and never gets resolved. Your pack sends your wife into a site of the company she has already infiltrated a while back. You are uneasy about it, but don't worry, backup won't be necessary, as it's a myth that a corporation might have more than one brain cell.Needless to say, the company does have more than one brain cell, (as opposed to those it hires) and your wife ends up getting killed by a werewolf of the enemy faction. You fight werewolf, kill it, give into rage, maul your brother-in-law and kill you teleporting wolf friend who are there now,... in the facility... when just moments before, they were outside...Plot holes aside, you go into exile. After five years in which your daughter gives into Angst and Ecoterrorism and rebels against being a werewolf (which she is? I don't know, it was never concluded as to whether or not she was actually capable of becoming a wolf). You return after mauling to death an arms dealer who thought he could take a werewolf standing two feet from his face.Stupidity aside (for now), you venture home to stop a small skirmish involving guns, a mech, ecoterrorists, and werewolves. You are welcomed back tentatively, so long as you go on a rampages to save the forest which I am reasonably sure is under government protection...Once several sites worth of para-military murder and aiding a large spirit-tree guy, your daughter proves just how like her mother she is. Only this time, it is EXACTLY THE SAME. I mean sure, she gets experimented on before dying at the hands of a werewolf (you! Getting all kinds of family murder in this game). On the way, you kill a girl in a mech that doesn't have more than two brain cells (but she had two!), then your brother-in-law, oh and a guardian spirit.At the moment, I don't know how it ends, but I suspect I will soon. After I get by the monster-boxes. All I can say for sure is regardless of how it ends, the story is dull. The devs just don't make you care about anyone. I mean, Cahal clearly cares about the people present, but I don't. His wife didn't get much build-up, his daughter didn't get much build-up, his hacker... cousin? Well whatever she is, she has a character, but not much personality. And that's the real problem. You don't really get to know anyone. They're all cardboard cutouts of characters. Your daughter is pissed at you for leaving and then... well, not much, you talk with her briefly before she goes on her suicide mission.If you want me to care about someone, or multiple someones in a game, show me something about them. Without personality, this is just a really bland hack-and-slash that wanted to be a stealth game or a spectacle fighter, but gave up half-way through either.

_childDocuments_.review: While I can see some other people's comments about the voice acting being a LITTLE rough in spots and the graphics for the talking scenes being a little last generation graphics (not the cinematics though), this was still a very good game, and I would recommend it to my friends. I have been waiting 20 years for them to finally come out with a Werewolf: Apocalypse game, and I'm thrilled with what I got here. The gameplay was simply designed but direct, and it didn't take a huge learning curve to get the hang of either slinking around in shadows or running great distances as a wolf, or just going brutal on hordes of enemies as Crinos. Limiting the number of forms from 5 down to 3 is a little sad, but totally understandable for a gameplay and programming perspective, and all the really important forms are there for situational needs. While I was hoping that the game that came out for Werewolf would be a little more RPG grounded (character creation, birth form, auspice, etc.), I am thrilled with this game and do not regret purchasing it. my only regret is that I didn't realize it had been made until last week. :)

_childDocuments_.review: When I saw the trailers for this game, the only way I could describe my hype for this type of game was indescribably high. Go into an area, sneak around and tear everything to pieces; it seemed like everything I could've wanted. Having the multiple forms of the Lupus and the Crinos seemed like such a blessing to me, but the most joy I got out of this game was jumping up and down as the Lupus.Instead, all I got was a clunky 2010-2015 game with horrible graphics, worse controls, inputs from my mouse that wouldn't register so I would have to either get hits in or stealth kills by the skin of my teeth, stale protagonist and voice acting, and combat that devolved into me spamming one ability to build up Frenzy just to get through that portion of the game.The game was clunky all throughout, but I could manage it in the first half. It just seemed to be a pretty standard stealth-action game with some jank that I could get through.Then the Wyrm enemies came in.I found myself groaning in frustration when each fight gave each enemy two health bars, losing interest in the game when I found that I just simply couldn't do a full stealth playthrough because you can't takedown the bigger grunts without alerting the entire continent of Europe about your sneaky antics. Playing this was hellish. Admittedly, I put myself on the hardest difficulty (which would likely explain why everything was so tanky), but hard should actually have some scaling difficulties, not just a massive HP increase. Other games with harder difficulties have more involved in their scaling, so why was this difficulty level so lazy in comparison?I expected a lot more from a game released in 2022. It needs more time in the oven. 3/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Dear fellow werewolf enthusiasts,I am writing this message to express my undeniable love for our kind. Being a werewolf is not just a curse or a burden, but a privilege and a blessing.As one of the few creatures who can shift between two forms, I am in awe of our strength, speed, and agility in both werewolf and wolf form. Our primal nature and our unbreakable bond with the moon fill me with a sense of belonging and purpose that I have never found among humans.To me, werewolves are not just mythical creatures, but a way of life. I embrace our transformation, our howls, and our pack mentality with open arms. I feel most alive when I am running through the forest under the full moon, howling at the top of my lungs with my packmates by my side.I understand that not everyone may share my love for werewolves, and that is okay. But for those who do, I invite you to join me in celebrating our unique and powerful existence. Let us continue to embrace our inner wolf and howl at the moon with all the passion and ferocity that comes with being a true werewolf.With love and respect,A fellow werewolf.

_childDocuments_.review: Wolves are social creatures, that run in packs and have their own set of complex issues they work out together. However, In a World of Darkness - Earthblood, being half man and half beast doesn't make you a wolf; it don't make you a werewolf either. In this title, you play a rampaging werewolf that might as well be a hairy version of The Hulk. I call him Harry the Hulk. You could sneak around but why? Hulk NO sneak!Also, your social interaction could be complex or interesting, but instead you get to click on stationary NPC allies to have awkward conversations between missions; in a generic lobby none the less.The graphics aren't terrible, but the animation or action feels aged. In fact, many features seem very past tense. If you are like me and were hoping for a more dynamic open world that you can balance nature, mankind, destroy the Evil Wyrm, all the while maintaining your secrecy and protecting "The Masquerade", then you wont find that here.I feel like I get my werewolf ears a scratch when I play WolfQuest. If you hated WolfQuest and the open world it has, perhaps this would be a better fit for you. Werewolf Earthblood is disappointingly linear.

_childDocuments_.review: I think all the criticism of this game is more or less fair, and I had the same sinking feeling when I first got into game, but as a whole it feels like a single-player Werewolf campaign, with side quests for the Caern spirit and running around in Lupus form being stealthy. The punchy summary is as someone else posted - it is a delightful "B Movie"-esque game with a tonne of heart.At its heart this game is trying to be a stealth game with combat sections when you either fail your stealth or are drawn into a combat, and the Rage you have generated from stealth kills contributes to your starting Special bar. It is nice and fluid transition from one to the other and as far as fail states go it feels amazing. My main complaint is that every 50m there is your next step marked on the HUD so it feels like I don't have much agency with the stealth sections. I think maybe a small PDA with maps may have helped this, or the use of Penumbra vision to show claw marks to where you need to go.Combat feels really fluid, with its destructive environments and plenty of mooks to ragdoll around that really gives you the Power role trip. Challenging mini-bosses and I would assume bosses fruther into the game. Frenzy looks amazing, but I feel like there should be some drawback or a use-counter for using it (maybe there is as I have only cleared the first level). Also the music slaps when fights kick off!It would be nice when a section is completed we can see a tally of stealth kills/ enraged kills and time spent changed as well as times frenzied. Maybe in a future game there could be 4 skill trees for four different spirit types:Can't wait to have another session of this over the next few days - It is however pronounced Ga-ROOOOOOOO, not Gahh-rue. They are wolves, not chefs!!

_childDocuments_.review: Games made by Cyanide Studio's usually entail simple but fun gameplay, Mixed with an above average story, And Werewolf: The Apocalypse - Earthblood is no exception. The story is very rich for those who are familiar with the tabletop game of the same name that it was adapted from, That being said, I would "highly" recommended people to watch some lore videos before playing Earthblood if they are not immediately familiar with the Werewolf: The Apocalypse series or the "World of Darkness" setting made famous by White Wolf, Mainly because you are dropped right into the thick of things as a veteran Garou (Werewolf) fighting for Gaia.Players who want to play this should be aware of the shortcomings going in, It has very simple gameplay, It's also a very on-rails experience, And some of the gameplay can get repetitive after awhile as well as some lag spikes from time to time, Earthblood has it's flaws yes, But it is a very true and fun game.  And you will absolutely love this game if you enjoy the idea of striking back at a painfully obviously-evil corporation, Turning into a massive werewolf to fight corrupted monsters, Sneaking by guards in wolf-form like a furry John McClane and fighting against giant technological marvel Exo-suits as a completely earty and natural werewolf beefcake.

_childDocuments_.review: I paid less than 3€ for this. For that price, I'd say this game was mediocre.Pros:- When you fail at stealth, you can just wreck the current room and try the next.- Some of the (combat, wolf form) animations are nice.- The combat system is reliable.Neutral:- It's a practically linear game.- Individual rooms are isolated and enemies can't reach you as soon as you cross a door threshold.- Your actions have no consequences at all.Bad:- This game has REALLY bad writing! This could actually be the worst-written game I've played through so far.- A graphical(?) issue made story-relevant textures not show up, which sent me on a wild goose chase.- Lots of small but very noticeable instances of bad game design. Feels like they didn't iterate.- Features some real-world racism and it's blundered so the game seems kinda racist.- Which ending you get is a last-five-minutes choice between labelled doors.- Very bad character animation. Faces snap into expressions instantly.- The badly made or rushed parts of this game aren't funny.- Pretty sure there's no chapter-select option.- Pricey DLC with negligible content.I didn't bother to play on anything but the lowest difficult level for long.Get Spiritual Link (skill point radar) and Camouflage (wolf form cloaking) early, then it's not too frustrating.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Good video game, highly recommend it for werewolf fans.Took me roughly 11 hours to finish the story for the first time so it's a good length for us adults without a lot of time on our hands.Story: The bones of the story are very good and enticing, but the execution of it and the scripted events need a little fixing. Laughed at a few instant twists that made no sense here and there.Mechanics: The gameplay is good and simple, the difficulty is fairly balanced since I played on Medium and had my arse handed to me a few times. Stealth is very easy since the AI is questionable, still enjoyable though.Graphics: It's nice, managed to make a good-looking game without requiring a supercomputer from the European Space Agency to run it. All 3 of Cahal's models are very nice looking and detailed. However, one thing that was kind of hard to look at was everyone's faces, they just looked a bit odd and especially the eyes. Made me feel like I was talking to a bunch of mannequins instead of convincing representations of people.Audio: Very good, and the soundtrack deserves some special praise since it is superb for Metalheads like myself.Overall: I enjoyed playing this game, I only had to look past a few things that were quite odd but that was easily done since I got to play as a lycanthrope. This is simply just a good ol' video game and I recommend it, especially for werewolf fans.

_childDocuments_.review: Lemme preface this by echoing a lot of other reviews: if I could, I'd give this game a neutral rating, rather than the thumbs down. Because it's not an *awful* game, it's just mediocre. It was a fun romp, for what it's worth. But in saying that, the bad outweighs the good for me, hence siding with the thumbs down.So first off, the combat as the crinos is where it shines; it's just really fun and satisfying hack and slash with your big paws and teeth with the edgy music psyching you up. But that leads to one of the game's many problems: it can be noticeably clunky to control Cahal in all his forms. It's at its worst when going through forced stealth areas, many of which remain so, even after the danger is clear, or the story has progressed to a point where stealth should no longer be needed when backtracking through those areas. So you're frustratingly slow, even when swapping to lupis form and hop-dashing constantly. Speaking of the stealth, it's hit or miss. It's satisfying to quietly clear a room, but more often than not it's simply too easy to get spotted and punished. And while I did mention that I enjoy the combat, I *also* enjoy stealth in equal measure. Sometimes you just want to avoid people and causing a scene, y'know? Yet in spite of the couple of introductory forced stealth missions, the game kinda seems to prioritise smashing things up with reckless abandon. You're not really penalised for it or anything, at the very least. Which isn't a problem per se... just a nitpick.The story.... from a writer's standpoint, it made me cringe. I'm not at all familiar with the source material it's drawing from, but there are some interesting worldbuilding things going on if you peep the notes scattered about the levels. However... mostly I just found myself detached from the story being told and pretty much all of the characters tbh. Simply because the pacing is too fast and choppy, and there are some plot points (particularly one supporting character's death) that could've been approached in better ways. Hell, it's hard to care much for a lot of the cannon fodder side characters because, well.... they're just that. There are several pack members that die, for example, but it's hard to be emotionally invested in those characters when we don't really know who they are beyond a throwaway comment or two from the NPCs mourning their deaths. More setup/worldbuilding via more cutscenes and gameplay involving them, or even just more notes scattered around the world touching on them, would've remedied that, I feel.Overall the game's pretty awkward; it looks, runs, and has the vibes of a previous gen release. But it scratches the itch for general werewolf content real nice, and the gameplay is fun despite its flaws. Definitely get it on a heavy sale like I did, because the full pricetag isn't justifiable.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved playing Werewolf and was really looking forward to dipping into this world. Instead we've got what could be an interesting story line, but the poor everything else makes it almost impossible to have any interest in the story and characters.So the everything else:- Poor character acting and bland voice work.- Poor character animation, particularly for something released so recently.- Poorly laid out, railroading levels.- Glitchy and immersion breaking transitions (like moving in and out of ventilation ducts).- Limited AI with repetitive patterns and janky movement.- Limited and rather bland upgrade tree.- Janky movement of character.- Bland button mashing combat.- Stealth doesn't feel stealthy, just walking around as a wolf and stealth status is lost with little warning and instantaneous ant like response from AI. Overall just a poor implementation of a stealth mechanic.- Models and textures are OK, but they get repetitive very rapidly so places look very samey.Overall it looks like a 10 year old console game and plays like a 20 year old one.
