_childDocuments_.review: The story is mainly an excuse to put you in a situation where you're stalking prey as a wolf and then ripping stuff to pieces as a werewolf. Don't expect anything out of the story except an excuse to get you to the wolf parts. Whoever made this had a particular idea--a really good one--and seemed to care about that and only that. And that's cool. What this game does well, it does pretty well and unapologetically--art design and unique playstyle as a wolf / werewolf. The technical gameplay elements aren't exactly next gen or incredibly well done, but someone had fun making this and knew what elements they wanted to polish. And it's fun to play as a result. The art style is great--wolves and werewolves look awesome. The music is absolutely metal to the point of comedy. As with most games, a good reshade mod tweaked to your liking really helps. There's a really good one on the Nexus that makes the game more monochrome with red highlights like the trailer. For those of you who like stealth games, this is a serviceable stealth game where you play as a wolf so really unique in that regard. If you're into old school horror like werewolves and vampires and stuff, this is probably worth picking up.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has proven really hard to review for me. There's a lot of not great parts to it, but it's definitely got some high points.Gameplay wise, its fine? The combat was fun, maybe a little spammy, but still a good time. The stealth sections took time to get the hang of, but felt really good the few times I was able to completely clear a room without going into combat, and I wish there were more instances where that felt possible (Could just be a skill issue on me though)Plot wise is there this game starts to fall apart for me. I could not bring myself to care about any of the characters, they all felt flat, and were killed off so fast it was hard to ever remember them. Every death felt like it was trying to get me to care about a character, but there was only one that I felt legitimately sad for. That might not matter to some people, but this is a game based on a RPG, I thought maybe there would be at least a little more effort put into the characters and story. However, i will say that there was one section in the game that was near perfect in my eyes, a great understanding of the whole werewolf mythos, really well executed, but once that section was over  I never really regained the high of that section.I'd recommend if you really want a werewolf game with fun action, and maybe don't care about story in games at all. Other than that, this one might not be the best fit for you.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game. Now, you must understand I don't think it's a 10/10 game, but it was a lot of fun to play. The story was pretty good, although it seems like the only choice you make in the game that truly makes an impact, is the last decision. And let me say it wasn't an easy choice for me, but I think I did the right thing.The fighting for me was fun as h*ll. Yes, sometimes the controls could be wonky, especially when you were in a smaller room. The last boss fight, which I guess is the 2nd last fight, was the worst. The room seemed too small for what is going on and when you get close to the outer wall, sometimes the camera zooms in and you can't see well. On top of that, sometime you will dash left or right instead of forward or backwards and vice versa because of it. Did it get me killed? Yes. Did I learn how to manage it? Yes.  Now, I do have one real gripe with the game, though. The stealth. You should be able to stealth most of this, but the way some of these rooms are set up, it's pretty much impossible without getting into a fight. I know that is probably the point with a few of these areas, but most of them? If that's the case there shouldn't be a stealth option. I mean, I enjoyed tearing things apart. It brought out the primal in me, but also, sometimes I would've liked to have not fought anything at all. Sometimes I really did try but the game said no. My recommendation is buy this on sale if this appeals to you. Not sure I could recommend it for full price.

_childDocuments_.review: Because gamer Youtubers were very critical of the game, my expectations were low.  The game is quite fine and comparable to many other combat/stealth adventure games.  If you play it on Easy, I imagine it must get boring.  Otherwise, they really respected the Werewolf tabletop RPG, the presentation is good, and the combat is challenging if you choose the hardest difficulty.  Stealth is rewarding and important also when you play on the hardest difficulty. It is not a RPG, in the sense you play a given character and you can unlock all the skills if you find all the Spirits, but there is one real story choice along the way. The game takes between 10 and 20 hours, depending if you take your time to read, talk and find all Spirits (hard to spot sometimes).  I recommended paying about 15 to 20 USD. Like many, I feel the hardest difficulty is recommended, because it means your Gifts (powers) are important and learning the combos becomes useful; otherwise the game can become too easy.  : a) On the hardest difficulty, some of the first bosses will be tough if you did not invest in your combat skills (if you invested mostly in tactics/stealth).  I made that mistake, but I still succeeded. b)  bosses will of course be tough fights that might take you a few tries and a particularly fat one near the end will be extra spongy (a lot of hit points).  I am not a pro yet only one boss fight took me  tries (it forced me though to learn the combos). Might as well name the basic combos, which the game does not explain...* Jumping and doing a Heavy attack to the ground (right-click) does a very useful slam (and cost nothing). Attacking an enemy at the same time you jump sometimes does a fun uppercut. * The attack combos are pretty much all: Light attack, Light attack, Heavy attack. Finishing with two Heavy attacks, if you are in Heavy stance, will do a different move. - Note that Heavy attacks make you more vulnerable to damage for a moment, so use them in combos only.  * Arbitrary autosaves !  Sometimes the autosave is not far, but sometimes you need to re-clear an entire room because the autosave is not recent.  I also missed an achievement because their is no way back (tip: you can manually make copies of the save folder just in case!).  I am missing only one achievement for 100%, so I regret not making manual backups! * There was one boss fight (Pachua) where the camera sometimes did not show the battle for a moment and the enemy sometimes had me stun locked to death.  But that was just one boss out of many, so not bad.

_childDocuments_.review: The games quite nice for the most part, though it does have some major issues, and by major issues, I mean poor development choices.Right of the start, somebody had the bright idea to release it as what appeared to be an Epic Games exclusive. At least I remember it not being on Steam early on. This is primarily why I didn’t get it, and also why about 3 other people I know didn’t get it either. Some people just prefer Steam, and they don’t want to spend money on other platforms because they already have this one. It sounds weird, but that’s how it is for some people. Me included. Now I’m not going to pretend to know why they released on Epic Games originally, but I certainly hope it wasn’t because of an illusion of getting more money because Epic Games takes a smaller tax. Since, you know, releasing on Steam gets you about 10x the publicity and 10x more people who want to buy your game.Now that we covered why this game went under a lot of peoples radar, we get to the actual game. And for the most part, its ok. However, there are a few things that I personally am not a fan of.The gameplay is… Uughh.. Problematic. First of all, there’s the actual combat. When I first went in after seeing a dev trailer, with all its stance swapping and combos, I was worried that this game was going to be a clunky nightmare. So you can imagine my surprise when I found out the gameplay was smooth as a whistle. The movement was nice, and whoever was working on the combat gameplay was smart enough to realize the value of NOT animation locking the player. The combat in this game really is well done for something that was intended for a controller.Then there’s the stealth. The stealth, is actually better than in most other games. Both mechanically and sensically, its quite good.So what’s the problem?The problem is that there IS stealth. You see, when people think about a werewolf game, they think about a giant rampaging monster. Having the whole thing be a partial stealth game messes up the experience. Now both the combat and the stealth are well done, it’s just that they don’t mesh that well in this setting. And I’m 98% sure that every negative review of this game is for that exact reason, consciously or subconsciously.The fact of the matter is, that for the average player, the stealth likely just ruins the experience, like so:The moment you get caught, the fight starts and the stealth part is basically over. So the result is that you kill everyone and your left feeling dissatisfied because you messed up the stealth. Meanwhile if you succeed the stealth, your left feeling dissatisfied because you just stealthed your way through a game where you signed up for gory action.If you’re a perfectionist or OCD, this is likely gonna annoy you.There’s also the upgrade system. Like the stealth, it’s an example of the game trying to do a lot with a concept that doesn’t need to be that complicated. And I am specifically talking about the fact that most of your upgrade points come from hidden collectables. Instead of going for some gory, fast paste action, the player is left dealing with unnecessary stealth, and having to spam-toggle that atrocious penumbra vision every second in fear of not missing anything.Additionally, I should mention the respect I have for this game because it didn’t go with something as lazy as eye-frames on the dodging mechanic. Instead, its an actual dodging mechanic. And extra props for letting you push enemies away while dodging into them instead of them being immovable walls like in almost every other game. Though I am a bit sad to see the typical “Your legs stop working while attacking” system.She story is pretty bland, in my opinion. The fact that pollution is a subplot doesn’t help it either, especially in this day and age where people are sick of getting that kind of messaging in every piece of media they look at. When you take the “Evil mankind polluting the earth” thing away, the story still falls short of being too interesting. The whole pseudo-god thing with the Worm, Gaia and Weaver feels a bit pretentious too, like somebody was afraid to go for a more simple and down-to-earth story, so they crammed in some cosmic entities. The story, in my opinion is simply trying to be bigger than it needs to be. The fact that your enemies are an evil corporation that seems to have silver bullets in most squads also takes a lot away from making you feel the slightest bit unique, your basically another Garou causing them trouble and not much more. Though I suppose it is a good way to have an excuse to give the player a massive amount of bodies to go through.Overall, the game is still quite good. There are a lot of individual aspects that show just how much work went into it. It’s just that the result didn’t mesh all that well with itself. I firmly believe that this game would have been ten times better if it had a different story, different setting, and less stealth, because the actual combat gameplay is quite good.Though as it is, it’s still a good game by my standards. Its stealth part is sort of advertised, so I can’t complain too much about it being there. +You do have the option of simply not doing it, so that’s nice.The game has a sizable degree of polish. And above all, smooth gameplay.So it’s worth a try for anyone who doesn’t have severe OCD.

_childDocuments_.review: First off, lets get one thing straight: this isn't $60. So I don't expect a $60 game. If it did cost that much then maybe I'd be a little upset. Perspective is important. Who would've thought the first World of Darkness video game I'd play after Bloodlines in 2000 was this? Crazy. But here we are, still waiting for Bloodlines 2. Second, IGNORE everyone complaining about getting game over after being spotted. This only happens at the VERY early intro to the game. After you talk to the suit about the silver, you can handle the situation in stealth or rage out. Your call. This isn't open world. Didn't expect it to be for the price. Animations and graphics are reminiscent of a decade ago, but still cool. In some ways its impressive, and others its meh. Personally I don't see anything wrong with the graphics. Mechanics are simplistic, but again, didn't expect this to be Metal Gear or something. Characters are paper thin so far, but who knows that might change. Maybe it won't. Story-line is basic, but everyone can get behind a good revenge story. Hell, many games still have that as a premise. Fine by me. Put some meat in front of me and let 'er rip.However, when it comes to combat, it feels a little stilted. Not as smooth as I like. It tells you to perform combos with 3 basic buttons. And you have two stances you can go into to be more agile or tank. The game is linear, and I'm okay with that too. Not everything has to be a sprawling open-world MMORPG battle-royale egocentric free-for-all.The story was probably written by someone who plays the tabletop version of this game occasionally. Seriously, is it that hard to hire a writer?  I agree they could've worked on the story a bit more. But hey, I enjoyed Castlevania and Resident Evil, and those plots are **** too.Unless everything takes a nose-dive after the two hour mark, I think I will enjoy this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Even as someone who genuinely enjoys low-budget and B-games, I just can't recommend this one for the most basic of reasons: it's BORING. Despite having some cool ideas at its core, the actual gameplay is painfully stale and repetitive. Every mission, every encounter, is basically the same: a big boxy room full of people and hiding places, and maybe a few side paths your wolf form can take.  Then you sneak past, or else you're spotted and it turns into a mediocre brawler. Every single time. And the environments don't change either, at least not in the first half of the game. The repetition is soul-crushing.This is a game that simply needed more time, more work, and more money. It fails at even being kusoge.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a button-mash-fest in its finest, and honestly, that’s the main reason I couldn’t put it down. The gameplay had me hooked, and I ended up finishing it on my Steam Deck in just two days. Playing handheld was awesome, but I wouldn’t have stuck with it on keyboard and mouse.I really liked the skill upgrade system, super satisfying to keep leveling up and getting stronger. That said, some of the enemy arenas got a bit repetitive. There were maybe five different types of baddies, so it started to feel a little samey. The bosses? Pretty easy, tbh. What sparked my interest, was the pre-rendered cinematic opener. Let’s be real, there aren’t many good werewolf/dogman games out there, and that intro was legit cool. But the in-game cutscenes? For a 2022 game, they’re rough, like, early 2000s rough. Feels like the budget went all-in on gameplay, which is fine, but still.Overall, the game’s fun, no doubt. Is it worth 30-40 bucks? Maybe, but you could find games with way better graphics for that price. If you’re just looking for some quick-fix, addictive gameplay, it’s a good pick. But if you’re after a full package with great visuals and story, I’d wait for a sale to avoid feeling let down.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is one of those games that has a lot of things wrong with it but is so heartfelt that I can't in any good conscience call it a bad game. Sure, the graphics are dated, the story is dull and the voice direction's a little rough but I never really found myself caring about any of those things. I was too busy having fun.There's not too much depth in the stealth or combat mechanics on their own, but together, they create something kind of interesting, sort of playing on one of the most important parts of a beat em' up: Challenging yourself to do things that aren't strictly necessary just because you want to.Because yeah, at the end of the day you could just tear everything in your path to shreds, solve every last one of your problems with violence and not be punished for it at all and if you're only a fan of the combat you might do that anyway. But you might also get burnt out if you only do that.People end up only playing half of the game that way, and whereas the stealth mechanics - as previously mentioned - aren't exactly the deepest thing in the world, it's only when you're indulging in both the wolf side, and the man side that you're appreciating the whole werewolf package.All in all, for one of the only games available where you can play as a werewolf (please make more werewolf games please, please, PLEASE) I'd say it does a really good job at blending two different genres together, even if it does seem like a jack-of-all-trades, master of none, sometimes.At barest minimum, it's good dumb fun. The price could be a little lower, maybe. But hey, that's what sales are for.

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately there are hardly any werewolf games on the market, so I was happy to have found one with "Werewolf: The Apocalypse - Earthblood."The design is pretty good, but the characters have little personality and seem static. You have 14-16 hours of playtime if you want to get 100% achievements. It's possible to do 100% in one run, but I would still definitely recommend to read up on the collectibles. Collecting in this game is boring. Just like the gameplay loop. Stealth, fighting, talking to characters and collecting. Not a problem in itself, but the way it's implemented is really, really average to bad. The game actually has potential, but doesn't use it. The feeling/ vibe just doesn't come across. Well, it's not a AAA title, but it would have been better to make compromises in the design and establish great gameplay instead.Because it is a werewolf game and the werewolves were staged really WELL. (Looking damn fierce. Even their behaviour is totally fitting: They can't escape their rage sometimes and attack everyone on sight.)That's why I give the game a thumbs up, because the devs have at least dared to "tackle" the werewolves.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing the game, i leave my honest review about the game:Game overall 8/10:Overall it is an very ok game. The gameplay is decent, however i wish it would not be the same technique and standard gameplay on the whole run. I am aware that this was made from a small developer team and i am very happy to say, that this game was enjoyable, however i suppose this game's potential was not fully used yet. I would hope the game developers are making notes of the up's and down's of the game and i am looking forward of a sequel. Maybe where Cahal, the main protagonist, is fighting against pendex? Who knows?Story 7.5/10:In my honest opinion, the story of Werewolf: The apocalypse is quite interesting. It is nice to see how a group of climate activist and a pack of nature's defenders are holding up against a multi-millonaire oil company, who uses that title to disguise themselves from the naive public. However i am more of a "keep-it-simple" guy. The more complex the story is, the more you need to focus on the story instead of the heart of the game: The Gameplay. Although I am compelled to add, that this is just my personal wish for a great game.The Gameplay 8.5/10: I am most impressed of the gameplay though. The ability to change the agility of the player manually based on the current situation, is what makes the game more enjoyable. You need to go 500 m away to the next mission? No problem! Just change to your agility form(wolf form) and you dont have to go on only two feet. Oh! The enemy is nearby and you gonna alert them if you move too fast? Use your human form and eliminate them without being noticed! Ah Dang! One of the enemies noticed you and now you no choice but to fight? Turn yourself into a werewolf and defeat your enemie with claws and raw strength. However the bugs and not the ability to free roam on the entire map at will is what keeps me from giving this game a solid 10/10.Personal wishes: I wish for one a sequel, where the developers rather use the full potential of the game and work together to make a solid 10/10 title. Furthermore i wish for the oppertunity to use the entire map on the end of the game to explore the map and its design. Thank you Cynide for making this game and i hope you listen to the community for your own interest of making a great sequel

_childDocuments_.review: This game felt like such a freaking disappointment. Marketing promises a werewolf power fantasy complete with a kickass metal soundtrack. It promises good stealth mechanics and an interesting story. The only part it delivers on is the werewolf power fantasy and even  in that it is dragged down by wonky tracking, a bad camera, seriously bullet sponge enemies in the latter half, and good lord the dead falls on the final level. The soundtrack is probably the most repetitive I've ever seen, and that goes double for the level design. Prepare to go through a lot of empty offices, labs, warehouses, and industrial areas before running into groups of goons to tear through over and over again. The stealth mechanics are barely passable and honestly the game is more fun when you ignore them. The story has so many interesting concepts that it just does nothing with and its just really frustrating. This whole game is frustrating because it really does feel like there is something special hidden underneath all this meh. I really wish it either had a bigger budget or that its design was narrowed down because as it stands its completely bloated and lacking in real substance. Pass on this and go play a Skyrim mod if you want a more satisfying werewolf game.

_childDocuments_.review: Was not expecting much from this game but was still disappointed. Cyanide never makes good games and theyre always janky but I figured this might be better and although not terrible its just not good. The game is super repetitive, with you doing the same thing from start to finish. The combat has some satisfaction and its cool to morph into a werewolf the first 10 times but after 8 hours of it it just gets old. All you do is go into these same boxy rooms and just mash light and heavy attack and dodge, and thats it. You have a few abilities but combat was almost the exact same from start until end. And most of the enemies are pretty similar as well. They make fights longer with reinforcements that even though I sabotaged the boxes for some reason they still came. They also add in mutated guys later which if they were seperate enemies would be cool but no its after you kill someone they come back meaning you have to kill all reinforcements then everyone again which is just lazy design and made to even extend fights and the game longer. The story is boring and is just you a group of rebels fighting a corporate and thats it because i skipped most of the inane dialogue because of how boring it all was. All the environments are the same, just compounds and facilities, with no variation. There is a stealth system but its pretty wonky and due to layouts of arenas youre mostly forced to fight people in the end anyways. The graphics look late PS3/early ps4 which for a game from 2021 is kind of wild. Boss fights are ok, more of the same, except final boss which is just cheap lazy game design with a weak guy but never ending countless waves of enemies spawning all around you making it artificially hard. Theres a skill tree with a few abilities but not much excitement and wont change how you play. Theres dialogue with characters that does literally nothing to vary as its meaningless. Its just a game where you do the exact same thing from start to finish for 8 hrs and the other things it tries it doesnt do well and the combat isn't varied enough to stay interesting. 5.5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: First off Cons:This game had a a lot of potential, but the lack of stealth abilities you can do as a human and wolf form make its limited to a crinos bash em up fighting game. The fighting mechanics while varied in crinos are repetitious and become pretty much standard when out of stealth mode. The facial animations are a bit stiff and unnatural. it would have been nice if the spirit world had more interactive elements other then detection on whose an enemy and whose not like perhaps you had to use the power to access different environments in the spirit world or fight new enemies in it that only show up in that world.   For the Pros:the environments are pretty interesting in the game and looking for spirits makes the lore somewhat worthwhile and they put Alot of effort in making the rooms interconnected and accessible. Some of the stealth is clever and sometimes not, but the placement makes for a fun experience nonetheless.  The graphics and special effects are pretty good, although it would have been nice to see the intro/promotional  pre-rendered cutscene wolves/werewolves in the game real time then models that didn't match the look, and felt less than the pre-rendered counterparts. the bosses look pretty awesome in the game and they spent alot of time making them visually relevant but the lack of personality does undermine their functional appearance to some degree. Enemies are interesting and have varied abilities that make the combat a bit more dynamic. Overall i think this game tried to do alot of things with werewolf Apocalypse lore and succeeded in some areas and fell short of the mark in others. I would recommend this game even with its faults, because there aren't alot of shape shifting character protagonists in the video game scene, and they put an honest effort in this game content and lore even though the acting could use a bit of polish. that being said, if they do continue making expansions or more content for this franchise , I hope they expand the capabilities of the three forms at least so that their are more creative ways to play Garou, in a modern setting.

_childDocuments_.review: I can understand why the game-play loop has been criticised for this game; it is stealth until it goes wrong then button mash, then win.  It is not particularly inspiring.  However, I think there is, potentially, a reason for this: it seems to me that Cyanide may have been trying to be way more ambitious but fell short - likely for time or budgetary reasons.The stealth element makes no real sense as you play an Ahroun (warrior), but it would make sense if you were playing a Ragabash (trickster / rogue), likewise the heavy interaction with Spirits really only makes sense from a Theurge (shaman) point of view; and I do therefore wonder if originally Cyanide intended to allow us to pick our Auspice.So, the interactions with the game world seem to me to make more sense when looked at through that perspective; and when I do that I find this is a much better game than its, fairly one-dimensional, game-play loop would indicate.If you are a 1st Ed WWtA fan-boi - and I VERY MUCH AM - then this is actually a little gem of a game.  Kind of wish I had found it sooner.

But it would be nice to have.You should not stealth in this game. Do it only to disable some reinforcements doors. Other than that it's a lot quicker and more fun to just go in and destroy.This game also showcases why Werewolf: the Apocalypse is a bastard child of World of Darkness. _childDocuments_.review: It has heart and that immediately puts it above many far more polished, high budget games. Turning into a giant beastman and tearing apart mercenaries provided me with exactly the kind of easy fun I was after. Sometimes it was just as fun to take it slow and try to sneak through the levels. Stealth has been incorporated in a pretty clever way, as it gives you the opportunity to make the combat encounter easier by reducing the initial amount of enemies and weakening the reinforcements. Story was kind of bland and I'm not sure how to feel about it turning into Resident Evil by the end. The characters were also boring and the voice acting in supposed high tension moments was comically bad. So not much to write about there. However I do love that we are a bunch of eco-terrorists taking down an oil company, it's a very topical subject. Gameplay was very simple and had gotten a bit repetitive by the end. You spam the same 2-3 buttons until you win, on normal difficulty at least. What little depth exists is because of the ability to sneak around the level before combat and sabotage some security measures. Rarely you might be able to go through a room without transforming, but most rooms don't give you that option. There's a few different enemy types to brutalize, my favorite being the Exo (giant robot suit). One thing I didn't like is that the enemies don't react in a satisfying way, plus you get thrown around and stunned a lot, which really detracts from the rampaging 500kg beast experience. But I understand some concessions have to be made for the sake of providing challenging combat. The boss battles (except the final desert one) were awesome. Music is cool and very appropriate for an angry werewolf. Level design, eh, everything felt the same, but I actually like generic industrial / laboratory settings so I didn't mind. Animations, graphics etc were serviceable, except for during dialogues. Voice acting, as previously mentioned, ranged from "ok" to "laughable".  So, everything considered, a very unique, janky, and fun game that's definitely worth a shot for anyone looking to kill a few hours without stressing their cognitive functions too much.
_childDocuments_.name: Werewolf: The Apocalypse - Earthblood

_childDocuments_.review: It's okay. Not as completely horrible as some articles have said. I just like to play as big wolfman and destroy things.The initial premise seemed cool. Unfortunately, the dialogue and story is pretty lackluster and unnatural. Cahal and other characters will provide exposition by talking to nobody. It feels off when it happens.The graphics are so-so. Decent, but it can get really crusty, especially during cutscenes. The gameplay loop is okay; the stealth doesn't feel well implemented but it can be satisfying. The difficulty of the beat'em-up sections are affected by the stealth gameplay, which is a nice touch, but that can be very overwhelming in certain segments. Overall, the game is decent. Would recommend if you like Bayonetta/Sonic Unleashed's Nighttime stages, stealth games and werewolves.

_childDocuments_.review: Somehow I had a lot more fun to play the real RPG instead of this digitalized version. Okay, building a computer-based RPG out of a real pen & paper is always a disappointment. But here I lost already interest shortly after the tutorial. Its simply a straight forward sneaker. The parts where you start splattering in horde mode is boring af. The big aspect of a real RPG - the freedom of doing WHATEVER you wanna do - is missing completely. Already during the tutorial there was something I don't get:If you ever played the p&p you know never to get in line of a raging Crinos - at least unless you are crinos yourself. In a cutscene a Human and a Hispos get in line of fire and the Hispos is killed with one slam by the raging Crinos. Thats BS imo. Why didn't they come in crinos? Why did the Hispos die with one single slam? ...btw. this game HAS NO HISPOS! It only offers Human, Lupus and Crinos.Since my real RPG group fell apart during Corona I had big hopes in this game to play at least a little bit in between.But THIS game is not even worth to spend more time with. Did white Wolf really give a license for it?I dunno if the game gets better after a while, since I lost already interest after 1 hour and probably will not continue to find out.

_childDocuments_.review: Werewolf was a pretty good game. Combat was great, the stealth wasn't bad at all, and the soundtrack is probably the best part about this game. However, I don't think the motivation and reasoning why you're fighting is good for this type of game. I honestly thought the game was about a man trying to control his werewolf form and he's being hunted down along with it. But instead the game was about a group of Nature Activists Literally at War with a energy company which is secretly doing experiments on people.Personally I don't think it's a good setting and motive for this type of game and the type of character you are. The story was a little boring for me but what Really angered me was the very end of the game when I had to make a choice, I made the choice finished the game. But I reloaded the game to pick the other option but it left me after I made my original choice, meaning I had to replay the entire game in order to get just a different ending, nothing else. The actual game itself was great, but the story and motive was dull, and the save after the decision irritated me. But overall the gameplay and soundtrack saved this game for me to like it enough. Wish there's more games like this one, just with a better story.

_childDocuments_.review: Party like it's 2004!I don't know the story behind the development of this game, but it looks and plays like something out of early 2000's, and not in a "timeless classic" way. The combat is... functional, fun for 5-10 minutes and then boring and uninspired. Stealth is pretty basic, would be okayish 20 years ago, but it's not up to current standards. Earthblood is full of unintentionally hilarious throwbacks to old game design: constant button-pushing to open doors, elevator rides, detours through ridiculous ventilation ducts, backtracking, semi-open worlds intended to stretch play time, mannequin-like NPC talks and annoying repetition (including "this area is divided into four sectors" BS). Overall, I finished the game out of nostalgia for the lore, but I wish I hadn't. There's very little to salvage for a WtA fan, the only good thing about this game is the intro.

_childDocuments_.review: First off I do not think this is a bad game and should not be that negatively reviewed. However, this game has many problems. Namely low detail on NPCs and other things in the environment is one. That is passable at least, but the combat and stealth need some work. Combat is good in my eyes, aside from maybe you dying too fast (I only died once in combat and that was from turrets) and enemies having some BS knockback attacks (The knockback animation sends you flying way too far). Stealth is completely optional (aside from one mission in the beginning so anyone complaining about that needs to play more) and it has many flaws that come with an underdeveloped stealth system. The flaws are enemies seeing through cover, wonky detection, crossbow being nearly useless in most areas, and takedowns being random in time and placement after it finishes causing you to get spotted from it.Now I think this game is good, but it is definitely a 40 dollar or less title. The character model for your character and the werewolves are great (aside from the goofy handlebar mustache on the MC). The story is shallow and it doesn't allow time to connect to characters at all. Yet the story is surprisingly long and the game will take a minute to complete (If you go for every spirit). All in all I recommend this game on sale, but it is highly repetitive and at times annoying so a possible avoid for most.
_childDocuments_.name: Werewolf: The Apocalypse - Earthblood

_childDocuments_.review: A very decent hack and slash/stealth game, although it's mechanics could have been better explored. There are very few combos, the stealth is really simple, and there are even some overlooked anoying details, like the fact the character always stands to aim with the crosbow, which makes you visible when crouching behind cover. Anyways, it's a fun game if you are into simple and direct action.That said, if you were into the lore of the pen and paper game, you will hardly be disapointed. There's no meaningless fan service here. The references and the lore work solidly in favour of the experience. Also, on a quick comment, the voice acting isn't as half as bad as most people think, the actors could have made some more effort, true, but all the voices are nicely cast and a match for how the characters look.A fun 7/10 game for fans of the pen and paper game, and perhaps 5/10 for others, but still fun.

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game at around the $15 price point.  Stealth is simple and the level layouts are spartan and artificial to accommodate that play style.  The fight sequences are solid and the Alien Weaponry soundtrack is outstanding.  Aside from that, the entire experience is far more bare bones that I expected going into a licensed title.  The models, animations, level scale, voice acting and every other aspect of this game are B-tier, not AAA.  More than  anything it reminds me of Bungie's 2001 third person action game Oni - fun to play through once and gets the job done, but nothing more.  It might merit a second play through stealth style and to collect and missed lore, but that's about it.  In conclusion, not a great game or novel use of the license but decent fun if you can find it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Werewolf: The Apocalypse - Earthblood

_childDocuments_.review: I can't shake the feeling that with just a little more effort put into it, a little more variety, more polished graphics and animations and a bit more depth to the story, this game could have become something memorable. Especially considering the vast World of Darkness lore (that I can not claim to be too familiar with).But the way it is now it's just kind of bland and repetetive. Like a remnant of the PS2 era rediscovered in 2021.Don't get me wrong, it's not a bad game in its own right. Voice acting is good, story is ok, gameplay is ok, the skill tree is ok, the graphics are... kind of ok I guess (aside from facial expressions and dialogue animations, obviously). Everything is neat but nothing is great. Except for the fact that you can turn into a nine foot werewolf, ripping your enemies to shreds. But that is probably the only thing that sets it apart from a bunch of other games that already covered all other aspects in a more fun and exciting way.The current Steam price however is fair and if you happen to get it on sale you can't really go wrong with it.Despite its obvious shortcomings I still had fun playing it and if you are down for a dark fantasy werewolf sneak/slasher game then it's the best you can get at the moment. If Splinter Cell had an edgy teenage furry child, it would be this.
_childDocuments_.name: Werewolf: The Apocalypse - Earthblood

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fun for what it is. It's not pushing a message at me, it doesn't punish me for not being stealthy, and the story while not fantastic also isn't horrible. I like that I can challenge myself by trying to clear an entire room without a single person seeing me, or just hulk out and whole sale slaughter everyone. The Crinos form FEELS powerful and I love that, it takes something of my own caliber to actually stand against me and thats fun. That being said there's the obvious issues like the graphics. The facial expressions are very robotic and things look like they're from 2010, not 2021. Spirit hunting, while fun at times, can get tiresome. They give you a crossbow, and talents to increase it, but theres so little ammo I never saw a reason to use it. One of the times I did use it two bolts hit an invisible wall and the third  disappeared. If you're going to get this I highly recommend waiting until its 10 to 15.

name: OUTRIDERS
detailed_description: OUTRIDERS COMPLETE EDITION OUTRIDERS COMPLETE EDITION includes all the released content for OUTRIDERS: OUTRIDERS WORLDSLAYER Expansion HELL'S RANGERS Content pack Five Exclusive Emotes OUTRIDERS is a brutal looter-shooter with unique classes, visceral gunplay and powers, set in an original dark universe. Play both the story and endgame modes in single-player or with up to two friends in seamless drop-in drop-out co-op. OUTRIDERS WORLDSLAYER EXPANSION The WORLDSLAYER EXPANSION allows owners of OUTRIDERS to dive straight into the new WORLDSLAYER game content. With new horrors to challenge you and new weapons, mods and gear to discover, you’ll be further developing your build through the new PAX hybrid branch class trees. Survive the campaign and you’ll face even greater horrors in the Trials of Tarya Grata, the brand new endgame. Which partnered with Ascension Points offers a new long term progression system for the most committed players. Finally, push hard through the new Apocalypse difficulty tiers, with each step up to level 40 increasing the chances of obtaining incredible Apocalypse gear and its game changing third mod slot. Reviews & Accolades 'Brutal and Unrelenting' - MMORPG Absolutely Incredible” - Gamers Heroes “THE SCI-FI RPG EPIC WE’VE BEEN WAITING FOR” - COGConnected “Grisly combo of gunplay and superpowers” - IGN “A bonafide hit” - Heavy About the Game OUTRIDERS is a 1-3 player co-op RPG shooter set in an original, dark and desperate sci-fi universe. As mankind bleeds out in the trenches of Enoch, you’ll create your own Outrider and embark on a journey across the hostile planet. With rich storytelling spanning a diverse world, you’ll leave behind the slums and shanty towns of the First City and traverse forests, mountains and desert in the pursuit of a mysterious signal. Combining intense gunplay with violent powers and an arsenal of increasingly twisted weaponry and gear-sets, OUTRIDERS offers countless hours of gameplay from one of the finest shooter developers in the industry – People Can Fly. A JOURNEY OF DEATH As mankind bleeds out in the trenches of Enoch, you must journey across the hostile alien planet in the pursuit of a mysterious signal that could save what’s left of humanity. Should you survive, the powerful Ereshkigal will be your ultimate test. FOUR UNIQUE CLASSES Choose from four distinct classes, each with its own unique abilities to define your personal playstyle. Assassinate your enemies as the Trickster, incinerate them as the Pyromancer, punish them up close as the Devastator, or engage them at range as the Technomancer, master of heavy ordinance. LOOK AND FEEL LEGENDARY Equip yourself with twisted guns and gear with unique savage sci-fi designs made from heavy, brutal metal and feral organic materials. And transmog your appearance effortlessly to any piece of gear you've collected. DEADLY BUILDCRAFTING Discover countless builds to crush your enemies in new and unique ways. Fine-tune your loadout with hundreds of mods across your guns and gear, multiple class-based skill trees, and attribute points. Once your build is perfected, you can turn up the heat by increasing the world tier to face harder enemies and receive better loot. APOCALYPTIC ENDGAME Put your skills to the test in Expeditions: 18 hand-crafted endgame levels featuring unique mechanics and challenges. And even greater horrors await in The Trial of Tarya Gratar, an intense dungeon crawl with brutal bosses.

What benefits you may ask?  Well the benefits such as input lag, the game lagging in general, and my absolute personal favorite... Not being able to pause the game! _childDocuments_.review: 11/23/2022 Update: After playing the DLC a bit, getting each character through it and playing with the new options I am reversing my recommendation. If you understand the game is not about the story, it's about a chaotic mess of fast-paced shooting that rewards aggressive behavior, then yes - I recommend the game. You no longer have to fear being 1-shot by snipers across the map, you feel powerful and the build diversity is much better. At the current point you can take basically any skill in the game and make a build around it, adding in some other skills to support that playstyle.I know the DLC is expensive and agree with many reviews saying it is more costly than it should be, that aside, the customization it adds are awesome. I recommend trying to get the DLC on sale. If you're looking for a game that rewards aggressive use of gunplay and skills with smooth connectivity, the game has finally arrived.----------6/16/2021 Update: The developers recently updated the game and did buff some skills which is great - However, 1 month between meaningful updates that are entirely numerical changes (anyone with programming experience will tell you the updates they performed should have taken a single developer a day max, let alone taking a team a month to do) is not enough. What makes matters worse is it appears as though the update causes crashes in the Expeditions, today alone I have had two issues where I was disconnected from the game's servers and lost the progress - Losing progress on a Tier 14 Expedition while in the final room is a low blow. The game gets new connectivity bugs every update, the developers are incredibly slow, it's hard to believe the same team worked on the Gears of War franchise. This game has so much potential but you'd end up with more productive progress after teaching a rodent that to program after giving it a frontal lobotomy.To make matters worse with the amount of money this game has raked in some actual servers should have been purchased to help with lag when connecting to lobbies, instead People Can Fly has opted to leave the game as a Peer-to-Peer setup. What does this mean? This means that when you join a game whoever started the game (The Host) is acting as the server, this results in their computer acting as the server, so lets say you're in California and the host is in North Carolina, every time you press a button it sends a signal to NC and returns it to you confirming the action - This results in an incredibly laggy experience when joining a game, so why not host? That means you have to carry your team, this is NOT a game where carrying is viable due to downscaling and the enemy health and damage scaling when it comes to multiplayer gameplay. So unless you have friends within a short distance to play with, someone will be lagging. The game has raked in over 3.5 Million players in the first month alone, why wasn't some of this money reallocated to new servers? Your guess is as good as mine, and if they involve greed, it's probably right.----------This will be quite lengthy as I want to explain a few things about the game. As you can see I have quite a bit of play time at 152 hours and I do thoroughly enjoy the game's mechanics and combat. So why won't I recommend it?Well there are many other reviews that explain the core dislikes of the game, nerfs in the first week, terrible launch, laggy servers, etc. Which are valid (the nerfs were kind of necessary as those builds are still incredibly strong, but the devs nerfed the top instead of buffing the bottom - which sucks.)I personally am not recommending the game due to the connectivity experience - I have had none of these issues in single player, if you plan to play the game exclusively single player then I DO recommend the game, just keep in mind the high end expeditions (very endgame) are incredibly difficult to solo.In multiplayer the game appears to be peer-to-peer, what this means is that the individual hosting the game (person who started it/group leader) is acting as the server. This is fine if you're in the same house, city, potentially even same state/province/territory but becomes a big problem when you're matched with someone in another country, or the opposite side of your own. This can be something like a .5 second delay to complete freezes for 3+ seconds after which you're dead. See the game requires an internet connection, so we are connecting to servers - Those servers aren't where the game's connection comes from though, this is the issue.That is of course IF you manage to get into a game. The majority of the time you play in multiplayer the group leader is AFK and you have to leave to find a new game, that would be fine if not for the continued issue (for several weeks now) that causes your game to crash to the desktop after selecting "Return to Lobby" (the alternate option being to go to the Desktop.) And when that doesn't happen you run the risk of the group leader kicking you just before the loot drops, as it's all pooled for the end in endgame content - Meaning you could do 10x the damage of me as the group leader, and I can opt to boot you from my group before you get any loot... Sound fun?The developers are currently sending anyone with reports to Reddit, by all means I invite you to check out r/Outriders on Reddit, there you will see videos of people posting lag and the pre-loot kicks. But here's the ultimate reason I decided to not recommend the game... These videos being posted and all of the complaints of lag/pre-loot kicking? The developers say don't exist. If they don't exist how are there videos showing it? Sure... Don't believe EVERYTHING you see/read on the internet but there comes a point when the overwhelming majority say there is an issue and it must be the case.Now, if the developers pick up their act and treat this as a AAA game from a AAA company I will turn this around and highly recommend it as the gameplay is fun - When it works. But the constant crashing is simply infuriating to deal with and the constantly threat of being pre-loot kicked from a group is too stressful to bother with. The latter isn't an issue if you play with friends - but the former is, hard to play with friends when all but the host is constantly lagging.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a story junkie, and so far I'm LOVING the story in this game.  It's intriguing, the characters are interesting, and you're literally like a kind of god in here.  Someone described it as an "aggressive Gears of War", and that is really accurate.  There are even mini cut scenes when you transition to some areas (something I'm not fond of about Gears either btw lol) The classes are fun, but the play style does require some getting used to and it IS very aggressive, but that is totally by design.  You have to kill things to heal, which makes for constant action and excitement!  There are a lot of things in this game you can customise, from your build, to your gear, and you can change anything about your appearance any time (except gender).Now the bad.  There are admittedly some issues with crossplay between platforms, so if you're looking to play with a friend on their console you'll have to wait a bit.  There are also some stuttering issues due to Direct X, so they are advising to launch using the DX11 version until that is sorted out.  Also, the recommended specs are real; don't try to play this on ultra unless you have a 3080 or better.  I have a GTX 2070 super card and I'm playing on medium to low for better frames.  It still looks pretty great at those settings though.  All in all, worth the money IMO, and the devs are responsive to issue and keeping their community updated on the issues.

_childDocuments_.review: So while major crashing and connectivity issues still occur (A reason to keep this negative) I have more problems with the game itself.(Also each crash adds 300mb of bloat files to your computer, I don't think I even need to write down why that's atrocious) But first the good out of the way:The story is fun to play through, it's a PCF game so the story is just ball to the walls edge-jokes, so nothing big the game just is fun.The core gameplay is fast, aggressive and well made.And there it kinda ends.After getting to the end game and challenge tier 11-12 I have to say this is the worst balanced looter shooter I've played.I have looked at all my options and I have all damage boosts I can pretty much have as a Vanquisher subclass of the Devastator class if I don't brainlessly grind for legendaries needed for a tier progression.Yet another class can just ape with one skill and infinite ammo on shotguns and do double my combined damage with just a passive.And this game is said to "not be a live service game", okay let's compare it to Borderlands 2 and actual non-game as a service looter.Salvador is busted, Salvador has been busted for nearly a decade now in Borderlands 2, no-one has a problem with it.Yet week 1 of this game being online they nerf the best build available at a budget, sure a development oversight, but at the same time there's at least a combined 7 starter builds that just cannot perform compared to it, and then they make the time trial harder in the easier end game maps while they blanket nerf damage multiplier debuffs.So in essence they make every weak build weaker while nerfing the best build out there and make it harder to pass new tiers of difficulty.And this is in a non-live service game? What?I can go instant kill raid bosses with Salvador in Borderlands 2 right now if I wanted to, that ♥♥♥♥ hasn't been touched in 9 years and yet week 1 of this unbalanced mess the players who rolled the statistically a bit better characters get stomped.So yeah unless you want a charade of crashes, bad servers and a game that's being balanced on a whim then do come in and play.

_childDocuments_.review: Can you Double Jump in this Game? No.All I heard of Outriders was that it looked like mid western slop much like many games. I expected to play it for an hour maybe then uninstall in, but I trucked on through for almost 27 hours because of that first hour (and the gameplay felt good).Outriders starts out with a Colony ship that left earth like 80 years ago because, well, Earth was basically ruined because humans cant stop fighting so they select humans got to leave to a new planet they found. You finally land there and I thought it was some fun Sci-Fi. Beautiful alien planet and the Outriders being a group that explores this new planet. It all goes to ♥♥♥♥ once you find the probe that tells if the planet is cool or not because your group get infected with these mushrooms and a Anomaly Storm literally eviscerates some of your party. You try to get the Leader guy to stop the landing party (you are just a small recon party) because this is not safe for humans, but uhhh, there basically is no choice, humans gotta land here. You get put in Cryo for 30 years and when you come back out, surprise!, humans are fighting each other because they literally cannot stop being ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Turned this beautiful valley you landed in into a WW1 Trench war zone. They cant leave because the Anomaly Storms keep them in place and it also fried all electronics. They cant get resources from the Flores (the ship they came in on) so everyone is basically in the same situation as back on Earth, ♥♥♥♥ and hell.This game feels very nihilistic, cause while there may be hope of getting these resources to help people, nothing ever really changes and it just sticks on humans always wanting death wars. SPOILERS FOR THE END:---------------------- In fact, the humans that were left behind on Earth repaired the first space ship that destroyed in orbit and gave it a better engine and got to the new planet first (and way faster than you). They landed, met the natives who used strange powers to keep the Anomaly Storms in control and went "hmmm, strange powers, I want those for myself". Then the guy in charge enslaves them all, and when they sacrifice their beautiful naivety to become bloodhungry brutal "savages" (a literal transformation from their powers) to fight back, he does a genocide and saves a few for his internment camp. So humans came to this planet early and killed the only things keeping the planet liveable and ruined it for themselves (again). There are a couple of minor things, but there isn't really a good outcome, at least not in base game, don't really want to buy the expansion cause I got what I wanted out of thisSPOILER END.So the story is nihilistic, but the mystery is what kept me going, and it was fine (revealed above). The sci-fi probably isn't mind blowing or new, but it was fine enough for me.I've also notice that AAA budget is just a nice thing, because ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ its nice to look at expensive landscapes. The first main area of this game is, like I said earlier, WW1 Trench Warzones, with some variances. The second is a jungle that eventually has alien architecture, and the last place is a desert (that I think looks surprisingly not boring!). I think there are a lot of cool looking areas in this game.But lets get to the real thing here, the gameplay. Its cover shooter kiiiind of like Gears of War, but way less reliant on actual cover. Like in Gears, you feel that oomph of sliding into cover, and everything feels heavy like it should in that game. This game I rarely ever went into cover just because it didnt feel good and I didnt really need to. This is also the Developer who made Gears of War Judgement, so there is some connection there.The guns felt good, I mainly sticked with assault rifles and LMG's and god the sound design was great. It really felt like i was chugging bullets and I would get lost in that sound. You also get power depending on your class. Im pretty all classes heal off their powers, dont know if they work different or not; but mine had to mark enemies with my powers then kill them to heal. One of my abilities just healed on use and that ♥♥♥♥ was essential.The crafting in this game was also so extremely easy to understand and that rules. Every equipment has 3 stats like "ability leech, weapon power bonus, etc", but you dont really need to pay attention to those (maybe end game?). Equipment Epic and above have 2 Mod slots (and the Mods have tiers 1-3). If you dismantle something with a mod (everything rare and up does), you get that mod forever and can put it one whatever you want. I found a mod that just did a ♥♥♥♥ tone of damage on a cooldown of 3 seconds and I put that on every weapon. The mods felt cool and powerful and I liked the power fantasy of that.Another dope thing this game does is the cosmetic system. Once you get an item for the first time, you unlock its skin and can swap any other same equipment it to it visually for no charge.Overall, better than I expected with a intriguing nihilistic Sc-Fi story and satisfying shooting and looting.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit 2: The game is mostly fixed now. There are still some random technical glitches, but it's pretty smooth sailing. The Devs listened and got rid of some of the really terrible mechanics (including timed missions and instakill snipers). It's fun to dink around with different builds and treat this like the arcade shooter it is.  Edit: I retract my positive review. The first patch for the game nerfs everything without addressing any of the real balance issues. We were promised this wouldn't be treated like a live service game. The devs lied. I dealt with this kind of BS approach in the Division 2, and I will never do so again. Don't bother with this: They will nerf your fun before you even have a chance to get real enjoyment out of anything. After a bumpy initial launch, Outriders is very smooth now and lots of fun to coop on. On Windows, be sure to do the Windows Defender folder exception workaround, otherwise your game (like mine was) may randomly hitch. The game has tons and tons of content. The story is interesting, albeit poorly acted and written, but the cinematics are cool. The weapons are ridiculous and a huge part of the appeal is figuring out what oddball combinations will work well to wreak absolute havoc on your foes. The visuals are very much "Mass Effect Unreal Engine." If you like those kinds of visuals (I do), then this game will appeal to you. Really am enjoying this game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a hard sell. A primarily single player game that requires constant internet connection to unstable servers.EDIT: Turns out a big factor for my connectivity was the signal leaving the house travelling across a faulty wire. This might make the below comments about bad connectivity no longer true.The story itself is something you have to laugh at. It frequently contradicts itself and the characters are all varying levels of jerks. A single abrasive character can be impactful in story telling. This game cranks the mood and bitterness up to 11 and... eventually comes down.Combat is fun for the most part as a close range focused character. Anyone who picked the Technomancer, the long range support class, I can only hope they played in a party setting. The game has so many rush down type enemies that long range is not viable in single player.Like Diablo 3, This game has a selectable difficulty that gives modifiers to loot while buffing enemies. _childDocuments_.review: Devastator is a tank class that can't tank because there's no taunt or aggro control in this game.The core gameloop is speedrunning end-game content. That's it. Speed is all that matters. And yet, Devastator doesn't have an elemental ammo skill, so the only way it can complete the speedruns is to cheese gun-swapping with mods that have nothing to do with the class itself. And since the only thing that matters is speed, and there's always a mathematical fastest way to deal damage, even the other three classes have very defined build paths.If you want to enjoy this game, only pick one of the three dps classes, and follow the meta. Choice is an illusion, and replayability is limited. It feels like the devs didn't have a very clear idea of what to do with this game beyond the initial class-based shooter concept, sadly.Steam says I'm in the top 2.1% of achievement earners in this game (oof) so maybe my review is accurate. But the devs are updating it periodically, so maybe it'll be better by the time you read this. Hopefully.

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to recommend this game, but in it's current state I am unable to do so. While the core combat and game play loop are really fun. Technical and end game design issues make this a wait for patch game.The "end game" expeditions are timed meaning to get the best rewards you need to complete them as fast as possible. Depending on time you get a gold, silver or bronze rating that effects the quality of your rewards. Given that this is the intended design, its kind of essential that the game supports you to complete maps quickly.Here are a couple of examples from the other night while playing co-op with a friend (I was not the host). There is a skill you activate that reloads your gun with special rounds that do more damage. Activating this skill worked one time in a full 18+ minute run. This is shown on the in game state sheet at the end of the mission. This skill which normally does most of my damage did around 3% of total damage. This is clearly a peer to peer issue as my client registered the ammo reload part (infinite ammo FTW!) but failed to activate the damage part or put the skill on cool down. I could hit it as much as I wanted, each time reloading the gun and getting more ammo not taken from my reserves but since the bullets in this state to about 10% to 20% of the buffed damage it's kind of pointless. This puts all the pressure to finish the map on my friend and leaves me unable to kill in a kill to heal game.Second issue, there is a skill that allows you to mark a spot on the map and later recall to that spot to get out of a tricky situation. However, if you use that skill you break the ability to self-revive from a downed state. Given the difficulty of friends actually getting to you and having enough time to revive, the self-revive can be essential. Having it not work because you chose to use one the of the powers available to your class is dumb and frustrating. You wonder how stuff like this got past testing.Right now the co-op bugs and performance make this not fun to play and I feel the demo tricked people into buying a game which wasn't actually the released version. I wanted to support the demo first approach, but when it's not representative of the final product it just made me a fool for pre-ordering the game. Guess I'll go back to never pre-ordering and wait for other to discover the bugs for me.Do not buy this game at the moment! It'll be cheaper later and maybe you can actually have some fun playing it if they fix the game. However given that this is a buy once, non-live service game with no cash shop. There's nothing to stop the devs taking the money they have and moving on anthem style.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is shallow. Pick class, mash buttons, fill bullet sponges. Re-hash of the eternal loot shooter, but very basic. 3rd person cover-based shooter, except it tries to redefine the rules by adding a bunch of overpowered skills. Difficulty comes from enemy scaling, not skillsets or any different AI behaviour.Level design is 100% linear and consists of separated areas that don't flow or connect in any way. The game presents a string of these levels, but they all consist of one basic concept. Shoot stuff, move to next area. The overall gameplay of taking cover, shooting, or hitting buttons 1-3 for your skills works properly. But there is so little to work with, imagine if the little there was, didn't work proper...This really is the epitome of copied concepts with no real twist to it other than some weird future with a protagonist getting superpowers. Oh yeah, the Earth is dead and people are apparently fighting over scraps in a new place with some sort of anomaly. OK, very original /s. While the (voice) acting is great, its also utterly forgettable because the cutscenes are entirely disconnected from the gameplay. Might as well be any random story about you fighting a bunch of enemies. Some voiced sequences are also straight up wrong: you can hear lines about meeting aliens and you're then fighting the same old riflemen and bandits you saw all game long.The game has two sets of enemies: aliens and shooty guys, and they re-appear in numerous 'factions' but they're all the exact same, maybe carrying a different name or weapon. It gets so stale, so fast, I think I saw everything the game had to offer post tutorial. So maybe the endgame saves it? NO. You're burnt out, probably even before finishing the story and hitting the top World Tier. What follows are Expeditions (random missions with amazing numbers of enemies to maximize the repetitiveness) where you get set back some world tiers and do the exact same thing all over again... to... euhm... progress? To a higher level of scaling... so none of it really feels like progress regardless.This twisted idea of 'scaling' to make a game needs to stop. Its not a game. Its a meaningless grind that is not fun. Its a treadmill that keeps turning slower as you go, to inspire a sense of difficulty that borders on going straight for braindead since the first minute of the game.Avoid. Play other loot shooters that excel in some area. Borderlands. The Division. Whatever. Just save those 30 hours, and spend them elsewhere.(Official) Reviews place this at a 6-7/10. I would put it at a 4~5 / 10 score, if not less, because the overall execution is rather poor, the game is short, and the hours you do spend are dreadfully boring even if the game manages to catch you in the eternal 'progression hype' that we tend to get when we see bars get filled with XP. Its as shallow as, say, Vermintide 2, but it also lacks the satisfying combat that might make a shallow game enjoyable nonetheless. Such as enemies that give you reason to pause and adopt a strategy. Challenges that feel different or unique. Actual assets you can interact with beyond a key dropping off the last enemy in an area. It lacks a quick way to use other classes without suffering all those crappy scenes again. It lacks variety within the class themselves: some stuff just works, most other stuff is horrible to use. It has cool areas, but that quickly turns out to be just scenery and you are left running from one stack of sandbags to the next box of crates. The list goes on. Every time, the execution is lacking. Even the game of progression is not interesting, because it may easily happen you figure out and build the best setup around halfway through the game. Legendary sets are unobtanium and why would you, the skills aren't powerful enough to play off on their own, you'll prefer shooting as it's faster.So what does the game come down to? Min-maxing a stat like Firepower, making sure you don't die by stacking tier 2 mods (very simple...), proceed to hold the fire button all game long and then you're done. Its really that simple, because most classes heal back up when you kill enemies, making the whole cover concept redundant ever since past the first level. Why play an endgame when there is no progress or discovery left? Why build a game around that idea alone? Why is the progression path so incredibly short? Puzzling indeed. I think this was playtested by a bunch of zombies, and they nodded in approval.

_childDocuments_.review: When I first saw that my friend bought me this game, I was disappointed in him.But this game saved my life.I am 27.My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and adopted our son together. They are now both 4 years old.When we were going through our separation, I found myself lost and miserable. I was self destructive. I got so mad one day from everything spiraling out of my control that I punched some concrete in a moment of overwhelming emotion. That caused me to break my 5th metacarpal in my right hand... my working hand... my games hand.. the hand that I held and carried my children to bed with.. The hand I desperately needed to make sure I could continue to provide.After learning of the severity of my self-inflicted damage, I was borderline suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man with no history of depression or anxiety. I have never had fits of rage, or been one to break down and cry, but I was in a low spot that just really buried me from being able to see the light on the other side.Having nothing better to do, I searched for a game I could play, ONE HANDED while I recovered. I somehow stumbled upon this game and read some of the reviews. I decided that it had to be worth a shot... I must admit, I didn't beat the game, or play nearly as long as some of you. In fact, I may have only played this game a day or two.. With that being said, after doing so, I had a new found joy and hope for life. I was able to put behind me the pain and suffering that had been cast over me. I was able to experience other peoples joy and happiness. I was able to see the fruits of my "labor". I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ minutes to this JOI game long enough to realize that I was going to be okay.After coming to that realization, I turned the game off, and I went back to work. It hurt my hand like hell but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so damn sorry for myself, and I became the father I needed to be in that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving as.Today, I am close friend with my kids mother. We don't fight, or argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents, and friends.I now have 3 kids. My third child is, wait for it, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my own separation, and we just stumbled in to each others life unexpectedly. We have been in a relationship for a year now, and are very happy together.Moral of the story, you never know what life holds in store for you, and if I would have given up when all the odds were stacked against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.Thank you

_childDocuments_.review: I find the game a ton of fun for what it is, but it's absolutely riddled with bugs, unfortunately.For whatever reason the game is now unfathomably blurry (the demo wasn't this way -- must have been the "game ready" driver).  Motion blur should be off by default as it essentially just tosses a bunch of mud on your screen when you move around.  Audio bugs galore -- I haven't heard a single enemy gunshot, or my own footsteps (even during the demo).  On higher world tiers, this means when you're surrounded by 10 enemies, you have NO idea where the bullets are coming from and more often than not means you flail around chasing damage indicators as your health bar depletes to zero.  I'm on a 3700X / RTX 2080 and can barely manage 60FPS during combat.  Add in the stuttering, and you've got yourself a perfect recipe for nausea and indigestion.Sad to see so many games release in this kind of state over the last few years.  While the game is fun and challenging and a good time sink for the people who like what it has to offer, it definitely isn't quite on the finish line yet.  I'd recommend waiting for patches to roll in if this game interests you.EDIT -- The more I play, the more janked this game becomes.  Doors / interactable objects in the world randomly decide to bug out half way through the button hold animation, rendering it totally unusable.  The only thing that seems to fix this is restarting the game entirely.  I've also managed to get this game to hold a relatively decent framerate by dumping all the graphics settings down to Low, and even then it barely nets me a decent improvement.  So instead of being at 40 FPS during combat, I'm at around 65 FPS.And let's not forget to mention the server issues.  The amount of times this game has kicked me back to the main menu when I'm at the home stretch through a tough combat encounter is laughable.  The first couple times it happened, I was pissed.  Now I just find it funny.  The devs are charging people $79.99 to beta test their game for them.  Welcome to the games industry in 2021, folks!Major audio sync issues with well over half of the cutscenes in the game so far.  Some scenes actually feel like there's a kid behind you with a remote pressing the fast forward button every time someone speaks just to annoy you.  What a mess.  Anyway, is this game worth the full AAA price tag?  Absolutely not. Save your money and find something else to do.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games where every good aspect of the game itself is overshadowed with a myriad host of problems that makes it less fun every time you play through it. The plot had so much to offer to almost make this a new Mass Effect-like game but instead you get really bad voice acting, dialogues written by kids and a huge lack of imagination. All of this is just the tip of the iceberg as the game developers nerf classes making you question the point of creating a game which soon becomes more of a drag than a fun experience. I initially wanted to return this game because of technical issues which is an added layer of pain to any player trying to immerse themselves in it. The very concept of having internet connectivity to play the single player campaign is utterly ridiculous and even with it you will get randomly booted out of servers anyway.The map design is extremely simplistic and is reminiscent of old games where invisible walls would restrict the player from wandering around the non-playable area. The game has surprisingly diverse types of enemies that you face in battle which would have been a positive aspect if not for bugs where some enemies can one shot you even when you have some of the best gear after grinding for loot. Ahh yes.... Grinding for loot is not fun when legendary item drop rates are rare to the point that I just gave up on getting more of those in game until you reach the expedition phase which compensates for the extremely short main campaign. Expeditions raise the difficulty levels for each tier you cross to the point where you get swarmed by enemies who are either bullet sponges or will one shot you and the timer makes you rush through it to get the legendary items, only to get killed faster.Even after so many hindrances I finished the campaign and the expeditions and that's it.....I will never get back to this game again even if future DLC or other content is added to it.

_childDocuments_.review: I have at least over 20 hours in the demo.  Yes, to farm, but also because I liked the game.  The gear is pretty fun, the graphics good (even better in full release), and the story decently written.  The skills make sense for the game world as well.I like the fact that legendaries don't drop that often.  They should feel special, and well, unique.  Some complain about that, but I like seeing the special drop I received.The cover system isn't that great, but depending on the character you play, you may not use it a lot.  The loot indicators could be better, but the sound effects for good stuff dropping do help.  There is an option to pick up items upon leaving an area, but it's not completely reliable.  Also, there is a lot of running around for no reason sometimes, but it's a minor grievance.Of course it was buggy upon release, with plenty of server issues.  However, as of the fourth day since release, the servers appear to be stable.However, in the end, I don't like how the endgame works.  For some reason the devs thought adding support and tanky abilities, even though the endgame is all about beating a timer to get the best rewards. It's a poor choice and ruins build variety.  The end game is very repetitive too.  Nothing is random.  Enemies spawn at specific times, always in the same spot, and mostly with the same skills.I think it has a solid foundation, just a very poor execution in the end game.  I don't understand how developers make an end game like this and think it's good.  Stat inflation is lazy.  There is zero variety in that.  While it's a great shooter, the end game will make me quit because there is no substance to it.I have been a gamer for over 30 years.  I tend to play mostly PC games.  I also bounce around between games A LOT.  I may purchase a $60 game and play it for 2 hours or spend $10 on a game and spend 50 hours on it.  Even if I played a game a short time, it does not mean it is bad.  It just means another game caught my attention.  I also complain about flaws in games a lot, even about the littlest of things.  Keep that in mind when reading my reviews.  If I do not have a complaint, then the game must be special!
