_childDocuments_.review: How to waste AAA game? Bugs + crappy end game + crappy coop = no players.I'll probably play it a bit longer after I've beat the main game with one character once.. I'll probably even buy DLC if it goes to a 90% discount (yet, DLC is way too expensive and game is so crap) to do it with another character and try few things it offers.. but I won't recommend to pay more than 20-25 EUR for game to anyone else.+ AAA game, nice vfx, sounds, animations, dialogues + voices;+ good performance;+ beautiful surroundings, various biomes, great art design;+ good story, interesting world settings, good lore;+ 4 classes, each with bunch of skills and class trees (+pax points and ascension with DLC);+ good combat: plenty of different enemies with different behaviors (aka AI);+ good gear and itemization, unlocking mods is fun, set bonuses are ok;+ different weapons, upgrade, mod customization, even sub-type change;+ difficulty balancing, world level, apocalypse level,+ despite levels are tunnel-like, there are hidden secrets to find: chests, ore deposites, lore...- lots of bugs;- no way to communicate in coop;- endgame is running expeditions (somewhat boring), feels grindy and not good rewarding, devs expect players to play hundereds of hours, there is another activity possible - resetting or doing in coop main quests, which is even less rewarding and overall feel pointless (poorly thought);- UI is also poor, worst is the map/minimap, it's VERY hard to navigate in this game,y lacking and limited stash, lack of hotkeys, many screen in screens, lack of description (e.g. buffs/debufs), timing mods cooldowns is impossible;- I dislike arenas design, basically I am approaching enemy defenses and can use outmost cover, but melee/charge enemy types force me to backpedal, unless my character is strong enough to survive/take them down.. this can lead to a VERY long backpedaling (sometime game doesn't allow it and my reset the fight after a countdown) and then forward to get another meaty enemy.. perhaps I should always play on world level 1 or what?- useless and annoying repeatable cut-scenes: when transitioning between levels and sub-levels, when using vendors, turning in quests;- some checkpoints are poorly thought, e.g. saving before loading a sub-level starting with long cut-scene before a boss fight.Biggest NO GO for me is a lack of communication in coop. I could easily spend hundreds of hours here, enjoying coop while farming gear, talking to players, sharing knowledge, making friends.. The devs were lazy to give anything to me, no server lists, no lookup, no filters by language, region, anything..Another thing which I couldn't master - is a controlling of character. It looks simple at first, but e.g. same key is used to dodge and to hop over obstacles, I often jump over the cover straight into bullets from enemies, instead of just quickly reaching the cover. Switching cover function (holding space) is a crappy idea in fast-paced action shooter, would be a good option in tactical turn-based shooter though.. I can't master switching to a right shoulder, there are always obstacles between my gun and enemy, but not between his gun and my face somehow.. Add to it bugs: the character may stuck in place, unable to run forward (due to a large collider of nearby item?) or refuse to use skill.I wish this game will be further developed. It has potential. It could be as fun as Deep Rock Galactic is (rather buy it, than this game). Removing bugs, adding or altering a thing or two. But I have feeling those devs are very greedy, look at price of their DLC (compared to a base game, which was reduced and that's why I bought it myself), which adds just a bit (compared to a base game).

_childDocuments_.review: This game sure has its problems. Connection problems, some bugs, some crashes... But stopping here would be a mistake. At the time I write this, Outriders came out less than a week ago, and the devs are already hard at work to fix the various issues. So let's focus on the good part.It's the best shooter I've played in a long time. The blend of skills and guns is awesome, leading to some really intense gun fights, where you both feel powerful and at the same time threatened, forcing you to constantly move and rethink the situation. Outside of fights, the crafting system and skill trees will allow you to really prepare for the battles to come and completely change the way you play, further enhancing the variety already offered by the 4 classes.And if you can play with friends, multiply the fun by two times their number!

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, first and foremost. Highly recommended giving the demo a go if you're unsure -- don't forget to try out all the classes, I was surprised by what I have ended up with as my main! There have been issues, as there is with any game at launch, but the communication from the Social Media team and Devs has been amazing, they have constantly kept the community updated on what they are working on and responding to messages and tweets across the board. I've been very lucky not to face many issues beyond not being able to play with friends cross-platform at launch, beyond that all I've really come up against is a few game and sever crashes. The idea of my inventory being wiped is terrifying, I do hope they come up with a solid fix for that (and give people back their hard earned gear!) soon. Beyond all of that: The story line is great, the characters are solid, the voice lines have a good dose of dark humour, expeditions have the right amount of challenge whilst still being re-playable and achievable. The armour, weapon and mod system is easy to understand with a wide selection of gear/mods to fit different play styles. All-in-all, a really enjoyable game that I look forward to playing and talking about every day.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty cool original IP. Good art & designs. Writing is campy but hits the notes it's going for and gets it's point across. Shooting guns and using powers is fun and satisfying once you get a grasp of how to build your character and make good synergies of mods abilities and skills. Not a live service game, so what you see is what you get. Probably the biggest downside of the game is that the amount of grinding it will ask you to do in order to finish builds using legendary gear and mods is not proportional to the amount of actual content in the game. Once you've done Eye of the Storm 90 times to finish your big endgame build the only thing for you to do is Eye of the Storm 90 more times. A good value on sale. Probably not worth full price unless you're thirsty for fresh sci-fi, or just really want to congratulate SE for taking a chance on an original IP.

_childDocuments_.review: OUTRIDERS was without a doubt one of those games that take me by surprise! It was one of those games that I might not even have tried if was not by my friends, if was not to be able to play it with them! Yes you can play it solo, and you will have great fun playing it... But being able to play it with a team of friends, that you can even join across platforms, is how the game shine more brightly. I will not forget laughing like crazy with my buds with some of the gory jokes or coordinate efforts to play it at the higher difficulty possible.Speaking a bit about the game, it is like Gears of War, Mass Effect Andromeda, Destiny found a way to have a baby all together. You have an amazing gameplay that resembles Gears, with an similar cover system and intense gunfight with lots of blood, a story that resembles Andromeda, at least the part that we crossed the galaxy to find a new home elsewhere and when we get there things were far from what we planned, and Destiny for the looter-shooter system, where People Can Fly have made an amazing job with a very rewarding system, with weapons and armour with amazing skins, interesting mods that made us think at every level in the best way we could take advantage of them and use their max potential and great legendary drops that make us feel special when he get one.Honestly I can understand and feel for all the gamers that left a bad review of the game. The game had a rough start, with bugs, servers that were down all the time and even people losing all their inventory after 100 hours or more of gameplay. But let's be real, was it the worst start in the gaming history? Was it an Anthem situation? I don't think so...The developers were active all the time on the social networks addressing the concerns and explaining all they were doing on the game and all about the game updates. Things are not yet perfect at the point of my review, but I honestly believe that they will keep working on it, improving it and expand the game universe that we only start to scratch.But, and to summarise this very extensive review, do I recommend the game? I honestly do, I had a lot of fun and that is what matters in the end. Alone, with randoms or with friends it is an amazing game that I fully recommend. But if you still have doubt after this review, you have a Demo available for free, so give it a go! Try it by yourself, you will not regreat it...

_childDocuments_.review: 50 hours under the belt (albeit some of it was just having game launched). Reached endgame, with Eye of the Storm left. Haven't touched multi yet.Generally, I'd give it 8/10 with possibility to put it notch higher if multi is bringing another hours of game.Pros:+ no BS. you really get what you pay for. Standalone, contained experience with no MTX, lootboxes, GAAS bloated skeleton of a game. This is fully executed product for 30-50 hours of gameplay you've paid for.+ builds, synergies, minmaxing, power fantasy. The general jist of looter shooters+ if Destiny 2 and Warframe had a violent threesome with Borderlands 3 while Division 2 was filming the whole thing and Deep Rock Galactic was peeping through the window - this is Outriders+ full support of devs. I just can't imagine frustration that they have due to Square Enix's faulty online infrastructure+ shooting feeling. Vital in game where you spend 90% of your time spewing bullets + performance. You can see that PCF put a lot of time into thinking this one through and optimizing the gorgeous Unreal engine 4 to make it work like a charm. Fast loadings (albeit frequent), no major bugs, visual clarity, sporadic audio cut-offs when there are 20938 sound channels overlapping, + a bit less obvious yet important thing - no grave imbalance between the classes. Cons:- servers, but frankly, for 50 hours straight I would say I had relatively unhindered experience.- enemies variety. This is a bit of lackluster, yet it might be fatigue due to long time already put into it.- frankly, I don't see much of the solo endgame at the moment. Eye of the storm and level 50 is my go to and then probably another character, however game would really benefit from like set items, more build defining uniques...- missing pvp which would be fun if PCF would change it's stance on GAAS and balance such mode properly Final thoughts. If you are in the market for looter shooter for foreseeable 50-100+ hours and got your index finger bored with Destiny & co., the Outriders might just scratch that itch. It is truly enjoyable game, occassionally (frequency might vary) hampered by repetitive encounters and server issues (which I'm certain it will be ironed out very soon). Ideas and concepts for future:* transmogrification is a must and despite game not having players' hub (since it's not GAAS) where you can flash out your sparkling new WMDs and robes, it would be nice to have outfit that you fully like rather than orange sneakers with predator skull helmet, tight spandex pants with a wet rag on your back. * Hunts, assassinations with more modifiers. Instances with affixed giving you bonuses, akin Borderlands 3 system. Increasing game longevity.* Environment interaction. Doubtly this can be implemented but as PCF worked wonders with environmental kills in BulletStorm, I thought we might have some of that in Outriders. * new biomes and enemies. At some point. Enjoy,DissTurbo

_childDocuments_.review: The game promotes itself as a Looter Shooter with RPG and Power element.And here's why it fails absolutely miserably. For anyone avid gamer (especially shooters) since the 2000, you'll probably be able to share the same sentiment.This game tries to be many things, but yet absolutely fails to deliver in every single aspect.Looter - Whether from enemies, or boss, or chests, the amount of loot is scarce. Despite being at World Tier 15 (Higher WT means better quality and quantity of drops). And before you may think, perhaps it's quality over quantity... You'd be dead wrong.RPG - The skill tree seems vast at first glance, but there are little to nothing to do about it, your level caps at 30, and you have a measly 20 skill points to spend. Build diversity is hard to achieve if you're trying to unlock one of the class nodes at the end, you'll only have 7 points left to spend on whatever else, if you spec a beeline towards the last node of a class, there won't be any sort of hybrid build possibility.Power - In cutscenes, your character have been portrayed like an immortal god. Shrugging off bullets like a soft breeze caressing your body. But in reality? Once you get past intro areas, and advance up the world tier in hopes for better loot drop, dying became a regular occurrence. But unlike Dark Souls, where if you die, it's mostly your fault; Here in Outriders, you also have to struggle against clunky controls / imprecise movements, enemy bullet sponges, and awkward camera handling, compound all that with seemingly endless waves and enemies spawning wherever at whim. (I had enemies poofed (spawned) into existence right before my eyes.)Design - Pre-Legendary loot (weapons) designs feels like it was something out of Gears of War chunky and blocky, nothing to boast or brag at. Legendary loot designs feels like developers copied Remnants: From the Ashes' weapon designs, to a 90% of similarities. None of the gun audio felt satisfying to use, and weapon accuracy was all over the place, except for Sniper Rifles and the such.Gameplay - The gameplay feels strongly inspired by Mass Effect 3's Co-Op mode, but difference is. Mass Effect 3 a 2012 game did it better. Outrider's performance feels clunky, weapons doesn't sound or feel powerful, and powers/ abilities feels lackluster. From map design to graphic, it feels all too outdated for a game that's released in 2021.Service - This game is an online ONLY product, despite the lack of PvP mode, or Micro-transactions. Your gameplay experience, inventory, time and effort are all at the whims of the company's server competence, which frankly, paying a  starving homeless man to run on a hamster wheel may provide better stability than Outriders' servers. Not to mention, even in Solo mode, game does not have Pause feature. (Menu / Settings / Inventory does not pause the game)Ultimately (TL:DR;) Game's worth maximum of $40. And even then, personally I'd still wait for a steep sale. Outriders tries to take and combine multiple genre and titles into one, but fails at almost every single aspects of it. It have been a very generic experience for me.I got this for free as a birthday gift, and I'd still like a refund for the friend that gifted this to me.

_childDocuments_.review: OUTRIDERS is...rushed clearly, its a fun game if you are a fan of drilling health bars and combing abilities, unique legendary loot and cranking up difficulty it can be awesome.It sort of just sucks that you will never see it unless you're really lucky with drops or invested into grinding the end game, In honesty i haven't even finished the story and I don't feel motivated to, But its cool there is methods to getting a guaranteed legendary armour or weapon drops via hunt and wanted missions (although they can be very repetitive).Launch was crap and we all know it but looking at the core game its fun, it is just very clunky and many design aspects can leave players wanting more (UI, Sound. Character Design, Story, Player Movement).I hate to do it but Outriders is very similar to Anthem.- The loot is interesting (if you get any).- There is guaranteed ways to get loot but it will be a grind- The game is really sold more on its graphics rather than content. - Loading Screens...- Most loot that's not legendary or epic are either not unique enough or strong enough to keep- Legendary guns look cooler than they perform- Both games had issues within the development cycles or publisherOutriders's unique gimmick being dismantling guns to gain their affects to place on other guns is cool but can be very odd. _childDocuments_.review: Playing during a free weekend, and I can not recommend this game without caveats.If you enjoy cover-based third person shooters, you will still probably want friends to play this with. If you do not enjoy cover-based shooters, I would not play this game. Cover-based shooting and movement is the core of gameplay. Expect to duck into cover, move between cover, vault over cover, and get hit at every stage of the process. Maybe it's industry standard for cover-based shooters, but I did not like how hard my character stuck to the cover. Early on there is a sidequest, culminating in a mini-boss fight against someone you, the player have motivation to dislike. This fight takes place in a room smaller than a basketball court, and you are being tailed by a fire tornado the entire fight. If you duck into cover, you start moving slower than the fire tornado. It will clip through cover to pursue you, and it will eat your health if it touches you. If the mini-boss was the only enemy in the room, this wouldn't be too bad, for a solo player (I understand the game is built around teams BUT, I did not play that way) you have to deal with him, his tornado, and about twelve mooks. You take cover against the mooks, and the fire tornado eats you alive, you step out of cover and you WILL take multiple shots, there's just too many people with too many angles on you, and the animation for getting in and out of cover locks you into taking more damage.I think the game could have been better if it removed much of the cover-based gameplay. I know someone worked really hard on all of the wall-tracking and the animations for following walls and changing directions on them, but the cover-based gameplay takes all of the focus off of the seemingly cool abilities, instead forcing you to ignore your build in favor of moving from one waist-high wall to another. Follow this with two non-sidearms per player (I assume this was done to Encourage multiplayer) and the inventory system starts getting in the way of the gameplay. Long, cover-filled corridors mean you can either push through with short-range weapons, and get filled with lead; or bring a sniper and hang at the back, which stalls out gameplay in favor of survivability.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr Outrider's crafting is nothing groundbreaking, but it solves the problem I've had with so many other looter shooters and I can say that I am now hooked.----------------------------------------------------------------------------At first, I wasn't impressed. I played the demo for a day. Got to the max level. Graphics were decent enough but performance was a little meh. Gunplay was fun enough but it was "nothing special". Pretty much a standard looter shooter. So I bought it and waited. Played the first day unlocked the crafting and my whole perception shifted for the better. The 2 most important things for a "looter shooter" is the lootin' and the shootin'. What I have witnessed a lot of recent games in this genre is that they may get the shootin' right, but they fail at providing a lootin' experience that  compliments the shootin' and hooks the player into wanting to play for an extended period of time. These games tend to have a hard time keeping their players interested in their endgame. Outrider's crafting is nothing groundbreaking, but it solves the problem I've had with so many other looter shooters and I can say that I am now hooked. The crafting combined with the character progression has the potential to hold interest far into the endgame. The moment I knew I was hooked was when I was able to know exactly the type of character I wanted to build start building that character as soon as crafting was unlocked.You like a certain weapon? You can keep that weapon throughout the entire game by being able to level it up, mod it, and upgrade its rarity with the right amount of resources. The major problem other looter shooters has is  they force the player to rely too much on RNGesus in order to build themselves to the way they want to play. Then they artificially limit the best of RNGesus in order to arbitrarily extend playtimes. Not in Outriders. Build the way you want to play from the *beginning* and spend your time grinding towards making your style stronger instead of grinding towards *hoping* to get the right combinations of gear that will make your style possible.

Not going to worry about the server issues early on. However I'd like to spend more time actually shooting rather than reloading... I shoot for about 2 seconds, then spend the next 2-3 reloading, then in about 20 seconds of shooting you run out of ammo having killed maybe 5-10 enemies cause you just don't carry much on your person, this all just doesn't make for very fun gunplay.Anything and everything that mildly interrupts your reloading animation completely stops it, which kills momentum, dropping off a short ledge, STOPS RELOADING, get bumped into, STOPS RELOADING, all abilities you activate while reloading stops it also, which makes sense but having to restart a reload animation 2-3 times before you can actually go back to shooting just feels awful.Weapons that were doing fine about 5 minutes ago stop being relevant even if you don't find a proper replacement(happens often in my case and I can't bump up the world level for better loot ause my guns are already outpaced by enemies), which is boring and kinda ruins the fun for me personally, if I find a good weapon while leveling that is powerful, I want it to stay powerful for at least 20 more minutes before it just stops having much of any impact whatsoever.At this time I think I am done playing, the demo seemed alright, I liked the transparency of the Devs, appreciate selling a non live service game, but enough of the core systems are working against me in a very un-fun and un-engaging way that I am just not having any fun the farther I get into the game. And I don't honestly see these systems changing as they do feel intentional like design decisions, just not good ones in my opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: Looter shooters had it rough in the last couple of years, personally I think this franchise is really hit or miss, as games like the Borderlands Series or Destiny are some of the best games I've played (might even consider them my favorite games in generall).So I was scared when they announced Outriders, as it looked promising but I feared it would suffer the same fate as some other games I won't mention.Now 2 weeks after release I can savely say that Outriders is 100% worth it for fans of the genre, I have been having a lot of trouble with most of my new games recently, a lot of them I put down after a couple of days.But Outriders has been an enjoyable experience for these 2 weeks straight.The things I enjoyed most about the game are the skill trees which are very good as each class kind of has 3 subclasses which all have their own unique playstyle, class balance is fine despite the technomancer class being very dominant.The loot system is very nice too, high rarity drops aren't too common and all weapons spawn with random mods which can be taken off and put on any weapon you wish, giving you a lot of freedom with your builds.The story however is very basic and feels like an edgy superhero movie, your character constantly pulls some wannabe badass lines and a lot of character are just killed off like a mission after meeting them.Endgame is mostly just doing one of 15 missions over and over and doing it faster and faster for better lootwhich is pretty fun as it gets harder over time and challenges you. However that might not be for everyone.So if you really need a break from the same looter shooter that you've played for years now, then in my opinion, Outriders might be worth looking into even if it's just for a couple of weeks.

_childDocuments_.review: Great graphics, great story, very bad implementation - definitely not worth the money.If your GPU can handle it, the graphics are really amazing, skill effects, the characters and monsters as well as the alien landscape.The story is also very interesting, both from a "how realistic is that this happens in our future?" and how it all plays together when you go through the story, do all the side quests, talk to the people and understand how all this happened. Without trying to spoiler anything here, a sequel to the story would be great.But unfortunately that is all that is good about the game. First you have forced online mode for single player, which especially in the beginning was painfully annoying to the server outages on the developer's side. Then there are those annoying bugs here and there in the game world that has you repeat quests or wonder why you can't progress the area anymore. Lastly the very boring skill trees and unbalanced classes and archetypes (inside the classes).For me the worst part was having a way to play together with other people but at the same time have no way to communicate with them, neither text nor voice chat are available in the game. Add to that random matchmaking and you are playing roulette for the success of your expedition. I don't understand this decision from a feature/gameplay perspective.I could add the massive issues with multiplayer matchmaking, lost inventory / items and scaling problems, but those are probably well known by everyone now already.I paid 60€ for the game, which is far too much for the content provided. A price of 30€ for the awesome story would have been fine. The multiplayer mode and grinding endgame has no value to me, or even reduces it due to bugs and lack of balancing.

_childDocuments_.review: Basically Gears of War meets Diablo with a Destiny-esque aesthetic and less emphasis on cover and more getting in enemies faces. Use cover only if you're desperate.Fast paced combat and each class requires a different approach which is nice. Skills are pretty decent and varied, they can all be improved/modded by gear slot mods to refine a build. Crafting plays into this and is encouraged in order to maximise your damage output and skill synergy etc.Story is not award winning but for me still engaging if you like sci-fi. Go in expecting some Sly or Arnie 80/90s movie level of writing and you won't be disappointed. (Fortunately I love those old movies so this is right up my alley).There are a few technical issues on PC as of launch days but Devs are doing well communicating and pushing fixes as fast as they can. Check out the stickied discussions or reddits for work arounds/fixes right. Windows defender exclusion cleared my issues right up and can now enjoy the game pretty smooth maxed out with quality DLSS on my 2060 at decently high frame rates.A really good loot shooter more in the vein of Diablo than any of the others (which it should be) and is not a Game as a Service which is fantastic. This is what we all wanted Anthem to be I think, and as that game is never going to get the updates it needs I would seriously urge any interested to try the demo and then get this game and support some great developers. 8/10 for me, smooth fast combat with interesting and effective loot/gear mods.

_childDocuments_.review: Saw the Negative reviews and thought I'd chip in here.For all the people who are having performance issues it's most likely your variation of parts as I have these specs, and play at Ultra 1080p 60fps with no frame dips.Ryzen 7 2700X, RTX 2060S, 16GB RamGames react differently with different combinations of hardware. I've had this game running for the last 10 hours and it's stayed stable.The Demo ran so much worse as it wasn't optimized, while the full version seems to be optimized better. Could still use a little work but I haven't noticed any frame dips or stutters. In terms of the connection to the servers, I have only been disconnected once out of the 10 hours I've been playing.This game is very similar to that of Destiny. Requires an Internet connection to play even singleplayer. This was announced with the game I do believe, so people who are complaining about it, That's on you for not knowing what you were buying. Thru my 10 hours of gameplay, I haven't encountered even 1 game breaking bug, The overall Gameplay has felt smooth and bugfree as of now. Obviously this varies from person to person.The games World Tier and Player Levels makes the enemies feel pretty difficult depending if you have your world tier on the highest possible level for you. The struggle to keep your gear and weapons up to the power of the world tier is quite grindy and difficult as you'd expect. Feels alot like Destiny where the gear you're getting for quite a long while is just leveling gear. Not meant to be used long term but to just help you level creep. But the interesting part to me is the fact that you can upgrade the rarity of any armor or weapons giving better attributes to the items and mods. So you could take a basic gun and upgrade it to an Epic and get the perks associated with it being an epic. Plus with the inter-changeable mods say you had a gun that you like the mod of but not the weapon itself, but you do have a weapon that you'd like to upgrade in some way. You can switch the mod you like to the gun you want to use, and with the better rarities and such you''ll get a 2nd mod slot on your gear.So all around I find this game to be amazing. The gameplay feels good and familiar as it feels like a combo of Destiny, The Division, and Gears of War. The graphics are really good, especially if you have RTX and DLSS enabled. The different world spaces feel unique and diverse. I feel this game will keep getting better with time. all around as of now I'm giving this game a 8.6 out of 10. and I'd say if you're on the ropes with this game I'd say it was worth the $60 for me as I find the game fun and enjoyable. if it's the same for you idk only you can answer that. I can't tell you if this game is worth it to you or not. I'm just giving my opinion and experience with this game thus far. Anyway there's my review just thought I'd put my thoughts on this game out there as seeing the ratings be mixed if quite sad-ning.

_childDocuments_.review: INITIAL THOUGHTS:After 12 hours invested in the main Outriders game, over 50hrs during the demo and a full completion of the main game storyline, I can say honestly that I didn't know if I was playing "Outriders" when there were so many borrowed mechanics or attributes from other successful games like Gears of War, Division, Destiny, Anthem, Diablo, etc. It's almost as if Outriders attempted to source their gameplay from all of the different core mechanics that made other games successful. This is a red flag for me as new games, especially looter-shooters, need to explore "new" mechanics to enhance their unique approach. The fact that when characters make the almost exact animation of opening loot chests or restocks like Anthem javelins, this leads me to believe originality in animations became difficult. Although Outriders successfully delivered very well on an overall good experience for a new looter-shooter IP, the constant reminder of other game's mechanics left me scratching my head.MAIN CAMPAIGN/NARRATIVE:Although the main campaign itself is longer than other looter-shooters on release and there is a "somewhat" accessible endgame content, the repetitiveness of every fight creates a very stagnant gameplay experience. Despite the Diablo-style loot system, you'll find yourself crutching the same weapons and/or armor due to mod reliance. Unless you're playing higher tiers and hoping for legendary drops or higher base power weapons, there isn't much need to swap weapons at all. Although anomaly power has you pushing aggressively, focus on gunplay forces players behind constant cover and playing incredibly passively with distance between you and enemies.The narrative of Outriders is a solid step into what other games have done before and flows very well in linear fashion. Dialogue is pretty dry and sometimes uterly awful, but the character development and surprises are very refreshing.LEVEL DESIGN:Level design is incredibly unique, though texture and scaling issues make graphical clarity somewhat less admirable than other games. In some instances it actually inhibits the experience due to slow texture loads. In addition, it's very easy to find yourself running into walls where you thought you'd be able to explore due to U/I map misinformation. Kudos to the skybox artists though for what feels like an incredibly unique environment to explore.WEAPONS:Legendary weapon designs are very intriguing, but from a precursory glance they all have the same callous "bone" aesthetic that leaves no weapon feeling "original." Weapons as a whole are suitable for whatever play experience you find yourself in. Sniping is very satisfying when headshots connect, though the sniper movement bounce is extremely annoying and unnecessary. Range-to-damage ratio for all weapons seems very well done, though shotguns seem to need a slight buff to damage to not feel so mod-reliant in high-energy fights. Sidearms with the right modifications are incredibly overpowered and I found myself crutching them constantly without a need for other weapons.MODS:The focus on mod use and discovery to create "builds" in game is awesome, but some mods in the game are so unbelievably overpowered that gameplay can suffer from it by turning enemies to 1-shot kills. The mod system overall is extremely well done, though the restriction to per-character and not per-account is extremely frustrating since it forces players to double, triple, or quad-grind for the same results. Mods need to shift to account-based.ENDGAME:The repetitive endgame leaves players begging the question of "why does it matter?" There is a huge focus for obtaining legendary weapons with new mods or armor set completions, but grinding for endgame loot that doesn't serve a purpose other than character customization makes the endgame extremely dry, repetitive and pointless. Given that the game is still early-release, it's possible that endgame may improve, but playing the same thing over and over again is not enticement for the reward purpose at hand.MULTIPLAYER:Surprisingly, multiplayer was very stable for the most part (despite crossplay issues). Squading up with teammates and hard-pushing was a fun and exciting experience, though the uncertainty of enemy scaling gives the impression that more players = easier fights (almost too easy). It's like the world tier level is the only scaling modifier across all players. Crossplay as a launch option is incredible, but clearly new territory for PCF and will need time to be configured more appropriately.FINAL THOUGHTS & SCORE: 7.5 OUT OF 10Overall, Outriders is an incredibly fun, highly-energetic looter-shooter that breathes life into the LT genre, but suffers major drawbacks from its clear lack of distinction from other games that make the main campaign playthrough the real focus of the game. If you're a player who loves campaign-based gameplay w/ friends, satisfying shooter aspects and abilities that make you feel incredibly powerful, Outriders will easily satisfy your needs with roughly 80-100hrs of total gameplay across all 4 character types. Unfortunately, if you're looking for a purposeful and meaningful endgame grind, Outriders will likely leave you wondering whether it's currently worth the investment or whether to wait a few more months for new endgame content to be released.

_childDocuments_.review: The launch was rough. We all know it and they know it. It has a few problems that are pretty annoying but nothing truly game breaking. The servers not working for the first 2 days was pretty ridiculous in this day and age. However, the game is a solid 9.1/10. The Gears of War/BulletStorm/Division/Destiny combo is fun. There's plenty of blood, guts, humor, and beautiful scenery in between to keep you coming back. People need to accept the fact that the people making the gameplay have nothing to do with the server capacity and launch problems. The main problems with the game boil down to  main categories:1. Server Problems : haven't run into anymore past April 3rd as of writing this.2. Poor Performance: The game is essentially unplayable on DX12 for most people. This is circumvented by playing on DX11. The performance even after switching is still dodgy at times. Whether the servers or the optimization of the game is the cause I do not know.3. Bugs. There are a few annoying ones. Crashes being the most prevalent. They happen enough to be an annoyance but not enough to warrant throwing the game away. Quest trails not bringing you to the quest you have tracked is annoying but proper use of the map can mitigate that. Trying to enter a quest area only for the area to just not work. Usually you have to go to a marked area (Usually a wall that you jump over, a log that you go under, or some rocks that you squeeze through) but the game just doesn't let you in. This is quickly fixed by hopping into the main menu and back into the game. Thankfully, the process of quitting to the menu and coming back takes about 15-20 seconds if even. The longest part is most likely the walk back. The problems listed will most likely be fixed with time. They won't be fixed by bombarding the game with negativity but by allowing the developers time to fix the bugs, and whatever problems they have with the servers... well... I for one didn't see this game being anywhere near as popular as it is. I thought the game was fun and interesting but my god I didn't think this many people wanted a good looter shooter right now. The people behind this game are exactly that... people. They make mistakes and have problems. It happens. What they do now is what's important. I for one can't wait to see the future of this game. Endgame is promising and if all goes well this will be a great game for years to come.If anything happens in the future that changes my mind I'll change my review. For right now I see no reason this game isn't a solid recommendation from me. See you on Enoch fellow Outriders!

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: game is pretty and the campaign is entertaining but it's also full of bugs and the endgame is one of the worse deign I've ever seen outside of the "FTP" worldEdit: I came back to the game top see if a few years had improved it. Unfortunately,m it has not: bug that were here day 1 are still present and the gameplay has not improved. On the contrary: whatever they did to end game made it completely unappealing: expeditions are unplayable solo due to the "one death, back to start" and the fact that they are faaaar too long (30-45 minutes for one run with NO reward unless you complete them). Progression solo is a complete, unappealing grind. The fact that matchmaking pretty much always drops you in game with on guy AFK waiting for someone to complete the exp makes this even more aggravating.I guess that endgame is kind of playable if you have a few friends to play his with but, in all honesty, I simply cannot fathom how any professional game dev can cook up such a bad bad design and still look at himself in the mirror.Original review:The campaign is kind of fun if you don't mind the nonsensical scenario paper-thin characters. The game, however, is riddle with problems:- Group play is borked beyond recognition: when you join a team, you're dependent your connection to the TEAM LEADER. That's right, not a server or anthing: if he drops, your game dies. If he has lag, you won't play.Speaking of lag: any kind of lag/dropped packet will cause the game to be unplayable: skill going in CD without triggering, enemies teleporting all over the place, etc. The netcode of this thing probably has been lifted from DOOM 2 without any modification.- End game is unappealing: beyond the 5 different scales that hides the reality, there is only a grind for meaningless drop: there is really nothing to get excited ever.- UX is unclear to the extreme. From the "skip cutscene" command that switch between escape, space and "not available" to the completely unreadable weapon statistics screens. Seriously, hire a UX professional next time. And listen to her.If you want a shooter/looter, wait until that game is 15 bucks: by that time they might have ironed some of the most outrageous bugs out

_childDocuments_.review: So i've seen that there is a mixture of reviews on this game, some with good valid comments, some with comment that have apparently been made by an adult but ultimately some pompous puss puss meow meow has thrown their toys out the pram and cried over not getting what they want then and there. Anyway thought i'd drop in and give a realistic and honest review (my opinion) on this game.Firstly, lets raise the issue of the launch and servers and people losing progress with invent wipes. The invent wipes are terrible i feel for anyone whose lost all that hard earned loot, but credit to the developers who are actually communicating constantly with twitter and reddit to update and resolve these issues. If you honestly expect a game to be released now days without its problems first 2 weeks, then you're honestly disillusion and please see a doctor. I know this shouldn't be the case, but it is how it is so go down to the shop, buy a bottle of tequila, snort the salt, squeeze the lemon in your eye and bang your head on the desk and relax whilst it's all sorted.Anyway...If you're looking for a deep story to get invested in, then this really isn't a game for you. The story is okay at best, would rate it a 6/10. Don't really ever get invested in the characters and its a bit samey, but then again what game isn't now days? It gives a simple to follow and tells you why you're doing it etc. Fine, was able to finish it in about 15 hours and if it was 5-10 more hours I reckon I would have lost interest. It wasn't bad, but it certainly wasn't great, was okay.However, I believe the story was only a bridge you had to cross to reach the full purpose of this game. Which is the end game or more known as Expeditions. if you're looking to become an absolute walking colossus and pump some guns into aliens limbs to send them flying into the oblivion then you'll be right at home.Expeditions can be very challenging, the first few, say 1-7 are quite easy to get through, need some sort of idea what you're doing and combination of your mods are a big priority. However the higher up you go the more difficult it becomes and the more you need to deep dive into your class and combine both your armour mods with your abilities and your abilities with your selected class tree etc. Then the satisfaction of literally becoming a human/alien flesh lawnmower when you find that build is beyond satisfying. I've refused myself to look at any 'Guides' because tbh there are so many different routes and combinations that I can't really see their being a 'meta' unless you play techno, those green F**** are so OP it makes me want to spoon out my eyeballs so I can see myself eat them. I play a devastator and i've seen multiple suggestions that they are the hardest to play, well i tell you now, you're all wrong. If you're a lazy Flamingo you can just look up guides. But honestly that'll just ruin the whole point of the game. You'll be done in about 20 hours of end game, subject to you actually hitting T15 and getting all the gear you want. Also if you can't handle the stress of doing stuff in time because I know how soft humanity is now days, then do us all a favour and don't get this game, because i'll only see your stupid review on here and its not warranted. So all in all. If you are looking for a Single player RPG game with a deep story to get invested in, probably not worth it. If you want to bulldoze through crowds of enemies, screaming at the top of your lungs whilst your endless clip of automatic shotgun pulverises everything in its path. A 3rd person shooter , that is challenging and rewarding, with NO recycled content, HOLY F*** no recycled content, yes you heard. With lots of loot? then go right ahead, get it. Remember, don't be a puss puss meow meow, cover is for cowards.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to recommend this game, but I can't. I won't be mentioning all the bugs and technical difficulties, which there were many and still are, because besides the connection issues and couple random crashes, I was fortune enough to avoid all inventory wipe bugs and such. I liked all the different areas the story takes you and the story itself was really nice. The story itself was the best part of this game. It took me about 35-40 hours or so, which was nice. However... there's no variety or meaningful dialog choices to be made during the story, so it was a really boring to play it through the second time with my second character.After the story, there is the end game. You clear expeditions and the goal is to unlock challenge tier (ct) 15 so you can travel to the final expedition to have a date with the final boss. After unlocking the ct 15 I was already bored. Once again, there's no variety to spice up expeditions. Once you clear them the first time, it's just the same old. Expeditions are also the place to get the highest level gear. There are two ways; get lucky straight away or play same boring expeditions for hundreds of hours and maybe you get lucky, because it's all about the luck. During expeditions you gather this expedition exclusive currency. This is used to travel to the final destination, but you can use it to purchase whopping 8 different kind of legendary items, 4 weapons which are the same for all classes and 4 different legendary armor pieces, 1 for each set of your class and that's it. I really don't understand why to create a special currency to end game if there's nothing to buy with it.In short! The story was a nice experience, but the end game is boring garbage.

_childDocuments_.review: I've waited this long to post a review because I was not going to write one.  I usually don't do these sort of thing unless I feel really strongly about the game, and after this "Appreciation package" update I felt that it was time.My group of friends all got the game day one thanks to a buddy purchasing it for us (Thanks Phil!) as a gift.  I'm not going to describe everything that happened just the same stuff as most people at launch including one of us four friends getting his character wiped. _childDocuments_.review: Quite a nicely done looter-shooter with great sounds, graphics and ambience.  It plays more like Mass Effect, rather than Destiny in how combat works (it utilises a cover system).  There is a decent story and the way that the world tier system works is very good as well; that you can decrease the tier for fights that you haven't yet found gear high enough to cope and go back up again afterwards.  You can also, should you wish, start again from the beginning (or any unlocked story point) with a character you have levelled and geared up.Playing co-operatively with friends is really easy, and a huge amount of fun. Combat is gloriously visceral, and beautifully done at that.  I have introduced one of my friends to this genre of game and she is now as addicted to this as I am... :)I highly recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: So my review is based on the fact that I was new to the franchise. I was given the expansion for free, but i did make sure to go through the main/base game first.I recommend this game with a big asterisk, because it would be very very hit or miss with the audience it's going for. The game is based around a lot of grinding and buildcrafting. The gunplay itself is decent enough, but it's hard to sell a game with such a weak story and characters, the setting itself isn't very interesting either. So you sell the game on the endgame itself, which itself is also rather weak. The expansion's end game on paper is interesting, but at the end of the day it's just more of the same. Just think the drop pod end game of the base game but paced in a somewhat choose your own path linear deal; with a few bosses scattered here and there. The game itself rounds out to being rather mediocre, not bad or really all that good. which is a shame cause i can see potential in the series (if it is to become a series). The reason mediocrity is a shame to me is because i'll soon forget that i played this game or anything about it, while i still remember good games and bad games alike. I'll probably join Remnant From the Ashes and Anthem in the mediocre looter shooters that I forced myself to remember to make a comparison to something.TL;DR  if you enjoy decent gunplay, build crafting, and grinding for gear check it out. If that's not what you're into just skip it. (The 3 mod slots on gear is a very powerful change and a good change though)

_childDocuments_.review: It's now two weeks after release and this game is basically in a paid alpha right now.  I know that's kind of always the case these days, but this one is unusually bad.  There are so many bugs and disconnections that it's just super frustrating.  I want to like it.  Some day this will probably be pretty fun.  The good:+ Good Story+ Long basic campaign+ Several play style / build choices+ Some truly epic fights in the campaign+ Fun End Game MissionsThe bad:- All the different ways you can crash: joining game, leaving game, middle of a fight- Skills randomly locking out- load in game, but no HUD, can't shoot or use skills- just got crashed and reloading the game? Here watch the super long intro and then the anti-cheat will trigger and close you out of the game so you can do it again- Epics are usually better than Legendary items because Legendary items have fixed stats with nonsensical combinations (boggle).  Kind of ruins the loot chase.  Set items are even worse.  You can chose to wear 3 items with subpar stats to get a set bonus that isn't that great.... Basically the only reason you want Legendary or set armor is to disassemble it to get the mod to put on an epic.  And that's only a couple of them per class.- You can't chose what challenge tier you want to join in match making.  This results in under geared players constantly joining matches too high for them. - endgame requires a lot of joining and leaving games, and each time there's a good chance of disconnect- in multiplayer, only the host has a lag free game.  The other two players get to try to shoot stuff while rubber banding like madWith that said, i'm off to play more stable games.  I may try this again after a few more patches.

_childDocuments_.review: [Review in progress] I'll keep it short and sweet, for now. The game's awesome, so far! _childDocuments_.review: Let's just get down to it.If the reason you are buying this game because it look and felt similar to destiny then no, don't buy the game. The game play itself is similar to games like gear of war. Wherein you are in a third person shooter that place emphasis on using cover to avoid taking damage and moving forward while mowing down enemy and getting to the goal. The game give you four playable classes. Each class has eight skills in total, starting with a single one and unlocking more as you level up. Each class also has three sub-classes you can spec out with the Class Trees, and you are free to change that at any time. Class trees are split into three branches made up of small and large nodes, granting bonuses to your character's attributes or greater percentage-based bonuses affecting other skills respectively. While each branch is unique for each class, they're essentially grouped into weapon damage, survival, or Anomaly power.The classes are as follows:-Devastator : Close range tanker play-style -Pyromancer : Medium range play-style -Technomancer : Long range play- style-Trickster : Hit and run play-styleIn my opinion out of this four classes the best to used would be technomancer. Since you are require to just deal damage to regain back your hp. Pyromancer regain hp by killing marked target. Devastator heals through all closed ranged kills. Lastly Trickster heals when killing enemy at a closed range. -Gameplay/customizationThe combat for the game is satisfying for the most part. Abilities felt impact full and rewarding for some of the classes. Customization for the character is pretty lackluster. The addition of transmog later on in the game atleast make my character didn't look like he just got robbed and put on any clothes that he find. The grind for the most part is alright, but it is understandable if everyone not down for it.  But if you are looking to farm legendary item would require to be in late game and at least the world level need to be higher. But if you are just playing casual , there are side mission that you are able to do to get better equipment and so on. Side note don't play this game more than 90 fov. If you feel it is not enough trust me its enough . If you play on +100 fov i respect you. I don't know how people able to play it without motion sickness, I tip my hats of to you sir. -Story-I am just gonna simplified it to not spoil for people that haven't play this yet. Basically, after earth literally can't be livable. Earth decide to build a spaceship and go to a distant planet that similar to earth. The game start as you the player called Outrider, Outrider are soldier that are send beforehand to new planet to scout if it is safe for the colonist. Long story short you found a distress call from a ship similar to yours. You try to find the source of the signal. You gain power from the mystical planet. Lastly you use the power you receive to pave the way. -Cons-I don't know why they choose to have the cinematic camera to be film like they getting chase by people. I am not getting the feel of the story, the only thing i got was motion sickness. The scaling for some of the bosses are pretty weird at one point they felt like pushover and another part they almost one shot you. Gears are pretty much randomize good luck with that, pray to the rng god that you get good loot.-End note-Is the game worth to buy ? Not really. Don't get me wrong it's fun and all but doesn't really pull you in from my perspectiveOnly buy this game if there is a promotion or sale.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're not like me and you don't buy EVERY game that looks even half-way decent that comes out, I suggest you hold off on buying this game (and probably never buy it).This game has really bad netcode, really poor optimization (graphically), poor servers with connectivity issues, an interesting story but poorly presented.The netcode: It's awful man, you rubber band CONSTANTLY when using skills, moving around near other players or monsters, even dodgeroll is glitchy in multiplayer. The terrible netcode makes the game's multiplayer feel like you're getting a ton of lag even though you aren't, even when you have great pings to the players you're playing with.Optimization: This isn't a beta, this is a full release. I'm using a 2080 RTX and I had to completely nerf my graphics, turn OFF DLSS, etc just to get the game to stop hitching frames. It really runs worse than ANY of the "full release" games i've played over the recent years.The servers drop people constantly, for no real reason there are CRAZY LONG load screens and waiting for connection screens - you spend half your time waiting on these, and if you're trying to "matchmake" you'll spend nearly 100% of the time looking at loading screens that are already at 100% bar but never loads up, ALT+F4 the game try again, even when matchmaking works you'll get massive lag and disconnects all the time. The way all of this is coded is seriously really bad, worse than Division 2 or Destiny 2 or any other similar genre game.Story : The story itself is actually pretty good - like if I were to spoil the whole story and tell you about it, it'd probably sound cool to you... however in-game it's represented TERRIBLY with bad actors, constantly cringy cutscenes made by a Polish company and I can only assume it's a lost-in-translation / cultural difference issue.. it's bad, and there are SO many un-needed cutscenes showing your character climb something, open a door, do down a rope etc for NO reason instead of just loading the next zone you get a pointless cutscene to watch and THEN a loading screen on top of that!All of this being said,The skill tree system for classes is very coolThe gear and itemization is handled BETTER than Destiny, BETTER than Division 2, and any other similar game!The way the World Tier system works, levels work, damage works, how difficult the game is, these things are all executed so well it's actually amazing. It's like the developers making this game REALLY KNOW how to make an amazing game! The problem is, the netcode totally ruins the experience.. just like we all feared when playing the demo and seeing how bad the netcode was.. they promised us the release would have better netcode.. but it's really ♥♥♥♥.The rubberbanding and "Not smooth feeling" gameplay in multiplayer is so bad it's hard to even compare it to another game because i've never seen a game of this genre do it this poorly.Also, while the game IS fun...The enemies you fight are not fun. Many times in this game - single or multiplayer - you will think to yourself, "WHAT THE ♥♥♥♥ JUST KILLED ME?!"There are marksman, trappers, and all kinds of random things that hit you from seemingly no where. (Especially captains and their anomaly abilities). MOST of their stupid abilities you will not see until you get hit by them.Part of this is because you are AIMING DOWN SIGHTS and this game has AoE warning circles on the ground beneath  you which you CANNOT SEE because you are aiming down sights (lol)   You could try hipfiring, but the inaccurate fire while hipfiring is so bad you'll probably not even hit enemies and you're not likely to hit their crit spots.The melee enemies are even worse, the bigger nasty ones, which the game throws a *lot* at you are almost totally immune to CC and resist everything, while constantly using anomaly magic samurai dash lunges at you which are extremely difficult to dodge unless you are only dealing with 1 or maybe 2 at a time. When there's 5+ of them, and there often are that many in multiplayer, - - combined with TERRIBLE NETCODE - - you will just die. You'll be running against invisible enemies, getting rubberbanded, all kinds of stupid stuff that shouldn't happen.I enjoy a challenge, I like "hard" games and I love difficult co-op games, and while this game has amazing potential, I don't recommend it to anyone that is expecting a "finished product" this is most certainly NOT a finished product. It's a buggy mess with awesome game design, but terrible netcode and terrible optimization and a LOT of frequent game-breaking bugs.

_childDocuments_.review: Do Not purchase this game...Please save yourself the time and money and DO NOT purchase it. Here my breakdownNormally i wait for 3-4 weeks before i purchase basically any game, to which i can then read reviews and see how the game has left players feeling. I got suckered into this one and bought it on day 2 due to friends asking me to and wanting to play together. I should have waited...1. Story - (No Spoilers dont worry) - Eh, its not bad..i actually enjoyed how they set up the powers part of it and how the overall idea of the shooter/power looter. The voice acting is actually really good but there are still some audio voiceline mis-syncs that go on...which they had in the demo and stated they would fix...they didnt.  The NPCs that follow you and basically are part of the crew do actually have some personality unlike some other recent games that have basically really easily forgettable characters. The story is good overall but nothing thatll put you on the edge of your seat..some parts couldve been better while others were just right. 2. Combat - Pretty solid actually, pretty much got a good feel of every gun class and they all have their own different feel and sounds. it was fun getting to blow thru some enemies early on while trying to figure out which class of gun you liked. The powers feel pretty strong at times when you synergize them well. Some powers will feel really good while others seem to have maybe a little lack-luster feel or effect. After a while though once you hone in on what class you like and seem to have things rolling, youll get to the ridiculous bullet spongey mess that it is. Now dont get me wrong, i understand that if looter shooters didnt have bullet sponge effects..then youd mow thru everything and it wouldnt matter what loot you had..i get it..but my point is that i wish some Devs would take the idea to make the enemies more fun to shoot so that we didnt realize so easily that its just blasting 1000 rounds into this guys face..until he eventually dies...make it fun.. make the enemies arms blow off..armor falls apart when its shot to ♥♥♥♥..make it fun ..pretty much the only thing they did along those lines is make head pop when you headshot em..but if you focus on that all the time..youll get swarmed. So the combat is good, but becomes kinda mundane after a few hours..its basically go here, shoot some guys, kill the mini boss or boss, move on to a new area and do it again until you reach the end. 3. Loot - OMG, one of the worst parts of the game imo. Looter/shooter..right...youd think the loot is good though or should be close because thats what its all about..the loot...Well...sorry to tell you.. it sucks. So like most looter games, in the beginning..its all cool getting new items and goin over the stats and skill and abilities...blah blah..but of course comes the part where you figure out what you want and what things you need. ugh, where to start. first off i guess...theres 3 main components on armor (Firepower, Anomaly power, Max Health) that roll. Basically doesnt matter much in the beginning but after a few hours of gameplay youll know what your class needs. My friend and I would constantly get gear with the main stat of which we didnt use..which is eh..its RNG baby..but youll realize that you cant re-roll that stat to the other..so when youre waiting to get some high end gear ..and you finally do..and it rolls one of the others..its trash basically.. and this will happen time and time again..to the point that its frustrating as hell because you may not be able to move forward without that piece. Then theres the abilities that roll with the gear, some are effects while others boost your skills. and its the same thing as before..however, you can re-roll your abilities..but only one and after you re-roll it...that becomes the only slot that you can re-roll...you can do it as many times as you like, but again..once you get high end that finally rolls ur main stat...you better hope that one of the abilities is the one you need, because if both arent what you need..its trash. Then theres the guns..not much here, they also roll abilities..same effect..you can only re-roll one and then its locked. but there sniper rifles with a bonus to close range damage (cant re-roll that stat but you can increase it) SMGs with long range dam boost..sometimes your weapon will roll the same ability twice, example: ive gotten several weapons where both abilities inflict bleed or ash effect..which again..you can change one of em..but you shouldnt get that anyway..Basically the loot system needs an entire over-haul.4. Trading - there is none...no...none..sorry...So if youre playing with friends and one of them uses LMGs and you dont and you just got a really really good one that they could use....well equip it i guess and let em see it..then break it down because too bad...This game really needs trading to some extent (all loot based games do). Maybe something like Diablo 3...you know, if ur playing with friends and an item drops for you..but u dont need it or use it..you can trade it only to the people that were in ur group when it dropped..yeah no..ok5. Bugs - Holy SHiiiii friends buckle up...i wont go too far into em- Server issues -  Jesus H...you know the rest.. well idk how some of these studios measure things,,but i swear these guys must not know how to count. Day 1 and even now still constant crashes....game will crash while playing solo...and even wayyy more so when playing with friends. the only way i could re-connect with friends after a crash is by completely closing down and re-starting steam... and even then it would sometimes still not connect or crash very shortly after re-joining. the "they must not know how to count" comment pertained to them having the same issue with the demo. If 300k people login and play the demo...youd think they would AT LEAST prep the servers to handle 300k..but instead it seems like they lowered the bandwidth...idk but yeah..still having crashes all over the place. - Players Disappearing - Yup pretty self explanatory, some players will have the glitch of there charcter just suddenly disappear upon using a skill..problem is you cant do anything when it happens except ctrl-alt-del and force close the game. - Enemies falling thru map - another self explanatory one. Mostly happens during the end-game expeditions..but an enemy or enemies will randomly fall thru the map which causes you to ultimately fail the exp since you have to kill all the enemies. - Inventory wipe -  So they released a patch a day ago and that introduced the inventory wipe glitch. they had this problem with the demo so...welcome back! Lately players would log in and attempt to join a party to quickly have yet another crash sequence..and once they came back..theyd find a naked character and completely empty inventory...yeah...ouch..hurt feelings..the devs have stated that they are goin to check logs and whatnot to get the players their stuff back..but we're talking thousands of people..so yeah, doubt this will happen for them all..also..how long of a wait are they talking here...i mean, they still havenet fixed the servers yet... - They are already nerfing builds and items...yeah..or as they put it "balancing"...basically they said that they were questioning why some build were being played more than others ( the builds being played were more efficient and worked well when built correctly) but instead of buffing or making the unpopular builds viable...they just nerf the ones that were working well...you know..cause logic. Why are they nerfing or balancing anything in the game right now instead of working on making the servers stable and fixing actual bugs and glitches is beyond me. So the constant crashing and horrible loot system and coupled with the complete lack of trading and lack of end-game content..i cant recommend this game right now.

_childDocuments_.review: "Gears of Diablo 3"If the sound of those two games mashed together does not appeal to you, then this is probably not your game. It takes the best of Diablo 3's ARPG looting experience and combines it with the best of Gears of War's third person style shooting mechanics to make for an outstanding fast-paced, high-risk, high-reward style looter shooter experience. This game values your time by giving you full character customization whenever you want it, full build customization via skill changes, skill trees, gear customization, interesting loot to chase, a difficulty system that let's you play at your tempo, and a solid campaign that leaves you looking forward to the new expansion the developers have announced for Spring 2022.  I can't be more thrilled to have purchased this game. I can't speak for what it was when it launched because I stayed away after hearing it was a bit half-baked out of the gate, but as of today, it plays well and performs well on my computer with only one quest that produced any bugs during my entire campaign runthrough on my Trickster class. If you're sick of the likes of Destiny 2's pithy looting system and loot, if you're tired of isometric ARPGs, if Borderlands 3 just isn't doin it for ya, if you're tired of waiting for Diablo 4...hell, if you've ever wanted to play Gears of War but with less need for cover shooting a LOT faster paced...give Outriders a try. What a fantastic experience. Thank you, thank you, yes, I know that was an outstanding review, but I must depart for the Porcelain Bowl. The lips don't seem to be awkwardly when talking (yay), and their facial expressions have variety as you go through the game.The main character is relatively complex as far as main characters go. Nice.Gun/Ash tree is decent for slowing and controlling crowds, pairs well with the fiery skill "Vulcan Rounds" or wotever it's called, especially with LMGs...But the incendiary abilities, aside from the gun-buffing one? They all SUUUUUUUUUUCK.The fire-beam-blast is a massive pain to aim and is super finicky. Worse, it can't be used from behind even half-cover and usually hits the side of things you're trying to aim OVER.And like many abilities, it pulls your body back from said cover, negating the benefits of cover instantly. Basically, it's a requirement that you use it out in the open. AND YET.The damage is GARBAGE compared to almost every other ability AND it has a long-ass cooldown.Then there's the starting ability, the fire wave. The low cooldown is nice and all, but the cast speed is absurdly slow, pulls you from cover and the wave itself travels so slowly that it only typically hits foes that are literally running directly at you or which are behind cover and immobile...But the fact that it takes so long to cast and pulls you from cover just isn't worth the garbage damage it deals, even with that low cooldown on use. Basically the only reason to use it is to spread fire, using the class effects to make other stuff stronger...Except again, Vulcan Rounds are just better for that. Apply it to a Suppression LMG, spray and you'll more easily and more quickly light every enemy you can spot on fire without nearly the same risk or level of pain-in-the-ass-ery.No slow-moving wave. No pulled-from-cover BS slow-animation. No stupid-short range.The problem isn't that abilities like Vulcan Rounds are too gud, but that the alternatives are BAD. Like, they expose you to harm and barely have better DPS than guns.Speaking of, let's talk gunsThe greatest rarity of weapons and armor? ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. They look cool and can carry lvl.3 mods... But why even keep them? You can break them down, apply their lvl.3 bonus to some other gear. There's even an INCENTIVE to do so, since all golden-rarity guns have ONE firing variant and you cannot change that at all.The golden-rarity guns literally have less flexibility than regular purple-rarity guns and have the exact same number of maximum mod slots: 2Why? Y'all had the opportunity to make the golden-rarity weapons the shining stars, give them 3 slots for mods and make it so you can alter up to 2 with only 1/3rd being locked once you do so.As-is, there is actually LESS reason to keep a golden-rarity weapon than there is to just break it down for its mod. Do the above, please, for the love of fun.Also, fix some of those gun mods... Things like the "bubble which explodes" have such pitiful range that even if you make an effort to use it yourself, it rarely hits more than one or two enemies. Similarly, the damage scaling on some weapon mods is just god-awful.The same applies to armor. So, so many armor sets are basically worn for their looks... Because the mods themselves are meaningless after purple rarity armor is picked up.Give golden-rarity gear 3 mod slots, guys...And make golden-rarity weapon variants something we can change. That no-alteration ♥♥♥♥ stinks.Next... Difficulty balancing.Enemies that can oneshot in higher difficulties? Fine. That's okay, skill and we'll live.Enemies with 100% perfect aimbot accuracy? Uh... Bit difficult, but we can stagger and hide? It'll be a strategic fight, but we can prevail.Bosses with so much HP that we have to spend a fifteen to thirty minutes in a firefight spraying them down to kill them? Now, that's getting on our nerves.This game suffers from bullet-sponge enemies... And it's not a small thing, it's infuriating. Mobs, whatever, a few extra shots. Maybe twice the clip or a few abilities to soften them up.But the elite units? The elite units have so much health and stagger/status resistance it's just ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ absurd. I've been chased across entire arenas and even to the outskirts, looping back around with cover to maintain distance as they bum-rushed me fearlessly. The aggression in combination with these factors just makes it a frustrating ordeal, as you jab them over and over, spatter them with ash and fire, only for them to be stopped for a second or two at most.I've spent HOURS fighting multiple elites in a single battle, simply because of how aggressive their AI is and how much HP they have, alongside their resistances.We can handle the aimbot BS. Can handle even their oneshot damage. But their HP and resistances? That is just way too inflated. It's not "HARD". It's just slow, tedious and frustrating as a single death will force us to suffer them again and again.Lastly... Do you WANT us to seek cover? Because with how often enemies throw grenades, use carpet-bombing powers and how huge AoE attacks are... It really feels like we're not meant to sit behind cover for fights. AND YET. That's all you can do in higher difficulties, due to the aimbot precision of the AI and their massive damage output.So please, decide if we should be allowed to take cover or not.If so, please lessen the use of AoE attacks, or at least make cover block the attacks if they land on the other side of it. The fact that grenades on the other side of a barrier hit you is kind of BS, unless you're hiding behind destructible wooden planks.And if you don't want us in cover often, judging by how many wide-range AoE attacks are lobbed at us and how many abilities pull us from cover and make us easy targets in the midst of their slow animations... Then please severely tone down enemy accuracy.And again, I cannot stress this enough: Remove bullet-sponginess. Enemy HP inflation as it stands is insane. Yeah, the loot is ass. Golden rarity loot is still barely any different than purple in worth, while the guns are actually LESS worthwhile to keep since... Ya know... They still have a locked variant, making them LESS flexible to your playstyle. And with the same number of mod slots and the same pick-one-lock-the-other mechanic, there's seriously no actual reason to keep them.It's better in like 90% of cases to just break them down for their  innate tier-3 mod, then apply it to a purple gun with the variant and appearance you like.And you can really feel the loot drop rate issue, too. So not only is golden rarity gear basically just more restrictive in use and slightly abnormal-looking compared to purple rarity, its also absurdly low drop rate means that it'll only be rewarded for .Yeah.I've picked up a total of exactly two golden rarity items in all my play time. Chest armor and a pair of boots. That's it.The rest were items from chain quests. Most chain quests gave me one of these, such as the bounty quests once you got ALL of them... Same for hunting and the artifact quests for that old lady back in the first city or whatever.Best I got was for the vault quest for that Outrider and his missing family, which gave me a handful of golden rarity items... Mostly bony-looking guns, which were broken down for their perks since none of them aside from one LMG appealed to me due to their types and fire modes.And don't get me started on th'last boss, fighting in a crashed ship while your buddy'n his briefcase try to get the pods from orbit to drop.Hint: No checkpoint for the 2nd phase. That ♥♥♥♥ made me quit & uninstall.

_childDocuments_.review: There definitely is a great game somewhere in there, but we still have to find it.  The designs are neat, the animations are clean, the environments are interesting.But good god, the performance,  Every time I launch the game, the HUD will not load.  I have to quit to menu and relog in every time just to get the HUD back.  Alright, that only slows down the start by about 20 seconds so it's not so bad.  Where the performance issues become problematic is when they meet the difficulty of the game.  The game is split in 15 difficulties that you unlock as you go through.  Higher the difficulty, higher the reward - so yes, I'm always at the highest unlocked.  It usually still goes by smoothly and is very reasonable yet challenging, it IS well balanced.  But then some enemies will jump me and i get a frozen frame for about half a second, which can often mean the difference between life and death.  This rapidly gets VERY frustrating.  Then there are some rarer but still important control issues.  I play keyboard and mouse, and sometimes the vault or the cover key just decide to stop working until I die.  I had a moment where the "walk left" key stopped working also, resulting in infuriating deaths that feel unjust.Just to be clear, my computer is closer to a military grade weapon than anything else.  Game is on an SSD, I have a rtx3080 and an I9 processor so frame stuttering is pretty much unacceptable and is only a results of the game's poor performances.I truly believe this game could be amazing in a month or two, if the team decides they want to make it a success.  The difficulty is appropriate and welcomed, as long as the game allows you to really fight back.  The foundation is really solid, there is just a bunch of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ on top of it.• The ability to fast travel anywhere;  it's really annoying to have to travel to camp, take the car to teleport to another camp and then fast travel again.  It's just time consuming and doesn't bring anything other than a slowed pace.• The ability to see my number of shards (?).  It's kind of disappointing because I spent a few without having no idea how many I had.• Show the map in the mini map.  Right now it's just a radar for red dots - that's nice, but i've often just rolled into walls because I thought I could roll over some tall grass, only to be stuck and killed.  Show the wall, the chests are not hard to find anyways.
