_childDocuments_.review: This game is almost good!  It almost quickly became the "best game of the year" for me!  Until: I spent more game time with it. Outriders checked almost all the right boxes for a 3rd person shooter, looter, character skill building game, but for 1 very important one.  Whoever the idiots are who planned and approved all the empty square boxes (arenas) for the boss fights should be fired!  (It totally killed the game for me!)  EACH BOSS FIGHT IS ESSENTIALLY ONLY A VERY POORLY SCALED PISSING CONTEST!!!  You are placed in a well decorated somewhat empty square box of various dimensions and is tasked to face off with OP boss(es). The ONLY strategy available for you is to slug it out against anything that shows up in that box (who are now all OP, mostly never misses, and can see and shoot you through barriers) until someone drops - usually that's you, if you are wondering.  You just keep repeating this empty, hopeless and FRUSTRATING exercise until you eventually ends up with bigger, badder gear and a higher level than what the boss(es) are scripted to hand.  Then you move onto the next box.  That's it, that's the THE WHOLE GAME IN A NUT SHELL!  Very linear and non-story driven. No thinking, no planning needed!  All you need is your FRUSTRATION!  Another MINDLESS, MASSACRE, and MUTILATION game from the 80s but dressed with modern apparels.  Outriders could have been sooo much more!!!!  The big pay off only comes after the endgame and after you have acquired all the OP gears so to make yourself VERY, VERY OP (see youtube).  At which point, the hardest tasks remaining is to talk yourself into (via farming for things you most likely won't need) continue playing this game so you can use your new found VERY, VERY OP skill level to find enough stuff to kill continuously for 2 secs or more.  Also at this point, 99% of your real challenge becomes locating all bosses and enemies in that box (arena) so you can blindly finish them off in 5 secs or less, thus the Expeditions.  Questions here are; 1.Why would anyone need to play co-op when the game's hardest task has now becomes looking for enough things to continuously kill for 2 sec or more?  2. How does anyone have fun with a team member who's MO is just that?

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think the game looks bad. To be honest, I don't think any game made with Unreal nowadays looks ugly. I think Outriders biggest issue is that it doesn't sell the power fantasy well enough. It's like the game tells you that you're a badass, and then you go out and get your ass kicked by a series of mooks because you're not quite at the gear curve expected of you because of the world tier system.My other issue is the sort of lack of ability slots. It's clearly a concession imo for controllers and quick access. But I play on PC, with a lot more buttons to press. To follow on from the idea that you're supposed to be a badass, you spend a lot of time running around away from people. The game expects you to be aggressive, but then it puts things on 20+ second cooldowns. Which is an eternity in an action shooter. Even as a Devastator speccing the middle tree (Warden? - aka the tanks - tank) I had to run around for ages hiding. Skillup once said that the cover is for the badguys; I don't think that's quite true because of that reason I said before.Another issue is the usually very boring boss design. Minor spoilers but the Chrysaloid boss is a prime example of this that I can think of. It's a gigantic bullet sponge boss that has 2 phases to the fight, neither is particularly difficult in my mind, but takes ages because of it's hit points. This could be because of not keeping up with the world tier system, but if you don't and you're at this point there is basically nothing you can do about it because of how this section of the game is set up.Having said all that, when the game hits its combat loop and is in its stride it's quite fun, I just wish I could be using my abilities more. I wish I was playing more as an Altered rather than just a gun totting badass.Also; give me a damn pause button!

_childDocuments_.review: One of the few bright spots in the game is the weapons. The variety is extensive, and their design is imaginative. Weapons have unique properties and abilities, adding a level of strategy in choosing and using them.The shooting mechanics and combat are fairly enjoyable. The feel of shooting is satisfying, and the action sequences can be intense and adrenaline-pumping when everything works as it should.The graphical quality is very high. The environmental details, effects, and overall visual presentation are truly impressive. The game looks visually appealing and can capture your attention with its aesthetics.Missions are monotonous and quickly become repetitive, making the game boring.The story is a major letdown. Instead of an epic sci-fi saga, we get a banal and clichéd plot with flat, uninteresting characters. The dialogues are often poorly written, and the voice acting is subpar, further contributing to the lack of depth and meaning. Characters are emotionless, making it hard for players to empathize with their stories and motivations.

_childDocuments_.review: Outriders is by no means a perfect game, but it's damn fun to play. In my opinion, the good outweighs the bad. The premise of the game is fairly interesting, while the execution will be hit or miss for most people. When the game start off it gives the vibe of a Mass Effect: Andromeda type story, however things quickly go to ♥♥♥♥ and we fast forward a couple decades to see a pretty bleak situation. As the Outrider who was among those who first landed on Enoch, affected by the Anomaly, and then accidentally put into cryo for 30-ish years, you awake having newfound powers. Your goal is to find the source of the anomaly and hopefully put an end to it so Enoch can be a paradise for humans. Like I said, the execution is hit or miss, as the writing can be pretty rough, and the style People Can Fly is going for here (similar to Bulletstorm) won't be for everyone.There are four classes in this game, however I've only been playing thus far as the Pyromancer. I've been browsing the Outriders subreddit and watching youtube videos, and it's apparent that People Can Fly did a good job to make each class unique and sustainable by themselves. Weapons and armor aren't tied to specific classes, the only differences between classes are the skills they can use, and how they heal. For example, the Pyromancer heals whenever an enemy "marked" by one of their skills dies. (I.e. your skill burns a group of enemies and then you finish them off with your gun, you'll get health for all of those kills) The skills for each class and how they heal will inherently affect how you play.Reach a camp or large settlement. Get some side quests or continue main quest. Check out any vendors. Travel to a new area. Explore the area to its fullest to complete main quest and side quest objectives. Explore nooks and crannies of the map to find journal entries and loot chests. Take your hard-earned booty and either dismantle or sell to upgrade. Rinse and repeat. Combat requires an almost even mixture of skill use and guns. There is a cover system in the game which works similar to Gears of War, but this game really isn't meant to be played as a strict, tactical cover shooter like the Division. Enemies WILL either flank you or force you out of cover with perfectly tossed grenades, so you'll be on the move a lot. This works, because there's no automatic healing. There are no health packs. You regain health by playing aggressively. In the case of the Pyromancer, if I'm just stuck behind cover picking enemies off, I'm never going to heal. I need to be a little aggressive, cast my skills to aid my kills and regain health. And because there's obviously a limited range with my skills, I need to keep pushing and get close enough to enemies to do that. Occasionally during an encounter you'll be faced with tougher elite characters, and even tougher Altered enemies. The game really keeps you on your toes when you're facing a mob of enemies plus an Altered enemy. There's not a whole lot here that you haven't seen before. Basic weapon types (assault, submachine, long machine, shotgun, auto shotty, rifle, sniper rifle, pistol, revolver) and you get to equip two primaries with limited (it's not THAT limited, but I suppose it can eventually run out if you don't restock) and a secondary pistol or revolver with unlimited ammo. Basic gear types (helmet, chest piece, pants, boots). Color coded rarity levels. The rarer the item, the more mods they have equipped and the better those mods are. Selling equipment is simple. Sell it to get currency, use the currency to buy new equipment from the shops. Crafting however, is surprisingly a well fleshed system. Using fundamental resources (iron for weapons, leather for gear, titanium for epic or higher equipment, etc) you can do the following things when you craft:The crafting system really allows you to fine-tune all of your equipment to specifically fit your playstyle, and to compliment the skill loadout you choose. Once I began to really delve into the crafting menu and look at all of the possibilities, it's wealth of potential becomes obvious.Aside from the main quest and the typical side quests that we see in games like this, there are also Bounties and Monster Hunts. Both of these types of quests are unlocked as you get a little further in the main story and you reach Trench Town. You'll meet two different people in the tavern there. One who puts up the bounties, and one who is interested in hunting large monsters. There are 10 bounties and 10 monster hunts to complete. When you turn the contracts in, you'll receive Epic loot that matches your characters level.I haven't gotten there yet, but I've heard a lot about it and can't wait to get there. Endgame comes in the form of Expeditions. They unlock after you finish the main story and there are 15 of them. If you want to fully max out your character with the best gear possible, this is where you'll spend your time after completing the main story.These tier based system is Outriders dynamic difficulty scaling system. For the main game, you'll progress through 15 World Tiers. As you go up in tiers, enemies get tougher, but the rewards get better. For example, there's a better chance of enemies dropping rarer loot, and you can level up gear past your character level. Challenge tiers work the same way but they only effect the endgame Expedition content. At the end, if you reach WT15 and CT15, your character will be at a max level of 30, but will have level 50 weapons and gear.

_childDocuments_.review: NOTE: Contrary to the positive rating, I DO NOT recommend buying this game as it is now, or at full price.I'm going to give this a positive so people don't just see the rating and abandon it, because this game DOES have a lot of potential, especially if you're into multiplayer PvE TPS games. That being said, I totally get why someone wouldn't care for it as is. It needs a lot more time and thought put into making this game something different, especially with a game giant like Squeenix behind it. There's no reason for it to feel generic as it does with everything it has going for it. The pleasing visuals and great feeling combat are held up by the generic non-combat quest hub into instanced combat area speedbump that makes this kind of game a drag to play unless you have friends that you enjoy running the same missions (there aren't many per area) over and over with for the rush of the RNG, which is pretty much the whole loot system. Probably sounds boringly familiar if you've played a looter-shooter in the last decade. The character customization is also a joke. You get like a handful of faces (prefab, no further options or sliders) and even less skin colors. Pretty much every male hairstyle makes you look like a hipster joined the service. No voice or body options, so you're stuck looking like a Hollywood action movie stunt-double with even worse lines. Like, I'd have taken a text-based protagonist over the kind of cringe-worthy tough guy crap you have to put up with every time he speaks. It's bad. Punish whoever wrote that garbage.It DOES look good though, and doesn't run as roughly as a few other recent and more notorious release flops, especially on mid to lower spec rigs. The gunplay and powers play pretty solid, other than enemies becoming bullet sponges if you aren't geared at your highest possible level. Not being able to 1-shot a trash mob by shooting it in the head with a sniper rifle because it's 2 levels lower than your maximum equip limit feels like bogus no matter how you look at it. This isn't Halo. Leave surviving sniper rounds to the head with that franchise... But hey! The story isn't a total wash (if you can put up with the main character's cardboard action star personality).ANYHOW, if they fleshed out this game a bit (lot) more, it could definitely be a hit. Things that I'd love to see:-World needs to feel more open and less static. -A LOT MORE customization/personalization. Character needs to feel more like your own rather than just a lame reskin of everyone else's.-Damage numbers reworked. Sniping someone twice/Sinking an entire LMG mag into an enemy makes people feel they're going to war with pellet guns.Now let's see what they do with their game in the next few months to a year. Total coin toss.

_childDocuments_.review: At the time of writing, I have almost 40 hours spent in Outriders. TL;DR: It's a fun game, lots of loot and you don't feel like you are grinding for better gear. The story has humor in it to break up the otherwise 'end of the world for the second time' tone, through an ongoing war and hostile nature of Enoch the planet you are on. I'm not sure I'm halfway through the story, but I've done all side quests available so far. There's plenty to keep you playing.You can be forgiven for feeling like there is a generic story at the start. Things don't go as planned and quite soon you find factions have been fighting it out for decades as a battle for survival in a hostile alien world of Enoch, which doesn't seem to like the arrival of new travelers.The story gets better as you venture through and has left me wanting to continue playing to discover the secrets of Enoch. There is plenty of humor in the writing. No other video game has made me laugh at events or dialogue (mainly through the main quest) than any other video game I've played in the last 30 years. There is one side quest when you reach Trench Town, which had an absolutely hilarious ending.There is plenty to keep you going, at 40 hours I have all the available side quest completed, and maybe I'm around halfway through the story? An assumption based on where I am on the map.I'm now level 27 and just recently gained 3 legendary weapons to equip.The gunplay is very good, guns available range from Shotguns, to various types of assault rifles (inc. submachine guns) to sniper rifles. Now and then I miss not having any grenades, but that is where your anomaly powers come in.  Guns have mod slots applying status effects on enemies, increasing damage/critical shots, and applying additional damage from either just shooting an enemy to cause lightning to strike them from above, or getting kills on frozen enemies to cause them to explode damaging anyone around.You get to select 3 out of 8 anomaly powers (you unlock them as you level up). These skills vary depending on your class (I went for Trickster), and you would be best investing your skill points into a single tree path for best effect rather than trying to spread them around.Your armor allows for skill slots that have various effects on your skills (i.e. increasing duration of the effect of the skill, adding a second activation before cooldown, increasing your armor for rolling/being out or in cover, etc). You can change the skill in the mod slot to customize and cater and get the best out of the skills you like to use the most. Skills aren't a equip once and use forever, there have been many times where I needed to change up skills to deal with situations (usually with boss encounters).You will want to explore the areas of Enoch as much as you can. There are plenty of equipment crates scattered around which you could easily miss if you just follow the guide marker. At the start, you are rewarded quite well with these locations, but then they feel like they get less, where you will go around edges for nooks and crannies which feel like there should be a crate but there isn't.Same with the glowing blue rocks which you will want to mine to gain resources for upgrading your gear. Having said that, I have plenty of resources and you can always recycle unwanted equipment to make up for any lack.As you level up you also unlock world tiers. This is your difficulty level. At times you will find certain encounters more difficult than others. I found switch up weapons and skills is enough to overcome these hurdles. But, If you are really struggling you can lower the tier (at the expense of less quality loot) to keep your progression going.Its clear Outriders lack polish in certain aspects, mostly interaction events. You'll find yourself holding down the E key just for your character to wiggle as they trying to interact with a gate or to mine rock. You'll be tempted to try and adjust your position, it's best that you just interact again without moving your character. I've found no more than by the 3rd time the interaction will happen.Animations are off in places: scrunching up a wanted poster as it levitates a couple of meters off to your side, or suddenly jumping off location as you interact with a switch to open a gateThere are varying audio levels during the dialogue when characters are speaking over the radios. At times the audio will just increase quite noticeably.Others have reported more game-breaking bugs like lost inventory and multiple crashes. The game has only crashed on me twice in the 40 hours played. I have not come across the inventory wipe bug, but then I have not tried playing with others and have soloed the entire game so far.I've enjoyed what I've played so far and have not been bored. I played the game in some large stints, I have a bit of an addiction playing Outriders wanting better loot and continue on with the story.For me, it's definitely worth a buy.

_childDocuments_.review: It's very hard to decide whether or not I should give this game: a "yes" or "No" recommendation; Developed by 'People Can Fly'; the same people who made Bulletstorm and Painkillers comes in with this always online multiplayer loot shooter that takes notes from other looter shooters in the past like Destiny, Borderlands, etc. What is OUTRIDERS? Developed by "People Can Fly" you and two other buddies or solo journey across the planet Enoch as you try to understand the "Anomaly" all the while protecting the last bastion of humanity against other humans, monsters and "altered" (Altered are essentially "Guardians").The story is total B movie nonsense- at least the lore is there for you to discover, straight and to the point rather than Destiny where it can take many lore dives just to find the answer you are looking for!You have 4 main classes to choose from with many ways you can play. However, as of this time due to the infamous "Nerf patch" i can't really say which is the best class because the 'nerf patch' really did some major damage across the board; in addition crossplay is off, and there is an inventory wipe bug, and of course; server issues.While the shooting and using your powers is fascinating and fun, the loot drops (to me anyways) are fine, there not under or over excessive.  Customization is limited, but you can customize in the 'social hub' (if you want to call it that), you can skip the tutorial, and there is a demo for this game; which by the way you can do a transfer over when you buy the full game which is nice.Audio and visuals play it's part nicely; although the cutscenes need be tone down because there is a lot of it and sometimes unnecessary in addition some of the visuals palette can be tone down just a bit.Overall, the best comparison to this game is Destiny; where there are pretty cool concepts, but executed in pieces and not a full puzzle set- if that makes any sense; Try the demo, see for yourself if you like it- and if so wait for deep sale and the patches to be put out because oof it ain't ready (yet) to be a full $60 title.

_childDocuments_.review: DISCLAIMER: I HAVEN'T BEATEN THE ENTIRE GAME SO TAKE THIS WITH A GRAIN OF SALT. (I am pretty confident with what I'm saying though)Look, this game isn't that good. Though the bugs really suck in this game, a lot of people have covered them, so I'm going to cover my biggest gripe in the game: the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ repetition and corniness. The story isn't anything special. The voice acting is mediocre at best, almost silly in some cases. The gameplay, while satisfying in some cases, boils down to the same mission being played over and over, changing the scenery and some of the enemies in each one. I also never feel like I need to approach each level or mission in a different way. I always pick some off from afar with a sniper or something of that nature and then rush in with a shotgun. That's the gameplay. Disappointing.On to some good stuff though. While it is repetitive, the powers are satisfying to use from what I've gathered (I've only played with the Devastator class). The weaponry is unique, especially with the modding system. I love looter shooters, so the progression is mildly entertaining even with all the flaws. And, one of the bigger pieces, I really do enjoy the way this game looks. It's nice to go from a war-torn area to a hectic-peaceful summit that's both snowy and volcanic. Pretty great.Overall, this game is both good and bad. Keep in mind, again, I haven't completely beaten it, so take this with a grain of salt. From what I've experienced, definitely not worth a full price, but if it's ever on sale, try it if you want to. I don't recommend it, but who am I to tell you what to do.The biggest kick in the balls is that I'm going to keep on playing just to beat it. 4/10Update: I played the game for a bit longer, got some more gear, progressed a bit in the story. I learned some things:1. I like the modding system for weapons and armor. This is something I didn't touch on before in my initial review, but it is a nice system. It makes sure that you can cater to your specific build, whether you want to be more defensive or offensive, cause more damage or heal yourself, etc. There are plenty of options and that part of the game deserves some merit.2. This game is long and tedious. At this point, I feel like I've been playing the same mission for hours, and the repetitiveness is wearing me down. I tried to give myself some time to cool down so I could finish it, but I've found that I'm really not too invested in the goofy story, nor am I particularly wanting to continue doing the same thing over and over and over.In the end, I've given this game some chances, stuck around to see it through, and I couldn't make it all the way through. Not a terrible game, just not too great by any means. This game isn't on sale anymore so I wouldn't recommend buying it. Still a 4/10

_childDocuments_.review: Outriders has a lot of potential if the devs can sort out the bugs and other issues asap. It's a lot of fun, I love the progression system and the combat. It's a shame the whole cover fire is wasted, but that was a weird decision putting a cover system in a game where the endgame is time-trials. Nobody uses cover in the endgame expeditions. The game crashes have eased up a lot, although they do still occur on occasion. The loot sometimes drops for the wrong class spec, and you can even lose all your inventory items when you try and matchmake. But, these issues are a priority and updates on social media are keeping the player-base in touch. My biggest criticism of the game is that it's more a single player experience, rather than mult-player, You can party with 1-3 players (4 would have been better, to incorporate all the classes) but the matchmaking is ♥♥♥♥, and the netcode and servers are absolute garbage. It's a game of Russian roulette as to whether the map will rubber-band or lag out in party's, and if the "host" disconnects, the rest of the team crashes or DC's as well. I can only play with my Steam buddies, if I want to have a good time in group-play in Outriders.   I'm at the point now though, where there is nothing else to do. Once you've clocked the expeditions and timed them on gold, there is nothing left. And with Outriders not being a live service game with regular updates, story, or expedition missions, things are going to get stale very quickly.

_childDocuments_.review: 18 hours played in full game and over 40 in the demo (NO SPOILERS in this review)Fun game, lots of customization, great statistic work on behalf of people can fly.  Leave you wanting to get more loot and try new builds and see what you can come up with to be OP. Story is kind of a played out sci-fi story, but still makes you want to finish it and understand what happened (and happens).  Voice actor for the male character models is a bit lackluster in emotion, as I have both female and male characters and the female voice actor does a bit better in most scenes. once unlocked, is super thorough and very well put together, and at this point I can see the point of the gear farm that will be required to min max builds but I don't feel it getting old as fast as I did with Anthem or Division 2.It's different in a good way, looks like a cover shooter, but plays like an intense firefight where cover is a disadvantage for the outriders at certain points, as the AI is pretty good and you will be pushed out by grenades shortly after utilizing cover or trying to stay in it for long.  The weapon and character model animations make the effects of skills and bullet hits super enticing and satisfying in a way that makes you seem like you are actually doing something to the enemies. The world tiers are challenging at points that make you rethink your gear and skill choices and will have to determine an action plan based on prioritizing enemies and skills before just running in and blasting up the place, but still doable solo if that is your play style. super fun, and awesome working with others to create a meta in taking down bosses and mini-bosses as well as the small dungeon crawling sections. I'm excited to see what the endgame content has to offer more of in this situation. A few of the bosses are reminiscent of some other game, if the mechanics continue the way I have seen already, it looks to be a fun time, kind of like raids or trials from an MMO standpoint but with 3 players.  If they increase the team size in the future for even more extremely hard content I could see that elongating the lifespan of the game. More personal research is needed.Fairly glitch free upon release, a few server drops initially at release, to be expected on day one especially with being free on game pass, only issues I have experienced are frame locked at 60fps after exiting a cut scene, easily rectified by hitting the pause menu (esc) and then right back to the game, a few item interactions have glitched the character model to one direction or another but doesn't break the game.  Options to fix the horrible camera shake and the 30fps frame lock in cut scenes was a great addition by the devs. Edit: servers wont stay connected, kinda irritating to say the least, would appreciate it if the game had a standalone solo mode where you weren't connected to their servers so you could play that would be greeaaaaaaaat.Very similar to a few other games, like the division 2, Anthem, Destiny 2, Gears of War, Diablo, and Borderlands.  With that out of the way, since looter shooters have been tried and failed multiple times *cough* looking at you BIOware *cough* its done

_childDocuments_.review: Reached WT15 and CT15+Eye solo. For the price of the game, i would say it should be around $40. Story wise, same usual looter shooter concept.As for amount of Content, i would say, after the campaign (end game), there is nothing much to do, once you are fully grinded up. Other than repeating the same thing with other class. As for Unique build, there are not many mix and matches of builds, as a lot of skills and mods are inbalance which does not scale properly towards the endgame grind, mobs have extremely high tankiness unless you play with certain build to bypass it. (Why would you use other builds, when it takes 1 to 2 second to kill a mob, and other "not meta" skills takes over 10 times the amount of effort to do it, bossing is worst.)Difficulty was kind of weird, it started out normal, and around mid-game, it was hard (basically you will be down more often, unless you lower down the difficulty; I did not lower it down, because of gear progression). Towards almost unlocking endgame, it became quite easy, until 1 of the boss which starts with an initial 'Y'. The 'Y' boss, is able to CC you down, while your character animation of getting up will not stop you from being CC-ed to death.In Endgame, it starts out easy, because it does not scale with the story difficulty and had its own difficulty. As you progress, the difficulty rise extremely high, due to under powered gears. The only way to solo progress is to Fail and open 'Failed Gear Crates', which enables you to get gear match of that difficulty level. Once your progressing smoothly, you will find the game quite easy until the final current endgame boss. Strangely the boss is not hard, it is the mob, that spawn which have the same mechanics as the 'Y' boss in the campaign, which spawn 2 of it. Once those two are down, the boss fight can be said to be cleared, unless your using a funny build, that does not melt the boss. As for now, we are just waiting for new content... which i would not think it will be available in 3 ~ 5 months, due to all the bugs and developer funny "balance patch".

_childDocuments_.review: I should have listened to my inner voice the third week into playing the demo and not ended up pre-ordering this for launch.  It was fun that first week then by the second week and third I wasn't playing it much figuring I'd wait till release.  That should have told me I could skip it as I didn't have the desire to login for days at a time.  To be perfectly honest at full price it's just not worth it for the issues involved to whats offered.  30ish? Sure I'd hold my nose and overlook the flaws and wait it out, but at full AAA price of 60 no it better be spotless from the get go and playable on and offline.  I say offline as well as even though it isn't a game as service like a Destiny, you couldn't tell with the server connection issues that were prevalent a times and I won't even go into the coop matchmaking since I avoided that once inventory issues were known to stem from that.   I tried to overlook the fact that the maps were small/confined in design that reminded me of UE3 era MMO's where you're basically in a small designed area for a "zone" instead of what I prefer  in a open world game to go anywhere at a time types like a Ghost Recon Breakpoint etc or if confined to maps a Division type of design..  I tried to get that they were going for a looter shooter more like Diablo instead of the ones I mentioned, but confined is still confined.  The environments were nicely done, can't fault the art/design department side of the game, but otherwise that leads to the biggest flaw of the game of the encounters/AI for mobs.  Frankly they're stupid, not stupid in a AI sense but stupid in design.  I used to tank and heal in MMO's so I don't mind hard encounters, just don't give me some BS poorly designed and say it's "hard.  You want flying bosses/mini-bosses fine do it, but don't have them basically have no cooldowns on their attacks and have homing ranged attacks of spit for the most part.  They're creatures spitting or firing abilities off not mechanics shooting guided weaponry.  If that isn't bad enough throw in a few ground attacking ones that spam their abilities at the same time.  Sure there are ground markers for their cone of attacks but when they all go off at once and through objects, mind you this is while you're being attack from other trash, you won't see the ground markers at times since they are all one color that blends into the screen indicators while you're being attacked, bled, or shield depletions.  In other words change the dam shaders to not be the same color.   I'm just going to stop here before it becomes a full on wall of text while bringing up everything I hate about the game that I had high hopes for from the demo they released.  Wait for a sale, or maybe EGS will throw it as a freebie down the road, play through for the storyline and place it on the same shelf to be compared with Anthem as such a game concept that was squandered.

You pay a lot of money for a supposedly AAA game then it falls flat out of the gate. It SUCKS.However, I'm reviewing what I've been able to play of the game so far. Combat is snappy, the loot-shoot cycle is addicting, and I'm so invested in the world of Enoch. I know I'm going to sink a lot of time into this game once the technical issues are out of the way. It has all the makings of a master-class experience. However, hold off if you're easily incensed by Day One hiccups. Very few modern games--especially that aim for this kind of scope--release without a hitch. And before someone comments that old games didn't have these issues, you're right; they had completely different issues that could never be fixed and were also far less complex. You'd think that Cyberpunk would've taught a lot of consumers about not buying in right away if they're afraid to wait.As for people complaining about online-only when they're playing single-player... _childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Pretty good game to play when brain is turned off, probably better if co-op, but balance isn't great.Some specific observations:1) Game crashed a bit often for a few hours after the 7/17 patch, but other that no real stability issues or serious bugs in 100 hours of playtime. That being said, stuff like captain hunter/sharp eye/deathshield etc. are almost mandatory for endgame builds. Again, the gameplay loop is sufficiently satisfying to keep you grinding for gear, but it would be nice if there was an item rebalance sometime soon.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish Steam had a "so-so" or a "meh" rating, as this game falls squarely into that category. Personally, the game runs well for me. 4k @ 60fps Ultra settings no problem with an RTX2070 and a Ryzen 2700x. Other similar games arent quite as good performance wise so that's definitely a plus.The storyline is alright. Contains a few tropes here and there but nothing cringey or overpowering. No dumb plot twists or convoluted plots, just a simple premise and a decent execution. The game has a good sense of humour, not being ridiculous in its jokes or premises but quite down to earth (or down to Enoch) in their execution and grittiness. Voice acting is another hit or miss, with most of the main characters being very well voice acted and feeling alive, with a few being quite bad or just bland. The gunplay is decent, a decent variety of gun types and customisation options. The "mod" system is also very nice, lots of room to play around and work up tactics, playstyles etc.Although there is a large variety of weapons, mods and the 4 classes with 8 skills each, I'm not sure about the replayability of the game as it's much less an RPG in the traditional sense and more a Linear Action-Dungeon Looter, something akin to Destiny, Diablo, Torchlight. The enemy variety is, again, mediocre. Humanoid enemies are usually reskins of the same 6 or 7 unit types, and each monster species has between 2 to 5 varieties. While that sounds decent enough, many of the varieties are just visual reskins. Boss fights is another hit or miss. Some of the bossfights are quite unique and I would even say enjoyable, whilst others are terrible. The last Boss is hands down the worst bossfight I have ever seen and boy have I seen some ♥♥♥♥. Utterly atrocious.The game is decent enough, quite enjoyable to sink your time into. Fun with a friend or two. Probably something you'll only play through once, maybe once again in several years when that one broke friend buys a copy for £10.I wish I could give a mediocre score but since I can't, I don't think I could recommend this to anyone for the full price. It's decent enough but I don't think I could justify shilling this game to anyone.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a masterpiece of the sci-fi shooter RPG genre! The base campaign is designed around a 30 level cap but there is also an expansion which I have just reached after finishing the base campaign just a couple minutes ago. At this stage in all shooters I am ready to move on due to the monotony having been playing the same game, with the same mechanics and crafting system for many hours on end. HOWEVER not with this game! I am anxious to go back into a few of the main campaign side quests I left undone then progress onto the expansion. Enemies seem to scale with your current level even in the main campaign so all of this is like new content that I "skipped" over in my rush to finish the main campaign story line.The real draw is the amazing crafting system which seems like a bit much at first but you quickly get the hang of it as you play the game. I can honestly see myself playing for another 50-100 hours or more just to create the perfect Outrider for my game style. I already achieved this for the main campaign BUT the final boss level had me dying several times as I realized I had used the amazing strategy capabilities in this game to get to the end a couple levels too low! The fact that I was able to use strategy to push forward and enjoy the game at the higher levels while being a level or two too low is proof of the depth of game play on offer with this game! This is a form of chess not tic-tac-toe as so many shooters these days are!As a developer trust me when I tell you the AI in this game is top notch. If you try there are some choke points in some areas you can funnel enemies into and knock them down as they come through but in most cases battle areas are expansive with multiple pathways to protect. Also the enemy has "tank" characters that will storm your position along with ancillary forces if you sit at it too long as a sniper in a shooter such as this is apt to do. It is truly brilliant shooter design to make such a game enjoyable for all play styles. I am a sniper at heart so when these enemy rushes came I had to use the tricks up my sleeve (special skills) to stave them off then return to the long distance mayhem.The story is top notch and the voice acting is superb in the English version (the one I play). The IGN review said, "The game takes its story a bit too seriously..". For me this is one of the best parts of Outrider.  It is a true sci-fi classic as the story is CLASSIC sci-fi from its golden age. Not to spoil it for you but generation ships and their idiosyncrasies form the main basis of the story. If humanity ever goes to another star system as of current scientific understanding it will be sub-light which will require generation ships. It feels good to see a top notch sci-fi shooter embrace this staple of the golden age of sci-fi and do it justice. Also the constraints set were realistic as per the technology and the time frames.I felt connected with the characters, the story flow was very well done, levels were also very well designed. Difficulty was well balanced but at the higher game difficulty settings you will probably stop playing due to the difficulty spikes at those higher difficulty settings. Be warned, take it slow and find your ideal setting to enjoy this game to the fullest. I would strongly recommend any true sci-fi fan get this game and play it at the lower difficulty settings for just the story. That's how good this game's story arc is. The writing is also top notch and a hard core sci-fi story NEEDS to take itself too seriously sometimes. I'd give this a 10/10. I am VERY happy I purchased and played this game. I was expecting to be done with it by now and instead I have my "forever RPG shooter" at least for a while. I feel like how I felt playing the original Borderlands while in the middle of the story but this is past the end of the story! I let all of the credits roll at the end and it ran for what felt like 15 minutes! These guys take game AI seriously and in a multiplayer game that is almost unheard off. They have created a true masterpiece of a shooter that also makes you part of an epic sci-fi story. This harkens back to a time when story had to make up for level size and content. Game makers had to truly invest in the story. This art has faded away as technology has allowed games to dump so much content story is forgotten. I deeply enjoyed the Outrider experience and if you like what you read in this review I advise you give the game a try. Thus concludes my review on the base campaign of Outriders.

_childDocuments_.review: Worldslayer: New Horizon Update: Honestly the game is vastly improved from a stability perspective. The new expeditions are pretty neat. The lag online is there, but less terrible since no one actually plays this game. Performance is improved, frames are fine now. The game still doesn't have any depth or variety in abilities, skills, or loot though. Set based gear is boring a la Diablo 3.  Hopefully the expansion addresses some of these things, but it doesn't look promising. There's fun to be had here, but I definitely still wouldn't recommend the game unless its vastly discounted. I tricked myself into purchasing this game despite not enjoying the demo. Playing Remnant from the Ashes this past month on PS+ to 100% was a lot of fun and I was in search of something similar and this game happened to come out. I thought the developers were very transparent in marketing leading up the the release and outlined their scope very distinctly so it seemed worth giving them a shot. In the end the game is an okay looter shooter that's rather shallow for the most part, but is a decent time passer while watching a stream or something else more engaging. It has a number of problems that leads me to not want to recommend it. For reference, I finished the game solo at WT 13 as the trickster and level 30 and completed a handful of expeditions up to about CT 7 just to try it out.In the end I wouldn't recommend this game especially at full price on PC. If this was available on PC game pass the package would be more excusable. I think the game is an okay side distraction, but it won't have any staying power unless the mods and classes were more diverse. Everything about the game feels like it misses the mark. Every action in the game is split into 15 cut scenes like opening a door, climbing a wall, boss transitions, its all jarring. Nothing about the story is interesting. The battlefields are all identical with the same enemy recolors. The game in my opinion doesn't have any staying power. I would just get Remnant: From the Ashes for a fairly priced, vastly superior game in every single aspect (including working coop that doesn't delete your inventory) and not have to deal with any server issues or shortcomings.

_childDocuments_.review: It's sad to see that there is so many negative reviews for the game when in reality it is a fantastic looter shooter. There is issues currently with the servers causing numerous disconnects but I don't think that means it deserves leaving a negative review when it will be fixed some time soon. This game genuinely makes you feel like a god only a few hours in as all of the powers and abilities are unique and fun to use, the way enemies just explode into mist or disintegrate depending on the class you are using truly makes you feel like a beast.The armor and weapons are also fantastic to use and collect as there is dozens of unique modifiers and abilities for you to collect with each upgrade to armor you get allowing you to essentially play a entirely different play style every few levels keeping things fresh and exciting. The crafting system also allows for some pretty deep customization to how you play your character as you are able to change one of the mods on any weapons or armor you are using into a different mod you have collected by dismantling older gear. For example with my devastator I crafted a set of armor and weapons that essentially allow me to life steal and regen health very quickly as I kill enemies allowing me to steam roll through the fodder and weaker enemies.The main downside I have with the game is that there is a lot of small loading screens when you go from one area to another that can get quite frustrating. There will be a cut scene that is 3 seconds long just showing your character jumping over a gap or opening a door that just seems not needed.Overall I am having a blast playing this game and I really think anyone who is on the fence about the game because of the mixed reviews should give it a shot and see for yourself if you enjoy it or not.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic Game!I hesitated a long time before buying this game due to the relatively high number of bad reviews, but I thoroughly enjoyed it and I don't know why there isn't more hype around it!I think it got a lot of bad reviews because apparently it had/has a lot of technical issues, but I didn't have any problems, it runs smoothly on my middle-class-laptop, didn't crash once, no bugs at all, only 2 disconnects in over 40 hours playing time.The guns all feel great an give satisfying feedback, the skills feel really powerfull, the mix between shooting and skills works perfectly, the path-of-exile-like way to mod your skills through your gear and the passive-talent-tree a great ideas, as are the world tiers that determine the difficulty.The mix between human enemies, where you have to aim and take cover and the monsters, where you can just blast off ensure a certain variety in gameplay.Graphics are nice to and story is ok.Some things could have been better though:- although the guns feel great, they could have been a bit more creative, basically there are just three types of guns, shotguns, machine guns and sniper rifles (plus pistols that i never used). In a science fiction shooter on an alien planet that's a bit boring- some bosses are bullit sponges, escpecially the last one- you get your last active skill at level 23, your last passsive skillpoints at level 30, after that the only progression you get ist through loot. Also there aren't any new gameplay mechanics in the late game, sometimes it gets a bit repetitive in the end.- in my opinion, they could focus even more on the rpg aspects, more active skills, being able to equip more than 3 at the same time, more different ways to built your character.But all in all it was a great game, I can thoroughly recommend it.I usually don't play games twice since I'm trying to reduce my pile of shame, but I'm really tempted with this one, to try another character.

_childDocuments_.review: I am doing an early review because I am seeing tons of people with less than an hour played trying to bomb this game. First off, what game in the last 10+ years that is a live service game has released without issues... Hell, even games that have been in this business for years (WoW, FF14, Destiny, etc.) STILL to this day have issues on launch. So... Ignoring the privileged that think games should launch at an absolute perfect state with no room to grow... :)The game is fun as hell. From a purely gameplay perspective, it hooks you in almost immediately. It thrust you into the story from the tutorial and sets you up to push forward to figure out "what next...". Whether you jump in with friends and go on a warpath destroying everything in your path or go it alone facing the vast world and extremely challenging difficulty curve. Diving into the game's world immediately reminds you of some of your favorite games. I have heard, "It feels like gears... Looks like Mass Effect... Plays like Destiny... Fantasy Division...This reminds me of the good parts of Anthem..." the list goes on. You can clearly see that this game was inspired by so many games that came before it while maintaining its own unique identity in the lootershooter realm. For me the story feels a bit forced, but let's be real... most of us are not playing for the story anyways. We are just here to shoot, loot, and get epic gear.In terms of the visuals, the game is gorgeous. There are clipping issues, and some visual designs that I don't personally agree with, but I can tell the effort was put in to really polish specific areas of the game.The sound is the major sore thumb for me right now. I am noticing a lot of audio bugs (gun getting extremely loud when activating skills, voices in general, random sounds that don't belong...). It kind of ruins a bit of that immersive value, but I assume this will resolve as the game goes on (as it is a live service game). Bugs.... There are many, but this is the life of BRAND NEW GAME. Find the bugs, point them out. If it is game breaking or makes it so you can't progress or use something correctly, just report it to them so they can queue it up for fixing. WE are the ultimate playtesters/QA because if we can ride on a rocket into combat wearing the severed head of our enemy as a crown, we will. The game has had a strong start and I think we are in for a treat as time goes on. Don't look at the thumbs down that have less than an hour and be skeptical if they have played less than 3 (that is most likely the demo experience for most). Grab your friends and have a great time or go it alone and face challenging foes. I am sure you will enjoy it either way.

_childDocuments_.review: I played the demo... enjoyed it enough... I bought the game on launch day, played it whenever work wasn't keeping me from it.  I was having a hard time, but then I read some stuff that basically pointed out I was doing it wrong.  the game forces you in to certain builds essentially.  you pretty much have to use the DOT bullet ability or you will never have enough ammo to make it through the higher tiers.  not only that, you have to mod you gear to enhance that ability or same story.  No clue how the 1 class that doesn't have a DOT bullet ability fairs... I'm guessing poorly without help.  in  any case, I adjusted my skills and remodded my gear, and the difference was massive!  I was easily able to progress where I had gotten stuck before.  now the trick was always killing a mob before I ran out of DOT bullets so that it would auto refill my clip with more DOT bullets, as per the mods added to my game.  I had to switch from sniper rifles to an assault rifle with a high capacity clip but now I was able to kill things I had a lot of trouble with before.  I still died some times... usually because something was hitting me from somewhere and I couldn't even see where it was coming from, so as I frantically tried to find someplace safe to take cover, they would keep shooting me from who knows where till i died.  still it was fun and I was enjoying it, right up until they kicked me out of my single player game for "maintenance"... the next day when I logged in, I was getting my ass kicked again.  not quite as bad as before... but it was just taking too long to kill stuff and I kept getting overrun.  at first I thought it was just the new area I had entered.  I reset my story point back to the volcano boss and fought it again... even that was harder than before.  then I thought maybe it was the world tier I was in now... i thought I had been in the same tier the previous night, but maybe I had leveled up and been too busy fighting for my life to notice... I ran the volcano boss several times... reset back to the farthest point I had made it so far.  and decided to go after some of the bounties.  the one in the very first zone, which I would expect to be the easiest... tore me apart... after many tries I finally got him and moved on to the one in the next zone, and then the first beast mark on the map and so on.  each one was more difficult than it should have been.  one of the beasts I killed easily... but only because it bugged and acted like there was a wall between us, i.e. just stood there, while I shot it.  all the bounties/beasts I tried, I got overrun and had a hell of a time killing them, to the point it got really tedious.  well, I found out after the fact that "maintenance" was a nerf and now I do less damage.  allegedly just 15% less, but it really feels far more significant than 15%.  now the game is a frustrating chore to play and I have pretty much lost interest.  thanks a lot devs for ruining my fun!

_childDocuments_.review: Very nice game. Very nice graphics. Way better than the demo that is slow & rigid!This is Diablo4 as third person shooter.The pace is different from TheDivision. This is not a cover shooter.You have to dodge ennemies attack and position yourself at the good distance to have life leech on attacks (depending on you class you need to be either close or far range from your target).The level of the items you can have is linked to the difficulty level you play. You can only play a higher difficulty if you can sustain the one before... (it as has an XP bar to fill) This is a very NICE system. I would love that in Diablo4.Most of the power you get is linked to the combination of item+class talents you choose (theory crafting). You have 30lvl (unlock class talent tree) + 15 Ilvl to grind on base game.Expansion adds a little more story, more expedition/random dungeon, more item talents, more ilvel to grind, more difficulty levels. So it's just the continuation. Not necessary as the base game has lot of content already.

_childDocuments_.review: Outriders captivated me with it's well designed world and fun story. Unfortunately that's all I can say has immersed me because I have no desire to play the raids after beating the campaign. I don't see the point in repeating a mission over and over again in hopes of a new item dropping that will make it easier to unlock other items. That's the only thing you can do with the items anyway since there's no more plot after the campaign besides some interesting side missions. But if you are like me and only cared for the campaign, you should be satisfied for a solid 30-40 hours. It will be shorter if you play with a friend (if you somehow know someone who wants to play this game) since coop is easier. Overall I did really enjoy the storyline along with the characters and would look forward to a sequel and/or expansion in the future that continues the story.

_childDocuments_.review: 8.5/10 - A few minor buggaboos aside, this is a fantastic little looter shooter that could well end up being a modern classic...so long as the devs are on the ball. Don't let the review bombing put you off.Full review below:= Intro =Been waiting for this one for ages, as I'm a sucker for loot games and really like People Can Fly as a developer.= Gameplay: 8/10 =It's very much Gears of War by way of Destiny, with a hint of Borderlands. You play a single, powerful character, choosing one of four classes and mowing down hundreds of enemies in the hopes of getting cool gear. While it's not as wacky as Borderlands, it plays well and it always feels like there is something new around the corner...potentially.While this is a cover based shooter, you'll likely find yourself running and gunning more than sticking to walls (at least unless you are playing a Technomancer ie. doing it wrong). Guns are mostly standard machineguns, sniper rifles and shotguns, with a few flavors of each. Your character can also equip 3 (out of 8) unique abilities, which are all decently powerful and varied.Gear is decent - offering both changes to your abilities and other modifiers, which can allow you to specialize your character in a nicely varied number of ways. Do you want to focus on one skill, or diversify? Do you want to focus on augmenting your gunplay, or rather utilize your skills as your main method of killing?It all flows well, aside from the extremely punishing difficulty (as someone who's beaten Blood on Extra Crispy, let me tell you that this game occasionally makes me want to eat a kitten) and the boss fights I've seen thus far (in particular a certain lava spider) are deserving of special recognition.However, there are a few major problems. Firstly, the balance between guns is wonky. Automatic rifles are head and shoulders better than most other choices, with submachineguns falling off too fast to be all that useful and shotguns having such a minute maximum ammo limit (lower than sniper rifles!) that it honestly baffles me.Beyond this, the developers thought that it would be a fantastic idea to nerf loot droprates between the demo and full version by several hundred percent, making epics insanely rare and legendaries...well, I haven't seen one in over 12 hours of gaming. Gah.The difficulty can also be a little much at times - enemies can chunk your hp in a matter of seconds, and can be major bullet sponges. If droprates were a tad more generous (seriously, the devs could triple legendary drops and they would still feel chintzy) you could probably grind to get past harder sections, but as things stand, you'll dread levelling up as enemies will be getting a major boost, and you won't be.There are also a number of minor to major bugs, but - as far as a day 1 online game release goes - it's not that bad. Yes, there is an Nvidia driver issue at present, but I can hardly blame the devs for that.= Graphics & Audio : 7/10 =The game looks...decent. A bit washed out, and special abilities are a little meh visually, but nothing to complain about, and it runs fairly well at 4k on my 1080ti, with some settings turned down. It is always great to play a game where I can see places I will visit later in the distance.The audio though...ugh. Most guns sound okay (aside from enemy miniguns, which sound like someone dropped a rabbit into a blender) but the voicework is hilariously bad and the music may as well not be there for how bland it is.= Value: 9.5/10 =Holy crap, is there a lot of game here. 14 hours in and I don't think I'm halfway through the campaign yet, and still have tons of sidequests, hunts, bounties and the like to do. And that's before touching on endgame, which I doubt I'll be seeing before next week. It's so nice to see a game that isn't afraid to run a little longer.Beyond this, there isn't a single microtransaction in sight. Good on you, devs.= Overall =+ Fun shooting+ Challenging+ Nice mix of OTS shooting and cover based shooting+ Compelling loot (if it ever drops)- Droprates are far too low- Difficulty, even at middle tiers is perhaps a little too punishing- Some bugs- Enemy variety is a tad lackingAt the end of the day, this is a pretty damn good game and I can foresee me getting dozens of hours of fun out of it. With a little more refinement, this will hopefully go the distance.

_childDocuments_.review: Outriders is a 1-3 player co-op RPG shooter set in an original, dark and desperate sci-fi universe. As mankind bleeds out in the trenches of Enoch, you'll create your own Outrider and embark on a journey across the hostile planet. With rich storytelling spanning a diverse world, you'll leave behind the slums and shanty towns of the First City and traverse forests, mountains and desert in the pursuit of a mysterious signal. Combining intense gunplay with violent powers and an arsenal of increasingly twisted weaponry and gear-sets, Outriders offers countless hours of gameplay from one of the finest shooter developers in the industry People Can Fly.
